Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs he said: they are the signs that were placed in his hands such as reviving the dead and creating him from clay in the form of a bird, and healing diseases. And the report of many of the unseen things, and what was brought to them from the Torah and the Gospel that God revealed to him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And We supported him he said: We strengthened him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The Spirit of Jerusalem is the name by which Jesus revived the dead. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: Jerusalem is God Almighty. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas narrated something similar. He narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Jerusalem is purity. He narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi that he said: Jerusalem is blessing. He narrated on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid that the Spirit of Jerusalem is Gabriel. He narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The Spirit of Jerusalem is Gabriel. It has been proven in Sahih that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, support Hassan with the Spirit of Jerusalem. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr regarding his statement: A group, he said: A group. He narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The heart was named so because of its changeability. Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat on his authority that he used to recite Our hearts are covered with a heavy meaning: How can we learn while our hearts are covered for wisdom? Meaning vessels for wisdom. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: “And they said: Our hearts are covered,” filled with knowledge that do not need the knowledge of Muhammad or anyone else. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: Our hearts are covered, he said: In a covering. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said: In coverings. Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said: They are the hearts that are sealed. Waki’ narrated from Ikrimah and Ibn Jarir from Mujahid similarly. Abd Ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah that he said: They are those that do not understand. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in the book of Al-Ikhlas and Ibn Jarir from Hudhayfah that he said: Hearts are of four types: A covered heart, and that is the heart of the disbeliever; a plated heart, and that is the heart of the hypocrite; a bare heart in which is like a lamp, and that is the heart of the believer; and a heart in which is faith and hypocrisy. So the example of faith is like a tree that is nourished by what is good, and the example of the hypocrite is like a sore that is nourished by pus and blood. Ahmad narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Saeed that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hearts are of four types: a bare heart in which there is a shining lamp; a covered heart tied to its covering; an inverted heart; and a plated heart. As for the bare heart, it is the heart of the believer whose lamp has light in it; as for the covered heart, it is the heart of the disbeliever; as for the inverted heart, it is the heart of the hypocrite who recognized and then denied; as for the plated heart, it is a heart in which there is both faith and hypocrisy. So the example of faith in it is like that of a plant nourished by good water, and the example of hypocrisy in it is like that of an ulcer nourished by pus; whichever of the two substances overcomes the other, it overcomes it.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Salman al-Farisi, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: But few of them believe, he said: None of them believe except a few.
2:89: 89- And when there came to them meaning the Jews a book meaning the Qur'an, and confirming is a description of it, and it is in the Mushaf of Abu Mansur and its accusative is in the state, even though its owner is indefinite, it is specified by its description by his saying: from God and his confirmation of what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, that he informs them of what is in them and confirms it and does not contradict it. And the opening is seeking al-Nasr 110:that is, they used to ask God for victory over their enemies through the described prophet at the end of time whose description they find with them in the Torah, and it was said: The opening here means the conquest: that is, they inform them that he will be sent and they make them know that, and the answer to what is in his saying: And when there came to them a book it was said: it is his saying: So when there came to them what they did not recognize and what follows it, and it was said that it is omitted: that is, they lied or something like it, this is what Al-Akhfash and Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Mubarrad said: The answer to the first lama is his saying: they disbelieved. The second lama was repeated due to the length of the speech, and the lam in al-kafireen is for the genus. It is possible that it is for the covenant, and this is from placing the apparent in place of the implicit, and the first is more apparent.
2:90: And in his saying: 90- "B'isama" is a relative or a description: meaning, "B'is a thing or something they bought themselves with" said Sibawayh. Al-Akhfash said: "Ma" is in the accusative case as a specification, like your saying: "B'is a man Zayd". Al-Farra' said: "B'isama in its entirety is one thing that is composed like Habbatha". Al-Kisa'i said: "Ma and they bought" is in the position of one name that stands on its own, and the meaning is: "B'is their buying that they disbelieve". And his saying: "that they disbelieve" is in the nominative case as a subject according to Sibawayh, and its predicate is what precedes it. Al-Farra' and Al-Kisa'i said: If you wish, it was in the genitive case instead of the "ha in bih": meaning, they bought themselves by disbelieving. And he said in Al-Kashshaf: "Ma is an indefinite noun in the accusative case explaining the subject of B'is", meaning something they bought themselves with, and the one specifically blamed is that they disbelieve, and they bought means they sold. His saying: Baghyan means envy. Al-Asma’i said: Baghy is taken from their saying that the wound has become corrupted, and it was said: its origin is the request, and that is why the adulteress was called Baghyan. It is the reason for his saying: they bought and his saying: that He should descend is the reason for his saying: Baghyan meaning that He should descend. The meaning is: they sold themselves for this cheap price out of envy and competition that God should send down from His grace upon whomever He wills of His servants. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ya’qub, and Ibn Muhaisin read that He should descend with the light vowel. So they returned means they returned and became worthy with wrath upon wrath. The meaning of Baghya and the meaning of wrath have already been mentioned. It was said: the first wrath was for their worship of the calf, and the second was for their disbelief in Muhammad. It was said: their disbelief in Jesus then their disbelief in Muhammad. It was said: their disbelief in Muhammad then the transgression against him. It was said: other than that. Al-Muhin is taken from Al-Hawaan. It was said: it is what necessitates eternity in the Fire.
2:91: And His statement: 91- In what God has revealed is the Qur'an, and it was said: every book: meaning they believed in the Qur'an or believed in what God revealed of the books. "They said: We believe" meaning we believe in what was revealed to us meaning the Torah. And His statement: And they disbelieve in what is beyond it Al-Farra' said: in what is other than it. Abu Ubaidah said: in what is beyond it. Al-Jawhari said: Behind means behind, and it may mean in front of them and they are from the opposites. And from it is His statement, the Most High: And behind them was a king meaning in front of them, and this sentence, I mean and they disbelieve, is in the accusative case on the ropes: meaning they said: We believe in what was revealed to us while they were disbelievers in what is beyond it while this that is beyond what they believe in is the truth. His saying: confirming is a confirming state, and these are intertwined states, I mean his saying: and they disbelieve, and his saying: and it is the truth, and his saying: confirming. Then God, the Most High, objected to them when they said: We believe in what was revealed to us, with this sentence that includes a question that serves as a rebuke: that is, if you believe in what was revealed to you, then how do you kill the prophets when you were forbidden from killing them in what was revealed to you? And even if this address was to the Jews who were present, what is meant by it is their ancestors, but since they were satisfied with the actions of their ancestors, they were like them.
2:92: The lam in His statement: 92- And indeed is an answer to an implied oath. And the clear proofs may be intended to mean the Torah or the nine verses referred to in the statement of God Almighty: And We gave Moses nine clear signs or it may be intended to mean all of them, then you worshipped the calf after considering those clear proofs while you were wrongdoers with this worship that came from you out of stubbornness after the proof was established against you. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And when there came to them a Book from God, confirming, he said: It is the Qur’an, confirming what is with them, of the Torah and the Gospel. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Nu’aym, and Al-Bayhaqi, both of them narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Asim bin Umar bin Qatada Al-Ansari, who said: Our elders told me that none of the Arabs knew more about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than us, because there were Jews with us and they were People of the Book and we were idolaters. When they heard something they disliked from us, they would say: A Prophet will be sent now and his time has come, so we will follow him and kill you with him as ‘Aad and Iram were killed. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, we followed him and they disbelieved in him. So it was about us, by God, and about them that God revealed: And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala'il on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and some of the Companions who said: The Arabs would pass by the Jews and harm them, and they would find Muhammad in the Torah and ask God to send him as a prophet so they could fight the Arabs with him. But when Muhammad came, they disbelieved in him since he was not from the Children of Israel. Something similar to this has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas from more than one source with different wordings but similar meanings. Something similar has been narrated on the authority of others from the Salaf. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: How evil is that for which they have sold themselves, he said: They are the Jews who disbelieved in what God revealed and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of envy and spite for the Arabs. So they incurred wrath upon wrath, he said: God became angry with them twice for their disbelief in the Gospel and Jesus, and for their disbelief in the Qur'an and Muhammad. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Out of desire that God should send down meaning that God made him from someone other than them. So they incurred wrath for their disbelief in this prophet upon wrath that was upon them for what they had done to the Torah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar. He also narrated on the authority of Mujahid its meaning. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah regarding his statement: And they disbelieve in what comes after it he said: what comes after it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Suddi who said: what comes after it: meaning the Qur’an.
2:93: The interpretation of taking the covenant and raising the mountain has been presented. The command to listen means obedience and acceptance, and it does not mean merely perceiving with the sense of hearing. From this is their saying: God hears whoever praises Him, meaning He accepts and responds. From this is the saying of the poet: I called upon God until I was afraid that God might not hear what I was saying. 93- We heard is in its proper context and meaning: that is, we heard your words with our sense of hearing and we disobeyed you: that is, we do not accept what you command us to do. It is possible that they intended by their saying: We heard what is known of their playing and using deception in addressing their prophets, and that is by taking the words of God Almighty: Listen to their true meaning, that is, hearing with our senses. Then they answered by saying: We heard meaning we perceived that with our ears in accordance with what you commanded. However, since they knew that this was not what God Almighty intended, rather what He intended by the command to listen was the command to obey and accept, they did not limit themselves to this deception, but rather they added to that what is the answer according to them, so they said: And we disobeyed. And in His saying: And drink is a powerful simile: that is, their hearts were made to be able to love the calf as if they were drinking it. Similar to it is the saying of Zuhair: I woke up from it after an inner love, and love always drinks from your heart The love of the calf was expressed by drinking and not eating, because drinking water penetrates the organs until it reaches their interior, while food bypasses them and does not penetrate them. The ba in His statement, because of their disbelief is causal: that is, it was because of their disbelief as a punishment and failure for them. And His statement, Say, ‘How evil is that which your faith enjoins upon you’ means your faith in which you claimed that you believe in what was revealed to you and disbelieve in what is beyond it. For this action, which is your saying, We hear and disobey, in response to what you were commanded to do in your book and the covenant was taken from you, is a caller to you with the most eloquent call, contrary to what you claimed. Likewise, what you did of worshipping the calf and its love descending from your hearts to the level of drink is one of the greatest indications that you are liars in your statement, We believe in what was revealed to us, not truthful. If you claim that your book in which you believe commands you to do this, then how evil is that which your faith in your book enjoins upon you. And in this there is mockery of them that is not hidden.
2:94: And His statement: 94- "Say: If the home of the Hereafter is yours" is a response to them when they claimed that they will enter Paradise and no one else will share in entering it, and an obligation to them with what shows that they are lying in that claim, and that it is issued by them and not from proof, and purely is in the accusative case as a state and it is the predicate of was is with God or it is the predicate of was is purely, and the meaning of purity is that no one else will share in it with them if the lam in His statement: from among the people is for the genus or the Muslims will not share in it with them if the lam is for the covenant. This is more likely for their statement in the other verse: And they said, 'None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian' and He only ordered them to wish for death because whoever believes that he is from the people of Paradise, death is more beloved to him than life, and since that was a mere claim from them, they refrained.
2:95: That is why the Almighty said: 95- And they will never wish for it. And what is in His saying: Because of what their hands have put forth is a relative pronoun and the pronoun is omitted: that is, because of what they have put forth of sins, the doer of which is not safe from punishment, and is not even hopeful of entering Paradise, let alone being certain of it, let alone it being purely for him and specific to him. And it was said: God the Almighty turned them away from wishing in order to make that a sign for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. What is meant by wishing here is: uttering what indicates it, not just its occurrence in the heart and the soul’s inclination towards it, because that is not intended in the context of argument, situations of dispute, and situations of challenge. Their abandonment of wishing or their turning away from it is a miracle for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they used to behave arrogantly and boldly towards God and His prophets with false claims in situations other than what the revelation has narrated about them. They did not abandon their habit here except because it was established for them that if they did that wish, death would befall them, either for a matter they knew, or because of a turning away from God, the Almighty. It may be said: It is proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was forbidden from wishing for death, so how could God command him to command them with what is forbidden in His law? The answer is that what is meant here is to oblige them with the argument and establish the proof of the invalidity of their claim. His statement, And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers is a threat to them and a record against them that they are like that.
2:96: The lam in his saying: 96- And you will find them is the answer to an omitted oath, and the indefiniteness of life is for disparagement: that is, they are the most eager of people for the most insignificant life and the shortest stay in this world, so how about a long life and a long stay? And he said in Al-Kashshaf: He meant by the indefiniteness a specific life, which is the long life, and Al-Razi followed him in that in his interpretation. And his saying: And among those who associate others with God it was said: It is a new statement, and the meaning is: And among those who associate others with God are people one of whom would like and it was said: It is conjoined with al-Nas 114:that is, the most eager of people and more eager than those who associate others, and based on this his saying: one of whom would like refers back to the Jews to clarify their increased eagerness for life, and the reason for mentioning those who associate others with God after mentioning the people despite them being included among them is to indicate the increased eagerness of the polytheists among the Arabs and those similar to them from others. So whoever was more eager than them, and they are the Jews, was extremely eager to an extent that cannot be measured. They reached this level of greed that is superior to that of the polytheists, because they know what punishment will befall them in the Hereafter, unlike the polytheists of the Arabs and others like them, who do not acknowledge that, and their greed for life was less than that of the Jews. Although the first is a departure from the discussion of the Jews to other polytheists of the Arabs, it is more preferable because it does not entail any obligation, and there is no harm in digressing to mention the greed of the polytheists after mentioning the greed of the Jews. Al-Razi said: The second is more preferable because it is more effective in invalidating their claim and revealing their lie in their saying that the Hereafter is for us and not for others. The answer to this is that what made it preferable was indicated in the Almighty’s saying: And you will find them the most greedy of people. Resuming the discussion of the polytheists does not entail that they are not among the people, and the letter alif was mentioned specifically because the Arabs used to mention that when wanting to exaggerate. The root of sunnah is sanahah, and it was said: sanwah. There is a difference of opinion regarding the pronoun in his statement: And it is not a thing that will move him away, so it was said that it refers to one of them, and the meaning is: And not one of them will move him away from the punishment that he will live long, and on this basis his statement: that he will live long is the subject of move him away, and it was said: It is for what is indicated by live long from its source: that is, and life long longevity will not move him, and his statement: that he will live long would be a substitute for it. Al-Tabari narrated from a group that they said: It is a pillar, and it was said: It is the pronoun of the matter, and it was said: What is Hijazi and the pronoun is its subject and what follows it is its predicate and the first is more correct, and likewise the second and third are very weak because the pillar only occurs between two things, and for this reason they call it the pronoun of separation, and the fourth in it is that the pronoun of the matter is interpreted by a sentence free from a preposition as Ibn Atiyah narrated from the grammarians. And moving away is moving away, it is said: I moved him away so he moved away and distanced himself, and from this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: O He who takes the soul from a body that has disobeyed for a long time and forgives sins, save me from the Fire. Al-Basir: the one who knows something and is an expert in it. From this comes their saying: So-and-so is an expert in such-and-such: meaning he is an expert in it. From this comes the saying of the poet: If you ask me about women, I am a doctor who specializes in women’s diseases. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And they made the calf drink into their hearts, he said: They made its love reach their hearts. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah that when the Jews said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, the verse was revealed, the verse: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter is for you,” the verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement: Purely for you, apart from the people, means the believers, so wish for death, so the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said to them: “If you are truthful in what you say, then say: O God, cause us to die, for by the One in Whose hand is my soul, no man among you says it except that he chokes on his saliva and dies on the spot.” Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So wish for death, meaning they claimed death for whichever of the two groups was more lying, but they refused. If they had wished for it on the day he said that, there would not have remained a Jew on earth who did not die. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu Nu`aym narrated on his authority that he said: If the Jews wished for death, they would die. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on his authority. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on his authority that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If the Jews wished for death, they would die and see their seats in the Fire. Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on his authority regarding his statement: And you will find them the most greedy of people for life, he said: the Jews. And even more than those who associate others with God, he said: that is because the polytheists do not hope for resurrection after death, so a long life is required, and the Jew has realised his shame because he wasted the knowledge he had. And it will not remove him, he said: by giving him something. Saeed ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: One of them would like to live a thousand years, he said: it is the saying of the non-Arabs when one of them sneezes, He will be resurrected, meaning live a thousand years.
2:97: This verse has been unanimously agreed upon by the commentators that it was revealed about the Jews. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: All the commentators agreed that this verse was revealed in response to the Jews when they claimed that Gabriel was their enemy and that Michael was their guardian. Then they differed as to the reason for their saying that. Some of them said: The reason for that was because of a debate that took place between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the matter of his prophethood. Then he mentioned narrations about that which will come at the end of the discussion, God willing. The pronoun in His statement: 97- "For it" has two possible meanings: The first is that it refers to God and the pronoun in His statement: "He sent it down" refers to Gabriel: meaning that God, the Exalted, sent Gabriel down to your heart, and there is weakness in that as is indicated by His statement: "Confirming what was before it. The second is that it refers to Gabriel, and the pronoun in He sent it down" refers to the Qur'an: meaning that Gabriel sent down the Qur'an to your heart, and the heart was specifically mentioned because it is the seat of reason and knowledge. And his saying: By the permission of God means by His knowledge, will, facilitation and ease, and what is before Him is the Torah as mentioned above or all the revealed books. This is evidence of the honor of Gabriel and the high status of his position, and that there is no reason for the Jews to be hostile to him since he did what was mentioned about the revelation of the Book to your heart, or God’s revelation of it to your heart. This is the connection between the condition and the answer, meaning whoever is hostile to Gabriel among them, there is no reason for his hostility to him, since he did nothing but what necessitates love without enmity, or whoever is hostile to him, the reason for his hostility is that he did what they dislike of the revelation, and that is not a sin of his even if they exonerated him, for this hatred of him from them for this reason is injustice and aggression, because this book that he revealed is a confirmation of their book and guidance and good tidings for the believers.
2:98: Then the Almighty followed this speech with a sentence that includes a condition and a penalty that includes censure for whoever is hostile to Gabriel for that reason and a severe threat to him, so He said: 98- Whoever is an enemy to God and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael - then indeed, God is an enemy to the disbelievers. Enmity from the servant is the issuance of sins from him towards God and hatred for His friends, and enmity from God towards the servant is punishing him for his sin and not overlooking it or forgiving him - and Gabriel and Michael were mentioned specifically after mentioning the angels in order to honor them and indicate their excellence, and that even though they are from the angels, they have become, in consideration of what they have of excellence, in the position of another genus more honorable than the genus of angels, reducing the descriptive difference to the level of intrinsic difference as mentioned by the author of Al-Kashshaf and established by the scholars of rhetoric. And Gabriel has ten languages mentioned by Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari and others, and we have already indicated that. And in Michael there are six languages, and they are two foreign names, and the Arabs, when they pronounce it in a foreign language, are lenient with it. Al-Zamakhshari narrated on the authority of Ibn Jinni that he said: The Arabs, when they pronounce it in a foreign language, mix it up. And his saying: for the disbelievers is from placing the apparent in place of the implicit: meaning that God is an enemy to them, with the intention of indicating that this enmity necessitates the disbelief of whoever it occurs from. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu Nu`aym and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “A group of Jews attended the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Abu al-Qasim, tell us about characteristics that we ask you about and that only a prophet knows. ’ He said: ‘Ask me whatever you wish. ’ So they asked him and he answered them. Then they said: ‘Tell us who is your guardian among the angels, so that we may either have intercourse with you or leave you. ’ He said: ‘My guardian is Gabriel, and God never sent a prophet except that he is his guardian. ’ They said: ‘Then we will leave you. If your guardian were other than him among the angels, we would follow you and believe you. ’ He said: ‘What prevents you from believing him? ’ They said: ‘This is our enemy. ’ At that point God revealed the verse.” Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar in al-Musannaf, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of al-Sha`bi on the authority of `Umar ibn al-Khattab in a story that happened to him with them, and its chain of transmission is sound, but al-Sha`bi did not meet `Umar. It was narrated by `Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi and `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla on the authority of `Umar. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, al-Nasa’i and others narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: “Abdullah ibn Salam heard of the arrival of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in a land collecting dung beetles. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘I am going to ask you about three things that only a prophet knows: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food of the people of Paradise? What makes a child gravitate towards his father or mother?’ He said: ‘Gabriel told me about them just now.’ Gabriel said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘That is the enemy of the Jews from among the angels.’ Then he recited this verse: ‘Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart. ’ He said: ‘As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will come out from the east and will gather people to the west. As for the first thing that the people of Paradise will eat, it is the extra liver of a fish. As for what makes a child gravitate towards his father or mother, if the man’s semen precedes the woman’s semen, the child will be drawn to him. If the woman’s semen precedes the man’s semen, the child will be drawn to her.’ He said: ‘I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God. ’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: For He has brought it down upon your heart by permission of God, meaning: Gabriel brought down the Qur’an by the command of God, strengthening your heart and binding it to your heart. Confirming what was before it, meaning what came before it of the books that He revealed, the verses, and the messengers that God sent. Al-Suyuti mentioned in this place in his interpretation, Al-Durr Al-Manthur, many hadiths about Gabriel and Michael, but they are not related to interpretation so we should mention them.
2:99: The pronoun in His statement: 99- "To you" refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: meaning, We sent down clear signs indicating your prophethood. And His statement: "Except the wicked" has been explained previously, and it appears that what is meant is the wicked race, and it is possible that what is meant is the Jews because the speech is with them.
2:100: And the waw in his saying: 100- "or whenever" is for conjunction, the question hamza entered it as it enters the fa, and from that is the saying of the Almighty: "Is it the judgment of ignorance they seek? Do you then make the deaf hear? Do you then take him and his descendants?" and as it enters the then, and from that is the saying of the Almighty: "Athman when it occurs" and this is the saying of Sibawayh. Al-Akhfash said: The waw is redundant. Al-Kisa'i said: It is or the waw was moved for ease. Ibn Atiyah said: All of this is forced, and the correct saying of Sibawayh and the conjoined to it is deleted, and the estimate is they disbelieved in the clear verses and whenever they made a covenant. His saying: "A group rejected" Ibn Jarir said: The origin of nabdh is throwing and casting, and from that the foundling is called manbuth, and from that wine is called dates and raisins when they are thrown into water, Abu Al-Aswad said: I looked at his address and threw it away like you would throw away a worn-out sandal from your sandals. Another said: Those whom you commanded to be just have rejected your Book and made lawful what is forbidden.
2:101: And his saying: 101- Behind their backs meaning behind their backs, and it is a proverb used for someone who takes something lightly and does not act upon it. The Arabs say: Put this behind your back, behind your ear, and under your foot: meaning leave it and turn away from it. And from this is what Al-Farra’ recited: Tamim bin Zaid: Do not let my need be in the back, lest I be unable to answer it. And his saying: The Book of God meaning the Torah because when they disbelieved in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what was revealed to him after God took from them in the Torah and belief in him and confirmation of him and following him and explained to them his description, that was from them a rejection of the Torah and a breach of it and a rejection of what is in it. And it is possible that what is meant by the Book here is the Qur’an: that is, when the Messenger of God came to them from God confirming what they had of the Torah, they rejected the Book of God that this Messenger brought, and this is more evident than the first aspect. And his saying: As if they did not know is a likening of them to someone who does not know anything even though they know with certainty from the Torah what is required of them of belief in this Prophet, but since they did not know with knowledge but rather acted like someone who does not know who threw the Book of God behind their backs, they were in the position of someone who does not know.
2:102: His saying: 102- And they followed what the devils recited is connected to his saying: they cast aside, meaning they cast aside the Book of God and followed what the devils recited of magic and the like. At-Tabari said: they followed means they did. The meaning of recite is you say it and you read it and during the reign of Solomon is during the reign of Solomon, as Al-Zajjaj said. It was said: the meaning in the reign of Solomon: meaning in his stories, descriptions and report. Al-Farra' said: And in is suitable in this place, but the first is more apparent. They thought that this was the knowledge of Solomon and that he would permit it and say it, so God rejected that and said: And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved. It was not mentioned before that anyone attributed Solomon to disbelief, but when the Jews attributed magic to him, they became like someone who attributed disbelief to him because magic requires that, and for this reason God, the Most High, confirmed the disbelief of the devils and said: But the devils disbelieved meaning in their teaching. His saying: They teach people magic is in the accusative case as a state, and it is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a predicate after a predicate. Ibn Amir and the Kufians except Asim read but the devils with a lightened but and the raising of the devils, and the rest with a heavy and accusative. Magic is what the magician does of tricks and illusions that cause the bewitched to get corrupt thoughts similar to what happens to someone who sees a mirage and thinks it is water, and what the rider of a ship or an animal thinks that the mountains are moving. It is derived from the word sahart al-sabi if you deceived the boy. It was said: its origin is concealment, because the magician does it secretly. It was said: its origin is spending because magic is diverted from its direction. It was said: its origin is attracting because whoever bewitches you has attracted you. Al-Jawhari said: Magic is taking, and everything that is subtle and delicate is magic. He bewitched him, bewitches him with magic, and the magician is the scholar, and he bewitched him also means he deceived him. There is a difference of opinion as to whether it has a reality or not. The Mu'tazila and Abu Hanifa went to the view that it is [deception] that has no origin or reality. Others went to the fact that it has an influential reality. It has been authenticated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was bewitched by Labid bin Al-A'sam the Jew, until he imagined that something was happening to him when it was not, then God Almighty healed him. The discussion of that is long. And His statement: And what was revealed to the two angels means that they teach people what was revealed to the two angels, so it is conjoined with magic. It was said: It is conjoined with His statement: What the devils recite, meaning and they followed what God revealed to the two angels. It was said: What is in His statement: And what was revealed to the two angels is negative, and the waw is a conjunction with His statement: And Solomon did not disbelieve. There is an inversion of the statement, and the estimate is: And Solomon did not disbelieve, nor did he disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic in Babylon, Harut and Marut, so Harut and Marut are substitutes for the devils in His statement: But the devils disbelieved. Ibn Jarir mentioned this and said: If someone were to say to us: How did this come to be presented? It was said: The reason for presenting it is to say: And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, nor did God send down to the two angels. Rather, the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic in Babylon, and Harut and Marut. So it is protected by the two angels Gabriel and Michael, because the Jewish magicians, as mentioned, claimed that God sent down magic through the tongues of Gabriel and Michael to Solomon, son of David. So God denied them in that and informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Gabriel and Michael did not send down magic, and He acquitted Solomon of what they attributed to him of magic, and He informed them that magic is the work of the devils, and that they teach people that in Babylon, and that those who teach them that are two men, one of them is Harut and the other is Marut. So Harut and Marut, according to this interpretation, are a translation from the people and a response to them. End quote. Al-Qurtubi said in his interpretation after he narrated the meaning of this statement and preferred that Harut and Marut were a substitute for the devils, what he said: This is the most appropriate meaning of the verse and the most correct thing that has been said about it, and no attention should be paid to anything else, for magic is from the extraction of devils due to the delicacy of their essence and the sharpness of their understanding, and most of what is practiced by humans is women, especially during their menstruation. God said: And from the evil of those who blow on knots. Then he said: If it is said, how can two be a substitute for a group, and the substitute is only on the same level as the substituted? Then he answered that by saying that two may be called a group, or that they were specifically mentioned without others due to their rebellion, and this is supported by the fact that Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and Al-Hasan read the two angels with a kasra on the lam, and perhaps the reason for being certain of this interpretation, despite its remoteness and the apparent difficulty of it, is to exonerate God, the Most High, from sending magic to His earth as a trial for His servants through the tongues of His angels. I believe that there is no reason for this arbitrariness that contradicts what is apparent, for God Almighty can test His servants as He wills, just as He tested Talut with the River. For this reason, the two angels say: We are only a trial. Ibn Jarir said: Many of the predecessors believed that they were two angels from the heavens, and that they were sent down to the earth and what happened to them happened. Babylon is said to be Iraq, and it is said to be Nahavand, and it is said to be Nasibin, and it is said to be Morocco. Harut and Marut are two foreign names that are not declined. And his saying: And they do not teach anyone until they say Al-Zajjaj said: Teaching is a warning against magic, not teaching an invitation to it. He said: This is what most people of language and thought agree on, and its meaning is: that they teach as a prohibition, so they say to them: Do not do such and such. And from in his saying: from anyone is redundant for emphasis. And it has been said: that his saying: they teach is from informing, not from teaching. And in the speech of the Arabs it has come to mean teach, as Ibn al-Anbari and Ibn al-A’rabi narrated, and it is common in their poetry, like the saying of Ka’b ibn Malik: The Messenger of God learned that you will catch up with me and that a threat from you is like taking me by the hand. Al-Qatami said: Learn that after error comes guidance and that error will be dispelled. His statement: We are only a trial is to be taken literally. That is, we are only a trial and test from God for His servants. It was said that it was a mockery of them because they only say this to someone whose misguidance they have realized. In their statement: So do not disbelieve is the most eloquent and greatest warning: that this is a sin that makes the one who does it a disbeliever, so do not disbelieve. It is evidence that learning magic is disbelief. Its apparent meaning is that there is no difference between the one who believes and the one who does not believe, and between the one who learns it to be a magician and the one who learns it to be able to repel it. His statement: So they learn contains a pronoun that refers to his statement: From anyone. Sibawayh said: The meaning is that they learn. He said: And similar to it is Be and it is. It was said: It is conjoined with the position of what they know, because even though it is negated, it includes the affirmative. Al-Farra’ said: It is a response to his statement: They teach people magic, meaning they teach people so they learn. His statement: That by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, in attributing separation to magicians and making magic a cause for that, is evidence that magic has an effect on hearts through love and hate, unity and separation, closeness and distance. A group of scholars have said that the magician is not capable of doing more than what God has informed us about in terms of separation, because God mentioned that in the context of censuring magic and explaining what is the goal of teaching it. If he was capable of doing more than that, He would have mentioned it. Another group said: That was stated in a most likely manner, and that the magician is capable of doing other than what is stated explicitly. It was said: Magic has no effect in itself at all, because God the Almighty said: And they can harm no one thereby except by God’s permission. The truth is that there is no contradiction between his statement: And they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, and his statement: And they can harm no one thereby except by God’s permission. What is understood from all of that is that magic has an effect in itself, but it does not cause harm except to those whom God has permitted it to affect. The scholars have agreed that it has an effect on itself and is a proven fact, and no one disagreed with that except the Mu'tazila and Abu Hanifa, as mentioned above. His statement, And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them clearly states that magic does not benefit its practitioner and does not bring him any benefit, but rather it is pure harm and sheer loss. The lam in his statement, And indeed is the answer to an omitted oath, and in his statement, For whoever bought it is for emphasis, and from is a relative pronoun and is in the nominative case as a subject, and the predicate is his statement, He will have no share in the Hereafter. Al-Farra' said: It is a conditional particle for recompense. Al-Zajjaj said: This is not a conditional particle, and he preferred that it is a relative pronoun as we mentioned. What is meant by buying here is substitution, i.e. whoever substitutes what the devils recite in the Book of God. And the share is the portion according to the linguists, as Al-Zajjaj said. What is meant by his statement, For which they sold themselves is that they sold them. He affirmed knowledge for them in His statement: And they certainly knew, and denied it for them in His statement: If they only knew. They differed in interpreting that. Qutrub and Al-Akhfash said: What is meant by His statement: And they certainly knew are the devils, and what is meant by His statement: If they only knew are mankind. Al-Zajjaj said: The first refers to the two angels, even though it is in the plural form, so it is like their saying: The two Zayds stood up. The second refers to the scholars of the Jews, and He only said: If they only knew because they abandoned acting on their knowledge.
2:103: And His statement: 103- And if they had believed meaning in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought of the Qur’an, and feared what they fell into of magic and disbelief, and the lam in His statement: for a reward is the answer to if, and the reward is the recompense. Al-Akhfash said: The answer is omitted and the meaning is: And if they had believed and feared God, they would have been rewarded, so it was omitted because His statement: for a reward indicates it, and His statement: If they had known is either to indicate that they had no knowledge, or to lower their knowledge with the lack of action to the level of nothingness. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “Ibn Suriya said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘O Muhammad, you have not brought us anything that is known, and God has not sent down to you a clear sign.’ So God Almighty revealed regarding that: ‘And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs, and none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient.’” Malik ibn al-Sayf said when he sent the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he reminded them of the covenant that he had taken from them and what he had entrusted to them regarding Muhammad: ‘By God, he did not entrust us with anything regarding Muhammad nor did he take anything from us.’ So God revealed: ‘Or whenever they made a covenant’. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: ‘clear signs’, he said: So you recite it to them and inform them of it morning and evening and in between, and you are illiterate in their eyes and have not read the Book, and you inform them of what is in their hands in its entirety, so in that there is a lesson for them and an argument against them ‘if they only knew.’” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: ‘He rejected it’, he said: He broke it. He also narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi in his saying: Confirming what is with them, he said: When Muhammad came to them, they opposed him with the Torah, and the Torah and the Qur’an agreed, so they rejected the Torah and took the Book of Asif and the magic of Harut and Marut, as if they did not know what was in the Torah of the command to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believe in him. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The devils used to eavesdrop from the sky, so if one of them heard a word of truth, he would tell a thousand lies with it, so the hearts of the people would absorb it and they would take it as records, so God informed Solomon, son of David, of that, so he took it and buried it under the throne, and when Solomon died, a devil stood up on the road and said: Shall I not guide you to the treasure of Solomon, which no one has like his forbidden treasure? They said: Yes, so they took it out and it turned out to be magic, so the nations copied it. And God revealed the excuse of Solomon for what they said about magic, so He said: And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon 10:13. Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Asaf was the scribe of Solomon, and he knew the Greatest Name. He used to write down everything by Solomon’s command and bury it under his throne. When Solomon died, the devils brought him out and wrote between every two lines something like magic and blasphemy. They said: This is what Solomon did, the devils brought him out. They wrote between every two lines something like magic and blasphemy. They said: This is what Solomon used to do. The ignorant people declared him an unbeliever and cursed him. Their scholars stood up, and their ignorant people continued to curse him until God revealed to Muhammad, And they followed what the devils recited. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: When Solomon wanted to go to the toilet or do something of his business, he would give his ring to the locust, which was his wife. When God wanted to test Solomon with what He tested him with, he gave the locust his ring one day. Then Satan came in the form of Solomon and said to it: Give me my ring. So he took it and put it on. When he put it on, the devils, jinn and humans obeyed him. Then Solomon came and said: Give me my ring. It said: You lie, you are not Solomon. So he knew that it was a test with which he was tested. So the devils went and wrote books in those days that contained magic and blasphemy. Then they buried them under Solomon’s throne. Then they took them out and read them to the people and said: It was Solomon who was overpowering the people with these books. So the people disavowed Solomon and disbelieved in him until God sent Muhammad and revealed to him: It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding His statement: And they did not recite, he said: What they followed. He also narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding His statement: And they did not recite, he said: We see that they did not speak. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: during the reign of Solomon he said: during the reign of Solomon. He also narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And what was revealed to the two angels he said: This is another magic that they disputed with him about, because if the speech of the angels among themselves is taught to mankind and they do and act upon it, it is magic. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And what was revealed to the two angels he said: God did not reveal magic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali who said: They are two angels from the angels of heaven. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from another chain of transmission on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history and Ibn Al-Mundhir on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And what was revealed to the two angels meaning Gabriel and Michael in Babylon, Harut and Marut teaching people magic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Al-Bazi that he used to recite it: And what was revealed to the two angels David and Solomon. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: They are two giants from the people of Babylon. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu’ab Al-Iman from the hadith of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The angels looked down upon the world and saw the children of Adam disobeying, so they said: O Lord, how ignorant these are! How little these people know of Your greatness. God said: If you were in their places, you would disobey Me. They said: How can this be when we glorify You and sanctify You? He said: So they chose two angels from among you, and they chose Harut and Marut. Then they were sent down to the earth and the desires of the children of Adam were in them, and a woman appeared to them, but they did not disobey until they committed the sin. God said: Choose the torment of this world or the torment of the Hereafter. One of them looked at the other and said: What do you say? He said: I say that the torment of this world will end and the torment of the Hereafter will not end. So they chose the torment of this world, and they are the ones whom God mentioned in His Book: “And what was sent down to the two angels” verse. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Umar that he used to say: The red rose after a while, and when he saw it, he said: No welcome. Then he said: Two angels from the angels, Harut and Marut, asked God to bring them down to earth, so they were brought down to earth and they used to judge between people. When evening came, they spoke words and ascended with them to heaven. A woman from the most beautiful of women was appointed for them, and desire was cast upon them, so they delayed it and it was cast into their souls. They did not stop doing that until I promised them an appointment. Then she came to them for the appointment and said: Teach me the word with which you ascend. So they taught her the word and she spoke it, so he ascended to heaven and she was transformed and became as you see. When evening came, they spoke the word and did not ascend. So he sent to them: If you wish, then the torment of the Hereafter, and if you wish, then the torment of this world until the Hour comes, so that you may meet God. If He wills, He will punish you, and if He wills, He will have mercy on you. Then one of them looked at the other and said: Rather, we choose the torment of this world a thousand thousand times. So they are tormented until The Day of Resurrection. This story has been narrated from Ibn Umar with different wordings, and in some of them it is stated that Ibn Umar narrated it from Kaab al-Ahbar, as narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sha`b on the authority of al-Thawri on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah on the authority of Salim on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of Kaab, who said: The angels mentioned the deeds of the children of Adam and the sins they commit, and it was said: If you were in your place, you would have committed the same as they commit, so choose two of you, and they chose Harut and Marut. He said to them: I send messengers to the children of Adam, and there is no messenger between Me and you. Come down and do not associate anything with Me, and do not commit adultery, and do not drink wine. Kaab said: By God, they did not spend the evening of the day on which they were sent down until they had done everything they were forbidden to do. Ibn Kathir said: This is more authentic, meaning than the two chains of transmission he mentioned before it. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that is authentic on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, who said: This flower is called Al-Zahra by the Arabs, and Anahid by the Persians. He mentioned something similar to the previous narration on the authority of Ibn Umar in Al-Hakim. Ibn Kathir said: The men of this chain of transmission are trustworthy and it is very strange. Abd bin Hamid and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that is authentic on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Zahra was a woman. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd bin Hamid narrated on his authority: The woman with whom the two angels were tempted was transformed, so she is this red constellation: meaning Al-Zahra. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that is authentic, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated with a chain of transmission that is authentic on the authority of Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Zahra was sent down to them in the form of a woman and they committed the sin. In this regard, long stories and various narrations have been narrated, which Al-Suyuti has included in Al-Durr Al-Manthur. Ibn Kathir mentioned some of them in his interpretation, then said: The story of Harut and Marut has been narrated by a group of the Successors, such as Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Zuhri, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and others. It has been narrated by many of the commentators, both early and later. The gist of it is that its details refer to the stories of the Children of Israel, as there is no authentic hadith in it with a continuous chain of transmission to the Truthful, Trusted, Infallible One who does not speak from his own desires. The apparent context of the Qur’an is to summarize the story without elaboration or length. We believe in what is mentioned in the Qur’an as God Almighty intended, and God knows best the truth of the matter. Al-Qurtubi said: After narrating some of that: We said that all of this is weak and far from Ibn Umar and others, and none of it is authentic, as it is a statement that is rejected by the principles regarding the angels who are the trustees of God over His revelation and His ambassadors to His messengers, they do not disobey God in what He commands them and they do what they are commanded, then he mentioned what means: that the mind allows that to happen from them, but the occurrence of this permissible thing is not known except by hearing and it is not authentic. And I say that this is just a rejection. The Noble Book has been mentioned in this place as you see, and there is no reason to take it out of its apparent meaning with these efforts, and what he mentioned that the principles reject that, then assuming the existence of these principles, they are specific to what happened in this story and there is no reason to prevent specification, and Iblis had the great status and became the most evil of creation and the most disbelieving of the worlds. Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: We are only a trial, he said: A calamity. Al-Bazzar narrated with a sound chain of transmission and Al-Hakim and authenticated it from Ibn Masoud who said: Whoever goes to a soothsayer or magician and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad. Al-Bazzar narrated on the authority of Imran bin Husain who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever practices omens or has omens practiced for him, or practices divination or has divination practiced for him, or practices magic or has magic practiced for him, or ties a knot, or goes to a soothsayer and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad.” Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Safwan bin Salim who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever learns a little or a lot of magic, his last covenant with God will be that of his. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: From a creation, he said: A foundation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: From a creation, from a share. Ibn Jarir narrated likewise on the authority of Mujahid. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Hasan: He will have no share in the Hereafter, he said: He has no religion. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: And evil is that for which they exchange, he said: They sold. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: For a reward, he said: A reward.
2:104: His saying: 104- "Ra'ana" means watch over us and preserve us. The form of the verb "mufa'ala indicates the meaning of ra'ana", watch over us and we will watch you, and preserve us and we will preserve you, and watch over us and we will watch over you. It is possible that it is from "ara'ana sama'ak" meaning, free it for our speech. The reason for the prohibition of that is that this word was an insult in the language of the Jews. It was said that in their language it means "listen not you heard", and it was said: something else. So when they heard the Muslims saying to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "ra'ana" asking him to take care of them, they seized the opportunity. They were saying the same to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, showing that they wanted the Arabic meaning, but implicitly meaning that they intended the insult, which is the meaning of this word in their language. In that is evidence that words that are likely to lead to insult and belittlement should be avoided, even if the speaker does not intend that meaning that is useful for cursing, in order to block the pretext, prevent the means, and cut off the source of corruption and its approach. Then God commanded them to They address the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a way that does not allow for deficiency or insinuation, so he said: And say, ‘Look at us,’ meaning, come to us and look at us. This is a case of deletion and connection, as the poet said: The phenomena of beauty and goodness are seen as the arak gazelles are seen. That is, to the arak tree. It was said: Its meaning is, Wait for us and be patient with us. From this comes the poet’s saying: If you give me an hour, it will benefit me with Umm Jundub. Al-A’mash read: Anzurni with the hamza cut off and the dhad broken, meaning give us time and give us respite until we understand from you. From this is the poet’s saying: Abu Hind, do not rush us and wait for us to tell you for sure. Al-Hasan read: "Ra'ina" with the tanween, and he said: "Ra'in" is a mocking statement. And after this prohibition and command, He ordered them with another command, which is His saying: "And listen", meaning listen to what you have been ordered and forbidden to do, and its meaning is: Obey God in not addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with that wording and address him with what you have been ordered to do, and it is possible that its meaning is: Listen to what the Messenger addresses you with from the Sharia until you obtain what you want without asking for consideration, then He threatened the Jews with His saying: "And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment" and it is possible that it is a comprehensive threat for all types of disbelievers. Ibn Jarir said: The correct statement in our view on that is that God forbade the believers from saying to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Ra'ina" because it is a word that God hates for them to say to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to what was mentioned about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "Do not say to the grapes the vineyard, but say the rope, and do not say my servant, but say my boy" and the like.
2:105: And His saying: 105- "The disbelievers among the People of the Scripture do not wish" the verse, in it is a statement of the intensity of the disbelievers' enmity towards the Muslims, as they do not wish for good to be sent down upon them from God, the Most High, then God, the Most High, responded to that by saying: "And God chooses for His mercy whom He wills" the verse. And His saying: "To send down is in the accusative case as a direct object, and min" in His saying: "of good is redundant, as stated by An-Nahhas, and in Al-Kashshaf it is stated that min" in His saying: "of the People of the Scripture" is explanatory, and in His saying: "of good" is redundant to include good, and in His saying: "from your Lord" is to begin the goal, and it has been said that good is revelation, and other things have been said, and it appears that they do not wish for any good to be sent down upon the Muslims, as it is not specific to a specific type, as is indicated by the occurrence of this idea in the context of negation and the confirmation of generality by the addition of "min" to it, even if some types of good are greater than others, this does not necessitate specialization. Mercy, it was said, is the Qur’an, and it was said: prophecy, and it was said: the type of mercy without specifying it, as is indicated by the addition to His Almighty pronoun: And God is the possessor of great bounty, meaning the possessor of great bounty, so how can you not wish that He would single out for His mercy whomever He wills of His servants? Saeed bin Mansour narrated in his Sunan, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilya, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu`ab on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that a man came to him and said: Give me a testament. He said: When you hear God say: O you who believe, then listen to it, for it is either good that He commands or evil that He forbids. Abu Nu`aym narrated in Ad-Dala`il on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Ra`ina in the language of the Jews means ugly cursing. The Jews used to say that to the Messenger of God in secret, but when they heard his companions saying that, they made it public. They used to say that and laugh among themselves, so God revealed the verse. Abu Nu`aym narrated in Ad-Dala`il on his authority that the believers said after this verse: Whoever you hear saying it, strike his neck. So the Jews stopped after that. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: There were two Jewish men, Malik bin Al-Saif and Rifa’ah bin Zaid, whenever they met the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would say to him while they were speaking to him: Listen to us and listen to someone who is not being listened to. The Muslims thought that this was something that the People of the Book used to do to glorify their prophets, so they said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then God revealed the verse. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Sakhr who said: Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away, whoever among the believers had an argument would call out to him and say: Listen to us. God glorified His Messenger so much that this should be said to him, and He commanded them to say: Give us time, so that they would honor and respect the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Abu Nu’aym narrated on the authority of Qatadah that the Jews used to say this in mockery, so God disliked for the believers to say as they said. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Mercy is the Qur’an and Islam.
2:106: Abrogation in the speech of the Arabs has two aspects: One is transfer, such as transferring one book from another, and based on this the entire Qur’an is abrogated: I mean from the Preserved Tablet, so this meaning has no place in this verse, and from it Indeed, We were transcribing what you used to do meaning We would order its abrogation. The second aspect is nullification and removal, which is what is meant here. This second aspect is divided into two sections according to the linguists: One is nullifying something and its disappearance and establishing another in its place, and from it the sun abrogated the shadow if it removed it and took its place, and this is the meaning of His statement: 106- We do not abrogate a verse and in Sahih Muslim There was never a prophecy except that it was abrogated meaning it changed from one state to another. The second is removing something without another taking its place, as they say: the wind abrogated the trace, and from this meaning God abrogates what Satan casts meaning He removes it. It was narrated from Abu Ubaid that this used to happen during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so a surah would be revealed to him and then it would be removed and not recited or written. And from it is what was narrated on the authority of Abu and Aisha that the secret of the parties was equal to Surat Al-Baqarah in length. Ibn Faris said: Abrogation is the abrogation of the Book, and abrogation is that you remove a matter that was previously acted upon and then abrogate it with another event, like a verse that is revealed with a matter then abrogates with another, and everything that comes after something has abrogated it. It is said: the sun abrogated the shadow, and gray hair abrogated youth, and the transmigration of heirs is that heirs die after heirs, and the origin of inheritance remains, and so is the transmigration of times and centuries. Ibn Jarir said: What we abrogate is what we transfer from the ruling of a verse to another, so we change and alter it, that is, we transform the permissible into the forbidden, the forbidden into the permissible, the permissible into the prohibited, and this only occurs in the case of commands, prohibitions, prohibitions, generalizations, preventions, and permissibility. As for the reports, there is no abrogating or abrogated in them. The origin of abrogation is the abrogation of the Book, which is its transfer from one copy to another. Likewise, the meaning of abrogating a ruling to another is only its transfer to another, regardless of whether its ruling or its script is abrogated, since both of its states are abrogated. The scholars of Usul have made the discussion of abrogation part of the objectives of this art, so we will not prolong its mention, but we will refer whoever wants to seek healing to it. The people of Islam have agreed on its establishment, past and present, and no one has disagreed with that except those whose disagreement is not taken into account and whose words are not given attention. It is well known that the Jews, may God exalt them, denied it, and they are proven by what is in the Torah, that God said to Noah, peace be upon him, when he came out of the ship: I have made every animal food for you and your descendants, and I have released it to you like the plants of grass, except for blood, so do not eat it. Then He forbade Moses and the Children of Israel many animals. It is established in the Torah that Adam used to marry his brother to his sister, and God forbade that to Moses, peace be upon him, and others. It is established in it that Abraham, peace be upon him, was ordered to slaughter his son, then God said to him: Do not slaughter him, and that Moses ordered the Children of Israel to kill those among them who worshipped the calf, then He ordered them to lift the sword from them, and there is much like this in the Torah that is in their hands. And His statement: or We cause it to be forgotten Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read it with the opening of the noon, the seen, and the hamza, and it is the same reading of Omar, Ibn Abbas, Ata, Mujahid, Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Ubayd ibn Umair, Al-Nakha’i, and Ibn Muhaysin. The meaning of this reading is that we postpone it from abrogation, from their saying: I postponed this matter if I delayed it. Ibn Faris said: They say: May God delay your term and May God delay your term. People have been delayed and distanced, and I delayed them means that I delayed them. It was said: Its meaning is that we delay the abrogation of its wording: that is, we leave it in the Mother of the Book so that it does not exist. It was also said: We remove it from you so that it is not read or remembered. The rest read: We forget it with a damma on the nun from al-nisyan which means to leave: that is, we leave it so we do not change it or abrogate it. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: They forgot God, so He forgot them meaning: they abandoned His worship, so He left them in the torment. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this reading. Al-Azhari narrated that its meaning is that we order it to be left. It is said: I made him forget the thing: that is, I ordered him to leave it, and I forgot it means I left it. From this is the saying of the poet: I have an obstacle to overcome, I will not forget it nor will it be forgotten Nor do I command to abandon it. Al-Zajjaj said: The reading with the damma on the letter noon does not carry the meaning of abandonment. It is not said: Ansa means left. He said: What Ali bin Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas: Or we forget it means we leave it and do not change it, so it is not correct. What most linguists and scholars agree on is that the meaning of Or we forget it is we barked at you to abandon it from nasa if you leave it and then it is transitive. The meaning of: We brought something better than it or similar to it is we brought what is more beneficial to people than it in this life and the hereafter, or in one of them, or what is similar to it without any increase. This refers to the application of reasoning regarding the abrogated and the abrogating, for the abrogating may be lighter and thus be more beneficial to them in this life, or it may be heavier and its reward is greater and thus be more beneficial to them in the hereafter, or they may be equal and thus similarity is achieved.
2:107: And His statement: 107- Do you not know that God has power over all things? indicates that abrogation is within His capabilities, and that denying it is a denial of the divine power. Likewise, His statement: Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? That is, He has control over the heavens and the earth by creating and inventing and by influencing all of His creations. He is most knowledgeable about the interests of His servants and what is beneficial to them from His rulings that He has made them worship Him with and has made lawful for them. This may differ according to the circumstances, crises, and people, and this is the doing of those who have no guardian. This may differ according to the circumstances, times, and people, and this is the doing of those who have no guardian other than Him and no supporter other than Him. So they must receive it with acceptance, compliance, reverence, and veneration. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim in Al-Kuna, Ibn Adi and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The revelation would come down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at night and he would forget it during the day. So God revealed: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring [one] better than it or similar to it. In its chain of transmission is Al-Hajjaj Al-Jazari, who can be consulted. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “Two men from the Ansar recited a surah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had taught them, and they used to recite it. One night they stood up to recite it and prayed, but they could not find a letter of it. So they went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the morning, and he said: It is one of those things that were abrogated or forgotten, so forget about it.” In its chain of transmission is Sulayman ibn Al-Arqam, who is weak. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, he said: What We change or leave, we do not change, We bring [one] better than it or similar to it, he said: It is better for you in terms of benefit and easier for you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: We cause it to be forgotten means we delay it. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding his statement: Whatever verse We abrogate, he said: We confirm its script and change its ruling. Or cause it to be forgotten, he said: We delay it. Abd bin Hamid and Abu Dawud in his Naskh and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And bring forth one better than it or similar to it, he says: It contains leniency, it contains a concession, it contains a command, it contains a prohibition. Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif, and Abu Dharr al-Harawi in his Fada’il narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf: “A man had a surah with him, so he got up at night and recited it but was not able to do it. Another got up and recited it but was not able to do it. Another got up and was not able to do it. They came in the morning and came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and gathered with him and informed him, so he said: It was abrogated last night.” Something similar was narrated on his authority from another chain of transmission. It has been proven in Bukhari and others on the authority of Anas that God revealed about those who were killed in the Well of Ma’unah Inform our people that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and He is pleased with us then it was abrogated. It has also been proven in Muslim and others on the authority of Abu Musa who said: We used to recite a surah that was similar in length and severity to Bara’ah, but I forgot it, except that I memorized from it If the son of Adam had two valleys full of wealth, he would seek a third valley, and nothing would fill his belly except dust. We used to recite a surah that was similar to one of the tasbihs, the beginning of which was: Glorify God, whatever is in the heavens, but we forgot it, except that I memorized from it: O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? So it would be written as a testimony around your necks and you would be asked about it on the Day of Resurrection. Something similar to this has been narrated through a group of the Companions, including the verse of stoning as narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, and Ibn Hibban on the authority of Umar.
2:108: 108- Umm is the disconnected particle that means rather, meaning rather you want, and in this there is rebuke and reprimand, and the kaf in his saying: as he was asked is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source: meaning a question that is similar to what Moses was asked before when they asked him to show them God openly, and they asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come to God and the angels face to face.
