And his saying: Equally is the middle of everything, Abu Ubaidah said, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: In the midst of Hell and from it is the saying of Hassan mourning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Woe to the companions of the Prophet and his family after sunset in the midst of the atheists Al-Farra’ said: “Al-Sawa’ is the intention: meaning he went astray from the intended path and his reputation: meaning the path of obedience to God.”
2:109: And the Almighty's saying: 109- And many of the People of the Scripture wish informs the Muslims of the Jews' eagerness to tempt them and turn them away from Islam and cast doubt on their religion. And His saying: If only they could turn you back is in the accusative case as the object of the mentioned verb. And His saying: From themselves may be related to His saying wish meaning they wished that from themselves, and it may be related to His saying: Out of envy meaning envy arising from themselves, and it is the reason for His saying: wish. Pardon: is to leave off being held accountable for a sin. And forgiveness: is to remove its effect from the soul. I forgave someone: if I turned away from his sin, and I turned away from him: if I turned away from him, and in it is encouragement to do that and guidance towards it - and that was abrogated by the command to fight, said Abu Ubaidah. His saying: Until God brings about His command is the ultimate command of God Almighty regarding forgiveness and pardon: that is, do that until the command comes to you from God Almighty regarding their matter, as He chooses and desires, and as He has decreed in His previous work, which is to kill whoever of them was killed, to exile whoever was killed for my sake, to impose the jizya on whoever was imposed it, and to convert whoever converted to Islam.
2:110: And His saying: 110- And establish prayer is an urging from God Almighty to them to occupy themselves with what benefits them and brings them benefit, such as establishing prayer and paying zakat. And providing good for which they will be rewarded so that God may empower them and grant them victory over those who oppose them. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Rafi’ ibn Huraymila and Wahb ibn Zayd said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, bring us a book that can be sent down to us from the sky so that we can read it, or cause rivers to gush forth for us so that we may follow you and believe you. So God revealed concerning that: Or do you want to ask your Messenger - to His saying - the right way. Huyayy ibn Akhtab was one of the Jews who was most envious of the Arabs because God and His Messenger had singled them out. They were striving to turn people away from Islam as much as they could, so God revealed concerning them: Many of the People of the Scripture wish al-Baqarah 2:17. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi that he said: The Arabs asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to bring them God so that they could see Him openly, so this verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah who said: A man said: If our expiation were the expiations of the Children of Israel, then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “What God has given you is better. When one of the Children of Israel committed a sin, he would find it written on his door and its expiation. If he expiated it, he would have disgrace in this world, and if he did not expiate it, he would have disgrace in the Hereafter. God has given you better than that. He said: “And whoever does evil or wrongs himself” (al-Baqarah 2:17), and the five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday are expiations for what is between them.” Then God revealed: Or do you want to ask your Messenger? (al-Baqarah 2:17). Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The Quraysh asked Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to make Safa into gold for them, so he said: Yes, and it is for you like the table for the Children of Israel if you disbelieve. But they refused and returned, so God revealed: Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? that he would show them God openly. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding his statement: And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief, he said: He exchanges hardship for ease. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: He has certainly strayed from the right path, he said: He has deviated from the path. Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ka’b ibn Malik who said: The Jews and polytheists of Medina used to harm the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions severely, so God commanded us to be patient with that and to forgive them. God revealed, Many of the People of the Scripture wish al-Bukhari and Muslim and in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions used to forgive the polytheists and the People of the Scripture as God commanded them and they used to be patient with the harm. God the Most High said, And you will surely hear much abuse from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God. And He said, Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back al-Dala’il. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to interpret the forgiveness as God commanded him to do until God permitted killing them, and God killed those of the leaders of Quraysh who were killed because of it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas regarding His statement, from themselves, he said: from themselves, “after the truth has become clear to them,” meaning that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So pardon and overlook and his statement: And turn away from the polytheists something similar to this regarding pardoning the polytheists. He said: All of that was abrogated by his statement: Fight those who do not believe in God and the verse, and his statement: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: And whatever good you put forward for yourselves meaning of good deeds in this world. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding his statement: You will find it with God he said: You will find its reward.
2:111: His saying: 111- Hud Al-Farra' said: It is possible that Hud means a Jew, or that it is the plural of Ha'id. Al-Akhfash said: The singular pronoun in kana is he in consideration of the word min, and the plural in his saying: Hud is in consideration of the meaning of min. It was said: There is an omission in this statement, and its original form is: And the Jews said: No one will enter Paradise except he who is Jewish, and the Christians said: No one will enter Paradise except he who is Christian. This is what many of the commentators said, and some of the predecessors preceded them in that. The apparent structure of the Qur’an is that this statement was made by the two sects of the Jews and Christians and that they are unique in this regard, and the reason for this statement is that there is an omission in the speech of what is known, that each sect of these two sects misleads the other and denies that they have anything of religion, let alone entering Paradise, as in this place, for God has narrated about the Jews that they said: The Christians are not on anything, and they said: The Christians are not on anything, and the Jews are not on anything. The interpretation of the wishes has been given above, and the reference in His saying that is to what preceded them from the wishes, the last of which is that none will enter Paradise except them. It was said: The reference is to this last wish, and the estimation is similar to that wish, their wishes, with the omission of the complement to match their wishes. His saying: Bring is originally Bring and the damma was omitted due to its heaviness, then the ya was omitted due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. It is said for the singular masculine Haat and for the feminine Haati, and it is a sound meaning bring. The proof is the evidence by which certainty is achieved. Ibn Jarir said: Seeking evidence here requires proving the theory and responding to those who deny it. And his saying: If you are truthful means in those abstract hopes and false claims.
2:112: Then he responded to them and said: 112- Yes, whoever submits and this is an affirmation of what they denied about others entering Paradise: that is, it is not as they say, but whoever submits to God will enter it. The meaning of submitting is surrendering, and it was said: sincere. The face was mentioned specifically because it is the most honorable thing that can be seen of a person and because it is the location of the apparent senses, and in it honor and humiliation appear. It was said: The Arabs describe the face as a whole, and that the meaning here is the face and other things. It was said: What is meant by the face here is the purpose: that is, whoever sincerely intends it. His saying: And he is a doer of good is in the accusative case as a state, and the pronoun in his saying: His face is and for him in consideration of the word from, and in his saying: upon them in consideration of its meaning. And his saying: from if it is the relative, then it is the subject of an omitted verb, that is, yes, whoever submits will enter it. His saying: For him is connected to whoever converts to Islam, even if it is a conditional clause. His saying: For him is the reward, and the combination of the condition and the reward is a response to the People of the Book and a nullification of that claim.
2:113: And his saying: 113- And the Jews said and what follows it, that each group denies goodness from the other, and this includes affirming it for itself, in defiance of the mercy of God, the Most High. He said in Al-Kashaf: The thing is that which is correct and taken into account. He said: This is a great exaggeration because the impossible and the non-existent are called things, and if the name of things is denied to it, then it has been exaggerated in leaving it to what is not after it, and thus their saying less than nothing. And his saying: And they recite the Book means the Torah and the Gospel, and the sentence is a circumstantial, and it was said: What is meant is the type of Book, and in this is the greatest rebuke and the most severe rebuke, because falling into false claims and speaking about what there is no proof for is, even if it is ugly in general, but from the people of knowledge and study of the Books of God, it is even more ugly, more heinous in crime, and more serious in sin. And His statement: Thus said those who do not know, what is meant by them are the Arab infidels who have no book and who said something similar to what the Jews said, following their example because they are ignorant and are not able to do anything other than imitate those whom they believe are people of knowledge. It was said: What is meant by them is a group of Jews and Christians who are those who do not have knowledge. Then the Almighty informed us that He is the One who will settle this dispute in which there is disagreement when we refer to Him, so He will punish those who deserve to be punished and save those who deserve to be saved. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding his statement: And they say, ‘None shall enter Paradise’ 1:13, he said: The Jews said: None shall enter Paradise except the Jewish, and the Christians said: None shall enter Paradise except the Christian. These are their wishful thinking, he said: Wishful thinking that they wish for from God without right. Say, ‘Produce your proof,’ he said: Your argument, if you are truthful, in what you say, that it is as you say. Yes, whoever submits his face to God, he said: is sincere to God. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Say, ‘Produce your proof,’ he said: Your argument. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: Yes, whoever submits his face, he said: is sincere in his religion. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the Christian delegation from Najran came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the Jewish rabbis came to them and they argued before the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Rafi’ ibn Huraymila said: You are on nothing and disbelieved in Jesus and the Gospel. A man from Najran said to him: You are on nothing and denied the prophethood of Moses and disbelieved in the Torah. God revealed concerning that: And the Jews say, ‘The Christians are not on anything.’ And the Christians say, ‘The Jews are not on anything.’ And they recite the Scripture. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: I said to Ata’: Who are these who do not believe? He said: They are nations that existed before the Jews and Christians. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: They are the Arabs who said: Muhammad is not on anything.
2:114: This question is the most eloquent indication that this injustice is infinite and that it is of a status that no other types of injustice should befall it: i.e. no one is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God. The interrogative noun is in the nominative case as a subject and more unjust is its predicate. And His statement: 114- that His name be mentioned therein It was said: It is a substitute for mosques - and it was said: It is a direct object with the estimation of the dislike of it being mentioned, and it was said: The estimation is from it being mentioned, then the preposition was deleted due to the length of the speech, and it was said: It is a second direct object for His statement: prevented and what is meant by preventing the mosques from mentioning the name of God is preventing those who come to them for prayer, recitation, remembrance and teaching it. What is meant by striving to destroy it is striving to demolish it and raise its structure. It is possible that what is meant by destruction is to prevent it from performing the acts of worship for which it was established, and so it is more general than his saying: that His name be mentioned therein, so it includes all that is forbidden from the matters for which mosques were built, such as learning and teaching knowledge, sitting for seclusion, and waiting for prayer. It is possible that what is more general than the two matters is meant by the generality of the metaphor, as was said in the saying of God Almighty: The mosques of God are only to be maintained and His saying: It is not for them to enter them except in fear, meaning: it is not appropriate for them to enter them except in a state of fear. In it is guidance for the servants of God Almighty that they should prevent the disbelievers from entering the mosques of God, without differentiating between one mosque and another, and between one disbeliever and another, as is indicated by the generality of the wording, and the specificity of the reason does not contradict it, and that they should put them in a state where if they wanted to enter, they would be in a state of fear and apprehension lest one of the Muslims should notice them and bring upon them what would necessitate humiliation and degradation. It does not include permission for us to enable them to do that in a state of Their fear, but rather it is a metaphor for preventing them from entering our mosques. And shame: it was said: it is imposing the jizya on them and humiliating them, and it was said, something else, and its explanation was presented above.
2:115: And the East: is the place of sunrise. And the West: is the place of sunset, meaning they are the kingdom of God and what is between them of directions and creatures, so it includes the whole earth. His statement: 115- So wherever you turn meaning whatever direction you face, there is the Face of God: meaning the place that He is pleased for you to face, and that occurs when the direction of the Qiblah that we were commanded to face is unclear, as He, the Most High, said: "So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it." It was said in al-Kashshaf: The meaning is that if you are prevented from praying in al-Masjid al-Haram: meaning in Jerusalem, then the earth has been made a mosque for you, so pray in any spot you wish from its spots, and do the turning there, because turning is possible in every place, its places are not specific to one mosque over another mosque or to one place over another. End. This specification has no basis, because the wording is broader than it. If what is meant by it is to explain the reason, then there is no problem. And His statement: Indeed, God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing is a guide to the breadth of His mercy. And that He is generous to His servants in their religion and does not burden them with what is beyond their capacity. It was said: Vast in the sense that His knowledge encompasses everything, as He said: His knowledge encompasses everything. Al-Farra’ said: The Vast is the Generous One whose giving encompasses everything. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Quraysh prevented the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from praying at the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque, so God revealed: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God? Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that they are the Christians. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi that they are the Romans who supported Nebuchadnezzar in destroying the Holy House. Concerning His statement: It is not for them to enter it except in fear, he said: There is no Roman on earth who enters it today except in fear that his neck will be struck, and he was frightened by paying the jizyah, so he pays it. Concerning His statement: For them is disgrace in this world, he said: As for their disgrace in this world, when the Mahdi rises and Constantinople is conquered, he will kill them, and that is the disgrace. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah that they are the Romans. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam that he said: They are the polytheists when they prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the House on the day of Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Abu Salih who said: The polytheists are not to enter the mosque except in fear. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: For them in this world is disgrace, he said: They pay the jizyah willingly while they are humiliated. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The first thing that was abrogated from the Qur’an, as we have been told - and God knows best - was the matter of the qiblah. God the Most High said: To God belong the east and the west (al-Baqarah 2:14). So the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) faced and prayed towards Jerusalem and left the Ancient House. Then God turned him towards the Ancient House and abrogated it, saying: And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and others narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar that he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pray voluntarily on his mount, wherever it faced. Then Ibn ‘Umar recited this verse: Wherever you turn, there is the Face of God and said: This is why this verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir, al-Daraqutni and al-Hakim narrated something similar on his authority, and he authenticated it. It is proven in Saheeh al-Bukhari from the hadeeth of Jabir from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he used to pray on his mount facing the east. When he wanted to pray the obligatory prayer, he would dismount, face the qiblah and pray. A similar hadeeth was narrated on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Dawud. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi who declared it weak, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir and others narrated on the authority of Amir bin Rabi’ah who said: We were with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on a dark, black night. We stopped at a place and a man began to take stones and make a place of prayer and pray in it. When morning came, we found that we had prayed in a direction other than the qiblah. We said: O Messenger of God, we have prayed this night in a direction other than the qiblah. Then God revealed the verse, To God belong the east and the west. He said: Your prayer has passed. Ad-Daraqutni, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Jabir with a similar chain of transmission, except that he mentioned that they drew lines. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a similar chain of transmission. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated something similar on the authority of Ata’ with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), but it is mursal. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then there is the face of God meaning: The qiblah of God wherever you face, east or west. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: Whatever is between the east and the west is the qiblah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Darqutni, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Umar.
2:116: His saying: 116- And they said they are the Jews and Christians - and it was said the Jews: that is they said: Ezra is the son of God and it was said the Christians: that is they said: The Messiah is the son of God and it was said: they are the infidel Arabs: that is they said: the angels are daughters of God. And His saying: Glory be to Him has been explained previously, and what is meant here is God Almighty's disavowal of what they attributed to Him of taking a son. And His saying: Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth is a response to those who say that He took a son: that is, rather, He is the owner of whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and these speakers are included under His kingdom, and the son is of their kind and not of His kind, and the son is only of the kind of the father. And the obedient: the submissive: that is, everyone in the heavens and the earth is obedient to Him, submissive to His greatness, humbled before His majesty, and the qunut in the original language means standing. Al-Zajjaj said: “The creation is obedient, meaning they stand in worship, either by acknowledgment or by the opposite, so the effect of the creation is clear to them. It was said: Its origin is obedience, and from it is “and the obedient men and women.” It was also said: stillness, and from it is His statement: And stand before God, obedient. For this reason Zaid bin Arqam said: We used to talk during prayer until And stand before God, obedient, was revealed, so we were commanded to be silent and forbidden from speaking. It was said: Qunut is prayer, and from it is the saying of the poet: Obedient to God, reciting His Books and deliberately separating himself from people The first is that Qunut is a word that has many meanings. It has been said that there are thirteen meanings, and they are clear. Some scholars have organized them, as I explained in my explanation of Al-Muntaqa.
2:117: And Badi': Fa'il for exaggeration and it is the predicate of a subject, omitted: that is, He is the Creator of His heavens and earth. He created something: He created it without an example, and whoever creates something that has not been done before is called a creator. And His statement: 117- And when He decrees a matter means He perfects it and perfects it. Al-Azhari said: In the language, Qada has many aspects that refer to the cessation of something and its completion. It was said: It is shared between meanings. It is said: Qada means created, and from it: So He decreed them as seven heavens and in the sense of He informed, and from it: And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book and in the sense of command, and from it: And your Lord decreed that you worship none but Him and in the sense of He obliged, and from it: The judge decreed upon him, and in the sense of He fulfilled it, and from it: So when Moses fulfilled the term and in the sense of He intended, and from it: So when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, Be, and it is. And the matter is one of the matters. It has been mentioned in the Qur’an in fourteen meanings: The first is religion, including: until the truth came and the command of God appeared. The second is the meaning of speech, including: So when Our command comes. The third is punishment, including: When the matter is decided. The fourth is Jesus, including: So when He decides a matter. That is, Jesus, peace be upon him, came into existence. The fifth is killing, including: So when the command of God comes. The sixth is the conquest of Mecca, including: Then wait until God brings about His command. The seventh is the killing of Banu Qurayzah and the expulsion of Nadir, including: So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command. The eighth is the Resurrection, including: The command of God came. The ninth is judgment, including: He manages the matter. The tenth is revelation, including: The command descends between them. The eleventh is the command of creation, including: Unquestionably, to God do all matters return. The twelfth is victory, including: Do we have any part in the matter? The thirteenth: sin, and from it: So she tasted the evil consequences of her deed. The fourteenth: affair, and from it: And Pharaoh’s command was not right. This is how some of the commentators have mentioned these meanings with principles from this, and there is not much benefit in that, and its application to different matters is because the name of command is true for them. And His saying: Then He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. The apparent meaning in this is the true meaning, and that He, the Most High, says this wording, and there is nothing in that to prevent it, nor did anything come that necessitates its interpretation. And from it is His saying, the Most High: His command, when He intends a thing, is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. And He, the Most High, said: Our command to a thing when We intend it is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. And He said: And Our command is only one, like the twinkling of an eye. And from it is the saying of the poet: If God wants something, He just says to it, Be, and it is. It has been said: This is a metaphor, and that it is not a statement, but rather a judgment that he makes, so he expressed it with a statement, and from this is the statement of the poet, who is Omar bin Hammah Al-Dawsi: So I became like an eagle whose young ones fly away when they want to fly. It is said that they have fallen. Another said: His wings said to his legs, Go ahead and escape, for your judgment is to tear them apart.
2:118: What is meant by His statement: 118- And those who do not know said is the Jews, and it was said: the Christians, and Ibn Jarir preferred it because they are the ones mentioned in the verse, and it was said: the polytheists of the Arabs, and if only is a particle of incitement: that is, why does not God speak to us about the prophethood of Muhammad so that we know that he is a prophet or bring us that as a sign of his prophethood. What is meant by His statement: those before them said is said: they are the Jews and Christians according to the opinion of those who made those who do not know the infidels of the Arabs, or the previous nations according to the opinion of those who made those who do not know the Jews and Christians, or the Jews according to the opinion of those who made those who do not know the Christians: they resembled that is in their obstinacy and suggestion, and Al-Farra' said: they resembled in their agreement on disbelief. We have made clear the verses for a people who are certain. That is, they acknowledge the truth, are fair in their speech, and submit to the commands of God Almighty because they believe in Him, believe in His verses, and follow what He has prescribed for them. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Ibn Abbas from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God Almighty said: “The son of Adam has lied to Me and reviled Me. As for his lying to Me, he claims that I am not able to restore him to the way he was. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying: ‘I have a son, so glory be to Me that I should take a wife or a son.’” He also narrated something similar from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and there are hadiths on this topic. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Glory be to God, he said: God is free from evil. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat from Musa ibn Talhah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was asked about glorifying God, that a person should say: Glory be to God. He said: God is free from evil. Al-Hakim narrated it and Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi authenticated it on the authority of Talha bin Yahya bin Talha on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather Talha bin Ubaidullah who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the interpretation of Subhan God, and he said: It is the purification of God from all evil. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on his authority through another chain of transmission with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Abu Nu’aym in Al-Hilyah, and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Every letter in the Qur’an in which qunut is mentioned is obedience. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: All are devoutly obedient to Him, he said: Obedient. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding the statement: Originator of the heavens and the earth, he said: He originated their creation and no one shared with Him in their creation. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Rafi’ ibn Huraymila said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, if you are a messenger from God as you say, then say to God, Let Him speak to us so that we may hear His words. So God revealed concerning that: And those who do not know say, the verse. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah that they are the infidel Arabs. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: They are the Christians and those before them the Jews.
2:119: His statement: 119- A bearer of good tidings and a warner may be in the accusative case as a state, or it may be an object for it: meaning We sent you for the purpose of giving good tidings and warning. And his statement: And do not ask was read by the majority in the nominative case in the passive voice: meaning in the case of you not being asked, and it was read in the nominative case in the active voice. Al-Akhfash said: And it is in the place of the state in apposition to a bearer of good tidings and a warner meaning in the case of you not asking about them, because God's knowledge of their disbelief after warning them makes it unnecessary for Him to ask about them, and Nafi' read: And do not ask in the accusative case: meaning do not ask about these people or do not ask about those of them who died in their disbelief and disobedience, magnifying their situation and making their status more severe: meaning that this is a terrible matter and a hideous incident, which the speaker would be too great to say or the listener would be too great to hear.
2:120: His saying: 120- And the Jews will never be pleased with you the verse: meaning their aim and the extent of their satisfaction is not what they suggest to you of signs and what they present of obstinacy, for if you came to them with everything they suggest and answered them about every obstinacy, they would not be pleased with you. Then he informed him that they would not be pleased with him until he entered their religion and followed their way. And the way is: the name of what God has legislated for His servants in His books on the tongues of His prophets and thus the law, then He responded to them, the Most High, and ordered him to say to them: Indeed, the guidance of God is the true guidance, not what you are upon of the abrogated law and distorted books. Then He followed that with a severe threat to the Messenger of God if he followed their desires and tried to please them and exhausted himself in seeking what agrees with them, and it is possible that it was an exposition to his nation and a warning to them not to fall into any of that, or enter into the desires of the people of religions and seek the pleasure of the people of innovations. This verse contains a severe warning that makes hearts tremble and souls crack, which requires the people of knowledge who carry the proofs of God, the Most High, and who are responsible for explaining His laws to leave the anointing of the people who follow evil doctrines, who abandon working according to the Book and the Sunnah, and prefer mere opinion over them. For most of these people, even if they appear to be accepting and show leniency in their morals, are not satisfied with anything except following their innovations, entering into their traps, and falling into their deceptions. If the scholar does that after God has taught him knowledge that benefits him, that God’s guidance is what is in His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, not what they are upon of those innovations that are pure misguidance, clear ignorance, a collapsing opinion, and imitation on the brink of a collapsing precipice, then he will have no guardian or supporter from God, and whoever is like that will inevitably be let down and will perish without a doubt or suspicion.
2:121: And His statement: 121- Those to whom We gave the Scripture It was said: They are the Muslims and the Scripture is the Qur'an, and it was said: Those who submitted from the People of the Scripture, and what is meant by His statement: They recite it is that they know what is in it, so they make lawful what is lawful and forbid what is forbidden, so whoever recites it recites it if he follows it, and from this is His statement, the Most High: And the moon when it recites it meaning follows it, as it was said, and it is possible that it is from recitation: meaning they read it as it should be read, they do not distort it or change it. And His statement: Those to whom We gave the Scripture is a subject and its predicate is They recite it or the predicate is His statement: Those with what comes after it. Abdul Razzaq, Abdul bin Humaid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I wish I knew what happened to my parents. Then the verse was revealed: “Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire.” He did not mention it until God took him. Al-Suyuti said: This is a mursal with a weak chain of transmission. Then he narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jarir on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Asim, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: It is a weak chain of transmission that cannot be used as evidence, nor can it be used as evidence with the previous one. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik who said: Hellfire is the great part of Hellfire. Al-Tha’labi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Jews of Medina and the Christians of Najran preferred that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, pray towards their Qiblah, but when God changed the Qiblah towards the Ka’bah, this was difficult for them and they despaired of him agreeing with them in their religion. Then God revealed: And never will the Jews or the Christians approve of you Al-Madinah 10:13. Abdul Razzaq narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Those to whom We gave the Scripture, he said: They are the Jews and Christians. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: They recite it with its true recitation, he said: They make lawful what it makes lawful and forbid what it forbids and they do not distort it from its proper places. They also narrated on his authority that he said: They follow it with its true recitation, then they recited: And the moon when it follows it, meaning: It follows it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said regarding his statement: They recite it with its true recitation, if he is reminded of Paradise, he asks God for Paradise, and if he passes by mentioning Hell, he seeks refuge in God from Hell. Al-Khatib narrated in his book al-Rawaat with a chain of transmission that includes unknown narrators on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding his statement: They recite it with its true recitation, he said: They follow it with its true recitation. Al-Qurtubi said the same in his interpretation that there are unknown narrators in its chain of transmission, but he said: But its meaning is correct. Abdul Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Masoud in his interpretation of this verse, similar to what was previously narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his statement: They make lawful what is lawful to Him until the end. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, who said: They speak it as it was revealed and do not conceal it. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding this verse, who said: They are the companions of Muhammad. Then he narrated something similar to that on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab. Wakee’ and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: They recite it with its true recitation, who said: They know its clear verses, believe in its ambiguous verses, and leave whatever is unclear to its Knower.
2:122: His statement: 122- O Children of Israel to His statement: Nor will they be aided. Something similar to this has been mentioned previously at the beginning of the surah, and its interpretation has already been presented. The reason for the repetition is the urging to follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet. Ibn Kathir mentioned its meaning in his interpretation. Al-Baqa'i said in his interpretation: Since the time has gone on in thoroughly reminding them of the blessings, then in explaining their faults and exposing their veils, and concluding that with intimidation for wasting their religion through their actions, conditions and words, he repeated what he began their story with, reminding them of the blessings, and warning against the coming of punishments on the Day when the nations will be gathered, and regret will last for whoever slips, so that he may know that this is the gist of the story, and the purpose in itself is to urge them to seize the opportunity. End. And I say: This is nothing, for if the reason for the repetition was what he mentioned about the length of the period and that he returned to what he began their story with, then it would have been more appropriate to repeat it, and what is more deserving of repeating the mention is the saying of the Most High: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and fulfill My covenant, and I will fulfill your covenant, and fear Me. For this verse, despite being the first speech with them and the address to them in this surah, is also more deserving of being repeated and reiterated because of what it contains of the command to remember the favors and fulfill the covenant and fear God the Most High. And with this you know the correctness of what we presented to you when explaining the law of God the Most High in addressing the Children of Israel in this surah, so refer to it. Then Al-Baqa’i narrated after his previous speech on the authority of Al-Hawali that he said: The Most High repeated it to show the purpose of the coherence of the end of the speech with its beginning, and to take this clarification and instruction as a basis for what can be mentioned similarly in the rest of the Qur’an, so that when the speech reaches the end of its conclusion, the heart must notice that end in itself and recite it so that in its recitation it will be a collection of the two sides of praise, and in its understanding. It is a collection of the meanings of both sides of the meaning. And I say: If this were the reason for the repetition, it would have been more appropriate for us not to have made it known to you. As for his saying: And let this be taken as a basis for what is mentioned of repetition in the rest of the Qur’an, it is known that the occurrence of this matter in the minds and its establishment in the understandings is not limited to the repetition of a specific verse that opens this purpose with it, so the point in repeating these two verses in particular is not complete, and to God belongs the perfect wisdom that the minds cannot reach nor the intellects comprehend, so there is nothing in the assignment of these arbitrary occasions except what we made known to you there, so remember.
2:123: 123- And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be aided.
2:124: His saying: 124- And when He tested Testing: the examination and choice: that is, He tested him with what He commanded him to do, and Ibrahim means in Syriac a merciful father, as Al-Mawardi said. Ibn Atiyah said: And its meaning in Arabic is that. Al-Suhayli said: And agreement often occurs between Syriac and Arabic. The author of Al-Kashshaf mentioned here a question about the pronoun referring back to Ibrahim, even though his rank is later, and he answered it by saying that it had come forward verbally so it referred back to him, and the matter in this is clearer than to be occupied with mentioning it, or for questions to be asked in such a case or for the face of the paper to be blackened by explaining it. His saying: With words the scholars differed in identifying them. It was said: They are the laws of Islam, and it was said: The slaughter of his son, and it was said: The performance of the message, and it was said: They are the characteristics of the fitrah, and it was said: They are His saying: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people, and it was said: With purity as will be explained. Al-Zajjaj said: These statements are not contradictory, because all of this was what Abraham was tested with. The apparent structure of the Qur’an is that the words are His saying: “He said: I will make you” and what follows it, and that is an explanation of the words, and some of the predecessors will come with what agrees with that, and others with what contradicts it. Based on this, His saying: “He said: I will make you” is a new statement as if it were what he said to him. Ibn Jarir said, in summary, that it is possible that the words mean all of that, and it is possible that it is some of that, and it is not possible to be certain that any of them is specifically meant except by a hadith or consensus, and there is no authentic report on that by a single narration or a group narration that must be accepted. Then he said: If someone were to say: What Mujahid, Abu Salih, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said is more correct: meaning that the words are His saying: Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people and His saying: And We enjoined upon Abraham and what follows. Ibn Kathir preferred that they include all of what was mentioned, and the clarification of what is true will come after citing what was reported from the righteous predecessors. And His saying: So he completed them means he performed them in the most perfect manner, and complied in the most perfect manner. The imam is that which is followed, and from this the path is called an imam and the building is called an imam, because it is followed by that: meaning the traveler is guided by it, and since the imam is the role model for the people because they follow him and are guided by his guidance, this word was applied to him. His saying: And from my descendants may be a supplication from Abraham, meaning: And make from my descendants leaders. It may be that this was from Abraham with the intention of asking, even if it was not in its form: Meaning: And from my descendants, what will be, O Lord? So he informed him that among them are disobedient and unjust, and that they are not fit for that and will not carry it out and the covenant of God, the Most High, will not reach them. The descendants are taken from the atom, because God brought forth the creation from the back of Adam when he made them witness against themselves like the atom. It was said: It is taken from God scattered the creation, He scatters them when He created them. And in the Noble Book: So it became chaff, scattered by the winds. It was said in As-Sahih: The wind scattered the clouds and other things, scattering them and scattering them, scattering and scattering: meaning it blew them away. Al-Khalil said: They were called descendants because God, the Most High, scattered them on the earth as a sower scatters the seed. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of the covenant. Some say it is the Imamate, others say it is the Prophethood, others say it is the covenant of God, and others say it is security from the punishment of the Hereafter. Al-Zajjaj preferred it, but the first is more apparent as indicated by the context. A group of scholars have used this verse as evidence that the Imam must be just and act according to the Shariah as stated, because if he deviates from that, he is an oppressor. It is possible to look at what the name of the covenant applies to and what the addition indicates of generality, so that it includes all of that based on the generality of the wording without looking at the reason or the context. It is used as evidence for the condition of being free from the description of oppression in everyone who is related to religious matters. Ibn Jarir chose that this verse, although it is clear in the report that the covenant of God for the Imamate will not be attained by an oppressor, contains information from God to Abraham the Friend that there will be among his descendants those who are oppressors to themselves. End quote. It is clear from you that his words are useless. It is better to say: This report is in the meaning of a command to His servants not to entrust the affairs of the Shariah to an oppressor. We only said: It is in the meaning of a command because His report, the Most High, cannot be broken. And we know that his era of leadership and other things has been overtaken by many oppressors.
2:125: His saying: 125- And when We made the House is the Sacred Kaaba, it was used as a star was used as a place of refuge, and a place of refuge is a source of the verb thaba which means to return, meaning a place of refuge for the pilgrims to return to after they have dispersed from it. From this is the saying of Waraqa ibn Nawfal about the Kaaba: A place where all tribes flock to, where the withered beasts flock to. Al-A'mash read Muthabat and it was said that Muthaba comes from Thawaab meaning they will be rewarded there. Mujahid said: What is meant is that they will not get their fill of it. The poet said: Make the house a place of rest for them, not a place of rest for them to spend their time in. Al-Akhfash said: The letter ha was added because of the large number of people who return to it, so it is like a sign and a genealogist. Others said: It is for the feminine and not for exaggeration. His statement: And we were safe is a place name: meaning a place of safety. A group of scholars have used this as evidence that the punishment is not carried out on whoever seeks refuge in it, and this is supported by the statement of God the Almighty: And whoever enters it shall be safe. It was said: This was abrogated. His statement: And take from the station of Abraham a place of prayer. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read with the opening of the kha’ as a past tense verb: meaning We made the House a place of return for the people and a place of safety and they took it as a place of prayer. The rest read it in the imperative form in apposition to remember mentioned at the beginning of the verses, or to remember which is understood as an agent in His statement: And when. It is permissible for it to be in the sense of say: meaning, And we said, ‘Take.’ The place in the language is the place of standing. An-Nahhas said: It is from qama yaqūm, it is a source and a name for the place, and the place of qama is from aqama, and this is not from the statement of the poet: They have beautiful positions, faces, and clubs that are filled with words and deeds. Because it means people of stations. There are different opinions about specifying the station, the most correct of which is that it is the stone that people know and pray the two rak’ahs of circumambulation at it. It was also said that the station is the entire Hajj. This was narrated from Ata’ and Mujahid. It was also said that it is Arafat and Muzdalifah. This was also narrated from Ata’. Al-Sha’bi said: The entire Haram is the station of Abraham. This was narrated from Mujahid. Abdul Razzaq, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, And when his Lord tested Abraham, he said: God tested him with purification: five for the head and five for the body. For the head: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, inhaling water from the nose, using the siwak, and parting the hair. And for the body: trimming the nails, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, plucking the armpit hair, and washing the place of defecation and urination with water. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar from him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on his authority that he said: No one was tested with this religion and performed it completely except Abraham. He recited this verse and it was said to him: What are the words? He said: The arrows of Islam are thirty arrows: ten in Bara’ah, The repentant, the worshippers to the end of the verse, ten at the beginning of Surah Qad Aflah, A questioner asked, “And those who believe in the Day of Judgment,” the verses, and ten in Surah Al-Ahzab, Indeed, the Muslims to the end of the verse, So he completed them, all of them, so he wrote for him Bara’ah. God Almighty said: And Abraham who fulfilled. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Hakim narrated from him that he said: Among them are the rituals of Hajj. Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said: The words Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people, “And when Abraham raises the foundations,” and the verses are about the rituals, the station that was made for Abraham, the provision that the inhabitants of the House were provided with, and the sending of Muhammad among their descendants. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, he said: He was tested with the verses that follow them. They also narrated from Al-Sha’bi something similar. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The words with which Abraham was tested and he fulfilled them: Separation from his people for the sake of God when he was commanded to leave them, and his argument with Nimrod for the sake of God when he made him stand up to the danger of the matter in which he disagreed with them, and his patience in their throwing him into the fire to burn him for the sake of God, and the migration after that from his homeland and country when he was commanded to leave them, and what he was commanded to do of hospitality and patience with it, and what he was tested with of slaughtering his son, so when all of that had passed, God said to him, His Lord has submitted, and he said, I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: He tested him with the star and He was pleased with him, and He tested him with his son and He was pleased with him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, and he fulfilled them, he said: He performed them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Among the fitrah of Abraham is the siwak. I said: This, even if its chain of transmission to Ata’ is sound, is mursal and cannot be used as evidence. It is not permissible to rely on such a thing in interpreting the words of God, the Most High. Likewise, it is not permissible to rely on such as what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Among the fitrah of Abraham is washing the penis and the knuckles, and such as what Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in his Musannaf on his authority who said: “Six are from the fitrah of Abraham: trimming the moustache, the siwak, parting, trimming the nails, istinja’, and shaving the pubic hair.” He said: Three for the head - and three for the body. It has been proven from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in Sahih and other sources through a group of the Companions that these ten are permissible for this ummah. It has not been authentically reported from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that they were the words with which Abraham was tested. The best that has been narrated from him is what was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi who classed it as hasan on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to trim or remove from his moustache. He said: The friend of the Most Merciful, Abraham, used to do it. It is not hidden from you that the action of Al-Khalil to him does not necessitate that it is one of the words with which he was afflicted. If nothing is authentic from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor has it come to us through a path that establishes proof specifying those words, then all that remains for us is to say: They are what God, the Most High, mentioned in His Book in His saying: He said, ‘I will make you’ to the end of the verses. This would be an explanation of the words or silence and referring knowledge of that to God, the Most High. As for what was narrated from Ibn Abbas and similar companions after them in specifying them, they are firstly the sayings of companions that do not establish proof, let alone the sayings of those after them. Assuming that there is no room for ijtihad in that, and that it has the ruling of elevation, then they differed in specifying them in a way that prevents acting on some of what was narrated from them without the other part. Rather, the narrations differed from one of them, as we mentioned before from Ibn Abbas. So how is it permissible to act on that? And with this you know the weakness of the saying of the one who said: It is resorted to the general and it is said: Those words are all that we mentioned here, because this necessitates interpreting the speech of God as weak and contradictory and that which does not establish proof. And Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “He said: Verily, I will make you a leader for mankind” to be followed in your religion, guidance and Sunnah. “He said: And of my descendants” an imam for other than my descendants. “He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers” that their religion, guidance and Sunnah are to be followed. Al-Faryabi and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: God said to Abraham: Verily, I will make you a leader for mankind. He said: And of my descendants” but he refused to do so, then He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said: This is with God on the Day of Resurrection, His covenant does not include the wrongdoers. As for in this world, they had attained His covenant and inherited from the Muslims through it, fought them and married them. But when the Day of Resurrection came, God limited His covenant and His honor to His friends. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid in the interpretation of the verse that he said: I will not make an unjust leader to be followed. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, saying: It informs him that if there is a tyrant among his descendants, his covenant will not be fulfilled and he should not entrust him with any of his affairs. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: There is no covenant with you for a tyrant in disobedience to God. Wakee’ ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers, he said: There is no obedience except in what is good, with its chain of transmission with Ibn Mardawayh as follows: He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Hamid narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Sa’d al-Asadi narrated to us, Salim ibn Sa’id al-Damaghani narrated to us, Wakee’ narrated to us on the authority of al-A’mash on the authority of Sa’d ibn Ubaydah on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami on the authority of Ali on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it. Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no obedience to any created being in disobedience to God. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said in his interpretation of the verse: “There is no covenant for the oppressor. Even if you make a covenant with him, then break it.” Ibn Kathir said: Something similar was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ata’, Muqatil and Ibn Hibban. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: A place of return for the people and a place of security. He said: They will return to it and then return. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: They will not satisfy their desire for it. They will come to it and then return to their families and then return to it. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And a place of security. He said: Security for the people. Al-Bukhari and others narrated from the hadith of Anas on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: I agreed with my Lord in three matters and my Lord agreed with me in three matters. I said: O Messenger of God, why don’t you take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer? Then the verse was revealed: And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. I also said: O Messenger of God, both the righteous and the wicked enter upon your women, so why don’t you order them to cover themselves? Then the verse of hijab was revealed. The wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered around him in jealousy, so I said to them: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you. Then the verse was revealed likewise. Muslim and others narrated it in an abbreviated form from the hadith of Ibn Umar on his authority. Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Jabir that “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked three times and walked four, until he finished, he went to the Station of Abraham and prayed two rak’ahs behind it, then he recited: ‘And take, [O Muhammad], the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. ’” There are many hadiths about the Station of Abraham, peace be upon him, which are complete in the Ummah and elsewhere. The authentic hadiths indicate that the Station of Abraham is the stone that Abraham used to stand on to build the Kaaba when the wall rose. Ishmael brought it to him so that he could stand on it, as in Bukhari from the hadith of Ibn Abbas. It was the stone that was attached to the wall of the Kaaba. The first to transmit it was ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, as narrated by ‘Abd al-Razzaq, al-Bayhaqi with a sound chain of transmission, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh through different chains of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Jabir describing the Hajj of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the Tawaf, ‘Umar said to him: Is this the Station of Abraham? He said: Yes. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar. His saying: Our covenant means here: We ordered and made obligatory. His saying: That they purified is in the accusative case, removing the preposition: that is, that they purified, as the Kufians said. Sibawayh said: It is with the estimation of that they purified, meaning that they purified, so it has no place in grammar. What is meant by purification, it was said: from idols, and it was said: from plagues and doubts, and it was said: from the infidels, and it was said: from impurities and the circumambulation of the ritually impure and the menstruating woman and every unclean thing. It appears that it is not specific to any of these types, and that everything that is true of the name purification, it includes it either comprehensively or alternatively. The addition in his saying: My house is for honor and respect. Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, the people of Medina, Hisham and Hafs read My house with the opening of the yaa, and the others read it with the closing of it. And the one who circumambulates is the one who circumambulates, and it was said: the stranger who visits Mecca. Al-Aakif: the resident. The root of Ma'kof in the language is: adherence and turning towards something. It was said: it is the neighbor without the resident from its people. What is meant by his saying: Bows and prostrations is the praying ones. He mentioned these two pillars specifically because they are the most honorable pillars of prayer.
2:126: And His saying: 126- And when Abraham said The hadiths will come indicating that Abraham was the one who made Mecca sacred, and the hadiths indicating that God made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and combining these hadiths in this research. And His saying: A secure city means Mecca, and what is meant is: supplication for its people from his descendants and others, like His saying: A life of contentment meaning its owner is content. And His saying: Whoever believes is a substitute for the saying of his al-Nas 114:meaning provide for whoever believes from his family, not for whoever disbelieves. And His saying: And whoever disbelieves, it appears that this is from the words of God Almighty in response to Abraham, where he asked for provision for the believers and not others: that is, and I provide for whoever disbelieves, so I grant him enjoyment of provision for a little while, then I force him to the punishment of the Fire. And it is possible that it is an independent statement explaining the state of whoever disbelieves, and it is like informing about the state of the disbelievers with this conditional sentence: that is, whoever disbelieves, then I grant him enjoyment in this world with what he needs of provision, then I force him after this enjoyment to the punishment of the Fire. So God Almighty informed that the disbelievers will not attain any good except their enjoyment in this world, and they will have nothing after that except what is pure evil, which is the punishment of the Fire. As for the reading of those who read so I grant him enjoyment in the imperative form, and likewise His saying: then I force him in the imperative form, it is based on the fact that this is from the words of Abraham, and that when he finished praying for the believers, he prayed for the disbelievers to enjoy a little while, then he prayed against them that He force them to the punishment of the Fire. The meaning of forced him is that he forced him to do it until he was forced to do it and could not find a way out of it or a way out of it.
2:127: His statement: 127- And when it is raised is a narration of a past situation, evoking its amazing image. The foundations: the basis, said Abu Ubaidah and Al-Farra. Al-Kisa'i said: they are the walls. What is meant by raising them is raising what is built above them, not raising them in themselves, for they did not rise, but since they were connected to the building raised above them, they became as if they were raised by its height, just as it is said the building rose, and it is not said the tops of the building rose or its bottoms. His statement: Our Lord, accept from us is in the place of the state with the estimation of the saying: meaning saying, Our Lord. Abi and Ibn Mas'ud read: And when Abraham raised the foundations of the House and Ishmael and they said: Our Lord, accept from us.
2:128: And His saying: 128- And make us Muslims to You meaning make us steadfast upon it or increase us from it - It was said: What is meant by Islam here is the sum of faith and deeds. And His saying: And from our descendants meaning make from our descendants, and from is for partiality or clarification. Ibn Jarir said: He meant by descendants the Arabs in particular, and so did Al-Sahli. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is weak because his call appeared among the Arabs and others who believed in him. And the nation: the group in this place, and it may be applied to one person, and from it is His saying the Most High: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God and it is applied to religion, and from it is Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion and it is applied to time, and from it is: And remember after a nation. And His saying: And show us our rites is from visual vision. Omar bin Abdul Aziz, Qatadah, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin and others read show us with a silent ra, and from it is the saying of the poet: Show us Abdullah's water jug so that he can fill it with Zamzam water, for the people are thirsty. Rituals is the plural of nasak, and its root in the language is washing. It is said: he washed his garment, meaning he washed it. In Islamic law, it is a name for worship, and what is meant here are the rituals of Hajj. It was also said: the places of slaughter, and it was also said: all the places of worship. And his statement: And accept our repentance, it was said: what is meant by their request for repentance is steadfastness, because they are infallible and have no sin. It was also said: what is meant is accept the repentance of the oppressors among us. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: And We commanded Abraham meaning We ordered him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Purify My House he said: From idols. He also narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Sa’id ibn Jubayr something similar, and they added doubt, false speech and impurity. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: If he is standing, then he is one of those who circumambulate, and if he is sitting, then he is one of those who are praying, then he is one of those who bow and prostrate. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he was asked about those who sleep in the mosque, and he said: They are those who are praying. It has been proven that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I have made Medina sacred, and that which is between its two lava plains, so its game should not be hunted nor its trees cut. Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa’i and others on the authority of Jabir. This meaning has been narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, through a group of the Companions, including Rafi’ ibn Khadij according to Muslim and others, Abu Qatada according to Ahmad, Anas according to the two Sheikhs, Abu Hurairah according to Muslim, Ali ibn Abi Talib according to al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Usamah ibn Zayd according to Ahmad and al-Bukhari, and Aisha according to al-Bukhari. It has been proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and it will remain sacred until the Day of Resurrection. Narrated by al-Bukhari in a mu’allaq form, and by Ibn Majah from the hadith of Safiyyah bint Shaybah. Narrated by al-Bukhari and others from the hadith of Ibn Abbas. Narrated by al-Bukhari and others from the hadith of Ibn Abbas. Narrated by al-Bukhari and the Sunan scholars from the hadith of Abu Hurairah. There are other hadiths on this topic other than what we have mentioned, and there is no contradiction between these hadiths, because when Ibrahim, peace be upon him, informed the people that God had made it sacred and that it had always been a safe sanctuary, it was attributed to him that he made it sacred: that is, he made God’s ruling on it clear to the people. Ibn ‘Atiyyah and Ibn Kathir agreed with this group. Ibn Jarir said: It was forbidden and God did not command creation to worship Him with that until Ibrahim asked Him, so He forbade it and they worshipped Him with that. End quote. Both combinations are good. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta’ifi who said: It reached me that when Ibrahim called for the sanctuary and said: And provide its people with fruits, God moved al-Ta’ifi from Palestine. Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Azraqi narrated something similar on the authority of al-Zuhri. Al-Azraqi also narrated something similar on the authority of some of the sons of Nafi’ ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im. Al-Azraqi narrated something similar on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir. He also narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi who said: Ibrahim called for the believers and left the disbelievers and did not call for anything for them. God said: And whoever disbelieves, then grant him enjoyment (al-Baqarah 2:17). Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Whoever among them believes in God, he said: It is as if Abraham reserved it for the believers and not the people, so God revealed: And whoever disbelieves, also, “I will provide for them as I provide for the believers. Shall I create a creation for whom I will not provide? I will grant them enjoyment for a little while, then I will force them to the punishment of the Fire.” Then Ibn Abbas recited: No! We provide for these and those, the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah who said: Ubayy ibn Ka’b said regarding his statement: And whoever disbelieves, that this is from the statement of the Lord. Ibn Abbas said: This is from the statement of Abraham asking his Lord that whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little while. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The foundations are the pillars of the House. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir and others narrated a long story on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, the last of which was about the building of the House. He said: At that time, Ibrahim raised the foundations of the House, and Ismail brought stones while Ibrahim built. When the building was high, he brought this stone and placed it for him. He stood on it while he was building, and Ismail handed him the stones, and they were saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.” Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And when Ibrahim raised the foundations, he said: The foundations that were the foundations of the House before that. The commentators have often narrated the sayings of the predecessors in their interpretation of this verse about how the House was built, what stones were made of earth, in what time it was known, who performed Hajj, and what evidence was mentioned in it indicating its virtue or the virtue of some of it, such as the Black Stone. In Al-Durr Al-Manthur there is that which is not found elsewhere, so refer to it. There is some of that in Ibn Kathir’s interpretation, but since what they mentioned is not related to the interpretation, we did not mention it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Salam bin Abi Mutee’ regarding this verse, Our Lord, and make us Muslims to You, he said: They were Muslims, but they asked him to be steadfast. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abdul Karim, he said: Sincere. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement, And of our descendants, he said: They mean the Arabs. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Abraham said, My Lord, show us our rites, so Gabriel came to him and brought him to the House and said: Raise the foundations, so he raised the foundations and completed the building, then he took him by the hand and led him out and went with him towards Mina, and when he was at Al-Aqaba, there was Satan standing by the tree, so he said: Say Allahu Akbar and throw at him, so he said Allahu Akbar and threw at him, then Satan went until he came to the middle Jamarat and Abraham did to him as he had done with the first, then likewise with the third Jamarat, then Gabriel took Abraham by the hand until he came to Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram and said: This is Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, then he went until he came to Arafat, he said: Have you recognized what I have shown you? He said it three times. He said: Yes. He said: Then announce the Hajj to the people. He said: How do I announce it? He said: Say: O people, answer your Lord three times. The servant answered: Here I am, God, here I am. So whoever answers Ibrahim on that day from among the creation is a pilgrim. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab on the authority of Ali who said: When Ibrahim finished building the House, he said: I have done so, O Lord, so show us our rituals: He made them clear to us and taught them. So God sent Gabriel and he performed the Hajj with him. There are many narrations on this topic from the early generations of the Companions and those who came after them which include that Gabriel showed Ibrahim the rituals, and in most of them the devil came to him as mentioned above from Mujahid. Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab narrated something similar to that from Ibn Abbas. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi also narrated on his authority.
2:129: The pronoun in his saying: 129- And send among them refers to the Muslim nation mentioned previously. My father read: And send among their last ones. It is possible that the pronoun refers to the offspring. God answered this call to Abraham, peace be upon him, so He sent among his offspring a messenger from among themselves who is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He has informed about Himself that Abraham's call, as will be explained in the interpretation of that, God willing, and what He meant was this call. And the messenger is the one who is sent. Ibn al-Anbari said: It is likely that its origin is a she-camel that is a messenger and a messenger if it is easy to walk and goes ahead of the she-camels. It is said: The people came in groups: meaning some of them follow each other, and what is meant by the book is the Qur'an. What is meant by wisdom is knowledge of the religion and understanding of the interpretation and understanding of the Shari'ah. And his saying: He purifies them means He cleanses them from polytheism and all other sins. It was said: What is meant by the verses is the apparent meaning of the words, the book is their meanings, and wisdom is the ruling, which is what God intended by the address, and the Almighty is the one for whom nothing is incapable, said Ibn Kaysan. Al-Kisa’i said: The Almighty is the predominant.
2:130: 130- And whoever desires is in the nominative case as a subject, and the question is for denial. And his saying: Except he who fools himself is in the predicate, and it was said: It is a substitute for the subject of yaghriba, and the estimate: And no one desires from the religion of Abraham except he who fools himself. Al-Zajjaj said: Foolishness means ignorance: that is, he was ignorant of his own affairs and did not think about them. Abu Ubaidah said: The meaning is he destroyed himself. Tha'lab and Al-Mubarrad narrated that foolishness with a kasra on the fa' is transitive like safaha with a fatha on the shaddah on the fa'.
