Al-Akhfash said: Foolishness of himself means he did with it such foolishness that he became foolish, and it was said: That his self is erected by removing the preposition, and it was said: It is a distinction, and these two are very weak, and as for foolishness with a damma on the fa', it is not transitive, Al-Mubarrad and Tha'lab said. And selection: choice, that is, we chose him in this world and made him among the righteous in the hereafter, so how can a desirer desire to turn away from his religion? His saying: When he said to him may be related to his saying: We chose him, meaning we selected him at the time we ordered him to convert to Islam. It may also be related to something omitted, which is remember. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: It is as if it was said: Remember that time so that it may be known that he is the chosen, righteous one who does not turn away from the religion of his like.
2:131: 131- "When his Lord said to him, 'Submit,' he said, 'I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.'"
2:132: The pronoun in his saying: 132- "And he recommended it" refers to the religion or to the word: i.e. I have submitted to the Lord of the Worlds. Al-Qurtubi said: This is more correct because it is the closest mentioned: i.e. say we have submitted. End. The first is more likely because what is required of those after him is to follow his religion, not just to speak the word of Islam. Therefore, recommending that is more appropriate for Abraham and more appropriate for them. And he recommended and he recommended means the same thing, and they were read with both of them. In the Mushaf of Uthman, it is "and he recommended" which is the reading of the people of Ash-Sham and Madinah. In the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Masoud, it is "and he recommended" which is the reading of the rest. "And Jacob" is conjoined with Abraham: i.e. and Jacob recommended his sons as Abraham recommended his sons. Omar bin Fayed Al-Aswari and Ismail bin Abdullah Al-Makki read Jacob in the accusative case, so he is included among those whom Abraham recommended. Al-Qushayri said: This is far-fetched because Jacob did not meet his grandfather Abraham, but was born after his death. And his saying: "O my son" is by estimation that. Abi, Ibn Masoud and Al-Dahhak read it with confirmation. Al-Farra’ said: An was omitted because the recommendation is like a statement, and every statement that goes back to a statement can be entered into by An and can be omitted. It was said: It is on the assumption of the statement: meaning saying: O my son. This was narrated from the Basrans. His statement: He has chosen for you the religion means He has selected it for you, and what is meant is His religion which no one would turn away from except the foolish, and it is the religion that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, came with. His statement: So do not die except as Muslims is a clear brevity. What is meant is adhere to Islam and do not leave it until you die. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding his statement: And whoever turns away from the religion of Abraham, he said: The Jews and Christians turned away from his religion, and adopted Judaism and Christianity as an innovation that is not from God. They abandoned the religion of Abraham, Islam. Thus, God sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the religion of Abraham. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah similarly. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: And We have chosen him, he said: We selected him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons, he said: He enjoined them to Islam, and Jacob enjoined the same upon his sons. Al-Tha’labi narrated on the authority of Fudayl bin ‘Iyad regarding his statement: So do not die except as Muslims, meaning having good thoughts about your Lord.
2:133: His saying: 133- "Or were you witnesses? This am" is said to be the disconnected one, and it is said to be the connected one, and in the hamza there is a denial that is useful for rebuke and reprimand, and the address is to the Jews and Christians who attribute to Abraham and his sons that they are Judaists and Christians, so God rejected that and said to them: Did you witness Jacob and you knew what he commanded his sons to do, so you claim that out of knowledge, or did you not witness? Rather, you are inventing. And the witnesses are the plural of witness, and it was not declined because it contains the feminine alif that is for the feminine of the group, and the factor in the first "idh is the meaning of testimony, and the second idh is a substitute for the first, and what is meant by the presence of death is the presence of its preliminaries, and it came with what is not min" in His saying: "what you worship" because the worshipped things other than God are mostly inanimate like idols, fire, the sun, and the planets. And the meaning of "after me" is after my death. And his saying: Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac is an explanatory apposition to his saying: your fathers. And Ishmael, even though he was Jacob’s uncle, because the Arabs call an uncle a father. And his saying: a god is a substitute for your god, even though it is indefinite, that is permissible, especially after specifying it with the attribute, which is his saying: one, because the desired substitution with this attribute has been achieved. And it was said: that god is accusative for specification, and it was said: that it is a state. Ibn Atiyah said: and it is a good saying, because the purpose is to prove the state of oneness. And Al-Hasan, Yahya bin Ya’mar, and Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi read and the god of your father, and it was said: he meant Abraham alone. And his saying: and Ishmael is an apposition to your father, and so is Isaac, even though he is his father in reality and Abraham is his grandfather, but Abraham has more specificity. And it was said: that his saying: your father is a plural, as was narrated from Sibawayh that abin is a plural of soundness, and likewise abon, and from it the saying of the poet: When our voices became clear, we cried and we built our house with our father. His saying: And we are Muslims to Him is a circumstantial clause: meaning we worship Him while we are Muslims to Him. Al-Zamakhshari allowed it to be an interjection to what he believes in the permissibility of interjectional clauses occurring at the end of a speech.
2:134: And the reference in his saying: 134- That is to Abraham and his sons and Jacob and between him and a nation is a substitute for it and its predicate has passed away or a nation is its predicate, and has passed away is an attribute of a nation, and his saying: For it is what it earned and for you is what you earned and you will not be asked about what they used to do is a statement of the state of that nation and the state of those addressed that each of the two groups has his own earnings, the earnings of others will not benefit him and nothing will reach him from him and the sin of others will not harm him, and in it is the response to those who rely on the work of their predecessors and comfort themselves with false hopes, and from it is what was mentioned in the hadith: Whoever is slowed down by his work will not be hastened by his lineage and what is meant is: that you do not benefit from their good deeds and you are not held accountable for their bad deeds and you are not asked about their deeds just as they are not asked about your deeds, and similar to it is and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, and that man will have nothing but what he strives for.
2:135: When the Jews and Christians claimed that guidance is in their hands and that goodness is limited to them, God responded to them by saying: 135- "Rather, the religion of Abraham" meaning, say, O Muhammad, this statement, and the accusative of millah is an implied verb: meaning we follow, and it was said that the estimate is: we will be the religion of Abraham: meaning the people of his religion, and it was said: Rather, we are guided by the religion of Abraham, so when the preposition was deleted, it became accusative. Al-A'raj and Ibn Abi Ubla read millah in the nominative case: meaning, rather, the guidance is the religion of Abraham. And the Hanif is the one who inclines away from false religions to the religion of truth, and in the original language it is: the one whose feet incline each one to its sister. Al-Zajjaj said: It is accusative in the state: meaning, we follow the religion of Abraham while he is a Hanif. Ali bin Sulayman said: It is accusative with the estimate of I mean and the state is wrong as it is not permissible. A young boy from Hind came to me in a hurry. He said in Al-Kashshaf: It is a state of the complement, like your saying: I saw Hind’s face standing. Some people said: Hanif means uprightness, so the religion of Abraham was called Hanif because of its uprightness, and the one with crooked legs was called Hanif out of optimism for uprightness, just as someone who has been bitten is called safe, and someone who has been destroyed is called a wilderness. Those who said that Hanif in the language means crooked, not straight, provided evidence for this by the poet’s saying: If the shadow turns in the evening, you will see him as a monotheist, and in the morning he will become a Christian. That is, the chameleon faces the Qiblah in the evening, and faces the East in the morning, which is the Qiblah of the Christians. Hence the poet’s saying: By God, if it were not for the defect in his foot, there would not be anyone like him among your men. His saying: And he was not among the polytheists is an allusion to the Jews for saying: Ezra is the son of God and to the Christians for saying: The Messiah is the son of God. That is, Abraham was not in this state that you are in of polytheism with God, so how can you claim that he was Jewish or Christian?
2:136: And His saying: 136- "Say: We believe in God" is addressed to the Muslims and an order for them to say this statement, and it was said: It is addressed to the infidels to say the same so that they will be on the truth, and the first is more apparent. And the tribes: the sons of Jacob and they are twelve sons, and each one of them has a group of sons, and the tribe in the Children of Israel is like the tribe in the Arabs, and they were named the tribes from the tribe which is succession, so they are a group in succession, and it was said: Its origin is from the tribe with the movement which is the tree: meaning they are in the majority like the tree, and it was said: the tribes are the grandchildren of Jacob: meaning the sons of his sons not his sons, because the majority was only in them and not the sons of Jacob in himself, so they are individuals not tribes. And His saying: We do not differentiate between any of them Al-Farra' said: Its meaning is that we do not believe in some of them and disbelieve in some of them as the Jews and Christians did. He said in Al-Kashshaf: And one in the meaning of the group, and therefore it is correct to enter between it.
2:137: And His saying: 137- If they believe in the same as you believe in, this address is also to the Muslims: meaning, if the People of the Book and others believe in the same as you believe in all of the books of God and His messengers and do not differentiate between any of them, then they have been guided. And based on this, like is redundant, like His saying: There is nothing like Him, and the poet’s saying: So become like eaten straw It was said: The similarity occurred between the two faiths: that is, if they believed in the same faith as you. And he said in Al-Kashshaf: It is from the category of rebuke because the religion of truth is one and has no equal, and it is the religion of Islam. He said: That is, if they obtained another religion like your religion, equal to it in soundness and correctness, then they have been guided. And it was said: The ba’ is an additional emphasis, and it was said: It is for assistance. And the origin of the word shaqq is from shaqq which means side, as if each of the two groups is on a side other than the side that the other is on. And it was said: It is taken from the verb what is difficult and hard, so each of the two groups is keen to do what is difficult for the other, and it is correct to carry the verse to each of the two meanings, and likewise the saying of the poet: Otherwise, know that you and I are rebels as long as we remain in discord. And the other said: How long will you accept scholars by force and boast of discord and hypocrisy? His saying: God will suffice you against them is a promise from God Almighty to His Prophet that He will suffice him against those who oppose him and contradict him from among the followers, and He fulfilled His promise to him with what He sent down of His might upon Qurayza, Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa.
2:138: And his saying: 138- The dye of God Al-Akhfash and others said: meaning the religion of God. He said: It is in the accusative case as a substitute for religion, as Al-Farra' said. And he said in Al-Kashaf: It is a confirmed source in the accusative case for his saying: We believe in God just as -God's promise- was in the accusative case for what preceded it, and it is a verb from sabagh like jalsah from jals, and it is the state in which dyeing occurs, and the meaning is the purification of God because faith is the purification of souls, and this is what Sibawayh said: meaning it is a confirmed source. And the commentators mentioned that the origin of that is that the Christians used to dye their children in water, which is what they call baptism, and they made that a purification for them, so if they did that they said now he has become a true Christian, so God responded to them by saying: The dye of God meaning Islam, and he called it dye as a metaphor, and from it is the saying of some of the poets of Hamdan: Every people have a different color and Hamdan is the best color. We dyed our children on that, so He honored us by dyeing us in dyeing It was said: The dye is the bathing for those who want to enter Islam instead of Christian baptism, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. Al-Jawhari said: The dye of God is His religion, and this supports what was mentioned above by Al-Farra. It was also said: The dye is circumcision.
2:139: And His statement: 139- "Say: Do you argue with us about God?" That is, do you argue with us about God: that is, about His religion, closeness to Him, and favor with Him? This is like their saying: We are the sons of God and His beloved. Ibn Muhaisin read Do you argue with us with assimilation due to the meeting of the two similar letters. And His statement: And He is our Lord and your Lord That is, we and you share in His Lordship over us and our servitude to Him, so how do you claim that you are more deserving of Him than we are and argue with us about that? And His statement: For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds That is, for us are deeds and for you are deeds, so you are not more deserving of God than us. This is like His statement, the Most High: "Then say: To me is my work, and to you is your work. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do." His statement: And we are sincere to Him means that we are the people of sincerity in worship, unlike you, and this is the standard by which differentiation takes place and the characteristic by which the one who possesses it is more deserving of God Almighty than anyone else. So how do you claim for yourselves what we are more deserving of and more worthy of than you? In it is a rebuke to them and an end to what they have come with in terms of argument and debate.
2:140: And his saying: 140- Or do they say? Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Asim read in the narration of Hafs you say with the upper ta', and according to this reading, the am here is equivalent to the hamzah in his saying: Do you argue with us? meaning, do you argue with us about God, or do you say that these prophets are of your religion? And according to the reading with the lower ya', it is a disconnected am: meaning, rather, they say. And his saying: Say, Are you more knowledgeable or God? In it is a rebuke and rebuke: meaning, God informed us that they were neither Jews nor Christians, and you claim that they were Jews or Christians, so are you more knowledgeable or God, glory be to Him. His statement: And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God? It is possible that what he means by that is to criticize the People of the Book because they know that these prophets were neither Jews nor Christians, but rather they were of the Islamic faith, so they wronged themselves by concealing this testimony, and even by claiming something that contradicts it, and this is a greater sin than someone who merely conceals it, for no one is more unjust than him. It is possible that what is meant is that if the Muslims concealed this testimony, no one would be more unjust than them, and what is meant by that is to insinuate the People of the Book. It was said that what is meant here is what they concealed of the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. In His statement: And God is not unaware of what you do, there is a severe threat and a warning that cannot be added, and a notification that God, the Exalted, will not leave them alone in punishment for this ugly injustice and terrible sin.
2:141: And He repeated His Almighty saying: 141- That was a nation that has passed on until the end of the verse, to include the meaning of threat and intimidation, which is what is intended in this context. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding his statement: Or were you witnesses? meaning the People of the Book. He also narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: Or were you witnesses? He said: He says that neither the Jews nor the Christians nor any of the people witnessed Jacob when he took a covenant from his sons when death approached him that they would not worship except God, and they acknowledged that and he testified against them that they had acknowledged their worship and that they were Muslims. He narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to say: The grandfather is a father and he recited the verse. He also narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding the verse that he said: The paternal uncle was called a father. He also narrated something similar on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Abdullah bin Suriya Al-A’war said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is no guidance except what we are upon, so follow us, O Muhammad, and you will be guided. The Christians said the same, so God revealed about them: And they said, ‘Be Jews’ 10:10. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Hanif that he said: Following. They also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Hanif he said: A pilgrim. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b who said: The upright Hanif. He also narrated on the authority of Khasif who said: The sincere Hanif. He also narrated on the authority of Abu Qilabah who said: The Hanif is the one who believes in all the Messengers from the first of them to the last of them. Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I was sent with the easy Hanif. Ahmad also narrated, and Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “It was said: O Messenger of God, which religion is most beloved to God? He said: The easy Hanif.” Al-Hakim narrated in his history and Ibn Asakir from the hadith of As’ad bin Abdullah bin Malik Al-Khuza’i with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) likewise. Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud and Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite in the two rak’ahs of Fajr in the first of them the entire verse in Surat Al-Baqarah “Say: We believe in God” and in the second We believe in God and bear witness that we are Muslims. Al-Bukhari narrated from Abu Hurairah who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it to the Muslims in Arabic. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not believe the People of the Book nor disbelieve them, but say: We believe in God” (al-An’am 2:17). Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: The tribes, the sons of Jacob, were twelve men, each of whom gave birth to a nation of people. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Al-Suddi, and Ibn Kathir narrated it in his Tafsir from Abu Al-Aliyah, Al-Rabi’ and Qatadah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat from Ibn Abbas who said: Do not say: If they believe in what you believe in, then there is none like God, but say: If they believe in what you believe in. Ibn Abi Dawud narrated in Al-Masahif and Al-Khatib in his History from Abu Jamrah who said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: If they believe in what you believe in. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Al-Aliyah regarding His statement: Then they are in dissension, he said: separation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The dye of God, he said: The religion of God. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The nature of God upon which He created mankind. Ibn Mardawayh and Ad-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The Children of Israel said: O Moses, does your Lord dye? He said: Fear God. His Lord called out to him: O Moses, they asked you, does your Lord dye? Say: Yes, I dye colors, red, white, black, and all colors are in my dye.” And God revealed to His Prophet: The dye of God, and who is better than God in dyeing? Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated it in Al-Azmah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with no chain of transmission ending with him. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: The Jews dye their children as Jews, and the Christians dye their children as Christians, and the dye of God is Islam, and there is no dye better than the dye of Islam, nor is it purer. It is the religion of God with which He sent Noah and the prophets who came after him. Ibn Al-Najjar narrated in Tarikh Baghdad on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The dye of God he said: Whiteness. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Do you argue with us? he said: Do you quarrel with us. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority: He said: Do you argue with us? Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And who is more unjust than he who conceals testimony the verse, he said: Those are the People of the Book who concealed Islam while knowing that it is the religion of God, and adopted Judaism and Christianity, and concealed Muhammad while knowing that he is the Messenger of God. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Khasan something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada and Al-Rabi’ regarding his statement: That is a nation that has passed on, he said: He means Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes.
2:142: His saying: 142- He will say This is report from God the Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers that the foolish Jews and hypocrites will say this statement when the Qiblah is changed from the Holy House to the Kaaba. It was said that He will say means he said, and the past was expressed in the future tense to indicate its continuity and persistence. It was said that the report of this report was before the change to the Kaaba, and that the benefit of that is that if report of something bad happens before it happens, it is a way of belittling its shock, alleviating its terror, and breaking its spirit. Fools is the plural of fool, which is the liar who relies on falsehood and contradicts what is known, as some linguists said. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: They are light-hearted, and the same is in Al-Qamoos. We have already mentioned in the interpretation of His statement: Except for he who makes a fool of himself what should be referred to, and the meaning of: What turned them away is what turned them away from the qiblah which they were facing which is Jerusalem. So God responded to them by saying: “Say: To God belongs the east and the west” so He has the right to command facing in any direction He wishes. And in His statement: He guides whom He wills there is an indication that turning the qiblah to Mecca is a guidance for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for the people of his religion to the straight path.
2:143: And His statement: 143- And thus We have made you meaning, like that making, We have made you. It was said that its meaning is: And just as the Kaaba is in the middle of the earth, so We have made you a middle nation. And the middle is the choice or the just, and the verse is open to both meanings, and among what is open to them is the saying of Zuhair: They are the middle ground, and people are satisfied with their judgment if one of the nights descends upon most of them. And the same is said by another: You are the middle of the neighborhood, know the small matter or one of the big ones It has been proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, interpreted the middle here as justice, as will come, so it is necessary to refer to that, including the words of the rajaz poet: Don't go overboard with things. Don't ask if you ask too much Be moderate among all people Since the middle ground is free from exaggeration and shortcoming, it is praiseworthy: that is, this nation did not go to extremes like the Christians did with regard to Jesus, nor did they fall short like the Jews with regard to their prophets. It is said that so-and-so is the middle and central of his al-Nas 114:that is, their best. And His statement: So that you may be witnesses over mankind means on the Day of Resurrection you will bear witness for the prophets over their nations that they conveyed to them what God commanded them to convey to them, and the Messenger will be a witness over his nation that they did what he commanded them to convey to them. And similar to it is His statement, the Most High: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? It was said that His statement, over you means for you: that is, he bears witness to their faith. And it was said that its meaning is: he bears witness over you for conveying the message to you. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: Since the witness is like the watcher and the one who dominates over the one who is witnessed to, the word of superiority was brought, and from it is His statement, the Most High: And God is Witness over all things. “You were the watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things.” End quote. A group said: The meaning of the verse is that some of you will bear witness against others after death. It was also said: What is meant is that you will be witnesses over people in this world in matters that are not valid except with the testimony of just people. And what will come from the hadith that explains the meaning of the verse, God willing, is that the word upon was delayed in the testimony of the nation over people, and it was presented in the testimony of the Messenger over them, because the purpose, as the author of Al-Kashshaf said in the first, is to prove their testimony over the nations, and in the second, to specify them with the Messenger being a witness over them. And his statement: And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing It was said: What is meant by this qiblah is Jerusalem: that is, We did not make it except to know who follows and who turns away. This is supported by his statement: You were facing it if the revelation of this verse was after the qiblah was changed to the Kaaba. It was also said: What is meant is the Kaaba: that is, We did not make the qiblah which you are facing now after it was toward Jerusalem except for that purpose, and you were means the state. It was also said: What is meant by this is the qiblah which he was facing before facing Jerusalem, because he used to face the Kaaba in Mecca, then when he migrated he headed toward Jerusalem to win over the Jews, then he was changed to the Kaaba. And his saying: Except that We may know. It was said that what is meant by knowledge here is seeing. And it was said that what is meant is except that you may know that we know that the hypocrites were in doubt. And it was said: So that the Prophet may know. And it was said: What is meant is so that we may know that it is present and occurring. And thus what was mentioned with the explanation of the knowledge of God, the Most High, must be interpreted with something like this, like his saying: And that God may know those who believe and take from among you witnesses. And his saying: And if it were a great sin means that it was nothing but a great sin, as al-Farra’ said regarding an and inna that they have the same meaning as ma and illa. The Basrans said: It is the heavy one that was lightened, and the pronoun in kana refers to what is indicated by His statement: And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing of changing, turning away, making, or apostasy. Al-Akhfash mentioned the meaning of that, and there is nothing to prevent the pronoun from referring to the mentioned qiblah: that is, even if the qiblah described as being yours was difficult except for those whom God guided to faith, so their hearts expanded to believe you, and their minds accepted what you brought. This exception is empty because what preceded it is in the strength of negation: that is, because it is not light or easy except for those whom God guided. And His statement: God would not let your faith go to waste, Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars agreed that it was revealed about the one who died while praying towards the Holy House, then he said: So He called prayer faith because it comes together in intention, word, and action. And it was said: What is meant is the steadfastness of the believers in faith when the qiblah is changed, and their lack of doubt as others doubted. And the first must be said, and the destination is due to what will come from his interpretation of the verse by the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in that regard. And the Compassionate is the one who is very compassionate, and it is more severe than mercy. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: Compassion is greater than mercy, and the meanings are similar. Abu Ja’far ibn Yazid ibn al-Qa’qa’ read rauf without a hamza, and it is the language of Banu Asad, and from it is the saying of al-Walid ibn Utbah: The worst of the victors, so do not be like him, he is fighting his uncle, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’ that “the first time the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Madinah, he came to his maternal uncles from the Ansar, and that he prayed towards the Holy House for sixteen or seventeen months, and he liked that his qiblah be towards the House, and the first prayer he prayed was the afternoon prayer, and some people prayed with him. Then a man who had prayed with him came out and passed by the people of the mosque while they were bowing and said: I bear witness by God that I prayed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) towards the Ka’bah, so they turned as they were towards the House. The Jews were amazed that he prayed towards the Holy House, and the People of the Book, but when he turned his face towards the House, they disapproved of that. The ones who died facing the qiblah before it was changed towards the House were men, and they were killed, so we did not know what to say about them, so God revealed: ‘And God would never let your faith go to waste. God is Most Kind and Merciful to mankind. ’” And there are other chains of transmission and similar wordings. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing abrogated in the Qur’an was the qiblah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray in Mecca facing Jerusalem with the Kaaba in front of him. After he moved to Medina for sixteen months, God turned him towards the Kaaba.” There are many hadiths on this topic with the same content as mentioned above. Likewise, hadiths were narrated about the time when facing the Qiblah was revealed, and about how the worshippers should turn when they heard about it, and they were praying, so we will not go on mentioning them at length. Saeed bin Mansour, Ahmad, Al-Nasa’i, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Isma’ili in his Sahih, and Al-Hakim who authenticated it, narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, And thus We have made you a just community, he said: Just. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i and others narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Noah will be called on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him: Did you convey the message? He will say: Yes. His people will be called and it will be said to them: Did he convey the message to you? They will say: No warner came to us, and no one came to us. Noah will be asked: Who will bear witness for you? He will say: Muhammad and his nation." This is what God said: And thus We have made you a just community. He said: The middle way is justice. So you will be called and you will bear witness for him that you conveyed the message, and I will bear witness against you. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Sa'id. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "My nation and I will be on a hill overlooking the creation on the Day of Resurrection. There will be no one among the people who will not wish that he were one of us, and there will be no prophet who was denied by his people but that we will bear witness that he conveyed the message of his Lord." Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed in his statement: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people that the messengers had conveyed and the Messenger will be a witness over you of what you did. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “They passed by a funeral procession and it was praised well, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is due, due, due. They passed by a funeral procession and it was praised badly, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is due, due, due. Umar asked him and he said: Whoever you praise well, Paradise is due for him, and whoever you praise badly, Hell is due for him. You are the witnesses of God on earth, you are the witnesses of God on earth, you are the witnesses of God on earth.” Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi added: “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “And thus We have made you a just community” the verse.” There are hadiths on this topic, some of them on the authority of Jabir with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, according to Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and some on the authority of Umar with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, according to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i. And from it on the authority of Abu Zuhair Al-Thaqafi, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, as narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Majah, Al-Tabarani, Al-Daraqutni in Al-Ifrad, Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sunan, and from it on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, as narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim, and from Salamah bin Al-Akwa’, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, as narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Al-Tabarani. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ata’, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face he said: meaning Jerusalem except that We might test he said: We would test them to know who would submit to His command. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his words: except that We might test he said: to distinguish the people of certainty from the people of doubt and indeed it is a great sin meaning turning it against the people of polytheism and doubt. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: It reached me that some people who had accepted Islam returned and said: Once here and once there. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, Al-Tabarani and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned towards the Qiblah, they said: ‘O Messenger of God, what about those who died while praying towards Jerusalem?’ So God revealed: ‘And God would never let your faith go to waste.’” The hadith of Al-Bara’ was mentioned above. There are many hadiths on this topic, as well as reports from the early Muslims.
2:144: His saying: 144- We have certainly seen the turning of your face. Al-Qurtubi said in his interpretation: The scholars said: This verse was revealed before His saying: The fools will say. The meaning of has certainly is to increase the vision, as the author of Al-Kashshaf said, and the meaning of turn your face is to turn your face to the sky, as Qatrub said. Al-Zajjaj said: You turn your eyes in looking at the sky, and the meaning is close. His saying: Then We will surely turn you is either from the word wilayah: meaning We will give you that. Or from the word tawali: meaning We will make you turn towards its direction, and this is more appropriate for His saying: Then turn your face towards Al-Masjid Al-Haram. What is meant by the direction here is the side and the direction, and it is in the accusative case as a circumstantial case, and from it the poet said: I say to Umm Zinba’: Set the camels’ chests towards Banu Tamim. And from it also the saying of another: Is there anyone who can convey the message of Omar as a messenger? But a message is of no avail to half of Omar. Half may mean half, such as Ablution is half of faith, and such as the saying of Antarah: I am a man from the best of Abs, I have a strong position in my side and I protect the rest with the sword He said that because his father was from the leaders of Abs and his mother was a slave woman, and it is used to mean some in general. There is no dispute that what is meant by the part of the mosque here is the Kaaba. Al-Qurtubi narrated the consensus that facing the Kaaba is obligatory for the one who sees it, and that the one who does not see it faces the side, and he provides evidence for that with whatever evidence he can provide, and the pronoun in his saying: that it is the truth refers to what the speech indicates of turning to the direction of the Kaaba, and the knowledge of the People of the Book of that is either because it was conveyed to them from their prophets or they found in the revealed books of God that this prophet faces the Kaaba, or because they knew from their books or their prophets that there would be abrogation in this Shariah, so that would require them to enter Islam and follow the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. His saying: And God is not unaware of what they do has already been explained. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read ya ta’malunu with the upper tha’ to address the People of the Book or the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the rest read it with the lower ya’.
2:145: And his saying: 145- And if you came This lam is an introduction to the oath, and the meaning is: By God, if you came. And his saying: They would not follow is the answer to the estimated oath. Al-Akhfash and Al-Farraa said: I answer if with the answer to if because the meaning is: And if you came, and similar to it is the saying of the Most High: And if We sent a wind and they saw it yellow, they would remain astray meaning, even if We sent, and they only said it this way because if is the opposite of if, and that is because the first requires in its answer the past and the occurrence, and if requires in its answer the future. Sibawayh said: The meaning of if differs from the meaning of if, so one does not enter into the other, so the meaning is: And if you brought to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your direction. Sibawayh said: The meaning of and if We sent a wind and they saw it yellow is that they would remain astray. End. This verse contains great exaggeration and includes consolation for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and to cheer him up, because these people are not affected by every verse, and they do not return to the truth even if it brings them every proof, let alone one proof. This is because they did not abandon following the truth because of a proof they had or because of a doubt that came to them, until they weighed what they had with what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought and abandoned their misguidance when the truth became clear. Rather, their abandonment of the truth was rebellion and stubbornness, knowing that they were not on anything, and whoever is like this will never benefit from the proof. And His statement: And you will not follow their Qiblah This information could mean a prohibition from God the Almighty to His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): that is, do not follow their Qiblah, O Muhammad. It could also be, on its surface, to repel the desires of the People of the Book and to cut off what they hope for from his (peace and blessings of God be upon him) return to the Qiblah he was on. His statement: And some of them do not follow the qiblah of others is information that the Jews and Christians, despite their eagerness to pledge allegiance to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of what they have, differ in their religion, even in this specific ruling that God Almighty related to His Messenger, for some of them do not follow others in facing their qiblah. It says in Al-Kashshaf: That is because the Jews face Jerusalem and the Christians face the rising of the sun. End quote. And His saying: And if you were to follow their desires to the end of the verse, contains a great threat and a powerful warning that makes the skin shudder and the heart tremble. If the inclination towards the desires of those who oppose this pure Shari’ah and the noble religion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who is the master of the children of Adam, necessitates that he be, God forbid, among the oppressors, then what do you think of others from his nation? God has protected this Islamic sect, after the establishment of the age of Islam and the elevation of its beacon, from inclining towards any of the desires of the People of the Book. Nothing remains except a satanic plot and a tyrannical means, which is the inclination of some of those who bear God’s proofs towards the desires of some groups of innovators, because of what they hope for of immediate ruin from their hands or prestige with them if they have power among the people, or if they are among those with influence. This inclination is not without that inclination, rather following the desires of the innovators is similar to following the desires of the People of the Book, just as water is similar to water, an egg is similar to an egg, and a date is similar to a date. The corruption of following the desires of the innovators may be more severe than these. The religion is one of the evils of following the whims of the people of religions, for the innovators belong to Islam, and they show to the people that they support those who follow the best of it, but they are the opposite of that and the opposite of what is there, so they continue to transfer whoever inclines to their whims from one innovation to another and push him from one abomination to another, until they strip him of the religion and expel him from it, while he thinks that he is from it in the core, and that the path he is on is the straight path. This is if he is among the deficient, and among the ignorant, and if he is among the people of knowledge and understanding who distinguish between truth and falsehood, then in his following their whims he is one of those whom God has shaded with knowledge and sealed his heart, and he has become a curse upon the servants of God and a calamity that God has poured upon the deficient, because they believe that in his knowledge and understanding he only inclines to the truth, and only follows what is correct, so they go astray because of his misguidance, so his sin and the sin of those who follow him will be upon him until the Day of Resurrection. We ask God for kindness, safety, and guidance.
2:146: And His statement: 146- Those to whom We gave the Scripture know it. It was said: The pronoun refers to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: that is, they know his prophethood. This was narrated from Mujahid, Qatadah, and a group of scholars. It was also said: They know the change of the qibla from Jerusalem to the Kaaba by the method we mentioned earlier, and a group of commentators said the same, and the author of Al-Kashshaf preferred the first. In my opinion, the other is preferred, as indicated by the context for which these verses were cited. And His statement: So that they may conceal the truth is, according to the people of the first opinion, the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and according to the people of the second opinion, facing the Kaaba.
2:147: And his saying: 147- The truth is from your Lord may mean the first truth, and it may mean the type of truth as the predicate of a deleted subject or a subject and its predicate is his saying: from your Lord, meaning the truth is that which is from your Lord and not from anyone else. Ali bin Abi Talib read the truth in the accusative case as a substitute for the first or in the accusative case for enticement, meaning adhere to the truth. And his saying: So do not be among those who doubt is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and doubt is suspicion. God Almighty forbade him from doubting whether it is the truth from his Lord, or whether they concealed the truth despite their knowledge. According to the first, it is an exposition of the nation: meaning that no one from his nation should be among those who doubt, because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, does not doubt that it is the truth from God Almighty. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ who said: We prayed with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) towards Jerusalem for eighteen months, and the qiblah was changed to the Kaaba two months after he entered Medina. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed towards Jerusalem, he would often turn his face towards the sky. God knew in the heart of His Prophet that he loved the Kaaba, so Gabriel ascended and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would follow him with his eyes as he ascended between heaven and earth, watching what he would bring him. Then God revealed: We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the heaven (al-Baqarah 2:14). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Gabriel, how are we in our prayer towards Jerusalem? Then God revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste. At-Tabarani narrated it from the hadith of Muadh in an abbreviated form, but he said: seventeen months. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani in al-Kabir, and Al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr regarding the words of God the Almighty: Then We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased (al-Baqarah 2:14), he said: The qiblah of Abraham was towards the gutter. And Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’ concerning his statement: Then turn your face toward Al-Masjid Al-Haram, he said: In front of it. And Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ali something similar. And Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: In front of it something similar. And Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. And Ibn Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah who said: In front of Al-Masjid Al-Haram means facing it. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The entire House is a qiblah and the qiblah of the House is the door. And Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on his authority that it was transmitted with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet who said: The House is a qiblah for the people of the mosque and the mosque is a qiblah for the people of the Haram and the Haram is a qiblah for the people of the earth in its east and west from my nation. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi concerning his statement: And those who were given the Scripture, he said: This was revealed concerning the Jews. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: That they may know that it is the truth, he said: He means the Qiblah. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And some of them do not follow the Qiblah of others, he said: The Jews do not follow the Qiblah of the Christians, nor do the Christians follow the Qiblah of the Jews. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: Those to whom We gave the Scripture, he said: The Jews and the Christians recognize him, he said: They recognize the Messenger of God in their book as they recognize their own sons. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: recognize him, meaning they know that the Sacred House is the Qiblah. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Rabi’. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know, he said: They conceal Muhammad even though they find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. Abu Dawud included in his Naskh and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah who said: God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt. He said: Do not be in doubt, O Muhammad, that the Kaaba is your qiblah, and it was the qiblah of the prophets before you.
2:148: His statement: 148- And for each with the deletion of the complement due to the indication of the tanween on it: meaning for each people of a religion there is a direction, and the direction is a verb from the face and its meaning is direction and face, and what is meant is the qiblah: meaning that they do not follow your qiblah and you do not follow their qiblah. And for each either rightly or wrongly, and the pronoun in his statement: He turns it refers to the word each. The ha' in his statement: Turning it is the first object, and the second object is deleted: meaning turning its face. The meaning is: that for each follower of a religion there is a qiblah of the follower of the qiblah turning his face to it, or for each of you, O nation of Muhammad, there is a qiblah towards which he prays from the east or west or south or north if the address is to the Muslims - and it is possible that the pronoun refers to God, the Most High, even if He is not mentioned, since it is known that God is the doer of that, and the meaning is: that for each follower of a religion there is a qiblah of God turning it to him. Al-Tabari narrated that some people read wa lakul wajha with the addition of wa lakul for each direction, and Abu Amr al-Dani attributed this reading to Ibn Abbas. He said in al-Kashaf: The meaning is: And every direction is God’s direction, so the lam was added to precede the object, like you saying to Zayd, I hit and to Zayd’s father hit him. End. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Amir read: his master for what the agent was not named. Al-Zajjaj said: The pronoun, according to this innocence, refers to one: that is, for each one of the people, the direction of the One is its master: that is, he is directed towards it. And His statement: So race to good deeds means to good deeds, by deletion and connection: that is, hasten to what God has commanded you of facing the Sacred House, as the context indicates, even though its apparent meaning is a command to race to everything that is true to be good, as the generality derived from the definition of good deeds indicates. What is meant by racing to face is racing to prayer at the beginning of its time. The meaning of his saying: Wherever you may be, God will bring you is that wherever you may be, God will bring you for recompense on the Day of Resurrection, or He will gather you all together, and He will make your prayers in different directions as if they were in one direction.
2:149: And His saying: 149- And from wherever you came out He repeated this, glory be to Him, to emphasize the command to face the Kaaba, and to pay attention to it, because the location of the transformation was of interest to their souls. It was said: The reason for the repetition is that abrogation is from the places of temptation and the places of doubt, so if they hear it again and again they become steadfast and what is in their hearts is dispelled. It was said: He repeated this ruling because of the multiplicity of its reasons, for He, glory be to Him, mentioned three reasons for the transformation: the first is seeking His pleasure, the second is the divine custom that He assigns every person of a religion and the one who calls to a direction that he is independent of, and the third is to repel the arguments of the opponents, so He paired each reason with its effect. It was said that He meant by the first: Turn your face toward the Kaaba when you pray facing it. Then He said: And wherever you are, O Muslims, in all the mosques in Madinah and elsewhere, turn your faces toward it. Then He said: And from wherever you came out meaning the obligation of facing in travel, so this was a command to face the Kaaba in all places. From all corners of the earth.
2:150: And His saying: 150- "So that people will have no argument against you." It was said that its meaning is: So that the Jews will have no argument against you except for the obstinate ones among them, for those who say: He did not abandon our Qiblah towards the Kaaba except out of inclination towards the religion of his people. So based on this, what is meant by those who did wrong are the obstinate ones among the People of the Book. It was said that they are the polytheists of the Arabs, and their argument is their saying: I have returned to our Qiblah. It was said that its meaning is: So that people will have no argument against you, so that they will not say to you: You were ordered to face the Kaaba and you do not see it. Abu Ubaidah said: "In illa ha" here has the meaning of waw: that is, and those who did wrong is an exception with the meaning of waw, and from it is the saying of the poet: There is no house in the city except for one, the house of the Caliph, and that is Marwan. As if he said: Except the house of the Caliph and the house of Marwan. Al-Zajjaj invalidated this statement and said: It is an isolated exception: that is, but those who were unjust among them, they are hidden. Its meaning is: Except for those who were unjust by arguing in what has been made clear to them, as you say: You have no argument against me except that you wrong me: that is, you have no argument against me at all, but you wrong me. He called his injustice an argument because the one arguing with it called it an argument even if it was invalid. Qatrib said: It is possible that the meaning is: So that the people will have no argument against you except those who were unjust, so those are a substitute for the kaf and the mim in upon you. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari preferred that the exception is connected, and he said: God denied that anyone had an argument against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions in facing the Kaaba, and the meaning is: No one has an argument against you except the invalid argument, as they said: What made them leaders? And they said: Muhammad was confused about his religion, and he did not face our qibla except that I took from him. And other than that of the statements that were only issued by an idol worshipper, a Jew, or a hypocrite. He said: The argument means the argumentation which is the dispute and the argument, and the Almighty called it an argument and ruled that it was corrupt since it was from an oppressor. Ibn Atiyyah preferred that the exception is disconnected as Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Qurtubi said: This is on the basis that what is meant by the people are the Jews, then he excluded the Arab infidels as if he said: But those who were unjust in their saying Muhammad has returned to our Qiblah and will return to our entire religion. And his saying: "So do not fear them" means the al-Nas 114:that is, do not fear their attacks, for they are invalid and false and will not harm you. And his saying: "And that I may complete My favor upon you is conjoined with lest it be" that is, and that I may complete, said Al-Akhfash. And it was said: It is disconnected from what came before it in the place of raising by the beginning, and the predicate is implied, and the meaning: And that I may complete My favor upon you, I will make you know my Qiblah, said Al-Zajjaj. And it was said: It is conjoined with an implied reason as if it was said: And fear Me so that I may guide you and complete My favor upon you. And the completion of the favor is guidance to the Qiblah, and it was said: entering Paradise.
2:151: And his saying: 151- As We sent The kaf is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source. The meaning is: And I will complete My favor upon you as I sent, as Al-Farra' said, and Ibn Atiyyah preferred it. It was said: The kaf is in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is: And I will complete My favor upon you in this state, and the comparison is based on the fact that the favor in the Qiblah is like the favor in the message. It was said that the meaning of the speech is in the presentation and delay: So remember Me as We sent, as Al-Zajjaj said.
2:152: And His saying: 152- So remember Me, I will remember you is a command and its answer, and it contains the meaning of recompense. Saeed bin Jubair said: The meaning of the verse is remember Me with obedience, I will remember you with reward and forgiveness. Al-Qurtubi narrated it from him in his interpretation, and Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated it from him. A similar narration has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, as will come. And His saying: And be grateful to Me Al-Farra' said: He thanked you and I thanked you. Gratitude is knowing and speaking about kindness, and its root in the language is purity. We have already discussed it. And His saying: And do not be ungrateful is a prohibition, and therefore the group's nun was deleted, and this one found in the verb is the speaker's nun, and the ya' was deleted because it is the beginning of a verse, and its inclusion is good in places other than the Qur'an. And kufr here is covering up a blessing, not denying it, and we have already discussed it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And for each is a direction toward which he turns, he said: He means by that the people of religions, he said: For every qiblah they are pleased with. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said in the interpretation of this verse: Pray toward Jerusalem once, and toward the Kaaba another time. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh on the authority of Qatada something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Then race to do good deeds, he said: Do not be overcome in your qiblah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: Then race to do good deeds, he said: The righteous deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding his statement: Then race to do good deeds, he said: So hasten in doing good deeds. Wherever you may be, God will bring you all together, he said: On the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud and some of the Companions who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned towards the Kaaba after praying towards Jerusalem, the polytheists of Mecca said: Muhammad is confused about his religion, so he turned towards you as his qiblah and he knew that you were more guided than him and that he was about to enter your religion. So God revealed: “So that mankind will have no argument against you, except for those who do wrong among them. So fear them not, but fear Me.” Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: So that mankind will have no argument against you, he said: He meant the People of the Book when the Prophet of God turned towards the Kaaba. They said: The man yearned for his father’s house and the religion of his people. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Their argument was their saying that he loved our qiblah. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir on the authority of Qatadah and Mujahid on his statement: Except those who have wronged among them, he said: Those who have wronged among them are the polytheists of Quraysh that they will argue with you about that, and they argued with the Prophet of God about his turning to the Sacred House and they said: He will return to our religion as he returned to our Qiblah, so God revealed about all of that: “O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, God is with the patient.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah on his statement: Just as We have sent among you a Messenger from among you, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid on his statement: Just as We have sent among you a Messenger from among you, he said: As you did, remember Me. Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Juwaybir on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Remember Me, I will remember you, meaning: Remember Me, O people of worship, by obeying Me and I will remember you with My forgiveness. Al-Daylami and Ibn Asakir narrated a similar hadith with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Abu Hind al-Dari, who added: “Whoever remembers Me while being obedient, it is My right to remember him with My forgiveness. Whoever remembers Me while being disobedient, it is My right to remember him with hatred.” Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: God says: My remembrance of you is better than your remembrance of Me. Many hadiths have been narrated about the virtue of remembering God in general and the virtue of gratitude.
2:153: When He, the Almighty, finished guiding His servants to remember Him and thank Him, He followed that by guiding them to seek help through patience and prayer. Whoever combines remembering God and thanking Him, and seeks help through patience and prayer to carry out what God has commanded, and to repel the trials that befall him, has been guided to the right path and guided to goodness. This companionship that God made clear in His saying: 153- Indeed, God is with the patient contains the greatest encouragement for His servants, the Almighty, to adhere to patience in the face of the calamities that befall them. Whoever has God with him does not fear the terrors, even if they are mountains.
2:154: 154- And do not say about those who are killed in the way of God, 'They are dead.' Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not. Dead and alive are raised as two predicates for two omitted words: that is, do not say about those who are killed in the way of God, 'They are dead.' Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive this life when you see their bodies after their souls have been taken away, because you judge them to be dead in appearance according to what your knowledge reaches, which is in relation to God's knowledge as a bird takes seawater in its beak. But in reality, they are not like that, but rather they are alive in the intermediate realm. And in the verse there is evidence of the proof of the torment of the grave, and no attention should be paid to the disagreement of those who disagreed with that, as it has been transmitted in many authentic hadiths and the verses of the Qur'an have indicated it, and an example of this verse is the saying of God the Most High: "And do not think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision."
2:155: The origin of the affliction is the trial, and the meaning of Nabloonkum is: We test you to test you, will you be patient with the decree or not? The indefiniteness of something is to diminish: meaning with a small amount of these matters. Ad-Dahhak read it with things. What is meant by fear: what happens to someone who fears harm from an enemy or someone else. And by hunger: the famine that occurs due to drought and famine. And by the decrease in wealth: what happens to it due to disasters and what God has directed in it from zakat and the like. And by the decrease in souls: death and killing in jihad. And by the decrease in fruits: what befalls it from calamities, and it is from the conjunction of the specific to the general because wealth includes fruits and other things. It was said: what is meant by the decrease in fruits: the death of children. And His statement: 155- And give good tidings to the patient is a command to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone who is able to give good tidings. The meaning of good tidings has already been mentioned. And patience is originally confinement, and He described them as those who seek refuge in the face of calamity, because that is submission and contentment.
2:156: And the calamity is one of the calamities: it is the disaster that harms a person, no matter how small. And His saying: 156- Indeed we belong to God and to Him we shall return is a statement that these words are a refuge for the afflicted and a protection for those who are tested, for they combine the acknowledgment of servitude to God and the recognition of resurrection and revival.
2:157: The meaning of prayers here is forgiveness and good praise, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. Based on this, mercy was mentioned for the purpose of emphasis. He said in Al-Kashshaf: Prayer is mercy and compassion, so it was placed in place of compassion, and it was combined with mercy, as in His saying: compassion and mercy, Most Kind, Most Merciful. The meaning is: upon them is compassion after compassion and mercy after mercy. It was said: what is meant by mercy is: relieving distress and fulfilling need. 157- The meaning of the guided ones has already been mentioned, and they were described as such here because they did what would lead to the right path of seeking refuge in God and submitting. Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abdul-Rahman bin Awf who said: Abdul-Rahman bin Awf fainted during his illness and they thought that he had passed away, so they got up from him and covered him with a cloth. Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah, his wife, went out to the mosque to seek help as she had been commanded to do of patience and prayer. They remained in a coma for an hour while he was in a coma, then he regained consciousness. Ibn Mandah narrated in Al-Ma’rifah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Tamim bin Al-Hammam was killed at Badr, and about him and others the verse was revealed: And say not of those who are killed in the way of God, ‘They are dead’ 10:1. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: In the way of God in obedience to God in fighting the polytheists. There are hadiths that the souls of the martyrs are in the bodies of green birds that eat from the fruits of Paradise. Some of them are narrated on the authority of Ka’b bin Malik with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, as narrated by Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah. It was narrated that the souls of the martyrs are in the form of white birds, as narrated by Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Qatada, who said: It has reached us, and he mentioned that. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir also narrated it on his authority in a similar manner. It was narrated that they are in the form of green birds, as narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab al-Iman on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Ba’th wa al-Nushur on the authority of Ka’b. It was narrated by Hanad ibn Yasra on the authority of Hudhayl. It was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding his statement: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger, he said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We will surely test you 1:13, he said: God informed the believers that this world is a place of trial and that He will test them in it, and He commanded them to be patient and gave them good report, saying: And give good report to the patient. And He informed that if the believer submits to the command of God and returns and seeks refuge in God when a calamity befalls him, God will write for him three good qualities: prayers from God, mercy, and an easing of the path of guidance. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever seeks refuge in God when a calamity befalls him, God will compensate for his calamity, make his end good, and provide him with a righteous successor whom He will be pleased with. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Raja bin Haywah regarding his statement: And a decrease in fruits, he said: A time will come upon the people when the palm tree will bear nothing but dates. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My nation has been given something that no other nation has been given, which is to say when a calamity befalls them: ‘To God we belong and to Him we shall return.’” Many hadiths have been narrated about the virtue of seeking God’s help when a calamity befalls them.
2:158: Origin 158- Al-Safa in the language: smooth stone, and here it is a name for a well-known mountain in Mecca, and likewise Al-Marwah is a name for a well-known mountain in Mecca, and its origin in the language: one of the marwa, and they are the small stones that are soft. And it was said: those that are hard, and it was said: it includes everyone. Abu Dhu'ayb said: As if I am a Marwa, a clear, shining star, knocking every day for the events. It was said: They are the shiny white stones. It was also said: They are the black stones. The rituals are the plural of ritual, which is the sign: that is, one of the signs of His rituals. What is meant by it are the places of worship that God has made known to the people regarding the standing, the running, and the slaughtering. From this is the notifying of the sacrificial animal: that is, informing it by sticking an iron rod into its hump. From this is the saying of Al-Kumait: We kill them generation by generation. You see them as ritual sacrifices through which people draw near. Hajj in the language means: intending to visit the House, and from this comes the poet’s saying: I witness many obstacles from Awf who resort to cursing the saffron-colored Al-Zubayr. And the curse: the turban. In Islamic law: performing the Hajj rituals that God the Almighty has prescribed. Umrah in the language: the visit. In Islamic law: performing the known ritual in the fixed manner. The wing is originally from the word januh, which means inclination, and from it the wings due to their crookedness. And his saying: to circumambulate its origin is to circumambulate and it was assimilated. And it was read: that he circumambulates, and raising the wing indicates that it is not obligatory, and Abu Hanifa and his companions and al-Thawri said the same. Al-Zamakhshari narrated in Al-Kashshaf on the authority of Abu Hanifa that he says: It is obligatory and not a pillar, and there is a blood sacrifice for the one who abandons it. Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Anas bin Malik and Ibn Sirin have said that it is not obligatory. What strengthens the evidence of this verse for the non-existence is the Almighty’s statement at the end of the verse: And whoever volunteers good - then indeed, God is appreciative and Knowing. The majority of scholars are of the view that the Sa’i is obligatory and a ritual among the rituals, and they provided evidence for this with what the two sheikhs and others narrated on the authority of Aisha that Urwah said to her: Have you seen the statement of God: “Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs ‘Umrah - there is no blame upon him for walking between them.” So I do not see any blame upon anyone for not walking between them? Aisha said: What a bad thing you have said, my nephew! If it had been as I interpreted it, then there would have been no blame on him for not circumambulating them. However, it was revealed because the Ansar, before they converted to Islam, used to perform the ritual of pilgrimage to the tyrant Manat, which they used to worship. Some of those who worshipped it were reluctant to circumambulate Safa and Marwa in the pre-Islamic era, so God revealed: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God (al-Baqarah 2:14). Aisha said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained circumambulating them, so no one should neglect circumambulating them. Muslim and others narrated on her authority that she said: By my life, God does not complete the Hajj of one who does not walk between Safa and Marwa, nor his Umrah, because God said: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked and he said: God has prescribed for you the act of walking, so walk. Ahmad included in his chain of transmission, as did Ash-Shafi’i, Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Qani’ and Al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Habeeba bint Abi Tajra’a, who said: “I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performing Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and the people were in front of him, and he was running behind them until I could see his knees from the intensity of his running, his garment circling around him and he was saying: Run, for God, the Almighty, has prescribed running for you.” It is in Musnad Ahmad on the authority of his Sheikh Abdullah bin Al-Mu’ammil on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah on the authority of Safiyya bint Shaibah on her authority. He narrated it on another authority on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq. Mu’ammar informed us on the authority of Wasil, the freed slave of Abu Uyaynah, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaydah on the authority of Safiyya bint Shaibah, that a woman informed her and she mentioned it. This is supported by the hadith: Learn your rituals from me.
2:159: His saying: 159- Indeed, those who conceal to the end of the verse, in it is the report that the one who conceals that is cursed - and they differed about who is meant by that? It was said: The Jewish rabbis and Christian monks who concealed the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: Everyone who concealed the truth and failed to explain what God made it obligatory to explain, and this is the most correct because the consideration is based on the generality of the wording and not on the specificity of the reason as established in the principles. So assuming that the reason for revelation was what the Jews and Christians did in concealing, this does not contradict this verse including everyone who concealed the truth. And in this verse there is a severe threat that cannot be estimated, for whoever God curses and whoever among His servants is cursed by Him has reached a level of misery and loss that cannot be reached or understood. In his saying: Of the clear proofs and guidance is evidence that it is permissible to conceal other than that, as Abu Hurairah said: “I memorized two vessels from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: As for one of them, I spread it, and as for the other, if I spread it, this throat would be cut.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari.
