The pronoun in his saying: After We made it clear refers to what We revealed. The Book is a generic noun, and its definition indicates that it includes all books. It was said that what is meant by it is the Torah. Cursing is banishment and expulsion. What is meant by his saying: Those who curse are the angels and the believers, as stated by Al-Zajjaj and others, and Ibn Atiyyah preferred it. It was said: Everyone from whom cursing is possible, so this includes the jinn. It was said: They are insects and animals.
2:160: And His saying: 160- Except those who repent etc., in it is an exception for those who repent and reform their corrupted deeds, and clarifying to the people what God clarified in His books and on the tongues of His messengers.
2:161: His statement: 161- And they died while they were disbelievers. This sentence is a circumstantial one, and it has been used as evidence that it is not permissible to curse a specific disbeliever, because his condition at the time of death is not known. This does not contradict what has been proven from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he cursed a group of disbelievers specifically, because he knows through revelation what we do not know. It has been said that it is permissible to curse him based on the apparent state of affairs, just as it is permissible to fight him. His statement: Those are the ones upon whom is the curse of God etc., has been used as evidence that it is permissible to curse disbelievers in general. Al-Qurtubi said: There is no disagreement about that. He said: Cursing a disbeliever is not a way of deterring him from disbelief, rather it is a punishment for disbelief and showing the ugliness of his disbelief, whether the disbeliever was sane or insane. Some of the early Muslims said: There is no benefit in cursing those who have gone mad or died among them, neither as a punishment nor as a deterrent. He said: What is indicated by this statement is that the verse indicates that God, the angels and people are informing us of their curse, not as a command to do so. Ibn al-Arabi said: Cursing a specific sinner is not permissible by consensus, because it was narrated: “A person who had been drinking alcohol repeatedly was brought to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and some of those present said: ‘May God curse him, how much he drinks.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Do not help the devil against your brother.’” The hadeeth is in Saheeh al-Bukhari and Muslim. As for his statement: and all of the people, it was said: This is on the Day of Resurrection. As for in this world, it is among the people, the Muslim and the disbeliever, and those who know about sins and their sins and those who do not know. So cursing him cannot be done by all of the people. It was said: In this world, and what is meant is that most of the people curse him, or everyone among them who knows about his sins.
2:162: And His saying: 162- They will abide therein eternally meaning in the Fire, and it was said: in the curse. And the postponement: is the delay, and it was said: the meaning of they do not wait: God does not look at them, so it is from the look, and it was said: it is from the waiting: meaning they do not wait to apologize.
2:163: The interpretation of 163- The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful has been presented. His statement: And your God is one God contains guidance to monotheism and severing ties of polytheism, and an indication that the first thing that must be made clear and that it is forbidden to conceal is the matter of monotheism. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Muadh bin Jabal, the brother of Banu Salamah, Saad bin Muadh, the brother of Banu Al-Ashhal, and Kharijah bin Zaid, the brother of Banu Al-Harith bin Al-Khazraj, asked a group of Jewish rabbis about some of what was in the Torah, but they concealed it from them and refused to tell them. So God revealed about them: Indeed, those who conceal what We have revealed (al-Baqarah 2:17). It was narrated on the authority of a group of the Salaf that the verse was revealed about the People of the Book because they concealed the prophethood of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Majah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib that he said: “We were in a funeral procession with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘The unbeliever will be struck between his eyes and every beast of the two heavy burdens will hear him, and every beast that hears his voice will curse him. This is what God, the Most High, said: “And the cursers will curse them” (al-Baqarah 2:17) meaning the beasts of the earth. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ata’ that he said: The jinn, mankind and every beast. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Abu Nu`aym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu`ab al-Iman narrated in their interpretation of the verse: “The beasts of the earth, scorpions, and beetles say: ‘We were prevented from rain because of their sins,’ so they curse them.” Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Ikrimah. Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Abu Ja`far who said: Everything curses them, even the beetle. Many hadiths have been narrated about the prohibition of concealing knowledge and the threat to the one who does so. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah regarding the statement of God, Except those who repent and amend, he said: They amended what was between them and God, and made clear what came to them from God and did not conceal it or deny it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sa`id ibn Jubayr regarding the statement of God, I will forgive them, meaning I will pardon them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu al-`Aliyah who said: The disbeliever will be brought to the Day of Resurrection and God will curse him, then the angels will curse him, then all the people will curse him. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: He means by all people the believers. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding His statement: They will abide therein forever meaning: They will abide in Hell in the curse. He said regarding His statement: Nor will they be reprieved meaning: Will they not be reprieved so that they can apologize. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Nor will they be reprieved he said: They will not be delayed. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Darimi, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Asma bint Yazid bin Al-Sakn from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he said: “The greatest name of God is in these two verses: ‘And your God is one God; there is no god except Him, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful’ and ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. God - there is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence.’” Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Anas that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “There is nothing more difficult for the rebellious jinn than these verses in Surat al-Baqarah 2:‘And your God is one God’ and the two verses.”
2:164: When God, the Almighty, mentioned monotheism in His saying: And your God is one God, He followed that with the evidence indicating it, which is these matters that are among the greatest creations of the Wise Maker, with every rational person knowing that it is not possible for any of the gods that the disbelievers have established to refuse any of them, or to be able to do them or some of them, and they are the creation of the heavens, the creation of the earth, the alternation of night and day, the running of the ships in the sea, the sending down of rain from the sky, the revival of the earth by it, the spreading of animals from it because of it, and the control of the winds. Whoever looks deeply and applies his mind to one of them will be amazed by it, and his mind will be unable to imagine its reality. He is obliged to believe that its Creator is God, the Almighty. He only gathered the heavens together because they are different kinds, each heaven being of a different kind from the other, and He unified the earth because it is all of one kind, which is dust. What is meant by the alternation of night and day is their alternation with one coming and the other going away, one being illuminated and the other being dark. Day: the period between sunrise and sunset. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The beginning of the day is sunrise, and what comes before that is not counted as part of the day. Tha’lab said the same, and he cited as evidence the words of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: And the sun rises every last night red, its color turning rosy And so said Al-Zajjaj. Ibn Al-Anbari divided time into three parts: One part he made pure night, which is from sunset to dawn. One part he made pure day, which is from sunrise to sunset. And one part he made common between day and night, which is between sunrise and sunrise due to the remnants of the darkness of the night and the beginnings of the light of day. This is according to the terminology of the people of language. As for the Shari’ah, the discussion of this is well-known. The ark: ships, and its singular and plural are expressed in one word, which is this, and it is masculine and feminine. God the Almighty said: In the laden ark, 164- And the arks that sail in the sea, and He said: Until, when you are in the ark and they sail with them, and it was said: its singular is a falak with a fat-ha, like asad and asad. His saying: that which benefits people may be a relative pronoun, meaning that which benefits them, or a verbal noun, meaning that which benefits them. What is meant by what He sent down from the sky is the rain by which the world lives and plants and provisions come out. And spreading means spreading. It appears that his saying spread is conjoined with his saying so He revived because they are two matters caused by the sending down of rain. He said in Al-Kashshaf: The apparent meaning is its conjoining with sent down. What is meant by the winds' direction is sending them barren, fertile, abundant, victorious, destructive, hot, cold, soft and stormy. It was said that their direction is sending them south, north, west, pouring and calamity, which comes between the blowing winds. It was said that their direction is that the large ships come according to what they can carry, and the small ones do the same. There is nothing to prevent the direction from being applied to all of what was mentioned. The cloud is called a cloud because it withdraws in the air. I dragged my tails with a drag and someone dragged someone on someone: he dared. And the one who is subdued: the one who is tamed, and to subjugate him: to send him from one place to another, and it was said that his subjugation: is his being fixed between the sky and the earth without pillars or connections. The first is more apparent. And the verses are evidence of His Oneness, glory be to Him, for whoever looks with his sight and thinks with his mind. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Quraysh said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Ask God to turn Safa into gold for us so that we may gain strength against our enemy. God revealed to him: I will give them, so I will turn Safa into gold for them, but if they disbelieve after that, I will punish them with a punishment such as I have not punished anyone in the worlds. He said: My Lord, leave me and my people alone so that I may call them day by day. So God revealed this verse. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr. Wakee’, Al-Firyabi, Adam ibn Abi Iyas, Saeed ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Duha who said: When the verse And your god is one God was revealed, the polytheists were amazed and said: Muhammad says And your god is one God. So let him bring us a sign if he is truthful. So God revealed: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth 10:13. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ata. Abu al-Shaykh narrated in al-Azmah on the authority of Sulayman who said: The night is entrusted to an angel called Sharaheel. When the time of night comes, he takes a black bead and hangs it from the direction of the west. When the sun looks at it, it sets faster than the blink of an eye. The sun has been ordered not to set until it sees the bead. When it sets, night comes and the bead remains hanging until another angel called Haraheel comes with a white bead and hangs it from the direction of the rising sun. When Sharaheel sees it, he extends his bead to it, and the sun sees the white bead and rises. It has been ordered not to rise until it sees it. When it rises, day comes. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: and the ark, he said: the ship. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: Bath means creation. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And the direction of the winds, he said: If He wills, He makes them a mercy that fertilizes the clouds, and a good tiding before His mercy. And if He wills, He makes them a torment, a barren wind that does not fertilize. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b who said: Everything in the Qur’an about winds is a mercy, and everything in the Qur’an about winds is a torment. Many hadiths have been narrated about the prohibition of cursing the wind and describing it that have no connection to the verse.
2:165: When He, the Almighty, finished proving His Oneness, He informed us that along with this clear and useful proof of His great authority, His great power and His uniqueness in creation, He found among the people those who would take with Him, the Almighty, a rival to worship from among the idols. The explanation of rivals has been presented, although these infidels did not limit themselves to merely worshipping rivals, but rather loved them with a great love and went to extremes in that, until their love for these idols and the like became firmly rooted in their hearts like the believers’ love for God, the Almighty. So the source in His statement: 165- like the love of God is added to the object, and the subject is omitted, which is the believers. It is possible that what is meant by like their love for God is: idol worshippers, as Ibn Kaysan and Al-Zajjaj said. It is possible that this source is from the passive voice: meaning as God loves. The first is more appropriate because of his saying: And those who believe are stronger in love for God, for it is a correction of what the simile indicates of equality: that is, the love of the believers for God is stronger than the love of the disbelievers for rivals, because the believers single out God, the Most High, in worship and supplication, and the disbelievers do not single out their idols for that, rather they associate God with them, and they acknowledge that they only worship their idols to bring them closer to God. This can be made: I mean his saying: And those who believe are stronger in love for God, as evidence for the second, because the believers were stronger in love for God, the love of the disbelievers for rivals was not like the love of the believers for God. It was said: What is meant by rivals here are the leaders: that is, they obey them in disobeying God. This pronoun is strengthened in their saying: They love them, for it is for those who understand. It is also strengthened by his saying, the Most High, after that: When those who followed disavowed themselves 1:13. His saying: And if those who did wrong could see is the reading of the people of Mecca, Kufa, and Abu Amr with the lower ya’, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid. The people of Medina and the people of Ash-Sham read it with the superiority, and the meaning according to the first reading: If those who did wrong in this world could see the punishment of the Hereafter, they would know when they see it that all power belongs to God. Abu Ubaid said. An-Nahhas said: This is the statement that the people of interpretation hold. End quote. Based on this, the vision is the visual one, not the heart. It was narrated from Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Mubarrad that he said: This interpretation that Abu Ubaid came up with is far-fetched, and his expression is not good, because he estimates: If those who did wrong could see the punishment, so it is as if he makes it doubtful. God has made it obligatory, but the estimate, which is better, is: If those who did wrong could see that all power belongs to God. And seeing means knowing: that is, if they knew the reality of God’s power and the severity of His punishment. He said: The answer to if is omitted: that is, so that they may realize the harm of their taking gods, as was omitted in His statement: And if you could but see when they are made to stand before their Lord. And whoever reads with the superiority, the estimate is: If you could see, O Muhammad, those who did wrong when they see the punishment and are terrified by it, you would know that all power belongs to God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew this, but he was addressed with this address, and what was meant by it was his nation. It was said: that is in the position of an accusative object for which: meaning because power belongs to God, as the poet said: Forgive the generous person’s shortcomings and turn away from the slander of the ignoble person out of generosity. That is, to save it, and the meaning is: And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who did wrong when they see the punishment, because power belongs to God, you would know the extent of their punishment. And when was included, and it is for what has passed in proving these future events, to approximate the matter and to correct its occurrence. Ibn Amir read when they see with a damma on the ya’, and the rest with a fatha on it. Al-Hasan, Ya’qub, and Abu Ja’far read that the power and that God with a kasra on the hamza in both of them as a resumption, and as an estimate of the saying.
2:166: His statement: 166- When those who followed disavowed themselves instead of his statement: When they see the punishment and its meaning is: that the masters and leaders disavowed those who followed them in disbelief. And his statement: And they saw the punishment is in the accusative case as a state: meaning the followers and the followed. It was said: when witnessing in this world, and it was said: when being presented and questioned in the Hereafter. And it can be said for both of them as there is no objection to that. His statement: And their causes were cut off is the plural of cause, and its origin in the language is: the rope with which something is tied and pulled, then everything that pulled something was made a cause, and what is meant by it is: the connection by which they used to communicate in this world from kinship and other things, and it was said: it is deeds.
2:167: And the ball: the return and the return to a state that had been, and if here it is in the meaning of a wish as if it was said: If only we had a chance, and that is why the fa was in the answer. The meaning is: The followers said: If only we were returned to the world so that we could do good deeds and disown them as they disowned us. And the kaf in his saying: 167- As they disowned us is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source, and it was said: In the accusative case as a state, but I do not see it as correct. And his saying: Thus does God show them is in the nominative case: meaning the matter is thus: meaning as God showed them the punishment, He shows them their deeds, and if this vision is visual, then his saying: regrets is in the accusative case as a state, and if it is the tribe, then it is the third object, and the meaning is: That God shows them their corrupt deeds and they are regrets for them, or He shows them the righteous deeds that He made obligatory upon them and they abandoned them and that is regret for them. His saying: And they will not come out of the Fire is evidence of the eternal existence of the infidels in the Fire. The apparent meaning of this construction indicates exclusivity, and Al-Zamakhshari made it for emphasis for a purpose of his that goes back to the school of thought, and research into this would take a long time. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And of mankind are those who take for themselves rivals to God, he said: To show off and harm the truth with rivals. And those who believe are stronger in love for God, he said: than the disbelievers for their gods. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Zaid regarding this verse, he said: These polytheists, their rivals are their gods whom they worshipped along with God, they love them as those who believe love God. And those who believe are stronger in love for God, than their love for their gods. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: The rivals among men obey them as they obey God. If they command them, they obey them and disobey God. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar to what Ibn Zaid said. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Az-Zubairi regarding his statement: And if those who did wrong could see, he said: And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who wronged themselves and took for themselves rivals besides Me whom they love as you love Me when they witness My punishment on the Day of Resurrection which I have prepared for them, you would know that all power is Mine, not rivals, and the gods will not avail them at all there nor will they ward off from them the punishment that I have inflicted upon them, and I have made them certain that My punishment is severe for whoever disbelieves in Me and claims with Me a god other than Me. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: When those who followed disassociate themselves, he said: They are the tyrants, leaders and chiefs in polytheism. From those who followed, he said: They are the devils who disassociated themselves from mankind. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And ties have been severed for them, he said: Love. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: They are the dwelling places. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: They are the wombs. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilya narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: It is the bonds that were between them in this world and the love. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Abu Salih who said: It is the deeds. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi' who said: It is the dwellings. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: If only we had another chance he said: A return to this world. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding his statement: Regrets he said: Their evil deeds will become a regret for them on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: And they will never get out of the Fire he said: Those are its people who are its people. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Thabit bin Ma'bad who said: The people of the Fire continued to hope to get out of it until the verse And they will never get out of the Fire was revealed.
2:168: His saying: 168- O people It was said: It was revealed about Thaqeef, Khuza'ah and Banu Mudlij regarding the livestock they forbade themselves. Al-Qurtubi narrated it in his interpretation, but the consideration is the generality of the wording and not the specificity of the reason. And his saying: Halal is an object or a state, and the lawful was called lawful because the knot of prohibition was dissolved from it. And the good here is the pleasant as Al-Shafi'i and others said. Malik and others said: It is the lawful, so it is an emphasis on his saying: Halal. And the min in his saying: from what is on earth is for the partiality to definite that on earth there is what is forbidden Khatawat is the plural of Khatwa with the fatha and damma, and it is with the fatha for the time, and with the damma for what is between the feet. The reciters read Khatu'at with the fatha of the kha, and Abu Samak read with the fatha of the kha and the ta, and Ali, Qatadah, Al-A'raj, Amr bin Maymun and Al-A'mash read Khatu'at with the damma of the kha and the ta and the hamza on the waw. Al-Akhfash said: They went with this reading to the fact that it is the plural of khatīyah from khatū, not from khatū. Al-Jawhari said: The khatwa with the fathah means one time, and the plural is khatāt and khatā. The meaning according to the reading of the majority is: Do not follow the traces of Satan and his work, and everything that is not mentioned in the Shari’ah is attributed to Satan. It was said: It is vows and sins, and it is better to generalize and not to specify an individual or type. His statement: Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy means apparent enmity, and similar to it is the statement of the Most High: Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy and His statement: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.
2:169: And his saying: 169- With evil Evil is called evil because it makes its owner bad with the bad outcome, and it is the source of sa’ahu which means it makes him sad. And obscenity is originally bad sight, and from it the poet said: Good as the good of the womb is not obscene Then it was used in ugly meanings. It was said: evil: ugly, and obscenity: exceeding the limit in ugliness. It was said: evil: what has no limit, and obscenity: what has a limit. It was said: obscenity: adultery. It was said: everything that the Shariah forbade is obscenity. And His statement: And that you say about God what you do not know Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: He means what they forbade from the bahīrah and the sā'ibah and the like of them which they made a law. It was said: It is their saying this is permissible and this is forbidden without knowledge. And it appears that it is true for everything that was mentioned in the Shariah without knowledge. And in this verse is evidence that everything that has no text or apparent meaning from the objects found on earth is originally permissible until evidence is presented that requires its prohibition. And the clearest evidence of that from this verse is the statement of God the Most High: It is He who created for you whatever is on the earth.
2:170: The pronoun in His statement: 170- And when it is said to them refers to the people, because the infidels are among them and they are the ones meant here, and it was said: the infidels of the Arabs in particular, and we found means we found, and the alif in His statement: Or if their fathers had been is for interrogation, and the waw is opened because it is the waw of conjunction. In this verse there is blame for the imitators and the call for their blatant ignorance and corrupt belief that cannot be estimated, and similar to this verse is the statement of God Almighty: And when it is said to them, Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger, they say, Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers" (Al-Quran 2:170). In that is evidence of the ugliness of imitation and the prohibition of it, and research into that would take a long time. I have devoted an independent book to it and called it [Al-Qawl Al-Mufid: On the Ruling of Imitation] and I have discussed it in detail in [Adab Al-Talab and Muntaha Al-Arab].
2:171: And His statement: 171- And the example of those who disbelieve is like that of one who calls out to the heavens and the earth in it is a comparison of the preacher of the disbelievers and their caller, who is Muhammad, peace be upon him, to a shepherd who calls out to the sheep or camels, but he hears nothing but a call and a cry and does not understand what he is saying. This was explained by Al-Zajjaj, Al-Farraa, and Sibawayh, and a group of the Salaf said the same. Sibawayh said: They did not liken him to the one who calls out to the one who is being called out to, and the meaning is: Your example, O Muhammad, and the example of those who disbelieve, is like the one who calls out to the one who is being called out to, from the animals that do not understand, so it was deleted because the meaning indicates it. Qatrib said: The meaning is the example of those who disbelieved in their calling to what is not understood, meaning idols, is like the example of a shepherd who calls out to his sheep and he does not know where they are, and Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari said the same. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is: The example of those who disbelieved in their supplication to inanimate deities is like that of a caller in the dead of night who is answered by an echo. He calls out to something that cannot be heard, and it answers him with something that has no truth in it. And bleating is driving sheep and shouting at them. It is said: The shepherd bleated to his sheep, bleating and bleating, meaning he shouted at them and drove them away. The Arabs use the example of a shepherd of sheep as an example of ignorance and say: More ignorant than a shepherd of sheep. His saying: deaf and what follows are predicates of an omitted subject: meaning they are deaf, dumb and blind. The explanation of that has been presented above. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “This verse was recited to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), meaning: ‘O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth that is lawful and good. ’ Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, pray to God to make my supplication answered. ’ He said: ‘O Sa’d, make your food pure and your supplication will be answered. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, a man may put a morsel of unlawful food into his stomach and it will not be accepted from him for forty days. As for any servant whose flesh grows from unlawful earnings and usury, the Fire is more deserving of him. ’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And do not follow the footsteps of Satan, he said: His deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Whatever contradicts the Qur’an is from the footsteps of Satan. Abd ibn Hamid ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: His footsteps. They also narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: They are the temptations of Satan. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr who said: They are the adornments of Satan. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: Every disobedience to God is from the footsteps of Satan. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Any oath or vow made in anger is from the footsteps of Satan, and its expiation is the expiation of an oath. Abd al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Masoud that a sheep and salt were brought to him and he started eating, so a man from the people withdrew, so Ibn Masoud said: Give it to your companion, so he said: I do not want to, so he said: Are you fasting? He said: No. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: I have forbidden myself to eat sheep, so Ibn Masoud said: This is from the footsteps of Satan, so eat and expiate for your oath. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Ghiyath who said: I asked Jabir bin Zaid about a man who vowed to put a gold ring in his nose, so he said: This is from the footsteps of Satan and he will continue to disobey God, so let him expiate for his oath. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of al-Hasan that he considered the oath of someone who swore to perform Hajj crawling to be from the footsteps of Satan. And Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abu Majlaz who said: They are vows to commit sins. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: He only orders you to do evil he said: sin and immorality he said: adultery. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Jews to Islam and encouraged them to do so, and warned them of the punishment and vengeance of God. Then Rafi bin Kharijah and Malik bin Awf said to him: Rather, we will follow, O Muhammad, what we found our fathers doing, for they were more knowledgeable and better than us. So God revealed regarding that: And when it is said to them, ‘Follow what God has revealed,’ they say, ‘Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.’ Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ and Qatadah regarding his statement: We found they said: We found. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the parable of those who disbelieve the verse, he said: It is like the parable of the cow, the donkey, and the sheep. If you say something to some of them, they do not understand what you are saying, but they hear your voice. Likewise, if you command a disbeliever to do good or forbid him from evil, or admonish him, he does not understand what you are saying, but he hears your voice. Something similar to that was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, narrated by Abd ibn Humayd, and on the authority of Ikrimah, narrated by Wakee’. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata’ said to me regarding this verse: They are the Jews about whom God revealed: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book until His statement: How patient they are toward the Fire.
2:172: His statement: 172- Eat from the good things with which We have provided you. This is an emphasis on the first command: I mean His statement: O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth [that is] lawful and good. He only singled out the believers here because they are the best kind of people. It was said: What is meant by eating is benefit, and it was said: What is meant by it is regular eating, and this is the apparent meaning. His statement: And be grateful to God. It was previously mentioned that it is said to thank Him and to thank Him is transitive by itself and by the preposition. And His statement: If it is Him that you worship, meaning that you single Him out for worship, as is indicated by the precedence of the object.
2:173: His saying: 173- He has only forbidden you dead animals. Abu Ja'far read haram in the passive form, and innama is a word used for limitation, confirming what the speech includes and negating what is other than it. Here, I have limited the prohibition to the matters mentioned after it. His saying: dead animals. Ibn Ubla read it in the nominative case, and the reason for that is that it makes what is in innama a separate relative pronoun in writing, and dead animals and what follows it the predicate of the relative pronoun, and everyone reads it in the accusative case. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa' read dead animals with a shaddah on the ya, and linguists have mentioned that it is permissible to make both the light and heavy dead animals. Dead animals are those from which the soul has departed without slaughter. This generality has been made specific by a hadith such as Lawful for us are two dead animals and two types of blood. It was narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Majah, Ad-Daraqutni, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and similar to the hadeeth of Jabir about ambergris, which is proven in the Two Saheehs with the statement of God, the Most High: Lawful to you is game from the sea. What is meant by dead animals here is dead animals from the land, not from the sea. Most scholars have permitted eating all sea animals, alive or dead. Some scholars have said that what is forbidden from sea animals is similar to what is forbidden on land. Ibn Habeeb hesitated regarding the capybara. Ibn Al-Qasim said: I avoid it and do not see it as forbidden. His statement: and blood The scholars have agreed that blood is forbidden. In another verse: or blood poured forth, so the general meaning is interpreted according to the specific, because what is mixed with meat is not forbidden. Al-Qurtubi said: By consensus. Aisha narrated that she used to cook meat and the yellowish color would appear on the pot from the blood, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would eat that and not disapprove of it. His saying: and the flesh of swine The apparent meaning of this verse and the other verse, I mean the saying of God Almighty: “Say: I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it, unless it be a dead animal or blood poured forth or the flesh of swine” is that what is forbidden is only the meat. The nation has unanimously agreed on the prohibition of its fat, as Al-Qurtubi narrated in his interpretation. A group of scholars have mentioned that the meat includes fat. Al-Qurtubi also narrated the consensus that the whole of the pig is forbidden except for hair, as it is permissible to sew it. His saying: and that which is dedicated to other than God Ihlal means raising the voice. It is said that he dedicated something to something: meaning he raised his voice. The poet said, describing a desert: Its riders arrive at Al-Farqad, just as a pilgrim arrives for Umrah. Al-Nabigha said: Or a pearl shell, its diver is delighted, whenever he sees it he bows down and prostrates himself And from it is the infant’s ihlāl and istihlāhu: which is his cry at birth. What is meant here is: what is mentioned in the name of other than God, such as al-Lat and al-‘Uzza if the slaughterer is a pagan, and fire if the slaughterer is a Zoroastrian. There is no disagreement in the prohibition of this and similar things, and similar to it is what is done by those who believe in the dead by slaughtering on their graves, because it is something that is dedicated to other than God, and there is no difference between it and slaughtering for an idol. His statement, But whoever is forced was read with a damma on the noon for the sake of following and with a kasra on the basis of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and in it is an implication: that is, whoever is forced to do any of these forbidden things. Ibn Muhaysin read with the assimilation of the dad into the ta’. Abu al-Sammak read with a kasra on the ta’. What is meant by whoever made him is hunger and poverty leading him to be forced to eat dead meat. His statement, not desiring is an accusative in the state. It was said that what is meant by the aggressor is the one who eats more than he needs, and the ordinary is the one who eats these forbidden things while he finds an alternative to them. It was also said that he is not an aggressor against the Muslims and transgresses against them, so the aggressor and the ordinary include highway robbers, those who rebel against the ruler, those who sever family ties, and the like. It was also said that what is meant is not one who transgresses against another in need, nor one who transgresses to satisfy the hunger of one who is in need. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: Eat from the good things with which We have provided you, he said: From the lawful. Ibn Saad narrated on the authority of Umar bin Al-Aziz that what is meant by the verse is: good earnings, not good food. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: that it is lawful sustenance. Ahmad, Muslim, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God is good and does not accept anything but that which is good. God commanded the believers with what He commanded the Messengers, saying: ‘O Messengers, eat from the good things and work righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing.’ And He said: ‘O you who have believed, eat from the good things with which We have provided you.’ Then he mentioned a man who has traveled a long way, disheveled and covered in dust, stretching his hands to the sky, saying: O Lord, O Lord, while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with unlawful things. So how can his supplication be answered?” Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And what he slaughtered, he said: Slaughtered. Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said: What is dedicated to the tyrants. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid that he said: What is slaughtered for other than God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Al-Aaliyah that he said: What is mentioned in the name of other than God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Neither transgressing nor exceeding the limits he said: Whoever eats something of this while he is compelled, there is no blame on him, but whoever eats it while he is not compelled has transgressed and transgressed. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: Neither transgressing nor exceeding the limits he said: Regarding dead meat. Neither exceeding the limits he said: Regarding eating. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hameed, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: Neither transgressing nor exceeding the limits he said: Not transgressing against the Muslims nor exceeding the limits against them. So whoever goes out to sever family ties or block the way or spread corruption on earth or separates from the community and the imams, or goes out in disobedience to God and is compelled to eat dead meat, it is not permissible for him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Saeed bin Jubayr that he said: The one who cuts off the road. His statement: There is no sin upon him means in eating it. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful to whoever eats from what is forbidden, He is Merciful to him because He made what is forbidden permissible for him out of necessity. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada: But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limits] not desiring in his eating, nor transgressing beyond what is permissible to what is forbidden, and he finds a way out and alternative.
2:174: His saying: 174- "Indeed, those who conceal" It was said: What is meant by this verse are the Jewish scholars, because they concealed what God revealed in the Torah about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And purchasing here: replacement, and its investigation has been presented, and he called it little because its duration was cut off and its consequences were bad, and this reason, although it was purely considered in the generality of the wording, includes everyone who concealed what God legislated, and took bribes for it, and mentioning heroism is an indication and confirmation that this eating is real, since it may be used metaphorically in something like someone eating something on the ground and the like. And he said in Al-Kashshaf: The meaning of "in their bellies" He said: He says: So-and-so ate in his stomach, and he ate in some of his stomach. End. His statement: except the Fire means that He will punish them with the Fire, so He called what they ate Fire because it will lead them to it, this is what most of the commentators said. It was said that they will be punished for their concealment by eating the Fire in Hell in reality. Similar to this is His statement, the Most High: Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire. His statement, and God will not speak to them is a metaphor for the descent of God’s wrath upon them and His displeasure with them. It is said: So-and-so does not speak to so-and-so if he is angry with him. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: The meaning is that He will not speak to them for what they love, not for what they hate. Like His statement, the Most High: Be gone therein, and do not speak to them. His statement, He will not purify them means that He will not speak well of them. Al-Zajjaj said: It was said that its meaning is that He will not rectify their evil deeds and purify them.
2:175: And his saying: 175- They purchased error in exchange for guidance its meaning has already been explained. And his saying: How patient they are with the Fire the majority, including Al-Hasan and Mujahid, said that its meaning is astonishment. What is meant is the astonishment of the creatures at the state of those who directly dealt with the causes of the torment of the Fire, as if by this dealing with the causes they were patient with the punishment in the Fire of Hell. Al-Zajjaj narrated that the meaning is: What kept them in the Fire, from their saying: How patient so-and-so is with imprisonment: meaning what kept him in it. And it was said that the meaning is: How little their anxiety about the Fire is, so he made little anxiety patience. Al-Kisa'i and Qutrub said: Meaning how persistent they are in the work of the people of the Fire. And it was said: What is an interrogative, and its meaning is a rebuke: meaning what made them patient with the work of the Fire. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Al-Suddi, Ata' and Abu Ubaidah.
2:176: 176- That is because God has sent down the Book with the truth. The reference with the demonstrative pronoun to the command: that is, that command, which is the punishment. This was said by Al-Zajjaj. Al-Akhfash said: The predicate of the demonstrative pronoun is omitted, and the meaning is: that is known. What is meant by the Book here is the Qur’an with the truth, that is, with honesty, and it was said: with proof. And His statement: And those who differed over the Book It was said: What is meant by the Book here is the Torah, so the Christians claimed that it contains the description of Jesus, and the Jews denied them, and it was said: They contradicted what was in the Torah about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they differed over it, and it was said: What is meant by the Qur’an, and those who differed are the infidels of Quraysh, some of them say: it is magic, and some of them say: it is legends of the ancients, and some of them say otherwise. In discord, that is, disagreement far from the truth, and the meaning of discord has been presented. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed he said: It was revealed about the Jews. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: They concealed the name of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and took it out of a little greed. Ibn Jarir also narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah something similar. Al-Tha’labi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with two weak chains of narration that it was revealed about the Jews. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding his statement: Those are the ones who have purchased error at the price of guidance he said: They chose error over guidance and torment over forgiveness. How patient they are for the Fire he said: How bold they are to commit the deeds of the Fire. Sa’id bin Mansour, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: How patient they are for the Fire he said: How knowledgeable they are about the deeds of the people of the Fire. Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his statement: How patient they are for the Fire he said: By God, they have no patience for it, but he says: How bold they are for the Fire. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Qatada. Ibn Jarir also narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: This is in the form of a question, he says: What made them endure the Fire? And His statement: And indeed, those who differ over the Scripture he said: They are the Jews and Christians are in extreme dissension he said: In extreme enmity.
2:177: His saying: 177- Righteousness Hamzah and Hafs read it in the accusative case as the predicate of not and the subject that you turn away and the rest read it in the nominative case as the subject. It was said: This verse was revealed to respond to the Jews and Christians, when they spoke a lot about the matter of the Qiblah when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to the Kaaba. It was said: The reason for its revelation was that a questioner asked the Messenger of God, and this will come at the end of the discussion, God willing. And His saying: Before the East and the West It was said: The Almighty referred by mentioning the East to the Qiblah of the Christians because they face the rising of the sun, and He referred by mentioning the West to the Qiblah of the Jews because they face the Holy House, which was in the direction of the West at that time. And His saying: But righteousness is a comprehensive name for good, and its predicate is omitted, meaning: righteousness of he who believes. Al-Farra’, Qatrub and Al-Zajjaj said: It was said that the estimation is: But the righteous is he who believes. The reason for this estimation is: fleeing from informing with the name of the eye about the name of the meaning. It is permissible for righteousness to mean righteous, and the source is often used for the active participle. From this in the revelation: If your water becomes sunken meaning sunken, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaidah. What is meant by the book here is the genus or the Qur’an, and the pronoun in his statement: for His love refers to the money. It was said: It refers to the giving indicated by his statement: and he gave the money. It was said: It refers to God, the Exalted: that is, for the love of God. The meaning according to the first is: He gave the money while he loved it and was stingy with it. From this is His statement, the Exalted: You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. The meaning according to the second is: He loves giving money and his soul is pleased with it. The meaning according to the third is: He gave to the one included in the verse in the love of God, the Exalted, not for another purpose. It is like his statement: And they feed the poor in spite of their love for Him. And similar to it is the statement of Zuhair: The generous man, despite his faults, is a pyramid. And relatives are given priority because giving them money is charity and maintaining ties of kinship if they are poor. Thus, poor orphans are more deserving of charity than the poor who are not orphans, because of their inability to earn. And the needy: the one who resides in what is in people’s hands because he cannot find anything. And the wayfarer is the stranded traveler and he was made a wayfarer because he stays with him. And his saying: and for freeing slaves means in helping the slaves whose owners have written to them. And it was said: what is meant is buying slaves and freeing them. And it was said: what is meant is freeing captives. And his saying: and give zakat is evidence that the previous giving is voluntary charity, not obligatory charity. And his saying: and those who fulfill it was said: it is conjoined with those who believe, as if it was said: but righteousness is the believers and those who fulfill. Al-Farra and Al-Akhfash said it. It was said: It is raised as a subject, and the predicate is omitted. It was said: It is for a deleted subject: i.e. they are the ones who fulfill. It was said: It is conjoined with the pronoun in believed. Abu Ali denied it and said: The meaning is not on it. His saying: and the patient is accusative as a compliment like the saying of God Almighty: and those who establish prayer. And from it is what Abu Ubaidah recited: They do not distance my people who are the poison of enmity and the scourge of the islands Those who fight in every battle and are good in every way Al-Kisa'i said: It is connected to the relatives as if he said: And give to the patient ones. An-Nahhas said: It is a mistake. Al-Kisa'i said: It is the reading of Abdullah: And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made a covenant and the patient ones. An-Nahhas said: According to this reading, they would be connected to the relatives or to praise. Ya'qub and Al-A'mash read And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made a covenant and the patient ones with the nominative in both of them. Al-Basa' means hardship and poverty. Al-Dira' means sickness and time. And in the time of battle It was said that what is meant is the time of war, and Al-Basa' and Al-Dira' are two nouns built on Fa'alaa and do not have a verb because they are nouns and not descriptions. And his saying: They were truthful describes them as truthful and pious in their affairs and fulfilling them and that they were serious. It was said that what is meant is that they were truthful to them in battle, but the first is more appropriate. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abu Dharr that he asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) about faith, so he recited: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces until he finished it, then he asked him again and he recited it, then he asked him and he recited it. He said: If you do a good deed, your heart will love it, and if you do a bad deed, your heart will hate it. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abd Al-Rahman, who said: A man came to Abu Dharr and said: What is faith? So he recited this verse to him, then he mentioned to him something similar to the previous hadith. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: He says: Righteousness is not that you pray and you do not teach, this was when he moved from Mecca to Medina and the obligatory duties were revealed. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: This verse was revealed in Medina, it says: Righteousness is not that you pray, but righteousness is that which is established in the heart of obedience to God. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a man asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) about righteousness, so God revealed: Righteousness is not… And Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: The Jews used to pray before sunset and the Christians before the east, so righteousness is not the verse was revealed. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah. And Abd al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, he said: He gives while he is healthy and stingy, hoping for a living and fearing poverty. And he narrated something similar on his authority from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Shu’ab on the authority of al-Muttalib, "It was said: O Messenger of God, he does not give wealth out of love for it, for we all love it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You give it when you give it, and your soul speaks to you of long life and poverty." And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr regarding his statement: and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, meaning out of love for money. And he also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: those of kin, meaning his relatives. It was reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Charity given to a poor person is charity, and to a relative it is two things: charity and upholding the ties of kinship.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan from the hadeeth of Salman ibn ‘Aamir al-Dhabi. In the two Sahihs and others, from the hadeeth of Zaynab, the wife of Ibn Mas’ood, “that she asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) if spending on her husband and orphans in her care would suffice as charity on her behalf?” He said: “You will have two rewards: the reward of charity and the reward of kinship.” At-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Umm Kulthum bint ‘Uqbah that she heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: The best charity is given to a relative who is estranged. Ahmad, al-Darimi and at-Tabarani narrated something similar from the hadeeth of Hakim ibn Hizam from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas that he said: The wayfarer is the guest who stays with the Muslims. Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid that he said: He is the one who passes by you while he is travelling. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: And those who ask, he said: The one who asks you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: And for the freeing of slaves, he said: It means freeing slaves. He also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And establishes prayer, meaning and completes the prescribed prayer, And gives zakat, meaning the obligatory zakat. At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Adi, Ad-Daraqutni, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Fatimah bint Qais who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is a right in wealth other than zakat, then he recited: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces, the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding his statement: And those who fulfill their covenant, he said: Whoever gives a covenant to God and then breaks it, God will take revenge on him, and whoever gives the protection of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then betrays it, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is his opponent. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: And those who fulfill their covenant when they make a covenant, meaning between themselves and the people. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding the verse, he said: Al-Basa` means poverty, Al-Dara` means sickness, and The time of battle means during fighting. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr regarding the statement: Those are the ones who have been truthful, he said: They did what God mentioned in this verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Rabi` regarding the statement: Those are the ones who have been truthful, he said: They spoke the words of faith, so the reality of their actions was that they were truthful to God. Al-Hasan used to say: These are the words of faith and their reality is actions, so if there is no action along with the words, then there is nothing.
2:178: His saying: 178- Written means imposed and established, and from it is the saying of Omar bin Abi Rabia: Killing and fighting are written on us and on the prostitutes who drag their tails This is a notification from God the Almighty to His servants that He has prescribed this for them. It was said that wrote here refers to what the pen wrote in the Preserved Tablet. Retribution originally means cutting the trace: i.e. following it. From this comes the word qass because he follows traces, and cutting hair is following its traces. So it is as if the killer takes a path of murder, tracing his traces in it. From this comes the saying of God the Almighty: So they returned upon their traces, tracing them back. It was said that retaliation is derived from qass which means cutting. It is said that I cut what is between them: i.e. I cut it off. This verse was used as evidence by those who say that a free man is not killed for a slave, and they are the majority. Abu Hanifa and his companions, al-Thawri, Ibn Abi Layla, and Dawud held that he is killed for it. Al-Qurtubi said: This was narrated from Ali and Ibn Masoud. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah and Al-Hakam bin Utaybah said the same. They used as evidence the words of God the Almighty: And We ordained for them therein a life for a life. The first scholars responded to this evidence by saying that the words of God the Almighty: The free for the free, and the slave for the slave explain the words of God the Almighty: A life for a life. They also said that His words: And We ordained for them therein indicate that this is a narration of what God legislated for the Children of Israel in the Torah. Among the things that the others used as evidence is the words of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): The blood of Muslims is equal. The response to this is that it is general and the verse is clear. However, it is said that the words of God the Almighty: The free for the free, and the slave for the slave only indicate in their explicit meaning that the free is killed for the free, and the slave is killed for the slave. There is nothing in it that indicates that the free is not killed for the slave except by considering the implication. Whoever takes such an implication must say it here, and whoever does not take such an implication is not obligated to say it here. The discussion of this is detailed in the science of Usul. This verse was used as evidence by those who say that a Muslim is killed for a disbeliever, and they are the Kufians and Thawri, because a free man includes a disbeliever as he includes a Muslim, and likewise a slave and a female include a disbeliever as they include a Muslim. They also used as evidence the words of God the Almighty: A life for a life, because a life applies to a disbelieving soul as it applies to a Muslim soul. The majority of scholars are of the view that a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever, and they used as evidence what was reported in the Sunnah from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever, and this explains what is intended in the two verses, and discussing this would take a long time. This verse was used as evidence by those who say that a male is not killed for a female, and they decided to prove that with something similar to what was mentioned previously, unless the woman’s guardians hand over the excess blood money to the man’s blood money. Malik, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, al-Thawri, and Abu Thawr said the same. The majority of scholars are of the view that a man is killed for a woman and there is no increase, and this is the truth. We have discussed this in detail in the explanation of al-Muntaqa, so please refer to it. His statement: But if a man is pardoned by his brother here refers to the killer. The intended meaning of the murdered brother or guardian, and the thing is the blood, and the meaning is: if the killer or the offender is pardoned by the victim or the guardian for blood that he took from him on the condition that he takes from him something from the blood money or land, then the victim should follow the guardian of the one who owes the blood money in what he takes from him from that, following in a good manner, and the offender should pay what he is obligated to of the blood money or compensation to the victim, or to the guardian, performing it with kindness. It was said: what is meant by the expression of the guardian and the brother is the killer, and the thing is the blood money, and the meaning is that if the guardian tends to pardon the retaliation in exchange for the blood money, then the killer has the choice between giving it or surrendering himself for retaliation, as narrated from Malik that the choice is established for the killer in that, and those other than him went to that he does not have the choice, but if the guardians are satisfied with the blood money, then there is no good for the killer, but he must hand it over. It was said: the meaning of pardoned is given: that is, whoever is given something from the blood money, then he should accept and follow in a good manner. It was said: what is meant by that is whoever from the two groups has something of the blood money over the other, then he is pardoned. Meaning: favor, and in all cases, the indefiniteness of something is for the sake of belittling, so it includes pardoning a small amount of blood money, and pardon issued by one of the heirs. His saying: Then follow is raised by an omitted verb, meaning let there be following from it, or as a predicate of a deleted subject: meaning the matter is following, and likewise his saying: And pay him with kindness and his saying: That is a mitigation is a reference to pardon and blood money: meaning that God has prescribed for this nation pardon without compensation or compensation, and He did not make things difficult for them as He made things difficult for the Jews, for He made retaliation obligatory for them, and no pardon, and as He made things difficult for the Christians, for He made pardon and no blood money obligatory for them. His saying: But whoever transgresses after that means after the mitigation, such as taking the blood money then killing the killer, or pardoning then retaliating. The scholars differed regarding the one who kills the killer after taking the blood money. A group of them, including Malik and Al-Shafi'i, said: He is like the one who killed initially, if the guardian wishes he kills him and if he wishes he pardons him. Qatada, Ikrimah, Al-Suddi and others said: His punishment is to be killed absolutely, and the ruler or guardian will not be able to pardon him. Omar bin Abdul Aziz said: His matter is up to the Imam to do with him as he sees fit.
2:179: And His saying: 179- And in retaliation there is life for you meaning, in this ruling that God has legislated for you, there is life for you, because if a man knows that he will be killed in retaliation if he kills another, he will refrain from killing and will be deterred from rushing to it and falling into it, so that it is like life for human souls. This is a type of eloquence that is eloquent and a high type of rhetoric, because He made retaliation, which is death, a life in consideration of what it leads to in terms of people being deterred from killing each other, preserving their souls and sustaining their lives, and He made this address directed to those with understanding, because they are the ones who consider the consequences and avoid what causes long-term harm. As for the one who is afflicted with foolishness, rashness and frivolity, he does not consider his consequences when his anger is boiling and his rashness is boiling, nor does he think about a future matter, as one of their young men said: I will wash away my shame with the sword, bringing upon me the judgment of God that it was to bring. Then, the Almighty explained this ruling that He legislated for His servants by saying: That you may become righteous, meaning that you may avoid killing by preserving retaliation, and that will be a reason for righteousness. Abu al-Juza’ read: And for you in retaliation is life. It was said that by stories he meant the Qur’an: meaning for you in the Book of God in which retaliation was legislated is life, meaning salvation. It was also said that he meant the life of hearts. It was also said that it is a source meaning retaliation, and all of them are weak, and reading it with it is objectionable. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: Two tribes of Arabs fought in the pre-Islamic era shortly before Islam, and there was killing and wounding between them until they killed slaves and women, and they did not take anything from each other until they converted to Islam. One of the two tribes was attacking the other in terms of numbers and money, so they swore that they would not be satisfied until a free man among them was killed for a slave, and a man among them was killed for a woman. Then this verse was revealed. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Sha’bi. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: They did not kill a man for a woman, but they killed a man for a man and a woman for a woman. Then God revealed a life for a life and made the free men and women equal in retaliation for intentional killings and for less than a life, and made the slaves equal in intentional killings and less than a life, their men and women. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Malik who said: There was a fight between two tribes of the Ansar, one of which had the upper hand over the other, and it was as if they were seeking a favor. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to reconcile between them, and this verse was revealed: The free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. Ibn Abbas said: Then it was abrogated by ‘a life for a life.’ Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: But whoever is pardoned he said: He is the one whose family is satisfied with the pardon. Then follow up with kindness he ordered the one seeking it. And pay it back to him with goodness on the part of the one who is seeking it. He said: He pays back the one sought with goodness. That is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy from what was upon the Children of Israel. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on his authority from another chain of transmission. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Children of Israel used to practice retaliation, but they did not practice blood money. So God said to this nation: Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder until His saying: But if a man pardons his brother for anything, pardon means accepting blood money for premeditated murder. “Then follow up with kindness and pay him back with good treatment. That is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy,” from what was prescribed for those who came before you. But whoever transgresses after that, it was said: after accepting blood money, will have a painful punishment. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: The people of the Torah only practiced retaliation or pardon, with no compensation between them. The people of the Gospel only practiced pardon, which they were commanded to do. God made for this nation killing, pardon, and blood money if they wished. He made it permissible for them, and it was not for any nation before them. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Shuraih al-Khuza’i that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever is afflicted by murder or madness, he has the choice of one of three things: either to take retribution, or to pardon, or to accept blood money. If he wants the fourth, then seize him. Whoever commits aggression after that will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah that if someone kills after taking blood money, he will be severely punished. He said: He must be killed and no blood money will be accepted from him. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will not pardon a man who kills after taking blood money. Samuyah narrated in his Fawa’id on the authority of Samurah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: He is to be killed. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: And there is life for you in retaliation, he said: God has made retaliation a life, a punishment, and a lesson. If the unjust aggressor remembers it, he will refrain from killing. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: Perhaps you will fear God he said: Perhaps you will fear killing him and then be killed for it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: O you of understanding he said: Whoever has a mind will remember retaliation and the fear of retaliation will prevent him from killing. Perhaps you will fear God he said: So that you will avoid bloodshed for fear of retaliation.
2:180: The meaning of 180- wrote may have been presented soon, and the presence of death: the presence of its causes and the appearance of its signs, and from this is the saying of Antarah: Death is at my disposal if I reach my fingertips with the Hindu Jarir said: I am the death you spoke about, so no one can escape me The verb attributed to the will, which is wrote, was not made feminine because of the separation between them. It was said: because it means a will. It has been reported that it is permissible to attribute something that is not feminine to a feminine without separation. Sibawayh reported: A woman stood up, which is contrary to what the imams of Arabic agreed upon. God Almighty stipulated what He wrote of the will that the testator leave something good. There was a difference of opinion about the answer to this condition: What is it? Two opinions were reported from Al-Akhfash: One of them is that the estimate is: If he left something good, then the will, then the fa was deleted as the poet said: Whoever does good deeds, God will reward them, and evil is recompensed for evil in the sight of God. The second: Its answer was estimated before it: i.e. writing a will for the parents and relatives if he left something good. The scholars differed about the amount of the good. It was said: what is more than seven hundred dinars, and it was said: one thousand dinars, and it was said: what is more than five hundred dinars. The will in origin: is an order to do something and a covenant with it in life and after death, and here: is an order to do something after death. The scholars agreed on the obligation of a will for someone who is in debt or has a deposit or the like. As for someone who is not like that, most of them went to the view that it is not obligatory for him, whether he is poor or rich, and a group said: it is obligatory. And God the Almighty did not clarify here the amount that he wrote the will for the parents and relatives, so it was said: one-fifth, and it was said: one-quarter, and it was said: one-third. The scholars differed about this verse, is it decisive or abrogated? A group went to the view that it is decisive, they said: And even if it is general, its meaning is specific. What is meant by it from the parents is those who do not inherit, such as the disbelieving parents and those who are slaves, and from the relatives are those who are not heirs. Ibn al-Mundhir said: All the scholars from whom we have preserved have agreed that a will for the parents who do not inherit and the relatives who do not inherit is permissible. Many scholars said: It was abrogated by the verse of inheritance, along with the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): There is no will for an heir. This is a hadeeth that some scholars have authenticated, and it has been narrated from other sources. Some scholars said: It abrogated the obligation and negated the recommendation, and it was narrated from al-Sha’bi, al-Nakha’i and Malik. His saying: with what is right means justice, with no excess or excess. God has permitted the deceased to have a third, without anything in excess. His saying: rightly is a source that means confirmation and obligation.
2:181: His statement: 181- So whoever changes it this pronoun refers to the bequest understood from the will, and likewise the pronoun in his statement: he heard it and the change is the alteration, and the pronoun in his statement: then his sin refers to the alteration understood from his statement: he changed it and this is a warning to whoever changes the bequest that is in accordance with the truth in which there is no injustice or harm, and that he will bear the sin, and the testator is not responsible for that, for he has been freed from what he was responsible for by bequeathing it.
2:182: Al-Qurtubi said: There is no disagreement that if he bequeaths something that is not permissible, such as bequeathing wine, pork, or something sinful, then it is permissible to change it, but it is not permissible to carry it out, just as it is not permissible to carry out what exceeds a third. Abu Omar said this. End quote. And janf means going beyond, from janfa yajnaf: if he goes beyond, said Al-Nahhas. It was said that janf means inclination, and from this is the saying of Al-A'sha: Turn away from the stone of Yamamah, O young man, and I did not seek anyone from its people except you. He said in Al-Sahah: Al-Janf means inclination, and likewise in Al-Kashshaf. And Labid said: I am a man who has prevented the descendants of Amer from oppressing me, and my enemies have wronged me. And his saying: 182- “So make peace between them” meaning, he made peace with what happened between the heirs of discord and disorder because of the will by nullifying what is harmful and contradictory to what God has legislated, and establishing what is right, such as a will for a good deed to a non-heir. The pronoun in his saying: between them refers to the heirs, even if they were not mentioned before, because it is known that they are the ones intended from the context. And it was said: it refers to those to whom the will was made, and they are the parents and relatives. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: If he leaves behind wealth, he said: Money. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Whoever does not leave behind sixty dinars has not left behind wealth. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Urwah that Ali bin Abi Talib entered upon a freed slave of theirs who was dying and he had seven hundred or six hundred dirhams and said: Should I not make a will? He said: No. Rather, God said: If he leaves behind wealth, and you do not have much wealth, so leave your wealth for your heirs.
