Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Aisha that a man said to her: I want to make a will. She said: How much is your wealth? He said: Three thousand. She said: How many dependents do you have? He said: Four. She said: God said: If he leaves behind wealth, and this is something small, so leave it for your dependents, for that is better. Abdul Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: If the deceased leaves seven hundred dirhams, then he should not make a will. Abdul Razzaq and Abdul bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri who said: God has made the will a right, whether it is small or large. Abdul Razzaq and Abdul bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said and mentioned a hadith in it: Look at your relatives who are in need and do not inherit, and bequeath to them from your wealth according to what is reasonable. They also narrated on the authority of Tawus who said: Whoever makes a will to a group of people and names them and leaves his relatives in need, it will be taken from them and returned to his relatives. Saeed bin Mansour, Ahmad, Abdul bin Hamid, Abu Dawud in Al-Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Bashir on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: This verse was abrogated. Abu Dawud in his Al-Nasikh, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority from another chain of transmission that this verse was abrogated by the statement of God the Almighty: Men shall have a share of what parents and near relatives leave (Al-Nasikh 2:100). Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him from another chain of transmission that it was abrogated by the verse of inheritance. Abu Dawud narrated something similar from him in his Sunan and Al-Bayhaqi. Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said: In the verse, it abrogated who inherits, but it did not abrogate the relatives who do not inherit. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Umar that he said: This verse was abrogated by the verse of inheritance. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, But whoever changes it the verse, he said: The reward of the testator is with God and he is absolved from his sin. He said regarding the statement of God, injustice (i.e. sin), and reconcile between them (i.e., if the deceased makes a mistake in his will or deviates from it, then there is no blame on the guardians if they return his mistake to the right path. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Saeed ibn Jubayr, but he interpreted injustice as inclination. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Biasal or sin, he said: By mistake or intentionally. Saeed bin Mansour and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on his authority that he said: Bias in a will and causing harm in it are among the major sins.
2:183: The meaning of 183- wrote has been presented, and there is no disagreement among all Muslims that fasting Ramadan is an obligation imposed by God the Almighty upon this nation. The root of fasting in the language is: abstinence and refraining from moving from one state to another. Silence is called fasting because it is abstaining from speech, and from this is I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast meaning abstaining from speech, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: Fasting horses, non-fasting horses in the dust, and horses chewing on bridles Any horse that is restrained from running and moving. In Islamic law, it means abstaining from things that break the fast, with the intention of doing so, from sunrise to sunset. His statement, as it was written, means fasting as it was written, with the kaf in the accusative case as a description, or fasting was written upon you, resembling what was written, with the kaf in the accusative case as a state. Some grammarians said that the kaf is in the nominative case as a description of fasting, but this is weak because fasting is defined by the lam, and the hidden pronoun in his statement, as it was written, refers back to what. The commentators differed about the reason for the comparison, what it is. It was said: It is the amount of fasting and its time, because God prescribed the fasting of Ramadan for the Jews and Christians, but they changed it. It was said: It is the obligation, because God obligated fasting for the nations. It was said: It is the description, i.e. refraining from eating and drinking and the like at a time. According to the first, its meaning is: God prescribed the fasting of Ramadan for this nation as He prescribed it for those before them. According to the second, God obligated fasting for this nation as He obligated it for those before them. According to the third, God Almighty obligated this nation to abstain from things that break the fast as He obligated it for those before them. And the Almighty’s saying: Perhaps you will become righteous is by maintaining it. It was said: You will become righteous from sins because of this worship, because it breaks desire and weakens the motives for sins, as mentioned in the hadith that it is a shield and that it came.
2:184: And his saying: 184- Days is in the accusative case as a second object of his saying: It was written Al-Farra' said: It was said: It is in the accusative case as a circumstance: meaning fasting was written for you in days. And his saying: Counted means specified in a known number, and it is possible that in this plural because it is from the plurals of fewness there is an indication of the shortening of the days. And his saying: So whoever among you is ill it was said that the sick person has two cases: If he is unable to fast, then breaking the fast is obligatory, and if he is able to do so with harm and hardship, then it is a dispensation, and this is what the majority said. And his saying: On a journey the scholars differed regarding the journey that permits breaking the fast, so it was said: The distance of shortening the prayer, and the disagreement over its amount is well-known, and this is what the majority said, and others said: In amounts for which there is no evidence. The truth is that what is true of travel is what is permissible for breaking the fast, and likewise what is true of illness is what is permissible for breaking the fast. There was consensus on breaking the fast during a journey of obedience. They differed about permissible journeys, and the truth is that the license is established in it, and they also differed about the journey of disobedience. And his saying: then a number means he has a number, or the ruling is a number, or the duty is a number, and the number is its action from the number, and it means the counted. And his saying: from other days Sibawayh said: It was not declined because it was modified from the other, because the way of this chapter is to bring the definite article. Al-Kisa'i said: It is modified from the other, and it was said: It is the plural of another, and there is nothing in the verse that indicates the obligation of succession in making up. His saying: and upon those who are able to do it The majority read with a kasra on the ta' and a sukoon on the ya', and its original is yatuquhu, the kasra was transferred to the ta', and the waw was changed to a ya' because of the kasra of what preceded it. Hamid read according to the original without defect. Ibn Abbas read with a fatha on the ta' with a lightened letter and a shaddah on the waw: meaning they impose on him. Ibn al-Anbari narrated from Ibn Abbas yatuquhu with a fatha on the ya' and a shaddah on the ta' and the ya' with both open, meaning they are able to do it. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha, Ibn Abbas, Amr bin Dinar and Tawus that they read yatqiqunuhu with a fatha on the ya and a shaddah on the ta with a fatha. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read fidya ta'am with an addition. They also read masakeen and Ibn Abbas read ta'am miskeen which is the reading of Abu Amr, Asim, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i. The scholars differed regarding this verse, is it decisive or abrogated? It was said that it was abrogated, but it was a concession when fasting was first made obligatory because it was difficult for them, so whoever fed a poor person every day would stop fasting even though he was able to do so, then that was abrogated, and this is the opinion of the majority. It was narrated on the authority of some scholars that it was not abrogated, and that it was a concession for the elderly and the old especially if they were not able to fast except with difficulty, and this is consistent with the reading of shaddah: that is, they force them as mentioned above. The abrogator of this verse according to the majority is the saying of God the Almighty: And whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it. They differed regarding the amount of the ransom, and it was said: Each day one sa' of other than wheat, and half a sa' of it, and it was said: only one mudd. And his saying: And whoever volunteers good - it is better for him. Ibn Shihab said: Its meaning is that he intended feeding along with fasting. Mujahid said: Its meaning is whoever feeds more than the mudd, and it was said: whoever feeds the poor another musk. Isa bin Amr, Yahya bin Waththab, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read yataw'u with a shaddah and the verb is jussive with the meaning of yatawudhu, and the rest read it with a light ta' as a past tense verb. And his saying: And that you fast is better for you means: that fasting is better for them than breaking the fast with a ransom, and this was before the abrogation, and it was said that its meaning is: and that you fast while traveling and sick, but not while it is difficult. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, who said: Prayer was permitted in three cases, and fasting was permitted in three cases. He mentioned the cases of prayer, then said: As for the cases of fasting, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came to Madinah, and he began to fast three days of every month, and he fasted on Ashura. Then God, the Exalted, imposed fasting on him and revealed to him: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting until His saying: And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person. So whoever wanted to fast, he fasted, and whoever wanted to feed a poor person, that was sufficient for him. Then God revealed the other verse: So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. So God confirmed its fasting for the sound resident, and permitted it for the sick and the traveler, and confirmed feeding the elderly who are unable to fast. Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: As it was decreed upon those before you, he said: He meant the People of the Book. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Daghfal bin Hanzalah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Christians were required to fast the month of Ramadan. Their king fell ill and they said: ‘If God heals him, we will add ten more.’ Then there was another who ate meat and his mouth hurt. He said: ‘If God heals him, we will add seven more.’ Then there was another king who said: ‘We will not leave anything of these three days. We will complete them and make our fast in the spring.’ So he did so and it became fifty days.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: Perhaps you will become righteous, he said: You will be righteous from food, drink and women as they were righteous. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar to what was previously mentioned on the authority of Muadh. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fasting Ramadan was prescribed by God for the nations before you. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: Ashura used to be a fast, but when Ramadan was revealed, whoever wanted to fast could and whoever wanted to break the fast could. Abd bin Hamid narrated that Ibn Abbas said: The Almighty’s saying: And upon those who are able to fast has been abrogated. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar to that from him, and he added that what abrogated it is the Almighty’s saying: And whoever among you witnesses the month [al-Naskh]. Abu Dawud narrated something similar to that from him. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and others also narrated something similar from him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’ who said: When this verse was revealed: And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person, whoever wanted to fast could, and whoever wanted to break the fast and ransom could, until this verse was revealed after it and abrogated it: And whoever among you witnesses the month. Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn Abi Laila who said: The companions of Muhammad told us, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ali bin Abi Talib regarding his saying: And upon those who are able to fast he said: The old man who is unable to fast should break the fast and feed a poor person in place of each day. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ad-Daraqutni and Al-Bayhaqi narrated that Anas ibn Malik was too weak to fast for a year before his death, so he made a bowl of tharid and invited thirty poor people and fed them. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ad-Daraqutni narrated who authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said to his pregnant or nursing mother: You are like those who cannot fast. You must eat, but you do not have to make up for it. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that one of his daughters sent him a message asking him about fasting Ramadan while she was pregnant. He said: Break your fast and feed a poor person every day. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the statement of God, But whoever does good voluntarily, he said: Feed two poor people. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Tawus regarding the statement of God, But whoever does good voluntarily, he said: Feed the poor people. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab regarding the statement of God, And that you fast is better for you, meaning that fasting is better for you than blood money. There are many hadiths about the virtue of fasting.
2:185: 185- Ramadan is taken from the word ramad which means the fasting person ramadh, meaning that his stomach is burned from intense thirst, and ramdaa is extended: intense heat. From this comes the authentic hadith in Sahih The prayer of the penitents is when the camels are ramadh, meaning the scorching heat burns their stomachs. Al-Jawhari said: The month of Ramadan is pluralized as Ramadanat and armadaa. It is said that when they transferred the names of the months from the ancient language, they named them according to the times in which they occurred, and this month coincided with the days of heat, so it was named thus. It was also said that it was named Ramadan because it ramadhs sins, meaning it burns them with good deeds. Al-Mawardi said: Its name in pre-Islamic times was Natiq, and Al-Mufaddal recited: In Nataq, the knights of Khatham fled to the battlefield. And they called it that because he used to criticize them for his severity on them, and Shahr is raised in the reading of the group as a subject whose predicate is in which the Qur’an was revealed or as a predicate for a deleted subject: meaning, fasting the month of Ramadan is obligatory upon you, and it is permissible to be a substitute for the fasting mentioned in the Almighty’s saying: Fasting is prescribed for you. Mujahid and Shahr bin Hawshab read Shahr in the accusative case, and Harun al-A’war narrated it from Abu Amr and it is in the accusative case with the estimation of adhere to or fast. Al-Kisa’i and al-Farra’ said: It is in the accusative case with the estimation of the verb fasting was prescribed for you and al-Nahhas denied that and said: It is in the accusative case for enticement. Al-Akhfash said: It is in the accusative case as an adverb, and the inflection is prevented because of the extra alif and nun. His saying: in which the Qur’an was revealed It was said: It was revealed from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, then Gabriel would bring it down star by star. It was said: Its beginning was revealed in it, and it was said: The Qur’an was revealed concerning it, and this verse is more general than the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And His saying: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night means the Night of Decree. The Qur’an is the name for the speech of God Almighty, and it means that which is recited, just as a drink is called a drink, and that which is written is called a book. It was said that it is the source of the verb qara’a to read, and from it the poet said: They sacrificed Ashmat, the title of prostration, with which he spends the night glorifying and reciting the Qur’an. Any reading, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And the Qur'an of dawn meaning the recitation of dawn. And His saying: A guidance for mankind is in the accusative case as a state: meaning a guide for them. And His saying: And clear proofs of guidance is from the conjunction of the specific with the general to show the honor of the conjoined by singling it out for mention, because the Qur'an includes its clear and ambiguous verses, and clear proofs are specific to the clear verses. And the Criterion: is that which distinguishes between truth and falsehood: meaning a separation. His saying: So whoever among you witnesses the month meaning he is present and not traveling but rather he is residing, and the month is in the accusative case as a circumstance, and it is not correct for it to be a direct object. A group of the Salaf and Khalaf said: Whoever the month of Ramadan comes to him while he is a resident and not traveling, he is obligated to fast it, whether he travels after that or stays, based on this verse. The majority said: If he travels, he breaks his fast, because the meaning of the verse is: If he attends the month from its beginning to its end, not if he attends part of it and travels, then he is not obligated to fast except what he attends, and this is the truth, and the authentic evidence from the Sunnah indicates this. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to go out during Ramadan and break his fast. His statement, But whoever among you is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days has already been explained. His statement, God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship indicates that this is one of the purposes of the Lord, the Most High, and what is intended in all matters of religion. Similar to this is His statement, the Most High: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty al-Baqarah 2:17. It has been proven that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to guide people to ease and forbid people from making things difficult, as in his statement, the Most High: Make things easy and do not make them difficult, and give good tidings and do not repel people al-Sahih. Ease is the ease in which there is no difficulty. His statement, And that you may complete the number appears to be connected to His statement, God intends for you ease, meaning He intends ease for you, and He intends for you to complete the number and glorify Him. It has been said that it is related to something omitted, the meaning of which is: He has given you this concession so that you may complete the number, and He has prescribed fasting for those who witness the month so that you may complete the number. The Basrans went with the first. They said: The estimation is that you complete the waiting period. Similar to it is the saying of Katheer bin Sakhr: I want to forget her name, but she appears to me at night in every way. The Kufians went to the second, and it was said: The waw is inserted, and it was said: This lam is the lam of command, and the waw is to connect the sentence that comes after it to the sentence that comes before it. He said in Al-Kashshaf: His saying: That you may complete the number is the reason for the command to observe the number, And that you may glorify is the reason for what is known about how to make up for and get out of the obligation of breaking the fast, And that you may be grateful is the reason for permission and facilitation, and what is meant by glorification here is the saying of the speaker God is greater. The majority said: Its meaning is the urging of glorification at the end of Ramadan. There was a disagreement about its time, so it was narrated from some of the predecessors that they used to glorify God on the night of breaking the fast, and it was said: When they saw the crescent of Shawwal, they would glorify God until the end of the sermon, and it was said: Until the imam comes out, and it was said: It is the glorification on the day of breaking the fast. Malik said: It is from the time he leaves his house until the imam comes out, and Al-Shafi'i said the same. Abu Hanifa said: He glorifies God on Eid al-Adha and does not glorify God on Eid al-Fitr. His saying: And that you may be grateful has already been explained. Abu Hatim, Abu Sheikh, Ibn Adi and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with both chains of transmission traceable to the Prophet and those traceable to the Companions, that he said: Do not say Ramadan, for Ramadan is one of the names of God, but say the month of Ramadan. It has been authenticated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and in the hope of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven. It has also been authenticated that he said: Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan out of faith and in the hope of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven. It has been authenticated that he said: “Two months of celebration that will never diminish: Ramadan and Dhul-Hijjah.” He said: When Ramadan begins, the gates of Paradise are opened. All of this is in Sahih. It has been authenticated in many other hadiths that he used to say Ramadan without mentioning the month. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Asbahani narrated in Al-Targheeb on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It was called Ramadan because Ramadan burns away sins. They also narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Aisha, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Asakir narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Umar in his history. Many hadiths have been narrated about the virtues of Ramadan. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The verse of Abraham was revealed on the first night of Ramadan, and the Psalms were revealed on the eighteenth of Ramadan, and God revealed the Qur'an on the twenty-fourth of Ramadan. Abu Ya'la and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Jabir, but he said: And the Psalms were revealed on the twelfth, and he added: And the Torah was revealed on the sixth of Ramadan, and the Gospel was revealed on the eighteenth of Ramadan. Muhammad ibn Nasr narrated something similar to what Jabir said, except that she mentioned the revelation of the Qur'an. Ibn Jarir, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat on the authority of Muqsim who said: 'Atiyyah ibn al-Aswad asked Ibn 'Abbas and said: 'Doubt has entered my heart concerning the statement of God, The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was revealed.' And his saying: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree and his saying: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Ibn Abbas said: It was sent down on the Night of Decree and in Ramadan and on a blessed night all at once, then after that it was sent down according to the positions of the stars as messengers during the months and days. Muhammad bin Nasr, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Al-Bayhaqi and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Qur’an was sent down all at once on the twenty-fourth of Ramadan, then it was placed in the House of Honour in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel began to send it down to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in measured recitation. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: The Night of Decree is the blessed night and it is in Ramadan that the Qur’an was sent down all at once from the remembrance to the Frequented House. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his saying: A guidance for mankind, he said: They are guided by it, And clear proofs of guidance, he said: In it is the lawful and the unlawful and the prescribed punishments. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: So whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it, he said: It is destroying the home. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali who said: Whoever witnesses Ramadan while he is a resident and then travels, he is obligated to fast because God says: So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. Saeed bin Mansour narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: God intends for you ease, he said: Ease means breaking the fast while traveling, and hardship means fasting while traveling. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ regarding His statement: And complete the number, he said: The number of days for the month of Ramadan. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak that he said: The number of days for which a sick person breaks his fast while traveling. It was authentically reported on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he said: Fast when you see it and break your fast when you see it, and if it is hidden from you, then complete the number of thirty days. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It is obligatory upon those who are fasting when they see the month of Shawwal to glorify God until they finish their Eid, because God says: And complete the number and glorify God for having guided you. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he used to say: God is Great, God is Great, there is no god but God, God is Great, God is Great, and to God be praise. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to say: God is Great, God is Great, God is Great, God is Great, and to God be praise and glory, God is Great for what He has guided us to.
2:186: His statement: 186- And when My servants ask you concerning Me may be about nearness and distance, as indicated by His statement: Indeed, I am near. It may be about answering the supplication, as indicated by His statement: I answer the supplication of the supplicant. It may be about something more general than that, and this is what appears regardless of the reason that will be explained. His statement: Indeed, I am near was said to be about answering, and it was said: with knowledge, and it was said: with favor. He said in Al-Kashshaf: It is a representation of his state in the ease with which he answers the one who calls upon him, and the speed with which he fulfills the need of the one who asks him by someone close to him, so if he is called upon, he quickly answers him. The meaning of the answer is the same as what is in the Almighty’s saying: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. It was said that its meaning is that I accept the worship of whoever worships Me through supplication, as it was proven from him, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that supplication is worship, as Abu Dawud and others reported from the hadith of Nu’man ibn Bashir. It appears that the answer here remains in its linguistic meaning, and the fact that supplication is worship does not necessitate that the answer is acceptance of the supplication: i.e. making it an accepted act of worship, for the answer is something other than accepting this act of worship. What is meant is that He, glory be to Him, answers with whatever He wills and however He wills. The request may happen soon or it may happen far away, and He may avert from the supplicant a calamity that he does not know because of his supplication. This is restricted to the supplicant not transgressing in his supplication, as in the Almighty’s saying: “Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly. Indeed, He does not like transgressors.” Transgression includes asking for what one does not deserve and is not suitable for, such as someone who asks for a status in Paradise equal to or above the status of the prophets. His saying: So let them respond to me means as I responded to them when they called upon me, so let them respond to me in what I called them to of faith and obedience. It was said that its meaning is that they seek God’s answer to their call by responding to it: that is, doing what He commanded them to do and abandoning what He forbade them from. Guidance is the opposite of error. Guidance means guidance, guidance and right guidance. Al-Harawi said: Guidance, guidance and right guidance: guidance and righteousness. He said: And from it is this verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Salt bin Hakim on the authority of a man from the Ansar on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, is our Lord near so that we may speak to Him, or is He far so that we may call upon Him? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) remained silent, and this verse was revealed. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: The companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked: Where is our Lord? So God revealed this verse. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that a Bedouin asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Where is our Lord? So it was revealed. Ibn Asakir narrated in his history on the authority of Ali who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do not be helpless in supplication, for God revealed to me: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. A man said: O Messenger of God, does our Lord hear supplications, or how? So God revealed this verse. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ that he heard that when the verse Call upon Me, I will respond to you was revealed, they said: If only we knew at what time we would supplicate. So it was revealed. It is proven in Sahih from the hadith of Abu Saeed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no Muslim who calls upon God with a supplication that does not contain sin or severing family ties, except that God will give him one of three things: either He will grant him his supplication, or He will store it up for him in the Hereafter, or He will divert from him an equivalent amount of evil.” It is also proven in Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The supplication of one of you will be answered as long as he is not hasty, saying: I called upon God but I was not answered.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Anas regarding his statement, So let them respond to Me, he said: Let them call upon Me, and believe in Me, meaning that if they call upon Me, I will respond to them. Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid who said: So let them respond to Me, meaning let them obey me. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from al-Rabi’ ibn Anas regarding his statement, Perhaps they will be guided, he said: May they be guided.
2:187: His saying: 187- Lawful for you indicates that what God made lawful was forbidden to them, and this is how it was, as the reason for the revelation of the verse indicates, and it will come. And rifth: is a euphemism for sexual intercourse. Al-Zajjaj said: Rifth is a comprehensive word for everything that a man wants from his wife, and Al-Azhari said the same, and from it is the saying of the poet: They see Anas talking to adulterers and they are averse to the obscenities of men. It was said that Al-Rafth: Its origin is saying obscenities, Rafth and Arfath: if he speaks ugly, and this is not what is meant here, and Al-Rafth is transitive with the preposition “to” to include the meaning of approval, and women are made a garment for men, and men are made a garment for them because each one of them mixes with the other during intercourse like the mixing that occurs between a garment and its wearer. Abu Ubaidah and others said: It is said that a woman is called: a garment, a bed, and a loincloth. It was said: Each one of them is made a garment for the other because it covers him during intercourse from the eyes of people. And His statement: You betray yourselves means you betray them by having intercourse on the nights of fasting. It is said: Khan and Ikhtan mean the same thing, and they are from betrayal. Al-Qatibi said: The origin of betrayal is that a man is entrusted with something and does not fulfill the trust in it. And He called them traitors to themselves because the harm of that would come back to them. And His statement, Then He turned to you has two possible meanings: One is accepting their repentance from their betrayal of themselves, and the other is making things easier for them by giving them permission and permission, like His statement, He knew that you would not be able to count it, so He turned to you meaning He made things easier for you. And like His statement, But whoever cannot find [anything], then a fast of two consecutive months as repentance from God meaning making things easier. And likewise His statement, And He pardoned you has the potential to mean pardon for the sin, and it has the potential to mean expansion and facilitation. His saying: And seek it was said that it is the child: that is, seek by having intercourse with your wives to obtain what is most intended from marriage, which is obtaining offspring. It was said that what is meant is seek the Qur’an with what is permitted to you in it, as stated by Al-Zajjaj and others. It was said: seek the concession and expansion. It was said: seek what has been written for you of female slaves and wives. Other things were said that are not supported by the Qur’anic arrangement, nor is there any other evidence for it. Al-Hasan Al-Basri read and follow with the silent ‘ayn from following. His saying: until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn is a powerful simile. What is meant here by the white thread is the one that is across the horizon, not the one that is like the tail of a scorpion, for dawn is the false dawn that neither permits nor forbids anything. What is meant by the black thread is the blackness of the night, and distinction is that one of them is distinguished from the other, and that does not happen except at the time of dawn. His saying: Then complete the fast until nightfall clearly states that the end of fasting is nightfall. When night falls from the east and day departs from the west, the fasting person breaks his fast and it is permissible for him to eat, drink, and so on. His saying: And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques It was said that what is meant by sexual relations here is intercourse. It was also said that it includes kissing and touching if they are for lust, not if they are not for lust. They are permissible, as stated by Ata’, Al-Shafi’i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and others. Based on this, what Ibn Abd Al-Barr narrated about the consensus that the person in retreat does not have sexual relations or kisses is possible. So this narration of the consensus is restricted to them being for lust. In the language, retreat means adherence. It is said that he adhered to something if he adhered to it. From this is the saying of the poet: And the girls of the night remained around me, stumbling like mourners, stumbling around me Since the person performing itikaf is committed to the mosque, he is called: I’tikaf in the mosque and I’tikaf in it, because he confines himself to this act of worship in the mosque. I’tikaf in Islamic law means: committing to a specific act of obedience on a specific condition. There is consensus that it is not obligatory and that it can only be done in a mosque. There are rulings for itikaf that are fully explained in the books of jurisprudence and the commentaries on hadith. His statement, These are the limits of God, means that these rulings are the limits of God. The root of the limit is prevention, and from this the doorman and the subhan were called Hadad. The commands and prohibitions were called the limits of God because they prevent what is not from entering them and what is from them from exiting them. From this the limits were called limits because they prevent their owners from returning. The meaning of the prohibition of approaching them is the prohibition of transgressing them by disobeying them. It was said that the limits of God are only His prohibitions, and from them is sexual intercourse with the person performing itikaf and breaking the fast in Ramadan without an excuse and other things that were previously prohibited. The meaning of the prohibition of approaching them is clear. And His statement: Thus does God make clear His signs, meaning, just as He made clear to you these boundaries, He makes clear to you the signs that guide to the truth. Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i and others narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin ‘Azib who said: When the companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) were fasting and the time for breaking the fast came and he slept before breaking the fast, he would not eat until evening came. Qays bin Sarmah Al-Ansari was fasting, and that day he worked on his land. When the time for breaking the fast came, he came to his wife and said: Do you have any food? She said: No, but I will go and look for some for you. Sleep overcame him and he slept. His wife came and when she saw him sleeping, she said: What a pity that you slept. When it was midday, he fainted. This was mentioned to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and this verse was revealed: Lawful to you on the night of fasting until His statement: from dawn. They rejoiced greatly at that. Al-Bukhari also narrated from his hadith that he said: When the fasting of the month of Ramadan was revealed, they would not approach women during the entire month of Ramadan. There were men who were betraying themselves, so God revealed: God knows that you were betraying yourselves 1:10. Hadiths were narrated from a group of the Companions explaining the reason for the revelation of this verse, similar to what Al-Bara’ said. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: When people first converted to Islam, if one of them fasted, he would fast that day until evening came and he would eat some food. Then he said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab came to his wife, then he came to the Messenger of God and said: O Messenger of God, I apologize to God and to you for myself, and he mentioned what happened from him, so the words of God were revealed: Lawful to you on the night of fasting 1:10. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: When the Muslims prayed the Isha prayer in the month of Ramadan, women, food and drink were forbidden to them until the same time the following year. Then some Muslims had intercourse with women and food in Ramadan after the Isha prayer, including Umar ibn Al-Khattab, so they complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed, Lawful to you on the night of the fast 1:13. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Rafath means sexual intercourse. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Penetration, covering, penetration, touching and sexual intercourse means sexual intercourse. However, God is Modest and Generous and uses whatever euphemism He wills for whatever He wills. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them, that he said: They are a comfort for you and you are a comfort for them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, You are deceiving yourselves, he said: You are wronging yourselves. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, So now have sexual relations with them, he said: Marry them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And seek what God has prescribed for you, he said: Children. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak similarly. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And seek what God has prescribed for you, he said: The Night of Decree. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history on the authority of Anas similarly. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: And seek the concession that God has prescribed for you. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d. He said: And eat and drink until the white thread of prayer becomes distinct to you from the black thread was revealed, but of dawn was not revealed. So when some men wanted to fast, one of them would tie a white thread and a black thread to his feet, and he would continue eating and drinking until he could clearly see them. So God revealed of dawn and they knew that He meant night and day. In the two Sahihs and others, “On the authority of Adi bin Hatim, that he put two threads, white and black, under his pillow, and he kept looking at them, but he could not tell the white from the black. So he went to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in the morning and told him. He said: Then your pillow is wide, for that is the whiteness of the day from the blackness of the night.” And in a narration in Bukhari and others, “He said to him: You have a wide nape.” And in a narration in Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim, He laughed at him. And Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak, who said: They used to have intercourse while they were in seclusion until the verse And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in seclusion in the mosques was revealed. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: If the person performing I’tikaf has intercourse, his I’tikaf is invalidated and he should start over again. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: These are the limits set by God, he said: He means obeying God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: The limits set by God are disobedience to God, meaning sexual intercourse during I’tikaf. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil that it means intercourse. He also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: Likewise, meaning: This is how God makes it clear.
2:188: This includes the entire nation and all wealth. Nothing is excluded from this except what the evidence of the Shari'ah indicates is permissible to take, for it is taken by right, not by wrong, and it is eaten by what is permissible, not by sin, even if its owner is reluctant, such as paying off a debt if the one who owes it refuses to do so, or paying what God has made obligatory of zakat and the like, or providing for someone whose expenses the Shari'ah has made obligatory. The bottom line is that whatever the Shari'ah does not permit to be taken from its owner is eaten by wrong, even if the owner is happy with it, such as the dowry of a prostitute, the fee of a soothsayer, or the price of wine. In the language, wrong means that which is gone and vanishes. His saying: 188 - And you lowered is in the subjunctive mood in apposition to you eat, so it is part of the prohibition against it. It is said: A man lowered his argument or the matter that he hopes will succeed in, likening it to someone who lowers a bucket into a well. It is said that he lowered his bucket: he sent it. The meaning is that you do not combine consuming wealth unjustly with lowering it to the rulers with false arguments. In this verse is evidence that the ruling of the ruler does not make permissible what is forbidden nor forbid what is permissible, without differentiating between wealth and private parts. So whoever the judge rules in his favor with something based in his ruling on false testimony or an immoral oath, it is not permissible for him to eat it, because that is consuming people’s wealth unjustly. Likewise, if the ruler is bribed and he rules in his favor unjustly, then he is consuming people’s wealth unjustly. There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that the ruling of the ruler does not make permissible what is forbidden nor forbid what is permissible. It has been narrated from Abu Hanifa that which contradicts this, and it is rejected by the Book of God and the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as in the hadith of Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You bring your disputes to me, and perhaps some of you are more eloquent in their argument than others, so I rule in his favor based on what I hear. So whoever I rule in his favor regarding his brother’s right, he should not take it, for I am only giving him a piece of the Fire.” This is in the two Sahihs and others. His saying: A group means a piece, a portion, or a group, so he expressed this by the word group. The origin of the word group is a piece of sheep that is an exception to most of them. It has been said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is that you eat the money of a group of people sinfully, and injustice and aggression are called sins based on their connection to the one who does them. His saying: And you know means that you are aware that this is false and has nothing to do with the truth, and this is more severe for their punishment and greater for their crime. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not consume one another’s wealth 1:13, he said: This is about a man who owes money but has no proof, so he denies the money and disputes with the judges even though he knows that he is in the wrong. Saeed bin Mansour and Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Its meaning is do not dispute while you know that you are unjust. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that the wife of Al-Qais bin Abis and Abdan bin Ashwa’ Al-Hadrami disputed over a piece of land, and Imru Al-Qais wanted to swear, so the verse: And do not consume one another’s wealth 1:13 was revealed.
2:189: His saying: 189- They ask you will be explained who are the questioners of him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the crescents are the plural of crescent, and its plural is considering the crescent of each month, or each night, to put the difference in times in the same position as the difference in entities, and the crescent is the name for what appears at the beginning of the month and at the end of it. Al-Asma'i said: It is a crescent until it turns round - and it was said: It is a crescent until it lights up the sky with its light, and that is on the night of the seventh. It was called a crescent because people raise their voices to inform about it when they see it, and from this the boy cried out: if he cried out, and his face became bright and cheerful: if joy appeared in it. His saying: “Say: These are appointed times for mankind and for Hajj.” This explains the wisdom behind the increase and decrease of the crescent moon, and that this is in order to explain the times by which people set their worship and transactions, such as fasting, breaking the fast, Hajj, the period of pregnancy, waiting period, contracts, oaths, and other things. Similar to this is the saying of God the Almighty: That you may know the number of years and the reckoning. The appointed times are the plural of miqat, which is time. The majority of scholars read Hajj with a fatha on the ha’. Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a kasra throughout the Qur’an. Sibawayh said: Hajj with a fatha is like radd and shadd, and with a kasra is like dhikr, two sources with the same meaning. It was said: with a fatha it is a source, and with a kasra it is the name. God the Almighty singled out Hajj for mention because it is something in which one needs to know the time, and it is not permissible to postpone it from its time, and because of the great hardship on one who is confused about the time of his rituals or makes a mistake in their time or the time of some of them. Some scholars of meaning have considered this answer, I mean his saying: “Say: They are fixed times” as a wise style, which is to receive the addressee with something other than what he anticipates, as a warning that it is more appropriate to intend, and the reason for that is that they asked about the celestial bodies with regard to their waxing and waning, so they were answered with the wisdom for which that waxing and waning was due, because that is more appropriate for the questioner to intend, and more deserving of his looking forward to his work. His saying: And righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs The reason for connecting this to the question about the crescents and the answer that they are fixed times for the people and the Hajj is that the Ansar, when they performed Hajj, would not enter through the doors of their houses if one of them returned to his house after his ihram before completing his Hajj, because they believed that no barrier could be allowed between the person in ihram and the sky, and they would climb the backs of their houses. Abu Ubaidah said: This is a proverb, and the meaning is: Righteousness is not to ask the ignorant, but righteousness is piety, so ask the scholars, as you say: I came to this matter from its door. It was said: It is a proverb about intercourse with women, and that they were ordered to have intercourse with them in the vagina, not the anus. Other than that was said. Houses is the plural of house, and it was read with a damma or a kasra on the ba. The interpretation of piety and success was presented previously, and it was also mentioned that the estimate in such as his saying: But righteousness is of he who fears God but righteousness is righteousness of he who fears God. Ibn Asakir narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: They ask you about the new moons. He said: It was revealed about Muadh ibn Jabal and Tha’laba ibn Uthma. They were two men from the Ansar who said: O Messenger of God, what is wrong with the crescent moon that appears and rises thin like a thread, then increases until it becomes large and even, then it continues to decrease and become thinner until it returns to its previous state? So, “They ask you about the new moons. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for the people.’” was revealed regarding the resolution of their religion, their fasting, their breaking of the fast, the number of their wives, and the conditions that are subject to a term. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: They asked the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about the new moons, why were they made? So God the Almighty revealed: They ask you about the new moons, the verse, and made it for the fasting of the Muslims, their breaking of the fast, their rituals, their Hajj, the number of their wives, and the place of their religion. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has appointed the new moons as times for the people, so fast when they see it and break your fast when they see it. If it is hidden from you, then count thirty days.” Ahmad, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Adi, and Al-Daraqutni narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Talq bin Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Umar. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: When they entered ihram in the pre-Islamic era, they would come to their houses from their backs, so the verse and not the land was revealed. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that was authentic on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Quraysh were called Al-Hams, and they would enter through the gates in the state of ihram, while the Ansar and the rest of the Arabs would not enter through a gate in the state of ihram. While the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was in a garden, he went out through its gate and Qutbah ibn Amir Al-Ansari went out with him. They said: O Messenger of God, Qutbah ibn Amir is a wicked man, and he went out with you through the gate. He said to him: What made you do what you did? He said: I saw you do it, so I did as you did. He said: I am an Ahmasi man. He said: My religion is your religion. Then God revealed the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. This meaning was narrated on the authority of a group of the Companions and the Followers.
2:190: There is no disagreement among scholars that fighting was forbidden before the migration, based on the Almighty’s saying: So pardon them and overlook and His saying: And leave them with gracious abandonment and His saying: You have no control over them and His saying: Repel evil with that which is better and similar things that were revealed in Mecca. When he migrated to Medina, God Almighty commanded him to fight, and this verse was revealed. It was said that the first thing that was revealed was the Almighty’s saying: Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged. When the verse was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would fight whoever fought him and refrain from whoever refrained from him until the Almighty’s saying was revealed: Kill the polytheists and His saying: And fight the polytheists all together. A group of the Salaf said: What is meant by His statement: 190- those who fight you is anyone other than women, children, monks, and the like. They considered this verse to be decisive and not abrogated. What is meant by aggression according to the people of the first opinion is fighting those who fight from the disbelieving sects. What is meant by it according to the second opinion is going beyond killing those who deserve to be killed to killing those who do not deserve it from those mentioned above.
2:191: His saying: 191- Where you find them It is said: Thaqaf, yathaqafan, thaqfan, and a man is thaqif: if he is well-versed in what he undertakes of matters. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: Thaqaf is existence in the manner of taking and dominating, and from it a man is thaqaf: quick to take from his peers. End. And from it is the saying of Hassan: If Banu Luayy defeats Juthaymah, killing them is a cure. His statement: And expel them from where they expelled you, meaning Mecca. Ibn Jarir said: The address is to the Muhajireen, and the pronoun refers to the infidels of Quraysh. End quote. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, obeyed the command of his Lord and expelled from Mecca those who had not converted to Islam when God conquered it for him. His statement: And persecution is worse than killing, meaning the persecution that they wanted to tempt you, which is your return to disbelief, is worse than killing. It was said that what is meant by persecution is the trial that befalls a person in his person, family, wealth, or honor. It was said that what is meant by persecution is the polytheism that the polytheists are upon, because they considered killing in the Sacred Mosque to be too great, so God informed them that the polytheism that they are upon is worse than what they considered too great. It was said that what is meant is their temptation of you to prevent you from the Sacred Mosque is worse than your killing them in the Sacred Mosque or their killing you if they kill you. It appears that what is meant is persecution in religion, for whatever reason it may be, and in whatever form it occurs, for it is worse than killing. His statement: And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram, the verse. Scholars differed on this. A group said that it is a decisive ruling and that fighting in the Sacred Sanctuary is not permissible except after a transgression is committed by fighting in it, in which case it is permissible to repel it by fighting him, and this is the truth. A group said that this verse was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. The response to this argument is that it is possible to combine the general with the specific, so the polytheist is killed wherever he is found except in the Sacred Sanctuary. What supports this is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): It was not permissible for anyone before me, but it was only permissible for me for one hour of the day. This is in Saheeh. Those who say that it was abrogated have cited as evidence the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) killing Ibn Khatal while he was clinging to the curtains of the Kaaba. The response to this is that it happened at that hour when God made it permissible for His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him).
2:192: His saying: 192- If they cease meaning from fighting you and enter Islam.
2:193: His statement: 193- And fight them until there is no more fitnah This is the command to fight the polytheists until there is no more fitnah and that the religion is for God, which is entering Islam and abandoning all other religions that oppose it. So whoever enters Islam and abandons polytheism, fighting him is not permissible. It was said: What is meant by fitnah here is polytheism, and it appears that it is fitnah in religion in general as mentioned above. His statement: There is no aggression except against the wrongdoers means do not transgress except against the one who has been wronged, which is the one who has not stopped the fitnah and has not entered Islam. Rather, the punishment of the wrongdoers is called aggression in imitation of the statement of God the Almighty: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it. And His statement: So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding his statement: And fight in the way of God that the verse was the first verse revealed about fighting in Madinah. When it was revealed, the Messenger of God would fight whoever fought him and refrain from whoever refrained from him, until Surah Bara’ah was revealed. Abd bin Hamid narrated from Mujahid regarding this verse, he said: The companions of Muhammad were ordered to fight the infidels. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not transgress, he said: Do not kill women, children, the elderly, or those who have offered their peace and withdrew their hands, for if you do, then you have transgressed. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Umar bin Abdul Aziz that he said: This verse is about women and children. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding his statement: And persecution is worse than killing, he said: Polytheism is worse than killing. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: A believer turning back to idolatry is worse for him than being killed justly. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you therein, he said: Until they initiate fighting. Then it was abrogated after that and he said: And fight them until there is no more persecution. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, and Abu Dawud in his Naskh narrated on the authority of Qatada that his statement: And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram, and his statement: “They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say, “Fighting therein is great,” was thus until these two verses were abrogated together in Bara’ah, his statement: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, “And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Then if they desist, he said: If they repent. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And fight them until there is no more persecution, he said: Associating partners with God is established, “and the religion is established,” and monotheism is sincere to God. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: Polytheism. And His statement: But if they desist, then there shall be no aggression except against the wrongdoers, he said: Do not fight except those who fight you. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ regarding His statement: And religion shall be for God, he said: Until you worship none but God. And he also narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding His statement: Then there shall be no aggression except against the wrongdoers, he said: They are from the one who refused to say there is no god but God. Abd bin Hamid bin Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada something similar.
2:194: His saying: 194- The sacred month for the sacred month meaning if they fight you in the sacred month and violate its sanctity, you will fight them in the sacred month as a reward for them and recompense for their action. And the sacred things is the plural of sacredness, like darkness is the plural of darkness. He only pluralized the sacred things because he meant the sacred month, the sacred land, and the sanctity of ihram. Sanctity is what the law forbids violating. And retaliation is equality, and the meaning is that retaliation is applied to every sacred thing, so whoever violates a sacred thing upon you, you may violate a sacred thing upon him in retaliation. It was said: This was in the beginning of Islam, then it was abrogated by fighting. It was said: It is established among the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was not abrogated. And it is permissible for someone who transgressed against him in money or body to transgress in the same way that he transgressed against him, and this is what Al-Shafi'i and others said. Others said: The matters of retaliation are limited to the rulers, and so is money, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Return the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you. Narrated by al-Daraqutni and others, and Abu Hanifa, the majority of the Malikis, and Ata’ al-Khurasani said the same. The first opinion is more correct, and Ibn al-Mundhir said the same, and Ibn al-Arabi and al-Qurtubi chose it, and al-Dawudi narrated it from Malik. It is supported by his permission (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for the wife of Abu Sufyan to take from his money what would suffice her and her child, and this is in Saheeh al-Bukhaari. There is nothing clearer and more explicit than the statement of God the Most High in this verse: But whoever has transgressed against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you. This sentence is an emphasis of the first sentence, I mean His statement: And for sacred things there is retaliation. Rather, He called the recompense a similar transgression, as mentioned above. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out to perform Umrah in the year six of the Hijrah, and the polytheists prevented him from entering and reaching the House, and they prevented him and the Muslims who were with him in Dhul-Qa’dah, which is a sacred month, he ordered them to enter the following year. So he entered it the following year, he and the Muslims who were with him, and God punished him for it. This verse was revealed concerning that: ‘A sacred month for a sacred month, and for sacred things there is legal retribution.’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah something similar. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar as well. They also narrated on the authority of Qatadah something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj something similar. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: ‘But whoever transgresses against you’ the verse. And His saying: And the recompense for evil verse, and His saying: And for him who retaliates after being wronged verse, and His saying: And if you punish verse, he said: This and similar things were revealed in Mecca, and the Muslims at that time were few and had no authority to subjugate the polytheists, so the polytheists used to treat them with insults and harm, so God commanded the Muslims, whoever among them was punished, to be punished in the same way as he was given, or to be patient and forgive. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina and God strengthened his authority, God commanded the Muslims to refer their grievances to their authority, and not to transgress against one another like the people of the Age of Ignorance, so He said: And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority verse, meaning: The authority supports him until he is justified against the one who wronged him, and whoever supports himself without the authority is a disobedient and extravagant who has acted with the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance and was not satisfied with the ruling of God Almighty. End quote. And I say: This verse that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, made abrogating, supports what is indicated by the verses that he made abrogated and confirms it. What is apparent from his statement: We have given his heir authority is that he gave him authority: that is, he gave him power by which he can control the killer. That is why he said: So let him not exceed limits in killing. Then, if we were to accept that the meaning of the verse is as he said, then that would be a specification of killing from the generality of the aforementioned verses, not an abrogator of them, because in this verse he only mentioned killing alone, and those verses include it and others. This is known from the language of the Arabs, which is the reference in interpreting the words of God Almighty.
2:195: In this verse there is an order to spend in the way of God, which is jihad, and the wording includes other things that are true of being in the way of God. The preposition ba in His statement: 195- with your hands is redundant, and the meaning is: and do not throw your hands, and similar to it is: Does he not know that God sees? Al-Mubarrad said: with your hands meaning with yourselves, expressing some of the whole, like His statement: for what your hands have earned. It was said: this is a proverb, it is said: So-and-so threw his hand in such-and-such a matter: if he surrendered, because the one who surrenders in battle throws his weapon with his hands, so the same is the action of every helpless person in any action. Some people said: the meaning is: and do not throw yourselves with your hands. Destruction: a source of destruction, yahliqu, hulkan, and hulkat: meaning do not engage in that which will destroy you. The predecessors have statements regarding the meaning of the verse, which will be explained, as well as the reason for the revelation of the verse. The truth is that the consideration is based on the generality of the wording and not on the specificity of the cause. Everything that is true of being a loss in religion or in this world is included in this, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said the same. Among the things that are included in the verse is a man who rushes into war and attacks the army while he is unable to escape and has no effect that benefits the mujahideen. This is not prevented from being included in the verse by the denial of those who denied it from those who saw the cause, for they thought that the verse does not go beyond its cause, and this is an assumption that the Arabic language rejects. His statement, and do good, means in spending in obedience, or have good thoughts about God in His failure to reward you. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Hudhayfah regarding the statement: And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction, he said: It was revealed about spending. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse: It is abandoning spending in the cause of God for fear of poverty. Abd bin Hamid and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar. Abd bin Hamid and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab on his authority: It is miserliness. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam regarding the verse: There were men who would go out on expeditions that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would send without spending, so either they would be cut off or they would have children, so God commanded them to spend from what God had provided for them and not to throw themselves with their own hands into destruction. And destruction: that men perish from hunger, thirst and walking. And he said to the one who had a surplus in his hand: And do good, for God loves the doers of good. And Abd bin Hamid, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Al-Baghawi in his Mu’jam, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mani’ and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Abi Jubayr: That the Ansar used to spend in the way of God and give charity, then a famine struck them and they thought badly of it and refrained from doing that, so God revealed the verse. And Abd bin Hamid, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, An-Nasa’i, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Aslam bin Imran who said: We were in Constantinople, and the people of Egypt were led by Uqba bin Amir, and the people of Ash-Sham were led by Fadala bin Ubayd, so a large column of Romans came out and we clapped for them, then a man from the Muslims charged the column of Romans until he entered them, so the people shouted and said: Glory be to God, is he throwing himself into destruction? Abu Ayyub, the companion of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), stood up and said: O people, you interpret the verse in this way. This verse was revealed about us, the Ansar, because when God made His religion victorious and its supporters increased, some of us said to one another secretly, without the Messenger of God (peace be upon him): The wealth of the people has been lost, and God has made Islam victorious and its supporters increased, so why don’t we stay with our wealth and repair what has been lost? So God revealed to His Prophet, responding to us: And spend in the cause of God and do not throw [yourselves] with your [own] hands into destruction. Destruction was staying with wealth, repairing it, and abandoning fighting. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, who said in his interpretation of the verse: It is a man who commits a sin and then throws his hands in it and says: God will never forgive me. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated something similar on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated that he said in his interpretation of the verse: It is despair. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Destruction is the punishment of God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth that they besieged Damascus and a man rushed to the enemy alone, so the Muslims criticized him for that, and his hadith was reported to Amr bin Al-Aas, so he sent for him and returned him, and said: God said: And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of a man from the Companions regarding His statement: And do good, he said: Fulfill the obligatory duties. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq something similar. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: Think well of God.
2:196: His statement: 196- And complete the Hajj. The scholars differed regarding the intended meaning of completing the Hajj and Umrah for God. It was said: Performing them and coming to them without any forbidden thing tainting them, and without violating a condition or obligation, as God the Almighty said: Then complete them and His statement: Then complete the fast until the night. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Their sin is that you go out for them and not for anyone else. It was said: Their completion is that you separate each one of them without enjoying or combining, and Ibn Habib said the same. Muqatil said: Their completion is that they do not make permissible in them what is not appropriate for them. It was said: Their completion is that he enters ihram for them from the circle of his family. It was said: That he spends on their journey what is lawful and good. The reason for the revelation of the verse and what is narrated from the predecessors regarding the meaning of their completion will come. This verse was used as evidence for the obligation of Umrah because the command to complete them was an order to do so. This is what Ali, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Ata, Tawoos, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Al-Sha'bi, Saeed Ibn Jubayr, Masruq, Abdullah Ibn Shaddad, Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Ubaid and Ibn Al-Jahm from the Malikis said. Malik, Al-Nakha'i and the people of opinion said, as narrated by Ibn Al-Mundhir, that they are Sunnah. It was narrated from Abu Hanifa that he said that they are obligatory. Among those who said that it is Sunnah are Ibn Mas'ud and Jabir Ibn Abdullah. Among the evidence used by the first scholars is what was proven from him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in Sahih that he said to his companions: Whoever has a sacrificial animal with him, let him enter into ihram for Hajj and Umrah. It was also proven from him in Sahih that he said: Umrah is included in Hajj until the Day of Resurrection. Ad-Daraqutni and Al-Hakim narrated from Zaid Ibn Thabit that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Hajj and Umrah are two obligations, and it does not matter which one you start with. Others cited as evidence what Al-Shafi’i narrated regarding the verse, and Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, and Abd Bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Abu Salih Al-Hanafi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hajj is jihad and Umrah is voluntary. Ibn Majah narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Talhah Bin Ubaidullah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Bin Hamid, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Jabir, “A man asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Umrah, is it obligatory? He said: No, and performing Umrah is better for you.” They responded to the verse and the hadiths that explicitly state that it is obligatory by interpreting that as meaning that one has entered into it, and that it is obligatory after beginning it, without dispute. Although this is far-fetched, it must be adhered to in order to reconcile the evidence, especially after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explicitly stated what was mentioned in the hadith of Jabir about it not being obligatory. This is what is reported that indicates its obligation, as Al-Shafi’i narrated in Al-Umm that in the letter that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to Amr Bin Hazm, it says: Umrah is the lesser Hajj. And as for the hadith of Ibn Umar in Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha`b, he said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Advise me.
