He said: Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, establish prayer, pay zakat, fast the month of Ramadan, perform Hajj and Umrah, listen and obey, and adhere to what is public, and avoid what is secret.” And thus should be understood what was reported from the hadiths in which Hajj and Umrah are linked, that they are among the best deeds, and that they are expiation for what came between them, and that they destroy what came before them, and so on. His statement: If you are prevented: prevention means confinement. Abu Ubaidah, Al-Kisa’i and Al-Khalil said: It is said: prevented by illness, and prevented by the enemy. In Al-Mujmal by Ibn Faris, the opposite is said: prevented by the enemy, and prevented by illness. Ibn Al-Arabi preferred the first and said: It is the opinion of most linguists. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the same according to all linguists. Al-Farra’ said: They have the same meaning in illness and enemy. Abu Amr Al-Shaibani agreed with him and said: The thing prevented me and prevented me: meaning it detained me. Because of this difference between the linguists, the scholars of jurisprudence differed in the meaning of the verse. The Hanafis said: The one who is prevented from entering Mecca after entering the state of ihram due to illness, enemy, or other reasons. The Shafi’is and the people of Medina said that what is meant by the verse is the one who is prevented from entering the state of ihram by an enemy. The majority of scholars have stated that the one who is prevented by an enemy is released from the state where he is prevented and slaughters his sacrificial animal if there is one and shaves his head, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions did at Al-Hudaybiyyah. His statement, and whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal is in the nominative case as a subject or predicate: meaning, it is obligatory or upon you. It is possible that it is in the accusative case, meaning, sacrifice or offer whatever is easy, meaning, what is easy. It is said, the matter became easy and was made easy, just as it is said, difficult and difficult. Hadi and Hadi are two languages, and they are the plural of Hadiyyah, which is what is offered to the House of a camel or other animal. Al-Farra’ said: The people of Hijaz and Banu Asad make the hadiy light, while Tamim and Lower Qays make it heavy. The poet said: I swear by the Kaaba, the place of prayer, and the necks of the sacrificial animals He said: The singular of hadi is hadiyyah, and it is said: in the plural of hadiyy it is ahd. The scholars differed about what is meant by his statement: what is easy. The majority of scholars said that it is a sheep. Ibn Umar, Aisha, and Ibn al-Zubayr said: a camel or a cow. Al-Hasan said: the highest hadiyy is a camel, the middle one is a cow, and the lowest is a sheep. His statement: And do not shave your heads until the hadiyy reaches its place is addressed to the entire nation, without differentiating between those who are prevented from performing Hajj or those who are not prevented. This is what a group of scholars agreed with. A group of scholars agreed that it is addressed to those who are prevented in particular: that is, do not end your state of ihram until you know that the hadiyy that you sent to the Haram has reached its place, which is the place where it is permissible to slaughter it. They differed about specifying it. Malik and al-Shafi’i said: it is the place of confinement, following the example of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when he was prevented in the year of al-Hudaybiyah. Abu Hanifa said: it is the Sacred Sanctuary, based on the statement of God the Almighty: Then its place of confinement is to the Ancient House. The response to this is that the one addressed is the one who is safe and can reach the House. The Hanafis responded to the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) slaughtering in Al-Hudaybiyah by saying that the end of Al-Hudaybiyah that is lower than Mecca is part of the Haram, and responded that the place where the slaughtering took place is not part of the Haram. His statement: But whoever among you is ill Al-Haytham 2:17, the meaning of illness here is what is true to the term illness in the language. What is meant by harm to the head is: lice or wounds and the like. The meaning of the verse is that whoever is ill or has harm to his head and shaves his head must pay a ransom. The Sunnah has explained what is stated here about fasting, charity and rituals. It is proven in the Sahih that “the Messenger of God saw Ka’b bin Ujrah while he was in the state of ihram and his lice were falling on his face, so he said: Are the lice on your head harming you? He said: Yes. So he ordered him to shave his head and feed six poor people, or sacrifice a sheep, or fast for three days.” Ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned that there is no disagreement among scholars that the ritual here is a sheep. It was reported from the majority that the fasting mentioned in the verse is three days, and feeding ten poor people. The authentic hadith mentioned above refutes them and refutes their statement. Malik, Ash-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifah, their companions and Dawud held that the feeding in this case is one mudd of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), i.e. for each poor person. Ath-Thawri said: Half a sa' of wheat or a sa' of other food. This was narrated from Abu Hanifah. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: This is wrong because in some of the reports of Ka'b it is mentioned that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Give in charity three sa' of dates to six poor people. The narrations from Ahmad ibn Hanbal differed. It was narrated from him like what Malik and Ash-Shafi'i said. It was narrated from him that if he fed wheat, then he should give a mudd to each poor person, and if he fed dates, then he should give half a sa'. They differed about the place of this ransom. Ata' said: Whatever was from blood, then it is in Makkah, and whatever was from food or fasting, then it is wherever he wants. The people of opinion said the same. Tawus and Ash-Shafi'i said: Feeding and blood can only be in Makkah, and fasting is wherever he wants. Malik and Mujahid said: Wherever he wants in all cases, and this is the truth because there is no evidence to specify the place. His statement: And when you are safe, whoever performs ‘Umrah until Hajj, then whatever is easy of sacrificial animal means you are free from sickness. It was said: from your fear of the enemy, according to the previous disagreement. However, safety from the enemy is more evident than the use of you are safe to mean the disappearance of sickness, so it strengthens the statement of those who said that his statement: But if you are prevented means being prevented by the enemy, just as his statement: But whoever among you is ill strengthens the statement of those who said that because the excuse of sickness is mentioned alone. There was disagreement as to whether the addressees of this are those who are prevented specifically or the entire nation, according to what was mentioned previously. What is meant by the enjoyment mentioned in the verse is that a man enters ihram for ‘Umrah, then resides in Makkah as a permissible pilgrim until he enters ihram for Hajj. In doing so, he has made permissible what is not permissible for the pilgrim to make permissible, and this is the meaning of enjoyment and enjoyment. There is no disagreement among the scholars regarding the permissibility of enjoyment, rather in my opinion it is the best type of Hajj, as I explained in my explanation of Al-Muntaqa. The disagreement regarding the meaning of his statement: Then whatever is easy of sacrificial animal has already been mentioned. His saying: And whoever does not find the verse, meaning whoever does not find the sacrificial animal, either due to lack of money or lack of an animal, fasts three days during Hajj: meaning during the days of Hajj, which is from when he begins to enter ihram until the Day of Sacrifice. It was said: He fasts one day before the Day of Tarwiyah, the Day of Tarwiyah, and the Day of Arafah. It was said: What is between entering ihram for Hajj and the Day of Arafah. It was said: He fasts them from the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. It was said: As long as he is in Mecca. It was said: It is permissible for him to fast the three days before entering ihram. Some scholars have permitted fasting the days of Tashreeq for someone who does not find the sacrificial animal, while others have forbidden it. His saying: And seven when you return The majority read it with the accusative of seven, and Zaid bin Ali and Ibn Abi Ubla read it with the accusative as if it is the object of an implied verb: meaning and fast seven. It was said: It is conjoined with three, because even though it is in the genitive case in form, it is in the accusative case as if it was said: So fasting three. What is meant by returning here is returning to the homelands. Ahmad and Ishaq said: Fasting on the road is sufficient for him, and the obligation is not restricted to him unless he reaches his homeland. This is what Ash-Shafi’i, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’, Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan and others said. Malik said: If he returns from Mina, there is no problem with him fasting, and the first is more correct. It is proven in Sahih from the hadith of Ibn Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever cannot find the days should fast three days during Hajj and seven when he returns to his family. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) explained that the return mentioned in the verse is the return to the family. It is also proven in Sahih from the hadith of Ibn Abbas with the wording: and seven when you return to your cities. The Almighty said: Those are ten complete days even though everyone knows that three and seventeen are ten, to prevent someone from imagining that he has a choice between the three days during Hajj and the seven when he returns. Az-Zajjaj said: Al-Mubarrad said: This was mentioned to indicate the expiration of the number so that someone would not imagine that something was lost after mentioning the seven. It was said: It is an emphasis, as you say, I wrote it with my own hand. The Arabs used to come up with such eloquence in less than this number, as the poet said: Three and two, so they are five and six, tending towards my arrows And so said the other. Three on the counter and that's enough for me, and six when I get to dinner That is nine times a day, and drinking more than that is a disease. His saying: Complete is another emphasis after the explanation to increase the recommendation to fast it, and not to reduce its number. His saying: That is for those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque The reference in his saying: That is said to refer to enjoyment, so it indicates that there is no enjoyment for those present at the Sacred Mosque, as Abu Hanifa and his companions say. They said: Whoever enjoys among them must offer a blood sacrifice, which is the blood sacrifice of a crime, and he should not eat from it. It is said: It refers to the ruling, which is the obligation of the sacrifice and fasting, so that is not obligatory for those present at the Sacred Mosque, as Al-Shafi’i and those who agreed with him say. What is meant by those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque is: those who do not reside in the Haram, or those who do not reside at the miqats or below them, according to the difference of opinion among the Imams on that. His saying: And fear God means in what He has imposed upon you in these rulings. It is said: It is an order to fear God in general and a warning against the severity of the punishment of God, the Most High. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu`aym in Ad-Dala’il, and Ibn `Abd al-Barr in At-Tamhid narrated on the authority of Ya`la ibn Umayyah who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Al-Ji`ranah, wearing a cloak and with traces of saffron on it. He said: ‘What do you command me, O Messenger of God, to do with my `Umrah?’ So God revealed: ‘And complete the Hajj and `Umrah for God.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And complete the Hajj and `Umrah for God.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Where is the one who asked about `Umrah?’ He said: ‘Here I am.’ He said: ‘Take off the cloak and wash away the traces of saffron from yourself, then do with your `Umrah whatever you were doing in your Hajj.’” Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated it from his hadith, but in them it was revealed to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the question was asked, and he did not mention what was revealed to him. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of `Ali regarding his statement: ‘And complete the Hajj and `Umrah for God.’ He said: ‘That you enter ihram from your family’s house.’ Ibn `Adi and Al-Bayhaqi narrated a similar hadith from Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: Part of completing it is to separate each one of them from the other, and to perform Umrah outside the months of Hajj. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The completion of Hajj is on the Day of Sacrifice when one throws the pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqabah and visits the House, then he has become free from the obligation. The completion of Umrah is when one circumambulates the House, Safa and Marwah, then he has become free from the obligation. Many hadiths have been narrated about the merits of Hajj and Umrah, but this is not the place to mention them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: But if you are prevented he said: Whoever enters into Ihram for Hajj or Umrah and is prevented from entering the House due to an illness that exhausts him or an enemy that prevents him, then he must slaughter whatever he can of sacrificial animal, a sheep or more, and if it is the Hajj of Islam then he must make it up, but if it is after the obligatory Hajj then he does not have to make it up. Sa`id ibn Mansur, `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement: But if you are prevented meaning: If a man enters ihram for Hajj and is prevented, he sends whatever is easy of sacrificial animals. If he hastens before the sacrificial animals reach their destination and shaves his head, or applies perfume, or takes medicine, he must pay a ransom of fasting, charity or a sacrifice. Fasting is three days, charity is three sa`s given to six poor people, each poor person gets half a sa`, and the sacrifice is a sheep. But when you are safe meaning: If he recovers and proceeds from that destination to the House, he is released from his Hajj with an `Umrah, and Hajj is required of him the following year. If he returns and does not complete that destination to the House, he must perform Hajj and `Umrah. If he returns enjoying himself during the months of Hajj, he must pay whatever is easy of sacrificial animals, a sheep. If he cannot find any, he must fast for three days during Hajj and seven upon his return. Ibrahim said: I mentioned this hadith to Sa`id ibn Jubayr and he said: This is what Ibn `Abbas said about the entire hadith. Malik, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ali regarding the statement of God, Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, he said: A sheep. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated similarly on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Shafi’i narrated in Al-Umm, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi, Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, he said: A cow or a camel. It was said: Is a sheep sufficient for him? He said: No. Abd Al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour and Abd bin Humayd narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said in the interpretation of What is easy: What he can find. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: If he is well off, then from a camel. Otherwise, then from a cow. Otherwise, then from sheep. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Qasim on the authority of Aisha and Ibn Umar that they did not consider the sacrificial animal as easy except camels and cows. Ibn Abbas used to say: The sacrificial animal as easy as a sheep. Ash-Shafi’i narrated in al-Umm, Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: There is no confinement except the confinement of the enemy. As for the one who is afflicted with illness, pain or straying, there is nothing upon him. God only said: When you are secure, so security can only come from fear. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: There is no confinement except from an enemy. He also narrated something similar on the authority of al-Zuhri. He also narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: There is no confinement except from illness, an enemy or a new matter. He also narrated on the authority of Urwah who said: Everything that prevents the pilgrim from performing Hajj is confinement. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of al-Miswar that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) slaughtered an animal before shaving his head and ordered his companions to do the same. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination, then he made an exception and said: But whoever among you is ill, the verse. At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah who said: It was revealed about me and I, meaning: But whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his head. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: But whoever among you is ill, meaning whoever is severely ill. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority. He said: What is meant by illness is that there is an ailment or sores on his head, or an ailment in his head. He said: The ailment is lice. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The ritual mentioned in the verse is a sheep. A similar hadith was also narrated on the authority of Ali. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: But whoever performs ‘Umrah until Hajj, he said: whoever enters ihram for ‘Umrah during the months of Hajj. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that Az-Zubayr used to say: Mut'ah is only for those who are prevented, not for those who are released. Ibn Abbas said: It is for those who are prevented and those who are released. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ali regarding his statement: {And when you are secure, whoever performs the 'Umrah during the Hajj} that he said: If he delays the 'Umrah until he combines it with the Hajj, then he must offer a sacrifice. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ali Ibn Abi Talib regarding his statement: {Then fasting three days} that he said: One day before Tarwiyah, the day of Tarwiyah and the day of 'Arafah. If he misses them, he fasts them during the days of Tashreeq. These people except Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Umar something similar except that he said: If he misses them, he fasts the days of Mina, because they are part of the Hajj. Ibn Jarir, Ad-Darqutni and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from Ibn 'Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar from Alqamah, Mujahid and Sa'id Ibn Jubayr. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Fasting for the one performing Tamattu’ is between his Ihram and the Day of Arafah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: If the one performing Tamattu’ for Umrah does not find a sacrificial animal, then he must fast three days during Hajj before the Day of Arafah. If the Day of Arafah is the third, then his fast is complete, and seven days when he returns to his family. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Aisha who heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “Whoever does not have a sacrificial animal with him should fast three days before the Day of Sacrifice. Whoever has not fasted those three days should fast the Days of Tashreeq.” He also narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Hudhafah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered him and a group of people to circumambulate Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and to call out: These are days of eating, drinking, and remembering God, so we should not fast during them except fasting as a sacrificial animal. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding the words of God the Almighty: That is for those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque, he said: Six towns: Arafat, Urnah, Raji’, An-Nakhlataan, Marr Adh-Dhahran, and Dajnan. Mujahid said: They are the people of the Sacred Sanctuary. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He said: They are the people of the Sacred Sanctuary. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar.
2:197: His saying: 197- The Hajj is months is omitted, and the meaning is: the time of Hajj is months, meaning the time of performing Hajj. It was said that the meaning is: Hajj is in months, and in it it is necessary to put the accusative with the deletion of the preposition, not the nominative. Al-Farra' said: The months is nominative because its meaning is the time of Hajj, the known months, and it was said that the meaning is: Hajj is Hajj in the known months. There is disagreement regarding the known months, so Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Umar, Ata', Al-Rabi', Mujahid and Al-Zuhri said: They are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and all of Dhul-Hijjah, and Malik said the same. Ibn Abbas, Al-Suddi, Al-Sha'bi and Al-Nakha'i said: They are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, and Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and others said the same. It was also narrated from Malik. The benefit of the disagreement appears in what happened from the Hajj actions after the Day of Sacrifice, so whoever said that the entirety of Dhul-Hijjah is from the time, he is not required to pay the blood money for delay, and whoever said: Only ten days of it said: he is required to pay the blood money for delay. This verse was used as evidence by those who said that it is not permissible to assume ihram for Hajj before the months of Hajj. They are Ata’, Tawoos, Mujahid, Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr. They said: Whoever assumes ihram for Hajj before that, then he is released from ihram for Umrah, and it does not suffice for him as ihram for Hajj, just like someone who begins a prayer before its time, for it does not suffice for him. Ahmad and Abu Hanifa said: It is only disliked. Something similar was narrated from Malik, and the well-known opinion from him is that it is permissible to assume ihram for Hajj throughout the year without dislike. Something similar was narrated from Abu Hanifa. According to this opinion, the benefit of timing Hajj with the months mentioned in the verse should be considered. It was said: The text on this was to increase its virtue. It has been narrated that Ihram is permissible throughout the year from Ishaq bin Rahawayh, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, al-Thawri, and al-Layth bin Sa’d. They provided evidence for this with the words of God Almighty: “They ask you about the new moons. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj.’” So he made all the new moons measurements of time for Hajj, and did not specify the three months. The response is that this verse is general, and that one is specific, and the specific takes precedence over the general. Among the things they used as evidence is the analogy of Hajj to Umrah. Just as it is permissible to enter ihram for Umrah throughout the year, it is also permissible for Hajj. It is clear that this analogy contradicts the Qur’anic text and is therefore invalid. The truth is what the first scholars went for if the months mentioned in His statement: Hajj is months are specific to the three mentioned by text or consensus. If that is not the case, then months is the plural of month, which is a plural of fewness that fluctuates between three and ten, and three is the certainty and must be stopped at. The meaning of His statement: well-known is that Hajj is once a year in well-known months of its months, not like Umrah. Or what is meant is well-known by the explanation of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or well-known to those addressed and it is not permissible to advance or delay them. And His statement: So whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them The root of obligation in the language is: cutting and severing, and from it is the obligation of the bow, the river and the mountain. So the obligation of Hajj is binding upon the free slave as the cutting is binding upon the bow. It was said that the meaning of obligation is: to make clear, and it also refers to cutting, because whoever cuts something has made it clear from something else. The meaning of the verse: Whoever commits himself to Hajj during them by starting it with the intention inwardly, and by entering ihram outwardly, and by uttering the Talbiyah. Abu Hanifa said: He commits himself to it by the Talbiyah or by wearing the sacrificial animal and driving it. Al-Shafi’i said: The intention is sufficient for entering ihram for Hajj. Al-Rafth Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jarir, Al-Suddi, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Al-Zuhri, Mujahid and Malik said: It is sexual intercourse. Ibn Omar, Tawus, Ata’ and others said: Al-Rafth is obscene speech. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Rafth is idle talk, and he recited: And the pilgrims' flocks are restrained from idle talk and obscene speech. It is said: Rafth yarfath with a kasra or damma on the fa. Fusuq: going beyond the limits of the Sharia. It was also said: it is slaughtering to idols. It was also said: calling each other names. It was also said: cursing. It appears that it is not specific to a particular sin, but rather it was specified by those who specified it with what was mentioned, considering that the name Fusuq was given to that individual, as God the Almighty said about slaughtering to idols: Or a sin dedicated to other than God. And He said about name calling: A bad name is Fusuq. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said about cursing: Cursing a Muslim is Fusuq. It is not hidden from anyone who knows that giving the name Fusuq to an individual sin does not necessitate that it is specific to it. Al-Jadaal is derived from Al-Jadaal, which means killing, and what is meant by it here is argument. It was also said: cursing. It was also said: boasting about one’s fathers. The first appears. It has been read with the accusative and nominative of the three, the nominative of the first two, the accusative of the third, and vice versa. The meaning of negating these matters is prohibiting them. His statement: And whatever good you do, God knows it is an exhortation to do good after mentioning evil, and to obey after mentioning disobedience. It indicates that everything they do is known to God and nothing of it is missed. His statement: And take provisions is an order to take provisions, because some Arabs used to say: How can we perform Hajj to the House of our Lord without Him feeding us? So they used to perform Hajj without provisions and say: We trust in God, the Most High. It was said that the meaning is: Take provisions for your return from righteous deeds, For indeed, the best provision is fear of God. The first is more likely, as is indicated by the reason for the revelation of the verse, which will come. His statement: For indeed, the best provision is fear of God is informing us that the best provision is avoiding prohibitions. It is as if he said: Fear God in doing what He has commanded you to do by going out with provisions, for indeed, the best provision is fear of God. It was said that the meaning is: Indeed, the best provision is that which protects the traveler from destruction and the need to ask and beg. His saying: And fear God, O you of understanding specifically addresses those of understanding after urging all servants to fear God, because those of understanding are those who accept God’s commands and rise to them, and the core of everything is His essence.
2:198: His statement: 198- There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord This includes permission for those who perform Hajj to engage in trade and similar work that brings in some provision, which is what is meant by bounty here, and from this is the statement of God the Almighty: So spread throughout the land and seek from the bounty of God meaning there is no sin upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. While you are traveling to perform what He has made obligatory upon you of Hajj. His statement: Then when you have poured out means you have paid, it is said that the vessel has poured out: if what He has made obligatory upon you of Hajj is filled. His statement: Then when you have poured out means you have paid, it is said that the vessel has poured out: if it is filled with water until it pours out from its sides, and a man who is generous: meaning his hands are overflowing with giving, and its meaning is: you have poured out yourselves, so he left out mentioning the object, as he left out in their statement they pushed from such and such a place. Arafat: is the name of that spot, meaning the place of standing. The group read it with tanween. The tanween here is not to differentiate between what is declined and what is not, but it is like the nun in Muslims. An-Nahhas said: This is good. Sibawayh narrated from the Arabs the deletion of the tanween from Arafat. He said: When they made it a definite noun, they deleted the tanween. Al-Akhfash and the Kufians narrated the opening of the ta’ in imitation of the ta’ of Fatima, and they recited: Her skirt is from the arms and her people are in Yathrib, the lowest part of her house, a high view He said in Al-Kashshaf: If you say, Why didn’t it prevent inflection? and it has two reasons, definiteness and femininity, I say: The femininity is not without it, either by the ta’ in its wording, or by an implied ta’ as in Su’ad, the one in its wording is not for femininity but rather it is with the alif before it, a sign of the feminine plural, and it is not correct to implied the ta’ in it because this ta’, due to its being specific to the feminine plural, prevents its implied implied, just as the ta’ of femininity is not implied in bint because the ta’ that is a substitute for the waw due to its being specific to the feminine like the ta’ of femininity, so it refused to be implied. It was called ‘Arafat because people get to know each other there, and it was said that Adam and Eve met there and got to know each other, and other things were said. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: It appears that it is an improvised name like all the names of places, and he used the verse as evidence for the obligation of standing at ‘Arafat. Because the Ifadah does not happen except after it, and what is meant by the remembrance of God at the Sacred Monument is supplication to it, including the Talbiyah and Takbir. The Mash'ar was named Mash'ar from the sign, which is the mark, and supplication at it is one of the rituals of Hajj, and it was described as Sacred because of its sanctity. It was said that what is meant by remembrance is the Maghrib and Isha prayers at Muzdalifah combined. The scholars have unanimously agreed that the Sunnah is for the pilgrim to combine them there. The Mash'ar is Mount Qazah on which the Imam stands, and it was said that it is the area between the two mountains of Muzdalifah from the passes of Arafat to Wadi Muhsar. His saying: And remember Him as He has guided you. The kaf is an attribute of an omitted source, and ma is a source or a collective noun, meaning remember Him with a good remembrance, as He has guided you with a good guidance. The command to remember is repeated for emphasis. It has been said that the first is a command to remember at the sacred monument, and the second is a command to remember according to the rule of sincerity. It has been said that what is meant by the second is to enumerate the blessings upon them, and in His saying: And if you were before it it is lightened as is indicated by the inclusion of the lam in the report. It has been said that it means qad: meaning you were, and the pronoun in His saying: before it refers back to the guidance, and it has been said: to the Qur’an. Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said regarding the verse: The Hajj is in well-known months, Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah, and Dhul-Hijjah. Al-Tabarani also narrated in Al-Awsat on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Al-Khatib also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Sa’id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Al-Shafi’i narrated in Al-Umm, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ata’, and Al-Dahhak narrated similarly. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan, through the chains of transmission of Ibn Umar, regarding his statement: The Hajj is in well-known months, he said: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah, and ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah. They narrated similarly, except for Al-Hakim, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas through similar chains of transmission. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Daraqutni, Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr also narrated something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Hasan, Muhammad and Ibrahim. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding the statement of God, And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein, he said: Whoever intends to perform Hajj therein. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: The obligation is Ihram. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr who said: Ihram. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Daraqutni and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority who said: The obligation of Hajj is Ihram. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The obligation is Ihram. Something similar was narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un. Ash-Shafi’i narrated in Al-Umm, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: No one should assume Ihram for Hajj except during the months of Hajj because of the statement of God, the Most High, Hajj is [during] well-known months. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Khuzaymah, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from him. Al-Shafi’i narrated in Al-Umm, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Jabir from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: No one should assume ihram for Hajj except during the months of Hajj. Al-Tabarani narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said regarding the verse: There is no obscenity, no wickedness and no disputing during Hajj, “Rubbish means exposing oneself to women for sexual intercourse, wickedness means all sins, and disputing means a man arguing with his companion.” Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Asbahani narrated in Al-Targheeb from Abu Umamah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is no obscenity, no sexual intercourse, and wickedness means sins and lying. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan through various chains of narration from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: Rubbish means sexual intercourse, wickedness means sins, and disputing means argument. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar from him. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat narrated from Ibn Umar who said: Al-Rafth means intercourse with women, Al-Fusuq means cursing, and Al-Jidal means argument. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from him. Something similar to what was mentioned above was narrated from a group of the Tabi’een with different wordings. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i and others narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: The people of Yemen used to perform Hajj without taking any provisions and would say: We are relying on God. Then they would go and ask people for provisions, so God revealed: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him who said: There were people who would leave their families and not have any provisions with them and would say: Shall we perform Hajj to the House of God and He will not feed us? So the verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: When they entered ihram and had their provisions with them, they would throw them away and start over with other provisions. Then God revealed: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. They were forbidden from that and were commanded to take provisions of cakes, flour, and gruel. At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr who said: People used to rely on one another for provisions, so God commanded them to take provisions. A group of the Tabi’een narrated something similar to what was mentioned above from the Companions. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: They used to avoid buying and selling during the Hajj season and Hajj and would say: These are the days of remembrance of God. Then, There is no blame upon you was revealed. Al-Bukhari and others narrated something similar from him. Abd ibn Humayd, Abd al-Razzaq, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Tamimi who said: I said to Ibn Umar: We are people who rent, so is there any Hajj for us? He said: Do you not circumambulate the House, and between Safa and Marwa, and come to Al-Ma`rif, and throw stones at the Jamarat, and shave your heads? I said: Yes. Ibn `Umar said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him about what you asked me about, but he did not answer him until Gabriel revealed to him this verse: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called him and recited the verse to him and said: And you are pilgrims. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas that he used to recite There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the Hajj seasons. `Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr that he recited it as Ibn `Abbas had recited it. Ibn Abi Dawud narrated in al-Masahif that Ibn Mas`ud recited it in the same way. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas that he said: It was called `Arafat because Gabriel used to say to Abraham (peace be upon him) when he saw the rituals: I have recognised them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn `Umar. And Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ali. And Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Umar that he was asked about Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram. And Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on his authority that he said: Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram is all of Muzdalifah. And Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on his authority that he said: It is the mountain and what is around it. And Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: It is what is between the two mountains that are in the vicinity of Al-Mash'ar. And Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr regarding the statement of God, And remember Him as He has guided you, that he said: This is not general. It is for the people of the city, they used to depart from Jam' and the rest of the people would depart from Arafat, but God refused that for them, so He revealed: Then depart from where the people depart. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Sufyan regarding his statement: And if you were before it, he said: before the Qur’an. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And if you were before it among those astray, he said: among the ignorant.
2:199: It was said: The address in His statement: 199- Then hasten is to the people of Quraysh because they did not stand with the people at Arafat, but they stood at Muzdalifah, which is part of the Haram, so they were commanded to do so - and based on this, then is to connect one sentence to another, not for order - and it was said: The address is to the entire nation, and what is meant by the people is Abraham: that is, then hasten from where Abraham hastened, so it is possible that it is an order for them to hasten from Arafat, and it is possible that it is another hasten, which is from Muzdalifah, and based on this, then is in its context, that is for order. This last possibility was preferred by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari, and they were commanded to seek forgiveness because they were in the places of mercy, the places of acceptance, and the places of expectation of response - and it was said: The meaning is seek forgiveness for what was contrary to the Sunnah of Abraham, which is your standing at Muzdalifah rather than Arafat.
2:200: What is meant by the rituals are the acts of Hajj, and from this is the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): Learn from me your rituals meaning when you have finished the acts of Hajj, then remember God. It was said that what is meant by the rituals are the sacrifices, and the Almighty said 200- like your remembrance of your fathers because when the Arabs finished their Hajj, they would stand at the Jamrah and remember the glories of their fathers and the virtues of their ancestors, so God commanded them to remember Him in place of that remembrance, and to make it a remembrance like their remembrance of their fathers or more intense than their remembrance of their fathers. Al-Zajjaj said: His saying: or more intense is in the accusative case in apposition to your remembrance, and the meaning is: or more intense in remembrance, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case: meaning remember Him more intensely. He said in Al-Kashshaf: It is in apposition to what the remembrance was added to in His saying: like your remembrance just as you say like the remembrance of Quraysh of their fathers or a people more intense in remembrance than them. His saying: And among the people is he who says the verse, when the Almighty guided His servants to remember Him, and supplication was a type of remembrance, He made those who call upon Him divided into two groups: one of them seeks the portion of this world and does not pay attention to the portion of the Hereafter, and the other group seeks both matters together, and the object of the verb, I mean His saying: Give us is omitted: meaning what we want or what we ask for, and the waw in His saying: And what does he have is the waw of the state, and the sentence after it is a state. And the creator: the share: meaning what this supplicant has in the Hereafter of a share, because his concern is limited to this world, he does not want anything other than it and does not ask for anything other than it. And in this report there is the meaning of prohibiting limiting oneself to seeking this world and blaming whoever makes it the ultimate goal of his desire and the majority of his aim.
2:201: There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of the two good deeds mentioned in the verse. It was said: They are what the righteous seek in this world of well-being and what is necessary of provision, and what they seek in the Hereafter of the bliss of Paradise and contentment. It was said that what is meant by the good deed of this world is a beautiful wife, and the good deed of the Hereafter is the houris. It was said: The good deed of this world is knowledge and worship, and other things were said. Al-Qurtubi said: What most scholars agree upon is that what is meant by the two good deeds is the bliss of this world and the Hereafter. He said: This is correct, because the wording requires all of this, because the good deed is indefinite in the context of supplication, so it is possible for every good deed to be substituted, and the good deed of the Hereafter is Paradise by consensus. End quote. His statement: 201- "َقَقنا" And protect us is originallyأَقَقناand the waw was deleted as it was deleted inيتقي(yaqī because it is between a ya and a kasra likeَقدhe uses, this is the opinion of the Basrans. The Kufians said: It was deleted to differentiate between the intransitive and the transitive.
2:202: And his saying 202- Those refers to the second group They will have a share of the type of what they have earned of deeds: that is, of their reward, and among their deeds is supplication, so whatever good God has given them because of it is from what they have earned, and it was said: The meaning of his saying: of what they have earned is the al-Sharh 94:that is, because of what they have earned, and this is far-fetched, and it was said: His saying: Those refers to both groups together: that is, the first ones have a share of this world and no share in the hereafter, and the last ones have a share of what they have earned in this world and in the hereafter. And sari' from sara'a yasra' like azama yazam sara'a and sara'a, and the account is a source like accounting, and its origin is the number, it is said: hasaba yasaban hisaban, and hisabah and hisaban and hisaban. What is meant here is the account, it is called a reckoning, naming the object with the source, and the meaning is: His reckoning of His servants on the Day of Resurrection will come quickly, so hasten to do good deeds, or he described himself as being quick to reckon with the creatures despite their large number, and that no matter distracts Him from another matter, so He reckons them in one instance, as God Almighty said: He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul.
2:203: His saying: 203- On appointed days Al-Qurtubi said: There is no disagreement among scholars that the appointed days in this verse are the days of Mina, which are the days of Tashreeq, which are the days of stoning the Jamarat. Al-Tha'labi said: Ibrahim said: The appointed days are the ten days, and the designated days are the days of sacrifice. This was also narrated from Makki and Al-Mahdawi. Al-Qurtubi said: It is not correct for what we mentioned of consensus on what Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr and others transmitted. Al-Tahawi narrated from Abu Yusuf that the designated days are the days of sacrifice. He said: Because of the saying of God the Almighty: And mention the name of God on appointed days over what He has provided for them of cattle. Al-Karkhi narrated from Muhammad bin Al-Hasan that the designated days are the three days of sacrifice: the day of Al-Adha and the two days after it. Al-Kaya Al-Tabari said: According to the saying of Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, there is no difference between the designated and the appointed days, because the designated days mentioned in the Qur'an are the days of Tashreeq without disagreement. It was narrated from Malik that the numbered days and the known days are collected into four days: the Day of Sacrifice and the three days after it. The Day of Sacrifice is known but not numbered, the two days after it are known but numbered, and the fourth day is numbered but not known. This was narrated from Ibn Umar. Ibn Zayd said: The known days are other than Dhul-Hijjah and the days of Tashreeq. The addressee of this address mentioned in the verse, I mean the Almighty’s saying: And remember God during the appointed days, is the pilgrim and others, as the majority have stated. It was also said that it is specific to the pilgrim. The scholars differed regarding its time. It was said: From the dawn prayer on the Day of Arafah until the afternoon prayer of the last days of Tashreeq. It was also said: From the morning of Arafah until the afternoon prayer of the last days of Sacrifice. This is what Abu Hanifa said. It was also said: From the noon prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the dawn prayer of the last days of Tashreeq. This is what Malik and Ash-Shafi’i said. His saying: But whoever hastens the verse, the two days are the second day of Sacrifice and its third day. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah and Al-Nakha’i said: Whoever stones on the second of the appointed days, there is no blame upon him, and whoever delays until the third, there is no blame upon him. The meaning of the verse is that all of that is permissible. This division was expressed as a concern and emphasis, because some Arabs condemned haste, and some condemned delay. So the verse was revealed to remove success in all of that. Ali and Ibn Mas’ud said: The meaning of the verse is: Whoever hastens will be forgiven, and whoever delays will be forgiven. The verse indicates that haste and delay are permissible. His statement, for him who fears God means that the choice and removal of sin are established for the one who fears God, because the one who has taqwa avoids everything that would cause him doubt, so he is more deserving of being singled out for this ruling. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is for whoever fears God. It was also said: for whoever fears God after returning from the Hajj from all sins. It was also said: for whoever fears killing game. It was also said that its meaning is: safety for whoever fears God. It was also said that it is related to the remembrance: meaning the remembrance is for whoever fears God. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: “The Quraysh and those who followed their religion used to stand at Muzdalifah and they called it Al-Hams, and the rest of the Arabs used to stand at Arafat. When Islam came, God ordered His Prophet to come to Arafat, then stand there, then depart from it. This is what God the Almighty said: ‘Then proceed from where the people proceed.’” They also narrated on her authority a similar hadith. There are narrations on this meaning from the Companions and the Followers. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: When the Day of Arafat comes, God descends to the lowest heaven with the angels and says to them: My servants believed in My promise and believed in My messengers, what is their reward? It is said: That you forgive them. This is what God the Almighty said: ‘Then proceed from where the people proceed and ask forgiveness of God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.’ Many hadiths have been narrated about the forgiveness of the people of Arafat, the descent of mercy upon them, and the answering of their supplications. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding the words of God the Almighty: And when you have completed your rites, he said: your Hajj. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the words of God the Almighty: And when you have completed your rites, he said: shedding blood. Then remember God as you remember your fathers, he said: The Arabs used to boast among themselves about the deeds of their fathers on the Day of Sacrifice when they finished, so they were commanded to remember God instead of that. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The polytheists used to sit during Hajj and remember the days of their fathers and what they counted of their lineages on that day, so God revealed to His Messenger: Then remember God as you remember your fathers or with a greater remembrance. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah something similar as well. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: As you remember your fathers, he said: as children remember their fathers. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the statement of God, Like your remembrance of your fathers, that a day may come upon a man and he does not remember his father, so he said, That is not the case, but he says, ‘You become more angry for the sake of God if He is disobeyed than you are if your father is mentioned in a bad way.’ Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said, “A group of Bedouins used to come to the gatherings and say, ‘O God, make it a year of rain, a year of fertility, and a year of good offspring.’ They did not mention anything about the Hereafter, so God revealed about them, “And among the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter.” And others of the believers come after them and say, Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. So God revealed about them, Those will have a share of what they have earned, and God is swift in account. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr who said: When people in the pre-Islamic era stopped at the sacred monument, they would supplicate. One of them would say: O God, provide me with camels, and the other would say: O God, provide me with sheep. Then God revealed the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Anas that they would circumambulate the Kaaba naked and supplicate: O God, send us rain, grant us victory over our enemy, and return us righteous to righteous people. Then the verse was revealed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding His statement: Those will have a share of what they have earned, he said: of the good they did. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: Swift in account, he said: Swift in counting. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali who said: The numbered days are three days: the day of Al-Adha and the two days after it. Slaughter on whichever of them you wish, but the best of them is the first. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that they are the three days of Tashreeq. In another version: These three days after the day of sacrifice. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab and Al-Dhiya' in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The appointed days are the ten days, and the numbered days are the days of Tashreeq. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr, who said regarding His statement: And mention the name of God during the appointed days, that they are the days of Tashreeq, in which he mentions with glorification, praise, magnification, and thanks. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The appointed days are four days: the Day of Sacrifice and the three days after it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he used to say the takbir on those days in Mina and said that the takbir is obligatory, and he interpreted this verse: And remember God during the appointed days. Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to say the takbir on the Day of Sacrifice and recite this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding His statement: And remember God during the appointed days, that he said: The takbir is on the days of Tashreeq, in which he says after each prayer: God is Great, God is Great, God is Great. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he used to say Allahu Akbar three times after the prayers and say: There is no god but God alone, with no partner, His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. Malik narrated on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id that he heard that Umar ibn al-Khattab went out the next day on the Day of Sacrifice to Mina when the day had risen a little, so he said Allahu Akbar and the people said Allahu Akbar with him. Then he went out a second time that day after the day had risen, so he said Allahu Akbar and the people said Allahu Akbar with him until their takbir reached the Ka`ba. Then he went out a third time that day when the sun had declined, so he said Allahu Akbar and the people said Allahu Akbar with him. It is proven in Sahih from the hadith of Ibn Umar that “the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to stone the Jamarat and say Allahu Akbar with every pebble.” Something similar to this was narrated from Aisha by al-Hakim, who authenticated it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: But whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, he said: in his haste, And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, he said: in his delay. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: Departure in two days is for the one who fears God. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: “If the sun sets for someone on the day about which God said: ‘But whoever hastens in two days’ while he is in Mina, then he should not depart until he has stoned the Jamarat the next day.” Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: For the one who fears God, he said: For the one who avoids hunting while he is in a state of ihram. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, the people of Sunan and al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya`mar al-Dailami: I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say while he was standing in Arafat, and the people of Makkah came to him and said: O Messenger of God, how is the Hajj? He said: “The Hajj is Arafat, so whoever reaches the night of Jumu` before dawn has reached it. The days of Mina are three days. ‘But whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him.’ He said: He is forgiven. ‘And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him.’ He said: He is forgiven.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: For whoever fears God, he said: For whoever fears God during his Hajj. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that Ibn Masoud used to say: Whoever fears God during his Hajj, his previous sins will be forgiven. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding his statement: So there is no sin upon him who fears God, he said: All his sin will be removed if he fears God during the rest of his life.
2:204: When God the Almighty mentioned the two groups of Muslims in His saying: And among the people is he who says He followed that by mentioning the group of hypocrites, who are those who show faith but conceal disbelief. The reason for the revelation was Al-Akhns bin Shuraik, as will be explained. Ibn Atiyyah said: It has never been proven that Al-Akhns converted to Islam. It was said that it was revealed about a group of hypocrites, and it was said that it was revealed about everyone who concealed disbelief, hypocrisy, or lying, but showed the opposite with his tongue. The meaning of His saying: 204- you like it is clear. The meaning of His saying: And God is witness to what is in his heart is that he swears to that and says: God is witness to what is in my heart of love for you or of Islam, or he says: God knows that I am saying the truth, and that I am truthful in what I say to you. Ibn Muhaisin read: And God bears witness with the opening of the letter of the present tense and raising the noble noun as the subject, and the meaning is: And God knows from him the opposite of what he said. And similar to it is the saying of the Most High: And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars. The reading of the group is more eloquent in condemnation. Ibn Abbas read: And God bears witness to what is in his heart. And Abi and Ibn Masoud read: And God bears witness to what is in his heart. And his saying: In the life of this world is related to the saying, or it pleases you, so according to the first, the saying is issued in life, and according to the second, the admiration is issued in it. And the stubborn: the fierce opponent. It is said: a man is stubborn, and a woman is stubborn, and I argued with him and defeated him, and from it is the saying of the poet: And the most stubborn of people is as if the enmity in his chest is boiling in a cauldron. And the word khasam is derived from the verb khasama to quarrel, as stated by Al-Khalil. It is also said that it is the plural of khasam to quarrel, as stated by Al-Zajjaj: like dog and dogs, difficult and difficult severe. The meaning is that he is the most quarrelsome of the quarrelsome, due to his frequent arguments and strong arguments. Adding al-ald to khasam means in: that is, the most quarrelsome, or making khasam the most quarrelsome is an exaggeration.
2:205: And His saying: 205- And if he turns away means he turns away and leaves you, O Muhammad. It was said that it means he went astray and became angry. It was also said that it means guardianship: that is, if he was a ruler, he would do what the evil rulers do of corruption on earth. The mentioned striving may mean working in corruption, even if there is no striving with the feet, such as plotting against the Muslims in a way that harms them, and working tricks against them. Every action that a person does with his limbs or senses is called striving, and this is what is apparent from this verse. His saying: And he destroys is in apposition to his saying: To corrupt. In the reading of Abu, And he destroys. Qatada read it with the nominative case. It was narrated from Ibn Kathir: And he destroys with the opening of the ya' and the damma of the kaf and the raising of the harth and the offspring, and this is the reading of al-Hasan and Ibn Muhaisin. What is meant by harth is the crops and the offspring is the children. It was said that harth is the women. Al-Zajjaj said: This is because hypocrisy leads to division of speech and the occurrence of fighting, and in it is the destruction of creation. It was said that its meaning is: that the oppressor corrupts the earth, so God withholds the rain, which destroys the crops and offspring. The root of harth in the language is: splitting, and from it comes the plow for what is split by the earth, and harth: earning and collecting money. The root of an-nasl in the language is: coming out and falling, and from it comes the offspring of poetry, and from it also to their Lord they rush, “and they rush from every hill,” and it is said of what comes out of every female for its exit from her. His saying: And God does not love corruption includes every type of it without differentiating between what contains corruption of religion and what contains corruption of the world.
2:206: And pride: strength and dominance, from the word ‘izza ya’izzuhu: if he defeated him, and from it and he defeated me in the speech, and it was said that pride here: is zeal, and from it the poet’s saying: He was overcome by pride due to his ignorance, so he angrily did the act of boredom. It was said that pride here means: invincibility and strength of soul. The meaning of: 206- Pride took him by sin is that pride made him commit sin, from your saying I took him by such and such: if you made him do it and forced him to do it. It was said: Pride took him by what made him sin: meaning he committed disbelief out of pride. From this: Rather, those who disbelieved are in pride and discord. It was said that the ba in his saying: by sin means the lam: meaning pride and zeal took him from accepting the sermon because of the sin in his heart, which is hypocrisy. It was said that the ba means with: meaning pride took him from the sin. And his saying: So Hell is sufficient for him means it is sufficient for him as punishment and recompense, just as you say to a man: What happened to you is enough for you, while you consider what happened to him too great for him. The cradle is the plural of cradle, which is the place prepared for sleeping, and from it comes the cradle of the child. Hell was called a cradle because it is the abode of the infidels. It was said that the meaning is: that it is a substitute for the cradle for them, like his saying: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment and the saying of the poet: Greetings between them are painful
2:207: 207- "And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And God is Kind to His servants." And sells means to sell: that is, he sells himself for the pleasure of God, such as jihad, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. Similar to this is the saying of God the Almighty: And they sold him for a cheap price. Its origin is the exchange, and from this is His saying: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. And from this is the saying of the poet: I bought a cold, I wish I was important after the cold And from it the other said: He gives her a price, but her friend refuses and says, Why don’t you buy it? And contentment: satisfaction, you say: he was satisfied, he is satisfied, satisfaction and contentment. The reason for mentioning compassion here is that He made what He made obligatory upon them in order to reward them and recompense them for it, so that was compassion and kindness to them. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the expedition that included Asim and Murthad was lost, some of the hypocrites said: Woe to these people who were killed and who perished like this, they did not stay with their families, nor did they deliver the message of their master? So God revealed: And of mankind is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life meaning what he shows of Islam with his tongue. And he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart that it is contrary to what he says with his tongue. And he is the most quarrelsome of opponents meaning he is argumentative when he speaks to you and argues with you. And when he turns away he leaves you, “he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And God does not like corruption” meaning he does not like his work and is not pleased with it. And of mankind is he who sells himself those who sell themselves to God by striving in His cause and fulfilling His right, until they perished on that basis: meaning this expedition. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And among the people is he who pleases you 1:13, he said: It was revealed about Al-Akhns bin Shuraiq Al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, who came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in Madinah and said: I have come seeking Islam and God knows that I am truthful. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was amazed by that from him, so that is why he said: And God bears witness to what is in his heart. Then he went out from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and passed by a farm belonging to some Muslims and a donkey. He burned the farm and hamstrung the donkeys, so God revealed: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land 1:13. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And he is the most quarrelsome of opponents 1:13, he said: He is a severe opponent. Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land 1:13, he said: He works on the land. And destroys the crops 1:13, he said: The plants of the earth. And the offspring 1:13, the offspring of all things from animals, people and beasts. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he was asked about the statement of God, And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land, he said: He takes charge of the land and practices aggression and injustice therein, so God withholds rain from the sky because of that, and the crops and offspring are destroyed by the withholding of rain, and God does not love corruption. Then Mujahid recited: Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, the verse. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the statement of God, And destroys crops and offspring, he said: Crop means crops, and offspring means the offspring of every animal. Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: One of the greatest sins before God is for a man to say to his brother, Fear God, and he says, Take care of yourself; you are commanding me. Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Sufyan that a man said to Malik ibn Mughul, Fear God, so he fell and put his cheek on the ground out of humility before God. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And what an evil resting place, he said: What an evil home. They narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: What an evil witness they have given to themselves. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Suhaib who said: When I wanted to migrate from Mecca to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Quraysh said to me: O Suhaib, you have come to us without any wealth, and you will leave with your wealth. By God, that will never happen. So I said to them: Tell me, if I give you my wealth, will you let me go? They said: Yes. So I gave them my wealth and they let me go. So I left until I reached Madinah. report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Suhaib made a profit in the sale twice. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah, and Ibn `Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Sa`id ibn Al-Musayyab. At-Tabarani, Al-Hakim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated something similar on the authority of Suhaib. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Anas who said: It was revealed about Suhaib going out to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: They are the immigrants and the helpers.
2:208: When God the Almighty mentioned that people are divided into three groups: believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites, He then ordered them to be of one religion. The word faith was applied to the three groups because the People of the Book believe in their children and their book, and the hypocrite is a believer with his tongue even if he does not believe in his heart. As-Salam with the fatha or kasra of the seen, Al-Kisa'i said: Their meaning is one, and so it is with the Basrans, and they both refer to Islam and peace. Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala' said: It is with the fatha for the question, and with the kasra for Islam. Al-Mubarrad denied this distinction. Al-Jawhari said: As-Salam with the fatha of the seen: reconciliation, and it is broken and is masculine and feminine, and its origin is from submission and obedience. Al-Tabari preferred that here it means Islam, and from it the saying of the poet Al-Kindi: I called my tribe to peace when I saw them turn back and flee That is, to Islam. Al-A'mash read as-Salam with the opening of the seen and the lam. The Basrans have related that in Salam, Salam, and Salam they have one meaning and all the states of the Muslim or the pronoun of the believers, so its meaning according to the first is: none of you shall go out, and according to the second: none of the types of Salam shall go out, but enter into them all: that is, into the characteristics of Islam, and it is derived from their saying kafafat: meaning I prevented, meaning none of you shall refrain from entering Islam, and kufr means prevention, and what is meant by it here is all. 208- Enter into Salam all of it that is, all of you. And His saying: And do not follow the footsteps of Satan that is, do not take the path to which Satan calls you, and we have already discussed steps.
2:209: His saying: 209- You have strayed means you have deviated from the path of righteousness. The root of zalal is foot, then it was used for beliefs, opinions, and other things. It is said: Zalal yazal, zallan, and zalulun meaning his foot slipped. It was also read: Zalaltum with a kasra on the lām and they are two languages, and the meaning is: If you have gone astray and deviated from the truth after the clear proofs have come to you meaning the clear arguments and correct evidence, that entering Islam is the truth, then know that God is Exalted in Might Victorious, and revenge against you is not incapable of Him: Wise He does not take revenge except with justice.
2:210: His saying: 210- Do they look meaning do they wait? It is said: I looked at him and waited for him with the same meaning, and what is meant is: Do those who leave wait to enter into peace? And the shadows are the plural of shadow, which is what shades you. Qatada and Yazid bin Al-Qaqa read in shadows and Yazid also read and the angels in the accusative case in apposition to the clouds or to shadows. Al-Akhfash said: and the angels in the genitive case meaning: and in the angels. He said: and the nominative is better. Al-Zajjaj said: The estimate is in the shadows of the clouds and of the angels. The meaning is: Do they wait except for God to bring them what He promised them of accountability and punishment in the shadows of the clouds and the angels. Al-Akhfash said: It may be possible that the meaning of coming refers to the recompense, so the recompense was called coming just as the intimidation and torment in the story of Thamud were called coming. He said: So God attacked their building from the foundations. And he said in the story of An-Nadir: So God came upon them from where they did not expect. And this coming was possible because its origin according to the linguists is the intention to do something, so the meaning of the verse is: Do they wait for anything but for God to manifest an action from among the actions of His creation with the intention of fighting them? And it was said that the meaning is: God’s command and judgment will come to them. And it was said that His statement: in the shade means in the shade. And it was said that the meaning is: He will come to them with His might in the shade. And the cloud is the thin white cloud, it was called that because it covers: that is, it conceals. And the reason for the punishment coming in the clouds, on the assumption that this is what is meant, is the horror and enormity of the coming of fear from a place of security, because the cloud is a place of mercy, not a place of torment. His saying: And the matter was decided is in apposition to It will come to them which is within the scope of waiting. Rather, it was changed to the past tense to indicate that it was realized, so it is as if it had been, or a renewed sentence that was brought to indicate that its content will inevitably happen: that is, and the matter of their destruction was finished. Muadh ibn Jabal read And the matter was decided as a verbal noun in apposition to The angels. Yahya ibn Ya’mar read And the matters were decided in the plural. Ibn ‘Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa’i read The matters will return in the active form of the verb, while the rest read it in the passive form. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: “O you who have believed, enter into peace completely,” he said: He means the believers of the People of the Book, for they were holding fast to some of the commands of the Torah and the laws that were revealed to them, saying: Enter into the laws of the religion of Muhammad and do not leave anything of it, and it is sufficient for you to believe in the Torah and what is in it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah: That this verse was revealed about Tha’laba, Abdullah bin Salam, Ibn Yamin, Asad, Asid bin Ka’b, Sa’id bin Amr, and Qays bin Zaid, all of them Jews. They said: O Messenger of God, Saturday is a day we used to venerate, so leave it and let us recite it, and the Torah is the Book of God, so let us stand in prayer by it at night. So the verse was revealed: “O you who have believed, enter into peace completely.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Peace is obedience to God, and all means: all together. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Peace is Islam, and error is abandoning Islam. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: If you slip after the clear proofs have come to you, meaning: If [you go astray] after Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to you. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God will gather the first and the last for a known time on a known day, standing with their eyes fixed on the heavens, awaiting the passing of judgment.
