And God will descend in canopies of clouds from the Throne to the Footstool.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding this verse: He said: When He descends, between Him and His creation are seventy thousand veils, including light, darkness, and water. The water will make a sound in that darkness that will shake hearts. Abu Ya’la, Abd Ibn Hamid, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: God will come on the Day of Resurrection in canopies of clouds that have been cut off. Ibn Jarir and Al-Daylami narrated on his authority that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Among the clouds are windows in which God comes surrounded by angels. This is in reference to His statement: Do they await aught but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds? Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, In the canopies of clouds, he said: windows with angels around them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, he said: God comes to them in the canopies of clouds, and the angels come to them at the time of death. And he narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding His statement, And the matter has been decided, he said: The Hour has come.
2:211: The one who was ordered to ask the Children of Israel was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is possible that he was each individual questioner, and it is a question of rebuke and reproach. 211- "How much is in the accusative case with the verb mentioned after it as the object of came", and it is possible that it is in the accusative case with an implied verb indicated by the mentioned: i.e. how much We gave them, and it is implied to be late because it is at the beginning of the sentence, and it is either interrogative for the statement or declarative for the multiplicity. "From a sign" is in the accusative case as a distinguishing feature, and they are the proofs that their prophets brought regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that what is meant by that are the signs that Moses brought, which are nine. What is meant by the blessing here is what came to them of the signs. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: The blessing here refers to Islam, and it appears that it includes every blessing that God has bestowed upon one of His servants, whoever he may be, and he has changed it and not been thankful for it. This does not contradict the context being about the Children of Israel, or them being the reason for the revelation, as it has been established that consideration is given to the generality of the wording, not to the specificity of the reason. In His statement: Then God is severe in penalty, there is an intimidation and fear that cannot be measured.
2:212: His statement: 212- Zain is in the passive voice, and the adorned is the devil or the souls that are created with the love of the immediate. What is meant by those who disbelieved are the leaders of Quraysh or every disbeliever. Mujahid and Hamid bin Qais read Zain in the active voice. An-Nahhas said: It is an anomalous reading because the subject was not mentioned before. Ibn Abi Ubla read Zainab, and those who disbelieved were specifically mentioned, even though the world is adorned for the Muslim and the disbeliever, as God described that He made what is on the earth an adornment for it to test the creation as to which of them is best in deed, because the disbeliever was tempted by this adornment and turned away from the Hereafter, while the Muslim was not tempted by it, rather he turned towards the Hereafter. His saying: And they ridicule those who believe. This sentence is in the accusative case as a state: that is, while the situation is that those disbelievers ridicule those who believe because they are poor and have no share in this world like the share of the leaders of disbelief and the pillars of misguidance. This is because the worldly goods, to them, are the things that whoever attains them is happy and profitable, and whoever is deprived of them is miserable and loses. Most of the believers at that time were poor because they were busy with worship and the matter of the Hereafter, and did not pay attention to this world and its adornments. Al-Akhfash narrated that it is said: I ridiculed him and I mocked him, I laughed at him and I laughed at him, I mocked him and I mocked him, and the noun is mockery and derision. When the infidels mocked the believers, God responded to them by saying: And those who feared God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. What is meant by above here is the elevation in degree, because they are in Paradise and the infidels are in Hell. It is possible that what is meant by above is the place, because Paradise is in the sky and Hell is at the lowest of the low, or that the believers are the victors in this world, as happened with the emergence of Islam and the fall of infidelity and the killing of its people, their capture and displacement, and the imposition of the jizya on them. There is nothing to prevent the verse from being interpreted as referring to all of that, were it not for the restriction that it is on the Day of Resurrection. His saying: And God provides for whom He wills without account. It is possible that it indicates that God Almighty will provide for the weak among the believers and will provide for them abundantly, and will make what He gives them of provision without account: that is, without estimation. It is possible that the meaning is: God will provide for some of His servants abundantly, just as He provided for those leaders among the infidels, in order to lure them in. There is no evidence in the expansion that whoever He provides for is pleased with. It is possible that what is meant by without account is those who are provided for, as God Almighty said: And He will provide for him from where he does not expect.
2:213: His statement: 213- Mankind was one nation meaning they were of one religion then they differed so God sent the prophets and what indicates this omission is: I mean his statement: then they differed, the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, for he read Mankind was one nation then God sent the prophets. And there is a difference of opinion about the people mentioned in this verse, who are they? It was said: They are the children of Adam when God brought them forth as a soul from the back of Adam, and it was said: Adam alone, and he was called people because he is the origin of the lineage, and it was said: Adam and Eve, and it was said: What is meant is the first generations that were between Adam and Noah, and it was said: What is meant is Noah and those in his ship, and it was said: The meaning of the verse is that people were one nation, all of them disbelievers then God sent the prophets, and it was said: What is meant is the report about the people who are the entire species that they were one nation in their lack of laws and their ignorance of the truths, had God not bestowed upon them the favor of sending messengers. And the word nation is taken from their saying I intended something meaning I aimed at it, meaning their aim is one and not different. His saying: So God sent the prophets. It was said: Their total was one hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand, and the messengers among them were three hundred and thirteen. His saying: Bringing good tidings and warnings is in the accusative case as a state. His saying: And He sent down with them the Book means the genus. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: The alif and lam are for the covenant and what is meant is the Torah. His saying: So that he may judge is attributed to the Book according to the majority, and it is a metaphor like the saying of God the Almighty: This is Our Book that speaks against you with the truth. It was said: The meaning is that every prophet may judge with his book, and it was said: So that God may judge. The pronoun in his saying: in it the first refers to what is in his saying: in what they differed over. The pronoun in his saying: and what they differed over may refer to the Book, and it may refer to the one who was sent down to him, which is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as al-Zajjaj said. It may refer to the truth. His saying: Except those who were given it means those who were given the Book, or those who were given the truth, or those who were given the Prophet: meaning they were given his knowledge. His saying: Out of envy among themselves is in the accusative case as a direct object: meaning they did not differ except for envy: meaning envy and greed for this world. This is an indication of the foolishness in their actions and the ugly thing they fell into, because they made the revelation of the Book a reason for the severity of the disagreement. His saying: Then God guided those who believed to the truth about which they differed means that God guided the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the truth, and that is by what He explained to them in the Qur'an about the differences of those who came before them. It was said: Its meaning is that God guided the nation of Muhammad to believe in all the books unlike those who came before them, for some of them denied the book of others. It was said: God guided them to the truth from the Qiblah. It was said: He guided them for Friday. It was said: He guided them to believe in the truth in Jesus after the Jews denied him and the Christians made him a god. It was said: What is meant by the truth is Islam. Al-Farra' said: There is an inversion in the verse, and its meaning is: So God guided those who believed in the truth about which they differed. Ibn Jarir chose this and Ibn 'Atiyyah weakened it. And his saying: With His permission. Al-Zajjaj said: It means with His knowledge. Al-Nahhas said: This is a mistake, and the meaning is with His command. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Ask the Children of Israel he said: They are the Jews How many clear signs We gave them what God mentioned in the Quran and what He did not mention And who would exchange the favor of God he said: Disbelieves in it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah who said: God gave them clear signs: the staff of Moses, and his hand, and he cut them off from the sea, and he drowned their enemy while they were looking, and he provided shade from the clouds, and he sent down upon them manna and quails And who would exchange the favor of God he said: Who would deny the favor of God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve he said: The disbelievers seek and demand the life of this world And they mock those who believe in their seeking the Hereafter. Ibn Jurayj said: I do not think it was except from Ikrimah who said: They said: If Muhammad were a prophet, our leaders and nobles would have followed him, and by God, no one followed him except those in need like Ibn Masoud and his companions. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And they ridicule those who believe, they say: These are not upon anything, mocking and ridiculing. And those who feared God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. Here is how much is the difference? Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: Above them in Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about this verse: And God provides for whom He wills without account. He said: Its interpretation is: There is no observer over God nor does He hold Him to account. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr who said: The Lord will not be held to account. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Ya’la and al-Tabarani narrated with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The people were one nation. He said: All of them were upon Islam. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated on his authority that he said: There were ten centuries between Adam and Noah, all of them upon a law of truth, then they differed, so God sent the prophets. He said: And likewise in the recitation of Abdullah: The people were except one nation, then they differed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: They were one Muslim nation, then they differed after Adam. Wakee', Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: People were one nation, he said: Adam. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ubayy that he used to recite it: Mankind was one nation, then God sent the prophets and God only sent the messengers and revealed the books after the differences. And those who were given it did not differ - meaning the Children of Israel who were given the book and knowledge - out of envy among themselves, meaning envy for the world and seeking its kingdom and its adornments, as to which of them would have the kingdom and awe among the people. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: People were one nation he said: disbelievers. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah regarding his statement: Then God guided those who believed, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, and the first people to enter, and it will begin with them. They were given the Book before us and we were given it after them, so God guided us to the truth regarding which they differed. This is the day regarding which they differed and God guided us to it, so the people will follow us in it. Tomorrow will be for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow will be for the Christians.” And it is in the Sahih without mentioning the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam regarding his statement: So God guided those who believed to the truth about which they differed, he said: They differed about Friday, so the Jews took Saturday and the Christians took Sunday, so God guided the nation of Muhammad to Friday. They differed about the qiblah, so the Christians faced the east and the Jews faced Jerusalem, and He guided the nation of Muhammad to the qiblah. They differed about prayer, so some of them bowed and did not prostrate, and some of them prostrated and did not bow, and some of them prayed while talking, and some of them prayed while walking, so God guided the nation of Muhammad to the truth from that. They differed about fasting, so some of them fasted during the day, and some of them fasted after eating, so God guided the nation of Muhammad to the truth from that. They differed about Abraham, so the Jews said: He was a Jew, and the Christians said: He was a Christian and God made him a monotheist Muslim, so God guided the nation of Muhammad to the truth from that. They differed about Jesus, so the Jews denied him and said: His mother was a great slanderer, and the Christians made him a god and a son, and God made him his spirit and his word, so God guided the nation of Muhammad to the truth from that.
2:214: 214- Am here is disconnected and means rather. Some linguists have said that it may come as a question mark that begins a sentence. Accordingly, the meaning of the question mark here is confirmation and denial: that is, have you actually withheld your entry into Paradise, and have you not been tested in the same way as those who came before you were tested, so be patient as they were patient. God the Almighty mentioned this consolation after mentioning the nations' differences with their prophets, to strengthen the believers and fortify their hearts. An example of this verse is the Almighty's saying: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive? And His saying: "Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe and they will not be tested? And His saying: has touched them is an explanation of His saying: Like those who passed on. The explanation of al-Basa' and al-Dira' has already been given. The word al-Zalzalah means intense movement that occurs in people and situations. It is said: God shook the earth with an earthquake and an earthquake with the kasra, so it was shaken: if it moved and was disturbed, so the meaning of al-Zalzalu is: they frightened and disturbed with intense disturbance. Al-Zajjaj said: The root of al-Zalzalah is to move something from its place. So if you say: I shook it, then it means I repeated its shaking from its place. His statement: until he says means that it continued until a limit, which is the saying of the Messenger and those with him: When is the victory of God? The Messenger here is said to be Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is said to be Isaiah, and it is said to be every Messenger sent to his nation. Mujahid, al-A'raj, Nafi' and Ibn Muhaisin read it with the nominative in his statement: until he says and others read it with the accusative in the nominative as a narration of a past situation, and the accusative with the omission of an as a limit for what came before it. Al-A'mash read: And they were shaken until the Messenger said with the waw instead of hatta, and the meaning of that is that the Messenger and those with him were so fed up that they said this statement that required seeking victory and the delay of its occurrence and the length of its delay, so God Almighty gave them good report by saying: Indeed, the victory of God is near. A group said about the speech that there is an advancement and delay, and the meaning is: until those who believe say, When is the victory of God? and the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, says, Indeed, the victory of God is near. There is no resort to this effort, because the saying of the Messenger and those with him: When is the victory of God contains nothing but seeking victory from God Almighty, and it does not contain what they claimed of doubt and suspicion that would require that arbitrary interpretation. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada that this verse was revealed on the Day of the Confederates. On that day, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions were afflicted with affliction and siege. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God informed the believers that this world is a place of affliction and that He will test them in it, and He informed them that He did this to His prophets and chosen ones so that their souls would be at ease, so He said: They were touched by poverty and hardship. Affliction means trials, and hardship means illness, and they were shaken by trials and the harm of people towards them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And when there has not come to you the like of those who passed on, he said: This happened to them on the Day of the Confederates until their speaker said: God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion. Perhaps he meant by his statement until their speaker said: He meant the speaker of the hypocrites, as is indicated by the statement of the Most High: “When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when eyes turned away and hearts reached to the throats and you assumed about God [various] assumptions. There the believers were tried and shaken with a severe shaking. And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, ‘God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion.’”
2:215: The questioners here: They are the believers who asked about the thing they spend, what is it? They were answered by stating the purpose in which they spend it, indicating that it is the first to be intended, because a thing is not taken into account unless it is placed in its place and meets its purpose. It was said: His statement: 215- Whatever you spend of good includes a statement of what they spend, which is all good. It was said: They only asked about the aspects of righteousness in which they spend, which is contrary to what appears. We have already discussed the relatives, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer.
2:216: And His saying: 216- was written meaning imposed, and the explanation of its meaning has been presented. The Almighty explained that this: meaning the imposition of fighting upon them is among the things with which they were tested. And what is meant by fighting is fighting the infidels. And hatred with the damma: hardship, and with the fatha: what you were forced to do, and the damma is permissible in the meaning of the fatha so they are two languages, it is said: I hated the thing with hatred and hatred and hatred and hatred and I forced him to do it with compulsion, and the jihad was only hated because it involves spending money, and leaving one's family and homeland, and exposing oneself to loss of life, and in the expression with the source which is His saying: hated is an exaggeration, and it is possible that it means hated as in their saying: the dirham is the prince's strike. And His saying: And perhaps you hate something it was said: perhaps here means might, and that was narrated from Al-Asamm. Abu Ubaidah said: Perhaps from God it is an obligation. The meaning is: Perhaps you hate jihad because of the hardship it entails, and it is good for you. Perhaps you will be victorious, triumphant, gain booty, and rewarded. Whoever dies will die a martyr. Perhaps you love ease and abandoning fighting, and it is bad for you. Perhaps the enemy will become stronger than you and defeat you, and will attack your homes, and he will bring upon you something worse than what you fear from jihad, which you hate, along with the immediate and deferred benefits that you will miss out on in that. And God knows what is good for you and your success, and you do not know. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: They ask you, what they should spend, he said: On the day this verse was revealed, there was no zakat, which is the expenditure that a man spends on his family, and charity is given in charity, so zakat abrogated it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: The believers asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, where they should put their money. Then They ask you, what they should spend, the verse was revealed. So spending in voluntary acts and zakat are all the same. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated that Amr ibn Al-Jamuh asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: What should we spend of our money and where should we put it? Then it was revealed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: Fighting has been prescribed for you, he said: God commanded the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in Mecca to have monotheism, to establish prayer, to pay zakat, and to refrain from fighting. When he migrated to Medina, all the other obligations were revealed and He permitted them to fight, so the following was revealed: Fighting has been prescribed for you, meaning it is obligatory upon you and He permitted them after He forbade them from it, while it is hateful to you, meaning fighting, which is a hardship for you, and perhaps you dislike a thing, meaning jihad, fighting the polytheists, and it is good for you, and God makes its outcome a victory, spoils, and martyrdom, and perhaps you love a thing, meaning sitting back from jihad, and it is bad for you, so God makes its outcome evil, so you do not attain victory or spoils. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: I said to Ata’ what he says about the statement: Fighting is prescribed for you Is it obligatory for people to fight for it? He said: No, it was prescribed for those people at that time. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab regarding the verse: Jihad is prescribed for everyone who fights or stays behind. If one who stays behind is asked for help, he helps, if he is called upon to help, he goes out, and if he is dispensed with, he stays behind. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the statement: And it is hateful to you he said: This verse abrogated it: And they said, ‘We hear and obey.’ Ibn Jarir narrated it in a connected chain of transmission on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ali who said: Perhaps it is obligatory from God. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Suddi as well. There are many hadiths about the merits of Jihad and its obligation, and there is not enough space to elaborate on them.
2:217: His statement: 217- "Fighting in it" is a badal ishtiml inclusive as Sibawayh said. Its reason is that the question about the month was only in consideration of the fighting that took place in it. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that they ask you about fighting in the sacred month, and Sibawayh recited the words of the poet: Qais's death was not the death of one person, but rather the destruction of a people's edifice. His saying, "He perished him" is an inclusion from Qais. Al-Farra' said: It is in the accusative case, meaning his saying, "Fighting in it is with the intention of about." Abu Ubaidah said: It is in the accusative case of "neighborhood." Al-Nahhas said: It is not permissible to parse something as "neighborhood in the Book of God or in any speech, but it occurred in an unusual thing, which is their saying, This is a ruined lizard's hole." Al-Nahhas followed Ibn Atiyyah in criticizing Abu Ubaidah. Al-Nahhas said: It is not permissible to omit "about, and the statement about it is and" instead. Ibn Mas'ud and Ikrimah read: "They ask you about the sacred month - fighting in it." Al-A'raj read fighting in it in the nominative case. Al-Nahhas said, and it is ambiguous in Arabic, and the meaning is: They ask you about the sacred month - fighting in it is ready. His saying, "Say, fighting in it is a great sin" is a subject and predicate: meaning fighting in it is a great sin, and the sacred month means the genus. The Arabs did not shed blood or raid the enemy, and the sacred months are: Dhul-Qi'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab, three in succession and one in isolation. His statement, and averted from the way of God is the subject. His statement, and disbelieved in it is conjoined with avert. His statement, and the Sacred Mosque is conjoined with the way of God. His statement, and expelling his people from it is also conjoined with avert. His statement, greater in the sight of God is the predicate of avert and what is conjoined to it: that is, averting from the way of God, disbelief in it, averting from the Sacred Mosque, and expelling the people of the sanctuary from it is greater in the sight of God meaning greater in sin and more severe in guilt than fighting in the sacred month. This is what Al-Mubarrad and others said. The pronoun in his statement, and disbelieved in it refers to God. It was also said that it refers to the Hajj. Al-Farra’ said, and averted is conjoined with great, and the mosque is conjoined with the pronoun in his statement, and disbelieved in it, so the statement is coherent, connected and not separate. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is wrong because the meaning leads to his saying: And disbelieve in Him meaning in God is also in apposition to major, and it comes from that that expelling the people of the mosque from it is greater than disbelief in God, and this is clearly corrupt. The meaning of the verse according to the first opinion that the majority went to is: You, O disbelievers of Quraysh, consider fighting in the sacred month too great for us, and what you do of preventing from the path of God whoever wants to Islam and disbelief in God, and preventing from the Sacred Mosque, and expelling the people of the sanctuary from it is a greater crime before God. The reason supports this meaning, and indicates that it is intended as will be explained, because the question from them mentioned in this verse is a question of denial of what happened from the secret mission that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent. What is meant by fitnah here is disbelief: that is, your disbelief is greater than the killing that happened from the secret mission that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent. It was said that what is meant by fitnah is the expulsion of the people of the sanctuary from it, and it was said that what is meant by the fitnah that the disbelievers are upon. This is more likely than the first two views, because disbelief and expulsion have been mentioned previously and that they, along with turning away, are greater in the sight of God than fighting in the sacred month. His statement, and they will not cease is the beginning of a statement that includes the information from God, the Almighty, to the believers that these disbelievers will not cease to fight you and be hostile to you until they turn you back from Islam to disbelief if they are able to do so and you allow them to do so. Adhering to this condition indicates the improbability of their being able to do so and their ability to do so. Then God, the Almighty, warned the believers against being deceived by the disbelievers and engaging in what they want of turning them back from their religion, which is the ultimate goal of what they want of fighting the believers. He said, And whoever among you turns back from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless until the end of the verse. Apostasy is returning from Islam to disbelief, and the restriction with His statement, and dies while he is a disbeliever indicates that the deeds of the one who apostatizes are only nullified if he dies as a disbeliever. Habbat: means invalid and corrupted. From this comes the word habat, which is a corruption that affects livestock in their stomachs from eating too much grass, so their stomachs swell, and they may die from that. In this verse there is a threat to the Muslims to remain steadfast in the religion of Islam. The meaning of His statement: in this world and the Hereafter is that he will not have the rule of the Muslims in this world, so he will not take anything that the Muslims will be entitled to, nor will he attain any of the portions of Islam, nor will he attain anything of the reward of the Hereafter that Islam requires and that its people deserve. The scholars have differed regarding apostasy: does it invalidate the deed by itself or is it not invalidated except by death in disbelief? What is required is to interpret what the verses stated in general terms in other places according to what is in this verse of restriction. We have already discussed the meaning of eternity.
2:218: His saying: 218- And they emigrated. Emigration means moving from one place to another, leaving the first in favor of the second. Abandonment is the opposite of connection, and emigration means crossing over. What is meant by it here is emigration from the abode of disbelief to the abode of Islam. Striving: exerting effort, striving and striving, and striving and striving: doing one's best. His saying: they hope means they are greedy, and he only said: they hope after those praiseworthy descriptions with which he described them, because no one in this world knows that he will go to Paradise, even if he reaches every level in obeying God. Hope is hope, it is said: I hoped for so-and-so, I hope for him, hope and expectation. Hope may also mean fear as in the saying of God the Almighty: What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? That is, you do not fear the greatness of God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Jundub ibn Abdullah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he sent a group of people and sent Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah or Ubaidah ibn al-Harith over them. When he went to set out, he cried out of longing and yearning for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he sat down and he sent in his place Abdullah ibn Jahsh and wrote him a letter and ordered him not to read the letter until he reached such and such a place and said: Do not force any of your companions to travel with you. When he read the letter, he said: I hear and obey God and His Messenger. So he told them the report and read the letter to them. Two men returned and the rest of them went on and met Ibn al-Hadrami and killed him. They did not know whether that day was from Rajab or Jumada. The polytheists said to the Muslims: You killed in the sacred month. So God revealed: “They ask you about the sacred month” 2:170. Some of them said: If they have not committed a sin, then they will have no reward. So God revealed: Indeed, those who have believed and those who have been killed in the sacred month 2:170. They migrated to the end of the verse. Al-Bazzar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the reason for the revelation of the verse was that. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The polytheists prevented the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and turned him back from the Sacred Mosque in a sacred month, so God granted victory to His Prophet in a sacred month of the following year. The polytheists criticized the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for fighting in a sacred month. God said: “Say: Fighting therein is a great sin, and averting people from the way of God and disbelief in Him and the Sacred Mosque and the expulsion of its people therefrom are greater in the sight of God” than fighting there. And that Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent a detachment, and they encountered Amr ibn al-Hadrami as he was coming from Taif on the last night of Jumada and the first night of Rajab. And the companions of Muhammad thought that that night was from Jumada, but it was the first night of Rajab and they did not realize it, so one of them killed him and took what he had with him, and the polytheists sent to taunt him about that, so the verse was revealed. Ibn Ishaq narrated on his authority that the reason for the revelation of the verse was the affliction of Amr ibn al-Hadrami. It has been reported in many ways to specify the reason, such as what was mentioned above. Ibn Abi Dawud narrated on the authority of Ata’ bin Maysarah who said: Fighting in the sacred month was permitted in Bara’ah in His statement: So wrong not yourselves therein, and fight the polytheists all together. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri that he was asked about this verse and he said: This is something that has been abrogated, and there is nothing wrong with fighting in the sacred month. An-Nahhas narrated in his Naskh on the authority of Ibn Abbas that this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword in Bara’ah: So kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: And fitnah is greater than killing. He said: Polytheism. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid: And they will not cease fighting you. He said: The infidels of Quraysh. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas regarding His statement: Those are the ones who hope for the mercy of God. He said: These are the best of this nation. God has made them people of hope. Indeed, whoever hopes seeks, and whoever fears flees. Abd bin Hamid narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah.
2:219: The questioners in His statement: 219- They ask you about wine are the believers, as will be explained when mentioning the reason for the revelation of the verse. Wine is taken from khamr if it covers, and from it is the woman's veil, and everything that covers something has become khamr, and from it they covered their vessels and it was called khamr because it covers the mind: that is, it covers it and conceals it, and from that the intertwined tree is called: khamr with the opening of the m, because it covers what is beneath it and conceals it, and from it is said the earth became khamr: its wine became abundant. The poet said: Oh Zaid and Ad-Dahhak, go ahead, for you have crossed the road’s wine. That is, you have crossed the valley. It was said: Wine was called khamr because it was left until it ripened, as it is said that dough has fermented, meaning it has reached maturity. And the opinion has been fermented, meaning it was left until the face became clear in it. It was said: Wine was called khamr because it mixes with the mind from fermentation, which is mixing. These three meanings are close and exist in wine because it was left until it ripened, then it mixed with the mind and fermented it, meaning it covered it. Wine is the grape juice that has boiled and become strong and thrown up foam. Whatever ferments the mind from something other than it is subject to its ruling, as the majority have stated. Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, Ibn Abi Laila, Ibn Ikrimah, and a group of the jurists of Kufa said: Whatever intoxicates in large quantities other than grape wine is permissible, meaning what is less than intoxicating in it. Abu Hanifa held that what two-thirds of it is gone by cooking is permissible, and the disagreement on this is well-known. I have discussed wine at length in my commentary on al-Muntaqa, so please refer to it. Gambling is derived from the word yusr, which means that something is obligatory for its owner. It is said, He made such-and-such easy for me, if it is obligatory, then he makes it easy, yusr, and yasir is the player with lots. Yasr may also mean making things easy. The poet said: So help them and make things easy for them as they made things easy for them. And if they are in distress, then make them easy for you. Al-Azhari said: Maysir is the camels that they used to gamble on. It is called Maysir because it is divided into parts, so it is as if it is the place of division, and everything that you divide, you have made easy. Al-Yasir is the butcher. He said: This is the origin of Al-Yasir, then it is said to those who throw lots and gamble on the camels: Yasroon, because they are butchers, as they were the cause of that. And he said in Al-Sahah: And the people gambled the camels: if they butchered them and divided their parts, then he said: And it is said that the people gambled: if they gambled, and a man Maysir and Yasir mean the same thing, and the plural is Aysar. Al-Nabigha said: I complete my left hand and give them the ability to walk and clothe the handful of leather What is meant by gambling in the verse is the Arabs’ gambling with arrows. A group of the early Muslims, the Companions and the Followers, and some of them, said that everything in which there is gambling, such as dice, chess, or other things, is gambling, even children playing with nuts and dice, except for what is permitted of betting on horses and drawing lots to allocate rights. Malik said: Gambling is of two types: gambling of amusement and gambling of the kind. Among the gambling of amusement are dice, chess, and all kinds of entertainment. Gambling of the kind that people take risks on, and everything that is gambled on is gambling. We will discuss this in detail in Surat Al-Ma’idah, when God says: Intoxicants and gambling are only. His statement: “Say: In them is a great sin.” He means alcohol and gambling. The sin of alcohol, that is, the sin of consuming it, arises from the corruption of the mind of the one who uses it, so he does what a person with a corrupt mind does, such as quarreling, insulting, saying obscene and false words, neglecting prayers, and everything else that is obligatory upon him. As for the sin of gambling: that is, the sin of engaging in it, it is what results from that of poverty and the loss of money in vain, and enmity and agitation in the hearts. As for the benefits of wine, it is the profit of trading in it. It was said: what results from it of joy and activity and strength of the heart and steadfastness of the mind and reformation of the stomach and strength of the libido. The poets of the Arabs referred to something of that, saying: If I drink, I am the lord of Al-Khawarnaq and Al-Sudair And when I wake up, I am the master of the little girl and the camel Another said: We drink it and it leaves us kings and lions, and the encounter will never end. And he who pointed out the harms and benefits in it said: I saw that wine is good, but it has qualities that corrupt a patient man. I swear to God, I will never drink it while healthy, nor will I ever cure a sick person with it. I would never give my life for it, and I would never call for a companion for it. The benefits of gambling: the destiny of something to a person without effort or toil, and the pleasure and profit that comes from him when he gets a good share of it. The shares of gambling are eleven, seven of which have shares according to the number of their shares. The first is al-Fadh with a fat-ha on the fa’ followed by a voiced letter, and it has one mark and he has a share and he owes a share. The second is al-Tawa’am with a fat-ha on the second tha’, a sukoon on the waw, and a fat-ha on the hamza, and it has two marks and he has and owes two shares. The third is al-Raqeeb, and it has three marks and he has and owes three shares. The fourth is al-Hals with two silent letters, the first one is broken and the lam is silent, and it has four marks and he has and owes four shares. The fifth is al-Nafer with a nun, fa’, and silent letter, and it is said: al-Nafis with a silent sin instead of a ra’, and it has five marks and he has and owes five shares. The sixth is al-Musabil with a damma on the mim, a sukoon on the silent letter, and a fat-ha on the unified ba’, and it has six marks and he has and owes six shares. The seventh is Al-Mu'alla, with a damma on the meem, a fatha on the silent letter, and a shaddah on the open lam. It has seven marks, and it has seven shares and is subject to it. It is the most fortunate of the arrows, and the highest in value, so the total is twenty-eight individuals. The roots are made into twenty-eight parts, this is what Al-Asma'i said. There remain four arrows that have no fixed shares, and they are: Al-Munih, with a fatha on the meem, a kasra on the noon, and a sukoon on the lower yaa, followed by a silent letter; Al-Safīh, with a fatha on the silent letter, a kasra on the faa, and a sukoon on the lower yaa, followed by a silent letter; Al-Wafd, with a fatha on the waw, a sukoon on the voiced letter, followed by a silent letter; and Al-Da'f, with a voiced letter, followed by a silent letter, then a faa. They only included these four that have no fixed shares among those that have fixed shares so that the arrows would be many for the one who moves them and strikes with them, so that he would not find a way to lean towards anyone. The arrow-shooter would cover himself with a garment, throw it on his knees, and stick his head out of the garment. Then he would put his hand in the rababa, with a broken silent letter followed by a unified ba, and after the alif, a unified ba as well. This is the map in which the arrows are placed, and an arrow would be taken out in the name of each man. Whoever had an arrow that had a share taken it, would take it, and whoever had an arrow that had no share took nothing and paid the value of the camels. They would give those shares to the poor. Ibn Atiyah said: Al-Asma’i made a mistake in saying that the camels are divided into twenty-eight parts, and he said: They are divided into ten parts. The Almighty said: And their sin is greater than their benefit. The Almighty informed that even if there is benefit in wine and gambling, the sin that befalls those who take them is greater than this benefit, because there is no good equal to the corruption of the mind that results from wine, as it produces countless evils. Likewise, there is no good in gambling equal to what it involves of risking money, being exposed to poverty, and attracting enmities that lead to bloodshed and the violation of sanctity. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read Katheer with the triangle. The rest read it with the unified Ba. Abi read: And their sin is nearer than their benefit. His statement, "Say: The pardon" The majority read it in the accusative. Abu Amr alone read it in the nominative. Ibn Kathir differed on it, and Al-Hasan and Qatadah read it in the nominative. An-Nahhas said: If you make Dha in the meaning of who, the choice is to raise it to mean that which they spend is the pardon. If you make Ma and Dha one thing, the choice is to lower it to mean: Say: They spend the pardon. The pardon is what is easy and simple and is not difficult for the heart. The meaning is: Spend what is left over from your needs and do not exhaust yourselves. It was said: It is what is left over from the expenses of your family. The majority of scholars said: It is voluntary expenses. It was said: This verse was abrogated by the verse of the obligatory zakat. It was said: It is decisive, and there is a right in money other than zakat. His statement, Thus does God make clear to you the verses means in the matter of spending.
2:220: His statement: 220- "In this world and the Hereafter" is related to his statement: "You ponder" meaning you ponder their matter, so you keep from your wealth what you can use to improve your worldly life, and you spend the rest in ways that bring you closer to the Hereafter. It was said that there is an inversion in the speech: that is, thus God explains to you the signs in this world and the Hereafter so that you may ponder the world and its passing and the Hereafter and its permanence, so that you may turn away from the immediate to the deferred. It was said: It is possible that it is a reference to his statement: "And their sin is greater than their benefit" meaning so that you may ponder the matter of this world and the Hereafter, and this is not good. His statement: "And they ask you about orphans" This verse was revealed after the statement of God the Most High: "And do not approach the property of an orphan" and His statement: "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans" and the matter was difficult for the guardians as will be explained, God willing, so this verse was revealed. What is meant by reform here is mixing with them in a way that reforms their wealth, as this is better than avoiding them. This is evidence of the permissibility of disposing of the wealth of orphans by guardians and trustees through selling, speculation, renting, and the like. His statement, But if you mix with them, then they are your brothers. There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of mixing with them. Abu Ubaidah said that mixing with orphans is when one of them has wealth and it is difficult for his guardian to separate his food from him and he finds no alternative but to mix with his family, so he takes from the orphan’s wealth what he sees is sufficient for him based on his investigation and puts it with the expenses of his family. This may be increased or decreased, so this verse indicates permission and it abrogates what came before it. It was said that what is meant by mixing is: living with orphans, and it was said that what is meant by it is: marrying with them. It is better not to limit mixing to a specific type, but rather to include all mixing, as is understood from the conditional sentence. His statement, then they are your brothers is the predicate of an omitted subject: i.e. they are your brothers in religion. In His statement: And God knows the corrupter from the reformer, there is a warning to the saints: that is, nothing of this is hidden from God, for He rewards everyone according to his deeds. Whoever reforms, it is for his own good, and whoever corrupts, it is against himself. His statement: I would have made you suffer, that is, if He had willed, He would have made that difficult and tiring for you and caused you to fall into that which is difficult and stressful. It was said that the adjective here means destruction. This was said by Abu Ubaidah, and the origin of suffering is hardship. Ibn al-Anbari said: The origin of suffering is intensification, then it was transferred to the meaning of destruction. His statement: Mighty, that is, nothing is impossible for Him, because He is dominant and cannot be defeated. Wise, that is, He disposes of His kingdom as His will and wisdom dictate, and you do not have the right to choose for yourselves. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Umar that he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about wine, for it takes away wealth and reason. Then, They ask You about wine and gambling meaning this verse was revealed. Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about wine. Then, in Surat al-Nisa’, it was revealed: O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated. When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) stood up to pray, he would call out that one should not approach prayer while drunk. Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about wine. Then, the verse in al-Ma’idah was revealed. Umar was called and it was recited to him, and when he reached Will you then desist? Umar said: We have desisted, we have desisted. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Anas who said: We used to drink wine and the verse was revealed: They ask you about wine and gambling 10:1. We said: We will drink from it what will benefit us. Then the verse was revealed in al-Ma’idah 5:Indeed, wine and gambling 10:1. They said: O God, we have stopped. Abu Ubaid, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: Gambling is gambling. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. He said: In the pre-Islamic period, a man would gamble about his family and his wealth, and whichever of them gambled with the other would take his family and wealth. And His statement: “Say: In them is great sin” means: what is diminished from religion when drinking it and some benefit for people meaning: in what they gain from its pleasure and joy when they drink it and their sin is greater than their benefit meaning: what is lost from religion, so the sin in it is greater than what they gain from its pleasure and joy when they drink it, so after that God revealed: Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated the verse, so they would not drink it during prayer, but when they prayed the evening prayer they would drink it, then some of the Muslims drank it and fought each other, and they said things that did not please God, so God revealed: Indeed, wine, gambling, and idolatry the verse, so He forbade wine and prohibited it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him that he said: Their benefits were before they were forbidden, and their sin was after He forbade them. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that when a group of the Companions were commanded to spend in the way of God, they came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: We do not know what this spending that we have been commanded to do from our wealth is, so what should we spend from it? So God revealed: “And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘The excess.’” Before that, he used to spend his wealth until he could not find anything to give in charity, nor anything to eat until he could give charity to it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The excess is what is not apparent in your wealth, and this was before charity was made obligatory. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’b narrated on his authority that regarding the verse, he said: The excess is what is left over from your family, and in another version he said: The excess from your dependents. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding His statement: Say, ‘The excess,’ he said: No known obligation was imposed on it, then he said: Take what is easy and enjoin what is right. Then it was revealed about the obligations after that and named. It has been proven in Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best charity is that given from surplus wealth, and start with those under your care. A similar hadith has been proven in Sahih from the hadith of Hakim bin Hizam. There are many hadiths on this topic. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Perhaps you will give thought * In this world and the Hereafter, he said: He means in the passing of this world and its passing away and the coming of the Hereafter and its permanence. Abu Dawud, An-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on his authority that he said: When God revealed, And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best and Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans 10:1, those who had an orphan separated his food from their food and his drink from their drink, and began to separate some of his food and keep it for him until he ate it or spoiled it and threw it away. This was very difficult for them, so they mentioned it to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so God revealed, And they ask you about orphans 10:1. So they mixed their food with their food and their drink with their drink. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi'un. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {And if you mix with them} he said: Mixing is that he drinks from your milk and you drink from his milk, and he eats from your bowl and you eat from his bowl, and he eats from your fruit and you eat from his fruit. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer he said: He knows who deliberately eats the orphan’s money, and who is cautious about it and does not spare any effort to reform it. And if God had willed, He could have made you miserable he said: If He had willed, He would not have made lawful for you what you do not do intentionally. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: {I would have made you miserable} he said: He would have made you miserable and made things difficult for you, but He made things easy and facilitated. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: {And if God had willed, He could have made you miserable} he said: And if He had willed, He could have made what you take from the orphans’ money a cause of destruction.
2:221: His saying: 221- And do not marry. The majority read it with the opening of the ta', and it was read in the exceptions with the closing of it. It was said: The meaning is: The one who marries her marries her from herself. In this verse there is a prohibition against marrying polytheistic women. It was said: What is meant by polytheistic women are idolaters. It was said: It includes the People of the Book because the People of the Book are polytheists. And the Jews said, 'Ezra is the son of God,' and the Christians said, 'The Messiah is the son of God.' The people of knowledge differed regarding this verse. A group said: God forbade marriage to polytheistic women in it, and the People of the Book are included in the generality. Then the verse of Al-Ma'idah came and made the People of the Book specific from this generality. This is narrated from Ibn Abbas, Malik, Sufyan ibn Sa'id, Abd al-Rahman ibn Umar, and al-Awza'i. A group went to the view that this verse abrogates the verse of Al-Ma'idah, and that it is forbidden to marry the People of the Book and polytheistic women. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, and a group of scholars said the same. The answer to their claim that this verse abrogates the verse of al-Ma'idah is that Surat al-Baqarah was among the first to be revealed and Surat al-Ma'idah was among the last to be revealed. The first statement is the most correct. It was said by Uthman ibn Affan, Talhah, Jabir, Hudhayfah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Tawus, Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak, as narrated by al-Nahhas and al-Qurtubi. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it from those mentioned, and Umar ibn al-Khattab added and said: It is not authentic from any of the early scholars that he forbade that. Some of the scholars said: The term polytheist does not include the People of the Book, because God the Almighty said: Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists do not like that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. And He said: It was not for those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists. Assuming that the term polytheists is general, this generality is specific to the verse of al-Ma'idah, as we have mentioned. His saying: And for a believing slave woman means and for a believing slave woman. It was said that what is meant by the slave woman is the free woman because all people are the slaves and handmaids of God, and the first is more appropriate for what will come because it is the apparent meaning of the wording and because it is more eloquent. The preference of the believing slave woman over the free polytheist woman is understood from it that the preference of the believing free woman over the polytheist woman is a fortiori. His saying: Even if she pleases you means even if the polytheist pleases you because of her beauty, wealth or honor. This sentence is a circumstantial statement. His saying: And do not marry polytheists means do not marry them to believing women until they believe. Al-Qurtubi said: The nation is unanimously agreed that the polytheist does not have intercourse with the believing woman in any way because of the disgrace in that for Islam, and the reciters are unanimous in adding the ta’ of tankhawa. His saying: And for a slave the discussion of it is like the discussion of his saying: And for a slave woman and the preference is like the preference. His saying: Those refers to the polytheists, both men and women. They invite to the Fire meaning to the deeds that lead to the Fire. Thus, marrying into their marriages, associating with them, and keeping company with them is a great danger that the believers should not expose themselves to or enter into. And God invites to Paradise meaning to the deeds that lead to Paradise. It was said that what is meant is that the allies of God are the believers who invite to Paradise. His saying: By His permission means by His command, as Al-Zajjaj said. It was also said: By His facilitation and guidance, as the author of Al-Kashshaf said. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan who said: This verse was revealed about Abu Marthad Al-Ghanawi. He asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for permission to marry Anaq, and she was very beautiful, but she was a polytheist, and Abu Marid was a Muslim at that time. He said: O Messenger of God, I please you. So God revealed: And do not marry polytheistic women. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And do not marry polytheistic women, that God made an exception for the women of the People of the Book, and said: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture. This meaning has been narrated from him through various chains of narration. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding His statement: And do not marry polytheistic women, meaning people of idols. Abd bin Hamid and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from Mujahid, and Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd bin Hamid narrated something similar from Qatadah. Abd bin Hamid narrated something similar from Al-Nakha’i. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he disliked marrying women of the People of the Book, and he interpreted: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. Al-Bukhari narrated on his authority that he said: God has forbidden marriage to polytheistic women for Muslims, and I do not know of anything greater than polytheism than a woman saying that her Lord is Jesus or one of God’s servants. Al-Wahidi and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, he said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Rawahah, who had a black slave woman and he became angry with her and slapped her. Then he became frightened and came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and told him about her. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: What is she, Abdullah? He said: You fast, pray, perform ablution well, and testify that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God. He said: O Abdullah, this is a believer. Abdullah said: By Him Who sent you with the truth, I will free her and marry her. So he did so, and some Muslims criticized him and said: He married a female slave. They wanted to marry to polytheists and marry them out of desire for their lineage, so God revealed about them: And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Muqatil ibn Hayyan regarding his statement: And a believing slave woman, he said: We were informed that she was a black slave woman of Hudhayfah, so he freed her and Hudhayfah married her. Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali who said: Marriage is mentioned in the Book of God. Then he recited: And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe.
2:222: His saying: 222- Menstruation is menstruation, and it is a source. It is said: A woman menstruated, menstruating, and she is menstruating and menstruating. This is what Al-Farra’ said, and he recited: Like a menstruating woman who commits adultery while not pure Menstruating women and menstruating women. Menstruation with a kasra means one time. It was also said: the name. It was also said: menstruation refers to time and place, and it is a metaphor for both. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: menstruation is the name for menstruation, and similar to it is the saying of Ru’bah: I complain to you about the hardship of life Any living, and the origin of this word is from flow and explosion. It is said: the flood flowed and overflowed, and the tree flowed: meaning its moisture flowed, and from it is menstruation: meaning the basin, because the water is pooled to it: meaning it flows. And His statement: “Say: It is harmful” means say: It is something that is harmful: meaning by its smell, and harmful is a metaphor for filth and is used to refer to a disliked statement, and from it is the statement of the Most High: Do not invalidate your charities with reminders or harm. And from it is His statement: And leave their harm and His statement: So keep away from women during menstruation meaning avoid them during the time of menstruation if menstruation is taken as a source or in the place of menstruation if it is taken as a noun. What is meant by this isolation is to refrain from sexual intercourse, not to refrain from sitting or touching, as that is permissible. Rather, it is permissible to enjoy her with anything other than the vagina or with anything below the izar, although there is disagreement on that. What is narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ubaydah al-Salmani that a man must refrain from his wife’s bed if she menstruates is not a good thing, and there is no disagreement among scholars regarding the prohibition of intercourse with a menstruating woman, as it is known from the necessity of religion. His statement: And do not approach them until they are pure. Nafi’, Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr read yatahirna with a shaddah on the ta’ and a fathah on the ha’ and a shaddah on the ha’. In the Mushaf of Abu and Ibn Mas’ud, it is yatahirna. Purity is the cessation of menstruation, and purification is bathing. Because of the differences in the reciters, scholars differed. The majority held that it is not permissible for a menstruating woman to have intercourse with her husband until she purifies herself with water. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qudhi and Yahya ibn Bakir said: If a menstruating woman purifies herself and performs tayammum where there is no water, she is permissible for her husband even if she does not bathe. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: If the bleeding stops, she is permissible for her husband, but she must perform ablution. Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said: If her bleeding stops after ten days, he is permitted to have intercourse with her before performing ghusl. If it stops before ten days, it is not permissible until she performs ghusl or the time for prayer begins. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari preferred the double reading. It is preferable to say that God, the Exalted, made two goals for permissibility, as required by the two readings: one is the cessation of the bleeding, and the other is purification from it. The other goal includes an addition to the first goal, so it must be adhered to. It has been indicated that the other goal is the one that is considered. God, the Exalted, says after that: And when they have purified themselves, which indicates that what is considered is purification, not merely the cessation of the bleeding. It has been established that the two readings are like two verses, so just as it is necessary to combine two verses, one of which includes an addition by acting on that addition, likewise it is necessary to combine the two readings. His statement: Then have intercourse with them from where God has commanded you, means, have intercourse with them, and He referred to it by coming. What is meant is that they have intercourse with them in the place that God has permitted, which is the vagina. It has been said that from where means in where, as in the Almighty’s saying: When the call is made for prayer on Friday, meaning on Friday, and His saying: What have they created on earth? meaning on earth. It has been said that the meaning is from the place that God has permitted you to have intercourse with, meaning without fasting, ihram, or seclusion. It has been said that the meaning is from before purity, not from menstruation. It has been said that it is from what is permissible, not from fornication. His saying: Indeed, God loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves, it has been said that what is meant is those who repent from sins and those who purify themselves from major ritual impurity and minor ritual impurity. It has been said that it is those who repent from having intercourse with women in their anuses, and it has been said that it is from having intercourse with them during menstruation, and the first is more apparent.
2:223: His saying: 223- Your women are a place of cultivation for you, so approach your place of cultivation however you wish. The word place of cultivation indicates that permission only occurs in the vagina, which is the vagina in particular, since it is the place where offspring are sown, just as place of cultivation is the place where plants are sown. He likened what is cast into their wombs of sperm from which offspring are produced to what is cast into the earth of seeds from which plants are produced, in common that each one of them is a material for what is produced from it. This sentence is an explanation of the first sentence, I mean his saying: So approach them from where God has commanded you. His saying: However you wish means from any direction you wish, from behind, in front, kneeling, lying down, or lying down, if it is in the place of cultivation. Tha'lab recited: The wombs are our cultivated lands. We have to plant it and God will take care of the plants. The Almighty expressed it with the word how because it is more general in language than how, where, and when. As for Sibawayh, he interpreted it here as how. The predecessors and successors from the Companions, Followers, and Imams have adopted what we have mentioned in the interpretation of the verse, and that intercourse with one’s wife in her anus is forbidden. It was narrated from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Nafi’, Ibn Umar, Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, and Abdul Malik bin Al-Majishun that it is permissible. Al-Qurtubi narrated it from them in his interpretation. He said: This was narrated from Malik in a book of his called The Book of Secret, and the most skilled companions of Malik and their sheikhs deny this book, and Malik is too noble to have a book of secrets, and this statement was mentioned in Al-Utbiyyah. Ibn al-Arabi mentioned that Ibn Shaban attributed the permissibility of this to a large group of the Companions and Followers and to Malik from many narrations in the book of Jama' al-Nisa'an wa Ahkam al-Qur'an. Al-Tahawi said: Asbagh ibn al-Faraj narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim who said: I have not met anyone whom I follow in my religion who doubted that it is permissible - meaning anal intercourse with a woman. Then he recited: Your women are a place of cultivation for you and said: What is clearer than this? Al-Hakim, al-Daraqutni and al-Khatib al-Baghdadi narrated from Malik through chains of transmission that indicate that this is permissible. However, there is weakness in their chains of transmission. Al-Tahawi narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam that he heard al-Shafi'i say: There is nothing authentically reported from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding its permissibility or prohibition, and the analogy is that it is permissible. Abu Bakr al-Khatib narrated this. Ibn al-Sabbagh said: al-Rabi' used to swear by God, there is no god but Him. Ibn Abd al-Hakam lied about al-Shafi'i regarding this, as al-Shafi'i explicitly stated its prohibition in six of his books. His saying: And send forth for yourselves means good, as in the saying of God Almighty: And whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with God. It was said: seeking a child, and it was said: marrying chaste women, and other things were said. His saying: And fear God contains a warning against falling into any of the forbidden things. In His saying: And know that you will meet Him is an exaggeration in the warning. In His saying: And give good tidings to the believers is a comfort to those who do good and avoid evil. Muslim, the Sunan scholars and others narrated on the authority of Anas that “when a Jewish woman among them menstruated, they would expel her from the house and would not eat or drink with her or have intercourse with her in the house. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about that, so God revealed: “And they ask you about menstruation” 10:13. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Have intercourse with them in the houses and do everything except intercourse. An-Nasa’i and Al-Bazzar narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Jews said: Whoever has intercourse with a woman in her anus will have a cross-eyed child. So they came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him about that and about having intercourse with a menstruating woman, so that verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: The impurity is blood. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So keep away from women means: keep away from having intercourse with their private parts. Regarding his statement: And do not approach them until they are pure he said: from blood. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Until the bleeding stops. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: And when they have purified themselves he said: With water. Abd al-Razzaq and Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’ that they said: If she sees that she is pure, there is nothing wrong with her cleaning herself with water and having intercourse with her before she bathes. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: Then have intercourse with them from where God has commanded you he said: Meaning that he should have intercourse with her when she is pure and not menstruating. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: Then have intercourse with them from where God has commanded you he said: From where He has commanded you to keep away from them. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: From where He forbade you from approaching them while they are menstruating meaning from the vagina. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Hanafiyyah, who said: Then approach them from where God has commanded you from the side of marriage. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding His statement: He loves those who repent he said: from sins, and He loves those who purify themselves he said: with water. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: Repentance from sins and purification from polytheism. Al-Bukhari, the Sunan scholars, and others narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Jews used to say that if a man approaches his wife from behind in her vagina, the child will be born cross-eyed. Then this verse was revealed: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so go into your tilth when or how you will if you wish, sitting cross-legged, and if you wish, not sitting cross-legged, except that it is in one valve. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Humayd, and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Murrah Al-Hamadani. This was narrated by a group of the Salaf and they stated that it was the reason. Among those who narrated this were Abdullah bin Omar according to Ibn Asakir, and Umm Salamah according to Abdul Razzaq, Abdul bin Hamid and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shaab. It was also narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Darimi, Abdul bin Hamid and Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, “She asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about greeting, so he recited the verse to her and said: One valve.” Valve means the path. Ahmad, Abdul bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Omar came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, I am ruined. He said: What ruined you? He said: I moved my saddle last night. He did not answer him at all. Then God revealed this verse to His Messenger: Your women are a place of sowing for you. He said: Come forward and back, and avoid the anus and menstruation. Ahmad narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that this verse was revealed about some people from the Ansar who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him, so he said: Go to her in any case, if it is in the vagina. Ad-Darimi, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, At-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on his authority that Ibn Umar said: “May God forgive him or her. Rather, this tribe of the Ansar, who were idolaters, and this tribe of the Jews, who were the People of the Book, saw that they had superiority over them in knowledge, so they followed many of their actions. It was the custom of the People of the Book that they would not approach women except on the edge, and that is the most modest way for a woman to be. This tribe of the Ansar had taken to their actions, and this tribe of the Quraysh would treat women with great pleasure, whether they were facing forward, backward, or lying down. When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, a man from them married a woman from the Ansar.” So he went to do that to her, but she denied it and said: We only used to have intercourse on the edge, so do that, otherwise avoid me. So their affair spread and reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed the verse: Your women are a place of sowing for you. He said: From the front and the back, after it is in the vagina, and if it is from the front of her anus, then in her vagina. At-Tabarani added: Ibn Abbas said: Ibn Umar said: In her anus, so he was mistaken, and God will forgive him. This is how this hadith was. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ad-Darimi and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he said: The private parts of women are forbidden to you. Al-Shafi’i narrated in Al-Umm, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan on the authority of Khuzaymah ibn Thabit that “A man asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about having intercourse with women in their back passages. He said: It is permissible or there is no problem. When he turned away, he called him and said: What did you say? From her back passage in her vagina, yes. Or from her back passage in her anus, no. God is not ashamed of the truth: Do not come to women in their back passages.” Ibn ‘Adi and Al-Darqutni narrated something similar on the authority of Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Hibban narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: God will not look at a man who has intercourse with a woman in her back passage.
