Ahmad and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn ‘Amr that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The one who has intercourse with his wife in her back passage is the lesser sodomite. Ahmad, Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Cursed is he who has intercourse with his wife in her anus. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Humayd, An-Nasa’i and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority that he said: Men and women having intercourse in their anuses is disbelief. Ibn ‘Adi narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Kathir said: The chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) is more authentic. The prohibition of this has been narrated in many ways, including Al-Bazzar on the authority of ‘Umar with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and An-Nasa’i narrated it on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and this is more authentic. It has been narrated by Ibn ‘Adi in Al-Kamil on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), also on the authority of ‘Uqbah Ibn ‘Amir with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and Ahmad on the authority of Talq Ibn Yazid or Yazid Ibn Talq with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad and At-Tirmidhi who classified it as hasan on the authority of ‘Ali Ibn Talq with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Something similar has been proven on the authority of a group of the Companions and Followers with both chains of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Nafi’ who said: I read one day: Your women are a place of tilth unto you. Ibn Umar said: Do you know why this verse was revealed? I said: No. He said: It was revealed about having intercourse with women in their backsides. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: Go to your place of tilth however you wish. He said: In the anus. This has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar through many chains of narration. In a narration by Al-Daraqutni, it is narrated that Nafi’ said to him: Who has intercourse with her behind in her vagina? He said: No, except in her anus. Ibn Rahawayh, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, At-Tahawi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a hasan chain of narration on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri that a man had intercourse with his wife in her anus, and the people denounced him for that, so the verse was revealed. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali who said: I was with Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi when a man came to him and said: What do you say about having intercourse with a woman in her anus? He said: This is an old man from Quraysh, so ask him - meaning Abdullah bin Ali bin Al-Sa'ib - and he said: It is impure, even if it is permissible. The statement that this is permissible has been narrated from Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir according to Ibn Jarir, and from Ibn Abi Malekah according to Ibn Jarir also, and from Malik bin Anas according to Ibn Jarir, Al-Khatib and others, and from Al-Shafi'i according to Al-Tahawi, Al-Hakim and Al-Khatib. We have already mentioned something like this, and there is absolutely no proof in the statements of these people. It is not permissible for anyone to act on their statements, because they did not provide evidence indicating its permissibility. So whoever among them claims that he understood this from the verse has made a mistake in his understanding. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his most prominent companions have explained it to us in a way that is different from what this mistaken person in his understanding has said, whoever he may be. Whoever among them claims that the reason for the revelation of the verse is that a man had intercourse with his wife from behind, there is nothing in this to indicate that the verse has permitted that, and whoever claims that has made a mistake. Rather, what the verse indicates is that it is forbidden. The fact that that is the reason does not necessitate that the verse was revealed to permit it, because the verses that are revealed for reasons sometimes permit this and sometimes prohibit it. It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas that he interpreted this verse in a way other than what was mentioned above, and he said: Its meaning is: If you wish, then practice isolating, and if you wish, then do not. This was narrated from him by Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Dhiya in al-Mukhtara. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Umar. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah and from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir.
2:224: Ardah: the setting up, as Al-Jawhari said. It is said: I made so-and-so an exposure to such-and-such: meaning an exposure. It was also said: Ardah is from severity and strength, and from this is their saying to a woman, Ardah for marriage: if she is suitable for it and strong for it, and for so-and-so, Ardah: meaning strength, and from this is the saying of Ka’b bin Zuhair: From every freshness of the Dafry, if it sweats, its display is obscured by the unknown flags Similar to this is the saying of Aws bin Hajar: And a bloody calf like a calf, one day I presented it to my companions, and it was shaking and tossing about. Al-Ardah is used to refer to ambition, and from this the poet said: They are the supporters who presented the meeting Any of its ambition, and it is said: So-and-so is exposed to people who continue to fall into it - according to the meaning mentioned by Al-Jawhari, that the erection of the object like the fist and the room, that is the name of what you expose without the thing: that is, you make it a barrier for it and a deterrent from it: that is, do not make God a barrier and a deterrent to what you have sworn to, and that is because the man used to swear to some good, such as maintaining kinship ties or doing good to others or reforming between people, not to do that, then he refrains from doing it, explaining that refusal by saying that he had sworn not to do it, and this is the meaning that the majority mentioned in the interpretation of the verse, God forbids them from making it an exposure to their oaths: that is, a barrier to what they swore to and a deterrent from it, and the thing sworn to is called an oath because it is associated with the oath, and according to this his saying: 224 - that you be righteous is an explanatory apposition to your oaths: that is, do not make God a deterrent to the oaths that are your righteousness, piety, and reforming between people, and his saying: to your oaths is related to his saying: do not make that is, do not make God a deterrent to your oaths And a barrier, and it is permissible for it to be related to an objection: that is, do not make it something that stands between you and righteousness and what comes after it. And according to the second meaning, which is that the objection is severity and strength, the meaning of the verse is: Do not make the oath by God a strength for yourselves, and a means to refrain from good, and it is not correct to interpret the verse according to the third meaning, which is to interpret the objection as the determination. As for the fourth meaning, which is from their saying, So-and-so is always exposed to people, meaning they fall into it, then the meaning of the verse according to it is: Do not make God an object of your oaths, so you waste Him by swearing by Him a lot, and from it: And guard your oaths. And God has condemned those who swear a lot, saying: And do not obey every worthless swearer. And the Arabs used to praise each other for their few oaths, until one of them said: He who rarely does bad deeds keeps his oath, and if he rarely does bad deeds, he will be saved. Therefore, his statement, that you be righteous is a reason for the prohibition, i.e. do not make God an object of your oaths, intending that you be righteous, pious, and righteous, because whoever swears by God a lot will be emboldened to break his oath and commit an immoral act. There have been statements made in interpreting the verse that go back to the aspects we mentioned. Among them is the statement of Al-Zajjaj that the meaning of the verse is that if a man is asked to do something that is good, he will swear by God, and say, I swear by God, even though he did not swear. It has also been said that its meaning is: Do not swear falsely by God if you intend righteousness, piety, and reform. It has also been said that its meaning is: If you swear not to maintain ties of kinship, give charity, or reform, and similar acts of righteousness, then atone for your oath. It has also been said that his statement, that you be righteous is a subject whose predicate has been omitted, i.e. righteousness and piety, and reform is more appropriate. Al-Zajjaj said it, and it was said that it is in the accusative case: meaning, do not let an oath to God prevent you from righteousness, piety, and reform. This was also narrated from Al-Zajjaj, and it was said that its meaning is that you do not be righteous, so he deleted la, like his saying: God makes clear to you lest you go astray, meaning do not go astray. Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari said it, and it was said that it is in the genitive case according to Al-Khalil and Al-Kisa’i, and the meaning is in that you be righteous. And his saying: Hearer means of the words of the servants, Knower of what they issue.
2:225: And the word lagha is the source of lagha yalgoo ghawan, and lagha yalighi laghayan means if he said something that is not needed in speech or something that is not good, and it is the fallen that is not taken into account, so the lagha from the oath is the fallen that is not taken into account, and from it the lagha in blood money, and it is the fallen that is not taken into account from the offspring of camels, Jarir said: And the patient goes between them in vain, just as the dialogue was abolished in blood money. Another said: And the pilgrims' flocks are restrained from idle talk and obscene speech. That is, do not speak about what is depraved and obscene. The meaning of the verse is: God will not punish you for what is depraved in your oaths, but He will punish you for what your hearts have earned: that is, what you have committed with the intention of doing so: which is the binding oath. Similar to this is the Almighty’s statement: But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn in deed. Similar to this is the statement of the poet: I am not taken by the eloquence he says if the determined ones do not intend it Scholars have differed in the interpretation of lahjud. Ibn Abbas, Aisha and the majority of scholars also said: It is a man saying, No, by God, and Yes, by God, in his speech and words, not believing in an oath or intending it. Al-Marwazi said: This is the meaning of lahjud oath that most scholars have agreed upon. Abu Hurairah and a group of the Salaf said: It is when a man swears about something, thinking it is it, but it is not what he thought. This is the view of the Hanafis and Zaidis, and Malik said the same in Al-Muwatta. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: A lahjud oath is when you swear while you are angry. This was also said by Tawus and Makhul, and it was narrated from Malik. It was said: A lahjud is an oath of disobedience. This was said by Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr and his brother Urwah, like the one who swears to drink alcohol or to sever family ties. It was also said: A lahjud oath is a man’s supplication against himself, such as saying: May God blind his sight, may God take away his wealth, he is a Jew, and he is a polytheist. Zayd ibn Aslam said: Mujahid said: The idle oath is when two men buy and sell, and one of them says: By God, I will not sell to you for such-and-such, and the other says: By God, I will not buy it for such-and-such. Ad-Dahhak said: The idle oath is the one that expiates: that is, if it expiates, it is dropped and becomes idle. The first statement is more correct because it is consistent with the linguistic meaning, and because the evidence indicates it, as will come. And His statement: 225- And God is Forgiving and Forbearing means that He does not hold you accountable for what you say with your tongues without intention or purpose. And He holds you accountable for what your hearts intend and your tongues speak, and that is the intended binding oath. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not make God an object of your oaths, he said: Do not make me an object of your oath not to do good, but expiate for your oath and do good. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority: It is when a man swears not to speak to his relatives or not to give charity, and there is anger between two men, so he swears not to reconcile them and says: I have sworn. He said: He expiates for his oath. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: A man came to Aisha and said: I vowed that if I spoke to so-and-so, then every slave of mine would be freed, and every wealth of mine would be a covering for the house. She said: Do not make your slaves freed and do not make your wealth a covering for the house, for God says: And do not make God an object of your oaths, so expiate for your oath. It was reported that this verse was revealed about Abu Bakr regarding Mastih. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, and the story is well-known. It has been proven in the authentic hadiths in the two Sahihs and others that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him do what is better and expiate for his oath. It has also been proven in the two Sahihs and others that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, if God wills, I will not swear an oath and then see something better than it, except that I will do what is better and expiate for my oath. Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Aishah that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath to sever family ties or to commit a sin, then his righteousness is to break it and go back on his oath. Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no vow or oath regarding that which the son of Adam does not possess, nor in disobedience to God nor in severing family ties. Abu Dawud and al-Hakim narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Umar. An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Malik Al-Jashmi who said: I said, O Messenger of God, my cousin comes to me and I swear that I will not give him anything or connect with him. He said: Make expiation for your oath. Malik narrated in Al-Muwatta', and Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Humaid, Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Aisha who said: This verse was revealed: God will not punish you for what is unintentional in your oaths regarding a man who says: No, by God, and Yes, by God, and No, by God. Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah that he was asked about unintentional oaths and he said: Aisha said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is a man's speech in his house, 'No, by God' and 'Yes, by God.' Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Humaid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said in her interpretation of the verse: Unintentional oaths are people who evade a matter, saying, "This one says, 'No, by God' and this one says, 'No, by God'. They evade a matter but their hearts are not settled on it." Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: It is idle talk in jest and playfulness, which is a man saying: No, by God, and yes, by God. There is no expiation for that, but expiation is for what he has decided in his heart to do and then does not do it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by some people who were shooting arrows, and with him was a man from his companions. A man from the people shot and said: I hit, by God, and I missed, by God. The one who was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The man broke his oath, O Messenger of God. He said: No, the oaths of archers are idle talk and there is no expiation or punishment for them.” Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Aisha, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar and Ibn Amr that idle talk is: No, by God, and yes, by God. It was narrated by Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Saeed bin Mansour and Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: A idle oath is when you swear while you are angry. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: A idle oath is when a person swears to something thinking that it is what he swore to, but it is not what it is. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Aisha something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is when a man swears to forbid what God has made lawful for him. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: It is a man who swears to commit a sin. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Nakha’i: It is when a man swears to do something and then forgets. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: And God is Forgiving meaning that He overlooks the oath that a person swears, Forbearing because He did not make it an expiation.
2:226: His saying: 226- They swear means they take an oath: and the source is ilaan, alia, and al-wa, and Ibn Abbas read: those who swore. It is said: ala ya'ali and ya'tali with the ta' itila': meaning he swore, and from it: And let not those among you who are endowed with virtue swear, and from it: He who has few sighs keeps his oath the house. Scholars have differed regarding ila'. The majority said: ila' is when a man swears not to have intercourse with his wife for more than four months. If he swears for four months or less, he is not considered to have ila' and in their view it is a pure oath. This is what Malik, Ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Abu Thawr said. Ath-Thawri and the Kufians said: ila' is when he swears for four months or more, and this is the opinion of Ata'. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he is not considered to have ila' until he swears not to touch her ever. A group said: If he swears not to approach his wife for a day or less or more, and then does not have intercourse for four months, she is separated from him by ila'. This is what Ibn Mas'ud, An-Nakha'i, Ibn Abi Laila, Al-Hakam, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, Qatadah and Ishaq said. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: Many scholars rejected this opinion. His saying: Of their women includes free women and slave women if they are wives. Likewise, the slave who swears an oath from his wife is included under his saying: For those who swear an oath. This is what Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Abu Thawr said. They said: His oath is like that of a free man. Malik, Al-Zuhri, Ata’, Abu Hanifa, and Ishaq said: His term is two months. Al-Sha’bi said: The oath of a slave woman is half that of a free woman. Waiting is to be patient and to delay. The poet said: The vicissitudes of fate lie in wait for her, perhaps she will be divorced one day, or her husband will die. God the Almighty set this period to protect the wife from harm. The people of the Age of Ignorance used to swear that they would spend one or two years or more than that, intending to harm women. It has been said that the four months are the months that a woman cannot bear to be away from her husband for more than that. His statement, Then if they return means they go back. And from this: Until it returns to the command of God means it returns. And from this, the shadow after noon is called fā’i because it returns from the east to the west. It is said: fā’i yafī’ and fī’u he returned quickly, and it is quick to return, meaning to return. And from this is the saying of the poet: It came and did not fulfill what it came for, and there are human needs that cannot be fulfilled. Ibn al-Mundhir said: All those who have preserved knowledge have agreed that fay’ is intercourse for someone who has no excuse. If he has an excuse such as illness or imprisonment, then she is his wife. If the excuse is removed and he refuses intercourse, then they are separated if the period has passed. This was stated by Malik. A group said: If he testifies to his fay’ in his heart while he has an excuse, then it is sufficient for him. This is what al-Hasan, Ikrimah, al-Nakha’i, al-Awza’i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said. The majority of scholars have made it obligatory for a master to pay expiation if he has intercourse with his wife. Al-Hasan and al-Nakha’i said: He does not have to pay expiation.
2:227: His saying: 227- And if they decide on divorce Resolve: is a contract on something, and it is said that he resolved, he resolves, and he resolves, and he resolves, so the meaning of they resolved on al-Talaq 65:they resolved on it in their hearts. Divorce is from the word talaqat a woman is divorced, like nasara yansur victory, divorce, so she is divorced and divorced also, and it is permissible to say talaqat with a damma on the lam, like azam ya'zam greatness, and Al-Akhfash rejected it. Divorce is the dissolution of the marriage contract, and in that is evidence that she is not divorced after the passage of four months as Malik said, unless a divorce is initiated after the period, and also he said: All-Hearing, and All-Hearing requires something heard after the passage. Abu Hanifa said: All-Hearing for his oath, All-Knowing of his decision which was indicated by the passage of four months. Know that the people of every school of thought have interpreted this verse in a way that matches their school of thought and have taken upon themselves what the wording does not indicate, nor any other evidence, and its meaning is clear and obvious, which is that God has made the term for the one who swears an oath from his wife four months. Then He said: Informing His servants of the ruling of this Master after this period, If they return they return to the continuation of the marriage and the continuation of the marriage, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning He will not hold them accountable for that oath, but will forgive them and have mercy on them. But if they decide on divorce, meaning they decide on it and intend it, then indeed, God is Hearing, of that from them, Knowing, so this is the meaning of the verse about which there is no doubt or suspicion. So whoever swears to have intercourse with his wife and does not set a period or sets a period of more than four months, we must give him four months. If that period passes, he has the choice, either to return to marrying his wife, and his wife after the period has passed is the same as his wife was before it, or to divorce her and he has the ruling of one who has divorced his wife from the beginning. As for if he sets a time limit without four months, if he wants to fulfill his oath, he should separate from his wife from whom he swore until the period expires, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did when he swore from his wives for a month, then he separated from them until the month passed. And if he wants to have intercourse with his wife before that period has passed, If he is less than four months old, he broke his oath and must make expiation. He was complying with what was authentically reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said: Whoever swears to do something and then sees something better than it, let him do something better than it and make expiation for his oath. Al-Shafi’i, Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Ila’ is when he swears that he will never have intercourse with her. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on his authority regarding the statement: For those who swear not to have intercourse with their wives, he said: It is a man who swears to his wife by God that he will not marry her, so she waits four months. If he marries her, he expiates for his oath. If four months pass before he marries her, the ruler gives him the choice, either he returns to her or he decides to divorce her, as God Almighty said. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority that he said: Ila’ in the Age of Ignorance was one or two years or more than that, so God set a time limit of four months for them. If his Ila’ was the Ila’ of the Age of Ignorance, one or two years or more than that, then God set a time limit of four months for them. If his Ila’ was less than four months, then it is not Ila’. Abdul bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ali who said: There are two types of ila’: ila’ in anger and ila’ in consent. As for ila’ in anger: if four months have passed, she is separated from him, but as for what was in consent, he will not be held accountable for it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: There is no ila’ except in anger. Abu Ubaid narrated in his Fadhail and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b that he recited: If they return therein, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Abdul bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ali who said: Fay’ is sexual intercourse. Saeed bin Mansour, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud something similar. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali who said: Fay’ is consent. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud something similar. Abdul bin Hamid narrated on the authority of al-Hasan who said: Fay’ is witnessing. Abdul Razzaq narrated on his authority who said: Fay’ is sexual intercourse, but if he has an excuse, it is sufficient for him to return with his tongue. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: If illness, travel, imprisonment, or something that excuses him, comes between him and her, then his witnessing it is a compensation. The salaf had different opinions regarding compensation, so we should refer to the meaning of compensation in language, which we have explained. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said regarding ila’: If four months have passed, nothing is due from him until he stops and divorces her or keeps her. Ash-Shafi’i, Ibn Jarir, and al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from Uthman ibn Affan. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from Ali. Al-Bukhari and Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar from Ibn Umar. Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from Aisha. Ibn Jarir, Ad-Daraqutni, and al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih from his father who said: I asked twelve men from the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about a man who swears to divorce his wife, and all of them said: Nothing is due from him until four months have passed, then he stops and divorces her or keeps her. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Thabit ibn Ubaydah, the freed slave of Zayd ibn Thabit, on the authority of twelve men from the Companions, something similar. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umar, Uthman, Ali, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Umar, and Ibn Abbas, who said: The oath of abstention is an irrevocable divorce if four months pass before he returns, then she has full control over herself. The Companions and the Followers have different and contradictory opinions on this, and it is necessary to refer to what is in the noble verse, which is what we have made clear to you, so be firm on it. Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Umar, who said: The oath of a slave is two months. Malik narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: The oath of a slave is similar to the oath of a free man.
2:228: His statement: 228- And the divorced includes under its generality the divorced before consummation, then it was made specific by the Almighty's statement: So you have no waiting period for them to count so it is necessary to build the general on the specific, and the divorced before consummation is excluded from this generality, and likewise the pregnant woman is excluded by the Almighty's statement: And those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth and likewise the woman in despair is excluded by the Almighty's statement: Their waiting period is three months and waiting is waiting, it was said: it is report of the meaning of a command: i.e. let them wait, the intention by bringing it out as report is to confirm its occurrence, and he added to it confirmation of its occurrence as report for the subject. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is false, rather it is report about the ruling of the Shari'ah, so if a divorced woman is found who does not wait, then that is not from the Shari'ah, and it does not necessarily follow from that that the report of God the Almighty occurs in a way that contradicts its informant. And the menstrual periods are the plural of qur'. It was narrated from Nafi' that he read qur' with a shaddah on the waw. The majority read it with a hamza. Al-Hasan read it with the opening of the qaf, the sukoon of the ra’ and the tanween. Al-Asma’i said: The singular is qara’ with the damma of the qaf. Abu Zaid Al-Fath said: Both of them said: A woman menstruated: she became pure, and aqra’t: she became pure. Al-Akhfash said: A woman menstruated: if she became a woman of menstruation, then when she menstruated you say: qara’t without an alif. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ said: Some Arabs call menstruation qir’, and some call purity qir’, and some combine them and call menstruation and purity qir’. It should be known that qir’ originally means time. It is said: the winds blew for its qir’ and for its qari’, meaning for its time. From this is the saying of the poet: I hated the barrenness of the Banu Shaleel when the winds blew for its reader Menstruation is called a qur' and purity is called a qur', because each of them has a specific time. The Arabs sometimes used it to refer to purity, and sometimes to menstruation. One of its uses for purity is the saying of Al-A'sha: Every year you are a brave warrior, pulling your resolve to its furthest reaches A legacy of wealth and honor in the neighborhood because of the menstrual periods of your women that were lost in it That is, their purity. And from its application to menstruation, the poet said: Oh God, the one who is angry with me has a wound like a menstruating woman’s wound Meaning that he stabbed him and he had blood like the blood of a menstruating woman. Some people said: It is taken from the word qarra’ al-ma’ water pouring into a basin, which is its collection, and from it comes the Qur’an, because the meanings are combined in it. Amr ibn Kulthum said: My arms are broken, blood-stained, virgin, of mixed color, and have never read before. That is, she did not collect it in her womb. The result is that in the Arabic language, menstruation and purity are shared, and because of this shared meaning, the scholars differed in identifying what is meant by the menstrual periods mentioned in the verse. The people of Kufa said: It is menstruation, and this is the opinion of Omar, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Abu Musa, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ikrimah, As-Suddi and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. The people of Hijaz said: It is purity, and this is the opinion of Aisha, Ibn Omar, Zaid ibn Thabit, Az-Zuhri, Aban ibn Uthman and Ash-Shafi’i. Know that they agreed that menstruation is time, so the meaning of the verse became clear to all of them, and the divorced women wait by themselves for three times, so on this basis it is explained in the number and general in the counted, so it is necessary to seek clarification for the counted from someone other than her. The people of the first opinion provided evidence that what is meant in this verse is menstruation by the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Leave prayer during your menstrual periods and by his saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The divorce of a slave woman is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstrual periods and by the fact that what is meant by waiting period is to cleanse the womb, which occurs with menstruation, not with purity. The proponents of the second opinion cited as evidence the words of God the Almighty: So divorce them during their waiting period. There is no disagreement that divorce is commanded at the time of purity. And the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Umar: “Tell him to take her back, then to keep her until she is pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure. This is the waiting period that God has commanded women to be divorced during.” This is because the time of purity is when women are divorced. Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman said: We did not find any of our jurists who did not say that the menstrual periods are the periods of purity. So if a man divorces during a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse, she must observe the waiting period for what remains of it, even if it is an hour or a moment. Then she begins a second period of purity after a menstrual period. If she sees blood from the third menstrual period, she ends the waiting period. End quote. In my opinion, there is no proof in some of what the proponents of both opinions cited as evidence. As for the statement of the first scholars that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Leave prayer during your menstrual periods, the most that can be said about this is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used the term menstrual periods to mean menstruation, and there is no dispute about the permissibility of that, as is the case with a general term, as it is sometimes used to mean this and sometimes to mean that. The dispute is only about the menstrual periods mentioned in this verse. As for his statement (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the female slave: Her waiting period is two menstrual periods, it is a hadeeth narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Daraqutni and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, on the authority of Aishah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was also narrated by Ibn Majah and al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and its evidence for what the first scholars said is strong. As for their statement that the purpose of the waiting period is to cleanse the womb, and this occurs with menstruation, not with purity. The answer to this is that it is only completed if there is nothing of menstruation in this waiting period, assuming that menstruation is interpreted as purity, and this is not the case, rather it includes menstruation as it includes purity. As for the evidence of the proponents of the second opinion based on the Almighty’s saying: So divorce them for their waiting period, the answer to this is that the dispute over the lam in His saying: for their waiting period, makes it possible, and the argument does not stand on possible. As for their evidence based on the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Umar: Order him to take her back, the hadith is in the Sahih, and its evidence is strong for what they have gone to, and it can be said: The waiting period ends with three purity periods or three menstruation periods, and there is no objection to that, as a group of scholars have permitted applying the ambiguous meaning to both of them, and in this way the evidence is combined, the disagreement is resolved, and the dispute is dispelled. Al-Zamakhshari found it difficult to distinguish the three by saying: Menstruation, which is a plural of abundance, not menstruation, which is a plural of paucity. He answered that they are broad in this, so they use each of the two plurals in place of the other because they share in the collection. His saying: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs. It was said that what is meant by this is menstruation, and it was said: pregnancy, and it was said: both. The reason for the prohibition of concealment is that it harms the husband in some cases and takes away his right. So if a woman says: I menstruated when she did not menstruate, she takes away his right to take her back, and if she says: I did not menstruate when she did menstruate, she obliges him to pay maintenance that he was not obligated to, and she harms him. Likewise, pregnancy may be concealed in order to cut off his right to take her back, and she may claim it in order to oblige him to pay maintenance, and other similar purposes that entail harming the husband. There are different opinions about the period in which a woman is to be believed if she claims that her waiting period has ended. His saying: If they believe in God and the Last Day contains a severe warning to those who conceal, and a statement that whoever conceals that among them does not deserve the name of faith. Ba'ulah is the plural of Ba'l, which means husband. It is called Ba'l because it is higher than the wife because they call it the Lord. Hence the saying of God the Almighty: Do you call upon Ba'l? meaning Lord? It is also said: Ba'ul and Ba'ulah as it is said in the masculine plural, dhikruh and dhikruh. This ta' is for the feminization of the plural, which is irregular and cannot be used as an analogy, but rather what is heard is taken into account. Ba'ulah is also a source of the man's ba'l, like mana'a yanma'a: meaning he became a husband. His saying: More entitled to take them back means to take them back. This is specific to those whom the husband may return to, so it is considered a specialization due to the generality of his saying: And divorced women shall wait concerning themselves because it includes divorced women and others. His saying: In that means during the waiting period. If the waiting period expires, she is more entitled to herself, and she is not permissible for him except through a new marriage with a guardian, witnesses, and a new dowry. There is no disagreement about that. Taking back can be verbally or by intercourse, and none of the rulings of marriage are binding on the woman who returns, without disagreement. And his saying: If they desire reconciliation meaning by returning: meaning to reform his situation with her and her situation with him, if he intended to harm her then it is forbidden because of the saying of God the Almighty: And do not keep them for harm in order to transgress It was said: And if he intended harm by returning then it is valid even if he committed a forbidden act and wronged himself, and based on this the condition mentioned in the verse is to urge husbands to intend reconciliation and to deter them from intending harm, and it is not intended to make the intention of reconciliation a condition for the validity of returning. His saying: And they have rights similar to those against them according to what is equitable meaning they have marital rights over men like what men have over them, so he treats her well in what is known from the custom of people that they do for their wives, and she likewise treats her husband well in what is known from the custom of women that they do for their wives, and she likewise treats her husband well in what is known from the custom of women that they do for their husbands of obedience, adornment, endearment and the like. His saying: And men have a degree over them means a status that they do not have, which is his responsibility to provide for her, and his being one of the people of jihad, reason and strength, and his inheritance being greater than hers, and her being obligated to obey his command and abide by his pleasure. If there was no superiority of men over women except that they were created from men, it would not have been proven that Eve was created from Adam’s rib. Abu Dawud, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Asma bint Yazid bin Al-Sakan Al-Ansariyyah, who said: I was divorced during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and the divorced woman did not have an ‘iddah. When she was divorced, God revealed the ‘iddah for divorce, saying: Divorced women shall wait Al-Ma’idah 2:17. Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods Al-Ma’idah 2:17. Then He said: And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you doubt, their period is three months Al-Ma’idah 2:17. Then He abrogated and said: Then you divorced them before you touched them, then you have no ‘iddah to count for them. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Daraqutni and Al-Bayhaqi narrated through the chains of narration of Aisha that she said: The menstrual periods are the pure periods. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar and Zaid bin Thabit. The aforementioned ones narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar who said: Menstruation means menstruation, on the authority of the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: three menstrual periods he said: three menstrual periods. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs he said: a woman used to conceal her pregnancy until she gave it to another man, then God forbade them from that. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding the verse he said: pregnancy and menstruation. Abd al-Razzaq and Saeed ibn Mansur narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And their husbands have more right to take them back he said: if a man divorces his wife once or twice while she is pregnant, he has more right to take her back as long as she has not given birth, and this is His statement: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And their husbands have more right to take them back during that period, he said: During the waiting period. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah something similar, and he added: Unless he divorces her three times. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: And they women have rights similar to those of men over them, he said: If they obey God and obey their husbands, then he must treat them well, refrain from harming them, and spend on them from his wealth. The people of Sunan narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Al-Ahwas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Behold, you have rights over your women and your women have rights over you. Your right over your women is that they should not share your beds with anyone you dislike, nor allow anyone you dislike into your homes. Behold, their right over you is that you treat them well in their clothing and food.” At-Tirmidhi authenticated it. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mu'awiyah ibn Haidah al-Qushayri that he asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): What is the right of a woman over her husband? He said: That you feed her when you eat, clothe her when you clothe yourself, do not strike her in the face, and do not abandon her except in the house. 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the statement of God, But men have a degree over them, that he said: The superiority with which God has given him superiority over her in jihad, the superiority of his inheritance over her inheritance, and everything with which He has given her superiority. 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding the verse: He divorces her, but she has no say in the matter. They narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Leadership.
2:229: What is meant by the aforementioned divorce is the revocable one, as evidenced by what was mentioned in the first verse: that is, the divorce in which the husbands are able to return to her is two times: that is, the first and second divorces, since there is no return after the third. Rather, the Almighty said: 229- two times and did not say two divorces, indicating that the divorce should be one time after another, not two divorces at once, as a group of commentators said. And since there is nothing after the second divorce except one of two things, either the occurrence of the third one by which the wife is separated, or keeping her and continuing her marriage, and not performing the third upon her, the Almighty said: Then keep her on acceptable terms or release her with kindness. That is, after the return, for the one whom her husband divorced twice on acceptable terms: that is, according to what is known among people of good treatment, or release her with kindness, that is, by performing a third divorce upon her without causing her harm. It was said that what is meant is: Then keep her on acceptable terms, that is, by returning after the second divorce, or release her with kindness. “With kindness” meaning by not taking her back after the second time until her waiting period has expired. The first is more apparent. His saying: divorce is a subject with an estimated addition: meaning the number of divorces in which taking her back is established twice. The scholars have differed about sending the three divorces at once, does it count as three or only one? The majority went with the first, and those other than them went with the second, which is the truth. I have stated it in my writings with a comprehensive statement, and I have devoted an independent letter to it. His saying: And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them is addressed to the husbands: that is, it is not lawful for the husbands to take anything of what they have given to their wives as a dowry in a way that would harm them. The indefiniteness of anything is for disparagement: that is, a small amount, let alone a lot. He made specific what they gave them by not allowing it to be taken, even though it is not lawful for the husbands to take anything of their money that they own other than the dowry, because that is what the husband’s soul is attached to and seeks to take, not what is other than it, which is in her possession. However, if taking what he gave her is not lawful for him, then what is other than it is forbidden to him a fortiori. It was said: The address in His saying: And it is not lawful for you is to the imams and judges to match His saying: But if you fear, because the address in it is to the imams and judges, and on this basis the taking is attributed to them because they are the ones who command that. The first is more appropriate because of his saying: from what you have given them, for its attribution to other than the husbands is very far-fetched, because giving to the husbands was not by their command. It was said that the second is more appropriate so that the system does not get confused. His saying: except if they both fear means that it is not permissible for you to take anything from what you have given them unless they both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits set by God, meaning that they will not be able to keep within the limits set by God for the spouses, and that He has made it obligatory for them to fulfill them of good treatment and obedience. If they both fear that, there is no blame upon them for what she ransoms herself with, meaning there is no blame upon the man for taking, and upon the woman for giving, by ransoming herself from that marriage by giving some money that the husband is satisfied with and he divorces her for it. This is khul‘. The majority of scholars have held that this is permissible for the husband, and that it is permissible for him to take despite that fear, which is what the Qur’an clearly stated. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from some of the people of knowledge that what he took is not permissible for him and he is not forced to return it, and this is extremely flawed. Hamzah read: except that they fear in the passive voice, and the subject is omitted, which is the imams and the rulers. Abu Ubaid chose it, saying: for his saying: if you fear, so he made the fear for other than the spouses. This was used as evidence by those who made the divorce to the ruler, namely Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin. An-Nahhas weakened the choice of Abu Ubaid mentioned above. And his saying: if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God means if the imams and rulers, or those who mediate between the spouses, even if they are not imams and rulers, fear that the spouses will not keep within the limits of God, which is what He has made obligatory upon them as mentioned above. It was narrated from Bakr bin Abdullah Al-Madani that this verse was abrogated by the saying of God the Almighty in Surat An-Nisaa': "And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount [of wealth], do not take from it anything. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?" This is a statement outside of consensus, and there is no contradiction between the two. Scholars have differed as to whether it is permissible for a husband to ask his wife for more than what he paid her as a dowry and what accompanies it, and the woman accepts that. The apparent meaning of the Qur’an is that it is permissible because it is not restricted to a specific amount. This is what Malik, Ash-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr said. A similar statement was narrated from a group of the Companions and Followers. Tawus, Ata’, Al-Awza’i, Ahmad and Ishaq said that it is not permissible. We will see what was narrated about that from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). God the Almighty said: These are the limits set by God meaning the rulings on marriage and separation mentioned are the limits set by God that you have been commanded to abide by. Do not transgress them by disobeying them, lest you deserve what God mentioned of recording the one who does that as being unjust.
2:230: God Almighty says: 230- If he divorces her meaning the third divorce that God Almighty mentioned in His saying: or releases her with good treatment meaning if that happens from him then she is forbidden to him by the triple then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband meaning until she marries another husband. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and those who agreed with him took the literal meaning of the verse. They said: The mere contract is sufficient because it is what is meant by His statement: until she marries another husband. The majority of the early and later generations held that intercourse is necessary with the contract, because it was proven from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that this was considered, and it is an addition that must be accepted. Perhaps Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and those who followed him did not reach this. The verse is evidence that this must be a legitimate marriage intended for its own sake, not a marriage not intended for its own sake, but rather a trick to make it permissible and a means to return her to the first husband, because that is forbidden due to the evidence that came in condemning it and condemning the one who does it, and that it is the borrowed goat that the Lawgiver cursed and cursed the one who took it for that purpose. His statement: But if he divorces her meaning the second husband there is no blame upon them meaning the first husband and the woman if they return to each other meaning each one of them returns to the other. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The scholars have agreed that if a free man divorces his wife three times, then her waiting period ends and she marries another husband and he consummates the marriage with her, then he separates from her, and her waiting period ends and the first husband marries her, she remains with him on three divorces. His statement, If they think that they will keep the limits of God means the marital rights that are due to each of them from the other. However, if that is not thought to be the case, such that they or one of them knows that they will not keep the limits of God, or they or one of them hesitate and they do not think so, then it is not permissible to enter into this marriage because it is likely to lead to disobedience to God and falling into what He has forbidden for spouses. His statement, And these are the limits of God is an indication of the aforementioned rulings, as mentioned above, and it is specific to those who know, with the generality of the call to the scholar and others, and the obligation of conveying it to every individual, because they are the ones who benefit from the aforementioned explanation. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Abd ibn Humayd, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father who said: If a man divorced his wife and then took her back before her waiting period was over, that would be his, even if he divorced her a thousand times. Then a man went to his wife and divorced her, and when the time for her waiting period was approaching he took her back, then divorced her, then said: By God, I will not take you back to me and you will never be permissible for me. Then God revealed: “Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.” So people faced divorce anew from that day, those among them who had divorced and those who had not. A similar narration was narrated by At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Hakim who authenticated it on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha. Al-Bukhari narrated on her authority that a woman came to her and asked her about divorce. She said: So she mentioned that to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so the verse: Divorce is twice was revealed. Abdul Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ahmad, Abdul bin Hamid, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Razan Al-Asadi who said: “A man said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of God’s statement, ‘Divorce is twice,’ so where is the third? He said: ‘Release with kindness for the third time.’” Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Abdul bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: God said for the third time, ‘Either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with kindness.’ Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib who said: Release in God’s Book is divorce. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, and some of the companions of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) regarding his statement, ‘Divorce is twice,’ they said: It is the time at which the woman can be taken back. So if he divorces her once or twice, he can either keep her and take her back with kindness, or he can remain silent until her waiting period ends, and she will have more right to herself. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: A man used to eat from his wife’s money that he had given her as a gift and other things without thinking that it was a sin. Then God revealed: And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them 1:10. After this verse, it was not permissible for them to take anything from their money except according to its right. Then He said: “Unless they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God. But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God” 1:10. And He said: But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, then take it in satisfaction and ease. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Unless they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God 1:10. He said: Unless the rebellion and bad character are on her part, so she invites you to ransom herself from you, then there is no sin on you for what she ransoms herself with. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, An-Nasa’i and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umrah bint Abd ar-Rahman ibn As’ad ibn Zararah, “On the authority of Habibah bint Sahl Al-Ansari that she loved Thabit ibn Qays, and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out for the dawn prayer and found her at his door in the early hours of the morning. He said: Who is this? She said: I am Habibah bint Sahl. He said: What is the matter with you? She said: Neither I nor you. When Thabit ibn Qays came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: This is Habibah bint Sahl. She mentioned what God willed her to mention, and Habibah said: O Messenger of God, everything that He has given me is with Him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take from her. So he took from her and she stayed with her family.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: This verse was revealed about Thabit ibn Qays and Habeeba, who had complained about him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Will you return his garden to him?’ She said: ‘Yes.’ So he called him and mentioned that to him, and he said: ‘I like that.’ He said: ‘Yes.’ Thabit said: ‘I have done so.’ Then the verse, ‘And it is not lawful for you to take’ was revealed.” Abd al-Razzaq, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umrah on the authority of Aishah, something similar. Al-Bukhari, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Jamilah bint Abdullah ibn Salul, the wife of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I do not find fault with Thabit ibn Qays in his character or religion, but I cannot stand him out of hatred and I hate disbelief in Islam.’ He said: ‘Will you return his garden to him?’ She said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Accept the garden and divorce her once.’” Ibn Majah said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered him to take his garden from it and not to take more.” Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: “A woman came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘I hate my husband and I want to leave him.’ He said: ‘Do you want his garden that I gave you as a dowry?’ She said: ‘Yes and more.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘As for the extra from your money, no.’” Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr that Thabit ibn Qays mentioned the story, and in it: ‘As for the extra, no.’ Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and in it: ‘The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered Thabit to take what he had brought and not to take more.’ Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id and mentioned the story, and in it: ‘His garden was returned to him and more.’ Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of ‘Umar that he said about some women who had been divorced by khul‘: Divorce her even if it was her earring. In a wording narrated by ‘Abd al-Razzaq on his authority, he said to the husband: ‘Take even if it was her turban.’ Al-Bukhari said: ‘Uthman permitted khul‘ without her turban.’ And Abd bin Hamid and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ata’ that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked taking from the woman who sought divorce more than he gave her. There are hadiths that criticize women who sought divorce, including those narrated on the authority of Thawban, narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without a valid reason, the fragrance of Paradise will be forbidden to her. And he said: Women who seek divorce are hypocrites. And there are hadiths narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, narrated by Ibn Majah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A woman should not ask her husband for divorce for no reason, lest she find the fragrance of Paradise, even though its fragrance can be detected at a distance of forty years. And there are hadiths narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, narrated by Ahmad and Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Women who seek divorce and those who seek divorce are hypocrites. And there are hadiths narrated on the authority of Uqbah, narrated by Ibn Jarir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, like the hadith of Abu Hurairah. Scholars have differed regarding the waiting period of a woman who has been divorced by khul‘. The most correct opinion is that she must observe a menstrual period, based on what was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi who classed it as hasan, al-Nasa’i and al-Hakim who classed it as saheeh, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the wife of Thabit ibn Qays to observe a menstrual period.” And al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’ bint Mu’adh ibn ‘Afra, “She was divorced by khul‘ during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered her to observe a menstrual period, or she was ordered to observe a menstrual period.” Al-Tirmidhi said: The correct opinion is that she was ordered to observe a menstrual period. Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated on her authority that she said: I divorced my husband by khul‘, so I went to ‘Uthman and asked him what my waiting period is. He said: There is no waiting period for you unless you have recently been divorced, in which case you should wait until you menstruate once. She said: I am only following the ruling of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding Maryam al-Mughaliyah, who loved Thabit ibn Qays and so she divorced him by khul‘. Al-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi' bint Mu'awwidh that "the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the wife of Thabit ibn Qays to wait one menstrual period and then join her family." Nothing that contradicts this has been reported in the Prophet's (blessings and peace of God be upon him) hadith. Rather, it has been reported on the authority of a group of the Companions and Followers that the waiting period for a woman who has been divorced by Khul' is like the waiting period for divorce, and this is what the majority of scholars said. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is the opinion of most of the scholars among the Companions and others. They based their evidence for this on the fact that a woman who has been divorced by Khul' is among the divorced women, so she is included under the general meaning of the Qur'an. The truth is what we have mentioned, because what has been reported on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifies the general meaning of the Qur'an. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: But if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him, meaning: If he divorces her three times, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ali. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ash-Shafi’i, ‘Abdur-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Muslim, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of ‘Aa’ishah who said: “The wife of Rifa’ah Al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and said: ‘I was with Rifa’ah and he divorced me, so my divorce was final. ‘Abdur-Rahman ibn Az-Zubayr married me, and he had nothing but the hem of a garment. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) smiled and said: ‘Do you want to go back to Rifa’ah? Not until you taste his honey and he tastes your honey.’” Something similar to this has been narrated on her authority through various chains of narration. ‘Abdur-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of ‘Umar with a similar chain of narration on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) as well. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Anas with a similar chain of narration on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) as well. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah with a similar chain of narration on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). These three companions did not name the one who told the story. Ahmad and al-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that "al-Amisa' or al-Rumaisa' came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace" and at the end of it "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is not for you until another man tastes your honey." The cursing of the muhallil has been proven in hadiths, including those on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, according to Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, and al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, who said: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the muhallil and the one for whom he is muhallil." There are also hadiths on the authority of Ali, according to Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and al-Bayhaqi, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, like the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. There are also hadiths on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, according to al-Tirmidhi, like it. There are also hadiths on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, according to Ibn Majah, like it. There are also hadiths on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, according to Ibn Majah, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, like it. There are also hadiths on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, according to Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Bayhaqi, like it. There are also hadiths on this topic condemning the muhallil and its doer. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: But if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them if they return to each other, meaning: If she marries after the first one and the second one consummates the marriage with her, there is no blame upon the first one if he marries her if the second one divorces her or dies, then she is lawful for him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil regarding his statement: That they establish the limits set by God, he said: The command of God and obeying Him.
2:231: Reaching something: its true meaning is reaching it. Reaching something is not used in the sense of approach except metaphorically due to a relationship with an indication as here. It is not correct to intend the true meaning, because the woman has reached the last part with an indication as here. It is not correct to intend the true meaning, because the woman has reached the last part of the waiting period and passed it to the part that is the term for its expiration. She has left the waiting period and the husband has no way to deal with her. Al-Qurtubi said in his interpretation: The meaning of 231- reached here is that they approached by consensus of the scholars. He said: And because the meaning is that he is forced to do that, because after reaching the term he has no choice in keeping her, and keeping her in a good manner is fulfilling the rights of the wife: that is, if you divorce women and they are close to the end of the waiting period, do not harm them by returning without intending to continue the marriage and make it last, but rather choose one of two things: either keeping her in a good manner without intending to cause harm or releasing her with kindness: that is, leaving her until her waiting period ends without returning her in a harmful manner, and do not keep them in a harmful manner as the Jahiliyyah used to do by divorcing a woman until her waiting period ends, then returning her, not out of need or love, but with the intention of prolonging the waiting period and extending it during the waiting period in a harmful manner with the intention of aggression from you towards them and injustice towards them and whoever does that has wronged himself because he exposed himself to the punishment and wrath of God. Al-Zajjaj said: It means exposing oneself to punishment, because doing what God has forbidden exposes one to God’s punishment. And do not take the verses of God in jest, meaning do not take the rulings of God in jest, for they are all serious, and whoever jokes about them, they are binding on him. God, the Almighty, forbade them from doing what the people of ignorance used to do, for a man among them would divorce, or free, or marry, and say, I was joking. Al-Qurtubi said: There is no disagreement among the scholars that whoever divorces in jest, the divorce is binding on him. His statement: And remember the favor of God upon you, meaning the favor that you have attained through Islam and its laws after you were in ignorance, ignorant, and darknesses one above the other. The Book is the Qur’an. The commentators said that wisdom is the Sunnah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, established for them. He admonishes you thereby, meaning he frightens you with what He has revealed to you. The mention of the Book and wisdom, despite their primary inclusion in the favor, is a warning of their danger and the greatness of their importance. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: A man would divorce his wife and then take her back before her waiting period was over, then he would divorce her. He would do that to her, harming her and delaying her. Then God revealed: And when you divorce women 1:18. Malik, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Thawr ibn Yazid. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement: And do not keep them, to injure them, in order to aggravate their condition 1:18, he said: It is a man who divorces his wife and when her waiting period ends he yearns for her to take her back, meaning that he will prolong her waiting period. Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Musa who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “What is the matter with people who play with the limits set by God? He says: I have divorced you, I have taken you back, I have divorced you, I have taken you back. This is not the divorce of Muslims. Divorce a woman before her waiting period.” Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: “At the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a man would say to another man: ‘I have married you to my daughter,’ then he would say: ‘I was joking,’ and he would say: ‘I have been freed,’ and he would say: ‘I was joking.’ Then God Almighty revealed: ‘And do not take the verses of God in jest.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Three things, if said in jest or not, are binding upon him: divorce, marriage, and freeing a slave.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ said: “A man would divorce and then say: I played, and he would free and then say: I played. So God revealed: ‘And do not take the verses of God in jest.’ So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever divorces or frees a woman and says: I played, his statement is nothing and it applies to him and is binding on him.’” Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: A man divorced his wife while he was playing, not intending a divorce. So God revealed: ‘And do not take the verses of God in jest.’ So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made him divorce her. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to the hadith of Ubadah. Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah and Al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There are three things which are serious if done seriously and are done in jest: marriage, divorce and taking back a wife.”
2:232: The address in this verse in His saying: 232- And when you divorce and His saying: Do not prevent them either is to the husbands, and the meaning of preventing them is that they prevent them from marrying whomever they want from the husbands after the end of their waiting period due to the jealousy of the pre-Islamic era, as often happens among the caliphs and sultans out of jealousy for the women who were under them to become under others, because when they attained leadership in this world and what they became in of pride and arrogance, they imagine that they have left the race of the sons of Adam except for those whom God protected from them through piety and humility, or the address is to the guardians, and the meaning of attributing the divorce to them is that they are the cause of it because they are the ones who marry the divorced women from the husbands who divorced them. And reaching the term mentioned here is intended to mean the real meaning: its end, not as mentioned previously in the first verse. And preventing: confinement. Al-Khalil narrated a story about a hen with a blocked egg. It was said that ‘adhal means constriction and prevention, and it goes back to the meaning of confinement. It is said: I wanted something but you blocked me from it, meaning you prevented me and made things difficult for me. And ‘adhal’ means if you are at a loss for ways to do it. Al-Azhari said: The origin of ‘adhal comes from their saying ‘adhal’ the she-camel became blocked: if her young became stuck and it was not easy for them to come out. And ‘adhal’ the hen became stuck: its eggs became stuck. And every problem among the Arabs is ‘adhal’ constraint, and from this is the saying of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him: If the dilemmas confront me, I will reveal their hidden meanings by looking. It is said that the matter is difficult: if it becomes severe, and an incurable disease: meaning severe and difficult to cure, which has exhausted doctors, and someone prevented his wife: meaning he prevented her. The word ya’dhilha with the damma and the kasra are two languages. And his saying: that they marry meaning from that they marry, its place is the genitive according to Al-Khalil, and the accusative according to Sibawayh and Al-Farra’, and it was said: it is a substitute for inclusion of the accusative pronoun in his saying: so do not prevent them. And his saying: their husbands if it is intended by it those who divorce them then it is a metaphor in consideration of what was, and if it is intended by it those whom they want to marry then it is a metaphor in consideration of what will be. And his saying: that is an indication of what was separated from the rulings, and it was only made singular despite the fact that the aforementioned was plural, based on the meaning of the plural by interpreting it as the group and the like. And his saying: that is based on the wording of the plural, God Almighty differed between the two signs as a trial. And his saying: purer means more beneficial and more beneficial, and purer from impurities, and God knows what is good for you in it, and you do not know that. Al-Bukhari, the Sunan scholars and others narrated on the authority of Ma'qil ibn Yasar who said: I had a sister and my cousin came to me so I married her to him, and she remained with him as she was, then he divorced her once and did not take her back until the waiting period ended. He loved her and she loved him, then he proposed to her with the suitor, so I said to him: O wretch, I honored you with her and married you to her, so you divorced her and then you came to propose to her, and by God she will never return to you. He was a man of no consequence, and the woman wanted to return to him, so God knew his need for her and his need for her husband, so He revealed: And when you divorce women (al-Baqarah 2:17). He said: So the verse was revealed about her, so I atoned for my oath and married her to him.
