Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: This verse was revealed about a man who divorces his wife once or twice, and her waiting period ends, then he decides to marry her and take her back, and the woman wants that, but her guardian prevents her from doing so, so God forbade them from preventing her. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: This verse was revealed about Jabir bin Abdullah Al-Ansari. He had a cousin whose husband divorced her once and her waiting period had ended. He wanted to take her back, but Jabir refused. He said: You divorced our cousin and now you want to marry her a second time. The woman wanted her husband, so God revealed: And when you divorce women. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil: If they agree among themselves on what is reasonable. He meant a dowry, proof, and a new marriage. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Marry those who are single. A man said: O Messenger of God, what is the relationship between them? He said: What their families agree upon. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: And God knows and you do not know. He said: God knows about the love of each of them for the other what you, O guardian, do not know.
2:233: When God the Almighty mentioned marriage and divorce, He mentioned breastfeeding, because the spouses may separate and have a child between them, and for this reason it was said: This is specific to divorced women, and it was said: It is general. And His statement: 233- breastfeed It was said: It is a statement in the meaning of a command to indicate the fulfillment of its content, and it was said: It is a statement in its category and it is not in the meaning of a command according to what was mentioned previously in His statement: They wait and His statement: Completely is an emphasis to indicate that this estimation is actual and not approximate. And His statement: For whoever wants to complete the breastfeeding That is for whoever wants to complete the breastfeeding, and in it is evidence that breastfeeding for two years is not obligatory, but rather it is complete, and it is permissible to limit it to less than that. Mujahid and Ibn Muhaisin read for whoever wants to sleep with the opening of the taa and the raising of breastfeeding on the attribution of the action to it. Abu Haywah, Ibn Abi Ubla and Al-Jarud Ibn Abi Sabrah read with the kasra of the raa from breastfeeding, and it is a language. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he read the word al-Ruḍāḍah, and Ibn Abbas read it for whoever wanted to complete the breastfeeding. An-Nahhas said: The Basrans do not know the word al-Ruḍāḍah except with the fathah on the ra. The Kufians reported the permissibility of the kasrah. The verse indicates the obligation of breastfeeding on the mother for her child, and this was interpreted as if the infant did not accept anyone other than her. His statement: And upon the father of the child is their provision and clothing means upon the father for whom the child is born, and this wording was preferred over his statement: And upon the father to indicate that the children are for the fathers and not the mothers, and for this reason they are attributed to them without them as if they were only born for them. Its meaning was mentioned in Al-Kashshaf, and what is meant by provision here is the sufficient food that is known among people, and what is meant by clothing is what they also know, and in that is evidence of the obligation of that on the fathers for the breastfeeding mothers. This is in the case of divorced women, as for non-divorced women, their maintenance and clothing are obligatory on the husbands without their breastfeeding their children. His saying: No soul shall be charged except [with that within] its capacity is a restriction of his saying: with what is reasonable, meaning that these expenses and clothing that are obligatory upon the father are what people are accustomed to. He shall not be charged with anything of them except what is within his capacity and ability, not what is difficult for him and he is unable to do. It was said: What is meant is that the woman shall not be charged with patience in stinginess in wages, and the husband shall not be charged with what is extravagance, rather moderation shall be observed. His saying: Do not be harmed. Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir and a group read it, and Aban narrated it from Asim in the nominative case as a statement. Nafi’, Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Asim, according to the well-known report from him, read Tadharar with a fatha on the doubled ra’ as a prohibition. Its original form is La tadharar or La tadharar as an active or passive construction: meaning, do not harm the father because of the child by asking him for what he is unable to provide of sustenance and clothing, or by being stubborn in taking care of the child and doing what he needs, or do not be harmed by her husband by him falling short in anything that is required of him or taking her child from her without a reason. And thus the reading of the nominative case is open to both interpretations. Umar ibn Al-Khattab read La tadharar according to the original form with a fatha on the first ra’. Abu Ja’far ibn Al-Qa’qa’ read La tadharar with a sukoon on the ra’ and a light sukoon on it. It was narrated from the sukoon and the shaddah. Al-Hasan and Ibn Abbas read La tadharar with a kasra on the first ra’. It is possible that the ba’ in his saying with his child is a connection to his saying Tadharar as meaning do not harm: meaning, do not harm the mother. With her child, she raises him badly or neglects his food. The child is sometimes attributed to the father and sometimes to the mother, because each of them deserves to be attributed to him, with what is in that of sympathy. This sentence is an explanation of the sentence before it and a confirmation of it: that is, neither of them burdens the other with what he cannot bear, so do not harm him because of his child. His statement, and upon the heir is conjoined with his statement, and upon the child for him, and what is between them is an explanation of the known, or a justification for it, interrupted between the conjoined and the conjoined to. The scholars differed on the meaning of his statement: And the heir is obligated to do the same. It was said: It is the heir of the boy: that is, if the child dies, the heir of this child is obligated to breastfeed him, just as his father was obligated to do so. This was said by Umar ibn al-Khattab, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata’, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Hanifa, and Ibn Abi Laila. There is a difference of opinion among them as to whether the obligation is on the one who takes a share of the inheritance, or on the males only, or on every relative of his even if he is not his heir. It was said: What is meant by the heir is the heir of the father, and he is obligated to provide for the wet nurse and clothe her according to what is reasonable. This was said by al-Dahhak. Malik said in his interpretation of this verse something similar to what al-Dahhak said, but he said: It is abrogated, and the woman is not obligated to provide for a brother, relative, or relative of hers. Al-Dahhak stipulated that the boy should not have any money. If he had money, the wages for breastfeeding should be taken from his money. It was said: What is meant by the heir mentioned in the verse is the boy himself: that is, he must breastfeed himself from his own money if his father dies and he inherits from his money, said Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb and Bashir bin Nasser, the judge of Omar bin Abdul Aziz. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i, and it was said: He is the one who remains from the parents of the child after the death of the other one of them, so if the father dies, the mother is responsible for providing for the child if he has no money, said Sufyan Al-Thawri. It was said: The meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And upon the heir is the same means: The heir of the wet nurse must do with the child as the mother used to do with him in terms of breastfeeding, service and upbringing. It was said: The meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And upon the heir is the same is that it is forbidden for him to harm the mother just as it is forbidden for the father, and this is what a group of scholars said. They said: This is the basic principle, so whoever claims that it refers to all of what came before, then he must provide evidence. Al-Qurtubi said: This is correct, because if he meant all of them, which are breastfeeding, spending, and not causing harm, it would be said: And upon the heir is the like of these, which indicates that it is conjoined with the prevention of harm, and all the commentators interpreted it in this way, as reported by Judge Abdul Wahhab. Ibn Atiyyah said: Malik and all his companions, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Zuhri, Al-Dahhak, and a group of scholars said: What is meant by his saying like that is that she should not be harmed. As for sustenance and clothing, none of it is obligatory. Ibn Al-Qasim reported from Malik the same as we mentioned from him in the interpretation of this verse and the claim of abrogation. The weakness of what this group went to is not hidden from you, because what they specified with the meaning of his saying: And upon the heir is the like of that from that meaning: meaning not causing harm to the breastfeeding woman is indicated by his saying: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, because this is true of every harm that befalls her from the child or someone else. As for Al-Qurtubi’s statement: If he had meant all of them, he would have said the likes of these, it is clear that there is a clear weakness in it, because the demonstrative pronoun is suitable for the multiple as it is suitable for the single by interpreting the mentioned or something similar. As for what the people of the first opinion went to, that what is meant by the heir is the heir of the boy, it is said of him if he is not a real heir while the boy is alive, but he is a metaphorical heir considering what he leads to. As for what the people of the second opinion went to, even if it includes carrying the heir in its real meaning, there is something in the obligation of maintenance upon him while the boy is rich, and for this reason the one who said it restricted it to the boy being poor, and the point of difference in the interpretation of the heir is what was mentioned previously from mentioning the mothers, the one for whom the child was born, and the father, so it is possible that the heir is added to each of them. His statement: If they both desire weaning, the pronoun refers to the parents. Weaning: is the separation of the boy from the breast, and from it the young camel is called because it is separated from its mother. And His statement: By mutual consent of both of them means issued by mutual consent of both parents if the weaning is before two years then there is no blame upon them in that weaning. When God, the Almighty, explained that the period of breastfeeding is two complete years, He restricted that by saying: For whoever desires to complete the nursing and it appears that if the father alone wants to wean the boy before the two years, that is permissible for him. Here, the Almighty considered the consent of both parents and their consultation, so it is necessary to combine the two matters by saying: The will mentioned in His statement: For whoever desires to complete the nursing must be from them, or it can be said: That will is if the boy’s parents are not alive, such as if one of them is present, or the wet nurse of the boy is a wet nurse other than his mother. Consultation means extracting an opinion. It is said: I bought honey means I extracted it, and I bought an animal means I made it run to extract its milk. So if one of the parents wants to wean the infant, he must consent to the other and consult him until they reach an agreement on that. His saying: And if you wish to have wet nurses for your children, Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that you should have a wet nurse for your children other than the mother. And on the authority of Sibawayh, he deleted the lam because it takes two objects, and the first object is deleted, and the meaning is: that you should have wet nurses for your children. If you have given what you have given, with the extension, meaning you have given, and this is the reading of the group except Ibn Kathir, who read with the shortened: meaning you have done, and from this is the saying of Zuhair: Whatever good they did was inherited by their forefathers before them. The meaning is that there is no harm in you asking someone other than your mothers to breastfeed your children if you give the mothers their wages based on what they breastfed you until the time you want to breastfeed. This was stated by Sufyan al-Thawri and Mujahid. Qatada and al-Zuhri said: The meaning of the verse is: If you give what you have given of the intention of breastfeeding, i.e. each of the parents gives and is satisfied, and that was by agreement between them and the intention of good and the intention of what is known from the matter. Based on this, his statement: you have given is general for men and women, with emphasis, and according to the first statement, the address is only to men. It was said that the meaning is: If you give the wages of the one you want to breastfeed, then the meaning is if you give what you want to give: i.e. give it to the wet nurses according to what is known to people as the wages of the wet nurses without delaying them or reducing some of what is due to them from that, because not providing their wages will lead them to be lenient with the matter of the boy and neglect it. And Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Mothers shall suckle their children he said: divorced women two years he said: two years No mother shall be harmed by her child he said: she shall not refuse to suckle him to harm him so as to make it difficult for his father nor a father by his child he said: the father shall not be harmed by his child so as to prevent his mother from breastfeeding him so as to grieve her and upon the heir he said: he means the guardian whoever is like that he said: maintenance according to what is acceptable and his sponsorship and breastfeeding if the child does not have money, and that his mother shall not be harmed but if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation he said: not wronging themselves or their child, there is no blame upon them and if you wish to have your children nursed he said: fearing the child will be lost there is no blame upon you if you hand over what you have given in an acceptable manner he said: accounting for what the child was breastfed with. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair in his interpretation of this verse that he said: What is meant by His statement: And mothers shall nurse their children is in the case of a man who divorces his wife and has a child from her. He said in His statement: If you have given what you have given he said: What you give the wet nurse in addition to her wages. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam in his statement: And mothers shall nurse their children he said: It is the woman who is divorced or whose husband dies. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the woman who gives birth after six months that she should nurse for two full years, and if she gives birth after seven months she should nurse for twenty-three months, then he recited: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak in his statement: And upon the father of the child is their provision and clothing on equitable terms he said: According to what is easy. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam regarding his statement: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, nor shall a father by his child, she does not have the right to throw her child upon him and he does not find anyone to breastfeed him, and he does not have the right to harm her by taking her child away from her when she loves to breastfeed him. And upon the heir, he said: He is the guardian of the deceased. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’, Ibrahim and Ash-Sha’bi regarding his statement: And upon the heir, he said: He is the heir of the boy who spends on him. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd Bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah something similar, and he added: If the child has no money, he has the same as what his father has from the wage of breastfeeding. Abd Bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd Bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin something similar as well. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qubaysah Bin Dhu’ayb regarding his statement: And upon the heir likewise, he said: He is the boy. Wakee’ narrated on the authority of Abdullah Bin Mughaffal something similar. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the heir is responsible for the same, he said: He should not be harmed. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid. He said: Consultation before two years: she does not have the right to wean him unless he agrees, and he does not have the right to wean him unless she agrees. They narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding the statement of God the Almighty: And if you wish to have your children nursed, he said: his mother or someone else. There is no blame upon you if you hand over, he said: if you hand over her wages, what you have given, what you have given.
2:234: When God, the Almighty, mentioned the waiting period for divorce and connected it with mentioning breastfeeding, He then mentioned the waiting period for death, lest it be thought that the waiting period for death is like the waiting period for divorce. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse, And the men among you who die and leave wives behind means, and they have wives, so the wives wait. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: Its meaning is, And those among you who die and leave wives behind them wait after them, and it is like saying, Samn Manwan is a dirham, meaning from it. Al-Mahdawi narrated from Sibawayh that the meaning is: And among what is recited to you are those who die, and it was said that the meaning is: And the wives of those among you who die wait, mentioned by the author of Al-Kashshaf, and in it is that his statement: 234- and leave wives behind does not fit that estimation, because the apparent meaning of the repeated indefinite noun is different. Some grammarians from Kufa said: The report about those who are left out, and the intention is to inform about their wives that they wait. The wisdom behind making the waiting period for death this long is that the male fetus usually moves for three months, and the female for four months, so God the Almighty added ten to that, because the fetus may become weak in movement and its movement is delayed a little but not delayed beyond this period. The apparent meaning of this verse is general, and that every woman whose husband dies has this waiting period, but this generality has been made specific by God the Almighty’s saying: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth (al-Baqarah 2:17). This is the view of the majority. It was narrated from some of the Companions and a group of scholars that the pregnant woman observes the waiting period until the last of the two periods, combining the general and the specific and applying them, and the truth is what the majority said. Combining the general and the specific in this manner does not suit the laws of language or the rules of Sharia, and there is no meaning to excluding the specific from among the individuals of the general except to clarify that its ruling is different from the ruling of the general and contradicts it. It was authentically reported from the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he gave permission to Sabi’ah al-Aslamiyyah to marry after giving birth and the second waiting period and being patient about marriage. The apparent meaning of the verse is that there is no difference between the young and the old, the free and the slave woman, the menstruating woman and the woman who has reached menopause, and that their waiting period for death is all four months and ten days. It was said that the waiting period for a slave woman is half that of a free woman, which is two months and five days. Ibn al-Arabi said: By consensus, except for what is narrated from al-Asamm, who equated the free woman with the slave woman. Al-Baji said: We do not know of any disagreement on this except what is narrated from Ibn Sirin, who said that her waiting period is the same as that of a free woman, but this is not proven from him. The reason for what al-Asamm and Ibn Sirin went with is the generality in this verse, and the reason for what those who went with them went with is comparing the waiting period for death to the prescribed punishment, as it is justified for the slave woman by the Almighty’s saying: Then upon them is half that upon the free women of the punishment. The hadith The divorce of a slave woman is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstrual periods has been presented, and it is suitable to be used as evidence, but it is not what is meant by it. Except that he made her divorce half of the divorce of a free woman, and her waiting period half of her waiting period. However, since it could not be said: her divorce is one and a half divorces and her waiting period is one and a half menstrual periods, because that is not reasonable, her waiting period and her divorce were that amount mentioned in the hadith to make up for the brokenness. However, here there is a matter that prevents this analogy that the majority worked with, which is that the wisdom in making the waiting period for death four months and ten days is what we have presented about knowing that she is free of pregnancy, and it is not known except for that period, and there is no difference between a free woman and a slave woman in such a case, unlike her waiting period in a case other than death is two menstrual periods, because that is how the emptiness of the womb is known, and the lack of difference is supported by what will come in the waiting period of the mother of the child. The scholars differed regarding the waiting period of the mother of the child for the death of her master. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Al-Zuhri, Umar bin Abdul Aziz, Al-Awza’i, Ishaq, Ibn Rahawayh, and Ahmad bin Hanbal in one narration from him said: She observes an iddah of four months and ten days, based on the hadith of Amr bin Al-Aas who said: Do not confuse us with the Sunnah of our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: The iddah of a mother of a child if her master dies is four months and ten days. It was narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, and Al-Hakim, who authenticated it. Ahmad and Abu Ubaid deemed it weak. Al-Daraqutni said: The correct view is that it is attributed to someone who has not yet been married. Tawus and Qatadah said: Her iddah is two months and five nights. Abu Hanifah and his companions, Al-Thawri, and Al-Hasan bin Salih said: She observes an iddah of three menstrual periods, and this is the opinion of Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Ata’, and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad said in the well-known narration from him: Her iddah is one menstrual period, while a non-menstruating woman is one month. This is what Ibn Umar, Al-Sha’bi, Makhul, Al-Layth, Abu Ubaid, Abu Thawr, and the majority of scholars say. His saying: And when they have reached their term what is meant by reaching puberty here is the expiration of the waiting period there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves of adorning themselves and exposing themselves to proposition in an acceptable manner that does not contradict the Shari’ah or a desirable custom. This has been used as evidence for the obligation of mourning for a woman in the waiting period of a divorce in the absence of death. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others from more than one source that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not permissible for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days except for a husband, four months and ten days. Likewise, it has been proven from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the two Sahihs and others that he forbade the woman in the waiting period of a divorce due to her death from wearing kohl. Mourning is to refrain from wearing perfume, not fine clothes, jewelry, and other things. There is no disagreement about the obligation of this in the waiting period of a divorce due to death, and there is no disagreement about its non-obligation in the waiting period of a divorce due to a revocable divorce. They differed regarding the waiting period of a divorce due to two opinions, and the place for that is in the books of branches. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And those of you who die, he said: If a man died and left his wife, she would observe a year of waiting in his house, and he would spend on her from his money. Then God revealed: And those of you who die, the verse. This is the waiting period of the woman whose husband dies, unless she is pregnant, in which case her waiting period is until she gives birth. He said regarding her inheritance: And for them is a fourth of what you leave, so he explained the woman’s inheritance, leaving a will, and spending. But when they have fulfilled their term, there is no blame upon you, meaning: If a woman is divorced or her husband dies, then when her waiting period has ended, there is no blame upon her if she adorns herself, dresses up, and exposes herself to marriage, for that is what is well-known. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, who said: These ten days were added to the four months, because the soul is breathed into the body during the ten days. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: And when they have fulfilled their term, he said: When her waiting period has ended. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab regarding his statement: There is no blame upon you meaning her guardians. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he disliked for a woman whose husband had died to wear perfume and adorn herself. Malik, Abd al-Razzaq and the people of Sunan narrated, and at-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim authenticated it, on the authority of al-Fari’ah bint Malik ibn Sinan, the sister of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, that she came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) asking to return to her family in Banu Khudra, and that her husband had gone out in search of her slaves whom they had left, and when the time came to return he caught up with them and they killed him. She said: So I asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) to return to my family, for my husband did not leave me in a house that he owned or provide for me. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Yes. So I went back until she was in the room or in the mosque, and he called me or commanded that I be called, and he said: What did you say? She said: So I repeated to him the story that I had mentioned to him about my husband, and he said: Stay in your house until the appointed time has come. She said: So I observed my waiting period for four months and ten days. She said: Then when Uthman ibn Affan was in power, he sent for me and asked me about that, so I told him, and he followed it and ruled accordingly.
2:235: Al-Janah: The sin, meaning there is no sin upon you, and the allusion is the opposite of the statement, and it is from the display of something: meaning its side as if he is hovering around the thing and not showing it, and it was said that it is from your saying: I offered the man: meaning I gave him a gift. And from this that a group of Muslims offered the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr white clothes: meaning they gave them gifts, so the allusion with speech conveys to its companion a word whose meaning is understood. And he said in Al-Kashshaf: The difference between the allusion and the allusion is that the allusion is to mention something in a word other than its intended word. And the allusion is to mention something that indicates something that he did not mention, as the needy person says to the one he needs: I came to you to greet you, and to look at your noble face, and for this reason they said: It is enough for you to surrender to me as a claim It is as if the speech is inclined to an offer that indicates the purpose, and it is called allusion because what he wants is hinted at from it. The end. The sermon with the kasra: what the seeker does of request, and gentleness in speech and action, it is said: he proposed to her, he proposes to her, a sermon and a sermon. As for the sermon with the damma of the kha, it is the speech that a man makes as a suitor. And his saying: 235- Aknantum means you concealed and concealed from marriage after the expiration of the waiting period. Al-Iknan: covering and concealing: it is said: I concealed him and I concealed him with the same meaning. And from it is hidden eggs, and hidden pearls. And from it also is the house, its owner, I concealed it: meaning he covered it. And his saying: God knew that you would mention them meaning God knew that you would not be patient about speaking to them about your desire for them, so He permitted you to allude without being explicit. And he said in Al-Kashshaf: There is a part of rebuke in it like his saying: God knew that you were betraying yourselves. His saying: But do not make a secret appointment with them means: in secret. The letter was omitted because the verb does not take two objects. The scholars differed about the meaning of secret. It was said: it means marriage: that is, the man should not say to this woman in her waiting period: marry me, but rather he should insinuate. The majority of scholars have said that this is the meaning of the verse. It was said that secret: adultery, that is, there should not be any of you making a promise to commit adultery during the waiting period and then marrying after it. This was said by Jabir ibn Zayd, Abu Majlaz, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and al-Nakha’i. It was chosen by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. From this is the saying of al-Hutay’ah: Their neighbor's secret is forbidden to them, and their neighbor eats the tip of the bowl. It was said that the secret is intercourse, meaning do not describe yourselves to them by having frequent intercourse to encourage them to marry. This is what Al-Shafi’i went with in the meaning of the verse, and from it is the saying of Imru’ Al-Qais: Didn't you claim today that I have grown old and that people like me do not like to keep secrets? And similar to it is the saying of Al-A’sha: You will not seek its secret for wealth, nor will you surrender it to its asceticism. He meant: You seek to marry her because of her great wealth, and you will not hand her over because of her little wealth. The correction is in his saying: but from an implied omitted word indicated by you will mention them meaning mention them but do not make secret appointments with them. Ibn Atiyyah said: The nation has unanimously agreed that speaking to a woman in her waiting period with anything that is obscene, such as mentioning intercourse or inciting it, is not permissible. He also said: The nation has unanimously agreed on the undesirability of making an appointment during the waiting period for a woman in relation to herself, for a father in relation to his virgin daughter, and for a master in relation to his female slave. His saying: unless you say a proper word It was said: It is an interrupted exception meaning but, and the proper word is what is permissible of insinuation. The author of Al-Kashshaf prevented it from being disconnected and said: It is an exception to his statement: Do not make an appointment with them meaning do not make an appointment with them at all except a known appointment that is not unknown, so he made it on this basis an empty exception, and the reason for preventing it from being disconnected is that it leads to making the insinuation a promise, and it is not so, because insinuation is the way of the promise, not that it is the promise in itself. His statement: And do not resolve to tie the knot of marriage We have already discussed the meaning of determination. It is said: he resolved something, and he resolved upon it, and the meaning here is: do not resolve to tie the knot of marriage, then upon was deleted. Sibawayh said: The deletion in this verse cannot be compared to it. Al-Nahhas said: It is possible that the meaning is do not tie the knot of marriage, because the meaning of resolve and make an agreement is one, and it was said: the resolve to do precedes it, so there is an exaggeration in this prohibition, because if something that precedes something is prohibited, then the prohibition of that thing is more appropriate. His saying: Until the prescribed period has come to an end means until the waiting period has expired. The book here is the limit and amount of time that has been set. He called it a book because it is limited and imposed, like the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times. This ruling, I mean the prohibition of the marriage contract during the waiting period, is agreed upon. Abdul Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdul bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And there is no blame upon you for that which you insinuate of marriage proposal to women, that he said: Insinuation is to say: I want to get married, and I love women for their affairs and their affairs, and women are my nature, and I wish that God would make a righteous wife easy for me. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he says to her: If you see fit, do not get ahead of me with yourself, and I wish that God had prepared a way between me and you, and similar statements. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he says: I am interested in you, and I wish that I married you. Abdul bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, or you concealed it, that he said: you kept it secret. Abdul Razzaq narrated something similar on the authority of Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdul bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, God knows that you will mention them, that he said: with sin. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: He mentioned her to himself. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {But do not make a secret promise to them}, he said: He says to her: I am in love, and promise me that you will not marry me except me and something similar to this, {Unless you say a respectable word}, which is his statement: If you see that you will not precede me with yourself. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the secret that it is adultery, a man would enter for the sake of adultery and he would offer marriage. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: {Unless you say a respectable word}, he said: He says: You are beautiful, and you are good to me, and women are in my need. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: {And do not resolve on the marriage contract}, he said: Do not marry {Until the prescribed term has been fulfilled}, he said: Until the waiting period has expired.
2:236: What is meant by the wing here is the responsibility for the dowry and the like, so raising it is raising for that reason: that is, you are not responsible for the dowry and the like if you divorce the women in the mentioned manner, and what is in his saying: 236- as long as you have not touched them is a circumstantial source with the estimation of the added: that is, the period of time for you not to touch them. Abu al-Baqa' reported that it is conditional from the perspective of the condition's objection to the condition so that the second is a restriction on the first as in your saying: If you come to me if you do good to me, I will honor you: that is, if you come to me doing good to me, and the meaning is: if you divorce them without touching them. It was said that it is a relative pronoun: that is, if you divorce the women whom you have not touched, and thus they differed in his saying: or impose, so it was said: or in the meaning of except: that is, unless you impose, and it was said in the meaning of until: that is, until you impose, and it was said in the meaning of and: that is, and impose. I do not see any justification for this prolongation, and the meaning of the verse is clearer than to be confused, for God the Almighty has lifted the blame from the divorced as long as one of the two matters has not occurred: i.e. the period of time during which that one of them is not present, and the ambiguous one is not present except by the absence of both matters together, so if there is contact, then the specified amount or the dower of an equal value is due, and if the prescribed amount is present, then half of it is due without contact, and each one of them is a blame: i.e. the specified amount or half of it or the dower of an equal value. And know that there are four divorced women: a divorced woman who has been consummated with and whose dower is due, and she is the one mentioned before this verse, and in it the husbands are forbidden from taking anything from what they have given them, and that their waiting period is three menstrual periods. A divorced woman for whom neither a prescribed amount nor consummated with, and she is the one mentioned here, so she is not entitled to a dower, but rather a pleasure, and it is explained in Surat Al-Ahzab that if a woman who has not been consummated with is divorced, then there is no waiting period for her. A divorced woman for whom a dower has been imposed but who has not been consummated, and she is the one mentioned in the words of God the Almighty here: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dower, and a divorced woman for whom a dower has been imposed but who is not a dower, and she is the one mentioned in the words of God the Almighty: Then give them their dowers for whatever you have enjoyed of them, and what is meant by His words: as long as you have not touched them is as long as you have not had intercourse with them. Ibn Mas’ud read before you have intercourse with them. It was narrated from him by Ibn Jarir, and Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn ‘Amir, and ‘Asim read it as as long as you have not touched them. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it as touching them from the verb mufa’ala. What is meant by the dower here is naming the dower. His saying: And provide for them means give them something that will be a provision for them. The apparent meaning of the command is that it is obligatory, and this is what Ali, Ibn Umar, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Saeed Ibn Jubayr, Abu Qilabah, Al-Zuhri, Qatadah, and Al-Dahhak said. Among the evidence for the obligation is the saying of God the Almighty: “O you who believe! When you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period to count for them. So provide for them and release them with gracious release.” Malik, Abu Ubaid, Judge Shuraih, and others said: The provision for the divorced woman mentioned is recommended, not obligatory, because God the Almighty says: A duty upon the doers of good. If it were obligatory, He would have made it general for all of creation. The answer to this is that this does not contradict the obligation, but rather it is an emphasis on it, as in His saying in the other verse: A duty upon the righteous. That is, fulfilling that and carrying it out is the concern of the righteous, and every Muslim must fear God the Almighty. There has also been a dispute as to whether provision is permissible for someone other than this divorced woman before touching and imposing the obligation, or is it only permissible for her? It was said: It is permissible for every divorced woman, and this is what Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, Ata, Jabir bin Zaid, Saeed bin Jubair, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Al-Shafi’i in one of his two opinions, Ahmad and Ishaq went to, but they differed as to whether it is obligatory for a woman who is not divorced before consummation and the obligation or only recommended, and they provided evidence for it with the words of God Almighty: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous and the words of God Almighty: “O Prophet, tell your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release” and the first verse is general for every divorced woman, and the second is for the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who had been obligated to and had been consummated with. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It is obligatory for the divorced woman if she was divorced before consummation, even if it was obligatory for her, because God the Almighty said: O you who believe! When you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period to count for them, so give them a provision. He said: This verse in Al-Ahzab abrogated the one in Al-Baqarah. A group of scholars said that the provision is specific to the divorced woman before consummation and naming, because the one who has been consummated with is entitled to all of the specified amount or a dowry similar to that of her peers, and the one who has not been consummated with and for whom her husband has specified a dowry (i.e. he specified a dowry for her and divorced her before consummation) is entitled to half of the specified amount. Among those who said this are Ibn Umar and Mujahid. There is consensus that the divorced woman before consummation and the obligation is only entitled to the provision if she is free. If she is a slave, the majority of scholars are of the opinion that she is entitled to enjoyment. Al-Awza’i and Al-Thawri said: She is not entitled to enjoyment because she belongs to her master, and he is not entitled to money in return for the harm caused to his slave, because God, the Almighty, only prescribed enjoyment for the divorced woman before consummation and the obligation, because she is harmed by the divorce before that. They differed about the permissible enjoyment, is it determined by a certain amount or not? Malik and Al-Shafi’i said in the new hadith: There is no known limit for it, but rather what is called enjoyment. Abu Hanifa said: If the spouses dispute over the amount of enjoyment, she is entitled to half the dowry of her peers, and it is not less than five dirhams, because the minimum dowry is ten dirhams. The predecessors have opinions on this, which will be mentioned, God willing. His saying: The wealthy person is entitled to his due and the poor person is entitled to his due indicates that the consideration in this is the husband’s condition, so enjoyment from the wealthy person is higher than enjoyment from the poor person. The majority of scholars read it as the wealthy person with a silent waw and a kasra on the seen, which is the one whose condition is better. Abu Haywah read it with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the seen and a fatha on it. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr read qadr with a sukoon on the dal in both. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Asim read it with a fatha on the dal in both of them. Al-Akhfash and others said: They are two eloquent languages, and this is how it is read in the verse of God the Almighty: And the valleys flowed according to their capacity. And His statement: And they did not estimate God according to His true capacity. The poor is the one who is poor, and enjoyment is a temporary source for His statement: And give them provision. What is known is what is known in the Shari'ah and the custom that agrees with it. And His statement: Truly is a description of His statement: Provision, meaning a source for an omitted verb: meaning that is true, it is said: I made the judgment upon him and I made it obligatory.
2:237: His statement: 237- And if you divorce them before you have touched them the verse, there is evidence that the enjoyment is not obligatory for this divorced woman because it occurs in exchange for the divorced woman before consummation and the obligation who is entitled to the enjoyment. And his statement: Then half of what you have imposed means: What is obligatory upon you is half of what you have specified for them of the dowry, and this is agreed upon. The majority read then half in the nominative case. Those other than the majority read it in the accusative case: meaning, then pay half of what you have imposed. It was also read with the damma and kasra of the noon, and these are two languages. It was also agreed that the woman whose husband did not consummate the marriage with her and died and he had imposed a dowry for her, she is entitled to it in full upon death, and she is entitled to inheritance and she must observe the waiting period. They differed about whether seclusion takes the place of consummation and the woman is entitled to the full dowry as she is entitled to it upon consummation or not? Malik, al-Shafi'i in the old days, the Kufians, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs and the majority of scholars went with the first, and according to them the waiting period is also obligatory. Al-Shafi’i said in Al-Jadid: Only half of the dowry is due, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse, based on what was mentioned earlier, that touching is sexual intercourse, and the waiting period is not due in this case. A group of the Salaf agreed with his statement: Unless they forgive, meaning the divorced women, and its meaning is: they leave and pardon, and its weight is yaf’alun, and it is an exception emptied from the most general of the general, and it was said that it is disconnected, and its meaning is: they leave the half that is due to them from their husbands. The nun was not dropped with in, because the feminine plural in the present tense is in one state in the nominative, accusative, and jussive because the nun is a pronoun and not a sign of inflection as in the masculine in your saying: men forgive, and this is the opinion of the majority of commentators. It was narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi that he said: Unless they forgive, meaning men, and it is weak in wording. The meaning of his statement: or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives is conjoined to the place of his statement: unless they forgive because the first is constructed and the latter is parsed. It was said: it is the husband, and this is what Jubayr ibn Mut'im, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Shuraih, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Ikrimah, Nafi', Ibn Sirin, al-Dahhak, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Jabir ibn Zayd, Abu Majlaz, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah, Makhul, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said. This is the new statement of al-Shafi'i, and this is what Abu Hanifah and his companions, al-Thawri, Ibn Shubramah, and al-Awza'i said, and Ibn Jarir preferred it. This statement has strength and weakness. As for its strength, it is because the one in whose hand is the marriage contract is in reality the husband, because he is the one to whom it can be referred by divorce. As for its weakness, it is because his forgiveness is not reasonable. What they said, that what is meant by his forgiveness is that he gives her the full dowry, is not clear, because forgiveness is not applied to an increase. It was said that what is meant by his saying: or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives is the guardian. This is what An-Nakha’i, Alqamah, Al-Hasan, Tawus, Ata’, Abu Al-Zinad, Zayd ibn Aslam, Rabi’ah, Az-Zuhri, Al-Aswad ibn Yazid, Ash-Sha’bi, Qatadah, Malik, and Ash-Shafi’i said in his old statement. There is strength and weakness in it. As for its strength, it is because the meaning of forgiveness in it is reasonable. As for its weakness, it is because the marriage contract is in the hand of the husband, not his. What makes this statement even weaker is that the guardian does not have the right to forgive the husband for something he does not own. Al-Qurtubi narrated the consensus that the guardian does not own anything of her money, and the dowry is her money. So what is more correct is what the first scholars said for two reasons: The first is that the husband is the one who truly has the marriage contract in his hand. The second is that his pardon of completing the dowry is issued by the owner with absolute discretion, unlike the guardian, and calling the increase a pardon even if it is contrary to what appears, but since it is most common that they pay the full dowry at the time of the contract, the pardon is reasonable, because he left it to her and did not take back half of it, and there is no need in this to say that it is a case of similarity as in Al-Kashshaf, because it is a real pardon: i.e. leaving what is worthy of being claimed, unless it is said that it is a case of similarity, or it is permissible to pay the dowry before the husband pays it. His statement: And to pardon is closer to righteousness It was said: It is addressed to men and women, by predominance, and the majority read it with the upper taa, and Abu Nahik and Al-Sha’bi read it with the lower yaa, so the address is to men. And in this is evidence of what we preferred, that the one who has the marriage contract in his hand is the husband, because the pardon of the guardian of something that he does not own is not closer to righteousness, but closer to injustice and oppression. His saying: And do not forget graciousness between you The majority read it with a damma on the waw, and Yahya bin Ya'mar read it with a kasra, and Ali, Mujahid, Abu Haywah, and Ibn Abi Ubla read and do not forget. The meaning is that the spouses do not forget the generosity of each other, and among that is that the woman is generous in forgiving half and the man is generous in completing the dowry. It is guidance for the men and women among the spouses to stop being scrupulous about each other, and to forgive what one of them takes from the other for the sake of the connection that has been a share of some of them going to each other, and it is a connection that no other connection resembles, so from taking care of its right and knowing it properly is keenness on their part to forgive. His saying: Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do contains encouragement of the doer of good and intimidation of others that is not hidden. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Unless you have touched them or appointed for them a dowry, he said: Touching means marriage, and dowry means the bride price. Provide for them a benefit, he said: It is for a man who marries a woman without specifying a dowry for her, then divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, so God commanded him to provide for her according to his ease and difficulty. If he is wealthy, he provides for her with a servant, and if he is poor, he provides for her with three garments or something like that. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The maximum of the pleasure of divorce is a servant, and less than that is paper, and less than that is clothing. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd Bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the minimum of the pleasure is thirty dirhams. Al-Qurtubi narrated in his Tafsir on the authority of Al-Hasan Bin Ali that he provided for twenty thousand and honey chips. Shuraih narrated that he provided for five hundred dirhams. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Bin Ali that he provided for ten thousand. Abdul Razzaq narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin that he used to enjoy the service of a servant and maintenance or clothing. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: before you touch them he said: touching means intercourse, so she is entitled to half of her dowry, and she is not entitled to more than that unless they forgive it. This is the woman who has been married or the virgin who is married by someone other than her father, so God made forgiveness for them if they wish they forgive by leaving them, and if they wish they take half of the dowry or he in whose hand is the marriage tie forgives and he is the father of the virgin slave girl, he made forgiveness up to him and she has no say in it if she divorces what she is in his custody. Al-Shafi’i, Saeed bin Mansour and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said about a man who marries a woman and is alone with her and does not touch her then divorces her: she is not entitled to more than half of the dowry, because God says: and if you divorce them [al-Bayhaqi 3:10]. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: She is entitled to half of the dowry even if he sits between her legs. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the husband. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Daraqutni, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ali something similar to his statement. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority that he said: He is her father, her brother, and the one she cannot marry except with his permission. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And do not forget graciousness between you, he said: In this or something else. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi who authenticated it reported that some people came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: A man from among us married a woman and did not set a dowry for her and did not take her back until he died. He said: I think that I should set a dowry for her like the dowries of her other wives, neither too much nor too much. She is entitled to inheritance and her waiting period is four months and ten days. Some people from Ashja', including Mughaffal ibn Sinan, heard about that and said: We bear witness that you have ruled as the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ruled regarding a woman from among us called Baru' bint Washiq. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Bayhaqi reported on the authority of Ali that he said about a woman whose husband died and he did not set a dowry for her: She is entitled to inheritance and her waiting period is not due. He said: The statement of a Bedouin from Ashja' is not acceptable according to the Book of God. Ash-Shafi'i and al-Bayhaqi reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said about a woman whose husband died and he set a dowry for her: She is entitled to the dowry and the inheritance. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab that he ruled concerning a woman whom a man marries: If she lowers the curtain, the dowry becomes due. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umar and Ali that: If he lowers a curtain and closes a door, she is entitled to the full dowry and must observe the waiting period. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa that: The Rightly-Guided Caliphs ruled that if someone closes a door or lowers a curtain, the dowry and the waiting period become due. Malik and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Thawban that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever uncovers a woman and looks at her private parts, the dowry becomes due.
2:238: Maintaining something: persistence and persistence in it, and the middle: the feminine of the middle, and the middle of something and its middle: its best. And from it is the saying of God Almighty: And thus We have made you a middle nation, and from it is the saying of some Arabs: praising the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O the most average of people, the most ostentatious in their boasting, and the most generous of people in terms of a pious mother and father And in the middle of so-and-so among the people, he is in the middle of them: that is, he is in their middle. And the middle prayer was mentioned separately after it was included in the general prayers in order to honor it. Abu Ja`far 238- read and the middle prayer in the accusative case for enticement, and so did Al-Halwani, and Qaloon read on the authority of Nafi` the middle with a sad because of the proximity of the ta and they are two languages: like sirat and sirat. The people of knowledge differed in specifying it into eighteen opinions that I mentioned in my explanation of Al-Muntaqa, and I mentioned what each group adhered to, and the most correct and sound opinion is what the majority went for, that it is the afternoon prayer, because it was proven by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, the people of Sunan and others from the hadith of Ali who said: “We used to consider it the dawn until I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say on the day of the confederates: They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May God fill their graves and their bellies with fire.” Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and others narrated a hadith from Ibn Mas`ud with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) similar to it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Tabarani also narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from the hadith of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Al-Bazzar narrated it with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Al-Bazzar also narrated it with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Hudhayfah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. There are hadiths traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that specify that it is the afternoon prayer without mentioning the Day of the Confederates: some of them on the authority of Ibn Umar, according to Ibn Mandah, and some on the authority of Samurah, according to Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, and al-Tabarani, and some on his authority, according to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, and al-Tirmidhi, and it was authenticated by Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi, and on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, according to Ibn Jarir, al-Bayhaqi, and al-Tahawi. It was also narrated on his authority by Ibn Saeed, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, and al-Tabarani, and on the authority of Ibn Abbas, according to al-Bazzar, with sound chains of transmission, and on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, according to Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani. These hadiths traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, clearly state that it is the afternoon prayer. Many reports have been narrated on the authority of the Companions that specify that it is the afternoon prayer, and there is evidence that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has that which does not require anything else. As for what was narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas that they said: It is the dawn prayer, as Malik narrated it in Al-Muwatta’ on their authority, and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and likewise Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated it on his authority, and likewise Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Umar, and likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Jabir, and likewise Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Abu Umamah, and all of that is from their statements and there is nothing in it that is traced back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and such an argument cannot be established. Especially if it contradicts what has been proven from him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a way that can be claimed to be mutawatir. If the evidence is not established by the sayings of the Companions, it is not established by the sayings of those who came after them from the Followers and those who followed them a fortiori. Thus, the evidence is not established by what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The middle prayer is the Maghrib prayer. Thus, there is no consideration for what was reported from a group of the Companions that it is the Dhuhr prayer or any other prayer. However, what is needed to look closely and think is what was reported to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that indicates that it is the Dhuhr prayer, as Ibn Jarir narrated from Zayd ibn Thabit with a chain of transmission to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The middle prayer is the Dhuhr prayer. It is not correct to say that it is the Dhuhr prayer, but what was narrated from Zayd ibn Thabit is from his saying. And evidence for that is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pray at noon, and it was the heaviest prayer for his Companions. Where does this evidence fit in those authentic hadiths that are proven from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and thus consideration is given to what was reported from Ibn Umar that he said: It is the Dhuhr prayer. Likewise, what was narrated on the authority of Aisha, Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, and others, there is no proof in the statement of anyone from the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for what was narrated by Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, and others, that Hafsa said to Abu Rafi, her servant, when she ordered him to write a copy of the Qur’an for her: If you come to this verse, Guard strictly the prayers, especially the middle prayer, then come so that I may dictate it to you. When he reached that, she ordered him to write, Guard strictly the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer. Malik, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it from her in his Sunan, and they added: And she said, “I bear witness that I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Malik, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, and others narrated from Abu Yunus, the freed slave of Aisha, that she ordered him to write a copy of the Qur’an for her and said, “When you reach this verse, notify me: ‘Guard strictly the prayers, especially the middle prayer.’” He said, “When I reached it, I notified her and she dictated to me, ‘Guard strictly the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer.’ Aisha said, “I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Wakee’, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Umm Salamah that she ordered someone to write a copy of the Qur’an for her, and she said to him as Hafsa and Aisha had said. The most that is in these narrations from the three Mothers of the Believers, may God be pleased with them, is that they narrate this wording in this manner from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there is nothing in it that indicates that the middle prayer is specified as the noon prayer or something else. Rather, the most that is indicated by the conjunction of the afternoon prayer with the middle prayer is that it is something else. Because the conjoined is not the conjoined to, and this evidence does not contradict what was proven from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a proof that does not negate that it is the afternoon prayer, as we have previously explained. The result is that this reading that was transmitted by the three mothers of the believers by confirming his saying: and the afternoon prayer, is contradicted by what Ibn Jarir narrated, “On the authority of Urwah, who said: In the Mushaf of Aisha, it was: “Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the afternoon prayer.” And Wakee narrated on the authority of Hamida, who said: I read in the Mushaf of Aisha, Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the afternoon prayer. And Ibn Abi Dawud narrated on the authority of Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb something similar. And Saeed ibn Mansur and Abu Ubaid narrated on the authority of Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam that Aisha ordered a Mushaf of hers to be written and she said: When you reach Guard the prayers, do not write it until you inform me. So when they informed her that they had reached it, she said: Write it as the middle prayer, which is the afternoon prayer. Ibn Jarir, Al-Tahawi and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Amr bin Rafi’ who said: It was written in Hafsah’s copy of the Qur’an: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the ‘Asr prayer. Abu Ubaid narrated in his Fadhail and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b that he used to recite it: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the ‘Asr prayer. Abu Ubaid, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari in his History, Ibn Jarir and Al-Tahawi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He used to recite it: Guard the prayers and the middle prayer is the ‘Asr prayer. Al-Muhammadi narrated on the authority of Al-Sa’in Ibn Yazid that he recited it in this way. These narrations contradict those narrations in consideration of the recitation and transmission of the recitation, and what is authentically reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the specification remains free from any taint of opposition. However, there is evidence that the recitation transmitted by Hafsah, ‘A’ishah, and Umm Salamah was abrogated. ‘Abd Ibn Humayd, Muslim, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ Ibn ‘Azib who said: Guard the prayers and the ‘Asr prayer was revealed, and he recited it during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as much as God willed, then God abrogated it and revealed: Guard the prayers and the middle prayer. It was said to him: And what about the ‘Asr prayer? He said: I have told you how it was revealed and how God abrogated it, and God knows best. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority with another chain of transmission similar to it. If this is established for you and you know what we have presented, it will become clear to you that nothing has been reported that contradicts the fact that the middle prayer is the afternoon prayer. As for the arguments of the remaining statements, there is nothing in them that should be taken into account because nothing has been proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding that. Some of those who said this relied on something that cannot be relied upon, saying: It is such-and-such a prayer, that it is middle in relation to it, except that before it is such-and-such prayers and after it is such-and-such prayers. This pure opinion and mere guesswork should not be used as the basis for legal rulings, assuming that there is nothing that contradicts it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so how about when there is something that is at the highest levels of soundness, strength, and confirmation from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? Oh, how amazing it is for a people who were not satisfied with their shortcomings in knowledge of the Sunnah and their turning away from the best and most beneficial of knowledge, until they burdened themselves with speaking about the rulings of God and investigating the interpretation of the Book of God without knowledge or guidance, so they came with what makes one laugh at times and cry at other times. His saying: And stand before God, devoutly obedient. It was said that qunut means obedience, meaning stand before God in your prayer, obediently. This was said by Jabir ibn Zayd, Ata’, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, and Ash-Sha’bi. It was also said that it means humility, as was said by Ibn ‘Umar and Mujahid. And from this is the saying of the poet: Obedient to God, calling upon his Lord, and deliberately separating himself from people It was said: It is supplication, and Ibn Abbas said the same. In the hadith: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for a month, supplicating against Ra’l and Dhakwan.” Some people said: Qunut is standing for a long time, and it was said: Its meaning is being silent, as Al-Suddi said, and this is indicated by the hadith of Zaid bin Arqam in the two Sahihs and others, who said: “A man would talk to his companion during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about a need in prayer until this verse was revealed: ‘And stand before God, devoutly obedient,’ so he commanded us to be silent.” It was said: The root of Qunut in the language is to persevere in something, so any meaning that is appropriate for perseverance can be applied to Qunut. The scholars have mentioned that Qunut has thirteen meanings, and we have mentioned that in the explanation of Al-Muntaqa, and what is required here is to interpret Qunut as silence, based on the hadith mentioned.
2:239: His saying: 239- But if you fear, then on foot or riding. Fear is panic, and men is the plural of man or rajil, from their saying: a man's man yarjilan rajilan: if he does not have a mount and walks on his feet, then he is a man and a rajil. The people of Hijaz say: So-and-so walked to the House of God barefoot, on foot. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari and others. When God the Almighty mentioned the command to maintain the prayers, He mentioned the state of fear that they will waste what they can in it and it falls within their ability to maintain the prayer by doing it while on foot and while riding, and He made clear to them that this act of worship is obligatory in all circumstances according to their ability. The scholars have differed regarding the limit of fear that permits this, and the discussion is complete in the books of branches. His saying: Then when you are secure meaning when your fear has gone away, then return to what you were commanded to do, which is to complete the prayer facing the qiblah, performing all of its conditions and pillars. This is His saying: Then remember God as He taught you. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: You have left the abode of travel for the abode of laws that which you did not know. The kaf is an attribute of a deleted source: meaning a remembrance that is like His teaching you, or like His teaching you. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab who said: The companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) differed about the middle prayer like this, and he interlaced his fingers. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he was asked about the middle prayer. He said: It is among them, so maintain them. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit that a man asked him about the middle prayer, so he said: Maintain the prayers and you will catch them. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi bin Khaitham that a questioner asked him about the middle prayer, so he said: Maintain them, for if you do, you will attain it, for it is only one of them. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin who said: Shuraih was asked about the middle prayer, so he said: Maintain them and you will attain it. We have already mentioned what was narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his companions may God be pleased with them regarding its specification. At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: And stand before God, devoutly obedient, like what we mentioned on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Masoud. Saeed bin Mansour and Abd bin Hameed narrated from Muhammad bin Kaab something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar from Ikrimah. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hameed and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse {And stand before God, devoutly obedient} that he said: Praying. Ibn Jarir narrated from him regarding the verse that he said: Every religious person stands in it disobediently, so stand obediently. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar from Ad-Dahhak. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hameed, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid regarding the verse {And stand before God, devoutly obedient} that he said: From qunut is bowing and humility, and lengthening bowing means lengthening standing, lowering the gaze, lowering the wing and fearing God. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Indeed, there is distraction in prayer. And in Sahih Muslim and others that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This prayer is not appropriate for any of the words of people; rather, it is tasbeeh, takbeer and recitation of the Qur’aan. The ahaadeeth differed regarding the technical term qunut. Is it before or after bowing? Is it the same in all prayers or some of them? Is it specific to calamities or not? The most correct opinion is that it is specific to calamities. We have explained this in our explanation of al-Muntaqa, so please refer to it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Most High: But if you fear, then on foot or riding, he said: The rider prays on his mount and the pedestrian prays on his feet. So remember God as He has taught you that which you did not know, meaning as He has taught you that the rider prays on his mount and the pedestrian prays on his feet. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: If there is a duel, then he should wave his head wherever he is facing. This is what is meant by the words: On foot or riding. Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: But if you fear, then on foot or riding. He said: One rak’ah at a time. Wakee’ and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid: And when you are safe, he said: You have left the place of travel for the place of residence.
2:240: This is a return to the rest of the detailed rulings above. The early Muslims and those who followed them from the commentators differed regarding this verse: is it decisive or abrogated? The majority went to that it was abrogated by the four months and ten as mentioned above, and that the will mentioned in it was abrogated by what God imposed for them of inheritance. Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid that this verse is decisive and there is no abrogation in it, and that the waiting period is four months and ten, then God made for them a will from Him to live for seven months and twenty nights, so if the woman wishes she may live in her will, and if she wishes she may leave. Ibn Atiyah and Judge Iyad narrated that there is consensus that the year is abrogated and that her waiting period is four months and ten. Al-Bukhari narrated from Mujahid what Ibn Jarir narrated from him in his Sahih. And his saying: 240- A will Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr and Al-Kisa’i read it in the nominative case on the basis that it is the subject of a deleted predicate that is understood to be advanced: i.e. they have a will. And it was said that the predicate is his saying: for their wives. And it was said that it is the predicate of a deleted predicate: i.e. the will of those who die is a will or the ruling of those who die is a will. And Abu Omar, Hamza and Ibn Amir read it in the accusative case on the basis of an omitted verb: i.e. let them make a will, or God made a will, or God wrote a will upon them. And his saying: Provision is accusative by a will or by an omitted verb: i.e. provide them with provision, or God made that provision for them. And it is permissible for it to be accusative as a state. And provision here is: the year’s expenses. His saying: other than expelling is an attribute of his saying: provision. Al-Akhfash said: It is a source as if he said: No expulsion. It was said that it is a state: meaning, provide for them without expelling them. It was said: It is accusative by removing the preposition: meaning without expelling. The meaning is that it is obligatory for those who die to bequeath before death descends upon them to their husbands that they should enjoy after them for a full year with maintenance and housing from what they left behind and that they should not leave their homes. His saying: But if they go out means by their own choice before the year there is no blame upon you meaning there is no blame upon the guardian, the ruler, and others for what they did with themselves of exposing themselves to speech and adorning themselves for them. His saying: of what is known means: of what is known in the Shari’ah and not reprehensible. In it is evidence that women were given the choice to live for a year and that is not obligatory upon them. It was said: The meaning is there is no blame upon you for cutting off maintenance from them, and this is weak because the object of the blame is mentioned in the verse in His saying: for what they did.
2:241: And his saying: 241- And for the divorced women is a provision. The commentators differed regarding this verse. It was said: It is the pleasure, and that it is obligatory for every divorced woman.
