It was said: This verse is specific to the previously married women who have had sexual intercourse, because before this verse the mention of pleasure for those with whom the husbands have not consummated the marriage was presented. We have already discussed this pleasure and the disagreement over whether it is specific to those who were divorced before consummation and the obligation or general for the divorced women. It was said: This verse includes the obligatory pleasure, which is the pleasure of the divorced woman before consummation and the obligation, and the non-obligatory pleasure, which is the pleasure of all the divorced women, as it is only recommended. It was said: What is meant by pleasure here is maintenance. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr who said: I said to Uthman ibn Affan: And those of you who die and leave wives behind has been abrogated by the other verse, so why did you not write it or did you not leave it? He said: O son of my brother, I will not change anything in its place. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: The woman whose husband dies was entitled to her maintenance and housing in the house for a year, but the verse of inheritance abrogated it and gave them a quarter and an eighth of what the husband left behind. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ata. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas from another chain of transmission. Al-Shafi’i and Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The woman whose husband dies is not entitled to maintenance; it is considered part of the inheritance. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Ikrimah who said: It was abrogated by And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days. Ibn al-Anbari narrated something similar in his Mus-haf on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam. And he also narrated from Qatada something similar. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: There is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner, he said: Lawful and good marriage. And Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Zayd who said: When the statement: Provision in a reasonable manner is a duty upon the doers of good was revealed, a man said: If I did well I would have done so, and if I did not want to do that I would not have done so, so God revealed: And for divorced women is a provision in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the righteous. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab who said: This verse was abrogated by his statement: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation, then half of what you specified. And he also narrated from Atab bin Khasif regarding his statement: And for divorced women is a provision, he said: That was before the obligations. And Malik, Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Shafi’i, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Umar who said: Every divorced woman is entitled to a provision except the one whom she divorced without consummating the marriage with him and he specified for her, half is sufficient as provision. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: For every believing woman who is divorced, whether free or slave, there is a temporary marriage. And he recited: And for divorced women there is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: “When Hafs ibn al-Mughirah divorced his wife Fatimah, she came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to her husband: Provide her with a provision. He said: I do not find anything to provide her with. He said: Provide her with a provision, even if it is half a sa’ of dates.” Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah regarding the verse, he said: For every divorced woman there is a temporary marriage.
2:242: 242- Thus does God make clear to you His signs that you may understand.
2:243: The question here is for confirmation, and the vision mentioned is the vision of the heart, not the vision of the eyes. The meaning according to Sibawayh is: alerting to the matter of those who went out, and this vision does not need two objects, as it was said. The gist of it is that the vision here, which means perception, includes the meaning of alerting, and it is possible that it includes the meaning of ending: i.e. did not your knowledge end with them, or the meaning of arriving: i.e. did not your knowledge reach them, or it is possible that it means visual seeing: i.e. did not you look at those who went out. God Almighty made the story of these people, since it was in a place of prevalence and fame, it leads everyone to acknowledge it as something known to every individual, or seen by every sighted person, because the People of the Book have informed about it, recorded it, and made its matter famous, and the address here is to everyone who is suitable for it. The speech is like a proverb in the place of amazement, claiming its appearance and clarity such that the witness and the absent are equal in their perception of it. 243- And his saying: And they are thousands is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun they went out, and thousands is from the plural of multitude, so it indicates that they are many thousands. And his saying: He feared death is an object for it. And his saying: Then God said to them, ‘Die’ is a command to form an expression of His will being attached to their death all at once, or a representation of His, the Most High, causing them to die the death of a single soul as if they were commanded and they obeyed. His saying: Then He revived them is conjoined with an implied meaning required by the situation: that is, God said to them, ‘Die’ so they died, then He revived them, or with He said since it was an expression of causing death. And his saying: Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind the indefiniteness in His saying, bounty is for glorification: that is, full of great bounty to all people. As for those who went out, it is because He revived them so that they would take heed, and as for those addressed, it is because He guided them to take heed and gain insight through the story of these people.
2:244: His statement: 244- And fight in the way of God is conjoined to an implied meaning, as if it was said: Thank His favor by considering what He has told you and fight. This is if the address in His statement: And fight is referring back to those addressed in His statement: Have you not seen those who went out? as the majority of commentators have said. Based on this, the mention of this story is to encourage the Muslims to jihad. It was said: The address is to those of the Children of Israel who were kept alive, so it is conjoined to His statement: Die. And in the speech there is something omitted, the meaning of which is: And He said to them, fight. Ibn Jarir said: There is no basis for the statement of those who said: The command to fight is for those who were kept alive.
2:245: And His saying: 245- Who is it that will lend to God? When He, the Most High, commanded fighting and jihad, He commanded spending in that, and who is an interrogative nominative in place of the subject, and that is its predicate, and what it is connected to is a description of it or a substitute for it, and lending to God is an example of presenting the righteous deed for which its doer deserves reward, and the origin of the loan is a name for everything for which a reward is sought, it is said: So-and-so lent so-and-so: meaning he gave him what he would repay. The poet said: If you are given a loan, pay it back. Al-Zajjaj said: “A loan in the language means: a good or bad affliction.” Umayya said: Every person will be repaid for his loan, good or bad, and will be indebted for what he has lent. Another said: So he rewarded loans with the like of them, so good with good and evil with evil. Al-Kisa'i said: Al-Qard: What you have advanced of good or bad deeds. The root of the word is cutting, and from it comes the word Al-Siqaraad. The invocation of the loan in the verse is only to make people feel comfortable and bring them closer to what they understand. And God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy: He likened the giving of the believer, whose reward he hopes for in the Hereafter, to a loan, just as he likened giving souls and money in taking Paradise to buying and selling. And His saying: good means: his soul is content with it without favor or harm. And His saying: He will multiply it Asim and others read it with the alif and the accusative of the fa. Nafi', Abu Amr, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with the alif and the nominative of the fa. Ibn Amir and Ya'qub read it with the emphasis and the nominative of the fa. So whoever puts the accusative then it is because it is the answer to the question, and whoever raises it then it is the subject: meaning He will multiply it. There are different opinions regarding the estimation of this doubling. It was said: Only God knows it. And His statement: And God contracts and expands is general in everything, for He is the Constrictor and the Expander, and contraction is stinginess, and expansion is expansion, and in it is a warning that whoever is stingy in expansion is likely to have it replaced with contraction, and for this reason He said: And to Him you will return meaning He will reward you for what you have put forth when you return to Him, and if you spend from what He has provided for you, He will be good to you, and if you are stingy, He will punish you. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes? He said: They were four thousand who went forth fleeing from the plague and said: Let us go to a land where there is no death. When they were in such and such a place, God said to them: Die. So they died. Then a prophet from among the prophets passed by them and called upon his Lord to revive them so that they might worship Him, and He revived them. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: The village from which they went forth was Dawud. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this story in detail on the authority of Abu Malik, in which it says that they were thirty-some thousand. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Abd Al-Aziz: Their homes were Adhraat. He also narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: They were nine thousand. A group of hadith scholars and commentators narrated this story in various ways, but repeating its chains of transmission will not be of any benefit. It has been reported in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he forbade fleeing from the plague and entering the land in which it was, from the hadith of Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa`d, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha`b narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: “When the verse, ‘Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan?’ was revealed, Abu Al-Dahdah Al-Ansari said: ‘O Messenger of God, does God want a loan from us?’ He said: ‘Yes, O Abu Al-Dahdah.’ He said: ‘Show me your hand, O Messenger of God.’ So he gave him his hand and said: ‘I have loaned my garden to my Lord, and He has six hundred palm trees in it.’” This story was narrated by `Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam. Al-Tabarani added on the authority of his father on the authority of `Umar ibn Al-Khattab, Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir on the authority of Ibn `Abbas. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement, ‘many times over.’ He said: ‘No one knows what this doubling means.’ Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi who said: I heard a hadith on the authority of Abu Hurayrah in which he said: God writes for His believing servant a single good deed a thousand thousand good deeds. So I performed Hajj that year and I did not want to perform Hajj except to meet him in this hadith. So I met Abu Hurayrah and said to him, and he said: This is not it. I said: “He did not memorize this hadith that he narrated to you. Rather, I said: ‘God gives the believing servant a single good deed two thousand thousand good deeds.’ Then Abu Hurayrah said: “Do you not find this in the Book of God?” Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? So a lot with God is more than two thousand thousand and two thousand thousand. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God multiplies a good deed two thousand thousand good deeds. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab al-Iman narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: “When the verse ‘The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a seed [of grain] which grows seven ears’ was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O Lord, increase my nation.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over?’ He said: ‘O Lord, increase my nation.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘Only the patient will be paid in full without account.’” Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Sufyan, who said: “When the verse was revealed: ‘Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof,’ he said: ‘O Lord, increase my nation.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘Who is it that would loan God?’ He said: ‘O Lord, increase my nation.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a seed [of grain] which grows seven ears’. He said: ‘O Lord, increase my nation.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘Only the patient will be paid in full.’” There are ahaadeeth on this topic, the best of which will come when interpreting the verse of God, the Most High, ‘The parable of a seed [of grain] which grows seven ears’, so research them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And God withholds and grants, he said: He withholds the charity, and grants grants: he said: He replaces, and to Him you will be returned, he said: From dust and to dust you will return. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, he said: God knows that among those who fight in the cause of God there are those who do not find strength and among those who do not fight in the cause of God there are those who find wealth, so He encouraged these people to lend, saying: Who is it that would lend to God? He said: He grants you abundance while you are too heavy to go out and do not want to, and He withholds from this one while he is content with going out and makes it easy for him, so be strong from what you have and you will have the portion.
2:246: His saying: 246- Have you not seen the assembly? The discussion of it is like the discussion of His saying: Have you not seen those who went out from their homes? We have already presented it, and the assembly are the nobles of the people as if they were filled with honor. Al-Zajjaj said: They were called that because they were filled with what is needed from them, and it is a collective noun like the people and the group. God Almighty mentioned in the incitement to fight another story that happened among the Children of Israel after the previous story, and His saying: After Moses is from the beginning and its factor is understood: meaning two beings after Moses: meaning after his death. And His saying: To a prophet for them it was said: He is Samuel bin Yar bin Alqamah and he is known as Ibn Al-Ajouz, and it is said about him Shimon, and he is from the descendants of Jacob, and it was said: From the descendants of Aaron, and it was said: He is Joshua bin Nun, and this is very weak because Joshua is the young man of Moses, and he did not exist until a long time after that, and it was said that his name was Ishmael. His saying: Send us a king means a prince to whom we may return and act according to his opinion. His saying: We fight with the letter nun and the jussive mood as a response to the command, and this is how the majority read it. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Abi Ubla read it with the letter ya and raised the verb as an attribute of the king. It was read with the letter nun and raised as a state or a renewed statement. His saying: Hall 'asitum with the fatha on the letter sin and with the kasra are two dialects, and Nafi' read with the second, and the rest read with the first. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: The reading with the kasra is weak. Abu Hatim said: The kasra has no basis. End quote. Abu Ali said: The basis for the kasra is the Arabs' saying: He is 'asa with that, like hara and shaja, and fa'l and fa'l have come in the likes of naqam and naqam, so like 'asita and 'asita, and this is what Makki said. Al-Hasan and Talha also read it with the kasra, so there is no reason to weaken that, and it is one of the verbs of approximation: i.e. have you come close to not fighting? The introduction of the interrogative letter to the verb of approximation is to confirm what is expected of it and to indicate that it is happening, and the introduction of the interrogative letter to the verb of approximation is to confirm what is expected of it and to indicate that it is happening, and the separation between ‘asa and its predicate with the condition to indicate the attention paid to it. Al-Zajjaj said: That you do not fight is in the accusative case: i.e. are you likely to fight? Al-Akhfash said: And what is it to us that we should not fight is redundant. Al-Farra’ said: It is based on the meaning: i.e. what prevented us as you say Why do you not pray? It was said that the meaning is: what is it to us that we should not fight? Al-Nahhas said: This is the best of them. His saying And we have brought them out is an explanation and the sentence is a state, and the children were mentioned separately because they were the ones who were taken captive, or because they were in a place above the place of the rest of the relatives. So when it was written i.e. imposed, the Almighty informed that they turned away due to the confusion of their intentions and the weakness of their resolve. There is a difference of opinion regarding the small number of people whom God Almighty excluded, and they are those who were satisfied with the room.
2:247: And His saying: 247- And their prophet said to them is the beginning of detailing what happened between them and their prophet of words and actions. And Talut: is a foreign name, and he was a water carrier, and it was said: a tanner, and it was said: a muleteer, and he was not from the tribe of the prophets, who are Banu Luwā, nor from the tribe of the kings, who are Banu Judah, so "they said: How can he have kingship over us?" That is, how is that, and he was not from the royal house, nor was he one of those who were given ample wealth so that we would follow him for his honor or his wealth, and this sentence, I mean His saying: And we are more deserving is a circumstantial statement, as is the sentence conjoined to it. And His saying: He chose him over you that is, He chose him, and the choice of God is the conclusive proof. Then he explained to them the reason for the selection: that God increased him in knowledge, which is the essence of man and the head of virtues and the greatest aspect of preference, and increased him in body, which shows its effect in wars and the like, so he was strong in his religion and body, and that is what is considered, not the honor of the most appropriate. For the virtues of the soul are given precedence over him. And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills. So the kingdom is His kingdom, and the slaves are His slaves, so what is the matter with you in objecting to something that is not yours and whose command is not up to you? Some of the commentators have said that His statement, And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills is from the words of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: It is from the words of their Prophet, and that is what is apparent. His statement, Vastful means Vast in grace, He gives generously to whomever He wills of His slaves. Knowing of who deserves the kingdom and is fit for it.
2:248: 248- The Ark is a noun derived from the verb to return, because they return to it: meaning the sign of his kingship is the arrival of the Ark that was taken from them: meaning its return to you, which is the chest of the Torah. And the word sakina is a noun derived from sakun, waqar, and al-mininah: meaning in it is the reason for the tranquility of your hearts regarding the matter of Talut that you differed over. Ibn Atiyyah said: The correct view is that the Ark contained excellent things from the remnants and traces of the prophets, so souls were reassured by that, were comforted by it, and were strengthened. There is disagreement about the meaning of sakina in statements, some of which will be explained, and there is also disagreement about the rest. It was said: It is the staff of Moses and the fragments of the tablets, and other things were said. It was said: What is meant by the family of Moses and Aaron are the same: that is, what Aaron and Moses left behind, and the word family is inserted to magnify their status. It was said: What is meant are the prophets from the sons of Jacob because they are from the descendants of Jacob, so all of his relatives and those who descended from him are descendants of them.
2:249: And the meaning of the verb fasl is: he went out with them. I separated the thing and it was separated, meaning I cut it off and it was cut off. Its origin is transitive. It is said: he separated himself, then it was used as an intransitive verb like fasl. It is said that fasl is used as an intransitive and transitive verb. It is said: he separated from the country several chapters, and he separated himself as a chapter. And the trial: the test. And the river: it is said: it is between Jordan and Palestine, and the majority read it as Nahr with the ha open. Hamid, Mujahid and Al-A'raj read it with the ha closed. What is meant by this trial is to test their obedience, so whoever obeys in that water obeys in everything else, and whoever disobeys in this and his soul overcomes him, then he is more likely to disobey in all other hardships. And he gave them permission to drink from the water in order to lift the harm of thirst from those who are patient in the hardship of life and push themselves away from luxury. So what is meant by his saying: 249- So whoever drinks from it means he drank from it and did not limit himself to drinking from the water, and min is an introductory word. The meaning of his saying: He is not from me is that he is not from my companions, from his saying: So-and-so is from so-and-so, as if he is part of him, due to their mixing and long companionship. This is a well-known distinction in the speech of the Arabs, and from it is the saying of the poet: If you try to commit adultery with a lion, then I am not from you and you are not from me And his saying: And whoever does not taste it it is said: I tasted something: meaning I tasted it, and I fed him the water: meaning I made him taste it, and in it is evidence that water is called food, and scooping: taking from something with the hand or with a tool, and scooping is like scooping, and scooping is a single time. It has been read with the opening of the ghain and its closing, so the opening is for the time, and the closing is the name of the thing scooped, and it was said: with the opening is the room with a single hand, and with the closing is the room with the two hands, and it was said: they are two languages with one meaning, and from it the saying of the poet: They do not enter water with a vessel except to scoop from the pools with wine. His saying: Except a few will be explained, and it was read: Except a few and there is no basis for it except what was said that it is from abandoning the wording to the side of the meaning: i.e. he did not give him except a few, and this is arbitrary. His saying: So when he crossed it i.e. Talut crossed the river and those who believed with him and they are the few who obeyed him, but they differed about the strength of certainty, so some of them said: We have no strength and those who think i.e. are certain that they will meet God said the group: the community, and the piece of them is the one whose head was cut off with the sword: i.e. cut it off.
2:250: And his saying: 250- They came out means they were in the open space, which is the wide area of land. And Goliath was the prince of the giants. They said: meaning all the believers with him, and emptying conveys the meaning of abundance. And his saying: And made our feet firm this is an expression of strength and not failing, it is said: So-and-so's feet were firm on such-and-such if it was established for him and did not move from it, and his feet were firm in war if he was victorious and the victory was with him. His saying: And gave us victory over the disbelieving people they are Goliath and his soldiers. And the apparent was placed in place of the implicit to show what is the reason for the victory over them, which is their disbelief, and the victory was mentioned after the question of making the feet firm, because the second is the goal of the first.
2:251: His saying: 251- So they defeated them by God's permission Al-Hazm: with a kasra: and from it is a defeated water skin: meaning that some of it folded over some of it with dryness, and from it is what was said about Zamzam that it was defeated by Gabriel: meaning he defeated it with his foot so the water came out, and Al-Hazm: what is broken from dry firewood, and the meaning of the speech is that God sent down victory upon them: So they defeated them by God's permission meaning by His command and will. His saying: And David killed Goliath is David bin Isha with a kasra on the hamza then a silent taa' after it an emphatic letter, and it is said: David bin Zakariya bin Bishwi from the tribe of Judah bin Jacob, God combined for him between prophethood and kingship after he was a shepherd, and he was the youngest of his brothers, Talut chose him to fight Goliath and he killed him. What is meant by wisdom here is prophethood, and it was said: it is teaching him the making of armor and the language of birds, and it was said: it is giving him the chain by which they used to resort to arbitration. His saying: And taught him of what He willed. It was said that the present tense here is in place of the past tense, and the subject of this verb is God, the Most High, or it was said: David. The apparent meaning of this construction is that God, the Most High, taught him of what His will decreed and His desire was attached to, and it was said that among that is what we mentioned about his teaching the craft of armor and what came after it. His saying: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, the group read it as And had God not repelled, and Nafi’ read def’a, and they are two sources of def’a, as Sibawayh said. Abu Hatim said: def’a and def’a are one, like: Taraqt na’li and Taraqtuhu. Abu Ubaidah chose the reading of the majority and rejected the reading of def’a, saying: Because no one can defeat God, the Most High. Makki said: Abu Ubaidah suggests that this is from the category of reciprocal verbs, but it is not. According to both readings, the infinitive is added to the agent: that is, And had God not repelled the people and some of them are a substitute for the people, and they are the ones who directly cause evil and corruption with some other of them, and they are the ones who restrain them from that and turn them away from it. The earth would have been corrupted because the people of corruption would have prevailed over it and caused evils that destroy crops and offspring. The indefinite form of fadl is for emphasis.
2:252: And the signs of God: are what this story included of the mentioned matters. What is meant here by 252- in truth is the correct report that there is no doubt about it for the People of the Book and those who are familiar with the report of the world. And his saying: Indeed, you are among the messengers is information from God, the Most High, that he is among the messengers of God, the Most High, to strengthen his heart, to establish his soul, and to make his matter more difficult. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Have you not seen the assembly of the Children of Israel? He said: This was when prophethood was lifted and the people of faith were extracted, and the tyrants had expelled them from their homes and their children. And when fighting was prescribed for them, that is when the Ark came to them. He said: There were two tribes of Israel: a tribe of prophethood and a tribe of caliphate, so the caliphate would not be except in the tribe of caliphate, and prophethood would not be except in the tribe of prophethood. And their prophet said to them, ‘Indeed, God has sent to you Saul as a king.’ They said, ‘How can he have kingship over us when we are more deserving of kingship than he?’ He was not from either of the two tribes, neither from the tribe of prophethood nor from the tribe of caliphate. He said, ‘Indeed, God has chosen him over you.’ So they refused to hand over leadership to him until he said to them, Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you, in which is tranquility from your Lord and a remainder. When Moses threw down the tablets, they were broken and he lifted some of them and gathered what remained and put it in the Ark. The Amalekites had taken that Ark captive, and the Amalekites were a group from ‘Aad. In Jericho, the angels came with the Ark, carrying it between heaven and earth while they were looking at it until they placed it with Talut. When they saw that, they said: Yes, so they surrendered to him and made him king. When the prophets attended a battle, they would bring the Ark before them and say: Adam descended with that Ark, the Corner, and the Staff of Moses from Paradise. It has been reported to me that the Ark and the Staff of Moses are in Lake Tiberias, and that they will emerge before the Day of Judgment. This meaning has been reported in brief and in length from a group of the Salaf, so mentioning it at length does not provide any benefit that can be relied upon. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And He increased him abundantly meaning: excellence in knowledge and body meaning: he was great and large, surpassing the Children of Israel by his neck. He also narrated on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, And He increased him abundantly in knowledge meaning: knowledge of war. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he was asked: Was Saul a prophet? He said: No, no revelation came to him. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he was asked about the Ark of Moses, what was its capacity? He said: About three cubits by two cubits. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Tranquility is mercy. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on his authority that he said: Tranquility and peace of mind. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: “Sakinah is a creature the size of a cat with two eyes that shine. When two armies meet, it extends its hands and looks at them, causing the army to flee from fear.” Al-Tabarani narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ali that he said: Sakinah is a strong wind with two heads. Abd al-Razzaq, Abu Ubaid, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it. On the authority of Ali, he said: Tranquility has a face like a human face, then it is a gentle wind. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Tranquility from God is like the wind, it has a face like a cat's face, two wings, and a tail like a cat's tail. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: In it is tranquility from your Lord, he said: A golden basin from Paradise with which the hearts of the prophets were washed, and the tablets were thrown into it. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih that he said: It is a spirit from God that does not speak. If they differ about something, it speaks and informs them of what they want. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: It is something that their hearts find peace in. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: In it is tranquility, meaning: dignity. I say: These contradictory interpretations may have reached these scholars from the Jews, may God have mercy on them, so they came up with these matters with the intention of playing with the Muslims, may God be pleased with them, and casting doubt on them. Look at how they sometimes made it an animal, sometimes an inanimate object, and sometimes something that has no reason, like the saying of Mujahid: Like the form of the wind, it has a face like the face of a cat, two wings, and a tail like the tail of a cat. And thus, everything transmitted from the Children of Israel contradicts itself and includes what is usually not reasoned. It is not correct that such contradictory interpretations were narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor an opinion that its speaker saw, for they are too great a degree to interpret based on opinion and in which there is no room for ijtihad. If this is decided for you, you will know that it is obligatory to refer in such a case to the meaning of tranquility in language, which is well-known, and there is no need to ride these arbitrary and contradictory matters, for God has made it spacious for us. If we had established for us an interpretation of tranquility from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then it would have been obligatory for us to turn to it and say it, but it has not been established from a sound source, rather it has been established that it was revealed from some of the Companions when he was reciting the Qur’an, as in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Al-Baraa’, who said: “A man was reciting Surat Al-Kahf and he had a horse tied up, and a cloud covered him and it began to spin and draw near, and his horse began to flee from it. So when morning came, he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that.” To him, he said: That tranquility was sent down for the Qur’an. And there is nothing in this except that what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called a cloud that circled over that reciter, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the remainder of what the family of Moses left behind, he said: His staff and the fragments of the tablets. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Salih, he said: In the chest were the staff of Moses and the staff of Aaron, the clothes of Moses and the clothes of Aaron, two tablets of the Torah and manna, and the word of relief: There is no god but God, the Forbearing, the Generous, and glory be to God, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. Abd al-Razzaq and Abd bin Hamid narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: The angels carry him, he said: The angels came carrying him until they placed him in the house of Talut, and he became in his home. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas: Indeed in that is a sign, he said: A sign. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas: Indeed, God He has tested you with a river. He said: With thirst. So when he reached the river, which was the Jordan River, most of the people drank from it and drank from it. Whoever drank from it only became thirstier, and whoever took a handful with his hand was satisfied and his thirst was relieved. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: So they drank from it except a few of them. He said: The few are three hundred and a few. Ten are the number of the people of Badr. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’ who said: We, the companions of Muhammad, used to say that the people of Badr were the same number as the companions of Saul who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except a few dozen and three hundred believers. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions on the day of Badr: You are the same number as the companions of Saul on the day he met Goliath. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Juwaybir on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: They were three hundred thousand and three thousand and three hundred and thirteen, and they all drank from it except three hundred and thirteen men, the same number as the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr. Saul turned them back and three hundred and thirteen passed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi regarding his statement: those who think he said: those who are certain. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Talut was the commander of the army, so Abu Dawud sent with Dawud something to his brothers, and Dawud said to Talut: What is for me, and Goliath came and said: You have a third of my kingdom and I will marry you to my daughter, so he took a bag and put three dirhams in it, then he named Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, then he put his hand in it and said: In the name of God, my God and the God of my fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, so he went out to Abraham and made him in his mercy, so he threw it at Goliath and it pierced thirty-three eggs from his head and killed thirty thousand behind him. The commentators have mentioned many stories of this type, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu’ab al-Iman on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, he said: God repels those who pray for those who do not pray, those who perform Hajj for those who do not perform Hajj, and those who give zakat for those who do not give zakat. Ibn Adi and Ibn Jarir narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will repel calamity from one hundred of the families of his neighbors through the righteous Muslim. Then Ibn Umar recited the verse: And had God not repelled the people, and in its chain of transmission is Yahya ibn Saeed al-Attar al-Himsi, who is very weak.
2:253: His saying: 253- Those messengers It was said: It is a reference to all the messengers, so the alif and lam are for comprehensiveness. It was also said: It is a reference to the prophets mentioned in this surah, and it was also said: To the prophets whose knowledge reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. What is meant by preferring some of them over others is that God Almighty gave some of them more advantages of perfection than He gave to others, so the one with more advantages was superior and the other was inferior. Just as this verse indicated that some prophets are better than others, so did the other verse, which is the Almighty’s saying: And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Psalms. A group of scholars have questioned the reconciliation between this verse and what is proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with the wording: Do not give me precedence over the prophets. In another wording: Do not give precedence over the prophets. In another wording: Do not choose between the prophets. In another wording: Do not choose between the prophets. Some people said: This statement of his, may God bless him and grant him peace, was before the revelation of preference was sent to him, and that the Qur’an abrogates the prohibition of preference. It was said: He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that out of humility, as he said: “Let none of you say, ‘I am better than Jonah, son of Matta. ’” Out of humility, knowing that he is the best of the prophets, as is indicated by his saying: I am the master of the children of Adam. It was said: He only forbade that in order to prevent argument and dispute over the prophets, so it would be specific to such a thing, not if its issuance was trustworthy. It was said: The prohibition is only with regard to prophethood, because it is a single characteristic in which there is no preference, and there is no prohibition against preference by increasing special characteristics and honors. It was said: What is meant is the prohibition against preference merely for whims and fanaticism. All of these statements are weak. I believe that there is no contradiction between the Qur’an and the Sunnah, because the Qur’an indicates that God preferred some of His prophets over others, but that does not necessitate that we are permitted to prefer some of them over others, because the advantages that are the basis for preference are known to God and nothing of them is hidden from Him, and they are not known to humans. The followers of a prophet may be ignorant of some of his advantages and special features, let alone the advantages of others. Preference is not permissible except after knowing all the reasons that make this one superior and that one inferior, not before knowing some of them or most of them or least of them, because that is preference based on ignorance and undertaking something that the doer does not know and is forbidden from it. So if we assume that nothing came except the Qur’an to inform us that God preferred some of His prophets over others, there is no evidence in it that it is permissible for humans to prefer between prophets, so how about when the authentic Sunnah came forbidding that? If you know this, you will know that there is no contradiction between the Qur’an and the Sunnah in any way. The Qur’an contains the information from God that He prefers some of His prophets over others, and the Sunnah contains the prohibition for His servants to prefer between His prophets. Whoever attempts to reconcile between them, claiming that they are contradictory, has made a clear mistake. His statement: Among them are those to whom God spoke is Moses and our Prophet, peace be upon them. It has been narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said about Adam: He is a prophet who was spoken to. What supports this has been proven in Sahih Ibn Hibban from the hadith of Abu Dharr. His saying: And He raised some of them in degrees This some may be intended to refer to those whose status with God, the Most High, is great among the prophets. It may also be intended to refer to our Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, due to the abundance of his merits that necessitate his being preferred. It may also be intended to refer to Idris, because God, the Most High, informed us that He raised him to a high place. It was said: They were the ones of resolve. It was said: Abraham. It is not hidden from you that God, the Most High, knows which of them is this raised some. It is not permissible for us to address the explanation of it except with proof from God, the Most High, or from His prophets, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them. Nothing has been reported that guides us to that. Addressing the explanation of it is from the interpretation of the Noble Qur’an based on pure opinion. You have known what is in it of severe warning, even though that is a means to preferring among the prophets, and we have been forbidden from that. Many of the imams of interpretation have asserted that it is our Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and they have elaborated on that, and they have provided evidence for what God has singled him out with of miracles, merits of perfection, and characteristics of virtue. With this assertion, they have provided evidence that does not indicate what is required. They fell into two dangers and committed two prohibitions, which are interpreting the Qur’an based on opinion, and entering into pretexts for preferring one prophet over another. Even if that is not an explicit preference, it is a pretext for it without a doubt or suspicion, because whoever asserts that this person who is elevated in degrees is a certain prophet has moved from that to the forbidden preference. God has made our chosen Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, independent of that in a way that does not require him to have other virtues and merits. So beware of seeking to get closer to him, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, by entering into doors that he has forbidden you to enter, so that you disobey him and do wrong while you think that you are obedient and do good. His statement, And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs means the dazzling signs and apparent miracles of bringing the dead back to life, healing the sick, and other things. His statement, And We supported him with the Holy Spirit refers to Gabriel, and we have already discussed this. His saying: And if God had willed, those after them would not have fought one another, meaning after the messengers. It was said: after Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, because the second is mentioned explicitly, and the first and third are referred to by His saying: Among them are those to whom God spoke, meaning: if God had willed that they not fight, they would not have fought. So the object of the will is omitted according to the rule, but they differed as an exception to the conditional clause: meaning, but the fighting arose from their great differences until they became different sects, “some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. And if God had willed” that they not fight after this difference, “they would not have fought. But God does what He wills.” There is no one who can reverse His judgment, nor change His decree, so He does what He wills and rules what He wills. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the words of God the Almighty: We have preferred some of them over others, that he said: God took Abraham as a friend, and spoke to Moses directly, and made Jesus like Adam, creating Him from dust, then He said to him: Be, and he was. He is the servant of God, His Word, and His Spirit. He gave David the Psalms, and gave Solomon a kingdom that no one after him would have, and He forgave Muhammad his past and future sins. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the words of God the Almighty: Among them are those to whom God spoke, that he said: God spoke to Moses, and sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to all people. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Amir Al-Sha’bi regarding the words: And raised some of them by degrees, that he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada: And if God had willed, those after them would not have fought each other, that is, after Moses and Jesus. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Muawiyah when Ali came and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Muawiyah: Do you love Ali? He said: Yes. He said: There will be a brief tribulation between you. Muawiyah said: What will come after that, O Messenger of God? He said: God’s forgiveness and pleasure. He said: We are satisfied with God’s decree. Then this verse was revealed: ‘And if God had willed, they would not have fought, but God does what He intends.’” Al-Suyuti said: Its chain of transmission is weak.
2:254: The apparent command in His saying: 254- Spend is obligatory, and a group of people have interpreted it as obligatory charity for this reason, and because of the severe threat at the end of the verse. It has been said that this verse combines obligatory and voluntary zakat. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is correct, but the verses that preceded it mentioning fighting and that God repels the believers in the hearts of the disbelievers suggest that this exhortation is only for the sake of God. Al-Qurtubi said: According to this interpretation, spending money is sometimes obligatory, and sometimes exhortation according to whether jihad is obligatory or not. His saying: Before a Day comes when there is no trading means: Spend as long as you are able Before a Day comes when you cannot spend, which is a Day when there is no trading meaning that people will not trade on it. Friendship: pure affection taken from the secrets that are shared between two friends. God the Almighty has informed us that there is no beneficial friendship on the Day of Resurrection and no effective intercession except for one whom God has given permission. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with the accusative case of la bay’a, la khalah, la shafa’ah without a tanween. The rest read it with the nominative case and with a tanween. These are two well-known dialects of the Arabs, and two aspects known to grammarians. Among the first is the saying of Hassan: No stabbing, no ordinary knights, no stuffing around your skirts The second is the shepherd’s saying: I did not cut you off until I said openly, I have no camel or horse in this It is permissible in other than the Qur’an to change the meaning by raising some and lowering others, as is established in the science of grammar. His statement, And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers is evidence that every disbeliever is wronging himself. Among those who fall under this generality is the one who withholds zakat in a way that necessitates his disbelief, since this occurs in the context of the command to spend. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding the words of God the Almighty: O you who have believed, spend from that which We have provided for you, he said: from zakat and voluntary giving. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Sufyan who said: It is said that zakat abrogated every charity in the Qur’an, and the month of Ramadan abrogated every fast. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse who said: God knows that people will intercede for one another in this world, but on the Day of Resurrection there will be no friendship except the friendship of the righteous. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: Praise be to God who said: And the disbelievers - they are the wrongdoers, and did not say the wrongdoers - they are the disbelievers.
2:255: His saying: 255- There is no god but He meaning there is no true deity except Him, and this sentence is the predicate of the subject. The Ever-Living: The Eternal, and it was said: The One who does not disappear or change, and it was said: The Disposer of affairs and the Determiner of things. At-Tabari said on the authority of some people that it is said: The Ever-Living as He described Himself, and that is accepted without looking into it, and it is a second predicate and a deleted subject. The Self-Sufficient One is the One who is established over every soul for what it has earned, and it was said: The One who is established by His own self and the One who establishes others, and it was said: The One who is established in managing creation and preserving it, and it was said: He is the One who does not sleep, and it was said: The One who has no substitute. The root of Qayyum is Qayyum, the ya and the waw came together and one of them was preceded by a sukoon, so the first was assimilated into the second after changing the waw to a ya. Ibn Mas'ud, Alqamah, An-Nakha'i, and Al-A'mash read Al-Hayy Al-Qiyam with an alif, and that was narrated on the authority of Umar, and there is no disagreement among the linguists that the Self-Sufficient One is more well-known to the Arabs and has a more correct construction, and a more proven cause. The Sunnah: Drowsiness according to the majority, and drowsiness: what precedes sleep from lethargy and closing of the eyes, so when it reaches the heart it becomes sleep. Al-Mufassal differentiated between Sunnah, drowsiness and sleep, saying: Sunnah is from the head, drowsiness is in the eye, and sleep is in the heart. What should be relied upon in the difference between Sunnah and sleep is that the mind is not lost with Sunnah, unlike sleep, which is the relaxation of the brain organs from the moisture of vapors until the mind is lost with it, and even all perceptions with all the senses. What is meant is that nothing of them affects Him, and He mentioned Sunnah before sleep, because it precedes it in existence. Al-Razi said in his interpretation: Sunnah is what precedes sleep, so if it is an expression for sleep, then if it is said: drowsiness does not overtake him, it indicates that sleep does not overtake him by a fortiori, so mentioning sleep was a repetition. We said: The interpretation of the verse is that drowsiness does not overtake him, let alone sleep, and God knows best what he meant. And I say: This priority that he mentioned is not accepted, because sleep may come initially without what was mentioned of drowsiness. If it occurs to the heart and the eye at the same time, then he said to it sleep, but it is not called a year, so the negation of a year does not entail the negation of sleep. It has been reported from the Arabs that they both negated, including the saying of Zuhair: Not a year can take him throughout his life, nor can he sleep, and there is no doubt about his situation. He was not satisfied with denying the Sunnah. Also, a person is able to repel the Sunnah from himself, but he is not able to repel sleep from himself. Sleep may overtake him, but the Sunnah does not overtake him. If the Qur’anic system were limited to denying the Sunnah, that would not mean denying sleep. Likewise, if it were limited to denying sleep, it would not mean denying the Sunnah. How many people with a Sunnah are not asleep? The letter of negation was repeated to emphasize the inclusion of the negation for each of them. His saying: Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? This question is a denial of those who claim that any of His servants is able to benefit any of them through intercession or otherwise, and a rebuke and rebuke of him that is beyond measure. It contains a repulsion in the hearts of the worshippers of graves, a turning away from them, and a severing of their limbs that cannot be measured or reached. What is learned from it is more than what is learned from the saying of God the Most High: And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased. And His saying the Most High: And how many are there angels in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after God has given permission to whom He wills and is pleased with. And His saying the Most High: They do not speak except to whom the Most Merciful has given permission. To many degrees. The authentic hadiths established in the books of Islam have explained the nature of intercession, for whom it is, and who performs it. His saying: He knows what is before them and what is behind them the two pronouns refer to what is in the heavens and the earth, with rational beings being given precedence over others, and what is before them and what is behind them is an expression for what is before them and what is after them, or for this world and the hereafter and what is in them. His saying: And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge the meaning of encompassing has already been presented, and knowledge here means what is known: that is, they do not encompass anything of His information. His saying: His Throne encompasses the throne apparently is the body whose description has been reported in the narrations, as will be explained. A group of the Mu'tazila denied its affinity, and they made a clear mistake in that, and they made a grave error. Some of the Salaf said: The throne here is an expression for knowledge. They said: And from this the scholars were called chairs, and from this the notebook in which knowledge is collected, and from this the poet said: They are surrounded by white faces and a group of chairs with report when the time comes. This statement was preferred by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. It was said that His Kursi is His power by which He holds the heavens and the earth, as one says: Make a Kursi for this wall, meaning something to support it. It was also said that the Kursi is the Throne. It was also said that it is a depiction of His greatness, but it has no reality. It was also said that it is an expression for the kingdom. The first statement is correct, and there is no reason to deviate from the true meaning except for mere imaginations resulting from ignorance and misguidance. What is meant by His encompassing the heavens and the earth is that they are in Him and that He encompassed them and was not too narrow for them because He is simple and vast. His statement, And their preservation does not burden Him means that He is not burdened by the weight of the slightest thing, meaning that it burdened me and I endured hardship from it. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that the pronoun in His statement, burdens Him refers to God, the Most High, and it is possible that it refers to the Kursi because it is from the command of God. The Most High means the loftiness of power and status. Al-Tabari narrated from some people that they said: He is the Most High above His creation by the elevation of His place above the places of His creation. Ibn Atiyah said: These are the statements of ignorant anthropomorphists, and it should not have been narrated. The disagreement over proving direction is well-known, but the one who grows up on a school of thought sees others as outside the Shariah and does not look into its evidence or pay attention to it. The Book and the Sunnah are the criterion by which truth is known from falsehood, and by which the correct is distinguished from the corrupt. And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been ruined. There is no doubt that this expression is applied to the apparent and predominant as in His statement: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land. And the poet said: Then, when we had gained control over them, we left them slain before an eagle and a bird of prey. The word Azeem means the greatness of His status and danger. Al-Kashshaf says: The first sentence explains His management of creation and His dominance over it, not being heedless of it. The second sentence explains His being the owner of what He manages. The third sentence explains His great status. The fourth sentence explains His encompassing of the conditions of creation and His knowledge of those among them who are approved and deserving of intercession and those who are not approved. The fifth sentence explains the breadth of His knowledge and its connection to all information, or His majesty and great power. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in his statement: The Ever-Living meaning the Ever-Living who never dies. The Self-Sustaining means the One who is eternal and has no substitute. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Sheikh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mujahid in his statement: The Self-Sustaining he said: The One who is eternal over everything. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: The Self-Sustaining is the One who never ceases. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his statement: He is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep he said: Slumber is drowsiness, and sleep is sleep. They narrated except Al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: Slumber is the scent of sleep that overtakes the face and makes a person drowsy. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid in his statement: He knows what is before them he said: what has passed of this world and what is behind them of the Hereafter. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas what is before them what they have sent forth of their deeds and what is behind them what they have lost of their deeds. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, His Throne encompasses all things, he said: His knowledge. Do you not see his statement, and He does not tire in preserving them? And Al-Daraqutni in Al-Sifat and Al-Khatib in his history narrated on his authority that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about God’s statement, “His Throne encompasses all things,” he said: His Throne is the place of His feet, and no one can estimate the extent of the Throne except God, the Almighty and Majestic.” And Al-Hakim narrated it and declared it authentic. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari a similar hadith, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: If the seven heavens and the seven earths were spread out and then connected to each other, they would not be in His expanse, meaning the Throne, except in the position of a ring in a desert. Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr Al-Ghifari that he asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the Kursi, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, the seven heavens are nothing compared to the Kursi except like a ring thrown in a desert. The superiority of the Throne over the Kursi is like the superiority of the desert over that ring.” Abd Ibn Hamid, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Tabarani, and Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Umar that he said: “A woman came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘Supplicate to God to admit me into Paradise.’ So he glorified the Lord, glory be to Him, and said: ‘His Kursi encompasses the heavens and the earth, and it creaks like the creaking of a new saddle because of its weight.’” In its chain of transmission is Abdullah Ibn Khalifa, who is not well-known. There is doubt about his hearing it from Umar, and some of them narrate it from Umar as a murūk. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that it is the place of the feet. In its chain of transmission is Al-Hakam Ibn Dhahir Al-Fazari Al-Kufi, who is rejected. A group of the Salaf from the Companions and others have reported on the description of the Throne, and there is no need to elaborate on them. Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunnah book from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut’im a hadith describing it. Ibn Mardawayh also reported on the authority of Buraydah, Jabir and others. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, nor does He tire Him in preserving them, he said: It does not burden Him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, nor does He tire Him, he said: Nor does He multiply it. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: The Great One who has been perfected in His greatness. Know that there are hadiths about the virtue of this verse. Ahmad and Muslim narrated, and the wording is his, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him, 'Which verse of God's Book is the greatest?' He said, 'The Throne Verse.' He said, 'May knowledge be blessed for you, O Abu al-Mundhir.'" An-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azmah, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he had a jar of dates, and he used to look after it. He found that it was decreasing, so he guarded it one night and it looked like a young boy who had reached puberty. He said, 'So I greeted him and he returned the greeting.' I said, 'Who are you, a jinn or a human?' He said, 'A jinn.' I said, 'Give me your hand.' He gave it to me and I saw that his hand was the hand of a dog and his hair was the hair of a dog. I said, 'Is this how the jinn were created?' He said, 'I know that there is no one among them who is stronger than me.' I said, 'What made you do what you did?' He said, 'I heard that you are a man who loves charity, so we wanted to share in your food.' My father said to him, 'What will protect us from you?' He said: This verse is the Throne Verse in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Whoever says it in the evening will be protected from us until the morning, and whoever says it in the morning will be protected from us until the evening. When morning came, he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him. He said: The evil one has spoken the truth. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, as did Al-Tabarani and Abu Nu’aym in Al-Ma’rifah with a chain of narrators whose men are trustworthy, on the authority of Ibn Al-Asqa’ Al-Bakri: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to them regarding the description of the Muhajireen, and a man asked him which verse in the Qur’an is the greatest. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep,’ until the verse ended.” Ahmad narrated from the hadith of Abu Dharr with a similar chain of narration from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi narrated in his history from Anas with a similar chain of narration from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Darimi narrated from Anfa’ bin Abdullah Al-Kila’i with a similar chain of narration. Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurairah who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entrusted me with guarding the zakat of Ramadan. Then someone came to me and started to scoop it up and told me a story, at the end of which he said to him: ‘Let me teach you some words by which God will benefit you.’ I said: ‘What are they?’ He said: ‘When you go to bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi, for there will always be a guardian from God over you, and no devil will come near you until morning.’ Abu Hurairah informed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of that, and he said: ‘He has told you the truth, although he is a liar. Do you know who you are addressing, O Abu Hurairah?’ He said: ‘No.’ He said: ‘That was such-and-such a devil.’” Ahmad narrated something similar to this from Abu Ayyub. At-Tabarani, Al-Hakim, Abu Nu’aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from Mu’adh ibn Jabal. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas’ud that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘The greatest verse in the Book of God is God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.’ Ahmad, Al-Hakim narrated something similar, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated something similar from Abu Dharr. Ahmad and Al-Tabarani also narrated something similar from the hadith of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Surat Al-Baqarah contains a verse that is the master of the verses of the Qur’an. If it is recited in a house in which there is a devil, he will leave it, the Ayat Al-Kursi.” Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, although Al-Bukhari and Muslim did not narrate it. Al-Hakim narrated from the hadith of Za’idah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Everything has a peak, and the peak of the Qur’an is Surat Al-Baqarah. It contains a verse that is the master of the verses of the Qur’an, the Ayat Al-Kursi.” He said: It is strange, we do not know it except from the hadith of Hakim bin Jubayr. Shu’bah spoke about it and declared it weak, as did Ahmad, Yahya bin Ma’in and others. Ibn Mahdi abandoned it, and Al-Sa’di called him a liar. Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it from the hadith of Asma’ bint Yazid bin Al-Sakan, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about these two verses: God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and “Alif, Lam, Meem. God, there is no god but He,” for in them are the greatest name of God. There are hadiths about its merit other than this, and there are also hadiths about the merit of reciting it after prayers and other things. There are also hadiths about its merit, along with others, and there are many hadiths about this from the predecessors.
2:256: Scholars have differed regarding his statement: 256- There is no compulsion in religion into statements: The first is that it is abrogated because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forced the Arabs to accept the religion of Islam and fought them and was not satisfied with anything from them except Islam, and what abrogated it is the statement of God the Almighty: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and God the Almighty said: O you who believe, fight those of the disbelievers who are near you and let them find in you harshness and know that God is with the righteous and He said: You will be called to a people of great strength - you will fight them or they will submit, and many commentators have adopted this view. The second view is that it is not abrogated and was revealed specifically regarding the People of the Book, and that they are not forced to accept Islam if they pay the jizyah, rather those who are forced are the people of idols, so nothing is accepted from them except Islam or the sword, and this is what Al-Sha'bi, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Al-Dahhak adopted. The third view: This verse is specifically regarding the Ansar, and we will explain what was reported about that. The fourth statement: Its meaning is do not say to someone who converted to Islam under the sword that he was forced, for there is no compulsion in religion. The fifth statement: It was mentioned about captives, as long as they were from the People of the Book, they were not forced to convert to Islam. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation: That is, do not force anyone to enter the religion of Islam, for its evidence and proofs are clear and evident, and there is no need for anyone to be forced to enter it. Rather, whoever God guides to Islam, opens his chest, and enlightens his insight, enters it with clarity. And whoever God blinds his heart and seals his hearing and sight, then entering the religion under compulsion and coercion will not benefit him. This could be a sixth statement. Al-Kashshaf said in his interpretation of this verse: That is, God did not force the matter of faith by compulsion and coercion, but by empowerment and choice. Similar to this is His statement: {And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together. Then would you compel mankind until they are believers?} That is, if He had willed, He could have forced them to believe, but He did not, and the matter was based on choice. This could be a seventh statement. What should be relied upon and must be considered is that it is a decisive and unabrogated verse for the reason for which it was revealed, which is that a woman from the Ansar would be poor and her children would hardly survive, so she would make it a vow that if she had a child alive, she would convert to Judaism. When the Jews of Banu Nadir were expelled, there were some of the sons of the Ansar among them, so they said: We will not leave our sons, so it was revealed. This was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara on the authority of Ibn Abbas. This story has been narrated from various sources, the gist of which is what Ibn Abbas mentioned with additions that include that the Ansar said: We only made them adhere to their religion, meaning the religion of the Jews, and we see that their religion is better than our religion, and that God brought Islam so we will force them. So when it was revealed, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave the best of children and did not force them to Islam. This requires that the People of the Book are not forced to convert to Islam if they choose to remain in their religion and pay the jizyah. As for the people of war, the verse, although it includes them, because the indefinite noun in the context of negation and the definition of religion indicates that, and consideration is given to the generality of the wording and not to the specificity of the reason, yet this generality has been made specific by the verses that have been reported about forcing the people of war from the infidels to Islam. His statement: “The right way has become distinct from the wrong way” here is faith, and the wrong way is disbelief: meaning one has become distinct from the other. This is a resumption that includes the explanation of what came before it. And taghut is a noun of action from tagha yagha yaghtu yaghtu: if he exceeds the limit. Sibawayh said: It is a singular masculine noun: that is, a generic noun that includes little and much. Abu Ali al-Farsi said: It is a source like karhabut and jabrut that describes the singular and the plural, and its lam was changed to the position of the ‘ayn and its ‘ayn to the position of the lam like jabth and jadhab, then the waw was changed to an alif because of its movement and the movement of what preceded it, so it was said: taghut, and this statement was chosen by al-Nahhas. It was said: The origin of taghut in the language is taken from tyranny, which conveys its meaning without derivation, as it was said: pearls from pearls. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a plural. Ibn Atiyyah said: That is rejected. Al-Jawhari said: Taghut is the soothsayer, the devil, and every leader in misguidance. It may be one. God the Almighty said: They want to refer judgment to Taghut, while they have been commanded to disbelieve in him. It may be a plural. God the Almighty said: Their allies are Taghut. The plural is Taghut, meaning whoever disbelieves in Satan, idols, soothsayers, and leaders of misguidance, or all of them, and believes in God the Almighty after distinguishing right from wrong, has succeeded and held fast to the firm rope: that is, the firm one. Al-Wuthqa is from the word Wuthqa and its plural is Wuthqa like Al-Fadl and Al-Fadl. The commentators differed in the interpretation of the firmest bond after agreeing that it is a matter of likening and representing what is known by evidence to what is perceived by the senses. It was said: What is meant by the bond is faith, and it was said: Islam, and it was said: There is no god but God, and there is no objection to applying it to all of them. And schism: breaking without separation. Al-Jawhari said: Fasam means breaking something without making it clear. As for qasm with the letter qaf, it is breaking with separation. The author of Al-Kashshaf interpreted infisam as interruption.
2:257: His statement: 257- God is the protector of those who believe. The protector is fa'il, meaning active, and he is the helper. His statement, He brings them out is an explanation of the protectorate, or a state of the sub-samir in protector, and this indicates that what is meant by his statement, Those who believe are those who wanted to believe, because whoever has faith has come out from the darkness into the light, unless what is meant by bringing them out is taking them out from the doubts that the believers are exposed to, in which case there is no need to estimate the will. What is meant by the light in his statement, They bring them out from the light into the darkness is what the prophets of God brought of calling to the religion, for that is a light for the disbelievers, and their protectors brought them out from it into the darkness of disbelief: that is, their protectors confirmed them in their state of disbelief because of their turning them away from answering the caller to the prophets. It was said: The one who is referred to here by those who disbelieved is those whose disbelief is proven in the knowledge of God Almighty. Their guardians from the devils and the leaders of misguidance bring them out from the light that is the nature of God upon which He created people to the darkness of disbelief into which they fell because of that bringing them out. Saeed bin Mansour, Abdul bin Hameed bin Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair something similar to what was mentioned above on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the reason for the revelation of the verse: There is no compulsion in religion, and he added that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the best of sons. Abdul bin Hameed, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi something similar as well, and he said: Those who did not convert to Islam joined them meaning Banu An-Nadir, and those who converted to Islam remained. Saeed bin Mansour, Abdul bin Hameed, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: “The people of the Ansar were breastfed by Banu Qurayzah and they remained steadfast in their religion. When Islam came, their families wanted to force them to convert to Islam, so it was revealed.” Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Hasan. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: There is no compulsion in religion, he said: It was revealed about a man from the Ansar from Banu Salim ibn Awf called Al-Hussain, who had two Christian sons, and he was a Muslim man. He said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Shall I not force them, for they have refused to accept anything but Christianity? So it was revealed.
