Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Al-Hanafiyyah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were people from the Ansar who had lineage and kinship to Qurayzah and An-Nadir, and they were afraid not to give charity to them and wanted them to become Muslims, so this verse was revealed: You are not responsible for their guidance Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Amr al-Hilali who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked: Do you give charity to the poor among the People of the Book? So God revealed: You are not responsible for their guidance al-Baqarah 2:170. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani who said regarding the verse: And you do not spend except seeking the countenance of God al-Baqarah 2:170: If you give for the sake of God, then you are not responsible for what you did. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God al-Baqarah 2:170, he said: They are the people of the Suffa. Ibn Sa’d narrated something similar on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: They are the emigrants from Quraish in Madinah with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), they were commanded to give charity to them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’ regarding the verse: Those who are restricted in the cause of God al-Baqarah 2:170: They restricted themselves in the cause of God for fighting and they are unable to trade. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: They are people who were wounded in the way of God and became poor, so He gave them a right in the wealth of the Muslims. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Raja bin Haywah regarding His statement: They are unable to travel in the land, he said: They are unable to trade. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding His statement: The ignorant think them rich, he said: God guided the believers to them and made their expenses for them, and ordered them to spend their expenses on them and was pleased with them. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: You will recognize them by their mark, he said: Greed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ that its meaning is: You will recognize in their faces the effort of need. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, You will recognize them by their appearance, he said: The shabbiness of their clothes. It was proven in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The poor person is not the one who is satisfied with a date or two, or a morsel or two, but the poor person is the one who refrains from asking. And if you wish, recite: They do not ask people insistently.” Many hadiths have been narrated about the prohibition of asking except for someone in authority or in a matter that he finds no alternative to. Ibn Sa’d, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Adi, al-Tabarani, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Gharib al-Maliki, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: This verse, ‘Those who spend their wealth by night and by day,’ was revealed about the owners of horses. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili, who said: About those who do not tie their horses out of pride, showing off, or seeking fame. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Darda’. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Hanash Al-San’ani that he heard Ibn Abbas say about this verse: They are those who feed the horses in the way of God. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Wahhab bin Mujahid on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: It was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib, he had four dirhams, he spent one dirham at night, one dirham during the day, one dirham secretly, and one dirham openly. Abd Al-Wahhab is weak, but Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding this verse, he said: These are people who spent in the way of God, which He has made obligatory upon them, without extravagance, poverty, waste or corruption. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: It was revealed about Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf and Uthman bin Affan regarding their spending in the Army of Hardship.
3:131: Riba in the language: increase absolutely, it is said that something grows, and in the Sharia it is applied to two things: Riba al-Fadl and Riba al-Nasee'ah as is separate in the books of branches, and what was mostly done in the pre-Islamic era was that when the due date of the debt came, the one who owed it would say to the one who owed it: Will you pay it or will it increase? If he did not pay it, he would add an amount to the money that he had delayed the term for a while. This is forbidden by consensus, and the analogy of writing Riba with a Ya because of the Kasra at the beginning. They wrote it in the Qur’an with a Waw. It was said in Al-Kashaf: In the language of those who emphasize, as prayer and zakat were written, and the Alif was added after it to resemble the Waw of the plural. I said: This is merely a convention that is not necessary to follow, for these written inscriptions are conventional matters that are not disputed over except in what indicates the letter that was in the root of the word and the like, as is established in the discussions of calligraphy in the science of morphology. In any case, writing the word and making its written inscription according to what the pronunciation requires is preferable. So whatever is pronounced as an alif, such as prayer and zakat and the like, it is preferable to write it like that. And the fact that the root of this alif is a waw or a ya’ is not hidden from anyone who knows morphology. These inscriptions are only for understanding the word that indicates it, how it is in the pronunciation of the one who pronounces it, not for understanding that the root of the word is such and such, which is not the case in pronunciation. So know this and do not concern yourself with what many of the people of knowledge consider in these inscriptions and oblige themselves to it and criticize those who disagree with it, for that is from the dispute over conventional matters that do not oblige anyone to adhere to it. So you should write these inscriptions according to what the speaker pronounces when reading them, for that is the required matter from It is not required of it to be indicative of what is the origin of the word that the speaker pronounces, which does not occur in his pronunciation now. So do not be deceived by what is narrated from Sibawayh and the grammarians of Basra that interest is written with a waw, because he says in its dual form ribwan. The Kufians said: It is written with a ya, and its dual form is ribyan. Al-Zajjaj said: I have not seen a mistake uglier or more heinous than this. It is not enough for them to make a mistake in writing until they make a mistake in the dual form when they read: And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the people’s wealth, it does not increase. What is meant by his saying here: 275- Those who consume interest is not that this threat is specific to those who consume it, rather it is general for everyone who deals with interest, taking it and giving it. Rather, he specified eating to increase the ugliness of its doer, and because it is the most important purpose, since the one who takes interest only takes it for eating. His saying: They will not rise means on the Day of Resurrection, as is indicated by the reading of Ibn Masoud: They will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has beaten to madness. It was narrated by Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim, and this is how the majority of commentators interpreted it. They said: He will be resurrected like a madman as a punishment for him and as a sign of abhorrence among the people of the gathering place. It was also said: What is meant is to liken someone who is greedy in his trade and collects his money from usury to the standing of a madman, because greed, covetousness and the desire to collect have provoked him until he became similar in his movements to a madman, just as it is said of someone who walks quickly and moves unsteadily: he has gone mad. From this is the saying of Al-A’sha about his she-camel: And after a long night, it becomes as if it has been seized by a jinn or a demon. So he made her walk quickly and energetically like a madman. His statement: Except as he stands whom Satan has afflicted with insanity means except standing like the standing of one who is afflicted with insanity. And striking is hitting unevenly like the striking of the blind, which is the one who is possessed. And insanity: madness, and yesterday: the madman, and so is the first, and it is related to his statement: They stand meaning: they do not stand from the possession that is in them except as he stands whom Satan has afflicted with insanity or it is related to stands. And in the verse is evidence of the corruption of the statement of those who said: Epilepsy is not from the side of the jinn, and claimed that it is from the action of nature, and said: The verse is outside what the Arabs claimed that Satan afflicts a person, and this is not correct, and Satan does not enter into a person and there is no possession from him. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sought refuge from Satan afflicting him, as narrated by al-Nasa’i and others. His saying: That is a reference to what was mentioned about their condition and punishment because of their saying: Trade is just like usury, meaning: they made trade and usury one thing, and they only likened trade to usury as an exaggeration by making usury the basis and trade a branch, meaning: trade without an increase when the due date is due is like trade with an increase when it is due, because the Arabs did not know any usury except that, so God responded to them by saying: And God has permitted trade and forbidden usury, meaning: God has permitted trade and forbidden a type of it, which is trade that includes usury. Trade is the source of ba’a yabee’, meaning he paid a consideration and took something in return, and the sentence is explanatory and has no syntactic position. His saying: So whoever receives an admonition from his Lord, meaning whoever receives an admonition from God from the admonitions that are included in the commands and prohibitions, including what occurred here of the prohibition of usury, then he desisted, meaning he complied with the prohibition that came to him and the warning against what was prohibited, and it is conjoined, meaning his saying: then he desisted, with his saying: came to him. His saying: from his Lord is related to his saying: came to him or to something omitted that was an attribute of the sermon: that is, from from his Lord, so he desisted, so he will have what is past that is, what he did of usury will not be held accountable for, because he did it before the prohibition of usury reached him or before the verse prohibiting usury was revealed. And his saying: And his affair is with God. It was said: The pronoun refers to what came before: that is, his affair is with God in pardoning him and dropping the responsibility for it. And it was said: The pronoun refers to the one who is engaged in usury: that is, the affair of the one who deals with usury to God in confirming him to stop or return to disobedience. And whoever returns to eating usury and dealing with it, they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. The reference is to the one who returns, and the plural of companions is based on the meaning of whoever. And it was said: The meaning of the one who returns is that he returns to saying: Trade is like usury and that he disbelieves in that and thus deserves eternity. And according to the first estimation, eternity is borrowed in the sense of exaggeration, as the Arabs say a king who is eternal: that is, long-lived. And arriving at this interpretation is obligatory due to the successive hadiths that determine the exit of the one who has been innovated from the Fire. His saying 131- And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers. This is guidance to avoid what the disbelievers do in their dealings. Many commentators said: It is that whoever permits usury is a disbeliever. It was said that its meaning is: Fear the usury which strips you of faith and you deserve the Fire. Usury was specifically mentioned in this verse because it is the one for which God threatened war against its doer.
2:276: His statement: 276- God destroys usury meaning: He takes away its blessing in this world, even if it is a lot, so that it does not remain in the hand of its owner. It was also said: He destroys its blessing in the Hereafter. His statement: And He increases the charity meaning: He increases the money from which charity is given. It was also said: He blesses the reward of charity and multiplies it and increases the reward of the one who gives charity. There is nothing wrong with interpreting this to mean both matters. His statement: And God does not love every ungrateful sinner meaning: He is not pleased, because love is specific to those who repent. It contains great severity and harshness on whoever commits usury, as He judges him to be an unbeliever and describes him as a sinner for the sake of exaggeration. It was also said: To remove the ambiguity, as it may apply to farmers. It is possible that what is meant by His statement: Every ungrateful is whoever commits a characteristic that necessitates unbelief. The reason for its connection to the situation is that those who said: Trading is like usury, it is unbelief.
2:277: The interpretation of his statement: 277- Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds to the end of the verse has been presented. Abu Ya'la narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity, he said: They will be known on the Day of Resurrection by that, they will not be able to stand except as one who is being beaten by Satan into insanity stands. That is because they said, 'Trade is [just] like interest,' and they lied about God. And God has permitted trade and forbidden interest. And whoever returns to consuming interest, These are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: The one who consumes interest will be raised on the Day of Resurrection insane, strangling. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from another chain of transmission on his authority also regarding his statement: They will not stand, he said: That is when he is raised from his grave. Al-Asbahani narrated in his Targhīb on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The usurer will come on the Day of Resurrection in a dazed state, dragging his lips. Then he recited: They will not rise except as one rises who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. Many hadiths have been narrated about the enormity of the sin of usury, including the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, which was narrated by al-Hakim and authenticated by al-Bayhaqi, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: Usury has seventy-three forms, the least of which is like a man marrying his mother, and the worst usury is the honor of a Muslim. And from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), narrated by Ibn Majah and al-Bayhaqi with the wording: Seventy forms. This meaning was narrated, with different numbers, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam, Ka’b, Ibn Abbas, and Anas. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’ regarding the verse, saying: They will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with madness from Satan in them, and in some readings it is: They will not rise on the Day of Resurrection. He meant the reading of Ibn Mas’ud mentioned above. In the two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Aisha, she said: When the verses at the end of Surat Al-Baqarah were revealed about usury, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the mosque and recited them to the people, then he forbade trade in alcohol.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab that he gave a sermon and said: The last verse of the Qur’an to be revealed was the verse on usury, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died without explaining it to us, so leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt.” Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The last verse revealed to His Messenger was the verse on usury. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il a similar narration on the authority of Umar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the usury that God has forbidden, he said: The people of ignorance would have a man who owed another man a debt and he would say: You have such and such and you will defer it from me, so he would defer it from him. He also narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair something similar, and he added to his statement: But whoever receives an admonition from his Lord, meaning the clarification in the Qur’an regarding the prohibition of usury, and he desists from it, shall have what is past, meaning he shall have what he had eaten of usury before the prohibition, and his affair is with God, meaning after the prohibition and after abandoning it. If He wills, He will protect him from it, and if He wills, He will not do so. And whoever returns, meaning to usury after the prohibition and permits it by saying: Trade is but like usury, “they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally,” meaning they will not die. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: God destroys usury, he said: He decreases usury, and gives increase for charity, he said: He increases it. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, “Whoever gives in charity a date’s worth of lawful earnings—and God does not accept except that which is lawful—then God will accept it with His right hand and then give it increase for its owner as one of you gives his foal increase until it becomes like a mountain.” Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Hibban and Al-Tabarani narrated a similar hadith from Aisha. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawader Al-Usul on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. In the hadith of Aisha and Ibn Umar, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited after citing the hadith, God destroys interest and gives increase for charities. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abu Barzah Al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A servant gives a piece of bread in charity, and it increases with God until it becomes like Mount Uhud. These hadiths explain the meaning of the verse.
2:278: His statement: 278- Fear God meaning protect yourselves from His punishment and leave the remainder of usury that remains for you. It appears that he nullified usury that was not collected. His statement: If you are believers It was said: It is a metaphorical condition for the sake of exaggeration. It was also said: The if in this verse means when. Ibn Atiyah said: It is rejected and is not known in the language. It appears that the meaning is: If you are believers in truth, then that necessitates compliance with the commands and prohibitions of God.
2:279: His statement: 279- If you do not do meaning what you were ordered to do of avoiding and abandoning what remains of usury then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger meaning be aware of it, from the verb to be informed if you know about it, it was said: it is from the word to be informed which means listening because it is one of the ways of knowing. Abu Bakr read from Asim and Hamza be informed meaning then inform others that you are at war with them. This indicates that consuming usury and acting upon it are major sins, and there is no disagreement about that, and the indefiniteness of war is for glorification, and its glorification was increased by its relation to the greatest name of God and to His Messenger who is the most honorable of His creation. His statement: But if you repent meaning from usury then you shall have your principal you shall take it and you shall not be wronged your debtors by taking the increase nor shall you be wronged you by delaying or reducing, and the sentence is a circumstantial or a new sentence. This is evidence that their money, without repentance, is permissible for those who take it from the imams and others like them who represent them.
2:280: His saying: 280- And if he is in hardship When the Almighty ruled for the people of usury to have their principal when they have money, He ruled for those in hardship by looking to ease, and hardship is the tightness of the situation due to the lack of money, and from it the army of hardship. And the postponement is the delay, and ease is a source meaning ease, and the word dhu was raised with the perfect kan which means found, and this is the saying of Sibawayh and Abu Ali al-Farisi and others. Sibawayh recited: May the sons of Dhuhl bin Shaiban be sacrificed for you, O young man, when it is a day with gray stars. In the Mushaf of Abi, And if he is in hardship means: And if the one who is owed is in hardship. Al-A’mash read And if he is insolvent. Abu Amr Al-Dani said on the authority of Ahmad bin Musa, and this is also in the Mushaf of Abi bin Ka’b. Al-Mu’tamir narrated on the authority of Hajjaj Al-Warraq, who said in the Mushaf of Uthman: And if he is in hardship. An-Nahhas, Makki and An-Naqqash said: According to this, the wording of the verse is specific to those who owe usury, and according to those who read Dhu, it is general for all who owe a debt, and this is the opinion of the majority. The group read Fanzrah with a kasrah on the Dhad. Mujahid, Abu Raja and Al-Hasan read it with a sukoon, and this is the language of Tamim. Nafi’ alone read Maisarah with a damma on the Seen, and the majority read it with a fatha, and it means ease. His statement And that you give in charity by deleting one of the two Ta’s, and it was read with a shaddah on the Sad: meaning that you give in charity to your insolvent creditors by releasing them is better for you, and in it is an encouragement for them to give in charity from their principal to those who are in hardship, and making that better than giving them a respite, as stated by As-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and Ad-Dahhak. Al-Tabari said: Others said: The meaning of the verse is that giving charity to the rich and the poor is better for you. The first is correct, and the verse does not include the rich. His statement: If you only knew has an omitted answer: that is, if you knew that it was better for you, you would have acted upon it.
2:281: His statement: 281- And fear a Day is the Day of Resurrection. Its indefiniteness is for emphasis and it is accusative as a direct object, not an adverb. His statement: On which you will be returned to God is a description of it. Abu Amr read it with a fatha on the taa and a kasra on the jim, and the rest read it with a damma on the taa and a fatha on the jim. Some people said that this mentioned day is the day of death. The majority said that it is the Day of Resurrection as mentioned above. His statement: To God contains an omitted complement, the meaning of which is to God's judgment. Then every soul will be paid in full from the souls that are accountable. What it has earned means the reward for what it has done of good or evil. The phrase and they will not be wronged is a circumstantial clause, and the pronoun is plural because it is more appropriate to the state of reward, just as the singular is more appropriate to the state of earning. This verse contains good advice for all people. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of interest, he said: It was revealed about al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and a man from Banu al-Mughira who were partners in the pre-Islamic era, lending interest to people from Thaqeef. Islam came and they had great wealth in interest, so God revealed this verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: Thaqif had made peace with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the condition that whatever interest they had on people, and whatever interest people owed them, would be abolished. When the conquest took place, he appointed Atab ibn Asid over Mecca, and Banu Amr ibn Awf used to take interest from Banu al-Mughira, and Banu al-Mughira used to charge them interest in the pre-Islamic period. Islam came and they had a lot of money on them, so Banu Amr came to them asking for their interest, but Banu al-Mughira refused to give them any in Islam, and they brought that to Atab ibn Asid, so Atab wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of interest. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote about it to Atab and said: If they are satisfied, then fine, otherwise declare war on them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then declare war, he said: Whoever persists in usury and does not desist from it, then it is the duty of the leader of the Muslims to ask him to repent, and if he desists, otherwise his head is to be struck. They also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Then declare war, he said: Be certain of war. The people of Sunan and others narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Al-Ahwas that he witnessed the Farewell Pilgrimage with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and he said: “Beware, all usury in the pre-Islamic era is abolished. You shall have your principal; you shall neither wrong nor be wronged. The first usury to be abolished was the usury of Al-Abbas.” Ibn Mandah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: This verse was revealed about Rabi’ah ibn Amr and his companions: But if you repent, you shall have your principal. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And if he is in hardship, he said: It was revealed regarding usury. Abd Al-Razzaq, Sa’id ibn Mansur and Abd ibn Hamid narrated something similar from Shuraih. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding the verse, saying: And so is every debt owed by a Muslim. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr. There are authentic hadiths in the two Sahihs and others encouraging someone who has a debt owed by someone in difficulty to postpone it. Abu Ubaid, Abd ibn Humayd, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, At-Tabarani, Ibn Al-Mundhir, At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The last verse of the Qur’an revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of As-Suddi and Atiyah Al-Awfi something similar. Ibn Al-Anbari narrated on the authority of Abu Salih and Saeed ibn Jubayr something similar. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was the last verse revealed, and there were eighty-one days between its revelation and the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived for nine nights after its revelation and then died.
2:282: This is a beginning to explain the state of debt that occurs between people after explaining the state of usury: that is, if some of you owe one another and deal with them in that way, and the debt was mentioned after mentioning what makes it unnecessary from debt for the purpose of emphasis, such as his saying: nor a bird that flies with its wings. It was said: that it was mentioned so that the pronoun in his saying: 282- write it down. If he had said: write down the debt, there would not have been as good in it as in his saying: if you contract a debt. The debt is an expression for every transaction in which one of the two exchanges is cash, and the other is on credit, because the cash among the Arabs is what is present, and the debt is what is absent. The poet said: You promised us two dirhams of paint, whether it is immediate or not. The other said: If they light a fire and wood, then that is death in cash, not in religion. God the Almighty has explained this meaning by saying: for a specified term. He has used it as evidence that an unknown term is not permissible, especially the term of salam. It has been proven in Sahih from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever advances dates, let him advance a known measure for a known term. The majority have said this, and stipulated that it be timed in days, months, or years. They said: It is not permissible until the harvest, or the threshing, or the return of the caravan, or the like. Malik permitted it. His saying: Then write it down means the debt with its term, because this prevents disputes and ends disagreement. His saying: And let a scribe write between you is a clarification of the manner of writing that is commanded, and the apparent meaning of the command is obligation, and this is what Ata’, Ash-Sha’bi, and others said. They made it obligatory for the scribe to write if he is asked to do so, and there is no scribe other than him. It has been said that the command is for encouragement. His saying: with justice is related to an omitted word describing the writer, i.e. a writer who is just: i.e. writes equally, neither adding nor subtracting, nor leaning towards one side. It is a command to the debtors to choose a writer who has this characteristic, who has no leniency in his heart or pen for one over the other, but rather seeks out the truth between them and is just towards them. His saying: And no writer shall refuse the indefinite noun in the context of negation indicates generality: i.e. no writer shall refrain from writing the debt book as God taught him: i.e. in the way that God taught him to write, or as God taught him by His saying: with justice. His saying: And let him who has the right dictate. Dictation and dictation are two languages: the first is the language of the people of Hijaz and Banu Asad and the second is the language of Banu Tamim. So this verse came in the first language, and in the second language came the saying of God the Almighty: So it is dictated to him morning and evening. And the one who has the right is the one who has the debt. God the Almighty commanded him to dictate, because the testimony is only on his acknowledgment of the existence of the debt in his account, and God commanded him to be pious in what he dictates to the writer. He went to great lengths in that by combining the name and the description in His saying: And let him fear God, his Lord. And He forbade him from shortcomings, which is deficiency. It was said: It is a prohibition of the writer. The first is more appropriate because the one who has the right is the one from whom deficiency is expected. If it were a prohibition of the writer, it would not be limited in its prohibition to deficiency, because an increase is expected from him as well as a deficiency is expected from him. The foolish is the one who has no opinion in good behavior, so he does not know how to take or give. He was likened to a foolish garment, which is lightly woven. The Arabs use foolishness to mean weakness of mind sometimes, and weakness of body other times. From the first is the saying of the poet: We fear that our dreams will be fooled and we will live ignorantly with the ignorant The second is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: Walking as spears shake, their tops are blown away by the passing winds That is, he weakened it and made it easy with its movement. In short, the foolish person is the spendthrift, either because of his ignorance of spending or because he plays with money in vain, although he is not ignorant of what is right. The weak person is the old man or the child. Linguists say: Weakness is with a damma on the letter Ḍād in body, and with a fathah on the letter Ḍād in opinion. The one who cannot dictate is the mute or the one who is unable to express himself as he should. It was said: The weak person is the one whose mind is bewildered, whose intelligence is deficient, and who is unable to dictate. The one who cannot dictate is the child. His statement: So let his guardian dictate with justice The pronoun refers to the one who has the right, so the guardian of the fool dictates for him after preventing him from disposing of his money, and his trustee or guardian dictates for the child, and likewise he dictates for the weak person who is unable to dictate due to the weakness of his guardian because he is in the position of the child or the one appointed for him by the imam or judge, and he dictates for the one whose agent is unable if he is of sound mind and has a defect in his tongue or not, but he is ignorant and is unable to express himself as he should. Al-Tabari said: The pronoun in his statement: his guardian refers to the right, and it is very weak. Al-Qurtubi said in his interpretation: The actions of the fool who is under guardianship without his guardian are invalid by consensus and are abrogated forever, do not require a ruling and do not affect anything. If the actions of a fool who is not under guardianship are disputed, then that is the end. His statement: And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men Martyring means asking for testimony, and he called them two witnesses before testimony from the metaphor of the first, i.e. in consideration of what their matter leads to in terms of testimony, and from among your men is related to his statement: And bring to witness or to an omitted word that is a description of two witnesses: i.e. two from among your men: i.e. from the Muslims, so the infidels are excluded, and there is no reason to exclude slaves from this verse, for if they are Muslims, they are from the men of the Muslims, and this is what Shuraih, Uthman al-Batti, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and Abu Thawr said. Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Shafi’i, and the majority of scholars said: The testimony of a slave is not permissible because of the deficiency in slavery that accompanies him. Al-Sha’bi and al-Nakha’i said: It is valid in the case of a small amount but not a large amount. The majority of scholars have argued that the testimony of a slave is not permissible because the address in this verse is to those who deal in debt, and slaves do not own anything that the transaction is conducted with. The response to this is that the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. Also, the debt and other transactions are valid from a slave if his owner permits him to do so. People have differed as to whether witnessing is obligatory or recommended. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Ibn 'Umar, al-Dahhak, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Jabir ibn Zayd, Mujahid, Dawud 'Ali al-Dhahiri and his son said that it is obligatory. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari preferred this view. Al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifah and his companions held that it is recommended. This disagreement among them is about the obligation of witnessing a sale. Those who hold this view argued with the Almighty's saying: And bring to witness when you make a sale. There is no difference between this command and His saying: And bring to witness. Therefore, those who say that witnessing is obligatory in a sale must say that it is obligatory in a debt. His statement: If they are not two men, then a man and two women, meaning: let a man and two women testify, or a man and two women, that is, they will suffice. His statement: of those whom you accept as witnesses is related to an omitted word that is an attribute of a man and two women, meaning they are among those whom you accept as witnesses. What is meant is those whose religion and justice you are satisfied with, meaning they are among those whom you are satisfied with as witnesses. What is meant is those whose religion and justice you are satisfied with. It indicates that two women are witnesses with a man, and that the testimony of women is not permissible except with a man, not alone, except in matters that no one else can see, due to necessity. They differed as to whether it is permissible to rule with the testimony of two women with the oath of the plaintiff, just as it is permissible to rule with the oath of a man with the oath of the plaintiff. Malik and al-Shafi’i held that this is permissible, because God, the Exalted, made the two women like the man in this verse. Abu Hanifa and his companions held that this is not permissible, and this goes back to the disagreement over ruling with a witness with the oath of the plaintiff, and the truth is that it is permissible because of the evidence for it, and it is an addition that does not contradict what is in the Noble Book, so it must be accepted. We have explained this in our explanation of Al-Muntaqa and other books of ours, and it is known to everyone who understands that there is nothing in this verse that would reject the ruling of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) with a witness and an oath, and they did not refute this except with a principle established on the edge of a precipice, which is his saying: Adding to the text is abrogation, and this is a false claim, rather adding to the text is an established law that was brought to us by the one who brought us the text that preceded it, and also it was necessary for them not to rule with the refusal of the requested nor with an oath to respond to the claimant. And they ruled with both, and the answer is the answer. His saying: that one of them should go astray and the other should remind her, Abu Ubaid said: The meaning of go astray is forget, and going astray from testimony is only forgetting part of it and remembering part. Hamza read in tadal with a kasra on the hamza. His saying: So remember is his answer to this reading, and according to the reading of the majority, it is in the accusative case in apposition to you go astray, and whoever raises it, it is on the resumption. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read so remember with a light dhal and kaf, and its meaning is: you increase her remembrance. The reading of the group with a shaddah: that is, a reminder if she is heedless and forgetful. This verse is an explanation for considering the number in women: that is, let one man bear witness and two women bear witness instead of the other man in order for one of them to remind the other if she goes astray. According to this, there is an omission in the speech, which is a questioner's question about the reason for considering two women instead of one man. It was said: its reason is that one of them goes astray, so one of them reminds the other. The reason in reality is the reminder, but since going astray was the cause of it, it was relegated to its status, and the subject in you go astray and you remember was ambiguous, because both descriptions are permissible for each of them. So the meaning is: if this one goes astray, this one reminds her, and if this one goes astray, this one reminds her, not specifically: that is, if one of the two women goes astray, the other woman reminds her. This reminder was only considered in them because of the weakness that women suffer from, unlike men. The reason for the ambiguity may be that it means that the misguidance and the reminder occur between them alternately, so perhaps this one goes astray in one direction and that one goes astray in another direction, so each one reminds the other. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: The meaning of his statement: So one of them reminds the other is that she becomes a male, meaning that the total testimony of two women is like the testimony of one man. Something similar was narrated from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’, and there is no doubt that this is false and is not indicated by the Shari’ah, language or reason. His statement: And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon means to give the testimony that they had previously borne, and it was said: when they are called upon to give the testimony, and calling them witnesses is a metaphor as mentioned above, and al-Hasan applied it to both meanings. The apparent meaning of this prohibition is that refusing to give testimony is forbidden. His statement: And do not be weary of writing it down means to be weary. Al-Akhfash said: It is said: I got tired, I get tired, boredom and weariness, and from this is the saying of the poet: I am tired of the costs of life, and whoever lives eighty years, may you have no father, gets tired. That is, do not tire of writing it down: that is, the debt you have incurred. It was said: the truth, and it was said: the witness, and it was said: the book. God the Almighty forbade them from that because they might tire of writing it down from the abundance of debt. Then He exaggerated in that and said: small or large that is, whether that which is written is small or large: that is, do not tire in any case, whether the debt is large or small. It was said: He used a metaphor for laziness by tiresomeness. The first is better. He mentioned the small here before the large to pay attention to it to prevent what might be said: that this is a small amount of money: that is, little, there is no need to write it down. The reference in His saying: that is to the written thing mentioned in the pronoun in His saying: that you write it down. “And more just” means more just: that is, more correct and more memorizing. And more upright for testimony that is, more helpful in establishing testimony and more reliable for it. It is derived from the root aqama, and likewise aqsat is derived from the root fa’ala: that is, more just. Sibawayh stated that it is analogical: that is, it is based on the comparative form af’al. The meaning of his statement: And it is more likely that you will not have doubts is closer to negating doubt in your dealings: that is, suspicion. Therefore, the book that they write removes whatever doubts they encounter, whatever they may be. His statement: Except that it be a present trade which you conduct among yourselves "that" is in the accusative case as an exception, as stated by Al-Akhfash. It is complete: that is, unless a trade occurs or is found, and the exception is disjunctive: that is, but at the time of your exchange and your trade is present with the presence of the two parties, "you conduct it among yourselves" you conduct it hand to hand. So, administration means conducting and receiving, so what is meant is the completed exchange hand to hand, so there is no blame upon you if you leave his book. And it was read with the accusative of trade as if it is incomplete: that is, unless the trade is a present trade. His saying: And have witnesses when you make a transaction. It was said that its meaning is: And have witnesses when you make this transaction mentioned, which is the present trade, on the condition that witnessing is sufficient in it. And it was said that its meaning is: If you make a transaction, any transaction, whether it is present or not, because that removes the source of disagreement and puts an end to the source of quarrels. The difference of opinion on whether this witnessing is obligatory or recommended was mentioned earlier. His saying: "And neither scribe nor witness shall be harmed" may be in the active or passive form. According to the first, it means: Neither scribe nor witness shall be harmed by the one who asks them for that, either by not answering, or by distorting, changing, adding or subtracting from his letter. This is indicated by the reading of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Abbas and Ibn Abi Ishaq, "nor shall a scribe or witness be harmed" with a kasra on the first ra. According to the second, neither scribe nor witness shall be harmed by being called to do that while they are busy with something important to them and being restricted in answering and being harmed if they delay, or being asked to come from a distant place. This is indicated by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, "nor shall a mother be harmed on account of her child", which, if you refer to it, will increase your insight, God willing. His statement: And if you do meaning what you have been forbidden from causing harm, then it meaning this action of yours is a transgression on your part meaning a departure from obedience to disobedience that is entangled in you. And fear God in doing what He has commanded you to do and leaving what He has forbidden you from. And God will teach you what you need of knowledge, and in it is the promise to whoever fears Him that He will teach it, and from it is the statement of the Most High: If you fear God, He will grant you a criterion.
2:283: His saying: 283- And if you are on a journey When the Almighty mentioned the legitimacy of writing and having witnesses to protect money and remove doubt, He followed that by mentioning the case of an excuse for not having a writer and He specified the case of travel, as it is among the cases of excuse, and every excuse that takes the place of travel is included in that, and He made the pledge taken in place of writing: that is, if you are traveling and you cannot find a scribe in your journey then a pledge taken in The people of knowledge said: The pledge in travel is established by the revelation, and in residence by the action of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as it was established in the two Sahihs "that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged his armor to a Jew". The majority read a writer, meaning a man who writes for you. Ibn Abbas, Ubayy, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Ikrimah, and Abu Al-Aaliyah read a book. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Mujahid explained it and said: Its meaning is if you cannot find ink: meaning in travel. Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read a pledge with a damma on the ra and the ha. It was narrated from them that the letter ha’ is pronounced lightly in the plural of rahan. This was said by al-Farra’, al-Zajjaj, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. Asim ibn Abi al-Najud read farhan with a fatha on the ra’ and a sukoon on the ha’. And the reading of the majority is rahan? Al-Zajjaj said: It is said in the case of a mortgage I mortgaged or I mortgaged, and so said Ibn al-A’rabi and al-Akhfash. Abu Ali al-Farsi said: It is said arahant in transactions, and as for a loan or sale I mortgaged. Tha’lab said: All the narrators are in the words of the poet: When I feared their claws, I escaped and gave them Malik as a pledge. On their mortgage that it is permissible to mortgage it and I mortgaged it except for Al-Asma’i who narrated it and he mortgaged it as an appositive of a future verb to a past verb and he likened it to his saying: I stood up and slapped his face. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: I mortgaged in both of them means I loaned, and the mortgagee is the one who takes the mortgage, and the thing is mortgaged and mortgaged, and I bet someone on such and such a bet on his mind. The majority considered taking possession as stated in the Qur’an, and Malik believed that it is permissible to mortgage by offer and acceptance without taking possession. His saying: If one of you trusts another, then let him who is trusted discharge his trust meaning if the one who owes the right is trustworthy with the owner of the right because of his good opinion of him and his trustworthiness with him and he is satisfied with his trustworthiness without being held hostage, then let him who is trusted discharge his trust meaning the debt that he owes, and trustworthiness is a source by which the one who is in the conscience is named and he added it to those who owe the debt because it has a relation to him, and it was read aytaman by changing the hamza to a ya’, and it was read by assimilating the ya’ to the ta’, which is a mistake, because the one that is changed from the hamza is not assimilated because it is in its ruling, and let him fear God, his Lord in not concealing anything of the truth. His saying: And do not conceal testimony is a prohibition for witnesses to conceal what they have been given of testimony, and it is in the ruling of an interpretation of His saying: And let no scribe be harmed meaning let him not be harmed by breaking the first ra’ according to one of the two previous interpretations. His saying: And whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful. The heart was specifically mentioned because concealment is one of its actions, and because it is the chief of the organs, and it is the morsel of flesh which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. The heart is raised as an agent or a subject and sinner is its predicate, according to what is established in the science of grammar. It is possible that his heart is a substitute for a sinner, a substitute for some of the whole, and it is also possible that it is a substitute for the pronoun in a sinner referring back to whom, and his heart was read in the accusative as in his saying: Except for he who fools himself. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt, he said: It was revealed regarding a loan with a known measure for a known term. Ash-Shafi’i, Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Bukhari and others narrated on his authority that he said: I bear witness that a guaranteed loan for a specified term is that God has set its term, and he recited this verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse. He said: Witnessing is commanded when contracting a debt so that there is no denial or forgetfulness involved in that. Whoever does not bear witness to that has disobeyed. And let not the witnesses refuse, meaning whoever is needed from the Muslims to bear witness to a testimony or has testimony, so it is not permissible for him to refuse if he is called upon. Then he said after this: And let not a scribe or a witness be harmed. Harm is when a man says to another man when he has no need of him: God has commanded you not to refuse when called upon, thus harming him while he is sufficient with someone else, so God forbade him from that. He said: And if you do, then it is a transgression on your part meaning a sin. He said: Among the major sins is concealing testimony, because God the Almighty says: And whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart is sinful. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated regarding His statement: And let not the scribe refuse that it is obligatory for the scribe to write. Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak that he said: Writing was a duty, then it was abrogated by: And let not the scribe nor the witness be harmed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid that he said: But if the one upon whom the right is is a fool that is the ignorant or weak that is the foolish. Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak and al-Suddi that he said: A fool that is the young boy. Ibn Jarir narrated from the path of Atiyah al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas that then let his guardian dictate that is the creditor. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan that he said: The guardian of the orphan. Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak that he said: The guardian of the foolish or the weak. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hameed, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Of your men, he said: Of the free men. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ regarding his statement: Of those whom you accept as witnesses, he said: Just. Ash-Shafi’i and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Two just, free Muslims. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: That one of them should err, he said: That one of the two women should forget the testimony, and one of them should remind the other, meaning that the one whose testimony was invalidated should remind her. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And let not the witnesses refuse, he said: If they have testimony. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ who said: A man would go around among a large group of people calling them to testify, but none of them would follow him, so God revealed: And let not the witnesses refuse. Abd bin Hameed and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Aisha regarding his statement: More just with God, she said: More just. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And neither scribe nor witness shall be harmed, he said: A man comes to two men and invites them to write and testify, and they say: We are in need, so he says: You have been ordered to respond, so he has no right to harm them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Tawus: And scribe shall not be harmed, so he writes what he was not dictated to, nor witness, so he testifies to what he was not asked to testify to. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding his statement: And if you are on a journey, the verse, he said: Whoever is on a journey and makes a sale on credit but does not find a scribe, then he is permitted to use a pledge that has been received, but if he finds a scribe, he does not have the right to use it as a pledge. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: A pledge can only be made while traveling. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr who said: A pledge can only be made when received. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Majah, Abu Nu`aym and Al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri that he recited this verse: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt… until he reached if some of you trust others… He said: This abrogated what came before it. I say: May God be pleased with this noble companion, this is not a case of abrogation, as this is restricted to trust and what came before it is established and decisive and was not abrogated, and it is in the absence of trust. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: sinful of heart he said: wicked of heart. Ibn Jarir narrated with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Sa`id bin Al-Musayyab that he heard that the most recent verse of the Qur’an to mention the Throne is the verse of debt. Abu Ubaid narrated in his Fadhail on the authority of Ibn Shihab who said: The last verses of the Qur’an to mention the Throne are the verses of usury and the verse of debt.
2:284: His statement: 284- To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth has already been explained. His statement: And if you disclose what is in your souls to the end of the verse, its apparent meaning is that God will hold His servants accountable for what they concealed or revealed of the matters for which He will be held accountable, so He forgives whomever He wills of them whatever He forgives of them, and punishes whomever He wills of them for what he concealed or revealed of them. This is the meaning of the verse according to the Arabic language. The scholars have differed regarding this verse in various opinions: The first is that although it is general, it is specific to concealing testimony, and that the one who conceals testimony will be held accountable for concealing it whether he reveals to people that he concealed testimony or not. This has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Al-Sha'bi and Mujahid, and it is rejected by the generality of the wording in the verse, and what came before this verse about the prohibition of concealing testimony cannot be specific to it. The second opinion: That what is in the verse is specific to what occurs to the souls of matters that are between doubt and certainty, said Mujahid, and this is also a specification without a specification. The third opinion: That it is a general ruling, but the punishment for what is in the soul is specific to the disbelievers and hypocrites. At-Tabari narrated it from some people, and this is also a specification without a specification, because His statement: He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills is not specific to a specific person except with evidence. The fourth opinion: That this verse is abrogated, said Ibn Masoud, Aisha, Abu Hurairah, Ash-Sha’bi, Ata’, Muhammad ibn Sirin, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, and Musa ibn Ubaydah, and it is narrated from Ibn Abbas and a group of the Companions and Followers, and this is the truth because of what will come of the explicit statement of its abrogation, and because it was proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God has forgiven this nation for what their souls have thought about. His saying: God will call you to account for it He placed the prepositional phrase before the subject to show its importance, and he placed the disclosure before the concealment, because the origin of the matters for which one will be held to account is the apparent deeds. As for placing the concealment before the statement of the Almighty: "Say: Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, God knows it", it is because knowledge is related to the hidden and apparent deeds in equal measure. He placed forgiveness before punishment because His mercy precedes His wrath. The sentence of His saying: Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills is a new sentence: meaning, He forgives and it includes the details of what was summarized in His saying: God will call you to account for it, and this is according to the reading of Ibn Amir and Asim. As for the reading of Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu Amr, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i with the jazm of the ra' and the ba', the fa' is a conjunction of what comes after it with the jazm before it, and it is the answer to the condition: I mean His saying: God will call you to account for it. Ibn Abbas, Al-A'raj, Abu Al-A'aliyah, and Asim Al-Jahdary read the ra' and ba' in the words He forgives and He punishes with the accusative case, implying that an is in apposition to the meaning. Talha bin Masraf read He forgives without fa as a substitute, and Al-Ja'fi and Khallad read it this way. Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “When the verse: ‘To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and if you disclose what is in yourselves’ was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it was difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then knelt down and said: O Messenger of God, we have been charged with deeds that we are able to bear: prayer, fasting, jihad, and charity, but God has revealed this verse to you and we are not able to bear it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you want to say as the People of the Book before you said: We hear and disobey? Rather, say: ‘We hear and obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination.’ When the people recited it and their tongues were on it, God revealed immediately after it: ‘The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord’. When they did that, God abrogated it and revealed: ‘No soul is charged except [with that within] its capacity’ to the end of it.” Ahmad, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a similar hadith, and he added: Then God revealed: Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake. He said: I have already done so. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. He said: I have already done so. And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us. He said: I have already done so. This story has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas through various chains of narration. Al-Bukhari and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Marwan Al-Asfar, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom I think was Ibn Umar: Whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, he said: The verse that follows it abrogated it. Abd Ibn Humayd and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ali something similar. Saeed Ibn Mansour, Ibn Jarir and Al-Tabarani narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Aisha. From the above, it becomes clear to you the weakness of what Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, that he said: It was revealed regarding concealing testimony, for if it had been like that, the matter would not have been so difficult for the Companions. In any case, after these hadiths that clearly state abrogation and the abrogating verse, there is no room left to contradict it. What supports this is what is proven in the two Sahihs and the four Sunans from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has forgiven my nation for what their souls have thought about, as long as they do not speak about it or act upon it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: Every servant who has an evil thought or sin and thinks about it, God will hold him accountable in this world, fearing and grieving, and his anxiety will be intense, but he will not attain any of that, just as he had an evil thought but did not act upon it. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on her authority, and the hadiths that have previously stated abrogation refute this. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:My scribes did not write down your deeds except what was apparent of them. As for what you kept secret in your souls, I will hold you accountable for it today, so I will forgive whomever I wish and punish whomever I wish. This is refuted by what was mentioned above.
2:285: His statement: 285- In what was revealed to him from his Lord meaning in all that God revealed and the believers is in apposition to the Messenger, and his statement: Everyone meaning of the Messenger and the believers believed in God and it is possible that his statement: and the believers is a subject. And his statement: Everyone is a second subject. And his statement: Believed in God is the predicate of the second subject, and it and its predicate are the predicate of the first subject, and the individuals of the pronoun in his statement: Believed in God with its reference to all the believers, because the intended meaning is to clarify the belief of each individual of them without considering the group as that was considered in the statement of God Almighty: And all came to Him humbled. Al-Zajjaj said: When God, the Most High, mentioned in this Surah the obligation of prayer and zakat, and explained the rulings of Hajj, the rulings of menstruation, divorce and ila’, and the stories of the prophets, and explained the ruling on usury, He mentioned His glorification by saying: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Then He mentioned the belief of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then He mentioned the belief of the believers in all of that, so He said: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord. That is, the Messenger believed in all of these things that were mentioned, and likewise all the believers believed in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. It was said that the reason for its revelation was the verse before it. This has been explained previously. His saying: and His angels means: in terms of their being His honored servants who are intermediaries between Him and His prophets in revealing His books. His saying: and His books because they include the laws by which His servants worship. His saying: and His messengers because they are the ones who convey to His servants what was revealed to them. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr and Ibn Amir, read and his books in the plural. They read in At-Tahrim and his books and Ibn Abbas read here and his books and Hamza and Al-Kisa'i also read it. It was narrated from him that he said: The book is more than the books. The author of Al-Kashshaf explained it and said: Because if what is meant by the singular is the genus and the nationality is present in all the singulars of the genus, then nothing is excluded from it. As for the plural, only what has the nationality of the plurals is included under it. End. Whoever wants to understand the matter, let him refer to the long explanation of At-Talkhees when the author of At-Talkhees said: The comprehensiveness of the singular is more comprehensive. The majority read and his messengers with a damma on the seen. Abu Amr read with a light seen. The majority read we do not separate with a noon. The meaning is: they say: we do not separate. The meaning is: they say: we do not separate. Saeed bin Jubair, Yahya bin Ya'mar, Abu Zur'ah, Ibn Omar, Ibn Jarir, and Ya'qub read we do not separate with a lower yaa. He said: Between one and did not say between individuals because one includes both the individual and the plural as in the saying of God the Almighty: There is none of you who can prevent Him from it so He described it by saying: preventing because it is in the meaning of the plural, and this sentence may be in the accusative case as a state or as another predicate for His saying: all. And His saying: Of His messengers is more apparent in the place of concealment to guard against the assumption that the angels are included in the ruling, or to indicate the reason for not differentiating between them. And His saying: And they said, We hear and obey is conjoined with His saying: Believe. And even though it is for the singular and this is for the plural, it is permissible in view of the meaning: that is, we perceived it with our hearing and understood it and obeyed what is in it. And it was said that the meaning of heard is: we answered your call. His saying: Your forgiveness is a source accusative with an implied verb: that is, forgive your forgiveness. This was said by Al-Zajjaj and others, and hearing and obedience were presented before the request for forgiveness because the means precede the one to whom it is sought.
2:286: His saying: 286- God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. The charge is the command to do what is difficult and costly, and capacity is the energy, and capacity is what is sufficient for a person and does not constrict him, and this is an independent sentence that came after the Almighty's saying: And if you disclose what is in your souls, the verse to reveal the distress of the Muslims, and to remove the hardship on them in charging what is in their souls, and it is like His saying, the Almighty: God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship. His saying: For her is what she has earned, and against her is what she has acquired contains encouragement and intimidation: that is, for her is the reward for what she has earned of good, and against her is the burden of what she has acquired of evil. He mentioned for her and against her before the two verbs to indicate that this is for her and not for anyone else, and against her and not against anyone else. This is based on the fact that he earned is for good only, and he acquired is for evil only, as the author of Al-Kashshaf and others said. It was said that each of the two verbs applies to both matters, but the verb was repeated and the two conjugations were different to improve the structure, as in the saying of God the Almighty: “So grant respite to the disbelievers. Grant them respite a little.” His saying: Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake means: Do not impose blame upon us for the sin of these two matters that we commit. A group of commentators and others have questioned this supplication, saying that mistakes and forgetfulness are forgiven and no one is held accountable for them. So what is the meaning of supplicating with this, since it is a foregone conclusion. The answer to that is that what is meant is seeking accountability for the reasons that led to forgetfulness and error from negligence and indifference, not for the sake of forgetfulness and error, for there is no accountability for them, as is indicated by the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Error and forgetfulness have been lifted from my nation, and its explanation will come. It was said that it is permissible for a person to pray for what he has before the prayer to happen with the intention of its continuity. It was said that even if it is proven in the Shari’ah that there is no accountability for them, there is no impossibility in holding them accountable for them rationally. It was said that because they were on a great level of piety such that they did not commit a sin intentionally, but rather it happened from them by mistake or forgetfulness, so it is as if he described them by praying for that as an indication of the purity of their arena from what they will be held accountable for, as if it was said: If forgetfulness and error are among the things for which one will be held accountable, then there is no reason for them to be held accountable except error and forgetfulness. Al-Qurtubi said: There is no disagreement about this that the sin is lifted, but there is disagreement about the rulings related to that, is that lifted and nothing is required from it, or are the rulings of all of that required? There is disagreement about it, and the correct view is that it varies according to the incidents. A category is not dropped by consensus, such as fines, debts, and obligatory prayers. A category is dropped by consensus, such as retaliation and uttering a word of disbelief. A third category is disputed, such as someone who ate forgetfully in Ramadan or broke his oath absentmindedly, and what is similar to it that occurs by mistake or forgetfulness. This is known in the branches. End quote. His statement: Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us is in apposition to the sentence before it, and the repetition of the call is to indicate more supplication and resorting to God, the Most High. And burden is the heavy load that constrains its owner: that is, it confines him in his place and he cannot bear it due to its weight. What is meant by it here is the difficult task and the harsh and difficult matter. It was said that burden is the severity of the work and what was difficult for the Children of Israel in terms of killing people and cutting off the place of impurity. From this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: O He who prevents injustice from covering their hearts and bears their burdens after they have drowned It was said that Isr means transformation into monkeys and pigs, and it was said that it means the covenant, and from it is the saying of God the Almighty: And you took upon you My covenant. This disagreement goes back to explaining what is the Isr that was upon those before us, not to the meaning of Isr in the language of the Arabs, for what was mentioned above without dispute, and Isr is the rope with which loads and the like are tied, it is said: Asr ya’sir isran: to imprison, and Isr with a kasra on the hamza is from that. Al-Jawhari said: The place is Ma’sar, and the plural is Ma’asir, and the common people say Ma’asir. The meaning of the verse is that they asked God the Almighty not to burden them with the burden of obligations that He burdened the nations before them. His saying: As You burdened it is an attribute of a deleted source: meaning a burden like Your burdening it upon those before us, or an attribute of Isr: meaning a burden like the burden that You burdened those before us. His saying: Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear is also an apposition to what came before it, and the repetition of the call for the reason mentioned before this. The meaning is: Do not burden us with more work than we can bear. It was said: It is an expression for inflicting punishments, as if he said: Do not inflict punishments on us because of our negligence in maintaining those difficult duties that You imposed on us. It was said: What is meant by it is the difficult duties that are almost impossible to bear. Al-Kashshaf said: This is a confirmation of his saying: And do not place a burden on us. His saying: And pardon us means our sins. It is said that you pardoned his sin: if you left it and did not punish him for it. And forgive us means cover our sins. Forgiveness is covering. And have mercy on us means favor us with Your mercy. You are our Master means our Guardian and Supporter. This was brought out as a teaching of how they should supplicate. It was said that its meaning is: You are our Master and we are Your slaves. So support us against the disbelieving people because it is the right of the Master to support His slaves, and what is meant is the disbelievers in general, and it is an indication of raising the word of God in jihad in His cause. We have already mentioned in the explanation of the verse before this one, I mean His statement: If you disclose what is in your souls etc., that it is proven in the Sahih from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that God Almighty said after each of these supplications, I have done it. So that was evidence that He, glory be to Him, did not hold them accountable for anything of their error or forgetfulness, nor did He burden them with anything of the burden that He burdened those before them, nor did He burden them with what they could not bear, and He pardoned them and pardoned them and had mercy on them, and gave them victory over the disbelieving people, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil ibn Hibban, We make no distinction between any of His messengers, we do not disbelieve in what the messengers brought, nor do we make any distinction between any of them, nor do we lie about them. And they said, ‘We hear,’ to the Qur’an that came from God. And we obey, they acknowledged to God that they should obey Him in His commands and prohibitions. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Your forgiveness, our Lord, he said, I have forgiven you, and to You is the destination, he said, To You is the return and the destination on the Day of Judgment. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Hakim ibn Jabir, who said: When the verse, The Messenger has believed, was revealed, Gabriel said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, God has praised you and your nation well, so ask and you will be given. He said, God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, until he finished the surah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, he said: They are the believers. God has made their religion easy for them, so He said: He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty. He said: God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship. He said: So fear God as much as you are able. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: For it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has earned, he said: Of deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr regarding his statement: Except what it can bear, he said: Except what it can bear. Ibn Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak something similar. Ibn Majah, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, At-Tabarani, Ad-Darqutni, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has forgiven my nation for mistakes, forgetfulness and what they are forced to do. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, and At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Thawban, and on the authority of Ibn Umar and on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it on his authority. It was narrated by Ibn Adi in Al-Kamil and Abu Nu'aym from the hadith of Abu Bakra. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from the hadith of Umm Ad-Darda. It was narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur and Abd ibn Hamid from the hadith of Al-Hasan as a mursal, and it was narrated by Abd ibn Hamid from the hadith of Al-Sha'bi as a mursal. There is some criticism regarding the chains of transmission of these hadiths, but they strengthen each other and do not fall short of the rank of Hasan for others.
