The hadith, God said, 'I have done it,' was mentioned earlier, and it is in Sahih, and it supports these hadiths. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, a burden, he said: a covenant. Abd ibn Hamid narrated from Mujahid something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Jurayj something similar. He also narrated from Ata ibn Abi Rabah regarding His statement, and do not place a burden upon us, he said: do not transform us into apes and pigs. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse that burden is the sin for which there is no repentance or expiation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Fudayl regarding the verse, he said: When a man from the Children of Israel committed a sin, it was said to him: Your repentance is to kill yourself, so he killed himself, and the burdens were lifted from this nation. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: When these verses were revealed: Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us etc., whenever Gabriel said it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Prophet said: Amen, Lord of the worlds. Abu Ubaid narrated on the authority of Maysarah that Gabriel taught the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the ending of Surat Al-Baqarah, Amen. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal that whenever he finished reciting this surah, he would say: Amen. Abu Ubaid narrated on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr that he would say: Amen, Amen. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr who said: It is specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding this verse, he said: The Prophet of God asked his Lord for it and He gave it to him, so it was specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It has been proven by the two Sheikhs, the Sunan scholars and others on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him. Abu Ubaid, Al-Darimi, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God wrote a book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and He sent down two verses from it with which He concluded Surat Al-Baqarah. If they are recited in a house for three nights, Satan will not be able to recite them.” Ahmad, Al-Nasa’i, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated with a saheeh chain of transmission on the authority of Hudhayfah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “I was given these last verses of Surat Al-Baqarah from a treasure beneath the Throne. No prophet before me was given them.” Ahmad and Al-Bayhaqi narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Abu Dharr. Abu Ubaid, Ahmad and Muhammad ibn Nasr narrated on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “Recite these two verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah 2:‘The Messenger has believed’ until the end, for God chose Muhammad with them.” Its chain of transmission is good. Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached Sidrat al-Muntaha and was given three things: the five daily prayers, the last verses of Surat al-Baqarah, and those of his nation who do not associate anything with God will be forgiven for their sins. Al-Hakim narrated and al-Bayhaqi authenticated it in al-Shu’ab on the authority of Abu Dharr that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God concluded Surat al-Baqarah with two verses which He gave me from His treasure which is under the Throne, so learn them and teach them to your women and children, for they are prayer, Quran and supplication.” Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Two things are Quran and they heal, and they are among the things that God loves: the two verses at the end of Surat al-Baqarah.” Al-Tabarani narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Shaddad ibn Aws who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God wrote a book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and He revealed two verses from it with which He concluded Surat Al-Baqarah. If they are recited in a house for three nights, no devil will come near it.” Ibn Adi narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud Al-Ansari that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God revealed two verses from the treasures of Paradise. The Most Gracious wrote them with His hand two thousand years before He created the creation. Whoever recites them after the last ‘Isha’ prayer, they will suffice him for the night prayer.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the last verse of Surat Al-Baqarah or Ayat Al-Kursi, he would laugh and say: They are from a treasure beneath the Throne. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Muqal ibn Yasar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was given the Opening of the Book and the closing verses of Surat Al-Baqarah from beneath the Throne. Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated, and this wording is his, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “While the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was with Gabriel, he heard a creaking sound. Gabriel raised his eyes and said: ‘This is a door that has been opened in heaven that has never been opened before.’ Then an angel came down and came to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and said: ‘Receive glad tidings of two lights that have been given to you that no prophet before you was given: the Opening of the Book and the last verses of Surat al-Baqarah. You will not recite a letter from them without being given it.’” These are thirteen hadiths on the virtue of these two verses that are traced back to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). It has been narrated on the virtue of them, other than those traced back to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), on the authority of Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas`ud, Abu Mas`ud, Ka`b al-Ahbar, al-Hasan, and Abu Qilabah. The words of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) suffice without any other hadith.
3:1: It is Madani, Al-Qurtubi said unanimously, and what indicates that is that its beginning, which is eighty-three verses, was revealed about the delegation of Najran, and their arrival was in the ninth year of the Hijra. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala'il from various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Imran was revealed in Madinah. The hadiths that are common between it and this surah indicating their virtue were mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, as well as what was mentioned in the seven long surahs. Al-Tabarani narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites the surah in which Al-Imran is mentioned on Friday, God and His angels will send blessings upon him until the sun sets. Saeed bin Mansour and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha'b on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, who said: Whoever recites Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, and An-Nisa' will be recorded with God among the wise. Al-Daylami, Muhammad bin Nasr, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha'b on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud: Whoever recites Al-Imran will be rich. Ad-Darimi, Abd bin Hamid and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority that he said: Yes, the treasure of the vagabond is Al Imran, which a man recites at the end of the night. Saeed bin Mansour narrated on the authority of Abu Atif that he said: The name of Al Imran in the Torah is Taybah. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Abd al-Malik bin Umair that he said: “A man recited Al-Baqarah and Al Imran, and Ka’b said: He has recited the two surahs, for in them is the name which, if called upon by it, He will answer.” Al-Hasan, Amr ibn Ubayd, Asim ibn Abi Al-Najoud, and Abu Jaafar Al-Rawasi read Alif-Lam-Meem* God by cutting off the Alif of connection, assuming the pause on 1- Alif-Lam-Meem as they assume the pause on the names of numbers such as one, two, three, four with their connection. Al-Akhfash said: Alif-Lam-Meem* God is permissible by breaking the hamza due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a mistake and the Arabs do not say it because of its difficulty. Sibawayh mentioned in the book that the openings of the surahs that are not parallel to the singular by way of pronouncing them only by narration are quiescent at the end of the surah upon stopping, whether they are made as names or narrated in the manner of enumeration, even if it requires the meeting of two quiescent letters at the end of the surah upon stopping, whether they are made as names or narrated in the manner of enumeration, even if it requires the meeting of two quiescent letters, since that is excusable in the matter of stopping, so it is right for this opening to be stopped on and then begin with what comes after it as Al-Hasan and those with him did in their previously narrated reading. As for the opening of the meem according to the famous reading, its reason is what was narrated from Sibawayh that the meem was opened due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Kisa’i said: If the letters of spelling are met by an alif of connection, then the alif is deleted and the meem is moved with the movement of the alif. Al-Farra’ said the same. If these openings are placed in a list in the manner of enumeration, then they have no place in parsing. If they are made names for the surah, then their place is either the nominative as they are report of the subjects that are understood before them, or the accusative as the estimation of verbs that the situation requires such as remember or read or the like. What has been presented at the beginning of Surah Al-Baqarah makes it unnecessary to repeat it.
3:2: And his saying: 2- God, there is no god but He is a subject and predicate, and the sentence is resumed: meaning He is the One who deserves servitude. And the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining: two other predicates for the noble name or two predicates for a deleted subject: meaning He is the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. And it was said: that they are two attributes of the first subject or substitutes for it or for the predicate, and the interpretation of the Ever-Living and the Self-Sustaining has been presented. And a group of the companions read the standing: Omar, Ubayy bin Kaab, and Ibn Masoud.
3:3: His statement: 3- The Book has been sent down to you meaning the Qur'an. He put the adverb before the direct object to emphasize what was sent down to him, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is either a new sentence or another predicate for the first subject. His statement: With the truth meaning with honesty - and it was said: with the overwhelming argument. It is in the accusative case as a state. His statement: Confirming is another state of the Book, emphasizing it, because it can only be confirmed, so the state is not transitional at all. This is what the majority said, and some of them allowed the transition to mean that he is confirming for himself and for others. His statement: What was before it meaning of the revealed books, and it is related to his statement: confirming, and the lam is for emphasis. His statement: And He sent down the Torah and the Gospel this sentence is in the ruling of explanation for his statement: what was before it. He said here that it was revealed, and in what preceded it was revealed, because the Qur’an was revealed in parts, and the two books were revealed at once, and he did not mention in the two books who they were revealed to, and he mentioned in what preceded that the book was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the intention here is only to mention the two books, not to mention who they were revealed to.
3:4: His statement: 4- Before meaning He sent down the Torah and the Gospel before the revelation of the Book. And His statement: A guidance for the people is either a state of the two books or a reason for the revelation. What is meant by the people are the people of the two books, or something more general, because this nation worships what has not been abrogated from the laws. Ibn Furak said: A guidance for the righteous people, as He said in Surat al-Baqarah 2:A guidance for the righteous. His statement: And He sent down the Criterion meaning: the criterion between truth and falsehood, which is the Qur'an. He repeated its mention to honor it with what this other mention includes of the description of it as distinguishing between truth and falsehood. He mentioned the revelation first and the sending down second because it combines the two descriptions, for it was sent down to the lowest heaven all at once, then it was sent down from it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in stages according to the events, as mentioned previously. It was said: By the Criterion he meant all the books revealed by God Almighty to His Messengers, and it was said: He meant the Psalms because it includes good sermons, and His saying: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God means: in what is true of it being a verse from the revealed books and others, or in what is in the revealed books mentioned by placing the verses of God in the place of the pronoun referring to it, and in it is a statement of the matter by which they deserved disbelief for them because of this disbelief is a severe punishment meaning great and God is Exalted in Might no one can overcome Him Of Retribution great, and retribution is power, it is said that he took revenge on him: if he punished him because of a sin that he had committed previously.
3:5: His saying: 5- Indeed, nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven. This sentence is a resumption to show the breadth of His knowledge and His encompassing of information. He expressed His knowledge by what is on earth and in heaven, even though it is broader than that, due to the inability of His servants to know what is other than them of the places of His creation and the rest of His information. Among what is not hidden from Him is the faith of those of His creation who believe and the disbelief of those who disbelieve.
3:6: His saying: 6- It is He who shapes you in the wombs however He wills. The root of the derivation of the word image is from sarahu ila kadha meaning He inclined it towards it. So the image is inclined to indicate the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, and that among His information is that which does not enter into existence, which is the shaping of His servants in the wombs of their mothers from the sperm of their fathers however He wills of good and bad, black and white, tall and short. And how is the object of wills and the sentence is a circumstantial one. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Zubayr, who said: “A delegation of Najran, sixty riders, including fourteen of their nobles, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Haritha ibn Alqamah, Al-`Aqib, `Abd Al-Masih, and Al-Sayyid, who is Al-Ayham, spoke to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them. Then they mentioned the story in the conversation that took place between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that God revealed the beginning of Surat Al-`Imran to eighty-some verses of it.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi`, who mentioned the delegation of Najran and their dispute with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding Jesus, peace be upon him, and that God revealed, “Alif, Lam, Meem. God - there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence.” `Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, Confirming what came before it, he said: What came before it of a Book or Messenger. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Hasan. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada something similar, and he said about His statement, And He sent down the Criterion, that it is the Qur’an, distinguishing between truth and falsehood, making lawful what He made lawful and forbade what He made unlawful, and legislated in it His laws, defined His limits, and imposed His obligations, and clarified in it His explanation, and commanded obedience to Him, and forbade disobedience to Him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ja’far bin Az-Zubayr regarding His statement, And He sent down the Criterion, that is, the distinction between truth and falsehood in what the parties differed about regarding the matter of Jesus and others. And regarding His statement, Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God will have a severe punishment, and God is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution, that is, God will take revenge on those who disbelieve in His verses after having knowledge of them and understanding what He brought in them. And in His statement: Indeed, nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven meaning: He knows what they want and what they plot and what they imitate in their saying about Jesus, since they made him a lord and a god, and they have knowledge other than that, as a deception of God and disbelief in Him. It is He who shapes you in the wombs however He wills. Jesus was one of those who were shaped in the wombs, and they do not deny that, just as other children of Adam were shaped, so how can he be a god when he was in that position? Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding His statement: He shapes you in the wombs however He wills, he said: Males and females. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud and some of the Companions, regarding His statement, He shapes you in the wombs however He wills, that he said: When the sperm falls into the wombs, it flies in the body for forty days, then it becomes a clot for forty days, then it becomes a lump of flesh for forty days. When it reaches the age of creation, God sends an angel to shape it. The angel brings dust between his two fingers and mixes it with the lump of flesh, then kneads it with it and shapes it as he is commanded. He says: Male or female, wretched or happy, what is his provision, what is his lifespan, what is his legacy and what are his misfortunes? God says and the angel writes. When that body dies, it is buried where that dust was taken. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement, He shapes you in the wombs however He wills, that he said: Male or female, red or black, fully formed or not fully formed.
3:7: The Book is the Qur'an, so the lam is for the covenant, and the adverb, which is upon you, was brought forward because it indicates specificity. And his saying: 7- From it are clear verses is in accordance with the rules of Arabic, that the adverb be an advanced predicate, and it is more appropriate in meaning that it be a subject whose estimated value is from the Book, clear verses, as was mentioned in his saying: And among the people is he who says, and it is more appropriate because the intended meaning is the division of the Book into the two mentioned sections, not merely informing about them that they are from the Book, and the sentence is a circumstantial in the accusative case or a new sentence with no position. Scholars have differed in interpreting the decisive and ambiguous verses. It has been said that the decisive is that which is known to be interpreted and its meaning and explanation understood, and the ambiguous is that which no one has a way to know. Among those who said this are Jabir ibn Abdullah, Al-Sha’bi and Sufyan Ath-Thawri. They said: This is similar to the separate letters at the beginning of the surahs. It has been said: The decisive is that which does not have one interpretation, and the ambiguous is that which has several interpretations. If they are returned to one interpretation and the rest is nullified, then the ambiguous becomes decisive. It has been said: The decisive is its abrogator, its fines, its permissibles, its obligations, and what we believe in and act upon. The ambiguous is its abrogated, its likes, its divisions, and what we believe in but do not act upon. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was said that the decisive is the abrogator, and the ambiguous is the abrogated. It was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud, Qatadah and Al-Rabi’. The ambiguous is that which contains inflection, prohibition and interpretation. This was said by Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq. Ibn Atiyah said: This is the best of the sayings. It was said that the decisive is that which is self-sufficient and does not need to be referred to something else, and the ambiguous is that which is referred to something else. An-Nahhas said: This is the best that has been said about the decisive and ambiguous verses. Al-Qurtubi said: What An-Nahhas said clarifies what Ibn Atiyah chose, which is the current usage of the tongue, and that is that the decisive is a passive participle from the verb to rule, and the ruling is perfection. There is no doubt that what is clear in meaning is not ambiguous or hesitant, it is only like that due to the clarity of its individual words and the perfection of their structure, and whenever one of the two matters is missing, then the ambiguous and ambiguous result. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said that the ambiguous has aspects about which the scholars differed, which verse abrogates the other, as in the case of a pregnant woman whose husband has died, for some of the companions said that the verse of giving birth abrogated the verse of the four months and ten, and some of them said the opposite. And like their disagreement about the will to the heir, and the conflict of analogies, this is the meaning of his words. It is better to say: The decisive is that which has a clear meaning and apparent indication, either by considering itself or by considering something else, and the ambiguous is that which has a meaning that is not clear, or its indication is not apparent, neither by considering itself nor by considering something else. If you know this, you will know that this difference that we have presented is not as it should be, because the people of each opinion defined the decisive by some of its attributes, and defined the ambiguous by what is opposite to them. The explanation of this is that the people of the first opinion made the decisive what there is a way to implement, and the ambiguous what there is no way to know, and there is no doubt that the concept of the decisive and the ambiguous is broader in scope than what they mentioned, for mere obscurity or lack of appearance or possibility or hesitation necessitates similarity, and the people of the second opinion limited the decisive to what there is no possibility, and the ambiguous to what there is possibility, and there is no doubt that some of the descriptions of the decisive and the ambiguous are mentioned, not all of them, and so are the people of the third opinion, for they limited each of the two sections to those specific descriptions and not others, and the people of the fourth opinion limited each of them to some of the descriptions mentioned by the people of the third opinion, and the matter is broader than what they all said, and the people of the fifth opinion limited the decisive to the description of not being inflected or distorted, and they made the ambiguous its opposite, and they neglected what is more important than that which there is no way to implement without inflection and distortion like the openings of the disconnected surahs, and the people of the sixth opinion limited the decisive to what is established by itself, and the ambiguous to what is not established by it, and that this is some of their descriptions, and the owner of the seventh opinion, who is Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad, intended the image of agreement and made it A decisive one, and to the image of disagreement and conflict, so he made them similar, so he neglected what is the most specific description of each of them, whether it is in itself understood in meaning or not understood. His saying: They are the mother of the Book means: its origin that is relied upon, and what differs from it is referred to it. This sentence is a description of what preceded it. His saying: And other similar ones is a description of an implied omission: meaning, and other similar verses, which is the plural of other, and it was not declined because he changed it from the other, because its origin is to be like that. Abu Ubaid said: It was not declined because its singular is not declined in definite or indefinite, and Al-Mubarrad denied that. Al-Kisa’i said: It was not declined because it is a description, and Al-Mubarrad also denied that. Sibawayh said: It is not permissible for the other to be modified from the alif and lam because if it were modified from it, it would be definite. Do you not see that magic is definite in all sayings, so it would not be modified. His statement: As for those in whose hearts is deviation Deviation means inclination. From this, the sun deviated and the eyes deviated. It is also said: he deviated, yazigh, zaighan: if he abandoned the straight path. From this, the Most High said: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate. This verse includes every sect of the sects that have deviated from the truth. The reason for revelation was the Christians of Najran, as mentioned above and will come. His statement: And they follow that which is ambiguous therein means: they cling to the ambiguous verses of the Book, casting doubt on the believers by it, and they make it evidence of the innovation that they are in that deviates from the truth, as you find in every sect of innovation. They play with the Book of God greatly, and they bring from it to awaken their ignorance what is not evidence at all. His statement: Seeking discord means: seeking to interpret it in the way they want and that agrees with their corrupt doctrines. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of their seeking its interpretation is that they sought the interpretation of their resurrection and revival, so God the Almighty informed that the interpretation of that and its time are known only to God. He said: The evidence for that is His statement: Do they await anything but its interpretation? The Day its interpretation comes meaning: the Day they see what they are promised of resurrection, revival, and punishment. Those who forgot it meaning: they abandoned it, The messengers of our Lord have come with the truth meaning: We have seen the interpretation of what the messengers informed us of. His statement: And none knows its interpretation except God Interpretation can mean explanation, like their saying the interpretation of this word as such and such: meaning its interpretation. It can also mean what the matter will lead to, and its derivation is from the word the matter ended up in such and such meaning it became, and I interpreted it with an interpretation means I made it, and this sentence is a circumstantial one: meaning they follow the ambiguous in seeking its interpretation, and the fact is that none knows its interpretation except God. The scholars have differed regarding His statement: and those firmly rooted in knowledge is it a statement separated from what preceded it or conjoined with what preceded it? So the waw is for all of them, so what the majority say is that it is cut off from what precedes it, and that the speech is complete when he says: except God. This is the saying of Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abu al-Shatha’, Abu Nahik, and others. It is the school of thought of al-Kisa’i, al-Farra’, al-Akhfash, Abu Ubaid, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated it from Malik and chose it. Al-Khattabi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud and Ubayy ibn Ka`b, who said: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he arranged the firmly grounded in knowledge on what preceded it, and claimed that they knew it. He said: Some of the linguists provided evidence for him, saying: Its meaning is that those firmly grounded in knowledge know it, saying: We believe in it. He claimed that the position of they say is in the accusative case as a state, and most linguists reject it and reject it, because the Arabs do not imply the verb and the object together, and do not mention a state except with the appearance of the verb. So if the verb does not appear, it is not a state. If that were permissible, it would be permissible to say: `Abdullah is riding, meaning: `Abdullah came riding. But that is only permissible with the mention of the verb, like his saying: `Abdullah speaks, reconciling between people, so he was reconciling a state, like the poet’s saying: Abu `Amr recited to me. He said: Abu al-`Abbas Tha`lab recited to us: I sent a man to Kalka who walks short and stands tall So the statement of the majority of scholars with the help of the grammarians’ schools of thought is more appropriate than the statement of Mujahid alone. Also, it is not permissible for God, the Exalted, to deny something from creation and attribute it to Himself, so that He would have a partner in that. Do you not see His, the Exalted’s, saying: “Say: None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except God,” and His, the Exalted’s, saying: None reveals it at its time except Him, and His, the Exalted’s, saying: Everything will perish except His Face. So all of this is something that God, the Exalted, has kept to Himself and no one else shares it with Him. Likewise His, the Exalted’s, saying: And none knows its interpretation except God. If the waw in His, the Exalted’s, statement was for the sake of sequence, there would be no benefit to His statement: All is from our Lord. End quote. Al-Qurtubi said: What Al-Khattabi narrated that no one else said what Mujahid said. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that the word the firm is conjoined with the name of God, the Exalted, and that they are included in the knowledge of the ambiguous, and that with their knowledge of it they say: We believe in it. Al-Rabi’, Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn al-Zubayr, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and others said: They say according to this interpretation is in the accusative case as a state of those firmly rooted, as he said: The wind cries with sorrow and lightning flashes in the clouds This verse has two possible meanings. It is possible that and the lightning is the subject and the predicate glimmers according to the first interpretation, so it is cut off from what precedes it. It is possible that it is conjoined with the wind, and glimmers is in the place of a state according to the second interpretation, i.e. glimmering. It is clear from you that what Al-Khattabi said in the face of the impossibility of his saying: They say, ‘We believe in it’ being a state, because the Arabs do not mention a state except with the appearance of the verb until the end of his speech, is not complete except on the assumption that there is no verb here, and this is not the case. The verb is mentioned, which is his saying: And he does not know its interpretation, but the state came from the conjoined, which is his saying: and the firm ones, without the conjoined to it, which is his saying: except God. And that is permissible in the Arabic language. And something similar to it came in the Noble Book. And from this is the saying of the Most High: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes until His saying: And those who came after them say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us’ the verse, and like His saying: And your Lord came with the angels, rank upon rank meaning: And the angels came, rank upon rank. But here there is another obstacle to making that a state, which is that restricting their knowledge of its interpretation to the state of their saying: We believe in it is not correct, because those who are firmly grounded in knowledge, according to the view of the validity of the conjunction with the noble name, know it in every state, not in this particular state. So this necessitated making His saying: And those firmly grounded in knowledge a subject whose predicate is: they say. And among the evidence that those who say the conjunction used is that God, the Most High, praised them for being firmly grounded in knowledge, so how could He praise them when they do not know that? The answer to this is that their abandonment of seeking knowledge that God did not permit, nor did He make a way for His creation to do it, is due to their being firmly rooted, because they knew that this was something that God had kept to Himself in knowledge, and that those who follow Him are the ones in whose hearts is deviation. This is sufficient for you as being firmly rooted. The root of steadfastness in the Arabic language is: to be fixed in something, and everything that is fixed is firmly rooted. Its root in bodies is that horses or trees are firmly rooted in the ground, and from this is the saying of the poet: I have a deep-rooted love for Laila in my heart that no sign of her will change. These people were steadfast in complying with what came to them from God, of abandoning following the ambiguous, and referring its knowledge to God, the Most High. Some of the people of knowledge took a middle position between the two positions and said: Interpretation is used and intended in the Qur’an to mean two things: One of them is interpretation in the sense of the reality of a thing and what its matter leads to, and from that is His statement: This is the interpretation of my vision, and His statement: Do they await anything but its interpretation on the Day its interpretation comes? That is, the reality of what they were informed of regarding the matter of the Resurrection. If this is what is meant by interpretation, then the pause is on the majesty, because the realities and essence of matters are known only to God, the Most High, and His statement: and those firmly rooted in knowledge is the subject, and they say, ‘We believe in it’ is its predicate. If the other meaning is intended by the interpretation, which is explanation, clarification, and expression of something, as in his saying: Inform us of its interpretation, meaning: its explanation, then the pause is at and those firmly rooted in knowledge, because they know and understand what they are addressed with in this regard, even if they do not encompass knowledge of the realities of things as they are. Based on this, they say, ‘We believe in it,’ is a state of them. Ibn Furak preferred that those firmly rooted know its interpretation, and he elaborated on that, and so did a group of the most knowledgeable commentators who preferred that. Al-Qurtubi said: Our Sheikh Abu al-Abbas Ahmad bin Omar said: This is correct, because calling them firmly rooted indicates that they know more than the clear verses, the knowledge of which is equal to that of all who understand the speech of the Arabs. In what is their firmness if they only know what everyone knows? However, the ambiguous varies, and some of it is not known at all, such as the matter of the soul and the Hour, which God has kept to Himself in knowledge, and no one engages in knowledge of this. So whoever among the skilled scholars said that the firmly rooted do not know the ambiguous verses, he only meant this type. As for what can be interpreted in various ways in the language, it is interpreted and its correct interpretation is known, and any incorrect interpretation in it is removed. Know that the most significant cause of this confusion in the articles of scholars is the difference in their statements regarding the meaning of the decisive and the ambiguous. We have presented to you what is correct in their investigation, and here we will add to you clarification and explanation, so we say: Among what is true of the interpretation of the ambiguous that we have presented are the openings of the surahs, for their meaning is not clear, nor is their indication apparent, not with respect to themselves because no one who knows the language of the Arabs and knows the custom of the Shari’ah knows what the meaning of Alif Laam Meem, Alif Laam Meem, Ha Mim, Ta Seen, Ta Seen Meem and the like is known, because he will not find their explanation in any of the speech of the Arabs or the speech of the Shari’ah, so their meaning is not clear, neither in themselves nor in terms of another matter that explains and clarifies them, and similar to that are the words transferred from the language of the non-Arabs, and the strange words that do not exist in the language of the Arabs or in the custom of the Shari’ah what clarifies them, and similarly what God has kept to Himself in His knowledge, such as the spirit and what is in His saying: Indeed, with God is knowledge of the Hour to the end of the verse, and similarly what its indication is not clear, neither in terms of itself nor in terms of something else, such as the occurrence of a thing as being possible for two matters with a possibility that does not outweigh one another in terms of that thing in itself, and that is Such as ambiguous words without any clarification of the intended meaning of that ambiguous matter from the external matters, and also the occurrence of two completely contradictory proofs such that one cannot be preferred over the other, neither by considering itself nor by considering another matter that gives it preference. As for what is clear in meaning by considering itself, such as being known in the language of the Arabs or in the custom of the Shari’ah or by considering something else, such as the ambiguous matters whose explanation has been mentioned elsewhere in the Noble Book or in the pure Sunnah, or the matters whose meanings are contradictory, then what has been mentioned that clarifies the stronger of them from the weaker of them has been mentioned elsewhere in the Book or the Sunnah or other well-known preferential matters among the people of the principles that are accepted by the people of fairness, then there is no doubt or suspicion that these are from the decisive and not from the ambiguous, and whoever claims that they are from the ambiguous has confused the truth, so tighten your hands on this, for you will be saved by it from the difficulties and pitfalls that have befallen people in this situation until every group has called what indicates what it has gone to decisive and what indicates what the one who opposes it goes to ambiguous, especially the people of theology, and whoever denies this should refer to their writings. Know that there is evidence in the Noble Book that it is all decisive, but not in this sense mentioned in this verse, but in another sense. Among these is the saying of God the Almighty: A Book whose verses are decisive and His saying: These are the verses of the Wise Book. What is meant by decisive in this sense is that it has correct words, sound meanings, and is superior in eloquence and fluency to all speech. There is also evidence that it is all ambiguous, but not in this sense mentioned in this verse that we are trying to interpret, but in another sense. Among these is the saying of God the Almighty: A Book that is allegorical. What is meant by ambiguous in this sense is that it resembles one another in soundness, eloquence, beauty, and rhetoric. The scholars have mentioned benefits for the occurrence of ambiguous verses in the Qur’an: one of them is that reaching the truth, even though they are present in it, is more difficult and arduous, and this necessitates more reward for those who extract the truth, who are the diligent imams. Al-Zamakhshari, Al-Razi, and others have mentioned aspects, this is the best of them, and the rest are not worth mentioning here. His statement: All is from our Lord contains an implied pronoun referring to the two sections, the definitive and the ambiguous: that is, all of it, or the omitted non-pronoun: that is, each one of them. This is part of the completion of the statement mentioned before it. And his statement: And none will remember except those of understanding means the pure intellects: and they are the ones firmly grounded in knowledge, who stop at its ambiguous parts, who know its definitive parts and act according to what God has guided them to in this verse.
3:8: And His saying: 8- Our Lord, do not let us deviate etc. is from the completion of what the firmly grounded say: that is, they say we believe in it, all of it is from our Lord, and they say: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate. Ibn Kaysan said: They asked that their hearts not deviate, similar to the saying of the Most High: So when they deviated, God made their hearts deviate. It is as if when they heard His saying, the Most High: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that which is ambiguous thereof, they said: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate by following that which is ambiguous after You have guided us to the truth by what You have permitted us to do of working with the clear verses, and the circumstance, which is His saying: after, is in the accusative case with His saying: do not let us deviate. His saying: And grant us from Yourself mercy means that which is from You. Min is for the beginning of the goal, wa-l-dan with the opening of the lam, the damma of the dal, and the sukoon of the nun. There are other languages of this, the most eloquent of which is that it is an adverb of place and it may be added to time. The indefiniteness of mercy is for glorification, meaning a great and vast mercy. His saying: Indeed, You are the Giver is an explanation for the question or for giving to the one being asked.
3:9: And His statement: 9- Our Lord, indeed You will gather mankind meaning You will raise them up and revive them after their dispersion for a Day which is the Day of Resurrection, meaning for the reckoning of a Day or for the recompense of a Day, assuming the addition is deleted and the addition to it is placed in its place. His statement: There is no doubt about it meaning: in its occurrence and the occurrence of what is in it of reckoning and recompense. The explanation of doubt has been presented, and the whole of His statement: Indeed, God does not fail in His promise is to explain the meaning of what preceded it: meaning that fulfilling a promise is the affair of God, glory be to Him, and failing to do so contradicts divinity, just as it contradicts and contrasts it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The clear verses are its abrogators, its lawful and unlawful, its limits and its obligations, what we believe in and act upon, and the ambiguous verses are its abrogated, its beginning and end, its likes and its divisions, what we believe in but do not act upon. Saeed Ibn Mansour, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said regarding his statement: Among its verses are clear verses he said: The three verses at the end of Surat Al-An’am are clear verses: Say, ‘Come,’ and the two verses after it. In a narration from him narrated by Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim regarding his statement: Clear verses he said: From here Say, ‘Come,’ to three verses, and from here And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him to three verses after it. I say: May God have mercy on Ibn Abbas, how little is the benefit of these words attributed to him. So specifying three verses or ten or one hundred from all the verses of the Qur’an and describing them as decisive is of no benefit, as the decisive verses are the majority of the Qur’an according to all opinions, even according to his statement that is close to what is transmitted from him that the decisive verses abrogate it and make it permissible, etc. So what is the meaning of specifying those verses from the end of Surat Al-An’am? And Abd bin Hamid narrated from him that he said: The decisive verses are the permissible and the forbidden. And the predecessors had many opinions that go back to what we mentioned at the beginning of this research. And Ibn Jarir Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation meaning the people of doubt, so they interpret the decisive verses as ambiguous and the ambiguous verses as decisive, and they confuse, so God confuses them. And none knows its interpretation except God he said: Its interpretation on the Day of Resurrection, none knows it except God. And Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Mas’ud deviation he said: doubt. In the two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Aisha, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘It is He who has sent down to you the Book’ until His saying: ‘But as for those in whose hearts is deviation’ until His saying: ‘People of understanding’, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If you see those who dispute therein, they are the ones meant, so beware of them.’ And in another version: ‘But if you see those who follow that which is ambiguous therein, they are the ones whom God has named, so beware of them.’ This is the wording of Al-Bukhari, and the wording of Ibn Jarir and others: ‘But if you see those who follow that which is ambiguous therein and those who dispute therein, they are the ones meant by God, so do not sit with them.’” And ‘Abd ibn Humayd, ‘Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Abu Umamah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding His saying: ‘But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that which is ambiguous therein,’ he said: They are the Khawarij. Ibn Jarir and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that he authenticated on the authority of Ibn Masoud on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The first Book was revealed from one chapter and in one dialect. The Qur’an was revealed in seven dialects: prohibiting, commanding, lawful, unlawful, clear, ambiguous, and parables. So make lawful what it makes lawful and forbid what it forbids, do what you are commanded to do and refrain from what you are forbidden to do, learn from its parables, act upon its clear, believe in its ambiguous, and say: We believe in it, all of it is from our Lord.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Masoud as a continuation of the narration. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Salamah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abdullah ibn Masoud and mentioned something similar. Al-Bukhari narrated in At-Tarikh on the authority of Ali with a weak chain of transmission something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Dawud narrated something similar in Al-Masahif on the authority of Ibn Masoud. Ibn Jarir and Abu Ya'la narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The Qur'an was revealed in seven letters, and disputing about the Qur'an is disbelief. Whatever you know, act upon it, and whatever you do not know, refer it to its scholar." Its chain of transmission is sound. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu'ab on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in which it says: And follow the clear verses and believe in the ambiguous verses. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Tawus, who said: Ibn Abbas used to recite it: "And none knows its interpretation except God. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, 'We believe in it.'" Ibn Abi Dawud narrated in Al-Masahif on the authority of Al-A'mash, who said regarding Abdullah's recitation: "And the true interpretation of it is with God. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, 'We believe in it.'" Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Shathaa and Abu Nahik who said: You pray this verse while it is disconnected: “And none knows its interpretation except God. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it. All is from our Lord.’” So their knowledge ended with what they said. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Urwah who said: Those firmly rooted in knowledge do not know its interpretation, but they say, “We believe in it. All is from our Lord.” Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Umar bin Abdul Aziz something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf on the authority of Abu who said: The Book of God, whatever is clear, act upon it, and whatever is unclear to you, believe in it and entrust it to its scholar. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: The Qur’an has a beacon like a beacon on the road, so whatever you know, hold fast to it, and whatever is unclear to you, leave it. He also narrated on the authority of Muadh something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The interpretation of the Qur’an is of four types: an interpretation that scholars know, an interpretation that people are excused for not knowing, whether it is permissible or forbidden, an interpretation that the Arabs know in their language, and an interpretation whose interpretation is known only to God, and whoever claims to know it is a liar. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: The Qur’an was revealed in seven letters: permissible and forbidden, no one is excused for not knowing it, an interpretation that the Arabs interpret, an interpretation that the scholars interpret, and ambiguous verses that only God knows, and whoever claims to know it is a liar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: I am one of those who know its interpretation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi on his authority regarding His statement: They say, ‘We believe in it’ We believe in the decisive verses and believe in them, and we believe in the ambiguous verses but do not believe in them, and it is all from God. Ad-Darimi narrated in his Musnad and Nasr Al-Maqdisi in Al-Hujjah on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar that a man called Dhubay’ came to Madinah and began to ask about the ambiguous verses of the Qur’an. So Omar sent for him and prepared palm clusters for him. He said: Who are you? He said: I am Abdullah Dhubay’. He said: And I am Abdullah Omar. Omar took a cluster of those clusters and beat him until his head bled. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, that is enough. What I felt in my head has gone away. Ad-Darimi also reported it from another chain of transmission, in which it says: He beat him three times, leaving him alone each time until he recovered, then he beat him. Ibn Asakir reported the original story in his history on the authority of Anas. Ad-Darimi and Ibn Asakir reported that Omar wrote to the people of Basra not to sit with Dhubay’. This story was reported by a group of people. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and At-Tabarani reported on the authority of Anas, Abu Umamah, Wathilah ibn Al-Asqa’ and Abu Ad-Darda’ that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about those who are firmly grounded in knowledge. He said: He who keeps his oath, speaks truthfully, keeps his heart straight, and keeps his stomach and private parts chaste, then he is one of those firmly grounded in knowledge. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Yazid Al-Azdi on the authority of Anas, with a similar chain of transmission. Abu Dawud and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Disputing about the Qur’an is disbelief. Nasr Al-Maqdisi narrated in Al-Hujjah on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out and from behind his room were some people who were disputing about the Qur’an. He came out with his cheeks red as if they were dripping blood. He said: ‘O people, do not argue about the Qur’an, for those who came before you went astray because of their arguments. The Qur’an was not revealed to contradict some of it, but it was revealed to confirm some of it. So whatever is clear in it, act upon it, and whatever is ambiguous in it, believe in it.’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: ‘O Changer of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.’ Then he recited: ‘Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us’” 10:10. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from her, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this, but longer. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Aisha, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this. Similar to this has been narrated through other chains of transmission. Ibn Al-Najjar narrated in his history, regarding the statement of God, Our Lord, You will surely gather mankind for a Day, the verse, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad Al-Khalidi, who said: It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Whoever recites this verse over something that he has lost, God will restore it to him. And he should say after reciting it: O Gatherer of mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt, gather me and my wealth, for You are over all things competent.”
3:10: Those who disbelieve are meant to be the disbelievers - and it was said: the delegation of Najran, and it was said: Qurayzah, and it was said: An-Nadir, and it was said: the polytheists of the Arabs. As-Salami read lan yaghni with a dhammah, and Al-Hasan read it with the final ya’ as a relief. His statement: 10- From God something meaning: from His punishment something of enrichment, and it was said: the word min means with: meaning it does not avail anything with God, Abu Ubaid said, and it was said: it means a substitute. The meaning is a substitute for God’s mercy, and this is far-fetched. His statement: And those are the fuel of the Fire Fuel: is the name for firewood, and we have already discussed it in Surat Al-Baqarah. That is: they are the firewood of Hell with which it is set ablaze, and they are the subject, and fuel is its predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of those, or they are a disjunctive pronoun, and in both cases the sentence is resumed and confirms His statement: Their wealth will not avail them the verse. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Talha bin Masraf read waqood with a damma on the waw, and it is a verbal noun. Likewise, waqood with a fatha on the waw in the reading of the majority may be a name for firewood, as mentioned above, so it does not need to be estimated. It may also be a verbal noun, because it is one of the verbal nouns that come in the form of fa’ul, so it needs to be estimated: that is, they are the people of the fuel of the fire.
3:11: His saying: 11- Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh Perseverance: diligence. It is said: A man persevered in his work, he persevered, diligently: if he was serious and worked hard. The two who are diligent are night and day. Perseverance: habit and affair. From this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: As usual, from Umm Al-Huwairith before her and her neighbor Umm Al-Rabab in Masal What is meant here is like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and their condition. They differed about the Kaf. It was said: It is in the nominative case, and its meaning is that the people of Pharaoh were accustomed to it with Moses. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is that the Arabs disbelieved as the people of Pharaoh disbelieved. Al-Nahhas said: It is not permissible for the Kaf to be related to disbelieve, because disbelieve is included in the relative clause. It was said: It is related to God taking them, meaning He took them as He took the people of Pharaoh. It was said: It is related to it will not avail them, meaning it did not avail them at all, as it did not avail the people of Pharaoh. It was said: The agent is an implied verb from the word fuel, and the simile is in the burning itself. They said: It is supported by the Almighty’s saying: “The Fire will be exposed to them morning and evening. And on the Day the Hour will come, [say], ‘Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment.’” The first statement is what the majority of scholars said, including Al-Azhari. His saying: And those before them means before the people of Pharaoh from the disbelieving nations: meaning, as was the habit of those before them. His statement: They denied Our signs, so God seized them. It is possible that he means the recited signs, or the recited signs, or the signs that are in the accusative case to indicate monotheism, and it is correct to mean all of them. The sentence is a statement and explanation of their habit, and it is possible that it is in the accusative case as a state of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, with the omission of had: meaning the habit of these is like the habit of those, they denied, etc. And his statement: for their sins means for all of their sins, one of which was their denial.
3:12: His saying: 12- Say to those who disbelieve It was said: They are the Jews, and it was said: They are the polytheists of Mecca, and the reason for the revelation of the verse will come. And His saying: You will be overcome was read with the upper and lower letters, as well as: You will be gathered. And God fulfilled His promise by killing Banu Qurayzah, expelling Banu Nadir, conquering Khaybar, and imposing the jizya on the rest of the Jews, and praise be to God. His saying: And what an evil resting place may be part of the statement that God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them, and it may be that the sentence is a new sentence to intimidate and terrify.
3:13: His statement: 13- It has already been a sign for you meaning: a great sign indicating the truth of what I say to you, and this sentence is the answer to an omitted oath, and it is part of the commanded statement to confirm the meaning of what preceded it, and he did not say was because the feminine is not real. Al-Farraa said: He mentioned the verb in order to separate it from the noun by saying: for you. What is meant by the two groups are the Muslims and the polytheists when they feared God on the day of Badr. His statement: A group fighting in the way of God the majority read with the nominative case of group. Al-Hasan and Mujahid read group and disbeliever in the genitive case, so the nominative case is for the report of the omitted subject, meaning: one of them is a group. His statement: fighting is in the place of the nominative case as an attribute, and the genitive case is in apposition to his statement: two groups. His statement: and another meaning: and another group of disbelievers. Ibn Abi Ubla read them both in the accusative case. Tha'lab said: It is in the state: meaning they met different, a believer and a disbeliever. Al-Zajjaj said: The accusative is by estimation of I mean, and the group of people was called a group to which one cannot return: that is, one who returns in times of hardship. Al-Zajjaj said: The group: the division is taken from fawwat ra’su bis-sif: if you cut it off, and there is no disagreement that what is meant by the two groups are the two fighting on the day of Badr, but the disagreement occurred in who is addressed by this speech, so it was said: the believers are addressed by it, and it was said: the Jews. The benefit of the speech to the believers is to strengthen and encourage their souls, and its benefit if it is with the Jews is the opposite of the benefit intended by the speech to the Muslims. His statement: They see them twice their number Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: The vision in this verse is the vision of the eye, and therefore it is transitive to one object, and this is indicated by his statement: the vision of the eye and what is meant is that the polytheists see the Muslims twice the number of the polytheists or twice the number of the Muslims, and this is according to the reading of the majority with the lower ya, and Nafi’ read it with the upper ya. And his statement: Two of them is accusative in the state. The majority of scholars have said that the subject of you see, O Muslims, the polytheists, twice as many as they are in number, and in it, after God multiplies the polytheists in the eyes of the believers, and He has informed us that He has diminished them in the eyes of the believers, the meaning is that you see, O Muslims, the polytheists, twice as many as you are in number, and they were three times as many, so God diminished the polytheists in the eyes of the Muslims and made them see them twice as many as me in their number, so that their souls may be strengthened. They knew that one hundred of them would overcome two hundred of the infidels, and it is possible that the pronoun in twice as many refers to the Muslims: that is, you see, O Muslims, yourselves, twice as many as you are in your number, so that your souls may be strengthened by that. Those who have adopted the first interpretation have said: I mean that the subject of the vision is the polytheists, and that they saw the Muslims twice as many as me in their number, that this does not contradict what is in Surat al-Anfal, where God the Most High says: and diminish you in their eyes, rather they were first diminished in their eyes so that they would meet them and be bold with them, but when they met them, they became many in their eyes until they were defeated. His saying: The vision of the eye is a source confirming his saying: You will see them meaning: a clear, obvious vision in which there is no ambiguity. And God supports with His victory whom He wills meaning He strengthens whom He wills to strengthen, and among that is the support of the people of Badr with that vision. Indeed in that meaning in seeing a lot of little is a lesson a verb from crossing like sitting is from sitting. What is meant is admonition, and the indefiniteness is for glorification: meaning a great lesson and a serious admonition. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Like the way of the people of Pharaoh, he said: Like the actions of the people of Pharaoh. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on his authority: Like a deed. Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’: Like their way. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, suffered from the people of Badr what he suffered and returned to Medina, he gathered the Jews in the market of Banu Qaynuqa’ and said: O group of Jews, accept Islam before God afflicts you with what afflicted the Quraysh. They said: O Muhammad, do not be deceived by killing a group of people who were ignorant and did not know how to fight. By God, if you had fought us, you would have known that we are the people and that you have not encountered the likes of us. Then God revealed: ‘Say to those who disbelieve, ‘You will be overcome. ’” until His statement: Those of insight. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Ishaq, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: Phinehas the Jew said and mentioned something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, There has certainly been for you a sign, a lesson and reflection. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, “There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met. One company was fighting in the cause of God,” the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Badr. And the other was disbelieving, the group of the disbelieving Quraysh. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated that this verse was revealed regarding the people of Badr. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ regarding his statement, There has certainly been for you a sign, he said: There has certainly been for you in these people a lesson and reflection. God supported them and gave them victory over their enemy. On the day of Badr, the polytheists numbered nine hundred and fifty men, and the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were three hundred and thirteen men. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding the verse, he said: This was on the day of Badr. We looked at the polytheists and saw that they had become weaker than us, then we looked at them and did not see them increase over us by a single man. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, saying: It was revealed to alleviate the burden on the believers on the day of Badr. They were three hundred and thirteen men on that day, and the polytheists were twice as many, six hundred and twenty-six. So God supported the believers.
3:14: His statement 14- Beautified for people etc.: A renewed statement to explain the insignificance of what souls enjoy in this world, and the beautifier is said to be God, the Most High, and this is what Omar said as narrated by Al-Bukhari and others, and this supports the statement of God, the Most High: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them. It was said: The beautifier is Satan, and this is what Al-Hasan said, narrated by Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim from him. Ad-Dahhak read adornment in the active form. The majority read it in the passive form. What is meant by people is the species. Desires is the plural of desire, and it is the inclination of the soul towards what it wants. What is meant here are the desired things, expressed by desires, exaggerating the fact that they are desirable or belittling them because they are considered despicable by rational people as being characteristics of animal natures, and the reason for God, the Most High, beautifying them is to test His servants as He stated in the other verse. His saying: Of women and sons is in the place of the state: that is, He has made attractive to people the love of desires when they are of women and sons, etc. And He began with women because of the large number of souls turning to them because they are the snares of Satan, and He specified sons without daughters because of the lack of consistency in loving them. Qintar is the plural of qintar, which is a name for a lot of money. Al-Zajjaj said: Qintar is taken from the knotting and tightening of something: the Arabs say qintart something: if you tightened it, and from this the qintarah was named for its tightness. There is disagreement in its estimation according to the sayings of the predecessors that will come, God willing. They disagreed about the meaning of muqantara. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: It means doubled. Qintar said: three, and muqantara is nine. Al-Farra’ said: Qintar is the plural of qintar, and muqantara is the plural of plural, so it is nine qintars. It was said: muqantara is the multiplied, and it was said: the complete as it is said: a scattered pearl, and thousands composed, and Makki said and al-Harawi narrated it. Ibn Kaysan said: muqantara is not less than seven qintars. And his saying: Of gold and silver is a statement of the qintars, or the state of and the marked horses it is said that they are the ones that graze in the meadows and pastures, it is said: the animal or the sheep is samt: if it is let out, and it is said: it is prepared for jihad, and it is said: it is the beautiful, and it is said: the marked, from the mark: meaning that which is marked to distinguish it from others. Ibn Faris said in Al-Mujmal the marked: the sent and its riders are on it. Ibn Kaysan said: the bleating. And the livestock are the camels, cows and sheep, so if you say yes, then it is the camels specifically, Al-Farra’ and Ibn Kaysan said, and from it is the saying of Hassan: And there was still a companion in its meadows, yes and God willing. Al-Harth: is the name for everything that is plowed, and it is a source from which the plowed is named. He says: A man plowed, if he stirred up the earth so that it fell on the earth and the crops. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Al-Harth: is searching. His saying: That is the enjoyment of worldly life means that what is mentioned is what is enjoyed then it goes away and does not remain, and in it is asceticism in this world and desire for the hereafter. And the destination: the place of return, ab, ya'ubu'iban: if he returns, and from it is the saying of Imru' al-Qais: I have traveled the world until I was satisfied with the spoils of war.
3:15: His statement 15- "Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that?" That is: Shall I inform you of something better for you than those pleasures? The vagueness of good is for emphasis. Then He explained it by saying: For those who fear God are gardens with their Lord. And with is in the accusative case as a state of gardens and it is the subject, and its predicate is for those who fear God. It is permissible for the lam to be related to good. And gardens is the predicate of an implied subject: that is, it is gardens. He specified the righteous because they are the ones who benefit from that. The explanation of His statement: Underneath which rivers flow and what follows has already been presented.
3:16: His statement 16- Those who say is a substitute for his statement for those who feared God or the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning they are those, or it is accusative of praise, and the patient ones and what follows it is an adjective for the relative pronoun on the assumption that it is a substitute, or accusative of praise and on the assumption that it is the predicate, the patient ones and what follows it is accusative of praise and the explanation of patience, truthfulness and devotion has been presented.
3:17: His saying 17- And those who seek forgiveness in the early hours of the morning are those who ask for forgiveness in the early hours of the morning, and it was said that they are the ones who pray. The early hours of the morning is the plural of sahar with the ha’ open or closed. Al-Zajjaj said: It is from the time the night ends until dawn breaks, and he specified the early hours of the morning because they are among the times when prayers are answered. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that when the verse The love of desires has been made fair-seeming to people was revealed, he said: Now, O Lord, when You have made them fair-seeming to us, then the verse Say, ‘Shall I inform you?’ was revealed. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it on his authority with the wording good and it ended with the words Say, ‘Shall I inform you of something good?’ Then he cried and said: After what, after what, after You have made them fair-seeming. Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A qintar is twelve thousand awqiyah. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith on the authority of Hammad on the authority of Asim on the authority of Abu Salih on his authority. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah on the authority of Abd al-Samad on his authority. Ibn Jarir narrated it with a chain of transmission ending with Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Kathir said: This is more authentic. Al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about the heaped qintars and he said: A qintar is one thousand awqiyah. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on his authority with the wording one thousand dinars. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A qintar is one thousand and two hundred qintar. It was narrated by Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Mu'adh ibn Jabal. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ibn Umar. It was narrated by Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri who said: A qintar is as much as a bull's hide filled with gold. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: A qintar is seventy thousand. It was narrated by Abd ibn Humayd on the authority of Mujahid. It was also narrated on the authority of Sa'id ibn Al-Musayyab who said: A qintar is eighty thousand. It was also narrated on the authority of Abu Salih who said: A qintar is one hundred pounds. It was also narrated on the authority of Qatada. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Ja'far who said: A qintar is fifteen thousand mithqals, and a mithqal is twenty-four carats. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: It is a lot of money of gold and silver. He also narrated it on the authority of Ar-Rabi’. He narrated on the authority of As-Suddi that Al-Muqantara is the one that is struck. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and the branded horses, he said: the shepherds. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: They are the shepherds and the beautiful ones that are marked. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, he said: They are the beautiful ones that are marked. They both narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Their branding is their beauty. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, he said: The branded horses are the forelock and the hooves. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His statement, the patient ones, he said: A people who were patient in obeying God and were patient in abstaining from His prohibitions. The truthful ones are a people whose intentions are true and whose hearts and tongues are upright and who are truthful in secret and in public. The obedient ones are the obedient and seek forgiveness in the early hours of the morning, the people of prayer. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated that he said: They are those who attend the dawn prayer. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded us to seek forgiveness seventy times in the early hours of the morning. Ibn Jarir and Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd on the authority of Saeed Al-Jariry that he said: It has reached us that David (peace be upon him) asked Gabriel (peace be upon him), saying: O Gabriel, which night is best? He said: O David, I do not know except that the Throne shakes at dawn. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of a group of the Companions that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God, the Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven until the last third of the night remains, and He says: Is there anyone who asks so that I may give him? Is there anyone who calls on Me so that I may answer him? Is there anyone who seeks forgiveness so that I may forgive him?”
3:18: His saying 18- God has borne witness means He has made clear and informed. Al-Zajjaj said: The witness is the one who knows and explains something, so He has shown us His Oneness through what He created and made clear. Abu Ubaidah said: God has borne witness means He has decided: that is, He knows. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is rejected from several aspects, and it was said that His evidence of His Oneness through His actions and revelation was likened to the testimony of the witness in that it is constructed. And his saying that it is with the opening of the hamza. Al-Mubarrad said: That is, then the ba was deleted as in I have ordered you good: that is, with good. Ibn Abbas read that it is with the breaking of the hamza, implying the meaning of said in witness. Abu Al-Muhallab read witnesses for God in the accusative case as a state of the patient ones and what follows it, or as praise. And the angels is in apposition to the noble name, and their testimony is their acknowledgment that there is no god but God. His saying, and those of knowledge is also connected to what came before it, and their testimony means faith from them and what is stated to people on their tongues. Based on this, the testimony must be taken to mean that it includes the testimony of God, the testimony of the angels, and those of knowledge. There is a difference of opinion about who these people of knowledge are. It was said that they are the prophets, and it was said that they are the immigrants and the helpers, as Ibn Kaysan said, and it was said that they are the believers among the People of the Book, as Muqatil said, and it was said that they are all the believers, as al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said, and this is the truth since there is no reason for specification. In that there is a great virtue for the people of knowledge, and a noble merit because of their closeness to His name and the name of His angels. What is meant by those of knowledge here are the scholars of the Book and the Sunnah and what is used to reach knowledge of them, since no attention should be paid to knowledge that has no role in the knowledge contained in the Noble Book and the pure Sunnah. His saying, establishing justice means fairness: that is, establishing justice in all his affairs or establishing it, and the accusative of establishing is in the state of the noble name. He said in Al-Kashaf: It is a confirmed state like his saying: And He is the truth, confirming and it is permissible to single Him out for that without what is conjoined to Him from the angels and the people of knowledge to avoid confusion. It was said: It is accusative for praise. It was said: It is an attribute of his saying: God meaning there is no god who establishes justice except Him or it is a state of his saying except Him and the factor in it is the meaning of the sentence.
