Al-Farra’ said: It is accusative for cutting because its origin is the alif and lam, so when it was cut it was made accusative like his saying there is no god except Him repetition for the purpose of emphasis. It was said that his saying that there is no god except Him is like a claim, and the latter is like a ruling. Ja’far Al-Sadiq said: The first is a description and monotheism, and the second is a drawing and instruction. His saying the Almighty, the Wise are raised as a substitute for the pronoun or as a description of the agent of witness to confirm the meaning of oneness.
3:19: His saying 19- Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. The majority read it with a kasra on in so that the sentence is a resumption confirming the first sentence, and it was read with a fatha on in. Al-Kisa'i said: He put both of them in the accusative case, meaning his saying God testifies that and his saying Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam means God testifies that it is such and that the religion in the sight of God is Islam. Ibn Kaysan said: The second in is a substitute for the first. The majority have gone to the view that Islam here means faith, even though they are originally different, as in the hadith of Gabriel in which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained the meaning of Islam and the meaning of faith, and Gabriel confirmed him, and it is in the two Sahihs and others, but each one of them may be called by the name of the other, and this has been mentioned in the Qur'an and Sunnah. His saying And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves in it is the report that the difference between the Jews and Christians was merely out of jealousy after they knew that they must enter the religion of Islam with what was included in their books revealed to them. Al-Akhfash said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: Those who were given the Scripture did not differ out of envy among themselves except after knowledge had come to them. What is meant by this difference that occurred between them is their difference over whether our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a prophet or not. It was said: Their difference over the prophethood of Jesus, and it was said: Their difference over the nature of their own souls until the Jews said: The Christians are on nothing, and the Christians said: The Jews are on nothing. His statement, And whoever disbelieves in the signs of God, meaning the signs indicating that the religion with God is Islam, then indeed, God is swift in account, so He will reward him and punish him for his disbelief in His signs. The explicitness in His statement, then indeed, God, while being the subject of concealment, is to intimidate and threaten them.
3:20: His saying 20- If they dispute with you meaning they argue with you with false doubts and distorted statements, say, 'I have submitted my face to God' meaning I have devoted my being to God. The face is used to refer to the rest of the being because it is the most noble of the human organs and the most comprehensive of the senses. It was said that the face here means the intention. His saying and whoever follows is in apposition to the agent of I submit and it is permissible for separation. Nafi'il, Abu Amr and Ya'qub confirmed the ya' in I follow according to the original and the others deleted it in accordance with the writing of the Qur'an. It is permissible for the waw to mean with and what is meant by the illiterate here are the polytheists of the Arabs. His saying Have you submitted? is a question of confirmation that includes the command: meaning submit, as Ibn Jarir and others said. Al-Zajjaj said: Have you submitted is a threat, and the meaning is: that evidence has come to you that necessitates Islam, so have you known the reason for that or not? To rebuke them and belittle their status in fairness and accepting the truth. His statement, They have been guided, means they have attained guidance, which is the greatest good fortune, and have won the good of this world and the Hereafter. But if they turn away, meaning they turn away from accepting the argument and do not act in accordance with it. Then upon you is only the conveyance, meaning upon you is only the conveyance of the message. So do not let your soul be consumed by regret over them. Conveyance is a source. His statement, And God is Seeing of His servants, contains a promise and a threat, as it implies that He is All-Knowing of all their conditions. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, establishing justice, that he said: with fairness. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam, that he said: Islam is the testimony that there is no god but God, and the acknowledgment of what He brought from God, and it is the religion of God that He prescribed for Himself and with which He sent His messengers and to which His saints guided Him, and He does not accept anything else. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, that he said: God did not send a messenger except with Islam. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, that he said: There were three hundred and sixty idols around the Kaaba, and each tribe of the Arabs had one or two idols, so God revealed, God bears witness that there is no god but Him, the verse, and all the idols fell down in prostration to the Kaaba. Ibn al-Sunni narrated in Amal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah and Abu Mansur al-Shahami in al-Arba’in on the authority of Ali who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Opening of the Book, the Throne Verse, and the two verses of Al-Imran, ‘God bears witness that there is no god but He, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge, maintaining justice. There is no god but He, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam.’” “Say: O God, Owner of the Kingdom, You give the kingdom to whomever You will and take the kingdom away from whomever You will. You honor whomever You will and abase whomever You will,” to His saying: without account. They are suspended from the Throne, between them and God is a veil. They say: O Lord, will You send us down to Your land and to those who disobey You? God said: I have sworn that none of My servants will recite them after every prayer except that I will make Paradise his abode, regardless of what he has done, or that I will reside in the Holy Sanctuary, or that I will look at him with My hidden eye seventy times every day, or that I will fulfill for him seventy needs every day, the least of which is forgiveness, or that I will protect him from every enemy and aid him against them.” Al-Daylami narrated in Musnad al-Firdaws on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, similar to this, and in it: “No servant will recite it after every prescribed prayer except that I will forgive him for what he did, and I will make him dwell in the Garden of Firdaws, and I will look at him seventy times each day and fulfill seventy of his needs, the least of which is forgiveness.” Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn al-Sunni narrated on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was in Arafat reciting this verse: ‘God bears witness that there is no god but He, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - maintaining justice. There is no god but He, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.’ He said: ‘And I am among the witnesses to that.’” The wording of al-Tabarani is: And I bear witness that there is no god but You, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Ibn Adi, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman and its weakness, Al-Khatib in his History, and Ibn Al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Ghalib Al-Qattan who said: I came to Kufa for business and passed by this verse: God bears witness that there is no god but He to His saying: Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. He said: And I bear witness to what God bears witness to, and I entrust this testimony to God, and it is a trust for me with God. He said it repeatedly. I said: He heard something about it, so I asked him, and he said: Abu Wa’il told me on the authority of Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Its owner will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and God will say: My servant made a covenant with Me, and I am the most deserving of fulfilling the covenant. Admit My servant to Paradise.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding His saying: And none differed therein except those to whom it was given, he said: The Children of Israel. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding His saying: Out of envy among themselves, he said: Envy for the world and seeking its kingdom and authority, so some of them killed each other for the world after they had been the scholars of the people. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, If they argue with you, he said: If the Jews and Christians argue with you. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And say to those who were given the Scripture, he said: The Jews and Christians, and the unlettered ones, he said: They are those who do not write.
3:21: His statement 21- By the signs of God apparently there is no difference between one verse and another and they kill the prophets without right meaning the Jews killed the prophets and they kill those who enjoin justice among the people meaning justice, and they are those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. Al-Mubarrad said: There were people from the Children of Israel to whom the prophets came and called them to God, so they killed them. Then some people from the believers arose after them and enjoined them to Islam, so they killed them. So the verse was revealed about them. And his saying, Then give them tidings of a painful punishment is the predicate of Indeed, those who disbelieve etc., and the letter fa entered it so that the relative pronoun includes the meaning of a condition. Some grammarians went to the view that the predicate is his saying, Those are the ones whose deeds have been lost, and they said that the letter fa does not enter into the predicate of in even though its subject includes the meaning of a condition, because it has been abrogated by the entry of in into it. Among them are Sibawayh and Al-Akhfash, and others went to the view that what the subject includes of the meaning of a condition is not abrogated by the entry of in into it, and like the open kasra, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: And know that whatever you gain of anything, a fifth of it is for God.
3:22: And His saying 22- Their deeds have been in vain. The explanation of vain has already been presented, and the meaning of their being in vain in this world and the hereafter is that their good deeds have no effect in this world, so that they are treated in it as people of good deeds are treated. Rather, they are treated as people of bad deeds are treated, so they are cursed and shame and humiliation have befallen them, and in the hereafter they will have the punishment of Hell.
3:23: His saying 23- Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? This is an amazement to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to everyone who can see the state of these people, who are the rabbis of the Jews. The Scripture is the Torah, and the indefinite article of the portion is for glorification: meaning a great portion, as is indicated by the position of exaggeration. Whoever says that the indefinite article is for belittling is not correct, for they did not benefit from that, and that is because they call to the Book of God those who were given a portion of it, which is the Torah: That He may judge between them, then a party of them will turn away, and the fact is that they are turning away from responding to what they are called to, despite their knowledge of it and their acknowledgment of the obligation to respond to it.
3:24: 24- And that is a reference to what was mentioned previously about turning away and turning away because they said, 'The Fire will not touch us except for a few days,' which is the amount of time they used to worship the calf. The explanation of that has already been presented. And they were deceived in their religion by what they used to invent, of lies, including this statement.
3:25: His statement 25- How then will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt? is a response to them and a refutation of the lies that deceived them: that is, how will their state be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, which is the Day of Judgment, about which no doubter will doubt its occurrence? They will inevitably occur and will be unable to repel it with tricks and lies. And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, that is, the recompense for what it has earned, with the deletion of the complement. And they will not be wronged, with any increase or decrease. What is meant is all people, indicated by every soul. Al-Kisa'i said: The lam in his statement for the Day means in. The Basrans said: The meaning is for the reckoning of the Day. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: The meaning is for what happens on the Day. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah: “I said: O Messenger of God, which people will be most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection? He said: A man who killed a prophet or a man who enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And they kill the prophets without right and they kill those who enjoin justice among the people’ until His saying: ‘And they will have no helpers.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Ubaidah, the Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets at the beginning of the day in one hour. Then one hundred and seventy men from the servants of the Children of Israel stood up and enjoined what is right upon those they killed and forbade what is wrong. They were all killed at the end of the day on that day. They are the ones whom God mentioned.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Jesus sent John, son of Zechariah, with twelve men from the disciples to teach people. He used to forbid marriage to one’s brother’s daughter. He had a niece whom he liked, so he wanted her and would fulfill a need for her every day. Her mother said to her: If he asks you about a need, say: My need is to kill John, son of Zechariah. He said: Ask for something other than this. She said: I will not ask you for anything other than this. When she refused, he ordered him to be slaughtered in a basin, and a drop of his blood came out and continued to boil until God sent Nebuchadnezzar. An old woman pointed him out, and he made it his mind to keep killing until this blood subsided. So he killed seventy thousand in one day, with one blow and one year, and it subsided. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Muqal bin Abi Maskeen regarding the verse, he said: The revelation would come to the Children of Israel and they would mention their people, but no book would come to them. Then men from among those who followed them and believed them would stand up and mention their people and they would be killed. They are the ones who command justice among the people. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Those who command justice among the people are the rulers of justice. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the school house upon a group of Jews and called them to God. Then Al-Nu’man bin Amr Al-Harith bin Zaid said to him: To what religion have you come, O Muhammad? He said: To the religion and faith of Abraham. He said: Abraham was a Jew. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Come to the Torah, for it is between us and you. But they refused, so God revealed: ‘Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are invited to the Book of God…’” 10:10. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement, a portion, he said: a share, of the Book, he said: the Torah. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, They said, ‘The Fire will not touch us except for a few days,’ he said: they mean the days in which God created Adam. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, And they were deceived in their religion by what they used to invent, when they said, We are the children of God and His beloved. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr regarding his statement, And every soul will be fully compensated, meaning: every soul, righteous or wicked, will be fully compensated for what it has earned, what it has done of good or evil, and they will not be wronged, meaning of their deeds.
3:26: His saying 26- Say O God. Al-Khalil, Sibawayh and all the Basrans said: The original form of Allahumma ya Allah, but when the word was used without the vocative letter which is ya, they replaced it with this doubled meem, so they brought two letters, which are the two meems, instead of two letters, which are ya and alif, and the damma in the ha is the damma of the singular vocative noun. Al-Farra and the Kufians believed that the original form of Allahumma ya Allah gave us security with goodness, so the two words were deleted and mixed, and the damma in the ha is the damma that was in amna, so when the hamza was deleted, the movement was transferred. Al-Nahhas said: This is a great mistake according to the Basrans, and the opinion on this is what Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said. The Kufians said: The vocative letter may enter Allahumma, and they recited in that the saying of the rajaz poet: Forgive or punish, O God And the other said: What do you have to say every time you glorify or praise God? Oh God. And the other said: Whenever I feel pain, I say, Oh God, oh God. They said: If the letter mim was a substitute for the letter of address, we would not have met. Al-Zajjaj said: This is anomalous and its speaker is not known. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Whoever says O God has called upon God with all of His names. His saying O Owner of the Kingdom means the owner of the genus of the kingdom in general, and Malik is in the accusative case according to Sibawayh as a second address, meaning O Owner of the Kingdom, and it is not permissible for him to be a description of his saying O God because the letter mim according to him prevents description. Muhammad ibn Yazid Al-Mubarrad and Ibrahim ibn Al-Sarri Al-Zajjaj said: It is a description of the name of God Almighty, and so is His saying Say, O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: This is the opinion of Al-Mubarrad, and what Sibawayh said is more correct and clearer, because it is a singular noun with a sound added to it, and sounds are not described like ghaq and the like. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is the owner of the servants and what they own, and it was said that the meaning is the owner of this world and the hereafter, and it was said that the kingdom here means prophecy, and it was said that it means dominance, and it was said that it means money and slaves. It appears that it includes everything to which the name of kingship applies without specifying it. You give the kingdom to whomever You will means: whomever You will to give it to. And You take away the kingdom from whomever You will means taking it away from him. What is meant by what He gives of the kingdom and takes away is a type of that general kingdom. His statement, And You honor whomever You will means in this world or in the Hereafter or in both. It is said, honored means: to overcome, and from this is and honored me in speech. His statement, And You humiliate whomever You will means in this world or in the Hereafter or in both. It is said, he was humiliated, humiliated means: to overcome and subjugate. His statement, In Your Hand is all good brings forward the predicate for specification: that is, in Your Hand is all good, not in the hand of anyone else. He mentioned good without evil because good is by pure grace, unlike evil, which is a reward for an action that he has reached. It was said that because every evil, in terms of being from His decree, the Most High, includes good, so all His actions are good. It was said that it was deleted as was deleted in His statement, garments that protect you from the heat and its origin is in Your Hand is all good and evil. It was said that good was specified because the situation is one of supplication. His saying, Indeed, You are capable of all things, is an explanation and confirmation of what came before.
3:27: His saying 27- "He brings the night into the day and brings the day into the night" meaning: He brings what is missing from one into the other. It was said that the meaning is that they alternate between each other and the disappearance of one is entering into the other. His saying "And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living" It was said that what is meant is bringing forth the animal while it is alive from the sperm while it is dead, and bringing forth the sperm while it is dead from the animal while it is alive. It was said that what is meant is bringing forth the bird while it is alive from the egg while it is dead, and bringing forth the egg while it is dead from the chicken while it is alive. It was said that what is meant is bringing forth the believer from the disbeliever and the disbeliever from the believer. His saying "without account" meaning: without restriction or stinginess as you say so-and-so gives without account. The baa is related to an omitted word that occurred as a state. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked his Lord to make the kingdom of Persia and Rome in his nation, so the verse was revealed. At-Tabarani and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The greatest name of God is “Say: O God, Owner of the Kingdom” until His saying without account. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Muadh “that he complained to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about a debt he owed, so he taught him to recite this verse, then say: The Most Gracious of this world and the Hereafter and the Most Merciful of them, You give from them to whomever You will and withhold from whomever You will, have mercy on me with a mercy that will make me independent of the mercy of anyone other than You, O God, enrich me from poverty and pay off my debt.” At-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Saghir on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Muadh: Shall I not teach you a supplication that you can make, if you had a debt the size of Mount Uhud on you, God would pay it off for you? So he mentioned it, and its chain of transmission is good. Some of the virtues of this verse were mentioned earlier when interpreting the words of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God bears witness that there is no god but He. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, You give dominion to whom You will, he said: Prophethood. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement, You cause the night to enter the day, the verse, he said: You take summer from winter, and you take winter from summer. And You bring forth the living from the dead, you bring forth the living man from the dead sperm. And You bring forth the dead from the living, you bring forth the dead sperm from the living man. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, You bring forth the night into the day, he said: What is missing from the day, You make it the night, and what is missing from the night, You make it the day. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Al-Suddi. Abd bin Hamid narrated something similar from Mujahid. Abd bin Hamid narrated something similar from Ad-Dahhak as well. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, You bring forth the living from the dead, he said: You bring forth the dead sperm from the living, then a living human being comes forth from the sperm. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, He brings forth the living from the dead. He said: It is the egg that comes forth from the living while it is dead, then the living comes forth from it. And Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: The palm tree from the seed, and the seed from the palm tree, and the seed from the ear of wheat, and the ear of wheat from the seed. And Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Malik. And Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The believer from the disbeliever, and the disbeliever from the believer. And the believer is a slave with a living heart, and the disbeliever is a slave with a dead heart. And Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Salman Al-Farisi. And Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on his authority, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he also narrated it on his authority, or on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa`d, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah that Khalidah bint al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Who is this? They said: Khalidah bint al-Aswad. He said: Glory be to Him who brings the living out of the dead. She was a righteous woman and her father was an unbeliever. Ibn Sa`d narrated something similar on the authority of Aishah.
3:28: His statement 28- Do not take contains a prohibition for the believers from befriending the infidels for any reason, and similar to it is the statement of the Most High: Do not take as intimates those other than yourselves 3:10, and His statement: And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed, he is one of them 3:10, and His statement: You will not find a people who believe in God 3:10, and His statement: Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies 3:10, and His statement: O you who believe, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies. His statement: Other than the believers is in the place of the state: meaning, bypassing the believers to the infidels independently or jointly, and the reference in His statement: And whoever does that is to the union indicated by His statement: Do not take 3:10, and the meaning of His statement: Then he is not from God in anything 3:10, meaning: from His guardianship in any of the things, rather he is separated from Him in every case. His saying, Except that you fear them with piety is in the form of address by way of turning away: that is, do not fear from them a matter that must be avoided, and it is an exception emptied of the most general conditions. And piety is a source in the position of the object, and its origin is waqiyah with the weight of fa`lah, the waw was changed to a ta and the ya to an alif, and Raja and Qatadah read taqiyah. And in that is evidence of the permissibility of friendship with them with fear of them, but it is apparent and not hidden. A group of the Salaf disagreed on that, and said: There is no piety after God has honored Islam. His saying, And God warns you of Himself means His holy self, and applying that to Him, glory be to Him, is permissible in the case of similarity, like His saying, You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in your soul and other things. Some of the later scholars forbade that except in the case of similarity. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is, and God warns you of it, then they dispensed with that with this and it became the usual. He said: As for his saying, You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in your soul, its meaning is, you know what is with me and what is in my reality, and I do not know what is with you or what is in your reality. Some scholars said: Its meaning is that God warns you of His punishment, like And ask the town, so the self was placed in the place of the implied, and in this verse there is a severe threat and great intimidation for His servants that they will be exposed to His punishment by befriending His enemies. Do I know?
3:29: His saying 29- “Say: If you conceal what is in your hearts” The verse contains that everything that the servant conceals and hides or shows and reveals is known to God Almighty, nothing of it is hidden from Him and not even the weight of an atom escapes Him. And He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth which is more general than the matters that they conceal or show, so nothing that is more specific than that is hidden from Him.
3:30: His statement 30- On the Day you find is in the accusative case with his statement And God warns you of Himself. It was said that it is omitted: that is, remember, and present is a state, and his statement and whatever evil you have done is conjoined with the first what: that is, and you find whatever evil you have done present, you wish that there was a long time between it and that. So present was omitted because the first indicates it, and this is if find is from finding the lost thing, but if found is in the sense of knowledge, then present is the second object, and it is possible that his statement and whatever evil you have done, you wish that there was a long time between it and that is a renewed sentence, and what in what you have done is the subject and wish is its predicate. And the term al-Amad means the goal, and its plural is Amad meaning you wish that there was a long period between it and what you did of evil. It was said that his statement the day you find is in the accusative case with his statement you wish and the pronoun in his statement and between it refers to the day, and there is some distance in it. And he repeated his statement and God warns you of Himself for emphasis and to bring to mind so that this great threat would be remembered by them. And in his statement and God is Kind to the servants is evidence that this severe warning is coupled with compassion from Him, glory be to Him, towards His servants, out of kindness to them. And what is better than what is narrated about some of the Arabs that it was said to him: You will die and be resurrected and return to God, so he said: Do you threaten me with someone from whom I have never seen good except? Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Al-Hajjaj bin Amr, an ally of Ka’b bin Al-Ashraf, Ibn Abi Al-Haqiq and Qais bin Zaid, had gathered a group of Ansar to tempt them away from their religion. Rafa’ah bin Al-Mundhir, Abdullah bin Jubayr and Sa’d bin Khathmah said to those al-Nas 114:So God revealed about them: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies until His saying: And God has power over all things. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of transmission on his authority that he said: God forbade the believers from being kind to the disbelievers and taking them as allies instead of the believers, unless the disbelievers are dominant over them, in which case they show them kindness and differ from them in religion. This is what God the Almighty said: Unless you fear them out of fear. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi: And whoever does that has nothing to do with God, for God has disassociated himself from him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Unless you fear them with a fear, he said: Taqiyyah with the tongue is someone who is compelled to speak about something, which is a sin against God, so he speaks it out of fear of people while his heart is at peace with faith, for that will not harm him. Rather, taqiyyah is with the tongue. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: Taqiyyah is speaking with the tongue while the heart is at peace with faith, and he does not stretch out his hand to kill or to commit sin, for that is no excuse for him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding the verse, he said: Taqiyyah is with the tongue, not with actions. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, Unless you fear them with a fear, he said: Unless there is a kinship between you and him, so you maintain ties with him for that. Abd ibn Humayd and Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Taqiyyah is permissible until the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Darda’ that he said: We scour the faces of people while our hearts curse them. The permissibility of taqiyya is indicated by the statement of God the Almighty: “Except for one who is forced [to do so] while his heart is at rest in faith. But as for him who opens his breast to disbelief, upon them is wrath from God, and for them is a great punishment.” Among those who say that taqiyya with the tongue is permissible are Abu Al-Sha’tha’, Ad-Dahhak, and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi regarding the statement of God the Almighty: “Say: If you conceal” 4:10, he said: He informed them that He knows what they concealed and what they declared. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the statement of God the Almighty: Present, meaning: Prepared. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse: “One of you would be pleased that his work would never be met, for that would be his desire. As for his sin in this world, he enjoyed it.” They also narrated on the authority of As-Suddi: A distant time, meaning: A distant place. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: A distant time, meaning: A term. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement, And God warns you of Himself, and God is Kind to His servants, he said: Out of His kindness to them, He warns them of Himself.
3:31: 31- "Say, 'If you love God, then follow me, God will love you and forgive you your sins. God is Forgiving and Merciful.'" Love and affection are the soul's inclination towards something. It is said: I love him, so he is loving, and his love loves him with the kasra, so he is beloved. Al-Jawhari said: This is anomalous, because it does not come in the doubled form, yaf'al with the kasra. Ibn Al-Dahan said: There are two languages for love, love and I love, and the root of love in this chapter is to love like to traverse, and love for God the Almighty has been interpreted as the will to obey Him. Al-Azhari said: The servant's love for God and His Messenger is his obedience to them and following their commands, and God's love for the servants is His favor upon them with forgiveness. Abu Raja' Al-Attari read fat-ha on me. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr Ibn Al-Ala that he assimilated the ra' of yaghfir into the lam. Al-Nahhas said: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh do not permit the assimilation of the letter ra into the letter lam, and Abu Amr is too noble to make a mistake in this, and perhaps he was concealing the vowel as he does many things.
3:32: His statement 32- "Say: Obey God and the Messenger." The deletion of the subject indicates generalization, i.e. in the collection of commands and prohibitions. His statement But if they turn away may be from the words of God the Most High, and thus it would be past. His statement Then God does not love the disbelievers is a negation of love, a metaphor for hatred and anger. The reason for the explicitness in his statement Then God, despite the context being one of concealment, is for the purpose of glorification or generalization.
3:33: His saying 33- Indeed, God chose Adam etc. When He, the Almighty, finished explaining that the acceptable religion is Islam, and that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the Messenger whom no one can love God except by following him, and that the difference of opinion among the People of the Book about him is only due to transgression and envy towards him, He began to establish the message of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and explained that he is from the family of the Prophethood and the source of the message. And selection is choice. Al-Zajjaj said: He chose them with prophethood over the worldly people of their time. And it was said: The speech is based on the estimation of an added meaning: that is, He chose the religion of Adam, etc. And the speech has already been presented on the interpretation of the worlds, and Adam was singled out for mention because he is the father of mankind, and likewise Noah, for he is the second Adam. As for the family of Abraham, it is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is from them despite the large number of prophets from them. As for the family of Imran, even though they are from the family of Abraham, since Jesus, peace be upon him, was from them, there was a reason for singling them out for mention. And it was said: What is meant by the family of Abraham is Abraham himself, and by the family of Imran is Imran himself.
3:34: His saying: 34- Some of them are descendants of others. The word descendants is in the accusative case as a substitute for what preceded it, as stated by Al-Zajjaj, or as a conditional case, as stated by Al-Akhfash. The explanation of descendants has already been presented, and some of them are descendants of others is in the accusative case as a description of descendants, and its meaning is reproducing and branching out or supporting and supporting one another in religion. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, through various chains of transmission, that he said: Some people said during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): By God, O Muhammad, we love our Lord. So God revealed: Say, If you love God the verse. Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi narrated something similar on the authority of Yahya ibn Kathir. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mundhir also narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn Az-Zubayr regarding his statement: Say, If you love God meaning: If this is what you say about Jesus out of love for God and glorification of Him, Then follow me, God will love you and forgive you your sins meaning: What has passed of your disbelief, And God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Ad-Darda’ regarding his statement: Say, If you love God, then follow me, God will love you he said: On righteousness, piety, humility and lowliness of soul. Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi, Abu Nu’aym, Ad-Daylami and Ibn Asakir also narrated it on his authority. Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Aisha. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah, and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Polytheism is more hidden than the crawling of an ant on a smooth rock in the dark of night. The least of it is that one loves something out of injustice and hates something out of justice. Is religion anything but love and hatred for the sake of God?” God the Most High said: Say, ‘If you love God’ (Al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the family of Abraham and the family of Imran, he said: They are the believers from the family of Abraham, the family of Imran, the family of Yasin, and the family of Muhammad. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Descendants, some of them from others, he said: In intention, action, sincerity, and monotheism.
3:35: His saying 35- When she said Abu Amr said: When is redundant. Muhammad bin Yazid said: It is related to something omitted, the meaning of which is remember when she said. Al-Zajjaj said: It is related to his saying He chose and it was said that it is related to his saying: All-Hearing, All-Knowing. The name of Imran's wife is Hannah with a silent ha and a noon, the daughter of Faqud bin Qabil, the mother of Mary, so she is the grandmother of Jesus. Imran is the son of Mathan, the grandfather of Jesus. His saying My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb is the introduction of the preposition and its object for the sake of complete care, and this vow was permissible in their law. The meaning of to You is for Your worship. And Freed is in the accusative case as a state: meaning freed, devoted to God, serving the church. What is meant here is freedom, which is the opposite of slavery. It was said: What is meant by freed here is the one devoted to God Almighty, who is not tainted by anything of worldly affairs. This is supported by the fact that there is no dispute that Imran and his wife are free. His saying, So accept it from me. Acceptance is taking something with satisfaction: that is, accept from me what I vowed with what is in my stomach.
3:36: His statement 36- When she delivered her The feminine gender is based on what is known from the context that what is in her womb is female, or because it is female in the knowledge of God, or by interpreting what is in her womb as the soul or the breath or something similar. His statement She said, 'My Lord, I have delivered a female' She only said this statement because nothing was accepted in vows except a male without a female, so it is as if she regretted and was saddened by what she missed of that which she had hoped for and estimated, and female is a confirmed state of the pronoun or a substitute for it. His statement And God knows best what she delivered Abu Bakr and Ibn Amir read it with a damma on the ta', so it is part of her statement and is connected to what preceded it, and in it is the meaning of submission to God, obedience and sanctification of Him from anything being hidden from Him. The majority of scholars read laid as was placed, so it is from the speech of God, the Most High, in order to glorify what she has placed, to magnify its status, and to honor it, as she expressed regret and sorrow, even though this female whom she has placed, God will make her and her son a sign for the worlds and a lesson for those who consider, and He will single her out with what He has singled out no one else. Ibn Abbas read ma-ma-has placed with a kasra on the ta’ as an address from God, the Most High, to her: meaning, you do not know the value of this gift and what God knows about it of matters that are beyond understanding and that are beyond reason. His statement, and the male is not like the female, means: and the male whom she requested is not like the female whom she placed, for the most she wanted from him being a male was for him to be a vow serving the church, and the matter of this female is great and her status is magnificent. This sentence is parenthetical, explaining what is in the first sentence of glorifying the subject and raising its status and high position. The lam in the word male and female is for the covenant. This is according to the reading of the majority and according to the reading of Ibn Abbas. As for the reading of Abu Bakr and Ibn Amir, his saying and the male is not like the female is part of her speech and the completion of her regret and sadness: that is, the male whom she wanted to be a servant and fit for the vow is not like the female who is not fit for that. It is as if she excused herself to her Lord for having her existence contrary to what she intended. His saying and I have named her Mary is in apposition to I have given birth to a female. Her purpose in this information about the name is to draw closer to God Almighty, and for her action to be consistent with the meaning of her name. The meaning of Mary is the servant of the Lord in their language. Even if she was not fit to serve the church, that does not prevent her from being one of the worshippers. His saying and I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the accursed is in apposition to his saying I have named her Mary, and the accursed is the one who is cast out, and its origin is the one who is thrown with stones. She sought refuge for herself and her child from Satan and his helpers.
3:37: His statement, So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance, meaning He was pleased with her in the vow, and made her follow the path of the happy ones. Some people said: The meaning of acceptance is to take care of her, raise her, and take care of her. Acceptance is a source confirming the previous verb, and the ba’ is redundant, and the original is taqbulan, and the same is true of his statement, And He caused her to grow in a good manner, and its original is inbatan, so the redundant letter was deleted. It was said that it is a source for a deleted verb: meaning that He made her well-mannered, without increase or decrease. It was said that she used to grow in a day what a newborn grows in a year. It was said that it is a metaphor for the good upbringing that would return to her in a way that would benefit her in all her circumstances. His statement, And Zakariya took her under his care, meaning: He took her into his care. Abu Ubaidah said that he took care of her. The Kufians read and he took care of her with emphasis: meaning God made him her guarantor and committed to her interests, and the same meaning is found in the Mushaf of Abu and he took care of her. The rest read it with a light pronunciation, attributing the action to Zakariya, and its meaning is what was mentioned above, that he took her into his chamber and guaranteed her care. Amr bin Musa narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer and Abu Abdullah Al-Muzani, and he protected her with a kasra on the fa. Al-Akhfash said: I did not hear him protect her. Mujahid read fataqubalha with a sukoon on the ta’ and kafalaha with a shaddah on the broken fa’ and a sukoon on the lam and the accusative of Zakariya with a long vowel. Hafs, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read Zakariya without a long vowel, and the rest extended it. Al-Farra’ said: The people of Al-Hijaz extend Zakariya and shorten it. Al-Akhfash said: There are languages of lengthening and shortening in it, and Zakariya with a shaddah on the ya’, which is impossible in all estimates due to foreignness and the definition with the feminine alif. His statement Whenever Zakariya entered upon her in the sanctuary he presented the adverb to emphasize it, and the word every is an adverb, and the time is deleted, and ma is a source or an indefinite noun described, and the factor in that is his statement he found meaning: whenever he entered upon her, he found with her a provision: meaning a type of provision. The mihrab in the language: the most honorable place in the assembly, said Al-Qurtubi, and it is accusative for expansion. It was said: Zachariah made a mihrab for her that could not be ascended except by a ladder, and he used to call her until she grew old, and when he entered upon her, he would find with her winter fruits in the summer and summer fruits in the winter, so he said: O Mary, where did you get this? meaning: Where does this provision come to you from that is unlike the provisions of this world? “She said: It is from God.” This is not strange or strange, and the sentence of his saying: Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account is an explanation of what preceded it, and it is from the completion of her speech, and whoever said that it is from the speech of Zachariah, then the sentence is renewed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Indeed, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated, that he said: She vowed to make it in the church to be worshipped there, and she hoped that it would be a boy. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, that he said: She vowed to make it dedicated for worship. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, dedicated, that he said: A servant of the covenant. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, that he said: Dedicated and pure, not mixed with anything of worldly affairs. Al-Bukhari and Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “No child is born except that Satan touches him when he is born, so he cries out in agony from Satan’s touch, except for Mary and her son. Then Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish, “And I seek refuge for her with You and for her offspring from Satan, the accursed.” The hadith has other wordings on the authority of Abu Hurairah, this is one of them, and it was narrated from a hadith from someone else. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Zachariah took care of her. He entered the prayer chamber and found grapes with her in a basket out of season. He said: ‘How did you get this?’ She said: ‘It is from God.’ He said: ‘Indeed, He who provides you with grapes out of season is able to provide me with a son from a barren, old, infertile woman.’” At that time, Zachariah called upon his Lord. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: “Mary was the daughter of their master and leader, and their rabbis disputed over her and drew lots regarding her, as to who would take care of her. Zachariah was her sister’s husband, so he took care of her, and she was with him and he nursed her.” Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas and some of the Companions. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And Zachariah took care of her, meaning: He placed her with him in his prayer chamber.
3:38: His saying 38- There is an adverb used for time and place, and its origin is for place, and it was said: it is for time specifically, and there is for place, and it was said: it is permissible to use each one of them in place of the other, and the lam is to indicate distance, and the kaf is for addressing. The meaning is that he prayed in that place where he was standing with Mary, or at that time, that God would grant him good offspring, and what prompted him to do that was what he saw of Hannah giving birth to Mary, and she was barren, so he had hope of a child even though he was old and his wife was barren, or what prompted him to do that was what he saw of the winter fruit in the summer and the summer in the winter with Mary, because the one who creates that at a time other than its season is able to create a child from a barren woman, and on this basis this speech is a renewed story that was brought up within the story of Mary because of the connection between them, and offspring and lineage can be for one and can be for the plural, and it indicates that here it is for one. His saying, Then grant me from Yourself a protector, and he did not say protectors, and the feminine of Tayyiba is because the word offspring is feminine. 5- And I feared the loyalists after me Uthman bin Affan, Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hussein, his father Ali, and Yahya bin Ya'mar read khaft with a fatha on the kha, a shaddah on the fa, and a kasra on the ta, and its subject is the loyalists, meaning they were few and unable to carry out the religious affairs after me, or they were cut off by death, taken from khafat al-qawm if they departed, and this reading is anomalous and far from the truth. The rest read khaft with a kasra on the kha and a sukoon on the fa, on the basis that its subject is a pronoun referring to Zakariya, and its object is the loyalists, and min ra'i is related to something omitted, not khaft, and its meaning is: I feared the actions of the loyalists after me. The majority read wa'i with a hamza, a long vowel, and a sukoon on the ya, and Ibn Kathir read it with a hamza, a long vowel, and a fatha on the ya. It was narrated that he read it with a short vowel and an open ya’, like ‘asai’. The Mawali here are the relatives who inherit and all the agnates from the paternal uncles and the like. The Arabs call these Mawali. The poet said: Hold on, cousins, hold on, loyalists. Do not spread among us what was buried. It was said that the loyalists supported him. They differed about the reason for Zakariya’s opposition to his loyalists after him. It was said that he feared that they would inherit his money, and he wanted his son to inherit him, so he asked God, the Almighty, to grant him a son. Others said that they were neglecting the matter of religion. He feared that the religion would be lost with his death, so he asked for a guardian to take care of it after his death. This statement is more correct than the first because the prophets do not leave an inheritance and he is too noble to care about worldly matters. So what is meant here is not the inheritor of money, but rather the inheritor of knowledge, prophethood, and taking care of the matter of religion. It has been proven from our Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he said: “We prophets do not leave an inheritance. What we leave behind is charity.” And my wife was barren. Barren is the one who does not give birth due to old age, and the one who does not give birth also for other than old age, and this is what is meant here. A man who does not give birth is also called barren, and from this is the saying of Amer bin Tufail: What a bad boy you are if you are one-eyed and barren Ibn Jarir said: His wife's name was Ash'a' bint Faqud bin Mail, and she was the sister of Hannah, and Hannah was the mother of Mary. Al-Qatibi said: She is Ash'a' bint Imran. According to the opinion, Yahya bin Zakariya was the son of the maternal aunt of the mother of Jesus. According to the second opinion, they were the sons of a maternal aunt, as mentioned in the authentic hadith: Then grant me from Yourself a guardian, meaning, give me from Your grace a guardian. He did not explicitly ask for a child because he knew that he and his wife had reached a state in which it was not permissible for a child to occur between them or for them to have one. It was said that he was ninety-something years old, and it was said that what he meant by the guardian he asked was a child. There is no objection to asking for something like that, since it is extraordinary, for God, the Almighty, may honor His messengers with something like that, and it is among the miracles that prove their truthfulness.
3:39: His saying 39- "The angels called him", Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read: "He called him" and Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud read it that way. The rest read "The angels called him" It was said: What is meant here is Gabriel, and expressing the singular in the plural is permissible in Arabic, and from that is "those to whom the people said", and it was said that all the angels called him and this is apparent from attributing the verb to the plural and the real meaning is preferred so metaphor is not resorted to except for a clue. His saying "and he is standing is a circumstantial clause, and praying in the sanctuary is an attribute of his saying standing or a second predicate of his saying and he His saying that God gives you good tidings It was read with the fatha of an", and the estimation is that God, and it was read with its kasra on the estimation of the saying. The people of Madinah read "gives you good tidings" with emphasis. Hamza read with alleviation. Humayd ibn Qays Al-Makki read with the kasra and damma of the letter of the present tense. Al-Akhfash said: They are three languages with one meaning, and the first reading is the one that is mentioned frequently in the Qur’an, and from it: So give good tidings to my servants, “So give him good tidings of forgiveness,” So we gave her good tidings of Isaac, “They said, We give you good tidings of the truth,” and it is the reading of the majority. The second is the language of the people of Tihamah, and Abdullah bin Masoud also read it with it. The third is from abshar yubashar ibsharan. Yahya is not allowed either because it is foreign or because it has the weight of the verb like umar with the science. Al-Qurtubi said, quoting from al-Naqqash: His name in the first book was Hanna. What we saw in places in the Gospel is that it is John. It was said: He was called that because God revived him with faith and prophethood, and it was said because God revived people with guidance through him. What is meant here is the good tidings of his birth: that is, He gives you good tidings of the birth of Yahya. And His statement, Confirming a word from God, means Jesus, peace be upon him, and he was called the Word of God because he was by His saying, Be, and it was said that he was called the Word of God because people are guided by him as they are guided by the word of God. Abu Ubaid said: The meaning of by a word from God is by a book from God. He said: The Arabs say: Recite to me his word, meaning his poem, as it was narrated that Al-Huwaidra mentioned to Hassan and said: May God curse his word, meaning his poem. End quote. Yahya was the first to believe in Jesus and confirm it, and he was older than Jesus by three years, and it was said by six months. Sayyid: is the one who rules his people. Al-Zajjaj said: The Sayyid is the one who surpasses his peers in everything from the report. The origin of Al-Hasr is from Al-Hasr, which means confinement. It is said: The thing confined me and confined me, and from it the saying of the poet: Laila did not abandon you because she was distant from you, nor because she was busy with things. Al-Hasur: is the one who does not come to women as if he is refraining from them, as it is said: a man who is hasur and hasir: if he withholds his provision and does not release it, so Yahya, peace be upon him, was hasur from coming to women: that is, he was restricted and did not come to them like other men, either due to his inability to do so, or because he refrains from them except for an acquired matter that its doer is able to do otherwise, not due to what was from the origin of creation and in the nature itself. And his saying of the righteous means: originating from the righteous, because he is from the lineage of the prophets, or being from the group of the righteous, as in his saying and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous. Al-Zajjaj said: The righteous is the one who fulfills what God has imposed upon him, and fulfills the rights of the people.
3:40: His saying 40- He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a boy?' This appears to indicate that the address was to God Almighty, even though the address that reached him was through the angels, and that was to increase supplication and earnestness in seeking an answer to his question. It was said that he meant Gabriel by Lord, meaning, My master. It was said that there are two meanings to this question: One of them is that he asked, Will this child be granted from his barren wife or from someone else? It was said that its meaning is, By what means do I require this, while my wife and I are in this state? The result is that he ruled out the possibility of a child occurring from them, even though custom dictates that it does not occur from someone like them, because on the day of the good report he was old, it was said that he was ninety years old, and it was said that he was one hundred and twenty years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. Therefore, he said, And old age has overtaken me, meaning that in this case, he made old age as if it were seeking it, because it is a precursor to death, so he attributed the action to it. Barren: the one who does not give birth, i.e. barren in lineage, and if it were in action, he would have said barren, i.e. she has barrenness that prevents her from having children. This questioning came from him due to the power of God, the Most High, not for the sake of mere exclusion. It was said that forty years had passed after his supplication until a time his Lord willed, and it was said: twenty years, so the exclusion was from this aspect. His saying, Thus does God do what He wills, i.e. God does what He wills of wondrous deeds such as that deed, which is creating a child from an old man and a barren woman. The kaf is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source, and the reference is to the source of yaf’al or the kaf is in the nominative case as a predicate: i.e. in this wondrous affair is the affair of God, and his saying, He does what He wills, is an explanation of it, or the kaf is in the accusative case as a state: i.e. God does the deed being like that.
3:41: His saying 41- "He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign' meaning a sign by which I will know the health of the pregnancy, so that I may receive this blessing with gratitude. He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture' meaning: Your sign is that you will hold your tongue from speaking to people for three days, not from any other remembrances. The reason for making this sign is to devote those days to the remembrance of God, the Most High, in gratitude for what He has bestowed upon him. It was said that this was a punishment from God, the Most High, to him because he asked for the sign after the angels spoke to him directly. Al-Qurtubi narrated this from most of the commentators. The symbol in the language is: a gesture with the lips, eyes, eyebrows, or hands. Its origin is movement, and it is a disconnected exception, because the symbol is not of the same type as speech. It was said: It is connected in the sense that speech is that by which understanding is achieved, whether by word, gesture, or writing, and this is far-fetched. The first is correct, and Al-Akhfash and Al-Kisa'i said the same. His saying, And glorify Him, meaning glorify Him, in the evening, which is the plural of evening. It was said that it is one and it is from the time the sun declines until it sets. It was said that it is from the afternoon until the middle of the night has passed, which is very weak. And the early morning is from the rising of dawn until the time of the forenoon. It was said that what is meant by glorification is prayer.
3:42: His saying 42- When the angels said, O Mary, the circumstance is related to something omitted like the first circumstance, Indeed, God has chosen you, He chose you, and purified you, from disbelief or from impurity in general, and has chosen you over the women of the worlds. It was said: This other selection is not the first selection, for the first is when she accepted her with a good acceptance, and the other is for the birth of Jesus. What is meant by the worlds here, it was said: The women of the world of her time, which is the truth, and it was said: The women of all the world until the Day of Resurrection, and Al-Zajjaj chose it, and it was said: The other selection is an emphasis on the first selection, and what is meant by both of them is one.
3:43: His statement 43- O Mary, be devout towards your Lord meaning, prolong your standing in prayer or continue. We have already discussed the meanings of qunut, and prostration was mentioned before bowing because it is better or because their prayer is not arranged in order, with the waw being for the sake of gathering without order. His statement and bow with those who bow appears to mean that her bowing is with their bowing, which indicates the permissibility of congregational prayer. It was said: The meaning is that she does what they do even if she does not pray with them.
3:44: And the reference in his saying 44- that is to what preceded from the matters that God informed about. Revelation in the language is: informing in secret, it is said: he revealed and he revealed with the same meaning. Ibn Faris said: Revelation is the indication, writing, message, and everything that you convey to someone other than you so that you know it. His saying and you were not with them means those who disputed about the upbringing of Mary, and he only denied his presence with them despite it being known because they denied the revelation, that denial was correct and there was no way to know it except by witnessing and being present, and they do not claim that, so it was proven that it was revelation by their acceptance that he was not one of those who read the Torah nor one of those who associate with its people. Pens is the plural of pen, from the word qalamuhu, meaning to cut it: that is, pens with which they write. It was said: their lots, Which of them will take care of Mary? that is, who will embrace her. That is, they cast their pens to know which of them will take care of her, and that was when they disputed over her care. So Zachariah said: He is more entitled to her because her maternal aunt is with him, and she is Ashba’, the sister of Hannah, the mother of Mary. And the Children of Israel said: We are more entitled to her because she is the daughter of our scholar. So they drew lots and put their pens in the running water on the basis that whoever’s pen stopped and did not run with the water is her owner. So their pens flowed and Zachariah’s pen stopped. This was used as evidence by those who established the drawing of lots, and the disagreement over that is well-known, and authentic hadiths have been established regarding its validity. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When Zakariya saw that, meaning the summer fruits in the winter and the winter fruits in the summer with Mary, he said: He who brought this to Mary out of season is able to give me a son, so that is when he called upon his Lord. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, good offspring means: blessed. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Hammad who said: In the recitation of Ibn Masoud: Gabriel called him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary, and Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi that he said: The angels called him meaning Gabriel. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: The sanctuary is the place of prayer. Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of these altars, meaning the prayer niches. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf on the authority of Musa Al-Juhani who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My nation will continue to be fine as long as they do not make altars in their mosques like the altars of the Christians. It has been narrated that a group of the Companions disliked this. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: He was named Yahya because God revived him with faith. They narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Confirming a word from God he said: Jesus, son of Mary, is the word. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on his authority who said: Yahya and Jesus were the sons of the maternal aunt, and Yahya’s mother used to say to Maryam 19:I find that which is in my womb prostrating to that which is in your womb, so that is his belief in Jesus as he prostrated in his mother’s womb, and he was the first to believe in Jesus. Ahmad narrated in al-Zuhd and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and a master he said: forbearing and pious. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The master is the generous one with God. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab who said: The master is the knowledgeable jurist. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, and a master and chaste, he said: A master is the forbearing one, and chaste is the one who does not have intercourse with women. Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr regarding Al-Husr something similar. Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Chaste is the one who does not have water coming down. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: His penis was like the hem of a garment. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ahmad narrated it in Az-Zuhd from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Amr, and it is stronger. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Shu’ayb Al-Jubba’i who said: The name of Yahya’s mother is Ash’i’. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, Make for me a sign, he said: By conceiving him. Abdul Razzaq, Abdul bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the statement of God, Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days, that he said: He was punished with that because the angels spoke to him directly and gave him the good report of John, so he asked for the sign after the angels spoke to him, so he took him by the tongue. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, except by a sign, that he said: The sign is with the lips. Abdul bin Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, that he said: The sign is the indication. Abdul bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the statement of God, And glorify God in the evening and the morning, that he said: The evening is the inclination of the sun to set, and the morning is the first part of dawn. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Ali who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The best of their women is Mary, daughter of Imran, and the best of their women is Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best women of the worlds are Khadija, Fatima, Mary, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, and Al-Hakim narrated a similar hadith on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. In the two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Many men have attained perfection, but none of the women have attained perfection except Mary, the daughter of Imran, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh. The superiority of Aisha over other women is like the superiority of tharid over other food.” There are many hadiths with the same meaning, all of which indicate that Mary, peace be upon her, is the mistress of the women of her world, not the women of all the world. It is supported by what Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Muqatil on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Four women are the masters of the women of their world: Mary, daughter of Imran, Asiya, daughter of Muzahim, Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, and the best of them in knowledge is Fatima.” Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement, O Mary, be obedient to your Lord, he said: Prolong your standing. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, Be obedient to your Lord, he said: Be sincere. And he narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Obey your Lord. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, And you were not with them when they cast their pens, he said: When Mary was born in the mosque, the people of the place of prayer drew lots for her while they were writing down the revelation, so they drew lots with their pens as to who would take care of her. God said to Muhammad, And you were not with them, the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: They threw their pens into the water and it went with the flow and Zakariya’s pen went up and Zakariya took care of it. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ar-Rabi’. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that the pens are what they write the Torah with. Abd Ibn Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ that they are arrows.
3:45: His saying 45- When she said is a substitute for his saying When she said mentioned before it and what is between them is an objection. It was said that it is a substitute for When they dispute and it was said that it is accusative with an implied verb. It was said that it is based on his saying They dispute and it was said that it is based on his saying And you were not with them. There is a difference of opinion about the Messiah, what did he take from? It was said that he wiped the earth, meaning he went into it and did not hide in it. It was said that he did not wipe a person with a defect except that he was healed, so he was called Messiah. According to these two, it is fa’il with the meaning of fa’il. It was said that he wiped with the oil that the prophets used to wipe themselves with. It was said that his soles were wiped. It was said that camels wiped him. It was said that he wiped with purification from sins. According to these four opinions, it is fa’il with the meaning of maf’ul. Abu al-Haytham said: Messiah is the opposite of al-Masih, with the voiced kha’. Ibn al-A’rabi said: Messiah the truthful. Abu Ubaid said: Its origin in Hebrew is mashikhan with the two voiced kha’s, so it was Arabized as Musa was Arabized by Musa. As for the Antichrist, he was called Messiah because one of his eyes was wiped. It was said that he wipes the earth, meaning he travels around its countries except Mecca, Medina, and Jerusalem. His saying Jesus is an apposition or a substitute, and it is a foreign name. It was said that it is Arabic, derived from ‘asa ya’usa, meaning he ruled it. He said in Al-Kashaf: It is an Arabization of Ayshua end. What we have seen in the Gospel in several places is that his name is Joshua without a hamza, and it was said son of Mary even though the address was to her, indicating that he was born without any, so he was attributed to his mother. And the prominent person is the one with prestige: which is strength and protection, and his prestige in this world is prophecy, and in the hereafter it is intercession and high status, and it is in the accusative case as a state of a word, and if it is indefinite then it is described, and likewise his saying and of those brought near is in the accusative case as a state. Al-Akhfash said: It is in apposition to a prominent person.
3:46: The cradle: the baby's bed while breastfeeding, and I prepared the matter: I made it ready and prepared it. And the old man is the one who is between the age of youth and old age: that is, he speaks to people while he is an infant in the cradle and while he is an old man with the revelation and the message, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. Al-Akhfash and Al-Farraa said: that the old man is in apposition to the honorable. Al-Akhfash said 46- And from the righteous is in apposition to the honorable: that is, he is from the righteous servants.
3:47: His statement 47- How can I have a son? That is, how can he be in the usual way of exclusion and no man has touched me A circumstantial clause: that is, while the situation is in a state that is contrary to the usual state of having a father. He said, 'Thus does God create what He wills' is from the speech of God Almighty. The origin of the decree is the rulings, and it has been mentioned before, and here it is the will: that is, if He wills a matter He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is without action or practice, and it is a representation of the perfection of His power.
3:48: His statement 48- And teaches him the Book. It was said: It is conjoined with gives you good report: that is, God gives you good report and God teaches him. It was also said: It is conjoined with creates: that is, God teaches him likewise, or the statement of a subject that was brought to comfort her heart. The Book is writing. Wisdom is knowledge. It was also said: It is the refinement of morals. The nominative case of a messenger is based on the estimation of and makes him a messenger, or and speaks to them as a messenger, or and I sent a messenger. It was said: It is conjoined with his statement a distinguished person, so it is a state because it has the meaning of speech: that is, a speaker. Al-Akhfash said: If you wish, you can make the and in his statement: and a messenger an intrusion, and the messenger a state.
3:49: His saying 49- I have come to you is an object of the Messenger because it has the meaning of speech as mentioned before, and it was said that its origin is that I have come to you so the preposition was deleted, and it was said that it is accusative with an implied word, meaning you say that I have come to you, and it was said that it is conjoined with the previous states.
