And his saying with a sign is in the accusative case as a state: meaning clothed in a sign that will be from your Lord. And his saying that I create means I form and determine for you from clay like the form of a bird and this sentence is a substitute for the first sentence, which is that I have come to you or a substitute for a sign or the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning it is that I, and it was read with a kasra on the hamza as a resumption. Al-A'raj and Abu Ja'far read like the form of a bird with emphasis, and the kaf in his saying like the form of a bird is an attribute of a deleted source: meaning I create for you a creation or something like the form of a bird. His saying, Then I will breathe into it, meaning into that creation, or that thing. The pronoun refers to the kaf in his saying, like the form of a bird. It was said that the pronoun refers to the bird, meaning one of them. It was said that it refers to the clay. It was read, So it will be a bird and a bird, like merchant and merchant. It was said that He did not create anything other than the bat because of the wonders of craftsmanship in it. It has breasts, teeth, ears, menstruates and purifies itself. It was said that they asked for the creation of the bat because of the aforementioned wonders, because it flies without feathers, gives birth as other animals do, despite being a bird, does not lay eggs as other birds do, does not see in daylight or in the darkness of night, but only sees in two hours: one hour after sunset and one hour after dawn. It laughs as a human laughs. It was said that their question to him was to be stubborn. It was said that he would fly as long as people were watching him, but if he disappeared from their sight, he would fall dead, so that God’s action could be distinguished from the action of others. His saying, by God’s permission, is evidence that if it were not for God Almighty’s permission, he would not have been able to do that, and that the creation of that was by God Almighty’s action, which He carried out at the hand of Jesus, peace be upon him. It was said that the shaping of the clay and the blowing were from Jesus, and the creation was from God Almighty. His saying, And I will heal the blind. The blind is the one who is born blind, as Abu Ubaidah said. Ibn Faris said: “Blindness is the blindness that a person is born with, and it may also occur. It is said: ‘Kamahu yakumahu kamahan’ if he is blind, and ‘Kamahat ‘aynuhu’ if he is blinded. It is also said that ‘Akmah’ is the one who sees during the day but not at night, and it is also said that he is the one whose eye is anointed. Leprosy is well-known, and it is a whiteness that appears on the skin. Jesus, peace be upon him, cured many diseases, as mentioned in the Gospel. God Almighty mentioned these two diseases specifically because they are not usually cured by treatment. The same applies to the revival of the dead, as mentioned in the Gospel. His statement, “And I will inform you of what you eat,” means I will inform you of what you eat and what you will store.
3:50: His statement 50- And confirming is in apposition to his statement and a messenger. It was said: The meaning is I have come to you confirming. His statement and to make permissible means and in order to make permissible: that is, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord and I have come to make permissible for you some of the foods that were forbidden to you in the Torah, such as fats and everything with claws. It was said: What was only made permissible for them was what the rabbis forbade them but the Torah did not forbid. Abu Ubaidah said: It is possible for some to mean all, and he recited: There are places where I don't like them, or some souls are attached to their bathrooms. Al-Qurtubi said: This statement is wrong according to the people of insight among the people of language, because some and part do not mean the whole, and because Jesus did not make permissible for them everything that the Torah forbade them, for he did not make permissible killing, theft, fornication, and other prohibitions established in the Gospel, even though they are established in the Torah, and they are many, and this is known from the prohibitions established in the Gospel, even though they are established in the Torah, and they are many, and this is known by those who know the two books, but some may be in the place of the whole with the evidence, like the poet’s saying: Abu Munther, you have perished, so let some of us outlast your kindness. Some evil is less serious than others. Some evil is better than all evil.
3:51: His saying with a sign from your Lord is his saying 51- Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord. This was only a sign because the messengers before him used to say that, so his coming with what the messengers came with would be a sign of his prophethood. It is possible that this previous verse would be a repetition of his saying Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, that I create for you from clay the verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, with a word, that he said: Jesus is the word from God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The cradle is the place where the baby lies while being breastfed. It has been proven in the Sahih that only three spoke in the cradle: Jesus. There was a man among the Children of Israel called Jurayj who used to pray. His mother came to him and called him. He said: Should I answer her or should I pray? She said: O God, do not let him die until you show him the faces of prostitutes. Jurayj was in a monastery and a woman approached him and spoke to him, but he refused. She went to a shepherd and allowed him to have intercourse with her. She gave birth to a boy and said: Who is Jurayj? They came to him and broke his monastery and brought him down and took him captive. He performed ablution and prayed, then came to the boy and said: Who is your father, boy? He said: The shepherd. They said: Shall we build your monastery of gold? He said: No, except of clay. A woman from the Children of Israel was breastfeeding her son. A rider with a badge passed by her, so she said: O God, make my son like him. So he left her breast and turned to the rider and said: O God, do not make me like him. Then he turned to her breast and sucked it. Then he passed by a slave girl who was dragging her feet and playing with her, so she said: O God, do not make my son like this one. So he left her breast and said: O God, make me like her. She said: Why is that? He said: “The rider is a tyrant among tyrants, and this slave girl will be told: ‘You committed adultery,’ and she will say: ‘God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’ They will say: ‘You have stolen,’ and she will say: ‘God is sufficient for me.’” Abu al-Shaykh and al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: None spoke in the cradle except Jesus, the witness of Joseph, the companion of Jurayj, and the son of Pharaoh’s hairdresser. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And he will speak to the people in the cradle and as an adult, that he said: He will speak to them when they are young and when they are old. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Kahl is the one who is in middle age. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The Kahl is the forbearing one. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, And teaches him the Book, he said: Writing with a pen. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj something similar. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Jesus was created as one bird, which is the bat. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The blind is the one who is born blind. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority who said: The blind is the one whose eyes are wiped away. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The blind is the one who sees during the day but does not see at night. They narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: The blind is the one who has a miscarriage. Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’ who said: When Jesus, son of Mary, sent his messengers to revive the dead, he would say to them: Say such-and-such. If you feel a shiver or a tear, then supplicate at that time. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And I will inform you of what you will eat, he said: What food you ate last night and what you have hidden from it. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Yasir who said: I will inform you of what you will eat from the table and what you will store from it. And he had taken a covenant with them in the table when it was revealed that they should eat and not store, so they ate and stored and betrayed, and they became monkeys and pigs. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Wahb that Jesus followed the law of Moses, and he would spend the Sabbath and face Jerusalem, and he said to the Children of Israel: I did not call you to a letter contrary to what is in the Torah except to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you and to relieve you of the burdens. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ regarding the verse: He said: What Jesus brought was softer than what Moses brought. He had forbidden them, in what Moses brought, the meat of camels and sheep, but he permitted them to them through the tongue of Jesus. He had forbidden them fats, but they were permitted to them in what Jesus brought. He also forbade them from fish, and from birds, and from other things that he forbade them and made things difficult for them. Jesus came to them with a lenient interpretation of it in the Gospel. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Qatadah. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, he said: What Jesus explained to them of all things and what his Lord gave him.
3:52: His saying 52- So when he sensed meaning he knew and found: Al-Zajjaj said: Abu Ubaidah said the meaning of sensed is he recognized, and the origin of that is the existence of something by the senses, and sense is the knowledge of something. God the Almighty said: Do you sense any of them? What is meant by sense here is strong perception that runs the course of observation. And by disbelief is their insistence on it, and it was said: He heard the word of disbelief from them. Al-Farraa said: They wanted to kill him. Based on this, the meaning of the verse is: So when Jesus perceived from them the desire to kill him, which is disbelief, he said: Who is my helper to God? Ansar is the plural of supporter. And his saying to God is related to Majdhuf, which occurred as a state: meaning turning to God and seeking refuge in Him or going to Him. And it was said: To means with like His saying the Almighty: And do not consume their wealth with your wealth. And it was said that the meaning is: Who is my helper on the path to God? And it was said that the meaning is: Who adds his support to the support of God. Hawariyyun is the plural of hawari, and hawari of a man is his best and his essence. It is taken from hawr, which means whiteness according to the linguists. Clothes turned white, and hawari of food: what turned white, and hawari is also the helper, and from this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Every prophet has a hawari, and my hawari was Az-Zubayr, which is in Bukhari and others. There is disagreement about the reason for naming them thus. Some say: because of the whiteness of their clothes, and some say: because of the purity of their intentions, and some say: because they are the special ones of the prophets, and they were twelve men, and the meaning of ansar God is: the helpers of His religion and His messengers. His saying, We have believed in God, is a resumption of the reason for what came before it, because faith leads to victory. His saying, And bear witness that we are Muslims, means: bear witness for us on the Day of Resurrection that we are sincere in our faith and obedient to what you want from us.
3:53: The meaning of 53- with what You have revealed is what God Almighty revealed in His books. And the Messenger is Jesus, and the deletion of the related word indicates generalization: that is, we followed him in everything he brought, so write us down with those who bear witness to Your Oneness and to the Message of Your Messenger. Or write us down with the prophets who bear witness to their nations, and it was said: with the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
3:54: His saying 54- And they plotted meaning those whom Jesus sensed were unbelievers, and they were the unbelievers of the Children of Israel. And God's plot was to lure His servants from where they did not know. This was said by Al-Farra' and others. Al-Zajjaj said: God's plot was to punish them for their plot, so the punishment was named after the beginning, like His saying, the Most High, God mocks them, And He is deceiving them. The root of plotting in the language is: assassination and deception: Ibn Faris narrated it, and based on this, it is not attributed to God Almighty except through the path of similarity. It was said: God's plot here is to cast the likeness of Jesus on others, and to raise Jesus to Himself. And God is the best of plotters meaning: the strongest of them in plotting and the most effective in their treachery and their words to cause harm to whomever He wants to cause harm to from where he does not expect.
3:55: His saying 55- "When God said, O Jesus The agent in when": they plotted, or his saying "the best of plotters" or an implied verb, the meaning of which is that it happened. Al-Farra' said: There is an advancement and delay in the speech, the meaning of which is that I will raise you up and purify you from those who disbelieved and I will take you after sending you down from the sky. Abu Zaid said: I will take you and take you. He said in Al-Kashshaf: I will fulfill your term, and its meaning is: I will protect you from being killed by the disbelievers, and I will postpone your term to a term that I have written for you, and I will cause you to die a natural death, not a killing by their hands. Rather, the commentators needed to interpret death as mentioned, because the correct view is that God raised him to the heavens without death, as many commentators preferred, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari chose it. The reason for that is that it has been authenticated in the reports from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he descended and killed the Antichrist. It was said that God, the Exalted, took him in three hours of the day, then raised him to the heavens, and this is weak. It was also said that what is meant by death here is sleep, and similar to it is And it is He who takes you by night meaning He causes you to sleep, and many said the same. His statement And He will purify you from those who disbelieve means in terms of their being permitted to raise him to the heavens and his being far from them. His statement And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection means those who followed what you brought, and they are his sincere companions who did not go to the extremes of making him a god, and among them are the Muslims, for they followed what Jesus, peace be upon him, brought and described him as he deserved without exaggeration, so they did not go to extremes in describing him as the Jews did, nor did they go to extremes as the Christians did. Many scholars have adopted this view. It has been said that what is meant by the verse is that the Christians, who are followers of Jesus, will continue to prevail over the Jews, overpowering them and subduing those of them who are found. Thus, what is meant by those who disbelieve is the Jews in particular. It has also been said that they are the Romans, who will continue to prevail over those who oppose them from among the disbelievers. It has also been said that they are the disciples, who will continue to prevail over those who disbelieve in Christ. In any case, the Christians’ dominance over a group of disbelievers or over all groups of disbelievers does not contradict their being subdued and vanquished by the groups of Muslims, as is indicated by many verses, that this Islamic religion is dominant over all religions, subduing them and rising above them. This verse has been devoted to a book called Bal al-Ghamamah in its interpretation of And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever seeks to complete what is in this position, let him refer to that. Superiority here is more general than being by the sword or by argument. It has been proven in the authentic hadiths that Jesus, peace be upon him, will descend at the end of time and break the cross, kill the pig, abolish the jizya, and judge between the servants according to the Muhammadan law, and the Muslims will be his supporters and followers at that time. It is not far-fetched that this verse refers to this state. His statement, Then to Me is your return, means your return, and the circumstance is brought forward for restriction, and I will judge between you on that day regarding that over which you differed, of matters of religion.
3:56: And His saying 56- As for those who disbelieved to His saying And God does not love the wrongdoers is an explanation of the ruling. His saying in this world and the Hereafter is related to His saying I will punish them. As for their punishment in this world, it is by killing, captivity, tribute, and humiliation. As for in the Hereafter, it is by the punishment of the Fire.
3:57: His statement 57- And He will give them their wages in full meaning: We will give them to them in full and in abundance. It was read with the letter ta’ and with the letter noon. And his statement He does not love the wrongdoers is a metaphor for hating them, and it is a concluding sentence confirming what preceded it.
3:58: His saying 58- That is a reference to what came before of the report of Jesus and others, and it is a subject whose predicate is what comes after it, and of the signs is a state or predicate after a predicate. And the wise is the one who includes the ruling or the decisive one in whom there is no defect. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, But when Jesus perceived disbelief on their part, he said: They disbelieved and wanted to kill him, and that was when his people sought help. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They were called the disciples because of the whiteness of their clothes; they were hunters. Abd Ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: The disciples were short men whom Jesus passed by and they believed in him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: The disciples are those who are fit for the caliphate. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They are the chosen ones of the prophets. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak something similar. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: The disciple is the minister. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sufyan Ibn Uyaynah, who said: The disciple is the helper. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Then write us down with the two witnesses, he said: With Muhammad and his nation that they testified to him that he had conveyed, and they testified to the messengers that they had conveyed. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Saleh on his authority that he said, With the two witnesses, with the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi that he said: The Children of Israel besieged Jesus and nineteen of the disciples in a house, so Jesus said to his companions: Who will take my image so that he may be killed and have Paradise? One of them took it and Jesus ascended to the heaven, and that is what His statement means, And they planned, and God planned, and God is the best of planners. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Indeed, I will cause you to die, he said: He will cause you to die. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: I will cause you to die from the earth. The other two narrated on his authority that he said: Death in a dream. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada who said: This is from the one who raises you up to Me and takes you to Me. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Matar al-Warraq who said: He takes you to Me from this world, but not by a death. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Wahb who said: God took Jesus to Himself for three hours during the day until He raised him up to Him. Ibn Asakir narrated from him who said: He caused him to die for three days, then He resurrected him and raised him up. Al-Hakim narrated from him who said: God took Jesus to Himself for seven hours. Ibn Saad, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd and Al-Hakim narrated from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab who said: Jesus was raised up when he was thirty-three years old. Ibn Asakir narrated from Wahb something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Hasan regarding the words of God Almighty: And purify you from those who disbelieve, he said: He purified him from the Jews, Christians, Magians and the disbelievers of his people. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatada regarding the words of God Almighty: And make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve, he said: They are the people of Islam who followed him according to his nature, religion and Sunnah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar as well. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of An-Nu'man ibn Bashir: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: A group of my nation will continue to be victorious upon the truth, not caring about those who oppose them until the command of God comes. An-Nu'man said: Whoever says: I say about the Messenger of God something he did not say, then the confirmation of that is in the Book of God. God said: And He will make those who follow you (al-Baqarah 2:14). Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Mu'awiyah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), something similar. Then Mu'awiyah recited the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, who said: The Christians are above the Jews until the Day of Resurrection. There is no country in which there are Christians except that they are above the Jews, in the east or the west. They are humiliated in all countries.
3:59: Jesus is likened to Adam in that he was created without a father like Adam, and the fact that the thing being compared to includes something more, which is that he has no mother, just as he has no father, does not detract from the comparison, for that is something outside the scope of the comparison, even if the thing being compared to is more strange than the thing being compared, more astonishing and more bizarre in style. His statement, He created him from dust is an explanatory sentence for what was left ambiguous in the parable: that is, Adam had no father or mother, but God created him from dust. This refutes the denial of those who deny the creation of Jesus without a father, while acknowledging that Adam was created without a father or mother. His statement, Then He said to him, 'Be,' and he was, means, Be a human being, and he was a human being. His statement, and he was, is a narration of a past event, and the explanation of this has already been presented.
3:60: And his saying 60- The truth is from your Lord Al-Farra' said: It is raised by the omission of he. Abu Ubaidah said: It is a resumption of speech and its predicate is his saying from your Lord. It was said: It is the subject of an omitted verb: meaning the truth came to you from your Lord. His saying So do not be among those who doubt The address is either to all of the people who are suitable for it: meaning let none of you be doubtful, or to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the prohibition is for him to increase confirmation because there is no doubt from him about that.
3:61: His statement 61- So whoever disputes with you about it This, even if it is general, what is meant by it is specific, and they are the Christians who came to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Najran, as will be explained. It can also be said that it is general, even if the reason is specific, indicating the permissibility of the Mubahala from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, for everyone who disputes with him about Jesus, peace be upon him, and his nation is his example, and the pronoun in it refers to Jesus, and what is meant by the coming of knowledge here is the coming of its reason, which is the clear signs, and the argument: the dispute and the debate. And his statement Come means: Come and approach, and its origin is the request for the approach of the self, and it is used in opinion if the one being addressed is present, as you say to someone who is present with you: Come, let us look into this matter. His saying, We call our sons, etc. It is sufficient to mention the sons instead of the daughters, either because they are included among the women, or because they are the ones who attend the situations of dispute without them. The meaning of the verse: Let each of us and you call his sons, his women, and himself to the Mubahalah. And in it is evidence that the sons of daughters are called sons because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meant by sons the good ones, as will come. His saying, We implore. The origin of implore is striving in supplication with cursing and other things. It is said, May God curse him, meaning, May God curse him, and Bahl is cursing. Abu Ubaid and Al-Kisa’i said: We implore, we curse, and it is used to mean striving for destruction, and from it is the saying of Labid: Among the elders of his people, time looked at them and supplicated. Meaning: He strived to destroy them. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: Then it was used in every supplication in which one strives, even if it is not a supplication. His statement, Then we will place the curse of God upon the liars, is in apposition to we will supplicate, clarifying its meaning.
3:62: His saying 62- This meaning what God told His Messenger of the report of Jesus is the true story. Stories are successive. It is said: So-and-so is following so-and-so, meaning he is following him. So it was applied to speech that follows one another. The separating pronoun is for limitation, and the addition of the lam to it is to increase its emphasis. It is permissible for it to be a subject, and what follows it is its predicate. The addition of min in His saying min ilaah is to emphasize the generality, and it is a response to those Christians who said that there is a trinity. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Hudhayfah: “The ‘aqīb and the ‘sayyid came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and he wanted to curse them. One of them said to the other: ‘We will not curse him, for by God, if he is a prophet and curses us, neither we nor our descendants after us will ever succeed.’ They said to him: ‘We will give you what you asked for, but send with us a trustworthy man.’ He said: ‘Get up, Abu ‘Ubaydah.’ When he got up, he said: ‘This is the trustworthy man of this nation.’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the path of al-‘Awfi from Ibn ‘Abbas: “A group of people from Najran came to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and among them were the ‘sayyid and the ‘aqīb. They said: ‘What is the matter with you that you mention our companion?’ He said: ‘Who is he?’ They said: ‘Jesus, you claim that he is the servant of God.’ They said: ‘Have you seen the likeness of Jesus and been informed of him?’ Then they left him and Gabriel came and said: ‘Tell them when they come to you: ‘The likeness of Jesus with God is like that of Adam.’” to the end of the verse. This story has been narrated in various ways from a group of the Tabi’īn. Al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Naim in Al-Dala’il, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “Al-Aqib and Al-Sayyid came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he invited them to Islam. They said: We have become Muslims, O Muhammad. He said: You have lied. If you wish, I will tell you what prevents you from Islam. They said: Then tell me. He said: Love of the cross, drinking alcohol, and eating pork.” Jabir said: So he invited them. To the cursing, so they promised him the next day. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went in the morning and took the hand of Ali, Fatima, Hassan and Hussein, then he sent for them, but they refused to answer him and confessed to him. So he said: By Him who sent me with the truth, if they did, I would rain fire down upon them in the valley. Jabir said: The verse Come, let us call our sons was revealed about them. Jabir said, Ourselves and yourselves the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ali, and our sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and our women Fatimah.” Al-Hakim also narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Jabir and authenticated it, and in it they said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Would you like us to curse you? Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas who said, “When this verse was revealed, ‘Say, Come,’ the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn and said, ‘O God, these are my family.’” Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad on the authority of his father, Come, let us call our sons, the verse. He said, So he brought Abu Bakr and his sons, and Umar and his sons, and Uthman and his sons, and Ali and his sons. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then we supplicate we strive. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘This is sincerity.’” He points with his finger next to the thumb, and this is the supplication, so he raised his hands to the level of his shoulders, This supplication, so he raised his hands in supplication.
3:63: 63- But if they turn away, then indeed, God is Knowing of the corrupters.
3:64: It was said: The address is to the people of Najran, as evidenced by what came before this verse. It was also said: To the Jews of Medina. It was also said: To the Jews and Christians together. This is the apparent structure of the Qur’an. There is no reason to limit it to some, because this is a general call that is not specific to those who argued with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And justice: fairness. Al-Farra’ said: It is said in the meaning of justice, fairness and fairness. If you open the seen, you lengthen it, and if you close it or break it, you shorten it. Zuhair said: I narrate a plan in which there is no injustice, and its plants are irrigated with equality. In Ibn Mas`ud’s reading: to a word of justice between us and you, the meaning is: come to what you have been called to, which is the just and upright word in which there is no deviation from the truth. He explained it by saying: 64- that we worship none but God, which is in the accusative case as a substitute for a word, or in the nominative case as an implied subject: that is, that we do not worship. It is possible that an is an explanatory noun with no place for the sentence that it entered into. In his saying: and let not some of us take others as lords, there is a rebuke to those who believed in the lordship of Christ and Ezra, and an indication that these are from the human race and some of them, and a disparagement of those who imitated men in the religion of God, so they permitted what they permitted for him, and forbade what they forbade for him, for whoever did that has taken the one he imitated as a lord, and from it: they took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ permitted the jussive in and let not associate and and let not take based on the assumption. His statement, But if they turn away, meaning, they turn away from what they have been called to, then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims,’ meaning, we submit to his rulings, are satisfied with him, and acknowledge what God has bestowed upon us of this upright religion. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and Al-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: "Abu Sufyan told me that Heraclius called for the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and read it. It said: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, from Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Heraclius, the Great Roman Emperor: Peace be upon him who follows guidance. As for what follows: I invite you to the call of Islam. Submit and you will be safe, God will give you your reward twice. But if you turn away, then upon you will be the sin of the Arians. O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is just between us and you, until His saying: We are Muslims." At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the infidels was: "Come to a word that is just" the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: It has reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, invited the Jews of Medina to what is in this verse, but they refused, so he fought them until they agreed to the jizyah. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, invited the Jews of Medina to a word that is just. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ar-Rabi'. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada, to a common word, he said: justice. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, and let not some of us take others as lords, he said: let not some of us obey others in disobeying God. It is said: that lordship is that people obey their masters and leaders in other than worship, even if they do not pray to them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, and let not some of us take others as lords, he said: prostration of some of them to others.
3:65: When each of the Jewish and Christian sects claimed that Abraham, peace be upon him, was of their religion, God, the Almighty, rejected that from them and made it clear that the Jewish and Christian religions were only revealed after him. Al-Zajjaj said: This verse is the clearest proof against the Jews and Christians that the Torah and the Gospel were revealed after him, and they do not contain the name of any of the religions, and the name Islam is in every book. End quote. There is a view on this, because the Gospel is filled with verses from the Torah and mentions the Law of Moses and uses it as evidence against the Jews. Likewise, the Psalms contain in places mentioning the Law of Moses, and at the beginning of it the good report of Jesus, then in the Torah many of the previous laws are mentioned, and everyone who knows these revealed books knows this. There is a difference of opinion regarding the amount of time between Abraham and Moses and the period between Moses and Jesus. Al-Qurtubi said: It is said that there were a thousand years between Abraham and Moses, and a thousand years between Moses and Jesus. And so it is in Al-Kashshaf. His saying 65 - Do you not reason? That is, do you not think about the refutation of your argument and the invalidity of your statement?
3:66: His statement Here you are, you have argued about that of which you have knowledge. The original meaning of Here you are is you. The first hamza was replaced with a ha' because it is its sister. This is what Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' and al-Akhfash said. An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement. Qanbal read Here you are. It was said that the ha' is for emphasis and was added to the sentence that follows it: meaning here you are, these foolish men have argued. There are two dialects for these: lengthening and shortening. What is meant by that which they have knowledge of is what was in the Torah, even if they contradicted its requirements and argued about it falsely. What they have no knowledge of is their claim that Abraham was of their religion due to their ignorance of the time in which he lived. The verse is evidence of the prohibition of arguing falsely. Rather, there is encouragement for the one who is right to abandon argumentation, as in the hadith: Whoever abandons argumentation, even if he is right, then I guarantee him before God that he will spend the night in the outskirts of Paradise. It has been reported that arguing in the best way is permissible, as God Almighty says: And argue with them in a way that is best and And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best and the like. Therefore, its permissibility should be limited to situations where the benefit in doing so is greater than the harm, or to situations where arguing is done in a polite manner, not in a harsh manner. His statement: And God knows means everything, so that includes what they argued with.
3:67: 67- “Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim [submitting to God]. And he was not of the polytheists.” The interpretation of inclining toward truth has already been presented.
3:68: His statement 68 - The people who are most deserving of it meaning the most deserving of it and the most special of them are those who followed his religion and followed his example and this Prophet meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He singled him out for mention to magnify and honor him, and his banners, may God bless him and grant him peace, are with Abraham in terms of being from his descendants, and in terms of his agreement with his religion in many aspects of the Muhammadan law and those who believe from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala'il on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Christians of Najran and the Jewish rabbis gathered in the presence of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and they disputed in his presence. The rabbis said: Abraham was nothing but a Jew, and the Christians said: Abraham was nothing but a Christian. So the verse was revealed about them: O People of the Scripture, why do you argue? A similar verse was narrated about a group of the Salaf. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah: Here you are, arguing about that of which you have knowledge. He said: about that which you witnessed, saw, and witnessed. So why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? He said: about that which you did not witness, see, or witness. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse: As for that of which they have knowledge, it is what was forbidden to them and what they were commanded to do. As for that of which they have no knowledge, it is the affair of Abraham. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: He who argues with knowledge is excused, but he who argues with ignorance is not excused. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority on the authority of Al-Sha’bi regarding his statement, What was Abraham? He said: God denied them and refuted their argument. Al-Rabi’ also narrated something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil ibn Hibban something similar. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab who told Ibn Ghanim that when the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the Negus, he mentioned their story with him and what they said to him when Amr ibn Al-Aas told him that they were cursing Jesus, and it is a famous story. Then he said: So that day, their dispute was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Medina, The most worthy of Abraham among the people verse. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every prophet has guardians from among the prophets, and my guardian among them is my father, the friend of my Lord. Then he recited, The most worthy of the people verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Mina’ that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O people of Quraysh, the people most deserving of the Prophet are the righteous, so be the path to that. Be careful that people do not meet me carrying deeds and you meet me carrying the world and I turn my face away from you.” Then he recited to them: The people most deserving of Abraham verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Sunnah regarding the verse, he said: Every believer is a friend of Abraham, from those who have passed away and those who remain.
3:69: The group of the People of the Book are the Jews of Banu Nadir, Qurayza and Banu Qaynuqa when they called a group of Muslims to their religion, and it will come. It was said: They are all the People of the Book, so the word min is used to indicate the type. And His statement 69- And they mislead only themselves is a circumstantial clause to indicate the steadfastness of the believers in faith, so the burden of those who wanted to tempt them will only return upon themselves.
3:70: What is meant by the verses of God is what is in their books of evidence of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. 70- And you bear witness to what is in your books of that, or you bear witness to similar verses of the prophets whose prophethood you acknowledge, or what is meant is concealing all the verses out of stubbornness while you know that they are true.
3:71: And mixing the truth with falsehood is mixing it with what they intentionally distort. 71- And you know is a circumstantial clause.
3:72: His saying 72- And a group of the People of the Book said They are their leaders and nobles, they said this statement to the lowly among their people. The face of the day: its beginning, and it was called a face because it is the most beautiful of it. He said: And it shines in the face of the day, bright as the sea’s ocean, its system is smooth It is in the accusative case as a circumstance. They ordered them to do that in order to cast doubt on the believers, because they believed that the People of the Book had knowledge. So if they disbelieved after believing, doubt would fall on others and they would be overcome by suspicion, and they would not know that God had made firm the hearts of the believers and established their feet, so the rumors of God’s enemies would not shake them, nor would the winds of the obstinate ones move them.
3:73: His statement 73- "And do not believe except in him who follows your religion" This is from the speech of the Jews to one another: meaning that the leaders said that to the lowly ones, do not believe in a true belief except for those who follow your religion from the people of the religion that you are upon, and as for others who have become Muslims, they showed them that deceitfully "at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end so that they would be tempted, and his statement that someone should be given what you have been given" on this basis is related to something omitted: meaning that you did that so that someone should be given what you have been given: meaning that what you have of envy and aggression that someone should be given what you have been given of the virtue of knowledge and the Book prompted you to say what you said. And his statement "or that they argue with you" is connected to that someone should be given: meaning that they do not believe in a true belief and you acknowledge what is in your hearts with a true acknowledgment to someone other than those who follow your religion, you did that and planned for the Muslims to argue with you on the Day of Resurrection before God with the truth. His saying, Guidance is the guidance of God is an interjectional clause. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is: Do not believe except in those who follow your religion, and do not believe that someone will be given the like of what you have been given, and do not believe that they will argue with you. So he went to the view that it is connected. It was said: What is meant is: Do not believe at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at the end of it except in those who follow your religion: that is, in those who entered Islam and were from the people of your religion before his conversion to Islam, because the conversion of those who were from them is what killed them out of rage and caused them to die of regret and sorrow. And his saying that someone will be given on this basis is related to something omitted like the first. And it was said: His saying that someone will be given is related to his saying Do not believe that is, do not show your belief in that someone will be given the like of what you have been given that is, keep your belief that the Muslims have been given from the Books of God the same as what you have been given, and do not spread it except to the followers of your religion. And it was said: The meaning is: Do not believe except in those who follow your religion that someone will be given the like of what they have been given. So on this basis, that and what follows it are in the nominative case as the subject, and the predicate is omitted, its estimate is that you believe in that. And it is permissible for it to be In the accusative case, with the implied verb, meaning you acknowledge that it will be brought. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Hamid read that it will be brought with a long vowel. Al-Khalil said: An is in the genitive case, and the preposition is omitted. Ibn Jurayj said: “The meaning is: do not believe except for those who follow your religion, out of aversion to being brought. It was also said that the meaning is: do not tell what is in your book about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, except for those who follow your religion, lest that be a reason for others to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Farra’ said: “It is possible that the speech of the Jews was cut off at his saying, “except for those who follow your religion,” then he said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, ‘Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God,’ meaning: the true clarification is God’s clarification, so that no one will be brought the like of what you have been given, based on the estimation of la, like the Almighty’s saying, God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, meaning: lest you go astray. Or in his saying, or they argue with you, means until. Al-Kisa’i said the same, and according to Al-Akhfash, it is a conjunction, as mentioned above. It was said: Indeed, God’s guidance is a substitute for guidance, and that someone is given is the predicate of that, meaning, “Say: If God’s guidance is not to give anyone the like of what you have been given.” It was said: This verse is the most problematic of the verses in this surah, and that is correct. Al-Hasan read that someone is given with a kasra over the ta’. Sa’id ibn Jubayr read that someone is given with a kasra over the hamza, as if it were the negative.
3:74: And His saying 74- He chooses for His mercy whomever He wills. It was said: It is prophecy, and it was said: It is more general than that, and it is a response to them and a refutation of what they said and planned. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sufyan who said: Everything in Al Imran that mentions the People of the Book is about the Christians. This is refuted by the fact that many of the addresses to the People of the Book mentioned in this Surah cannot be applied to the Christians at all, including these verses that we are about to interpret. The group that wanted to mislead the Muslims, as well as the group that says, Believe in that which has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, are specifically from the Jews. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while you bear witness? He said: You bear witness that the description of the Prophet of God, Muhammad, is in your Book, then you disbelieve in him and deny him and do not believe in him, while you find him written with you in the Torah and the Gospel, the unlettered Prophet. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of al-Rabi’. They also narrated something similar on the authority of al-Suddi. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Muqatil. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And you bear witness that the religion with God is Islam, and that God has no other religion. They narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’, regarding his statement, Why do you mix truth with falsehood? He said: Why do you mix Judaism and Christianity with Islam, while you know that the religion of God that is not accepted from anyone other than Him is Islam? And you conceal the truth He said: You conceal the matter of Muhammad, while you find it written with you in the Torah and the Gospel. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Sayf, Adi ibn Zayd and al-Harith ibn Awf said to each other: Come, let us believe in what was revealed to Muhammad and his companions in the morning and disbelieve in it in the evening, so that we may confuse them about their religion, perhaps they will do as we do and turn back from their religion. So God revealed about them, O People of the Scripture, why do you mix truth with falsehood? until His statement, And God is All-Encompassing and Knowing. Something similar to this has been narrated on the authority of a group of the Salaf. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Abu Dhibyan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, And a group said, he said: They would be with them at the beginning of the day and sit with them and talk to them, but when the evening came and the time for prayer came, they disbelieved in him and abandoned him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, And do not believe except in him who follows your religion, he said: This is what some of them said to each other. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’ something similar. He also narrated on the authority of al-Suddi something similar. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, That someone should be given what you have been given, out of envy on the part of the Jews that prophethood would be for someone other than them, and the desire that they would follow in their religion. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik and Sa’id ibn Jubayr, That someone should be given what you have been given, he said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi that God said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God, that someone should be given the like of what you have been given, O nation of Muhammad, or that they should argue with you before your Lord, the Jews said: God did such and such an honor to us until He sent down manna and quails upon us. What I have given you is better, so say: “Say: Indeed, bounty is in God’s hand; He gives it to whom He wills.” Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada: “Say: Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God, that someone should be given the like of what you have been given,” meaning: When God sent down a book like your book and sent a prophet like your prophet, you envied him for that. “Say: Indeed, bounty is in God’s hand; He gives it to whom He wills.” Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Rabi’. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, “Say: Verily, the guidance is the guidance of God, that someone should be given the like of what you have been given.” He said: This is the matter that God has bestowed upon him. That someone should be given the like of what you have been given, or that they should argue with you before your Lord. He said: Some of them said to each other, Do not tell them what God has made clear to you in His Book, “so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord, so that it will be an argument for them against you. “Say: Verily, the bounty is in God’s hand.” He said: Islam. He chooses for His mercy whom He wills. He said: The Qur’an and Islam. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, He chooses for His mercy whom He wills. He said: Prophethood. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: His mercy is Islam, and He chooses for it whom He wills.
3:75: This is the beginning of explaining the Jews' treachery in money after explaining their treachery in religion, and the prepositional phrase in his saying 75- And among the people of the Book is in the nominative case as the subject, as mentioned in his saying And among the people is he who says and the explanation of Qintar has already been presented. And his saying You trust him is the reading of the majority. Ibn Waththab and Al-Ashhab Al-Uqaili read Taymanu with a kasra on the upper ta' according to the language of Bakr and Tamim, and similar is the reading of those who read Nasta'een with a kasra on the noon. Nafi' and Al-Kisa'i read yu'addah with a kasra on the ha' in Ad-Daraj. Abu Ubaid said: Abu Amr, Al-A'mash, Hamzou and Asim agreed in the narration of Abu Bakr on the sukoon on the ha'. An-Nahhas said: The sukoon on the ha' is not permissible except in poetry according to some grammarians, and some of them do not permit it at all and see that it is a mistake for those who read it, and it gives the impression that the jazm falls on the ha' and Abu Amr is too noble for anything like this to be permissible for him, and the correct thing about him is that he used to break the ha'. Al-Farra’ said: The doctrine of some Arabs is to make the ha’ quiescent if what precedes it is moved, so they say: We struck him with severe striking, just as they make the mim quiescent in you and you stood up. And he recited: When he saw that there was no peace or satisfaction, he turned to his land and lay down. Abu al-Mundhir Salam and al-Zuhri read it with a damma on the ha’ without a waw. Qatada, Hamza and Mujahid read it with a waw in the inclusion. The meaning of the verse is that among the People of the Book is the trustworthy one who fulfills his trust even if it is large, and among them is the traitor who does not fulfill his trust even if it is small. Whoever is trustworthy in much, is even more trustworthy in little, and whoever is traitorous in little, is even more traitorous in much. His statement, except as long as you are standing over it is an empty exception, meaning that he will not return it to you under any circumstances except as long as you are standing over it, demanding it, pressuring it, and demanding its return. The reference in his statement, that, is to the omission of fulfillment indicated by his statement, does not return it. The illiterate are the Arabs who are not People of the Book: meaning, there is no blame on us for their injustice because they oppose us in our religion, and they claim, may God curse them, that this is in their book, so God Almighty responded to them by saying, “And they tell lies about God while they know. * Yes.” meaning, yes, there is a way for them because of their lies and their taking the Arabs’ money as permissible.
3:76: His saying: 76- Yes is confirmation of what they denied from the path. Al-Zajjaj said: The speech was completed by his saying Yes then he said whoever fulfills his covenant and fears God and this is a new sentence: meaning whoever fulfills his covenant and fears God is not among the liars. Or God loves him, and the pronoun in his saying with his covenant refers to whom, or to God the Most High, and the generality of the righteous takes the place of the one who refers to whom, meaning: God loves him.
3:77: His statement 77- Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God means: they exchange, as was previously stated more than once. The covenant of God is what they pledged to Him regarding belief in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the oaths are what they swore that they would believe in him and support him, and the reason for the revelation of the verse will come, Those meaning: those described with this description will have no portion in the Hereafter meaning: no share nor will God speak to them at all as is indicated by the deletion of the subject of the generalization, that He will not speak to them with what pleases them nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection with a look of mercy, rather He will be angry with them and punish them for their sins as is indicated by His statement and for them is a painful punishment. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will return it to you, he said: This is from the Christians. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a dinar, he said: This is from the Jews. Except as long as you stand over him, he said: Except as long as you seek him and follow him. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: That is because they said, ‘There is no blame upon us for the unlettered ones,’ he said: The Jews said: There is no blame upon us for what we have taken from the wealth of the Arabs. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Al-Suddi. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: That is because they said, ‘There is no blame upon us for the unlettered ones,’ the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The enemies of God have lied. There is nothing that existed in the Age of Ignorance but that it is under these two feet of mine, except for the trust, for it is returned to the righteous and the wicked.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa`sa`ah that he asked Ibn Abbas and said: We take from the wealth of the People of the Covenant during the conquest, chickens and sheep. Ibn Abbas said: What do you say? He said: We say that there is no harm in that. He said: This is like what Ibn Abbas said: There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered ones if they pay the jizyah, their wealth is not lawful for you except with their willing consent. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Yes, whoever fulfills his covenant and fears God meaning fears polytheism then indeed, God loves the righteous meaning those who fear polytheism. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, the Sunan scholars and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever swears an oath in which he is wicked in order to seize the wealth of a Muslim will meet God while He is angry with him. Al-Ash`ath ibn Qays said: “By God, that was the case. There was a land between me and a Jewish man and he denied it, so I brought him to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me: “Do you have proof?” I said: No. He said to the Jew: Swear. I said: O Messenger of God, then he will swear and my wealth will be lost. Then God revealed: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price until the end of the verse. It has been narrated that the reason for the revelation of the verse was that a man was swearing in the market that he had given for his goods what he had not been given for them. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and others. It has been narrated that the reason for its revelation was a dispute that took place between Al-Ash`ath, Imru` al-Qays and a man from Hadhramaut. Narrated by Al-Nasa’i and others.
3:78: That is: a group of Jews who distort, that is, they distort and deviate from the intended meaning. The root of lay is inclination. He says: He twisted his head meaning he inclined it. It was also read: yalawun with emphasis, and yalawun with the conversion of the waw to a hamza, then its softening by deletion. The pronoun in His statement 78- that you may think it refers back to what yalawun indicates, which is the distortion that they brought. His statement and it is not from the Book is a circumstantial clause, as is His statement and it is not from God and His statement and they know meaning that they are liars and fabricators. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And among them is a party who distort their tongues, he said: They are the Jews, they used to add to the Book what God had not revealed. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, he said: They distort it.
3:79: That is, it was not appropriate and proper for a human being to say this statement while he has that characteristic. And in it is a statement from God, the Most High, to His servants that the Christians fabricated against Jesus, peace be upon him, what was not authentically attributed to him, and he should not have said it. The ruling is: understanding and knowledge. His saying 79- But be that is: But the Prophet says: Be Rabbaniyyin, and Rabbaniyyin is attributed to the Lord with the addition of the alif and the nun for emphasis, just as someone with a large beard is called Lahayaniyy, someone with a large forelock is called Jammaniyy, and someone with a thick neck is called Raqbaniyyin. It was said: The Rabbaniyyin is the one who educates people with the small things of knowledge before the big things, so it is as if he follows the example of the Lord, the Most High, in making things easy. Al-Mubarrad said: The Rabbaniyyin are the masters of knowledge, and the singular is Rabbaniyyin, from His saying Rabbi yarubihu, so he is Ban: if he manages it and corrects it, and the Ya is for the relation, so the meaning of Rabbani is: the one who knows the religion of the Lord, the strong one who adheres to the obedience of God, and it was said: the knowledgeable and wise one. His saying, Because you used to know means: because you are scholars: that is, be rabbis for this reason, because a person’s attainment of knowledge and his study results in rabbiyyah, which is teaching knowledge and the strength of adherence to obedience to God. Ibn Abbas and the people of Kufa read Because you used to know with emphasis. Abu Amr and the people of Medina read it with emphasis. Abu Ubaid chose the first reading. He said: Because it combines both meanings. Makki said: The emphasis is more eloquent because a scholar may be a scholar who is not a teacher, so the emphasis indicates knowledge and teaching, while the emphasis only indicates knowledge. Abu Hatim chose the second reading. Abu Amr said: And its confirmation is that you study with emphasis without emphasis. The conclusion is that whoever reads with emphasis must interpret rabbiyy as something in addition to knowledge and teaching, which is that he is also sincere or wise or forbearing so that the causality becomes clear. Whoever reads with emphasis is permitted to interpret rabbiyy as a scholar who teaches people, so the meaning is: Be teachers because you are scholars and because you study knowledge. This verse is the greatest incentive for those who know to act, and one of the greatest acts of knowledge is teaching it and being sincere to God Almighty.
3:80: His saying 80- And He does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords in the accusative case in apposition to Then He says and nor is added to emphasize the negation: meaning, He does not have the right to command the worship of Himself, nor does He command the taking of the angels and the prophets as lords, but He forbids it, and it is permissible to conjoin it with that He gives it, meaning, it is not for a human being to command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords, and Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamzah read in the accusative case, and the rest read in the nominative case as a resumption and a break from the first statement: meaning, and God does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords, and this is supported by the fact that in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud it is And He will not command you. The hamzah in his saying Does He command you is to deny what was negated from the humans. And his saying after you are Muslims was used as evidence by those who said that the reason for the revelation of the verse was the permission of those Muslims who asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to prostrate to him. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Abu Rafi’ Al-Qurazi said when the Jewish and Christian rabbis from Najran gathered at the presence of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and he called them to Islam: Do you want us, O Muhammad, to worship you as the Christians worship Jesus? The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: “God forbid that we should worship other than God or command the worship of other than Him. This is not what He sent me for nor did He command me for that.” So God revealed in this regard, It is not for a human being verse. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: “It reached me that a man said: O Messenger of God, we greet you as we greet one another. Should we not prostrate to you? He said: No, but honor your Prophet and recognize the right of its people, for it is not appropriate to prostrate to anyone other than God. So God revealed, “It is not for a human being” verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Rabbaniyyin, that he said: Jurists and scholars. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Wise, knowledgeable, and patient. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Scholars, jurists. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he said: Wise, knowledgeable. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Razin regarding his statement, And what you used to study, he said: Discussing jurisprudence. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, And He does not command you to take, he said: And the Prophet does not command them.
3:81: There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying 81- And when God took the covenant of the prophets. Saeed bin Jubair, Qatadah, Tawus, Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said that God took the covenant of the prophets that they would believe in each other and command each other to do so. This is the meaning of supporting Him and believing in Him, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse. The gist of it is that God took the covenant of the first of the prophets to believe in what the other brought and support him. Al-Kisa’i said: It is possible that the meaning of And when God took the covenant of the prophets is: And when God took the covenant of those with the prophets. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas’ud: And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture. It was said: There is an omission in the speech. The meaning is: And when God took the covenant of the prophets, that you will teach people what came to you of the Book and wisdom, and that you will take from people that they will believe. This omission is indicated by His saying: And you took upon yourselves My covenant for that. What is in His saying: When I gave you means that which. Sibawayh said: I asked Al-Khalil about his statement, And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘When I gave you,’ and he said: What means which. An-Nahhas said: The meaning in Al-Khalil’s statement is what I gave you, then the ha’ was deleted due to the length of the noun, and the lam is the lam of initiation, and Al-Akhfash said this, and what is in the nominative case as initiation, and its predicate is from the Book and Wisdom. His statement, Then it came to you, and what follows it is a sentence conjoined to the relative clause, and the pronoun is deleted, meaning it is believed in. Al-Mubarrad, Al-Zajjaj, and Al-Kisa’i said: What is a conditional clause that the lam of verification entered upon, just as it enters upon in, and you shall surely believe in it is the answer to the oath, which is taking the covenant, as it is like an oath, as you say, I took your covenant that you shall do such-and-such, and it is the equivalent of the recompense. Al-Kisa’i said: The recompense is his statement, So whoever turns away. He said in Al-Kashshaf: The lam in his statement when I gave you is the lam of introduction and the lam in his statement you will surely believe is the answer to the oath, and what is possible is that it includes the meaning of the condition, and you will surely believe is the answer to the oath and the condition together, and that it is connected with the meaning of for that which I gave you so that you will surely believe in it. Hamza read when I gave you with a kasra on the lam and what means who and it is related to took. The people of Madinah read ataynakum as a sign of glorification. The rest read ataytukum as a singular. It was said: that what in the reading of those who read with a kasra on the lam is a source. Its meaning is: for the sake of my giving you some of the Book and wisdom, then for the coming of a Messenger confirming what is with you, and the lam is the lam of al-Sharh 94:that is, for that reason God took a covenant from those who were given the Book to believe in it. His statement you acknowledged is from acknowledgment. And Isr in the language means: heaviness, the covenant is called Isr because of the severity in it. The meaning is: and you took my covenant on that. His statement, They said, ‘We acknowledge it,’ is an introductory sentence, as if it was said: What did they say at that time? It was said: They said, ‘We acknowledge it,’ and none of them mentioned the burden because that was sufficient. His statement, He said, ‘Then bear witness,’ means that God Almighty said, “Then bear witness,’ meaning that some of them should bear witness against others. “And I am with you among the witnesses,” meaning: I am among the witnesses to your admission and the testimony of some of you against others.
3:82: His saying 82- So whoever turns away meaning turns away from what was mentioned after that covenant they are the wicked meaning: those who are outside of obedience. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: The companions of Abdullah used to recite: “And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, ‘When I have given you a Book and wisdom,’ but we recite: “The covenant of the prophets.” Ibn Abbas said: God only took a covenant from the prophets from their people. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Tawus regarding the verse, he said: God took a covenant from the prophets that they would believe in each other. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And when God took a covenant from the prophets, he said: It is a mistake in the book, and in Ibn Masoud’s reading it is the covenant of those who were given the Scripture. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ali who said: God did not send a prophet, Adam or anyone after him, except that He took a covenant from him regarding Muhammad that if he was sent while he was alive, he would believe in him and support him and command him to take a covenant from his people, then he recited: And when God took a covenant from the prophets the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on his authority regarding his statement, My covenant, he said: My covenant. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ali regarding his statement, He said, ‘Then bear witness,’ he said: So bear witness against your nations regarding that, and I am with you among the witnesses, against you and against them, But whoever turns away, from you, O Muhammad, after this covenant from all nations, they are the wicked, they are the disobedient in disbelief.
3:83: His statement 83- Afghair is in apposition to an implied word, meaning: Do you turn away and seek other than the religion of God? The object is brought forward because it is the intended meaning of the denial. Abu Amr alone read Yabghoon with a lower case and Taraj'oon with a higher case. He said: Because the first is specific and the second is general, so a distinction was made between them due to their difference in meaning. Hafs read with a lower case in both instances. The rest read with a higher case in both instances, and Ta'wil wa-Khara was in the accusative case as a state, meaning willingly and under duress. Ta'wil means submission and following with ease, and Khara means that which involves hardship, and it is from someone who became Muslim for fear of being killed, and his Islam is his surrender from him.
3:84: His statement 84- We believe is a statement from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, about himself and his nation. We make no distinction between any of them, just as the Jews and Christians made distinctions, believing in some and disbelieving in others. The interpretation of this verse has already been presented. And we are Muslims to Him, meaning: obedient and sincere.
3:85: His statement 85- A religion is the object of the verb: meaning he seeks a religion while it is other than Islam. It is permissible for other than Islam to be in the accusative case as the object of the verb, and religion is either a distinguishing feature or a state if it is interpreted by the derivative, or a substitute for other. His statement and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers is either in the accusative case as a state or a renewed sentence: meaning among those who will fall into loss on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Tabarani narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, he said: As for those in the heavens, they are the angels, and as for those on the earth, they are those who were born as Muslims, and as for those who were forced, they are those who were brought from the captives of the nations in chains and shackles, they are led to Paradise unwillingly. Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the verse, The angels obeyed him in the heaven, and the Ansar and Abd al-Qais obeyed him on the earth. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said regarding the verse, Whoever is in the heavens and the earth submits, when He took the covenant from them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And to Him submits, he said: Knowledge. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, he said: As for the believer, he submitted willingly, so that benefited him and was accepted from him. As for the disbeliever, he submitted when he saw the wrath of God, but that did not benefit him and was not accepted from him. So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our wrath. Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has a bad character among slaves, animals, or children, then recite in his ear, ‘Do they seek other than the religion of God?’ Ibn Al-Sunni narrated in Amal Al-Yawm Wal-Laylah on the authority of Yunus bin Ubaid who said: There is no man who is on a difficult animal and recites in its ear, ‘Do they seek other than the religion of God?’ the verse except that it will be humbled by the permission of God Almighty. Ahmad and Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The deeds will come on the Day of Resurrection, and the prayer will come and say: O Lord, I am the prayer. He will say: You are on the right path. The charity will come and say: O Lord, I am the charity. He will say: You are on the right path. The fasting will come and say: I am the fasting.
