He will say: You are on the right path. Then the deeds will come, and God will say: You are on the right path. Then Islam will come and say: O Lord, You are peace and I am Islam. He will say: You are on the right path. Through you today I take and through you I give. God the Most High said in His Book: ‘And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted of him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.’”
3:86: His saying 86- How can God guide a people? This question means denial: that is, God does not guide. Similar to it is the Almighty’s saying: How can the polytheists have a covenant with God? That is, they have no covenant. Similar to it is the saying of the poet: How can I sleep on the bed while a fierce raid covers Damascus? That is: I have no sleep. The meaning of the verse is: God does not guide a people to the truth who disbelieved after their belief, and after they witnessed that the Messenger was true, and after the clear proofs came to them from the Book of God, the Most High, and the miracles of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. His statement, And God does not guide the wrongdoing people is a circumstantial clause: that is, how can He guide the apostates, when the fact is that He does not guide those among them who merely wronged themselves, and among them are those who remain in disbelief? There is no doubt that the sin of the apostate is more severe than the sin of one who remains in disbelief, because the apostate has known the truth, then turned away out of stubbornness and rebellion.
3:87: His statement 87- Those refers to the people who are described by the previous characteristics, and it is a subject whose predicate is the sentence that follows it. The explanation of the curse has been presented previously.
3:88: His saying 88- nor do they give respite means: they delay and give respite.
3:89: Then he made an exception for the repentant. He said 89- Except for those who repent after that: meaning after apostasy and reform with Islam what they had corrupted of their religion through apostasy. This is evidence of the acceptance of the repentance of the apostate if he returns to Islam sincerely, and there is no disagreement about that as far as I remember.
3:90: His saying 90- "Then they increased in disbelief." Qatada, Ata' al-Khurasani and al-Hasan said: It was revealed about the Jews and Christians who disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after believing in his description and attributes. "Then they increased in disbelief" by continuing in their disbelief. It was said: They increased in disbelief because of the sins they acquired. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari preferred this and made it specific to the Jews. A group of commentators found difficulty in the words of God Almighty: "Their repentance will not be accepted" even though repentance is accepted as in the first verse, and as in His words: "And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants" and other than that. It was said: The meaning is that their repentance will not be accepted at death. Al-Nahhas said: This is a good statement, as God Almighty said: And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, ‘Indeed, I have repented now.’ Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ata’ said the same. From this is the hadith: God accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he is not at the point of death. It was said: The meaning is that their repentance that they were upon before they disbelieved will not be accepted, because disbelief is nullified. It was said: Their repentance will not be accepted if they repent from their disbelief to another disbelief. It is better to interpret the non-acceptance of their repentance in this verse as referring to someone who died as a disbeliever without repenting, as if he expressed death in disbelief as the non-acceptance of repentance, and the aforementioned verse comes after this verse.
3:91: And it is His statement, Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers in the ruling of explaining it. His statement, filling the earth with gold, filling with the kasra is the amount that fills something, and filling with the fatha is the source of filling something, and gold is a distinction, as stated by al-Farra' and others. Al-Kisa'i said: It is accusative because of the implication of from gold. Like his statement, or the equivalent of that in fasting, meaning from fasting. Al-A'mash read gold with the nominative as a substitute for filling, and the waw in his statement, even if he ransomed himself with it, it was said: It is an intrusive and redundant letter, and the meaning is if he ransomed himself with it, and it was said: It is based on the rich as if it was said: No ransom will be accepted from any of them even if he ransomed himself with the earth full of gold, and it was said: It is an appositive to something implied: that is, no one will be accepted from him filling the earth with gold even if he gave it in charity in this world, even if he ransomed himself with it from the punishment: meaning with its like. Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: "There was a man from the Ansar who converted to Islam, then he apostatized and joined the polytheists. Then he regretted it and sent to his al-Nas 114:Send to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), is there any repentance for me? So the verse was revealed: 'How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief?' until His saying: 'Forgiving, Most Merciful.' So his people sent to him and he converted to Islam." 'Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid, and he said: He is Al-Harith Ibn Suwaid. 'Abd Ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Suddi. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was also narrated on the authority of a group similarly. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-'Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: 'How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief?' He said: They are the People of the Book from the Jews who knew Muhammad then disbelieved in him. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: They are the People of the Book from the Jews and Christians, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Al-Bazzar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that some people converted to Islam then apostatized, then converted to Islam then apostatized, so they sent to their people asking for them, so they mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief Al-Suyuti said: This is a mistake by Al-Bazzar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse, he said: The repentance of the Jews and Christians will not be accepted at the time of death. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, he said: They are the Jews who disbelieved in the Gospel and Jesus, then increased in disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding the verse, he said: It was revealed about the Jews and Christians who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief due to sins they committed, then went to repent from those sins in their disbelief. If they had been on the right path, their repentance would have been accepted, but they are still misguided. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the words Then they increased in disbelief, he said: They grew in their disbelief. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the words Then they increased in disbelief, he said: They died while they were disbelievers. Their repentance will not be accepted, he said: If he repents at the time of his death, his repentance will not be accepted. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding the words Their repentance will not be accepted, he said: They continued committing sins but did not repent from the beginning. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the words And they died while they were disbelievers, he said: It refers to every disbeliever. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The disbeliever will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him: ‘Tell me, if you had the earth full of gold, would you ransom yourself with it?’ He will say: ‘Yes.’ It will be said to him: ‘You were asked for something easier than that,’ and that is what God Almighty said: ‘Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers’ 17:10.”
3:92: This is a renewed speech addressing the believers after mentioning what does not benefit the disbelievers. His statement, "You will never attain righteousness." It is said: "A favor from so-and-so has reached me. And an-Nawal means giving, from your saying, I bestowed upon him a favor, meaning, I gave him. And an-Nawal" means righteous deeds. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Ata', Mujahid, Amr ibn Maymun, and As-Suddi said: It is Paradise. So the meaning of the verse, "You will never attain righteous deeds or Paradise," means, you will not reach that and attain it until you spend from what you love, meaning until your spending is from your money that you love. 92- "Min is a particle, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, until they spend some of what you love." It was said: It is explanatory. "And" is a relative or a description, and what is meant is spending in the way of goodness from charity or other acts of obedience. It was said: What is meant is the obligatory zakat. His saying, of anything, is an explanation of his saying, whatever you spend, meaning: whatever you spend of anything, whether good or bad, then indeed, God is Knowing of it. “What” is a conditional particle that makes it imperative. His saying, then indeed, God is Knowing of it, is an explanation of the answer to the condition, and it is in its place. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Anas that “when this verse was revealed, Abu Talha came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, the most beloved of my possessions to me is Bir Ha’, and it is charity.” The hadith has been narrated with different wordings. Abd ibn Humayd and Al-Bazzar narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: This verse came to my mind: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. So I remembered what God had given me and found nothing more beloved to me than Marjana, my Roman slave girl. I said: She is free for the sake of God, so if I were to seek refuge in something that I have made for God, I would marry her. So I married her to Nafi’.” Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab that he wrote to Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari to buy him a slave girl from the captives of Jalula. Umar called for her and said: God says: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. So Umar freed her. Sa`id ibn Mansur, `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: When the verse was revealed, Zayd ibn Haritha came with his horse called Subul, and he had no wealth that he loved more than it, so he said: It is charity. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding the words of God the Almighty: You will never attain righteousness, he said: Paradise. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of `Amr ibn Maymun and al-Suddi something similar. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Masruq something similar.
3:93: His statement 93- All food means the food, and the solution is a source that is the same for the singular and plural and the masculine and feminine, and it is the lawful and Israel is Jacob as was previously explained. The meaning of the verse is that all foods were lawful for the children of Jacob, nothing was forbidden to them except what Israel forbade himself. An explanation of what he forbade himself will come, and this exception is connected to the name of was. His saying, before the Torah was revealed, is related to his saying, it was lawful, meaning that all foods were lawful, before the Torah was revealed, meaning that everything except what was excluded was lawful for them, before the Torah was revealed, including the prohibition of what He prohibited for them because of their injustice. It contains a response to the Jews when they denied what God Almighty told His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the reason for what God prohibited for them was their injustice and transgression, as in His saying, Because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We prohibited for them [certain] good things which had been lawful for them, the verse. And His statement, And We forbade the Jews every animal with claws, and of the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fat, until His statement, That is how We recompensed them for their transgression, and they said: It is a mercy for the prophets before them, meaning by that to deny what God related to our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in His Noble Book. Then God, the Exalted, commanded him to argue with them with their Book and to make between him and them a judgement that God revealed to them, not what He revealed to him, so He said, Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful,’ so that you would know the truth of what God related in the Qur’an that nothing was forbidden to the Children of Israel before the revelation of the Torah except what Jacob forbade himself. And in this there is fairness to the opponents that cannot be measured or reached.
3:94: Then he said 94- So whoever invents a lie against God after that meaning: after bringing the Torah and reciting it they are the wrongdoers meaning: those who are excessive in their wrongdoing and who go to extremes in it, for there is no one more unjust than one who is judged by his book and what he believes to be correct law.
3:95: Then he argued after that, fabricating lies against God. Then, since what they fabricated of lies after the proof was established against them in their book was false and rejected, and what God Almighty narrated in the Qur’an and the Torah confirmed was true and honest, and the proof of this honesty was with evidence that the opponent could not refute, God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call out God’s honesty after he recorded the lie against them, so He said 95- “Say: God has spoken the truth, so follow the religion of Abraham,” meaning: the religion of Islam that I am upon. The meaning of Hanif has been explained previously, and it is as if He said to them: If my honesty and the honesty of what I have brought are clear to you, then enter my religion, for among the things that God revealed to me is And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him. Al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “The Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell us what Israel forbade himself? He said: He lived in the desert and suffered from the sweat of women and did not find anything suitable for him except the prohibition of camels and their milk, so he forbade them. They said: You have spoken the truth.” He mentioned the hadith. Ahmad and al-Nasa’i also narrated it. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: The sweat I find is the sweat of women, so he used to spend the night in a water skin, meaning a screaming camel, so he made a promise to God that if he cured him, he would not eat meat in which there was a sweat, so the Jews forbade it. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibn Abbas from his saying what al-Tirmidhi narrated previously on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to say: What Israel forbade himself was the two appendages of the liver and kidneys and the fat except what was on the back. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the Torah was revealed prohibiting what Israel prohibited. So God said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful.’ They lied. It is not in the Torah.
3:96: This is the beginning of explaining something else that the Jews argued about falsely, which is that they said: The Holy House is better and greater than the Kaaba because it is the place where the prophets migrated and it is in the Holy Land. God responded to them by saying 96- Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind verse. His saying established is a description of the House and the report of His saying for that at Makkah so God Almighty pointed out that it was the first place of worship and that it is better than others. There is a difference of opinion about who built it in the beginning. It was said the angels, it was said Adam, and it was said Abraham. This is reconciled by the fact that the first one to build it was the angels, then Adam renovated it, then Abraham. Bakkah is a name for the Sacred Land, as is Mecca, and they are two languages. It was said that Bakkah is the name of the location of the House, and Mecca is the name of the Sacred Land. It was said that Bakkah is for the mosque, and Mecca is for the entire Sanctuary. It was said that it was named Bakkah because of the crowding of people during the circumambulation. It is said that the people crowded together, and it was said that Bakkah means to break the neck. It was named that because it used to break the necks of tyrants. As for naming it Mecca, it was said that it was named that because of its little water. It was also said that it is because it pulls the marrow from the bone due to the hardship that its inhabitant endures. From this comes the word makakat to extract what is in it, and maka to suck the udder of a young camel, and imtaka to suck it. It was also said that it was named that because it destroys someone who has been wronged there. His statement, blessed is a state of the pronoun in the context, or of the object of the circumstance, because the estimate is for the one who settled in Bakkah blessed, and blessing is the abundance of good that comes to those who settle in it or intend to go there, meaning the doubled reward. The clear and evident signs: Among them are Safa and Marwa, and the footprint on the solid rock, and that if the rain falls in the direction of the Yemeni corner, there will be fertility in Yemen, and if it falls in the direction of the Levant, there will be fertility in the Levant, and if it covers the House, there will be fertility in all countries, and the birds’ deviation from flying in its air at all times, and the destruction of those who intend to go to it from the tyrants, and other things.
3:97: And his saying the station of Abraham instead of signs, Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Mubarrad said. And he said in Al-Kashaf: It is an explanatory apposition. Al-Akhfash said: It is a subject, and its predicate is omitted, and the estimation from it is the station of Abraham, and it was said: It is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning: It is the station of Abraham. The author of Al-Kashaf had difficulty explaining the signs, which are plural with the station, which is singular. And he answered that the station alone was made in the position of signs due to the strength of its status or because it includes signs. He said: It is permissible to mean in it clear signs, the station of Abraham, and whoever enters it is safe, because the two are a type of plural. His saying and whoever enters it is safe is a renewed sentence to explain a ruling of the rulings of the sanctuary, which is that whoever enters it is safe, and this is what was proven by those who said: Whoever seeks refuge in the sanctuary and a punishment of the punishments is due to him, then the punishment is not carried out on him until he leaves it, and this is the saying of Abu Hanifa and those who followed him, and the majority disagreed with him and said: The punishments are carried out on him in the sanctuary. A group of people said: The verse is a statement in the sense of a command: that is, whoever enters it, then make it safe, like His saying: There shall be no obscenity, nor wickedness, nor disputing, that is, do not be obscene, nor wicked, nor dispute. His saying: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God. The lam in His saying to God is what is called the lam of obligation and compulsion, then this meaning is emphasized by the letter upon, as it is one of the clearest indications of obligation among the Arabs, as if someone says to someone, I owe such and such, then God, the Exalted, mentioned Hajj in the most eloquent way that indicates obligation, emphasizing its right and magnifying its sanctity. This address includes all people, and only those who are specifically excluded from it are those for whom evidence has specified, such as a boy or a slave. His saying: Whoever is able to do so is in the accusative case as a substitute for some of the people. Most grammarians said the same. Al-Kisa’i permitted it to be in the nominative case with Hajj. The meaning is: that whoever is able to do so should perform Hajj to the House. It was said: Min is a conditional letter, and the consequence is omitted: that whoever is able to do so should perform Hajj. The scholars have differed about what is the ability? It was said: The provisions and the mount. A group of the Companions agreed with this view, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from most of the scholars, and it is the truth. Malik said: If a man is confident in his strength, then Hajj is obligatory for him even if he does not have provisions and a mount if he is able to earn a living. Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayr, Al-Sha’bi and Ikrimah said the same. Ad-Dahhak said: If he is a strong, healthy young man who does not have money, then he should hire himself out to complete his Hajj. Among the things that are primarily included in being able to do Hajj is that the road to Hajj is safe, such that the pilgrim feels safe for himself and his money, as he cannot find any other provisions. However, if it is not safe, then there is no ability, because God the Almighty says: Whoever can afford a way to it, and this person who fears for himself or his money cannot afford a way to it, without a doubt or suspicion. The scholars differed if there are oppressors on the road who take some money in a way that does not deprive him of the provisions for Hajj. Ash-Shafi’i said: He should not be given a single grain, and the obligation of Hajj is dropped from him. A group agreed with him, but others disagreed. It appears that whoever is able to obtain provisions and a mount and the road is safe such that he can pass through it even if he has to compromise with some oppressors to pay some money that will enable the pilgrim and will not reduce his provisions or cause him harm, then Hajj is not dropped from him, but rather it is obligatory upon him because he has been able to travel by paying some money. However, this money paid on the road is part of what ability depends on. So if a man finds provisions and a mount but does not find what to pay to the one who collects the tax on the road, Hajj is not obligatory upon him because he is unable to travel to it, and this is necessary. It does not contradict the interpretation of ability as provisions and a mount, because it is impossible to pass through the Hajj road for whoever finds provisions and a mount except with the amount that the tax collectors take. Perhaps the reason for Al-Shafi’i’s statement that Hajj is dropped is that taking this tax is reprehensible, so the pilgrim is not obligated to enter into reprehensible, and that he is therefore not able. Among what is included in ability is that the pilgrim be physically healthy in a way that enables him to ride. If he is at a time such that he is not able to walk or ride, then even if he finds provisions and a mount, he is not able to travel. His statement, And whoever disbelieves, then indeed, God is independent of the worlds. It was said that he used the word disbelief to refer to abandoning Hajj, emphasizing its obligation and making it more severe for the one who abandons it. It was also said that the meaning is: And whoever disbelieves in the obligation of Hajj and does not see it as an obligation. It was also said that whoever abandons Hajj while being able to do so is a disbeliever. In His statement, then indeed, God is independent of the worlds, there is evidence of the hatred of the one who abandons Hajj despite being able to do so, and his abandonment and distance from God, the Exalted, which is overwhelming to the one who hears it and makes his heart tremble, for God, the Exalted, only legislated these laws for His servants to benefit and benefit them, and He, the Most High and Most Holy is His Power, is independent, and all of the obedience of His servants does not return to Him with any benefit. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib regarding his statement, The first House al-Baqarah 2:13, that there were houses before it, but it was the first house established for the worship of God. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “I said, ‘O Messenger of God, which mosque was established first?’ He said, ‘The Sacred Mosque.’ I said, ‘Then which?’ He said, ‘The Al-Aqsa Mosque.’ I said, ‘How much time is between them?’ He said, ‘Forty years.’” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: “God created the House two thousand years before the Earth, and when His Throne was on the water it was a white foam, and the Earth beneath it was like a small crust, then the Earth was rolled out from beneath it.” Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Azraqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: It has reached us that the Jews said: Jerusalem is greater than the Kaaba because it is the place of migration of the prophets, and because it is in the Holy Land. The Muslims said: Rather, the Kaaba is greater. This reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the following verse was revealed: Indeed, the first House until in it are clear signs is the station of Abraham and that is not in Jerusalem. And whoever enters it shall be safe and that is not in Jerusalem. And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God and that is not in Jerusalem. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Al-Zubayr who said: It was called Bakkah because people come to it from every direction as pilgrims. Saeed Ibn Mansour, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mujahid: It was called Bakkah because people weep in it, meaning they crowd together. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil Ibn Hibban regarding his statement: Blessed he said: He made goodness and blessing in it. And a guidance for the worlds meaning: with guidance their qibla. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, In it are clear signs, among them is the Station of Abraham and Al-Mash’ar. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, In it are clear signs, he said: The Station of Abraham. “And whoever enters it shall be safe. And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God.” Al-Azraqi narrated something similar on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And whoever enters it shall be safe, he said: This was in the days of ignorance. If a man committed every sin against himself and then sought refuge in the Sacred Sanctuary, he would not be denied or sought. As for Islam, he is not prevented from the limits set by God. Whoever steals therein shall have his hand cut off, whoever commits adultery therein shall have his punishment carried out, and whoever kills therein shall be killed. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Azraqi narrated on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, he said: If I found the killer of Al-Khattab therein, I would not touch him until he came out of it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And whoever enters it shall be safe, he said: Whoever seeks refuge in the House, the House will grant him refuge, but he shall not be given shelter, food or drink. So if he goes out, he will be punished for his sin. This meaning has been narrated on his authority through various chains of narration. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: If I had found my father’s killer in the Sacred Sanctuary, I would not attack him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: If I had found my father’s killer in the Sacred Sanctuary, I would not attack him. Al-Bukhari and Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Shuraih al-Adawi that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up the next day on the day of the conquest and said: “Indeed, God has made Mecca a sanctuary, but not the people. It is not permissible for a person who believes in God and the Last Day to shed blood there or cut down a tree there. If someone seeks permission to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then say: God has given permission to His Messenger but has not given you permission. He only gave me permission for an hour of the day, then its sanctity today has returned to being like its sanctity yesterday.” Ad-Daraqutni and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that was authenticated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about his statement, Whoever can find a way to it, and it was said, What is the way? He said, Provisions and a mount. Ash-Shafi’i, Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Adi, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that a man stood up and said, What is the way? He said, Provisions and a mount. Ad-Daraqutni and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in their Sunan on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Aisha, who said, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked, ‘What is the way to Hajj?’ He said, ‘Provisions and a mount.’” Ad-Daraqutni narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), similarly. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), similarly. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This hadith has been narrated through chains of transmission, the least of which is that it is good for others, so it is not harmed by what was said through some of its chains of transmission, as is well known. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ali, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, regarding the verse: “The Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, was asked and he said: ‘You can find the back of a camel.’” Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab regarding his statement, Whoever can afford it, he said: Provisions and a mount. They narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Majah, At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority that he said: The way is for the body of the slave to be healthy and for him to have the price of provisions and a mount without being deprived of it. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd ibn Humayd narrated on his authority that he said: A way is for whoever has the means to it and nothing stands between him and it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr that he said: Ability is strength. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of An-Nakha’i that he said: The mahram for a woman is from the way that God said. It has been proven that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade a woman from traveling without a mahram. The hadiths differed regarding the length of time. Some say three days, some say a day and a night, and some say a postal mail. There are hadiths that severely threaten those who possess provisions and a mount but do not perform Hajj. At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever possesses provisions and a mount to take him to the House of God but does not perform Hajj to the House of God, then there is no harm in him dying as a Jew or a Christian. This is because God says: "And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses for one's expenses. But whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is independent of the worlds." In its chain of transmission is Hilal Al-Khurasani Abu Hashim. Al-Bukhari said: He is a fabricator of hadith. It was also said: He is unknown. Ibn 'Adi said: This hadith is not trustworthy. Its chain of transmission also includes Al-Harith Al-A'war, who is weak. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad in the Book of Faith, Abu Ya'la, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Whoever dies without performing Hajj al-Islam, and is not prevented by an incapacitating illness, a tyrannical ruler, or an obvious need, then let him die in whatever state he wishes, as a Jew or a Christian." Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet and without a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, similar to this. Saeed ibn Mansur narrated, and al-Suyuti said with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: I was about to send men to these cities to look for everyone who had a grandmother and did not perform Hajj and impose the jizyah on them. They are not Muslims, they are not Muslims. Al-Ismaili narrated from him, who said: Whoever is able to perform Hajj but does not perform Hajj, it is the same to him whether he dies a Jew or a Christian. Ibn Kathir said after citing his chain of transmission: This is a sound chain of transmission. Saeed ibn Mansur and Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar from him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Umar, Whoever dies while he is well-off and did not perform Hajj will come on the Day of Resurrection with the words ‘unbeliever’ written between his eyes. Saeed ibn Mansur narrated from him, “Whoever finds a way to perform Hajj for a year, then a year, then a year, then dies without performing Hajj, no funeral prayer will be performed for him, and it is not known whether he died a Jew or a Christian.” Saeed ibn Mansur narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: If people abandoned Hajj, I would fight them for it as we fight them for prayer and zakat.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And whoever disbelieves, then indeed, God is Free of need, he said: Whoever claims that it is not obligatory upon him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: Whoever disbelieves in Hajj, then he does not see his Hajj as righteousness nor does his abandonment of it as sin. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ikrimah who said: “When the verse, ‘And whoever desires other than Islam as religion,’ was revealed, the Jews said: So we are Muslims. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: God has made Hajj obligatory upon the Muslims. They said: It was not prescribed for us and they refused to perform Hajj. God said: ‘And whoever disbelieves, then indeed, God is Free from need of the worlds.’” And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar. And Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: “When the verse of Hajj was revealed: ‘And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind’, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gathered the people of the religions, the polytheists of the Arabs, the Christians, the Jews, the Zoroastrians and the Sabians, and said: ‘God has made Hajj obligatory upon you, so perform Hajj to the House.’ But none accepted it except the Muslims. Five religions disbelieved in it, and said: ‘We do not believe in it, nor do we pray towards it, nor do we face it.’ So God revealed: ‘And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is independent of the worlds.’” And Abd bin Hamid and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Dawud Nafi’ who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: ‘And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind’, and a man from Hudhayl stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, whoever abandons it has disbelieved?’ He said: ‘Whoever abandons it does not fear its punishment, and whoever performs Hajj not hoping for its reward, that is it.’” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah regarding the verse, he said: Whoever disbelieves in the House. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God, And whoever disbelieves, he said: Whoever disbelieves in God and the Last Day. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar to his statement. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd that he was asked about that, so he recited, Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind to His statement, as a way, then he said, And whoever disbelieves, with these verses. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding the verse, he said, And whoever disbelieves, and did not believe in it, then he is a disbeliever.
3:98: His statement 98- Say, O People of the Book is addressed to the Jews and Christians, and the question in his statement Why do you disbelieve? is for denial and rebuke. And his statement And God is Witness over what you do is a circumstantial clause emphasizing rebuke and denial, and thus the use of the exaggerated form in witness indicates further emphasis and intimidation.
3:99: The question in his saying 99- Why do you turn away? indicates what the first question indicates. Al-Hasan read Tasdoon from Asda, and they are two languages: like Sada Al-Laham and Asda: if it changed and rotted, and the path of God is His religion which He has chosen for His servants, which is the religion of Islam, and Awj means inclination and deviation, it is said: Awj with a kasra if it is in religion, speech and action, and with a fatha in bodies like a wall and the like, this was narrated from Abu Ubaidah and others, and the place of his saying They seek it to be crooked is the accusative case as a state. The meaning is: You seek for it to be crooked and inclined away from the intended and straight path by making it vague to people that it is like that, as a means of educating people about your distortion and correcting your false claims. His statement, And you are witnesses, is a circumstantial clause: that is, how do you demand that by the religion of Islam while you bear witness that it is the religion of God, and that no other religion is acceptable to Him, Islam, and that it contains the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? It was said that what is meant by And you are witnesses is rational. It was also said that the meaning is that you are witnesses among the people of your religion, accepted by them, so how do you bring falsehood that contradicts what you are upon among the people of your religion? Then the Almighty threatened them with His statement, And God is not unaware of what you do.
3:100: Then the Almighty addressed the believers, warning them against obeying the Jews and Christians, explaining to them that this obedience leads to them turning them back into disbelievers after their belief. The reason for the revelation of the verse will come later. 100- O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back into disbelievers after your belief.
3:101: The question in His statement 101- And how do you disbelieve is for denial: that is, where does that come to you from when you have what prevents it and cuts off its effect, which is the recitation of God's verses to you and the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among you? The place of His statement and you and what He worshipped is the accusative case as a state. Then He guided them to hold fast to God so that they would thereby attain guidance to the straight path, which is Islam. In describing the path as straight, He responded to what they claimed of its crookedness. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for this address to be to the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among them and they witnessed him. It is permissible for this address to be to the entire nation, because his effects and his sign and the Qur'an that he was given are among us, so it is as if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is among us even if we did not witness him. The meaning of holding fast to God is to adhere to His religion and obey Him. It has also been said: to the Qur’an. It is said: he held fast to it, he held fast to it, he held fast to it, he held fast to it, he held fast to it, he held fast to it: if he refrained from anything else with it, and food protected him: he prevented hunger from him.
3:102: His saying 102- Fear God as He should be feared" meaning: the fear that is due to Him, which is that the servant does not leave anything that he is obligated to do nor does he do anything that he is obligated to leave, and he exerts his utmost effort and ability in that. Al-Qurtubi said: The commentators mentioned that when this verse was revealed, they said: O Messenger of God, who is able to do this? That was difficult for them, so God revealed: "So fear God as much as you are able" and this verse was abrogated. This was narrated from Qatadah, Al-Rabi' and Ibn Zayd. Muqatil said: There is nothing in Al Imran that was abrogated except this. It was said that His saying "Fear God as He should be feared is explained by His saying So fear God as much as you are able" and the meaning is: Fear God as He should be feared as much as you are able. He said: This is more correct, because abrogation only occurs when there is no combining, and combining is possible, so it is more appropriate. His saying, And do not die except as Muslims, meaning: Do not be in a state other than the state of Islam. So the exception is empty, and the location of the sentence: I mean his saying, and you are Muslims, is the accusative case of state. An explanation of a verse like this has already been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah.
3:103: His saying 103- And hold fast, all together, to the rope of God." The rope is a common word, and its origin in the language is the reason by which one reaches the goal, and it is either a metaphor or a representation. God, the Almighty, commanded them to unite in adhering to the religion of Islam or the Qur'an, and forbade them from division resulting from differences in religion, then He commanded them to remember God's blessing upon them and explained to them from this blessing what was appropriate for the situation, which is that they were enemies who differed in killing each other and plundering each other, so because of this blessing they became brothers and they were on the brink of a pit of fire because of their disbelief, so God saved them from this pit with Islam. The meaning of His saying "you have become" is you have become, and it is not intended to mean its original meaning: which is entering the time of morning, and the shafa of everything is its edge and so is its edge, and asfa on something: it overlooks it, and it is a representation of the state they were in during the time of ignorance. His saying, Likewise, is an indication of the source of the verb that follows it: that is, like that eloquent statement, God makes clear to you. His saying, So that you may be guided, is guidance for them to remain steadfast in guidance and increase in it. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, who said: Shas bin Qais passed by. He was an old man who had been a great disbeliever in the pre-Islamic era, and he was very harsh towards the Muslims and very envious of them. He had gathered a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Aws and Khazraj in a gathering where they were talking. He was angered by what he saw of their harmony, their unity, and their reconciliation with Islam, after the enmity that had existed between them in the pre-Islamic era. He said: The leaders of Banu Qaylah have gathered in this country, and by God, we will not have any stability with them when their leaders gather here. So he ordered a young Jewish man who was with him and said: Go to them and sit with them. Then he mentioned to them the day of Bu’ath and what had come before it, and recited to them some of the poems they used to recite on that day. It was the day of Bu’ath and what had come before it, and he recited to them some of the poems they used to recite on that day. The day of Bu’ath was a day when the Aws and Khazraj fought, and the Aws were victorious over the Khazraj, so he did so. The people spoke at that time. They argued and boasted until two men from the two tribes jumped on the camel, Aws bin Qayzi, one of the Banu Haritha of the Aws, and Jabbar bin Sakhr, one of the Banu Salamah of the Khazraj. They argued, then one of them said to his companion: If you wish, by God, we will return it now as a young camel. Both groups became angry and said: We have done so. The weapon, the weapon, your meeting place is the Dhahirah, and the Dhahirah is the Harrah. So they went out to it and the Aws joined together and the Khazraj joined together in their claim that they had in the pre-Islamic period. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he went out to them with those of his companions who were with him from the Muhajireen until he came to them and said: O group of Muslims, by God, by God, is the claim of the pre-Islamic period while I am among you after God has guided you to Islam and honored you with it and cut off from you the matter of the pre-Islamic period and saved you from disbelief and united you with it? Will you return to what you were upon as disbelievers? The people realized that it was a temptation from Satan and a plot from their enemy against them, so they threw down their weapons from their hands and wept, and the men embraced each other. Then they departed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, listening and obeying, God having extinguished from them the plot of God’s enemy, Shas. God revealed concerning Shas bin Qais and what he did, Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while God is Witness to what you do?’ to His saying, And God is not unaware of what you do. And He revealed concerning Aws bin Qayzi and Jabbar bin Sakhr and those who were with them from their people who did what they did, O you who believe, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, to His saying, And those will have a great punishment. This story has been narrated in short and long versions through various chains of narration. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi concerning His statement, Why do you avert [people] from the way of God? He said: If someone asked them, Do you find Muhammad? They said, No. He said, So they averted people from it and sought to destroy Muhammad crookedly. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada: Why do you turn away from Islam and from the Prophet of God those who believe in God, and you are witnesses to what you read in the Book of God that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that Islam is the religion of God, which does not accept anything other than it and does not reward except with it? They find it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, And whoever holds fast to God, he said: He believes in Him. They narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, he said: Holding fast is trust in God. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement, Fear God as He should be feared, he said: That He should be obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not ungrateful. Al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated it on the authority of Ibn Mardawayh from another chain of transmission on his authority, without the statement, and thanked and not ungrateful. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The right to fear Him is that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, for you will not be able to. Then God revealed after that: So fear God as much as you are able. Abd bin Hamid narrated something similar on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Masoud. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: The right to fear Him, he said: It was not abrogated, but the right to fear Him is that they strive in God’s cause as it should be striven for, and they do not let the blame of a blamer deter them in God’s cause, and they stand up for God with justice even if it is against themselves, their fathers, and their children. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Tabarani narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding His statement: And hold fast to the rope of God, he said: The rope of God is the Qur’an. There are hadiths that say that the Book of God is the extended rope of God. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, who said: And hold fast to the rope of God by being sincere to God alone. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: By obeying Him. He also narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: By his covenant and command. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, who said: By Islam. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, When you were enemies, he said: What happened between the Aws and the Khazraj regarding Aisha. Ibn Ishaq narrated, he said: The war between the Aws and the Khazraj lasted one hundred and twenty years, until Islam came, then God extinguished that and united them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement, And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, he said: You were on the edge of the Fire, whoever died among you fell into the Fire, then God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and rescued you from that pit through him.
3:104: His saying 104- And let there be The majority read it with a sukoon on the lam, and it was read with a kasra on the lam according to the original, and min in his saying from you is for partiality and it was said: to clarify the type. The first is preferred because enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong are communal obligations that are specific to the people of knowledge who know that what they enjoin is right and what they forbid is wrong. Al-Qurtubi said: The first is more correct because it indicates that enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is a communal obligation, and God the Almighty has designated them with His saying those who, if We establish them in the land [al-Muslim] and the verse. Ibn al-Zubayr read: And let there be from you a community inviting to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and seeking help from God for what has befallen them. Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari said: This addition is an interpretation from Ibn al-Zubayr and some of his words were erroneously stated by some of the narrators, so they included it with the words of the Qur'an. It was narrated that Uthman read it like this but did not write it in his Mus-haf, which indicates that it is not the Qur'an. This verse is evidence of the obligation of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. Its obligation is proven by the Book and the Sunnah, and it is one of the greatest obligations of the pure Shari’ah, a great principle of its principles, and a fortified pillar of its pillars. By it, its system is completed and its summit is elevated. His statement, They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong is a case of linking the specific to the general, to demonstrate their honor, and that they are the two perfect individuals of the good that God has commanded His servants to call to, as was said in linking Gabriel and Michael to the angels. The object of the three verbs was omitted: that is, they call, enjoin, and forbid, with the intention of generalization: that is, everyone who has a reason that requires that. The reference in His statement, And those refers back to the nation in consideration of its being described by what was mentioned after it, They are the successful ones, that is, those who are special in success. The definition of the successful ones is for the covenant or for the truth that everyone knows.
3:105: His saying 105- And do not be like those who were divided They are the Jews and Christians according to the majority of commentators, and it was said: They are the innovators of this nation, and it was said: The Kharijites, and the first is apparent. And the clear proofs are the clear verses that explain the truth and necessitate the absence of difference. It was said: This prohibition of division and difference is specific to the fundamental issues, and as for the subsidiary issues of ijtihad, difference in them is permissible, and the companions and those who came after them from the followers and their followers continued to differ in the rulings of incidents, and there is a view in it because in those eras the denial of difference continued to exist and specifying some issues of religion as permissible to differ in them and not others is not correct, so the legal issues are equal in their affiliation to the law.
3:106: And his saying 106- On the Day when faces will be white is in the accusative case with an implied verb: i.e. remember, and it was said: with what is indicated by his saying for them is a great punishment, its meaning is that a great punishment is established for them on the Day when faces will be white, i.e. on the Day of Resurrection when they are raised from their graves, the faces of the believers will be white and the faces of the disbelievers will be black. And it is said: that is when the book is read, when the believer reads his book he sees his good deeds and is happy and his face whitens, and when the disbeliever reads his book he sees his bad deeds and is sad and his face blackens. And the indefiniteness in faces is for many: i.e. many faces. Yahya bin Waththab read tabbayd and tasawud with a kasra on the two ta's. And al-Zuhri read tabiyad and tasawwad. His saying: Did you disbelieve? That is, it will be said to them: Did you disbelieve? The hamza is for rebuke and astonishment at their state. This is a detailed account of the states of the two groups after the summary. The statement of the state of the disbelievers was presented because the situation is one of warning and intimidation. It was said: They are the People of the Book, and it was said: The apostates, and it was said: The hypocrites, and it was said: The innovators.
3:107: And his saying 107- Then in the mercy of God meaning: in His Paradise and the abode of His honor. He expressed that with mercy as an indication that the work does not alone enter its doer into Paradise, rather mercy is necessary, and from it is the hadith No one will enter Paradise by his work which is in the Sahih. And his saying: They will abide therein eternally is an introductory sentence in response to an implied question. And that is an indication of what came before about the punishment of the disbelievers and the comfort of the believers.
3:108: And His saying 108- We recite it to you in truth is a circumstantial clause, and in truth is related to something omitted: i.e. clothed in truth, which is justice. And His saying And God does not desire injustice for the worlds is a tail clause confirming the content of what preceded it, and in the negation being directed to the will of the indefinite noun, there is evidence that He, glory be to Him, does not desire an individual from the individuals of injustice that befall an individual from the individuals of the world. What is meant by what is in the heavens and what is on the earth are His creations, glory be to Him: i.e. He has that, and He disposes of it as He wills and as He wills, and He expressed it with what to give precedence to the irrational over the rational because of their large number, or to place the rational in the same position as others. Al-Mahdawi said: The connection between this and what came before it is that when he mentioned the conditions of the believers and the unbelievers and that he does not want injustice for the worlds, he connected it to mentioning the breadth of his power and his independence from injustice because what is in the heavens and what is on the earth is in his grasp. It was said: It is the beginning of a statement that includes the statement to his servants that everything in the heavens and what is on the earth belongs to him so that they ask him and worship him and do not worship anyone other than him.
3:109: And his saying 109- And to God all matters return meaning: not to anyone else, neither in partnership nor independently. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Baqir who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And let there be among you a community inviting to good. ’ He said: ‘Good is following the Qur’an and my Sunnah. ’ Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah who said: ‘Every verse that God mentioned in the Qur’an regarding enjoining good is Islam and forbidding evil is worshipping idols and Satan. ’ This is a specification without specifying it, as there is nothing in the language of the Arabs or in the terminology of the Shari`ah that indicates this. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil ibn Hibban who said: ‘Inviting to good’ means Islam, ‘enjoining what is right’ means obeying their Lord, ‘and forbidding what is wrong’ means disobeying their Lord. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding the verse, saying: ‘They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically, and he is the narrators. ’ I do not know what justified this specification, as the address in this verse is like the address in all the matters that God has prescribed for His servants and charged them with. Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Jews split into seventy-one sects, and the Christians split into seventy-two sects, and my nation will split into seventy-three sects.” Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Al-Hakim narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Mu’awiyah, with the addition: All of them are in Hell except one, which is the group. Al-Hakim narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, with the addition: “All of them are in Hell except one religion. It was said to him: What is the one? He said: What I and my companions are upon today.” Ibn Majah narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Awf ibn Malik, with the addition: One is in Paradise and seventy-two are in Hell. It was said: O Messenger of God, who are they? He said: The group.” Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Anas, with the addition: “It was said: O Messenger of God, who is that group? He said: The group.” Many verses and hadiths have been narrated about enjoining good and forbidding evil, enjoining being in the group and forbidding division. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Khatib narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, On the Day when faces will be white, he said: The faces of the people of the Sunnah and the Community will be white, and the faces of the people of innovation and misguidance will be black. Al-Khatib and Al-Daylami narrated it on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, and Abu Nasr Al-Sajzi also narrated it in Al-Ibanah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, on the authority of Abu Saeed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b regarding the verse, he said: They will become two groups on the Day of Resurrection. It will be said to the one whose face was blackened, Did you disbelieve after your belief? This is the belief that was in the lineage of Adam, when they were one nation. As for those whose faces were white, they are those who were steadfast in their belief and sincere in religion, so God whitened their faces and admitted them into His pleasure and Paradise. Other than that has been narrated.
3:110: His saying 110- You were the best nation. This is a new statement that includes a statement of the state of this nation in terms of superiority over other nations. And before it was the perfect one: meaning you were found and created the best nation. And similar to it is what Sibawayh recited: Our neighbors were generous. And from it is the saying of God Almighty: How can We speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? And His saying: And remember when you were few and He made you many. Al-Akhfash said: He means the people of a nation: that is, the best people of religion, and he recited: I swore and left no doubt for you. Can a slave be held accountable while he is obedient? It was said that its meaning is: You were in the Preserved Tablet, and it was said: You were since you believed. And in it is evidence that this Islamic nation is the best nation in general, and that this freedom is shared between the first of this nation and its last in relation to other nations, even if they differ in themselves. As was mentioned in the superiority of the Companions over others. His statement, Brought forth for mankind, means: It was made apparent to them. And his statement, You enjoin what is right, etc. is a new statement that includes a statement that they are the best nation with what it includes of them being the best nation as long as they persist in that and are characterized by it. So if they abandon enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, that will be removed from them. For this reason, Mujahid said: They are the best nation according to the conditions mentioned in the verse. This requires that enjoining what is right and what follows it be in the accusative case as a state, meaning: You were the best nation while you were enjoining and forbidding, believing in God and in what you must believe in from His Book and His Messenger and what He has legislated for His servants, because belief in God, the Exalted, is not complete except by believing in these matters. His saying, And if the People of the Book had believed, meaning the Jews, with a belief like the Muslims believe in God, His Messengers, and His Books, it would have been better for them, but they did not do that. Rather, they said, We believe in some of the Book and disbelieve in some. Then He explained the state of the People of the Book by saying, Among them are believers, meaning those who believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them. They believed in what was revealed to him and what was revealed before him. But most of them are wicked, meaning those who have deviated from the path of truth, rebelled in their falsehood, and denied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought. So this detail, in this case, is a new statement, an answer to an implied question, as if it were said, Is there among them one who believed and thus deserved what God promised him?
3:111: His statement 111- "They will not harm you except with a slight harm" meaning: They will not harm you with any type of harm except with a type of harm, which is lying, distortion, and slander. They are not able to cause harm that is harm in reality through war, looting, and the like. So the exception is empty, and this is a promise from God to His Messenger and to the believers that the People of the Book will not defeat them and that they will be victorious over them. It was said: The exception is disconnected. The meaning is: They will not harm you at all, but they will harm you. Then the Almighty clarified what He denied of harm by saying: "And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you" meaning: They will be defeated and will not be able to resist you, let alone harm you. And His statement: "Then they will not be victorious" is in apposition to the conditional clause: meaning: Then there will be no victory for them and they will not be victorious under any circumstances. Rather, their condition is to be let down as long as they are. We have found what God Almighty promised us to be true, for the Jews did not see their banner of victory wave, nor did they gather an army that defeated them after the revelation of this verse. It is one of the miracles of prophecy.
3:112: His statement 112- "Humiliation has been imposed upon them." The meaning of this construction has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. The meaning is: Humiliation has surrounded them in every situation and in every situation, wherever they are found. "Except by a rope from God." That is, unless they hold fast to a rope from God. Al-Farra' said: That is, by the covenant of God or by His Book. "And a rope from the people." That is, by a covenant from the people, who are the Muslims. It was said: What is meant by the people is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. "And they returned, that is, they returned with wrath from God." It was said: they endured it. Its original meaning in the language is necessity and deservingness: that is, wrath from God has been imposed upon them, and they deserve it. The meaning of being struck with poverty is that it surrounds them from all sides. This is the case of the Jews, who are under extreme poverty and severe destitution, except for the rare and exceptional among them. The reference in His saying that is to what preceded of the humiliation, poverty and wrath, meaning: that befell them because they disbelieved in the signs of God and killed the prophets unjustly, and the reference in His saying that is to the disbelief and killing of the prophets because of their disobedience to God and their transgression of His limits. The meaning of the verse is: that God struck them with humiliation, poverty and calamity through His wrath because they disbelieved in His signs and killed His prophets because of their disobedience and transgression. Abdur-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ahmad, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, You are the best nation, that he said: They are those who migrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse that he said: Umar bin Al-Khattab said: If God had willed, He would have said: You, so we would have been all of us, but He said: You were among the special companions of Muhammad, and whoever did what they did, they were the best nation brought forth for mankind. And in another version on his authority he said: It will be for the first of us and not for the last of us. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah that he said: It was mentioned to us that Umar bin Al-Khattab recited this verse, then he said: O people, whoever is pleased to be from that nation, let him fulfill God’s condition for it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the verse that he said: It was revealed regarding Ibn Mas'ud, Ammar bin Yasir, Salim the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, Ubayy bin Ka'b and Mu'adh bin Jabal. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah regarding the verse, he said: The best people for people are those who will be brought in chains around their necks until they enter Islam. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Haidah that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say regarding the verse: You will complete seventy nations, and you are the best and most honorable of them. A similar hadith was narrated on the authority of Muadh and Abu Saeed. Many hadiths were narrated in the two Sahihs and others that seventy thousand of this nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account or punished. This is one of the benefits of it being the best of nations. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, They will not harm you except with annoyance, meaning: You will hear from them lies about God, calling you to misguidance. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Their associating partners with God in Uzair, Jesus and the cross. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatadah, Humiliation has been imposed upon them, meaning: They will pay the jizyah willingly and they will be humiliated. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of al-Dahhak. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Except by a rope from God and a rope from the people. He said: By a covenant from God and a covenant from the people.
3:113: His statement 113- They are not equal meaning: The People of the Book are not equal, but rather different, and the sentence is a resumption that came before to explain the difference between the People of the Book. His statement an established nation is also a resumption that includes explaining the aspect in which they differed from some of them being an established nation to his statement of the righteous Al-Akhfash said: The estimate from the People of the Book is one with a nation, meaning: one with a good way, and he recited: Is it worth a nation if it is obedient? It was said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: Among the People of the Book there is a nation that is established and another that is not established, so he left out the other and was satisfied with the first, like the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb. My heart disobeyed her, I am obedient to her command, so I do not know how to guide her seekers? He wanted Arshad or Ghay. Al-Farra’ said: A nation is raised equally, and the meaning is: A nation of the People of the Book who are standing and reciting the verses of God and a nation of disbelievers are not equal. Al-Nahhas said: This statement is wrong for several reasons: One of them is that it raises a nation equally so that it does not refer to the name of there is nothing, and it raises with what is not running on the verb, and it implicitly implies what is not needed because the mention of the disbeliever has already been presented, so there is no basis for implicitly implicating this. Abu Ubaidah said: This is like their saying: The fleas ate me and your companions left. Al-Nahhas said: This is wrong, because they have already been mentioned, and the fleas ate me, and no mention of the prohibition has been presented for them. I believe that what Al-Farraa said is strong and sound. The gist of it is that the meaning of the verse is: A nation from the People of the Book whose status is such and such is not equal to another nation whose status is such and such. Estimating this omission is not a matter of estimating what is not needed as Al-Nahhas said, because the previous mention of the unbeliever does not provide the meaning of estimating her mention here. As for his saying that it does not refer to a noun that is not something, this is refuted by the fact that estimating the referent is common and well-known among the people of the art. As for his saying: And it is raised by what does not run on the verb, this is not accepted. And the standing: is the straight and just, from their saying: I set up the stick and it stood up, meaning it became straight. And his saying it changes color is in the place of raising as a second description of the nation, and it is permissible for it to be in the place of accusative as a state the hours of the night its hours, and it is accusative as a circumstance. His statement, and they prostrate, appears to indicate that the recitation is from them in a state of prostration. This is not correct if what is meant by this nation described in the verse are those who have converted from the People of the Book, because it has been authentically reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he forbade reciting the Qur’an in prostration. Therefore, this apparent meaning must be interpreted to mean that what is meant by his statement, and they prostrate is while they are praying, as al-Farra’ and al-Zajjaj said. Rather, prostration is used to refer to the entirety of the prayer, because it involves submission and humility. The apparent meaning of this is that they recite the verses of God in their prayer without specifying that prayer with a specific prayer. It has been said that what is meant by it is the prayer between the two ‘Isha’s, and it has been said that it refers to the night prayer in general.
3:114: And His saying 114- They believe in God is another description of a nation: that is, they believe in God, His books, and His messengers, and the head of that is belief in what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. And His saying, And they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong are also two descriptions of a nation: that is, this is their nature and description. Its apparent meaning indicates that they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong in general. And it was said: What is meant by enjoining what is right here is their command to follow the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and by forbidding what is wrong is their prohibition from disobeying him. And His saying, And they hasten to do good deeds is also among the descriptions: that is, they hasten to do them, not being hesitant to perform them because they know the extent of their reward. And His saying, And those are among the righteous means among them. And it was said that from means with: that is, with the righteous, and they are the Companions, may God be pleased with them. And it appears that what is meant is every righteous person, and the reference in His saying, those is to the nation described by those descriptions.
3:115: His saying 115- And whatever good you do meaning good they will never deny it meaning: you will never be deprived of its reward, and it is transitive to two objects, and it is only transitive to one because it includes the meaning of deprivation, as if it was said: you will never be deprived of it as the author of Al-Kashshaf said. Al-A'mash, Ibn Waththab, Hafs, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read with the lower ya' in both verbs, and it is the reading of Ibn Abbas and Abu Ubaid chose it. The rest read with the doubled ya' from above in both of them, and it seems that Abu Amr sees both readings together. What is meant by the pious is everyone who has the attribute of piety, and it was said: What is meant is those mentioned above, and they are the nation described with that attribute, and the apparent was placed in place of the implicit in praise of them and raising their status.
3:116: And His saying 116- Indeed, those who disbelieved It was said: They are Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir. Muqatil said: When God the Almighty mentioned the believers of the People of the Book, He mentioned their disbelievers in this verse. And it appears that what is meant by that is everyone who disbelieved in what must be believed in. And the meaning of will not avail is will not repel, and He specified children because they are the most beloved of kinship and He hopes them to repel what befalls him.
3:117: And His saying 117- Like what they spend is a statement of the lack of enrichment of their money that they depended on.
