And patience: intense cold, its origin is from the creaking which is the sound/ so it is the sound of a strong wind. And Al-Zajjaj said: the sound of the flames of the fire that is in that wind. And the meaning of the verse: Like the spending of the disbelievers in its invalidity and disappearance and lack of benefit is like the example of a crop that was struck by a cold wind or fire that burned it or destroyed it, so its owners did not benefit from anything from it after they had been hoping for its benefit and advantage. Therefore, it is necessary to estimate the aspect of the simile, so it is said: like a crop that has been struck by a wind in which there is a chill, or like the destruction of what they spend is like the destruction of a wind in which there is a chill that struck the crops of a people who wronged themselves. And God did not wrong them, meaning the disbelievers who spend, but they wrong themselves, by the disbelief that prevents the acceptance of the expenditure that they spent. The object is presented to take care of the pauses, not to specify, because the speech is about the verb in consideration of its connection to the agent, not to the object. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Ma`rifah, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala`il, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When Abdullah bin Salam, Tha`laba bin Sa`id, and Asid bin Sa`id, and those Jews who converted with them, believed, were truthful, and desired Islam, the Jewish rabbis and the unbelievers among them said: None believed in Muhammad and followed him except the worst of us, and if they were the best of us they would not have abandoned the religion of their fathers and gone to another one. So God revealed: They are not equal Al-Baqarah 2:17. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: A nation that stands firm meaning: guided and upholding the command of God, not turning away from it, nor did others abandon it and waste it. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that he said: A nation that stands firm is just. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: the hours of the night he said: the middle of the night. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi` who said: the hours of the night. And Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari in his history, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement, They are not equal, he said: The People of the Book and the nation of Muhammad are not equal. They recite the verses of God during the hours of the night, he said: The Isha prayer is performed by them, and those other than them from the People of the Book do not pray it. Ahmad, Al-Nasa’i, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delayed the Isha prayer one night, then he went out to the mosque and saw the people waiting for the prayer, so he said: There is no one from the people of these religions who remembers God at this hour except you.” And the wording of Ibn Jarir and Al-Tabarani is: He said: No one from the People of the Book prays this prayer. He said: And this verse was revealed, They are not equal. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mansur that he said: I was informed that this verse was revealed, They recite the verses of God during the hours of the night and they prostrate, between the sunset and the night. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada, They will not deny it, meaning: it will not lead you astray. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, They will not deny it, meaning: you will not wrong it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse, Like what they spend, meaning the polytheists, and it will not be accepted from them, like this crop when the wrongdoing people planted it and a wind in it struck it and destroyed it, so they spent and their polytheism destroyed them. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, In it is cold, meaning: severe cold.
3:118: Al-Batana: a noun used to name the singular and plural, and the man’s batana: his confidants who conceal his affair, and its origin is the belly which is the opposite of the back, and the belly of so-and-so with so-and-so, he conceals bellies and batana: if he is pure with him, and from it the poet’s saying: They are all my loyalists, my confidants, and my family, more than any other relative. His saying 118 - From other than you means: from other than you. Al-Farra’ said: that is, from other than the Muslims, and they are the infidels: that is, an entourage that is other than you. It is permissible for it to be related to his saying Do not take. And his saying They will not spare you any trouble is in the accusative case as an attribute of the entourage. It is said: I will not spare any effort: that is, I will not fall short. Imru’ al-Qais said: As long as the heart of a person is in control of the dangers, he will not be able to What is meant is that they do not fall short in what causes corruption for you. It is transitive with two objects because it includes the meaning of prevention: that is, they do not prevent you from corruption. Corruption and madness are corruption in actions, bodies, and minds. Aws said: My sons, my sons, you are not one hand but a hand with a mad arm That is, corrupted arm. His statement, And they wished for your suffering is ma, meaning they wished for your suffering. Suffering is hardship and severe harm. The sentence is a resumption of the prohibition. His statement, The hatred has already appeared is the intensity of hatred, like distress is due to severe harm. The mouths are the plural of mouth. The meaning is that the hatred has appeared in their speech because when the intensity of hatred and envy overcame them, their tongues revealed what was in their hearts, so they abandoned taqiyya and declared their denial. As for the Jews, the matter in that is clear. As for the hypocrites, the slips of their tongues would appear that revealed the evil of their inner selves. This sentence is a resumption of the statement of their condition, And what their hearts conceal is greater because the slips of the tongue are less than what the hearts harbor, rather those slips in comparison to what is in the hearts are very few. Then, the Almighty bestowed upon them the clarification of the verses indicating the necessity of sincerity if they were among the people of minds that comprehend that statement.
3:119: His statement 119- Here you are is a sentence beginning with the letter of warning: meaning you are the ones who are wrong in their loyalty, then he explained their mistake in that loyalty with this humiliating sentence. So he said You love them and they do not love you, and it was said that his statement You love them is a second predicate for his statement you, and it was said that those are a relative pronoun and you love them is its clause, meaning: you love them because they showed you faith or because of the kinship between you and them and they do not love you because of the anger and envy that has taken hold in their hearts. His statement and you believe in the entire Book meaning in all of the Book. The location of the sentence is the accusative case as a state: meaning they do not love you and the fact is that you believe in the books of God, the Most High, which include their book, so why do you love them while they do not believe in your book. And in it is a severe rebuke to them, because the one who holds the truth is more deserving of firmness and severity than the one who is on falsehood. And when they meet you, they say, ‘We believe,’ out of hypocrisy and dissimulation. But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage, regretting and regretting that they were unable to take revenge on you. The Arabs describe the angry and regretful person biting his fingers and toes. Then God, the Most High, commanded him to invoke curses upon them, saying, Say, ‘Die in your rage,’ which implies that their rage will continue as long as they are alive until death comes to them while they are still in that state. Then He said, Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts, so He knows what is in your breasts and their breasts. What is meant by that within the breasts are the thoughts that are present in them, and it is a statement included in His saying, Say, so it is part of what is said.
3:120: His statement 120- If good befalls you, it distresses them. This sentence is a resumption to explain the extent of their enmity, and good and bad encompass everything that is good and bad. He used the expression touch in the good and hit in the bad, to indicate that merely touching good brings distress, and they do not rejoice except when they are afflicted with evil. It was said that touch is borrowed to mean hitting. The meaning of the verse is that whoever is in this state is not worthy of being taken as a confidant. And if you are patient in their enmity or in the difficult tasks and fear their friendship, or what God has forbidden you, their plot will not harm you at all. It is said: Dharahu yudhuru and Yadhuru dharan and Dhiyuran meaning Dharahu yadhuru, and Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it this way. The Kufians and Ibn Amir read la yadhurkum with a damma on the ra’ and a shaddah on it from darra yadhur. According to the first reading, it is in the jussive mood as the answer to the condition. According to the second reading, it is in the nominative case, assuming that the fa’ is omitted, as in the poet’s saying: Whoever does good deeds, God will reward them. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said this. Sibawayh said: It is raised with the intention of advancement: meaning it will not harm you if you are patient. Abu Zaid narrated on the authority of Al-Mufaddal on the authority of Asim it will not harm you with the opening of the ra’, and something is an attribute of a deleted source. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Some Muslims used to maintain close relations with some Jews because of their neighborliness and alliance during the pre-Islamic era. So God revealed concerning them, forbidding them from keeping close relations with them for fear of temptation from them: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates (al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: They are the hypocrites. Abd bin Hamid narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) who said: They are the Khawarij. Al-Suyuti said: Its chain of transmission is good. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And you believe in the entire Book meaning: in your Book and their Book and in the previous Books, and they disbelieve in your Book, so you are more deserving of hatred for them than they are for you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil, If good befalls you, meaning victory over the enemy, provision, and good, it distresses them, but if evil befalls you, meaning killing, defeat, and hardship.
3:121: The agent in idh is an omitted verb: i.e., remember when you went out from your family's home: i.e., from the home in which your family was. The majority of scholars have said that this verse was revealed in the Battle of Uhud. Al-Hasan said: On the day of Badr. Mujahid, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: In the Battle of the Trench. His statement 121- Tabwa means: you take for them positions for fighting. The origin of tabwa is to take a home. It is said, Bawatuhu Manzilan if you make him live in it. The verb is in the accusative case as a state. The meaning of the verse is: And remember when you went out from your family's home, you take for the believers positions for fighting: i.e., places where they sit. He expressed the exit as Ghadh which is the exit in the morning, even though he, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out after the Friday prayer, as will come, because the exit and entry may be expressed as Ghadh without considering their original meaning, as is said, Adha even if it was not at the time of the forenoon.
3:122: His statement 122- When two parties from among you were about to lose heart is a substitute for when you went forth, or it is related to his statement: settle down, or to his statement: All-Hearing, All-Knowing, and the two parties were Banu Salamah from the Khazraj, and Banu Haritha from the Aws, and they were the two wings of the army on the day of Uhud, and failure is cowardice, and the concern of the two parties was after the departure, when Abdullah bin Ubayy returned with those hypocrites who were with him, so God preserved the hearts of the believers so they did not return, and that is his statement: And God is their protector.
3:123: His statement 123- And God had already given you victory at Badr is a new sentence that was brought to make them patient by reminding them of the victory that results from patience. Badr is the name of a body of water that was at the site of the battle, and it was said that it is the name of the site itself. The context of the story of Badr will come in Al-Anfal, God willing. And humiliation is the plural of paucity, and its meaning is that they were humiliated because of their small number, and it is the plural of humiliated that was borrowed for paucity, since they were not humiliated in themselves, but rather they were honorable. And victory means support. The historians and biographers have explained the Battle of Badr and Uhud in a complete manner, so we do not need to give a context for that here.
3:124: His statement 124 - When you say is related to his statement your victory. The hamza in his statement will it not suffice you? is for his denial, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their not being satisfied with that support from the angels. The meaning of sufficiency is filling the gap and carrying out the matter. Support in the original sense is giving something one moment after another, and the use of lan is to emphasize the negation.
3:125: The root of al-Fawr is to intend something and to take it seriously. It is from their saying, the pot boiled, meaning it boiled, and al-Fawr means boiling. Far means boiling, and Far means boiling. His anger boiled means it raged. He did it immediately, meaning before it boiled over. Al-Fawwarah is what boils from the pot. It is used as a metaphor for speed. That is, if they come to you at this hour, your Lord will reinforce you with angels when they come, and He will not delay that. His statement: 125- Masmoomin with a fat-ha on the waw is a passive participle. This is the reading of Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Nafi': meaning marked with signs. Ibn Amr, Ibn Kathir, and Asim read Masmoomin with a kasra on the waw as an active participle: meaning marking themselves with a sign. Ibn Jarir preferred this reading. Tasweem is to show the mark of something. Many commentators said, marked, meaning: sending their horses on the raid. It was said that the angels wore white turbans, and it was said: red, and it was said: green, and it was said: yellow. This is the sign by which they knew themselves. This was narrated from Al-Zajjaj. It was said: they were on piebald horses, and other things were said.
3:126: His statement 126- And God made it only as good tidings for you is a subject statement not included in the statement of the statement, and the pronoun in his statement made it refers to the support indicated by the verb, or to the setting, or to the sending down, and Al-Zajjaj and the author of Al-Kashshaf preferred the first. And his statement except as good tidings is an exception emptied from the most general of the general, and good tidings is a noun from the good report: that is, except that you may receive good tidings that you will be victorious and that your hearts may be reassured by it: that is, by the support, and the lam is the lam of ki, God made that support good tidings of victory and reassurance for the hearts, and in restricting the support to them there is an indication that the angels will not directly fight on that day And victory is only from God not from anyone else, so the multitude of fighters and the presence of equipment are of no benefit.
3:127: His statement: 127- To cut off a party of those who disbelieved is related to his statement And God had already given you victory at Badr. It was also said: It is related to his statement And victory is only from God. It was also said: It is related to his statement He reinforces you. The party is the group, and the meaning is: God gave you victory at Badr to cut off a party of the disbelievers, and they are those who were killed on the day of Badr, or the victory is only from God to cut off that group or He reinforces you to cut off. The meaning of suppresses them is to grieve them, and the subdued is the grieved. Some linguists said: Its meaning is to plot against them: that is, to afflict them with sadness and anger in their livers, and this is incorrect, because the meaning of suppress is to grieve, anger, and humiliate, and the meaning of strikes the liver is so they return disappointed meaning: not victorious in their goal.
3:128: His statement 128- You have no part in the matter is an interjectional clause between the conjoined and the conjoined to: meaning that God is the master of their matter, He does with them what He wills of destruction, defeat, repentance if they submit, or punishment. So His statement, or He turns to them in mercy or punishes them is conjoined with His statement, or He suppresses them. Al-Farra' said: If or means except that, meaning that you have no part in the matter except that He turns to them in mercy and you rejoice in that or punishes them and you are pleased with them.
3:129: His statement 129- And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is a new statement to explain the vastness of His kingdom. He forgives whomever He wills to forgive him. And He punishes whomever He wills to punish him. He does in His kingdom what He wills and decrees what He wants. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. And in His statement, And God is Forgiving and Merciful is an indication that His mercy precedes His wrath, and good tidings to His servants that He is characterized by forgiveness and mercy in an exaggerated manner. How great this sublime humiliation is and how beloved it is to the hearts of those who know the secrets of the revelation. Ibn Ishaq and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Asim bin Omar bin Qatada, Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban and Al-Hussain bin Abdul Rahman bin Asaad bin Muadh that they said: The day of Uhud was a day of trial and testing, in which God tested the believers and destroyed the hypocrites who used to show Islam with their tongues while belittling their disbelief, and it was a day in which God honored those whom He wanted to honor with martyrdom from among the people of His authority. Among what was revealed of the Qur’an on the day of Uhud were sixty verses from Al-Imran describing what happened on that day and reprimanding those of them who reprimanded. God said to His Prophet, And when you went forth from your family Al-Madinah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when you went forth from your family Al-Madinah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding His statement, The believers settled down Al-Madinah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that the verse was about the day of the confederates. It has been mentioned in the books of biography and history how there was disagreement in the advice to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Uhud. Some said we should go out to them, and some said we should stay in Medina. So he went out and among those who advised him was Abdullah bin Abi Salul, the leader of the hypocrites. His opinion was to stay in Medina and fight there, but when his opinion was contradicted, he withdrew with the hypocrites who were with him, and they were about a third of the people who the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out with. Al-Bukhari and Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Jabir who said: When two parties among you were about to lose heart was revealed about us, and I would not be pleased that and God is their protector was not revealed. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: When two parties were about to lose heart that he said: That was on the day of Uhud. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: They were the Banu Haritha and the Banu Salamah. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid And God had certainly helped you at Badr to three thousand angels sent down in the story of Badr. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, and you are weak, he said: and you are few, and on that day they were a few dozen or three hundred. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: that the Muslims were informed on the day of Badr that Kurz bin Jaber Al-Muharibi was supplying the polytheists, and that was difficult for them, so God revealed, Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand? to His statement, marked. He said: So it reached Kurz, but he did not reinforce the polytheists, nor did he reinforce the Muslims with the five. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi that on the day of Badr, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed, then he mentioned something similar, except that he said, And they will come to you in haste, meaning Kurz and his companions, Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked. So the report of the defeat reached Kurz and his companions, but he did not reinforce them, and the five were not revealed, and they were reinforced after that with a thousand, so they were four thousand. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: They were reinforced with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand, and that was on the day of Badr. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding His statement, Yes, if you are patient and fear God 3:10, he said: This was on the day of Uhud, but they were not patient and did not fear God, so they were not reinforced on the day of Uhud, and if they had been reinforced, they would not have been defeated that day. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ad-Dahhak. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, And they will come to you in full force, he said: From their journey. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, from their force, he said: From their face. And Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Hasan, Ar-Rabi’ and Qatadah As-Suddi. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, from their force, he said: From their anger. And they narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Salih, the freed slave of Umm Hani. And At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said in his saying marked he said: marked, and the mark of the angels on the day of Badr was black turbans, and on the day of Uhud they were red turbans. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr: that Al-Zubayr was wearing a yellow turban on the day of Badr, and the angels descended upon them with yellow turbans. Ibn Ishaq and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The mark of the angels on the day of Badr was white turbans that they had let down on their backs, and on the day of Hunayn they were red turbans, and the angels did not strike on any day except the day of Badr, and they were in numbers and reinforcements and did not strike. There is much disagreement about the explanation of the marking from the predecessors, which is not of much benefit. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his saying that He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieved he said: God cut off a portion of the disbelievers on the day of Badr, and killed their leaders, chiefs and leaders in evil. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated regarding his statement, To cut off a part, that he said: This was on the day of Badr, when God cut off a group of them and left a group. Ibn Jarir narrated from Al-Suddi, that he said: God mentioned the slain polytheists at Uhud, and they were eighteen men, so He said, To cut off a part of those who disbelieved, then God mentioned the martyrs, saying, And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement, Or He suppresses them, that he said: He grieves them. Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah and Al-Rabi’ similarly. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Anas that the Prophet’s front tooth was broken on the day of Uhud and his face was cut until blood flowed. He said, How can a people succeed who did this to their Prophet while he was calling them to their Lord? So God revealed, You have no part in the matter, the verse. This meaning has been narrated in many narrations. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of UHud 11:O God, curse Abu Sufyan, O God, curse Al-Harith bin Hisham, O God, curse Suhayl bin Amr, O God, curse Safwan bin Umayya. Then this verse was revealed: You have no part in the matter. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others also narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurairah: “Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to supplicate against someone, or to supplicate for someone, he would say after bowing: ‘O God, save Al-Walid bin Al-Walid, Salamah bin Hisham, Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah and the weak believers. O God, make Your punishment severe upon Mudar and make it years for them like the years of Joseph.’ He would say this out loud. And he would say in some of his prayers in the Fajr prayer: ‘O God, curse so-and-so and so-and-so for some tribes of the Arabs until God revealed, ‘You have no part in the matter.’” And in another version: “O God, curse Lihyan, Ra’la, Dhakwan and ‘Asiyah who disobeyed God and His Messenger. Then we were informed that he stopped doing this when the verse was revealed, ‘You have no part in the matter.’”
3:130: His saying 130- O you who believe It was said: This is an introductory statement to intimidate and encourage what was mentioned, and it was said: It is an interjection during the story of Uhud. And his saying multiplied multiples is not to restrict the prohibition to what is known of the prohibition of usury in all cases, but it was brought in consideration of what they were upon of the habit that they were accustomed to in usury, for they used to increase it for a term, and when the term came they would increase the money by an amount that they agreed upon, then they would increase the term of the debt, so they would do that time after time until the one who increased it would take multiples of the debt that he had at the beginning, and multiples is a condition, and doubling is a description of it, and in it is an indication of the repetition of the doubling year after year, and the exaggeration in this phrase indicates an emphasis on the rebuke.
3:132: And His saying 132- And obey God and the Messenger The deletion of the subject indicates generalization: that is, in every command and prohibition that you may receive mercy that is, hoping for mercy from God Almighty.
3:133: And his saying 133- And hasten is in apposition to obey, and Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read hasten without the waw, and this is also in the copies of the Mushafs of the people of Medina and the people of Ash-Sham, and the rest read it with the waw. Abu Ali said: Both matters are permissible and correct, and hastening means taking the initiative, and in the verse there is an omission, meaning hasten to what necessitates forgiveness from acts of obedience. And His saying, Its width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, meaning: its width is like the width of the heavens and the earth. And similar to it is the other verse, Its width is like the width of the heaven and the earth. And there is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of that. The majority of scholars have held that it links the heavens and the earth together, just as clothes are spread out and connected to each other, so that is the width of Paradise. And He pointed out the length by width because the length is usually greater than the width. And it has been said that this statement came in the manner of the speech of the Arabs, from metaphor rather than reality, and that is because Paradise was not extremely vast and spacious, and it was good to express it by the width of the heavens and the earth as an exaggeration because they are the most spacious of the creations of God Almighty in what His servants know, and He did not intend to specify by that.
3:134: And prosperity: ease, and adh-Dara': hardship. Their interpretation has been presented - and it was said that prosperity: ease, and adh-Dara': severity, and it is like the first, and it was said: prosperity in life, and adh-Dara' after death. His saying 134 - "And those who restrain anger" It is said that he suppressed his anger: meaning he kept quiet about it and did not show it, and from this, "kazmat al-saqqa'" means he filled it. And the repression: is what blocks the flow of water, and the camel represses its jar: if it returns it to its stomach, and it is in apposition to the relative pronoun before it. His saying "And those who pardon people" meaning: those who leave the punishment of those who sinned against them and deserved to be held accountable, and this is for the sake of types of good. Its apparent meaning is pardoning people whether they are slaves or not. Al-Zajjaj and others said: What is meant by them are slaves. The lam in "al-Muhsinin" may be for the genus, so it includes every doer of good from these and others, and it may be for the covenant, so it is specific to these. The first is more deserving of consideration in terms of the generality of the wording, not in terms of the specificity of the context. Thus, everyone who has ever performed the term benevolence is included under it: any benevolence.
3:135: His saying 135- And those who, when they commit an immorality This is a subject and its predicate is those. It was said: It is conjoined with the righteous. The first is more appropriate, and these are a category below the first category, attached to them, and they are the repentant ones. The reason for its revelation will be mentioned. The immorality is a description of an omitted description: i.e. an immoral act, and it is applied to every sin. It is often specified for adultery. His saying or wronged themselves i.e. by committing a sin. It was said: or in the meaning of and. What is meant is what was mentioned, and it was said: the major immorality, and the injustice of the small soul, and other things were said. His saying, They remembered God means: with their tongues or they thought of Him in their hearts or they remembered His promise and threat. Then they sought forgiveness for their sins means: they sought forgiveness for them from God, the Most High. Its interpretation as repentance is contrary to its meaning linguistically. In the question with His saying, And who forgives sins except God? there is denial along with what it includes of indicating that He is the only One who is unique in that, the Most High: meaning no one forgives the type of sins except God. It encourages seeking forgiveness from Him, the Most High, and motivates the sinners to stand in positions of submission and humility. This sentence is parenthetical between the conjoined and the conjoined to. His saying, And they did not persist in what they did is in apposition to they sought forgiveness meaning: they did not persist in their ugly action. The interpretation of persistence has already been presented. What is meant by it here is the determination to return to the sin and not stop it by repenting from it. His saying, and they knew is a circumstantial sentence: meaning: they did not persist in their action knowing its ugliness.
3:136: His statement, Their recompense refers to those mentioned in his statement, And those who, when they commit an immorality. His statement, Their recompense is a substitute for the demonstrative pronoun. His statement, Forgiveness is the predicate of from their Lord related to something omitted that is an attribute of forgiveness: meaning, coming from their Lord. His statement, And excellent is the reward of the workers that is specifically praised is omitted: meaning, their reward, or that which is mentioned. The explanation of the gardens and how rivers flow beneath them has already been presented. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: They used to trade on credit, and when the credit came, they would increase it and increase the credit, so the verse, O you who believe, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: Thaqif used to follow Banu Al-Mughira in the pre-Islamic period, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurra who said: People used to interpret this verse, And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers, as fear, lest I punish you for your sins in the Fire which I have prepared for the disbelievers. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah who said: The Muslims said: O Messenger of God, were the Children of Israel more honored by God than us? When one of them committed a sin, the expiation for his sin would be written on the threshold of his door: Cut off your nose, cut off your ear, do such and such. But the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent, so the verse, And hasten was revealed. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik in the interpretation of and hasten he said: the first takbir. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Suddi on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his statement its width is as the heavens and the earth like what we mentioned previously on the authority of the majority. Saeed ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on his authority on the authority of Kurayb. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his statement those who spend in prosperity and adversity he said: in ease and hardship and those who restrain anger he said: those who restrain anger: and many hadiths have been narrated about the reward of those who restrain anger. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Nakha’i in the verse he said: injustice is from immorality and immorality is from injustice. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, At-Tabarani, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: There are two verses in the Book of God: If a servant commits a sin and recites them and seeks forgiveness from God, God will forgive him. And those who, when they commit an immorality 2:100. And His statement, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself 2:100. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Thabit Al-Banati who said: It has reached me that when this verse was revealed, Iblis wept. And those who, when they commit an immorality 2:100. Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Attaf bin Khalid who said: It has reached me that when the verse was revealed, And who can forgive sins except God? And they do not persist in what they have done 2:100 Iblis shouted at his soldiers and threw dirt on his head and called for woe and destruction until his soldiers came to him from every land and sea. They said: What is the matter with you, O our master? He said: A verse was revealed in the Book of God after which no sin will harm any of the children of Adam. They said: What is it? So he informed them, and they said: We open the door of whims for them, but they do not repent, nor seek forgiveness, nor do they see anything except that they are on the truth. So he was satisfied with that from them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Humaidi, Abd Ibn Hamid, and the people of the four Sunans narrated, and Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, Al-Daraqutni in Al-Ifrad, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Al-Sunni, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab, and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no man who commits a sin, then stands up when his sin is mentioned, purifies himself, then prays two rak’ahs, then seeks forgiveness from God for that sin, except that God will forgive him.” Then he recited this verse: And those who, when they commit an immorality… Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab, on the authority of Al-Hasan, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, but he said: Then he went out to a clearing on the ground and prayed. Abd bin Hamid, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness is not persistent, even if he returns seventy times a day. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding the statement and they do not persist, they remain silent and do not seek forgiveness. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil, And excellent is the reward of the workers, he said: The reward of those who work in obedience to God is Paradise.
3:137: His statement 137- There have already been precedents before you. This refers back to the description of the rest of the story. What is meant by precedents is what God has established for the nations of His events: that is, there have already been precedents before your time that God established for the nations of disbelievers. The root of precedents is the plural of sunnah, which is the straight path. From this, al-Hudhali said: Do not be upset about a tradition that you have followed, for the first to be satisfied with a tradition is the one who follows it. Sunnah: the imam who is followed and imitated. From this comes the saying of Labid: From a group whose fathers have set a precedent for them, and every people has a tradition and an imam. The Sunnah is the nation, and the Sunnahs are the nations, as stated by Al-Mufaddal Al-Dabbi. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning in the verse is the people of Sunnah, so the complement was omitted, and the Fa in His statement travel is causal, and it was said that it is conditional: meaning if you doubt then travel. And the consequence: the end of the matter. The meaning is: travel and see how was the end of the deniers, for they disobeyed their messengers by being greedy for the world, then they became extinct, and no trace remained of their world that they preferred. This is the opinion of most of the commentators. What is required from this commanded travel is to gain knowledge of that, for if it is achieved without it, then the goal has been achieved, even if witnessing the effects is an increase that is not achieved by those who do not witness them.
3:138: And the reference in his saying 138- This to his saying has passed away and Al-Hasan said to the Qur'an An explanation for the people meaning an explanation for them, and the people's definition of the covenant and they are the deniers, or of the species, meaning the deniers and others. And in it is an urging to consider the evil end of the deniers and what their affair has come to. His saying and guidance and admonition meaning: this consideration, with it being an explanation, contains guidance and admonition for the righteous believers, so linking the guidance and admonition to the explanation indicates the difference even if it is in consideration of the related, and its explanation is that if the lam in the people is for the covenant then the explanation is for the deniers and the guidance and admonition are for the believers, and if it is for the species then the explanation is for all people, their believers and their disbelievers and the guidance and admonition are for the righteous alone.
3:139: His statement 139- And do not weaken and do not grieve He consoled them and comforted them for what they had suffered on the day of Uhud of killing and wounds, and urged them to fight their enemy and forbade them from weakness and failure, then he explained to them that they were superior to their enemy in victory and triumph, and it is a circumstantial clause: meaning, and the situation is that you are superior to them and to others after this battle. And God fulfilled His promise, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the battle of Uhud was victorious over his enemy in all his battles, and it was said that the meaning is: and you are superior to them because of what you inflicted on them on the day of Badr, for it is more than what they inflicted on you today. And His statement if you are believers is related to His statement and do not weaken and what follows it, or to His statement and you are superior meaning: if you are believers, then do not weaken and do not grieve, or if you are believers, then you are superior.
3:140: Qarh with dammah and fathah: wound and they are two dialects for it, said Al-Kisa'i and Al-Akhfash. Al-Farra' said: With fathah it is the wound, and with dammah it is its pain. Muhammad bin Al-Samee' read qarh with fathah on the qaf and the ra' as a source. The meaning of the verse: If they got from you on the day of Uhud, then you got from them on the day of Badr, so do not weaken for what happened to you on this day, for they did not weaken for what happened to them on that day, and you are more deserving of patience than they are. It was said: What is meant is what happened to the believers and the disbelievers on this day, for the Muslims were victorious over them in the beginning and killed a group of them, then the disbelievers were victorious over them and killed some of them. The first is more deserving, because what the Muslims got from the disbelievers on this day was not like what they got from them on it. His saying, And those days, meaning: those that exist between nations in their wars and those that will come after, such as the days that existed during the time of the Prophethood. Sometimes this group prevails, and sometimes the other prevails, as happened to you, O Muslims, on the day of Badr and Uhud. This is the meaning of his saying, We alternate it among the people. So his saying, Those is the subject, and the days are its description, and the predicate is we alternate it, and the origin of alternation is alternation: He alternated it among them and al-dawla means the ball, and it is permissible for the days to be the predicate and we alternate it to be a state, but the first is more appropriate. His saying, And that God may know is connected to an implied reason, as if he said: We alternate it among the people so that your affair may become apparent and so that it may be known, or the reason may be omitted: that is, so that God may know those who feared God, we did that, and it is a form of representation: that is, we did the action of one who wants to know because He, glory be to Him, has always been All-Knowing, or so that God may know those who believed through their patience a knowledge that will be rewarded as He knew them with eternal knowledge. And He will take from among you martyrs, that is, He will honor them with martyrdom. Martyrs is the plural of martyr, so called because he is witnessed to in Paradise, or the plural of witness because he is like one who witnesses Paradise, and min is for the partiality and they are the martyrs of Uhud. His saying, And God does not love the wrongdoers is an interjectional clause between the conjoined and the conjoined to it to confirm the meaning of what preceded it.
3:141: And His saying 141- And that God may purify those who believe is from the group of causes, connected to what preceded it. Purification is testing, and it was said: purification with the omission of an adjective: that is, to purify the sins of those who believe, said Al-Farra', and it was said: purifies, purifies, said Al-Khalil and Al-Zajjaj: that is, to purify the believers from their sins. And His saying and destroy the disbelievers means to uproot them by destruction, and the origin of tamhiq is the erasure of traces, and muhqiq is its essence.
3:142: His statement 142- Or do you think that you will enter Paradise? is a renewed statement to explain what was mentioned about the distinction, and am is the disconnected one, and the hamza is for denial: that is, rather, did you think? And the waw in his statement and God does not know is the waw of the state. And the current sentence, and in it is a representation like the first, or knowledge upon which the reward falls. And his statement and He knows the patient is in the accusative case with the implication of an as Al-Khalil and others said, on the basis that the waw is for the plural. Al-Zajjaj said: The waw means until, and Al-Hasan and Yahya bin Ya'mar read and He knows the patient in the jussive mood in apposition to and He does not know and it was read in the nominative case for the cut, and it was said that his statement and He does not know is a metaphor for the negation of the known, which is jihad. The meaning is: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise, while the situation is that jihad and patience have not been achieved from you: that is, the combination of them, and the meaning of lama is the meaning of lam according to the majority, and Sibawayh differentiated between them and made lam for the negation of the past, and lam for the negation of the past and the expected.
3:143: His statement 143- And you were wishing for death is addressed to those who wished to fight and be martyred in the cause of God and who did not attend the day of Badr, for they were wishing for a day in which there would be fighting. But when the day of Uhud came, they were defeated, even though they were the ones who urged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to go out, and only a few of them were patient, such as Anas bin An-Nadr, the uncle of Anas bin Malik. His statement before you meet him means: the fighting or martyrdom which is the cause of death. Al-A'mash read before you meet him and the prohibition of wishing for death has been mentioned, so it must be interpreted here as martyrdom. Al-Qurtubi said: The wishing for death among Muslims goes back to wishing for martyrdom based on steadfastness and patience in jihad, not to the killing of the infidels because it is a sin and disbelief, and it is not permissible to desire sin. Based on this, the Muslims' request to God to grant them martyrdom is interpreted as asking for patience in jihad even if it leads to killing. His saying, You have seen it, meaning: the fighting or what is the cause of death. The place of his saying, and you are looking, is the accusative case of state, and the restriction of seeing to looking, with the union of their meanings, is for emphasis: meaning you have seen it, witnessing it when he killed whoever was killed among you. Al-Akhfash said: Repetition is in the sense of emphasis, like his saying, nor a bird that flies with its wings. It was said: Its meaning is clearly, there are no defects in your eyes. It was said: Its meaning is while you are looking at Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
3:144: And his saying 144- And Muhammad is no more than a Messenger; before him there were Messengers. The reason for the revelation of this is what will come, that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wounded on the Day of Uhud, Satan cried out saying: Muhammad has been killed, so some of the Muslims were disheartened until one said: Muhammad has been wounded, so give them your hands, for they are your brothers, and another said: If he had been a Messenger, he would not have been killed, so God responded to them and informed them that he is a Messenger; before him there were Messengers; and he will pass away as they passed away, so the phrase before him there were Messengers is a description of a Messenger. The restriction is a restriction of separation as if they ruled out his death, so they established two attributes for him: the message, and the fact that he will not perish, so God responded to them by saying that he is a Messenger who does not go beyond that to the attribute of not perishing, and it was said: It is a restriction of the heart. Ibn Abbas read: Messengers have passed away before him, then God denounced him by saying: Then if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? That is: How can you turn back and abandon his worldly life if he dies or is killed, while you know that messengers pass away and their followers hold fast to their religion even if they are lost through death or killing? It was said: The denial was because they made the passing away of messengers before him a reason for their turning back because of his death or killing. Rather, he mentioned killing even though God, the Most High, knew that he would not be killed because it was permissible for those addressed. His saying: And whoever turns back on his heels That is: by turning away from fighting or by apostasizing from Islam, will never harm God at all of harm, but he only harms himself, and God will reward the grateful That is, those who were patient, fought, and were martyred, because by doing so they thanked God for His blessing upon them with Islam. And whoever complies with what he is commanded to do has thanked the blessing that God has bestowed upon him.
3:145: His statement 145- And no soul can die except by God's permission. This is a new statement that includes urging jihad and informing that death is inevitable. The meaning of by God's permission is by God's decree and destiny. It was said that this sentence includes a denial of those who failed because of that rumor of his killing, may God's prayers and peace be upon him. So he explained to them that death by killing or otherwise is dependent on God's permission, and attributing it to the soul despite it not choosing it is to indicate that no one should undertake it except by God's permission. His statement in writing is a source that confirms what came before it, because its meaning is that God wrote death in writing. And the deferred: the temporary that does not precede its appointed time nor is delayed. His saying, And whoever desires, that is, with his knowledge, the reward of this world, such as spoils and the like. The expression includes everything that is called the reward of this world, even if the reason is specific. And whoever desires, with his work, the reward of the Hereafter, which is Paradise, We will give him from its reward, and We will multiply his good deeds many times over. And We will reward the grateful, by complying with what We have commanded them to do, such as fighting, and what We have forbidden them from doing, such as fleeing and accepting rumours.
3:146: And his saying 146- And how many Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: It is that which the kaf of comparison entered upon it and was fixed with it, so after the composition it became with the meaning of how much, and it was represented in the Qur’an as a nun, because it is a word that was transferred from its origin, so its pronunciation was changed to change its meaning, then its use became widespread, so the Arabs manipulated it by changing and deleting, so it became four languages in which it was read: One of them is Ka’in like Ka’in, and Ibn Kathir read it with it, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: And there is a friend in the valleys whom you will see if you are afflicted, he is the one afflicted Another said: And we have turned away from you, a man armed with a live bullet in front of the caravan, wearing a mask Zuhair said: And if you see someone who admires you, whether he speaks too much or too little Ka'ayn with emphasis like Ka'ayn, and the rest read it this way and it is the original. The third: Ka'ayn like Ka'ayn without emphasis. The fourth: Ka'ayn with a ya' followed by a kasra hamza, and Abu Amr stopped without a noon and said: Ka'ay because it is a tanween, and the rest stopped with a noon, and the meaning is many of the prophets were killed with him, Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Ya'qub read it as qatal in the passive form, and it is the reading of Ibn Abbas, and Abu Hatim chose it, and there are two views: The first is that in qatal there is a pronoun referring to the prophet, and in that case his saying with him are rabeeyan is a circumstantial clause as it is said: the prince was killed with an army, meaning with him is an army. The second view is that the killing was directed at rabeeyan, so there is no pronoun in qatal, and the meaning is: some of his companions were killed and they are the rabeeyan. The Kufians and Ibn Amir read Qatil, which is the reading of Ibn Masoud and Abu Ubaid chose it. He said: If God praises the one who fights, then the one who is killed is included in it. If He praises the one who is killed and does not include the one who fights and is not killed, then Qatil is more general and praiseworthy. This other reading is preferred. The second aspect of the first reading is the statement of Al-Hasan: No prophet was ever killed in war. Saeed bin Jubair said the same. The rabbiyyun with a kasra on the ra is the reading of the majority. Ali read it with a damma and Ibn Abbas read it with a fatha. Its singular is rabbiyyun with a fatha and is attributed to the Lord. The rabbiyyun with a damma and kasra on the ra is accusative to the rabbah with a kasra and damma on the ra, which is the group. For this reason, a group of the Salaf interpreted them as large groups. It was said: They are the followers. It was said: They are the scholars. Al-Khalil said: The rabbiyyun is one of the servants who were patient with the prophets and they are the rabbiyyun. They are attributed to deity, worship, and knowledge of divinity. Al-Zajjaj said: The rabbiyyun with a damma are the groups. His statement They did not weaken is in apposition to Qatil or Qatal. Weakness: the breaking of seriousness due to fear. Al-Hasan read Wahanu with a kasra or a damma on the ha’. Abu Zaid said: There are two dialects for Wahan of a thing, Yahin and Wahan meaning weakness: they did not weaken because of the killing of their prophet or because of the killing of those who were killed from them. And they did not weaken meaning: from their enemy. And they did not submit for what happened to them in jihad. Submission means humiliation and submission. It was read Wa Wahanu and Wa Da’afu with a sukoon on the ha’ and the ‘ayn. Al-Kisa’i narrated Da’afu with a fatha on the ‘ayn. In this is a rebuke to those who were defeated on the day of Uhud and were humiliated, submitted and weakened because of that rumour that came from Satan and did not do as the companions of the messengers who came before them did.
3:147: His statement 147- And their saying was not meaning: the saying of those who were with the prophets was nothing but this saying, and their saying is in the accusative case as the predicate of was. Ibn Kathir and Asim read in a narration from them with the raising of their saying. And his statement except that they said is an empty exception: meaning what was their saying when some of their rabbis were killed or their prophet was killed except that they said, 'Our Lord, forgive us our sins' It was said: These are minor sins. And his statement: And our extravagance in our affair It was said: These are major sins, and it appears that sins include everything that is called a sin, whether minor or major. Extravagance is that in which there is exceeding the limit, so it is from the conjunction of the specific with the general, they said that despite being rabbis, to demean themselves and plant firmly our feet in the places of battle.
3:148: 148- So God gave them because of that the reward of this world of victory, spoils, honor, and the like and the good reward of the Hereafter from adding the attribute to the described: meaning the good reward of the Hereafter, which is the bliss of Paradise. May God make us among its people. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, There have already been precedents before you, he said: There was a trade-off between good and evil among the disbelievers and the believers. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in his book, Al-Masahif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The first thing to be revealed from Al Imran was, This is an explanation for the people, then the rest of it was revealed on the Day of Uhud. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, This is an explanation, meaning the Qur’an. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Khalid bin Al-Walid approached intending to climb the mountain over them, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, O God, do not let them climb over us, so God revealed, And do not weaken and do not grieve, the verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: The companions of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) were defeated in the ravine on the day of Uhud. They asked what had happened to the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) and what had happened to so-and-so. Some of them announced the report to one another and said that the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) had been killed. They were in a state of worry and grief. While they were like that, Khalid ibn Al-Walid climbed the mountain with the cavalry of the polytheists above them. They were on one of the flanks of the polytheists, and they were lower than the ravine. When they saw the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace), they rejoiced. The Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: O God! We have no power except through You, and no one worships You in this city except these people, so do not destroy them. A group of Muslim archers rose up and shot at the horses of the polytheists until God defeated them, and the Muslims climbed the mountain. This is what God said: And you will be the highest if you are believers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ad-Dahhak: And you will be the highest, he said: And you will be the victors. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid: If a wound should touch you, he said: Wounds and killing. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Hasan regarding His statement: If a wound should touch you, a wound similar to it has touched the people, he said: If one of you is killed on the Day of Uhud, one of them was killed on the Day of Badr. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And those days We alternate among the people, he said: The Day of Uhud was like the Day of Badr. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And those days, the verse. He said: The polytheists defeated the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud. It has reached me that the polytheists killed seventy-some thousand Muslims on the day of Uhud, the number of prisoners taken from the polytheists on the day of Badr. The number of prisoners on the day of Badr was seventy-three men. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And He takes from among you martyrs, he said: The Muslims used to ask their Lord: O God, our Lord, show us a day like the day of Badr, in which we fight the polytheists and test you with good, and seek martyrdom. So they met the polytheists on the day of Uhud, and He took martyrs from among them. And they narrated from him regarding His statement, And that God may test those who believe, he said: He tests them, and destroy the disbelievers, he said: He reduces them. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Awfi that some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: If only we could be killed as the companions of Badr were killed and be martyred, or If only we had a day like the day of Badr, in which we could fight the polytheists and test you with good, and seek martyrdom, Paradise, life, and provision. So God made them witnesses to Uhud, and they did not remain steadfast except for whomever God willed among them. Then God said, And you used to wish for death, the verse. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Kulayb who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab delivered a sermon to us, and he was reciting Surat Al Imran from the pulpit and saying: It is a one-sided verse. Then he said: We dispersed from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Uhud, so I climbed the mountain and heard a Jew saying: Muhammad has been killed. I said: I will not hear anyone say: Muhammad has been killed except that I will strike his neck. I looked and saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the people were returning to him. Then this verse was revealed: Muhammad is no more than a messenger; other messengers have passed away before him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak who said: A crier cried out on the day of UHud 11:Indeed, Muhammad has been killed, so return to your original religion. Then God revealed: Muhammad is no more than a messenger. He also narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. He also narrated on the authority of Ali regarding his statement: And God will reward the grateful, he said: Those who were steadfast in their religion were Abu Bakr and his companions. Ali used to say: Abu Bakr was the leader of the grateful. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim narrated on his authority that he used to say during the lifetime of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): God says: If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? By God, we will not turn back on our heels after God has guided us. By God, if he dies or is killed, I will be killed for what he was killed for until I die. Abd ibn Humayd ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement: Rabbiyoon he said: Thousands. Sa`id ibn Mansur narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak he said: One rabbiyoon is a thousand. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Rabbiyoon he said: Crowds. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority he said: Many scholars. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And they did not humble themselves he said: They feared. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his statement: And our extravagance in our affair he said: Our sins.
3:149: When God the Almighty commanded us to follow the example of those who came before us from the supporters of the prophets, He warned us against obeying the infidels, who are the polytheists of the Arabs, and it was said: the Jews and Christians, and it was said: the hypocrites in their saying to the believers when they were defeated: Return to the religion of your fathers. And His saying, They will turn you back on your heels means: They will take you out of the religion of Islam and into disbelief 149- Then you will return as losers meaning: You will return deceived.
3:150: And his saying 150- Rather, God is your protector is a departure from the meaning of the first sentence: that is, if you obey the disbelievers, they will abandon you and not support you. Rather, God is your protector, and no one else. And Rather, God was read in the accusative case, assuming Rather, obey God.
3:151: His saying 151- We will cast Al-Sakhtiyani read it with a lower ya’, and the rest read it with a noon. Ibn Amir and Al-Kisa’i read terror with a damma on the ‘ayn. The rest read it with sukoon, and they are two dialects. It is said: I terrified him, terrifying him, and he is terrified. It is possible that it is a source, and terror with dammah is a noun, and its origin is filling. It is said: a terrifying flood: meaning it fills the valley, and I terrified the pool: I filled it. So the meaning is: We will fill the hearts of the disbelievers with terror: meaning fear and panic. And throwing is used literally for bodies, and metaphorically for other things like this verse, and that is because the polytheists, after the Battle of Uhud, regretted that they had not exterminated the Muslims, and they said: How evil is what we have done. We killed them until, when none of them remained except the fugitives, we left them. Go back and exterminate them. So when they decided to do that, God cast terror into their hearts until they returned from what they intended to do. Because they associated partners with God is related to His saying: We will cast and what is a source: meaning because of their association. That for which He has not sent down authority meaning: that which God has not sent down to make him a partner with Him, an argument, clarification, and proof. The negation is directed to the restriction and the restricted: meaning no. Argument and no revelation, meaning: that associating partners with God has not been proven in any of the religions. And the abode is the place where one resides, it is said: he resides, he resides, he dwells.
3:152: His saying 152- And God has fulfilled His promise to you. It was revealed when some Muslims said, How did this happen to us when God promised us victory? That is because they were victorious at the beginning, until they killed the standard-bearer of the polytheists and nine men after him. When they were busy with the spoils and the archers left their post in pursuit of the spoils, that was the reason for the defeat. And has: is extermination by killing, said Abu Ubaid. It is said that a locust is felt: if the wilderness kills it, and its year is hasus: meaning a drought that eats everything. It was said: Its origin is from has which is perception by the senses, so the meaning of hashu is: he removed his sense by killing, and tahasunhum means you kill them and eradicate them. The poet said: We made them feel the sword, and the rest of them were scattered and dispersed. Jarir said: Swords feel them as the fire rises in the harvested thickets By His permission meaning: by His knowledge and judgment until you failed meaning: you became cowardly and weak. It was said: The answer to until is omitted, meaning: you were tested. Al-Farra' said: The answer to until is his saying and you disputed and the waw is an intrusive addition like his saying then when they both submitted and he laid him down on his forehead Abu Ali said: It is possible that the answer is that he turned you away from them. It was said that there is an inversion of it: meaning until when you disputed and disobeyed, you failed. It was said: The answer is you disobeyed, and the waw is an intrusive addition. Al-Akhfash permitted something similar in the saying of God Almighty: until when the earth, vast as it is, became strait for them and narrowed for them, and it was said: until means until, and then there is no answer for it. The dispute mentioned is what happened from the archers when some of them said: We will catch up with the spoils, and some of them said: We will remain in our place as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us. The meaning of his statement, After He showed you what you love, is what happened to them of victory in the beginning on the Day of Uhud, as mentioned above. Among you are those who desire this world, meaning the spoils. And among you are those who desire the Hereafter, meaning the reward for remaining in their positions in compliance with the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He turned you away from them to test you, meaning God turned you away from them by defeat after you had taken control of them, to test you. And He has pardoned you, because He knew of your remorse, so He did not eradicate you after your disobedience and opposition. The address is to all those who were defeated, and it was said: to the archers only.
3:153: His saying 153- When you ascend is related to his saying He turned you away or his saying And He has pardoned you or his saying To test you. The majority read it with a damma on the taa' and a kasra on the 'ayn, and Abu Raja' al-Attardi, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Hasan and Qatadah read it with a fatha on the taa' and the 'ayn. Ibn Muhaisin and Qanbal read you ascend with a taht. Abu Hatim said: I ascended if I went in front of you, and I ascended if I climbed a mountain, so ascending is walking on the ground level and in the valleys, and ascending is rising on mountains, roofs, stairs and steps, so it is possible that their ascension on the mountain was after their ascension in the valley, so the meaning is correct in both readings. Al-Qatibi said: I ascended if he went far and delved into it, and from this is the saying of the poet: Oh you who ask, where have you ascended? For there is an appointment for you in the valley of Yathrib. Al-Farra’ said: Ascension is the beginning of a journey, and descent is the return from it. It is said: We ascended from Baghdad to Mecca and to Khorasan and the like meaning we set out to it and began the journey, and we descended when we returned. Al-Mufaddal said: Ascended and ascended have the same meaning. The meaning of talawn is you ascend and stay meaning: do not turn to one another in order to flee, because the one ascending to something turns his neck or the neck of his mount towards it. On someone means: on one of those with you, and it was said: on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hasan read talawn with one waw, and Asim read it in a narration from him with a damma on the ta and it is a language. His statement and the Messenger calls you in your last ones means: in the last group of you. It is said: So-and-so came at the end of the people, and the last of the people, and the last of the people. And the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was: O servants of God, return. His statement, So He rewarded you is in apposition to your turning away: meaning: So God rewarded you with grief when He turned you away from him because of the grief you made the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) taste with your disobedience, or grief connected to grief because of that rumour, injury, killing and victory of the polytheists. Grief originally means covering. I covered something, and a day of grief and a night of grief: if they were dark. And from this is the grief of the crescent moon. It was said: The first grief was the defeat, and the second was the overtaking of Abu Hurairah and Khalid ibn al-Walid upon them on the mountain. His statement, So that you would not grieve: the lam is connected to his statement, So He rewarded you meaning: This grief after grief is so that you would not grieve over what was lost of the spoils nor what befell you of defeat, as training for you for calamities and training to endure hardships. Al-Mufaddal said: The meaning of so that you will not grieve is so that you will grieve, and la is redundant like the Almighty’s saying: What prevented you from prostrating? meaning: from prostrating, and His saying: so that the People of the Book would not know meaning so that they would know. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, he said: Do not advise the Jews and Christians about your religion and do not believe them in anything about your religion. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: If you obey Abu Sufyan bin Harb, he will turn you back into disbelievers. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, something similar to what we mentioned in the reason for the revelation of the verse. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Urwah regarding his statement: And God has fulfilled His promise to you, he said: God had promised them, for their patience and piety, that He would support them with five thousand marked angels, and He had done so. But when they disobeyed the command of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and left their ranks and the archers left, the Messenger promised them not to leave their homes, and they wanted the world, the support of angels was lifted from them. The story of Uhud is fully explained in biographies and histories, so there is no need to elaborate on it here. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Awf regarding his statement, When you were catching them, he said: catching means killing. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated the same on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority. He said: Failure means cowardice. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ Ibn Azib regarding his statement, After He showed you what you love, he said: spoils and the defeat of the people. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, And He has pardoned you, he said: God says, I have pardoned you, that I did not exterminate you. He also narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, When you ascend, he said: They ascended Uhud fleeing, and the Messenger was calling them from behind them: To Me, servants of God, return! To Me, servants of God, return. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, So He rewarded you with grief upon grief. He said: The first grief was due to the defeat, and the second was when it was said that Muhammad had been killed, and that was greater to them than the defeat. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Grief upon grief. He said: A panic after the first panic when they heard the voice that Muhammad had been killed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, he said: The first panic was the wounds and killing, and the second panic was when they heard that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of al-Rabi’.
3:154: Security and security are the same. It was said that security is only with causes of fear, and security is with its absence. It is accusative with anzala. Na'asan is a substitute for it or an explanatory apposition or an object for it. As for what was said that amna is a state of na'as that precedes it or a state of the addressees or an object for it, then that is far-fetched. Ibn Muhaisin read amna with a sukoon on the meem. His statement 154- Yaghsha was read with a lower case on the basis that the pronoun refers to sleepiness and with a higher case on the basis that the pronoun refers to security. The other group is Mu'tab bin Qushair and his companions. They had gone out hoping for the spoils and they began to call for attendance and say sayings. The meaning of they worried themselves is that they were worried, the matter worried me and made me anxious. The and in his statement and a group is for the state, and it is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun because it depends on the and of the state. It was said that the meaning of they worried themselves is that their concern became their only concern. They think about God other than the truth This sentence is in the accusative case as a state: that is, they think about God other than the truth that should be thought about, and the thought of the Jahiliyyah is a substitute for it. It is the thought specific to the religion of Jahiliyyah, or the thought of the people of Jahiliyyah, which is their thought that the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is false, and that what he called for from the religion of truth will not be supported or fulfilled. His statement they say is a substitute for they think meaning: they say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Do we have any part in the matter? meaning: Do we have a share in the matter of God? The meaning of this question is denial: that is, we do not have any part in the matter. It is victory and supremacy over the enemy. It was said that it is the exit: that is, we only went out under duress. So God, the Most High, responded to them by saying, Say, ‘Indeed, the matter is entirely God’s. Neither you nor your enemy have any share of it, so victory is in His hand and triumph is from Him. And His saying, They conceal it within themselves, means: They conceal hypocrisy within themselves and do not reveal it to you, rather they ask you the question of those seeking guidance. And His saying, They say, ‘If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here,’ is a new question, as if it was said: What is the matter that they conceal within themselves? So it was said: They say among themselves or within themselves, If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here, meaning: those who were killed in this battle would not have been killed.
