So God, the Most High, responded to them by saying, Say, ‘If you had been in your houses, those upon whom killing was decreed would have gone forth to their deathbeds,’ meaning: If you had been sitting in your houses, there would have been no escape from those upon whom killing was decreed going out to these places where they were killed, for the decree of God cannot be reversed. His saying, And that God may test what is in your hearts, is a reason for an action that was understood before it, conjoined with other reasons for it that are folded to indicate their abundance, as if it were said: Perhaps what he did was for many interests, and that God may test, etc. It was said that it is conjoined with a folded reason that was prominent, and the meaning is: To test what is in your hearts of sincerity, and to purify what is in your hearts of the whisperings of Satan.
3:155: His statement 155 - Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met meaning, they were defeated on the day of UHud 11:It was said that the meaning is: Those who turned back to the polytheists on the day of Uhud were only caused to slip by Satan he caused them to slip because of some of the sins they had committed, including disobeying the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And God has pardoned them because of their repentance and apology. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: God made them feel secure that day with a drowsiness that overcame them, and only he who feels secure feels drowsy. It has been proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari and others that Abu Talha said: We were overcome while we were in our ranks on the day of Uhud, and my sword kept falling from my hand and I would catch it, and it would fall and I would catch it. This is what God said: Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security, a drowsiness Al-Madinah 14:15. Al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it, and Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam, he said: I raised my head on the day of Uhud and I kept looking, and there was not one of them except that he was leaning under his veil from drowsiness, and he recited this verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: The hypocrites said to Abdullah bin Ubayy, who was the leader of al-Munafiqun 63:Banu Khazraj were killed today, so he said: Do we have any say in the matter? By God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humble. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ regarding his statement, the suspicion of the Age of Ignorance, he said: the suspicion of the polytheists. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Mu’tab is the one who said on the day of UHud 11:If only we had a part in the matter. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that the one who said that was Abdullah bin Ubayy. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf regarding his statement, Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met, he said: They are three, one from the Muhajireen and two from the Ansar. Ibn Mandah and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: It was revealed about Uthman, Rafi’ bin Al-Mu’alla, and Kharijah bin Zaid. Many narrations have been narrated about identifying those in the verse.
3:156: His saying 156- Do not be like those who disbelieved They are the hypocrites who said: If we had any part in the matter, we would not be here. His saying And they said to their brothers in hypocrisy or in lineage: That is, they said on their behalf When they traveled through the land If they traveled in it for trade or something similar. It was said: If here is useful for the meaning of the future with the same meaning as when it is useful for the meaning of the past. It was said: It is in its meaning, and what is meant here is the narration of the past state. Al-Zajjaj said: If here is a substitute for what has passed of time and what will come or they were a raid The plural of raid is like bowing and bowing, and absent and absent. The poet said: Tell the caravans and the invaders when they invade That God may make it a regret in their hearts. The lam is related to His statement, They said, meaning: They said that and believed it so that it would be a regret in their hearts. What is meant is that their belief that if they had not gone out they would not have been killed became a regret, or it is related to His statement, Do not be, meaning: Do not be like them in believing that so that God may make it a regret in their hearts only and not your hearts. It was said: The meaning is: Do not pay attention to them so that God may make your not paying attention to them a regret in their hearts. It was said: What is meant is a regret in their hearts on the Day of Resurrection because of the shame and remorse in it. And God gives life and causes death, in it is a response to their statement, meaning: That is in the hand of God, the Most High. He does what He wills and rules as He wills, so He gives life to whomever He wills and causes death to whomever He wills without travel or conquest having any effect on that.
3:157: The lam in his saying 157- And if you are killed is an introduction. His saying for forgiveness is the answer to the oath that takes the place of the answer to the condition, and the meaning is: Travel and conquest are not among the things that bring death, and if that happened by the command of God, the Most High, for forgiveness from God and mercy is better than what they accumulate meaning: the infidels of the benefits and pleasures of this world during their lives according to the reading of those who read with the lower yaa, or better than what you Muslims accumulate of this world and its benefits according to the reading of those who read with the upper yaa. The purpose of the verse is to explain the advantage of killing or dying in the way of God and increasing their effect in bringing forgiveness and mercy.
3:158: His statement 158- And if you die or are killed in any way according to the divine will, to God you will be gathered is the answer to the oath indicated by the preface lam, which takes the place of the answer to the condition as mentioned previously in the first sentence: that is, to the Lord, the Vast in forgiveness, you will be gathered, not to anyone else, as is indicated by the presentation of the circumstance before the verb, along with what is indicated in the specific mention of the name of God, the Most High, as is indicated by the kindness and power.
3:159: And in his saying 159- "So because of the mercy of God" is an additional emphasis, as Sibawayh and others said, and Ibn Kaysan said: It is an indefinite noun in the position of a genitive with a ya', and mercy is a substitute for it, and the first is more appropriate according to the rules of Arabic and similar to it is the saying of the Most High: "So because they broke their covenant and the preposition and the noun are related to his saying You were gentle with them" and it was presented before it to indicate restriction, and the tanween of mercy is for glorification, and the meaning is: His gentleness with them was only because of the great mercy from him, and it was said: Ma is an interrogative, and the meaning is: So by what mercy from God were you gentle with them, and it has a meaning of astonishment which is far-fetched, and if it were like that, the alif would have been deleted from Ma, and it was said: So by what mercy from God. And the rude: the rough and harsh. Al-Raghib said: The rude is the one with a bad character, and its origin is rudeness like caution. And the roughness of the heart is its hardness and lack of compassion and lack of reaction to good. And annihilation means dispersal. It is said: I scattered them and they dispersed, meaning they dispersed and the meaning is: If you were rough and hard-hearted and not gentle with them, they would have dispersed from around you out of awe of you and shyness from you because of what they had done in their charge. And if the matter is as mentioned, pardon them in what concerns you of rights, and ask forgiveness for them from God, the Most High, in what is up to God, the Most High, and consult them in the matter meaning: that which comes to you: any matter that is something that one consults about, or in the matter of war in particular as the context indicates, because that will please their feelings and gain their affection, and to inform the nation of the permissibility of that so that no one after you will be disgusted by it. What is meant here is consultation in matters other than those that the Shari’ah refers to. Linguists said: Consultation is taken from the Arabs’ saying: I bought the animal and consulted it if you knew its report, and it was said that it comes from their saying: I bought honey if you took it from its place. Ibn Khuz Mandad said: It is obligatory for the governors to consult the scholars regarding matters they do not know and regarding matters of this world that are unclear to them, and to consult the leaders of the army regarding matters related to war, and the leaders of the people regarding matters related to interests, and the leaders of the scribes, workers and ministers regarding matters related to the interests of the country and its development. Al-Qurtubi narrated from Ibn Atiyyah that there is no disagreement regarding the obligation to dismiss those who do not consult the people of knowledge and religion. His statement, Then when you have decided, then put your trust in God means: If you decide after consultation on something and your soul is reassured by it, then put your trust in God in doing that: that is, rely on Him and entrust Him. It was said that the meaning is: If you decide to carry out a matter, then put your trust in God, not in consultation. Determination originally means the intention to carry it out: that is, if you intend to carry out a matter, then put your trust in God. Ja’far al-Sadiq and Jabir ibn Zayd read If you have decided with a damma on the ta’, attributing the determination to God the Most High: that is, if I decide for you on something and guide you to it, then put your trust in God.
3:160: And His saying 160- If God helps you, none can overcome you is a renewed sentence to emphasize trust and urge it, and abandonment is abandoning support: that is, if God abandons your support, who is there who can help you after Him? This question is rhetorical. The pronoun in His saying: after Him refers to abandonment indicated by His saying and if He forsakes you or to God, and whoever knows that he has no supporter except God, the Exalted, and that whoever God helps, none can overcome him, and whoever He forsakes, none can support him, entrusts his affairs to Him and relies on Him and does not concern himself with anyone else. The prepositional phrase precedes the verb in His saying and upon God let the believers rely to indicate that it is restricted to Him.
3:161: His saying 161- And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war means: it is not right for him to do so, because theft and prophethood are incompatible. Abu Ubaid said: Theft is specifically from spoils of war, and we do not see it as treachery or hatred. What makes this clear is that it is said from treachery, aghal yaghul, and from hatred, ghal yaghul with the kasra, and from ghulul, ghal yaghul with the damma. It is said: he took spoils of war, ghululan: meaning he betrayed by taking something for himself and taking it back from his companions. So the meaning of the verse, according to the reading in the active form, is: it is not right for a prophet to betray anything from the spoils of war and take it for himself without his companions knowing. And in it is the exoneration of the prophets from theft. And its meaning, according to the passive reading: It is not right for a prophet to be betrayed by any of his companions: that is, to betray him in the spoils. According to this other reading, it is a prohibition for people from embezzling in the spoils. It only specifically refers to the betrayal of the prophets, while the betrayal of others, such as imams, sultans, and princes, is forbidden, because the betrayal of the prophets is a greater sin and a greater burden. And whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection, that is, he will come carrying it on his back, as was authenticated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he will disgrace him among the creation. This sentence includes confirmation of the prohibition of embezzlement and warning against it, as it is a sin for which its perpetrator will be punished in public, and the people of the gathering will see it, which is his coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying what he embezzled before he is fully held accountable for good and evil. This verse includes everyone who has earned good or evil, and embezzlement is included under it primarily because the context is about it.
3:162: His statement 162- Is he who pursues the pleasure of God like he who incurs the wrath of God? The question is for denial: meaning, he who pursues the pleasure of God in His commands and prohibitions, and acts according to His commands and avoids His prohibitions, is not like he who incurs: meaning, returns with great wrath from God because of his disobedience to what He commanded and prohibited. Included under this is he who pursues the pleasure of God by abandoning and avoiding embezzlement, and he who incurs the wrath of God because of his committing embezzlement.
3:163: Then he explained the difference between the two groups, saying: 163- They are of degrees with God, meaning: They differ in degrees, and the meaning is: They are of degrees, or they have degrees, so the degrees of those who follow the pleasure of God are not like the degrees of those who follow the wrath of God, for the first are in the highest degrees, and the last are in the lowest.
3:164: His saying 164- God has bestowed His favor upon the believers is the answer to an omitted oath, and He singled out the believers because they are the ones who benefit from His mission. The meaning of from themselves is that he is an Arab like them, and it was said: a human being like them, and the aspect of the favor on the first is that they understand him and comprehend his speech and do not need an interpreter, and its meaning on the second is that they are familiar with him due to the common humanity, and if he was a king, they would not have achieved complete familiarity with him due to the difference in nationality, and from themselves was read with the opening of the fa: meaning from the most noble of them because he is from Banu Hashim, and Banu Hashim are the best of Quraysh, and Quraysh are the best of the Arabs, and the Arabs are better than others, and perhaps the aspect of the favor on this reading is that since he was from the most noble of them, they were more obedient to him and closer to believing him, and it is necessary to specify the believers in this verse to the Arabs on the first aspect, but as for the second aspect, there is no need for this specification, and likewise on the reading of the one who reads with the opening of the fa, there is no need for the specification, because Banu Hashim are the most noble of the Arabs and the non-Arabs in the nobility of origin, the generosity of the carpenter, and the high status of the offspring. The first aspect is indicated by the Almighty's saying: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves and His saying: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people. His saying, He recites to them His verses, this is a second favor, meaning: He recites to them the Qur’an after they were people of ignorance who did not know anything about the laws. And purifies them, meaning: He cleanses them from the impurity of disbelief. This sentence is conjoined with the first sentence, and they are in the accusative case as a state, or as an attribute of the Messenger. Likewise, His saying, And teaches them the Book, and what is meant by the Book here is the Qur’an. And wisdom: the Sunnah. The explanation of that has already been presented in Al-Baqarah. And if they were before, meaning: before Muhammad, or before his mission, in manifest error, meaning: clear, without doubt. The lam is to differentiate between the lightened in from the heavy in, and the negative, so it enters into the predicate of the lightened in, not the negative, and its name is the pronoun of the matter, meaning: and the matter and the hadith. It was said: it is the negative, and the lam means except, meaning: and they were not before except in manifest error, and the Kufians said this, and the sentence, in both cases, is in the accusative case as a state. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: And they said to their brothers when they traveled throughout the land Al-Baqarah 2:13, he said: This is the statement of Abdullah bin Abi Salul and the hypocrites. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Suddi. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: That God may make that a regret within their hearts he said: Their statement saddens them but does not benefit them at all. They narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse: Then by mercy from God he said: By mercy from God you were lenient with them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: They would have dispersed from around you he said: They would have turned away from you. Ibn Adi and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha`b, Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said, when the verse, And consult them in the matter, was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Indeed, God and His Messenger have no need of it, but God has made it a mercy for my nation. So whoever consults them will not be considered rightly guided, and whoever abandons it will not be without error.” Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And consult them in the matter. He said: Abu Bakr and Umar. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about determination, and he said: Consulting people of opinion and then following them.” Abd bin Hamid, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse, And it is not for a prophet to take spoils, was revealed regarding a red quilt that was lost on the day of Badr, so some people said: Perhaps the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it, so it was revealed. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war, meaning: it is not for a prophet to be accused by his companions. Many hadiths have been narrated on the prohibition of spoils of war. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They have degrees with God, meaning: according to their deeds. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu’ab Al-Iman on the authority of Aisha regarding his statement, God has conferred a great favor upon the believers, the verse, she said: This is specific to the Arabs.
3:165: His saying 165- Or when a disaster befell you The alif is for interrogation with the intention of rebuking, and the waw is for conjunction. The disaster is the defeat and killing that befell them on the day of Uhud. You have suffered twice as much on the day of Badr, and that is because those killed from the Muslims on the day of Uhud were seventy. And they had killed seventy from the polytheists on the day of Badr and taken seventy prisoners, so the total of those killed and taken prisoner on the day of Badr was twice as many as those killed from the Muslims on the day of Uhud. The meaning is: I like what befell you from the polytheists to be half of what befell them from you before that, so you became alarmed and said, From where did this befall us? And we were promised victory. And his saying From where did this befall us? means from where did this defeat and killing befall us while we were fighting in the way of God, and with us was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God had promised us victory over them. His saying, Say, ‘It is from yourselves,’ is an order to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer their question with this answer: That is, what you asked about is from yourselves because the archers disobeyed what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to do, which was to remain in the place he had designated for them, and not to leave it under any circumstances. It was said that what was meant by his saying, It is from yourselves, was their leaving Medina. This is refuted by the fact that the promise of victory only came after that, and it was said that it was their choice of ransom on the day of Badr over killing.
3:166: 166- The day the two armies met the day of UHud 11:meaning what happened to you on the day of Uhud of killing, wounding and defeat was by the permission of God then by His knowledge, and it was said: by His decree and destiny, and it was said: by His imagination between you and them, and the fa entered into the answer to the relative pronoun because it resembles a condition as Sibawayh said. And his saying and that He may know the believers is in apposition to his saying then by the permission of God, in apposition of a cause to a cause.
3:167: And His saying 167- And that He may know those who are hypocrites is in apposition to what preceded it. It was said: He repeated the verb in order to honor the believers so that the verb attributed to them and to the hypocrites is one. What is meant by knowledge here is differentiation and manifestation, because His knowledge was established before that, and what is meant by the hypocrites here is Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions. His saying And it was said to them is in apposition to His saying They were hypocrites, meaning: So that God may know those who are hypocrites and those to whom it was said. It was said that it is a subject statement: meaning it was said to Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions Come, fight in the way of God if you are among those who believe in God and the Last Day or defend yourselves if you do not believe in God and the Last Day. They refused all of that and said: If we knew that there would be fighting, we would have followed you and fought with you, but there is no fighting there. It was said that the meaning is: If we were able to fight and were good at it, we would have followed you, but we are not able to do that and we are not good at it. He expressed the negation of the ability to fight by negating knowledge of it because it entails it, and in it there is a distance to which there is no refuge. It was said that its meaning is: If we knew what could be called fighting, we would have followed you, but what you are about to do is not fighting, but rather throwing oneself into destruction, due to the inability of us and you to repel what came from the army by going out to them and leaving the city. This also has a distance that is not the distance of what came before it. It was said that the meaning of repelling here is increasing the number of Muslims. It was said that its meaning is stay put, and the one who said this statement to the hypocrites that God the Almighty narrated was Abdullah bin Amr bin Haram Al-Ansari, the father of Jabir bin Abdullah. His statement, They are nearer to disbelief that Day than to faith means: On this day in which they were abandoned by the believers to disbelief they are nearer to faith in the eyes of those who thought that they were Muslims, because they had made their condition clear, torn their veils and exposed their hypocrisy at that time. It was said that the meaning is: They are nearer to the people of disbelief that Day than to the people of faith. His saying, They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts is a new sentence confirming the content of what preceded it: that is, they showed faith but concealed disbelief. The mouths are mentioned for emphasis, like his saying, He flies with his wings.
3:168: His statement 168- Those who said to their brothers etc.: meaning they are those who said to their brothers as a predicate of a deleted subject, and it is possible that it is a substitute for the waw of they conceal, or accusative of blame, or a description of those who were hypocrites. The meaning of they said to their brothers has already been presented, meaning: they said that to them, and the situation is that these speakers had sat back from fighting if they had obeyed us by not leaving the city, they would not have been killed, so God responded to that with His statement "Say: Then avert death from yourselves, if you should be truthful" and averting means repelling, meaning caution from fate is of no use, because the one who is killed is killed at his appointed time. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Or when a disaster befell you, the verse. He said: You have inflicted on the polytheists on the day of Badr twice as much as they inflicted on you on the day of Uhud. This was explained by Ikrimah. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: The Muslims killed seventy polytheists on the day of Badr and took seventy captive, and the polytheists killed seventy Muslims on the day of Uhud. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse that he said: When they saw those of them killed on the day of Uhud, they said, Where did this come from? It was not for the infidels to kill any of us. When God saw what they were saying about that, God said: They are like the captives you took on the day of Badr. God responded to them with that and hastened their punishment in this world so that they would be safe from it in the Hereafter. This is supported by what was narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ali, who said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, God has disliked what your people have done in taking prisoners, and He has commanded you to give them a choice between two things: either they come forward and their necks are struck, or they take ransom on the condition that you accept their number. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the people and mentioned that to them, and they said: O Messenger of God, our tribes and our brothers, rather we will take their ransom so that we will be strengthened to fight our enemy and their number will be martyred from us, so there is nothing in that that we dislike. So seventy men were killed from them on the Day of Uhud, the number of the prisoners of Badr. This hadith is in Sunan al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Hafri, on the authority of Yahya ibn Zakariya ibn Abi Zaydah, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, on the authority of Ali. Al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: It is hasan gharib, we do not know it except through the hadith of Ibn Abi Zaydah. Abu Usamah narrated something similar on the authority of Hisham. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a mursal form. The chain of transmission of Ibn Jarir for this hadith is as follows: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Ismail ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn ‘Awn, Sanid said, and he is Husayn, and Hajjaj narrated to me on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Zubaydah, on the authority of Ali, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, who said: Qurad bin Nuh told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Samak al-Hanafi Abu Zamil told us, Ibn Abbas told me on the authority of Umar bin al-Khattab, who said: When the day of Uhud came the following year, they were punished for what they had done on the day of Badr, by taking ransoms. Seventy of them were killed, and the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, fled from him. His front tooth was broken, the skull was smashed on his head, and blood flowed down his face. Then God Almighty revealed: Or when a disaster befell you verse. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Azwan, who is Qurad ibn Nuh, but in a longer version. However, what is problematic about the previous hadith of choice is what was revealed of the rebuke from Him, the Most High, to those who took the ransom, in His saying: It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a slaughter on the land. And what was narrated of his crying, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, regretting taking the ransom. If he had taken that after the choice was given to them by God, the Most High, He would not have rebuked them for it, nor would what happened from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those with him of regret and sorrow, nor did the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, approve of the opinion of Umar, may God be pleased with him, when he indicated killing the captives and said something to the effect of: If a punishment were revealed, none would be saved from it except Umar. All of them are in the books of hadith and biography. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, You said, ‘How is this?’ while we are Muslims fighting in anger for God, and these are polytheists. So He said, Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ This is a punishment for you for disobeying the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said, Do not follow them. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement, or defend, he said: Increase your numbers even if you do not fight. He also narrated something similar from al-Dahhak. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Awn al-Ansari regarding his statement, or defend, he said: Stay stationed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab and others who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Uhud with a thousand men from his companions, until when they were in the path between Uhud and Medina, Abdullah bin Ubayy with a third of the people withdrew from them and said: He obeyed them and disobeyed me, by God we do not know why we are killing ourselves here? So he returned with those who followed him from the hypocrites and the doubtful, and Abdullah bin Amr bin Haram from Banu Salamah followed them saying: O people, I remind you by God lest you abandon your Prophet and your people when their enemy confronts them. They said: If we had known that you would fight, we would not have surrendered you and we do not think that there will be fighting. Ibn Ishaq narrated: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Umar ibn Sa`d ibn Mu`adh and other scholars of ours narrated to me, and he mentioned it. He added that when they were stubborn with him and refused to leave, he said: May God distance you, enemies of God, for God will do without you. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, If we had known that there would be fighting, we would have followed you, he said: If we had known that we would find a place of fighting with you, we would have followed you.
3:169: When God Almighty explained that what happened to the believers on the day of Uhud was a test to distinguish the believer from the hypocrite, and the liar from the truthful, He explained here that whoever was not defeated and killed has this honor and blessing, and that such a thing is something that competitors compete over, not something that should be feared and guarded against as those whom God narrated said, If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed, and they said, If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed. So this sentence is a new sentence to explain this meaning, and the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone, and it was read with the letter ya below: meaning, let no one who thinks should think. Scholars have differed about the martyrs mentioned in this verse. Who are they? Some say: The martyrs of Uhud, others say: The martyrs of Badr, and others say: The martyrs of Bir Ma'unah. Assuming that it was revealed for a specific reason, then the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. The meaning of the verse according to the majority is that they are alive with a confirmed life. Then they differed. Some of them say: That their souls are returned to them in their graves and they enjoy themselves. Mujahid said: They are provided with the fruits of Paradise: meaning they find its fragrance, but they are not in it. Others than the majority went to the view that it is a metaphorical life, and the meaning is: That they are under the judgment of God and deserve to enjoy themselves in Paradise. The first is correct, and there is no reason to resort to metaphor. The pure Sunnah has reported that their souls are in the bodies of green birds, and that they are in Paradise, provided with, eating, and enjoying themselves. His saying, "those who were killed" is the first object. The one who calculates is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or everyone as mentioned above. It has been said that the relative pronoun may be the subject of the verb, and the first object is omitted: that is, do not think that those who killed themselves are dead. This is an unnecessary effort, and the meaning of the Qur’anic system is extremely clear and evident. His statement, Rather, they are alive, is the predicate of a deleted subject, that is, rather, they are alive. It was read in the accusative case based on the estimation of the verb: that is, rather, I think that they are alive. His statement, With their Lord, is either a second predicate, or an attribute of alive, or in the accusative case as a state. It has been said that there is an omission in the speech and the estimation is: With the honor of their Lord. Sibawayh said: This is with the honor, not with the nearness. His statement, they are provided for, can be parsed in the same ways that we mentioned in his statement, With their Lord. What is meant by provision here is the provision known in customs according to what the majority believe, as mentioned above. According to those other than the majority, what is meant by it is beautiful praise, and there is no reason that requires distorting the Arabic words in the Book of God Almighty and interpreting them as far-fetched metaphors, for no reason that requires that.
3:170: And his saying 170- "Rejoicing is a state of the pronoun in they are provided for, and with what God has given them of His bounty" is related to it. Ibn al-Sameefa' read "Farihin" and they are two dialects like farah and farah, and hazar and hadhar. What is meant by "with what God has given them" is what God has brought to them of honor through martyrdom, and what they have become in of life, and what reaches them of God's provision. "And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them" of their brothers the mujahideen who were not killed at that time. What is meant by catching up here is that they have not caught up with them in killing and martyrdom, but rather they will catch up with them later. It was said: What is meant is that they did not join them in virtue, even though they were people of virtue in general. The waw in and they rejoice is a conjunction to they are provided for, meaning: they are provided for and they rejoice. It was said: What is meant by their brothers here is all the Muslims, martyrs and others, because when they witnessed the reward of God and attained certainty in the truth of the religion of Islam, they rejoiced at that for all the people of Islam who are alive and have not died. This is stronger, because its meaning is broader and its benefit is greater, and the wording includes it, rather it is the apparent meaning. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Furak said this. His statement that there is no fear for them, nor do they grieve is a substitute for those: meaning they rejoice at this state that has occurred for their brothers, that there is no fear for them, nor do they grieve. An is the light form of the heavy form, and its subject is the pronoun of the deleted subject.
3:171: And he repeated his statement 172- they are rejoicing to emphasize the first, and to show that rejoicing is not merely due to the absence of fear and sadness, but rather due to it and to the grace and favor of God. And the grace is what God bestows upon His servants. And the favor is what He bestows upon them. And it was said that the grace is the reward, and the additional favor, and it was said that the grace is Paradise, and the favor is included in the grace mentioned after it to emphasize it, and it was said that the first rejoicing is related to the state of their brothers, and the second rejoicing is related to the state of themselves. His statement and that God does not waste the reward of the believers Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the hamza of an, and the rest read it with a fatha, so according to the first reading it is a new objection. And in it is an indication that God does not waste the reward of any of the deeds of the believers, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, and God does not waste the reward of the believers. And according to the second reading the sentence is an appositive to the favor included in the sentence of what they are rejoicing about.
3:172: And his saying 172- Those who responded is an attribute of the believers, or a substitute for them, or for those who did not join them, or it is a subject whose predicate is For those among them who did good and feared God is a great reward as a whole, or it is accusative for praise and the explanation of the ulcer has been presented.
3:173: His statement 172- Those to whom the people said What is meant by the people here is Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud as will be explained, and it is permissible to use the term people for him because he is from their kind, and it was said: What is meant by the people is the caravan of Abd al-Qays who passed by Abu Sufyan, and it was said: They are the hypocrites. What is meant by his statement The people have gathered against you is Abu Sufyan and his companions, and the pronoun in his statement And increased them refers to the statement indicated by the speaker or to the said, which is The people have gathered against you, so fear them or to the speaker, and the meaning is: They did not lose heart when they heard that nor did they pay attention to it, but rather they were sincere to God and increased in reassurance and certainty. And in it is evidence that faith increases and decreases. His statement And they said, God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs is according to the source of hasabahu: meaning He sufficed him and it means the doer: meaning muhsab means sufficiency. He said in Al-Kashshaf: The evidence that it has the meaning of the one who is sufficient is that you say: This man is sufficient for you, so you describe an indefinite noun with it because adding it to the meaning of an active participle is not real. End quote. And the agent is the one to whom matters are entrusted, meaning: Yes, the one to whom our matter is entrusted, or the sufficient one, or the guarantor, and the one specifically praised is omitted: meaning, yes, the agent is God, glory be to Him.
3:174: His statement 174- "So they returned" is in apposition to something omitted: that is, they went out to them and returned with a blessing. It is related to something omitted that occurred as a state. The tanween is for emphasis: that is, they returned clothed in a great "blessing", which is safety from their enemy and well-being. "And bounty", that is, a reward that God bestowed upon them. It was said: profit in trade. It was said: the blessing is specifically for the benefits of this world, and bounty is for the benefits of the Hereafter. Its interpretation was presented shortly in a manner that suits that situation, since the speech in it is with the martyrs who have already reached the Hereafter, and the speech here is with the living. His statement, No harm touched them is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, they were safe from harm, neither killing nor wounding nor anything they feared had befallen them. And they pursued the pleasure of God in what they did and left, including their going out for this raid. And God is possessor of great bounty whose value cannot be measured nor its extent reached. Among His bounty upon them is their steadfastness and their going out to meet their enemy and guiding them to say this statement which brings about all good and repels all evil.
3:175: His saying "That is only" meaning: the one who discourages you, O believers, "the devil is the best demonstrative pronoun, and it is possible that the devil is an attribute of the demonstrative pronoun and the predicate is his saying He frightens his allies, so according to the first, his saying He frightens his allies" is a new or circumstantial sentence, and it appears that what is meant here is the devil himself in consideration of what issues from him of whispering that requires discouragement, and it was said: what is meant is Nu'aym bin Mas'ud when he said that statement to them, and it was said Abu Sufyan when he issued a threat to them, and the meaning is: that the devil frightens the believers with his allies who are the disbelievers, and it was said that his saying "his allies" is accusative by removing the preposition, meaning he frightens you with his allies or from his allies, as stated by al-Farra', al-Zajjaj and Abu Ali al-Farsi. Ibn al-Anbari rejected it by saying that frightening can take two objects by itself, so there is no need to omit the preposition. According to al-Farra' and those with him, the object of frightens is omitted: meaning he frightens you. According to the first, the first object is omitted and the second is mentioned. It is possible that what is meant is that Satan frightens his allies, who are the hypocrites who sit back, so there is no omission. His statement, So do not fear them, meaning his allies with whom Satan frightens you, or do not fear the people mentioned in His statement, Indeed, the people have gathered against you, He, the Exalted, forbade them from fearing them lest they become cowardly in the encounter and fail to go out, and He commanded them to fear Him, the Exalted, so He said, And fear, so do what I command you to do and leave what I forbid you to do, because I am the one who deserves to be feared, and to be watched over for My command and prohibition, because good and evil are in My hands. He restricted it with His statement, If you are believers, because belief requires that. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse, And never think that those who are killed in the way of God was revealed about Hamza and his companions. Saeed bin Mansour and Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha that it was revealed about the killing of Uhud, and Hamza was one of them. And Abd bin Hamid, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When your brothers were afflicted with Uhud, God placed their souls in the bodies of green birds that frequent the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and take refuge in golden lanterns suspended in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their food and drink and the beauty of their resting place, they said: ‘If only our brothers knew what God has done for us.’” In another version: “They said: ‘And their drink and their resting place.’ They said: ‘Who will inform our brothers that we are alive in Paradise and are provided for, so that they do not lose interest in jihad or turn away from war?’ God said: ‘I will inform them on your behalf.’ Then God revealed these verses: ‘And do not think that those who have been killed…’ and what follows.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated with a hasan chain of transmission, Ibn Majah, Ibn Khuzaymah, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that his father asked God, the Exalted, to grant him success in what he was in, so this verse was revealed while he was among those killed at Uhud. It has been narrated through many chains of transmission that the reason for the revelation of this verse was the killing of Uhud. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Anas that the reason for the revelation of this verse was the killing of Bir Ma’unah. In any case, the verse, considering the generality of its wording, includes every martyr. It has been proven in many hadiths in Sahih and elsewhere that the souls of the martyrs are in the bodies of green birds. There is a long list of proven virtues of the martyrs that are well-known in the books of hadith. Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated with a saheeh chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the polytheists returned from Uhud, they said: You did not kill Muhammad, nor did you take the young maidens with you. What a bad thing you have done! Return. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of that, so he called upon the Muslims and they volunteered until they reached Hamra' al-Asad, or Bir Abi Utbah. Sufyan was not sure, so the polytheists said: He will return the next year. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, and it was considered a military campaign. Then God, the Exalted, revealed: Those who responded to God and the Messenger 1:13. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Aisha regarding the words of God, the Exalted: Those who responded to God and the Messenger 1:13, that she said to Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr: O son of my sister, your parents were among them: Az-Zubayr and Abu Bakr. When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, suffered what he suffered on the Day of Uhud, the polytheists turned away from him and he feared that they would return, so he said: Who will return after them? So seventy volunteered from them, including Abu Bakr and Az-Zubayr. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Hamra’ Al-Asad, and Abu Sufyan had decided to return to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and they said: We have returned before we eradicate them so that we may attack the rest of them. Then he heard that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had gone out with his companions seeking them, so Abu Sufyan and his companions thought about that, and a group of Abd Al-Qais passed by, and Abu Sufyan said to them: Inform Muhammad that we have decided to return to his companions so that we may eradicate them. When the group passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Hamra’ Al-Asad, they told him what Abu Sufyan had said, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims with him said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. So God revealed about that: Those who responded to God and the Messenger 1:13. Musa bin Uqbah narrated in his Maghazi and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Shihab who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) called the Muslims to meet Abu Sufyan at Badr. Then Satan took his followers from among the people and they walked among the people, frightening them, and they said: We have been informed that people have gathered against you like the night, hoping to attack you. There are many narrations on this subject that are included in the books of Hadith and Seerah. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: Wounds are wounds. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of As-Suddi that Abu Sufyan and his companions met a Bedouin and they promised him a reward to inform the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his companions that they had gathered against them. He informed the Prophet (peace be upon him) of that, and he and the companions said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Then they returned from Hamra’ Asad, and God revealed about them and the Bedouin, Those to whom the people said, the verse. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi’ that this Bedouin was from Khuza’ah. There are hadiths that have been narrated about the virtue of this phrase, I mean Hasbun God wa ni’mal wakeel, including what Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you are faced with a serious matter, say: ‘Hasbun God wa ni’mal wakeel.’” Ibn Kathir said after narrating it: This is a strange hadith from this perspective. Abu Nu’aym narrated on the authority of Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hasbun God wa ni’mal wakeel, security for every fearful person. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in al-Dhikr on the authority of Aisha, “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was intensified by his grief, he would wipe his hand over his head and beard, then he sighed deeply and said: Hasbun God wa ni’mal wakeel.” Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Hasbun God wa ni’mal wakeel, Ibrahim said it when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad said it when they said: The people have gathered against you. Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Awf ibn Malik that he told them, "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, judged between two men. When the one against whom the judgment was passed turned away, he said, 'God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.' The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, 'Bring the man back to me.' He said, 'What did you say?' He said, 'I said, 'God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.' The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, 'God blames incompetence, but you should be intelligent. If a matter overcomes you, say, 'God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'" Ahmad narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, "How can I enjoy myself while the one with the horn has put the horn in his mouth and bent his forehead, hearing when he is commanded to blow? Then he ordered the Companions to say, 'God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In God we trust.'" This is a good hadith. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Dala'il on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement, "And they returned with favor and bounty from God, he said, The favor is that they were safe, and the bounty is that a caravan passed by during the season, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, bought it and was given a reward and divided it among his Companions." Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: The virtue is what they obtained from trade and reward. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: As for the blessing, it is well-being, and as for the virtue, it is trade, and evil is killing. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, No evil touched them, he said: No one harmed them, And they followed the pleasure of God, he said: They obeyed God and His Messenger. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on his authority regarding his statement, That is only Satan frightening his allies, he said: Satan says that Satan frightens his allies. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik, he said: He magnifies his allies in your eyes. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar to what Ibn Abbas said. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan: That was only to frighten Satan, and Satan fears no one except the allies of Satan.
3:176: His saying 176- "And let it not grieve you." Nafi' read it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the zay, and Ibn Muhaisin read it with a damma on the ya' and the zay, and the rest read it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the zay, and they are two dialects. It is said: The matter grieved me and it grieved me, and the first is more eloquent. Talhah read "yasari'un." It was said: They are people who apostatized, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saddened by that, so God consoled him and forbade him from grieving, and he explained that by saying that they would not harm God at all, but they only harmed themselves by noticing them in the Hereafter and that they will have a great punishment. It was said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh, and it was said: They are the hypocrites, and it was said: It is general for all disbelievers. Al-Qushayri said: Grieving over the disbelief of a disbeliever is an act of obedience, but the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was excessive in his grief, so he was forbidden from that as God the Most High said: So let not your soul perish over them in regret “Perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over them, if they do not believe in this message” Al-Qushayri’un and the preposition fi instead of ila indicate that they are settled in it and will continue to be involved in it, and the same applies to they hasten in good deeds. His statement: Indeed, they will never harm God at all is an explanation of the prohibition, and the meaning is that their disbelief will not diminish the kingdom of God the Most High at all. It was said: What is meant is that they will never harm His friends, and it is possible that what is meant is that they will never harm His religion that He has legislated for His servants. Something is accusative as a source: meaning any harm, and it was said: accusative by removing the preposition: meaning with something. And fortune is the share. Abu Zaid said: It is said that a man is fortunate if he has a share of provision, and the meaning is that God does not want to give them a share in Paradise or a share of the reward, and the future tense is to indicate the permanence and continuity of the will and for them is a great punishment because of their haste in disbelief, so the harm of their disbelief returned to them, making clear to them the lack of fortune in the afterlife and their destiny in the great punishment.
3:177: His statement 177 - Indeed, those who have purchased disbelief in exchange for faith means: they have exchanged disbelief for faith. The realization of this metaphor has already been presented. They will not harm God at all means the same as the first, and it is to emphasize what was presented. It has been said: The first is specific to the hypocrites, and the second includes all disbelievers, and the first is more appropriate.
3:178: His saying 178- "And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is better for themselves. Ibn Amir, Asim, and others read yasibna" with a lower ya', and Hamza read it with a higher ya'. The meaning according to the first reading is: Let not the disbelievers think that Our granting them respite by giving them a long life and a comfortable life or by what they achieved of victory on the day of Uhud "is better for themselves." This is not the case, rather We grant them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment. According to the second reading: Do not think, O Muhammad, that granting respite to those who disbelieved in what was mentioned is better for themselves. Rather, it is an evil that has befallen them and descended upon them. That is, granting respite to those who disbelieved in what was mentioned is better for themselves. Rather, it is an evil that has befallen them and descended upon them. That is, the respite that We grant them is so that they may increase in sin. The relative pronoun in the first reading is the subject of the verb, and anma namlī and what follows it replaces the two objects of hisabān according to Sībawayh, or replaces one of them, and the other is omitted according to al-Akhfash. As for the second reading according to Sībawayh, or replaces one of them, and the other is omitted according to al-Akhfash. As for the second reading, al-Zajjaj said: The relative pronoun is the first object, and anma and what follows it is a substitute for the relative pronoun and replaces the two objects. It is not correct for anma and what follows it to be the second object, because the second object in this case is the first in meaning. Abu Ali al-Farsi said: If this were correct, it would have been khayr in the accusative case because basīr is a substitute for alladhī kāfiru, so it is as if he said: Do not think that granting respite to those who disbelieve is good. Al-Kisa’i and al-Farra’ said: The verb can be repeated as if he said: Do not think that those who disbelieve and do not think that “anma namlī for them, then it replaces the two objects. Al-Kashāf said: If you say: How can the substitute be correct when only one of the two objects is mentioned, and it is not permissible to limit the verb of hisabān to one object? I said: This is correct in that relying on the substitute and the substituted is in the ruling of the gift, do you not see that you have placed some of your belongings on top of each other while it is not permissible for you to remain silent about your belongings? End. Yahya bin Waththab read innama namli with a kasra on in in both of them, and this is a weak reading considering the Arabic language. And his statement: innama namli lahum so that they may increase in sin is a renewed sentence explaining the reason for granting respite to the disbelievers. The majority have used this verse as evidence to prove the invalidity of what the Mu’tazila say, because God Almighty has informed us that He extends the lives of the disbelievers and makes their life comfortable so that they may increase in sin. Abu Hatim said: I heard Al-Akhfash mention the kasra of the first innama namli and the fatha of the second, and he uses this as evidence for the people of predestination because he is one of them, and he makes it on this estimation: And let not those who disbelieve think that We grant them respite so that they may increase in sin. We grant them respite only for their own good. He said in Al-Kashaf: The increase in sin is a cause, and not every cause is an accident. Do you not see yourself saying: I stayed away from the war due to inability and poverty, and I left the country for fear of evil, and nothing happened to you, but rather they are causes and reasons.
3:179: His statement 179- "God would not leave the believers in the state you are in" is a new statement, and the address according to the majority of commentators is to the disbelievers and hypocrites: meaning God would not leave the believers in the state you are in of disbelief and hypocrisy "until He distinguishes the wicked from the good." It was said: The address is to the believers and hypocrites: meaning God would not leave you in the state you are in of mixing until He distinguishes some of you from others. It was said: The address is to the polytheists. What is meant by the believers are those in the loins and wombs: meaning God would not leave your children in the state you are in until He separates you from them. It was said: The address is to the believers: meaning God would not leave you, O group of believers, in the state you are in of mixing with the hypocrites until He distinguishes between you. In this way, and the second way there is a shift in the speech. And it was read "yamiz" with emphasis for the lighter one, from maza a thing yamizhu yamizan if he differentiates between two things, if they are things it is said: mazhu tamayzan "And God would not inform you of the unseen" so that you could differentiate between the good and the bad, for He is the One who keeps the knowledge of the unseen to Himself and does not reveal His unseen to anyone except whomever He chooses from among His messengers, whom He chooses and informs of something from His unseen so that he can differentiate between you, as happened with our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he appointed many of the hypocrites, for that was by God teaching him, not by his knowing the unseen, and it was said that the meaning is: And God would not inform you of the unseen in who deserves prophethood, so that the revelation would be by your choice "but God selects that is, He chooses from among His messengers whomever He wills." His statement, So believe in God and His Messengers, meaning: Do the faith required of you and leave being occupied with what is not your concern, such as seeking knowledge of God Almighty. And if you believe in what was mentioned, and fear God, then for you, instead of that, is a great reward, the extent of which is unknown and the nature of which is not attained.
3:180: His saying 180- And let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. The relative pronoun is in the nominative case as the subject of the verb according to the reading of those who read with the lower ya’, and the first object is omitted: that is, let not the stingy people think that stinginess is good for them. This was said by Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and Al-Farra’. They said: It was omitted because they are stingy with it, and from that is the saying of the poet: If a fool is forbidden, he will run after it and disobey, and the fool will go after disobedience. That is, it led to foolishness, so the foolish person indicates foolishness. As for the reading of those who read with the superior, the verb is attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the first object is omitted: that is, do not think, O Muhammad, that the miserliness of those who are miserly is good for them. Al-Zajjaj said: It is like And ask the town, and the pronoun mentioned is the pronoun of separation. Al-Mubarrad said: The seen in his statement They will be encircled by what they were miserly with is the seen of threat, and this sentence explains the meaning of his statement Rather, it is worse for them. It was said: The meaning of encircling here is that what they were miserly with of money will be a collar of fire around their necks. It was said: Its meaning is that they will bear the punishment for what they were miserly with, so it is from energy and not from encircling. It was said that the meaning is that they are bound by their deeds as a collar binds the neck. It is said: So-and-so encircled his deeds with the collar of a dove, meaning he was bound by the punishment for his deeds. It was said: That which is not paid in zakat from money will be represented to him as a bald-headed snake until it is encircled around his neck, as was reported in a chain traced back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qurtubi said: Stinginess in the language means that a person prevents a right that is due to him. As for the one who prevents what is not due to him, he is not stingy. His statement, And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, means: It belongs to Him alone and not to anyone else, as the introduction indicates. The meaning is: He owns what is in them that is inherited by its people, so why are they stingy with that and do not spend it when it belongs to God, the Most High, not to them? Rather, it was with them as a loan that can be returned. Similar to this verse is the statement of God, the Most High, Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and His statement, And spend out of that which He has made you successors therein. Inheritance in origin is what is transferred from one owner to another and was not owned by that other before it was transferred to him by inheritance. It is known that God, the Most High, is the true owner of all His creations. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Indeed, those who have purchased disbelief at the price of faith, he said: They are the hypocrites. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: There is no soul, righteous or wicked, but death is better for it than life, if he was righteous, for God said: And what is with God is better for the righteous, and if he was wicked, for He said: And let not those who disbelieve think, the verse. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Darda’. Sa’id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Barzah as well. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: They said: If Muhammad is truthful, then let him inform us who among us believes in him and who disbelieves. So God revealed: God would never leave the believers, the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He distinguishes the people of happiness from the people of misery. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, who said: He distinguishes between them in jihad and migration. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement: And God would not inform you of the unseen, he said: No one knows the unseen except a Messenger. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, But God selects, he said: He singles out. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Malik, who said: He extracts. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement: And let not those who are stingy think, he said: They are the People of the Book, who were stingy in explaining it to the people. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They are the Jews. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: They were stingy in spending it in the way of God, they did not pay its zakat. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever God gives wealth and he does not pay its zakat, a bald-headed snake with two tufts of hair will appear before him on the Day of Resurrection, and it will take hold of his jaw and say: ‘I am your wealth, I am your treasure.’ Then he recited this verse.” This meaning was mentioned in many hadiths on the authority of a group of the Companions, with chains of transmission traceable to the Prophet.
3:181: The commentators said: When God revealed, Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? some of the Jews said this statement to deceive their weak ones, not because they believed it, because they are the People of the Book, but rather they meant that if what He asked of us regarding the loan on the tongue of Muhammad was true, then He is poor, so that they would cast doubt on their brothers in the religion of Islam. His statement 181- We will write down what they said We will write it down in the records of the angels, or We will preserve it. Or We will reward them for it. What is meant by the threat to them, and that this will not be missed by God, but rather it is prepared for them on the Day of Judgment. The phrase We will write down is a new sentence in response to an implied question, as if it was said: What did God do with those from whom He heard this heinous statement? He said: He said to them, We will write down what they said. Al-A'mash and Hamza read Sayyiktub with a doubled dot underneath, in the passive form. And he read with the raising of the lam from Qataluhum and Yaqul with a doubled ya underneath. His saying, And their killing of the prophets is in apposition to what they said: meaning, We write down their killing of the prophets: meaning, their ancestors killed the prophets. This was attributed to them because they were pleased with it. This saying was made a companion to the killing of the prophets, indicating that it is of a great and heinous nature, equal to the killing of the prophets. His saying, And We say is in apposition to We will write down meaning, We will take revenge on them after writing down with this saying that We will say to them in the fire, or at death, or at the reckoning. And burning is a name for blazing fire, and using the word tasting to refer to the feeling of torment is a significant exaggeration. Ibn Mas’ud read, And it is said, taste.
3:182: And the reference in his saying 182- that is to the punishment mentioned before it, and he referred to the near by the formula with which the distant is referred to to indicate the distance of its status in horror, and he mentioned the hands because they are the direct cause of most sins. And His saying, And that God is not unjust to the servants, is connected to for what your hands have put forth, and the reason is that He, glory be to Him, punished them for the sin they committed and rewarded them for their actions, so that was not injustice, or in the sense that He is the Owner of the kingdom, disposing of His kingdom as He wishes, and He is not unjust to those He punishes for their sin. It was said that the reason for it is that the negation of injustice entails justice, which requires rewarding the doer of good and punishing the wrongdoer. It was responded that leaving the punishment while its cause exists is not injustice rationally or legally. It was said that the sentence of His saying, And that God is not unjust to the servants, is in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, the matter is that God is not unjust to the servants, and the expression of that is the negation of injustice, even though punishing them without sin is not injustice according to the people of the Sunnah, let alone being extreme injustice, to show that He is free from that, and the negation of the injustice of the one who feels the abundance indicates the establishment of the origin of injustice. The answer to that is that what he threatened to do to them, if it were injustice, would be great, so he denied it to the extent of its greatness if it were proven.
3:183: His saying 183- Those who said is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning: they are the ones who said. It was said: an adjective for the slaves, and it was said: it is accusative for blame, and it was said: it is in the place of a genitive substitute for God has heard the statement of those who said, and this is weak, because the substitute is what is intended and not what is substituted for, and the matter is not like that here, and these speakers are a group of Jews as will come, and this statement, which is that God commanded them not to believe in a messenger until he brings them a sacrifice, is among their false claims. It was the custom of the Children of Israel that they would bring a sacrifice. The prophet would stand up and call, and fire would come down from the sky and burn him, and God did not command all of His prophets to do that, nor did He make it evidence of the truth of the claim of prophethood, and for this reason God responded to them and said: "Say: Messengers came to you before me with clear proofs and with what you said" of the sacrifice so why did you kill them if you should be truthful? Like Yahya bin Zakariya and Isaiah and the rest of the prophets who were killed. The sacrifice: what one draws closer to God through sacrifice, charity, and good deeds. It is two forms of the act of drawing closer.
3:184: Then God consoled His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying 184- If they deny you, then messengers before you were denied who came with the same clear proofs as you brought. And al-Zubur is the plural of al-Zabur which means the book, and its explanation has been presented. And the illuminating book is the clear, obvious, and luminous. It is said that something ignited, illuminated, and was illuminated, meaning it was illuminated. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr entered the school and found the Jews gathered around a man among them called Finhas, who was one of their scholars and rabbis. Abu Bakr said: Woe to you, Phinehas! Fear God and submit, for by God you know that Muhammad, the Messenger of God, is written in your Torah. Phinehas said: By God, Abu Bakr, we are not poor before God, and He is poor before us. We do not supplicate to Him as He supplicates to us, and we are rich from Him. If He were rich without us, He would not have borrowed from us, as your companion claims. He forbids you from usury and gives to us. If He were rich without us, He would not have given us usury. Abu Bakr became angry and struck Phinehas’ face with a severe blow, and said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, were it not for the covenant between us and you, I would have struck your neck, O enemy of God. Phinehas went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, look at what your companion did to me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr: What made you do what you did? He said: O Messenger of God, he said a terrible thing, claiming that God is poor and that they are rich in need of Him. When he said that, I became angry for God's sake because of what he said, so I slapped him in the face. Finhas denied it and said: I did not say that. So God revealed what Finhas said, confirming what Abu Bakr had said: God has heard the statement of those who said 3:10. And it was revealed about Abu Bakr and what he had become angry about that: And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God much abuse 3:10. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated this story on the authority of Ikrimah. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of al-Suddi in a shorter version. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Dhiya' in al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Jews came to Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when God revealed: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? They said: O Muhammad, is your Lord poor and would ask His servants for a loan? So God revealed the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah that the one who said this statement was Huyayy ibn Akhtab and that it was revealed about him. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Badr that he was asked about his statement, And their killing of the prophets unjustly, and they did not realize that. He said: By their allegiance to those who killed the prophets. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And that God is not unjust to His servants, he said: I will not punish those who did not commit a crime. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement, Those who said, ‘God has made a covenant with us,’ he said: They are the Jews. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Until he brings us an offering that the fire will consume, he said: A man from us gives charity, and when it is accepted from him, fire descends upon him from the sky and consumes him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, Those who said, ‘God has made a covenant with us,’ he said: They lied about God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, With clear proofs, he said: The lawful and the unlawful. And the Scriptures, he said: The books of the prophets. And the enlightening Book, he said: It is the Qur’an.
3:185: His saying 185- Taste comes from taste, and from it is the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: He who does not die in happiness will die old. Death is a cup and one must taste it. This verse includes the promise and the threat to the believer and the disbeliever after informing him about the misers who say, God is poor, and we are rich. Al-A’mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read the taste of death with tanween and the accusative of death. The majority read it with the addition. His statement, And you will only be given your wages in full on the Day of Resurrection, the reward of the believer is the reward, and the reward of the disbeliever is the punishment. That is, the payment and completion of wages will only be on that day, and whatever wages occur in this world or in the intermediate realm is only some of the wages. Al-Zahzaha: to move away, and al-Ibaad: repeating the word Zah which means to pull quickly. It was stated in Al-Kashshaf and it was previously discussed: Whoever is far from the Fire on that Day and is removed has succeeded: meaning he has attained what he wants and escaped from what he fears. This is the true success that no success can come close to, for every success, even if it is in all demands but Paradise, is nothing compared to it. O God, there is no success except the success of the Hereafter, and no life except its life, and no bliss except its bliss. So forgive our sins, and cover our faults and be pleased with us with a pleasure after which there is no discontent, and combine for us Your pleasure with us and Paradise.” And enjoyment: what a person enjoys and benefits from, then it disappears and does not remain. This is what most of the commentators said. Arrogance: Satan deceives people with false hopes and false promises. God, the Almighty, likened the world to enjoyment that he deceives those who want it, and it has a beloved appearance and a hated interior.
