Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf and his companions came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Prophet of God, we were in glory while we were polytheists, but when we believed we became humiliated. He said: I have been commanded to forgive, so do not fight the people. When God moved him to Madinah, He commanded him to fight, but they refrained. Then God revealed: ‘Have you not seen those who were told, “Restrain your hands?”’ 1:100. ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah in their interpretation of the verse something similar. ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: It was revealed about the Jews. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: ‘But when fighting was prescribed for them, at once a party’ 1:100, he said: God forbade this nation from doing what they did. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding His statement: ‘Until a near term,’ he said: It is death. And they narrated something similar to it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. And Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada, In fortified towers, he said: In fortified palaces. And Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah, he said: They are palaces in the sky. And Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Sufyan. And Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And if good befalls them, he said: A blessing, And if evil befalls them, he said: A calamity, “Say: All is from God,” he said: Blessings and calamities. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah, regarding his statement, And if good befalls them, he said: This is in prosperity and adversity. And regarding his statement, Whatever good befalls you, he said: This is in good and bad deeds. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Say, ‘All is from God,’ meaning: The good and the bad are from God. As for the good, He bestowed it upon you, and as for the bad, He tested you with it. Regarding his statement, And whatever evil befalls you, he said: What befell him on the Day of Uhud, that his face was wounded and his front tooth was broken. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on his authority regarding his statement, And whatever evil befalls you is from yourself, he said: This was on the Day of Uhud, meaning: Whatever calamity befell you, it was because of your sin, and I have decreed it for you. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid that Ibn Abbas used to recite, And whatever evil befalls you is from yourself, and I have decreed it for you. Mujahid said: This is how Ubayy and Ibn Mas`ud read it. Ibn Al-Anbari narrated something similar to this statement of Mujahid in Al-Masahif. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And they say, ‘We obey.’ He said: They are people who used to say in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, We believe in God and His Messenger, so that their blood and property would be safe. But when they went out from the presence of the Messenger of God, a party of them went to sleep, meaning: They went against what they said in his presence, so God criticized them. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: Other than those, what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said.
4:82: The hamza in His statement 82- Do they not then reflect? is for denial, and the fa' is for connecting to something understood: that is, do they turn away from the Qur'an and not reflect on it? It is said that you reflected on something: you thought about its consequences and pondered it, then it is used for every reflection, and contemplation: is that a person contemplates his matter as if he is looking at what its consequences will lead to, and this verse and the statement of God Almighty Do they not then contemplate the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts? indicate the necessity of contemplating the Qur'an in order to know its meaning. Meaning: If they had contemplated it properly, they would have found it to be harmonious and not contradictory, correct in meaning, strong in structure, and reaching the highest levels of eloquence. And if it had been from other than God, they would have found within it much discrepancy, meaning: disparity and contradiction. This does not include the difference in the amounts of verses and chapters, because what is meant is the difference of contradiction and disparity and the lack of conformity with reality. This is the nature of human speech, especially if it is long and its speaker is concerned with informing about the unseen, because nothing of it is found to be correct and conform to reality except a rare little.
4:83: His statement 83- And if there comes to them report of security or fear, they broadcast it. It is said: he broadcasted something and broadcasted it: if he disclosed it and made it known. These are a group of weak Muslims who, if they heard something about the Muslims that contained security, such as the victory of the Muslims and the killing of their enemy, or that contained fear, such as the defeat of the Muslims and their killing, they broadcast it, thinking that there is nothing wrong with that. His statement, And if they had referred it to the Messenger or to those in authority among them, and they are the people of knowledge and sound minds to whom they refer in their affairs, or they are the rulers over them, then those who extract it from them would have known of it, meaning: they would have extracted it through their planning and sound minds. The meaning is that if they had left broadcasting the report until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the one who broadcasted it or those in authority among them were the ones who took charge of that, because they know what should be disclosed and what should be concealed. And the deduction is taken from the word istanabatt al-ma' meaning to extract it. Nabat: The extracted water is the first thing that comes out of the well when it is dug. It was said that these weak people used to hear the rumours of the hypocrites against the Muslims and they would spread them, thus causing corruption. His statement, And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few. That is, had it not been for the grace of God upon you by sending His Messenger and revealing His Book, you would have followed Satan and remained in your disbelief except for a few of you, or except for a few of you following. It was said that the meaning is: They spread it except for a few of them, for it was not spread or diffused. This was said by Al-Kisa’i, Al-Akhfash, Al-Farra’, Abu Ubaidah, Abu Hatim, and Ibn Jarir. It was said that the meaning is because those who extract it knew it except for a few of them. This was said by Al-Zajjaj. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, And if it had been from other than God, they would have found within it much contradiction. He said: The word of God does not differ and it is the truth and there is no falsehood in it, but the word of people differs. Abd bin Hamid, Muslim and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew from his wives, I entered the mosque and found the people poking themselves with pebbles and saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divorced his wives. So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: He did not divorce his wives. Then this verse was revealed: “And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it. But if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those in authority among them, the ones who are able to investigate it would have known about it.” So I was the one who investigated that information. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: This is about informing when a Muslim army goes on a raid and informs the people about it, and they say: The Muslims have killed such and such from their enemy, and the enemy has killed such and such from the Muslims, so they spread it among themselves without the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, telling them about it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, And when there comes to them, he said: They are the people of hypocrisy. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Muadh something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, he said: Then the speech was interrupted. His statement, except a few, is at the beginning of the verse informing about the hypocrites. He said, And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they spread it around, meaning about the few believers.
4:84: The Fa' in His statement 84- Then fight It was said: It is related to His statement And whoever fights in the cause of God etc.: meaning for this reason, then fight. It was also said: It is related to His statement And what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the cause of God? So fight. It was also said: It is the answer to an omitted condition indicated by the context, which is: If the matter is what was mentioned about not obeying the hypocrites, then fight, or if they single you out and leave you, then fight. Al-Zajjaj said: God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to wage jihad even if he fought alone, because He has guaranteed him victory. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is the apparent meaning of the wording, except that it has never been reported that fighting was made obligatory for him but not for the nation. So the meaning, and God knows best, is that it is addressed to him in wording, and in meaning to him and his nation: that is, you, O Muhammad, and every one of your nation, it is said to him, “Fight in the way of God. You are not charged except for yourself.” That is, you are not charged except for yourself, and you are not obligated to do the actions of anyone other than yourself. This is a resumption confirming what came before it, because the obligation to do one’s own actions is one of the reasons for him to directly fight alone. Do not be charged was read with the subjunctive mood indicating prohibition, and it was read with the letter nun. His statement, and incite the believers, that is, he urged them to fight and jihad. It is said, I incited so-and-so to such-and-such, if you commanded him to do it. And inciting so-and-so to do something, devote himself to it, and persevere in it have the same meaning. His saying, Perhaps God will restrain the violence of those who disbelieve, is a hope for the believers that the violence of those who disbelieve will be restrained from them, and hope from God, the Almighty, is obligatory, for it is a promise from Him, and His promise will inevitably come to pass. And God is more severe in violence, meaning more powerful and greater in authority. And more severe in punishment, meaning more severe in punishment. It is said: I punished the man severely, from punishment, which is torment. Munkal is the thing that is inflicted on a person.
4:85: 85- Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it. The origin of intercession, intercession, and the like is from the word shafa' which means a pair, and from it the word shafi' because he becomes with the one in need as an intercessor, and from it a she-camel is shafu': if it brings together two milkings in one milking, and a she-camel is shafi': if it brings together a pregnancy and a child that follows it. And the shafa' is the joining of one to another. And the shafa'ah is the joining of the partner's property to his property, so the intercession is the joining of someone else to your position and your means, so it is in fact a manifestation of the status of the intercessor with the intercessor and the connection of benefit to the one for whom the intercession is made. And the good intercession is in righteousness and obedience. And the bad intercession is in sins, so whoever intercedes for good in order to benefit will have a share of it, meaning of its reward, and whoever intercedes for evil, such as someone who seeks to gossip and backbite, will have a share of it, meaning of its burden. Al-Kafl: the burden and sin, and its derivation is from the cloak that the rider puts on the camel’s hump so that it does not fall. It is said that you have covered the camel: if you have caught a cloak on its hump and ridden on it, because the whole back was not used, but a portion of it was used. It is used for a portion of good and evil. Among its uses for good is the Almighty’s saying: He will give you a double portion of His mercy “And God is over all things Muqitan” meaning: Able, said Al-Kisa’i. Al-Farra’ said: Al-Muqit is the one who gives every person his sustenance. It is said: Qattuhu aqtuhu qutan, and Iqtuhu aqtuhu iqatah, so I am qa’it and Muqit. Al-Kisa’i narrated that Aqat yaqit. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Muqit is the preserver. Al-Nahhas said: Abu Ubaidah said because it is derived from qut, and qut means: the amount that a person preserves. Ibn Faris said in Al-Mujmal: Al-Muqit is the powerful. Al-Muqit: the preserver and the witness. As for the poet’s saying: Is it to me or against me that if I am held accountable, I will be held accountable. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said that it is not of this meaning.
4:86: His saying 86- And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, or return it equally. Greeting is a verb derived from hayyat, and the root is tahiya, like tardiyya and tasmiya, so they assimilated the ya into the ya, and its root is a supplication for life. Greeting is peace, and this is the meaning intended here, and similar to it is the saying of God Almighty: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you, and this is what a group of commentators went with, and it was narrated from Malik that what is meant by greeting here is may God have mercy on you when someone sneezes. The companions of Abu Hanifa said that the tadhiyya here is a gift based on his saying or return it, and it is not possible to return the greeting itself, and this is corrupt and should not be paid attention to. What is meant by his saying, So greet them with something better than it, is that he should add to the answer what the initiator said with the letter ta lower vowel. So if the initiator says, “Peace be upon you,” the respondent says, “And upon you be peace and the mercy of God.” And if the initiator adds a word, the respondent adds to the total of what the initiator said with a word or words, such as: And His blessings, His pleasure, and His greetings. Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars agreed that initiating the greeting is a recommended Sunnah, and returning it is an obligation, based on the statement of God, So greet with something better than it, or return it. They differed as to whether one of the group responds to it, is it sufficient or not? Malik al-Shafi’i was of the opinion that it is sufficient, while the Kufians were of the opinion that it is not sufficient for another, and the hadith of Ali from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is refuted by them, who said: It is sufficient for a group when they pass by if one of them greets with the greeting, and it is sufficient for sitting if one of them responds. Narrated by Abu Dawud, and in its chain of transmission is Saeed bin Khalid al-Khuza’i al-Madani, and there is nothing wrong with him, although some have declared him weak. Ibn Abd al-Barr classified the hadith as hasan. The meaning of his statement, or return it, is to limit oneself to the same wording used by the initiator. So if he says, “Peace be upon you,” the respondent says, “And upon you be peace.” There is a report in the pure Sunnah specifying who initiates the greeting, who deserves the greeting, and who does not deserve it, which makes it unnecessary to elaborate here. His saying, Indeed, God is ever, over all things, a Reckoner. He will hold you accountable for everything. It was said that its meaning is Guardian. It was said that it means Sufficient, from their saying, I think that such and such is sufficient for me. And similar to it is God is sufficient for you.
4:87: His saying 87- God, there is no god but He is a subject and predicate, and the lam in his saying to gather you is the answer to an omitted oath: meaning, by God, God will gather you together at the gathering until the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:meaning, until the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection. It was said: to means in, and it was said: it is redundant. The meaning is: He will gather you on the Day of Resurrection, and the Day of Resurrection is the Day of Resurrection from the graves there is no doubt about it meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, or in the gathering: meaning a gathering there is no doubt about it and who is more truthful than God in statement denying that anyone is more truthful than Him, glory be to Him. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Man Azdaq read it with a zay. The rest read it with a sad, and the sad is the original. It may be changed to a zay because of its closeness to its point of articulation. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Sinan regarding the statement of God, and urge the believers, he said: admonish them. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the statement of God, whoever intercedes with a good intercession, the verse, he said: the intercession of people for one another. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the statement of God, shall have a share thereof, he said: a portion thereof. And the statement of God, a share thereof, he said: the share is the sin. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: the share is the share. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, and God is ever a Guardian over all things, he said: a Preserver. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Rawahah that a man asked him about the statement of God, and God is ever a Guardian over all things, he said: He preserves every person according to his deeds. There is an unknown man in its chain of transmission. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Muqeetan, he said: A witness. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, Muqeetan, he said: A witness, a reckoner, a guardian. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement, Muqeetan, he said: Able. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: The Muqeet is the All-Powerful. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: The Muqeet is the Provider. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If anyone from among God’s creation greets you, then greet him back, even if he is a Jew, a Christian or a Zoroastrian, because God says, And when you are greeted with a greeting, (Al-Bukhari: 100). Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated in al-Zuhd. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Salman al-Farsi, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘And upon you be the mercy of God.’ Then another came and said: ‘Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God, and the mercy of God.’ He said: ‘And upon you be the mercy of God and His blessings.’ Then another came and said: ‘Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.’ He said to him: ‘And upon you.’ The man said to him: ‘O Prophet of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, so-and-so and so-and-so came to you and greeted you and you responded to them more than you responded to me?’ He said: ‘You did not leave anything for us. God said: ‘And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, or return it equally.’ So we returned it to you.” Al-Bukhari narrated in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad on the authority of Abu Hurairah: “A man passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting and said: ‘Peace be upon you.’ He said: ‘Ten good deeds.’ Another man passed by and said: ‘Peace be upon you and God’s mercy.’ He said: ‘Twenty good deeds.’ Another man passed by and said: ‘Peace be upon you and God’s mercy and blessings.’ He said: ‘Thirty good deeds.’” Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu’ab Al-Iman on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Hunayf, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ahmad, Al-Darimi, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi - who classed it as hasan - Al-Nasa’i and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of ‘Imran ibn Husayn, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. He added after each time that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, responded to him, then said: ‘Ten,’ etc. Abu Dawud and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Anas Al-Juhani, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. He added after his words ‘and His blessings,’ and his forgiveness, and said: ‘Forty,’ meaning one good deed.
4:88: The interrogative in his saying 88- What is wrong with you? is for denial, and the interrogative noun is the subject and what follows is its predicate. The meaning is: What is wrong with you in the hypocrites? That is: in their matter and their condition while you are two groups in that. The gist of it is the denial of those being addressed that they have something that necessitates their disagreement regarding the matter of the hypocrites. The grammarians differed regarding the accusative of two groups. Al-Akhfash and the Basrans said that it is in the accusative case, like your saying: What is wrong with you standing? The Kufians said that it is in the accusative case as the predicate of kana, which is implied, and the meaning is: What is wrong with you regarding the hypocrites that you were two groups. The reason for the revelation of the verse is what will come, and the meaning becomes clear from it. And his saying, And God has made them revolt, means: He has returned them to disbelief for what they have earned. Al-Farra’, Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, and Al-Kisa’i narrated that He has made them revolt and has turned them upside down: that is, He has returned them to disbelief and has turned them upside down. Reversing and turning something upside down means turning its beginning upside down, or returning its beginning to its end. The upside down is the turned upside down. In the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud and Abi, And God has made them revolt, and from this is the saying of Abdullah ibn Rawahah: They were thrown into a dark category as black as night, followed by tribulations. The letter ba in His statement, because of what they have earned, is causal: that is, He caused them to fall because of what they earned, which is their arrival in the abode of disbelief. The question in His statement, Do you want to guide one whom God has led astray? is for rebuke and rebuke, and in it is evidence that the one whom God has led astray will not be helped by human guidance: Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills. His statement, And he whom God leaves astray - you will not find for him a way, means: a path to guidance.
4:89: His statement 89- They wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. This is a new statement that includes a statement of the state of these hypocrites and clarification that they wish that the believers would disbelieve as they disbelieved and they wish that out of stubbornness and extremism in disbelief and persistence in misguidance. So the kaf in his statement as is a description of a deleted source: meaning disbelief like their disbelief, or a state as narrated from Sibawayh. His statement so you would be alike is in apposition to his statement you would disbelieve and is included in its ruling: meaning they wish that your disbelief would be like their disbelief, and they wish that you would be equal to them. His saying, So do not take from among them allies is the answer to an omitted condition: that is, if their condition is as mentioned, then do not take from among them allies until they believe and confirm their belief by emigrating. But if they turn away from that, then seize them if you are able to overpower them and kill them wherever you find them in the sacred precincts and outside it. And do not take from among them an ally whom you befriend nor a helper whom you seek help from.
4:90: His statement 90- Except those who join a people between you and whom there is a treaty is an exception to his statement Then seize them and kill them meaning: except those who join and enter into a people between you and whom there is a treaty of neighborhood and alliance, then do not kill them because of the treaty and covenant between them and those between you and whom there is a treaty, for the treaty includes them. This is the most correct of what has been said about the meaning of the verse. It has been said: The connection here is the connection of lineage. The meaning is: except those who are related to a people between you and whom there is a treaty, said Abu Ubaidah, and the people of knowledge have rejected that from him because lineage does not prevent fighting by consensus, as there were lineages between the Muslims and the polytheists, but that did not prevent fighting. There is a difference of opinion about these people who had a covenant with the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). It was said that they were Quraysh, who had a covenant with the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace). And those who pray to Quraysh were Banu Mudlij. It was also said that it was revealed about Hilal ibn Uwaimir, Saraqa ibn Ju’sham, and Khuzaymah ibn Amir ibn Abd Manaf, who had a covenant with the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace). It was also said that it was Banu Bakr ibn Zayd. His statement, Or they came to you with their breasts constrained is an appositive to his statement, they pray and is included in the ruling of exception: that is, except those who pray and those who came to you. It is permissible for it to be an appositive to a description of a al-Nas 114:that is, except those who pray to a people between you and whom there is a covenant. And those who pray to a people who came to you with their breasts constrained: that is, their breasts were constricted from fighting so they refrained from it. Constriction means narrowness and contraction. Al-Farra’ said: “It, i.e., their chests are constricted, is a state of the implied nominative in ‘they came to you’, just as you say: ‘So-and-so came and lost his mind’, i.e., his mind has been lost.” Al-Zajjaj said: “It is a predicate after a predicate, i.e., they came to you, then he informed and said, ‘their chests are constricted’, so on this basis, ‘constricted’ is a substitute for ‘they came to you’, and it was said: ‘Constricted’ is in the accusative case as an adjective for a people, and it was said that the meaning is: or men or people came to you whose chests are constricted’. Al-Hasan read ‘or they came to you whose chests are constricted’ in the accusative case as a state. ‘Hasarat’ and ‘Hasirat’ were also read, and Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Mubarrad said: ‘Constricted their chests’ is a supplication against them, just as you say: ‘May God curse the disbeliever’, and some commentators weakened it, and it was said: ‘or’ means ‘and’. His statement, “that they fight you or fight their people,” is related to his statement, their hearts are constrained, meaning: their hearts are constrained from fighting you and fighting with you for their people, so their hearts are constricted from fighting the two groups and they dislike that. And if God had willed, He would have given them power over you, as a trial and test from Him to you, as the Almighty said, And We will surely test you until We make evident those among you who strive [for the cause] and the steadfast, and We will make evident your report, or as a test for you or a punishment for your sins, but He, the Almighty, did not will that, and the lam in His statement, they would have fought you is the answer to if to repeat the answer: meaning, if God had willed, He would have given them power and they would have fought you, and the fa’ is for the purpose of following up. But if they withdraw from you, and do not expose themselves to fighting you, “and offer you peace,” meaning: they surrender to you and submit, then God has not made for you a way over them, meaning: a path, so it is not permissible for you to kill them, or take them prisoner, or plunder their wealth, so this surrender prevents that and makes it forbidden.
4:91: 91- You will find others who want to be safe from you and their people so they show you Islam and show their people disbelief so that they can be safe from both groups, and they are a people from the people of Tihamah who asked for safety from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they can be safe with him and their people. It was said: It is about a people from the people of Mecca, and it was said: It is about Nu'aym bin Mas'ud, for he used to be safe from the Muslims and the polytheists, and it was said: It is about a people from the hypocrites, and it was said: It is about Asad and Ghatafan. Every time they are returned to the fitnah meaning their people called them to it and asked them to fight the Muslims they are thrown back into it meaning: They turned back into it and returned to their people and fought the Muslims, and the meaning of throwing back is reversal Then if they do not withdraw from you meaning: these are those who want to be safe from you and their people to be safe "and offer you peace" meaning: They surrender to you and enter into your covenant and peace and separate themselves from their people "and refrain Their hands from fighting you so seize them and kill them wherever you overtake them meaning: wherever you find them and are able to overpower them and those described with those attributes We have given you clear authority over them meaning: a clear argument by which you can control them and subjugate them because of what is in their hearts of disease and what is in their chests of deceit, and their falling into temptation with the easiest action and the least effort. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Zaid bin Thabit that “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to Uhud, and some people who had gone out with him returned. The companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were divided into two groups, one group saying, ‘We will kill them’ and the other group saying, ‘No.’ So God revealed, ‘Then why are you divided into two parties concerning the hypocrites? ’” the entire verse. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, It is good and it removes impurity as fire removes impurities from silver. This is the most authentic report about the reason for the revelation of the verse. Other reasons have been reported. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, And God has made them fall. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him, saying, He has turned them back. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Except those who join a people between you and whom there is a treaty. He said, It was revealed about Hilal bin Uwaimir and Suraqa bin Malik al-Mudlaji, and about Banu Khuzaymah bin Amir bin Abd Manaf. Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, An-Nahhas and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on his authority regarding the statement of God, Except those who pray 2:173, that it was abrogated by Bara’ah, So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi, Their chests are constricted, meaning: their chests are constricted. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’, “And they offer you peace,” meaning: peace. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the statement of God, But if they withdraw from you, 2:173, that it was abrogated by Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ikrimah regarding this verse, that it was abrogated by Bara’ah. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, You will find others and the verse, he said: There were people from Mecca who used to come to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and convert to Islam out of hypocrisy, then they would return to their people and indulge in idolatry, seeking thereby to be safe here and there. So he ordered that they be fought if they did not withdraw and make peace. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah that they were people who lived in Tihamah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi that it was revealed about Nu’aym bin Mas’ud.
4:92: His saying 92- And it is not for a believer This negation is in the sense of a prohibition that requires prohibition, like his saying And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God If this negation had its meaning, it would have been a report and it necessitates its truth, for there is no believer who ever killed a believer, and it was said: The meaning is he did not have that in the covenant of God, and it was said: He did not have that in the past just as the believer does not have that in any way, then he made an exception from it with a discontinuous exception and said: Except by mistake, meaning he did not have the right to kill him at all, but if he killed him by mistake then he is liable for such and such, this is the saying of Sibawayh and Al-Zajjaj, and it was said: It is a connected exception, and the meaning is: It was not proven nor found nor permissible for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake since he is defeated at that time, and it was said: The meaning is: Nor by mistake. Al-Nahhas said: This is not known in the speech of the Arabs, and it is not correct in meaning because a mistake is not forbidden, and it was said that the meaning is: He should not kill him for any reason except by mistake alone. So his saying: by mistake is in the accusative case as an object for it. It is also possible that it is an attribute of a deleted source: i.e. except for accidental killing. The forms of mistake are many and are defined as lack of intent. The noun for mistake is derived from to make a mistake if one does not rely on it. His saying: then freeing a believing slave means: then he must free a believing slave, freeing her as an expiation for accidental killing. He used the word slave to refer to the entire self. Scholars differed in the interpretation of the believing slave. It was said: It is the one who prayed and understood faith, so a young girl is not sufficient. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Al-Sha'bi, Al-Nakha'i, Qatadah and others said the same. Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: It is sufficient for a young girl born among Muslims. A group of them, including Malik and Al-Shafi'i, said: It is sufficient for anyone who has been ruled to be obligated to pray over him if he dies. According to the majority of scholars, it is not sufficient for a blind person, a crippled person or a paralyzed person. According to the majority, it is sufficient for a lame or one-eyed person. Malik said: Except if he is severely lame. According to the majority of them, it is not sufficient for an insane person. There are long details mentioned in the science of branches. His statement, and a blood money paid to his family. Blood money is what is given in exchange for the blood of the murdered person to his heirs. The blood money means what is paid and paid. The family means the heirs. The types of blood money and its details have been explained in the pure Sunnah. His statement, unless they give alms means: unless the family of the murdered person gives alms to the killer. Forgiving it is called charity to encourage that. And my father read: unless they give charity. This exception clause is related to his saying, a Muslim ransom, meaning: he must pay a Muslim blood money unless the heirs forgive him. His saying, but if he was from a people who are your enemies, meaning: if the one killed was from a people who are your enemies, and they are the infidels who are at war. This is the issue of a believer who is killed by Muslims in the land of the infidels from whom he was, then he converted to Islam and did not emigrate, and they think that he did not convert to Islam and that he remained on the religion of his people, then there is no blood money on his killer, but he must free a believing slave. They differed about the reason for dropping the blood money. It was said: its reason is that the guardians of the killed person are infidels who have no right to the blood money. It was said: its reason is that the sanctity of this one who believed but did not emigrate is little, because God the Most High said: And those who believed but did not emigrate - you have no right to their guardianship in any way. Some scholars said: his blood money is obligatory for the public treasury. His saying, but if he was from a people between you and whom there is a treaty, meaning: temporary or supportive. Al-Hasan read: “And he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave. But if he is from a people between whom and you there is a treaty, then a ransom to be paid to his family.” That is, his killer must pay blood money to his family from among the Muslims, who are his heirs. And the freeing of a believing slave. As mentioned above, But whoever cannot find that is, the slave, nor does he have enough money to buy one, then a fast of two consecutive months. That is, he must fast two consecutive months, without breaking the fast during the day. If he breaks the fast, he must start over. This is the opinion of the majority. As for breaking the fast for a legitimate excuse, such as menstruation and the like, it does not require starting over. There is disagreement about breaking the fast due to illness. His statement, repentance from God is in the accusative case as an object for it: that is, He prescribed that for every repentance, that is, as an acceptance of your repentance. Or it is in the accusative case as a source: that is, He accepted your repentance with repentance. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a state: that is, the state of his being the one who has repentance from God.
4:93: His saying 93- And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell. When God Almighty explained the ruling on the one who kills by mistake, He explained the ruling on the one who kills intentionally. Scholars have differed on the meaning of premeditated murder. Ata’, Al-Nakha’i and others said: It is killing with an iron object such as a sword, dagger, spearhead, or similar sharp objects, or with something known to cause death, such as heavy stones and the like. The majority said: It is every killing by a murderer who intends to commit the act with an iron object, stone, stick, or other object. Some scholars have restricted it to something that usually kills its like. Some scholars have said that murder is divided into three categories: premeditated murder, semi-premeditated murder, and accidental murder. They have provided evidence for this, but this is not the place to elaborate on it. Others have said that it is divided into two categories: premeditated murder and accidental murder, and there is no third category. They have provided evidence that there are only two categories in the Qur’an. The response to this is that the fact that the Qur’an is limited to the two categories does not negate the existence of a third category in the Sunnah, and this has been proven in the Sunnah. This verse came to increase the punishment of the deliberate murderer, so God combined for him Hell as a punishment for him: that is, he deserves it because of this sin, and between his being eternal in it, and between God’s wrath upon him and His curse upon him and His preparation for him a great punishment. There is no more severity behind this severity, nor is there a threat like this. And the word eternally is in the accusative case as a state. And His statement and God’s wrath upon him is connected to something understood, as indicated by the context: that is, He made his punishment Hell or He judged him or punished him and was angry with him and prepared for him. Scholars differed as to whether a premeditated murderer has repentance or not. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he said: The scholars of Kufa differed on this, so I traveled to Ibn Abbas and asked him about it. He said: This verse was revealed: And whoever kills a believer intentionally and it was the last to be revealed and nothing abrogated it. Al-Nasa’i narrated something similar to this from him. Al-Nasa’i narrated something similar from Zaid bin Thabit. Among those from the Salaf who were of the opinion that there is no repentance for him were Abu Hurairah, Abdullah bin Amr, Abu Salamah, Ubaid bin Umair, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from them. The majority were of the opinion that his repentance is acceptable, and they provided evidence for it with the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds and His words: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants. And His statement, And He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills, they also said: It is possible to combine this verse of An-Nisa with the verse of Al-Furqan, so their meaning would be: His recompense is Hell, except for he who repents, especially since the reason, which is killing, and the cause, which is the threat of punishment, are the same. They also provided evidence for this with the hadith mentioned in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ubadah ibn As-Samit that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with God, nor commit adultery, nor kill the soul which God has forbidden except by right. Then he said: Whoever commits any of that and God conceals it, then it is up to God. If God wills, He will pardon him, and if He wills, He will punish him.” And with the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, which Muslim narrated in his Sahih and others about the one who killed a hundred souls. A group of them, including Abu Hanifah and his companions and Ash-Shafi’i, held that the intentional killer is included under the will, whether he repents or not. I have explained in my commentary on Al-Muntaqa the basis of each group. The truth is that the door of repentance is not closed to every sinner, but rather it is open to everyone who intends it and seeks to enter through it. If polytheism, which is the greatest and most severe of sins, is erased by repentance to God and is accepted from its perpetrator to exit from it and enter the door of repentance, then how about the lesser sins, including intentional murder? However, in the repentance of the intentional murderer, it is necessary to confess to the murder and surrender himself to retaliation if it is obligatory, or to pay the blood money if retaliation is not obligatory and the murderer is wealthy and able to pay it or some of it. As for the mere repentance of the intentional murderer and his determination not to return to killing anyone without confession or surrendering himself, we do not definitively accept it, and God is the Most Merciful of the merciful. He is the One who judges between His servants concerning that over which they differ. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, that he said: He was not allowed to do that because of the covenant that God had given him from his Lord. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, And it is not for a believer, that he said: Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah killed a believing man whom he and Abu Jahl, his brother on his mother’s side, had been torturing for following the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ayyash thought that the man was an unbeliever. And clearer in this context is what Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Al-Harith bin Yazid from Banu Amir bin Luayy was torturing Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah with Abu Jahl, then he went out as an immigrant to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning Al-Harith, and Ayyash met him in Al-Harrah and struck him with the sword, thinking that he was an infidel, then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him, so the verse It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake was revealed, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it to him and then said to him: Get up and set him free.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi a longer version than this. It has been narrated through other chains of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, who said: It was revealed about a man killed by Abu Al-Darda’, who was in a military expedition, so Abu Al-Darda’ went to a valley to help him, and he found a man from the people with sheep, so he attacked him with the sword and he said: There is no god but God, so he struck him. Ibn Mandha and Abu Nu’aym narrated something similar to this, but in it it says that the one who killed the one who sought refuge in the word of testimony was Bakr bin Haritha Al-Juhani. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Then the freeing of a believing slave, he said: By believing woman he means one who has understood faith and prayed. And every slave in the Qur’an that is not called a believer, then it is permissible for a newborn or older who is not in a state of illness. And regarding his statement, And a blood money to be paid to his family unless they give it as charity, he said: The blood money must be paid unless he gives it in charity on his behalf. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd Bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: In the version of Abu, the freeing of a believing slave does not suffice for a boy. Abd Bin Hamid, Abu Dawud and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a black slave girl and said: O Messenger of God, I owe the freeing of a believing slave. He said to her: Where is God? She pointed to the sky with her finger, so he said to her: Who am I? She pointed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the sky, meaning you are the Messenger of God. He said: Free her, for she is a believer. It has been narrated through various chains of transmission and it is in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Muawiyah Bin Al-Hakam Al-Sulami. There are hadiths about estimating blood money, and about the difference between accidental and semi-intentional blood money, the blood money of a Muslim and the blood money of a non-Muslim. These are well-known and we have no need to mention them here. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i regarding his statement, The blood money is to be paid to his family, he said: This Muslim whose inheritance is Muslims. But if he is from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, he said: This Muslim man and his people are polytheists and there is no covenant between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. But if he is from a people between you and whom there is a treaty, he said: This Muslim man and his people are polytheists and there is a covenant between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he is killed and his inheritance goes to the Muslims and his blood money goes to his people because they pay blood money for him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, But if he is from a people at war with you and he is a believer, he said: If he was among the people of war and he is a believer and he killed him by mistake, then his killer must atone by freeing a believing slave, or fasting for two consecutive months, and there is no blood money on him. And regarding his statement, But if he is from a people between you and whom there is a treaty, he said: If he is a disbeliever under your protection and he is killed, then his killer must pay the blood money to be paid to his family and free a slave. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib on the authority of Abu Ayyash who said: A man would come and convert to Islam, then he would come to his people who were polytheists and stay among them, and the armies of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would attack them, and the man would be killed among those killed, so God revealed this verse, But if he is from a people at war with you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave, and there is no blood money on him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib on the authority of Abu Yahya on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement, Repentance from God, meaning: God has forgiven this nation, as He has made expiation for accidental killing. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah: A man from the Ansar killed the brother of Muqays bin Subaba. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave him the blood money, which he accepted, then he attacked his brother’s killer, and the verse was revealed about him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair something similar, and it says that Muqays bin Subaba went to Mecca after that and apostatized from Islam. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse, And whoever kills a believer intentionally, was revealed eight years after the verse in Surat Al-Furqan, which is His statement, And those who do not invoke with God another deity, until His statement, Forgiving, Most Merciful. Abd al-Razzaq, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit that his statement, And whoever kills a believer intentionally, was revealed six months after his statement, And those who do not invoke with God another deity, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: This verse in Surat al-Nisa’ was revealed four months after his statement, And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills, and the narrations from the Companions on this matter are very numerous, and the truth is what we know of you.
4:94: This is connected to the mention of jihad and fighting, and striking: walking on the earth. The Arabs say ḍarabat fi al-ardh: if you traveled for trade or conquest or other, and they say ḍarabat al-ardh without fi: if you intended to relieve oneself, and from this is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Two men should not go out striking the stool. His saying fat-tabīnū comes from tabīn, which means contemplation, and this is the reading of the group except for Hamzah, who read fat-tabṭabṭabī from at-taṭabṭabīn. Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim chose the first reading, and they said: because whoever commanded ascertainment has commanded verification, and the travel was specifically commanded ascertainment, although verification and verification in the matter of killing are obligatory in the presence and travel without disagreement, because the incident that is the reason for the revelation of the verse was during travel, as will come. His saying "And do not say to one who offers you peace" and it was read as-salām. Their meaning is the same. Abu Ubaidah chose as-salām. The people of insight disagreed with him and said that as-salām here is more similar because it means submission and surrender. What is meant here is: Do not say to one who throws his hand towards you and surrenders, You are not a believer. Peace and peace both mean surrender. It was said that they mean Islam, meaning: Do not say to one who throws Islam towards you, meaning his word, which is the testimony, You are not a believer. It was said that they mean submission, which is the greeting of the people of Islam, meaning: Do not say to one who throws his hand towards you and says, “Peace be upon you,” You are not a believer. What is meant is to forbid Muslims from neglecting what the infidel has brought that can be used as evidence of his Islam, and saying that he only brought it as a means of protection and caution. Abu Ja`far read, I am not a believer, from I am safe, meaning if you grant him protection, then he is a believer. This verse was used as evidence that whoever kills a disbeliever after he says There is no god but God will be killed because of it, because his blood, property and family are protected by this word. The killing was dropped for whoever did that during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) because they interpreted it and thought that whoever says it out of fear of weapons is not a Muslim and his blood is not protected by it, and that he must say this word while he is reassured and not afraid. The ruling on uttering the word of Islam is showing submission by saying: I am a Muslim or I am on your religion, because you know that the meaning of the verse is surrender and obedience, and it is achieved by everything that indicates Islam from word or action, including the word of testimony and the word of submission. The other two opinions on the meaning of the verse are included under the first opinion. His statement, Seeking the goods of this worldly life: the sentence is in the accusative case as a state: that is, do not say that statement seeking booty, on the condition that the prohibition refers to the restriction and the restricted, not just the restriction. The enjoyment of this world is called a provision because it is a temporary, non-permanent provision. Abu Ubaidah said: It is said: All worldly goods are ‘arād’ with the opening of the ‘ra’. As for ‘arād’ with the sukūn of the ‘ra’, it is everything other than dinars and dirhams. So every ‘arād’ with the sukūn is ‘arād with the fathah, but not every ‘arād with the fathah is ‘arād with the sukūn. In the book ‘Al-‘Ayn’: ‘arād’ is what is obtained from the world, and from it is the saying of the Most High: You desire the goods of the world and its plural is ‘arūd. In Al-Mujmal by Ibn Faris: ‘Arād’ is what befalls a person from illness and the like, and the ‘arād’ of the world is what is in it of money, little or much, and the ‘arād’ of furniture is what is not cash. His saying, So with God are many spoils is an explanation of the prohibition: that is, with God, from what is lawful for you without committing a forbidden act, there are many spoils that you seize and with which you do not need to kill someone who has surrendered and obeyed, and seize his money. Thus were you before that is, you were disbelievers, so your blood was spared when you spoke the word of testimony, or that is how you were before, hiding your faith from your people out of fear for yourselves until God bestowed upon you the honor of His religion, so you showed faith and declared it, and the command to clarify was repeated to confirm it for them because it is an obligation in which there is no latitude or dispensation. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Some Muslims caught up with a man who had some spoils of war and he said, “Peace be upon you.” They killed him and took the spoils, so the following verse was revealed: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from Banu Sulaym passed by some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was herding his sheep, so he greeted them. They said: He only greeted us to seek refuge from us. So they attacked him, killed him, and brought his sheep to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Nu`aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Abi Hudud Al-Aslami who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent us to Idam. I went out with a group of Muslims among whom were Abu Qatada Al-Harith Ibn Rib`i and Muhallim Ibn Jaththama Ibn Qais Al-Laithi. We went out until we reached the valley of Idam. Amir Ibn Al-Adbat Al-Ashja`i passed by us on his camel with provisions and a bowl of milk. When he passed by us, he greeted us with the greeting of Islam, but we held back from him. Muhallim Ibn Jaththama attacked him because of something that had happened between them, so he killed him and took his camel and provisions. When we came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him the report, the Qur’an was revealed about us: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate (Al-Baqarah 2:17). And in a version with Ibn Ishaq, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim from the hadith of Abu Hadrad, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Muhallim: Did you kill him after he said, I believe in God? Then the Quran was revealed. Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar that a dreamer sat in front of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to ask forgiveness for him, so he said: May God not forgive you. So he stood up and covered his tears with his cloak. Not even an hour had passed before he died and they buried him and the earth threw him out. Then they came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him, so he said: The earth accepts those who are worse than your companion, but God wanted to admonish you. Then they threw him on a mountain and threw stones at him, so the verse was revealed: O you who believe! When you strike… Al-Bazzar, Al-Daraqutni in Al-Ifrad, Al-Tabarani and Al-Dhiya in Al-Mukhtara narrated from Ibn Abbas that the reason for the revelation of the verse was that Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad killed a man after he said: There is no god but God. There are many narrations about the reason for the revelation, and what we have mentioned is the best of them. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr regarding his statement, Thus were you before, he said: You concealed your faith just as this shepherd concealed his faith, meaning those who killed him after he greeted them. And in another version, you concealed your faith from the polytheists. Then God bestowed His favor upon you, so He revealed Islam and you declared your faith. Then verify it, he said: A second warning from God. And Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, Thus were you before, he said: You were disbelievers until God bestowed His peace upon you and guided you to it.
4:95: The difference between the degrees of those who sit back from jihad without an excuse, and the degrees of those who struggle in the way of God with their wealth and themselves, even if it is known, but God the Almighty wanted with this information to motivate the mujahideen so that they would desire and to rebuke the sitters so that they would be disgusted. His statement 95- except those who are disabled The people of Kufa and Abu Amr read it in the nominative case as a description of the sitters, as Al-Akhfash said, because they do not mean by them specific people, so they became like indefinite nouns, so it was permissible to describe them with other. Abu Haywah read it with a kasra on the ra' as a description of the believers. The people of the two sanctuaries read it with a fatha on the ra' as an exception from the sitters or from the believers: that is, except those who are disabled, for they are equal to the mujahideen. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a state of the sitters: that is, the healthy sitters are not equal in their state of health, and the state of them is permissible, because their wording is the word of the definite noun. Scholars said: Those who are harmed are those who have excuses because they have harmed them to the point of preventing them from jihad. The apparent meaning of the Qur’anic system is that the one with an excuse is given the same reward as the one who fights. It was also said that he is given his reward without doubling it, so the one who fights is given a doubling because of his involvement. Al-Qurtubi said: The first is more correct, God willing, due to the authentic hadith on this subject: “Indeed, in Madinah there are men who, if you cross a valley or travel a journey, they will be with you. They are people who are held back by an excuse.” He said: In this sense is what was mentioned in the hadith: “If a servant falls ill, God Almighty says: Write down for My servant what he used to do when he was healthy until he recovers or I take him to Me.” His statement: God has favored those who fight with their wealth and their lives by a degree over those who sit back by a degree. This is a clarification of the difference between the two groups, which is understood from the mention of the lack of equality in general. What is meant here is those who are not harmed, applying the absolute to the restricted. He said here a degree, and later he said degrees. Some people said: The preference by degree and then by degrees is only an exaggeration, clarification, and emphasis. Others said: God preferred the mujahideen over those who sit at home from those who are harmed by one degree, and God preferred the mujahideen over those who sit at home from those who are not harmed by degrees. This was said by Ibn Jurayj, As-Suddi and others. It was said that the meaning of degree is higher: that is, He raised their mention and elevated them with praise and commendation. Degree is in the accusative case as a distinguishing or verbal noun because it occurs in the position of the time of comparison: that is, God preferred His preference or by removing the preposition or as a state of the mujahideen, meaning: those of degree. His statement and each is the first object of his statement God promised it was presented before it to indicate restriction: that is, each one of the mujahideen and the sitters God promised him the best: that is, the reward, which is Paradise. His statement a reward is in the accusative case as a distinguishing, and it was said: as a verbal noun because fadl means a reward, the estimate is He rewarded them a reward, and it was said: a second object of fadl because it includes the meaning of giving, and it was said: it is in the accusative case by removing the preposition, and it was said as a state of degrees presented before it.
4:96: 96- “Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” As for the accusative of degrees, forgiveness, and mercy: they are in apposition to reward. It was said that forgiveness and mercy are the subject of implied verbs: that is, He forgave them with forgiveness and had mercy on them with mercy. Al-Bukhari, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i and others narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) dictated to him: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who strive in the cause of God. Ibn Umm Maktum came while he was dictating it to me and said: O Messenger of God, if I could strive I would strive. And he was blind. So God revealed to His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while his thigh was on my thigh: except those who are disabled. This meaning was narrated by Abd bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim from the hadith of Al-Bara’. It was also narrated by Saeed bin Mansour, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani and Al-Hakim who authenticated it from the hadith of Kharijah bin Zaid bin Thabit from his father. Al-Tirmidhi and he authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who are disabled from Badr and those who went out to Badr. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated it from him. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority that he said: It was revealed about a people who were preoccupied with illnesses and pains, so God sent down an excuse for them from the sky. Saeed bin Mansour and Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik that he said: This verse was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, and I saw him in one of the battles of the Muslims with the banner. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, God has favored those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home by a degree, he said: Over those who are harmed. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, And to each of them God has promised good, he said: Paradise. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that he said: It was said that Islam is a degree, and emigration is a degree in Islam, and jihad in emigration is a degree, and killing in jihad is a degree. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Muhairiz regarding his statement, Degrees, he said: The degrees are seventy degrees, and between each degree is the enemy of a well-trained horse, which is seventy years. Abdul Razzaq narrated something similar in Al-Musannaf on the authority of Abu Majlaz. Al-Bukhari and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred levels that God has prepared for those who strive in the way of God. Between each two levels is like the distance between the heavens and the earth. So if you ask God for something, ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it flow the rivers of Paradise.”
4:97: His statement 97- He takes them may be a past tense verb from which the feminine marker was deleted, because the feminine of angels is not real, and it may be future tense, and the original is He takes them, so one of the two tas was deleted. Ibn Furak narrated from Al-Hasan that the meaning is He gathers them to the Fire - and it was said: He takes their souls, which is more apparent. What is meant by the angels are the angels of death, as God Almighty said: "Say: The Angel of Death who is set over you will take you." And His statement wronging themselves is a state: meaning in a state of wronging themselves, and the angels' statement in what were you is a question of rebuke: meaning in what were you in the affairs of your religion? And it was said: The meaning is: Were you among the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or were you polytheists? And it was said: The meaning of the question is to rebuke them because they were not in anything of the religion. And their saying, We were oppressed in the land, means Mecca, because the reason for the revelation was that they converted to Islam there and did not emigrate, as will come. Then the angels stopped them in their religion and made the argument binding upon them and cut off their excuse, so they said, Was not the earth of God spacious enough for you to emigrate therein? It was said that what is meant by this land is Medina, and the first is generality based on the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason, as is the truth. So what is meant by the land is every spot on earth that is suitable for emigration to, and what is meant by the first land is every land from which emigration is necessary. His saying, Their refuge is Hell, this sentence is the predicate of those, and the sentence is the predicate of inna in His saying, Indeed, those whom the angels take in death, and the introduction of the fa to include the name of inna with the meaning of the condition, and evil meaning Hell, is a destination, meaning a place to which they will end up.
4:98: His statement 98- Except the weak is an exception from the pronoun in their shelter, and it was said: a discontinuous exception because the weak are not included in the relative pronoun and its pronoun. And his statement of men, women and children is related to something omitted, i.e.: being from them, and what is meant by the weak from men is the temporal and the like, and the children like Ayyash bin Abi Rabi'ah and Salamah bin Hisham, and the children were mentioned even though they were not obligated to do so in order to exaggerate the matter of migration, and to suggest that it is obligatory if the one who is not obligated can do it, so how about the one who is obligated? And it was said: he meant by the children adolescents and slaves. His statement they are unable to find a way is a description of the weak or the men, women and children, or a state of the pronoun in the weak, and it was said: the way is a general term for the types of means of escape: i.e.: they do not find a way or a path to that, and it was said the way is the way of the city.
16:110: 99- So those refers to the weak ones described as mentioned. Perhaps God will pardon them. The word desire was used to emphasize the matter of migration, so that it is thought that abandoning it by someone who is not obligated to it is a sin for which pardon must be sought. 110- Then your Lord is for those who emigrated from the abode of disbelief to the abode of Islam, and the predicate of indeed is omitted, and the meaning is forgiving, merciful, and it was only omitted because the predicate of indeed your Lord that came later indicates it, and it was said that the predicate is for those who emigrated: that is, your Lord is for them with guardianship and support, not against them, and there is a distance in it, and it was said that its predicate is His saying forgiving, merciful, and the second indeed your Lord is an emphasis on the first. He said in Al-Kashaf: Then here to indicate the distance between the state of these people, meaning those about whom the verse was revealed, and the state of those, and they are Ammar and his companions, and what is reported that it was revealed about Abdullah bin Abi Sarh indicates that, and the explanation of that will come after they were tried meaning the infidels tried them by torturing them so that they would return to disbelief, and they were tried was read in the active form: meaning those who tried the believers and tortured them for Islam then strove in the way of God and were patient with what befell them from the infidels, and with what they encountered of the hardships of the obligation is Forgiving and Merciful meaning He is Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful to them, and the meaning of the verse according to the reading of those who read they were tried in the active form is clear and apparent: meaning that your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful to these infidels who tempted those who had become Muslim and tortured them then they strove and were patient. As for the passive form reading, which is the reading of the majority, the meaning is that these tempted ones who spoke the word of disbelief under duress and their hearts were not They are open to disbelief if their deeds are good and they strive in the cause of God and are patient in the face of hardships, for He is Forgiving and Merciful to them. However, if the reason for this verse is Abdullah bin Abi Sarh, who apostatized from Islam and then returned to Islam, then the meaning is: This person who is tempted in his religion by apostasy, if he converts to Islam, strives and is patient, then God is Forgiving and Merciful to him. The pronoun in its verse refers to the temptation or to the emigration, jihad and patience, or to all of them.
4:100: His saying 100- And whoever emigrates for the cause of God will find on the earth many [alternative] locations and abundance. This sentence includes encouragement and motivation to emigrate. His saying for the cause of God is evidence that emigration must be with a correct intention and a pure purpose, not tainted by any worldly matters. From this is the authentic hadith: "So whoever emigrates for the sake of God and His Messenger, his emigration is for the sake of God and His Messenger. And whoever emigrates for a worldly gain or a woman to marry, his emigration is for that for which he emigrated." There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of the words of God, the Most High, He will find on earth places to turn away from. Ibn Abbas and a group of the Tabi’un and those who came after them said: Maraghim means the one who moves and departs. Mujahid said: Maraghim is the one who moves away. Ibn Zayd said: Maraghim is the one who emigrates, and Abu Ubaidah said the same. An-Nahhas said: These sayings agree in meaning. Maraghim means the place where one turns away from God, and it is derived from ragham, which means dirt. Gham anfu so-and-so means he stuck to the dirt. Raaghmat so-and-so means I migrated from him and was hostile to him, and I did not care that his nose was in vain. It was said that he was called a muhajir and maraghim because when a man converted to Islam, he would be hostile to his people and abandon them, so his departure was called maraghim, and his journey to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was called migration. The gist of the verse is that the muhajir finds on earth a place to live in despite the noses of his people whom he migrated from, meaning despite their humiliation and disgrace. His saying, and spaciousness means: in the country, and it was said: in the provision, and there is nothing preventing spaciousness from being interpreted as something more general than that. His saying, And whoever emigrates from his home for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has become incumbent upon God It was read: overtakes him in the subjunctive mood as if it is conjoined with the conditional verb, and in the nominative as if it is the predicate of a deleted subject, and in the accusative as if it is implied that. The meaning is: whoever death overtakes him before he reaches his goal, which is the place to which he intended to emigrate or the matter for which he intended to emigrate, his reward has become incumbent upon God meaning: it is established with him in a way that does not change, and God is Forgiving meaning: He is very forgiving, and Merciful meaning: He is very merciful. This verse has been used as evidence that emigration is obligatory upon everyone who is in a land of polytheism or in a land where he openly commits sins against God if he is able to emigrate and is not among the weak, because of the generality in this noble verse, even if the reason is specific as mentioned above. Its apparent meaning is that there is no difference between one place and another, one time and another. There are hadiths about migration, and there is evidence that there is no migration after the conquest. We have explained what is true in our commentary on Al-Muntaqa, so please refer to it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were people from Mecca who had converted to Islam and were hiding their Islam. The polytheists took them out with them on the day of Badr, and some of them were wounded and others were killed. The Muslims said: These people of ours were Muslims and were forced, so ask forgiveness for them. Then this verse was revealed about them: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves. He said: Then those Muslims who remained in Mecca wrote to me with this verse, and that they had no excuse. So they went out, and the polytheists caught up with them and subjected them to temptation. Then this verse was revealed about them: And among the people is he who says, ‘We believe in God,’ but when he is harmed for the cause of God, to the end of the verse. The Muslims wrote to them about this and they were saddened and despaired of all good. Then this verse was revealed about them: “Then indeed, your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient. Indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful.” So they wrote to them about this and said: God has made a way out for you, so go out. So they went out, and the polytheists caught up with them. So they fought them until those who escaped escaped and those who were killed were killed. Al-Bukhari and others narrated it from him, but limited it to the beginning.
