Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah regarding his statement, Indeed, those whom the angels take in death to his statement, and evil is the destination, he said: It was revealed about Qays bin Al-Fakih bin Al-Mughira, Al-Harith bin Rabi’ah bin Al-Aswad, Qays bin Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, Abu Al-‘As bin Munabbih bin Al-Hajjaj and Ali bin Umayyah bin Khalaf. He said: When the polytheists from Quraysh and their followers went out to prevent Abu Sufyan bin Harb and the Quraysh caravan from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and his companions from seeking what they had taken from them on the Day of Nakhl, they went out with them with unwilling young men who had converted to Islam and had gathered at Badr without an appointment. They killed infidels at Badr and turned away from Islam, and they are those whom we have named. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Ibn Ishaq. Something similar to this has been narrated from various chains of narration. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited this verse: Except for the weak among men, women and children, and said: My mother and I were among the weak, I was among the children and my mother was among the women. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: They are not able to devise a plan, he said: Strength. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: They are not able to devise a plan, he said: Going to Madinah, “Nor are they shown a way,” he said: A path to Madinah. Abd Bin Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Much and abundantly and abundantly, he said: The one who is weak is the one who moves from one land to another. And abundance is provision. Abd Bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: Murdering, he said: Moving away from what he dislikes. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding his statement: Ample, he said: And ease. He also narrated on the authority of Malik, who said: The vastness of the country. Abu Ya`la, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Tabarani narrated - al-Suyuti said: With a chain of transmission whose men are trustworthy - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Damrah ibn Jundub left his home as an emigrant and said to his al-Nas 114:Carry me and take me out of the land of polytheism to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He died on the way before he reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then the revelation was revealed: And whoever emigrates from his home for the sake of God 1:17. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from him from another chain of transmission. Ibn Sa'd, Ahmad and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Abdullah bin Atik who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "Whoever leaves his home to fight in the cause of God - and where are those who fight in the cause of God? - and falls from his mount and dies, his reward is with God. Or he is bitten by a mount and dies, his reward is with God. Or he dies a natural death, his reward is with God: meaning, he dies a natural death in his bed. By God, this is a statement that I did not hear from any of the Arabs before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And whoever kills a hyena, he deserves Paradise." Abu Ya'la and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu'ab Al-Iman on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever goes out for Hajj and dies, the reward of the pilgrim will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. And whoever goes out for Umrah and dies, the reward of the pilgrim will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. And whoever goes out for Ghazi in the cause of God and dies, the reward of the Ghazi will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection." Ibn Kathir said: This is a strange hadith from this chain of transmission.
4:101: His saying 101- And if you travel The explanation of traveling on the ground was presented shortly. His saying there is no blame upon you is evidence that shortening is not obligatory, and this is the view of the majority. The minority held that it is obligatory, including Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, the Kufians, Judge Ismail, and Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and it was narrated from Malik. They provided evidence for this with the hadith of Aisha, which is proven in Sahih: Prayer was made obligatory as two rak'ahs by two rak'ahs, so it was increased in the city and left in the traveler. The fact that it contradicts what she narrated does not detract from that, so the second narration from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is acted upon. Similar to it is the hadith of Ya'la ibn Umayyah, who said: I asked Umar ibn al-Khattab, saying: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that the disbelievers will tempt you, and the people are safe. Umar said to me: I was amazed by what you were amazed by, so I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and he said: It is charity that God has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity. Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim, and the Sunan scholars. The apparent meaning of his statement: Accept his charity is that shortening is obligatory. His statement: If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you The apparent meaning of this condition is that shortening is not permissible during travel except when there is fear of temptation from the disbelievers, not when there is security. However, it has been established in the Sunnah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, shortened his prayers when there is security, as you know. Shortening with fear is established in the Book, and shortening with security is established in the Sunnah. The meaning of the condition does not stand in opposition to what has been transmitted from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, about shortening with security. It has been said that this condition was stated as the norm, because it was common for Muslims at that time to shorten their prayers due to fear when traveling. This is why Ya`la ibn Umayyah said to `Umar what he said, as mentioned above. In Abu’s reading: Shorten your prayers if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, by omitting if you fear. The meaning according to this reading is: disliking that those who disbelieve may tempt you. A group of scholars have said that this verse only permits shortening prayers when traveling for one who fears the enemy, so whoever is safe should not shorten them. Others said that his saying, If you fear, is not connected to what preceded it and that the speech ended when he said, of prayer, then he began by saying, If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you, then establish for them, O Muhammad, the prayer of fear. His saying, Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy, is an objection. Al-Jurjani, Al-Mahdawi, and others mentioned the meaning of this. Al-Qushayri and Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi rejected it. Al-Qurtubi narrated from Ibn Abbas the meaning of what Al-Jurjani and those with him mentioned. What refutes and repels this is the waw in his saying, And when you are among them. Some commentators took it upon themselves to say that the waw is redundant and that the answer to the mentioned condition, I mean his saying, If you fear, is his saying, So let a group stand up. Some people said that the mention of fear was abrogated by the Sunnah, which is the hadith of Umar that we mentioned earlier, and what was reported in its meaning. His statement, that those who disbelieve may tempt you. Al-Farra’ said: The people of Hijaz say fatanat al-rajul, and Rabi’ah, Qays, Asad, and all the people of Najd say aftanat al-rajul. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh differentiated between them and said, fatanatuhu means I put a temptation in him like his kohl, and aftanatuhu means I made him a tempter. Al-Asma’i claimed that he did not know aftanatuhu. What is meant by fitnah is fighting and exposing oneself to something one dislikes. His statement, enemy, means enemies.
4:102: His saying 102- And if you are among them and lead them in prayer This is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those who come after him from the people of authority, its ruling is as is well known in the fundamentals, and similar to it is the saying of God the Almighty: Take from their wealth a charity and similar to it, and the majority of scholars have adopted this view, but Abu Yusuf and Ismail bin Aliyah deviated and said: The prayer of fear is not performed after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because this address is specific to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: No one else is included in it because of the great merit that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, had. This is refuted, as God has commanded us to follow His Messenger and take him as an example, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Pray as you have seen me pray. The Companions, may God be pleased with them, are more knowledgeable about the meanings of the Qur'an, and they prayed it after his death more than once, as is well known. The meaning of I lead them in prayer is to intend the establishment, like His saying: When you rise to pray, wash your faces. His saying, So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge with God. His saying, Let a group of them stand with you means: after you divide them into two groups, one group standing facing the enemy, and one group standing with you in prayer. And let them take their weapons meaning: the group that prays with him. It was said that the pronoun refers to the group facing the enemy, and the first is more apparent, because the group standing facing the enemy must be standing with their weapons. Only the one who is praying needs to be commanded to do that, because he thinks that that is forbidden from him during prayer, so God commanded him to be holding his weapon: that is, not putting it down. What is meant is not taking it with the hand, but what is meant is that they should be carrying their weapons so that they can reach it from close by if they need it, and so that this will cut off the hope of their enemy from the possibility of his opportunity in them. Ibn Abbas said that the pronoun in his statement, and let them take their weapons refers to the group standing in front of the enemy. He said: Because the praying woman does not fight. Another said: The pronoun refers to the praying woman. Al-Zujaj and Al-Nahhas permitted that this be an order to both groups because it is more terrifying to the enemy. The people of the apparent meaning have made taking weapons obligatory in this prayer, interpreting the order as obligatory. Abu Hanifa held that the praying people do not carry weapons and that this invalidates the prayer. This is refuted by what is in this verse and by what is in the authentic hadiths. His statement, So when they prostrate means: those standing in prayer. Then let them be means: the group standing in front of the enemy. From behind you means behind the praying people. It is possible that the meaning is: So when the worshippers prostrate with him: i.e. they complete the rak’ah, expressing prostration for the entire rak’ah or the entire prayer. Then let them be behind you i.e. let them turn after finishing to face the enemy for guard. And let another group come which is: the one standing opposite the enemy that did not pray. Let them pray with you in the manner that the first group was. And let them take i.e. this other group their precautions and their weapons an additional recommendation to the other group to take precautions along with taking weapons. It was said: Its reason is that this time is likely to be that the disbelievers will notice that the group standing with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is busy. As for the first time, they may think that they are standing for war. It was also said: Because the enemy does not delay his intention beyond this time, because it is the end of the prayer, and the weapon is what a person uses to defend himself in war. The noble verse did not clarify how much each group of the two groups prays? The fear prayer has been mentioned in the pure Sunnah in different ways and with multiple descriptions, all of which are correct and sufficient. Whoever performs one of them has done what he was commanded to do. Whoever among the scholars chose one description over another has strayed from the truth. We have explained this in our explanation of Al-Muntaqa and in all our other works. His statement, Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage so that they could attack you with a single attack. This sentence includes the reason for which God commanded them to be cautious and take the right path: that is, they wished that you would neglect taking up arms and being cautious so that they could reach their goal and seize their opportunity, so that they could attack you with a single attack. Baggage is what is enjoyed in war, including provisions and a mount. His statement, And there is no blame upon you if you are harmed by rain or you are ill for you to lay down your weapons. God, the Almighty, permitted them to lay down their weapons if they are harmed by rain or if they are ill, because it is difficult to carry weapons with these two matters. Then He commanded them to be cautious so that the enemy would not come to them by surprise while they are unaware. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Abu Hanzalah who said: I asked Ibn Umar about the prayer of travel, and he said: Two rak'ahs. I said: Where is the saying of God the Almighty: If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you while you are safe? He said: The Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umayyah ibn Abdullah ibn Khalid ibn Asid that he asked Ibn Umar: What do you think about shortening the prayer while traveling? We do not find it in the Book of God, rather we find mention of the prayer of fear. Ibn Umar said: O son of my brother, God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we do not know anything, so we only do what we saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do, and shortening the prayer while traveling is a Sunnah established by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Haritha ibn Wahb al-Khuza'i who said: “I prayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the noon and afternoon prayers in Mina, the most of the people and the safest, two rak'ahs.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it and Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “We prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, between Mecca and Medina, and we were safe and not afraid of anything.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ali, who said: “A group of merchants asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we travel the earth, so how do we pray? So he revealed: God said: “And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer.” Then the revelation was cut off. Then, a year later, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on an expedition and prayed the noon prayer. The polytheists said: Muhammad and his companions have given you power over their backs. Why did you not attack them more severely? One of them said: They have another like it in its wake. So God revealed between the two prayers: “If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you - indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy. And when you are among them” until His saying: Indeed, God has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. So the prayer of fear was revealed. Abd al-Razzaq, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Daraqutni, and al-Hakim narrated - and he authenticated it - on the authority of Abu Ayyas al-Zarqi who said: “We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Usfan when the polytheists, led by Khalid ibn al-Walid, confronted us and they were between us and the qiblah. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in prayer. They said: They were in a state that if we had caught them by surprise, then they said: Now a prayer will come upon them that is dearer to them than their children and themselves. So Gabriel revealed these verses: “And when you are among them and lead them in prayer” then he mentioned the description of the prayer that they performed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.” There are many hadiths describing the prayer of fear. It is fully explained in its proper context, so we will not prolong its mention here. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, If you are harmed by rain or are ill, he said: It was revealed about Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf who was wounded.
4:103: 103- Qadatum means you have finished the prayer of fear, and it is one of the meanings of Qada, and similar to it is So when you have completed your rituals "So when the prayer is completed, then disperse in the land". His statement "Then remember God standing, sitting, and lying on your sides" means: in all circumstances, even in the case of fighting. The majority of scholars have stated that this commanded remembrance is only an effect of the prayer of fear: that is, if you have finished the prayer, then remember God in these circumstances. It was said that the meaning of his statement "So when you have completed the prayer is if you have prayed, then pray standing, sitting, or lying on your sides according to what the situation requires when engaged in intense fighting, so it is like his statement Then if you fear, then on foot or riding". His statement, So when you are reassured, meaning: you feel secure and your hearts are at peace. Reassurance is the peace of the soul from fear. Establish prayer, meaning: perform the prayer whose time has come in the prescribed manner of remembrances and pillars. Do not do what is possible, because that is only in a state of fear. It was said: The meaning of the verse is that they make up what they prayed in a state of combat, because it is a state of anxiety, distress and negligence in remembrances and pillars. This was narrated from Al-Shafi’i, and the first is more correct. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times, meaning: limited and specific. It is said: its time is specified, and its time is specified. The meaning is: God has enjoined upon His servants the prayers and prescribed them for them at their specified times. It is not permissible for anyone to perform them at any other time except for a legitimate excuse such as sleep, forgetfulness, or the like.
4:104: His statement 104- And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy meaning: do not weaken in seeking them and show strength and endurance. His statement If you are suffering, then they are suffering as you are suffering is an explanation for the prohibition mentioned before it: meaning that what you find of pain from wounds and engaging in fighting is not specific to you, but rather it is something shared between you and them, so they are not more deserving than you of patience in the heat of fighting and the bitterness of war. Despite that, you have an advantage over them that they do not have, which is that you hope from God a reward and a great recompense that they do not hope for due to their disbelief and denial. So you are more deserving of patience than them and more deserving of not being weak than them, for your souls are strong because they see death as gain, while they see it as loss. Similar to this verse is the statement of God the Most High: If a wound should touch you, then a wound like it has touched the people It was said: hope here means fear, because whoever hopes for something is not certain that it will happen, so he is not free from fear of what he hopes for. Al-Farra and Al-Zajjaj said: “Raja is not used to mean fear except with negation, as in the Almighty’s saying: ‘What is the matter with you that you do not hope for God with dignity?’” meaning that you do not fear His greatness. Abd al-Rahman al-A’raj read in takunu with a fatha on the hamza, meaning: because you were. Mansour ibn al-Mu’tamir read tailamun with a kasra on the ta’, and the Basrans do not allow a kasra on the ta’ because of its heaviness. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, So remember God standing, sitting, and [lying] on your sides, that he said: At night and during the day, on land and at sea, while traveling and at home, in wealth and poverty, sickness and health, in secret and in public, and in every situation. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he heard that some people remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides, so he said: This is only if a man is unable to pray standing, so he prays while sitting. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: Then when you are secure, that is, when you leave the place of travel for the place of residence, establish prayer, that is, complete it. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Jurayj as well. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times, that is, imposed. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: The specified time is the obligatory. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And do not weaken, he said: Do not become weak. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement, You suffer, he said: You are in pain, and you hope from God that which they do not hope for, he said: You hope for good.
4:105: His statement 105- By what God has shown you either by revelation or by what is in accordance with the laws of what God has revealed. What is meant here is not what the eye sees because the ruling cannot be seen, but what is meant is what God has made known to him and guided him to. His statement And do not be an advocate for the traitors means: for the sake of the traitors: that is, arguing on their behalf and disputing with those who are in the right because of them. And in it is evidence that it is not permissible for anyone to argue on behalf of someone except after he knows that he is in the right.
4:106: His saying 106- And ask forgiveness of God is an order to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask forgiveness. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning is ask forgiveness of God for your sin in your quarrel with the traitors. The reason for which the verse was revealed will be explained, and thus the meaning will become clear. It was said that the meaning is: And ask forgiveness of God for the sinners among your nation and those who quarrel falsely.
4:107: His saying 107- And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves meaning: Do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Argumentation is taken from the word jadal which means twisting, and it was said that it is taken from jadalah which means the face of the earth because each of the two opponents wants to throw his companion on it, and this is called betrayal of themselves because the harm of their disobedience returns to them. And the traitor is the one who betrays a lot, and the sinner is the one who sins a lot, and the lack of love is a metaphor for hatred.
4:108: His saying 108- They hide from the people meaning: they conceal themselves from them, as in His saying And whoever hides by night meaning: concealed. It was said that its meaning is: they hide from the people but do not hide from God: meaning: they do not hide from Him or are not ashamed of Him, and the situation is that He is with them in all their circumstances, knowing what they are in, so how can they hide from Him? When they spend the night meaning: they discuss the opinion among themselves. He called it spending the night because it is most common for the discussion of opinion to take place at night. What is not pleasing of the statement meaning: of the opinion that they discussed among themselves. He called it a statement because it does not happen except after the agreement between them.
4:109: His statement 109- "Here you are" meaning the people who argued on behalf of their thief friend as will come, and the sentence is subject and predicate. Al-Zajjaj said: "These means those and you argued means you argued in the life of this world, so who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection?" The question is for denial and rebuke: meaning who will argue and dispute with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection when they are punished for their sins? "Or who will be their guardian?" meaning: arguing and disputing. The guardian in the original is: the one who manages affairs. The meaning is: who is it who will take care of their affairs when God seizes them with His punishment. Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Qatada ibn al-Nu’man, who said: There was a family among us called Banu Ubayraq, Bishr, Bashir and Mubashir. Bishr was a hypocrite who used to write poetry satirizing the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then some Arab would attribute it to him and say: So-and-so said such-and-such, so-and-so said such-and-such. When the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard that poetry, they would say: By God, none but this wicked man would write this poetry. So he said: Or whenever men say a poem, they become deaf and say, Ibn Al-Abirq said it. He said: They were a family of need and poverty in the pre-Islamic era and Islam, and the people’s food in Medina was dates and barley. If a man was wealthy, a load of dirhams would arrive from Syria, and the man would buy some of it and set aside for himself. As for the family, their food was dates and barley. A load of dirhams arrived from Syria, and my uncle Rifa’ah ibn Rafi’ bought a load of dirhams and put it in a drinking place. In the drinking place were weapons for him, two shields and their swords and what was suitable for them. Then, he was attacked in the middle of the night, so the drinking place was dug up and the food and weapons were taken. When morning came, my uncle Rifa’ah came to me and said: O son of my brother, do you know that we were attacked last night? Our drinking place was dug up and our food and weapons were taken. He said: So we searched the house and asked, and it was said to us: We saw Banu Ubayraq lighting a fire this night, and we do not see from what we see except some of your food. He said: And Banu Ubayraq said while we were asking in the house: By God, we do not see your companion except Labid ibn Sahl, a man. He is a good and Muslim man. When Labid heard that, he drew his sword and went to Banu Abiraq and said: I steal? By God, this sword will mix with you, or you will reveal this theft. They said: Go away from us, O man, by God, you are not its owner. So we asked around in the house until we had no doubt that they were its owners. My uncle said to me: Oh, is it so? If you go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mention that to him. Qatada said: So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, a family of ours who are rude has gone to my uncle Rifa’ah ibn Zayd and dug into his drinking place and taken his weapons and food. Let them return our weapons to us, but as for the food, we have no need for it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will look into that. When Banu Ubayraq heard that, they went to a man from among them called Aseer ibn Urwah and spoke to him about it. Some of the people of the house gathered around him and came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, Qatada ibn al-Nu’man and his uncle have gone to a family of ours who are people of Islam and righteousness and accused them of theft without evidence or proof. Qatada said: So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So I spoke to him and he said: You went to a family among whom there was mention of Islam and righteousness, and you accuse them of theft without evidence or proof. Qatada said: So I went back and wished that I had given away some of my money and not spoken to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that. Then my uncle Rifa’ah came to me and said: O nephew, what did you do? So I told him what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said to me, and he said: God is the one sought for help. It was not long before the Qur’an was revealed: “Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the deceitful.” Banu Ubayraq. And seek forgiveness from God. That is, from what I said to Qatada. “Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves.” To His saying: Then he seeks forgiveness from God, he will find God Forgiving and Merciful. That is, if they had sought forgiveness from God, He would have forgiven them. And whoever earns sin. To His saying: He has certainly taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin. Their saying to al-Bayd. And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, a party of them would have resolved to mislead you. That is, Aseer ibn Urwah. When the Qur’an was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought the weapon and returned it to Rifa’ah. Qatada said: When I brought the weapon to my uncle, he was an old man who had fainted in the pre-Islamic period, that is, he had grown old. I saw that his Islam was questionable, but when I brought him the weapon, he said: O son of my brother, he is in the way of God. So I knew that his Islam was correct. When the Qur’an was revealed, Bashir caught up with the polytheists and went to Salafah bint Sa`d, and God revealed: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken until His saying: far astray. When he went to Salafah, Hassan ibn Thabit threw some verses of poetry at her, so she took his saddlebag and put it on her head, then went out and threw it in the valley, then said: Hassan’s poetry was given to me as a gift, you never used to bring me any good.” Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange hadith, we do not know of anyone who narrated it except Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani. Yunus ibn Bakir and others narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq on the authority of Asim ibn `Umar ibn Qatadah, without mentioning his father on the authority of his grandfather. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Sani`, Ahmad ibn Abi Shu`ayb al-Harrani told us, Muhammad ibn Salamah told us, and he mentioned it in full. Abu Al-Shaykh Al-Asbahani narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Abbas bin Ayoub and Al-Hasan bin Yaqub, both of them on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ahmad bin Abi Shuaib Al-Harrani on the authority of Muhammad bin Salamah on his authority. Then he said at the end of it: Muhammad bin Salamah said: Yahya bin Ma’een, Ahmad bin Hanbal and Ishaq bin Abi Isra’il heard this hadith from me. Al-Hakim narrated it in Al-Mustadrak on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm on the authority of Ahmad bin Abdul-Jabbar Al-Attardi on the authority of Yunus bin Bakir on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq with a more complete meaning than it. Then he said: This is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim. Ibn Sa’d narrated it on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid who said: Bashir went tomorrow, and he mentioned it in an abbreviated form. This story was narrated in an abbreviated and extended form on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un.
4:110: This is part of the previous story, and what is meant by evil is: the ugly thing that causes evil 110- or wrongs himself by committing a sin or a transgression that does not extend to others and then seeks forgiveness from God asking Him to forgive him for the sin he committed he will find God Forgiving for his sin Merciful to him, and in it is an encouragement for whoever committed theft from Banu Ubayraq to repent to God and seek His forgiveness, and that He is Forgiving and Merciful to whoever seeks His forgiveness. Ad-Dahhak said: This verse was revealed regarding Wahshi, the killer of Hamza, who associated partners with God and killed Hamza, then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Is there any repentance for me? So it was revealed. In any case, the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason, so it is for every servant of God who committed a sin and then sought forgiveness from God, the Most High.
4:111: His saying 111- And whoever earns a sin from sins by committing a sin he only earns it against himself meaning its consequences will return to him, and earning is what a person brings to himself in benefit or repels harm, and for this reason the Lord’s action is not called earning, as Al-Qurtubi said.
4:112: 112- And whoever earns a sin or a crime It was said: They are one meaning, repeated for emphasis. Al-Tabari said: Sin can be intentional or unintentional, and a crime can only be intentional. It was said: A small sin, and a crime: a large one. His saying Then he throws it at an innocent person is a singular pronoun because the conjunction is with or, or to make the sin predominate over the crime. It was said: It refers to the earning. His saying Then he has taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin Since sins are inseparable from their doer, they are like a weight that is carried, and similar to it is And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens with their own burdens. Slander is derived from the word baht which means lying to an innocent person in a way that causes him to be alarmed and confused. It is said: He slandered him if he said something about him that he did not say. It is also said that a man was baht with the kasra: if he was astonished and confused, and baht with the damma, and from this fabat al-dhi kufr the one who disbelieved is baht. The clear sin is: the obvious.
4:113: His statement 113- And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. What is meant by this grace and mercy for the Messenger of God is that he alerted to the truth in the story of Banu Ubayraq. It was said that what is meant by them is prophethood and infallibility. A party of them would have resolved that is, of the group who supported Banu Ubayraq as mentioned above to mislead you from the truth. But they mislead none but themselves because the consequences of that will return to them. And they will not harm you at all because God, the Exalted, is your protector from the people, and because you acted according to the outward appearance and there is no harm to you in ruling by it before the revelation came down. The preposition and its object are in the accusative case as a source: that is, they will not harm you at all. His statement And God has sent down the Book upon you It was said that this is the beginning of a statement, and it was said that the and is for the state: that is, they will not harm you at all while God sent down the Book and wisdom upon you, or with God sending that down upon you. His saying, And He taught you what you did not know is connected to He revealed: meaning He taught you through revelation what you did not know before. And the favor of God upon you was great because there is no greater favor than prophethood and the revelation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself 3:100, the verse. He said: God informed His servants of His forbearance, pardon, generosity, and the breadth of His mercy and forgiveness. Whoever commits a sin, whether small or great, and then seeks forgiveness from God, will find God Forgiving and Merciful, even if his sins were greater than the heavens, the earth, and the mountains. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: Whoever recites these two verses from Surat An-Nisa’ and then seeks forgiveness from God, God will forgive him: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God, will find God Forgiving and Merciful 3:100, And if they, when they were wronging themselves, had come to you, [O Muhammad], and asked forgiveness from God, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them 3:100. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, And taught you that which you did not know 3:100, he said: God taught him the distinction between what is lawful in this world and what is unlawful in the Hereafter, so that he might use that as evidence against His creation. He also narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: He taught him good and evil. Many hadiths have been reported about the acceptance of forgiveness and that it erases sin, recorded in the books of Sunnah.
4:114: Al-Najwa: The secret between two people or a group. You say: I whispered to someone, a whisper and a secret, and they were producing and whispering, and I saved someone, I saved him, a secret: meaning I talked to him, so Najwa is derived from Najwat al-Shai’ anjuwwa: meaning I saved it and isolated it. And Najwa is from the high ground because it is isolated by its height from what is around it, so Najwa: the conversation is a source. And the group may be called by it, as it is said, people of nothing, God Almighty said: And when they whispered So according to the first, the exception is disconnected: meaning for everyone who ordered charity, or connected on the assumption of except a secret from someone who ordered charity, and according to the second, the exception is connected in the position of the accusative as a substitute for many: meaning there is no good in many except for someone who ordered charity. A group of commentators said: The secret conversation is the speech of a group, isolated or two, whether that is secret or openly, and Al-Zajjaj said the same. His saying 114 - With charity it appears that it is voluntary charity, and it was said that it is obligatory charity. And what is known is voluntary charity, and the first is more appropriate. And what is known is a general term that includes all types of righteousness. Muqatil said: What is known here is a loan. And the first is more appropriate, and from it is the saying of Al-Hutay’ah: He who does good will not lose his reward. Customs between God and people will not be lost. And from it is the hadith: Every good deed is charity, and one of the good deeds is to meet your brother with a cheerful face. It was said: Good deeds are helping the distressed. Reconciliation between people is general in blood, honor, and money, and in everything in which disputes occur. His saying and whoever does that is an indication of the matters mentioned, making merely commanding them good, then he encouraged doing them by saying and whoever does that because doing them is closer to God than merely commanding them, since the goodness of commanding them is only because it is a means to doing them. His saying seeking the pleasure of God is a reason for the action, because whoever does it for other than that is not deserving of this praise and reward, rather he may not be saved from sin, and actions are by intentions.
4:115: 115- And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him Conflict: hostility and opposition. Guidance becomes clear by knowing the truth of the message through evidence indicating that, then he commits conflict and follows other than the way of the believers meaning: other than their path, which is what they are on of the religion of Islam and adherence to its rulings We will give him what he has taken meaning: We will make him a guardian of what he has followed of misguidance and drive him into Hell Asim, Hamza, and Abu Amr read Nawlh and Naslah with a sukoon on the ha' in both places. The rest read them with a kasra, and they are two dialects. It was read Naslah with a fatha on the noon from prayer, and this was explained previously. A group of scholars have used this verse as evidence for the validity of consensus, based on the statement, and follows other than the way of the believers. I do not see this as evidence, because what is meant by other than the way of the believers here is leaving the religion of Islam for another, as the wording indicates and the reason attests to. So do not believe that a scholar of this Islamic religion made ijtihad in some issues of the religion of Islam, and his ijtihad led him to contradict the mujtahids of his time, because he only sought to follow the path of the believers, which is the upright religion and the pure religion, and he did not follow a path other than theirs. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and others narrated on the authority of Umm Habibah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: All the speech of the son of Adam is against him and not for him, except enjoining what is right or forbidding what is wrong or remembering God, the Almighty and Majestic. Sufyan Al-Thawri said this in the Book of God: There is no good in much of their private conversation Al-An’am 2:17, and His statement: The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits and he says what is right, and His statement: By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience. There are authentic hadiths about silence and warning against the evils of the tongue and encouraging one another to guard it, and urging reconciliation between people. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan regarding his statement: And whoever does that he gives charity or lends or makes peace between people. Abu Nasr al-Sajzi narrated in al-Ibanah on the authority of Anas who said: “A Bedouin came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘God has revealed to me the Qur’an, O Bedouin, “There is no good in much of their private conversation” until His saying, Then We will give him a great reward. O Bedouin, the great reward is Paradise. The Bedouin said: Praise be to God who has guided us to Islam.” Al-Tirmidhi and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will never unite this nation in misguidance, and the hand of God is with the group, so whoever deviates will be scattered into the Fire. Al-Tirmidhi and al-Bayhaqi also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet.
4:116: His saying 116- Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him. The interpretation of this verse and its repetition with its wording for emphasis have been presented. It was said: It was repeated here for the story of Banu Ubayraq, and it was said: It was revealed here for a reason other than the story of Banu Ubayraq. It is what Al-Tha'labi and Al-Qurtubi narrated in their interpretation of Al-Dahhak: That an old man from the Bedouins came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I am an old man who is immersed in sins and transgressions, but I have not associated anything with God since I knew Him and believed in Him, and I have not taken a guardian besides Him, and I have not committed sins out of boldness towards God or out of stubbornness towards Him. I am regretful, repentant, and seeking forgiveness. So what is my state with God? Then God the Most High revealed: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him. The verse: And whoever associates anything with God has certainly strayed far astray from the truth, a great straying because polytheism is the greatest type of straying and the furthest from the truth.
4:117: 117- They invoke besides Him only female deities meaning: they invoke besides God only idols with feminine names such as Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat. It was said that what is meant by females is the dead that have no soul such as wood and stone. It was also said that what is meant by females are the angels because of their saying: The angels are the daughters of God. It was read as Wathana with a damma on the waw and the tha', the plural of wathan. This reading was narrated by Ibn Al-Anbari from Aisha. Ibn Abbas read Ila athana as the plural of wathan also, and its original form is wathan, so the waw was replaced with a hamza. Al-Hasan read Ila antha with a damma on the hamza and the noon after it with a triangle, the plural of anith like ghadeer and ghadr. Al-Tabari narrated that it is the plural of inath like thamar and thamar. Abu Amr Al-Dani narrated this reading from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Abu Haywah read it. According to all these readings, this speech is outside the context of rebuking the polytheists, denigrating them, and weakening their minds, because they worshipped a type of weak one besides God. And they do not invoke except a rebellious devil, meaning: And they do not invoke besides God except a rebellious devil, who is Iblis, may God curse him, because if they obeyed him in what he suggested to them, then they have worshipped him. The derivation of the word devil has already been mentioned. And the rebellious is the one who rebels, from mard: if he rebels. Al-Azhari said: The rebel is the one who goes beyond obedience. And a man has rebelled and gone beyond obedience, so he is a rebel, a rebel, and a rebel. Ibn Arafa said: He is the one whose evil has become apparent. It is said that a tree is mardah: if its leaves have fallen and its branches have become apparent, and from this a man is called a beardless man: meaning one whose hair is visible from his cheeks.
4:118: His statement 118- May God curse him. The root of cursing is expulsion and banishment. It has been mentioned before, and in common parlance it is banishment coupled with wrath. His statement: And he said, 'I will surely take from among Your servants a prescribed portion.' is conjoined with his statement, May God curse him. Both phrases are an attribute of Satan, meaning a rebellious Satan who combines God's curse upon him with this heinous statement. The prescribed portion is the cut-off, destined portion, meaning that I will make a destined portion of God's servants subject to my misguidance and on the side of my misguidance until I lead them from the worship of God to disbelief in Him.
4:119: His statement 119- And I will surely mislead them The lam is the answer to an omitted oath. Misguidance means diverting from the path of guidance to the path of misguidance. And so is the lam in his statement: And I will arouse in them false hopes and I will command them What is meant by the hopes that Satan arouses in them are the false hopes that arise from his insinuations and whisperings. And his statement: And I will command them, so they will cut off the ears of the cattle means: And I will command them to cut off the ears of the cattle: that is, to cut them off, so they will cut them off according to my command. And cutting means cutting, and from it is the sword of batak, it is said: bataka and bataka with a light and heavy vowel, and from it is the statement of Zuhair: She flew away with a feather in her hand Meaning: cutting. The infidels did that in compliance with the command of Satan and following his example, so they slit the ears of the bahīr and sawa’ib as is well known. His statement, And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God means: And I will command them to change the creation of God, and they will change it according to my command to them. The scholars differed about what this change is. A group said: It is castration, gouging out eyes, and cutting off ears. Others said: What is meant by this change is that God, the Exalted, created the sun, the moon, stones, fire, and similar creatures for the purpose for which He created them, so the infidels changed them by making them gods to be worshipped. Al-Zajjaj said the same. It was said: What is meant by this change is changing the nature upon which God created people, and there is nothing to prevent the verse from being interpreted to include all of these matters in a comprehensive or alternative interpretation. A group of scholars permitted castration of animals if the intention was to increase their benefit for fat or something else, while others disliked it. As for castrating human beings, it is forbidden, and some people disliked buying a castrated person. Al-Qurtubi said: They did not differ that castrating human beings is not permissible and is not permitted, and that it is mutilation and changing the creation of God, as is cutting off the rest of their limbs without a prescribed punishment or retaliation. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: And whoever takes Satan as a friend instead of God by following and complying with what he commands without following or complying with what God commanded, has certainly suffered a clear loss, meaning clear and apparent.
4:120: 120- He promises them false promises and fills them with false hopes "But Satan promises them nothing but delusion" meaning: Satan promises them nothing but delusion with what he puts in their minds of empty whispers "but delusion" with which he deceives them and makes it appear to them to be beneficial when it is pure harm. The accusative of "delusion" is because it is an attribute of a deleted source: meaning a delusional promise, or because it is a second object or a source with a different wording. Ibn Arafa said: Delusion is that which you see as having an appearance that you like but an interior that you dislike, and this sentence is parenthetical.
4:121: His statement 121- Those refers to the allies of Satan. This is a subject and its predicate is the sentence, which is his statement, Their abode is Hell. His statement, a refuge, meaning: a place, from haas to be safe, and it was said: a refuge and a sincere one. Al-Muhais is a place name, and it was said: a source.
4:122: His statement 122- And those who believed etc., made this promise to those who believed coupled with the previous threat to the disbelievers. His statement The promise of God is true He said in Al-Kashshaf two sources: the first confirms itself, and the second confirms something else, and the reason for that is that the first confirms the content of the nominal sentence and its content is a promise, and the second confirms something else: that is, that is, that is, truly true. His statement And who is more truthful than God in statement? This sentence confirms what preceded it, and the word qayl is a source of qal like qawl: that is, I do not find a word more truthful than God, the Almighty, and it was said that qayl is a noun, not a source, and that it is in the accusative case as a distinction. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Ali that he said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that is dearer to me than this verse: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abu Malik regarding his statement: They invoke not besides Him except female deities, he said: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza and Manat are all feminine. Abd God ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id al-Musnad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara from Abi ibn Ka’b regarding the verse: He said: With every idol is a jinn. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas: They invoke not besides Him except female deities, he said: Dead. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from al-Hasan. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir also narrated something similar from Qatadah. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Every tribe of the Arabs had an idol that they worshipped and called it the female of Banu Fulan. Then God revealed: They invoke not besides Him except female deities. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: The polytheists said: The angels are daughters of God, and we worship them only to bring us closer to God. He said: They took them as lords and depicted them as female slaves, so they were permissible and imitated, and they said: These resemble the daughters of God whom we worship. They meant the angels. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan regarding his statement: “And he said: I will surely take from among your servants” etc., he said: This is Iblis saying: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine will go to Hell and one will go to Paradise. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar from Ar-Rabi’. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: Then let them slit the ears of the cattle, he said: The slitting in Bahirah and Sa’ibah is that they slit their ears for their idols. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Anas that he disliked castration and said about it, And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God was revealed. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade castrating animals and horses.” Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade the killing of a soul and castrating animals.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, he said: The religion of God. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of al-Dahhak. Sa’id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan that he said: Tattooing.
4:123: Abu Ja'far read with a lightened ya' of amani in both places, and the name is not deleted: meaning that entering Paradise or virtue or being close to God is not by your wishes nor by the wishes of the People of the Book as is indicated by the reason for the revelation of the verse that follows. It was said: The pronoun refers to the promise of God, which is far-fetched. Among the wishes of the People of the Book are their saying, None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, and their saying, We are the children of God and His beloved, and their saying, The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. His saying 123- Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. It was said: What is meant by evil is polytheism, and the apparent meaning of the verse is more general than that, so whoever does evil, whatever evil it may be, will be recompensed for it, with no difference between a Muslim and a disbeliever. This sentence contains a severe threat that makes hearts tremble. It had a great impact on the hearts of Muslims when it was revealed, as is proven in Sahih Muslim and other verses from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: “When the verse ‘Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it’ was revealed, it reached a great level among the Muslims. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Be moderate and aim straight, for for everything that befalls a Muslim there is expiation, even a calamity that befalls him or a thorn that pricks him.’” His statement, nor will he find for himself, was read by the group in the subjunctive mood, in apposition to the recompense. Ibn Bakkar narrated from Ibn Amir, nor will he find for himself, in the nominative case, as a new beginning: meaning, whoever does evil other than God has no guardian to befriend him or supporter to aid him.
4:124: 124- And whoever does righteous deeds meaning some of them whether male or female and the state of being a believer, the first state is to clarify who does it, and the other state is to indicate the condition of faith in every righteous deed those referring to the deed characterized by faith will enter Paradise Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read they will enter with a damma on the letter of the present tense in the passive voice. The rest read it with a fatha on the active voice nor will they be wronged a speck meaning: they will not be deprived of anything insignificant, and the explanation of the speck has been presented above.
4:125: 125- And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God meaning: he devotes himself to Him while being a doer of good deeds, and follows the religion of Abraham meaning: his religion while being a follower, upright meaning: he inclines away from false religions to the religion of truth, which is Islam, and God took Abraham as a friend meaning: he made him an elite for Him and singled him out with His miracles. Tha'lab said: The friend is called a friend because his love permeates the heart and does not leave a friend in it except that it fills it, and he recited the words of Bashar: The path of the soul has penetrated me, and because of it, Khalil was named Khalil. Khalil is a verb that means an agent, just as al-‘Alim means the learned. It has also been said that it is in the sense of the passive participle, just as al-Habib means the beloved. Abraham, peace be upon him, was beloved by God and loved by Him. It has also been said that al-Khalil is from specialization, so God, the Exalted, singled out Abraham for His message at that time and chose him for it, and chose this al-Nahhas. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of al-Khalil is that in whose love there is no defect.
4:126: 126- And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. This indicates that He, glory be to Him, took Abraham as a friend out of His obedience, not out of need for him or to gain strength through his friendship. And God encompasses all things. This sentence confirms the meaning of the sentence before it: that is, His knowledge encompasses everything. He leaves out nothing small or great without enumerating it. Saeed bin Mansour, Abdul bin Hameed, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The Arabs said: We will not be resurrected and we will not be held accountable. The Jews and Christians said: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians. They said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. So God revealed: It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Masruq who said: The Muslims and the People of the Scripture argued. The Muslims said: We are better guided than you. The People of the Scripture said: We are better guided than you. So this verse was revealed and the Muslims prevailed over them: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Masruq who said: The Christians and the Muslims boasted. The former said: We are better than you, and the latter said: We are better than you. So this verse was revealed. The meaning of these narrations has been transmitted through many chains of transmission, both brief and long. Abd bin Humaid, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him when this verse was revealed: “As for you and your companions, O Abu Bakr, you will be rewarded for that in this world until you meet God with no sins on you. As for the others, that will be gathered for them until they are rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa’eed that they heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: No fatigue, illness, sorrow, or even worry befalls a believer but that God expiates some of his sins because of it. Many hadeeths have been narrated with this meaning. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Ibn ‘Umar met him and asked him about this verse: And whoever does righteous deeds, he said: The obligatory duties. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Jundub that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say before he died: God has taken me as a close friend just as He took Abraham as a close friend. Al-Hakim also narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Are you surprised that the friendship was for Abraham, the speech was for Moses, and the vision was for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace?
4:127: The reason for the revelation of this verse was a question from some of the Companions about the matter of women and their rulings in inheritance and other matters. So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them, God gives you a fatwa, meaning, He explains to you the ruling on what you asked about. This verse refers back to what the surah began with regarding the matter of women. They still had rulings that they did not know, so they asked, and it was said to them, God gives you a fatwa. His statement, and what is recited to you, is connected to His statement, God gives you a fatwa, and the meaning is: And the Qur’an that is recited to you gives you a fatwa on them. And what is recited in the Book in the meaning of orphans is the Almighty’s saying: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls. It is possible that His saying and what is recited is conjoined with the pronoun in His saying He gives you a fatwa referring back to the subject, due to the separation between the conjoined and the conjoined to it by the object and the preposition and the noun. It is also possible that it is the subject and in the Book is its predicate, on the basis that what is meant by it is the Preserved Tablet. Other than what we mentioned has been said about its parsing, but we did not mention it due to its weakness. His saying in the orphan women in the first and second versions is a connection to His saying is recited, and in the third version is a substitute for His saying in them. “Those to whom you do not give what is written for them” meaning: what was prescribed for them of inheritance and other things. And you desire is conjoined with His saying do not give them, conjoining an affirmative sentence with a negative sentence. It was said: a state of the subject of you give them. His saying, that you marry them, may mean that you desire to marry them for their beauty. It may mean that you desire to marry them for their beauty. It may mean that you desire to marry them for their beauty. It may mean that you are reluctant to marry them for their lack of beauty. His saying, and the weak among children, is conjoined with the orphans of women: that is, what is recited to you about the orphans of women and the weak among children, which is the saying of God Almighty, God instructs you concerning your children. The people of ignorance did not give inheritance to women or to those who were weak among children, as mentioned above. Rather, they gave inheritance to the men who were engaged in fighting and other matters. His statement, And that you act justly towards orphans, is connected to his statement, with regard to female orphans, such as the weak, meaning: And what is recited to you regarding female orphans and the weak, and that you act justly towards orphans, meaning justice. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, meaning: And He commands you to act and whatever you do of good, in the rights of those mentioned, Indeed, God is ever Knowing, He will reward you according to your actions, good and evil. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that Ibn Abbas said about the verse: And they ask you about women he said: The people of the Jahiliyyah did not give an inheritance to a newborn until he grew up and they did not give an inheritance to a woman. When Islam came, it said: “And they ask you about women. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them and what is recited to you in the Book” at the beginning of the Surah in the chapter on inheritance. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid about the verse he said: The people of the Jahiliyyah did not give an inheritance to women or children. They said: They will not fight or gain any good booty, so God imposed inheritance on them as a binding right. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar but longer from Saeed bin Jubair. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibrahim about the verse he said: If a girl was an orphan and ugly, they would not give her her inheritance and would prevent her from being married until she died so that they could inherit from her, so God revealed this. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Aisha regarding his statement, And they ask you about women until his statement, and you desire to marry them, she said: It is a man who has an orphan girl with him and he is her guardian and heir and he has shared his wealth with her, even in the bunch of dates, so he desires to marry her and he hates for a man to marry her so that she shares his wealth with him in what he shared with him, so he prevents her, so this verse was revealed. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Awn on the authority of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin regarding this verse, one of them said: You desire them, and the other said: You desire them.
4:128: A woman is raised by an implied verb that is explained by what follows: that is, if a woman fears, and fear means: she expected what she fears from her husband. It was said: its meaning is she was certain, which is wrong. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning 128- And if a woman fears from her husband is constant rebellion. Al-Nahhas said: The difference between rebellion and turning away is that rebellion is distancing, and turning away is that he does not speak to her or feel comfortable with her. The apparent meaning of the verse is that reconciliation is permissible when there is fear of any rebellion or the most obvious turning away, and consideration is given to the generality of the wording, not the specific reason that will come, and its apparent meaning is that reconciliation is permissible in any of its types, either by dropping the shift or some of it or some of the maintenance or some of the dowry. His saying that they reconcile is how the majority read it, and the Kufians read that they reconcile and the reading of the majority is more appropriate because the rule of the Arabs is that if the action is between two or more, it is said: the two men or people reconciled, not I reconciled. His saying, reconciliation is in the accusative case as a verbal noun or as a verbal noun with the missing affixes, or in the accusative case with a deleted verb: that is, their situation is reconciled. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a direct object. His saying, between them is an adverb for the verb or in the accusative case as a state. His saying, and reconciliation is better is a general expression that implies that reconciliation that calms souls and removes differences is better in general or better than separation or dispute. This sentence is parenthetical. His saying, and the souls have brought forth greed is a statement from Him, the Almighty, that greed is present in each one of them, and in all human souls, and that He made it as if it were present to them and would never be absent from them under any circumstances. This is by virtue of nature and disposition. A man is stingy with what is required of his wife in terms of good treatment, good spending, and the like, and a woman is stingy with her rights that are required of her husband and does not leave him anything of them. The stinginess of souls: their miserliness with what is required of them or what is good to do in some way. From this, And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. His statement, And if you treat women well and fear God, meaning, if you treat women well and avoid what is not permissible of rebellion and turning away, then God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted, so He will reward you, O group of spouses, with what you deserve.
4:129: His saying 129- "And you will never be able to be equal between women" God Almighty informed us of the denial of their ability to be equal between women in a way that has no inclination at all, due to what human natures are created with, of the inclination of the soul towards one without the other, and the increase of one in love and the decrease of the other, and this is by virtue of creation such that they do not control their hearts and are not able to stop themselves to equality, and for this reason the Truthful, the Trusted One, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, used to say: "O God, this is my portion in what I own, so do not blame me for what I do not own." And since they were not able to do that even if they were keen on it and exaggerated in it, God Almighty forbade them from inclining completely, because leaving that and avoiding injustice completely is within their ability and within their capacity, so it is not permissible for them to incline completely away from one of them towards the other until they leave the other like a woman who is suspended and has no husband or divorced, likening it to something that is suspended and not stable on anything, and in the reading of Abu, "So leave her like a prisoner His saying and if you reconcile" means: what You have corrupted the matters in which you have left what is required of you in terms of treating women fairly and justly among them. And you should avoid all the inclinations that you have been forbidden from. For indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. He will not hold you accountable for what you have neglected.
4:130: His statement 130- And if they separate meaning: they do not reconcile, but rather each one of them leaves the other, God will enrich each of them meaning He will make him independent of the other by providing for the man a woman who will agree with him and delight his eyes, and for the woman a man whose company she will rejoice in, and He will provide for them from His abundance provision that will make them independent of need, and God is Bountiful and Wise Bountiful in His bounty, and His actions proceed in a manner of perfection and mastery. At-Tirmidhi narrated with a hasan chain of transmission, Ibn al-Mundhir, at-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Sawdah feared that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would divorce her, so she said: O Messenger of God, do not divorce me and I will give my day to Aisha. So he did so and this verse was revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion 10:13. Ibn Abbas said: Whatever they agree upon is permissible. Abu Dawud, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Aisha that the reason for the revelation of this verse was the story of Sawdah mentioned above. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on her authority regarding the verse that she said: A man has a wife with him who he does not like much of and he wants to leave her, so she says: I will release you from my business, so this verse was revealed. Ash-Shafi’i, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab that the daughter of Muhammad ibn Salamah was married to Rafi’ ibn Khadij, and he disliked something from her, either because of her arrogance or something else, so he wanted to divorce her, but she said: Do not divorce me, and divide for me whatever you wish. So they reconciled, and this was the Sunnah, and the Qur’an revealed: And if a woman fears desertion from her husband, the verse. Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ali that he was asked about this verse, and he said: It is a man who has two wives, and one of them becomes incapable or ugly, so he wants to separate from her, so she reconciles with him on the condition that he spends one night with her and another night with the other, and he does not separate from her. Whatever she pleases is fine, but if she returns, he treats them equally. A group of the Companions narrated something similar to this, and it was confirmed in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Aisha who said: “When Sawdah bint Zam’ah grew old, she gave her day to Aisha, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to divide Sawdah’s day for her.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And souls are seized with greed, he said: His desire for something that he is keen on. Regarding his statement, And you will never be able to be equal between wives, he said: In love and sexual intercourse. Regarding his statement, So do not incline completely [toward marriage] and leave her hanging, he said: She is neither a widow nor married. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Aisha who said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to divide his time between his wives fairly, then he would say: ‘O God, this is my division in what I own, so do not blame me for what You own and I do not.’” And its chain of transmission is sahih. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd and the Sunan scholars narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever has two wives and is inclined towards one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side of his body hanging down. At-Tirmidhi said: It was only narrated by Hammam. Hisham Ad-Dastawai narrated it on the authority of Qatada who said: It was said, and this hadith is not known to be traced back to the Prophet except through the hadith of Hammam. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, he said: Intercourse. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Love.
4:131: His statement 131- And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. This sentence is a resumption to confirm the perfection of His vastness, glory be to Him, and the comprehensiveness of His power. And We have already enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you, We enjoined upon them in what We sent down to them of the Scriptures, and the lam in the Scripture is for the genus, and you, in apposition to the relative pronoun, that you fear God, meaning: We enjoined upon them and you to fear God, and it is in the accusative case by His statement, We enjoined, or in the accusative case by removing the preposition. Al-Akhfash said: That is, that you fear God. It is permissible for that to be explanatory, because the recommendation is in the sense of a statement. His statement, And if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, is in apposition to His statement, that you fear God, meaning: We enjoined upon them and you to fear God, and We said to them and to you, if you disbelieve. The benefit of this repetition is to emphasize so that the servants may be aware of the vastness of His kingdom and consider that and know that He is independent of His creation.
4:132: 132- To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs.
4:133: 133- If He wills, He will do away with you meaning He will annihilate you and bring others meaning: another people other than you, and it is like the Almighty’s saying: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you.
4:134: 134- Whoever desires the reward of this world meaning the one who seeks through his work something of worldly matters, like the mujahid who seeks booty without the reward, then with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter so why does he limit himself to the lower and more insignificant of the two rewards, and why doesn't he seek through his work what is with God, the Most High, which is the reward of this world and the Hereafter, so that he may attain them both and win them both? The apparent meaning of the verse is general. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: It is specific to the polytheists and hypocrites. And God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing He hears what they say and sees what they do. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And God is Free of need of His creation, Praiseworthy, he said: Praised by them. They also narrated on the authority of Ali something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And sufficient is God as a Disposer of affairs, he said: A Preserver.
