Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement, If He wills, He can do away with you, O mankind, and bring others, he said: By God, our Lord, He is able to do that, to destroy whomever He wills of His creation and bring others after them.
4:135: His saying 135- Qawwamin is an exaggerated form: meaning that you should repeat the establishment of justice, which is fairness in your testimony against yourselves, which is the acknowledgment of the rights that you owe. As for his testimony against his parents, it is that he testifies against them for the right of others, and likewise the testimony against the closest relatives. He mentioned the parents because of the obligation to be dutiful to them and because they are the most beloved of creation to him, then he mentioned the closest relatives because they are the ones who are suspected of love and fanaticism. So if they testify against these people for what they owe, then the stranger among the people is more deserving of being a witness against him. It has been said that the meaning of testifying against oneself is to testify for the right of someone from whom he fears harm will befall him and he is far away. His saying witnesses for God is a predicate after the predicate of was, or a state and it was not declined because it contains the feminine alif. Ibn Atiyyah said: The state in it is weak in meaning because it limits the establishment of justice to the meaning of testimony only. And his saying for God means: for His pleasure and reward. His saying, even if against yourselves is related to witnesses. This is the apparent meaning of the verse. It was said that the meaning of witnesses for God is oneness, so his saying, even if against yourselves is related to two guardians, and the first is more appropriate. His saying, if he is rich or poor is the noun of was that is understood: that is, if the one being testified against is rich, then he is not taken into consideration because of his wealth in order to gain his benefit and out of compassion for him, so he leaves the testimony against him, or if he is poor, then he is not taken into consideration because of his poverty, out of mercy for him and compassion for him, so he leaves the testimony against him. Rather, he said, God is more worthy of both of them and did not say it even though the choice only indicates obtaining one, because the meaning is that God is more worthy of each of them. Al-Akhfash said: Or is in the sense of and, and it was said that it is permissible with the previous mention of them as in his saying, And he has a brother or a sister, then for each of them is a sixth. Something simpler than this has already been mentioned before. Abi read, God is more worthy of them. Ibn Mas’ud read, if he is rich or poor with the word was being complete. So do not follow desire, he forbade them from following desire. His saying, that you be just is in the accusative case, and it is either from justice, as if he said: Do not follow desires out of aversion to being just among people, or from deviation, as if he said: Do not follow desires for fear that you will deviate from the truth, or out of aversion to deviate from the truth. His saying, And if you twist is from to twist, it is said: I twisted someone's right: if I pushed him away from it. What is meant is for me to testify out of inclination towards the one testified against. Ibn Amir and the Kufians read And if you twist from to give testimony: that is, if you give testimony and leave what is required of you to give it in the right manner. It has been said that this reading conveys two meanings: guardianship and turning away. The first reading conveys one meaning, which is turning away. Some grammarians claimed that the second reading is a mistake and a grammatical error, because there is no meaning for guardianship here. An-Nahhas and others said: This is not necessary, but talawa means talawa, because its original form is talawa, and the damma on the waw, followed by another waw, was considered too heavy, so the vowel was placed on the lam and one of the two waws was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Zajjaj mentioned something similar. His statement, or you turn away means: from giving testimony from the original form, for indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Knowing means: with what you do of turning away and ignoring or of every action. In this is a severe warning for whoever does not give testimony as is required of him. It has been narrated that this verse includes the judge and the witnesses. As for the witnesses, this is apparent. As for the judge, this means that he turns away from one of the two opponents or turns away from speaking with him. It was said: It is specific to the witnesses.
4:136: His saying: 136- O you who have believed, believe in God and His Messenger meaning: Be steadfast in your faith and continue with it, and the address here is to all believers. And the Book that was sent down to His Messenger is the Qur'an, and the lam is for the covenant. And the Book that was sent down before is every book, and the lam is for the genus. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read nazzal and anzala with the damma. The rest read them with the fatha. It was said that the verse was sent down about the hypocrites. The meaning is: O you who have believed, outwardly, be sincere to God. It was said that it was sent down about the polytheists, and the meaning is: O you who have believed in Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, believe in God, and they are weak. His statement: And whoever disbelieves in God and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day meaning in any of that has certainly strayed far astray from the goal into error. The Messenger was mentioned previously to mention the book that was revealed to him, and the messengers were mentioned here to mention the books as a whole, so it was appropriate to mention the messengers as a whole, and to present the angels before the messengers because they are the intermediaries between God and His messengers. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm Al-Baqarah 2:17, he said: God commanded the believers to speak the truth even if it is against themselves, their fathers, or their children, not to show favoritism to the rich because of his wealth, nor to have mercy on the poor because of his poverty. And regarding his statement, So do not follow [your] desire, lest you abandon the truth and commit injustice, even if you twist meaning with your tongues in the testimony, or turn away from it. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah narrated on his authority regarding the meaning of the verse, he said: Two men sit before a judge, and the judge is mine, and his turning away is for one of the two men over the other. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority that he said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Madinah, Surat al-Baqarah was the first Surah to be revealed, then Surat al-Nisa was revealed after it. He said: So a man would have testimony before his cousin or his relatives, but he would twist his tongue or conceal it because of what he saw of his hardship until he became able to pay the debt when he was able to pay. Then, Be persistently standing firm in justice al-Baqarah 2:17 was revealed. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority that: But if they twist or turn aside al-Baqarah 2:17 meaning: twist your tongue unjustly, which is stammering, so you do not give testimony properly. Turning aside means abandoning. Al-Tha’labi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that “Abdullah bin Salam, Asad and Asid, the sons of Ka’b, Tha’laba bin Qais, Salam the nephew of Abdullah bin Salam, Salamah the son of his brother, and Yameen bin Yameen came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we believe in you and your book, Moses, the Torah, and Ezra, and we disbelieve in all the books and messengers other than them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, believe in God and His Messenger Muhammad and His book the Qur’an and every book that came before it. They said: We will not do that. Then the verse, ‘O you who believe, believe in God’ was revealed.” The authenticity of this should be examined, as Al-Tha’labi, may God have mercy on him, is not one of the men of narration and he does not differentiate between the authentic and the fabricated. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding this verse, saying: He means by that the People of the Book. God had taken a covenant from them in the Torah and the Gospel, and they had agreed upon themselves to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then when God sent His Messenger, he called them to believe in Muhammad and the Qur’an and reminded them of the covenant that He had taken from them. Some of them believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and followed him, and some of them disbelieved.
4:137: 137- Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - never will God forgive them or guide them to a way. God, the Exalted, informed us about this group that believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief after all of that, that God, the Exalted, will not forgive their sins nor guide them to a way by which they can reach the truth and follow it to goodness, because it is very far from them to be sincere to God and believe with a correct faith. This confusion on their part, sometimes claiming that they are believers and sometimes abandoning the faith and returning to what is their habit and their way of continuous disbelief and constant denial, is the most eloquent indication that they are toying with the religion, and they have no correct intention or sincere purpose. It was said: What is meant by these Jews is that they believed in Moses, then disbelieved in Ezra, then believed in Ezra, then disbelieved in Jesus, then increased in disbelief by disbelieving in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: They believed in Moses, then disbelieved in him by worshipping the calf, then believed in him when he returned to them, then disbelieved in Jesus, then increased in disbelief by disbelieving in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. What is meant by the verse is that they increased in disbelief and continued in that, as is apparent from their condition. Otherwise, if the disbeliever believes and makes his faith sincere and abandons disbelief, then God has guided him to the path that requires forgiveness, and Islam wipes out what came before it. However, since this was very unlikely from them, the forgiveness of their sins and their guidance to the path of truth was unlikely.
4:138: His saying 138- Give the hypocrites good tidings that they will have a painful punishment. Giving good tidings to what is pure evil for them is mockery of them, and its verification has been mentioned.
4:139: And His saying 139- Those who take the disbelievers as allies is a description of the hypocrites or is accusative of blame: that is, they make the disbelievers their allies, befriending them in their disbelief and supporting them in their misguidance. And His saying: Other than the believers is in the accusative case as a state: that is, they befriend the disbelievers, exceeding the allegiance of the believers. Do they seek honor with them? This question is for rebuke and rebuke, and the sentence is parenthetical. His saying For indeed, honor belongs to God entirely This sentence is an explanation of what came before of their rebuke for seeking honor with the disbelievers. All types of honor and its individuals are specific to God, the Most High, and whatever of it is with others is from His bounty and favor as in His saying: And to God belongs honor and to His Messenger and to the believers. Honor is victory, it is said that He honored him with honor: if He defeated him.
4:140: 140- And it has already been revealed to you in the Book is addressed to all who have shown faith, whether believers or hypocrites, because whoever has shown faith is obligated to comply with what God has revealed. It has been said that it is addressed to the hypocrites only, as is indicated by the emphasis and rebuke. Asim and Ya'qub read nazzal with the fatha on the noon and the zay and its emphasis, and its subject is a pronoun referring to the name of God the Most High in His statement For indeed, honor belongs to God entirely. Hamid read with the zay softened and open with the noon opened, and the rest read with the noon closed and the zay broken and stressed in the passive construction. His statement that if you hear the verses of God is in the accusative case according to the first reading as the object of nazzal. In the nominative case according to the second reading as the subject, and in the nominative case as the object of what its subject is not named according to the third reading. And that is the lightened form of the heavy, and the estimation is that if you hear the verses of God. The Book is the Qur'an. His statement, disbelieves in it and mocks it is two states: that is, if you hear disbelief and mockery of the verses of God, then the hearing is directed to the verses, and what is meant is hearing disbelief and mockery. His statement, So do not sit with them until they engage in a conversation other than that means: It was revealed to you in the Book that when you hear this disbelief and mockery of the verses of God, you should not sit with them as long as they are like that until they engage in a conversation other than the conversation of disbelief and mockery of them. What God revealed to them in the Book is His statement, And when you see those who engage in discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they engage in a conversation other than that. A group of those who entered Islam used to sit with the polytheists and Jews when they mocked and ridiculed the Qur’an, so they were forbidden from doing so. In this verse, considering the generality of its wording, which is the valid one, rather than the specificity of the reason, there is evidence to avoid every situation in which its people engage in what indicates the belittling and mockery of the evidence of the Shari’ah, as happens often among the prisoners of imitation who replaced the opinions of men with the Book and the Sunnah, and nothing remained in their hands except that the Imam of our school of thought said such-and-such, and so-and-so of his followers said such-and-such, and if they heard someone provide evidence for that issue with a Qur’anic verse or a Prophetic hadith, they mocked him and did not raise his head to what he said nor did they care about it at all, and they thought that he had come with a terrible matter and a heinous speech and contradicted the school of thought of their Imam, whom they placed in the position of a teacher of the Shari’ah, rather they exaggerated in that until they made his opinion the author and his ijtihad, which is inclined from the path of truth, precedence over God, His Book, and His Messenger, so we belong to God and to Him we shall return. What these schools of thought did to their people and the Imams to whom these imitators belong are innocent of their actions, for they have explicitly stated in their writings the prohibition of imitating them, as We have explained this in our message entitled [The Useful Statement on the Rule of Imitation] and in our book entitled [The Etiquette of Request and the Ultimate Goal]. O God, benefit us with what you have taught us and make us among those who follow the Book and the Sunnah and distance us from the opinions of men that are built on the brink of a collapsing precipice, O Answerer of those who ask. His saying, Then you will be like them is an explanation for the prohibition: meaning, if you do that and do not stop, then you will be like them in disbelief. It was said: This similarity is not in all the attributes, but it is an imposition of a likeness by virtue of the apparent meaning, as in the saying of the speaker: Every companion follows the example of the one he accompanies. This verse is decisive according to all scholars except what is narrated from Al-Kalbi, who said: It was abrogated by the statement of God the Almighty: And there is not upon those who fear God any account for them. This is rejected, because it is part of piety to avoid the gatherings of those who disbelieve in the verses of God and mock them. His statement: Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell, all together. This is an explanation for their being like them in disbelief. It was said: They are the ones who sit and those who are sat upon according to those who made the address directed to the hypocrites.
4:141: His saying 141- Those who lie in wait for you meaning: they wait for you for what will happen to you of good or evil, and the relative pronoun is in the accusative case as a description of the hypocrites or a substitute for them only, not the disbelievers, because the aforementioned lying in wait is from the hypocrites and not the disbelievers, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a criticism, "But if you have a victory from God, they will say: Were we not with you?" This sentence and the sentence after it are a narration of their lying in wait: meaning if you have a victory from God in victory over those of the disbelievers who oppose you, they will say to you Were we not with you in being described by the outward appearance of Islam and adhering to its rulings and demonstrating and dominating and increasing the number, And if the disbelievers have a share of your victory and triumph over you, they will say to the disbelievers Did we not gain control over you? meaning: Did we not subdue you and overcome you and have power over you, but we left you alone. It was said that the meaning is: They said to the infidels who had defeated the Muslims, Did we not gain control over you until the Muslims feared you and we abandoned them from you? The first is more appropriate, because the meaning of dominance is to overcome. It is said that he overcame something, meaning he overcame it. From this is the saying of God Almighty: Satan overcame them. It is not correct to say: Did we not overcome you until the Muslims feared you? Rather, the meaning is: Did we not overcome you, O group of disbelievers, and gain power over you, so we left you and kept you until you achieved this victory over the Muslims. And prevent you from the believers by discouraging them and discouraging them from you until their hearts weakened from repelling you and they were unable to take revenge on you. What is meant is that they lean towards the one who has the upper hand and victory from the two groups and show them that they were with them against the defeated group. This is the way of the hypocrites, may God distance them, and the way of those who follow their example from the people of Islam, who show that they are with each group over the other, and lean towards the one who has a share of the world in money or prestige, so he meets him with flattery, affection, submission and humiliation, and he meets the one who has a share of the world with severity, harshness and bad manners, and he despises him and fights him with every dislike. So God has made ugly the morals of The hypocrites and the furthest. His statement, Then God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, based on what their consciences contain of hypocrisy and hatred for the truth and its people. On that day, the truths will be revealed and consciences will be made clear, even if they spared their blood in this world and preserved their wealth by speaking the word of Islam hypocritically. And God will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers, this is on the Day of Resurrection if what is meant by the way is victory and dominance, or in this world if what is meant by it is an argument. Ibn Atiyyah said: All the people of interpretation said that what is meant by this is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is weak because the report of it is useless, and its cause is the assumption of those who assume that the end of the speech refers to its beginning, meaning his saying, So God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and that nullifies its benefit, since it is a repetition. This is the meaning of his speech. It was said that the meaning is: God does not give the disbelievers a way over the believers that would wipe out their state, remove their traces, and violate their honor, as is indicated by the authentic hadith in Sahih: “And that I will not give authority over them to an enemy other than themselves, who would violate their honor, even if they were to gather against them from all corners of the world, until some of them would destroy others and take others captive.” It was said: He, the Almighty, does not give the disbelievers a way over the believers as long as they are acting in accordance with the truth, not satisfied with falsehood, and do not abandon forbidding evil, as God, the Almighty, said: And whatever strikes you of disaster is for what your hands have earned. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is very valuable. It was said: God does not give the disbelievers a way over the believers according to the Shari’ah, and if it is found, it is contrary to the Shari’ah. This is the summary of what the people of knowledge have said about this verse, and it is suitable for use as evidence in many matters. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the statement of God, Indeed, those who believed and then disbelieved the verse, he said: They are the Jews and Christians. The Jews believed in the Torah and then disbelieved, and the Christians believed in the Gospel and then disbelieved. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: These Jews believed in the Torah and then disbelieved. Then he mentioned the Christians and said, Then they believed and then disbelieved meaning: We believed in the Gospel and then disbelieved, Then they increased in disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, he said: These hypocrites believed twice and then disbelieved twice, then they increased in disbelief after that. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abbas regarding the statement of God, Then they increased in disbelief he said: They remained in their disbelief until they died. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Wa’il who said: A man may say a lie in a gathering to make his companions laugh, and God will be angry with them all. They mentioned that to Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, who said: “Abu Wa’il is right. Isn’t that in the Book of God?” So do not sit with them until they engage in another conversation. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Until they engage in another conversation was revealed in Surat Al-An’am, then the emphasis was revealed in Surat An-Nisa’ Indeed, then you would be like them. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubair that God will gather the hypocrites from the people of Madinah and the disbelievers from the people of Makkah who engaged in lying and mocked the Qur’an in Hell all together. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Those who lie in wait for you, he said: They are the hypocrites lying in wait for the believers. But if you have a victory from God, if the Muslims take spoils from their enemy, the hypocrites will say, Were we not with you? So give us from the spoils the like of what you take. And if the disbelievers have a share, they will take from the Muslims, the hypocrites will say to the disbelievers, Did we not gain the upper hand over you? Did we not make clear to you that I am on what you are, and we were holding them back from you. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, Did we not gain the upper hand over you? He said: We defeated you. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab, and Al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, on the authority of Ali, that it was said to him, Do you see this verse, ‘And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers?’ And they fight us and are victorious and killed, so he said: Come closer, come closer. Then he said, Then God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: In the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Malik something similar as well. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, A way, he said: An argument.
4:142: His statement 142- "Indeed, the hypocrites deceive God." This is an introductory statement that includes an explanation of some of the ugliness and scandals of the hypocrites. The meaning of deception has been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, and their deception of God is that they do the deceiver's action of showing faith while concealing disbelief. The meaning of God deceiving them is that He did to them the deceiver's deceiver's action, that is, He left them as they were, showing Islam in this world, thus He protected their wealth and blood, and delayed their punishment until the Hereafter, thus He rewarded them for their deception with the lowest level of Hell. It was said in Al-Kashaf: The deceiver is an active participle from the verb khadhiqatuhu fakhadutuhu if I overcame him and I was more deceitful than him. The lazy ones with a damma on the kaf are the plural of kaslan. It was also read with a fatha, and what is meant is that they pray while they are lazy and sluggish, neither hoping for reward nor fearing punishment. Hypocrisy is showing off beauty so that people can see it, not to follow God’s commands. This has been explained previously. Hypocrisy is the reciprocal action. His statement, and they do not remember God except a little is connected to they show off: meaning they do not remember Him, glory be to Him, except a little remembrance, or they do not pray except a little prayer. The description of remembrance as little is due to a lack of sincerity, or because it is not accepted, or because it is little in itself, because the one who does an act of obedience with the intention of showing off only does it in groups and does not do it in private like the one who is sincere.
4:143: Mould 143- "Volatile between that" The oscillating person is the one who hesitates between two things, and oscillation is disturbance. It is said: He oscillated it, so it oscillated, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: Have you not seen that God has given you a surah that makes every king waver before it? Ibn al-Jinni said: The waverer is the anxious one who does not remain in one state. These hypocrites waver between the believers and the polytheists, neither sincere in their faith nor openly declaring their disbelief. He said in al-Kashshaf: The true meaning of the waverer is the one who defends from both sides: that is, he is repelled and pushed back and does not remain on one side, as it is said: So-and-so is being thrown by the hopefuls, except that the wavering has a repetition that is not in defending, as if the meaning is: whenever he leans to one side, he defends it. The majority read it with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the two dhaals. Ibn Abbas read it with a kasra on the second dhaal, and in the letter of Abi, it is mutahazazeen. Al-Hasan read it with a fatha on the meem and the two dhaals. The accusative of mudahazeen is either in the state or in the blame, and the reference in his saying between that is to faith and disbelief. His saying, Neither to these nor to those, meaning: neither related to the believers nor to the disbelievers. The location of the sentence is in the accusative case as a state, or as a substitute for wavering, or as an explanation of it. And whomever God leaves astray, meaning: He lets him down and deprives him of success, you will not find for him a way, meaning: a path that leads him to the truth.
4:144: His statement 144- O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers. That is, do not make them your special confidants and confidants whom you befriend rather than your brothers among the believers, as the hypocrites did in their befriending of the disbelievers. Do you want to make for God a clear authority over you? The question is for rebuke and rebuke: that is, do you want to make God a clear argument against you with which He will punish you because of your committing what He forbade you from, which is befriending the disbelievers.
4:145: 145- The hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire. The Kufians read ad-Darak with a sukoon on the ra', while others read it with a fatha. Abu Ali said: They are two dialects and the plural is adrak. It was said that the plural of the fatha is adrak like camel and ajmal, and the plural of the sukoon is adarak like fals and aflas. An-Nahhas said: The fatha is more eloquent. Ad-Darak is the level. The Fire has seven levels, and the hypocrite will be in the lowest level of it, which is the abyss, due to the severity of his disbelief and the abundance of his calamities. The highest level is Jahannam, then al-Hutama, then al-Sa'ir, then Saqar, then al-Jahim, then al-Hawiyah. All of them are called by the name of the highest level. May God protect us from its punishment. And you will not find for them a helper to save them from that level, and the address is to everyone who is suitable for it or to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
4:146: 146- Except those who repent is an exception from al-Munafiqun 63:that is, except those who repented from hypocrisy and reformed what they had corrupted of their conditions and made their religion sincere for God that is, they made it sincere for Him, not tainted by obedience to anyone other than Him. Holding fast to God means holding fast to Him and trusting in His promise. The reference in His saying those is to those who repented and possessed the previous qualities. His saying with the believers Al-Farra' said: that is, from the believers, meaning those who did not commit hypocrisy at all. Al-Qatibi said: He turned away from their speech out of anger at them, so he said those are with the believers and he did not say they are the believers. End quote. It appears that the meaning of with is considered here: that is, those are the companions of the believers in the rulings of this world and the hereafter. Then he explained what God has prepared for the believers who are with them, saying, And God will give the believers a great reward. The ya was deleted from yu’ta in writing, just as it was deleted in pronunciation, due to its being silent and the lam after it being silent. Similar to it is the Day the caller calls, “we will call the guards,” the Day the caller calls, and the like, for the deletion in all of them is due to the meeting of two silent letters.
4:147: His saying 147- What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? This sentence includes an explanation that He, glory be to Him, has no purpose in tormenting except merely to punish the disobedient. The meaning is: What benefit would He have in tormenting you if you are grateful and believe? This does not increase His kingdom, just as leaving your torment does not decrease His authority. And God is Ever Appreciative and Knowing. That is, He thanks His servants for their obedience to Him, so He rewards them for it and accepts it from them. In the language, gratitude means to appear. It is said, Shakoor if its fat appears above what it is given of fodder. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the words of God, Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive God, the verse, he said: A light will be cast upon a believer and a hypocrite with which they will walk on the Day of Resurrection until, when they reach the Sirat, the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished and the believers will proceed with their light. This is God’s deception of them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi something similar. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair something similar as well, and I do not know where they got this interpretation from, because something like it is only transmitted from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding the verse, he said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubayy and Abu Amir bin An-Nu’man. The description of the prayer of the hypocrite has been reported in the authentic hadiths, and that he watches the sun until it is between the horns of Satan, then he stands and pecks it four times, and he does not mention anything about it except a little. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, wavering between that, he said: They are the hypocrites. Neither to these, he said: Neither to the companions of Muhammad. Nor to these, he said: The Jews. It is proven in Sahih from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The example of the hypocrite is like that of a sheep wandering between two flocks, switching to this one at one time and to that one at another, and you do not know which of them to follow. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, Do you want to make for God a clear authority over you? He said: God is the authority over His creation, but He says a clear excuse. Abd Al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Firyabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Every authority in the Qur’an is a proof, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement, Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, he said: In iron coffins locked over them, and in another version, unknown over them, meaning locked so that one cannot find the place to open them. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah something similar. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud as well. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful? the verse, he said: God does not punish a grateful person or a believer.
4:148: Negation of love is a metaphor for hatred, and the reading of the majority 148- except for the one who wronged is in the passive form. Zaid bin Aslam, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Ata bin As-Sa'ib read except for the one who wronged in the active form, and according to the first reading it is an exception connected to the estimation of a deleted complement: i.e. except for the one who wronged, and it was said: according to the first reading it is also disconnected: i.e. but the one who wronged, he may say so-and-so wronged me. Scholars differed about how to speak ill of someone who has been wronged. Some said: It is to invoke God against the one who wronged him. Others said: There is nothing wrong with speaking ill of someone who has wronged him by saying: So-and-so wronged me or he is an unjust person or something similar. Others said: Its meaning is: Except for someone who is forced to speak ill of someone who has disbelieved or something similar, then it is permissible for him. The verse according to this is about compulsion. Qatrub said the same. He said: It is also permissible for it to be an alternative, as if he said: God loves only the one who has been wronged, meaning He does not love the unjust, but rather He loves the one who has been wronged. What appears from the verse is that it is permissible for the one who has been wronged to speak ill of someone who has been wronged, and this is supported by the hadith in Sahih with the wording: Whoever finds injustice, his honor and punishment are permissible. As for the second reading, the exception is discontinuous: meaning: Except for the one who has been wronged in an action or a word, then speak ill of him in the sense of forbidding his action and rebuking him. Some people said: The meaning of the statement is: God does not like anyone to speak evil aloud, but whoever is wronged, then he speaks evil aloud unjustly and aggressively, and he is a wrongdoer in that. This is the case of many wrongdoers, for in addition to their wrongdoing, they use their tongues to attack the one they wronged and attack his honor. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that the meaning is except for the one who is wronged and says evil, for he should be held by the hand, and it is an exception that is not from the first. And God is Hearing and Knowing. This is a warning to the wrongdoer that God hears what he does and knows about it. Then after He permitted the wronged to speak evil aloud, He encouraged what is better and preferable.
4:149: He said 149- Whether you disclose good or conceal it or pardon an evil that befalls you then indeed, God is ever Pardoning of His servants Powerful to take revenge on them for what their hands have earned, so follow His example, glory be to Him, for He pardons while being able. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, God does not like the public mention of evil speech, that he said: God does not like anyone to supplicate against another, unless he is wronged, in which case He has permitted him to supplicate against the one who wronged him, but if he is patient, it is better for him. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, that he said: It was revealed about a man who hosted a man in a deserted area and did not host him, then he mentioned that he did not host him and did not say anything more than that. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ismail, God does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged, that he said: Ad-Dahhak Ibn Muzahim used to say: This is in order of precedence and delay, God says: What would He do with your punishment if you were grateful and believed except by one who was wronged, and he used to recite it like that, then he said: God does not like the public mention of evil speech, meaning: In any case, this is how he said it, and this is close to distorting the meaning of the verse. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever invokes curses against the one who wronged him has taken revenge. Abu Dawud narrated something similar on her authority from another chain of transmission. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The two who insult each other shall have no right to say anything, and the one who started it is liable unless the one who was wronged retaliates.
4:150: When he finished mentioning the polytheists and hypocrites, he mentioned the disbelievers from the People of the Book, who are the Jews and Christians, because they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that was like disbelief in all the Messengers and revealed books, and disbelief in that is disbelief in God, and his statement 150- Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His Messengers should be understood as meaning that this entails their disbelief in some of the books and messengers, not that they disbelieved in God and His Messengers all together, for the People of the Book did not disbelieve in God or in all of His Messengers, but when they disbelieved in some of them, that was disbelief in God and in all of the Messengers. The meaning of: And they want to make a distinction between God and His messengers is that they disbelieved in the messengers because they disbelieved in some of them and believed in God, so that was a distinction between God and His messengers. And they say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others.’ They are the Jews who believed in Moses and disbelieved in Jesus and Muhammad, and likewise the Christians who believed in Jesus and disbelieved in Muhammad. And they want to adopt a way in between. That is, they adopt a religion that is intermediate between belief and disbelief. So the reference in His saying that is to His saying, We believe and disbelieve.
4:151: 151- Those are the disbelievers meaning: those who are complete in disbelief. His saying truly is a source confirming the content of the sentence: meaning that is truly true, or it is an attribute of the source of the disbelievers: meaning truly disbelief.
4:152: His statement 152- And they made no distinction between any of them by saying: We believe in some and disbelieve in others, and the entry of between on one is because it is general in the singular, masculine and feminine, their dual and their plural. Its investigation has been presented previously, and the reference in His statement those is to those who believed in God and His messengers and did not make any distinction between any of them. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: Those are the enemies of God, the Jews and the Christians. The Jews believed in the Torah and Moses and disbelieved in the Gospel and Jesus, and the Christians believed in the Gospel and Jesus and disbelieved in the Qur’an and Muhammad. They adopted Judaism and Christianity, which are two innovations that are not from God, and they abandoned Islam, which is the religion of God with which He sent His messengers. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj.
4:153: His statement 153- The People of the Book ask you are the Jews. They asked him, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ascend to the heavens while they see him, so he would bring down to them a written book in what he claims, proving his truthfulness all at once, just as he brought Moses the Torah out of their stubbornness. God distanced them, so God Almighty informed him that they had asked Moses a question greater than this question, so they said, Show us God openly meaning: clearly, and its meaning was presented in Al-Baqarah, and openly is an attribute of a deleted source: meaning seeing clearly. His statement, They have asked is the answer to an implied condition: meaning if you find this question too great for them to ask you, then they asked Moses something greater than that. His statement, So the thunderbolt seized them is the fire that descended upon them from the sky and destroyed them. The ba in His statement, because of their wrongdoing is for a reason: that is, because of their wrongdoing in their false question, because seeing it with the eye is impossible in this case. This does not necessitate its being impossible on the Day of Resurrection, as it came with that because seeing it with the eye is impossible in this case. This does not necessitate its being impossible on the Day of Resurrection, as the mutawatir hadiths have come with that. Whoever uses this verse as evidence for the impossibility of seeing it on the Day of Resurrection has made a clear mistake. Then they were not satisfied with this false question that arose from them because of their wrongdoing after they saw the miracles, but they added to it what is uglier than it, which is the worship of the calf. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So We revived them, so they took the calf. And the clear proofs: the evidence and proofs, and the miracles of the hand and the staff and the splitting of the sea and others. So We pardoned that meaning: what they did of stubbornness and worship of the calf. And We gave Moses a clear authority meaning: a clear argument, which are the signs that he brought, and it was called an authority because the one who brought it defeated his opponent, and from that is the command of God Almighty to him to order them to kill themselves in repentance for their disobedience, because it was part of the authority with which he defeated them.
4:154: 154- And We raised the mountain over them because of their covenant meaning: because of their covenant to give it, because it was narrated that they refused to accept the law of Moses, so God raised the mountain over them and they accepted it. It was said: The meaning is because of their breaking their covenant that was taken from them, which is to act according to what is in the Torah. The raising of the mountain was mentioned in Al-Baqarah, and likewise the interpretation of their entering the gate in prostration. And We said to them, Do not transgress on the Sabbath so that you take what you were ordered to leave in it of the fish. The interpretation of that was mentioned previously. It was read, do not transgress and do not transgress with the opening of the 'ayn and the emphasis on the dal. And We took from them a firm covenant confirming it, which is the covenant that He took from them in the Torah. It was said that it was a covenant confirming with an oath, so it was called firm for that reason.
4:155: His statement 155- Because they broke their covenant Ma is an additional word for emphasis, or an indefinite noun, and Naqdhum is a substitute for it, and Ba is related to something omitted, and the meaning is: Because they broke their covenant, We cursed them. Al-Kisa'i said: It is related to what preceded it and the meaning is: So the thunderbolt seized them because of their injustice until His statement Because they broke their covenant He said: So he explained their injustice for which the thunderbolt seized them by what came after it from their breaking their covenant and killing the prophets and what came after it. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari and others denied that, because those who were seized by the thunderbolt were during the time of Moses, and those who killed the prophets and accused Mary of slander were after Moses by a time, so the thunderbolt did not seize all of those who were seized by slander. Al-Mahdawi and others said: This is not necessary because it is permissible to talk about them, and what is meant is their fathers. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that because of their breaking their covenant, We forbade them good things that had been lawful for them, because this story extends to His statement, Then because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them. And their breaking the covenant means that they were required to explain the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that the meaning is: Because of their breaking their covenant and doing such and such, God sealed their hearts. It was said that the meaning is: Because of their breaking, they do not believe except a few. The fa in His statement, So they do not believe is inserted. His statement, And their disbelief in the signs of God is conjoined with what precedes it, and so is His statement, And their killing. What is meant by the signs of God are their books that they distorted, and what is meant by the prophets that they killed is John and Zechariah. Ghulaf is the plural of aghlaf, which means covered with a ghafil: meaning our hearts are in covers so you do not understand what they are saying. It was said: Ghalaf is the plural of ghalaf, and the meaning is: their hearts are vessels for knowledge, so they have no need for knowledge other than what their hearts contain, and it is like their saying our hearts are within coverings, and their purpose with this is to reject the argument of the messengers. His statement, Rather, God has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief, this sentence is parenthetical: meaning, their failure to accept the truth is not because they are covered according to their intended purpose, but rather because of the seal from God upon them. Sealing is the seal, and its meaning was explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. His statement, So they do not believe except a little, means: it is sealed upon them by God because of their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little, or except a little of them like Abdullah bin Salam and those who converted to Islam with him from them.
4:156: And His saying 156- And their disbelief is conjoined with their saying, and the repetition of the preposition occurs because of the separation between the conjoined and the conjoined to, and this repetition is to indicate that they disbelieved disbelief after disbelief, and it was said: What is meant by this disbelief is their disbelief in the Messiah, so it was deleted because what comes after indicates it. His saying And their saying against Mary a great slander is her accusing Joseph the carpenter, and he was one of the righteous. And slander is: the excessive lie that is astonishing.
4:157: His saying 157- "And their saying, 'We have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the Messenger of God'" is connected to what preceded it, and it is among their crimes and transgressions because they lied that they killed him and boasted about killing him and mentioned him as a messenger in mockery, because they deny it and do not acknowledge that he is a prophet, and what they claimed that they killed him included a statement of his description and clarification of his true nature in the Gospel, and what is in it is from the distortion of the Christians: May God distance them, for they lied and God spoke the truth when He said in His Noble Book, "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him" and the sentence is a circumstantial clause: that is, they said that while the reality is that they did not kill him and did not crucify him "but it was made to appear to them that is, his resemblance was cast on someone else, and it was said that they did not know his person and killed the one they killed while they were doubting him and those who differed about him that is, about the matter of Jesus, so some of them said, We killed him, and the one who witnessed his ascension to heaven said, We did not kill him", and it was said that the difference between them is that the Nestorians are Christians They said: Jesus was crucified in terms of his humanity, not in terms of his divinity. The Angelicists said: The killing and crucifixion occurred on Christ in his complete humanity and divinity. They have long statements about this type of difference that have no basis. That is why God said: And those who differ therein are in doubt about it. That is: in hesitation that does not go beyond the realm of correctness, nor into the realm of invalidity in their belief. Rather, they are hesitant and doubtful in their doubt, wandering blindly, and in their ignorance they are perplexed. They have no knowledge thereof except the following of conjecture. “Min” is redundant to emphasize the negation of knowledge, and the exception is disconnected: that is, but they follow conjecture. It was said: it is a substitute for what preceded it. The first is more appropriate. It cannot be said that following conjecture contradicts the doubt that God informed us about them being in, because what is meant here by doubt is hesitation, as we have mentioned, and conjecture is a type of it, and what is meant here by it is not the preference of one side. His saying, And they did not kill him for certain means: a killing for certain, as it is an attribute of a deleted source, or certain, as it is a state. This is based on the pronoun in they killed him referring to Jesus. It was said that it refers to the assumption, and the meaning is: they did not kill their assumption for certain, like you say you killed him with knowledge if you knew him with complete knowledge. Abu Ubaidah said: If the meaning was: and they did not kill Jesus for certain, he would have said only: and they did not kill him, and it was said that the meaning is: and they did not kill him, which was made to seem like it to them. It was said that the meaning is: rather, God raised him up to Himself for certain, and this is a mistake, because what comes after but does not work on what comes before it. Ibn al-Anbari permitted the accusative of certainty with an implied verb that is the answer to an oath, and rather, God raised him up to Himself would be a new statement, and there is no basis for these statements. The pronouns before they killed him and after they killed him refer to Jesus, and the mention of certainty here is intended to mock them to indicate their knowledge in general.
4:158: His saying 158- Rather, God raised him up to Himself is a response to them and proof of what is correct. The mention of his raising up, peace be upon him, has already been mentioned in Al Imran.
4:159: His saying 159- And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. What is meant by the People of the Scripture are the Jews and Christians, and the meaning is: There is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, and the pronoun in him refers to Jesus, and the pronoun in his death refers to what the speech indicates, which is the implied word one or the scriptural indicated by the People of the Scripture, and in it is evidence that no Jew or Christian dies except having believed in the Messiah, and it was said: Both pronouns refer to Jesus, and the meaning is: Jesus will not die until every person of the Scripture in his time believes in him, and it was said: The first pronoun refers to God, and it was said: to Muhammad, and Ibn Jarir chose that the two pronouns refer to Jesus, and a group of the Salaf said this, and this is the apparent meaning, and what is meant is belief in him when he descends at the end of time as the successive hadiths have mentioned. And on the Day of Resurrection Jesus will be over the People of the Scripture a witness testifying against the Jews for their denial of him, and against the Christians for their exaggeration in him until they said he is the son of God. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and said: Moses brought the tablets from God, so bring us the tablets from God so that we may believe you. God revealed: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven to and their saying about Mary is a great slander. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding the verse, he said: The Jews and Christians said to Muhammad (peace be upon him): We will not pledge allegiance to you on what you call us to until you bring us a book from God to so-and-so that you are the Messenger of God and to so-and-so that you are the Messenger of God. God revealed: The People of the Scripture ask you the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Show us God openly, he said: If they have seen Him, then they have seen Him. Rather, they said: Show us God openly. He said: It is brought forward and delayed. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And We raised above them the Mount, he said: It was a mountain where they were at the bottom, so God raised it and made it above them like a canopy, and He said: You must take My command or I will throw it at you, so they said: We will take it, so God withheld it from them. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And their saying against Mary a great slander, he said: They accused her of adultery. And Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When God wanted to raise Jesus to heaven, he went out to his companions and in the house were twelve men from the disciples, so he came out to them from a spring in the house and his head was dripping with water and he said: There is one among you who will disbelieve in Me twelve times after having believed in Me, then He said: Which of you will be cast upon my likeness so that he will be killed in my place and be with me in my degree? Then a young man from the youngest of them stood up and said to him: Sit down. Then he repeated it to them. The young man said: Sit down. Then he repeated it to them. The young man stood up and said: I am. Then he said: You are that. Then he cast the likeness of Jesus upon him, and Jesus was raised in a window in the house to heaven. He said: Then the Jews came to ask for him, so they took the likeness and killed him and crucified him. Some of them disbelieved in him twelve times after they had believed in him, and they split into three groups. One group said: God was with us as He willed, then He ascended to heaven. These are the Jacobites. A group said: The Son of God was with us as He willed, then God raised him to Himself. These are the Nestorians. A group said: God’s servant and messenger was with us, and these are the Muslims. Then the two disbelieving women joined forces against the Muslim woman and killed her. Islam remained obliterated until God sent Muhammad, and God revealed to him: So a party of the Children of Israel believed meaning: the party that believed in the time of Jesus. And a party disbelieved meaning: those who disbelieved in the time of Jesus. So We supported those who believed in the time of Jesus by making Muhammad’s religion prevail over the religion of the disbelievers. Ibn Kathir said after citing it with this wording on the authority of Ibn Abi Hatim: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it. This is a sound chain of transmission back to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Kathir is truthful, so all of these are men of the Sahih. An-Nasa’i reported it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Abu Muawiyah in a similar manner. His story, peace be upon him, has been narrated through different chains of transmission with different wordings, and Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir reported it on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih in a manner similar to what is in the Gospel, and Ibn Al-Mundhir reported it likewise on his authority. Ibn Jarir reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And they did not kill him for certain, he said: They did not kill him for certain. Ibn Al-Mundhir reported something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir reported something similar on the authority of Ibn Juwaybir and As-Suddi. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid and Al-Hakim reported it and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And there is none from the People of the Scripture but will believe in him before his death, he said: The emergence of Jesus, son of Mary. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him through various chains of transmission regarding the verse, he said: Before the death of Jesus. They also narrated from him that he said: Before the death of the Jew. Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said: Some people from the People of the Book will meet Jesus when he is sent and they will believe in him. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from him that he said: “No Jew will ever die until he believes in Jesus. It was said to Ibn Abbas, ‘What do you think if he falls from the top of a house?’ He said, ‘He speaks it in the air.’ It was said, ‘What do you think if one of them is beheaded?’ He said, ‘His tongue will stutter.’” Something similar to this was narrated from him through various chains of transmission, and a group of the Tabi’un said this. Many of the Tabi’un and those who came after them went to the view that what is meant is before the death of Jesus, as was narrated from Ibn Abbas before this, and many of them restricted it to those who meet him when he descends to earth believing in him. The hadiths about the descent of Jesus have been transmitted in succession, as we have explained in an independent book that includes mention of what was reported about the awaited one, the Antichrist and the Messiah.
4:160: The Baa in His statement 160- Fab Zulm is for causality, and the indefiniteness and tanween are for emphasis: meaning, because of a great injustice, We forbade them good things that were lawful for them, not because of anything else as they claimed that they were forbidden to those before them. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a substitute for His statement, Fab Zulm. The good things mentioned are what God, the Most High, stated: And upon those who were Jews, We forbade every clawed animal Al-Anfal 2:160. And because of their turning away themselves and others from the way of God which is following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their distortion and killing of the prophets and the known sins that were turned away from them. His statement, many is the object of the mentioned verb: meaning, because of their turning away many people, or it is an attribute of a deleted source: meaning, turning away many.
4:161: 161- And their taking of usury, although they were forbidden from it, meaning: their dealings with each other based on usury and their eating of it, which was forbidden to them, and their consuming of people’s wealth unjustly, such as bribery and ill-gotten gains, which they used to take.
4:162: His statement 162- But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them is a correction of his statement And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment or of those who are Jews because the Jews denied it and said: These things were originally forbidden and you permit them, so but those firmly rooted was revealed. The firmly rooted is the one who is most steadfast in the knowledge of the Book, and firmness is constancy. We have already discussed this in Al Imran. What is meant is Abdullah bin Salam and Kaab Al Ahbar and others like them. The firmly rooted is the subject, and they believe is its predicate, and the believers are conjoined with the firmly rooted. What is meant by the believers is either those who believed from the People of the Book or from the Muhajireen and Ansar or from all of them. His statement and those who establish prayer Al-Hasan and Malik bin Dinar and a group read and those who establish prayer in conjunction with what preceded it, and this is how it is in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud, and there is a difference in the reason for its being in the accusative case according to the reading of the majority of opinions: The first is the statement of Sibawayh that it is in the accusative case for praise: meaning I mean those who establish. Sibawayh said: This is a chapter on what is in the accusative case for emphasis, including and those who establish prayer. And he recited: Every nation obeyed the command of their master except Namir, who obeyed the command of her seducer. The stabbers who have not yet stabbed anyone, and those who say, Whose palm tree is it? And he recited: Do not distance my people, who are the poison of the enemy and the scourge of the islands. Those who participate in every battle and are good at all times Al-Nahhas said: This is the most correct of what has been said about the residents. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Khalil said: It is conjoined with His statement, In what has been revealed to you. Al-Akhfash said: This is far-fetched because the meaning would be: And they believe in the residents. Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Mubarrad explained that the residents here are the angels, so the meaning would be: They believe in what has been revealed to you and in what was revealed before you and in the angels, and he chose this. It was reported that the accusative case for praise is far-fetched because praise only comes after the completion of the report, and the report of the firmly grounded is His statement, Those - We will give them a great reward. It was said: The residents are conjoined with the pronoun in His statement, From them, and in it it is conjoined with an implied word without repeating the preposition. It was reported from Aisha that she was asked about the residents in this verse and about His statement, Indeed, these two are magicians and about His statement, and the Sabians in Al-Ma’idah? She said: O son of my brother, the scribes made a mistake. It was reported from her by Abu Ubaid in his Fada’il, Sa’id bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir. Abaan bin Othman said: The scribe would dictate to me and I would write, so he wrote: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them and the believers. Then he said: What should I write? He was told: Write: And those who establish prayer. And that is how this happened. It was narrated from him by Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir. Al-Qushayri said: This is false because those who compiled the book were role models in language, so it should not be thought of that. Al-Qushayri is answered by saying that it was narrated from Othman bin Affan that when he finished the Mushaf and it was brought to him, he said: I see in it something of a mistake that the Arabs will correct with their tongues. It was narrated from him by Ibn Abi Dawud through various chains of narration. Many of the imams of grammar and interpretation preferred the statement of Sibawayh, and the statement of Al-Khalil, Al-Kisa’i, Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari, and Al-Qaffal preferred it. According to the statement of Sibawayh, the sentence is parenthetical between the subject and the subject, according to the statement of those who said: The predicate of the firmly rooted is His statement, Those We will give, or between the conjoined and the conjoined to it, if we make the predicate of the firmly rooted believe, and we make His statement, and those who give zakat, conjoined to the believers, not according to the statement of Sibawayh that those who give zakat are raised as a subject or on the assumption of a deleted subject: that is, they are those who give zakat. His statement, and those who believe in God and the Last Day, are the believers among the People of the Book, described first as being firmly rooted in knowledge, then as believing in the Books of God, and that they establish prayer, pay zakat, and believe in God and the Last Day. It was said: What is meant by them are the believers from the Muhajireen and Ansar, as mentioned previously, and that they combine these descriptions, and the reference in His statement, Those We will give a great reward, is to the firmly rooted and what is conjoined to it.
4:163: His statement 163- "Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. This is connected to his statement, The People of the Book ask you." The meaning is that the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is like the matter of the prophets who came before him, so why do you ask him for something that no one else among the contemporaries of the messengers asked for? Revelation is information in secret. It is said: He was revealed to him in speech, revelation, and he revealed, he reveals, and Noah was singled out because he was the first prophet on whose tongue the laws were legislated. Other things have been said. The kaf in his statement, "as", is an attribute of a deleted source, meaning: a revelation like our revelation to Noah, or a state, meaning: We revealed this revelation to you while it is similar to our revelation to Noah. His saying, And We inspired Abraham is connected to We inspired Noah “And Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes” who are the sons of Jacob as mentioned above And Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon He mentioned these specifically after they were included in the term prophets to honor them like His saying, And His angels, His messengers, and Gabriel. He mentioned Jesus before Job and those who came after him even though they were in a time before his time, in response to the Jews who disbelieved in him. Also, the waw is only for the general plural. His saying, And We gave David the Psalms is connected to We inspired. The Psalms is the book of David. Al-Qurtubi said: It is one hundred and fifty surahs in which there is no ruling, nor what is permissible, nor what is forbidden, rather they are rulings and sermons. End quote. I said: It is one hundred and fifty psalms. Psalm: A section that includes the words of David, in which he seeks help from God against his enemies and prays to God against them and seeks His support. Sometimes he gives sermons. He mostly said that in church, and while speaking that, he used some instruments that had beautiful melodies, as is stated in many of those psalms. Al-Zubair: writing. Al-Zabur means Al-Muzbur: meaning written. Like the messenger, the milking, and the riding. Hamza read Zabur with a damma on the zay, the plural of Zabar like fils and fulus. Al-Zabur means Al-Muzbur, and the root of the word is documentation. It is said: a well is mazbura: meaning covered with stones, and the book was called Al-Zabur because of the strength of the documentation in it.
4:164: His saying 164 - And messengers is in the accusative case due to an implied verb that indicates it. We revealed meaning: And we sent messengers. We have told you about them before. It was said: It is in the accusative case due to a verb that indicates it. We told them meaning: And we told you about messengers. Similar to it is what Sibawayh recited: I no longer carry a weapon nor own the camel's head if they attack I fear the wolf if I pass by it alone, and I fear the wind and the rain. Meaning: And I fear the wolf. My father read messengers in the nominative case, assuming that among them are messengers. The meaning of before is that he told them about them before this surah, or before this day. It was said that when God told some of the names of His prophets in His book and did not mention the names of others, the Jews said: Muhammad mentioned the prophets but did not mention Moses, so And God spoke to Moses directly was revealed. The majority read the noble name in the nominative case, meaning that God is the one who spoke to Moses. Al-Nakha’i and Yahya bin Waththab read the noble name in the accusative case, meaning that Moses is the one who spoke to God, the Most High. Dialogue is a confirmed source. The benefit of confirmation is to dispel the notion that speaking is a metaphor, as Al-Farra’ said that the Arabs call what reaches a person speech by any means. It was said: What is not confirmed by the source, then if it is confirmed, it is nothing but the reality of speech. Al-Nahhas said: The grammarians agreed that if you confirm the verb by the source, it is not a metaphor.
4:165: His statement 165- "Messengers, bringing good tidings and warnings" instead of the first messengers, or in the accusative case with an implied verb: i.e. and We sent, or in the state of being messengers as a prelude to what comes after it, or in praise: i.e. bringing good tidings to the people of obedience and warning to the people of disobedience. His statement "so that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers" i.e. an excuse with which they can make an excuse as in the statement of God the Most High: "And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, 'Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could follow Your signs?'" And the excuse was called an argument even though none of the servants had an argument against God, as a reminder that this excuse is acceptable to Him out of His favor and mercy. The meaning of His statement "after the messengers is after sending the messengers, and God is Exalted in Might, no one can overcome Him, Wise" in His actions, which include sending the messengers. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, And they hinder many from the way of God, he said: themselves and others from the truth. Ibn Ishaq narrated in Ad-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them, he said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Salam, Asid bin Shu’bah and Tha’laba bin Shu’bah when they left the Jews and became Muslims. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Ad-Dala’il on his authority that some of the Jews said: O Muhammad, we do not know that God has sent down anything to any human being after Moses, so God revealed, Indeed, We have revealed to you, the verse. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi in Nawader Al-Usul, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, Al-Hakim and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: “I said, O Messenger of God, how many are the prophets? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand. I said: How many are the messengers among them? He said: Three hundred and thirteen, a large group.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, except that he said: And the messengers are three hundred and fifteen.” Abu Ya'la and Al-Hakim narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Among my brothers among the prophets who passed away were eight thousand prophets, then came Jesus, then after him came I." Al-Hakim narrated with a similar weak chain of transmission on the authority of Anas. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "No one is more jealous than God, for that reason He has forbidden indecencies, both apparent and hidden. No one loves praise more than God, for that reason He has praised Himself. No one loves excuses more than God, for that reason He sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners."
4:166: His saying 166- But God bears witness The noble name is the subject and the verb is its predicate, and with the emphasis on the letter nun it is in the accusative case as the name of but and the correction is from an implied omission as if they said: We do not bear witness for you, O Muhammad, to this: meaning the revelation and prophethood, so but God bears witness was revealed. And his saying and the angels bear witness is a clause conjoined to the first clause or a circumstantial clause, and likewise his saying He sent it down with His knowledge is a circumstantial clause: meaning clothed in His knowledge that no one else knows of your being worthy of what God chose you for of prophethood and sent down to you from the Qur'an and sufficient is God as a witness meaning: sufficient is God as a witness and the letter ba is redundant, and the testimony of God, the Exalted, is what He performs of miracles that indicate the truth of prophethood, for the existence of these miracles is a testimony for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the truth of what he informed of this and other things.
4:167: 167- Those who disbelieved in everything that must be believed in, or in this particular matter, which is what is in this case, and barred [people] from the way of God which is the religion of Islam, by denying the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying: We do not find his description in our book, but rather prophethood is in the children of Aaron and David, and by saying: The law of Moses is not abrogated, have certainly gone far astray from the truth by what they did, because with their disbelief they prevented others from the truth.
4:168: 168- Indeed, those who disbelieved by denying and wronged others by preventing them from the path, or wronged Muhammad by concealing his prophethood, or wronged themselves by their disbelief, and it is permissible to interpret all of these meanings God will never forgive them if they persist in their disbelief and die as disbelievers nor will He guide them to a path * except the path of Hell because they committed what would necessitate that for them by their bad choice and extreme misery, and they denied the obvious and opposed the clear.
4:169: 169- They will abide therein forever meaning: He will make them enter Hell, abiding therein forever, and this is a presumed state. His saying forever is in the accusative case as a circumstantial, and it is to eliminate the possibility that eternity here means a long stay. And that meaning: their eternal abode in Hell or the repetition of forgiveness and guidance for them along with their eternal abode in Hell, is easy for God because nothing is difficult for Him, glory be to Him. His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
4:170: 170- So believe, it is better for you. The imams of grammar differed on what the accusative of good is based on? Sibawayh and Al-Khalil said that it is an implied verb: meaning, intend or do what is better for you. Al-Farra' said: It is an adjective for a deleted source: meaning, then believe with a belief that is better for you. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Kisa'i went to the view that it is the predicate of the implied was: meaning, then believe, and belief will be better for you. The strongest of these sayings is the third, then the first, then the second, with a weakness in it. And if you disbelieve meaning: and if you persist in your disbelief, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth of His creations, and you are among them, and whoever is alone with you and them, then He is able to punish you for your ugly actions. So in this sentence there is a warning to them while clarifying the face of the proof and removing the veil from the evidence in a way that requires them to accept and submit. Because they acknowledge that God is their Creator. And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, God.
4:171: His saying 171- O People of the Scripture, do not go to extremes in your religion. Exaggeration: is going beyond the limit. From this, the word price went to extremes means to go to extremes, and the word man went to extremes means to go to extremes in a matter, and the word girl went to extremes means to go to extremes in regard to her flesh and bones if she hastened her youth and exceeded her sexual desires. What is meant by the verse is to forbid them from going to extremes sometimes and from being negligent at other times. Among the extremes is the exaggeration of the Christians regarding Jesus until they made him a god, and among the negligence is the exaggeration of the Jews regarding him, peace be upon him, until they made him not righteous. How beautiful is the saying of the poet: Do not go to extremes in anything and be moderate. Both sides of the matter are reprehensible.
