And do not say about God except the truth, which is what He described Himself and His messengers described Him with. Do not say falsehood, such as the Jews saying, Ezra is the son of God, and the Christians saying, The Messiah is the son of God. “The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, is only the Messenger of God.” The Messiah is the subject and Jesus is a substitute for him, and the son of Mary is an attribute of Jesus, and the Messenger of God is the predicate. It is possible that Jesus, the son of Mary, is an explanatory apposition, and the sentence is an explanation of the prohibition. We have already discussed the Messiah in Al Imran. His statement, and His word, is an apposition to the Messenger of God, and He cast it into Mary is a state, meaning that he was by His statement, Be, and he was a human being without a father. It was said, His word is the good report of God to Mary and His message to her on the tongue of Jibreen in His statement, “When the angels said, ‘O Mary, God gives you good tidings of a word from Him. ’” It was said that the word here means a sign, and from it is and she believed in the words of her Lord, and His statement, the words of God have not been exhausted. His saying, and a spirit from Him, meaning: He sends Gabriel and he blows into Mary’s armour and she becomes pregnant by God’s permission. This addition is for preference, even though all spirits are from His creation, the Most High. It has been said that the one from whom amazing things appear may be called a spirit and it is added to God, so it is said that this is a spirit from God, meaning from His creation, just as it is said about a blessing that it is from God. It has been said, a spirit from Him, meaning from His creation, as God the Most High said, And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him, meaning from His creation. It has been said, a spirit from Him, meaning a mercy from Him. It has been said, a spirit from Him, meaning a proof from Him, and Jesus was a proof and an argument against his people. His saying, from Him is related to something omitted that is an attribute of the spirit, meaning: it is from Him and the spirit was made from Him, glory be to Him, even though it was by Gabriel’s breathing, because He, glory be to Him, is the one who commanded Gabriel to breathe. So believe in God and His messengers, meaning: that He, glory be to Him, is one God who did not give birth and was not born, and there is none comparable to Him, and that His messengers are truthful, conveying from God what He commanded them to convey, and do not deny them and do not go to extremes regarding them, making some of them gods. His saying, And do not say three, the raising of three as the predicate of a deleted subject. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, do not say our gods are three. Al-Farra’ and Abu Ubaid said: That is, do not say they are three, like his saying, They will say three. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: Do not say he is the third of three. So the subject and the complement were deleted. The Christians, despite the dispersion of their doctrines, agree on the Trinity, and by three they mean the three hypostases, so they make Him, glory be to Him, one essence with three hypostases. They mean by the hypostases the hypostasis of existence, the hypostasis of life, and the hypostasis of knowledge. They may express the hypostases as the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, so by the Father they mean existence, by the Spirit life, and by the Son Christ. It was said: What is meant by the three gods is God, glory be to Him, Mary, and Christ. The Christians have been confused about this for a long time. We have come across in the four Gospels, which they call the Gospel, many differences in Jesus: sometimes he is described as the son of man, sometimes he is described as the son of God, and sometimes he is described as the son of God. This is a clear contradiction and a manipulation of religion. The truth is what God has told us in the Qur’an, and whatever contradicts it in the Torah, the Gospel, or the Psalms is from the distortion of distorters and the manipulation of the manipulation. One of the most amazing things we have seen is that each of the four Gospels is attributed to one of the companions of Jesus, peace be upon him. The gist of all of them is that each of these four mentioned the biography of Jesus from the time God sent him until He raised him up to Him, and mentioned the miracles that happened to him and the appeals to the Jews and the like, so their words differed, but their meanings agreed, and some of them might add to others according to what is required by preservation and accuracy, and mentioned what Jesus said and what was said to him, and there is nothing in them from the words of God Almighty, nor was a book sent down to Jesus from Him, rather Jesus, peace be upon him, used to argue with them with what is in the Torah and mention that he did not come with anything that contradicts it, and so is the Psalms, for from its beginning to its end it is from the words of David, peace be upon him. The words of God are more truthful, and His book is more true, and He informed us that the Gospel is His book that He sent down to His servant and Messenger Jesus, son of Mary, and that the Psalms is His book that He gave to David and sent down to him. His saying, Stop, it is better for you, means: Stop the Trinity, and the accusative of it is better for you here has the three aspects that were mentioned in His saying, Then believe, it is better for you. “God is only one God,” He has no partner, no companion, and no son. Glory be to Him that He should have a son, that is, I glorify Him with a glorification that He should not have a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and what you have made for Him a partner or a son is part of that, and the created slave cannot have a partner or a son. And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs, for all creation, their affairs are up to Him, and they do not possess for themselves any harm or benefit. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: "A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to them: By God, I know that you know that I am the Messenger of God. They said: We do not know that. So God revealed: "But God bears witness the verse. Abd Ibn Hamid, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Abu Musa that Al-Najashi said to Ja'far: What does your companion say about the son of Mary? He said: He says about him that the word of God is the spirit of God and His word, He brought him forth from the virgin, and no human being touched her. So he took a stick from the ground and raised it and said: O group of priests and monks, these people do not say more than what you say about the son of Mary, it does not weigh this. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Ad-Dala'il on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud at a longer length than this. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not exaggerate about me as the Christians exaggerated about Jesus, son of Mary, for I am only a servant, so say the servant of God and His Messenger.
4:172: The root of the verb istankaf is nakaf and the rest of the letters are redundant. It is said: nakaf from something, istankaf from it, and ankaftuhu meaning you cleared it of what it is that it is that it is that it is that which... is that which it is that is that is that is that which it is that is that is that is that is that which it is that is that is that is that is that which it is that is that is that is that is that which it is that is that is that is that is that which it is that is that is that is that is that which it is that is that is that is that is that which it is that is that is that is that is Those who say that angels are superior to prophets have used this as evidence, and the author of Al-Kashshaf decided on the evidence with something that is neither fattening nor satisfying, and he claimed that taste is the judge of that, and the best of Arab tastes is when it is mixed with love of doctrine and mixed with impurities of rigidity, and everyone who understands the language of the Arabs knows that whoever says that neither an imam nor a follower, nor a great nor a small, nor a noble nor a lowly person, does not disdain this statement. Then this indicates that the conjoined is of greater importance than the conjoined to it, and in any case, how bad is the preoccupation with this issue, and how little its benefit is, and how far it is from being a center of religious legal centers and a bridge from bridges. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant meaning: disdains arrogantly and prepares himself for worship, He will gather them all together to Himself the disdainful and others, and He will reward each according to his deeds. He left out mentioning others who disdain here because the beginning of the speech indicates it, and because the gathering is for both groups.
4:173: 173- As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full, without missing out on anything from them. But as for those who disdain and are arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, because of their disdain and arrogance. And they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper.
4:174: His saying 174- O mankind, there has come to you a proof from your Lord in what He sent down to you of His books and in whom He sent to you of His messengers, and what He established for them of miracles. Proof is what proves what is sought And We sent down to you a clear light which is the Qur’an, and He called it a light because it guides people from the darkness of misguidance.
4:175: 175- But as for those who have believed in God and held fast to Him meaning: in God, and it was said: in the mentioned light He will admit them to mercy from Him with which He will have mercy on them and bounty with which He will bestow upon them and guide them to Himself meaning: to comply with what He has commanded and avoid what He has forbidden, or to Him, glory be to Him, in consideration of their destiny to His reward and bounty a straight path meaning: a path that they follow to Him, straight and without crookedness, which is adherence to the religion of Islam and abandoning other religions. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: The ha' in His statement to Him refers to what came before of the name of God, and it was said: it refers to the Qur'an, and it was said: to bounty, and it was said: to mercy and bounty because they mean reward. The accusative of a path is that it is a second object of the mentioned verb, and it was said: in the state of the state. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said, The Messiah will not be disdainful means he will not be arrogant. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym in al-Hilyah and al-Isma’ili in his Mu’jam narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said regarding His statement, Then He will give them their rewards and increase them from His bounty, he said: Their rewards will admit them into Paradise and He will increase them from His bounty the intercession for those who are destined for Hell from those who did good to them in this world. Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir and said: Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Baqiyyah on the authority of Ismail ibn Abdullah al-Kindi on the authority of al-A’mash on the authority of Shaqiq on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud and he mentioned it and said: This chain of transmission is not proven, and if it is narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud as a mursal, then it is good. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah, There has come to you a proof, meaning: a clear evidence, and We have sent down to you a clear light, he said: This is the Qur’an. They also narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: A proof is an argument. They also narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, And hold fast to it, he said: The Qur’an.
4:176: The discussion of Kalalah has already been presented at the beginning of this Surah, and the intended mufti will be mentioned in His statement 176- They ask you for a legal opinion. His statement If a man dies means: If a man dies, as was previously stated in His statement And if a woman fears. His statement He has no child is either an attribute of a man or a state, and there is no reason to prevent it from being a state. A child is used for both males and females, and it was limited to the absence of a child here, although the absence of a parent is considered in Kalalah, relying on the appearance of that. It was said: What is meant by the child here is the son, and it is one of the two meanings of the common denominator, because a daughter does not exclude a sister. His statement And he has a sister is in apposition to his statement He has no child. What is meant by the sister here is the sister from both parents or from the father, not from the mother, so her share is one-sixth, as mentioned previously. The majority of scholars from the Companions and the Followers and those after them held that sisters from both parents or from the father are agnates for daughters even if there is no brother with them. Ibn Abbas said that sisters do not agnatic kinship with daughters, and Dawud al-Dhahiri and a group agreed with him and said: There is no inheritance for a sister from both parents or from a father with a daughter, and they argued with the apparent meaning of this verse, as it made the absence of a child that includes both males and females a condition for the sister’s inheritance, and this is a correct argument if there was no evidence in the Sunnah indicating the establishment of the sister’s inheritance with the daughter, which is what was proven in the Sahih that Muadh ruled during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a daughter and a sister, so he gave the daughter half and the sister half. It was also proven in the Sahih that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled regarding a daughter, a daughter of a son, and a sister, so he gave the daughter half and the daughter of the son one-sixth and the sister the remainder.” So this Sunnah required interpreting the son as the son and not the daughter. His saying, And he inherits her, meaning a man inherits her: meaning he inherits the sister if she has no son. It was mentioned that what was meant by his inheriting her was his possession of all that she left behind. If what was meant was the establishment of his inheritance for him in general, more generally than it being all or part, then it is correct to interpret the son as including the male and the female. And the Almighty limited himself in this verse to negating the son, even though the father excludes the brother just as the male son excludes him, because what was meant here was to clarify the rights of the brother with the son only. As for its being dropped with the father, it has been made clear by the Sunnah as it was established in the Sahih from his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Give the obligatory shares to those entitled to them, and whatever remains is for the closest male relative, and the father is more deserving than the brother. If there are two, that is, if those who inherit by brotherhood are two, and the conjunction is based on the previous conditional and the feminine and dual, and likewise the plural in his saying, And if they are brothers, considering the report, then for them are two-thirds of what he leaves, if the person does not have a child as mentioned previously, and more than two sisters, they are entitled to two-thirds by priority. And if they are, that is, those who inherit by brotherhood, brothers, men and women, that is, mixed males and females, then for the male among them is like the share of two females, by way of agnatic relationship. God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, that is, He makes clear to you the ruling on the kalalah and all other rulings, out of concern that you go astray. This is how Al-Qurtubi narrated it from the Basrans. Al-Kisa’i said: The meaning is so that you do not go astray. Al-Farra’ and other Kufians agreed with him. And God is All-Knowing of everything of the things that include these mentioned rulings. That is, He is All-Knowing. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, the Sunan scholars and others narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me while I was sick and out of my mind. He performed ablution and poured water over me and I regained my senses. I said: ‘None inherit from me except those who are not related to me, so how is the inheritance?’ Then the verse of inheritance was revealed.” Ibn Sa’d and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on his authority with the wording: It was revealed in “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not related to me.” Ibn Rahawayh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of ‘Umar that he asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): How do those who are not related to me inherit? Then God revealed “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not related to me.” Malik, Muslim, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of ‘Umar who said: “I did not ask the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about anything more than I asked him about those who are not related to me until he poked my chest with his finger and said: ‘The verse of summer at the end of Surat An-Nisa’ is not sufficient for you.” Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib who said: “A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him about kalalah. He said: ‘The verse of summer is sufficient for you.’” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of ‘Umar who said: “There are three things I wish the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had enjoined upon us so that we could adhere to them: the grandfather, kalalah, and some of the types of usury.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib who said: “The last surah to be revealed in its entirety was Bara’ah, and the last verse to be revealed was the final verse of Surat An-Nisa’: ‘They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning kalalah.’” ‘Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin who said: “When ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab would recite: ‘God makes clear to you, lest you go astray,’ he would say: ‘O God, to whom You have made kalalah clear but You have not made it clear to me.’” We have explained the discussion, disagreement, evidence and preference regarding the issue of kalalah at the beginning of this surah, so we will not repeat it. And here ends the first part of the blessed interpretation: called Fath al-Qadir, which combines the two arts of narration and knowledge of the science of interpretation, written by its author, who hopes that his Lord, the Most High, will help him complete it, and benefit from it whomever He wills of His servants, and make it a treasure for him when he arrives in the afterlife, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad al-Shawkani, may God forgive them both. And the end of this place was on the day of the greatest feast, the blessed day of sacrifice in the year two thousand two hundred and twenty-four after the Prophet’s migration, praising God and praying and sending peace upon His Messenger and beloved Muhammad ibn Abdullah and upon his family and companions. End quote. Praise be to Him: He completed his efforts, praise be to God, in the month of Dhul-Qi’dah in the year 1232. Yahya bin Ali Al-Shawkani.
5:1: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Al-Qurtubi said: It is Madani by consensus. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: Al-Ma’idah is Madani. Ahmad, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr who said: I performed Hajj and entered upon Aisha, and she said to me: O Jubayr, do you recite Al-Ma’idah? I said: Yes. She said: It is the last Surah to be revealed, so whatever you find in it that is permissible, then regard it as permissible, and whatever you find that is forbidden, then regard it as forbidden. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar who said: The last Surah to be revealed were Surah Al-Ma’idah and Al-Fath. Ahmad narrated on his authority that he said: Surah Al-Ma’idah was revealed to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) while he was riding his mount and it could not carry him, so he got off it. Ibn Kathir said: Ahmad is the only one who narrated it. I said: In its chain of transmission is Ibn Lahi'ah, and Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Muhammad ibn Nasr in the Book of Prayer, al-Tabarani, Abu Nu'aym in al-Dala'il, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated something similar on the authority of Asma' bint Yazid. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar in his Musnad, al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Dalail al-Nubuwwah on the authority of Umm Amr bint Isa on the authority of her uncle. Abu Ubayd narrated something similar on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi. He added that it was revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage between Mecca and Medina. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of al-Rabi' ibn Anas with this addition. Abu Ubayd narrated on the authority of Damrah ibn Habib and Atiyah ibn Qays, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Al-Ma'idah is among the last revelations of the Qur'an, so make lawful what is lawful in it and make unlawful what is unlawful in it. Abu Dawud and al-Nahhas both narrated in al-Naskh on the authority of Abu Maysarah Amr ibn Shurahbil, who said: Nothing of al-Ma'idah was abrogated. Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on his authority. And likewise it was narrated by Abd ibn Hamid, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir on the authority of al-Sha’bi. And likewise it was narrated by Abd ibn Hamid, Abu Dawud in his Naskh and Ibn al-Mundhir on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri. And Abd ibn Hamid, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Sha’bi who said: Nothing was abrogated from al-Ma’idah except this verse: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month or the offerings or the garlands. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Two verses of this Surah were abrogated: the verse of the necklaces and His statement: But if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them. Abd bin Hamid narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surat Al-Ma’idah and At-Tawbah in his sermon. Al-Naqqash mentioned on the authority of Abu Salamah that he said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Al-Hudaybiyah, he said: O Ali, did you know that Surat Al-Ma’idah was revealed to me? What a great benefit.” Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is a fabricated hadith and it is not permissible for a Muslim to believe it. Ibn Atiyyah said: In my opinion, this does not resemble the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This verse with which God opened this Surah until His saying: 1- God decrees what He wills contains eloquence that human powers fall short of, despite its comprehensiveness of several rulings: including fulfilling contracts, and the permissibility of the animals of livestock, and the exception of what will be recited from what is not permissible, and the prohibition of hunting for the pilgrim, and the permissibility of hunting for the one who is not in the pilgrim. Al-Naqqash narrated that the companions of the philosopher Al-Kindi said to him: O wise man, make for us something like this Qur’an, so he said: Yes, make something like some of it, so he hid for many days and then came out and said: By God, I am not able and no one can bear this, I opened the Qur’an and Surah Al-Ma’idah came out, so I looked and saw that it had spoken of fulfillment and forbade breaking it, and permitted a general permissibility, then made an exception after an exception, then informed about His power and wisdom in two lines, and no one can do this. His saying: Fulfill contracts It is said: awfa and fafa are two languages, and the poet combined them and said: As for Ibn Tauf, he fulfilled his duty as he fulfilled the duty of the camels of the star driver. Contracts: and covenants. The origin of contracts is ties, the singular of which is aqd. It is said: I tied the rope and the covenant. It is used for bodies and meanings. If it is used for meanings as here, it indicates that it is very tight and strong in its documentation. It was said: What is meant by contracts are those that God made with His servants and obligated them to follow in terms of rulings. It was also said that they are the contracts that they make among themselves from the contracts of transactions. The first is that the verse includes both matters, and there is no reason to specify some of them without others. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: Fulfill God’s contract upon you and your contract with each other. The contract that must be fulfilled is that which is in accordance with the Book of God and the Sunnah of the Messenger of God. If it contradicts them, then it is rejected and it is not necessary to fulfill it and it is not permissible. His statement: Lawful to you are the beasts of cattle is addressed to those who believe. Beast: is the name of every four-legged animal. It was named thus because of its ambiguity due to the deficiency of its speech, understanding, and mind. From this comes the word babahm meaning closed, and nail night, and bahmah for the brave man who does not know where he will be approached, and halaqah mubhamah meaning he does not know where its two ends are. Al-An'am: is the name for camels, cows and sheep. It was named thus because of the softness of their gait. It was also said that the beast of the cattle is the wild ones such as gazelles, wild cows, wild donkeys and others. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari on the authority of some people, and others narrated it on the authority of al-Suddi, al-Rabi', Qatadah and al-Dahhak. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is a good statement, because the cattle are the eight pairs, and what is added to them from the rest of the animals is called the cattle grouped with them, and it is as if the predator is like the lion, and every fanged animal is outside the limits of the cattle, so the beast of the cattle is the grazer among the quadrupeds. It was also said that the beast of the cattle is what is not game, because the game is called a wild animal and not a beast. It was also said that the beast of the cattle is the fetuses that come out of the bellies of the cattle when slaughtered, so they are eaten without slaughtering. According to the first opinion, I mean specifying livestock as camels, cows and sheep, the addition is explanatory, and what is permissible outside of them is included with it by analogy, and even by the texts in the Qur’an and Sunnah, such as the Almighty’s saying: “Say: I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it, unless it be dead” (al-Baqarah 2:17), and the Prophet’s saying: Every beast with fangs and talons is forbidden (al-Baqarah 2:17), for it indicates by its implication that everything else is permissible, and so are all the texts specific to a type as in the books of the pure Sunnah. His saying: Except what is recited to you is an exception to his saying: Lawful to you are the beast of cattle meaning except what is implied by what is recited to you, for it is not permissible. What is recited is what God has explicitly forbidden, such as His saying: Forbidden to you are dead animals (al-Baqarah 2:17), and what is explicitly forbidden by the Sunnah is included with it. This exception may mean that what is recited to you is only what is recited to you now, or it may mean that what is in the future, indicating the permissibility of delaying the explanation beyond the time of need, and both possibilities are possible. His saying: Except for what is recited to you The Basrans said that his saying: Except for what is recited to you is an exception from the cattle and his saying: Except for what is not locally hunted is another exception from it as well, so both exceptions are from the cattle, and the meaning is: The cattle have been made lawful for you except for what is recited to you except hunting and you are deprived, and it was said: The first exception is from the cattle, and the second exception is from the first exception, and it was responded that this necessitates the permissibility of hunting in the state of ihram, because it is an exception from the forbidden and so it is permissible, and Al-Farra’ permitted Except for what is recited to be in the place of raising as a substitute, and the Basrans do not permit it except in the indefinite and what is close to it from the types. He said: And the accusative of Except for what is not locally hunted is in the state of his saying: Fulfill the contracts and so said Al-Akhfash, and others said: A state of the Kaf and Meem in for you and the meaning is: The cattle have been made lawful for you except for the cattle, except for what is not locally hunted: meaning hunting in the land and eating its hunt. The meaning of not making it permissible for them is to confirm its prohibition in action and belief, and they are in a state of ihram: that is, they are deprived. The phrase and you are in a state of ihram is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in my place. The meaning of this restriction is clear to those who limit the beast of livestock to wild wild animals whose eating is permissible, as if he said: hunting on the land is permissible for you except in the state of ihram. As for those who make the addition explanatory, the meaning is: I have made permissible for you an animal, which is the livestock, while hunting is forbidden to you by entering into ihram because you are in need of that. So what is meant by this restriction is to show them gratitude by making permissible what is other than what is forbidden to them in that state. What is meant by the sacred is the one who is in a state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah or both, and it is called a sacred because hunting, perfume, and women are forbidden to him. This is the reason why the sacred is called a sacred place, and the state of ihram is ihram. Al-Hasan, Al-Nakha’i, and Yahya ibn Waththab read it as sacred with a silent ra and it is a Tamimi dialect, they say in the word rusul “rusul” and in the word kutub “kutub” and the like. His saying: God rules as He wills is one of the rulings that contradict what the Arabs were accustomed to, as He is the owner of everything, He does what He wills and rules as He wants, and there is no one to question His ruling.
5:2: His saying: 2- O you who have believed, do not violate the symbols of God. The symbols: the plural of a symbol, with the weight of fa'ila. Ibn Faris said: The singular is called: symbol, which is better, and from it is the notarization of the sacrificial animal. The monuments: the landmarks, the singular of which is a symbol, and they are the places that have been notified with signs. It was said that what is meant by them here is all the rituals of Hajj: and it was said that it is Safa and Marwa, the sacrificial animal, and the buildings. The meaning according to these two sayings: Do not violate these matters by neglecting any of them or by preventing them from being done by those who want to do them. The Almighty mentioned the prohibition of violating the symbols of God after mentioning the prohibition of hunting in the state of ihram. It was said that what is meant by the symbols here are the duties of God, and from it is and whoever honors the symbols of God, and it was said that they are the sacred things of God, and there is no objection to applying that to everyone, considering the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason, nor what the context indicates. His statement: nor the sacred month means the genus, so all the sacred months are included in that, which are four: Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab. That is, do not violate them by fighting in them. It was said that what is meant here is the month of Hajj only. His statement: nor the sacrificial animal is what is offered to the House of God from a camel, cow, or sheep, the singular being a hadiyyah. God Almighty forbade them from violating the sanctity of the sacrificial animal by taking it from its owner or preventing him from the place to which it is offered. The hadiy was linked to the rituals while being included under them in order to draw attention to its further specificity and to emphasize its matter. His statement: nor the necklaces is the plural of necklace, which is what the sacrificial animal is worn with, such as a sandal or the like. And its replacement by taking it by force, and in the prohibition of replacing necklaces there is an emphasis on the prohibition of replacing the sacrificial animal, and it was said that what is meant by necklaces are the ones hung with it, and its conjunction with the sacrificial animal is to increase the recommendation of the sacrificial animal, and the first is more appropriate, and it was said that what is meant by necklaces is what people used to wear as a security for themselves, so it is on the deletion of an added word: that is, and for the owners of the necklaces. His saying: nor those who are at the Sacred House meaning those who intend it from their saying I intended such-and-such: that is, I intended it. Al-A’mash read: nor those who are at the Sacred House with the addition. Meaning: Do not prevent those who intend to go to the Sacred House for Hajj or Umrah or to live there. It was said that the reason for the revelation of this verse was that the polytheists were performing Hajj and Umrah and offering sacrifices, and the Muslims wanted to attack them, so the following was revealed: O you who believe! Do not violate the rites of God to the end of the verse. This was abrogated by His statement: Kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and His statement: So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year, and His statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year. Some people said: The verse is decisive and it applies to the Muslims. His statement: They seek bounty from their Lord and approval is a circumstantial clause of the hidden pronoun in Ameen. The majority of commentators said: Its meaning is that they seek bounty and profits in trade, and they seek along with that the approval of God. It was said that some of them sought trade, and some of them sought the approval of God through Hajj, and this seeking of approval was according to their belief and in their opinion according to those who made the verse about the polytheists. It was said that what is meant by bounty here is the reward, not the profits in trade. His statement: And when you are in a state of ihram, hunt is an explicit statement of what is indicated by the concept of while you are in a state of ihram. He permitted them to hunt after He had prohibited it to them because the reason for which it was prohibited had disappeared, which was ihram. His saying: And let not the hatred of a people incite you to do so. Ibn Faris said: Jarama and Ajram and La Jarama mean what you say there is no escape nor inevitable. Its origin is from Jaram, meaning to gain. It was said that the meaning is: Do not let it make you bear it. Al-Kisa’i and Tha’lab said that it is transitive and takes two objects. It is said: Khada made me bear such-and-such in your hatred, meaning it made me bear it. From this is the saying of the poet: I stabbed Abu Uyaynah with a stab that made Fazara angry after that. That is, he made them angry. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of “do not let the hatred of a people cause you to transgress from truth to falsehood, justice to injustice and crime. The criminal means the gainer, and from this is the saying of the poet: A crime is committed against a weak-willed person who sees a cross for the bones he has collected. It means earning a living. The cross means your love, and from it the saying of another: O you who complain about Akl and what you have done to the tribes of killing and despair Any earned, and the meaning of the verse: Do not let the hatred of a people lead you to transgress against them, or do not let their hatred lead you to transgress against the truth into falsehood. It is said: Jarama yajriman: if he cuts off. Ali bin Isa Al-Rummani said: This is the original, so Jarama means to carry on something to cut it off from something else, and Jarama means to gain because it is cut off to earning, and La Jarama means Haqq because the truth is cut off from it. Al-Khalil said: The meaning of “La Jarama an lahum al-Nair” is that it is true that they will have the Fire. Al-Kisa’i said: Jarama and Ajram are two languages with one meaning: i.e. acquired. Ibn Mas’ud read: La yujrimnakum with a damma on the ya’, and the meaning is: do not make you gain, and the Basrans do not know Jarama, but they say Jarama and nothing else. Hatred: hatred. It is read with a fatha on the noon and a sukoon on it, it is said: Shanayt al-rajul ashnuhu shana’, masha’at and shananan all of that: if you hated him, and shanan here is added to the object: i.e. the hatred of a people from you, not the hatred of a people for you. His saying: that they turned you away with the opening of the hamza is an object for which: i.e. because they turned you away. Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read with the breaking of the hamza on the conditional, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid, and Al-A'mash read: that they turn you away and the meaning on the conditional reading: do not let their hatred for you if they turn you away from the Sacred Mosque lead you to attack them. An-Nahhas said: As for if they turned you away with the breaking of if, the great scholars of grammar, hadith and theory forbid reading it with it for several reasons: one of them is that the verse was revealed in the year of the conquest in the year eight, and the polytheists turned away the believers in the year of Hudaybiyyah in the year six, so the turning away was before the verse, and if it is read with the breaking it is not permissible for it to be except after it, as you say: Do not give so-and-so anything if he fights you, so this can only be for the future, and if it is opened it is for the past, and how beautiful this speech is. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaidah rejected Shan'an with the sukoon of the noon, because the sources only come in such a case with a vowel, and others disagreed with them and said: This is not a source, but rather an active participle on the weight of kaslan and ghadhban. When He forbade them from transgression, He ordered them to cooperate in righteousness and piety, whatever it may be. It was said that righteousness and piety are two words for one meaning, and it was repeated for emphasis. Ibn Atiyyah said: Righteousness includes what is obligatory and recommended, while piety is specific to what is obligatory. Al-Mawardi said: In righteousness is the pleasure of people, and in piety is the pleasure of God, so whoever combines both, his happiness is complete. Then He, the Almighty, forbade them from cooperating in sin and aggression. Sin is every action or saying that necessitates the sin of its doer or speaker, and aggression is transgressing against people in a way that involves injustice. There remains no type of what necessitates sin or any type of injustice to people, including the self, that is not included in this prohibition, because these two types apply to everything that has their meaning. Then He ordered His servants to be pious and threatened whoever disobeys what He commanded and leaves it, or disobeys what He forbade and does it, saying: Indeed, God is severe in penalty. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Fulfill contracts, he said: What God has permitted, what He has forbidden, what He has imposed, and what He has set in the entire Qur'an, do not betray or break it. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd Bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: They are the contracts of the Age of Ignorance, the oath. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: And fulfill the contracts of the Age of Ignorance, and do not introduce a contract into Islam. Abd Bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: Lawful to you are the beasts of cattle, he said: Camels, cows and sheep. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement: Lawful to you are the beasts of cattle, he said: What is in their bellies. I said: If it comes out dead, can I eat it? He said: Yes. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab al-Iman narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Except what is recited to you, he said: Dead animals, blood, pork, and that which has been dedicated to other than God, to the end of the verse. This is what God has forbidden of livestock. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Do not violate the rites of God, he said: The polytheists used to perform Hajj to the Sacred House, offer gifts, honor the sanctity of the sacred sites, and slaughter during their Hajj. The Muslims wanted to attack them, so God said: Do not violate the rites of God. And in His statement: nor the sacred month, meaning: do not permit fighting in it. nor those who are near the Sacred House, meaning: whoever faces the Sacred House. So the believers and polytheists used to perform Hajj together. So God forbade the believers from preventing anyone from performing Hajj to the House or interfering with anyone, whether a believer or a disbeliever. Then God revealed after this verse: The polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. And in His statement: seek bounty, meaning that they please God with their Hajj. And let not the hatred of a people incite you, meaning: the enmity of a people. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, he said: Righteousness is what I have commanded, and piety is what I have forbidden. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: The symbols of God are what God has forbidden you to do while you are in a state of ihram, and the sacrificial animal is what is not adorned with necklaces, and necklaces are the adornments of the sacrificial animal. Nor those who are at the Sacred House, he said: Those who set out on pilgrimage. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement, Do not violate the symbols of God, he said: The rituals of Hajj. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was at Al-Hudaibiyah and his companions when the polytheists prevented them from entering the House, and that was difficult for them. Some polytheists from the East passed by them wanting to perform Umrah, so the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We will prevent these people as our companions prevented us, so God revealed: “And let not the sinners” al-Bukhari and Muslim. Ahmad, Abd bin Humaid and Al-Bukhari narrated in his history on the authority of Wabisah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Righteousness is that which the heart finds reassurance in and the soul finds reassurance in, and sin is that which troubles the heart and causes hesitation in the chest, even if people give you a fatwa and issue a fatwa.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an who said: I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about righteousness and sin. He said: Righteousness is good character, and sin is that which troubles you in your soul and you would hate for people to know about. Ahmad, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Hibban, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that a man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about sin. He said: Whatever troubles you in your soul, leave it. He said: What is faith? He said: Whoever is upset by his bad deed and pleased by his good deed is a believer.
5:3: This is a start to the prohibitions that God the Almighty referred to in His saying: Except what is recited to you. The dead animal has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, as well as blood, pork, and that which has been sacrificed to other than God. The prohibition of blood in general here is restricted to it being spilled, as previously mentioned, by applying the general to the restricted. The specification of dead animal has been mentioned in the Sunnah in the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Two dead animals and two types of blood have been made lawful for us. As for the two dead animals, they are fish and locusts, and as for the two types of blood, they are the liver and the spleen." Narrated by Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ibn Majah, Al-Daraqutni, and Al-Bayhaqi. It is said in its chain of transmission, and it is strengthened by the hadith: Its water is pure and its dead animal is lawful. It is narrated by Ahmad, the people of Sunan, and others, and a group of them, including Ibn Khuzaymah and Ibn Hibban, have authenticated it. We have discussed it at length in our commentary on Al-Muntaqa. And the declaration of Ihlil is raising the voice to other than God, such as saying: In the name of Al-Lat and Al-Uzza and the like. We do not need here to repeat what we have mentioned before, as it contains what the observer does not need anything else. 3- The strangled is the one who dies by strangulation: which is the holding of the breath, whether that was done by her own action, such as putting her head in a rope or between two sticks, or by human action or otherwise. The people of the Jahiliyyah used to strangle the sheep, and when it died, they would eat it. The beaten is the one who is struck with a stone or stick until it dies without being slaughtered. It is said: Waqdhah yaqdhah waqdhaan so he is waqidh, and waqid is the severity of the beating, and so-and-so is waqidh meaning severely beaten. The people of the Jahiliyyah used to do that, they would beat the livestock with wood for their gods until they died and then they would eat them. From this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: A bush that kicks the faction with its foot, a scavenger hunt for the prey of the claws Ibn Abd al-Barr said: The scholars, both ancient and modern, differed about hunting with guns, stones and mu'arad. By gun, he means the bow of a gun, and by mu'arad, he means an arrow without feathers or a stick with a pointed tip. He said: Whoever went to it as waqeedh, it is not permissible for him to hunt with it except what he caught during slaughter, according to what was narrated from Ibn Umar, and it is the opinion of Malik, Abu Hanifa and his companions, al-Thawri and al-Shafi'i, and the people of Sham disagreed with them on that. Al-Awza'i said about al-Mu'aradh: It is all pierced or not pierced, as Abu al-Darda', Fadalah ibn Ubayd, Abdullah ibn Umar and Makhul did not see anything wrong with it. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: This is what al-Awza'i narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar, and what is known from Ibn Umar is what Malik narrated from Nafi'. He said: The basic principle in this matter, and what is practiced and in which there is evidence, is the hadith of Adi ibn Hatim, in which it says: Whatever is hit by its side, do not eat, for it is waqeedh. End quote. I said: The hadith is in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Adi who said: “I said, O Messenger of God, I shoot with a spear at game and I hit it. He said: If you shoot with a spear and it pierces it, then eat it. But if it hits its side, then it is a dead animal, so do not eat it.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) considered the piercing and the lack thereof. The truth is that only that which is pierced is permissible, not that which is struck. So it is necessary to slaughter it before death, otherwise it is a dead animal. As for the rifles known today, which are iron rifles in which gunpowder and lead are put and shot, the scholars did not discuss them because of the delay in their development. They did not reach the lands of Yemen until the tenth century AH. A group of scholars asked me about hunting with them if it dies and the hunter is unable to slaughter it alive. What appears to me is that it is permissible because it pierces and usually enters from one side and exits from the other. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the previous authentic hadith: If you shoot with a spear and it pierces it, then eat it. So the piercing is considered in making the game permissible. His saying: “And the one who falls from a height to a bottom and dies, without any difference between falling from a mountain, a well, a grave, or something else. Falling is taken from the word “rady,” which means destruction, whether it falls by itself or someone else returns it. His saying: And the one who is gored is fa’ilah in the sense of maf’ulah, and it is the one who is gored by another and dies without being slaughtered. Some people also said: fa’ilah in the sense of fa’ilah, because two animals butt heads and die. He said: natihah and did not say natih, although it is the analogy of fa’il, because the necessity of deletion is specific to what is from this category as an attribute of a mentioned described thing. If it is not mentioned, the ta’ is maintained to transfer from the descriptive to the nominative. Abu Maysarah read: and the one who is gored. His saying: And what the wild beast has eaten means what has been preyed upon by a fanged animal such as a lion, tiger, wolf, hyena, and the like. What is meant here is what the wild beast has eaten, because everything that the wild beast has eaten has been destroyed. Some Arabs specify the name of the wild beast to the lion. When the Arabs ate a sheep, then they freed it from it, they would eat it, even if it died and they did not slaughter it. Al-Hasan Abu Haywah read the word saba’ with a sukoon on the ba’, and it is the language of the people of Najd. From this is the saying of Hassan about Utbah ibn Abi Lahab: Whoever returns the year to his family, the lion will not be devoured by the one who returns Ibn Masoud read: And the eater of the seven. Ibn Abbas read: And the eater of the seven. His statement: Except what you have slaughtered is in the accusative case as a connected exception according to the majority of scholars, and it refers to what you have slaughtered from the previously mentioned animals, and in it is life. The people of Medina said: This is the well-known view of the Maliki school, and it is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i that if it reaches seven of them except what has no life in it, then it is not eaten. And he narrated it in Al-Muwatta’ from Zaid bin Thabit, and Ismail Al-Qadi agreed with him, so the exception according to this opinion is disconnected: that is, these things are forbidden to you, but what you have slaughtered is what is permissible and not forbidden, and the first is more appropriate. And slaughtering in the speech of the Arabs means slaughtering, as was said by Qatrib and others. The root of the word dhakah in the language is: to complete meaning the full completion of strength, and iqah is the sharpness of the heart and iqah is the speed of insight, and dhakah is that from which fire is kindled, and from this adkaytu I kindled war and fire: I lit them, and dhaka is the name of the sun, and what is meant here is: except for what you have found to be completely slaughtered, and slaughtering in the Sharia: is an expression for the flow of blood, and the rupture of the jugular veins in the slaughtered animal and the slaughtering of the slaughtered animal and the hamstringing of the unattainable, coupled with the intention of God and mentioning His name over it. As for the instrument by which slaughtering occurs, the majority went to the view that everything that causes blood to flow and the rupture of the jugular veins is an instrument for slaughtering except the tooth and bone, and this is how the authentic hadiths came. His saying: And what was slaughtered on al-nab stone idols. Ibn Faris said: The nab is a stone that was set up to be worshipped and the blood of the slaughtered animals was poured over it, and the nasa’ib are stones set up around the edge of the well and made into supports. It was said that the nab is the plural of its singular form nasab, like himar and hamar. Talhah read it with a damma on the nun and a sukoon on the sad. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr with the opening of the letter noon and the sukoon of the letter sad. Al-Jahdari read with the opening of the letter noon and the letter sad, making it a unified noun like the mountain and the camel, and the plural is ansaab like mountains and camels. Mujahid said: They are stones that were around Mecca and they used to slaughter on them. Ibn Jurayj said: The Arabs used to slaughter in Mecca and sprinkle the blood on whatever was facing the Kaaba and they would cut up the meat and place it on the stones. When Islam came, the Muslims said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: We are more deserving to honor this Kaaba with these actions, so God revealed: And that which is slaughtered on stone altars The meaning is: The intention behind that is to honor the stone altars, not that slaughtering on them is not permissible. For this reason it was said that on means lam: i.e. for its sake. Qatrib said it, and according to this it is included in what is dedicated to other than God, and it was specifically mentioned to emphasize its prohibition and to ward off what they thought of that to honor and glorify the Kaaba. His statement: And that you seek lots with arrows is connected to what preceded it: i.e. and it is forbidden for you to seek lots with arrows. And the arrows are the dice of gambling, the singular of which is zalam. The poet said: A young boy, who is neither a camel nor a sheep herder, is suffering from it. Nor a butcher on the back and the entrails Another said: If Juthayma killed its masters, its women will strike with arrows. The Arabs had three types of arrows: one of them had written on it do, another had written on it don’t do, and the third was neglected and had nothing on it, so he would put them in a map with him. If he wanted to do something, he would put his hand in and they were all the same and pull out one of them. If the first came out, he would do what he intended to do, but if the second came out, he would leave it. If the third came out, he would repeat the striking until one of the first two came out. This action was called istiqā because they used it to cast lots for sustenance and what they wanted to do, just as it is said that he asked for rain, meaning he asked for water. So istiqā is asking for a share and a portion. The total number of dice in gambling is ten, and we have already explained them. They used to play with them in gambling. It was said that the arrows were like the dice of the Persians and Romans that they gambled with, and it was said that it was chess. God forbade casting lots because it involved claiming to know the unseen and a type of soothsaying. His statement, That is transgression, is a reference to casting lots with arrows or to all the forbidden things mentioned here. Fisq: going beyond the limit. Its meaning has been explained above. This is a severe warning, because fisq is the most severe form of disbelief, not what some people have agreed upon as an intermediate position between faith and disbelief. His statement, This day those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion, refers to the day on which the verse was revealed, which is the day of the conquest of Mecca, eight days before the end of Ramadan in the year nine. It has also been said that the day refers to the present and what is connected to it, and it did not refer to a specific day. And despair has two dialects: yas with two yas meaning despair, and ays meaning despair and hopelessness. An-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: meaning they despaired of invalidating your religion and returning you to their religion as they claimed. So do not fear them means do not fear that they will defeat you or invalidate your religion. And fear Me, for I am capable of everything. If I support you, no one can defeat you, and if I abandon you, no one can support you except Me. His saying: This day I have perfected your religion for you made it complete and not in need of completion because it is apparent over all religions and prevails over them and because its rulings that Muslims need are complete, from what is permissible, what is forbidden, and what is doubtful, and it fulfilled what the Book and Sunnah included of that, and what is understood from the introduction of his saying: for you is not hidden. The majority said: What is meant by completion here is: the revelation of most of the obligations, the permissible and the forbidden. They said: And after that, the Qur’an was revealed, such as the verse on usury and the verse on kalalah and the like. What is meant by the day mentioned here is Friday, and the Day of Arafah was after the afternoon prayer in the Farewell Pilgrimage in the year ten, thus it was proven in the Sahih from the hadith of Omar bin Al-Khattab, and it was said: It was revealed on the day of the greater pilgrimage. His saying: And I have completed My favor upon you by completing the religion that includes the rulings and by the conquest of Mecca and the subjugation of the infidels and their despair of prevailing over you as I promised you by saying: And I will complete My favor upon you. His saying: And I have approved for you Islam as a religion means I have informed you of My approval of it for you, for He, the Almighty, has always been pleased with Islam for the nation of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So there is not much benefit in the specificity of approval to this day if we take it literally. It is possible that he means I have approved for you the Islam that you are upon today as a religion that will remain until the end of the days of this world. And religion is in the accusative case of specification, and it is possible for it to be a second object. His saying: But whoever is forced by severe hunger this is connected to the mention of the forbidden things, and what is between them is an interruption: meaning whoever is forced by necessity in severe hunger meaning famine to eat dead meat and what comes after it of the forbidden things. And al-Khamis means a shriveled stomach, and a man is al-Khamis and al-Khamisan, and a woman is al-Khamis and al-Khamisan, and from it comes the al-Khamis al-Qadam, and it is often used to refer to hunger. Al-A’sha said: You spend the winter with full bellies, while your neighbors go to bed hungry. His saying: not inclined towards sin. Inclination means leaning, and sin means the forbidden: that is, the state of the one forced to be in famine and not inclined towards sin, and it means not transgressing or exceeding what is necessary, and everyone who inclines towards sin is inclined towards and inclined towards sin. Al-Nakha’i, Yahya ibn Waththab, and Al-Salami read inclined towards and inclined towards sin, for God is Forgiving and Merciful, with it, and He does not hold him accountable for what necessity forced him to do in hunger, while he was not inclined towards sin by eating what was forbidden to him, such as transgressing against others or exceeding what necessity called for, as mentioned above. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated - on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to my people to call them to God and His Messenger and to present to them the symbols of Islam. While we were like that, they brought me a bowl of blood and gathered around it to eat it. They said: ‘Come, my friend, and eat.’ I said: ‘Woe to you! I have only come to you from someone who forbids you this, because God revealed it to him.’ They said: ‘What is that?’ He said: ‘So I recited to them this verse: ‘Forbidden to you are dead animals.’” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And that which is dedicated to other than God he said: And that which is dedicated to tyrants And the strangled he said: The one that is strangled and dies And the beaten to death he said: The sheep that butts another And that which a wild beast has eaten he said: What a wild beast has taken Except what you slaughter he said: You slaughtered from that, and it has a soul in it, so eat it And that which is slaughtered on altars he said: The altars were the idols that they used to slaughter and sacrifice on them And that you seek lots with arrows he said: They were the lots that they used to seek lots with in matters That is transgression meaning whoever eats all of that is transgression. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The rada is the one that falls into a well, and the rada is the one that falls from a mountain. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: And that you seek lots with arrows he said: White pebbles that they used to strike with. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse, he said: When they wanted to do something or travel, they would take three arrows and write on one of them: He commanded me, and on the other: He forbade me, and they would leave the third in between with nothing on it, then they would roll it over. If the one with the command on it came out, they would go on with their matter, and if the one with the prohibition on it came out, they would stop, and if the one with nothing on it came out, they would repeat it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: This day those who disbelieved have despaired of [defeating] your religion, he said: They have despaired of ever returning to their religion. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority regarding the verse, saying: He says that the people of Mecca despaired of ever returning to their religion of idol worship. So fear them not in following Muhammad, but fear Me in worshipping idols and denying Muhammad. So when he was standing in Arafat, Gabriel descended upon him while he was raising his hands and the Muslims were supplicating to God, This day I have perfected for you your religion, meaning your lawful and unlawful things, so nothing will be revealed after this, and I have completed My favor upon you, meaning My favor, so no polytheist performed Hajj with you. And I have chosen, meaning I have chosen Islam as your religion, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained after the revelation of this verse for eighty-one days, then God took him to Himself. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, saying: God informed His Prophet and the believers that He had perfected their faith so that they would never need anything more, and He had perfected it so that it would never decrease, and He was pleased with it so that He would never be displeased. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab who said: The Jews said to Umar: You recite a verse in your Book, if it had been revealed to us Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival. He said: Which verse? They said: This day have I perfected your religion for you. Umar said: By God, I know the day on which it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the hour in which it was revealed. It was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the eve of Arafah on a Friday. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: But whoever is forced meaning to do what is forbidden from what is mentioned at the beginning of this surah, in a state of famine meaning in a state of famine, without inclining to sin meaning not intentionally committing sin.
5:4: This is a start to explaining what God has made lawful for them after explaining what God has forbidden for them, and the reason for the revelation of the verse will be mentioned. His statement: 4- What is lawful for them meaning what is lawful for them, or what is lawful for them from foods in general and from hunting and from the food of the People of the Book and from their women. His statement: "Say: Lawful for you are the good things" are what the eater enjoys and finds good from what God has made lawful for His servants, and it was said that they are the permissible, and we have discussed this before, and it was said that the good things are the slaughtered animals because they became good by slaughtering, and this is a specification of the general without a specification, and the reason and context are not suitable for that. His statement: And what you have taught of the birds of prey is conjoined with the good things by estimating an addition to correct the meaning: meaning He has made lawful for you the good things and made lawful for you the hunting of what you have taught of the birds of prey. Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah read You have taught with a damma on the 'ayn and a kasra on the lam: meaning you have learned about the matter of the birds of prey and hunting with them. Al-Qurtubi said: Some of those who wrote about the rulings of the Qur’an mentioned that the verse indicates that the permissibility includes what we know of the birds of prey, and this includes the dog and all birds of prey, and this necessitates the permissibility of all forms of benefit, so it indicates the permissibility of selling dogs and birds of prey and benefiting from them in all forms of benefit except what the evidence specifies: which is eating from the birds of prey: meaning the hunting dogs and wild birds. He said: The nation is unanimously agreed that if the dog is not black and a Muslim taught it and did not eat from the prey that it hunted and left a mark on it with a wound or a reprimand and a Muslim hunted with it and mentioned the name of God when sending it, then its prey is valid and may be eaten without dispute. If one of these conditions is violated, then there is a dispute. If what is hunted is not a dog, such as a cheetah or the like, or a hawk or a falcon or similar birds, then the majority of the nation is of the opinion that everything that hunts after being trained is a bird of prey that earns. It is said that someone has wounded and earned, and from this comes the word jarah because it is earned by it, and from this comes the word ijara’a because it is used to earn, and from this comes the word ijara’a committing evil deeds, and from this comes the statement of God the Almighty: And He knows what you have wounded during the day. And His statement: Or do those who have committed evil deeds think? His statement: trained is a state, and the one who trains dogs for how to hunt is the most specific, and the one who trains other birds of prey is the same, because hunting with dogs is the most common. And He did not suffice with His statement: And what you have taught of birds of prey, even though training is training, in order to emphasize what is necessary in terms of training. And it was said that the wild beast is called a dog, so every wild beast that is hunted by it is included, and it was said that this verse is specific to dogs. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: Whatever is hunted by falcons and other birds, if you know how to slaughter it, it is permissible for you, otherwise do not feed it. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Abu Ja`far was asked about the falcon: Is its hunt permissible? He said: No, unless you know how to slaughter it. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: And what you have trained of birds of prey to be trained refers to dogs in particular. If the dog is black and dumb, then Al-Hasan, Qatadah and An-Nakha`i dislike hunting it. Ahmad said: I do not know of anyone who permits it if it is dumb, and Ibn Rahawayh said the same. As for the majority of scholars in Madinah and Kufa, they consider it permissible to hunt any trained dog. Those who forbade hunting a black dog cited as evidence the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The black dog is a devil. Narrated by Muslim and others. The truth is that it is permissible to hunt everything that falls under the general category of birds of prey, without any distinction between dogs and other types of birds, black dogs and other types of birds, and this is supported by the fact that the reason for the revelation of the verse was the question of Adi bin Hatim about hunting falcons, as will be mentioned. His statement: You teach them from what God has taught you. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state: that is, from what God has taught you, from what you have grasped through what He created in you of the mind by which you are guided to teach and train it until it becomes capable of catching prey when you send it out. His statement: Then eat of what they catch for you. The fa is for branching out, and the sentence is a branch of what was mentioned previously about the permissibility of hunting what they have taught of birds of prey. The min in His statement: from what they catch for you is for partiality, because some prey is not eaten, such as skin and bones, and what a dog has eaten and the like. This is evidence that it must be held for its owner, and if it eats from it, it has only held it for itself, as in the authentic hadith in Sahih. The majority of scholars are of the view that it is not permissible to eat prey that a bird of prey intends of its own accord without being sent out. Ata bin Abi Rabah and Al-Awza’i said: It was narrated on the authority of Salman Al-Farsi, Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas, Abu Hurairah and Abdullah bin Umar. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Al-Zuhri, Rabia, Malik and Al-Shafi’i in the old days that its catch may be eaten. The statement of God the Almighty: Of that which they catch for you is refuted by them, and the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Adi bin Hatim: If you send your trained dog and mention the name of God over it, then eat what it catches for you. It is in the two Sahihs and others, and in a wording of theirs: If it eats, do not eat, for I fear that it has caught for itself. As for what Abu Dawud narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Tha’labah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If you send your trained dog and mention the name of God, then eat even if it eats from it. He also narrated it with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Amr bin Shu’aib on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather. Al-Nasa'i also narrated it. Some Shafi'is combined these hadiths by saying that if he eats after catching it, then it becomes forbidden, based on the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim. If he catches it and then waits for its owner, and the wait is long and he gets hungry and eats from the hunted animal because of his hunger, not because he caught it for himself, then that does not affect it and the hunted animal is not forbidden because of it. They based this on the hadith of Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani and the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, and this is a good combination. Others said that if a dog eats from it, it becomes forbidden, based on the hadith of 'Adi. If someone else eats from it, it is not forbidden, based on the other two hadiths. It was said that the hadith of Abu Tha'labah is to be interpreted as if he caught it and left it, then returned and ate from it. Many scholars have taken the path of preference and not the path of combination because of the distance involved. They said: The hadith of Adi bin Hatim is more preferable because it is in the two Sahihs. I have established this approach in my explanation of Al-Muntaqa, which increases the viewer’s insight. His statement: And mention the name of God over it The pronoun in over it refers to what you have learned meaning mention the name of God over it when releasing it, or when it is caught for you: meaning mention the name of God over it if you want to slaughter it. The majority of scholars have held that it is obligatory to mention the name of God when releasing a predator, and they have used this verse as evidence. This is supported by the hadith of Adi bin Hatim, which is proven in the two Sahihs and others with the wording: If you release your dog, mention the name of God, and if you shoot your arrow, mention the name of God. Some scholars said that what is meant is mentioning the name of God when eating. Al-Qurtubi said: This is the most apparent, and they used as evidence the hadiths that guide to say Bismillah, but this is wrong, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, timed saying Bismillah with sending a dog and sending an arrow, and the permissibility of saying Bismillah when eating is another ruling, and a different issue from this issue, so there is no reason to interpret what was mentioned in the Book and Sunnah here as what was mentioned about saying Bismillah when eating, and there is no need to do that. In a wording in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Adi: If you send your dog and say Bismillah and it takes it, then eat. A group of people said that saying Bismillah is a condition, and others said that it is only a Sunnah, and a group said that it is a condition for the one who remembers, not the one who forgets. This is the strongest and most correct of the sayings, his statement: “And fear God. Indeed, God is swift in account,” meaning His account, glory be to Him, is swift in coming, and everything that comes is near.
5:5: His statement: 5- Today all good things have been made lawful for you. This sentence confirms the first sentence, which is His statement: All good things have been made lawful for you. The explanation of good things has already been presented. His statement: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you. Food: is the name for what is eaten, including slaughtered animals. Most scholars have limited it here to slaughtered animals. This verse is evidence that all food of the People of the Scripture, without distinction between meat and other things, is lawful for Muslims, even if they do not mention the name of God over their slaughtered animals. This verse is a specification of the generality of His statement: And do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned. The apparent meaning of this is that the slaughtered animals of the People of the Scripture are lawful, even if the Jew mentions the name of Ezra over his slaughtered animal, and the Christian mentions the name of Christ over his slaughtered animal. Abu Darda, Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Ibn Abbas, al-Zuhri, Rabi'ah, al-Sha'bi, and Makhul held this view. Ali, Aisha and Ibn Umar said: If you hear a People of the Book mentioning the name of someone other than God, then do not eat it. This is the opinion of Tawus and Al-Hasan. They held fast to the words of God the Almighty: And do not eat of that upon which the name of God has not been mentioned Al-Baqarah 2:174. This is also indicated by His words: And that which has been dedicated to other than God. Malik said: It is disliked but not forbidden. This is the difference of opinion if we know that the People of the Book mentioned the name of someone other than God over their slaughtered animals. As for not knowing, Al-Kaya Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir narrated the consensus on its permissibility due to this verse and what was reported in the Sunnah about the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) eating from the roasted sheep that the Jewish woman gave him as a gift, and it is in the Sahih. Likewise, the bag of fat that some of the Companions took from Khaybar and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knew about it, and it is also in the Sahih and others. What is meant by the People of the Book here are the Jews and Christians. As for the Magians, the majority of scholars are of the view that their slaughtered animals should not be eaten and their women should not be married because they are not People of the Book, according to the well-known view among scholars. Abu Thawr disagreed with this, and the jurists denounced him for this, until Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Abu Thawr is like his name, meaning in this issue. It seems that he held fast to what is narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a mursal report that he said about the Magians: Treat them as you treat the People of the Book. This wording has not been proven, and even if we assume that it has a basis, there is an addition in it that refutes what he said, which is his saying: Do not eat their slaughtered animals or marry their women. It was narrated with this addition by a group of commentators and jurists who have no experience in the art of hadith. Neither the original nor the addition were proven. Rather, what was proven in the Sahih is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the jizyah from the Magians of Hajar. As for Banu Taghlib, Ali ibn Abi Talib used to forbid their slaughtering because they were Arabs. He used to say: They did not adhere to anything of Christianity except drinking alcohol. This is the case with all the Arabs who converted to Christianity, such as Tanukh, Judham, Lahm, Amilah, and others like them. Ibn Kathir said: This is the opinion of more than one of the early and later generations.
