It was narrated from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan al-Basri that they saw no harm in the slaughtering of the Christians of Banu Taghlib. Al-Qurtubi said: The majority of the ummah said that the slaughtering of every Christian is permissible, whether he is from Banu Taghlib or not, and the same applies to the Jews. He said: There is no disagreement among the scholars that what does not require slaughtering, such as food, is permissible to eat. His statement: And your food is lawful for them means that the food of the Muslims is lawful for the People of the Book, and in it is evidence that it is permissible for the Muslims to feed the People of the Book from their slaughtered animals, and this is by way of reward and recompense and informing the Muslims that what they take from them of food is lawful for them by way of binding indication. His statement: And chaste women from among the believing women There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of chaste women here, some say chaste women, and some say free women, and Al-Sha’bi read it with a kasra on the sad, and Al-Kisa’i read it this way. We have already discussed this in detail in Al-Baqarah and An-Nisa’. Chaste women is the subject, and from among the believing women is a description of it, and the predicate is omitted, meaning lawful for you, and their mention here is an introduction and preparation for His statement: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you and what is meant by them are free women and not slave women, this is what the majority said, and Ibn Jarir narrated from a group of the Salaf that this verse includes every free or slave woman of the People of the Book, and it was said that what is meant by the People of the Scripture here is the Israelites, and Al-Shafi’i said this, and it is a specification without a specification. Abdullah bin Omar said: Christianity is not permissible. He said: I do not know of a greater form of polytheism than saying that her Lord is Jesus. God said: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe (al-Baqarah 2:14). The response to this is that this verse is specific to the People of the Book from among all polytheists, so the general is based on the specific. Those who forbade marrying female slaves from the People of the Book used this verse as evidence because they applied it to free women, and the words of God the Almighty: Then from those whom your right hands possess of believing girls (al-Baqarah 2:14). Many scholars have held this view, but some have disagreed with them and said that the verse is general or specific to chaste women, as mentioned above. The result is that this verse includes the free, chaste woman of the People of the Book according to all opinions except the opinion of Ibn Umar regarding Christianity. It also includes the free woman who is not chaste and the chaste slave woman, according to the opinion of those who say that it is permissible to use the word polytheist in both of its meanings. As for those who do not permit that, then interpreting the word chaste women here as referring to free women does not say that it is permissible to marry a slave woman, whether she is chaste or not, except with another proof, and he says that it is permissible to marry a free woman, whether she is chaste or not. If interpreting the word chaste women here as referring to chaste women, he says that it is permissible to marry a free, chaste woman and a chaste slave woman, but not an unchaste one of them. His saying: If you have given them their dowries means their bridal-money. The answer to if is omitted: meaning they are lawful, or it is a circumstance of the predicate. The chaste women are understood to mean: permissible for you. His saying: Chaste is in the accusative case as a state: meaning while you are chaste by marriage. Likewise his saying: Not fornicators is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in chaste or as a description of chaste. The meaning is: not publicizing adultery. His saying: Nor taking lovers is in apposition to not fornicators or to fornicators. “Nor” is added for emphasis, and lovers refer to both males and females: meaning they do not take lovers. God has stipulated for men chastity, not publicizing adultery, and not taking lovers, just as He has stipulated for women that they be chaste. And whoever disbelieves in the faith meaning the laws of Islam, his work has become worthless meaning it has become void and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers. Ibn al-Samīf’ read faḍḍābat with a fathah on the ba’. End quote. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi’ that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered him to kill dogs among the people. They said: O Messenger of God, what is permissible for us from this nation that you have ordered to kill? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) remained silent, and God revealed: They ask you, [O Muhammad], what is permissible for them al-Baqarah 2:177. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. He also narrated something similar on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr that ‘Adi ibn Hatim and Zayd ibn al-Muhalhil al-Ta’i asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, we are a people who hunt with dogs and falcons. So this was revealed. ‘Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Sha’bi that ‘Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta’i came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {And what you have trained of birds of prey as swarms}, he said: They are trained dogs, and the hawk and birds of prey, meaning dogs, cheetahs, falcons, and the like. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: The sign of a trained bird is that it holds its prey and does not eat from it until its owner comes. He also narrated on his authority that he said: If a dog eats, do not eat, for it only held it for its own sake. Abd ibn Hamid narrated something similar on his authority, and added: If a falcon eats, do not eat, because a dog can hit it, but a falcon cannot. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And the food of those who were given the Scripture, he said: Their slaughtered animals. And regarding his statement: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, he said: It is lawful for you when you have given them their due compensation, meaning their dowries, in chastity, meaning marry them with a dowry and proof, not fornicating, not committing excessive amounts of adultery, nor taking secret lovers, meaning concealing adultery. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And chaste women from among the believing women and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture, he said: God has made lawful for us two chaste women: a chaste believing woman and a chaste woman from among the People of the Scripture. Our women are forbidden to them, but their women are lawful for us. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Jabir who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Marry the women of the People of the Scripture, but do not marry our women. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: A Muslim man may marry a Christian woman, but a Christian man may not marry a Muslim woman. At-Tabarani and al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The slaughtering of the Jews and Christians was made permissible because they believed in the Torah and the Gospel. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture, he said: free women. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: chaste women.
5:6: His saying: 6- If you stand up if you wanted to stand up as an expression of the effect from the cause as in his saying: So if you read the Qur’an, seek refuge in God. Scholars differed regarding this matter when intending to stand up for prayer. A group said: It is general for every time one stands up for prayer, whether the one standing is pure or in a state of minor ritual impurity. When he stands up for prayer, he should perform ablution. This was narrated from Ali and Ikrimah. Ibn Sirin said: The caliphs used to perform ablution for every prayer. Another group said: This matter is specific to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and this is weak, as the address is to the believers and the command is theirs. A group said: The command is for encouragement in order to gain merit. Others said: Ablution for every prayer was obligatory upon them by this verse, then it was abrogated in the conquest of Makkah. A group said: This command is specific to one who is in a state of minor ritual impurity. Others said: What is meant is when you stand up from sleep for prayer, so the address includes everyone who stands up from sleep. Muslim, Ahmad and the Sunan scholars narrated on the authority of Buraydah who said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to perform ablution before every prayer. On the day of the conquest, he performed ablution, wiped over his socks and prayed the prayers with one ablution. ‘Umar said to him: ‘O Messenger of God, you have done something that you did not do before.’ He said: ‘I did it intentionally, O ‘Umar.’” This has been narrated through many chains of narration with similar wording. Al-Bukhari, Ahmad and the Sunan scholars narrated on the authority of ‘Amr ibn ‘Aamir al-Ansari that I heard Anas ibn Malik say: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to perform ablution before every prayer. I said: ‘What did you do?’ He said: ‘We used to pray the prayers with one ablution as long as we did not break our ablution.’ It is established by what has been mentioned that ablution is only obligatory for someone who has broken his ablution. This is what the majority of scholars have said, and it is the truth. His statement: ‘Wash your faces.’ The face in the language is taken from ‘confrontation.’ It is a limb that includes other limbs, and it has length and width. Its length is from the beginning of the surface of the forehead to the end of the beard, and its width is from ear to ear. Evidence has been reported by combing the beard. Scholars differed about washing what has been left unwashed, and the discussion of this is detailed in its places. Scholars also differed: Is rubbing with the hand considered in washing or is it sufficient to pass water through it? The difference of opinion on this is well-known, and the reference is the Arabic language. If it is proven that rubbing is included in the meaning of washing, then it is considered, otherwise it is not. It says in Shams al-Ulum: Washing something means running water over it and rubbing it. As for rinsing the mouth and nose, if the word “face” does not include the inside of the mouth and nose, then washing them has been proven by the authentic Sunnah, and the difference of opinion on whether it is obligatory or not is well-known. We have explained what is correct in our books. His statement: and your hands to the elbows is to the end, and as for what comes after it being included in what comes before it, this is a matter of disagreement. Sibawayh and a group of people said that what comes after it is included if it is of the same type as what came before it, otherwise it is not, and it was said that here it means with. Some people said that it indicates the end absolutely, and as for inclusion or not, this is a matter that revolves around the evidence. The majority of scholars have said that the elbows should be washed, and they have provided evidence for this with what was narrated by Al-Daraqutni and Al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil on the authority of his grandfather on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, he would run water over his elbows. However, this Al-Qasim is abandoned and his grandfather is weak. His statement: And wipe over your heads. It was said: The ba is redundant, and the meaning is: wipe over your heads, and that requires generalizing the wiping to the entire head. It was also said that it is for partiality, and that requires that wiping some of it is sufficient. Those who support generalization have cited as evidence the Almighty’s saying in tayammum: Then wipe your faces and wiping part of the face is not sufficient by consensus. It has been said that it is for sticking: that is, stick your hands to your heads. In any case, there is something in the pure Sunnah that indicates that wiping part of the head is sufficient, as we have explained in our writings. This was evidence for what is required, not as possible as the possibility of the verse, assuming that it is possible. There is no doubt that whoever orders another to wipe his head has complied by doing what is true of wiping. There is nothing in the Arabic language that requires that in such an action, the entire head must be wiped. This is also the case with all transitive verbs, such as hit Zayd or stab him or stone him. The Arabic meaning is found in the occurrence of the hitting, stabbing, or stoning on one of his limbs, and no one from the people of language or someone who is knowledgeable about it says that he is not a striker unless he strikes every part of Zayd’s body. This is also the case with stabbing, stoning, and all other verbs. Know this so that what is correct in the sayings about wiping the head will become clear to you. If you say: The same is required in washing the face, hands and feet. I say: It is obligatory, were it not for the clarification from the Sunnah regarding the face and the specification of the end in the hands and feet, unlike the head, since it was mentioned in the Sunnah to wipe the whole and wipe some. His statement: and your feet to the ankles Nafi’ read the feet in the accusative case, which is the reading of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Al-A’mash, and Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Hamzah read it in the genitive case. The accusative reading indicates that it is obligatory to wash the feet, because they are conjoined with the face, and this is what the majority of scholars agreed with. The genitive reading indicates that it is permissible to limit oneself to wiping the feet, because they are conjoined with the head, and this is what Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari said, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The Ummah agreed on the obligation of washing them, and I do not know of anyone who rejected that except Al-Tabari from the Muslim jurists and the Rafidis from others, and Al-Tabari relied on the genitive reading. Al-Qurtubi said: It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Ablution is two washings and two wipings. He said: Ikrimah used to wipe his feet, and he said: There is no washing for the feet, rather wiping was revealed for them. Aamer Al-Shaabi said: Gabriel came down with the wiping. He said: Qatada said: God has prescribed two wipings and two washings. He said: Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari went to the opinion that their obligation is the choice between washing and wiping and made the two readings like the two narrations, and An-Nahhas strengthened it, but it has been proven in the pure Sunnah with the authentic hadiths of his actions, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his saying to wash the feet only, and it has been proven from him that he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire and it is in the two Sahihs and others, so it indicates the obligation of washing the feet, and that wiping them is not sufficient, because the nature of wiping is to hit what it hits and miss what it misses, so if it was sufficient, he would not have said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. It has been proven from him that he said after he performed ablution and washed his feet: This is an ablution without which God does not accept prayer. It has been proven in Sahih Muslim and others that a man performed ablution and left on his foot a place the size of a fingernail, so he said to him: Go back and do your ablution well. As for wiping over the socks, it is proven by the mutawatir hadiths. His saying: to the ankles is like his saying: to the elbows. It has been said that the reason for pluralizing the elbows and dualizing the heels is that since each foot has two heels and each hand has only one elbow, the heels were dualized to indicate that each foot has two heels, unlike the elbows which were pluralized because since each hand has one elbow, it was not imagined that there was another one. Ibn Atiyyah mentioned the meaning of this. Al-Kawashi said: Dualizing the ankles and pluralizing the elbows is to negate the idea that each foot has two heels. Rather, each foot has one heel with two ends on either side of the foot, unlike the elbow which is further removed from imagination. The remaining obligatory parts of ablution are intention and saying Bismillah, and they are not mentioned in this verse. Rather, they are mentioned in the Sunnah. It has been said that this verse indicates intention, because when He said: When you rise to prayer, wash your faces, the meaning of the statement was: wash your faces for it, and that is the valid intention. His statement: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, purify yourselves, meaning wash yourselves with water. Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn Mas’ud held that the person in a state of major ritual impurity does not perform tayammum at all, but rather leaves the prayer until he finds water, based on this verse. The majority held that tayammum is obligatory for major ritual impurity in the absence of water, and this verse is for the one who finds it, on the basis that purification is more general than what is obtained with water or with what is a substitute for it in the absence of water, which is soil. It has been authentically reported from Umar and Ibn Mas’ud that they refer to what the majority said for the authentic hadiths reported about the tayammum of the person in a state of major ritual impurity in the absence of water. The explanation of major ritual impurity has been presented in An-Nisa’. His statement: And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy has already been explained in full in Surat An-Nisa’, and the discussion of touching women, dry ablution, and earth has already been discussed. The word from in His statement: from it is for the beginning of the goal, and it was said: for the partial. It was said: The reason for repeating this here is to complete the discussion of the types of purification. God does not intend to place any difficulty on you meaning that He does not intend by commanding you to purify yourself with water or earth to make your religion difficult, and from this is His statement, the Most High: And He has not placed any difficulty on you in religion then He said: But He intends to purify you from sins, and it was said from minor and major ritual impurity. And that He may complete His favor upon you meaning by permitting you to perform dry ablution when there is no water or by what He has prescribed for you from the laws by which He has exposed you to reward. That you may be grateful for His favor upon you and thus you will deserve the reward of the grateful through gratitude. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding his statement, When you rise to prayer, he said: When you rise from your beds, meaning sleep. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of As-Suddi something similar. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority that he said: When you rise while you are not in a state of purity. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Then wash your faces, he said: That washing is rubbing. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Anas that it was said to him: Al-Hajjaj delivered a sermon to us and said: Wash your faces and hands and wipe your heads and feet, and nothing in the son of Adam is closer to filth than his feet, so wash their insides, their backs and their heels. Anas said: God spoke the truth and Al-Hajjaj lied. God said: And wipe your heads and your feet, and Anas used to wet them when he wiped his feet. Sa’id ibn Mansur narrated on the authority of ‘Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, agreed to wash the feet. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: from hardship he said: from tightness. Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: and that He may complete His favor upon you he said: the completion of the favor is entering Paradise. His favor is not completed upon a servant who does not enter Paradise.
5:7: 7- The Grace of God It was said: It is Islam. And the covenant: The pledge, it was said: What is meant by it here: What He took from the children of Adam as He said: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam the verse. Mujahid and others said: Even if we did not mention it, God informed us of it, and it was said: It is addressed to the Jews, and the covenant: What He took from them in the Torah. The majority of the commentators from the Salaf and those after them went to the fact that it is the covenant that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took from them on the night of Al-Aqaba, which is hearing and obedience in ease and difficulty, and God added it to Himself because it is from His command and permission as He said: They only pledge allegiance to God, and the pledge of Al-Aqaba is mentioned in the books of biography, and this is connected to His saying: Fulfill the contracts. His saying: When you said, 'We hear and we obey' means the time of your saying this statement, and this is related to your covenant, or to an omitted word that occurred as a state: meaning being at this time. Dhat as-Sudur is what the chests conceal because it is specific to them and no one knows about it. For this reason, it was called Dhat which means companion. If He, glory be to Him, knows about it, then how about what is apparent and clear?
5:8: His statement 8- O you who have believed, be persistently standing. Its explanation has already been presented in An-Nisa', and the exaggerated form in steadfastly standing indicates that they are commanded to do so in the most perfect way for God, that is, for His sake, out of reverence for His command and hope for His reward. And justice is fairness. We have already discussed His statement: Let it not lead you to commit a crime in full: that is, do not let hatred of a people lead you to abandon justice and conceal testimony. Be just - it is that is, the justice indicated by His statement: Be just. Nearer to righteousness which you have been commanded to do more than once: that is, closer to your fearing God, or to your fearing the Fire.
5:9: His saying: 9- For them is forgiveness and a great reward. This sentence is in the accusative case as the second object of his saying: He promised, meaning that He promised them that they would have forgiveness, or He promised them forgiveness, so the sentence took the place of a singular noun and made it unnecessary. Similar to it is the saying of the poet: We found the righteous to have a reward, gardens, and a spring of pure water.
5:10: His saying: 10- The companions of Hell meaning its inhabitants.
5:11: His statement: 11- When they were a people is an adverb for his statement: Remember or for the blessing or for something omitted that occurred as a state of it: that they should spread out meaning that they should spread out. And his statement: So he refrained is conjoined with his statement: they and the reason for the revelation of this verse will come, and the meaning will become clear with it. Ibn Jarir and Al-Tabarani in Al-Kabeer narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: When you said, ‘We hear and we obey,’ meaning when God sent the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and revealed the Book to him, they said: We believe in the Prophet and the Book and we acknowledge what is in the Torah. So God reminded them of His covenant that they acknowledged upon themselves and He commanded them to fulfill it. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Blessings are favors, and His covenant which He has bound you with, meaning the one which He bound the children of Adam with in the back of Adam, peace be upon him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Kathir regarding his statement: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, the verse. He said: It was revealed about the Jews of Khaybar. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to them to ask them about the blood money, but they intended to kill him. That is why His statement: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just, the verse. And Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped at a place and the people dispersed among the wild trees to seek shade under them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hung his weapon on a tree, and a Bedouin came to his sword, took it and drew it, then turned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Who can protect you from me? He said: God. The Bedouin said it two or three times.” Who is stopping you from me? And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, so the Bedouin drew the sword, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called his companions and informed them of the Bedouin’s action while he was sitting beside him and did not punish him.” Muammar said: Qatada used to mention something similar to this. He mentioned that some Arabs wanted to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they sent this Bedouin, and he interpreted Remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you the verse, and Al-Hakim transmitted and authenticated it from him in a similar manner, and he mentioned that the man’s name was Ghawrath ibn Al-Harith, and that “when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the sword fell from his hand, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and said: Who will protect you from me? He said: Be the best taker, he said: So bear witness that there is no god but God.” Ibn Ishaq and Abu Nu’aym also transmitted it from him in Al-Dala’il. Ibn Nu’aym transmitted in Al-Dala’il from Ibn Abbas: that Banu Nadir intended to throw a stone at the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those with him, so Gabriel came and informed him of what had happened. They intended to, so he and those with him stood up, and the following verse was revealed: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when they were a people Al-Masdar 2:17. Something similar to this was narrated from other chains of transmission, and the story of the Bedouin, who is the aforementioned Ghawrath, is confirmed in Sahih.
5:12: His statement: 12- And God took is a new statement that includes mentioning some of the treachery committed by the Children of Israel. The covenant that God took from them has been explained previously. The commentators differed on how these leaders were sent after their consensus that the leader is the chief of the people who knows their affairs and investigates them and their interests in them. The leader is the great man who is among the people in this way, and it is said: the leader of the people for their witness and their guarantor. The leader is the path in the mountain, this is its origin, and the leader of the people was named after it because it is a path to knowing their affairs. The captain: is of a higher position than the overseer. It was said: What is meant by sending these captains is that they were sent as trustees to investigate the tyrants and to look into their strength and power. They set out to test the condition of those in it and to inform about that. They found out that the tyrants had great strength and thought that they were unable to handle it. They agreed among themselves to hide that from the Children of Israel and to inform Moses about it. When they returned to the Children of Israel, ten of them betrayed them and informed their relatives. The report spread until the matter of the invasion was nullified and they said: Go, you and your Lord, and fight. It was said: Each one of these captains guaranteed his tribe that they would believe and fear God. This is the meaning of sending them. Some of what a group of the Salaf said about that will be mentioned. His saying: And God said, ‘I am with you’ means He said that to the Children of Israel, and it was said: to the leaders, and the meaning is: I am with you with victory and support, and the lam in His saying: If you establish prayer is the one that introduces the omitted oath, and its answer is: I will disbelieve and it is the same as the answer to the condition. And ta’zir is: glorification and reverence, and Abu Ubaidah recited: How many a noble man is generous to them, and how many a lion is honored in the assembly That is, to magnify and respect. Ta'zir is used to mean hitting and turning back. It is said: I admonished someone if you disciplined him and turned him back from doing bad things. So his statement: And you honored them means you honored them according to the first meaning, or you turned away their enemies from them and protected them according to the second. His statement: And you loaned God a good loan means you spent in good ways, and a loan is a source with deleted extras like the statement of God the Almighty: And caused it to grow in a good growth or a second object of you loaned. It is said that good is what the soul is content with, and it is said that it is what is sought for the sake of God, and it is said that it is lawful. His statement: But whoever disbelieves after that meaning after the covenant or after the mentioned condition has certainly strayed from the right path meaning he has strayed from the middle of the road.
5:13: His saying: 13- Because they broke their covenant The letter ba is causal and ma is redundant, meaning because of their breaking their covenant We cursed them meaning We expelled them and made them distant and made their hearts hard meaning hard, they do not comprehend or understand good. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read Qasiyyah with a shaddah on the ya without an alif, and this is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, Al-Nakha'i and Yahya bin Waththab. It is said dirham qasi with a light seen and a shaddah on the ya: meaning false, this was mentioned by Abu Ubaid. Al-Asma'i and Abu Ubaidah said: dirham qasi as if it is an Arabized qasi. Al-A'mash read Qasiyyah with a light ya. The rest read Qasiyyah. They distort the words from their places The sentence is resumed to explain their condition or is a condition: meaning they replace it with something else or interpret it in a way other than its interpretation. Al-Salami and Al-Nakha'i read the speech. His saying: And you will not cease to find treachery among them means, O Muhammad, you will not cease to find treachery among them. Treason is betrayal. It was said that it is an adjective for something omitted, and the meaning is a treacherous group. It may also be used for exaggeration, such as a scholar or a genealogist, if you want to exaggerate in describing him with treachery. It was said that treachery is disobedience. His saying: Except a few of them is an exception to the pronoun in among them. “So pardon them and overlook.” It was said that this was abrogated by the verse of the sword, and it was said that it is specific to those with whom a treaty was made.
5:14: His statement: 14- "And from those who said, 'We are Christians,' We took their covenant" meaning in monotheism and belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what he brought. Al-Akhfash said: It is like saying, 'I took from Zayd his garment and a dirham,' so the rank of those after him is We took. The Kufians said otherwise, and it was said that the pronoun in his statement, "their covenant" refers to the Children of Israel: meaning, We took from the Christians the same covenant as those mentioned before them from the Children of Israel. He said: "From those who said, 'We are Christians' and did not say and from the Christians" to indicate that they are liars in their claim to Christianity and that they are supporters of God. His saying: So they forgot a portion of that of which they had been reminded meaning they forgot a large portion of the covenant taken from them after it was taken from them So We cast among them enmity and hatred meaning We stuck that to them, taken from glue: which is what sticks one thing to another like gum and the like. It is said that he was attracted to something, yaghri gharī with the opening of the ghain and shortened, and gharā with the breaking of the ghain and extended: meaning he became addicted to it until it was as if it had become attached to it, and the same as ighraa is harassment, and aghrayt al-kalb: meaning I made it addicted to hunting, and what is meant by his saying: among them is the Jews and Christians because they were all mentioned before, and it was said that it was among the Christians in particular, because they are the closest mentioned, and that is because they split into the Jacobites, Nestorians and Melkites, and some of them disbelieved in one another, and they pretended to be hostile to one another in themselves. An-Nahhas said: What is better than what has been said about the meaning of We cast among them enmity and hatred is that God Almighty commanded enmity towards the infidels and hatred towards them, so every group is commanded to be enmity towards and hate its companion. His statement: And God will inform them of what they used to do is a threat to them: that is, they will receive the punishment for breaking the covenant. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding his statement: And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel, he said: He took their covenants that they would be sincere to Him and not worship anyone other than Him. And We raised up from among them twelve leaders, meaning guarantors who guaranteed them that they would fulfill the covenants to God in what He had commanded them to do and in what He had forbidden them to do. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Twelve leaders he said: From each tribe of the Children of Israel there were men whom Moses sent to the giants and they found them, two of them would enter each one of them, and only five of them would carry a bunch of grapes on a piece of wood, and five or four would enter half of a pomegranate if its seeds were removed. So all the leaders returned and forbade their tribe from fighting them except Joshua bin Nun and Caleb bin Yafnah, for they ordered the tribes to fight the giants and struggle against them, but they disobeyed them and obeyed the others. They are the two men upon whom God bestowed His blessings, so the Children of Israel wandered for forty years, going to bed where they went in the morning and going to bed where they went in the evening in their wandering. So Moses struck a stone for each tribe, a spring for them to carry with them, and Moses said to them: Drink, you donkeys. So God forbade him from cursing them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Twelve leaders he said: They are from among Israel whom Moses sent to look at the city and they came with a grain of their fruit and a man’s ear, so he said: Estimate the strength of a people and their might and this is their fruit, then they were tempted and said: We cannot fight, So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Ibn Ishaq mentioned the names of these tribes, and their names are mentioned in the fourth book of the Torah, and in it there is a contradiction to what Ibn Ishaq mentioned. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And you supported them he said: You aided them. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And you supported them he said: You aided them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Because they broke their covenant he said: It is a covenant that God took from the people of the Torah and they broke it. Ibn Jarir narrated from him regarding his statement: They distort words from their [proper] usages, meaning the limits set by God. They say: If Muhammad commands you to do what you are upon, then accept it, and if he contradicts you, then beware. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: And they have forgotten a portion of that of which they were reminded, he said: They forgot the Book. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: And you will not cease to find out about treachery on their part, he said: They are Jews like the one they intended to do to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he entered their garden. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: And you will not cease to find out about treachery on their part, he said: Lies and immorality. Regarding his statement: So pardon them and overlook, he said: He was not commanded on that day to fight them, so God commanded him to pardon them and overlook, then that was abrogated in Bara’ah, so He said: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, the verse. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i regarding his statement: So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection, he said: He incited some of them against others with disputes and arguments about religion.
5:15: The definite article in the book is for the gender and the address is to the Jews and Christians 15- Our Messenger has come to you meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he is: Making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Book revealed to you, which is the Torah and the Gospel: such as the verse of stoning and the story of the Sabbath-breakers who were transformed into monkeys and pardons much of what you conceal, so he leaves its explanation because it does not include what must be explained of the legal rulings, because if it is not like that, there is no benefit related to its explanation except merely disgracing you. It was said that the meaning is: He pardons much and overlooks it and does not inform you of it. It was said: He pardons many of you and does not hold you accountable for what they do. The sentence is in the accusative case in apposition to the current sentence: I mean his saying: Makes clear to you. His saying: There has come to you from God a light is a renewed sentence that includes a statement that Muhammad's mission included benefits other than what came before from the mere explanation. Al-Zajjaj said: The light is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said: Islam. The clear book: the Qur’an, for it is the clear one.
5:16: The pronoun in His statement: 16- He guides thereby refers to the Book or to Him and to the light because they are like one thing. Whoever follows His pleasure means what God is pleased with, and “the paths of peace” are the paths of safety from torment that lead to peace free from every affliction. It was said that what is meant by peace is Islam. And He brings them out from the darkness of disbelief to the light of Islam. And He guides them to a straight path to a path by which they reach the truth, in which there is no crookedness or fear. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Our Messenger, he said: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir also narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: “The Jews came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him about stoning. He said: Which of you is more knowledgeable? They pointed to Ibn Suriya. So he implored him by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses and the One who raised the mountain with the covenants that were taken from them until he was overcome by weakness. He said: When there were many among us, we flogged them a hundred lashes and shaved our heads. So he ruled that they should be stoned. So this verse was revealed.” Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And pardons many, he said about many sins. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Suddi who said: “The paths of peace” are the path of God which He has prescribed for His servants and called them to it and sent His messengers with it: which is Islam.
5:17: The separating pronoun in his saying: 17- He is the Messiah indicates limitation. It was said that some Christian sects said this, and it was said that none of them accepted it, but it necessitated their saying: God is the Messiah and no one else. What was presented at the end of Surat An-Nisa’ was sufficient and makes repetition unnecessary. His saying: “Say: Who has control over God at all?” The question is for rebuke and rebuke, and ownership, and ownership: control, preservation and ability, from their saying I have control over so-and-so’s affair: meaning I have power over him: meaning who is able to prevent if He wills to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth together? And if no one is able to prevent that, then there is no god but God and no Lord other than Him and no true worshipped besides Him. And if the Messiah were a god as the Christians claim, then he would have had some control, and he would have been able to prevent the least of the situation from himself, but he would not have been able to prevent death from his mother when it came to her. And she was mentioned specifically despite her being included in the generality of those on earth because it is more appropriate and more deserving of it from Him than anyone else, so if he is not able to prevent it from anyone else, then he is unable to prevent it from anyone else. And the mention of those on earth is to indicate the comprehensiveness of His power, and that if He wills something, there is no one who opposes Him in His command nor does He share in His judgment. And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them meaning what is between the two types of creatures. His saying: He creates what He wills is a new sentence intended to explain that He, glory be to Him, is the Creator of creation according to His will, and that He is able to do everything and nothing is difficult for Him.
5:18: His saying: 18- And the Jews and the Christians said, 'We are the sons of God and His beloved.' The Jews proved for themselves what they proved for Ezra when they said: Ezra is the son of God. And the Christians proved for themselves what they proved for the Messiah when they said: The Messiah is the son of God. And it was said that it was with the deletion of an added word: that is, we are followers of the sons of God. And thus they proved for themselves that they are the beloved of God merely by the false claim and empty hopes. So God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to respond to them, and He said: Say, 'Then why does He punish you for your sins?' That is, if you are as you claim, then why does He punish you for what you commit of sins by killing, transforming, and by the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, as you admit to that by saying: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. For the son is of the same kind as his father, and nothing is impossible for the father to do, and you sin, and the beloved does not punish his beloved while you are being punished. So this indicates that you are liars in This claim. This proof is what dialecticians call the proof of contradiction. His statement: Rather, you are human beings from among those He created is in apposition to an implied meaning indicated by the speech: meaning, then you are not like that. Rather, you are human beings from among those He created meaning from the same kind as those whom God Almighty created. He holds them accountable for good and evil, and rewards every worker according to his work. “He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them” of the existents. And to Him is the destination meaning, you will go to Him when you move from this world to the hereafter. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Nu'man bin Ada', Bahri bin Amr, and Shas bin Adi came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and spoke to him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke to them and called them to God and warned them of His punishment. They said: What do you fear, O Muhammad? We are the children of God and His beloved, as the Christians say. So God revealed about them: And the Jews and the Christians say, to the end of the verse. Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Anas that he said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by with a group of his companions and a child on the road. When his mother saw the people, she feared that her child would be trampled on, so she came running and said: My son, my son. She ran and caught him. The people said: O Messenger of God, would this woman not throw her son into the Fire? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No, by God, He will not throw His beloved into the Fire." Its chain of transmission in the Musnad is as follows: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Anas, and he mentioned it. The meaning of the verse refers to the meaning of this hadith, and for this reason some Sufi sheikhs said to some jurists: Where do you find in the Qur’an that the beloved does not torment his beloved? He did not respond to him, so the Sufi recited this verse. Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd on the authority of Al-Hasan that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, by God, God does not torment his beloved, but He may test him in this world. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of As-Suddi regarding his statement: He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, he said: He guides among you whom He wills in this world and forgives him, and He causes to die among you whom He wills in disbelief and punishes him.
5:19: The people of the book are the Jews and Christians. The Messenger is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: 19- "And God makes clear to you" is a state. The clear is what God has prescribed for His servants and it was omitted for knowledge, because the mission of the messengers is only for that. The origin of the word "fatara" is stillness. It is said that something became still: it became still, and it was said that it is interruption. Abu Ali Al-Farisi and others said this. From this, the water became "fatara if it stopped from being cold to hot, and the man became fatara" from his work: if he stopped from being serious about it, and a woman who is "fatarat al-'ar" means she is cut off from the sharpness of her gaze. The meaning is that the messengers stopped before his mission, peace and blessings be upon him, for a period of time. There is disagreement about the length of that period and this will be explained. His saying: That you should say, ‘There has not come to us any bearer of good tidings or a warner’ is an explanation for the Messenger’s coming with the explanation at a time of some delay: that is, it is disliked that you should say this statement as an apology for your negligence. The min in his saying: of a bearer of good tidings is redundant to emphasize the negation of the coming, and the fa in his saying: there has come to you is the eloquent one, like the poet’s saying: We came to Khorasan That is, do not apologize, for a bearer of good tidings and a warner has come to you, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And God is over all things competent. Among His powers is sending His Messenger after a period of messengers. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala'il on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Jews to Islam, encouraging them to do so and warning them, but they refused. So Muadh bin Jabal, Saad bin Ubadah, and Uqbah bin Wahb said to them: O group of Jews, fear God, for by God, you know that he is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. You used to mention him to us before his mission and describe him to us in his description. Rafi bin Harmalah and Wahb bin Yahudah said: We did not tell you this, and God did not send down any book after Moses, nor did He send a bearer of good tidings or a warner after him. So God revealed: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you [what is in the Book], after a hiatus among the messengers Al-Ad-Dala'il. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, saying: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who came with the truth by which God distinguished between truth and falsehood. In it is clarification, exhortation, light, guidance, and protection for whoever takes it. He said: The period between Jesus and Muhammad was six hundred years and whatever God willed of that. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: It was five hundred and sixty years. Al-Kalbi said: Five hundred and forty years. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jarir that he said: It was five hundred years. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak that he said: It was four hundred and thirty-some years. Ibn Saad narrated in his book al-Tabaqat on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: There were one thousand nine hundred years between Moses and Jesus and there was no gap between them, for between them a thousand prophets from the Children of Israel were sent in addition to those who were sent from others. And between the birth of Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, there were five hundred and sixty-nine years, in the first of which He sent three prophets as God the Most High said: When We sent to them two, but they denied them, so We reinforced them with a third, and the one who was reinforced was Simon, who was one of the disciples. And the period in which God did not send a messenger was four hundred and thirty-four years. And other than what we have mentioned has been said.
5:20: These verses include a statement from God Almighty that the ancestors of the Jews who were present in the time of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, rebelled against Moses and disobeyed him, just as these rebelled against our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and disobeyed him, and in that is consolation for him, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Kathir that he read: 20- O my people, remember with a damma on the meem, and he read it likewise in what is similar to it, and its meaning is: O people, remember the favor of God upon you when He made prophets among you: meaning the time of this making, and the occurrence of the mention at the time while the intended meaning is what happened in it of incidents for the sake of exaggeration, because the command to mention the time is a command to mention what happened in it by way of priority, and God Almighty bestowed His favor upon them by making prophets among them although He had made prophets from other than them, due to the large number of prophets He sent from among them, His saying: And made you kings meaning and made kings from among you, and the preposition was deleted because it is clear that the meaning of the speech is as it is, and it is possible that It is said: The position of prophethood, due to its great value and great importance, is such that it cannot be attributed to anyone other than its owner, He said about it: When He made prophets among you. And since the position of kingship is something that can be attributed to anyone other than the one who said it, as the kinship of kingship says, We are kings, He said about it: And He made you kings. And it was said that what is meant by kingship is that they took control of their affairs after they were owned by Pharaoh, so they are all kings in this sense. And it was said that its meaning is that He made them people of status that no one else could enter upon except with permission, and other things were said. And it appears that what is meant by the verse is the real kingship, and if it had another meaning, there would not have been much meaning to the gratitude for it. If you say: He made others kings as He made them. You say: The kings have multiplied among them as the prophets have multiplied, so this is the aspect of gratitude. His statement: And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds, meaning manna, quails, stones, clouds, the multitude of prophets, the multitude of kings, and other things. And what is meant are the worldly people of their time. It was said that the address here is to the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is a deviation from the apparent meaning that is not necessary. The correct view is what the majority of commentators have stated, that it is from the speech of Moses to his people, and he addressed them with this speech as a prelude and preparation for what follows, of his command to them to enter the Holy Land.
5:21: There is a difference of opinion about its specification. Qatada said: It is Ash-Sham. Mujahid said: At-Tur and what is around it. Ibn Abbas, As-Suddi and others said: Jericho. Az-Zajjaj said: Damascus, Palestine and some of Jordan. Qatada’s statement: It includes all the statements mentioned after it. And the sacred: the purified, and it was said: the blessed 21- which God has decreed for you meaning He has divided and determined for them in His prior knowledge and made it a dwelling place for you. And do not turn back meaning do not go back on My command and abandon My obedience and what I have obligated upon you of fighting the tyrants out of cowardice and failure for you will become because of that losers of the good of this world and the hereafter.
5:22: 22- They said, 'O Moses, indeed therein are a people of tyrants.' Al-Zajjaj said: A tyrant is a violent human being, and he is the one who forces people to do what he wants. Its origin is from compulsion, which is coercion, as he forces others to do what he wants. It is said that he compelled him: if he forced him, and it was said that it is taken from the word jabr al-azm, so the origin of the word jabr is the one who reforms his own affairs, then it was used for anyone who brings benefit to himself, whether rightly or wrongly. It was said that jabr al-azm goes back to the meaning of compulsion. Al-Farra' said: I did not hear a fa'al from af'al except in two letters, jabar from ajbara, and draak from draak. What is meant here is that they are a people of large bodies, tall and proud. It is said that they are a people from the remnants of the people of Aad, and it is said that they are from the descendants of Esau, son of Isaac, and it is said that they are from the Romans. It is said that among them is Awj ibn Anq, who is famous for his excessive height, and Anq is the daughter of Adam. It is said that his height was three thousand, three hundred and thirty-three cubits and a third of a cubit. Ibn Kathir said: This is something that is embarrassing to mention, and it contradicts what is proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God created Adam and his height was sixty cubits, and then creation continued to decrease. Then they mentioned that this man was a disbeliever, and that he was the son of fornication, and that he refused to board the ship and that the flood did not reach his knees, and this is a lie and slander, because God mentioned that Noah called upon the people of the earth from the disbelievers and said: My Lord, leave not upon the earth from the disbelievers a single dwelling, and God the Almighty said: “So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship. Then We drowned after him the rest,” and God the Almighty said: There is no protector this day from the decree of God except for him on whom He has mercy. If the disbelieving son of Noah drowned, then how could Awj ibn Anq remain while he was a disbeliever who was the son of fornication? This is not permissible in reason or Sharia, and in the presence of a man called Awj ibn Anq, and God knows best. End of his words. I said: There is nothing in the matter of this man that would require a long discussion about him, and this is not the first lie that has become famous among the people, and we are not obligated to reject the lies that storytellers have fabricated and that have been spread by those who do not distinguish between the correct and the unsound. How many lies, calamities and stories are there in the books of interpretations, all of which are mere myths. How much more deserving is someone who has no distinction or knowledge of the art of narration to abandon the interpretation of the Book of God, and to place these foolishnesses and jokes in their appropriate places in the books of storytellers. His saying: But if they leave it, then we will enter is an explicit statement of what is understood from the sentence before this sentence to show that their refusal to enter is for this reason only.
5:23: His saying: 23- Two men said they were Joshua and Caleb bin Yufna or bin Fania, and they were among the twelve leaders as explained earlier. And his saying: of those who fear meaning they fear God Almighty, and it was said of the tyrants: meaning these two men are among the people who fear the tyrants, and it was said of those who fear the weakness and cowardice of the Children of Israel, and it was said that the waw in they fear is for the Children of Israel: meaning of those whom the Children of Israel fear. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubayr read they fear with a damma on the ya: meaning others fear them. His saying: God bestowed His favor upon them is in the nominative case as a second description of two men, with faith and certainty in obtaining what they were promised of victory and triumph Enter upon them through the gate meaning the gate of the land of the tyrants and when you enter it, you will be victorious they said: This statement is for the Children of Israel. It appears that they knew this from the story of Moses, or they said it out of trust in God’s promise, or they knew that the hearts of the tyrants were filled with fear and terror.
5:24: 24- They said meaning the Children of Israel to Moses We will never enter it as long as they are in it and this statement from them was failure and cowardice or stubbornness and boldness towards God and His Messenger So go, you and your Lord, and fight they said this out of ignorance of God Almighty and His attributes and disbelief in what is due to Him, or disdain for God and His Messenger, and it was said that by going they meant the will and purpose, and it was said that by the Lord they meant Aaron, who was older than Moses, and Moses used to obey him We are sitting here meaning we will not leave here, we will not advance with you nor will we fall behind from this place, and it was said that by that they meant not advancing, not not falling behind.
5:25: 25- He said Moses My Lord, I have no control over anyone except myself and my brother It is possible that my brother is linked to myself, and that it is linked to the pronoun in I meaning that I have no control over anyone except myself and that my brother has no control over anyone except himself. He said this out of regret and sorrow and seeking victory from God the Almighty. So separate us from the wicked people meaning separate us - meaning himself and his brother - from the wicked people and distinguish us from their group and do not include us with them in the punishment. It was said that the meaning is: so judge between us and them. It was said that he only meant in the Hereafter. Ubayd ibn Umair read so separate with a kasra on the ra.
5:26: 26- "He said, 'It is forbidden to them' meaning the Holy Land, 'for forty years', meaning these disobedient ones, because of their refusal to fight the tyrants. This is a circumstance for the prohibition: meaning that it is forbidden to them to enter it for this period, no more. This prohibition does not contradict what was mentioned before in His statement, 'which God has decreed for you', for it is written for whoever remains after this period. It was said that none of those who said, 'We will never enter it' entered it, so the timing of the prohibition is this period in consideration of their offspring. It was said that 'forty years' is a circumstance for His statement, 'They will wander in the land', meaning they will wander this amount of time, so the prohibition is absolute. Al-Muwaqqit: is wandering, and in the language it means confusion. It is said from it: he wandered, wanders, wanders, wandering, or wandering, if he is confused. So the meaning is: they are confused in the land. It was said that this land in which they wandered was small, about six leagues. They would spend the evening where they woke up and wake up where they spent the evening. They were constantly traveling in that, with no rest. Scholars differed as to whether Moses and Aaron were with them or not. It was said that they were not with them because wandering is a punishment. It was also said that they were with them but that God made it easy for them, just as He made the fire cool and safe for Abraham. It was also said, how could this happen to a group of rational people in such a small area for such a long period of time? Abu Ali said: This would be because God would move the land they were on when they slept to the place they started from. It could also be due to other reasons that prevent them from leaving it by way of an extraordinary miracle. Abdur-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And made you kings, he said: He made them kings of servants, and they were the first to own servants. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: If a man from the Children of Israel had a wife, a servant and a house, he was called a king. Abdur-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse: He said: The wife, the servant and the house. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And made you kings, he said: The woman and the servants. And gave you that which He had not given to anyone in the worlds, he said: Those who were among them at that time. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) who said: If one of the Children of Israel had a servant, an animal and a woman, he was written as a king. Ibn Jarir and Al-Zubayr bin Bakkar narrated in Al-Mawqeet on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever has a house and a servant is a king. Abu Dawud narrated in his Marasil on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam regarding the verse who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A wife, a home, and a servant. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas that a man asked him: Are we not among the poor emigrants? He said: Do you have a wife to take refuge with? He said: Yes. He said: Do you have a home to live in? He said: Yes. He said: Then you are among the rich. He said: I have a servant. He said: Then you are among the kings. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And made you kings, he said: He made for them wives, servants, and homes. And gave you that which He had not given to anyone in the worlds, he said: Manna, quails, stones, and clouds. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: Manna, quails, stones, and clouds. It has been proven in the authentic hadith: Whoever among you wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his home, and has his daily sustenance, it is as if the entire world has been given to him. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Enter the Holy Land, he said: At-Tur and what is around it. He also narrated on his authority that he said: It is Jericho. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal that he said: It is what is between Arish and the Euphrates. Abd al-Razzaq and Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah that he said: It is Ash-Sham. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of As-Suddi regarding his statement: which God has prescribed for you, he said: Which God has commanded you to do. And Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: The people were commanded to do it as we were commanded to do the prayer, the zakat, the Hajj and the Umrah. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Moses was commanded to enter the city of the giants, so he marched with those with him until he stopped near the city, which is Jericho, so he sent to them twelve spies, one from each tribe, to bring him report of the people, so they entered the city and saw a great matter in their appearance, their body and their size, so they entered a garden belonging to some of them, so the owner of the garden came to pick the fruits from his garden, so he started picking the fruits and looked at their tracks and followed them, and whenever he found one of them, he took him and put him in his sleeve with the fruit until he picked all twelve and put them in his sleeve with the fruit, and he went to their king and scattered them before him, so the king said: You have seen our matter and our matter, go and inform your master, he said: So they returned to Moses and informed him of what they had seen of their matter, so he said: Keep it secret from us, so the man started telling his father and his friend He said: Hide it from me. So it was spread in their camp, and only two men kept it a secret: Joshua bin Nun and Caleb bin Yufna, and they are the ones about whom God revealed, Two men of those who feared said. Something similar to this has been narrated, which includes exaggeration in describing these people and the size of their bodies. There is no benefit in expanding on that, as most of it is lies of storytellers, as we have mentioned. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then separate, he said: Judge. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Separate between us and them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then it is forbidden to them, he said: Forever. And regarding his statement, They will wander in the land, he said: Forty years. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They wandered for forty years, and Moses and Aaron perished in the wilderness, as did everyone who was over forty years old. When the forty years had passed, Joshua bin Nun, who was the one who took over the matter after Moses, and he was the one who opened it and he was the one who was told that today is Friday, opposed them. They intended to open it, but the sun was about to set, and he feared that if Saturday night came, they would sleep. So he called out to the sun, I am commanded and you are commanded, and it stopped until it opened it. He found in it wealth that had never been seen before, so they brought it close to the fire, but it did not come. So he said: There is embezzlement among you. So he called the heads of the tribes, who were twelve men, and pledged allegiance to them, and the hand of one of them stuck to his hand. So he said: The embezzlement is with you, so bring it out. So he brought out the head of a cow made of gold with eyes of ruby and teeth of pearls, and he placed it with the offering, and the fire came and consumed it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Clothes were created for them in the wilderness that would not wear out or get dirty.
5:27: The connection between this and what came before it is the warning from God that the injustice of the Jews and their breach of covenants and agreements is like the injustice of a son of Adam to his brother. The disease is ancient and the evil is original. Scholars differed about the two sons of Adam mentioned, were they from his loins or not? The majority held the first opinion. Al-Hasan and Al-Dahhak held the second opinion, and said: They were from the Children of Israel, and they were used as an example to demonstrate the envy of the Jews. There was a dispute between them, so they offered two sacrifices, and sacrifices were only offered by the Children of Israel. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is an illusion. How could anyone from the Children of Israel be ignorant of the manner of burial, so that he would follow the example of the crow? The majority of the Companions and those who came after them said: Their names were Qabil and Abel, and Qabil’s sacrifice was a bundle of ears of corn, because he was a farmer and chose it from the worst of his crops, until he found a good ear of corn in it, so he rubbed it and ate it. Abel’s sacrifice was a ram, because he was a sheep owner and took it from the best of his sheep. Abel’s sacrifice was accepted, so he was taken to Paradise, and he continued to graze it until he ransomed the sacrificed one, peace be upon him. This is what a group of the Salaf said, and Qabil’s sacrifice was not accepted, so he envied him and said: I will kill you. It was said that the reason for this sacrifice was that Eve gave birth in every womb to a male and a female, except for Seth, peace be upon him, for she gave birth to him alone. Adam, peace be upon him, used to marry the male from this womb to the female from the other womb, and his sister who was born with him was not permissible for him. So she gave birth with Cain to a beautiful sister named Iqlim, and with Abel to a sister who was not like that and her name was Lewdha. So when Adam wanted to marry her, Cain said: I have more right to my sister. So Adam ordered him but he did not obey, and he rebuked him but he did not refrain. So they agreed on the sacrifice and that the one who accepted his sacrifice would marry her. 27- His saying: with truth is related to an omitted word that was an attribute of the source of and recite meaning a recitation that is clothed in truth, or an attribute of report: meaning report clothed in truth, and what is meant by one of them is Abel and by the other is Cain. And he said, I will kill you is a rhetorical resumption as if it were: So what did the one whose sacrifice was not accepted say? His saying: He said, ‘God only accepts from those who fear Him’ is a resumption like the first, as if it were said: So what did the one whose offering was accepted say? It is only for the sake of limitation: that is, God only accepts the offering from those who fear Him, not from others. It is as if he is saying to his brother: You only came from yourself, not from me, for the non-acceptance of your offering is due to your lack of piety.
5:28: His saying: 28- If you stretch out your hand against me to kill me meaning if you intend to kill me, and the lam is the introductory particle, and I am not stretching out is the answer to the oath that takes the place of the answer to the condition, and this is a surrender to killing from Abel, as mentioned in the hadith: "If there is a trial, then be like the best of the sons of Adam, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse." Mujahid said: It was obligatory for them at that time that no one should draw a sword and that he should not resist whoever wanted to kill him. Al-Qurtubi said: Our scholars said: This is something that may be mentioned as an act of worship, except that in our law it is permissible to repel him by consensus, and there is a difference of opinion regarding the obligation of that upon him. The most correct view is that it is obligatory because it forbids evil. Among the literalists are some who do not permit the one who is attacked to repel, and they cited the hadith of Abu Dharr, and the scholars interpreted it as meaning leaving fighting in trial and refraining from fighting when there is doubt, as we explained in the book of At-Tadhkirah. End of Al-Qurtubi's words. The hadith of Abu Dharr referred to is in Muslim and the Sunan scholars except al-Nasa’i, and it says: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: O Abu Dharr, what do you think if people kill one another? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Sit in your house and close your door. He said: If I do not leave you alone? He said: Then go to whoever you are from among them and be with them. He said: Should I take my weapon? He said: Then you will participate with them in what they are doing, but if you fear that the radiance of the sword will deter you, then throw the edge of your cloak over your face so that he will bear his sin and your sin.” There are hadiths with a similar meaning from a group of the Companions, Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, Abu Hurayrah, Khabbab ibn al-Arat, Abu Bakr, Ibn Mas’ud, Abu Waqid, and Abu Musa.
5:29: His saying: 29- I want you to bear my sin and your sin and be among the companions of the Fire. This is an explanation for his refraining from fighting after the first explanation, which is I fear God, Lord of the worlds. The commentators differed on the meaning. It was said: Abel meant that I want you to bear the sin that would have befallen me if I had been keen to kill you, and the sin that you bore because of killing me. It was also said that what is meant is my sin that is specific to me because of a reason that will come and be cast upon you because of your injustice towards me and you will bear your sin in killing me. This is consistent with the meaning of what was proven in Sahih Muslim from the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “On the Day of Resurrection, the oppressor and the oppressed will be brought, and the good deeds of the oppressor will be taken and added to the good deeds of the oppressed until justice is done. If he has no good deeds, the bad deeds of the oppressed will be taken and cast upon him.” Similar to this is the saying of God the Almighty: And they will bear their burdens and other burdens with their burdens. It was also said that the meaning is: I want you not to bear my sin and your sin, as in the saying of God the Almighty: And He has cast into the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with you. That is, so that it would not shake with you. And His saying: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray. That is, so that you do not go astray. Most scholars said: The meaning is, I want you to bear my sin, meaning the sin of killing me, and your sin, which has been committed on you because of your sins before killing me. Al-Tha’labi said: This is the opinion of most commentators. It was also said that it is in the form of denial, meaning or I want in the form of denial, like the Almighty’s saying: And that is a blessing, meaning or that is a blessing. Al-Qushayri said this, and his explanation is that the intention to kill is a sin. Abu al-Hasan ibn Kaysan was asked: How can a believer want his brother to sin and enter Hell? He said: The intention occurred after he stretched out his hand to kill him, and this is very far-fetched, as is the one before it. The root of ba’ returns to maba’ah, which is the place of residence - and they returned with wrath from God - meaning they returned.
5:30: His statement: 30- So his soul made the killing of his brother easy for him meaning his soul made the matter easy for him and encouraged him and made it appear to him that killing his brother was easy for him. It is said that something was made easy and compliant and someone made it easy for him. Al-Harawi said: I made it easy and complied with someone. It is said that someone obeyed him: if he did it willingly. In mentioning his making himself willing to do it after what preceded from Cain's saying: I will kill you and Abel's saying: So that you kill me is evidence that he had not yet been willing to do it at that contract. His statement: So he killed him. Ibn Jarir, Mujahid and others said: It was narrated that he did not know how to kill his brother so Satan came to him with a bird or other animal and started smashing his head between two stones so that Cain would follow his example and he did it. Other things were said that require verification of the narration.
5:31: His saying: 31- So God sent a raven digging in the ground to show him how to hide his brother's private parts. It was said that when he killed his brother, he did not know how to hide him because he was the first human being to die, so God sent two ravens, brothers, and they fought, and one of them killed the other, so he dug a hole for him and threw it over him. When Cain saw him, he said, Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and hide my brother's private parts? So he hid him, and the pronoun implied in to show him refers to the raven, and it was said to refer to God, the Most High, and how is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun to hide and the sentence is the second object of show him. What is meant by the private parts here is his entire self because it is dead, and said is a resumption of the answer to a question implied from the context of the speech, as if it was said: So what did he say when he saw the raven doing that?
