Woe to me is a word that expresses regret and sadness. The alif is a substitute for the speaker's ya, as if he called for his woe to be present at that time. Woe is destruction. The speech is outside the context of astonishment at his not being guided to bury his brother as the crow was guided to do. So I bury is in the accusative case as the answer to the question. It was read with the sukoon on the assumption that I bury. So he became one of the regretters for killing him. It was said that his regret was not the regret of repentance, but regret for losing him, not for killing him. Others were said. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: “He forbade a woman to marry her twin brother, or to marry another of her brothers. He used to have a man and a woman born to him in every pregnancy. While they were like that, a beautiful woman was born to him and another ugly, hideous woman was born to him. The brother of the ugly woman said: Marry me to your sister and I will marry you to my sister. He said: No, I have more right to my sister. So they offered a sacrifice. The owner of the sheep brought a white, horned ram, and the owner of the farm brought a heap of food. It was accepted from the owner of the ram, but it was not accepted from the owner of the farm.” Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation: Its chain of transmission is good. Al-Suyuti said the same in al-Durr al-Manthur. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: It was the custom of the sons of Adam that there was no poor person to whom charity was given, but the sacrifice was offered by a man. While the sons of Adam were sitting, they said: If we offered a sacrifice, then they remembered what they offered. Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: If you should stretch out your hand against me, he said: It was written for them that if a man wanted to kill a man, he should let him go and not refrain from him. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar from Ibn Jurayj. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin, he said: I want your sin and my blood to be upon you, so that you bear both of them. Ibn Jarir narrated from him: With my sin, he said: By killing me. And your sin, he said: For what you did before that. And he narrated something similar from Qatada and al-Dahhak. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: Then his soul encouraged him to kill his brother, he said: It encouraged him to kill his brother. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Qatada regarding the verse: He said: His soul made it seem good to him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud and some of the Companions regarding his statement: Then his soul prompted him to kill his brother, so he sought him out to kill him. The boy finished with him on the mountaintops. One day, he came to him while he was grazing his sheep and he was asleep. He lifted a rock and smashed his head with it, so he died. He left him in the open and did not know how to bury him. Then God sent two ravens, brothers, and they fought. One of them killed the other, so he dug a grave for him and threw stones at him. When he saw him, he said, ‘Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven?’ It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others from the hadith of Ibn Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam will bear a share of its blood, because he was the first to institute killing. Narrations have been narrated about the description of his killing of his brother, and God knows best their authenticity.
5:32: His saying: 32- For that meaning for that murderer and his crime and because of his disobedience. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning because of his crime. He said: It is said that a man postponed an evil upon his family, he postpones a term if he committed a crime like he took, he takes, taking. Abu Ja`far read for that with a kasra on the noon and deleting the hamza, and it is a language. He said in the explanation of Al-Durrah: Abu Ja`far read alone for that with a kasra on the hamza and transferring its vowel to the noon before it. It was said that it is permissible for his saying: for that to be related to his saying: of the regretful ones so the pause would be at his saying: for that and what is preferable is what we have presented, and the meaning is: that the report of the two sons of Adam is what caused the aforementioned writing upon the Children of Israel, and this is the majority of the commentators. The Children of Israel were mentioned specifically because the context enumerates their crimes, and because they were the first nation to whom the threat of killing people was sent down, and the severity was imposed on them at that time due to their frequent bloodshed and killing of prophets. The placement of the prepositional phrase before the verb to which it is related, I mean our books, indicates restriction: that is, because of that and not otherwise, and from is for the beginning of the goal. Whoever kills a soul one of these souls unless for a soul that is, without a soul, retaliation is required, so whoever kills a soul for a soul is excluded from this. His statement: or corruption in the land The majority read it in the accusative case in apposition to soul. Al-Hasan read it in the accusative case, estimating an omitted verb indicated by the beginning of the speech, which is: or causing corruption in the land, and this is weak. The meaning of the reading of the majority is that whoever kills a soul without a reason for retaliation or corruption in the land, it is as if he killed all of mankind. It has been decided that every conditional ruling in which one of two things is achieved, its opposite is conditional on their absence together, and every ruling in which both are achieved, its opposite is conditional on the absence of one of them, because the opposite of everything is conditional on the opposite of its condition. There is a difference of opinion about this corruption mentioned in this verse: What is it? Some say it is polytheism, and others say it is highway robbery. The apparent meaning of the Qur’anic system is that it is true that it is corruption on earth. So polytheism is corruption on earth, highway robbery is corruption on earth, shedding blood, violating the sanctity, and plundering wealth is corruption on earth, and oppressing God’s servants without right is corruption on earth, and demolishing buildings, cutting down trees, and draining rivers is corruption on earth. So you know from this that it is true of these types that it is corruption on earth, and likewise the corruption that will come in His statement: And they strive to cause corruption in the land is true of these types, and we will discuss the full meaning of corruption soon. His statement: As if he had killed all mankind. The commentators differed in the realization of this simile to determine that the punishment of one who kills all mankind is more severe than the punishment of one who kills one of them. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The meaning is that whoever kills a prophet or a just imam is as if he had killed all mankind, and whoever revives him by strengthening his arm and supporting him is as if he had revived all mankind. This was narrated from him by Ibn Jarir. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: The meaning is that whoever intentionally kills a believing soul, God will make his punishment Hell, become angry with him, curse him, and prepare for him a great punishment. If he killed all of the people, it would not be more than this. He said: And whoever is saved from being killed and has not killed anyone, it is as if he has saved all of the people. Something similar to this was narrated from him by Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said in his interpretation of this verse: Whoever destroys himself is as if he had killed all of humanity. It was narrated from him by Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. It was narrated from Al-Hasan that he said: It is as if he had killed all of humanity in sin, and as if he had saved all of humanity in reward. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is that whoever kills a soul is liable for the same retaliation and retribution as whoever kills all of humanity. And whoever saves a life means whoever pardons someone whose killing is obligatory. Al-Qurtubi narrated this from him. It was narrated from Al-Hasan that it means pardoning after being able to do so: meaning, saving a life. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that reviving it means saving it from drowning, burning, demolition or destruction. This was narrated on his authority by Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir. It was said that the meaning is that whoever kills a soul, all the believers are his opponents, because he has made everyone weak. And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, meaning everyone must thank him. It was also said that the meaning is that whoever considers one person permissible has considered all of them permissible because he has denied the Shari’ah. In any case, reviving here is an expression for abandonment and saving from destruction, so it is a metaphor, since the true meaning is specific to God Almighty. What is meant by this simile in the aspect of killing is to exaggerate the matter of killing and magnify its matter in people so that the bold and daring will be deterred from it. In the aspect of reviving, it is to encourage forgiveness of the criminals and rescue those involved in destruction. His saying: And Our messengers came to them with clear proofs is an independent clause confirmed by the lam that introduces the oath and includes the report that the messengers, peace and blessings be upon them, came to the servants with what God has prescribed for them of rulings, among which is the command to kill. Then in His saying: Then indeed many of them is for the hierarchical delay and rational improbability, and the reference in His saying: That is to what was mentioned of what God wrote for the Children of Israel: that is, indeed many of them after that writing in the land are transgressors in killing.
5:33: His saying: 33- The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger People differed about the reason for the revelation of this verse. The majority of scholars said that it was revealed about the Arabs. Malik, Al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr, and the People of Opinion said: Because it was revealed about those Muslims who went out to cut off the road and spread corruption in the land. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: Malik's statement is correct.
5:34: Abu Thawr said, arguing for this statement: His statement in this verse 34 - Except those who repent before you have them in your power indicates that it was revealed for people other than polytheists, because they have agreed that if the polytheists fall into our hands and submit to Islam, their blood is forbidden, so this indicates that the verse was revealed for the people of Islam. End quote. Similarly, the statement of God the Almighty: Say to those who disbelieve, if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them, and the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Islam destroys what came before it. Narrated by Muslim and others. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated in his interpretation from some of the people of knowledge that this verse - I mean the verse on fighting - abrogated the action of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with the two 'Arniyyin, and the matter was limited to these punishments. It was narrated from Muhammad ibn Sirin that he said: This was before the punishments were revealed, meaning his action with the two 'Arniyyin, and this is what a group of the people of knowledge said. Another group went to that his action with the two Arabs was abrogated by the Prophet’s prohibition of mutilation, and the one who says this is required to explain the delay of the abrogator, and the context of the narrations mentioned in the reason for revelation will come. The truth is that this verse includes the polytheist and others who committed what it includes, and no consideration is given to the specific reason, but rather consideration is given to the generality of the wording. Al-Qurtubi said in his interpretation: There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that the ruling of this verse is based on those who fight among the people of Islam, even if it was revealed about the apostates or the Jews. The end. The meaning of his saying based: that is, established. It was said that what is meant by fighting God mentioned in the verse is fighting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and fighting the Muslims in his time and after his time by way of expression without indication and without analogy, because the text was not transmitted by way of verbal address so that its ruling is specific to those who are accountable at the time of revelation, so it requires another proof to generalize the address to others. It was said that it made fighting the Muslims fighting God and His Messenger in order to magnify their war and magnify their harm, because God, the Almighty, does not fight or overcome. It is better to interpret fighting God the Almighty with disobeying Him and violating His laws, and fighting the Messenger should be understood in its true meaning, and the rule of his nation is his rule and they are his role models. Striving to spread corruption on earth refers to types of evil, as we mentioned earlier. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation: Many of the Salaf, including Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, said: Lending dirhams and dinars is a form of corruption on earth, and God the Almighty said: “And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And God does not like corruption.” End quote. If you have decided what we have decided regarding the generality of the verse and the meaning of fighting and striving to spread corruption on earth, then know that this applies to everyone who has done that, whether he is a Muslim or a disbeliever, in Egypt or elsewhere, in every little and big thing, great and insignificant, and that the ruling of God in that is what is mentioned in this verse of killing or crucifixion, or cutting off the hands and feet from opposite sides, or banishment from the land, but this is not the ruling of one who has committed any sin, rather of one whose sin is transgression against the blood and wealth of the servants except for what has been mentioned in the Book of God or the Sunnah of His Messenger, such as theft and what requires retaliation, because we know that in his time, may God bless him and grant him peace, there were those who committed sins and transgressions other than that, and this ruling mentioned in this verse does not apply to him, may God bless him and grant him peace. And with this you will know the weakness of what was narrated from Mujahid in interpreting the fighting mentioned in this verse as adultery and theft, and the reason for that is that these two sins have been mentioned in the Book of God and in the Sunnah of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, for them to have a ruling other than this ruling. If you know what is apparent from the meaning of this verse according to the language of the Arabs, which we were commanded to interpret the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger with, then beware of being deceived by any of the narrated details and the narrated doctrines, unless you come to evidence that requires specifying this generality or restricting this meaning understood from the language of the Arabs, then you and that is it, act upon it and put it in its place. As for what is other than that: So leave the loot that was shouted at in its rooms and bring up a story that is not the story of the camels We will mention from these schools of thought what you will hear. Know that scholars have differed about who deserves the name of a bandit. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Ata, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Ad-Dahhak and Abu Thawr said: Whoever brandishes a weapon in the sanctuary of Islam and frightens the wayfarer, then is captured and overpowered, the Imam of the Muslims has the choice regarding him: if he wishes, he can kill him, if he wishes, he can crucify him, or if he wishes, he can cut off his hand and foot. Malik said this and he made it clear that a bandit in his view is someone who attacks people in Egypt or in the wilderness or who attacks them with their lives and wealth without any fear, humiliation or enmity. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: There is a difference of opinion regarding Malik regarding this issue. He affirmed fighting in the country once and denied it another time. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas other than what was mentioned above. He said regarding highway robbers: If they kill and take money, they are killed and crucified. If they kill but do not take money, they are killed but not crucified. If they take money but do not kill, their hands and feet are cut off from opposite sides. If they frighten the wayfarer but do not take money, they are banished from the land. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Majlaz, Saeed bin Jubair, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, As-Suddi and Ata’ with differences in narration from some of them. Ibn Kathir narrated it from the majority. He also said: And this is how it was narrated on the authority of more than one of the predecessors and imams. Abu Hanifa said: If he kills, he is killed. If he takes money and does not kill, his hand and foot are cut off on opposite sides. If he takes money and kills, the ruler has a choice: if he wants, he may cut off his hands and feet, or if he does not want, he may kill him and crucify him. Abu Yusuf said: Killing comes for everything, and Al-Awza’i said something similar. Al-Shafi’i said: If he takes money, his right hand is cut off and branded, then his left foot is cut off and branded and he is released, because this crime is more than theft by banditry. If he kills, he is killed. If he takes money and kills, he is killed and crucified. It was narrated on his authority that he said: He is crucified for three days. Ahmad said: If he kills, he is killed, and if he takes money, his hand and foot are cut off, as al-Shafi’i said. I do not know of any evidence for these details, neither from the Book of God nor from the Sunnah of His Messenger, except what Ibn Jarir narrated in his Tafsir, and he was the only one to narrate it. He said: Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib: Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to Anas ibn Malik asking him about this verse, so he wrote to him informing him that this verse was revealed about those Arab men who were from Bajila. Anas said: They apostatized from Islam, killed the shepherd, drove away the camels, frightened the wayfarer, and violated the forbidden vagina. Anas said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel about the ruling on those who wage war, and he said: Whoever steals and frightens the wayfarer, cut off his hand for his theft and his foot for his treason, and whoever kills, kill him, and whoever kills, frightens the wayfarer, and permits the forbidden vagina, crucify him. And this, with its extreme strangeness, it is not known how authentic it is. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation after mentioning some of the details that we mentioned, the following: This detail is supported by the hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir in his interpretation, if its chain of transmission is sound, and then he mentioned it. His statement, and they strive to cause corruption in the land is either in the accusative case as a source, or as an object for it, or as a state by interpretation: i.e. corrupters. His statement, or they are crucified appears to mean that they are crucified alive until they die, because it is one of the types that God has given a choice between. Some people said: Crucifixion only occurs after killing, and it is not permissible to crucify before killing, preventing one from praying, eating, and drinking. The answer is that this is a punishment that God, the Exalted, has prescribed in His Book for His servants. His statement, or their hands and feet are cut off on opposite sides appears to mean cutting off one of the hands and one of the feet on opposite sides, whether the severed hand is the right or the left, and likewise the feet. It is not considered unless the cutting is through either the right hand with the left foot or the left hand with the right foot. It was said that what is meant by this is cutting off only the right hand and the left foot. His statement: or banished from the land The commentators differed in its meaning. Al-Suddi said: It is that he is sought by horse and foot until he is captured and the prescribed punishment is carried out on him or he is expelled from the land of Islam by fleeing. This is narrated from Ibn Abbas, Anas, Malik, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Al-Suddi, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Rabi bin Anas and Al-Zuhri. Al-Rumani narrated it in his book from them. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i that they are taken from one country to another and sought out for the prescribed punishments to be carried out on them. Al-Layth bin Sa’d said the same. It was narrated from Malik that he is banished from the country in which he committed the sin to another and imprisoned there like the adulterer. Ibn Jarir and Al-Qurtubi preferred this view. The Kufians said: Their banishment is their imprisonment, so he is banished from the spaciousness of this world to its narrowness. What is apparent from the verse is that he is expelled from the land in which he committed what he committed, without imprisonment or anything else. Banishment may mean destruction, but it is not intended here. His statement: That is for them a disgrace in this world refers to what was previously mentioned of the rulings, and disgrace means humiliation and scandal. His statement: “Except for those who repent before you have power over them. Know that God is Forgiving and Merciful.” God, the Exalted, has excluded those who repent before you have power over them from the generality of those who are punished with the previous punishments. It appears that there is no difference between blood and property and other sins that warrant specific, limited punishments, so the one who repents before he has power is not required to do anything of that, and this is what the Companions did. Some scholars have said that retaliation and all other human rights are not dropped by repentance before he has power, and the first right. As for repentance after he has power over them, the punishment mentioned in the verse is not dropped by it, as is indicated by the mention of the condition before you have power over them. Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars are unanimously agreed that the ruler is the guardian of the one who wages war. If a warrior kills a man’s brother and comes to him in a state of war, then the one seeking blood money has no right to do anything regarding the war, and the pardon of the guardian of the blood is not permissible. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel meaning: because of the son of Adam who killed his brother unjustly. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he was asked about this verse, meaning his statement: It is as if he had killed all of mankind, is it for us as it was for the Children of Israel? He said: That is, by the One besides Whom there is no god. Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger he said: It was revealed regarding the polytheists, so whoever among them repents before he is overpowered, there is no way against him. This verse does not protect a Muslim man from the prescribed punishment if he kills or spreads corruption on earth or wages war against God and His Messenger. Ibn Jarir and Al-Tabarani in Al-Kabeer narrated on his authority regarding this verse, he said: There were some people from the People of the Book who had a covenant and pact with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they broke the covenant and spread corruption on earth. So God gave His Prophet the choice regarding them: If He wished, he could kill them, or if He wished, he could crucify them, or if He wished, he could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. As for exile, it is striking them throughout the land. If they come repentant and enter Islam, it is accepted from them, and what came before is not taken into account. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas that this verse was revealed about the Kharijites. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Anas that a group of Ukl came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), converted to Islam and settled in Madinah. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to go to the camels of charity and drink their urine and milk. They killed their shepherd and drove them away. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent a tracker in pursuit of them, and he brought them. He cut off their hands and feet, gouged out their eyes, and did not cauterize them and left them until they died. Then God revealed: The only reward of those who wage war is that they be killed or flogged. In Muslim, on the authority of Anas, he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only gouged out the eyes of those people because they had gouged out the eyes of the shepherds. Al-Shafi’i in Al-Umm, Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: If the warrior goes out and takes property but does not kill, he is to be cut off on opposite sides. If he goes out and kills but does not take property, he is to be killed. If he goes out and takes property and kills, he is to be killed and crucified. If he goes out and frightens people on the road but does not take property or kill, he is to be banished. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: Whoever brandishes a weapon in the sanctuary of Islam and corrupts the way and is overcome and oppressed, the leader of the Muslims has a choice regarding him: if he wants, he is to kill him, or if he wants, he is to crucify him, or if he wants, he is to cut off his hand and foot. He said: Or be banished from the land, they flee and leave the land of Islam to the land of war. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: His banishment is to be sought. He also narrated something similar on the authority of Anas. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Sha’bi who said: Haritha ibn Badr al-Taymi from the people of Basra had spread corruption and waged war on the earth. He spoke to some men from Quraysh asking Ali for protection for him, but they refused. So he went to Sa’id ibn Qays al-Hamdani and came to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is the punishment for those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption on earth? He said: That they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. Then he said: Except for those who repent before you are able to seize them. Sa’id said: What if it was Haritha ibn Badr? He said: What if it was Haritha ibn Badr? He said: This is Haritha ibn Badr, he has come repentant, so he is safe. He said: Yes. So he brought him to him and pledged allegiance to him, and he accepted that from him and wrote him a letter of protection.
5:35: 35- Seek seek to Him not to anyone else, and the means is a verbal noun from I sought to seek to Him: if you approached Him. Antara said: Men have a way to get to you. If they take you, apply kohl and henna. Another said: If the informers are absent-minded, we will return to our connection and the children will return between us and the means Al-Wasila: The closeness that should be sought. Abu Wa’il, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said the same. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ata’, and Abdullah bin Kathir. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation: What these imams said, there is no disagreement among the interpreters about it. Al-Wasila is also a degree in Paradise that is specific to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari from the hadith of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says when he hears the call to prayer: ‘O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad the wasila and excellence and raise him to the praised station which You promised him,’ then intercession will be permitted for him on the Day of Resurrection.” In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When you hear the muezzin, say what he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends blessings upon me, God will send blessings upon him ten times. Then ask for me al-Wasila, for it is a station in Paradise that is not appropriate for anyone but one of God’s servants, and I hope that I am that one. Whoever asks for me al-Wasila, intercession will be granted to him.” There are hadiths on this topic, and the conjunction of and seek a means of approach to Him with O you who believe, fear God indicates that the means of approach is not piety. It was said that it is piety, because it is the essence of the matter and all good, so the second sentence, according to this, explains the first sentence. It appears that the means of approach, which is nearness, applies to piety and other good qualities by which servants draw near to their Lord. And strive in His cause for those whose religion is not accepted, that you may succeed.
5:36: His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve is a statement introduced to deter the disbelievers and encourage the Muslims to obey the commands of God, the Most High. If they had all that is on the earth of its wealth and benefits, and it was said that it is meant for each one of them to be more terrifying, although the apparent meaning of the collective pronoun is otherwise, and all together is an emphasis. His statement: And the like of it is in apposition to what is on the earth, and with it is in the accusative case as a state that they may ransom themselves with it to make it a ransom for themselves, and the pronoun was singular either because it refers back to what is mentioned or because it is in the position of a demonstrative pronoun: that is, that they may ransom themselves with that, and from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection is related to the mentioned verb that would not be accepted from them, and this is the answer to if.
5:37: His statement: 37- They want to get out of the Fire. This is a rhetorical resumption, as if it was said: How is their situation in this painful torment they are in? So it was said that they want to get out of the Fire. It was read that they get out from to get out. This reading is weakened by and they are not going out of it. The location of this sentence, I mean his statement: and they are not going out of it, is the accusative case of state, and it was said that it is an interjectional sentence. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And seek the means of approach to Him, that he said: The means of approach is nearness. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Hudhayfah, similarly. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, And seek the means of approach to Him, that he said: Draw near to God by obeying Him and doing what pleases Him. Muslim, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise. He said: He means the poor. So I said to Jabir, does God say, They want to get out of the Fire, but they will not get out of it? He said: Recite the beginning of the verse, Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and the like thereof with it, they would ransom themselves thereby. Indeed, they are the ones who disbelieved. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah: Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq said to Ibn Abbas: You claim that people will come out of the Fire, and God Almighty said: And they will never come out of it. Ibn Abbas said: Woe to you, read what is above it. This is for the disbelievers. Al-Zamakhshari said in Al-Kashshaf after mentioning this: It is one of the fabrications of the Jabariyah. Oh God, how amazing is a man who does not differentiate between the most authentic of the authentic hadiths and the most false of lies against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and discusses something he does not know and does not understand what it is? The hadiths have been transmitted in a continuous chain of transmission that is not hidden from anyone who has the slightest familiarity with the science of narration that the sinners among the monotheists will come out of the Fire. Whoever denies this is not qualified for debate, because he has denied what is one of the essentials of the Shari’ah. Oh God, forgive us.
5:38: When the Almighty mentioned the ruling on the one who takes money openly, which is the muharib, He followed it by mentioning the one who takes money secretly, which is the thief. He mentioned the female thief with the male thief for the sake of clarity, because most of the Qur’an limits its legislation to men. The scholars of grammar differed on the report of the male and female thief, is it implied or is it cut off? Sibawayh went with the first, and said that it is implied: in what is imposed upon you or in what is recited to you, the male and female thief: meaning their ruling. Al-Mubarrad and Al-Zajjaj went to the second, and the entry of the fa to include the subject with the meaning of the condition, as the meaning is: the one who stole and the one who stole, and it was read 38- and the thief and the female thief in the accusative case on the assumption of cut off, and Sibawayh preferred this reading, he said: The face in the speech of the Arabs is the accusative as you say Zaidan Idribah, but the common people refused except the nominative, meaning the majority of the readers, and theft with the kasra of the ra is the name of the stolen thing and the source is from saraqa yusraqa siraqa, Al-Jawhari said: It is taking something secretly from the eyes, and from it is the eavesdropping and the stealing of the sight. His saying: so cut off cutting means separation and removal, and the plural of hands is due to the undesirability of combining two duals, and the pure Sunnah has explained that the place of cutting off is the wrist. Some people said: It is cut off from the elbow. The Khawarij said: From the shoulder. Theft must be a quarter of a dinar or more, and it must be from a safe place as mentioned in the authentic hadiths. The majority have considered the quarter of a dinar as a quarter. Some people have estimated it at ten dirhams. The majority of scholars have considered the amulet as a safe haven. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: If the clothes are collected in the house, they are cut off. The scholars of jurisprudence and hadith commentators have discussed theft at length, and lengthening them up here will not be of much benefit. His statement: A recompense for what they have earned is an object for it: meaning, cut off for the recompense, or a source emphasizing an omitted verb: meaning, a recompense exceeded them, and the ba is causal, and ma is a source: meaning, because of what they have earned, or a relative: meaning, a recompense for what they have earned from theft. His statement: As a punishment is a substitute for as a punishment, and it was said that it is a reason for the recompense: and the recompense is a reason for the cutting off. It is said that I punished him: if you did to him what he should be punished for that action.
5:39: His saying: 39- Then God will accept his repentance but the wording is general and includes the thief and other sinners, and consideration is given to the generality of the wording and not to the specificity of the reason. Ata' and a group used this as evidence that the amputation is dropped by repentance, but this evidence is not correct, because this conditional sentence only indicates the acceptance of repentance, and God accepts the repentance of the one who repents, and there is nothing in it that indicates that there is no amputation for the one who repents. During the time of the Prophethood, someone who was required to receive a hadd would come to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, repenting for the sin he had committed, seeking to purify himself with the hadd, and the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, would punish him. It was narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, "that he said to the thief after his amputation: Repent to God, then he said: God accepts your repentance." Narrated by Ad-Daraqutni from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. Ahmad and others narrated that this verse was revealed about the woman who used to steal goods, when she said to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, after her amputation: Is there any repentance for me? The Sunnah contains evidence that if the punishments are referred to the imams, they are obligatory and it is not permissible to drop them.
5:40: His statement: 40- Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? This question is for denial while confirming knowledge, and it is like the title for His statement: He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills. That is, whoever has the dominion of the heavens and the earth, He is able to do this punishment entrusted to the will and forgiveness entrusted to it. Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: The recompense for what they have earned is a deterrent from God, he said: Do not feel sorry for them in it, for it is the command of God that He has commanded. He said: It was mentioned to us that Umar bin Al-Khattab used to say: Be harsh with the wicked and make them hand in hand and foot in foot. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, then indeed, God will turn to him in forgiveness, he said: The prescribed punishment is its expiation. The hadiths about the amount of the theft penalty and all other matters related to the details of this punishment are mentioned in the books of hadith, so we will not elaborate on that.
5:41: His saying: 41- Do not let it grieve you. Nafi' read it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the zay, and the rest read it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the zay. Grief and sadness are the opposites of joy, and a man grieved with a kasra, so he is grief and hapiness: and someone else grieved him and made him sad. Al-Yazidi said: Hazanahu is the language of Quraysh and ahzanahu is the language of Tamim, and both have been read. And in the verse is the prohibition of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from being deeply affected by the haste of the disbelievers in their disbelief, because God, the Exalted, has promised him victory over them in more than one place, and hastening to something means falling into it quickly. What is meant here is that they quickly fall into disbelief when the opportunity arises. The word fi is preferred over the word ila to indicate their stability in it. min in His statement, of those who said is explanatory, and the sentence explains those who rush into disbelief. The bi in with their mouths is connected to they said, not with our faith. These are the hypocrites who said they believed with their mouths, but their hearts did not believe. And of those who were Jews means the Jews, and it is conjoined with of those who said, “We believed, and it is the rest of the statement. The meaning is that those who rush into disbelief are a group of hypocrites and a group of Jews.
5:42: And his saying: 42- listeners to lies is the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning they are listeners to lies, so it refers to the two groups or to those who hasten, and the lam in his saying: to lies is for emphasis or to include the meaning of acceptance in listening, and it was said that his saying: listeners is the subject whose predicate is from among those who were Jews meaning and among those who were Jews are people listeners to lies meaning they are receptive to the lies of their leaders who distorted the Torah. His saying: listeners to another people is a second predicate, and the lam in it is like the lam in for lies, and it was said that the lam is for explanation in both places, meaning they are listeners to the words of the Messenger of God in order to lie about him, and listeners for the sake of another people whom they directed as spies for them in order to convey to them what they heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. His saying: They did not come to you is an attribute of a al-Nas 114:i.e. they did not attend your gathering, and they are a group of Jews who did not attend the gathering of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) out of arrogance and rebellion. It was also said that they were a group of hypocrites who avoided the gatherings of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Farra' said: Two hearings are permissible, as he said: Cursed wherever they are found. His saying: They distort words from their [proper] usages is among the attributes of the aforementioned al-Nas 114:i.e. they divert them from the usages in which God placed them and they interpret them in a way other than their interpretation. The distorters are the Jews, and it was said that this sentence is the predicate of a deleted subject, and it was said that it is in the accusative case as a state of they did not come to you, and it was said that it is a new sentence with no syntactic position in order to enumerate their faults and shortcomings. The meaning of after its places is after it was placed in its places, or after it was placed in the places in which God placed it in terms of its wording, or in terms of its meaning. His statement, They say, ‘If you are given this, then take it,’ is a circumstantial clause with the pronoun they distort, or a new sentence, or an attribute of a people, or the predicate of a deleted subject. The reference in their statement, this, is to the distorted speech: that is, if you are given this speech from Muhammad that we distorted, then take it and act upon it, and if you are not given it, but he comes to you with something else, then beware of accepting it and acting upon it. His statement: And he whom God intends to put to trial meaning his misguidance you will not possess for him anything from God meaning you will not be able to repel that from him nor will you be able to benefit him and guide him. This sentence is a new sentence confirming what preceded it, and its appearance is general and includes in it those with whom the context of the speech was initially included. The reference in His statement: those is to those mentioned previously from those who said with their mouths, We believe and from those who were Jews, and it is a subject and its predicate is those whose hearts God did not intend to purify: meaning He did not intend to purify them from the filth of disbelief and hypocrisy as He purified the hearts of the believers for them in this world is disgrace with the emergence of the hypocrisy of the hypocrites and the imposition of the jizya on the disbelievers and the emergence of their distortion and concealment of what God revealed in the Torah. His statement: listeners to falsehood He repeated it to emphasize its ugliness, and to be like an introduction to what follows it, which is devourers of unlawful gain and they are among the predicates of that previously implied subject. Al-Saht, with a dammah on the seen and a sukoon on the ha’, means unlawful money. Its origin is destruction and hardship, from the word sahtahu, meaning to destroy it. From this comes He will destroy you with torment. From this comes the saying of Al-Farazdaq: There was a time, O Ibn Marwan, when he did not leave any money except that it was wiped or shaved. The one who shaves is called ashat meaning he eradicated it. The forbidden is called sahtan because it eradicates and uproots acts of obedience. Al-Farra’ said: Its origin is the dog of hunger. It was also said that it is bribery, but the first is more correct. Bribery is included in the forbidden in a primary way. A group interpreted it as a specific type of forbidden things, such as a gift to someone who fulfills a need, or a soothsayer’s fee. Generalization is more correct. His statement: But if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them gives the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) a choice between judging between them and turning away from them. It has been used as evidence that Muslim rulers have a choice between the two matters. Scholars have agreed that Muslim rulers must judge between a Muslim and a dhimmi if they bring a case before them. They differed regarding the People of the Covenant if they bring a case against each other. Some people held that they have a choice, while others held that it is obligatory. They said that this verse was abrogated by the statement: And judge between them by what God has revealed. This is what Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Az-Zuhri, Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, and As-Suddi said. It is the correct statement of Ash-Shafi’i, and Al-Qurtubi narrated it from most scholars. His statement: But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. That is, if you choose to turn away from judging between them, they will have no power over you, because God is your protector and supporter against them. If you choose to judge between them, then judge between them with justice, that is, with the justice that God has commanded you and revealed to you.
5:43: His statement: 43- And how can they make you judge while they have the Torah in which is the judgment of God? In it is an astonishment to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, for their making him judge while they do not believe in him or in what he came with, even though what they make him judge is present in their Torah, such as stoning and the like. Rather, they come to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and make him judge out of their hope that it will agree with their distortion and what they have done to the Torah of changing it. His statement: Then they turn away is in apposition to they make you judge, "after that" meaning after they make you judge, and the whole of his statement: "And those are not believers" is to confirm the meaning of what preceded it.
5:44: And His saying: 44- Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. This is a resumption that includes the glorification of the Torah and the magnification of its status, and that it contains guidance and light, and it is the clarification of the laws and the good report of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the obligation to follow him. His saying: The prophets judge by it refers to the prophets of the Children of Israel, and the sentence is either a resumption or a conditional one, and those who submitted is a praiseworthy description of the prophets, and in it is a humiliation of the Jews who were his contemporaries, may God bless him and grant him peace, that their prophets followed the religion of Islam that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed. It was said that what is meant by the prophets is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he expressed it in the plural form for the sake of glorification. His saying: For those who are Jews is related to judges. The meaning is: that the prophets judge by it for those who are Jews over them. The rabbis are the learned wise men, and its explanation has been mentioned previously, and the rabbis are the learned scholars, taken from the word tahbeer which means improvement, so they improve knowledge: meaning they perfect it. Al-Jawhari said: The rabbi is one of the rabbis of the Jews, with the fat-ha and with the kasra, and the kasra is more eloquent. Al-Farra’ said: It is with the kasra, and Abu Ubaidah said: It is with the fat-ha. His statement: Because they preserved of the Book of God the ba’ is for causality, and they preserved were commanded to preserve: meaning the prophets commanded them to preserve the Torah from change and alteration, and the preposition and its object are related to they rule: meaning they rule by it because of this preservation. His statement: And they were witnesses over it meaning over the Book of God, and the witnesses are the watchers, so they protect against change and alteration with this watch, and the address in His saying: So fear not the people is to the leaders of the Jews, and likewise in His saying: And do not exchange My verses for a small price and purchasing is substitution, and its investigation has been presented. His saying: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then those are the disbelievers is a word from the forms of generality, indicating that this is not specific to a specific group, but to everyone who holds a position of authority. It was said that it is specific to the People of the Book, and it was said to the disbelievers in general because a Muslim does not disbelieve by committing a major sin, and it was said that it is based on the fact that ruling by other than what God has revealed occurred out of contempt, or permissibility, or denial, and the reference in His saying: those is to whom, and the plural is in consideration of its meaning, and likewise the pronoun of the group in His saying: They are the disbelievers. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you, he said: They are the Jews. Of those who say, ‘We believe,’ with their mouths, but their hearts do not believe, he said: They are the hypocrites. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: God revealed, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, “the wrongdoers,” and the wicked. God revealed it regarding two groups of Jews, one of which overpowered the other in the pre-Islamic period until they agreed that for every person killed by a powerful woman from a humiliated woman, the blood money would be fifty wasqs, and for every person killed by a humiliated woman from a powerful woman, the blood money would be one hundred wasqs. They continued on this path until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina. Both groups were humiliated by the arrival of the Messenger of God, and at that time the Messenger of God had not been defeated. So the humiliated woman killed the powerful woman, so the powerful woman sent to the humiliated woman saying, Send us one hundred wasqs. The humiliated woman said, Has this ever happened in two groups whose religion is one, their lineage is one, their country is one, and the blood money of one is half the blood money of the other? We gave you this only out of your oppression of us and fear of you. But if Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, comes, we will not give you that. So war was raging between them, then they agreed to make the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, between them. Then the Azizah thought and said: By God, Muhammad will not give you from them twice what we give them from you, and they have told the truth. They did not give us this except out of oppression and subjugation of them. So they sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, someone to tell you his opinion. If he gives you what you want, you will rule according to him, and if he does not give you, you will be wary of him and not rule according to him. So they sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, some hypocrites to test their opinion. So when they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God informed His Messenger of their entire affair and what they wanted, so God revealed: O Messenger, let not grieve you until His saying: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. Then He said about them: By God, it was revealed and they were about me. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, Abd ibn Hamid, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The first Jewish person to be stoned by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the one who committed adultery with a man and a woman. Some of them said to one another: ‘Let us go to this prophet, for he is a prophet who was sent to make things easier. If he gives us a fatwa less than stoning, we will accept it and use it as evidence before God and say: ‘The fatwa of one of your prophets.’ So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with his companions, and they said: ‘O Abu al-Qasim, what do you think of a man and a woman among them who committed adultery?’ So he did not speak to them until he came.” Their school house, so he stood at the door and said: I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah about someone who commits adultery if he is married? They said: He should be bathed, flogged and flogged. The stoning is that the two adulterers should be carried on a donkey and their backs should be opposite each other and they should be paraded around. A young man among them remained silent. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw him, he remained silent and insisted on asking him, so he said: O God, if You ask us, we will answer, for we find stoning in the Torah. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What was the first thing that you made permissible for God’s command? He said: A man who was a relative of one of our kings committed adultery, so stoning was delayed for him. Then a man committed adultery in a family of people, so he wanted to stone him, but his people prevented him and said: By God, you will not stone our companion until you bring your companion and stone him. So they agreed on this punishment among themselves. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I will rule according to what is in the Torah. So he ordered them to be stoned. Al-Zuhri said: It was reported to us that this verse was revealed about them: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The Prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it.” So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was one of them. It was narrated by Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he mentioned in it that the young man mentioned is Abdullah bin Suriya. Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud and Al-Nasa’i included a hadith similar to Abu Hurairah from the hadith of Al-Bara’ bin Azib. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Abdullah bin Umar: “The Jews came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned to him that a man and a woman among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: ‘What do you find in the Torah?’ They said: ‘We will disgrace them and flog them.’ Abdullah bin Salam said: ‘You have lied, for it contains the verse of stoning.’ So they brought the Torah and spread it out. One of them put his hand on the verse of stoning and read what came before it and what came after it. Abdullah bin Salam said: ‘Raise your hand.’ So he raised his hand and it was the verse of stoning. They said: ‘He has spoken the truth.’ So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to be stoned.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Jabir bin Abdullah regarding his statement: And among those who are Jews are some who listen to falsehood, he said: The Jews of Medina. They listen to other people who have not come to you. He said: The Jews of Fadak. They distort the words. He said: The Jews of Fadak say to the Jews of Medina: If you are given this, the flogging, then take it, and if you are not given this, then beware, stoning. Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: A man from the people of Fadak committed adultery, so the people of Fadak wrote to some of the Jews in Medina to ask Muhammad, and he mentioned the story. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Devouring what is unlawful, he said: They took bribes in judgment and passed judgments with lies. And he narrated Abdul Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he said: Al-Siht is bribery in religion. Sufyan said: He means in judgment. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman also narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he said: Whoever intercedes for a man to remove an injustice from him or restore his right, and he gives him a gift and he accepts it, then that is Al-Siht. It was said to him: O Abu Abdul Rahman, we used to consider Al-Siht to be bribery in judgment, so he said: That is disbelief: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. Something similar to this was narrated on his authority through various chains of narration. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Bribery of judges is forbidden. It is the Al-Siht that God mentioned in His Book. Abdul bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit that Al-Siht is bribery. Abdul bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib that he was asked about Al-Siht and he said: Bribery, so he was asked about judgment, so he said: That is disbelief. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Umar who said: There are two types of ill-gotten gains that people consume: bribery in judgment, and the dowry of an adulteress. It has been proven from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that bribery is forbidden, and what is well-known is that it is prohibited. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Two verses were abrogated from Surat al-Ma’idah 5:the verse about necklaces, and His statement: But if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had a choice: if he wanted to, he could judge between them, or if he wanted, he could turn away from them, and return them to their own judgments. Then the verse was revealed: And judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations. He said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was commanded to judge between them by what is in our Book. Abu Ubaidah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar about the last verse on his authority. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the verses of al-Ma’idah in which He said: Then judge between them or turn away from them until His saying: those who are just were revealed regarding the blood money of Banu Nadir and Qurayzah. This is because those killed by Banu Nadir had the honor to pay the full blood money, while Banu Qurayzah paid half the blood money. They brought their case to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) regarding this, and God revealed this regarding them. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) held them to the truth in this matter, so he made the blood money equal. Similar to this was narrated on his authority by Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan. Ibn Jarir narrated Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: And with them is the Torah, in which is the judgment of God, meaning the limits set by God, so God informed him of His judgment in the Torah. He said: And We prescribed for them therein, until His statement: And for wounds, retaliation. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Hasan regarding his statement: The prophets who have submitted will judge by it, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for those who are Jews, meaning the Jews. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ikrimah who said: Those who submitted to the Prophet and those before him of the prophets judge by what is in it of truth. Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Hasan who said: The rabbis and scholars are the jurists and scholars. He narrated from Mujahid who said: The rabbis are the learned jurists, and they are above the rabbis. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan who said: The rabbis are the worshippers, and the rabbis are the scholars. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: The rabbis are the learned jurists. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him who said: The rabbis are the believers, and the rabbis are the reciters. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi: So do not fear the people so that you conceal what was revealed. And do not exchange My verses for a small price on the condition that you conceal what was revealed. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd: And do not exchange My verses for a small price he said: Do not eat ill-gotten gains based on My Book. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mudher, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed he said: Whoever denies the ruling by what God has revealed has disbelieved, and whoever acknowledges it but does not rule by it is a wrongdoer and a sinner. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers he said: It is not the disbelief that they are going to and it is not a disbelief that removes one from the religion but less than disbelief. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ata bin Abi Rabah regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, they are the wrongdoers, they are the sinners he said: It is disbelief less than disbelief and wrongdoing less than wrongdoing, and sin less than sin. Saeed bin Mansour, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: God revealed And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers and the wrongdoers and the sinners in reference to the Jews in particular. Something similar to this has been narrated from a group of the Salaf. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Hudhayfah that these verses were mentioned to him: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, “the wrongdoers,” and the wicked. A man said: This is about the Children of Israel. Hudhayfah said: The Children of Israel are good brothers for you, if you have every sweet thing. And every time they will say, No, by God, you will surely follow their path, and you will be snared. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
5:45: His statement: 45- And We wrote is in apposition to We sent down the Torah, and its meaning is We imposed. God the Almighty explained in this verse what He imposed on the Children of Israel: retaliation for the soul, the eye, the nose, the ear, the tooth, and wounds. Abu Hanifa and a group of scholars used this verse as evidence and said: A Muslim is killed for a dhimmi because he is a soul. Al-Shafi'i and a group of scholars said: This verse is report of the law of those before us and is not our law. We have already presented in Al-Baqarah in explaining the statement of God the Almighty: Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder what is sufficient. Scholars differed on whether the law of those before us is binding on us or not. The majority held that it is binding on us if it has not been abrogated, and this is the truth. Ibn al-Sabbagh mentioned in al-Shamel the consensus of scholars on using this verse as evidence for what it indicates. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation: All the imams used this verse as evidence that a man may be killed for a woman, based on the generality of this noble verse. We have explained what is true in this in our explanation of Al-Muntaqa, and in this verse for the Jews and a rebuke for their disobedience to what God has written for them in the Torah as He has narrated here, and they differentiate between souls as previously explained, and they used to restrict Banu Nadir from Banu Qurayzah and not restrict Banu Qurayzah from Banu Nadir. His statement: An eye for an eye Nafi’, Asim, Al-A’mash and Hamzah read in the accusative in all of them as a conjunction. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Amr and Abu Ja’far also read in the accusative in all except in Al-Jarh, which is in the nominative. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaid read in the nominative in all of them as a conjunction to the place, because the soul before the letter that makes the accusative entered it was raised as a beginning. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a conjunction to the implied in the soul, because the estimate is: The soul is taken by the soul, so the names are conjoined to it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: And whoever reads in the nominative made that the beginning of a statement that includes a statement of the ruling for the Muslims. It is apparent from the Qur’anic system that if the eye is gouged out until there is no longer any room for perception, then the eye of the offender is gouged out with it. If the nose is completely cut off, then the nose of the offender is cut off with it. If the ear is completely cut off, then the ear of the offender is cut off with it. Likewise the tooth. However, if the crime has taken away some perception of the eye, or some of the nose, or some of the ear, or some of the tooth, then there is nothing in this verse that indicates the establishment of retaliation. Scholars have differed on this if the amount is known and its reality can be ascertained, and their words are recorded in the books of branches. What appears from his statement, and a tooth for a tooth, is that there is no difference between the incisors, canines, molars, and canines, and that some are taken for others, and there is no preference for some over others. Most scholars have adopted this view, as Ibn al-Mundhir said, and ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and those who followed him disagreed on this, and their words are recorded in their places, but what is taken in retaliation from the offender should be the equivalent of the tooth taken from the victim, and if it is lost, then what is next to it. His statement, and wounds are retaliation, means those for which there is retaliation. Scholars have stated that there is no retaliation for wounds from which there is fear of death, nor for wounds whose depth, length, or width is not known. The imams of jurisprudence have estimated the blood money for each wound according to known amounts, and this is not the place to explain their statements, nor the place to fully explain what has been reported for which there is an estimated blood money. His statement: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him meaning whoever gives charity from among those deserving of retaliation by pardoning the offender, it is an expiation for the one giving charity, God will expiate his sins with it. It was said that the meaning is: it is an expiation for the one who hurt him, so he will not be held accountable for his crime in the Hereafter, because pardon takes the place of taking the right from him. The first is more likely, because the pronoun in this other interpretation refers to something not mentioned. His statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers The disjunctive pronoun with the demonstrative pronoun and the definite article indicate that this injustice committed by them is a great injustice that has reached the limit.
5:46: His saying: 46- And We followed in their footsteps with Jesus, son of Mary. This is the beginning of explaining the ruling of the Gospel after explaining the ruling of the Torah: that is, We made Jesus, son of Mary, follow in their footsteps: that is, the footsteps of the prophets who converted to Islam from the Children of Israel. It is said, I followed him, like I followed him, if you followed him. Then it is said, I followed him with so-and-so, and it is transitive to the second with the preposition with, and the first object is omitted because it is dispensed with by the circumstance, and it is in their footsteps, because if he followed him in his footsteps, then he followed him with him. The accusative of confirming is in the state of Jesus. And We gave him the Gospel is in apposition to We followed, and the location of the sentence, I mean, in it is guidance, is in the accusative as a state of the Gospel. And light is in apposition to guidance. His saying: And confirming is in apposition to the place of in which is guidance, meaning that the Gospel was given to Jesus while he was encompassing guidance and light and confirming what was before him of the Torah. It was said that confirming is in apposition to the first confirming, so it is a state of Jesus, confirming the first state and establishing it. The first is more appropriate because establishing is better than confirming. His saying: And guidance and admonition for the righteous is in apposition to confirming, which is included under its ruling and joined to it: meaning confirming, guiding, and admonishing for the righteous.
5:47: His statement: 47- And let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein. This is a command to the People of the Gospel to judge by what God has revealed therein, because before the mission of Muhammad it was true. As for after it, they were commanded in more than one place to act according to what God revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Quran, which abrogates all revealed books. Al-A'mash and Hamzah read the verb man yahkam in the accusative case, on the basis that the lam is the lam of ki. The rest read it in the jussive case, on the basis that the lam is for command. According to the first reading, the lam is related to His statement: And We gave him the Gospel so that his people might judge by what God has revealed therein. According to the second reading, it is a new statement. Makki said: The preferred choice is the jussive case, because the group is upon it, and because what follows it of threats and intimidation indicates that it is an obligation from God to the People of the Gospel. Al-Nahhas said: The correct view in my opinion is that they are two good readings, because God, the Exalted, did not reveal a book except for it to be acted upon.
5:48: His statement: 48- And We have sent down to you the Book is an address to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Book is the Qur'an and the definition is for the covenant, and with the truth is related to something omitted that occurred as a state: that is, clothed in the truth. It was said that it is a state of the subject of We sent down, and it was said that it is from the pronoun of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Confirming what was before it is a state of the Book, and the definition in the Book, I mean his statement: Confirming what was before it of the Book is for the genus: that is, We sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Qur'an while he was clothed in the truth and while he was confirming what was before him of the revealed Books of God because it includes the call to God and the command to do good and the prohibition of evil, as His statement includes: And a guardian over it in apposition to confirming, and the pronoun in over it refers to the Book that the Qur'an confirmed and dominated. The guardian is the watcher, and it was said that the dominant is the elevated, and it was said that the witness, and it was said that the preserver, and it was said that the trustee. Al-Mubarrad said: Its origin is mu’aymin, with the hamza replaced with a ha’, as was said in araqat al-ma’, and this is what al-Zajjaj and Abu Ali al-Farsi said. Al-Jawhari said: It is from the one who feels secure from fear, and its origin is a’man, so he is mu’amin with two hamzas, the second was changed to a ya’ because of their unwillingness to come together, so it became mu’amin, then the first was changed to a ha’, as they said haraqa al-ma’ and araqahu. It is said hayman over something yahayman: if he is its guardian, then he is its guardian. Thus on the authority of Abu Ubaid. Mujahid and Ibn Muhaisin read it with a fat-ha on the meem, meaning that God, the Most High, has dominion over him. The meaning according to the reading of the majority is that the Qur’an has become a witness to the authenticity of the revealed books and a confirmation of what is in them that has not been abrogated and an abrogator of what contradicts it, and a watcher over them and a protector of what is in them of the principles of the laws, and a dominant one for them because it is the reference for what is definitive and what is abrogated, and a trustee for them because it includes what is acted upon and what is abandoned. His statement, So judge between them by what God has revealed means by what He revealed to you in the Qur’an because it includes everything that God has legislated for His servants in all the books that preceded it. And do not follow their inclinations means the inclinations of the people of previous religions. His statement, from what has come to you of the truth is related to la tataba’ because it includes the meaning of do not deviate or do not deviate from what has come to you of the truth following their inclinations. It was said that it is related to something omitted: meaning do not follow their inclinations, whether just or deviating from the truth. It forbids him, may God bless him and grant him peace, from following the whims of the People of the Book and deviating from the truth that God revealed to him, because every religion desires that the matter be as they are and as they found their predecessors upon, even if it is false, abrogated, or distorted from the ruling that God revealed to the prophets, as happened in stoning and similar things that they distorted from the Books of God. His statement: For each of you We prescribed a law and a method. The law and the Shari’ah originally mean the apparent way by which one reaches water, then they were used in what God legislated for His servants of religion. The method is the clear and evident way. Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Mubarrad said: The Shari’ah means the beginning of the path, and the method is the continuous path. The meaning of the verse is that He made the Torah for its people, the Gospel for His people, and the Qur’an for His people. This was before the abrogation of the previous laws by the Qur’an. As for after that, there is no law or method except what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. His statement: And if God had willed, He would have made you one nation with one law, one book, and one messenger. But that He might test you means, but He did not will that union, rather He willed to test you with the differences in laws. So, that He might test you is related to something preserved and indicated by the context of the speech, which is what we mentioned. The meaning of in what He has given you is in what He sent down to you of the different laws according to the times and people. His statement: So race to do good deeds means, if the will has decreed the differences in laws, then race to do what you were commanded to do and leave what you were commanded to leave. Racing means hastening. To God is your return, all of you, not to anyone else. This sentence is like the reason for what preceded it.
5:49: His statement: 49- And judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations. In apposition to the Book: meaning, We revealed to you the Book and the judgment by what is in it. This has been used as evidence for the abrogation of the previous choice in His statement: Or turn away from them. The explanation of and do not follow their inclinations has already been presented. His statement: And beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what God has revealed to you. That is, they lead you astray from it and divert you because of their inclinations that they want you to act upon and give preference to. But if they turn away, then know that God only intends to afflict them with some of their sins. That is, if they turn away from accepting your judgment by what God has revealed to you, then that is because God intended to punish them for some of their sins, which is the sin of turning away from you and turning away from what you have brought. And indeed, many of the people are wicked. Rebellious against accepting the truth and outside of fairness.
5:50: His statement: 50- Do they then seek the judgment of the time of ignorance? The question is for denial and rebuke, and the fa is for connecting to an implied word as in its counterparts. The meaning is: Do they turn away from your judgment by what God has revealed to you and turn away from it and seek the judgment of the time of ignorance?
