The question in And who is better than God in judgment for a people who are certain? is also for denial: meaning there is nothing better than God's judgment for the people of certainty, not for the people of ignorance and whims. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, We have prescribed for them therein in the Torah. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, he said: This was prescribed for them in the Torah, and they used to kill a free man for a slave, and they would say: It was prescribed for us that a life be for a life. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement, But whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, he said: It erases from him some of his sins in proportion to what he gave in charity. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Jabir Ibn Abdullah, It is an expiation for him, he said: For the one who is wounded. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no Muslim who is afflicted with something in his body and gives it in charity, except that God will raise him a degree thereby and remove a sin from him thereby. Saeed Ibn Mansour, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And a guardian over it, he said: A trustee over it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority that he said: Al-Muhaymin is the trustworthy one, and the Qur’an is the trustworthy one over every book before it. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: A law and a way, he said: A path and a tradition. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Ka’b bin Asad, Abdullah bin Suriya, and Shas bin Qais said: Let us go to Muhammad so that we may tempt him away from his religion. So they came to him and said: O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis of the Jews, their nobles, and their leaders, and if we follow you, we will follow the Jews. There is a dispute between us and our people, so we will bring them to you for judgment, so that you may judge for them and we will believe in you and confirm you. But he refused, and God revealed about them: And judge between them by what God has revealed until His statement: For a people who are certain. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Do they then seek the judgment of the time of ignorance? He said: Jews. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: This is about the Jews who killed.
5:51: His statement: 51- O you who have believed, do not take It appears that it is addressed to the true believers, and it was said that what is meant by them are the hypocrites, and their description of faith is based on what they used to show. They used to befriend the Jews and Christians, so they were forbidden from doing so. It is better to be addressed to everyone who is characterized by faith, more generally than it being apparent and hidden or only apparent, so that includes the Muslim and the hypocrite, and this is supported by His statement: Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease and consideration of the generality of the wording, and what is meant will come in explaining the reason for the revelation of the verse, which will clarify what is meant. What is meant by the prohibition of taking them as allies is that they should be treated as allies in terms of encounter, companionship, and support. His saying: Some of them are allies of others is an explanation for the prohibition, and the meaning is: Some of the Jews are allies of others, and some of the Christians are allies of others. What is meant by some is not one of the two groups of Jews and Christians, and by other is not the other group, because it is certain that they are in the utmost enmity and discord. And the Jews say, ‘The Christians have nothing,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Jews have nothing.’ It was said that what is meant is that each of the two groups is loyal to the other, supports it, and aids it in its enmity towards the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and what he brought, even though they are hostile and opposed to each other. The reason for explaining the prohibition with this sentence is that it requires that this loyalty is the affair of these disbelievers, not your affair, so do not do what they do, lest you become like them. For this reason, this causal sentence was followed by what is like a result of it, saying: And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them, meaning that he is among them and counted among them, and this is a severe threat, because the sin that leads to disbelief is that which has reached an extreme beyond which there is no other end. His saying: Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people is an explanation for the sentence before it: that is, their falling into disbelief is due to His, glory be to Him, not guiding those who wrong themselves in a way that necessitates disbelief, such as those who befriend the disbelievers.
5:52: His saying: 52- And you will see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into them The fa is for causality, and the address is either to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone who is fit for it: meaning that what they committed of allegiance and fell into of disbelief is because of what is in their hearts of disease of hypocrisy. And his saying: hastening is in the accusative case either as the second object if the vision is from the heart or as a state if it is visual, and he made hastening into their allegiance hastening into them to exaggerate in stating their desire for that until it is as if they are settled among them and included in their number. And he will see was read with the ta'dah and there was a difference of opinion as to what its subject is? It was said that it is God Almighty, and it was said that it is everyone from whom the vision is correct, and it was said that it is the relative and its object hastening into them with the deletion of the source an: meaning that the people in whose hearts is disease will see that they will hasten into them, so when it was deleted the verb was raised like his saying: Oh, you who blame me, come to the battlefield The disease in the hearts: is hypocrisy and doubt in religion. His statement: They say, ‘We fear that a misfortune may befall us,’ is a sentence that includes the reason for hastening to befriend: that is, this fear is what drives them to hasten. It was said that the sentence is a state of the pronoun hasten. And the misfortune: is what revolves of the misfortunes of time: that is, we fear that the infidels will gain victory over Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the state will be theirs and his state will be invalidated, and a misfortune will befall us from them. From this is the saying of the poet: Fate and destiny prevent you from turning Any states of time that go from one people to another. And His statement: Perhaps God will bring about victory is a response to them and a rebuttal of what happened to them of fear, and perhaps in the words of God is a true promise that will not fail. And the al-Nasr 110:is the victory of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, over the disbelievers, and from it what happened of killing the fighters of Banu Qurayzah and taking their children captive, and expelling Banu Nadir, and it was said that it is the conquest of the lands of the polytheists to the Muslims, and it was said that it is the conquest of Mecca. What is meant by the command from Him, glory be to Him, is everything that repels the attack of the Jews and those with them and breaks their power, and it was said that it is revealing the matter of the hypocrites and informing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what they kept secret in their souls and his command to kill them, and it was said that it is the jizya that God imposed on them, and it was said that it is the fertility and abundance for the Muslims, so the hypocrites become regretful of what they kept secret in their souls of the hypocrisy that led them to the alliance, over that because the reasons they imagined are invalid and their opposite is revealed.
5:53: His saying: 53- Those who believe say. Abu Amr, Ibn Abi Ishaq and the people of Kufa read with the addition of the waw, and the rest read without it. According to the first reading with the raising of yaqool, it is a subject statement presented to explain what happened from this group. According to the accusative reading, it is in apposition to they become and it was said to come and the first is more appropriate, because this statement is only issued by the believers when the remorse of the disbelievers appears, not when the conquest comes. It was said that it is in apposition to the conquest like the poet's saying: To wear an abaya and please my eyes As for the reading with the deletion of the waw, the sentence is a new sentence in response to an implied question, and the reference in His saying: Are these to al-Munafiqun 63:that is, those who believed say, addressing the Jews, pointing to the hypocrites, Are these the ones who swore by God with their most earnest oaths that they were with you in supporting and assisting in the fighting, or some of the believers say to each other, pointing to the hypocrites, and this sentence explains the statement. The most earnest oaths: the most emphatically, and it is accusative as a source or as a state: that is, they swore by God with effort. His saying: Their deeds were in vain means they were invalidated, and it is from the completion of the statement of the believers or a new sentence, and the speaker is God Almighty. And the deeds are what they did in allegiance or every action they do.
5:54: His statement: 54- O you who have believed, whoever among you should revert The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read yartaddad with two dals without assimilation, and this is the language of Tamim, and others read with assimilation. This is a start to explaining the rulings on apostates after explaining that a Muslim’s friendship with the infidels is disbelief, and that is a type of apostasy. The people whom God the Almighty promised to bring are Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him and his army of companions and followers who fought the apostates, then everyone who came after them from among the fighters of the apostates throughout time. Then God the Almighty described these people with these great descriptions that include the utmost praise and the ultimate commendation of their love for God and He loves them, and of their being humble toward the believers, mighty toward the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of God and do not fear the blame of a blamer. Humble is the plural of humble, not submissive, and mighty is the plural of dear: that is, they show compassion, tenderness, and humility toward the believers and show severity, harshness, and superiority toward the disbelievers, and they combine striving in the cause of God with not fearing blame in religion. Rather, they are stubborn and do not care about what the enemies of the truth and the party of Satan do of denigrating the people of religion and turning their good qualities into bad qualities and their virtues into faults out of envy, hatred, and loathing for the truth and its people. The reference in His saying: that is to what Advancement of the qualities that God has distinguished them with. And the virtue: kindness and benevolence.
5:55: His statement: 55- Your ally is only God When He, the Almighty, finished explaining who it is not permissible to befriend, He explained who is the ally whose loyalty is obligatory, and the location of those who establish prayer is the nominative case as an attribute of those who believe or a substitute for it or the accusative case for praise. And His statement: And they bow is a circumstantial clause of the subject of the two verbs that preceded it. What is meant by bowing is humility and submission: that is, they establish prayer and give zakat while they are humbly submissive and not arrogant. And it was said that it is a circumstantial of the subject of zakat. What is meant by bowing is the aforementioned meaning: that is, they place zakat in its proper places, neither arrogant nor haughty towards the poor. And it was said that what is meant by bowing in the second meaning is bowing in prayer, and this is refuted by the impermissibility of giving zakat in that situation.
5:56: 56- And whoever takes God and His Messenger and those who believe as allies - then indeed, the party of God - they will be the victorious. Then the Almighty promised whoever takes God and His Messenger and those who believe as allies that they will be the victorious over their enemy. This is from placing the apparent in place of the implicit, and placing the party of God in place of the pronoun of those loyal to God, His Messenger, and the believers. The party: is a group of people, from their saying his party is such-and-such: meaning it has afflicted him, so it is as if the partisans are gathered like the gathering of the people of a calamity that befalls them. The party of a man: his companions, and the party: the rose. In the hadith: So whoever misses his party of the night. And they gathered: they gathered. And the parties: the sects. And, praise be to God, what God promised to His friends, the friends of His Messengers, and the friends of His believing servants, of defeating their enemy, has happened. They defeated the Jews by captivity, killing, exile, and imposing the jizya, until they became, may God curse them, the most humiliated of the infidel sects and the least powerful. And they have continued to be under the yoke of the believers, crushing them however they wished and humiliating them as they wished from after the noble Muhammadan mission until this end. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit who said: “When Banu Qaynuqa’ fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul held fast to their cause and stood up for them. Ubadah ibn al-Samit walked to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and disavowed them to God and His Messenger. He was one of Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, and he had the same allegiance to them as Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had. He renounced them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I disavow to God and His Messenger the allegiance and allegiance of these infidels. It was about him and Abdullah ibn Ubayy that the verses in al-Ma’idah were revealed: ‘O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies’ until His saying: ‘For indeed, the party of God - they will be the victorious.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul converted to Islam, then he said: There is an alliance between me and Qurayzah and Nadir, and I fear the consequences, so he apostatized as an unbeliever. Ubadah bin As-Samit said: I disavow before God the alliance between Qurayzah and Nadir, and I take God and His Messenger as my ally, so this verse was revealed. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin As-Samit, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, something similar to that. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Atiyyah bin Sa`d, who said: Ubadah came and mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Az-Zuhri, who said: When the people of Badr were defeated, the Muslims said to their Jewish allies: Believe before God afflicts you with a day like the day of Badr. Malik bin As-Saif said: You were deceived by the fact that you afflicted a group of Quraysh who had no knowledge of fighting. If we had insisted on uniting against you, you would not have been able to fight us. Ubadah said and mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above from him and from Abdullah bin Ubayy. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, O you who believe, he said: It refers to the sacrifices. Whoever enters the religion of a people is one of them. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said: Let one of you beware of being a Jew or a Christian without realizing it, and he recited, And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Atiyyah, Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease, like Abdullah bin Ubayy, hastening to them, in their allegiance. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: God revealed this verse, O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert, and He knew that apostates would revert from the people. When God took the soul of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, most of the Arabs reverted from Islam except for three mosques: the people of Madinah, the people of Makkah, and the people of Al-Jawathi from Abd Al-Qais. Those who reverted said: We will pray the prayer but we will not pay zakat, and by God, our wealth will not be seized. So he spoke to Abu Bakr about that to forgive them. And it was said to him that if they had understood, they would have paid the zakat. So he said: By God, I will not separate between something that God has united, and if they withhold from me even a hobble from what God and His Messenger have imposed, I will fight them for it. So God sent groups with Abu Bakr and they fought until they acknowledged the ma’un, which is the zakat. Qatada said: So we used to think that this verse was revealed about Abu Bakr and his companions, Then God will bring forth a people whom He will love and who will love Him, to the end of the verse. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Shuraih bin Ubayd who said: “When God revealed: ‘O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion’ verse, ‘Umar said: ‘Me and my people, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘No, rather this one and his people’, meaning Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari.” And Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musnad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Iyad Al-Ash’ari who said: “When God revealed: ‘Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him’, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: And he (peace be upon him) said: They are the people of this, and he pointed to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Hakim in his collection of the hadith of Shu'bah, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: "The verse, 'God will bring forth a people' was recited to the Prophet (peace be upon him), so the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Your people, O Abu Musa, are the people of Yemen." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in al-Kuna, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: "The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was asked about his statement, 'God will bring forth a people', and he said: These are people from Yemen, then Kindah, then Sakun, then Tajib." Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: They are people from Yemen, then Kindah, then Sakun. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on his authority, he said: They are the people of al-Qadisiyah. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymirah, who said: I came to Ibn Umar and he welcomed me, then he recited, "Whoever among you turns back from his Lord, God will bring forth a people' - whoever... His religion, then God will bring a people” the verse, then he struck my shoulder and said: I swear by God that you are from among the people of Yemen three times. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Atiyah bin Saad. He said regarding his statement: Your guardian is only God and His Messenger that it was revealed about Ubadah bin al-Samit. Al-Khatib in Al-Muttafaq wa Al-Muftariq narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: “He gave me a ring as charity while he was bowing. The Prophet said to the questioner: Who gave you this ring? He said: That one who was bowing. So God revealed about him: ‘Your guardian is only God and His Messenger.’” Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It was revealed about Ali Bin Abi Talib. Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Ali Bin Abi Talib. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ammar as well. Al-Tabarani narrated something similar in Al-Awsat with a chain of transmission that includes unknown narrators on his authority.
5:57: His statement: 57- Do not take those who take your religion in jest. This prohibition of befriending those who take religion in jest and play includes everyone who does that from the polytheists, the People of the Book, and the people of innovations who claim to be Muslims. The explanation in His statement: Of those who were given the Book to the end does not contradict the inclusion of others under the prohibition if the aforementioned reason is found in it which is the motive for the prohibition. His statement: And the disbelievers Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read it in the accusative case on the basis of of: meaning, of the disbelievers. Al-Kisa'i said: In the letter of Abu and of the disbelievers, and those other than them read it in the accusative case. Al-Nahhas said: It is clearer and more evident. Makki said: If the group had not agreed on the accusative case, I would have chosen the genitive case because of its strength in grammar and meaning. What is meant by the disbelievers here are the polytheists, and it was said the hypocrites. And fear God means to abandon what He has forbidden you from this and other things if you are believers because faith requires that.
5:58: The call is the supplication by raising the voice. He called him by calling and calling: he shouted it, and they called each other: that is, they called each other. And they called each other: that is, they sat in the club, and the pronoun in 58- took it for prayer: that is, they took your prayers as mockery and play, and it was said that the pronoun is for the call indicated by you called. It was said that there is no mention of the call in the Book of God Almighty except in this place, and as for His Almighty’s saying in al-Jumuah 62:When the call is made for prayer on Friday it is specific to the call to Friday. The scholars differed as to whether the call to prayer is obligatory or not, and as to its wording, and it is explained in detail in its places. His saying: That is because they are a people who do not reason means that because they are a people who do not reason, because mockery and play are the business of the foolish, frivolous, and rash.
5:59: His saying: 59- Say, O People of the Scripture, do you blame us? It is said: I blamed the man with the kasra, so I am a naqim: if you criticize him. Al-Kisa'i said: I blamed with the kasra is a language, and I blamed the matter also and I blamed: if you hated it, and God took revenge on him: that is, punished him, and the noun from it is the vengeance, and the plural is vengeances, like word and words, and if you wish, you can make the qaf quiescent and transfer its movement to the nun, and the plural is naqam like ni'mah and ni'am, and it was said that the meaning is they are angry, and it was said that they disapprove. Abdullah bin Qais al-Ruqayyat said: They only blamed the Umayyads for being angry when they were angry. God the Almighty said: And they did not resent them The meaning of the verse: Do you find fault with us, or are angry, or disapprove, or hate us for anything other than our belief in God and His revealed books, and you know that we are on the truth? And that most of you are wicked for abandoning faith and disobeying God’s commands. His statement: And that most of you are wicked is connected to that we believed: meaning that you do not resent us for anything other than combining our faith with your rebellion and departure from faith. And in it is that the believers did not combine the two mentioned matters, for faith is on their part and rebellion and rebellion are on the part of the resentful. It was said that it is on the assumption of an omitted word: that is, and our belief that most of you are wicked. It was said that his saying: that we believed is in the accusative case as an object for it and the object is omitted, so and that most of you are wicked is conjoined to it by the conjunction of the cause to the cause, and the estimate is: and you do not resent us except because we believed, and because most of you are wicked. It was said that it is conjoined to a deleted cause, that is, because of your lack of fairness, and because most of you are wicked. It was said that the waw in his saying: and that most of you are wicked is the one with the meaning of with: that is, you do not resent us except for faith even though most of you are wicked. It was said that it is in the accusative case with a deleted verb that indicates it. Do you resent? That is, and do you not resent that most of you are wicked. It was said that it is raised as the subject and the predicate is omitted: that is, and your wickedness is known, so the sentence is a circumstantial. It was read with the kasra of in from his saying: and that Most of you are wicked. So it is a new sentence.
5:60: His statement: 60- "Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?" God the Almighty explained to His Messenger that they have a defect that is more deserving of being defective, which is their disbelief that incurs God's curse, wrath, and transformation. The meaning is: Shall I inform you of something worse than your vengeance against us, or something worse than what you want for us of harm, or something worse than the People of the Book, or something worse than their religion? His statement: "Reward" means a fixed recompense, and it is specific to good, just as punishment is specific to evil. It is placed here in the place of punishment in the manner of "So give them tidings of a painful torment, and it is in the accusative case as a distinguishing feature of good report." His statement: "He whom God has cursed" is the predicate of a deleted subject with an estimated deleted complement: meaning he is the curse of whom God has cursed, or he is the religion of whom God has cursed. It is permissible for it to be in the genitive case instead of evil. His saying: And made from them apes and pigs means He transformed some of them into apes and some into pigs, and they are the Jews, for God transformed the Sabbath-companions into apes and the infidels of Jesus’ table from them into pigs. His saying: And worshipped Taghut Hamzah read it with a damma on the ba’ of ‘abd and a kasra on the ta’ of taghut meaning He made from them worshippers of Taghut by adding ‘abd to Taghut. The meaning is: And He made from them those who go to extremes in worshipping Taghut, because the verb is from the forms of exaggeration, like ‘hadarah’ and ‘fatan’ for conveying caution and acumen. The rest read it with a fatha on the ba’ of ‘abd’ and a fatha on the ta’ of taghut as a past tense verb conjoined with a past tense verb which is ‘ghadabah’ and ‘alaan’, as if it was said: And from the worship of Taghut, or conjoined with the apes and pigs: meaning He made from them apes and pigs and made from them worshippers of Taghut based on the word ‘min’. Abi and Ibn Mas’ud read and the worship of Taghut based on its meaning. Ibn Abbas read "wa-'Abd" with a damma on the 'ayn and the ba' as if it were the plural of 'Abd, as is said: "saqf and saqf". It is possible that it is the plural of 'Ubaid, like "ragheef and raghaf, or the plural of 'Abid, like bazel and bazel". Abu Waqid read "wa-'Ibad as the plural of 'Abid for emphasis, like 'Amil and 'Ummal". The Basrans also read "wa-'Ibad as the plural of 'Abid, like Qaim and Qiyam, and it is possible that it is the plural of 'Abd". Abu Ja'far al-Raqqashi read "wa-'Abd al-Taghut in the passive voice, and the meaning is wa-'Abd al-Taghut" among them. Awn al-'Uqaili and Ibn Buraydah read "wa-'Abid al-Taghut" in the singular. It was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and Abi that they read "wa-'Abdat al-Taghut and Ubaid bin 'Umair read wa-'Abd al-Taghut like Kalb and A'kalab". "wa-'Abd al-Taghut" was read in apposition to the relative pronoun based on the estimation of a deleted complement, and it is a very weak reading. "Taghut" means the devil or the priests or other than what has been mentioned in full. His saying: Those are in the worst place refers to those described with the aforementioned attributes, and the spark was made for the place, and it is for its people for emphasis, and it is possible for the attribution to be metaphorical. His saying: And more astray from the straight path is conjoined with evil, meaning they are more astray from the straight path than others, and the preference in both places is for the increase absolutely or because they are more evil and more astray than those who share with them in the origin of the spark and misguidance.
5:61: His statement: And when they come to you, they say, 'We believe.' That is, when they come to you, they display Islam. His statement: And they entered in disbelief, and they left in it. These are two circumstantial sentences: That is, they came to you in a state of being in your company, clothed in disbelief, and they left you clothed in it. What they heard from you did not affect them, rather they left as they entered. And God knows best what they were concealing. From you of disbelief, and in it is a severe threat. These are the hypocrites, and it was said that they are the Jews who said: Believe in that which was revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end.
5:62: His saying: 62- And you see many of them hastening into sin. The address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone who is suitable for it, and the pronoun in of them refers back to the hypocrites or the Jews or to both groups together. Hastening into sin is in the accusative case as a state, on the basis that the narration is visual, or it is a second object of you see on the basis that it is cardiac, and haste: initiative, and sin: lying or polytheism or forbidden, and aggression: injustice that is transmitted to others or exceeding the limit in sins. And saht: the forbidden, so according to the opinion of those who interpreted sin as forbidden, its repetition is for exaggeration, and the rabbis are the scholars of the Christians, and the rabbis: the scholars of the Jews, and it was said that all of them are from the Jews because these verses are about them, then He rebuked their scholars for abandoning their prohibition and said: How evil is what they used to do. This is an addition to His saying: How evil is what they used to do, because work does not reach the level of craftsmanship until its owner trains in it, and for this reason the Arabs say a sword of good craftsmanship if its worker does his work well, so craftsmanship is good work, not absolute knowledge, so He, glory be to Him, rebuked the special ones, and they are the scholars who abandon enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, with what is harsher and more severe than the rebuke of the doer of sins, so let the scholars open their ears to this verse and open their hearts to it, for it came with what contains a clear explanation for them that their refraining from sins while abandoning their denunciation of those who do them does not satisfy hunger, rather they are in a worse state and a greater calamity than the sinners, so may God have mercy on a scholar who did what God has obligated upon him of the duty of commanding. Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is the greatest thing that God has enjoined upon us and the most obligatory thing that He has made it obligatory for us to do. O God, make us among Your righteous servants who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, who do not fear the blame of any blamer in Your cause. Help us to do that, strengthen us in it, make it easy for us, and grant us victory over those who transgress Your limits and oppress Your servants. Indeed, we have no helper but You, and no one to seek help from but You, O Master of the Day of Judgment. You alone do we worship and You alone do we ask for help. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Rafa’ah bin Zaid bin Al-Tabut and Sayyid bin Al-Harith had outwardly declared Islam but were hypocrites, and there were some Muslim men who were friendly with them. Then God revealed: O you who have believed, do not take as your followers those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement until His saying: And God knows best what they used to conceal. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and amusement that he said: When the caller of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) called for prayer and the Muslims stood up for prayer, the Jews and Christians would say: They have stood up, they have not stood up. When they saw them bowing and prostrating, they would mock them and laugh at them. He said: There was a Jewish merchant who, when he heard the caller calling the adhan, would say: May God burn the liar. He said: While he was like that, his slave girl entered with a torch of fire, and a spark from it flew into the house and burned it down. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: There was a Christian man who mentioned a story similar to that of the Jewish man. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “A group of Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, They asked him about the messengers he believed in. He said: I believe in God and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes, and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims to Him. When Jesus was mentioned, they denied his prophethood and said: We do not believe in Jesus, nor do we believe in those who believe in him. So God revealed about them: “Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, do you blame us?’” until His saying: Disobedient ones. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: And made from them apes and pigs, he said: They were transformed from Jews. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Malik that he was asked: Were there apes and pigs before they were transformed? He said: Yes, and they were among the nations He created. Muslim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about apes and pigs, they are among what God transformed, so he said: God did not destroy a people, or he said: He did not transform a people and make for them And the apes and pigs were before that.” And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And when they come to you, they say, ‘We believe’ the verse, he said that some of the Jews used to enter upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and inform him that they are believers and satisfied with what he brought, while they were clinging to their misguidance and disbelief, so they used to enter with that and leave with it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: These are people from the hypocrites who were Jews, he said: They entered as disbelievers and left as disbelievers. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Zaid regarding his statement: And you will see many of them hastening into sin and aggression he said: These are the Jews How evil is that which they used to do until His statement: How evil is that which they used to do. He said: They make and work one. He said to these when they did not finish as he said to these when they worked.
5:63: Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: 63- Why do the rabbis and scholars not forbid them? He said: So do the rabbis and scholars not forbid them? Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: There is no verse in the Qur'an that is more severe in rebuke than this verse: Why do the rabbis and scholars not forbid them? Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated it in Az-Zuhd, and Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated it on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, similarly. Many hadiths have been narrated on enjoining good and forbidding evil, and we do not need to elaborate on them here.
5:64: His saying: 64- The hand of God is chained The hand among the Arabs is used to refer to the limb, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And take in your hand a bunch and to the blessing, they say how many hands do I have with so-and-so, and to the ability, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: "Say: Indeed, the bounty is in the hand of God" or to support, and from this is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The hand of God is with the judge when he judges and it is used to refer to other meanings. This verse is by way of representation like the saying of God the Almighty: And do not make your hand chained to your neck and the Arabs use the chaining of the hand to mean miserliness and its extension to mean generosity metaphorically, and they do not mean the limb as they describe the miser as having curly fingers and a clenched fist, and from this is the saying of the poet: Khorasan was a land where Yazid lived and every door of goodness was open. Then his fingers were replaced with curly hair, as if his face was sprinkled with vinegar. The Jews here mean that God is stingy, so He, the Most High, answered them by saying: Their hands are chained, a supplication against them for being stingy. So the answer to them is in accordance with what they meant by saying: The hand of God is chained. It is possible that the meaning of their hands being chained is in reality captivity in this world or punishment in the hereafter. The first meaning is strengthened by the fact that stinginess has stuck with the Jews as a shadow sticks to the sun, so you will not see a Jew, even if his wealth is extremely abundant, except that he is one of the stingiest of God’s creation. Also, the metaphor is more appropriate for the situation because it matches what precedes it. His saying: And they were cursed for what they said is connected to what preceded it, and the ba is causal: that is, they were removed from the mercy of God because of their saying: The hand of God is chained. Then the Almighty responded by saying: Rather, His hands are spread wide, meaning, rather, He is at the peak of generosity. He mentioned the two hands, even though they only mentioned one hand, as an exaggeration in responding to them by establishing what indicates the peak of generosity, for attributing generosity to the two hands is more eloquent than attributing it to one hand. This interjectional sentence is connected to an implied sentence that the situation requires: that is, no, it is not like that. Rather, His hands are spread wide. It was said that what is meant by His saying: Rather, His hands are spread wide is the apparent and hidden blessings of this world, and it was said the blessings of rain and plants, and it was said the reward and punishment. Al-Akhfash narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he read: Rather, His hands are two simple ones: meaning, they are released as He wills. His statement: He spends as He wills is a renewed sentence emphasizing the perfection of His generosity, glory be to Him: that is, His spending is according to what His will requires. If He wills, He is generous, and if He wills, He is stingy. He is the Expander, the Constrictor. If He contracts, it is because of what His dazzling wisdom requires, not for anything else, for the treasures of His kingdom do not run out and the resources of His generosity are endless. His statement: And He will surely increase many of them etc. The lam is the lam of the oath: that is, what has been revealed to you of the Qur’an, which includes these good rulings, will surely increase many of the Jews and Christians in transgression and disbelief meaning transgression to their transgression and disbelief to their disbelief. His statement: And We cast among them meaning between the Jews enmity and hatred or between the Jews and the Christians. His saying: Whenever they kindle a fire for war, God extinguishes it means whenever they gather for war and prepare equipment for it, God disperses their gathering and takes away their wind, so they do not gain anything nor do they return with any benefit, rather they do not obtain from that except victory for themselves, and thus they continue to incite wars and gather for them, then God nullifies that. The verse contains an eloquent metaphor and a wonderful style and strive to cause corruption in the land meaning they strive to do what is corrupt, the greatest of which is what they want to do away with Islam and plot against its people. It was said that what is meant by fire here is anger: meaning whenever they stir up anger in themselves, God extinguishes it with what He puts of terror in their hearts and the humiliation and poverty that are imposed upon them. His saying: And God does not love the corrupters If the lam is for the genus, then they are included in that primarily, and if it is for the covenant, then the apparent is placed in place of the implicit to clarify the severity of their corruption and the fact that they are inseparable from it.
5:65: His statement: 65- And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared God meaning if those who adhered to the Scripture, namely the Jews and Christians, with the definition being for the gender, had believed the faith that God demanded of them, and the most important of which is belief in what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought as they were commanded to do in the books of God revealed to them, and feared the sins, the greatest of which is what they are doing of associating partners with God and denying what the Messenger of God brought, We would have removed from them their misdeeds that they committed, even though they were many and varied. It was said that the meaning is: We would have expanded their provisions.
5:66: 66- And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel meaning they had upheld the rulings contained in them, including belief in what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. His statement, and what was revealed to them from their Lord from the rest of the books of God, including the Qur'an, for all of them, even if they were revealed to others, are considered to have been revealed to them because they worshipped what is in them. They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet. The mention of above and below is to emphasize the ease of the means of provision for them and their abundance and variety of types. His statement, Among them is a moderate nation is the answer to an implied question, as if it were said, are all of them described by the previous descriptions, or some but not others? The moderate ones among them are the believers, such as Abdullah bin Salam and those who followed him and a group of Christians. And many of them - evil is what they do and they are those who persist in disbelief and rebel against answering Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believing in what he brought. Ibn Ishaq, Al-Tabarani in Al-Kabeer, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: A Jewish man called Al-Nabbash bin Qais said: Your Lord is stingy and does not spend. So God revealed: And the Jews say, ‘The hand of God is chained’ (Al-Baqarah 2:17). Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority that it was revealed about Phinehas the Jew. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the Jews say, ‘The hand of God is chained’ meaning stingy. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on his authority. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief, he said: The envy of Muhammad and the Arabs led them to abandon the Qur’an and disbelieve in Muhammad and his religion even though they found it written in their possessions. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Whenever they kindled the fire of war, he said: The war of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse, Whenever they agreed upon something, God scattered it, extinguished their fire and their fire, and cast terror into their hearts. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And if only the People of the Scripture had believed and feared God, he said: They had believed in what was revealed to Muhammad and feared what God had forbidden. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel, he said: Acting upon them. As for what was revealed to them, it is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what was revealed to him. As for they would have eaten from above them, I sent rain upon them. As for from beneath their feet, he says, I will grow for them from the earth from My provision what will suffice them. Among them is a moderate nation, and they are the Muslims, the People of the Book. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: they would have eaten from above them, meaning, I would have sent down rain upon them. And from beneath their feet, he said: The earth brings forth its blessings. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, who said: The moderate nation is those who are neither immoral in religion nor are they extreme. He said: Elevation is desire, and immorality is falling short of it. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi: A moderate nation, he says, a believing nation. Ibn Mardawayh narrated: Abdullah bin Ja`far told us, Ahmad bin Yunus al-Dhabi told us, Asim bin Ali told us, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Ya`qub bin Zayd bin Talhah, on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned a hadith. He said: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them: “The nation of Moses split into seventy-two sects, one of which is in Paradise and seventy-one of which is in Hell. The nation of Jesus split into seventy-two sects, one of which is in Paradise and seventy-one of which is in Hell. My nation will be superior to both groups, one sect in Paradise and seventy-two of which are in Hell.” They said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? He said: The groups, the groups. Yaqub bin Zaid said: Whenever Ali bin Abi Talib narrated this hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would recite the Qur’an in which he said: And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared God, We would have removed from them their misdeeds until His saying: Among them is a moderate nation, but many of them - evil is what they do. He also recited: And among those We created is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby, meaning the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation after mentioning this hadith, the following wording: The hadith about the nations splitting into seventy-something is narrated through many chains of narration that we have mentioned elsewhere. I said: As for the addition that they are in the Fire except for one, a group of hadith scholars have declared it weak. Rather, Ibn Hazm said that it is fabricated.
5:67: The generality of what was revealed indicates that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, must convey all that God revealed to him and not conceal anything of it. This is evidence that he did not divulge anything to anyone related to what God revealed to him. For this reason, it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: Whoever claims that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealed anything of the revelation has lied. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Juhayfah Wahb bin Abdullah Al-Suwai’i, he said: I said to Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: Do you have anything of the revelation that is not in the Qur’an? He said: No, by Him who split the seed and created the soul, except an understanding that God gives a man of the Qur’an and what is in this document. I said: What is in this document? He said: Reason, the release of the prisoner, and that a Muslim should not be killed for a disbeliever. If you do not do what you were commanded to do of conveying all of it, but rather conceal even some of it, then you have not conveyed His message. Abu Amr and the people of Kufa, except Shu’bah, read his message in the singular form. The people of Medina and the people of Ash-Sham read his messages in the plural form. An-Nahhas said: The plural is clearer because the revelation was sent down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, little by little, then he would explain it. This is questionable, because denying the communication of a single message is more eloquent than denying it of messages, as the scholars of rhetoric have mentioned, with a difference of opinion. That, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conveyed to his nation what was revealed to them, and he said to them in more than one place: Have I conveyed? So they testified for him with the explanation, so God rewarded him well on behalf of his nation. Then God, the Exalted, promised him protection from the people to repel what was thought to be a reason for concealing the explanation, which was fear of harm from the people, and that happened, praise be to God, for he explained to the servants of God what was revealed to them in full, then he forced those who refused to enter the religion to enter it willingly or unwillingly, and he killed the leaders of polytheism and dispersed their groups and scattered their ranks, and the word of God was supreme, so everyone who disputed with him, for whom the sword had not preceded the reproach, became Muslim until he said on the day of the conquest to the leaders and notables of Quraysh 106:What do you think I will do to you? They said: A noble brother and a noble nephew. He said: Go, for you are free. And so it is with those scholars of this nation who have been given care, God will protect them from the people, if they stand up to explain God’s proofs and clarify His evidence, and cry out among those who oppose God and are stubborn and do not comply with His law, like the groups of innovators. We have seen this in ourselves and heard it in others, which increases the believer’s faith and steadfastness in God’s religion and his strength in standing up for God’s proof. Everything that those who are weak in their feet and disturbed in their hearts think about harm befalling them and trials befalling them is just delusions and false delusions, because all of this… An ordeal in appearance is an ordeal in reality, because it only brings good in the first and the last: Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or listens while he is present. His statement: Indeed, God does not guide the disbelieving people is a sentence that includes an explanation for what came before regarding infallibility: that is, God will not give them a way to harm you, so do not fear and convey what you have been commanded to convey. Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: When the verse, Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, was revealed, he said: O Lord, I am only one, what can I do? People will gather around me. So the verse, And if you do not, then you have not delivered His message, was revealed. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God sent me with His message and I felt very weak because of it and I knew that people would deny me. So He promised me that I would deliver it or He would punish me. So the verse, “O Messenger, deliver what has been revealed to you from your Lord,” was revealed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And if you do not, then you have not delivered His message, meaning that if you conceal a verse of what was revealed to you, you have not delivered His message. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri who said: This verse, O Messenger, deliver what has been revealed to you, was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Ghadir Khumm regarding Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: We used to recite during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Ali is the Master of the Believers. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And God will protect you from the people.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Antara who said: I was with Ibn Abbas when a man came to him and said: Some people come to us and tell us that you have something that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not reveal to the people. He said: Did you not know that God said: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and by God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not inherit us anything black or white. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Which verse was revealed from the heaven that was most difficult for you? He said: I was in Mina during the season, and the polytheists of the Arabs and the majority of the people gathered during the season, so Gabriel came down to me and said: “O Messenger, announce what has been revealed to you” the verse. He said: So I stood at Al-Aqaba and called: O people, who will help me to announce the message of my Lord and for him is Paradise? O people, say there is no god but God and I am the Messenger of God to you, you will prosper and be successful and for you is Paradise. He said: There was not a man, woman or child who did not throw dirt and stones and spit in my face and say: A lying Sabean. Then someone came to me and said: O Muhammad, if you are the Messenger of God, then it is time for you to call down a curse upon them as Noah called down a curse upon his people. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, guide my people for they do not know. Then his uncle Al-Abbas came and saved him from them and drove them away from him.” Al-A’mash said: The Abbasids boast about that and say about them: Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills. The Prophet fell in love. May God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Talib, and God willed that Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib. Abd ibn Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym, and Al-Bayhaqi, both in Al-Dala’il, narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was guarding until the verse, And God will protect you from the people, was revealed. Then he stuck his head out of the dome and said, O people, go back, for God has protected me. Al-Hakim said in Al-Mustadrak: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not narrate it. At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa’id. There are narrations with this meaning. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, invaded Banu Anmar, he alighted at Dhat ar-Raqee’ at the top of a palm grove. While he was sitting at the head of a well with his feet dangling, al-Warith from Banu al-Najjar said: ‘I will kill Muhammad.’ His companions said to him: ‘How will you kill him?’ He said: ‘I will tell him to give me his sword.’ When he gives it to me, I will kill him with it. So he came to him and said: ‘O Muhammad, give me your sword so I can smell it.’ So he gave it to him, and his hand trembled until it fell from his hand. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God came between you and what you want.’ So God, the Exalted, revealed: ‘O Messenger, proclaim what has been revealed to you’ (al-Masjid an-Nisa’ 4:100).” Ibn Kathir said: This is a strange hadith from this source. Ibn Hibban narrated in his Sahih and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar to this story from Abu Hurayrah, but he did not name the man. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, and there are narrations on this topic. The story of Ghawrath ibn al-Harith is confirmed in Sahih, and it is well-known and famous.
5:68: His statement: 90- On something contains contempt and belittling of what they are upon: meaning you are not upon anything that is worthy of consideration until you establish the Torah and the Gospel: that you act upon what is in them of God's commands and prohibitions, including His command to you to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and His prohibition against disobeying him. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: It is possible that this was before their abrogation. His statement: And what has been revealed to you from your Lord It was said that it is the Qur'an, because establishing the two books is not valid without establishing it, and it is possible that what is meant is what was revealed to them on the tongues of the prophets other than the two books. His statement: And many of them will surely increase in transgression and disbelief what has been revealed to you from your Lord. That is, disbelief upon disbelief and transgression upon transgression. What is meant by many of them is those who did not submit and continued to be stubborn. It was said that what is meant by this is the scholars among them. Prefacing this sentence with an oath is to emphasize its meaning. His statement: So do not grieve over the disbelieving people. That is, leave off feeling sorry for these people, for the harm of that will return to them and will befall them, and in those believers who follow you you will be sufficient for you without them.
5:69: His statement: 69- Indeed, those who believed etc., is a renewed sentence to encourage those other than them from the believers. What is meant by the believers here are those who believed with their tongues and they are the hypocrites, and those who were Jews i.e. entered the religion of the Jews, and the Sabians is raised as a subject and its predicate is omitted, and the meaning is: and the soap and the Christians are likewise. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: The raising is carried by the advancement and delay, and the meaning is: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews are those who believed in God and the Last Day and did righteousness - there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve, and the soap and the Christians are likewise, and Sibawayh recited the words of the poet: Otherwise, know that you and I are rebels as long as we remain in discord. Otherwise, know that I am aggressors and so are you. Similar to this is what Dabi Al-Barjami said: Whoever spends the night in the city, then I and Qiyar are strangers there So I am a stranger, and so is Qiyar. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Akhfash said: The Sabians are conjoined to the pronoun in they have become Jews. An-Nahhas said: I heard Az-Zajjaj say, when Al-Kisa'i and Al-Akhfash's statement was mentioned to him: This is wrong for two reasons: The first is that the pronoun in the nominative case is not conjoined to it until it is emphasized. The second is that the conjoined is a partner to the conjoined to, so the meaning becomes: The Sabians have entered Judaism, and this is impossible. Al-Farra' said: The raising is permissible because in is weak and only affects the noun and not the predicate. According to this, it is, in his view, conjoined to the place of the noun of in, or to the combination of in and its noun. It was said that the predicate of in is implied, and the following sentence is the predicate of the Sabians and Christians, as in the poet's saying: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs It was said that in here means yes. So, soap is raised by the beginning, and similar to it is the saying of Qais bin Al-Ruqayyat: Early in the morning, the censurer will blame me and I will blame him. They say, Gray hair has covered you, and you have grown old. I said, It is... Al-Akhfash said: It means yes and the ha is for pause. We have already discussed the Sabians and Christians in Surat Al-Baqarah. The Sabians were read with an explicit ya to lighten the hamza, and soap was read without a ya, and it is from saba yasbu because they were inclined to follow desires, and the Sabians were read in apposition to the noun of in. His statement, Whoever believes in God is a subject whose predicate is there is no fear concerning them, nor do they grieve. The subject and its predicate are the predicate of in, and the fa’ was included to include the subject with the meaning of a condition, and the referent to the noun of in is omitted: i.e. whoever believes among them, and it is permissible for whoever believes to be a substitute for the noun of in and what is conjoined to it, and the predicate of in is there is no fear concerning them, nor do they grieve. The meaning, assuming that what is meant by those who believed are the hypocrites, as we have stated, is that whoever from these groups believed with a sincere belief in the required manner and did righteous deeds, then he is the one for whom there is no fear or sorrow. As for assuming that what is meant by those who believed is all the people of Islam: the sincere and the hypocrites, then what is meant by those who believed is the one who was characterized by pure faith and continued in it, and the one who innovated pure faith after his hypocrisy.
5:70: His statement: 70- We took a covenant from the Children of Israel is an introductory statement to explain some of their evil deeds. The meaning of the covenant was explained in Al-Baqarah. And We sent to them messengers to inform them of the laws and warn them. Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire is a conditional clause that occurred in response to a question from some of the rabbis about sending messengers, as if it was said: What did they do to the messengers? The answer to the condition is omitted: i.e. they disobeyed him. His statement: A group they denied and a group they killed is also a renewed clause in response to a question from some about the first answer, as if it was said: How did they do to them? So it was said that a group of them denied them and did not harm them, and another group of them killed them. He only said: And a group they killed to take into account the beginnings of the verses. Among those they denied was Jesus and his likes from the prophets, and among those they killed were Zachariah and John.
5:71: His saying: 71- And they thought that there would be no trial meaning, those whom God took a covenant from thought that there would be no trial or test from God Almighty with hardships, being deceived by their saying: We are the sons of God and His beloved. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read takun in the nominative case on the basis that it is the lightened form of the heavy one, and hasab means knowledge, because an means to confirm. The rest read it in the accusative case on the basis that an is the subject of the verb, and hasab means to think. An-Nahhas said: The grammarians use the nominative case in hasabt and its sisters ajwaad, and similar to it: Didn't you claim today that I have grown old and that people like me will not witness entertainment? His saying: Then they became blind and deaf means they became blind to seeing guidance, and deaf to hearing the truth. This is a reference to what happened from the Children of Israel in the beginning, in disobeying the rulings of the Torah, and killing Isaiah, then God accepted their repentance when they repented, and removed the famine from them. Then many of them became blind and deaf This is a reference to what happened from them after repentance, in killing John the son of Zechariah and intending to kill Jesus. The raising of many is a substitute for the pronoun in the two verbs. Al-Akhfash said: Just as you say I saw your people, the three of them, and if you wish it is on the implication of the subject: meaning the blindness and deafness are many of them. It is permissible for many to be raised as the agent in the language of the one who said: The fleas ate me, and from this is the saying of the poet: But his father and mother's warm clothes in Hauran squeeze the salt of his relatives It was read as blind and deaf in the passive form: meaning God made them blind and deaf.
5:72: His statement: 72- They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'God is the Messiah, the son of Mary.' This is an introductory statement that includes a statement of some of the scandals of the People of the Book. Those who say this statement are a group of them: they are called the Jacobites, and it was said that they are the Angels. They said that God Almighty was incarnated in the essence of Jesus. So God responded to them by saying: And the Messiah said, 'O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord.' That is, while the Messiah had said this statement, how can they claim divinity for someone who admits that he is a servant like them? His statement: Whoever associates partners with God, God has forbidden him Paradise. The pronoun refers to the matter, and this is an introductory statement that includes a statement that polytheism necessitates the prohibition of entering Paradise. It was said that it is from Jesus' statement: And the wrongdoers will have no helpers, who will help them and admit them into Paradise or save them from the Fire.
5:73: His statement: 73- They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'God is the third of three.' This is also a statement that is a beginning to explain some of their shameful deeds. What is meant by the third of three is one of three, and for this reason it is added to what comes after it. It is not permissible to add the tanween as Al-Zajjaj and others said. Rather, what comes after it is added and the nasb is added if what comes after it is lower in rank, such as the third of two and the fourth of three. Those who say that He, glory be to Him, is the third of three are the Christians. What is meant by the three is God, glory be to Him, Jesus, and Mary, as is indicated by His statement: Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as gods?' This is what is meant by their statement of three hypostases: the hypostasis of the father, the hypostasis of the son, and the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit. We have already discussed this in Surat An-Nisa'. Then God, glory be to Him, responded to this false claim by saying: And there is no god except God, the One. That is, there is nothing in existence except God, glory be to Him. This sentence is a circumstantial statement, and the meaning is: They said that statement, and the situation is that there is no existent except God. And the word in His statement: From a god to emphasize the comprehensiveness derived from the negation. And if they do not desist from what they say of disbelief, a painful punishment will befall those who disbelieve among them. The answer to a deleted oath that took the place of the answer to the condition, and from in from them is explanatory or partial.
5:74: 74- Do they not repent to God and seek His forgiveness? The fa is for connecting to something understood, and the hamza is for denial.
5:75: His statement: 75- The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. That is, he is limited to the message, and does not go beyond it as you claim. The phrase and messengers have passed away before him is an attribute of a messenger: that is, he is no more than a messenger from the same category as the messengers who passed away before him. The miracles that occurred from him do not necessitate that he be a god, as the messengers before him were similar to them. For God revived the staff in the hand of Moses and created Adam without a father. So how do you make Jesus's revival of the dead and his existence without a father necessitate that he be a god? If he is a god as you claim, then the messengers before him who came with the same as he came with were gods, and you do not say that. His statement: And his mother was a truthful woman is in apposition to the Messiah: that is, his mother was no more than a truthful woman: that is, truthful in what she says or believing in what her son brought of the message, and that does not necessitate her being a god, rather she is like all other women who have this description. His saying: They were eating food is a resumption that includes the confirmation of what was indicated, that they are like all other human beings: that is, whoever eats food like all other creatures is not a lord, but rather a servant who is a servant born of women. So when is he fit to be a lord? As for your saying that he was eating food with his humanity and not his divinity, this is a false statement that necessitates the mixing of the divine with the non-divine and the coming together of humanity and divinity. If it were permissible for the eternal to mix with the created, then it would be permissible for the eternal to be created. If this were true for Jesus, then it would be true for other servants. See how We make clear to them the signs meaning the evidence. In it is astonishment at the state of those who make those descriptions necessitate divinity and ignore that they existed at a time when they do not say that he is a god. Then see how they are turned away meaning how they are diverted from the truth after this explanation. It is said: afkahu ya’fukahu if he diverts him. The command was repeated with regard to exaggeration in astonishment, and thumma was used to show the difference between the two astonishments. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “Nafi’ bin Haritha, Salam bin Mishkam, Malik bin Al-Sayf and Rafi’ bin Harmalah came and said: O Muhammad, do you not claim that you are on the religion and faith of Abraham and believe in what we have of the Torah and testify that it is the truth from God? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, but you have innovated and denied what was in it from the covenant taken from you and disbelieved in what you were commanded to explain to the people, so I disavow your innovations. They said: We are taken by what is in our hands and we are on the guidance and the truth and we do not believe in you nor follow you. So God revealed about them: ‘Say, O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel’ until His saying: ‘the disbelieving people.’” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding His statement: ‘And they thought that there would be no trial’: He said: A trial. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi something similar. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the third of three,’ that he said: The Christians say that God is the third of three and they lied. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The Children of Israel split into three groups regarding Jesus. One group said, He is God, another group said, He is the son of God, and another group said, He is the servant and spirit of God. They are the moderate ones, and they are the Muslims of the People of the Book.
5:76: God the Almighty ordered His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say this to them, to oblige them and to put an end to their doubts: Do you suffer, instead of God, by being neighbors to something that has no power to harm or benefit you? Rather, he is a commanded servant, and whatever benefit comes through his hand, or harm is repelled, it is by God’s decree and enabling him to do so. As for him, he is incapable of owning any of that for himself, let alone owning it for someone else. And if someone does not benefit or harm, how can you take him as a god and worship him? And what reason necessitates that? What is meant here is the Messiah, peace be upon him. And God the Almighty mentioned harm before benefit because repelling harm is more important than bringing benefits. 76- And God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. That is, how can you worship something that has no power to harm or benefit you, when the fact is that God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, and whoever is like that is able to harm and benefit because He encompasses everything that is heard and known, including your harms and benefits.
5:77: His statement: 77- "Extremists in your religion" When God Almighty invalidated all the false doubts they clung to, He forbade them from extremism in their religion, which is going beyond the limit, such as affirming the divinity of Jesus, as the Christians say, or lowering him from his lofty status, as the Jews say, for all of that is from the reprehensible extremism and following the path of excess or neglect and choosing them over the path of correctness. "And other" is in the accusative case as an adjective for a deleted source: that is, extremism other than the extremism of the truth. As for extremism in the truth by conveying all the effort in searching for it and extracting its truths, it is not reprehensible. It was said that the accusative case is for the connected exception, and it was said that it is for the disconnected. "And do not follow the desires of a people who have gone astray before," and they are the ancestors of the People of the Book from the two sects of the Jews and Christians: that is, before the mission of Muhammad, upon him be the best prayers and peace. "And they led many astray" of the people. "And they have gone astray from the straight path," that is, from their intention of the path of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the mission. What is meant is that their ancestors went astray before the mission and led many people astray at that time, and they went astray after the mission, either by themselves, or by making the misguidance of those they led astray their misguidance because they established that for them and followed it for them. It was said that what is meant by the first is their disbelief in what reason requires, and by the second is their disbelief in what the law requires.
5:78: His statement: 78- Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed meaning God Almighty cursed them by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary meaning in the Psalms and the Gospel by the tongue of David and Jesus for what they did of sins such as their transgression on the Sabbath and their disbelief in Jesus. His statement: That is because they disobeyed is a new sentence in response to an implied question, and the reference in that is to the curse: meaning that the curse is because of the disobedience and transgression and not for any other reason.
5:79: Then the Almighty explained disobedience and aggression by saying: 79- They did not forbid one another from the evil they were doing. So the action was attributed to them because the one who did it was one of them, even if they did not all do it. The meaning is that they did not forbid the sinner from repeating a sin he had already done, or was preparing to do. It is possible that their description of having done the evil was in consideration of the state of revelation, not the state of not forbidding it. Disobedience and aggression were explained by not forbidding the evil, because whoever neglects the duty of forbidding the evil has disobeyed God the Almighty and transgressed His limits. Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong are among the most important Islamic principles and the most important religious obligations. For this reason, the one who abandons it is a partner with the one who commits the sin and deserves the wrath and vengeance of God, as happened to the people of the Sabbath.
