God, the Exalted, transformed those who did not participate with them in the act but failed to denounce them, just as He transformed the aggressors, so that they all became monkeys and pigs. Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or listens while he is a witness. Then God, the Exalted, said, condemning the failure to forbid evil, How evil is that which they used to do, meaning their failure to denounce what they were obligated to denounce.
5:80: 80- "You see many of them meaning of the Jews such as Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions taking as allies those who disbelieve" meaning the polytheists and are not of their religion. "Evil is that which their souls have put forward for them" meaning what they have made attractive and beautified, or what they have put forward for themselves in order to be returned to on the Day of Resurrection. What is specifically condemned is "that God is angry with them" meaning the reason for God's anger with them due to the deletion of an added word, or it is God's anger with them due to the deletion of a subject. It was said that it is: meaning that God's anger with them is a substitute for what.
5:81: 81- And if they had believed in God and the Prophet meaning their Prophet and what was revealed to him of the Book they would not have taken them meaning the polytheists as allies because God Almighty and His Messenger sent to them and His Book revealed to them forbade them from that but many of them are wicked meaning they are outside the guardianship of God and outside the belief in Him and His Messenger and His Book. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Do not go to extremes in your religion, that he said: Do not innovate. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, that among the things in which they went to extremes was that they claimed that God had a wife and a son. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, and have strayed from the right path, that he said: The Jews. And Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The first deficiency that befell the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another man and say to him: ‘O man, fear God and leave what you are doing, for it is not permissible for you. ’ Then he would meet him the next day and that would not prevent him from being his food, drink, or seat. When they did that, God struck the hearts of some of them with others and then said: ‘Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David’ until His saying: ‘disobedient. ’ Then He said: ‘No, by God, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you must take the hand of the oppressor and force him to follow the truth. ’” This hadith has been narrated through many chains of narration, and the hadiths on this topic are very numerous, so we will not prolong their mention. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David meaning in the Psalms and by Jesus, son of Mary meaning in the Gospel. Abu Ubaid, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ghifari regarding the verse, saying: They were cursed by the tongue of David and were made into apes, and by the tongue of Jesus and were made into pigs. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Mujahid. Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Qatadah. Al-Daylami narrated in Musnad al-Firdaws on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: The Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets at the beginning of the day, then one hundred and twelve men from among their servants stood up and commanded them to do good and forbade them from doing evil, so they were all killed at the end of the day. They are the ones whom God mentioned, Cursed those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel in the verses. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, Evil is that which their souls have put forward for them, he said: What they commanded them. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Kharaiti in Masawi Al-Akhlaq, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman and he declared it weak narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “O Muslims, beware of adultery, for there are six things in it: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for that which is in this world: the loss of splendor, perpetual poverty, and a short life. As for that which is in the Hereafter: the wrath of God, a bad reckoning, and eternity in the Fire. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them: that God is angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.’” Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation: This hadith is weak in any case. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: ‘And if they had believed in God and the Prophet and in what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. ’ He said: The hypocrites.
5:82: His saying: 82- You will find etc. This is a renewed sentence that confirms what it contains of enumeration of the Jews' faults and shortcomings, and the addition of the oath lam to it increases its emphasis and confirmation, and the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to anyone who is suitable for him as in other places in the Noble Book. The meaning in the verse is that the Jews and polytheists, may God curse them, are the most hostile of all people to the believers and the most stubborn in that, and that the Christians are the closest people in affection to the believers, and the lam in for those who believed in both places is related to an omitted word that was an attribute of enmity and affection, and it was said that it is related to enmity and affection, and the indication in his saying: that is to their being the closest in affection, and the ba in because among them are priests is for causality: that is because among them are priests, and it is the plural of qass and qasis said by Qatrib. And the priest is the scholar, and its origin is from qass: if he follows something and seeks it. The rajaz poet said: They become oblivious to the severity of harm. Their voices were scattered at night, I heard them. The priest: gossip. The priest is also: the leader of the Christians in religion and knowledge, and its plural is also qusus, and so is the priest: like evil and evil, and it is said in the plural of qasis by breaking it into qasausa by replacing one of the two sins with a waw, and the origin is qasasa, so what is meant by the priests in the verse: the followers of the scholars and worshippers, and it is either foreign that the Arabs mixed with their speech, or Arabic. The monks: the plural of rahabib like rakban and rakib, and the verb rahbah God yarhabihu: meaning he feared Him. Monasticism and monasticism: worship in monasteries. Abu Ubaid said: It may be rahban for the singular and plural. Al-Farraa said: It is pluralized rahban if the singular has rahban and habeen like qurban and qarbain. Jarir said in the plural: The monks of Medina would become monks if they saw you. The poet said about using the word monks in the singular: If you saw the monks of a monastery on the mountain, the monks would run down and come down
5:83: Then God the Almighty described them as not being too proud to say the truth, but rather they are humble, unlike the Jews who are the opposite of that, and this sentence is connected to the sentence before it 83- And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger is connected to the sentence and that they are not arrogant. "Overflowing with tears" means filled and overflowing, because overflowing does not happen except after being full, making the eyes overflow, and the overflowing: is only tears intended for exaggeration like their saying his eye shed tears. Imru' al-Qais said: My tears flowed down my throat until my tears soaked my saddle. His saying: From what they have known of the truth from the first is for the beginning of the goal, and the second is explanatory: that is, the beginning of the overflow was arising from knowing the truth, and it is possible for the second to be partial, and their eyes see was read in the passive form. And his saying: They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed’ is a resumption introduced to answer an implied question, as if it was said, so what is their state when they hear the Qur’an? So he said: They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses’ meaning we have believed in this book that was sent down from You to Muhammad and to whom You sent it down, so register us among the witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection from the nation of Muhammad, or with the witnesses that it is true, or with the witnesses to the truthfulness of Muhammad and that he is Your Messenger to the people.
5:84: His statement: 84- "And why do we not believe in God?" is a new statement, and the question is for exclusion. "And for us is related to something omitted, and we do not believe" is in the accusative case in the state, and the estimate is: What happened to us while we do not believe in God and what came to us of the truth? The meaning is: They excluded the absence of faith from them while there is a reason for it, which is the desire for God's favor, so the question and the negation are directed to the restriction and the restricted together like the Almighty's saying: "Why do you not hope for God with dignity? And the waw in and we hope that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people" is also for the state with the estimation of the subject: meaning what happened to us who are not believers while we hope to enter with the righteous? So the first and second states are accompanied by the pronoun in "for us" and their agent is the estimated verb: meaning it happened, and it is possible for the second state to be from the pronoun in "we believe" and the estimate is: And why do we combine abandoning faith with the desire for the company of the righteous.
5:85: His saying: 85- So God rewarded them for what they said etc. He rewarded them for this saying, as they were sincere in it and believed in its content.
5:86: His statement: 86- And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire. Denying the signs is disbelief, so it is a case of connecting the specific to the general. Hellfire is a very intense fire. It is said that someone ignited the fire intensely, and it is also said that the eye of a lion is a ignition because of its intense ignition. The poet said: War does not leave its enemies with tricks and jokes Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection Al-Baqarah 2:173, that he said: They are the delegation who came with Ja’far and his companions from the land of Abyssinia. Abu Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No Jew was alone with a Muslim except that he thought of killing him. In another version: Except that he thought of killing him. Ibn Kathir said: It is very strange. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: Whatever good God mentions about the Christians is only intended for the Negus and his companions. Abu Sheikh narrated on his authority that he said: They are people from Abyssinia who believed when the migration of the believers came to them, that was for them. An-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani, Abu Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr who said: This verse was revealed about the Negus and his companions: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilya and Al-Wahidi narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Sa`id ibn Al-Musayyab, Abu Bakr ibn `Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Harith ibn Hisham and `Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr informed me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent `Amr ibn Umayyah Ad-Damri and wrote a letter with him to the Negus. He went to the Negus and read the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he called Ja`far ibn Abi Talib and the Muhajireen with him. The Negus sent for the monks and priests and gathered them together. Then he ordered Ja`far ibn Abi Talib to recite the Qur’an to them. So he recited to them Surat Maryam, and they believed in the Qur’an and their eyes overflowed with tears. They are the ones about whom God revealed, And you will find the nearest of them in love until His saying, of the witnesses. And Abd bin Hamid bin Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding the verse, he said: They are the messengers of the Negus about his Islam and the Islam of his people. They were seventy men whom he chose from his people, the best of whom were in jurisprudence and age. And in another version: He sent thirty of his best companions to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they entered upon him and he recited to them Surat Yasin. They wept when they heard the Qur’an and knew that it was the truth. So God revealed about them: That is because among them were priests and monks and the verse. And this verse was revealed about them also: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it until His saying: Those will be given their reward twice for what they were patient. And Abd bin Hamid, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar without mentioning the number. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: The Negus sent twelve men to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), seven priests and five monks, to look at him and ask him questions. When they met him and he recited to them what God had revealed, they wept and believed. Then God revealed about them: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger (al-Baqarah 2:17). There are many narrations on this subject, and this amount is sufficient, as the only purpose is to explain the reason for the revelation of the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: priests he said: They are their scholars. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd who said: The priests are their servants. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then write us down among the witnesses he said: The nation of Muhammad (peace be upon him).
5:89: Good things: are the pleasures that God has permitted for His servants. He has forbidden those who believe to forbid themselves anything of them, either because they think that this is an act of obedience to God and a way of drawing closer to Him, and that it is part of asceticism in this world to lift oneself from its desires, or because they intend to forbid themselves something that He has permitted them, as many of the common people do when they say: It is forbidden to me, and I have forbidden it to myself, and similar expressions that fall under this Quranic prohibition. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: It is not permissible for any Muslim to forbid himself anything that God has permitted for his believing servants, such as good foods, clothing, and marriages. For this reason, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rejected celibacy from Uthman ibn Maz'un. It has been proven that there is no virtue in abandoning something that God has permitted for His servants, and that virtue and righteousness are only in doing what God has urged His servants to do, and what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did and set as a Sunnah for his Ummah, and the Rightly-Guided Imams followed in his path, since the best guidance is the guidance of our Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). If that is the case, then the error of those who prefer wearing hair and wool to wearing cotton and linen if they are able to wear that because it is permissible, and who prefer eating coarse food and leaving meat and other things out of caution against the danger of needing women, becomes clear. He said: If someone thinks that virtue lies other than what we have said, because wearing and eating coarse food is difficult for the soul and spending the excess value between them on those in need, then he has thought wrong, because what is best for a person is to improve his soul and help it to obey its Lord, and nothing is more harmful to the body than bad food, because it corrupts his mind and weakens his tools that God has made a means to obey Him. His statement: And do not transgress means do not transgress against God by forbidding the good things that God has made lawful for you, or do not transgress and make lawful what God has made unlawful for you: that is, you take concessions and make lawful what is unlawful, just as you were forbidden from making things difficult for yourselves by forbidding what is lawful. The majority of scholars have stated that whoever forbids himself something that God has made lawful for him, it is not forbidden for him and he is not required to make expiation. Abu Hanifa, Ahmad and those who followed them said: Whoever forbids something, it becomes unlawful for him, and if he consumes it, he is required to make expiation. This is contrary to what is in this verse and contrary to what is indicated by the authentic hadiths. Perhaps something simpler than this will come in Surat At-Tahrim, God willing. His statement: God does not love transgressors is an explanation for what preceded it, and it appears that it is a prohibition of all transgression: that is, going beyond what God has prescribed in every matter. The interpretation of idle talk and the disagreement about it have been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah, and 89- in your oaths is the connection of He will hold you accountable. It was said that in means from and oaths are the plural of oath. And in the verse is evidence that God will not hold the one who swears by idle oaths accountable and no expiation is required for them. The majority of the companions and those who came after them went to the view that it is a man saying: No, by God, and yes, by God in his speech, not believing in the oath, and the companions interpreted the verse in this way and they are more knowledgeable about the meanings of the Qur'an. Al-Shafi'i said: This is in the case of obstinacy, anger and haste. His statement: But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have made was read with emphasis on aqdtum and with emphasis on it, and it was read with emphasis on aqdtum. And the contract is of two types: tangible like the contract of a rope, and legal like the contract of sale, the oath and the covenant. The poet said: A people who, when they make a contract with their neighbor, tighten the knot and burden him with hardship. The oath that is complex is a covenant in the heart to do or not do in the future: that is, but you will be held accountable for your complex oaths that are documented with intention and purpose if you break them. As for the false oath: it is an oath of deceit, trickery and lying, and the one who swears bears the sin of it. It is not a covenant and there is no expiation for it, as the majority have stated. Al-Shafi’i said: It is a covenanted oath because it is acquired in the heart, covenanted with report coupled with the name of God. The first is more correct, and all the hadiths that have been narrated about expiation for oaths are directed to the covenanted oath, and none of them indicate the false oath. Rather, what has been narrated about the false oath is only warning and intimidation, and it is one of the major sins, indeed one of the greatest of the major sins. And regarding it, the Almighty said: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price (al-Baqarah 2:17). His saying: His expiation Expiation: is taken from takfir which means covering, and likewise kafr is covering, and the kafir is the coverer, because it covers the sin and conceals it, and the pronoun in his expiation refers to what is in his saying: with what you have decided. “Feeding ten poor people from the average of what you feed your families” What is meant by the average here is the average between the two extremes of extravagance and stinginess, and it does not mean the highest as in other places: that is, feed them from the average of what you usually feed your families from, and you are not obligated to feed them from the highest, and it is not permissible for you to feed them from the lowest, and it appears that feeding ten people until they are full is sufficient. It was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: It is not sufficient to feed ten people lunch without dinner until he feeds them breakfast and dinner. Abu Omar said: This is the saying of the imams of fatwa in the regions. Al-Hasan al-Basri and Ibn Sirin said: It is sufficient for him to feed ten poor people one meal of bread and ghee or bread and meat. Umar ibn al-Khattab, Aisha, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Maymun ibn Mihran, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, al-Hakam, Makhul, Abu Qilabah and Muqatil said: Each of the ten should be given half a sa' of wheat or dates. This was narrated from Ali. Abu Hanifa said: Half a sa' of wheat and a sa' of anything else. Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) disbelieved with a sa' of dates and the people disbelieved with it. Whoever cannot find anything should give half a sa' of wheat. In its chain of transmission is Umar ibn Abdullah ibn Ya'la al-Thaqafi, who is unanimously agreed to be weak. Ad-Daraqutni said: He is rejected. His statement: or clothing them is in apposition to feeding. It is read with a damma on the kaf or a kasra, and they are two dialects like aswa and iswa. Saeed bin Jubair and Muhammad bin Al-Samee’ Al-Yemeni read or their equals meaning like the equals of your families. Clothing for men refers to what covers the body, even if it is a single garment. The same applies to women’s clothing. It was said that clothing for women is a shield and a veil. It was said that what is meant by clothing is what is used for prayer. His statement: or the freeing of a slave means freeing a slave. Freeing means releasing from slavery. Freeing is used to release a prisoner, exempting someone who is exhausted from his work, and not causing harm to him. From this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: My son Ghadana, I have freed you and given you to Atiya bin Jaal. I freed you from satire that would have brought you down and harmed your reputation. Scholars have researched the neck that is sufficient for expiation. The apparent meaning of this verse is that any neck is sufficient, regardless of its nature. A group of them, including Al-Shafi’i, held that faith is a condition for it, based on analogy with the expiation for murder. But whoever cannot find [a slave], then a fast of three days. That is, whoever cannot find any of the things mentioned, then his expiation is fasting for three days. It was read consecutively, as was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud and Ubayy, so this reading restricts the general fast. Abu Hanifa and Al-Thawri said the same, and it is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. Malik and Al-Shafi’i said in his other statement: Separation is sufficient. That is the expiation for your oaths when you swear. That is, what was mentioned is the expiation for your oaths if you swear and break them. Then he ordered them to preserve their oaths and not rush to them or to break them. The reference in his statement: Thus is to the source of the verb mentioned after it, that is, like that explanation. God makes clear to you. This has been repeated in several places in the Noble Book. That you may be grateful for what He has bestowed upon you of explaining His laws and clarifying His rulings. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the verse: O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you was revealed about the people who had forbidden themselves women and meat, they said: O Messenger of God, what should we do with the oaths that we have sworn? So God revealed: God will not punish you for what is unintentional in your oaths. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding the unintentional oath, he said: It is a man who swears an oath that is lawful. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: They are two men who are engaged in a transaction, one of them says: By God, I will not sell it to you for such-and-such, and the other says: By God, I will not buy it for such-and-such. Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Nakha'i who said: Unintentional oaths are when a person connects his words with an oath: By God, you will eat, by God, you will drink, and the like, without intending an oath or intending an oath, so it is an unintentional oath for which there is no expiation. This has been discussed previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, But He will punish you for what you have deliberated on, he said: For what you worshipped. Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Qatada. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to set the expiation for an oath as a mudd of wheat. In its chain of transmission is Al-Nadr bin Zurarah bin Abdul Karim Al-Dahli Al-Kufi. Abu Hatim said: He is unknown. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. The hadith of Ibn Abbas and its weakness have been mentioned above. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Asma bint Abi Bakr that she said: We used to give as expiation for an oath a mudd that we used to eat. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Umar bin Al-Khattab that he said: I swear that I will not give to some people, then I change my mind and give them something, so I feed ten poor people, each one a saa of barley or a saa of dates or half a saa of wheat. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdul bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib who said: The expiation for an oath is to feed ten poor people, giving each one half a sa’ of wheat. Abdul bin Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdul bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated through various chains of narration that: The expiation for an oath is to give each poor person a mudd of wheat. All of them, except Ibn Abi Hatim, narrated something similar on the authority of Zayd bin Thabit. All of them also narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Abdul bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib who said: You can feed them lunch and dinner, if you wish, with bread and meat, or bread and oil, or bread and ghee, or bread with dates. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: From the best of what you feed your families, he said: From your hardship and ease. Ibn Majah narrated on his authority: A man provides for his family with a food that is easy for him, and a man provides for his family with a food that is difficult for him, so the statement: From the best of what you feed your families was revealed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on his authority. At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: Or their clothing, he said: A cloak for each poor person. Ibn Kathir said: It is a strange hadith. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah who said: I said, O Messenger of God, Or their clothing, what is it? He said: A cloak, a cloak. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: A cloak for each poor person or a shawl. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: Clothing is a garment or a loincloth. Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Regarding the expiation for an oath, he has a choice in these three: the first, then the first. If he does not find any of that, then he should fast for three consecutive days. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on his authority.
5:88: 88- And eat from what God has provided for you if it is lawful and good meaning not forbidden or disgusting, or lawful and good food, or eat lawful and good food from what God has provided for you, then God Almighty commanded them to fear God and said: And fear God, in whom you are believers. Al-Tirmidhi narrated with a hasan chain of transmission, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Adi in Al-Kamil, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, when I eat meat, I become inclined towards women and I am overcome by desire, and I have forbidden myself meat, so this verse was revealed: O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you. It was narrated from another source as a mursal, and it was narrated as a mursal attributing it to Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding the verse, saying: “It was revealed about a group of the Companions who said: We will cut off our penises and abandon worldly desires and wander the earth as monks do. This reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he sent for them and mentioned that to them. They said: Yes. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: But I fast and break my fast, I pray and sleep, and I marry women. Whoever follows my Sunnah is of me, and whoever does not follow my Sunnah is not of me.” Something similar to this has been proven in the two Sahihs and others without mentioning that this was the reason for the revelation of the verse. Abd bin Hamid, Abu Dawud in Al-Marasil, and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Malik that these people are Uthman bin Mazun and his companions. There are many narrations with this meaning on this topic, and many of them explicitly state that this was the reason for the revelation of the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam: “Abdullah bin Rawahah was hosted by a guest from his family while he was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he returned to his family and found that they had not fed their guest, waiting for him. So he said to his wife: ‘You have detained my guest for my sake. He is forbidden to me.’ His wife said: ‘He is forbidden to me.’ The guest said: ‘He is forbidden to me.’ When he saw that, he put his hand on it and said: ‘Eat in the name of God.’ Then he went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘You have done well.’ So God revealed: ‘O you who believe! Do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you.’” This is an interrupted report, but in Sahih al-Bukhari in the story of Abu Bakr and his guests there is something similar to this. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Masruq who said: We were with Abdullah when an udder was brought to him. A man moved away, so Abdullah said to him: ‘Come closer.’ He said: ‘I have been forbidden to eat it.’ Abdullah said: ‘Come closer, feed it, and expiate your oath,’ and he recited this verse.” Al-Hakim also included it in his Mustadrak, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it.
5:90: His statement: 90- O you who have believed is addressed to all believers. The explanation of gambling has already been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. And the idols are the idols erected for worship. And the arrows. Its explanation has already been presented at the beginning of this Surah. And filth is used to refer to excrement and filth. It is a predicate for wine, and the predicate for the word conjoined to it is omitted. And His statement: From the work of Satan is an attribute of filth: meaning that it is from the work of Satan, because of his making it look good and beautifying it. And it was said that he was the one who did these things himself, so the children of Adam followed his example. And the pronoun in So avoid it refers to filth or to what was mentioned. And His statement: That you may succeed is the reason for what came before it. He said in Al-Kashaf: He emphasized the prohibition of alcohol and gambling in several ways, including starting the sentence with only, and linking them to idol worship, including his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: The one who drinks alcohol is like the one who worships an idol, and making them an abomination, as he said: So avoid the abomination of idols, and making them the work of Satan, and Satan only brings about pure evil, and ordering avoidance, and making avoidance a source of success, and if avoidance is success, then committing it is a failure and destruction, and mentioning the calamity that results from them, which is the occurrence of hostility and hatred between those who drink alcohol and gamble, and what they lead to in terms of turning away from the remembrance of God and from observing the times of prayer. End quote. This verse is evidence of the prohibition of alcohol, as it includes the obligation to avoid it and the prohibition of turning away, and as it is established in the Sharia that it is prohibited to offer sacrifices to impurities, let alone make it a drink that is drunk. The scholars of interpretation and others said: The prohibition of alcohol was gradual and due to many incidents, because they had become accustomed to drinking it and Satan had made it beloved to their hearts. The first thing that was revealed concerning it was: “They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people.’” At that point, some of the Muslims stopped drinking it, but others did not. Then the verse of God the Almighty was revealed: Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated. Some of them stopped drinking it as well, and said: We have no need for what distracts us from prayer. Some of them drank it at times other than prayer, until this verse was revealed: Intoxicants and gambling are only what is forbidden. So it became forbidden to them, until some of them said: God has not prohibited anything more severe than wine. This is because of what they understood from the severity of what this verse included in terms of deterrents, and what the authentic hadiths came with in terms of warnings for those who drink it, and that it is one of the major sins.
5:91: Muslims have unanimously agreed on this, without any doubt or suspicion, and they have also unanimously agreed on the prohibition of selling it and benefiting from it as long as it is wine. Just as this verse indicates the prohibition of wine, it also indicates the prohibition of gambling, idols, and arrows. This verse has indicated the worldly corruption of wine and gambling, saying: 91- Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred and the religious corruption, saying: and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. His statement: Will you then desist? contains a strong warning, which is indicated by the question that indicates rebuke and reprimand. That is why Omar, may God be pleased with him, said when he heard this: We have desisted.
5:92: Then God Almighty confirmed this prohibition by saying: 92- And obey God and obey the Messenger and beware meaning disobeying them: meaning disobeying God and His Messenger, for even if this is an absolute command, bringing it in this place indicates what we mentioned of emphasis, and likewise what He indicated by saying: But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification meaning if you turn away from compliance, then the Messenger has done what was required of him of the notification in which is your guidance and your well-being, and you have harmed none but yourselves by disobeying, and in this there is a deterrent whose value cannot be measured and whose extent cannot be reached.
7:32: His statement: 93- There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten meaning of the foods that they desire, and although food is used more for eating, it is permissible to use it for drinking, and from this is the statement of the Most High: And whoever does not taste it, then it is from me God Almighty permitted them in this verse everything they have eaten, whatever it was, restricted by His statement: If they fear meaning fear what is forbidden to them, such as alcohol and other major sins, and all transgressions and believe in God and do righteous deeds of the deeds that God has prescribed for them: meaning they continue to do them. His saying: Then fear is in apposition to the first fear: that is, fear what was forbidden to them after that, even though it was permissible before, and believe in its prohibition, then fear what was forbidden to them after the prohibition mentioned before it, which was permissible before, and do good, that is, do good deeds. This is the meaning of the verse. It was said that the repetition is in consideration of the three times, and it was said that the repetition is in consideration of the three levels, the beginning, the middle, and the end, and it was said that the repetition is in consideration of what a person fears, for he should leave the forbidden things to avoid punishment, and the doubts to avoid falling into the forbidden, and some of the permissible things to preserve the soul from baseness, and it was said that it is for the sake of emphasis, as in the saying of the Most High: “No, you will surely know. Then, no, you will surely know.” All of these aspects are without regard to the reason for the revelation of the verse. Either with regard to the reason for its revelation, which is that when the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, some of the Companions said: What about those among us who died while drinking it and gambling? So it was revealed. It has been said that the meaning is fear polytheism and believe in God and His Messenger then fear the major sins and believe that is, increase in faith then fear the minor sins and do good that is, perform voluntary acts. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: The first verse is to fear God by accepting His command, believing in it, adhering to it, and acting upon it. The second verse is to fear God by remaining steadfast in believing in it. The third verse is to fear God by doing good and drawing closer to Him through voluntary acts of worship. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sha’b narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: “Three verses were revealed concerning wine. The first was: ‘They ask you about wine and gambling. ’ The verse was said: ‘O Messenger of God, let us benefit from it as God said. ’ He remained silent about them. Then this verse was revealed: ‘Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated. ’ It was said: ‘O Messenger of God, let us benefit from it as God said. ’ He remained silent about them. Then this verse was revealed: ‘O you who believe, wine is only… ’ The verse was revealed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Wine has been forbidden. ’ Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: Wine was forbidden three times, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar, ‘The people said: O Messenger of God, people were killed in the way of God and died on… Their bed was drinking wine and gambling, and God has made it an abomination from the work of Satan, so God revealed: “There is no blame upon those who believe” 2:100. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If it had been forbidden to them, they would have abandoned it as you have abandoned it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas in his Naskh, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: When the prohibition of wine was revealed, a man from the Ansar made food and invited some people to come to him. They ate and drank until they were intoxicated from the wine, and that was before wine was prohibited, so they boasted. The Ansar said: The Ansar are better than the Muhajireen, and the Quraysh said: The Quraysh are better. A man reached for the jawbone of a camel and hit me on the nose. I went to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him, so this verse was revealed: O you who believe, indeed, wine and gambling 2:100. `Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The prohibition of alcohol was revealed concerning two tribes of the Ansar who drank. When the people became drunk, they played with each other. When they sobered up, one of them would see the marks on his face, head and beard, and he would say: My brother so-and-so did this to me. They were brothers with no grudge in their hearts. By God, if He had been kind and merciful to me, He would not have done this to me until grudges had settled in their hearts. Then God revealed this verse: O you who have believed, indeed, indeed, wine and gambling are but… until His saying: Will you then desist? Some of the pretenders said: It is an abomination, and it is in the stomach of so-and-so who was killed on the day of Badr and so-and-so who was killed on the day of Uhud. Then God revealed this verse: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten… Many narrations have been narrated about the reason for revelation that agree with what we have mentioned. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: Gambling is all gambling. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Kaysan who said: I said to Jabir, when was alcohol prohibited? He said: After Uhud. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: The prohibition of alcohol was revealed in Surat Al-Ma'idah, after the Battle of the Confederates. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: All gambling is from maysir, even the children playing with nuts and cubes. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali Ibn Abi Talib who said: Backgammon and chess are from maysir. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Ali who said: Chess is the gambling of the non-Arabs. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim Ibn Muhammad that he was asked about dice, is it from maysir? He said: Everything that distracts from the remembrance of God and from prayer is gambling. Abd Ibn Hamid and Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in Dhamm Al-Malahi and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab also narrated on his authority that it was said to him: You hate dice, so what about chess? He said: Everything that distracts from the remembrance of God and from prayer is from maysir. They also narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr who said: O people of Mecca, it has reached me about men who play a game called dice, and God says in His Book: O you who believe, indeed, wine and gambling are but… until His saying: Will you then desist? And I swear by God that if I bring anyone playing it, I will punish him in his hair and skin, and I will give his spoils to whoever brings them to me. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated on the authority of Malik ibn Anas who said: Chess is from dice. It has reached us on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was in charge of the money of an orphan and burned it. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far that he was asked about chess and he said: That is Zoroastrianism, so do not play with it. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash`ari who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever plays dice has disobeyed God and His Messenger. Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahim al-Khatmi who heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The example of the one who plays dice and then stands up and prays is like the example of the one who performs ablution with pus and pig blood and then stands up and prays. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar who said: The one who plays dice gambling is like the one who eats pork, and the one who plays it without gambling is like the one who greases the belly of a pig. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Katheer who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by some people who were playing dice and said: Heedless hearts, sick hands, and idle tongues. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: Gambling is gambling. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Layth on the authority of Ata, Tawus, and Mujahid who said: Everything in which there is gambling is gambling, even children playing with nuts and heels. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin who said: Gambling is gambling. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Shuraih that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Three things are gambling: whistling with pigeons, gambling, and hitting heels. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ansab are stones to which they used to slaughter, and Azlam are arrows with which they used to cast lots. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: They had pebbles, and if one of them wanted to go on a raid or sit, he would cast lots with them. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding Azlam, he said: They are the Persian arrows with which they used to cast lots, and the arrows of the Arabs. Many hadiths have been narrated condemning alcohol and its drinker, and the severe threat to it, and that every intoxicant is forbidden. They are recorded in the books of hadith, so we will not dwell on them, as we are not concerned with that, but rather with what is related to interpretation. His saying: 32- "Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants?" Adornment is what a person adorns himself with, such as clothing or other permissible things, such as metals that have not been prohibited from adorning themselves with, and jewels and the like. It was said: Clothing is specific and there is no basis for that, rather it is part of what the verse includes. So there is no blame on someone who wears good, expensive clothes if it is not something that God has forbidden, and there is no blame on someone who adorns himself with something that has a role in adornment and is not prohibited by a legal prohibition. Whoever claims that this is contrary to asceticism has made a clear mistake. We have already presented enough on this, and likewise with good foods, drinks and the like that people eat, there is no asceticism in abandoning good things from them. That is why this verse came with a title that includes a question that includes denunciation of whoever forbids that for himself or forbids it for others. How good is what Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: “He who prefers to wear hair and wool over cotton and linen, despite the fact that it is permissible to do so, and he who eats legumes and lentils and chooses them over wheat bread, and he who refrains from eating meat for fear of the temptation of lust, has erred. We have already quoted something similar from him at length.” And the good and enjoyable foods, and it was said: It is a general name for what is good to earn and eat: His statement: “Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world” meaning that it is theirs in principle, even if the disbelievers share it with them as long as they are alive, pure on the Day of Resurrection meaning it is exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection, and the disbelievers will not share it with them. Nafi’ read pure in the nominative case, which is the reading of Ibn Abbas, as if it is report after report. The rest read it in the accusative case as a state. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: It is not permissible to stop at the world because what comes after it is related to His statement: for those who believe is a state of it, with the estimation: Say: It is fixed for those who believe in the life of this world in the state of its purity for them on the Day of Resurrection. His saying: Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know. That is, in this way We detail the verses that include what is permissible and what is forbidden.
5:94: His saying: 94- To test you meaning to try you, and the lam is the answer to an omitted oath. Hunting was one of the livelihoods of the Arabs, so God tested them by forbidding it while in ihram and in the sanctuary, just as He tested the Children of Israel so that they would not transgress on the Sabbath. The verse was revealed in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, some of them entered ihram and some did not, so if game was presented, their conditions differed regarding it. Scholars have differed about who is addressed in this verse: are they those who are in a state of ihram or those who are in a state of ihram? Malik went for the former, and Ibn Abbas went for the latter. The most likely opinion is that the address is for everyone, and there is no reason to limit it to some and not others. The min in min as-sayd is for partiality, which is land hunting, as stated by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari and others. It was said that min is explanatory: any insignificant game, and the indefiniteness of shay is for belittling. His statement: Your hands and spears reach it. Ibn Waththab read yanaluh with a lower ya’. This sentence implies the generalization of hunting, and that there is no difference between what is taken by hand, which is what cannot escape, such as young animals and eggs, and what is taken by spears, which is what can escape. He specifically mentioned hands because they are what the hunter uses most to capture the game, and he specifically mentioned spears because they are the greatest hunting tools among the Arabs. His saying: That God may know who fears Him in secret, meaning that God may distinguish who among you fears Him because of His punishment in the Hereafter, for He is absent from you and not present. But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment, meaning after this clarification with which God tested you, because transgression after knowing the prohibition is defiance of God Almighty and an audacity towards Him.
5:95: His statement: 95- Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram He forbade them from killing game while in a state of ihram, and in its meaning Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram and this prohibition includes everyone from the males and females of the Muslims, because it is said that a man is in a state of ihram and a woman is in a state of ihram, and the plural is ihram, and a man entered the sanctuary: he entered the sanctuary. His statement: And whoever among you kills it intentionally The intentional: is the one who intends something while knowing that he is in a state of ihram, and the mistaken: is the one who intends something and hits game, and the forgetful: is the one who intentionally hunts and does not remember his ihram. Ibn Abbas and Ahmad in one narration, and Dawud from him, based on His limiting it to the intentional, that there is no expiation for anyone other than him, rather it is only obligatory for him alone. Saeed bin Jubair, Tawus and Abu Thawr said the same. It was said that expiation is obligatory for the one who makes a mistake or forgets, just as it is obligatory for the one who does it intentionally. They made the condition of intentionality an exception, excluding the most common. It was narrated from Omar, Al-Hasan, Al-Nakha’i, and Al-Zuhri. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, and their companions said the same. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was said that expiation is obligatory for the one who deliberately forgets his ihram. Mujahid said the same. He said: If he remembers his ihram, then he has become permissible and his Hajj is not valid because he committed a forbidden act during his ihram, so it is invalid for him, just as if he spoke during the prayer or broke his ablution during it. His statement: Then the penalty is like that which he killed from the livestock means that he must pay a penalty similar to that which he killed, and from the livestock is an explanation of the similar penalty. It was said that what is meant is similarity in value, and it was said in creation. Abu Hanifa went with the first, and Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and the majority went with the second. This is the truth because explaining to the one who is similar in livestock indicates that, and it also indicates an offering to the Kaaba. It was narrated from Abu Hanifa that it is permissible to give the value even if he finds the same, and that the one in ihram has a choice. It was read: Then the penalty is like what he killed. It was read: Then the penalty is like what he killed. It was read: The penalty is like what he killed. It was read: The penalty is like what he killed. Al-Hasan read: The blessings with a sukoon on the 'ayn for ease. They judge with it meaning with the penalty or with the like of what he killed. Two just men among you meaning two men known for their justice among the Muslims. If they judge with something, it is binding. If they disagree, it is referred to someone else. It is not permissible for the offender to be one of the two arbitrators. It was said that it is permissible. Abu Hanifa said the first, and Al-Shafi'i said the second in one of his two opinions: The apparent meaning of the verse requires two arbitrators other than the offender. His statement: A sacrifice that reaches the Ka'bah is the accusative of a sacrifice as a state or a substitute for like, and reaching the Ka'bah is an attribute of a sacrifice, because the addition is not real. The meaning is that if they judge with the penalty, then what is done with the sacrifice is done with it, such as sending it to Mecca and slaughtering there, and announcing and embroidering. He did not mean the Ka'bah itself, because the sacrifice does not reach it. Rather, he meant the Sacred Sanctuary, and there is no disagreement about this. His saying: or expiation is in apposition to the place of blessings: and it is in the nominative case because it is the predicate of a deleted subject, and food for the poor is an apposition to expiation or a substitute for it or the predicate of a deleted subject, or the equivalent of that is in apposition to food, and it was said that it is in apposition to reward, and there is weakness in it, as the offender has a choice between these mentioned types, and the equivalent of something is what is equivalent to it from a different kind, and fasting is in the accusative case as a distinction, and the scholars have decided the equivalent of every hunted animal from feeding and fasting, and the majority of scholars have said that the offender has a choice between the mentioned types. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that feeding and fasting are not sufficient for the pilgrim unless he does not find the sacrificial animal, and the equivalent with the opening of the ‘ayn and its breaking is two languages, and they are the inclination, as Al-Kisa’i said. Al-Farra’ said: The equivalent of something with the opening of the ‘ayn is its like from its kind, and with the opening of the ‘ayn is its like from a different kind, and the Basrans said the same as Al-Kisa’i. His saying: That he may taste the evil consequences of his deed is to impose the punishment upon him: meaning, We imposed that upon him so that he may taste the evil consequences of his deed. Taste is a metaphor for realizing hardship. The same is true of Taste, for you are the mighty, the generous. The evil consequences are: the bad end, the bad pasture is that which causes harm after eating it, and bad food is: if it is heavy. His saying: God has pardoned what is past means in your ignorance of killing game, and it was said that it was about what happened before the expiation was revealed. And whoever returns to what you were forbidden from killing game after this explanation, then God will take vengeance upon him is the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning, then God will take vengeance upon him. It was said that the meaning is: God will take vengeance upon him in the Hereafter, so He will punish him for his sin, and it was said that He will take vengeance upon him through the expiation. Shuraih and Saeed bin Jubayr said: He will be judged the first time, but if he returns, he will not be judged, rather it will be said to him: Go, and God will take vengeance upon you: meaning, your sin is greater than can be expiated.
5:96: His statement: 96- Lawful to you is sea game is addressed to every Muslim or to those in ihram in particular. Sea game is what is hunted in it, and what is meant by sea here is any water in which sea game is found, even if it is a river or a pond. His statement: And its food is provision for you and for the travelers Food is everything that is eaten, and this has been mentioned. There is a difference of opinion as to what is meant by it here. It was said: It is what the sea throws up and floats on, and this is what many of the Companions and Followers said. It was said: Its food is what is salted and remains, and this is what a group said, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was said: Its food is its salt that forms from its water and everything else in it of plants and other things, and this is what some people said. It was said: What is meant by it is what is eaten from the game: that is, what is permissible to eat, which is fish only, and this is what the Hanafis said. Meaning: He has made lawful for you to benefit from everything that is caught in the sea, and He has made lawful for you that which is eaten from it, which is fish. So the specification comes after the generalization, and this is a farce that has no basis. And the accusative of enjoyment is made as a source: that is, you enjoyed it as a benefit. And it was said that it is a direct object specific to food: that is, He has made lawful for you the food of the sea as a benefit. And this is a farce that was brought by the one who said the latter statement. Rather, if it was a direct object, it would be from all of them: that is, He has made lawful for you the catch of the sea and its food as a benefit for you: that is, for whoever among you is a resident who eats it fresh, and for the travelers, that is, the travelers among you who stock up on it and make it dried. And it was said that the travelers are those who ride it specifically. His statement: And game on land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram means that whatever is hunted on land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram. The apparent meaning is that it is forbidden to hunt it for the person in the state of ihram even if the hunter is lawful. This is the view of the majority if the lawful person hunted it for the person in the state of ihram, not if he did not hunt it for it. This is the most correct view, and it reconciles the hadiths. It was said that it is permissible for him absolutely, and this is the view of a group. It was also said that it is forbidden for him absolutely, and this is the view of others. We have explained this in detail in our explanation of al-Muntaqa. His statement: And fear God, to whom you will be gathered means fear God in that which He has forbidden you, to whom you will be gathered, not to anyone else. This is an emphasis and exaggeration in the warning. It was read And game on land is forbidden to you in the active form, and it was read as long as you are with a kasra on the dal.
5:97: His saying: 97- God made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a place of support for people. Here, made means created. The Kaaba was called a Kaaba because it is square, and cubing means squaring. Most Arab houses are round, not square. It was said that it was called a Kaaba because of its protrusion and prominence. Everything that protrudes is a heel, whether it is round or not. From this comes the heel of the foot, the heels of spears, and the heel of a woman's breast. The Sacred House is an explanatory apposition, and it was said that it is a second object and has no basis. It was called a house because it has roofs and walls, which are the reality of a house, even if there is no one in it. It was called a sanctuary because God Almighty forbade it. And his saying: A standing for the people is how the majority read it, and Ibn Amir read Qayman and it is accusative as the second object if it was made transitive with two objects, and if it means created as mentioned above then it is accusative as a state, and the meaning of it being a standing is that it is the center of their livelihood and religion: that is, they do in it what is good for their religion and their worldly life: their light ones are safe in it, their weak are aided in it, their merchants profit in it, and their worshippers worship in it. His saying: And the sacred month is in apposition to the Kaaba, which is Dhul-Hijjah, and it was singled out from among the sacred months because it is the time for performing Hajj, and it was said that it is a generic name. What is meant by it are the sacred months Dhul-Qi'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab, because they did not seek blood in them, nor did they fight the enemy in them, nor did they violate sanctity in them, so from this perspective it was a standing for the people and the offerings and the necklaces meaning and God made the offerings and the necklaces a standing for the people. What is meant by necklaces: the necklaces of the sacrificial animals, and there is no objection to the necklaces themselves being meant, and the reference by that is to the making: that is, that making so that you may know that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth meaning so that you may know that God knows the details of the matter of the heavens and the earth and knows your religious and worldly interests, for they are part of what is in them, so everything that He has legislated for you brings about your interests and repels what harms you and that God is Knowing of all things This is a generalization after specification.
5:98: 98- Know that God is severe in punishment and that God is Forgiving and Merciful. Then He commanded them to know that God is severe in punishment for those who violate His prohibitions and do not repent, and that He is Forgiving and Merciful for those who repent and return.
5:99: 99- The Messenger has no duty except to convey the message, and God knows what you reveal and what you conceal. Then he informed them that the Messenger has no duty except to convey the message to them, and if they do not comply and obey, then they have harmed only themselves and have committed no sin except against themselves. As for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, he did what was required of him and carried out what God commanded him to do. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever among you kills it intentionally, he said: If he kills it intentionally, forgetfully, or by mistake, he is to be judged. If he kills it again intentionally, he is to be punished quickly, unless God pardons him. Regarding his statement: Then the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock, he said: If a person in ihram kills a game animal, he is to be judged for it. If he kills a gazelle or something similar, he is to slaughter a sheep in Mecca. If he cannot find one, he is to feed six poor people. If he cannot find one, he is to fast for three days. If he kills a deer or something similar, he is to give a cow. If he cannot find one, he is to feed twenty poor people. If he cannot find one, he is to fast for twenty days. If he kills an ostrich or a wild donkey or something similar, he is to give a camel. If he cannot find one, he is to feed sixty poor people. If he cannot find one, he is to fast for thirty days. The food is a mudd that will satisfy them. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hakam that Umar wrote that he should be judged for both accidental and deliberate killings. They narrated something similar on the authority of Ata’. Something similar to this has been narrated from groups of the Salaf, without differentiating between the deliberate, the mistaken, and the forgetful. It has been narrated from others that this is specific to the deliberate. The Salaf have detailed sayings in their places regarding the estimation of the equivalent penalty and the estimation of its value. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said about an ostrich egg: Fasting for a day or feeding a poor person. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Dhakwan on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. He also narrated on the authority of Aishah on his authority, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Muhzam on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is a price for an ostrich egg. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, excluded the five harmful animals from the sacred animals, as mentioned in the hadiths, so it is permissible for the pilgrim to kill them and there is no sin on him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the verse: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you, whatever is thrown out dead is its food. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission ending with him, something similar. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq something similar. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said regarding the statement of God, Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food, that he said: Game from the sea is what you catch with your hands, and its food is what the sea swallows. In another version: Everything in it. In another version: Its food is its dead animal. This is supported by what is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of the ambergris that the sea cast up and the Companions ate from it and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, confirmed that, and the hadith is: Its water is pure and its dead animal is lawful. And the hadith: Lawful to you are two dead animals and two types of blood. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, God has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, that he said: A means of support for their religion and a landmark for their Hajj. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: Its means of support is that whoever heads towards it is safe. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab who said: God made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, and the Sacred Month a means of support for the people in the first days of ignorance, so that they would not fear one another when they met them at the House or in the Sacred Sanctuary or in the Sacred Month. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: God has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, and the Sacred Month, the sacrificial animals, and the garlands, he said: These are barriers that God left between the people in the days of ignorance. So if a man committed any crime and then sought refuge in the Sacred Sanctuary, he would not touch or approach it. If a man met his father’s killer in the Sacred Month, he would not confront him or approach him. If a man met the sacrificial animals wearing garlands while they were eating their sinews from hunger, he would not confront them or approach them. When a man wanted to enter the House, he would wear a necklace of hair to protect him and prevent him from the people. If he fled, he would wear a necklace of idhkhir or samr to prevent him from the people until he reached his family. These are barriers that God left between the people in the days of ignorance. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, Standing for the people. He said: We are safe.
5:100: It was said that what is meant by the wicked and the good is: the forbidden and the permissible, and it was said the believer and the unbeliever, and it was said the sinner and the obedient, and it was said the bad and the good. It is better to consider the generality of the wording so that it includes these mentioned and others that are described as wicked and good from people, actions and words, so the wicked is not equal to the good in any case. His saying: 100- "Even if the abundance of the wicked pleases you" It was said that the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said to every addressee who is suitable to be addressed in this way. The meaning is to deny equality in all cases, even if the evil is pleasing to the viewer because of its abundance, for this abundance with the evil is like nothingness, because the evil of something nullifies its benefit, destroys its blessing, and takes away its benefit. The waw is either for the state or for conjunction with something understood: that is, the evil and the good are not equal if the abundance of the evil does not please you, and if the abundance of the evil pleases you, like your saying, Be good to so-and-so even if he does evil to you, meaning be good to him even if he does not do evil to you even if he does evil to you. The answer to if is omitted: that is, even if the abundance of the evil pleases you, they are not equal.
5:101: His statement: 101- "O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, will distress you." That is, do not ask about things that you have no need to ask about, nor do they concern you in your religious affairs. His statement, "If they are made known to you, they will distress you" is in the accusative case, describing things: that is, do not ask about things that have this characteristic of being, if they are made known to you, that is, if they appear and you are charged with them, they will distress you. God forbade them from asking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, too much, because asking about something that does not concern you or that there is no need for it may be a reason for obligating it on the questioner or on others. His statement, "And if you ask about it when the Qur'an is being revealed, it will be made clear to you." This sentence is part of the description of things. Meaning: Do not ask about things that you cannot ask about when the Qur’an is revealed, and that is while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is among you and the revelation is being sent down to him. It will be made clear to you means it will be made clear to you by what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, answers you with, or what the revelation is sent down to him with, and that will be a reason for difficult duties and the obligation of what was not obligatory and the prohibition of what was not prohibited, unlike asking about it after the revelation has ceased with the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for there is no obligation or prohibition resulting from asking. Some of the commentators thought that the second conditional clause permitted asking questions in the presence of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the revelation was sent down to him. He said: The first conditional clause indicated that asking is not permissible, and the second clause indicated that it is permissible. He said that the meaning is: And if you ask about other things that are needed, it will be revealed to you by the answer of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He made the pronoun in about it refer to things other than the things mentioned, and made that like His statement: And We created man from an extract of clay, which is Adam. Then He said: Then We made him a sperm-drop, meaning the son of Adam. His statement: God has pardoned it, meaning what you asked before, so do not return to that. It was said that the meaning is: Those things that you asked about are among those that He pardoned and did not make obligatory upon you, so how do you cause the question to be obligatory for what is pardoned by God but not obligatory? The pronoun about it refers to the first issue, and to things in the second, so that the phrase God has pardoned it is a third description of things, and the first is more appropriate, because the second requires that what is being asked about has been legislated by God and then He pardoned it. It can be said that pardon means abandonment: that is, God left it and did not mention it in any way, so do not search for it. This is a correct meaning that does not entail that false consequence. Then the Almighty came with the formula of exaggeration in His being Forgiving and Forbearing to indicate thereby that He does not hasten to punish those who disobey Him due to the abundance of His forgiveness and the breadth of His forbearance.
5:102: His statement: 102- "A people before you asked about it, then they became disbelievers in it. The pronoun refers to the issue understood from do not ask," but it is not this issue itself, rather it is similar to it in that it is something that is not needed and is not required by religious necessity, then they did not act upon it, rather they became disbelievers in it: that is, they covered it up and abandoned acting upon it, and that is like the people of Salih asking about the she-camel, and the companions of Jesus asking about the table. It is necessary to restrict the prohibition in this verse to what is not called for by need, as we have mentioned, because the matter that is called for by need in matters of religion and this world, God has permitted asking about it, so He said: "So ask the people of the message if you do not know." And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "May God fight them, for they did not ask, for the cure for ignorance is asking."
6:143: His statement: 103- What God has made of a bahīrah This is an introductory statement that includes a response to the people of ignorance in what they innovated, and made here means named as He said Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an. And bahīrah is a fa'īlah with the meaning of maf'ūlah like an-naṭihah and an-ḍabīhah, and it is taken from the bahīrah, which is the splitting of the ear. Ibn Sidah said: The bahīrah is the one that is left without a shepherd, it was said that it is the one whose milk is given to the tyrants so that no one among the people milks it, and the splitting of its ear was made a sign for that. Al-Shafi’i said: If a female camel gave birth to five female offspring, its ear would be pierced and it would be forbidden. It was also said that if a female camel gave birth to five offspring, if the fifth was a male, its ear would be pierced and men and women would eat it. If the fifth was a female, its ear would be pierced and its meat and milk would be forbidden to women. It was also said that if a female camel gave birth to five offspring without specifying females, its ear would be pierced and riding it and its milk would be forbidden. As-Sa’ibah is a female camel that is let loose, or a camel that is let loose is a vow made by a man that if God saves him from sickness or reaches his home, he will not be prevented from grazing or watering, and no one will ride him. This was said by Abu Ubaid. The poet said: And may God bless you, may you grow and prosper. May God grant you good health and happiness. It was said that it is the one that is left to God, with no restrictions on it and no shepherd for it. From this is the saying of the poet: You hamstrung a camel that was a slave to my Lord, so stand up for the punishment. It was said that it is the one that followed ten females, and there was no male among them. In that case, its back was not ridden. Its hair was not cut, and its milk was not drunk except by a guest. It was said that they used to let the slave go wherever he wanted, and no one had a hand on him. Al-Wasilah: It was said that it is the female camel that gave birth to a female after a female. It was also said that it is the ewe, if it gave birth to a female, it was for them. If it gave birth to a male, it was for their gods. If it gave birth to a male and a female, they said that it joined its brother, so they did not slaughter the male for their gods. It was also said that if a ewe gave birth to seven wombs, they would look. If the seventh was a male, it was slaughtered and the men and women ate from it.
