It was said: the intestines and what is mixed with a bone are in apposition to the fat. The meaning is: We forbade them their fat or the intestines or what is mixed with a bone except what their backs carry, for it is not forbidden. There is no reason for this effort or justification for it, because the meaning would be that God forbade them one of these mentioned things. What is meant by what is mixed with a bone is what sticks to the bones of fat in all parts of the animal, including the buttocks, for it sticks to the tailbone. The reference in His statement, that is to the prohibition indicated by We forbade, i.e. that prohibition We punished them with because of their transgression. It was said: The reference to the punishment indicated by His saying: We have rewarded them means that punishment We have rewarded them, which is the prohibition of what God has forbidden them. And We are truthful in everything that we inform about, and among that is this report, which is found in their Torah, and its text: Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, every animal that does not have a split hoof, and every fish that does not have a white spot in it. End.
6:147: And the pronoun in 147- They denied you refers to the Jews: meaning, if the Jews denied you in what you described about God forbidding them those things, say, your Lord is full of vast mercy. And from His mercy is His forbearance towards you and His not hastening you with punishment in this world. And even if He gives you respite and has mercy on you, His punishment will not be averted from the criminal people if He sent it down upon them and they deserved to be punished quickly. And it was said that what is meant is: His punishment in the Hereafter will not be averted from the criminal people. And the first is more appropriate, for He, the Almighty, has hastened them with punishments, including forbidding them good things in this world. And it was said: The pronoun refers to the polytheists who divided the livestock into those categories and made some of them permissible and some of them forbidden. And it was said that what is meant is: He is full of mercy for the obedient, and His punishment will not be averted from the criminal people and there is no refuge for this. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Everything with hoofs he said: It is that which does not have cleft fingers, meaning it does not have split fingers. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on his authority: Everything with hoofs he said: The camel and the ostrich. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid he said: It is everything whose legs do not spread among the animals, and whatever spreads is eaten by the Jews, he said: The legs of chickens and sparrows spread, so the Jews eat it, but the hoof of the camel or the ostrich does not spread, nor the leg of the hyena, so the Jews do not eat camels, ostriches, or hyenas, nor anything whose leg does not spread like that, nor do they eat the wild donkey. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And of the cows and the sheep We have forbidden them their fat, except that which adheres to their backs meaning the fat that is attached to the back or the entrails are the dung beetles. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Salih regarding his statement: Except what their backs carry, he said: the buttocks. Or the groin, he said: the hump. Or what is mixed with a bone, he said: the fat. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Or the groin, he said: the camels’ backs. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, Or the groin, he said: the rib cages and the camels’ backs. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Or what is mixed with a bone, he said: the buttocks. The fat of the buttocks is mixed with the coccyx, so it is permissible. All the fat of the legs, the side, the head, the eye and the ear, they say that it has been mixed with a bone, so it is permissible for them. What was forbidden to them was the omentum, the kidney fat and everything that was like that but not in a bone. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: But if they deny you, he said: the Jews. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: The Jews used to say: What Israel forbade, we forbid. This is what He said: If they deny you verse.
6:148: God informed about the polytheists that they will say this statement, and they are the infidels of Quraysh or all the polytheists, they mean that if God had willed that they would not have committed polytheism, they and their fathers would not have committed polytheism nor forbidden any of the livestock such as the bahīrah and the like, and they thought that this statement would free them from the argument that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, obligated them with and that what they did was right, and if it was not right, God would have sent to their fathers who died as polytheists, and as forbidding what God did not forbid, messengers who would command them to abandon polytheism and to abandon forbidding what God did not forbid, and to permit what He did not permit. 148- Thus did those before them deny meaning just as these denied, the polytheists before them denied the prophets of God until they tasted Our punishment meaning they continued to deny until they tasted Our punishment that We sent down upon them, then God commanded him to say to them: Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? meaning do you have a correct proof after the knowledge? The beneficial one, so bring it out to us so that we may look into it and ponder it. The purpose of this is to rebuke them, because he knew that they did not have any knowledge that would be suitable for argument and that would establish proof. Then he explained to them that they had no knowledge at all, and that they only followed conjectures: that is, they only followed conjecture, which is the source of error and the place of ignorance. And you are only guessing, that is, you are merely guessing, just as a guesser guesses, and this has been proven previously.
6:149: Then God the Almighty commanded him to inform them that God has the conclusive proof against the al-Nas 114:that is, the proof that cuts off their excuses and invalidates their doubts, suspicions and delusions. What is meant by this are the revealed books, the sent messengers, and the miracles they brought. 149- If He had willed to guide you all, He would have guided you all, but He did not will that. Similar to this is the Almighty’s statement: If God had willed, they would not have associated others with Him, and they would not have believed unless God willed. And there are many similar examples.
6:150: Then God commanded him to say to these polytheists: Bring your witnesses meaning bring them and bring them, and it is a verb that is the same for the masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural among the people of Hijaz, and the people of Najd say: Halma Halmi Halmu, and they pronounce it as they pronounce all other verbs, and the Qur'an was revealed in the language of the people of Hijaz, and from it the Almighty said: And those who say to their brothers, 'Come to us' and the origin according to Al-Khalil is Ha with Lam added to it, and another said: Its origin is Hal with Meem added to them, and in the book Al-Ain by Al-Khalil: Its origin is Hal A'um: meaning do I intend you, then they used it a lot, and this is also a way of rebuking them where he commands them to bring witnesses that God has forbidden those things even though he knows that they have no witnesses, and if they testify for them without knowledge but rather out of recklessness and fanaticism, then do not testify with them meaning do not believe them and do not accept them because they are ignorant liars. Their testimony is invalid. And do not follow the inclinations of those who deny Our signs. That is, do not follow their inclinations, for they are the chief deniers of Our signs. His statement, And those who do not believe in the Hereafter is conjoined to the relative pronoun, that is, do not follow the inclinations of those who deny Our signs, and the inclinations of those who do not believe in the Hereafter. And they equate others with their Lord. That is, they make others equal to Him from among His creations, such as idols. The sentence is either in the accusative case as a state, or conjoined to they do not believe. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Those who associate others with God will say, he said: This is the statement of Quraysh that God has forbidden this: meaning, the bahīrah, the sā’ibah, the wasīlah, and the Ḥām. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, “Say: God has the conclusive argument,” he said: The authority. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was said to him: Some people say that evil is not by fate, so Ibn Abbas said: Between us and the people of fate is this verse: Those who associate others with God will say, to His statement: “Then God has the conclusive argument. If He had willed, He could have guided you all.” Ibn Abbas said: Inability and intelligence are from fate. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd who said: The argument of the Qadārīyyah ended at this verse: “Say: God has the conclusive argument. If He had willed, He could have guided you all.” Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: “Say: Bring your witnesses,” he said: Show me your witnesses.
6:151: His saying: 151- "Say: Come" meaning advance. Ibn Al-Shajari said: The one commanded to advance in the original position of this verb is as if he was sitting, so it was said to him: come: meaning raise yourself by standing and advance, and they expanded in it until they made it for the one standing and the one walking. And thus Al-Zamakhshari said in Al-Kashshaf: It is from the specific that became general, and its origin is that someone who is in a high place says it to someone who is below him, then it became more common and expanded in it until it became general. His saying: Recite what your Lord has forbidden atal is the answer to the command, and ma is a relative in the place of the accusative with it: meaning recite what your Lord has forbidden you. What is meant by reciting what God has forbidden is reciting the verses that include it, and ma may be a source: meaning recite the prohibition of your Lord. Meaning: What includes prohibition. It was said: It is permissible for ma to be interrogative, meaning: recite what your Lord has prohibited, making recitation mean saying, which is very weak. And upon you is to attach atal, so the meaning is: I recite to you what your Lord has prohibited. And if it is attached to forbidden, then the meaning is I recite what your Lord has prohibited to you, and this is more appropriate, because the situation is one of explaining what is prohibited to you, not one of explaining what is prohibited absolutely. And it was said: In upon you is for enticement and has no connection to what preceded it. And the meaning is upon you that you do not associate anything to the end: that is, adhere to that, like the Almighty’s saying: Upon you yourselves, which is weaker than what preceded it. And in that you do not associate is an explanation of the act of recitation. An-Nahhas said: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case instead of ma: that is, I recite to you the prohibition of associating. And it was said: It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case with an estimation of the subject: that is, the recited one that you do not associate, and something is an object or a source, that is, do not associate anything with Him, or any of the associating. His saying: And to parents, do good means, be kind to them, and being kind to them means being dutiful to them, and obeying their commands and prohibitions. We have already discussed this. His saying: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty When he mentioned the right of parents over their children, he mentioned the right of children over their parents, which is that they should not kill them for poverty. Poverty is poverty, as the pre-Islamic era used to do this to males and females for fear of poverty, and they did it to females in particular for fear of shame. Al-Naqqash narrated from Mu'raj that poverty is hunger in the language of Khumm, and Mundhir bin Sa'id Al-Baluti mentioned that poverty is spending. It is said: he made his money poor, meaning he spent it. The first meaning is what the scholars of language and the scholars of interpretation agreed upon here. And do not come near to immoralities meaning sins, and from it And do not come near to adultery, for it is an immorality and what is in what is apparent is a substitute for immoralities, and so is what is hidden. What is meant by what is apparent is what is made public of it, and what is hidden is what is kept secret. It has been mentioned before, And do not kill the soul the lam in the soul is for the genus, and which God has forbidden is an attribute of the soul: that is, do not kill any of the souls that God has forbidden except by right that is, except by what the right requires, and the exception is empty: that is, do not kill it in any case except by right, or do not kill it for any reason except by right, and among the right is killing it in retaliation and killing it because of the adultery of the married, and killing it because of apostasy, and similar reasons for which the law came, and the reference in his saying: that is to what came before of what he recited to them, and it is the subject and He enjoined upon you is its predicate: that is, He commanded you to do it, and He made it obligatory upon you.
6:152: 152- And do not approach the property of an orphan meaning do not interfere with it in any way except by the characteristic that is best than others, which is what is in its improvement, preservation and growth, so it includes every aspect in which there is benefit for the orphan and an increase in his money, and it was said: What is meant by that which is best is trade until he reaches maturity meaning until the orphan reaches maturity, then if he reaches that point then give him his money, as God Almighty said: But if you perceive in them sound judgment, then give them their property. Scholars differed about the most severe age. The people of Medina said: It is reaching maturity and becoming mature. Abu Hanifa said: Twenty-five years. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is puberty. It was said: It is the end of middle age, and from this is the saying of Suhaim al-Rabahi: The brother of fifty is a more intense society, and in my talk, the affairs are rotated The first way to achieve reaching the age of maturity is to reach the age of accountability with the awareness of maturity, which is to behave in the way of rational people in dealing with his money, not the way of foolish and extravagant people. This is indicated by the words of God the Almighty in Surat An-Nisaa’: “And test the orphans until they reach the age of marriage. Then if you perceive in them sound judgment, release their property to them.” So He made reaching the age of marriage, which is reaching the age of accountability, restricted to the awareness of maturity. Perhaps we have previously discussed this. Ash-Ash... His statement: And give full measure and weight in justice meaning with justice in taking and giving when buying and selling. We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity meaning beyond its capacity in every duty, including the duty to give full measure and weight, so the one in charge of them is not addressed with what cannot be avoided in terms of increase or decrease. And when you speak, be just meaning if you say something in a report or testimony or criticism or praise, be just in it and seek the truth, and do not be biased in that towards a relative or a distant one, and do not favor a friend or an enemy, rather treat people equally, for that is from the justice that God has commanded. The pronoun in even if refers back to what it indicates. And when you speak because the statement must have someone said about it, or someone said to: meaning even if the one said about it, or someone said to is a relative meaning someone related to you. It was said that the meaning is: even if the right was against your relatives, and the former is more appropriate. And similar to this verse is His statement: even if it was against yourselves or your parents and your closest relatives. His saying: And fulfill the covenant of God means fulfill every covenant that God has enjoined upon you, and among what He has enjoined upon you is what His Messenger recited to you by His command in this context. It is permissible that it refers to every covenant, even if it is between created beings, because when God Almighty commanded fulfillment of it in many Qur’anic verses, that was a justification for adding it to Him, and the reference in His saying: That to what was mentioned previously, He has enjoined upon you He commanded you with it as an emphatic command, that you may remember so that you may be admonished by that.
6:153: His saying: 153- And that this is My straight path "that" is in the accusative case: meaning, recite that this is My path, as Al-Farra' and Al-Kisa'i said. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case: meaning, He commanded you to do it, and that this. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: The meaning is because this is My straight path, as in the saying of the Most High: "And that the mosques belong to God." Al-A'mash, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read: "And that this" with a kasra on the hamza as a new sentence, and the meaning is: what is mentioned in these verses is My path. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ya'qub read "And that this is My path" with a light vowel, estimating the pronoun of the matter. Al-A'mash read: "This is my path." In the Mushaf of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "This is the path of your Lord." In the Mushaf of Ubayy: "This is the path of your Lord." The path is the road, which is the path of the religion of Islam. The accusative of "straight is in the state of state," and straight is the level that has no crookedness in it. Then he ordered them to follow it and forbade them from following all other paths: the religions with different paths. "For they will separate you, that is, they will lead you away from His path," that is, from the straight path of God, which is the religion of Islam. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: These paths include Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and all other religions and people of innovations and misguidance from the people of whims and deviation in branches and other than that from the people of deep debate and delving into speech. All of these are subject to error and are likely to lead to bad belief. The reference with "that" is to what came before, and it is the subject and predicate. "He enjoined it upon you, that is, He emphasized the enjoinment upon you, so that you may guard against" what He forbade you from. Al-Tirmidhi narrated with a hasan chain of transmission, as did Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you will pledge allegiance to me on these three verses? Then he recited, Say, ‘Come,’ to three verses, then he said: “Whoever fulfills them, his reward is with God. Whoever falls short of them and God catches up with him in this world, his punishment will be his. Whoever delays him until the Hereafter, his affair is with God. If He wills, He will take him, and if He wills, He will pardon him.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Durais and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar who said: The first ten verses to be revealed in the Torah were these ten verses, and they are the ten that were revealed at the end of al-An’am 6:Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you,’ to the end of it. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abdullah bin Adi bin Al-Khayyar who said: Kaab heard a man reciting: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him.” Kaab said: By the One in Whose Hand is Kaab’s soul, this is the first verse in the Torah: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you.” to the end of the verses. I said: These are the Ten Commandments in the Torah, the first of which is: I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. You shall have no other god but Me. Among them are: Honor your father and your mother, that your life may be long in the land which the Lord your God is giving you. Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not bear false witness against your neighbor. Do not covet your neighbor’s house. Do not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male slave, nor his female slave, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to your neighbor. Perhaps this is what Kaab Al-Ahbar meant, and the Jews paid great attention to these commandments. The People of the Psalms wrote them at the end of their Psalms, and the People of the Gospel wrote them at the beginning of their Gospel. It is written on two tablets, and we have left out what relates to the Sabbath. Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated from Qatada, And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, he said: for fear of poverty. He said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to kill one of them his daughter for fear of poverty and captivity. And do not approach immoralities - whether apparent or concealed, he said: their secret and public. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, he said: for fear of poverty. And do not approach immoralities - whether apparent or concealed, he said: In the Jahiliyyah, they did not see any harm in fornication in secret and considered it ugly in public, so God forbade fornication in secret and in public. Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated from Qatada regarding His statement, And that this is My straight path, he said: Know that the path is one path, the group of guidance and its destination is Paradise, and that Satan legislated separate paths, the group of misguidance and its destination is Hell. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bazzar, al-Nasa’i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) drew a line with his hand and then said: This is the straight path of God. Then he drew lines to the right and to the left of that line and then said: And these paths, there is no path among them but that there is a devil upon it calling to it. Then he recited: And that this is My straight path, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path. Ahmad, Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith from Jabir. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that a man asked him: What is the straight path? He said: We left Muhammad (blessings and peace of God be upon him) at its lowest and at its edge is Paradise, and to his right is a mountain and to his left is a mountain, and there are men calling whoever passes by them. Whoever takes that mountain will end up in the Fire, and whoever takes the straight path will end up in Paradise. Then Ibn Mas’ud recited: And that this is My straight path, so follow it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And do not follow the paths of error. He said: The paths of error.
6:154: This statement is presented to establish the recommendation that God has recommended to His servants, and the connection with then has been questioned, given that the story of Moses and the giving of the Book to him comes before the thing to which it is connected, which is what was mentioned previously in His statement: That is what He has enjoined upon you. It has been said that then here has the meaning of and, and it has been said that the meaning of the statement is: Then We had given Moses the Book before We sent down the Qur’an to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It has been said that the meaning is: Say, Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you, then I will recite the giving of the Book to Moses. It has been said that the recommendation to which it is connected is ancient, and every prophet has always recommended it to his nation. It has been said that then is for the delay in reporting, as you say: I was informed of what you did today, then what you did yesterday is more amazing. His saying: 154 - Completely is an object for which or a source, and upon the one who does good was read in the nominative case, and this is the reading of Yahya bin Ya’mar and Ibn Abi Ishaq, so the nominative case of better is based on the assumption of a subject: meaning, on the one who is better. From this is what Sibawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Khalil that he heard: I am not the one who says anything to you. The rest read it in the accusative case as a past tense verb according to the Basrans. Al-Farra and Al-Kisa’i permitted it to be a noun describing who, and this is impossible according to the Basrans because it is a description of the noun before it is complete. The meaning according to them is completely upon whoever does good by accepting it and doing it, whoever he may be. This is supported by the fact that Ibn Mas’ud read: completely upon those who do good. Al-Hasan said: There were among them those who did good and those who did not do good, so God sent down the Book completely upon the doers of good. It was said that the meaning is: We gave Moses the Torah in addition to what Moses did well from what God taught him before the Torah was sent down to him. It was said that the meaning is: completely upon what God the Almighty did well to Moses with from the message and other things. It was said: completely upon Moses’ goodness in obeying God the Almighty, as Al-Farra said. His statement: And in detail for everything is conjoined with completely: meaning and for the sake of detailing everything. Likewise guidance and mercy are conjoined with it: meaning and for guidance and mercy. The pronoun in perhaps they refers to the Children of Israel indicated by the mention of Moses, and the ba in in meeting is related to they believe.
6:155: His statement: 155- And this is a Book which We have revealed, blessed. The reference is to the Qur’an, and the demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is Book, and We have revealed it is an attribute of Book, and blessed is another attribute of it, and the attribute of revelation is presented because the denial is related to it, and blessed is very blessed because of what it contains of worldly and religious benefits. So follow it, for since it is from God and contains blessing, following it is obligatory upon you. And fear opposing it and denying what is in it. Perhaps if you accept it and do not oppose it, you will receive mercy through the mercy of God, the Most High.
6:156: And in 156 - that you say is in the accusative case. The Kufians said: lest you say. The Basrans said: out of dislike for you to say. Al-Farra' and Al-Kisa'i said: The meaning is, beware of saying, O people of Mecca, The Book was only sent down - meaning the Torah and the Gospel - to two groups before us, namely the Jews and Christians, and no book was sent down to us, even though we were heedless of their study - meaning, of reciting their books in their languages - unaware - meaning, we do not know what is in them. What they mean is to prove the revelation of the two books while apologizing for following what is in them due to their lack of knowledge and heedlessness of their meaning.
6:157: His statement: 157- "Or you say, 'If only the Book had been sent down to us' is connected to you say meaning or that you say, If only the Book had been sent down to us as it was sent down to the two groups before us, we would have been better guided than they" to the truth that God asked for, for this statement and excuse from them is prompted by the sending of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them and the revelation of the Qur'an to him, and for this reason He said: "There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord" meaning a book that God sent down to your Prophet, and he is from you, O group of Arabs, so do not make excuses with false excuses and justify yourselves with false reasons, for the morning has dawned for him who has eyes "and guidance and mercy is connected to clear proof" meaning there has come to you the clear proof and guidance by which everyone who has a desire to be guided is guided, and mercy from God that includes everyone who seeks it and wants to obtain it, but you have wronged yourselves by denying the signs of God and turning away from them: meaning turning away From it, and turning away from those who wanted to turn to it, So who is more unjust than he who denies the signs of God which are mercy and guidance for the people, and turns away from them is better by turning away from them, and is more misguided by turning others away from turning to them, We will recompense those who turn away from Our signs with an evil punishment meaning the bad punishment because of what they used to turn away. It was said that the meaning of turn away is: turn away, and turn away means turn away, and it is close to the meaning of turning away, and the meaning of this word has been explained previously, and the question in who is more unjust is for denial: meaning denial that anyone is more unjust than he who denies the signs of God and turns away from them, along with what that indicates of rebuking them. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Completely upon the one who did good, meaning: upon the believing doers of good. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Sakhr, Completely upon the one who did good, meaning: Completely because God had done good. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, who said: Completely for His favor upon them and His kindness to them. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And this is a Book, he said: It is the Qur’an that God revealed to Muhammad. So follow it and fear God, meaning: Follow what God has permitted in it and fear what He has forbidden. These narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Upon two groups before us, he said: The Jews and the Christians, fearing that the Quraysh might say it. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They are the Jews and the Christians. And if we were to study them, he said: Their recitation. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: But we were better guided than they, he said: This is the saying of the Arab infidels. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, he said: There has come to you a clear proof in clear Arabic when they did not know how to study the two groups. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He turned away from it, he said: He turned away from it. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: They turn away, he said: They turn away.
6:158: That is, when We established the proof against them and sent down the Book to Our Messenger sent to them, it did not benefit them and they did not turn back from their misguidance with it. So after this, nothing remains except that they 158- wait that is, wait for the angels to come to them that is, the angels of death to take their souls, and at that time, faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before or your Lord comes O Muhammad, as they suggested in their saying: Why were the angels not sent down to us or did we not see our Lord? It was said that its meaning is: or the command of your Lord to destroy them comes, and it was said that the meaning is: or all the signs of your Lord come, as evidenced by His saying: or some of the signs of your Lord come. It was said that it is from the ambiguous ones whose interpretation is known only to God. The deletion of the complement has occurred in the Qur’an a lot, such as His saying: And ask the town and His saying: And they have drunk into their hearts the calf meaning the love of the calf. It was said that God’s coming is His coming on the Day of Resurrection to separate the judgment between His creation, such as His saying: And there will come Your Lord and the angels, rank upon rank. His saying: The Day some of the signs of your Lord come. Ibn Omar and Ibn al-Zubayr read the Day it comes with a fat-ha, and the rest read it with a dhamma. Al-Mubarrad said: The feminization is due to proximity to a feminine, not according to the original. From this is the saying of Jarir: When the report of Al-Zubayr came, the city walls and the mountains were humbled. Ibn Sirin read: It does not benefit from superiority. Abu Hatim said: This is a mistake on the part of Ibn Sirin. People have said something subtle about this grammar, which was mentioned by Naftawayh, and that is that faith and the soul each include the other, so faith is made feminine since it is from the soul. An-Nahhas said: There is another aspect to this, which is to make faith feminine, because it is a source, just as a feminine source is made feminine, such as So whoever receives an admonition from his Lord. The meaning of The Day some of the signs of your Lord come is the Day the signs that they proposed come, which compel them to believe, Faith will not benefit a soul from it or something more general than that, which includes what they are waiting for. It was said: They are the signs that are the signs of the Day of Resurrection mentioned in the authentic hadiths from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they are the ones that, when they come, faith will not benefit a soul. His saying: She had not believed before means before some of the signs came. As for the one who had believed before some of the signs came, her faith benefits her. The phrase she had not believed before is in the accusative case as a description of the soul. His saying: or earned good through her faith is connected to believed. The meaning is: that it does not benefit a soul to have faith when the signs come, if it is described as having not believed before, or believed before but did not earn good through its faith. So it came from this that nothing benefits except combining faith before the coming of some of the signs with earning good through faith. So whoever believed before only and did not earn good through his faith or earned good but did not believe, then that does not benefit him. This combination is like your saying: I do not give to a man who came to me today who did not come to me yesterday or did not praise me for coming to me yesterday. What is understood from this is that no one deserves to be given except a man who came to him yesterday and praised him for coming to him yesterday. Then God Almighty commanded him to say to them: Wait for what you want to come, for we are waiting for it. This is a severe threat and a great warning, and it strengthens what was said in the interpretation of the day some of the signs of your Lord come that they are the signs that they suggested of the angels coming and the punishment coming to them. By God, as previously stated. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them? He said: at death, or that your Lord should come? He said: on the Day of Resurrection. `Abd Al-Razzaq, `Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah in their interpretation of the verse something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil, or that your Lord should come? He said: on the Day of Resurrection in the shade of clouds. Ahmad, `Abd bin Humayd in his Musnad, Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, The Day some of the signs of your Lord will come, he said: the rising of the sun from the West. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange. Ibn Abi Shaybah and `Abd bin Humayd narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa`id, with no chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Al-Tabarani, Ibn `Adi, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with no chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Sa`id bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, `Abd bin Humayd, Nu`aym bin Hammad, and Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, with no chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. If it is proven that this prophetic interpretation was raised from a sound source that has no flaws, then it is obligatory to give precedence to it and it is imperative to accept it. It is supported by what is proven in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. When it rises and the people see it, they will all believe, and that is when faith will not benefit a soul.” Then he recited the verse. Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and others narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Abu Dharr. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi, regarding his statement: or earned good through her faith, he said: earned good deeds through her belief. These are the people of the Qiblah. If she believed and did not do good before that, then she did good after seeing the verse, it will not be accepted from her. But if she did good before the verse, then did good after the verse, it will be accepted from her. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Muqatil regarding his statement: or earned good through her faith, he said: It means the Muslim who did not do good through his faith and was persisting in major sins before the verse. The verses that are signs of the Day of Resurrection have been mentioned in many hadiths explaining and enumerating them, and they are mentioned in the books of Sunnah.
6:159: Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read 159- They divided their religion which is the reading of Ali bin Abi Talib: meaning they abandoned their religion and deviated from it. The rest read They divided with emphasis except Al-Nakha'i who read it with emphasis. The meaning is that they made their religion divided, so they took some of it and left some of it. It was said that what is meant by them are the Jews and Christians. The meaning of this has been mentioned in the Jews, in the words of God Almighty: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided until after there came to them clear evidence. It was said that what is meant by them are the polytheists, some of whom worshipped idols and some of whom worshipped angels. It was also said that the verse is general for all the disbelievers and everyone who innovated and came with what God did not command. This is correct because the wording indicates generality, so it includes the groups of the People of the Book, the groups of polytheists, and others who innovated from the people of Islam. The meaning of sects is groups and parties. So it applies to every people whose affair in religion was one and united, then each group of them followed the opinion of one of their leaders who contradicted the correct view and contradicted the truth. You are not from them in anything, meaning you are not from their division, or from asking about the reason for their division and searching for the reason for their partisanship in any of the things. You are not required to do anything about that and you are not addressed by it. Rather, you are required to convey it. It is like the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever deceives us is not from us, meaning we are innocent of him. The position of in anything is accusative as a state. Al-Farra’ said: It is on the deletion of an added word: meaning, you are not responsible for their punishment in any way, but you are only responsible for warning. Then God Almighty consoled him by saying: Their affair is only with God, so He is punishing them with what His will requires, and the restriction, only, is in the ruling of explaining what came before it and emphasizing it. Then is on the Day of Resurrection He will inform them, meaning He will inform them of what He will bring down upon them of punishment for what they used to do, i.e. of the deeds that contradict what God has legislated for them and made obligatory upon them. This verse is among the things that were abrogated by the verse of the sword.
6:160: His statement: 160- Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof. When the Almighty threatened those who disobeyed Him with what He threatened, He explained after that the amount of reward for those who acted according to what He commanded them to do and complied with what He legislated for them, that whoever brings a single good deed will have ten good deeds as a reward. The meaning is: He will have ten good deeds like it, so the description was used in place of the described. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: The feminization of ten like it is good because the likes were added to a feminine, such as some of his fingers were gone. Al-Hasan, Saeed bin Jubayr, and al-A'mash read he will have ten like it with them in the nominative case. This doubling has been proven in the Sunnah in many hadiths, and this doubling is the least that the doer of a good deed deserves. More than this has been mentioned in general and in particular, such as in the Qur’an, Like a seed which grows seven ears. It has been mentioned in some good deeds that the doer of them will be rewarded for them without account, and it has been mentioned in the pure Sunnah that the reward is multiplied to thousands upon thousands. We have already presented the investigation of this in two places in this interpretation, so let them be referred to. And whoever brings evil from evil deeds will not be recompensed except with the like thereof without any increase in its lightness or greatness. So the polytheist will be recompensed for the evil of polytheism by remaining in the Fire forever, and the doer of sin among the Muslims will be recompensed for it with the like thereof from what has been estimated of punishments, as has been reported in many hadiths that state that whoever does such and such will be subject to such and such. And as for what has not been estimated for his punishment from sins, we must say: God will recompense him with the like thereof, even if we do not know the truth of what he will be recompensed with. This is if he does not repent. However, if he repents or his good deeds outweigh his bad deeds or God covers him with His mercy and bestows His forgiveness upon him, then there is no recompense. The evidence of the Book and the Sunnah is explicit about this in an explicit manner after which no doubt remains for the doubter. And they meaning whoever brings good and whoever brings evil will not be wronged by reducing the reward of the good deeds of the righteous nor by increasing the punishments of the wrongdoers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Jews and Christians differed before Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent, so they split up. When Muhammad was sent, the verse, Indeed, those who have divided their religion was revealed to him. An-Nahhas narrated on his authority in his abrogator, Indeed, those who have divided their religion he said: The Jews and Christians abandoned Islam and the religion they were commanded to follow. And became sects different groups and parties. You are not of them in anything was revealed in Mecca, then it was abrogated by Fight the polytheists -. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority, And became sects he said: Different religions. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah regarding his statement, Indeed, those who have divided their religion the verse, he said: They are in this nation. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani, Al-Shirazi in Al-Alqab, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the verse, he said: They are the people of innovations and desires from this nation. In its chain of transmission is Abd Ibn Kathir, and his hadith is rejected, and no one else attributed it to the Prophet. Those other than him attributed it to Abu Hurayrah. Abd Ibn Hamid, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah regarding the verse, he said: They are the Kharijites. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Nahhas, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, but its chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet is not authentic. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Shaheen, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilya, Abu Nasr Al-Sajzi in Al-Ibanah, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Umar that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to Aisha: "O Aisha, those who divided their religion and became sects are the people of innovations, the people of desires, and the people of misguidance from this nation. There is no repentance for them. O Aisha, for every sinner there is repentance except for the people of innovations and the people of desires. There is no repentance for them and they are innocent of me." Ibn Kathir said: It is strange and its chain of transmission cannot be traced back to the Prophet (peace be upon him). Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: When the verse, Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, was revealed, a Muslim man said: O Messenger of God, is there a good deed? He said: Yes, the best of good deeds. This is a mursal hadith and we do not know how its chain of transmission goes back to Saeed. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Nu'aym narrated in Al-Hilya on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud: Whoever brings a good deed, he said: There is no god but God. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abu al-Sheikh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. We have already mentioned that authentic hadiths have been proven to multiply a good deed tenfold, so we will not prolong their mention. Many hadiths have been narrated about increasing it beyond this amount, and God’s grace is vast and His giving is abundant.
6:161: When the Almighty explained that the infidels had divided into groups and formed parties, He ordered His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them: 161- Indeed, my Lord has guided me meaning He has guided me with what He has revealed to me to a straight path which is the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, and a religion is in the accusative case as a state as Qatrub said, or as a direct object of guided me as Al-Akhfash said. It was said: It is in the middle of a verb indicated by guided me because its meaning is made me know meaning made me know a religion. It was said: It is a substitute for the place of to a path because its meaning is guided me to a straight path as in the Almighty’s saying: and guides you to a straight path. It was said: It is in the accusative case with an implied verb, as if it was said: follow a religion. His saying: straight The Kufians and Ibn Amir read it with a kasra on the qaf, a lightening and a fatha on the ya. The rest read it with the opening of the qaf and the breaking of the double yaa, and they are two dialects. Its meaning is the straight religion that has no crookedness in it, and it is an attribute of our religion, which is described with it, while it is a source of exaggeration. The accusative of the religion of Abraham is because it is an apposition to our religion, and it is permissible to make it accusative by estimating I mean, and hanifan is accusative as a state of Abraham, as Al-Zajjaj said. Ali bin Sulayman said: It is accusative with the omission of I mean. And the hanif is the one who inclines toward the truth, and its investigation has been presented above. And he was not of the polytheists is in the accusative case, conjoined with hanifan, or an interjectional clause confirming what preceded it.
6:162: His saying: 162- "Say: My prayer" God the Almighty commanded him to say this statement to them after He commanded him to say the previous statement to them. It was said: The reason for that is that what the first statement included is an indication of the fundamentals of religion, and this is its branches. What is meant by prayer is its genus, so all its types are included in it. It was said: What is meant by it here is the night prayer, and it was said: the Eid prayer. And the ritual: is the plural of nasikah, which is the sacrifice. This is what Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Saeed bin Jubayr and others said: meaning my sacrifice in Hajj and Umrah. Al-Hasan said: My religion. Al-Zajjaj said: My worship is from their saying: the ritual of so-and-so is a ritualist: if he worships, and a group of the people of knowledge said the same. And my life and my death meaning what I do in my life and my death of good deeds, and among the good deeds in death is the will to give charity and various types of acts of worship. It was said: The very life and the very death for God Al-Hasan read nasikah with a sukoon on the seen. The rest read it with a damma on it. The people of Medina read Muhyai with a sukoon on the ya'. The rest read it with a fatha so that two quiescent letters would not meet. An-Nahhas said: None of the grammarians permitted it, i.e. the sukoon, except Yunus. He only permitted it because the long vowel in the alif takes the place of the vowel. Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa ibn Umar, and Asim al-Jahdari read Muhyai without an alif, which is the language of the Ali of Mudar. From this comes the saying of the poet: They preceded my passion and embraced their passion, so they were destroyed, and every side has its fate. To God, Lord of the Worlds, meaning purely for Him, with no partner or associate.
6:163: And the reference 163- with that to what was conveyed by To God, Lord of the worlds * He has no partner of sincerity in obedience and making it for God alone. His saying: And I am the first of the Muslims means the first of the Muslims of his nation, and it was said: the first of all the Muslims, because even though he was late in the message, he was the first of them in creation, and from it is the saying of the Most High: And when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah the verse, and the first is more appropriate. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: Al-Shafi’i used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of opening the prayer with this remembrance, because God commanded His Prophet to do so and revealed it in His Book. Then he mentioned the hadith of Ali that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to pray, he would say: I have directed my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of the polytheists, until his saying: And I am the first of the Muslims. I said: This is in Sahih Muslim at length, and it is one of the mentioned remembrances, but it is restricted to the night prayer as in the authentic narrations. The most authentic remembrance that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to adhere to and guide people to is: O God, distance between me and my sins, until the end. We have explained this in our explanation of al-Muntaqa in a way that does not need any addition here. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil, regarding his statement: My prayer, he said: meaning the obligatory prayer, and my sacrifice, meaning the Hajj. Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, And my sacrifice, he said: my sacrifice. They also narrated on the authority of Qatada, My prayer and my sacrifice, he said: my Hajj and my sacrifice. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And my sacrifice, he said: my sacrifice in Hajj and Umrah. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And my sacrifice, he said: my sacrifice. And regarding his statement: And I am the first of the Muslims, he said: from this nation. Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Fatima, stand up and witness your sacrifice, for with the first drop of its blood that drips, every sin you have committed will be forgiven you, and say: ‘My prayer is to me, and I am the first of the Muslims.’ I said: O Messenger of God, is this for you and your family specifically, but is it for you or for all Muslims? He said: ‘No, rather for all Muslims.’”
6:164: The question in Should I seek a lord other than God? is for denial and is an answer to the polytheists when they called him to worship other than God: that is, how can I seek other than God as an independent lord and abandon the worship of God or a partner with God and worship them both, while the fact is that He is the Lord of everything, and the one you call me to worship is from the group of those who are subject to Him, a creation like me who is not able to benefit or harm, and in this speech there is a rebuke and rebuke to them that cannot be measured, and it is not subject to the verb that follows it, and lord is a distinguishing feature or a second object on the basis of making the verb subject to two objects, His statement: And no soul earns except against itself that is, no one will be held accountable for what it has done of sin and committed of disobedience other than it, so all its earning of evil against itself does not extend to others, and it is like His statement, the Most High: It shall have what it has earned, and against it what it has earned and His statement: That every soul may be recompensed for what it strives for. His statement: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. The root of wazr is heaviness, and from it is the statement of God Almighty: And We have removed from you your burden, which here means sin, and they shall bear their burdens on their backs. Al-Akhfash said: It is said: wazr yuwazr, and wazr yuzr “wazran,” and it is permissible to say izran, and in it is a rejection of what was done in the days of ignorance of holding a relative accountable for the sin of his relative, and one of the tribe for the sin of another. It has been said that what is meant by this verse is the Hereafter, as well as the one before it, because God Almighty says: And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively. Similar to this is the statement of Zainab bint Jahsh: O Messenger of God, will we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us? He said: Yes, if evil increases. The first is to take the verse at face value: I mean the generality and what was mentioned about being held accountable for the sin of others, such as the blood money that the agnatic kin bears and the like, so it is in the ruling of being specified by this generality and is established in its place and this verse does not contradict God Almighty’s statement: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens in addition to their own burdens. What is meant by the burdens in addition to their burdens are the burdens of those whom they mislead, as in the other verse: And they will bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. “Then to your Lord is your return” on the Day of Resurrection and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ in this world, and at that time the truth of the truthful will be revealed and the falsehood of the falsehoods will be revealed.
6:165: His saying: 165- And it is He who made you successors on the earth. Successors is the plural of successor: meaning He made you successors of past nations and previous centuries. Al-Shamakh said: I suffer from them, but fate misses me, and I am left behind in one region after another. Or what is meant is that some of them succeed others, or that this human species are God’s successors on His earth, And He has raised some of you above others in degrees in creation, provision, strength, virtue, and knowledge, and degrees is in the accusative case by removing the preposition: meaning to degrees, To test you in what He has given you meaning to test you in what He has given you of those matters, or to test some of you with others, as God Almighty says: And We have made some of you a trial for others then He frightened them and said: Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty for even if it is in the Hereafter, everything that comes is near, as He said: And the matter of the Hour is not but as the twinkling of an eye or even nearer then He encouraged those Muslims who deserve encouragement and said: And indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful meaning, He is abundant in forgiveness and mercy. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of sin, he said: No one will be held accountable for the sin of another. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And it is He who made you successors on the earth, he said: He destroyed the first generations and made us successors in them after them. And raised some of you above others in degrees, he said: In provision.
7:1: It is Meccan except for eight verses, which are: And ask them about the city to And when We lifted the mountain above them. Ibn Ad-Durais, An-Nahhas in his Naskh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-A'raf was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: One verse of Al-A'raf is Medinan, which is: And ask them about the city which was by the sea to the end of the verse, and the rest of it is Meccan. It has been proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite it in the Maghrib prayer, dividing it into two rak'ahs. It has two hundred and six verses. His saying: 1- Alif-Lam-Sad: We have already mentioned in the opening of Surat Al-Baqarah what makes it unnecessary to repeat it, and it is either a subject and its predicate is a book: meaning Alif-Lam-Sad is letters.
7:2: 2- A book revealed to you or it is the predicate of a deleted subject, the meaning of which is this, meaning the one named by it. However, if these openings are listed in the form of enumeration, then it has no place, and the book is the predicate of the subject according to the first method or the predicate of a deleted subject according to the second, meaning it is a book. Al-Kisa'i said: meaning this is a book, and revealed to you is an attribute of it. So let there not be in your breast any distress over it. Distress: tightness: meaning let there not be in your breast any distress over it from conveying it to the people for fear that they will lie to you and harm you, for God is your protector and supporter. It was said: What is meant is that your chest should not be constricted since they did not believe in it and did not respond to you, for upon you is only the conveyance. Mujahid and Qatadah said: The difficulty here is doubt, because the doubter is constricted in his chest: that is, do not doubt that it was sent down from God. Based on this, the prohibition to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, is by way of insinuation, and what is meant is his nation: that is, none of them doubts that. The pronoun in from it refers to the Book, so according to the first interpretation, it would be on the assumption of an omitted complement: that is, from conveying it. Based on the second interpretation, it would be on the assumption of its revelation. The pronoun in that you may warn with it refers to the Book: that is, to warn people with the Book that We have sent down to you. It is related to that which was sent down: that is, it was sent down to you for you to warn people with it, or it is related to the prohibition, because the absence of doubt that it was sent down from God or the absence of fear from his people strengthens him in warning and encourages him, because the one who is certain proceeds with insight and undertakes with strength of soul. His statement: And a reminder for the believers Reminder means reminding. The Basrans said: Reminder is in the nominative case with an implied subject. Al-Kisa’i said: It is in the nominative case in apposition to Kitab. The accusative case is permissible as a source: that is, and he mentioned it with a remembrance, as the Basrans said. The genitive case is permissible as a case of tandhahir, that is, for warning and remembrance, and the remembrance is specific to the believers because they are the ones on whom it is effective, and in it is an indication of the specification of the warning to the disbelievers.
7:3: His statement: 3- Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord means the Book and the Sunnah is similar to it, as He says: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from and similar verses, and it is a command to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to his nation, and it was said: It is a command to the nation after his command, may God bless him and grant him peace, to convey, and it was revealed to them by way of its revelation to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not follow other guardians besides Him a prohibition for the nation from following guardians besides God, worshipping them and making them partners with God, so the pronoun in this case in other than Him refers to the Lord, and it is permissible for it to refer to what is in what has been revealed to you: that is, do not follow other guardians besides the Book of God, imitating them in your religion as the people of ignorance used to do by obeying the leaders in what they permitted for them and prohibited for them. His saying: You rarely remember. The word little is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted verbal noun for the delayed verb: meaning, remembering little. Ma is an additional word for emphasis, or it is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of do not follow. “Ma” is a verbal noun: meaning, do not follow other guardians besides Him. You rarely remember is read with a lightened letter by deleting one of the two ta’s, and it is read with a shaddah due to assimilation.
7:4: His statement: 4- And how many a town have We destroyed "how many is the informative particle that indicates abundance and is in the nominative case as a subject, and we destroyed it is the predicate, and many town is a distinguishing feature, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with an implied verb after it and not before it, because it is at the beginning of the sentence, and if we destroyed it were not occupied with the pronoun, it would have been permissible for how many" to be in the accusative case with it, and the town is a place where people gather: that is, how many a town of the large towns have We destroyed itself by destroying its people, or We destroyed its people, and what is meant is that We wanted to destroy it. His statement: "So Our punishment came upon it is conjoined with we destroyed" with the estimation of the will as mentioned before, because the order of the coming of the punishment after the destruction is not correct except with this estimation, since the destruction is the same as the coming of the punishment. Al-Farraa said: The fa’ has the meaning of waw, so it is not necessary to estimate, and the meaning is: We destroyed it and Our punishment came to it, and waw is for the general plural, there is no order in it, and it was said: The destruction happened to some of the people of the village, so the meaning is: How many a village have We destroyed some of its people, so Our punishment came to it, so We destroyed them all, and it was said: The meaning is: How many a village have We decreed to be destroyed, so Our punishment came to it, and it was said: We destroyed it by sending angels of punishment to it, so Our punishment came to it, and punishment is the punishment. It was narrated from Al-Farraa that if the meaning of the two verbs is one or like one, you put whichever you want first, so the meaning is: How many a village has Our punishment come to it, so We destroyed it, like dana faqrab and qarab fadna by night meaning at night, because one spends the night in it, it is said: bata yabit baytan wa bayatan, and it is a source that takes the place of a state: meaning two nights. His saying: or they are sleeping is conjoined with bayatan meaning spending the night or sleeping. The present sentence came without a waw because of the difficulty of the two waws coming together, the waw of conjunction and the waw of state. This is what Al-Farra’ said. Al-Zajjaj objected to him and said: This is wrong, rather it does not need a waw. You say: Zaid came to me riding or he is walking because in the sentence there is a pronoun that refers back to the first, and the waw in this place is for detail, not for doubt. The siesta is sleeping in the middle of the day. It was said: It is merely resting during that time due to the intense heat without sleeping. He specified the two times because they are the times of calm and tranquility, so the coming of the punishment during them is more severe and terrible.
7:5: His saying: 5- "So their only supplication when Our punishment came to them was that they said, 'Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'" The supplication: the supplication: meaning, their only supplication to their Lord when the punishment descended was their admission of wrongdoing against themselves. And similar to it: "And their last supplication" meaning their last supplication. And it was said: the supplication here means the claim, and the meaning: what they claim for their religion and adopt it was nothing but their admission of its invalidity and corruption. And the subject of was "except that they said and its predicate is their supplication" and the opposite is permissible, and the meaning: their only supplication was their saying: Indeed, we were wrongdoers.
7:6: His saying: 6- "Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent." This is a severe threat, and the question is for the people to whom God sent messengers from the previous nations for rebuke and reprimand, and the lam is the lam of the oath: meaning, We will surely question them about what they answered their messengers with when they called them, and the fa is to arrange the conditions of the afterlife based on the conditions of the world. "And We will surely question the messengers" meaning the prophets whom God sent: meaning, We will ask them about what their nations answered them with, and who among them obeyed and who disobeyed. It was said that the meaning is: We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent: meaning the prophets, and We will surely question the messengers: meaning the angels. This does not contradict the saying of God Almighty: "And the criminals will not be asked about their sins" because we have mentioned more than once that the afterlife is a place, so in a place they will be asked, and in a place they will not be asked, and so is everything that was mentioned that appears to be a contradiction by affirming it sometimes and denying it at other times with regard to the Day of Resurrection, for it is based on multiple situations with the great length of that day.
7:7: 7- So We will narrate to them with knowledge meaning to the messengers and those to whom they were sent what happened between them when they called them with knowledge, not ignorance: meaning knowing what they concealed and what they declared. And We were not absent from them in any situation, so that anything that happened between them would be hidden from Us. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat, and Ibn Al-Najjar in his history narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, Alif, Alif, Lam, Mu’min, that he said: I, by God, am the best. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that this and similar openings of the surahs are an oath by which God swore, and they are among the names of God. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the statement of God, Alif, Alif, Lam, Mu’min, that he said: It is Al-Musawwir. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi regarding the statement of God, Alif, Alif, Lam, Mu’min, that he said: The Alif is from God, the Meem is from Ar-Rahman, and the Sad is from As-Samad. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak that he said: Its meaning is I am God, the Truthful. It is clear from you that all of this is based on conjecture and interpretation based on intuition, and there is no proof in any of that, and the truth is what we mentioned in the opening of Surat Al-Baqarah. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, So let there not be in your breast any distress therefrom, he said: Doubt. And he said to a Bedouin: What is the distress in you? He said: Confusion. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid something similar. And Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ad-Dahhak, he said: Difficulty. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Masoud, No people perished until they excused themselves, then he recited: So what was their call? And the verse. And Ibn Jarir narrated it from him with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas, Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers, he said: We will ask the people about what they answered the messengers, and We will ask the messengers about what they conveyed, and We will narrate to them with knowledge. He said: By placing the Book on the Day of Resurrection, then We will speak about what they used to do. And Abd bin Hamid narrated from Farqad regarding the verse, he said: One of them is the prophets, and one of them is the angels. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: We ask people about the statement There is no god but God and we ask Gabriel.
7:8: His saying: 8- "And the weighing on that Day will be the truth." The weighing is the subject and its predicate is the truth: meaning the weighing on that Day is justice in which there is no injustice, or the predicate is the day, and the truth is a description of the subject, meaning the just weighing will be on this Day, and it was said that the truth is the predicate of a deleted subject. Scholars differed about the nature of this weighing that will take place on this day. It was said: What is meant by it is the weighing of the scrolls of the servants’ deeds on the scales with a real weight, and this is the correct view, and it is what the evidence has established. It was also said: The deeds themselves will be weighed, even if they are accidents, for God will turn them into bodies on the Day of Resurrection, as came in the authentic hadith: Indeed, Al-Baqarah and Al-Imran will come on the Day of Resurrection as if they were two clouds or two clouds or two flocks of white birds. Likewise, it was proven in the authentic hadith that the Qur’an will come in the form of a pale young man and the like. It was said: The scale is the book in which are the deeds of creation. It was also said: The weight and the scale mean justice and judgment, and their mention is for the sake of striking an example, as you say this statement about the weight of this. Al-Zajjaj said: This is permissible from the point of view of the tongue, and it is better to follow what came in the authentic chains of transmission regarding the mention of the scale. Al-Qushayri said: Al-Zajjaj did well in what he said, because if the path is taken to refer to the true religion, and Paradise and Hell to refer to the souls and not the bodies, and the devils and jinn to refer to the blameworthy morals, and the angels to refer to the praiseworthy powers, then he said: The nation agreed in the early days to take these apparent meanings without interpretation, and if they agreed to prevent interpretation, then it is necessary to take the apparent meaning, then these apparent meanings become texts. And the truth is the first statement. As for those who exclude these phenomena from their reality, they do not bring anything from the Sharia to refer to in their exclusion, but rather the most they cling to is mere rational exclusions, and there is no proof in that for anyone. If their minds did not accept it, then the minds of people who were stronger than their minds from the Companions, the Followers, and those who followed them accepted it until innovations came like a dark night and they said: Whatever he wants, and they left the Sharia behind them. I wish they had brought rational rulings that the rational people would agree upon and their acceptance of them would be united. Rather, each group claims from reason what matches its desires and agrees with what it or those who follow it go to, so their minds contradict each other according to the contradiction of their doctrines. Every fair-minded person knows this, and whoever denies it should purify his understanding and mind from the impurities of fanaticism and doctrine, because if he does that, the morning will dawn for his eyes. Weights and scales are mentioned in several places in the Qur’an, such as His statement: And We will set up the just balances on the Day of Resurrection, so that not a soul will be wronged at all, and His statement: So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask about one another, and His statement: “So those whose scales are heavy - those will be the successful ones. And those whose scales are light - those are the ones who have lost their souls; in Hell they will abide eternally,” and His statement: Indeed, God does not wrong by as much as an atom’s weight, and His statement: “So as for he whose scales are heavy, * He will be in a pleasant life. * But as for he whose scales are light, * His mother will be in the abyss.” The fa in so as for he whose scales are heavy is for detail. The scales are the plural of scale, and its root is mawzan, the waw was changed to a ya because of the kasra of what precedes it. The weight of the scales is the weight of what is placed in them of the scrolls of deeds. It was said that the scales are the plural of mawzun, meaning whoever’s weighed deeds are heavier, and the first is more appropriate. The apparent meaning of the word mawazih his scales added to the worker is that each of the workers has scales, each of which weighs a type of his work. It has been said that it is a single scale expressed in the plural form, as is said: So-and-so went to Mecca on mules. The reference in his saying, those is to whom, and the plural is in consideration of its meaning, as the pronoun his scales refers to it in consideration of its wording, and it is the subject and its predicate is they are the successful ones.
7:9: And the speech in His saying: 9- "And those whose scales are light - then those are the ones who have lost themselves is similar to it, and the ba' in because they were unjust to Our signs" is causal, and ma is a source. The meaning of "they were unjust is they lie.
7:10: His saying: 10- And We have established you in the land meaning We have made a place for you in it and provided you with the means of livelihood. And livelihoods are the plural of livelihood: meaning that which one lives by, such as food and drink and what life is by. It is said, Asha ya'ish `ayshwan wa'ashan wa'ashan. Al-Zajjaj said: livelihood is that by which they attain livelihood, and livelihood according to Al-Akhfash and many grammarians is a verbal noun. Al-A'raj read Ma'aish with a hamza, and this is how Kharijah bin Mus'ab narrated from Nafi'. Al-Nahhas said: The hamza is a mistake that is not permissible, because the singular is Ma'ishah and the ya' is original, like Madinah and Mada'in and Sahifah and Sahaifah. His saying: You are rarely grateful The discussion of it is like the discussion of what came before, close to the saying of God Almighty: You are rarely remembered.
7:11: His statement: 11- "And We created you, then We shaped you." This is a mention of another blessing from God upon His servants. The meaning is: We created you from sperm, then We shaped you after that. It was also said that the meaning is: We created Adam from dust, then We shaped you in his back. It was also said that: "And We created you" means Adam was mentioned in the plural form because he is the father of mankind. "Then We shaped you refers back to him, and this is indicated by Then We said to the angels, prostrate to Adam."
