The arrangement of this statement on creation and sculpting indicates that the created being shaped is Adam, peace be upon him. Al-Akhfash said: "Then in Then We shaped you means and." It was also said that the meaning is: We created you from Adam's back, then We shaped you when We took the covenant from you. An-Nahhas said: This is the best of the sayings. It was said that the meaning is: We created the spirits first, then we formed the ghosts, then we said to the angels, Prostrate to Adam. That is, we commanded them to do so, so they obeyed the command, and they prostrated after the command, except Iblis. It was said: The exception is connected to the predominance of the angels over Iblis, because he was alone among them, or as was said: because among the angels there is a kind called the jinn. Other than that was said, and its investigation was presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. His saying: He was not among those who prostrated.
7:12: And the sentence 12- He said, 'What prevented you from prostrating?' is a new answer to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did God say to him? And the no in not prostrating is redundant for emphasis, as evidenced by the Almighty's saying in Surat Sad: What prevented you from prostrating? It was said that prevented means said, and the meaning is: Who told you not to prostrate? And it was said that prevented means called: that is, what called you not to prostrate? And it was said that there was an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: What prevented you from obedience and made you need not to prostrate? When I commanded you: that is, when I commanded you. It has been used as evidence that the command is immediate, and the discussion is established in the science of principles, and the question in what prevented you is for reprimand and rebuke, otherwise He, the Almighty, knows that. And the sentence He said, 'I am better than him' is a new answer to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did Iblis say? Rather, he said in response, I am better than him, and did not say, This prevented me, because in this sentence that he brought as a new sentence there is what indicates the obstacle, which is his belief that he is better than him. And the superior does not do such a thing for the inferior, despite what this sentence indicates of denying that someone like him would be ordered to prostrate to someone like him. Then he explained what he claimed of superiority by saying, You created me from fire and created him from clay, believing that the element of fire is better than the element of clay. The enemy of God made a mistake, for the element of clay is better than the element of fire in terms of its sobriety, stillness, and longevity, which is a turbulent reality that quickly runs out. Despite this, he is present in Paradise, but not in it, and it is a torment less than it, and it needs him to take refuge in it, and it is a mosque and purification. And if his misery had not preceded and the word of God had not come true regarding him, he would have had the angels who obeyed this command as an example and model, for their element of light is more noble than his element of fire.
7:13: And the sentence 13- He said, then descend is a resumption like the one before it, and the fa is to arrange the order to descend based on his opposition to the order: that is, descend from the sky, which is the place of the obedient angels who do not disobey God in what He commands them, to the earth, which is the place of those who disobey and obey, for the sky is not suitable for someone who is arrogant and disobeys the command of his Lord like you, and for this reason He said: It is not for you to be arrogant therein. And among the false interpretations is what was said that the meaning of descend from it is to come out of your fiery form that you were proud of, a dark, distorted form, and it was said: what is meant is his descent from Paradise, and it was said: from the group of angels, and the sentence then come out is to emphasize the order to descend, and the sentence Indeed, you are among the debased is an explanation of the order: that is, you are among the people of humiliation and disgrace before God and the righteous of His servants, and thus everyone who wears the cloak of arrogance is punished by wearing the cloak of humiliation and disgrace. Whoever wears the robe of humility, God will dress him in the robe of superiority.
7:14: And sentence 14 - He said, 'Respite me until the Day they are resurrected' is a resumption as mentioned in the previous sentences: meaning, give me respite until the Day of Resurrection, and it is as if he asked that he not die, because there is no death after the Day of Resurrection, and the pronoun in they are resurrected refers to Adam and his descendants.
7:15: So God answered him by saying: 15- You are among those who are given respite meaning those who are given respite until that day, then you will be punished with what God has decreed for you, and He will send you down into the depths of Hell. It was said: The wisdom behind His respite is to test the servants so that He may know who obeys Him and who disobeys Him.
7:16: Sentence 16- He said, 'Then by what you have led me astray' is a resumption like the previous sentences, coming in answer to an implied question. The ba in then by what is for causality and the fa is for the order of the sentence based on what preceded it. It was said that the ba is for an oath, like his saying: Then by your glory, I will surely lead them astray all together meaning, by your leading me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on your straight path. Leading astray means falling into error. It was said that the ba is in the sense of the lam, and it was said that it means with. The meaning is: So by what did you lead me astray? The first is more appropriate. What he meant by this seduction, which he made a reason for what he would do to the servants, was his abandonment of prostration, and that this was due to God’s seduction of him, until he chose misguidance over guidance. It was said: He meant by it the curse that God cursed him: that is, since you cursed me and destroyed me, I will sit in wait for them. From this, they will meet with error, meaning destruction. Ibn al-A’rabi said: It is said: A man went astray, yaghawi ghayyan, if his affair was corrupted or he himself was corrupted. From this, And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray, meaning his life in Paradise was corrupted. I will sit in wait for them, meaning I will strive to mislead them until they are corrupted because of me, just as I was corrupted because of my abandonment of prostration to their father. The straight path is the road leading to Paradise, and its accusative case is circumstantial: meaning, on your straight path, as Sibawayh narrated, Zayd struck his back and stomach. The lam in la’qa’adun is the lam of an oath, and the ba’ in bima aghwaytani is related to the deleted verb of the oath: meaning, then by what you have led me astray, I swear that I will sit.
7:17: His saying: 17- Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left He mentioned the four directions because they are the ones from which the enemy will come to his enemy, and for this reason he left out mentioning the direction above and below, and the verb was transitive to the first two directions with min, and to the last two with an, because the majority of those who come from the front and behind are directed towards what is coming to them with their entire body, and the majority of those who come from the right and left are deviating, so it was appropriate for the first two to be transitive with the letter of beginning, and for the last two to be transitive with the letter of passing, and this is a representation of his whispering and insinuations to those who come in reality, and it was said: What is meant is from before them from their worldly life, from behind them from their afterlife, from their right from the direction of their good deeds, and from their left from the direction of their bad deeds, and An-Nahhas approved of this. His saying: And you will not find most of them grateful means that when I do that, you will not find most of them grateful because of the effect of my whisperings on them and my tempting them. He said this based on conjecture, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: And Satan proved true about them his conjecture. It was said that he heard that from the angels and said it, and he expressed gratitude as obedience, or it is in its true sense and that they did not thank God because of the temptation.
7:18: And sentence 18 - He said, get out of it is a resumption like the sentences before it: that is, from the sky or paradise or from among the angels as mentioned before condemned that is, blamed from dhamahu if he condemned him. It is said: dhamathu and dhammutu have the same meaning. Al-A'mash read madhmoon. Al-Zuhri read madhmoon without a hamza, and it was said that madh'um means the exiled, and madhhur means the expelled. His saying: For those of them who follow you. The majority read it with the fatha on the lam as the lam of the oath, and its answer is I will fill Hell with you all. It was said: The lam in for those who follow you is for emphasis, and in I will fill it is the lam of the oath. The first is more appropriate, and the answer to the oath fills the answer to the condition, because from is a conditional, and in this answer there is a threat that cannot be estimated. Asim read in a narration from him: for those who follow you with the kasra on the lam, and some grammarians denied it. An-Nahhas said: Its meaning, and God knows best, is for the sake of those who followed you, as it is said: I honored so-and-so for you. It was said: It is a reason for I went out. The pronoun from you refers to him and to those who followed him. The pronoun of address prevailed over the pronoun of absence, and the original is from you and from them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And the weighing on that Day will be the truth, he said: justice. So he whose scales are heavy, he said: his good deeds. And he whose scales are light, he said: his good deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi that deeds will be weighed. Many hadiths have been narrated about the manner of the scales, the weighing and the weighed. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “A man from my nation will be called out before all of creation on the Day of Resurrection, and ninety-nine scrolls will be spread out for him, each scroll as far as the eye can see. He will say: ‘Do you deny any of this? Did the guardian scribes wrong you?’ He will say: ‘No, O Lord.’ He will say: ‘Do you have an excuse or a good deed?’ The man will be frightened and say: ‘No, O Lord.’ He will say: ‘Yes, you have a good deed with Us and you will not be wronged today.’ A card will be brought out for him on which will be written: ‘I bear witness that there is no god but God and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.’ He will say: ‘O Lord, what is this card compared to these scrolls?’ It will be said: ‘You will not be wronged.’ The scrolls will be placed on one side of the scale and the card on the other side, so the scrolls will fly away and the card will be heavy.” Al-Tirmidhi also authenticated it, and its chain of transmission is Hasan. Abdul Razzaq, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We created you, then We shaped you, he said: They were created in the loins of men and shaped in the wombs of women. Al-Faryabi narrated on his authority that he said: They were created in the back of Adam and then shaped in the wombs. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said: As for Our creation of you, it is Adam, and as for Then We shaped you, it is his offspring. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the verse that he said: Iblis was created from the fire of glory. It is proven in Sahih from the hadith of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The angels were created from light, Iblis was created from fire, and Adam was created from what He has described to you. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: The first one to make an analogy was Iblis in his statement: You created me from fire and created him from clay, and its chain of transmission back to Al-Hasan is sound. Abu Nu`aym narrated in Al-Hilyah and Al-Daylami on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The first one to measure the matter of religion by his own opinion was Iblis. God said to him, ‘Prostrate to Adam.’ He said, ‘I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.’” Ja`far said: Whoever measures the matter of religion by his own opinion, God will associate him with Iblis on the Day of Resurrection because he followed him in analogy. The chain of transmission of this hadith should be examined, as I do not think it is authentically attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and it does not resemble the words of the Prophet. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said, Because You have misled me, meaning, you have led me astray. `Abd ibn Humayd narrated on his authority, regarding His statement, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path, he said, The path to Mecca. `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And on their right, their religious affairs were unclear to them. And on their left, he said: sins were made lawful for them and falsehood was most deserving of them. And you will not find most of them grateful, he said: monotheists. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: Then I will come to them from before them, he said: from where they see. And from behind them, from where they do not see. And on their right, from where they see. And on their left, from where they do not see. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority regarding the verse: he could not say: from above them. In another version: he knew that mercy descends from above them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: censured, he said: blamed, banished: he said: hated. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid: censured, he said: banished. Rejected, he said: expelled.
7:19: His saying: 19- And O Adam is on the assumption of the saying: that is, and We said, O Adam. He said this saying to him after expelling Iblis from Paradise, or from the sky, or from among the angels as mentioned above. The meaning of the dwelling has been mentioned above, and the meaning of Do not approach this tree in Al-Baqarah. The meaning of from wherever you wish is from any type of Paradise you wish to eat, and similar to it is what was mentioned above from the saying of God Almighty: And eat from it in abundance wherever you wish and the deletion of the nun from fatakuna because it is conjoined to the jussive or in the accusative case as an answer to the prohibition.
7:20: His saying: 20- "Then Satan whispered to them" Whispering: a low voice, and whispering: self-talk, it is said: His soul whispered to him a whisper and a whisper with a kasra on the waw, and whispering with a fatha is the noun: like an earthquake and a quake, and it is said: the whispering of a hunter and dogs and the sounds of jewelry are whispers. Al-A'sha said: You hear the whispers of the jewelry when you leave And the whisperer: is the name of the devil. And the meaning of whispering to him is whispering to him or doing the whispering for his sake. His saying: to show them means to appear to them, and the lam is for the consequence as in his saying: to be an enemy and a grief to them, and it was said that it is the lam of ki: meaning he did that so that harm would follow it, or so that harm would occur. His saying: What was concealed meaning what was covered and covered from them of their private parts He called the vagina private part because its appearance would disgrace its owner. Satan wanted to disgrace them by revealing what was concealed from them of their private parts, because they did not see their own private parts nor did one of them see them from the other. The waw in wa-ra was not changed to a hamza because the second part is a long vowel. It was said: Their private parts were only revealed to them and not to anyone else, and there was a light on them that prevented them from being seen. And he said meaning Satan to them, What did your Lord forbid you from eating from this tree except that you should be angels “that” is in the accusative case, and in the speech there is an omitted complement, the meaning of which is: nor is it disliked that you should be angels. This is what the Basrans said. The Kufians said: The meaning is so that you would not be angels or be among the immortals in Paradise or among those who do not die. An-Nahhas said: God favored the angels over all of creation in more than one place in the Qur’an, including this, and nor do I say that I am an angel, and nor the angels brought near. Ibn Furk said: There is no proof in this verse, because it is possible that he means two angels who have no desire for food. People have differed greatly on this issue and have spoken at length for no reason. This issue is not one that God has charged us with knowledge of, so speaking about it does not concern us. Ibn Abbas, Yahya bin Abi Katheer and Ad-Dahhak read two angels with a kasra on the lam. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ rejected this reading and said: There was no king before Adam, so they would become two kings. Those who read with a kasra cited as evidence the words of God the Almighty: Shall I guide you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will not decay? Abu Ubaid said: This is a clear argument for the kasra reading, but people tend to abandon it, so we have abandoned it. An-Nahhas said: It is an anomalous reading. He rejected Abu Ubaid’s words and considered them a grave mistake. He said: Is it permissible to imagine that Adam, peace be upon him, would attain more than the kingdom of Paradise, which is the ultimate goal of seekers? Rather, the meaning of and a kingdom that will not decay is the status of the kingdom of Paradise and eternity therein.
7:21: His saying: 21- And he swore to them, ‘I am to you both a sincere adviser.’ That is, he swore to them and said: I swear an oath, that is, he swore. From this is the saying of the poet: And share with them, by God, the effort, for you are sweeter than the quail when we resurrect it. Although the form of the verb mufa`ala originally indicates participation, it has often been used for other purposes. We have already explained this in Al-Ma'idah, and what is meant here is the exaggeration in the oaths that Satan gave them. It was said that they swore to him to accept them, just as he swore to them to advise them.
7:22: His saying: 22- So he led them down with deception. The word dallā and adlā mean sending something from a high place to a low place. It is said that he sent his bucket down, meaning that he caused them to descend from the high place to eat from the tree. It was also said that its meaning was: he caused them to fall into destruction, and it was also said that he deceived them. Naftuwayh recited: If you want to deceive a generous person, you can deceive him. But you will see that the mean person is experienced and cannot be deceived. It was said: The meaning ofدلهماisدلمةfrom the word daala, which means boldness: i.e. he made them bold to commit a sin, so they left Paradise. His statement: So when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them means when they tasted it, their private parts became apparent to them because of the disappearance of what was covering it, which was the reduction of the light that was on it. It was mentioned in Al-Baqarah. His statement: And they began to fasten together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise tafaqa yaf'al kadha: meaning he began to do such and such. Al-Akhfash narrated: tafaqa yaffaqa like daraba yudhur: i.e. they began or began to fasten together over themselves. Al-Hasan read yakhsifaan with a kasra on the kha and a shaddah on the saad, and the original is yakhsifaan, so it was assimilated and the kha was broken because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn Buraydah and Ya'qub read with a fatha on the kha. Al-Zuhri read yakhsifaan from akhshaf. The majority read yakhsifaan from khasaf. Meaning: They began to cut the paper and stick it to their private parts to cover them, from the woven sandal: if you put it layer upon layer, And their Lord called to them, saying to them: Did I not forbid you from that tree? which I forbade you from eating, and this is a rebuke and rebuke from God to them since they did not beware of what He warned them against, And I say to you, in apposition to that you two, “that Satan is to you a clear enemy,” meaning he shows enmity.
7:23: His statement: 23- They said, ‘Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves.’ This is an introductory sentence based on an assumed question, as if it was said, So what did they say? This is an admission of guilt from them and that they wronged themselves because of the transgression that occurred from them. Then they said, And if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.
7:24: And sentence 24 - He said, 'Go down' is a resumption like the one before it, and the address is to Adam and Eve and their offspring, or to them and Satan, and the sentence Some of you are enemies to others is in the accusative case as a state, and for you on the earth is a settlement meaning a place of settlement, and for you provisions that you enjoy in this world and benefit from in terms of food and drink and the like, for a time meaning until a time, which is the time of your death.
7:25: And sentence 25 - He said, 'Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth' is a resumption like the one before it: meaning, on the earth you will live, and therein death will come to you, and from it you will be brought forth to the abode of the Hereafter. And similar to it is the statement of God Almighty: From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth another time. And know that this story has been explained in full previously in Surat Al-Baqarah, so refer to it. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir Al-Usul, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih regarding his statement: That He might make apparent to them that which was hidden from them of their private parts, he said: There was a light on each of them so that neither of them could see the private parts of the other, but when they committed the sin, it was removed from them. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Satan came to them and said: Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree except that you should be two angels like Him, meaning like God the Almighty, but they did not believe him until he entered the belly of the snake and spoke to them. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: Except that you should be two angels, if He made you mistaken for being two angels, He made you mistaken for being immortal and you would never die in it. And he swore to them, he said: He swore to them: Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisors. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b regarding his statement: So he led them astray with deception, he said: He made them deceive. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: The clothing of every animal, and the clothing of man, is the nail. So Adam repented when he got a nail. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The clothing of Adam and Eve was like a nail, but when they ate from the tree, nothing remained on them except the size of a nail. And they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. He said: They would remove fig leaves and place them on their private parts. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: When God made Adam dwell in Paradise, He clothed him in a garment of nails, but when he committed the sin, He stripped him of the garment and it remained on the tips of his fingers. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on his authority from another chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik who said: Adam’s clothing in Paradise was ruby, but when he disobeyed, it was cut short and became a nail. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they began to mend, he said: They patched together like a garment. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi: And their Lord called to them, ‘Did I not forbid you from that tree?’ Adam said: My Lord, he swore to me by You, and I did not know that any of Your creation would swear by You except truthfully. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of al-Hasan: They said, ‘Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves,’ the verse. He said: These are the words that Adam received from his Lord. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of al-Dahhak.
7:26: God, the Almighty, expressed the creation by sending down: meaning, We created for you clothing to cover your private parts that Satan revealed from your parents, and the private part is the private part as mentioned previously, and the discussion of its value and what must be covered of it is explained in the books of branches. His statement: and feathers Al-Hasan and Asim read from the narration of Al-Mufaddal Al-Dabbi and Abu Amr from the narration of Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Ja'fi and feathers and the rest read and feathers and feathers and feathers is the plural of feathers: which is clothing. Al-Farraa said: feathers and feathers as it is said: clothes and clothing, and the feathers of the bird are what God covers it with. It was said that what is meant by feathers here is: fertility and luxury of life. Al-Qurtubi said: What most linguists agree on is that feathers are what covers of clothing or livelihood. Abu Hatim narrated from Abu Ubaidah: And a beast was given to him and its feathers: meaning and what was on it of clothing. It was said that what is meant by feathers here is the clothing of adornment because it was mentioned after His statement: We have sent down upon you clothing and its conjunction with it. His saying: And the clothing of piety The people of Medina, Ibn Amir and Al-Kisa’i read clothing in the accusative case. The rest read it in the nominative case, so the accusative case is because it is conjoined with the first clothing, and the nominative case is because it is the subject, and the phrase that is better is its predicate. What is meant by the clothing of piety is the clothing of piety and avoiding the sins of God, which is piety itself and fear of God, so that is the best clothing and the most beautiful adornment. It was said: The clothing of piety is modesty, and it was said: It is righteous work, and it was said: It is the clothing of wool and coarse clothes because of what it contains of humility before God, and it was said: It is the armor and helmet worn by the one who strives in the way of God, and the first is more appropriate. It is true of everything in which there is piety to God, so all of the sayings mentioned are included under it, and such metaphors occur frequently in the speech of the Arabs, including: If a person does not wear clothes of piety, he will be naked, even if he is clothed. And the same: Cover yourself with the garments of generosity, for I see every fault, and generosity is its cover. The reference in His saying: That is to the garment of piety: that is, it is the best garment. Al-A’mash read: And the garment of piety, that is best. The reference in His saying: That is from the signs of God is to the revelation indicated by We sent down: that is, that revelation is from the signs of God indicating that He is its Creator. Then God, glory be to Him, repeated the call to the children of Adam as a warning to them against Satan.
7:27: He said: 27- "O children of Adam, do not let Satan tempt you" meaning do not let him cause you to fall into temptation. The prohibition, even if it is for Satan, is in reality for the children of Adam, so that they do not tempt you with his temptation and be affected by it. The kaf in "as he brought forth" is a description of a deleted source: meaning do not let him tempt you with a temptation like the expulsion of your parents from Paradise. The phrase "He strips them of their clothing" is in the accusative case as a state, and its explanation has already been presented. The lam in "to show them their private parts" is the lam of ki: meaning in order for him to show them, and its explanation has also been presented. His saying: "Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them" This phrase is an explanation of what preceded it, along with what it includes of exaggeration in warning them against him, because whoever is of this status, seeing the children of Adam from where they do not see him, is of great deceit, and it is appropriate for him to be wary of him as much as "and his tribe" are his helpers from the devils and his soldiers. A group of scholars have used this verse as evidence that seeing the devils is not possible, and there is nothing in the verse that indicates that. The most it says is that He sees us from where we do not see Him, and it does not say that we will never see Him. The fact that we do not see Him at the time He sees us does not necessarily mean that we do not see Him at all. Then God Almighty informed us that He made the devils allies of those of His servants who do not believe, and they are the disbelievers. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts, he said: Some Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked. Regarding his statement: and feathers, he said: Money. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr regarding his statement: and clothing to conceal your private parts, he said: Clothes. And feathers, he said: Money. And the clothing of righteousness, he said: Fear of God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Ali regarding his statement: and clothing to conceal your private parts, he said: The clothing of the common people. And feathers, he said: The clothing of adornment. And the clothing of righteousness, he said: Islam. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and feathers, he said: Money, clothing, living and comfort. Regarding his statement: And the clothing of righteousness, he said: Faith and righteous deeds. That is better, he said: Faith and deeds are better than feathers and clothing. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: and feathers, meaning money. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: He strips them of their clothing, meaning piety. And regarding his statement: Indeed, he and his tribe see you, he said: the jinn and devils.
7:28: Al-Fahishah: What is exaggerated in its obscenity and ugliness of sins. Most commentators said: It is the polytheists' circumambulation of the House naked. It was said: It is polytheism, and it appears that it applies to what is more general than both matters, and the meaning is: If they committed an ugly sin that was exaggerated in its ugliness, they apologized for it with two excuses: The first: That they did it in imitation of their fathers when they found them continuing to commit that obscenity, and the second: That they were commanded to do so by God, the Most High. Both excuses are extremely invalid and corrupt, because the existence of their fathers in the state of ugliness does not justify their doing it, and the command from God, the Most High, to them was not to commit indecency, rather He commanded them to follow the prophets and act according to the revealed books and forbade them from disobeying them, and among what He forbade them from was committing indecencies, and for this reason God, the Most High, responded to them by commanding His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, to say to them: 28- Indeed, God does not command indecency. So how can you claim that of Him, the Most High, then He denied what they added to it, saying: Do you say about God what you do not know? This is part of what the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was commanded to say to them, and it contains a great rebuke and rebuke, because if speaking out of ignorance is ugly in everything, then how is it if it is in attributing something to God? Indeed, in this noble verse there is the greatest deterrent and the most eloquent admonition for the imitators who follow their fathers in doctrines that are contrary to the truth, for that is an imitation of the people of disbelief, not the people of truth, for they are the ones who say: Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are following in their footsteps and the ones who say: We found our fathers upon it, and God has commanded us to do it. The imitator, if he were not deceived by the fact that he found his father upon that doctrine, while believing that it is what God has commanded and that it is the truth, would not have remained upon it. This is the characteristic by which the Jew remained upon Judaism, the Christian remained upon Christianity, and the innovator remained upon his innovation. What kept them upon these misguidances is the fact that they found their fathers in Judaism and Christianity or innovation and they thought well that what they were upon was the truth that God had commanded, and they did not look at themselves, nor did they seek the truth as they should, nor did they search for the religion of God as they should. This is pure imitation and utter deficiency. O you who grew up upon one of these Islamic doctrines, I am the most exaggerated warner to you. Warning against saying this article and continuing in misguidance, evil has been mixed with good, the correct with the unsound, and corrupt opinion with correct narration. God did not send to this nation except one prophet whom he commanded them to follow and forbade them from disobeying him, saying: Whatever the Messenger has given you, take it, and what he has forbidden you, refrain from it. If the mere opinion of the imams of the schools of thought and their followers were an argument against the servants, this nation would have had many messengers, as numerous as the people of opinion who charged people with what God did not charge them with. One of the most amazing forms of heedlessness and greatest disregard for the truth is the choice of the imitators of the opinions of men despite the existence of the Book of God, the existence of the Sunnah of His Messenger, the existence of those from whom they take them, and the existence of the tool of understanding and the faculty of reason with them.
7:29: His saying: 29- Say, 'My Lord has commanded justice.' Al-Qist means fairness, and in it is that God, the Exalted, commands justice, not as they claimed that God commanded them to commit immorality. It was said: Al-Qist here is There is no god but God. There is an omission in the speech: that is, say, My Lord has commanded justice, so obey Him. His saying: And direct your faces toward every masjid. is conjoined with the omitted and understood: that is, face Him in your prayers toward the qiblah in whatever masjid you are, or at every time of prostration, or in every place of prostration, on the basis that what is meant by prostration is prayer. And call upon Him, making religion sincere to Him. That is, call upon Him or worship Him while you are sincere in your supplication or worship of Him. It was said: Make Him One and do not associate partners with Him. His saying: As He began you, you will return. The kaf is an attribute of an omitted source. Al-Zajjaj said: It is related to what preceded it. The meaning is: Just as He created you at the beginning of creation, He will return you. The intended meaning is to argue with those who deny the resurrection, so He will reward the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil. It was also said: Just as He brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, you will return to Him, and likewise with nothing. It is like the Almighty’s saying: And you have certainly come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time. It was also said: Just as He began you from dust, you will return to dust.
7:30: 30- A group He guided is in the accusative case with a verb that is explained by what follows it. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a state of the implied word in you return: meaning you return as two groups: happy and miserable. This is strengthened by the reading of Abu Firaikan, A group He guided, and the group that God guided are the believers in God who follow His prophets, and the group that was destined for misguidance are the disbelievers. His statement, Indeed, they took the devils as allies instead of God is an explanation for his statement, And a group upon whom misguidance was destined, meaning that is because they obeyed the devils in disobeying God, and despite this they think that they are guided and did not admit that they were misguided, and this is more severe in their rebellion and stubbornness. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And those who, when they commit an immorality, he said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, so they were forbidden from doing so. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Ka’b something similar. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse: By God, God has never honored a servant for disobeying Him, nor has He been pleased with it for him or commanded it, but He was pleased with your obedience to Him and forbade you from disobeying Him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: My Lord has commanded justice, he said: with fairness. And turn your faces toward every masjid, he said: toward the Ka’bah, where you pray in a church or elsewhere. As He began you, you will return, he said: wretched and happy. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: As He began you, you will return Al-Baqarah 2:177, that he said: God began the creation of the children of Adam as believers and disbelievers, as He said: It is He who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer. Then He will return them on the Day of Resurrection as He began their creation, as believers and disbelievers. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Jabir regarding the verse that he said: They will be resurrected as they were: the believer in his faith and the hypocrite in his hypocrisy. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he mentioned the Qadarites and said: May God fight them! Has God not said: “As We began you, you will return. A party He guided and a party upon whom error was justly decreed.” Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse that He says: Just as We created you the first time, so will you return.
7:31: This is addressed to all of the children of Adam, even if it was mentioned for a specific reason. The consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. Adornment is what people adorn themselves with in terms of clothing. They were commanded to adorn themselves when coming to the mosques for prayer and circumambulation. The verse has been used as evidence for the obligation of covering the private parts during prayer, and this is what the majority of scholars have agreed upon. In fact, covering them is obligatory in all cases, even if a man is alone, as indicated by the authentic hadiths. The discussion of the private parts and what must be covered of them is detailed in the books of branches. His saying: 31- And eat and drink, but be not excessive. God, the Exalted, commanded His servants to eat and drink, and forbade them from extravagance. There is no asceticism in abandoning food or drink. Whoever abandons it completely is a murderer and is among the people of Hellfire, as is confirmed in the authentic hadiths. The one who reduces it in a way that weakens his body and makes him unable to perform what he is required to do of obedience or effort for himself and for those he supports is disobeying what God has commanded and guided to. The one who is extravagant in his spending in a way that only fools do, and wastefulness is disobedient to what God has prescribed for His servants and is included in the Quranic prohibition. Likewise, whoever forbids what is permissible or permits what is forbidden, he is included among the extravagant and excluded from the moderate. And among extravagance is eating without need, and at a time when one is full.
7:33: His saying: 33- Say, ‘My Lord has only forbidden immoralities’ is the plural of immorality. Its interpretation has already been presented, what is apparent of it and what is concealed, meaning what is declared of it and what is concealed. It has been said that it is specific to the immoralities of fornication, but there is no basis for that. Sin includes every disobedience that results in sin. It has been said that it is specifically alcohol, and from this is the saying of the poet: I drank sin until my mind went astray, so sin takes away the mind And the same is said by another: He drinks sin openly by the measure A group of scholars have denounced those who made the sin specific to wine. Al-Nahhas said: As for the sin being wine, that is not known, and its reality is that it is all sins, as the poet said: I found the matter to be guided by the fear of God and its evil is sin. Al-Farra’ said: Sin is anything less than the truth and oppression of people. End quote. And there is nothing in the application of sin to wine that indicates that it is specific to it, as it is one of the sins that can be applied to it. He said in Al-Sahah: Wine may be called a sin, and he recited: I drank the sin The house, and thus Al-Harawi recited it before it in his strange poem. His saying: And oppression without right meaning injustice that exceeds the limit, and he mentioned it alone after it was included in what came before it because it is a great sin like his saying: And he forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression “And that you associate with God that for which He has not sent down authority” meaning that you make a partner for God for which He has not sent down proof. What is meant is mocking the polytheists, because God does not send down proof that someone other than Him is a partner with Him, And that you say about God that which you do not know of its reality and that God said it, and this is like what they used to attribute to God, the Most High, of the permissible and forbidden things that He did not permit. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, Al-Nasa’i and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that women used to circumambulate naked, unless a woman put a rag over her private parts and said: Today some or all of it appears, and whatever appears of it I do not permit. Then the verse, Take your adornment for every masjid was revealed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: Men used to circumambulate the House naked, so God commanded them to adorn themselves. Adornment is clothing, what covers the private parts, and other good things and goods. Ibn Adi, Abu Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take your adornment for prayer. They said: What is the adornment for prayer? He said: Put on your sandals and pray in them. Al-Uqayli, Abu Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Anas from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the verse, Take your adornment for every masjid, he said: Pray in your sandals. There are many hadiths that indicate the permissibility of praying in sandals. As for whether this is the interpretation of the verse as narrated in these two hadiths, I do not know how their chains of transmission are. It has been reported that a man is forbidden to pray in a single garment with nothing of it on his shoulders, and this is in the two Sahihs and others from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: God has permitted eating and drinking as long as it is not extravagance or vanity. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding His statement: Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess, he said: In food and drink. Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Shu'ab on the authority of Amr ibn Shu'ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Eat, drink, give charity and dress without vanity or extravagance, for God, the Exalted, loves to see the effect of His blessings on His servant. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Quraysh used to circumambulate the House naked, whistling and clapping. Then God revealed: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God?” So they were commanded to wear clothes. “Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world, exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.” He said: They benefit from them in this world, and no sin will follow them on the Day of Resurrection. Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: “Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world.” He said: The polytheists share with the believers in the adornment of this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be exclusively for the believers, not the polytheists. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the good things of provision. He said: Fat, meat and butter. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to forbid things that God had permitted, such as clothing and other things. This is the saying of God: “Say: Have you seen what God has sent down to you of provision, then you have made of it lawful and unlawful?” This is this, then God revealed: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision? Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world.” Meaning, the Muslims shared with the infidels the good things in the life of this world, so they ate from their good food, wore their best clothes, and married their righteous women. Then God will keep the good things in the Hereafter for those who believe, and the polytheists will have nothing in them. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: What appeared of it was the cart, and what was hidden was fornication, and they used to circumambulate the House naked. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: What appeared of it was the circumambulation of the Jahiliyyah, which was shameful, and what was hidden was fornication. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And sin, meaning disobedience. And oppression, meaning that one oppresses people unjustly.
7:34: His statement: 34- And for every nation is a term meaning a specific, limited time in which their punishment from God descends or in which He causes them to die. The verse may be interpreted as more general than both matters, and the pronoun in their term refers to every nation: meaning when the term of every nation comes, what He has decreed for them will occur in that term, they will not delay it an hour nor advance it an hour. Abu al-Su'ud said that his statement, nor will they advance it is in a position to they will delay it, but not to clarify the denial of advancement while it is possible in itself like delay, but rather to exaggerate the denial of delay by arranging it in the chain of the rationally impossible. It was said that what is meant by coming is nearness such that it is possible to advance in the sentence like the coming of the day that was set for their destruction an hour of it, but it is not that. Ibn Sirin read their terms in the plural, and he mentioned the hour specifically because it is the least of the names of times. The have used this verse as evidence that every dead person dies at his appointed time, even if his death was by murder, falling, or something similar. The discussion of this is very long. An example of this verse is the Almighty’s saying: No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it.
7:35: His saying: 35- O children of Adam, if there come to you the verse, in is the conditional and ma is redundant for emphasis, and for this reason the verb requires the emphatic nun, and the meaning of the story has already been presented, and the meaning is: If there come to you messengers from among you who inform you of My rulings and explain them to you, then whoever fears God and amends that is, fears the disobedience of God and amends his condition by following the messengers and answering them, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve. This conditional sentence is the answer to the first condition, and it was said: Its answer is what the speech indicates: that is, if there come to you messengers from among you who narrate to you My verses, then obey them. The first is more appropriate, and Al-Zajjaj said the same.
7:36: 36- And those who denied Our signs which Our messengers told them and were arrogant about responding to them and acting upon what is in them they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally they will not leave it because of their disbelief in denying the signs and the messengers.
7:37: 37- So who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God or denies His signs? That is, no one is more unjust than him, and its investigation has already been presented. The reference in His statement: Those to the arrogant deniers will receive their share of the Book that is, from what God has written for them of good and evil. It has been said: They will receive from the punishment according to the extent of their disbelief. It has been said: The Book here is the Qur'an because the punishment of the disbelievers is mentioned in it. It has been said: It is the Preserved Tablet. His statement: Until, when Our messengers come to them that is, until a limit which is this, and the phrase They take their souls is in the accusative case as a state. What is meant by the messengers here is the Angel of Death and his helpers. It has been said that here even is for the beginning, but it is not hidden that its being for the beginning of the speech after it does not contradict its being the end of what came before it. The question in His statement, Where are those you used to call upon besides God? is for rebuke and rebuke: that is, where are the gods you used to call upon besides God and worship? The phrase They said, ‘They have gone astray from us’ is a resumption with the estimation of a question that it occurred as an answer to: that is, they have gone away from us and disappeared so we do not know where they are? And they testified against themselves that they were disbelievers. That is, they admitted disbelief against themselves.
7:38: His saying: 38- He said, 'Enter among nations that have passed away before you' The speaker is God, the Almighty, and in means with: that is, with nations. It was said: It is in its place, and the meaning is: Enter among them. It was said: It is the saying of Malik, the keeper of Hellfire, and what is meant by the nations that have passed away before them from the jinn and mankind are the disbelievers from the two groups of past nations. Whenever a nation enters from the past nations, it curses its sister meaning the other nation that preceded it to Hellfire, and it is made a sister to it in terms of religion, or misguidance, or being in Hellfire. Until when they overtake therein meaning they overtake each other. Overtaking means following one another, succession, and gathering in Hellfire. Al-A'mash read they overtook according to the original without assimilation. Ibn Mas'ud read until when they overtook one another meaning they overtook one another. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr that he read by cutting off the alif of connection, as if he paused on the word if for remembrance, and when his pause was prolonged, he cut off the alif of connection as if he were beginning with it, and it is like the saying of the poet: Oh soul, be patient, every living thing will meet another, and every two will have to part. Their last ones will say to their first ones: meaning their last ones entering the first ones entering, and it was said their last ones: meaning their lowest ones and their followers to their first ones to their leaders and elders, and this is the first as indicated by Our Lord, these have led us astray because the ones who lead astray are the leaders. It is possible that it is meant that they led them astray because they followed them and imitated their religion after them, so the first interpretation is correct, because their last ones followed the religion of their first ones. His statement: Then give them a double punishment from the Fire is the double that is added to its like once or times, and similar to it is His statement, the Most High: Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse and it was said: the double here is snakes and serpents, and the phrase He said to each double is a new sentence in response to an implied question, and the meaning is for each group of you double the punishment: meaning the first group and the other group but you do not know what each type of punishment is.
7:39: 39- And the first of them will say to the last of them, meaning the predecessors will say to the successors, or the followers will say to the followers, Then you had no superiority over us, rather we are equal in disbelief in God and deserving His punishment. So taste the punishment of the Fire as we tasted it for what you used to earn of disobeying God and disbelieving in Him. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Khatib and Ibn Al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ who said: We discussed the extension of lifespan in the presence of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and we said: Whoever maintains kinship ties will have his lifespan extended. He said: His lifespan will not be extended. God the Almighty says: {Then when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it}. Rather, a man will have righteous offspring, and they will supplicate to God after him, and that will be what will extend his lifespan. In another version: Their supplications will reach him in his grave, and that will be the extension of his lifespan. This hadith should be revealed in its chain of transmission, because it is a strange jurist. There are authentic hadiths in the two Sahihs and others that contradict it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah who said: Al-Hasan used to say: How foolish these people are! They say: O God, prolong his life, while God says: {Then when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it}. And Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab who said: When Umar was stabbed, Kaab said: If he had supplicated to God, He would have delayed his lifespan. So it was said to him: Didn’t God say: And when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it? Kaab said: And God said: And no one is granted a long life, nor is his lifespan diminished except in a book. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Those will receive their share of the Book, he said: What is destined for them of good and evil. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse: Of the deeds, whoever does good will be rewarded for it, and whoever does evil will be rewarded for it. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority: Their share of misery and happiness. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: What was previously written. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Ka’b regarding the verse: His provision, his life span and his deeds. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Salih regarding the verse: From the torment. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: It has passed away, he said: It has passed away. Whenever a nation entered, it cursed its sister, he said: Whenever the people of a religion entered, they cursed their companions for that, the polytheists declared the polytheists, the Jews the Jews, the Christians the Christians, the Sabians the Sabians, and the Magians the Magians. The last one curses the first one, until, when they all overtake therein, the last of them, who were in the end of time, will say to the first of them, who were prescribed that religion for them, Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment in the Fire. He will say to each double, the first and the last, And the first of them will say to the last of them, “You had no superiority over us, and you have gone astray as we have gone astray. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: A double punishment, he said: Doubled. He will say to each double, he said: Doubled. And regarding his statement: You had no superiority over us, he said: A lightening of the punishment.
7:40: His saying: 40- The gates of heaven will not be opened for them. Ibn Abbas, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read it with the fatha on the lower case because the feminine of the plural is not real, so it is permissible to make it masculine. The rest read it with the fatha on the upper case because of the feminine. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read it with the fatha on the lower case. The rest read it with emphasis, and the meaning is: that the gates of heaven will not be opened for their souls if they die. This meaning is indicated by what came in the authentic hadiths that when the angels reach the soul of the disbeliever to the lowest heaven they ask for permission, but the gates of heaven will not be opened for them. It was said: the gates of heaven will not be opened for their supplications if they supplicate, as Mujahid and Al-Nakha’i said. It was said: for their deeds, meaning they are not accepted, rather they are returned to them and they are struck in their faces. It was said: the meaning is: that the gates of heaven will not be opened for them so that they enter it, because heaven is in heaven, so according to this statement the conjunction of the phrase and they will not enter heaven is from the conjunction of interpretation. There is no objection to interpreting the verse as including souls, supplication, and deeds, and it is not contradicted by what was reported that the gates of heaven will not be opened for any of these, because that does not indicate that they will be opened for anything else that falls under the generality of the verse. His saying: And they will not enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle means that these disbelieving, arrogant infidels will not enter Paradise under any circumstances, and that is why He linked it to the impossible, so He said: Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle and it will never pass, and He mentioned the camel specifically because it is used as an example of greatness of self, and He mentioned the eye of the needle, which is the eye of the needle, specifically because it is extremely narrow, and the male camel is the camel and the plural is jamal and ajmal and jamalat, and it is only called a camel if it has four. Ibn Abbas read the camel with a damma on the jim and a fatha on the mim with a shaddah, and it is the rope of the ship which is called al-qals and it is a group of ropes, said Tha'lab, and it was said: the thick rope of hemp, and it was said: the rope by which one climbs the palm trees. Sa'id ibn Jubayr read the camel with a damma on the jim and a light mim. It is also al-qals. Abu al-Sammak read the camel with a damma on the jim and a sukoon on the mim. It was also read with a damma on both of them. Abdullah bin Masoud read: Until the smallest camel passes through the eye of a needle. It was read in the eye with the three vowels. The eye is every small hole, and from it comes the eye of a needle. The tailor is what is sewn with, and it is said: a tailor and a needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals. That is, like that terrible recompense, We recompense the criminals: that is, a type of criminal. Its investigation has been presented above.
7:41: And the mattress: the bedding, and the plural of Ghashiyah: meaning fires that cover them from above like blankets 41- And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers meaning, like that great recompense, We recompense whoever is characterized by the characteristic of injustice.
7:42: His statement: 42- We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity meaning, We do not charge the servants except with what is within their capacity and that they are able to do, and We do not charge them with what is not within their capacity. This sentence is parenthetical between the subject and the predicate, and similar to it is God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. Al-A'mash read Takkalluf with the superlative and raised the soul, and the reference in his statement: Those is to the relative pronoun, and its predicate is the companions of Paradise and the sentence is the predicate of the relative pronoun, and the sentence They will abide therein eternally is in the accusative case as a state.
7:43: His statement: 43- "And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment." This is among the blessings that God will bestow upon the people of Paradise, that God will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment toward one another until their hearts are pure and they will love one another. If resentment remained in their hearts as it was in this world, it would spoil the delights of Paradise, because neither of the quarreling parties will enjoy life with the other. Resentment is the hidden hatred in the chests, and say that removing resentment in Paradise means that they will not envy one another in the difference in status. "And they will say, 'Praise be to God, Who has guided us to this.'" That is, to this great reward, which is eternal life in Paradise, and removing resentment from their hearts. This guidance for this is guidance for its cause of faith and righteous deeds in this world. "And we would never have been guided." Ibn Amir read without the waw, and the rest read without it, and we could not have been guided by this matter had it not been for God’s guidance to us. The sentence is a new sentence or a state, and the answer to had it not been for God’s guidance to us is omitted and indicated by what preceded it: i.e. had it not been for God’s guidance to us, we would not have been guided. His statement: Indeed, the messengers of our Lord have come with the truth al-Lām is the lam of the oath. They said: This is when they reached the great reward they reached, rejoicing in what they had become because of what came before them of believing the messengers and the appearance of the truth of what they had told them in this world, that the reward for faith and righteous deeds is this which they had become. His statement: And it will be proclaimed to them, ‘This is Paradise, which you have inherited for what you used to do’ al-Baqarah 2:177, i.e. the call was made to those who believed and did righteous deeds, and it was said to them: This is Paradise, which you have inherited: i.e. you have inherited its dwellings through your deeds. It was said in al-Kashshaf: Because of your deeds, not by favor, as the falsifiers say. End quote. I say: O poor man, this is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in what is authentically reported from him: Straighten your path and come close, and know that no one will enter Paradise through his deeds. They said: Not even you, O Messenger of God? He said: Not even me, unless God covers me with His mercy. Explaining a reason does not necessitate denying another reason. Were it not for the favor of God, the Most High, upon the worker by enabling him to do the work, there would be no work at all. If the favor were only in this ability, then those who say it would be right, not false. In the Qur’an: That is the favor of God, and in it: Then He will admit them into His mercy and favor. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, meaning that nothing of their deeds will ascend to God. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from him that he said: Their deeds and supplications will not be opened for them. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh also narrated from him regarding the verse that he said: Their souls will not be opened, but it will be opened for the souls of the believers. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him that until a camel passes through, he said: one with legs, “into the eye of a needle,” he said: into the eye of a needle. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saeed ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Mas’ud regarding his statement: until a camel passes through, he said: the pair of a female camel. Abu Ubayd, Saeed ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated through various chains of transmission from Ibn Abbas that he used to recite al-jamal with a damma on the jim and a shaddah on the mim. He said: It is a thick rope or one of the ropes of ships. Abdul bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar that he was asked about the eye of a needle and he said: A camel in the eye of a needle. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: A mattress is a bedding and a blanket is a quilt. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib that he said: By God, this verse was revealed about us, the people of Badr: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment. An-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Everyone in Hell will see his place in Paradise and say, ‘If only God had guided us.’ This will be a regret for them. And every person in Paradise will see his place in Hell and say, ‘If only God had guided us.’ This is their gratitude.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Hamid, al-Darimi, Muslim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id and Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And it will be announced to them, ‘This is Paradise which you have inherited because of what you used to do.’ He said: It will be announced to them, Be healthy and do not get sick, be comfortable and do not become miserable, be young and do not grow old, and live forever and do not die.
7:44: The calling of the people of Paradise to the people of Hell was not intended to inform them of what they called them, but rather to make them cry and cause regret in their hearts. 44- Indeed we have found is the same call: that is, we have reached what God promised us of bliss, so have you reached what God promised you of painful torment? The question is for rebuke and rebuke, and the second object of the promise was omitted because the promise was not specifically for them, but for all people, such as resurrection, accountability, and punishment. It was said: It was omitted to remove the disbelievers from the rank of honor by addressing them when making the promise. They said, 'Yes,' meaning we found what our Lord promised us to be true. Al-A'mash and Al-Kisa'i read Yes with a kasra on the 'ayn. Makki said: Whoever says: Yes with a kasra on the 'ayn, it is as if he wanted to differentiate between the 'yes' which is an answer and the 'yes' which is a name for cows, sheep, and camels. The muezzin: the crier, that is, a crier called between them: that is, between the two groups. It was said: he is from the angels, that the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Al-Bazzi read with a shaddah on an, which is the original. The rest read with a lightened an, as if it were the lightened form of the heavy form or the explanatory form. Al-A’mash read with a kasrah on the hamza of in, as if the statement was implied.
7:45: And the sentence 45- Those who hinder [people] from the way of God is an attribute of the oppressors, and it is permissible to raise and lower the sentence on the basis of their omission, or I mean. And hindering: prevention: that is, they prevent people from following the path of truth and seek to make it crooked that is, they seek to make it crooked: that is, they turn people away from it and cast doubt on its straightness by saying that it is not true and that the truth is what it is in, and crookedness with the kasra in meanings and entities is what is not erect, and with the fatha is what is erect like a spear, and the sentence and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter is in the accusative case as a state.
7:46: His statement: 46- And between them is a veil meaning between the two groups or between Heaven and Hell. The veil is the wall mentioned in the Almighty's statement: And a wall will be placed between them. His statement: And on the heights are men al-A’raf 7:the plural of 'arf, and they are the balconies of the wall placed between them, and from it comes the 'arf of the horse and the 'arf of the rooster. Al-A'raf in the language means a high place, and this statement is outside the context of praise as in His statement: Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God. Scholars differed about who the people of A'raf are. It was said: They are the martyrs, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri and Shurahbil bin Sa'd. It was also said: They are the virtuous believers who have finished their own business and devoted themselves to studying the conditions of the people, as mentioned by Mujahid. It was also said: They are a people of prophets, as mentioned by Al-Zajjaj. It was also said: They are a people whose good and bad deeds are equal, as said by Ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha'bi, Al-Dahhak, and Sa'id bin Jubayr. It was also said: They are Al-Abbas, Hamza, Ali, and Ja'far Al-Tayyar. They know their lovers by the whiteness of their faces and their haters by the blackness of their faces, as narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was also said: They are the just ones on the Day of Resurrection who testify against the people about their deeds and they are in every nation, and this statement was chosen by Al-Nahhas. It was also said: They are the children of fornication, as narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was also said: They are angels assigned to this Surah who distinguish the disbelievers from the believers before they enter Paradise and Hell, as mentioned by Abu Majlaz. The phrase They know each by their mark is an attribute of men. The distinctive mark: meaning they will recognize both the people of Paradise and Hell by their marks, such as the whiteness and blackness of their faces, or the places of ablution of the believers, or a mark that God makes for each group in that situation by which the men of A'raf will recognize the happy ones from the wretched. And the companions of Paradise will call out to them, meaning the men of A'raf will call out to the companions of Paradise when they see them, “Peace be upon you,” meaning they will call out to them by saying, “Peace be upon you,” as a greeting, honor, and good report, or they will inform them of their safety from punishment. His statement, They did not enter it while they were hoping, meaning the companions of A'raf did not enter Paradise while they were hoping to enter it. It was said that the meaning of they were hoping is that they know that they will enter it, and this is well-known among the linguists: hope means knowledge, as mentioned by Al-Nahhas. This statement, I mean that they are the people of A'raf, is narrated from a group of people, including Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud. Abu Majlaz said: They are the people of Paradise: meaning that the people of A'raf will say to them, “Peace be upon you,” while the people of Paradise have not entered it while they were hoping to enter it.
7:47: His saying: 47- And when their sight is turned toward the companions of the Fire meaning when the sight of the people of the A’raf is turned toward the companions of the Fire: meaning toward the companions, the meaning of toward continues to be the direction of meeting, which is the direction of confrontation, and no source came on the form of tafa’al with a kasra on the first letter except for two sources, one of them is this, and the other is tabyan, and what is besides them is with a fatha they said meaning the people of the A’raf said: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people they asked God not to place them among them.
7:48: 48- And the companions of the A'raf will call out to men from the disbelievers whom they will recognize by their mark that is, by their signs They will say instead of call out "What availed you was your gathering" that you were gathering to obstruct the path of God, and the question is for rebuke and rebuke, His saying: "And you were not arrogant". "What" is a source: that is, "And what availed you was your arrogance.
7:49: 49- Are these the ones you swore that God would not grant them mercy? This is from the words of the people of al-A’raf 7:meaning they said to the disbelievers, pointing to the Muslims who had gone to Paradise, this statement. The disbelievers used to swear in this world when they saw the weak Muslims with this oath, and this is a rebuke to the disbelievers and a disappointment to them. His statement: Enter Paradise, no fear will there be upon you, nor will you grieve. This is the complete words of the people of al-A’raf 7:meaning they said to the Muslims, enter Paradise, for fear and grief have disappeared from you after entering. Talhah bin Musarraf read enter with a kasra on the kha. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: We have found what our Lord promised us to be true, he said: of bliss and honor. Have you then found what your Lord promised to be true? he said: of disgrace, humiliation and torment. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood at the well of Badr, he recited this verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: And between them is a veil, he said: It is the wall, which is al-A’raf. It was called al-A’raf because its companions would recognize the people. Sa’id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah who said: al-A’raf is a wall between Paradise and Hell. Abd al-Razzaq, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba’th wa al-Nushur on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: al-A’raf is the elevated thing. Al-Faryabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on his authority that al-A’raf is a wall with a crest like a rooster’s crest. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: Al-A'raf are mountains between Paradise and Hell, so they are on their peaks, meaning on their peaks. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it is a hill between Paradise and Hell, on which some sinners were detained. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: They claimed that it is the Sirat. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah who said: The people of Al-A'raf are people who did deeds by which God saved them from the Hellfire, and they are the last to enter Paradise. They have known the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud that they are those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal and they will stand on the Sirat. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Hudhayfah.
