Abd Al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on his authority. Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Zur’ah bin Amr bin Jarir who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the people of Al-A’raf. He said: They are the last of the servants to be judged. When the Lord of the Worlds finishes judging between the servants, He says: You are a people whose good deeds have taken you out of the Fire, but you have not entered Paradise. So you are My freedmen, so go from Paradise wherever you wish.” Ibn Kathir said: This is a good mursal. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th on the authority of Hudhayfah who I think said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and the people of Paradise will be ordered to Paradise, and the people of Hell will be ordered to Hell. Then the people of Al-A’raf will be told: What are you waiting for? They will say: We are waiting for your command. It will be said to them: Your good deeds have taken you beyond the Fire so that you do not enter it, and your sins have stood between you and Paradise, so enter with My forgiveness and mercy.” Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Mani', Abd bin Hameed, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba'th narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Al-Muzani who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the people of Al-A'raf. He said: They are people who were killed in the cause of God in disobedience to their fathers. What prevented them from the Fire was their killing in the cause of God, and what prevented them from Paradise was their disobedience to their fathers." Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, with a similar chain of transmission. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba'th on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Harith bin Abi Usamah narrated in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Abdullah bin Malik Al-Hilali on the authority of his father, with a similar chain of transmission. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a similar chain of transmission. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of a man from Muzaynah, with a similar chain of transmission. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah bin Muhammad bin Ammar that he was asked about His statement: They did not enter it, while they were hoping to, he said: The angels greeted them even though they had not entered it, and they were hoping to enter it when it was greeted. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: The people of the A’raf will recognize people by their marks, the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces and the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces. So when they pass by a group that is being taken to Paradise, they will say: “Peace be upon you,” and when they pass by a group that is being taken to the Fire, they will say: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the people of the A’raf will call out to men, he said: in the Fire, “whom they will recognize by their marks. They will say: ‘Your multitude and your being arrogant have availed you nothing,” he said: God will say to the people of arrogance: Are these the ones about whom you swore that God would not grant them mercy? meaning the people of the A’raf. Enter Paradise, no fear concerning you, nor will you grieve.
7:50: His saying: 50- Pour out upon us some water. Pouring out means expansion. It is said: He poured out His blessings upon him. They asked them to console them with some water or with something from what God had provided them with other than it, from drinks or foods. They responded by saying: God has forbidden them both meaning water and what God had provided them with other than it to the disbelievers. So we will not console you with anything from what God has forbidden you. It was said: This call from the people of Hell was after the people of Al-A’raf had entered Paradise.
7:51: And the sentence 51- those who took their religion as amusement and play is in the accusative case as an attribute of the disbelievers. The explanation of amusement, play, and deception has already been presented. His statement: So today We will forget them means We will leave them in the Fire as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs the kaf is an attribute of a deleted source, and ma is a source: meaning forgetfulness as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs. His statement: And they did not deny Our signs is in apposition to what they forgot: meaning as they forgot, and as they used to deny Our signs: meaning they rejected them.
7:52: The lam in 52- And We have certainly brought them is the answer to the oath. What is meant by the book is the genus, if the pronoun refers to all the disbelievers, and if it refers to the contemporaries of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then what is meant by the book is the Qur'an, and the explanation is clarification, and with knowledge is in the accusative case as a state: meaning knowing the state of it being guidance for the believers and a mercy for them. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: It is permissible to say guidance and mercy in the accusative case as an attribute of the book.
7:53: His saying: 53- Do they await anything but its interpretation? with the hamza from Al, and the people of Medina conceal the hamza. And the waiting is: do they await anything but what they were promised in the book of punishment that the matter will end up with, and it was said: its interpretation is its reward, and it was said: its consequence. And the meanings are close. And the day is an adverb to say: which day does its interpretation come, and it is the Day of Resurrection Those who forgot it before will say that is, they left it before its interpretation came The messengers of our Lord have come with the truth that God sent them to us So will we have any intercessors? An interrogative from them, and its meaning is a wish so that they may intercede for us is accusative because it is an answer to the interrogative. His saying: Or are we sent back? Al-Farra' said: The meaning is or are we sent back so that we may do other than what we used to do. Al-Zajjaj said: We are sent back is in apposition to the meaning: meaning will anyone intercede for us or are we sent back. Ibn Abi Ishaq read or we return and we work in the accusative case, like the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: I told him, "Don't cry. We are trying to become king or die and be excused." Al-Hasan read it with the nominative case, and the meaning of the verse is: Do we have intercessors who will save us from the torment we are in, or will we be returned to this world so that we may do good deeds other than the sins we used to do? They have lost themselves meaning they did not benefit from them, so their souls were a trial and a trial for them, as if they had lost them as a merchant loses his capital. It was said: They lost the bliss and the portion of their souls. And what they used to invent has vanished from them meaning their invention or what they used to invent. The meaning is that their lie that they used to say in this world has become invalid, or what they used to make a partner with God has disappeared from them, so it did not benefit them or attend with them.
7:54: His saying: 54- Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days. This is a type of the wonder of God's creation and the greatness of His power and His uniqueness in creation, which obliges the servants to unify Him and worship Him. The root of six is six, the taa' was replaced from one of the two sins and the dal was assimilated into it. The evidence for this is that you say in the diminutive form sadisa, and in the plural asdas, and you say someone came sixth. And today is from sunrise to sunset. It was said: These days are from the days of this world, and it was said: From the days of the Hereafter. These six days begin on Sunday and end on Friday, and He, glory be to Him, is able to create them in a single moment. He says to them, Be, and they are. But He wanted to teach His servants gentleness and deliberation in matters, or He created them in six days because everything has a term with Him. And in another verse: And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness. His saying: Then He rose over the Throne: Scholars have differed on the meaning of this into fourteen opinions, the most correct and most deserving of being the doctrine of the righteous predecessors, that He, glory be to Him, rose over him without asking how, but in the manner that befits Him, while being free from that which is not permissible for Him. And rising in the language of the Arabs means elevation and stability. Al-Jawhari said: He rose over the back of his beast: meaning he settled down. And he rose to the sky: meaning he ascended. And he rose: meaning he took control and appeared. And from this is the saying of the poet: Bashar has taken over Iraq without sword or bloodshed. The man became straight: that is, his youth ended. He became straight: that is, he became balanced and balanced. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah that the meaning of he became straight here is: he rose, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: He brought them to the water of Thaqif in a desert, and the Yemeni star had risen and become straight. That is, elevated and raised. And the throne. Al-Jawhari said: It is the king’s bed. The throne is used for other meanings, including the throne of the house: its roof, the throne of the well: its covering with wood, and the throne of the fish: four small planets, and it is used for the king, the sultan, and glory. From this, Zuhair said: You two overtook Abs, whose throne had fallen, and Dhubyan, whose sandals had slipped under their feet. And the other said: If they kill you, their thrones will be destroyed by Otaiba bin Al-Harith bin Shihab. And the other said: They saw my throne with its sides cracked, so when it was cracked, they singled me out. It has been proven in the authentic hadiths the description of the Throne of the Most Gracious and its encompassing of the heavens and the earth and what is between them and what is above them, and this is what is meant here. His statement, He makes the night cover the day, means that He makes the night like a veil over the day, covering its light with its darkness. Asim, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read Yaghshy with a shaddah, while the rest read it with a tafsir. These are two dialects. It is said: aghshy yaghshy, and ghashy yaghshy. The original meaning of to clothe is to dress something with something else. In this verse, Yaghshy al-layl bi-day is not mentioned, as one of the two matters is sufficient instead of the other, like the statement of the Most High: garments that protect you from the heat. Humayd ibn Qays read Yaghshy al-layl wa al-nahar He covers the night and the day as ascribing the action to the night. The location of this sentence is the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is: He rose over the throne, covering the night with the day. And so is his saying: He seeks it hastily as a state of al-Layl 92:that is, the state of the night seeking the day with a hastily seeking that does not cease at all. And hastily is an attribute of a deleted source, that is, He seeks it with a hastily seeking: or a state of the subject of He seeks. And hastily means to hasten and to speed. It is said He turned away hastily: that is, in a hurry. His saying: And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Al-Akhfash said: It is conjoined with the heavens. Ibn Amir read them all in the nominative case as the subject and the predicate. The meaning according to the first is: And He created the sun, the moon, and the stars while they were subjected. And according to the second: The report about these being subjected. His saying: Indeed, His is the creation and the command. This is an announcement from Him, the Most High, to His servants that they are His, and creation is the created, and the command is His speech, which is Be in His saying: Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, “Be, and it is.” Or what is meant by the command is what He commands in detail, or the disposition of His creations. And when He, the Most High, mentioned in this verse the creation of the heavens and the earth in that short period, then He mentioned His establishment on His throne and the subjection of the sun, moon, and stars, and that His is the creation and the command. He said: Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds, meaning His blessings are abundant and extensive, and from this the thing is blessed and blessed in it, thus said Ibn Arafah. Al-Azhari said about Blessed its meaning is exalted and great. And the explanation of Lord of the worlds has been presented in full in Al-Fatihah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise. He said: A man will call out to his brother and say: O my brother, help me, for I have been burned. So pour some water on me. It will be said: Answer him. He will say: God has forbidden them both to the disbelievers. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you, he said: Food. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding the verse: They ask them for water and food. Regarding his statement: God has forbidden them both to the disbelievers, he said: The food and drink of Paradise. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So this Day We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs, he said: We will leave them in the Fire as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: So today We will forget them, he said: We will delay them. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: Do they await anything but its interpretation? he said: Its consequence. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The Day its interpretation comes is its recompense. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, The Day its interpretation comes he said: The Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They did not invent, he said: They did not lie in this world. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He rose over the Throne, the how is not comprehensible, and the rising over it is not unknown, and acknowledging it is faith, and denying it is disbelief. Al-Lalaka’i narrated on the authority of Malik that a man asked him: How did He rise over the Throne? He said: The how is not comprehensible, and the rising over it is not unknown, and belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in his book Al-Du’aa’ and Al-Khatib in his history on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ali who said: I guarantee that whoever recites these twenty verses every night that God will protect him from every unjust ruler, every rebellious devil, every ferocious beast, and every hostile thief: Ayat Al-Kursi, three verses from Al-A’raf Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth and ten from the beginning of Surat Al-Saffat, and three verses from Al-Rahman, the first of which is O company of jinn and mankind and the end of Surat Al-Hashr. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ubaid bin Abi Marzouq who said: Whoever recites before going to sleep Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth the verse, an angel will spread his wings over him until morning and he will be protected from theft. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais, the companion of Omar bin Abdul Aziz, who said: A man from the people of Medina fell ill and a group of his companions came to visit him. One of them recited the entire verse, Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth, and the man was speechless, then he moved and sat up straight, then he prostrated that day and night until the next day, from the time he prostrated. His family said to him, Praise be to God, who has cured you. He said, “An angel was sent to me to take my soul, and when your companion recited the verse he recited, the angel prostrated and I prostrated with his prostration. This is when he raised his head, then he leaned over and passed away.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding His statement, The night covers the day, he said: The night covers the day, taking away its light and pursuing it quickly until it overtakes it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, who said: The night covers the day. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Briskly, he said: Quickly. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah regarding his statement: Is not His the creation and the command? He said: Creation is what is below the throne, and command is what is above that. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority that he said: Creation is creation, and command is speech.
7:55: God the Almighty commanded them to supplicate, and restricted that to the supplicant being humbly and secretly supplicating to Him, and the accusative 55- supplicating and secretly is in the state: meaning humbly and secretly supplicating to Him, or an attribute of a deleted source: meaning call upon Him with a supplication of humility and a secret supplication. Supplication comes from humility, which is humility, submission and submission, and secretly: keeping it secret, for that is more effective in cutting off the vein of hypocrisy and decisive in the core of what contradicts sincerity, then He explained that by saying: Indeed, He does not love transgressors meaning those who go beyond what they are commanded to do in supplication and in everything, so whoever goes beyond what God has commanded him to do in any of the things has transgressed, and God does not love transgressors, and going beyond is included in supplication in this generality as a primary inclusion. It is an aggression in supplication for the supplicant to ask for something he does not have, such as immortality in this world, or to attain what is impossible in itself, or to request to reach the stations of the prophets in the afterlife, or to raise his voice in supplication, crying out with it.
7:56: His statement: 56- And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation. God the Almighty forbade them from causing corruption on the earth in any way, whether little or much, including killing people, destroying their homes, cutting down their trees, and drowning their rivers. And corruption on the earth includes disbelief in God and falling into His disobedience. The meaning of after its reformation is after God has reformed it by sending messengers, revealing books, and establishing laws. His statement: And call upon Him in fear and hope. The parsing of these two meanings can be interpreted in the two previous meanings in in humility and fear. In it, it is prescribed for the supplicant to be fearful and anxious when he supplicates, hoping that God will answer his supplication, because if he combines fear and hope when supplicating, he will attain what he seeks. Fear is being disturbed by harm that one is not certain will not occur, and hope is anticipating the occurrence of beloved things. His saying: Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good. This is a statement from God Almighty that His mercy is near to His doers of good, whatever their type of goodness may be. In this is an encouragement for the servants to do good and an activation for them, for the nearness of this mercy, by which success is achieved in every desired goal of every servant of God’s worship. The scholars of language and grammar differed on the reason for the masculinization of the report of God’s mercy, where he said: close and did not say close. Al-Zajjaj said: Mercy is interpreted as womb because it means forgiveness and pardon. Al-Nahhas preferred this interpretation. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Mercy is a source meaning mercy, and the right source is to be masculine. Al-Akhfash Saeed said: He meant by mercy here rain, and the masculinization of some feminine is permissible. He recited: No rain, no thunder, no rain, no green land Abu Ubaidah said: The masculine form of qarib is based on the masculine form of place: that is, a place that is close. Ali bin Sulaiman Al-Akhfash said: This is wrong. If it were as he said, qarib would be in the accusative case, as you would say: Zaid is close to you. Al-Farra’ said: If qarib means distance, it is masculine or feminine, but if it means lineage, it is feminine, without any difference between them. It was narrated from Al-Farra’ that he said: It is said in relation to lineage, so-and-so is close, and in other than lineage, it is permissible to make the masculine or feminine, so it is said: Your house is close to us, and so-and-so is close to us. God the Almighty said: And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. And from this is the saying of Imru’ Al-Qais: Woe to you if I spend the night without Umm Hashim near, nor Basbasa, the daughter of Yashkur. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Zajjaj that Al-Farra’ was wrong in what he said and said: The way for the masculine and feminine is to follow their actions. It was said: Since the feminization of mercy is not real, it is permissible for its predicate to be masculine. He mentioned its essential meaning.
7:57: His statement: 57- And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy is in apposition to His statement: He covers the night with the day, which includes mentioning one of the blessings that He bestowed upon His servants, along with what is in that of evidence of His Oneness and the proof of His divinity. Riyyah is the plural of wind, and the root of wind is ruh. The people of the two sanctuaries and Abu Amr read Nashra with a damma on the nun and sun, the plural of nashir, in the sense of relation: meaning one who spreads. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Amir read Nashra with a damma on the nun and a sukoon on the shin from nashr. Al-A'mash, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read Nashra with a fatha on the nun and a sukoon on the shin as a source, and it is permissible for it to be a source in the place of a state, and the meaning of these readings goes back to the spreading, which is the opposite of folding, so it is as if the wind, when it is still, was folded and then sent from its folding so it becomes like an open wind. Abu Ubaidah said: Its meaning is scattered in its faces, in the sense that we spread it here and there. Asim read bashir with a unified ba and a sukoon on the shin, the plural of bashir, meaning the winds that herald rain. Similar to this is the Almighty’s statement: He sends the winds as good tidings. His statement: before His mercy here means the rain, meaning before His mercy. The meaning is that He, glory be to Him, sends the winds as spreaders or good tidings before the rain. His saying: Until it carried heavy clouds. Someone carried something: he carried it and lifted it. Clouds are both masculine and feminine. The meaning is: until the winds carried heavy clouds with the water that they began to carry. We drove it, meaning the clouds, to a dead land, meaning barren, with no vegetation. It is said: I drove it to such-and-such a land, or to such-and-such a land. It was said that the lam here is the lam of cause: meaning for a dead land, and the land is the inhabited place on earth. So We sent down water with it, meaning for the land for which We drove it. Or with the clouds: meaning We sent down the water that it carried. Or with the wind: meaning We sent down water with the wind sent before the rain. It was said that the ba’ here has the meaning of from, meaning We sent down water from it. So We brought forth with it, meaning with the water, of all fruits, meaning of all their types. His saying: Thus do We bring forth the dead means like that bringing forth, which is bringing forth the fruits. We bring forth the dead from the graves on the Day of Resurrection. That you may remember means that you may remember and know the greatness of God’s power and the wonder of His creation and that He is able to resurrect you just as He was able to bring forth the fruits that you see.
7:58: His saying: 58- And the good land - its vegetation comes forth by permission of its Lord. That is, the good soil - its vegetation comes forth by permission of God and His facilitation in a good, complete and complete way. And that which is bad - nothing comes forth except bad. That is, the bad soil - nothing brings forth its vegetation except bad: that is, there is no good in it. Talhah ibn Musarraf read Nakadan with a sukoon on the kaf. Ibn al-Qa'qa' read Nakadan with a fatha on the kaf: that is, of bad. The rest read Nakadan with a fatha on the noon and a kasra on the kaf. It was read Yakhruj meaning the land brings it forth. It was said Kaf: that is, of bad. The rest read Nakad with a fatha on the noon and a kasra on the kaf. It was read yakhruj meaning the country took him out. It was said: The meaning of the verse is the simile. God Almighty likened the one who is quick to understand to the good country, and the dull one to the bad country. This was mentioned by An-Nahhas. It was also said that this is a metaphor for hearts, so He likened the heart that is receptive to admonition to the good country and the one that is far from it to the bad country. This was said by Al-Hasan. It was also said: It is a metaphor for the heart of the believer and the hypocrite. This was said by Qatadah. It was also said: It is a metaphor for the good and bad among the children of Adam. This was said by Mujahid. Thus do We diversify the verses meaning like this diversion for a people who are grateful to God and acknowledge His blessings. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret. He said: The secret. He does not like transgressors in supplication or otherwise. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah, who said: Supplication is public and secret is a secret. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret, meaning submissive, and secretly means in humility and stillness regarding your needs in the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. He does not like transgressors, he said: Do not supplicate evil against the believing man or woman: O God, disgrace him and curse him and the like, for that is transgression. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Majlaz, regarding his statement, He does not like transgressors, he said: Do not ask about the stations of the prophets. Ibn Al-Mubarak, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: The Muslims used to strive hard in supplication, but no sound was heard from them. It was only a whisper between them and their Lord. This is because God says: Call upon your Lord in humility and in secret. This is because God mentioned a righteous servant and was pleased with his words, so He said: When he called upon his Lord a secret call. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Salih regarding His statement: And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation. He said: After the prophets and their companions had reformed it. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abu Sinan regarding the verse, he said: I have made lawful what I have made lawful and forbidden what I have forbidden, and I have set My boundaries, so do not corrupt them. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Call upon Him in fear and hope. He said: Out of fear of Him and hope for what is with Him. Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good. He means the believers, and whoever does not believe in God is among the corrupters. Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement, And it is He who sends the winds, that he said: God sends the wind and brings the clouds from between the two horizons, the edge of the sky and the earth from where they meet, and He brings them out from there, then He spreads them out and extends them in the sky as He wills, then He opens the gates of the sky and the water flows on the clouds, then He causes the clouds to rain after that. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, As good tidings before His mercy, that he said: People are gladdened by it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement, Before His mercy, that he said: It is the rain. Regarding his statement, Thus do We bring forth the dead, that he said: Thus will you be brought forth, and thus is the resurrection as the crops are brought forth by water. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Thus do We bring forth the dead. He said: When God wants to bring forth the dead, He sends rain from the sky until the earth splits open, then He sends the souls and each soul falls into its own body. Thus God brings the dead back to life with rain, just as He brings the earth back to life. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And the good land al-Baqarah 2:173, that it is an example that God gave for the believer, saying: It is good and its deeds are good, just as the fruit of a good land is good. And that which is bad al-Baqarah 2:173 He gave an example for the disbeliever, such as a salty, swampy land from which no blessing comes out. So the disbeliever is the bad one and his deeds are bad. Something similar to this was narrated from a group of the Tabi’un.
7:59: When God, the Almighty, explained the perfection of His power and the wonder of His creation in the previous verses, He mentioned here the stories of the nations and what they contain of warnings and threats against the infidels, to alert this nation to the truth and not to follow the example of those who opposed the truth from the previous nations. The lam is the answer to an omitted oath. He is the first of the messengers to the people of the earth after Adam. Noah was mentioned before in Al Imran, so there is no need to repeat it here. What was said about Idris coming before Noah, Ibn al-Arabi said: This is an illusion. Al-Mazari said: If what the historians mentioned is correct, it is based on the fact that Idris was a prophet who was not sent, and the sentence 59- So he said, O my people, worship God is an introductory sentence in answer to an implied question. His saying: You have no god other than Him This sentence is like the reason for his saying: Worship meaning worship Him because you have no god other than Him so that He deserves to be worshipped by you. Nafi`, Abu `Amr, `Asim, Hamzah, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn `Amir read ghayrihu in the nominative case as an adjective for the god in position. Al-Kisa’i read it in the genitive case throughout the Qur’an as an adjective in word. Al-Farra` and Al-Kisa’i permitted the accusative case as an exception: meaning, you have no god but Him. Abu `Amr said: I do not know of the genitive or accusative cases, and this is refuted by the fact that some of Banu Asad put ghayrihu in the accusative case in all cases, and from this is the saying of the poet: Nothing prevented drinking from it except the cooing of a dove in the branches of the Arqaal. The phrase I fear for you the punishment of a terrible Day is a phrase that includes an explanation of the command to worship: that is, if you do not worship Him, then I fear for you the punishment of the Day of Resurrection or the punishment of the Day of the Flood.
7:60: His statement: 60- The chiefs of his people said. An introductory sentence in response to an implied question. The chiefs are the nobles and leaders of the people. It was said: They are the men. Its explanation was presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. Misguidance: Deviating from the path of truth and departing from it: That is, we see you in your call to worship God alone in misguidance from the path of truth.
7:61: And sentence 61 - He said, O my people is also a resumption in response to an implied question There is no error in me as you claim but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds: He sent me to you to bring good to you and to ward off evil from you. He denied error from himself, and established for himself what is of a higher position and more honorable elevation, which is that he is the Messenger of God to them.
7:62: And the sentence 62- I convey to you the messages of my Lord is in the nominative case as an attribute of the Messenger, or it is a new sentence explaining the condition of the Messenger. And the messages: what God sent to them from what He revealed to him. And I advise you is in apposition to I convey to you. It is said: I advised him and I advised him, and the addition of the lam indicates exaggeration in the purity of the advice. Al-Asma'i said: The advisor: is the one who is free from rancor, and everything that is pure has advised, so the meaning of I advise here: I purify my intention for you from the impurities of corruption, and the noun is advice. And the sentence And I know from God what you do not know is in apposition to the sentence before it, confirming his message and explaining the increase of his knowledge, and that he is exclusively knowledgeable of things that they do not know by God informing him of that.
7:63: His saying: 63- Or were you amazed? The waw was opened because it is the conjunction, and the question hamza entered it to denounce them. And the conjoined to it is understood: as if it was said you rejected and were amazed or you lied and were amazed or you denied and were amazed that a reminder came to you from your Lord meaning a revelation and an admonition on a man from among you meaning on the tongue of a man from among you whom you know, and it was not on the tongue of someone you do not know or whose language you do not know. And it was said on means with: meaning with a man from among you so that he warns you with it and that you may fear what contradicts it and perhaps you will receive mercy because of what the warning to you and the fear from you benefit from being exposed to the mercy of God Almighty for you and His pleasure with you.
7:64: 64- So they denied him meaning after that they denied him and did not act upon the warning he brought, so We saved him and those with him of the believers in him who were settled with him in the ship, and We drowned those who denied Our signs and they continued in that and did not return to repentance. The phrase Indeed, they were a blind people is the reason for His statement: And We drowned meaning We drowned the deniers because they were blind of heart, and admonition was of no use to them and reminders were of no benefit to them. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Anas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The first prophet to be sent was Noah. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Abu Nu’aym and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Yazid Al-Raqashi who said: Noah was called Noah because of the length of time he mourned for himself. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: There were ten centuries between Adam and Noah, all of them following a law of truth. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik who said: The elite means the nobles of the people. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, If there comes to you a reminder from your Lord, meaning a statement from your Lord. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, they were a blind people, he said: disbelievers. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Indeed, they were a blind people, he said: About the truth.
7:65: His statement: 65- And to the people of 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud meaning, and We sent to the people of 'Aad their brother: that is, one of their tribe or their companion or he called him a brother because he was the son of Adam like them, and 'Aad is from the descendants of Sam, son of Noah. It was said: He is 'Aad, son of 'Aws, son of Iram, son of Shalih, son of Arfakhshad, son of Sam, son of Noah, and Hud is the son of Abdullah, son of Rabah, son of Al-Khulud, son of 'Aws, son of Iram, son of Shalih, son of Arfakhshad, son of Sam, son of Noah, and Hud is an explanatory apposition. He said, 'O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him.' The explanation of this has already been presented, and the question in Do you not then fear God? is for denial.
7:66: The interpretation of the assembly has also been presented, and foolishness, frivolity and stupidity. This has been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. They attributed it to frivolity and rashness, and they were not satisfied with that until they said 66- Indeed, we think you are among the liars, confirming their belief that he was lying in what he claimed of the message.
7:67: 67- He said, ‘O my people, there is no foolishness in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.’ Then he responded to them by denying any foolishness from him, and added from that that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds. The meaning of this was explained shortly.
7:68: And likewise the interpretation of 68- I convey to you the messages of my Lord was previously mentioned, and the meaning of the advisor and the trustworthy one known for his trustworthiness was presented.
7:69: The interpretation of 69- Or do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you to warn you was also mentioned in the story of Noah that preceded this story. His statement: And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah reminded them of a blessing from God upon them, which is that He made them successors after the people of Nuh 71:meaning He made them inhabitants of the land they were on, or He made them kings, and when is in the accusative case with remember and the mention was made for the time. What is meant is what was in it of succession on the earth for the purpose of exaggeration, because if something is worthy of mention at its time, then it is worthy of it a fortiori And He increased you in creation meaning height in creation and greatness of body in addition to what their fathers were like in bodies. Stories have been narrated from the predecessors about the greatness of the bodies of the people of Aad. His saying: So remember the favors of God. The favors are the plural of to, and among them are the blessing of succession on earth, and the expansion of creation, and other things that He bestowed upon them. The reminder was repeated to increase emphasis, and the favors are the blessings that you may succeed if you remember that, because remembering the blessing is a reason for giving thanks for it, and whoever gives thanks has succeeded.
7:70: His statement: 70- They said, 'Have you come to us so that we may worship God alone?' This is a denunciation from them of his call to worship God alone without their deities which they made partners with God. This was denounced to them because they found their fathers doing something contrary to what he called them to. And we will abandon what our fathers used to worship. That is, we will abandon what they used to worship. This is included in the group of things they denounced. His statement: Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful. This is a hastening from them of the punishment that Hud was threatening them with, due to the severity of their rebellion against God and their turning away from the path of truth and their distance from following the right path.
7:71: So he answered them by saying: 71- There has indeed befallen you from your Lord an abomination and wrath. He made what was expected as reality, warning of the certainty of its occurrence, as mentioned by the imams of meanings and rhetoric. It was said that the meaning of became is necessary. And the abomination is punishment. It was said that here it is rust on the heart due to the increase in disbelief. Then he denounced them for what happened from them of argument, and said: Do you argue with me about names? meaning the names of the idols that they used to worship? He made them names, because their names have no reality, rather calling them gods is false, so it is as if they do not exist and did not exist, rather only their names exist. You and your fathers named them, meaning you named your deities with them from yourselves, you and your fathers, and there is no reality to that. For which God has sent down no authority, meaning no argument with which you can argue for what you claim for them of false claims. Then he threatened them with the most severe threat, saying: Then wait, for I am with you among those who wait, meaning wait for what you asked for from The torment, for I am with you among those awaiting it, and it will inevitably befall you and will descend upon you without a doubt.
7:72: Then God Almighty informed us that He saved Hud and those who believed in Him from the punishment that befell those who disbelieved in Him and did not accept His message, and that He cut off the root of the people who denied, meaning He eradicated them all. The meaning of this has already been explained, and the sentence 72- and they were not believers is connected to they denied, meaning We eradicated these people who combined denial of Our signs with disbelief. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And to the people of ‘Aad We sent their brother Hud, he said: He was not their brother in religion, but he was their brother in lineage because he was from them, and that is why he was made their brother. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham, who said: The people of ‘Aad were between Yemen and Syria like an ant. Ibn ‘Asakir narrated on the authority of Wahb, who said: A man from ‘Aad was sixty cubits tall by their cubits, and the crown of a man was like a great dome, and the eyes of a man were such that wild beasts hatched in them, and so were their nostrils. ‘Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that they were twelve cubits tall. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawadir al-Usul on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from them was eighty cubits tall, and the barley among them was like the kidney of a cow, and a single pomegranate would be enough for ten people to sit in its peel. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on his authority: And He increased you in creation abundantly, he said: Strength. Abdullah bin Ahmed in Zawa'id al-Zuhd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: If a man from the people of Aad were to make a door from stones, even if five hundred of this nation gathered around him, they would not be able to carry him, and if one of them were to put his foot in the ground, it would enter. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The favors of God he said: God's blessings, and regarding his statement: Abomination he said: Anger. Ibn Asakir narrated that: When God sent the wind upon Aad, Hud and the believers with him secluded themselves in a pen, and nothing of the wind affected them except what softened the skin and pleased the souls, and it would pass by the wind and carry it between the sky and the earth and crush it with stones. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: And We cut off the root of those who denied he said: We exterminated them. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Asakir on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib who said: The grave of Hud is in Hadramaut in a red dune at the top of which is a lote tree. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Abi Al-Atika, who said: The qibla of the Damascus mosque is the grave of Hud. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: Hud lived for four hundred and seventy-two years.
7:73: His saying: 73- And to Thamud We sent their brother Salih is connected to what came before: meaning, and We sent to Thamud their brother, and Thamud is a tribe named after their father, who is Thamud bin Aad bin Iram bin Shalih bin Arfakhshad bin Sam bin Noah, and Salih is an explanatory apposition, and he is Salih bin Ubaid bin Asf bin Mashh bin Ubaid bin Hathir bin Thamud, and Thamud is not declined because it was made the name of the tribe. Abu Hatim said: It was not declined because it is foreign. An-Nahhas said: It is a mistake because it is from thamad, which means a small amount of water, and the reciters read Unquestionably, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord as a name for the tribe, and the dwellings of Thamud were in Al-Hijr between Al-Hijaz and Ash-Sham to Wadi Al-Qura. His statement: He said, ‘O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him.’ Its explanation has already been presented in the story of Noah. There has come to you a clear sign from your Lord, meaning a clear miracle, which is the she-camel being brought out from the solid rock. The phrase This is the she-camel of God, a sign for you, includes an explanation of the aforementioned sign, and the verb sign is in the accusative case as a state, and the agent in it is the meaning of a reference. In adding the she-camel to God, there is an honor and respect for her. His statement: Then leave her to graze in God’s land, meaning leave her to graze in God’s land, for she is God’s she-camel, and the earth is His land, so do not prevent her from what is not yours and you do not own it. And do not touch her, with anything bad, meaning do not expose her to any way that would harm her. His statement: Then a painful punishment will seize you, is the answer to the prohibition, meaning if you do not leave her to be touched with anything bad, a painful punishment will seize you, meaning severe pain.
7:74: His statement: 74- And remember when He made you successors after 'Aad meaning He made you successors on earth or made you kings in it, as mentioned in the story of Hud And settled you in the land meaning He made for you a home in it, which is the house you live in You take from its plains palaces meaning you take from the plains of the earth palaces, or this sentence explains the sentence: And settled you in the land, and the plains of the earth are its soil from which they make mud bricks and the like and build palaces with it And carve out the mountains, houses meaning you take in the mountains which are rocks houses in which you live, and because of their strength and the hardness of their bodies they carve out the mountains and make in them caves in which they live because the buildings and roofs would perish before their lives ended, and the accusative of houses is as a state understood or as a second object of you carve to include the meaning of you take. His statement: So remember the favors of God its explanation was mentioned in the story before this. His saying: And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption. Al-‘Uthī and ‘Uthū are two words, and its investigation has already been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it.
7:75: 75- The leaders of his people who were arrogant said: meaning the arrogant leaders of Salih's people said to the weak ones who were oppressed by the arrogant ones, and to those among them who believed is a substitute for those who were oppressed by repeating the preposition as a substitute for some of the whole, because among the weak ones there are those who are not believers. This is based on the pronoun of them referring back to those who were oppressed, so if it refers back to his people it would be a substitute for all of the weak ones, and the statement is: Do you know that Salih is a messenger from his Lord? They said this by way of mockery and ridicule. His statement: They said, 'Indeed, we are believers in that with which he was sent.' They answered them that they believed in his message, although the question of the arrogant ones to them was only about their knowledge, do you know about his message or not, in order to hasten to show what they have of faith and to draw attention to the fact that his being a messenger is a clear and obvious matter that does not need to be asked about.
7:76: So they responded in rebellion and stubbornness by saying: 76- "Indeed, we disbelieve in that in which you have believed." These moral sentences are said to be renewed because they are answers to implied questions, as was previously explained.
7:77: His saying: 77- So they hamstrung the she-camel. A hamstring means wounding, and it was said: cutting off a limb that affects the loss of life. It is said that the horse was hamstrung: if its legs were struck with a sword. It was also said that the origin of hamstring is: breaking the heel of the camel. Then the slaughter was called hamstring, because hamstringing is usually the cause of slaughter. Hamstringing was attributed to everyone, even though the one who hamstrung the she-camel was one of them, because they were satisfied with that and agreed to it. There was a difference of opinion about the one who hamstrung the she-camel, what was his name? It was said: Qidar bin Salaf, and other things were said. And they rebelled against the command of their Lord, meaning they were arrogant. It is said that someone was arrogant, and someone was rebellious if he did not obey. The harsh night is the intense darkness. And they said, 'O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you should be one of the messengers.' This is a hastening of the punishment and a request from them for the punishment to descend and the affliction to befall them.
7:78: 78- So the earthquake seized them meaning the tremor. It is said: the thing trembled, trembling, and its origin is movement with a sound, and from it the day the earthquake trembles, and it was said: it was a severe shout that tore their hearts apart and they became in their homes meaning their country crouching stuck to the ground on their knees and faces like a bird crouches, and the origin of the word juthum is for rabbits and the like, and it was said: for people and birds. What is meant is that they became in their homes dead and motionless.
7:79: 79- So he turned away from them Salih when he despaired of their answer and said to them this statement I have conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisers. It is possible that he said this statement to them after their death in the way of narrating their past condition, as happened from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he spoke to the people of the well of Badr after his death, or he said it to them when the punishment descended upon them, as if he was witnessing that and regretted what they had missed of faith and safety from the punishment, then he made it clear about himself that he had spared no effort in conveying the message to them and giving them pure advice, but they refused that and did not accept it from him, so the punishment became due to them, and what they denied and hastened befell them. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Tayyal that he said: Thamud said to Salih, Bring us a sign if you should be of the truthful. He said, Go out. So they went out to a hill on the ground and behold, it was laboring like a pregnant woman labors. Then it parted and the she-camel came out from its middle. Salih said to them, This is the she-camel of God as a sign for you. When they got tired of her, they hamstrung her. Then He said, ‘Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days.’ Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada that Salih said to them when they hamstrung the she-camel, Enjoy yourselves for three days. Then he said to them, The sign of your destruction is that your faces will become yellow tomorrow, red the next day, and black on the third day. So it became like that. When the third day came, they were certain of their destruction, so they shrouded themselves and embalmed themselves. Then the blast overtook them and killed them. The one who hamstrung the camel said: I will not kill her until you are all satisfied. So they would enter upon the woman in her chamber and say: Are you satisfied? She would say: Yes, and the boy, until they were all satisfied. Then he hamstrung her. Ahmad, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim (who authenticated it), and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) descended to Al-Hijr, he stood up and delivered a sermon, saying: O people, do not ask your Prophet about signs. The people of Salih asked their Prophet to send them a sign, so God sent them a she-camel. She used to come back from this pass and drink their water on the day she came, and they used to milk her milk like they used to take from her water on the day she left, and she used to come back from this pass. They rebelled against the command of their Lord and hamstrung her. So God promised them punishment after three days, and it was a promise from God that is not to be denied. Then the shout came to them, and God destroyed everyone of them in the east and west of the earth, except for a man who was in the sanctuary of God, so the sanctuary of God protected him from the punishment of God. It was said: O Messenger of God, who is he? He said: Abu Righal. When he left the sanctuary, what happened to his people happened to him. Ibn Kathir said: This hadith meets the conditions of Muslim. Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Abu al-Tayyib, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to it. Ahmad narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was at al-Hijr 15:‘Do not enter upon these people who are being punished unless you are weeping. If you are not weeping, then do not enter upon them, lest what befell them befall you.’” The original hadith is in the two Sahihs from more than one source. In a wording of Ahmad from this hadith, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended upon Tabuk, he descended upon them at al-Hijr near the houses of Thamud. Ahmad and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar to it, on the authority of Abu Kabsha Al-Anmari. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, And do not touch them with harm, he said: Do not hamstring them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement, And carve out of the mountains, houses, he said: They used to carve houses in the mountains. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And they rebelled against the command of their Lord, he said: They went to extremes in falsehood. So the earthquake seized them, he said: The blast. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, So they became within their homes fallen down, he said: Dead. Abd bin Hamid narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah.
17:32: His statement: 80- And Lot is connected to what came before: meaning, and We sent Lot, or it is accusative with an implied verb: meaning, and remember Lot when he said to his people. Al-Farra' said: Lot is derived from their saying: This is alit bi-qalbi: meaning it is stuck. Al-Zajjaj said: Some grammarians claimed that Lot could be derived from latat al-hawd if you smoothed it with mud, and this is wrong, because foreign names are not derived. Sibawayh said: Noah and Lot are foreign names, but they are light, and that is why they were declined. Lot is the son of Haran, the son of Tarah, so he is the nephew of Abraham. God sent him to a nation called Sodom. Do you commit immorality? meaning the immoral trait that persists in obscenity and ugliness. He said: This is to denounce them and rebuke them. No one before you has done it. meaning no one before you did it, because sodomy did not exist in any nation before this nation. Min is an additional emphasis for the generality in the negation, and it includes what it entered into, and the sentence is intended to emphasize the denunciation and rebuke of them. And when the Almighty forbade the killing of children, which would lead to the annihilation of the offspring, He mentioned the prohibition of adultery, which would lead to that, because of the mixing of lineages, and He said: 32- And do not come near adultery. And in the prohibition of coming near it by directly engaging in its preliminaries, there is a prohibition against it a fortiori, because if the means to something is forbidden, then the means to it is forbidden by the implication of the address, and adultery has two dialects: lengthening and shortening. The poet said: It was a duty to say what you say, just as adultery was a duty to be stoned. Then he explained the prohibition of adultery by saying: It is an abomination, meaning it is ugly, exceedingly ugly, and exceeding the limit. And an evil path, meaning it is an evil path, because it leads to Hellfire. There is no disagreement that it is one of the major sins. There is evidence that condemns it and warns against it, which is well-known.
7:81: His saying: 81- You indeed approach men with desire. Nafi’ and Hafs read the hadith with one broken hamza. The rest read with two hamzas as a question that requires rebuke and reproach. Abu Ubaid, Al-Kisa’i and others chose the first reading, while Al-Khalil and Sibawayh chose the second reading. According to the first reading, this sentence explains his saying: Do you commit immorality? Likewise according to the second reading with the addition of the question and its repetition, which is useful for exaggerating the rebuke and reproach, and the accusative of desire as a source: that is, you desire them with desire. It is permissible for it to be a source in the place of the state: that is, desiring, and it is permissible for it to be an object for it: that is, for the sake of desire. It includes that they have no purpose in committing this immorality except merely satisfying desire without having a purpose in that that agrees with reason. They are in this like beasts that mount each other for what they get from desire except for women meaning, exceeding in your action the women who are the place for satisfying desire and the place for seeking pleasure. Then he turned away from the previous denial to informing about what they are upon of extravagance that resulted in committing this. A terrible abomination.
7:82: His statement: 82- And the answer of his people who had committed this immorality to what he had denounced of them was only that they said, ‘Drive them out’ meaning Lot and his followers from your city: meaning they had no answer except this statement that was contrary to fairness and opposed to what he had asked of them and denounced of them. The phrase they are people who purify themselves is an explanation for what they were ordered to do in terms of driving them out, and describing them as purified could be true, and that they meant that these people would abstain from falling into this immorality and would not live with us in our city. It is possible that they said that in a mocking and derisive manner.
7:83: Then God the Almighty informed that He saved Lot and his believing family, and He excluded his wife from the family because she did not believe in him. The meaning of "she was among those who remained behind" is that she was among those who remained in God's punishment. It is said: "Ghabar means that something has passed, and Ghabar" means that it remains, so they are from the opposites. Ibn Faris narrated in Al-Mujmal from some people that they said: The past is fleeting with the silent 'ayn, and the remaining is Ghabbir with the voiced 'ayn. Al-Zajjaj said: "Min al-Ghabir" means among those absent from salvation. Abu Ubaid said: The meaning of "Min al-Ghabir" means among those who live long, and she had become old. Most linguists agree that Ghabbir is the remaining.
7:84: His statement: 84- "And We rained down upon them a rain." It was said: "Rained" means sending rain. Abu Ubaidah said: "Rained in mercy and rained" in punishment. The meaning here is that God rained down upon them a rain other than what they were accustomed to, which is throwing stones at them, as in His statement: "And We rained down upon them stones of baked clay. Then see how was the end of the criminals." This is addressed to everyone who is suitable for it, or to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The story of Lot will come in Hud more clearly than here. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Do you commit immorality? He said: The backsides of men. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The beginning of the action of the people of Lot was that Satan came to them in the form of a boy, the most beautiful boy that people had ever seen. He invited them to himself, so they married him, and then they dared to do that. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement, Indeed, they are people who purify themselves, he said: From the backsides of men and the backsides of women. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Except his wife, she was among those who remained behind, he said: Among those who remain in the punishment of God. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Sa’id bin Abi ‘Aruba, who said: The people of Lot were four thousand thousand.
7:85: His statement: 85- And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb is connected to what came before: that is, and We sent. Madyan is the name of a tribe, and it was said the name of a country, but the former is more appropriate. The tribe was named after their father: he is Madyan bin Ibrahim, just as it is said: Bakr and Tamim. His statement: Their brother Shu'ayb Shu'ayb is an explanatory apposition, and he is Shu'ayb bin Mika'il bin Yashjub bin Madyan bin Ibrahim, as stated by Ata', Ibn Ishaq and others. Ash-Sharfi bin Al-Qatami said: he is Shu'ayb bin Aifa bin Thuwaib bin Madyan bin Ibrahim. Ibn Sam'an claimed that he is Shu'ayb bin Hura bin Yashjub bin Lawi bin Ya'qub bin Ishaq bin Ibrahim. Qatada said: he is Shu'ayb bin Safwan bin Aifa bin Thabit bin Madyan bin Ibrahim. His statement: He said, O my people to his statement: A clear proof from your Lord has been explained previously in the story of Noah. His saying: So give full measure and weight He ordered them to give full measure and weight because they were people who dealt with measure and weight, and they did not know them. He mentioned the measure, which is the source, and attached to it the scale, which is the name of the instrument. There is a difference of opinion about the interpretation of this. It was said: What is meant by the measure is the measuring instrument, so it is appropriate to connect the scale to it. It was also said: What is meant by the scale is the weight, so it is appropriate to connect the measure, and the fa’ in fa’fulu is to connect it to i’badu. His statement: And do not deprive people of their things. Deprivation is deficiency, and it is done by finding fault with the commodity or showing disdain for it or deceiving its owner and cheating him. All of that is from consuming people’s money unjustly. The apparent meaning of his statement: their things is that they used to deprive people of all things. It was also said: They were bargainers who would bargain over everything that entered their markets. From this is the statement of Zuhair: Is there a tribute in all the markets of Iraq and a dirham tax on everything a man sells? His statement: And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation has been explained previously. It includes corruption, both minor and major, and the reference in His statement: that is to doing what He commanded them to do and leaving what He forbade them from doing. What is meant by goodness here is absolute increase, because there is no good in not giving full measure and weight, in cheating people, and in corruption on the earth at all.
7:86: His saying: 86- And do not sit on every path, threatening people with punishment. Path means the road: that is, do not sit on every path, threatening people with punishment. It was said: They used to sit on the roads leading to Shu'ayb, threatening whoever wanted to come to him, and they would say: He is a liar, so do not go to him, as the Quraysh used to do with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Mujahid, Al-Suddi and others. It was said: What is meant is sitting on the paths of religion and preventing whoever wanted to take them, and what is not meant by it is sitting on the roads in reality, and this is supported by and you hinder from the way of God whoever believes in Him. It was said: What is meant by the verse is the prohibition of highway robbery and taking spoils, and that was their action. It was said: They were tax collectors who took taxes from people's money on the roads, so they were prohibited from doing that. The first statement is the closest to the truth, although there is nothing preventing the prohibition from being applied to all of these statements mentioned. The phrase you are promised is in the accusative case as a state, as is what is conjoined to it: that is, do not sit on every road, turning away its people from the path of God, seeking to make it crooked. What is meant by turning away from the path of God is turning people away from the path they are sitting on and preventing them from reaching Shu`ayb, because people’s behavior on that path to reach the Prophet of God is the behavior of the path of God. Whoever believes in him is the object of you turn away, and the pronoun in believes in him refers to God, or to the path of God, or to every path or to Shu`ayb. And you seek to make it crooked means you seek the path of God to be crooked and not straight. We have already discussed crookedness. Al-Zajjaj said: The kasra of the ‘ayn in the meanings and the fatha of it in the ihram. And remember when you were that is, when you were few in number and He made you many in offspring. It was also said: You were poor and He enriched you. And see how was the end of the corrupters of the past nations, because God destroyed them and sent down upon them punishments that took them away and erased their traces.
7:87: 87- And if a party of you believes in that with which I have been sent to you of the rulings that God has legislated for you and a party of you do not believe, then be patient until God judges between us, and He is the best of judges. This is a severe threat and warning to them. It is not a command to be patient in disbelief. God's judgment between the two parties is to support those who are right over those who are wrong. Similar to this is His Almighty saying: Then wait, for we are with you waiting. Or it is a command to the believers to be patient in the face of the harm that befalls them from the disbelievers until God gives them victory over them.
7:88: 88- The leaders of his people who were arrogant said, meaning the arrogant nobles said, We will surely expel you, O Shu'aib, and those who have believed with you. They were not satisfied with abandoning faith and rebelling against answering what he called them to, but they went beyond that in transgression, arrogance, and threatening their prophet and those who believed in him with expulsion from their city or his and those with him returning to their religion of disbelief: meaning one of two things is necessary: either expulsion, or returning. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible for returning to mean beginning, it is said: something bad has returned to me from so-and-so: meaning it happened, even if nothing bad had happened before that, so it does not apply to what is said: How could Shu'aib have been of their religion of disbelief before God sent him as a Messenger? And he needs the answer by making his people who follow him prevail over him in the address to return to their religion, and the phrase He said or if we were reluctant is a new answer to an implied question, and the hamza is to deny the occurrence of what they asked of expulsion or return, and the waw is for the state: that is, do you return us to your religion in a state of our aversion to returning to it, or do you expel us from your village in a state of our aversion to leaving it, or in a state of our aversion to both matters, and the meaning is: it is not for you to force us to one of the two matters and it is not valid for you to do so, because the one who is forced has no choice and his agreement under duress is not considered agreement nor is his return to your religion under duress a return, and with this report what many commentators have found problematic in this position is dispelled until it caused the lengthening of the tails of the speech.
7:89: 89- We have certainly fabricated a lie against God if we return to your religion which is polytheism after God has saved us from it through faith, so there is no return from us to it at all. And it is not for us that is, it is not right for us nor is it proper to return to it under any circumstances except if God wills that is, except when He wills, glory be to Him, for whatever He wills will be and whatever He does not will will not be. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, except by the will of God, the Almighty and Majestic. He said: This is the saying of the people of the Sunnah, and the meaning is that it is not for us to return to disbelief except if God wills that, so the exception is discontinuous. It was said: The exception here is in the direction of submission to God, the Almighty and Majestic, as in His statement: And my success is not except by God. It was said: It is like their saying, I will not speak to you until the crow lays eggs, and until the camel passes through the eye of a needle, but the crow does not lay eggs, and the camel does not pass through, so it is a case of suspension of the impossible. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge meaning His knowledge encompasses all information, so nothing of it escapes Him. Knowledge is in the accusative case as a specification. It has been said that the meaning is and it is not for us to return to it meaning the village after you hated our proximity to you unless God wills that is, our return to it. In God we have relied meaning we depend on Him to make us steadfast in faith, and to stand between us and disbelief and its people, and to complete His favor upon us, and to protect us from His wrath. His statement: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of judges al-Fatah is government, meaning judge between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of judges. They called upon God, the Exalted, to judge between them, and His judgment will not be except by supporting the truthful over the false, as He has informed us of in more than one place in His Book. It is as if they asked for the punishment to descend upon the disbelievers and for God's wrath to descend upon them.
7:90: 90- And the chiefs of his people who disbelieved said is connected to The chiefs who were arrogant said it is possible that these are those, and it is possible that they are others from the groups of disbelievers to whom Shu'ayb was sent, and the lam in If you follow Shu'ayb is an introduction to the answer to an omitted oath: that is, if you entered his religion and abandoned your religion then you would surely be losers the answer to the oath took the place of the answer to the condition, and their loss: their destruction or what they lose because of giving full measure and weight and leaving the cheating with which they dealt with people.
7:91: 91- So the earthquake seized them, meaning the quake. It was also said that it was the blast, as in His statement: And the blast seized those who did wrong, “So they became in their homes, fallen down,” the explanation of which was presented in the story of Salih.
7:92: His statement: 92- Those who denied Shu'aib, it is as if they had never prospered therein. This sentence is a resumption explaining what happened to them of punishment, and the relative pronoun is the subject, and as if they had never prospered is its predicate: It is said, I prospered in a place if I stayed there, and the people prospered in their home meaning their stay in it was long, and the house is the home, and the plural is the places of residence. Hatim al-Ta'i said: We sang for a time with vagabondage and wealth, and time gave us both their cups. Our enmity towards our relatives does not increase our wealth, nor does poverty diminish our good deeds. The meaning of the verse: Those who denied Shu`ayb are as if they had never lived in their home, because God Almighty exterminated them with punishment. The subject in those who denied Shu`ayb is the subject and the predicate is they were the losers. This sentence is resumed like the first, including a statement of the loss of the people who denied.
7:93: 93- So he turned away from them meaning Shu'aib when he saw the punishment descending upon them and said, 'O my people, I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord' with which He sent me to you and I have given you good advice by explaining what is in it for the safety of your religion and your worldly life so how can I grieve meaning should I be sad for a people who disbelieve" in God, persisting in their disbelief, rebelling against answering or grief is intense grief, grief over that is so he is sad. Shu'aib said this statement regretting the lack of faith of his people, then he consoled himself by asking how he could be sad for a people who are not worthy of being sad for them because of their disbelief in God and their refusal to accept what His Messenger brought. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Suddi that they said: God did not send a prophet twice except Shu`ayb: once to Madyan, and the blast overtook them, and once to the Companions of the Thicket, and God overtook them with the punishment of the Day of Shadow. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And do not deprive people of their due rights, meaning: Do not wrong people. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah, And do not deprive people of their due rights, meaning: Do not wrong them. And do not sit on every path, threatening, meaning: They used to threaten whoever came to Shu`ayb, crossed his path and wanted to become Muslim. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And do not sit on every path, threatening, meaning: They used to sit on the road and tell whoever came to them that Shu`ayb was a liar, so do not let him tempt you away from your religion. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, On every path you are promised, he said: on every right path. And you bar from the path of God, he said: you bar its people. And you seek to make it crooked, he said: you seek to make it deviant. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi, And do not sit on every path you are promised, he said: it is the tenth. And you bar from the path of God, he said: you bar from Islam. And seek to make it crooked, he said: destruction. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, he said: they are the tenth. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah or someone else - Abu al-Aliyah was not sure - he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came on a piece of wood on the road on the night of his Israa ascension. Not a single garment passed by it without it tearing it, and nothing else without it tearing it. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is like people from your nation who sit on the road and cut it off. Then he recited, And do not sit on every path you are promised. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And it is not for us to return to it, he said: It is not appropriate for us to return to your polytheism after God has saved us, unless God, our Lord, wills, and God does not will polytheism, but He says: Unless God knows something, for He has encompassed all things in His knowledge. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat, and Ibn Al-Anbari in Al-Waqf wa Al-Ibtida’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I did not know what His statement: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth meant until I heard his son Dhi Yazan say: Come, let me open the matter with You, meaning I will sue You. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Our Lord, open, he said: Judge. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Fath opening is a Yemeni dialect. If someone says: Come, let me sue You, he says: Come, let me open the matter with You. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They did not live in it, he said: They did not live in it.
