And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatada something similar. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, How can I be sad? He said: I am sad. And Ibn Asakir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: In the Sacred Mosque there are two graves and there is no other one in it, the grave of Ismail and the grave of Shuaib. The grave of Ismail is in the Hijr, and the grave of Shuaib is opposite the Black Stone. And Ibn Asakir narrated from Wahb bin Munabbih that Shuaib died in Mecca and the believers with him, and their graves are to the west of the Kaaba between Dar Al-Nadwa and Bab Bani Sahm. And Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yaqub bin Abi Maslama told me that whenever the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) mentioned Shuaib, he said: That is the orator of the prophets, because of his good argument with his people regarding what he wanted from them. But when they denied him and threatened him with stoning and exile from their country and rebelled against God, the punishment of the Day of Shadow seized them.
7:94: His saying: 94- And We did not send to any city any prophet When God Almighty detailed the conditions of some of the prophets with their nations, and they are the ones mentioned previously, He summarized the condition of all the nations to which they were sent: that is, and We did not send to any city any prophet from the prophets, and in the speech there is an omission, that is, if its people denied it, We seized them, and the exception is empty: that is, We did not send in any condition except in a condition in which We seized its people, so the place of seized is the accusative, and misery: misery and poverty, and distress: harm, and the meaning of misery and distress has been explained previously that they may humble themselves that is, so that they may supplicate and humble themselves, so that they may abandon what they are upon of arrogance and denial of the prophets.
7:95: His saying: 95- Then We replaced is connected to We seized: meaning, then after seizing the people of the towns, We replaced the bad with good meaning the good trait: so they became well-off, comfortable, and secure until they became abundant: it is said: to be abundant means to increase, and to be destroyed means to be destroyed, so it is one of the names of opposites, and what is meant here is that they became abundant in themselves and in their wealth: meaning, We gave them good in place of bad until they became abundant. And they said, ‘Our fathers have been touched by hardship and prosperity’: meaning, they said this statement when they became in good after bad: meaning, this hardship and distress that has befallen us, then of prosperity and fertility after that, is something that happened to our fathers before us like it, so they were touched by the same hardship and distress that befell us, and by the same blessing and good that we attained. Their meaning is that this is the custom that is prevalent among the predecessors and successors, and that this is not a test for them from God Almighty. And as a test of what they have, and in this is the intensity of their stubbornness and the strength of their rebellion and their insolence what is not hidden, and for this reason God hastened the punishment upon them and did not give them respite, so He said: So We seized them suddenly meaning suddenly after they said this statement without delay or respite, and the situation is that they do not perceive that and do not anticipate it.
7:96: The lam in 96- the villages is for the covenant: that is, and if only the people of the villages to whom We sent Our messengers had believed in the messengers sent to them and feared what they resolved to do of disbelief and did not persist in what they did of the ugly things We would have opened for them blessings from the heaven and the earth that is, We would have made easy for them the good of the heaven and the earth just as closed doors are made easy by opening their doors. It was said that what is meant by the good of the sky is the rain, and the good of the earth is the vegetation, and it is better to interpret what is in the verse as something more general than that, and it is permissible for the lam in the villages to be for the genus, and what is meant is: if the people of the villages, wherever they were and in whatever country they lived, had believed and feared God until the end of the verse but they denied the signs and the prophets and did not believe or fear God so We seized them with the punishment because of what they were earning of sins that necessitated their punishment.
7:97: And the question in 97- Are the people of the towns secure? is for rebuke and reprimand, and the people of the towns are the people of the towns mentioned before it, and the fa is for conjunction, and it is like Are they seeking the judgment of the time of ignorance? And it was said: What is meant by the towns is Mecca and what is around it because of their denial of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the general application is more appropriate. His saying: That Our punishment may come upon them at night means at night, which is at night, and it is accusative as a circumstantial, and it is permissible for it to be a source: meaning spending the night, or a source in the place of the state: meaning spending the night, and the phrase while they are asleep is in the place of accusative as a state.
7:98: The question in 98- Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come to them at noon while they are playing? is like the question before it. Ad-Duha is the noonday, and it is originally a name for the light of the sun when it rises and rises. Ibn Amir and Al-Haramiyan read or feel secure with a sukoon on the waw, and the rest read it with a fatha on it. The phrase while they are playing is in the accusative case as a state: meaning they are busy with things that will not bring them any benefit.
7:99: The question in 99- Do they then feel secure from the plan of God? is for rebuke and rebuke and denial of what they are upon of security from what is not secure from the plan of God with them and His punishment for them, and in repeating this question there is an increase in confirming the denial of what He denied them, then He explained the state of those who feel secure from the plan of God, so He said: None feel secure from the plan of God except the people who are losers meaning those who have gone too far in loss and have fallen into His severe threat, and it was said: The plan of God here is His enticement with blessings and health. The first is to carry it to what is more general than that.
7:100: His saying: 100- Have there not been a guidance for those who inherit the earth after its people? Nahad was read with the letter nun and with the letter taht. According to the reading with the letter nun, the subject of the verb is God Almighty and the object of the verb is that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins. That is, this is the case. According to the reading with the letter taht, the subject of yahid is that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins. That is, We would seize them for their disbelief and denial. Guidance here means clarification, and for this reason it is transitive with the letter lam. His saying: And We seal their hearts means, And We seal their hearts is a new verse, and it is not correct to connect it to We have afflicted because they are among those whose hearts God has sealed due to their refusal to believe. It was said: It is connected to an implied verb indicated by the speech, as if it was said: They are heedless of guidance and We seal. It was said: It is connected to they inherit. His saying: So they do not hear is the answer to if: meaning, because of Our afflicting them with their sins and the sealing of their hearts, they do not hear what is recited to them by the one whom God sent to them of preaching, excuses, and warning. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then We replaced the bad with good, he said: instead of hardship, ease, until they became abundant, he said: they multiplied and their wealth multiplied. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: until they became abundant, he said: they gathered. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: Our fathers were touched by hardship and prosperity, he said: they said: something similar to this had happened to our fathers, and it was nothing. Then We seized them suddenly while they perceived not. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And if only the people of the towns had believed, he said: in what God had revealed, and feared God, he said: what God had forbidden, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth, he said: the heaven gave them its blessings and the earth its vegetation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muadh bin Rifa’ah on the authority of Musa al-Ta’ifi who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Honor bread, for God sent it down from the blessings of the sky and brought it forth from the blessings of the earth. Al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani narrated, and al-Suyuti said: With a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Abdullah bin Umm Haram who said: I prayed the two qiblas with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “Honor bread, for God sent it down from the blessings of the sky and subjected the blessings of the earth to it. Whoever follows what falls from the plate, God will forgive him.” Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of al-Hasan who said: There were people of a village whom God had given so much to the extent that they used bread to clean themselves, then God sent hunger upon them. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Have they not been guided? He said: Have We not made clear. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding His statement: For those who inherit the earth after its people, he said: The polytheists.
7:101: His statement: 101- Those towns meaning those that We destroyed, and they are the towns of Noah, Salih, Lot, and Shuaib, which were mentioned earlier. We relate to you meaning We recite to you some of their report meaning some of their stories. This is a consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for the believers. Nas is either in the accusative case as a state, and those towns is the subject and predicate, or it is in the nominative case as the predicate, and the towns is an attribute of those, and min in of their report is for partiality: meaning We relate to you some of their report, and the lam in Indeed, their messengers came to them with clear proofs is the answer to the oath. Meaning: Among their report is that the Messengers of God came to them with His proofs, as was previously explained in the stories of the prophets mentioned before this. So they would not believe when the Messengers came in what they denied before their coming, or they would not believe in what the Messengers brought them in any situation or at any time in what they denied before their coming. Rather, they persisted in disbelief, clinging to the tails of tyranny always, and the coming of the Messengers did not work on them nor did any effect of it appear. Rather, their state upon their coming was like their state before it. It was said that the meaning is: So they would not believe after their destruction in what they denied if We revived them, as He said: And if they were returned, they would return. It was said: They asked for miracles, but when they saw them, they did not believe in what they denied before seeing them. The first is more appropriate, and the meaning of their denial before the coming of the Messengers is that in the Age of Ignorance they denied everything they heard about the sending of Messengers and the revelation of Books. His saying: Thus does God set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers. That is, God sets a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers with such a severe seal that no preaching, reminder, encouragement, or intimidation will be effective in them after that.
7:102: His saying: 102- "And We did not find for most of them any covenant" The pronoun refers to the people of the villages mentioned previously: meaning, We did not find for most of the people of these villages any covenant: any covenant that they maintain and adhere to, rather their habit is to break covenants in every situation. It was said: The pronoun refers to people in general: meaning, We did not find for most of the people any covenant. It was said that what is meant by the covenant is what was taken from them in the world of the atoms. It was said: The pronoun refers to the disbelievers in general without restricting it to the people of the villages: meaning, most of them have no covenant or loyalty, and a few of them may fulfill their covenant and maintain it. And in "And if we find most of them are wicked" is the lightened form of the heavy, and the pronoun of the matter is omitted: meaning, the matter is that we found most of them are wicked, or it is the negative, and the lam in "wicked" means except: meaning except wicked who have gone out of obedience with a severe departure. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abi Ibn Kaab regarding his statement: And they would not believe in what they denied before, he said: It was in the knowledge of God on the day they acknowledged the covenant to Him who would deny it and who would believe it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they would not believe in what they denied before, he said: It is like his statement: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: And We did not find for most of them any covenant, he said: Fulfillment. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the verse: It is that covenant on the day the covenant was taken. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We found most of them to be wicked, he said: That is because God destroyed the towns because they did not keep what He commanded them.
7:103: His saying: 103- Then We sent after them Moses meaning after Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shuaib: meaning then We sent Moses after sending these messengers. It was said: The pronoun in after them refers to the previous nations: meaning after their destruction to Pharaoh and his chiefs Pharaoh is a title for everyone who rules the land of Egypt after the giants and Pharaoh’s chiefs: the nobles of his people and the mention is specific with the generality of the message to them and others, because those other than them are like followers to them. His saying: So they wronged them means they disbelieved in them. The term wrong is applied to disbelief because their disbelief in the signs that Moses brought was an exaggerated disbelief due to the existence of what necessitates belief from the great miracles that he brought to them. What is meant by the signs here is the nine signs, or the meaning of so they wronged them is that they wronged the people because of them when they turned them away from believing in them, or they wronged themselves because of them. Then see how was the end of the corrupters meaning those who denied the signs and disbelieved in them and made them corrupters, because their denial and disbelief are among the ugliest types of corruption.
7:104: His saying: 104- And Moses said, O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds. He informed him that he was sent by God to him and made that the title of his speech with him, because whoever was sent by the One who is the Lord of the worlds altogether is worthy of acceptance for what he brought, just as someone sent by the king with a need for his subjects says: I am the king’s messenger to you, then he narrates what he was sent with, for in that there is a nurturing of awe and the introduction of awe that cannot be measured.
7:105: His saying: 105- It is true that I should not say about God except the truth It was read it is true that I should not say: meaning it is obligatory and necessary for me not to say in what I convey to you from God except the truth, and it was read it is true that I should not say without a pronoun in Ali, it was said: in explaining it that on means the preposition: meaning it is true that I should not say, and this is supported by the reading of Abu and Al-A'mash, as they read it is true that I should not say. It was said: that true includes the meaning of keen, and it was said: that since it was necessary for the truth, the truth was necessary for it, so the saying of the truth is true for him and he is true to the saying of the truth, and it was said: that he immersed himself in describing himself in that position until he made himself true to the saying of the truth as if it was necessary for the truth that Moses was the one who said it. Abdullah bin Mas'ud read it is true that I should not say by projecting it on, and its meaning is clear, then he said after this: I have come to you with a clear proof from your Lord meaning with what proves my truthfulness and that I am a Messenger from the Lord of the Worlds. Here, he has omitted the mention of the dialogue that took place between them, as in another place, Pharaoh said, Who is your Lord, O Moses? Then he said after Moses’ answer, And who is the Lord of the worlds? The verses that describe what took place between them. His saying, Then send with me the Children of Israel is his command to let the Children of Israel go with him and return to their homelands, which are the Holy Land. They remained with him, enslaved and forbidden from returning to their homeland. The fa is to arrange what comes after it according to what came before it.
7:106: When he said that 106- Pharaoh said to him If you have come with a sign from God as you claim, then bring it so that we may see it and consider it if you are of the truthful in this claim that you have come with.
7:107: His statement: 107- So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a clear serpent. That is, he placed it on the ground and it turned into a serpent: that is, a large male snake. The meaning of clear is that its being a serpent in that state is a clear, obvious matter that is not ambiguous.
7:108: 108- And he took out his hand meaning he took it out and showed it from his pocket or from under his armpit. In the revelation: And put your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without disease. His saying: And behold, it is white to the beholders meaning, his hand that he took out was white, shining with light that is apparent to every sighted person.
7:109: 109- The chiefs meaning the nobles of Pharaoh’s people said when they saw the staff turning into a snake, and his hand turning white without any harm, This meaning Moses is indeed a learned magician meaning he has great knowledge of magic. There is no contradiction between attributing this statement to the chiefs here and to Pharaoh in Surat Ash-Shu’ara’, as they all said it, so that was a confirmation of its attribution to them at one time and to him at another.
7:110: And sentence 110- He wants to expel you from your land is a description of a magician, and the land attributed to them is the land of Egypt: This is from the speech of the leaders, and as for So what do you command? It was said: It is from the speech of Pharaoh, he said: To the leaders when they said what came before: That is, what do you command me, and it was said: It is from the speech of the leaders: That is, they said to Pharaoh, so what do you command us to do? And they addressed him with what you address the group with, to honor him as leaders address their followers, and what is in the position of the accusative with the verb that comes after it, and it is permissible for that to mean who as the grammarians mentioned in What did you do?
7:111: And that this is from the words of Pharaoh is the first, as evidenced by what follows, which is 111- They said, 'Put him off and his brother.'" He said: The leaders responded to the words of Pharaoh when he consulted them and asked for their opinion. He put him off: that is, he delayed him and his brother. It is said: I postponed him and I postponed him: I delayed him. Asim, Al-Kisa'i, Hamza and the people of Medina read "arja" without a hamza, and the rest read it with a hamza. The people of Kufa except Al-Kisa'i read "arja" with a sukoon on the ha'. Al-Farra' said: It is a dialect of the Arabs, they stop on the ha' in connection, and the Basrans denied that. It was said that the meaning of arja is: detain him. It was said that it is from rajaa yarju: meaning give him hope and leave him hoping for you. An-Nahhas narrated it from Muhammad ibn Yazid Al-Mubarrad. "And he sent a group of gatherers into the cities meaning he sent a group of gatherers into the cities where the magicians were, and gatherers is the object of arsaal, and it was said that it is accusative as a state.
7:112: And 112- They will come to you" is the answer to the command: meaning, those whom you sent will come to you "with every learned magician" meaning every skilled magician with great knowledge of his craft. The people of Kufa, except for Asim, read "magician and those other than them read sorcerer".
7:113: His saying: 113- "And the magicians came to Pharaoh" in the speech Tay: meaning, he sent gatherers in the cities and the magicians came to Pharaoh. His saying: "They said, 'Indeed, we have a reward' meaning, when they came to Pharaoh, they said to him, We have a reward." The sentence is a resumption in response to an implied question, as if it was said: What did they say to him when they came to him? The reward is the prize and the reward. They obliged Pharaoh to give them a reward if they defeated Moses with their magic. Nafi' and Ibn Kathir read "indeed, we have as a statement, and the rest read indeed, we have" as a question. They asked Pharaoh about the reward that he would give them for defeating them, and the meaning of the question is confirmation. As for the first reading, it is as if they were certain of the reward and that they must have it.
7:114: So Pharaoh answered them by saying: Yes, and you are among those brought near. That is, you will have a reward, and in addition to this reward required of you, you are among those brought near to Us.
7:115: His statement: 115- "They said, 'O Moses, either you throw or we will be the throwers.'" This sentence is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did they say to Moses after Pharaoh said to them: "Yes, and indeed, you are among those brought near." The meaning is: They gave Moses the choice between him starting with what he threw at them or they starting with that, out of respect for him and confidence in themselves that they would be victorious even if they were late. And "that" is in the accusative case, as Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: meaning either you do the throwing or we do it.
7:116: So Moses answered them by saying: 116- "Throw" He chose that they should be the first to throw what they throw, not caring about them or fearing what they brought. Al-Farra' said: There is an omission in the speech, the meaning is: Moses said to them that you will never defeat your Lord and you will never invalidate His signs, and it was said that it is a threat: that is, begin with throwing and you will see what will happen to you of disgrace. The reason for these two interpretations according to those who said them is that it is not permissible for Moses to order them to practice magic. "So when they threw that is, their ropes and staffs they bewitched the eyes of the people that is, they turned them and changed them from the correctness of their perception with what they brought of deception and illusion that magicians and magicians do and terrified them that is, they instilled fear in their hearts greatly and they produced a great magic in the eyes of those who watched what they brought, even though it had no reality in reality.
7:117: His saying: 117- And We inspired Moses, saying, 'Throw down your staff.' God the Almighty commanded him when the magicians came with what they had brought of magic to throw down his staff. And behold, it meaning the staff devoured what they were fabricating. Hafs read talqaf with a sukoon on the lam and a light qaf from laqaf yalqaf. The rest read with a fatha on the lam and a shaddah on the qaf from talaqafa yaltaghaf. It is said: I laqaft al-shay' and talaqafatuhu: if you took it or reached it. Abu Hatim said: I was informed in some readings that it is talqam with a shaddah on the meem. The poet said: You are the staff of Moses that never ceases to feed the magician what he fabricates. And what is in what they fabricate is a source or a relative pronoun: meaning their fabrication or what they fabricate, he called it fabrication, because it has no truth to it in reality, but rather it is a lie, falsehood, camouflage, and sorcery.
7:118: 118- Then the truth came to pass meaning it became apparent and clear what Moses had brought and what they were doing was invalidated of their magic: meaning its invalidity became clear.
7:119: 119- So they were defeated meaning the magicians there meaning in the situation in which they displayed their magic and they turned back from that situation humiliated humiliated and subjugated.
7:120: 120- And the magicians fell down prostrating meaning they fell down prostrating as if someone had thrown them down in the form of prostration, or they could not control what they saw, so it was as if they had thrown themselves down.
7:121: And the sentence 121 - They said, 'We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron' is a new answer to an implied question, as if it was said, what did they say when they prostrated or in their prostration, and they only said this statement and declared that they believed in the Lord of the worlds.
7:122: Then they were not satisfied with that until they said: 122- Lord of Moses and Aaron so that no one from the people of Pharaoh who acknowledged his divinity would imagine that prostration to him was necessary. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then We sent after them Moses, he said: He was called Moses because he was thrown between water and trees. Water in Coptic is mo and trees are si. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: Pharaoh was a Persian from the people of Istakhr. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah: He was from the sons of Egypt. Abu Al-Sheikh also narrated on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Al-Munkadir who said: Pharaoh lived for three hundred years. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali Ibn Abi Talhah that Pharaoh was a Copt born of fornication and his height was seven spans. He also narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: He was a foreigner from Hamadan. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Ibn Muqsim Al-Hudhali who said: Pharaoh lived for four hundred years without a headache. And Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: So he threw down his staff, he said: It was mentioned to us that that staff was Adam’s staff that an angel had given him when he set out for Midian, so it would shine at night and he would strike the ground with it during the day, and it would bring forth his provisions, and he would use it to frighten his sheep. Then it was a clear serpent, he said: A snake that almost attacked him. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Moses entered upon Pharaoh, and he was wearing a woolen robe that did not extend beyond his elbows, so he asked permission to enter upon Pharaoh, and he said: Let him in, so he entered and said: My God has sent me to you, so he said to the people around him: I do not know of any god for you other than me, take him. He said: I have come to you with a sign. He said: Bring it, if you are of the truthful. So he threw down his staff and it became a serpent between his jaws, between the ceiling and the ground. He put his hand in his pocket and took it out like lightning, flashing the eyes, so they fell on their faces. Moses took his staff and went out, and there was no one among the people who did not flee from him. When he regained consciousness and the fear had left Pharaoh, he said to the leaders around him: What do you command me? They said: Put him and his brother off. And do not bring him to us, nor let him come near us. And send gatherers into the cities. The magicians feared Pharaoh, so when he sent to them, they said: Your god needs you. He said: This one did such and such. They said: This is a magician who has done magic. We will have a reward if we are the victors. He said: Yes, and you will be among those brought near. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him that he said: The name of Moses’ staff was Masha. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from him through various chains of transmission regarding his statement: Then it was a clear serpent. He said: The male snake. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: Then it was a serpent manifest, he said: The male snake opened its mouth and placed its lower jaw on the ground and its upper jaw on Surat Al-Qasr, then it headed towards Pharaoh to seize him. When he saw it, he was terrified by it and jumped up, so he broke his fast and he had not broken his fast before that, so he shouted: O Moses, take it and I believe in your Lord and send with you the Children of Israel. So Moses took it and it became a staff. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Postpone it, he said: Delay it. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: Imprison him and his brother. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas through various chains regarding his statement: And sent gatherers into the cities, he said: The police. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And the magicians came, he said: They were seventy men who became magicians in the morning and martyrs in the evening. The Salaf differed in their number. It was said: They were seventy, as Ibn Abbas said. It was said: They were twelve. It was said: Fifteen thousand. It was said: Seventeen thousand. It was said: Nineteen thousand. It was said: Thirty thousand. It was said: Seventy thousand. It was said: Eighty thousand. It was said: Three hundred thousand. It was said: Nine hundred thousand. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada regarding his statement: Indeed, for us is a reward. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So when they threw, he said: They threw thick ropes and long pieces of wood, and it approached, and it seemed to him from their magic that it was crawling. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Al-Suddi that he said: Moses threw his staff and every snake ate them. When they saw that, they prostrated. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Qatada. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: It swallows up what they fabricate, he said: What they lie. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement: It swallows up what they fabricate, he said: What they lie. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement: It swallows up what they fabricate, he said: Their ropes and sticks are drawn. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud and some of the Companions who said: Moses and the chief magician met, and Moses said to him: Tell me, if I defeat you, will you believe in me and testify that what you have brought is true? The magician said: I will come tomorrow with magic that no magic can defeat, and by God, if you defeat me, I will believe in you and testify that it is true, while Pharaoh was looking at them. This is what Pharaoh said: This is indeed a plot you have plotted in the city. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awza’i, who said: When the magicians prostrated, Paradise was raised up for them so that they could look at it.
7:123: His saying: 123- You believed in him was read with the deletion of the hamza in the report and with its confirmation. Pharaoh denied the magicians' belief in Moses before he gave them permission to do so, then he said after denying them, explaining what he claimed motivated them to do so, This is indeed a plot that you plotted in the city meaning a trick that you and Moses took over through a previous agreement between you to expel from the city of Egypt its people from the Copts and seize it and live in it, you and the Children of Israel. The meaning of in the city is that this trick and agreement was between you and you in the city of Egypt before you and Moses went out to this desert, then he threatened them by saying: Then you will come to know the consequences of this action of yours and the evil outcome of it.
7:124: Then he did not stop at this general threat, but rather he detailed it and said: 124- I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, meaning the right foot and the left hand, or the left foot and the right hand. Then the enemy of God did not stop at this, but rather he went beyond it to something else and said: Then I will crucify you, on the trunks of palm trees: meaning I will make you crucified on them, to further torment them and to go to extremes in torturing them.
7:125: And the sentence: 125- They said, 'Indeed, to our Lord we will return' is a resumption of the answer to a question as mentioned above, and its meaning is: If you did this deed to us, then you will be promised it on the Day of Judgment. God will reward you for your deed and will be good to us for what happened to us in His essence. So they threatened him with the punishment of God in the Hereafter, just as He threatened them with the punishment of this world. It is possible that the meaning is: Indeed, to our Lord we will return with death: meaning that death is inevitable for us and it does not harm us that it is due to you.
7:126: His saying: 126- "And do not blame us." Al-Hasan read it with the opening of the qaf. Al-Akhfash said: It is a language, and the rest read it with a kasra. It is said: Naqmat al-Amr Ankartuhu: meaning you do not criticize us and disapprove of us except that we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us even though this is the great honor and complete good, and something like it is not a place for criticism and a place for denial, rather it is worthy of good praise and great approval. Then they left his address and cut off the conversation with him and turned to address the Most High, entrusting the matter to Him, asking Him, the Almighty, to make them steadfast in this ordeal with patience, saying: Our Lord, pour upon us patience. Pouring: pouring: meaning pour it upon us until it overflows and engulfs us. They asked for the most eloquent types of patience in preparation for what would befall them of torment from the enemy of God and to prepare themselves for steadfastness in the truth and steadfastness in faith. Then they said: And take us as Muslims meaning take us to You while we are steadfast in Islam, not distorting, changing, or tempted. And what they were upon of magic and skill in its knowledge, despite it being… Pure evil is a reason for winning happiness because they knew that what Moses brought was beyond the control of humans and that it was the doing of God Almighty, so they reached goodness through evil, and none of the followers of Pharaoh who did not know this knowledge achieved what they achieved in terms of submission, recognition, and faith. If skill in the knowledge of evil can bring such benefit, then what about skill in the knowledge of good? O God, benefit us with what you have taught us, and make our feet firm on the truth, and pour out upon us the battle of patience and let us die as Muslims.
7:127: His statement: 127- And the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, 'Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land?' This question from them is to denounce him: meaning, will you leave him and his people to cause corruption in the land by causing division and scattering the people. What is meant by the land here is the land of Egypt. His statement: And leave you and your gods Nu'aym bin Maysarah read and leave you in the nominative case, assuming the subject: meaning, and he leaves you, or in conjunction with will you leave Moses: meaning, will you leave him and leave you? Al-Ashhab Al-'Uqayli read and leave you in the jussive case: either to lighten it with the sukoon due to the heaviness of the damma, or according to what was said in and be among the righteous in explaining the jussive case. Anas bin Malik read and leave you with the nominative case, and its meaning is: that they informed about themselves that they would leave him and his gods. The rest read and leave you in the accusative case, with the letter an understood to be the answer to the question, and the letter waw is a substitute for the letter fa or in apposition to yufsidu meaning to corrupt, and wa yufsidru because they are corrupt in their opinion, and it leads to abandoning Pharaoh and his gods. The commentators differed on the meaning of and your gods because Pharaoh claimed divinity as in his saying: I know of no god for you other than Me, and his saying: I am your Lord. It was said that the meaning of and your gods is: and your obedience, and it was said that its meaning is: and your worship, and this is supported by the reading of Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and your gods, and in the letter of Abu, Do you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land while they have abandoned you to worship you? It was said that he worshipped a cow, and it was said that he worshipped the stars, and it was said that he had idols that his people worshipped to draw closer to him, so they were attributed to him, and this is why he said: I am your highest lord. This was said by Az-Zajjaj, and it was said that he worshipped the sun, so Pharaoh said in response to them and to confirm their hearts in disbelief: We will kill their sons. Nafi’ and Ibn Kathir read we will kill with a light pronunciation. The rest read with emphasis: meaning we will kill the sons and spare the women: meaning we will leave them alive. He did not say we will kill Moses because he knew that he would not be able to do anything to him. And We are over them, dominating them, meaning we are superior to them by force and dominance, or they are under our force and in our hands. Whatever we wish to do to them, we will do.
7:128: The sentence: 128- Moses said to his people is a resumption of the answer to an implied question. When Moses heard what Pharaoh had said, he ordered his people to seek help from God and to be patient in the ordeal. Then he told them, The land meaning the land of Egypt "is God's. He gives it as an inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants" or the type of land, and it is a promise from Moses to his people of victory over Pharaoh and his people, and that God will give them their land and their homes. Then he gave them good report that the ultimate outcome is for the righteous: meaning the praiseworthy outcome in this world and the hereafter is for the righteous among His servants, and they are Moses and those with him. The ultimate outcome of everything is its end. And the ultimate outcome was read in the accusative case in apposition to the earth.
7:129: And the sentence 129- They said, 'We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question like the one before it: that is, we were harmed before you came to us as a messenger, and that was by Pharaoh killing our sons at your birth when he was informed that a child would be born at whose hand his kingdom would be destroyed. And after you came to us as a messenger by killing our sons now. It was said: the meaning is we were harmed before you came to us by using us in hard labor without permission. And after you came to us by what we are in now of fear for ourselves, our children, and our families. It was said: the harm before and after is one, which is the collection of the jizya from them. The sentence He said, 'Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy' is a resumption like the one before it, promising them that God will destroy their enemy, which is Pharaoh and his people. His saying: And will make you successors in the land is an explicit statement of what was previously indicated, that the land belongs to God. God fulfilled his hope, and they ruled Egypt during the time of David and Solomon, and they conquered Jerusalem with Joshua bin Nun, and destroyed Pharaoh and his people by drowning and saved them. So He will see how you will do of deeds after He bestowed upon you the favor of destroying your enemy. And He will make you successors in the land and He will reward you for what you did in it of good and evil. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: This is indeed a plot that you have plotted in the city if you meet to show off and its people leave it I will surely cut off your hands the verse, he said: So he killed them and cut them off as he said. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The first to be crucified was Pharaoh. And he was the first to cut off hands and feet from opposite sides. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: from opposite sides he said: A hand from here and a foot from there. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us he said: Before God sent you and after it. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih regarding the verse, he said: The Children of Israel said to Moses, Pharaoh used to charge us with milk before you came to us, but when you came, he charged us with milk along with straw. Moses said: O Lord, you have destroyed Pharaoh, until when will you keep him? So God revealed to him that they did not commit the sin for which he destroyed them. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: Shame on the enemy of God, it has happened that a boy will be born in that year who will usurp your kingdom. He said: So he pursued their children that year by slaughtering the male among them, then he slaughtered them also after Moses came to them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The beginning and end will be with us, the people of the house, and a state will inevitably occur for Banu Hashim, so consider who will be from Banu Hashim? And about them was revealed the verse: Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land and see how you act. It is necessary to look into the authenticity of this from Ibn Abbas. The verse was revealed about the Children of Israel, not the Children of Hashim. It is located in this story that tells what happened between Moses and Pharaoh.
7:130: What is meant by the people of Pharaoh here is his people, and what is meant by the years of famine is the drought, and this is well known to the linguists. They say that a year struck them, meaning a year of famine. And in the hadith: O God, make them years like the years of Joseph. And most Arabs parse the years as a sound masculine plural, and some Arabs parse it as a singular and apply the vowels to the nun. Al-Farra’ recited: I see the passing years taking from me as secrets are taken from the crescent moon With a kasra on the letter nun from al-sanin. Al-Nahhas said: Sibawayh recited this verse with a fatha on the letter nun. I say: What is not likely has been reported, which is the poet’s saying: Why do people despise me when I have passed the age of forty? And after that: The brother of fifty is a strong society and the passing of the years attracts me The verses before and after it are broken. The first of these verses is: I am the son of Jala and Talaa Al-Thnaya. When I put on the turban, you will know me. Al-Farra’ narrated on the authority of Banu Amir that they say: I stayed with him for years, spending. He said: Banu Tamim do not spend it. It is said: The people became barren, meaning they became dry. From this is the saying of Ibn al-Zubayri: The men of Mecca are old and lean 130- And a decrease in the fruits due to the lack of rain and the many defects so that they may remember so that they may learn a lesson and turn away from their misguidance.
7:131: His statement: 131- So when good comes to them, they say, ‘This is ours’ meaning the good quality of fertility, abundant rain, good fruits, and cheap prices. They say, ‘This is ours’ meaning, we were given it by merit, and it is specific to us. But if evil befalls them meaning, a bad quality of drought, famine, frequent diseases, and the like, they take ill omen from Moses and those with him meaning, they take ill omen from Moses and those with him from the believers in him. The original is yatatawyara, the ta’ was assimilated into the ta’. Talhah read tatayyurna as a past tense verb. The Arabs used to take ill omen from birds and animals, then it was used later for anyone who took ill omen from something. An example of this is the statement of God the Almighty: And if evil befalls them, they say, ‘This is from you’ It was said: The reason for defining good is that it occurs frequently, and the reason for defining bad is that it occurs rarely. His saying: Indeed, their omen is with God means the cause of their good and evil, with all that befalls them of fertility and famine, is from God, not because of Moses and those with him. This answer was in keeping with what they believed and what they understood. For this reason, he used the word bird to refer to the good and evil that occurs by God’s decree, wisdom, and will. But most of them do not know this, rather they attribute good and evil to other than God out of ignorance.
7:132: Al-Hasan read their bird, his saying: 132- And they said, ‘No matter what sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not believe you.’ Al-Khalil said: The root of whatever is the conditional ma, to which ma for emphasis is added, as is added to all other letters, such as: wherever, “wherever,” however, and whenever, but they disliked the meeting of two identical letters, so they replaced the first alif with a ha. Al-Kisa’i said: Its origin is mah meaning: refrain from what you bring us of a sign, and the conditional ma was added to it. It was said: it is a single word with which it is rewarded, and the place of mahma is the nominative case as a subject, or the accusative case with a verb that is explained by what follows it, and min aya is to clarify mahma, and they called it a sign in mockery of Moses as is indicated by what follows it, and it is to bewitch us with it meaning to divert us from what we are doing as the magicians do with their magic, and the pronoun in bih refers to mahma, and the pronoun in bih refers to ayah, and it was said: they both refer to mahma, and the masculinity of the first is based on the wording, and the femininity of the second is based on the meaning fa-ma nahwa laka bi-mu’minin is the answer to the condition: meaning: we are not believing in you: they informed about themselves that they do not believe in anything that he brings of the signs that are, in their opinion, magic.
7:133: Then the punishment from God the Almighty descended upon them, as explained in His saying: 133- So We sent upon them the flood which is heavy rain. Al-Akhfash said: The singular form is tufanah, and it was said: It is a source like rajhan and niqas so it has no singular form, and it was said that tufan means death. Al-Nahhas said: The flood in the language is what is destructive from death or flood: that is, what surrounds them and destroys them. And the locusts are the well-known animals that God sent to eat their crops and they ate them. And the lice it was said: They are the gourd, and the gourd is the locust before it flies, and it was said: They are weevils, and it was said fleas, and it was said small black animals, and it was said a type of monkeys, and it was said dung beetles. Al-Nahhas said: It is possible that all of these things were sent upon them. Al-Hasan read al-qamil with a fatha on the qaf and a sukoon on the meem. The rest read it with a damma on the qaf and a fatha on the meem with a shaddah. Ata Al-Khurasani interpreted lice as lice, and frogs as the plural of frog, which is the well-known animal that lives in water, and blood it was narrated that the Nile flowed blood on them, and it was said that it is nosebleeds. His statement: detailed signs means clear. Al-Zajjaj said: It is accusative as a state. The meaning is: We sent these things upon them while they were clear and evident signs, but they were arrogant meaning they were too proud to believe in God, and they were a criminal people who were not guided to the truth nor did they refrain from falsehood.
7:134: His saying: 134- And when the punishment fell upon them meaning the torment with these matters that God sent upon them, and it was read with a damma on the ra' and they are two languages, and it was said: This punishment was a plague that killed seventy thousand Copts in one day They said, O Moses, call upon your Lord for us with what He has entrusted to you meaning with what He has entrusted to you of knowledge, or with what He has chosen for you of prophethood, or with what He has entrusted to you to call upon and He will answer you, and the ba' is related to the word supplicate in the sense of help us to what we ask for from supplication by the right of what you have of God's covenant, or supplicate for us seeking intercession with Him through His covenant with you, and it was said that the ba' is for an oath, and its answer is that we will believe: meaning we swear by God's covenant with you If you remove the punishment from us, we will believe in you on the basis that the answer to the condition prevailed in place of the answer to the oath, and on the basis that the ba' is not for an oath, the lam in If you remove the punishment from us is the answer to an omitted oath, and we will believe is the answer to the condition The answer to the oath, And We will surely send with you the Children of Israel, was in apposition to We will surely believe. They had been keeping the Children of Israel with them, treating them with disgrace in their work, so they promised him to send them with him.
7:135: 135- So when We removed the punishment from them for a term they were to reach meaning, We removed the punishment from them when they returned to Moses and asked him what they asked, but not an absolute removal, rather a removal restricted to a goal, which is the term set for their destruction by drowning, and the answer to when they break meaning they break what they had agreed upon for themselves. And when is the suddenness: meaning they suddenly break the promise and rush to it.
7:136: 136- So We took revenge on them meaning We wanted to take revenge on them for their breach of faith due to the many sins they had committed. So We drowned them in the sea meaning the ocean. It was said that it is the one whose bottom cannot be comprehended, and it was said that it is its depth and middle. The phrase because they denied Our signs is an explanation for the drowning. And they were heedless of them is conjoined with they denied: meaning they were heedless of the punishment indicated by We took revenge, or of the signs in which they did not believe, but rather denied them, and in their denial they were in the position of those who are heedless of them. The second is more appropriate because both phrases are an explanation for the drowning. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine, he said: years of famine. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, he said: years of disasters, and a decrease in the fruits, less than that. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawadir Al-Usul and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When God seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine, everything dried up for them, and their livestock was lost, even the Nile of Egypt dried up. They gathered before Pharaoh and said: If you are as you claim, then bring us water from the Nile of Egypt. He said: Water will come to you in the morning. So when they left him, he said: What have I done if I am not able to bring water from the Nile of Egypt in the morning? They have denied me. When it was the middle of the night, he got up, washed himself, put on a woolen coat, then went out barefoot until he came to the Nile of Egypt and said: O God, You know that I know that You are able to fill the Nile of Egypt with water, so fill it with water. He did not know until the water level was low, so he went out and the Nile began to gush with water because of what God had intended for them of destruction. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: But when good comes to them, he said: well-being and prosperity, they say, ‘This is for us,’ we are more deserving of it. But if evil befalls them, he said: calamity and punishment, they see Moses as an ill omen, he said: they see him as a bad omen. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Unquestionably, their bad omen is with God, he said: The command is from God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The flood is death. Ibn Kathir said: It is a strange hadith. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The flood is drowning. These narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The flood is death in every case. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The flood is rain that rained continuously day and night for eight days. The lice are the winged locusts. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority who said: The flood is a command from your Lord, then he recited: And a scourge from your Lord swept over it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The flood is water, plague and locusts. He said: It eats the nails of their doors and clothes, and the lice are the crawling frogs and frogs that fall on their beds and in their food, and the blood is in their clothes, water and food. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The lice are the crawling frogs. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The frogs were wild, but when God sent them to the people of Pharaoh, they heard and obeyed, so they started throwing themselves into the boiling pot and into the ovens while they were bubbling. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The Nile flowed with blood, so the Israelite would draw pure water and the Pharaoh would draw blood, and they would share one vessel, so what was on the Israelite would be pure water and what was on the Pharaoh would be blood. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam regarding His statement: and the blood, he said: God sent nosebleeds upon them. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Moses stayed with the people of Pharaoh for forty years after he defeated the magicians, showing them signs, locusts, lice and frogs. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding His statement: detailed signs, he said: They were detailed signs, one after the other, so that God would have an argument against them. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: One follows the other, remaining among them from one Saturday to another, then it is lifted from them for a month. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Al-Rajz: the torment.” Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr that he said: Al-Rajz is the plague. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Until a term they are about to reach, he said: drowning. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: the sea is the ocean. And he also narrated something similar on the authority of al-Suddi.
7:137: His statement: 137- And We caused to inherit the people meaning the Children of Israel who were oppressed meaning humiliated and degraded by serving Pharaoh and his people the easts and wests of the earth in the accusative case by We caused to inherit. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: The original meaning of the easts and wests of the earth then it was deleted in then they were in the accusative case. The first is more apparent because it is said: I caused him to inherit the money, and the land is Egypt and the Levant, and its easts are the directions of its east. And its wests are the directions of its west, and it was that which belonged to Pharaoh and his people from the Copts. It was said: What is meant is all of the earth because David and Solomon were from the Children of Israel, and they owned the land. His statement: which We blessed is a description of the easts and wests. It was said: The description of the earth and the blessing in it is the production of crops and fruits from it in the most perfect way and the most beneficial way to spend. His saying: And the good word of your Lord has been fulfilled means it has passed and continued in its entirety. The word is And We desired to bestow favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them heirs. This is a promise from God, the Most High, of victory and triumph over the enemies and seizing their possessions. Al-Hasna is an adjective for the word, and it is the feminine of al-Ahsan. The completion of this word is upon the Children of Israel because of their patience in the face of what they suffered at the hands of Pharaoh and his people. His saying: And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were making Destruction is annihilation: meaning We destroyed with ruin what they were making of buildings and what they were building Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim, ya’rshūn with a damma on the ra’. Al-Kisa’i said: It is the language of Tamim. Ibrahim bin Abi Ubla read ya’rshūn with a shaddah on the ra’ and a damma on the letter of the present tense. The rest read it with a kasra on the ra’ and a light sukoon: meaning what they used to build of gardens, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: And it is He who produced gardens trellised and untrellised. It was said: the meaning of trellising is building. It is said: a throne trellises: meaning he built, he builds.
7:138: His saying: 138- And We crossed the sea with the Children of Israel. We crossed it with them and cut it. It was read We crossed it with emphasis, and it has the same meaning as the reading of the majority: Then they came upon a people who were devoted to their idols. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read ya’kifun with a kasra on the kaf, while the rest read it with a damma. It is said: ‘Akaif ya’kif: and ya’kif means to stay on something and stick to it, and the source of both is ‘akuf. It was said: These people whom the Children of Israel came to were from Lakhm who were staying in Ar-Raqqah, and their idols were statues of cows. It was also said: They were Canaanites. They said meaning the Children of Israel when they saw those statues O Moses, make for us a god meaning an idol that we can worship like the one these people had. So the kaf is related to an omitted word that was an attribute of a god, so Moses answered them, and He said, ‘Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly’ He described them as ignorant because they had seen signs of God that would deter anyone with the slightest knowledge from seeking to worship other than God. However, these people, I mean the Children of Israel, were the most stubborn, ignorant, and fickle of God’s creation. What they did in this regard has already been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:139: Then Moses said to them: Indeed, these meaning the people who were devoted to idols are in ruins ruin is destruction, and every broken vessel is ruined: meaning that these people are in ruins, destroyed and broken, and what they are in is idol worship. He informed them that this religion that these people are following is ruined and destroyed, and nothing of it is completed. His statement: And what they were doing is in vain meaning that all the deeds they were doing with their worship of idols are gone and vanished. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: In making these people a name for in and presenting the predicate of the subject from the sentence that is its predicate, he marked the idol worshippers as being the ones exposed to ruin, and that it does not exceed them at all, and that it is a lasting blow to warn them of the consequences of what they sought and to make hateful to them what they loved.
7:140: His statement: 140- Should I seek for you a god other than God? The question is for denial and rebuke: that is, how can I seek for you a god other than God to worship, when you have witnessed from His great signs what is sufficient for some of them? The meaning is that what you have sought will never happen. The introduction of the hamza to ghayr is to indicate that the reprehensible thing is that the one seeking is other than Him, glory be to Him, as a god. Ghayr is the object of the verb that follows it, and god is a distinguishing feature or a state, and the phrase And He has favored you over the worlds is in the accusative case as a state: that is, and the situation is that He favored you over the worlds of the people of your time with what He bestowed upon you of destroying your enemy and making you successors on earth and bringing you out from humiliation and disgrace to honor and elevation, so how do you respond to these blessings by seeking to worship other than Him.
7:141: His saying: 141- And when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh meaning, remember the time when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh after they had been your masters, enslaving you in whatever they wanted from you and treating you with all kinds of humiliation. This is on the basis that this speech was narrated from Moses. However, if it is in the sense of addressing the Jews who were present in the time of Muhammad, then it means remember when We delivered your ancestors from the people of Pharaoh. The phrase they subject you to the worst of torment is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh while they were subjecting you to the worst of torment. It is possible that it is a new sentence to explain what they were in from which He saved them, and the phrase they kill your sons and spare your women explains the phrase before it, or is a substitute for it. This has been explained previously, and the reference in His saying: And in that is to the torment: meaning in this torment in which you were a great trial upon you from your Lord. It has been said: the reference is to salvation, and the trial is the blessing. The first is more appropriate. Abdul Razzaq, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: The eastern regions of the earth and the western regions which We have blessed, he said: Ash-Sham. These people narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada. Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Shawdhab who said: It is Palestine. Hadiths have been narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the virtues of Ash-Sham, but this is not the place to mention them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And the good word of your Lord has been fulfilled, he said: The victory of the people of Moses over Pharaoh and the establishment of God for them in the land and what He inherited from them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they did not build, he said: They did not build. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Then they came upon a people devoted to their idols, he said: Lakhm and Judham. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Jawni something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding the verse: “Statues of cows made of copper. When it came to the Samaritan calf, it appeared to them that it was from those cows. That was the beginning of the matter of the calf, so that God would have an argument against them and take revenge on them after that.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laythi, who said: “We went out with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) before Hunayn and we passed by a lote tree. I said: O Messenger of God, make this for us Dhat Anwat as the infidels have Dhat Anwat. The infidels used to hang their weapons on a lote tree and devote themselves around it. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: God is Great. This is like what the Children of Israel said to Moses: Make for us a god as they have gods. You are following the ways of those who were before you.” Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Katheer bin Abdullah bin Awf on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Katheer is very weak. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, destruction, he said: loss. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on his authority that he said: destruction.
7:142: This is among the things with which God honored and glorified Moses, peace be upon him. The thirtieth is Dhul-Qi'dah and the tenth is Dhul-Hijjah. God set this period as a time for Moses to confide in Him and speak to Him. It was said that the conversation was on the Day of Sacrifice. The benefit is in 142- So the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights. Knowing that the thirtieth and ten are forty nights, it is assumed that what is meant is that we completed the thirty with ten of them, so it was made clear that the ten is not the thirty, and forty nights is accusative in the state of state: meaning, so the state of his being an adult was completed as forty nights. His statement: And Moses said to his brother Aaron, Take my place among my people, meaning, be my successor among them. Moses said: This is when he wanted to proceed to the confinement. And amend the affairs of the Children of Israel by governing them well, being kind to them, and checking up on their conditions. And do not follow the way of the corrupters, meaning, do not follow the way of the disobedient and do not be an aid to the oppressors. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: And We made an appointment with Moses 1:100, he said: Dhu al-Qa’dah and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. Abd al-Razzaq and Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: “Moses said to his al-Nas 114:My Lord promised me thirty nights that I would meet Him and take Aaron’s place among you. When Moses departed to his Lord, God increased him by ten, and their trial was in the ten that God increased him by. When thirty nights had passed, the Samaritan saw Gabriel, so he took a handful of dirt from the horse’s footprint, then he mentioned the story of the Samaritan.”
7:143: The lam in 143- for our appointed time is for specificity: that is, his coming was specific to the mentioned appointed time, meaning that he came at the promised time. And his Lord spoke to him means He made him hear His speech without an intermediary. His saying: Show me so I may look at you means show me yourself so I may look at you: that is, he asked him to look at Him, longing to see Him when he heard His speech. Moses's asking to see Him indicates that it was permissible for him in general, and if it were impossible for him, he would not have asked for it. The answer with his saying: You will not see Me indicates that he will not see Him at this time in which he asked to see Him, or that he will not see Him as long as the one seeing Him is alive in this world. As for seeing him in the Hereafter, it has been proven by the successive narrations that are not hidden from those who know the pure Sunnah. Arguing about such matters and evading them is of no benefit. The path of truth is clear, but believing in a doctrine that a person grew up with and learned from his fathers and his people, without paying attention to what is required of the servants of this pure Shariah, leads to fanaticism. Even if the fanatic’s sight is sound, his insight is blind. His ear is deaf to hearing the truth. He rejects the truth while thinking that he has rejected nothing but falsehood and he thinks that what he grew up with is the truth, out of negligence and ignorance of what God has obligated upon him of correct contemplation and receiving what the Book and Sunnah have brought with submission and surrender. How few are the fair-minded after the appearance of these doctrines in the fundamentals and branches, for with them the door of truth has become blocked, and the path of fairness has become rugged. The command is God’s, the Most High, and guidance comes from Him. The young man refuses to follow anything but his desires, and the path of truth is clear to him. The phrase He said, 'You will not see Me' is a resumption of the sentence because it is an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: What did God say to him? And the correction in His saying: But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me means that you will not be able to see Me, nor will what is greater than you in mass, solidity, and strength, which is the mountain, be able to see Me. So look at it. If it remains in its place and does not shake when I see it, then you will see Me. And if it is weaker than that, then you are weaker than it. So this statement is like giving an example to Moses, peace be upon him, of the mountain. It was said: It is from the category of suspending the impossible. If we accept this, then it is in the vision in this world, for what we have presented. Both the Mu'tazila and Ash'ari sects have held fast to this verse: The Mu'tazila used as evidence His statement: You will not see Me, and His command to look at the mountain, and the Ash'aris said: The condition of the vision on the stability of the mountain indicates that it is permissible and not impossible. It is not hidden from you that the vision in the afterlife is separate from all of this, and the disagreement between them is about it, not about the vision in this world, as the disagreement about it was in the time of the Companions and their speech about it is well known. His statement: So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He rendered it level means: appeared, from your saying: I exposed the bride, meaning I brought her out, and I exposed the sword: I purified it from rust, and something became exposed. Meaning: When his Lord appeared to the mountain, He made it level. It was said that the manifestation is His command and power. Qatrub and others said that “Dakka” is a source with the meaning of the passive participle: that is, He made it crushed and pounded so it became dust. This is according to the reading of those who read Dakka with the source, and they are the people of Medina and Basra. As for the reading of the people of Kufa, Ja’aluhu Dakka is feminine, and the plural is Dakkawat like Hamra and Hamrawat, and it is a name for a protruding hill from the ground or for flat land, so the meaning is that the mountain became small like a hill or flat land. Al-Kisa’i said: Dakka: the wide mountains, the singular of which is Adak, and Dakkawat is the plural of Dakka, and they are hills of clay that are not thick, and Dakkadik: what appears from the ground and does not rise, and a she-camel Dakka: it has no hump. And Moses fell unconscious meaning unconscious, taken from the thunderbolt. The meaning is that his state when he was unconscious became like the state of someone who faints when struck by lightning. It is said: The man was struck by lightning, so he is struck by lightning. When he recovered from his fainting spell, “he said: Glory be to You” meaning I declare You to be far removed from asking something You did not permit me to ask. I repent to You from returning to such a question. Al-Qurtubi said: The nation agreed that this repentance was not for a sin, for the prophets are infallible. It was said: It was repentance for killing the Copt, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri, but it has no basis in such a situation. And I am the first of the believers in You before my people who are present in this age and acknowledge Your greatness and majesty.
7:144: And the sentence 144- He said, O Moses is a new sentence like the one before it, including the honoring of Moses and his being singled out for what God singled him out with. And selection: choosing and choosing: meaning I chose you over the people of your time with my message. Thus Nafi' and Ibn Kathir read it in the singular, and the rest read it in the plural. And the message is a source, and the origin of it is the singular, and whoever pluralizes it, it is as if he considered that the message is of types, so he pluralized it because of the difference in types, and what is meant by speech here: speaking. God the Almighty bestowed upon him these two great types of honor, which are the message and speaking without an intermediary, then He commanded him to take what He gave him: meaning He gave him of this noble honor, and He commanded him to be among those who are grateful for this great gift and great honor.
7:145: His saying: 145- And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things. Of all things: meaning of everything that the Children of Israel needed in their religion and their worldly life, and these tablets: are the Torah. It was said: it was made of green emerald, and it was said: of red ruby, and it was said: of peridot, and it was said: of solid rock. There is a difference of opinion regarding the number of tablets and the extent of their length and width. Tablets: the plural of tablet, and it was called a tablet because the meanings appear on it. God Almighty attributed writing to Himself as an honor to what is written on the tablets, and it is written by His command, glory be to Him. It was said: It is a writing that God created on the tablets, and of everything is in the accusative case as the object of We wrote and admonition and detailing is a substitute for the place of everything, meaning an admonition for those who learn from it from the Children of Israel and others and a detailing of the rulings that need detailing. Take it with strength meaning take the tablets with strength: meaning with diligence and activity. It was said: The pronoun refers to the messages, or to everything, or to the Torah. It was said: This command is based on the implication of the saying: meaning, so We said to him, take it. It was said that take it is a substitute for His saying: Take what I have given you “And command your people to take the best of it” meaning the best of what is in it for its reward is greater than others, and it is like His Almighty saying: Follow the best of what has been revealed to you from the Your Lord, and His saying: and they follow the best of it, and it is better to be patient with others and forgive them and act according to the determination rather than the concession, and according to the obligation rather than the voluntary, and to do what is commanded and leave what is forbidden. His saying: I will show you the abode of the wicked, it was said: it is the land of Egypt which belonged to Pharaoh and his people, and it was said: the dwellings of Aad and Thamud, and it was said: it is Hell, and it was said: the dwellings of the infidels from the tyrants and giants so that they may take a lesson from it, and it was said: the abode is destruction. The meaning: I will show you the destruction of the wicked. The meaning of wickedness has been explained above.
7:146: His statement: 146- I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right. It was said: The meaning of I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant is that I will prevent them from understanding My Book. It was also said: I will turn them away from believing in it.
