It was also said: I will turn them away from benefiting from it as a punishment for their arrogance, as in His statement: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate. It was also said: I will seal their hearts so that they will not reflect on it or take heed from it. There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of the verses. Some say they are miracles, others say they are the revealed books, and others say they are the creation of the heavens and the earth and their turning away from them so that they do not consider them. There is nothing to prevent the verses from being interpreted as meaning all of that, as interpreting the interpretation as meaning all of the aforementioned meanings. Without right is either related to His statement, they are arrogant, meaning they are arrogant with what is not right, or to an omitted word that is a state: meaning they are arrogant while engaging in something other than right. His statement, And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, is conjoined with they are arrogant, and is consistent with it in the ruling of the relative clause. The meaning is, I will turn away from My signs the arrogant ones who abandon belief in what they see of the signs. Under every sign are the revealed signs, the signs of creation, and the miracles: meaning they do not believe in any sign, whatever it may be. Malik bin Dinar read yaru with a damma on the ya in both places, and the sentence And if they see the path of right guidance, they will not take it as a path is conjoined to what precedes it and is included in its ruling, as is the sentence And if they see the path of error, they will take it as a path, and the meaning is that if they find a path of right guidance, they will abandon it and avoid it, and if they see a path of error, they will follow it and choose it for themselves. The people of Medina and Basra read al-Rashd with a damma on the ra and a sukoon on the sheen. The people of Kufa, except for Asim, read it with a fatha on the ra and the sheen. Abu Ubaidah said: Abu Amr differentiated between rashd and rashd and said: rashd is righteousness and rashd is in religion. Al-Nahhas said: Sibawayh holds that rashd and rashd are like saghd and ghadhd. Al-Kisa'i said: What is correct from Abu Amr and others is what Abu Ubaidah said. The root of guidance in the language is that a person obtains what he wants, and it is the opposite of disappointment. The reference in his saying that is to the diversion: that is, that diversion is due to their denial, or the reference is to arrogance and lack of belief in the signs, avoiding the path of guidance, and following the path of error. The demonstrative pronoun is the subject, and its predicate is the sentence because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them, meaning because of their denial of the signs and their heedlessness of them.
7:147: The relative pronoun in 147- And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter is the subject, and its predicate is their deeds have become worthless. What is meant by the meeting of the Hereafter is the meeting of the Hereafter: that is, their meeting it or their meeting what they were promised in it, on the basis that the addition is to the circumstance. And the nullification of deeds is their invalidity: that is, the invalidity of what they did of what was conceived as obedience such as charity and kinship, even if they were in a state of disbelief and had no acts of obedience. It is possible that what is meant is that they are invalidated after they were expected to benefit, assuming their conversion to Islam, according to what is in the authentic hadith: When I converted to Islam for what I had sent before of good. "Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?" of disbelief in God, and the denial of His signs, and turning away from the path of truth, and following the path of error. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawader Al-Usul on the authority of Ka’b who said: When God spoke to Moses, he said: O Lord, is this how you speak? He said: O Moses, I only speak to you with the power of ten thousand tongues and I have the power of all tongues, and if I spoke to you with the essence of my speech, you would be nothing. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu’aym in Al-Hilya and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Jabir who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God spoke to Moses on the Day of Mount Sinai, He spoke to him with a speech other than the one with which He spoke to him on the Day He called him. Moses said to Him: O Lord, is this the speech with which you spoke to me? He said: O Moses, I only spoke to you with the power of ten thousand tongues and I have the power of all tongues and stronger than that. When Moses returned to the Children of Israel, they said: O Moses, describe to us the speech of the Most Merciful. He said: You cannot do it. Have you not seen the sounds of the thunderbolts that kill? It is the sweetest sweetness you have ever heard. That is close to it, but it is not the same.” Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Abu al-Huwayrith Abd al-Rahman ibn Muawiyah who said: God only spoke to Moses as much as he could bear of His words. If He had spoken all of His words, nothing would have been able to bear it. So Moses remained for forty nights without anyone seeing him except that he died from the light of the Lord of the Worlds. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: “He said: My Lord, show me, that I may look at You,” meaning: Give me, that I may look at You. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, who said: When he heard the speech, he hoped to see You. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When Moses said to his Lord, the Blessed and Exalted: My Lord, show me, that I may look at You, God said: O Moses, You will not see Me. He said: He says: You do not see Me, and that will never happen. O Moses, no one will see Me and then live. Moses said: My Lord, I see You and then die, which is more beloved to me than not seeing You and then living. So God said to Moses: O Moses, look at the great, tall, strong mountain. If it remains in its place, he said: If it remains in its place, it does not weaken or collapse because of some of what it sees of My greatness, then you will see Me, you because of your weakness and humiliation, and if the mountain collapses because of its strength, strength, and greatness, then you are weaker and more humiliated. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi - who authenticated it - Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Adi in Al-Kamil, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Kitab Al-Ru’yah narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘But when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He rendered it level.’ He said: ‘Like this,’ and he pointed with his two fingers and placed his thumbs on the tip of the little finger, and in another version on the upper joint of the little finger, and the mountain crumbled, ‘and Moses fell unconscious.’” In another version: The mountain crumbled into the earth and will continue to fall into it until the Day of Resurrection. This hadith is authentic according to the criteria of Muslim. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The mountain that God commanded him to look at was Mount Tur. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Kitab Al-Ru'yah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain," he said: He revealed only the size of a little finger from it. "He made it crumble," he said: dust. "And Moses fell unconscious," he said: unconscious. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilyah and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When God revealed Himself to the mountain, six mountains flew away because of His greatness. Three fell in Madinah and three in Makkah. In Madinah: Uhud, Warqan and Radwa, and in Makkah: Hira, Thabir and Thawr." Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God revealed Himself to Moses, seven mountains flew apart. Five of them were in the Hijaz, and two were in Yemen. In the Hijaz: Uhud, Thabir, Hira, Thawr, and Warqan, and in Yemen: Hadur and Sabr.” Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that when Moses’ Lord spoke to him, he wanted to look at Him, so he asked Him, and He said: You will not see Me, but look at the mountain. He said: So the angels surrounded the mountain, and fire surrounded the angels, and angels surrounded the fire, and fire surrounded them. Then his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, and a figure like the little finger appeared from it, and He made the mountain crumble and Moses fell unconscious. He remained unconscious for as long as God willed, then he regained consciousness and said: Glory be to You, I repent to You, and I am the first of the believers from among the Children of Israel. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, who said: God wrote the tablets for Moses while he heard the scratching of the pens on the tablet. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The tablets that were sent down to Moses were made of lote trees in Paradise. The length of the tablet was twelve cubits.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: They used to say that the tablets were made of ruby. I say that they were made of emerald and their writing was gold. God wrote it with His own hand, and the people of the heavens heard the scratching of the pens. I say: May God have mercy on Saeed, how he did not need to say what he said on his own authority, for such things cannot be said based on opinion or intuition. What is most likely is that many of the Salaf, may God have mercy on them, used to ask the Jews about these matters, and for this reason they differed and became confused. This one said it was made of wood, this one said it was made of ruby, this one said it was made of emerald, this one said it was made of chrysolite, this one said it was made of hail, and this one said it was made of stone. Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things, everything they were commanded to do and forbidden to do. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Mujahid. The Salaf differed greatly regarding what was written on the tablets, and there is no objection to interpreting what was written as meaning all of that for lack of contradiction. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, Take it firmly, he said: with seriousness and firmness. I will show you the abode of the wicked, he said: the abode of the disbelievers. Ibn Jarir narrated from him, And command your people to take the best of it, he said: Moses was commanded to take it more severely than he commanded his people. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi ibn Anas, Take it with strength, he said: with obedience. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Shaykh narrated on the authority of As-Suddi, regarding his statement, Take it with strength, meaning with diligence and effort, and command your people to take the best of it, he said: with the best they can find of it. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, I will show you the home of the wicked, he said: their destiny in the Hereafter. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, he said: their homes in this world. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Hell. Abu Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada, he said: Egypt. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Shaykh narrated on the authority of As-Suddi, regarding his statement, I will turn them away from My signs, he said: from pondering over My signs. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, from My signs, he said: from the creation of the heavens and the earth and the signs contained therein. I will turn them away from pondering over them or taking heed. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah regarding the verse, saying: I will take away from them the understanding of the Qur’an.
7:148: His statement: 148- And the people of Moses took after him meaning after his exit to the mountain from their ornaments is related to took or to an omitted word that occurred as a state, and from is for partiality, or for beginning, or for clarification, and ornaments is the plural of ornaments. The people of Medina and Basra read from their ornaments with a damma on the ha’ and a shaddah on the ya’. The people of Kufa except for Asim read it with a kasra on the ha’. Ya’qub read it with a fatha on the ha’ and a light ya’. An-Nahhas said: The plural of halli is halli and halli is halwa like thadi and thadi and thadi. The original is halwa. The waw was assimilated into the yaa and the lam was broken because of its proximity to the yaa and the haa was broken because of the kasra of the lam and its damma according to the original. The halli was attributed to them even though it was for others because the addition is permissible for the slightest connection. Ajlan is the object of akhtada and it was said that it means making, so it takes two objects, the second of which is deleted: that is, they took a calf as a god. Jassadan is a substitute for ajlan and it was said that it is a description of it. The bellowing is the screaming: it is said: he bellowed loudly if he screamed, and likewise he bellowed loudly. The taking of the calf was attributed to all the people even though the Samaritan alone took it because he was one of them and they were pleased with his action. It was narrated that when Moses promised his people thirty nights and delayed them in the additional ten, the Samaritan said to the Children of Israel, and he was obeyed by them: You have with you some of the jewelry of the people of Pharaoh that you borrowed from them to adorn yourselves with on the feast, and you went out while he was with you, and God drowned his people from the Copts, so bring it, so they gave it to him and he made from it the aforementioned calf. His statement: Have they not seen that he does not speak to them? The question is for rebuke and rebuke: that is, have they not considered that this one whom they have taken as a god is not able to speak to them, let alone be able to bring them benefit or ward off harm from them. Nor does he guide them to a way that is, a clear path for them to follow. They took him and were wrongdoers that is, they took him as a god. And they were wrongdoers to themselves in taking him or in everything, and this taking includes this.
7:149: His saying: 149- And when it fell into their hands meaning they regretted and were perplexed after Moses returned from the appointed time. It is said of the regretful and perplexed person: he has fallen into his hand. Al-Akhfash said: It is said: he fell into his hand and he dropped. And whoever said: he fell into their hands in the active form, grief, then the meaning according to him is: the regret fell. Its origin is that it is the nature of someone whose regret and remorse are intense to bite his hand in grief, so his hand becomes fallen into it, because his mouth has fallen into it. Al-Azhari, Al-Zajjaj, Al-Nahhas and others said: The meaning of fell into their hands is: in their hearts and souls, as it is said: Something bad happened to him in his hand, even though it is impossible for it to be in the hand, likening what happens in the heart and soul to what happens in the hand, because doing things is usually done by hand. God Almighty said: That is because of what your hands have put forth. Also, regret, even if it takes place in the heart, its effect appears in the body, because the regretful person bites his hand and hits one hand against the other. God Almighty said: So he began to turn his hands over what he had spent therein. And from this is The Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands, meaning from regret. Also, the regretful person places his chin in his hand. And they saw that they had gone astray. Fell: meaning they realized that they had gone astray by taking the calf and that they had been afflicted with disobeying God Almighty. They said, ‘If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us,’ Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read with the superlative in both verbs, and the rest read with the subjunctive and the lam is for swearing. And his answer is, We will surely be among the losers. And in this speech of theirs there is that which indicates seeking help from God and supplication and entreaty in the question, and there will come in Surat Taha, God willing, what indicates that this speech narrated from them here occurred after the return of Moses, and it was only mentioned here before his return in order to narrate what they said and did in one place.
7:150: His saying: 150- And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. This is a statement of what happened with Moses after his return, and the accusative of angry and grieved is in the state of the state, and grief means intense anger. It was said: It is a position behind anger, more severe than it, and it is sorrow, regret, and sorrow. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: God informed him before his return that they had been tempted, so he returned angry and sad. He said, ‘How evil is that which you have done after me.’ This is a censure from Moses to his al-Nas 114:that is, how evil is the work that you have done after me: that is, after my absence from you. It is said: He succeeded him with good and he succeeded him with evil. He denounced what they did and denounced them because they had witnessed signs that some of which necessitate aversion and belief in God alone. However, this is the way of the Children of Israel in the changing of their state and the confusion of their actions. Then he said, denouncing them: You hastened the command of your Lord. Haste means advancing something before its time. It is said: I hastened the thing, I preceded it, and I hastened the man, I made him rush, and the meaning is: You hastened from waiting for the command of your Lord: that is, His appointment that He promised me, which is forty, so you did what you did. It was said that its meaning is: You hastened the wrath of your Lord. It was said that its meaning is: Did you hasten to worship the calf before the command of your Lord came to you? And he threw down the tablets meaning he threw them away because of the intensity of his anger and regret when he looked down upon his people while they were worshipping the calf. His statement: And he seized his brother by the head, dragging him towards him meaning he seized his brother Aaron by the head or by the hair of his head while he was dragging him towards him: he did that to him because he did not denounce the Samaritan or anyone else for what he saw of the Children of Israel worshipping the calf, so Aaron said apologizing to him: Son of my mother, indeed the people have weakened me and almost killed me meaning I could not change what they did for these two matters: their weakening of me and their coming close to killing me. He only said son of my mother despite being his brother from his father and mother, because it is a word of kindness and compassion, and because it was, as was said, a believer. Al-Zajjaj said: It was said that Aaron was the brother of Moses through his mother, not through his father. Ibn Umm was read with a fatha on the m to liken it to fifteen, so it became like saying: O fifteen, come forward. Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra' and Abu Ubaid said: The fat-ha is based on the estimation of Ya Ibn Umma. The Basrans said that this statement is wrong: because the alif is light and is not deleted, but the two names are made into one name like fifteen, and this was chosen by Al-Zajjaj and Al-Nahhas. As for those who read with the kasra of the meem, it is based on the estimation of Ibn Ummi, then the ya' was deleted and the kasra was kept to indicate it. Al-Akhfash and Abu Hatim said: Ibn Umm with the kasra is like you say: Ya boy come, and it is an irregular language and reading it is far-fetched, and this is only in what is added to you. And Ibn Umm was read with the ya' confirmed. His saying: So do not let the enemies gloat over me Gloating is the pleasure of the enemies for what befalls those they oppose with calamities, and from it is his saying, may God's prayers and peace be upon him: O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of judgment, the attainment of misery, the effort of affliction, and the gloating of the enemies and it is in the Sahih, and from it is the saying of the poet: If time brings its scourge upon some people, it will bring down the last of us. So tell those who gloat over us to wake up. Those who gloat will meet what we met. Meaning: Do not do to me what would cause them to gloat. Mujahid and Malik ibn Dinar read do not let the enemies gloat over me with a fatha on the letter of the present tense and a fatha on the meem and raising the enemies so that the action is attributed to them: meaning that this will not be from them for an action you do to me. It was narrated from Mujahid that he read tashmāt as mentioned above with the enemies in the accusative case. Ibn Jinni said: The meaning is do not let you gloat over me, O Lord. This is permissible as in His statement: God mocks them and similar to it. Then he returned to the intended meaning and implied a verb with which he made the enemies in the accusative case as if he said: Do not let the enemies gloat over me, O Lord. How far this reading is from the truth and how far its interpretation is from the aspects of grammar. His statement: and do not place me with the wrongdoing people means do not place me, in Your anger with me, among the wrongdoing al-Nas 114:meaning those who worshipped the calf or do not believe that I am one of them.
7:151: His statement: 151- He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother.' This is a new statement in response to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did Moses say after these words of Aaron? So it was said: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother.' He asked for forgiveness for himself first, and for his brother second, to remove from his brother what he feared of gloating, as if he was denouncing what he did to his brother, and showed that he had no reason to, and asked forgiveness from God for what he had neglected on his part, then he asked forgiveness for his brother if he had fallen short in what is required of them in terms of denouncing them and changing what they had done, then he asked to include him and his brother in the mercy of God that encompasses everything, for He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And the people of Moses took the verse, he said: When they buried her, the Samaritan threw a handful of dirt on her from the footprints of Gabriel’s horse, peace be upon him. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: They borrowed jewelry from the people of Pharaoh, so the Samaritan gathered it and fashioned from it a calf and made it a body flesh and blood that had a lowing sound. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: Mooing he said: The sound. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak he said: The calf moaned a lowing sound, did you not see that God said: Did they not see that it does not speak to them? Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: It fell into their hands he said: They regretted. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated through various chains on the authority of Ibn Abbas regretfully he said: Sad. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ who said: Grief is a station after anger, more severe than that. Abd Bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Muhammad Bin Ka’b who said: Grief is intense anger. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When Moses threw down the tablets, they were broken and lifted up except for one-sixth. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority that he said: God lifted up six-sevenths of them and seven remained. Abu Nu’aym narrated in Al-Hilyah on the authority of Mujahid or Sa’id Bin Jubayr who said: When Moses threw them down, the details were gone and the guidance remained. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: There were nine, two tablets were lifted up and seven remained. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And do not place me with the wrongdoing people, he said: With the people of the calf.
7:152: Anger is the punishment that befell them in this world by killing themselves, and the torment that will befall them in the Hereafter. Humiliation is what God imposed upon them by saying: Humiliation was imposed upon them. It was said that it was their expulsion from their homes, and it was said that it was the jizya, and there is a view on this because it was not taken from them, but rather it was taken from their descendants. It is better to restrict anger and humiliation to this world, because He said: 152- in the life of this world and that this is specific to those who took the calf as a god, not to those of their descendants after them. The mere fact that they were ordered to kill themselves is anger from God upon them, and because of it they become humiliated. Likewise, their exodus from their homes is from the anger of God upon them, and because of it they become patient and humiliated. As for the humiliation that befell their descendants, it is not correct to interpret what is in the verse with it unless it is impossible to carry the verse with its true meaning, and it is not impossible here. And thus do We recompense the slanderers meaning, as we did to these, we do to the slanderers. Slander is lying, so whoever slanders God will receive anger and humiliation from God in this world, even if it is not the same as what these were punished with. Rather, what is meant is what is true to be from the anger of God, glory be to Him, and that there is humiliation in it of any kind.
7:153: 153- And those who have committed evil deeds meaning any evil and then repented from them after doing after them and believed in God indeed, your Lord, after them meaning after this repentance, or after committing these evil deeds for which the doer has repented and believed in God is Forgiving and Merciful meaning He is very forgiving of the sins of His servants and very merciful to them.
7:154: His saying: 154- "And when Moses' anger subsided" The root of silence is stillness and restraint. It is said: The valley ran three times then calmed down: meaning it stopped running. It was said: This is a metaphor as if anger was tempting him to do what he did, and it was saying to him: Say to your people such and such and throw down the tablets and drag your brother's head, so he stopped tempting and was silent. It was said: This statement has a reversal, and the root is Moses was silent from anger, like their saying: I put the finger into the ring, and the ring is the finger, and I put the cap into my head, and my head is the cap. Muawiyah bin Qurra read: And when Moses' anger subsided, and it was read: He was silent and was silent, "He took the tablets that he threw down when he was angry, And in its copy is guidance and mercy." Abrogation is the transfer of what is in a book to another book, and the original from which the transfer was made is called a copy, and the transferred is also called a copy. Al-Qushayri said. The meaning of and in its copy: that is, in what was copied from the broken tablets and transferred to the new tablets guidance and mercy. It was said that the meaning is: and in what was copied for him from it: that is, from the Preserved Tablet. It was also said that the meaning is: and in what was written for him in it, guidance and mercy, so he does not need an original to transfer from it. This is like saying: copy what so-and-so says: that is, record it in your book. The copy is a verb, meaning a passive participle like the sermon. Guidance is what they are guided by of the rulings, and mercy is what they obtain from God when they act upon what is in it of vast mercy. The lam in for those who are is related to something omitted: that is, it is for them or for their sake. The lam in for their Lord they fear is to strengthen the verb because its object precedes it, so it is somewhat weakened by that. Al-Kisa’i stated that it is redundant. Al-Akhfash said: it is the lam of the term, that is, for the sake of their Lord they fear. Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Mubarrad said: it is related to the source of the aforementioned verb, and the meaning is: for those who are their fear for their Lord they fear. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ayoub who said: Abu Qilabah recited this verse: Indeed, those who took the calf until His saying: And thus do We recompense the innovators. He said: It is the recompense of every innovator until the Day of Resurrection that God will humiliate him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Moses was given the Torah on seven tablets of emerald, in which was clarification of everything and an admonition. When he came and saw the Children of Israel devoted to the calf, he threw the Torah from his hand and it shattered. He turned to Aaron and took hold of his head, so God removed six sevenths of it and seven remained. And when Moses’ anger subsided, he took up the tablets, and in their inscription was guidance and mercy. He said: In what remained of it. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid or Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: The tablets were made of emerald, and when Moses threw them down, the details disappeared, and guidance and mercy remained. He read, and We wrote for him on the tablets an admonition and a detailed account of everything. He read, And when Moses’ anger subsided, he took up the tablets, and in their inscription was guidance and mercy. He said: The details were not mentioned here.
7:155: His saying: 155- And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time. This is the beginning of explaining what happened from Moses and from the people he chose, and seventy is the object of chose, and his people is accusative by removing the preposition: that is, from his people by deletion and connection, and similar to it is the saying of Al-Ra’i: People chose you when their character was deteriorating and those who had hope in you became ill. He wants to choose you from among the people, and the meaning of for our appointed time is the time that we set for him after what happened from his people happened, and the appointed time is the speech that was mentioned before because God ordered him to come to the mountain with some people from the Children of Israel who apologized to Him, glory be to Him, for worshipping the calf, as it was said, and the tremor in the language: is the severe earthquake, it was said: they were shaken until they died, so when Moses saw the tremor taking place for them: “He said: My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me,” he said it, peace be upon him, with regret and longing, because the reason for the tremor taking place for them was And when you said, O Moses, we will not believe in you until we see God clearly, so the thunderbolt seized you, as mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, and it was said: these seventy are not those who said, Show us God clearly, but the tremor took them, because of their not stopping the worship of the calf, and it was said: they were people who were not satisfied with the worship of the calf nor forbade the Samaritan and those with him from worshipping it, so the tremor took them because of their silence, and the meaning is if You had willed to destroy us He would have destroyed us for our sins before this time, an admission of his guilt, and his longing for what his people had neglected. The question in his statement: Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done? is for denial: I am not one of those who do that. He said it out of confidence in God’s mercy. The intended meaning is to implore and beseech. It was said that its meaning is supplication and request: i.e. do not destroy us. Al-Mubarrad said: What is meant by the question is a question of reverence, as if he is saying: Moses knew that no one would be destroyed for the sin of another, but it is like the statement of Jesus: If You punish them, they are Your servants. It was said that what is meant by the fools is the seventy, and the meaning is: Will You destroy the Children of Israel for what these fools did in their statement: Show us God openly? It was said that what is meant by them is the Samaritan and his companions. His saying: It is nothing but Your trial means that the trial that these fools have fallen into is nothing but Your trial by which You test whomever You will and examine whomever You will. Perhaps the Prophet, peace be upon him, derived this from the saying of the Most High: Indeed, We have tested your people after you “You misguide with it whomever You will and guide whomever You will” meaning You misguide with this trial whomever You will of Your servants and guide with it whomever You will of them. And similar to it is: To test you as to which of you is best in deed then he returned to supplication and prayer and said: You are our protector meaning the one who is in charge of our affairs so forgive us for our sins and have mercy on us with Your mercy that encompasses all things and You are the best of forgivers of sins.
7:156: 156- And decree for us in this world [that which is] good by granting us success in righteous deeds, or by bestowing upon us abundant blessings in this world of well-being and abundant provision, and in the Hereafter meaning, and decree for us in the Hereafter Paradise by what You reward us with or by what You bestow upon us of bliss in the Hereafter. The phrase Indeed, we have turned to You is an explanation of what preceded it of asking for forgiveness, mercy, and good in this world and in the Hereafter, meaning, we have repented to You and turned back from the misguidance that the Children of Israel fell into. And hud means repentance. It was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah, and the phrase He said, 'My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will' is a new sentence like its counterparts in what came before. It was said that what is meant by punishment here is the trembling. It was also said that it is His, the Most High, command to them to kill themselves, meaning, this is not up to you, O Moses, but whatever you will will be, and whatever I do not will will not be. It appears that the punishment here includes all punishments and the punishment of these people is included in it primarily. It was said: What is meant is whomever I will of those who deserve punishment or whomever I will to lead astray and deprive of success. And My mercy encompasses all things of things from those who are accountable and others. Then the Almighty informed that He will write this vast mercy for those who fear sins and give the zakat imposed on them and those who believe in Our verses meaning they believe in them and submit to them.
7:157: Then the Almighty explained those for whom He has written this mercy in a clearer and more explicit statement than what came before it, saying: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, that is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. So the Jews, Christians, and all other religions were excluded. Unlettered is either a reference to the unlettered nation that does not write or count, and they are the Arabs, or a reference to the mother. The meaning is that he will remain in the state in which he was born, neither writing nor reading what is written. It was said: in reference to the mother of villages, which is Mecca. Who they find means the Jews and Christians: that is, they find his description written with them in the Torah and the Gospel and they are their reference in religion. This speech from Him, the Most High, with Moses before the Gospel was revealed, so it is from the category of informing about what will happen. Then He described this prophet whom they find thus as one who enjoins what is right: that is, everything that the hearts know and do not reject from the things that are from the noble morals. And forbids them from what is wrong that is, what the hearts reject and do not know, which is what was from the bad morals. It was said that His statement: He enjoins what is right to His statement: Those are the successful ones is a statement that includes details of the rulings of mercy that He promised. Its meaning was mentioned by Al-Zajjaj. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a state of the prophet, and it was said that it is an explanation of His statement: written. His saying: He makes lawful for them the good things meaning the pleasures. It was also said: He makes lawful for them the things that were forbidden to them because of their sins. And He makes unlawful for them the evil things meaning the hidden things like insects and pigs. And He removes from them their burden. Burden means heaviness: meaning He removes from them the difficult and heavy duties. It was previously explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. And the shackles that were upon them meaning, He removes from them the shackles that were upon them. The shackles are borrowed for the difficult duties that they had been charged with. Then those who believed in him meaning, in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and followed him in what he brought of laws, and honored him meaning, they glorified and respected him, said Al-Akhfash. It was said that its meaning is, they prevented him from his enemy, and the origin of azzr is prevention. Al-Jahdary read and honored him with a light and supported him meaning, they supported him against those who oppose him. And followed the light that was sent down with him meaning, they followed the Qur’an that was sent down to him along with his prophethood. It was said that the meaning is: and they followed the Qur’an that was sent down to him while following him by acting according to his Sunnah, which he commands and forbids, or they followed the Qur’an, accompanying him in following it. The reference by those is to those who are described by these characteristics. They are the successful ones the ones who win goodness and success, not any other nations. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And Moses chose his people verse. He said: God had commanded him to choose seventy men from his people, so he chose seventy men and led them out to call upon their Lord. Among what they called upon God was that they said: O God, give us what You have not given to anyone before us and will not give to anyone after us. God disliked that from their supplication, so the earthquake seized them. Moses said: “My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me. Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done? It is nothing but Your trial.” He said: It is nothing but Your punishment, which You inflict upon whomever You will and avert from whomever You will. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid: For Our appointed time, he said: For the completion of the appointment. And regarding his statement: So when the earthquake seized them, he said: They died, then He brought them back to life. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding his statement: It is nothing but Your trial, he said: Your affliction. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, It is nothing but Your trial, meaning: Your will. Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The seventy whom Moses chose from his people were only struck by the earthquake because they were not satisfied with the work and were not forbidden from it. Saeed bin Mansour narrated on his authority regarding His statement, And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter, but Moses was not given it, He said, ‘My punishment - I will afflict with it whom I will,’ until His statement, the successful ones. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding His statement, And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter, he said: So mercy was decreed on that day for this nation. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, Indeed, we have turned to You, he said: We have repented to You. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Wajza al-Sa’di, who was one of the most knowledgeable people in Arabic. He said: No, by God, I do not know of the word ‘hadana’ in the speech of the Arabs. It was said: “How did he say ‘hadana’ with a kasra on the ‘ha’? He says: ‘We turned away.’” Abd al-Razzaq and Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatadah regarding his statement: And My mercy encompasses all things, he said: His mercy encompasses the righteous and the wicked in this world. And on the Day of Resurrection it will be specifically for those who feared God. Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Salman on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God has one hundred mercies, among which is a mercy by which creation is merciful to one another and by which wild beasts are kind to their young. And He has reserved ninety-nine until the Day of Resurrection.” Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim and al-Dhiya’ al-Maqdisi narrated something similar on the authority of Jundub ibn Abdullah al-‘Ajli. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: When the verse And My mercy encompasses all things was revealed, Satan said: And I am from the thing. So God abrogated it, and the verse Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God was revealed until the end of the verse. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: When the verse And My mercy encompasses all things was revealed, Satan said: I am from the thing. God the Most High said: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God and give the zakat. The Jews said: So we fear God and give the zakat. God said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet. So God separated it from Satan and the Jews and made it for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Qatadah. Al-Bazzar narrated in his Musnad, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Moses asked his Lord something and He gave it to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. His saying: And Moses chose his people to His saying: Then I will write it down for those who fear God. So Muhammad was given everything that Moses asked of his Lord in this verse. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him regarding His saying: Then I will write it down for those who fear God, he said: God wrote it for this nation. Ibn Jarir narrated from him regarding the verse: He said: They fear polytheism. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Nakha’i regarding His saying: The unlettered prophet, he said: He could neither read nor write. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding the verse: He is your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was unlettered and could not write. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding His saying: Which they find written down with them, he said: They find his description, his command, and his prophethood written down with them. Ibn Sa'd, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ata' bin Yasar who said: I met Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-'As and said to him: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Yes, by God, he is described in the Torah with some of his description in the Qur'an: "O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner and a protection for the unlettered. You are My servant and Messenger. I have named you Al-Mutawakkil. He is not rude nor harsh nor loud in the markets. And you do not repay evil for evil, but pardon and overlook. And God will not take him until He establishes through him the crooked religion by making them say, 'There is no god but God.' And He opens through him blind eyes, deaf ears and sealed hearts." Ibn Sa'd, Ad-Darimi in his Musnad, Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam. Similar to this has been narrated with differences in some wording, some additions and some omissions from a group of people. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: And He will make lawful for them the good things, he said: the lawful, and remove from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them, he said: the burden that was in their religion. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And He will prohibit for them the evil things, he said: such as pork, usury, and whatever they considered lawful of the forbidden foods that God had forbidden. And regarding his statement: And remove from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them, he said: it is what God had taken from them of the covenant regarding what He had forbidden them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr regarding his statement: And remove from them their burden, he said: what was difficult for the Children of Israel from urine scraping off their skins if it happened to them and the like. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they honored him, meaning: they glorified and respected him.
7:158: When the descriptions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, written in the Torah and the Gospel were mentioned earlier, God Almighty commanded him to say this statement that necessitates the generality of his message to all people, not as was the case with other messengers, peace be upon them, for they were sent to their people specifically, and all is accusative in the state: that is, the state of you all, and He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth is either in the place of a genitive as an attribute of the noble name or accusative in praise, or raised as a predicate of a deleted subject, and the phrase There is no god but He is a substitute for the relative clause, confirming its content and explaining it, because He who owns the heavens and the earth and what is in them is God in reality, and likewise He who gives life and causes death is the one who deserves to be unique in His Lordship and to deny partners from Him, and the command to believe in God and in His Messenger is a branch of what preceded it, and the explanation of the unlettered prophet has been presented, and they are two descriptions of His Messenger, and likewise He who believes in God and His Words is a description of Him, and what is meant by the words is what God revealed Upon him and the prophets before him, or the Qur’an only, and the phrase and follow him is a confirmation of the phrase then believe in God, and that you may be guided is a reason for the command to believe and follow. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the red and the black and said: O people, I am the Messenger of God to you all. The many authentic hadiths with this meaning are well-known, so we will not prolong their mention. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: He believes in God and His words, he said: His verses. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: And His words, he said: Jesus.
7:159: His statement: 159- And from the people of Moses When God told us what happened with the Samaritan and his companions and what happened with the Children of Israel of the shaking in religion: He, the Most High, told us that from the people of Moses there is a nation that is different from those who were mentioned before, and He described them as guiding with the truth meaning calling people to guidance while they are adorned with the truth and with it meaning with the truth they are just between people in ruling, and it was said: They are those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among them.
7:160: 160- And We divided them into twelve tribes The pronoun refers to the people of Moses mentioned earlier: not to this nation of them who guide with the truth and are just with it, and the meaning is: We made them into scattered groups and distinguished some of them from others, and this is part of what God has told us of the blessings that He bestowed upon the Children of Israel, and the meaning is: He distinguished some of them from others until they became tribes, each tribe known separately, each tribe has a leader as in the Almighty's saying: And We raised up from among them twelve leaders and it has been mentioned previously. And His saying: twelve is the second object of we divided because it includes the meaning of making, and tribes is a distinction for it or a substitute for it, or nations is an attribute of the tribes or a substitute for it, and tribes is the plural of tribe: which is the son of the son, they became twelve nations from twelve sons, and by tribes he meant tribes, and for this reason he feminized the number as in the saying of the poet: The Quraysh are made up of ten clans, and you are innocent of their ten tribes. By the belly he meant the tribe, and the meaning of the tribes in Al-Baqarah has been previously investigated. Al-Mufaddal narrated on the authority of Asim that he read We cut them off in a lightened form, and called them nations, because each tribe was a large group: and they had different opinions, some of them would lead others in prayer, And We inspired Moses when his people asked him for water that is, when they asked him for water when they were afflicted with thirst in the wilderness, Strike the rock with your staff an explanation of the action of inspiration, and there gushed forth in apposition to an implied meaning indicated by the context: that is, he struck and it gushed forth, and gushing forth means bursting forth, that is, there gushed forth from it twelve springs according to the number of the tribes, each tribe has a spring from which they drink. Every people has known their drinking place that is, each tribe has its own spring from which it drinks, and what has been presented in Al-Baqarah is sufficient to dispense with repetition. And We shaded them with clouds that is, We made it a shade for them in the wilderness, moving with their movement and staying with their staying. And We sent down upon them manna and quails that is, taranjabin and quail, as the investigation has been presented. In Surat al-Baqarah 2:Eat from the good things which We have provided for you. That is, We said to them: Eat from the pleasures which We have provided for you. And they did not wrong Us. What they did was disobey Us and deny Our blessings and do not appreciate them properly. But they wronged themselves. That is, their wrongdoing was specific to them and limited to them and did not extend beyond them to others.
7:161: 161- And when it was said to them meaning, remember the time when this statement was said to them, which is, Dwell in this city meaning Jerusalem or Jericho, and other things were said that were explained above, and eat from it meaning from the foods found in it where you wish meaning in any place you wish from its locations, there is no objection to you eating there, and say, 'Forgive me' its explanation was presented in Surat Al-Baqarah, and enter the gate meaning the gate of the aforementioned city while you were prostrating they were ordered to combine their saying, Forgive me with entering prostrating, so it cannot be said: How did the command to say here precede the entering and delay it in Surat Al-Baqarah? The meaning of the prostration that they were ordered to do has been explained above, We will forgive you your sins the answer to the command. And it was read, your sins then He promised them by saying, We will increase the doers of good meaning, We will increase their forgiveness of sins with what He bestows upon them of blessings, and the sentence is a resumption of the answer to an implied question as if it was said: So what will they have after forgiveness?
7:162: 162- Then those who did wrong among them substituted a statement other than that which had been said to them. This has been explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. So We sent upon them a punishment from the sky, meaning a punishment coming from it, because they were wronging, meaning because of their wrongdoing.
7:163: His statement: 163- And ask them about the town that was by the sea is connected to the agent of when which is understood: that is, remember when it was said to them and ask them. This is a question of rebuke and rebuke. What is meant by asking the town is asking its al-Nas 114:that is, ask them about this incident that happened to them there that was contrary to what God commanded them to do. And within this question is a great benefit, which is informing the Jews that this is something that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, knows, and that his knowledge can only be through God Almighty informing him, so it is evidence of his truthfulness. The commentators differed about this village: which village is it? Some said it was Ayla, some said it was Tiberias, some said it was Madyan, some said it was Ilya, and some said it was a village from the villages of the coast of the Levant that was by the sea: that is, near the sea. It is said I was in the presence of the house: that is, near it. The meaning is: Ask, O Muhammad, these Jews who are present about the story of the people of the mentioned village. It was read ask them and it was read ask them “when they are preparing” meaning when they are preparing and it is a circumstance of an omitted word indicated by the speech because the question is about their condition and story when they are preparing. It was said that it is a circumstance of kanat or hadira. It was read ya’duun with a damma on the ya’, a kasra on the ‘ayn, and a shaddah on the dal from i’da’ for the instrument. The majority read ya’duun with a fatha on the ya’, a sukoon on the ‘ayn, and a damma on the dal with a shaddah: that is, they transgress the limits of God by hunting on the Sabbath on which they were forbidden to hunt. It was read ya’duun with a fatha on the ya’ and the ‘ayn, and a damma on the dal with a shaddah meaning they transgress, the ta’ was assimilated into the dal. Saturday is the well-known day and its origin is stillness. It is said: Sabbath if it is still. The Jews left work on their Sabbath. The plural is asbat, sabat, and asbat. Ibn al-Sameefa’ read in asbat in the plural idh yatyawahim haitanhum as an adverb for ya’adun. Whales: the plural of hawt and it was added to them to further distinguish them from what was of them in this manner of coming on the Sabbath and not on the other days. Yawm asbathum is an adverb for ya’adun. It was read as the day of their rest and shari’an is a state, and it is the plural of shara’: meaning apparent on the water. It was said raising their heads, and it was said that they were spread out at their doors like white rams. He said in Al-Kashaf: It is said: So-and-so came to us if he came close to us and looked down on us, and I came to so-and-so in his house and I saw him doing such-and-such. End quote. And on the day when they do not observe the Sabbath, the whales will not come to them meaning they will not observe the Sabbath, and that is when the Sabbath ends, the whales will not come to them, as they used to come to them on the Sabbath. Thus do We test them meaning like that great trial, We test them because of their immorality, and the trial is the examination and the test.
7:164: 164- And when a nation said is in apposition to when they count, the object of its agent and is included in its ruling. The nation is the group: that is, a group of righteous people from the village said to others who were striving to preach to the transgressors on the Sabbath when they despaired of their accepting the preaching and abandoning the sin Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy that is, is about to punish them or punish them with a severe punishment for what they violated of the sanctity and committed of the sin. It was said: The group that said Why do you preach to a people? are the sinners who hunt on the Sabbath. They said that to their preachers when they preached to them. Meaning: If you knew that God would destroy us as you claim, why do you preach to us? They said, ‘An apology to your Lord.’ That is, the preachers said to the group who said to them, Why do you preach? They were a group of the righteous people of the village according to the first version, or the doers according to the second version, An apology to your Lord. Isa bin Omar and Talha bin Masraf read an apology in the accusative case, which is the reading of Hafs from Asim, and the rest read it in the nominative case. Al-Kisa’i said: Its accusative case has two meanings: one is as a source, and the second is based on the assumption that we did that as an apology: that is, for the sake of the apology. And the nominative case is based on the assumption of a subject: that is, our preaching is an apology to God so that He does not hold us accountable for abandoning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, which He has made obligatory upon us, and in the hope that they will learn a lesson, become pious, and desist from the sin they are doing. The majority of commentators said: The Children of Israel split into three groups: a group that disobeyed and persecuted, and they numbered about seventy thousand; a group that withdrew and did not forbid or disobey; and a group that withdrew and forbade but did not disobey. The group that did not forbid or disobey said to the forbidding group, Why do you preach to a people meaning the disobedient group, whom God will destroy or punish? They said that based on the preponderance of thought, because it is God’s custom to destroy or punish the disobedient without eradicating them by destruction. So the forbidding group said, Our preaching is an excuse to God, and perhaps they will fear God. If they had been only two groups, a forbidding group that was not disobedient, and a disobedient group, He would have said, Perhaps you will fear God.
7:165: His saying: 165- So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded meaning when the disobedient people of the town abandoned that by which the righteous people who forbade evil had reminded them, as someone who forgets something completely turns away from it abandons it, We saved those who forbade evil meaning those who did what was forbidden, but did not abandon it, And We seized those who did wrong meaning the disobedient ones who transgressed on the Sabbath with a wretched punishment meaning severe from the wretchedness of something, which is wretchedness if it is severe, and there are eleven readings of it for the seven and others, because they were wicked meaning because of their wickedness, and the preposition and its object are related to We seized.
7:166: 166- So when they rebelled against what they were forbidden meaning they went beyond the limit in disobeying God Almighty in rebellion and arrogance We said to them, 'Be apes' meaning we commanded them with a cosmic command not a verbal command: meaning we transformed them into apes. It was said that He, Almighty, first punished them because of the disobedience, then when they did not desist He transformed them into apes. It was also said that His statement, So when they rebelled against what they were forbidden is a repetition of His statement, So when they forgot what they had been reminded of for emphasis and confirmation, and that transformation is the severe punishment, and the disgraced is the humbled and humiliated or the banished and expelled. It is said: I disgraced him, so he was disgraced: meaning I distanced him, so he was distanced. Know that the apparent meaning of the Qur’anic system is that only the group that forbids and does not disobey is saved from punishment, as He says: We saved those who forbid evil. And that only the disobedient group is punished by transformation, as He says: But when they transgressed against what they were forbidden, We said to them, ‘Be apes, despised.’ If the groups among them were three, as mentioned above, then the group that did not forbid and did not disobey is likely to have been transformed along with the disobedient group, because it wronged itself by remaining silent about the prohibition and was transgressing against what God forbade it from, by abandoning the prohibition of evil. And it is likely that it was not transformed, because even though it was unjust to itself and transgressed against the command and prohibition of its Lord, it did not wrong itself with this particular disobedience, which is hunting a whale on the Sabbath, nor was it transgressing against His prohibition of hunting. But if the third group was a prohibitor like the second group, and it was only made an independent group because it had a contract with the other group of the isolated prohibitors, then they are in The truth is that they are one sect because they meet in prohibition, isolation, and salvation from transformation. Al-Faryabi and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Moses said: O Lord, I find a nation whose Gospels are in their hearts. He said: That is a nation that will come after you: the nation of Ahmad. He said: O Lord, I find a nation that gives charity from their wealth, then it returns to them and they eat. He said: That is after you: the nation of Ahmad. He said: O Lord, make me from the nation of Ahmad. Then God revealed, as was pleasing to Moses, And among the people of Moses was a nation guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding His statement: And among the people of Moses was a nation the verse, he said: It has reached me that when the Children of Israel killed their prophets and disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes, one tribe of them disavowed what they had done and apologized and asked God to separate them from them, so God opened for them a tunnel in the earth and they traveled through it until they came out from behind China, and there they are monotheists, Muslims, facing our Qiblah. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: That is what He said: “And We said after him to the Children of Israel, ‘Dwell in the land. Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you in droves.’” And the promise of the Hereafter is Jesus, son of Mary. Ibn Abbas said: They traveled in the flock for a year and a half. I say: Such strange and bizarre report needs to be corrected in its transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib who said: The Children of Israel split into seventy-one sects after Moses, all of them in Hell except one sect. The Christians split into seventy-two sects after Jesus, all of them in Hell except one sect. This nation will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in Hell except one sect. As for the Jews, God says: And among the people of Moses was a nation guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby. This is the one who will be saved. As for the Christians, God says: Among them is a moderate nation. This is the one who will be saved. As for us, He says: And among those We created is a nation guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby. This is the one who will be saved from this nation. We have already mentioned that the addition of all of them in Hell is not authentic, neither as a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) nor as a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And it gushed forth, he said: It burst forth. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: I entered upon Ibn Abbas while he was reciting this verse: And ask them about the city that was by the sea. He said: O Ikrimah, do you know which city this is? I said: No. He said: It is Ayla. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri who said: It is Tiberias. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: When they transgressed on the Sabbath, he said: They were wronged. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Across the river, he said: From every place. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority who said: Apparently on the water. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority who said: Coming. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, saying: It is a village on the seashore between Egypt and Medina, called Ayla. God forbade them from taking whales on their Sabbath day, so they would come to them on their Sabbath day in a lawful manner from the seashore. When the Sabbath day passed, they could not overpower them, and they remained like that as long as God willed. Then a group of them took the whales on their Sabbath day, and another group forbade them, but they only increased in error. Then a group of those who forbade them said, knowing that these were people upon whom the punishment was due, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? They were more angry than the other group, and all of them had forbade them. When God’s wrath fell upon them, the two groups were saved: those who said, Why do you preach? and those who said, Excuse me before your Lord. And God destroyed the people of His disobedience who took the whales, and made them into monkeys. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on his authority that they were three groups: a group of disobedient ones, a group of those who forbade, and a group of those who said, You did not preach. None was saved except those who forbade, and the rest of them perished. Then those who forbade were in their gatherings one morning, checking on the people, but they could not see them. They had spent the night there and locked themselves in their homes. They began to say, The people have a matter, so see what their matter is. So they looked into their homes and saw that the people had been transformed, recognizing a man by his eye, even though he was an ape, and a woman by her eye, even though she was an ape. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who mentioned the story, and at the end of it he said, “I see that those who forbade were saved, and I do not see the others mentioned. We see things that we disapprove of but do not speak about.” Ikrimah said: I said: May God make me your ransom, don't you see that they hate what they are doing and oppose them, and they say: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? He said: So he ordered that I be dressed in two coarse garments. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Those who forbade were saved and those who did were destroyed, and I do not know what happened to those who remained silent. Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on his authority that he said: By God, for me to have known that the people who said: Why do you preach to a people were saved from those who forbade evil is more beloved to me than what I have taken as an equal. In another version: than red camels. But I fear that the punishment has befallen them all. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that Ibn Abbas said: I do not know whether those who said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy were saved or not. He said: I kept looking at him until he knew that they had been saved, and he dressed me in a garment. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, who said: They were transformed into stones those who said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: With a terrible punishment, he said: Painful and painful.
7:167: His statement: 167- And when your Lord proclaimed is connected to what preceded it: that is, ask them when your Lord proclaimed. And to proclaim is a verb from to announce, which means to inform. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: To proclaim with a long vowel means to inform, and to proclaim with a shaddah means to call. Some people said: both of them mean to know, just as one says: to be certain and to be certain. The meaning of the verse: And ask them at the time when the notification from your Lord has come to them, that He will surely send upon them It has been said: In this action there is the meaning of an oath, as God knows and God bears witness, and therefore He answered with what an oath is answered with, where He said: that He will surely send upon them meaning that He will send upon them and give them power, as He said: We have sent upon you servants of Ours, possessors of great might “until the Day of Resurrection” The ultimate goal of their punishment is the severe torment from those whom God sends upon them. And God had established them thus, humiliated, weak, and tormented at the hands of the people of religions, and thus they are in this Islamic religion in every country on earth in the humiliation imposed upon them, torment, and degradation. They pay the jizya in order to spare their blood, and the Muslims treat them with humiliation in the actions that other groups of disbelievers abstain from. The meaning of that He will surely make them taste is that He will make them taste, and the original meaning of this has been explained above, then He explained that by saying: Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment He hastens it in this world as happened to these people, and indeed, He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful meaning, He is Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful.
7:168: 168- And We dispersed them throughout the land meaning We scattered them in its corners, or We scattered their affair so that they did not come together as a word, and nations is in the accusative case as a state or a second object of We dispersed to include the meaning of We made, and the phrase among them are the righteous is a substitute for nations. It was said: They are those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who died before the Muhammadan mission without changing it, and it was said: They are those who lived beyond China as was explained before this, and among them are those below that meaning below this description that the first group was characterized by, which is righteousness, and the place of below that is the nominative case as it is the predicate of a deleted subject, and the estimate: And among them are people below that, and what is meant by these are those who did not believe, but rather were preoccupied with disobeying what God commanded them to do. Al-Nahhas said: Don is an accusative of circumstance, and we do not know of anyone who raised it. And We tested them with good and bad, meaning We tested them with good and evil in the hope that they would return from their disbelief and sins.
7:169: 169- And after them came a generation meaning the children of those whom God has separated on earth. Abu Hatim said: The successor with a sukoon on the lam is the children, singular and plural alike. The successor with a fatha on the lam is the substitute, whether a child or otherwise. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The successor with a fatha is the good, and with a sukoon is the bad. Labid said: Those who lived in their care are gone, and I am left behind like the skin of a mangy dog. Hence, the bad kind of speech is called khalaf with a sukoon, and each of them may be used in place of the other, and from this is the saying of Hassan bin Thabit: We are the first to come to you and we are behind you in the obedience of God. Follow They inherited the Book meaning the Torah from their ancestors. They read it but do not act upon it. They take the goods of this lower world God informed us about them that they take whatever is presented to them of worldly pleasures due to their intense greed and strong desire. The lower is taken from the word closeness, which means closeness. That is, they take the goods of this lower thing, which is the world. They hasten its benefits with bribes and what is made for them from ill-gotten gains in return for their distortion of the words of God, their belittling of acting upon the rulings of the Torah, and their concealment of what they conceal from it. It was said that the lower is taken from baseness and fall, meaning that they take the goods of the previous lowly thing. And they say, ‘We will be forgiven’ meaning that they excuse themselves with forgiveness while they persist in misguidance and do not return to the truth. The phrase they take may be a new sentence to explain their condition or in the accusative case as a state. The phrase they say is conjoined with it. What is meant by this statement is to rebuke and reprimand them. The phrase And if something like it comes to them, they take it is in the place of The accusative case is in the state of: that is, they make excuses for forgiveness, while the fact is that if an offer like the one they used to take comes to them, they take it, not caring about the punishment or fearing the consequences. It has been said that the pronoun in comes to them refers to the Jews of Medina: that is, if an offer like the one their ancestors used to take comes to these Jews who are in the time of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they take it as their ancestors took it. Was not a covenant taken from them in the Book meaning the Torah that they would not say about God except the truth? The question is for rebuke and rebuke. The phrase and studied what is in it is conjoined with is taken in the meaning. It has been said that it is in the place of they inherited the Book. It is better for it to be in the accusative case in the state of: had. The meaning is that they abandoned working with the covenant taken from them in the Book, while the fact is that they studied what was in the Book and taught it, so their abandonment was due to knowledge, not ignorance. That is a greater sin and a greater crime. It was said: The meaning of they studied what was in it is to erase it by abandoning working with it and understanding it, from their saying the wind erased the traces: if it erased them. And the home of the Hereafter is better than that display which they took and preferred over it for those who fear God and avoid His disobedience. Do you not understand? So you will know this and understand it. And in this there is a rebuke and reprimand that cannot be measured.
7:170: His saying: 170- And those who hold fast to the Book The majority read yamsak with emphasis from masak and tamsak: meaning hold fast to the Book, which is the Torah. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Asim read it in Abu Bakr’s narration with emphasis from amaska yamsak. It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab that he read Muskwa and the meaning is: that a group of the People of the Book do not adhere to the Book and do not act according to what is in it, although they have studied it and known it and they are those mentioned above, and a group adhere to the Book: meaning the Torah and act according to what is in it and refer to it in matters of their religion, so they are the doers of good whose reward with God will not be lost, and the relative pronoun is the subject, and We do not waste the reward of the righteous is its predicate: meaning We do not waste the reward of the righteous among them, and the specific mention of prayer occurred despite it being included in all the acts of worship that those who adhere to the Torah do because it is the head of acts of worship and the greatest of them, so that was a reason for specifying it for mention, and it was said: because it is performed at specific times, and adherence to the Book is continuous so it was mentioned for this reason, and there is a view on it, because every act of worship is usually specific to a specific time, and it is permissible for the relative pronoun to be conjoined with the relative pronoun before it which is for those who fear God, and because Do you not understand is an interjectional clause. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He will subject them to a terrible torment, he said: Muhammad and his nation until the Day of Resurrection. The terrible torment is the jizya. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority that he said: The terrible torment is the tax. Regarding his statement: And We dispersed them, he said: They are the Jews whom God spread throughout the earth, so that there is no spot in it except that there is a group of them and a faction.
