Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated regarding his statement: He will surely send upon them, he said: Upon the Jews and Christians, until the Day of Resurrection someone who will subject them to a terrible torment, so God sent upon them the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who will take the jizya from them while they are humiliated. And We dispersed them throughout the earth as nations, he said: Jews. Among them are the righteous, they are the Muslims of the People of the Book. And among them are less than that, he said: Jews. And We tested them with good, he said: prosperity and well-being. And with evil, he said: affliction and punishment. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We tested them with good and bad, with fertility and drought. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority that he was asked about this verse, Then there came after them a generation who inherited the Scripture, taking the goods of this lower world, he said: People who turn to the world, consume it, and follow the concessions of the Quran, and say, ‘We will be forgiven,’ and nothing of this world is offered to them except that they take it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then there came after them a generation, he said: the Christians, taking the goods of this lower world, he said: Whatever is most honorable to them of this world, lawful or unlawful, they desire it, they take it and wish for forgiveness, and if they find something similar tomorrow, they take it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then there came after them a generation, the verse, he said: They take what they got and leave what they want of lawful or unlawful, and say, ‘We will be forgiven,’ he said: Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Was not a covenant taken from them by the Book that they would not say about God except the truth? regarding what they require from God regarding forgiveness of their sins that they continue to return to and do not repent from. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Zayd regarding his statement: And they studied what was in it, he said: They knew what was in the Book and did not come to it out of ignorance. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: And those who hold fast to the Book, he said: It refers to the people of faith among them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And those who hold fast to the Book, he said: Of the Jews and Christians.
7:171: His statement: 171- And when is in the accusative case with an implied verb conjoined to what preceded it: meaning, ask them when We raised the mountain above them, and as if it were a canopy meaning, as if it were a cloud that shaded them due to its height. Canopy is the name for everything that shades. It was read as tala with a ta from atala alayhi if it looks down. And they thought that it would fall upon them meaning, falling upon them. It was said: Thinking here means knowledge, and it was said: It is in its context. Take what We have given you with strength is in the estimation of the saying: meaning, and We said to them, Take, and strength is seriousness and determination: meaning, taking it with strength. And remember what is in it of the rulings that God has prescribed for you and do not forget it. That you may become righteous hoping that you will fear what I have forbidden them from and do what you have been commanded to do. The explanation of what is here has already been fully presented in Surat Al-Baqarah, so we will not repeat it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And when We lifted the mountain above them meaning: We raised it, and this is His statement: And We raised the Mount above them and he said: Take what We have given you with strength or else I will send it upon you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse: The angels raised it above their heads, and it was said to them: Take what We have given you with strength so when they looked at the mountain they said: We hear and obey, and when they looked at the book they said: We hear and disobey. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority that he said: I know why the Jews prostrated on a letter when God said: And when We lifted the mountain above them He said: You must take My command or I will throw it at you, so they prostrated while looking at it for fear that it would fall on them, and it was a prostration that God the Almighty was pleased with so they took it as a Sunnah. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada, And when We pulled the mountain up, meaning: God pulled it up from its base, then placed it above their heads, then said: You must take my command or I will throw it at you.
7:172: His statement: 172- "And when" is in the accusative case with an implied verb conjoined to what preceded it, as mentioned above. His statement: "Of the children of Adam" is used as evidence that what is meant by those taken here are the offspring of the children of Adam, whom God brought forth from their loins, generation after generation. A group of commentators have adopted this view. They said: The meaning of He made them witness against themselves is that He showed them through His creation that He is their Creator, so this evidence took the place of making them witness. Thus, this verse is a metaphor, as in the Almighty’s saying: Then He said to it and to the earth, ‘Come both of you, willingly or by compulsion.’ They said, ‘We come willingly.’ It was said that the meaning is that God, the Exalted, brought forth the souls before creating the bodies, and that He placed in them the knowledge that they understood from His address. It was said that what is meant by the children of Adam here is Adam himself, as occurred in other places. The meaning is that when God, the Exalted, created Adam, He wiped his back and extracted from him his offspring and took a covenant from them. These are the world of the atoms. This is the truth from which one should not deviate or turn to anything else, because it is proven to be traced back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to others among the Companions. There is no recourse to metaphor. When the river of God comes, the river of Maqal becomes void. We will mention at the end of this research, God willing, some of what was mentioned in this regard. His saying: From their backs is a substitute for the sons of Adam, a substitute for some of the whole, and it was said: a substitute for the inclusion of his saying: their offspring, the Kufians and Ibn Kathir read their offspring in the singular, and it occurs for the singular and the plural, and the rest read their offspring in the plural, and and I testify to them over themselves meaning I testify every one of them Am I not your Lord meaning saying: Am I not your Lord, so it is on the intention of saying, “They said: Yes, we testify” meaning over ourselves that you are our Lord. His saying: That you say, Abu Amr read with the lower ya’ in this. And in his saying: That they say it is in the third person as it was in the third person as in what came before it, and the rest read with the upper ya’ in the address. The meaning: disliking that they say or lest they say: meaning we did that taking and calling to witness, disliking that they say: On the Day of Resurrection, we were unaware of this meaning that God is our Lord alone, with no partner.
7:173: His statement: 173- Or you say, 'Our fathers associated others with God before' is connected to the first say, meaning we did that out of dislike for you to apologize with heedlessness or attribute polytheism to your fathers without you, and or is to prevent the absence of the combination, as they may apologize with the combination of the two matters before meaning before our time and we were descendants after them not guided to the truth nor knowing what is right so will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did from our fathers and we are not to blame for our ignorance and inability to see and follow the footsteps of our predecessors. God Almighty explained this wisdom for which He brought them out from the back of Adam and made them witness against themselves, and that He did that to them so that they would not say this statement on the Day of Resurrection, and cite this false excuse and make excuses with this weak excuse.
7:174: 174- And thus meaning and similar to that detail We detail the verses so that perhaps they will return to the truth and abandon what they are doing of falsehood. Malik narrated in Al-Muwatta’, Ahmad in Al-Musnad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari in his History, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat, and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara that ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab was asked about this verse, And when your Lord took… and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, being asked about it. He said: “God created Adam, then He wiped his back with His right hand and extracted from him offspring. He said: ‘I created these for Paradise and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise.’ Then He wiped his back and extracted from him offspring. He said: ‘I created these for Hell and they will do the deeds of the people of Hell.’ A man said: ‘O Messenger of God, what is the purpose of the deeds?’ He said: ‘When God creates a servant for Paradise, He uses him to do the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Paradise and He enters him into Paradise because of it. But when He creates a servant for Hell, He uses him to do the deeds of the people of Hell until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Hell and He enters him into Hell.’” Ahmad, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: “God took the covenant from the back of Adam in Na’man on the day of Arafah, and brought forth from his loins all of his offspring and spread them out before him, then He spoke to them and said: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes, we bear witness’ until His saying: ‘the falsifiers.’” Its chain of transmission is not questionable. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it as being attributed to Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mandah narrated in the book Al-Radd ‘ala Al-Jahmiyyah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their offspring, He said: He took them from his back as a comb is taken from the head, and said to them: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ The angels said: ‘We bear witness’ lest you should say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:‘Indeed, we were unaware of this.’” In its chain of transmission is Ahmad ibn Abi Thaybah Abu Muhammad Al-Jurjani, the judge of Qumis, who was one of the ascetics. Al-Nasa'i included it in his Sunan. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: His hadith should be written. Ibn 'Adi said: He narrated many strange hadiths. This hadith was narrated by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi from Sufyan al-Thawri from Mansur from Mujahid from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, and these are trustworthy imams. 'Abd ibn Hamid, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azmah, and Ibn Mardawayh from Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When God created the creation and completed the matter and took the covenant of the prophets and His Throne was over the water, He took the people of the right hand with His right hand and the people of the left hand with His other hand, and both of the hands of the Most Merciful are right, so He said: O people of the right, and they responded to Him and said: At Your service, our Lord, and at Your pleasure. He said: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes." The hadith and hadiths on this topic are many, some of which are restricted to the interpretation of this verse, and some are general and include mention of bringing forth the descendants of Adam from his back, and taking a covenant from them as in the hadith of Anas with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet in the two Sahihs and others. As for what has been narrated from the Companions in interpreting this verse as bringing forth the offspring of Adam from his loins in the world of atoms and taking a covenant from them and making them testify about themselves, there are many of them, including from Ibn Abbas, according to Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh, regarding His statement: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam 1:13, he said: God created Adam and took a covenant from him that He is his Lord and wrote his life span and his provision, then He brought forth his offspring from his loins in the form of atoms, so He took their covenants that He is their Lord and wrote their life spans, their provisions, and their calamities. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated something similar from him. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar from him. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mandah narrated something similar from him. This meaning has been narrated from him through many chains of transmission other than this, all of which are attributed to him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar regarding the verse: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam 1:13, he said: He took them as a comb is taken from the head. Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated in al-Tamhid on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud and some of the Companions regarding the interpretation of the verse something similar. Abd ibn Humayd, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal in the narration of al-Musnad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mandah, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat, al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara, and Ibn Asakir in his history narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b regarding the verse: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam 1:13, he said: He gathered them all together and made them spirits in their forms, then He made them speak, then He took a covenant and a pledge from them, then He made them bear witness against themselves. It has been narrated on the authority of a group of those who came after the Companions that this verse is interpreted as bringing forth the offspring of Adam from his back. What the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said in its interpretation, as we have mentioned, is sufficient to make this long.
7:175: His saying: 175- And recite is connected to the actions implied in the previous al-Qasas 28:And the mention of this story is from Him, glory be to Him, and the reminder of it to the People of the Book because it was mentioned to them in the Torah. There is a difference of opinion about the one who was given the signs and then slipped out of them. It was said that he was Balaam bin Ba’oura’, and he had memorized some of the revealed books. It was also said that he had been given prophethood and his prayers were answered. God sent him to Madyan to call them to faith, so they gave him generous gifts, so he followed their religion and left what he was sent with. When Moses came with the Children of Israel to fight the tyrants, the tyrants asked Balaam bin Ba’oura’ to invoke curses upon Moses. He stood up to invoke curses upon him, but his tongue turned to invoking curses upon his companions. He was asked about that, but he said: I am not able to do more than what you hear. His tongue stuck out on his chest, and he said: Now the world and the hereafter have gone from me, so nothing remains but deceit, trickery, and stratagem. I will plot against you. I see that you should send out to them your girls, for God hates adultery. If they fall into it, they will perish. So the Children of Israel fell into adultery, so God sent a plague upon them, and seventy thousand of them died. It was said that this man’s name was Ba’am, and he was from the Children of Israel. It was also said that what was meant by it was Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt Al-Thaqafi, who had read the books and knew that God had sent a messenger for that purpose, but when God sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, he envied him and disbelieved in him. It was said that he was Abu Amir bin Saifi, who used to wear hair-sacks during the pre-Islamic era, so he disbelieved in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. It was also said that it was revealed about the Quraysh, when God gave them His signs that He sent down to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, so they disbelieved in them. It was also said that it was revealed about the Jews and Christians, who awaited the emergence of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, so they disbelieved in him. His statement, So he peeled off from them means from these signs that he was given, as a sheep peels off its skin, so he had no connection to them. So Satan pursued him when he peeled off the signs: that is, he caught up with him and overtook him and became his companion, or he followed his footsteps. It was read So he followed him with emphasis, meaning he followed him. So he was among the deviators those who are firmly established in misguidance, and they are the disbelievers.
7:176: His saying: 176- And if We willed, We could have elevated him thereby. The pronoun refers to the one who was given the signs, and the meaning is: If We willed to elevate him: by the signs We gave him, We could have elevated him thereby: that is, because of them, but We did not will that because of his turning away from them and abandoning acting upon them. It was said that the meaning is: If We willed, We could have caused him to die before he disobeyed, so We raised him to Paradise thereby: that is, by acting upon them. But he clung to the earth. The root of ikhlaad is adherence. It is said: So-and-so clung to a place if he resided there and adhered to it. The meaning here is that he inclined toward the world and desired it and preferred it over the Hereafter. And he followed his desires, that is, he followed what he desired and abandoned acting upon what the knowledge that God taught him required, which is the debris of the world. It was said: His desires were with the infidels, and it was said: He followed the pleasure of his wife, and she was the one who led him to turn away from the signs of God. His saying: His likeness is like that of a dog means that when he has abandoned the verses and has not acted upon them, he has descended to the lowest rank, resembling the most vile of animals in baseness, resembling them in the ugliest of characteristics, which is that he pants in both cases, whether a person intends to attack him or leaves him. He is panting whether he is reprimanded or left alone, chased or not chased, attacked or not attacked. There is nothing more vile and base than this. The phrase If you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, his likeness is like that of a dog when he is described with this characteristic. The meaning is that this one who has abandoned the verses does not desist from disobedience in all his states, whether the preacher admonishes him, the one who reminds him reminds him, the one who warns him reprimands him, or nothing of that happens. Al-Qatibi said: Everything that pants only pants from exhaustion or thirst, except the dog, which pants when tired, at rest, sick, healthy, quenched, and thirsty. So God made it an example for those who deny His signs, saying: If you admonish it, it will go astray, and if you leave it, it will go astray. So it is like a dog, if you leave it, it will pant, and if you drive it, it will pant, as God the Almighty said: And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you - it is all the same to you whether you invite them or are silent. Panting is sticking out the tongue due to exhaustion, thirst, or something else. Al-Jawhari said: The dog pantes with the fat-ha, panting, and panting with the damma, if it sticks out its tongue due to exhaustion or thirst, and the same is true for a man when he becomes exhausted. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: If you attack a dog, it will bark and run away, and if you leave it alone, it will attack you and bark, tiring itself out by coming towards you and turning away from you, and it will suffer from what happens to it when it is thirsty, sticking out its tongue. The reference in his saying that is to what was mentioned previously about the example of that vile state. It is a subject and its predicate is The parable of the people who denied Our signs meaning that this vile example is like the people who denied Our signs from the Jews after they knew about them and recognized them, so they distorted and changed and concealed the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denied it. So relate the story meaning relate to them this story, which is the description of the man who has abandoned the signs, for his example mentioned is like the example of these people who denied from the Jews, whom you relate to, Perhaps they will reflect on that and use their understandings in it, so they will be deterred from misguidance and turn to the truth.
7:177: His saying: 177- A bad example is the people who denied Our signs. This sentence includes a description of the state of these people who reached the extreme in ugliness: It is said: The thing became bad, it is ugly, so it is intransitive, and it became bad, it is transitive and is from the verbs of blame, like ba'isa, and its subject is a hidden pronoun, and an example is a specification explaining it and the one specifically blamed is those who denied Our signs, and it is necessary to estimate a deleted complement for the sake of conformity, i.e. a bad example like the people who denied. Al-Akhfash said: He made the example of the people a metaphor, and the people is raised by the beginning or by the implication of the subject, the estimate: The example is bad, it is like the people, so he said. Abu Ali Al-Farisi estimated it: A bad example like the people as we mentioned. Al-Jahdary and Al-A'mash read: A bad example is the people. His statement: And they were wronging themselves means that they were wronging themselves by denying it. Their wrongdoing did not extend beyond it to others, nor did it go beyond it. The sentence is connected to the one before it, meaning that they combined the denial of God’s verses with wrongdoing themselves.
7:178: 178- He whom God guides is the one who is guided to what He has commanded and legislated for His servants. And he whom He sends astray - those are the losers the complete losers. He whom He guides, none can lead astray, and he whom He sends astray, none can guide him: whatever He wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen. Al-Faryabi, Abd al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding his statement: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, he said: He is a man from the Children of Israel called Balaam bin Abiz. Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: He is Balaam bin Ba’oura. In another version: Balaam bin Ba’er who was given the name was from the Children of Israel. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {And recite to them the report of him to whom We gave Our signs}, he said: He is a man from the city of the tyrants called Balaam, he learned the greatest name of God, and when Moses descended upon them, his cousins and his people came to him and said: Moses is a man of iron and has many soldiers, and if he prevails over us he will destroy us, so pray to God to repel Moses and those with him from us, he said: If I pray to God to repel Moses and those with him, my world and the hereafter will pass, so they kept on at him until he prayed to God and he stripped him of what he was in. And regarding his statement: {If you attack him, he pants, or leave him alone, he pants}, he said: If he is charged with wisdom, he does not carry it, and if he is left alone, he does not seek good, like a dog that if it lies down, it pants, and if it is chased, it pants. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: He is a man who was given three supplications that were answered for him, and he had a wife with whom he had a child, so she said: Make one for me from her, he said: You have one, so what do you want? She said: Ask God to make me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. So he asked God and He made her the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was no one like her among them, she turned away from him and wanted something else. So he asked God to make her a dog, and she became a dog. Then two prayers were fulfilled. Then her sons came and said: We cannot stay here. Our mother has become a dog that people taunt us about. Ask God to return her to the state she was in. So he asked God and she returned to the way she was, and the three prayers were fulfilled. And she was called Al-Basoos. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr regarding the verse. He said: He is Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt Al-Thaqafi. And in another version: It was revealed about your companion Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi regarding this verse. He said: Ibn Abbas said: He is a man from the Children of Israel called Balaam bin Ba’oura. The Ansar used to say: He is the son of the monk who built the mosque of Al-Shaqaq for him. The Thaqeef used to say: He is Umayya bin Abi Al-Salt. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He said: He is Saifi bin Al-Raheb. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Then he slipped out of it he said: Knowledge was taken from him. And regarding his statement: And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby he said: God elevated him with His knowledge. Muslim, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would praise God in his sermon and extol Him as He deserves, then he would say: ‘He whom God guides, none can misguide him, and he whom He misguides, none can guide him. The most truthful speech is the Book of God, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The worst of matters are their innovations, and every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Fire.’ Then he would say: ‘I and the Hour were sent like these two.’”
7:179: 179- And We have certainly created meaning We have created. The original meaning of this has been fully explained, and this sentence confirms the content of what preceded it for Hell meaning for torture therein many meaning many of the jinn and mankind meaning from the two groups of jinn and mankind He, glory be to Him, made them for the Fire by His justice and by the deeds of its people. And He knew what they were doing before they were, as was proven in the authentic hadiths. Then He described these people and said: They have hearts with which they do not understand, just as others understand with their minds. The phrase they do not understand with them is in the nominative case as an attribute of hearts, and the phrase they have hearts is in the accusative case as an attribute of many. God Almighty made their hearts, since they were not understanding what benefits them and guides them, not understanding at all, even if they understand what does not benefit or guide them, then it is as if they do not exist. And this is the meaning of They have eyes with which they do not see and they have ears with which they do not hear. What is absent from the eyes is seeing what contains guidance through contemplation and consideration, even if they see in other than that. What is absent from the ears is hearing beneficial sermons and laws that are included in the revealed books and what the Messengers of God brought, even if they hear other than that. The reference in His saying: those is to those described by these descriptions like livestock in the absence of their benefit from these feelings. Then He ruled on them. That they are more astray than her, because she perceives in these matters what benefits and harms her, so she benefits from what benefits and avoids what harms. These people do not distinguish between what benefits and what harms in consideration of what God has asked of them and charged them with. Then He judged them to be completely heedless of what they are upon in terms of the lack of discrimination that is the nature of one who has a mind, sight, and hearing. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We have certainly created he said: We created. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse: He said: We created for Hell. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God created for Hell from creation, the offspring of fornication were among those created for Hell. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And We have certainly created for Hell he said: We have certainly created for Hell. They have hearts with which they do not understand he said: They do not understand anything of the affairs of life. And they have eyes with which they do not see guidance. And they have ears with which they do not hear truth. Then He made them like livestock. Then He made them worse than livestock, saying: Rather, they are more astray then He informed that they are the heedless.
7:180: This verse includes information from God Almighty about His names in general without detail, and Al-Husna is the feminine of Al-Ahsan: meaning that they are the best names because they indicate the best named and the most honorable meaning. Then He ordered them to call upon Him with them when needed, because if one calls upon Him with His best names, that is one of the reasons for the prayer to be answered. It has been proven in the Sahih: God has ninety-nine names, whoever counts them will enter Paradise. And an explanation of their number will also come at the end of the research, God willing. His saying: 180- And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names. Blasphemy means inclination and abandonment of the right path. It is said: A man blasphemed in religion and al-lahd means if he deviated. From this comes the word lahd in the grave because it is on a side. It was also read yal-lahdun and they are two languages. Blasphemy concerning His names, glory be to Him, can be of three types: either by changing them as the polytheists did, for they took the name al-Lat from God, al-Uzza from al-Aziz, and Manat from al-Mannan, or by adding to them by inventing names from themselves that God did not permit, or by subtracting from them by calling Him by some of them and not others. The meaning of And leave those who blaspheme is leave them and do not argue with them or expose yourself to them. According to this meaning, the verse was abrogated by the verses of fighting. It was said that its meaning is: the threat as God the Most High said: Leave Me and he whom I created alone, and His saying: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves. This is more appropriate for His saying: They will be recompensed for what they used to do, for it is a threat to them with the punishment descending and a warning to the Muslims not to do as they did. Muqatil and other commentators have mentioned that this verse was revealed about a Muslim man who used to say in his prayer, O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful. A polytheist said, Does Muhammad and his companions not claim that they worship one Lord? Why does this man call upon two Lords? Al-Qurtubi narrated this. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Khuzaymah, Abu ‘Awanah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever counts them will enter Paradise. He is odd and loves odd numbers.” In the wording of Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu’aym: Whoever calls upon God with them, God will answer his call. And Al-Tirmidhi added in his Sunan after saying that he loves the odd number: “He is God, other than whom there is no god, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Preserver, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Proud, the Expander, the Abaser, the Rafid, the Giver of Honor, the Humiliator, the Hearer, the Seeing, the Judge, the Just, the Kind, the All-Knowing, the Forbearing, the Great, the Forgiving, the Appreciative, the High, the Great, the Preserver, the Supporter, the Reckoner, the Majestic, the Generous, the Watchful, the Responder, the Vast, the Wise, the Loving, the Glorious, the Resurrecter, the Witness, the Truth, the Agent, the Strong, the Firm, the Guardian, the Praiseworthy, the Counter, the Beginner, the Restorer, the Giver of Life, the Giver of Death, the Living, the Self-Sustaining, the Finder, the Majestic, the One, the Eternal Refuge, the Able, the Powerful, the Advanced, the Delayer, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Guardian, the Most High, the Righteous, the Accepter of Repentance, the Avenger, the Pardoner, the Kind, the Possessor of Sovereignty, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, the Just, the Gatherer.” The Rich, the Enricher, the Preventer, the Harmful, the Beneficial, the Light, the Guide, the Ingenious, the Eternal, the Inheritor, the Rightly Guided, the Patient. Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated this addition on the authority of Al-Jawzajani on the authority of Safwan bin Salih on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim on the authority of Shuaib bin Abi Hamza on the authority of Abi Al-Zinad on the authority of Al-Araj on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: This is a strange hadith. It has been narrated from Abu Hurairah through other chains of transmission, and it is not known in many narrations that the names are mentioned except in this hadith. It was narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, Ibn Khuzaymah and Al-Hakim on the authority of Safwan with his previous chain of transmission. It was narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan through another chain of transmission on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah on the authority of Al-Araj on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He listed the names mentioned above with additions and omissions. Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir, which a group of Hafiz relied upon, that the listing of the names in this hadith is inserted in it. Rather, it is as Al-Walid bin Muslim and Abdul Malik bin Muhammad Al-San’ani narrated on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad that he heard from more than one of the people of knowledge that they said that: meaning that they collected them from the Qur’an, as was narrated on the authority of Ja’far bin Muhammad, Sufyan bin Uyaynah and Abu Zayd Al-Lughawi. He said: Then let it be known that the beautiful names are not limited to the ninety-nine, as evidenced by what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun on the authority of Fadil ibn Marzuq on the authority of Abu Salamah al-Juhani on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of his father on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “No one is ever afflicted with worry or grief and says, ‘O God, I am Your servant and the son of Your servant and Your female servant. My forelock is in Your hand. Your command over me is carried out, and Your judgment over me is just. I ask You by every name that is Yours, with which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or have kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You, to make the Noble Qur’an the life of my heart, the light of my chest, the dispeller of my grief, and the remover of my grief and sorrow,’ except that God removes his worry and grief and replaces it with relief. It was said, O Messenger of God, should we not learn it? He said, ‘Yes, whoever hears it should learn it.’” Imam Abu Hatim ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih with a similar wording. Al-Bayhaqi also included it in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat. Ibn Hazm said: There are confused hadiths about their enumeration, meaning the beautiful names, none of which are authentic at all. He included them with the same number that Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu’aym included on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and they mentioned it, and I do not know how its chain of transmission is. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Al-Tabarani, both of them in Al-Du’aa’, and Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: “God has ninety-nine names, whoever counts them will enter Paradise: I ask God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, the God, the Lord, the King, the Holy, Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Proud, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner, the Forbearing, the Knowing, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Living, the Self-Sustaining, the Vast, the Kind, the All-Aware, the Compassionate, the Generous, the Innovator, the Forgiving, the Loving, the Appreciative, the Glorious, the Originator, the Restorer, the Light, the Maker. In another version: the Qa’im, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Pardoner, the Forgiving, the Giver, the Unique. In another version: the Able, the One, the Self-Sufficient, the Agent, the Sufficient, the Eternal, the Helper, the Eternal, the Most High, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, the Master, the All-Seeing, the Truth, the Firm, the Inheritor, the Illuminator, the Resurrector, the Powerful. In another version: the Responder, the Giver of Life, the Giver of Death, the Praiseworthy.” In other words: The Beautiful, the Truthful, the Preserver, the All-Encompassing, the Great, the Near, the Watchful, the Opener, the Accepter of Repentance, the Eternal, the Odd, the Creator, the Provider, the All-Knowing, the Most High, the Great, the Rich, the King, the Powerful, the Most Generous, the Compassionate, the Manager, the Owner, the Subduer, the Guide, the Grateful, the Generous, the Exalted, the Witness, the One, the Possessor of Heights, the Possessor of Grace, the Creator, the Guarantor, the Majestic. Abu Naim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Jaafar who said: I asked Abu Jaafar bin Muhammad al-Sadiq about the ninety-nine names that whoever counts them will enter Paradise? He said: They are in the Qur’an. In Al-Fatihah there are five names: O God, O Lord, O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful, O King. In Al-Baqarah there are thirty-three names: O All-Encompassing, O Powerful, O All-Knowing, O All-Wise, O Most High, O Great, O Accepter of Repentance, O All-Seeing, O Guardian, O Vast, O Sufficient, O Kind, O Creator, O Creator of Blessings, O One, O All-Hearing, O Withholder, O Responder, O Mighty, O Helper, O Strong, O Severe, O Swift, O All-Aware. In Al-Imran there are: O Giver, O Qa’im, O Truthful, O Resurrector, O Bestower, O Generous, and in An-Nisa’ there are: O Watcher, O Reckoner, O Witness, O Assured, O Trustee, O High, O Great. In Al-An’am there are: O Creator, O Subduer, O Subtle, O Proof. In Al-A’raf there are: O Reviver, O Death. In Al-Anfal there are: O Best Master, O Best Helper. In Hud there are: O Preserver, O Glorious. O Loving One, O Doer of what You will, and in Ar-Ra’d: O Great, O Most High, and in Abraham: O Generous, O Inheritor, and in al-Hijr 15:O Creator, and in Maryam 19:O Unique, and in Ta-Ha: O Forgiver, and in Qad Aflah, O Generous, and in al-Nur 24:O Truth, O Manifest, and in al-Furqan 25:O Guide, and in Saba 34:O Opener, and in al-Zumar 39:O Knower, and in Ghafir 40:O Accepter of repentance, O Possessor of magnificence, O Exalted, and in al-Dhariyat 51:O Provider, O Possessor of strength, O Firm, and in al-Tur 52:O Righteous, and in It approached: O Powerful, O King, and in al-Rahman 55:O Possessor of majesty and honor, O Lord of the two Easts, O Lord of the two Wests, O Eternal, O Helper, and in Iron: O First, O Last, O Manifest, O Hidden, and in al-Hashr 59:O King, O Holy, O Peace, O Believer, O Dominant, O Mighty, O Compeller, O Proud, O Creator, O Maker, O Fashioner, and in al-Buruj 85:O Originator, O Repeater, and in Fajr: O Witr, and in al-Ikhla 112:O One, O Eternal Refuge. Ibn Hajar mentioned in Al-Talkhees that he traced it from the Noble Book until he had freed ninety-nine of them, then he listed them, so search for it. This is supported by what Abu Naim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has ninety-nine names. Whoever counts them will enter Paradise, and they are in the Qur’an.” Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Aisha, “She said: O Messenger of God, teach me the name of God by which if He is called upon, He answers. He said to her: Get up, perform ablution, enter the mosque, pray two rak’ahs, then supplicate so that I may hear. So she did, and when she sat down to supplicate, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, guide her. So she said: O God, I ask You by all of Your beautiful names, those we know of them and those we do not know, and I ask You by Your great, greatest, great name by which whoever calls upon You, You answer him, and whoever asks You by it, You give him. The Prophet said: You have attained it, You have attained it.” Scholars have discussed the beautiful names at length, to the extent that Ibn al-Arabi, in his commentary on al-Tirmidhi, narrated from some scholars that he had collected a thousand names of God from the Qur’an and Sunnah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And leave those who err in His names, he said: Err is to call upon al-Lat and al-Uzza among the names of God. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him that he said: Err is to deny. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding the verse that he said: They derived al-Uzza from al-Aziz, and they derived al-Lat from God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ata regarding the verse that he said: Err is to imitate. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-A’mash that he read yalhadun from lahad, and he said its interpretation is: they include in it what is not from it. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah regarding the verse that he said: they associate others with God.
7:181: His statement: 181- And of those We created is an advanced predicate, and a nation is a delayed subject, and they guide and what follows it is an attribute of it. It is possible that and of those We created is the subject, as was mentioned previously in His statement: And of the people is he who says and the meaning is: that among those whom God created is a nation who guide the people while wearing the truth or guide them with what they know of the truth and with the truth they are just among them. It was said: they are from this nation, and they are the group who continue to be on the truth, apparent, as was mentioned in the authentic hadith.
7:182: Then when he explained the state of this righteous nation, he explained the state of those who oppose them, saying: 182- And those who deny Our signs - We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know. And leadership means taking gradually, one station after another, and stepping means holding something, it is said: I guided it and his level, and from this is the burying of the dead in his shrouds, and it is said: it is from degree, so leadership means taking step after step to the goal, and from this is the daraj of the boy: if he brought his steps closer together, and idraj al-Kitab means folding it little by little, and daraj al-Qawm means some of them died in the footsteps of others, and the meaning is: We will lead them on gradually to that which will destroy them, and that is by bestowing blessings upon them and making them forget to thank for them, so they become engrossed in misguidance and avoid the paths of guidance because they are deceived by that and that they did not obtain it except through what they have with God of status and closeness.
7:183: His statement: 183- And I will grant them respite is in apposition to We will lead them on: that is, I will extend their period and give them respite and delay their punishment. The phrase Indeed, My plan is firm confirms and emphasizes what came before it of leading on and giving them respite. Kayd means deceit, and matin means strong and powerful. Its origin is from matn, which is the thick flesh on the side of the back. He said in Al-Kashshaf: He called it Kayd because it is similar to Kayd in that it is apparently kindness but in reality it is betrayal.
7:184: And the question in 184- Did they not reflect is to denounce them since they did not reflect on the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought, and what is in what is with their companion is for the rhetorical question, and it is in the place of raising as the subject and the predicate is with their companion, and the paradise is a source: meaning they committed the denial and did not reflect on any madness that is with their companion as they claim, because if they had reflected they would have found their claim to be false, and their statement false and slanderous, and it was said that what is negative and its subject is from paradise and its predicate is with their companion: meaning there is nothing in their companion of what they claim of madness, so this is a response to their saying: O you to whom the message has been sent down, you are mad and the speech would have been completed when he said: Did they not reflect and stopping at it is one of the good stops, and the phrase He is only a clear warner confirms the content of what preceded it, and explains the true state of the Messenger of God May God bless him and grant him peace.
7:185: And the question in 185- Have they not considered the kingdom of the heavens and the earth? is for denial, rebuke, and rebuke, and for the purpose of expressing astonishment at their turning away from considering the clear signs indicating the perfection of His power and His uniqueness in divinity. The kingdom is one of the structures of exaggeration, and its meaning is the great kingdom, and its explanation has been presented. The meaning is: These people did not think so that they would benefit from thinking, nor did they look at the creations of God so that they would be guided thereby to faith in Him. Rather, they are lost in their misguidance, immersed in their error, not working with thought nor contemplating deeply. His statement: And God has not created anything means that they did not look at the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, nor at what God has created of things, whatever they may be. Indeed, in all of His creations there is a lesson for those who consider and an admonition for those who reflect, whether they are from the great things of His creations, such as the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, or from the small things of the rest of His creations. His saying: And that perhaps their time has drawn near is in apposition to kingdom. And that is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its subject is the pronoun of the matter, and its predicate is perhaps and what follows it: meaning, or have they not considered that the matter and the discussion is that perhaps their time has drawn near, so they will die soon? The meaning is: if they are going to pass the nearness of their times, why do they not consider what will guide them and benefit them from by contemplating and considering it? Then in what statement after it will they believe? The pronoun refers to what came before of contemplating and considering the matters mentioned: meaning, then in what statement after this statement that was explained above will they believe? In this question there is a rebuke and rebuke that cannot be estimated. It was said that the pronoun refers to the Qur’an, and it was said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said to the term mentioned before it.
7:186: And the sentence 186 - He whom God sends astray, there is no guide for him confirms what came before it: that is, this heedlessness on their part regarding these clear and evident matters is only because they are among those whom God has sent astray, and he whom He sends astray, there is no guide for him: that is, there is no one to guide him to the truth and remove him from misguidance at all. And He leaves them wandering blindly in their transgression. It was read in the nominative case as a resumption and in the jussive case in apposition to the place of the penalty. It was read with the nun, and the meaning of they wander blindly is they are confused, and it was said they hesitate, and it is in the accusative case as a state. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: And among those We have created is a nation guiding with the truth, he said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is my nation with the truth; they judge and decide, take and give. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, he said: It has reached us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when he recited it: This is for you, and the people before you have been given something similar to it, ‘And among the people of Moses is a nation guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby.’ Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ regarding the verse, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Among my nation are people who are on the truth until Jesus, son of Mary, descends when he descends. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: We will gradually seize them from where they do not know, he said: We will seize them from where they do not know. He said: The punishment of Badr. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Muthanna regarding the verse, he said: Every time they commit a sin, We renew for them a blessing that makes them forget to seek forgiveness. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Abu Al-Sheikh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat on the authority of Sufyan regarding the verse, he said: We bestow blessings upon them and prevent them from being grateful for them. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Thabit Al-Banani that he was asked about enticement and he said: That is God’s plan for the negligent servants. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of His statement, And I grant them respite, meaning: I restrain myself from them. Indeed, My plan is firm, meaning: My plan is severe. Then God abrogated it and revealed: So kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God’s plan is punishment and vengeance. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that “the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on al-Safa and called out to the Quraysh, clan by clan: O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so, warning them of God’s wrath and the events of God until morning, until someone said: This companion of yours is mad, he has been making noise all night until morning, so God revealed: ‘Have they not considered? There is no madness in their companion. He is only a clear warner.’”
7:187: His saying: 187- They ask you about the Hour. The questioners: are the Jews, and it was said the Quraysh, and the Hour: the Resurrection, and it is one of the most common names, and its application to the Resurrection is because it occurs suddenly or because of the speed of its reckoning, and Ayan is a time adverb built on the Fatha. The rajaz poet said: When will my need be fulfilled? Don't you see that it is time for its success? Its meaning is the meaning of when, and its derivation is from any: and it was said from where. Al-Salami read ayan with a kasra on the hamza, and it is in the nominative case as a predicate, and marsaha is the subject according to Sibawayh, and marsaha with a damma on the meem: meaning the time of its anchoring from arsaha God: meaning He made it firm, and with a fatha on the meem from rasat: meaning it was fixed, and from it wa qadur rasayyat pots are firmly fixed, and from it the mountain was anchored. Meaning: When will God establish it? That is, establish it and make it happen. The apparent meaning of They ask you about the Hour is that the question is about the Hour itself, and the apparent meaning of When will it be established is that the question is about its time. Thus, it was concluded from all of them that the aforementioned question is about the Hour in terms of its occurrence at the appointed time for that. Then God, the Exalted, commanded him to answer them by saying: “Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord.” That is, its knowledge in terms of its occurrence is with God. No one knows it or is guided to it except Him. None reveals it at its time except Him. That is, no one reveals it at its time or reveals it except God, the Exalted. Manifestation means revealing something. It is said: So-and-so revealed the report to me, meaning he made it clear and evident. In God, the Exalted, keeping the knowledge of the Hour to Himself, there is great wisdom and profound planning, like all the things that God has hidden and kept the knowledge of to Himself. This sentence confirms the meaning of the one before it. His saying: It is heavy in the heavens and the earth. It was said that the meaning of this is that since its knowledge was hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth, it was heavy, because everything whose knowledge is hidden is heavy on the hearts. It was also said that the meaning is: The heavens and the earth cannot bear it because of its greatness, because the sky splits, the stars scatter, and the seas dry up. It was also said that its description was heavy for them. It was also said that the question was heavy for them. This sentence also confirms the meaning of what preceded it. It will not come to you except suddenly. Except suddenly, without warning. Suddenly is a source in the place of a state. This sentence is like the one before it in confirming. His saying: They ask you as if you are knowledgeable about it. Ibn Faris said: The knowledgeable is the one who knows about something, and the knowledgeable is the one who investigates the question. From this is the saying of Al-A’sha: If you ask about me, then, O Lord, ask me about Al-A’sha, where he ascended. It is said: He is afḥā in the question and in the request, so he is afḥāf, and afḥā is for multiplication like mukhṣab and khāsib. The meaning is: They ask you about the Hour as if you know about it, or as if he is investigating the question about it and multiplying it. The simile sentence is in the accusative case as a state, meaning they ask you likening your state to the state of one who is afḥāf about it. It was also said that the meaning is: They ask you about it as if you are afḥāf of them: meaning afḥāf of their righteousness and happy with their question. The first is the meaning of the Qur’anic arrangement according to the Arabic approach. His statement: Say, ‘Its knowledge is only with my Lord.’ God Almighty commanded him to repeat what he had answered them previously to confirm and emphasize the ruling. It was also said that it is not a repetition, but rather one of them means to monopolize its occurrence, and the other is to monopolize its essence itself. But most people do not know, with God monopolizing this and His creation not knowing about it. No close angel or sent prophet knew it.
7:188: His saying: 188- "Say: I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm except what God wills." This sentence includes confirmation of what was mentioned before about his not knowing the Hour, when it will be and when it will occur, because if he is not able to bring benefit to himself or ward off harm from himself except what God, the Most High, wills of benefit for him and ward off from him, then it is more appropriate that he be able to know what God has kept to Himself in knowledge. In this there is a manifestation of servitude and an admission of inability to do things that are not the concern of slaves and an admission of weakness in claiming what he does not have, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which there is the greatest deterrent and the most eloquent admonition for whoever claims for himself what is not his concern, and claims knowledge of the unseen through astrology, geomancy, or knocking on pebbles or warning. Then he confirmed this and decided it by saying: And if I knew the unseen, I would have increased in goodness. That is, if I knew the kind of unseen, I would have exposed myself to what is good and brought it to myself and timed what is bad so that it would not touch me, but I am a slave who does not know what is with my Lord, nor what He decreed it for me and predestined it for me, so how can I know anything other than that and take the trouble to know it? It was said that the meaning is: If I knew what God Almighty wanted from me before He made it known to me, I would have done it. It was said: If I knew when I would be victorious in war, I would have fought and not been defeated. It was said: If I knew the unseen, I would have answered everything I was asked about. It is better to take the verse as general, so that these matters and others are included under it. It was said that and no harm has touched me is a new statement, meaning that I do not have what you claim of madness. It is better that it is connected to what came before it. The meaning is: If I knew the unseen, harm would not have touched me and I would have been wary of it, as we have mentioned. His statement: I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe. That is, I am only a conveyor of God’s rulings, warning some people with them and giving good tidings to others with them, and I do not know the unseen of God, the Most High. The lam in to a people is related to both attributes: that is, a bringer of good tidings to a people, and a warner to a people. It was said that it is related to a bringer of good tidings, and what is related to a warner is omitted: that is, a warner to a people who disbelieve, and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.
7:189: His saying: 189- It is He who created you from one soul. This is an introductory statement that includes mentioning God’s blessings upon His servants and not rewarding them for them, which is required in terms of gratitude and acknowledgment of servitude and that He is the only One with divinity. The majority of commentators said: What is meant by the single soul is Adam, and His statement: And made from it its mate is connected to He created you, meaning He is the One who created you from the soul of Adam and made from this soul its mate, which is Eve, He created her from one of his ribs. It was said that the meaning is He made from it of its kind as in His statement: He made for you from yourselves mates, and the first is more appropriate. So that he may dwell in tranquility with her is a reason for the making: meaning He made him from it so that he may dwell in tranquility with her, feel comfortable with her and be reassured by her, for the kind is more comfortable with its kind and more comfortable with it. This was in Paradise as the reports have reported. Then the Almighty began with another state that was between them in this world after their descent, so He said: So when he covered her, and covering her is a metaphor for intercourse: meaning when he had intercourse with her, she bore a light burden, she became attached to him after intercourse. He described it as light because when the sperm is emitted it is lighter than when it is a clot, and when it is a clot it is lighter than when it is a lump of flesh, and when it is a lump of flesh it is lighter than what comes after it. It was said that this burden was made light for her from From its beginning to its end, and she did not find it burdensome as pregnant women find it, because of his saying: So she passed by it, meaning she continued with that pregnancy, standing and sitting and going about her business, not finding it burdensome. The first interpretation is more appropriate because of his saying: So when she became heavy, because its meaning is: So when she became heavy due to the growth of the child in her belly. It was read So she passed by it with a light pronunciation, meaning she was distressed by it. It was read So she passed by it from mawr, which is coming and going. It was said that the meaning is: So she continued with it. The reading of alleviation has been narrated from Ibn Abbas and Yahya bin Ya’mar, and the reading of Fa-Marat has been narrated from Abdullah bin Omar, and it has been narrated from Ibn Abbas that he read Fa-Mat-ar-Rahmat with his saying: They called upon God, their Lord is the answer to when: meaning Adam and Eve called upon their Lord and the owner of their affair If You give us a righteous child meaning a righteous child, and the lam is the answer to an omitted oath, and We will surely be among the grateful is the answer to the oath that took the place of the answer to the condition: meaning among those who are grateful to You for this blessing, and in this supplication there is evidence that they knew that what happened in Eve’s belly as a result of that intercourse was of their kind and they knew that the offspring affected by that cause would be established.
7:190: 190- So when He gave them what they asked for of a righteous son and answered their prayer, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. Many commentators said: Satan came to Eve and said to her: If you give birth to a son, name him after me. She said: What is your name? He said: Al-Harith. If he had named himself for her, she would have known him. So she named him Abd al-Harith. This was polytheism in the name, but not polytheism in the worship. Rather, they meant that Al-Harith was the reason for the son's salvation, just as a man names himself the slave of his guest, as Hatim al-Ta'i said: I am the guest's slave as long as he is staying, and that is the only characteristic of a slave. A group of commentators said: The one who made a partner in what he gave them is the same race as the children of Adam, as happened with the polytheists among them, and it was not from Adam and Eve. This is indicated by the plural of the pronoun in his statement: So exalted is God above what they associate with Him. A group of commentators went to the meaning of from one soul from one form and one shape, and made from it its mate meaning from its own race, and when it covered her meaning the male race and the female race, and based on this, there is no mention of Adam and Eve in the verse and the dual pronouns refer to both genders. We have already indicated something like this and mentioned that it is not preferable for matters including and made from it its mate that this is for Eve, and including they called upon God, their Lord because every child born between the two genders is not from them when this call is made. The people of Medina and Asim read shirk in the singular form, and Abu Amr and the rest of the people of Kufa read it in the plural form. Al-Akhfash Saeed rejected the first reading, and it was answered that it is correct with the deletion of the complement: that is, they made for him a partner, or people of polytheism.
7:191: And the question in 191- Do they associate with Him that which does not create anything? is for rebuke and rebuke: that is, how do they make a partner for God that does not create anything and is not able to benefit them or protect them? His statement: And they create is in apposition to that which does not create and the pronoun refers to the partners who do not create anything: that is, and those whom they made partners from the idols or devils are created, and their plural is the plural of rational people because those who made them partners believe that they are so.
7:192: 192- And they cannot help them meaning those whom He made partners nor can they help themselves if He demands it from them nor can they help themselves if something happens to them from someone other than them, and whoever is unable to help himself is even more unable to help someone else. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Haml bin Abi Qais and Shamul bin Zaid said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell us when the Hour will be, if you are a prophet as you say, for we know what it is. So God revealed: “They ask you about the Hour: When will it come? Say: The knowledge thereof is only with my Lord.” until His saying: But most people do not know. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada: When will it come? meaning when will it come? “Say: The knowledge thereof is only with my Lord. None can reveal its time except Him.” He said: Quraysh said: O Muhammad, tell us about the Hour, because of the kinship between us and you? He said: “They ask you as if you are aware of it. Say: The knowledge thereof is only with God.” He mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “The Hour will come upon the people while a man is watering his livestock, while a man is repairing his trough, while a man is lowering his scales and raising them, while a man is displaying his merchandise in the market. The decree of God will not come upon you except suddenly.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: When will it be anchored? He said: Its end. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid: None can reveal it at its time except Him. He said: None can bring it about except God. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse: He will reveal it at its time, and none knows that except God. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Its burden is heavy upon the heavens and the earth. He said: There is nothing among creation that will not be afflicted with harm on the Day of Resurrection. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Its burden is heavy upon the heavens and the earth. He said: Its knowledge is heavy upon the people of the heavens and the earth, meaning it is too great for them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: It is heavy in the heavens and the earth, he said: When it comes, the heaven will split, the stars will scatter, the sun will be rolled up, the mountains will move, and whatever befalls the earth will happen, and what God, the Most High, said will happen, so that is its weight in them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: It will not come to you except suddenly, he said: Suddenly, while you are safe. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Baath on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: As if you were aware of it, he said: You were afraid to ask about it until you knew it. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: As if you were aware of it, he said: As if you knew about it, meaning you do not know it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority: As if you were aware of it, he said: Gentle with it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi also narrated from him, As if you are well-versed in it, meaning: As if there is love between you and them, as if you are their friend. He said: When the people asked Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, about the Hour, they asked him the question of people as if they thought that Muhammad was well-versed in them, so God revealed to him, The knowledge thereof is with God only, He kept its knowledge to Himself and did not reveal it to any angel or messenger. Abd bin Hamid narrated from Amr bin Dinar who said: Ibn Abbas used to recite, As if you are well-versed in it. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Jurayj, Say, ‘I do not control for myself any benefit or harm,’ he said: guidance and misguidance. And if I knew the unseen, meaning when I would die, I would have increased in good, meaning righteous deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And if I knew the unseen, I would have increased in good, he said: I would know that if I bought something I would not profit from it, so I would not sell something in which there is no profit, And no harm would have touched me, he said: I would avoid whatever evil would happen before it happens. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Ruwayani, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Samurah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “When Eve gave birth, Satan went around her, and she did not have a living child. He said: ‘Name him Abd Al-Harith, for he will live.’ So she named him Abd Al-Harith, and he lived. This was from the inspiration and command of Satan.” Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Samurah, regarding the statement of God, ‘But when He gave them both a good child, they ascribed to Him partners. ’ He said: They named him Abd Al-Harith. Abd ibn Humayd and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abi ibn Ka’b a similar hadeeth of Samurah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Eve became pregnant and Satan came to her and said: I am your companion who expelled you from Paradise. You must obey me or I will make for him two horns of a deer and he will come out of your belly and split it open. I will do this and I will do that, frightening them. They named him Abd Al-Harith, but they refused to obey him and he came out dead. Then she became pregnant and he came to them again and said the same thing. They refused to obey him and he came out dead. Then she became pregnant and he came to them and mentioned it to them. They were overcome by the love of a child and they named him Abd Al-Harith. This is what God said: They attributed to Him partners in what He has given them. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse. He said: This was with some of the people of religions and not with Adam. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Samurah regarding His statement: She bore a light burden that was not obvious and she passed by it when her pregnancy was obvious. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So she passed by him, he said: So she doubted whether she was pregnant or not. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ayoub who said: Al-Hasan was asked about his statement: So she passed by him, he said: If I were an Arab, I would have known that she only continued to be pregnant. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: She carried a light pregnancy, he said: It is the sperm. So she passed by him, he said: She continued with it. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So she passed by him, he said: She took it lightly. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Salih regarding his statement: If You give us a good one, he said: They feared that he would be an animal, so they said: If You give us a perfect human being. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Mujahid. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse, he said: A perfect boy. And Abd bin Hamid narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: They made partners for Him, he said: He was a partner in obedience, but he was not a partner in worship. And Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, he said: Adam did not associate partners, the beginning of which was gratitude, and the end of which was an example for those who came after him. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Suddi regarding his statement: So exalted is God above what they associate with Him, this is a section from the verse about Adam specifically regarding the gods of the Arabs. And Ibn Abi Malik narrated something similar. And Abd bin Hamid and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Al-Hasan regarding the verse, he said: This is about the disbelievers who call upon God, and when He gives them goodness, they give them guidance or victory. Then He said: Do they associate with Him that which does not create anything and they themselves are created? He said: They obey that which does not create anything, and they are the devils who do not create anything and they themselves are created. And they are not able to give them victory, he said: for those who call upon them.
7:193: His statement: 193- And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. This is addressed to the polytheists: that is, if you call these partners to guidance and right conduct by asking them to guide you and direct you, they will not follow you nor respond to you in that, and it is less than what you ask of them in terms of bringing benefit, repelling harm, and victory over the enemies. Al-Akhfash said that its meaning is that if you call them, meaning the idols, to guidance, they will not follow you. It was said that what is meant is those who are predetermined in God's knowledge that they will not believe. It was read they will not follow you with a shaddah and a light sukoon, and they are two dialects. Some linguists said: I followed him in the light form: if he went behind him and did not catch up with him, and I followed him in the heavy form: if he went behind him and caught up with him. The sentence It is the same for you whether you call upon them or are silent confirms the meaning of what preceded it: that is, your calling upon them in times of hardship or not is the same, there is no difference between them, because they do not benefit or harm, and they do not hear or respond. He said: Or are you silent in place of you were silent because of the exaggeration in the nominal sentence. Muhammad bin Yahya said: The nominal sentence came because it is the beginning of a verse, meaning to match nor will they help themselves and what preceded it.
7:194: His statement: 194- Indeed, those you call upon besides God are servants like you. God Almighty informed them that these whom you have made into gods are servants of God just as you are His servants, although you are more perfect than them, because you are alive and speak and walk and hear and see, and these idols are not like that, but they are like you in that they are owned by God and subjected to His command, and in this there is a severe rebuke and a great rebuke to them, and the phrase So call upon them and let them respond to you confirms the content of what preceded it that if you call them to guidance they will not follow them, and that they are not able to do anything: that is, call upon these partners, and if they are as you claim, then let them respond to you if you are truthful in what you call upon them of their ability to benefit and harm.
7:195: And the question in His saying: 195- Have they inspired legs and what follows is for rebuke and rebuke: meaning, those whom you have made partners do not have any of the tools that are fixed for you, let alone being able to do what you ask of them, for as you see, these idols that you are devoted to worshiping do not have legs with which they walk in benefiting themselves, let alone walking in benefiting you, and they do not have hands with which they strike as others among the living strike, and they do not have eyes with which they see as you see, and they do not have ears with which they hear as you hear, so how do you call those who are in this state of being deprived of tools, and in this state of inability, and the mother in these places is the disconnected one that means rather and the hamza as the imams of grammar mentioned. Saeed bin Jubair read Indeed those you call upon with a light in and the accusative of ibbadan meaning what are those you call upon besides God, servants like you on the basis of the negative in working as the Hijazi ma.
