This reading was weakened because it contradicts what Sibawayh and others preferred in choosing the nominative in its predicate, and because Al-Kisa'i said: It hardly comes in the speech of the Arabs with the meaning of ma unless it is followed by an affirmative as in His statement: Indeed the disbelievers are only in delusion, and batsh means taking by force. Abu Ja'far read yabatshun with a damma on the ta, and it is a language, then when he explained to them the state of these idols, and the aspects of their deficiency and inability from every aspect, God commanded him to say to them: Call upon your partners whom you claim have the ability to benefit and harm, then plot you and them together with whatever aspects of plotting you wish, so do not wait meaning do not give me time or delay in bringing harm upon me from their side, and kayd means deceit, and there is nothing after this challenge to them and this incapacitating of their idols.
7:196: Then he said to them: 196- "Indeed, my ally is God, who revealed the Book meaning, how can I fear these idols that have these characteristics when I have a ally to whom I can resort and seek help from, and He is God, the Almighty, Who revealed the Book" This sentence is an explanation for not caring about them, and the ally of something is the one who protects it, supports it, and prevents harm from it. "And He is the Guardian of the righteous" meaning He protects them and supports them, and comes between them and their enemies. Al-Akhfash said: It was read "Indeed, my ally is God, who revealed the Book" meaning Gabriel. Al-Nahhas said: This is the reading of Asim Al-Jahdary, and the first reading is clearer because of his saying: "And He is the Guardian of the righteous".
7:197: His statement: 197- And those whom you call upon besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves. The Almighty repeated this for further emphasis and confirmation, and because the repetition of rebuke and reprimand humiliates and belittles the polytheists, and reveals the foolishness of their minds and the weakness of their dreams.
7:198: 198- "And you see them looking at you" is a nominative sentence to show their inability, or a state: that is, while the situation is that you see them looking at you while they do not see, and what is meant is the idols, they resemble the observers, but they do not have eyes with which they see. It was said: They used to make eyes for the idols from manufactured jewels, so they were in the form of observers but did not see. It was said that what is meant by that are the polytheists, God informed about them that they do not see when they do not benefit from their eyes, and if they see with them other than what is of benefit to them. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: The sun and the moon will be brought and will stand before God Almighty, and those who used to worship them will be brought and it will be said: Call upon them and let them respond to you if you are truthful. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And you will see them looking at you, he said: These are the polytheists. These also narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And you will see them looking at you, but they do not see, what he is calling them to of guidance.
7:199: His saying: 199- Take what is easy when God enumerated what He enumerated of the conditions of the polytheists and the foolishness of their opinion and the misguidance of their efforts: He ordered His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to take what is easy from their morals. It is said: I took my right easily: meaning easily, and this is a type of facilitation that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to command as it was proven in the Sahih that he used to say: Make things easy and do not make them difficult and give good tidings and do not repel. What is meant by forgiveness here is the opposite of effort, and it was said that what is meant is: Take what is easy from their charity and do not be strict with them in it and take what is difficult for them, and this was before the revelation of the obligation of zakat. And enjoin what is right meaning what is right. Isa bin Omar read with al-'urf with two dammahs, and they are two languages, and al-'urf, al-'aruf, and al-'arfah: every good characteristic that the minds accept and the souls are reassured by, and from it is the saying of the poet: He who does good will not lose his reward. Customs between God and people will not be lost. And turn away from the ignorant meaning if you establish proof in ordering them to do good and they do not do it, then turn away from them and do not argue with them or be foolish with them as a reward for their argumentation and foolishness. It was said: This verse is among the things that were abrogated by the verse of the sword, as stated by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd and Ata’. It was also said: It is decisive, as stated by Mujahid and Qatadah.
7:200: His saying: 200- And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan An evil suggestion is a whisper, as well as a nagging or stabbing. Al-Zajjaj said: An evil suggestion is the slightest movement, and from Satan is the slightest whisper. The root of evil is corruption. It is said: He caused corruption between us, meaning he corrupted. It is also said that evil is seduction, and the meanings are close. God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, if he became aware of something from Satan's evil suggestion, to seek refuge in God. It was said: "When His statement, 'Take what is easy' was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How about anger, O Lord? So it was revealed. The phrase, 'Indeed, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing' is the reason for His command to seek refuge, meaning seek refuge in Him and turn to Him, for He hears that from you and knows about it.
7:201: And sentence 201 - Indeed, those who fear God - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember confirms the content of what preceded it: that is, the state and condition of those who fear God is to remember what God has commanded of seeking refuge with Him and turning to Him when an impulse touches them from Satan, even if it is slight. The people of Basra read tayf and so did the people of Mecca. The people of Medina and Kufa read tayf. Saeed bin Jubair read tayf with emphasis. An-Nahhas said: The speech of the Arabs in such a case is tayf with emphasis, as it is a verbal noun from tafa yatif. Al-Kisa'i said: It is lightened like mayyt and mayyt. An-Nahhas said: Its meaning in the language is what is imagined in the heart or seen in a dream, and this is the meaning of tayf. Abu Hatim said: I asked Al-Asma'i about tayf and he said: There is no fa'il in the verbal nouns. An-Nahhas said: It is not a source, but it has the meaning of a wanderer. It was said: The spectre and the wanderer have two different meanings. The first is imagination, and the second is the devil himself. The first is from the imagination wandering, wandering a specter, and they did not say from this a wanderer. Al-Suhayli said: Because it is imagination and has no reality. As for his saying: And a wanderer from your Lord wandered over them, it is not said a specter in it because it is a real active participle. Al-Zajjaj said: I wandered over them, I wander, so the imagination wandered, wanders. Hassan said: So leave this but it is nice to keep me awake when dinner is over The whispering was called a specter because it is a gathering of the devil similar to the gathering of the imagination. So they will see because of the remembrance: meaning they will be alert, and it was said with insight. Saeed bin Jubair read they remembered with a shaddah on the dhal. An-Nahhas said: There is no basis for this in Arabic.
7:202: His saying: 202- And their brothers extend them in error. It was said that the meaning is: And the brothers of the devils, who are the wicked among the misguided people, on the basis that the pronoun in their brothers refers to the devil mentioned previously, and what is meant by him is the genus, so it is permissible to refer the collective pronoun to him extend them in error, meaning the devils extend them in error and are an extension for them, and the wicked among people are called brothers of the devils because they accept them and follow their example, and it was said that what is meant by the brothers are the devils and by the pronoun is the wicked among people, so the report is applicable to whoever it belongs to. Al-Zajjaj said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: And those whom you call upon besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves. And their brothers extend them in error, because the disbelievers are brothers of the devils. Then they do not stop. Stopping means refraining from something, meaning the devils do not stop in extending the disbelievers in error. It was said: In error is connected to His saying: extend them, and it was said: With the brothers, and error is and ignorance. Nafi’ read extend them with a damma on the letter of the present tense and a kasra on the meem. The rest read with a fatha on the letter of the present tense and a damma on the meem, and they are two dialects: it is said: to extend and to amplify. Makki said: and to extend more. Abu Ubaid and a group of linguists said: It is said that if something increases something by itself, it is extended, and if it is increased by something else, it is said: it is extended, like Your Lord extends you with five thousand angels. It was said: It is said: I extended in evil and I extended in good. Asim Al-Jahdary read extend them in error. Isa bin Omar read Then they will not be shortened with the opening of the ya’, the damma of the sad, and the softening of the qaf.
7:203: His saying: 203- And if you do not bring them a sign, they say, 'Why did you not select it?' The word select means collect for itself: that is, gather it, i.e. why did you not gather it together, making it up from yourself? It was also said that the meaning is: you fabricated it. It is said: you fabricated the speech: you assumed it, invented it, and fabricated it, if you brought it from yourself. They used to say this statement to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the revelation was delayed, so God commanded him to respond to them by saying: I only follow what is revealed to me, i.e. I am not one of those who bring signs from himself as you claim. Say, 'I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord,' so what He revealed to me and sent down to me, I conveyed to you. Basair is the plural of Basira, i.e. this Qur'an revealed to me is insights from your Lord, with which one can see from before it. It was also said: Basairs are arguments and proofs. Al-Zajjaj said: Insights are paths, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe. It is connected to insights: meaning this Qur’an is insights and guidance by which the believers are guided, and a mercy for them.
7:204: His saying: 204- And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent. God Almighty commanded them to listen to the Qur'an and be silent when it is recited so that they may benefit from it and ponder the wisdom and benefits in it. It was said: This command is specific to the time of prayer when the imam is reciting, and it is not hidden from you that the wording is broader than this and the general is not limited to its reason, so listening and being silent when reciting the Qur'an is in every situation and in any manner that is required of the listener. It was said: This is specific to the recitation of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the Qur'an and not others, and there is no basis for that. Perhaps you will receive mercy, meaning that you will attain mercy and win it by obeying the command of God Almighty. Then God Almighty commanded him to remember Him in himself, for concealment is more conducive to sincerity and more likely to be accepted. It was said: What is meant by remembrance here is what is more general than the Qur'an and other remembrances with which God is remembered.
7:205: Al-Nahhas said: There is no disagreement about the meaning of 205- And remember your Lord within yourself that it is supplication, and it was said that it is specific to the Qur'an: that is, read the Qur'an with contemplation and reflection, and supplicating and fearing are in the accusative case as a state: that is, suppliantly and fearfully, and fear is fear, and its origin is fear, and the waw was changed to a ya because of the kasra of what preceded it. Al-Farra' narrated that the plural of fear is said to be khayf. Al-Jawhari said: Fear is fear, and the plural is khayf, and its origin is waw: meaning fear. And without the loudness of speech meaning without the loudness of speech, and it is conjoined with what precedes it: meaning supplicating, fearful, and speaking words that are without the loudness of speech, and in the morning and the evenings is related to I remember meaning the times of the mornings and the times of the evenings, and the morning is the plural of morning, and the evenings is the plural of aseel, as al-Zajjaj and al-Akhfash said, like yameen and ayman, and it was said: the evenings is the plural of asl, and the origin is the plural of aseel, so according to this it is the plural of the plural, as al-Farra’ said. Al-Jawhari said: the afternoon is the time from after the afternoon until sunset, and its plural is asl, asals, and asail as if it is the plural of aseelah. The poet said: By my life, you are the house whose people are most honored, and I sit in its courtyard in the evenings. It is also pluralized as Aslan, such as Ba’ir and Ba’ran. Abu Majlaz read Al-Isal, which is a verbal noun. He singled out these two times for their honor, and what is meant is constant remembrance of God. And do not be among the heedless, meaning of the remembrance of God.
7:206: 206- Indeed, those who are with your Lord are not too proud to worship Him meaning the angels. Al-Qurtubi said: By consensus. Al-Zajjaj said: He said: With your Lord and God Almighty is in every place because they are close to His mercy, and everyone who is close to the mercy of God Almighty is with Him. Another said: Because they are in a place where nothing but God's judgment is implemented. It was said: They are the messengers of God, just as it is said that there is a large army near the caliph. It was said: This is to honor and glorify them. The meaning of glorify Him is to glorify Him and declare Him free from all shame. And to Him they prostrate means they single Him out with the worship of prostration, which is the most honorable worship. It was said: What is meant by prostration is submission and humility, and in mentioning the highest assembly there is an allusion to the children of Adam. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa'i, An-Nahhas in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr regarding his statement: Adopt forgiveness, the verse, he said: This verse was not revealed except regarding the differences of people. In another version: God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pardon people's morals. Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement: Adopt forgiveness, he said: God commanded His Prophet to pardon people's morals. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi who said: “When God revealed, ‘Accept forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant,’ the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: I do not know until I ask the scholar. So he went and then came back and said: God has commanded you to forgive those who wrong you, give to those who deprive you, and connect with those who cut you off.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Jabir. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Qays bin Sa’d bin Ubadah who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, he said: By God, I will mutilate seventy of them. Then Gabriel came to him with this verse. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha regarding his statement, ‘Accept forgiveness,’ he said: Whatever good morals He has forgiven you. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Take what is easy, he said: Take what is easy from their wealth, whatever they bring to you, take it. This was before the revelation of Bara’ah with the obligatory charity and its details. Ibn Jarir and An-Nahhas narrated in his Naskh on the authority of As-Suddi regarding the verse: The surplus of wealth was abrogated by Zakat. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd who said: When the verse Take what is easy was revealed, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: What about anger, O Lord? Then the verse And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan was revealed. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Indeed, those who fear God, he said: They are the believers. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: When an impulse touches them from Satan, he said: Anger. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The evil suggestion is anger. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: Remember, he said: If they slip, they repent. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: Al-Ta’if said: The gathering is from Satan. Remember, then at once they have insight, he said: Then at once they are desisting from sin, taking God’s command and disobeying Satan. And their brothers, he said: The brothers of the devils. They extend them in error and then do not stop, he said: Neither do the humans refrain from what they do of evil, nor do the devils refrain from them. “And when you do not bring them a sign, they say: Why did you not choose it?” He said: Why did you not invent it? Why did you not receive it and create it? Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority: And their brothers extend them in error, he said: They are the jinn who inspire their human allies. Then they do not stop, he said: They do not get tired. “And when you do not bring them a sign, they say: Why did you not choose it?” He said: Why did you not make it up on your own. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah regarding the statement of God's Messenger (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), And when the Qur'an is recited, the verse, he said: It was revealed regarding raising the voices while they were behind the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) in prayer. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: It means in the obligatory prayer. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority, he said: The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), and some people recited behind him and they mixed up, so the verse, And when the Qur'an is recited, was revealed. This applies to the obligatory prayer. He said: Even if we do not listen to those who recite in a quieter voice than in a loud voice. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka'b Al-Qurazi. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar in his Sunan on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Abdullah bin Mughaffal. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Mas`ud something similar to this. Something similar to this has been narrated from a group of the Salaf, and they stated that this verse was revealed regarding the recitation of the prayer by the Imam. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from al-Hasan regarding the verse: During the prescribed prayer and during remembrance. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: During prayer and when the revelation is sent down. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from him regarding the verse: This is regarding prayer. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah regarding His statement: And remember your Lord within yourself al-Bayhaqi 3:11, that God commanded him to remember Him and forbade him from heedlessness. As for the morning, it is the Fajr prayer, and the evenings, it is the evening prayer. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Sakhr, who said: The evenings are between Dhuhr and Asr. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse: Do not recite that aloud, ‘in the mornings and the evenings’, in the early morning and the evening. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, In the morning, he said: The last part of the dawn prayer is the morning prayer, and the last part of the evening prayer is the afternoon prayer. The hadiths and reports from the Companions about the prostration of recitation, the number of places in which one prostrates, the manner of prostration, and what is said in it are fully mentioned in the books of hadith and jurisprudence, so we will not prolong the mention of that here.
8:1: Many commentators have stated that it was revealed in Medina and did not exclude anything from it, and this is what Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Jabir bin Zaid and Ata' said. Something similar has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, narrated by An-Nahhas in his Naskh, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh from him, who said: Surat Al-Anfal was revealed in Medina. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from Zayd bin Thabit. Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: It was revealed in Badr. In another version: This is Surat Badr. Al-Qurtubi said: Ibn Abbas said that it is Medinan except for seven verses from the words: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you until the last seven verses, and the total number of verses in this Surah is seventy-six, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite it in the Maghrib prayer, as narrated by At-Tabarani with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Ayyub. Zaid bin Thabit also narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to recite Surat Al-Anfal in the two rak’ahs of the Maghrib prayer. Al-Anfal is the plural of Nafl, which means spoils. From this comes the saying of Antarah: When the battle rages, we quench our thirst with spears and protect ourselves at the spoils-of-war. Any spoils, and the root of the word nafl is: increase, and it was called ghanimah because it is an increase in what God has made lawful for this nation from what was forbidden to others, or because it is an increase over what the mujahid obtains from the reward of jihad, and the word nafl is used for other meanings including an oath, seeking, and a known plant. The voluntary act is voluntary because it is an increase over the obligatory act, and the voluntary act is the child of a child, because it is an increase over a child. The reason for the revelation of the verse was the disagreement of the companions, may God be pleased with them, on the day of Badr, as will be explained, so God took what they had taken from their hands and made it for God and the Messenger, so He said: 1- "Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger" meaning its ruling is specific to them, the Messenger of God divides it among you by the command of God, the Most High, and you have no ruling in that. A group of the Companions and Followers believed that the spoils of war were specifically for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that no one else had a share in them, until God Almighty revealed His words: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God. Then He commanded them to be pious, to reconcile people, and to obey God and the Messenger by submitting to their commands and abandoning the differences that occurred between them. Then He said: If you are believers, meaning, comply with these three commands if you are believers in God. There is in it a provocation and incitement that is not hidden, while they were in that state of faith, so it is as if He said: If you continue to believe in God, because these three matters, which are fear of God, reconciling people, and obeying God and the Messenger, faith is not complete without them, rather it is not established at all for the one who does not comply with them, because the one who is not pious and does not obey God and His Messenger is not a believer. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: I asked Ubadah bin Al-Samit about the spoils of war, and he said: It was revealed about us, the companions of Badr, when we disagreed about the voluntary spoils of war and our morals deteriorated, so God took it from our hands and gave it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Messenger of God divided it among the Muslims equally. Saeed bin Mansour, Ahmad, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and I witnessed Badr with him. The people met and God defeated the enemy. A group set out in their tracks, defeating and killing them, and a group attacked the army, seizing and gathering it. A group surrounded the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so that the enemy would not be taken by surprise. When night fell, the people returned to each other. Those who had collected the spoils said: We have collected them and gathered them, so no one has a share in them. Those who went out in pursuit of the enemy said: You are not more deserving of them than we are. We drove the enemy away from him and defeated them. Those who surrounded the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You are not more deserving of them than we are. We surrounded the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and feared that the enemy would take him by surprise, so we occupied ourselves with him. Then the verse was revealed: “They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among the Muslims. Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raided enemy territory, he would give away a quarter, and whenever he returned and left the people, he would give away a third. He disliked spoils of war and would say: Let the strong Muslims return to the weak among them. Ishaq bin Rahawayh in his Musnad, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a military expedition and God aided it and granted it victory. Whoever brought him something, he would give him a fifth of the spoils. Then some men who had been sent forward, killed and taken captive returned and left the spoils behind them, and they did not get anything from the spoils. They said: O Messenger of God, what is the matter with some of our men who were sent forward and taken captive, while some men who had not fought stayed behind, so we gave them a fifth of the spoils? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent and the verse: “They ask you about the spoils of war” was revealed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them and said: Return what you have taken and divide it equally and fairly, for God commands you to do so. They said: We have spent and eaten. He said: Seek reward for that.” Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu’aym in Al-Hilyah, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas who said: “I said: O Messenger of God, God has cured me today of the polytheists, so give me this sword. He said: This sword is neither for you nor for me, put it down. So I put it down, then I returned and said: Perhaps this sword will be given today to someone who will not suffer as I did when a man calls me from behind me. I said: Has God revealed anything about me? He said: You asked me for this sword and it was not mine, but it has been given to me and it is yours. God revealed this verse: ‘They ask you about the spoils of war. ’” And in a wording of Ahmad: “Sa’d said: When my brother was killed on the day of Badr and I killed Sa’id ibn Al-’As and took his sword, which was called Dhu Al-Kunayfah, I brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above.” This hadith has been narrated on the authority of Sa’d through other chains of narration. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather: “The people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the spoils of war on the day of Badr, so this verse was revealed: ‘They ask you about the spoils of war.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not give any spoils of war after this verse was revealed to him, except from the fifth, for he gave a spoils of war on the day of Khaybar from the fifth. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: On the day of Badr, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever kills someone will have such and such, and whoever takes a prisoner will have such and such. As for the elders, they stood firm under the banners, and as for the young men, they hastened to kill and take the spoils. The elders said to the young men: ‘Include us with you, for we have been a support for you. If you had anything against us, you would have taken refuge with us.’ They disputed before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the verse was revealed: ‘They ask you about the spoils of war’. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divided the spoils equally among them.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: They ask you about the spoils of war. He said: The spoils of war are the booty, which were exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one had a share of it. Whatever the Muslims took from the raids they brought to him, so whoever withheld a needle or a wire from it, it was theft. So they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give them something from it, so God revealed: “They ask you about the spoils of war. Say, ‘The spoils of war,’ I have given them to my Messenger, you have no share in them. ‘So fear God and amend your affairs among yourselves,’” until His statement: If you are believers. Then God revealed: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils of war,’ the verse, then he divided that fifth for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the emigrants in the way of God, and He made four-fifths of the people equal, with two shares for the horse, one share for its owner, and one share for the foot soldier. Abu Ubaid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: They ask you about the spoils of war, he said: They are the booty, then it was abrogated by And know that whatever you obtain of spoils of war, the verse. Malik, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Ubaid, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, An-Nahhas, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad who said: I heard a man asking Ibn Abbas about the spoils of war, so he said: The horse is from the spoils of war and the spoils of war are from the spoils of war. So he repeated the question and Ibn Abbas said: This is like Dhubay’ whom Umar struck. In another version: He said: How much you need for what Umar did to Dhubay’ Al-Iraqi to be done to you, and Umar struck him until blood ran down his heels. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: The spoils of war are the spoils of war. They were commanded to reconcile their differences in it, so the strong would be given back to the weak. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, An-Nahhas and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding his statement, They ask you about the spoils of war, that he said: It is what the polytheists strayed from to the Muslims without fighting, such as a slave, an animal or property, so that is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do with it as he wishes. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr who said: We sent to Saeed bin Al-Musayyab to ask him about the spoils of war, so he said: You are asking me about the spoils of war, and there is no voluntary charity after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Saeed also who said: They did not give voluntary charity except from the fifth. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on his authority that he said: There is no voluntary charity in the spoils of war of the Muslims except from the fifth of the fifth. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Anas that one of the princes wanted to give it as a voluntary charity before giving it as a fifth, but Anas refused to accept it until he gave it as a fifth. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi regarding his statement, They ask you about the spoils of war, that he said: What the raiding parties took. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and An-Nahhas in his Naskh narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah who said: The spoils of war were for God and the Messenger until the verse on the fifth abrogated it: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils al-Khums. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And amend that which is between you al-Adab Al-Mufrad, he said: This is a command from God to the believers to fear God and amend that which is between them when they differed regarding the spoils of war. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Makhul who said: The reconciliation between them was that the spoils of war were returned and divided between those who remained with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and those who fought and took spoils of war. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding his statement: And obey God and His Messenger al-Adab Al-Mufrad, he said: Obeying the Messenger means following the Book and the Sunnah.
8:2: Wajal: Fear and terror. What is meant is that fear of God and terror of Him when He is mentioned is the concern of believers who have perfect faith and are sincere to God. The restriction is based on the perfection of faith, not on the origin of faith. A group of commentators said: This verse includes an incitement to obey the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he commanded regarding the division of spoils. It is clear to you that even if this is correct to include it under the meaning of the verse, from the perspective that the fear of hearts when mentioned and the increase of faith when reciting the verses of God necessitate compliance with what He, the Most High, commanded regarding the spoils being for God and the Messenger. However, it appears that the purpose of the verse is to prove this advantage for those whose faith is perfect without restricting it to one condition rather than another, or to one time rather than another, or to one event rather than another. What is meant by reciting His verses is the recitation of the revealed verses or the expression of the wonder of His creation and the perfection of His power in His verses of creation by mentioning their wondrous creation and their wonders, when the believers are reminded of them, they are in awe. It was said: What is meant by increasing faith is increasing the expansion of the chest, the reassurance of the heart, and the delight of the mind when reciting the verses. It was also said: What is meant by increasing faith is increasing action, because faith is one thing that does not increase or decrease, and the many verses and the successive hadiths refute and reject that. 2- And upon their Lord they rely not upon anyone else, and relying upon God is entrusting the matter to Him in all matters.
8:3: The relative pronoun in his saying: 3- Those who establish prayer is in the nominative case as a description of the relative pronoun before it, or a substitute for it or an explanation of it, or in the accusative case as praise. He singled out establishing prayer and charity because they are the origin and foundation of goodness, and the min in mama is for partiality.
8:4: And the reference in his saying: 4- those to those who are described with the above descriptions is the subject and its predicate is they are the believers meaning that these are the ones who are perfect in faith and have reached its highest degrees and furthest ends, and truly is a source confirming the content of the sentence they are the believers: meaning that is truly true or a description of a deleted source: meaning they are the believers with true faith, then he mentioned what is prepared for those who combine these descriptions of honor, so he said: For them are degrees meaning homes of goodness, honor, and glory in Paradise that are with their Lord, and in their being with Him, glory be to Him, there is an increase in their honor, respect, glorification, and magnification, and the sentence for them are degrees with their Lord is a second predicate for those or a new sentence in response to an implied question, and and forgiveness is conjoined with degrees meaning forgiveness for their sins, and generous provision with which God honors them from His vast grace and abundant goodness. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And their hearts became fearful, he said: Their hearts became frightened. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse: The hypocrites do not have any remembrance of God in their hearts when performing His obligations, nor do they believe in any of the signs of God, nor do they put their trust in God, nor do they pray when they are absent, nor do they pay the zakat of their wealth. God informed us that they are not believers, then He described the believers and said: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, so they performed His obligations. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab on the authority of Umm Al-Darda’ who said: Fear in the heart is like the burning of a palm branch, O Shahr bin Hawshab. Do you not feel a shiver? I said: Yes. She said: Then supplicate at that time, for supplication is answered at that time. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Thabit Al-Bunani who said: So-and-so said: I know when my supplication will be answered. They said: Where did you get it from? He said: When my skin shivers, my heart fears, and my eyes overflow with tears, that is when my supplication will be answered. And he also narrated from Aisha, who said: Fear in the heart of the believer is like the blaze of a palm frond, so when one of you fears, let him supplicate at that time. And Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: It is a man who wants to wrong or is about to commit a sin, but it is said to him: Fear God, so his heart fears. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: It increased them in faith, he said: Confirmation. And these narrated from al-Rabi’ ibn Anas regarding his statement: It increased them in faith, he said: Fear. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And upon their Lord they rely, he said: They do not hope for anyone other than Him. And they narrated from him regarding his statement: Those are the believers, truly, he said: They are free from disbelief. And Abu al-Shaykh narrated from him: Truly, he said: Purely. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: For them are degrees, meaning virtues and mercy. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: For them are degrees, he said: Exalted deeds. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: For them are degrees, he said: The people of Paradise are some of them above others, so the one who is above will see his superiority over the one who is below him, and the one who is below will not see that anyone is superior to him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: And forgiveness, he said: By abandoning sins, And generous provision, he said: Good deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi who said: When you hear God say: And generous provision, then it is Paradise.
8:5: His saying: 5- As your Lord brought you out from your home with truth. Al-Zajjaj said: The Kaf is in the accusative case: meaning the spoils are fixed for you as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth: meaning like your Lord brought you out, and the meaning is: Go about your business with the spoils and give spoils to whomever you wish even if they hate it, because some of the companions said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he made something for everyone who brought a prisoner: Most of the people remained without anything, so the position of the Kaf is in the accusative case as we mentioned, and Al-Farraa said the same. Abu Ubaidah said: It is an oath: meaning the one who brought you out, so the Kaf means the waw, and ma means the one who. Al-Akhfash Saeed bin Mas'adah said: The meaning is those are the true believers as your Lord brought you out. And Ikrimah said: The meaning is: Obey God and His Messenger as your Lord brought you out. It was said: As he brought you out is related to His saying: For them are degrees meaning this promise to the believers is true in the Hereafter as your Lord brought you out from your home with the truth that is due to Him, so He fulfilled your promise and made you triumph over your enemy and fulfilled for you. An-Nahhas mentioned it and chose it. It was said: The kaf in kama is a kaf of comparison by way of recompense like the saying of the one who says to his servant: As I directed you to my enemies and they weakened you and you asked for help and help so I helped you and strengthened you and removed your illness, so take them now and punish them. It was said: The kaf is in the place of raising as it is the predicate of a deleted subject, the meaning of which is: This situation is like the situation of your expulsion, meaning that their situation in hating what you saw of the annihilation of the invaders is like their situation in hating your going out to war. The author of Al-Kashshaf mentioned it. And with the truth is related to something deleted, and the meaning is: An expulsion that is clothed in the truth in which there is no doubt. The phrase and indeed a party of the believers are hating is in the place of the accusative as a state: meaning as He sent you out when they hated it, because when God promised them one of the two groups, either the caravan or the army, they desired the caravan because of the spoils it contained and the safety from fighting, as will be explained.
8:6: And the sentence 6- They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear is either in the accusative case as a state after a state, or it is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, and their argument is when he summoned them to one of the two groups, and the caravan passed and he ordered them to fight the mobilization and they did not have much equipment with them, so it was difficult for them and they said: If you had told us about the fight, we would have taken the equipment and completed the preparation, and the meaning of in the truth is in the fight after it became clear to them that you do not order anything except with the permission of God, or after it became clear to them that God promised them victory over one of the two groups, and that if the caravan passed they would be victorious with the mobilization, and after is a circumstance to argue with you and what is a source meaning they argue with you after the truth became clear to them. His saying: As if they were being driven to death while they were looking on. The kaf is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in la-kahiroon, meaning that the state of their being in the intensity of their fear of fighting is like the state of someone who is being driven to be killed while he is witnessing the reasons for his killing, looking at them and not doubting them.
8:7: His statement: 7- And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours The circumstance is in the accusative case with an implied verb: that is, remember the time when God promised you one of the two parties and ordered them to remember the time, although the intention was to mention the events in it for the purpose of exaggeration. The two parties are the caravan and the mobilization. One is the second object of the verb promised, and that it would be yours is a substitute for it, a substitute of inclusion, and its meaning is: that it is subject to you and that you will defeat it and take from it spoils and do with it whatever you wish of killing, capturing and taking booty. They will not be able to repel you and they do not possess for themselves from you any harm or benefit. In this sentence there is a reminder to them of a blessing from the blessings that God bestowed upon them. His statement: And you wish is conjoined with promised you from the group of events whose time they were ordered to mention that the one without the power of the two parties, which is the caravan group, would be yours without the one with the power, which is the mobilization group. Abu Ubaidah said: That is, without an edge. The thorn is the weapon, and the thorn is the plant that has an edge. From this comes the word a man with a thorny weapon, meaning an iron weapon, then it is reversed and it is said: a man with a thorny weapon. The thorn is borrowed from the singular form of thorn. The meaning is: And you wish to be victorious over the group that has no weapon, which is the group of the caravan because it is pure booty free from the turbidity of fighting since there is no one with it to defend it. His statement: And God wants to establish the truth with His words is connected to you wish, and it is among what they were commanded to mention its time: That is, God wants other than what you want, which is to establish the truth by revealing what He has decreed of your victory over the thorn, and their killing of their leaders, and the capture of many of them, and the taking of what you have taken as booty from their wealth that they brought upon you and sought to repel you with. What is meant by the words are the verses that He revealed in fighting the thorn, and His promise to you of victory over it, and to cut off the root of the disbelievers, the other root, and cutting it off is an expression for extirpation. Meaning: He will eradicate them all.
8:8: His statement: 8- So that the truth may be established and falsehood may be invalidated. This sentence is the reason for what God wants: that is, He wants that, or He wants that to make the truth apparent and exalt it and invalidate falsehood and put it down, or the lam is related to something omitted: that is, He did that to establish the truth, and it was said: It is related to cut off, and this sentence does not repeat what came before it because the first is to clarify the difference between the two wills, and this is to clarify the wisdom calling for that, and the reason requiring it, and the interest resulting from it. And establishing the truth is to make it apparent, and invalidating falsehood is to annihilate it. Rather, We cast the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it, and thereupon it departs. And the object of even if the criminals dislike it is omitted: that is, even if they disliked that the truth be established and falsehood be invalidated, and the criminals are the polytheists from Quraysh, or all groups of the infidels. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us while we were in Medina, and he was informed that the caravan of Abu Sufyan had arrived, so he said: What do you think about it? Perhaps God will take it as booty and keep us safe. So we went out, and after we had traveled for a day or two, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered us to return, so we did, and we were three hundred and thirteen. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us of our number, and he was pleased with that and praised God and said: The number of the companions of Talut. He said: What do you think about fighting the people, for they have been informed of your departure? We said: O Messenger of God, no, by God, we do not have the strength to fight the people, we only went out for the caravan. Then he said: What do you think about fighting the people? We said the same, so Al-Miqdad said: Do not say as the people of Moses said to Moses: ‘Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.’ So God revealed: ‘As your Lord brought you out’ until His saying: “And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours.” So when God promised us one of the two parties, either the people or the caravan, our souls were at peace. Then we gathered with the people and lined up. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, I ask You to fulfill Your promise. Ibn Rawahah said: O Messenger of God, I want to advise you, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is better than To point it out to him, God is greater and more majestic than for you to ask Him for His promise. He said: O Ibn Rawahah, I will call upon God for His promise, for God does not break His promise. So he took a handful of dirt and threw it at the faces of the people, and they fled. Then God revealed: It was not you who threw when you threw, but God threw. So we were killed and taken prisoner. Umar said: O Messenger of God, I do not think that you should have any prisoners, for we are only supplicants who are reconciled. We said: O group of Ansar, Umar is only motivated to do what he said out of envy of us. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slept and then woke up and said: Call Umar for me. So he called for him and said: God has revealed to me: It is not for a Prophet to have captives verse. And in its chain of transmission is Ibn Lahi’ah, and there is a well-known criticism of him. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Alqamah ibn Waqqas Al-Laythi on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Badr, and when he was at Rawaha, he addressed the people and said: What do you think?” Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, we have been informed that they are such and such. Then he addressed the people and said: What do you think? Umar said the same as Abu Bakr. Then he addressed the people and said: What do you think? Sa`d ibn Mu`adh said: O Messenger of God, it is us you want. By the One who honored you and sent down the Book to you, I have never crossed it and I have no knowledge of it. If you travel until you reach Bark al-Ghamad in Dhi Yemen We will walk with you and not be like those who said to Moses, “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.” Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are following you. Perhaps you have gone out for a reason and God has revealed to you something else. So look at what God has revealed to you and go for it. Separate the ropes of whomever you wish, cut the ropes of whomever you wish, return to whomever you wish, make peace with whomever you wish, and take from our wealth whatever you wish. So the Qur’an was revealed according to the words of Sa’d, As your Lord brought you out from your home with the truth until His saying, And cut off the root of the disbelievers. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only wanted the spoils with Abu Sufyan, but God brought him out to fight. Ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement, As your Lord brought you out from your home with the truth, that he said: This is how they argue with you about going out to fight. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding His statement, As your Lord brought you out from your home with the truth, that he said: The Prophet’s going out The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went to Badr, And indeed, a party of the believers are averse, he said: to seeking out the polytheists. They argue with you concerning the truth after it has become clear, that you do nothing except what God has commanded you to do. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding his statement, And you wish that the one without power should be yours, he said: It is the caravan of Abu Sufyan. The companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wished that the caravan was theirs and that the fighting had been diverted from them. Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada, And cuts off the root of the disbelievers, meaning their strength. The Battle of Badr has been fully covered in the books of hadith, biographies, and history, so we will not prolong its mention.
8:9: His saying: 9- When you seek help The circumstance is related to something omitted: that is, remember the time of your seeking help. It was said: instead of And when God promised you, the object of its agent. It was said: related to his saying: So that the truth may be established. Seeking help: asking for aid. It is said: So-and-so sought help from me, so I helped him. The noun is aid. The meaning is: when the Muslims knew that it was necessary to fight the powerful group, which was the mobilization, as God had commanded them to do and wanted from them, and they saw the large number of the mobilization and the small number of them, they sought help from God, the Exalted. It was established in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, "that the number of polytheists on the day of Badr was one thousand, and the number of Muslims was three hundred and seventeen men, and that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw that, he faced the qiblah, then stretched out his hands and began to call out to his Lord: O God, fulfill for me what You promised me. O God, give me what You promised me. O God, if this group of the people of Islam perishes, You will not be worshipped on earth." The Hadith. So He answered you is in apposition to You seek help and is included with it in the masculine, and although it is future tense, it has the meaning of the past, and that is why He answered it. His saying: I will reinforce you with a thousand angels means that I will reinforce you, so the preposition was deleted and the verb was connected to the object and it was read with a kasra on the hamza to mean the saying, or that in I responded the meaning of the saying. His saying: In succession Nafi' read with a fatha on the dal as a passive participle, and the rest read with a kasra on it as an active participle and its accusative as a state, and the meaning according to the first reading is that he made some of them follow each other, and according to the second reading is that they made some of them follow each other, and it was said that in succession according to both readings is an attribute of alif, and it was said that according to the first reading it is a state of the pronoun mansur in your support: meaning your support in the state of your being followed by a thousand angels, and it was said that radfa and ardhafa have the same meaning, and Abu Ubaidah denied it and said: because of the saying of the Most High: The one who follows her and did not say the one who follows her. Sibawayh said: There is a third reading of the verse, which is mardafin with a damma on the ra and a kasra on the dal with a shaddah. There is a fourth reading with a fatha on the ra and a shaddah on the dal. Ja’far ibn Muhammad and Asim al-Jahdari read it with alifs as the plural of alif, which is in agreement with what was mentioned previously in Al Imran.
8:10: The pronoun in 10- And what God has made refers to the support indicated by His saying: I will support you, except as good tidings meaning except as good report for you of His victory, and it is an empty exception: meaning He did not make your support for anything except as good tidings for you of victory and that your hearts may be reassured thereby meaning with the support, and in this there is an indication that the angels did not fight, rather God supported the Muslims with them to give them good tidings and to reassure and strengthen their hearts, and the lam in to be reassured is related to an omitted verb that is understood to be delayed: meaning and that your hearts may be reassured, He did that not for anything else and victory is only from God not from anyone else, the angels have no effect in that, for He is the true supporter, and they are only a cause of the causes of victory that God caused for you and provided you with Indeed, God is Exalted in Might cannot be overcome Wise in all His actions. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him who said: Gabriel descended with a thousand angels on the right flank of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Abu Bakr was in it, and Michael descended with a thousand angels on the left flank of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and I was on the left flank. Sunayd, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was not supported by more than this thousand that God mentioned in al-Anfal, and the mention of the three thousand and the five thousand was only good report. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: in succession he said: in succession. Ibn Jarir narrated on his statement: in succession he said: the reinforcements. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority regarding the verse he said: behind every king there is a king. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Sha’bi who said: There were a thousand in succession and three thousand descending, so they were four thousand, and they were the reinforcements of the Muslims in their borders. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: in succession he said: in succession. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: in succession. God supported them with a thousand, then with three, then completed them with five thousand. And God made it not but good tidings for you, and that your hearts might be reassured thereby. He said: He meant the descent of the angels. He said: It was mentioned to us that Umar said: As for the day of Badr, we do not doubt that the angels were with us, but as for after that, God knows best. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd in succession he said: one after the other.
8:11: His statement: 11- When He covers you The circumstance is in the accusative case with an implied verb like the one before it, or a second substitute for when He promises you, or in the accusative case with the victory mentioned before it, and say other things that have no basis, and covers you is the reading of Nafi' and the people of Medina that the subject is God, the Most High, and this reading is consistent with what precedes it: I mean his statement: And victory is only from God and with what comes after it, I mean and He sends down upon you so the speech is similar and consistent. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read covers you with the subject being sleep, and the rest read covers you with a fatha on the ghain and a shaddah on the shin, and it is like the reading of Nafi' and the people of Medina in attributing the action to God, and placing sleep in the accusative case. Al-Makki said: The choice is to add the ya’ and to give emphasis, and to put an-Na’as in the accusative case because after it is Amanah minhu and the ha’ in minhu li-llah, so He is the One who overcomes them with drowsiness, and because the majority is on this, and according to the first and third readings, the accusative case of Amana is as a direct object, and there is no need for interpretation or effort in that, because the subject of the verb that is justified and the reason is one, unlike its accusative case as a reason, considering the second reading, which requires effort. As for making Amana a source, there is no problem, it is said: Amana amana, ammanan, and amana. This verse includes mention of a blessing that God bestowed upon them, which is that despite their fear of meeting the enemy and their awe of his side, God calmed their hearts and made them secure until they slept securely, not afraid, and this sleep was on the night that the fighting was to take place the next day. It was said: There are two aspects to God’s gratitude to them for sleeping that night: One: That He strengthened them by resting for the battle the next day, the second: That He reassured them by removing fear from their hearts, and it was said: Sleep overcame them when the two lines met, and something similar to this was mentioned on the day of Uhud in Surat Al Imran. His statement: And He sends down upon you from the sky water to purify you thereby This rain was after drowsiness, and it was said: before drowsiness. Al-Zajjaj narrated that the infidels on the day of Badr preceded the believers to the water of Badr, so they camped there and the believers were left with no water, so God sent down rain on the night of Badr. What is in the biography of Ibn Ishaq and others is that the believers were the ones who preceded the water of Badr and that it prevented the Quraysh from being the first to the water with a heavy rain and the Muslims did not get anything from it except what made it difficult for them to trample the valley and helped them to travel. The meaning of to purify you with it is to remove the events from you and remove from you the evil of Satan meaning his whispering to you of what had preceded in their hearts of thoughts that were from him of fear and failure until their condition was the condition of someone being driven to death and to bind your hearts making them patient, strong and steadfast in the places of war. The pronoun in with it in His statement: and to make firm with it the feet refers to the water that God sent down: meaning that with this water that He sent down upon you when you needed it, your feet are firm in the places of battle. It was said: the pronoun refers to the binding indicated by the action.
8:12: His saying: 12- When your Lord revealed to the angels, 'I am with you.' The circumstance is in the accusative case with an omitted verb specific to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because no one else knows about it: that is, remember, O Muhammad, the time of your Lord's revelation to the angels. It was said: It is a substitute for when He promised you, as mentioned above, but he rejects that because Muslims do not know about this, so it is not among the blessings that God has enumerated for them. It was said: The factor in it is to establish, so the meaning is: to establish the feet at the time of revelation, and this restriction has no meaning. It was said: The factor in it is to bind, and there is no reason to restrict the binding to the hearts at the time of revelation. The meaning of the verse is: I am with you in victory and assistance. So, according to the opening reading of the hamza, it is the object of inspire, and according to the breaking reading, it is by estimating the saying. The meaning of So make firm those who believe is to give them good tidings of victory or to make them firm in fighting by being present with them and increasing their numbers. This is a command from Him, the Most High, to the angels to whom He revealed that He is with them. The fa is to arrange what comes after it according to what comes before it. His statement, I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve has already been explained in the meaning of casting terror in Al Imran. It has been said that this sentence is an explanation of His statement, I am with you. His statement, Then strike above the necks It has been said that what is meant is the necks themselves and above is redundant. This was said by Al Akhfash and others. Muhammad bin Yazid said: This is a mistake, because above conveys a meaning and it is not permissible to make it redundant, but the meaning is that they were permitted to strike the faces and what is close to them. It has been said that what is meant above the necks is the heads. It has been said that what is meant by above the necks is their upper parts because they are the joints in which striking is quicker to cut off. It has been said that this is a command to the angels and it has been said to the believers. According to the first, it has been said that it is an explanation of His statement, Then make firm those who believe and His statement, And strike from them every fingertip. Al-Zajjaj said: The singular of banan is banana, and here it refers to the fingers and other limbs. Banan is derived from their saying Ibn al-rajul bi-makan a man resides in a place, because he does with it what is required for residence and life. It was said that what is meant by banan here is the tips of the fingers of the hands and feet, and it is an expression for steadfastness in war. So if the banan is struck, the one struck is prevented from fighting, unlike the rest of the limbs. Antara said: In battle, he used to protect her honor and strike every finger in distress. Antara also said: Death is at my disposal if I step on the Indian flag with my fingers Ibn Faris said: The fingers are the fingers, and it is also said: the extremities.
8:13: And the reference in his saying: 13- That is to what happened to them of killing and the terror that entered their hearts, and it is the subject, and because they opposed God and His Messenger is its predicate: meaning that is because of their opposition, and the origin of opposition is that each of the two opponents becomes on an opposition, and the investigation of that has been presented. And whoever opposes God and His Messenger, then indeed, God is severe in penalty for him, He punishes him because of what occurred from him of opposition.
8:14: His statement: 14- That is you, so taste it, and indeed for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire. The reference here is to the previous punishment or address to the disbelievers, just as the address in His statement: That is you is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to anyone who is suitable for addressing. Al-Zajjaj said: That is you is raised by implying the command or the story: meaning the command or the story is that is you, so taste it. He said: It is permissible to imply and know. He said in Al-Kashaf: It is permissible for it to be accusative on: Upon you is that, so taste it, like you say: Zaid, hit him. Abu Hayyan said: It is not permissible to estimate upon you because it is a verb, and verb names are not implied, and likening it to Zaid, so hit him is incorrect because it was not estimated upon you, rather it is from the category of preoccupation, and the phrase And indeed for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire is conjoined to what preceded it, so the reference in this is to the immediate punishment that they were afflicted with, and And indeed for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire is a reference to the deferred punishment. Abu Ya'la and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala'il on the authority of Ali who said: There was no knight among us on the day of Badr except Al-Miqdad, and I saw us and there was none among us except those who were asleep except the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) praying under a tree until morning. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab regarding the verse, he said: It has reached us that this verse was revealed regarding the believers on the day of Badr when God covered them with drowsiness as a security from Him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: A security from Him he said: Security from God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: A security from Him he said: Mercy from Him, security from the enemy. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Drowsiness is in the head, and sleep is in the heart. Abd bin Hamid also narrated on his authority that he said: Drowsiness was a security from God, and drowsiness was of two types: drowsiness on the day of Badr and drowsiness on the day of Uhud. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab regarding his statement: And He sends down upon you from the sky water to purify you thereby, he said: Tash was on the day of Badr. These narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: “The rain that God sent down upon them before drowsiness, so the rain extinguished the dust, and the earth was covered with it, and their souls were content with it, and their feet were firm with it.” Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: “God sent the sky and the valley was trampled, and what struck the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions was covered with what did not prevent them from moving, and what struck the Quraysh was such that they were unable to travel with it.” Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The polytheists defeated the Muslims at the beginning of their affair at the water, so the Muslims woke up and prayed while they were ritually impure and in a state of ritual impurity, so Satan cast sadness into their hearts and said: ‘Do you claim that there is a prophet among you and that you are the friends of God, yet you pray while you are ritually impure and in a state of ritual impurity?’” Then God sent down water from the sky, and the valley flowed with water upon them. The Muslims drank and purified themselves, and their feet became firm, and the whisper of Satan went away. We have already mentioned that it is well-known in the reliable biographies that the polytheists did not overpower the believers in the water, but rather the believers were the ones who overpowered them from the beginning. This is what was narrated from Ibn Abbas in his chain of transmission Al-Awfi, and it is very weak. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: The filth of Satan he said: His whisper. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: And to bind your hearts he said: with sight. And to make firm thereby your feet he said: The valley floor was flat, but when it rained, the sand became hard. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And to make firm thereby your feet he said: until they become firm on the sand, which is like the ground. Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was praying that night and saying: ‘O God, if this group is destroyed, You will not be worshipped.’ Heavy rain fell on them that night, and that is what He meant by ‘and makes the feet firm thereby.’” Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The angels did not fight except on the day of Badr. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah bin Sahl bin Hanif who said: My father said to me: O my son, you saw us on the day of Badr and when we were about to break our fast, he would point with his sword at the head of the polytheist and his head would fall off his body before the sword reached it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas who said: On the day of Badr, the people would recognize those who were killed by the angels from those they had killed by striking them on the necks and fingers like the mark of fire that had burned them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding His statement: strike above the necks, meaning the heads. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Atiyyah, strike above the necks, meaning strike the necks. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, Strike above the necks, meaning: Strike the necks. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And strike off every fingertip of theirs. He said: By fingertip he means the extremities. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Atiyah: And strike off every fingertip of theirs. He said: Every joint.
8:15: Crawling: approaching little by little, and its origin is rushing towards the buttocks, then every walker in war towards another was called a crawler. Crawling: drawing near and getting close, you say: he crawled towards the enemy crawling, and the people crowded together: meaning some of them walked towards each other. The accusative of crawling is either as a source for a deleted verb: meaning you crawl crawling, or as a state of the believers: meaning the state of you crawling towards the disbelievers, or a state of those who disbelieved: meaning the state of the disbelievers crawling towards you, or a state of the two groups, meaning crawling. So do not turn your backs to them. God forbade the believers from fleeing from the disbelievers if they meet them and some of them have crawled towards each other to fight, so the apparent meaning of this verse is general for all believers at all times, and in all states except the state of deviation and bias. It was narrated on the authority of Umar, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Abu Saeed, Abu Nadra, Ikrimah, Nafi’, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Yazid, Ibn Abi Habib and Al-Dahhak that the prohibition of fleeing from the battle in this verse is specific to the day of Badr, and that the people of Badr were not allowed to withdraw, and if they had withdrawn, they would have withdrawn to the polytheists, since there were no Muslims on the earth at that time other than them, and they had no group except the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for after that, some of them were a group for others, and Abu Hanifa said the same.
8:16: They said: This is supported by his statement: 16- And whoever turns his back to them that day, as it is a reference to the day of Badr. It was said: This verse was abrogated by the verse of weakness. The majority of scholars held that this verse is a general ruling, not a specific one, and that fleeing from the battlefield is forbidden. This is supported by the fact that this verse was revealed after the war had ended on the day of Badr. The response to the statement of the first scholars is that the reference in that day to the day of Badr is that it is a reference to the day of the battlefield, as the context indicates, and there is no contradiction between this verse and the verse of weakness. Rather, this verse is restricted by it, so fleeing from the battlefield is forbidden under the condition that God has made clear in the verse of weakness. There is no basis for what they mentioned that there were no Muslims on the earth on the day of Badr other than those who were present, as there were many people in Medina at that time whom the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not order to go out, because he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and those who went out with him did not think that there would be fighting at the beginning. This is supported by the authentic hadiths that explicitly state that fleeing from battle is among the major sins, as in the hadith: Avoid the seven deadly sins, and in it: And fleeing in succession on the day of battle, and similar hadiths. This discussion is long and its paths are branched, and it is explained in its proper places. Ibn Atiyyah said: The backs are the plural of back, and the expression back in this verse is well-established in eloquence because of the ugliness and blame it contains for the one who flees.
