His statement: Except when turning away for the sake of fighting, turning away means moving away from the straight path, and what is meant by it here is turning from one side to another in battle in search of war tricks and deceiving the enemy, and like someone who makes one think that they are defeated so that the enemy follows him and attacks him and is able to overpower him, and similar tricks of war, because war is deception. His saying: or turning to a party meaning to a group of Muslims other than the group facing the enemy. The accusative of turning away and turning away is an exception from turning away meaning and whoever turns his back to them except a man from them turning away or turning away. It is permissible for both to be accusative as a state, and the letter of exception is superfluous and has no function. The phrase has incurred the wrath of God is a recompense for the condition. The meaning is: whoever flees and runs away from the battle has returned with the wrath of God except the one turning away and turning away. And his refuge is Hell meaning the place to which he seeks refuge is the Fire, so his decision has led him to something more severe than what he fled from and a greater punishment. Refuge is what a person seeks refuge in. And evil is the destination is what he has come to of the torment of the Fire. This verse includes this severe threat to whoever flees from the battle, and in that is an indication that it is one of the major sins that lead to destruction.
8:17: His statement: 17- So you did not kill them, but God killed them. The fa is the answer to an implied condition: that is, if you knew what God told you about His support for you with angels and instilling terror in their hearts, then you did not kill them, but God killed them with the means that He made easy for you to achieve victory. His statement: And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw. The commentators differed regarding this throwing in sayings: It was narrated from Malik that what was meant by it was what he did, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn, as he threw a handful of pebbles from the valley and it hit every one of them. It was said: What was meant by it was the throw that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threw at Ubayy ibn Khalaf with a spear in his neck, so he fled and died from it. It was said: What was meant by it was the arrow that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threw in the fortress of Khaybar, so it traveled through the air until it hit Ibn Abi al-Haqiq while he was on his bed. These sayings are weak, as the verse was revealed after the Battle of Badr. Also, what is well-known in the books of biography and hadith about the killing of Ibn Abi Al-Haqiq is that it happened in a way other than this one. What is correct, as Ibn Ishaq and others said, is that what is meant by the throwing mentioned in this verse is what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did on the day of Badr, when he took a handful of dirt and threw it in the faces of the polytheists, hitting each one of them and entering their eyes, nostrils and nose. Tha`lab said: The meaning is and you did not throw the fear and terror in their hearts when you threw the pebbles and they were defeated but God threw meaning He helped you and made you victorious. The Arabs say: God threw for you, meaning He helped you, made you victorious and did for you. Abu Ubaidah narrated something similar to this in his book Al-Majaz. Muhammad bin Yazid al-Mubarrad said: The meaning is and you did not throw with your strength when you threw but rather you threw with the strength of God. It was said that the meaning is: that throw of the handful of dirt that you threw was not really thrown by you, because if you had thrown it, its effect would not have reached anything other than what a human throw reaches, but it was God’s throw as it had that great effect. So he affirmed the throw for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because its form was found in him, and he denied it from him because its effect that humans cannot bear was the action of God Almighty, so it was as if God was the doer of the throw in reality, and as if it did not occur from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at all. This is in al-Kashshaf. His saying: And that He may test the believers with a good test from Him. The test here is the blessing, and the meaning is: And that He may bestow upon the believers a beautiful blessing. The lam is related to something omitted: that is, and to bestow upon them His beautiful blessings, He did that and not for anything else, or the waw is a conjunction for what comes after it based on an implied cause before it: that is, but God threw to destroy the disbelievers and to test the believers with a good test from Him. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing of their supplication, and He is Knowing of their conditions.
8:18: And the reference in His saying that is to the good trial, and it is in the nominative case as a predicate for a deleted subject: meaning the purpose 18- That, and indeed God weakens the plot of the disbelievers meaning that the purpose of Him, glory be to Him, in what happened from what the previous verses narrated was to test the believers and weaken the plot of the disbelievers, and it was said that what is referred to is killing and shooting. It was read with a shaddah on the ha' and a light ha' with the tanween. Al-Hasan read it with a light ha' with the addition. And the plot is the deceit, and its explanation was presented above. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, as did Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Nafi' that he asked Ibn Umar, saying: We are a people who do not stand firm when fighting our enemy, and we do not know who is in front of us or our army? He said to me: The group is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: God says: When you meet those who disbelieve in battle, do not turn your backs to them. He said: This verse was revealed about the people of Badr, not before or after it. Abd bin Hamid, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, An-Nahhas in his Naskh, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri regarding his statement: And whoever turns his back to them that day the verse, he said: It was specifically for the people of Badr. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, who said: Do not be deceived by this verse, for it was revealed on the day of Badr, and I am a group for every Muslim. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: It was revealed specifically about the people of Badr, it was not for them to flee from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and abandon him. The specificity of this verse to the people of Badr has been narrated by a group of the Tabi’in and those who came after them, and we have already mentioned that. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: Except one who turns aside for battle meaning digressing, meaning he wants to attack the polytheists, or withdraws to a company meaning or withdraws to his companions without being defeated, then he has incurred the wrath of God meaning they deserved the wrath of God, and his refuge is Hell, and an evil destination. This is the day of Badr in particular, it was difficult for the Muslims that day to cut off the roots of the disbelievers, and it was the first battle that the polytheists fought from the people of Mecca. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: The one who turns aside and is ahead of his companions is to see the enemy’s weakness and attack it. And the one who withdraws is the one who flees to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and likewise the one who flees today to his leader and companions. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ata’ Ibn Abi Rabah regarding his statement: And whoever turns his back to them that Day he said: This verse was abrogated by the verse in al-Anfal 8:Now God has lightened your burden the verse. Sa’id Ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd Ibn Hamid, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad and the wording is his, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and he authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, An-Nahhas, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “We were in a raid and the people were in a state of confusion. We said: How can we meet the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when we have fled from the battlefield and have been afflicted with anger? So we came to the Messenger of God before the dawn prayer, and he came out and said: Who are the people? We said: We are the ones who fled. He said: No, rather you are the ones who are stubborn. We kissed his hand and he said: I am your group and I am the group of the Muslims. Then he recited: “Except one who turns aside for the sake of fighting or withdraws to another group.” It has been narrated in the hadiths that forbid fleeing from battle and that it is a major sin. It has been narrated from a group of the Companions that it is a major sin, as narrated by Ibn Jarir from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Shaybah from Ibn Umar. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim from Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: And why did you kill them? He said to the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said: This one I killed and this one I killed. And you did not throw when you threw, he said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he threw pebbles at the infidels. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: And you did not throw when you threw, he said: He threw pebbles at them on the day of Badr. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Hakim bin Hizam who said: “When the day of Badr came, we heard a sound from the sky to the earth like the sound of a pebble falling into a basin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threw those pebbles and said: ‘May your faces be disfigured,’ so we fled. This is what God Almighty said: And you did not throw when you threw the verse. Abu Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir who said: I heard the sound of pebbles falling from the sky on the day of Badr as if they had fallen into a basin. When the people lined up, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took them and threw them in the faces of the polytheists and they fled. This is what he said: And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw. At-Tabarani, Abu Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And you did not throw when you threw, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: Give him a handful of pebbles. So he gave them to him and he threw them in the faces of the people. No one remained from the people but his eyes were filled with pebbles. So this verse was revealed: And you did not throw when you threw. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab who said: "On the day of Uhud, Ubayy bin Khalaf began to gallop his horse until he came close to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some Muslims intercepted Ubayy bin Khalaf to kill him, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: And he said: They delayed, so they delayed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took his spear in his hand and threw it at Abi bin Khalaf and broke one of his ribs, so Abi bin Khalaf returned to his companions, heavy, and they carried him when they turned back and began to say, “There is nothing wrong with him.” When they said that to him, Abi said: “By God, if it were among the people, I would have killed them. Didn’t he say, ‘I will kill you, God willing?’ So his companions went with him to revive him until he died on the way, and they buried him.” Ibn al-Musayyab said: And regarding that, God revealed, And you did not throw when you threw. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Saeed bin al-Musayyab and al-Zuhri, and its chain of transmission is sound back to them. Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak. Ibn Kathir said: This statement from these two imams is very strange, and perhaps they meant that the verse includes them in its generality, and this is what he said in what Abd al-Rahman bin Jubayr said, as will come. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr that on the day of Ibn Abi al-Haqiq, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) called for a bow and shot with it at the fortress. The arrow came and killed Ibn Abi al-Haqiq in his bed. Then God revealed: And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr regarding his statement: But God threw meaning that it would not have been your throw had it not been for what God made of your victory and what He cast into the hearts of your enemy until He defeated them. And that He may test the believers with a good test meaning that He may make the believers aware of His favor upon them in giving them victory over their enemy despite their large number and small number, so that they may recognize His right thereby and be grateful for His favor.
8:19: The opening: asking for victory. There is disagreement about who the verse is addressing. It was said: It is a speech to the infidels mocking them, and the meaning is: If you seek victory from God against Muhammad, then victory has come to you. When they left Mecca, they asked God to grant victory to the more deserving of victory of the two groups, so God mocked them and called the destruction that befell them victory. The meaning of the rest of the verse according to this statement is: And if you desist from what you were doing of disbelief and enmity towards the Messenger of God, it is meaning desisting “it is better for you. But if you return” to what you were doing of disbelief and enmity, We promise to give power to the believers over you and grant them victory as We gave power to them and granted them victory on the day of Badr. And your company meaning your group will not avail you at all, even if it is large meaning it will not avail you in any situation, even if it is large. Then He said: And that God is with the believers and whoever God is with him is the victorious and whoever God is against is the forsaken. It was read with a kasra on in and a fatha on it, so the kasra is for resumption, and the fatha is based on the estimation: And because God is with the believers, He did that. It was said: The verse is addressed to the believers, and the meaning is that if you seek help from God, then victory has come to you on the day of Badr, and if you stop doing what you did of taking spoils and ransoming prisoners before permission was given to you, then that is better for you, and if you return to doing such things, then we will rebuke you again as in His statement: Had it not been for a previous decree from God verse. It is not hidden that this statement rejects the meaning of and your company will not avail you at all and also rejects and that God is with the believers. And directing that cannot be done except by difficulty and arbitrariness. It was said: The address in if you seek help, then help has come to you is to the believers and what follows it is to the disbelievers, and it is not hidden what is in this of dismantling the system and returning the pronouns running in speech in one pattern to two different groups. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Mandah, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Abdullah ibn Tha'labah ibn Saghir that Abu Jahl said when the people met: "O God, we have severed our ties of kinship and brought upon us what we do not know, so destroy it tomorrow. That was his opening supplication, so the verse If you seek victory" was revealed. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Atiyyah, who said: Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: "O God, support the more guided of the two groups, the better of the two groups, and the best of the two groups." So the verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "If you seek victory, victory has already come to you." He said: The infidels of Quraysh said: "Our Lord, decide between us and Muhammad and his companions." So He decided between them on the day of Badr. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: If you seek victory, he said: If you seek a just end, then the judgment came to you on the day of Badr. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And if you desist, he said: From fighting Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And if you return, We will return, he said: If you seek victory a second time, We will grant victory to Muhammad. And that God is with the believers, he said: With Muhammad and his companions. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada: And if you return, We will return, he said: We will return to you with captivity and killing.
8:20: God the Almighty commanded the believers to obey Him and His Messenger and forbade them from turning away from His Messenger. The pronoun in 20- from him refers to the Messenger, because obeying the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is part of obeying God, and whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God. It is possible that this pronoun refers to God and His Messenger, as in His statement: And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should be pleased. It was said: The pronoun refers to the command indicated by obey, and the root of tawalawu is tatawallu, so one of the two ta's was dropped. This is the interpretation of the verse based on the apparent address to the believers, and this is what the majority said. It was said: It is addressed to the hypocrites, and the meaning is: O you who have believed with your tongues only. Ibn Atiyah said: Even if this is remotely possible, it is very weak, because God described the one He addressed in this verse as having faith, which is belief, and the hypocrites are not described as believing in anything. Even more remote than this is the one who said: The address is to the Children of Israel, for that is foreign to the verse, and the phrase and you hear is in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is: and you hear what is recited to you of arguments and proofs and you believe in them and you are not like the deaf and dumb.
8:21: 21- And do not be like those who said, ‘We hear.’ They are the polytheists, the hypocrites, the Jews, or all of these, for they hear with their ears without understanding or acting. They are like someone who did not hear at all because he did not benefit from what he heard.
8:22: Then the Almighty informed us of 22- Indeed, the worst of living creatures meaning everything that creeps on the earth in the sight of God meaning in His judgment are the deaf and dumb meaning those who neither hear nor speak, and they were described as such despite being among those who hear and speak because they do not benefit from hearing and speaking who do not reason what is beneficial to them so they do it, and what is harmful to them so they avoid it, so they are the worst of living creatures in the sight of God, because they distinguish between what benefits them and what harms them.
8:23: 23- And if God had known any good in them, meaning in these deaf and dumb people, He would have made them hear, the answer to everything they asked about. It was said, He would have made them hear, the speech of the dead who asked to be revived because they asked to revive Qusayy ibn Kilab and others to testify to the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse, because it had already been known to Him that they would not believe. The phrase and you see them turning away is in the accusative case as a state. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they do not hear, he said: They are angry. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib regarding his statement: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God, the verse. He said: This verse was revealed about so-and-so and his companions. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God, he said: They are a group of Quraysh from Banu Abd al-Dar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: The deaf and dumb who do not use reason, he said: They do not follow the truth. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: This verse was revealed about al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and his people, and perhaps he was referred to as so-and-so in what Ali may God be pleased with him said above. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr regarding his statement: And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear, meaning He would have carried out what they said with their tongues, but their hearts contradicted that. Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the verse, saying: They said, We are deaf to what Muhammad calls us to, we do not hear him, and we are mute, we do not respond to him in it with belief. They were all killed at Uhud, and they were the standard-bearers on the day of Uhud.
8:24: The command here to respond confirms what came before of the command to obey, and the pronoun is singular here where he said: If he calls you as he did in his saying: And do not turn away and we have already discussed the reason for that, and responding is obedience. Abu Ubaidah said: The meaning of respond is: answer, and if respond is transitive with the preposition lam, and respond by itself as in his saying: O our people, answer the caller of God, and respond by itself may be transitive as in the saying of the poet: Farewell, he called, O He who answers to the generosity, but no one answered him at that time. If He calls you to that which gives you life The lam is related to His saying: respond meaning respond to that which gives you life if He calls you. There is nothing wrong with it being related to innovation: meaning if He calls you to that which gives you life from the sciences of the Shari'ah, for knowledge is life just as ignorance is death, so life here is borrowed for knowledge. The majority of commentators said: The meaning is respond to obedience and what the Qur'an includes of commands and prohibitions, for in it is eternal life and everlasting blessing. It was said: What is meant by His saying: that which gives you life is jihad, for it is apparently the cause of life, because if the enemy does not attack, he attacks. This command to respond is used as evidence that every Muslim, if he hears a saying of God or a saying of His Messenger regarding a ruling of the Shari'ah, must hasten to act upon it, whatever it may be, and abandon any opinion or sayings of men that contradict it. In this noble verse is the greatest incentive to act upon the texts of the evidence and to abandon adherence to schools of thought, and not to pay attention to what contradicts what is in the Qur'an and Sunnah, whatever it may be. His saying: And know that God intervenes between a person and his heart. It was said that its meaning is: Hasten to respond before you are unable to do so due to the disappearance of the hearts with which you understand due to the death that God has decreed for you. It was also said that its meaning is: The Muslims feared on the day of Badr the great number of the enemy, so God informed them that He intervenes between a person and his heart by replacing their fear with security, and replacing their enemy with fear from security. It was also said that it is a metaphor for His nearness, glory be to Him, to the servant, like His saying: And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. Its meaning is: He is aware of the secrets of the hearts, and nothing of them is hidden from Him. Ibn Jarir chose that this is from the category of informing from God the Almighty that He has more control over the hearts of His servants than they do, and that He intervenes between them and them if He wills so that man does not perceive anything except by His will the Almighty, and it is not hidden from you that there is no objection to interpreting the verse with all of these meanings and that to Him you will be gathered is connected to that God intervenes between a person and his heart and that you will be gathered to Him and He will reward you for good with good, and for evil with evil. Al-Farra’ said: If you had started again and broken the hamza of that it would have been correct, and perhaps what he meant is that such a thing is permissible in Arabic.
8:25: His saying: 25- And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively. That is, fear a trial which will extend beyond the wrongdoer and strike the righteous and the wicked, and will not be limited to those among you who engage in wrongdoing. Grammarians differed about the inclusion of this emphatic nun in tasibun. Al-Farra' said: It is like your saying: Get down from the beast, do not let it throw you away. It is the answer to the command with the wording of a prohibition: that is, if you get down from it, do not let it throw you away. Similar to it is the saying of God Almighty: Enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you meaning, if you enter, do not let them crush you. The nun was included because of the meaning of recompense in it. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a prohibition after a command. The meaning is: The prohibition is for the oppressors: that is, do not come near oppression. Similar to it is what was narrated from Sibawayh: La araynak haana, for its meaning is: Do not be here, for whoever is here, I will see him. Al-Jurjani said: In la yasibna is a prohibition in the place of describing a trial. Ali, Zaid bin Abi Thabit, Ubayy and Ibn Mas’ud read la yasibna with the lam being the answer to an omitted oath, and the meaning is: Beware of a trial, and by God it will strike those who have wronged among you in particular. So the meaning of this reading is different from the meaning of the reading of the group, because it indicates that the trial will strike the wrongdoer in particular, unlike the reading of the group. And know that God is severe in penalty. And from the severity of His punishment is that He afflicts with torment those who did not directly engage in its causes. The verses of the Qur’an state that no one is afflicted except for his sin, and no one is punished except for his crime. So what is in this verse can be interpreted as referring to the punishments that are caused by the servants’ authority over one another. This verse can also be specific to general punishments, and God knows best. It can also be said that those who did not wrong caused the punishment through causes such as abandoning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. So the affliction that extends from the wrongdoer to others is specific to the one who abandons what is required of him when injustice appears. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, When He calls you to that which gives you life, he said: For the truth. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, he said: It is this Qur’an in which there is life, trust, salvation and protection in this world and the Hereafter. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr regarding his statement, When He calls you to that which gives you life, meaning for the war by which God has honored you after humiliation, strengthened you after weakness, and protected you from punishment after their subjugation of you. It has been proven in Sahih from the hadith of Abu Sa’id ibn al-Mu’alla who said: “I was praying in the mosque when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me but I did not answer him. Then I came to him and said: O Messenger of God, I was praying. He said: Did not God, the Most High, say: ‘Respond to God and to the Messenger when He calls you.’” The hadith contains evidence for what we have mentioned, that the verse includes every supplication from God or His Messenger. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And know that God intervenes between a person and his heart, he said: He intervenes between the believer and disbelief and disobeying God, and He intervenes between the disbeliever and faith and obeying God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas regarding the verse: His knowledge intervenes between a person and his heart. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: He intervenes between a person and his heart until he leaves him unaware. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan... In being close to Him. Ahmad, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Mutraf who said: I said to Az-Zubayr: O Abu Abdullah, you neglected the Caliph until he was killed, then you came seeking revenge for his blood. Al-Zubayr said: We read during the time of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman: And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively, and we did not think that we were its people until it happened to us where it happened. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Hasan who said: Al-Zubayr read: And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively, and he said: The affliction and the matter that is going to happen. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Al-Hasan regarding the verse: It was revealed about Ali, Uthman, Talhah and Al-Zubayr. Abd bin Hamid narrated from Al-Dahhak who said: It was revealed about the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) specifically. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Al-Suddi who said: It was revealed about the people of Badr specifically and it struck them on the Day of the Camel and they fought, and among those killed were Talhah and Al-Zubayr, and they were from the people of Badr. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Al-Suddi regarding the verse: It will strike the oppressor and the righteous in general. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Mujahid. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, saying: It is like He comes between a man and his heart until he leaves him without reason. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, saying: God commanded the believers not to tolerate evil among them, lest God punish them all. Many authentic hadiths have been reported that if this nation does not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, God will punish them all.
8:26: The address in His saying: 26- And remember when you were few to the immigrants: that is, remember the time when you were few, and weakened is a second predicate for the subject, and the land: is the land of Mecca, and snatching: taking quickly, and what is meant by the al-Nas 114:the polytheists of Quraysh, and it was said: the Persians and the Romans Then He sheltered you it is said: He sheltered him with the extension and the shortening meaning: He joined him, so the meaning is: God joined you to Medina or to the Ansar And supported you with His victory that is, He strengthened you with victory in the places of war, including the Day of Badr, or He strengthened you with the angels on the Day of Badr And provided you with good things which include spoils that you may be grateful that is, wanting you to be grateful for these blessings that He bestowed upon you.
8:27: And the origin of the word khūn as stated in Al-Kashaf is: deficiency, just as loyalty is completeness. Then it was used in the opposite of trust and loyalty, because if you betray a man in something, you have introduced deficiency into him. It was said that its meaning is: treachery and concealing something. And from this is the saying of the Most High: He knows the treachery of the eyes. God forbade them from betraying Him by leaving something that He made obligatory upon them, or betraying His Messenger by leaving something that He entrusted them with, or by leaving something that He prescribed for them, or betraying any of the trusts that they were entrusted with. They are called trusts because with them one is safe from withholding the right, taken from security. And the sentence 27- and you know is in the accusative case as a state: that is, and you know that this action is treachery, so you do treachery intentionally, or you are among the people of knowledge, not among the people of ignorance.
8:28: Then he said: And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial because they are the cause of falling into many sins, so from this perspective they have become a trial by which God tests His servants, even though from another perspective they are the adornment of worldly life as in the other verse: And that God has with Him a great reward so prefer His right over your wealth and your children so that you may obtain what He has of the aforementioned reward. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And remember when you were few, he said: This tribe of Arabs was the most humiliated of people, the most miserable in life, the hungriest in stomachs, the most naked in skins, and the most clearly astray. Whoever lived lived miserably, and whoever died among them was thrown into the Fire, being eaten but not eating. By God, we do not know of a tribe among the inhabitants of the earth at that time that was more miserable than them until God brought Islam, and He empowered them in the lands through it, and expanded their provision through it, and made them kings over the necks of the people. And through Islam, God gave what you have seen, so be grateful to God for His blessings, for your Lord is a benefactor who loves gratitude, and the grateful will have more from God Almighty. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: People would snatch you away, he said: In the pre-Islamic period in Mecca, then He gave you shelter to Islam. And Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Wahb regarding his statement: The people will snatch you away, he said: The people at that time were the Persians and the Romans. And Abu al-Shaykh, Abu Nu`aym, and al-Daylami narrated in Musnad al-Firdaws on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: “And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that the people would snatch you away,” it was said: O Messenger of God, and who are the people? He said: The people of Persia.” And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: Then he gave you shelter, he said: to the Ansar in Medina, and supported you with his victory, he said: on the day of Badr. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah that Abu Sufyan left Mecca and Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Abu Sufyan is in such and such a place in Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abu Sufyan is in such and such a place, so go out to him and conceal yourselves. A hypocrite wrote to Abu Sufyan, Muhammad wants you, so be careful. Then God revealed: O you who believe, do not betray God and the Messenger, the verse. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Qatada, who said: This verse, Do not betray God and the Messenger, was revealed about Abu Lubabah bin Abdul Mundhir. They asked him on the day of Qurayza, What is this matter? He pointed to his throat, meaning slaughter, and then it was revealed. Abu Lubabah said: My feet did not move until I knew that I had betrayed God and His Messenger. Sunayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri something similar, but longer. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) sent Abu Lubabah to Qurayzah, who was an ally of theirs. He gestured with his hand that it was slaughter, and so the verse was revealed. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding this verse that it was revealed regarding Abu Lubabah and was abrogated by the verse in Bara’ah: And others have confessed their sins. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Do not betray God he said: by abandoning His obligations and the Messenger by abandoning His Sunnah and committing disobedience to Him and betray your trusts he said: do not diminish them, and the trust is the deeds that God has entrusted to His servants. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah who said: This verse was revealed regarding the killing of Uthman, and perhaps he meant that among the things that fall under its generality is the killing of Uthman. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib regarding the verse, he said: It is the failure to carry out weapons in military campaigns, and perhaps he meant that this is among what falls under its generality. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: There is not one of you who is not afflicted with a trial, because God says: Your wealth and your children are but a trial. So whoever among you seeks refuge, let him seek refuge with God from the misleading trials. And these narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, he said: The trial of testing, He tested them, and he recited: And We test you with evil and with good as trial.
8:29: God Almighty made piety a condition for the aforementioned making, with His prior knowledge that they would be pious or not, in accordance with what people say to one another. Piety is avoiding disobeying His commands and falling into His prohibitions. Al-Furqan is what distinguishes between truth and falsehood. The meaning is that He gives them firmness of heart, insights, and good guidance by which they distinguish between them when they are confused. It has been said that Al-Furqan is the way out from doubts and salvation from everything they fear. From this is the saying of the poet: Why are you grieving so long? Farqan, after two cats have departed and disappeared. And from it the other said: How can I hope for immortality when death is seeking me, and I have no choice but to separate myself from the cup of death? Al-Farra’ said: What is meant by Al-Furqan is conquest and victory. Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Furqan is the distinction between truth and falsehood, and Ibn Zayd said something similar. Al-Suddi said: Al-Furqan is salvation. The interpretation of Al-Furqan as a way out and salvation is supported by the Almighty’s saying: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. This is what Mujahid and Malik ibn Anas said. 29- And He will remove from you your misdeeds meaning He will conceal them so that they are not apparent. And He will forgive you what you have committed of sins. It has been said that what is meant by misdeeds are minor sins, and by sins that are forgiven are major sins. It has also been said that the meaning is that He will forgive them what has passed of sins and what will come after. And God is the possessor of great bounty He is the One who bestows favors upon His servants by removing misdeeds and forgiving sins. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He will make for you a criterion, he said: It is the way out. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority: It is salvation. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is Al-Nadr.
8:30: His statement: 30- And when those who disbelieved plotted against you The circumstance is the object of an omitted verb: that is, remember, O Muhammad, the time when the disbelievers plotted against you, or it is conjoined with what came before from His statement, “And remember that God reminded His Messenger of this great blessing that He bestowed upon him, which is his salvation from the plot and treachery of the disbelievers, as will be explained. “To make you steadfast” means to make you steadfast with wounds, as Tha’lab, Abu Hatim, and others said. And from it is the saying of the poet: I said, Woe to you, what is in your newspaper? They said, The Caliph has become ill and in pain. It was said: The meaning is to detain you. It is said: Ithbathu: if he detained him. It was said: To bind you. From this: So tighten the bonds. Al-Sha’bi read: They spend the night from bayat. It was read lithbatuwak with emphasis. Or they expel you is conjoined to what preceded it: meaning they expel you from Mecca, which is your country and the country of your family. The phrase and they plot and God plots is a new sentence. The plot is the planning of a matter in secret. The meaning is that they hide what they are preparing for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of plots, so God will reward them for that and turn their plot back on them. He called what happens from Him a plot as a resemblance as in similar verses. And God is the best of plotters, meaning those who repay the plotting of the plotters with the same action, so He punishes them for their plotting without them realizing it. This will be more harmful to them and a greater affliction than their plotting.
8:31: His statement: 31- And when Our verses are recited to them, meaning that which you bring to them and recite to them, they say, out of stubbornness, rebellion, and distance from the truth, We have heard, what you recite to us, If we wished, we could say the like of this, which you recite to us. It was said that they said this out of the belief that they were able to do so, but when they tried to say the like of it, they were unable to do so. Then He said, out of stubbornness and rebellion: This is nothing but legends of the ancients, meaning what the copyists write down of the stories of the ancients. Its explanation has been presented in full.
8:32: 32- And when they said meaning, remember when they said, O God, if this is the truth from You with the accusative of truth as the predicate of was, and the pronoun is for separation, and the nominative is permissible. Al-Zajjaj said: I do not know of anyone who read it with it, and there is no difference between the two grammars in permitting it. But the reading is a Sunnah, and the meaning is if the Qur'an that Muhammad brought to us is the truth, then rain upon us they said: This statement is an exaggeration in denial and rejection. Abu Ubaidah said: It is said, rain in punishment and rain in mercy. And he said in Al-Kashshaf: Rain has been used frequently in the meaning of punishment. Or bring us a painful punishment they asked to be punished by stoning from the sky or other types of severe punishment.
8:33: So God answered them by saying: 33- And God would not punish them while you O Muhammad are among them, for as long as you are among them they are in a reprieve from the punishment which is extermination. And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. It was narrated that they used to say during the circumambulation, Your forgiveness: meaning, God would not punish them while they were seeking forgiveness. It was said that the meaning is: If they were among those who believe in God and seek His forgiveness, He would not have punished them. It was said that the seeking of forgiveness refers to the Muslims who are among them: meaning, God would not punish them while among them are those who seek forgiveness from the Muslims. So when they left among them, He punished them on the Day of Badr and after it. It was said that the meaning is: God would not punish them while in their loins there is someone who seeks forgiveness from God. Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in al-Dala’il and al-Khatib narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, he said: Quraysh consulted one night in Mecca. Some of them said: When morning comes, tie him up, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them said: Rather, kill him. Some of them said: Rather, take him out. God informed His Prophet of that, so Ali spent the night on the Prophet’s bed, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he reached the cave. When morning came, they rushed to him. When they saw Ali, God thwarted their plot, so they said: Where is your companion? He said: I do not know. So they followed his tracks, but when they reached the mountain, they were confused. They climbed the mountain and passed by the cave and saw a spider’s web over its door. They said: If he had entered here, the spider’s web would not have been over its door. He stayed in it for three nights. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu'aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who mentioned the story in a longer manner than this one. In it, the Najdi sheikh mentioned: that is, Satan and his advice to them when they met in Dar Al-Nadwa to consult about the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that Abu Jahl suggested that they take a young man from each tribe of Quraysh and give each one of them a sword and then strike him with one blow, so that when they killed him his blood would be distributed among the tribes. The Najdi sheikh said: This, by God, is the opinion, so they dispersed on that basis. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, who said: When they plotted against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to imprison him, kill him or expel him, his uncle Abu Talib said to him: Do you know what they plotted against you? He said: They want to imprison me, kill me or expel me. He said: Who told you this? He said: My Lord. He said: Yes, my Lord, your Lord, so treat him well. He said: I will treat him well. Rather, he recommends me. Ibn Jarir narrated it from another chain of transmission on his authority. This is not correct, as Abu Talib died years before the time of the Hijrah. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, he said: To restrain you, meaning to tie you up. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Saeed ibn Jubayr who said: “On the day of Badr, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, Tu’aymah ibn ‘Adi, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Al-Miqdad had taken al-Nadr prisoner, so when he ordered him to be killed, al-Miqdad said: O Messenger of God, my prisoner. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He used to say what he said about the Book of God. He said: And this verse was revealed about him: “And when Our verses are recited to them,” and this is a mursal. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi that it was revealed about al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik that he said: Abu Jahl bin Hisham said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then the verse was revealed: And God would not punish them, the verse. Abd bin Humayd narrated on the authority of Qatadah that it was revealed about Abu Jahl. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding the verse that it was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith. Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Abu Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ata’ something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The polytheists used to circumambulate the House and say: Here I am, O God, here I am. You have no partner except a partner who is Yours. You own him and what he owns. And they would say: Your forgiveness, Your forgiveness. Then God revealed: And God would not punish them, the verse. Ibn Abbas said, “There were two things that were a security for them: the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and seeking forgiveness. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away, and seeking forgiveness remained.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated, and declared it weak, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “God sent down two things a security for my nation: ‘And God would not punish them,’ and when I passed away, I left seeking forgiveness among them.” And he narrated, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: There were two types of security among you, one of which has passed and the other remains. He said: And God would not punish them the verse. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Hakim and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari. The hadiths on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about seeking forgiveness in general are very numerous and are well-known in the books of hadith.
8:34: His statement: 34- "And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them?" Because God, the Most High, explained that what prevented them from being punished were the two aforementioned matters: the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them, and the occurrence of seeking forgiveness. He then mentioned that these infidels, I mean the infidels of Mecca, deserved God's punishment for the evil deeds they committed. The meaning is: What is there for them that prevents them from being punished? Al-Akhfash said: "An" is redundant. Al-Nahhas said: If it were as he said, then "Ya'thbuhum would have been raised, and the phrase and they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque" is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, what prevents them from being punished? The fact is that they prevent people from the Sacred Mosque, just as they did in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah when they prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from the House. The phrase and they were not its guardians is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of they prevent, and this is like a response to what they used to say that they were the guardians of the House, and that its matter was delegated to them. Then he said, explaining who has that right: His guardians are only the righteous, meaning his guardians are only those who are among those who are righteous against polytheism and sins. But most of them do not know, that, and the ruling that the majority are ignorant indicates that the minority know but they are stubborn.
8:35: His saying: 35- And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. Whistling: the whistle from muka yamku muka, and from it is the saying of Antarah: And the lover of a prostitute left a wounded man, his prey being chewed like the cheek of a learned man That is, it makes a sound, and from it the animal made a sound: if it blew with wind. It was said that the meowing is the whistle to the tune of a white bird in the Hijaz called the meowing. The poet said: If the hawk chirps outside a tree, woe to the people of sheep and donkeys. And applause: clapping. It is said: Sada yasdi tasadia: if he clapped, and from this is the saying of Omar bin Al-Atnabah: They all made a cacophony of noise at home. That is, by clapping. It was said that clapping means hitting with the hands, and shouting means screaming. It was said that clapping means putting their fingers in their mouths, and whistling means whistling. It was said that shouting means turning them away from the House. It was said that the origin of this is taṣaddadah, so one of the two dāls was replaced with a ya’. The meaning of the verse is that the polytheists used to whistle and clap at the House, which is a place for prayer and worship. They put that in place of prayer, intending to distract the praying Muslims from prayer. It was read with the accusative of their prayer as the predicate of kāna, and what follows it is its subject. His statement, Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. This is a shift to addressing the disbelievers, threatening them and exaggerating in striking terror into their hearts. What is meant by it is the punishment of this world, like the Day of Badr, and the punishment of the Hereafter.
8:36: His statement: 36- “Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God.” After God, the Almighty, finished explaining the conditions of these disbelievers in physical acts of obedience, He followed it with explaining their conditions in financial acts of obedience. The meaning is that the purpose of these disbelievers in spending their wealth is to avert people from the path of truth by fighting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and gathering armies for that purpose, and spending their wealth on them. This is as happened with the disbelievers of Quraysh on the Day of Badr, the Day of Uhud, and the Day of the Confederates. The leaders spent their wealth on the army. Then God, the Almighty, informed us of the unseen in a miraculous manner, saying: So they will spend it, meaning this spending will occur from them. Then it will be, as God promised in His statement: God has decreed, ‘I and My messengers will surely prevail.’ The meaning of then in both places is either a lapse in time due to the extension between the spending mentioned and the emergence of the Islamic state, or a lapse in rank due to the expenditure of money and the failure to achieve the intended purpose of the separation. Then He said: And those who disbelieved will be gathered to Hellfire, meaning they continued in disbelief, because among these previously mentioned disbelievers there were those who converted to Islam and whose conversion was good: meaning they will be driven to it and not to anything else.
8:37: Then He explained the reason for which He did what He did to them, saying: 37- “That God may distinguish the wicked” meaning the wicked group of disbelievers from the good group, which are the believers, and place the wicked on top of each other meaning that He places the wicked group of disbelievers on top of each other, and heap them all together is an expression of gathering and joining: meaning that He gathers some of them on top of each other, and puts some of them together until they accumulate due to their excessive crowding. It is said: He piled something up means he gathered it and threw some of it on top of each other. The reference in His saying: Those to the wicked group are the losers meaning the complete losers. It was said: the wicked and the good are an attribute of the money, and the meaning is that He distinguishes the wicked money that the polytheists spent from the good money that the Muslims spent, so He gathers that wicked money together and throws it into Hell and torments them with it, as in the saying of the Most High: and their foreheads, their flanks, and their backs will be branded with it. He said in Al-Kashaf: The lam in this case is related to his saying: Then there will be regret upon them, and in the first case they will be gathered, and those is a reference to those who disbelieved. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. Then He made an exception for the polytheists, saying, And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them? Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, regarding His statement, And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them? He said: Their punishment was the conquest of Mecca. Ibn Ishaq and Abu Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them? while they deny the signs of God and belie His Messengers. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding His statement, And they hinder [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram, meaning whoever believes in God and worships Him, you and those who follow you. “And they are not his allies. His allies are only the righteous,” meaning you and those who believe in you. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, His allies are only the righteous, he said: Whoever they are, wherever they are. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr who said: The Quraysh used to oppose the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) during the circumambulation, mocking him, whistling, and clapping. So this verse was revealed: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Dhiya’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Quraysh used to circumambulate the Kaaba naked, whistling and clapping. So God revealed: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. He said: “Whistling is whistling; they likened it to the whistle of birds. Clapping is clapping. And God revealed about them: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God?” (Surah al-Anfal 11:10) Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Faryabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated something similar on his authority. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: Whistling is whistling, and clapping is clapping. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: Blagging means putting their fingers in their mouths, and saddiya means whistling. They mix all of these things up with the prayers of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi that he said: Blagging is a whistle similar to a white bird called al-Makkah that is found in the Hijaz, and saddiya means clapping. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr regarding the statement of God interpretation of the meaning: except for blinking, that he said: They would interlock their fingers and whistle on them. And clapping, that is: The people turned them away. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: The polytheists would circumambulate the House facing the left, and this is the meaning of the statement: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping, so blinking is like blowing a trumpet, and clapping is their circumambulation facing the left. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding his statement: Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve, that he said: He means the people of Badr, whom God punished with killing and captivity. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il, all narrated from his chain of transmission: He said: Al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, and al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr narrated to me: When the Quraysh were defeated on the day of Badr and returned to Mecca, and Abu Sufyan brought his camel back, Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi’ah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Sufyan ibn Umayyah walked with some Quraysh men whose fathers and sons had been killed. They spoke to Abu Sufyan and those of Quraysh who had business with that caravan and said: O people of Quraysh, Muhammad has left you and killed your best, so help us with this money in his war, for perhaps we can take revenge on him. So they did, and it was about them, as Ibn Abbas mentioned, that God revealed: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God until And those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: This verse was revealed about Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Mujahid. These people and others narrated something similar from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah regarding the verse: It was revealed about Abu Sufyan who spent forty ounces of gold on the polytheists of Quraysh on the day of Uhud. At that time, an ounce was equivalent to forty-two mithqals of gold. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Shimr ibn Atiyyah regarding the verse: until the wicked is distinguished from the good, that he said: On the Day of Resurrection, the righteous life of this world will be distinguished, then the entire world will be taken and thrown into Hell. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse: and heaps it all up, that he said: He will gather it all together.
8:38: God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say this meaning to the disbelievers, whether he said it with this phrase or another. Ibn Atiyyah said: If it were as Al-Kisa’i said, that it is in the copy of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, Say to those who disbelieve, if you desist meaning with the double ta’ above, then the message would not have been conveyed except with those exact words. He said in Al-Kashaf: That is, say this statement for their sake, which is 38- if they desist. If it had the meaning of addressing them, it would have been said, If you desist, you will be forgiven, which is the reading of Ibn Mas’ud. Similar to it is And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it,’ they addressed others with it for them so that they would hear it, meaning if they desist from their enmity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and fighting him by entering Islam, what has previously occurred will be forgiven for them for them of enmity. End quote. It was said that its meaning is: if they desist from disbelief. Ibn Atiyyah said: The reason for this is the answer to the condition with He will forgive them what has passed, and forgiveness of what has passed only occurs for one who has ceased to disbelieve. In this verse, there is evidence that Islam cancels what came before it. But if they return to fighting and enmity or to the disbelief they are upon, and return means continuation. The precedent of the former peoples has already passed. This phrase includes a threat, a warning, and an example of those nations who perished in the past with the punishment of God: that is, God’s precedent has passed for whoever does what these people did from the first nations, that he will be afflicted with a punishment, so let them expect the same.
8:39: 39- And fight them until there is no more persecution meaning disbelief. The explanation of this has already been presented in full in Surat Al-Baqarah. But if they desist from what was mentioned, then indeed, God is Seeing of what they do what they have done of desisting is not hidden from Him.God
8:40: 40- And if they turn away from what they were ordered to do, then know O believers, rather, God is your Protector that is, He is your Helper against them. What an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper! Whoever supports Him will succeed, and whoever supports Him will prevail. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: The precedent of the ancients has passed, he said: In Quraysh and others on the day of Badr, and the nations before that. Ahmad and Muslim narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Al-Aas who said: When God put Islam in my heart, I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Extend your hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you. He extended his right hand, but my hand was held back, and he said: What is the matter with you? I said: I wanted to stipulate. He said: What do you stipulate? I said: That you ask forgiveness for me. He said: Did you not know that Islam destroys what came before it, and that migration destroys what came before it, and that Hajj destroys what came before it? It has been proven in the Sahih from the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Islam wipes out what came before it, and repentance wipes out what came before it. Many of the Salaf interpreted the statement of God, the Most High: The precedent of the ancients has passed, as meaning what happened to the previous nations of punishment for those who fought the prophets and persisted in disbelief. Al-Suddi and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: What is meant by the verse is the Day of Badr. The majority of the Salaf interpreted the tribulation mentioned here as disbelief. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It was conveyed to me from Al-Zuhri from Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr and other scholars of ours, until there is no tribulation, so that no Muslim is tempted away from his religion.
8:41: When God Almighty commanded fighting by saying: And fight them until there is no more persecution, and fighting was a likely means of obtaining spoils, He mentioned the ruling on spoils and spoils. We have already mentioned that its origin is the capture of sheep from the enemy, then it was used for everything that is captured from them and it may be used for everything that is obtained through effort, and from this is the saying of the poet: I have traveled the world until I was satisfied with the spoils of war and returned And the same is said by another: The sheep are fed on the day of the sheep, wherever you go, and the deprived are deprived. As for the meaning of spoils in Islamic law, Al-Qurtubi reported that there is consensus that what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils is the wealth of the infidels if the Muslims conquer them by force and coercion. He said: The language does not require this specification, but Islamic law has defined the word as being restricted to this type. Ibn Abd al-Barr claimed that there was consensus that this verse, after his saying: They ask you about the spoils of war, and that four-fifths of the spoils of war are divided among the conquerors, and that his saying: They ask you about the spoils of war was revealed when the people of Badr quarrelled over the spoils of Badr, as mentioned at the beginning of the surah. It was said that I mean his saying: They ask you about the spoils of war, is decisive and not abrogated, and that the spoils of war belong to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and are not divided among the conquerors, and likewise for those who came after him from the imams. Al-Mawardi narrated this from many of the Malikis. They said: The imam has the right to take it away from them, and they cited as evidence the conquest of Mecca and the story of Hunayn. Abu Ubaidah used to say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca by force and attacked its people, so he returned it to them and did not divide it or make it spoils of war. A group of scholars have narrated consensus that four-fifths of the spoils of war belong to the conquerors, and among those who narrated this are Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abd al-Barr, al-Dawudi, al-Mazari, al-Qadi Iyadh, and Ibn al-Arabi, and the hadiths. There are many hadiths on the division of spoils among the conquerors and how they were to be divided. Al-Qurtubi said: No one, as far as I know, has said that the words of God the Almighty: They ask you about the spoils of war al-Anfal abrogate the words: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils al-Anfal. Rather, the majority said: His words: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils abrogates them, and they are the ones who are not permitted to distort or change the Book of God. As for the story of the conquest of Mecca, there is no proof in it due to the scholars’ disagreement about its conquest. He said: As for the story of Hunayn, when the Ansar said, You will give the spoils to Quraysh and leave us while our swords drip with their blood, he compensated himself by saying to them: “Are you not pleased that the people return with the world and you return with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to your homes?” As in Muslim and others, and no one else has the right to say this, rather it is specific to him. His statement: Whatever you take as spoils includes everything that can be described as spoils, and of anything is an explanation of the relative pronoun, and the consensus has specified from the generality of the verse: the captives, because the choice in this is up to the Imam without dispute, and likewise the spoils of the slain if the Imam calls out for them, and it was said: likewise the spoils of war. It was replied that there is no consensus on the land. His statement: Then a fifth of it belongs to God An-Nakha’i read: Then a fifth of it belongs to God with a kasra on in. The rest read it with a fatha on the basis that in and what follows it is the subject and its predicate is omitted, and the meaning is: It is right or obligatory that a fifth of it belongs to God. Scholars differed on how to divide the fifth into six opinions: The first: A group said: The fifth is divided into six, so the sixth is given to the Kaaba, which is for God, the second: for the Messenger of God, the third: for relatives, the fourth: for orphans, the fifth: for the poor, and the sixth: for the wayfarer. The second opinion: Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Rabi’ said: The spoils are divided into five, so one share is set aside from it and four are divided among the spoils, then he strikes his hand with the share that he set aside and whatever he collects from it he gives to the Kaaba, then he divides the rest of the share that he set aside into five for the Messenger, and after him the verse. The third opinion: It was narrated on the authority of Zain Al-Abidin Ali bin Al-Hussein that he said: The fifth is for us, so it was said to him: God says: And the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, so he said: Our orphans, our needy and our wayfarers. The fourth opinion: The opinion of Al-Shafi’i: The fifth is divided into five, and the share of God and the share of His Messenger are one and are spent on the interests of the believers, and the four fifths are divided into the four categories mentioned in the verse. The fifth opinion: The opinion of Abu Hanifa: The fifth is divided into three: orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer. The ruling on the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was lifted with his death, just as the ruling on his share was lifted. He said: And the fifth begins with repairing bridges, building mosques, and the provisions of judges and soldiers. Something similar to this was narrated from Al-Shafi’i. The sixth opinion: The opinion of Malik: It is left to the Imam’s consideration and effort, so he takes from it without limitation, and gives from it to the warriors based on his effort, and the remainder is spent on the interests of the Muslims. Al-Qurtubi said: And the four caliphs said this and acted on it, and it is indicated by his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have nothing from what God has bestowed upon you except the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you, for he did not divide it into fifths or thirds, but rather he mentioned what was mentioned in the verse in order to alert them, because they are among those to whom it is given. Al-Zajjaj said, in support of this statement: God Almighty said: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say: Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer.” It is permissible by consensus to spend on other than these categories if he sees that. His statement: and for relatives It was said: The repetition of the lam in thī al-qirb and not thā min ḍayh is to remove the suspicion that they share in the share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Scholars have differed regarding the kinship: The first is that they are all Quraysh. This was narrated from some of the Salaf, and evidence was given by what was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when he ascended Safa, he began calling out to all the clans of Quraysh, saying: O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Abu Thawr, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and Muslim ibn Khalid said: They are Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, based on the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib are one thing, and he interlaced his fingers. This is in Sahih. It was also said that they are Banu Hashim specifically, and Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, and others said the same. It was narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn and Mujahid. His statement: If you believe in God. Al-Zajjaj said about a group: The meaning is: Know that God is your Master if you believe in God. Another group said: If is connected to His statement: And know that whatever you have gained. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is the correct view because His statement: And know includes the command to submit and surrender to God’s command regarding the spoils, so If was connected to His statement: And know according to this meaning: that is, if you believe in God, then submit and surrender to God regarding what He has informed you of regarding the division of the spoils. He said in Al-Kashshaf: It is connected to something omitted that is indicated by And know meaning: if you believe in God, then know that one-fifth of the spoils must be used to draw near to God, so cut off your desires for it and be content with the four-fifths. What is meant is not mere knowledge, but rather knowledge that includes action and obedience to God’s command, because mere knowledge is the same for the believer and the disbeliever. His statement: And what We have sent down upon Our servant is connected to the sublime name: that is, if you believed in God and in what We sent down, and the Day of Discrimination is the Day of Badr, because it distinguished between the people of truth and the people of falsehood, the two groups are the two groups of Muslims and disbelievers, and God is over all things competent and from His great power is the victory of the smaller group over the larger group.
8:42: His saying: 42- When you were on the lower side of the valley and they were on the farthest side. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ya'qub read with a kasra on the 'ayn in the word adwah in both places, and the rest read with a damma in it, and idh is a substitute for the Day of Criterion, and it is possible that the factor is omitted: that is, remember when you were. Adwah: the side of the valley, and the lower is the feminine of the nearest, and the farthest is the feminine of the farthest, from dana yadnu, and qasa yaqusu, and it is said: al-qasiya, and the origin is waw, and it is the language of the people of Hijaz, and the lower side of the valley was next to Madinah, and al-qaswa was next to Makkah. The meaning is: the time of your descent on the lower side of the valley towards Madinah, and your enemy was on the farthest side of it next to Makkah. The phrase and the caravan is lower than you is in the accusative case as a state, and the accusative of lower is in the circumstance, and its place is the nominative as a report: that is, and the situation is that the caravan is in a place lower than the place where you are. Al-Akhfash, Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' permitted the raising of afl to mean more lower than you. Al-Rukub is the plural of Rukub. The Arabs do not say Rukub except for a group of camel riders, and they do not say Rukub for someone who is on a horse or otherwise. Ibn Faris said the same, and Ibn Al-Sikkit narrated it from most linguists. What is meant by Rukub here is the Rukub of Abu Sufyan, which is what is meant by the caravan, for they were in a place lower than them, which is near the seashore. It was said: The benefit of mentioning this state they were in, that they were on the lower side of the valley and their enemy was on the farthest side, and the Rukub was lower than them, is to indicate the strength of the enemy and their power. This is because the farthest side where the polytheists had stopped had water, and it was a land with no dry land. As for the lower side, it was soft, feet would sink in it, and there was no water in it. The caravan was behind the enemy despite their large numbers, so God bestowed His favor upon the Muslims by granting them victory over them in this situation. His saying: And if you had made an appointment, you would have differed about the appointment.
