That is, if you and the polytheists of Mecca had made an appointment to meet in this place to fight, some of you would have differed with one another, and your small number and great number would have prevented you from fulfilling the appointment, and what was in their hearts of awe for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have prevented them. But God gathered you together in this place that God might accomplish a matter that was to be accomplished. That is, it was true that He would accomplish, such as the victory of His allies, the defeat of His enemies, the honor of His religion, and the humiliation of disbelief. So He brought out the Muslims to take the caravan and its spoils for themselves. And He brought out the disbelievers to defend it. It was not in the calculations of the two groups that this agreement would occur in this manner. The lam in li-yaqdi is related to something omitted, and the meaning is: He gathered them in order to accomplish. The phrase that he who perishes may perish with clear evidence, and he who lives may live is a substitute for the phrase before it: that is, so that he who lives may die. He dies with clear evidence and lives with clear evidence so that no one will have an argument against God. It was said: Destruction and life are borrowed for disbelief and Islam: that is, the Islam of the one who embraces Islam is based on clear evidence and certainty that it is the religion of truth, and the disbelief of the one who disbelieves is based on clear evidence and not on the interference of doubt. Nafi’, Khalaf, Sahl, Ya’qub, Al-Bazzi and Abu Bakr read min Hayy with two Ya’s according to the original. The rest read it with one Ya’ with assimilation, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid because it is also found in the Mushaf. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing means He hears the disbelief of the disbelievers and knows it, and He hears the faith of the believers and knows it. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibad bin Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr who said: Then he divided up the spoils and said: And know that whatever you gain of anything after what had happened at Badr a fifth of it is for God until the end of the verse. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Qays bin Muslim Al-Jadali who said: I asked Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Ali bin Abi Talib bin Al-Hanafiyyah about the statement of God: And know that whatever you gain of anything, a fifth of it is for God He said: This is the key to the statement, to God belongs this world and the Hereafter and to the Messenger and to the near relatives So they differed after the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding these two shares. One of them said: The share of the near relatives is for the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. One of them said: The share of the relatives is for the relatives of the Caliph. Another of them said: The share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is for the Caliph after him. The opinion of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was unanimous that these two shares be for horses and equipment in the way of God, and that was during the caliphates of Abu Bakr and Umar. Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a military expedition and they captured a fifth of the spoils, he would multiply that by his fifth. Then he recited: And know that whatever you take as spoils Al-Baqarah 2:17. He said: His statement: A fifth of it is for God is the key to the statement. To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, so God made the share of God and the Messenger one, and for the relatives, so he made these two shares a strength in horses and weapons, and made the share of orphans, the poor and the wayfarer, and no one else would give it to him. He made the remaining four shares, one share for the horse, one share for its rider and one share for the foot soldier. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The spoils of war were divided into five fifths: four of them were for those who fought over them, and one fifth was divided into four fifths, a quarter for God, the Messenger and the near of kin, meaning the relatives of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Whatever was for God and the Messenger was for the relatives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not take anything from the fifth. The second quarter was for orphans, the third quarter was for the poor, and the fourth quarter was for the wayfarer, who was the poor guest who stayed with the Muslims. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding his statement: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils al-Baqarah 2:177, he said: The spoils of war would be brought and placed, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would divide them into five shares, setting aside one share and dividing four shares among the people, meaning those who witnessed the battle, then… He would strike with his hand all the shares he had set aside, and whatever he seized he would give to the Kaaba, for it is what God had named: Do not assign to God a share, for God owns this world and the Hereafter. Then he would take the rest of the share and divide it into five shares: a share for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a share for the near of kin, a share for the orphans, a share for the needy, and a share for the wayfarer. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would put God’s share in weapons and forelegs, in the way of God, in the covering of the Kaaba and its perfume, and whatever the Kaaba needed. He would put the Messenger’s share in forelegs, weapons, and the expenses of his family, and the share of the near of kin for his relatives, which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would put among them with his share with the people. There were three shares for the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would put among whomever he wished, wherever he wished. The Banu Abd al-Muttalib did not have any of these three shares, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a share from the people’s shares. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Husayn al-Mu'allim who said: I asked Abdullah ibn Buraydah about his statement: Then a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger. He said: What God has for His Prophet is for Him and what the Messenger has for His wives. Ash-Shafi'i, Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Najdah wrote to him asking him about the relatives whom God mentioned. He wrote to him: We used to think that they were them, but our people refused to do so and said that all of Quraysh were relatives. The addition of his statement: And they said that all of Quraysh were relatives was reported only by Abu Ma'shar, and it is weak. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Najdah al-Haruri sent to him asking him about the share of relatives, and he said: To whom do you think it belongs? Ibn Abbas said: It is for the relatives of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) divided it for them. Umar had offered us something that we saw as less than our right, so we rejected it and refused to accept it. He had offered them to help their husbands, to pay off their debts, and to give to their poor, but he refused to give them more than that. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I prefer you to wash your hands, because in the fifth of the fifth you have what is sufficient for you or makes you independent. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibrahim bin Mahdi Al-Masisi, who narrated to us Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman on the authority of his father on the authority of Hanash on the authority of Ikrimah on his authority, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace be upon him). Ibn Kathir said: This hadith has a good chain of transmission, and Abu Hatim authenticated this Ibrahim bin Mahdi. Yahya bin Ma'in said: He brings strange things. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri and Abdullah bin Abi Bakr on the authority of Jubayr bin Mut'im: "The Prophet (peace be upon him) divided the share of the relatives of Khaybar among Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib. He said: So I and Uthman ibn Affan walked until we entered upon him, and we said: O Messenger of God, these are your brothers from Banu Hashim. We do not deny their virtue because of your position among them. Have you seen our brothers from Banu al-Muttalib, whom you gave to without us? We and they are of the same status in lineage. He said: They did not leave us in the pre-Islamic era and in Islam. Muslim included it in his Sahih. Ibn Mardawayh included it on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, who said: The family of Muhammad who were given the fifth: the family of Ali, the family of Abbas, the family of Jaafar, and the family of Aqeel. Ibn Mardawayh included it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had one thing from the spoils that he would choose for himself, either a servant or a horse, and then he would take from the fifth after that. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh included it on the authority of Ali, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, why don’t you appoint me to what God has made special for us from the fifth? So I appointed him. Al-Hakim included it and authenticated it from him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed me to the fifth of the fifth, and I put it in its proper places during the lifetime of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, and Umar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh included it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: The Day of Discrimination, he said: It is the Day of Badr, and Badr is between Mecca and Medina. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim included it and authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh included it. And Al-Bayhaqi in Evidences from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The Day of Criterion He said: It is the Day of Badr, on which God distinguished between truth and falsehood. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: The Night of Criterion was the night when the two armies met on the morning of Friday night, seventeen days after the end of Ramadan. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: When you were on the lower slope He said: The lower slope is the shore of the valley and the caravan was below you. Abu Sufyan said: Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ikrimah who said: The lower slope is the edge of the lower valley, and the farthest slope is the edge of the farthest valley.
8:43: When is an accusative with an implied verb: i.e. remember, or it is a second substitute for the Day of Criterion. The meaning is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw them in his dream a little, so he told his companions about that, and that was a reason for their steadfastness. If he had seen them in his dream a lot, they would have failed and been cowardly in fighting them and disputed over the matter of whether to meet them or not. 43- But God saved meaning He saved them and protected them from failure and dispute, so He made them few in the eyes of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the dream. It was said: What is meant by the dream is the place of sleep, which is the eye: i.e. in the place of your sleep, which is your eye. This was narrated from Al-Hasan. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a good opinion, but the first is more acceptable in Arabic, because of His statement: And when He showed you them, when you met, as few in your eyes, and made you few in their eyes. This indicates that this is a vision of meeting, and that is a vision of sleep.
8:44: His statement: 44- And when He showed them to you The circumstance is in the accusative case with an implied noun in apposition to the first: meaning, remember the time when you saw them, when they were few, until one Muslim said to another: Do you see them as seventy? He said: They are about a hundred, and the Muslims were made small in the eyes of the polytheists until one of them said: They are only eaters of camels, and this was before the fighting, but when they started it, God multiplied the Muslims in the eyes of the polytheists, as He said in Al Imran 3:They see them twice their number, as seen by the eye, and the reason for the Muslims being made small in the eyes of the polytheists is that if they see them as few, they rush into the fight without fear, then they see them as many and fail and the circle turns against them, and the punishment of God and the scourge of His punishment befalls them, and the lam in that God may decree a matter which was already done is related to something omitted, as was mentioned previously, and it was only repeated because of the difference in the reason for it, and to God all matters return, all of them, He does what He wills in them and decrees what He wills in their affairs. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, When God showed them to you in your dream as few, he said: God showed them to him in his dream as few, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed his companions of that and that was to strengthen them. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, And if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart, he said: you would have become cowardly, and you would have disputed in the matter, he said: you would have differed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, But God saved, meaning He completed it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, But God saved, meaning He saved their matter until He made them victorious over their enemy. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement, And when He showed them to you, the verse, he said: They were few in our eyes on the day of Badr until I said to a man next to me: Do you think they are seventy? He said: No, they are one hundred, until we took one of them and asked him, he said: We were one thousand. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the verse, he said: He incited some of them against others. Ibn Kathir said: Its chain of transmission is authentic. Ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Ibad bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr regarding his statement: That God may accomplish a matter which was to be done, meaning that He may bring about war between them to exact vengeance on whoever He wanted to exact vengeance on, and to bestow favors on whoever He wanted to bestow favors on from among the people of His authority.
8:45: His statement: 45- If you meet a company The encounter is war, and the collective company: that is, if you fight a group of polytheists then stand firm for them and do not be cowardly towards them, and this does not contradict the previous dispensation in His statement: Except turning away for fighting or withdrawing to a company because the command to stand firm is in a state of ease, and the dispensation is in a state of necessity. And steadfastness may not be achieved except by turning away and withdrawing And remember God that is, remember God when your hearts are anxious because remembering Him helps to remain steadfast in hardships, and it was said that the meaning is: Be steadfast with your hearts and remember with your tongues because the heart may calm down when meeting and the tongue may become disturbed, so He commanded them to remember until the steadfastness of the heart and the tongue are united, and it was said: And the remembrance in this case should be like what the companions of Talut said: Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people. This verse is evidence of the legitimacy of remembrance in all situations, even in this situation in which hearts tremble and insights are scattered.
8:46: Then he ordered them to obey God in what He commands them to do and to obey His Messenger in what He guides them to. He forbade them from disputing, which is a difference in opinion, because that leads to failure, which is cowardice in war. The letter fa is the answer to the prohibition, and the verb is in the accusative case with the omission of an, and it is permissible for the verb to be conjoined withَن ناُظواand made jussive by its jussive. His statement: 46- And your wind will go away was read with the verb in the accusative case, and its jussive is in conjunction with َنَناُظواin both ways, and the wind: strength and victory, as it is said: the wind is for so-and-so if he is dominant in the matter, and it was said: the wind is the state, and it was likened in the enforcement of its matter to the wind in its blowing, and from this is the saying of the poet: If your winds blow, seize them, for after every fluttering wind there is stillness. It was said: What is meant by the wind is the north wind, because with it the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was aided. Then he commanded them to be patient in the hardships of war and informed them that he is with the patient in every matter in which patience is required. How wonderful is this company, whose provision cannot be overcome by a conqueror, and whose owner cannot be attacked from any direction, even if it is many.
8:47: Then he forbade them from being like those who left their homes in arrogance and to show off to people, and they were the Quraysh, for they left on the day of Badr to protect the caravan that was with Abu Sufyan, and with them were the female singers and the musical instruments, and when they reached Al-Juhfah, they heard that the caravan had escaped and was safe, so they did not return, but rather said: They must reach Badr to drink wine and have the female singers sing for them and the Arabs hear about their departure, so that was from them arrogance and wickedness and seeking praise from the people and to be flattered and boastful to them, which is hypocrisy. It was said that arrogance in the language is: piety with God’s blessings over His disobedience, and it is a source in the place of the state: that is, they left in arrogance and hypocrisy, and it was said: it is the object of it and so is hypocrisy: that is, they left for arrogance and hypocrisy. His statement: And they turn away is connected to insolence, and the meaning is as mentioned above: that is, they went out insolently, showing off, turning people away from the path of God, or turning away from the path of God. Turning away means misleading people and preventing them from the paths of guidance. It is possible that and they turn away is connected to they go out, and the meaning is: they combine going out in that manner and turning away. And God encompasses what they do, nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, so He will reward them for it.
8:48: His saying: 48- And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them The circumstance is related to something omitted: that is, remember, O Muhammad, the time when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them. And beautification means improvement. It has been narrated that Satan appeared to them and said to them that statement, which is: No one from among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector meaning I will protect you from every enemy or from Banu Kinanah. The meaning of protector here is: the one who repels all kinds of harm from his companion, as a neighbor repels another. He was in the form of Suraqah bin Malik bin Ja'sham, who was from Banu Bakr bin Kinanah. Quraysh feared that Banu Bakr would come to them from behind. It has been said that the meaning is that he put this statement in their minds, and they imagined that they could not be defeated or overcome. So when the two groups came into sight meaning the group of Muslims and polytheists he turned back on his heels meaning he retreated. From this is the saying of the poet: Backtracking is not an honor, but honor is taking the initiative in hope. And the other said: What benefit did the backward ones get from their regression, nor did the advances of the forerunners harm them? It was said: The meaning of Nakkas here is that his plot was nullified and his imagination was gone. And he said, ‘I am innocent of you.’ That is, he disavowed them when he saw signs of victory with the Muslims through God’s support for them with angels. Then he explained that by saying: I see what you do not see, meaning the angels. Then he explained it with another reason and said: I fear God. It was said: He feared that he would be afflicted with harm from the angels who were present at the battle. It was said: His claim of fear was a lie on his part, but he saw that he and the polytheists had no power, so he explained it with that. The phrase And God is severe in penalty may be part of the words of Satan, or it may be a new statement from God Almighty.
8:49: His saying: 49- When the hypocrites said The circumstance is the object of an omitted verb which is remember, and it is possible that it is related to a relapse or to adorn or to severe punishment. It was said: The hypocrites are those who showed faith and concealed disbelief. And those in whose hearts is disease are those who doubt without hypocrisy, but because they were new to Islam, so they agreed with the hypocrites in their saying this statement, I mean These meaning the Muslims have been deceived by their religion until they undertook what they could not bear of fighting Quraysh. It was said: Those in whose hearts is disease are the polytheists, and it is not far-fetched that what is meant by them are the Jews living in Medina and its surroundings, and that they and the hypocrites from the people of Medina said this statement when the Muslims went out to Badr when they saw them few in number and weak in number, so God answered them by saying: Whoever relies upon God - then indeed, God is Exalted in Might No one can overcome Him, and He does not humiliate whoever relies upon Him. Wise He has the perfect wisdom that minds fall short of. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And remember God, that he said: God has made His remembrance obligatory when they are most busy: when fighting with swords. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two things will not be rejected: supplication at the call to prayer and during battle when some of them fight each other.” Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abu Musa that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked making noise during fighting. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And do not dispute and [thus] lose courage and your strength departs, that he said: Do not differ and become cowardly and your victory departs. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, and your strength departs, that he said: Your strength departed, and the strength of the companions of Muhammad departed when they disputed with him on the day of Uhud. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not be like those who left their homes the verse, meaning the polytheists who fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi who said: When the Quraysh left Mecca for Badr, they went out with singing girls and drums, so God revealed this verse. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid in The verse: He said: Abu Jahl and his companions on the day of Badr. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse: “The polytheists of Quraysh who fought the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr went out with transgression and pride, and it was said to them on that day: Go back, for your caravan has set out and you have been victorious. They said: No, by God, not until the people of Hijaz talk about our march and our numbers. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on that day: O God, Quraysh has come with its pride and arrogance to argue with your Messenger.” It was mentioned to us that he said on that day: Its best men have come from Mecca. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Iblis came with an army of devils, and with him was a banner in the form of men from Banu Mudlij, and the devil was in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju’sham. The devil said: No one from among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector. Gabriel approached Iblis, and when he saw him, his hand was in the hand of a man from the polytheists. Iblis withdrew his hand and turned away, along with his followers. The man said: O Suraqah, you are our protector. The angels said: I see what you do not see. That was when he saw the angels: I fear God, and God is severe in penalty. He said: When the people came close to each other, God made the Muslims few in the eyes of the polytheists, and made the polytheists few in the eyes of the Muslims. The polytheists said: “These are not these people, their religion has deceived them, but they said that because they were few in their eyes, and they thought that they would defeat them, and they had no doubt about that. So God said: “And whoever relies upon God - then indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” At-Tabarani and Abu Nu’aym narrated on the authority of Rifa’ah. Ibn Rafi' Al-Ansari said: When Iblis saw what the angels were doing to the polytheists on the day of Badr, he feared that he would be killed, so Al-Harith bin Hisham clung to him, thinking that he was Suraqa bin Malik. He poked Al-Harith in the chest and threw him down, then he ran away until he threw himself into the sea and raised his hands and said: O God, I ask You to spare me. Al-Waqidi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: Indeed, I see what you do not see, he said: It was mentioned to us that he saw Gabriel and the angels descending with him, so the enemy of God knew that he could not be matched by the angels and he said: Indeed, I fear God. The enemy of God lied, he did not fear God, but he knew that he had no power or protection from Him. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Muammar, who said: It was mentioned that they approached Suraqa bin Malik after that, and he denied that he had said anything of that. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: When the hypocrites said, he said: They were among the Muslims on that day. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement: And those in whose hearts is disease, he said: They are people who did not witness the fighting on the day of Badr, so they were called hypocrites. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Kalbi regarding his statement: And those in whose hearts is disease, he said: They are people who had acknowledged Islam while they were in Mecca, then they went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr, and when they saw the Muslims they said: These people have been deceived by their religion. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of al-Sha’bi.
8:50: His saying: 50- And if you could see is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to anyone who is suitable for it, as was previously explained in more than one place. The meaning is: And if you could see, because if the present tense is changed to past tense, and when is an adverb for you could see, and the object is omitted: that is, if you could see the disbelievers at the time the angels take their souls, it was said: He meant by those who disbelieved those who were not killed on the day of Badr, and it was said: It is about those who were killed at Badr, and the answer to if is omitted, its meaning is: You would have seen a great matter, and the phrase they strike their faces is in the accusative case as a state, and what is meant by their backs is their buttocks, it was referred to by the backs, and it was said: Their backs, it was said: This striking will be at death as indicated by the mention of taking them, and it was said: It is on the Day of Resurrection when they are led to the Fire. His saying: And taste the punishment of the burning fire, Al-Farra’ said, meaning: And they say, Taste the punishment of the burning fire, and the sentence is connected to strike, and it was said: That the keepers of Hell say this to them, and the taste may be tangible, and it may be placed in the place of trial and testing, and its origin is from tasting with the mouth.
8:51: And the reference in His saying: 51- That is to what preceded of the beating and torment, and the ba in because of what your hands have put forth is causal: meaning that this will happen because of what you have earned of sins and committed of transgressions, and the sentence and that God is not unjust to the servants is in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning that the matter is that He does not wrong them, and it is permissible for it to be conjoined with the sentence that is the predicate of His saying: That and it is because of what your hands have put forth meaning that this torment is because of the sins, and because that God is not unjust to the servants because He, glory be to Him, sent His messengers to them, and revealed to them His books, and made clear to them the path, and guided them to the two paths as He, glory be to Him, said: And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.
8:52: His statement: 52- Like the habit of Pharaoh’s people When God Almighty mentioned what He sent down upon the people of Badr, He followed it with what indicates that this is His way with the groups of disbelievers. Habit means custom, and the kaf is in the nominative case as a predicate for a deleted subject: meaning the habit of these people is like the habit of Pharaoh’s people and those before them. The meaning is: He punished these people as He punished those people, so the custom of punishing these people was like the past custom of God in punishing groups of disbelievers. The phrase they disbelieved in the signs of God explains the habit of the people of Pharaoh: that is, their habit was that they disbelieved in the signs of God, so their disbelief caused God Almighty to seize them. What is meant by their sins: their transgressions that resulted from their disbelief, so the ba in by their sins is for association, that is, He seized them while they were involved in their sins and had not repented from them. The phrase God is Powerful and Severe in Punishment is an interjection confirming the meaning of what preceded it.
8:53: And the reference in his saying: 53- That is to the punishment that God brought down upon them, and it is the subject and its predicate is what comes after it, and the sentence is in the course of explaining what happened to them of God's punishment. Meaning: That punishment is because God usually does not change the blessings He bestows upon His servants until they change what is in themselves of conditions and morals by being ungrateful for God’s blessings, belittling His kindness, and neglecting His commands and prohibitions, as was the case with the people of Pharaoh and those before them, and with Quraysh and those like them from the polytheists. God opened for them the doors of goodness in this world and bestowed upon them the favors of sending messengers and revealing books, but they responded to these blessings with disbelief and thus deserved to have the blessings changed, just as they changed what they should have followed and acted upon by thanking and accepting them. The phrase and that God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing is connected to that God would not change a blessing and is included with it in the al-Sharh 94:that is, because God would not change, etc., and because God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, He hears what they say and knows what they do. It was read with a kasra on the hamza as a new sentence.
8:54: Then he repeated what came before, saying: 54- Like the way of the people of Pharaoh and those before them who denied the signs of their Lord for the purpose of emphasis with the addition that it is like the explanation of taking sins by drowning, and it was said: The first is in consideration of what the people of Pharaoh and those who resembled them did, and the second is in consideration of what was done to them, and it was said: What is meant by the first is their disbelief in God, and by the second is their denial of the prophets, and other things were said that are not without arbitrariness, and the speech in We destroyed them for their sins is like the speech that came before in So God seized them for their sins, And We drowned the people of Pharaoh is connected to We destroyed them, connecting the specific to the general because of its horror and being one of the most severe types of destruction, then he ruled on the two groups of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, and the disbelievers of Quraysh with injustice to themselves, because of what they caused for God's punishment from disbelief in God and His signs and messengers and injustice to others, as was the case with them in their dealings with people With all kinds of injustice. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, he said: Those polytheists whom God killed at Badr. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, I saw something like thorns on the back of Abu Jahl. He said: That is the beating of the angels. This is a mursal. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And their backs, he said: And their buttocks, but God is Generous and uses a euphemism. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: That is because God will not change a favor which He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves, he said: The favor of God is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God bestowed his favor upon the Quraysh, so they disbelieved, so God transferred him to the Ansar.
8:55: His statement: 55- Indeed, the worst of living creatures meaning the worst of what creeps on the face of the earth in the sight of God meaning in His judgment are those who disbelieve meaning those who persist in disbelief and persist in misguidance. For this reason, He said: So they will not believe meaning that this is their nature, they will never believe, and they will not turn back from misguidance at all. And making them the worst of living creatures, not the worst of people, is an allusion to their shedding of humanity and their entering into a species other than people from the types of animals due to their lack of reasoning about what is in them to guide them.
8:56: His statement: 56- Those of them with whom you made a covenant is a substitute for those who disbelieved, or an apposition, or in the accusative case of blame. The meaning is that these disbelievers who are the worst of creatures in the sight of God are those with whom you made a covenant: that is, you took their covenant from them. Then they break their covenant that you made with them every time of the covenant. And the condition is that and they do not fear the breaking, nor do they fear its consequences, nor do they avoid its causes. It was said that from in his statement: of them is for partiality, and the object of I made a covenant is omitted: that is, those with whom you made a covenant, and they are some of those disbelievers: meaning the nobles among them. The conjunction of the future, which is then they break their covenant with the past, which is I made a covenant, is to indicate the continuation of their breaking. These are the Qurayzah with whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a covenant that they would not help the disbelievers, but they did not fulfill that, as will come.
8:57: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they be treated harshly and severely, saying: If you encounter them in battle, then scatter them from behind meaning, if you encounter them in a scatter and meet them in a situation where you are able to overpower them and defeat them, then scatter them from behind meaning, then kill and torment them and scatter those who are fighting you from among the polytheists behind them until they fear your side and refrain from fighting you for fear that what happened to these will happen to them. And scatter in the original language: what is used to tie a canal or something similar, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: She calls Qaib, and the iron chokes her like a culture choking on the connection of pipes. It is said: I found him, and so-and-so is thaqafa: quick to find what he tries, and dispersion: separation with confusion. Abu Ubaidah said: He was dispersed by them means he heard about them. Al-Zajjaj said: Do to them an act of killing by which you scatter those behind them, it is said: I dispersed the sons of so-and-so: I uprooted them from their places and expelled them from them until they left them. The poet said: I roam the valleys every day for fear that a wise man will make me wander And from it is the word sharadha al-ba’ir: if it separated from its owner. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he read: fasharadha bihum with the voiced dhal. Qatrib said: tasharadha with the voiced dhal means to torture, and with the silent dhal it means to separate. Al-Mahdi said: The voiced dhal has no basis except that it is a substitute for the silent dhal due to their similarity. He said: fasharadha is not known in the language, and it was read min khalfahum with the kasra on the meem and the fa.
8:58: His statement: 58- And if you fear treachery from a people meaning deceit and breach of the covenant from the people with whom you have a covenant, then throw back to them meaning throw to them the covenant that is between you and them on an equal footing on a level path. The meaning is that he should inform them clearly and openly of the breach and not engage them in war suddenly. It was said that the meaning of on an equal footing is in a way that the farthest and nearest of them are equal in knowledge of the breach, or you and they are equal in it. Al-Kisa’i said: Equity is justice, and it may mean the middle, and from this is his statement: In the middle of Hellfire, and from this is the statement of Hassan: Woe to the supporters of the Prophet and his family after sunset in the midst of the atheists The first is the poet’s saying: Strike the faces of your treacherous enemies until they respond to you equally. It was said that the meaning of: Then throw it to them on equal terms is out loud, not secretly. It appears that this verse is general and applies to every treaty holder who fears that he will break it. Ibn Atiyyah said: What appears from the wording of the Qur’an is that the matter of Banu Qurayzah ended when He said: Then disperse with them those behind them. Then the Blessed and Exalted began in this verse to command him what to do in the future with those from whom he fears treachery. The phrase Indeed, God does not like traitors is an explanation of what preceded it. It is possible that it is a warning to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about confronting him before throwing it to them on equal terms. It is possible that it refers to the people from whom treachery is feared.
8:59: His saying: 59- And do not think Ibn Amir, Yazid and Hafs read it with the lower ya', and the rest read it with the doubled ya' from above. According to the first reading, those who disbelieved are the subject of the reckoning, and its first object is omitted: that is, those who disbelieved should not think that they are ahead, and its second object is they preceded, meaning: they came and escaped from being caught. According to the second reading, the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its first object is those who disbelieved, and the second is they preceded, and it was read And do not think that those who disbelieved have outstripped, for they will not escape and it was read they will not think that they have outstripped, for they will not fail, and the phrase they will not fail is an explanation of what preceded it, meaning that they will not escape and will not find their seeker unable to catch up with them. Ibn Amir read it with a fatha on the hamza, while the rest read it with a kasra. Both readings are useful because the sentence is causal. It was said that what is meant by this verse is those polytheists who escaped the battle of Badr. The meaning is that even if they escaped this battle and were saved, they will not be helpless, rather they will fall into God’s punishment in this world or in the hereafter. A group of grammarians, including Abu Hatim, claimed that the reading of those who read yasabna with a ta’ is a mistake, and it is not permissible to read it with it because li-yasabna did not come with an object, and it needs two objects. An-Nahhas said: This is a severe bias, and the meaning of this reading is: And do not think that those who come after them who disbelieve have outstripped them, so the pronoun refers to what came before, except that the reading with a ta’ is clearer. Al-Mahdawi said: According to this reading, it is permissible for those who disbelieved to be the subject, and the first object is deleted. The meaning is: And do not think that those who disbelieved have outstripped them. Makki said: It is permissible to imply with they preceded that it replaces the two objects, and the meaning is: And let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped, so it is like Do people think that they will be left alone in that that replaces the two objects.
8:60: Then the Almighty ordered the preparation of strength for the enemies, and strength is everything that is used to strengthen oneself in war, including weapons and bows. It has been proven in Sahih Muslim and others from the hadith of Uqbah bin Amir who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the pulpit saying: "And prepare against them whatever you are able of strength. Indeed, strength is archery, he said it three times." It was said that it refers to fortresses, and the destination is to the interpretation proven from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. His saying: 60- And from the tying of horses. Al-Hasan, Amr bin Dinar, and Abu Haywah read and from the tying of horses with a damma on the ra and the ba like katab: the plural of kitab. Abu Hatim said: The tether of the five horses or more, and they are the horses that are tied to the enemy's belt, and from it the saying of the poet: God ordered to tie it to his enemy in war. God is the best guide. Al-Kashshaf said: “Al-Ribat is the name for the horses that are tied up in the way of God. It is permissible to call it Ribat, which means murabata, and it is permissible to use the plural of ribait, like faseel and fasal.” Whoever interprets strength as everything that is strengthened by in war, makes the conjunction of horses an conjunction of the specific to the general, and the phrase you terrify thereby the enemy of God and your enemy is in the accusative case as a state, intimidation and fear, and the pronoun in it refers to what is in what you are able to or to the source understood from and prepare which is preparation. What is meant by the enemy of God and their enemy are the polytheists of Mecca and others from the polytheists of the Arabs. His statement: and others besides them is in apposition to the enemy of God and your enemy, and the meaning of besides them is: from other than them. It was said that they are the Jews, and it was said that they are the Persians and the Romans, and it was said that they are the jinn, and Ibn Jarir preferred it. It was said that what is meant by others besides them is everyone whose enmity is not known, as Al-Suhayli said. It was said that they are Banu Qurayzah specifically, and it was said otherwise, and it is better to stop at specifying them because of His statement: You do not know them, God knows them. His statement: And whatever you spend in the cause of God meaning in jihad, even if it is truly insignificant, It will be fully repaid to you its reward in the Hereafter, so a good deed is multiplied by ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, up to many times as we have stated previously, and you will not be wronged in anything of this spending that you spend in the cause of God: meaning in its reward, rather it will become for you in full, abundant and complete: And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward “I will not allow to be lost the work of any worker among you.” Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: The worst of beasts in the sight of God the verse was revealed about six men of the Jews, among them Ibn Tabut. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Those of them with whom you made a treaty and then broke their treaty he said: The Qurayzah on the day of the Trench sided with the enemies of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then disperse through them those behind them he said: He punished those after them. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse he said: He punished those behind them. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding the verse he said: Warn them. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: He admonished other people through them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd who said: He made them fearful. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: Perhaps they will remember, they say: Perhaps they will beware of breaking their oath and the same will be done to them. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab who said: Gabriel entered upon the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and said: You have laid down your weapons and we are still pursuing the people, so go out, for God has given you permission to deal with Qurayzah, and revealed about them: And if you fear treachery from a people, the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, they will not escape, he said: They will not escape us. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power, he said: Archery, swords, and weapons. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibad bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr regarding his statement: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power, he said: He ordered them to prepare horses. Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the verse who said: The strength is the male horses, and the ribat is the females. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Mujahid. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab regarding the verse, he said: Strength is the horse up to the arrow and below. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah, he said: Strength is the fortresses, and from the tethering of horses he said: the females. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And you terrify thereby the enemy of God and your enemy he said: You disgrace thereby the enemy of God and your enemy. Many hadiths have been narrated about the desirability of archery and the reward in it. Likewise, hadiths have been narrated about the desirability of keeping horses and preparing them and the great reward for their owner, which there is not enough space to explain here. A group of scholars have devoted books to this.
8:61: Inclination: leaning. It is said: a man inclined towards a man: he leaned towards him. From this, the ribs were called jawaneh because they leaned towards the hanawah. And camels inclined: if their necks leaned while walking. From this, the saying of Dhu al-Rummah is said: If he dies on a saddle, his soul is revived by your memory, and the sent camels are at their zenith. And similar to it is the saying of Antarah: Jawah has become certain that if the two armies meet, his tribe will be the first to prevail. It means bird, and peace means reconciliation. Al-A'mash, Abu Bakr, Ibn Muhaisin, and Al-Mufaddal read it with a kasra on the seen, and the rest read it with a fatha. Al-Uqayli read fajanh with a damma on the noon, and the rest read it with a fatha. The first is the language of Qais, and the second is the language of Tamim. Ibn Jinni said: The language of Qais is analogy, and peace is feminine as war is feminine, or it is interpreted as a trait or an action. Scholars have differed as to whether this verse is abrogated or decisive. It was said: It is abrogated by His statement: Then kill the polytheists. It was said: It is not abrogated, because what is meant by it is accepting the jizyah, and the Companions and those who came after them accepted it from them, so it is specific to the People of the Book. It was said: If the polytheists are called to peace, it is permissible for them to respond to it. Those who forbid peace with the polytheists hold fast to the statement of God the Almighty: “So do not weaken and call for peace while you are superior and God is with you.” They restricted the impermissibility to when the Muslims are in a state of honor and strength, not when they are not. It is permissible, as the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did when he made a truce with the Quraysh, and the Caliphs and Companions continued to do so. The speech of scholars on this issue is well-known and established in its proper places. And put your trust in God in your inclination towards peace and do not fear their generosity, for He the Almighty is the Hearer of what they say, the Knower of what they do.
8:62: 62- And if they intend to deceive you with a peace treaty, while they intend treachery and deception, then sufficient for you is God meaning He will suffice you from what you fear of their evils of breaking the covenant and treachery. The phrase It is He who supported you with His victory and with the believers is explanatory: meaning do not fear their deception and treachery, for God, who strengthened you against them with victory in the past, which was on the day of Badr, is the one who will support you and strengthen you against them when the deception and breaking of the covenant occur, and what is meant by the believers are the Muhajireen and Ansar.
8:63: Then he explained how he was supported by the believers, saying: 63- And He brought their hearts together. The apparent meaning is general, and that the unity of the hearts of the believers is one of the reasons for victory by which God supported His Messenger. The majority of commentators said: What is meant is the Aws and the Khazraj, as there was intense partisanship and great wars between them, so God brought their hearts together through faith in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: He meant to bring the Muhajireen and the Ansar together, and it is more appropriate to carry it in general, as the Arabs before the mission of Muhammad used to eat each other and not respect their money or blood, until Islam came and they became one hand, and the partisanship that was between them disappeared. The phrase If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together confirms the meaning of what preceded it. The meaning is that the fanaticism and enmity between them had reached a point that could not be stopped under any circumstances, and even if the seeker spent everything on earth, he would not be able to achieve what he sought of reconciliation, because their situation in that regard had become very serious. But God reconciled them with His great power and wonderful creation. He is Exalted in Might with no one to overcome Him, and no matter is too difficult for Him. Wise in His management and the enforcement of His prohibitions and commands. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: “And if they incline to peace,” he said: Qurayzah. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: It was revealed about Banu Qurayzah, and it was abrogated by: “So do not weaken and call for peace,” to the end of the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Peace is obedience. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: If they are satisfied, then be satisfied. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: If they want peace, then reject it. Abu Ubaid, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: It was abrogated by this verse: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, to His statement: while they are subdued. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Nahhas in his Naskh, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Then that was abrogated by: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And if they intend to deceive you, he said: Qurayzah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: And the believers, he said: The Ansar. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir something similar. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar as well. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: It is written on the Throne: There is no god but God, I am God alone, I have no partner, and Muhammad is My servant and Messenger, I supported him with My knowledge, and that is His statement: It is He who supported you with His victory and with the believers. Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, al-Nasa’i, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that this verse was revealed regarding those who love one another for the sake of God: If you spent all that is in the earth al-Baqarah 2:170. Abu Ubaid, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab al-Iman narrated, and this wording is his, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Kinship can be severed, and the favor of a benefactor can be denied. We have not seen anything like the closeness of hearts. God says: If you spent all that is in the earth (al-Baqarah 2:174). Ibn al-Mubarak, Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on his authority. There is nothing in this on the authority of Ibn Abbas that indicates that it was the reason for revelation. However, the issue is in the statement of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him: This verse was revealed about those who love one another for the sake of God, even though what precedes it is He is the One who supported you with His victory and with the believers and what follows it is O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers. And with the pronoun in His statement: What You have brought their hearts together refers to the believers mentioned before it without a doubt or suspicion. Likewise the pronoun in His statement: But God brought them together indicates that the mentioned bringing together is between the believers with whom God supported His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
8:64: His saying: 64- O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and whoever follows you of the believers. This is not a repetition of what came before it, as the first is restricted to the intention of deception. And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is God. This is a specific sufficiency. In His saying: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God, there is a general sufficiency that is not restricted: that is, God is sufficient for you in every situation. The waw in His saying: and whoever follows you may be for the purpose of connecting to the noble name. The meaning is: God is sufficient for you and the believers are sufficient for you: that is, God is sufficient for you and the believers are sufficient for you. It may also be in the sense of with, as you say: A dirham is sufficient for you and Zayd, and the meaning is: God is sufficient for you and the believers are sufficient for you, because connecting the apparent to the implicit in such a form is forbidden, as is established in the science of grammar, and the Kufians permitted it. Al-Farra’ said: It is not often in their speech to say: Hasabka wa-akheeka. Rather, what is used is to say: Hasabka wa-Hasabka akheeka, repeating the preposition. So if his statement: And whoever follows you were in the genitive case, it would have been said: Hasabka God wa-Hasab mani atabaka. An-Nahhas chose the accusative case as the complement with it. And it was said: It is possible that the meaning is: And whoever follows you from the believers, God is sufficient for them, so the predicate was deleted.
8:65: His saying: 65- "He urged the believers to fight" meaning he urged them and urged them. Incitement in the language is: exaggeration in urging and it is like incitement, taken from the verb "haradh", which is that the illness exhausts him and exaggerates it until he recovers on the verge of death as if he is attributing him to destruction if he fails to do what is commanded. Then he gave them good report to strengthen their hearts and calm their thoughts that those who are patient among them in fighting will overcome ten times their number of disbelievers, so he said: "If there are twenty of you who are patient, they will overcome two hundred." Then he added this as a useful clarification of the fact that this good report is not limited to this number, but rather it is current in every number, so he said: "And if there are one hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand." In this there is evidence that a group of believers, whether they are few or many, will not be overcome by ten times their number of disbelievers under any circumstances, and there has been found in the outside world what contradicts that, so how many groups of disbelievers overcome those who are one-tenth of them from Muslims, rather like half of them, rather like them. The answer to that is that the existence of this in the outside world does not contradict what is in the verse, because it is possible that the group of believers is not characterized by the quality of patience. It was said: This report of the verse is in the meaning of a command, like the Almighty’s saying: And mothers shall breastfeed and And divorced women shall wait. The believers were commanded by God, the Exalted, to have the group of them steadfast for ten times their number. Then, when that was difficult for them and they considered it great, He made it easier for them and permitted them because He, the Exalted, knew that there was weakness in them, so He said: So if there are a hundred of you, patient, they will overcome two hundred to the end of the verse. So He made it obligatory for one person to be steadfast for two of the disbelievers. Hamza read from Asim weakness with the opening of the letter Ḍād. His saying: Because they are a people who do not understand is related to his saying: They will be overcome, meaning that this overcoming is due to their ignorance and lack of understanding, and that they fight without insight, and whoever is like this is mostly defeated. It has been said that the reason for specifying that twenty would outnumber two hundred and one hundred would outnumber one thousand is that the number of raids that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out did not fall short of twenty and did not exceed one hundred. It has been said that specifying later that one hundred would outnumber two hundred and one thousand two thousand is good report for the Muslims that the number of the armies of Islam will exceed tens and hundreds to thousands.
8:66: 66- "Now God has lightened your burden, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred of you, patient, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand by God's permission. And God is with the patient." Then He informed them that this victory is by God's permission, facilitation, and ease, not by their strength and endurance. Then He gave them good report that He is with the patient, and in it is encouragement to be patient and an emphasis on them to adhere to it and recommend it, and that it is one of the greatest causes of success, prosperity, victory, and triumph, because whoever God is with, no one can overcome him. The scholars have differed over whether this lightening was abrogated or not. There is not much benefit related to that. Al-Bazzar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When Omar embraced Islam, the polytheists said: Today the people have taken their revenge on us. Then God revealed: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers. At-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When thirty-nine men and women embraced Islam with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then Omar embraced Islam, they became forty, so this was revealed: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr that he said: When thirty-three women embraced Islam with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then Omar embraced Islam, this was revealed: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Az-Zuhri regarding the verse that he said: It was revealed about the Ansar. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi regarding his statement: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers, that he said: God is sufficient for you and those who follow you. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the verse, If there are twenty among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, was revealed, it was decreed upon them that not one out of ten should flee, and that twenty out of two hundred should not flee. Then the verse, Now God has lightened your burden was revealed, and it was decreed that not one out of two hundred should flee. Sufyan said: Ibn Shabrumah said: I see enjoining good and forbidding evil as something like this. If there are two men, he orders them, but if there are three, he is at liberty to leave them alone. Al-Bukhari, An-Nahhas in his Naskh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the verse, If there are twenty among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims when it was decreed upon them that not one out of ten should flee, so the alleviation came, Now God has lightened your burden verse. He said: When God lightened their number, He reduced their patience by the same amount that He had lightened their burden.
8:67: This is another ruling of the rulings of Jihad. The meaning of 67- "It was not for a prophet" is what was correct for him and what was upright. Abu Amr, Suhayl, Yaqub, Yazid and Al-Mudallal read "that it be" with the upper vowel and the rest read it with the lower vowel. Yazid and Al-Mudallal also read "captives and the rest read captives". The captives are the plural of "captive, like killed and killed, and wounded and wounded". The plural of "captive is also called captive with the damma and fatha of the hamza, and it is taken from captivity, which is the string, because they used to tie up the captive with it, so every captive, even if he was not tied up with the string", was called a captive. Al-A'sha said: Poetry tied me to its house as families tied up donkeys. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala said: The prisoners are those who are not bound when they are taken, and the captives are those who are bound as slaves. Ithkhan means to kill a lot and exaggerate in it. The Arabs say: So-and-so killed a lot in this matter, meaning he exaggerated in it. So the meaning is: It is not appropriate for a prophet to have prisoners until he exaggerates in killing the disbelievers and increases it. It was said that the meaning of Ithkhan is: to be able to do so, and it was said that it is strength. God the Almighty informed us that killing the polytheists on the day of Badr was better than taking them prisoner and ransoming them. Then when the Muslims became many, God permitted that and said: Then either by favor afterwards or ransom as will come in Surat al-Qital, God willing. His statement: You desire the goods of worldly life, meaning its benefit and enjoyment through what you have received as ransom. It is called an goods because it quickly disappears, just as the goods that are the opposite of jewels disappear. And God desires the Hereafter meaning He desires for you the Hereafter through what you obtain of reward for killing a lot. It was read, He wants the Hereafter in the accusative case, based on the assumption of an added word, which is the one mentioned before it: meaning, by God, He wants to present the Hereafter. And God is Exalted in Might cannot be overcome. Wise in all His actions.
8:68: His saying: 68- "Had it not been for a previous decree from God, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took." The commentators differed regarding this decree that preceded what it is? According to the following statements: The first: What preceded in God's knowledge that this nation would be permitted to take spoils of war after it had been forbidden to all other nations, and the second: It is God's forgiveness of the people of Badr for their past and future sins as in the authentic hadith: "God looked at the people of Badr and said, 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" The third statement: That He would not punish them while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among them as God, the Most High, said: "And God would not punish them while you were among them." The fourth statement: That He would not punish anyone for a sin he committed out of ignorance of it being a sin. The fifth statement: That it is what God decreed of erasing minor sins by avoiding major sins. The sixth statement: That He would not punish anyone except after confirming the argument and presenting the prohibition and no prohibition of that preceded. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari believed that all of these meanings are included in the wording and that it includes them. A great punishment has befallen you means for what you took means for what you took as ransom.
8:69: And the fa in 69- "So eat from what you have taken as spoils" is to arrange what comes after it according to an omitted reason: i.e. I have made the spoils permissible for you, so eat from what you have taken as spoils. It is also possible that it is a conjunction to an implied omitted reason: i.e. leave the ransom and eat from what you have taken as spoils other than it. It was said that "what" is an expression for the ransom: i.e. eat from the ransom that you have taken as spoils, for it is part of the spoils that God has made permissible for you. And "lawful and good" are in the accusative case as a state or a description of the omitted source: i.e. lawful and good eating. "And fear God" in what is to come, so do not proceed with something that God has not permitted you to do. "Indeed, God is Forgiving" for what you have neglected. "Merciful" towards you. Therefore, He has permitted you to take the ransom in the future. Ahmad narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted the people about the prisoners on the day of Badr and said: ‘God has given you power over them.’ ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, strike off their heads.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and said: ‘O people, God has given you power over them, and they were your brothers yesterday.’ ‘Umar stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, strike off their heads.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him. Then he returned and said the same thing. Then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, we think that you should pardon them and accept their ransom.’ So he pardoned them and accepted their ransom, and God revealed: ‘Had it not been for a previous decree from God…’” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: “When the day of Badr came, the prisoners were brought, among them Al-Abbas. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you want with these prisoners? Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, they are your people and your family, so spare them so that God may accept their repentance. Umar said: O Messenger of God, they lied to you, expelled you and fought you, so bring them forward and strike their necks. Abdullah bin Rawahah said: O Messenger of God, look for a valley with plenty of firewood and set it on fire.” And Al-Abbas said while he was listening: You have severed your ties of kinship. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon them and did not answer them anything. Some people said: He should take the words of Abu Bakr. Others said: He should take the words of Umar. Some people said: He should take the words of Abdullah bin Rawahah. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out and said: God softens the hearts of men in it until they are softer than milk, and God hardens the hearts of men in it until they are harder than stones. Your example, O Abu Bakr, is like that of Abraham, peace be upon him, who said: Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, You are indeed Forgiving and Merciful. And your example, O Abu Bakr, is like that of Jesus, peace be upon him, who said: If You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And your example, O Umar, is like that of Noah, peace be upon him, when he said: My Lord, do not leave on the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers. And your example, O Umar, is like that of Moses, peace be upon him, when he said: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment. You are a burden, so none of them will escape except by ransom or beheading. So Abd al-Rahman said: God said: O Messenger of God, except for Suhayl ibn Bayda, for I heard him mention Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent. I have never seen myself more afraid of stones falling from the sky on me than that day, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Except for Suhayl ibn Bayda. Then God revealed: It is not for a prophet to have captives the verse. Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ali, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the captives on the day of Badr: If you wish, kill them, and if you wish, ransom them and enjoy the ransom, and martyrs from among you were martyred in their number. The last of the seventy was Thabit ibn Qays, who was martyred at Yamamah.” Abd al-Razzaq narrated in his Musannaf and Ibn Abi Shaybah on the authority of Ubaydah, something similar. Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “When the captives were taken prisoner on the day of Badr, Al-Abbas was among those he captured. A man from the Ansar had captured him and the Ansar had promised to kill him. This reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I did not sleep last night because of my uncle Al-Abbas, and the Ansar claimed that they had killed him. Umar said to him: Should I go to them? He said: Yes, so Omar came to the Ansar and said: Send Al-Abbas, they said: No, by God, we will not send him, so Omar said to them: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is pleased, they said: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is pleased, then take him, so Omar took him, and when he was in his hand he said to him: O Abbas, convert to Islam, for by God, if you convert to Islam, it is more beloved to me than Al-Khattab converting to Islam, and that was only because I saw that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with your conversion, he said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr said: Your clan, so send them, so he consulted Omar and said: Kill them, so the Messenger of God ransomed them, and God revealed: "It is not for a prophet to have captives" [al-Ansari], the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: "Until he makes slaughter in the land" meaning until they prevail on the earth. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid who said: slaughter is killing. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: Then the permission was revealed after, if you wish So whoever, if you wish, then ransom. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Qatada, “You desire the worldly goods,” he said: The companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted ransom on the day of Badr, so they ransomed them with four thousand, four thousand. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah, You desire the worldly goods, he said: The tax. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement, Had it not been for a previous decree from God, he said: Forgiveness had already been given to them. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Saeed ibn Jubayr, he said: What preceded the people of Badr of happiness. Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, he said: Mercy from God preceded them before they committed the sin. Abu Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, he said: It preceded that no one would be punished until it was made clear to him and he came forward to him.
8:70: The difference in the readers’ opinions about prisoners and captives is here as it was mentioned in the verse before this one. God addressed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with this: That is, say to these prisoners who are in your hands, whom you captured on the day of Badr and took ransom from them. 70- If God knows good in your hearts of good faith, righteousness of intention, and sincerity of heart He will give you better than what was taken from you of ransom: that is, He will compensate you in this world with a provision better than it, and more beneficial to you, or in the Hereafter with what He writes for you of reward for righteous deeds and forgive you your sins and God is Forgiving and Merciful His nature is to forgive His servants and have mercy on them.
8:71: And when he mentioned what he mentioned about the compensation for the one who knows good in his heart, he mentioned those who are the opposite of that from them, so he said: 71- And if they intend to betray you with what they said to you with their tongues that they have believed in you and confirmed you, and that was not from them out of a correct resolve and pure intention, but rather it is deceit and trickery, then that is not unlikely from them, for they have done something greater than that, which is that they betrayed God before you defeated them, so they disbelieved in Him and fought His Messenger, so He prevailed over them by giving you victory over them on the day of Badr, so you killed from them those you killed and took captive those you took captive, and God is Knowing of what is in their hearts, Wise in His actions toward them. Al-Hakim narrated, and Al-Bayhaqi authenticated it in his Sunan, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “When the people of Mecca sent to ransom their prisoners, Zainab, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to ransom Abu Al-Aas, and she sent with him a necklace.
