When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw her, he felt pity for her and said: If you see fit to release her prisoner for her, Al-Abbas said: I was a Muslim, O Messenger of God. He said: God knows best about your Islam, so if you are as you say, then God will reward you. Ransom yourself, your two nephews, Nawfal bin Al-Harith, and Aqeel bin Abi Talib, and your ally, Utbah bin Amr. He said: I do not have that, O Messenger of God. He said: Where is the money that you and Umm Al-Fadl buried? I said to her: If you find it, this money will be for my sons? He said: By God, O Messenger of God, this is something that no one but me and her knows about. So calculate for me what you have found from me, twenty ounces of money that I had with me. He said: I will not do that. So he ransomed himself, his two nephews, and his ally, and this verse was revealed: ‘Say to those who are in your hands of the captives. ’” The verse, so he gave me instead of the twenty ounces in Islam twenty slaves, all of whom had money in their hands to strike with, along with what I hope for from God’s forgiveness.” Ibn Saad and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abu Musa, “that Al-Ala’ bin Al-Hadrami sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, money from Bahrain, eighty thousand, and no money greater than that came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he spread it.” On a mat, and the people came and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to give them, and there was no number or weight at that time, so Al-Abbas came and said: O Messenger of God, I have been given my ransom and the ransom of Aqeel on the day of Badr, give me some of this money, so he said: Take it, so he threw it in his cloak and then went to leave but could not, so he raised his head and said: O Messenger of God, lift it up to me, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled and left while saying: As for one of the two things that God promised, we have fulfilled and we do not know what will happen with the other one, “Say to those in your hands of the captives, ‘If God knows in your hearts any good, He will give you better than what was taken from you and forgive you. ’ This is better than what was taken from me, and I do not know what will happen with forgiveness.” There are many narrations on this subject. Ibn Saad and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: It was revealed regarding the captives on the day of Badr, among them Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, Nawfal bin Al-Harith, and Aqeel bin Abi Talib. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And if they intend to betray you, if their statement was a lie. They betrayed God before they disbelieved and fought you so God gave you power over them.
8:72: God the Almighty concluded this Surah by mentioning loyalty so that each group would know its guardian whom it seeks help from. He the Almighty called the emigrants to Medina by this name because they left their homelands and departed from them in search of what is with God, and in response to His call. And those who gave shelter and aided are the Ansar. The reference in His saying: those is to the first and last relative pronoun, which is the subject and its predicate is the sentence mentioned after it. It is possible that some of them is a substitute for the demonstrative pronoun, and the predicate is guardians of one another meaning some of them are guardians of one another in support and assistance. It was said that the meaning is: some of them are guardians of one another in inheritance. They used to inherit from one another through emigration and aid, then that was abrogated by His saying the Almighty: And those of kinship are more worthy of one another. His saying: And those who believe is the subject, and its predicate is You have no part in their guardianship. Yahya bin Waththab, Al-A’mash, and Hamzah read from their guardianship with a kasra on the waw. The rest read it with the fat-ha: meaning, what do you have of their support and assistance, or of their inheritance, even if they were from your relatives because they did not emigrate, until they emigrate, so they will have what the first group had, who combined faith and emigration. And if they seek your aid, meaning those who believed but did not emigrate if they asked you to aid them against the polytheists, then upon you is aid, meaning it is obligatory upon you to aid, unless, they seek your aid against a people between whom and you there is a treaty, so do not aid them and do not break the treaty between you and those people until its term expires. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible, and upon you is aid, in the accusative case, for the purpose of enticement.
8:73: His statement: 73- "And those who disbelieve is a subject and its predicate is some of them are allies of one another" meaning some of them support others and take care of them in their affairs, or inherit from them if they die, and in it is an allusion to the Muslims that they do not support the disbelievers nor take them as allies. His statement: "If you do not do it the pronoun refers to what they were commanded to do before this of befriending the believers and supporting them in the aforementioned detail, and leaving the befriending of the disbelievers there will be a trial on earth meaning a trial will occur if you do not do that and great corruption meaning a great corruption in religion and the world.
8:74: Then the Almighty explained another ruling related to the believing emigrants who struggled in the way of God and the believers who sheltered those who emigrated to them and supported them, and they are the Ansar. He said: 74- Those are the true believers, meaning those who are complete in faith. This is not a repetition of what came before it, as it was mentioned in praise of these people, and the first was mentioned in requiring loyalty and support. Then the Almighty informed that for them from Him is forgiveness for their sins in the Hereafter, and for them in this world is a generous provision, free from turbidity, good and delicious.
8:75: Then the Almighty informed that whoever migrated after their migration and fought with the first mujahideen and the Ansar is from among them: that is, from among the first emigrants and the Ansar in deserving what they deserved of loyalty and support and perfect faith and forgiveness and generous provision. Then the Almighty explained that the relatives are more deserving of each other than others who do not have a kinship between them in inheritance, and what is meant by them are the relatives so it includes all kinship, and it was said that what is meant by them here are the agnates, they said: And from this is the saying of the Arabs: And a kinship has connected you, for they do not mean the kinship of the mother. They said: And from this is the saying of Qatilah: The swords of his father's sons kept attacking him. God has wombs there that are cracked. It is not hidden from you that there is nothing in this that prevents it from being applied to other than agnates. This verse has been used as evidence by those who have established the inheritance of uterine relatives, who are neither agnates nor those with a share according to the terminology of the people of inheritance knowledge. The disagreement on this is well-known and established in its places. It has been said that this verse abrogates inheritance by loyalty and support according to those who interpreted what came before from His saying: Some of them are allies of others and what follows it as inheritance. As for those who interpreted it as support and assistance, they make this verse a statement from Him, the Most High, that relatives are more worthy of others in the Book of God meaning in His ruling or in the Preserved Tablet or in the Qur’an. Inheritance is included in this priority as a primary inclusion due to the existence of its cause, I mean kinship. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things. Nothing is hidden from Him, whatever it may be. Among that is what these verses include. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Those who believed and emigrated the verse, he said: The believers were in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in three ranks, among them the believing emigrant who was separated from his people, and in his statement: And those who gave shelter and aided he said: They gave shelter and aided and declared what the people of emigration declared and brandished swords against those who lied and denied, so these are two believers whom God made allies of each other, and in his statement: And those who believed and did not emigrate he said: They inherited from each other if the believing emigrant died by virtue of guardianship in religion, and the one who believed but did not emigrate did not inherit because he did not emigrate or aid, so God absolved the believing emigrants from their inheritance, and it is the guardianship that He said: “You have no share in their guardianship until they emigrate. And if they seek help of you in religion, then you must aid them, except against a people between you and whom there is a treaty.” It was the right of the believers who gave shelter and aided, if they sought help from them in religion, to aid them if they were fought, unless they sought help from them. On a people between whom and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, there is a covenant, so they have no victory over them except against an enemy with whom they have no covenant. Then God revealed after that that He would join every relative with his relative from the believers who believed, and those who believed but did not emigrate, so He made for every person from the believers a prescribed share, based on His saying: And those of kinship are nearer to one another, the verse. And in a narration by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: Those are allies of one another, he said: meaning in inheritance, God made the inheritance for the Muhajireen and Ansar without the relatives. And those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no right to their guardianship in anything, you have no right to their inheritance in anything, “until they emigrate. And if they seek help from you in religion,” meaning if the Muslim Bedouins seek help from the Muhajireen and Ansar against an enemy of theirs, then it is upon them to help them except against a people between whom and you there is a covenant. So they worked on that until God revealed this verse: And those of kinship are nearer to one another, so the verse before it was abrogated, and the inheritances became for those of kinship. Abu Ubaid, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding these verses, saying: The emigrant did not take the Bedouin as his guardian or inherit from him while he was a believer, and the Bedouin did not inherit from the emigrant, so this verse abrogated it: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the ordinance of God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority, saying: A man from the Muslims said: We will inherit from our relatives among the polytheists, so this verse was revealed: “And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption.” Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, on the authority of Jarir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The emigrants are allies of one another in this world and the hereafter, and the freed slaves of Quraysh and the freed slaves of Thaqeef are allies of one another in this world and the hereafter. Al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Usamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: People of two religions do not inherit from each other, and a Muslim does not inherit from an unbeliever, nor an unbeliever from a Muslim. Then he recited: And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim narrated, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Az-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam, who said: God revealed concerning us, the Quraysh, in particular: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God. That was because when we, the Quraysh, arrived in Madinah, we arrived without any wealth, and we found the Ansar to be excellent brothers. So we made them brothers and inherited from them, and they made us brothers. Abu Bakr made Kharijah bin Zaid a brother, and Umar made so-and-so a brother, and Uthman bin Affan made a brother of a man from Banu Zuraiq bin Saad Al-Zuraqi. Az-Zubayr said: I made Ka’b bin Malik a brother, and they inherited from us, and we made them inherit from them. Then, on the day of Uhud, it was said to me: Your brother Ka’b bin Malik has been killed. So I went to him and moved to him, and I found that the weapon was heavy, as he could see. By God, my son, if he had died on that day for this world, no one would have inherited him except me, until God revealed this verse about us, the Quraysh and the Ansar, and we returned to our inheritance. Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi, At-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made his companions brothers, and they inherited from each other, until this verse was revealed: And those of kinship are nearer to one another. So they abandoned that and inherited by lineage.
9:1: It is one hundred and thirty verses, and it was said one hundred and twenty-seven verses, and it has names: one of them is Surat At-Tawbah, because it contains repentance for the believers, and it is called Al-Fadihah because it kept revealing: And from them, and from them until it almost left no one, and it is called Al-Buhuth because it searches for the secrets of the hypocrites, and it is called Al-Mubthara, and Al-Bathara Al-Bahth, and it is also called by other names such as Al-Muqashshasha, because it denies hypocrisy: that is, it disavows it, and Al-Mukhziyya because it disgraces the hypocrites, and Al-Muthir because it excavates their secrets, and Al-Hafir because it digs for them, and Al-Munkala because it contains torment for them, and Al-Mumdamma because it rumbles over them. It is Madani. Al-Qurtubi said: By consensus. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Bara’ah was revealed after the conquest of Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: Surat At-Tawbah was revealed in Medina. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr something similar. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah something similar as well. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Ad-Durais, Ibn Al-Mundhir, An-Nahhas, Abu Al-Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ who said: The last verse to be revealed was: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not yet descendants.” And the last complete Surah is Bara’ah. Scholars have differed about the reason for the omission of the Basmala from the beginning of the verse. The first: According to Al-Mubarrad and others: It was the custom of the Arabs that if there was a covenant between them and a people, if they wanted to break it, they would write a letter to them and not write the Basmala in it. So when Bara’ah was revealed about the breaking of the covenant that was between the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the polytheists, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent it to Ali ibn Abi Talib, who read it to them and did not write the Basmala in it, as was the custom of the Arabs. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I asked Ali ibn Abi Talib, why is it not written in Bara’ah, In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful? He said: Because In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful is a guarantee. Bara’ah was revealed by the sword. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi - who authenticated it - Al-Nasa'i and Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: I said to Uthman ibn Affan: What made you choose Al-Anfal, which is from the Mathani, and Bara'ah, which is from the Mi'in, and pair them together and did not write between them a line saying In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful and put them among the seven long ones? Uthman said: The time would come upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and surahs of many numbers would be revealed to him. Whenever something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who used to write and say: Put these verses in the surah in which such and such is mentioned. Al-Anfal was among the first of what was revealed in Madinah, and Bara'ah was among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed. Its story was similar to its story, so I thought it was from it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away without explaining to us that it was from it, so for that reason I paired them together and did not write between them a line saying In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful and put them among the seven long ones. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Raja' that he said: I asked Al-Hasan about Al-Anfal and Bara'ah, were they two surahs or one surah? He said: Two surahs. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah who said: They call this Surah At-Tawbah, but it is the Surah of torment. These narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said about this Surah: It is the disgrace that has not ceased to be revealed, and from them until we thought that none of us would remain except mentioned in it. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Umar. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam that a man said to Abdullah ibn Umar: Surah At-Tawbah, so Ibn Umar said: Which of them is Surah At-Tawbah? Then he said: Has anything done to people other than it? We used to call it nothing but Al-Muqashqashah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: They call it Surah At-Tawbah, but it is a Surah of torment. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq who said: Bara’ah was called Al-Mubtahthrah during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and after him because of what was revealed of the secrets of the people. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ubaidullah ibn Ubaid ibn Umair who said: Bara’ah was called Al-Munqarah, it revealed what was in the hearts of the polytheists. Abu Ubaid, Saeed bin Mansour, Abu Al-Sheikh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shaab narrated on the authority of Abu Atiyah Al-Hamadani who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab wrote: Learn Surah Bara’ah and teach your women Surah An-Nur. Among the opinions about deleting the Basmalah is that it was equal to Surah Al-Baqarah or close to it, and that when the beginning of it was dropped, the Basmalah was dropped. This was narrated on the authority of Malik bin Anas and Ibn Ajlan. Among the opinions about dropping the Basmalah is that when they wrote the Qur’an during the caliphate of Uthman, the companions differed. Some of them said: Bara’ah and Al-Anfal are one Surah, and some of them said: They are two Surahs, so a space was left between them according to the opinion of those who said they are two Surahs, and I left out Bismillah Al-Rahman Al-Raheem according to the opinion of those who said they are one Surah, so both groups agreed. This was said by Kharijah, Abu Usmah and others. The opinion of those who made them one Surah is more apparent, because they are both about fighting, and they are both considered the seventh of the seven long Surahs. His saying: 1- Disclaimer from God and His Messenger I am innocent of something, I am innocent of it, and I am innocent of it: if you remove it from yourself and cut off the reason between you and it, and disclaimer is raised as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning this is disclaimer, and it is permissible for it to be raised as the subject because it is an indefinite described, and the predicate is to those with whom you have made a treaty. Isa bin Omar read disclaimer in the accusative case, assuming listen to disclaimer, or assuming commit to disclaimer, because it contains the meaning of enticement, and from in his saying: from God for the beginning of the goal is related to an omitted word that occurred as an attribute: meaning a connection from God and His Messenger to those with whom you have made a treaty. Ruh and Zaid read with the accusative of His Messenger, and the rest read with the nominative case. The covenant: the contract secured by an oath. The address in you made a covenant is to the Muslims, and they had made a covenant with the polytheists of Mecca and others with the permission of God and the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning is: informing the Muslims that God and His Messenger have disavowed that covenant because of the breach that the infidels had committed, so it became obligatory for the Muslims who had made a covenant to abandon it. The meaning of God’s disavowal is that permission from Him, may He be glorified, for the Muslims to abandon the covenant with the polytheists after they had broken it. In that there is an exaggeration of the importance of disavowal and an exaggeration of it and a recording of humiliation and disgrace upon the polytheists, which is not hidden.
9:2: His saying: 2- And travel freely in the land for four months. This is a command from Him, the Most High, to travel after informing of that innocence. Travel means walking. It is said: So-and-so traveled in the land, traveling, traveling, and traveling. From this comes the flow of water in the land and the flow of horses. From this comes the saying of Tarafa bin al-Abd: If I was afraid of this from you, you wouldn't have gotten to me until you saw horses galloping in front of me. The meaning of the verse is that after God, the Exalted, permitted the polytheists to abandon their covenant, He permitted the polytheists to travel the earth and go wherever they wanted and prepare for war during these four months. The command to travel does not mean that they are obligated to do so. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others said: The polytheists are of two types: One type whose covenant period was less than four months, so they were given a full four months, and the other type whose covenant period was longer than that, so they were limited to four months to explore for themselves. After that, it is war for God, His Messenger, and the believers, and they are killed wherever they are found. The beginning of this period is the day of the greater pilgrimage and its end is until the tenth of Rabi` al-Akhir. As for those who did not have a covenant, their period is only the end of the sacred months, which is fifty days: the twentieth of Dhul-Hijjah and the month of Muharram. Al-Kalbi said: The four months were only for those who had a treaty with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of less than four months. And whoever had a treaty of more than that, then he is the one whom God commanded to complete his treaty with, by His saying: Then fulfill their treaty with them until their term. This was preferred by Ibn Jarir and others. And what will come at the end of the research from the narration will clarify the meaning of the verse: And know that you will not cause failure to God. That is, know that this respite is not due to inability, but for the benefit of those who repent, so that those who repent will repent. And in that there is a kind of threat, as if it were said: Do during this period everything you can of preparing tools and equipment, for you will not escape God, and He will disgrace you: that is, He will humiliate and humiliate you in this world by killing and captivity, and in the Hereafter by torment. And in placing the apparent in place of the implicit, there is an indication that the reason for this disgrace is disbelief, and it is possible that what is meant is the type of disbelievers, so that those addressed are included in it primarily.
9:3: His statement: 3- And an announcement from God and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage. The statement of and an announcement is raised as the predicate of a deleted subject, or as the subject whose predicate is what comes after it, as was mentioned previously in the raising of innocence. This sentence is conjoined with the sentence innocence from God and His Messenger. Al-Zajjaj said: His statement, and an announcement is conjoined with his statement innocence. It was objected to him that if the matter were thus, the call to prayer would have been reported in the first report, which is to those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty, and that is not correct. Rather, the report is to the people, and the call to prayer means notification, which is informing, just as security and giving mean faith and giving. The meaning of his saying, to the people, is generalization in this: that is, it is a call from God to all people, not specific to one people rather than another. So this sentence includes the report of the obligation to inform all people, and the first sentence includes the report of innocence to those with whom you have made a treaty in particular, and the day of Hajj is a circumstance for his saying and the call to prayer, and he described it as the greatest because the people gather on it, or because most of the actions of Hajj are on it. Scholars differed in specifying this day mentioned in the verse. A group of them, including Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abi Awfa, Al-Mughirah ibn Shuba and Mujahid, said that it is the Day of Sacrifice, and Ibn Jarir preferred it. Others, including Umar, Ibn Abbas and Tawus, said that it is the Day of Arafah. The first is more likely, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the one he sent to convey this to the polytheists to convey it to them on the Day of Sacrifice. His statement, God is free from the polytheists and so is His Messenger was read with a fatha on the estimation that God is free from the polytheists, so the ba was deleted for ease. It was read with a kasra on the izhaan because there is a meaning of saying, and the elevation of His Messenger is based on the fact that it is conjoined with the position of the name of an, or on the pronoun in bare’, or on the fact that it is a subject and its predicate is deleted, and the estimation is: and His Messenger is free from them. Al-Hasan and others read and His Messenger in the accusative case in conjunction with the wording of the name of an. And it was read, and His Messenger, in the accusative case, on the basis that the waw is for swearing. This was narrated from Al-Hasan, and it is a very weak reading, since there is no meaning to swearing by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, here, with what has been proven of the prohibition of swearing by other than God. It was said that it is in the accusative case due to proximity. His statement, If you repent, meaning from disbelief, and in it is a shift from the third person to the second person. It was said: The benefit of this shift is to increase the threat, and the pronoun in His statement, Then it refers to the repentance understood from you repent, is better for you than what you are in of disbelief. But if you turn away, meaning if you turn away from repentance and remain in disbelief, then know that you will not escape God, meaning you will not escape Him, rather He will overtake you and reward you for your deeds. His statement, And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment, this is mockery of them, and in it is a threat that is not hidden. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty to the people of the treaty, Khuza’ah, Mudlij, and whoever had a treaty before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Tabuk when he finished it and wanted to perform Hajj. Then he said: There will be polytheists who will come to the House and will circumambulate naked, so I do not want to perform Hajj until that does not happen. So he sent Abu Bakr and Ali, and they circumambulated the people in Dhu al-Majaz, and in their places where they used to sell, or in the entire season. They gave permission to the people of the treaty to be safe for four months, which are the sacred months that are consecutive, twenty from the end of Dhu al-Hijjah to the tenth of Rabi’ al-Akhir. Then there is no treaty left, and he gave permission to all the people to fight until they die. Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal narrated in Zawa’id al-Musnad, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali who said: When ten verses of Bara’ah were revealed about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he called Abu Bakr to recite them to the people of Mecca. Then he called me and said to me: Catch up, Abu Bakr, and wherever you meet him, take the letter from him and recite it to the people of Mecca. So I caught up with him and took the letter from him, and Abu Bakr returned and said: O Messenger of God, has something been revealed about me? He said: No, but Gabriel came to me and said: No one will deliver it on your behalf except you or a man from you. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Anas. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas as well. Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: I was with Ali when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent him to the people of Mecca with the declaration of innocence. We were calling out that none shall enter Paradise except a believer and that no one shall circumambulate the House naked. Whoever has a treaty with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), his term and duration shall be four months. When the four months have passed, then God and His Messenger are free from the polytheists, and no polytheist shall perform Hajj to this House after this year. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: Abu Bakr sent me on that pilgrimage with the muezzins whom he had sent on the Day of Sacrifice to announce in Mina that no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year and no one shall circumambulate the House naked. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Ali ibn Abi Talib behind him and ordered him to announce the declaration of innocence. So Ali announced on the Day of Sacrifice the declaration of innocence that no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year and no one shall circumambulate the House naked. Al-Tirmidhi narrated with a hasan chain of transmission, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Abu Bakr and ordered him to proclaim these words. Then he sent Ali after him and ordered him to proclaim these words. They set out and performed Hajj. Ali stood up during the days of Tashreeq and called out: God is free from the polytheists and so is His Messenger. Travel freely throughout the land for four months. No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year. No one shall circumambulate the House naked. No one shall enter Paradise except a believer. So Ali kept calling out, and when he became exhausted, Abu Bakr would stand up and call out these words. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Al-Mundhir, An-Nahhas, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated with Zaid ibn Tabi' who said: I asked Ali: What was I sent with Abu Bakr on Hajj? He said: I was sent with four things: No one shall enter Paradise except a believing soul. No one shall circumambulate the House naked. A believer and a disbeliever shall not meet in the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. And whoever has a treaty with the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), his treaty shall last for its term, and whoever has no treaty, his term shall be four months. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God, a declaration of freedom from God and His Messenger 2:100, that God set a limit for those who made a treaty with His Messenger of four months in which they may travel wherever they wish, and He set a limit for those who have no treaty as the expiration of the four sacred months from the Day of Sacrifice until the expiration of Muharram, fifty nights. When the sacred months have passed, He commands him to put the sword to the sword against those who made a treaty if they do not enter Islam, and he breaks the treaty and covenant that was named for them, and he removes the first condition, except those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque, meaning the people of Mecca. An-Nahhas narrated something similar to this from him, and he said: And the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) did not make a treaty with anyone after this. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Nahhas narrated on the authority of al-Zuhri, And travel freely throughout the land for four months. He said: It was revealed in Shawwal, so they are the four months: Shawwal, Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement, And an announcement from God and His Messenger, he said: It is an announcement from God and His Messenger. At-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the greatest day of Hajj, and he said: The Day of Sacrifice. Ibn Abi Shaybah, At-Tirmidhi and Abu al-Shaykh narrated it on his authority. Abu Dawud, An-Nasa’i and Al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Qart, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The greatest day before God is the Day of Sacrifice, then the Day of Qarr. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Awfa, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: This Day of Sacrifice is the greatest day of Hajj. Al-Bukhari narrated in a suspended form, as did Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Sheikh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Naim in al-Hilya, on the authority of Ibn Umar: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood between the Jamarat on the Day of Sacrifice during the Hajj that he performed and said: ‘What day is this? ’ They said: ‘The Day of Sacrifice. ’ He said: ‘This is the greater day of Hajj. ’” Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: Abu Bakr sent me among those who would announce on the Day of Sacrifice in Mina that no polytheist should perform Hajj after this year, and that no one should circumambulate the House naked. The greater day of Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice, and the greater Hajj is the Hajj. It was only called the greater because people say the lesser Hajj. Abu Bakr announced to the people that year, so no polytheist performed Hajj in the year of the Farewell Hajj in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj. God revealed in the year that Abu Bakr announced to the polytheists: O you who have believed, indeed, the polytheists are unclean (al-Baqarah 2:17). Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub that the Messenger of God said at the time of the conquest: This is the year of the greater pilgrimage. He said: “The pilgrimage of the Muslims and the pilgrimage of the polytheists will be held on three consecutive days, and the Christians and Jews will be held on three consecutive days. So the pilgrimage of the Muslims, the polytheists, the Christians and the Jews will be held on six consecutive days. It has not been held like this since the creation of the heavens and the earth before this year, and it will not be held after this year until the Hour comes.” Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan that he was asked about the day of the greater pilgrimage, and he said: What do you have to do with the greater pilgrimage? That was the year in which Abu Bakr performed the pilgrimage and the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) appointed him as his successor, so he led the people in pilgrimage. The Muslims and polytheists gathered on it, and that is why it was called the greater pilgrimage. It coincided with the festival of the Jews and Christians. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The greater pilgrimage is the second day of the Day of Sacrifice. Did you not see that the imam delivers the sermon on it? Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: This is the day of Arafah, the day of the greater pilgrimage. Ibn Saad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: The greater pilgrimage is the day of Arafah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu al-Suhaiba al-Bakri who said: I asked Ali ibn Abi Talib about the greater day of pilgrimage and he said: The day of Arafah. Abu Ubaid, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The day of Arafah is the greater day of pilgrimage. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of al-Zubayr. It is not hidden from you that the hadiths that were reported about the Day of Sacrifice being the greater day of Hajj are proven in the two Sahihs and others through their chains of transmission, so these narrations that explicitly state that it is the Day of Arafah are not strong enough to contradict them. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi that he was asked: This is the greater Hajj, so what is the lesser Hajj? He said: Umrah in Ramadan. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: I asked Abdullah bin Shaddad about the greater Hajj and he said: The greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice, and the lesser Hajj is Umrah. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar from Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Mas’ud that he said: Sufyan bin Uyaynah was asked about the good report that comes in times of hardship, so he said: Have you not heard His statement: And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.
9:4: The exception in his saying: 4- Except those with whom you made a treaty. Al-Zajjaj said: It goes back to his saying: Disavowal and the meaning: Disavowal from God and His Messenger to the treaty-holders from the polytheists except those among them who did not break the treaty. He said in Al-Kashshaf: It is an exception from his saying: So go forth and the meaning: So say to them, Go forth except those with whom you made a treaty and then they did not break it with you, so fulfill their treaty with them. He said: The exception means a correction as if it was said after they were ordered regarding the breakers, but those who did not break it, then fulfill their treaty with them and do not treat them as they did. It was objected to that there was a break between the exception and what is excepted from. It is and a declaration from God etc. It was answered that this does not harm because it is not foreign, and it was said: The exception from the polytheists mentioned before it is connected and this is weak. His saying: Then they did not decrease you in the least means they did not decrease anything. And if it was easy, and Ikrimah and Ata bin Yasar read yanqdqukum with the voiced Ḍād: meaning they did not break your covenant, and in it is evidence that there were among the people of the covenant those who broke their covenant, and among them were those who remained on it, so God Almighty permitted His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to break the covenant of those who broke it, and to fulfill the covenant of those who did not break it until its term and they did not support anyone against you support: assistance: meaning they did not support anyone against you from your enemies so complete their covenant with them meaning fulfill their covenant with them completely and not incomplete until their term that you made a covenant with them even if it was more than four months, and do not treat them as those who broke the covenant from fighting after the expiration of the period mentioned previously, which is four months or fifty days according to the previous disagreement.
9:5: His saying: 5- So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. The passing of the month: its completion, part by part, until it ends, like the shedding of skin from what it contains. He likened the departure of something that is timed from its time to the separation of something that is established from its place. Its origin is the shedding that occurs between an animal and its skin, so it was used as a metaphor for the passing of the months. It is said: I peeled the month, I peeled it, I peeled it, I peeled it, meaning I left it. From this is the saying of the poet: If I finish the month, I start the same month. It is enough for me to kill myself by finishing the months and starting them. It is said: A woman stripped her armor: she took it off. In the Qur’an: “And a sign for them is the night. We strip thereof the day.” Scholars differed in identifying the sacred months mentioned here. It was said: They are the well-known sacred months, which are Dhul-Qi'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab: three in a row, and one in a row. The meaning of the verse according to this is the obligation to refrain from fighting those polytheists who do not have a covenant during these sacred months. The call and the announcement of their covenant to the polytheists took place on the Day of Sacrifice, so the remaining sacred months, which are the three in a row, were fifty days, ending with the end of Muharram. So God commanded them to kill the polytheists wherever they were found, and this is what a group of scholars said, including Ad-Dahhak and Al-Baqir. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and chosen by Ibn Jarir. It was said that what is meant by them are the months of the covenant referred to in His statement: Then fulfill their covenant with them until their term and they were called sacred because God, the Almighty, forbade the Muslims in them to shed the blood of the polytheists and to harm them. This is what a group of scholars said, including Mujahid, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Zayd, and Amr ibn Shu'ayb. It was said: They are the months mentioned in His statement: Then travel freely throughout the land for four months. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and a group, and Ibn Kathir preferred it. He narrated it on the authority of Mujahid, Amr ibn Shuaib, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. The ruling on fighting during the sacred months that occur every year will be explained in this Surah, God willing. The meaning of wherever you find them is wherever you find them, whether in the sacred or non-sacred areas. The meaning of take them is captivity, as the captive is the prisoner. The meaning of confinement is preventing them from moving around in the lands of the Muslims except with their permission. The watchtower is the place where the enemy is watched. It is said: I watched so-and-so, I watched him, meaning I watched him, meaning lie in wait for them in the places where you watch them. Amir ibn At-Tufayl said: I knew, and I think you do not know, that death lies in wait for a young man. Al-Nabigha said: O critics, ignorance is a pleasure for youth, and death is an ambush for souls. And every word in every watchtower is in the accusative case as a circumstance, and this is the choice of Al-Zajjaj. It was said that it is in the accusative case by removing the preposition: i.e. in every watchtower. Abu Ali Al-Farisi Al-Zajjaj made a mistake in making it a circumstance. This verse, which includes the command to kill the polytheists when the sacred months have passed, is general for every polytheist, and only those who are specifically mentioned in the Sunnah are excluded from it, and they are women, children, and the disabled who do not fight. Likewise, the People of the Book who pay the jizyah are specifically mentioned, assuming that the word polytheists includes them. This verse abrogated every verse that mentioned turning away from the polytheists and being patient with their harm. Ad-Dahhak, Ata’, and As-Suddi said: It was abrogated by His statement: Then either by favor afterwards or by ransom, and that the prisoner is not killed in patience, but rather he is shown favor or ransomed. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Rather, it abrogates it by His statement: Then either by favor afterwards or by ransom, and that nothing is permissible for the prisoners of polytheism except killing. Ibn Zayd said: The two verses are decisive. Al-Qurtubi said: It is correct because the killing, killing and ransom were the rulings of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) regarding them from the first war he brought them, which was the day of Badr. His statement: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah means if they repent from the polytheism that was the reason for the killing and they truly repent by doing what is one of the greatest pillars of Islam, which is establishing prayer. This pillar was sufficient for him to mention the acts of worship related to the body because it is its head, and he was sufficient with the other financial pillar, which is giving zakah for all acts of worship related to money because it is the greatest of them. Then let them go means leave them alone, do not capture them, besiege them or kill them. Indeed, God is Forgiving to them, Merciful to them.
9:6: His saying: 6- And if one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection. It is said: I sought protection from so-and-so: meaning I asked him to be a neighbor: a protector and a protector from being wronged by an oppressor, or from being exposed to an attacker, and one is raised by an implied action that is explained by the one mentioned after it: meaning if one seeks your protection, then he has protected you, and they disliked combining the interpreter and the interpreted, and the meaning is: If one of the polytheists whom you were ordered to fight seeks your protection, then grant him protection: meaning be a neighbor to him, a believer and a protector until he hears the word of God from you and contemplates it properly, and understands the truth of what you are calling for then take him to his place of safety meaning to the house in which he is safe after he hears the word of God if he does not submit, then after you take him to his place of safety, fight him, for he has left your protection and returned to what he was upon of permitting his blood, and the obligation to kill him wherever he is, and the reference in his saying: that is to what came before from the command to grant protection and what comes after it "that they are a people who do not They know, that is, because they lack the beneficial knowledge that distinguishes between good and evil in the present and the future. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Except those with whom you made a treaty, he said: They are Quraysh. He also narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh with whom the Prophet of God made a treaty at the time of Hudaybiyyah, and there were four months left of their term after the Day of Sacrifice, so he ordered his Prophet to fulfill this treaty until their term. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Ja`far regarding his statement: Except those with whom you made a treaty, he said: They are Banu Juthaymah ibn `Amir from Banu Bakr ibn Kinanah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Then fulfill their treaty with them until their term, he said: There was a treaty left for Banu Madhhij and Khuza`ah, so it is that which God said: Then fulfill their treaty with them until their term. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: Except for those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty, he said: These are Banu Damrah and Banu Mudlij from Banu Kinanah, who were allies of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Al-Ushayrah from the tribe of Yanbu. Then they did not fail you in the least, then they did not fail you in the least, by treachery, nor did they support anyone against you, he said: They did not support your enemy against you. Then fulfill their treaty with them until their term, he said: The term you stipulated for them. Indeed, God loves the righteous, he said: Those who fear God in what He has forbidden them, so they fulfill their treaty. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not make a treaty with anyone after these verses. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: Then when the sacred months have passed, he said: They are the four: the twenty of Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi’ al-Awwal, and the tenth of Rabi’ al-Akhir. I said: Al-Suddi meant that these months are called sacred because the security of those with whom a treaty is made during them necessitates the prohibition of fighting, not that they are the well-known sacred months. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding the verse, saying: They are ten of Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, seventy nights. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, saying: They are the four months of which He said: "So travel freely throughout the land for four months." Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah something similar to the previous statement of As-Suddi. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: "So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them," then it was abrogated and an exception was made. He said: "But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way," and he said: "And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the Word of God." Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: "And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection," he said: Whoever comes to you and listens to what you say and listens to what was revealed to you, he is safe when he comes to you and hears the Word of God until he reaches his place of safety from where he came. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: Then escort him to his place of safety, he said: If what he is told and informed about does not agree with him, then escort him to his place of safety. This is not abrogated. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Until he hears the Word of God, meaning the Book of God. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah who said: A man would come if he heard the Book of God and acknowledged it and became a Muslim, then that is what he was called to. If he denied it and did not acknowledge it, he was returned to his place of safety. Then that was abrogated and He said: And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together.
9:7: His saying: 7- How can the polytheists have a covenant with God and with His Messenger? The question here is for astonishment that includes denial, and covenant is the name of to be. There are three aspects to its predicate: The first: that it is how, and it was presented for questioning, and the second: for the polytheists, and with on these two is a circumstance for the covenant, or for to be, or an attribute of the covenant, and the third: that the predicate is with God, and in the verse there is an omission. Meaning: How can the polytheists have a covenant with God that will secure them from His punishment? It has been said that the meaning of the verse is: It is impossible for a covenant to be established for these people while they are your enemies, intending treachery, so they should not hope for that or think of it in their souls. Then he added, saying: Except those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque. That is, but those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque and did not break it or violate it, then do not fight them. As long as they are upright with you in the treaty between you and them. Then be upright with them. It has been said that they are Banu Bakr, and it has been said that they are Banu Kinanah and Banu Damrah. There are two interpretations: One of them is that it is a temporal source. The second is that it is conditional. In His statement: Indeed, God loves the righteous, there is an indication that fulfilling a covenant and being upright in it are among the deeds of the righteous, so it is a justification for the command to be upright.
9:8: His statement: 8- How, even if they gain the upper hand over you? He repeated the astonishing question for emphasis and confirmation, and the meaning is: How can they have a covenant with God and His Messenger? And the situation is that if they gain the upper hand over you by defeating you, they will not observe, that is, they will not observe in you except: that is, a covenant nor a pledge. He said in Al-Sahah: The pledge is the covenant and kinship, and from it is the saying of Hassan: By your life, you are to the Quraysh like the ostrich's tail is to the ostrich's tail. Al-Zajjaj said: “Il, according to what the language requires, revolves around the meaning of sharpness, and from it is the word ‘ilah’ for a spear, and from it is the word ‘al-mu’allaf’ah’ a sharpened ear, and from it is the saying of Tarafa bin al-Abd describing the ears of his camel as sharp and erect: Two instruments from which the neck is known, like the ears of a sheep with a single hoof Abu Ubaidah said: “Il is the covenant, the pledge, and the companion.” Al-Zuhri said: “It is a name for God in Hebrew, and its origin is from ‘alil, which means brilliance. It is said: ‘al-lunu yul ila’ meaning it became clear and shiny. ‘Dhimmah’ is the covenant, and its plural is ‘dhimmah’. Whoever interprets ‘il’ as the covenant, the repetition is for emphasis, despite the difference in the two words.” Abu Ubaidah said: Dhimmah is the protection. Abu Ubaidah said: “Dhimmah is security, as in the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): ‘And the lowest of them strives to protect their pledge.’” It was also narrated from Abu Ubaidah that the pledge is that which is protected, meaning that which is avoided. His saying: They please you with their mouths means they say with their tongues what is flattering and kind to you, seeking to please you and please your hearts, but their hearts refuse that and swear by it and desire what offends and harms you, as the hypocrites and the two-faced do. Then he ruled that they were immoral, which is rebellion, daring, and deviating from the truth because they broke covenants and did not respect contracts.
9:9: Then he described them by saying: 9- They have exchanged the verses of God for a small price. That is, they exchanged the verses of the Qur’an, which include the command to fulfill covenants, for a small, insignificant price, which is what they preferred from the debris of this world. So they turned away from His path. That is, they deviated and turned away from the path of truth, or they turned others away from it.
9:10: His statement: 10- They do not observe any pact or covenant with regard to a believer. An-Nahhas said: This is not a repetition, but the first is for all polytheists, and the second is for the Jews in particular. The evidence for this is They have purchased with the verses of God a small price meaning the Jews. It was said: This includes consideration of the rights of believers in general, while the first includes consideration of the rights of a group of believers in particular. And those are the transgressors meaning those who go beyond what is permissible to what is forbidden by breaking the covenant, or those who go to the extreme in evil and rebellion.
9:11: 11- If they repent from polytheism and adhere to the rulings of Islam then they are your brothers meaning they are your brothers in religion meaning in the religion of Islam and We detail the verses meaning We explain them and clarify them for a people who know what rulings they contain and understand them, and He singled out the people of knowledge because they are the ones who benefit from them, and what is meant by the verses is what was mentioned of the verses related to the conditions of the polytheists of different types. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Except those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram, he said: Quraysh. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Ibn Zayd. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Muqatil who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a treaty with some people from Banu Damrah, Banu Bakr and Kinanah in particular. He made a treaty with them at al-Masjid al-Haram and made their term four months. They are the ones whom God mentioned: “Except those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram. So long as they are upright with you, be upright with them.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi who said: They are Banu Juthaymah. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: Except those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram, he said: It is the day of al-Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Except and no covenant, he said: The covenant is kinship and the covenant is the covenant. Al-Faryabi, Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The deity is God, the Almighty. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: They have purchased with the signs of God a small price, he said: Abu Sufyan bin Harb fed his allies and left the allies of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: But if they repent, the verse says: If they abandon Al-Lat and Al-Uzza and bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, then they are your brothers in religion. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: This verse forbids fighting or shedding the blood of those who pray.
9:12: His saying: 12- And if they break their covenant is in apposition to if they repent and breaking is breaking, and its origin is breaking the thread after it is tied, then it was used for every breaking, including breaking faith and covenants by way of metaphor. The meaning of after their covenant is after they made a covenant with you. The meaning is that if the infidels break the covenants that they made with the Muslims, and trusted them with them and added to that insulting and disparaging the religion of Islam, then it is obligatory upon the Muslims to fight them, and the leaders of disbelief: the plural of imam, and what is meant is the leaders of the polytheists, and the people of leadership among them in general, and Hamza read a'imamah. Most grammarians believe that this is a mistake, because it combines two hamzas in one word. The majority read by making the second hamza between bayn between bayn: that is, between the point of articulation of the hamza and the ya'. It was read by making the ya' sincere, and this is a mistake. As Al-Zamakhshari said: His saying: They have no oaths this sentence is an explanation of what preceded it: and oaths: the plural of oath according to the reading of the majority. Ibn Amir read They have no oaths with a kasra on the hamza. The meaning according to the reading of the majority is that the oaths of the disbelievers, even if they appear to be oaths, are not in reality an oath. According to the second reading: that these oath-breakers who attack the religion are not among the people of faith in God to the point that they deserve protection for their blood and wealth, so fighting them is obligatory upon the Muslims. His saying: Perhaps they will desist means from their disbelief, their breaking of oaths, and their attacking of the religion of Islam. The meaning is that fighting them will be to the point of ending that. This verse was used as evidence that if a dhimmi attacks the religion, he is not to be killed until he breaks the covenant, as Abu Hanifa said, because God only ordered their killing under two conditions: one of them is the breaking of the covenant, and the second is attacking the religion. Malik, al-Shafi’i, and others held that if he attacks the religion, he is to be killed because his covenant is thus broken. They said: Likewise, if the dhimmi merely breaks the covenant without attacking the religion, then he is to be killed.
9:13: His saying: 13- Will you not fight a people who have broken their oaths? The hamza that comes before the letter of negation is for a question of reproach, along with what is understood from it of incitement to fight and exaggeration in its realization. The meaning is: whoever is in a state like these people in breaking the covenant and expelling the Messenger from Mecca and initiating the fight, then he deserves that his fight not be abandoned, and that whoever neglects that should be rebuked. Then he increased the rebuke and said: Do you fear them? This question is for rebuke and reprimand: that is, you fear that something bad will happen to you from them, so you stop fighting them because of this fear. Then he explained what the matter should be like, and said: Then God is more deserving of your fearing Him, if you are believers. That is, He is more deserving of being feared than you, for He is the One who harms and benefits in truth, and from your fear of Him is that you fight the one who ordered you to fight him, for the issue of faith requires that of you.
9:14: Then he increased the emphasis on the command to fight, saying: 14- Fight them. And he arranged benefits for this command: The first: God's punishment of the infidels at the hands of the believers by killing and capturing them, the second: their humiliation, it was said by captivity, and it was said by what befell them of humiliation and disgrace, the third: the victory of the Muslims over them and their victory over them, and the fourth: that God heals through fighting the hearts of a group of believers who did not witness the fighting or attend it.
9:15: Fifth: That He, glory be to Him, removes through fighting the anger in the hearts of the believers that they have suffered because of the things that caused anger and distress in the chest that the disbelievers did. If it is said: Healing the chests and removing the anger of the hearts both have the same meaning, so it is a repetition, it is said in response: The heart is more specific than the chest, and it is said: Healing the chest is an indication of the promise of conquest, and there is no doubt that waiting for the fulfillment of the promise with trust in it in both is healing for the chest, and removing the anger of the hearts is an indication of the occurrence of the conquest, and praise be to God all of these things have happened to the believers, then He said: And God accepts the repentance of whom He wills and it is the beginning of a statement that includes report of what will happen, which is that some of the disbelievers repent from their disbelief as happened with some of the people of Mecca on the day of the conquest, for they converted to Islam and their conversion was good, and this is according to the reading of the nominative in yatoob, which is the reading of the majority: And it was read with the accusative of yatoob by implying that, and the inclusion of repentance in the whole of what the matter was answered with by way of meaning. Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa Al-Thaqafi and Al-A'raj read this way. If it is said: How does repentance occur as a reward for fighting? The answer is that fighting may be a reason for it if it is on the part of the infidels. However, if it is on the part of the Muslims, then the reason for it is that victory and triumph on the part of God is a reason for purity of intention and repentance from sins.
9:16: His statement: 16- Or do you think that you will be left as you are? This am is the disconnected particle that means but, and the hamza and the question mark are for rebuke, and the letter of interruption is to indicate the transition from one statement to another. The meaning is: How do you think that you will be left as you are? And his statement: that you will be left is in the position of the two objects of al-hisbān according to Sibawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: The second was deleted, and the meaning is: Or do you think that you will be left without being tested with what appears to the believer and the hypocrite, the appearance by which he deserves reward and punishment? The phrase And God has not yet known those among you who strive is in the accusative case as a state, and what is meant by negating knowledge is negating what is known, and the meaning is how do you think that you will be left without distinguishing the sincere among you in his striving from the non-sincere? The phrase And they did not take is conjoined with struggled and is included with it in the ruling of negation and falls within the scope of the relative clause. The walijah comes from the word waljuh which means entering, and waljuh means entering: if he enters, so the walijah is the intruder. Abu Ubaidah said: Everything that you insert into something that is not from it is a walijah. Abaan bin Tha’lab said: What a miserable refuge for fugitives, aggressors, and suspicious people. Al-Farra’ said: “Al-Walijah is the inner circle of the polytheists, and the meaning is the same: that is, how do you take an inner circle or inner circle of the polytheists to whom you divulge your secrets and teach them your affairs without God? And God is All-Knowing of what you do,” that is, of all your actions. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And if they break their oaths, he said: Their covenant. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: God says to His Prophet: And if they break the covenant that is between you and them, then fight them, for they are the leaders of disbelief. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: The leaders of disbelief, he said: Abu Sufyan bin Harb, Umayyah bin Khalaf, Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham and Suhayl bin Amr, and they are those who broke the covenant of God and intended to expel the Messenger from Mecca. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Malik bin Anas something similar. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then fight the leaders of disbelief, he said: The leaders of Quraysh. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: Abu Sufyan bin Harb is one of them. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that they are the Daylamites. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah that they mentioned this verse and said: The people of this verse have not been fought yet. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ali. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah that he said: There are only three left of the people of this verse, and only four of the hypocrites. A Bedouin said: You are the companions of Muhammad, and you inform us but we do not know, so what is the matter with these who are digging into our houses and stealing our money? He said: Those are the wicked ones. Indeed, there are only four left of them, one of them is an old man who, if he drank cold water, would not find it cold. The first: that the verse is general in all the leaders of the infidels without restricting it to a specific time or a specific group, considering the generality of the wording and not the specificity of the reason. What indicates this is what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr that during the reign of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq when he sent them to the Levant, he said: You will find a people with hollowed-out heads, so strike the seats of Satan among them with swords, for by God, killing one man among them is more beloved to me than killing seventy others, and that is because God says: Fight the leaders of disbelief. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah, They have no oaths, meaning they have no covenants. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ammar. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Will you not fight a people who have broken their oaths? He said: Fighting the Quraysh, the allies of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their intention to expel the Messenger. They claimed that this was the year of the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) Umrah, in the year following Hudaybiyyah. Quraysh broke the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and they made it a point to themselves that if they entered Mecca they would leave it. This was their intention to expel him, but Khuza’ah did not follow them in that. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) left Mecca, Quraysh said to Khuza’ah: You have blinded us from expelling him. So they fought them and killed some of their men. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: Fight them; God will punish them by your hands and disgrace them 1:13 was revealed about Khuza’ah. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of al-Suddi. Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah as well. Ibn Ishaq narrated the story in his biography, and included in it the poem that Khuza’ah sent to the Prophet (peace be upon him), which begins: Oh God, I implore Muhammad by the oath of our father and his father, the Atlda Al-Bayhaqi narrated the story in Al-Dala’il. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Walijah means a close associate of someone other than their religion. Abd Bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: Walijah means betrayal.
9:17: The majority read 17- ya'marowu with the fat-ha of the present tense letter and the damma of the meem from 'Umar ya'mawr. Ibn al-Samee' read with the damma of the present tense letter from 'A'mar ya'mawr: meaning they appoint someone to inhabit it. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn Muhaisin, Sahm, and Ya'qub read Masajid God in the singular. The rest read Masajid in the plural, and Abu Ubaidah chose it. An-Nahhas said: Because it is more general, and the specific is included under the general. It is possible that the plural refers to the Sacred Mosque in particular, and this is permissible in the names of species, as it is said that so-and-so rides horses, even though he only rides a horse. He said: They agreed on the plural in His statement: Only the mosques of God are to be inhabited. It was narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that God Almighty said masajid and what was meant was the Sacred Mosque because it is the qiblah of all mosques and their imam, so the one who inhabits it is like the one who inhabits all mosques. Al-Farra’ said: The Arabs may put the singular in place of the plural, as in their saying: So-and-so has many dirhams, and vice versa, as in their saying: So-and-so sits with kings, and perhaps he only sat with one king. What is meant by construction is either the literal meaning or the metaphorical meaning, which is to stay there and worship in it, and neither of them is for the polytheists. As for the first: because it entails a favor upon the Muslims by constructing their mosques, and as for the second: because the infidels do not have worship, despite their being forbidden from approaching the Sacred Mosque. The meaning of it was not for the polytheists is that it is not correct for them to do that, and bearing witness against themselves of disbelief is a state: that is, it was not for them to do that while they were bearing witness against themselves of disbelief by showing what is disbelief, such as setting up idols and worshipping them and making them gods, for this is a testimony from them against themselves of disbelief even if they refused that with their tongues. So how can they reconcile two contradictory matters: constructing mosques, which is the affair of the believers, and bearing witness against themselves of disbelief, which is not the affair of those who draw near to God by constructing His mosques. It was said: The rebellious one in this testimony is their saying during their circumambulation: “Here I am, You have no partner except a partner who is Yours. You own him and what he owns.” It was said: Their testimony against themselves of disbelief: The Jew says: He is a Jew, the Christian says: He is a Christian, the Sabean says: He is a Sabean, and the polytheist says: He is a polytheist. Their deeds have become worthless, which they boast about and think are good deeds: that is, they have become void and no trace of them remains. And in the Fire they will abide eternally. In this nominal sentence with the presentation of the circumstance related to the report, there is emphasis on its content.
9:18: Then the Almighty explained who is truly worthy of building the mosque, saying: 18- The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day and do what is required of faith, such as establishing prayer and giving zakat and fear no one except God. So whoever combines these attributes is truly worthy of building the mosques, not whoever is devoid of them or some of them. He limited himself to mentioning prayer, zakat, and fear, drawing attention to what is among the greatest matters of religion over what is other than it, which God has made obligatory upon His servants, because all of that is among the requirements of faith. We have already discussed the reason for gathering the mosques and explaining the nature of building, and whoever permits combining the literal and the metaphorical, applies building here to them. In His saying: Perhaps those will be among the guided He puts an end to the desires of the disbelievers to benefit from their actions, for if those described with those attributes are only hoped for, then how about the disbelievers who do not have any of those attributes? It was said that perhaps is obligatory from God, and it was said that it means It is fitting: that is, it is fitting that they be among the guided ones. It was said that hope refers to the servants.
9:19: The question in 19- Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque? is for denial, and the provision of water and maintenance are two sources like striving and protection, and there is an omission in the speech, and the estimate is: Have you made the people who provide water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of the mosque, or their people like those who believe so that the subject and the predicate agree, or the estimate in the report is: that is, you made the provision of water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque like the work of those who believe or like the faith of those who believe. Ibn Abi Wajzah Al-Saadi, Ibn Al-Zubayr, and Saeed Ibn Jubayr read: Have you made the pilgrims’ water-carriers and the Umrah-housers of the Sacred Mosque? The plural of saq and ‘amr. According to this reading, there is no need to estimate an omitted word. The meaning is that God denied them the equality between what the Jahiliyyah used to do of deeds that were depicted as good, even if they did not benefit from them, and the faith of the believers and their jihad in the way of God. The polytheists used to boast about water-carriers and construction and preferred them over the work of the Muslims, so God denied them that. Then He, the Most High, made clear the distinction between the two groups and their differences and their lack of equality, saying: They are not equal in the sight of God. That is, that group of infidels who provide water for the pilgrims and construct the Sacred Mosque are not equal to this group who believe in God and the Last Day and strive in His way. God, the Most High, indicated by denying equality the denial of the virtue that the polytheists claim: that is, if the deeds of the infidels do not reach the point of being equal to the deeds of the Muslims, then how can they be superior to them as they claim? Then He ruled that they were unjust and that they are, with their injustice, because of what they are. It contains polytheism and they do not deserve guidance from God Almighty, and this is an indication of the group.
9:20: Then he stated the virtuous group, saying: 20- Those who believe to the end: meaning those who combine faith, migration, and jihad with money and souls are greater in degree with God and more deserving of what He has of goodness than that polytheistic group that boasts of its surrounding false deeds.
