In His saying: with God there is a great honor for the believers, and the reference in His saying: those to those who are characterized by the aforementioned qualities are the successful ones meaning those who are special in winning with God.
9:21: Then he explained the victory by saying: 21- Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and approval and gardens for them wherein is lasting pleasure. The indefiniteness in mercy, approval, and gardens is for glorification, and the meaning is that they are beyond the description of describers and the imagination of imaginers. And lasting pleasure is the permanent, continuous one that never leaves its owner.
9:22: And the mention of eternity after immortality is an emphasis on it, and the sentence 22 - Indeed, with God is a great reward is an emphasis on what came before it, while it includes the reason: that is, God Almighty gave them these great rewards because the reward with Him is great, and He gives from it whatever He wills to whomever He wills, and He is the possessor of great bounty. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God, and he said: The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day, so he excluded the polytheists from the mosque. Whoever believes in God means: whoever believes in the Oneness of God and believes in what God has revealed, and establishes prayer means the five daily prayers, and fears none but God means: none but God is worshipped, then it is likely that those means: those are the ones who are guided, like his statement to his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is likely that your Lord will raise you to a station of praise, meaning: your Lord will raise you to a station of praise, which is intercession, and every it is likely in the Qur’an is obligatory. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Darimi, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you see a man frequenting the mosques, then bear witness to his faith. God the Almighty said: The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day. Many hadiths have been narrated about the desirability of staying in mosques, maintaining them, and frequenting them for acts of worship. Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, who said: “I was with The pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among a group of his companions. One of them said: I do not care if I do not do any work for God after Islam except providing water to the pilgrims. Another said: Rather, maintaining the Sacred Mosque. Another said: Rather, jihad in the way of God is better than what you have said. Umar rebuked them and said: Do not raise your voices at the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was on a Friday. But when you have prayed the Friday prayer, go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him about what you have differed about. Then God revealed: “Have you made the provision of water to the pilgrims” until His saying: He does not guide the wrongdoing people. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: Have you made the provision of water to the pilgrims the verse. That is because the polytheists said that maintaining the House of God and taking care of the water supply is better than believing and striving. They were proud of the Sacred Mosque and were arrogant about it because they were its people and its maintainers. Then God, the Exalted, mentioned their arrogance and turning away, and said to the people of the Sacred Mosque from the polytheists: “My verses were recited to you So you were turning back on your heels, arrogantly, ignorant of it, and you were devouring it. That is, they were arrogant in the Sacred Sanctuary. He said, “They were devouring it and devouring it with the Qur’an and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.” So the best belief in God and jihad with the Prophet of God is over the polytheists’ construction of the House and their standing up to provide water, and it would not benefit them with God if they were to associate partners with Him, even if they were to provide for His House and serve it. God said, They are not equal in the sight of God, and God does not guide the wrongdoing people. That is, those who claimed that they were the people of construction, so He called them wrongdoers because of their polytheism, so construction did not benefit them at all. In its chain of transmission is Al-Awfi, who is weak. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Abbas said when he was taken prisoner on the day of Badr: If you preceded us in Islam, migration, and jihad, we used to provide water for the pilgrims, and free the captives. Then God revealed, Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims? The verse means that that was in polytheism, so I do not accept what was in polytheism. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: It was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib and Al-Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: Ali, Al-Abbas and Shaiba boasted about providing water and guardianship, so God revealed: Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims? The meaning of this has been narrated through various chains of transmission.
9:23: 23- "O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over faith. And whoever takes them as allies among you - then those are the wrongdoers." The address is to all believers, and it is a ruling that will remain until the Day of Resurrection, indicating the severing of allegiance between believers and disbelievers. A group of scholars said: It was revealed to encourage emigration and reject the lands of disbelief, so the address is to those who were believers in Mecca and other Arab lands. They were forbidden to take allegiance to fathers and brothers, so that they would be their followers in residing in the lands and disbelief if they preferred: that is, they loved, as it is said: he responded with the meaning of he answered, and it is originally a request for love. The investigation of the matter has already been presented in Surat Al-Ma'idah in the Almighty's saying: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. Then he ruled that whoever takes allegiance to those who preferred disbelief over faith from among fathers and brothers is unjust, so this indicates that taking allegiance to someone who is like that is one of the greatest and most severe sins.
9:24: Then God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them: 24- If your fathers to the end, and the clan: the group that goes back to one contract, and the clan of a man is his closest relatives, and they are those who live with him and it is a collective noun. Abu Bakr and Hammad read your clan in the plural. Al-Akhfash said that the Arabs hardly collect clan as clans, but rather collect them as clans. Al-Hasan read your clan. The rest read your clan. And the acquisition: is the acquisition, and its origin is the cutting off of something from its place, and the construction revolves around the proximity, and the earner brings the thing close to himself and brings it under his ownership, and trade is the goods that they buy to profit from it, and the recession is the lack of hypocrisy due to the loss of the time to sell it by migration and leaving the homelands. Among the strange interpretations is what was narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, who said: What is meant by trade in this verse is daughters and sisters who, if they are idle in the house and cannot find a suitor for themselves, he cited as evidence for that the words of the poet: They were poor among their people, and my presence only increased their poverty. Although this verse includes the use of the word stagnation to refer to the absence of a suitor for them, it does not permit the use of the term trade for them. What is meant by the dwellings that they are satisfied with are the dwellings that they like and that their souls are drawn to and that they see as more beloved to them than migrating to God and His Messenger. Better is the predicate of was: meaning these things mentioned in the verse are more beloved to you than God and His Messenger and jihad in the way of God. Then wait means wait until God brings about His command regarding you and what His will requires of your punishment. It was said that what is meant by God’s command is fighting. It was also said that the conquest of Mecca was, and there is some distance in that, as it was narrated that this surah was revealed after the conquest. This is a severe warning, and it is confirmed by the ambiguity of the command and the lack of explicitness in it, so that their souls go in every direction and hesitate between types of punishment. And God does not guide the wicked people meaning those who disobey Him and are averse to complying with His commands and prohibitions. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: They were ordered to emigrate, so Al-Abbas Ibn Abdul Muttalib said: I will provide water for the pilgrims. Talhah, the brother of Banu Abdul Dar, said: I will block the Kaaba, so we will not emigrate. Then the verse was revealed: Do not take your fathers and your brothers as your wives. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil regarding this verse, he said: It is emigration. Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada: You have committed it he said: You have committed it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Until God brings about His command he said: With the conquest in His command to emigrate, all of this was before the conquest of Mecca. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Abdullah bin Shawdhab who said: Abu Abi Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah began to describe the gods to him on the day of Badr, and Abu Ubaidah began to avoid him. When Al-Jarrah increased his talk, his son Abu Ubaidah went after him and killed him. Then God revealed: You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day, the verse, which confirms the meaning of this verse. The ruling on migration was previously explained in Surat An-Nisa.
9:25: The citizen is the plural of citizen, and the citizens of war: its positions, and the positions in which God granted victory to the Muslims are the Day of Badr and the positions in which God granted victory to the Muslims over the infidels before the Day of Hunayn, 25- And the Day of Hunayn is conjoined with citizens by an estimated addition: either in the first and its estimate is in the days of citizens, or in the second and its estimate is and the place of the Day of Hunayn, so that time is not conjoined with place. It was responded that there is no improbability in conjoining time with place so it does not need an estimate, and it was said: The Day of Hunayn is victorious by an estimated action conjoined with your victory meaning and your victory on the Day of Hunayn, and the author of Al-Kashshaf preferred this, he said: The implication of that is that his saying: When it pleased you is a substitute for the Day of Hunayn, so if it was made the subject of this apparent, it would not be correct, because their large number did not please them in all of those positions, and they were not many in all of them. It was said that the conjunction does not require the two parties to share in everything that is established for the conjunction, as you say: Zaid and Amr came to me with his people, or in his clothes, or on his horse. It was said that when your multitude pleased you is not a substitute for the day of Hunayn, but rather it is accusative with an implied verb: that is, remember when your multitude pleased you. Hunayn is a valley between Mecca and Taif, and it was declined as a name for the place. Some Arabs deny it as a name for the spot, and from this is the saying of the poet: They supported their prophet and strengthened his resolve with Hanin on the day when heroes were helpless. The Muslims were amazed by their great number because they were twelve thousand, and it was said: eleven thousand, and it was said: sixteen thousand. Some of them said: We will not be defeated today because of fewness, so they were left to this word, but the large number did not benefit them at all, rather they were defeated and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood firm and with him stood firm a small group of them, his uncle Al-Abbas and Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith, then the Muslims retreated and there was victory and triumph. Enrichment means giving what satisfies a need: i.e. the large number did not give you anything to satisfy your need and did not benefit you. His statement: By how spacious Al-Rahb with a damma on the ra’ means spaciousness, and Al-Rahb with a fatha on the ra’ means a wide place, and the ba’ means with, and ma is a source, and the location of the preposition and the genitive is the accusative as a state. Meaning: The earth, despite its vast expanses, became narrow for them because of the fear and dread that befell them. It was said that the preposition ba means on: that is, on its vastness. Then you turned back in retreat means you were defeated while you were retreating: that is, turning your backs and making them towards your enemy.
9:26: His statement: 26- Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers: They are those who were not defeated, and it was said those who were defeated, and it appears that it was all of those who were present because they remained steadfast after that and fought and were victorious. His statement: And He sent down soldiers you did not see: They are the angels. Their number has been disputed in some sayings: It has been said five thousand, and it has been said eight thousand, and it has been said sixteen thousand, and it has been said other than that. This is not known except through the path of prophecy. They also differed as to whether the angels fought on this day or not. It has been mentioned previously that the angels did not fight except on the day of Badr, and that they were only present on occasions other than Badr to strengthen the hearts of the believers and to strike fear into the hearts of the polytheists. And He punished those who disbelieved with what befell them of killing, captivity, taking of wealth, and capturing of children. The reference in His statement: And that is to the punishment understood from He punished, and what befell them of punishment on this day was called a recompense, although it is not sufficient. Rather, there must be the punishment of the Hereafter, as an exaggeration in describing what befell them and to magnify it.
9:27: 27- Then after that God will turn in mercy to whomever He wills meaning after this punishment to whomever He wills of those He guided to Islam. And God is Forgiving He forgives whoever sinned and then repented. Merciful to His servants. He favors them with forgiveness for what they committed. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: Hunayn is between Mecca and Taif. The Prophet of God fought Hawazin and Thaqif, and Malik bin Awf was in charge of Hawazin, and Abd Yalil bin Amr Al-Thaqafi was in charge of Thaqif. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: “When the people of Mecca and Medina gathered, they said: Now we will fight as we have gathered. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked what they said and was amazed by their great numbers. So they met and were defeated until none of them could stand against the other until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began calling out to the tribes of the Arabs: ‘To me, to me.’ By God, no one would ascend to him until he had laid bare his place. So he turned to the Ansar who were far away and called out to them: ‘O supporters of God and supporters of His Messenger, to me, servants of God, I am the Messenger of God.’ So they knelt down crying and said: ‘O Messenger of God, by the Lord of the Kaaba, to you, by God.’ So they lowered their heads crying and brought forward their swords to strike in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until God granted them victory.” Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Ad-Dala’il on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ that “a man said on the day of Hunayn: We will not be defeated because of our small number. This was difficult for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: ‘And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you. ’ Ar-Rabi’ said: ‘They were twelve thousand, two thousand of whom were from Mecca. ’” At-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Abu Nu’aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Ad-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn, and the people turned away from him, and I remained with him with eighty men from the Muhajireen and Ansar. We were on foot for about eighty feet and did not turn our backs on them, and they were the ones upon whom God had sent down tranquility. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on his white mule, moving forward, and he said: Give me a handful of dirt. So I gave it to him and he struck their faces with it, and their eyes were filled with dirt, and the polytheists turned their backs. The Battle of Hunayn is mentioned in the books of biography and hadith in its entirety and details, so we will not elaborate on that. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And He sent down soldiers you did not see, he said: They are the angels, And He punished those who disbelieved, he said: He killed them with the sword. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: On the day of Hunayn, God supported His Messenger with five thousand marked angels, and on that day God called the Ansar believers. He said: So He sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Jubair bin Mut’im who said: Before the defeat of the people and the people were fighting, I saw something like a black scorpion coming from the sky until it fell among the people. I looked and saw black ants scattered and filling the valley. I had no doubt that they were the angels, and it was nothing but the defeat of the people.
35:10: Impure: A verbal noun that is neither dual nor plural. It is said: an impure man, an impure woman, two impure men, two impure women, impure men, impure women. It is also said: impure and impure with a kasra on the jim and a damma on it, and it is also said: impure with a kasra on the nun and a sukun on the jim, which is a softening of the vowel. It was said: It is not used unless it is said with it impurity, and it was said that it is more common, not universal. The polytheists are the subject, and its predicate is the verbal noun, an exaggeration in describing them with that, so that it is as if they are the essence of impurity, or according to the estimation of an added noun: meaning those with impurity, because with them is polytheism, which is like impurity. Qatada, Muammar, and others said: They were described with that because they do not purify themselves, do not wash themselves, and do not avoid impurities. The verse was used as evidence by those who said that the polytheist is impure in his essence, as some of the Zahiris and Zaidis believed. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and it was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The majority of the early and later generations, including the people of the four schools of thought, believed that the disbeliever is not impure in his essence, because God, the Exalted, made their food lawful, and it was proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his actions and words that indicate that they are not impure. He ate from their utensils, drank from them, performed ablution in them, and accommodated them in his mosque. His statement: 28- So let them not approach Al-Masjid Al-Haram The fa is for branching out, so their not approaching Al-Masjid Al-Haram is a branch of their impurity. What is meant by Al-Masjid Al-Haram is the entire Sanctuary, as was narrated on the authority of Ata’, so they are prevented from entering the entire Sanctuary, according to him. Other scholars believed that what is meant is Al-Masjid Al-Haram itself, so the polytheist is not prevented from entering the rest of the Sanctuary. Scholars have differed regarding the polytheist entering any mosque other than the Sacred Mosque. The people of Medina forbade every polytheist from any mosque. Ash-Shafi’i said: The verse is general and applies to all polytheists, especially in the Sacred Mosque, so they are not prevented from entering any other mosque. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a stagnation on his part, because the Almighty’s statement: The polytheists are unclean, is an indication of the reason for polytheism and impurity. The response to this is that this analogy is rejected by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) tying up Thamamah ibn Aththal in his mosque and hosting the delegation of Thaqeef in it. A similar statement was narrated from Abu Hanifa, who added that it is permissible for a non-Muslim to enter any other mosque without need, and Ash-Shafi’i restricted it to need. Qatadah said: This is permissible for a non-Muslim, but not for a polytheist. It was also narrated from Abu Hanifa that it is permissible for them to enter the Haram, the Sacred Mosque, and all other mosques. He forbade the polytheists from approaching the Sacred Mosque, which is a prohibition for the Muslims from allowing them to do that. It is similar to their saying: I will not see you here. His statement: After this year of theirs has two opinions: One of them: It is the year nine, which is the year in which Abu Bakr performed Hajj during the season. The second: It is the year ten, as stated by Qatadah. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is the correct opinion that gives the meaning of the wording. It is strange to say that it is the year nine, which is the year in which the call to prayer was made. If a slave of a man enters his house one day and his master says to him: Do not enter this house after your day, what is meant is not the day in which he entered. The answer to this is that what the wording implies is contrary to what he claimed, for the reference in his saying: after this year of theirs is to the year mentioned before the demonstrative pronoun, which is the year of the call. Thus in the example he mentioned, what is meant is the prohibition of entering it after the day of entry in which the address occurred, and the matter is clear and not hidden. Perhaps he intended to explain what is after the addition to their year, and there is no doubt that it is the year of ten. As for the explanation of the year referred to by this, there is no doubt that it is the year of nine, and this is what Qatada’s statement is based on. And those who said that it is permissible for the polytheists to enter the Sacred Mosque and other mosques have used this restriction, I mean his saying: after this year of theirs, saying that the prohibition is specific to the time of Hajj and Umrah, so they are forbidden from Hajj and Umrah only, not from entering in general. The answer to this is that the apparent prohibition of offering sacrifices after this year indicates the prohibition of offering sacrifices at all times that come after it, and specifying some of them as permissible requires a specification. His saying: And if you fear poverty, then God will enrich you from His bounty. Poverty is poverty. It is said: A man became poor if he became needy. The poet said: The poor man does not know when he will become rich, and the rich man does not know when he will be dependent. Alqamah and others from the companions of Ibn Masoud read it as ‘A’ila, which is a verbal noun like ‘Al-Qa’ila, ‘Al-Afiya, and ‘Aqiba. It was said that its meaning is: a difficult trait. It is said: ‘The matter ‘alaani ya’ulni’ meaning it was difficult and severe for me. Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari narrated that it is said ‘alaani ya’ul’ if he became poor. When the Muslims prevented the polytheists from the Hajj season, and they used to bring food and trade to it, Satan cast fear of poverty into their hearts, and they said: Where will we live? So God promised them that He would enrich them from His bounty. Ad-Dahhak said: So God opened the door of the jizyah from the People of the Covenant for them by His saying: Fight those who do not believe in God (al-Nisa’ 2:10). Ikrimah said: He enriched them by providing them with rain, plants, and fertile land. The Arabs converted to Islam and carried to Mecca what God had enriched them with. It was said that He enriched them with the shade. The benefit of restricting it to the will is to teach the servants to say that in everything they say that has to do with the future time, and so that they do not stop supplicating and beseeching. Indeed, God is Knowing of your conditions, Wise in giving and withholding. What He wills will be and what He does not will will not be. 10- Whoever desires honor Al-Farra’ said: It means whoever knows who owns honor, then it belongs entirely to God. Qatada said: Whoever desires honor should seek honor through obedience to God, so he made the meaning of To God belongs honor: the call to obey the One who has honor, just as one says: Whoever desires money, then the money belongs to so-and-so, meaning let him seek it from him. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: Whoever desires honor through the worship of God, and honor belongs to Him, glory be to Him, then God the Almighty will honor him in this world and the hereafter. It was said that what is meant by His statement, Whoever desires honor is the polytheists, for they were strengthened by worshipping idols, as in His statement, And they took besides God gods that they might be for themselves a source of honor. It was also said that what is meant is those who were strengthened by them from among those who believed with their tongues, “Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honor from them?” The verse, To God belongs all honor, meaning let him seek it from Him, not from anyone else. The apparent meaning of the verse is that whoever desires honor and seeks it should seek it from God, the Almighty and Majestic: To God belongs all honor, no one else has any of it. So the verse includes everyone who seeks honor, and its purpose is to alert those of high standing and high ambitions, from where honor can be attained, and from which direction should it be sought? To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it. That is, it ascends to God and not to anyone else. The meaning of its ascension to Him is its acceptance, or the ascension of the scribes among the angels with what they write in the scrolls. The good word was specifically mentioned to indicate the reward for it. It includes every word that is characterized as being good, such as remembrance of God, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, reciting, and other things. So there is no reason to specify it with the word of monotheism, or with praise and glorification. It was said that what is meant by its ascension is its ascension to the lowest heaven. It was also said that what is meant by its ascension is God's knowledge of it. The meaning of and the righteous deed raises it is that the righteous deed raises the good word, as al-Hasan, Shahr ibn Hawshab, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah, Abu al-'Aliyah, and al-Dahhak said. The reason is that the good word is not accepted except with the righteous deed. It was also said that the agent of raises it is the good word, and its object is the righteous deed. The reason for this is that the righteous deed is not accepted except with monotheism and faith. It was also said that the agent of raises it is a pronoun that refers to God, the Almighty. Meaning: God elevates righteous deeds over good words, because deeds confirm speech. It was said that righteous deeds elevate their doer, and that is what He intended for glory. Qatada said: The meaning is that God elevates righteous deeds to their doer, meaning He accepts them. So His statement, and righteous deeds, according to this is a subject whose predicate elevates them. And similarly according to the statement of those who say elevates their doer. The majority read yus’ud from the triliteral verb asada’a. And al-kalim al-tayyib in the nominative case as an agent. Ali and Ibn Mas’ud read yus’ud with a damma on the letter of the present tense from asada’a, and al-kalim al-tayyib in the accusative case as an object. Ad-Dahhak read it in the passive form, and the majority read al-kalam. Abu Abd al-Rahman read al-kalam, and the majority read and righteous deeds in the nominative case as an conjunction or as a subject. Ibn Abi Ubla and Isa bin Omar read it in the accusative case, indicating preoccupation: And those who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment. The accusative case of bad deeds is an attribute of a deleted verbal noun, meaning they plot evil deeds. This is because plotting is intransitive, and it is permissible for they plot to include the meaning of they earn, so that bad deeds would be the direct object. Mujahid and Qatadah said: They are the people of hypocrisy. Abu Al-Aliyah said: They are those who plotted against the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when they gathered in Dar Al-Nadwa. Al-Kalbi said: They are those who commit evil deeds in this world. Muqatil said: They are the polytheists. The meaning of they will have a severe punishment is that they will have a punishment of extreme severity. And the plotting of those is to be ruined, meaning it will be nullified and destroyed. From this comes the phrase and you were a ruined people. Plotting originally means deception and trickery. The reference in His statement: those is to those who plotted evil deeds, according to the different opinions in interpreting their plotting. The phrase is to be ruined is the predicate of the plotting of those.
9:29: His saying: 29- Fight those who do not believe in God the verse, in it is the command to fight those who combine these descriptions. Abu al-Wafa' bin Aqil said: His saying: Fight is a command to punish, then he said: Those who do not believe in God so he explained the sin that requires the punishment, then he said: Nor in the Last Day so he emphasized the sin in the aspect of belief, then he said: And they do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden in it is an increase in the sin of violating actions, then he said: And they do not follow the religion of truth in it is an indication of emphasizing the disobedience by deviation, obstinacy and disdain for submission, then he said: Of those who were given the Scripture to emphasize the argument against them because they found it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, then he said: Until they pay the jizyah so he explained the end to which the punishment extends. His saying: Of those who were given the Scripture is an explanation of the relative pronoun with what is in its predicate and they are the people of the Torah and the Gospel. His saying: Until they pay the jizyah willingly. The jizyah is of the form fa’lah from jaza yajzi: if he recompenses for what was given to him, so it is as if they gave it as a reward for what they were granted of security. It was said: It was called jizyah because it is a group of what the People of the Covenant must reward: that is, they pay it, and in the Shari’ah it is what the covenantor gives according to his covenant. ‘an id is in the accusative case as a state. The meaning is: by a favorable hand that is not withheld. It was said that its meaning is: they give it with their own hands without appointing anyone to do it on behalf of them. It was said that its meaning is: cash, not deferred. It was said that its meaning is: by force. It was said that its meaning is: by a favor from you to them, because taking it from them is a type of favor to them. It was said that its meaning is: blameworthy. A group of scholars, including al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Abu Hanifah and his companions, al-Thawri and Abu Thawr, held that the jizyah is not accepted except from the People of the Book. Al-Awza’i and Malik said: The jizyah is taken from all types of infidels, whoever they may be, and the People of the Book, according to the first opinion, include the Magians. Ibn al-Mundhir said: I do not know of any disagreement that the jizya should be taken from them. Scholars have differed on the amount of the jizya. Ata’ said: It has no amount, but is taken according to what they agree upon. Yahya bin Adam, Abu Ubaid and Ibn Jarir said the same, except that he said: The minimum is one dinar and the maximum has no limit. Ash-Shafi’i said: A dinar is due from the rich and the poor among the free adults, and nothing is reduced from it. Abu Thawr said the same. Ash-Shafi’i said: If they agree on more than one dinar, it is permissible, and if they increase and are willing to do so, it is accepted from them. Malik said: It is four dinars for those who own gold, and forty dirhams for those who own silver, the rich and the poor are equal, even if he is a Zoroastrian, it does not increase or decrease. Abu Hanifa and his companions, Muhammad bin al-Hasan and Ahmad bin Hanbal said: It is twelve, twenty-four and forty-eight. The discussion of the jizya is established in its proper places, and we have established the truth of these opinions in our explanation of al-Muntaqa and other works of ours. His saying: and they are humiliated is in the accusative case as a state, and humiliation means disgrace. Meaning: The dhimmi pays the jizya while he is humiliated. It was said: It means that he brings it himself, walking, not riding, and hands it over while standing, and the recipient is sitting. In short, the one who receives the jizya should make the one who receives it humiliated and submissive when he receives it. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, regarding the verse: The polytheists are unclean al-Baqarah 2:173, he said: Unless they are slaves or one of the People of the Covenant. It has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from another source. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Jabir, who said: No polytheist will enter this mosque of ours after this year of ours, except the people of the covenant and your servants. Ibn Kathir said: Ahmad is the only one who narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but the chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is more authentic. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The polytheists used to come to the House and bring food with them to trade with. When they were forbidden from coming to the House, the Muslims said: Where will we get food from? So God revealed: But if you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. So God sent down rain upon them, and their goodness increased when the polytheists left them. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: So God enriched them from His bounty and ordered them to fight the People of the Book. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: And if you fear poverty, he said: Need. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: Then God will enrich you from His bounty, he said: With the jizyah. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak similarly. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: The polytheists are unclean, he said: Dirty. Abu Al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority that he said: Whoever shakes hands with them should perform ablution. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever shakes hands with a polytheist should perform ablution or wash his hands. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Fight those who do not believe in God, he said: This verse was revealed when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were ordered to go on the Battle of Tabuk. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab who said: It was revealed regarding the infidels of Quraysh and the Arabs: And fight them until there is no more persecution, and it was revealed regarding the People of the Book: Fight those who do not believe in God, the verse until His statement: Until they pay the jizyah, so the first to pay the jizyah were the people of Najran. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: Fight those who do not believe in God, meaning those who do not believe in the Oneness of God, and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, meaning wine and silk, and do not adopt the religion of truth, meaning the religion of Islam, from among those who were given the Scripture until they pay the jizyah with willing submission, meaning humiliated. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: with willing submission, he said: by force. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah regarding his statement: by hand, he said: From his hand and no one else sends it. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Sinan regarding his statement: by hand, he said: By power. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and they are humbled, he said: They walk with it in a state of swaying motion. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: They pounce. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Salman regarding the verse that he said: Not praised.
9:30: His saying: 30- And the Jews said, 'Ezra is the son of God' is a new statement to explain the polytheism of the People of the Book. Ezra is the subject and the son of God is its predicate. Asim and Al-Kisa'i read Ezra with the tanween, and the rest read without the tanween because of the combination of foreignness and knowledge in it. Whoever reads with the tanween has made it Arabic. It was said that the tanween was dropped not because it is impossible, but because of the combination of two quiescent letters. From this is the reading of whoever reads: Say, 'He is God, the One * God, the Eternal Refuge.' Abu Ali Al-Farisi said, and it is common in poetry, and Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari recited: To find me with the prince on land and with the canal, I will be a sly man If you cover the peaceful one, it will fly away The apparent meaning of his statement: And the Jews said is that this statement is for all of them. It was said: It is a general expression, but its meaning is specific because only some of them said it. Al-Naqqash said: There is no Jew left who says it? Rather, they have become extinct. It was said: A group of them said that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the verse was revealed including the narration of that from the Jews, because the statement of some of them is binding on all of them. His statement: And the Christians said, ‘The Messiah is the son of God’ They said this when they saw him bringing the dead back to life despite not having a father, so that was the reason for this statement. It is better to say: They said this statement because the Gospel describes him sometimes as the son of God and sometimes as the son of man, as we have seen in many places in the Gospel, and they did not understand that this was for the purpose of honoring and glorifying, or it did not become clear to them that this was a distortion of their predecessors for a corrupt purpose. It was said: This statement is for some of the Christians, not all of them. His statement: That is their statement with their mouths refers to what they issued from this false statement. The justification for their saying with their mouths despite the knowledge that speech can only be done by the mouth is that since this statement is naive and does not contain any explanation or proof, it is merely a claim with no meaning underneath it, empty and issued by them, issuing meaningless statements that have nothing in them except that they come out of the mouths, not providing any benefit that can be relied upon. It was said that mentioning the mouths is for emphasis, as in I wrote with my hand and I walked with my feet. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: They write the Book with their hands. And His saying: And no bird flies with its wings. Some of the people of knowledge said: God the Almighty did not mention a statement coupled with mentioning the mouths and tongues except that it was a false statement, like His saying: They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts. And His saying: A great word comes out of their mouths. And His saying: They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. His saying: They imitate the saying of those who disbelieve. Imitation means resemblance. It was said: And from this is the saying of the Arabs, a woman who does not menstruate, because she resembled men. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: Whoever said They imitate is taken from their saying a woman who is imitating men, then his statement is wrong, because the hamza in Dahā is original, and in Dahīya is extra like Hamra', and its original is Yadhāhi'ūn and A woman who is imitating men. And the meaning of their imitating the saying of those who disbelieve has been stated by the scholars: The first: That they imitated with this statement the idol worshippers in their saying, Al-Lat, Al-'Uzza, and Manat are the daughters of God. The second statement: That they imitated their ancestors who said that Uzair is the son of God and that the Messiah is the son of God. His saying, May God fight them is a prayer for their destruction, because whoever God fights is destroyed. It was said: It is astonishment at the hideousness of their statement. It was said that the meaning of May God fight them is: May God curse them. And from this is the saying of Abaan bin Tha'lab: May God kill her, she insulted me, and she knew that I was the one who corrupted and reformed myself. Al-Naqqash narrated that the origin of Qatal God is supplication, then it became more common in their use until they said it to express astonishment about good and evil, and they did not mean supplication. Al-Asma’i recited: Oh God, kill Laila. How can I please you while I tell people that I don’t care about her? How are they turned away from the truth to falsehood?
9:31: His statement: 31- They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides God. Al-Ahbar: the plural of habbar, which is the one who speaks well, and from it is a robe called muhbar, and it was said: the plural of habbar with a kasra on the ha. Yunus said: I did not hear it except with a kasra on the ha. Al-Farraa said: The fatha and the kasra are two languages. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: The habbar with a kasra is the scholar, and the habbar with a fatha is the scholar. And the monks are the plural of rahib, taken from fear, and they are the scholars of the Christians, just as the rabbis are the scholars of the Jews. The meaning of the verse is that when they obeyed them in what they commanded them to do and what they forbade them from, they were in the position of those who took them as lords because they obeyed them as lords are obeyed. His statement: And the Messiah, son of Mary is conjoined with their monks: meaning the Christians took him as a lord who is worshipped, and in it is an indication that the Jews did not take Ezra as a lord who is worshipped. In this verse there is what deters whoever has a heart or listens attentively and is a witness from imitating the religion of God and the influence of what the predecessors say over what is in the Noble Book and the pure Sunnah. For the obedience of the follower of a doctrine to the one whose words he follows and whose Sunnah he follows from the scholars of this nation, while contradicting what the texts have brought and what God’s proofs and evidences have established and what His books and prophets have spoken of, is like the Jews and Christians taking the rabbis and monks as lords besides God, because it is certain that they did not worship them, but rather obeyed them and forbade what they forbade and permitted what they permitted. This is the action of the imitators of this nation, and it is more similar to it than comparing an egg to an egg, a date to a date, and water to water. O servants of God and followers of Muhammad ibn Abdullah, why have you left the Book and the Sunnah aside and turned to men who are like you in God’s worship of them through them and His request of them to act upon what they have indicated and benefited from? You have done what they have brought of opinions that are not based on the pillar of truth and are not supported by the arm. Religion and the texts of the Book and the Sunnah call out in the most eloquent voice and raise your voice in the loudest voice that contradicts and opposes that. So you have given them deaf ears, sealed hearts, sick understandings, exhausted minds, dull intellects, and sick thoughts. You have chanted in the language of the situation: I am only from Ghazia, if it goes astray, I go astray, and if Ghazia is guided, I am guided. So, may God guide you and me, leave the books that were written for you by the dead among your ancestors, and replace them with the Book of God, their Creator and your Creator, their worshipper and your worshipper, their object of worship and your object of worship, and replace the sayings of those you call your imams and the opinions they brought you with the sayings of your imam and their imam and your role model and their role model, who is the first imam, Muhammad ibn Abdullah, may God bless him and grant him peace. Leave every saying when Muhammad says, for I do not take risks in his religion. O God, Guide of the lost, Instructor of the astray, Clarifier of the path, guide us to the truth and show us what is right, and make clear to us the path of guidance. His statement, And they were commanded not but to worship one God This sentence is in the accusative case as a state: that is, they took their rabbis and monks as lords, while the fact is that they were not commanded except to worship God alone, or those rabbis and monks whom they took as lords were not commanded except with that, so how can they be fit for what He has qualified them to do by taking them as lords? His statement, There is no god but He is a second description of His statement, Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him meaning, He is far removed from associating partners with Him in His obedience and worship.
9:32: His saying: 32- They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths This is a statement that includes mentioning another type of their misguidance and distance from the truth, which is what they sought to invalidate the truth with their false statements that are nothing but simple words and false arguments. This is a representation of their state in trying to invalidate the religion of truth and the prophethood of the Prophet of Truth, like the state of someone who wants to blow on a great light that has illuminated the world and dispelled the darkness, in order to extinguish it and extinguish its lights. But God refuses except to perfect His light meaning His upright religion. It has been said: How did the exception enter into ya'bā, and it is not permissible to hate or hate except Zayd. Al-Farra' said: It only entered because there is a touch of denial in the speech. Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs delete with aba, and the meaning is and God refuses everything except to perfect His light. Ali bin Sulayman said: This is only permissible in aba, because it is a prevention or refusal, so it resembles negation. Al-Nahhas said: This is better, as the poet said: And do I have another mother if I leave her? God wills that I be nothing but her son. The author of Al-Kashshaf said: “Abra has been treated as if he did not want: that is, he does not want anything but that his light should be completed.” His statement: Even if the disbelievers dislike it is connected to the implied sentence before it: that is, God refused except that his light should be completed, even if the disbelievers did not dislike it, even if they disliked it.
9:33: Then he confirmed this by saying: 33- It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance meaning with what he guides people with from proofs, miracles, and rulings that God has legislated for His servants and the religion of truth which is Islam to make it manifest meaning to make His Messenger manifest, or the religion of truth with what it contains of arguments and proofs, and this has happened, praise be to God, even though the polytheists dislike it the discussion of it is like the discussion of even though the disbelievers dislike it as we have mentioned before. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Salam bin Mishkam, Nu'man bin Awfa, Abu Anas, Shas bin Qais and Malik bin Al-Saif came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and said: How can we follow you when you have abandoned our Qiblah and you do not claim that Ezra is the son of God? So God revealed: And the Jews say, 'Ezra is the son of God' (Al-Baqara 2:17). Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: The women of the Children of Israel used to gather at night to pray, isolate themselves and remember what God had bestowed upon the Children of Israel and what He had given them. Then the worst of His creation, Nebuchadnezzar, was sent over them. He burned the Torah and destroyed the Temple in Jerusalem, and Ezra was a young boy at that time. Ezra said: Was this it? So he went to the mountains and the wilderness and began to worship there, and he began to avoid mixing with people. Then one day he came across a woman at a grave and she was crying. He said: O mother, fear God and seek reward and be patient. Do you not know that the path of people is death? She said: O Ezra, do you forbid me to cry when you have left behind the Children of Israel and have gone to the mountains and the wilderness? Then she said: I am not a woman, but I am the world. A spring will gush forth in your place of prayer and a tree will grow, so drink from the water of the spring and eat from the fruit of the tree, for two angels will come to you and let them do what they want. The next day, the spring gushes forth and the tree grows, so he drank from the water of the spring and ate from the fruit of the tree. Two angels came with a bottle containing light and they made him flow with what was in it, so God inspired him with the Torah. He came and dictated it to the people, at which point they said, ‘Ezra is the son of God. God is exalted above that.’ Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him a story in which he said: After Ezra had made the Children of Israel forget the Torah and abrogated it from their hearts, he asked God to restore what had been abrogated from his heart. While he was praying, a light from God, the Almighty, descended and entered his stomach, and what had been removed from his stomach of the Torah returned to him. He announced to his people, saying: O my people, God has given me the Torah and restored it to me. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ka’b who said: Ezra supplicated to his Lord to place the Torah in his heart as it was revealed to Moses, so God revealed it to him. After that, they said: Ezra is the son of God. Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: There are three things about which I have doubts: I do not know whether Ezra was a prophet or not? I do not know whether he cursed Tubba or not? He said: I forgot the third. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: They imitate he said: They resemble. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: May God fight them he said: May God curse them and everything in the Qur’an that is killing is a curse. Ibn Sa'd, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Adi ibn Hatim who said: I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was reciting in Surat Bara'ah the verse: They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God. He said: They did not worship them, but when they made something permissible for them, they considered it permissible, and when they made something forbidden for them, they considered it forbidden. Ahmad and Ibn Jarir also narrated it. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Buhturi who said: A man asked Hudhayfah and said: Tell me about the words of God: They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God, did they worship them? He said: No, but when they made something permissible for them, they considered it permissible, and when they made something forbidden for them, they considered it forbidden. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: Their rabbis were their reciters and their monks were their scholars. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: The rabbis are from the Jews, and the monks are from the Christians. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi something similar. He also narrated on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Iyad who said: The rabbis are the scholars, and the monks are the worshippers. He also narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, he said: They want to extinguish Islam with their words. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding his statement: They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, he said: They want to destroy Muhammad and his companions. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, he said: They are the Jews and Christians. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi, It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance, meaning with monotheism, Islam, and the Qur’an.
9:34: When God finished mentioning the state of the followers of the rabbis and monks who take them as lords, He mentioned the state of those who are followed, saying: 34- Indeed, many of the rabbis to the end. The meaning of their eating people's money unjustly is that they take it through false means, such as bribery. He established this for many of them, because among them are those who did not engage in that, but rather remained as their religion requires without distorting or changing or leaning towards the debris of this world. And countless scholars of Islam followed the example of these rabbis and monks in every age, so God is the One sought for help. And they hinder [people] from the way of God meaning from the path to Him, which is the religion of Islam, or from what was true in their Shari'ah before it was abrogated, because of their eating people's money unjustly. His saying: And those who hoard gold and silver. It was said: They are the rabbis and monks mentioned earlier, and that they used to do this. It was also said: They are those Muslims who do that. The first is to interpret the verse in general terms, as it is broader than that. The root of the word kanz in the language is to join and gather, and it is not limited to gold and silver. Ibn Jarir said: A treasure is everything that is gathered together, whether in the belly of the earth or on its back. And from this is a she-camel that is kanaz, meaning full of meat. And kanaz means to gather something. Scholars differed about the money on which zakat has been paid, is it called a treasure or not? Some people said: It is a treasure, and others said: It is not a treasure. Among those who said the first opinion was Abu Dharr, and he limited it to what is in excess of need. Among those who said the second opinion were Omar bin Al-Khattab, Ibn Omar, Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Abu Hurairah, Omar bin Abdul Aziz and others, and this is the truth because of the evidence that will come that clearly states that what zakat has been paid is not a treasure. His statement: nor do they spend it in the way of God. There is a difference of opinion about the reason for singling out the pronoun when the two things mentioned before it are gold and silver. Ibn al-Anbari said: He intended the most general, which is silver. He said: And similar to it is the saying of God Almighty: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult. He referred the metaphor to prayer because it is more general. And similar to it is His saying: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it. He referred the pronoun to trade because it is more important. And it was said that the pronoun refers to gold and silver, conjoined with it. The Arabs feminize and masculine gold. And it was said that the pronoun refers to the treasures indicated by His saying: they hoard. And it was said to money. And it was said to zakat. And it was said that He was satisfied with the pronoun of one of them instead of the pronoun of the other with understanding the meaning, and it is common in the speech of the Arabs. And Sibawayh recited: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs He did not say satisfied, and the same is said by another: He threw me into a matter that my father and I were innocent of, and for the sake of the long life he threw me into it And he did not say Brian, and the same is true of Hassan’s saying: The crack of youth and black hair, unless it is treated, is crazy. He did not say ya'adha, and it was said that the singular pronoun is for the sake of going to the meaning rather than the word, because each one of gold and silver is a sufficient sentence, and a large number, and dinars and dirhams, so it is like his saying: And if two parties among the believers should fight and gold and silver were mentioned specifically without the rest of the money because they are the prices of things, and most of what is hoarded, even though other than them has their ruling in the prohibition of hoarding. His saying: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment is the report of the relative pronoun, and it is from the category of mocking them as in his saying: Greetings between them are painful It was said: Good report is the report that changes the color of the skin due to its effect on the heart, whether in joy or sorrow.
9:35: The meaning of 35- On the Day it is heated in the Fire of Hell is that the fire is kindled on it while it is very hot and scorching. If he had said On the Day it is heated meaning the treasures, this meaning would not have been given, so the heating of the fire would have been an exaggeration, then the fire was deleted and the action was attributed to the preposition, as you say the story was raised to the prince, but if the story is not mentioned you say it was raised to the prince. Ibn Amir read is heated with the upper thaa'. Abu Haywah read is cauterized with the lower thaa'. He specified the foreheads, sides and backs because the pain of cauterizing them is more severe because of the noble organs inside them. It was said that cauterization should be in the four directions: from the front, behind, to the right, and to the left. It was said: because beauty is in the face, and strength is in the back and sides, and man only seeks money for beauty and strength. Other things were said that are not without affectation. His saying: This is what you have hoarded for yourselves means it will be said to them: This is what you have hoarded for yourselves: meaning you hoarded it to benefit from it, so this is its benefit in the manner of mockery and rebuke. So taste what you have been hoarding “ma” is a source or relative pronoun: meaning taste its harm, the evil of its outcome, the ugliness of its consequences, and the ominousness of its benefit. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: Indeed, many of the rabbis and monks meaning the scholars of the Jews and Christians devour the wealth of people unjustly. Falsehood is books that they wrote that were not revealed by God, so they devour the wealth of people with them. This is the statement of God the Most High: So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, ‘This is from God.’ Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And those who hoard gold and silver, he said: These are the ones who do not pay zakat from their wealth. All wealth whose zakat is not paid, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its depths, is a treasure, and all wealth whose zakat is paid is not a treasure, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its depths. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated it on his authority from another chain of transmission. Malik, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Adi and Al-Khatib narrated something similar on the authority of Jabir with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding the verse, he said: This was before Zakat was revealed, but when Zakat was revealed, God made it a means of purifying wealth. Then he said: What would I care if I had gold like Mount Uhud, I knew its number, paid Zakat on it, and used it to do acts of obedience to God? Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, he said: It is not a treasure that has been paid Zakat on. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in his Musnad, Abu Dawud, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘And those who hoard gold and silver’, it was difficult for the Muslims, and they said: None of us can afford for his children what will not remain after him. Umar said: I will relieve you. Umar set out, followed by Thawban, and came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Prophet of God, this verse has been difficult for your companions. He said: God did not impose zakat except to purify what remains of your wealth, but He imposed inheritance from wealth that will remain after you. Umar felt great distress, then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Shall I not tell you of the best thing a man can hoard? A righteous woman who pleases him when he looks at her, obeys him when he commands her, and protects him when he is away from her.” Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja`d through other chains of transmission on the authority of Thawban. Al-Bukhari narrated that Salim did not hear it from Thawban. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And those who hoard gold and silver, he said: They are the People of the Book, and he said: It is specific and general. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, who said: Four thousand or less is a provision and above that is a treasure. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The adornment of swords is from treasures. I will not tell you except what I heard. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Arak bin Malik and Umar bin Abdul Aziz that they said regarding his statement: And those who hoard gold and silver, that it was abrogated by the other verse: Take from their wealth a charity, the verse. Al-Bukhari and Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay its zakat except that it will be made into plates on the Day of Resurrection, then heated in the fire of Hell, then his sides, forehead and back will be branded with it on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years until judgment is passed between the people and he will see his path, either to Paradise or to Hell.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Wahb who said: I passed by Abu Dharr in Al-Zubdah and said: What brought you to this land? He said: We were in Ash-Sham and I recited: And those who hoard gold and silver Al-Baqarah 2:176. Muawiyah said: This is not for us, this is only for the People of the Book. I said: It is for us and for them.
9:36: His statement: 36- Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months. This is an introductory statement that includes mentioning another type of the ugliness of the disbelievers, and that is that when God, the Most High, ruled with a specific ruling for each time, they changed those times by intercalation and leap year. So God informed us of what His ruling is, saying: Indeed, the number of months meaning the number of months of the year with God in His ruling, judgment and wisdom is twelve months. His statement: In the Book of God meaning in what He established in His Book. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: It is not permissible to relate in the Book of God to His statement: the number of months, because of the separation by the foreigner, which is al-Naba 78:I mean twelve months, so His statement: in the Book of God, and His statement: on the day of creation are a substitute for His statement from God, and the meaning is: Indeed, the number of months with God is in the Book of God on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and the benefit of the two substitutions is to establish the statement in the minds because it is known from it that that number is obligatory with God in the Book of God, and is established in His knowledge from the first time God created the world. It is possible that there is a description of twelve in the Book of God: that is, twelve established in the Book of God, which is the Preserved Tablet. In this verse, there is a statement that God, the Exalted, placed these months and named them with their names in this known order on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and that this is what the prophets brought and the books were revealed with, and that no attention should be paid to the months that the Persians, Romans, and Copts agree upon, some of which they make thirty days, some more, and some less. His statement, Of them, four are sacred are Dhul-Qa’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab: three in succession, and one alone, as was stated in the pure Sunnah. His statement, That is the right religion means that these months are like that, and among them are four sacred months, which is the straight religion, the correct calculation, and the complete number. His statement, So wrong not yourselves therein means in these sacred months by fighting in them and violating their sanctity. It was said that the pronoun refers to all the sacred months and others, and that God forbade injustice in them, but the first is more appropriate. A group of scholars have stated that the prohibition of fighting during the sacred months is established and has not been abrogated by this verse, and by His statement: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month, and by His statement: So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists, the verse. Another group of people have said that the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months was abrogated by the verse of the sword. The answer to this is that the command to kill and fight the polytheists is restricted to the expiration of the sacred months as in the aforementioned verse, so all the verses that include the command to fight are restricted by what was mentioned in the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months, just as they are restricted by the prohibition of fighting in the sanctuary due to the evidence mentioned in the prohibition of fighting in it. As for what they used as evidence that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) besieged the people of Ta’if in a sacred month, which is Dhul-Qa’dah, as proven in the two Sahihs and others, the answer to this is that he did not begin besieging them in Dhul-Qa’dah, but in Shawwal, and the sacred month is the beginning of fighting in the sacred months, not its completion, and in this way the combination is achieved. His statement: And fight the polytheists all together means all together, and it is a source in the place of a state. Al-Zajjaj said: Sources like general and specific are not dualized or pluralized. As they fight you all together means all together. It contains evidence of the obligation to fight the polytheists, and that it is an obligation on individuals if some do not do so. And know that God is with the righteous, meaning He will support them and make them steadfast, and whoever God is with is the victor, and he will have the outcome and victory.
9:37: His saying: 37- The postponement is only an increase in disbelief. Nafi' read in the narration of Warsh from him the postponement with a double yaa without a hamza. The rest read with a yaa followed by a hamza. An-Nahhas said: No one narrated this reading from Nafi' except Warsh alone, and it is derived from nasa'ahu and ansa'ahu: if he delayed it, as Al-Kisa'i narrated. Al-Jawhari said: The postponement is a fa'il with the meaning of maf'ul from your saying: I postponed something so it is manso': if you delayed it, then manso' was transformed into nasi' just as maqtool was transformed into maqtool. Ibn Jarir said: In the postponement with the hamza there is the meaning of an increase. It is said: nasa' yansa': if he increased, he said: And it does not happen by leaving the hamza except from forgetfulness as God the Almighty said: They forgot God so He forgot them, and he responded to Nafi's reading. The Arabs used to forbid fighting in the mentioned sacred months. If they needed to fight in them, they would fight in them and forbid others. If they fought in Muharram, they would forbid Safar instead, and so on in other months. What made them do this was that many of them lived by raiding each other and plundering whatever they could of the money of those they raided, and fighting would break out between them because of that. The three months mentioned would harm them if they were to follow one another, and their need would increase and their poverty would become great, so they would make some of them permissible and forbid in their place the amount of other than the sacred months. This is the meaning of the intercalation that they used to do. There was a dispute about who first did this. It was said that he was a man from Banu Kinanah called Hudhayfah ibn ‘Atid, and he was nicknamed al-Qalmas, and al-Kumait refers to him when he said: Aren't we the ones who forget the months of permissibility and make them forbidden? And their speaker says: And we forget the pen month It was said that he is Amr bin Luhay, and it was said that he is Naim bin Tha’labah from Banu Kinanah, and God the Almighty called the intercalation an increase in disbelief because it is a type of their disbelief, and a sin of their sins that are added to their disbelief in God, His Books, His Messengers, and the Last Day. His statement: Thus He misguides those who disbelieve. The people of the Two Sanctuaries, Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read yadhill in the active form. The Kufians read in the passive form, and the meaning of the first reading is that the disbelievers go astray by what they do of intercalation, and the meaning of the second reading is that the One who prescribed that for them makes them go astray by this bad practice. Abu Hatim chose the first reading, and Abu Ubaid chose the second reading. Al-Hasan, Abu Raja’ and Ya’qub read yadhill with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the dad, so that its relative subject and object are deleted, and it is possible that its subject is God the Almighty and its relative object. It was read with a fatha on the ya’ and the dad fromضل يضل. And nadhill was read with a noon. His statement: They make it lawful one year and forbid it another year. The pronoun refers to the intercalation: that is, they make the intercalation lawful one year and forbid it another year, or to the month that they postpone and fight in: that is, they make it lawful one year by replacing it with another month from the permissible months, they forbid it another year: that is, they preserve it and do not make fighting lawful in it, rather they keep it sacred. His statement: To agree with the number of what God has forbidden means to agree, and agreement is agreement. It is said: The people agreed on such-and-such: that is, they agreed on it and gathered. The meaning is: They did not make a month lawful except that they made a month forbidden so that the sacred months would remain four. Qatrub said: Its meaning is that they deliberately went to Safar and added it to the sacred months and linked it to Muharram in forbidding. At-Tabari said the same. His statement: And to make lawful what God has forbidden means from the sacred months that they replaced with others. The evil of their deeds made attractive to them means that Satan made the evil deeds that they do attractive to them, including the intercalation. It was read in the active construction: And God does not guide the disbelieving people, meaning those who persist in their disbelief and continue upon it, so He does not guide them with guidance that leads them to what they want. As for guidance in the sense of indicating the truth and directing to it, God Almighty has appointed it for all of His servants. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Bakr that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon during his pilgrimage and said: “Time has come full circle to the way it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, four of which are sacred, three of which are consecutive: Dhul-Qa’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which is between Jumada and Sha’ban.” Similar to this was narrated by Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Ibn Umar. Similar to this was narrated by Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Ibn Abbas. Similar to this was also narrated by al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurairah from his uncle, with a long chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Sa’id ibn Mansur and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas: Four of them are sacred, and he said: Muharram, Rajab, Dhul-Qa’dah and Dhul-Hijjah. Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Dahhak who said: They were called sacred so that there would be no war in them. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God. Then He singled out four months from that and made them sacred, and magnified their sacredness, and made religion greater in them, and righteous deeds and reward greater. So do not wrong yourselves therein. He said: In all of them. And fight the polytheists all together. He said: All of them. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Muqatil regarding his statement: And fight the polytheists all together. He said: This verse abrogated every verse that contained a dispensation. At-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Shu'ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather who said: The Arabs used to perform Hajj once every twenty years, and they would not perform Hajj except once every twenty years, and it is the intercalation that God mentioned in His Book. When the year Abu Bakr performed Hajj with the people coincided with that year, God called it the greater Hajj, then the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) performed Hajj the following year. The people welcomed the new moon, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Time has returned to its original state as it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood at Al-Aqabah and said: The postponement is from Satan, an increase in disbelief by which he misleads those who disbelieve, making it permissible one year and forbidding it the next. So they would forbid Muharram one year and consider Safar permissible, and they would forbid Safar one year and consider Muharram permissible. This is the postponement. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Junada bin Auf Al-Kinani would come to the Hajj season every year, and his nickname was Abu Thamama.
