He would call out, Abu Thamama will not be disappointed or criticized, and Safar of the first year is permissible, so he would make it permissible for the people, making Safar permissible one year and forbidding Muharram the next year. This is the meaning of the verse: The postponement is only an increase in disbelief. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, saying: They used to call Muharram Safar, and Safar they say Safraan al-Awwal and al-Akhir, and sometimes the first and sometimes the last were permissible for them. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, saying: Al-Nisa’ah were a tribe of Banu Malik from Kinanah from Banu Fuqaym, and the last of them was a man called Al-Qalmas, and he is the one who postponed Muharram.
9:38: His statement: 38- O you who have believed When he explained the faults of those infidels, he returned to encouraging the believers to fight them, and the question What is wrong with you? is for denial and rebuke: meaning what is preventing you from that, and there is no dispute that this verse was revealed as a rebuke to those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk, and it was in the year nine of the Hijra, one year after the conquest, and the departure: is moving quickly from one place to another for something that happened. His statement: You moved heavily to the earth its origin is you moved heavily, the ta' was assimilated into the tha' because of its proximity to it, and the alif of connection was brought to reach the pronunciation of the consonant, and similar to it: adrakū, atīrū, and atīrū, and Al-Kisa'i recited: The sleeper follows her when he misses her, and the taste is sweet when he follows the kiss Al-A'mash read ataqalatum in the original form, and its meaning is you were slow, and it was transitive with ila because it includes the meaning of inclination and devotion, and it was said that its meaning is: you inclined to reside in your land and remain in it. ataqalatum was read as a question, and its meaning is a rebuke, and the factor in the circumstance is what is in ma lakam of the meaning of the verb, as if it was said: what prevents you, or what do you do if it is said to you? And ila al-ard is related to ataqalatum and as mentioned above. His statement: are you satisfied with the life of this world means with its pleasures instead of the hereafter, like the statement of the Most High: And if We willed, We could have made from you angels on the earth, succeeding you meaning instead of you, and similar to it is the statement of the poet: She made us a cold drink of Zamzam water and put it to cook. That is, instead of Zamzam water, and the cooking is a stick that is set up in the corner of the house for the air, and water is hung on it to cool it, and the meaning of in the hereafter is in the side of the hereafter, and in contrast to it is except a little meaning except for insignificant enjoyment that is not worthy of attention, and it is possible that what is meant by little is nothingness, since there is no relation between the finite and the transient and the infinite and the everlasting, and it appears that this heaviness did not come from the whole, since it is far-fetched that they all apply to slowness and heaviness, but rather it is from the aspect of relating what occurs from some to the whole, and it is common and widespread.
9:39: His statement: 39- If you do not go forth, He will punish you. This is a severe threat and a confirmed warning for those who do not go forth with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He will punish you with a painful punishment. That is, He will destroy you with a severe, painful punishment. It was said that it is only in this world, and it was said that it is more general than that. His statement: And He will replace you with another people. That is, He will make them for His messengers in place of you, people who will not delay when they need them. There is a difference of opinion about who these people are. Some say they are the people of Yemen, and some say they are the people of Persia. There is no basis for specifying them without evidence. His statement, And do not harm him at all is connected to replaces, and the pronoun is said to be for God, and it is said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: that is, do not harm God at all by not obeying His command to mobilize, or do not harm the Messenger of God at all by not supporting him and mobilizing with him. And God is over all things competent, and among His powers is your punishment and your replacement.
9:40: His saying: 40- "If you do not support him, God has already supported him" meaning if you abandon supporting him, God will take responsibility for it, for He supported him in situations of fewness, and made him prevail over his enemy by force and subjugation, or He will support him from those who supported him when there was only one man with him at the time when those who disbelieved expelled him while he was "the second of two" meaning one of two, and they were the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. And it was read with a sukoon on the ya'. Ibn Jinni said: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' narrated it, and its reason is to make the ya' sukoon in imitation of the alif. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is like the reading of al-Hasan "what remains of usury", and like the saying of Jarir: He is the Caliph, so impose what he has approved for you. The past of determination has no deviation in his rule. His saying: When they were in the cave is a substitute for When he brought him out is a partial substitute. The cave is a hole in the mountain called Thawr, which is the famous Cave of Thawr, and it is a mountain near Mecca. The story of his exit, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca to Medina with Abu Bakr and their entry into the cave is well-known and mentioned in the books of biography and hadith. His saying: When he said to his companion is a second substitute: that is, the time when he said to Abu Bakr: Do not be sad, God is with us meaning leave the sadness, God is with us with His victory, support and assistance, and whoever God is with will not be defeated, and whoever is not defeated has the right not to be sad. His saying: So God sent down His tranquility upon him. Tranquility means calming his mind and reassuring him until his fear went away and he was safe. The pronoun in upon him refers to Abu Bakr. It was also said that it refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. What is meant by the tranquility that descended upon him is that he was protected from any cause of fear occurring to him. The pronoun in upon him refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is supported by the pronoun in He supported him with soldiers you did not see, which refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is supported by these soldiers, which are the angels, as was the case on the day of Badr. It was also said that there is no objection to the pronoun referring from upon him to Abu Bakr and from He supported him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because that is common in the Qur’an and in the speech of the Arabs. And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, meaning the word of polytheism, which is their call to Him and their calling to idols. And the word of God is the highest. Al-A’mash and Ya’qub read word in the accusative case based on made, while the rest read it in the nominative case as a new sentence. Al-Farra and Abu Hatim have weakened the reading of the accusative, and in the separating pronoun, I mean it, there is confirmation of the superiority of His word in elevation and that it is specific to Him and no one else, and the word of God is the word of monotheism and the call to Islam. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise, meaning He is the Victorious, the Subduer, and He does nothing but what is wise and right.
9:41: Then when he threatened those who did not go forth with the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and gave him examples that he mentioned, he followed it with the decisive command, saying: 41- Go forth, whether you are light or heavy. That is, whether you are light or heavy. It was said that it means alone or together, and it was said that it means active or inactive, and it was said that it means the poor and the rich, and it was said that it means young men and old men, and it was said that it means men and knights, and it was said that it means those who have no children and those who have children, and it was said that it means those who precede except in war, like the vanguard, and those who lag behind, like the army, and other things were said. There is nothing to prevent the verse from being interpreted in all of these meanings, because the meaning of the verse is: Go forth, whether the movement is easy for you or heavy. It was said: This verse was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the ill, and it was said that the abrogating verse was His saying: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth 3:100. It was said that it is decisive and not abrogated, and excluding the blind and the lame by His saying: There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame and excluding the weak and the ill by His saying: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the ill is a specification, not an abrogation, assuming that these are included under His saying: Whether light or heavy, and it appears that they are not included under the generality. His saying: And strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of God contains the command to strive with your lives and wealth and makes it obligatory upon the servants, so the poor strive with themselves, and the rich with their wealth and themselves. Jihad is one of the most important and greatest obligations. It is a communal obligation, no matter how many people are fighting the enemy and repelling him. If only all the Muslims in a country or countries are fighting the enemy, then it is obligatory for them as an individual obligation. The reference in his saying: That to what came before regarding the command to mobilize and the command to jihad is better for you means a great good in itself, and better than calm and ease if you only knew that and knew the virtuous things and distinguished them from the lesser ones.
9:42: His saying: 42- "If it had been a near gain and a short journey, they would have followed you." Al-Zajjaj said: If it had been the one being invited to, then it was omitted because of the indication of what preceded it, and the gain: what is offered of worldly benefits. The meaning: a near gain, not far. "And a short journey" is in apposition to what preceded it: meaning a journey that is intermediate between near and far, and everything that is intermediate between excess and deficiency is intended. "But the distance was too far for them." Abu Ubaidah and others said: The distance is the journey to a distant land, and it is said from it a difficult journey. Al-Jawhari said: The distance with the dammah is from clothing, and the distance also: the distant journey, and they may have said it with the kasrah, and what is meant by this is the Battle of Tabuk, as it was a distant and difficult journey. And Isa bin Omar read the verse Ba’dat ‘alayhim al-shaqqah with a kasra on the ‘ayn and the shin. And they will swear by God meaning those who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk while you are saying If we were able, we would have gone out with you meaning if we were able to go out and found what we needed there from what is necessary we would have gone out with you. This sentence is a master in place of the answer to the oath and the conditions. His saying They will destroy themselves is a substitute for his saying They will swear because whoever swears falsely has destroyed himself or it is a state: meaning destroying themselves and putting themselves in the position of destruction And God knows that they are liars in their oath that they will swear to you. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told to go forth… 1:18, he said this when they were ordered to go forth for the Battle of Tabuk after the conquest, and when he ordered them to go forth in the summer when the palm trees were in bloom and the fruits were good and they desired shade and the way out was difficult for them, so God revealed: Go forth, whether light or heavy. Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Sheikh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment. He said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) called forth a tribe of the Arabs and they were reluctant to go forth, so God revealed this verse and withheld rain from them and that was their punishment. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: When the verse: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment was revealed, some people had stayed behind in the deserts who were teaching their people. The believers said: There are still some people in the deserts and they said: The people of the deserts have perished. So the verse: And it is not for the believers to go forth all together was revealed. Abu Dawud, Ibn Abi Hatim, An-Nahhas and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: If you do not go forth the verse said: It was abrogated by And it is not for the believers to go forth all together. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: If you do not aid him - God has aided him he said: He mentioned what happened at the beginning of his affair when he was sent, saying: So I will do that to him, and I will aid him as I aided him then and he was the second of two. Abu Nu`aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Shihab and Urwah: They rode in every direction, meaning the polytheists, seeking the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They sent to the people of the waters, ordering them and assigning them a great load. They came to Thawr, the mountain in which was the cave and in which was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they climbed over it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr heard their voices, so Abu Bakr became afraid and was overcome with worry and fear. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Do not be sad, for God is with us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplicated, and tranquility descended upon him from God, so God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and the believers, the verse. Ibn Shahin, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Habshi ibn Junadah, who said: “Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, if one of the polytheists were to raise his foot, he would see us. He said: O Abu Bakr, do not be sad, for God is with us.” And Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Zuhri regarding his statement: When they were in the cave, he said: It is the cave in the mountain called Thawr. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il, and Ibn Asakir in his history narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then God sent down His tranquility upon him, he said: Upon Abu Bakr, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was always tranquil. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr entered the cave of Hira’, and Abu Bakr said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If one of them could see where he stepped, he would see me and you. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you think of two, with God as their third, O Abu Bakr? Indeed, God sent down His tranquility upon you and supported me with soldiers that they did not see.” And al-Khatib narrated in his history on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, Then God sent down His tranquility upon him, he said: Upon Abu Bakr, as for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, tranquility was upon him. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And He has made the word of those who disbelieve the lowest, he said: It is associating partners with God. And the word of God is the highest, he said: There is no god but God. Al-Faryabi and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, he said: The first part of Bara’ah that was revealed was: Go forth, whether light or heavy, then the beginning and the end of it were revealed. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Malik. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Light or heavy, he said: Active and not active. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hakam regarding the verse: Busy and not busy. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: In hardship and ease. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, he said: Young men and middle-aged men. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Young men and old men. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: They said: Among us are the heavy-handed, the needy, the poor, and the busy. So God revealed: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and He refused to excuse them unless they went forth light or heavy, and for what they were doing. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: A man came who they claimed was Al-Miqdad, and he was a great and fat man. He complained to him and asked him to give him permission, but he refused. So this was revealed: Go forth, whether light or heavy. When this verse was revealed, the people were upset about it, so God abrogated it and said: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the sick, the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why don’t you go to war against the yellow people so that you may capture the daughter of the great Roman ruler? Two men said: O Messenger of God, you know that women are a trial, so do not tempt us with them, so give us permission. So he gave them permission, and when we set off, one of them said: It is only fat for the first eater. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out and nothing was revealed to him about that. When he reached some of the way, the verse was revealed to him while he was on some of the hills: If it had been a near gain and a short journey, they would have followed you. And the verse was revealed to him: God has pardoned you for giving them permission. And the verse was revealed to him: Only those ask your permission who do not believe in God and the Last Day. And the verse was revealed to him: Indeed, they are unclean, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If it had been a near gain, he said: Near booty, but the distance was too far for them. He said: The journey. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: And God knows that they are liars, he said: They were able to go out, but it was a delay from themselves and a lack of interest in jihad.
9:43: The question in 43- May God forgive you, why did you give them permission? is a denial from God Almighty to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, since he gave permission to those who asked him for permission to stay away before it was clear who among them was truthful in his excuse that he presented, and who was lying in it. And in the mention of his forgiveness for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, there is evidence that this permission issued by him was contrary to what was best, and in this there is a gentle rebuke from God, the Most High, and it was said that this is a rebuke to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, for giving permission to the hypocrites to go out with him, not for giving them permission to stay away from going out. The first is better, and God, the Most High, has given him permission in Surat An-Nur by saying: So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whomever you wish among them. It is possible to reconcile between the two verses by saying that the rebuke here is directed to the permission before verification until it is clear who is truthful from who is lying, and the permission there is directed to the permission after verification, and God knows best. It was said: His saying: May God forgive you is the opening of a speech, as you say: May God guide you, honor you, and have mercy on you. How did you do such and such? This is what Makki, An-Nahhas, and Al-Mahdawi narrated. According to this interpretation, it is good to stop at May God forgive you. According to the first interpretation, it is not good. Do not be afraid that the first interpretation is what is required by the wording according to the Arabic language, and there is no reason to take it out of its Arabic meaning. In the verse there is evidence of the permissibility of his, may God bless him and grant him peace, ijtihad, and the issue is recorded in the principles. It also indicates the legitimacy of avoiding haste and being deceived by the appearances of things, and even in until it becomes clear to you who are truthful for the purpose, as if it was said: Why did you hasten to give them permission, and why not make it feminine until it becomes clear to you the truth of those who are truthful among them in the excuse they presented, and the lie of those who are lying among them in that?
9:44: Then the Almighty mentioned that it was not the custom of the believers to ask permission from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to stay away from jihad, rather it was their custom that if he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave permission to one of them to stay away, it would be difficult for him. So He said: 44- Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your permission to fight. This is based on the fact that the meaning of the verse is that they should not fight, with the negation letter omitted. It was said that the meaning is: The believers do not ask your permission to stay behind out of dislike for jihad. It was said that the meaning of asking permission for something is dislike for it. As for what the apparent meaning of the wording requires, the meaning is: The believers do not ask your permission for jihad, rather it is their custom to rush to it without hesitation or anticipation of your permission, let alone asking your permission to stay behind. Al-Zajjaj said: that they fight is in the accusative case with an implied in: meaning that they fight. And God is Knowing of the righteous, and they are those who did not ask permission.
9:45: 45- Only those who do not believe in God and the Last Day ask your permission to sit out of jihad and stay behind from it are those who do not believe in God and the Last Day and they are the hypocrites. Belief in God is mentioned first, then in the Last Day secondly in both places, because they are the motivators for jihad in the way of God. His statement: And their hearts are in doubt is in apposition to His statement: Those who do not believe and the past tense was used to indicate the realization of doubt in their hearts, which is suspicion. His statement: So in their doubt they waver means in their doubt that has settled in their hearts they are confused, and wavering is confusion. The meaning is: These who ask your permission are not believers, but rather doubters and confused, not guided to the right path, and they do not know the truth.
9:46: His statement: 46- "And if they had intended to go out, they would have prepared for it some equipment." That is, if they were truthful in what they claim and tell you about, that they intended to fight with you, but they did not have the equipment for the fight that was needed, they would not have neglected to prepare and obtain the equipment before the time of the fight, as the believers prepare for it. So the meaning of this statement is that they did not intend to go out at all, nor did they prepare for the fight. The equipment is what the fighter needs of provisions, a mount, and weapons. His statement: But God disliked their going out means, but God disliked their going out, so they were discouraged from going out. So the meaning is: They did not go out, but were discouraged, because God’s dislike of their going out necessitates their being discouraged from going out. Going out means that God prevented them from going out with you and let them down, because they said: If we are not given permission to sit, we will corrupt and incite against the believers. It was said that the meaning is: If they wanted to go out, they would have prepared for it, but they did not want it because God disliked it. His statement: And it was said, ‘Sit with those who sit’ It was said that the one who said it to them was Satan, with what he casts into them of whisperings. It was said that some of them said it to each other. It was said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it out of anger with them. It was said that it is an expression of abandonment, meaning that God put sitting in their hearts as an abandonment of them. The meaning of with those who sit is with those who are harmed, such as the blind, the sick, the women, and the children. It contains blame, disparagement, and disparagement of them that is not hidden.
9:47: His statement: 47- If they had gone out with you, they would have only increased you in confusion. This is a consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for the believers for the hypocrites' failure to return. And confusion: corruption, backbiting, causing discord and rumors. It was said that this exception is disconnected: that is, they did not increase your strength, but they sought confusion. And it was said that the meaning is: they will only increase you in what you hesitate about in opinion, confusion, so it is connected. And it was said that it is an exception from the most general of the general: that is, they would only increase you in confusion, so the exception is from the section of the connected, because confusion is among what something is true of. His statement: And they would have placed themselves among you, seeking to cause you discord. Idda': speed of movement, and from it is the saying of Waraqa ibn Nawfal: I wish I was a tree trunk in it, so I could hide and put it there It is said: Awda’a al-Ba’eer means to walk quickly. It is also said: Ida’a means to walk at a trot. Khalal is the gap between two things. The plural is Khalal meaning the gaps that are between the rows. The meaning is: They seek to cause corruption among you with what they invent of lies that include slander and gossip that lead to corruption between people. His statement: They seek to cause you discord. It is said: I sought it for him. And Abghitihu means: I helped him in seeking it. The meaning is: They seek to cause discord among you with what they do of incitement and corruption. It is also said: Discord here means polytheism. The phrase and among you are those who listen to them is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, while the situation is that among you are those who listen to what they say of lies and transmit it to you, and are affected by that, the disagreement between you and the corruption of your brothers. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers and what would happen from them if they went out with you, so His perfect wisdom required that they not go out with you, and He disliked their going out with you. Their situation if they went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, does not contradict what was mentioned previously of his rebuke for giving them permission to stay behind, because he hastened to give them permission, and he did not know from their conditions if they went out that they would do these actions, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was rebuked for his haste in giving them permission before he could tell who among them was truthful in his excuse and who was lying. For this reason, God, the Exalted, said in what follows in this surah: But if God returns you to a party of them and they ask your permission to go out, say, ‘You will never go out with me’ [al-Fath], and He said in Surah al-Fath 48:Those who stayed behind will say when you set out to take spoils [al-Fath] until His saying: Say you will not follow us.
9:48: His saying: 48- They had sought discord before meaning they had sought to cause corruption and chaos and to divide the word of the believers and to scatter them before this battle in which they stayed behind from you. As was said by Abdullah bin Ubay and others But God refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers hate it. His saying: And they turned matters upside down for you meaning they diverted them from one matter to another, and they plotted tricks and schemes for you, and from this is the saying of the Arabs to turn a heart if he is revolving around tricks and schemes, turning his mind around and pondering them. And it was read and they turned with the lightening until the truth came meaning to an end which is the coming of the truth, which is victory and support for you and the command of God appeared by honoring His religion and making known His law and subduing His enemies, and it was said: the truth is the Qur'an and they were averse meaning while the situation was that they were averse to the coming of the truth and the appearance of God's command, but that was in spite of them.
9:49: 49- And among them meaning the hypocrites is he who says to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Give me permission to stay away from jihad and do not tempt me meaning do not cause me to fall into temptation: meaning sin if you do not give me permission and I stay away without your permission. It was said that its meaning is: Do not cause me to perish by going out. Indeed, they have fallen into temptation meaning they have fallen into temptation itself, which is the temptation of staying away from jihad and the false excuse. The meaning is that they thought that by going out or by not being given permission they would fall into temptation, and by this staying away they fell into the great temptation. The expression falling indicates that they have fallen into it as someone falling from the top to the bottom, and that is more severe than merely entering into temptation. Then He threatened them for that by saying: And Hell will surely encompass the disbelievers meaning it encompasses them from all sides, they will not find a way out of it, and they will not be able to get out of it under any circumstances. Abdul Razzaq in Al-Musannaf and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Amr bin Maymun who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did two things for which he was not commanded to do anything: his permission for the hypocrites and his taking of prisoners, so God revealed: “God has pardoned you. Why did you give them permission?” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah who said: Have you heard of a better reproach than this? He began with the pardon before the reproach, and said: “God has pardoned you. Why did you give them permission?” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: God has pardoned you and the verse, he said: People said they asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for permission, so if he gives you permission then stay, and if he does not give you permission then stay. An-Nahhas narrated in his Naskh on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: “God has pardoned you. Why did you give them permission?” and the three verses, he said: It was abrogated by But when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whomever you wish of them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and An-Nahhas in his Naskh narrated from him regarding his statement: Those who believe in God will not ask your permission 2:100. He said: This is an expression for the hypocrites when they asked permission to stay away from jihad without an excuse, and God excused the believers and said: But when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whomever you wish among them. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan also narrated from him regarding his statement: They will not ask your permission 2:100. He said: It was abrogated by the verse in Surat al-Nur 24:The believers are only those who have believed in God and His Messenger 2:100 to Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. So God made the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) the one with the highest views in that, whoever goes out to fight goes out to fight with virtue, and whoever stays back stays back without difficulty, God willing. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: But God disliked their going out, he said: their going out. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So He held them back, he said: He detained them. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: If they had gone out with you, they would not have increased you except in confusion, he said: These are the hypocrites in the Battle of Tabuk. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: And they would have placed their ranks among you, he said: They would have hastened among you. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they would have placed their ranks among you, he said: They would have turned aside, seek to cause you discord, they would delay you, Abdullah bin Nabtal, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, Rifa’ah bin Tabut, and Aws bin Qayzi, and among you are those who listen to them, who narrate your hadiths to them, and are not hypocrites, and they are spies for the hypocrites. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu’aym narrated in Al-Ma’rifah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to go out for the Battle of Tabuk, he said to Jadd bin Qays: O Jadd bin Qays, what do you say about fighting the Banu Al-Asfar? He said: O Messenger of God, I am a man who has women, and whenever I see the women of the yellow people, I will be tempted, so give me permission and do not tempt me. So God revealed: And among them is he who says, ‘Give me permission’ (al-Baqarah 2:170). Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Aisha. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not tempt me he said: Do not expel me. Unless they fall into temptation meaning into expulsion. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: And do not tempt me he said: Do not make me sin. Unless into temptation he said: Unless into sin. The story of Tabuk is mentioned in the books of hadith and biographies, so we will not prolong its mention.
9:50: His saying: 50- If good befalls you meaning good for any reason that happened as indicated by its occurrence in the scope of the condition, and the same is said about the calamity, and the good and the calamity that occur in the battle are included as indicated by the context as a primary entry, so among what is true of good is booty and victory, and among what is true of calamity is disappointment and defeat, and this is mention of another type of the evil consciences of the hypocrites and the evil of their actions, and the report of the greatness of their enmity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers, for the harm of good, and the joy of calamity from the greatness of what indicates that they have reached the limit in enmity, and the meaning of they turn away is that they returned to their families from the places of meeting and the places of speaking while they were happy with the calamity that befell the believers, and the meaning of their saying: We have already taken our matter before meaning we took precautions for ourselves and took firmness, so we did not go out to fight as the believers went out until what befell them befell them From the calamity.
9:51: Then when they said this statement, God ordered His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to respond to them by saying: 51- Nothing will happen to us except what God has decreed for us meaning in the Preserved Tablet, or in His Book revealed to us. The benefit of this response is that if a person knows that what God has decreed will happen, and that everything that befalls him of good or evil is by the decree and judgment of God, then calamities will become easy for him, and he will not find the bitterness of the gloating of enemies and the schadenfreude of envy. He is our Master meaning He is our Supporter and the One who makes the outcome for us and makes His religion prevail over all religions. Trusting in God means entrusting matters to Him, and the meaning is that it is the right of the believers to make their trust specific to God, the Exalted, and not to trust in anyone else. Talhah ibn Masraf read yusibna with a shaddah on the ya'. A'yun Qadi al-Rayy read yusibna with a shaddah on the noon, which is a mistake because the report is not confirmed, and it was responded with something like the saying of God, the Exalted: Will His plan remove that which enrages him? Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that nothing will happen to us except what God has chosen for us of victory over you or martyrdom.
9:52: According to this statement, his saying: 52- "Say: Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things?" is a repetition for the purpose of emphasis, and the first is more appropriate so that each of the two answers that God Almighty commanded His Messenger to answer them with is useful for a benefit other than the benefit of the other, and establishing is better than emphasis, and the meaning of Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things? is do you await for us anything but one of the two good qualities: either victory or martyrdom, and both of them are good for us, and good is the feminine of better, and the meaning of the question is rebuke and reprimand and we await for you one of the two evils for you: either that God will afflict you with a punishment from Himself meaning a calamity descending from the sky and He will destroy you with His punishment, or with a punishment for you by our hands meaning that God will make us prevail over you by killing, capturing, looting, and capturing. The letter fa in fatarabasu is eloquent, and the imperative is for threatening, as in His statement: Taste, for you are the mighty, the generous. That is, wait for us for what we have mentioned of our end, for we are waiting with you for what will be your end, and then you will see what pleases us and displeases you. Al-Bazzi and Ibn Falih read hal tarbasuun with a pronounced lam and a doubled ta. The Kufians read it by assimilating the lam into the ta. The rest read it with a pronounced lam and a soft ta.
9:53: His saying: 53- "Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly, it will never be accepted from you." This command means condition and reward, because God Almighty does not command them to do what He will not accept from them. The meaning is: If you spend willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you. It was said that it is a command in the sense of report: that is, if you spend willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you. It is like his saying: Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. In it is the indication of the equality of the two matters in not being accepted, and the accusative of willingly or unwillingly is in the state, so they are two sources in the position of the two derivatives: that is, spend willingly without the command of God and His Messenger or unwillingly by the command of them. The matter from them was called compulsion because they are hypocrites who do not obey the command, so they were with their command that they do not obey like those who are forced to spend, or obedient without compulsion from your leaders or forced by them, and the phrase Indeed, you were a wicked people is an explanation for not accepting their spending. And wickedness: rebellion and insolence, and it was previously explained linguistically and legally.
9:54: Then the Almighty explained the reason that prevented their expenditures from being accepted, saying: 54- And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger. That is, their disbelief in God and His Messenger made the reason that prevented acceptance three things: The first: disbelief, the second: that they do not pray under any circumstances except in a state of laziness and sluggishness, because they do not hope for reward nor fear punishment, so their prayer is nothing but hypocrisy to people and showing off Islam, which they conceal is contrary to, and the third: that they do not spend their money except unwillingly, and they do not spend it willingly because they consider spending it as putting it in a waste due to their lack of faith in what God and His Messenger promised.
9:55: His saying: 55- So do not let their wealth or their children impress you. Admiration for something means being pleased with it, amazed by its beauty. It was said that it is with a kind of pride and belief that nothing else is equal to it. The meaning is: Do not admire the wealth and children they have. God only wants to punish them with them in the life of this world. With what happens to them of grief and sadness when the Muslims seize it and take it by force from their hands, even though it is the adornment of their lives and the delight of their eyes. Likewise, in the Hereafter, He punishes them with the punishment of the Fire because of their lack of gratitude to their Lord who gave it to them, and their abandonment of what is required of them in terms of zakat, and giving charity with what is right to give charity. It was said that there is an order in the speech, and the meaning is: Do not let their wealth or their children impress you in the life of this world. God only wants to punish them with them in the Hereafter because they are hypocrites, so they spend unwillingly and are punished for what they spend. His saying: And their souls will perish while they are disbelievers. Perishing means coming out with difficulty. The meaning is that God wants their souls to perish and their spirits to leave while they are disbelievers due to their refusal to accept what the prophets brought and what the messengers were sent with, and their determination to disbelieve and their persistence in misguidance.
9:56: Then God Almighty mentioned another type of the ugliness of the hypocrites, saying: 56- And they swear by God that they are of you meaning that they are of your group in the religion of Islam and submission to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the Book of God Almighty but they are not of you in that only in their outward appearances and not in their inward selves but they are a people who fear meaning that they fear that what happened to the polytheists of killing and captivity will happen to them, so they show you Islam out of caution from them, not out of truth.
9:57: 57- If they find a refuge to which they can resort and protect themselves from you, from a fortress or other or caves plural of cave, from cave of yaghir. Al-Akhfash said: It is possible that it is from aghar yaghir, and caves: caves and tunnels, and they are the places in which one hides, and from it the cave of water and the cave of the spring, and the meaning is: If they find places to disappear in their persons fleeing from you or an entrance from the entrance: meaning a place they enter from the places that are not caves. Al-Nahhas said: The original of it is mutadakhil, the ta was changed to a dal, and it was said that its original is muddakhil. Abi read mutadakhil and it was narrated from him that he read mandakhil with a nun. Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Ibn Muhaisin read aw madkhal with a fathah on the mim and a sukoon on the dal. Al-Zajjaj said: It is read aw madkhal with a damma on the mim and a sukoon on the dal. The rest read it with emphasis on the dal and a damma on the meem, they turned to him meaning they sought refuge in him and put themselves in him. And the condition is that and they are rushing meaning they are rushing so fast that nothing can stop them, from the word jamah of the horse: if the bridle does not stop it, and from this the poet said: Glory be to God, and bring it like a commotion of burning palm fronds Meaning: If they found any of these mentioned things, they would have quickly fled to it, escaping from the Muslims. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The hypocrites who stayed behind in Madinah began to tell bad report about the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, saying: Muhammad and his companions had exhausted themselves in their journey and perished. Then they heard that their hadith was being denied and that the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and his companions were well, so they were upset by that, so God revealed: If good befalls you, it distresses them (al-Baqarah 2:17). Sunayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If good befalls you, it distresses them means: If good befalls you in your journey, this Battle of Tabuk, it distresses them. He said: Al-Jadd and his companions, meaning Al-Jadd ibn Qays. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi: “Say: Nothing will ever happen to us except what God has decreed for us” He said: Except what God has decreed for us. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things? He said: Victory or martyrdom. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: Or by our hands He said: Killing with swords. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Al-Jadd bin Qais said: When I see women, I cannot be patient until I am tempted, but I help you with my money. He said: It is about him that the verse was revealed: “Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly” 1:13. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: So let not their wealth impress you he said: This is from the old sayings, he says: Do not let their wealth or children impress you in this worldly life, God only wants to punish them with it in the Hereafter. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: God only wants to punish them with it in the Hereafter. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And their souls depart while they are disbelievers he said: Their souls depart in this worldly life and they are disbelievers he said: This is a verse in which there is an inversion. Abu Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: So let not their wealth impress you he said: Do not be deceived and they depart he said: Their souls depart, he said: In this world while they are disbelievers. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: If they could find a refuge 3:10, he said: A refuge is a safe place in the mountains, and caves are caverns, and an entrance is a passage. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi: And they rush headlong 3:10, he said: They hurry.
9:58: His saying: 58- And among them is he who slanders you. This is a mention of another type of their ugliness. It is said: Yalmazhu if he finds fault with him. Al-Jawhari said: Lamz means fault, and its origin is pointing with the eye and the like. He slandered him, yalmazhu, yalmazhu, and a man is a lamaz, and lamza: meaning a faultfinder. Al-Zajjaj said: I slandered a man, lamzahu, and lamzahu, with a kasra or damma on the meem: if I found fault with him, and so is his hamza. The meaning of the verse: And among the hypocrites is he who finds fault with you in regard to charity: meaning in distributing and dividing it. It was narrated from Mujahid that he said: The meaning of Yalmazuk is He begs you and asks you, and the opinion of the linguists is the first as Al-Nahhas said. And it was read Yalmazuk with a damma on the meem, and Yalmazuk with a kasra and with emphasis. The majority read it with a kasra and a lightened if they are given from it meaning from the charity as much as they want they are satisfied with what happened from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they do not criticize him, because they have no goal except the debris of this world, and they have nothing to do with religion. and if they are not given from it meaning from the charity what they want and ask for then they are angry meaning if they are not given, then the anger will suddenly come upon them. The benefit of the sudden if is that the condition is sudden for the reward and attacks it. The sudden if has taken the place of the fa of the reward.
9:59: 59- And if they had been satisfied with what God and His Messenger gave them meaning what God imposed on them and what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them of charity. The answer to if is omitted: meaning it would have been better for them, for in what He gave them there is immediate and deferred good. And they said, 'God is sufficient for us; God will give us from His bounty, and so will His Messenger.' That is, they said this statement when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them what was theirs: meaning God is sufficient for us, He will give us from His bounty and His Messenger will give us after this what we hope for and expect. Indeed, we are desirous toward God that He will give us from His bounty what we hope for.
9:60: His saying: 60- The alms are only for the poor. When the hypocrites criticized the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the distribution of the alms, God explained to them its destination, in order to prevent their slander and to put an end to their troublemaking. Only is one of the forms of restriction, and the definition of alms is for the type: that is, the type of these alms is limited to these mentioned categories and does not go beyond them, rather it is for them and not for others. Scholars have differed as to whether it is obligatory to divide the charity into these eight categories, or is it permissible to give it to some and not others, according to what the imam or the charity giver sees fit? Al-Shafi’i and a group of scholars held the former view, while Malik and Abu Hanifah held the latter view, and this is what ‘Umar, Hudhayfah, Ibn ‘Abbas, Abu al-‘Aliyah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Maymun ibn Mihran said. Ibn Jarir said, and this is the view of most scholars: The first scholars cited as evidence the restriction in the verse and the hadith of Ziyad ibn al-Harith al-Sada’i, as narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Daraqutni, who said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and pledged allegiance to him. Then a man came and said: Give me some of the charity. He said to him: “God was not pleased with the ruling of a prophet or anyone else regarding charity until he ruled on it and divided it into eight categories. If you are one of those categories, I will give you.” The others responded that the restriction in the verse is only to clarify the spending and the recipient, not to make it obligatory to include all categories, and that the chain of transmission of the hadith includes ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An’am al-Ifriqi, who is weak. What supports what others have said is the saying of God the Almighty: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you. Charity refers to what is obligatory as well as what is recommended. It was authentically reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I have been commanded to take charity from your rich and give it to your poor. Malik claimed consensus on the other statement. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: He means the consensus of the Companions, as he does not know of any of them who disagreed with him. His statement: for the poor He mentioned them first because they are more in need than the rest, according to the well-known view, due to their extreme poverty and need. Scholars have differed on the difference between the poor and the needy. Yaqub ibn al-Sikkit, al-Qutaibi and Yunus ibn Habib said: The poor are in a better situation than the needy. They said: Because the poor are the ones who have some of what is sufficient for them and sustains them, and the needy are the ones who have nothing. This was the opinion of some of the scholars of jurisprudence, including Abu Hanifa. Others said the opposite, and they made the needy in a better situation than the poor, and they cited as evidence the words of God the Almighty: As for the ship, it belonged to the needy. He informed that they had a ship from the ships of the sea, and it may be worth a sum of money. This is supported by the Prophet’s seeking refuge from poverty with his saying: O God, let me live as a poor person and let me die as a poor person. This is what al-Asma’i and other linguists believed, and al-Tahawi narrated it from the Kufians. It is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi’i and most of his companions. Some people said: The poor and the needy are the same, there is no difference between them. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi’i, and this was the opinion of Ibn al-Qasim and the rest of the companions of Malik, and Abu Yusuf said the same. Some people said: The poor is the needy who is self-sufficient, and the needy is the beggar. Al-Azhari said this, and Ibn Shaban chose it, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Other statements have been said, but the abundance of them does not provide any significant benefit. The best explanation of the nature of the needy is what was proven from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Al-Bukhari. Muslim and others narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The poor person is not the one who goes around among the people and is turned away with a morsel or two, or a date or two. They said: Who is the poor person, O Messenger of God? He said: The one who does not find enough wealth to make him independent, and no one notices him so that he can be given charity, and he does not ask people for anything. His saying: and those who work on it means the messengers and collectors whom the Imam sends to collect the zakat, for they deserve a share of it. There is a difference of opinion about the amount they take from it. It was said that it is an eighth. This was narrated from Mujahid and Al-Shafi’i. It was also said that it is according to the wages they do, this was narrated from Abu Hanifa and his companions. It was also said that they are given from the House of God according to their wages, this was narrated from Malik. There is no basis for this, for God has informed us that they have a share of the charity, so how can they be prevented from it and given from something else? They differed as to whether it is permissible for the worker to be Hashemite or not? Some people forbade it, while others permitted it. They said that he is given from something other than charity. His saying: And those whose hearts are to be reconciled are a people who were in the early days of Islam. It was said: They are the infidels whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to reconcile so that they would convert to Islam. They did not enter Islam by force or the sword, but rather by gifts. It was also said: They are a people who converted to Islam outwardly but did not convert to Islam well, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to reconcile them by gifts. It was also said: They are those Jews and Christians who converted to Islam. It was also said: They are a group of the great polytheists who had followers to whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave gifts so that they would reconcile their followers to Islam. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave gifts to a group of those who converted to Islam outwardly, such as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, and Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza. He gave each one of them one hundred camels to reconcile them with that, and he gave others who were less than them. Scholars differed as to whether the share of those whose hearts were to be reconciled remained after the emergence of Islam or not. Omar, Al-Hasan and Al-Shaabi said: This category was cut off with the glory and emergence of Islam. This is well-known from the Maliki school of thought and the people of opinion. Some Hanafis claimed that the companions unanimously agreed on this. A group of scholars said: Their share remains because the imam may need to reconcile people to Islam, and Omar cut them off because he saw the glory of the religion. Yunus said: I asked Al-Zuhri about them and he said: I do not know of its abrogation. According to the first opinion, their share returns to all other categories. His statement: And in slaves means in freeing slaves by buying slaves and then freeing them. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Omar, and Malik, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq and Abu Ubaid said the same. Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Zuhri and Ibn Zayd said: They are the freed slaves who suffer from the charity on the money of the contract. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i and the people of opinion and a narration from Malik. It is better to interpret what is in the verse according to both opinions, because the slaves are believed to buy and free a slave, and to help the freed slave with the money of the contract. His statement: and the debtors are those who are burdened with debts and cannot pay them. There is no disagreement on this except for the one who is in debt out of foolishness, then he is not given from it or from anything else unless he repents. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) helped from charity those who bear a burden and guided us to help them from it. His statement: and in the way of God is the fighters and the guards who are given from the charity what they spend in their fighting and guarding, even if they are rich. This is the opinion of most scholars. Ibn Omar said: They are the pilgrims and those performing Umrah. It was narrated from Ahmad and Ishaq that they considered Hajj to be from the way of God. Abu Hanifa and his two companions said: The fighter is not given unless he is poor and cut off from it. His saying: And the wayfarer is the traveler, and the way is the road, and the traveler is attributed to it because he is constantly on it, and what is meant is the one who has lost all means of transportation while traveling from his country and his place of residence, then he is given from it even if he is rich in his country, and even if he finds someone to lend him. Malik said: If he finds someone to lend him, then he is not given. His saying: An obligation from God is a confirmed source, because his saying: Zakat is only for the poor means: God has imposed zakaah on them. The meaning is: That zakaah is limited to these categories is a binding ruling that God has imposed on His servants and has forbidden them from exceeding it. And God is Knowing of the conditions of His servants, Wise in His actions. It was said: An obligation is erected by an implied verb: that is, God imposed that as an obligation. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: If you say, why did He change from lam to fi in the last four? I said: To indicate that they are more firmly established in their entitlement to charity than those previously mentioned. It was said: The point of the just is that the money is given to the first four categories so that they can dispose of it as they wish, and in the last four categories the money is not given to them, rather it is given to the needs considered in the characteristics for which they are entitled to the share of zakat. This is what was said. Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri who said: "While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was distributing, Ibn Dhi Al-Khuwaysira At-Taymi came to him and said: Be just, O Messenger of God. He said: Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just? 'Umar Ibn Al-Khattab said: Give me permission to strike off his head. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Leave him, for he has companions whom one of you will consider insignificant compared to their prayer, and whom one of you will consider insignificant compared to their fasting. They will depart from the religion as an arrow departs from its target." The hadith continued until he said: "And about them was revealed the verse: 'And among them is he who criticizes you concerning the charities.'" Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And among them is he who criticizes you, he said: He asks you for something and begs you. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: He will slander you. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: “When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divided the spoils of Hunayn, I heard a man saying: ‘This is a division that was not intended for God.’ So I went to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him. He said: ‘May God have mercy on Moses, he was harmed more than this and he was patient.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: This verse abrogated every charities in the Qur’an: ‘The charities are only for the poor’ 10:18. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah regarding His statement: ‘The charities are only for the poor’ 10:18, he said: ‘If you wish, you can make it for one of the eight categories that God has named, or two or three categories.’ Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-‘Aliyah, al-Hasan, ‘Ata’, Ibrahim, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr. Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: ‘The poor are the poor Muslims and the needy who go about.’” Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: The poor person who is in distress, and the needy person who is not in distress. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Umar regarding his statement: Zakat is only for the poor, he said: They are the People of the Book. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And those who work on it, he said: The seekers and givers of charity. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And those whose hearts are to be reconciled, he said: They are people who used to come to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and have become Muslims, and he used to give them some charity. If he gave them charity and they gained something good from it, they would say: This is a good religion. But if it was otherwise, they would criticize him and abandon him. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed who said: “Ali ibn Abi Talib sent a gold coin to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from Yemen, and he divided it among four of those who were to be reconciled: Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis Al-Hanthali, Alqamah ibn Alathah Al-Amiri, Uyaynah ibn Badr Al-Fazari, and Zayd Al-Khail Al-Ta’i. The Quraysh and the Ansar said: He will divide it among the leaders of Najd and leave us? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I am only trying to reconcile them.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri that he was asked about those whose hearts were to be reconciled. He said: Whoever converts to Islam from a Jew or a Christian. I said: Even if he is wealthy? He said: Even if he is wealthy. These narrated on the authority of Abu Ja’far who said: Today, those whose hearts are not to be reconciled. These also narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil regarding his statement: and for the slaves, he said: They are those who were freed from slavery. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Nakha’i. It was also narrated on the authority of Omar bin Abdullah that he said: The share of slaves is two halves: one half for each slave who claims to be a Muslim, and the other half is used to buy slaves from those who prayed and fasted and who had converted to Islam before, male and female, who are freed for God. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Ubayd and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he saw no harm in a man giving from his zakat for Hajj and freeing a slave from it. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri that he was asked about the debtors, he said: the people of debt. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far regarding his statement: and the debtors he said: he is the one who is asked about blood money or a calamity that befalls him, and in the cause of God he said: they are the fighters, and the wayfarer he said: the one who is stranded, he is given an amount that reaches him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: the wayfarer is the poor guest who stays with the Muslims. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Charity is not permissible for a rich person except for five: the one who collects it, the man who buys it with his own money, the one who is in debt, the one who fights in the cause of God, or a poor person who receives charity and gives some of it to a rich person.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Charity is not permissible for the rich or the one who has a strong livelihood. Ahmad narrated on the authority of a man from Banu Hilal who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mention something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud and Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin `Adi bin Al-Khayyar who said: “Two men told me that they came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) during the Farewell Pilgrimage while he was distributing the charity and asked him for some of it. He looked up and down at us and saw that we were strong. He said: If you wish, I will give it to you, but the rich or the strong who can earn a living have no share in it.”
9:61: His saying: 61- And among them This is another type of what God narrated of the scandals and ugliness of the hypocrites, and that is that they used to say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a way of slander and blame, He is an ear. Al-Jawhari said: It is said that a man is an ear if he hears what everyone says, whether it is one person or a group, and their intentions are the same, may God make them retarded. If they hurt the Prophet and spread their tongues against him, and he hears of that, they apologize to him and he accepts that from them, because he hears everything that is said to him and believes it. The Arabs called the one who hears what is said to him an ear as an exaggeration, because they called him the organ that is the instrument of hearing, so that his entirety is as if he is a hearing ear. Similar to that is their saying to the observer an eye. Their hurting him is their saying: He is an ear, because they attributed to him that he believes everything that is said to him and does not differentiate between the true and the false, being deceived by his patience with them and his pardon of their crimes, out of generosity, patience, and overlooking. Then God answered their saying, and said: Say, ‘An ear is better for you,’ in addition to the reading of the majority. Al-Hasan read it with the tanween, and so did Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr from him, as if it was said: Yes, he is an ear, but yes, an ear because he is an ear that is better for you, and he is not an ear for anything else, like their saying a man of truth, meaning goodness and righteousness. The meaning is that he hears good but does not hear evil. Adhan was read with a sukoon on the dhal and a damma on it, then it was explained that it is an ear of good by saying: He believes in God and believes in the believers meaning he believes in God and believes in the believers because he knows that their faith is pure, so the lam in for the believers is for emphasis, as the Kufians said, or it is related to a deleted source, as al-Mubarrad said. The majority read and mercy in the nominative case in apposition to Adhan. Hamzah read it in the genitive case in apposition to good. The meaning according to the first reading is that it is an ear of good and that it is a mercy for the believers, and according to the second reading it is that it is an ear of good and an ear of mercy. An-Nahhas said: This is far-fetched according to the Arabs, meaning the genitive reading because there is a distance between the two nouns, and this is ugly in the genitive case. Meaning: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave permission for the hypocrites to be good and mercy for them, as he did not reveal their secrets or disgrace them. It is as if he said: He is permission as you said, but it is permission for good for those who do not have permission for evil. So he accepted their statement about him, except that he interpreted it as praise and commendation for him, even though they intended by it to criticize and criticize his intelligence. The meaning of for those among you who believe is those who showed faith even if they were not true believers. And those who harm the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with what was mentioned above of their saying: He is permission. And similar things that are true to be considered harm to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). For them is a painful punishment, meaning severe pain. Ibn Abi Ubla read and mercy for the believers in the accusative case as a reason for an omitted reason: meaning and mercy for you, He gives you permission.
9:62: Then he mentioned that one of the ugly things about hypocrites is their willingness to swear false oaths, so he said: 62- They swear to you by God to please you, and the address is to the believers. This is because the hypocrites were in private slandering the believers and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When this reached the Messenger of God and the believers, the hypocrites came and swore that they did not say what was reported about them, intending with these false oaths to please the Messenger of God and the believers with him. God denied this about them and said: And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should please Him. That is, they are more deserving of that than pleasing the believers with false oaths, for if they had feared God and believed in Him and abandoned hypocrisy, that would have been more appropriate for them. The singular pronoun in please Him is either to magnify the divine presence by singling it out in mention, or because there is no difference between pleasing God and pleasing His Messenger, so pleasing God is pleasing His Messenger, or what is meant is: God is more deserving that they should please Him and so is His Messenger, as Sibawayh said, and An-Nahhas preferred it, or because the pronoun is used in the place of a demonstrative pronoun, so it refers to one and multiple, or the pronoun refers to the one mentioned, and it applies to both. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is that His Messenger is more deserving that they should be pleased with Him. God is the opening of a sentence, just as you say, Whatever God wills and you will. This sentence, I mean, And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should be pleased with Him is in the accusative case as a state, and the answer to If they are believers is omitted: meaning, if they are believers, then let them please God and His Messenger.
9:63: His saying: 63- Do they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger, then for him is the fire of Hell? Al-Hasan and Ibn Hormuz read Have you not learned with the upper syllable. The rest read with the lower syllable: and the opposition is the occurrence of this in a limit, and that in a limit like the quarrel: it is said that someone opposed someone else: meaning he became in the limit of someone else's limit then for him is the fire of Hell. The majority read with the opening of the hamza as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning it is true that for him is the fire of Hell. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: The second an is replaced by the first, and Al-Mubarrad claimed that this statement is rejected, and that what Al-Jarmi said is correct: the second an is repeated for emphasis because the speech is long. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is that the fire is obligatory for him, and Al-Mubarrad denied it and said: This is a mistake because the open, shaddah an does not begin with it and the predicate is implied. It was read with the kasrah of the hamza. Sibawayh said: It is a good reading, and he recited: If my mounts become bored with its atmosphere, then I am unruly in my share of the matter. The accusative case of Khalid is in the state of the state, and the reference in his saying: that is to what was mentioned of the punishment, and it is the subject and its predicate is the great disgrace, meaning the disgrace that reaches the point that no one else can reach, which is humiliation and disgrace.
9:64: His saying: 64- The hypocrites are afraid that a surah will be sent down to them. It was said: It is a piece of report and not a command. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is to beware. So the meaning according to the first opinion is that the hypocrites were afraid that the Qur'an would be sent down to them. According to the second opinion: It is the command for them to beware of that. And that it will be sent down is in the accusative case: that is, from being sent down. It is permissible according to Sibawayh's opinion that it be in the genitive case based on the estimation of from and its application. It is permissible for the accusative to be on the two objects. Sibawayh permitted I warned Zayd and recited: Beware of things that do not harm you and be safe from things that do not save you from fate. And the object of the object is prevented from being accusative. The meaning of upon them is upon the believers in the matter of the hypocrites, on the condition that the pronoun refers to the believers, and it is better for the pronoun to refer to al-Munafiqun 63:that is, in their matter informs them meaning the hypocrites of what is in their hearts of what they conceal in addition to what they show, and even though they know what is in their hearts, the meaning of the Surah informing them is to inform them that the believers have known what is in their hearts, then God commanded His Messenger to respond to them, so He said: Say, ‘Mock on, for God will bring out what you fear’ is a threatening command: that is, do the mocking, for God will bring out what you fear from appearing until the believers know about it, either by sending down a Surah, or by informing His Messenger of that or something like that.
9:65: His statement: 65- And if you ask them, they will surely say, 'We were only conversing and joking.' That is, if you ask them about what they said of attacking the religion and slandering the believers after that reaches him and God informs you of it, they will surely say, We were only conversing and joking, and we had nothing to do with your affair or the affair of the believers. Then God commanded him to answer them, saying: Say, 'Was it at God and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?' The question is for rebuke and rebuke, and He established that this had happened from them and did not pay attention to their denial, because they were lying in their denial. Rather, He made them as if they had acknowledged that this had happened from them, as He made the one being mocked, and the ba is for the letter of negation, because that only happens after the mockery has occurred and been established.
9:66: Then he said: 66- Do not apologize forbidding them from engaging in false apologies, as that is not acceptable from them. Al-Wahidi narrated from the imams of language that the meaning of apology is to erase and cut off the trace of the sin, from their saying, The house apologized if it was ruined, and The water apologized if it was cut off. You have disbelieved meaning you showed disbelief in what happened from you of the aforementioned mockery after your belief meaning after showing faith while you concealed disbelief If We pardon a party of you and they are those who sincerely believed and abandoned hypocrisy and repented from it. Al-Zajjaj said: The party in the language is the group.
