Ibn Al-Anbari said: The word plural is used for the singular among the Arabs We punish a party because they were criminals because they were criminals persisted in hypocrisy and did not repent from it. It was read We punish with a noon and a taa above it in the passive form and with a taa below it in the active form, which is God, the Most High. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Nabtal bin Al-Harith used to come to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and sit with him and listen to him, then he would convey his talk to the hypocrites. He was the one who said to them: Muhammad is only an ear; whoever tells him something he believes it. So God revealed about him: And among them are those who annoy the Prophet and say, ‘He is only an ear’ (al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi that he said: A group of hypocrites gathered, among them Khalas bin Suwaid bin Samit, Mukhshi bin Himyar and Wadi’ah bin Thabit, and they wanted to attack the Prophet (peace be upon him), but some of them forbade each other and said: We are afraid that Muhammad will reach you and attack you. Some of them said: Muhammad is only an ear, we swear to him and he will believe us. So this was revealed: And among them are those who annoy the Prophet (al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement: He is only an ear means that he hears from everyone. God the Almighty said: A better ear for you, who believes in God and believes in the believers. That is, he believes in God and believes in the believers. At-Tabarani, Ibn Asakir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umair bin Saad, who said: This verse was revealed about him: And they say, ‘He is an ear.’ That is because Umair bin Saad used to hear the conversations of the people of Madinah, so he would come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and whisper to him until they were annoyed by Umair bin Saad and hated to sit with him. He said: He is an ear, so it was revealed about him. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that a man from the hypocrites said: By God, these are the best and most noble of us, and if what Muhammad says is true, they are worse than donkeys. A man from the Muslims heard him and said: By God, what Muhammad says is true and you are worse than a donkey. The man went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. The Prophet sent for the man and called him and said: What made you say what you said? So he began to curse and swear by God that he had not said that, and the Muslim man began to say: O God, the truthful one is true and the liar is false. So God revealed concerning that: They swear to you by God to please you (al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi something similar, and he named the Muslim man Aamer bin Qais from the Ansar. Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Dahhak: Do they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger (al-Baqarah 2:17) means: he is hostile to God and His Messenger. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid concerning His statement: The hypocrites are wary (al-Baqarah 2:17) that he said: They say the statement among themselves, then they say: Perhaps God will not disclose this to us. Abu Nu`aym narrated in al-Hilyah from Shuraih bin Ubayd that a man said to Abu al-Darda’: O group of reciters, why are you more cowardly than us, stingier when asked, and more generous with your mouthfuls when you eat? Abu Darda' turned away from him and did not respond to him with anything. He informed Umar ibn al-Khattab about that. Umar went to the man who had said that, took his garment, strangled him and led him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The man said: We were only conversing and joking. God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if you ask them, they will surely say, 'We were only conversing and joking.' Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar that he said: A man said in a gathering one day during the Battle of Tabuk: We have never seen anyone like our reciters, neither more greedy, nor more lying, nor more cowardly in battle. A man in the gathering said: You have lied, but you are a hypocrite. I will tell the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. That reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur'an was revealed. Abdullah said: I saw him clinging to the saddle of the Messenger of God's camel, may God bless him and grant him peace, while stones were hitting him and he was saying: O Messenger of God, we were only conversing and joking. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saying: Was it at God, His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? It was narrated by Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Uqayli in al-Du'afa, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Khatib in the narration of Malik on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I saw Abdullah ibn Ubayy running in front of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the stones were hitting him, and he was saying: O Muhammad, we were only joking and playing, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saying: Was it at God, His verses, and His Messenger that you were mocking? Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, who said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on a campaign to Tabuk, and there were some hypocrites before him, they said: Does this man hope that the palaces and fortresses of Ash-Sham will be opened for him? No way, no way. So God informed His Prophet of that, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hold these men back for me. So he came to them and said: You said such and such. They said: O Prophet of God, we were only joking and playing, so God revealed about them what you hear. Something similar to this has been narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of a group of the Companions. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: If We pardon a group, he said: The group is a man and a group of people.
9:67: His statement: 67- The hypocrites, men and women, are of one another. Here he mentioned the general conditions of the hypocrites, and that their males are like their females in this, and that they are extremely hypocritical and far from faith. It indicates the denial that they are from the believers, and it was rejected because of their statement: And they swear by God that they are from you. Then he separated that general statement by explaining the opposite of their condition to the condition of the hypocrites, so he said: They enjoin what is wrong, which is everything that is ugly according to reason or the law, and forbid what is right, which is everything that is good according to reason or the law. Al-Zajjaj said: This is connected to his statement: And they swear by God that they are from you, but they are not from you, meaning they are not from the believers, but some of them are from one another: meaning they are similar in enjoining what is wrong and forbidding what is right. And they withhold their hands, meaning they are stingy with what should be given of money in charity, kinship, and jihad. So withholding is a metaphor for stinginess, just as expansion is a metaphor for generosity. And forgetfulness is abandonment: meaning they abandoned what He commanded them to do, so He abandoned them out of His mercy and grace, because true forgetfulness cannot be applied to God Almighty, but rather it is applied to Him here as a matter of similarity known in the science of rhetoric. Then He ruled that they were immoral: meaning they departed from the obedience of God to His disobedience, and this construction indicates that they are the ones who are perfect in immorality.
9:68: Then he explained the ultimate state of the people of hypocrisy and disbelief, which is 68- the fire of Hell and they will abide therein is a predicate state: meaning they are destined to remain forever. In this verse is evidence that a promise is said about evil as it is said about good: It is sufficient for them meaning it is sufficient for them, they do not need anything more than its punishment, and despite that, God has cursed them meaning He has expelled them and removed them from His mercy and for them is a lasting punishment meaning another type of punishment that is permanent and will not be separated from them.
9:69: His statement: 69- Like those before you He likened the state of the hypocrites to the disbelievers who were before them, turning from the third person to the second person, and the kaf is in the nominative case as a predicate of a deleted subject: meaning you are like those before you, or its place is in the accusative case: meaning you did as those nations before you did. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that God promised the disbelievers the fire of Hell, a promise as He promised those before you, and it was said that the meaning is: you did as those before you did in abandoning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, so the complement was deleted. Then he described the state of those disbelievers who were before them, and explained the reason for their likening to them and comparing their state to their state, that they were stronger than those hypocrites and disbelievers who were contemporary with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in strength and more wealth and children, so enjoy that is, enjoy their portion that is, your share that God has decreed for them of the pleasures of this world, so you have enjoyed that is, your share that God has decreed for you, just as those before you enjoyed their portion that is, you benefited from it just as they benefited from it, and the purpose of this comparison is to criticize these hypocrites and disbelievers because of their resemblance to the disbelievers who came before them in enjoying what God had provided for them. It has been said: What is the benefit of mentioning enjoying the portion in the case of the first ones once, then in the case of the hypocrites a second time, then repeating it in the case of the first ones a third time? The answer is: God Almighty blamed the first people for enjoying the worldly pleasures they were given, and for depriving them of the happiness of the Hereafter because they were absorbed in those pleasures. So when God Almighty decided this, He returned and likened the state of the hypocrites to their state, and that would be the ultimate in exaggeration. His saying: And you waded like those who waded is connected to what preceded it: that is, like the group who waded, or like the wading that they waded. It was said: Its origin is like those, so the nun was deleted. It is better to say: that which is a relative pronoun like who and what, and it is used to express the singular and the plural. It is said: I waded into the water, wading and khayyadan, and the place is a ford, which is what people cross on foot and on horseback. Its plural is makhad and makhawwad. It is said: from it the people waded into the hadith and they negotiated about it, meaning: you waded into the causes of this world and amusement and play. It was said regarding the command of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to deny: that is, you entered into that. The reference in his saying: those is to those described by these descriptions from the similes, and those to whom they are likened, their deeds have become in vain, meaning they have become invalid. What is meant by deeds is what they did that is in the form of obedience, not these deeds mentioned here, for they are sins. The meaning of in this world and the hereafter is that they are invalid in every case. As for its invalidity in this world, it is because what results from their actions in it will not be attained by them, rather what they hope for of wealth will become poverty, and what they hope for of honor will become humiliation, and what they hope for of strength will become weakness. As for in the Hereafter, it is because they will be sent to the torment of the Fire and will not benefit from anything they did of the actions that they thought were obedience and drawing near to God. And those are the losers, meaning those who are firmly established in complete loss in this world and the Hereafter.
9:70: 70- Has there not come to them meaning the hypocrites the report of those before them meaning their report that has significance, which is what they did and what was done to them, and since he likened their condition to their condition in what preceded about the generality of the simile, he mentioned six groups of them here whose report the Arabs had heard, because their country, which is the Levant, is close to the country of the Arabs, so the question is for confirmation, and the first of them: the people of Noah, who were destroyed by drowning, and the second: the people of Aad, who were destroyed by the barren wind, and the third: the people of Thamud, who were seized by the blast, and the fourth: the people of Abraham, who were seized by mosquitoes, and the fifth: the people of Madyan, who were the people of Shu'ayb, who were seized by the earthquake, and the sixth: the people of the overturned, which are the villages of the people of Lot, and God destroyed them with the stones that He rained upon them, and they were called overturned because they were overturned until their top became their bottom, and overturning is overturning their messengers came to them with clear proofs meaning The messengers of these six groups, and it was said: the messengers of the people of the overthrown cities because their messenger was Lot and he sent a messenger to each of their cities, and the fa in God would not wrong them is for conjunction with an implied meaning indicated by the speech: that is, they denied them so God destroyed them and He did not wrong them by that, because He sent His messengers to them who warned them and cautioned them but they were wronging themselves because of what they did of disbelieving in God and not obeying His prophets, and this structure indicates that their injustice to themselves was continuous. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: They enjoin evil, he said: It is denial, he said: It is the worst of evils, and forbid what is right, the testimony that there is no god but God and the acknowledgment of what God has revealed, which is the greatest of good deeds. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they withhold their hands, he said: They do not extend them to spend in charity, which is right. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: They forgot God, so He forgot them, he said: They abandoned God, so He abandoned them from His honor and reward. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Like those before you, he said: The actions of the disbelievers are like the actions of the disbelievers. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: How similar tonight is to last night: Like those before you who were stronger than you until His saying: And you plunged as they plunged These are the Children of Israel. We resemble them. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, we will follow them until if a man entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority regarding His saying: By their character he said: By their religion. They also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The character is the religion. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding His saying: Then enjoy their character he said: By their share in this world. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding His saying: And you plunged as they plunged he said: You played as they played. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding His saying: And the overturned lands he said: The people of Lot, their land was overturned, turning its top into its bottom.
9:71: His statement: 71- Some of them are allies of others meaning their hearts are united in affection, love and sympathy because of what brought them together in the matter of religion and brought them together in belief in God. Then He explained their praiseworthy descriptions as He explained the descriptions of those before them from the hypocrites, saying: They enjoin what is right meaning what is known in the law and not reprehensible, including the oneness of God Almighty and leaving the worship of other than Him. And they forbid what is wrong meaning what is reprehensible in the religion and not known. He singled out establishing prayer and paying zakat for mention from among the acts of worship because they are the two great pillars with regard to bodies and wealth. The meaning of this has already been mentioned. And they obey God in doing what He commanded them to do or forbade them from leaving. The reference with those is to the believing men and women who are characterized by these descriptions, and the seen in God will have mercy on them is to exaggerate the fulfillment of the promise. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might cannot be overcome. Wise in His words and actions.
9:72: Then he mentioned the details of what falls under mercy in general, considering mercy in the Hereafter, so he said: 72- God has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow. The explicit is in place of the implicit for the sake of increasing the statement, and the meaning of the rivers flowing beneath the gardens is that they flow beneath their trees and their floods, and its investigation has been presented in the cow. And good dwellings means houses in which they live of pearls and rubies, and Gardens of Eden it is said: Eden in a place: if he resides in it, and from it the mine, it was said that it is the highest part of Paradise, and it was said its middle, and it was said palaces of gold that no one enters except a prophet or a friend or a martyr, he described Paradise with descriptions: the first: the rivers flowing beneath it, the second: that they will remain in it forever, the third: the goodness of its dwellings, and the fourth: that it is the house of Eden: meaning an uninterrupted residence, this is according to what is the meaning of Eden in the language, and it was said that it is a proper noun, and the indefiniteness in Ridwan is for disparagement: meaning and Ridwan is insignificant and conceals from Ridwan God is greater than all of that Which God has given them, and in it is evidence that nothing of the blessings, no matter how great and immense, is comparable to the pleasure of God Almighty, and that the slightest pleasure of it is not equal to any of the physical pleasures, even if they are at an ultimate level with no ultimate limit. O God, be pleased with us with a pleasure that is not tainted by discontent and is not marred by misery, O He in whose hand is all good, its small and great. The reference in His saying: That is to what came before of what God promised to the believing men and women. It is the great attainment, not every attainment that people consider to be attainment. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: They enjoin what is right, he said: They call to belief in God and His Messenger and spending in the way of God and whatever is from obedience to God. And they forbid what is wrong, from polytheism and disbelief. He said: Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is an obligation of God’s obligations that God has prescribed for the believers. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Some of them are allies of others, he said: Their brotherhood in God, they love one another for the sake of God’s majesty and allegiance to God. And it has been proven from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong from the hadiths that are well-known. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: I asked Imran bin Husain and Abu Hurairah about the interpretation of the verse: And goodly dwellings in gardens of perpetual bliss. They said: It has been revealed to the expert. We asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about it and he said: A palace of pearls in Paradise. In that palace are seventy houses of red rubies. In each house are seventy houses of green emerald. In each house are seventy beds. On each bed are seventy mattresses of every color. On each bed is a woman from the houris. In each house are seventy tables. On each table are seventy types of food. In each house are seventy female servants. The believer is given strength every morning that he will be able to bear all of that. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Gardens of perpetual bliss. He said: The place of residence of the man who will be in it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Their place of residence is in it forever. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: And the pleasure of God is greater, meaning: If they are informed that God is pleased with them, then it is greater to them than gifts and praises. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will say to the people of Paradise: O people of Paradise, and they will say: At your service, our Lord, and at your pleasure, and goodness is in your hands. He will say: Are you satisfied? They will say: Our Lord, why should we not be satisfied when you have given us what you have not given to any of your creation? He will say: Shall I not give you something better than that? They will say: O our Lord, what is better than that? He will say: I will bestow My pleasure upon you, and I will never be angry with you after that.”
9:73: The command to the Prophet (peace be upon him) to carry out this jihad is a command to his nation after him. Jihad against the infidels is to fight them until they submit, and jihad against the hypocrites is to establish proof against them until they abandon it and believe in God. Al-Hasan said: Jihad against the hypocrites is to establish the prescribed punishments against them, and Qatada chose this view. It was said in explaining it that the hypocrites were the ones who did most of the things that required the prescribed punishments. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a claim that has no proof, and the sinner is not a hypocrite, rather the hypocrite is the one who is always in his heart of hypocrisy, not the one who is outwardly adorned with his limbs, and the reports of those who were punished testify by their context that they were not hypocrites. His statement: 73- And be harsh with him Harshness is the opposite of compassion, and it is hardness of heart and roughness of side. It was said: This verse abrogated everything from forgiveness, reconciliation and pardon.
9:74: Then he mentioned that among the characteristics of the hypocrites is that they swear false oaths, and he said: 74- They swear by God that they did not say it. The scholars of interpretation differed about the reason for the revelation of this verse. It was said that it was revealed about Al-Jalas bin Suwaid bin Al-Samit and Wadiah bin Thabit. This is because when the Qur’an was frequently revealed during the Battle of Tabuk regarding the hypocrites and their condemnation, they said: If Muhammad is truthful about our brothers who are our leaders and best, then we are worse than donkeys. Aamer bin Qais said to him: Yes, by God, Muhammad is truthful and believed, and you are worse than donkeys. Aamer informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that. Al-Jalas came and swore by God that Aamer was lying, and Aamer swore that he had said something, and he said: O God, reveal something to your Prophet. So it was revealed. It was said that the one who heard that was Asim bin Adi, and it was said Hudhayfah, and it was said that his wife’s son heard it: meaning the wife of Al-Jalas, and his name was Umair bin Saad. Al-Jalas intended to kill him so that he would not tell his story. It was said: This verse was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubay, the leader of the hypocrites, when he said: Our example and that of Muhammad is like that of someone who says: Fatten your dog and it will eat you, and If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed of that, and Abdullah bin Ubay came and swore that he did not say it. It was said: It was said: It was the saying of all the hypocrites and that the verse was revealed about them. Assuming that the speaker was one or two, then attributing the saying to all of them is based on the agreement of the one who did not say or swear from the hypocrites with the one who said and swore. Then God responded to the hypocrites and their lies and showed that they swore falsely, so He said: And they had certainly said the word of disbelief, which is what was explained above despite the different previous sayings, and disbelieved after their Islam, meaning they disbelieved in this word after they had shown Islam even though they were disbelievers in secret. The meaning is that they did what necessitated their disbelief, assuming that their Islam was correct. His saying: And they intended what they did not attain. It was said: It was their intention to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of Al-Aqaba in the Battle of Tabuk. It was also said: They intended to tie the crown on the head of Abdullah bin Ubayy. It was also said: It was Al-Jalas’ intention to kill whoever he heard say that, so he informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. His saying: And they did not find fault except because God and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty. That is, they did not criticize or deny anything except what was worthy of praise and commendation, which was God enriching them from His bounty. The exception is devoid of the most general of the general, and it is similar to the saying of Al-Nabigha: There is no fault in them except that their swords have dents from the clashing of the battalions. And as the poet said: They did not resent the Umayyads except that they were patient when they got angry. It is an emphasis on praise with something resembling blame. These hypocrites were living in hardship, but when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, their livelihood expanded and their wealth increased. His statement, If they repent, it will be better for them means that if they repent and return to the truth, what they did of repentance will be better for them in their religion and their worldly life. Al-Jalas ibn Suwaid repented and his Islam was good, and in that is evidence of the acceptance of repentance from the hypocrite and the disbeliever. Scholars have differed about accepting it from the heretic. Malik and his followers were prevented from accepting it, because he did not know the validity of his repentance, since he always showed repentance and Islam. But if they turn away, that is, they turn away from repentance and faith, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world, by killing, captivity, and looting of wealth, and in the Hereafter, by the punishment of the Fire. And they will have no protector or helper on earth, to support them. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ka`b ibn Malik who said: When the Qur’an was revealed, mentioning the hypocrites, Al-Jalas said: By God, if this man is truthful, then we are worse than donkeys. Umair ibn Sa`d heard him and said: By God, O Jalas, you are the dearest of people to me, the best in my reputation, and the most difficult for me to have something happen to you that I dislike. You said something that if I mentioned it, it would disgrace you, and if I kept quiet about it, it would destroy me, and one of them is more severe for me than the other. So he went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned to him what Al-Jalas had said. Al-Jalas swore by God that he had not said it, but Umair had lied to me. Then God revealed: They swear by God that they did not say it Al-An`am 2:17. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: “Zayd bin Arqam heard a man from the hypocrites saying while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering a sermon: If this man is truthful, then we are worse than donkeys. Zayd said: By God, he is truthful and you are worse than donkeys. This was reported to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he denied the speaker, so God revealed: ‘They swear by God that they did not say it’ [the verse].” Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the shade of a tree and said: ‘A man will come to you. ’” He looks at you with the eyes of a devil, so if he comes to you, do not speak to him. Soon after, a blue-eyed man appeared, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and said: Why do you and your companions curse me? The man went and brought his companions and they swore by God that they did not say anything until he forgave them, and God revealed: They swear by God that they did not say anything verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: It was mentioned to us that two men fought, one of them from Juhayna and the other from Ghifar, and Juhayna were allies of the Ansar, so the Ghifarite defeated the Juhayni, so Abdullah bin Ubay said to the Aws: Support your brother, by God, our example and the example of Muhammad is as the one who said: Fatten your dog and it will eat you, by God, If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humble. A man from the Muslims went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he sent for him and asked him, and he began to swear by God that he did not say anything, so God revealed: They swear by God verse. There are different hadiths on this topic about the reason for this verse, and in what we have mentioned Sufficiency. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they intended that which they could not attain, he said: A man called Al-Aswad intended to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And they intended that which they could not attain, he said: They wanted to crown Abdullah bin Ubay with a crown. Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: A man was killed during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his blood money was set at twelve thousand. This is what is meant by his statement: And they resented nothing except that God and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty, he said: By taking the blood money.
9:75: The first lam, which is 75- If God gives us from His bounty is the lam of the oath, and the second lam, which is we will certainly give in charity is the lam of the answer to the oath and the condition. The meaning of we will certainly give in charity is to give charity, which is more general than the obligatory charity and other things, and to be among the righteous meaning among the group of righteous people from the believers who fulfill the obligations of religion and abandon its prohibitions.
9:76: 76- But when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away, averse. That is, when He gave them what they asked for of provision, they were stingy with it: that is, with what He gave them of His bounty, so they did not give in charity anything from it as they swore by. And turned away, that is, they turned away from obeying God and from giving in charity what God had given them of His bounty. And the situation is that and they were averse at all times before God gave them what He gave them of provision and after it.
9:77: His statement: 77- "So He made hypocrisy in their hearts as a consequence until the Day they meet Him." The subject is God, the Exalted: meaning, so God made hypocrisy in their hearts, deeply rooted in them, and continuing in them, "until the Day they meet Him." It was said that the pronoun refers to stinginess: meaning, so He made stinginess in what they had promised God as a consequence of hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him. Their stinginess: meaning, the recompense for their stinginess. The meaning of "So He made hypocrisy in their hearts as a consequence until that end" is that God, the Exalted, made the hypocrisy that was deeply rooted in their hearts until that end the consequence of their stinginess. The "ba in because they broke their promise to God" is for causality: meaning, because of their breaking their promise to Him of giving charity and righteousness. Likewise, the "ba in and because they used to lie" means, and because of their denial of what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought.
9:78: Then he denied them and said: 78- Do they not know meaning the hypocrites, and it was read with the upper case, addressing the believers, that God knows their secrets and their private conversations meaning everything they conceal of hypocrisy and everything they whisper among themselves of slandering the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and the religion of Islam, and that God is Knower of the unseen so nothing of the unseen things is hidden from Him, whatever it may be, and among that is what comes from the hypocrites.
9:79: His saying: 79- "Those who criticize those who volunteer" The relative pronoun is in the accusative case, or in the nominative case as a blame, or in the genitive case as a substitute for the pronoun in their secret and their private conversations. The meaning of "they criticize" is they find fault. Its explanation has been presented above. The volunteers: means the volunteers, and volunteering: is donation. The meaning is: that the hypocrites used to criticize the Muslims if they volunteered something from their money and gave it in charity, so they used to say: God does not need this, and they used to say: they did this only to show off, and it was not purely for God, and "in charity is related to they criticize": meaning they criticize them in their affair. His statement: And those who find nothing but their effort is in apposition to the volunteers: that is, they criticize the volunteers, and they criticize those who find nothing but their effort. It was also said that it is in apposition to the believers: that is, they criticize the volunteers among the believers, and those who find nothing but their effort. The word their effort is read with a fatha on the jim, and effort with a damma means energy, and with a fatha it means hardship. It was also said that they are two languages and their meaning is the same, and this has been explained previously. The meaning is that the hypocrites used to criticize the poor believers who used to give in charity what was in excess of their needs. His statement: and they mocked them is in apposition to they mocked them: that is, they mocked them for the insignificance of what they gave in charity, despite it being the effort of the poor and the most that he is able to do and is capable of. His saying: God mocked them means that He rewarded them for what they did of mocking the believers with the same, so God mocked them by humiliating them, degrading them, and tormenting them. The expression in this way is a form of similarity as in other verses. It was said that it is a supplication against them that God mock them as they mocked the Muslims. And for them is a painful punishment meaning permanent, ongoing, and extremely painful. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Askari in al-Amthal, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah, al-Barudi, Abu Nu`aym, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn `Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili, who said: “Thalaba ibn Hattab came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, ask God to grant me wealth.’ He said: ‘Woe to you, Tha`laba! A little that you can thank for is better than a lot that you cannot bear.’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, ask God to grant me wealth.’ He said: ‘Woe to you, Tha`laba! Don’t you like to be like me? If I wanted my Lord to make these mountains flow with me in gold, they would flow.’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, ask God to grant me wealth. By the One Who sent you with the truth, if God gives me wealth, I will give everyone his due right.’ He said: ‘Woe to you, Tha`laba! A little that you can thank for is better than a lot that you cannot bear.’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, ask God Almighty.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O God, grant him wealth.’ He said: ‘So he took sheep.’ It grew like worms until the city became too small for it, so he moved away and attended the prayer during the day with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he did not attend it at night. Then it grew like worms grow, so he moved away and did not attend the prayer at night or during the day except from one Friday to the next with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then it grew like worms grow and the city became too small for it. His place, so he moved away from it and did not attend Friday prayers or funerals with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he began to meet the riders and ask them about the report, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, missed him and asked him about him. They told him that he had bought sheep, and that the city was too small for him, and they told him his story. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to Tha’laba bin Hatib, woe to Tha’laba bin Hatib! Then God Almighty commanded His Messenger to take alms, and revealed: “Take alms from their wealth” the verse. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent two men, a man from Juhayna and a man from Banu Salamah, to take alms. He wrote for them the ages of the camels and sheep, how to take them and their faces, and he ordered them to pass by Tha’laba bin Hatib and a man from Banu Salim. So they went out and passed by Tha’laba and asked for alms. He said: Show me your letter. He looked at it and said: This is nothing but a tribute. Go until you branch off, then pass by me. So they went, and As-Salami heard of them and met them with the best of his camels. They said: You only have less than this. He said: I only seek to draw closer to God with the best of my wealth. So they accepted. When they finished, they passed by Tha’laba, and he said: Show me your letter. He looked at it and said: This is nothing but a tribute, go until I see what I think. So they went until they reached Madinah. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw them, he said before he spoke to them: Woe to Tha’laba bin Hatib, and he prayed for blessings for Al-Salami. God revealed: And among them are those who made a covenant with God the three verses. He said: Some of Tha’laba’s relatives heard it, so he went to Tha’laba and said: Woe to you, O Tha’laba, such and such has been revealed about you. He said: So Tha’laba came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my money. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has prevented me from accepting it from you. So he began to cry and throw dirt on his head. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is what you did to yourself. I commanded you and you did not obey me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not accept it from him until he left. Then he went to Abu Bakr and said: O Abu Bakr, accept my charity from me, for you know my status among the Ansar. Abu Bakr said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not accept it, and I accept it? Abu Bakr did not accept it. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab took over and came to him and said: O Abu Hafs, O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity. He said: And he is burdened by the Muhajireen, the Ansar, and the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Umar said: Neither the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor Abu Bakr accepted it. Should I accept it? He refused to accept it. Then Uthman took over and asked him to accept his charity. He said: Neither the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor Abu Bakr accepted it, nor Umar. Should I accept it from you? He did not accept it from him, so he died during the caliphate of Uthman, and in it was revealed: Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity “He said: This is about charity, and this hadith is narrated from the hadith of Muadh bin Rifa’ah from Ali bin Zaid from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Qasim bin Abd al-Rahman, the client of Abdullah bin Yazid bin Mu’awiyah from Abu Umamah al-Bahili. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And among them are those who made a covenant with God the verse, and that is that a man called Tha’laba from the Ansar came to a gathering and made them witness, and he said: If God gives me from His bounty, I will give every person with a right his right, and I will give charity from it, and I will give some of it to relatives, so God tested him and gave him from His bounty, but he broke his promise, so he angered God by breaking his promise, so God related his affair in the Qur’an. Abu al-Sheikh narrated from al-Hasan that a man from the Ansar is the one who said this, and his cousin died and he inherited money from him, but he was stingy with it and did not fulfill what he had promised. He made a covenant with God, but he followed it with hypocrisy in his heart until he meets Him. He said: Because they broke their promise to God and because they used to lie. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: When the verse on charity was revealed, we were carrying loads on our backs. Then a man came and gave a lot of charity. They said: He is a hypocrite. Abu Uqayl came with half a Sa’. The hypocrites said: God is independent of this man’s charity. Then the verse was revealed: Those who slander those who give themselves freely al-Baqarah 2:177. There are many narrations on this topic. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: Those who slander those who give themselves freely al-Baqarah 2:177, meaning they criticize those who give themselves freely.
9:80: God the Almighty informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that whether he asks for forgiveness from Him for the hypocrites or not is the same, because they are not worthy of asking for forgiveness from Him, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor of forgiveness from God the Almighty for them. It is like His Almighty saying: Say, 'Spend willingly or unwillingly, it will never be accepted from you.' Then He said: 80- If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will never forgive them. This is a statement of the lack of forgiveness from God the Almighty for the hypocrites, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked forgiveness for them frequently. This does not mean that if he had asked for more than seventy, it would have been acceptable, as in all other concepts of numbers. Rather, this means exaggeration in the lack of acceptance. The Arabs used to use this as a proverb in their speech when they wanted to exaggerate, and the meaning is that God will not forgive them, even if you ask forgiveness for them in an extremely large number. Some jurists have said that restricting this specific number indicates that an increase is acceptable, and this is indicated by what will come from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: I will increase to seventy. Some of them mentioned a reason for specifying seventy, saying: Seven is a noble number, because it is the number of the heavens, the earths, the seas, the regions, the stars, the limbs, and the days of the week, so each one of the seven was made into ten, because a good deed is worth ten times. It was said: Seventy was specifically mentioned because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said seventy takbirs over his uncle Hamzah, as if he said: If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times in return for your takbirs over Hamzah. The accusative of seventy is in the source, like their saying: I struck him twenty times. Then he explained the reason for not forgiving them by saying: That is because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger, meaning that this refusal was due to their disbelief in God and His Messenger. And God does not guide the wicked people, meaning the rebellious ones who go beyond obedience and transgress its limits. What is meant here is guidance that leads to what is desired, not guidance that means indication and showing the way.
9:81: Then the Almighty mentioned another type of the ugliness of the hypocrites, saying: 81- Those who stayed behind rejoiced at their sitting behind the Messenger of God. Those who stayed behind were the ones who were left behind, and they are those who asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hypocrites, so he gave them permission and left them behind in Medina in the Battle of Tabuk, or those whom God left behind and discouraged, or Satan or their laziness, or the believers, and the meaning of their sitting is their sitting. It is said: he sat, sitting, and someone else made him sit, Al-Jawhari mentioned its meaning, so it is related to joy: meaning those who stayed behind rejoiced at their sitting, and against the Messenger of God is in the accusative case as an adverb for their sitting. Al-Akhfash and Yunus said: The difference means the successor: meaning after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that is because the direction of the Imam that a person intends differs from the direction of the successor. Qatrib and Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of opposing the Messenger of God is opposing the Messenger when he set out and they stayed, so its accusative is as an object for it: meaning they sat down for the sake of opposing, or as a state like and the fight sent it: meaning opposing him, and what Al-Akhfash and Yunus said is supported by Abu Haywah’s reading of behind the Messenger of God. His saying: And they disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God. The reason for that is the stinginess of wealth and lives, and the absence of a motive for faith and a reason for sincerity and the presence of a deterrent from that, which is what they are in of hypocrisy, and in it is an allusion to the believers who sacrifice their wealth and lives in the cause of God because of the presence of a motive with them and the absence of a deterrent from them. And they said, ‘Do not go forth in the heat.’ That is, the hypocrites said to their brothers: This statement is to discourage them and break their energy and to advise each other to disobey the command of God and His Messenger. Then God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them: The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if they only understood. The meaning is: How can you, O hypocrites, flee from this slight heat, when the fire of Hell, which you will enter and abide in it forever, is more intense in heat than what you fled from? You only fled from a slight heat in a short time, and you fell into a great heat in a great time, rather an infinite one, forever and ever. I was like someone running to a difficult place, one of the paths of thunder. The answer to if in if they had understood is understood: that is, if they had understood that it was like that, they would not have done what they did.
9:82: His saying: 82- So let them laugh a little and cry a lot. These two commands mean report, and the meaning is: So they will laugh a little and cry a lot. They were brought in the form of a command to indicate that this is an inevitable matter and nothing else will happen. Little and much are in the accusative case as a source or circumstance: meaning laugh a little and cry a lot, or a little time and a lot of time. A recompense for what they used to earn. That is, a recompense because of what they used to earn of sins. The accusative case of recompense is in the accusative case as a source: meaning they will be recompensed with a recompense.
9:83: 83- If God returns you to a group of them Return is transitive like reply and return is intransitive, and the fa is to branch off what comes after it from what comes before it. He only said to a group because not all of those who stayed in Madinah were hypocrites, but there were others among them from the believers who had valid excuses, and among them were believers who had no excuse, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgave them and God accepted their repentance like the three who stayed behind, and an explanation of that will come. It was said that he only said: to a group, because among them were those who repented from hypocrisy and regretted staying behind, and they asked your permission to go out with you in another raid after this raid of yours, then say to them, You will never go out with me, nor will you fight an enemy with me meaning say to them that as a punishment for them, and because of the corruption in accompanying them as mentioned previously in His statement: If they had gone out with you, they would only have increased you in ruin. And it was read with the opening of the ya of with me in both places. It was read with a sukoon in both of them, and the phrase you were satisfied with sitting the first time is for the reason: that is, you will not go out with me and you will not fight because you were satisfied with sitting and staying behind the first time, which was the Battle of Tabuk, and the fa in so sit with the successors is to branch off what comes after it from what comes before it, and the successors are the plural of khalaf as if they left behind the goers, and what is meant by them is the one who stayed behind from going out. It was said that the meaning is: so sit with the corrupt ones, from their saying: So-and-so contradicted his family if he was corrupt among them, from your saying behind the milk: meaning it spoiled from staying too long in the water skin. Al-Asma'i mentioned its meaning. And it was read so sit with the successors and Al-Farra' said: its meaning is the dissenters. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Urwah that Abdullah bin Ubayy said: If you did not spend on Muhammad and his companions, they would have dispersed from around him. He is the one who said: The more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. So God revealed: Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I will add more than seventy. So God revealed: Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, God will never forgive them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ahmad, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu’aym in al-Hilyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: I heard Umar say: When Abdullah bin Ubayy died, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was called to pray over him. He stood over him. When he stood, I said: Is it Abdullah bin Ubayy, the enemy of God, who said such and such, and said such and such? I counted his days, and the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) was smiling, until when I said a lot, he said: O Umar, stay away from me, for I have been given a choice. It was said to me: Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them. If I had known that if I increased it to seventy, he would have been forgiven, I would have increased it. Then the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) prayed over him and walked with him until he stood at his grave until he finished. I was amazed at myself and my audacity towards the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), and God and His Messenger know best. By God, it was only a short time before these two verses were revealed: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) did not pray over a hypocrite after that until God took him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: And those who stayed behind rejoiced the verse, he said: About the Battle of Tabuk. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered the people to set out with him, and that was in the summer. Some men said: O Messenger of God, the heat is intense and we cannot go out, so do not set out in the heat. God said: “Say: The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood.” So He ordered him to set out. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: So let them laugh a little and weep much, that they are the hypocrites and disbelievers who have taken their religion as a joke and a game. God says: So let them laugh a little in this world and weep much in the Hereafter. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: But if God returns you to a party of them, that he said: It was mentioned to us that they were twelve men from the hypocrites, and about them what was said was said. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So sit with those who stayed behind, he said: They are the men who stayed behind from the conquest.
9:84: His statement: 84- "died is an attribute of someone, and forever" is an adverb of perpetuating the negation. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of his statement: "And do not stand at his grave" is that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, buried the dead, he would stand at his grave and pray for him, so he was forbidden from doing so here. It was said that its meaning is: Do not undertake the important tasks of repairing his grave. The phrase "they disbelieved" is an explanation for the prohibition. He only described them as immoral after describing them as disbelievers, because a disbeliever may be just in his religion, and lying, hypocrisy, deceit, cowardice, and malice are ugly in every religion.
9:85: 85- "And let not their wealth and children impress you. God only intends to punish them through them in this world and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers." Then He forbade His Messenger from being impressed by their wealth and children, which is a repetition of what came before in this Surah and a confirmation of its content. It was said that the previous verse was about one people, and this one was about others. It was said that this one was about the Jews, and the first was about the hypocrites, and other things were said. All that is needed in explaining this verse was presented in the first verse.
9:86: Then God the Almighty returned to rebuking the hypocrites, saying: 86- And when a surah is revealed meaning from the Qur'an, and it is possible that it is meant to be part of the surah, or to mean its entirety, and it was said that it is this surah: meaning Surat Bara'ah, and that in that they believed in God is an explanation of what is in the revelation of the meaning of saying, or a source from which the preposition was deleted: meaning that they believed, and the command to believe was presented before because engaging in jihad is not beneficial except after belief those of them of wealth ask your permission meaning those of virtue and wealth, those who have been given a long time, this is what Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said, and Al-Asamm said: the leaders and the great ones who are looked at, and He singled them out for mention because censure is more necessary for them, since they have no excuse for sitting and they said, Leave us meaning leave us that we will be with those who sit meaning those who are excused from the conquest, such as the weak and the chronically ill.
9:87: And the Khawaalif: the women who stay behind the men in sitting at home, the plural of Khalafah, and some of them allowed it to be the plural of Khalaf, which is someone who has no good in him. 87- And He has sealed their hearts and it is like His saying: God has sealed their hearts and its interpretation has been mentioned, so they do not understand anything that benefits or harms them, rather they are like livestock. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: When Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul died, his son Abdullah came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him to give him his shirt to shroud him in. He gave it to him, then he asked him to pray over him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up, and Umar stood up, took his garment and said: O Messenger of God, will you pray over him when God has forbidden you to pray over the hypocrites? He said: My Lord has given me a choice and said: “Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them,” and I will add to the seventy. He said: He is a hypocrite. So he prayed over him, and God revealed: And never pray over any of them who dies 1:13, so he stopped praying over them. Ibn Majah, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: The leader of the hypocrites died in Madinah and he left instructions that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) should pray over him and that he should be shrouded in his shirt. His son came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: My father left instructions that he should be shrouded in your shirt. So he prayed over him and put his shirt on him and stood at his grave. God revealed: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Those of wealth he said: The wealthy. These narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: They were content to be with the ones who stayed behind he said: With the women. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse that he said: They were content to sit as the women sat. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said: The ones who stayed behind are the women.
9:88: The purpose of the correction in His saying: 88- But the Messenger to the end is to indicate that the failure of these people to do so is not harmful, because the obligation of jihad has been carried out by those who are better than them and more sincere in intention, as in His saying: But if these disbelieve in it, then We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it. The explanation of jihad with wealth and lives has been presented, then the benefits of jihad are mentioned, so He said: And those will have good things, which is the plural of good, so it includes the benefits of this world and religion. It has been said that what is meant by it are beautiful women, as in His saying, the Most High: In them are good and beautiful things, and the singular form of goodness is with emphasis, then it is lightened, like easy and easy. The meaning of success has been presented, and what is meant by it here are those who win what is sought, and the repetition of the demonstrative pronoun is to magnify their status and magnify their matter.
9:89: And the gardens: the orchards. The rivers flowing beneath them, the eternity and the victory have been explained before, and the reference in His saying: 89- that is to what came before of the good things and success, and the preparation of the gardens described with that description, and the description of the victory as being great indicates that it is the complete individual from the types of victory. Al-Qurtubi narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said the good things: they are the beautiful women.
9:90: Al-A'raj and Al-Dahhak read 90- Al-Mu'adhdhiroon with a light pronunciation, from A'dhar, and Abu Kurayb narrated it from Abu Bakr from Asim, and the people of readings narrated it from Ibn Abbas. It is said in Al-Sahah: Ibn Abbas used to read: And the excusers came with a light pronunciation from A'dhar, and he would say: By God, it was revealed like this. Al-Nahhas said: Except that it is based on Al-Kalbi, and it is from A'dhar: if he exaggerated in the excuse, and from it is from andhar he has excused, meaning he exaggerated in the excuse. The majority read Al-Mu'adhdhiroon with a shaddah, and there are two views on it, one of them is that its origin is Al-Mu'adhdhiroon, so the ta' was assimilated into the dhal, and they are those who have an excuse, and from it is the saying of Labid: Until the year, then peace be upon you both. Whoever cries for a full year has apologized. Those who are excused for this are those who are justified in their apology. This has been narrated from Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj Ibn Al-Anbari. It has been said that it is from ‘adhdhar, which is the one who apologizes but has no excuse. It is said that ‘adhdhar’ in a matter means that he fell short and apologized for something that is not an excuse. This was mentioned by Al-Jawhari and the author of Al-Kashshaf. Those who are excused for this are those who are wrong, because they apologized with false excuses that have no basis. It has been narrated from Al-Akhfash, Al-Farra’, Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaidah that it is permissible to break the ‘ayn due to the meeting of two quiescent letters and to close it for the sake of following. Meaning: These Bedouins came with what they came with of excuses, whether true or false, according to both interpretations, in order for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give them permission to stay behind from the invasion. Another group did not apologize, but rather stayed away from the invasion without an excuse. They are the hypocrites among the Bedouins who denied God and His Messenger and did not believe or tell the truth. Then God, the Exalted, threatened them, saying: A painful punishment will befall those among them who disbelieved, meaning among the Bedouins, who were those who made false excuses, and those who did not apologize, but rather denied God and His Messenger, a painful punishment, meaning very painful, so it applies to the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the excuse-makers among the bedouins came, meaning those who had an excuse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar to that from him. Ibn al-Anbari also narrated in his book The Opposites that he used to say: May God curse the excuse-makers, and he read it with emphasis, as if the matter with him was that the excuse-maker with emphasis is the one who shows an excuse, making excuses without reality. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq regarding his statement: And the excuse-makers among the bedouins came, he said: It was mentioned to me that they were a group of Banu Ghafar who came and apologized, among them was Khafaf ibn Ima’, and they were called: The people of Amir ibn al-Tufayl. They said: If we go on a raid with you, the Bedouins of Tayy will raid our families and livestock.
9:91: When God the Almighty mentioned those who have excuses, He mentioned after them those who have valid excuses that excuse them from fighting. He began with the excuse in the original creation, saying: 91- Not upon the weak, who are the masters of time, old age, blindness, lameness, and the like. Then He mentioned the temporary excuse, saying: Nor upon the sick, and what is meant by sickness is everything that is called sickness linguistically or legally. It was said that it includes the sick, the blind, the lame, and the like. Then He mentioned the excuse related to money, not the body, saying: Nor upon those who do not find what they can spend, meaning they do not have money to spend on what they need to prepare for jihad. So God the Almighty denied the hardship from these people, and made clear that jihad with these excuses is dropped from them and is not obligatory upon them, restricted by His saying: If they are sincere to God and His Messenger, and the origin of sincerity is sincerity in action from deception, and from it is sincere repentance. Naftawayh said: To advise something means to be sincere, and to advise him of the saying means to be sincere to him, and advice to God means to believe in Him and act according to His law, and to leave what contradicts it, whatever it may be. And under it falls primarily the advice of His servants, and the love of the mujahideen in His path and offering advice to them in the matter of jihad, and leaving assistance to their enemies in any way, and the advice of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, means to believe in his prophethood and in what he brought, and to obey him in everything he commands or forbids, and to befriend whoever befriends him. And to be hostile to those who are hostile to him, and to love him and to venerate his Sunnah, and to revive it after his death to the best of one’s ability. It has been proven in the authentic hadith that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Religion is sincerity three times. They said: To whom? He said: To God, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common people.” The phrase there is no way for the doers of good confirms the meaning of what came before: that is, there is no way for the excused sincere ones: that is, there is no way for punishment and accountability. Min is added for emphasis. Based on this, the word the doers of good is used in the place of the pronoun referring to those mentioned previously, or what is meant is: there is no way for the good-doers and those mentioned previously are among them, so the phrase is causal, and the phrase and God is Forgiving and Merciful is a tail. In the meaning of this verse is the saying of God Almighty: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, and His saying: There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the sick, and dropping the obligation from these excused ones does not necessitate that the reward for the conquest that God excused them from, despite their desire for it, were it not for their excuse preventing them from it, and from this is the hadith of Anas with Abu Dawud and Ahmad, and its origin is in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have left behind you a people who did not travel any journey, nor did you spend any money, nor did you cross a valley except that they were with you in it. They said: O The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How can they be with us while they are in Medina? He said: They are held back by an excuse. Narrated by Ahmad and Muslim on the authority of Jabir.
9:92: Then God the Almighty mentioned among the group of those who have an excuse, what is included in His statement: And there is no blame upon those who, when they come to you for you to mount them, you say, 'I find nothing on which to mount you,' and the conjunction with the sentence There is no blame upon the doers of good, meaning nor upon those who, when they come to you, to the end of it, there is any blame. It is permissible for it to be a conjunction with the weak: meaning nor upon those who come to you to the end of it, there is no blame. The meaning is that among the group of those who have an excuse are those who came to you for you to mount them on what they ride in the conquest, but you did not find what they asked of you. It was said: The sentence I find nothing on which to mount you is in the accusative case as a state of the kaf in they came to you with the omission of may: meaning if they come to you saying, I find nothing, and it was said that it is a substitute for they came to you, and it was said that it is an interjectional sentence between the condition and the consequence, and the first is more appropriate. His saying: They turned away is the answer to if, and the phrase and their eyes overflowed with tears is in the accusative case as a state: that is, they turned away from you when you said to them, I do not find what to carry you with while they were crying, and sadness is in the accusative case as a source, or as a cause, or as a state, and that they do not find is the object for it, and sadness makes it accusative. Al-Farra’ said: that means not, that is, sadness that they do not find, and it was said that the meaning is: sadness that they do not find, and it was said that the meaning is: sadness that they do not find what to spend, neither with themselves nor with you.
9:93: Then God, the Most High, mentioned those who were left behind and said: 93- The way meaning the path of punishment and accountability is only for those who ask your permission to stay behind from the conquest, and the situation is that while they are rich meaning they find what will carry them and what they will be equipped with, and the phrase they were satisfied to be with the stay-behind ones is a new sentence as if it was said why did they ask permission while they were rich? The explanation of the stay-behind ones was presented shortly. The phrase and God has sealed their hearts is conjoined with they were satisfied meaning the reason for asking permission while rich is two things: one of them is satisfaction with the losing deal, which is to be with the stay-behind ones, and the second is the seal from God on their hearts so they because of this seal do not know what is profitable for them so they choose it over what is loss. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ad-Daraqutni in Al-Ifrad, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit who said: I was writing for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when Bara’ah was revealed. I was writing what was revealed to him, and I was putting the pen away from my ear when we were commanded to fight. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was looking at what was revealed to him when a blind man came and said: How will I be, O Messenger of God, when I am blind? Then the verse: There is no blame upon the weak was revealed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: This verse was revealed about Abid bin Umar Al-Muzani. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: It was revealed from the words: God has pardoned you to the words: There is no blame upon the doers of good, and God is Forgiving and Merciful about the hypocrites. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak regarding his statement: There is no blame upon the doers of good, he said: There is no blame upon these people because they advised God and His Messenger and were not able to fight in jihad, so God excused them and gave them the same reward as He gave to the mujahideen. Have you not heard that God says: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who are disabled, so God gave to those who have an excuse from the weak, those who are disabled, and those who do not find what to spend the same reward as He gave to the mujahideen. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: There is no blame upon the good-doers, he said: And God to the wrongdoers is Forgiving and Merciful. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: nor upon those who, when they come to you, the verse, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they should go out to fight with him, so a group of his companions came, among them Abdullah bin Mughaffal Al-Muzani, and they said: O Messenger of God, give us some mounts, so he said: By God, I do not find anything to mount you on, so they turned away crying and it was difficult for them to sit out the jihad and they did not find any money or a mount, so God revealed their excuse: nor upon those who, when they come to you, the verse. Ibn Saad, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Mughaffal, who said: I do not find the group that God mentioned: nor upon those who, when they come to you, that you may mount them, the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka'b who said: They are seven men from Banu Amr bin Awf Salim bin Umair, from Banu Waqif Harmi bin Amr, from Banu Mazen bin An-Najjar Abdurrahman bin Ka'b, whose nickname is Abu Laila, from Banu Al-Mu'alla Salman bin Sakhr, from Banu Haritha Abdurrahman bin Zaid Abu Ubla, from Banu Salamah Amr bin Ghanmah and Abdullah bin Amr Al-Muzani. The narrators agreed on some of these seven, and they differed on others, and going into detail about that would not be of much benefit. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Yazid bin Ruman, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, Asim bin Omar bin Qatada and others that some Muslim men came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and they were the Baka'un, and they were seven men from the Ansar and others, then they mentioned their names, and in it they asked the Messenger of God to carry them, and they were in need. He said: I do not find anything to carry you on. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Maqal bin Yasar was one of the weepers about whom God said: And there is no blame upon those who, when they come to you that you may mount them (al-Baqa’i 4:10). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik regarding His statement: I find nothing on which to mount you (al-Baqa’i 4:10), he said: Water and provisions. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali bin Salih who said: The elders of Juhaynah told me that they met those who asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) for mounts, and they said: We asked him for nothing but mounts on sandals. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibrahim bin Adham from someone who told him regarding His statement: And there is no blame upon those who, when they come to you that you may mount them (al-Baqa’i 4:10), he said: They did not ask him for mounts, they only asked him for sandals. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Salih regarding the verse, he said: They asked him to carry sandals. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: The way is only against those who ask your permission, he said: It and what follows it until his statement: Indeed, God is not pleased with the wicked people, regarding the hypocrites.
9:94: His statement: 94- They apologize to you is information from God Almighty about the hypocrites who make false excuses, that they apologize to the believers when they return from the conquest, and this is a new statement. Rather, He said: To them, meaning to those who make false excuses, and He did not say: To the city, because the basis of the apology is to return to them, not to return to the city, and perhaps the apology occurs upon meeting before arriving there. Then God Almighty informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what He would respond to them with, so He said: “Say: Make no excuses; we will never believe you.” So He first forbade them from making false excuses, then He explained it by saying: We will never believe you, meaning we will never believe you, as if they claimed that they were truthful in their apology, because the purpose of the one making an apology is to be believed in what he apologizes with, so if he knows that he will not be believed, he leaves the apology. The phrase God has already informed us of your report is an explanation of the one before it: meaning that we will not believe you because God has informed us by revelation what contradicts the truth of your apology. Rather, He singled out the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to respond to them, so He said: “Say: Make no excuses,” even though the apology from them is to all the believers, because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, is their head, and the one who takes care of what comes to them from others. It is possible that what is meant by the pronoun is In His saying: to you is the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to the well-known interpretation in such a case. His saying: And God will see your work means what deeds you will do in the future. Will you stop what you are doing now of evil or will you remain in it? And His saying: and His Messenger is conjoined with the noble name, and the object of the seeing is in the middle, indicating that God Almighty’s seeing of what they will do of good or evil is what the reward or punishment revolves around.
