And in the phrase then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen to the end, there is severe intimidation, because of what it includes of threat, especially what it includes of placing the apparent in place of the implicit, to indicate that He encompasses everything that happens from them that they conceal and show, and that He informs them of it and punishes them for it.
9:95: Then he mentioned that these false excuse-makers will confirm the false excuses they have come up with by swearing when the believers return to them from the invasion. Their purpose in this confirmation is that the believers will turn away from them, not rebuke them or hold them accountable for staying behind, and will show satisfaction with them, as is indicated by the mention of satisfaction afterwards. The object of the oath was omitted because the speech indicates it, which is their false apology. The command to the believers to turn away from them means leaving them and emigrating to them, not being satisfied with them and pardoning their sins, as is indicated by the sentence 95- Indeed, they are unclean which is the reason for the command to turn away. The meaning is that they are unclean in themselves because all their actions are impure, so it is as if they have made their selves impure, or that they are people of impurity: meaning people of ugly actions. Similar to it is Indeed, the polytheists are unclean and since they were like this, they were not qualified to accept guidance to good and warning against evil, so they have no choice but to leave it. His saying: And their abode is Hell is a complete explanation, for whoever is among the people of Hell will not benefit from calling to goodness. Abode is any place to which something takes refuge, day or night. So-and-so took refuge in his home, he takes refuge, and reward is in the accusative case as a source, or as a cause, and the ba in because of what they used to earn is for causality.
9:96: And sentence 96 - They swear to you instead of what came before. Here the thing sworn by was omitted because it is known from what came before, and the thing sworn upon is for the same as what came before, and the Almighty made clear that their purpose with this oath is for the believers to be pleased with them, then He mentioned what indicates that it is not permissible to be pleased with these people who make false excuses, so He said: But if you are pleased with them as is required of them to help them, then indeed, God is not pleased with the wicked people. And if this is what God the Almighty wants from not being pleased with these wicked disobedient people, then it is necessary for you, O believers, not to do otherwise, rather it is obligatory upon you not to be pleased with them, even though your pleasure with them, if it happened, would be of no value and would not benefit them, and the purpose of God the Almighty informing us of His not being pleased with them is to forbid the believers from that because being pleased with someone with whom God is not pleased is something that a believer would not do.
9:97: His saying: 97- The bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy. When God the Almighty mentioned the conditions of the hypocrites in Medina, He mentioned the condition of the bedouins who were outside of it, and He explained that their disbelief and hypocrisy are more severe than the disbelief and hypocrisy of others, because they are harder in heart, more coarse in nature, more rude in speech, and further from hearing the books of God and what His messengers brought. The bedouins are those who inhabit the deserts, unlike the Arabs, as it is general for this type of human beings, whether they inhabit the deserts or the villages. This is what the linguists said, and for this reason Sibawayh said: The bedouins are a plural form and not the plural form of the Arabs. Al-Naysaburi said: The linguists said: An Arab man if his lineage to the Arabs is established, and his plural is Arabs like the Magian and the Magi, and the Jew and the Jews, so if a bedouin is told, O Arab, he is happy, and if an Arab is told, O Bedouin, he becomes angry. This is because whoever settles in Arab villages is an Arab, and whoever settles in the desert is a Bedouin. For this reason, it is not permissible to call the Muhajireen and Ansar Bedouins, but rather they are Arabs. He said: It was said that the Arabs were called Arabs because the children of Ishmael, peace be upon him, grew up among the Arabs, which is from Tihamah, so they were attributed to their country, and everyone who lives in the Arabian Peninsula and speaks their language is from them. It was also said: because their tongues express what is in their hearts, and because of the eloquence and rhetoric in their language. The end. And more worthy is connected to more worthy, and its meaning is more appropriate. It is said: So-and-so is worthy of such-and-such: meaning he is worthy of it, and you are worthy of doing such-and-such. The plural is Jadar or Jadiroon, and its origin is from Jadar al-Ha’it, which means raising it by building. The meaning is: that they are more deserving and more appropriate not to know the limits of what God has revealed of laws and rulings, because of their distance from the places of the prophets and the lands of revelation. And God is Knowing of the conditions of His creatures in general, and these among them are Wise in what He will reward them with of good and evil.
9:98: His saying: 98- And among the bedouins are those who consider what they spend as a loss. This is a variation of a genus or two types, the first of which are these, and the second is And among the bedouins are those who believe in God. The loss is the fine and the loss, and the origin of the fine and the fine is what a man spends and it is not obligatory for him in his belief, but he spends it for show and dissimulation, and it was said that the origin of the fine is the obligation as if he believed that it is obligatory for him for an external matter that the soul does not arise for. And circles is the plural of circle, and it is the state that changes from blessing to calamity, and its origin is what surrounds something, and the circles of time: its turns and its vicissitudes and its revolutions, and it is as if it is only used for something disliked, then the Almighty invoked against them by saying: Upon them is the circle of evil and made what he invoked against them similar to what they intended for the Muslims, and evil with the fat-ha according to the majority of the readers is a source to which the circle was added for the connection like you say a man of truth. Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read with the damma of the seen, and it is the disliked. Al-Akhfash said: That is, upon them is the circle of defeat and evil. Al-Farra’ said: Upon them is the circle of evil meaning torment and affliction. He said: Evil with the fat-ha is the source of his evil, evil and misfortune, and with the damma is a noun, not a source, and it is like saying the circle of affliction and misfortune. And God is All-Hearing of what they say, All-Knowing of what they conceal.
9:99: His statement: 99- And among the bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day. This is the second type of bedouins as mentioned above: that is, he believes in them both. And takes what he spends as an offering. That is, he makes what he spends in the way of God as an offering. It is the plural of qurbah, and it is what one draws near to God, the Most High. You say, I have drawn near to God as an offering. The plural is qurbah and qurbah. Meaning: He makes what he spends a reason for attaining closeness with God and a reason for the prayers of the Messenger, meaning the supplications of the Messenger for them, because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate for those who give charity. From this is his saying: And pray for them, for your prayer is a comfort to them, and from this is his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: O God, pray for the family of Abu Awfa. Then He, the Most High, made clear that what this type of Arab spends as a way of drawing closer to God is acceptable and occurs in the way they intended, so He said: Indeed, it is a way of drawing closer to them. So He, the Most High, informed of its acceptance as a confirmed piece of report by the nominalization of the sentence and the letters of warning and verification. In this there is a comfort to their thoughts and reassurance to their hearts that cannot be estimated, along with what it includes of censure for those who take what they spend as a loss, and a rebuke to them in the most eloquent way. The harm is that it refers to what is in what they spend and its feminization is in consideration of the report. Nafi’ read, in a narration from him, qurbah with a damma on the ra, and the rest read it with a sukoon for ease. Then the Almighty explained qurbah by saying: God will admit them into His mercy, and the seen is to confirm the promise. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: God has informed us of your report, he said: He informed us that if you had gone out, you would have only increased our confusion. “And regarding his statement: “So turn away from them,” he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, he said to the believers: Do not speak to them and do not sit with them, so turn away from them as God has commanded.” Abu Sheikh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: So turn away from them, he said: So overlook them. Abu Sheikh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: The bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, he said: than the hypocrites of Medina. And they are more likely not to know the limits of what God has revealed to His Messenger, meaning the obligations and what he has commanded of jihad. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi that this verse was revealed regarding Asad and Ghatafan. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever lives in the desert is rough, whoever follows game is heedless, and whoever comes to the ruler will be tempted. Ahmad’s chain of transmission is as follows: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he mentioned it. He said in Al-Taqreeb: Abu Musa, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, is unknown from the sixth narrator, and those who said that he was Isra’il bin Musa were mistaken. Al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: It is hasan gharib, we do not know it except from the hadeeth of Al-Thawri. Abu Dawud and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever starts out is rough, whoever follows game is heedless, and whoever comes to the doors of the ruler will be tempted, and no one increases in closeness to his ruler except that he increases in distance from God.” Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: And among the desert Arabs are those who consider what they spend as a loss, he said: What is meant by loss is that he does not expect any reward or recompense from God, but rather he gives from the charity unwillingly. And he awaits for you the worst destruction. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding the verse: These are the hypocrites among the desert Arabs who only spend for show, out of fear that they will invade, fight and battle, and they see their spending as a loss. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And among the desert Arabs are those who believe in God, he said: They are Banu Muqrin from Muzaynah, and they are the ones about whom God said: And there is no blame upon those who, when they come to you that you may mount them 3:10. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Muqil who said: We were ten sons of Muqrin, and the verse: And among the desert Arabs are those who believe in God 3:10 was revealed about us. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and the prayers of the Messenger, meaning the Prophet’s seeking of forgiveness, may God bless him and grant him peace.
9:100: When God the Almighty mentioned the categories of the Arabs, He mentioned the Muhajireen and the Ansar, and explained that among them were those who were the first to migrate, and those who followed them. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he read 100- "and the Ansar in the nominative case in apposition to and the forerunners", and the rest of the reciters from the Companions and those who came after them read in the genitive case. Al-Akhfash said: The genitive case in the Ansar is correct, because the forerunners among them are included in His statement: "and the forerunners" and in the verse there is preference for the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar, and they are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs according to Saeed ibn al-Musayyab and a group, or those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan, which is the Pledge of Hudaybiyyah according to al-Sha'bi, or the people of Badr according to Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Ata' ibn Yasar, and there is no objection to applying the verse to all of these categories. Abu Mansur al-Baghdadi said: Our companions are unanimous that the best of them are the four caliphs, then the remaining six, then the Badris, then the people of Uhud, then the people of the Pledge of Ridwan at Hudaybiyyah. His saying: "And those who followed them with goodness" Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him read: "Those who followed them" without the waw as a description of the Ansar, according to his reading with the Ansar in the nominative case. Zaid bin Thabit reviewed this with him, so he asked Ubayy bin Ka'b and he believed Zaid, so Omar changed his mind about the aforementioned reading, as narrated by Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh. The meaning of those who followed them with goodness is: those who followed the first predecessors from the Muhajireen and the Ansar, and they are the companions who came after them until the Day of Resurrection. What is meant by them is not the followers in technical terms, and they are everyone who met the companions but did not meet the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), rather they are among those who fall under the verse, so the "min" in his saying: "of the Muhajireen" according to this is for partiality. It was said that it is for clarification, so the praise includes all the companions and what is meant by the followers is those who came after them from the nation until the Day of Resurrection. His saying: "with goodness" is a restriction for the followers: that is, and those who followed them, wearing goodness in actions and words, following the example of the first predecessors. His saying: God is pleased with them is the predicate of the subject and what is conjoined to it. The meaning of His pleasure with them is that He accepted their obedience and overlooked them and was not angry with them. And they were pleased with Him for what He gave them of His grace. And along with His pleasure with them, He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow in the Hereafter. Ibn Kathir read under which rivers flow with the addition of min. The rest read it without it and with the accusative as a circumstantial adverb. The explanation of the flow of rivers beneath the gardens and the explanation of eternity and success have already been presented.
9:101: His statement: 101- And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites. This is a return to explaining the conditions of the hypocrites from the people of Medina and those who are close to it from the bedouins. And among those around you is an advanced predicate, and among the bedouins is a statement, and it is in the accusative case as a state, and hypocrites is the subject. It was said: And those who are around Medina from the hypocrites are Juhayna, Muzayna, Ashja', and Ghaffar, and the phrase And among the people of Medina are those who are accustomed to hypocrisy is conjoined to the first phrase, conjoining one sentence to another. It was said: From the people of Madinah is in apposition to the predicate in the first sentence, so according to the first, the subject is understood: that is, from the people of Madinah are people who are stubborn in hypocrisy, and according to the second, the meaning is: and from those around you from the Bedouins and from the people of Madinah are stubborn hypocrites, and since the sentence stubborn in hypocrisy is a new sentence, it has no syntactic position, and the root of mard and tamarad is softness, smoothness and detachment, so it is as if they were detachment for hypocrisy, and from it is a beardless branch: without leaves on it, and a beardless horse: without hair in it, and a beardless boy: without hair on his face, and a barren land: without vegetation in it, and marrad is explicit: bare, so the meaning is: that they remained in hypocrisy and persisted in it and did not turn away from it. Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is that they persisted in it and did something else, and the sentence you do not know them explains the first sentence, which is stubborn in hypocrisy: that is, they persisted in it with a strong persistence and were skilled in it until their matter was hidden from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so how about the rest of the believers? What is meant is that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know about their identities, not in general terms, because the hypocrite has evidence that is not hidden from him, may God bless him and grant him peace. The phrase We know them confirms what preceded it because it indicates their skill in hypocrisy and their entrenchment in it in a way that is hidden from people and is not apparent to anyone but God, the Exalted, because He knows what is hidden and what the consciences conceal and what the secrets conceal. Then He, the Exalted, threatened them and said: We will punish them twice. It was said that what is meant by twice is the punishment of this world by killing and captivity, and the punishment of the Hereafter. It was said that it is the disgrace when their hypocrisy is exposed, and the punishment in the Hereafter. It was said that it is the calamities in their wealth and children, and the punishment of the grave. It was said that it is other things that would take too long to mention, with no evidence that it is meant specifically. It appears that this repeated torment is in this world, in a way that is true of the name torment, and that they are tormented time after time, then they are returned after that to the torment of the Hereafter, which is what is meant by His statement: Then they are returned to a great torment. And whoever says that the torment the second time is the torment of the Hereafter said that the meaning of His statement: Then they are returned to a great torment is that they are returned after their torment in the Fire like all the disbelievers to the lowest level of it, or that they are tormented in the Fire with a torment specific to them and not to all the other disbelievers, then they are returned after that to the torment that includes them and all the other disbelievers.
9:102: Then God the Almighty mentioned the state of a group of Muslims who were mixed up in their religion, saying: 102- And others who have acknowledged their sins and it is connected to His statement: hypocrites: meaning, and among those around you from the Bedouins and the people of Medina are other people, and it is possible that others is the subject, and they have acknowledged their sins is its description, and they mixed a good deed with another bad one is its predicate, and the meaning is: that this group stayed away from the raid without a valid excuse for staying away, then they regretted that, and they did not apologize with false excuses as the hypocrites did, rather they repented and admitted their sin and hoped that God would accept their repentance. What is meant by the good deed is what preceded their conversion to Islam and their implementation of the laws of Islam and their going out to jihad in all situations. What is meant by the bad deed is their staying away from this raid, and they followed this bad deed with a good deed, which is admitting it and repenting from it. The origin of confession is the admission of something, and mere admission does not constitute repentance unless it is accompanied by regret for the past and the determination to abandon it now and in the future. They did something that indicates this, as will be explained, God willing. The meaning of mixing is that they mixed each one of them with the other, like when you say, I mixed water with milk and milk with water. It is also possible for the waw to mean the ba’, like when you say, I sold the sheep for a sheep and a dirham, meaning for a dirham. In His statement, Perhaps God will accept their repentance, is evidence that something that indicates repentance was done by them along with the confession, or that the introduction to repentance, which is the confession, took the place of repentance. The letter of hope, which is ‘asa, in the words of God, the Most High, indicates the occurrence of the occurrence, because hope from God, the Most High, is an affirmation of His being the Most Generous of the generous. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning He forgives sins and bestows His favors upon His servants.
9:103: His statement: 103- Take from their wealth a charity. The scholars differed regarding this commanded charity. Some said: It is the obligatory charity, and others said: It is specific to this group who confess their sins, because after they repented, they presented their wealth to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so this verse was revealed. From is for partiality according to both interpretations, and the verse is absolute and explained by the pure Sunnah, and charity is taken from truthfulness, as it is evidence of the truthfulness of its giver in his faith. His statement: You purify them and sanctify them with it. The pronoun in the two verbs refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: meaning, you purify them and sanctify them, O Muhammad, with what you take from them in charity. It was said that the pronoun in their purification for charity means that this charity taken from them purifies them, and the pronoun in their purification is for the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, meaning that you purify them, O Muhammad, with the charity taken, and the first is more appropriate because of the difference in the second in the pronouns in the two connected verbs, and according to the first, the two verbs are in the accusative case as a state, and according to the second, the first verb is an attribute of charity and the second is a state of it, peace and blessings of God be upon him. The meaning of purification is to remove the traces of sins that are attached to them, and the meaning of purification is to exaggerate in purification. Al-Zajjaj said: It is better to address the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him: that is, then you, O Muhammad, purify them and sanctify them with it, in the definite and resumptive sense, and it is permissible to use the jussive mood as an answer to the command. The meaning is: that you take from their wealth a charity that purifies them. Al-Hasan read purifying them with the jussive mood, and according to this reading, and purify them is in the estimation of a subject: that is, and you purify them with it. His saying: and pray for them means: pray for them after you take that charity from their wealth. Al-Nahhas said: All linguists have narrated, as far as we know, that prayer in the speech of the Arabs means supplication. Then the Almighty explained His command to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray for those who take charity from him, saying: Indeed, your prayer is a reassurance for them. Hafs, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read your prayer in the singular form. The rest read it in the plural form, and reassurance is that which the soul finds peace and tranquility in.
9:104: His statement: 104- Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants? When God, the Exalted, accepted the repentance of those mentioned previously. God said: Do they not know meaning those who did not repent, or those who repented before God accepted their repentance and accepted their charity that it is God who accepts repentance because He is independent of the obedience of the obedient, and does not care about the disobedience of the disobedient. Have you not known was read with the superlative, and it is either addressed to the repentant, or to a group of believers, and the meaning of and takes the charity: is that He accepts it from them, and in attributing the taking to Him, the Exalted, after His command to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to take it, there is a great honor for this obedience and for those who did it. His statement: And that God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful is conjoined with His statement: that God is the Accepter of Repentance from His servants with it including an emphasis on what the conjoined to includes: that is, that this is His way, the Exalted. In the exaggerated form of the Forgiving and the Merciful, with the separation pronoun in the middle, and the emphasis on giving good tidings to His servants and encouraging them, there is something that is not hidden.
9:105: His saying: 105- And say, ‘Work, and God will see your work, and so will His Messenger and the believers.’ In it is intimidation and threat: that is, your work is not hidden from God, nor from His Messenger, nor from the believers, so hasten to do good deeds and make your deeds sincere for God, the Almighty and Majestic. In it is also encouragement and motivation, for whoever knows that his work is not hidden, whether it is good or evil, will desire good deeds and avoid evil deeds. How beautiful is the saying of Zuhair: Whatever a person has of character, even if he thinks it is hidden from people, it will be known. What is meant by seeing here is knowledge of the deeds they perform. Then the Almighty came with a severe threat, saying: And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. That is, after death you will be returned to God, the Almighty, who knows what you conceal and what you declare, what you conceal and what you reveal. Putting the unseen before the witnessed indicates the vastness of His knowledge, the Almighty, and that nothing is hidden from Him and that everything known is equal to Him. Then the Almighty mentioned what will happen after their return to Him, saying: Then He will inform you, that is, He will tell you, about what you used to do in this world, so He will reward the doer of good for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing, and He will bestow His favor upon whomever He wills of His servants.
9:106: His statement: 106- And others are deferred to the command of God. God the Almighty mentioned three categories of those who stayed behind: The first: The hypocrites who persisted in hypocrisy, the second: The repentant ones who confessed their sins, the third: Those whose matter remained suspended in that state, and they are the ones deferred to the command of God, from arjatuhu and raj'tuhu: if you postponed it. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Nafi' and Hafs read marjoon with a waw without a hamza. The rest read it with a dammah after the jim. Meaning: They are delayed in that state, and it is not certain that they will repent or not, but rather they are according to what is clear from the command of God Almighty regarding them, Either He punishes them if they remain as they are and do not repent, or He forgives them if they repent with a true repentance and are completely sincere. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is and others are awaiting the command of God while they are either punished or forgiven, and God is Knowing of their states, Wise in what He does to them of good or evil. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Sheikh and Abu Naim in Al-Ma'rifah narrated on the authority of Abu Musa that he was asked about the statement of God, And the first to foretake, so he said: They are those who prayed towards both Qiblahs. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Naim narrated a similar report on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Naim narrated a similar report on the authority of Al-Hasan and Muhammad bin Sirin. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They are Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Salman and Ammar bin Yasir. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Sheikh, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Naim in Al-Ma'rifah, on the authority of Al-Sha'bi, who said: They are those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the statement of God, And those who followed them with goodness, he said: The Followers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, who said: They are those who remain from the people of Islam until the Hour comes. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Sakhr Hamid bin Ziyad who said: I said to Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi: Tell me about the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and I only mean the tribulations. He said: God has forgiven all the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and has made Paradise obligatory for them in His Book, the good and the bad among them. I said to him: And in what place has God made Paradise obligatory for them in His Book? He said: Do you not read the words of God the Most High: And the first to forefront (al-Baqarah 2:17). He made Paradise and contentment obligatory for all the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and He stipulated a condition for the followers that He did not stipulate for them. I said: What did He stipulate for them? He said: He stipulated that they follow them in doing good. He said: They follow their example in their good deeds, and they do not follow them in anything else. Abu Sakhr said: By God, it was as if I had not read it before and I did not know its interpretation until Ibn Kaab read it to me. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Awza’i, who said: Yahya bin Abi Katheer, Al-Qasim, Makhul, Abdah bin Abi Lubabah, and Hassan bin Atiyah told me that they heard a group of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say when this verse was revealed: And the first to foretake until His saying: And are pleased with Him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is for all of my nation, and after pleasure there is no displeasure. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: And among those around you of the desert Arabs and the verse. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) stood up one Friday as a preacher and said: Stand up, so-and-so, and go out, for you are a hypocrite. Go out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite. So he called them by name and disgraced them. Umar ibn al-Khattab did not attend that Friday prayer because of a need he had. Umar met them as they were leaving the mosque, so he hid from them out of shyness that he had not attended the Friday prayer. The people thought that they had left, and they hid from Umar, thinking that he had learned about their affair. Umar entered the mosque and found that the people had not left, so a man said to him: Be of good cheer, Umar, for God has disgraced the hypocrites today. This is the first punishment, and the second punishment is the punishment of the grave. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding His statement: And among those around you of the bedouins, he said: Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Ashja’, Aslam, and Ghifar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding His statement: They persisted in hypocrisy, he said: They persisted in it and did not repent as others repented. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding the verse, he said: They died upon it: Abdullah bin Ubayy, Abu Amir the monk, and al-Jadd bin Qais. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, We will punish them twice, he said: With hunger and killing. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Malik, he said: With hunger and the punishment of the grave. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Punishment in the grave, and punishment in the Fire. A group of the Salaf narrated something similar to this in specifying the two punishments, and what we have mentioned is apparent. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: “And others have acknowledged their sins. They mixed righteous deeds,” he said: There were ten men who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. When the time came for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to return, seven of them tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pass by them when he returned. When he saw them, he said: Who are these who tied themselves? They said: This is Abu Lubabah and his companions who stayed behind you, O Messenger of God, until you release them and excuse them. He said: And I swear by God that I will not release them nor excuse them until God is the one who releases them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the battle with the Muslims. When that reached them, they said: And we will not release ourselves until God is the one who releases us. So the following was revealed: Perhaps God will accept their repentance. And perhaps is obligatory from God. So when it was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to them and released them and excused them. So they came with their money and said: O Messenger of God, this is our money, so give it in charity on our behalf and ask forgiveness for us. He said: I was not commanded to take your money. So God, the Almighty, revealed: Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and sanctify them, and pray for them. He said: Ask forgiveness for them. Indeed, your prayers are a comfort to them. He said: Mercy for them. So he took the charity from them and asked forgiveness for them. They were three men who had not tied themselves to the pillars, so they were postponed for a year, not knowing whether they would be punished or repented to. Then God the Almighty revealed: God has certainly forgiven the Prophet until His saying: And the three who stayed behind until His saying: “Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful” meaning: if they were upright. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated from Mujahid regarding His saying: Confess their sins he said: He is Abu Lubabah when he said to Qurayza what he said, and pointed to his throat that Muhammad would slaughter you if you submitted to his judgment. The story is mentioned in the books of biography. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Suddi regarding His saying: They mixed a righteous deed he said: Their raid with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and another evil he said: Their staying behind him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: And pray for them he said: Ask forgiveness for them for the sins they had committed. Indeed, your prayers are a comfort to them he said: Mercy for them. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa who said: “Whenever charity was brought to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he would say: ‘O God, bless the family of so-and-so.’ My father brought him his charity and he said: ‘O God, bless the family of Abi Awfa.’” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: Work, and God will see your work and so will His Messenger, that he said: This is a warning from God, the Almighty. Ahmad, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab, Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If one of you were to work in a solid rock that had no door or window, God would reveal his work to the people, whatever it was. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the verse: And others are awaiting the command of God, that he said: They are the three who were left behind. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: He said: They are Hilal bin Umayya, Murarah bin al-Rabi’ and Ka’b bin Malik from the Aws and Khazraj. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: Either He punishes them meaning: He kills them for their disobedience or He forgives them so he postponed their matter then abrogated it and said: and the three who were left behind.
9:107: When God mentioned the types of hypocrites and explained their different ways, He connected this group of them to what preceded, and they are those who took a mosque to cause harm, so the meaning would be: And among them are those who took, on the basis that those is the subject, and its predicate is from them which is omitted, and the sentence is connected to what preceded it, and it is permissible for the relative pronoun to be in the accusative case for blame. The Medinans and Ibn Amir read those who took without a waw, so it would be an independent story, the relative pronoun is the subject, and its predicate is do not stand, said Al-Kisa'i. Al-Nahhas said: The predicate is their building which they built will not cease and it was said that the predicate is omitted, and the meaning is they are tormented, and the explanation of these builders of the mosque of harm will come, and harm is accusative as a source, or as a cause, and disbelief and division among the believers and ambush is connected to harm. God the Almighty informed that the motive for them to build this mosque was four things: The first: harming others, which is harm. Second: Disbelief in God and boasting to the people of Islam, because they wanted to strengthen the hypocrites by building it. Third: To divide the believers, because they wanted them not to attend the Quba Mosque, so that the congregation of Muslims would decrease, and in that there is a difference of opinion and the nullification of harmony that is not hidden. Fourth: Watching for those who fought God and His Messenger: meaning preparing for those who fought God and His Messenger. Al-Zajjaj said: Watching is waiting. Ibn Qutaybah said: Watching is waiting with enmity. Most said: It is preparation, and the meaning is close. It is said: I watched for something: if I prepared it, waiting for it. Abu Zayd said: It is said I watched him and watched him for good, and I watched him for evil. Ibn al-A'rabi said: It is not said except arsadat, and its meaning is irtaqbat, and what is meant by those who fought God and His Messenger are the hypocrites, and among them is Abu Amir the monk: that is, they prepared it for these people and anticipated their arrival and waited for them to pray in it so that they could boast about them to the believers. His statement: before is related to took: that is, they took a mosque before these people became hypocrites and built the Mosque of Harm, or it is related to hareb: that is, for those who waged war against God and His Messenger before building the Mosque of Harm. His statement: And they will swear, We intended nothing but the best" means, we intended nothing but the best characteristic, which is kindness to the Muslims. So God responded to them by saying: "And God bears witness that they are liars" in what they swore.
9:108: Then God the Almighty forbade His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from praying in the Mosque of Harm, saying: 108- Do not stand in it ever meaning at any time, and the prohibition of standing in it entails the prohibition of praying in it. Prayer may be expressed by standing, it is said that someone stands at night: meaning he prays, and from this is the authentic hadith: Whoever stands in Ramadan out of faith in it and in the hope of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven. Then God the Almighty mentioned the reason for the prohibition of standing in it by saying: A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more deserving for you to stand in it and the lam in masjid is the lam of the oath, and it was said that it is the lam of beginning, and in that there is emphasis on the meaning of the sentence, and the foundation of the building: is its stability and elevation. The meaning of its foundation on piety: its foundation on the qualities that protect against punishment. Scholars differed regarding the mosque that was founded on piety. A group said: It is the Quba Mosque, as narrated by Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Ash-Sha’bi and others. Others said that it is the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The first is more likely, as will come soon, God willing. From the first day is related to founded, meaning it was founded on piety from the first day of its foundation. Some grammarians said: From here means since, meaning from the first day it was built. His saying: more deserving that you stand in it is the predicate of the subject. The meaning is: If standing in any other mosque was permissible, then it would be more deserving of your standing in it for prayer and remembrance of God, because it was founded on piety from the first day, and because in it are men who love to purify themselves. This sentence is a new sentence to explain the right of his standing in it, may God bless him and grant him peace: just as this mosque is more deserving in terms of location, it is more deserving in terms of its condition. It is permissible for this sentence to be in the accusative case as a condition: meaning the condition of there being men who love to purify themselves. It is also permissible for it to be another description of a mosque. The meaning of their love for purification is that they prefer it and are keen on it when its necessity arises. It was said that it means: they love to purify themselves from sins through repentance and seeking forgiveness. The first is more appropriate. It was said: they love to purify themselves with a purifying fever from sins, so they all became feverish. This is very weak. The meaning of God’s love for them is to be pleased with them and to be kind to them as a lover does to his beloved.
9:109: Then the Almighty made clear that there is a great distance between the two groups, saying: 109- Is he who founded his building? The hamza is for the affirmative denial, and the building is a source like the construction, and what is meant by it is the built, he founded his religion on the opposite of that, which is falsehood and hypocrisy, and the relative is the subject, and its predicate is good, and the foundations of his building was read in the form of the verb for the agent, and the building of his was placed in the accusative, and Abu Ubaidah chose this reading, and it was read in the passive form, and the foundation of his building was read by adding foundation to his building, and the foundations of his building were read and what is meant is: the foundations of the building, and Abu Hatim narrated another reading, and the foundations of his building are in the plural, and from it: The king became fixed-founded with the Abbasids' thugs Al-Shafa: the lip, and Al-Jarf: what is swept away by the floods, and they are the sides that are swept away by the water, and Al-Ijtiraaf: uprooting something from its origin, and it is read with a damma on the Ra from Jarf and with a sukoon on it. Al-Haar: the fallen, it is said that the building has fallen: if it has fallen, and its origin is Ha’ir as they said: Shak Al-Silah and Sha’iq, thus said Al-Zajjaj. Abu Hatim said: its origin is Hawar. He said in Shams Al-Ulum: Al-Jarf is what the flood has swept away its origin, and its top is prominent, so if its top is cracked, then it is Al-Haar. God the Almighty made this an example for what they built their false religion upon, which quickly decays, then He said: So it collapsed with it into the fire of Hell. The subject of So it collapsed is a pronoun that refers to Al-Jarf: meaning, the building collapsed with the cliff into the fire, and it is possible that the pronoun in with it refers to Man, who is the builder. Meaning: The falsehood collapsed with the building, or the builder into the fire of Hell. He came with the collapse, which is for the cliff, as a nomination for the metaphor. Glory be to God, how eloquent this speech is, how powerful its structures are, how effective its meaning is, and how clear its structure is.
9:110: Then the Almighty mentioned that their building is a reason for their increasing doubt, and their continued hesitation and suspicion, so He said: 110- Their building which they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts, meaning doubt and hypocrisy in their hearts. From this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: I swore, I did not leave any doubt for you, and there is no way for a person to go beyond God. It was said that the meaning of doubt is regret and remorse, because they regretted building it. Al-Mubarrad said: It means heat and anger. Those who built the Mosque of Harm were hypocrites who doubted their religion, but their hypocrisy and determination to disbelieve increased with the demolition of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and their hatred of Islam increased because of the intense anger and great wrath that befell them because of its demolition. Then God the Almighty mentioned what indicates the continuation and permanence of this doubt, which is His statement: Unless their hearts are cut out, meaning this will not cease unless their hearts are cut out and scattered into pieces, either by death or by the sword. What is meant is that this doubt will remain for them as long as they are alive, and it is possible that the mention of being cut out is a description of the state of doubt disappearing. It was said that its meaning is: Unless they repent a repentance that tears their hearts out of regret and sorrow for their negligence. Ibn Amir, Hamzah, Hafs, Yaqub, and Abu Ja`far read the present tense with a fat-ha. The majority read it with a damma. It was narrated on the authority of Yaqub that he read taqata’ with a light pronunciation, and the address was to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: that is, unless you, O Muhammad, cut their hearts. The companions of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud read: even if their hearts were cut. Al-Hasan, Yaqub, and Abu Hatim read ila an taqata’ with a heavy pronunciation. That is, they will remain like this until they die. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And those who built a mosque to cause harm, he said: They were people from the Ansar who built a mosque. Abu Amir the monk said to them: Build your mosque and seek whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Caesar, the king of the Romans, and I will bring an army from the Romans, and I will bring Muhammad and his companions out. When they finished building their mosque, they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We have finished building our mosque, so you must pray in it and ask for blessings. Then God revealed: Do not stand in it ever again. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, built the Quba Mosque, some men from the Ansar went out, including Bujdah, the grandfather of Abdullah bin Hanif, Wadi’ah bin Hizam, and Mujammi’ bin Jariyah al-Ansari, and they built the Mosque of Hypocrisy. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Bujdah: Woe to you, Bujdah! You did not want what I see. He said: O Messenger of God, by God, I only wanted goodness, and he is lying. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, believed him and wanted to excuse him, so God Almighty revealed: ‘And those who have taken a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as an ambush for him who wages war against God and His Messenger’ meaning a man called Abu Amir who was a warlord against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had gone to Heraclius, and they were ambushing Abu Amir when he arrived to pray in it, and he had left Medina fighting against God and His Messenger.” Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Malik ibn al-Dakhshum, and Malik said to Asim: Give me time until I bring you fire from my family. So he entered upon his family and took palm fronds from the fire, then they went out, rushing forward until they entered the mosque with his family in it, and they burned it and demolished it, and his family went out and dispersed from it, so God revealed this verse. Perhaps in this narration there is an omission between his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the Messenger of God called Malik bin Al-Dakhshum and his saying, Malik said to Asim. This is explained by what Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Ruhm Kalthum bin Al-Hussain Al-Ghifari, who was one of the Companions who pledged allegiance under the tree. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came until he stopped at Dhi Awan: a town between it and Madinah an hour of the day. The people of the Mosque of Harm had come to him while he was preparing for Tabuk. They said: O Messenger of God, we have built a mosque for those who are sick and in need, and for the winter night and the rainy night, and we would like you to come to us and pray for us in it. He said: I am on the verge of a journey, and if we were to come, God willing, we would come to you and pray for you in it. When he stopped at Dhi Awan, the report of the mosque came to him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called God’s peace and blessings be upon him, Malik bin Ad-Dakhshum, the brother of Banu Salim bin Auf and Ma’n bin Adi, and his brother Asim bin Adi, one of Banu Al-Ajlan, said: Go to this mosque whose people are oppressors and demolish and burn it. So they left quickly until they reached Banu Salim bin Auf, who are the people of Malik bin Ad-Dakhshum. Malik said to Ma’n: Give me time until I come out to you. So he entered to his people and took a palm frond and set it on fire. Then they left quickly, and his people were inside. They burned it and demolished it and dispersed from it. The following was revealed about them in the Qur’an: “And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief” to the end of the story. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that those who built the mosque of harm were twelve men, and they mentioned their names. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri said: Two men disagreed: a man from Banu Khudra, and in another version: I and a man from Banu Amr ibn Awf disputed about the mosque that was founded on piety. Al-Khudri said: It is the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-`Umari said: It is the mosque of Quba. So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about that. He said: It is this mosque, the mosque of the Messenger of God. God, and he said in that a lot of good, meaning the Quba Mosque. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Az-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in Akhbar Al-Madinah, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Hibban, At-Tabarani, Al-Hakim in Al-Kuna, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d Al-Sa’idi something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Khatib, and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Abi ibn Ka’b who said: “I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the mosque that was founded on piety. He said: It is this mosque of mine.” At-Tabarani and Al-Dhiya’ Al-Maqdisi narrated in Al-Mukhtara on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, with a similar chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Mardawayh, and At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit who said: The mosque that was founded on piety from the first day was the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Urwah said: The mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is better than it. It was only revealed about the mosque of Quba. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The mosque that was founded on piety is the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The two mentioned mentioned narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri something similar. And a group other than these narrated something similar to what they said. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it is a mosque. Quba. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated something similar from Ad-Dahhak. It is not hidden from you that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, designated this mosque that was founded on piety, and he asserted that it was his mosque, may God bless him and grant him peace, as we have presented from the authentic hadiths. This cannot be opposed by the statement of an individual from the Companions, nor a group of them, nor others, nor is it correct to present it in opposition to what has been authenticated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There is no benefit in presenting what was reported about the virtue of praying in the Quba Mosque, as that does not necessitate that it is the mosque that was founded on piety. Moreover, what was reported about the virtues of his mosque, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more than what was reported about the virtue of the Quba Mosque, without a doubt or general suspicion. Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: This verse was revealed about the people of Quba’: In it are men who love to purify themselves. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) sent to ‘Uwaim ibn Sa’idah and said: What is this purification that God has praised you for? They said: O Messenger of God, no man or woman among us has ever relieved himself without washing his private parts, or he said: his buttocks. The Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: This is it. Ahmad, Ibn Khuzaymah, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of ‘Uwaim ibn Sa’idah Al-Ansari that the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) came to them in the mosque of Quba’ and said: God has praised you for purification in the story of your mosque, so what is this purification that you purify yourself with? They said: By God, O Messenger of God, we do not know anything except that we had Jewish neighbors who used to wash their backsides after defecating, so we washed them as they did. Narrated by Ahmad on the authority of Hasan ibn Muhammad. Abu Uwais narrated to us, Shurahbil narrated to us, on the authority of Uwaim bin Sa’idah, and he mentioned it. Ibn Khuzaymah included it in his Sahih. Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Jarud in al-Muntaqa, al-Daraqutni, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir included it on the authority of Talhah bin Nafi’ who said: Abu Ayyub, Jabir bin Abdullah, and Anas bin Malik told me that when this verse was revealed: In it are men who love to purify themselves, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “O group of Ansar, God has praised you for your purification. What is this purification of yours?” They said: We perform ablution for prayer and take a bath after sexual impurity. He said: Is there anything else besides that? They said: No, except that when one of us goes out to relieve himself, he likes to clean himself with water. He said: That is it, so you should do it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bukhari in his History, Ibn Jarir, al-Baghawi in his Mu’jam, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu’aym included it on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Salam on the authority of his father who said: “When he came to The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited the mosque that was founded on piety, the Quba Mosque, and said: God has praised you for purification, so will you not tell me? Meaning the words of God the Almighty: “In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves.” They said: O Messenger of God, we find it written for us in the Torah to clean ourselves with water, and we do it today. Ahmad’s chain of transmission for this hadith is as follows: Yahya ibn Adam told us, Malik told me, meaning Ibn Mughul, I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakam, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Salam. It has been narrated from a group of the Tabi’un in mentioning the reason for the revelation of the verse something similar to this. It is clear to you that some of these hadiths do not specify the Quba Mosque and its people, and some of them are weak, and some of them do not explicitly state that the mosque that was founded on piety is the Quba Mosque. In any case, those hadiths that explicitly state that the mosque that was founded on piety is the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, cannot be compared in their authenticity and clarity. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell, he said: He means its foundations in the fire of Hell. Musaddad narrated in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: I saw smoke coming out of the Mosque of Harm when it collapsed during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Their structure which they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts, meaning doubt, unless their hearts are cut out, meaning death. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit regarding his statement: Doubt in their hearts, he said: Rage in their hearts, unless their hearts are cut out, he said: until they die. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sufyan regarding his statement: unless their hearts are cut out, he said: unless they repent.
9:111: When he explained the scandals and ugliness of the hypocrites because of their failure to participate in the Battle of Tabuk, and mentioned their categories, and based on each category what is appropriate for it, he returned to explaining the virtue of jihad and encouraging it, and mentioned the purchase as an example, as in His saying: Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance. God Almighty likened the reward of the mujahideen with Paradise for their sacrifice of their souls and their wealth in the way of God by purchasing, and its origin is purchasing between servants, which is the removal of something from ownership in exchange for something else like it or less than it or more beneficial than it, so these mujahideen sold themselves to God for Paradise that He has prepared for the believers: that is, to be among the people of Paradise, and among those who inhabit it, for they have given themselves, and they are the most precious of things, and giving them is the ultimate in giving: He is generous with his soul even if the coward is stingy with it, and generosity with his soul is the ultimate level of generosity. And God bestowed Paradise upon them, which is the greatest thing that the servants seek, and they seek it through deeds. What is meant by souls are the souls of the mujahideen, and by wealth is what they spend in jihad. His statement: 111- They fight in the cause of God is an explanation of the sale that is required by the aforementioned purchase, as if it was said: How do they sell their souls and wealth for Paradise? So it was said: They fight in the cause of God. Then this fighting in the cause of God was explained by His statement: They kill and are killed. What is meant is that they proceed to kill the infidels in war and sacrifice themselves in that, so if they do so then they deserve Paradise, even if they are not killed after their sacrifice in jihad and exposure to death by proceeding against the infidels. Al-A’mash, Al-Nakha’i, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and Khalaf read it by placing the passive voice before the active voice. The rest read it by placing the active voice before the passive voice. His saying: A promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an is a statement from God Almighty that the obligation of jihad and the entitlement to Paradise through it has been confirmed as a promise from God in the Torah and the Gospel, just as it occurred in the Qur’an. The accusative of a promise and a truth is a source, or the second is an attribute of the first, and in the Torah is related to something omitted: that is, a promise confirmed therein. His saying: And who is more faithful to his covenant than God? This is an emphasis on encouraging the mujahideen in jihad and motivating them to sacrifice their lives and wealth, which is not hidden. First, He informed that He has purchased from them their lives and wealth, for Paradise is theirs, and He came with this magnificent phrase, which is that Paradise has become their property. Then He informed secondly that He has promised that in His revealed books. Then He informed that after this true promise, what was promised must come true, for no one is more faithful to His covenant than God, the Most High, and He is the Truthful in His promise and does not break His promise. Then He increased their joy and happiness, and He said: Then rejoice in your transaction which you have made. That is, show joy in that, and good report is showing joy, and its appearance is in the complexion of the face, and that is why it is said the features of the face: that is, in which joy appears. This has been explained previously, and the fa is to arrange the good report on what precedes it. Meaning: Show joy in this sale that you have made to God Almighty, for you have gained a profit in it that no one else has gained except those who have done what you have done. The reference in His saying: that is to Paradise, or to the sale itself in which they have gained Paradise. The description of the victory, which is the attainment of the desired thing, as great, indicates that it is a victory like no other.
9:112: His statement: 112- The repentant is the predicate of an omitted subject: meaning they are the repentant, meaning the believers, and the repentant is the one who returns: meaning they are those who return to obeying God from a state that is contrary to obedience. Al-Zajjaj said: What I think is that his statement: The repentant, the worshippers is raised by the subject and its predicate is implied: meaning the repentant and those who come after them until the end of the verse also have Paradise even if they did not strive. He said: This is better, because if these were descriptions of the believers mentioned in his statement: He purchased from the believers then the promise would be specific to the mujahideen. A group of commentators have agreed with what Al-Zajjaj has agreed with, that this statement is separate from what preceded it, and others have agreed that these descriptions refer to the believers in the first verse. And that it is in the form of a condition: meaning that no one deserves Paradise by that pledge except those believers who have these descriptions. And in the copy of Abdullah bin Masoud's copy: The repentant, the worshippers until the end of it. There are two views on this: The first: that they are descriptions of the believers. The second: that the accusative is for praise. It was said: that the elevation of these descriptions is in apposition to the pronoun of they fight, and the author of Al-Kashshaf allowed that the repentant ones are the subject, and its predicate is the worshippers, and what comes after it is also predicates: that is, those who repent from disbelief in truth are the ones who combine these qualities, and there is a distance in it that is not hidden, and the worshippers are those who perform what they are commanded to do of worshipping God with sincerity, and the praisers are those who praise God, the Most High, for ease and hardship, and the travelers it was said: they are the fasting ones, and the majority of commentators went to this, and from it is His Almighty saying: Worshipping and traveling ones and the fasting one is called a traveler, because he leaves pleasures as the traveler leaves them on earth, and from it is the saying of Abu Talib bin Abdul Muttalib: And the tourists do not taste the nature of their Lord and the stagnant factors Another said: You see him praying day and night, constantly remembering God and wandering. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Hasan’s school of thought is that the travelers here are those who fast the obligatory fasts. It was also said that they are those who fast continuously. Ata’ said: The travelers are the mujahidin. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: The travelers are the emigrants. Ikrimah said: They are those who travel in search of hadith and knowledge. It was also said: They are those who wander with their thoughts on the oneness of their Lord, His kingdom, and the lessons He created. Tourism in the language originally means going on the face of the earth as water flows, and it is one of the things that helps the servant to obey because he is cut off from creation, and because of the consideration he obtains by contemplating the creations of God Almighty, and those who bow and prostrate means those who pray, and those who enjoin good are those who command people with what is known in the Sharia, and those who forbid evil are those who denounce those who do evil: that is, something that the Sharia denounces, and those who preserve the limits of God are those who preserve His laws that He revealed in His books and on the tongues of His messengers, and the waw was only inserted in the other two descriptions, which are those who forbid evil and the preservers etc., because enjoining good and forbidding evil are like one characteristic, then the preservers were connected to it with the waw because of its proximity, and it was said that the connection in the attributes comes with the waw and without it like His saying: Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, and it was said that the waw is redundant, and it was said that it is the waw of the eight known in Grammarians, as in the Almighty’s saying: Wives and virgins, and His saying: And its gates were opened, and His saying: Seven and the eighth of them was their dog. Abu Ali al-Farsi denied the waw of the eight, and Ibn Khalawayh debated him on that, and and give good tidings to the believers, described with the previous attributes. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi and others who said: “Abdullah ibn Rawahah said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Set conditions for your Lord and for yourself as you wish.’ He said: ‘I set a condition for my Lord that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and I set a condition for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your wealth from.’ They said: ‘If we do that, what will we get?’ He said: ‘Paradise.’ He said: ‘A profitable sale, from which we will not take a break or ask for a severance.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their souls and selves.’ Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: ‘This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the mosque: ‘Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their souls and selves.’ The people in the mosque were saying takbir, and a man from the Ansar came up, folding the ends of his cloak over his shoulders and said: ‘O Messenger of God, was this verse revealed?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ The Ansari said: ‘A profitable sale, from which we will not take a break or ask for a severance.’” Ibn Saad narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stipulated in the Pledge of Aqaba on those of the Ansar who pledged allegiance to him: that they should testify that there is no god but God and that he is the Messenger of God, establish prayer, pay zakat, listen and obey, not dispute authority with those in authority, and prevent him from what they prevent themselves and their families from. They said: Yes. A speaker from the Ansar said: Yes, this is for you, O Messenger of God, but what is for us? He said: Paradise. Ibn Sa’d also narrated it from another chain of transmission, and there is nothing in the story of ‘Aqaba that indicates that it was the reason for the revelation of the verse. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Whoever dies with these nine qualities is in the path of God, those who repent and worship until the end of the verse. Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The martyr is the one who has the nine qualities mentioned in this verse. Abu al-Shaykh narrated from him, who said: The worshippers who establish prayer. Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab al-Iman also narrated from him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first to be called to Paradise are the praisers who praise God in prosperity and adversity. Ibn Jarir narrated from ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umair, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the travelers, and he said: They are the fasting ones.” Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu’ab al-Iman from the path of ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umair from Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, similarly. Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn al-Najjar narrated from the path of Abu Salih from Abu Hurairah narrated a similar hadith from the Prophet. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith from Ibn Masoud. It was narrated from Abu Hurairah as a mursal hadith, which is more authentic than the hadith from his chain of transmission. The hadith of Ubaid ibn Umair is mursal, and he narrated it from Abu Hurairah in the second narration. It was narrated from a group of the Companions like this: Among them is Aishah according to Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir, and among them is Ibn Abbas according to Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Abu al-Shaykh, and among them is Ibn Masoud according to those mentioned before him. Something similar was narrated from a group of the Followers. Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab al-Iman narrated from Abu Umamah that “a man asked permission from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) to travel, so he said: The travel of my nation is jihad in the way of God.” And Abdul Haqq authenticated it. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ regarding this verse, saying: These are deeds about which the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: God has decreed for Himself in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an for this nation that whoever among them is killed for these deeds will be a martyr with God, and whoever among them dies for them, his reward is due from God. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The martyr is he who, if he died in his bed, would enter Paradise. He said: Ibn Abbas said: Whoever dies with nine in him is a martyr. And he recited this verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, meaning Paradise, then he said: Those who repent. To his saying: And those who preserve the limits of God meaning those who obey God, which is a condition that God has imposed on the people of jihad, and if they fulfill God’s condition, He will fulfill their condition for them.
9:113: When God the Almighty made clear at the beginning of the Surah and after it that disavowal of the polytheists and hypocrites is obligatory, He the Almighty made clear here what further emphasizes that, and stated that this is inevitable, even if they were relatives, and that kinship has no effect in such a ruling. The commentators have mentioned that what was in the Qur’an comes in two ways: The first: in negation, such as No soul can die except by God’s permission. 113- It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists. This verse includes severing allegiance to the infidels, and prohibiting asking forgiveness for them, and supplicating for what is not permissible for one who is a disbeliever. This does not contradict what was proven from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Sahih that “he said on the day of Uhud when the polytheists broke his front tooth and split his face: O God, forgive my people, for they do not know.” Because it is possible that this was before he was informed of the prohibition of asking forgiveness for the polytheists. And assuming that it had been informed to him, as the reason for revelation indicates, it was a long time before the day of Uhud, and it will come, so the issuance of this asking forgiveness from him for his people was only by way of narration from those who came before him from the prophets, as in Sahih Muslim from Abdullah, he said: “It is as if I see the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating a prophet from the prophets who was struck by his people while he was wiping…” The blood was flowing from his face and he said: O Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know. In Bukhari, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned a prophet before him whose people had wounded him, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to tell about him that he said: O God, forgive my people, for they do not know.” His saying: After it became clear to them that they are the people of Hellfire. This sentence includes the reason for the prohibition of seeking forgiveness. The meaning is that this clarification requires severing allegiance to those who were like this, and not considering kinship because they died as polytheists. God Almighty said: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him. So seeking forgiveness for them is a violation of God’s promise and threat.
19:47: His saying: 114- And it was not Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father The verse: God the Almighty mentioned the reason for Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father, which was because of a promise that Abraham had made to his father to seek forgiveness for him. But he left that and disavowed him when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, and that he did not deserve forgiveness. This indicates that He only promised him before it became clear to him that he was one of the people of the Fire and one of the enemies of God. So there is no need for the question that many commentators raise, how was that hidden from Abraham, since the prohibition of seeking forgiveness for one who persists in disbelief and dies upon it was not hidden from him, and he did not know that except by God the Almighty informing him that he was an enemy of God. For the establishment of this enmity indicates disbelief. Likewise, our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know that it was forbidden until after God informed him of this verse. This is a ruling that is only established by hearing, not by reason. It was said: What is meant by Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father is his calling to Islam, and this is very weak. It was said: What is meant by seeking forgiveness in this verse is the prohibition of praying over the funerals of the infidels, so it is like His saying: And never pray over any of them who dies. There is no need to interpret seeking forgiveness as prayer, nor is there any resort to that. Then God Almighty concluded this verse with great praise for Abraham, saying: Indeed, Abraham was one of those who grieved. And he grieved a lot, as the exaggerated form indicates. Scholars differed about the meaning of Al-Awwah. Ibn Masoud and Ubaid bin Umair said: It is the one who supplicates a lot. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: It is the one who is merciful to the servants of God. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: It is the believer in the language of Abyssinia. Al-Kalbi said: It is the one who remembers God in the barren land. The same was narrated from Ibn Al-Musayyab. It was also said: It is the one who remembers God a lot without restriction. This was narrated from Uqbah bin Amir. It was also said: It is the one who recites a lot. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was also said: It is the jurist. This was said by Mujahid and Al-Nakha’i. It was also said: It is the one who is humble and submissive. This was narrated from Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Haad. It was also said: It is the one who seeks forgiveness for his sins when he remembers them. This was narrated from Abu Ayoub. It was also said: It is the compassionate.
