This was said by Abdul Aziz bin Yahya. He said: It is the teacher of good. It was also said: It is the one who turns away from everything that God hates. This was said by Ata’. The meaning of awaah in the language is the one who groans a lot because of his sins, so he says for example: Ah, from my sins, ah, from what I am being punished with because of them, and the like. Al-Farra’ said the same, and it was narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr. The meaning of groaning is that the chest hears the sound of a deep sigh. It is stated in Al-Sahah: A man groans a groaning, and groans a groaning if he says Oh, and the noun derived from it is ahah with a long vowel. He said: If I leave her at night, she groans like a sad man Haleem is the one who is very patient, as the exaggerated form indicates. He is the one who forgives sins and is patient with harm. It was said that he is the one who never punishes anyone except God. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab on the authority of his father who said: “When the death of Abu Talib was approaching, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered and Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Umayya were with him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O uncle, say there is no god but God and I will argue for you with it before God.’ Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Umayya said: ‘O Abu Talib, do you reject the religion of Abdul Muttalib?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to present it to him, while Abu Jahl and Abdullah were refusing to say that statement. Abu Talib said the last thing he said to them: ‘He is on the religion of Abdul Muttalib,’ and he refused to say there is no god but God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I will seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so.’ Then the verse ‘It is not for the Prophet’ was revealed, and God revealed about Abu Talib: ‘Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills.’” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman, and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ali who said: I heard a man asking forgiveness for his parents even though they were polytheists. I said: Do you ask forgiveness for your parents even though they were polytheists? He said: Did not Ibrahim ask forgiveness for his father? I mentioned that to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the verse It is not for the Prophet was revealed. Ibn Sa’d narrated Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: “I informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the death of Abu Talib, and he cried. He said: ‘Go and wash him, shroud him and bury him, may God forgive him and have mercy on him.’ So I did, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept asking God’s forgiveness for him for days and would not leave his house until the verse ‘It was not for the Prophet’ was revealed to him.” It has been narrated that the reason for the revelation of the verse was the Prophet’s asking God’s forgiveness for Abu Talib through many chains of transmission: one of them is from Muhammad ibn Ka’b according to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh, mursal. One of them is from Amr ibn Dinar according to Ibn Jarir, and it is also mursal. One of them is from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab according to Ibn Jarir, and it is also mursal. One of them is from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab according to Ibn Sa’d, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir. One of them is from al-Hasan al-Basri according to Ibn Asakir, and it is mursal. It was narrated that it was revealed because of the Prophet’s visit to his mother’s grave and his seeking forgiveness for her, from the chain of transmission of Ibn Abbas according to At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh, and from the chain of transmission of Ibn Masoud according to Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il, and from Buraydah according to Ibn Mardawayh. What is in the two Sahihs takes precedence over what is not in them, assuming that it is authentic, especially since it is mostly weak. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him to his statement: As they brought me up [when I was] small, he said: Then he made an exception and said: It was not for the Prophet to his statement: Except because of a promise He had made to him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he said: It became clear to him when he died and he knew that repentance had ceased from him. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Abu Bakr Al-Shafi’i in his Fawa’id and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Ibrahim kept asking forgiveness for his father until he died. When he died, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, so he disavowed him. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir that a man used to raise his voice in remembrance of God. A man said: Why don’t you lower your voice? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Leave him, for he is a pious person. At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to a man called Dhu Al-Najadayn: He is a pious person, because he used to mention God a lot in the Quran and in supplication. Ahmad also narrated on the authority of Musa ibn Lahi’ah on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Yazid on the authority of Ali ibn Rabah on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn Al-Haad who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, what is a pious person? He said: The one who is humble and supplicates with humility. If this is proven, then it is necessary to accept it and give it precedence over what the linguists have mentioned regarding the meaning of al-wah, and its chain of transmission according to Ibn Jarir is as follows: Al-Muthanna told me, Al-Hajjaj bin Munhal told me, Abdul Hamid bin Bahram told us, Shahr bin Hawshab told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing, he said: Part of his forbearance was that if a man from his people harmed him, he would say to him: May God guide you. 47- "He said, 'Peace be upon you'" meaning a greeting of farewell and parting, like his saying: "And when the ignorant address them, they say, 'Peace.'" It was said that its meaning is: a guarantee from me to you, said Ibn Jarir, and he only granted him security despite his disbelief because he was not ordered to fight him, and the first is more appropriate, and the majority said this, and it was said that its meaning is: praying for his safety, winning him over and being gentle with him, then promising him that he would ask forgiveness for him from God Almighty, to win him over and in the hope that he would be gentle and his harshness would go away: The Sheikh does not abandon his morals until he is buried in the dust of his grave This promise was made before he knew that he would die as an unbeliever, and that the word would come true against him. That is why God Almighty said in another place, But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him after His saying, And Abraham’s seeking of forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. The phrase Indeed, he was ever gracious to me is an explanation of what came before it, and the meaning is that I will ask God for forgiveness for you, for he was very kind and merciful to me. It is said that he was gracious to him and merciful to me if he was merciful to him. Al-Kisa’i said: It is said that he was gracious to me, affectionately and mercifully. Al-Farra’ said: Indeed, he was gracious to me, meaning that he was knowledgeable and merciful, and he would answer me when I called upon him.
9:115: When the previous verse was revealed prohibiting seeking forgiveness for the polytheists, a group of those who sought forgiveness for them feared punishment from God because of that seeking forgiveness, so God Almighty revealed: 115- And God would never lead a people astray etc.: meaning that God Almighty does not cause misguidance upon a people, nor does He call them astray after He has guided them to Islam and the implementation of its laws, unless they commit any of the forbidden things after it becomes clear to them that it is forbidden. However, before it becomes clear to them, there is no sin upon them and they will not be held accountable for it. The meaning of until He makes clear to them what they should avoid is until it becomes clear to them what they must avoid of the forbidden things of the law. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things of what is permissible for His servants and what is forbidden to them, and of all the things that He created.
9:116: 116- "Indeed, to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And you have not besides God any protector or helper." Then He explained to them that He, glory be to Him, has the dominion of the heavens and the earth. No one shares that with Him, and no one disputes with Him. He disposes of His dominion as He wills, including that He gives life to whomever He wills to give life, and causes death to whomever He wills to cause death. And for His servants besides Him, there is no protector to befriend them or helper to aid them. So do not ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they are relatives, for kinship does not benefit anything and does not have any effect. Rather, the disposition of all things belongs to God alone.
9:117: His saying: 117- God has forgiven the Prophet for what he did, may God bless him and grant him peace, of giving permission to stay behind, or for what he did of seeking forgiveness for the polytheists. It is not necessary for repentance to precede the sin from whomever or for whom it occurred, because all servants are in need of repentance and seeking forgiveness. And repentance from God the Most High for the Prophet may be due to his leaving what was more appropriate and more fitting, as in His saying: God has forgiven you for giving them permission. And it is possible that the Prophet’s mention, may God bless him and grant him peace, was for the purpose of informing the sinners that they should avoid sins and repent for what they had committed, and likewise God the Most High forgave the Muhajireen and Ansar for what they had committed of sins. And of this type is what was authentically reported from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his saying: “God looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.” Then He, the Most High, described the Muhajireen and the Ansar as those who followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and did not stay behind him. The hour of hardship was the Battle of Tabuk, for they were in great hardship. What is meant by the hour is all the times of that battle, and it did not refer to a specific hour. Hardship is the difficulty of the matter. His statement: After the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated in al-Kad is the pronoun of the matter, and hearts is raised by tazigh according to Sibawayh. It was said: It is raised by al-Kad, and the meaning would be after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated. Al-A’mash, Hamza, and Hafs read yazigh with a lower ya’. Abu Hatim said: Whoever reads with a lower ya’, it is not permissible for him to raise hearts with al-Kad. Al-Nahhas said: What he did not permit is permissible according to others in the masculine form of the plural. The meaning of yazigh is to perish through effort, hardship and severity. It was said that its meaning is: to deviate from the truth and abandon support and resistance. It was said that its meaning is: to intend to stay behind from the invasion because of the great hardship they are in. In the reading of Ibn Masoud, after they had deviated is and they are the ones who stayed behind according to this reading. In repeating the repentance upon them in His saying: Then He turned to them so that they might repent, there is an apparent emphasis and attention to its matter. This is if the pronoun refers to those whose repentance was mentioned previously. If the pronoun refers to the group, then there is no repetition.
9:118: His saying: 118- And as for the three who stayed behind meaning, He accepted the repentance of the three who stayed behind: meaning, they delayed and their repentance was not accepted immediately, as the repentance of those who stayed behind mentioned above was accepted. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of they left behind is they left, it is said: I left so-and-so" means I left him. Ikrimah ibn Khalid read "they left behind" with a light pronunciation: meaning, they stayed after the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the believers set out for the conquest. Ja'far ibn Muhammad read "they differed" and these three are: Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi' or Ibn Rabi'ah al-'Amiri, and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqfi, and all of them were from the Ansar, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not accept their repentance until the Qur'an was revealed that God had accepted their repentance. It was said that the meaning of "they stayed behind is they corrupted", taken from the bad breath. His statement: until the earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for them means that they delayed accepting repentance until this point, which is the time when the earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for them. Ma is a source: meaning with its vastness, because people turned away from them and did not speak to them from anyone, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade people from speaking to them. Wide means spacious. It is said: a spacious house, wide and wide. In this verse is evidence of the permissibility of abandoning people who commit sins as a discipline for them so that they will be deterred from sins. The meaning of their souls becoming too narrow for them is that their chests became too narrow because of the loneliness that befell them and the estrangement that occurred to them. He expressed the word thinking in his statement: and they thought that there is no refuge from God except to Him with knowledge: meaning they knew that there was no refuge to which they could ever turn except to God, the Most High, through repentance and seeking forgiveness. His statement: Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent means He returned to them with acceptance and mercy, and He revealed in the Qur’an repentance to them so that they might be upright, or He guided them to repentance in the future if they had committed a sin, so that they might repent for it and return to God in it and regret what they had done. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance meaning the One who greatly accepts the repentance of those who repent, the Most Merciful meaning the One who greatly has mercy on those of His servants who seek it.
9:119: His saying: 119- And be with the truthful. This command to be with the truthful after the story of the three indicates that these three attained through truthfulness what God’s repentance attained, and the apparent meaning of the verse is the command to the servants in general. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And God would not mislead a people after He had guided them, he said: It was revealed when they took the ransom from the polytheists on the day of the captives. He said: It was not for you to take it until you were given permission, but God would not punish a people for a sin they committed until He makes clear to them what they should avoid, he said: Until He forbids them before that. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: God’s clarification to the believers regarding seeking forgiveness for the polytheists in particular, and in His clarification of His obedience and disobedience, there is no ambiguity in what they did or left. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym, Al-Bayhaqi and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said to Umar ibn Al-Khattab: Tell us about the Hour of Hardship. He said: We went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Tabuk in intense heat. We stopped at a place where we were afflicted with such thirst that we thought our necks would break. A man would slaughter his camel, squeeze out its dung and drink it, and put what was left on his liver. Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said: O Messenger of God, God has accustomed you to goodness in supplication, so supplicate for us. He raised his hands and did not bring them back until the sky spoke, and it rained and then poured. They filled what they had with them. Then we went to look, but we did not find it had passed the camp. The narrators agreed that the Hour of Hardship was the Battle of Tabuk. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mandah, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, regarding his statement: And concerning the three who stayed behind, he said: Ka’b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayyah, and Murarah ibn al-Rabi’, and all of them were from the Ansar. Ibn Mandah and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ka’b ibn Malik, who said: I never stayed behind from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in any campaign he participated in except the campaign of Tabuk, except for the campaign of Badr, and he did not rebuke anyone who stayed behind. Rather, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) went out seeking the caravan of Quraysh until God gathered them and their enemy without an appointment. I was present with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on the night of al-‘Aqabah when we agreed upon Islam, and I would not have liked to have witnessed Badr in return, even though Badr is more famous and more famous than it among the people. Then he mentioned the long story that is famous in the books of hadith and biographies, and it is well-known among the people of knowledge, so we will not prolong its mention. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: And as for the three who were left behind, he said: meaning they were left behind from repenting, they were not forgiven when God forgave Abu Lubabah and his companions. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Sheikh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Nafi’ regarding his statement: And be with the truthful, he said: It was revealed regarding the three who were left behind. It was said to them: Be with Muhammad and his companions. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: And be with the truthful, he said: With Abu Bakr and Umar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Sheikh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding the verse: he said: With Abu Bakr, Umar and their companions. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: he said: With Ali bin Abi Talib. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Ja’far: he said: With the three who were left behind.
9:120: In His saying: 120- It was not for the people of Medina etc., to further emphasize the obligation to fight with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the prohibition of staying behind him: that is, it was not correct and right for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins such as Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ashja’, Aslam, and Ghifar to stay behind the Messenger of God may God bless him and grant him peace in the Battle of Tabuk. God Almighty singled them out because they had been called upon to fight and did not go out, unlike other Arabs who were not called upon to fight, even though these, due to their proximity and proximity, were more deserving of support and following the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Nor should they prefer themselves over himself that is, they should not prefer themselves over himself, so they should be generous with themselves and protect them, nor should they be generous with the soul of the Messenger of God and protect it as they were generous with themselves and protected it. It is said: I was reluctant about such-and-such: I was above it. Rather, it is obligatory for them to endure hardships with him, and to fight before him against the people of discord, and to sacrifice themselves for his sake. In this report there is a meaning of command. For them, with what is indicated by its being mentioned in this form of rebuke and severe reprimand, and provocation of them, and disparagement of them. And the reference by his saying: that to what is indicated by the context of the obligation to follow the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: that is, that obligation upon them is because they are rewarded for all kinds of troubles and types of hardships. Thirst: thirst, fatigue: exhaustion, and starvation: severe famine in which the stomach shrinks. Ubayd ibn Umayr read thama’ with a long vowel. Others read it with a short vowel, and they are two dialects like khata’ and khata’. And la in these places is redundant for emphasis. And the meaning of in the way of God is in obeying God. His saying: nor do they tread a path that enrages the disbelievers means that they do not tread a place of the places of the disbelievers with their feet or the hooves of their horses or the hooves of their mounts, so that the disbelievers become enraged because of that. Al-Muwatta': a place name, and it may be a verbal noun. And they do not gain from their enemy any niylan meaning they do not inflict death, capture, defeat, or booty on their enemy. Its origin is from the verb nalt which means to be struck. Al-Kisa'i said: It is from their saying something similar to it, and it is not from itad, rather itad is from naltuh by al-'atiyyah. Another said: naltuh means to attain from al-'atiyyah, and naltuh means to catch up with him. The pronoun in bih refers to each of the mentioned matters, and the righteous deed: the accepted good deed: meaning except that God writes it for them as an accepted good deed with which He rewards them, and the phrase God does not waste the reward of the righteous is in the ruling of explaining what came before, although it includes every righteous deed and is primarily true of those mentioned here.
9:121: His statement: 121- And they do not spend a penny is connected to what preceded it: meaning, they do not spend in war, even if it is a small, insignificant thing. And they do not cross a valley which is originally any gap between mountains and hills that is an outlet for a flood. The Arabs say: valley and valleys, not by analogy. An-Nahhas said: And the doer and the verbs are not known, as far as I know, except that it is written for them meaning that what they did of spending and traveling in jihad is written for them so that God may reward them with it the best of what they used to do meaning the best reward for what they used to do of deeds. It is possible that in His statement: except that it is written for them is a pronoun referring to a good deed. A group of people have said that this verse was abrogated by the verse mentioned after it, which is His statement: And it is not for the believers to go forth all together, as it indicates the permissibility of some staying behind while others are engaged in jihad, and this will come. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Malik on the authority of some of the Companions who said: “When the verse, ‘It is not for the people of Madinah’ was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘By Him who sent me with the truth, were it not for the weak among the people, there would not have been a raid except that I was in it.’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement, It is not for the people of Madinah, he said that this was when Islam was small and no one had the right to stay behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. But when Islam increased and became widespread, God said, It is not for the believers to go forth all at once. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awza’i, Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad Al-Fazari, and Isa ibn Yunus Al-Sabi’i that they said regarding the statement of God Almighty, And they shall not gain from the enemy any benefit, they said: This verse is for the Muslims until the Day of Resurrection.
9:122: The commentators differed on the meaning of 122- And it is not for the believers to go forth all together. A group went to the view that it is from the rest of the rulings of jihad, because when God, the Almighty, exaggerated in the command to jihad and volunteering for conquest, the Muslims, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a detachment of the infidels, would go forth all together and leave the city empty. So God, the Almighty, informed them that it was not for them to do that: that is, it was not right or proper for them to go forth all together, rather a group from each group of them would go forth from that group and those other than this group that went forth would remain. They said: And the pronoun in His statement: that they may gain understanding would refer to the remaining group. Meaning: A group from this sect goes out to fight, and whoever remains from the sect stands to seek knowledge, and they teach the fighters when they return to them from the fight, or they go in search of it to the place where they find someone to learn from so that they can take from him the understanding of religion and warn their people when they return to them. Others went to the view that this verse is not from the rest of the rulings on jihad, and it is an independent ruling in itself regarding the legitimacy of going out to seek knowledge and understanding of religion. God the Almighty made it connected to what indicated the obligation of going out to fight, so travel is of two types: the first: travel for jihad, and the second: travel to seek knowledge. There is no doubt that the obligation of going out to seek knowledge only occurs if the student does not find someone to learn from in the city without traveling. Jurisprudence: is the knowledge of the rulings of the Shariah, and what leads to knowledge of it from language, grammar, morphology, rhetoric, and principles. The meaning of why not go out is why not go out, and the sect in the language is the group. God Almighty has made the purpose of this to be to gain understanding of the religion and to warn those who do not gain understanding. He has combined the two righteous objectives and the two correct demands, which are learning knowledge and teaching it. So whoever’s purpose in seeking knowledge is other than these two, then he is a seeker for a worldly purpose, not a religious purpose. So he is as I said: And the one who seeks the world with religious knowledge is as miserable as one who wipes his shoes with a cap. The meaning of perhaps they will beware is the hope that they will beware of neglecting what should be done and will leave it, or of doing what should be left and will do it.
9:123: Then the Almighty commanded the believers to strive hard in fighting the infidels who are closest to them, and to take their war with severity and intensity, and jihad is obligatory for all infidels, even though starting with those closest to the mujahideen is more important and older, then the closest, then the closest, then God informed them of what would strengthen their resolve and make their feet firm, saying: 123- And know that God is with the righteous, meaning with victory for them and support for them against their enemy, and whoever God is with, nothing will stand against him. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: These verses, Go forth, whether light or heavy, and If you do not go forth, He will punish you, were abrogated by His statement, And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once, meaning that one group should go forth and another group should stay with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). So those who stayed with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) were those who would gain understanding of the religion and warn their brothers when they returned to them from the battle, and perhaps they would beware of what would come down after them of God’s decree in His Book and His limits. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on his authority through another chain of transmission with a more complete context. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding this verse, he said: This verse is not about jihad, but when the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) called for years of drought against Mudar, their land became barren, and the tribe among them would come with all of its members until they were free of hardship in Madinah and accepted Islam, although they were liars, so they oppressed the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and exhausted them, so God revealed informing His Messenger that they were not believers, so he returned them to their clans and warned their people not to do what they did, so that is His saying: And that they may warn their people when they return to them that they may beware. There are narrations on this topic from a group of the Tabi’un. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah regarding His saying: Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you, he said: The nearest, then the nearest. Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar from al-Dahhak. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Umar that he was asked about the conquest of Daylam, so he said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) say: Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you, he said: The Romans. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And let them find in you harshness, he said: severity.
9:124: His statement: 124- "And when a surah is revealed" is a narration from Him, the Most High, of the remaining scandals of al-Munafiqun 63:that is, when God, the Most High, reveals to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, a surah from His Noble Book, then some of the hypocrites "say to their brothers among them Which of you has this the surah that was revealed increased in faith?" They say this in mockery of the believers, and it is permissible for them to say it to a group of Muslims, intending thereby to turn them away from Islam and make them lose interest in it. And which of you is raised by the subject and its predicate is "it increased." The meaning of the surah has been explained previously. Then God, the Most High, narrated after their statement that the believers have increased in faith upon their faith, and the fact is that they are rejoicing with this increase in the revelation and what it contains of religious and worldly benefits.
9:125: 125- And as for those in whose hearts is disease, and they are the hypocrites, it will increase them, the revealed surah, in filth upon their filth, meaning evil upon the evil upon which they are, which is disbelief and corruption of belief, and showing something other than what they conceal, and they persisted in that and continued upon it until they died as disbelieving hypocrites. What is meant by disease here is doubt and hypocrisy, and it was said that the meaning is: it will increase their sin upon their sin.
9:126: His saying: 126- Or do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice? The majority read they see with a lower ya lower letter. Hamza and Ya'qub read it with a higher ya high letter, addressing the believers. Al-A'mash read or they did not see. Talha ibn Musarraf read or you do not see addressing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. The meaning of they are tested is that they are tested, as stated by Ibn Jarir and others, or that God, the Exalted, tests them with famine and hardship, as stated by Mujahid. Ibn Atiyyah said with diseases and pains. Qatada and Al-Hasan said about the conquest and jihad with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they see what God has promised of victory, then they do not repent because of that, nor do they remember. “Then” is to connect what comes after it to they see, and the hamza in or they do not see is for denial and rebuke, and the waw is to connect to something understood: that is, they do not look and they do not see. This is an astonishment from God Almighty to the believers about the state of the hypocrites and their stubbornness in hypocrisy and their neglect of looking and considering.
9:127: Then God the Almighty mentioned what they were doing when the Surah was revealed after mentioning what they were saying, so He said: 127- And when a Surah is revealed, some of them look at one another meaning some of the hypocrites look at one another saying Does anyone see you from the believers so that we may leave the place where the revelation is being sent down, for we cannot be patient to listen to it, and we may say whatever we want of slander, mockery and laughter. It was said that the meaning is: And when a Surah is revealed in which God mentions the scandals and disgraces of the hypocrites, some of those who attend the gathering of the Messenger of God say to some of them: Does anyone see you? Then they return to their homes. Ibn Jarir narrated from some of the people of knowledge that he said: Look in this verse is a place where he said: meaning some of them say to one another: Does anyone see you. His saying: Then they turned away means from that gathering to their homes, or from what requires guidance and faith to what requires disbelief and hypocrisy. Then He supplicated against God Almighty, saying: God turned their hearts away meaning He turned them away from goodness and what brings them guidance and righteousness, and He Almighty is the One who turns hearts and turns them. It was said that the meaning is that He let them down from accepting guidance. It was said that it was a supplication that did not intend its content to occur, like their saying: May God kill him. Then God Almighty mentioned the reason for which they turned away from the place of guidance, or the reason for which they deserved the supplication against them by His saying: God turned their hearts away and He said: Because they are a people who do not understand what they hear due to their lack of contemplation and fairness.
9:128: Then God the Almighty concluded this Surah with something that would make some of the difficult tasks it contained seem easy to Him, so He said: 128- There has certainly come to you O group of Arabs a Messenger whom God has sent to you, who has great importance from among yourselves from your kind in that he is an Arab. The majority of commentators agreed that this verse is addressed to the Arabs. Al-Zajjaj said: It is addressed to the entire world. The meaning is There has certainly come to you a Messenger from your kind in humanity Hard for him is what you suffer “what” is a source. The meaning is: your suffering is difficult for him because he is from your kind and was sent to guide you. And suffering is the fatigue for them and the hardship for them with the torment of this world by the sword and the like, or with the torment of the Hereafter by fire, or both of them together eager for you meaning stingy with you entering the fire, or eager for your faith. The first is more appropriate, and Al-Farra’ said: “And the Compassionate: the Merciful. Their meanings have been explained previously: that is, this Messenger is “compassionate and merciful to the believers” among you, O Arabs or people.
9:129: Then he said, addressing his Messenger, comforting him, and guiding him to what to say when he disobeys 129- But if they turn away meaning they turn away from you and do not act upon what you have brought nor accept it then say O Muhammad God is sufficient for me meaning God, the Exalted, the One and Only in divinity, is sufficient upon Him I have put my trust meaning I have entrusted all my affairs and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne describing Him as being great because He is the greatest of all creations. The majority of scholars read it with the accusative case as an attribute of the Throne. Ibn Muhaysin read it with the nominative case as an attribute of the Lord. This reading was narrated from Ibn Kathir. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: As for those who believed, it increased them in faith, he said: Whenever a surah was revealed, they believed in it, so God increased their faith and belief, and they were happy with it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: An abomination to their abomination, he said: A doubt to their doubt. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Or do they not see that they are being tried? he said: They are being killed. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Mujahid, and he said: By famine and hunger. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: By the enemy. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: By fighting in the way of God. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Bakkar Ibn Malik, he said: They would get sick once or twice every year. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed, he said: They would tell a lie or two every year. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah who said: We used to hear one or two lies every year, and many groups of people would tell them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: They looked at each other, that they were the hypocrites. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Do not say we have turned away from the prayer, for some people have turned away, God has turned their hearts away, but say we have completed the prayer. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar. I say: Turning away can be from good as it can be from evil, and its application here to the return of the hypocrites from a good gathering does not indicate that it is only used in this manner. Otherwise, it would follow that any word used in the language of the Arabs in various matters, if it is used in the Qur’an to narrate what happened from the disbelievers, it is not permissible to use it to narrate what happened from the people of good, such as returning, going, entering, exiting, standing and sitting. The necessary consequence is invalid by consensus, so the necessary consequence is the same. The reason for the necessary consequence is clear and obvious. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Harith bin Abi Usamah in his Musnad, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in Dalil Al-Nubuwwah, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, that he said: There is no tribe among the Arabs but that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was born from its Mudari, Rabi`, and Yamani tribes. Ibn Sa`d narrated on his authority regarding his statement: from among yourselves, that he said: You gave birth to him, O group of Arabs. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated in al-Musannaf, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, and Abu al-Shaykh on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad on the authority of his father regarding his statement: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, he said: Nothing of the birth of the Age of Ignorance affected him. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I came from marriage and not from fornication. This has an interruption, but al-Hafiz al-Ramharmuzi connected it in his book al-Fasil Bayn al-Rawi wal-Wa’i, and he said: Abu Ahmad Yusuf ibn Harun ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: I bear witness that my father narrated to me on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I came from marriage and not from fornication from the time of Adam until my father and mother gave birth to me. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘Indeed there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves.’ Ali ibn Abi Talib said: ‘O Messenger of God, what is the meaning of ‘from among yourselves?’ He said: ‘By lineage, marriage, and lineage. There is no fornication in me or in my fathers since Adam. We are all intercourse.’” Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘Indeed there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves.’ He meant from the greatest of you in status. Ibn Sa’d narrated on his authority something similar to the first hadith of Ali. At-Tabarani also narrated something similar on his authority. Ibn Sa’d and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Aisha. There are hadiths with the same meaning on this topic, and it is supported by what is in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere from the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Indeed God chose Ishmael from the descendants of Abraham, and He chose Banu Kinanah from the descendants of Ishmael, and He chose Quraysh from Banu Kinanah, and He chose Banu Hashim from Quraysh, and He chose me from Banu Hashim.’” Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn `Abd Al-Muttalib who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When God created the creation, He made me from the best of His creation, then the best of their souls, then when He created the houses, He made me from the best of their houses. So I am the best of them in house and the best of them in soul.” There are ahaadeeth on this topic. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Mani`, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Abi ibn Ka`b who said: The last verse revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and in another version: the last of the Qur’an to be revealed, was: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves until the end of the verse. A similar version was narrated on his authority through another chain of transmission narrated by `Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id Al-Musnad, Ibn Ad-Durais in his Fadha’il, Ibn Abi Dawud in Al-Masahif, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il, Al-Khatib in Talkhees Al-Mutashabih, and Ad-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived in Medina, Juhayna came to him and said to him: You have settled among us, so give us assurance that we will be safe from you and you will be safe from us. He said: Why did you ask this? They said: We seek safety. So God revealed this verse: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: But if they turn away, then say, ‘God is sufficient for me,’ meaning that the disbelievers turned away from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The Throne was called the Throne because of its height. Many hadiths have been narrated about the description of the Throne, its nature, and its magnitude. Here ends the first third of the interpretation called Fath al-Qadir, which combines the two arts of narration and knowledge of the science of interpretation, written by its author: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shawkani, may God forgive them both. The completion of this third was during the day on Tuesday, perhaps the twentieth of Muharram in the year 1227 AH. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds, and prayers and peace be upon the Master of Messengers, his family and all his companions. Praise be to Him: It was completed by listening to its author, may God prolong its life, in the month of Jumada al-Ula of the year 1235 AH. Yahya bin Ali Al-Shawkani May God forgive them, Amen
10:1: It is Meccan except for three verses from His saying: If you are in doubt to the end of them, this is how Al-Qurtubi narrated in his interpretation from Ibn Abbas. It was narrated from Muqatil that it is Meccan except for two verses, which are His saying: If you are in doubt, which was revealed in Medina. It was narrated from Al-Kalbi that it is Meccan except for His saying: And among them are those who do not believe in him, which was revealed in Medina. It was narrated from Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir that it is Meccan without exception. An-Nahhas, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah Yunus was revealed in Mecca. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Sirin that he said: Surah Yunus was after the seventh. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas that he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God has given me the ra'iyyat to the Ta-Sin in place of the Gospel. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf from Al-Ahnaf that he said: I prayed behind Omar one morning and he recited Yunus, Hud and others. His saying: 1- Alif, Lam, Ra. The discussion of these letters that occur at the beginning of the surahs has already been completed at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, so we will not repeat it, as it contains what suffices from repeating it. Abu Amr, Hamza, Khalaf, and others read with imala. A group of people read without imala. It has been said that the meaning of Alif, Lam, Ra is I am God, I see. An-Nahhas said: I saw Abu Ishaq leaning towards this statement, because Sibawayh had narrated something similar from the Arabs, and he recited: Good things come to us, even if they are noble Any, and if evil, then evil. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said, Alif, Lam, Ra is an oath. Saeed said on the authority of Qatadah, Alif, Lam, Ra is the name of the surah. Other things have been said, which involve difficulty in knowing what God has kept to Himself. The reciters have agreed that Alif, Lam, Ra is not a verse, and that Ta-Ha is a verse. In Muqni’ Abi Amr Al-Dani, it is stated that only the Kufians regard Ta-Ha as a verse. It has been said that perhaps the difference is that Alif, Lam, Ra does not resemble the sections of the verses that come after it, and the reference in His saying, That is to the verses that the surah includes, and the distancing is for emphasis. The demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is what comes after it. Mujahid and Qatadah said: He meant the Torah, the Gospel, and all the previous books, for that is a reference to an absent feminine. It was said that those means these: that is, these are the verses of the Wise Book, which is the Qur’an. The fact that the reference is to the Qur’an is supported by the fact that the previous books were not mentioned, and that the Wise is one of the attributes of the Qur’an, not one of the attributes of anything else. The Wise is the one who rules on what is permissible and what is forbidden, the limits, and the rulings, as Abu Ubaidah and others said. It was said: The Wise means the judge, so it is fa’il in the sense of fa’il, like His statement: And He sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between the people concerning that in which they differed. It was said: The Wise means the one judged, so it is fa’il in the sense of maf’ul, meaning that God ruled in it with justice and kindness, as al-Hasan and others said. It was said: The Wise is the possessor of wisdom because it includes it.
10:2: And the question in his saying: 2- Was it a wonder to the people? is to deny the wonder with what it indicates of rebuke and reprimand, and the subject of was that We inspired and its predicate is a wonder meaning was Our inspiration a wonder to the people. Ibn Masoud read wonder as the subject of was, on the basis that was is complete, and that We inspired is a substitute for wonder. And it was read with a sukoon on the jim from man in his saying: to a man from among them meaning from their kind. And in this revelation to a man from their kind there is nothing that requires astonishment, for no one associates with the kind and guides it and informs it about God Almighty except one who is from his kind. And if he was from other than their kind, he would be from the angels or the jinn, and the intended purpose of sending is difficult then, because they do not feel comfortable with him nor do they see him. And if we assume that he takes shape for them and appears, then either he appears in a form other than the human kind, and that is more alien to their hearts and more distant from their familiarity, or in the human form, then it is necessary for them to deny that he is originally not a human. This is if the astonishment from them is because he is from their kind. And if it is because he is an orphan or poor, then that does not prevent the one who is like that from gathering the qualities of goodness and honor that no one else gathers and reaching the perfection of the qualities to a degree that one who is rich or who is not an orphan falls short of. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before God chose him by sending him, had the qualities of perfection according to the Quraysh, which He is more famous than the sun and more apparent than the day, so they used to call him Al-Amin. His saying: That I warn people is in the accusative case with the preposition removed: that is, that I warn people. It was said: It is the explanatory because in inspiration there is the meaning of saying. It was said: It is the lightened form of the heavy. His saying: A house of truth means a house of truth. Al-Zajjaj said: A high degree. And from this is the saying of Dhu Al-Rummah: You have a foot that people do not deny that, with its high lineage, it has floated on the sea. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The one who is ahead in honor. Abu Ubaidah and al-Kisa'i said: Everything that is ahead in good or evil is considered by the Arabs to be ahead. It is said: So-and-so has precedence in Islam, and with me he has a true precedence, a good precedence, and an evil precedence. From this is the saying of al-Ajjaj: The Banu Awam tribe slipped before the Al-Hakam family and left the kingdom to a king of advanced age. Tha’lab said: The foot is everything you have presented of good. Ibn al-Anbari said: The foot is a metaphor for the work in which there is no delay or procrastination. Qatada said: A true advance. Al-Rabi’ said: A true reward. Al-Hasan said: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi said: He presented him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the praised station. Muqatil said: Deeds they presented, and Ibn Jarir chose it. From it is the saying of al-Waddah: Pray to the Lord of the Throne and take a people who will save you on the Day of Dispute and Error. Other than what was mentioned above, which there is no need to elaborate on, is what he said: They said, ‘This is clear magic.’ Ibn Kathir, ‘Asim, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Khalaf, Al-A’mash, and Ibn Muhaisin read a magician meaning that they meant the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the demonstrative pronoun. The rest read a magician meaning that they meant the Qur’an. The meaning of magic was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. The phrase the disbelievers said is a new sentence, as if it was said: What did they do after the astonishment? Al-Qaffal said: There is an implication in it, and the meaning is: So when he warned them, the disbelievers said that.
10:3: Then God, the Most High, came with words that invalidate the astonishment that the infidels had from the revelation to a man among them, saying: 3- Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days. That is, whoever has this great power that minds are unable to imagine, how can His sending a messenger to people of their kind be a source of astonishment, while the infidels acknowledge that, so how can they not acknowledge the validity of this message with this messenger? The interpretation of this verse has already been presented in Al-A'raf in His saying: Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then He established Himself on the Throne. So it is not far-fetched here. Then He mentioned what indicates His increased power and great status, saying: "He directs the affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission." And He left out the conjunction, because the phrase directs is like an explanation and detail of what preceded it. It was said: It is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun established Himself. It was said: It is a new answer to an implied question, and the origin of direction is looking at the consequences of matters and their outcomes so that they occur in an acceptable manner. Mujahid said: He alone decrees and determines it. It was also said: He sends the command. It was also said: He sends down the command. It was also said: He orders it and carries it out. The meanings are close. It is derived from the root word dabar, and the word matter means thing, which is the states of the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, the throne, and all of creation. Al-Zajjaj said: The infidels who were addressed by this verse used to say: The idols are our intercessors with God. God responded to them by saying that no one has the right to intercede with Him in anything except after His permission, because He knows best where wisdom and right are. The meaning of intercession has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, and in this is a statement of His sovereignty over all matters, glory be to Him, the Most High. The reference in His statement, That, is to the Doer of these things of creation and management: that is, the One Who did these great things, God, your Lord. The demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is the noble name, and your Lord is a substitute for it or a clarification of it or a second predicate. In this sentence is an additional emphasis on His statement, Indeed, your Lord is God, Who created the heavens and the earth. Then He, glory be to Him, commanded them to worship Him after He made clear to them that He is the One truly worthy of it, without anyone else, due to the wonder of His creation and the greatness of His power. So how can they worship inanimate objects that do not hear or see or benefit or harm? The question in His statement, Do you not remember? is for denial, rebuke, and rebuke, because the one who has the slightest remembrance and the least consideration knows this and it is not hidden from him.
10:4: Then He explained to them what their final affair will be after this worldly life, saying: 4- To Him is your return, all of you. In this there is a threat and intimidation that is not hidden, and the accusative of God's promise is in the source, because in His saying: To Him is your return, all of you there is the meaning of a promise or it is accusative with an implied verb, and what is meant by the return is returning to Him, glory be to Him, either by death or resurrection or by both of them, then He confirmed that promise by saying: Truly so it is an emphasis on an emphasis and so there is in the speech from the reiteration what is the ultimate in that. Ibn Abi Ubla read God's promise is true as a resumption, then He, glory be to Him, explained what came before by saying: Indeed, He begins creation and then repeats it meaning that this is His way, He begins His creation from dust and then returns it to dust, or the meaning of the repetition is the reward on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: He creates it and then kills it, then revives it for resurrection, and it was said: He creates it from water and then returns it from one state to another. Yazid bin Al-Qaqa’ read: Indeed, He begins creation with the opening of the hamza, so the sentence is in the accusative case because of what God’s promise was made accusative with: that is, He promised you that He begins creation and then repeats it. It is permissible for the estimation to be because He begins creation, and Al-Farra’ permitted that that be in the nominative case and thus be a noun. Ahmad bin Yahya bin Tha’lab said: The estimation is truly His creation, then he mentioned the ultimate outcome of the repetition and said: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds with justice meaning with justice in which there is no injustice and those who disbelieve will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve It is possible that the other relative pronoun is conjoined with the first relative pronoun: meaning that He may reward those who believe and reward those who disbelieve, and the phrase for them a drink of scalding water is in the accusative case as a state of it and what is conjoined to it: meaning and a painful punishment, and the estimation would be thus and He will reward those who disbelieve while they have this drink and this punishment, but it is problematic that this drink and this painful punishment are from the reward, and it can be said that the relative pronoun in and those who disbelieve is the subject and what follows it is its predicate, so it is not conjoined with the first conjoined, and the ba’ in because they used to disbelieve is for causality: meaning because of their disbelief, and scalding water is hot water, and everything heated according to the Arabs is scalding water. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Alif, Lam, Ra. He said: The openings of the names of God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa al-Sifat, and Ibn al-Najjar in his history narrated on his authority that he said: Regarding his statement: Alif, Lam, Ra. He said: I am God, I see. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak something similar as well. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: These are the verses of the Book. He said: He means these. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: These are the verses of the Book. He said: The books that came before the Qur’an. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When God sent Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a Messenger, the Arabs or those who denied it from among them denied it, and they said: God is greater than for His Messenger to be a human like Muhammad. So God revealed: Is it a wonder to the people that We have revealed to a man from among themselves? “And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed.” When God, the Exalted, repeated the Hajj to them, they said: If he was a human, then someone other than Muhammad was more deserving of the message. Why was this Qur’an not sent down to a great man from the two cities? He said: more noble than Muhammad, meaning Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah from Mecca and Mas’ud bin Amr Al-Thaqafi from At-Ta’if. So God revealed in response to them: Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority regarding His statement: And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing with their Lord. He said: What preceded them of happiness in the first mention. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him that he said: A good reward for the deeds they have done. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas`ud that he said: The footsteps are the deeds they have done. God the Almighty said: And We record what they have done and their footprints. The footprints are their walking. He said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) walked between two pillars of their mosque and then said: This is a written footprint. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri regarding his statement: A true footstep, he said: Muhammad (blessings and peace of God be upon him) will intercede for them. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from Ali bin Abi Talib. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it from Abi bin Ka`b that he said: A true forerunner. There are many narrations from the Tabi`un and others regarding this, and we have presented most of them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: He directs the affair, he said: He alone decrees it. And regarding his statement: Indeed, He begins creation and then repeats it, he said: He brings it to life, then causes it to die, then brings it to life.
10:5: Here he mentioned some of his blessings upon those who are accountable, which are what proves his existence, unity, power, knowledge and wisdom by perfecting his creation in these two lights that alternate continuously after he mentioned before this his creation of the heavens and the earth, his establishment on the throne and other things. And the light is said to be the plural of light like whips and pools. Qanbal read from Ibn Kathir light by making the ya a hamza with the hamza, and there is no basis for this because its ya was an open waw, and its original is light but it was changed to a ya because of the kasra of what preceded it. Al-Mahdawi said: Whoever reads Ḍiyā’ with a hamzah, it is inverted. The hamzah that comes after the alif was brought forward, so it came before the alif, then the ya’ was changed to a hamzah. It is better for Ḍiyā’ to be a verbal noun, not a plural, like qāma yaqūm qiyamān, and sāma yāsūm sāyāman. It is necessary to estimate an adjective: that is, He made the sun Ḍiyā’ and the moon Ḍiyā’, unless it is interpreted as an exaggeration, as if they made the Ḍiyā’ and Ḍiyā’ themselves. It was said: Ḍiyā’ is stronger than Ḍiyā’, and it was said: Ḍiyā’ is what is intrinsic, and Ḍiyā’ is what is incidental. Hence, the sages said: The light of the moon is derived from the light of the sun. His saying: 5- And its measure is mansions meaning the measure of its journey in mansions, or its measure is with mansions, and the pronoun refers to the moon, and the mansions of al-Qamar 54:are the distance it travels in a day and a night with its own movement, and their total is twenty-eight and they are well-known, the moon descends in each night of them a mansion that it does not exceed, so it appears small in the first of its mansions, then it grows little by little until it appears full, and if it is in the last of its mansions it thins and becomes curved, then it is hidden for two nights if the month is full, or one night if it is deficient, and the discussion of this is long. We have compiled a separate letter in response to a question that some scholars brought to us. It was said: The pronoun refers to each one of the sun and the moon, as was said in the Almighty’s saying: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it. And in the saying of the poet: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs We have already presented the investigation of this in what preceded this interpretation, and it is better to refer the pronoun to the moon alone, as in the Almighty’s saying: And the moon - We have determined for it phases. Then He mentioned some of the benefits related to this determination, saying: That you may know the number of years and the reckoning. For in knowledge of the number of years there are countless religious and worldly interests, and in knowledge of the reckoning of the months, days, and nights there is that which is not hidden, and were it not for this determination that God Almighty determined, people would not have known about that nor would they have known what many of their interests are related to it. The year is made up of twelve months, and the month is made up of thirty days if it is complete, and the day is made up of known hours, which are twenty-four hours for the night and day, each of which may have twelve hours on the days of equinox, and one of them is more than the other on the days of increase and decrease, and the difference between the solar and lunar year is well known, then the Almighty explained that He did not create the sun and the moon and the difference in those conditions except with truth and correctness, not falsehood and frivolity, so the reference in His saying: that is to what was mentioned before it, and the exception is emptied of the most general conditions, and the meaning of detailing the verses is to clarify them, and what is meant by the verses of creation or revelation or their combination, and these verses of creation mentioned here are primarily included in that. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hafs, and Ya'qub read yafsal with the lower case. Ibn al-Samif' read tafsal with the upper case in the passive form. The rest read it with the letter noon. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose the first reading, and perhaps the reason for this choice is that before this verb, God did not create this except with truth, and after it, And God did not create in the heavens and the earth.
10:6: Then God, the Almighty, mentioned the benefits that come from the alternation of night and day and what He created in the heavens and the earth of those creatures, saying: 6- Indeed, in the alternation of night and day and in what God has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear God. That is, those who fear God, the Almighty, and avoid His disobedience. He singled them out with these signs because they are the ones who contemplate and reflect on the creations of God, the Almighty, in order to avoid falling into anything that contradicts the will of God, the Almighty, and in view of the consequences of their affair, and what will benefit them in their afterlife. Al-Qaffal said: Whoever ponders these conditions will know that the world was created for people to remain in it, and that its Creator and their Creator did not neglect them, but rather made it a place of work for them. If this is the case, then there must be commands and prohibitions. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the words of God the Almighty: He made the sun a shining light and the moon a light, he said: He did not make the sun like the moon so that night could be distinguished from day, which is His words: Then We erased the sign of the night, the verse. Abu Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: Their faces are toward the heavens, and their backs are toward the earth. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Khalifa Al-Abdi, he said: If God the Blessed and Exalted were not worshipped except by seeing Him, no one would worship Him. But the believers pondered the coming of this night when it came and filled everything and covered everything, and the coming of the power of the day when it came and erased the power of the night, and the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth, and the stars, and the winter and summer, so by God, the believers continued to ponder over what their Lord the Blessed and Exalted created until their hearts were certain of their Lord.
10:7: God Almighty has begun to explain the conditions of those who do not believe in the afterlife, and those who do believe in it, and He has presented the group that did not believe, because the speech in this Surah is with the disbelievers who are amazed by what is not amazed, and neglect to look and think about what should not be neglected, which is seen by every living being throughout his life, so neglecting to look and think honestly results in: not believing in the afterlife, and the meaning of hope here is fear, and from it the poet said: If a bee stings him, he does not want to be stung by it and he stays in a house full of honey bees. It was said that they hope: they covet, and from this is the saying of the poet: Do you hope that the Banu Marwan will listen to me and obey me, while my people are Tamim and the desert is behind me? The meaning according to the first is that they do not fear punishment, and according to the second is that they do not hope for reward if what is meant by the meeting is not its reality. If what is meant by it is its reality, then the meaning is: they do not fear seeing Us or do not hope to see Us. It was said that what is meant by hope here is expectation, so fear and hope are included under it, so the meaning is they do not hope to meet Us they do not expect to meet Us, so they do not fear it or hope for it. And they are satisfied with the life of this world meaning they are satisfied with it in disregard of the Hereafter, so they work for it. And they are reassured by it meaning their souls are at peace with it and they are happy with it. And those who are heedless of Our signs they do not consider them or reflect on them.
10:8: 8- Their abode meaning their place of residence and dwelling is the Fire, and the reference is to those who have the previous characteristics of lack of hope, and the attainment of contentment and reassurance, and heedlessness for what they used to earn meaning because of what they used to earn of disbelief and denial of the afterlife. This is the state of those who do not believe in the afterlife.
10:9: As for the state of those who believe in Him, He, the Almighty, has explained it by saying: 9- Indeed, those who have believed meaning, have done the faith that God has asked of them because of what they have done of contemplation and consideration regarding the verses mentioned above, and done righteous deeds that faith requires, which is what God has prescribed for His believing servants, their Lord will guide them because of their faith meaning, He will provide them with guidance because of this faith combined with righteous deeds, and thus they will reach Paradise. The phrase rivers flow beneath them is a new sentence, or a second piece of report, or in the accusative case as a state. The meaning of beneath them is from beneath their gardens or from before them because they are on raised couches. His saying: in gardens of delight is related to flowing or guides them or another piece of report or a state of the rivers.
10:10: His saying: 10- Their supplication meaning their supplication and calling upon God. It was said: Supplication is worship, like the Almighty's saying: And I will leave you and what you call upon besides God. It was said: The meaning of their supplication here is the claim that exists between the disputants. The meaning is: The people of Paradise will call upon God Almighty in this world and the hereafter to be free from faults and to acknowledge His divinity. Al-Qaffal said: Its origin is from supplication, because the opponent calls upon his opponent to someone who will judge between them. It was said that its meaning is: Their method and conduct, and that is because the one claiming something is consistent in it, so the claim can be made a metaphor for consistency, even if there is no claim or supplication in his saying: Glory be to You, O God. It was said that its meaning is: Their wish, like His saying: And they will have what they call upon. It is as if their wish in Paradise is nothing but glorifying and sanctifying God, and it is the subject and its predicate is Glory be to You, O God, and in it means in Paradise. The meaning of the first statement: That their supplication that they will supplicate with in Paradise is the glorification and sanctification of God, and the meaning is: We glorify You, O God, with glorification. His statement: “And their greeting therein is, ‘Peace’” means the greeting of some of them to others, so the source is added to the subject, or the greeting of God or the angels to them, so it is from the addition of the source to the object. The explanation of this has already been mentioned in Surat An-Nisa’, His statement: And the last of their supplication is, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds’ meaning the conclusion of their supplication, which is glorification, is that they say: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. An-Nahhas said: Al-Khalil’s school of thought is that this ‘an’ is a lightened form of the heavy ‘an’. The meaning is: It is praise be to God. Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Mubarrad said: It is permissible to make it light as it is made heavy. The raising is more correct, and Abu Ubaid only narrated the lightening. Ibn Muhaisin read it with a shaddah on ‘an’ and the accusative of ‘al-hamd’. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they are satisfied with the life of this world, he said: Like his statement: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, We fully repay them for their deeds therein, the verse. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Their Lord will guide them by their faith, he said: They will have a light by which they will walk. Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Their Lord guides them by their faith, he said: Al-Hasan narrated to us: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the believer emerges from his grave, his deeds will be presented to him in a beautiful form and with a pleasant scent, and he will say to him: Who are you? By God, I see you are the eye of a truthful person. He will say to him: I am your deeds, and it will be a light for him and a guide to Paradise. As for the disbeliever, when he emerges from his grave, his deeds will be presented to him in a bad form and with a foul odor, and he will say to him: Who are you? By God, I see you are the eye of a bad person. He will say to him: I am your deeds, and he will be taken away until he enters the Fire.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When they say, ‘Glory be to You, O God,’ they will be given what they desired of Paradise from their Lord. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Hudhayl, who said: Praise is the beginning and the end of the speech. Then he recited: “And the last of their supplication will be: ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’”
10:11: When God the Almighty mentioned the threat for not believing in the afterlife, He mentioned that this punishment is right to be delayed from this worldly life. Al-Qaffal said: When He described them as heedless, He emphasized that by saying that the extent of their heedlessness was that when the Messenger warned them, they hastened the punishment. So God the Almighty explained that there is no benefit in bringing evil to them, so perhaps they will repent and someone will come out of their loins who will believe. It was said that the meaning of 11- And if God were to hasten the evil for the people as they hasten the good is if God were to hasten the punishment for the people as they hasten the reward and good their term would have been completed for them meaning they would have died. It was also said that the meaning is: If God did with the people in responding to His dislike as they wanted to do with them in responding to His good, He would have destroyed them. It was said that the verse is specific to the disbelievers who denied the resurrection and what results from it. He said in Al-Kashshaf: He put their hastening of good in place of His hastening of good for them, indicating the speed of His response and assistance to their request, as if their hastening of good was hastening it, and what is meant is the people of Mecca, and His saying: Then He rained down upon us stones from the sky Al-Kashshaf verse. It was said that the meaning is: And if God were to hasten for them evil when they hastened it, just as He hastened for them good when they hastened it, so what was deleted was omitted because the rest indicated it. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is And if God were to hasten for the people evil just as they hastened for good, then he omitted hastening and put its description in its place, then he omitted its description and put the complement to it in its place. He said: This is the doctrine of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, and it is the saying of Al-Akhfash and Al-Farraa, who said: Its origin is like their hastening, then the kaf was omitted and it was placed in the accusative. Al-Farra’ said: “As you say, ‘I hit Zayd, I hit you’: that is, like you hit him. The meaning of ‘their term would have been fulfilled for them’ is that they would have been destroyed. However, He, the Exalted, did not hasten the evil for them, so they were given respite. It was also said that it means: they were killed. Ibn ‘Amir read ‘the term would have been fulfilled’ in the active form, which is a good reading because it is appropriate for His statement, ‘And if God were to hasten it’.
