His statement, ‘Then we leave those who do not expect to meet Us, in their transgression they wander blindly’: the ‘fa’ is for conjunction with an implied word indicated by the speech, because His statement, ‘And if God were to hasten it’ includes the negation of hastening, so it is as if it was said: But He does not hasten the evil for them, nor does He decree their term for them, so we warn them, etc.: that is, we leave them and give them respite. Transgression is arrogance, which is loftiness and elevation. The meaning of ‘blindness’ is they are perplexed: that is, we leave them perplexed in their arrogance, haughtiness, and refusal to accept the truth, as a means of tempting them from Him, the Exalted, and as a betrayal.
10:12: Then God the Almighty made it clear that they are liars in hastening evil, and if what they asked for had happened to them, they would have shown helplessness and impatience, so He said: 12- "And when harm touches man meaning this type that is true for everything that causes harm he calls upon Us at his side" the lam is for time like his saying I came to him in such and such a month, or in the accusative case as a state indicated by the conjunction sitting or standing with it, and the lam can mean on: meaning he called upon Us lying down "or sitting or standing" as if he said: He called upon Us in all the mentioned states and others, and He specifically mentioned the mentioned ones because they are the most common for man, and other than them are rare like bowing and prostration, and it is permissible to mean that he calls upon God while lying down and unable to sit, and sitting but not sitting to stand, and standing and unable to walk, and the first is more appropriate. Al-Zajjaj said: Adjusting the states of supplication is more eloquent than enumerating the states of harm, because if he was a constant supplicant, then forgot at a time of ease, it would be more amazing. His saying: So when We removed his harm from him, he passed on as if he had never called upon Us to remove the harm that had befallen him. That is, when We removed the harm that had befallen him, as the letter fa indicates, he continued on his way that he was on before the harm befell him and forgot the state of effort and affliction, or he passed on from the position of supplication and entreaty and did not return to it as if he had no knowledge of it, as if he had not called upon Us when the harm befell him to remove that harm that befell him. It was said that the meaning of passed on is that he continued in his disbelief and did not give thanks and did not learn a lesson. Al-Akhfash said: The word in “as if he had not called upon Us is the lightened form of the heavy form, and the meaning is: as if he had finished.” The simile is in the accusative case as a state. This state that God the Almighty mentioned for the supplicant is not limited to the people of disbelief, rather it happens to many Muslims, their tongues soften with supplication and their hearts with humility and submission when what they dislike befalls them. When God removes it from them, they neglect supplication and entreaty, and forget what is required of them in terms of thanking God for the blessing that He has bestowed upon them, such as answering their supplications, removing the harm that has befallen them, and repelling the evil that has befallen them. This is one of the things that indicates that the verse includes both Muslims and non-Muslims, as is indicated by the wording of people and the wording of human beings. “O God, enable us to be thankful for Your blessings, and remind us of the conditions in which You have bestowed upon us the answer to our supplications, so that we may increase our thanks for the things that we cannot bear or are able to do otherwise, and how much You are independent of them and how much we need them.” If you are grateful, I will surely increase you. The reference in His statement, Thus has He made fair-seeming to the transgressors what they used to do, is to the source of the verb mentioned after it, as mentioned more than once, meaning that like that amazing adornment, He made fair-seeming to the transgressors in their work. The transgressor in the language is the one who spends a lot of money for a vile purpose, and the place of thus is the accusative as a source. And adornment is either from God Almighty in the way of beautification and not being kind to them, or from the way of Satan through whispering, or from the way of the soul that commands evil. Meaning: He made it seem attractive to them to turn away from supplication, to neglect gratitude, and to be preoccupied with desires.
10:13: Then the Almighty mentioned what is in the course of deterrence and warning against what these people did, saying: 13- And We have destroyed generations before you when they committed injustice, meaning the past nations before these infidels who were contemporary with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: that is, We destroyed them before your time. It was said: The address is to the people of Mecca in the way of turning to exaggerate the warning, and when is an adverb for We destroyed: that is, We destroyed them when they committed injustice by denying, trading with the messengers, and going too far in sins without delaying their destruction as We delayed your destruction. The waw in and their messengers came to them with clear proofs is for the state by implying had: that is, and their messengers whom We sent to them came to them with clear proofs: that is, with clear signs that clearly indicate the truthfulness of the messengers. It was said that the waw is for conjunction with they wronged, and the first is more appropriate. It was said that what is meant by injustice here is polytheism, and the waw in and they were not “So that they may believe” is in apposition to they wronged, or the sentence is parenthetical, and the lam is to emphasize the negation: that is, it is not right for them and it is not right for them to believe due to their lack of readiness for that and the deprivation of kindness from them. Thus do We recompense the criminal people, that is, We recompense the criminal people with the same recompense, which is the complete extermination of every criminal, and this is a severe threat to the infidels who were in his time, or to the infidels of Mecca in particular.
10:14: Then He, the Almighty, addressed those to whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, saying: 14- Then We made you successors, meaning We made you successors on earth after those generations whose report you hear and whose effects you see. Successors is the plural of successor, and we have already discussed it at the end of Surat Al-An’am. The lam in to see how you do is the lam of to see how you do good and evil deeds, meaning to see how you do good and evil deeds, and how is in the accusative case with the verb that follows it: meaning to see what deeds you do, or in the accusative case of the state: meaning in what state you do the deeds appropriate for succession.
10:15: Then God, the Most High, narrated a third type of their stubbornness and their tampering with the verses of God, saying: 15- And when Our verses are recited to them as clear proofs, and in it there is a shift from addressing to the third person, turning away from them. What is meant by the verses are the verses in the Noble Book: that is, when the reciter recites to them Our verses indicating the establishment of monotheism and the invalidation of polytheism while they are clear proofs: that is, clear proof of what is required, those who do not expect to meet Us say, and they are the deniers of the Resurrection, and its interpretation was presented shortly: that is, they said to the one who recited them to them, and he was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Bring a Qur’an other than this or change it. They asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they heard what angered them in what he recited to them from the Qur’an of condemning the worship of idols, and the severe threat to those who worship them, one of two things: either to bring a Qur’an other than this Qur’an while this Qur’an remains as it is, or to change this Qur’an by abrogating some or all of its verses and putting others in their place that match it. Their will and their purpose, so God commanded him to say in response to them, It is not for me, meaning it is not appropriate for me and it is not permissible for me to change it on my own. So he denied one of the two parts, which is the change because it is what he could do if it were permissible, unlike the other part, which is bringing another Qur’an, because that is not within his power and he is not able to do it. It was said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, denied the easier of the two parts for himself to be evidence of the denial of the more difficult of the two by the first way, and this from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, is from the aspect of keeping up with fools, since such a suggestion does not come from rational people after God, the Most High, commanded him to do so. He knows best what is in the interests of His servants and what repels the disbelievers from these base requests and cold questions, and on my own is a source used as an adverb, on my own. Al-Zajjaj said: They asked him to omit what it contained of mentioning resurrection and revival. It was also said: They asked him to omit what it contained of faults in their gods and belittling their dreams. It was also said: They asked him to turn the promise into a threat, the forbidden into lawful, and the lawful into forbidden. Then he ordered him to confirm what he had answered them with, that it was not right or proper for him to change it of his own accord, by saying: I follow nothing except what is revealed to me, meaning: I follow nothing except what is revealed to me from God Almighty, without changing, transforming, distorting, or misrepresenting. So he limited his situation, may God bless him and grant him peace, to following what was revealed to him. Perhaps the intention of the infidels with this question was to expose the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the fact that the Qur’an was his speech and that he was able to bring something else and change it. Then God Almighty ordered him to say to them, completing the answer to them: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day. This sentence is like an explanation for what he had presented in the answer before it, and the tremendous Day is the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:meaning: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day. I disobeyed my Lord by doing what you are asking for, assuming that it is possible for me to be punished on the Day of Resurrection.
10:16: Then the Almighty confirmed that this Qur'an is from God and that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, only conveys to them what God has commanded him to convey, and he is not able to do anything else. He said: 16- "Say: 'If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you'" meaning that this Qur'an that is recited to you is by God's will and desire, and if God had willed that I not recite it to you or convey it to you, I would not have recited it. The whole matter is subject to God's will, and I have no say in that. His statement: nor would I have made you aware of it is connected to what I recited. And if God had willed, I would not have made you aware of the Qur'an: meaning I would not have informed you of it on my tongue. It is said: I knew the thing and God made me aware of it. This is how the majority read it with the alif from adarahu yadarihu a'lamu ya'lamuhu. Ibn Kathir read nor did I make you aware of it without an alif between the lam and the hamza, and the meaning is: And if God had willed, He would have informed you of it without me reciting it to you, so the lam is the lam of emphasis that entered the alif of af'al. It was read adra'kum with a hamza, so it was said: it is derived from the alif because they are from the same root, and it is possible that it is from dar'atuhu if you push it, and adhra'tuhu if you make it daryan. The meaning is: I will make you opponents by reciting it, you push me away with argument and you accuse me of lying. Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan read: And I do not know you by it. Abu Hatim said: its original form is wa la adhra'tukum by it, so the ya' was replaced with an alif. An-Nahhas said: this is a mistake. The narration from al-Hasan is wa la adra'tukum with a hamza. His saying: I have remained among you for a lifetime before it is an explanation of why that was by the will of God and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did nothing but convey the message: that is, I have remained among you for a lifetime before it: that is, a long time, which is forty years before the Qur’an. You know me for my truthfulness and trustworthiness. I am not one of those who read or write. Do you not understand? The hamza is for rebuke and rebuke: that is, do you not follow what reason requires of not denying me for what you know from the continuous habit over a long period of time of truthfulness and trustworthiness, and my not reading the books revealed to the messengers and learning what their people have of knowledge, nor my seeking anything of this matter nor my keenness on it, then I came to you with this book from which you were unable to produce a surah, and you fell short of opposing it, and you are the Arabs who are known for their perfect eloquence and who are acknowledged to have reached a level in it that no one else is concerned with? Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, And if God were to hasten evil for the people 3:10, he said: It is a person’s saying to his children and wealth when he is angry with them: O God, do not bless him and curse him. “Their term would have been fulfilled for them.” He said: He would have destroyed the one who called upon him and caused his death. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding the verse, he said: It is a man’s saying to another man: O God, curse him, O God, disgrace him, and he loves that his prayer be answered. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, he said: It is a man’s supplication against himself and his wealth for something he hates to be answered. Al-Qurtubi narrated in his Tafsir on the authority of Ibn Ishaq and Muqatil regarding the verse, they said: It is the saying of Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky. If He had hastened this for them, they would have perished. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, He called upon Us lying on his side, he said: Lying down. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: He called upon Us lying on his side, sitting, or standing, he said: In any case. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ who said: Call upon God on the day of your prosperity, and He will answer you on the day of your adversity. And I say: Thanking God more for prosperity will ward off adversity from you, for His promise to the grateful to increase blessings is a sign of His ward off calamities from them, because the sweetness of blessings is gone when the bitterness of calamity is present: O God, unite for us the bringing of blessings and the taking away of calamities, for we thank You as much as the grateful have thanked You in every tongue in every age, and we praise You as much as the praisers have praised You in every tongue in every age. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding His statement: Then We made you successors on the earth al-Baqarah 2:17, he said: It was mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab recited this verse and said: Our Lord has spoken the truth. He did not make us successors on the earth except to look at our deeds, so show God the best of your deeds by night and by day, in secret and in public. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Successors on the earth for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Bring a Qur’an other than this or change it, he said: This is what the polytheists of Mecca said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: nor did I make you aware of it, he said: I informed you of it. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: nor did I make you aware of it, he said: I did not make you aware of it. Saeed Ibn Mansour and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite: nor did I warn you of it. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: I have remained among you a lifetime before it, he said: I did not recite to you nor did I mention. They narrated on his authority that he remained forty years before revelation came to him and he saw the vision for two years, and God revealed to him for ten years in Mecca and ten in Medina, and he died when he was sixty-two years old. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent for forty years, and he remained in Mecca for thirteen years, receiving revelation. Then he was ordered to emigrate, so he emigrated for ten years, and he died at the age of sixty-three years.
10:17: His statement: 17- So who is more unjust is an interrogative with the meaning of denial, i.e. no one is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God with a lie and more a lie even though invention can only be a lie to show that this, in addition to being an invention against God, is a lie in itself. So perhaps the invention is a lie in the attribution only, as when he attributes the sin of Zaid to Amr. Abu al-Su`ud mentioned the meaning of this in his interpretation. It was said: This is part of his response, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the polytheists when they asked him to bring a Qur’an other than this Qur’an, or to change it, so he explained to them that if he did that, it would be an invention against God, and there is no injustice comparable to that. It was said: Those who invent a lie against God are the polytheists, and those who deny the verses of God are the People of the Book. Indeed, the criminals will not succeed is an explanation for the fact that there is no one more unjust than he who invents a lie against God or denies His verses: i.e. they will not attain what they seek nor They win good, and the pronoun in it refers to the matter: that is, this is the matter.
10:18: Then God, the Most High, condemned them for worshipping idols, and explained that they do not benefit those who worship them nor harm those who do not worship them, so He said: 18- And they worship besides God meaning, bypassing God, the Most High, to worship others besides Him, not in the sense of abandoning His worship altogether, that which neither harms them nor benefits them meaning that which is not capable of harming or benefiting. It is the right of the worshipped to reward those who obey Him and punish those who disobey Him. The waw is to connect this sentence to the sentence And when Our verses are recited to them, and what in that which does not harm them is a relative pronoun or a description. The waw in and they say, ‘These are our intercessors with God’ is to connect to and they worship. They claimed that they intercede for them with God, so He does not punish them for their sins. This is the height of ignorance on their part, as they await intercession in the end from someone from whom there is no benefit or harm at the moment. It was said: They intended by this intercession to improve the conditions of Their worldly life, then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer them, saying: “Say: ‘Do you inform God of that which He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?’” Abu al-Samal al-Adawi read tanbi’un with a light emphasis from anba’ yanbi’. Those who did not read it with a heavy emphasis from naba’ yanbi’. The meaning is: Do you inform God that He has partners in His kingdom who are worshipped as He is worshipped, or do you inform Him that you have intercessors without His permission, while God the Almighty does not know of any partner or intercessor without His permission from among all His creatures who are in His heavens and on His earth? The gist of this statement is that there is no one like that at all, and in this there is mockery of the disbelievers that is not hidden, then God the Almighty cleared Himself of associating partners with them, and it is possible that it is the beginning of a statement that is not included in the statement that God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to answer them with, and it is possible that it is part of what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to say to them in response to them. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read ‘amma yashrikoon with a lower vowel. The rest read it with a higher vowel. Abu Ubaid chose the first reading.
10:19: His statement: 19- And mankind were but one community, then they differed. Its interpretation has been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. The meaning is: that mankind were all but one community, united for the sake of God, the Most High, and believing in Him. Then some became disbelievers and others remained believers, so they differed with one another. Al-Zajjaj said: They were the Arabs who were polytheists. He said: Every newborn is born in a state of fitrah, then they differed upon reaching puberty, and the first is more apparent. It is not meant that every group created a religion of disbelief that was different from the others, but what is meant is that some disbelieved and some remained monotheistic as we have mentioned. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, which is that He, glory be to Him, will not judge between them in what they differed over except on the Day of Resurrection, it would have been judged between them in this world in that they difference over. But that was prevented by the word that does not change. It was said that the meaning of it would have been judged between them is the establishment of the Hour upon them. It was said that their destruction would have been completed. It was said that the word is that God has given this nation respite so that He will not destroy them with punishment in this world. It was said that the word is that He does not take anyone except with an argument, which is sending messengers as God, glory be to Him, said: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger. It was said that the word is His statement: My mercy precedes My wrath. Isa bin Omar read it would have been judged in the active form. Those other than him read it in the passive form. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: An-Nadr said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Al-Lat and Al-Uzza will intercede for me, so God revealed: “Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed. And they worship besides God that which can neither harm them nor benefit them.” Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And mankind were but one community, then they differed. Ibn Mas’ud said: They were on guidance. It was narrated that he read it like this. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: And mankind were but one community, he said: Adam alone. And they differed, he said: When one of the sons of Adam killed his brother. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse: The people were people of one religion, following the religion of Adam, then they disbelieved. Had your Lord not extended their lifespan until the Day of Resurrection, judgment would have been passed between them.
10:20: His statement: 20- And they say God Almighty mentioned here a fourth type of their shame, and it is connected to His statement: And they worship and He used the present tense to evoke the image of what they said. It was said: And those who said it are the people of Mecca, as if they did not take into account what was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the dazzling signs and overwhelming miracles, which if there were nothing among them except the Qur'an, it would have been sufficient as clear evidence and conclusive confirmation: That is, why was not a sign revealed to him from the signs that we suggest to him and ask of him, such as reviving the dead and turning mountains into gold and the like? Then God Almighty commanded him to answer them, saying: “Say: ‘The unseen belongs only to God.’” That is, the revelation of the verse is unseen, and God is the One who is unique in His knowledge, and He keeps it to Himself. I, you, and all of His creations have no knowledge. So wait for the revelation of the verses you have proposed. I am with you among those who wait for their revelation. It was said that the meaning is: Wait for God’s judgment between me and you to make the truth prevail over falsehood.
10:21: His statement: 21- And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has befallen them, at once they plot against Our signs. Because the Almighty explained in the previous verse that they asked for a sign out of stubbornness, deceit and obstinacy, and He confirmed that with what He mentioned here that when the Almighty let them taste mercy from Him after adversity befalls them, they did in return for this great blessing, deceit against the signs of God. What is meant by letting them taste His mercy, the Almighty, is that He expanded their provisions and bestowed blessings upon them through rain and good fruits after adversity befell them through drought and hardship in their lives. So they did not thank for His blessings nor did they appreciate them properly, rather they added them to their idols that neither benefit nor harm, and they attacked the signs of God and used every trick to repel them, and this is the meaning of deceit in them. The first if is conditional, and its answer is if they have deceit, and it is sudden. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh mentioned the meaning of that. Then God the Almighty ordered His Messenger to answer them, saying: “Say: God is swifter in plotting,” meaning He hastens punishment. The comparative form Af’al indicates that their plotting was swift, but God’s plotting was swifter than that. And the suddenness of the word indicates speed, because the meaning is that they surprised the plotting, meaning they brought it about suddenly and quickly. Calling God’s punishment a plot is a matter of similarity, as has been stated in several places in the Noble Book: Indeed, Our messengers write down what you plot. Ya’qub in one narration and Abu Amr in another narration read they plot with a lower syllable, while the rest read it with a higher syllable. The meaning is that God’s messengers, who are the angels, write down the plotting of the disbelievers. This is not hidden from the angels who are the guardians, so how could it be hidden from the All-Knowing, All-Aware? This is a severe warning to them, and this sentence is an explanation of the sentence before it, for if their plot is apparent and not hidden, then God’s punishment will inevitably come to pass. The meaning of this verse is close to the meaning of the previous verse, which is And when harm touches a person, and in this there is an addition, which is that they do not limit themselves to merely turning away, but rather they seek to bring about disasters for God’s signs through the plotting they plot.
10:22: 22- It is He who makes you travel on land and sea. The Almighty gave an example for these people so that the intended meaning would be completely revealed. The meaning of making them travel on land is that they walk on their feet, which He created for them so that they may benefit from them, and they ride the beasts that God created for them to ride. The meaning of making them travel on sea is that He inspired them to make ships in which they ride in the depths of the sea, and He made that easy for them and removed from them the causes of destruction. Ibn Amir read He who spreads you out in the sea with the letter nun and the letter shin with the dot from nashr as in his saying: Then spread out in the land meaning He, the Most High, spreads them out in the sea, saving whomever He wills and drowning whomever He wills until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them “al-alk” is used for the singular and plural and is masculine and feminine, and its investigation has been presented above. And they sail means the ships with them: that is, with those riding on them, and until for the end of the goal and the goal is the content of the conditional sentence in its entirety, so the restrictions considered in the condition are three: the first: being in the ship, the second: its sailing with them with a pleasant wind that is not a storm, and the third: their joy. The restrictions considered in the penalty are three: the first is it came to her meaning a stormy wind came to the ship or the good wind came: meaning a stormy wind met it, and the storm is the strong blowing of the wind, the second is and the waves came to them from every place meaning from all sides of the ship and what is meant is that it came to the riders in it, and the wave is what rises from the water above the sea, and the third is they thought that they were surrounded meaning that their thoughts were overwhelmed by destruction, and its origin is from the enemy surrounding a people or a country, so this surrounding was made an example of destruction even if it was not by the enemy as here, and the answer to if in his saying: if you were in the ship is his saying: it came to her until the end, and his saying: call upon God is a substitute for they thought because this supplication that occurred from them was only when they thought of destruction and it is the reason for it, so it was a substitute for it, a substitute of inclusion because it includes it, and it is possible that the sentence they called upon is a new sentence as if it was said: What did they do? It was said: They called upon God, and in His statement: And they ran with them is a shift from direct address to third person, the benefit of which is the author of Al-Kashshaf, exaggeration. Al-Razi said: The transition from direct address to third person in this situation is evidence of hatred and alienation, just as the opposite of that in His statement: You alone do we worship is evidence of satisfaction and closeness, and the accusative of sincerely is in the state: meaning they did not taint their call with any impurities, as was their custom in other places, that they associate their idols in their call, and this was not for the sake of belief in God alone, but rather for Him to save them from what they were on the verge of destruction, because they knew that no one could save them except God, the Exalted. In this is evidence that people were created to turn to God in times of hardship, and that the call of the one in need is answered, even if he is a disbeliever. In this verse, it is stated that these polytheists did not pay attention to their idols in this situation and similar situations, so how strange is the occurrence of sects in Islam who believe in the dead? If such a situation were to occur to them at sea, they would call upon the dead and not sincerely call upon God as the polytheists did, as has been transmitted to us in a manner that is sufficient to establish certainty. So look, may God guide you, at what these satanic beliefs have done and where their people have led them, where Satan has thrown them, and how he has led them and taken control of them? Until they submitted to him in a manner that no idol worshipper could have ever hoped for, nor even some of it. So, to God we belong and to Him we shall return. The lam in If You save us from this is the lam that introduces the oath: that is, saying that, and the reference in His saying: from this is to what they fell into of being on the verge of destruction at sea, and the lam in we will surely be is the answer to the oath: that is, we will surely be in every situation among those who are grateful for Your blessings that You have bestowed upon us, including this blessing that we are about to ask You to relieve us of and save us from. It has been said that this sentence is the object of the verb supplicated.
10:23: 23- So when God delivered them from this ordeal that they had fallen into, and answered their prayer, they did not fulfill what they had promised themselves, but rather they did the deed of the ungrateful, not the deed of the grateful, and they made transgression on earth without right a place for gratitude. And if in if they transgress is the suddenness: that is, they surprised transgression on earth without right, and transgression is corruption, from their saying the wound transgressed: if it spreads in corruption, and an increase in the earth to indicate that their corruption is comprehensive to the regions of the earth, and transgression, even if it contradicts being right, rather it can only be wrong, but an increase without right is an indication that they did that without any doubt on their part, rather out of rebellion and stubbornness, because they may do that for a doubt that they believe in, even though it is false. His statement: O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves, the enjoyment of worldly life. When the Almighty mentioned that those mentioned earlier transgress upon the earth unjustly, He mentioned the consequence of transgression and its evil outcome. Ibn Ishaq, Hafs and al-Mufaddal read the word mataa' in the accusative case, while the rest read it in the nominative case. Whoever reads it in the accusative case makes what precedes it a complete sentence: that is, your transgression is a burden upon yourselves. Thus, your transgression is the subject and against yourselves is its predicate, and mataa' is in the position of the confirmed verbal noun, as if it were said: you enjoy the enjoyment of worldly life. The verbal noun with the implied verb is a resumption. It was said that mataa' in the accusative reading is a circumstance of time like the arrival of the pilgrim: that is, the time of the enjoyment of worldly life. It was said that it is its object for it: that is, for the sake of the enjoyment of worldly life. It was said that it is accusative by removing the preposition: that is, like mataa'. It was said that it is in the state as a verbal noun in the sense of the object: that is, enjoying. Most of these opinions have been discussed in explaining the interpretation of the accusative case. As for those who read with the raising of mataa’, they made it the predicate of the subject: that is, your transgression is the provision of worldly life, and upon yourselves is related to the source, and the estimate is: your transgression is only against your likes and those whose kind is your kind, the provision of worldly life and its benefit that does not last, so what is meant by yourselves in this way is their kind, and they are expressed by the souls because of the compassion that a kind perceives for its kind, and it was said: the raising of mataa’ is as a second predicate, and it was said that it is as predicate of a deleted subject: that is, it is mataa’. Al-Nahhas said: According to the reading of the raising, your transgression is raised by the subject and its predicate is the provision of worldly life, and upon yourselves is the object of the transgression, and it is permissible for its predicate to be upon yourselves and an implied subject: that is, that is, the provision of worldly life, or it is the provision of worldly life. End. Some of these mentioned aspects have also been discussed in explaining the raising in a way that lengthens the discussion to no avail. The result is that if the predicate of the subject is upon yourselves, then the meaning is: that what occurs of oppression against others is oppression against the oppressor himself, considering what the matter leads to in terms of revenge against him as retribution for his oppression. If the predicate is made enjoyment, then what is meant is that the oppression of this human race against one another is quickly disappearing and close to disappearing, like all the pleasures of worldly life, for they are soon to go away and quickly vanish, and there is no great benefit or use for that. Then the Almighty mentioned what will be the retribution for that oppression on the Day of Resurrection with a severe threat, saying: Then to Us is your return. The predicate is presented to indicate restriction, and the meaning is: that after this worldly life and its enjoyment, you will return to God, so He will reward the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing and the doer of good for his good. Then We will inform you of what you used to do in this world: that is, We will inform you of what you used to do in this world of good and evil. What is meant by that is retribution, as you say to someone who did wrong: I will tell you what you did, and in it is the most severe threat and the most terrible intimidation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ regarding his statement: Then wait, indeed, I am with you among those who wait, he said: He is frightening them with His punishment and chastisement. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And when We let the people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, at once they devise a plan against Our signs, he said: Mocking and denying. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: And they think that they are encompassed, he said: They are doomed. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, and the gist of it is that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) declared the blood of a group of people, including Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, shed the blood of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of the conquest, he fled from Makkah and boarded a ship, but a storm struck them. The ship’s owners said to the people on the ship: Be sincere, for your gods will not help you at all. Ikrimah said: “If sincerity does not save me at sea, nothing else will save me on land. O God, I promise You that if You spare me from what I am in, I will go to Muhammad and place my hand in his hand, and I will find him to be forgiving and generous.” So he came and became Muslim. Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym and al-Khatib in his history narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Three things will come back to their al-Nas 114:deceit, breaking a covenant, and transgression.” Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O people, your aggression is only against yourselves. “Evil plotting only encompasses its own people.” So whoever breaks his promise, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself. Al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman on the authority of Abu Bakrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not transgress and do not be an aggressor, for God says: ‘Your aggression is only against yourselves.’” Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Makhul who said: Three things, whoever has them will be against them: plotting, aggression, and breaking their promise. God the Almighty said: Your aggression is only against yourselves. I say: These three things that the Qur’an indicates will return to the one who does them should be included in the list: deception, for God says: They seek to deceive God and those who believe, but they deceive none but themselves. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a mountain were to attack another mountain, the aggressor of the two would be crushed. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Ibn Umar.
10:24: When God the Almighty mentioned the previous worldly pleasures, He came with a new statement that includes explaining its condition and the speed of its passing, and that it returns after it fills the eyes with its splendor, and attracts the souls with its delight. And it prompts its people to shed each other's blood, and violate their sanctities out of love for it and passion for its apparent beauty, and in a race to enjoy it, and in a rush to obtain what the souls desire from it with a type of complex simile, so He said: 24- The example of the life of this world is only like water which We send down from the sky to the end of the verse. Meaning: That its likeness in the speed of its departure and the description of a characteristic that contradicts and contrasts what it was like is like the types of plants on the earth in the disappearance of its splendor and the departure of its joy and the speed of its passing, after it was fresh, green and tender, its swaying branches intertwined, its intertwined leaves flourished, the lights of its light sparkled, and the flowers wove their types of flowers. The simile is not what the kaf entered in His statement: like water which We sent down from the sky, but rather what is understood from the speech, and the ba’ in and the vegetation of the earth mingled with it is for causality: that is, because of it the vegetation of the earth mingled with it by intertwining some of it with others until it reached the level of perfection. It is possible that what is meant is that the plant was in its first emergence and the beginning of its occurrence not shaking or growing, so when water fell upon it, it shook and grew until some types mixed with others of what people and livestock eat of grains, fruits, grass and straw, and the earth took on its adornment. It is said in As-Sahah that adornment means gold, then everything that is fake and counterfeit is likened to it. Meaning: The earth took its beautiful color, some of which resembles the color of gold, some of which resembles the color of silver, some of which resembles the color of ruby, and some of which resembles the color of emerald. The root ofاَقيلنتisَقَقيلنتshe was decorated. The taa was assimilated into the zay, and the alif of connection was brought because the assimilated letter takes the place of two letters, the first of which is silent, and it is not possible to begin with a silent letter. Ibn Mas`ud and Abi bin Ka`b readْقَقيلنت she was decorated according to the original. Al-Hasan, Al-A`raj, and Abu Al-`Aliyah readْقَقيلنتshe was decorated according to the weight of a`f`alat, meaning the adornment on her was adorned, likening her to a bride who wears fine clothes of many colors. `Awf bin Abi Jamila said: Our elders readْقَقيلنتshe was decorated according to the weight of aswadat, and in Al-Muqaddami’s narrationْقَقيلنتshe was decorated, and the root of it isَقَقيلنتshe was decorated according to the weight of tafa`alat. Al-Sha'bi and Qatadah read it as azinta, and the meaning of all these readings is what we mentioned. And its people thought that they were able to harvest it, meaning that their assumptions were overwhelming or they were certain that they were able to harvest it and benefit from it. The pronoun in alayhi refers to the land, and what is meant is the vegetation that is on it. Our command came to it is the answer to if, meaning Our command came to it to destroy it, uproot it, and strike it with some defects. So We made it a harvest, meaning We made its crops similar to harvested crops in that they were cut off from their roots. Abu Ubaidah said: The uprooted harvest is as if it had not flourished yesterday, meaning as if its crops had not been present in it yesterday, green and fresh, from ghani in place with a kasra, yaghni with a fatha if he resided in it, and what is meant by yesterday is the recent time, and maghani in the language is the homes. Qatadah said: As if it had not enjoyed. Labid said: I sang for years before the Dahis River, if only the stubborn soul had immortality Qatada read ka’an lama yaghna with a sukoon, referring the pronoun to az-Zukhruf. Those other than him read taghanna with a sukoon, referring the pronoun to the earth. Likewise, meaning like that beautiful detail. We detail the verses of the Qur’an, including this verse, that they may reflect on what it contains. It is possible that what is meant is the verses of creation.
10:25: His statement: 25- "And God invites to the abode of peace." When He turned His servants away from inclining toward this world with what He had given them of the previous example, He encouraged them to the abode of the Hereafter by informing them of this call from Him, the Almighty, to the abode of peace. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Peace is God Almighty, and His abode is Paradise. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is God invites to the abode of safety. The meaning of peace and safety is one, like breastfeeding and suckling, and from it the saying of the poet: Greetings, Umm Bakr. Do you have any peace after your people? It was said: He meant the abode of peace, which is greeting, because its people receive peace from God in the sense of greeting, as in His statement: “Their greeting therein is peace.” It was also said: Peace is the name of one of the seven gardens: one of them is the abode of peace, the second is the abode of glory, the third is the garden of Eden, the fourth is the garden of refuge, the fifth is the garden of eternity, the sixth is the garden of paradise, and the seventh is the garden of delight. It was also said: What is meant is the abode of peace that occurs between the believers in Paradise, and they agreed that the abode of peace is Paradise, but they differed about the reason for naming it the abode of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path. God, the Almighty, made the call to the abode of peace general, and guidance specific to whomever He wills to guide, to complete the argument and demonstrate His independence from His creation.
10:26: Then the Almighty divided the people of the call into two groups, and explained the condition of each group, saying: 26- For those who do good is the best and more. That is, those who do good by performing the deeds that God has obligated upon them and refraining from the sins that He has forbidden them to do. What is meant by the best is the best reward. Ibn al-Anbari said: The Arabs apply this word to a beloved and desired quality, and therefore left out its description. It was said that what is meant by goodness is Paradise. As for the increase, it was said that what is meant by it is what is more than the reward of favor, like His saying: That He may give them their rewards and increase them from His bounty. It was said that the increase is looking at His noble face. It was said that the increase is doubling the good deed to ten times its value. It was said that the increase is a room of pearls. It was said that the increase is forgiveness from God and His pleasure. It was said that He, glory be to Him, gives them from His bounty in this world what He will not hold them accountable for. Other things were said that are of no benefit in mentioning, and an explanation of what is true will come at the end of the research. And neither dust nor humiliation shall cover their faces. The meaning of shall cover is to overtake. From this it was said: an adolescent boy if he catches up with men. It was said: he ascends. It was said: he covers. The meaning is close. Qatar is dust. From this is the saying of al-Farazdaq: Crowned with the king's robe, followed by waves above which you can see the banners and the qitra Al-Hasan read qatr with a sukoon on the second letter, and the meaning is the same, as Al-Nahhas said, and the singular of qatr is qatra, and humiliation is what appears on the face of submission, brokenness and disgrace, and the meaning is that no dust covers their faces and no disgrace appears in them. It was said that qatr is gloom, and it was said that it is the blackness of the faces, and it was said that it is the smoke of the Fire. Those are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein eternally. The reference to those described by the previous qualities is that they are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein and enjoy its various types of pleasures.
10:27: 27- And those who have earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil is like it. This is the second group of the people of the call, and it is connected to for those who have done good, as if it was said: And for those who have earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil is like it, or it is estimated and the recompense of those who have earned evil deeds is the recompense of an evil with like it: meaning He recompenses one evil deed with one evil deed, nothing is added to it, and this is more appropriate than the first because it is from the category of connecting to the objects of two different agents, and what is meant by evil is either polytheism or sins that are not polytheism, which are the sins that the sinners commit, Ibn Kaysan said: The ba is redundant, and the meaning is: the recompense of an evil deed is like it, and it was said: The ba with what follows it is the report, and it is related to something omitted that took its place, and the meaning is: the recompense of an evil deed is like it, like your saying, I am only with you, and it is permissible for it to be related to recompense and the estimate is the recompense of an evil deed with like it is, so the report of the subject is deleted, and it is permissible for recompense to be raised on the assumption that they will have the recompense of an evil deed It would be like his saying: Then a number of other days meaning he has a number, and the ba in this estimation is related to something omitted as if he said to them the recompense of a fixed evil is its like, or it could be emphatic or redundant. His saying: Disgrace and disgrace will overwhelm them meaning humiliation and disgrace will overwhelm them. It was read Yarhiqhum with the lower They have no protector from God meaning no one, whoever he may be, can protect them from the wrath and punishment of God, or they have no one from God or from Him to protect them as is the case for the believers, and the first is more appropriate, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state, or renewed As if their faces were covered with pieces of the dark night Qata'a is the plural of Qata'a, and based on this it would be dark in the accusative case as a state of al-Layl 92:meaning their faces were blinded with pieces of the night in a state of its darkness. The majority of the reciters read it in the plural. Al-Kisa'i and Ibn Kathir read Qata'an with the sukoon on the ta', so dark based on this is an attribute of Qata'an, and it is possible that it is a state of the night. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: The cutting off is a group of the night. Those meaning those described with these reprehensible qualities are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. The generality of eternity here is restricted to what is transmitted in the Sunnah about the emergence of the disobedient monotheists.
10:28: His statement: 28- "And the Day We shall gather them all together The gathering is the plural, and all together is in the accusative case as a state, and the Day" is in the accusative case with an implied pronoun: meaning warn them of the Day We shall gather them, and the sentence is resumed to explain some of their ugly conditions. The meaning is that God, the Exalted, will gather the worshipper and the worshipped to question them. "Then We will say to those who associated" in the state of gathering and the time of gathering, rebuking them in front of all witnesses, and rebuking them for the presence of those who share in worship with them and the presence of their worshipped ones, "In your place meaning stick to your place and remain in it and stand in your place, you and your partners" on the basis that the waw is a waw with. His statement: "So We removed them from each other": meaning We separated and cut off the communication that was between them in this world: It is said, "Zaylathu fatazel meaning, scattered him, so he separated, and al-Mizā'ilah" means separation. It is said, "Zā'iluh means Mizā'ilah and Zayyālan if he left him, and al-Mizā'ilah" means dispersion. Al-Farra’ said: Some of them read Fazilna and what is meant by partners here are the angels, and it was said the devils, and it was said the idols, and that God the Almighty speaks them at this time. And it was said the Messiah, and Ezra, and it appears that it is every deity of the polytheists, whoever it may be, and the phrase And their partners said, ‘You did not worship us’ is in the accusative case as a state with the estimation of had, and the meaning is: And their partners whom they worshipped and made partners of God the Almighty said, ‘You did not worship us, but you only worshipped your desires and your misguidance and your devils who misled you’, and the partners were added to them even though they made them partners of God the Almighty, because they gave them a share of their wealth, so they are their partners in their wealth from this perspective, and it was said: because they are their partners in this address, and this denial from the partners, even if it is contrary to what the polytheists did in worshipping them, its meaning is denying their worship of them regarding their command to worship them.
10:29: 29- "Then sufficient is God as a witness between us and you if we were commanded to worship Him or were pleased with that from you if we were, of your worship, unaware, if" is the lightened form of the heavy one, and the lam is the distinguishing factor between it and the negative, and the one who said this statement is the worshipped ones. They said: to those of the polytheists who worshipped them: "Indeed, we were, of your worship of us, unaware", and what is meant by heedlessness here is: not being pleased with what the polytheists did in worshipping them, and in this is evidence that these worshipped ones are not the devils because they are pleased with what the polytheists did in worshipping them, and it is possible that they are devils, and this denial from them is interpreted as them not forcing them to worship them nor compelling them to do so.
10:30: 30- "There every soul will be tested for what it has put forth" meaning in that place and in that situation, or at that time, using the metaphor of the name of time for place, every soul will taste and experience the reward for what it has put forth of deeds. The meaning of "tablu" is to taste and experience, and it was said to learn, and it was said to follow, and this is according to the reading of those who read yatalu with the superscript double, attributing the action to every soul. As for the reading of those who read nablaw with the nun, the meaning is: that God tests every soul and examines it, and what it has put forth is a substitute for every soul. The meaning is: that He treats it as one who tests it and inspects its conditions. His statement: And they will be returned to God, their true Master is in apposition to Our refuge. The pronoun in returned refers to those who associated others with God, meaning they will be returned to His reward and what He has prepared for them of punishment. Their Master is their Lord, and the Truth is an attribute of Him, meaning the Truthful in Lordship, unlike the false deities they took. The Truth is read in the accusative case as an expression of praise, like their saying: Praise be to God, the People of Praise. “And what they used to invent has vanished from them,” meaning what they used to invent, that the deities that He truly deserves to be worshipped, to intercede for them with God and bring them closer to Him, has been lost and invalidated. The result is that these polytheists return to the Truth in that situation, acknowledge it, and admit it, and acknowledge the invalidity of what they used to worship and make a god, but when that does not benefit them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the vegetation of the earth mingled with it, he said: It mixed and grew with the water every color of what people eat, such as wheat and barley, and all the grains of the earth, legumes and fruits, and what the cattle and beasts eat of grass and pastures. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And it was adorned, he said: It was made to grow and look good. And regarding his statement: As if it had never prospered yesterday, he said: As if it had never lived, as if it had never enjoyed life. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Ibn Abbas and Marwan ibn Al-Hakam that they used to recite after his statement: And its people thought that they had power over it, “And God would not have destroyed it except for the sins of its people.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd Al-Rahman that he used to recite: And We did not destroy it except for the sins of its people, “Thus do We detail the verses.” Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Majlaz who said: It was written in Surah Yunus up to this verse: Until, when the earth takes on its adornment up to they reflect, and if the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would wish for a third valley, and nothing satisfies the soul of the son of Adam except dust, and God accepts the repentance of whoever repents, so it was erased. Abu Nu`aym and al-Damiati narrated in his Mu`jam on the authority of al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: “And God invites to the abode of peace,” meaning: He invites to the work of Paradise. And God is peace, and Paradise is His abode. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah regarding his statement: And guides whom He wills, he said: He guides them to the way out from doubts, tribulations, and misguidance. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “There is no day whose sun rises but that there are two angels on either side of it calling out a call that all of God’s creation hears, except for the two heavy burdens: ‘O mankind, come to your Lord.’ That which is little and sufficient is better than that which is much and distracts. And there is no day whose sun sets but that there are two angels on either side of it calling out a call that all of God’s creation hears, except for the two heavy burdens: ‘O God, give to the one who spends a replacement, and give to the one who withholds destruction.’ ‘By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears,’ until His saying: ‘for hardship.’” Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Sa’id bin Abi Hilal that he heard Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ali recite: “And God invites to the abode of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.” He said: Jabir told me that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) came out to us one day and said: “I saw in a dream that Gabriel was at my head and Michael was at my feet, one of them saying to the other: Give him an example. He said: Listen, your ear hears, and understand, your heart understands. Your example and that of your nation is like that of a king who took a house, then built a house in it, then held a banquet in it, then sent a messenger inviting the people to his food. Some of them responded to the messenger and some of them left. So God is the king, the abode is Islam, the house is Paradise, and you, O Muhammad, are the messenger. Whoever responds to you enters Islam, and whoever enters Islam enters Paradise, and whoever enters Paradise eats from it.” The meaning of this has been narrated through various chains of transmission. Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Qatada narrated on the authority of God, the Almighty, regarding His statement, “And God invites to the abode of peace,” that he said: It was mentioned to us that it is written in the Torah: O seeker of good, come, and O seeker of evil, fear Him. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that when he recited, “And God invites to the abode of peace,” he would say: At Your service, our Lord, and at Your pleasure. Ahmad, Muslim, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and others narrated on the authority of Suhaib that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse, For those who do good is the best and more, that he said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, a caller will call out: O people of Paradise, you have an appointment with God that He wants to fulfill for you. They will say: What is it? Did He not make our scales heavy, make our faces white, admit us to Paradise, and remove us from Hell? He said: Then the veil will be lifted for them and they will look at Him, and by God, God has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking at Him, nor anything more soothing to their eyes.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ad-Daraqutni in Al-Ru'yah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Musa on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “On the Day of Resurrection, God will send a caller who will call out in a voice that the first and the last of them will hear: ‘God has promised you the best and more.’ The best is Paradise, and the more is looking at the face of the Most Gracious.’ Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ka’b ibn Ujrah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding his statement: “For those who have done good is the best and more.” He said: The more is looking at the face of the Most Gracious. These people, Ad-Daraqutni and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu ibn Ka’b that he asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about his statement: For those who have done good is the best and more. He said: Those who have done good are the people of monotheism, the best is Paradise, and the more is looking at the face of God. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Al-Shaykh, Ad-Daraqutni, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Khatib and Ibn Al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Anas with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Daraqutni, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq regarding the verse, he said: The best is Paradise, and the extra is looking at the face of God. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, on the same authority regarding the verse. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Daraqutni, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah regarding the verse, he said: The extra is looking at the face of God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Daraqutni, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Musa something similar. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Lalaka’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud something similar. Sa’id bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ali, he said: The extra is a room made of a single pearl with four doors, its rooms and doors made of a single pearl. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And more, he said: It is like his statement: And with Us is more, meaning He rewards them for their deeds and increases them from His bounty. He said: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof. Narrations have been narrated on the authority of the Tabi’in and those after them regarding the interpretation of the increase, most of which are that it means looking at the face of God, the Most High. This interpretation has been established from the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. At that time, there was no speech left for the speaker, nor any attention paid to the arguments that occurred between the followers of the madhhab who do not know what they can benefit from from the pure Sunnah. If they knew that, they would refrain from much of their nonsense, and God is the source of help. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And let not darkness overwhelm their faces, he said: Darkness shall not cover them, he said: The blackness of the faces. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding the verse, he said: Darkness is the blackness of the face. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: Disgrace. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Suhaib on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, And neither darkness nor humiliation shall cover their faces, he said: after they look at Him, the Almighty. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding His statement, And those who have earned evil deeds, he said: those who have committed major sins. The recompense of an evil deed is like it, he said: the Fire. As if their faces had been covered with pieces of a dark night, the pieces: the blackness. The verse in Al-Baqarah abrogated it. Yes, whoever has earned evil, the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, And humiliation shall cover them, he said: humiliation and hardship shall cover them. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority regarding His statement, They will have no protector from God, he said: no protector. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement, And the Day We shall gather them, he said: the gathering is death. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding His statement, Then We shall separate them, he said: We shall separate them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The deities that they used to worship besides God will be set up, and He will say: Are these the ones you used to worship besides God? They will say: Yes, these are the ones we used to worship. The deities will say to them: By God, we did not hear, see, understand, or know that you used to worship us. They will say: Yes, by God, we used to worship you. The deities will say to them: God is sufficient as a witness between us and you, if we were unaware of your worship. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What they used to worship besides God will be presented to them on the Day of Resurrection, and they will follow them until they are driven to the Fire. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: There every soul will be made to see what it has put before. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi: There it will be made to see means it will be followed. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: It will be tested means it will be tried. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, Tablu meaning: it will see every soul will see what it has put forth what it has done and what they used to invent will be lost to them what they used to call upon of rivals with Him. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement, and they will be returned to God, their true Master he said: it was abrogated by his statement, God is the Master of those who believe, and the disbelievers will have no Master.
10:31: When He explained the scandals of the polytheists, He followed them by presenting conclusive arguments about the conditions of sustenance, the senses, death, life, beginning, return, guidance and right guidance. The Almighty built the argument on questioning and delegating the answer to those responsible so that it would be more effective in compelling the argument and more effective in the souls. He said: 31- Say O Muhammad to the polytheists as an argument for the truth of monotheism and the invalidity of what they are upon of polytheism Who provides for you from the sky and the earth from the sky with rain, and from the earth with plants and minerals. If they acknowledge, the desired will be achieved. If they do not acknowledge, then they must acknowledge that it is God who created them. Who owns the hearing and the sight or is it the disconnected? In this there is a transition from one question to another. He specifically mentioned hearing and sight because of what they contain of amazing craftsmanship and great dazzling power: that is, who can own them and make them in this amazing quality and strange creation so that they can benefit from them with this great benefit, and obtain from them benefits that do not fall under He confined the confinement, then moved to a third argument, and said: And who brings forth the living from the dead the human being from the sperm, the bird from the egg, the plant from the seed, or the believer from the disbeliever and brings forth the dead from the living meaning the sperm from the human being or the disbeliever from the believer, and what is meant by this question is who gives life and causes death. Then he moved to a fourth argument, and said: And who manages the affair meaning who determines it and decides it, and this is from the connection of the general to the specific because he has made general what came before and other than it Then they will say, ‘God’ meaning their statement in response to these questions will be that the doer of these matters is God Almighty if they are fair and act according to what is required by sound thought and intellect, and the elevation of the noble name as the predicate of a deleted subject or a subject whose predicate is deleted, meaning God does that, then God Almighty commanded him after they answered with this answer to say to them Do you not fear God? The question is for denial, and the fa is for connecting to something understood: meaning you know that, so will you not fear God and do what this knowledge requires of Fear God who does these actions.
28:88: 32- That is God, your Lord, the Truth. That is, that is, the One who does these actions is your Lord, who is described as the Truth, not what you have made partners with Him. The question in His statement, What is there after the Truth except error? is for rebuke and rebuke if what is an interrogative, not if it is negative as the speech implies. The meaning is: What is there after the Truth except error? If the proof of the Lordship of the Lord, glory be to Him, is true by their acknowledgement, then anything other than Him is false, because the Necessary Being must be one in His Essence and Attributes. Then how do you turn away? That is, how do you permit deviation from the apparent Truth and fall into error, since there is no intermediary between them? Whoever transgresses one of them falls into the other. The question is for denial, exclusion, and astonishment. Likewise, His statement: 88- And do not invoke with God another god, for this is an allusion to someone other than Him. Then He, glory be to Him, made Himself one and described Him as eternal and everlasting, saying: “There is no god but He. Everything,” of things, whatever it may be, will perish except His Face, meaning except His essence. Al-Zajjaj said: His Face is in the accusative case as an exception. If it had been in a place other than the Qur’an, it would have been in the nominative case, meaning everything other than His Face will perish, as the poet said: Every brother who leaves his brother, by your father’s life, except Al-Farqadhan The meaning is that every brother, except the two stars, is separated from his brother. His is the judgment, meaning the effective judgment. He decides as He wills and rules as He wants. And to Him you will be returned, at the resurrection, so that He may reward the doer of good for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. There is no god but Him, glory be to Him, the Most High. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, eternally, he said: always. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, And lost from them on the Day of Resurrection, what they used to invent, he said: they used to lie in this world. Ibn Abi Shaybah in Al-Musannaf, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority, Qarun was from the people of Moses, he said: He was his cousin and he used to pursue knowledge until he gathered all knowledge. He continued in that matter until he transgressed against Moses and envied him. Moses said to him, God commanded me to take the zakat, but I refused. Moses said, “Moses wants to consume your wealth. He came to you with prayer and brought you things, and you tolerated them. Would you tolerate giving him your wealth?” They said, “We cannot tolerate them. What do you think?” He said to them, I think I should send for one of the prostitutes of the Children of Israel, so that we may send her to him and she may accuse him of wanting to have intercourse with her. So they sent for her and said to her, We will give you your judgment on condition that you testify against Moses that he committed adultery with you. She said, Yes. So Korah came to Moses and said, Gather the Children of Israel and tell them what your Lord has commanded you. He said, Yes. So he gathered them and they said to him, What has your Lord commanded you? He said, "He commanded me to worship God and not to associate anything with Him, and to uphold the ties of kinship, such and such. And He commanded me, if a married person commits adultery, to be stoned." They said, Even if it is you? He said, Yes. They said, Then you have committed adultery. He said, I have? So they sent for the woman and she came. They said, What do you testify against Moses? Moses said to her, I adjure you by God to tell the truth. She said, If you adjure me by God, they will leave me alone and offer me a reward so that I accuse you of adultery and testify that you are innocent and that you are the Messenger of God. Moses fell down in prostration weeping. Then God revealed to him, What makes you weep? We have given you authority over the earth, so command it and it will obey you. ’ He raised his head and said, ‘Take them.’ So I took them up to their heels. They kept saying, ‘O Moses, O Moses.’ He said, ‘Take them.’ So I took them up to their knees. They kept saying, ‘O Moses, O Moses.’ He said, ‘Take them.’ So I took them up to their necks. They kept saying, ‘O Moses, O Moses.’ He said, ‘Take them.’ So I took them and covered them. Then God revealed, ‘O Moses, My servants asked you and begged you but you did not answer them. By My Glory, if they had called upon Me, I would have answered them.’ Ibn Abbas said, ‘That is why He said, So We caused the earth to swallow him and his house meaning He caused him to sink to the lowest earth. Ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Khaithamah who said, “The keys to Qarun’s treasures were made of hides, each key the size of a finger, each key to a separate treasury. When he mounted, the keys were carried on seventy white, white-footed mules.” Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him that he said: I found in the Bible that the mules that held the keys to Qarun's treasures were white and had white feet, and each key did not exceed a finger, and each key contained a treasure. I said: I did not find in the Bible what Khaithamah mentioned. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse {to be a burden for a company} that he said: it is heavy. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him that he said: a company of strong men cannot lift it. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him that he said: a company is forty men. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding the verse {Indeed, God does not like the exultant} that he said: the exultant. And regarding the verse {and do not forget your portion of this world} that he said: to work in it for your hereafter. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the verse {then he went out to his people in his finery} that he said: with four thousand mules. A group of the Tabi'un narrated statements about the adornment he wore to his people, but none of them are authentically attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Rather, they are from the reports of the People of the Book, as we have mentioned to you more than once. I do not know how the chain of transmission of this hadeeth attributed to Ibn Mardawayh is. Whoever obtains his book should look into it. Al-Faryabi narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home, that he said: He was swallowed up to the lowest part of the earth. Al-Muhammadi and Al-Daylami narrated in Musnad Al-Firdaws from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), regarding his statement, “That is the home of the Hereafter.
