We assign it to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption,” that he said: tyranny upon the earth and taking what is not right. A similar narration was narrated from Muslim Al-Batin, Ibn Jurayj, and Ikrimah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saeed ibn Jubayr, who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth, that he said: transgression upon the earth. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Hasan, that he said: It is honour and elevation with those in authority. And I say: If that is done to strengthen oneself in the truth, then it is a good characteristic, not an evil characteristic. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: “A man might like his sandal strap to be better than his companion’s sandal strap, so this verse, ‘That is the home of the Hereafter which We assign to those who do not desire exaltation upon the earth or corruption,’ is included.” Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir after mentioning this narration on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him: “This applies to someone who likes that, not just for the sake of adornment, so there is nothing wrong with that, as it has been proven that a man said, ‘O Messenger of God, I like my garment to be nice and my shoes to be nice. Is that arrogant?’ He said, ‘No, God is beautiful and loves beauty.’” Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: This verse, meaning, ‘That is the home of the Hereafter,’ etc., was revealed about the just and humble rulers and the powerful among the people. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Adi bin Hatim who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon me, a pillow was thrown to him, so he sat on the ground and said: I bear witness that you do not seek exaltation on earth or corruption, so I became a Muslim. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Waqid that the verse: Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) at Al-Juhfah when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left as an emigrant to Madinah. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd bin Humayd narrated on the authority of Al-Bukhari, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi, through various chains of narration, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: To bring you back to a place of return, he said: To Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh added: Just as He brought you out of it. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Humayd, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: To bring you back to a place of return, he said: The Hereafter. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Abu Ya'la and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority regarding his statement, To bring you back to a place of return, he said: His place of return is Paradise. In another version, To bring you back to the hereafter, Al-Hakim narrated in Tarikh and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Ali Ibn Abi Talib, who said: To bring you back to a place of return, Paradise. Sa'id Ibn Mansur, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that when the verse, Everything on it will perish, was revealed, the angels said: The people of the earth have perished. When the verse, Every soul will taste death, was revealed, the angels said: Every soul has perished. When the verse, Everything will perish except His Face, was revealed, the angels said: The people of the heavens and the earth have perished. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Everything will perish except His Face, he said: Except for that which is intended by His Face.
10:33: 33- Thus has the word of your Lord come into effect upon those who defiantly disbelieve, that they will not believe. That is, just as the truth came into effect and was established after misguidance, or just as it came into effect that they were turned away from the truth, so has the word of your Lord come into effect: that is, His judgment and decree upon those who defiantly disbelieved: that is, they departed from the truth to falsehood and rebelled in their disbelief out of stubbornness and obstinacy. The phrase that they will not believe is a substitute for the word. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, this word came into effect upon them, which is their disbelief. It is permissible for the phrase to be an explanation of what preceded it by estimating the lam: that is, because they will not believe. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for them to not believe, with the kasra, as a resumption. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read for the words of my Lord in the plural. The rest read it in the singular.
10:34: His saying: 34- "Say: Is there among your partners one who initiates creation and then repeats it?" The Almighty mentioned in this a fifth argument against the polytheists, the command of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say it to them, and even though they do not acknowledge the Resurrection, but since it was an apparent and clear command, and He established evidence for it in this Surah in a manner that cannot be rejected by anyone who is fair and does not deny it, he was like a Muslim to them who has no denial or rejection in him. Then the Almighty commanded him to say to them: "Say: God initiates creation and then repeats it, so how are you deluded?" That is, He is the One who does that and no one else. This statement that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the command of God Almighty to him is on behalf of the polytheists in the answer, either by way of prompting them and informing them of how to answer and guiding them to what to say, or because this meaning has reached a level of clarity that does not require the admission of the opponent and knowledge of what he has, or because the polytheists do not speak what is correct in This answer is to avoid being forced to accept the argument or being recorded as stubborn and obstinate if they deviate from the truth. The meaning of How are you turned away? is: How are you turned away from the truth and turned away from it to something else.
10:35: Then God the Almighty commanded him to present a sixth argument to them, so He said: 35- "Say: Is there among your partners any who guides to the truth?" The question here is like the previous questions, and the evidence of guidance after the evidence of creation occurred frequently in the Qur'an, such as His saying: He who created me, and He guides me and His saying: He who gave to each thing its form and then guided and His saying: He who created and proportioned * And He who measured and guided and the verb of guidance comes transitive with lam and ila, and they have the same meaning. This was narrated from Al-Zajjaj. The meaning is: Say to them, O Muhammad, is there among your partners any who guides to the religion of Islam and calls people to the truth? If they say no, then say to them: God guides to the truth and no one else, and the evidence for that is what preceded from the evidence indicating that He, glory be to Him, is the exclusive right to this, and God, glory be to Him, guides His servants to the truth through what He has established for them of signs in creation, and His sending of messengers and His revelation of books, and His creation of what the servants can use to reach that from minds, understandings, hearing and sight, and the question in His statement: Is he who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who guides not unless he is guided? is for confirmation and to make the argument binding. The reciters differed in la yahdi no guidance. The people of Medina read except Nafi' yahdi with a fatha on the ya', a sukoon on the ha', and a shaddah on the dal, and they combined two sukoon letters in their reading. An-Nahhas said: No one can pronounce combining two sukoon letters. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: Whoever seeks such a thing must move a light vowel to a kasra, and Sibawayh calls this stealing. Abu Amr and Qalun read in one narration between the fatha and the sukoon. Ibn Amir, Ibn Kathir, Warsh and Ibn Muhaisin read with a fatha on the ya' and the ha' and a shaddah on the dal. An-Nahhas said: This reading is clear in Arabic, and the original in it is yahtadi guided, the ta' was assimilated into the dal and its movement was changed to the ha'. Hafs, Ya'qub and Al-A'mash read like Ibn Kathir except that they broke the ha'. They said that because the breaking is the original when two sukoon letters meet. Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim, confirmed yahdi with a kasra on the ya' and the ha' and a shaddah on the dal, and this is for imitation. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and Yahya bin Waththab read yahdi with a fatha on the ya', a sukoon on the ha' and a soft dal from hada yahdi. An-Nahhas said: This reading has two aspects in Arabic, although they are far-fetched: The first is that Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: In yahdi means is guided. The second is that Abu Al-Abbas said: The meaning is or he who is not guided except by him, then the speech was completed and he said after that: except that he is guided, meaning but he needs to be guided, so it is a discontinuous exception as you say so-and-so does not hear except that he hears, meaning but he needs to hear. The meaning according to the previous readings is: Is the one who guides people to the truth, and He is God, the Most High, more deserving of being followed and emulated, or is the one who is not guided himself except by someone else guiding him, let alone guiding someone else? The exception in this case is an exception devoid of the most general conditions. His saying: What is the matter with you? How do you judge? This is an expression of astonishment at their condition with two successive questions: meaning, what is the matter with you? How do you judge by taking these people as partners for God? Both questions are for rebuke and rebuke, and how is in the accusative case with you judge.
10:36: Then the Almighty explained what these people are upon in their religion, and on what they built it, and with what they followed this false religion, which is polytheism, so He said: 36- "And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture is of no avail against the truth at all." This is an introductory statement that is not included in the previous commands. The meaning is: What these polytheists follow in their association with God and their making rivals for Him is nothing but conjecture, guesswork, and intuition. This was not based on insight, rather it was the conjecture of those who thought among their predecessors that these deities bring them closer to God and that they intercede for them. This conjecture of theirs was not based on any foundation at all, rather it was merely a confused imagination and false intuition. Perhaps the indefiniteness of conjecture here is for the sake of belittling: that is, except a weak conjecture that is not based on what other conjectures are based on. It was said that what is meant by the verse is that most of them follow nothing in their belief in God and their acknowledgment of Him except conjecture. The first is more appropriate. Then God Almighty informed us that mere suspicion does not replace the truth at all, because the matter of religion is built on knowledge, and through it the truth is made clear from falsehood, and suspicion does not take the place of knowledge, nor is the truth attained through it, nor does it replace the truth in anything. It is permissible for something to be in the accusative case as a source or as a direct object, and from the truth is a state of it, and the sentence is resumed to explain the matter of suspicion and its invalidity, Indeed, God is Knowing of what they do of ugly actions that are not based on proof.
10:37: His statement: 37- "And this Qur'an could not have been invented by anyone other than God." When He, the Most High, finished with the proofs and arguments of monotheism, He began to establish the matter of prophethood: that is, it is not correct and not right that this Qur'an, which includes clear arguments and evident proofs, could have been invented by people other than God. Rather, it is from God, the Almighty, the Majestic. How can it be correct that it could have been invented, when the people who were the most eloquent of the Arabs in speech and the most precise of them in mind were unable to produce a surah from it? "But this Qur'an was a confirmation of what was before it" of the books revealed to the prophets, and this confirmation itself is an independent miracle, because its stories agree with what is in the previous books, even though the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not see that, nor did he learn it, nor did he ask about it, nor did he contact anyone who had knowledge of that. The accusative of confirmation is as a predicate of the implied "was after but," and it is possible that its accusative is as a cause for an omitted verb: that is, but God revealed it as a confirmation of what was before it. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of the verse, And this Qur’an should not be fabricated is like His statement, And it is not for a prophet to take spoils and And it is not for the believers to go forth all together. It was said that an has the meaning of lam: meaning, this Qur’an should not be fabricated. It was also said that it has the meaning of la: meaning, it should not be fabricated. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said: The meaning in His statement, but it is a confirmation is but it was a confirmation, and the nominative case is permissible according to them, meaning, but it is a confirmation. It was also said that the meaning is: But the Qur’an is a confirmation of what was before it of the books: meaning, they were given glad tidings of it before its revelation, so it came confirming it. It was also said that the meaning is: But it is a confirmation of the Prophet who was before the Qur’an, who is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they saw him before they heard the Qur’an from him. His statement, and the details of the Book is in apposition to His statement, but it is a confirmation of what was before it, so the nominative and accusative cases come in the two ways mentioned in confirmation. The comparative: clarification, meaning, it clarifies what is in the previous books of God, and the Book is for the genus. It was said that what is meant is what is explained in the Qur’an of rulings, so what is meant by the Book is the Qur’an. His saying: There is no doubt about it The pronoun refers back to the Qur’an, and it is included in the ruling of the correction as a third predicate. It is possible that this sentence is in the accusative case as a state of the Book, and it is possible that the sentence is a resumption with no position, and from the Lord of the Worlds is a fourth predicate: that is, being from the Lord of the Worlds. It is possible that it is a state of the Book, or from the pronoun of the Qur’an in His saying: There is no doubt about it that is, being from the Lord of the Worlds. It is possible that it is related to confirmation and detail, and the sentence There is no doubt about it is exposed.
10:38: His statement: 38- Or do they say he invented it? The question is to deny them while confirming the proof, and Am is the disconnected letter that means rather and the hamza: meaning, rather, do they say he invented it and fabricated it? Abu Ubaidah said: Am means and: meaning, and they say he invented it, and it was said that the mim is redundant, and the meaning is: Do they say he invented it, and the question is for rebuke and rebuke. Then God, the Exalted, commanded him to challenge them until their inability is revealed and their weakness is clear, so He said: Say, then bring a surah like it meaning, if the matter is as you claim, that Muhammad invented it, then bring, on the basis of fabrication, a surah like it in eloquence and quality of craftsmanship, for you are like him in knowledge of the Arabic language, eloquence of tongues and eloquence of speech. And call with your supporters and helpers whoever you are able to call upon and seek help from among the Arab tribes, and from your gods whom you make partners with God. His saying: other than God is related to call upon: that is, call upon someone other than God from among His creation if you are truthful in your claim that this Qur’an is fabricated. Glory be to God the Almighty, how strong, clear and evident this argument is to the minds! When they attributed the slander to one of them in humanity and Arabic, He said to them: This which you have attributed to me, and I am one of you, you have no choice but to produce a surah similar to one of His surahs, and seek help from whomever you wish from the people of this Arabic language despite their large number and the diversity of their dwellings, or from others from the sons of Adam, or from the jinn, or from the idols. If you do this after this and that, then you are truthful in what you have attributed to me and attached to me. But when they heard this fair speech and the extreme condescension, they did not come up with a word nor did they utter a single word. Rather, they refrained from answering and clung to the tails of cold stubbornness and obstinacy devoid of argument, and that is something that no falsifier is unable to do.
10:39: That is why the Almighty said after this great challenge 39- Rather, they denied that which they did not encompass in knowledge. So, ignore the first statement, and move on to explaining that they hastened to deny the Qur'an before they pondered it and understood its meanings and what it contained. This is what was done by those who were stubborn in their imitation and did not care about what was brought by those who called to the truth and held fast to the tails of fairness. Rather, they rejected it simply because it did not agree with their desires, nor did it come in accordance with their claim before they knew its meaning and understood its foundation, as you see it clearly and learn it by heart. The result is that whoever denied the clear proof and clear evidence before he encompassed its knowledge, he did not hold fast to anything in this denial except for being ignorant of what he denied and not knowing it. So, with this denial, he was calling out his own ignorance in the loudest voice, and recording his inability to comprehend the proofs in the most eloquent recording. There is nothing against the proof or against the one who brought it in his denial: What the ignorant person can do to his enemies is what the ignorant person can do to himself. His statement: And its interpretation has not yet come to them is conjoined with they have not encompassed its knowledge, meaning, rather, they denied what they have not encompassed its knowledge and what its interpretation has not come to them. Or this sentence is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, they denied it while they did not understand the interpretation of what they denied nor did their minds reach it. Meaning: That their denial occurred before they had encompassed its knowledge, and before they knew what it would lead to in terms of the truth of what it contained of the narration of the past report of the previous messengers and the previous nations, and of the narrations of what would happen of the future matters that he had informed about before they happened, or before they understood it with true understanding and their minds could comprehend it, for if they had contemplated it completely, they would have understood it as they should have, and they would have known what it contained of matters that most eloquently indicate that it is the word of God. Based on this, the meaning of its interpretation is what it would lead to for those who contemplate it of the graceful meanings and elegant subtleties, and the word of expectation is more apparent in the first meaning. Thus did those before them deny, meaning like that denial, the denial of those before them from the nations when the messengers came to them with the proofs and evidence of God, for they denied it before they had encompassed its knowledge, and before its interpretation came to them. Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers, from the previous nations of the evil end of the sinking and transformation and similar punishments that befell them as the Qur’an narrated. About them, and it was included in the books of God revealed to them.
10:40: His statement: 40- And among them is he who believes in it meaning, among those who denied the Qur'an is he who believes in it in himself and knows that it is true and right, but he denied it out of stubbornness and obstinacy. It was said that what is meant is: And among them is he who believes in it in the future even if he denied it at the present time. The relative pronoun is the subject, and its predicate is among them is he who does not believe in it and does not believe it in himself, but rather denied it out of ignorance as was previously explained, or does not believe in it in the future, but rather remains in his denial and insistence. It was said that the pronoun in both places refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that this division is specific to the people of Mecca, and it was said that it is general for all the disbelievers. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters so He will punish them for their deeds, and what is meant by them is: the stubborn and persistent ones, or both groups, and they are those who believe in it in themselves and deny it outwardly, and those who deny it out of ignorance, or those who believe in it in the future, and those who do not believe in it.
10:41: Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them if they persisted in denying Him and continued to do so: 41- For me is my work and for you is your work meaning, for me is the reward for my work and for you is the reward for your work, for I have conveyed to you what I was commanded to convey, and there is nothing else upon me. Then He confirmed this by saying: You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do meaning, you will not be held accountable for my work, and I will not be held accountable for your work. It has been said that this was abrogated by the verse of the sword, as a group of commentators have stated. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Thus has the word of your Lord come true, he said: The word of your Lord has preceded. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: It has spoken the truth. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Or is there one who guides not except that he is guided? he said: The idols. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: And if they deny you, then tell me my work, the verse, he said: He ordered him to do this then abrogated it and ordered him to fight them.
10:42: His statement: 42- And among them are those who listen etc. God the Almighty explained in this that among those disbelievers there are those whose state of aversion and enmity has reached this level, which is that they listen to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he recites the Qur'an and teaches the laws outwardly, but they do not listen in reality because the effect of listening does not occur, which is the occurrence of acceptance and action in what they hear. For this reason He said: Then can you make the deaf hear? meaning that even if these people listen outwardly, they are deaf, and deafness prevents them from hearing, so how can you hope for that from them when the obstacle exists, which is deafness? How then if it is added to that that they do not understand, for whoever is deaf and not rational does not understand anything and does not hear what is said to him. The pronoun in they listen is pluralized based on the meaning of from, and He made it singular in and among them is he who looks based on its wording. It was said that the joke is: the number of listeners is greater than the number of viewers, because listening does not depend on what viewing depends on, such as the fighter, the absence of an obstacle, the separation of the ray, and the light corresponding to the light of sight.
10:43: And the estimation in his saying: 43- And among them are those who listen "And among them are those who look and among them are people who listen, and among them are some who look, and the two hamzas in Do you listen Do you guide" are for denial and the fa in both places is for conjunction with an estimated as if it was said: Do they listen to you so you hear them? Do they look at you so you guide them? And the discussion of "And among them are those who look at you so can you guide the blind even if they do not see is like the discussion of And among them are those who listen" etc., because blindness is an obstacle so how can one hope for sight from its owner? And the loss of sight is joined to the loss of insight, because the blind person who has insight in his heart may have a correct intuition with which he understands in some cases an understanding that takes the place of sight, and likewise the deaf person who is intelligent may intuit an intuition that benefits him some benefit, unlike the one who has both blindness of sight and insight, for it is difficult for him to perceive. Likewise, whoever has both deafness and loss of reason has had the door of guidance closed to him. The answer to if in both places is omitted and what precedes them indicates them. The purpose of these words is to console the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because if a doctor sees a patient who does not accept treatment at all, he turns away from him and rests from being preoccupied with him.
10:44: His saying: 44- Indeed, God does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves. This was mentioned after what came before about not being guided by hearing and sight to show that this was not due to a deficiency in what God created for them of hearing, reason, sight and insight, but rather due to what became in their natures of fanaticism and stubbornness towards the truth, arguing with falsehood, and insisting on disbelief. They are the ones who wronged themselves by that, and God did not wrong them at all, but created them and made for them from the feelings what they perceive with the most complete perception, and installed in them from the senses what they reach with what they want, and provided for their worldly interests for them, and left them with their religious interests, so Baraqish reaps upon herself. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read but people with a lightened nun and raising people, and the rest read it with a heavy emphasis and placing people in the accusative. An-Nahhas said: A group of grammarians, including Al-Farra', claimed that when the Arabs say but with a waw, they stress the nun, and if they delete the waw, they lighten it. It was said: The point of placing the apparent in place of the implicit is to increase specificity and confirmation, and to present the object before the verb to indicate restriction, or simply for the sake of interest while taking into account the comma.
10:45: His saying: 45- And the Day We gather them The circumstance is in the accusative case with an implied pronoun: that is, remember the Day We gather them as if they had not remained that is, as if they had not remained, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state: that is, similar to the one who did not remain except for an hour of the day that is, a short time of it, and what is meant by remaining is remaining in this world, and it was said in the graves, they considered the long period of time insignificant either because they wasted their lives in this world, so they made its existence like nothingness, or they considered it short due to astonishment and confusion, or due to the length of their standing in the place of assembly, or due to the severity of the torment they are in, they forgot the pleasures of this world as if it had not existed, and similar to this is their saying: We remained a day or part of a day and the sentence they get to know each other is in the accusative case as a state, or it is a new sentence. Meaning: They will know each other as if they had only parted a little, when they emerge from the graves. Then the acquaintances between them will cease due to the amazing matters that are before them, which astound the minds and the understandings. It was said: This acquaintance is an acquaintance of rebuke and reprimand, some of them say to each other: You led me astray and led me astray, not an acquaintance of compassion and mercy, as God Almighty said: And no intimate friend will ask an intimate friend and His statement: So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask about one another so it is gathered that what is meant by acquaintance is an acquaintance of rebuke, and this is based on His statement: And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, referring to each other’s statement and He gathered the different verses in such a way and others by saying that the situations on the Day of Resurrection are different, as there may be in some situations what will not be in others Those who denied the meeting with God have certainly lost, and they were not guided this is a recording from God Almighty upon them of the loss, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state, and what is meant by meeting with God on the Day of Resurrection is at the reckoning and recompense, and He denied that they are of the same kind as the guided ones due to their ignorance and not seeking what would save them and benefit them.
10:46: His saying: 46- And if We show you some of what We promise them Its original form is if We show you and ma is added to emphasize the meaning of the condition, and the nun of emphasis was added, and the meaning is if We show you some of what We promised them of manifesting your religion in your lifetime by killing them and taking them captive, and the answer to the condition is omitted, and the estimate is then you see it, or that's it, and the phrase or We cause you to die is conjoined with what preceded it, and the meaning is: Or We do not show you that in your lifetime, but We cause you to die before that then to Us is their return so at that time We will punish them in the Hereafter and show you their punishment in it, and the answer to or We cause you to die is also omitted, and the estimate is: Or We cause you to die before the showing, then We show you that in the Hereafter, and it was said: The answer to or We cause you to die is His saying: then to Us is their return to indicate what is meant by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, showing them their punishment in the Hereafter, and it was said: The shift to the future tense in both places To evoke the image, the original is We showed you or We caused you to die. This is questionable, because his (peace and blessings of God be upon him) showing some of the punishment that God promised the polytheists had not yet occurred, such as death. The meaning of this verse is: If We do not take revenge on them soon, We will take revenge on them later. God, the Exalted, showed him their killing, their capture, their humiliation, the loss of their glory, and the breaking of their pride by what He inflicted on them on the Day of Badr and the subsequent battles. Praise be to God. His statement, Then God is Witness over what they do, came with then indicating distance, even though God, the Exalted, is Witness over what they do in both worlds, to indicate that what is meant by these actions is the punishment that results from them, or what is obtained from the speech of the limbs as testimony against them on the Day of Resurrection. So He made that equivalent to God’s testimony against them, as mentioned by Al-Naysaburi.
10:47: 47- And for every nation of the past nations at a certain time is a messenger whom God sends to them, and he explains to them what God has legislated for them of rulings according to what the interest requires. So when their messenger comes to them and conveys to them what God has sent him with and they all deny him, it will be judged between them that is, between the nation and its messenger with justice that is, fairness, so the messenger is saved and those who denied him are destroyed, as God Almighty said: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger and it is permissible for the pronoun in between them to mean the nation, assuming that some of them denied him and others believed him, so the deniers are destroyed and those who believe are saved and they will not be wronged in that judgment, so they will not be punished without sin, nor will they be held accountable without an argument. From this is God Almighty's saying: And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them and His saying: How then, when We bring from every nation a witness? What is meant by exaggeration in showing justice and fairness among the servants.
10:48: Then the Almighty mentioned another doubt of the doubts of the infidels, and that is that whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, threatened them with the descent of punishment, they would 48- say, ‘When will this promise be?’ The question from them is for denial and exclusion and to cast aspersions on the prophethood if you are truthful, addressing them to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers, and the answer to the condition is omitted and is indicated by what preceded it, and it is possible that what is meant by those who say this statement is all the nations who did not submit to their messengers whom God sent to them.
10:49: Then God Almighty commanded His Messenger to answer them with what would settle the matter of doubt and put an end to the obstinacy, so He said: 49- Say, ‘I do not possess for myself any harm or benefit.’ That is, I am not able to bring any benefit to myself or ward off any harm from myself, so how can I possess that for someone else? He mentioned harm first because the context is to show the inability to attend the promise that they hastened and excluded, and the exception in His saying: except what God wills is disconnected as the imams of interpretation have mentioned: That is, but what God wills of that happened, so how can I possess any harm or benefit for myself. This is the greatest sermon and the most eloquent warning for those whose habit and habit has become to call upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and seek his help when calamities befall them that no one but God Almighty can avert. Likewise, for those who ask the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, for that which no one but God Almighty can obtain, for this is the station of the Lord of the Worlds who created the prophets and the righteous and all of creation and provided for them and gave them life and caused them to die. So how can one ask a prophet from the prophets or an angel from the angels or a righteous person from the righteous for that which he is incapable of and unable to do, and leave the request to the Lord of Lords who is capable of everything, the Creator, the Provider, the Giver, the Withholder? This verse is enough as a lesson for you, for this is the master of the children of Adam and the Seal of the Messengers, whom God commands to say to His servants: I do not possess for myself any harm or benefit, so how can He possess it for others, and how can someone whose rank is lower than his rank and status does not reach his status for himself, let alone possess it for others? How strange is it that people devote themselves to the graves of the dead who have become under layers of earth, and ask them for needs that only God, the Almighty, is able to fulfill? How can they not be aware of the polytheism they have fallen into, and not be aware of what has happened to them in terms of contradiction to the meaning of There is no god but God and the significance of Say, He is God, the One? What is more amazing than this is that the people of knowledge are aware of what these people are doing and do not denounce them or prevent them from returning to the first ignorance, but rather to what is worse than it, for those people acknowledge that God Almighty is the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of Life, the Giver of Death, the Harmful and the Beneficial, but they only make their idols intercessors for them with God and bring them closer to Him, while these people give them the ability to harm and benefit, and sometimes call them to be independent, and sometimes with the Majestic, and God is sufficient for you from the evil of hearing it, and God is the supporter of His religion and the purifier of His law from the filth of polytheism and the defilements of disbelief. Satan, may God disgrace him, has resorted to this pretext to what pleases his eye and cools his heart from the disbelief of many of this blessed nation, while they think that they are doing well. “Indeed we belong to God and to Him we shall return.” Then the Almighty made clear that every group has a limited limit that they will not exceed, so there is no reason to hasten the punishment, saying: For every nation is a term. So when that time comes, He will fulfill His promise and reward each one according to what he deserves. The meaning is that every nation between whom and their Messenger, or between each other, has a specific term and a specific time in which what God Almighty wants for them will happen to them when it comes. When their term comes, that is, that specific time, and the pronoun refers to every nation, they will not delay from that specific term an hour, that is, a short time, nor will they advance it. The phrase they will not advance is conjoined with the phrase they will not delay. Similar to it is the Almighty’s saying: No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it. The discussion of this verse mentioned here has already been presented in the interpretation of the verse at the beginning of Al-A’raf, so we will not repeat it. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: They recognize one another, he said: A man recognizes his companion next to him, but he cannot speak to him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And if We show you the verse, he said: the evil of the torment in your life, or We cause you to die before to Us is their return. And regarding his statement: And for every nation is a messenger, so when their messenger comes, he said: the Day of Resurrection.
10:50: His statement: 50- "Say: Have you considered, if His punishment comes to you?" This is from Him, the Most High, a falsification of the opinion of the disbelievers in hastening the punishment after the first falsification: that is, tell me, if the punishment of God comes to you at night, that is, the time of night, and what is meant by it is the time in which they spend the night and sleep and neglect to be cautious, and night in the sense of spending the night is a verbal noun like peace in the sense of submission, and it is accusative in the circumstance, and likewise during the day: that is, the time of being busy seeking a livelihood and earning, and the pronoun in it refers to the punishment, and it was said: it refers to God, and the question in what are the criminals hastening from is for denial that includes prohibition as in His statement: The command of God has come, so do not hasten it and the reason for denouncing them in their hastening is that the punishment is abhorrent and hearts are repelled by it and natures reject it, so what is the reason for their hastening it? The sentence beginning with the question is the answer to the condition by deleting the fa. It was said that the answer is omitted, and the meaning is: Regret your haste, or recognize your mistake in it. It was said that the answer is his statement: A sin when it occurs. The sentence What are the criminals hastening from it? is an objection, and the meaning is: If His punishment comes to you, you will believe in it after it occurs when faith will not benefit you. The first is more appropriate. He said that the criminals are hastening from it and did not say that they are hastening from it to indicate what necessitates abandoning haste, which is the crime, because it is the right of the criminal to fear the punishment because of his crime, so how can he hasten it? Just as it is said to someone who finds something unpleasant when he asks for it: What are you bringing upon yourself? Al-Nahhas narrated from Al-Zajjaj that if the pronoun in from it refers to the punishment, then you have two interpretations in what: One of them is that what is in the nominative case as a subject, and that means which, which is the predicate of what, and the pronoun is omitted. Another interpretation: that what is a single noun in the nominative case as the subject, and the predicate is what comes after it. If the pronoun in from it is made to refer back to God Almighty, then what is a single thing in the accusative case as is hastening, and the meaning is: what thing are the criminals hastening from: that is, from God Almighty.
10:51: And the interrogative hamza in 51- Ath-thumma ma ma-ha-tham-tum-bih is used on thumma as it is used on waw and fa, and it is to deny their faith when faith is of no benefit, and that is after the punishment descends, and it includes the meaning of terrifying them and the horror of what they did at the wrong time while they left it at the right time when benefit and protection are obtained, and this sentence is included under the commanded statement, and the word thumma was used for delay indicating the exclusion, and idha was used with the addition of ma for emphasis indicating the realization of the occurrence of faith from them at the wrong time so that in that there is an increase in their ignorance. The meaning is: The most distant thing from the punishment of God to befall you, and His wrath and vengeance to descend upon you, is that you believed when this faith does not benefit you at all, nor does it protect you from harm, and it was said: This sentence is not included under the commanded statement, and that it is from the words of the angels mocking them and belittling them. The first is more appropriate. It was said: Then here is with the opening of the thaa so it is circumstantial with the meaning of there. The first is more appropriate. His statement: Now, while you were hastening it, it was said: It is a resumption with the estimation of the statement not included under the statement that God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them: that is, it was said to them when they believed after the punishment occurred: Now you have believed in it, while you were hastening it: that is, the punishment, as a denial from you and a mockery, because their hastening was in the form of a denial and a mockery, and the purpose of his command, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say this statement to them is to rebuke them, mock them, and belittle them. The phrase and you were hastening it is in the accusative case as a state, and now was read by deleting the hamza after the lam and placing its vowel on the lam.
10:52: His saying: 52- Then it will be said to those who did wrong, 'Taste the punishment of eternity' is connected to the implied verb, it was said: now, and what is meant by it is: rebuke and reprimand for them: that is, it was said to those who wronged themselves by disbelief and lack of faith: that what you are seeking is pure harm, devoid of benefit in every way, and a wise person does not seek that. And it is said to them by way of humiliation: Taste the punishment of eternity: that is, the everlasting punishment that does not cease, and the one who said to them this statement and the one before it was said: they are the angels who are the guardians of Hell, and it is not far-fetched that the one who said that was the prophets in particular, or the believers in general Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn in life of disbelief and sins, and the question is for confirmation, and it is as if this statement was said to them about their cry for help from the punishment and the arrival of the vengeance.
10:53: Then God the Almighty narrated about them after these comprehensive statements and the answers to their false statements: that they asked you another time about the realization of the punishment, so He said: 53- And they ask you whether it is true meaning they ask you about the direction of their mockery and denial that is more true than what you threaten us with of punishment in the immediate and the future, and this question from them is pure ignorance, and darknesses one above the other, as it was mentioned about them with the answer to it, so their action in this repetition is the action of one who does not understand what he says or what is said to him, and it was said: What is meant by this inquiry from them is about the truth of the Qur’an, and the elevation of truth as a predicate that is presented, and the subject is the pronoun that comes after it, and the presentation of the predicate is for emphasis, or it is a subject, and the pronoun is raised by it and it takes the place of the predicate, and the sentence is in the accusative case with they ask you, and it was read as the truth is it, because the lam is for the genus, so it is as if it was said: Is it the truth and not falsehood. His saying: “Say: Yes, by my Lord, it is the truth.” God, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say this statement to them in response to their question that was intended to mock: that is, say to them, O Muhammad, without paying attention to what they intended of mockery: Yes, by my Lord, it is the truth. That is, yes, by my Lord, what He promised you of punishment is the truth, established and will inevitably happen. This answer is confirmed in several ways: First: the oath with the entry of the letter specific to the oath in the place of yes, second: the entry of the emphatic in, third: the lam in the truth, fourth: the nominal nature of the sentence, and this indicates that they had reached the limit in their denial and rebellion, beyond which there is no limit, then He threatened them with the most severe threat, and terrified them with the greatest terror, so He said: And you will not escape, that is, you will not escape the punishment by fleeing and by trickery that does not benefit, and by stubbornness that does not ward off anything from God’s decree. This sentence is either conjoined with the sentence in response to the oath, or it is a new sentence to show that they are not free from God’s punishment in any way.
10:54: Then he increased the emphasis, saying: 54- And if every soul that has wronged itself had all that is in the earth, it would ransom itself with it. That is, if every soul that has wronged itself by disbelieving in God and not believing in Him had all that is in the earth of everything that it contains of precious wealth and superior treasures, it would ransom itself with it: that is, it would make it a ransom for itself from the punishment. Similar to this is the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - never will the earth full of gold be accepted from one of them, even if he were to ransom himself with it. And this has been mentioned previously. His statement: And they concealed regret when they saw the punishment. The pronoun refers to the disbelievers with whom the context of the speech is directed, and it was said: it refers to the souls indicated by every soul. The meaning of concealed is hid: that is, they did not show remorse, but rather concealed it because of what they had witnessed in that place, which had robbed their minds and taken away their patience. It is possible that while they were in that state, there remained in them a vein that inclined them to the fanaticism that they had in this world, so they concealed their remorse so that the believers would not gloat over them. It was said that the leaders concealed it among themselves without their followers, fearing their rebuke of them because they were the ones who led them astray and prevented them from Islam. This happened when they saw the punishment. As for after entering it, they were the ones who said, ‘Our Lord, our misery has overcome us.’ It was said that the meaning of concealed is shown. It was said that they found the pain of regret in their hearts, because remorse cannot be shown. This is the saying of Kathir: So I felt remorse when the caller called for the cold beauty of the city of Adra Al-Mubarrad mentioned two aspects of this: The first: that the signs of regret appeared on their faces, which is brokenness, the singular of which is sirar, and the plural of which is asarir, and the second: what was mentioned previously, and it was said that the meaning of they concealed the regret is that they made it sincere, because concealing it is making it sincere, and when in his saying: when they saw the punishment is an adverb meaning when, accusative with they concealed, or a conditional particle whose answer is omitted because what preceded it indicates it, and it was judged between them with justice, meaning God judged between the believers and the disbelievers, or between the leaders and the followers, or between the oppressors among the disbelievers and the oppressed, and it was said: the meaning of the judgement between them: inflicting punishment upon them, and justice is fairness, and the phrase and they are not wronged is in the accusative case as a state: meaning God will not wrong them in what He did to them of the punishment that befell them, for it is because of what they earned.
10:55: And the sentence 55 - Indeed, to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth is intended to establish the perfection of His power, because He who owns whatever is in the heavens and the earth disposes of it as He wishes, and He has overcome the irrational because they are the majority of creation. It was said: When the Almighty mentioned the ransom of the infidels with what is on the earth if they had that, He made clear that all things belong to God, and they have nothing with which they can ransom themselves. It was said: When He swore by the truth of what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought, He wanted to accompany that with clear proof that everything in the world, with its different types, belongs to Him and He disposes of it as He wishes. In beginning the sentence with the letter of warning, there is a warning to the heedless and an awakening to the absent-minded. Then He confirmed what came before by saying: Indeed, the promise of God is true, meaning it will inevitably happen. It is general and includes what they hastened of punishment in a primary way. And beginning the sentence with the letter of warning, as we said in the one before it, with the indication of the realization of the content of the two sentences, But most of the people, meaning the infidels, do not know, what is good for them so they act upon it, and what is bad for them so they avoid it.
10:56: 56- He gives life and causes death He gives life and takes it away and to Him you will be returned in the Hereafter. He rewards each person according to what he deserves, and He bestows favors upon whomever He wills of His servants.
10:57: His saying: 57- O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord meaning that the Qur'an contains what is admonished by whoever reads it and knows its meaning. Admonition in origin is: reminding of consequences, whether by encouragement or intimidation, and the preacher is like a doctor who forbids the patient from what harms him, and the from your Lord in from your Lord is related to the verb, which is came to you, so it is introductory, or related to something omitted, so it is partial and a cure for what is in the breasts of doubts that befall some of the doubters because of the existence of what is benefited from it of true beliefs, and its inclusion of the falsification of false beliefs, and guidance: guidance for whoever follows the Qur'an and thinks about it and contemplates its meanings to the path that leads to Paradise, and mercy: is what is found in the Noble Book of matters by which God shows mercy to His servants, so whoever wants that seeks it until he attains it, so the Noble Qur'an includes these matters.
10:58: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered and made the address to him after his address to the people in general, so he said: 58- "Say: By the grace of God and by His mercy, so in that let them rejoice." What is meant by the grace of God, the Most High, is His favor upon His servants in the hereafter and the hereafter in a manner that cannot be encompassed by limitation, and mercy: His mercy to them. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The grace of God is the Qur'an, and His mercy is Islam. It was narrated from Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid, and Qatadah that the grace of God is faith, and His mercy is the Qur'an. The first: to carry the grace and mercy in general, and what is in the Qur'an of them is included in that primarily, and the original statement is: Say: By the grace of God and by His mercy, so let them rejoice, then this verb was deleted because the second is indicated in His statement: So in that let them rejoice on it. It was said: The fa in this deleted verb is included in the answer to an implied condition as if it was said: If they rejoice in something, then let them specify the grace and mercy of God with the rejoicing. The repetition of the letter ba in bi-rahmathu indicates that each of the bounty and mercy is an independent cause of joy. Joy is the pleasure in the heart due to realizing what is desired. God, the Exalted, has condemned joy in several instances, such as His statement: “Do not rejoice. Indeed, God does not love those who rejoice.” He has permitted it in His statement: Rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty, and as in this verse. It is also possible for the letter ba in bi-rahmathu to be related to His statement: It has come to you, and the meaning is: A sermon has come to you with the bounty of God and His mercy, so with that: meaning, with its coming, let them rejoice. Yazid ibn al-Qa’qa’ and Ya’qub read fa-l-fa-r-hu with the superscript, while the majority read it with the subscript. The pronoun in huwa khayr refers to what is mentioned of the bounty and mercy, or to the coming in the second way, or to the demonstrative pronoun in His statement: fa-l-dhalik and the meaning is: This is better for them than what they collect of the debris of this world. It has been read with the superscript ta in ya-jma’un in accordance with the reading with it in wa-la-tafrahu. It has been decided in Arabic that the imperative lam is deleted with addressing, except in a few languages where this reading came, and the majority read with the lower thaa’ in yajma’un as they read in falayfrahu. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Amir that he read with the upper thaa’ in yajma’un and the lower thaa’ in falayfrahu. Al-Tabarani and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas who said: A man came to Abdullah bin Masoud and said: My brother is complaining of stomach pain, so he prescribed wine for him. He said: Glory be to God! God has not placed a cure in any impurity. Rather, the cure is in the Qur’an and honey. They are a cure for what is in the chests and a cure for people. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: God made the Qur’an a cure for what is in the chests, but He did not make it a cure for your diseases. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: I am complaining of my chest. He said: Recite the Qur’an, God says: It is a cure for what is in the chests. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu’ab Al-Iman on the authority of Wathilah bin Al-Asqa’ that a man complained to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about a sore throat. He said: You should recite the Qur’an and honey, for the Qur’an is a cure for what is in the chests, and honey is a cure for every disease. Abu Dawud, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) taught me the recitation with the letter ta’, meaning the upper ta’. Something similar to this has been narrated through other chains of transmission. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Say: ‘By the grace of God and by His mercy,’” He said: By the grace of God the Qur’an, and by His mercy that He made you among its people. At-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat on the authority of Al-Bara’ something similar to his statement. Sa’id bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri. Sa’id bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: By the Book of God and by Islam. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority: His grace is Islam, and his mercy is the Qur’an. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi also narrated on his authority: By the grace of God the Qur’an, and by His mercy that He made them among its people. Similar narrations have been narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it is better than what they collect of money, crops, and livestock.
10:59: God Almighty indicated in His saying: 59- "Say: Have you considered what God has sent down" etc. to another way other than what was mentioned above in proving prophethood, and the report of that is that you rule by permitting some and forbidding others, if it is merely out of desire and whim then it is abandoned by the agreement of rational people, Muslims and non-Muslims, and if it is because of your belief that it is God's rule regarding you and in what He has provided for you then you do not know that except by a way that leads to God, and there is no way by which the lawful is distinguished from the unlawful except through the messengers whom God sent to His servants, and the meaning of have you considered: inform me and what is in the accusative case of have you considered which includes the meaning of inform me. It was said: What is in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is Has God permitted you? and say in His statement: Say Has God permitted you? is a repetition for emphasis and the link is omitted, and the subject and predicate are in the accusative case as you have seen, and the meaning is: Tell me what God has sent down to you of sustenance and you have made some of it forbidden and some of it permissible, has God permitted you to make it permissible and forbidden or do you invent lies about God? And in both ways, so from it is forbidden for partiality, and the estimate is: so you have made some of it forbidden and made some of it permissible, and that is as they used to do with livestock according to what was previously narrated about them in the Noble Book, and the meaning of sending down sustenance is that the rain descends from above, and likewise the matter is decided in the sustenance of the servants in the sky according to what has been established in the Preserved Tablet from His mention, glory be to Him, of everything in it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Zajjaj that what is in the accusative case is an-Nazal, and an-Nazal means created, as he said: And We sent down for you eight pairs of livestock and And We sent down iron, wherein is great force. According to this statement and the first statement, his statement: “Say: Has God given you permission?” is a new sentence. It was said: It is permissible for the hamza in Has God given you permission? to be for denial, and the am is disconnected meaning: Rather, do you fabricate against God? The manifestation of the noble name and its presentation before the verb is to indicate the complete fabrication. In this noble verse there is what will deafen the ears of those who issue fatwas to the servants of God regarding His law, regarding what is permissible and what is forbidden, permissible and what is not, even though they are imitators who do not understand the proofs of God, nor do they understand them nor know what they are, and the extent of their knowledge is the narration of the words of a speaker from this nation whom they imitated in their religion, and they made him an independent legislator. Whatever he acted upon from the Book and the Sunnah is what is acted upon by them, and whatever he did not reach or reached but did not understand it properly, or he understood it and erred in his ijtihad and preference, then it is considered abrogated according to them and its ruling is lifted from the servants, even though the one they imitated worships this law as they worship it and is ruled by its rulings as they are ruled by it, and he exerted his opinion and did what was required of him, and he won two rewards with the right and one reward with the wrong, but the matter is in their making his opinion in which he erred an independent law and an evidence to be acted upon, and they made a clear mistake in this. They made a grave mistake, because the permission granted to the mujtahid to use his own opinion is for him alone, and no one among the people of Islam whose words are respected says that it is permissible for others to act upon it by imitating and following his example. What the imitators have brought in order to establish this falsehood is from idle ignorance. O God, just as You have provided us with knowledge by which we can distinguish between truth and falsehood, provide us with fairness by which we can attain what is true with You, O Giver of goodness.
10:60: Then he said: 60- "And what do those who invent lies about God think about the Day of Resurrection?" That is, what do they think about this Day, and what will be done to them on it? This interrogative sentence that includes the greatness of the threat to them is not included in the statement that God ordered His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them, but rather it is a beginning that is brought to explain what will befall them of God's punishment, and the Day of Resurrection is accusative by the assumption, and the lie is mentioned after the invention, although the invention can only be a lie for greater emphasis. And Isa bin Omar read and what he thought as a verb "Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind He bestows upon them various kinds of blessings in this world and the hereafter but most of them do not thank God for His blessings that reach them from Him, glory be to Him, at all times, and a funny story.
10:61: His saying: 61- And what you are doing is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ma is a negative particle. The matter means the matter in the sense of intention, and its root is the hamza, and its plural is shu'un. Al-Akhfash said: The Arabs say: Ma shana shahu meaning what you did "and what you recite from it of the Qur'an". Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: The pronoun in "from it" refers to the matter, and the preposition and noun are an attribute of a deleted source: meaning a recitation that occurred from him, since the recitation of the Qur'an is one of the greatest matters of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the meaning is: that he recites for the sake of the matter that the Qur'an occurred in order to know how it is ruled, or he recites the Qur'an that was revealed in that matter. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: The pronoun in minhu refers to the Book: that is, what is from the Book of God from the Qur’an, and he repeated it to magnify it like his saying: Indeed, I am God. The address in and you do not do any work is to the Messenger of God and the nation, and it was said that the address was to the infidels of Quraysh except that We are witnesses over you an exception emptied of the most general conditions for those addressed: that is, witnesses over you with His work from you, and the pronoun in fih from his saying: you are pouring into it refers to the work, it is said: so-and-so poured into the talk and the work: if he rushed into it. Ad-Dahhak said: The pronoun in fih refers to the Qur’an, and the meaning is: when you spread lies in the Qur’an. His saying: And not an atom’s weight is hidden from your Lord on earth or in heaven. Al-Kisa’i read ya’zib with a kasra on the zay, and the rest read it with a damma, and they are two eloquent languages, and the meaning of ya’zib is: disappears, and it was said: is distant. Ibn Kaysan said: It goes, and these meanings are close, and the min in min mithqal is redundant for emphasis: that is, and nothing is hidden from your Lord, the weight of an atom: that is, a red ant. And He used the earth and the sky as an expression, although nothing is hidden from Him, glory be to Him, neither in them nor in what is outside of them, because people do not see anything other than them and what is in them of creation. And He mentioned the earth before the sky because it is the place of stability of the world, so they see what is in it of proximity. And the waw in nor smaller than that nor larger is for conjunction with the word mithqal, and they are in the accusative case because they are impossible, and it is possible that the conjunction is with atom, and it was said: Their in the accusative case is with la which negates the genus, and the waw is for resumption, and min is related to what is hidden, and the predicate of la is except in a book, and the meaning is: and there is nothing smaller than the weight of an atom nor larger than it except that it is in a clear book, so how can it be hidden from Him? Yaqub and Hamzah read with the nominative case of asghar and akbar, and the reason for that is that it is conjoined with the place of mithqal, and its place is the nominative case. A problem has been brought up regarding the explanation of the accusative and nominative cases in conjunction with the word mithqal and its place, or with the word atom, which is that the interpretation of the verse becomes: Nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven except in a book, and it necessitates that that thing which is in the book be outside the knowledge of God, which is impossible. The response to this problem has been made by saying that created things are of two types: a type that God brought into existence from the beginning without an intermediary, such as the creation of the angels, the heavens, and the earth, and another type that He brought into existence through the first type of the events of the world of creation and corruption. There is no doubt that this second type is far from the level of the first type in the chain of causality, so what is meant by the verse is that nothing is far from the level of His existence, glory be to Him, on earth or in heaven except that it is in a clear book in which He established the image of that information, and the purpose is to respond to those who claim that He is not knowledgeable of the particulars. It has also been made clear that the exception is disjunctive: that is, but it is in a clear book. Abu Ali al-Jurjani mentioned that illa has the meaning of waw, and that the speech was completed when he said: nor greater then the beginning occurred with his saying: except in a clear book meaning it is also in a clear book. The Arabs may put illa in place of waw, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: Indeed, no messengers fear in My presence * Except for he who wrongs meaning and he who wrongs, and his saying: So that mankind will have no argument against you except for those who do wrong meaning and those who do wrong, and it was estimated that it is after waw that came illa with its meaning as in his saying: And say, ‘Forgive me’ meaning it is a forgiveness, and similarly And do not say three “And not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And no grain is there in the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry thing but is in a clear book.” Al-Zajjaj said: The nominative is for the beginning in the reading of those who read in the nominative, and its predicate is except in a book and the author of al-Kashshaf chose it, and he chose in the accusative reading that the majority read it that they are accusative with la to negate the genus, and the conjunction was problematic in a manner similar to what we have presented.
10:62: Then when He, the Almighty, explained His encompassing of all things, and that this strengthened the hearts of the obedient and broke the hearts of the disobedient, He mentioned the state of the obedient, saying: 62- Unquestionably, for the allies of God there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. The word friend in the language means: the close one. What is meant by the allies of God are the sincere believers, as if they have drawn close to God, the Almighty, through their obedience to Him and avoidance of disobedience to Him.
10:63: And the Almighty has explained these guardians by saying: 63- Those who believed and were fearing God meaning they believe in what must be believed in, and fear what they must fear from the sins of God, the Almighty. What is meant by denying fear from them is that they never fear as others fear, because they have done what God has obligated upon them, and have stopped the sins that He has forbidden them from, so they are confident in themselves and have good thoughts about their Lord. Likewise, they do not grieve over missing out on a request, because they know that it is by the decree and destiny of God, so they submit to the decree and destiny, and they relieve their hearts of worry and sorrow, so their chests are open, their limbs are active, and their hearts are happy. The location of the relative pronoun is the accusative as a substitute for guardians, or the nominative as a predicate for a deleted subject, or it is a subject and its predicate is good report for them, so it is not connected to what precedes it, or the accusative is also for praise or because it is Description of the guardians.
10:64: His statement: 64- For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter is an explanation of the meaning of them being the friends of God: that is, for them is good tidings from God as long as they are alive, through what He inspires to His prophets and reveals in His books, that the state of the believers with Him is their entry into Paradise and His pleasure with them, as many good tidings have occurred for the believers in the Noble Qur’an, as well as what they get from righteous visions, and what God bestows upon them from answering their prayers, and what they witness of good tidings for them when their appointed times are approached by the angels descending upon them saying to them: Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive good tidings of Paradise. As for good tidings in the Hereafter, the angels meet them, giving them good tidings of winning bliss and safety from punishment. The good report is a source intended to refer to the one who is given good report, and the two adverbs are in the accusative case as a state: that is, the state of their being in this world and the state of their being in the Hereafter. The meaning of there is no change in the words of God is no change in His sayings in general, so what He promised to His righteous servants is included in it primarily. The reference in His saying that to what was mentioned before it of them being given good report of the two good tidings in the two abodes is the great attainment whose value cannot be measured and nothing else is comparable to it. The two sentences: I mean there is no change in the words of God and that is the great attainment are an interjection at the end of the speech according to those who allow it, and their benefit is to confirm the one who is given good report and magnify its importance, or the first is an interjection and the second is a conclusion. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Say, ‘Have you seen what God has sent down for you of provision?’ He said: They are the polytheists who used to make lawful whatever they wished of livestock and crops and forbid whatever they wished. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, When you are spending therein, He said: When you do. Al-Faryabi and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement, And nothing is hidden from your Lord, He said: Not even the weight of an atom is hidden from Him, nor is it smaller than that or greater, but is in a clear book, He said: It is the book that is with God. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement, Unquestionably, the allies of God, It was said: Who are they, O Lord? He said: They are those who believed and were fearing God. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr who said: They are those who, when they are seen, God is remembered. At-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ad-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with both chains of transmission traceable to the Prophet and others, who said: They are those who, when they are seen, God is remembered because of their sight. Ibn Al-Mubarak, Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi in Nawadir Al-Usul, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Al-Mubarak, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair with both chains of transmission traceable to the Prophet and others. Ahmad, Al-Hakim and At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Amr bin Al-Jamuh that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “A servant does not attain the true meaning of true faith until he loves for the sake of God and hates for the sake of God. If he loves for the sake of God and hates for the sake of God, then he has earned loyalty from God. My friends and beloved ones among My creation are those who are remembered by My remembrance and I am remembered by their remembrance.” Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanem that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best of God’s servants are those who, when they are seen, remind them of God. The worst of His servants are those who go about spreading gossip, separate loved ones, and seek to harm the innocent.” Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Aas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best of you are those whose sight reminds you of God, whose speech increases your knowledge, and whose actions make you desire the Hereafter. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, and the prophets and martyrs will envy them on the Day of Resurrection because of their closeness and their sitting with them. Then a Bedouin knelt down and said: O Messenger of God, describe them to us and make them lawful for us? He said: A people from the lowest ranks of mankind, from the disputes of the tribes, who lined up in line for the sake of God and loved one another for the sake of God. On the Day of Resurrection, God will place for them pulpits of light and seat them. People will fear, but they will not fear. They are the friends of God, who have no fear and will not grieve.” Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilya, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu`ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Kathir said: Its chain of transmission is good. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ash'ari, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to this. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God: 'Indeed, the allies of God' the verse, and he said: 'Those who love one another for the sake of God.'" Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to this. There are hadiths that have been narrated about the virtue of those who love one another for the sake of God, but they do not mention that they are the ones meant by the verse. Sa'id bin Mansur, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu'ab Al-Iman on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, "On the authority of a man from Egypt, who said: I asked Abu Al-Darda' about the meaning of His statement: 'For them is good tidings in the life of this world.' He said: 'No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.' He said: 'No one has asked me about it except you since the revelation was sent down to me: It is a righteous dream that a Muslim sees, or is seen for him, and it is good tidings for him in this life, and good tidings for him in the Hereafter are Paradise.'" And in its chain of transmission is this unknown man.
