Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, al-Darimi, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the statement: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world.’ He said: ‘It is a righteous vision that a believer sees or is seen for him.’” Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement: ‘For them is good tidings in the life of this world.’ He said: ‘A righteous vision that a believer is given good tidings of is one of forty-six parts of prophecy, so whoever sees that should tell about it.’” The hadith. Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the verse: In this world, it is a righteous vision that a righteous servant sees or is seen for him, and in the Hereafter, Paradise. Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Mandah narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, interpreted glad tidings in this worldly life as a beloved vision, and in the Hereafter as the glad tidings of the believer at death: God has forgiven you and the one who carried you to your grave. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority a hadith similar to that of Jabir. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud a hadith similar to that of Jabir. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas a similar hadith. There are authentic hadiths that indicate that a good vision is one of the glad tidings and that it is a part of prophethood, but they were not restricted to explaining this verse. It has been narrated that what is meant by glad tidings in the verse is His statement: And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from God great bounty. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority on the authority of Muqsim that it is His statement: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast. Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Nafi’ who said: Al-Hajjaj delivered a sermon and said: Ibn Al-Zubayr has changed the Book of God. Ibn Umar said: You and Ibn Al-Zubayr cannot do that. The words of God cannot be changed.
10:65: His saying: 65- "And let not their statement grieve you" is a prohibition to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from being saddened by the words of the infidels, which include slandering him, belying him, and casting aspersions on his religion. The intention is to console him and give him good tidings. Then the Almighty resumed speaking to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, explaining what he mentioned of the prohibition to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: "Indeed, all honor belongs to God" meaning that victory and subjugation belong to Him in His kingdom and authority, not to any of His servants. And if all of that belongs to Him, then how can they have power over you so that you are saddened by their false words when they do not possess any of the power? And it was read "grieves you from made him sad". It was read that glory is with the opening of the hamza, meaning because glory belongs to God. What is in this verse about making all glory to God Almighty does not contradict His Almighty saying: And to God belongs glory and to His Messenger and to the believers, because all glory is to God, it is all to God. From this is His saying: God has decreed, ‘I will surely prevail, I and My messengers,’ “Indeed, We will support Our messengers.”
10:66: 66- Indeed, to God belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth." Among them are these polytheists who were contemporary with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If they were in his kingdom and he disposed of them as he wished, then how could they harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a way that God did not permit, and the rational people prevailed over others because they were more noble. In the verse, there is a reproach to the servants of humans, angels and inanimate objects, because they worshipped the slave and abandoned the owner, and that is contrary to what reason requires, and for this reason he followed it with his saying: And those who invoke besides God do not follow partners. The meaning is that even if they called their deities partners to God, they are not partners to Him in reality, because that is impossible. If there were within them gods other than God, they both would have been ruined. “What is in and what follows” is a negative and partners is the object of follows, and based on this, the object of they invoke is omitted. The original is and those who invoke besides God do not follow partners, partners in reality: they are only names without names, so one of them was omitted because the mentioned indicates it. It is permissible for the mentioned to be the object of they invoke, and the object of follows was omitted because the mentioned indicates it. It is permissible for it to be an interrogative meaning what thing follows those who invoke besides God partners, and in this way partners is the object of they invoke, and the speech is outside the context of rebuking them and disparaging them. It is possible that ma is a relative pronoun conjoined with man fi al-samawan whoever is in the heavens: that is, to God belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and what those who call upon other than God follow are partners. The meaning is that God is the owner of their deities because they are among those in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. Then the Almighty increased the emphasis on the response to them and the refutation of their statements, saying: They follow nothing but conjecture, that is, they do not follow certainty, they only follow conjecture, and conjecture is of no avail against the truth. They only guess, that is, they estimate that they are partners with a false estimate and pure lie. This verse was mentioned earlier in Al-An’am.
10:67: Then the Almighty mentioned some of the effects of His power, along with gratitude to His servants for some of His blessings. He said: 67- It is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day giving sight. That is, He made time for His servants divided into two parts: One of them is dark, which is the night, so that the servants may rest in it from movement and fatigue and rest themselves from toil and earning. The other is seeing, so that they may strive in it for what benefits them and provides for their livelihood, and obtain what they need in a bright, luminous time, in which neither great nor small things are hidden from them. The Almighty’s making the day giving sight is a metaphor. The meaning is: that it is a sight for its owner, as they say: he fasts during the day. The reference in His saying: Indeed in that is to the mentioned making are signs many wondrous for a people who listen meaning they listen to what is recited to them of the verses of revelation that alert to the verses of creation, which God Almighty mentioned here and other than them which He did not mention. So when they hear that, they reflect and consider, and that is one of the greatest reasons for faith.
10:68: His statement: 68- "They said, 'God has taken a son. Glory be to Him! He is the Rich.'" This is another type of the falsehoods of the polytheists that they used to speak, which is their claim that God, glory be to Him, has taken a son. So He, glory be to Him, is the Rich. So He, glory be to Him, is far removed from what they attributed to Him of this clear falsehood. He explained that He is rich in need of that and that a son is only sought for a need, and the absolutely rich has no need to have a son to fulfill it. And if the need is eliminated, the son is eliminated. Also, only the one who is on the verge of extinction needs a son to take his place, and the Eternal and Ancient One is not in need of that. The interpretation of the verse has been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. Then He went to great lengths to respond to them with what is like proof, so He said: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And if everything is His and in His kingdom, then it is not right for anything in them to be a son of His, due to the contradiction between kingdom, sonship, and fatherhood. Then he refuted their false claim and showed that it was without evidence, saying: Indeed, you have some authority for this, meaning that you have no argument or proof for this statement that has been completely distorted. Min in min sultan is redundant for emphasis, and the prepositional phrase in bihdha is either related to sultan because it means argument and proof, or related to what you have because it has a meaning of stability. Then he rebuked them for this statement that is devoid of evidence and is false according to rational people, saying: Do you say about God that which you do not know? It is understood from this that every statement that has no evidence for it is not from knowledge at all, but rather from pure ignorance.
10:69: Then he ordered his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them something that would indicate that what they said was a lie, and that whoever lies about God will not succeed. He said: 69- “Say: Those who invent lies about God will not succeed.” That is, every slanderer has this nature, and these people are included in this primarily. Lying is mentioned with invention for emphasis, as previously mentioned in other places in the Noble Book. The meaning is that those who lie about their Lord will not succeed in any of their demands.
10:70: 70- Enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return, then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve. Then the Almighty explained that even if the one who made this slander wins something from the immediate demands, it is a short enjoyment in this world, then it is followed by death and returning to God, so the slanderer will be punished with an eternal punishment. So enjoyment is the predicate of a deleted subject, and the sentence is resumed to clarify that what the slanderer gets through his slander is not a benefit that is worth considering, rather it is a short enjoyment in this world followed by severe punishment because of the disbelief that occurred due to reasons including lying about God. Al-Akhfash said: The estimate is that they have enjoyment in this world, so the deleted part according to this is the predicate. Al-Kisa'i said: The estimate is that it is enjoyment or it is enjoyment, so the deleted part according to this is the subject. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said about the words of God Almighty: And let not their statement grieve you, because they did not benefit from what came to them from God and persisted in their disbelief. This was too much for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God came to him in what He rebuked him: “And let not their statement grieve you. Indeed, all honor belongs to God. He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” He hears what they say and knows it, so if He willed with His honor, He would have taken revenge on them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his words: And the day is seeing, he said: Illuminating. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his words: Indeed, you have authority for this, he said: You do not have authority for this.
10:71: When the Almighty exaggerated in stating the clear proofs and repelling the collapsed doubt, He began to mention the stories of the prophets, as that would be a consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He said: 71- And recite to them, meaning to the disbelievers who were your contemporaries and who opposed what you brought with their false statements, the report of Noah, meaning his story. The story is the story that has a serious and important significance, and what is meant is what happened to him with his people who disbelieved in what he brought, as the disbelievers of Quraysh and his likes did. When he said to his people, meaning when he said to his people, and the circumstance is accusative with report or a substitute for it, a substitute of inclusion, and the lam in to his people is the lam of notification. O my people, if my stay has become too great for you, meaning it is great and heavy. The place with the fatha on the meem is the place where one stays, and with the damma it is the residence. The reciters agreed on the opening, and the place was used as a metaphor for itself, as it is said: I did it for the sake of so-and-so, and from this: And for him who feared the place of his Lord, meaning he feared his Lord. It is possible that the place is meant to stay, meaning my staying among you was difficult for you. It is possible that the place is meant to stand, because the preacher stands while preaching. The meaning is: If my standing up to preach in your gatherings is hard for you, and my reminding you of the signs of God, the creation and revelation, is hard for you, then in God I have put my trust. This sentence is the answer to the condition, and the meaning is: I do not meet that from you except by putting my trust in God, for that is my habit that I have been on in the past and present. It is possible that he intended to create a specific level from the levels of trust, and it is possible that the answer to the condition is So gather together, and the sentence So in God I have put my trust is an interjection like your saying: If you have denied me something, then God is sufficient for me. The meaning of So gather together your affair is resolve upon it, from ajma’ al-amr: if he intended it and resolved upon it. Al-Farra’ said: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Farra’ that he said: To gather something means to prepare it. Mu’arraj Al-Sadosi said: To gather the matter is more eloquent than to gather it, and he recited: I wonder, for hopes are of no avail, will I ever become one day when my affair is resolved? Abu Al-Haitham said: He gathered his affair: he made it all together after it was scattered, and its separation is that you say once I will do such and such, and once I will do such and such, so when he decided on one thing he gathered it: that is he made it all together, so this is the origin of consensus, then it came to mean determination. The majority of the reciters agreed on the accusative of your partners and the severing of the hamza from ajma`u. Ya`qub and Asim Al-Jahdary read with a hamzat wasl in ajma`u on the basis that it is from jam`a yajma` jam`. Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ya`qub, and your partners read it in the nominative case. Al-Nahhas said: There are three aspects to the accusative of partners according to the reading of the majority: The first: It means and call upon your partners, Al-Kisa`i and Al-Farra` said: That is, call upon them to support you, so on this it is accusative with an implied verb. Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Mubarrad said: It is conjoined to the meaning. The poet said: I wish your husband was in the battlefield, carrying a sword and a spear. The spear is not girdled with it, but it is carried like a sword. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is with your partners, so the waw in this case is a waw with. As for the reading of ajma'u with a hamzat wasl, the conjunction is clear: that is, agree upon your affair and agree upon your partners. As for the interpretation of the reading of the nominative case, it is based on the conjunction of the partners with the nominative pronoun in ajma'u, and the goodness of this conjunction without emphasis with a separate word as is considered in that, since the speech has become long. Al-Nahhas and others said: This reading is far-fetched because if your partners were nominative, it would have been written in the Qur'an with a waw, and that is not found in it. Al-Mahdawi said: It is permissible for the partners to be raised by the beginning, and the predicate is omitted: that is, and your partners, so that they may agree upon their affair, and attributing that to the partners, despite the fact that the idols do not have reason, is intended to rebuke and reprimand those who worship them. It was narrated from Abu Qara: And call upon your partners, showing the action. His saying: Then let not your affair be a burden upon you. The burden is the covering from their saying, the crescent is covered: if it is hidden: meaning let your affair be apparent and clear. Tarafa said: By your life, my day is not sad, nor my night is eternal. This is what Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Haitham said: Its meaning is: Do not let your affair be vague for you. It was said that the gloom is the narrowness of the matter, as narrated by Abu Ubaidah. The meaning is: Do not let your affair be very narrow for you by my company and courtesy towards me, rather, repel this narrowness and hardship as you wish and are able to. According to the first two aspects, what is meant by the second matter is the first matter, and according to the third, what is meant by it is something else. His statement: Then decide to me and do not wait means that matter which you want from me. The origin of Iqda is from Qada which means to make sure. The meaning is: Make that matter perfect. Al-Akhfash and Al-Kisa’i said: It is like And we decided to him that matter meaning we completed it for him and conveyed it to him. Then do not wait: meaning do not delay, rather hasten your matter and do what you see fit. It was said that its meaning is: Then go to me and do not delay. Al-Nahhas said: This is a correct statement in the language, and from it the dead person passed away. Al-Farra’ narrated on the authority of some of the reciters that he read then they went out with the letter fa and the hamza cut off, meaning they headed out. In these words of Noah, peace be upon him, there is evidence of his trust in the victory of his Lord and his indifference to what his people threatened him with.
10:72: Then he explained to them that all that he had brought to them of excuses, warnings, and conveying the Shari'ah from God was not for worldly greed, nor for a base purpose, so he said: 72- But if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward meaning if you turn away from acting upon my advice and reminding you, then I have not asked you in return for that any reward that you would give me so that you would accuse me of what I have brought, and the fa in if you turn away is to arrange what comes after it according to what came before it, and the fa in then I have not asked you is a conditional my reward is only upon God meaning my reward for advising and reminding is upon Him, the Most High, so He will reward me whether you believe or turn away. The people of Medina, Abu Omar, Ibn Amir, and Hafs read with a vowel on the ya of ajri, and the rest read with a sukoon and I was commanded to be among the Muslims those who submit to the rule of God and who make their actions purely for God, the Most High, and do not take any reward for them and do not hope for anything immediate.
10:73: His statement: 73- But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship. That is, they continued to deny him and insisted on that. It is not meant that they innovated his denial after it did not exist. What is meant by those with him is those who responded to him and adhered to his religion. Successors is the plural of successor. The meaning is that He, glory be to Him, made them successors who inhabit the land that was for those who were destroyed by drowning and succeed them in it. And We drowned those who denied Our signs. Of the disbelievers who were stubborn with Noah and did not believe in him, God drowned them in the flood. Then see how was the end of those who were warned. In it is consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a threat and intimidation for the polytheists.
10:74: 74- Then We sent after him meaning after Noah messengers such as Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, and Shuaib and they came to them with clear proofs meaning miracles and what God sent them with of the laws that God legislated for the people of each prophet but they were not to believe meaning they did not innovate in faith but rather they continued in disbelief and insisted on it. The meaning is: It was not right or proper for a people from those peoples to whom God sent His messengers to believe at any time in what they had denied before meaning before their denial that occurred from them when the messengers came to them. Meaning: That every people in the world did not believe when God sent to them the Messenger sent to them specifically, in what they had denied before his coming to them, because they were not believers, rather they denied the religion, and if they had been believers, He would not have sent them a Messenger. This is based on the fact that the pronoun in they would not have believed and in because they denied refers to the people mentioned in His statement: to their people. It was said: The pronoun they denied refers to the people of Noah, meaning the people of the messengers would not have believed in what the people of Noah denied before these people who came after them and their messengers came to them with clear proofs. It was said: The ba in because they denied before is for causality, meaning they would not have believed when the messengers came because of what they had become accustomed to denying the truth before their coming, and this is questionable. It was said that the meaning is because they denied before: meaning in the world of atoms, for among them are those who denied in their hearts, even if they believed outwardly. An-Nahhas said: Among the best things that have been said is that it is for specific al-Nas 114:Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors. That is, like that great seal, We seal the hearts of those who transgress the customary limit in disbelief. The explanation of this has been presented in more than one place. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-A'raj regarding his statement: Then decide your plan, you and your partners, meaning: Then decide your plan and call your partners. He also narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse: That is, let them decide their plan with you. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Then let not your plan be a burden to you, he said: Let not your plan be difficult for you. Then decide, he said: What you will decide. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then decide, he said: Rise up. To Me and do not give me respite, he said: Do not delay.
10:75: His statement: 75- Then We sent after them is connected to His statement: Then We sent after him messengers and the pronoun in after them refers to the messengers mentioned previously, and Moses and Aaron were mentioned specifically despite their inclusion under the messengers due to their greater honor and the seriousness of what happened between them and Pharaoh, and what is meant by the elite are the nobles, and what is meant by the signs are the miracles, which are the nine mentioned in the Noble Book But they were arrogant about accepting them and did not humble themselves to them and submit to what they contained of miracles that necessitated belief in what they brought And they were a criminal people meaning they were people of great crimes and great sins, so because of that they dared to reject them, because sins prevent their owner from realizing the truth and seeing what is right. It was said: This sentence is an interjection confirming the content of what preceded it.
10:76: His saying: 76- So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, ‘This is clearly magic.’ That is, when Pharaoh and his people came with the truth from God, which is the miracles, they did not believe in them, but rather they attributed them to magic out of their stubbornness.
10:77: Moses responded to them saying: 77- Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' It was said that there was an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: Do you say about the truth, magic? So do not say that. Then he resumed another denial from his own side, and said: Is this magic? So he omitted their first statement, sufficing with the second. The reason for this is that they did not ask him about magic until he narrated what they said by saying: Is this magic? Rather, they were certain that it was magic, because they said, Indeed, this is clear magic. So then his saying: Is this magic? is not from their saying. Al-Akhfash said: It is from their saying, and there is a consideration in it for what we have presented. It was said that the meaning of Do you say is: Do you criticize the truth and attack it, and you should have submitted to it? Then he said: Is this magic, denying what they said. It was said that the object of Do you say is omitted, and this is what is indicated by their saying: Indeed, this is magic. The meaning is: Do you say what you say, meaning their saying that this is magic. Then it was said: Is this magic? According to this estimation and the first estimation, the sentence Is this magic? is resumed from the side of Moses, peace be upon him, and the question is for rebuke and reprimand after the first resumed sentence that occurs in answer to an assumed question, as if it was said: What did Moses say to them when they said: This is clearly magic? So it was said: He said: Do you say about the truth when it has come to you? in the manner of a rhetorical question, and the meaning is: Do you say about the truth when it has come to you that this is clearly magic, and it is the furthest thing from magic. Then he denied them and rebuked them and rebuked them and said: Is this magic? So Moses, peace be upon him, came with denial after denial and rebuke after rebuke and ignorance after ignorance, and the sentence And magicians will not succeed is in the accusative case as a state: that is, do you say about the truth that it is magic, while the fact is that magicians will not succeed, they will not obtain what they seek, nor will they attain good, nor will they escape from harm, so how could someone who is a messenger from God fall into this, and He supported him with miracles and clear proofs?
10:78: And sentence 78 - They said, 'Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers doing?' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it were said: So what did they say after Moses said to them what he said? This indicates that they were cut off from the evidence and were unable to present the argument, and they did not deny what they responded to what he brought against them, but rather they resorted to what the ignorant and dull-witted resort to, which is the argument of what their fathers were upon of disbelief, and they added to that what was their purpose and the ultimate goal of their demand and the reason for their stubbornness against the truth and their denial of the clear signs, which is the worldly leadership that they feared for and thought would go away from them if they believed, and how many remained upon falsehood, and he knows that it is falsehood by this pretext from the sects of this world in the past and not its right, so some of them were prevented by that from leaving disbelief, and some of them were prevented from leaving the Sunnah from innovation, and to the correct narration from pure opinion, it is said that he turned him away from something and twisted him away from it, and from this the poet said: I looked around the neighborhood until I saw myself getting sick from listening to the noise and the deception That is, you want to divert us from the thing we found our fathers doing, which is idol worship. What is meant by pride is kingship. Al-Zajjaj said: Kingship was called pride because it is the greatest thing sought in worldly matters, and it was said that it was called that because the king is arrogant. The result is that they justified their refusal to accept Moses’ call with two things: adherence to the tradition of the fathers and keenness on worldly leadership, because if they answered the prophet and believed him, the reins of his nation’s affairs would be transferred to him and the king would no longer have complete leadership, because managing people through religion raises the management of kings over them through policies and customs. Then they said: And we are not believers in you two, explicitly declaring denial and cutting off the desire for their belief. The address was given to Moses alone in their saying: Have you come to us to distract us? Then they combined him with Aaron in the address in their saying: And you will have pride on the earth, and we are not believers in you two. The reason for that is that they attributed the coming and the turning away through their fathers to Moses, because he was the intended one in the message conveying what God had prescribed for them, and they combined them in the other two pronouns, because pride includes them both in their opinion and because abandoning belief in Moses necessitates abandoning belief in Aaron.
10:79: The story was mentioned in Al-A'raf, where he said: 79- And Pharaoh said, 'Bring me every learned magician.' He said: This is how it was when he saw the white hand and the staff, because he believed that they were from magic, so he ordered his people to bring him every learned magician. This is how Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Ibn Waththab, and Al-A'mash read it: magician. The rest read it: sorcerer. We have already discussed this in Al-A'raf. The magician is an exaggerated form: meaning one who does a lot of magic, who has a lot of knowledge of its work and types.
10:80: 80- So when the magicians came there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is as follows: And Pharaoh said, Bring me every learned magician. So they brought them to him. So when the magicians came, so the fa is for conjunction with the omitted meaning. His statement: Moses said to them, 'Throw down what you are going to throw down.' That is, he said this statement to them after they said to him: Either you throw down, or we will be the ones who throw down. That is, throw down on the ground whatever you have of your ropes and sticks.
10:81: 81- So when they threw what they threw of that Moses said to them, What you have brought is magic meaning what you have brought is magic, on the basis that what is a relative pronoun is the subject and the predicate is magic, and the meaning is that it is magic, not that it is a sign of God's signs. Al-Farra' permitted the accusative of magic with you have brought, and what is a conditional, and the condition is you have brought, and the recompense is that God will invalidate it, on the basis of the fa': meaning that God will invalidate it. It was said: Magic is accusative as a source: meaning what you have brought is magic, then the alif and lam entered, so there is no need for the deletion of the fa', and Al-Nahhas chose it. He said: The deletion of the fa' in the recompense is not permitted by many grammarians except in poetic necessity. Abu Amr and Abu Ja'far read magic on the basis that the hamza is for interrogation, and the estimation is: is it magic, so what according to this reading is interrogative. My father recited: “What you have brought is magic. God will nullify it, that is, He will destroy it and it will become invalid by the miraculous signs that He will reveal through me. ‘God does not uphold the work of corrupters,’ that is, the work of this type, so it includes everyone who is truly corrupt, and magic and sorcerers are included in it primarily.
10:82: And the waw in 82- And God will establish the truth is to connect with He will invalidate it: that is, He will clarify and explain it with His words that He revealed in His books to His prophets because they contain arguments and proofs even though the criminals hate it from the people of Pharaoh or the criminals in general, and the people of Pharaoh are included under them primarily, and crime is sins.
10:83: His saying: 83- None believed in Moses except a few of his people The pronoun refers to Moses: that is, from the people of Moses, and they are a group of the descendants of the Children of Israel. It was said: What is meant is a group of the descendants of Pharaoh, so the pronoun refers to Pharaoh. It was said: And among them is the believer of Pharaoh's family, his wife, his daughter's hairdresser, and the wife of his treasurer. It was said: They are a people whose fathers were Copts and whose mothers were from the Children of Israel. This was narrated from Al-Farra' For fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs The pronoun refers to Pharaoh, and it was pluralized because since he was a tyrant, they pluralized his pronoun to glorify him. It was said: The people of Pharaoh were called Pharaoh like Thamud, so the pronoun refers to them in this regard. It was said that it refers to a deleted noun, and the estimate is: For fear of Pharaoh's family. This was narrated from Al-Farra'. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh prevented this, so it is not permissible according to them: Hind stood up and you mean her slave. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Akhfash that the pronoun refers to the offspring, and Al-Nahhas strengthened it to tempt them meaning to divert them from their religion with the torment that he would inflict upon them, and it is a substitute for inclusion. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with the verbal noun And Pharaoh was exalted in the land meaning arrogant, haughty, and dominating the land of Egypt And he is among the transgressors exceeding the limit in disbelief and what he did of killing, crucifixion, and various punishments.
10:84: His saying: 84- "And Moses said, 'O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you should be Muslims.'" It was said: This is a repetition of the condition, so the condition for relying upon God is belief in Him and Islam: meaning submission to His judgment and destiny. It was said: This is not from the suspension of the ruling on two conditions, rather what is suspended on faith is the obligation of reliance, and what is conditioned on Islam is its existence. The meaning is: that they submit themselves to God: meaning that they make them safe and pure for Him, with no share for Satan in them, because reliance cannot be with confusion. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: Its equivalent in speech is if Zaid strikes you, then strike him if you have the strength to do so.
10:85: 85- "They said meaning the people of Moses, answering him, In God we trust." Then they called upon God sincerely and said: "Our Lord, do not make us a trial meaning a place of trial for the wrongdoing people." The meaning is: Do not give them power over us so that they torture us until they tempt us away from our religion, and do not make us a trial for them so that they tempt others through us, so that they say to them: If these people were right, we would not have given them power over us and tortured them. According to the first meaning, the trial means the tempted.
10:86: And when they presented their supplication to God Almighty to protect their religion from corruption, they followed it with a request for the protection of their souls, so they said: 86- And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people. And in this is evidence that they were concerned with the matter of religion above their concern for the safety of their souls.
10:87: His saying: 87- And We inspired Moses and his brother, saying, ‘Provide houses for your people in Egypt.’ “An” is the explanatory particle, because the inspiration has the meaning of provide houses: that is, take houses for your people in Egypt. It is said: I provided Zayd with a place and I provided for Zayd a place. The place of residence is the obligatory home, and from this, God provided him with a home: that is, He obliged him to it and made him live in it. From this, the hadith: Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire. From this, the rajaz poet said: We are the sons of Adnan, there is no doubt that glory and kingship are ours. It was said: Egypt in this verse is Alexandria, and it was said: It is the well-known Egypt, not Alexandria. And make your houses qiblah meaning facing the direction of the qiblah. It was said: What is meant by houses here are the mosques, and this is what a group of the Salaf went with. It was said: What is meant by the houses in which they live, they were ordered to make them qiblahs, and what is meant by the qiblah according to the first opinion is the direction of Jerusalem, which is the qiblah of the Jews to this day. It was said: The direction of the Kaaba, and that it was the qiblah of Moses and those with him. It was said: What is meant is that they make their houses facing the qiblah to pray in them secretly so that they will not be afflicted by the infidels with shame because of prayer. What supports this is His statement: And establish prayer meaning that which He commanded you to establish, for it indicates that the qiblah is the qiblah of prayer, either in the mosques or in the houses, not making the houses facing each other. Rather, the address was made at the beginning of the speech with Moses and Aaron, then it was made for them and their people in His statement: And make your houses qiblah and establish prayer then He singled out Moses for address after that, and He said: And give good tidings The believers because the choice of place is delegated to the prophets. Then it was made general in facing the qiblah and establishing prayer, because that is obligatory for everyone and is not specific to the prophets. Then it was made specific to Moses because he is the origin of the message and Aaron was subordinate to him, so that was to magnify the good report and the one who was given the good report. It was said that the address in And give good tidings to the believers is to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the manner of turning away and objection, and the first is more appropriate. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: to turn us away he said: to turn us away. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: to turn us away from our gods. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: and you will have pride on the earth he said: greatness, kingship and authority. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and none believed in Moses except a few offspring he said: the offspring are a few. And these narrated on his authority regarding his statement: offspring from his people he said: from the Children of Israel. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: they are the children of those to whom Moses was sent after a long time and their fathers died. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: the offspring who believed in Moses were from people other than the Children of Israel from the people of Pharaoh, among them were the wife of Pharaoh, the believer of Pharaoh’s family, the treasurer of Pharaoh and the wife of his treasurer. And Abd al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Naeem bin Hammad in al-Fitan and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, he said: Do not give them power over us so that they tempt us. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from him that he said in his interpretation of the verse: Do not punish us at the hands of the people of Pharaoh or with a punishment from You, so that the people of Pharaoh would say: If they were on the truth, they would not have been punished, nor would We have given them power over them, so that they would be tempted by us. And Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abu Qilabah regarding the verse that he said: He asked his Lord that our enemy not prevail over us so that they would think that they are more deserving of justice and would be tempted by that. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Majlaz something similar. Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: And We inspired Moses and his brother, the verse that he said that when Pharaoh prevented them from praying, so they were ordered to make their places of worship in their houses and to face the Qiblah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: That you settle for your people in Egypt, he said: Egypt is Alexandria. Saeed Ibn Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: They used to pray only in churches until they feared the people of Pharaoh and were ordered to pray in their homes. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: They were ordered to make mosques in their homes. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Sinan who said: The qiblah is the Kaaba, and he mentioned that Adam and those who came after him used to pray facing the Kaaba. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And make your houses qiblah, he said: They face each other.
10:88: When Moses, peace be upon him, exaggerated in showing miracles and establishing clear proofs, and this had no effect on those to whom he was sent, he called upon them after explaining the reason for their insistence on disbelief and their adherence to denial and stubbornness. He said, explaining the reason first: 88- Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world. It was previously mentioned that the chiefs are the nobles, and adornment is the name for everything that is adorned with, such as clothing, mounts, ornaments, bedding, weapons, and other things. Then he repeated the call for emphasis, saying: Our Lord, that they may go astray from Your way. There is a difference of opinion regarding this lam that comes before the verb. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: It is the lam of consequence and becoming. The meaning is that since the consequence of their matter was misguidance, it became as if God Almighty gave them what He gave them of blessings so that they would go astray. So the lam in this case is related to aatiyyat. It was said that it is the lam of kay, meaning I gave them that so that they would go astray. Some people said that the meaning is I gave them that so that they would not go astray, so la was deleted as God Almighty said: God makes clear to you lest you go astray. An-Nahhas said: The apparent meaning of this answer is good, except that the Arabs do not delete la except with an. So the author of this interpretation deceived them by citing as evidence His statement: God makes clear to you lest you go astray. It was said that the lam is for supplicating against them. The meaning is: Test them with destruction from Your path. This speaker cited as evidence His statement after this: Erase and Strengthen. The author of Al-Kashshaf elaborated on this in a way that is of no use, but the first statement is preferable. The Kufians read li-yidaloo with a damma on the letter of the present tense: meaning they cause others to be misguided. The rest read it with a fatha: meaning they go astray in their own selves. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth. Al-Zajjaj said: obliterating something means removing its original form. The meaning is: praying against them that God will destroy their wealth and annihilate it. It was read with a damma on the meem from atma. And harden their hearts means make them hard and imprinted, not accepting the truth and not opening to faith. His statement: So they will not believe. Al-Mubarrad and Al-Zajjaj said: It is conjoined with li-yidaloo, and the meaning is: I gave them blessings so they would go astray and not believe. The space between the conjoined and the conjoined is an objection. Al-Farra', Al-Kisa'i and Abu Ubaidah said: It is a prayer with the wording of a prohibition, and the meaning is: O God, so they will not believe. From this is the saying of Al-A'sha: Do not let what is hidden appear before your eyes, and do not meet me except with your nose downcast. Al-Akhfash said: It is the answer to the command: meaning, obliterate and intensify so that they will not believe, so it is in the accusative case. This was also narrated from Al-Farra’, and from it: Oh camel, go with a broad neck to Solomon, so that we may rest. Until they see the painful punishment means that they will not have faith unless they see what God will punish them with, and at that point their faith will be of no use. Some scholars have questioned the supplication against these people in this verse, and said: The messengers only seek guidance for their people and their faith. It was answered that it is not permissible for a prophet to supplicate against his people except with the permission of God, the Most High, and God only permits that because He knows that there is no one among them who will believe. For this reason, when God informed Noah, peace be upon him, that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, he said: My Lord, do not leave on the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers.
10:89: 89- He said, 'Your prayer has been answered, so be steadfast.' He made the prayer here attributed to Moses and Aaron, and previously he attributed it to Moses alone, so it was said: Aaron believed in Moses' prayer, so he was called here a caller, even though the caller was Moses alone. At the beginning of the speech he attributed the prayer to Moses because he was the caller, and here he attributed it to them both, lowering the believer to the status of the caller, and it is possible that they were both callers, but he attributed the prayer to Moses at the beginning of the speech because of his originality in the message. Al-Nahhas said: I heard Ali bin Sulayman say: The evidence that the prayer was for them is Moses' saying, Our Lord, and he did not say, Lord. Ali and Al-Salami recited, Your prayer, and Ibn Al-Sameefa' recited, Your prayer, and steadfastness means steadfastness in what they are upon of calling to God. Al-Farra and others said: They were commanded to be steadfast in their matter and to remain steadfast in it, in calling Pharaoh and his people to faith until the interpretation of the answer came to them for forty years, then they were destroyed. It was said: The meaning of steadfastness is to abandon haste and to adhere to tranquility, contentment and submission to what God, the Most High, decrees. His statement: And do not follow the way of those who do not know with a shaddah on the noon for emphasis and it was moved with a kasrah because it is the original and because they resemble the dual noon. Ibn Dhakwan read with a light noon as a negation, not a prohibition. It was read with a light second supra from tabaa’ban. The meaning is: The prohibition for them from following the way of those who do not know of God’s habit of conducting matters according to what interests require, whether hastening or delaying.
10:90: His saying: 90- And We made the Children of Israel cross the sea is from the verb jawwaz meaning to go beyond a place, and the ba is for transitivity: meaning We made them cross the sea until they reached the shore, because God, the Most High, made the sea dry, so they passed through it until they came out of it to the land. The explanation of this has been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah in His, the Most High's, saying: And when We parted the sea for you. Al-Hasan and jawzna read, and they are two dialects, So Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them. It is said: taba'a and ataba'a have the same meaning: if he caught up with him. Al-Asma'i said: It is said ataba'a with a cut-off alif: if he caught up with him and overtook him, and ataba'a with a connected alif: if he followed a trace that he either caught up with or did not catch up with. Abu Zaid also said: Abu Amr said: If he followed him in connection: he imitated him. The accusative of baghiya and ‘adwā is in the state, and baghiya means injustice, and ‘adwā means aggression. It is possible that their accusatives are in the cause: that is, for baghiya and ‘adwā. Al-Hasan read ‘adwā with a damma on the ‘ayn and the dal and a shaddah on the waw like ‘ala ya’lu ‘alwan. It was said that baghiya means seeking superiority in speech without right, and ‘adwā is in the action until drowning overtakes him meaning it reached him, reached him, and bridled him. This is because Moses went out with the Children of Israel while Pharaoh was unaware. When Pharaoh heard of that, he caught up with them with his soldiers, so God parted the sea for Moses and the Children of Israel, so they walked in it until they came out from the other side, and Pharaoh followed them while the sea remained in the state it was in when Moses and those with him had gone. When Pharaoh’s soldiers had entered completely and were about to come out from the other side, it closed in on them and they drowned as God, the Most High, narrated that. He said, 'I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe' meaning I believe that with the opening of the hamza, as the original is that, so the ba' was deleted, and the pronoun is for the matter. It was read with the kasra of in as a resumption, and Abu Hatim claimed that the statement was deleted: i.e. I believe, so I said that this belief did not benefit him because it occurred from him after he had completely drowned, as mentioned in An-Nisa', and the accursed one did not say I believe in God or in the Lord of the worlds, rather he said: I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe, because a vein of the claim of divinity remained in him. His saying: And I am of the Muslims meaning those who submit to the command of God, who obey Him, who make Him One and deny everything else, and this sentence is either in the accusative case as a state or conjoined with I believe.
10:91: His statement: 91- Now, and you disobeyed before and were among the corrupters is a statement of an implied statement connected to I said, I believe: meaning, it was said to him: Do you believe now? There is a difference of opinion about who said this statement to Pharaoh. It was said that it was from the words of God, the Most High, and it was said from the words of Gabriel, and it was said from the words of Michael, and it was said from the words of Pharaoh, he said that to himself. The phrase and you disobeyed before is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of the implied verb after the implied statement, which is do you believe now? The meaning is: his denial of faith when drowning stopped him, and the fact is that he had disobeyed God before, and the intended meaning is to rebuke and reprimand him. The phrase and you were among the corrupters is conjoined with disobeyed and is included in the state: that is, you were among the corrupters on earth by your straying from the truth and misleading others.
10:92: His saying: 92- So today We will save you with your body. Nanjik was read with a light ha', while the majority read it with a heavy ha'. Al-Yazidi read: Nanhik with a silent ha' from tanhih, and Alqamah narrated it from Ibn Mas'ud, and the meaning of Nanjik with a jim is: We will cast you on a high place on the earth, and that is because the Children of Israel did not believe that Pharaoh had drowned, and they said: He is greater than that, so God cast him on a high place on the earth, meaning a high place on the earth so that they could see him, and it was said that the meaning is: We will extract you from what your people fell into from the Messenger in the bottom of the sea and make you float so that they may see you dead from drowning, and the meaning of Nanhik with a silent ha' is: We will cast you on a side of the earth. It was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he read with your bodies. The commentators differed about the meaning of with your body. It was said that it means: with your body after the soul has been taken from it. It was also said that it means: with your armor, and the armor is called a body. From this is the saying of Ka’b ibn Malik: You see the bodies therein covered with heroes and the strong cores. By bodies he meant armor, and Amr bin Ma’di Karib said: Their women went away with great resentment, their faces covered with blood and their bodies torn. That is, with long armor and short armor: which is called bodies as Abu Ubaidah said. Al-Akhfash said: As for the statement of those who said with your armor, it is nothing, and he preferred that the body here refers to the body. His statement: So that it may be a sign to those who come after you is an explanation for his salvation with his body, and in that he did not show his body without his people except for this reason and nothing else, and what is meant by the sign is the mark: that is, so that it may be a sign for those who come after you from the people by which they know your destruction, and that you are not as you claim and so that doubts about you having become dead by drowning are removed from them, and it was said: What is meant is that your being thrown on the shore alone without the drowned from your people may be a sign from the signs of God, by which people may consider or by which those who will come from the nations may consider if they hear that so that they may beware of arrogance, tyranny and rebellion against God, the Exalted, for this one who reached what he reached in claiming divinity and continued in that for a long time had this ugly end. It was read to those who came after you in the past tense, meaning those who will come after you from the generations or those who came after you in leadership or in residing in the dwelling in which you lived. And indeed, many of the people, of Our signs, which require consideration and contemplation and awaken from the sleep of heedlessness, are heedless of what the signs require. This sentence is a conclusion. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, meaning: destroy and annihilate their wealth, and harden their hearts, meaning: stamp, so they will not believe until they see the painful punishment, which is drowning. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi who said: Umar bin Abdul Aziz asked me about his statement: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, so I told him that God obliterated the wealth of Pharaoh and the family of Pharaoh until it turned into stones. Umar said: Stay where you are until I come to you. So he called for a sealed bag and opened it, and in it were silver cut into pieces as if they were stones, and dinars, dirhams and similar wealth, all of it stones. It has been narrated that their wealth turned into stones by a group of the Salaf. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Your supplication has been answered. He said: So He answered him and prevented Pharaoh from believing. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: When Moses supplicated, Aaron would say: Amen to his supplication. Abu Hurayrah said: It is one of the names of God, so that is His saying: Your supplication has been answered. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Saeed bin Mansour narrated something similar on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: They claim that Pharaoh remained forty years after this supplication. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Be steadfast and carry out my command, which means steadfastness. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: Enemy, arrogance, and haughtiness in the Book of God mean tyranny. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the last of Moses’ companions left and the last of Pharaoh’s companions entered, God inspired the sea to close on them, and Pharaoh’s finger came out, saying, There is no god but He in whom the Children of Israel believed. Gabriel said: Then I knew that the Lord is Merciful, and I feared that mercy would reach him, so I touched him with my wing and said, ‘Is it now that I disobeyed before?’ When Moses and his companions left, those of Pharaoh’s people who had stayed behind said, Pharaoh and his companions did not drown, but they are on the islands of the sea hunting. God inspired the sea to vomit Pharaoh naked, so it vomited him out naked, bald, short, and this is what He said: This day We will save you with your body that you may be a sign to those who come after you, for those who said, Pharaoh is surely drowning, and it is as if the salvation of anyone other than him is a safe salvation. Then God inspired the sea to vomit what is in you, so it vomited them out onto the shore. The sea does not vomit out a drowning person in its belly until the fish eat him, so the sea will not accept a drowning person until the Day of Resurrection. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God drowned Pharaoh and he said: ‘I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe.’ Gabriel said to me: ‘O Muhammad, if you could see me when I take some of the mud of the sea and put it in my mouth for fear that mercy would reach him.’” Al-Tirmidhi narrated this hadith through more than one chain of transmission, and he said: It is good, authentic and rare. Al-Hakim also authenticated it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas through other chains of transmission. Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: “Gabriel said to me: There was nothing on earth more hateful to me than Pharaoh. When he believed, I began to fill his mouth with mud and cover it for fear that mercy would reach him.” Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Umar. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, similar to this. In the chain of transmission of the hadith of Abu Hurairah is an unknown man, while the rest of its men are trustworthy. It is truly amazing that someone who has no knowledge of the art of narration among the commentators, and can hardly distinguish between the most authentic hadith and the most false of them, can engage in speaking about the hadiths of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by invalidating what is authentic among them, and he sends his tongue and pen with pure ignorance and blatant shortcomings that make anyone who has even the slightest practice in the art of hadith laugh. O poor man, what do you have to do with this affair that you have nothing to do with? Do you not cover yourself and sit on your side, and know that with this knowledge you are one of the most ignorant of the ignorant, and occupy yourself with what is your knowledge that you do not exceed, and your result that you have no other, which is the science of language and its subsidiary sciences of the mechanical sciences, and the author of Al-Kashshaf, may God have mercy on him, has become, because of what he deals with in his interpretation of the science of hadith that is not from it in the report or the chest, a mockery for the mockers and a lesson for those who consider, so sometimes he narrates in his book fabrications without knowing that they are fabrications, and sometimes he deals with rejecting what is authentic, and he is certain that it is from lying on the Messenger of God and slandering him, and it may be in the two Sahihs and others that are attached to them from the narration of a group of the Companions with chains of transmission all of them are imams who are trustworthy and proven proofs, and the smallest share of reason prevents its owner from speaking about a science that he does not know or have the least knowledge of, even if that science is from the sciences of terminology that a group of people agree upon, and they agree on matters among themselves, so what about the science of the Sunnah which is the division of the Book of God, and its speaker is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its narrator On his authority: The best of generations, then those who follow them, then those who follow them, and every letter of its letters and word of its words establishes a general law for all the people of Islam. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {So this day We will save you with your body}, he said: God saved Pharaoh for the Children of Israel from the sea, so they looked at him after he drowned. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: He said: With your body. He said: Some of the Children of Israel denied the death of Pharaoh, so he was thrown on the shore of the sea so that the Children of Israel would see him, red and short like a bull. Ibn al-Anbari narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b regarding his statement: {So this day We will save you with your body}, he said: With your armor, and his armor was made of pearls with which he would encounter wars.
10:93: His saying: 93- And We have certainly provided This is among the blessings that God Almighty has enumerated with the Children of Israel. The meaning of We provided is We have settled. It is said: I provided Zayd with a home means I settled him in it. The place of residence is a noun of place or a source, and adding it to the truth is according to the rule of the Arabs, for if they praised something, they added it to the truth, and what is meant by it here is the praised and chosen home. It was said that it is the land of Egypt, and it was said that it is Jordan and Palestine, and it was said that it is the Levant. And We provided them with good things meaning the pleasures of provision. So they did not differ in the matter of their religion and branched out in it into people after they had been on one path and not differing until knowledge came to them meaning that they did not differ in religion except after knowledge came to them through their reading of the Torah and their knowledge of its rulings, and what it contained of report about the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that the meaning is: They did not differ until knowledge came to them, which is the Qur’an revealed to our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then they differed in its description and attributes, and those of them who believed believed in it and those who disbelieved disbelieved in it. So what is meant by those who differed according to the first opinion are the Jews after the Torah was revealed to them and they learned about it, and according to the second opinion they are the Jews who were contemporary with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ. So He will reward the doer of good for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing, and the one who is right will be rewarded for his work with truth and the one who is wrong will be rewarded for his work with falsehood.
10:94: 94- "If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you" Doubt in the original language: adding one thing to another, and from it the doubt of the substance in a contract, and the doubter is as if he adds to what he imagines something else other than it, so he hesitates and is confused, and the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is someone other than him as mentioned in the Qur’an in more than one place. Abu Omar Muhammad bin Abdul Wahid Al-Zahid said: I heard the two Imams Tha’lab and Al-Mubarrad saying: The meaning of If you are in doubt is: Say, O Muhammad, to the disbeliever: If you are in doubt, then ask those who read the Scripture before you, meaning the Muslims of the People of the Book, such as Abdullah bin Salam and his likes. The idol worshippers acknowledged the Jews’ knowledge and acknowledged that they were more knowledgeable than them. So God, the Exalted, commanded His Prophet to guide those who doubted what God had revealed to him of the Qur’an to ask the People of the Book who had become Muslims, for they would tell them that it is truly the Book of God, and that this is His Messenger, and that the Torah bears witness to that and speaks of it. In this interpretation, despite its goodness, there is a contradiction to the apparent meaning. Al-Qatibi said: What is meant by this verse is the one among the disbelievers who is not certain of denying the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor of believing him, but rather is in doubt. It was said: What is meant by the address is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one else. The meaning is: If you were one of those who doubted what We have told you, and you asked the People of the Book, they would remove your doubt. It was said: Doubt is tightness of the chest: that is, if your chest is tight due to the disbelief of these people, then be patient and ask those who read the Book before you to tell you about the patience of the prophets before you in the face of the harm of their people. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: assumption and estimation, as if he said to him: If, for example, doubt occurs to you and Satan imagines an illusion from it to you as an estimation, then ask those who read the Book, for they will tell you about your prophethood and what was revealed to you, and they will acknowledge that because they find it written with them, and what required them to conceal what they had has been removed from those who converted to Islam. His statement: The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters in this is a statement of what uproots doubt from its origin and removes it entirely, which is the testimony of God, the Most High, that what doubt occurred about, despite the different interpretations of the doubter, is the truth that is not mixed with falsehood and is not tainted with doubt, then he followed it with the prohibition of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from doubting what God revealed to him, but rather he should continue with what he is upon of certainty and the absence of doubt.
10:95: This prohibition of his could be an allusion to others, as in some places in the Noble Book. This is also the case with his prohibition, may God bless him and grant him peace, of denying the verses of God. The apparent meaning of this is an allusion, especially after he followed it up with his saying: 95- "Then you will be among the losers." In this allusion is a deterrent to those who doubt and deny, which is more eloquent and effective than the prohibition of them themselves, because if it is such that someone who cannot imagine it coming from him is prohibited from it, then how about someone who can do so?
10:96: His statement: 96- Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe. Something similar has already been mentioned in this surah, and the meaning is that God’s decree and predestination have come into effect upon them, that they will persist in disbelief and die upon it, and faith will not occur from them under any circumstances. And if what appears to be faith occurs from them, such as those among them who believe when they witness the punishment, then it is considered nonexistent.
10:97: 97- And if every sign came to them of the verses of creation and revelation, that would not benefit them because God Almighty has sealed their hearts and the word has come true upon them until they see the punishment and what appears to them is what appears to be faith but is not faith, and none of its rulings result from it.
10:98: His saying: 98- Why was there not a village that believed and its faith benefited it? This Why is the preparatory particle that means Why as Al-Akhfash, Al-Kisa'i and others said. This is indicated by what is in the Mushaf of Abi and Ibn Mas'ud: Why was there not a village? The meaning is: Why was not a single village from these villages that we destroyed that believed with a belief that was valid, and that is by being sincere to God before witnessing His punishment and not delaying it as Pharaoh delayed it, and the exception in his saying: Except the people of Yunus is disconnected, and it is an exception from the villages because what is meant are their people, and the meaning is: But the people of Yunus when they believed with a belief that was valid before witnessing the punishment or at the beginning of witnessing it before it came upon them We removed from them the punishment of disgrace. A group of imams, including Al-Kisa'i, Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra', said that this exception is disconnected. It was said: It is possible for it to be connected, and the sentence is in the meaning of negation, as if it was said: No village from the destroyed villages believed except the people of Yunus. And its accusative is based on the origin of the exception. And it was read in the nominative case as a substitute. Al-Zajjaj said in explaining the nominative case: The meaning is other than the people of Yunus, but illa was applied to it and it was difficult to make the i’rab based on it, so the noun that follows it was parsed with the i’rab of ghayr. Ibn Jarir said: The people of Yunus were singled out from among the nations by being forgiven after witnessing the punishment, and this was reported from a group of commentators. Al-Zajjaj said: The punishment did not occur, but they saw the sign that indicates the punishment, and if they had seen the punishment itself, faith would not have benefited them, and this is more appropriate than what Ibn Jarir said. What is meant by the punishment of humiliation is that which God removed from them, and it is the punishment that Yunus had promised them would befall them but they did not see it, or the signs of which they saw but not its exact meaning. And We gave them enjoyment for a time means after the punishment was removed from them, God gave them enjoyment in this world for a time whose amount was known to them.
10:99: Then the Almighty explained that faith and its opposite are both by the will and decree of God, saying: 99- And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them, such that no one would have left them, all together, united in faith, not divided and differing in it. But He did not will that because it is contrary to the interest that God Almighty wanted, and the accusative of all together is in the state of the state, as Sibawayh said. Al-Akhfash said: He came with the phrase all of them after all of them for emphasis, like his saying: Do not take two gods. And since the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was keen on the faith of all people, God informed him that this would not happen, because His will, which is based on perfect wisdom and prevailing interests, does not require this, so He said: Would you then compel people until they become believers? For this is not within your power, O Muhammad, nor is it within your ability. And in this there is consolation for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a repulsion of what constricts his chest from seeking the good of all, which if it were, it would not be a true good, but rather would be closer to corruption. And God has perfect wisdom.
10:100: Then the Almighty explained what came before by saying: 100- "And it is not for a soul to believe except by God's permission" meaning it is not correct or right for a soul to believe in God except by His permission: meaning by His facilitation, ease and will for that reason nothing happens except what He wills, whatever it may be. "And He places defilement upon those who do not reason" meaning torment, disbelief or abandonment which is the cause of torment. Al-Hasan, Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read "and make" with a noon. There are two dialects for "defilement": with a damma or a kasra on the ra'. What is meant by "those who do not reason" are the disbelievers who do not understand God's proofs, nor do they reflect on His verses, nor do they ponder over the evidence He has set up for them. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And We had certainly settled the Children of Israel in a place of truth, he said: God settled them in Ash-Sham and Jerusalem. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: The places of truth are Egypt and Ash-Sham. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: And they did not differ until knowledge came to them, he said: Knowledge is the Book of God which He revealed and His command which He commanded them with. It was mentioned in the hadith that the Jews differed into seventy-one sects, and that the Christians differed into seventy-two sects, and this nation will split into seventy-three sects. It is in the Sunan and Musnads, and the discussion of it is long. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ad-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: If you are in doubt, the verse, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not doubt and did not ask. And Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not doubt nor do I ask. And it is a mursal. And Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {So ask those who read the Scripture before you} he said: The Torah and the Gospel are those who met Muhammad from the People of the Scripture and believed in him, he said: Ask them if you are in doubt that you are written among them. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: {Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe} he said: The wrath of God has come into effect upon them because they disobeyed Him. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: {Why was there not a city that believed} he said: There was no city that believed. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse: He said: This did not happen among the nations before the people of Jonah. It did not benefit a city that disbelieved and then believed when it witnessed the punishment except the people of Jonah, so God excluded the people of Jonah. He said: It was mentioned to us that the people of Yunus were in Nineveh in the land of Mosul. When they lost their prophet, God cast repentance into their hearts, so they put on sackcloth and brought out their livestock and separated every animal from its young. They cried out to God for forty mornings. When God knew the sincerity in their hearts and the repentance and regret for what had happened from them, He removed the punishment from them after it had descended upon them. There was only a mile between them and the punishment. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Yunus supplicated for his people, and when they refused to answer him, he promised them the punishment. He said: It will come to you on such and such a day. Then he left them. When the prophets promised their people punishment, they left. When the punishment overtook them, they left and separated the woman from her child, and the young goat from her child. They went out crying out to God. God knew their sincerity, so He accepted their repentance and averted the punishment from them. Yunus sat in the road asking about the report. A man passed by him and said: What happened to the people of Yunus? So he told him what they had done, and he said: I will not return to a people whom I have lied to, and he left in anger, meaning in spite of himself. Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: The torment overcame the people of Yunus as a garment overtakes a grave when its occupant enters it, and the sky rained blood. Ahmad in Az-Zuhd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the torment had descended upon the people of Yunus, and there was no distance between them and it except two-thirds of a mile, so when they called upon God, He removed it from them. Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Jild who said: When the torment overcame the people of Yunus, they went to a sheikh from among their remaining scholars and said to him: What do you see? He said: Say: O Ever-Living when there is no living, and O Ever-Living, the Reviver of the dead, and O Ever-Living, there is no god but You, so they said: So the torment was removed from them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And He places the impurity, he said: Anger. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: Rijs is the devil, and rajs is torment.
10:101: His statement: 101- "Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth."
