Since the Almighty has made clear that faith does not occur except by the will of God, He has commanded us to look and reason with the heavenly and earthly evidence. What is meant by looking is contemplation and consideration: that is, say, O Muhammad, to the unbelievers: Think and consider what is in the heavens and the earth of the created things that indicate the Creator, His Oneness, and the perfection of His power. And what is the subject, and its predicate is in the heavens and the earth. Or the subject is what, and that means which, and in the heavens and the earth is its relative clause, and the relative pronoun and its relative clause is the predicate of the subject: that is, what is in the heavens and the earth? In both cases, the sentence is in the accusative case with the verb that precedes it. Then the Almighty mentioned that contemplation and reflection on these signs are of no benefit to those whose misery has become entrenched, so He said: And what do the signs and the warnings avail? meaning what does it avail, since ma is negative, and it is possible for it to be interrogative: meaning what is of benefit? The signs are what He expressed by saying: What is in the heavens and the earth? and the warning is the plural of warner, and they are the messengers, or the plural of warning, which is the source from a people who do not believe in the knowledge of God Almighty, and the meaning is: that whoever is like this, nothing will avail him and nothing will push him away from disbelief.
10:102: His statement: 102- Do they then await anything other than the like of the days of those who passed away before them? That is, do these disbelievers who were contemporary with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, await anything other than the events of God Almighty with the disbelievers who passed away before them? The previous prophets used to threaten the disbelievers of their time with days that included various types of punishment, and they denied them and persisted in disbelief until God sent down His punishment upon them and His vengeance descended upon them. Then He said: Say, O Muhammad, to these disbelievers who were contemporary with you, Then wait, that is, wait for the promise of your Lord. Indeed, I am with you among those who wait for the promise of my Lord. In this is a severe threat and a severe warning that what happened to those people of destruction will happen to these people.
10:103: Then in His statement: 103- Then We will save Our messengers is for conjunction with an implied meaning indicated by what preceded it, as if it was said We destroyed the nations, then We saved Our messengers who were sent to them. And Yaqub read Then We will save in a lightened form. And he also read it in It is incumbent upon Us to save the believers. And it was narrated in the same way from Al-Kisa'i and Hafs in the second. The rest read it with emphasis, and they are two eloquent languages: anja yanji inja’, and naja yanji tanjiyyah with one meaning. And those who believed is in apposition to Our Messengers: that is, We saved them and saved those who believed. The expression with the wording of the future tense verb is to evoke the image of the past state, to exaggerate its matter. Likewise, it is a right upon Us: that is, it is a right upon Us truly, or a rescue like that rescue truly. We save the believers from Our punishment of the disbelievers. What is meant by the believers is the gender, so the messengers and their followers are included in that, or it is specific to the believers, and they are the followers of the messengers, because the messengers are included in that a fortiori.
10:104: His saying: 104- "Say, 'O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion,'" God Almighty commanded His Messenger to show the difference between his way and the way of the polytheists, addressing all people, or the disbelievers among them, or the people of Mecca in particular, by saying: If you are in doubt about my religion that I am upon, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, and you do not know its reality nor recognize its validity, and that it is the true religion that there is no religion other than it, then know that I am innocent of the religions that you are upon. "I do not worship those you worship other than God" in any case. "But I worship God, who takes your souls," meaning I single Him out for worship, I do not worship anyone other than Him from your idols and other things. He singled out the description of the one who takes your souls from among the descriptions because of the threat that this contains for them: meaning I worship God, who takes your souls and does to you what He does of severe torment, and because it indicates creation first, and resurrection second, and because it is the most awe-inspiring of states in the hearts, and because it is It indicates creation first, and resurrection second, and because it is the most awe-inspiring state in the hearts, and because the mention of destruction and the events that befell the disbelievers of previous nations has already been made, it is as if he said: I worship God who promised me to destroy you. And when he mentioned that none is to be worshipped except God, he made clear that he was commanded to believe, saying: And I was commanded to be among the believers, meaning that I was from the same kind as those who believed in God and devoted their religion to Him.
10:105: And the sentence 105- "And that you set your face toward the religion is conjoined to the sentence That I be among the believers and this is not prevented by the fact that the conjoined is in the imperative form because the intended meaning of that" is to indicate the source, and this does not differ between the declarative and the imperative, or the conjoined to it is in the meaning of the imperative, as if it was said: Be a believer then establish, and the meaning is: that God the Almighty commanded him to be upright in the religion and steadfast in it, and not to waver from it in any way. And He specified the face because it is the most honorable of the organs, or He commanded him to face the Qiblah in prayer and not to turn away from it. And Hanif is a state of religion, or of the face: meaning inclined from every religion to the religion of Islam. Then He emphasized the previous command to prohibit its opposite and said: "And do not be among the polytheists" and it is conjoined with establish, and it is from the category of allusion to someone other than the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
10:106: His statement: 106- And do not invoke besides God that which neither benefits you nor harms you is connected to Say, O people and is not included in the command. It was said that it is connected to And do not be meaning do not invoke besides God in any case that which neither benefits you nor harms you with any benefit or harm if you invoke it. And the invocation of one who is like this does not bring benefit, nor is able to cause harm, and is lost and no sane person would do it, assuming that there is no one who is able to cause benefit or harm other than him. So how about if he exists? For turning from the invocation of the able to the invocation of the incapable is uglier and uglier. Then if you do meaning if you invoke, but he used a metaphor for the saying with the action Then you would then be among the wrongdoers This is the reward of the condition: meaning if you invoke besides God that which neither benefits you nor harms you, then you are among those who wrong themselves. The purpose of this address is to allude to other than him, may God bless him and grant him peace.
10:107: And the sentence 107 - And if God should touch you with harm to the end confirms the content of what preceded it. The meaning is that God, the Exalted, is the One who harms and benefits. If He sends harm upon His servant, no one can remove it, whoever he may be. Rather, He is the One who is unique in removing it, just as He is unique in sending it down. And if He intends for you good means good, no one can repel it from you or come between you and it, whoever he may be. He used the word favor instead of good to indicate that He bestows upon His servants what they do not deserve through their deeds. Al-Wahidi said: His statement, And if He intends for you good is from the heart, and its root is and if He intends for you good, but since each of them is related to the other, it is permissible for each of them to be in place of the other. Al-Naysaburi said: In specifying the will with the side of good, and the touch with the side of evil, there is evidence that good comes from Him, the Exalted, intrinsically, and evil is by accident. I said: There is a consideration in this, because the touch is a matter beyond the will, so it entails it, and the pronoun in He afflicts with it refers to His grace: that is, He afflicts with His grace whomever He wills of His servants, and the phrase And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful is a tail.
10:108: Then he concluded this surah with what is used as evidence of His judgment and destiny, saying: 108- “Say, ‘O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord. Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment. ’” That is, the benefit of his guidance is specific to him, and the harm of his disbelief is limited to him and does not extend beyond him, and God has no need for any of that, nor does it serve any purpose. And I am not a guardian over you. That is, a guardian who preserves your affairs and entrusts them to Him: I am only a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
10:109: Then God the Almighty commanded him to follow what God revealed to him of the commands and prohibitions that God legislated for him and his nation, then He commanded him to be patient with the harm of the infidels and the hardships he faced in conveying the message and what he suffered from the changing morals of the polytheists and their arrogance, and He made that patience extend to an end, which is His saying: Until God judges, and He is the best of judges. That is, God judges between him and them in this world with victory for him over them, and in the Hereafter with their punishment in the Fire while they watch him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation, those who follow him and believe in him, who act according to what he commands them to do, and refrain from what he forbids them from doing, reveling in the bliss of Paradise that is inexhaustible, cannot be described, and the slightest of its advantages cannot be stopped at. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And signs and warnings do not avail a people he says: with a people who do not believe it abrogated his statement: A profound wisdom, so warnings do not avail. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Do they then await anything but the like of the days of those who passed on before them? he said: The events of God with those who passed on before them, the people of Noah, Aad and Thamud. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ regarding the verse, he said: He frightened them with His punishment, vengeance and chastisement, then He informed them that if something of that happened, God would save His messengers and those who believed, so He said: Then We will save Our messengers and those who believed the verse. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And if God intends for you good, he says: With well-being. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha’b on the authority of Amer bin Qais who said: Three verses in the Book of God have satisfied me with them for all of creation: The first: “And if God touches you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He intends for you good, there is no repeller of His favor.” The second: Whatever mercy God opens for mankind, there is none who can withhold it, and whatever He withholds, there is none who can release it. The third: There is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated something similar from Al-Hasan. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And none can repel His favor, he said: It is the truth mentioned in His statement: The truth has come to you from your Lord. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated regarding his statement: And be patient until God decides, he said: This is abrogated, he ordered him to fight them and be harsh with them.
11:1: It is Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: Except for one verse, which is His statement: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day. An-Nahhas in his Naskh, Abu Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Surah Hud was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr. Ad-Darimi, Abu Dawud in his Marasil, Abu Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Asakir and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ka'b who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Recite Hud on Friday. Ibn Al-Mundhir, At-Tabarani, Abu Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Abu Bakr As-Siddiq who said: I said: O Messenger of God, your gray hair hastened, so he said: Hud, Al-Waqi'ah, Al-Mursalat, 'Amma Yatas'alun, and Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat have made my gray hair turn white. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Anas on his authority, with the wording: I said: O Messenger of God, your gray hair hastened. He said: Hud and its sisters, Al-Waqi’ah, Al-Haqqah, ‘Amma Yatas’aloon, and Has there come to you the hadith of the Overwhelming? Sa’id ibn Mansur and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your gray hair hastened. He said: Hud and its sisters from the Mufassal have made my gray hair. At-Tirmidhi narrated it and classed it as hasan, Ibn al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim narrated it and classed it as saheeh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba’th wa Al-Nushur on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, your gray hair hastened. He said: Hud, Al-Waqi’ah, Al-Mursalat, ‘Amma Yatas’aloon, and Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat have made my gray hair. Ibn ‘Asakir narrated on the authority of ‘Ata’ on his authority that the Companions said: O Messenger of God, your gray hair hastened. He said: Yes, Hud and its sisters have made my gray hair. ‘Ata’ said: Its sisters: The Hour has drawn near, Al-Mursalat, and Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala'il on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri who said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab said: O Messenger of God, your gray hair has come quickly to you. He said: "Hud and its sisters: Al-Waqi'ah, 'Amma Yatas'aloon, and Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat have made my gray hair." Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa'd Al-Sa'idi who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Hud and its sisters: Al-Waqi'ah, Al-Haqqah, and Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat have made my gray hair." They also narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud that Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, what has made your gray hair? He said: Hud and Al-Waqi'ah. In its chain of transmission is 'Amr ibn Thabit who is rejected. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a saheeh chain of transmission on the authority of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir that a man said: O Messenger of God, my gray hair has come to you. He said: Hud, Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat and its sisters have made my gray hair. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir Al-Usul, Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd, Abu Ya’la, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Juhaifa who said: They said: O Messenger of God, we see that you have grown old. He said: Hud and its sisters have made my hair grey. Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Imran bin Husayn that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Your hair has turned grey quickly. He said: Hud and its sisters from Al-Mufassal have made my hair grey. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ja’far bin Muhammad on the authority of his father that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hud and its sisters have made my hair grey, and what was done to the nations before me. His saying: 1- Alif, Lam, Ra if it is listed in a way of enumeration as in all the openings of the surahs then it has no place, and if it is the name of the surah then it is in the place of raising as a subject whose predicate is what comes after it or the predicate of a deleted subject, and Kitab in this way is the predicate of a deleted subject: i.e. this is a book and likewise on the assumption that Alif, Lam, Ra has no place, and it is permissible for Alif, Lam, Ra to be in the place of the accusative by estimating a verb that suits the situation such as: remember, or read, so Kitab in this way is the predicate of a deleted subject, and the reference in the estimated subject is either to some of the Qur’an or to the entire Qur’an, and the meaning of Ihkmat Ayatuhu is that it became decisive and perfect with no deficiency or violation in it like a decisive construction, and it was said that its meaning is: it was not abrogated unlike the Torah and the Gospel, and based on this this description of the book is based on the majority, which is decisive that was not abrogated, and it was said that its meaning is: its verses were decisive with commands and prohibitions, then they were separated with promise and threat and reward and punishment, and it was said: God perfected it from falsehood, then separated it with what is lawful and what is unlawful. It was said: He perfected His entirety, then separated His verses. It was said: They were collected in the Preserved Tablet, then separated by revelation. It was said: They were supported by conclusive evidence indicating that they are from God. It was said: The meaning of perfecting it is that there is no corruption in it, taken from their saying: The beast is perfected: if wisdom is placed upon it to prevent it from running wild. Then it is separated is conjoined with perfected, and its meaning is what was mentioned above. The delay derived from then is either temporal if the separation is interpreted as astrology according to interests, or sequential if it is interpreted with something other than what was mentioned above. The sentences are in the nominative case as an attribute of a book or another predicate for the subject or predicate for a deleted subject. In His saying: From the Wise, All-Knowing, there is twisting and spreading, because the meaning is: He perfected it, and He separated it, All-Knowing, the Knower of the locations of matters.
11:2: His saying: 2- "That you worship none but God" is an object from which the lam was deleted: thus in Al-Kashshaf, and in it it is not a verb for the agent of the reasoned verb, and it was said: that it is the explanation of what is in the details of the meaning of the saying, and it was said: it is a statement of the beginning disconnected from what preceded it, narrated on the tongue of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: The meaning is I have determined that you worship none but God. Al-Zajjaj said: I have determined then detailed so that you worship none but God, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them that he is a warner and a bringer of good tidings, so he said: "Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings" meaning he warns them and frightens them from His punishment for those who disobey Him and gives them good tidings of Paradise and pleasure for those who obey Him, and the pronoun in from Him refers to God, the Most High: meaning I am to you a warner and a bringer of good tidings from the side of God, the Most High, and it was said: it is from the speech of God, the Most High, like His saying: "And God warns you of Himself.
11:3: His statement: 3- And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord is connected to that you do not worship, and the discussion is that this is like the discussion of the previous one. And his statement: Then repent to Him is connected to seek forgiveness, and guidance to seeking forgiveness was presented before repentance because it is a means to it, and it was said: Repentance is one of the complements to seeking forgiveness, and it was said: The meaning of seeking forgiveness is repent, and the meaning of repent is: be sincere in repentance and be steadfast in it, and it was said: seek forgiveness for past sins then repent for future ones, and it was said: seek forgiveness for polytheism then return to Him in obedience. Al-Farra’ said: “Then here, with the meaning of the waw, that is, repent to Him because seeking forgiveness is repentance and repentance is seeking forgiveness. It was said: The mention of seeking forgiveness was brought forward because forgiveness is the desired goal, and repentance is the reason for it, and that which was last in obtaining was first in seeking. It was said: Seek forgiveness for minor sins and repent to Him for major sins. Then He arranged two matters based on what came before, the first: “He will grant you good enjoyment.” The root of enjoyment is to prolong, and from it is God granted you enjoyment. So the meaning of the verse is: He will prolong your benefit in this world with good and pleasing benefits from abundant provision and comfortable living for a specified term, until a time determined by God, which is death. It was said: The Resurrection, and it was said: Entering Paradise, and the first is more appropriate. The second matter is the statement: And He will give every possessor of virtue his virtue, meaning He will give every possessor of virtue in obedience and action his virtue: meaning the reward for his virtue, either in this world or in the Hereafter or in both. The pronoun in His virtue refers to every possessor of virtue. It was said: It refers to God Almighty, meaning that God gives everyone whose good deeds are superior His virtue with which He bestows favor upon His servants. Then He threatened them for disobeying the command, saying: But if you turn away, meaning if you turn away and turn away from sincerity in worship, seeking forgiveness, and repentance, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great Day, which is the Day of Resurrection. He described it as great because of the horrors in it. It was said: The great day is the Day of Badr.
11:4: Then the Almighty explained the torment of the Great Day by saying: 4- To God is your return meaning your return to Him through death, then resurrection, then recompense, not to anyone else and He is over all things competent and part of that is your torment for not complying, and this sentence confirms what came before it.
11:5: Then God the Almighty informed that this warning, caution and threat did not work on them, nor did their hearts soften to it, but they persist in their stubbornness and are determined to disbelieve, so He said, as a source for this information, the word warning, which indicates astonishment at their state, and that it is a matter that the wise should be aware of and understand: 5- Indeed, they turn their breasts away. It is said: He turned his breast away from something: if he turned away from it and deviated from it, so the speech is a metaphor for turning away, because whoever turns away from something turns his chest away from it and folds his flank from it, and it was said that its meaning is: they turn their breasts towards what is in it of disbelief and turning away from the truth, so the speech is a metaphor for concealing what they believe of disbelief as was the habit of the hypocrites. The second aspect is more appropriate, and it is supported by his saying: So that they may hide from Him, meaning that they may hide from God so that His Messenger and the believers do not see it, or that they may hide from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he repeated the word of warning, explaining the time when they would fold their chests, saying: Not when they cover themselves with their garments, meaning that they would hide at the time of covering themselves with garments, which is covering themselves with them. They used to say, If we close our doors and cover ourselves with our garments and fold our chests in enmity to Muhammad, then who will know about us? It was said: The meaning of when they cover themselves is when they go to bed and cover themselves with their clothes. It was said: It is the reality, and that is because some of the infidels, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by, would bend their chests and turn their backs and cover themselves with their clothes so that he would not hear the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The phrase He knows what they conceal and what they declare is a new sentence to clarify that there is no benefit to them in concealing, because God, the Exalted, knows what they conceal in themselves or in what is between them and what they reveal. The apparent and the hidden are the same to Him, and the secret and the public are the same. The phrase He is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts is an explanation of what preceded it and a confirmation of it. The what is in the breasts are the pronouns that the breasts contain. It was said that they are the hearts. The meaning is: He is All-Knowing of all pronouns, or He is All-Knowing of the hearts and their states in secret and in public, so nothing of that is hidden from Him.
11:6: Then he confirmed that he is knowledgeable of all information, including the utmost gratitude and the ultimate benevolence, saying: 6- And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision meaning the provision that it needs of food appropriate for animals of all kinds, as a favor and benevolence from Him. It was brought in the way of obligation, as is indicated by the word upon in consideration of the previous promise of it from Him, and from is redundant for emphasis. The connection of this statement to what came before it is that since God, the Exalted, does not neglect every animal in consideration of what He has apportioned for it of provision, how could He neglect its conditions, words, and actions? A creature is every animal that moves, and He knows its resting place meaning its place of settlement in the earth or its place of settlement in the loins, and its place of storage its location in the wombs, and what comes after it, such as the egg and the like. Al-Farra’ said: Its resting place is where it takes refuge during the night and the day, and its warehouse is the place where it dies. The full statements have been mentioned in Surat Al-An’am. The reason for the precedence of the settled place over the warehouse according to Al-Farra’ is clear. As for the first statement, perhaps the reason for that is that the settled place is more appropriate considering what it is like when it is an animal. The meaning is: There is no animal on earth but that God provides for it wherever it is in its places after it was an animal and before it was an animal, and that is when it is in the womb and the like. Then he concluded the verse by saying: All is in a clear book, meaning all of what was mentioned above of the animals and their resting place, warehouse, and provision are in a clear book, which is the Preserved Tablet, meaning it is recorded in it.
11:7: Then he confirmed the evidence of His power by mentioning the creation of the heavens and the earth, and how things were before their creation, so he said: 7- And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days. This was explained previously in Al-A'raf. It was said: What is meant by days is times: that is, in six times, as in His statement: And whoever turns his back to them that Day. It was also said: the amount of six days. It is not correct that what is meant by days here is the known days, which are the equivalent of the nights, because at that time there was neither earth nor sky, and the day is nothing but an expression for the period of time that the sun was above the earth. The creation of the heavens was in two days, and the earths in two days, and what was on them of the types of animals, plants, and inanimate objects in two days, as will come in Ha Mim As-Sajdah. His statement: And His Throne was over the water means that before their creation, His Throne was over the water, and in it is a statement of the precedence of the creation of the Throne and the water over the heavens and the earths. His statement: To test you, which of you is best in deed. The lām is related to khalq, meaning He created these creatures to test His servants with consideration, contemplation, and reasoning about the perfection of His power and about resurrection and reward, which of them is better in deed than others. Belief is included in deed, because it is from the deeds of the heart. It was said that what is meant by best deed is the one who is most perfect in intellect, and it was said that it is the one who is most ascetic in this world, and it was said that it is the one who is most grateful, and it was said that it is the one who is most pious to God. His statement: And if you were to say, Indeed, you will be resurrected after death, those who disbelieve would say, This is not but obvious magic." Then since the test includes talk about resurrection, He followed that with mentioning it, and the meaning is: If you were to say to them, O Muhammad, as the issue of the test requires, "You will be resurrected after death, then He will reward the good-doer for his good and the evil-doer for his evil, those who disbelieved among the people would say, This that you say, O Muhammad, is nothing but falsehood like the falsehood of magic and a deception like its deception." It is possible that the reference in this is to the Qur'an, because it includes report of resurrection. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read This is nothing but magic, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The in of his saying you was broken because it came after the saying. Sibawayh reported the opening on the basis of I said including the meaning of I mentioned, or on the basis that an means perhaps, meaning And if you said, perhaps you will be resurrected. The hope is based on the state of those being addressed, meaning expect that, and do not base the statement on denying it.
11:8: 8- And if We delay the punishment from them meaning that which was mentioned previously in His statement: The punishment of a great Day and it was said the punishment of the Day of Resurrection and what comes after it, and it was said the Day of Badr to a limited number of days meaning to a group of few days, because what is limited by the number is little, and the nation is derived from the mother: which is the intention, and what is meant by it is the intended time for the punishment to be inflicted, and it was said: it is originally a group of people, and the time may be called by the name of what occurs in it like your saying I was with so-and-so at the afternoon prayer: meaning at that time, so what is meant by this is until a limited number of people pass they will say, 'What is holding it back' meaning what is preventing it from descending in order to hasten it in a mocking and denying manner, so God answered them by saying: Behold, the Day will come upon them, it will not be averted from them meaning it will not be averted from them, but will inevitably befall them, and the Day is governed by the object of the verb and that which they used to ridicule will encompass them meaning it will encompass them The punishment they were hastening was in mockery of them. He used the word mocking instead of hastening, because their hastening was in mockery of them. He used the past tense to indicate that it would happen, as if it had already overtaken them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd that he recited: A Book whose verses are perfected. He said: They are all perfect, meaning Surah Hud. Then they are explained in detail. He said: Then he mentioned Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he judged between him and those who disagreed with him, and he recited the entire verse like the two groups, then he mentioned the people of Noah, then Hud. This was the explanation of that, and its beginning was perfect. He said: My father used to say that, meaning Zayd ibn Aslam. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement: A Book whose verses are perfected. He said: They are perfected with commands and prohibitions, and explained with promises and threats. And these narrated on the authority of Mujahid: It is explained. He said: It is explained. These people also narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: God made it perfect from falsehood, then He separated it with His knowledge, so He made clear what is lawful and unlawful, and His obedience and disobedience. And regarding His statement, from the presence of a Wise One, meaning from a Wise One. And regarding His statement, He will grant you good enjoyment, he said: So you are in that enjoyment, so take it through obedience to God and knowledge of His right, for God is the Giver of favors and loves the grateful, and the grateful are in more from God, and that is His decree that He has decreed. And regarding His statement, for a specified term, meaning death. And regarding His statement, He will give to every possessor of virtue his virtue, meaning in the Hereafter. And these people also narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement, He will give to every possessor of virtue his virtue, meaning in the Hereafter. And Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, he said: Every possessor of virtue in Islam will be given the virtue of degrees in the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement: And every possessor of virtue will be given his virtue, he said: Whoever does a bad deed, a bad deed will be recorded against him, and whoever does a good deed, ten good deeds will be recorded for him. If he is punished for the bad deed he did in this world, ten good deeds will remain for him. If he is not punished for it in this world, one of the ten good deeds will be taken away and nine good deeds will remain for him. Then he says: He is destroyed whose one-tenths outweigh his one-tenths. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, they fold their breasts, the verse, he said: They were ashamed to relieve themselves and go to the sky, and to have intercourse with their wives and go to the sky, so this was revealed about them. Al-Bukhari said: And on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, they cover their heads means they cover their heads. Al-Bukhari also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his interpretation of this verse, meaning doubt in God and doing evil deeds. It was also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Hasan and others: That is, they would turn their chests when they said or did something, thinking that they were hiding it from God. So God informed them that when they covered themselves with their garments when they slept in the darkness of the night, He knows what they conceal of speech and what they declare. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Haad regarding his statement, Indeed, they turn their chests, he said: When the hypocrites passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would turn his chest and cover himself with his garment so that he would not see him, so this was revealed. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, Indeed, when they cover themselves with their garments, he said: In the darkness of the night in the interior of their homes. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Razin regarding the verse, he said: One of them would bend his back and cover himself with his garment. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: They concealed their chests so that they would not hear the Book of God. God the Almighty said: {Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal.} That is the most concealed of the son of Adam when he bends his back and covers himself with his garment and conceals his concern in himself, for God does not hide that from Him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said regarding the verse: They conceal what is in their hearts. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they did by night and by day. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: {And there is no creature} the verse, he said: It means every creature. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: {And there is no creature} the verse, he said: It means whatever provision comes to it is from God, and perhaps He does not provide it until it dies of hunger, but whatever provision it has is from God. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And He knows its place of rest, he said: Where it takes refuge, and its place of deposit, he said: Where it dies. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: And He knows its place of rest, he said: Its provision comes to it wherever it is. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, he said: Its place of rest is in the wombs and its place of deposit is where it dies. This interpretation mentioned by Ibn Mas’ud is supported by what was narrated by al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim in Nawadir al-Usul, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “When the term of one of you is in a land, a need will be made available to him there, until when he reaches the furthest point of it, he is taken away, and the earth will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:This is what you entrusted to me.” Abdul Razzaq in Al-Musannaf, Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the statement: And His Throne was over the water, on what was the water? He said: On the wind. Many hadiths have been narrated about the description of the Throne and how the heavens and the earth were created, but this is not the place to mention them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim in Al-Tarikh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited this verse: That He may test you which of you is best in deed. It was said: What is the meaning of that, O Messenger of God? He said: That He may test you which of you is best in intellect. Then he said: And the best of you in intellect is the most pious of you in avoiding the forbidden things of God and the most devoted to obeying God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said: Which of you has the most perfect intellect? He also narrated on the authority of Sufyan that he said: The most ascetic of you in this world. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said: When the verse: The reckoning of the people has drawn near was revealed. Some people said: The Hour has drawn near, so they desisted. The people desisted for a while, then they returned to their evil deeds. Then God revealed: The command of God has come, so do not hasten it. Some of the people of misguidance said: This is the command of God that has come. The people desisted, then they returned to their evil plotting. Then God revealed this verse: And if We should delay the punishment from them for a specified term. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: for a specified term, he said: for a specified term. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah: “He will say: What is holding it back?” meaning the hypocrites. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: And that which they used to ridicule overtook them, he said: the punishment which they used to ridicule befell them.
11:9: The lam in 9- And if We let man taste is the introduction to the oath, and man is the species, so it includes the believer and the disbeliever, and this exception is indicated by His saying: Except those who are patient and it was said that what is meant is the species of disbelievers, and this is supported by the fact that despair, disbelief, joy and pride are descriptions of the people of disbelief, not the people of Islam in most cases, and it was said that what is meant by man is Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, and it was said: Abdullah bin Umayyah Al-Makhzumi. What is meant by mercy here is the blessing of providing sustenance, health and safety from hardships. Then We took it away from him means We deprived him of it. Indeed, he is despairing meaning he is hopeless of mercy, very hopeless of its return and the like. The ungrateful person is extremely ungrateful, which is to deny it. This was said by Ibn al-A’rabi. In the two forms of exaggeration in despairing, ungrateful there is what indicates that a person is very hopeless and very ungrateful when God takes away some of His blessings from him, so he does not hope for their return, nor is he grateful for what he has already received. And in the expression taste there is what indicates that this happens when the slightest blessing that God bestows upon him is taken away, because tasting and tasting are the least of what taste can be found in.
11:10: And the blessing is a favor whose effect is apparent on its owner, and the hardship is the appearance of the effect of harm on the one who was afflicted by it. The meaning is: If God the Almighty lets the servant taste His blessings of health, safety, and wealth after he was in hardship of poverty, sickness, or fear, he does not respond to that with what is appropriate for him of thanks to God the Almighty, but rather he says the bad things are gone: meaning the calamities that distressed him of hardship, poverty, fear, and sickness and their effect is gone, not thanking God or praising Him for His blessings. 10- Indeed, he is joyful and boastful meaning very joyful with arrogance and evil, very proud of people and arrogant towards them for the blessings that God bestows upon him, and in expressing the association of hardship with him by touching is appropriate to expressing the aspect of blessings by tasting, because both are the lowest thing that is called encounter, as mentioned above.
11:11: 11- Except those who are patient for their habit is patience when trials befall them, and gratitude when blessings are received. Al-Akhfash said: It is an exception not from the first: that is, but those who are patient and do righteous deeds in the states of blessing and trial. Al-Farra' said: It is an exception from if we let him taste: that is, from man, for man means people, and people include the disbeliever and the believer, so it is a connected exception, and the reference in his saying: those to the relative pronoun is in consideration of his being characterized by patience and doing righteous deeds. For them is forgiveness for their sins and a reward with which they will be rewarded for their good deeds great, exceedingly great.
11:12: Then God, the Most High, consoled His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: 12- Perhaps you are abandoning some of what is revealed to you meaning perhaps, due to the greatness of what you see from them of disbelief and denial, and the suggestion of the verses that they suggest to you according to their whims and their stubbornness, you are abandoning some of what is revealed to you of what God sent down to you and commanded you to convey, which is difficult for them to hear or which they find difficult to act upon, earning their gods and commanding them to believe in God alone. It was said: This statement is outside the context of a question: meaning are you abandoning? It was said: It is in the meaning of negation with exclusion: that is, that will not happen from you, but you will convey to them all that God has revealed to you, whether they like it or dislike it, whether they like it or not. And your breast is constricted by it is in apposition to abandoning, and the pronoun in by it refers to what or some, and He expressed it with constriction rather than distress because the active participle has the meaning of occurrence and occurrence, and the adjective has the meaning of necessity. That they say meaning, disliking to say, or fearing to say, or lest they say: Why was a treasure not sent down to him? meaning, why was a treasure not sent down to him: that is, stored, preserved money that can be used. Or an angel came with him who would confirm him and show us the truth of his message. Then the Almighty explained that his state, may God bless him and grant him peace, was limited to warning, so He said: You are only a warner, all that is required of you is to warn you of what has been revealed to you, and you are not required to fulfill their request or fulfill their proposals. And God is a Disposer of affairs, He preserves what they say and He does to them what He must do.
11:13: His statement: 13- Or do they say, 'He invented it'? "Am is the disconnected particle that means rather" and the hamza, and he struck out what came before about their negligence of the revelation, and their lack of contentment with what it brought of apparent miracles, and he began to mention their committing what is worse than that, which is their fabrication against him that he invented it, and the question is for rebuke and reprimand, and the hidden pronoun in "he invented it" for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the apparent one refers to what is revealed. Then God, the Most High, commanded him to answer them with what would sever their ties, reveal their lies, and demonstrate their inability, so He said: “Say: Then bring ten surahs like it,” meaning similar to it in eloquence, beauty of composition, richness of wording, magnificence of meanings, and describing the surahs with what is described as a single word. He said like them and did not say like them, because what is meant is the similarity of each one of the surahs, or to indicate the point of similarity, and its focus is similarity in one thing, which is eloquence reaching the level of miraculousness. This is only based on the statement that matching in the plural, dual, and singular is a condition. Then He described the surahs with another description, so He said: fabricated, and call upon, to demonstrate the opposition with the ten surahs, whomever you can, to call upon and are able to seek help from from this human kind, and from those whom you worship and make a partner with God, the Most High. And His statement: other than God is related to call upon, meaning call upon whomever you can, going beyond God, if you are truthful, in what you claim of my fabricating it.
11:14: 14- If they do not respond to you meaning if they do not do what you asked of them and challenged them to do by bringing ten surahs like it and they do not respond to the opposition required of them, and the pronoun in for you refers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers or to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone, and it is a collective expression of glorification and magnification. Then know is a command to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers or to the Messenger alone according to the interpretation that was mentioned earlier. The meaning of commanding them to know is commanding them to remain steadfast in it because they know that before the infidels were unable to bring ten surahs like it, or what is meant by the command to know is the command to increase it, to a level that is not tainted by doubt or mixed with suspicion, which is certain knowledge, and the first is more appropriate. The meaning of It was sent down with the knowledge of God is that it was sent down with the knowledge of God that is specific to Him, the essence of which cannot be comprehended by the minds nor its meaning clarified by the understandings, because it contains a miracle that is beyond the capacity of human beings. And that there is no god but He means, know that God is the One and Only in divinity, with no partner, and no one else is able to do what He is able to do. Then He concluded the verse by saying: Are you then Muslims? meaning, steadfast in Islam, sincere in it, increasing in acts of obedience, because the infidels’ inability to produce even ten Surahs of this Book has given you peace of mind and increased insight. If you were Muslims before this, then steadfastness in it, increased insight in it, and peace of mind are required of you. It was said that the pronoun in If they do not respond refers to the relative pronoun in whoever you are able to, and the pronoun for you refers to the infidels whom the Messenger of God challenged, and the pronoun for know is the same. Meaning: If those whom you called for support and assistance in bringing ten Surahs from all the infidels and those whom they worship, and claim that they can both harm and benefit, do not respond to you, then know that this Qur’an that God sent down to this Messenger is beyond the power of anyone other than Him, glory be to Him, because it contains miracles that the power of created beings cannot comprehend, and that it was sent down with the knowledge of God that minds cannot comprehend nor can understandings reach. And know that He is the One and Only in divinity, with no partner for Him. So are you Muslims after this? That is, have you entered Islam, followed its rulings, and emulated its laws. This aspect is stronger than the first aspect in one respect and weaker in another. As for its strength, it is not because the pronouns are consistent and compatible and some of them do not need interpretation. As for its weakness, it is because the arrangement of the command to know the lack of response from those you call upon and seek help from is hidden and requires effort, which is to say: The lack of response from those you call upon and seek help from among the infidels and deities, despite their eagerness to support and assist them and their exaggeration in their lack of faith and their persistence in disbelief, indicates that these infidels have acquired knowledge that this Qur’an is from God, and that God, the Exalted, is the only God with no partner, and that necessitates their entering Islam. Know that the challenge to the infidels to oppose the Qur’an has varied. Sometimes it occurred with the entire Qur’an, as in His statement: “Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur’an, they could not produce it.” And with ten surahs, as in this verse, because ten is the first decade of the decades, and with a surah from it, as mentioned above, because a surah is the smallest group of it.
11:15: Then God, the Most High, threatened those whose ambitions are limited to this world, seeking nothing but it and desiring nothing but it, saying: 15- Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein. Al-Farra’ said: If this is redundant, then the answer is in the subjunctive mood. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever is in a subjunctive mood with the condition, and its answer is We fully repay them: meaning whoever desires. The commentators differed regarding this verse. Ad-Dahhak said: It was revealed about the disbelievers, and An-Nahhas chose it based on the evidence of the verse that follows it: Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire. It was said: The verse was revealed about people in general, disbelievers and Muslims alike. The meaning is that whoever desires the worldly reward through his actions will be rewarded for that. What is meant by its adornment is what adorns and beautifies it, such as health, security, abundance in provision, high fortune, effective speech, and the like. The inclusion of was in the verse indicates that they continue to desire the worldly reward through their actions, and they hardly desire the Hereafter. For this reason, it was said that even though they are given the fortunes of the world, they will be tormented in the Hereafter because they devoted their intention to the worldly reward and did not work for the Hereafter. The apparent meaning of His statement: We will fully repay them for their deeds therein is that whoever desires the worldly reward through his actions will inevitably obtain the worldly reward, but the reality on the outside is contrary to that. Not every wisher will attain his wish from the worldly reward, even if he works for it and desires it. It is necessary to restrict that to the will of God, the Most High. Al-Qurtubi said: Most scholars have said that this verse is absolute, as is the verse in al-Shura 42:Whoever desires the cultivation of this world, We give him thereof, and also And whoever desires the reward of this world, We give him thereof, which is qualified and explained by the verse in Subhan: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whomever We intend. His statement: and they therein will not be diminished, meaning, and these people who desire their worldly deeds are in it: meaning, in this world, they will not be diminished: meaning, their reward therein will not be reduced according to their deeds for it, and this is usually not constant, rather if His will, glory be to Him, decrees it and His perfect wisdom favors it. Al-Qadi said: The meaning of the verse is: Whoever desires by doing good deeds the life of this world and its adornments, We will fully repay them for their deeds without diminishing them in this world, which is what they attain of health, sufficiency, and all other pleasures and benefits. So He specified the reward with something similar to what He mentioned, and it is obtained by every worker for this world, even if it is little and insignificant.
11:16: His statement: 16- Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire refers to the aforementioned seekers, and it is necessary to restrict this to the fact that they did not desire the Hereafter with any of the deeds that are considered to be good rewards in the Hereafter, or the verse is specific to the disbelievers as mentioned above. And what they did was in vain meaning that what they did of deeds that were in the form of acts of obedience that necessitate the Hereafter's reward was made in vain in the Hereafter, had it not been for the fact that they corrupted them with the corruption of their intentions, lack of sincerity, and desire for what is with God in the Hereafter, but rather they limited that to this world and its adornments, then the Almighty ruled that their work was in vain and said: And what they did was in vain meaning that their work was in itself in vain and not considered, because it was not done for a correct reason that necessitates reward, and what results from correct work results from it.
11:17: His statement: 17- Is he who has clear evidence from his Lord? God the Almighty made clear that there is a great difference and a far-reaching contrast between he who seeks only this world and he who seeks the Hereafter. The meaning is: Is he who has clear evidence from his Lord in following the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believing in God like others who desire the worldly life and its adornments? It was said: What is meant by he who has clear evidence from his Lord is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: that is, is he who has a statement from God and a miracle like the Qur'an and a witness like Gabriel, and the previous books gave glad tidings of him, like he who desires the worldly life and its adornments? The meaning of clear evidence is the proof that indicates the truth, and the pronoun in His statement: and a witness recites it refers to clear evidence in consideration of its interpretation as proof, and the pronoun in from it refers to the Qur'an, because it was mentioned previously in His statement: Or do they say, 'He has invented it' or it refers to God the Almighty. Meaning: And the proof, which is the evidence, is followed by a witness who testifies to its authenticity from the Qur’an, or from God, the Most High. And the witness is the miracle in the Qur’an, or the miracles that appeared to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for that is from the witnesses that follow the Qur’an. Al-Farra’ said: Some of them said: And a witness from it follows it, the Gospel, and if it was before it, then it follows the Qur’an in confirmation, and the ha in from it is for God, the Most High. And it was said: What is meant by those who have evidence from their Lord are the believers among the People of the Book, such as Abdullah bin Salam and his likes. His statement: And before it the Book of Moses is connected to the witness, and the meaning is: And the witness is followed by another witness from before it, which is the Book of Moses, so even if it was revealed before it, it follows the witness in testimony, and the witness was presented before the Book of Moses despite it being later in existence because it is a necessary description that does not separate, so it was more immersed in description than the Book of Moses. And the meaning of the testimony of the Book of Moses, which is the Torah, is that it gave good tidings of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed that he is a Messenger from God. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: And before him follows the Book of Moses, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is described in the Book of Moses, which they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. Abu Hatim narrated from some of them that he read: And before him the Book of Moses in the accusative case, and Al-Mahdawi narrated it from Al-Kalbi, so it is conjoined with the ha’ in yataluhu. The meaning is: And Gabriel follows the Book of Moses, and the accusative of Imam and Mercy is in the state. The Imam is the one who is followed in religion and emulated, and Mercy is the great blessing that God bestowed upon those upon whom He revealed it and upon those after them, considering what it contains of legal rulings that agree with the ruling of the Qur’an, and the reference in His saying: those is to those who are described with that virtuous characteristic, which is being upon the clear evidence from God, and the demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is they believe in him meaning they believe in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or in the Qur’an, and whoever disbelieves in him from the parties meaning in the Prophet or in the Qur’an. And the parties who are partisan against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the people of Mecca and others, or the parties from the people of all religions, the Fire is his appointed time, meaning he is one of the people of the Fire without fail. And in making the Fire his appointed time, there is an indication that in it are types of torment that cannot be described, and similar to it is the saying of Hassan: You brought her to the pools of death while she was awake, so the fire is her appointment and death will meet her. So be not in doubt about it meaning, do not be in doubt about the Qur’an. This is an allusion to someone other than him, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is protected from doubting the Qur’an or the promise. It is the truth from your Lord. There is no room for doubt in it under any circumstances. But most people do not believe in that, despite the obligation to believe in it and the emergence of evidence that requires it. However, they are stubborn, despite their knowledge that it is the truth, or that it has been sealed in their hearts so that they do not understand that it is the truth at all. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: So are you Muslims? He said: To the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas regarding his statement: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, he said: It was revealed about the Jews and Christians. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Ma’bad who said: A man stood up to Ali and said: Tell us about this verse: Whoever desires the life of this world to His statement: And what they used to do is futile, he said: Woe to you, that is for whoever desires the life of this world, not the Hereafter. An-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Whoever desires the life of this world meaning its reward and its adornments its wealth We will fully repay them We provide them with health and happiness in family, wealth and children and therein they will not be deprived they will not be diminished. Then it was abrogated by: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will the verse. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Suddi. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: Whoever does righteous deeds - seeking this world, fasting, praying, or staying up at night - and does nothing but seek this world, God says: Or in it is what he sought in this world. And his work that he used to do will be in vain, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: This verse was revealed about the polytheists. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding His statement, We will fully repay them for their deeds, he said: Their good deeds. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Ibn Jurayj. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding His statement, And whatever they did therein will be in vain, he said: Whatever good they did will be in vain and will be void in the Hereafter, and they will have no reward in it. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: They are the people of hypocrisy. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu`aym narrated in Al-Ma`rifah on the authority of Ali Ibn Abi Talib, he said: There was no man from Quraysh except that a portion of the Qur’an was revealed about him, so a man said to him: What was revealed about you? He said: Do you not read Surah Hud, Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord and a witness from Him recites it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it? Ibn Asakir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from another chain of transmission on his authority that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord, I, and a witness from Him recites it, Ali? Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding his statement, Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord? He said: That is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Ibrahim. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali bin Abi Talib that he said: I said to my father: People claim regarding the statement of God, the Most High, and a witness from Him recites it, that you are the one who recites it. He said: I wish I was him, but it is the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the witness is Gabriel, and Saeed bin Jubair agreed with him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Gabriel is a witness from God regarding what he recites of the Book of God that was revealed to Muhammad. And before it was the Book of Moses. He said: And before it was the Torah on the tongue of Moses, just as the Qur’an was recited on the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Ibn Ali regarding his statement: And a witness from Him recites it. He said: Muhammad is the witness from God. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibrahim, And before it was the Book of Moses. He said: And before it was the Book that came to Moses. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada, And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties. He said: The disbelievers are parties, all of them are in disbelief. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties. He said: Of the Jews and Christians.
11:18: His statement: 18- "And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God?" That is, no one is more unjust than them to themselves because they invent a lie against God by saying to their idols: These are our intercessors with God, and their saying: The angels are the daughters of God, and they attributed His words to others, and although the wording only requires the denial of the existence of someone more unjust than them, as is indicated by the rhetorical question, the situation indicates the denial of those who are equal to them in injustice. So the meaning according to this is: No one is like them in injustice, let alone that there is someone more unjust than them, and the reference in His statement "those" is to those described with extreme injustice, and it is a subject, and its predicate is that they will be presented before their Lord, and He will hold them accountable for their deeds, or what is meant by their presentation is the presentation of their deeds. "And the witnesses will say, 'These are the ones who lied against their Lord.'" The witnesses are the guardian angels, and it was said that they are the messengers. It was said that it is the angels, messengers, and scholars who conveyed what God commanded them to convey, and it was said that it is all of creation. The meaning is that these witnesses will say when they are presented: These are the ones who are exposed or whose deeds are presented who lied about their Lord by what they attributed to Him and did not state what they lied about as if it was a known matter to the people of that situation. His statement: Indeed, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers is part of the speech of the witnesses: that is, they say: These are the ones who lied about their Lord, and they say: Indeed, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers who wronged themselves by fabricating. It is possible that it is from the speech of God, the Most High, that He said it after the witnesses said: These are the ones who lied about their Lord. And the witnesses is the plural of witness, and Abu Ali preferred it due to the frequent occurrence of witness in the Qur’an, like His statement: And the Messenger will be a witness over you. “How then will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you as a witness over these?” It was said: It is the plural of witness like companions and friend, and the benefit of the witnesses saying this statement is to exaggerate the disgrace of the infidels, and to rebuke them in front of all witnesses.
11:19: Then he described these oppressors who were cursed as 19- those who avert [people] from the path meaning they prevent those they are able to prevent from the religion of God and from entering it and seek to make it crooked meaning they describe it as crooked in order to repel people from it, or they seek for its people to be crooked by deviating from it to disbelief. It is said, I sought evil for you meaning I sought it for you and the situation is that and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter meaning they describe it as crooked, and the situation is that they are not believers in the Hereafter, so how can they avert people from the path of truth while they are on pure falsehood? The repetition of the pronoun is to emphasize their disbelief and their exclusivity to it, as if the disbelief of others is not taken into account in comparison to the enormity of their disbelief.
11:20: 20- Those who are described with these attributes were not able to cause failure on earth meaning they could not cause failure for God in this world if He wanted to punish them and they had no protectors besides God to repel from them what God the Almighty wanted of their punishment and to bring down His wrath upon them. The phrase the punishment will be doubled for them is a new sentence to explain that delaying the punishment and delaying its hastening for them is to be a double punishment. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Yazid and Yaqub read the punishment will be doubled with emphasis they were not able to hear meaning they went to extremes in their turning away from the truth and hating it, to the point that it was as if they were unable to hear or see due to their extreme blindness to the truth. It is possible that what is meant by his saying: And they had no protectors besides God is that they made their gods protectors besides God, and that does not benefit them. These protectors were not able to hear, nor could they see, so how could they benefit them by bringing them benefit or repelling harm from them? It is possible that what is the extension is what is the extension. The meaning is that the punishment is doubled for them as long as they are able to hear and see. Al-Farra’ said: They were not able to hear because God led them astray in the Preserved Tablet. Al-Zajjaj said: Because of their hatred of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and their enmity towards him, they were unable to hear from him or understand from him. Al-Nahhas said: This is well-known in the speech of the Arabs. It is said: So-and-so cannot look at so-and-so, if he is too much for him.
11:21: 21- Those who have these qualities are those who have lost themselves by worshipping other than God. The meaning is: they bought the worship of gods with the worship of God, so their loss in their trade was the greatest loss. And what they used to invent has gone away from them, meaning what they used to invent of the gods that they claim would intercede for them has gone and been lost, and nothing remains in their hands except loss.
11:22: His saying: 22- La Jarm Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: La Jarm means Haqq, so according to them it is like one word, and Al-Farra' said the same. It was narrated from Al-Khalil and Al-Farra' that it is like saying La Bade wa La Mahala, then its use became so much that it became like Haqq. Al-Zajjaj said: That Jarm means Kasab: that is, that action earned them the loss, and the subject of Kasab is implied, and that is in the accusative case with rajm. Al-Azhari said: This is one of the best things that have been transmitted in this language. Al-Kisa'i said: The meaning of La Jarm is: There is no turning away or prevention from the fact that they are the greatest losers in the Hereafter. A group of grammarians said: The meaning of la jaram wa la qata’ qata’ is that in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers. They said: And jaram is severing, and jaram means cutting off the palm tree, meaning he cut it down. In this verse there is a statement that they are in loss and have reached a limit that others fall short of and cannot reach. These verses confirm what came before of denying the similarity between the one who wanted the life of this world and its adornments, and the one who was on clear evidence from his Lord.
11:23: 23- Indeed, those who have believed meaning, believed in everything that must be believed in, such as the Qur’an being from God and other characteristics of faith, and done righteous deeds and humbled themselves before their Lord meaning, turned to Him, and it was said, revered, and it was said, submissive. It was said: The origin of humility is to be level in the filth: which is the flat, spacious earth, so it fits the meaning of humility and reassurance. Al-Farra’ said: to their Lord, and their Lord is One. Those are described with those righteous attributes, are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein eternally.
11:24: His saying: 24- The example of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. He gave an example for the two groups, which is the comparison of the group of disbelievers to the blind and the deaf, and the comparison of the group of believers to the seeing and the hearing, on the basis that each group is likened to two things, or likened to someone who combined the two things. So the disbeliever is likened to someone who combined blindness and deafness, and the believer is likened to someone who combined hearing and sight. Based on this, the waw in and the deaf, and in and the hearing, is to connect the description to the description, as in the poet’s saying: To the venerable king and son of the hero The question in his statement: Are they equal? is for denial: meaning the two groups. This sentence confirms what came before in his statement: Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord? The accusative of for example is for distinguishing from the agent of are equal: meaning are they equal in state and description Do you not remember in their lack of equality and in what is between them of the apparent difference that is hidden from he who remembers and has thought and contemplation, and the hamza is for denying the lack of remembrance and the improbability of it coming from those addressed. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: And who is more unjust? He said: The disbeliever and the hypocrite. Those will be presented before their Lord, He will ask them about their deeds. And the witnesses will say, who used to record their deeds against them in this world, These are the ones who lied about their Lord, who will testify against them on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The witnesses are the angels. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah something similar. In the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Ibn Umar: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God brings the believer close until He places His protection and screens him from the people and makes him confess his sins and says to him: Do you recognize such-and-such sin? Do you recognize such-and-such sin? He says: My Lord, I know. Then when He makes him confess his sins and he sees in himself that he has perished, He says: I concealed them for you in this world and I forgive you today. Then he is given his book of good deeds. As for the disbeliever and the hypocrite, the witnesses will say: These are the ones who lied about their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.” Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: Those who hinder [people] from the way of God, he said: It is Muhammad, meaning the way of God, and the Quraysh hindered the people from it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: And they seek to make it crooked, meaning they hope for a religion other than Islam in Mecca. Ibn Jarir and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Those were not able to escape on earth, the verse. He said: God the Almighty informed that He stood between the polytheists and their obedience to Him in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, He said: They were not able to hear, nor were they able to see, and as for the Hereafter, He said: They were not able to * humbled. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: They were not able to hear, he said: They were not able to hear good and benefit from it, nor see good and take it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: They were afraid, he said: They were afraid. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: Submission is repentance. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Sheikh narrated that he said: Submission is humility and modesty. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: They were reassured. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The parable of the two parties is like that of the blind and the deaf, he said: the disbeliever. And the seeing and the hearing, he said: the believer.
11:25: When the Almighty mentioned to the unbelievers who were contemporary with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the types of evidence that are clearer than the sun, He emphasized that by mentioning the stories in a manner of skillful speech, and moving it from one style to another so that the sermon would be clearer, the argument more evident, and the acceptance more complete, so He said: 25- "And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Indeed, I am to you a clear warner. '" Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Al-Kisa'i read with the opening of the hamza on the assumption of the preposition: that is, We sent him with that speech, which is, 'Indeed, I am to you a clear warner.' The rest read with the breaking of the hamza on the meaning of the statement: that is, saying, 'Indeed, I am to you.' The waw in 'Indeed' is for the beginning, and the lam is the one that introduces the oath, and He limited it to the warning without the good report, because his call was merely a warning, or because they did not act upon what he had given them good report of.
11:26: And the sentence 26- That you worship none but God instead of Indeed, I am to you a clear warner: meaning, We sent him to not worship except God, or it could be an explanatory that related to We sent, or a warner, or a clear one. And the sentence Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day is causal.
