The meaning is: I forbade you from worshipping other than God because I fear for you, and in it is the realization of the meaning of the warning, and the painful day: is the Day of Resurrection, or the Day of the Flood, and describing it as painful is a metaphorical attribution of exaggeration.
11:27: Then he mentioned what his people answered him with, and this answer includes their attack on his prophethood from three aspects. He said: 27- Then the leaders of his people who disbelieved said and the leaders are the nobles as mentioned more than once, and he described them as disbelievers as a disparagement of them, and in it is evidence that some of the nobles of his people were not disbelievers We see you only as a human being like us This is the first aspect of their attack on his prophethood: that is, we and you share in humanity, so you did not have an advantage over us that would merit prophethood over us, and the second aspect: And we do not see you followed except by the lowest of us and none of the nobles followed you, so you have no advantage over us by these lowly people following you, and the lowest is the plural of ardal and ardhall is the plural of radhal like akaalib and aklab and kelb, and it was said that the lowest is the plural of ardhall like aswad is the plural of aswad, and they are the lowly. An-Nahhas said: the lowest are the poor and those who have no lineage, and lineage is the industries. Al-Zajjaj said: They attributed them to weaving, and they did not know that industries have no effect on religion. Tha’lab said on the authority of Ibn al-A’rabi: The lowly is the one who reforms the world with his religion. He was asked: Who is the lowly of the lowly? He said: The one who reforms the world of others with the corruption of his religion. What appears from the words of the linguists is that the lowly is the one who enters into the lowly letter, and the vision in both places if it is the heart, then Bashar in the first and Atabaka in the second are the second object, and if it is the vision, then they are in the accusative case as a state and the accusative case of Badi al-Ra’y is in the circumstance and the factor in it is Atabaka. The meaning is: in the apparent opinion without delving into it. It is said: Bada Bada’ if it appears. Al-Azhari said: Its meaning is in what appears to us from the opinion. The third aspect: From the aspects of their disparagement of his prophethood, And we do not see that you have any superiority over us, they addressed him in the first two aspects alone, and in this aspect they addressed him with his followers, meaning: We do not see that you and those who follow you from the lowly ones have any superiority over us by which they are distinguished and that you deserve what you claim. Then they turned away from the three objections and moved to their assumption devoid of proof, which has no basis except mere fanaticism, envy, and preserving what they have of worldly leadership, so they said: Rather, we think you are liars in what you claim. It is possible that this was addressed to the lowly ones alone, and the first is more appropriate, because the speech was with Noah, not with them except by way of following him.
11:28: Then the Almighty mentioned what Noah answered them with, saying: 28- He said, ‘O my people, have you considered, if I am on clear evidence from my Lord’ meaning, tell me, if I am on a proof from my Lord regarding prophethood that indicates its validity and requires you to accept it, even though what you have made a flaw is not a flaw in reality, for equality in the quality of humanity does not prevent difference in the quality of prophethood, and following the vile, as you claim, is not what prevents prophethood, for they are like you in humanity, reason, and understanding, so their following me is an argument against you, not for you. It is possible that he means by the proof the miracle and He has given me mercy from Himself which is prophethood, and it was said that mercy is the miracle, and the proof is prophethood. It was said: It is possible that mercy is the proof itself, and it is better to interpret mercy in a way other than what proof was interpreted, and the singular in fa’mait is to intend each of them, or to intend the proof, because it is what appears to the one who thinks and is hidden from the one who does not think, and the meaning of ‘‘amait’’ is ‘‘khafit’’, and it was said: Mercy is for creation, and it was said: It is guidance to knowledge of proof, and it was said: Faith, it is said: ‘‘amait’’ about such-and-such’’, and ‘‘amait’... Al-A'mash, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read Fa'mait with a damma on the 'ayn and a shaddah on the meem in the passive voice, meaning God made it blind to you. In Abu's reading, it is Fa'mait alaykum and the interrogative in Anlazimkumuha is for denial, meaning I cannot force you to know about it while you are averse to it. The meaning is tell me, if I have a clear proof of the truth of my prophethood but it is hidden from you, can we force you to know about it while you are averse to it and have not contemplated it? For no one is able to do that except God Almighty. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' narrated that the first meem in Anlazimkumuha is sukun for the sake of alleviation, as in the saying of the poet: Today I drink without deserving any sin from God nor being excessive. The sukoon of the letter Baa in Ashrab is for the sake of alleviation. Abu Amr read it like this.
11:29: His saying: 29- “And O my people, I do not ask of you any money for it. My reward is only from God.” This is an explicit statement from him, peace be upon him, that he does not ask for money for conveying the message, so that he would be subject to suspicion, and there would be room for the infidels to say that he only claimed what he claimed in pursuit of the world, and the pronoun in upon him refers to what he said to them before this. And His saying: And I will not drive away those who believe is like the answer to what is understood from their saying: And we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us from their hint to keeping the lowest of us away from him, and it was said that they asked him to drive them away explicitly, not implicitly, then he explained that by saying: Indeed, they will meet their Lord meaning I will not drive them away, for they will meet their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, so He will reward them for their faith because they sought with their faith what is with Him, glory be to Him, and it is as if he said this in order to show them respect, and it is possible that he said it out of fear of their quarreling with him before their Lord because of his driving them away, then he explained to them what they were upon in these demands that they asked of him and the reasons that they used to justify their answer to him, so he said: But I see you are a people who are ignorant of everything that should be known, including their despising of those who followed him and their asking him to drive them away.
11:30: Then he confirmed the impermissibility of expelling them by saying: 30- And O my people, who will protect me from God if I expel them? That is, who will protect me from God's punishment and vengeance if I expel them? For expelling them because they were the first to believe and respond to the call for which God sent His Messenger is a great injustice that does not occur from God's prophets who are supported by infallibility. If that had occurred from them as a hypothesis and as a presumption, it would have been an injustice that would not have occurred if it had been done by anyone other than them from among the people. His saying: Will you not remember? is connected to something presumed, as if it was said: Will you continue in your ignorance of what was mentioned? Will you not remember from their conditions what should be remembered and reflect on it so that you may know what you are doing wrong and what they are doing right.
11:31: His statement: 31- And I do not say to you that I have the treasures of God He explained to them that just as he does not ask them for anything from their money in order to convey the message, he does not claim that he has the treasures of God so that they can use their lack of it as evidence of his lying, as they said: And we do not see for you any favor over us What is meant by the treasures of God is the treasures of His provision. And I do not know the unseen meaning, I do not claim that I know the unseen of God, rather I only said to you that I am a clear warner, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day. And I do not say to you that I am an angel so that you say, We see you only as a human being like us. This was used as evidence by those who said that the angels are better than the prophets, and the evidence in this matter is different, and the seeker of the truth has no need to verify it, as it is not something that God has charged us with knowing. And I do not say to those whose eyes despise meaning that they despise, and despise is taken from the verb azra alayhi: if he finds fault with him, and zara alayhi: if he despises him, and al-Farra' recited: The friend distances himself, his mistress despises him, and the little one scolds him. Meaning: I do not say to those followers of mine who believe in God, whom you criticize and despise, God will never give them any good. Rather, He has given them great good through faith in Him and following His Prophet. He will reward them with a great reward in the Hereafter and will raise them in this world to the highest station. Your despising them will not harm them at all. God knows what is in their souls of faith in Him and sincerity towards Him, so He will reward them according to that. Neither I nor you have anything to do with their affair. Indeed, then I would be among the wrongdoers to them if I did what you wanted to them, or among the wrongdoers to themselves if I did that to them.
11:32: Then they answered him with other than what they had said and his, unable to provide the argument and falling short of the level of debate and breaking off from the competition, by saying: 32- O Noah, you have argued with us and prolonged your argument with us, meaning you have quarrelled with us with all kinds of quarrels, and you have pushed us with every need that has a bearing on the situation, and there is no room left for us in this matter, for the paths have become narrow for us and the doors of tricks have been closed, so bring us what you threaten us with, of the punishment that you fear for us and that you fear for us, if you should be of the truthful, in what you say to us.
11:33: So he answered that this is not up to him, but rather it is by the will and desire of God, and 33- He said, ‘God will only bring it to you if He wills.’ If His will and wisdom decree that it be hastened, He will hasten it for you, and if His will and wisdom decree that it be delayed, He will delay it. And you will not escape by escaping from what God wanted for you by fleeing or defending yourself.
11:34: 34- And my advice will not benefit you which I give you and I increase it in fulfillment of the right of advice to God by conveying His message, but by clarifying the truth and showing the falsehood of what you are upon if I wanted to advise you and the answer to this condition is omitted, and the estimate is: If I wanted to advise you, my advice will not benefit you, as indicated by what preceded it if God wants to mislead you meaning if God wants to mislead you, then my advice will not benefit you, so the answer to this condition was omitted like the first, and its estimate is what we mentioned, and this estimate is only according to the doctrine of those who forbid the consequence from precedence over the condition, but according to the doctrine of those who permit it, the consequence of the first condition is and my advice will not benefit you, and the consequence of the second condition is the first conditional sentence and its consequence. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of He leads you astray is He destroys you with His punishment. The apparent meaning of the Arabic language is that Ighwa means misguidance. So the meaning of the verse is: My advice will not benefit you if God wants to lead you astray from the path of guidance and let you down from the path of truth. It was narrated from Tayy that So-and-so has become misguided, meaning sick. This is not the meaning intended in the verse. Ighwa has also been used to mean destruction, and from it is they will meet with error, which is different from what is in this verse. He is your Lord, so to Him is the misguidance and to Him is guidance. And to Him you will be returned, so He will reward you for your deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And we do not see that you are followed except by those who are the lowest among us in outward opinion, he said: As it appears to us. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Ata’. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: If I am on clear evidence from my Lord, he said: I have known it and known by it His command, and that there is no god but Him, And He has given me mercy from Him, he said: Islam is guidance, faith, wisdom, and prophethood. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Shall We impose it upon you? He said: By God, if the Prophet of God had been able to do so, he would have imposed it upon his people, but he was not able to do so and it was not possible for him. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite: Shall We impose it upon you from a portion of ourselves, while you are averse to it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, he said regarding the recitation of Abu Anzalmaikumuha from a portion of ourselves, while you are averse to it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab that he read: We will not force you to follow them from the bottom of our hearts. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: And I will not drive away those who believe, he said: They said to him, O Noah, if you wish that we follow you, then drive them away, otherwise we will not be satisfied that we and they will be equal on earth. And regarding his statement: Indeed, they will meet their Lord, he said: He will ask them about their deeds. And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of God, which nothing will exhaust, so I only called you to follow me in them, not to give you my ownership of them. And I do not know the unseen, I do not say: Follow me based on my knowledge of the unseen. And I do not say that I am an angel, I came down from the heaven with a message. I am only a human being like you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, And I do not say to those whom your eyes despise, he said: You have belittled them. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: God will never give them any good, he said: He means faith. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: Then bring us what you promise us, he said: A denial of the punishment and that it is false.
11:35: His statement: 35- Or do they say, 'He invented it'? God Almighty denied their saying that what was revealed to Noah was invented, so He said: Or do they say, 'He invented it'? Then He commanded him to respond with a descriptive statement, so He said: Say, 'If I invented it, then upon me is my crime' with the breaking of the hamza according to the reading of the majority, the source of ajram: meaning doing what necessitates sin, and jarama and ajram have the same meaning as Al-Nahhas said, and the meaning is: upon me is my sin or the reward for my earnings. And whoever reads with the opening of the hamza said: It is a plural mentioned by Al-Nahhas And I am innocent of what you commit meaning of your crime because of what you attribute to me of fabrication. It was said: There is an omission in the statement and the meaning is: But what I invented, so the crime and its punishment are only upon you and I am innocent of it. The commentators differed regarding this verse. Some said: It is a narration about Noah and what he said to his people. Others said: It is a narration about the dialogue that took place between our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the infidels of Mecca. The first is more appropriate, because the speech before and after it is with Noah, peace be upon him.
11:36: His saying: 36- "And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed." That he will not believe is in the nominative case as a deputy of the subject who has not been named. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with the preposition ba': meaning that, and in the speech there is despair for him of their belief, and that they are continuing in their disbelief, determined upon it, none of them will believe except those who have previously believed. "So do not be sad about what they used to do." Misery: sadness, meaning do not be sad, and the miserable: the submissive, so God Almighty forbade him from being sad with the sadness of the submissive because sadness is sadness in submission. And from this is the saying of the poet: How many a friend or intimate friend I have lost, but I did not feel sad, even though the loss was great.
11:37: Then when God Almighty informed him that they would not believe at all, He made known to him the way to destroy them, and inspired him with the command by which he would be saved and those who believed with him would be saved, so He said: 37- And construct the ark under Our eyes and with Our inspiration. That is, construct the ship under Our eYa-Sin 36:that is, in Our sight, and what is meant by Our guarding you and preserving you, and He expressed that with eyes because they are the instrument of vision, and vision is what usually carries guarding and preserving, and the plural of eyes is for glorification, not for multiplication, and it was said that the meaning is: under Our eyes that is, with the eyes of Our angels whom We made eyes to preserve you, and it was said: under Our eyes with Our knowledge, and it was said with Our command. The meaning of Our revelation is: With what We revealed to you about how to make it. “And do not speak to Me about those who have wronged,” meaning do not ask for a respite for them, for the time for vengeance against them has come. The phrase they will be drowned is for al-Sharh 94:meaning do not ask Us to give them a respite, for they have been condemned by Us to drown and the decree has passed, so there is no way to prevent it or delay it. It was said: The meaning is do not speak to Me about hastening their punishment, for they will be drowned at the time set for that, and their drowning will not be delayed. It was said: What is meant by those who wronged is his wife and son.
11:38: 38- "And he made the ark" meaning he began to make the ark, or he began to make the ark, and it was said: it is a narration of a past state to evoke the image, and the phrase "And every time a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him" is in the accusative case as a state: meaning they mocked him for making the ark. Al-Akhfash and Al-Kisa'i said: It is said: I mocked him and from him. And there are two opinions about the reason for their mockery of him: One of them: that they saw him making the ark, and they would say: O Noah, you have become a carpenter after the prophethood. The second: that when they saw him making the ark, and they did not know it before that, they said: O Noah, what are you doing? He said: I walk with it on the water, so they were amazed by what he said, and they mocked him. Then he answered them by saying: "If you mock us, then we will mock you as you mock." This statement is resumed in the sense of a question as if it was said: So what did he say to them? Meaning: If you mock us because of our work on the ship today, then we will mock you tomorrow when it sinks. The meaning of mockery here is: to be ignorant, that is, if you are ignorant of us, then we will be ignorant of you as you are ignorant. His ignoring them is based on his showing them and speaking to them, otherwise they are ignorant before and after this. The simile in his statement: as you mock is merely for the sake of realization and occurrence, or renewal and repetition. The meaning is: We mock you with a mockery that is real and occurring just as you mock us, or renewed and repeated just as you mock us. It was said that its meaning is: We will mock you in the future with a mockery like your mockery if you are drowned. This is questionable, because their state at that time does not suit mockery, as they are busy with something else.
11:39: Then He threatened them by saying: 39- "Then you will know who will be afflicted with a punishment that will disgrace him which is the punishment of drowning in this world and upon whom will befall a lasting punishment" which is the eternal punishment of the Fire. The meaning of "will befall" is: He will make the deferred present, taken from the settlement of the deferred debt, and "from" is a relative pronoun in the accusative case, and it is permissible for it to be an interrogative in the nominative case: meaning who will be afflicted with a punishment that will disgrace him? It was said: In the nominative case as a subject, and "will befall him is the report, and will befall him is an attribute of punishment". Al-Kisa'i said: Some people from the Hijaz say "you will know", he said: And whoever says "you will know dropped both the waw and the fa, and the Kufians permitted you will know" but the Basrans forbade it. What is meant by the punishment of disgrace is the punishment that disgraces its owner and brings shame upon him.
11:40: His saying: 40- Until, when Our command came and the oven overflowed. Until is the introductory particle that entered the conditional sentence and was made the end of his saying: And construct the ark under Our eyes. The interpretation of the word Tanour has been disputed in various ways: First: It is the surface of the earth, and the Arabs call the surface of the earth Tanour. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Al-Zuhri, and Ibn Uyaynah. Second: It is the bread oven in which they bake bread. This was also said by Mujahid, Atiyah, and Al-Hasan. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Third: It is the place where water gathers in the ship. This was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan. Fourth: It is the rising of dawn, from their saying Tanour Al-Fajr. This was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib. Fifth: It is the mosque of Kufa. This was also narrated on the authority of Ali and Mujahid. Mujahid said: It was near Tanour in Kufa. Sixth: It is the upper parts of the earth and the elevated places. This was said by Qatada. Seventh: It is the spring on the island called Ain Al-Wardah. This was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah. Eighth: It is a place in India. Ibn Abbas said: Adam’s oven was in India. Al-Nahhas said: These statements are not contradictory, because God Almighty has informed us that the water came from the sky and the earth. He said: Then We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water, and caused springs to gush forth from the earth. These statements agree that this was a sign, as he said, and there is a consideration in it, because the fourth statement contradicts this combination, and the interpretation of the spring of water does not hold true on it, unless what is meant is merely a sign, as he mentioned at the end. The linguists have mentioned that al-fur means boiling, and al-tanur is a foreign name that the Arabs Arabized. It was said that the meaning of far in al-tanur is to represent the presence of torment, as they say: the battle has become intense when the war has become intense. From this is the saying of the poet: You left your destiny with nothing in it, and the destiny of the people is boiling hot He wants war. He said: “We said: ‘Load therein two of every kind’” meaning: We said: O Noah, load into the ark two of every kind of the animals on earth, a male and a female. Hafs read of every with the tanween of every: meaning of every thing two. The word two refers to two people who cannot do without each other, and each one of them is called a pair, just as a man is called a pair and a woman is called a pair. The word pair is used to refer to two people if it is used in contrast to an individual, and the word pair is used to refer to a type and a kind. Similar to this is the statement of God Almighty: And caused to grow of every kind a beautiful pair. Similar to this is the statement of Al-A’sha: And every kind of brocade that Abu Hudhafah wears is hidden with that together. He wanted every type of brocade and your family in apposition to two spouses, or to two according to the reading of Hafs, and to the location of each pair, as it is in the accusative case with carry, or to two according to the reading of the majority, and what is meant is: his wife, his children and their women except for those against whom the word has already been passed meaning those against whom the ruling has already been passed that they are among those who will be drowned in His statement: And do not speak to Me concerning those who have wronged, for indeed, they will be drowned according to the previous difference in them, so whoever made them all the infidels from his family and others, this was an exception from the sentence carry therein of every pair two and your family and whoever said: what is meant by them is his son Canaan and his wife Wa'ilah Umm Canaan, made the exception from your family, and it is connected if what is meant by family is what is more general than the Muslim and the infidel among them, and disconnected if what is meant by family is only the Muslims among them. His statement: And whoever believes is in apposition to your family: meaning and carry in the ship whoever believes from your people, and the family was singled out from them for more attention to them, or to exclude them according to the other statement. Then God Almighty described the small number of believers with Noah in comparison to those who disbelieved in him, saying: And none believed with him except a few. It was said: They were eighty al-Nas 114:three of them were his sons, namely Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives. When they left the ship, they built a village called the Village of the Eighty, which is located in the Mosul area. It was said that they were ten, and it was said seven, and it was said that they were seventy-two, and other things were said.
11:41: His saying: 41- And he said, ‘Embark therein.’ The speaker was Noah, and it was said that it was God Almighty. The first is more appropriate, because of his saying: Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. Riding: is to ascend on the back of something, literally, like the riding of an animal, or metaphorically, like the religion rode it. There is an omission in the speech: that is, ride the water in the ship, so it is not necessary that riding is transitive by itself. It was said: The benefit of adding in is that he ordered them to be in the interior of the ship, not on its back. It was said: It was added to take into account the aspect of being local in the ship, as in his saying: So when they embarked in the ark, and his saying: Until when they embarked in the ark. It was said: Perhaps Noah said this statement after entering what he was ordered to carry of the spouses, as if it was said: So he carried the spouses and entered them into the ark, and he said to the believers. It can be said: He ordered to ride everyone he was ordered to carry of the spouses, family, and believers. It is not impossible that his address could be understood by those who do not have reason among the animals, or this could be by way of predominance. His saying: In the name of God is related to rake or a state of its subject: meaning naming God, or saying: In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. The people of the Two Holy Mosques and the people of Basra read it with a damma on the meem in both of them, except for those who deviated from it, on the basis that they are nouns of time, and they are in the accusative case as circumstantial: meaning the time of its course and its anchorage. It is possible that they are two sources: meaning the time of its course and its anchorage. Al-A’mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Hafs read majraha with a fatha on the meem, and mursaaha with a damma. Yahya ibn Waththab read it with a fatha on the meem in both of them. Mujahid, Sulayman ibn Jundub, Asim al-Jahdari, and Abu Raja al-Attardi read its course and its anchorage as two descriptions of God. It is possible that they are in the nominative case with an implied subject: that is, He is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving of sins, Merciful to His servants. And from His mercy is the salvation of this group as a favor from Him for the survival of this animal species and not its extermination by drowning.
11:42: His statement: 42- And it sails with them in waves like mountains. This sentence is connected to an omitted sentence indicated by the command to ride, and the meaning is: So they rode, named, and it sails with them, and the wave is the plural of wave, and it is what rises above the mass of abundant water when the wind is strong, and he likened it to the mountains high on the earth. His statement: And Noah called to his son, he is Canaan, it was said: And he was a disbeliever, and it was excluded that Noah would call to someone who was a disbeliever with his statement: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dwelling, and it was answered that he was a hypocrite, so Noah thought that he was a believer, and it was said: The compassion of fatherhood led him to do that, and it was said: He was the son of his wife and not his son, and it is supported by what was narrated that Ali read and Noah called to her son, and it was said: He was not of sound mind, and he was born on Noah's bed. It was reported that his saying: And Noah called to his son, and his saying: Indeed, my son is of my family, refute this because it does not protect the position of prophethood. And he was isolated, meaning in a place where he isolated himself from his people and relatives, such that Noah’s words did not reach him: Embark in it. It was said: Embark in it. It was said: Embark in it. It was said: Embark in it. It was said: O my son, embark with us. Asim read it with the fatha of the ya’, and the rest with the kasra of it. As for the kasra, it is to make it a substitute for the ya’ of addition, because the original is O my son. As for the fatha, it is to change the ya’ of addition to an alif because of the lightness of the alif, then the alif was deleted and the fatha remained to indicate it. An-Nahhas said: Asim’s reading is problematic. Abu Hatim said: Its original is O my son, then it is deleted. Az-Zajjaj has given two ways for the fatha, and two ways for the kasra. As for the fatha in the first way, it is what we mentioned, and the second way: that the alif is deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. As for the kasra, the first way is as we mentioned, and the second is that it is deleted due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. This is what Al-Nahhas narrated from him. Abu Amr, Al-Kisa’i and Hafs read board with us by assimilating the ba’ into the meem because of their closeness in point of articulation. The rest read without assimilating. And do not be with the disbelievers He forbade him from being with the disbelievers: meaning outside the ship, and it is possible that what is meant by being with them is being on their religion.
11:43: Then God the Almighty narrated what Noah's son answered his father, saying: 43- "He said, 'I will seek refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water'" meaning that it will prevent me from the water reaching me due to its height. Noah answered him by saying, "There is no protector today from the command of God" meaning there is no protector, for it is a day in which the punishment has been decreed and the pen has dried up regarding what will happen in it. He negated the type of protector, so the protector from drowning on that day is included under it in a primary inclusion. He referred to the water or the drowning as the command of God the Almighty to magnify its importance and to intimidate its matter. The exception, Al-Zajjaj said: It is disconnected: meaning, but whoever God has mercy on, He will protect him, so "whom He has mercy on" is in the accusative case. It is permissible for the exception to be connected so that protector means infallible: meaning, there is no one infallible today from the command of God except whoever God has mercy on: like "flowing water a pleasant life" and from it the poet's saying: Let the noble deeds not rise for their desire and sit, for you are the one who feeds and clothes. Any one who is clothed and fed, and this face was chosen by Ibn Jarir, and it was said: Al-Asim means the one who has protection, like Ibn and Tamir, and the meaning is: There is no protector except in the place of the one upon whom God has mercy, which is the ship, and then what is said does not apply: The meaning of the one upon whom God has mercy is the one upon whom God has mercy, and the one upon whom God has mercy is protected, so how is it correct to exclude him from Al-Asim? Because in each of these faces there is a solution to the problem. And it was read except the one upon whom God has mercy in the passive form, and the waves came between them meaning it came between Noah and his son, so it was difficult for him to be saved from drowning, and it was said: between the son of Noah and the mountain, and the first is more appropriate, because the branching of and he was among the drowned upon it indicates the first and not the second, because the mountain is not a protector.
11:44: His saying: 44- And it was said, O Earth, swallow your water. It is said: Swallow the water, he swallows it, like prevented, he prevents, and swallow, he swallows, like praised, he praises, two dialects narrated by Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra': Swallowing is drinking, and from it is the drain, which is the place where water is drunk, and swallowing, it is said: he swallowed what was in his mouth of food if he swallowed it, and swallowing, which is an action of animals, was borrowed for drying up, indicating that this is not like the usual drying up that occurs gradually. O sky, desist. Deprivation is withholding, it is said: the rain desisted if it stopped. Meaning: He ordered the sky to hold back the water from being sent down, and He mentioned the earth’s call before the sky because the flood began from it. And the water subsided means it decreased. It is said: the water subsided and I subsided it. And the matter was accomplished means it was decided and finished: meaning God destroyed the people of Noah completely and perfectly. And the ship came to rest on al-Judi means the ship came to rest on the mountain known as al-Judi, which is a mountain near Mosul. It was said that al-Judi is the name of every mountain, and from this is the saying of Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl: Glory be to Him, then glory be to Him, we seek refuge in Him, and before us, glory be to Al-Judi and Al-Jamad. It is said: It is one of the mountains of Paradise, and that is why it settled on it. “And it was said: Away with the wrongdoing people.” The speaker is God, the Most High, to suit the beginning of the verse. It was also said: It is Noah and his companions. The meaning is: And it was said: Destruction for the wrongdoing people. It is one of the words that are specific to the supplication of the surahs and describing them as wrongdoers to indicate that it is the cause of destruction, and to allude to His saying: And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged. The scholars of rhetoric have agreed that this noble verse is extremely eloquent and rhetorical to a level that description falls short of, and the ability of those who are capable of the arts of rhetoric, who are firm in the science of rhetoric, who are firmly rooted in the science of language, who are familiar with what is recorded of the sermons of the most famous Arab orators and the poems of their poets, who are well-versed in the subtleties of the sciences of Arabic and its secrets. A group of them have presented some of what it contains of that, and they have elaborated and made it complete. May God have mercy on us and them with His vast mercy. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: My action is my crime, he said: My action, and I am innocent of what you commit, meaning what you do. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, that is when Noah supplicated against them, he said: Do not leave on the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers. Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Noah did not supplicate against his people until this verse was revealed, so his hope from them was cut off at that time, so he supplicated against them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So do not be sad, he said: Do not grieve. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And construct the ark under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, he said: Under the eye of God and His inspiration. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, he said: Noah did not know how to construct the ark, so God revealed to him to construct it like the prow of a bird. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Noah remained among his people for a thousand years minus fifty, calling them until the end of his time. He planted a tree and it grew large and went in all directions. Then he cut it down and began to make it into a ship. They would pass by and ask him, and he would say, ‘Make it into a ship.’ They would mock him and say, ‘Make a ship on land. How will it sail?’ He said, ‘You will soon find out.’ When he finished, the oven overflowed and the water in the alleys increased. The boy’s mother feared for him, and she loved him very much. So she went out to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went out until she was on the mountain. When the water reached his neck, she lifted him up in her hands until the water carried him away. If God had mercy on any of them, He would have had mercy on the boy’s mother.” Al-Dhahabi declared it weak in his Mustadrak on Al-Hakim’s Mustadrak. There are hadiths and reports about the description and size of the ship, but mentioning them here is not of much benefit. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Whoever is visited by a torment that disgraces him he said: It is drowning and a lasting torment will befall him he said: It is eternity in the Fire. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Hakim narrated - and he authenticated it - on his authority that he said: There were three hundred years between the call of Noah and the destruction of his people, and the oven was boiling in India and Noah’s ship circled the Kaaba for a week. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said: The oven is the spring in Al-Jazirah, the spring of the rose. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ali Ibn Abi Talib that he said: The oven boiled from the mosque of Kufa by the gates of Kinda. Something similar to this has been narrated on his authority through various chains of narration. Saeed Ibn Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The oven is the surface of the earth. It was said to him: If you see water on the surface of the earth, then embark, you and those with you. The Arabs call the surface of the earth the oven of the earth. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali, And the oven boiled over. He said: The dawn broke, and it was said to him: When the dawn breaks, then embark, you and your companions. Other than this has been narrated in the interpretation of the oven, and we have already mentioned that. Many narrations have been narrated about the description of the story and what Noah carried in the ship, and how the sinking happened, and how long the ship remained on the surface of the water, but they have no bearing on the interpretation of the words of God, the Most High. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: In the name of God is its course and its anchorage, he said: When they embark, sail, and anchor. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: When he wanted to anchor, he said: In the name of God, so it anchored, and when he wanted it to sail, he said: In the name of God, so it sailed. Abu Ya'la, Al-Tabarani, Ibn As-Sunni, Ibn Adi, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ali who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Safety for my nation from drowning when they board a ship is that they say: ‘In the name of God, the King, the Most Gracious, in the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. And they do not appreciate God with His true appreciation,’ until the end of the verse.” Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Al-Shaykh also narrated it on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: The name of Noah’s son who drowned was Canaan. Abd Al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: He is his son, except that he differed from him in intention and action. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: There is no protector this Day from the decree of God except for him on whom He has mercy, he said: No one is saved except the people of the ship. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Barra regarding his statement: And the waves came between them, he said: Between the son of Noah and the mountain. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: O earth, swallow, he said: It is in Abyssinian. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih regarding swallow, he said in Abyssinian: That is, swallow it. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ja’far bin Muhammad on the authority of his father, he said: Its meaning is drink in the language of India. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. I say: The presence of the word balaa’ and its derivatives in the language of the Arabs is clear and obvious, so what do we have to do with Abyssinia and India?
11:45: Meaning: 45- And Noah called upon his Lord he called upon Him, and what is meant is that he wanted to call upon Him, as evidenced by the letter fa in and he said, 'My Lord, indeed my son is of my family' and linking something to itself is not permissible, so the aforementioned estimation is necessary, and the meaning of his saying: Indeed my son is of my family is that he is from the family whom You promised me to save by Your saying: and your family. If it is said: How did Noah, peace be upon him, ask for the fulfillment of what God promised him by His saying: and your family which is the exception from, and leave out what the exception indicates, which is except for he against whom the word has already preceded? It is answered: He did not know at that time that he was one of those who had been spoken to, for he thought that he was one of the believers. And Your promise is the truth, which cannot be broken. This is from Him. And You are the most just of judges, meaning the most perfect of those who are perfect in what a judgement is, so no contradiction can come to your judgement. It was said: He meant by the most just of judges the most knowledgeable and just of them: meaning you are more knowledgeable and just than those who judge. It was said: The judge means the one with wisdom, like a shield.
11:46: Then God the Almighty answered Noah by explaining that his son is not included in the generality of the family, and that he is outside the restriction of exception, so He said, O Noah, he is not of your family those who believed in you and followed you, even though he was of your family by virtue of kinship. Then He stated the reason for his exclusion from the generality of the family, which explains to him that what is meant by kinship is religion, not kinship by lineage alone, so He said: Indeed, he did an evil deed. The majority read worked as a verbal noun. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read worked as a verb, and the meaning of the first reading is exaggeration in blaming him, as if he made the work itself, and its origin is of evil deed, then the added noun was deleted and the work itself was made, as Al-Zajjaj and others said. The meaning of the second reading is clear: that is, he did an unrighteous deed, which is his disbelief and his abandonment of following his father. Then he forbade him from such a question, saying: So do not ask about that of which you have no knowledge, because he showed him the invalidity of what he believed of his being one of its people. A branch of that is the prohibition against asking. Even though it is a general prohibition such that it includes every question whose owner does not know that obtaining what he wants from him is correct, his question is included under it primarily, and in it is the impermissibility of supplicating for that which a person does not know is in accordance with the Shari’ah. His supplication was called a question because it includes the meaning of a question. I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant, meaning I warn you lest you be among the ignorant, like his saying: God admonishes you lest you ever return to the like of it. It was said that the meaning is: I raise you above being among the ignorant. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is an addition from God and an admonition by which He raises Noah from the station of the ignorant and elevates him to the station of the scholars who work.
11:47: Then when Noah knew that his question did not match reality, and that his supplication was the result of an illusion he had imagined, he hastened to admit the mistake and ask for forgiveness and mercy, so 47- He said, ‘My Lord, indeed I seek refuge in You from asking You for that of which I have no knowledge.’ That is, I seek refuge in You from asking You for that which I have no knowledge of its validity or permissibility, and unless You forgive me the sin of what I asked for without knowledge on my part and have mercy upon me with Your mercy that encompasses all things, so accept my repentance I will be among the losers in my deeds, so that I will not profit from them.
11:48: The speaker is God, or the angels 48- It was said, 'O Noah, descend' meaning descend from the ship to the earth, or from the mountain to the low part of the earth, for the earth has swallowed its water and dried up "with peace from Us" meaning with safety and security, and it was said: with a greeting and blessings meaning permanent blessings, derived from the camel's brook which means its stability, and from it the blessing for the water to remain in it, and in this address to him is evidence of the acceptance of his repentance and the forgiveness of his mistake and upon nations from among those with you meaning emerging from among those with you, and they are the offspring of those who were with him in the ship, and it was said: He meant those in the ship, for they are different nations and different types of animals. It was said: God the Almighty meant by these nations who were with Him those of their descendants who became believers, and He meant by His saying: And nations We will grant enjoyment, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us those of their descendants who became disbelievers until the Day of Resurrection. The raising of nations in His saying: And nations We will grant enjoyment is as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning, and among them are nations. It was said that it is based on the estimation: and there will be nations. Al-Akhfash said: It is as you say: I spoke to Zaid and Amr was sitting. Al-Farra’ permitted in other readings: And nations We will grant enjoyment: meaning, and we will grant enjoyment to nations. The meaning of the verse is: And nations We will grant enjoyment in this world with what is in it of enjoyment, and We will give them from it what they live on, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us in the Hereafter. It was said: It will touch them either in this world or in the Hereafter.
11:49: And the reference in his saying: 49- That is to the story of Noah, and it is a subject, and the sentences after it are report of the report of the unseen of the same type as report of the unseen, and report is the plural of report, which is report: that is, of the report of the unseen that you have come across in this surah, and the pronoun in We revealed it to you refers to the story, and the use of the present tense is to bring to mind the image you O Muhammad did not know it, nor did "your people know it, rather it was unknown to you before the revelation, or before this time so be patient over what you encounter from the infidels of your time, and the fa is to branch off what comes after it from what comes before it indeed the outcome the praiseworthy one in this world and the hereafter is for the righteous" of God, the believers in what His messengers brought, and in this there is consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and good report for him that victory is for the righteous in the outcome of the matter, and its beginnings are not taken into account. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Noah called upon his Lord and said: My Lord, my son is of my family, and You have promised me to save my family, and my son is of my family. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Faryabi, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Sheikh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: No wife of a prophet has ever been unjust. His statement: He is not of your family means: He is not of your family whom I promised to save with you. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on his authority that he said: The wives of the prophets do not commit adultery. He used to recite it: It is an unrighteous deed meaning: Your asking of Me, O Noah, is an unrighteous deed and I do not approve of it for you. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: So do not ask about that of which you have no knowledge that he said: God made it clear to Noah that he was not his son. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding His statement: “O Noah, disembark in peace from Us” that he said: Disembark and God is pleased with them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: This peace and blessings will include every believing man and woman until the Day of Resurrection, and this painful punishment will include every unbeliever, man and woman, until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak: And upon nations from among those with you meaning those who were not born, for whom God has made blessings obligatory because of the happiness that has already been known to them in God’s knowledge. And nations We will grant enjoyment meaning the enjoyment of worldly life then a painful punishment will touch them from Us because of the misery that has already been known to them in God’s knowledge. Abu al-Shaykh narrated that he said: Then he returned to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: This is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]; you did not know it, nor did your people meaning the Arabs before this the Qur’an.
11:50: His statement: 50- And to 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud is in apposition to And We sent Nuh 71:meaning, and We sent to 'Aad their brother: meaning, one of them, and Hud is an explanatory apposition, and the people of 'Aad were idol worshippers, and something similar to this has been mentioned in Al-A'raf. It has been said: They are the first 'Aad and the other 'Aad, so these are the first 'Aad and the other 'Aad, they are Shaddad and Luqman and their people mentioned in His statement: Iram, who had lofty pillars. The origin of 'Aad is the name of a man, then it became the name of a tribe like Tamim and Bakr and the like. You have no god other than Him. "You have no god other than Him" is read in the accusative case based on the word, and in the nominative case based on the place of god, and it is read in the accusative case based on the exception. "You are nothing but inventers" meaning, you are not by taking a god other than God except lying about God, the Almighty.
11:51: Then he addressed them and said: 51- O my people, I do not ask of you any reward for it. That is, I do not ask of you any reward for what I convey to you and advise you with, which is guidance to worship God alone and that you have no god but Him. The pronoun refers to the content of this speech. The meaning of this has already been mentioned in the story of Noah. My reward is only from Him who created me. That is, the reward that I ask for is only from Him who created me: that is, He created me, so He is the One who will reward me for that. Do you not understand? That the reward of those who give sincere advice is from the Lord of the Worlds. It was said that he said previously in the story of Nuh 71:money, and here he said: a reward because of the mention of the treasuries after it in the story of Noah, and the word money is more appropriate for it.
11:52: Then He guided them to seek forgiveness and repentance. The meaning is: Seek His forgiveness for your past sins, then supplicate to Him through repentance. More clarification of something like this has already been presented in the story of Noah. Then He encouraged them to believe in the immediate good, saying: 52- He sends the sky meaning rain upon you in abundance meaning abundant rain, and it is in the accusative case as a state, the sky poured, it pours and it pours, so it is in abundance. The people of Hud were people of gardens, crops and buildings, and their dwellings were the sands between Syria and Yemen. And He increases you strength to your strength is in apposition to He sends: meaning strength added to your strength, or fertility to your fertility, or glory to your glory. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is He increases you strength in blessings. And do not turn away, criminals meaning do not turn away from what I call you to and persist in disbelief, insisting on it. Crime means sins as mentioned above.
11:53: Then his people answered him with what indicates their extreme ignorance and great stupidity, so they said, O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof meaning a clear argument that we can act upon and believe in you, not acknowledging what came to them of God's arguments and proofs, out of stubbornness and distance from the truth. Nor will we abandon our gods that we worship besides God. The meaning of from your saying is issued from your saying, so the circumstance is in the accusative case as a state. Nor will we believe in you meaning we will believe in anything that you have brought.
11:54: 54- "We say nothing but that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil" meaning, we say nothing but that some of our gods that you criticize and whose worship you belittle have afflicted you with evil and madness, until your madness resulted in what you say to us and repeat to us of alienation from them. It is said: the matter afflicted him and befell him: if it befell him, so he answered them with what indicates his indifference to them and his trust in his Lord and his reliance on Him, and that they are not able to do anything that the disbelievers want with him, rather God Almighty is the one who harms and benefits, so "He said, 'Indeed, I call God to witness and you bear witness' that I am innocent of what you associate' with Him.
11:55: 55- Without Him meaning from your associating partners with God without Him sending down any authority for it. Then plot against me all together you and your gods if they are as you claim, that they are able to harm me and have harmed me. Then do not wait meaning do not give me time, but rather hasten to do whatever you want. This shows a lack of concern for them and their idols that they worship, which deafens their ears and makes clear their helplessness and inability to do anything.
11:56: 56- Indeed, I have put my trust in God, my Lord and your Lord. He will protect me from your plotting, even if you go to any lengths in seeking to harm me. Whoever puts his trust in God, He will suffice him. Then, when he explained to them his trust in God and his confidence in His protection and guardianship, he described Him with what necessitates trust in Him and entrusting Him with, such as His Lordship encompassing him and them, and that He is the Owner of all, and that the forelock of every beast of the earth is in His hand, in His grasp and under His control, which is a metaphor for the ultimate subjugation and humiliation. When they captured a prisoner and wanted to release him, and showed him favor, they would cut off his forelock, making that a sign of His subjugation. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of I take her by the forelock is her owner and the one who has power over her. Al-Qatibi said: He has subdued her because whoever you take by the forelock, you have subdued him. The forelock is the hair cut from the front of the head. Then he explained what came before by saying: Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path, meaning He is on the truth and justice, so He can hardly give you power over me.
11:57: 57- "If you turn away meaning you turn away, so one of the two ta's was deleted, and the meaning is if you continue to turn away from answering and persist in what you are accustomed to of disbelief I have conveyed to you that with which I was sent to you I have no obligation except that, and the proof has become binding on you and my Lord will replace you with a people other than you" a renewed sentence to confirm the threat of destruction: meaning He will replace you with another people in your homes and wealth, and it is possible that it is in apposition to "I have conveyed to you". Hafs narrated on the authority of Asim that he read "and will replace you in the subjunctive mood, based on the position of I have conveyed to you". "And you will not harm Him at all" meaning by your turning away, and you will not be able to do much harm, nor even a small one. "Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things" meaning He is a watchful and dominant observer over it, protecting it from everything. It was said: "And over means the lam", so the meaning is: He is Guardian over all things, so He protects me from you harming me.
11:58: 58- “And when Our command came” meaning Our punishment, which is the destruction of Aad, We saved Hud and those who believed with him from his people by mercy from Us meaning by great mercy from Us because no one is saved except by the mercy of God, and it was said that it is faith from a severe punishment meaning severe, and it was said that it was the poisons that entered their noses.
11:59: 59- "And those were 'Aad" subject and predicate, and the demonstrative is feminine in consideration of the tribe. Al-Kisa'i said: Some Arabs do not decline 'Aad and make it a name for the tribe. "They denied the signs of their Lord" meaning they disbelieved in them and denied them and rejected the miracles. "And disobeyed His messengers" meaning Hud alone, because there was no messenger in his time other than him. The plural here is because whoever denies a messenger has denied all the messengers. It was said: They disobeyed Hud and the messengers who came before him, or they were such that if God had sent them multiple messengers, they would have denied them. "And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant" the arrogant tyrant, and the obstinate is the tyrant who does not accept the truth nor submit to it. Abu Ubaidah said: The obstinate is the stubborn, the obstinate and the obstinate, and he is the one who opposes with disagreement from him, and from it the vein that bursts with blood is called 'Aanad. The rajaz poet said: I am too old to be stubborn
11:60: 60- "And they were pursued in this world by a curse" meaning: they were inflicted with it, which is being removed from mercy and expelled from goodness, and the meaning is that it is a constant for them and will not leave them as long as they are in this world. "And they followed it on the Day of Resurrection" so they were cursed there as they were cursed in this world. "Behold, 'Aad disbelieved in their Lord" meaning in their Lord. Al-Farra' said: They disbelieved in the blessing of their Lord. It is said: I disbelieved in him and I disbelieved in him: like I thanked him and I thanked him. "Behold, away with 'Aad, the people of Hud" meaning they are still being distanced from the mercy of God. Distance means destruction, and distance means distancing from goodness. It is said: After he is delayed and distant, and after he is far away after: if he perishes. From this is the saying of the poet: Do not distance my people, who are the poison of the enemy and the scourge of the islands. Al-Nabigha said: Do not be far away, for death is a source of strength, and every person will one day perish. And from it the poet said: Their women were of no use to me, and I was killed instead of their men. Don't be far away. It was mentioned earlier that the Arabs use it to pray for destruction. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada, “Except for He who created me.” Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Adh-Dahhak, who said: God withheld rain from the people of ‘Aad for three years, so Hud said to them, Seek forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him, and He will send down upon you abundant rain. But they refused and persisted. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Harun At-Taymi, regarding His statement, He will send down upon you abundant rain, he said: rain. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, And will add strength to your strength, he said: strength to your strength. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, And will add strength to your strength, he said: childbirth. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, We say nothing except that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil, he said: they have afflicted you with madness. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed who said: There is no one who fears a common thief, or a ferocious beast, or a rebellious devil and recites this verse except that God will turn him away from it. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path. He said: The truth. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding His statement: A severe punishment. He said: Severe. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding His statement: Every obstinate tyrant He said: The polytheist. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: The obstinate is the one who makes trouble. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding His statement: And they were pursued in this world by a curse. He said: No prophet was sent after Aad except that a curse was on his tongue. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: Two curses from God followed them one after the other: a curse in this world and a curse in the Hereafter.
11:61: His statement: 61- And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih is connected to what came before, and the meaning is: And We sent to Thamud their brother Salih, and the discussion is about him, and about his statement: O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him as came before in the story of Hud. Al-Hasan and Yahya bin Waththab read and to Thamud with the tanween in all places. The rest of the reciters differed about it, so they declined it in one place and did not decline it in another place, so the decline is based on the interpretation of the tribe, and the prevention is based on the interpretation of the tribe, and so on for all that is valid in both interpretations, and Sibawayh recited in the feminine based on the interpretation of the tribe: Al-Walid defeated the forgivers and saved the Quraysh from their problems and ruled them. He created you from the earth meaning He began your creation from the earth, because all of the children of Adam are from the loins of Adam, who was created from the earth. And made you its inhabitants meaning He made you its inhabitants and its residents, from their saying: So-and-so made so-and-so inhabit his house, so it is his lifespan. So istaf’ala has the meaning of af’ala, like istijaba means ajaba. Ad-Dahhak said: Its meaning is He prolonged your lives, and their lives were from three hundred to one thousand. It was said that its meaning is: He ordered you to inhabit it by building houses and planting trees. So seek forgiveness of Him meaning ask Him to forgive you for worshipping idols. Then repent to Him meaning return to worshipping Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive meaning He is near in response to whoever calls upon Him. This has been discussed previously in Surat Al-Baqarah when God Almighty says: For indeed, I am near and I respond to the call of the caller.
11:62: 62- "They said, 'O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this'" meaning, we were hoping that you would be an obeyed master among us, that we would benefit from your opinion, and that we would be happy with your leadership before this that you showed of your claim to prophethood and your call to monotheism. It was said: Salih used to criticize their gods and they used to hope that he would return to their religion, but when he called them to God, they said, "There is no hope of it from you. The question in his saying, Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped?" is for denial. They denied him this prohibition. "And to worship" is in the accusative case with the deletion of the preposition: meaning that we worship. The meaning of "what our fathers worship" is: what our fathers used to worship. It is a narration of a past state to bring the image to mind. "And indeed, we are in doubt about that to which you call us, disturbing. From arabatuhu, so I am arabahu": if you did something to him that would cause him doubt, which is the anxiety of the soul and the absence of tranquility, or from "arab", a man: if he was suspicious. The meaning is: Indeed, we are in doubt about that which you call us to. It calls us to worship God alone and to abandon the worship of idols, which is a source of doubt.
11:63: 63- "He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord', i.e., a clear argument and a correct proof, 'and He has given me from Himself', i.e., from His side, 'mercy', i.e., prophethood? And although these matters are certain to occur, they were initiated with a word of doubt in consideration of the state of those being addressed, because they are in doubt about that, as they described about themselves. 'Then who will help me against God' is a question that means negation: i.e., I have no helper to prevent me from God's punishment. 'If I disobey Him' in conveying the message and I observe you and I slacken off from what I am required to convey. 'Then you will not increase me' by discouraging me 'except loss' by making me a loser by invalidating my work and exposing myself to God's punishment. Al-Farra' said: i.e., misguidance and distancing from good. And it was said that the meaning is: 'Then you will not increase me by your argument with the religion of your fathers except insight into your loss.
11:64: His saying: 64- "And O my people, this is the she-camel of God for you as a sign." The interpretation of this verse has already been mentioned in Al-A'raf. The meaning of "for you is a sign" is an apparent miracle. It is in the accusative case as a state, but in the accusative case as a state of a sign that precedes it. If it had been delayed, it would have been a description of it. It has been said that the she-camel of God is a substitute for this, and the predicate is for you. The first is more appropriate. He only said: the she-camel of God because He brought her out for them from a mountain according to their suggestion. It has also been said: from a solid rock. "So leave her to eat in the land of God." That is, leave her to eat in the land of God from what is in it of pastures that animals eat. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible to raise "to eat" as a state and to resume. Perhaps it originally means according to what the Arabic language requires, not in the verse. So the reliable readings that have been narrated as correct are: "And do not touch her with harm." Al-Farra’ said: By hamstringing it. It appears that the prohibition is more general than that: Then a near punishment will seize you. The answer to the prohibition: That is, close to hamstringing it, and that is for three days.
11:65: 65- So they hamstrung her meaning they did not comply with the command from Salih nor the prohibition, rather they disobeyed all of that and hamstrung her. Then Salih said to them, Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days meaning enjoy living in your homes for three days, for the punishment will descend upon you after that. It was said that they hamstrung her on Wednesday, so they stayed on Thursday, Friday and Saturday and the punishment came to them on Sunday. The reference in his saying: That to what is indicated by the command to enjoy for three days is a promise that is not false meaning there is no lie in it, so the preposition was omitted by imitation, or by way of metaphor as if the promise if fulfilled is true and not false, and it is permissible for it to be a source: meaning a promise that is not false.
11:66: 66- So when Our command came meaning Our punishment, or Our command for the punishment to occur, We saved Salih and those who believed with him by mercy from Us The explanation of this has already been presented in the story of Hud, and from the disgrace of that Day meaning, and We saved them from the disgrace of that Day, which is their destruction by the shout, and disgrace means humiliation and disgrace, and it was said from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, but the first is more appropriate. Nafi' and Al-Kisa'i read with the fatha on Day as if it acquired the construction from the complement to it. The rest read with the kasra, Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, the Exalted in Might the Able, the Victorious, for whom nothing is impossible.
11:67: 67- And the shriek seized those who did wrong meaning on the fourth day after the she-camel was hamstrung, a shriek was made upon them and they died. The verb was mentioned because the shriek and the shouting are one and the same, although the feminine is not real. It was said that it was Gabriel's shriek, and it was said that it was a shriek from the sky, so their hearts were torn apart and they died. It was mentioned in Al-A'raf So the earthquake seized them it was said that it occurred after the shriek and they became in their homes, prostrate meaning falling on their faces, dead, stuck to the dust like a bird when it perches.
11:68: 68- As if they had never slept therein meaning as if they had never resided in their country or their homes, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state and the meaning is: similar to someone who never existed and never resided in a place. Indeed, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord He put the apparent in place of the implicit for the sake of greater clarity, and He stated their disbelief even though it was known as a justification for the supplication against them by saying: Away with Thamud. Al-Kisa'i read it with the tanween. The explanation of this story has been presented in Al-A'raf in a way that needs to be reviewed in order to include the benefits in one of the two stories with the other. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Al-Suddi: He created you from the earth meaning: He created you from the earth. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid: And made you live therein meaning: He made you live therein. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd: And made you live therein meaning: He made you successors in it. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid: Then you only increase me in loss meaning: You only increase in loss. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Ata Al-Khurasani. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding His statement: Then they became in their homes fallen down meaning: Dead. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas: As if they had never prospered therein meaning: As if they had never lived therein. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from him: He said: As if they had never lived therein. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada: He said: As if they had never enjoyed therein.
11:69: This is the story of Lot, peace be upon him, and his people. He was the cousin of Abraham, peace be upon him. Lot's villages were in the Levant, while Abraham's were in Palestine. When God sent down the angels to punish Lot's people, they passed by Abraham and stayed with him. Everyone who stayed with him treated him well. Their visit was to give him the good report mentioned, so he thought they were guests, and they were Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil. 69- “They said, ‘Peace’” is in the accusative case with an implied verb: i.e. we greeted you with peace. “He said, ‘Peace’” is in the nominative case as a predicate of a deleted subject: i.e. your affair is peace, or in the nominative case as a subject and the predicate is deleted, and the meaning is: peace be upon you. So he did not delay i.e. Abraham to bring a roasted calf Most grammarians said that an here means until: i.e. he did not delay until he came, and it was said that it is in the accusative case due to the omission of the preposition, and the meaning is that he did not delay until he came: i.e. Abraham did not delay in bringing a calf, and ma is a negative, as Sibawayh said. Al-Farra’ said: His arrival was not delayed means how slow he was in coming. It was said that ma is a relative pronoun and is the subject and the predicate is an he came with a roasted calf. The meaning is: so what Ibrahim delayed was his coming with a roasted calf. “Haneeth” means grilled in general. It was said that what is grilled is a sea of stones without being touched by fire. It is said: Haneeth the sheep means he puts it on hot stones to cook it, so it is Haneeth. It was said that the meaning of Haneeth is fat. It was said that Haneeth is salted, and it was said that nadij is fa’il with the meaning of maf’ul. He only came to them with a calf because cows were the majority of his wealth.
11:70: 70- "When he saw that their hands did not reach it meaning that they did not extend their hands to the calf as someone who wants to eat extends his hand, he disapproved of them." It is said: I disapproved of him, I disapproved of him, and I disapproved of him: if I found him not as he expected, and from this is the saying of the poet: You denied me, but the only thing you denied of the events was gray hair and baldness. He combined the two languages, and among what he combined the two languages in is the poet’s saying: If a town denies me or I denies it, I go out with the falcon on the black sky. It was said: You disapproved of what you saw with your eyes, and you disapproved of what you saw with your heart. It was said: And they disapproved of that because their custom was that when a guest came to them and did not eat from their food, they thought that evil had come. And he felt a sense of fear from them means he felt in himself from them fear meaning fear and terror. It was said that the meaning of he felt a sense of fear is: he concealed fear in his soul, and the first is more closely related to the linguistic meaning, and from it is the saying of the poet: The mail came with a piece of paper urging him to do something, and his heart was frightened by the paper. As if he thought that they had come down to him for something he disapproved of, or to torture his people, They said, ‘Do not fear.’ They said this statement to him even though he did not speak in a way that indicated fear, but rather he felt that in himself. Perhaps they inferred his fear from signs such as the appearance of its effect on his face, or they said it to him after he said, following what he felt in himself of fear, a statement that indicated fear, as in His statement in Surat al-Hijr 15:He said, ‘Indeed, we are afraid of you.’ He did not mention that here, being satisfied with what was there. Then they explained his prohibition of fear by saying, Indeed, we were sent to the people of Lot, meaning that we were sent to them specifically. It is possible that Abraham, peace be upon him, said a statement that this would be an answer to: He said, ‘So what is the matter with you, O messengers?’ They said, ‘Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals.’
11:71: And sentence 71 - "And his wife was standing and laughing" is in the accusative case as a state. It was said: She was standing while they were talking behind the curtain, and it was said: She was standing serving the angels while he was sitting. And the laughter here is the well-known laughter that is for amazement or for joy as the majority said. And Mujahid and Ikrimah said: It is menstruation, and from it the poet said: I come to the wedding when she is purified, and I leave her one day if she is laughing. The other said: And the rabbits laughed on the rock like the blood of fear on the day of meeting The Arabs say: The rabbit laughed: if it menstruated.
