Some linguists have denied that there is in the speech of the Arabs laughed meaning menstruated. So We gave her good report of Isaac. It appears that the good report came after the laughter. Al-Farraa said: There is an inversion. The meaning is: So We gave her good report and she laughed with joy at the child. Muhammad ibn Ziyad, one of the Meccan reciters, read So she laughed with a fatha on the haa, and Al-Mahdawi denied it: And after Isaac, Jacob. Hamza, Ibn Amir and Hafs read with half of Jacob as the object of a verb indicated by So We gave her good report, as if he said: And We gave her after Isaac, Jacob. Al-Kisa’i, Al-Akhfash and Abu Hatim permitted Jacob to be in the accusative case. Al-Farraa said: The accusative case is not permissible except by repeating its letter. Sibawayh said: If you had said: I passed by Zaid the day before yesterday, and yesterday, Umar, it would have been ugly and vile, because you differentiated between the accusative and what it shares, just as you differentiate between the preposition and the accusative. The rest read it with the nominative case of Jacob as the subject and the predicate of the circumstance that preceded it. It was said: The nominative case is with the estimation of a deleted verb: meaning, it happens to her, or it is established for her. The good report was given to her here, and it was given to Abraham in the Almighty’s saying: So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy “And We gave him good tidings of a knowledgeable boy,” because each one of them deserved the good report of him because he was one of them.
11:72: And sentence 72 - "She said, 'Woe to me'" is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it were said: So what did she say? Al-Zajjaj said: Its origin is Oh woe to me, so the ya was replaced with an alif because it is lighter than the ya and the kasra. It did not mean to pray for woe upon herself, but it is a word that is often spoken by women when something happens to them that they are surprised by. The origin of woe is shame, then it became common for every terrible matter. The question in her saying Shall I give birth when I am an old woman is for astonishment: that is, how can I give birth when I am an old woman who has advanced in age? It is said: I am unable to give birth with a light and heavy Izzan and Izziza: that is, she has advanced in age. It is also said: Old woman and Ojoza. As for Ijaza with a kasra on the jeem, its meaning is that her buttocks are large. It was said that she was ninety-nine years old, and it was said that she was ninety years old. And this is my husband, an old man, that is, this is my husband Ibrahim, an old man like whom women do not get pregnant. Old man is in the accusative case as a state, and the factor in it has the meaning of a sign. Al-Nahhas said: In the reading of Abi and Ibn Masoud, it is a sheikh in the nominative case, as a predicate of the subject, or predicate after predicate, or predicate of a deleted subject. According to the first, it is ba’li instead of the demonstrative pronoun. It was said: Ibrahim was one hundred and twenty years old, and it was said: one hundred years old. This bearer of good tidings is Sarah, Ibrahim’s wife. Ibrahim had a son from his slave girl Hajar, Ishmael. Sarah wished to have a son and despaired of him because of her old age. So God gave her good tidings of him through His angels: This is indeed an amazing thing. That is, what the angels mentioned of the good tidings of having a son, despite her being at this advanced age at which nothing like her gives birth, is amazing.
11:73: And the sentence 73 - "They said, 'Do you wonder at the command of God?'" is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, and the question in it is for denial: that is, how can you wonder at the decree and destiny of God, and nothing is impossible for Him, and they only denied it to her despite the fact that what she wondered at was from the extraordinary because she was from the house of prophecy, and it is not hidden from someone like her that this is from His predestination, glory be to Him, and for this reason they said: "The mercy of God and His blessings upon you, O people of the house," that is, the mercy that encompassed everything, and the blessings, which are growth and increase, it was said that mercy is the prophecy, and the blessings are the tribes of the Children of Israel because of the prophets among them, and the erection of the people of the house is for praise or specialization, and the address was diverted from the singular form to the plural for the purpose of generalization, "He is Praiseworthy, that is, He does the reasons for His praise from His servants in abundance, Glorious," very kind to His servants with what He bestows upon them of good things, and the sentence is an explanation for His saying: "The mercy of God and His blessings upon you, O people of the house.
11:74: His saying: 74- When the terror left Abraham meaning the fear that he felt in his soul. It is said: he was terrified of something: if he was afraid, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: He was terrified by the sound of dogs, so he was subject to the evil eye out of fear and caution. "And the good tidings came to him" meaning of a son, or by their saying: Do not fear. His saying: "He argues with us about the people of Lot." Al-Akhfash and Al-Kisa'i said: If yujadilauna is in the place of jadilauna, then it is an answer to what, because it is established that its answer is in the past and not the future. An-Nahhas said: He made the future in its place just as the past is made in the place of the future in the condition. It was said: The answer is omitted, and yujadilauna is in the accusative case as a state, as Al-Farra' said, and its meaning is: So when the fear left him and the good tidings came to him, he dared to address us while he was arguing with us: meaning arguing with our messengers. It was said that the meaning is: He began to argue with us, and his arguing with them was said that when he heard their saying: "Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city," he said: Have you seen if there were fifty Muslims among them, would you destroy them? They said: No. He said: Then forty? They said: No. He said: Then twenty? They said: No. Then he said: Then ten? Then five? They said: No. He said: Then one? They said: No. He said, There is Lot in it. They said, “We know best who is in it. We will surely save him and his family.” This is the meaning of his argument about the people of Lot: that is, about their affair and their situation.
11:75: Then they praised Abraham, or God praised him and said: 75- "Indeed, Abraham was forbearing" meaning he was not hasty in matters, nor did he deal with them in a way other than what he should have done. And the one who groans a lot, and the one who turns back to God, is the one who turns back to God. And in Bara'ah speech, it is mentioned as the one who groans.
11:76: His statement: 76- "O Abraham, turn away from this." This is what the angels said to him: meaning, turn away from this argument about a matter that has been completed, and the pen has dried on it, and the decree has come true. "Indeed, the command of your Lord has come." The pronoun refers to the matter, and the meaning of the coming of God's command is the coming of His punishment that He has decreed for them, and His decree has preceded it. "And indeed, there will come upon them a punishment that cannot be repelled." That is, neither supplication nor argument can repel it, rather it will inevitably befall them, and will descend upon them in any case, neither averted nor repelled. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Muhsin regarding the guests of Abraham, he said: There were four of them: Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and Raphael. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: with a roasted calf, he said: Cooked. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, he said: Roasted. Abu Al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority, he said: Salted. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: The roasted calf is that which is cooked with stones. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Yazid Al-Basri regarding his statement: But when he saw that their hands did not reach it, he said: He did not see their hands, so he did not recognize them. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: He did not recognize them, he said: When a guest came to them and he did not eat from their food, they thought that he had not brought good, and that he was thinking evil to himself, then they told him what they had brought, and his wife laughed. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Mughira who said: In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas`ud, and his wife is standing while he is sitting. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, and his wife is standing, he said: serving the guests of Ibrahim. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: When Ibrahim felt fear in himself, they told him what they had come up with, so his wife laughed in amazement at the heedlessness of the people of Lot, and at the torment that had befallen them. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so she laughed, he said: so she menstruated and she was ninety-eight years old. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, so she laughed, he said: she menstruated and she was ninety-something years old, and Ibrahim was one hundred years old. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: she menstruated. Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn `Umar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And after Isaac, Jacob, he said: He is the son’s son. Ibn Al-Anbari narrated in the Book of Waqf and Ibtida’ on the authority of Hassan bin Abjar who said: I was with Ibn Abbas when a man from Hudhayl came, so Ibn Abbas said to him: What happened to so-and-so? He said: He died and left four sons and three descendants, so Ibn Abbas said: And We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob, he said: The son’s son. Ibn Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he forbade adding to the response to the greeting: “Upon you be peace and the mercy of God and His blessings,” and reciting this verse: The mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And when the fear had departed from Abraham, he said: The fear, He disputes with us concerning the people of Lot, he said: He disputes with us. Abdul Razzaq and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada in the interpretation of Al-Mujadalah that he said to them on that day: Tell me, if there are fifty Muslims among them? They said: If there are fifty among them, we will not punish them. He said: Forty? They said: And forty. He said: Thirty? They said: And thirty until they reached ten. They said: If there are ten among them, we will not punish them. He said: What people do not have ten good among them? Qatada said: There were four thousand thousand people in the village of Lot, or whatever God willed of that. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When the angels came to Abraham, they said to Abraham: If there are five among them who pray, the punishment will be lifted from them. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Amr bin Maymun that he said: The compassionate, the merciful. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The one who repents is the one who turns to obeying God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said: The one who repents is the one who is sincere.
11:77: When the angels left Abraham, and there were four farsakhs between Abraham and the village of Lot, they came to Lot. When Lot saw them, and they were in the form of handsome young men, he said: "It was bad for him 77- It was bad for him" means their coming was bad for him. It is said: "It was bad for him, and the origin of It was bad for them is It was bad for them". The movement of the "waw was transferred to the seen, so the waw was changed to a ya, and when the hamza was softened, its movement was placed on the ya". Nafi', Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa'i and Abu Amr read with the "seen as a dammah, and he was constricted by them". Al-Azhari said: The "dhira' is used in place of taqa", and its origin is that the camel stretches its hand in its walk according to the breadth of its stride: that is, it extends it, so if it is loaded with more than it can bear, its "taqa" is made a metaphor for lack of capacity and energy and the severity of the matter. It was said: It is from "dhira'u" vomiting if it overcomes him and he is unable to hold it back. The meaning is that he felt distressed when he saw the angels in that form, fearing for them from his people because of what he knew of their immorality and their committing of the abomination of sodomy. And he said, ‘This is a difficult day,’ meaning a severe one. The poet said: If you do not accept Bakr bin Wael, you will have a difficult day in Iraq. It is said: ‘Asib, ‘Asib, and ‘Asub, in the form of a large number: meaning a hated day in which evil gathers. From this it is said: ‘Asaba and ‘ASaba 34:meaning those who gather together in word, and a man who is ‘Asib: meaning those who gather together in creation.
11:78: 78- And his people came rushing to him meaning they came to Lot. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. The meaning of they rush to him is they hasten to him. Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra' and other linguists said: Hastening can only be hastening with trembling. It is said: The man rushed in haste, meaning he hurried in a trembling from cold, anger or fever. Muhalhil said: They came running, prisoners of their breasts, despite their noses. It was said that they rush: they run, and it was said: it is a walk between jogging and running. Meaning: When the people of Lot heard of the angels coming in that form, they rushed to him, as if they were pushing him away to demand immorality from his guests. And before that, they used to do evil deeds. That is, before the arrival of the messengers at this time, they used to do evil deeds. It was said: And before Lot, they used to do evil deeds. That is, it was their custom to go to men. So when they came to Lot and intended to go to his guests for that deed, Lot stood up to them, defending them. He said, ‘O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you.’ That is, marry them and leave what you are seeking of immorality with my guests. He had three daughters, and it was said two, and they used to ask him to marry them to them, but he refused because of their wickedness. They had two masters who were obeyed, so he wanted to marry them to his two daughters. It was said that he meant by his saying, These are my daughters, the women as a whole, because the prophet of the people was a father to them. A group said: This statement from him was only in the way of defense and did not mean the truth. The meaning of They are purer for you is more permissible and more pure. Purification is to be free from what is not permissible. The form purer does not indicate preference, but rather it is like God is greater. Al-Hasan and Isa bin Omar read purer in the accusative case, while the rest read it in the nominative case. The reason for the accusative case is that the demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is my daughters. "They is a separating pronoun, and purer" is a state. Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and Al-Akhfash forbade such a thing, because the separating pronoun, which is called a pillar, only comes between two statements such that the statement is not complete without what comes after it, such as "Zayd was your brother. So fear God and do not disgrace me in my guest," meaning fear God by leaving what you want of immorality with them, and do not humiliate me and bring shame upon me in my guest. The word "guest" is used for one, two, and a group, because it is originally a source, and from this is the saying of the poet: Never fail to provide the butcher's knife for the guest, and the guest is the most deserving visitor. It is permissible to use the dual or plural forms, but the former is more common. It is said: A man was disgraced meaning he was ashamed, humiliated, or disgraced. Khazā means he was disgraced. The meaning of fi difi is fi difi for my guest. So the guest’s disgrace is the host’s disgrace. Then he rebuked them and said: Is there not among you a man of sound mind who will guide you to abandon this ugly act and prevent you from it.
11:79: So they responded to him, turning away from what he advised them to do and guided them to, saying: 79- We have no right to your daughters meaning we have no desire or need for them, because whoever needs something, it is as if he has obtained some kind of right in it. The meaning of what they attributed to him of knowledge is that he knew of their eagerness to have intercourse with males and their intense desire for them, so from this perspective they are as if they have no need for women. It is possible that they meant: We have no right to marry them, because no one marries them and takes them in marriage except a believer, and we will never believe. It was said: They had proposed to his daughters before he rejected them, and it was their custom that whoever proposed to a rejected one, the fiancée would never be permissible. And you know what we want of having intercourse with males.
11:80: Then when he knew their determination to commit the immorality and that they would not abandon what they had asked for 80- He said, 'If only I had power over you,' and the answer to if is omitted, and the meaning is: I would defend you from them and prevent you from them, and this from him, peace be upon him, is in the way of wishing: that is, if I found a helper and supporter, so he called what he is strengthened by power or take refuge in a strong support in apposition to what comes after if because of the meaning of the verb in it, and the meaning is: If I had the power to repel you or take refuge in a strong support. And it was read or take refuge with victory in apposition to power as if he said: If only I had power over you, or take refuge in a strong support, and what he meant by the strong support is the clan, and what he and those with him are protected from them, and it was said that he meant by power the son, and by the strong support: whoever supports him other than his son, and it was said that he meant by power: his strength in himself.
11:81: And when the angels heard him say this statement, and found that his people had overcome him and he was unable to defend them 81- They said, 'O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you.' They first told him that they were messengers of his Lord, then they gave him the good report by saying: They will never reach you. This sentence explains what came before it, because if they were messengers from God to him, his enemy would not have reached him or been able to defeat him. Then they ordered him to leave them, so they said to him: Then travel with your family during a part of the night. Nafi' and Ibn Kathir read it with a continuous chain, and others read it with a chain, and they are two eloquent languages. God Almighty said: And the night when it departs. And He said: Glory be to Him who took you by night. The poet combined the two languages and said: Al-Nadir neighborhood and the housewife took him prisoner but she was not a prisoner It was said: Isra is for travelling from the beginning of the night, and sara is for travelling from the end of it, and the part of the night is a part of it. Ibn al-A'rabi said: In a part of al-Layl 92:in an hour of it, and al-Akhfash said: in the darkness of the night, and it was said: in the darkness of the night, and it was said: after the stillness of the night. It was said: The night journey only happens at night, so what is the reason for adding in a part of the night? It was said: If he did not say in a part of the night, it would have been permissible for it to be in the beginning before the darkness gathers, and that is not what is meant by and let none of you turn back meaning let him not look at what is behind him, or be occupied with what he has left behind of money or other things. It was said: The reason for the prohibition of turning away is so that they do not see the torment of their people and the horror of what has befallen them, so that they may have mercy on them and sympathize with them, or so that they do not stop the journey required of them due to what happens from turning away, because the one who turns away must have a break in his journey, except your wife in the accusative case according to the reading of the majority, and Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read it in the nominative case as a substitute, so according to the first reading his wife is excluded from his saying: So travel with your family meaning travel with all of your family except your wife, so do not travel with her, so what has befallen them will befall her of the torment, which is the stoning of them because she was a disbeliever, and a group of them, including Abu Ubaid, rejected the reading of the nominative case and said: This is not correct except by raising yaltaftā and it is an attribute, because the meaning becomes, if it is substituted and made certain, that the woman is permitted to turn away, and the meaning is not like that. Al-Nahhas said: This work of Abu Ubaid and others on the likes of Abu Amr, despite its majesty and its place in Arabic, should not be, and the raising of the substitute has a correct meaning, which is that it is an exception to the prohibition of turning around: that is, none of you should turn around except your wife, for she turns around and perishes. It was said: The raising of the substitute is from one, and turning around means staying behind, not looking behind, so it is as if he said: And none of you should stay behind except your wife, for she stays behind. The resort to this far-fetched interpretation is to escape the contradiction of the two readings, and the pronoun in that what befell them will befall her is for the matter, and the sentence is the report of that their appointment is the morning this sentence is a reduction of what came before of the command to perform the Night Journey and the prohibition of turning around, and the meaning is: that the appointment of their punishment is the morning that breaks the dawn of that night, and the question in is not the morning near is for the declarative denial, and the sentence is an emphasis of the reason. And Isa bin Omar read Is not the morning with a damma on the ba and this is a language. Perhaps he made the morning the time of their destruction because the souls are calmer in it and the people are gathered in it and have not dispersed to their work.
11:82: 82- So when Our command came meaning the appointed time for the punishment to occur, or what is meant by the command is the punishment itself, We turned it upside down meaning the upside down of the villages of Lot's people, and the meaning is that He turned it upside down in this state, which is that its upside down became its downside and its downside became its upside down, and that is because Gabriel put his wing under it and raised it from the edges of the earth until it was closest to the sky, then he turned it upside down on them, And We rained down upon it stones of baked clay It was said that it is said that it rained in punishment and it rained in mercy, and it was said that they are two languages, it is said: the sky rained and it rained, this was narrated by Al-Harawi, and sijjil is the clay petrified by cooking or otherwise, and it was said that it is the very hard of stones, and it was said that sijjil is a large amount, and it was said that sijjil is a non-Arabic word, its origin is sajj and jil, and they are in Persian stone and clay, the Arabs Arabized them and made them one name, and it was said that it is from the language of the Arabs. Al-Harawi said: As-Sajjil is the name of the lowest heaven. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is weak and is refuted by its description of it as being arranged. It was also said that it is a jar suspended in the air between the heaven and the earth. It was also said that they are mountains in the sky. Al-Zajjaj said: It is from the word tasjeel for them, meaning what was written for them of punishment, so it is in the meaning of sajjil, and from this is the saying of the Most High: And what will make you know what is “sajjil? A book inscribed.” It was also said that it is from asjalatuhu meaning you gave it, so it is as if it is a punishment that they gave it. And from this is the saying of the poet: Whoever debates with me debates with a noble man who fills the bucket to the limit of distress The meaning of arranged is that it is arranged one part on top of the other, and it is said that it is one part after the other. It is said: I arranged the goods if you put some of them on top of each other, so it is arranged and arranged.
11:83: And the marked: the one that has a mark: it was said: it had something like rings on it, and it was said: written on each stone was the name of the one who was milled with it. Al-Farra' said: They claimed that it was marked with red and black on white. That is its marking, and the meaning of 83- with your Lord is in His treasuries and they are not far from the wrongdoers meaning and these described stones are not far from the wrongdoers, who are the people of Lot, or they are not far from every wrongdoer from the wrongdoers, including the infidels of Quraysh and those who supported them in their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they deserve it because of their wrongdoing. And it was said: and they are not meaning villages from the wrongdoers from those who disbelieved in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, far because they are between Ash-Sham and Madinah. And there are two opinions about the raining of stones: One of them: that it rained on the cities when Gabriel raised them. The second: that it rained on those who were not in the cities from their people and were outside of them. And reminding the distant by interpreting stones as stones or applying it to a masculine description: meaning something distant, or a distant place, or because it is a source like sighing and neighing, and sources are equal in describing masculine and feminine. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed by them and felt straitened for them. He said: He had a bad opinion of his people and felt straitened for his guests. And he said, ‘This is a difficult day.’ He said: A severe one. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: They rush to him. He said: They hasten. And before that they used to do evil deeds. He said: They used to come to men. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority that he said: They rush to him. They listen to him. Abu Al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: These are my daughters. He said: Lot did not offer his daughters to his people, neither fornication nor marriage. Rather, he said: These are your women, because when a prophet is among a people, he is their father. God the Most High said in the Qur’an: And his wives are their mothers. He is their father according to Abu’s reading. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: They were not his daughters, but they were from his nation, and every prophet is the father of his nation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair something similar. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi something similar. He said: In Abdullah’s recitation, the Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves, and he is a father to them, and his wives are their mothers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, who said: He offered them his daughters in marriage, and he wanted to protect his guests by marrying his daughters. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement, And do not disgrace me regarding my guests, he said: Do not disgrace me. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik, Is there not among you a man of sound mind? He said: A man who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong. Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Is there not among you a man of sound mind? He said: One who says, There is no god but God. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, And indeed, you know what we intend, he said: We only want men. Lot said, “If only I had power against you, or could take refuge in a strong support, he said: a strong army to fight you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, or could take refuge in a strong support, he said: a clan. It has been proven in Al-Bukhari and others from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will forgive Lot if he takes refuge in a strong support, and it has been narrated in other than Al-Sahih from the path of other companions. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, In parts of the night, he said: the middle of the night. They narrated on his authority that he said: in the darkness of the night. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Qatadah that he said: in a part of the night. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And let none of you look back, he said: let him not stay behind. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And let none of you look back, he said: Let none look behind him, except your wife. Abu Ubaid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Harun, who said: In the version of Ibn Masoud: So set out with your family during a part of the night, except your wife. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: But when Our command came, We turned it upside down, he said: When they woke up, Gabriel attacked their village and uprooted it from its pillars, then he put his wing in and carried it on the inside of his wing with what was in it, then he ascended with it to the heavens until the people of the heavens heard the barking of their dogs, then he turned it over, and the first thing to fall from it was its canopy, so no people were afflicted with what afflicted them, then God blinded their eyes, then their village was turned over, and He rained down upon them stones of baked clay. The commentators have mentioned long and conflicting narrations and stories about how the people of Lot perished, and there is no benefit in mentioning them, especially since those who said something like that and the perishing of the people of Lot are long and cannot find a sound chain of transmission for such a thing, and most of that is taken from the People of the Book, and their situation in the narration is well known. We have been commanded not to believe them nor to disbelieve them, so know this, for it is the reason for our deletion of many of these narrations that are in the stories of the prophets and their people. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And it is not far from the wrongdoers, he said: He terrifies the Quraysh with it lest what happened to the people befall them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: From the oppressors of the Arabs, if they do not believe, then they will be punished with it. Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: From the oppressors of this nation.
11:84: And We sent to Madyan, who were the people of Shu'ayb, their brother in lineage Shu'ayb, and they named Madyan after their father, who was Madyan bin Ibrahim, and it was said after the name of their city. An-Nahhas said: Madyan is not declined because it is the name of a city, and we have already discussed this in Al-A'raf in a more detailed manner than here, and we have already explained He said, O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him at the beginning of the surah, and this sentence is a new sentence, as if it was said: What did Shu'ayb say to them when God sent him to them? Shu'aib, peace be upon him, was called the orator of the prophets because of his good argument with his people. He first ordered them to worship God Almighty, who is the only God with no partner. Then he forbade them from reducing the measure and the weight, because they were, with their disbelief, people of cheating. When a seller brought them food, they would take an extra measure, and when something weighed reached them, they would take an extra weight. When they sold, they sold with a lesser measure and a lesser weight. The phrase I see you in good health is an explanation for the prohibition: that is, do not reduce the measure and the weight, because I see you in good health: that is, with wealth and abundance in provision. So do not change God's blessing upon you by disobeying Him and harming His servants. In this blessing is what will make you independent of taking people's money unjustly. Then he mentioned another reason after this reason, saying: And I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing Day. This reason reminds them of the punishment of the Hereafter, just as the first reason reminds them of the pleasures of this world. He described the Day as encompassing, and what is meant is the punishment, because the punishment will occur on the Day, and the meaning of encompassing is The torment of this day is that none of them will escape from it, and they will find no refuge or escape from it. Today is the Day of Resurrection, and it was said: It is the day of vengeance against them in this world with the shout.
11:85: Then he emphasized the prohibition of reducing the measure and weight by saying: 85- And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice. Fulfillment is completion, and justice is fairness, which is the absence of excess and deficiency, even though excess over fullness is a virtue and goodness, but it is above what the name justice indicates, and the prohibition of deficiency, even though it necessitates fullness, in the mutual support of the two meanings there is a strong exaggeration and good emphasis. Then he added emphasis to that by saying: And do not deprive people of their due rights. The interpretation of this has already been mentioned in Al-A'raf, and in it is the prohibition of deprivation in general, and things are more general than what is measured and weighed, so deprivation by reducing the measure and weight is included in this primarily, and it was said: Deprivation is the tax specifically, then he said: And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption. Its interpretation has also been mentioned in Al-Baqarah, and deprivation on the earth includes everything that occurs in it of harm to people, so what is in the context of deprivation of the measure and weight is included in it, and he restricted it to the situation, which is his saying: Corrupters to remove what was in the form of evil on earth, and what is meant by it is reform, as happened with Al-Khidr in the ship.
11:86: 86- What remains from God is better for you meaning what He leaves for you of what is lawful after fulfilling rights in justice is more good and blessed than what you leave for yourselves of cheating, misappropriation, and corruption on earth. Its meaning was mentioned by Ibn Jarir and other commentators. Mujahid said: What remains from God is His obedience. Al-Rabi' said: His command. Al-Farra' said: His observation. This was said in His statement: If you are believers because that only benefits the believer, not the disbeliever, or what is meant by the believers here are those who believed in Shu'aib. And I am not a guardian over you I protect you from falling into sins such as cheating, misappropriation, and others, or I protect your deeds and hold you accountable for them and reward you for them.
11:87: And the sentence 87 - They said, 'O Shu'aib, does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers used to worship?' is a new answer to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did they say to Shu'aib? Your prayer was read in the singular, and that we should abandon is in the accusative case. Al-Kisa’i said: Its position is in the accusative case because of the implied Ba’, and what they mean by what their fathers worship is what they used to worship of idols, and the question is to denounce and mock him, because prayers, according to them, are not among the good deeds that are said to the one who does them when wanting to soften his heart and ease his difficulty, as is said to someone who gives a lot of charity if he does something that is not appropriate for what is right: I have given you charity, I have ordered you to do this. It was said: What is meant by prayer here is recitation, and it was said: What is meant by it is religion, and it was said: What is meant by prayers is following it, and from it is the one who prays who follows the previous one, and this from them is an answer to Shu’aib about his ordering them to worship God alone, and their saying: Or that we do with our wealth as we please is an answer to him about his ordering them to fulfill the measure and weight, and his forbidding them from decreasing them and from cheating people and from spreading mischief in the land, and this sentence is connected to what is in what our fathers worship. The meaning is: Your prayers command you to leave what our fathers worship and command you to leave doing with our wealth as we please of taking and giving, increasing and decreasing. It was read We do with our wealth what we wish with the superlative in both of them. An-Nahhas said: So the aw in this reading is for the conjunction with the first an, and the meaning is: Your prayers command you to do with our wealth what you wish. It was read naf'al with the nun and ma shaa with the superlative, and its meaning is: Your prayers command you to do with our wealth what you wish and leave what we wish and what is agreed upon between us, then they described him with two great descriptions and said: Indeed, you are the forbearing and the rightly guided in a mocking manner, because they believe that he is against them, or they mean that you are the forbearing and the rightly guided in yourself and in your belief, and their meaning is: that what you have forbidden us from and ordered us to do contradicts what you believe in yourself of forbearance and rightly guided, and it was said that they said that not in a mocking manner but rather it is like that with them, and they denied him the command and prohibition from them with what contradicts forbearance and rightly guided in their belief. The interpretation of forbearance and rightly guided has been presented.
11:88: And the sentence 88- He said, O my people, have you considered, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord is a new sentence like the sentences before it, and the meaning is: Tell me if I am upon clear proof from my Lord regarding what I have commanded you and forbidden you and provided me from it meaning from His grace and the treasuries of His kingdom a good provision meaning abundant, ample, lawful and good, and he, peace be upon him, had a lot of money, and it was said that he meant by provision prophethood, and it was said wisdom, and it was said knowledge, and it was said success, and the answer to the condition is omitted and indicated by the context of the speech, its estimation is: Should I leave your command and prohibition or do you say about me what you say, by which you intend to ridicule and mock And I do not intend to go against you in what I have forbidden you meaning and what I intend by my prohibition of you from cheating and shortchanging is that I go against you in what I have forbidden you and do it without you, it is said: He went against him to such and such if he intended it but turned away from it, and I went against him from such and such is the opposite of that I only intend reform meaning I do not intend By commanding and forbidding except to reform you and remove corruption in your religion and your dealings as much as I am able as much as my ability and capacity allow and my success is not but through God meaning I did not become successful, a guide, a prophet and a rightly guided except through the support of God the Almighty and His ability and His granting me upon Him I have relied in all my affairs, including your command and prohibition and to Him I turn meaning I return in all the matters that befall me and I entrust all my affairs to what He chooses for me from His judgment and destiny. It was said that its meaning is: and to Him I return in the Hereafter. It was said that turning is supplication, and its meaning is: and to Him I supplicate.
11:89: His saying: 89- And O my people, do not let my dissent lead you astray. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is, do not let my dissent lead you to be afflicted with punishment as it afflicted those who came before you. It was also said that its meaning is: Do not let my dissent lead you to be afflicted with punishment, and dissent means enmity, and from this is the saying of Al-Akhtal: Is there anyone who can convey my message? How did you find the taste of discord? And that there should befall you is in the accusative case as a second object of to cause you to sin "like that which befell the people of Noah of drowning or the people of Hud of the wind or the people of Salih" of the shout. The interpretation of "to cause you to sin and the interpretation of discord" have already been presented. "And the people of Lot are not far from you" may mean that their place is not far from your place, or their time is not far from your time, or they are not far from you in the reason that necessitates their punishment, which is absolute disbelief. The word "far was singled out for something similar to what was presented in and it is not far from the wrongdoers."
11:90: Then after terrifying them with the punishment, He ordered them to seek forgiveness and repent, saying: 90- "And seek forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving." The explanation of seeking forgiveness and the order of repentance have been presented at the beginning of the Surah, and the explanation of the Merciful has been presented, and what is meant here is that He is the One with great mercy to those who repent, and the Loving is the One who loves. It was said in As-Sahah: I loved the man, I loved him with love: if I loved him, and the Loving is the One who loves, and the Loving, the Loving, and the Loving: love, and the meaning here is that He does to His servants what one who is very loving does to the one he loves, from kindness to him and bringing good to him and repelling evil from him. And in this there is an explanation for what preceded it from the command to seek forgiveness and repent.
11:91: And sentence 91 - They said, 'O Shu'aib, we do not understand much of what you say'" is a new sentence like the previous sentences, and the meaning is: You bring us something we have no knowledge of, such as information about unseen matters, such as resurrection and the Hereafter, and we do not understand it: that is, we understand it as we understand present, observable matters, so the denial of understanding according to this is literal and not metaphorical. And it was said: They said that out of aversion to hearing it, and disdain for the speech, even though it was understood by them and known to them, so the denial of understanding is not literal but metaphorical. It is said that he understood, he understands, if he understood, understanding, and jurisprudence. Al-Kisa'i narrated "fiqhanan", and it is said that he became a jurist. "And indeed, we see you weak among us" meaning that you do not have the strength to be able to protect yourself from us and be able to oppose us. And it was said: What is meant is that he is weak in his body, as Ali bin Isa said, and it was said: that he was afflicted with his eyesight. Al-Nahhas said: The linguists have narrated that Himyar says to a blind person: weak, meaning he has become weak due to the loss of his sight, just as he is called blind: meaning he has been harmed by the loss of his sight. It has also been said that the weak person is the humiliated one, and it is close to the first statement: And if it were not for your people, we would have stoned you. A man’s people are his clan, whom he relies on and is strengthened by. From this comes the word rahit for the jerboa’s hole, because he trusts in it and hides his child in it. The word raht refers to three to ten people. They only made his people a barrier against harming him, despite their small number and the infidels being thousands in number, because they were of their religion, so they left it out of respect for them, not out of fear of them. Then they confirmed what they described him as weak by saying: And you are not mighty over us, so that we would refrain from you because of your might with us. Rather, we left stoning you because of the might of your people over us. The meaning of lamjamanaka is we would have killed you by stoning. When they killed a person, they would stone him with stones. It has also been said that the meaning of lamjamanaka is we would have cursed you. From this comes the saying: The curly-haired: Our translations are so bitter that we become like a racehorse Stoning is used to mean cursing, and from it comes the cursed devil.
11:92: And the sentence 92 - He said, O my people, is my family more honorable to you than God? is a new sentence. Rather, he said, is more honorable to you than God, and he did not say, is more honorable to you than me, because denying honor to him and affirming it for his people, as indicated by the pronoun giving the letter of negation, is belittling him, and belittling the prophets of God is belittling God, the Almighty. Their speech included that his family was more honorable to them than God, so he denounced that to them and was amazed by it and forced them to do something that they could not escape from nor get out of in the form of a question. In this there is strength of argumentation, clarity of debate, and throwing stones at the opponent that is not hidden, and for some reason Shu'aib was called the orator of the prophets, and the pronoun in and you took him refers back to God, the Almighty. Meaning: And you have taken God Almighty, because of your lack of respect for His Prophet whom He sent to you, behind your backs, meaning cast aside and behind your backs, not caring about him. It has also been said that the meaning is: And you have taken the command of God which He commanded me to convey to you, which is what I have brought to you, behind your backs. It is said: I made His command behind your backs, if I fell short in it. Behind is attributed to the back, and the kasra is to change the attribution. Indeed, my Lord encompasses what you do, nothing of your words and actions is hidden from Him.
11:93: 93- "And O my people, work according to your position. Indeed, I am working. You will soon know." When he saw their insistence on disbelief and their determination to adhere to the religion of their fathers, and the ineffectiveness of the sermon on them, he threatened them that they would work to the best of their ability and the limit of their capacity. It is said: to be able to do means to be able to do it. He informed them that he was working according to what he could and what God had destined for him. Then he exaggerated the threat and warning by saying: You will soon know meaning the consequence of what you are doing of worshipping other than God and harming His servants. A similar example has been presented in Al-An'am. Who will be visited by a punishment that will disgrace him? "Who is in the accusative case with you will know": meaning you will know who is the one who will be visited by the disgraceful punishment that will affect humiliation, scandal and disgrace. "And who is a liar is in apposition to who will be visited". The meaning is: You will know who is the one being punished and who is the liar? And in it is an allusion to their lie in their saying: If it were not for your people, we would have stoned you, and you are not powerful over us. It was said: Min is the subject and what follows it is its clause, and the predicate is omitted, and the meaning is: Whoever is a liar will know his lie and taste the consequences of his action. Al-Farra’ said: The reason for it being used in man huwa kazih is because they do not say man qayyim whoever stands, rather they say man qam whoever stands, man yaqūm whoever stands, and man qayyim whoever stands, so they added huwa whoever stands so that it would be a sentence that takes the place of fa’l verb and yaf’ul whoever does. An-Nahhas said: The opposite of this statement is indicated by the poet: From my messenger to Thuraya, I am fed up with abandoning her and the book. And wait, for I am with you, watching. That is, wait, for I am with you, waiting for what God will decide between us.
11:94: 94- And when Our command came, We saved Shu'aib and those who believed with him meaning when Our punishment came or Our command to punish them came, We saved Shu'aib and his followers who believed in him by a mercy from Us to them because of their belief, or by a mercy from Us to them: which is their guidance to faith and those who did wrong were seized by the blast that Gabriel shouted at them until their souls left their bodies, and in Al-A'raf so the earthquake seized them and so in Al-'Ankabut. We have already mentioned that the earthquake is an earthquake, and that it follows the blast due to the surging of the air leading to it and they became in their homes fallen down meaning dead.
11:95: Its interpretation and the interpretation of 95- As if they had never slept therein were presented shortly, as was the interpretation of Alas, away with Midian, as far as Thamud were far away. Al-Kisa'i narrated that Abu Abd al-Rahman read: As far as Thamud were far away with a damma on the 'ayn. Al-Mahdawi said: From the damma on the 'ayn of ba'dat, it is a language used for good and evil, and ba'dat with a kasra according to the reading of the majority is used for evil in particular, and here it means a curse. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, I see you in good health, he said: The low prices, and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing Day, he said: The high prices. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority: The remainder of God, he said: The provision of God. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada: The remainder of God is better for you, he said: Your portion from your Lord is better for you. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Obedience to God. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-A’mash regarding his statement: Your prayer commands you, he said: Your recitation. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Ahnaf: Shu’ayb was the prophet who prayed the most. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: or that we do with our wealth as we please, he said: He forbade them from cutting up these dinars and dirhams, so they said: They are our wealth, we do with them as we please. If we wish, we cut them up, if we wish, we burn them, and if we wish, we throw them away. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar from Muhammad Ibn Ka’b. They also narrated something similar from Zayd Ibn Aslam. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Abd Ibn Hamid narrated something similar from Sa’id Ibn Al-Musayyab. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided, he said: They say that you are neither forbearing nor rightly guided. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Mocking him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: And provided me from it a good provision, he said: What is lawful. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And I do not wish to go against you in that from which I forbid you, he said: He says: I did not forbid you from a matter and then commit it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And to Him I turn, he said: To Him I return. Abu Nu`aym narrated in Al-Hilyah “on the authority of Ali who said: He said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: Say: God is my Lord, then be steadfast. I said: My Lord is God, and my success is only with God. Upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn. He said: May knowledge be pleasant for you, O Abu Al-Hasan. He has drunk knowledge thoroughly and I have drunk it thoroughly.” In its chain of transmission is Muhammad ibn Yusuf Al-Kadimi. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada: Do not let my dissension lead you to sin, do not let separation from me lead you to separation. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: My dissension is my enmity. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: Do not let my enmity lead you to sin. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: {And the people of Lot are not far from you} that he said: They were only recent arrivals after Noah and Thamud. Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr {And indeed, We see you among us, weak} that he said: He was blind, and he only went blind because of his crying out of love for God Almighty. Al-Wahidi and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Shaddad ibn Aws that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Shuaib, peace be upon him, cried out of love for God until he went blind.” Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, al-Khatib and Ibn Asakir narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {And indeed, We see you among us, weak} that he said: He was blind. Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Salih. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Sufyan regarding his statement: {And indeed, We see you among us, weak} that he said: He was blind, and he was called the orator of the prophets. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi that he said: Its meaning is that you are only one. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib that he gave a sermon and recited this verse about Shuaib: And indeed, we see you among us weak. He said: He was blind, so they attributed weakness to him. And had it not been for your people, we would have stoned you. Ali said: By God, there is no god but Him, they did not fear the majesty of their Lord; they only feared their tribe. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said about the verse: Do not fear Him. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: You took it lightly.
11:96: What is meant by the verses is the Torah, and the clear authority is the goats. It was said that what is meant by the verses are the nine mentioned in other than this place, and the clear authority is the staff, and although it is one of the nine, since it was the most dazzling of them, it was mentioned alone. It was said that what is meant by the verses is what gives conjecture, and the clear authority is what gives certainty about what Moses brought. It was said that they are both an expression of one thing: that is, we sent him with what combines the description of being a verse and being a clear authority. It was said that the clear authority is what Moses brought to Pharaoh in the dialogue between them.
11:97: 97- To Pharaoh and his chiefs meaning, We sent him with that to these people. It was previously mentioned that the chiefs are the nobles of the people, and He only mentioned them specifically without the rest of the people, because they are their followers in issuing and bringing, and He singled out these chiefs without Pharaoh by saying: So they followed the command of Pharaoh on his command to them to disbelieve, because the state of Pharaoh in disbelief is a clear matter, since the disbelief of his people from the nobles and others is based on his disbelief, and it is possible that what is meant by Pharaoh's command is his affair and his method, so it includes disbelief and others. And Pharaoh's command was not right meaning there is no right guidance in it at all, rather it is misguidance and error, and right means the guide, and the attribution is metaphorical, or it means the one with right guidance, and in it is an allusion that the guidance is in the matter of Moses.
11:98: 98- He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection from the root word qadamah meaning to precede him: that is, he will be ahead of them on the Day of Resurrection, preceding them to the punishment of the Fire, just as he was ahead of them in this world. So he will lead them to the Fire, that is, he will continue to precede them and they will follow him until he leads them to the Fire. He used the past tense to indicate that it will happen, then he condemned the water to which he led them, saying: And what an evil watering place it is, because the one who comes to the water that he calls the watering place only goes to it to quench the heat of thirst and remove his thirst, and the Fire is the opposite of that.
11:99: Then He blamed them after blaming the place they were going to, saying: 99- And they were pursued in this world by a curse meaning the people of Pharaoh were pursued absolutely, or the leaders in particular, or they and Pharaoh in this world by a great curse: meaning expulsion and banishment and on the Day of Resurrection meaning and they were pursued by the curse of the Day of Resurrection, all the people of the place of assembly will curse them, then He made the curse a support for them in a mocking manner, saying: What an evil support is that which is provided. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Ubaidah said: I provided him with a support: I granted him security and gave him, and the name of the gift is support: meaning what an evil gift, and assistance is what they gave them and helped them with, and what is specifically blamed is omitted: meaning their support, and it is the curse that they were pursued in this world and the hereafter as if it were a curse after a curse that extends the other to the first and perpetuates it. Al-Mawardi mentioned a story on the authority of Al-Asma’i that Al-Rafd, with the fat-ha, means the cup, and with the kasra, means what is in it of drink, so it is as if he was criticizing what they draw from the fire, and this is more appropriate to the situation. It was said that Al-Rafd is the increase: meaning, what a bad thing they are given after drowning, and it is the increase, as Al-Kalbi said.
11:100: And the reference in His saying: 100- "This is from the report of the towns. We relate it to you" meaning what God the Almighty narrated in this Surah of the report of the previous nations and what they did with their prophets: meaning it is narrated to you, one story after another. The meaning of the stories has been explained previously, and the pronoun in from it refers to the towns: meaning some of the towns are standing, and some of them are harvested. The standing is what was standing on its trellises, and the harvest is what has no trace. It was said: the standing is the inhabited, and the harvest is the ruin. It was said: the standing is the villages that are empty of their trellises, and the harvest is the uprooted, meaning harvested. He likened the towns to the crop standing on its stem and cut off. The poet said: People are divided among themselves like crops, some of which are standing and some of which are harvested.
11:101: 101- “And We did not wrong them” by what We did to them of punishment but they wronged themselves by disbelief and sins so their gods did not avail them meaning their idols that they worshipped instead of God did not ward off any of the punishment when the command of your Lord came meaning when His punishment came and they did not increase them except in destruction: destruction and loss: meaning the idols that they worshipped did not increase them except in destruction and loss, and they believed that they helped them to obtain benefits.
11:102: 102- And thus is the taking of your Lord Al-Jahdari and Talha bin Masraf read taken as a verb. Others read taken as a source. When He takes the towns while they are wrongdoers meaning their people are wrongdoers. His taking meaning His punishment of the disbelievers is painful and severe meaning painful and severe.
11:103: 103- Indeed in that is a sign meaning in God Almighty’s taking of the people of the towns, or in the stories that He told His Messenger as a lesson and admonition for him who fears the punishment of the Hereafter because they are the ones who take lessons and are admonished by admonitions. The reference in His saying: That is a Day when the people will be gathered is to the Day of Resurrection, which is indicated by mentioning the Hereafter, that the people will be gathered on it for accountability and recompense. And that meaning the Day of Resurrection is a witnessed Day meaning that the people of the gathering will witness it, or the creation will witness it, so the circumstance was expanded by making it act like a direct object. Al-Wahidi said: According to all commentators 3- A witness and what is witnessed What is meant by the witness is whoever witnesses that day from the creation: that is, whoever is present on it, and what is meant by what is witnessed is the wonders that are witnessed on that day. A group of the Companions and Followers said that the witness is Friday, and that it witnesses against every worker for what he did on it, and what is witnessed is the Day of Arafah, because people witness the Hajj season on it, and the angels attend it. Al-Wahidi said: This is the majority opinion. Al-Qushayri narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ibn Al-Zubayr that the witness is the Day of Sacrifice. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: The witness is the Day of Tarwiyah, and what is witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Al-Nakha'i said: The witness is the Day of Arafah, and what is witnessed is the Day of Sacrifice. It was said that the witness is God, the Most High. Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubair said the same, based on his statement: And sufficient is God as a witness, and his statement: Say, ‘What is the greatest witness?’ Say, ‘God is Witness between me and you.’ It was also said that the witness is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, based on his statement: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? And his statement: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And his statement: And the Messenger will be a witness over you. It was also said that the witness is all the prophets based on his statement: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness? And it was also said that it is Jesus, son of Mary, based on his statement: And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them. The one witnessed according to these three statements is either the nation of Muhammad, or the nations of the prophets, or the nation of Jesus. It was also said that the witness is Adam, and the one witnessed is his offspring. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: The witness is the human being, because of His statement: Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner. Muqatil said: His limbs, because of His statement: The Day their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The witness is this nation, and the one being witnessed is all other nations, because of His statement: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over mankind. It was also said that the witness is the guardians, and the one being witnessed is the children of Adam. It was also said that it is the days and nights. It was also said that the witness is the creation, bearing witness to God’s Oneness, and the one being witnessed to as to His Oneness is God, the Exalted. An explanation of what was mentioned in the interpretation of the witness and the one being witnessed will come, and an explanation of what is the truth, God willing.
11:104: 104- And We do not delay it except for a specified term. That is, We do not delay that day except for the end of a specified term known by number, after which God Almighty has determined the occurrence of the recompense.
11:105: 105- The Day it comes The people of Medina, Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read with the ya' in the draj and deleted it in the pause. Abi and Ibn Mas'ud read with the ya' in both connected and paused. Al-A'mash read with the ya' in both, and the reason for deleting the ya' with the pause is what Al-Kisa'i said that the sound verb is stopped on like the jazm, so the ya' was deleted just as the damma is deleted. The reason for the reading of those who read with the ya' in connection is that they saw the writing of the Qur'an in this way. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh narrated that the Arabs say I do not know, so the ya' is deleted and they are bold with the kasra, and Al-Farra' recited in deleting the ya': Enough, a hand that does not befit a generous dirham and another that gives blood with the sword Al-Zajjaj said: The best grammar rule is to prove the ya’, and the meaning is: When the Day of Resurrection comes, no soul will speak meaning it will not speak. One of the two ta’s was deleted for ease: meaning no soul will speak on it except with what it has been permitted to speak. It was said: No soul will speak with an argument or intercession except with His permission Glory be to Him for it to speak with that. He combined this with His statement: This is a Day when they will not speak * Nor will they be permitted to make excuses with the difference in their conditions according to the different situations on the Day of Resurrection. And such a combination was repeated in places Among them are wretched and blessed meaning among the souls are wretched and among them are blessed. So the wretched is the one upon whom misery was written, and the blessed is the one upon whom happiness was written. The wretched is presented before the blessed because the situation is one of warning.
11:106: 106- As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire; for them therein will be sighing and sobbing. That is, as for those who have been predestined for misery, they will be settled in the Fire; for them therein will be sighing and sobbing. Al-Zajjaj said: Sighing is from intense groaning, which is very loud. He said: The linguists from Basra and Kufa claimed that sighing is like the beginning of the sound of donkeys. And sobbing is like its end. It was said that sighing is a loud sound, and sobbing is a weak sound. It was said that sighing is the expulsion of the breath, and sobbing is the return of the breath. It was said that sighing is from the chest, and sobbing is from the throat. It was said that sighing is the repetition of the breath from intense fear, and sobbing is a long, extended breath. The sentence is either a new sentence, like, What is their condition in it? or in the accusative case as a state.
11:107: 107- They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure. That is, as long as they endure. Scholars have differed in explaining the meaning of this timing, because it has been known with conclusive evidence that the punishment of the disbelievers in the Fire is eternal and will not cease for them, and it has also been proven that the heavens and the earth will go away when the days of this world come to an end. A group said: This information is in accordance with what the Arabs used to do when they wanted to exaggerate the permanence of something. He said: It is eternal as long as the heavens and the earth last. This is from His statement: I will not come to you as long as night falls, and as long as night and day differ, and as long as the doves moan, and the like. So the meaning of the verse is that they will remain there forever, with no interruption or end to it. It was said: What is meant is the heavens and earth of the Hereafter, because there has been evidence that the Hereafter has heavens and earth other than these that exist in this world, and they are eternal as long as the abode of the Hereafter lasts. Also, they must have a place to carry them and another to shade them, and they are earth and heaven. His statement: Except what your Lord wills. The scholars have differed in the meaning of this exception, and there are some statements: The first: That it is from His statement: Then in the Fire, as if he said: Except what your Lord wills of delaying a people from that. This was narrated by Abu Nadrah on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri. The second: That the exception is only for the disobedient monotheists, and that they will emerge from the Fire after a period of time, and based on this, His statement, As for those who are wretched, is general for the disbelievers and disobedient, and the exception is from eternally, and what has the meaning of from, and this is what Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Sinan, and others said. It has been proven by successive narrations that indicate the necessary knowledge that the people of monotheism will emerge from the Fire, so this was a specification for every generality. The third: That the exception is from the sighing and breathing in: that is, they will have in it sighing and breathing in except what your Lord wills, from the types of torment other than the sighing and breathing in, as Ibn Al-Anbari said. The fourth: That the meaning of the exception is that they will remain in it as long as the heavens and the earth exist, and they will not die except what your Lord wills, for He commands the Fire to consume them until they are annihilated, then God will renew their creation, this was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud. The fifth: That except has the meaning of except. The meaning is as long as the heavens and the earth remain, except for what exceeds that of eternity, as if he mentioned in their eternity what the Arabs do not have longer than it, then he added to it the perpetuity that has no end, narrated by Al-Zajjaj. Sixth: What was narrated from Al-Farra’, Ibn Al-Anbari and Ibn Qutaybah that this does not contradict the absence of will, like your saying: By God, I will strike him unless I see otherwise, and this was discussed by saying that the meaning of the verse is the ruling of their eternity except for the period that God wills, so the will has definitely occurred, and Al-Zajjaj also narrated this statement. Seventh: That the meaning is: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth remain, except for what your Lord wills of the amount of their standing in their graves and for the reckoning, narrated by Al-Zajjaj also. Eighth: That the meaning is: They will abide therein except for what your Lord wills of the increase of bliss for the people of bliss and the increase of torment for the people of Hell, narrated by Al-Zajjaj also, and Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi chose it. Ninth: That illa has the meaning of and as narrated by Al-Farra’, and the meaning is and whatever your Lord wills of the increase, Makki said: This statement is far-fetched according to the Basrans that illa has the meaning of and. Tenth: That except means kaf, and the meaning is: as your Lord wills, and from it is the saying of the Most High: And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred meaning as has already occurred. Eleventh: That this exception is only by way of the exception that the Lawgiver urged in every statement, so it is like His saying: You shall enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security. Something similar to this was narrated from Abu Ubaid, and these sayings are the sum of what we have come across from the sayings of the people of knowledge. Some of them have been discussed with discussions, and have been refuted with refutations. I have clarified that in an independent letter that I collected in response to a question that came from some of the scholars.
11:108: 108- And as for those who are blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure. Al-A'mash, Hafs, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read Sa'daw with a damma on the seen. The rest read it with a fatha on the seen, and Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim chose this reading. Sibawayh said: It is not said that someone is blessed, just as it is not said that someone is wretched, because it is one of the intransitive verbs. Al-Nahhas said: I saw Ali bin Sulayman expressing astonishment at Al-Kisa'i's reading with a damma on the seen, despite his knowledge of Arabic. This is an impermissible mistake, and the meaning of the verse is as mentioned in His statement: As for those who are wretched. His statement: Except what your Lord wills It has been known from the previous statements what is suitable for applying this exception to it, A gift that is not cut off meaning that God wills them a gift that is not cut off, and the cut off is the one that is cut off, from the word jadh which means to cut it off, and the meaning is that it extends without end. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection, meaning: He will lead them astray and lead them into the Fire. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Qatada regarding the verse: Pharaoh will go before his people until he throws them into the Fire. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then he will lead them into the Fire, he said: The entry is the entry. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: What an evil provision it is, he said: The curse of this world and the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: Some of them are standing and some are harvested, meaning inhabited villages and dormant villages. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Qatada: Some of them are standing and their place can be seen, and some are harvested but no trace of them can be seen. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Jurayj: Some of them are standing but empty on their trellises, and some are harvested and stuck to the ground. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Abu Asim: So it did not avail them, he said: It did not benefit. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement: And they did not increase them except in destruction, meaning destruction. Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, who said: Despair. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada its meaning. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Exalted, And He is Most High, that He may grant respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then he recited: “And thus is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe.” Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding His statement: Indeed in that is a sign for him who fears the punishment of the Hereafter, meaning: We will fulfill for them what We promised them in the Hereafter, just as We fulfilled for the prophets, that We will support them. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: That is a Day when the people will be gathered together, and that is a Day witnessed, he said: The Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid something similar. Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding His statement: The Day it comes, he said: That Day. At-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it, as did Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: “When the verse: ‘Some of them are wretched and some are happy,’ was revealed, I said: O Messenger of God, why should we act on something that has already been completed, or on something that has not been completed? He said: “Rather, it is about something that has already been completed and the pens have written about it, O Omar. But everyone is facilitated for what he was created for.” Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: These two are among the hidden things: the statement of God: And among them are the wretched and the blessed and The Day God will gather the messengers and say, ‘What was your response?’ They will say, ‘We have no knowledge.’ As for His statement: And among them are the wretched and the blessed, they are people from the People of the Book, from the people of this Qiblah. God will punish them with the Fire as He wills for their sins, then He will permit intercession for them, and the believers will intercede for them, and He will bring them out of the Fire and admit them into Paradise. So He called them wretched when He punished them in the Fire: “As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire. Therein they will be sighing and sobbing. They will abide eternally as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills,” when He permitted intercession for them and brought them out of the Fire and admitted them into Paradise while they were them. As for those who are blessed, meaning after the wretchedness they were in, they will be in Paradise, abiding eternally as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, meaning those who They were in the Fire.
