Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Qatada that he recited this verse: As for those who were wretched, and he said: Anas narrated to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A people will come out of the Fire, and we do not say as the people of Harura said: that whoever entered it will remain in it.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited As for those who were wretched, until His saying: Except what your Lord wills. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: If God wills, He will bring out some people from among those who were wretched from the Fire and admit them to Paradise, He will do so. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan regarding His saying: Except what your Lord wills, he said: It refers to monotheism from the people of the Qiblah. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Durais narrated Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Abu Nadrah on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, or on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, or a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding His statement: except what your Lord wills, he said: This verse is decisive for the entire Qur’an. He says that wherever there is in the Qur’an they will abide therein, it will come to pass. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Nadrah who said: The entire Qur’an ends with this verse: Indeed, your Lord is the Doer of whatever He intends. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: As long as the heavens and the earth endure, he said: For every Paradise there is a heaven and an earth. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of al-Suddi. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of al-Hasan as well. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba’th wa’l-Nushur on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: except what your Lord wills, he said: Your Lord willed that these people should abide in the Fire and that these people should abide in Paradise. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Except what your Lord wills, he said: God made an exception for the Fire to consume them. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: Then came after that from the will of God what abrogated it, so He revealed in Medina: Indeed, those who disbelieved and did wrong - God will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way, to the end of the verse, so hope was lost for the people of the Fire that… They will come out of it, and He has made eternal life obligatory for them. And His statement: And as for those who are blessed the verse. He said: Then came after that from the will of God what abrogated it, so He revealed in Medina: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens until His statement: a deep shade so He made eternal life obligatory for them. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from al-Hasan who said: Umar said: If the people of Hell remained in Hell for as long as the sand of Alij would be, they would have a day when they would come out. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: A day will come upon Hell when no one will remain in it, and he recited: And as for those who are wretched the verse. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibrahim who said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that is more hopeful for the people of Hell than this verse: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. He said: Ibn Mas’ud said: A time will come upon it when its gates will be shaken. Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Sha’bi who said: Hell is the quickest of the two abodes to be populated and the quickest to be destroyed. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: except what your Lord wills, he said: God knows best about its dual form as it occurred. It has been narrated on the authority of a group of the Salaf, such as what was mentioned by Umar, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas`ud, such as Ibn Abbas, Abdullah ibn Umar, Jabir and Abu Sa`id from the Companions, and on the authority of Abu Majlaz, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others from the Followers. A hadith was mentioned in this regard in the Great Lexicon of At-Tabarani on the authority of Abu Umamah Sadi bin Ajlan Al-Bahili, and its chain of transmission is weak. The author of Al-Kashshaf spoke in this regard in a way that he had the capacity to leave out, and in remaining silent about it there is sufficient, so he said: Do not be deceived by the statement of the Jabriyyah that what is meant by the exception is the exit of the people of major sins from the Fire, for the second exception calls out their denial and records their fabrications. What do you think of a people who rejected the Book of God when some of the constants were narrated to them on the authority of Ibn Amr: A day will come upon Hell when its doors will be slammed shut and there will be no one in it. Then he said: And I say that Ibn Amr did not have anything to occupy him with his two swords and his fighting with them against Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, from transmitting this hadith. And I say: As for the criticism of those who said that the people of major sins will be removed from the Fire, the one who said that, O poor man, is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as is authentically reported from him in the books of Islam, which are the books of the pure Sunnah, and as is authentically reported from him in other books through a group of companions who reach the number of continuous reports. So what is wrong with you criticizing people who knew what you did not know and acted according to what you did from a long distance away? And what prevents the exception from being interpreted as what the many authentic evidences have brought, as the majority of scholars from the early and later generations have stated? As for what you thought, that the second exception calls out their denial and records their fabrication, there is no calling out or contradiction. And what prevents the exception in the two places from being interpreted as referring to the sinners of this nation? The first exception is interpreted as meaning except what your Lord wills, regarding the sinners of this nation being removed from the Fire, and the second exception is interpreted as meaning except what your Lord wills, regarding their not remaining eternally in Paradise as others remain eternally, and that is because their remaining eternally in it is delayed for the amount of time they spent in the Fire. And this has been said by some of the scholars we have mentioned before, and with it Ibn Abbas said: The scholar of the nation. As for the criticism of the companion of the Messenger of God, the preserver of his Sunnah, and the worshipper of the Companions, Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with him, where are you going, O Mahmoud? Do you know what you have done, and into which valley you have fallen? And on which side did you fall? And who are you to ascend to this place and reach for the heavens with your short hands and lame leg? Did you not have in the breaking of your students from the people of grammar and language what would prevent you from entering into what you do not know and speaking about what you do not understand? Oh God, it is amazing what deficiency in the science of narration and distance from knowing it to the furthest place of disgrace does to one who does not know his own worth and does not stop it where God Almighty stopped it.
11:109: When God the Almighty finished telling the stories of the infidels and explaining the state of the happy and the miserable, He comforted His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, by explaining the state of the infidels among his people, within the prohibition for him from doubting that what they worship is neither beneficial nor harmful nor has any effect on anything. The letter nun was omitted in la tak due to frequent use, and doubt means suspicion, and the reference to these is to the infidels of his time, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that the meaning is: Do not be in doubt about the invalidity of what these people worship, and it was said: Do not be in doubt about the evil end of them. There is no objection to interpreting all of these meanings, and this prohibition for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, is an exposure to others who have some doubt, because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, never doubted that. Then God the Almighty explained to him that the deities of these people are like the deities of their fathers, or that their worship is like the worship of their fathers before, and in this there is an exception explaining the prohibition of doubt. Meaning: They are equal in associating partners with God and worshipping other than Him, so do not let there be in your heart any resentment over what you see from your people, for they are like the sects of polytheism before them. He used the present tense in as their fathers worship to bring the image to mind. Then He explained to him that He will reward them for their deeds, saying: And We will surely give them their share of the punishment, just as We gave their fathers their share, without anything being diminished from that. The accusative case is not a state, and giving them their share does not necessitate the absence of deficiency, for it may be permissible for it to be given incomplete, just as it may be permissible for it to be given incomplete. It was said: What is meant is their share of provision. It was said: What is more general of good and evil.
11:110: 110- And We gave Moses the Book meaning the Torah but there was disagreement over it meaning about its affair and the details of its rulings. Some people believed in it and others disbelieved in it, some people acted upon its rulings and others left some of them. So do not be distressed, O Muhammad, by what happened from these people in the Qur’an: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. That is, had it not been for the fact that God Almighty had ruled to delay their punishment until the Day of Resurrection, because He knew that there was good in that, it would have been judged between them: that is, between your people, or between the people of Moses regarding what they differed over. So the one who was right would have been rewarded and the one who was wrong would have been punished. Or the word is that His mercy preceded His wrath, so He gave them respite and did not hasten them for that. It was said that the word is that they would not be punished with the punishment of extermination, and this is part of the consolation for him, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he described them as being in doubt about the Book, saying: And indeed, they are in doubt concerning it, disquieting. That is, about the Qur’an if it is applied to the people of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or about the Torah if it is applied to the people of Moses, peace be upon him. Disquieting is the one who is in doubt.
11:111: Then he gathered the first and the last in the ruling of their fulfillment of the punishment, or it and the reward, so he said: 111- And indeed, each one will surely be fully compensated by his Lord for their deeds. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Abu Bakr read wa-in with a lightened in on the basis that it is the lightened in from the heavy in and it worked in both in the accusative case, and Al-Khalil and Sibawayh allowed it to work, and the Basrans allowed the lightening of in with its work, and Al-Kisa'i denied that and said: I do not know on what basis wa-in kala was read? Al-Farra' claimed that the accusative of both is by his saying ya-yufaihim, and the estimation is wa-in ya-yufaihim kala, and all grammarians denied that on him. The rest read with a shaddah on in and they put kala in the accusative case with it. And according to both readings, the tanween in kala is a substitute for the complement: that is, and indeed, all the different ones. Asim, Hamza, and Ibn Amir read lama with a shaddah, and the rest lightened it. Al-Zajjaj said: Lam of lama is the lam of in, and ma is an additional emphatic word. Al-Farra’ said: ma has the meaning of min, as in His statement: And indeed, among you are those who will slow down meaning, And indeed, every one of you is for those who will fulfill their promise. It was said: It is not additional, but rather it is a noun that has the lam of emphasis added to it, and the meaning is: And indeed, every one of you is for those who created. It was said that it is a compound word, and its origin is liman ma, so the nun was changed to a mim and three mims came together, so the middle one was deleted. An-Nahhas narrated this from the grammarians. Al-Zajjaj refuted this and said: Min is a noun with two letters, so it is not permissible to delete the nun. Some grammarians went to a, for this lam has the meaning of illa, and from this is the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it. Al-Mazini said: The origin is lam that was lightened, then it was made heavy. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a mistake, as the heavy is lightened and the lightened is not heavy. Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam said: It is possible that the emphasis is from their saying lammat al-shay’ lamhu: if you gathered it, then it was built from it, fa’la, as was read: Then We sent Our messengers one after the other. The best of these statements is that it has the meaning of illa as an exception. This was narrated from Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and all the Basrans. Al-Zajjaj preferred it. It is supported by the fact that in the letter Abi there is wa-in kulla ila li-wa-fi-hum as Abu Hatim narrated from him. It was read with tanween: meaning all together. Al-A’mash read wa-in kul lama with a light in and a raised kul and a heavy lama, and in in this reading is negative. Indeed, He is All-Knowing of what they do, O you who differ, and nothing of it is hidden from Him, and the sentence is an explanation of fa-lama before it.
11:112: Then the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a comprehensive word for the types of obedience to Him, may He be glorified, and He said: 112- So stand firm as you have been commanded, meaning as God commanded you, and this includes everything that He commanded him to do and everything that He forbade him from doing, because He commanded him to avoid what He forbade him from doing, just as He commanded him to do what he worshipped Him by doing, and his nation is his example in that, and for this reason He said: And whoever repents with you, meaning returns from disbelief to Islam and shares with you in faith, and it is conjoined with the pronoun in So stand firm, because the separation between the conjoined and the raised pronoun conjoined to it serves as emphasis: meaning, and let whoever repents with you stand firm. How great is the position of this verse and how severe its matter is, for standing firm as God commanded is only carried out by purified souls and holy beings, and for this reason the Chosen One, may God bless him and grant him peace, says: Hud made me gray, as mentioned above, and do not transgress, transgression is exceeding the limit, because God Almighty commanded standing firm. The above-mentioned hadith shows that extremism in worship and excess in obedience in a way that takes one beyond the limit He has set and the amount He has determined is forbidden and prohibited, such as someone who fasts and does not break his fast, prays at night and does not sleep, and abandons the lawful things that God has permitted and encouraged. For this reason, the Truthful, the Trusted One says in what is authentic: “As for me, I fast and break my fast, pray and sleep, and marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.” The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to his nation, giving precedence to their situation over his situation, or the prohibition of tyranny is specific to the nation. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do. He will reward you according to what you deserve, and the sentence is an explanation of what preceded it.
11:113: His saying: 113- And do not incline toward those who do wrong. The majority of scholars read it with the fat-ha on the kaf, and Talhah ibn Musarraf, Qatadah, and others read tarakana with the damma on the kaf. Al-Farra' said: It is the language of Tamim and Qais. Abu Amr said: The reading of the majority is the language of the people of Hijaz. He said: The language of Tamim is with the kasra on the ta' and the fat-ha on the kaf, and they break the letter of the present tense in everything that is from the category of 'ilm ya'lam. Ibn Abi Ubla read it with the damma on the ta' and the fat-ha on the kaf in the passive form of arkanahu. He said in As-Sahah: Rukan ilayhi yurkan with the damma. Abu Zaid narrated Rukan ilayhi with the kasra yurkan rukan fihina: meaning he leaned toward it and settled. God the Almighty said: And do not incline toward those who do wrong. As for what Abu Zaid narrated Rukan yurkan with the fat-ha on both of them, it is only to combine the two languages. End. He said in Shams Al-'Ulum: Rukun is stillness. It is said: He leaned towards him, God the Most High said: And do not incline towards those who do wrong. End quote. And it says in the dictionary: He leaned towards him like victory, knowledge and prevention, leaning: inclined and settled. End quote. So these imams from the narrators of the language interpreted the leaning as meaning absolute inclination and stillness without restricting it with what the author of Al-Kashshaf restricted it with where he said: Indeed, leaning is a slight inclination. And thus the commentators interpreted it as meaning absolute inclination and stillness without restricting it except for those who were bound by what the author of Al-Kashshaf transmitted. And some of the commentators mentioned restrictions in the interpretation of the leaning that the imams of the language did not mention. Al-Qurtubi said in his interpretation: The reality of leaning is to rely, depend, and settle on something and be satisfied with it. And some of the imams of the followers interpreted the leaning with what is more specific than its linguistic meaning. It was narrated from Qatadah and Ikrimah in their interpretation of the verse that its meaning is: Do not love them nor obey them. And Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said in his interpretation of the verse: The leaning here means abasement, and that is to not denounce their disbelief. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It means do not be satisfied with their actions. The imams of the commentators also differed regarding this verse: is it specific to the polytheists or general? It was said that it is specific, and that the meaning of the verse is the prohibition of relying on the polytheists, and that they are meant by those who did wrong, and this was narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was said that it is general for the oppressors without differentiating between a disbeliever and a Muslim, and this is what appears from the verse. Even if we assume that the reason for revelation was the polytheists, then the consideration would be the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. If you say: The authentic evidences have been reported, reaching a number of consecutive narrations that have been proven from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a way that is not hidden from anyone who has the slightest adherence to the pure Sunnah, regarding the obligation to obey the imams, sultans and princes, to the point that it was mentioned in some of the wordings of the Sahih: Obey the ruler even if he is an Abyssinian slave with a head like a raisin. And it was mentioned that it is obligatory to obey them as long as they establish prayer, as long as they do not show clear disbelief, and as long as they do not order disobedience to God. It is apparent from this that even if they reached the highest levels of oppression and committed the worst types of oppression without going as far as blatant disbelief, then obedience to them is obligatory as long as what they commanded was not disobedience to God. Among the things they command is taking over work for them and entering into religious positions that entering into is not disobedience to God. Among the things they command is jihad, taking the obligatory rights from the subjects, establishing the Shari’ah between the disputing parties among them, and implementing the prescribed punishments on those upon whom it is obligatory. In short, obedience to them is obligatory upon everyone who is subject to their command and prohibition in everything they command that is not disobedience to God. In such a case, it is necessary to mix with them and enter upon them, and so on, which is inevitable. There is no escape from what we have mentioned about the obligation to obey them with the mentioned restrictions due to the frequency of the evidence that has been transmitted. Rather, it has been reported in the Noble Book: Obey God and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. Rather, it has been reported that they give what is due to them of obedience, even if they withhold what is due from the subjects, as in some The authentic hadiths: Give them what is theirs, and ask God for what is yours. Rather, the command to obey the ruler was mentioned, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to extremes in this matter to the point of saying: Even if he takes your wealth and beats your back. If we consider absolute inclination and stillness, then this mere obedience that is commanded, along with what it entails of mixing with them, is inclination and stillness. If we consider inclination and stillness as apparent and hidden, then the prohibition in this verse does not include one who inclines towards them outwardly for a matter that requires that according to the Shari’ah, such as obedience, or for taqiyya and fear of harm from them, or to bring about a public or private benefit or to ward off a public or private corruption, if he does not have intrinsic inclination towards them, nor love nor approval of their actions. I said: As for obedience in its generality with all its divisions, as long as it is not in disobedience to God, then assuming the meaning of relying on it is true, it is specific to the general prohibition of it with its evidence that we have previously indicated, and there is no doubt about this and no suspicion, so everyone who they ordered from the beginning to enter into something of the works that he ordered them to do that was not in disobedience to God, such as religious positions and the like, if he is confident in himself to carry out what he was entrusted with, then that is obligatory upon him, let alone it being said that it is permissible for him. As for what was reported regarding the prohibition of entering into the emirate, this is restricted to the fact that the order did not occur from those whose obedience is obligatory from the imams, sultans and princes, in order to combine the evidence, or with the weakness of the one ordered to do what he was ordered to do, as the reason for the prohibition of entering into the emirate was reported in some authentic hadiths. As for mixing with them and entering upon them to bring about a general or specific benefit or to repel a general or specific corruption, while hating what they are upon of injustice and not inclining towards them and loving them, and hating to continue with them if it were not for bringing that benefit or repelling that corruption, then assuming the truth of the term reliance on this, it is limited by the evidence indicating the legitimacy of bringing about benefits and repelling corruptions, and actions are by intentions, and each person will get what he intended, and nothing is hidden from God. In short, whoever is afflicted with mixing with someone who is unjust must weigh his words and actions and what he does and leaves with the scale of the Shariah. If he refrains from that, then upon herself is a liar who reaps, and whoever is able to flee from them before he is ordered by them with an order he must obey. It is the first and most appropriate for him. O Master of the Day of Judgment, You alone do we worship and You alone do we ask for help. Make us among Your righteous servants who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, who do not fear the blame of any blamer in Your cause. Strengthen us in this and make it easy for us, and assist us in it. Al-Qurtubi said in his interpretation: And keeping company with the oppressor out of taqiyya is an exception to the prohibition in a state of compulsion. Al-Naysaburi said in his interpretation: The scholars said: The forbidden reliance is contentment with what the oppressors are doing, or improving and beautifying the way in the eyes of others, and participating with them in any of those matters. As for intervening with them to remove harm and bring immediate benefit, then it is not included in reliance. He said: And I say this is by way of livelihood and concession, and the requirement of piety is to avoid them completely. Is not God sufficient for His servant? End quote. His statement: Then the Fire will touch you because of leaning towards them, and in it is an indication that the oppressors are the people of the Fire, or like the Fire, and the company of the Fire inevitably necessitates touching the Fire, and the phrase And you have no protectors besides God is in the accusative case as a state of His statement: Then the Fire will touch you. The meaning is: The Fire will touch you while there is no one to help you and save you from it. Then you will not be helped on the part of God, the Exalted, since it was previously known to Him that He would punish you because of the leaning towards it that you were forbidden from, but you did not desist out of stubbornness and rebellion.
11:114: His saying: 114- And establish prayer at the two ends of the day. When God the Almighty mentioned righteousness, He singled out from its types establishing prayer because it is the head of faith, and the accusative of the two ends of the day is circumstantial, and what is meant is the morning and evening prayers, and they are the dawn and the afternoon, and it was said that Dhuhr is the place of the afternoon. And it was said that the two ends are the morning and the sunset, and it was said that they are the noon and the afternoon. Ibn Jarir preferred that they are the morning and the sunset, and he said: The evidence for this is the consensus of all that one of the two ends is the morning, so it indicates that the other end is the sunset. And at the approach of the night means at the approach of the night, and the approach is the hours that are close to each other, and from it Muzdalifah was named because it is a place after Arafat near Mecca. Ibn Al-Qaqa', Abu Ishaq and others read Zulfan with a damma on the lam, the plural of zaleef, and it is possible that its singular is zalfah. Ibn Muhaisin read it with a sukoon on the lam. Mujahid read negation like fa'li. The rest read it with a fat-ha on the lam like ghurfah and ghurf. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Zulf is the hours, the singular of which is zalfah. Some people said: Zulfah is the first hour of the night after sunset. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning of Zulfah min al-layl is the night prayer. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds means that good deeds in general, and among them, or rather their mainstay, is prayer, do away with misdeeds in general. It was said: What is meant by misdeeds are minor sins, and the meaning of do away with misdeeds is that they expiate them as if they had never existed. The reference in His statement: That is a reminder for those who remember is to His statement: So stand firm and what follows it. It was said: to the Qur’an, a reminder for those who remember, meaning an admonition for those who take heed.
11:115: 115- And be patient in what you have been commanded to do of righteousness and not transgressing and leaning towards those who have wronged. It has been said that what is meant is patience in what you have commanded rather than what you have forbidden, because there is no hardship in avoiding it. There is a consideration in this, because the hardship in avoiding what is forbidden does exist, and assuming that it is less than the hardship of obeying the command, that does not remove it from absolute hardship. For God does not waste the reward of the righteous, meaning He pays them their rewards and does not waste any of them, so He does not neglect them or diminish them by reducing them. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, And indeed, We will give them their share, undiminished, that is, what is decreed for them of good or evil. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, that he said: From the punishment. They narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah, that he said: From the provision. They also narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the statement of God, So stand firm as you have been commanded, that he said: God commanded His Prophet to stand firm in His command, and not to transgress in His blessings. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Sufyan regarding the verse, that he said: Stand firm in the Qur’an. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, that he said: When this verse was revealed, So stand firm as you have been commanded, he said: Roll up your sleeves, roll up your sleeves, and he was never seen laughing. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And whoever repents with you, that he said: Believe. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdullah bin Badr regarding his statement: And do not transgress, he said: He did not mean the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, but rather he meant those who come after them. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And do not transgress, he said: Do not wrong. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, he said: Transgression is disobeying His command and committing His disobedience. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, he said: He meant inclining toward polytheism. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: And do not incline, he said: Do not lean. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: And do not incline, he said: Do not be complacent. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the verse: He said: That you obey them, or love them, or treat them well. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day, he said: the Maghrib and Fajr prayers. And at the approach of the night, he said: the Isha prayer. They narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: the Fajr and Asr prayers. And at the approach of the night, he said: they are two approaches: the Maghrib and Isha prayers. He said: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are the two approaches of the night. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And at the approach of the night, he said: an hour after an hour, meaning the last Isha prayer. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he preferred to delay Isha and recite Zalaf min Al-Layl. Ibn Jarir, Muhammad ibn Nasr and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds, he said: the five daily prayers. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds, he said: the five daily prayers. The lasting good deeds are the five daily prayers. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, the Sunan scholars and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that a man kissed a woman, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him as if he was asking about its expiation, so the following verse was revealed to him: “And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds,” so the man said: O Messenger of God, is this for me? He said: It is for whoever among my nation does it. Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud and others narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that a man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, establish the limits of God once or twice. He turned away from him, then the prayer was called. When he finished, he said: Where is the man? He said: I am here. He said: Did you complete your ablution and pray with us just now? He said: Yes. He said: Then you are as free from your sin as on the day your mother bore you, so do not do it again. Then God revealed to His Messenger: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day. There are many hadiths on this topic with different wordings. There are also hadiths that say: The five daily prayers are expiations for what is between them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding His statement: That is a reminder for those who remember, he said: They are those who remember God in ease and hardship, in hardship and ease, in health and in affliction. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that he said: “When the one who was before the woman was removed, she remembered, and that is why He said: ‘A reminder for those who remember.’”
11:116: This is a return to the conditions of the past nations to show that the reason for the punishment of extermination that befell them was that there was no one among them who forbade corruption and commanded righteousness. He said: 116- Why meaning why were there not among the generations that existed before you those who had a remainder of opinion, reason and religion who would forbid their people from corruption in the land and prevent them from doing so because they were among those in whom God combined the quality of reason and the strength of religion? In this there is a rebuke to the disbelievers that is not hidden, and the remainder in origin is what a man keeps from what he puts out. And he keeps only the best and finest of it, so the word remainder became an example of quality, and the exception in except a little is discontinuous: meaning but a little of those We saved from among them who forbid corruption in the land. It was said: It is connected because the letter of exhortation has the meaning of negation, so it is as if he said: There were not in the generations those who had a remainder who forbade corruption on the earth except a few of those whom We saved, and whoever in whoever We saved is explanatory because only those who forbade it were saved. It was said: These few are the people of Yunus because of what was mentioned earlier: except the people of Yunus. It was said: They are the followers of the prophets and the people of truth from the nations in general. And those who did wrong followed that in which they indulged, is connected to an implied meaning required by the speech, its meaning is: Except a few of those whom We saved from them who forbade corruption, and the meaning is: Those who did wrong because of their direct involvement in corruption and their abandonment of forbidding it followed that in which they indulged. The luxurious: the one who was made arrogant by the blessings. It is said: a luxurious boy: one with a luxurious body, meaning they became dependent on the blessings that made them luxurious from the abundance of life, the comfort of the situation and the abundance of sustenance, and they preferred that over being busy with the works of the hereafter and they spent their lives in the desires of the soul. It was said: what is meant by those who did wrong are those who abandoned the prohibition. It was replied that it necessitates the exclusion of those who directly committed corruption from those who did wrong, and they are more unjust than those who did not directly commit it, and their sin was abandoning the prohibition. Abu Amr read in a narration from him: And those who did wrong followed in the passive form, and its meaning is: they followed the punishment for what they indulged in, and the phrase and they were criminals includes an explanation of the reason for their destruction, and it is conjoined with they indulged in luxury: meaning and those who followed what they indulged in were criminals, and crime: sins. Meaning: They are criminals because they follow their desires and are preoccupied with them instead of the things that are right to be preoccupied with. It is possible that the phrase and they were criminals is conjoined with and those who did wrong followed: meaning they followed their desires and were criminals by doing so.
11:117: 117- And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly while their people were righteous. That is, it is not correct or right for God, the Most High, to destroy the people of the cities because of the injustice they were involved in, which is polytheism, while the fact is that their people were righteous among themselves in dealing with rights and they did not wrong people in anything. The meaning is that He would not destroy them simply because of polytheism alone, so that corruption on earth would be added to it, just as He destroyed the people of Shu'ayb because of their insufficient measure and weight and their shortchanging of people of their things, and He destroyed the people of Lot because they committed a heinous indecency. It was said that His statement, unjustly is a description of the subject. The meaning is: And God would not destroy the cities unjustly while they were righteous and not corrupting on earth. The intended meaning of the verse is to absolve Him, the Most High, from doing that without a reason that would require Him to portray that in a way that is impossible from Him. Otherwise, all of His actions, whatever they may be, are not unjust, for He, the Most High, is not unjust to His servants. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that the meaning is: And your Lord would not destroy anyone while He was wronging him, even if he was at the peak of righteousness because His disposal is in His kingdom, and the evidence for that is the Most High’s statement: Indeed, God does not wrong the people at all. And it was said that the meaning is: And He would not destroy them for their sins while they were righteous: that is, sincere in faith, so injustice is sins according to this.
11:118: 118- And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community meaning people of one religion, either people of misguidance or people of guidance. It was said that its meaning is: He made them united on the truth without differing about it, or united on the religion of Islam without the other religions, but He did not will that, so it did not happen. That is why He said: And they will not cease to differ in themselves among themselves on various religions, or they will not cease to differ about the truth or the religion of Islam. It was said: differing in provisions: this one is rich, and this one is poor.
11:119: 119- Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy by guiding them to the true religion, for they did not differ, or except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy from those who differed in the truth or the religion of Islam, by guiding them to the correct path which is the rule of God, and it is the truth that there is no other truth, or except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy by contentment. The first: Explaining to make mankind one nation as united upon the truth so that the meaning of the exception in Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy is clear and does not need to be complicated. And for that meaning for what was mentioned of the difference He created them or for His mercy He created them, and it is correct to make the reference to mercy masculine because its feminine is not real, and the pronoun in their creation refers to people, or to those in those upon whom your Lord has mercy, and it was said: The reference in that is to the combination of difference and mercy, and there is no objection to referring to two things with it as in His saying: And between that "And seek a way between that So in that let them rejoice." His saying: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled. The meaning of fulfilled is that it is established as He decreed in eternity. If it is fulfilled, it is prevented from being changed or altered. It was said that the word is His saying: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together, meaning with those who deserve it from the two groups.
11:120: The tanween in wakala is to compensate for the complement, which is in the accusative case due to deficiency. The meaning is: And every piece of report of the messengers that is needed, we relate to you: that is, we inform you of it. Al-Akhfash said: Both is an introductory state, like when you say: Both, I struck the people, and the report is the report. What we make your heart firm with means what we make your heart firm with by increasing its certainty in what we have related to you and its abundance of reassurance, because the increase of evidence is firmer for the heart and more firmly rooted in the soul and stronger for knowledge. The phrase what we make firm is a substitute for the report of the messengers, and it is a clarification of both. It is possible that what we make firm is an object of deficiency, and both is an absolute object, and the estimate is: Every method of retaliation we relate to you what we make firm your heart with. And there has come to you in this truth means there has come to you in this surah, or in this report, the conclusive proofs indicating the truth of the beginning and the end. And an admonition by which the believers who stand upon it are admonished. And a reminder by which those of them who contemplate it are reminded. He singled out the believers because they are qualified to be admonished and remembered. It was said that the meaning is: And the truth has come to you in this world, which is prophethood. According to the first interpretation, this surah is specified by the coming of the truth in it. Although it came in other surahs with the intention of clarifying that they include it, not clarifying that it is present in them and not in others.
11:121: 121- And say to those who do not believe in this truth and do not learn a lesson or remember, Work according to your position according to your ability, your condition, and your direction, and its verification has been presented previously, Indeed, we are working according to our position, our condition, and our direction of belief in the truth, learning a lesson, and remembering, and in this there is an emphasis on the threat and intimidation for them.
11:122: Likewise, His statement: 122- And wait, for we are waiting. It contains a threat and intimidation that is not hidden. The meaning is: Wait for the outcome of our matter, for we are waiting for the outcome of your matter and what will befall you of God’s punishment and chastisement.
11:123: 123- And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth meaning He knows everything that is hidden from His servants in them. He made the unseen special from His knowledge of what is witnessed, as He knows what is hidden, because it is from the knowledge that no one else shares with Him. It was said that the unseen of the heavens and the earth is the descent of punishment from the sky and its rise from the earth, and the first is more appropriate, and Abu Ali Al-Farisi and others said the same. He added the unseen to the object as an extension. And to Him will return the entire matter meaning on the Day of Resurrection, when He will reward everyone according to his deeds. Nafi' and Hafs read yurji'u in the passive form. The rest read it in the active form. So worship Him and put your trust in Him for He will suffice you in everything you dislike, and will give you everything you love. The fa is to arrange the matter with worship and trust in the fact that the return of all matters is to God, the Most High. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do rather He knows all of that and will reward it, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. The people of Medina, Ash-Sham and Hafs read ta’malun with a fatha on the addressee. The rest read it with a ta’la. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: So why not? He said: Why not? Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited to me: Why were there not among the generations before you those of sound mind and wisdom who would forbid corruption on earth? Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Except a few of those We saved from among them. God considers them insignificant among every people. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid: And those who did wrong pursued that in which they indulged, he said: in their kingdom, their tyranny and their abandonment of the truth. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: Ibn Abbas said: They indulged in it, they were arrogant in it. At-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Jarir who said: “He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) being asked about the interpretation of this verse: “And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly while their people were righteous.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And its people are just to one another. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Kharaiti narrated it in Masawi Al-Akhlaq, with a chain of transmission traceable back to Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community, meaning people of one religion, people of misguidance or people of guidance. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they will not cease to differ, meaning the people of truth and the people of falsehood. Except whom your Lord has had mercy on, meaning the people of truth. And for that He created them, meaning for mercy. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, Except whom your Lord has had mercy on, meaning the people of His mercy, for they will not differ. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, saying, They will not cease to differ in their desires. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ata’ Ibn Abi Rabah, And they will not cease to differ, meaning the Jews, Christians, Zoroastrians, and Hanifites, and they are those on whom your Lord has had mercy on the Hanifites. And these people narrated from Al-Hasan regarding the verse, he said: People differ in various religions except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy. So those upon whom your Lord has mercy are not differing. And for that He created them he said: for the sake of difference. And Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, And they will not cease to differ he said: the people of falsehood, Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy he said: the people of truth, And for that He created them he said: for mercy. And Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ikrimah something similar. And they narrated from Al-Hasan, he said: they will not cease to differ in provision. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, and for that reason He created them, he said: He created them into two groups, a group that is merciful and does not differ, and a group that is not merciful and differs, so that is His statement: And among them is the wretched and the happy. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding His statement, And We relate to you, O Muhammad, from the report of the messengers that by which We strengthen your heart so that you may know what the messengers before you encountered from their nations. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: And there has come to you in this truth meaning: in this surah. Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash`ari something similar. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr something similar as well. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Hasan something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: In this world. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada, Work according to your station meaning your homes. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Then wait, for I am with you among those who wait meaning: wait for the promises made by Satan to you based on what he makes attractive to you. And in His statement: And to Him will return the entire matter he said: He will judge between them with just judgment. Abdullah bin Ahmed narrated in Zawa’id al-Musnad, Ibn al-Durais in Fadhail al-Quran, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-Sheikh on the authority of Ka’b, who said: The opening of the Torah is the opening of al-An’am, and the conclusion of the Torah is the conclusion of Hud. And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, to the end of the verse. Thank God, the second part has been printed, followed by the third part. The first: Interpretation of Surat Yusuf, peace be upon him
12:1: It is said that it is one hundred and eleven verses. It is all Meccan, and it was said that it was revealed between Mecca and Medina at the time of the migration. Ibn Abbas said in a narration from him and Qatadah: Except for four verses. An-Nahhas, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Yusuf was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Rafa’ah ibn Rafi’ al-Zarqi that he and his maternal cousin Muadh ibn Afra’ went out until they arrived in Mecca, and he mentioned a story at the end of which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) taught them Surat Yusuf and Read in the name of your Lord, then they returned. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il, on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “A Jewish rabbi entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he found him reciting Surat Yusuf. He said: O Muhammad, who taught you it? He said: God taught it to me. The rabbi was amazed at what he heard from him, so he returned to the Jews and said to them: By God, Muhammad recites the Qur’an as it was revealed in the Torah. He set off with a group of them until they entered upon him and recognized him by his description, and they looked at the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders. They listened to his recitation of Surat Yusuf and were amazed by him, and they converted to Islam at that time.” Al-Tha’labi narrated on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Teach your relatives Surat Yusuf, for any Muslim who recites it or teaches it to his family and those his right hand possesses, God will make the throes of death easy for him and give him the strength not to envy a Muslim.” In its chain of transmission is Salam bin Salim, and it is said Ibn Salim Al-Madani, and he is rejected on the authority of Harun bin Katheer. Abu Hatim said: He is unknown. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned a follower for him through the path of Al-Qasim bin Al-Hakam from Harun bin Katheer, and through the path of Shababah from Majlaz bin Abdul Wahid Al-Basri from Ali bin Zaid bin Jud’an, and from Ata bin Maymun from Zur bin Hubaish from Abi bin Ka’b with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar, and it is rejected in all its paths. Al-Qurtubi said: Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas said: The Qur’an was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited it to them for a period of time, and they said: Why don’t you tell us? Then the words of God Almighty were revealed: God has sent down the best statement. He said: The scholars said: God mentioned the stories of the prophets in the Qur’an and repeated them with one meaning in different ways with different wordings according to degrees of eloquence. He mentioned the story of Joseph and did not repeat it, so no opponent was able to oppose what was repeated, nor to oppose what was not repeated. His saying: 1- Alif, Lam, Ra. We have already discussed it in the opening of Surah Yunus, and the reference in his saying: Those is to the verses of the Surah, and the clear book: the Surah, meaning those verses that were revealed to you in this Surah, the verses of the Surah, the apparent matter of which is in the miracle of the Arabs and their rebuke, and the clear from aban meaning bana: meaning the apparent matter of it being from God and in its miracle, or the clear in the sense of the clear meaning such that it is not confused for its reader and listener, or the clear for what is in it of rulings.
12:2: 2- "Indeed, We sent it down meaning the clear book while it is an Arabic Qur'an". If we assume that the book is a surah, then it would be called the Qur'an because the Qur'an is a generic name that applies to all and to some. If we assume that what is meant by the book is the entire Qur'an, then calling it the Qur'an would be clear, and Arabic is an attribute of the Qur'an: that is, in the language of the Arabs "so that you may understand" meaning so that you may learn its meanings and understand what is in it.
12:3: 3- We relate to you the best of stories Stories follow something, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: And she said to his sister, 'Follow him', meaning follow his trace, and it is a source, and the meaning is: We relate to you stories, the best of stories, so it means retrieval, or it means the object: meaning the one narrated with what We have revealed to you meaning with Our revelation to you this Qur'an and the Qur'an is in the accusative case as an attribute of the demonstrative pronoun, or a substitute for it, or an explanatory apposition, and Al-Zajjaj permitted the nominative case on the assumption of a subject, and Al-Farra permitted the genitive case, and perhaps its face is to estimate the preposition in with what We have revealed as entering the demonstrative pronoun, so the meaning is: We relate to you the best of stories with this Qur'an And if you were before it among the unaware "If is the lightened form of the heavy one, as evidenced by the lam that distinguishes it from the negative, and the pronoun in from before it" refers back to the revelation understood from We have revealed, and the meaning is: that before Our revelation to you, you were among the unaware of this story. There is a difference of opinion as to why what is in this Surah is the best of stories. It has been said that it is because the stories in this Surah include lessons, sermons, and wisdom that are not found in any other Surah. It has also been said that it is because of the good dialogue in it and the patience of Joseph, peace be upon him, in the face of their harm and his forgiveness of them. It has also been said that it is because it mentions the prophets, the righteous, the angels, the devils, the jinn, mankind, livestock, birds, the lives of kings, slaves, merchants, scholars, the ignorant, women, their tricks and deceit. It has also been said that it mentions the beloved and the beloved and what happened between them. It has been said that the word best here means wonderful. It has been said that everyone mentioned in it will end up in happiness.
12:4: 4- His saying: When Joseph said to his father “when” is an adverbial phrase with an implied verb: that is, remember the time Joseph said. The majority read Yusuf with a damma on the seen, and Talha ibn Masraf read it with a kasra with a hamza instead of a waw, and Ibn Zayd narrated the hamza and the fatha on the seen, and it is not declined because it is foreign and proper, and it was said that it is Arabic, and the first is more appropriate as evidence of its not being declined for his father meaning Jacob ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim O father with a kasra on the ta’ in the reading of Abu Amr, Asim, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Nafi’ and Ibn Kathir, and it is according to the Basrans a sign of femininity, and it was added to the word father in the vocative especially instead of the ya’ and its origin is O my father, and its kasra is to indicate that it is a replacement for a letter with a suitable kasra, and Ibn Amir read it with a fatha, because the origin is from it O my father, and the replacement and the replaced are not combined, so it is said O my father, and Al-Farra’ permitted O father with a damma on the ta’ Inni ra’ita from the dream vision not from the visual vision as indicated by Do not relate your vision to your brothers. His saying: Eleven stars was read with a sukoon on the ‘ayn to make the succession of movements easier, and it was read with a fatha on it according to the original, and the sun and the moon He only delayed them after the stars to show their excellence and honor as in the conjunction of Gabriel and Michael with the angels, and it was said that the waw means with, and the phrase I saw them prostrating to me is a new sentence to explain the state in which he saw them, and it was treated like rational beings in the pronoun specific to them to describe it with the description of rational beings, which is that it is prostrating, thus said Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, and the Arabs pluralize what is not rational with the plural of rational if they place it in its position.
12:5: 5- He said, 'O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers.' Vision is a noun derived from the verb to see in a dream. Vision is of the form fa'li like saqya and good report. Its alif is for the feminine, and therefore it is not declined. Jacob, peace be upon him, forbade his son Joseph from relating his vision to his brothers, because he knew its interpretation and feared that he would relate it to his brothers and they would understand its interpretation and envy him. For this reason, he said: So they will plot against you a plot. This is the answer to the prohibition, and it is in the accusative case by the implication of an: meaning, so they will do to you: meaning for your sake a fixed and firm plot that you will not be able to escape from, or a plot hidden from your understanding. This meaning obtained by adding they will plot is more emphatic than saying they will plot, and it was said that the lam was brought to include the meaning of the transitive deception with the lam, so this inclusion conveys the meaning of both verbs, the plot and the deception, as is the rule in inclusion, that one of them is estimated as the origin and the other as the state. The phrase Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy is a new sentence, as if Joseph, peace be upon him, said: How can this happen to them? So he alerted him that Satan is leading them to do this, because he is an enemy of man who shows enmity and openly declares it.
12:6: 6- His saying And thus your Lord will choose you meaning like that wonderful selection that you saw in your sleep of the prostration of the planets, the sun and the moon, your Lord will choose you, and fulfill in you the interpretation of that vision, so He will make you a prophet and choose you over all the servants, and will subject them to you just as those bodies that you saw in your sleep were subjected to you and became prostrate to you. An-Nahhas said: The origin of selection is from the word jabayt al-shay' I obtained something, and from it the word jabayt al-ma' fi al-hawd I gathered the water in the basin, and the meaning of selection is: selection, and this includes praising Joseph and enumerating God's blessings upon him, including and He will teach you the interpretation of dreams meaning the interpretation of dreams. Al-Qurtubi said: They agreed that this is in the interpretation of the vision, and Joseph, peace be upon him, was the most knowledgeable of people about its interpretation. It was said that what is meant is: And He teaches you the interpretation of the hadiths of the nations and the books. It was said that what is meant by it is his brothers’ need for him. It was said that he saved him from every harm. It was said that he saved him from being killed in particular. And He completes His favor upon you, so He combines for you both prophethood and kingship, as this vision that God showed you indicates, or He combines for you the good of this world and the hereafter. And upon the family of Jacob, who are his relatives from his brothers and children and those after them. This is because God Almighty gave them prophethood, as a group of commentators said. It is not far-fetched that it is a reference to what happened to them after they entered Egypt of the blessings that included the kingship being among them despite their being prophets. As He completed it upon your fathers, meaning a completion like its completion upon your fathers: and it is the blessing of prophethood upon them, along with the fact that God took Abraham as a friend, and with the fact that God Almighty saved Isaac from being slaughtered and they had offspring. The good: They are Jacob, Joseph, and the rest of the tribes. The meaning of before is before this time in which you are, or before you. Abraham and Isaac are an apposition to your parents, and they are referred to as parents even though one of them is a grandfather: Abraham, because the grandfather is a father. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing of everything, Wise in all of His actions. The sentence is a resumption, confirming the content of what came before it, explaining it: that is, He did that because He is Knowing and Wise. This was a speech from Jacob to his son Joseph, expressing his vision in a general way, or he knew that through revelation, or he knew it through intuition and what the Josephite visions require. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: These are the verses of the clear Book, he said: God has made clear what is lawful and unlawful. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muadh who said: God made clear the [letters] that were dropped from the tongues of the non-Arabs, and they are six letters. Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited an Arabic Quran, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ishmael was inspired with this Arabic tongue. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The Quran was revealed in the language of Quraysh, which is their speech. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: They said, O Messenger of God, if you told us a story, so We relate to you the best of stories was revealed. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud something similar. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: We relate to you the best of stories, he said: from the previous books and the previous affairs of God among the nations, and if you were before it, meaning before this Quran, among the unaware. Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak We relate to you the best of stories, he said: the Quran. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Sheikh, Al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: I saw eleven stars, he said: The vision of the prophets is revelation. Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Uqaili, Ibn Hibban in Al-Du’afa, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah who said: “A Jewish gardener came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Muhammad, tell me about the stars that Joseph saw prostrating to him. What are their names?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent and did not answer him. Then Gabriel came down to him and told him their names. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for the Jewish gardener and said: ‘Will you believe if I tell you their names?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Kharthan, Al-Tariq, Al-Dhiyal, Dhu Al-Kutafan, Qabis, Waththab, Amudan, Al-Failaq, Al-Misbah, Al-Dharuh, Dhu Al-Fargh, Al-Dhiya’ and Al-Nur. He saw them in the horizon of the sky prostrating to him. When Joseph told Jacob about it, he said: ‘This is a scattered matter that God will gather later.’ The Jew said: ‘Yes, by God, they are their names.’” This is how Al-Suyuti narrated it in Al-Durr Al-Manthur. As for Ibn Kathir, he considered his statement: When he narrated etc. to be an isolated narration. He said: Al-Hakam bin Dhahirah Al-Fazari was the only one to narrate it. They weakened him and abandoned him. Al-Jawzajani said: It is invalid. Ibn Al-Jawzi said: It is fabricated. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: eleven stars he said: His brothers, and the sun he said: His mother, and the moon he said: His father. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd something similar as well. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And thus your Lord chooses you he said: He selects you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid: And He teaches you the interpretation of dreams he said: The expression of dreams. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, And He teaches you the interpretation of dreams, he said: The interpretation of knowledge and wisdom, and Joseph was one of the most knowledgeable of people. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, As He completed it for your parents, he said: So His favor upon Abraham was that He saved him from the fire, and upon Isaac was that He saved him from being slaughtered.
12:7: 7- That is, There were in their story signs indicating the greatness of God's power and the wonder of His creation for those who asked about it from among the people. The people of Mecca read a verse in monotheism, and the rest read it in the plural, and Abu Ubaid chose the plural reading. An-Nahhas said: The verse here is a good reading, and it was said that the meaning is: There were in Joseph and his brothers signs indicating the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for those who asked about him from among the Jews, for it was narrated that a group of Jews said to him while he was in Mecca: Tell us about a man from among the prophets who was in Ash-Sham who took his son to Egypt and cried over him until he went blind, and there was no one in Mecca from the People of the Book or anyone who knew the report of the prophets, but they directed some from the people of Medina to ask him about this, so God revealed Surah Yusuf all at once as in the Torah. It was said that the meaning of Signs for those who asked is a wonder to them, and it was said that it is insight, and it was said that it is a lesson. Al-Qurtubi said: Their names, meaning the brothers of Joseph, were: Reuben, who was the eldest, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Rialon, and Ishgar. Their mother was Leah, the daughter of Lian, who was Jacob’s maternal cousin. He had four children from two concubines: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. Then Leah died, and Jacob married her sister Rachel, who bore him Joseph and Benjamin. Al-Suhayli said: Joseph’s mother’s name was Waqfa, and Rachel died while giving birth to Benjamin, who was older than Joseph.
12:8: 8- When they said to Joseph and his brother that is, when they said, and the circumstance is related to was better to our father than us and what is meant by his saying and his brother is Benjamin, and they specified him as his brother even though they are all his brothers, because he is his brother from his parents as mentioned above, and he made the report singular and said: I love with the multiplicity of the subject, because the comparative form of the word is equal in it to one and what is above it if it is not known, and the lam in Joseph is the one that initiates the oath, and they only said this because the report of the vision reached them and they agreed on his plot, and the phrase and we are a group is in the accusative case as a state, and the group: the group, it was said that it is between one and ten, and it was said to fifteen, and it was said from ten to forty and it does not have a singular from its wording but rather it is like a group and a group, and they were ten Indeed, our father is in manifest error that is, in going astray from the path of management by giving them preference over us and preferring them over us even though we are equal in Affiliation with him, and it is not correct that they mean that he is clearly astray in his religion.
12:9: 9- Kill Joseph or cast him into the ground meaning they said: Do one of two things to him: either killing, or casting him into the ground, or the one who advised killing part of it and the one who advised casting the other part, or the speaker was one of them and the rest agreed with him, so they were like the speaker in attributing this to them, and the erection of the ground is for the circumstance, and the indefiniteness is for ambiguity: meaning an unknown land, and the answer to the command He will make your father's face pure for you meaning He describes and purifies and turns to you and loves you with a complete love and you will be is conjoined with He will make pure, and it is permissible for it to be erected by the implication that after him meaning after Joseph, and what is meant is after finishing killing him or casting him, and it was said after the sin they committed against Joseph a righteous people in the matters of your religion and obeying your father, or righteous in the matters of your worldly life because what was distracting you from that has gone, which is envy for Joseph and the troubled feelings due to his influence on you is him His brother, or what is meant by the righteous: those who repent from sin.
12:10: 10- One of them said meaning one of the brothers, it was said that it was Judah, it was said that it was Reuben, and it was said that it was Simeon Do not kill Joseph, and throw him into the bottom of the well. It was said that the reason for the appearance in do not kill Joseph is to bring about their pity for him. The people of Mecca, Basra, Kufa, and Ash-Sham read in the bottom of the well in the singular. The people of Medina read in the plural in ghayabat. Abu Ubaid chose the singular and denied the plural, because the place where they threw him was one. An-Nahhas said: This is a restriction in the language, and ghayabat in the plural is permissible, and ghayaba is everything that hides something from you, and the grave is called ghayaba, and what is meant by it here is the depth of the well that the sight cannot reach, or a window in it, the poet said: So stay for two months or a half or three months, just as you have kept me away Al-Jab: is the well that has not been covered. Before covering it, it is called a rick, but when it is covered, it is called a well. It is called a jiban because it is cut into the ground. The plural of jibb is jibab, jibab, and ajbab. Al-ghaybah and al-jib are combined as an exaggeration in that they throw him into a place in the well that is very dark so that the eyes of those looking at him cannot see him. It was said that this well is in Jerusalem, and it was said that it is in Jordan. The answer to the command is some caravan will pick him up. Mujahid, Abu Raja, al-Hasan, and Qatadah read tatiqatuhu with the thaa’ above, and its meaning is that some caravans are caravans. It was narrated from Sibawayh that some of his fingers fell off, and from this is the saying of the poet: I see the passing years taking from me as the secrets are taken from the crescent moon The rest read it as yataqituhu with a dhammah, and the caravan: the group that travels on the road, and picking up: is taking something that is about to be lost, and it is as if they meant that if some of the caravan picked it up, they would carry it to a distant place where it would be hidden from his father and those who know him, and they would not need to move themselves to the distant place, as their father might not give them permission to do so, and the meaning of if you are going to do is if you are doing what I advised you to do in his matter, as if he did not decide on the matter, but rather left it to what they agreed upon as an advisor does with someone he consults. And in this is evidence that Joseph’s brothers were not prophets, as it is not permissible for prophets to conspire to kill a Muslim unjustly and oppressively, and it was said that they were prophets, and that was a slip of the foot from them and caused them to fall into it because of the burning fire of envy in their chests and the burning coals of anger in their hearts. It was said that the prophets are infallible from such excessive sins, including severing family ties, disobeying parents, and telling lies. It was also said that they were not prophets at that time, but rather became prophets later on. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: Signs for those who ask, he said: A lesson. He also narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse: Whoever asks about that, then this is what God has told you and informed you about. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq who said: God only told Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the story of Joseph and his brothers’ oppression and envy of him when he mentioned his dream when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw his people’s oppression and envy of him when God honored him with his prophethood so that he might take him as an example. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: When they said to Joseph and his brother, meaning Benjamin, he is his brother from his father and mother. Regarding his statement: And we are a group, he said: A group is between ten and forty. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd who said: A group is a community. Indeed, our father is in manifest error, he said: In error in his opinion. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated in his statement: A speaker among them said, ‘Do not kill Joseph.’ He said: Their leader who stayed behind said it. He said: The well is a well in Ash-Sham. Some travelers picked him up. He said: Some Bedouins picked him up. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him in his statement: And cast him into the bottom of the well. He meant the pool. Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak that he said: The well is the well. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated that he said: It is a well in Jerusalem. He said: In one of its areas. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd that he said: The well is next to Tiberias, and there are miles between it and it.
12:11: When they agreed to throw him into the depths of the well, they came to their father and addressed him with the word fatherhood, to entreat him and stir up the compassion that fathers are naturally inclined towards their sons, and to use that to complete the plot they had plotted. They asked him the question of someone who is denial about something that should be the opposite of reality, so 11- They said, ‘O our father, what is the matter with you that you do not trust us with Joseph?’ That is, what is the matter with you that you do not make us trustees with him? It is as if they had asked him before that to let Joseph go with them, but he refused. Yazid bin Al-Qa’qa’, Amr bin Ubaid, and Al-Zuhri read don’t trust us with assimilation without ishmām. Talha bin Masraf read La Ta’manna with two apparent nuns according to the original. Yahya bin Waththab, Abu Razin, and Al-A’mash read La Taymanna, which is the language of Tamim, as mentioned above. The rest of the reciters read with assimilation and ishmām to indicate the state of the letter before its assimilation. And indeed, we are his sincere advisers, in preserving and protecting it until we return it to you.
12:12: 12- Send him with us tomorrow meaning to the desert they wanted to go to, and tomorrow is a circumstance, and the original according to Sibawayh is ghadwa. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: What is between dawn and sunrise is called ghadwa, and it is also called bakra He grazes and plays This is the answer to the command. The people of Basra, Mecca and the Levant read it with the letter noon and the letter 'ayn is silent as some have narrated from them. They also read it with ikhtilas, and the rest read it with the letter noon and the letter 'ayn is broken, and the first reading is taken from the Arabs' saying Ra'ta' al-Insan or al-Ba'ir: if he eats as he pleases, or the meaning is: We expand in fertility, and everything fertile is grazing: the poet said Shepherds of Fazara, there is no pasture there And from it the poet said: It rises as it grazes, until it is remembered, then it is only coming and going The second reading is taken from the pasture of sheep. Mujahid and Qatadah read yatra’ and yal’ab with a tanween in both of them, and raised yal’ab as a resumption, and the pronoun refers to Yusuf. Al-Qatibi said: The meaning of yal’ab is we guard and take care of each other, from their saying May God protect you meaning He preserved you, and yal’ab is from the word ya’lab play. It was said to Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’: How did they say wa’lab when they were prophets? He said: They were not prophets at that time. It was said that what was meant by it was the permissible play of the prophets, which is mere relaxation.
