It was said that it was the play by which they learned war and strengthened themselves for it, as in their saying We went racing, not the forbidden play that is against the truth. That is why Jacob did not denounce them for saying wa’lab play. From this is his saying, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, to Jabir: Why not a young camel for you to play with and for you to play with.
12:13: So Jacob answered them by saying: 13- Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away meaning that you should take him away, and the lam in it grieves me is the lam of beginning for emphasis and to specify the present tense with the state, he told them that he was saddened by Joseph's absence from him due to his great love for him and his fear for him, and I fear that the wolf will eat him meaning despite that I fear that the wolf will eat him. Jacob said this out of fear for him from them, so he used the wolf as a metaphor for that. It was said that he feared that the wolf would eat him in reality, because that place had many wolves, and if he feared that they would kill him, he would have sent someone with them to guard him. Tha'lab said: The wolf is taken from the wind that raged from every direction. He said: The wolf is hamzated because it comes from every direction. Ibn Kathir and Nafi' in a narration from him read it with a hamzah from the original, as did Abu Amr in a narration from him, Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamza. The rest read it with a light pronunciation, and you are heedless of it, because you are busy with pasture and play, or because they are not interested in preserving it.
12:14: 14- They said, 'If the wolf eats him while we are a group' The lam is the particle that introduces the oath. The meaning is: By God, if the wolf eats him, and the situation is that we are a group: that is, a large group of ten, then we will be losers meaning that at that time, when the wolf eats him, we will be losers, doomed by weakness and inability, or deserving of destruction because we are not taken into account, and the lack of ability to do the easiest and least thing, or deserving of being called losers and destroyed. It was said that we are losers because of those who are ignorant of his right, and this sentence is the answer to the oath implied in the sentence before it.
12:15: 15- So when they took him from Jacob and agreed their command to put him in the bottom of the well the explanation of the bottom and the well has been presented recently, and the answer to what is omitted due to its clarity and the indication of the situation, and the estimate: they did to him what they did, and it was said its answer is they said, O our father, indeed we went racing and it was said the estimated answer is they put him in it, and it was said the answer is we inspired and the waw is inserted, and similar to it is the saying of the Most High: So when they had both submitted and he prostrated himself on his forehead * And We called to him meaning We called to him and We inspired to him meaning to Joseph to make things easy for him and to comfort his loneliness despite his being young, ten men from his brothers gathered to harm him, with hard hearts from which mercy had been removed and compassion had been taken away from them, for human nature, let alone religion, overlooks the sin of a young person and forgives it due to his weakness in repelling and his inability to do the easiest thing that is wanted from him, so how about a young person who has no sin For him, but how about a young man who is his brother and they have a father like Jacob? He who said that they were prophets at that time is far from the truth, for this is not how the prophets acted nor did the righteous. And in this is evidence that it is permissible for God to inspire someone who was young and give him prophethood at that time, as happened with Jesus and John, son of Zechariah. And it has been said that at that time he had reached the age of manhood, and this is very far-fetched, for someone who had reached the age of manhood does not fear that a wolf will eat him. You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs means you will inform your brothers of this affair of theirs that they did to you after you were freed from what they wanted to do to you of plotting and inflicting upon you of harm. And the phrase and they do not perceive is in the accusative case as a state: meaning they do not perceive that you are their brother Joseph because they believe that you will perish by throwing you into the bottom of the well, and because of the distance between them and you, and because you have become at that time in a state other than what you were and contrary to what they knew of you. And what he said to them when they entered upon him after he became king of Egypt will come.
12:16: 16- His saying: And they came to their father at nightfall, weeping. Nightfall is an adverbial phrase, and it is the end of the day. It was said that it was at night, and weeping is in the accusative case as a state: meaning weeping or pretending to weep, because they did not truly weep, but rather they did the action of someone who weeps, promoting their lies and fulfilling their deceit and treachery.
12:17: When they reached their father 16- "They said, 'O our father, indeed we went racing' meaning we competed in running or in shooting, and it was said that we were trying to win, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, we were trying to win." Al-Zajjaj said: It is a type of competition. Al-Zuhri said: Struggle is in arrows, and betting is in horses, and the competition brings them together. Al-Qushayri said: We were racing, meaning in shooting or on horses or on foot. The purpose of the competition is to train in combat. "And we left Joseph by our belongings" meaning by our clothes to guard them. "And the wolf ate him the fa" is for follow-up: meaning it ate him after that. And they apologized to him for what they had previously feared for him, and many a word says to its speaker leave me "and you will not believe us by believing us in this excuse that we presented, and the word that we said even if we were in your opinion or in reality truthful" because of what had stuck in your heart of accusation against us in that despite the intensity of your love for him. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: If we were trustworthy and honest people in your view, you would not have believed us in this matter because of the intensity of your love for Joseph.
12:18: And Ibn Jarir and others mentioned it 18- And they came upon his shirt with false blood upon his shirt in the accusative case as an adverbial phrase: meaning they came upon his shirt with blood, and the description of the blood as false is an exaggeration as is known in describing the name of the eye with the name of the meaning, and it was said that the meaning is: with the blood of a lie or with the blood that is falsely attributed to it. Al-Hasan and Aisha read with the blood of a lie with the silent dal: meaning with fresh blood, fresh blood is called a lie. Al-Sha'bi said: It is the changed, and the lie is also the whiteness that appears in the nails of young people, so it is possible that the likening of the blood on the shirt to the whiteness that appears in the nails from the side of the two colors. Jacob proved their lie by the authenticity of the shirt, and he said to them: When was this wolf wise, eating Joseph and not tearing the shirt? Then God the Almighty mentioned what Jacob answered them with, saying: "He said: Rather, your souls have enticed you to a matter" meaning they have made it seem beautiful and easy. Al-Naysaburi said: Tasweel is a statement of the meaning of the self with the desire for its completion. It is an activation from sawl which means a wish. Al-Azhari said: “Its origin is hamzat, but the Arabs found the hamza heavy in it. “Fa sabr jameel” so patience is beautiful. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, my affair or what I believe is beautiful patience. Qatrib said: That is, my patience is beautiful patience. It was said: Fa sabr jameel is more appropriate for me. It was said: And beautiful patience is that with which there is no complaint. Al-Zajjaj said: Isa bin Omar recited, according to what Sahl bin Yusuf claimed, “Fa sabr jameel so patience is beautiful. He said: And this is also in the copy of Anas. Al-Mubarrad said: Fa sabr jameel in the nominative case is more appropriate than the accusative case. Because the meaning is: He said, My Lord, I have beautiful patience. The accusative case is based on the source, meaning, So I will be patient with beautiful patience. The poet said: My camel complained to me about the long journey. Be patient, for we are both afflicted. And God is the one sought for help meaning help is sought from Him against what you describe meaning to reveal the state of what you describe, or to bear what you describe. This from him, peace be upon him, is an act of creation, not information. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Send him with us tomorrow to graze and play, he said: We strive, be active and play. Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Salfi narrated in Al-Tayouriyat on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Do not prompt people lest they lie, for the children of Jacob did not know that the wolf eats people, but when their father prompted them, they lied and said the wolf ate him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And We inspired him, the verse, he said: It was inspired to Joseph while he was in the well that you should inform your brothers of what they did, and they were not aware of that revelation. And these narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: God inspired him with a revelation while he was in the well that he would inform them of what they did, and they - meaning his brothers - were not aware of that revelation, so that revelation made what he did to him easy for him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and they were not aware, he said: They did not know that God had inspired him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: When Joseph’s brothers entered upon Joseph and he recognized them while they did not recognize him, a measure was brought to him and he placed it on his hand, then he tapped it and became aware. He said: This cup tells me that you had a brother from your father called Joseph who used to bring him close to you, and that you went with him and threw him into the bottom of the well and came to your father and said: The wolf ate him, and you came upon his shirt with false blood. Some of them said to each other: This cup tells him your story. Ibn Abbas said: We do not think that this verse was revealed except for that, so that you will inform them of this matter of theirs while they do not perceive. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr Ibn Ayyash who said: Joseph was in the well for three days. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, And you will not believe us, meaning: He will believe us. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they came upon his shirt with false blood, meaning: It was the blood of a young goat. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they brought his shirt with false blood. He said: When Jacob was brought Joseph’s shirt and he did not see any tear in it, he said: You have lied. If it had been as you say, that a wolf had eaten him, the shirt would have been torn. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, he said: Your souls have commanded you. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Jarir and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, meaning, Rather, your souls have made something attractive to you, “So patience is most fitting, and God is the One sought for help against that which you describe,” meaning against that which you deny. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in his book, Patience, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Hubban bin Abi Hublah, who said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about his statement, ‘So patience is most fitting,’ and he said, ‘There is no complaint in it, for he who is patient is not patient.’” It is through the chain of transmission of Hisham on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman on the authority of Hubban bin Abi Hublah, and it is a mursal. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, So patience is most fitting, he said, There is no impatience. 11- The predicate of indeed, those who brought the slander is a group and from among you is an attribute of a group. It was also said that it is do not think it is evil for you, and a group would be a substitute for the subject of came. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is more consistent in meaning and more beneficial than the predicate being a group, and the sentence do not think it is, even if it is a request. So making it a predicate is correct by estimation as in similar examples. And slander is the worst and ugliest lie, and it is taken from afka something if he turned it upside down. So, ifk is the upside-down hadith, and it was said that it is slander. The Muslims agreed that what is meant by the verse is the slander that was committed against Aisha, the Mother of the Believers. God described it as slander because what is known about her condition, may God be pleased with her, is otherwise. Al-Wahidi said: The meaning of the inversion in this hadith that those people brought is that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, deserved praise for what she had of immunity and noble lineage and the reason, not slander. Those who accused her of evil turned the matter upside down, so it is an ugly slander and a clear lie. The group is the group of ten to forty, and what is meant by them here is Abdullah bin Abi Ras, the head of the hypocrites, Zaid bin Rifa’a, Hassan bin Thabit, Mastah bin Athatah, Hamna bint Jahsh, and those who helped them. It was said that the group is from three to ten, and it was said from ten to fifteen. Its root in the language is a group that is fanatical towards one another. The phrase do not think it evil for you if it is the predicate of in then it is clear, and if the predicate is a group as mentioned above then it is a new sentence. It was addressed to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, Aisha and Sufyan ibn al-Mu’attal who was slandered with the Mother of the Believers and as a consolation for them. Evil is that which exceeds its harm, and good is that which exceeds its benefit. As for good in which there is no evil, it is Paradise, and evil in which there is no good is Hellfire. The reason for it being good for them is that it will bring them a great reward while clarifying the innocence of the Mother of the Believers and making her story a general law. For each person among them is what he has earned of sin i.e. because of speaking the slander. And he among them who bore the greater part of it will have a great punishment. Al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, Abu Raja’, Hamid al-A’raj, Ya’qub, Ibn Abi Ulayyah, Mujahid and Umrah bint Abd al-Rahman read it with a damma on the kaf. Al-Farra' said: This is a good interpretation, because the Arabs say: So-and-so took on the greatness of such-and-such, meaning he took on the greatest of it. The rest read it with a kasra. It was said that they are two dialects, and it was said that with a damma it means most of the slander, and with a kasra it means starting with it, and it was said that with a kasra it means the sin. So the meaning is: The one who took on most of the slander from the group will have a great punishment in this world or in the hereafter or in both. There was a difference of opinion as to who among the group that perpetrated the slander was from. Some said it was Abdullah ibn Ubayy, others said it was Hassan; the former is more correct. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) flogged two men and a woman for slander, namely Mistah ibn Athatah, Hassan ibn Thabit, and Hamna bint Jahsh. Some said that Abdullah ibn Ubayy flogged, Hassan ibn Thabit, and Hamna bint Jahsh, but he did not flog Mistah because he did not explicitly state the slander, but he heard about it and spread it without explicitly. Some said that he did not flog any of them. Al-Qurtubi said: The well-known report and what is well-known among scholars is that those who were flogged were Hassan, Mistah, and Hamna. He did not hear of any punishment being given to Abdullah ibn Ubayy. This is supported by what is in Sunan Abi Dawud on the authority of Aisha, who said: When my excuse was revealed, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) stood up, mentioned it, and recited the Qur’an. When he came down from the pulpit, he ordered the two men and the woman to be flogged, and he named them: Hassan, Mistah ibn Athatah, and Hamna bint Jahsh. They differed as to why the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not flog Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Some said it was to spare him the great punishment in the Hereafter, and to punish those who came after him so that it would be an expiation for their sin, as it was proven from him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the prescribed punishments that he said: It is an expiation for whoever is subjected to it. Others said he did not flog his people out of respect for his son, as he was one of the righteous believers, and to extinguish the flames of sedition, the beginnings of which had appeared with Sa`d ibn `Ubadah and those with him, as in Sahih Muslim. Then God, the Almighty, diverted the address from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and those with him to the believers by way of a shift.
12:19: This is the beginning of the story of Joseph's salvation and what follows from his story. The explanation of the car has been presented, and what is meant here is a passing group traveling from Syria to Egypt, so they lost their way and wandered until they came down near the well, which was in a desert far from civilization, and the water-drawer was the one who brought water to draw for the people, and his name was mentioned by the commentators Malik bin Dhir from the pure Arabs. So he lowered his bucket means he sent it, it is said that he lowered his bucket: if he sent it to fill it, and he lowered it: if he took it out, as Al-Asma'i and others said. Joseph held on to the rope, and when the bucket came out of the well, the water-drawer saw him, so he said, 'O good report' This is how the people of Medina, Mecca, Basra, and Syria read it, adding the good report to the pronoun, and the people of Kufa read O good report without an addition, and the meaning of his calling to the good report is that he wanted her to come at that time, so it is as if he said: This is the time for your arrival and the time for your attendance, and it was said that he called a man named Bushra. The first is more appropriate. An-Nahhas said: The meaning of the call to good report is to give good report to those who are present, and it is more emphatic than saying, I gave him good report, as you say, Oh wonder, meaning, Oh wonder, this is one of your days, so attend. He said: This is the doctrine of Sibawayh. And they took him prisoner, meaning, the visitor and his companions who were with him took Joseph prisoner, but they did not reveal him to them. It was said that they did not hide him, but rather they concealed his presence in the well, and they claimed that the people of the water had given him to them to sell him to them in Egypt. It was said that the subject pronoun in they took him prisoner refers to Joseph’s brothers, and the object pronoun refers to Joseph, because his brother Judah used to bring him food every day. He came to him on the day he came out of the well and informed his brothers, so they came to the company and said, This is a boy who has escaped from us, so they bought him from them. Joseph remained silent for fear that they would take him and kill him. The first is more appropriate. And the erection of the commodity in the state: that is, they hid it while it was a commodity: that is, goods for trade, and the commodity: what is bought from the money: that is, it is cut from it because it is a piece of the money with which one trades, it was said that the visitor and his companions told them that it was a commodity that we bought from Syria for fear that they would share it with them, and in His saying: And God is Knowing of what they do is a severe warning to whoever whose action was the cause of what Joseph fell into of trials and what he became of vulgarity with the buying and selling taking place in it, and he is the generous son of the generous son of the generous son of the generous: Joseph son of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham as our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in describing him with that.
12:20: His saying: 20- And they sold him for a cheap price, a few dirhams. It is said that he bought him, meaning he bought him, and he sold him, meaning he sold him. The poet said: I bought a cloak. I wish I was important after the cold weather. I sold it. Another said: When he bought it, his eyes filled with tears. That is, he bought it. What is meant here is: and they sold it: that is, the visitor and his companions sold it for a cheap price, that is, incomplete or false. It was said that it refers to Joseph’s brothers according to the previous statement, and it was said that it refers to the company, and the meaning is: they bought it. It was said that it was cheap: injustice, and it was said that it was forbidden. It was said that they sold it for twenty dirhams, and it was said forty, and dirhams instead of a price: meaning dinars, and counted is a description of dirhams, and in it is an indication that they are few and counted and not weighed, because they did not weigh anything less than an ounce, which is forty dirhams. And they were among the ascetics in it. It is said that they were ascetic and renounced with the opening of the ha’ and its breaking. Sibawayh and Al-Kisa’i said: The linguists said: It is said that he was ascetic in it: meaning he was averse to it, and that he was averse to it: meaning he desired it, and the meaning is that they were among those who were averse to it and did not care about it, so that is why they sold it for that cheap price, and that is because they picked it up, and the one who picks up something: is careless with it, and the pronoun from they were refers to what precedes it according to the different opinions about it.
12:21: 21- And he who bought him from Egypt said He is Al-Aziz who was in charge of the treasuries of Egypt, and he was a minister to the king of Egypt, and he is Al-Rayyan bin Al-Walid from the giants, and it was said that the king was the Pharaoh of Moses, it was said that he bought him for twenty dinars and it was said that they increased his price so that it reached many times its weight in musk, amber, silk, paper, gold, pearls and jewels, so when Al-Aziz bought him he said to his wife and the lam is related to bought him Honor his abode meaning his home in which he resides with good food and fine clothing, it is said that he resided in a place: meaning he stayed in it Perhaps he will benefit us meaning that he will suffice us for some of the important things that we need someone like him in it or we will adopt him as a son meaning that we will adopt him and make him a son for us, it was said that Al-Aziz was chaste and did not have children, and it was said that he did not come to women, and it was speculated that he would represent him in what he had to do with the affairs of the kingdom. His saying: And thus We established Joseph The kaf is in the accusative case as a description of a deleted source, and the reference is to what came before of his rescue from his brothers and his removal from the well, and the affection of the Aziz’s heart towards him: that is, like that wonderful establishment, We established Joseph until he became able to command and forbid. It is said, We established him in it: that is, We established him in it, and We established him in it: that is, We made a place for him in it. And because the two meanings are close, each one of them is used in place of the other. His saying: And that We may teach him the interpretation of dreams is a reason for an omitted reason, as if it were said: We did that empowerment so that We may teach him the interpretation of dreams, or that salvation was for this reason, or it is conjoined with something understood, which is to say: We empowered Joseph so that what happened between him and the wife of the Aziz would result from that, and so that We may teach him the interpretation of dreams. The meaning of the interpretation of dreams is the interpretation of dreams, for it was one of the reasons by which he reached what he reached of empowerment. It was said that the meaning of the interpretation of dreams is understanding the secrets of the divine books and the traditions of the prophets who came before him, and there is no objection to applying that to all of them. And God is predominant over His affair, meaning over His own affair, nothing is prevented from Him, and no one else among His creations can overcome Him in it. His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. Among the things that fall under this generality, as indicated by the addition of the generic name to the pronoun, are the things that God the Almighty intended for Joseph, peace be upon him. It was said that the meaning of and God is predominant over His affair is that it was commanded by Jacob not to tell Joseph’s vision to his brothers, but God’s command was predominant until it was told to them and what happened from them happened. This is very far-fetched. But most people do not know, meaning they do not know God’s unseen and what is hidden in it of great secrets and beneficial wisdom. It was said that what is meant by most is everyone because no one knows the unseen except God. It was said that God the Almighty may inform some of His servants of some of His unseen as in His statement: And He does not disclose His secrets to anyone * Except to a messenger with whom He is pleased. It was said that the meaning is: But most people do not know that God is predominant over His affair, and they are the polytheists and those who do not believe in predestination.
12:22: And His saying: 22- And when he reached his full strength, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. The most intense. Sibawayh said that the singular form of shaddah is plural. Al-Kisa'i said: Its singular form is shadd. Abu Ubaid said: It does not have a singular form of its word among the Arabs, and this is refuted by the poet's saying: I remember him during the day, as if his fingers and head were dyed with bone The most severe: is the time of completing strength and then the decrease comes after it. It was said that it is thirty-three years, and it was said that it is reaching puberty, and it was said that it is eighteen years, and it was said that it is other than that which we have already explained in An-Nisa and Al-An'am. And the ruling: is what he did of rulings under the authority of the king of Egypt, and knowledge: is the knowledge of the ruling that he used to rule, and it was said that the mind, understanding and prophecy were a boy. He said: What is meant by this ruling and knowledge that God gave him is the increase in them. And thus do We reward the doers of good meaning and like that amazing reward We reward the doers of good, so whoever does good in his work, God rewards him well, and makes the good end part of what He rewards him with, and this is general and includes under it the reward of Joseph for his good patience as a primary entry, Al-Tabari said: Although its source is apparent for every doer of good, what is meant by it is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, God the Most High says: Just as Joseph did this, then I gave him what I gave him, thus I will save you from the polytheists of your people who intend to enmity against you, and I will establish you in the land. The first is what we mentioned about taking the generality at face value, so what Ibn Jarir al-Tabari mentioned falls under it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: And a caravan came he said: A caravan came and descended into the well So they sent their water-drawer he asked for water and brought out Joseph, they were happy because they had found a boy whose knowledge and status they did not know with his Lord, so they were reluctant to sell him, and selling him was forbidden, and they sold him for a few dirhams. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada So they sent their water-drawer he said: they sent their messenger So he lowered his bucket so the boy got stuck in the bucket, and when he came out he said, ‘O good report! This is a boy’ they were happy when they brought him out, and it is a well in Jerusalem whose location is known. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: O good report, he said: His companion’s name was Bushra, just as you would say O Zayd. This, despite its remoteness, is only complete according to the reading of those who read O good report without an addition. Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar from al-Sha’bi. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they concealed him as merchandise, meaning that Joseph’s brothers concealed his affair and hid that he was their brother, and Joseph concealed his affair for fear that his brothers would kill him and chose to sell him, so his brothers sold him for a low price. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The merchants concealed him from one another. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority: And they took him as merchandise meaning: The owner of the bucket and those with him said to their companions: We have taken him as merchandise for fear that they would share him with them if they knew about him. His brothers followed them saying to the one who carried him and his companions: Make sure he does not run away until they stopped in Egypt and he said: Who will buy me and give me good report? So the king bought him and the king was Muslim. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they sold him meaning: Joseph’s brothers sold him when the one carrying his bucket brought him out. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: He was sold among them for a cheap price. He said: It was forbidden and it was not permissible for them to sell him or eat his price. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada, And they sold him for a cheap price. He said: They are the caravan. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib that he ruled regarding the foundling that he was free and he recited: And they sold him for a cheap price. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Bakhs means little. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated the same on the authority of Al-Sha’bi. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani and Al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: Joseph was bought for twenty dirhams, and his family when he was sent to them in Egypt were three hundred and ninety al-Nas 114:their men were prophets and their women were friends. By God, they did not go out with Moses until they reached six hundred and seventy thousand. Other than this amount has been narrated regarding the price of Joseph, which there is no need to elaborate on. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And he who bought him from Egypt said, he said: His name was Qutfir. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Shu’ayb Al-Jubba’i that the name of Al-Aziz’s wife was Zulaykha. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Ishaq who said: The one who bought him was Atifir Ibn Ruhab, and his wife’s name was Ra’il bint Ra’il. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Ishaq and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The name of the one who sold him to Al-Aziz was Malik Ibn Dhi’r. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Honor his abode he said: His position. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada something similar. Sa’id Ibn Mansour, Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: The most discerning of people are three: Al-Aziz when he discerned Joseph and said to his wife: Honor his abode; perhaps he may benefit us or we may adopt him as a son. The woman who came to Moses and said to her father: O my father, hire him. And Abu Bakr when he appointed Umar as caliph. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And that We may teach him the interpretation of dreams, he said: The expression of dreams. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Al-Anbari in Kitab Al-Adad, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And when he reached his full strength, he said: Thirty-three years. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Forty years. He narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Twenty-five years. He narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Thirty years. He narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: Eighteen years. He narrated on the authority of Rabia, he said: The dream. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: Twenty years. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, We gave him wisdom and knowledge, he said: It is jurisprudence, knowledge and reason before prophethood. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And thus do We reward the doers of good, he said: The guided ones.
12:23: Seduction is the will and request with gentleness and softness - and it was said that it is taken from the root: meaning gentleness and patience, it is said that he gave me time: he gave me time, and it was said that seduction is taken from the root rad yarud: if he came and went, as if the meaning is: that she did in her seduction of him the action of a deceiver, and from it the pioneer for the one who seeks water and pasture, and it may be specific to the attempt to have intercourse, so it is said: So-and-so seduced his slave girl from herself and she seduced him from himself: if each of them tried to have intercourse and copulation, and it is a reciprocal action, and its origin is to be from both sides, so the cause here was made on one side in place of the effect, so it is as if Joseph, peace be upon him, when what he was given of perfect creation and increase in beauty was a reason for the Aziz’s wife to seduc him, was a seducer. Rather, he said, in whose house he is, and did not say the wife of Al-Aziz and Zulaykha, intending to increase the emphasis, while expressing disapproval of mentioning the woman’s name and preserving her privacy. And the doors were closed. It was said about this formula that which indicates abundance, so it is said, The doors were closed, and it is not said, The door was closed, rather it is said, The door was closed, and it may be said, The doors were closed, and from this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq about Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala: I kept closing and opening doors until I came to Abu Amr bin Ammar It was said that the doors were seven. His saying: Hayt laka. Abu Amr, Asim, Al-Kisa’i, Hamza, and Al-A’mash read it with the opening of the ha’, the sukoon of the ya’, and the opening of the ta’. Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Ikrimah read it this way. Ibn Mas’ud said: Do not be extreme in the reading, for it is like one of you saying Hallam wa ta’al. Ibn Abi Ishaq Al-Nahwi read it with the opening of the ha’ and the kasra of the ta’. Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami and Ibn Kathir read Hayt with the opening of the ha’ and the damma of the ta’. From this is the saying of Tarafa: My people are not the farthest away if a caller from the tribe says: Hit Abu Jaafar and Nafi’ read it with a kasra on the ha’, a sukoon on the ya’, and a fatha on the ta’. Ali, Ibn Abbas, in a narration from him, and Hisham read it with a kasra on the ha’ followed by a silent hamza and a damma on the ta’. Ibn Amir and the people of Ash-Sham read it with a kasra on the ha’, a hamza, and a fatha on the ta’. The meaning of hayt according to all readings is the meaning of ham and ta’al, because it is a verbal noun except in the reading of those who read with a kasra on the ha’ followed by a hamza and a damma on the ta’, because it means: it was prepared for you. Abu Amr rejected this reading. Abu Ubaidah said: Abu Amr was asked about the reading of those who read with a kasra on the ha’ and a hamza and a damma on the ta’, so he said: It is false to make it mean you were prepared. Go and review the Arabs until you reach Yemen. Do you know anyone who says this? Al-Kisa’i also rejected it. An-Nahhas said: It is good according to the Basrans, because it is said: A man’s ha’ is yaha’ and he prepares a state. Az-Zajjaj preferred the first reading, and recited the aforementioned verse of Tarafa, haytān with a fatha, and from it is the saying of the poet about Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: Tell the Commander of the Faithful, the brother of Iraq, when you come Iraq and its people are in your hands, so come and come The lam in laka in the first readings in which it has the meaning of a verbal noun is for clarification: i.e. to you. I say this as in halam laka. The grammarians said: Hayt came with the three vowels: the fatha for lightness, the kasra for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the damma as a resemblance to batha, and if it is explained by the lam like hayt laka then it is a sound that takes the place of the verbal noun like af lahu: i.e. to you I say this, and if it is not explained by the lam then it is a sound that takes the place of the verbal noun and so it is a verbal noun, either a predicate: i.e. I got ready, or a command: i.e. I came. And it says in Al-Sahah: It is said hawat bih and hayat bih if he shouted at him and called him, and from this is the saying of the poet: Every young man is motivated by it It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan that it is a Syriac word meaning that she invites him to herself. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Kisa’i used to say: It is a language of the people of Hawran that was transmitted to the people of Hijaz and means come. Abu Ubaidah said: So I asked a learned sheikh from Hawran and he said that it is their language. He said, ‘God forbid’ meaning I seek refuge in God from what you have invited me to. It is a verbal noun in the accusative case with a deleted verb added to the name of God Almighty. The phrase He is my Lord, He has made my stay good is an explanation of the refusal resulting from it for some reasons that are closer to the understanding of the wife of Al-Aziz. The pronoun refers to the matter: that is, the matter is my Lord, meaning Al-Aziz: meaning my master who raised me and made my stay good where he commanded you with his saying: Honor his stay. So how can I betray him in his family and respond to what you want from that? Al-Zajjaj said: The pronoun refers to God Almighty: meaning, God, my Lord, has taken care of me with His kindness, so I will not commit what He has forbidden. The phrase Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed is another explanation for his refusal to answer her question. Success means triumph. The meaning is that the wrongdoers will not achieve what they demand, and among the wrongdoers who fall into such a sin is the one that the wife of Al-Aziz demands of Joseph.
12:24: His saying: 24- And she certainly desired him and he desired her It is said that he desired a matter: if he intended it and resolved to do it. The meaning is that he desired to mix with her as she desired to mix with him and each of them inclined towards the other according to human nature and innate disposition, and it was not from Joseph, peace be upon him, to intend that by choice as is indicated by what was mentioned previously from his seeking refuge with God, and that this is a type of injustice. And since the prophets are infallible from the desire to sin and the desire to do it, the scholars went too far in interpreting this verse with a type of affectation, including what Abu Hatim said: I was reading to Abu Ubaidah the strange verses of the Qur’an, and when I came to And she certainly desired him and he desired her he said: This is on the basis of precedence and delay: as if he said: And she certainly desired him and had he not seen the proof of his Lord for them with her. Ahmad bin Yahya Tha’lab said: That is, Zulaykha intended to commit a sin but was determined, and Joseph intended to commit a sin but did not commit the sin. So there is a difference between the two intentions. From this is the saying of the poet: I wanted to meet them from the valley of Lulu, and I cured the burning passion in my heart. This is only a thought without resolve. It was said that he intended to do it: that is, he intended to hit her. It was also said that he intended to do it in the sense that he wished to marry her. The majority of the commentators from the early and later generations have adopted what we have presented of carrying the wording according to its linguistic meaning. This is indicated by what will come from his statement, That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret, and his statement, “And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil.” Merely intending does not contradict infallibility, for infallibility has occurred from falling into sin, and that is what is required. The answer to if in Had he not seen the proof of his Lord is omitted: that is, had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have done what he intended to do. There is a difference of opinion about this proof that he saw. What was it? It was said that Zulaykha stood up when she wanted to marry him and he wanted to marry her to an idol of hers in the corner of the house, so she covered it with a garment. He said: What are you doing? She said: I am ashamed before my God that He sees me in this state. Joseph said: I am more deserving of being ashamed before God Almighty. It was said that he saw written on the ceiling of the house: “And do not come near to adultery. Indeed, it is an immorality” 10:13. It was also said that he saw a hand written on it: And indeed, over you are guardians. It was also said that the proof was his remembrance of God’s covenant and pledge and what He took from His servants. It was also said that he was called: O Joseph, are you written among the prophets and yet you do the work of fools? It was also said that he saw the image of Jacob on the wall biting his fingertip threatening him. It was also said that there were other things that would take too long to mention. The result is that he saw something that came between him and what he intended to do. His statement: Thus did We avert from him evil and immorality. The kaf is an adjective of a deleted source, and the reference in that is to the showing indicated by His statement: Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, or to the confirmation understood from that: i.e. We showed him like that showing, or We confirmed like that confirmation. To avert from him evil, i.e. everything that would upset him. Immorality is every extremely ugly matter. It was said that evil is betrayal of the honorable one in his family, and immorality is adultery. It was said that evil is lust, and immorality is direct contact. It was said that evil is ugly praise. The first is to carry it in generality, so what the context indicates is included in it primarily. The phrase indeed, he is one of Our sincere servants is an explanation of what preceded it. Ibn Amir, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read al-mukhlisin with a kasra on the lam. The others read it with a fatha. The meaning according to the first reading is that Joseph, peace be upon him, was one of those who sincerely obeyed God, and according to the second, he was one of those whom God chose for the message.
12:25: And he, peace be upon him, was sincere and sincere 25- And they raced to the door meaning they raced to it, so the preposition was deleted and the verb was connected to the object, or the verb included the meaning of another verb that is transitive by itself such as they raced to the door, and this statement is connected to his saying: And she certainly desired him and he desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord and what is between them is an objection, and the reason for their racing is that Joseph wanted to flee and exit through the door, and the wife of the Aziz wanted to precede him to it to prevent him, and the door was made singular here and plural in what came before, because their racing was to the door through which he could escape to the outside of the house And she tore his shirt from the back meaning she pulled his shirt from behind so that it split to the bottom, and the cutting is the cutting, and it is most often used for what is long, and the cutting with the letter ta is used for what is wide, and this happened from her when Joseph fled when he saw the proof of his Lord, so she wanted to prevent him from exiting by pulling his shirt And they found her master at the door meaning they found the Aziz there, and by master he meant: the husband Because the Copts call the husband master, and he did not say their master, because his ownership of Joseph was not true, so he was not his master. The phrase She said, ‘What is the reward of one who intended evil for your family?’ is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said: What happened between them when they found her master at the door? What is interrogative, and what is meant by evil here is adultery. She said this statement seeking a trick and to cover herself up, so she attributed what happened from her to Joseph: what reward does he deserve for doing something like this? Then she answered her question by saying: Except that he be imprisoned, meaning what is his reward except that he be imprisoned. It is possible that what is negative: meaning his reward is nothing but imprisonment or painful torment. It was said that painful torment is whipping, and it appears that what is true of painful torment, whether beating or otherwise, and in the ambiguity of the torment there is an increase in terror.
12:26: And sentence 26 - He said, 'She sought to seduce me' is resumed like the first sentence. The meaning of seduce has already been explained: that is, she is the one who asked me to do that and I did not intend any harm to her. And a witness from her family testified that is, from her relatives. The judgment between them was called testimony because of the verification and contemplation required in it. It was said that when the matter became confusing to Al-Aziz, he needed a judge to judge between them to distinguish who was telling the truth from who was lying. It was said that he was her cousin standing with Al-Aziz at the door, and it was said that he was her maternal uncle's son, and it was said that he was a child in the cradle who spoke. Al-Suhayli said: This is correct, according to the hadith narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in mentioning those who spoke in the cradle, and he mentioned among them the witness of Joseph, and it was said that he was a wise man whom the Aziz would consult in his affairs, and he was a relative of the woman. If his shirt is torn from the front, meaning the witness said this statement, proving the truth of the truthful one of them and the lie of the liar, that if Joseph’s shirt was torn from the front: meaning from the front side, then she has told the truth, meaning she has told the truth that he intended to harm her, and he is among the liars, in his statement that she tried to seduce him. Yahya bin Ya’mar and Ibn Abi Ishaq read from before with a damma on the lam. This is how they read from behind. Al-Zajjaj said: They made them two ends like before and after, as if it was said from before him and from behind, but when the object of the genitive was deleted, which was intended, the object of the genitive became the end after the object of the genitive was the end.
12:27: 27- And if his shirt is torn from the back meaning from behind then she has lied in her claim against him and he is among the truthful in her claim against her. It is not hidden that these two conditional sentences do not last and there is no connection between their antecedents and their consequences, neither rationally nor habitually. There is nothing here but a mere non-constant indication, since it is possible that she pulls him towards her while he is facing her and he tears the shirt from the back, and that she pulls him while he is turning away from her and he tears the shirt from the front.
12:28: 28- And when he saw meaning the Aziz his shirt meaning Joseph’s shirt torn from the back, he said, “Indeed, it is meaning this matter over which the disagreement occurred between you, or that your saying: What is the reward of one who intended evil for your family “of your plot” meaning of the same kind as your plot, O women, indeed, your plot is great. And plotting is deceit and trickery.
12:29: Then Al-Aziz addressed Joseph, saying 29- Joseph, turn away from this meaning from this matter that happened and conceal it and do not talk about it, then he addressed her and said and ask forgiveness for your sin that occurred from you for you were because of that of the sinners meaning of their kind, and the sentence explains what preceded it of the command to ask forgiveness and he did not say of the sinners, giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine as in his saying and she was of the obedient, and the meaning of the sinners is of the deliberate, it is said that he sinned if he sinned deliberately, and it was said that the one who said this statement to Joseph and the wife of Al-Aziz was the witness who judged between them. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shuyukh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And she in whose house he was sought to seduce him, he said: She is the wife of Al-Aziz. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd who said: She sought to seduce him when he had reached the age of manhood. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Heyt laka, he said: Come to you, inviting him to herself. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: Iqla: Helma laka in Coptic. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: It is a word in Syriac: meaning come to you. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr who said: Its meaning is come. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: It is an Arabic language in which she invites him to herself. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: He is my Lord, he said: My Master, he said: He means the husband of the woman. And Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When she desired him, she adorned herself and then lay down on her bed. And he desired her, so he sat between her legs and untied his clothes. Then a call was made from the sky, O son of Jacob, do not be like a bird that plucks its feathers and is left without feathers. But he did not learn from the call at all until he saw the proof of his Lord, Gabriel, in the form of Jacob biting his finger. So he was startled and his desire came out of his fingers, so he jumped up and caught up with him. She put her hands in his shirt and tore it until she reached the muscle of his calf, and they found her master at the door. Abu Nu`aym narrated in al-Hilyah on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding his statement: She desired him and he desired her, he said: She desired him and he desired her. And there was such greed in him that he desired to untied the knot, so she went to an idol of hers crowned with pearls and rubies in a corner of the house and covered it with a white garment between them. So he said: What are you doing? She said: I am ashamed before my God to see me in this state. Joseph said: Are you ashamed before an idol that neither eats nor drinks, and I am not ashamed before my God who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? Then he said: You will never attain it from me, and this is the proof that he saw. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he said: Jacob appeared to him, so he struck his chest with his hand and his desire came out from his fingers. The commentators have gone into great detail in identifying the proof that he saw, and their statements on this matter differed greatly. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit: Al-Sayyid said: The husband, meaning in his statement: And they found her master at the door. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Unless he is imprisoned or a painful punishment, he said: The chain. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And a witness from among her people testified, he said: A boy whom God had made to speak who was in the house. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Four spoke when they were young: the son of Pharaoh’s hairdresser, the witness of Joseph, the companion of the wounded man, and Jesus, son of Mary.” Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And a witness from among her people testified, he said: He was a man with a beard. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Abu Sheikh narrated on his authority that he said: He was one of the king’s special people. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he was a man of understanding and knowledge. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam that he said: Her cousin was wise. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: He was neither a human nor a jinn, he was a creation of God. I said: Perhaps he did not remember the statement of God, the Most High: from among her people.
12:30: It is said Naswa with a damma on the letter noon, and this is the reading of Al-A'mash, Al-Fadl, and Sulayman. It is said Naswa with a kasra on the letter noon, and this is the reading of the rest, and what is meant is a group of women, and the masculine is permissible in the verb attributed to them as it is permissible to feminize. It was said: They are the wife of the cupbearer of the Aziz and the wife of his baker, the wife of the owner of his beasts, the wife of the owner of his prison, and the wife of his chamberlain. In the speech of the Arabs, it is said: the young man and the young woman: the young woman, and what is meant here: her slave, it is said: my boy and my girl: meaning my boy and my maid. Sentence 30- Qad aghafaha haban is in the nominative case as a second predicate for the subject, or in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning of aghafaha haban is: his love overcame her, and it was said that his love entered her pericardium. Abu Ubaidah said: The pericardium is its covering and it is its skin, and it was said that it is the middle of the heart. Thus, the meaning is: His love entered her heart and overwhelmed her. Al-Asma’i recited the words of the rajaz poet: He follows her and she is passionate about him Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Ibn Muhaisin and Al-Hasan read it with the silent 'ayn. Ibn Al-A'rabi said: It means he poured his love over her. Others read it with the voiced 'ayn. Al-Jawhari said: Love suffused him, burned his heart. Abu Zaid said: It made him sick. Al-Nahhas said: According to most linguists, its meaning is: He took her in every direction, because the 'highest parts of the mountains' are their peaks. He became infatuated with that with the silent 'ayn': if he became obsessed with it. Abu Ubaidah recited the verse of Imru' al-Qais: Will you kill me, whose heart I have captivated as a woman captivates a man who has been searching for a long time? He said: So the pain of love was likened to that. Al-Hasan read it as Qad saghafaha with a damma on the ghain. An-Nahhas said: It was narrated as Qad saghafaha with a kasra on the ghain, and this is not known in the speech of the Arabs except as saghafaha with a fatha on the ghain. It is said that the pericardium is the skin attached to the liver that is not seen, and it is the white skin, so it is as if his love stuck to her heart like the skin sticks to the liver. The phrase Indeed, we see her in manifest error confirms the meaning of what preceded it. The meaning is: Indeed, we see her: that is, we know her in this action of hers, which is the seduction of her in straying from the path of guidance. The right path is clear: obvious and not confusing to anyone who looks into it.
12:31: 31- When the wife of Al-Aziz heard of their plot meaning their absence from her, absence was called plotting because they shared in concealing it. It was said that they wanted to use that to see Joseph, so their words were called plotting. It was also said that she confided in them and they revealed her secret, so it was called plotting. She sent to them meaning she invited them to her to look at Joseph until they fell into what she fell into. And she prepared for them a reclining place meaning she prepared for them seats to recline on. I prepared for them a reclining place is from I'tiddad, which is everything you make a provision for something. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubayr read Muttak without a hamza, and Muttak is the citron in the Coptic language, and from it is the saying of the poet: We drink sin openly, and you see the incense among us borrowed. It was said that this is the language of Azdashnu'ah, and it was said that this was narrated from Al-Akhfash. Al-Farra' said: It is rose water. The majority read it as Mutaka' with a hamza and emphasis, and the most correct thing that was said about it is the council, and it was said that it is food, and it was said that Mutaka' is everything that one leans on when eating, drinking, or talking. Al-Qatibi narrated that it is said that we leaned on someone, meaning we ate, and from this is the saying of the poet: So we remained in comfort, reclined, and drank lawfully from its wells. This is supported by his statement: And she gave each one of them a knife, for that is for something they eat after they cut it. Knife is both masculine and feminine, as stated by Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’. Al-Jawhari said: The most common is the masculine, and what is meant by her giving each one a knife is that they cut whatever food needs to be cut, and it is possible that she meant by that what would be cut from them by cutting their hands. And she said to Joseph, Come out to them, meaning in that state they were in of reclining, eating, and cutting whatever food needs to be cut. And his statement: And when they saw him, they glorified him, meaning his greatness, and it was said, they exaggerated, and from this is the saying of the poet: If they see the stallion from above, they neigh and exaggerate the dripping semen. It was said: a hug. Al-Azhari said: Akbarna means hug, and the ha is for silence. It is said that a woman became old: meaning she entered old age with menstruation. This caused them astonishment and fear at what they saw of his surpassing beauty and exquisite charm. From that is the saying of the poet: We come to women when they are pure, but we do not come to women when they are very old. Abu Ubaidah and others denied this and said: This is not in the speech of the Arabs. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said: Ikbarnahu but not Hadaanhu so ikbar does not mean al-haydhu. Al-Azhari responded by saying: It is possible for the ha of pause to be a pronoun and not a pronoun. This has been falsified by the fact that the ha of pause is dropped in the connection. Ibn al-Anbari said: The ha is a pronoun for the source of the verb: i.e. Ikbarna ikbar means Hadaanhu menstruating. And they cut their hands means they injured them. What is meant by this is not the cutting from which the hand is revealed, but rather what is meant by it is the scratch and the cut, and this is well-known in the language as al-Nahhas said: It is said that he cut the hand of his companion if he scratched it. It was said that what is meant by their hands here is their fingers, and it was said that their sleeves. Meaning: When Joseph came out to them, they were amazed and astonished by his beauty, and their hands trembled, and the pieces fell on them while they were busy with what had befallen them, which makes dreams go astray, bodies shake, and minds go astray. And they said, ‘God forbid.’ This is how Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ read it, with the alif in hasha. The rest read it without it. Al-Hasan read hasha li-llah with a sukoon on the shin. It was narrated from him that he read hasha li-llah. Ibn Mas’ud and Abu read hasha li-llah. Al-Zajjaj said: The root of the word is from hasha meaning side. You say, I was in the side of so-and-so, meaning on his side. So your saying hasha li-Zaid min hada means stay away from him. Abu Ali said: It is from muhasha. It was said that hasha is a letter, and hasha is a verb. The grammarians’ discourse on this word is well-known, and its meaning here is sanctification, as you say, The people grieved, except Zaid. So the meaning of hasha li-llah is innocence and sanctification of God. His saying: This is not a human being. The use of what is not the same as is is the language of the people of Hijaz, and the Qur’an was revealed in this verse, and in His saying, the Most High: They are not their mothers. As for Banu Tamim, they do not use it as is. The Kufians said: Its original form is this is not a human being, but when the ba was deleted, it was in the accusative case. Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha’lab said: If you say what Zayd is not in narration, then the place of the ba is in the accusative case, and so are all the letters of the genitive case. As for Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and the majority of grammarians, they applied it to the work of not, and the Basrans said the same, and the research is established in the books of grammar with its evidence and arguments. They only denied him humanity because he appeared in a form that had been clothed with a beauty so exquisite that no human being has ever known, and those who see have not seen anything close to it in all human forms. Then, when they denied him humanity for this reason, they established for him kingship, even though they do not know the angels, but it has been established in nature that they are in a form above the form of humans in essence and attributes, and that they are superior in everything, just as it has been established that the devils are the opposite of that. From this is the saying of the poet: I am not human, but an angel who descends from the sky and sings Al-Hasan read Ma hada bi-shara’a what this is for purchase with the ba’ being a preposition and the shin being broken: meaning, this is not a slave who is bought. This is a weak reading that does not fit what follows it in His statement: This is nothing but a noble angel. And know that what the women said does not necessarily mean that the angels are better-shaped than the sons of Adam, for they did not say it for any evidence, rather they judged the unseen based on the mere belief based on their natures, and that is forbidden, for God the Almighty says, Indeed, We created man in the best stature. The apparent meaning of this is that there was nothing like him among the types of creation in the beauty of his stature and perfection of his form. So what the author of Al-Kashshaf said in this regard is from the bulk of his fanaticism due to the statements of the Mu’tazila that were firmly rooted in his mind. Moreover, this issue, I mean the issue of the preference between angels and humans, is not one of the issues of religion in any context or context. How much more needy are the servants of God from it and how much more in need of other issues of obligation.
12:32: 32- She said, 'That is what you blamed me for.' The reference is to Joseph, and the address is to the women: that is, you reproached me for it. She said this to them when she saw their infatuation with Joseph, to show her excuse for herself. The meaning of in it is: in her love for him. It was said that the reference is to love, and the pronoun also refers to it. The meaning is: That love for which you blamed me is that love, and the first is more appropriate. Ibn Jarir preferred it. The origin of blame: describing him as ugly, then when she showed her excuse to the women for what she saw of what they fell into when he appeared to them, her chest became tight to conceal what she found in her heart of love for him, so she admitted that and declared what happened from her of soliciting him, so she said, And I did indeed seek to solicit him for himself, but he refused, meaning he refused and refrained from what I wanted, seeking to protect himself from that, then she threatened him if he did not do what she wanted, revealing the veil of modesty and tearing off the veil of chastity, so she said, And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be among the humiliated, meaning if he does not do what I commanded him to do in what was mentioned above when the doors were closed and she said, Come to you, he will surely be imprisoned, meaning he will be detained in prison and will be among the humiliated and degraded because of the humiliation he will receive, and he will be stripped of the blessing and honor, in her opinion. It was read yakunna with emphasis and with emphasis. It was said that emphasis is more appropriate because the letter nun was written in the Qur’an as an alif according to the rule of stopping, and that does not happen except in Light, but as for he will be imprisoned, it is heavy and nothing else. When Joseph heard her words, and knew that they were firm on her part, along with what he knew of the validity of her words with her dear husband, he said, supplicating to his Lord, glory be to Him.
12:33: 33- Lord of the prison meaning, O Lord of the prison that this woman has promised me, is more beloved to me than what they invite me to of supporting her and falling into the great sin that takes away the good of this world and the next. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning entering the prison, so the noun was omitted. Abu Hatim narrated that Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, read the word sijn with the opening of the seen, and Ibn Abi Ishaq, Abd al-Rahman, al-A’raj, and Ya’qub read it likewise. It is the source of his imprisonment, and the attribution of the call to them all, because the women encouraged him to obey her and frightened him from disobeying her. Then he proceeded on this in attributing the plot to them all, so he said: And if not, turn away their plot from me. As for the plot of the wife of al-Aziz, it is what God Almighty has narrated in this surah. As for the plot of the rest of the women, it is what was mentioned previously of encouraging him to obey and frightening him from disobeying. It was said that each one of them would be alone with him and say to him: O Joseph, fulfill my need for me, for I am better for you than the wife of al-Aziz. It was said that he addressed the wife of al-Aziz in a manner appropriate for addressing a group of women, out of respect for her, or to move away from explicitness to compensation. Al-Kidd means deception, and he made asb ilaihin definite as the answer to the condition: that is, he hoped for them, from saba yasbu: if he inclines and longs. And from it the poet said: To Hind my heart yearns and to Hind my love yearns And I am among the ignorant is in apposition to I am wronged: meaning I am among those who are ignorant of what is forbidden to commit and proceed with it, or among those who do the work of the ignorant.
12:34: And his saying 34- So his Lord responded to him when he said: Otherwise, turn away their plot from me, that was from him exposing the supplication, and it was as if he said: O God, turn away their plot from me, so the response from God Almighty to him is in this regard, because no sincere supplication came before from him, peace be upon him, and the meaning is: He was kind to him and protected him from falling into sin, because if He turned away their plot from him, nothing of what they had intended from him would have happened, and the reason for attributing the plot has been presented, and the phrase Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing is an explanation for what came before it of turning away the women's plot from him: that is, He is the All-Hearing of the supplications of those who call upon Him: the All-Knowing of the conditions of those who seek refuge in Him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He overwhelmed her, he said: He overcame her. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority: He overwhelmed her, he said: The love of Joseph killed her. Shaghaf is a deadly love, and shaghaf is a love less than that, and the pericardium is the veil of the heart. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: He overwhelmed her, he said: He had seized her. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Then when she heard of their plot, he said: of their story. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sufyan: Then when she heard of their plot, he said: with their knowledge, and every plot in the Qur’an is an action. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in his statement: And I prepared for them a reclining place, he said: I prepared a place for them to sit, and it was their custom when they set the table to give each person a knife to eat with. Musaddad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him: The reclining place means the citron, and he used to read it lightly. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid: Reclining, he said: Food. Abu Ubaid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: It is the citron. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Al-Wazir bin Al-Kumait bin Zaid that he said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather that he said regarding His statement: So when they saw him, they glorified him, he said: Safe, and he recited: When the horses saw him from the high peak, they neighed and gushed out the gushing semen. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Samad Ibn Ali Ibn Abdullah Ibn Abbas, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when they saw him, they exalted him. He said: When Joseph came out to them, they were filled with joy. He mentioned the words of the poet whom we mentioned earlier: Women are more chaste than their husbands Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, They glorified him, he said: They magnified him, and cut their hands, he said: They cut them with a knife until they threw them away, and they said, ‘God forbid,’ he said: God forbid. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, This is none other than a noble angel, he said: They said, An angel from the angels, because of his beauty. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Munabbih, on the authority of his father, who said: Nineteen women died of grief from the women who cut their hands. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Joseph and his mother were given half of their beauty. Narrations have been reported from a group of the Salaf describing Joseph’s beauty and exaggerating that. In some of them, he was given half of his beauty, in others, a third of it, and in others, two-thirds of it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Fasta’sama means: he refused. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah, Fasta’sama means: he was defiant. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement, And if You do not avert their plot from me, he said: If it is not from You, the strong and powerful, then it will not be from me or with me. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated, I incline to them, he said: I follow them. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I obey them.
12:35: Meaning: 35- It appeared to them appeared to them, and the pronoun refers to Al-Aziz and his companions who were planning the matter with him and advising him. As for the subject of It appeared to them, Sibawayh said it is to imprison him: meaning it appeared to them that they should imprison him. Al-Mubarrad said: This is a mistake because the subject cannot be a sentence, but the subject is what it indicated, which is the source, as the poet said: It is right for the one whose father is Abu Musa to be guided by the One who set up the mountains. That is, by the truth of the truth, the subject was omitted because the verb indicated it. It was said that the omitted subject was saw: that is, an opinion appeared to them that they did not know before, and this subject was omitted [because it indicates] and they will imprison him for it, and the lam in and they will imprison him is the answer to an omitted oath based on the estimation of the saying: that is, it appeared to them after they saw the signs, saying and by God they will imprison him. It was read to imprison him with the doubled letter above the letter tha in address, either to Al-Aziz and those with him, or to him alone as a way of glorification. The verses were said to be the shirt, the testimony of the witness, and the cutting off of the hands. It was also said that they were the blessings that God opened upon them after Joseph reached them and did not find that in them, but rather his wife was the one who prevailed over his opinion, doing what suited her desires in Joseph, and implementing what she had previously threatened him with in her saying, And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be among the debased. It was said that the reason for the emergence of this opinion to them in Joseph's imprisonment was that they wanted to cover up the talk and conceal what had spread among the people about the story of Al-Aziz's wife with him. It was also said that Al-Aziz intended by his imprisonment to prevent him from his wife when he knew that she had become in a place of love for him and did not care with him about carrying herself with him in any way. The meaning of his saying until a time was for an unknown period, as most of the commentators said. It was also said that it was to stop what had spread in the city. Saeed bin Jubair said: Up to seven years, and it was said up to five, and it was said up to six months. The interpretation of time was discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah, and until means up to.
12:36: His saying: 36- And two young men entered the prison with him There is an omission in the speech that preceded it, and the meaning is: And it appeared to them after they saw the signs to imprison him for a time, so they imprisoned him, and two young men entered the prison with him, and with is for companionship, and young men is the dual of young man, and that indicates that they were his slaves, and it is possible that the young man is the name of the servant even if he was not a slave, and it has been said that one of them was the king's baker, and the other was his cupbearer, and they had put poison for the king when the people of Egypt guaranteed them money in return for that, then the cupbearer went back on that and said to the king: Do not eat the food, for it is poisoned, and the baker said: Do not drink, for the drink is poisoned, so the king said to the cupbearer: Drink, so he drank and it did not harm him, and he said to the baker: Eat, but he refused, so he tried the food on an animal and it died on the spot so he imprisoned them, and their entry into the prison was with the entry of Joseph, and it was said before him, and it was said after him. Ibn Jarir said: They asked Joseph about his knowledge, so he said: I interpret dreams. So they asked him about their dreams, as God Almighty narrated: “One of them said: I see myself pressing wine.” That is, I saw myself. The expression is in the present tense to conjure up the image. The meaning is: I see myself pressing grapes, so he called it by the name of what it leads to because it is the intended meaning of pressing. In Ibn Masoud’s reading, I press grapes. Al-Asma’i said: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told me that he met a Bedouin who had grapes with him, so he said to him: What do you have with you? He said: Wine. It was said that the meaning of I press wine.
