Any grape wine, so it is on the deletion of the complement, and the one who saw this vision is the cupbearer, and this sentence is resumed with the estimation of a question, as is the sentence that comes after it, which is And the other said, ‘Indeed, I saw myself carrying bread on my head,’ then he described this bread by saying, The birds eat from it, and the one who saw this vision is the baker. So they said to Joseph together after they told him their vision, Tell us its interpretation, meaning the interpretation of what we told you from the group of what was seen, or the interpretation of what was mentioned to you from our speech. It was said that each one of them said that to him after telling him his vision, so the pronoun refers to what each one of them saw. It was said that the pronoun in its interpretation is the subject of the demonstrative pronoun, and the estimation is the interpretation of that, Indeed, we see you among the doers of good, meaning among those who are good at expressing visions. Al-Farra’ said the same: The meaning of among the doers of good is among the scholars who have perfected knowledge. Ibn Ishaq said: He was one of those who did good to us, if you interpret that, or one of those who did good to the people of the prison, as it was narrated that he was like that.
12:37: And the sentence 37- He said, 'No food will come to you that you are provided with except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, and the meaning of that is that he knows something of the unseen, and that no food will come to them in prison except that he will inform them of its nature before it comes to them, and this is not from the answer to their question of the interpretation of what he narrated to him, rather he made it, peace be upon him, an introduction before his interpretation of their visions to show the high status of his knowledge, and that he is not one of the interpreters who interpret visions based on conjecture and guesswork, so it is like the saying of Jesus, peace be upon him, And I will inform you of what you will eat and Joseph, peace be upon him, only said this to her in order to obtain her submission to him in what he calls them to after that of belief in God and leaving disbelief, and the meaning of you will be provided with it: it will come to them from the king or something else, and the sentence is a description of the food, or God Almighty will provide for you, and the exception in his saying: Except that I will inform you of its interpretation is devoid of the most general conditions: that is, it will come to you, and he named it An interpretation by way of similarity, because the speech is about the interpretation of the vision, or the meaning: except that I inform you of what the speech leads to from the conformity of what he informed you with reality, and the reference in his saying: that is to the interpretation, and the address is to those who asked him about the interpretation of their vision from what my Lord taught me with what He revealed to me and what I cared about, not from the type of divination and astrology and the like in which mistakes are common, then he explained to them that what he attained of this high rank and general knowledge is because of leaving the religion whose people do not believe in God or the Hereafter and following the religion of the prophets from his fathers, so he said: Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in God and it is a renewed statement that includes the reason for what came before it, and what is meant by leaving is not engaging in that from the beginning, not that he had engaged in it, then he left it as indicated by his saying: It was not for us to associate with God then he described these people with what indicates their stubbornness in disbelief and their devotion to it. He said, And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter, meaning that they are the only ones who are excluded from that, due to their extreme disbelief in God.
12:38: And his saying: 38- And I followed is in apposition to I left, and he called them all fathers because grandfathers are fathers, and he mentioned the highest grandfather, then the closest skin, then the father, because Abraham was the origin of this religion that his children were upon, then Isaac received it from him, then Jacob, and this is from him, peace be upon him, to encourage his two companions to believe in God It was not for us to associate with God meaning it was not right for us to do that, let alone happen, and the pronoun in for us refers to him and to the mentioned prophets, and the reference in his saying: That is to the faith understood from his saying it was not for us to associate with God, and from the grace of God upon us is the report of the demonstrative pronoun: meaning arising from God's graces upon us and His kindness to us in what He made for us of prophethood that includes infallibility from His sins, and from God's grace upon all people by sending prophets to them and guiding them to their Lord and clarifying the paths of truth to them But most people do not thank God, glory be to Him, for His blessings that He bestowed upon them They believe in Him, worship Him alone, and do what He has prescribed for them.
12:39: His statement: 39- O my two companions of prison, are separate lords better or God, the One, the Prevailing? He made them companions of prison due to the length of their stay in it. It was said that what is meant is: O my two companions in prison, because prison is not a companion but rather one is accompanied in it, and that this is from the category of O thief of the night. According to the first, it is from the category of his statement: The companions of Paradise are the companions of the Fire. The question is for denial with rebuke and rebuke, and the meaning of separation here is separation in essences, attributes, and number: that is, are the lords who are separate in their essences, differ in their attributes, and conflict in their number better for you, O my two companions of prison, or God who is truly worshipped, unique in his essence and attributes, who has no opposite, peer, or partner, the Prevailing One whom no one can overcome and no one can oppose? Joseph, peace be upon him, presented this compelling argument to the two prison guards in the form of a question, because they were among those who worshipped idols, and it was said that they had idols in their hands that they worshipped when he addressed them with this speech.
12:40: And for this reason He said to them 40- "What you worship besides Him are only names you have named" meaning, except empty names that you have named and have no names, even if you claim that they have names, and they are the gods that you worship, but since they do not deserve to be named with that, the names became as if they have no names, and it was said that the meaning is: What you worship besides God are only names, names that you and your fathers have named of your own accord, and they have nothing of divinity except mere names because they are inanimate objects that do not hear, nor are patient, nor do they benefit or harm, and He only said: "What you worship in addressing the plural and so are what follows it from the pronouns, because He intended to address the two companions of the prison and whoever was on their religion, and the second object of you have named them" is omitted: meaning, you have named them gods from yourselves "God has not sent down for them meaning with that name any authority of proof indicating its validity The judgment is only for God" meaning, the judgment is only for God in worship, for He is the One who created you and created These idols that you have made into worship without any proof or evidence, and the phrase He has commanded you to worship none but Him is a new sentence, and the meaning is that He has commanded you to single Him out for worship, without any other of what you claim is worshipped. Then He explained to them that worshipping Him alone, without any other, is the religion of God, and there is no other religion besides Him. He said: That meaning singling Him out for worship, is the upright religion meaning the straight and steadfast but most people do not know that this is His upright religion and His straight path, due to your ignorance and distance from the truth. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs, so he said: No one asked me about it before you. Among the signs are the cut of the shirt and its mark on his body, and the mark of the knife, and the wife of Al-Aziz said: If you do not imprison him, the people will believe him. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd who said: Among the signs is the speech of a child. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: The signs are their hands and the cut of the shirt. And I say: If what is meant by the verses are the verses indicating his innocence, then it is not correct to count the cutting off of the women’s hands among them, because that happened to them because of the astonishment they felt when he appeared to them, with the beauty that God Almighty clothed him with, which, when seen, breaks the bonds of patience and weakens the powers of endurance. And if what is meant by the verses is that he was given beauty that takes away the minds of the sighted and takes away the perception of the onlookers, then yes, it is correct to count the cutting off of the hands among the verses, but these verses are not what is meant here. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Hakim narrated - and he authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Joseph was punished three times: The first time was by imprisonment because of his fever, the second time because of his saying: Mention me to your Lord “So he remained in prison for several years” he was punished by a long imprisonment, and the third time when he said: O caravan, indeed you are thieves and he faced him If he steals, a brother of his stole before. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And two young men entered the prison with him, one of them said the king’s keeper of his food, and the other his driver of his drink. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Indeed, I see myself pressing wine he said: grapes. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid Inform us of its interpretation he said: its wording. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Indeed, We see you among the doers of good. He said: His goodness, as we have been told, was that he used to console their sad ones and treat their sick ones, and they saw his worship and diligence and loved him. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Sheikh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: His goodness was that if someone in prison was sick, he would take care of him. If the place was too small for him, he would make room for him, and if he needed help, he would gather for him. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Yusuf supplicated for the people of the prison and said: O God, do not let the report be widespread to them and make the bitterness of the days easy for them. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: No food will come to you verse, he said: He disliked the expression to them, so he answered them with something other than their answer, to show them that he had knowledge. When the king wanted to kill someone, he would give him a specific food and send it to him. Joseph said: No food will come to you that you will be provided with verse, to his statement: give thanks. The two companions of the vision did not call him until he interpreted the vision for them. He disliked the expression, so he said: O companions of the prison, are they separate lords? verse, to his statement: But most people do not know? verse, he said: So he did not call him, so he interpreted the vision for them. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: That is from the grace of God upon us and upon mankind, he said: The believer is grateful for the blessings of God upon him, and is grateful for the blessings of God upon people. It was mentioned to us that Abu Al-Darda’ used to say: O Lord, one who is grateful for a blessing, but is not unaware of it, and O Lord, one who bears knowledge but is not knowledgeable. Ibn Jarir and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Or are they separate lords? the verse, he said: When Joseph knew that one of them would be killed, he called them to their share from their Lord and to their portion of their afterlife. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: That is the right religion, he said: Justice.
12:41: He said: This is the explanation of what they asked him to interpret their visions, and what is meant by his saying: As for one of you is the cupbearer, but he left it ambiguous because it is understood or because he disliked stating to the baker that he is the one who will be crucified and he will give his lord wine to drink meaning his owner, and it is his responsibility that he was carrying out in the service of the king, so it is as if he said: As for you, cupbearer, you will return to what you were and the king will call for you and release you from prison and as for the other meaning the baker he will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head expressing what he saw that he was carrying bread on his head and the birds were eating from it the matter about which you are asking for a fatwa has been decided which is what they saw and narrated to him, it is said that he asked him for a fatwa: if he asked him for an explanation of the ruling on something he asked him about that which was unclear to him, and they had asked him for an interpretation of what was unclear to them in the vision.
12:42: 42- And he said to the one he thought would be saved from the two of them meaning he said Joseph, and the one who thought was also Joseph, and what is meant by thought is knowledge because he knew from the vision that the drinker would be saved and the baker would perish, this is what the majority of commentators said. And it was said that the apparent meaning is based on it, because the one who sees the vision only thinks a thought, and the first is more appropriate and more appropriate to the state of the prophets. Especially since he informed about himself, peace be upon him, that God had informed him of everything from the knowledge of the unseen, as in his saying: No food will come to you that you will be provided with verse, and the phrase mention me to your Lord is the statement of the statement that ordered him to mention him to his master and describe him with what he saw from him of the quality of expression and knowledge of something from the knowledge of the unseen, and this statement from him, peace be upon him, was issued from fear and forgetfulness of mentioning God because of Satan, so the pronoun of the object in made him forget refers to Joseph, as some of the commentators said, and what is meant by his Lord in his saying: mentioned his Lord is God Almighty: meaning Satan made Joseph forget to mention God Almighty in that situation and he said to the one whom he thought would be saved from them mentioning him to his master so that this would be a reason for him to pay attention to what he had inflicted of clear injustice upon him by imprisoning him after he had seen signs that indicated his innocence. Many commentators have said that the one whom Satan made forget to mention his Lord is the one who was saved from the two boys: Al-Sharabi. The meaning is: Satan made Al-Sharabi forget to mention his master: that is, he mentioned him to his master, so he did not convey to him what Joseph had commanded him to do, despite mentioning him to his master. The meaning is: Satan made him forget to mention what Joseph had ordered him to do, despite his release from prison and his return to what he had been doing, providing water to the king. This has been supported by the fact that Satan has no power over the prophets. It has been answered that forgetfulness occurred from Joseph, and its attribution to Satan is a metaphor, and the prophets are not infallible from forgetting except in what they tell about God Almighty. It has been authenticated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I am only a human being like you, I forget as you forget, so if I forget, remind me. It has also been supported by the fact that forgetting is not a sin. If the one whom Satan made forget to mention his Lord was Joseph, he would not have deserved punishment for that by remaining in prison for a few years. And I answer that forgetfulness here means abandonment, and that he was punished because he sought help from other than God, the Most High. And the return of the pronoun to Joseph is supported by what follows from His statement: So he remained in prison a few years. And the return of it to the one who escaped from the two boys is supported by His statement in what will come: And the one who escaped from them said and remembered after a year. “So he remained” meaning Joseph in prison because of that statement he said to the one who escaped from the two boys, or because of that forgetfulness a few years. A few: between three and nine as Al-Harawi narrated from the Arabs. And it was narrated from Abu Ubaidah that a few: less than half a decade, meaning between one and four, and it was said between three and seven, narrated by Qatrib. And Al-Zajjaj narrated that it was between three and five. And there is disagreement in specifying the amount of time that Joseph remained in prison. It was said seven years, and it was said twelve years, and it was said fourteen years, and it was said five years. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: As for one of you, he said: He came to him and said: I saw in a dream that I planted a rope of grapes and it grew, and clusters came out of it, so I squeezed them and gave them to the king to drink, and he said: You will remain in prison for three days, then you will be released and give him wine to drink. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: The two companions of Joseph did not see anything, they only dreamed to test his knowledge, so when he interpreted their dreams, they said: We were only playing and did not see anything, so he said: The matter about which you were asking has been decided, meaning: The interpretation occurred and the matter became as Joseph interpreted it. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abu Majlaz, who said: One of the two who told Joseph the dream was lying. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Sabat, And he said to the one of them whom he thought would be saved, ‘Remember me to your Lord,’ he said: To the King of the Earth. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in his book Al-Aqabat, Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If Joseph had not said the word that he said, he would not have remained in prison as long as he did seeking relief from other than God. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but it is mursal. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but it is mursal. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah who mentioned something similar, but it is also mursal. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdullah Ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id Az-Zuhd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Anas who said: It was revealed to Joseph: Who saved you from being killed when your brothers were about to kill you? He said: You, O Lord. He said: Who saved you from the well when they threw you in it? He said: You, O Lord. He said: Who saved you from the woman when she desired you? He said: You, O Lord. He said: Why did you forget me and remember a human being? He said: Out of impatience and a word that my tongue spoke. He said: By my glory, I will make you remain in prison for a number of years. So he remained in it for seven years. The predecessors differed in estimating the length of his stay in prison according to what we have mentioned previously, so we will not concern ourselves here with mentioning who said that and who released him.
12:43: What is meant by the king here is the greatest king, and he is Rayyan bin Al-Walid, for whom Al-Aziz was a minister. He saw in his sleep, when the relief of Joseph, peace be upon him, was approaching, that he came out of a dry river. 43- Seven fat cows is the plural of fat and fat, followed by seven lean ones: meaning emaciated ones, and the lean ones approached the fat ones and ate them. The meaning is: I saw, but he used the present tense to conjure up the image, and likewise his saying he eats them used the present tense to conjure up, and lean is the plural of lean, and the analogy of its plural is lean, because fa’la’ and af’al are not pluralized as fa’al, but he deviated from the analogy by considering it fat, and seven ears of corn is conjoined with seven cows, and what is meant by his saying green is that its grain has been gathered, and the dry ones are those that have reached the harvest, and the meaning is: And I see seven other dry ones, and he had seen that the seven dry ears of corn had reached the green ones and the fruits had ripened on them until they overcame them, and perhaps the failure to mention this in the Qur’anic system is to suffice with what was mentioned about the state of the cows, O assembly is an address to the nobles of his people, advise me about my vision that is, inform me of the ruling on this vision, if you interpret visions that is, you know the meaning of the vision, and the origin of the expression is derived from crossing the river, so the meaning of crossing the river is: I reached its shore, so the interpreter of the vision tells what its matter will lead to. Al-Zajjaj said: The lam in al-ru’ya is for clarification: that is, if you interpret, then he clarified and said al-ru’ya and it was said that it is for emphasis, and the delay of the verb working in it is to take care of the pauses.
12:44: And the sentence 44 - They said, 'Confused dreams' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, and confusion is the plural of 'daghth', which is everything mixed from herbs or grass or other things, and the meaning is: mixtures of dreams is the plural of dream: which is the false vision that has no truth to it, as it is from self-talk and the whisperings of Satan, and the addition means from, and they collected the dreams and the king had only one vision, exaggerating in describing it as false, and it is possible that he saw with this vision something else that God did not tell us about, And we are not knowledgeable about the interpretation of dreams Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the interpretation of mixed dreams is that they denied from themselves the knowledge of what has no interpretation, not absolute knowledge of interpretation, and it was said that they denied from themselves the knowledge of interpretation absolutely and did not claim that there is no interpretation for this vision, and it was said that they intended to erase it from the king's chest so that he would not be preoccupied with it, and what they mentioned about denying knowledge was not true.
12:45: 45- And the one who was saved from them said meaning the two boys, and he was the cupbearer to whom Joseph said Remember me to your Lord, And remember after a time with the silent dāl according to the reading of the majority, which is the eloquent reading: meaning the cupbearer remembered Joseph and what he saw from him of knowledge of the interpretation of dreams. It was read with the voiced letter, and the meaning of after a time: after a while, and from it to a numbered nation meaning to a time. Ibn Durastawayh said: And the nation does not come in the form of a time except by deleting a noun and placing the noun to which it is added in its place, as if he said: By God, and remember after a while a nation or after a time a nation. And the nation: is a large group of people. Al-Akhfash said: It is one in wording and plural in meaning.. and every kind of animal is a nation. Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah read after a nation with the opening of the hamza and the lightening of the m: meaning after forgetting, and from it the saying of the poet: I lived and I never forgot a conversation, that's how time destroys minds It is said, his mother, his mother: if he forgot. Al-Ashhab Al-Uqaili read after a nation with a kasra on the hamza: meaning after a blessing: which is the blessing of salvation. I will inform you of its interpretation. That is, I will inform you of it by asking someone who has knowledge of its interpretation, and he is Joseph. Then send. He addressed the king with words of glorification, or he addressed him and those of the nobles who were with him, asking them to send him to Joseph to tell him the king’s dream so that he could tell him its interpretation and he would return with that to the king.
12:46: 46- Joseph, O friend, give us your evidence meaning, O Joseph, and there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So they sent him to Joseph, so he went to him, and Joseph said to him, O friend, until the end of the speech, and the meaning is: Tell us about the vision of someone who saw seven cows, etc. and he left that, being satisfied with what he was confident of from Joseph's understanding that it was a vision, and that what was required of him was its interpretation so that I may return to the people meaning to the king and those with him from the leaders so that they may know what you bring of the interpretation of this vision or they may know your virtue and your knowledge of the art of interpretation.
12:47: And sentence 47 - He said you plant etc. is a resumption of the answer to an implied question like others that come in this context seven years of perseverance meaning successive and consecutive, and it is a source, and it was said that it is a state: meaning persistent, and it was said that it is an attribute of seven: meaning persistent, and Abu Hatim narrated from Yaqub that he read perseverance with a vowel on the hamza, and Hafs narrated likewise from Asim and they are two dialects. Al-Farra' said: It was moved because it contains a letter from the throat letters, and likewise every letter whose first letter is opened and whose second is still, its emphasis is permissible in well-known words. So Joseph, peace be upon him, interpreted the seven fat cows as seven years of fertility, and the seven lean cows as seven years of drought. And thus he interpreted the seven green ears of corn and the seven dry ears of corn. He used the seven green ears of corn as evidence for what he mentioned in the interpretation of his statement, So whatever you harvest, leave it in its ear, meaning whatever you harvest in each of the fertile years, leave that harvest in its ear and do not separate it from it lest the weevil eat it, except a little of what you eat in these fertile years, for you must separate it from its ear and take it out of it. And he limited himself to excluding what is edible, not what they need of the seed that they sow in their wealth, because it is known from his statement, you plant.
12:48: 48- Then there will come after that meaning after the seven fertile years seven difficult years meaning seven barren years that are difficult for people they will eat what you have put away for them of those grains left in their ears. And the extension of eating to the years is a metaphor, and the meaning is: people will eat in them or their families will eat what you have put away for them: meaning what you have saved for them, so it is from the same principle: his day is fasting, and from this is the saying of the poet: Your day, you arrogant one, is full of negligence and heedlessness, your night is full of sleep, and destruction is inevitable for you. Except a little of what you preserve meaning what you consider to be grain to plant, because preserving the seed preserves the provisions. Abu Ubaidah said: The meaning of preserve is protect, and it was said that you store, and the meaning is the same.
12:49: And his saying: 49- Then there will come after that a year in which people will be given relief and in which they will press meaning after the years of famine, so the reference is to it, and the year is the year in which people will be given relief from relief or relief, and rain is the rain, and the rain has poured down on the earth: meaning it hit it, and God has poured down His rain on the country, raining on it, so the meaning of people will be given relief is that they will be given rain and in which they will press meaning they will press the things that are pressed such as grapes, sesame, and olives. It was said that he meant milking milk, and it was said that the meaning of they will press is that they will be saved. It is taken from the press which is the escape. Abu Ubaidah said: and the press with the movement is the refuge and the escape, and from it the saying of the poet: Sadiq, crying for help, but no one helped him. He was the one who was helped. And I took refuge with someone: I sought refuge with him. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read ya’siroon with the second person pronoun ta’. And it was read ya’siroon with the damma of the present tense letter and the fatha of the sad, and its meaning is they rain, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: And We sent down from the pressed clouds abundant water. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Joseph said to the cupbearer: Mention me to your Lord, meaning the Great King, and my injustice and my imprisonment for no reason. He said: I will do so. When the cupbearer went out, he returned to what he was doing and his companion was pleased with him, and Satan made him forget to mention the king whom Joseph had ordered him to mention to him. Joseph remained in prison for several years after that. Then King Rayyan bin Al-Walid saw the dream in which he had been shown, and it terrified him and he knew that it was a dream that would come true, but he did not know what its interpretation was. He said to the leaders around him from the people of his kingdom: Indeed, I have seen seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of corn and others dry. When he heard from the king what he heard from him and asked him about its interpretation, Joseph mentioned what he had interpreted for him and his companion and what had come of it as he had said, so he said: I will inform you of its interpretation. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: confused dreams, he said: ambiguous. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And remember after a time, he said: After a while. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid, al-Hasan, Hikrimah, Abdullah ibn Kathir and al-Suddi. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: After years. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Give us your judgment about seven cows, the verse, he said: As for the fat ones, they are years of abundance, and as for the lean ones, they are years of barrenness, and seven green ears of corn are the fertile years when the earth produces its vegetation, crops and fruits, and the last are dry and barren years that do not grow anything. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I was amazed by Joseph and his generosity and patience, and may God forgive him, when he was asked about the lean and fat cows. If I were in his place, I would not have told them until he stipulated that they send me out. I was amazed by Joseph and his patience and generosity, and may God forgive him, when the messenger came to him. If I were in his place, I would have rushed them to the door, but he wanted to have an excuse.” And Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Except a little of what you store, meaning: you store. And regarding his statement: And therein they press, meaning: grapes and oil. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Therein people are given rain, meaning: they are afflicted with rain, And therein they press, meaning: they press grapes and raisins and all kinds of fruits. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh also narrated on his authority: And in it they press, he said: They extract. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh also narrated on his authority: Then there will come after that a year, he said: He told them something they had not asked him about, as if God had taught it to him, in which people will be given rain, in which they will press sesame oil, grape wine and olive oil.
12:50: His saying: 50- And the king said, 'Bring him to me.' In the speech, there is an omission before this, and the meaning is: So the messenger went to the king and informed him of what Joseph had informed him of regarding the interpretation of that vision, and the king said to those in his presence, 'Bring him to me.' That is, Joseph, he desired to see him and know his condition after he learned of his virtue what he learned from the description of the messenger of him and his interpretation of his vision. So when the messenger came to him, that is, he came to Joseph, and summoned him to the presence of the king and ordered him to leave prison, Joseph said, to the messenger, Return to your Lord, that is, your master, and ask Him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands." He ordered him to ask the king about that and he stopped leaving prison, and he did not hasten to answer the king, to show the people his innocence and honesty, and that he was clearly wronged by the plot of the wife of the Aziz. And he, peace be upon him, was given from forbearance, patience, and composure what minds are unable to imagine, and for this reason it is proven in the authentic hadith of his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: And peace be upon him: And if I had remained in prison as long as Joseph, I would have responded to the caller, meaning the messenger who came to call him to the kingdom. Ibn Atiyyah said: This action of Joseph was patience and forbearance, and a desire to clear his name, because he feared that he would go out and attain a position of kingship, and he would remain silent about his sin, and people would see him with that eye and say, This is the one who sought the seduce of the wife of the Aziz. Rather, he said: Ask him what is the matter with the women, and he remained silent about the wife of the Aziz out of respect for the honor of the Aziz king, or out of fear of her treachery and the greatness of her evil. He mentioned the question about cutting off the hands but did not mention their seduce him, out of his abstinence from attributing that to them. Therefore, he did not attribute the seduce in what preceded to the wife of the Aziz except after she accused him of her illness and slipped away. Here, he was satisfied with the general indication by saying: Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their treachery, so he made the knowledge of God, the Most High, of what befell him of their treachery sufficient for him to state explicitly.
12:51: And the sentence 51- "He said, 'What was the matter with you when you sought to seduce Joseph for himself?'" is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did the king say after the messenger informed him of what Joseph said? The matter is the great matter that he has the right to address his companion in particular. The meaning is: What is the matter with you [if] you sought to seduce Joseph for himself? The meaning of the seduce has already been presented, and the seduce was only attributed to them because each one of them did that as presented, and among those included in the king's address was the wife of Al-Aziz, or he meant that it was attributed to them as a whole as it was from the wife of Al-Aziz, in order to avoid him being explicit about attributing it to her because she was the wife of his minister, who was Al-Aziz: So they answered him by saying, "They said, 'God forbid,' meaning God forbid, 'We know of no evil against him,' meaning any bad thing that could be attributed to him. Then the wife of Al-Aziz said,' absolving herself of his side and admitting to herself that she sought to seduce him, 'Now the truth has become clear,' meaning it has become apparent and evident. Its origin is Has, so it was said Hashas, just as it was said in Kabwa Kabkabwa, as Al-Zajjaj said. The origin of Has is the uprooting of something. It is said that he uprooted his hair, meaning he removed it. And from this is the saying of Abu Qais bin Al-Aslat: The egg has been cut off from my head, so I do not eat any sleep but restlessness. The meaning is that the truth was separated from falsehood by its appearance and clarification. And from it: Whoever reports something that is not true about me is a liar and an oppressor when the truth is revealed. It was said that it is derived from the word share, and the meaning is: the share of falsehood became apparent. Al-Khalil said: Its meaning is that the truth appeared after it had been hidden. Then she clarified that by saying, I tried to seduce him, and he did not seduce me at all. And he is among the truthful, in what he said, exonerating himself and attributing the seduce to her. By now, she meant the time when she said these words.
12:52: And his saying: 51- That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence. Most of the commentators went to that this is from the speech of Joseph, peace be upon him. Al-Farra' said: It is not far-fetched to connect the speech of one person to the speech of another if the evidence that turns each of them to what is appropriate for him indicates. And the reference to the incident that occurred from him, which is his confirmation and his delay: that is, I did that so that the Aziz may know that I did not betray him with his family in his absence, and the meaning is in his absence. And the preposition and the noun in the accusative case are in the place of the state: that is, while he was absent from me, or while I was absent from him. It was said that he said that while he was in prison after the messenger informed him of what the women said, and what the wife of the Aziz said, and it was said that he said that after he was with the king, and the first is more appropriate. The minority of the commentators said that this is from the words of the wife of Al-Aziz, and the meaning is: That statement that I said in exonerating him, and admitting to myself that I had tried to seduce him, so that Joseph would know that I did not betray him, and attribute to him what he did not do while he was absent from me, or while I was absent from him. And that God does not guide the plot of the traitors, meaning He does not establish it and make it right, or He does not guide them in their plot until they bring it about in a way that has an effect that is established and lasting. If it is from the words of Joseph, then it is an allusion to the wife of Al-Aziz, since she plotted against him and betrayed her husband, and an allusion to Al-Aziz, since he helped her to imprison him after he knew of his innocence and integrity.
12:53: 53- And I do not acquit myself. If it was from the words of Joseph, then it is a matter of humiliating the soul and not purifying it, even though he and others among the people knew that he was innocent and that was clear as the sun, and the woman who falsely accused him acknowledged it, and the women who cut off their hands declared him innocent. If it was from the words of the wife of the Aziz, then it is true, because she acknowledged the guilt and confessed to the solicitation and the slander against Joseph. It has been said that this is from the words of Al-Aziz, and it is very far-fetched. Its meaning is: I do not exonerate myself from having bad thoughts about Joseph, and from helping to imprison him after I knew of his innocence. Indeed, the soul is prone to evil. That is, this type of human soul is prone to evil because of its inclination toward desires, and its influence by nature, and the difficulty of subduing it and restraining it from that. Except for those upon whom my Lord has mercy. That is, except for those souls upon whom He has mercy, so He protected them from being prone to evil, or except for the time of my Lord’s mercy and His protection of them. It has been said that the exception is disconnected, and the meaning is: But the mercy of my Lord is what prevents them from being prone to evil. The phrase Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful is an explanation of what preceded it: that is, it is His nature to abundantly forgive and have mercy on His servants.
12:54: His saying: 54- And the king said, 'Bring him to me, that I may take him exclusively for myself.' The king is Rayyan bin Al-Walid, not Al-Aziz, as mentioned above. The meaning of take him exclusively for myself is: I will make him pure for me and no one else. Before that, he had been pure for Al-Aziz. Purification is seeking to purify something from the impurities of partnership. He said that because Joseph was precious, and it is the custom of kings to make personal things pure for them and no one else. So when he spoke to him is omitted in the speech, and its meaning is, So bring him to him. So when he spoke to him: meaning, when the king spoke to Joseph. It is possible that the meaning is: when Joseph spoke to the king. It was said that the first is more appropriate, because in the councils of kings, no one speaks except them at the beginning, without anyone who enters upon them. It was said that the second is more appropriate, because of the king’s saying, He said, ‘Indeed, you are today with us, established and trustworthy.’ This indicates that when Joseph spoke in the king’s position, he came up with something that endeared him to the king and brought him close to his heart, so he said this statement to him. The meaning of established is: of status and trustworthiness, such that he is able to do what he wants from the king and the king trusts him with what he learns of his affair, or with what he entrusts to him of that. It was said that when he reached the king, he sat him on his bed and said to him, I would like to hear from you the interpretation of my dream. So he interpreted it for him with the most complete statement and phrase. When the king heard that from him, he said to him, Indeed, you are today with us, established and trustworthy. So when Joseph heard that from him,
12:55: 55- He said, 'Appoint me over the storehouses of the land.' That is, appoint me over the land that he has entrusted to you, which is the land of Egypt, or appoint me over the treasuries of the land, which are the places where money is stored. Joseph, peace be upon him, asked him for this in order to spread justice and remove injustice, and to use it to call the people of Egypt to believe in God and abandon the worship of idols. This is evidence that it is permissible for someone who is confident in himself, if he enters into a matter of authority, to raise the beacon of truth and destroy whatever falsehood he can, and to ask for this for himself. It is permissible for him to describe himself with descriptions that encourage what he desires, and to motivate the kings who address him by giving him the reins of affairs and making them dependent on him. However, this permissibility is opposed by what was reported from our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the prohibition of seeking authority and the prevention of appointing someone who seeks it or is keen on it. The treasuries are the plural of treasury, and it is the name for the place where something is stored, and the guardian is the one who preserves the thing: that is, I am a guardian of what you have entrusted to me of preserving the money, I do not spend it in places other than its outlets, nor do I spend it in places other than its expenditures, Knowing of the existence of its collection and dispersion, its entrance and exit.
12:56: 56- And thus We established Joseph meaning, and like that amazing establishment, We established Joseph in the land: meaning, We gave him a place, and it is an expression of his complete power and the effectiveness of his command and prohibition until the kingdom began to issue from his opinion, and the people began to act according to his command and prohibition. He settles therein wherever he wills meaning, he descends from it wherever he wants and takes it as a residence, and it is an expression of his complete power as mentioned above, and it is as if he disposes of the land that he entrusted to the sultan of Egypt as a man disposes of his home. Ibn Kathir read it with the letter nun. He used this verse as evidence that it is permissible to take on work on behalf of an unjust, or even an infidel, sultan for someone who is confident in himself to do what is right. We have already discussed this in detail in the words of God Almighty: And do not incline toward those who do wrong. “We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will” of the servants, so We have mercy on him in this world by being kind to him and bestowing favors upon him, and in the Hereafter by admitting him into Paradise and saving him from Hell. And We do not waste the reward of the doers of good in their good deeds that God requires of them: that is, We do not waste their reward for them, and their recompense for them.
12:57: 57- And for the reward of the Hereafter meaning their reward in the Hereafter, and the reward was added to the Hereafter for the sake of simplicity, and their reward is the recompense with which God will reward them in it, and it is Paradise whose bliss does not run out and whose duration does not end is better for those who believe in God and were pious against falling into what He has forbidden them, and what is meant by them are the good and those mentioned above, and in it is a warning that the goodness that is considered is faith and piety. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: What is the matter with the women? He said: Yusuf wanted to excuse himself before he was released from prison. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on his authority that he said: When the wife of al-Aziz said: I sought to seduce him, Yusuf said: That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret. Gabriel nudged him and he said: Not even when I intended to do so? He said: And I do not acquit myself. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: The truth has become clear. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and al-Suddi something similar. Sa’id ibn Mansur and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Hakim ibn Juzam regarding his statement: That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret. Gabriel said to him: Not even when I untied my pants? He then said: And I do not acquit myself. Ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated in Futuh Misr, on the authority of al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “And the king said, ‘Bring him to me, that I may take him for myself. ’” He said: So the messenger came to him and said, Take off your prison clothes and wear new clothes and go to the king. The people of the prison called for him, and he was thirty years old at that time. When he came to him, he saw a young boy, and he said, Does this one know my vision, while the magicians and soothsayers do not? He seated him in front of him and said, Do not be afraid. He dressed him in a necklace of gold and silk clothes, and gave him a saddled and decorated beast like the king’s beast, and he beat the drum in Egypt: Joseph is the king’s successor. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The king said to Joseph, I like you to mix with me in everything except my family, and I am ashamed for you to eat with me. Joseph became angry and said, “I am more deserving of being ashamed. I am the son of Abraham, the friend of God, and I am the son of Isaac, the sacrifice of God, and I am the son of Jacob, the prophet of God.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Shaybah bin Naamah Ad-Dhabi regarding his statement: Put me in charge of the storehouses of the land meaning over all food. Indeed, I am a guardian of what was entrusted to me. Knowing of the years of famine. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: And thus We established Joseph in the land he said: We gave him control over it so that he could be wherever he wished in that world and do whatever he wished in it. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam that Joseph married the wife of Al-Aziz and found her to be a virgin, although her husband was impotent.
12:58: His saying: 58- And Joseph’s brothers came meaning they came to Egypt from the land of Canaan to buy provisions because of the famine that struck them. So they entered upon Joseph and he recognized them because he had left them as men but they did not recognize him because they had left him as a boy who was sold for dirhams in the hands of the caravan after they had taken him out of the well, and they entered upon him now while he was a man with the pomp of kingship and the splendor of leadership, and with him were servants and attendants. It was said that they did not recognize him because he was in that state in the form of the king of Egypt, and he wore his crown and was adorned with his collar. It was said that they were far from him so they did not recognize him, and other things were said.
12:59: 59- And when he had equipped them with their provisions what is meant here is that he gave them what they asked for of provisions and what they needed for their journey from the equipment that the traveler needs. It is said that he equipped the people with preparation: if he took care of their travel equipment. Al-Azhari said: All the readers open the jim, and the kasra is a good language. "He said: Bring me a brother of yours from your father." It was said: There must be a statement that results from his request for them to bring him a brother of theirs from their father. It was narrated that when he saw them and they spoke to him in Hebrew, he said to them: Who are you and what is your business, for I do not recognize you? They said: We are a people from the Levant who came to quarrel, and we have an old father, a friend of the prophets, whose name is Jacob. He said: How many are you? They said, Ten, and we were twelve. Then one of our brothers went into the wilderness and perished. He was the dearest of us to our father. After him, he lived with a younger brother of his who remained with him to entertain himself. Then he said to them, Bring me a brother of yours from your father, meaning his brother Benjamin, who was mentioned earlier. He was Joseph's brother from his father and mother. They promised him that, so he asked them to leave one of them as a hostage with him until they brought him the brother he had asked for. They drew lots and the lot fell on Simeon, so they left him with him. Then he said to them, Do you not see that I give full measure? That is, I complete it. He used the future tense, although he said this to them after they had been prepared to indicate that this was his constant habit. Then he told them what would increase their trust in him and their belief in his words, saying, And I am the best of those who give a place of refuge, meaning that I am the best of those who give a place of refuge to those who come to me, just as I did to you in terms of good hospitality and good accommodation. Al-Zajjaj said: Joseph said, And I am the best of those who give a place of refuge, because when he gave them a place of refuge, he treated them well.
12:60: Then he threatened them if they did not bring it to him, saying: 60- If you do not bring it to me, then you will have no measure with me, nor will you come near meaning I will not sell you anything after that, but as for now he has given them their measure, and the meaning of do not come near is: you will not enter my country, let alone that I treat you well. It was said that its meaning is: I will not house you with me as I housed you this time, and it did not mean that they will not come near his country, and come near is in the jussive mood, either because la is prohibitive or because it is negative, and it is conjoined to the place of the penalty and included in its ruling, as if he said: If you do not come to me, you will be forbidden and do not come near. So when they heard that from him, they promised him what he asked of them.
12:61: 61- So they said, 'We will surely seduce his father about him' meaning, we will demand it from him, and we will strive to do so as much as we are able. It was said that the meaning of seduce here is their deception of their father and their trickery of him until they take him away from him. And indeed, We will do so, not falling short in it. It was said that its meaning is: And indeed, We are able to do that, we will not suffer from it nor will we be arrogant about it.
12:62: 62- "And he said to his young men, 'Put their merchandise in their saddlebags.' The people of Medina, Abu Amr, and Asim, according to the narration of Shu'bah and Ibn Amir, read to his young men." This reading was chosen by Abu Hatim, Al-Nahhas, and others. The rest of the Kufians read "to his young men." This reading was chosen by Abu Ubaidah, and in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, it is like the last reading. Al-Nahhas said: To his young men is contrary to the vast majority, and the majority agreed upon is not abandoned due to this broken chain of transmission. Also, young men are more similar to fityan, because young men among the Arabs mean the smallest number, and ordering the few to put the merchandise in the saddlebags is more similar. The sentence is a resumption of the answer to a question, as if it was said: So what did Joseph say after they promised him that? So it was answered that he said to his young men. Al-Zajjaj said that young men and young men in this place are slaves. Al-Tha'labi said: They are two good languages like children and young men. What is meant by the merchandise here is what they brought from their country to buy food with, and it was sandals and leather. Joseph, peace be upon him, did that as a favor to them. It was said that he did that so that they would return to him again because he knew that they would not accept food except for a price, as Al-Farra’ said. It was also said that he did that so that they would use it to help them return to him to buy food. It was also said that he considered it ugly to take the price of the food from his father and brothers. Then Joseph, peace be upon him, explained what he was ordered to do with putting the merchandise in their saddlebags by saying: Perhaps they will recognize it when they return to their families. So he made the reason for putting the merchandise in the saddlebags their recognition of it when they return to their families, and that is because they do not know that the merchandise has been returned to them except when they empty the containers in which they put the food, and they do not empty them except upon reaching their families. Then he explained their recognition of the merchandise returned to them and placed in their saddlebags by saying: Perhaps they will return, because if they knew that and knew that they took the food without a price, and that what they paid in exchange for it had been returned to them, and he was favored. Those who reached it were encouraged to return to it, especially with the severe drought they were experiencing, the need for food, and the lack of it with them, as that was one of the greatest things that called them to return. Thus, it becomes clear that Joseph, peace be upon him, did not return the merchandise to them except for this purpose, which was their return to him. The explanation for a return cannot be complete without that. The plural of rafal is rafal, and what is meant here is what a man takes with him of furniture. Al-Wahidi said: Rahal is everything prepared for travel, such as a container for provisions, a mount for a camel, a seat, and a rein. What is meant here are the containers in which they put the food they buy. Ibn al-Anbari said: A container is called a rafal, and a house is called a rafal.
12:63: 63- So when they returned to their father, they said, 'O our father, we have been denied measure.' They meant by this what Joseph had said to them before: If you do not bring him to me, you will have no measure with me. That is, he would deny us measure in the future. This indicates that the choice was customary between them and him time and time again. Perhaps they said this to him before they opened their baggage and knew that their merchandise had been returned, as is indicated by his statement later: And when they opened their baggage, to the end. Then they mentioned to him what Joseph had ordered them to do, and they said: Then send our brother with us, meaning Benjamin. We will measure is the answer to the order: that is, we will measure because of his sending with us what we want of food. The people of the two sanctuaries, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Asim read we will measure with a nun. The rest of the Kufians read it with the lower ya’, and Abu Ubaid chose the first reading. He said: So that they will all be included in those who measure. He claimed that if it was with the ya’, it would be for the brother alone: meaning, our brother Benjamin measures. An-Nahhas objected to him, saying that attributing the measure to the brother does not contradict its being for everyone, and the meaning is: Benjamin measures for all of us. Al-Zajjaj said: “If you send him, we will measure, otherwise we will withhold the measure. “And indeed, we are his guardians,” meaning their brother Benjamin, from any harm or misfortune befalling him.
12:64: And the sentence 64 - He said, 'Shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother before?' is a new answer to an implied question as was mentioned previously in similar instances in many places, and the meaning is: He does not trust them with Benjamin except as he trusted them with his brother Joseph, and they said to him about Joseph, And indeed, We will guard him, as they said here, And indeed, We will guard him, then they betrayed him with Joseph, so if he trusted them with Benjamin, he feared that they would betray him with him as they betrayed him with Joseph. But God is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. Perhaps here there is an implication and the meaning is that Jacob put his trust in God and handed him over to them and said: So God is the best guardian. The people of Medina read Hafiz and it is in the accusative case as a distinguishing feature, and this is the reading of Abu Amr, Asim, and Ibn Amir. The rest of the Kufians read Hafiz and it is in the accusative case as a state. Al-Zajjaj said: “On the statement, meaning the distinction, and the meaning of the verse: that God’s preservation of him is better than their preservation of him, because when Jacob entrusted his preservation to God, the Most High, He preserved him and returned him to Him, and when he said about Joseph: “And I fear that the wolf will eat him,” what happened to him from the test happened.
12:65: 65- "And when they opened their baggage meaning the food containers or what is more general than that which is called baggage whether it contains food or other than food they found their merchandise returned to them meaning the merchandise that they carried to Egypt to buy with it, and its explanation has been presented, and the phrase they said, O our father is a new sentence as was presented what do we want" is an interrogative and the meaning is: what do we ask of this king after he did with us what he did of kindness by returning the merchandise and honoring us when we came to him, and providing what we wanted of [supplies], and the interrogative is for denial, and the phrase "this is our merchandise returned to us" confirms what the interrogative indicates of denial of requesting something even though it has been returned to them, and it was said that what in what should be is negative meaning what we want in the saying and what we exaggerate in what we described to you of the king's kindness to us and his honoring us, then they demonstrated what they encountered of exaggeration in describing the king by saying: "this Our merchandise has been returned to us. So whoever favors them by returning it is worthy of their praise, deserving of what they have described him with. The meaning of and we provide for our people is that we bring them the provisions, which is food, and the ma’ir is the one who brings the food. As-Salami read it with a damma on the nun, and it is connected to an implied meaning indicated by the context and the estimation: This is our merchandise that has been returned to us, so we will use it to help us return and provide for our people. And we will protect our brother Benjamin from what you fear for him. And we will increase because of his sending us a camel’s load, meaning an additional camel’s load over what we brought this time, because each man was measured with a camel’s load. The meaning of that is an easy measure is that increasing the camel’s load for our brother is easy for the king, and he is not prevented from increasing it for him because it is easy, he does not think it is great or bother us about it. It was said that the meaning is: That measure for us is small, we want to add to it a camel’s load for our brother. Az-Zajjaj chose the first. It was said that this was from Jacob’s words in response to what his sons said: And we will add a camel’s load, meaning that a camel’s load is something small and he would not risk the child for it, as he is weak.
12:66: Because Jacob's answer is 66- He said, 'I will not send him with you until you give me a pledge from God' meaning until you give me what I trust and rely on from God Almighty, which is swearing by Him, and the lam in to bring him to me is the answer to the oath, because the meaning of until you give me a pledge from God is: until you swear by God to bring him to me: meaning to return Benjamin to me, and the exception in his saying unless you are surrounded is from the most general of the general, because to bring him to me even if it is an affirmative statement, it is in the meaning of negation, so it is as if he said: You are not prevented from bringing him to me under any circumstances for any reason except for the reason of surrounding you, and surrounding is taken from the surrounding of the enemy, and whoever the enemy surrounds has been defeated or destroyed, so Jacob took a covenant from them that they would bring Benjamin to him unless they defeated him or perished while trying to save him, so that would be an excuse for you with me So when they gave him their pledge That is, give him what he asked of them in the oath. He said, God is a witness over what we say." That is, Jacob said: God is a witness over what we said of my trustworthy request from you and your giving me what I asked of you. He is the All-Knowing, All-Watching, and nothing is hidden from Him. He is the one who punishes whoever breaks his covenant and is wicked in his oath, or he is entrusted with carrying out what he testified to from us. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When Joseph's brothers entered upon him and he recognized them while they did not recognize him, he brought the king's cup from which he used to drink, put it on his hand and began to tap it and buzz. He said: This cup tells me something about you. Did you have a brother from your father called Joseph? His father loved him more than you, and you took him and threw him into the well and told your father that a wolf had eaten him, and you brought false blood on his shirt? He said: So some of them looked at each other and were amazed. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Wahib who said: When Joseph began to tap the cup and tell them, one of his brothers stood up and said: I ask you by God not to reveal our faults. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: "Bring me a brother of yours from your father" he said: He meant Binbamin, who was Joseph's brother from his father and mother. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: "And I am the best of hosts," he said: The best of those who host in Egypt. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: "For his young men, meaning his boys, Make their merchandise," meaning their papers. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: "We do not desire this, our merchandise has been returned to us," they say: We do not desire anything beyond this, "And we will be given an additional camel's load," meaning a camel's load. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, "And we will be given an additional camel's load," he said: A donkey's load. He said: It is a language. Abu Ubaid said: Mujahid meant that a donkey is called a camel in some languages. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: "Unless you are surrounded," he said: You will all perish. And regarding his statement: "So when they gave him their pledge," he said: Their covenant. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Unless you are surrounded, he said: Do not be overcome until you are unable to do so.
12:67: When the sons of Jacob prepared to go to Egypt, their father feared that the evil eye would strike them because they were obviously beautiful and had fine clothes, even though they were the sons of one man. So he forbade them from entering together through one gate because that would be a cause for the evil eye to strike them, and he ordered them to enter through separate gates. He did not stop at saying: 67- Do not enter through one gate instead of saying: And enter through separate gates because if they had entered through two gates, for example, they would have complied with the prohibition against entering through one gate. But since entering through two gates, for example, was a kind of gathering in which it was feared that the evil eye would strike them, he ordered them to enter through separate gates. It was said that Egypt had four gates. Some of the Mu'tazila, such as Abu Hashim and Al-Balkhi, denied that the evil eye has an effect, and said: It is not impossible that if the person who has the evil eye sees something and is impressed by it, it would be in his interest to be charged with it that God changes that thing so that the heart of the person charged with it would no longer be attached to it. This is not surprising from these two and their followers, as rejecting the evidence of the Qur’an and Sunnah based on mere rational exclusions has become their habit and practice. What prevents the evil eye from being afflicted by God’s decree for that? Authentic hadiths have been reported that the evil eye is real, and a group of people were afflicted by it during the era of the Prophethood, including the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. What is more astonishing than the denial of these people of what is stated in the texts of this Sharia is what some of them do to disparage those who act on the contrary evidence simply because of rational exclusion and exaggeration in expressions, such as al-Zamakhshari in his interpretation, for in many instances he does not stop at refuting the evidence of the Sharia with the exclusion that he claims on the mind until he adds to that impudence in expression in a way that leads those who fall short into false statements and false doctrines. In short, the statement of these people is refuted by the abundant evidence and the consensus of those who are respected from this nation, past and present, and by what is seen in existence, for how many people from this human species and other species of animals have perished because of this reason. Scholars have differed about someone who is known to have been afflicted by the evil eye. Some people said that he should be prevented from contacting people to avoid necessity by being imprisoned or otherwise confined to his home. It was said that he should be banished. The most distant of those who said that he should be killed, unless he did so intentionally and his affliction depended on his choice and intention and he did not do so, because if he was killed, he would be treated as a murderer. Then Jacob said to his sons, And I cannot avail you against God at all, meaning I cannot ward off harm from you nor can I bring you any benefit by this plan of mine, rather what God has decreed for you will inevitably happen. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn al-Anbari said: If it had been stated in God’s knowledge that the evil eye would destroy them even if they were together, then their dispersal would have been like their meeting. Others said: Jacob did not benefit them at all when they were afflicted with what afflicted them with their dispersion of the theft being attributed to them. Then Jacob stated that there is no wise person except God, the Most High, so he said: The judgment belongs only to God, not to anyone else, and no one shares it with Him in it, as in In Him I have relied in every incoming and outgoing, not in anyone else: meaning I relied and trusted, and in Him, not in anyone else, let the trustful put their trust, in general.
12:68: And his children enter it initially 68- And when they entered from where their father had commanded them meaning from entering from God meaning from his side from something of the things that God had decreed for them because caution does not prevent destiny, and the exception in his saying except for a need in Jacob's soul which he fulfilled is disconnected, and the meaning is: But there was a need in Jacob's soul, which is his compassion for them and his love for their safety which God fulfilled for them, and it was said that it occurred to Jacob that if the king saw them gathered together with what appeared in them of perfection of creation, especially courage, he would cause them to be envious and spiteful or fearful of them, so he ordered them to disperse for this reason. Al-Nahhas chose this and said: There is no meaning to the evil eye here. And in it is that if this was the reason, he would have ordered them to disperse and he would not have specified the prohibition of that with regard to gathering when entering from one gate, because this envy or fear would occur with their gathering inside the city as it would occur with their gathering when entering from one gate. It was said that the subject in Qadaha refers to the entrance, not to Jacob. The meaning is: The entrance did not avail them anything from God, but that entrance fulfilled a need in Jacob’s soul because it happened according to his will. And indeed, he was possessed of knowledge because of what We taught him. That is, Jacob was possessed of knowledge because God taught him what He revealed to him that caution does not avert fate, and that what God Almighty has decreed will inevitably happen. But most people do not know that as it should be. It was said that they do not know that caution is recommended even if it does not avail anything from fate, and the context supports this.
12:69: It was said that what is meant by most of the people are the polytheists 69- And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself meaning he took his brother Benjamin to himself. It was said that by placing every two in your home, so his brother remained alone, so he took him to himself and said, ‘Indeed, I am your brother’ Joseph, he said that to him secretly, without his brothers knowing about it, So do not be sad meaning do not grieve for what they used to do meaning your brothers from the past deeds that they did. It was said that he did not tell him that he was Joseph, but rather said to him: I am your brother in place of your brother Joseph, so do not grieve for what you used to receive from them of harshness out of envy and malice. It was said that he informed him of what he would plan with them by putting the water container in his bag, so he said I do not care. It was said that when Joseph told his brother Benjamin that he was his brother, he said: Do not return me to them, so he said I know the grief of our father Jacob, so if I keep you with me his grief will increase, so he came to Benjamin and Joseph said to him: You cannot be kept with me except by I attribute to you something that is not appropriate for you, so he said I do not care, so he put the saa in his saddlebag, which is what is meant by the water-trough, and its origin is the drinking-trough from which one drinks, it was made a saa to be measured, and it was said that the animals were watered with it and the grain was measured with it, and it was said that it was made of silver and it was said that it was made of gold, and other things were said. The explanation of the device and the saddlebag has been presented above. The meaning is that he put the water-trough, which is the saa, in his brother’s saddlebag, which is the container in which he puts the food he buys from Egypt.
12:70: 70- Then after that a crier called out meaning a crier called out saying: O caravan! Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is O owners of the caravan, and everything that is driven on from camels, donkeys and mules is a caravan, and it was said that it is a caravan of donkeys. Abu Ubaidah said: The caravan is the saddled camels that are ridden. Indeed, you are thieves, attributing the theft to them in its true form, because the crier was not aware of what Joseph had planned, and it was said that the meaning is: Your situation is like that of thieves, since the measure came to you without the king's consent.
12:71: 71- They said meaning the brothers of Joseph and they turned towards them meaning while they were turning towards the one who was called from among the king's companions What do you miss? meaning what did you lose? It is said that you lost something if you lost it due to loss or something similar, so it is as if they said what did you lose? And the future tense is to bring the image to mind.
12:72: 72- They said in their response We miss the king's cup. Yahya bin Ya'mar read sawagh with the voiced ghain. Abu Raja read sawa' with a damma on the sad and a sukoon on the waw followed by an 'ayn. Abu Siya' read it. Abu Ja'far read sa', and Abu Hurayrah read it the same way. The majority read sawa' with the sad and the 'ayn. Al-Zajjaj said: The sawa' is the sa' itself, and it is masculine and feminine, and it is the watering place, and from it the poet said: We drink wine by the cup openly And for whoever brings it, there is a camel-load. That is, they said: And for whoever brings the measure on his own behalf, there is a camel-load. The camel is the male camel, and in the language of some Arabs, it is the donkey. What is meant by the load here is what the camel carries of food. Then the crier said, And I am responsible for it. That is, for the camel-load that was given to whoever brought the measure before the vessels were searched. The guarantor is the guarantor. Perhaps the one who said, We have lost the king's measure, was the crier alone, because he is the one who said the truth.
12:73: 73- They said, 'By God, you have certainly known that we have not come to cause corruption on earth.' The ta' is a substitute for the waw of the oath according to the majority, and it was said that it is from the ba', and it was said that it is the origin of itself, and it is only used with this noble name without the rest of His names, glory be to Him, and it was rarely used with the Lord, and with the Most Gracious, and the discussion of this is completed in the science of grammar, and they made the thing sworn upon to be the knowledge of Joseph and his companions of the purity of their side and the cleanliness of their tail from being polluted by the filth of corruption on earth, the greatest of which is theft, because they had seen from them when they came to him the first time, and this time, of chastity and asceticism from what is less than theft by stages, from which it is inferred that there is firm knowledge that they are not among those who dare to commit this great type of corruption, even if there was nothing from that except their returning their goods that they found in their baggage. What is meant by the land here is the land of Egypt. Then they confirmed this sentence that they swore by God by saying, And we were not thieves, to further disavow what they had accused them of and to absolve themselves of this vile shortcoming and heinous vice.
12:74: 74- They said, 'What is his penalty, if you are liars?' This sentence is a new sentence, as was mentioned more than once in its counterparts. The speakers are the companions of Joseph, or the one calling out from them alone, as mentioned, and the pronoun in his penalty refers to the measure, with an omitted complement: that is, what is the penalty for stealing the measure according to you?
