Or the pronoun refers to the thief, that is, what is the penalty for the thief of the measure according to you, if you are liars in what you claim for yourselves of innocence from theft, and that is by finding the measure with you. So Joseph's brothers answered.
12:75: 70- They said, 'His punishment is whoever finds it in his saddlebag, so is his punishment' meaning the punishment for stealing the measure or the punishment for the thief of the measure, and his punishment is the subject, and the conditional sentence: which is whoever finds it in his saddlebag, so is his punishment is the predicate of the subject by making the apparent the place of the implied in it, and the original is his punishment is whoever finds it in his saddlebag, so the second pronoun refers to the subject, and the first to whoever, and it is permissible for the predicate of the subject to be whoever finds it in his saddlebag, and the estimate: the punishment for stealing the measure is taking whoever finds it in his saddlebag, and the sentence is it is his punishment to confirm and confirm the first sentence. Al-Zajjaj said: And his saying so is his punishment is an addition to the al-Sharh 94:meaning his punishment is taking the thief, so it is his punishment and nothing else. The commentators said: The punishment for a thief among the family of Jacob was to steal for a year, so they asked them about his punishment. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers, meaning, like that complete punishment, We recompense those who wrong others by stealing their belongings. This sentence confirms what came before it if it was from the words of Joseph’s brothers, and it is possible that it was from the words of Joseph’s companions: meaning, thus do We recompense the wrongdoers for theft. Then when they mentioned the punishment for the thief, they wanted to search their belongings until the matter was clear.
12:76: So Joseph began to do that 76- So he began with their vessels searching their vessels meaning the vessels of the ten brothers before his brother’s vessel meaning before he searched the vessel of his brother Benjamin to remove the accusation and remove the trick he had planned then he extracted it meaning the water cup or the measuring cup, because it is masculine and feminine Thus did We plan for Joseph meaning like that amazing plot We planned for Joseph: meaning We taught it to him and inspired him, and the beginning of the plot is striving for trickery and deception, and its end is throwing the deceived without realizing it into a hateful matter that there is no way to prevent, and it is carried with regard to God Almighty to the end not the beginning. Al-Qatibi said: The meaning of we planned is we planned. Ibn Al-Anbari said: We intended. The verse is evidence of the permissibility of achieving the correct goals through what is depicted as a trick and a scheme if it does not contradict an established law. He would not have taken his brother according to the king’s religion meaning Joseph would not have taken his brother Benjamin according to the king’s religion: meaning the king of Egypt, and according to his law that he followed. Rather, his religion and his judgment was to strike the thief and fine him double what he stole, without enslaving him for a year, as was the religion and law of Jacob. The result is that Joseph would not have been able to carry out Jacob’s judgment on his brother, despite it being contrary to the king’s religion and law, had it not been for what God plotted, planned, and willed for him until he found the way to it: which is what He made his brothers say: The punishment for a thief is slavery. So their saying this was by the will and planning of God, and it is the meaning of His statement: Except if God wills meaning except when He wills, permits, and desires it. This sentence: I mean he would not have taken his brother, etc., is an explanation of what God did of the plot against Joseph or an interpretation of it. We raise by degrees whom We will with various kinds of knowledge, information, gifts and honors, just as We raised the degree of Joseph with that. Above every possessor of knowledge of those whom God raised with knowledge is the All-Knowing of a higher rank than them and a higher degree, whose extent they cannot reach or ascend to. It was said that the meaning of this is that above all people of knowledge is the All-Knowing, and He is God, glory be to Him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And he said, O my sons, do not enter by one gate, he said: Jacob feared the evil eye for them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Ka’b who said: He feared the evil eye for them. Sa’id Ibn Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Nakha’i regarding his statement: And enter by different gates, he said: Jacob loved to meet his brother Joseph in seclusion. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Except for a need in Jacob’s soul which he fulfilled, he said: Fear of the evil eye for his sons. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And indeed, he was possessed of knowledge because of what We taught him, he said: He acts according to what he knows, and whoever does not act is not knowledgeable. And these narrated on his authority regarding his statement: He took his brother to himself, he said: He took him close to him. In His statement: So do not be sad, he said: Do not be sad or lose hope. In His statement: So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he said: He had fulfilled their need and measured out their food for them. In His statement: He placed the drinking vessel, he said: It is the king's vessel from which he drinks. In his brother's saddlebag, he said: In his brother's belongings. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: He placed the drinking vessel, he said: It is the measure, and everything from which one drinks is a measure. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: O caravan, he said: The caravan was donkeys. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding His statement: And for whoever brings it, a camel load, he said: A donkey loads food, and it is a language. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And I am its guarantor, meaning: I am a guarantor. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas regarding his statement: We did not come to cause corruption on the earth, meaning: We did not come to disobey on the earth. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: Then what is his recompense? He said: They knew the ruling in their ruling, so they said: Whoever is found in his saddlebag, then his recompense is his. The ruling among the prophets Jacob and his sons was that the thief should be taken for his theft as a slave who is enslaved. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: So he began with their vessels, he said: It was mentioned to us that whenever he opened a man’s belongings, he would seek forgiveness for what he had done, until the boy’s belongings remained. He said: I do not think that this one took anything. They said: Yes, so he made it clear. And Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Dahhak regarding his statement: Thus did We plan for Joseph, he said: Thus did We do for Joseph. It was not for him to seize his brother by the law of the king, he said: By the authority of the king. He said: It was by the law of their king that he had stolen, so the theft was taken from him and an equal amount from his money with it, so he would give him the stolen property. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: It was not for him to seize his brother by the law of the king, he said: By the authority of the king. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Except that God should will, he said: Except for a reason that God planned for Joseph, so he made it an excuse. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: We raise by degrees whom We will, he said: Joseph and his brothers were given knowledge, so We raised Joseph in knowledge above them by a degree. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr who said: We were with Ibn Abbas and he narrated a hadith, so a man who was with him said: And above every possessor of knowledge is one who is All-Knowing, so Ibn Abbas said: What a bad thing you said, God is the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, and He is above every scholar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b who said: A man asked Ali about a matter, so he answered it, so the man said: It is not like this, but such-and-such, so Ali said: You were right and wrong, And above every possessor of knowledge is one who is All-Knowing. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: And above every possessor of knowledge is one who is All-Knowing, he said: God’s knowledge is above every scholar.
12:77: His saying: 77- “They said, ‘If he steals’ meaning Benjamin, ‘a brother of his stole before’ meaning Joseph. The commentators differed about this theft that they attributed to Joseph. What was it? It was said that Joseph had an aunt who was older than Jacob, and she had Isaac's belt because she was the oldest of his children and they inherited it, so the eldest, male or female, would take it. She had taken Joseph in and loved him very much, and when he grew up, Jacob said to her: Give Joseph to me. She feared to be separated from him and plotted to keep him with her. She put the belt under his clothes and tied him with it. Then she said: Isaac's belt has been stolen, so see who stole it. They searched for it and found it with Joseph, so she took it with her, as was the law of the prophets at that time from the family of Abraham. Their law regarding theft was previously explained. It was said that Joseph took an idol that belonged to his maternal grandfather, broke it, and threw it on the road to change the evil. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Zajjaj that it was an idol made of gold. Al-Wahidi narrated on the authority of Al-Zajjaj that he said: God knows best, did his brother steal or not? Al-Qurtubi narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Al-Zajjaj that he said: They lied about him in what they attributed to him. I said: This is more appropriate, for this lie was not the first of their lies, and we have already presented what refutes the statement of those who said that they were prophets when these matters were issued by them. His saying: “So Joseph kept it to himself.” Al-Zajjaj and others said: The pronoun in He kept it to himself refers to the word or sentence, as if it was said that he kept the sentence to himself and did not reveal it to them, then he explained it by saying: He said, ‘You are the worst place.’ Abu Ali Al-Farisi rejected this and said: This type of concealment is not used on the condition of explanation. It was said that the pronoun refers to the answer, meaning that Joseph kept their answer to him at that time to another time. It was also said that he kept their saying to himself: If he steals, a brother of his stole before, and this is the first. The meaning of and did not reveal it to them is that he did not reveal to them this statement that he kept to himself by mentioning to them its truth or falsehood. The sentence He said, ‘You are the worst place,’ is explained according to the first statement and resumes according to the other two statements, as if it was said: So what did Joseph say when he said this statement? That is, you are the worst place, meaning a place and abode from those whom you accused of stealing, and he is innocent, for you have done what you did by throwing Joseph into the well and lying about your father and other things of your actions. Then he said: And God knows best what you describe of the falsehood of attributing theft to Joseph, and that there is no truth to that. Then they wanted to entreat him to release their brother Benjamin to be with them so that they could return him to their father, because of what had preceded from him taking a covenant from them to return him to him.
12:78: 78- They said, 'O noble one, indeed he has an old father.' That is, this Benjamin has a father who is described by this characteristic, which is that he is an old man whom he cannot be separated from, cannot bear to be away from, and cannot reach. So take one of us in his place. He will remain with you, for he has a position in his father's heart that no one else would be harmed by the separation from one of us as he is harmed by the separation from Benjamin. Then they explained that by saying, Indeed, we see you among the doers of good. To all people, and to us in particular, so complete your goodness to us by answering our request.
12:79: So Joseph answered them by saying: 79- God forbid that we should take except the one with whom we found our goods. That is, we seek refuge in God for a refuge. It is a verbal noun governed by an omitted verb, and the one seeking refuge in God is the one who holds fast to Him. And that we should take is governed by the removal of the preposition. The original meaning of that we should take except the one with whom we found our goods is Benjamin, because he was the one in whose saddlebag the measure was found. It was permissible for us to enslave him by your fatwa that you issued to us by saying: His recompense is whoever it is found in his saddlebag, so his recompense is his. "Indeed, then we would be wrongdoers. That is, if we took other than the one with whom we found our goods, then we would be wrongdoers in your religion and what your fatwa requires.
12:80: 80- So when they despaired of him meaning they despaired of Joseph and his assistance in their request that they asked for, and the seen and the ta are for emphasis, they separated in secret meaning they were alone while they were whispering to each other, and it is a source that applies to the singular and the plural as in His saying And We brought him near in secret. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that they were alone and their brother was not with them, whispering about what they were doing in their going to their father without their brother. Their eldest said, it was said that it was Reuben because he was the oldest, and it was said that it was Judah because he was the most intelligent, and it was said that it was Simeon because he was their leader. Did you not know that your father took a covenant from you from God? That is, a covenant from God to protect his son and return him to him, and the meaning of it being from God is that with His permission. And before that you neglected Joseph is conjoined with what came before it, and the estimate is: Did you not know that your father and you know your neglect of Joseph, this was mentioned by Al-Nahhas and others, and before is related to you learned: that is, and you know your neglect of Joseph before, on the basis that what is a source, and it is permissible for it to be redundant, and it was said that what you neglected is raised in place of the denial, and its predicate is before, and it was said that what is a relative or a description, and both are in the place of the accusative or the nominative, and what we mentioned is the first, and the meaning of you neglected: you fell short in his matter, and you did not keep your father’s covenant regarding him I will not leave the land. It is said, Baraha he left and Baruhan he departed, meaning he moved away. If the negation enters it, it becomes affirmative: meaning, I will not leave the land, but I will stick to it and will not cease to reside in it until my father gives me permission to leave it and go out of it. He only said that because he was ashamed of his father to come to him with someone other than his son, who had taken a pledge from them to return him to him unless they were surrounded, as mentioned above, or God judges for me to leave it and go out of it. It was said that the meaning is: or God judges for me victory over the one who took my brother, so I fight him and take my brother from him, or I become powerless and leave after that. And He is the best of judges because His judgments are only based on what is in accordance with the truth and what is correct.
12:81: Then their elder said, addressing them 81- Go back to your father and say, 'O our father, your son has stolen.' The majority of scholars read stolen as an active participle, because they had witnessed the extraction of the cup from its container. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and Abu Razin read it as a passive participle, and An-Nahhas narrated that from Al-Kisa'i. Az-Zajjaj said: stolen has two possible meanings: one is that the theft was known from him, and the other is that he was accused of theft. And we did not testify except to what we knew of the extraction of the cup from its container. It was said that the meaning is: We did not testify before Joseph that the thief would steal except by what we knew from your law and the law of your fathers. And we were not guardians of the unseen until it becomes clear to us whether the matter is as we witnessed or otherwise? It was said that the meaning is: We were not aware at the time we took him from you to go with us to Egypt, knowing that he would commit the theft that would disgrace us. It was said that the unseen is the night, and what they meant was that he stole while they were asleep. It was also said that what they meant was that he did that while he was absent from them.
12:82: So his action was hidden from him 82- And ask the town in which we were This is part of the statement of their elder to them: that is, say to your father, ask the town in which we were: that is, Egypt, and what is meant is its al-Nas 114:that is, ask the people of the town, and it was said that it is a town from the towns of Egypt where they settled and settled, and it was said that the meaning is: And ask the town itself even if it is inanimate, for you are the Prophet of God, and God Almighty will make it speak and it will answer you, and what supports this is that Sibawayh said: It is not permissible to speak to Hind while you mean Hind’s boy And the caravan in which we came That is, say to your father, ask the caravan in which we came: that is, its owners, and they were well-known people from the neighbors of Jacob And we are truthful in what we said, they came with this sentence confirming this confirmation because what had preceded from them with their father Jacob necessitates complete doubt in this report of theirs for the listener. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported on the authority of Mujahid in his statement: "If he steals, his brother has stolen He said: They mean Joseph. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: He stole a kohl container for his aunt, meaning Joseph. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Atiyyah who said: He stole two miles of gold in his youth. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Joseph stole an idol of his maternal grandfather, made of gold and silver, broke it and threw it on the road, and his brothers taunted him for that. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Saeed bin Jubair something similar, not with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. A group of the Tabi’un narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then Joseph kept it to himself, he said: He kept his statement to himself: You are in the worst position, and God knows best what you describe. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Qatadah. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Ishaq regarding his statement: So when they despaired of him, he said: They despaired of him and saw his severity in his matter. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: They were saved in secret, he said: They were alone. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Their eldest said, he said: Simeon, the eldest of them in intellect, and older than him in birth was Reuben. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada: Their eldest said, he is Reuben, and he is the one who forbade them from killing him and he was the eldest of the people. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Or God will judge for me, he said: I will fight with my sword until I am killed. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Salih. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah: And We were not guardians of the unseen, he said: We did not know that your son was stealing. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And ask the town, he said: They mean Egypt. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada.
12:83: His saying: 83- "He said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something,' meaning, they have made it seem good, and the matter here is their saying, 'Your son has stolen,' and he did not steal in reality. It was said that what was meant by the matter was their expulsion of Benjamin and their going with him to Egypt seeking benefit, but that resulted in harm. It was said that enticement is imagination, meaning, your souls have enticed you to do something that has no basis. It was said that the matter that their souls enticed their young men to do is that the thief will be taken for his theft. The interruption here is in consideration of what they have proven of their innocence, not in consideration of the origin of the statement, which is correct. The sentence is a new sentence built on an implied question like the others. The phrase so patience is beautiful is the predicate of an omitted subject or a subject whose predicate is omitted: that is, my affair is patience is beautiful, more beautiful for me and more appropriate for me. And beautiful patience is that in which its owner does not disclose his complaint, but rather entrusts his affair to God and seeks His forgiveness. It has been reported that patience at the beginning of the shock maybe God will bring them all to me meaning Joseph and his brother Benjamin, and the third brother who remained in Egypt, and he is their eldest as mentioned above. And he only said this because he knew that Joseph had not died, and that he remained alive even though his affair was hidden from him for He is the All-Knowing of my condition the All-Wise in what He decrees.
12:84: 84- And he turned away from them meaning he turned away from them and stopped talking to them and said, 'Oh, my sorrow over Joseph.' Al-Zajjaj said: The original was Oh, my sorrow, but the ya' was replaced with an alif because of the lightness of the fat-ha. Sorrow means intense grief, and it was said that it means intense sadness, and from this is the saying of Kathir: Oh, how sad for the heart, how it turned away, and for the soul, when it was consoled, it was consoled. Jacob said this statement when he was extremely sad because of his separation from Joseph, and his separation from his brother Benjamin, and he reached the point where he was a prisoner of the king of Egypt, so his sadness doubled, and the old anguish was stirred up in him by what the recent report had aroused. It was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair that Jacob did not have what is established in our Sharia of seeking forgiveness and patience in the face of calamities, and if he had that, he would not have said: Oh, grief over Joseph. The meaning of calling out in grief is a request for his presence, as if he said: Come, oh my grief, and come to me. And his eyes turned white from grief, meaning the blackness of his eyes turned white from much crying. It was said that his perception of sight was completely lost, and it was said that he had weak perception. It has been said that the reason for the great grief that Jacob, peace be upon him, suffered, which led to him losing his sight in whole or in part, was that he did so because he knew that Joseph was alive, so he feared for his religion, even though he was in Egypt and its people were infidels at that time. It has also been said that mere grief is not forbidden, but what is forbidden is that which leads to infatuation, tearing clothes, and speaking inappropriately. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said when his son Ibrahim died: The eyes weep, and the heart grieves, but we do not say what angers the Lord, and indeed, we are grieved for you, O Ibrahim. This is supported by his saying: So he is suppressed, meaning suppressed, for its meaning is that he is filled with grief, holding it back and not expressing it. From this comes the word kazum al-ghayth, which means concealing anger. So the suppressed is the one whose path to grief is blocked, from kazum al-siqā’, meaning to close it on what is in it. Kazum, with the opening of the Ḍād, means the outlet of the soul. It is said that he took hold of his udders, and it has been said that kazum means the one who suppresses, meaning the one who is overwhelmed by his grief and holds it back. From this comes: If I suppress the misfortune of people, then today my tongue is loose And from it is and those who restrain anger. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of kazeem is grieved. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Its meaning is sad and distressed. Some linguists said: Hazn with the damma and sukoon means crying, and with two fathahs: the opposite of joy.
12:85: Most linguists said: They are two languages with the same meaning 85- They said, 'By God, you will not cease to remember Joseph' meaning you will not cease, so the negative letter was deleted to avoid confusion. Al-Kisa'i said: Fata'at and Fata'at I do such-and-such meaning she did not stop, and Al-Farra' said: The 'in' la is implied meaning she will not cease. Al-Nahhas said: What he said is correct. It has been narrated from Al-Khalil and Sibawayh similar to what Al-Farra' said, and Al-Farra' recited as evidence for what he said: I said, By God, I will stay seated even if they cut off my head and limbs. It is said that Fata’ and Fata’ are two languages, and from this comes the saying of the poet: It did not stop until its dust was like a canopy on a windy day. Until you become a corpse. Al-Hardh is a verbal noun that is the same for singular and plural, masculine and feminine, and adjectives. Haradh with a kasra on the ra’ like danaf and danaf. The root of al-Hardh is corruption in the body or mind from sadness, love, or old age. This was narrated from Abu Ubaidah and others, and from it is the saying of the poet: My worries crept in and made me sick, and they made me sicker. Likewise, love before the day causes passion. It was said that al-Hardh is what is below death, and it was said that it is old age, and it was said that al-Hardh is the worn-out, circulating one. Al-Farra’ said: al-Hardh is the corrupt one in body and mind, and so is al-Hardh. Mu’raj said: It is the one who is melting from worry, and this is indicated by the poet’s saying: I am a man who is in love with you, so incite me until I am worn out and until illness heals me It is said that he is an inciting man, and from this the poet said: The horses wanted him for a whole day, and if they had trained him, he would have become an instigator. Al-Nahhas said: The linguists have said that worry made him sick, and a man who is a fool is a fool. Al-Akhfash said: Al-Harid is the one who goes. Ibn Al-Anbari said: He is the one who perishes. It is better to interpret Al-Harid here as meaning something other than death and perishing from these mentioned meanings so that his saying or you are among the perishing has a meaning other than the meaning of Al-Harid. So establishing is better than emphasizing, and the meaning of among the perishing is: among the dead, and their purpose is to prevent Jacob from crying and grieving out of pity for him even though they were the cause of his sorrows and the origin of his worries and griefs.
12:86: 86- He said, 'I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God.' This sentence is a new one, as if it was said, So what did Jacob say when they said to him what they said? And bath is what comes to a person from the things that greatly sadden its owner until he is unable to hide it, this is what the linguists said, and it is taken from baththahu meaning it separated him, so the calamity was called bath metaphorically. Dhu al-Rummah said: I stopped at a quarter of a mile, young man, and I kept crying and talking to him. I watered it until its stones and playgrounds almost spoke to me. The commentators have mentioned that if a person is able to conceal the calamities that have befallen him, then that is considered grief, and if he is not able to conceal it, then that is considered slander. So slander, according to this, is the greatest and most difficult grief. It has also been said that slander means worry, and it has also been said that it is need. According to this statement, the connection of grief to slander is clear in meaning. As for the interpretation of slander as great grief, then it is as if he said: I only complain of my great grief and what is less than that of grief to God, not to anyone else. It has been read as slander with a damma on the ha’ and a sukoon on the zay, and slander with a fatha on both of them. And I know from God what you do not know, meaning I know of His kindness, goodness, and reward for the calamity what you do not know. It has also been said that He meant His knowledge that Joseph is alive, and it has been said that He meant His knowledge that his dream is true, and it has been said that He knows of the response of those in need to God what you do not know.
12:87: 87- O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother. Finding out with neglected words: seeking something with the senses, taken from sense, or from feeling: meaning go and find out the report of Joseph and his brother and seek it, and it is read with a jim, and it is also seeking and do not despair of the mercy of God meaning do not lose hope in His relief and release. Al-Asma'i said: The spirit is what a person finds from the breeze of the air and finds peace in it, and the structure indicates movement and shaking, so everything that a person shakes with its existence and enjoys is the spirit. Al-Wahidi narrated from Al-Asma'i also that he said: The spirit is the rest from the heart's sorrow. Abu Omar said: The spirit is relief, and it was said that it means mercy Indeed, none despair of the mercy of God except the disbelieving people because they do not know the power of God, the glory of His creation and the hidden kindnesses.
12:88: His saying: 88- So when they entered upon him meaning upon Joseph, and there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So they went as their father ordered them to Egypt to find out about Joseph and his brother, and when they entered upon Joseph they said, O Mighty meaning the powerful and powerful king we and our family have been touched by hardship meaning hunger and need. And in it is evidence that it is permissible to complain in case of necessity if one fears that it will affect himself, just as it is permissible for the sick person to complain to the doctor about the illness he finds, and this time they entered Egypt was the third time as is indicated by what was mentioned previously from the context of the Noble Book and we brought mixed merchandise merchandise is a piece of money intended to buy something. It is said abda'at al-shay' and istabda'tuhu if you make it merchandise, and in the proverb like mustabda' al-tamar to Hajar. And izja' is the market by force. Al-Wahidi said: “Izja’ in the language means the market and paying little by little. From this comes the Almighty’s saying: ‘Have you not seen that God drives the clouds?’” The meaning is: It is a commodity that is paid and not accepted by merchants. Tha’lab said: The mixed commodity is the incomplete one. Abu Ubaidah said: The bad dirhams are called mazja’ah because they are returned, paid and not accepted. There was a difference of opinion about what this merchandise was. It was said that it was dried meat and hays, and it was said that it was wool and ghee, and it was said that it was green seeds and pine nuts, and it was said that it was bad dirhams, and it was said that it was sandals and leather. Then they asked him, after they informed him of the merchandise they had with them, to give them full measure: that is, to make it complete with no deficiency in it, and they asked him to give them charity either by adding to what he gave them in exchange for their merchandise, or by overlooking the poor quality of the merchandise they brought, and to make it like good merchandise in giving them full measure, and this is what most of the commentators said. It was said, how can they ask for charity for them when they are prophets and charity is forbidden for prophets? The answer is that this is specific to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Indeed, God rewards those who give charity with what He gives them of the reward in the afterlife, or by expanding it for them in this world. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Perhaps God will bring them all to me, he said: Yusuf, his brother and Rubil. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding the verse: Yusuf, his brother and their eldest who stayed behind. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Oh my grief for Joseph, he said: Oh sorrow. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada something similar. They narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Oh grief. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then he is suppressing his grief, he said: Sad. Ibn Al-Mubarak, Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shuyukh narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: He suppressed his grief and did not say anything but good. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani who said: A suppressing person is distressed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shuyukh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: Al-Kazim is grief. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shuyukh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: By God, you will not cease remembering Joseph he said: You will not cease remembering Joseph until you become ill he said: nearing sickness or you become among those who perish he said: the dead. And these people narrated something similar from Mujahid. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shuyukh narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement, You will not cease to remember Joseph, he said: You will not cease to remember Joseph, until you become infirm, he said: old, or are among those who perish, he said: Or you die. And Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shuyukh narrated from al-Dahhak, until you become infirm, he said: old, or are among those who perish, he said: Among the dead. And Ibn Jarir and Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Muslim ibn Yasar, tracing it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever persists in suffering cannot be patient, then he recited, I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God, and Ibn Mandah narrated in al-Ma’rifah from Muslim ibn Yasar from Ibn Mas’ud who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned it. And Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. And Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya’mar, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever persists in suffering cannot be patient, then he recited, I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God, and Ibn Mandah narrated in al-Ma’rifah from Muslim ibn Yasar from Ibn Mas’ud who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned it. And Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shuyukh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: I only complain of my distress, he said: My anxiety. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And I know from God that which you do not know, he said: I know that Joseph’s vision is true and that I will prostrate to him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, with merchandise, said: Dirhams. Mzja’ah, said: unsold. Abd al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on his authority that he said: Mzja’ah means worn-out merchandise, such as a rope, a knot, or something. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Sheikh also narrated on his authority that: Mzja’ah means counterfeit paper that is not spent until some of it is put away. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Jarir regarding his statement, and give us charity, that he said: Give us back our brother.
12:89: The question in His statement: 89- Did you know? is for rebuke and reprimand, and they were aware of that, but He intended what we mentioned, and it is understood from it that the incident is magnified because it is in the strength of: How great is the thing that you committed with Joseph and his brother, and how ugly is what you did? Just as it is said to the sinner: Do you know who you disobeyed? What they did to Joseph is what was mentioned previously of what God Almighty told us in this Surah. As for what they did to his brother, a group of commentators said that it is what they caused him of grief due to the separation from his brother Joseph, and what he suffered from them of contempt and humiliation, and He did not ask them about what they did to his father Jacob, although they suffered from them what God narrated previously of the types of harm. Al-Wahidi said: He did not mention his father, Jacob, despite the great grief that had befallen him due to his separation, out of respect for him and raising his status, and knowing that this was a trial for him from God Almighty to increase his status with Him. When you were ignorant, he denied them knowledge and affirmed the attribute of ignorance, because they did not know what knowledge requires. It was said that he affirmed the attribute of ignorance for them with the intention of apologizing to them and making the matter easier for them, as if he said: You only went ahead with that ugly, reprehensible act at a time when you did not know what sin it contained and your knowledge was insufficient about its consequences and what would result from it, or he meant that they were at that time in the time of youth and childhood, as an apology to them and to remove the shame and confusion that had befallen them, despite his knowledge and their knowledge that they were adults at that time.
12:90: 90-"They said, 'Are you indeed Joseph?' Ibn Kathir read inka" as a statement without a question. The rest read it as a question of confirmation, and that was from them in the way of astonishment and surprise: It was said that the reason for their knowing him as soon as he said to them, "What did you do with Joseph and his brother?" is that when he said that to them, they became alert and understood that no one would address them in such a way except him. It was said that when he said this to them, he took the crown off his head and they recognized him. It was also said that he smiled and they recognized his teeth. "He said, 'I am Joseph, and this is my brother.'" He answered them by confessing what they had asked him about. Ibn al-Anbari said that he made the name clear and said, "I am Joseph, and did not say, I am he, out of respect for the injustice done to him by his brothers, as if he said, I am the wronged one, the one who was made permissible, the one who was forbidden, and whose killing was intended." So he was satisfied with revealing the name about these meanings, and he said: And this is my brother, even though they know him and do not deny him, because what he meant is, and this is my brother who is wronged like my wrongdoing. God has bestowed His favor upon us with deliverance from what we have been afflicted with, and it was said that God has bestowed upon us all good in this world and the next, and it was said that He has brought us together after separation, and there is no objection to intending all of that Indeed, whoever fears God and is patient. The majority of scholars read it with the jussive mood, on the basis that min is conditional. Ibn Kathir read it with the confirmation of the ya’ in yataqi, as in the poet’s saying: Didn't the report come to you about what happened to the camels of Bani Ziyad? It was said that he made min a relative pronoun, not a conditional one, and this is far-fetched. The meaning is: whoever does righteousness or does what protects him from sins and is patient in the face of calamities, then indeed, God does not allow to be lost the reward of the righteous in general, so what the context indicates is included in it primarily, and he came with the apparent, and the situation was in the place of the implied: that is, their reward, to indicate that those described with righteousness are described with the attribute of righteousness.
12:91: 91- They said, 'By God, God has favored you over us' meaning, He has chosen you and favored you over us with the attributes of perfection that He has given you. This is an acknowledgment from them of His favor and great value. This does not necessarily mean that they were not prophets, for the ranks of prophets vary. God the Most High said: These are the messengers - We have favored some of them over others "And although we were sinners" meaning that is the case. Abu Ubaidah said: "Khataa and akhta'a" have the same meaning. Al-Azhari said: "The one who makes a mistake is the one who wanted to be right but then went to something else." This is how they say: "The one who strives makes mistakes and is right, and the one who makes a mistake is the one who deliberately does something that is not appropriate." They said this statement, which includes an admission of error and sin, in order to gain His pardon and attract His forgiveness.
12:92: 92- "He said, 'No reproach upon you.'" Reproach means reproach and rebuke: i.e. no reproach, rebuke, or blame upon you. Al-Asma'i said, "I condemned his actions. Al-Zajjaj said, The meaning is, there is no spoiling of the sanctity and brotherhood between me and you, and you have my peace and forgiveness." The root of reproach is corruption, and it is the language of the people of Hijaz. Ibn Al-Anbari said, "Its meaning is that my reproach upon you has ceased when you confess your sin. Tha'lab said, So-and-so reproached so-and-so" if he enumerated his sins. The root of reproach is from "tharab, which is the fat that covers the belly, and its meaning is to remove reproach, just as taglid and tadjild" are to remove the skin and slap. The word "today" is in the accusative case with reproach: i.e. no reproach upon you, or it is in the accusative case with the agent understood in "upon you," which is stable or fixed or something similar, i.e. no reproach is stable or fixed upon you. Al-Akhfash permitted stopping at "upon you, so that today" would be related to the verb that follows it. Ibn al-Anbari mentioned something similar to this. Then he prayed for them by saying: May God forgive you, assuming that the pause was on the day, or he informed them that God had forgiven them that day, assuming that the pause was on you. And He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, He has mercy on His servants with a mercy that they do not show mercy to one another with, so He rewards their good deeds and forgives their evil deeds.
12:93: 93- His saying Go with this shirt of mine. It was said that this shirt is the shirt that God dressed Abraham when he was thrown into the fire, and Abraham dressed Isaac with it, and Isaac dressed Jacob with it. Jacob had put this shirt in a reed and hung it around Joseph's neck because he feared the evil eye for him, so Gabriel told Joseph to send it to Jacob so that his sight would return because it contains the scent of Paradise, and the scent of Paradise does not fall on a sick person except that he is healed, nor on an afflicted person except that he is cured. So throw it on my father's face, and he will come back seeing. That is, he will insist on seeing, as it is one of the sisters of was. Al-Farra' said: He will return seeing. Al-Suddi said: He will be counted seeing. It was said that its meaning is: He will come to me in Egypt and he will be seeing, and his blindness will be gone from him. This is supported by his saying And bring me your families all together, meaning all those included in the word family of women and children. It was said that they were about seventy, and it was said that they were ninety-three.
12:94: 94- And when the caravan departed meaning it set out from Egypt to the Levant. It is said that it departed several times, and I separated it from a time, transitive and intransitive. It is said that he departed from the country several times: if he separated from it and passed its walls. Their father meaning Jacob to those of his family who were with him in the land of Canaan said, Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph. It was said that a wind blew and carried the scent of the shirt to Jacob despite the long distance, so he informed them of what he found, then he said, If only you would not refute if you would not attribute me to fand, which is the loss of reason due to old age. It is said that a man is senile and his mind has changed. Abu Ubaidah said, If only you would not be foolish, so he made fand foolishness. Al-Zajjaj said, If only you would not be ignorant, so he made fand ignorance. The statement of those who said that it is foolishness is supported by the statement of Al-Nabigha: Except for Solomon, when the king said to him, Go into the wilderness and determine its location. That is, prevent her from being foolish. Abu Omar Al-Shaibani said: Refutation means disgrace, and from this comes the saying of the poet: My friend, do not blame or refute me, for what has passed of my affair will not be returned. It was said that it is lying, and from it the poet said: Is there anyone who would like to be proud of the generous person, or is there anyone who would refute the words of a friend? Ibn al-A'rabi said: Lawla an tafnadoon means if you do not weaken my opinion. A similar narration was narrated from Abu Ubaidah. Al-Akhfash said: Tafnad is blame and weakening of opinion. All of these meanings refer to incapacitating and weakening opinion. It is said that he fandahu tafnadhan: if he made someone incapable, and afanda: if he spoke incorrectly. Fandad is a mistake in speech. What indicates that it is used to mean blame is the saying of the poet: Oh, you who criticize me, blame has come and gone. Love has been long and you have prolonged the refutation. Jacob told them that the morning had brought him the scent of his beloved, and that if he had not feared being refuted, he would not have doubted that: The morning breeze is a wind that blows on a worried soul, revealing its worries. If I say this, I will live, and the morning breeze will excite me from where the dawn rises. And the breeze blows to me from its land, and the touch of your breeze is pleasant and pleasant.
12:95: 95- They said, 'By God, you are indeed in your old error.' That is, those of his family present with him said: O Jacob, you are indeed straying from the right path that you were on in the past, due to your excessive love for Joseph. You do not forget him, nor do you slacken off from him. And Jacob's inner voice was saying to them: Only those who suffer from longing know what it is, and only those who experience it know what it is. Do not blame the one who is yearning for his yearnings until your heart is in his entrails It was said that the meaning is: You are in your old madness, and it was said: In your old erasure.
12:96: They said that to him because they had not heard of the arrival of the bearer of good report 96- So when the bearer of good report came The commentators said that the bearer of good report is Judah, son of Jacob. He said to his brothers: I came to him with the shirt stained with blood, so give me your shirt today so that I may tell him that you are alive, and I will make him happy as you made him sad. He threw it on his face meaning the bearer of good report threw Joseph's shirt on Jacob's face, or Jacob threw it on his own face. So he regained his sight. Reversion: the reversal of something to a state it had been in, and the meaning is: it returned and returned to its original state of healthy sight. "He said: Did I not tell you?" meaning Jacob said to those of his family who were with him to whom he said: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph: Did I not tell you this statement and you said what you said? His saying: Indeed, I know from God what you do not know is an introductory statement that is not related to the statement. It is possible that the phrase Indeed, I know from God what you do not know is the statement of the statement, and he means by that to inform them of what He said previously: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God, and I know from God that which you do not know.
12:97: 97- “They said, ‘O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins. Indeed, we were sinners.’” They asked him to ask forgiveness for them, and they confessed their sin. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: When they returned from Egypt and reached their father, they said this, and he promised them what they asked of him.
12:98: 98- He said, 'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord.' Al-Zajjaj said: Jacob wanted to ask forgiveness for them at the time of dawn, because he is more likely to have his supplications answered, not that he was stingy with asking forgiveness for them. It was said that he delayed it until Friday night, and it was said that he delayed it until he asked forgiveness for them from Joseph, and he did not know that he had forgiven them. The phrase Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful is an explanation for what preceded it. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: No reproach, he said: No reproach. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather who said: He said, "When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca, he turned to the people and said: What do you say and what do you think? They said: A generous cousin. He said: No reproach upon you today. May God forgive you." Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala'il on the authority of Abu Hurayrah with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani, who said: Asking for needs from young people is easier than asking from old people. Have you not seen the words of Joseph, There is no blame upon you today? And Jacob said, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. I say: There is a consideration in this statement, for they asked Joseph to pardon them by saying: God has favored you over us, and he said: There is no blame upon you today, because their intention was for him to pardon them, and they asked their father Jacob to seek forgiveness from God for them, and this can only happen by asking God Almighty for that, and there is a difference between the two situations, so Jacob’s promise to them was not miserliness towards them in asking God for them, especially if what was mentioned above is true, that he delayed that until the time of the answer, for if he had asked it for them immediately, he would not have had knowledge of the acceptance. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, who said: When the matter of Joseph’s brothers happened, Jacob wrote to Joseph, not knowing that he was Joseph: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, from Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, to the Aziz of the family of Pharaoh. Peace be upon you, for I praise God to you, there is no god but Him. As for what follows: We are a family that is infatuated with the causes of affliction. My grandfather, Abraham, the friend of God, was thrown into the fire in obedience to his Lord, so God made it cool and safe for him. God ordered my grandfather to slaughter my father for him, so God ransomed him with what He ransomed him for. I had a son who was one of the dearest people to me, so I lost him, and my grief over him took away the light of my sight. He had a brother from his mother, and whenever I remembered him, I would hug him to my chest, so he took away some of my sorrow. He is the one who is imprisoned with you for theft. I tell you that I steal, and I did not give birth to a thief. When Joseph read the letter, he cried and cried out, saying, Go with this shirt of mine and throw it over my father’s face, and he will regain his sight. Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his words, Go with this shirt of mine, that when Nimrod threw Abraham into the fire, Gabriel came down to him with a shirt from Paradise and a carpet from Paradise. He dressed him in the shirt and seated him on the carpet. He sat with him and talked. Then God revealed to the fire, Be cool and safe. Had he not said, And safe, the cold would have harmed him. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, that God clothed Abraham with a garment from Paradise, and Abraham clothed him with Isaac, and Isaac clothed him with Jacob. Jacob took it and put it in an iron reed and hung it around Joseph’s neck. If his brothers had known when they threw him into the well, they would have taken him. When God wanted to return Joseph to Jacob, there were forty years between his vision and its interpretation. He ordered the herald to give him good report of eight stages. Jacob smelled its scent and said, I smell the scent of Joseph, unless you think it is false. When he threw it on his face, his sight returned. Nothing from Paradise befalls any of the ailments of this world except that it heals it by God’s permission. And Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And when the caravan departed, he said: When the caravan set out, the wind blew and brought Jacob the scent of Joseph’s shirt, so he said: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph, unless you are foolish. So he smelled it from a distance of eight days. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on his authority that he smelled it from a distance of ten days. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from another chain of transmission on his authority that he found it from a distance of eighty farsakhs. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority: Unless you are foolish, he said: You are ignorant. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority that he said: You are lying. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: You become old, they say your mind has gone. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’ that he said: Unless you are foolish. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, you are in your old error, meaning: your old mistake. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, who said: your old madness. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: your old love. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: the bearer of good tidings is the messenger. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak similarly. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Sufyan, who said: the bearer of good tidings is Judah, son of Jacob. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: When the bearer of good tidings came to Jacob and threw the shirt over him, he said: On what religion did you leave Joseph? He said: On Islam. He said: Now the blessing is complete. Abu Ubaid, Saeed Ibn Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding his statement, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, he said: Jacob delayed his sons until dawn. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: he delayed them until dawn. And he used to pray at dawn. Abu Al-Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: He delayed them until dawn because the supplication at dawn is answered. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh also narrated on his authority that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in a story: “It is the saying of my brother Jacob to his sons: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, he says until Friday night comes.”
12:99: His statement: 99- So when they entered upon Joseph Perhaps there is an omission in the speech that is understood, which is that Jacob and his children and his family traveled to Egypt, and when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to him: that is, he embraced them and settled them with him. The commentators said: What is meant by the parents here is Jacob and his wife, Joseph's aunt, because his mother had died while giving birth to his brother Benjamin, as mentioned above. It was also said that God revived his mother to fulfill the vision until she prostrated to him. And he said, 'Enter Egypt, if God wills, in safety' from what you hate, and in the past they feared the kings of Egypt, and they would not enter it except with their permission. It was said that the restriction to the will refers to safety, and there is no objection to its referring to everyone, because their entry does not happen except with the will of God Almighty, just as they are not safe except with His will. It was also said that the restriction to the will refers to His statement: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, which is far-fetched. The apparent meaning of the Qur’anic system is that Joseph said this statement to them: Enter Egypt before they entered it. It has been said that he met them outside Egypt, so he stood waiting for them in a place or tent, and they entered upon him. He took his parents into his house and said, ‘Enter Egypt.’ So when they entered Egypt and entered upon him again in the place he had in Egypt.
12:100: 100- He raised his parents to the throne meaning he seated them with him on the bed on which he sits as is the custom of kings and they fell down before him in prostration meaning the parents and brothers, and the meaning is that they fell down before Joseph in prostration, and that was permissible in their law and was given the status of greeting, and it was said that it was not prostration but rather a mere gesture, and that was their greeting, and it contradicts the meaning of: and they fell down before him in prostration, because falling down in the language restricted to prostration does not happen except by placing the face on the ground, and it was said that the pronoun in his saying to him refers to God Almighty, meaning and they fell down before God in prostration, and this is very far-fetched, and it was said that the pronoun refers to Joseph, and the lam is for al-Sharh 94:meaning and they fell down for his sake, and in it also there is a dimension and Joseph said O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision meaning the one mentioned previously before meaning before this time my Lord has made it come true by its interpretation occurring as it indicated and He was kind to me when He brought me out of prison the origin is that The verb of kindness is transitive with the preposition to, and it may be transitive with the preposition to, as in the Almighty’s saying: And to parents, do good. It was said that he included the best meaning of be kind to me, a benefactor. He did not mention his being taken out of the well, because in mentioning it there is a kind of reproach to the brothers, and he said: There is no reproach upon you. The reason for his imprisonment and the length of his stay in it has already been mentioned. It was said that the reason for not mentioning his being taken out of the well is that the favor of taking him out of prison was greater than the favor of taking him out of the well, and there is a consideration in this. And he brought you from the desert, meaning the desert, which is the land of Canaan in the Levant, and they were people of livestock and wilderness. It was said that God did not send a prophet from the desert, and that the place where Jacob was was called Bada, and Jamil meant it in his saying: You are the one who made a people beloved to me and made my homeland beloved to other countries. And in it is a view: After Satan had sown discord between me and my brothers, meaning he corrupted us and made some of us fight each other. It is said that he nudged him if he prodded him, so its origin is from the prodding of an animal to strengthen its gait. Joseph attributed the sin of his brothers to Satan out of generosity and politeness. Indeed, my Lord is Kind to whomever He wills. Al-Lateef Al-Rafeeq. Al-Azhari said: Al-Lateef is one of the names of God, meaning the Kind to His servants. It is said that someone was kind to someone, meaning he was gentle with him. Amr bin Abi Amr said: Al-Lateef is the one who brings your concerns to you in kindness. Al-Khattabi said: Al-Lateef is the one who is kind to His servants, who is kind to them from where they do not know, and brings about their interests from where they do not expect. It was said that Al-Lateef is the one who knows the details of matters, and the meaning of whenever He wills is: for the sake of what He wills until it comes out right. Indeed, He is the Knowing, the Wise, meaning the One who knows matters and is wise in His actions. When God completed His blessings upon Joseph, peace be upon him, by saving him from great trials and granting him kingship and knowledge, his soul yearned for the eternal and unending good of the afterlife.
12:101: He said: 101- My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom Min is for partiality: meaning some of the kingdom, because he was not given all of the kingdom, but rather he was given a special kingdom, which is the kingdom of Egypt at a special time. And You taught me of the interpretation of dreams meaning some of it, because he was not given all of the knowledge of interpretation, whether it is intended by it absolute knowledge and understanding, or merely the interpretation of dreams. It was said that Min is for the genus as in His saying: So avoid the uncleanness of idols. It was said that it is redundant: meaning You gave me the kingdom and taught me the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and the earth is in the accusative case as an attribute of Lord, because it is a vocative with an added word. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a vocative with an implied letter: meaning O Creator, and the Creator is the Creator, the Originator, the Inventor, and the Maker. You are my protector meaning my helper and the one who takes care of my affairs. In this world and the hereafter You are my protector in them. Leave me as a Muslim and join me with the righteous meaning let me die upon Islam, it will not leave me until I die and join the righteous prophets from my fathers and others, so that I may obtain their reward from you and their ranks with you. It was said that when he supplicated with this supplication, God the Almighty took him. It was said that his age when he was thrown into the well was seventeen years, and he was in slavery, prison, and kingship for eighty years until the arrival of his father, Jacob, peace be upon him. Then he lived after their reunion until he completed his lifespan to the amount that will come and God took him. It was said that no one wished for death except Joseph, neither prophet nor anyone else. The majority went to the view that he did not wish for death with this supplication, but rather he supplicated to his Lord to take him as a Muslim and join him with the righteous among His servants when his time came. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: Jacob entered Egypt during the reign of Joseph when he was one hundred and thirty years old, and he lived during his reign for thirty years, and Joseph died when he was one hundred and twenty years old. Abu Hurairah said: It was reported to me that the age of Abraham, the friend of God, was one hundred and ninety-five years. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: He took his parents into his care he said: His father and mother took them in. They narrated on the authority of Wahb who said: And his maternal aunt. Joseph’s mother had died during the confinement of his brother Benjamin. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And raised his parents upon the throne he said: The bed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Adi bin Hatim regarding his statement: And they fell down before him in prostration he said: It was the greeting of those who came before you, then God gave you peace in its place. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zaid who said: This is a prostration of honor, just as the angels prostrated in honor for Adam, and it is not a prostration of worship. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Indeed, my Lord is Kind to whomever He wills, he said: He was kind to Joseph and did for him when He brought him out of prison, and brought his family from the desert, and removed from his heart the whisperings of Satan and his incitement against his brothers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: No prophet asked for death except Joseph. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Sheikh narrated on his authority who said: He longed to meet God and wanted to join Him and his fathers. So he supplicated to God to take him and join him with them. Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: And join me with the righteous, he said: He means Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac and Jacob. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: He means the people of Paradise.
12:102: The address is in the words: 102- That is for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is a subject whose predicate is from the report of the unseen, and We reveal it to you is a second predicate. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that that means that which and We reveal it to you is its predicate: that is, that which from the report of the unseen We reveal to you. Meaning: God Almighty informing His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that what he told him about the matter of Joseph and his brothers was from the report that was hidden from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed it to him and informed him of it and he did not have anything of that before the revelation. In it is an allusion to the infidels of Quraysh, because they were denying him, may God bless him and grant him peace, what he brought, out of denial, stubbornness and envy, even though they knew the truth of the situation. And you were not with them, meaning with Joseph’s brothers, when they decided to throw him into the well. Consensus: determination: meaning, you were not with Joseph’s brothers when they all decided to throw him into the well. And they, in that state, plotted against him, meaning against Joseph in this act that they did to him and sought to cause him calamities. It was said that the pronoun refers to Jacob, meaning they plotted against Jacob when they brought Joseph’s shirt stained with blood and said that a wolf had eaten him. If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not with them when they did that, then his knowledge of that was negated by observation, and there was no knowledge among people who had knowledge of the conditions of nations. The predecessors, nor did he mix with them nor did they mix with him, so his knowledge of that was negated by way of narration from others, so there remained no way for his knowledge of that except mere revelation from God Almighty, so this necessitates belief in what he brought, so when those of the infidels who were his contemporaries did not believe in that.
12:103: God the Almighty said, mentioning this103- And most of the people are not believers, even if you were eager to guide them. That is, most of the people who are your contemporaries, O Muhammad, or most of the people in general, even if you were eager to guide them and went to extremes in that, are not believers in God because of their insistence on disbelief, which is the religion of their fathers. It is said ḥarāṣa yaḥrāṣa like ḍarāb yaḍarūb, and in a weak language ḥarāṣa yaḥrāṣa like ḥamād yaḥmād, and eagerness is seeking something with diligence. Al-Zajjaj said that its meaning is: Most of the people are not believers, even if you were eager to guide them, because you do not guide whom you love, but God guides whom He wills. Ibn al-Anbari said: The Quraysh and the Jews asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the story of Joseph and his brothers, so he explained them in a comprehensive manner, hoping that this would be a reason for their conversion to Islam, but they contradicted his assumption, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saddened by that, so God consoled him by saying: And most of the people are not believers.
12:104: Verse 104 - And whatever payment you ask of them for it meaning for the Qur’an and what you recite to them of it, or for the faith and your eagerness for it to happen to them, or for what you tell them of this hadith of a reward of money that they give you and make it for you as their rabbis do. It meaning the Qur’an or the hadith that you told them is only a reminder for the worlds meaning it is only a reminder for all the worlds and is not specific to them alone.
12:105: 105- And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth? Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: The majority of scholars say that the root of how many is the letter ka-ayn, meaning that the letter kaf was added to it, but it was erased from the two individual letters, and the plural became ka-ma, meaning ka-ma, the report. The majority of scholars include min in its distinguishing feature, which is a distinguishing feature from the letter kaf, not an, meaning like you are a man. We have already discussed this in detail in Al Imran. Meaning: How many signs guide them to the Oneness of God, in the heavens, from being erected without pillars, decorated with the bright, moving and fixed planets, and on the earth, from its mountains, deserts, seas, plants and animals, guide them to the Oneness of God, the Most High, and that He is the Creator of that, the Provider, the Giver of life and death. But most people pass by these signs without contemplating them, nor thinking about them, nor paying attention to what they indicate of the existence of their Creator, and that He is the One alone in divinity, even though they are witnessing them. They pass by them, turning away from them. And if they look at them with their eyes, they have turned away from what is the fruit of looking with the pupil, which is contemplation, consideration and reasoning. Ikrimah and Amr ibn Fayid read the word the earth in the nominative case as the subject, and its predicate is they pass by it. Al-Suddi read the word the earth in the accusative case as a verb. Ibn Masoud read they walk on it.
12:106: 106- And most of them do not believe in God meaning, and most people do not believe and acknowledge God as the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of Life and Death except that they associate others with Him with God, worshipping others besides Him as the people of ignorance used to do, for they acknowledge God, the Exalted, and that He is their Creator And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, 'God' "And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, 'God', but they used to attribute partners to Him and worship them to bring them closer to God We only worship them that they may bring us closer to God" and like those who took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God, who believe that the dead are able to do what only God, the Exalted, is able to do, as many of the grave worshippers do. This does not contradict what was said that the verse was revealed about a specific people, so consideration is given to what the wording indicates, not what the reason indicates of being specific to those who were the reason for the revelation of the ruling.
12:107: 107- Do they then feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from God? The question is for denial, and the overwhelming is that which covers them and engulfs them from the punishment, as in the saying of God the Almighty: The Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and it was said that it is the Hour, and it was said that it is thunderbolts and calamities, and there is nothing preventing it from being carried on the generality or the Hour will come upon them suddenly meaning suddenly, and the accusative of suddenly is a state. Al-Mubarrad said: The Arabs came with a state after an indefinite noun, and it is their saying that a matter occurred suddenly, it is said that the matter surprised them suddenly and suddenly: if it surprised them while they were not aware of its coming, and it is permissible to make the accusative of suddenly as an attribute of a deleted source.
12:108: 108- "Say: This is my way" meaning, say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists, this is the call to which I call and the method which I am on. My way: meaning, my path and my Sunnah. The demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is my way. This was explained by saying: I call to God with insight meaning, with clear evidence. Insight is the knowledge by which truth is distinguished from falsehood. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. I and whoever follows me meaning, whoever follows me and is guided by my guidance calls to it. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is, whoever follows me calls to God as I call. This is evidence that every follower of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has the right to follow his example in calling to faith in him, to His Oneness, and to act according to what He has prescribed for His servants. And glory be to God, and I am not of those who associate others with God meaning, and say, O Muhammad, to them, glory be to God, and I am not of those who associate others with God who take others besides Him as equals. Ibn al-Anbari said: It is permissible to complete the speech when he said: I call to God, then he began, saying: With insight, I and whoever follows me. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And you were not with them when they decided their plan and they were plotting, he said: They are the sons of Jacob when they were plotting against Joseph. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse: And you were not with them when they threw him into the bottom of the well while they were plotting against Joseph. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And how many a sign, he said: How many a sign in the heaven, meaning its sun, moon, stars and clouds, and on the earth and what it contains of creation, rivers, mountains, cities and palaces. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And most of them do not believe in God except while they are associating others with Him, he said: Ask them who created them and who created the heavens and the earth, and they will say: God. That is their belief while they worship other than Him. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding the statement of God, And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him, that he said: They knew that God is their Lord and He is their Creator and Provider, and yet they associated others with Him.
