Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding the verse, that he said: They associated others with Him in their Talbiyah, saying, Here I am, O God, to You, You have no partner except a partner whom You possess and what He possesses. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse, that he said: That hypocrite acts out of hypocrisy and he is an associate in his actions. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the statement of God, A covering from the punishment of God, that he said: A calamity will overwhelm them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, This is my way, that he said: Say, This is my supplication. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority, Say, “This is my way, that he said: My prayer. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, he said: My command, my will, and my way. They narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: On insight meaning on guidance, I and whoever follows me.
12:109: His statement 109- And We did not send before you except men This is a response to those who said Why was an angel not sent down to him: meaning, We did not send from the prophets to those before you except men, not angels, so how can they deny sending you. The verse indicates that God Almighty did not send a prophet from among women or from among the jinn, and this responds to those who said: There were four prophets among women: Eve, Asiya, the mother of Moses, and Mary. The sending of prophets from among men and not women was a well-known matter among the Arabs, to the point that Qays bin Asim said about Sajjah the prophetess: Our prophet has become a female we circumambulate and the prophets of God have become male May God curse all people and whoever tempted us with blame We reveal to them as We reveal to you from the people of the towns meaning the cities, not the people of the desert, due to the prevalence of harshness and cruelty among the Bedouins and because the people of the cities are more perfect in mind, more complete in patience and more noble in virtue. Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? meaning the polytheists who denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: meaning, have these polytheists not traveled and observed the fates of past nations and taken a lesson from them so that they may abandon their denial? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God meaning the home of the Last Hour, or the state of the Hereafter, with the deletion of the described. Al-Farra’ said: The home is the Hereafter, and the thing is attributed to itself due to the difference in wording, such as Friday, the first prayer, and the congregational mosque, and the discussion of that is explained in the books of grammar. What is meant by this home is Paradise, meaning it is better for the righteous than the home of this world. It was read and for the home of the Hereafter and Nafi’, ‘Asim, and Ya’qub read Do you not then understand with the superscript ta’ as an address.
12:110: And the rest read with the letter ta'tiyah 110- Until when the messengers despaired This is the end of an omission indicated by the speech, and its meaning is: And We did not send before you, O Muhammad, except men, and We did not hasten to punish their nations who did not believe in what they brought, Until when the messengers despaired of victory by punishing their people, or until when the messengers despaired of their people's belief because they were immersed in disbelief, and they thought that they had been denied. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Ja`far ibn al-Qa`qa`, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Raja` al-`Attardi, `Asim, Hamza, al-Kisa`i, Yahya ibn Wathab, al-A`mash and Khalaf read it with a light sukoon: The people thought that the messengers had lied to them about what they had told them about the punishment and they did not believe them. It was also said that the meaning is: The people thought that the messengers had lied to them about what they claimed about their victory. It was also said that the meaning is: The messengers thought that their own selves had lied to them when they told them that they would be victorious over them, or their hope for victory had lied to them. The rest read it with a shaddah, and the meaning is clear: That is, the messengers thought that their people had lied to them about what they had promised them of punishment. It is permissible in this case for the subject of the word dhan they thought that the people had sent to them to mean that they thought that the messengers had lied about what they had brought of promise and threat. Mujahid and Hamid read Qad kuddasha with the opening of the kaf and the dhal, and with a light sukoon, meaning: And the people of the messengers thought that the messengers had been lied to. It has been said that the word suspect in this verse means certainty, because the messengers were certain that their people had lied to them, and it was not just a thought on their part. What should be interpreted as certainty in such a scenario and interpreted with its original meaning in what is merely a thought from the previous scenarios is Our victory came to them meaning the messengers were suddenly given victory from God Almighty, or the people of the messengers who had lied to them were given victory from God for His messengers by inflicting punishment on the deniers. So We saved whom We willed Asim read Fanji with one nun. The rest read Fanji with two nuns. Abu Ubaidah chose the first reading because it is also in the Mushaf of Uthman. Ibn Muhaisin read fanja in the active form, so min in the first reading is in the nominative case as a deputy subject, and in the second reading it is in the accusative case as a direct object, and in the third reading it is in the nominative case as a subject. And those whom God saved are the messengers and those who believed with them, and the deniers perished. And Our punishment cannot be averted from the criminal people when it descends upon them, and in it is a statement of whomever God wills to save from the punishment, and they are those other than these criminals.
12:111: 111- There was in their stories meaning the stories of the messengers and the nations to whom they were sent, or in the stories of Joseph, his brothers, and his father a lesson for those of understanding. A lesson is the idea and insight that frees one from ignorance and confusion. It was said that it is a type of consideration, and it is the passage from the known side to the unknown side, and the people of understanding are those with sound minds who consider with their minds and know what is in the interests of their religion, and this story was a lesson because it included report that matches reality despite the long period between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the messengers whose story he narrated, including Joseph, his brothers and his father, although he did not know their report nor contact their rabbis. It was not a story that was invented, meaning that this story that is indicated by mentioning the stories, which is the Qur’an that includes that, was not a story that was invented, but a confirmation of what was before it, meaning what came before it from the revealed books such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms. It was read with the nominative case of confirmation as the report of a deleted subject: meaning it is the confirmation and detail of everything from the general laws that need to be detailed, because God Almighty did not neglect anything in the book. It was said that the detail of everything from the story of Joseph with his brothers and his father. It was said that what is meant by it is not what it entails of generality, but rather what is meant by it are the principles and laws and what leads to them, and guidance in this world by which everyone whom God wants to guide is guided, and mercy in the Hereafter by which God has mercy on His servants who act according to what is in it the condition of correct faith. For this reason, He said: for a people who believe, meaning they believe in it and what it includes of belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, His laws, and His destiny. As for those other than them, they do not benefit from it nor are they guided by what it includes of guidance, so they do not deserve what they deserve. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We did not send before you, except men, he said: That is, they were not from the people of heaven as you said. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse: He said: We do not know that God ever sent a messenger except from the people of the villages, because they were more knowledgeable and patient than the people of the inhabited world. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: How was the end of those before them? He said: How did God punish the people of Noah, the people of Lot, the people of Salih and the nations that God punished. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Urwah that he asked Aisha about the statement of God, the Most High: Meaning: When the messengers despair and think that they have been denied, he said: I said: Did they deny or were they denied? Meaning, is this word light or heavy? She said: Rather, they lied, meaning with emphasis. I said: By God, they were certain that their people lied to them, so it is not a matter of suspicion. She said: Yes, by my life, they were certain of that. I said: Perhaps it is and they thought that they had been lied light. She said: God forbid, the messengers would not have thought that of their Lord. I said: What is this verse? She said: They are the followers of the messengers who believed in them and confirmed them, and the affliction was prolonged for them and victory was delayed for them, until when the messengers despaired of those among their people who had lied to them and the messengers thought that their followers had lied to them, then victory came to them at that time. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah that Ibn Abbas recited it to him: and they thought that they had been lied to lightly, meaning they broke their promise. Ibn Abbas said: They were human beings, and he recited: “Until the Messenger and those who believed with him say: When is the victory of God?” Ibn Abi Malekah said: And Urwah told me on the authority of Aisha that she disagreed with that and refused it, and she said: By God, God did not promise a Messenger anything except that He knew that it would happen before he died, but the trials of the Messengers continued until they thought that the believers who were with them had denied them, and she used to recite it with a heavy vowel. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And they thought that they had been denied with a light vowel. Abu Ubaid, Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite They had been denied with a light vowel. He said: The Messengers despaired of their people responding to them, and their people thought that the Messengers had denied them with what they had brought. Our victory has come to them he said: The Messengers have come with Our victory. And Abd al-Razzaq, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Tamim ibn Hudlam who said: I recited the Qur’an to Ibn Mas`ud, and he only accepted two letters from me. Each one came to him in humiliation, so he said: They came to him in the light form. And I recited to him: And they thought that they had been denied in the light form. He said: They were denied in the light form. He said: The messengers despaired of their people believing in them, and their people thought when the matter was delayed that they had been lied to. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas on his authority that he memorized from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Surat Yusuf 12:And they thought that they had been denied in the light form. And the predecessors have a statement on this that goes back to what we mentioned of the disagreement from the Companions. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then We will save whom We will in the light form. He said: So We will save the messengers and whom We will. And Our punishment will not be averted from the criminal people in the light form. That is because God sent the messengers to call their people, and they informed them that whoever obeys God will be saved, and whoever disobeys Him will be punished and led astray. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on his authority that he said: Our victory has come to them meaning the punishment. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi that Our punishment cannot be repelled meaning His punishment. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: There was certainly in their stories meaning Joseph and his brothers. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated that a lesson for those of understanding meaning: well-known to those of intellect. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Qatada that it was not a fabricated statement meaning: a lie but a confirmation of what was before it meaning: the Qur’an confirms the books that came before it from the books of God that He sent down to His prophets such as the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms, and confirms all of that and bears witness to it that all of it is the truth from God. And the details of everything meaning God distinguished between what is lawful and unlawful, and between obedience and disobedience to Him.
13:1: There was a dispute over whether it was revealed in Mecca or Medina. An-Nahhas narrated in his Naskh on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was revealed in Mecca. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that it was revealed in Medina. Among those who held that it was revealed in Mecca are Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir bin Zayd. Among those who claimed that it was revealed in Medina are Ibn Al-Zubayr, Al-Kalbi and Muqatil. A third opinion is that it was revealed in Medina except for two verses, which were revealed in Mecca, namely the words of God the Most High: And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains could be moved and it was said that it was: And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by what they have done by a terrible calamity. This was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Marwazi narrated in Funerals on the authority of Jabir bin Zayd who said: It was recommended that when a person is present, Surat Ar-Ra'd be recited near him, as this makes things easier for the person who is dying, and it makes his death easier and his situation easier. His saying: 1- Al-Murr We have already discussed these letters that occur at the beginning of the surahs in a way that makes repetition unnecessary. It is the name of the surah, raised in position as the predicate of a deleted subject, or as a subject whose predicate is what follows it. The meaning is that this surah is its name, and the reference in his saying: That is to the verses of this surah, and what is meant by the book is the surah: that is, those verses are the verses of the complete surah that are amazing in their status. And his saying: And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth is intended to mean the entire Qur'an: that is, it is the truth that has reached this description. Or the reference in his saying: That is to the verses of the Qur'an as a whole, so that what is meant by the book is the entire Qur'an, and his saying: And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth is a sentence explaining that this one who was revealed is the truth. Al-Farra' said: And that which is raised by resumption and its predicate is the truth. He said: And if you wish, you can make that which is lowered an attribute of the book, even if there is a waw in it as in his saying: To the venerable king and son of the hero It is possible that the place of and the one who revealed to you is the accusative, based on the estimation: and the verses of what was revealed to you, so the truth, according to this, is the predicate of the omitted subject, but most people do not believe in this truth that God revealed to you.
13:2: Al-Zajjaj said: When he mentioned that they do not believe, he mentioned the evidence that requires belief in the Creator, so he said: 2- God is He who raised the heavens without pillars. The pillars are the plural of pillar: meaning standing without pillars that are relied upon, and they are called pillars, but we do not see them. Al-Zajjaj said that the pillars are His power by which He holds the heavens, and they are not visible to us, and it was read as pillars as the plural of pillar that is supported by it: meaning it is leaned on. Al-Nabigha said: And the jinn were informed that I had given them permission to build a grove of stones and columns. The sentence you see it is a new sentence, as evidence of their seeing it like that. It was said that it is an attribute of pillars. It was said that there is an advancement and delay in the speech, and the meaning is: He raised the heavens, you see them, without pillars, and there is no resort to such an effort. Then He established Himself on the Throne means He took control of it by preservation and management, or His command was established, or He turned to the creation of the Throne. The speech on this has already been presented in full. And establishing Himself on the Throne is an attribute of God, the Most High, without how, as is established in its place in the science of theology. And He subjected the sun and the moon means He subdued them for what is desired from them of the benefits of creation and the interests of the servants. Each runs for a specified term means each of the sun and the moon runs for a known time: which is the passing of the world and the establishment of the Hour when the sun will be rolled up and the moon will be eclipsed and the stars will be scattered. It was said that what is meant by the specified term are their degrees and their stations that they will end at and they will not exceed them, and it is a year for the sun and a month for the moon. He directs the affair means He directs it to what He wants, and it is the affair of His kingdom and His Lordship. He details the signs means He explains it: They are the verses that indicate the perfection of His power and His Lordship, including what was mentioned previously about raising the sky without pillars and subjecting the sun and moon and their running for a specified term. The two sentences are in the accusative case as a state or predicate of inna for His statement: God is the One Who raised on the basis that the relative pronoun is an attribute of the subject. The purpose of this is to alert the servants that He who is able to do these things is able to resurrect and bring back. Therefore, He said: Perhaps you will be certain of the meeting with your Lord meaning that perhaps when you witness these verses you will be certain of that and not doubt it or cast doubt on His truthfulness.
13:3: And when he mentioned the heavenly signs, he followed them with mentioning the earthly signs, saying 3- And it is He who spread out the earth. Al-Farra' said that He spread it out in length and breadth. Al-Asamm said: Spreading is spreading out to an extent that cannot be reached, and this apparent spreading to the eye does not contradict its sphericity in itself due to the distance between its edges. And He placed therein firm mountains, meaning fixed mountains. The singular of it is raasiya because the earth is anchored by it: meaning it is fixed, and anchoring is stability. Antara said: So I became aware of that, so I am free to anchor if the coward's soul comes out Jamil said: I love her and he who laid down his foundations until his signs appeared hidden And rivers meaning running water in the earth in which there are benefits for creation, or what is meant is that He made watercourses in it. And of all fruits He has made therein two mates of all fruits is related to the verb that follows it: meaning He made therein of all fruits two mates: the mates are used to refer to two, and to one that is paired with another, and what is meant here by the mates is one, and for this reason the mates are emphasized with the two to dispel the notion that what is meant by the mates here is two. This has been fully explained, meaning that every type of worldly fruit has two kinds, or in quantity such as small and large, or in quality such as hot and cold. Al-Farra’ said that what is meant by the two mates here is the male and female, and the first is more appropriate. The night covers the day meaning it takes its place, so it becomes black and dark after it was white and luminous. It is similar to removing the light of guidance with darkness by covering the tangible things with covers that conceal them. This has been explained previously in al-A’raf 7:Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought. That is, in what was mentioned about the extension of the earth and its establishment by mountains, and what God placed in it of intermingled fruits, and the alternation of light and darkness, are clear signs for those who look, think, and consider.
13:4: 4- And on the earth are adjacent tracts This is a new statement that includes mentioning another type of verses. It was said that there is an omission in the statement: that is, adjacent tracts in His statement garments to protect you from the heat meaning and protect you from the cold. It was said that the adjacent tracts are cities and what was inhabited, and the non-adjacent tracts are deserts and what was not inhabited. It was said that the meaning is: adjacent and close together, their soil is the same and their water is the same, and in them are crops and gardens, then they vary in fruits, so some are sweet and some sour, some are good and some are not good, and some are suitable for one type and others another type. And gardens of grapes Gardens: orchards. The majority read with the nominative case of gardens, estimating: And on the earth are gardens, so it is conjoined with adjacent tracts, or estimating: And between them are gardens. Al-Hasan read it in the accusative case, estimating: And He placed therein gardens. The Almighty mentioned the crops between the grapes and the palm trees, because they are often like that outside. The same is true in His statement, the Almighty: We made for one of them two gardens of grapes and surrounded them with palm trees and placed between them crops “in pairs and not in pairs.” Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Hafs read and crops and palm trees in pairs and not in pairs with these four in the nominative case in apposition to gardens. The rest read it in the genitive case in apposition to grapes. Mujahid and Al-Salami read with a damma on the sad of Sunawan. The rest read it in the kasra, and they are two languages. Abu Ubaidah said Sunawan: the plural of Sunu, which is that the root is one, then it branches out and becomes palm trees, then it is carried. This is the statement of all the people of language and interpretation. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: Sunu is the like, and from it is his statement, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: A man’s paternal uncle is his father’s like. So the meaning of the verse according to this is that palm trees may be similar or they may not be. Al-Kashshaf said: “And the Sunwan is the plural of Sunu, which is a palm tree with two heads and one root. It was said that the Sunwan is combined, and other than the Sunwan is the scattered one.” An-Nahhas: It is the same in the language. It is said of the palm tree if there is another palm tree or more in it: Sunwan. And the Sunu is the like, and there is no difference between the dual and the Jun’ except by breaking the nun in the dual. And as required by the syntax in the plural is watered with one water Asim and Ibn Amir read: is watered with the lower case: meaning that all of that is watered. The rest read with the upper case by referring the pronoun to gardens. Abu Hatim, Abu Ubaid and Abu Amr chose it. Abu Amr said: The feminine is better because of his saying: And We prefer some of them over others in eating and he did not say some of it. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read Nafadl with the lower case as in his saying: He directs the matter, separates the verses and the rest read with the nun on the assumption: And we prefer. This is evidence of the wonder of His creation and the greatness of His power, which is not hidden from anyone who has reason. The adjacent plots and the adjacent gardens containing various types of plants, although they are watered with the same water and differ in the fruits in eating, so that the taste of some of them is sweet and the taste of others sour, and this is of the utmost goodness, and this is not good, and this is exceedingly good, and this is not exceedingly good, which is what makes one who thinks, considers, and considers with the view of the rational, that the reason requiring their difference is nothing but the power of the wise Creator, may His power be glorified and His status exalted, because the effect of the difference in what comes out of them and what is obtained from their fruits is only for two reasons in the view of the rational: either the difference in the place that is the plant, or the difference in the water with which they are watered. So if the place is adjacent, and the plots of land are adjacent, and the water with which they are watered is the same, then there remains no reason for the difference in the view of the mind except that dazzling power and wondrous creation. That is why God Almighty said, Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason, meaning they act on the issue of reason and what it requires, not neglecting what it requires of contemplation of creation and consideration of the lessons of existence. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The heavens are raised without pillars that you can see, he said: I am God, I see. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid: The heavens are the opening words with which one begins his speech. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding his statement: These are the verses of the Book, he said: The Torah and the Gospel. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, he said: The Qur’an. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, he said: And what do you know? Perhaps they are pillars that you do not see. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding the verse: He says to it pillars, but you do not see them: meaning the pillars. Ibn Jarir narrated from Iyas bin Muawiyah regarding the verse: He said: The sky is vaulted over the earth like a dome. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas: He said: The sky has four angels, each corner has an angel assigned to it. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated regarding his statement: for a specified term, he said: the world. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: He directs the affair, he said: He decrees it alone. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abdullah bin Amr who said: the world is a journey of five hundred years: four hundred years of destruction, and one hundred years of development in the hands of the Muslims, of which the journey of one year is in the hands of one year. A group of the Salaf narrated regarding this estimations for which there is no sound evidence. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ali bin Abi Talib who said: When God created the earth, it trembled and said: O Lord, do you make the children of Adam work on sins and make me commit wickedness? So God sent mountains into it that you see and that you do not see, and its settlement was like trembling flesh. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement: He made therein two mates, he said: a male and a female of every kind. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: He covers the night with the day, meaning that the night covers the day. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, he said: He means the good, fresh land whose vegetation grows by the permission of its Lord, and next to it is the ugly, salty marshland that does not grow, and they are one land, and its water is one thing, salty or fresh, so one of them is preferred over the other. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse, he said: It was read as neighboring, close to each other. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: The land produces sweet things, and the land produces sour things, and they are neighboring tracts watered by one water. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Bara bin Azib regarding his statement: In pairs and not in pairs, he said: The in pair is that which has one origin and is scattered, and the in pair is that which grows alone, and in another version: The in pair of palm trees is attached to the palm tree, and the in pair of palm trees is scattered. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In two rows meaning: palm trees gathered together on one root, and not in two rows meaning: palm trees that are scattered. At-Tirmidhi narrated and classified it as hasan, as did Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And We excel some of them over others in taste, he said: date palms, Persian dates, sweet dates and sour dates. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: This is sour, this is sweet, this is date palms, and this is Persian dates.
13:5: His saying: 5- "And if you are amazed, then be amazed by their statement" meaning if you are amazed, O Muhammad, by their denial of you after you were among the truthful ones in their eyes, then be amazed by their denial of the resurrection. And God Almighty is not permitted to be amazed, because the soul changes with something whose causes are hidden, and he only mentioned that so that his Messenger and his followers would be amazed by it. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, this is also a topic of wonder that they denied the resurrection, and He showed them from the creation of the heavens and the earth what indicates that the resurrection is easier in the ability, and it was said that the verse is about those who deny the Creator: that is, if you are amazed by their denial of the Creator with the clear evidence that the changeable must have a changer, then this is the place of amazement, and the first is more appropriate for His saying: If we are dust, will we then be in a new creation? This sentence is in the nominative case as a substitute for their saying, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as it is the predicate of the saying, and the amazement according to the first is their speech, and according to the second they spoke about that, and the factor in if is what is indicated by His saying: Will we then be in a new creation? which is resurrection or return. And the question from them is for denial that indicates complete exclusion, and the presentation of the circumstance in His saying: In a creation is to emphasize the denial of the resurrection. And likewise the repetition of the hamza in His saying: Will we then be in a new creation. Then when God, the Most High, narrated that about them, He judged them with three things: The first, Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, meaning those who deny His ability to resurrect are the ones who persist in their disbelief and are complete in it. The second, And those are the shackles on their necks, “Shackles” is the plural of ghal, which is a collar that the hand is tied with to the neck, meaning they will be shackled with them on the Day of Resurrection. It was said that the shackles are their evil deeds that are attached to them as collars are attached to necks. The third, And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally, they will never be separated from it under any circumstances. The placement of the separating pronoun indicates that eternity is reserved for those who deny the resurrection.
13:6: 6-"And they urge you to hasten the evil before the good" The evil is the fatal punishment. And the good: wellness and safety. They said this statement because of their extreme denial and their strong determination and their devotion to disbelief. It was said that the meaning of the verse is that they sought the punishment before the good, which is faith. "And there have already been before them examples. The majority read examples with a fatha on the meem and a damma on the triangle, the plural of mithla like samra", which is the punishment. Ibn al-Anbari said: The example is the punishment that remains in the punished person by changing some of his creation, from their saying: Like so-and-so with so-and-so if he disfigured his creation by cutting off his nose, gouging out his eyes, and slitting open his stomach. Al-A'mash read it with a fatha on the meem and a sukoon on the triangle to lighten the weight of the damma. In the language of Tamim, both the meem and the triangle are damma. Its singular, according to their language, is: Mithla, with a damma on the meem and a sukoon on the triangle, like "ghurfa and ghurfaat". It was narrated from Al-A'mash in another narration that he read this letter with a damma on it according to the language of Tamim. Meaning: These people are hastening you to bring down punishment upon them, and punishments have already been inflicted upon those like them who denied before them. So why do they not take heed of them and beware of what has befallen them? The sentence is in the accusative case as a state, and this hastening of these people is in the manner of mockery, like their saying: O God, if this is the truth from You verse, and indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness meaning the possessor of great tolerance for people for their wrongdoing themselves by committing sins and falling into transgressions if they repent from that and return to God, the Most High. The preposition and its object: meaning for their wrongdoing is in the accusative case as a state, meaning the state of their being wrongdoers, and on means with, meaning with their wrongdoing. In the verse there is great good report and great hope, because it is known that a person is not a representative when he is busy with wrongdoing, and for this reason it was said that it is specifically for the sinners among the monotheists, and it was said that what is meant by forgiveness here is delaying the punishment until the Hereafter to match what God narrated about the disbelievers hastening the punishment. As indicated by the sentence mentioned after this verse, And indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty, He punishes the disobedient, lying disbelievers with a severe punishment according to what His will requires in the Hereafter.
13:7: 7- And those who disbelieve say, 'Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?' That is, why was a sign not sent down to him other than the signs he had brought? These disbelievers who say this are the ones who are hastening the punishment. Al-Zajjaj said: They asked for signs other than the ones he brought, so they sought signs like those of Moses and Jesus. Then God the Most High said, You are only a warner, warning them of the Fire, and you have no signs. End quote. This is stubbornness and obstinacy on the part of the disbelievers. Otherwise, God had sent down signs to His Messenger that would suffice some of them. The word you are only a warner was used in the exclusive form to clarify that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to warn the servants and to clarify what they should beware of the consequences of, and that he had nothing else to do with it. He did what he had to do, and he warned with the most eloquent warning, and he did not leave anything that would achieve that without bringing it, clarifying it, and repeating it. May God reward him for his good deeds. And for every people there is a guide, meaning a prophet who calls them to what will guide and direct them, even if guidance does not actually occur to them and they do not accept it. The signs of the messengers are different. One comes with a sign or signs that the other did not bring, according to what God gives him of them. Whoever demands from some of them what others brought has reached a great level of obstinacy. The intended meaning of the signs is nothing but evidence of prophethood, because it is a miracle beyond human ability. This is not specific to one individual among them, nor to specific individuals. It has been said that the meaning is that for every people there is a guide, and He is God, the Almighty, for He is able to do that, and His prophets are only to warn.
13:8: 8- God knows what every female carries The sentence is a new sentence, introduced to clarify His comprehensive knowledge, glory be to Him, and His knowledge of the unseen from which these mentioned matters come. It was said that it is possible that the noble name is the predicate of a deleted subject: i.e. and for every people there is a guide, and He is God, and the sentence He knows what every female carries is an explanation of guide in the last way, and this is very far-fetched, and what is is a relative pronoun: i.e. He knows what every female carries in her womb of a clot, or a lump of flesh, or a male, or a female, or a handsome, or an ugly, or a happy, or a miserable one. It is possible that it is interrogative: i.e. He knows what is in her womb, and in what condition it is. It is possible that it is a source: i.e. He knows her pregnancy and what the wombs decrease and what they increase Ghayd means decrease: i.e. He knows what the wombs decrease, and He knows what they increase. It was said that what is meant is the deficiency of the creation of the pregnancy and its increase, such as the deficiency of a finger or its increase. It was said that what is meant is the deficiency of the pregnancy period to nine months, or its increase. It was said that if a woman menstruates during her pregnancy, that is a deficiency in her child. It was said that ghayd is what the wombs decrease from blood, and az-zadd is what they increase from it. What is in what decreases and what increases includes the three previous aspects in what every female carries. And everything with Him is by measure. That is, everything from the things that include the things mentioned with God Almighty is by measure. And the measure is the measure that God has determined, and this is the meaning of His statement, the Almighty: Indeed, We created all things with measure. That is, all things with God Almighty are running according to His measure that has already been completed and finished, nothing deviates from that.
13:9: 9- The Knower of the Unseen and the Seen meaning the Knower of everything that is absent from the senses, and everything that is seen and present, or everything that is non-existent and existent. There is no objection to interpreting the statement as something more general than that. The Great, the Most High meaning the Great, to whom everything is inferior, the One who is exalted above what the polytheists say, or the One who is superior to everything by His power, greatness, and might.
13:10: Then when He, the Almighty, mentioned that He knows those unseen matters, nothing of them escapes Him, He explained that He knows what they conceal in their souls and what they declare to others, and that this does not differ with Him, so He said: 10- It is the same among you who conceals his speech and he who declares it openly. So He knows what a person conceals just as He knows what he declares openly of good and evil. And His saying: of you is related to it is the same among you who conceals and he who declares openly, or it is the same among you who conceals and he who declares openly, "and he who hides by night," meaning he who hides in the darkness that is at night, hidden from the eyes. It is said that something is hidden and concealed: meaning it is concealed and hidden. "And he who is lost by day," Al-Kisa'i said: "He goes away," and from this is the saying of the poet: Every man approached the fetters of his stallion, and we removed his fetters, so he is a runner. Any gold. Al-Qatibi said: He traveled during the day, quickly disposing of his needs, from their saying: he traveled the water. Al-Asma’i said: He solved his path: meaning his way. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse is the one who speaks loudly, and the one who conceals himself, and the one who is apparent on the roads and the one who hides in the darkness, God knows them all equally, and this is more consistent with the meaning of the verse, as is indicated by the contrast between the one who hides and the one who travels, so the one who is hidden is the one who is concealed, and the one who is prominent is the one who is apparent.
13:11: 11- For Him are successors The pronoun in For Him refers to whoever in His statement: whoever conceals speech, whoever speaks it aloud, and who is concealed: meaning that each of these has successors, and the successors are the ones who alternate, each one of them succeeds the other and is a substitute for him, and they are the guardian angels according to the majority of commentators. Al-Zajjaj said: The successors are angels who come one after the other, and he only said: successors even though the angels are males because a group of angels is called a successor, then he pluralized successors as successors: Al-Farra' mentioned its meaning, and it was said that it was made feminine due to the large number of them like nasaba and alamah. Al-Jawhari said: And the follow-up is the return after the beginning. God the Almighty said: And he turned back, and did not look back. It was read as Mu'aqib, the plural of Mu'aqib. "From before him and from behind him" meaning from before the One who has the successors. What is meant is that the guardian angels are from all sides of him. It was said that what is meant by the successors are the deeds, and the meaning of "from before him and behind him" is: what came before and what came after. "They guard him from the command of God" meaning for the sake of the command of God. It was said that they guard him from despair of God if he sins by asking him to wait and seek forgiveness until he repents. Al-Farra' said: There are two opinions on this: One of them is that it is on the advancement and delay, meaning: He has successors from the command of God who guard him from before him and from behind him. The second is that the fact that the guardians guard him is from what God has commanded. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that they guarded him from the command of God: meaning from what He has commanded them to do, not that they are able to repel the command of God. Ibn Al-Anbari said: There is another opinion on this. It is that min has the meaning of ba: meaning they protect it by the command of God. It was also said that min has the meaning of an: meaning they protect it by the command of God, meaning from God, not from themselves, like His statement: He fed them from hunger meaning from hunger. It was also said that they protect it from the angels of punishment, and it was also said that they protect it from the jinn. Ibn Jarir chose that the mu’aqabat are the processions in front of the princes, meaning that this does not prevent the decree from him. Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people of blessing and well-being until they change what is in themselves of obedience to God. The meaning is that He will not deprive a people of a blessing that He has bestowed upon them until they change what is in themselves of goodness and righteous deeds, or change the nature that God created them with. It was said that what is meant is not that He does not send down punishment on any of His servants until he commits a sin, but rather calamities may befall them due to the sins of others, as in the hadith that “A questioner asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Will we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us? He said: Yes, if evil increases.” And if God intends evil for a people, meaning destruction and punishment, there is no repelling it, meaning there is no turning back. It was also said that the meaning is: If God intends evil for a people, He blinds their hearts until they choose what brings calamity. And they have no protector besides Him, to whom they can turn, so that he can ward off from them the punishment that befalls them from God, the Most High, or a supporter who can aid them and protect them from the punishment of God. The meaning is that there is no repelling of the punishment of God or overturning His judgment. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated from Al-Hasan regarding his statement: And if you are amazed, then their statement is amazed, he said: If you are amazed, O Muhammad, at their denial of you, then their statement is amazed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, he said: If you are amazed, O Muhammad, at their denial, and they saw of God’s power and command, and what He gave them of examples and showed them of the life of the dead and the dead earth, “Then their statement is amazed: ‘When we are dust, shall we then be in a new creation?’” Or do they not see that He created them from a drop of semen? Creation from a drop of semen is more severe than creation from dust and bones. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada regarding his statement: And there have already been examples before them, he said: Punishments. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated from Qatada regarding examples, he said: The events of God among the nations who came before you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, he said: Examples are the punishments that befell the past generations. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab who said: When this verse was revealed: “And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people, despite their wrongdoing. And indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty,” the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Were it not for the pardon and forgiveness of God, no one would enjoy life, and were it not for His threat and punishment, everyone would be tired. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And for every people is a guide, he said: A caller. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide, he said: The warner is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And for every people is a guide, he said: A prophet who calls them to God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: Muhammad is the warner and the guide is God, the Almighty. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid as well. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is the warner and the guide. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah and Abu Ad-Dahha something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Ma`rifah, Ad-Daylami, Ibn Asakir and Ibn An-Najjar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the verse, You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide, was revealed, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) placed his hand on his chest and said: I am the warner, and he pointed with his hand to Ali’s shoulder and said: You are the guide, O Ali, through you the rightly guided will be guided after me.” Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir: This hadith is very objectionable. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Barzah Al-Aslami who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Mardawayh and Ad-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) also something similar. Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id Al-Musnad, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib regarding the verse something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, God knows what every female carries. He said: Every female is from God’s creation. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding the verse, he said: He knows whether it is male or female. And what the wombs absorb he said: It is the woman who sees blood during her pregnancy. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, And what the wombs absorb he said: The exit of blood. And what they increase he said: Its retention. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And what the wombs absorb he said: That she sees blood during her pregnancy. And what they increase he said: In the nine months. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on his authority regarding the verse, he said: It does not increase beyond nine, and does not decrease from nine. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, And what the wombs absorb he said: The miscarriage. And what they increase she does not increase in pregnancy beyond what she absorbed until she gave birth to it completely. Some women carry it for ten months, some for nine months, and some for less. This is the increase and decrease that God mentioned, and He knows all of that. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, he said: The secret and the public. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated regarding his statement, And he who hides by night, he said: He who is stubborn in committing sins. And goes forth by day, he said: He who appears during the day in committing sins. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, And goes forth by day, he said: The apparent. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: He is a suspicious person who hides by night, and if he goes forth during the day, people will see that he is innocent of sin. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the reason for the revelation of this verse was the arrival of Amir ibn al-Tufayl and Arbad ibn Qays to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the famous story, and that when Amir ibn al-Tufayl was struck by a scorpion, the verse was revealed: God knows what every female carries until His saying: successive angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God. He said: The successive angels are by the command of God, guarding Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then he mentioned Arbad ibn Qays and what killed him, and said: It is He who shows you the lightning until His saying: And He is severe in assault. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: successive angels in the verse, he said: This is specifically for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: successive angels guarding him by the command of God. He said: That protection is by the command of God by the command of God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him: From the command of God. He said: By the permission of God. Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatada something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: The one who has authority has guards who guard him from before him and behind him. He says: They guard him from my command, for if I intend evil for a people, there is no repelling it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated from him regarding the verse: The kings appoint guards who guard him from before him and behind him and to his right and to his left to protect him from being killed. Have you not heard that God says: If God intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it. That is, if He intends evil, the guards will not help them at all. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ikrimah regarding the verse: These are the princes. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas: They are the angels who follow at night and write down what is upon the son of Adam. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: Angels guard him from before him and from behind him, so when God’s decree comes, they leave him alone. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ali regarding the verse, he said: There is no servant except that there are angels with him guarding him from a wall falling on him, or from him retreating into a well, or from a wild animal eating him, or from drowning or burning him, so when the decree comes, they leave him alone with the decree. Many hadiths have been narrated mentioning the guardians assigned to a person, mentioned in the books of hadith.
13:12: When God Almighty frightened His servants by sending down something that cannot be averted, He followed it up with things that are hoped for in some ways and feared in others, which are lightning, clouds, thunder, and thunderbolts. The explanation of these words and their causes was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah: 12- fear and hope has been disputed. Some say it is a source: that is, so that you may fear fear and hope hope. Some say it is a cause by estimating the intention of fear and hope so that the doer of the cause-based verb and the doer of the object for it do not differ, or it is a state of lightning, or of the addressees by estimating those with fear. Others say it is not needed. It has been said that what is meant by fear is what results from lightning, and by hope is what results from rain. Al-Zajjaj said: Fear is for the traveler because of what he is harmed by from the rain, and hope is for the resident, because if he sees lightning he hopes for the rain which is the cause of fertility. And He creates the heavy clouds is the definition of the genus and the singular is cloud, and heavy is the plural of heavy. What is meant is that God Almighty makes the clouds that He creates heavy by what He puts in them of water.
13:13: 13- And the thunder glorifies Him with praise meaning the thunder itself glorifies God with praise: meaning immersed in His praise, and this is not unlikely, and there is no objection to God uttering that and there is nothing but glorifies Him with praise. As for the interpretation of thunder as an angel from the angels, there is no improbability in that. And its mention is in the singular with the mention of the angels after it for more specialness to it, and attention to it, and it was said that what is meant is and the hearers of the thunder glorify: meaning they say: Glory be to God and praise be to God and the angels out of fear of Him meaning and the angels glorify out of fear of God, the Most High, and it was said out of fear of the thunder. A group of commentators have mentioned that these angels are the helpers of thunder, and that God, the Most High, has made helpers for it and sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills of His creation, destroying them, and the context of these matters here is for the purpose for which the verses before it were cited. It is an indication of the perfection of His power, And they dispute about God. The pronoun refers to the unbelievers addressed in His statement, It is He who shows you the lightning. That is, these unbelievers, with these signs that God showed them, dispute about the affair of God, the Exalted, so they deny the resurrection at times and hasten the punishment at other times, and they deny the messengers and disobey God. This sentence is in the accusative case as a state, and it is permissible for it to be a new sentence. And He is severe in penalty. Ibn al-A’rabi said: The penalty is deceit, and the deceit from God is planning with truth. An-Nahhas said: The deceit from God is delivering the harm to the one who deserves it without him realizing it. Al-Azhari said: The penalty is strength and severity, and the mīm is original, and I did not make someone suffer a hardship, which of us is more severe. Abu Ubayd said: The penalty is punishment and the harm. Az-Zajjaj said: It is said I did not make him suffer a hardship if you fought him until it became clear which of you was more severe, and the penalty in the language is severity. Ibn Qutaybah said: That is, severe in plotting. Its origin is from the trick of making the meem like the meem of place, and its origin is from the universe, then it is said tamkanat. Al-Azhari said: Ibn Qutaybah made a mistake that the meem in it is extra, rather it is original, and if you see the letter in the example of fa’al that begins with a kasra meem, then it is original like mahād, malāk, murās, and other letters. Al-A’raj read and it is severe in difficulty with a fathah on the meem. This reading has been interpreted as the year. The Companions and Followers have eight opinions regarding the interpretation of the impossible here: the first is enmity, the second is change, the third is taking, the fourth is hatred, the fifth is force, the sixth is anger, the seventh is destruction, and the eighth is deception.
13:14: 14- His is the call of truth Adding the call to the truth for the sake of association: meaning the call associated with the truth that is specific to him in which falsehood has no influence in any way, as it is said the word of truth, and the meaning is that it is a call that is answered and occurs in its place, not like a call from someone other than him. It was said that the truth is God, the Most High, and the meaning is that God, the Most High, has the call of the one called upon, the truth, and He is the One who hears and answers. It was said that what is meant by the call of truth here is the word of monotheism and sincerity, and the meaning is: God is the One from His creation that they should make Him One and be sincere to Him. It was said that the call of truth is His supplication, the Most High, when there is fear, for He does not call upon anyone other than Him, as God, the Most High, said: Those you call upon except Him have gone astray. It was said that the call is worship, for the worship of God is the truth and honesty. And those they call upon besides Him - they do not respond to them with anything meaning, and the gods they call upon - meaning the infidels besides God - the Almighty - do not respond to them with anything they ask of them, whatever it may be, except a response like the response of water to someone who stretches his hands towards it from afar, for it does not answer him, because it is inanimate and does not feel its need for it, nor does it know that he asked it to reach its mouth. For this reason, He said, And it will not reach it meaning it will reach it. Al-Zajjaj said: Except as the one who stretches his hands towards the water is answered, calling the water to his mouth, and the water does not respond. God, the Exalted, knows that their call to idols is like the call of a thirsty person to water, calling it to reach his mouth, and the water will not reach him. It was said that the meaning is: It is like someone who stretches his hands towards the water to grasp it, but nothing of it reaches his hand. The Arabs used to give an example of someone who strives for something he cannot attain, by grasping water, as the poet said: So, because of the love that was between us, I became like someone holding water in his hand. The other said: Whoever feels safe from this world will be like someone holding onto water whose fingers betray him. Al-Farra’ said: What is meant by water here is the water of the well because it is a source of water, and he likened it to someone who extends his hand into the well without a bribe. God Almighty gave this as an example for someone who calls upon other than idols. And the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but error. That is, that supplication leads them astray, so they do not find anything in it, and it does not benefit them in any way, rather it is lost and gone.
13:15: 15- And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly. If what is meant by prostration is its true meaning, which is placing the forehead on the ground to glorify with submission and humility, then this is clear in the case of the believers, the angels, and the Muslims among the jinn. As for the disbelievers, it is not correct to interpret prostration in this way in their case. Rather, the prostration mentioned in the verse must be taken to mean that God has the right to prostrate and it is obligatory so that prostration is reached in action and otherwise, or prostration must be interpreted as submission, because even if the disbelievers do not prostrate to God, the Most High, they are subject to His command and His rule over them in health and sickness, life and death, poverty and wealth. The intent of this meaning is indicated by His statement: willingly and unwillingly, because the disbelievers submit unwillingly just as the believers submit willingly, and they are both in the accusative case as a source: meaning submission willingly and submission unwillingly, or as a state: meaning obedient and unwilling. Al-Farraa said: The verse is specific to the believers, for they prostrate willingly, and some of the disbelievers prostrate under compulsion and fear, like the hypocrites, so the verse is applied to these people. It was also said that the verse is about the believers, for some of them prostrate willingly and prostration is not difficult for them, and some of them are difficult for them because adhering to the obligation is hardship, but they bear the hardship out of faith in God and sincerity to Him. And their shadows in the mornings and the evenings. Their shadows is the plural of shadow, and what is meant by it is the shadow of the person who follows him, made prostrating by his prostration since it has become necessary for him and inseparable from him. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Al-Anbari said: It is not far-fetched that God created for the shadows minds with which they prostrate to God, the Most High, just as He made for the mountains minds until they were occupied with glorifying Him. So the shadow of the believer prostrates to God willingly, and the shadow of the disbeliever prostrates to God unwillingly. And He specified the mornings and evenings for the one who remembers God because the shadows appear more in them, and they are a circumstance for the estimated al-Sajdah 32:that is, their shadows prostrate at these two times. The interpretation of morning and evening has been presented in Al-A’raf. In the meaning of this verse, the Almighty said: Have they not seen what God has created of things, whose shadows extend to the right and the left, prostrating to God, while they are humbled? And He mentioned those in the heavens and the earth, giving precedence to rational beings over others, and because the prostration of others is dependent on their prostration. What supports the interpretation of prostration as submission is what indicates that it is given precedence over the action of exclusivity, for the prostration of the infidels to their idols is known, and they do not submit to them as they submit to God in matters that they acknowledge to themselves are from God, such as creation, life, death, and the like.
13:16: 16- "Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to ask the infidels who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth? Then when they acknowledged and confessed to that as God the Almighty narrated in His saying: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, 'Then the Exalted in Might, the Knowing' created them, and His saying: And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, 'God', He ordered His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer, so he said: "Say: God," so it was as if he narrated their answer and what they believed, because they might have faltered in their answer out of fear of what would be required of them. Then He ordered him to make the argument obligatory upon them and rebuke them, so He said: "Say: Have you taken protectors besides Him?" The question is for denial: that is, if the Lord of the heavens and the earth is God as you acknowledge and confess as God the Almighty narrated about you in His saying: "Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne? * They will say: 'To God.'" So why have you taken for yourselves besides Him helpless protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm? How can you expect benefit or harm from them when they do not possess them for themselves? The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. Then God, the Most High, gave them an example and commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say it to them, saying: “Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?” That is, are the blind, who is the disbeliever, equal in his religion, who is the one who believes in God, the One Who has faith in Him, equal in it? The former is ignorant of what is required of him and what is binding upon him, while the latter is knowledgeable about it. Ibn Muhaysin, Abu Bakr, Al-A’mash, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read Or are darkness and light equal? with a ta’, while the rest read it with a ta’, and Abu Ubayd chose the second reading. What is meant by darkness is disbelief, and by light is faith. The question is for rebuke and reproach: how can they be equal while there is a difference between them like that between the blind and the seeing, and between darkness and light? He made light singular and darkness plural, because the path of truth is one and does not differ, while the paths of falsehood are many and countless. Or have they made for God partners who created like His creation? “Or” is the disconnected particle that means rather and the hamza: meaning, rather have they made for God partners who created like His creation? The question is to deny the occurrence. Ibn al-Anbari said: Its meaning is, have they made for God partners who created like what God created, so that the creation of the partners resembled God’s creation in their eYa-Sin 36:meaning, the matter is not like this so that it would be confusing to them, but if they thought with their minds, they would find that God is the One who is alone in creation, and the rest of the partners do not create anything. The phrase created like His creation is in the accusative case as an attribute of partners. Meaning: They did not make partners for God who were described as having been created like His creation, so that creation became similar for this reason to them so that they deserved to be worshipped by them. Rather, they made partners for Him in the form of idols and the like, and they were far removed from being like that. Then God, the Most High, commanded him to explain the truth to them and guide them to what is right, so He said: “Say: God is the Creator of all things,” whatever they may be, for no one else has any share in that in any way. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that He is the Creator of everything that could be created. Do you not see that He, the Most High, is something and He is not created? And He is the One, meaning the One who is unique in Lordship, the Subduer of everything other than Him, so everything other than Him is a subject, subdued, and overcome.
13:17: Then the Almighty gave another example of the truth and its people, and of falsehood and its claimants, saying: 17- "He sent down water from the sky meaning from its direction, and the indefinite article is for multiplication or quality, and the valleys flowed" is the plural of valley, which is every space between two mountains or the like. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: We do not know of a fa'il that is pluralized as af'alah except this, and it seems that it was based on fa'il, so it was with af'alah like jarib and ajribah, just as fa'il was based on fa'il, so it was pluralized as af'al like yateem and ayyataam and sharif and ashraf, like ashab and ansar in sahib and naasir. He said: And in His saying: "and the valleys flowed" there is an expansion: meaning its water flowed. He said: The meaning of "according to its amount" is according to its water, because the valleys did not flow according to their own amount. Al-Wahidi said: “The measure is the amount of something, and the meaning is: its amount of water, if the valley is small the water will be small and if it is wide it will be large.” He said in Al-Kashshaf: Its amount is the amount that God knows is beneficial to those upon whom the rain is rained on and not harmful. Ibn Al-Anbari said: He likened the revelation of the Qur’an, which includes guidance and clarification, to the descent of rain, as the benefit of the revelation of the Qur’an is general, just as the benefit of the descent of rain is general. He likened valleys to hearts, as water is hidden in valleys, just as the Qur’an and faith are hidden in the hearts of believers. Then the torrent carried a swelling foam. Foam is the white, rising foam on the surface of the torrent, and it is called scum and foam. Rabi is the high, rising foam above the water. Al-Zajjaj said: It is floating above the water. Another said: It is the excess due to its swelling, from riba yarbu, if it increases. What is meant by this is likening disbelief to the foam that rises on the water, as it disappears and sticks to the sides of the valley and is carried by the winds, so disbelief disappears and disappears. The first example was completed, then the Almighty explained in mentioning the second example, saying, And from that which they kindle in the Fire, “from” is for the beginning of the goal: meaning, and from it arises foam like the foam of water, or for partiality, meaning: and some of it is foam like it, and the pronoun refers to the people, it was implied despite not having been mentioned previously because it is clear, this is according to the reading of they kindle with the lower letter, and Hamid, Ibn Muhaysin, Al-A’mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read it with it. The rest read it with the higher letter as addressing, and Abu Ubaid chose the first reading. Meaning: And from what you kindle in the fire, it melts from the melted, pounded bodies, seeking adornment, meaning to seek to make adornments with which you adorn yourself and beautify yourself, such as gold and silver, or goods, meaning or to seek goods that you enjoy from vessels and tools made of iron, brass, copper, and lead, scum like it, what is meant by the foam here is impurity, for it rises above what has been melted from those bodies, just as foam rises on water, so the pronoun in scum like it refers to the rising foam, and the rising of foam is in the beginning and its predicate is from what they kindle. Thus does God set forth the truth and falsehood, meaning like that wonderful setting, God sets forth the example of the truth and the example of falsehood. Then he began to divide the example and said: As for the foam, it goes away as scum, it is said that the valley was thrown away with filth and foam. Al-Farra’ said: scum is throwing, it is said that the valley was thrown away with filth, scum is like scum. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said the same, and Abu Ubaidah narrated that he heard Ru’bah recite Jafal. Abu Ubaidah said: It is said that the pot ajfalat if it throws up its foam, and the wind ajfalat al-sahab if it cuts it. Abu Hatim said: It is not recited according to Ru’bah’s recitation, because he used to eat mice. Know that the similarity between the two foams, the foam carried by the flood and the foam that rises above the crushed bodies, is that when the dust of the earth mixes with the water and carries it with it, it becomes foam rising above it. Likewise, what is lit on fire until it melts from the crushed bodies, its origin is from the minerals that grow in the earth and mix with the dust, so when it is melted, that dust that mixed with it becomes impurity rising above it. As for that which benefits people from them, which is pure water and the dissolved, pure impurity, it remains in the earth meaning it is fixed in it. As for the water, it flows through the veins of the earth and people benefit from it. As for that which is melted from those bodies, it is made into ornaments and goods. These are two examples that God Almighty has given for truth and falsehood. He says: Even if falsehood appears over the truth in some cases and rises above it, God Almighty will annihilate it and invalidate it and make the outcome for truth and its people like the foam that rises above the water and the water throws it out and it disappears, and like the impurity of these bodies, for even if it rises above them, The bellows throw it and push it, this is like falsehood, as for the water that benefits people and grows pastures, it remains in the earth, and likewise the pure part of these bodies, it remains pure without any impurity in it, and it is like the truth. Al-Zajjaj said: The example of the believer and his belief and the benefit of faith is like this water that is beneficial in the plants of the earth and the life of everything, and like the benefit of silver and gold and other jewels because they all remain beneficial, and the example of the disbeliever and his disbelief is like the foam that disappears as scum, and like the dross of iron and what the fire produces of dirt of silver and gold that is not beneficial. We have narrated from Ibn al-Anbari in what came before that he likened the revelation of the Qur’an to the end of what we mentioned, so he made that an example that God struck for the Qur’an, Thus does God present parables, meaning like that wondrous striking, God strikes parables in every chapter to perfect His care for His servants and be kind to them, and this is an emphasis on His saying: Thus does God strike the truth and falsehood.
13:18: Then the Almighty explained who among His servants He gave the example of truth and the example of falsehood, so He said about those for whom He gave the example of truth: 18- For those who responded to their Lord meaning they responded to His call when He called them to His Oneness, to believe in His prophets, and to act according to His laws, and the best is an attribute of an omitted description: meaning the best reward, which is Paradise. And the Almighty said about those for whom He gave the example of falsehood and those who did not respond to His call to what He called them to, and the relative is the subject and its predicate is the conditional sentence, which is If they had all that is in the earth of the types of money that the servants own and collect so that nothing of it leaves their possession and the like of it with it meaning the like of all that is in the earth existing with it and joined to it they would ransom themselves with it meaning with the sum of what was mentioned, which is what is in the earth and the like of it. Meaning: To save them from the great torment and tremendous terror they are in. Then God Almighty explained what He has prepared for them, saying, Those meaning those who did not respond, for them is an evil reckoning. Al-Zajjaj said: Because their disbelief rendered their deeds worthless. Another said: An evil reckoning is the discussion of it. It was said that it is when a man is held accountable for all of his sins and nothing of it is forgiven. And their refuge is Hell meaning they will return to it. And an evil resting place meaning the resting place in which they will settle. The one specifically blamed is omitted. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: It is He who shows you the lightning, causing fear and hope. He said: Fear for the traveler who fears its harm and hardship, and hope for the resident who hopes for God’s provision and hopes for the blessing and benefit of rain. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Fear for the people of the sea and hope for the people of the land. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: Fear is what is feared from thunderbolts and hope is rain. Abd Bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Kharaiti in Makarim Al-Akhlaq and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ali Bin Abi Talib who said: Lightning is whips of fire in the hands of the angels of the clouds with which they drive the clouds. A group of the Salaf narrated what agrees with this and what contradicts it, and perhaps we have already mentioned something of that in Surat Al-Baqarah. Ahmad narrated on the authority of a sheikh from Banu Ghaffar who had accompanied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God creates the clouds and they speak the most beautiful speech and laugh the most beautiful laugh. It was said that what is meant by their speaking is thunder and what is meant by their laughter is lightning.
