It was proven by Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i in al-Yawm wa al-Laylah and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard… Thunder and lightning He said: O God, do not kill us with Your wrath, nor destroy us with Your punishment, and pardon us before that. Al-Aqili, who declared it weak, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God creates the clouds and then sends down water into them. There is nothing more beautiful than His laughter, and there is nothing more beautiful than His speech. His speech is thunder and His laughter is lightning.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, who was not an Ansari, asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the origin of the clouds. He said: “There is an angel assigned who gathers the distant and joins the near. In his hand is a whip. When he raises it, it flashes, when he rebukes, it thunders, and when he strikes, it is struck with a thunderbolt.” Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym in Al-Dala’il and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “The Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Abu Al-Qasim, we ask you about five things. If you inform us of them, we will know that you are a prophet and we will follow you. So he took from them what Israel took from his sons when he said: God is the witness over what we say. He said: Bring them. They said: Tell us about the sign of a prophet? He said: His eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep. They said: Tell us how a woman is made feminine and how she is made masculine? He said: The two waters meet, so if…” If a man's semen rises above a woman's semen, she becomes a male. If a woman's semen rises above a man's semen, she becomes a female. They said: Tell us about what Israel forbade himself? He said: He used to suffer from a sore throat, and he did not find anything suitable for him except the milk of such and such - meaning camels, so he forbade their meat. They said: You have spoken the truth. They said: Tell us, what is this thunder? He said: An angel of God's angels who is in charge of the clouds, in whose hand is a whip of fire with which he drives the clouds, driving them where God commands him. They said: What is this sound that we hear? He said: His voice. They said: You have spoken the truth, there remains only one thing, and it is the one we will follow if you tell us. There is no prophet but that he has an angel who brings him report. So tell us who is your companion? He said: Gabriel. They said: That Gabriel descends with destruction, fighting and torment, our enemy. If you had said: Michael who descends with mercy, plants and rain, it would have been him. So God revealed: “Say: Who is an enemy to Gabriel?” to the end of the verse. Al-Bukhari narrated in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in Al-Matar, and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that whenever he heard the sound of thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him Whom you glorify. He said: Thunder is an angel who calls out for rain as a shepherd calls out to his sheep. Something similar to this has been narrated on his authority from various chains of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that thunder is the voice of an angel, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Thunder is an angel whose name is Al-Ra’d, and this voice of his is his glorification. When his rebuke becomes intense, the clouds clash and become inflamed from fear of him, and lightning bolts emerge from between them. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Kharaiti and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Jawni, who said: Seas of fire below the Throne are formed from it. Thunderbolts. Abu Sheikh narrated from Al-Suddi who said: Thunderbolts are fire. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Sheikh narrated from Ibn Abbas, And He is severe in punishment, he said: severe in strength. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ali who said: severe in taking. Ibn Jarir and Abu Sheikh narrated from him regarding His statement, His is the call of truth, he said: monotheism: there is no god but God. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Sheikh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat through various chains from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, The call of truth, he said: the testimony that there is no god but God. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ali regarding His statement, Except like one who stretches out his hands toward water to reach his mouth, but it will not reach it, he said: a thirsty man would stretch out his hand to the well so that the water would rise to him, but it would not reach it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Sheikh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: This is like the polytheist who worships someone other than God, so his example is like the thirsty man who looks at his shadow in the water from afar. And he wants to take it but he is not able to. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated from him regarding his statement: Are the blind and the seeing equal? He said: The believer and the disbeliever. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh also narrated from him regarding his statement: He sends down water from the sky verse. He said: This is a parable that God has given, and hearts can bear it according to their certainty and doubt. As for doubt, action is of no benefit with it, but as for certainty, God benefits its people with it, and it is His statement: As for the foam, it vanishes as cast-off, which is doubt. But that which benefits people remains on the earth, which is certainty. Just as jewelry is placed in fire and its pure part is taken and its impurity is left, so God accepts certainty and leaves doubt. And these also narrated from him: Then valleys flow according to their capacity, he said: The small is according to its smallness and the large is according to its greatness.
13:19: The hamza in His statement: 19- Is he who knows is to denounce those who imagine the similarity between the one who knows, which God Almighty revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the truth in which there is no doubt or suspicion, which is the Qur’an, and the one who is blind and does not know that, for the situation between them is very far apart, like the distance between water and foam, and between filth and pure from those bodies. Then God Almighty explained that only people of sound minds can understand the difference between the two positions and the disparity between the two ranks, so He said: Only those of understanding will remember.
13:20: Then he described them with these praiseworthy descriptions, saying: 20- Those who fulfill the covenant of God meaning the covenants they made between themselves and their Lord, or between themselves and the servants and do not break the contract which they have bound themselves with, and confirmed with faith and the like. This is a generalization after specification, because everything that the servant has obligated upon himself, such as vows and the like, falls under the covenant. It is possible that the matter is the opposite, so it is from specification after generalization, so that what is meant by the covenant is all of God’s covenants, which are His commands and prohibitions that He has commanded His servants to do, and what is included in that are the obligations that the servant binds himself to, and what is meant by the covenant is what God took from His servants when He brought them out from the loins of Adam in the world of atoms mentioned in His Almighty’s saying: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam (al-An’am 2:10).
13:21: 21- And those who maintain what God has commanded to be maintained its apparent meaning is to include everything that God has commanded to be maintained and forbidden to be severed from the rights of God and the rights of His servants, and maintaining kinship ties is included under that primarily, and many commentators have limited it to maintaining kinship ties, and the wording is broader than that and they fear their Lord fearing that He will make them do what is obligatory and avoid what is not permissible and they fear the evil of the reckoning which is the investigation and discussion of the servant, so whoever is questioned about the reckoning will be punished, and it is right for this fear that they should hold themselves accountable before they are held accountable.
13:22: 22- And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord It was said that it is a new statement, and it was said that it is connected to what preceded it and that it is expressed in the past tense to draw attention to the fact that it should be achieved, and what is meant by patience is patience in doing what God has commanded, and avoiding what He has forbidden, and it was said that it is in calamities and misfortunes, and the meaning of that patience being for the sake of God is that it is purely for Him, without any taint for anyone else. And establish prayer means that they perform it at its times according to what God Almighty has prescribed in its remembrances and pillars with humility and sincerity, and what is meant by it are the obligatory prayers, and it was said that it is more general than that. And spend from what We have provided them means that they spend some of what We have provided them, and what is meant by secret is voluntary charity, and public is obligatory charity, and it was said that secret is for someone who is not known for money, or is not accused of abandoning zakat, and public is for someone who is known for money or is accused of abandoning Zakat: And they repel evil with good means they repel the evil of the one who wronged them by doing good to him, as in the Almighty’s saying: Repel evil with that which is better, or they repel evil with good deeds, or evil with good, or injustice with forgiveness, or sin with repentance. There is nothing to prevent the verse from being interpreted to include all of these matters, and the reference in His saying: Those to those described with the aforementioned attributes for them is the final home The final home is a source like the consequence, and what is meant by the final home is this world, and its final home is Paradise. It was said that what is meant by the final home is the Hereafter, and its final home is Paradise for the obedient, and the Fire for the disobedient.
13:23: 23- Gardens of Eden which they shall enter instead of the final abode, meaning for them are the Gardens of Eden. It is permissible for it to be a subject, and its predicate is they shall enter them. The origin of Eden is residence, then it became a proper noun for a garden of the gardens. Al-Qushayri said: The Gardens of Eden: the middle of Paradise, its reed, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful. However, in Sahih Al-Bukhari and others, If you ask God, ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise, and the highest part of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow. And whoever was righteous among their fathers includes fathers and mothers, and their wives and their offspring is in apposition to the pronoun in they enter, and this is permissible to separate the conjoined and the conjoined to: that is, and their wives and offspring will enter it. The mention of righteousness is evidence that no one will enter Paradise except those who are like that from among the relatives of those people, and merely being from the fathers or husbands or offspring without righteousness is of no benefit. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate that is, from all the gates of the houses in which they live, or what is meant by every gate are the gates of gifts and presents from God Almighty.
13:24: 24- "Peace be upon you" meaning saying "Peace be upon you": meaning you were saved from the calamities or safety continued for you because of your patience meaning because of your patience and it is related to peace: meaning you only obtained this safety through your patience or related to upon you, or to something omitted: meaning this honor is because of your patience or instead of the hardships of patience that you endured so excellent is the final home God Almighty came with this sentence that includes praise for what He gave them of the final home mentioned previously for the sake of encouragement and excitement.
13:25: Then he followed the conditions of the happy ones with the conditions of the wretched ones, saying: 25- And those who break the covenant of God after ratifying it and sever that which God has commanded to be joined The explanation of not breaking and not severing has already passed, so the explanation of breaking and severing is known from them, and he did not address the negation of fear and dread from them and what comes after them from the previous descriptions because they are included in breaking and severing and spread corruption on the earth through disbelief and committing sins and harming lives and wealth those who are described with these reprehensible characteristics for them because of that is the curse meaning expulsion and banishment from the mercy of God, the Most High and for them is the evil home meaning the evil consequence of the worldly home, which is the Fire or the torment of the Fire. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the words of God the Almighty: Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth? He said: These are people who benefited from what they heard from the Book of God and understood and comprehended it like one who is blind He said: about the truth so he does not see it or comprehend it Only those of understanding will remember So he explained who they are? He said: Those who fulfill the covenant of God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Those of understanding He said: He who has a mind: meaning intellect. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada that God mentioned fulfilling the covenant and the pact in twenty-odd verses of the Quran. Al-Khatib and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, righteousness and kinship will lighten the evil of the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And those who join what God has commanded to be joined and fear their Lord and dread the evil of the reckoning. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: And those who maintain what God has commanded to be maintained meaning belief in the prophets and all the books and fear their Lord meaning they fear severing what God has commanded to be maintained and fear the evil of the reckoning meaning the severity of the reckoning. There are many hadiths that have been narrated about maintaining family ties and the prohibition of severing them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, And they repel evil with good, meaning they repel evil with good. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding his statement, Gardens of Eden, he said: The two sides of Paradise, meaning its middle. Abd Ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that Umar said to Ka’b, What is Eden? He said, It is a palace in Paradise that none will enter except a prophet, a truthful person, a martyr or a just judge. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali, who said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘The Garden of Eden is a branch that God planted with His hand, then He said to it, “Be,” and it was.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, And those who were righteous among their fathers, he said, Those who believed in this world. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Abu Imran al-Joni regarding his statement: “Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured,” he said: for your religion. Then excellent is the final home, he said: excellent is what God has granted you in return from this world in Paradise. Ahmad, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilya, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu`ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The first of God’s creation to enter Paradise will be the poor emigrants who will fill the gaps and protect against hardships. One of them will die with a need in his chest that he cannot fulfill, so God will say to whomever He wills of His angels: ‘Go to them and greet them.’ The angels will say: ‘Our Lord, we are the inhabitants of Your heaven and the best of Your creation. Do You command us to go to these people and greet them?’ God will say: ‘Indeed, these are My servants who used to worship Me and not associate anything with Me. They will fill the gaps and protect against hardships.’ One of them will die with a need in his chest that he cannot fulfill, so the angels will come to them at that time and enter upon them from every gate: ‘Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. Excellent is the final home.’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, “The believer will be reclining on a couch when he enters Paradise, and with him will be two rows of servants, and at the edge of the rows there will be a gate with doors. An angel will come and ask permission, and the one closest to him will say to the one next to him: An angel is asking permission, and the one next to him will say: An angel is asking permission, until he reaches the believer, and he will say: Give him permission, and the one next to him will say to the one next to him: Give him permission, until he reaches the one closest to the believer, who is at the door, and it will be opened for him, so he will enter and greet him, then he will leave.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And for them is an evil home, meaning an evil end.
13:26: When God the Almighty mentioned the fate of the polytheists by saying: And for them is the worst home, someone might say: We see many of them whom God has provided with provision and expanded it for them, so He answered that by saying: 26- God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it He may expand provision for whomever He wills and restrict it for whomever He wills as a trial and test, and expansion does not indicate honor nor restriction indicates humiliation, and the meaning of restriction is restriction. And from it - and whoever has his provision restricted - meaning restriction, and it was said that the meaning of restriction is: He gives according to what is sufficient, and the meaning of the verse is that He alone is the doer of that and is able to do it and no one else and they rejoiced in the life of this world meaning the polytheists of Mecca rejoiced in the world and were ignorant of what is with God, it was said that there is an inversion in this verse. The estimation: Those who break the covenant of God after its ratification and sever what God has commanded to be joined and spread corruption on earth and rejoice in the life of this world, so and rejoice is connected to spoil. “And the life of this world is not compared to the Hereafter except enjoyment,” meaning it is nothing but something that is enjoyed. It was said that enjoyment is one of the provisions like a bowl and a sugar bowl and the like. It was said that the meaning is: a small, passing thing, from the pleasures of the day: if it rises, it must disappear. It was said that it is provisions like the provisions of the rider, which he supplies himself with from it until the Hereafter.
13:27: 27- And those who disbelieve say, 'Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?' That is, those polytheists from Mecca say, Why was a sign not sent down to Muhammad from his Lord? The explanation of this was presented earlier, and it was repeated in several places. Say, 'Indeed, God misguides whom He wills.' God, the Exalted, commanded him to answer them with this, which is that misguidance is by the will of God, the Exalted. Whoever He wills to misguide will go astray, just as those who say, Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord? "And He guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]" went astray. Or to Islam, or to His side, the Almighty and Majestic, whoever turns back: meaning whoever returns to God with repentance and abandoning what he was doing, and the origin of turning back is entering into a turn of goodness, this is what Al-Naysaburi said, and the place of those who believed is the accusative as a substitute for his saying whoever turns back meaning that they are those whom God guided and turned back to Him, and it is possible that those who believed is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning they are those who believed, or it is accusative as praise.
13:28: 28- And their hearts are reassured by the remembrance of God meaning they are calmed and comforted by the remembrance of God, the Most High, with their tongues, such as reciting the Qur'an, glorifying, praising, declaring God's Oneness, or by hearing that from others. God, the Most High, called the Qur'an a remembrance, saying: And this is a blessed remembrance which We have sent down, and He said: Indeed, it is We who sent down the remembrance. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, when God alone is mentioned, they believe in it without doubt, unlike those who described it by saying: And when God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter are filled with disgust. It was said that their hearts are reassured by the oneness of God, and it was said that what is meant by remembrance here is obedience, and it was said by the promise of God, and it was said by swearing by God, so if his opponent swears by God, his heart is calmed, and it was said by mentioning His mercy, and it was said by mentioning His evidence indicating His Oneness. Verily, by the remembrance of God alone without others hearts are reassured and looking at the creations of God, the Most High, and the wonders of His creation, even if it benefits reassurance in The sentence, but it is not like this reassurance, and also considering miracles is one of the things that humans cannot bear, so its benefit for reassurance is not like the benefit of mentioning God, so this is the aspect of what this structure benefits from restriction.
13:29: 29- Those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is bliss and a good return. The relative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is the supplication clause, which is bliss for them according to the well-known interpretation. It is permissible for the relative pronoun to be in the accusative case of praise, and bliss for them is the predicate of a deleted subject. It is permissible for the relative pronoun to be a substitute for the hearts with a deleted complement: meaning the hearts of those who believe. Abu Ubaidah, Al-Zajjaj and the linguists said: bliss is a verb from good. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Its interpretation is a pleasant state. It was said that bliss is a tree in Paradise, and it was said that it is Paradise, and it was said that it is an orchard in the language of India. It was said that the meaning of bliss for them is: good for them, and it was said that it is good for them, and it was said that it is an honor for them, and it was said that it is a blessing for them. Al-Nahhas said: These sayings are close, and the original is good, so the ya became a waw because of its sukoon and the damma of what precedes it, and the lam in them is for clarification like sakya lak and raiya lak. And it was read as Hasan Ma’ab in the accusative and nominative cases, from ‘aba, which means to return: meaning, and Hasan is the return, which is the afterlife.
13:30: 30- Thus have We sent you to a nation before which there have been nations meaning, like that great sending that includes the dazzling miracle, We have sent you, O Muhammad. It has been said that the favor upon the one to whom Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent is like the favor upon the one to whom the prophets were sent before him. The meaning of in a nation before which there have been nations is in a century before which there have been centuries, or in a group of people before which there have been groups. That you may recite to them what We have revealed to you meaning that you may recite the Qur'an to them. And the state while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful meaning the One with abundant mercy for His servants, and from His mercy to them is sending messengers to them and revealing books to them, as the Almighty said: And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds. The phrase Say, He is my Lord is a new sentence with the estimation of a question, as if they said: And who is the Most Merciful? So He, the Almighty, said: Say, O Muhammad, He is my Lord, meaning my Creator. There is no god but Him, meaning none deserves to be worshipped or believed in except Him. In Him I have relied, in all my affairs, and to Him, not to anyone else, I turn, meaning my repentance. In it is an allusion to the infidels and an urging for them to return to God and repent from infidelity and enter Islam. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Sabit regarding his statement: And the life of this world is not compared to the Hereafter except provision, he said: Like the provisions of a shepherd, which his family provides him with, a handful of dates, or some flour, or something to drink milk with. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: In the old days, a man would go out with his camels or sheep and say to his family, Prohibit me, so they would provide him with a piece of bread or dates. This is an example that God has given for the world. Al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slept on a mat and got up with marks on his side. We said, O Messenger of God, what if we were to make a mat for you?” He said, What do I have to do with the world? I am in the world like a rider who takes shelter under a tree, then he moves on and leaves it. Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Al-Mustawrid, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The world is not compared to the Hereafter except like one of you dipping his finger into the sea, so let him see what he brings back. And he pointed with his index finger. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And their hearts are assured by the remembrance of God, he said: They were delighted by it and found comfort in it. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse: If he swears to them by God, they are truthful. Verily, by the remembrance of God hearts are assured, he said: They are calmed. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: By Muhammad and his companions. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to his companions: ‘Verily, by the remembrance of God hearts are assured,’ do you know what that means? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: He who loves God and His Messenger and loves my companions.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali that when this verse was revealed, ‘Verily, by the remembrance of God hearts are assured,’ the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: That is he who loves God and His Messenger, and loves my family sincerely and not lying, and loves the believers, whether present or absent. Verily, by the remembrance of God they love one another.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Blessings for them, he said: Happiness and delight to the eye. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: Blessings for them, he said: Yes, what is for them? It has been narrated from a group of the Salaf similar to what we have mentioned of the sayings, and the most likely interpretation of the verse is what was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Utbah ibn Abd, who said: “A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, is there fruit in Paradise? He said: Yes, there is a tree in it called Tuba.” The hadith. Ahmad, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, and Al-Khatib in his history narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “A man said: O Messenger of God, blessed is he who sees you and believes in you. He said: Blessed is he who believes in me and sees me, then blessed, then blessed, then blessed is he who believes in me but has not seen me. A man said: What is blessed? He said: A tree in Paradise, a distance of one hundred years, the clothes of the people of Paradise emerge from its sleeves.” There are hadiths and narrations from the early Muslims on this topic, and it has been proven in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In Paradise is a tree, in the shade of which a rider can travel for one hundred years. Read if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” In some versions, it says: It is the tree of eternity. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, And a good place to return. He said: A good place to return. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious, he said: “It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the time of Al-Hudaybiyyah, when he made peace with Quraysh, wrote in the document: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Quraysh said: As for the Most Gracious, we do not know Him, and the people of ignorance used to write: In Your name, O God. His companions said: Let us fight them. He said: No, but write as they want.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj something similar regarding this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: And to Him is my return, he said: My repentance.
13:31: His statement: 31- And if there had been a Qur'an by which the mountains were moved It was said that this is connected to his statement: Why had not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord? And that a group of the infidels asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to move the mountains of Mecca for them until they became spacious, for it was a narrow land, so God, the Exalted, commanded him to answer them with this answer that included the greatness of the status of the Qur'an and the corruption of the opinion of the infidels, since they were not satisfied with it and insisted on their stubbornness and their request that if God, the Exalted, had done it, there would have remained what the divine wisdom requires of not sending down the signs that all servants believe in. The meaning of the mountains were moved by it: that is, by its revelation and its recitation, so they moved from their places of stability or the earth was split by it that is, it was cracked until it became scattered pieces or the dead were spoken by it that is, they became alive by its recitation to them, so they understood it when it was spoken to them as the living understand it. There is a difference of opinion regarding the answer to if what is it? Al-Farra’ said: It is omitted, and its meaning is: if this were the Qur’an. It was narrated from him that he said: The answer is that they would have disbelieved in the Most Gracious: meaning if this were done to them, they would have disbelieved in the Most Gracious. It was said that its answer is that they would not have believed, as was previously stated in His statement: They would not have believed unless God willed. It was said that the answer came before, and in the speech there is an inversion: meaning and they disbelieve in the Most Gracious if it were a Qur’an, etc. The Arabs often omit the answer to if if the context of the speech indicates it, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Even if it is a soul that dies as a whole, it is a soul that sheds souls That is, it is easy for me. Rather, the whole matter belongs to God. That is, if a Qur’an had done that, it would have been this Qur’an, but it did not do so. Rather, it did what is the case now. If He had willed that they believe, they would have believed. If He had not willed that they believe, moving the mountains and all the other signs they suggested would not have benefited. The interruption is directed at what the matter belongs to God Almighty leads to and what is required by the matter being dependent on what His wisdom and will dictate. What indicates that this is the intended meaning of that is His statement: Have not those who believe despaired that if God had willed, He could have guided all mankind? Al-Farra’ said: Al-Kalbi said: Have they not despaired means Have they not known? and it is the language of the Nakha’. He said in As-Sahih: It was said that it is the language of Hawazin, and this is what a group of the Salaf said. Abu Ubaidah said: Have they not known and made clear. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a metaphor because the one who despairs of something knows that it will not happen. Similar to this is the use of hope in the sense of fear, and forgetfulness in the sense of abandonment, because they include them. This is supported by the reading of Ali, Ibn Abbas, and a group: Did it not become clear? And from this is the saying of Rabah bin Adi: Did not the people despair that I am his son, even though I am far from the land of the tribe? Any pain he knows, and Abu Ubaidah recited in this regard the words of Malik bin Auf Al-Nadri: I say to them by the people when they capture me, have you not despaired that I am the son of a knight who has asceticism? Did you not know? The meaning of the verse according to this is: Did not those who believed know that if God had willed, He could have guided all mankind without them seeing the signs? It was said that despair has its true meaning: that is, did not those who believed despair of the faith of these disbelievers, because they knew that if God had willed to guide them, He would have guided them, because the believers wished for the revelation of the signs that the disbelievers had proposed, hoping for their faith. And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by a calamity because of what they have done. This is a warning to the disbelievers in general or to the disbelievers of Mecca in particular: that is, those who disbelieved will continue to be struck by a calamity because of what they have done of disbelief and denial of the messengers: that is, a calamity that will surprise them. It is said that the matter struck him, and the plural is qawari’, and the root of qaar is striking. The poet said: My children were wasted and I did not collect the sticks of the pitchers' drums. Meaning: The infidels will remain like this until a devastating calamity befalls them, whether it is killing, capturing, famine, or something similar to that kind of punishment. It has been said that the calamity is the disaster, and it has also been said that it is the vanguards and the raiding parties. It is not hidden that the calamity is applied to something more general than that, or it befalls meaning the calamity near their home, so they are terrified by it and see its effects that make their hearts tremble and their foreheads tremble. It has been said that the pronoun in befalls refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning is: Or you, O Muhammad, besiege them and take hold of their throats, as happened with him, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people of Taif, until the promise of God comes, which is their death, or the Hour comes upon them. For if the inevitable promise of God comes, then His punishment will come upon them that is the most severe. It has been said that what is meant by the promise of God here is His permission to fight the infidels, and the first is more appropriate, Indeed, God does not fail in His promise, so whatever His promise has come to pass will inevitably happen.
13:32: 32- And messengers were mocked before you, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved. The indefinite article in messengers is for multiplicity: that is, with many messengers, and respite is delay, and its investigation has already been mentioned in Al-A'raf. Then I seized them with the punishment that I brought down upon them. So how was My punishment? The question is for rebuke and threat: that is, so how was My punishment for these disbelievers who mocked the messengers, so I granted them respite and then seized them.
13:33: Then the Almighty asked another question of rebuke and reprimand, which is in the vein of arguments for the unbelievers, and to expose their actions and to scorn them, so He said 33- Is He then the One who is in charge of every soul? The One who is in charge, the Preserver, and the One in charge of affairs. And the Almighty meant Himself, for He is the One in charge of the affairs of His creation, the One who manages their conditions with terms and provisions, and the One who counts the deeds of every soul, whatever it may be. And the answer is omitted: that is, is the One who has this characteristic like the One who is not in this characteristic of your deities, who neither benefit nor harm. Al-Farra’ said: It seems that in meaning, Is He who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned like their partners whom they have taken besides God? The intended meaning of the verse is to deny the similarity between them. It was said that what is meant by He who is in charge of every soul is the angels assigned to the children of Adam, and the first is more appropriate. The phrase and they have made partners for God is connected to the implied answer, explaining it, or it is a conditional clause with the estimation of had: meaning, they have made, or it is connected to and they have been mocked meaning, they have mocked and made, Say, ‘Name them’ meaning, say, O Muhammad, you have made partners for Him, so name them. Who are they? This is a rebuke and rebuke to them, because this is only said about something that is insignificant and does not deserve attention. It is said: Call it if you wish, meaning that it is too insignificant to be called. It was said that the meaning is to call them gods as you claim, so that this would be a threat to them. Or do you inform Him meaning, rather do you inform God of what He does not know on the earth of the partners whom you worship, even though He is the All-Knowing of what is in the heavens and the earth. Or with an outward appearance of speech meaning, rather do you call them partners with an outward appearance of speech without it having a reality. It was said that the meaning is: Say to them, do you inform God of an inward appearance that He does not know, or an outward appearance that He knows? If they say an inward appearance that He does not know, then they have come with a false claim. If they say an outward appearance that He knows, then tell them to call them by that name. So if they name Al-Lat and Al-Uzza and the like, then tell them that God does not know of a partner for Himself, but rather He singled out the earth by denying a partner from it, even if He has no partner other than the earth, because they claimed a partner for Him on the earth. And it was said that the meaning of or by an apparent statement is or by a false statement, and from this is the saying of the poet: She lent us her milk and meat, and that is shameful, O son of Rayta. Any ephemeral falsehood, and it was said that it is a lie from the statement, and it was said that it means with the appearance of the statement with an apparent argument from the statement according to their claim, Rather, their plot was made attractive to those who disbelieved, meaning that God has no partner, rather, their plot was made attractive to those who disbelieved. Ibn Abbas read Zain in the active form, on the basis that what made that attractive to them was their plot. Those other than him read it in the passive form, and the one who made that attractive was God, the Most High, or Satan. It is permissible to call the plot disbelief, because their plot against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was disbelief, but its real meaning is plotting, or deception with falsehoods. And they were prevented from the path, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Asim read Sadawwa in the passive form, meaning God prevented them, or Satan prevented them. The rest read it in the active form: meaning they turned others away. Abu Hatim chose this reading. Yahya bin Waththab read it with a kasra on the sad, And whomever God sends astray, for him there is no guide. That is, He makes him astray and His will requires him to be misguided, so he has no guide to lead him to good. The majority read it Haad without adding the ya’ in the widespread and eloquent language. It was read with adding it in the rare language.
13:34: Then the Almighty explained what they deserve, saying 34- For them is a punishment in the life of this world with what they will suffer from killing, captivity, and other things. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe for them than the punishment of the life of this world. And they will have no protector from God to protect them from His punishment, nor any protector to save them from it.
13:35: Then when He, the Almighty, mentioned what the unbelievers deserve of punishment in the first and the last, He mentioned what He has prepared for the believers, saying 35- "The parable of Paradise, which the righteous have been promised: beneath it rivers flow." That is, its description is amazing in its strangeness, like a parable. Ibn Qutaybah said: The parable is the resemblance in the origin of the language, then it may come to mean the image of something and its description. It is said, I have represented such-and-such to you, meaning I have pictured it and described it. Here, by the parable of Paradise, He meant its image and description. Then He mentioned it, saying, underneath it rivers flow. This is like an explanation of the parable. Sibawayh said: Its meaning in what We have told you is the parable of Paradise. Al-Khalil and others said: The parable of Paradise is the subject and the predicate is flowing. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a metaphor for the absent with the present, and its meaning is like Paradise, a Paradise beneath which rivers flow. It was said that the benefit of the report goes back to its food is permanent, meaning it is not interrupted, and similar to it is the saying of the Almighty: neither cut off nor forbidden. Al-Farra’ said: The metaphor is inserted for emphasis, and the meaning is: Paradise which the righteous have been promised, beneath which rivers flow, and the Arabs do that a lot. And its shade, meaning it is also permanent, it does not shrink nor is it eclipsed by the sun. The reference in his saying that is to Paradise described with the aforementioned attributes, and it is the beginning of its report. The consequence of those who fear God, meaning the consequence of those who feared sins, and the end of their affair. And the consequence of the disbelievers is the Fire, they have no consequence or end except that. Al-Tabarani and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: They said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If it is as you say, then show us our old men from the dead so that we may speak to them, and make spacious for us these mountains of Mecca that have embraced us. So the verse, And if only a Qur’an by which the mountains could be moved was revealed. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Sheikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Awfi who said: They said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why not have the mountains of Mecca been cut to size so that we could plough them, or have the land been cut for us as Solomon used to cut it by the wind for his people, or have the dead been brought back to life as Jesus used to bring the dead back to life for his people? So God revealed, And if only a Qur’an by which the mountains could be moved until His saying, Have those who believe not despaired? He said: Have those who believe not become clear? They said: Do you narrate this hadith on the authority of one of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: On the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim who said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Munjab ibn al-Hart told us, Bishr ibn ‘Amara told us, ‘Umar ibn Hassan told us, on the authority of ‘Atiyyah al-‘Awfi, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-‘Awfi from Ibn ‘Abbas something similar in an abbreviated form. Abu Ya’la, Abu Nu’aym in al-Dala’il, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam in mentioning the reason for the revelation of the verse something similar to what was mentioned in detail. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas regarding his statement: Rather, to God belongs the entire command, He does not do of that except what He wills, and He would not have done it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, Have they not despaired? meaning, Have they not known? Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Ibn Zayd. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated something similar from Abu al-‘Aliyah, Have they not despaired? He said: Those who have believed have despaired of being guided. If God had willed, He would have guided all mankind. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: A calamity will strike them for what they have done, he said: the raids. Al-Tayalisi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated something similar from him, and he added: or it descends near their home, he said: You, O Muhammad, until the promise of God comes to pass, he said: the conquest of Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from Abu Sa’id. Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A calamity, he said: a disaster. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi from him: A calamity, he said: a torment from the sky, or it descends near their home: meaning the descent of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon them and his fighting their fathers. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Then is he who stands over every soul for what it has earned, he said: meaning himself. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding the verse: God the Most High stands with justice and fairness over every soul. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Or by an outward appearance of speech, he said: The outward appearance of speech is falsehood. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: The likeness of Paradise, he said: It is a description of Paradise; Paradise has no likeness. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi regarding his statement: Its food is constant, he said: Its pleasures are constant in their mouths.
13:36: Exegetes differed in interpreting the mentioned book. It was said: It is the Torah and the Gospel, and those who rejoice in what was revealed to the Messenger of God are those who converted from the Jews and Christians. It was said that those who rejoice are the People of the Two Books because it is in agreement with what is in their books and confirms it. According to the first, what is meant by His saying: And of the parties are those who deny some of it is those who did not convert from the Jews and Christians. According to the second, what is meant by it is the polytheists from the people of Mecca and those like them, or what is meant by it is some of the People of the Two Books: that is, from their parties, because they denied it because it includes the fact that it abrogates their laws, so the joy of those who rejoice in it is directed to what is in agreement with what is in the two books, and the denial of those who deny it is directed to what contradicts them. It was said that what is meant by the book is the Qur'an, and what is meant by those who rejoice in it are the Muslims, and what is meant by the parties is those who partisan against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the polytheists, Jews and Christians, and what is meant by some who denied it is those who contradict what they believe despite their different beliefs. It was objected to this that the Muslims’ joy at the revelation of the Qur’an is well-known, so there is no benefit in mentioning it. It was answered that what is meant is to increase joy and good tidings. Many commentators said: Abdullah bin Salam and those who believed with him from the People of the Book were upset by the small mention of the Most Gracious in the Qur’an, despite the large mention of Him in the Torah, so God revealed, Say, ‘Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious.’ They rejoiced at that. Then, when he explained what would happen with the revelation of the Qur’an, such as joy for some and denial for others, he made clear what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was doing, and he ordered him to say that to them, so he said, Say, ‘I have only been commanded to worship God and not to associate anything with Him.’ That is, I will not associate anything with Him in any way. That is, tell them, O Muhammad, to enforce the argument and refute the denial, I have only been commanded in what was revealed to me to worship God and to make Him One. This is a matter that all religions that follow the Messengers agreed upon, and all the religions agreed not to deny it. The reciters agreed to put and I will not associate anything with Him in the accusative case, in apposition to I worship. Abu Khalid read it with the nominative case as a resumption, and he narrated this reading from Nafi’ To Him I call meaning to God and not to anyone else, or to what I was commanded to do, which is to worship God alone. The first is more appropriate because of his saying And to Him is the return, for the pronoun refers to God Almighty: meaning to Him alone, not to anyone else, I return.
13:37: Then he mentioned some of the virtues of the Qur’an, and threatened those who turned away from following it, while exposing what they denied of its inclusion of abrogation of some of their laws, so he said: 37- And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic ruling. That is, like that wonderful revelation, We sent down the Qur’an, including the principles and branches of the laws. It was said that the meaning is: And just as We sent down the books to the messengers in their languages, so We sent down the Qur’an to you in the language of the Arabs. And by the ruling, we mean what is in it of rulings or Arabic wisdom translated into the language of the Arabs. And the accusative of ruling is in the state of and if you follow their desires, which they ask you to agree with them on, such as continuing to face their Qiblah and not disobeying anything they believe, after what has come to you of knowledge, which God taught you, you will have from God, that is, from His side, no protector, who will take care of your affairs and support you, nor a protector, who will protect you from His punishment. And the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an allusion to his nation, and the lam in and if you follow is The introduction to the oath. Malik is the answer to the oath and the condition.
13:38: 38- And We have certainly sent messengers before you and made for them wives and offspring. That is, the messengers whom We sent before you were from the human race, and they had wives from women and offspring who were born from them and their wives. We did not send messengers from the angels who do not marry and do not have offspring. This is a response to those who used to deny that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married women: That is, this was the way of the messengers of God who were sent before this messenger, so why do you deny what they were doing? And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by God's permission. That is, it was not for a messenger from the messengers to bring a sign, including what the disbelievers suggested to him, except by God's permission, the Most High. It contains a response to the infidels, as they suggested to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the verses they suggested previously, For every term there is a book, meaning for every matter that God has decreed, or for every time that God has decreed for a matter to occur, there is a book with God that He writes for His servants and rules over them. Al-Farra’ said: It contains an advancing and delaying. The meaning is: For every book there is a term, meaning for every matter that God has written there is a postponed term and a known time, as God, the Most High, says: For every matter there is a fixed time. The matter is not according to the will of the infidels and their suggestions, but rather according to what He wills and chooses.
13:39: 39- God erases and confirms whatever He wills meaning He erases from that book and confirms whatever He wills from it. It is said, I erased the book if you removed its trace. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Asim read and confirms with a light pronunciation. The rest read it with a heavy pronunciation, and Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid chose this reading. The apparent meaning of the Qur’anic system is that it is general in everything in the Book, so He erases whatever He wills to erase of misery or happiness or provision or life span or good or evil, and He replaces this with this, and He replaces this with this, He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. This is what ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud, Ibn ‘Abbas, Abu Wa’il, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Jurayj, and others went to. It was said that the verse is specific to happiness and misery. It was said that He erases whatever He wills from the register of the guardians, which is that which has no reward or punishment, and confirms what has reward and punishment. It was said that He erases whatever He wills from provision. It was said that He erases from the life span. It was said that He erases whatever He wills from the laws, abrogates it, and confirms whatever He wills, but He does not abrogate it. It was said that He erases whatever He wills from the sins of His servants and leaves whatever He wills. It was said that He erases whatever He wills from the sins with repentance and leaves whatever He wills from them without repentance. It was said that He erases the fathers and confirms the sons. It was said that He erases the moon and confirms the sun, as in His statement: So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day. Seeing and it was said that he erases whatever he wants of the souls that he takes during sleep. He causes its owner to die and establishes whatever He wills and returns it to its owner. It has been said that He erases whatever He wills of the generations and establishes whatever He wills of them. It has been said that He erases the world and establishes the Hereafter. Other things have been said that there is no need to mention them. The first is more appropriate, as is indicated by what is stated in His statement: Whatever He wills of generality, with the previous mention of the Book in His statement: For every term there is a book and His statement: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, meaning its origin, which is the Preserved Tablet. So what is meant by the verse is that He erases whatever He wills of what is in the Preserved Tablet, so it becomes as if it does not exist, and He establishes whatever He wills of what is in it, so His judgment and decree run in it according to what His will requires. This does not contradict what has been proven from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his statement: The pen has dried, because erasure and establishment are among the things that God Almighty has decreed. It has been said that the Mother of the Book is God Almighty’s knowledge of what He has created and what He will create. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: They rejoice in what has been revealed to you, he said: Those are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who rejoiced in the Book of God and in His Messenger and believed in it. And among the parties are those who deny part of it, meaning the Jews, Christians and Magians. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding the verse: He said: These are those who believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the People of the Book, who rejoice in that, and among them are those who believe in him and those who do not believe in him. And among the parties are those who deny part of it, he said: The parties are the nations, the Jews, Christians and Magians. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And to Him is the return, he said: To Him is the destination of every servant. Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade celibacy. Qatada recited the verse: And We have sent messengers before you 1:13. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham who said: I entered upon Aisha and said: I want to be celibate. She said: Do not do that. Haven’t you heard God say: And We have sent messengers before you and made for them wives and offspring 1:13. There is a well-known report prohibiting celibacy and encouraging marriage. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Quraysh said when the verse: It is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by God’s permission was revealed. We do not see you, O Muhammad, in control of anything, and the matter has been completed. So this verse was revealed to frighten them and warn them: God erases what He wills and confirms 1:13. If we will, we can innovate something of our affair for him. And God innovates every Ramadan, so He erases what He wills and confirms of people’s provisions and their calamities, what He gives them and what He allocates to them. And Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Nasr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, God blots out whatever He wills and confirms, that he said: God descends every month of Ramadan to the lowest heaven, and manages the affairs of the year according to the year, blotting out whatever He wills and confirming except misery and happiness, life and death. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, that he said: It is the man who spends his time in obedience to God, then returns to disobeying God and dies in misguidance, so he is the one who blots out, and the one who confirms is the man who works in disobedience to God, although good had preceded him, until he dies in obedience to God. And Ibn Jarir, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim also narrated on his authority, and he authenticated it, regarding the verse, that he said: They are two books, God blots out whatever He wills of one of them and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, meaning the entire Book. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority that he said: “God has a Preserved Tablet, the distance of five hundred years, made of white pearl, with two covers of ruby, and the two covers are tablets: God has sixty-three moments every day. God erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.” Its chain of transmission according to Ibn Jarir is as follows: Muhammad ibn Shahr ibn Askar narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God descends during the three hours remaining of the night, and opens the remembrance in the first hour of it, and looks at the remembrance in which no one else looks, so God erases what He wills and confirms.” The hadith was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh with a chain of transmission. Al-Suyuti said: It is weak on the authority of Ibn Umar. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God erases what He wills and confirms, except for misery and happiness, life and death. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Beware of destiny does not benefit, but God erases with supplication whatever He wills of destiny. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qais ibn Abbad, who said: The tenth of Rajab is a day on which God erases whatever He wills. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Shu’ab on his authority something similar, but longer. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said while circumambulating the House: O God, if You have written for me misery or a sin, then erase it, for You erase whatever You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book, so make it happiness and forgiveness. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Tabarani narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Madkhal narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: God blots out what He wills and confirms, he said: God changes whatever He wills of the Qur’an and abrogates it, and confirms whatever He wills and does not change it. And with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: The summary of that with Him in the Mother of the Book is: the abrogating and the abrogated, what is changed and what is confirmed, all of that is in a book. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And with Him is the Mother of the Book, he said: the remembrance. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Yasar on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he asked Ka’b about the Mother of the Book. He said: God knows what He is creating, and what He created is Knowing. So He said to His knowledge, Be a Book, and it was a Book.
13:40: 40- And if We show you is an extra word and its original form is: And if We show you some of what We promise them of the punishment as We promised them by saying: For them is a punishment in the life of this world, and by saying And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by what they have done, meaning We will show you some of what We promise them before your death, or We will cause you to die before you see that then upon you is only the conveyance meaning, you are only responsible for conveying the rulings of the message, and you are not required to obtain a response from them for what you conveyed to them and upon Us is the reckoning meaning holding them accountable for their actions and punishing them for them, and that is not upon you, and this is a consolation from God, the Most High, to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informing him that he has done what God commanded him to do, and there is no one else upon him, and that whoever does not answer his call and believe in his prophethood, God, the Most High, will hold him accountable for what he has committed and dared to do of that.
13:41: 41- Have they not seen meaning the people of Mecca, and the question is for denial: that is, have they not looked that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders that is, We come to the land of disbelief like Mecca, reducing it from its borders by conquering it for the Muslims little by little. Al-Zajjaj said: God knows that the statement of what He promised the polytheists of their subjugation has become clear, He says: Have they not seen that We opened for the Muslims from the land what has become clear to them, so how can they not take heed? It was said that the meaning of the verse is: the death of scholars and righteous people. Al-Qushayri said: According to this, the borders are the nobles, and Ibn Al-A'rabi said: The border is the noble man. Al-Qurtubi said: This statement is far-fetched, because the purpose of the verse is: We showed them the deficiency in their affair so that they may know that delaying the punishment from them is not due to inability, except that it is attributed to the death of the rabbis of the Jews and Christians. It was said that what is meant by the verse is: the destruction of the inhabited land until the inhabited land is in one part of it. It was said that what is meant by the verse is: the destruction of the nations that perished. It was said that what is meant is: the decrease in the fruits of the land. It was said that what is meant is: the injustice of its rulers until it decreases. And God judges, and there is no reversing His judgment. That is, He judges as He wills in His creation, so He raises this and lowers that, He gives life to this and causes this to die, He enriches this and impoverishes that. He has judged with the glory of Islam and its supremacy over the religions. The phrase there is no reversing His judgment is in the accusative case as a state. It was said that it is an interjection: and the one who reverts is the one who returns to something and nullifies it, and its reality is the one who follows it up by rejecting and nullifying it. Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is that there is no one who can reverse His judgment. He said: The one who follows something is the one who follows it and corrects it, and no one corrects it. What is meant by the verse is that no one can correct the judgment of God Almighty by reducing or changing it. And He is swift in account. So He rewards the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil, with speed.
13:42: 42- And those before them plotted, but to God belongs all the plotting. That is, the disbelievers who came before the disbelievers of Mecca plotted against the messengers whom God sent to them, so they plotted against them and disbelieved in them. This is a consolation from God, the Exalted, to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, as He informed him that this is the way of the disbelievers from ancient times with the messengers of God, the Exalted. Then He informed him that their plotting is as if it were nothing, and that all the plotting is to God, so He said, To God belongs all the plotting, no consideration is given to the plotting of others. Then He, the Exalted, explained this plotting that is established for Him and not for others, and said, He knows what every soul earns, of good and evil, so He will reward it accordingly. And He who knows what every soul earns and has prepared for it its reward, then all the plotting is His, because it comes to them from where they do not perceive. Al-Wahidi said: The cunning of the cunning ones is created and does not cause harm except by His will. It was said that the meaning is: To God belongs the recompense of the cunning ones. And the disbelievers will know to whom is the final home. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read the disbeliever in the singular, and the rest read the disbelievers in the plural: meaning, the disbeliever will know to whom of the two groups is the praiseworthy final home in this world, or in the afterlife, or in both. It was said that what is meant by the disbeliever is Abu Jahl.
13:43: 43- And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' That is, the polytheists or all the disbelievers say: You, O Muhammad, are not a messenger from God to the people. So God Almighty commanded him to answer them, and He said: Say, 'God is sufficient as a witness between me and you.' He knows the truth of my message and the truth of my calls, and He knows your lies. And he who has knowledge of the Book. That is, knowledge of the type of Book, such as the Torah and the Gospel, for their people who are knowledgeable about them know the truth of the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was reported by those who converted to Islam, such as Abdullah bin Salam, Salman al-Farsi, Tamim al-Dari, and others like them. The polytheists among the Arabs used to ask the People of the Book and refer to them, so God Almighty guided them in this verse to the fact that the People of the Book know this. It was said that what is meant by the Book and the Qur'an and the one who has knowledge of it are the Muslims. It was said that what is meant by the one who has knowledge of the Preserved Tablet is God Almighty. Al-Zajjaj chose this and said: Because it is more likely that God does not testify against His creation. Without it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said regarding the statement: We will reduce it from its borders, he said: The disappearance of the scholars. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Nu’aym ibn Hammad in al-Fitan, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: We will reduce it from its borders, he said: The death of its scholars and jurists and the disappearance of its best people. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid in his interpretation of the verse who said: The death of the scholars. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse who said: Do they not see that We will open for Muhammad land after land? Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from him through another chain of transmission. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding the verse who said: It means that the lands around the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were being reduced for him and they would look at that but not take heed. And God said in Surat al-Anbiya’: “We come to the land, reducing it from its borders. So are you the victors?” Rather, the Prophet of God and his companions are the victors. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, saying: The decrease of its people and its blessings. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, saying: Indeed, the lives and fruits decrease, but the land does not decrease. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, saying: Have they not seen the town being destroyed until the inhabited areas are in one part of it? Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, And God judges, and there is no reversing His judgment, no one follows His judgment and rejects it, just as the people of this world follow the judgment of one another and reject it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, saying: “A bishop from Yemen came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you find me in the Gospel? He said: No, so God revealed, “Say: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.” Abdullah bin Salam said, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair on the authority of Jundub who said: Abdullah bin Salam came and took hold of the doorposts of the mosque, then he said: I ask you by God, do you know that I am the one who revealed in And with him is the knowledge of the Book? They said: By God, yes. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on another authority on his authority something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas And with him is the knowledge of the Book he said: They are the People of the Book from the Jews and Christians. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated regarding the verse, he said: There were some people of the People of the Book who bore witness to the truth and knew it, among them Abdullah bin Salam, Al-Jarud, Tamim Al-Dari and Salman Al-Farsi. Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Adi narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited And with him is the knowledge of the Book he said: And from God is the knowledge of the Book. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite And with him is the knowledge of the Book meaning: And from God is the knowledge of the Book. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Nahhas in his Naskh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he was asked about the statement: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, is it Abdullah bin Salam? He said: How so, and this Surah is Meccan? Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi that nothing in the Qur’an was revealed about Abdullah bin Salam. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding the statement: And with Him is knowledge of the Book, he said: Gabriel. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: He is God.
14:1: Fifty-two verses. It was said fifty-one. It is Meccan as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it on the authority of Az-Zubayr, and Al-Qurtubi narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Jabir bin Zaid, and Qatadah, except for two verses, and it was said that it was revealed except for three verses about those who fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are His statement: Have you not seen those who have exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? until His statement: Then your destination is the Fire. An-Nahhas narrated in his Naskh on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is Meccan except for two verses that were revealed in Medina, and they are: Have you not seen those who have exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? The two verses were revealed about the polytheists killed at Badr. His saying: 1- Alif, Lam, Ra We have already discussed similar things, and explained the statement of those who said that it is ambiguous, and explained the statement of those who said that it is not ambiguous, and it is either a subject whose predicate is Kitab, or the predicate of a deleted subject, and Kitab is the predicate of the deleted one that is understood or a second predicate for this subject, or Alif, Lam, Ra is narrated in the manner of enumeration, so it has no place, and Anzala itu ilaikum is an attribute of Kitab: that is, We sent down the Book to you, O Muhammad, and the meaning of to bring mankind out of darkness into the light is to bring them out from the darkness of disbelief, ignorance, and misguidance into the light of faith, knowledge, and guidance. He made disbelief like darkness, and faith like light in the manner of metaphor, and the lam in to bring forth is for the purpose and goal, and the definite article in al-Nas is for the type, and the meaning is that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, brings forth with the Book that includes what God has legislated for them from the laws from what they were in of darkness to what they have become of light, and it was said that darkness is borrowed for innovation, and light is borrowed for the Sunnah, and it was said From doubt to certainty, and there is no objection to intending all of these matters, and the ba’ in by the permission of their Lord is related to to go out, and the action is attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is the caller, guide and warner. Al-Zajjaj said: By what He has permitted you to teach them and call them to faith, “to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy is a substitute for to the light by repeating the agent as is often the case: that is, to bring people out of the darkness to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, which is the clear way of God that He has prescribed for His servants, and He has commanded them to go to it and enter it. It is permissible for it to be resumed by estimating a question as if it was said: What is this light to which He has brought them out? So it was said: The path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. The Almighty is the Able, the Victorious. And the Praiseworthy is the Perfect in deserving praise.
