14:2: 2- God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth Nafi' and Ibn Amir read it in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning, He is God, who is described as the owner of whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. The majority read it in the accusative case as an apposition because it is one of the predominant proper nouns, so it is not correct to describe what precedes it with it, because proper nouns cannot be described with it. It was said that it is permissible to describe it with it in terms of meaning. Abu Amr said: The reading of the accusative case is based on the advancement and delay, and the estimate is: to the path of God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. And when Jacob stopped at Al-Hamid, he raised it, and when he connected, he lowered it. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Whoever lowers it stops at what is on the earth. Then He threatened those who do not acknowledge His Lordship, saying: And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment. The meaning of woe has been explained previously, and its origin is the accusative like all the sources, then it is raised to indicate steadfastness. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a word that is said for torment and destruction, so God Almighty called for that upon those disbelievers who did not leave with the guidance of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with what God revealed to him from the darkness of disbelief he was in to the light of faith. From severe torment is connected to woe, meaning they wail and groan from the severe torment in which they are.
14:3: Then he described these infidels by saying: 3- Those who prefer the life of this world meaning they prefer it because of their love for it over the Hereafter the permanent and everlasting bliss, and it was said that the relative pronoun is in the nominative case as a predicate for a deleted subject, meaning they are the ones, and it was said that the relative pronoun is a subject and its predicate is those, and the phrase and they turn away and likewise and they seek are conjoined with they prefer, and the meaning of turning away from the path of God is to turn people away from it and prevent them from it, and the path of God is His religion that He legislated for His servants and they seek to make it crooked meaning they seek to make it crooked and inclined to conform to their whims and fulfill their needs and purposes, and crookedness is with a kasra on the 'ayn in meanings and with a fatha on the 'ayn in objects, and its investigation has been previously mentioned. The original is they seek it for her, so the letter was deleted and the verb was connected to the pronoun. The combination of these characteristics is the ultimate in misguidance, and for this reason he described their misguidance as being far from the truth, so he said: Those are in extreme error. The reference is to those described with those ugly characteristics and distance, even if it is a characteristic of the misguided, but it is permissible to describe misguidance with it metaphorically for the purpose of exaggeration.
14:4: Then when He bestowed His blessings upon those charged with sending down the Books and sending the Messenger, He mentioned that among the perfections of that blessing was that the Messenger was in the language of his people, so He said: 4- And We did not send any Messenger except with the language of his people, meaning that he was immersed in their language and spoke their language, because if that were the case, the one to whom He was sent would understand what he was saying to them, and that would be easy for them, unlike if it were in the language of someone other than them, for they would not know what he was saying nor would they understand what he was addressing them with until they had learned that language for a long time. Despite that, it would inevitably be difficult for him to understand that somewhat, and for this reason, the Almighty explained what He bestowed upon His servants by saying, to make clear to them, meaning to clarify to them what God had commanded them to do of the Shari’ah that He had legislated for them, and He made the language unified because what was meant by it was language. It has been said that there is a problem with this verse, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to all people, even to the jinn and mankind, and their languages and tongues are different. It is answered that even though the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to the two worlds, as mentioned above, but since his people were the Arabs and they were more special to him and closer to him, sending him in their language was more appropriate than sending him in the language of others, and they explain it to those who did not speak their language and clarify it until they understood it as they understood it. If the Qur’an had been revealed in all the languages of those to whom it was sent, and the Messenger of God explained it to every people in their language, that would have been a source of disagreement and an opening for dispute, because every nation might claim meanings in its language that others do not know, and perhaps that would also lead to distortion and misprinting because of the false claims that fanatics fall into. The phrase God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills is a new sentence: that is, He misguides whom He wills to misguide and guides whom He wills to guide. Al-Farra’ said: If a verb is mentioned and after it is another verb, and the sequence is not similar to the first, then the nominative case is the correct way to resume. Thus, the meaning of this verse is: And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, to explain to them those laws in the language that they were familiar with and understood. However, the one who misleads and guides is God Almighty, and the explanation does not necessitate the occurrence of guidance unless God Almighty makes it an intermediary and a cause. Misguidance is presented before guidance because it precedes it, since it is maintaining the original and guidance is establishing what was not. And He is the Exalted in Might who cannot be overcome by anyone, the Wise who conducts His actions according to wisdom.
14:5: Then when he explained that the purpose of sending our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was to bring people out of darkness into the light, he wanted to explain that the purpose of sending the prophets was nothing but that, and he specifically mentioned Moses because his nation was the most advanced nation before this Muhammadan nation, so he said: 5- "And We sent Moses with Our signs" meaning he was clothed in them. What is meant by signs is the miracles that Moses had, and the meaning of "bring out" is to bring out, because sending has the meaning of saying, and it is permissible to estimate that he brought out, and what is meant by his people are the Children of Israel after the reign of Pharaoh "from darkness" from disbelief or from ignorance because of which they said: "Make for us a god as they have gods, to the light to faith or to knowledge and remind them of the days of God" meaning of His events. Ibn al-Sikkit said: The Arabs say days in the sense of events, it is said that someone is knowledgeable about the days of the Arabs: meaning of their events. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, he reminded them of the blessings of God upon them and of the vengeance of the days of God in which He took vengeance upon the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud. The meaning is: he admonished them with encouragement and intimidation, promise and threat. Indeed in that that is, in the reminder of the days of God or in the days of God themselves are signs of great indications of monotheism and the perfection of power for every patient that is, very patient in the face of trials and blessings, grateful very thankful for the blessings that God bestowed upon him. It was said that what is meant by that is every believer, and he expressed it with the two aforementioned descriptions because they are the essence of faith, and he mentioned the patient before the grateful because gratitude is the consequence of patience. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: That you may bring mankind out of darkness into the light, he said: From misguidance to guidance. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: They choose, he said: They select. Abd bin Hamid, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: God preferred Muhammad over the people of the heavens and the prophets. It was said: What is his preference over the people of the heavens? He said: God said to the people of the heavens: And whoever among them says, ‘I am a god besides Him,’ We will recompense him with Hell. And He said to Muhammad: That God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will come after. So He wrote for him a certificate of freedom from the Fire. It was said: What is his preference over the prophets? He said: God says: And We have not sent any messenger except with the language of his people. And He said to Muhammad: And We have not sent you except as a mercy to mankind. So He sent him to mankind and the jinn. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Uthman ibn Affan, Except in the language of his people, he said: The Qur’an was revealed in the language of Quraysh. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ata’ and Ubayd ibn Umair regarding his statement, And We sent Moses with Our signs, he said: With the nine signs: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the staff and his hand, the years and a decrease in fruits. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, That you bring your people out of darkness into the light, he said: From misguidance to guidance. An-Nasa’i, Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id al-Musnad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab al-Iman narrated on the authority of Abi ibn Ka’b on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, And remind them of the days of God, he said: The blessings and favors of God. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And remind them of the days of God, he said: The blessings of God. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, And remind them of the days of God, he said: admonish them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ regarding the verse, he said: with the events of God in the first generations. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful, he said: What an excellent servant is a servant who, when tested, is patient, and when given something, is grateful.
14:6: His saying: 6- And when Moses said The circumstance is related to something omitted, which is remember: that is, remember the time of Moses's saying, and when He saved you is related to remember: that is, remember His favor upon you at the time of His saving you from the people of Pharaoh, or with the favor, or related to upon you: that is, it is established upon you at the time of His saving, and it is a substitute for inclusion from the favor, meaning by it the favor or gift They subject you to the worst of torment meaning they seek you, it is said Samah zulm meaning he treated him unjustly, and the origin of sawm is to go in search of something, and the worst of torment: the source of sa'a yusu'u, and what is meant is the type of bad torment, which is their enslavement and use in hard work, and the conjunction of They slaughter your sons with They subject you to the worst of torment even though the slaughter is of the type of bad torment is to remove it from the level of the usual torment so that it is as if it is another type because of the severity in it, and with the omission of the and as in the other verse, the slaughter is an explanation For the severity of the torment, and they spare your women, meaning they leave them in life to humiliate and degrade them, and in that, the aforementioned of their actions, is a great trial from your Lord, meaning a trial for you. The interpretation of this verse has been presented in full in Surat Al-Baqarah.
14:7: 7- And when your Lord gave permission Ta'adhan means permission, as Al-Farra' said. He said in Al-Kashshaf: In Taf'al there must be an additional meaning that is not in Af'al, as if it was said: And when your Lord gave permission with a powerful permission that removes doubts and suspicions. The meaning is: And when your Lord gave permission and said, If you are grateful or he made Ta'adhan similar to Qal, because it is a type of speech. This is from the words of Moses to his people, and it is conjoined with the blessing of God: that is, remember the blessing of God upon you and remember when your Lord gave permission. It was said that it is conjoined with His statement: When He saved you: that is, remember the blessing of God Almighty at these two times, because this permission is also a blessing. It was said that it is from the words of God Almighty: that is, remember, O Muhammad, when your Lord gave permission. Ibn Mas`ud read: And when your Lord said, and the meaning is the same as mentioned above. The lam in if you are grateful is the one that introduces the oath. His saying: I will surely increase you is the answer to the condition and the oath. Likewise the lam in if you are ungrateful and his saying: Indeed, My punishment is severe is the answer to both. The meaning is: Because you are grateful for My favor upon you with what was mentioned, I will surely increase you from blessing to blessing as a favor from Me. It was said: I will surely increase you from My obedience, and it was said: I will surely increase you from the reward. The first is more apparent, so doubt is the reason for the increase. And if you are ungrateful for that and deny it, then indeed, My punishment is severe, so what befalls you from it will inevitably befall you. It was said that the answer is omitted: that is, if you are ungrateful, I will surely punish you. What was mentioned is an explanation for the omitted answer.
14:8: 8- “And Moses said, ‘If you and all those on earth are ungrateful,’ meaning if you and all of creation are ungrateful for His blessings, the Most High, and do not thank Him for them, ‘then indeed, God, the Most High, is free from need of your thanks, does not need them, and no deficiency will befall Him because of that. He is Praiseworthy,’ meaning He deserves praise for His own sake due to the abundance of His blessings, even if you do not thank Him, or if any of the angels praise Him.
14:9: 9- "Has there not come to you the report of those before you?" It is possible that this is an address from Moses to his people, and thus falls under the reminder of the days of God. It is possible that it is from the words of God Almighty, beginning an address to the people of Moses and reminding them of the first generations and their report and the coming of God's messengers to them. It is possible that it is the beginning of an address from God Almighty to the people of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, warning them against disobeying him. al-Naba 78:the report, and the plural is report. From this is the saying of the poet: Didn't the report come to you about what happened to the camels of Bani Ziyad? And the people of Noah is a substitute for the relative pronoun, or an apposition, and ‘Aad and Thamud, and those after them meaning after those mentioned none knows them except God meaning none can count their number and encompass their knowledge except God, the Most High, and the relative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is none knows them except God and the sentence is parenthetical, or the relative pronoun is conjoined with what precedes it and none knows them except God is an interjection, and the lack of knowledge from other than God either refers to their characteristics, conditions, morals, and the length of their lives: meaning none knows these matters except God and none knows them, or it refers to their selves: meaning none knows the selves of those who came after them except God, the Most High, and the sentence their messengers came to them with clear proofs is a resumption of the explanation of the report mentioned in Did there not come to you the report of those before you meaning the messengers came to them with apparent miracles and clear laws so they put their hands in their mouths meaning they put their own hands in their mouths to bite them out of rage at what the messengers had brought as in His statement God the Almighty said: They bit their fingertips in anger because the messengers came to them to belittle their dreams and insult their idols. It was said that the meaning is: They pointed with their fingers to their mouths when the messengers came to them with clear proofs: that is, be silent and leave what you have come with in denial of them and in response to their words. It was said that the meaning is that they pointed to themselves and what they said, which is their saying We have disbelieved in what you have been sent with meaning, you have no answer other than what we have said to you with these tongues of ours. It was said that they put their hands on their mouths in mockery and amazement as someone overcome by laughter does when he puts his hand on his mouth. It was said that the meaning is: They responded to the messengers’ words and belied them with their mouths. The first pronoun refers to the messengers and the second refers to the disbelievers. It was said that they put their hands in the mouths of the messengers in response to their words. The first pronoun in this case refers to the disbelievers and the second refers to the messengers. It was said that its meaning is: They gestured to the messengers to be silent. It was said that they took the hands of the messengers and placed them on the mouths of the messengers. To silence them and cut off their speech. It was said that the hands here are the blessings: that is, they responded to the blessings of the Messengers with their mouths: that is, by speaking and denying. What is meant by blessings here is what he brought to them of the laws. Abu Ubaidah said: And what he said is good: it is a proverb: that is, they did not believe and did not answer. The Arabs say to a man if he refrains from answering and is silent: He has put his hand in his mouth. Al-Akhfash said the same. Al-Qatibi objected to that and said: No one from the Arabs has been heard to say He has put his hand in his mouth: if he left what he was commanded to do. Rather, the meaning is that they bit their hands in anger and rage. Like the poet’s saying: They want to fill his mouth with the wrath of the envious until he bites his hands This is the statement that we presented over all these statements, including the poet’s statement: If Salma saw my renewal, she would bite down with her hand in pain This is the closest interpretation of the verse, if what Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash mentioned is not authentic from the Arabs. If what they mentioned is authentic, then the interpretation of the verse is closer to it. And they said, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent,’ meaning the disbelievers said to the messengers, “We have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent, according to your claim. “And indeed, we are in doubt about that to which you invite us,” meaning in great doubt about what you invite us to, which is belief in God alone and abandoning everything else. Suspicious, meaning causing doubt. It is said, arbattuhu means if you do something that causes doubt and suspicion. Doubt is the soul’s anxiety and lack of peace. It has been said, how did they openly declare their disbelief and then command them to doubt? The answer is that they meant, We disbelieve in your message. If we go below this level, then the least we can do is doubt the authenticity of your prophethood, and with complete doubt, there is no hope of recognizing your prophethood.
14:10: And sentence 10- Their messengers said, 'Is there any doubt about God?' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said, So what did the messengers say to them? The question is for rebuke and rebuke: that is, is there any doubt about His Oneness, glory be to Him? This is extremely clear and obvious. Then, the messengers mentioned, after their denial of the infidels, what confirms that denial from the evidence indicating the absence of doubt in His existence and Oneness, glory be to Him. They said: The Creator of the heavens and the earth meaning their Creator, Inventor, Maker, and Originator after nothingness calls you to believe in Him and His Oneness that He may forgive you some of your sins. Abu Ubaidah said: Min is redundant. The reason for that is His statement in another place: Indeed, God forgives all sins. Sibawayh said: “It is for partiality, and it is permissible to mention some and mean all of them. It was said that partiality is in its true form and it does not necessarily follow from the forgiveness of all sins for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that all of them are forgiven for others. This verse was used as evidence by those who permitted the addition of “min” in the affirmation. It was said that min is for substitution and is not redundant or partial: that is, so that forgiveness is a substitute for sins. And He delays you for a specified term meaning until a specified time with Him, glory be to Him, which is death, so He will not punish you in this world. “They said: You are only human beings like us” meaning you are only human beings like us in form and appearance, you eat and drink as we eat and drink and you are not angels. Want to turn us away He described them as human beings first, then Secondly, by wanting to turn them away from what their fathers used to worship: that is, you want to turn us away from the idols and the like that our fathers used to worship. Then bring us, if you are truthful that you are messengers from God, a clear authority, that is, a clear argument that indicates the truth of what you claim. And they brought them clear authority and a clear argument, but this is a type of their stubbornness and a type of their dissimulation.
14:11: 11- Their messengers said to them, 'We are only human beings like you' meaning we are only human beings in appearance and form, as you said. But God bestows favor upon whomever He wills of His servants meaning He favors whomever He wills of them with prophethood, and it was said with success and guidance. And it is not for us to bring you any authority meaning it is not correct or right for us to bring you any proof except by God's permission meaning except by His will, and that is not within our power. It was said that what is meant by authority here is what the disbelievers demand of signs by way of obstinacy, and it was said that it is more general than that, for what God wills will happen and what He does not will will not happen. And upon God let the believers rely meaning upon Him alone, and this is an order from them to the believers to rely upon God without anyone else.
14:12: It is as if the messengers intended by this command to the believers the command to themselves as a primary intention, and for this reason they said: 12- And what excuse do we have that we should not put our trust in God meaning, what excuse do we have for not putting our trust in Him, glory be to Him, while He has guided us to our ways meaning, and the situation is that He has done with us what necessitates our trust in Him by guiding us to the path that leads to His mercy, which is what He has prescribed for His servants and made obligatory for them to follow, And we will surely be patient over what you have harmed us by what you do of denying us and making false suggestions, And upon God alone without anyone else, let the trustful put their trust. It was said that what is meant by the first trust is its innovation, and by this effort in its continuity and establishment, and it was said that the meaning of the first is that those who seek miracles must put their trust in God, glory be to Him, in obtaining them, not in us, so if He, glory be to Him, will show them, and if He, glory be to Him, will not show them. The meaning of the second is to show trust in God in repelling the evil and foolishness of the disbelievers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ regarding his statement: And when your Lord proclaimed, ‘If you are grateful, I will surely increase you,’ he said: Moses informed them on the authority of his Lord that if they were grateful for the blessing, He would increase them from His grace, expand their provision, and make them victorious over the world. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, I will surely increase you, he said: From My obedience. Ibn Al-Mubarak, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated something similar on the authority of Ali ibn Salih. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri regarding the verse, he said: Do not let your souls perish in the world, for it is insignificant to God than that, but He says, If you are grateful, I will surely increase you from My obedience. Ahmad and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “A beggar came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he ordered that he be given a date, but he did not take it. Another came and he ordered that he be given a date, and he accepted it and said: A date from the Messenger of God. He said to the slave girl: Go to Umm Salamah and give him the forty dirhams that she has.” In its chain of transmission is Ahmad ‘Amara ibn Zadhan, who was deemed trustworthy by Ahmad, Ya’qub ibn Sufyan and Ibn Hibban. Ibn Ma’in said: He is sound. Abu Zur’ah said: There is nothing wrong with him. Abu Hatim said: His hadith may be written down but not used as evidence, for he is not strong. Al-Bukhari said: He may be confused in his hadith. Ahmad said: Some strange hadiths were narrated from him. Abu Dawud said: He is not that strong. Al-Daraqutni classified him as weak. Ibn ‘Adi said: There is nothing wrong with him. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history and Al-Dhiya’ Al-Maqdisi in Al-Mukhtara on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever is inspired with five things will not be deprived of five things. It also says: Whoever is inspired with gratitude will not be deprived of more. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawader Al-Agharr: Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are four things that whoever is given, God will not be denied four things, and in it: And whoever is given gratitude, will not be denied an increase.” There is no reason to restrict the increase to an increase in obedience, but rather the apparent meaning of the verse is general, as is indicated by making the increase a reward for gratitude. So whoever thanks God for what He has provided him, God will expand his provision. Whoever thanks God for what He has enabled him to do of obedience, God will increase his obedience. Whoever thanks Him for what He has bestowed upon him of health, God will increase his health, and so on. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he used to recite: And those after them, none knows them except God and he would say: The genealogists lied. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Amr bin Maymun. Ibn Al-Durais narrated on the authority of Abu Majlaz who said: A man said to Ali bin Abi Talib: I am the best at naming people. He said: You do not naming people. He said: Yes. Ali said to him: Have you seen His statement: And ‘Aad and Thamud, and the companions of Ar-Rass, and many generations between them? He said: I am the best at naming many. He said: Have you seen His statement: Has there not come to you the report of those before you - the people of Noah, and ‘Aad and Thamud, and those after them? None knows them except God. So he remained silent. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Urwah bin Az-Zubayr who said: We did not find anyone who knew what was beyond Ma’ad bin Adnan. Abu Ubaid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Between Adnan and Ishmael there are thirty fathers who are not known. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: So they put their hands to their mouths, he said: When they heard the Book of God, they were amazed and put their hands to their mouths, “and said: We disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed, we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us.” They said: We do not believe you in what you have brought, for we have strong doubts about it. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud: So they put their hands to their mouths, he said: They bit them. And in another version: on their fingertips in rage against their messengers.
14:13: His statement: 13- "And those who disbelieved said These speakers are a group of those who rebelled against answering the messengers, and the lam in We will surely expel you" is the one that introduces the oath: meaning, by God, we will surely expel you from our land or you will return to our religion. They were not satisfied with their rejection of what the messengers brought and their failure to comply with what they called them to until they dared to do this to them, and they gave them the choice between leaving their land or returning to their disbelieving religion. It has been said that the "or in or you will surely return" means until or: meaning unless you return as some of the commentators said. It was responded that there is no need for that, rather the "or" is in its place for the choice between one of the two matters, and the interpretation of the verse has been presented in Surat Al-A'raf. It was said that the return here means becoming, because the prophets were infallible from being of the religion of disbelief before and after prophethood. It was also said that the address was to the messengers and to those who believed in them, so the messengers prevailed over their followers. Then their Lord inspired them, meaning to the messengers, to destroy the wrongdoers, meaning He said to them: We will destroy the wrongdoers.
14:14: 14- And We will surely inhabit you in the land meaning the land of those infidels who threatened you with what they threatened of expulsion or return. An example of this verse is the Almighty’s saying: And We caused the people who were oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the earth, and He said: And We caused you to inherit their land and their homes. It was read li-yahlakaan and li-yaskanakum with a dhammah in both verbs, considering his saying fa-ha-ya, and the reference in his saying that to what came before of the destruction of the oppressors and the settlement of the believers in their dwellings for him who fears My standing, meaning My position, and that is on the Day of Judgment, for it is the standing of God Almighty, and the standing with the fathah on the meem is the place of residence, and with the damma is the action of residence, and it was said: the standing here is a source meaning standing: that is for him who fears My standing over him and My watching him like His saying, the Most High: Then is he who stands over every soul for what it has earned? Al-Akhfash said: that is for him who fears My standing: that is My punishment and fears My threat, that is, he fears My threat of punishment, and it was said with the Qur’an and its prohibitions, and it was said that it is the punishment itself, and the threat is the name of the promise.
14:15: 15- And they sought victory is in apposition to inspired, and the meaning is: that they sought victory from God against their enemies, or asked God to judge between them, from fatahah which means government, and from the first meaning is his saying: If you seek victory, then victory has come to you meaning if you seek victory, then victory has come to you, and from the second meaning is his saying: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth meaning judge, and the pronoun in seek victory refers to the messengers, and it was said to the infidels, and it was said to both groups And every stubborn tyrant has failed the arrogant tyrant who does not see anyone's right over him, this is how Al-Nahhas narrated it from the linguists, and the stubborn is the one who opposes the truth and deviates from it, and it is taken from the side, which means he took a side, turning away. The poet said: If you come down, make me the middle one, for I am old and cannot bear to be stubborn. Al-Zajjaj said: The stubborn one is the one who deviates from the right path, and Al-Harawi said something similar. Abu Ubaid said: He is the one who is stubborn and rebellious. Ibn Kaysan said: He is the one who is proud of his nose. It was said that what is meant by it are sins, and it was said that he who refuses to say there is no god but God. The meaning of the verse is that he who has this characteristic has lost and perished.
14:16: 16- Behind him is Hell meaning after him is Hell, and what is meant is after his destruction, as behind here means after, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: I swore, I did not leave any doubt for you, and there is no way for a person to go beyond God. That is, there is nothing after God. Similar to this is His statement: And behind him is a severe punishment, meaning after him. This is what Al-Farra’ said. It was also said that behind him means in front of him. Abu Ubaid said: It is one of the names of opposites, because one of them turns into the other. From this is the saying of the poet: And behind you is a day when you will reach it, and there is no present that can overcome it, nor any apparent that can. Another said: Do you expect the Banu Marwan to listen to me and obey me, while my people Tamim and the desert are behind me? That is, in front of me, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: And behind them was a king who seized every ship by force, that is, in front of them, and Qatrub said this with the saying of Abu Ubaidah. Al-Akhfash said: It is as one says: This matter is behind you, meaning it will come to you, and I am behind so-and-so, meaning in pursuit of him. Al-Nahhas said: From behind him, meaning in front of him, and it is not from the opposites, but rather from tawara, meaning he hid himself, so Hell was behind him, because it cannot be seen. Ibn al-Anbari narrated something similar to it, And he is given to drink from purulent water, in apposition to an implied answer to a questioner’s question, as if it was said, So what will it be then? It was said that he is thrown into it and given to drink, and purulent water is what flows from the skins of the people of Hell. Its derivation is from sadd, because it prevents onlookers from seeing it, and it is blood mixed with pus, and pus is an attribute of water, and it was said that it is an explanatory apposition from it.
14:17: And 17- He sips it in the accusative case as an attribute of water, or in the accusative case as a state, and it was said that it is a resumption based on a question, and sip is sipping: that is, he sips it time after time, not once because of its bitterness and heat. And he can hardly swallow it means he swallows it. It is said that the drink is swallowed easily in the throat, meaning it is easy. The meaning is: and it is not close to being swallowed, so how is swallowing it? Rather, he chokes on it, and his torment with thirst is prolonged at times, and he drinks it in this state at other times. It was said that he swallows it after intensity and delay, like His statement: And they could hardly do it meaning they do it after delay, as indicated by His statement, the Most High, in another verse: He melts with it what is in their bellies "And death comes to him from every side" meaning the causes of death come to him from every direction, or from every place in his body. Al-Akhfash said: What is meant by death here are the afflictions that befall the disbeliever in the Fire. He called it death because of its severity. And he is not dead means that he has not really died so that he can rest. It was said that his soul is stuck in his throat so that it does not exit his mouth so that he dies, nor does it return to its place in his body so that he can live. Similar to this is the statement of God the Almighty: He will neither die therein nor live. It was said that the meaning of and he is not dead is because the hardships of death will be prolonged for him and its agonies will extend over him. The first interpretation of the verse is that he is not really dead, based on what we mentioned from His statement the Almighty: He will neither die therein nor live, and His statement: It will not be decreed for them so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. “And behind it is a severe punishment” meaning in front of it, or after it is a severe punishment. It was said that it is eternity, and it was said that it is the confinement of the soul.
14:18: 18- The parable of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are as ashes. Sibawayh said: Like is raised as a subject, and the predicate is understood: that is, in what is recited to you, the likeness of those who disbelieve, and this is what Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is like the deeds of those who disbelieve, so the complement was deleted. It was narrated from him that he said that like was cancelled, and the meaning is those who disbelieved in their Lord, their deeds are as ashes, and it was said that it is: I mean like as a subject and its predicate is their deeds are as ashes, on the basis that its meaning is the description, so it is as if he said their strange description is their deeds are as ashes. The meaning is: that their deeds are invalid and not accepted, and ashes are what remain after something is burned. God Almighty gave this verse as an example for the deeds of the disbelievers in that He obliterates them as a strong wind obliterates ashes on a stormy day. The meaning of the wind blowing hard is: it carried it hard and fast, and the blowing is the force of the wind, and it was used to describe its time as an exaggeration, as one says: a hot day and a cold day, and the cold and heat are in both of them, not from them. They will not be able to do anything of what they have earned meaning the disbelievers will not be able to do anything of what they have earned from those false deeds, and they will not see any effect of it in the Hereafter for which they will be rewarded and recompensed, rather everything they did in this world is false and gone, like the wind blowing ashes when it blows hard. The reference in his saying: that is to what the metaphor indicates: meaning this invalidity of their deeds and the disappearance of their effect is the distant misguidance from the path of truth that contradicts the correct method, because this is a loss that cannot be remedied, so he called it distant. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: We will surely expel you from our land 1:13, he said: The messengers and believers were oppressed by their people, subjugated them, called them liars and called them to return to their religion, but God refused for His Messenger and the believers to return to the religion of disbelief, and He ordered them to put their trust in God, and ordered them to seek victory over the tyrants, and promised them that He would make them inhabit the land after them, so He fulfilled what He promised them, and they sought victory as God ordered them to seek victory. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: He promised them victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter, so God explained who of His servants will inhabit it, saying: And for him who fears the position of his Lord are two Gardens, and God has a position that He will stand in, and the people of faith fear that position, so they set out and persevere night and day. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they sought victory he said: for all the messengers he said: seek help. And regarding his statement: And every obstinate tyrant will fail he said: one who is stubborn against the truth and deviates from it. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse he said: the messengers sought help against their people And every obstinate tyrant will fail he said: one who is stubborn about the truth and turns away from it, refusing to say there is no god but God. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i he said: the obstinate one who deviates from the truth. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilyah who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding his statement: And he will be given to drink from a purulent water, gulping it down, he said: It will be brought close to him and he will dislike it, but when he comes close to it, it will burn his face and his scalp will fall off, and when he drinks it, it will sever his intestines until it comes out of his anus. God the Most High says: And they will be given to drink scalding water, which will sever their intestines, and He said: And if they call for help, they will be helped with water like molten brass, which will scald their faces. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: From a purulent water, he said: It flows from the skin and flesh of the disbeliever. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: From a purulent water means pus and blood. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And death will come to him from every side. He said: Types of torment, and there is no type of torment except death, which will come to him from it if he were to die, but he will not die because God says: They will not be decreed to die. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Maymun ibn Mihran: And death will come to him from every side. He said: From every bone, vein, and nerve. Abu al-Shaykh narrated in al-Azmah on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi, who said: From the location of every hair on his body. And behind him is a severe punishment. He said: Eternity. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Iyad: And behind him is a severe punishment. He said: Holding one’s breath. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The parable of those who disbelieved in their Lord verse, he said: The parable of those who worshipped other than Him is that their deeds on the Day of Resurrection are like ashes that the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They will not be able to do anything of their deeds that will benefit them, just as they will not be able to do anything about ashes if they are sent down on a stormy day.
14:19: His saying: "Have you not seen that God created the heavens and the earth in truth?" The vision here is of the heart, and the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an allusion to his nation, or the address is to everyone who is suitable for it. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read "He created the heavens and the meaning of in truth" is: in the correct manner in which He deserves to create them, to prove by it the perfection of His power. Then He explained the perfection of His power, glory be to Him, and His independence from any one of His creation, saying: "If He wills, He can do away with you and bring a new creation" so He can eliminate those who exist and bring those who do not exist, and He can destroy the disobedient and bring those who obey Him from among His creation. The situation may be that this new creation is of the human type, or it may be of another type.
14:20: 20- “And that is not difficult for God” meaning impossible, because He, glory be to Him, is capable of everything, and it indicates that God Almighty is the one whose reward should be hoped for and whose punishment should be feared.
14:21: Therefore, He followed it with a mention of the conditions of the Hereafter, saying: 21- And they will all appear before God, meaning they will appear from their graves on the Day of Resurrection. Prominence means appearance, and baraz is the wide place for one to appear. From this comes the word barzah, meaning she appears to men. So the meaning of prominence is that they will appear from their graves. And he used the past tense to refer to the future as a warning of its occurrence as is established in the science of meanings. Rather, he said: And they appeared before God, although He, glory be to Him, knows them and nothing of their conditions is hidden from Him, whether they appeared or not, because they were hiding from the eyes when they committed sins and they thought that this was hidden from God Almighty. So the speech is outside of what they believed. Then the weak said to those who were arrogant, meaning the weak followers said to the strong, arrogant leaders because of their leadership, Indeed, we were your followers, meaning in this world, so we denied the messengers and disbelieved in God, following you. Tabi’ is the plural of tabi’, or a source of description for exaggeration or on the assumption of those who follow. Al-Zajjaj said: He gathered them in their gathering, so the follower and the followed came together. So the weak said to those of their elders who were arrogant about worshipping God, Indeed, we were your followers, the plural of tabi’, like khadim and khuddam, “harass” and harass, and raasid and raasd, “so will you be able to relieve us?” meaning will you defend us from the punishment of God. It is said: He enriched him if he removed harm from him, and he enriched him if he brought him benefit. They said, ‘If God had guided us, we would have guided you.’ That is, the arrogant ones said, responding to the words of the weak. The sentence is resumed with an assumed question, as if it was said, How did they answer? That is, if God had guided us to faith, we would have guided you to it. It was also said, If God had guided us to the path of Paradise, we would have guided you to it. It was also said, If God had saved us from the punishment, we would have saved you from it. “It is the same for us whether we are impatient or patient. There is no escape for us.” That is, impatience and patience are equal for us. The hamza and the umm are to emphasize the equality, as in His statement, It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them. “There is no escape for us.” That is, there is no escape and escape from the punishment. It is said, So-and-so ran away from such-and-such, meaning he fled and deviated, he runs away, runs away, and runs away. The meaning is, we have no way to distance ourselves from the Fire. It is possible that this is from the speech of both groups, even though it appears that it is from the speech of the arrogant ones.
14:22: 22- And Satan said when the matter was decided meaning he said this statement to both groups, and the meaning of when the matter was decided is when the people of Paradise entered Paradise and the people of Hell entered Hell, as will be explained in Surat Maryam. Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth which is His promise, glory be to Him, of resurrection and accountability, and of rewarding the good-doer for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil. And I promised you, but I failed you meaning I promised you a false promise, that there would be no resurrection, no accountability, no Paradise, and no Hell, but I failed you in what I promised you of that. Al-Farra’ said: The promise of truth is from adding something to itself, as in their saying: the mosque of the congregation. The Basrans said: Your promise is the promise of today, the truth. And I had no authority over you meaning I had power over you by showing evidence for what I promised you and made attractive to you except that I invited you and you responded to me meaning except for my mere invitation to you to misguidance and error without evidence or proof. His invitation to them is not of the same kind as authority so that you can be excepted from it, rather the exception is disjunctive: meaning but I invited you and you responded to me: meaning you hastened to answer me. It was said that what is meant by authority here is coercion: meaning I had no coercion over you that would compel you to answer me. It was said that this exception is from the category of: Greetings between them are painful He exaggerated in denying authority over himself, as if he said: I will only have authority over you if the mere supplication is from the sultan, and certainly not from him. So do not blame me for what you have fallen into because of my false promise to you and my breaking this promise. But blame yourselves for responding to me merely because of the supplication that has no authority or proof, for whoever accepts false promises and claims that deviate from the path of truth has committed a sin against himself, and has cut off his way, especially since this false supplication of mine and my corrupt promise are in opposition to God’s promise to you, the promise of truth, and His call to you to the abode of peace, with the establishment of the proof that is not hidden from a rational person and is only confused by a forsaken one. Similar to this is the one who follows the opinions of men that contradict what is in the Book of God, the Most High, and what is in the Sunnah of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and prefers them over what is in them. He has responded to falsehood for which there is no proof or evidence, and he has left the proof and evidence behind him, as many of those who follow the men who have deviated from the path of truth do due to their bad choices. O God, forgive me. I am not your helper, and you are not my helper. It is said that someone cried out if he seeks help, he cries out with a cry and a scream. To cry out means to shout, and the one who cries out is the one who helps, and the one who seeks help is the one who seeks assistance. It is said that he cried out to me so I cried out to him. Crying is the voice of one who cries out, and crying is also the one who cries, which is the one who helps and the one who seeks assistance. It is one of the names of opposites as in As-Sahah. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: The one who cries out is the one who seeks assistance, and the one who cries is the one who helps. The meaning of the verse is: I cannot help you from the torment you are in, and you cannot help me from what I am in. It is guidance for them that the devil in that situation is afflicted with the torment they are afflicted with and is in need of someone to help him and deliver him from what he is in. So how can they hope to help someone who is in need of someone to help him? Among the sayings that have been reported from the Arabs that are similar to these sayings is the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: Do not be afraid, for I am not a cry to you, and you have no help or support from me. Masrakhi with the opening of the yaa according to the reading of the majority. Al-A'mash and Hamza read with the breaking of the yaa according to the original meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Farraa said: Hamza's reading is a mistake from him, and few are safe from error. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a bad reading and there is no basis for it except a weak basis, meaning what we mentioned that he broke it according to the original meeting of two quiescent letters. Qatrib said: This is the language of Banu Yarbu'; they add a yaa to the yaa of addition. Al-Farraa recited regarding what was reported about this reading the saying of the poet: I said to her, Oh Taa, would you like some? She said to him, You are not sick. I have disbelieved in what you associated before. When he revealed to them the mask that it would not avail them at all against the punishment of God, nor would it support them with any kind of support, he declared to them that he was a disbeliever because they associated him with God in Lordship before this time in which Satan said this statement to them, which was what they did in this world to make him a partner, and Satan stood up for them on this day in a position that would break their backs and sever their hearts, so he explained to them first that the promises he had made to them in this world were invalid and opposed to the promise of the truth from God, the Most High, and that he had broken his promises to them and had not fulfilled any of them. Then he explained to them secondly that they had accepted his statement with something that does not necessitate acceptance, and is not supported by a rational mind due to the lack of proof that a rational person must have in accepting the statement of another. Then he explained thirdly that he had done nothing but a call devoid of proof and devoid of the simplest thing that rational people hold on to. Then he rebuked them fourthly for what they had fallen into, and repelled their blame of him and ordered them to blame themselves, because they were the ones who accepted falsehood. The research whose invalidity is not ambiguous to anyone with the slightest intellect. Then he explained to them fifthly that he has no victory or relief and he cannot benefit them or ward off harm from them, but he is like them in falling into the calamity and being unable to be saved from this ordeal. Then he stated to them sixthly that he had disbelieved in what they believed in him and attributed to him, so their regrets were doubled and calamities followed one after the other. If the phrase Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment is part of his speech as some have gone to, then it is a seventh type of his speech with which he addressed them, so he established injustice for them, then he mentioned what their reward for it is of painful punishment, not according to the saying of those who said: It is the beginning of a speech from the side of God Almighty. The majority of commentators have gone to the fact that what is a source in what you associated and it was said that it is permissible for it to be a relative pronoun meaning that I disbelieved in what you associated with me, which is God Almighty, and this is a narration of his disbelief in God when He commanded him to prostrate to Adam.
14:23: 23- And admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. When God the Almighty informed about the state of the people of Hell, He informed about the state of the people of Paradise. The majority of scholars read I admit in the passive form, while Al-Hasan read And I admit in the future form and in the active form: meaning, I admit those who believe. Then God the Almighty mentioned their eternity in Paradise and the continuity of their bliss. Then He mentioned that this is by the permission of their Lord: meaning, by His guidance, kindness, and guidance. This is according to the reading of the majority of scholars. As for the reading of Al-Hasan, by the permission of their Lord is related to His statement: "Their greeting therein is, 'Peace.'" meaning, the greeting of the angels in Paradise is, 'Peace.' By the permission of their Lord. The explanation of this has been presented in Surah Yunus. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And He will bring a new creation, he said: Another creation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: Then the weak will say, he said: The followers, to those who were arrogant, he said: To the leaders. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his statement: It is the same for us whether we are impatient or patient, Zaid bin Aslam said: They were impatient for a hundred years, and they were patient for a hundred years. Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ka’b bin Malik tracing it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: It is the same for us, the verse, he said: The people of Hell will say: Come, let us be patient, so they will be patient for five hundred years, but when they see that it will not benefit them, they will say: Come, let us be impatient, so they will weep for five hundred years, but when they see that it will not benefit them, they will say: It is the same for us whether we are impatient or patient, there is no escape for us. It appears that this review was between them after they entered the Fire, as in the Almighty’s saying: “And when they dispute in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, ‘Indeed, we were your followers, so can you relieve us of a share of the Fire?’ Those who were arrogant will say, ‘Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, God has judged between His servants.’” Ibn al-Mubarak narrated in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, and he mentioned in it the hadith of intercession, then he said: And the disbeliever will say at that time, ‘The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so who will intercede for us?’” It is none other than Iblis, for he is the one who led us astray. So they go to Iblis and say: The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so go and intercede for us, for you are the one who led us astray. So Iblis rises and rises from his seat with the most foul odor anyone has ever smelled, then he admonishes them with Hell, and says at that time: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you verse. Al-Suyuti weakened its chain of transmission, and perhaps the reason for that is because in its chain of transmission is Rashdin ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An’am, on the authority of Dajin al-Hajzi, on the authority of Uqbah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Iblis will stand as a preacher on a pulpit of fire and say: Indeed, God promised you until His statement: And you are not my helpers He said: My helpers Indeed, I disbelieved in what you associated with me before He said: By your obedience to me in the world. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi regarding this verse, saying: “Two orators will stand on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Iblis and Jesus. As for Iblis, he will stand with his party and say this statement, meaning what is mentioned in the verse. As for Jesus, he will say: ‘I only said to them what You commanded me, namely, “Worship God, my Lord and your Lord.” And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them. But when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are Witness over all things.’” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, I will not be your savior, nor will you be my savior, he said: I will not be of benefit to you, nor will you be of benefit to me. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with Him before, he said: His association means His worship. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah, I will not be your savior, he said: I will not be your helper. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding His statement, “Their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace,’” he said: The angels will greet them in Paradise.
14:24: When He, the Most High, mentioned the example of the deeds of the unbelievers, and that they are like ashes that the wind blows hard, then He mentioned the bliss of the believers, and what God rewarded them with by admitting them into Paradise to abide therein, and the angels’ greeting to them, the Most High mentioned here an example of the good word, which is the word of Islam: meaning there is no god but God, or what is more general than that of the words of good, and He mentioned an example of the bad word, which is the word of polytheism, or what is more general than that of the words of evil, so He said, addressing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or addressing those who are suitable for the address: 24- Have you not seen how God sets forth a parable? meaning He chose an example and placed it in its appropriate place, and the accusative of an example is as the object of set forth and the word is a substitute for it, and it is permissible for the word to be accusative as an appositive of an example, and it is permissible for the word to be accusative with an implied verb: meaning like a good word like a tree is good, and He ruled that it is like it, and the place of like a tree is the accusative as an attribute of the word, or Raising on the assumption of a subject: that is, it is like a tree. It is permissible for the word first to be the object of strike, and it was delayed from the second object, which is for example, so that it would not be far from its description. The first is better, and the word and what follows it is an explanation of the example. Then he described the tree by saying: its root is firm, that is, firmly rooted, safe from being uprooted because of its attachment to the ground with its roots, and its branch is in the sky, that is, its top goes towards the sky, high in the air.
14:25: Then He, the Almighty, described it as 25- "It yields its fruit at all times at all times by permission of its Lord" by His will and desire. It was said that it is the palm tree, and it was said that it is something else. It was said that what is meant by it yielding its fruit at all times is: every hour of the hours of the night or day at all times without distinction between winter and summer. It was said that what is meant is at different times without specifying, and it was said every morning and evening, and it was said every month, and it was said every six months. Al-Nahhas said: These sayings are close and not contradictory because the report according to all linguists except for those who deviated from them in the meaning of time occurs for a short time or a long time, and Al-Asma'i recited the saying of Al-Nabigha: Sometimes you release it and sometimes you back down An-Nahhas said: This shows you that the word hain means time. The word hain has been mentioned in some places with more meaning, such as His statement: Has there not come upon man a period of time? The scholars’ statements about hain have already been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah in His statement: And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time. Al-Zajjaj said: “Hain is a time, whether long or short. “And God presents examples for the people that perhaps they will be reminded,” to ponder the states of the beginning and the end, and the wonders of His creation, glory be to Him, which indicate His existence and oneness. In presenting examples, there is an increase in reminder, understanding, and depiction of meanings.
14:26: 26- And like a bad word its interpretation has been presented, and it was said that it is the disbeliever himself, and the good word: the believer himself like a bad tree meaning like a bad tree, it was said that it is the colocynth tree, and it was said that it is the garlic tree, and it was said that it is the truffle, and it was said that it is the moss, and it was said that it is the kashuth with the dammah and the last letter is a triangle, and it is a tree that has no leaves or roots in the ground. The poet said: It is like chaff, with neither root nor fruit. And the word for example was read in the accusative case in apposition to the word good “uprooted from above the earth” meaning it was uprooted and plucked from its roots. From this is the poet’s saying: It is the evacuation that uproots your origin The historian said: He took her body and she was herself. The body is the person of a human being. It is said that he pulled it out: he uprooted it, and he uprooted it: he uprooted it. The meaning of from above the ground is that it has no firm roots or roots established in the ground. It has no stability meaning stability on the ground. It was said that it is from being fixed on the ground, just as the infidel and his word have no argument and no stability in it and no good comes from him at all, and no good word or good deed ascends to him.
14:27: 27- God confirms those who believe with the firm word meaning with the clear argument, which is the good word mentioned above. It has been proven in the Sahih that it is the word of testimony, the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that is when the believer sits in his grave. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So that is what God the Almighty said: God confirms those who believe with the firm word, and it was said that the meaning of God confirming them is that they persist in the firm word, and from that is the saying of Abdullah bin Rawahah: May God confirm what He has given you of the good confirmation of Moses and a victory like that which they gave victory. The meaning of in this worldly life is that they continue with the firm statement in this worldly life. A group said: What is meant by in this worldly life in this verse is the grave because the dead are in this world until they are resurrected, and what is meant by in the Hereafter is the time of reckoning. It was said that what is meant by in this worldly life is the time of questioning in the grave, and in the Hereafter is the time of questioning on the Day of Resurrection. What is meant is that if they are asked about their belief and religion, they will clarify that with firm statements without stuttering, hesitation, or ignorance, as someone who is not successful says: I do not know, and it is said to him: You neither knew nor recite. And God misleads the wrongdoers, meaning He misleads them from their argument, which is the firm statement, so they are not able to speak about it in their graves or at the reckoning, just as He misled them from following the truth in this world. It was said that what is meant by the wrongdoers here are the disbelievers, and it was said that everyone who wrongs himself, even by merely turning away from clear evidence, will not be steadfast in situations of tribulations and will not be guided to the truth. Then the Almighty mentioned that He does whatever He wills of confirmation and failure, and there is no one to reverse His judgment, and He is not questioned about what He does. Al-Farra’ said: That is, His power is not denied, nor is He questioned about what He does. The explicit pronoun is in place of the implicit pronoun in both places to instill awe, as was said, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Have you not seen how God presents a parable? A good word, he said: the testimony that there is no god but God, like a good tree, which is the believer, whose root is firm, meaning: there is no god but God is firm in the heart of the believer, and its branches are in the heaven, meaning: the believer’s deeds are raised by it, and the parable of a bad word, which is polytheism, is like a bad tree, meaning the disbeliever, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability, meaning: polytheism has no root that the disbeliever can take, nor any proof, and God does not accept any deed with polytheism. Something similar to this has been narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un and those who came after them. Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: “A veil of unripe dates was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘The parable of a good word is like a good tree,’ until he reached ‘brings forth its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord.’ He said: It is the palm tree. ‘And the parable of a bad word,’ until he reached ‘it has no stability.’ He said: It is the colocynth.” It was narrated with a chain of transmission ending with Anas. Al-Tirmidhi said: The chain of transmission ending with Anas is more authentic. Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: ‘like a good tree,’ he said: It is the one whose leaves do not decrease. He said: It is the palm tree. Al-Bukhari and others narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said one day to his companions: “There is a tree among the trees that does not shed its leaves like the believer. The people thought about the tree of the desert, and it occurred to me that it was the palm tree, but I was embarrassed until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is the palm tree. In a wording of Al-Bukhari he said: “Tell me about a tree like the Muslim man that does not shed its leaves and does not produce its fruit every time,” and he mentioned something similar. In a wording of Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Ibn Umar he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do you know what a good tree is? Then he said: It is the palm tree. Something similar to this was narrated from a group of the Companions and Followers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: It produces its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord, he said: Every hour, by night and day, in winter and summer. This is like the believer who obeys his Lord by night and day, in winter and summer. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding the verse: It will be green then it will be yellow. And he also narrated from him regarding his statement: every time he said: the cuttings of palm trees. And Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him: It yields its fruit every time he said: It is fed every six months. And Abu Ubaid, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him that he said: Hen here is a year. And Al-Bayhaqi also narrated from him that he said: Hen could be morning and evening. And many sayings were narrated from a group of the Salaf regarding this. And Al-Bukhari, Muslim, the people of Sunan and others narrated from Al-Bara’ bin Azib that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When a Muslim is asked in the grave, he testifies that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. So that is the meaning of the statement of God, the Most High: God will make firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Al-Bara’ bin Azib regarding his statement: God will make firm those who believe the verse that he said: Confirmation in the life of this world is when the two angels come to a man in the grave and say: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God. He says: What is your religion? He said: My religion is Islam. He said: Who is your prophet? He said: My prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. That is the confirmation in this worldly life. Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas. Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Saeed regarding the verse: In the Hereafter, the grave. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Aisha, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the verse: ‘God will make firm those who believe’ 1:136, he said: This is in the grave.” Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from her hadith. Al-Bazzar also narrated from her: “I said: O Messenger of God, this nation will be tested in its graves, so what about me, a weak woman? He said: ‘God will make firm those who believe’ 1:136. Many hadiths have been narrated about the angels’ questioning of the dead in their graves, and about their answers to them, and about the torment and trials of the grave. This is not the place to elaborate on them, as they are well-known.”
14:28: His saying: 28- Have you not seen? This is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to anyone who is suitable for him, and it is an expression of astonishment at the state of the infidels, as they replaced God’s blessing upon them with disbelief: that is, instead of thanking Him for it, they disbelieved in it, and that is by their denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when God sent him from among them and blessed them with him. The majority of commentators have said that they were the infidels of Mecca and that the verse was revealed about them. It was said that it was revealed about those who fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr. It was said that it was revealed about two clans of the Quraysh, Banu Makhzum and Banu Umayyah. It was said that it was revealed about the Christian Arabs, namely Jabalah ibn al-Ayham and his companions. There is a view on this, because Jabalah and his companions did not convert to Islam until the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. It was said that it is general for all polytheists. It was said that what is meant by exchanging God’s blessing for infidelity is that when they disbelieved in it, God took it away from them, so they became infidels. And they made their people dwell in the abode of ruin, meaning they made their people dwell in the abode of ruin, which is Hell, and ruin is destruction. It was said that they were the leaders of Quraysh who made their people dwell in the abode of ruin on the day of Badr, meaning destruction, which is the killing that they were afflicted with. From this is the saying of the poet: I have never seen heroes like them in war on the day after the war when destruction was feared.
14:29: And the first is more appropriate, because he said: 29- Hell because it is an explanatory apposition to the abode of destruction, and they will enter it is in the accusative case as a state, or it is a resumption to explain how they will end up in it. And what an evil resting place meaning what an evil resting place is their resting place in it, or what an evil abode is Hell, so the one specifically blamed is omitted.
14:30: 30- "And they made rivals to God" is in apposition to: and they permitted: meaning they made partners to God in Lordship, or in naming, which are idols. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read "li-yidalu" with a fat-ha on the ya': meaning to mislead themselves from the path of God, and the lam is for the consequence: meaning to follow their ignorance of God with rivals to their misguidance, because a wise person does not want his own misguidance, and the use of the lam of the consequence here is good because it resembles the purpose and goal in terms of its occurrence at the last levels, and similarity is one of the things that correct the metaphor. The rest read it with a damma on the ya' to cause their people to stray from the path of God, so this is the purpose of their making rivals to God. Then He, the Almighty, threatened them, saying to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “Say, ‘Enjoy yourselves,’ in what you are in of desires, and what your souls have made attractive to you of ingratitude and misleading people, ‘for your destination is the Fire,’ meaning your return and return to it is nothing but it. And since this was their state, and they had become so obsessed with it and immersed in it that they would not give it up, nor would they accept the advice of those who advise them, He made the command to do it in place of the prohibition, as an explanation of what their end would be, and that they would inevitably go to the Fire, so they must take the means that require that. So the phrase, “for your destination is the Fire,” is an explanation of the command to enjoy, and it contains a threat that cannot be measured. It is possible that this phrase is an answer to something omitted that the context of the speech indicates, as if it were said: If you persist in that, then your destination is the Fire. The first is more appropriate and the Qur’anic structure is more indicative of it, and that is like what is said to someone who seeks to disobey the ruler: Do whatever you want of disobedience, for your destination is the sword.
14:31: 31- Say to My servants who have believed to establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly. When He commanded him to say to those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief, who set up rivals to God, what He said to them, He commanded Him, the Most High, to say to the group opposite them, which is the group of believers, this statement, and the one said is omitted, as indicated by the one mentioned: that is, say to My servants to establish and spend, and to establish and to spend. So He made yaqimu in the jussive mood as an answer to the omitted command, and likewise yaqimu, Al-Farra' mentioned the meaning of this. Al-Zajjaj said: In yaqimu is in the jussive mood with the meaning of the lam: that is, to establish, so the lam was dropped. Then he mentioned another aspect of the jussive mood like what Al-Farra' mentioned: And the accusative of secretly and publicly, either as a state: that is, secretly and publicly, or as a source: that is, spending secretly and spending publicly, or as a circumstance: that is, a time of secret and a time of publicity. The majority said: The secret is what is hidden, and publicity is what is apparent. It was said that secret is voluntary, and public is obligatory. This was explained earlier when interpreting His statement: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good “before there comes a Day when there is no trading nor friendship.” Abu Ubaidah said: Trading here means ransom, and friendship is a verbal noun.
