Al-Wahidi said: This is the opinion of all linguists. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: It is possible that the plural of friendship is like burmah and baram and `alaba and `alaab, and the meaning is that there will be no trading on the Day of Resurrection until the negligent in his work ransoms himself from the punishment of God by paying compensation for that, and there is no friendship until the friend intercedes for his friend and saves him from the punishment. So God, the Almighty, commanded them to spend in charitable ways from what God has provided for them as long as they are able to spend their money in this worldly life before the Day of Resurrection comes, for they will not be able to do so, and they will have no money at that time. So the phrase, I mean before there comes a Day when there is no trading nor friendship is to emphasize the meaning of the command to spend from what God has provided for them. It may also contain an emphasis on the content of the command to perform the prayer, because abandoning it is often due to being busy with selling and taking care of the rights of friends. The explanation of selling and friends has already been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah.
14:32: 32- God is He Who created the heavens and the earth meaning He created them and invented them without example and created what is in them of the upper and lower bodies, and the noble name is the subject and what follows it is its predicate And sent down from the sky water what is meant by the sky here is the high place, so the heavens are included in that according to those who said that the beginning of rain is from it, and the clouds are included in it according to those who said that the beginning of rain is from it, and the causes that stir up the clouds are included in it such as the winds, and the indefiniteness of water here is for the type: meaning a type of water, which is rainwater Then He brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you meaning He brought forth thereby the water from the various fruits as provision for the children of Adam by which they live, and from in from the fruits is for clarification like your saying: I spent from the dirhams, and it was said for the partiality because some of the fruits are provision for the children of Adam, and some are not provision for them, which is what they do not eat or benefit from And He subjected to you the ships so it was made according to your will and you used it in Your interests, and that is why He said: to run in the sea as you want and as you request by His command meaning by God’s command and will. The explanation of this has already been presented in Al-Baqarah and He has subjected the rivers to you meaning He has made them subservient to you for riding on them and for them to flow to where you want.
14:33: 33- And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon so that you may benefit from them and be illuminated by their light. Constantly is in the accusative case, and constant is the passage of something in the work according to a regular habit: that is, constant in repairing what they repair of plants and other things. It was said constant in walking in compliance with God's command, and the meaning is: they will continue until the Day of Resurrection, not slackening or stopping in their movement. And He has subjected to you the night and the day they alternate, so the day is for your striving in the affairs of your livelihood and what you need of your worldly affairs, and the night is for you to rest as God Almighty said: And out of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty.
14:34: 34- And He gave you of all that you asked of Him. Al-Akhfash said: That is, He gave you of everything that you asked of Him, so he deleted something. It was also said that the meaning is: And He gave you of everything that you asked of Him and of everything that you did not ask of Him, so the other sentence was deleted. Ibn Al-Anbari said this. It was also said that it is from an extra word: That is, He gave you everything that you asked of Him. It was also said that it is for partialization: That is, He gave you some of everything that you asked of Him. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan and Qatadah read from every with the tanween of every. According to this reading, ma may be negative, meaning He gave you from all of that while you were not asking Him for it. It may also be a relative pronoun, meaning He gave you from everything that you asked Him for. And if you were to count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them. That is, if you were to enumerate the favors of God that He bestowed upon you in general, let alone in detail, you would not be able to count them in any way, nor would you be able to enumerate them in any case. The origin of counting is that when the calculator reaches a certain decade of the decades of numbers, he places a pebble to memorize it with. It is known that if an individual among the servants wanted to count what God bestowed upon him in the creation of one of his organs or one of his senses, he would never be able to do so, nor would he be able to do so at all. So how about the other favors in all that God created in his body? So how about the other favors that reach him at all times, in their diversity and different kinds. O God, we thank You for every blessing You have bestowed upon us, of which no one knows except You, and of which we have learned, a thanks that cannot be encompassed or counted, and the number of times that the grateful have thanked You in every tongue in every age. Indeed, man is unjust to himself by neglecting to thank God for His blessings upon him, and its apparent meaning includes every human being. Al-Zajjaj said: Indeed, man is in loss, meaning he is extremely ungrateful for God’s blessings upon him, ungrateful for them and not thankful for them - glory be to Him - as he should and must. Abdul Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, Have you not seen those who have exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? He said: They are the disbelievers of the people of Mecca. Al-Bukhari in his history, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab regarding the statement of God, Have you not seen those who have exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? He said: They are the two most wicked of Quraysh 106:Banu Al-Mughira and Banu Umayya. As for Banu Al-Mughira, you were spared from them on the day of Badr, but as for Banu Umayya, you were granted respite for a time. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Umar, something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ali regarding the verse something similar as well. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl that Ibn al-Kawwa' asked Ali about those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief. He said: They are the wicked ones from Quraysh, whom I spared on the day of Badr. He said: Who are those whose efforts were lost in the life of this world? He said: Among them are the people of Harura. Similar to this has been narrated in the interpretation of this verse on the authority of Ali. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: They are Jabalah ibn al-Ayham and those who followed him from the Arabs and joined the Romans. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they made their people dwell in the home of ruin, he said: Destruction. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement, And they set up rivals to God, he said: They associated partners with God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, And He has subjected to you the rivers, he said: For every benefit. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, both diligently pursuing their courses. He said: Their diligence in obeying God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, And He has given you of all that you asked of Him. He said: Of everything that you desired from Him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: Of all that you asked of Him. Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Shu’ab on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, who said: God bestowed blessings upon His servants according to His measure and commanded them to be grateful according to their measure. They also narrated on the authority of Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, who said: O son of Adam, if you want to know the extent of what God has bestowed upon you, then close your eyes. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: Whoever does not recognize God’s blessings upon him except in his food and drink, his deeds have been little and his punishment has come near. Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Qurashi, a client of Banu Hashim, who said: David, peace be upon him, said: My Lord, tell me what is the least of Your blessings upon me. So He revealed to me: O David, breathe, so I breathed, and He said: This is the least of My blessings upon you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab that he said: O God, forgive me for my injustice and my disbelief. Someone said: O Commander of the Faithful, this is injustice, but what about disbelief? He said: Man is indeed unjust and disbelieving.
14:35: His saying: 35- And when Abraham said is related to something omitted: that is, remember the time of his saying, and perhaps what is meant by the context of what Abraham, peace be upon him, said in this place is to explain the disbelief of the Quraysh in the special blessings that were bestowed upon them, which is their settlement in Mecca after their disbelief in the general blessings was explained, and it was said that mentioning the story of Abraham here is an example of a good word, and it was said that it is intended to call to monotheism and deny the worship of idols My Lord, make this city secure what is meant by the city here is Mecca: Abraham called upon his Lord to make it secure: that is, secure, and he presented the request for security over all the requests mentioned after it, because if security is absent, a person will not be free for anything else from the affairs of religion and the world, and the interpretation of a verse like this has already been presented in Al-Baqarah when God Almighty said: My Lord, make this city secure, and the difference between what is here and what is there is that what is required here is merely security for the city, and what is required there is the municipality and security and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols, it is said that you kept him away from such and such and kept him away from it, Meaning: Keep me and my children away from worshipping idols. It was said that he meant his children from his loins and they were eight. It was also said that he meant those who were present at the time of his call from his children and his children’s children. It was also said that he meant all of his offspring as they reproduced. This is supported by what was said that none of the children of Abraham worshipped an idol. An idol is a statue that the people of the Age of Ignorance used to make from stones and the like and worship it. Al-Jahdari and Isa bin Omar read and keep me away by cutting off the hamza, on the basis that its root is ajnab.
14:36: 36- My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people. He attributed the misguidance to the idols, even though they are inanimate objects that do not have reason, because they are the cause of their misguidance, as if they led them astray. This sentence is an explanation for his supplication to his Lord. Then he said: So whoever follows me, meaning whoever follows my religion from the people and becomes a Muslim monotheist, then he is of me, meaning of the people of my religion: he made the people of his religion like himself, as an exaggeration. And whoever disobeys me, so he does not follow me and enter my religion, then indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful, able to forgive him. It was said that he said this before he knew that God does not forgive associating partners with Him, as he did when he asked forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist. This is what Ibn al-Anbari said. It was said that what is meant here is his disobedience in something less than polytheism, and it was said that this forgiveness is restricted to repentance from polytheism.
14:37: Then he said 37- Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants. Al-Farra' said: Min is for partiality: meaning some of my descendants. Ibn Al-Anbari said: It is redundant: meaning I have settled my descendants, and the first is more appropriate, because Ishmael was settled, and he is some of his sons, in a valley without cultivation meaning there is no cultivation in it, and it is the valley of Mecca near Your sacred House meaning in which what is permitted elsewhere is forbidden, and it was said that it is forbidden to tyrants, and it was said that it is forbidden so that its sanctity would not be violated, or it would be treated lightly. In Surat Al-Ma’idah, we have already mentioned what makes it unnecessary to repeat it. Then He said: Our Lord, that they may establish prayer. The lām is related to askatan: meaning, You have made them dwell so that they may establish prayer in it, turning to it, seeking blessings from it. He singled it out from all other acts of worship because of its greater virtue. Perhaps the repetition of the call is to show complete concern for this act of worship. So make hearts among the people yearn toward them. “Af’idah” is the plural of fu’ad, which is the heart. He used it to refer to the entire body, because it is the most honorable organ in it. It was said that it is the plural of delegation, and the original is awfada, so the fa was brought forward, and the waw was changed to a ya, so it is as if he said: And he made delegations of people descend to them, and min in min al-nas is for partiality, and it was said that it is redundant and it does not necessitate that the Jews and Christians perform Hajj by entering under the word people, because what is required is to direct the hearts of the people to them to reside with them and attract them, not to direct them to Hajj, and if this was intended, he would have said tahwi ilayhi, and it was said that min is for the beginning like you say: The heart of me is sick, meaning my heart, and the meaning of tahwi ilayhi is: it inclines to them, it is said hawa like it: if it leans, and the she-camel fell tahwiyyan, so it is hawiya: if it runs a strong gallop as if it falls into a well, and it is possible that the meaning is: it comes to them or rushes to them, and the meaning is close, And provide them with fruits meaning I provide my offspring whom I settled there or they and those who live with them from the people from the types of fruits that grow in it, or are brought to it so that they may be grateful. Your blessings that you have bestowed upon them.
14:38: 38- Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we declare meaning what we conceal and what we reveal, because the apparent and the implicit are the same to Him, the Almighty. It was said that what is meant here by what we conceal is what is opposite to what we declare, so the meaning is what we reveal and what we do not reveal. What we conceal was mentioned before what we declare to indicate that they are equal in the knowledge of God, the Almighty. The apparent meaning of the Qur'anic system is the generality of everything that is not revealed and everything that is revealed without restricting it to a specific thing. It was said that what is meant is what Abraham concealed of his grief over Ishmael and his mother when he settled them in a valley without crops, and what he declares of that. It was said that what Abraham concealed of grief and declared of crying and supplication. The use of the pronoun of famine indicates that Abraham did not mean himself alone, but rather he meant all of the servants, so the meaning is that God, the Almighty, knows everything that the servants reveal and everything that they do not reveal. As for his statement: And nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven, the majority of commentators said: It is from the words of God, the Most High, confirming what Abraham said, that He, the Most High, knows what the servants conceal and what they declare. So He, the Most High, said: And nothing of the existing things is hidden from God, whatever it may be. He only mentioned the heavens and the earth because they are visible to the servants, otherwise His knowledge, the Most High, encompasses everything that is within the world, and everything that is outside of it, nothing is hidden from Him. It was said: It is possible that this is from the words of Abraham, confirming his first statement, and generalizing after specializing.
14:39: Then he praised God Almighty for some of His blessings that reached him, saying: 39- Praise be to God, who has given me, in my old age, Ishmael and Isaac. That is, He has given me, in my old age and the age of my wife. It was said that Ishmael was born to him when he was ninety-nine years old, and Isaac was born to him when he was one hundred and twelve years old. It was also said that on here means with: that is, and He is mine despite my old age and my despair of having a child. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication. That is, the Answerer of supplication, from their saying, He heard His speech: if He answered it, took it into account, and acted upon it. It is from adding the attribute that includes exaggeration to the object, and the meaning is: You are indeed the One who answers the supplications of those who call upon You.
14:40: Then he asked God, the Almighty, to make him one who establishes the prayer, maintaining it and not neglecting any of it. Then he said: 40- And of my offspring meaning some of my offspring: that is, make me and make some of my offspring establishers of the prayer. He only specified some of his offspring because he knew that among them were those who did not establish it as it should be. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, make among my offspring those who establish the prayer. Then he asked God, the Almighty, to accept his supplication in general, and his supplication in this context is included in that primarily. It was said that what is meant by supplication here is worship, so the meaning is: And accept my worship with which I worship You.
14:41: Then he asked God to forgive him for what he had done that deserved God's forgiveness, even if it was not a major sin, as is known about the infallibility of the prophets from major sins. Then he asked God to forgive his parents. It was said that he asked God to forgive them before he knew that they were enemies of God, as in His saying: "And Abraham's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him." It was said that his mother was a Muslim, and it was said that he meant Adam and Eve by his parents. Saeed bin Jubair read and for my parents in the singular form, meaning the father alone. Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i read and for my parents meaning Ishmael and Isaac, and Yahya bin Ya'mar read the same. Then he asked forgiveness for the believers. It appears to include every believer, whether he is from his descendants or not. It was said that he meant only the believers from his descendants. 41- The Day the reckoning is established meaning the day when the reckoning of those charged with a duty is established in the place of assembly. The word stands was borrowed for it, which is its true meaning in the man’s standing, to indicate that he is at the peak of righteousness. It was said that the meaning is the day when people stand for the reckoning, and the first is more appropriate. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And when Abraham said the verse, he said: So God answered Abraham’s prayer regarding his children, so none of his children worshipped an idol after his prayer, and God answered him, and made this city secure, and provided its people with fruits, and made him an imam, and made from his descendants those who establish prayer, and accepted his prayer and showed him his rituals and accepted his repentance. Abu Nu’aym narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Aqil bin Abi Talib that when the six men from the Ansar came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he sat with them at Jamrat Al-Aqaba, and called them to God and to His worship and to support in His religion, and they asked him to present to them what was revealed to him, so he recited from Surat Ibrahim And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols’ to the end of the surah, and the people were frightened and humbled when they heard from him what they heard and they responded to him. Al-Waqidi and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Amir bin Saad on the authority of his father who said: Sarah was married to Abraham, and she remained with him for a long time without having a child from him. When she saw that, she gave him Hagar, a Coptic slave girl of hers, and she bore him Ishmael. Sarah became jealous of that and felt bad about herself and rebuked Hagar, so she swore that she would cut off three of her limbs. Abraham said to her: Will you fulfill your oath? She said: What should I do? He said: Pierce her ears and lower them. Lowering means circumcision. So she did that to her, and Hajar put two earrings in her ears, and her beauty increased with them. Sarah said: I see that I have only increased her beauty, and she did not compare it to him being with her. Abraham was very fond of her, so he moved her to Mecca, and he used to visit her every day from Syria on Buraq, out of his passion for her and his lack of patience away from her. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: {Indeed, I have settled some of my descendants}, he said: I have settled Ishmael and his mother in Mecca. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: When Abraham said: {So make hearts among the people yearn toward them}, if he had said: The hearts of the people yearn toward them, the Persians and the Romans would have crowded around him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hakam that he said: I asked Ikrimah, Tawus and Ata bin Abi Rabah about this verse: {So make hearts among the people yearn toward them}, and they said: The House, their hearts yearn toward it, so they come to it. In another version, they said: Their yearning for Mecca is to perform Hajj. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: It descends towards them, he said: It is drawn to them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta’ifi that when Abraham supplicated for the sanctuary, And provide its people with fruits, God moved Ta’if from Palestine. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: God moved a village from the villages of Ash-Sham and placed it in Ta’if because of Abraham’s supplication. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu’ab Al-Iman. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they said: If Abraham, peace be upon him, had said: Then make the hearts of the people incline toward them, the Jews, Christians, and all the people would have made the pilgrimage, but he said: the hearts of the people, so he specified the believers. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: What we conceal and what we declare, he said: Out of grief. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i regarding his statement: Our Lord, You know what we conceal, he said: Out of love for Ishmael and his mother, and what we declare, he said: What we show to Sarah out of coldness towards them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Praise be to God, who has given me in my old age Ishmael and Isaac, he said: This was after that for some time. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr that he said: Abraham was given the good report after one hundred and seventeen years.
14:42: His statement: 42- And do not think is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is an allusion to his nation, so it is as if he said: And do not think, O Muhammad, your nation. It is permissible for it to be addressed to everyone who is fit for it from those who are accountable, and if the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, without allusion to his nation, then its meaning is to confirm what he was upon of not thinking, like his statement: And do not be among the polytheists and the like. It was said that what is meant is: And do not think that He treats them as someone who is unaware of what they do, but rather as someone who watches over them, or what is meant by the prohibition of thinking is to announce that He is aware of that and nothing of it is hidden from Him. In this there is consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and an announcement to the polytheists that delaying the punishment for them is not to please Him with their actions, but rather it is the way of God Almighty in granting respite to the disobedient He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare in horror meaning He delays their punishment and does not hold them accountable for their injustice. This sentence is an explanation for the previous prohibition. Al-Hasan and Al-Salami, and it is a narration from Abu Amr, read it with a noon in nukhrihim. The rest read it with a ta’. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it because of the statement, And do not think that God will be… and the meaning of for the Day when eyes will stare in horror is that the eyes of the people of the gathering will be raised and will not close from the horror of what they will see on that day. This is what Al-Farra’ said. It is said: A man stared and his eyes stared to the sky from the horror of what he saw, and what is meant is that the eyes remained open and did not move from the intensity of confusion and astonishment.
14:43: 43- Muhta'in means hurrying, from the verb ahta'a yahta'a ehta'an: if he hastens, and it is said that the word muhta'a is the one who looks with humility and reverence. And from it: Their home is in the Tigris, and I saw them rushing towards the sky in the Tigris. It was said that Al-Muhta' is the one who stares continuously. Abu Ubaidah said: It may have both meanings, meaning to hurry while staring continuously, and it was said that Al-Muhta' is the one who does not raise his head. Tha'lab said: Al-Muhta' is the one who looks in humiliation and submission, and it was said that he is the silent one. Al-Nahhas said: What is known in the language is Ahta': if he hastens Muqni'i Ra'sihim meaning raising their heads, and Iqna' al-Ras means raising it, and Aqna' Sawthu means raising it, and the meaning is: that on that day they will raise their heads to the sky, looking at it with a look of fear and humiliation and they will not look at each other. It was said that Iqna' al-Ras means lowering it, and it was said that it is said Aqna': if he raises his head, and Aqna': if he lowers his head in humiliation and submission, and the verse is open to both meanings. Al-Mubarrad said: The first saying is better known in the language. The poet said: He lowered his head towards me and looked at me as if he had seen something I was greedy for. Their glances will not return to them meaning their sight will not return to them. The root of the word at-taraf is the movement of the eyelids. The eye was called at-taraf because it is in it. An example of the use of at-taraf to refer to the eye is the saying of Antarah: I lower my gaze if my neighbor appears to me, until my neighbor hides her shelter. And their hearts are air. Air in the language means: the hollow, empty space that is not occupied by bodies. The meaning is: that their hearts are empty of reason and understanding because of what they witnessed of terror, confusion and astonishment. The soul of passion made it an exaggeration, and from this it was said to the fool and the coward his heart is air: meaning he has no opinion or strength in it. It was said that the meaning of the verse is that their hearts left their places and became in their throats. It was said that the meaning is: that the hearts of the disbelievers in this world are empty of goodness. It was said that the meaning is: and their hearts are full of air. What is close in meaning to this verse is the Almighty’s saying: And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty meaning empty of everything except the concern of Moses.
14:44: 44- And warn the people. This refers back to the address of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty commanded him to warn the people, and what is meant is the people in general. It was said that what is meant is the infidels of Mecca, and it was said that the infidels in general. The first is more appropriate because the warning is for the disbeliever as well as for the Muslim. Hence the Almighty’s saying: You can only warn those who follow the message. The meaning of the Day the punishment will come to them is the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:that is, to frighten them on this day, which is the day of the coming of the punishment. He only mentioned the coming of the punishment on it even though it is the day of the coming of the reward, because the situation is one of threat. It was said that what is meant by it is the day of their death, for it is the first time of the coming of the punishment. It was said that what is meant is the day of their destruction by immediate punishment, and the accusative case of day is that it is a second object of warned. “Then those who did wrong will say, ‘Our Lord, delay us for a short term.’” What is meant by those who did wrong here are the al-Nas 114:that is, they will say. The shift to the explicit instead of the implicit is to indicate that injustice is the reason for what happened to them. This is if what is meant by the people are the disbelievers. Assuming that what is meant by them is all Muslims, then the meaning is: Those who wronged among them, who are the disbelievers, will say: Our Lord, give us respite for a short term, for a known period of time, not far away. “We will answer Your call,” that is, Your call to Your servants through the tongues of Your prophets to Your monotheism, and we will follow the messengers, those sent by You to us, so we will act upon what they conveyed to us of Your laws, and we will make up for what we have neglected of. The messengers were only gathered together because their call to monotheism was in agreement, so following one of them is following all of them. This is a request from them to return to this world when the truth has become clear to them in the Hereafter. And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. Then the Almighty narrated what will be answered about them when they say this statement. He said: Did you not swear before that you would not perish? That is, this statement is said to them as a rebuke and a rebuke: That is, did you not swear before this day that you would not perish from this worldly abode? It was said that there was no real oath from them, but rather that was their state of mind due to their being absorbed in desires and their attachment to worldly life. It was said that their oath is what God related about them in His statement: And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that God would not raise up anyone who dies. The answer to the oath is that you would not perish. Rather, it came in the form of address in that you would not perish in order to take into account what you swore, and if it were not for that, He would have said: We would not perish.
14:45: 45- And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves meaning you settled down, it is said that he dwelt in the house and he dwelt in it, and it is the land of Thamud and others like them from the infidels who wronged themselves by disbelieving in God and disobeying Him. And it became clear to you how We dealt with them. Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read nabayyin with the letter noon and the present tense verb. And those other than him read with the letter taa above it and the past tense verb: meaning it became clear to you by observing the signs how We dealt with them of punishment and severe torment for what they committed of sins, and the subject of it became clear to you is what the aforementioned sentence indicates: meaning it became clear to you Our amazing action with them. And We presented examples for you in the Books of God and on the tongues of His Messengers to clarify for you, confirm, and complete the argument against you.
14:46: 46- And they plotted their plot The sentence is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, We did to them what We did, and the fact is that they plotted to reject the truth and establish falsehood, their great plot, in which they exhausted their efforts. And with God is their plot meaning, and with God is the recompense for their plot, or with God is written their plot, so He will recompense them, or with God is their plot with which He plots against them, so that the plot is added to the object. It was said that what is meant by them are the people of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who plotted against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they intended to kill him or exile him. It was said that what is meant is what happened with Nimrod when he tried to ascend to the sky, so he made for himself a coffin and tied its legs to four eagles. And their plot was such that mountains would move from it Omar, Ali, Ibn Masoud, and Abu read And their plot was almost such that mountains would move from it with the silent dal instead of the nun. Other reciters read And if it was with the nun. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Jurayj and Al-Kisa’i read to remove with a fatha on the lam as if it were the lam of initiation. The majority read it with a kasra as if it were the lam of negation. Ibn Jarir said: The preferred reading is this, meaning the reading of the majority, because if it had removed, it would not have been fixed. According to the reading of Al-Kisa’i and those with him, in is the lightened form of the heavy one, and lam is the distinguishing factor. The removal of mountains is like the greatness and severity of their plot: meaning, their plot was prepared for that. Al-Zajjaj said: Even if their plot reaches the point of removing mountains, then God will support His religion. According to the reading of the majority, there are two possible interpretations: One of them is that in is the lightened form of the heavy one, and the meaning is as mentioned above. The second is that it is negative and the broken lam is to emphasize the negation, like his saying: And God would not let your faith go to waste. The meaning is: It is impossible for the mountains to be removed by their plotting, given that the mountains are an example of God’s signs and laws that remain in their state throughout time. So the sentence in this case is a state of the pronoun in they plotted, not of his saying: And with God is their plotting, meaning that the situation is that their plotting was not such that the mountains would be removed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Kharaiti in Masawi Al-Akhlaq narrated on the authority of Maymun Ibn Mihran regarding his statement: And never think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do, he said: It is a consolation for the wronged and a warning to the wrongdoer. Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: For a Day when eyes will stare in horror, he said: By God, their eyes will stare in horror and will not return to them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Rushing, he said: He means by rushing, looking without blinking. With their heads raised, he said: Surrendering means raising their heads. Their glances will not return to them, he said: Their eyes are fixed. And their hearts are empty, there is nothing good in them, so they are like ruins. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Rushing, he said: Staring. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada, Rushing, he said: Hastening. These people narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And their hearts are air, he said: There is nothing in them, it came out of their chests and stuck in their throats. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Marra: And their hearts are air, he said: Perforated, not comprehending anything. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, he said: Warn them in this world before the punishment comes to them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The Day when the punishment will come to them is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: You will have no escape, he said: From what you are in to what you say. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: You will have no escape, he said: Resurrection after death. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, he said: You did the same deeds as them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And if their plot was to cause the mountains to move. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And if their plot was to cause the mountains to move, meaning their polytheism, like his statement: The heavens almost burst from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Al-Anbari narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib that he read this verse: And if their plot were to move the mountains, then he explained it and said: A tyrant among the tyrants said: I will not stop until I see what is in the sky. So he ordered the young eagles to be fed meat until they grew up and became thick. He ordered a coffin to be carved that would hold two men. Then he put a piece of wood in the middle of it, then he tied their legs to pegs, then he starved them, then he put meat on top of the wood. Then he and his companion entered the coffin, then he tied them to the legs of the coffin, then he left them wanting the meat. They went with it as God willed. Then he said to his companion: Open and see what you see. So he opened it and he said: Look at the mountains as if they were flies. He said: Close it, so he closed it, and they went with it as God willed. Then he said: Open it, so he opened it. He said: Look what you see. He said: I see nothing but the sky, and I see it only increasing in distance. He said the sound of the wood, so he aimed it and it swooped down wanting the meat. He heard the mountains. She guided it so that it almost fell from its position. A similar story was narrated to Nebuchadnezzar and Nimrod from the chains of transmission mentioned in Al-Durr Al-Manthur.
14:47: 47- Mukhalaf is in the accusative case as the object of tahsabna, and the accusative case of rusuluhu is in the accusative case as the object of wa'dahu, it was said that this is based on the expansion, and the meaning is: Mukhalaf rusuluhu wa'dahu. Al-Qatibi said: It is from the advanced which is clarified by the delay, and the delayed which is clarified by the advancement, and the same in that Mukhalaf rusuluhu wa'dahu and Mukhalaf rusuluhu wa'dahu, and like what is in the verse is the saying of the poet: You see the bull in it, its head and the rest of it are exposed to the sun. Al-Zamakhshari said: He mentioned the promise to indicate that He never breaks His promise, as in His statement: Indeed, God does not break His promise. Then He said His messengers to indicate that if He does not break His promise to anyone, and it is not His nature to break promises, then how could He break His messengers who are His chosen and best? What is meant by the promise here is what He promised them in His statement: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and God has decreed, “I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. It was also read as He who fails His promise to His messengers with His messengers in the genitive case and His promise in the accusative case. Al-Zamakhshari said: This reading is weak, like the one who read: Their partners killed their children. “Indeed, God is Exalted in Might,” Victorious, no one can overcome Him. Possessor of Retribution, He takes revenge on His friends from His enemies. The sentence is an explanation for the prohibition, and its interpretation was mentioned at the beginning of Al Imran.
14:48: 48- The Day the earth will be replaced by another earth. Al-Zajjaj said: The accusative of day is in replacement of the day that will come to them, or in the circumstance of vengeance. It is finished. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative with an implied meaning indicated by the speech: that is, remember or await. The replacement may be in the essence as in I replaced the dirhams with dinars, or in the attributes as in I replaced the ring with a ring. The verse is open to both possibilities. It has been said that what is meant is the change of its attributes, and most have said this. It has been said that its essence is changed. The meaning of and the heavens is that the heavens will be replaced by other heavens, according to the difference that has been mentioned. And they will emerge before God, the One, the Prevailing, that is, the servants of God or the wrongdoers will emerge as the context indicates: that is, they will emerge from their graves, or what they were concealing will appear from their deeds. The expression of the future with the past tense is to draw attention to the realization of its occurrence as in His statement: And the Trumpet will be blown. The One, the Prevailing, is the One in divinity, the One who is very subduing to those who oppose Him.
14:49: 49- And you will see the criminals, that Day, chained together in shackles is in apposition to they came forth or to changed, and the present tense is used to evoke the image, and the criminals are the polytheists, and that Day means the Day of Resurrection, and chained together means chained together either by making some of them chained together, or they are chained with the devils as in His statement: We have appointed for him a devil, so he is his companion or their hands are made chained to their feet, and the shackles: the chains and fetters, and the preposition and the noun are related to chained together or are a state of its pronoun, it is said I chained him, meaning I bound him, and the noun is chains, so if you want to increase it you say I chained him. Amr ibn Kulthum said: They returned with the loot and the captives, and our sons with the kings in chains. Hassan bin Thabit said: Among the captives, a falcon tightens his chains when he encounters calamity, protecting him. It is said: I handed him over and I handed him over: if you gave him, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: I did not show my father the curse of the chains
14:50: 50- Their garments are of pitch. The garments: the shirts, the singular of which is sirbal, and from it the saying of Ka`b ibn Malik: They meet you with a nerve around the Prophet, who has garments woven by David in battle. And tar: is the tar of camels that they enjoy: meaning their shirts are made of tar that they coat their skins with until that coating returns like garments, and tar was specifically mentioned because it quickly catches fire and has a foul smell. A group said it is copper: meaning their shirts are made of copper. Isa bin Omar read from tar with a fatha on the qaf and a sukoon on the ta’. It was also read with a kasra on the qaf and a sukoon on the ta’, and it was read with a fatha on the qaf and the ta’. This reading was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair, and Ya’qub. This sentence is in the accusative case as a state of and the fire covers their faces meaning it rises over their faces and strikes them, and the faces were specifically mentioned because they are the most honorable part of the body, and they contain the perceptive senses, and the sentence is also in the accusative case as a state of and the fire covers their faces meaning it rises over their faces and strikes them, and the faces were specifically mentioned because they are the most honorable part of the body, and they contain the perceptive senses, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state of and the fire covers their faces
14:51: And 51- That God may reward is related to something omitted: that is, He does that to them in order to reward every soul for what it has earned of sins: that is, a reward that is consistent with what it has earned of good or evil. Indeed, God is swift in account nothing distracts Him from it. Its explanation has been presented above.
14:52: 52- This is a message meaning that what was revealed to you is a message: meaning a notification and sufficient in admonition and reminder. It was said that the reference to what the Almighty mentioned here in His saying: And never think that God is unaware is to Swift in reckoning, meaning that this is sufficient without what the surah contains. It was said that the reference is to the entire surah, and it was said that it is to the Qur’an. The meaning of for people is for the disbelievers, or for all people based on what was said in His saying: And warn people, and and that they may warn with it is conjoined with something omitted: that is, that they may advise and warn with it. The meaning is: and that they may frighten with it. And that they may warn was read with the opening of the lower ya’ and the voiced dhal. It is said that you warned with something, you warned: if you knew about it and prepared for it. And that they may know that He is but One God, meaning that they may know with the previously mentioned cosmic evidence of the Oneness of God, the Almighty, and that He has no partner. And that those of understanding may remember, meaning that those of intellects may take heed. These lams are related to something omitted, and the estimate is: And thus We have sent down, or are related to the mentioned message: that is, it is sufficient for them to advise and warn and know what God has established of arguments and proofs. His Oneness, glory be to Him, and that He has no partner. Let those with minds that understand and comprehend take heed of this. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Possessor of Retribution, he said: Exalted in Might, and God is in His command, He gives respite and His plot is firm, then when He takes revenge, He takes revenge with power. Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Thawban who said: “A Jewish man came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and said: Where will the people be on the Day when the earth is replaced by another earth? The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: In the darkness beyond the Bridge.” Muslim and others also narrated on the authority of Aisha who said: “I was the first to ask the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about this verse: ‘The Day when the earth is replaced by another earth.’ I said: Where will the people be on that Day? He said: On the Bridge.” Al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th, and Ibn ‘Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said regarding his statement: ‘The Day when the earth is replaced by another earth,’ he said: ‘A white earth, as if it were silver in which no forbidden blood has been shed and no sin has been committed.’” It was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azmah, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th from him, with a chain of transmission ending with him, similar to this. Al-Bayhaqi said: The chain of transmission ending with him is more authentic. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: “The Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘They came to me asking me, and I will tell them before they ask me, “On the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth.” He said: ‘A white earth like silver.’ So he asked them, and they said: ‘A white earth like pure gold.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ali, with a chain of transmission ending with him, similar to what was mentioned above, from Ibn Mas’ud. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas, with a chain of transmission ending with him, similar to this. Something similar has been narrated from a group of the Companions, and it is proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa’d, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a white, pure earth, like a pure loaf of bread.’” And in them also from the hadith of Abu Saeed, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the Day of Resurrection, the earth will be a single loaf of bread, which the Almighty will turn over in His hand. The hadith. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: bound together in shackles, he said: the shackles. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah, in shackles, he said: the chains and shackles. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saeed ibn Jubayr, he said: in chains. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, in shackles, he said: in bonds. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, their garments, he said: their shirts. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Zayd something similar. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan regarding his statement: of tar, he said: the tar of camels. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah regarding the verse, he said: this tar is coated with until it burns like fire. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It is molten copper. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr that he read from tar and said: Qatr means yellow, and now means hot. Abu Ubaid, Saeed Ibn Mansour, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar. Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ash’ari who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: If the mourning woman does not repent before her death, she will be raised on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment of tar and a coat of scabies. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: This is a message to the people, he said: The Qur’an. And that they may warn thereby, he said: The Qur’an.
15:1: And it is ninety-nine verses. It is Meccan by consensus, as Al-Qurtubi said. An-Nahhas in his Naskh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Hijr was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr. His statement: 1- Alif, Lam, Ra. The discussion has already been presented in its proper place, and the reference in His statement: That is to what the Surah includes of verses and the definition in the Book. It was said that it is for the genus, and what is meant is the genus of the previous books. It was also said that what is meant by it is the Qur’an, and mentioning the Qur’an after the Book does not detract from this, as it was said that it combined the two names for it. It was also said that what is meant by the Book is this Surah, and the indefiniteness of the Qur’an is for emphasis: meaning the complete Qur’an. Meccan 1- Alif, Lam, Ra. It was said that its meaning is: I am God, I see. These are the verses of the Book. That is, these are the verses of the Book. And a Qur’an. That is, verses of the Qur’an. Clear. That is, clear between what is lawful and what is unlawful, and between truth and falsehood. If it is said: Why did he mention the Book and then say and a clear Qur’an when both are the same? We said: It has been said that each one provides another benefit, as the book is what is written, and the Qur’an is what is collected together. It was said: What is meant by the book is the Torah and the Gospel, and what is meant by the Qur’an is this book.
15:2: 2- Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they were Muslims. Nafi' and Asim read it with a light ba' from perhaps. The rest read it with a heavy ba', and these are two dialects. Abu Hatim said: The people of Hijaz lighten it, and from this is the saying of the poet: Maybe a blow with a polished sword between Basra and a stab from Najla Tamim and Rabi'ah use it heavily. The upper taa may be added, and its origin is that it is used for little. It may also be used for much. The Kufians said: meaning that the infidels wish at many times that they were Muslims. And from this is the saying of the poet: May God provide for his shedding that day and take captives from the tribe of Aqyal It was said that it is here for the sake of belittling because they wished that in some places but not in all of them because they were preoccupied with the punishment. It was said that here the word Lord was added to prepare it to enter the verb, and it was said that it is an indefinite noun meaning something, and that Lord entered here for the future although it only enters for the past, because what is anticipated in His report, glory be to Him, is like the actual reality, so it is as if it was said: Perhaps those who disbelieved would wish that they were Muslims: that is, obedient to His rule and submissive to Him from among His people. And this affection from them was at their death or on the Day of Resurrection. What is meant is that when the matter was revealed to them and the falsehood of what they were upon of disbelief became clear and that the religion with God, glory be to Him, is Islam and no other religion, this affection occurred from them that does not satisfy hunger or satisfy hunger, but is merely regret and remorse and self-blame for what they neglected in the side of God. And it was said that this affection from them was when they witnessed their condition and the condition of the Muslims, and it was said when the sinners among the monotheists came out of the fire, and it appears that this affection is present from them at every time and continues at every moment after the matter was revealed to them.
15:3: 3- Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves This is a threat to them: meaning leave them alone from what you are about to command and forbid them, for they will never heed what is wrong or enter into what is right. Rather, command them to do what they are doing of being busy with eating and enjoying the pleasures of this world, for they are like livestock that are only concerned with that and are not busy with anything else. The meaning is: Leave them as they are of being busy with eating and other worldly pleasures and of being distracted by hope from following you, for they will know the consequences of their actions and the evil of their deeds. In this there is a threat and a warning that cannot be estimated. It is said that such-and-such distracted him: meaning it occupied him, and he was distracted from something, meaning that hope distracted them from following the truth, and they continued in empty hopes and vain wishes until the morning dawned for those with eyes and the matter was revealed and they saw the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. At that time they will taste the consequences of what they did. The three verbs are in the subjunctive mood because they are the answer to the command, and this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
15:4: 4- And We did not destroy a city except that it had a known decree meaning, and We did not destroy a city with some type of punishment except that it had meaning for that city a decree meaning a predetermined term that cannot be preceded or delayed known not unknown or forgotten so it is not conceivable to fall behind it in any way, and the phrase it had a decree is in the accusative case as a state of village even though it is indefinite because it has become, with what it contains of generality, in the rule of the described, and the waw is to differentiate between this sentence being a state, or an adjective, as it specifies it for the state like you say my state is a man with a sword on his shoulder, and it was said that the sentence is an adjective of village, and the waw is to emphasize the connection between the adjective and the described.
15:5: 5- No nation can precede its term meaning no nation can precede its term written in the Preserved Tablet, meaning that its destruction will not come before its term comes. Nor do they delay it meaning nor do they delay it, so their destruction will come after the term set for it has passed. The verb is in the masculine plural form to carry the meaning with emphasis and to take into account the pauses, and for this reason the preposition and noun were omitted and the sentence explains what came before it, so it is as if it was said that this delay should not be deceived by rational people, because every nation has a specific time for the punishment to descend, which is neither earlier nor later. The explanation of the term was presented at the beginning of Surat Al-An'am.
15:6: Then when he finished threatening the infidels, he began to explain some of their arrogance in disbelief, and their persistence in error, while including a statement of their disbelief in the One upon whom the Book was revealed after explaining their disbelief in the Book, so he said: 6- "And they said, 'O you upon whom the Reminder was sent down'" meaning he said: The infidels of Mecca were addressing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mocking him, as they confirmed to him that the Reminder was sent down to him, while they denied that in reality with the most vehement denial and their denial of it with the most eloquent denial, or they meant: O you upon whom the Reminder was sent down, according to his claim, and according to what he claims, "Indeed, you are mad" meaning that because of this claim that you claim, that you are a Messenger of God commanded to convey His rulings, you are mad, because no one of sound mind would claim such a great claim, so their saying this to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is like Pharaoh's saying: "Indeed, your Messenger who has been sent to you is mad.
15:7: 7- "If you do not bring us the angels" Law is a letter of exhortation composed of Law, which is useful for wishing, and Ma, which is an additional particle. The whole indicates exhortation to the action that is included in it, and the meaning is: Why do you not bring us the angels so that they may testify to your truthfulness "if you are of the truthful ones?" Al-Farra' said: The meem in "law ma" is a substitute for the lam in lawla. Al-Kisa'i said: Lawla and Lawla are the same in report and interrogation. Al-Nahhas said: Lawma, Lawla and Hala are one and the same. It was said that the meaning is: Why do you not bring us the angels so that they may punish us for our denial of you.
15:8: 8- "We do not send down the angels except with the truth We do not send down was read with the letter nun in the active form, which is God Almighty, so according to this it is from the word tanzil", and the meaning according to this reading is: God Almighty said in response to the infidels when they asked for the angels to come to them, "We do not send down the angels except with the truth", meaning a sending down that is clothed in the truth that is right for us to send them down in what is required by divine wisdom and divine will, and this is not what you have suggested is what is right for us to send down the angels, and it was read "tanzil in the light form from inzaal": meaning we do not send down the angels except with the truth, and it was read "ma tanzil with the doubled form from farq in the present tense heavy in the active form from tanzil by deleting one of the two ta's": meaning they descend, and it was also read with the superlative in the present tense passive form, and it was said that the meaning of "except with the truth" is: except with the Qur'an, and it was said with the message, and it was said with the torment "and they would not then be reprieved" in the speech there is an omission, and the meaning is: and if We sent down the angels so that they would be hastened to punish, and they would not have been reprieved. The aforementioned sentence is a consequence of the deleted conditional sentence.
15:9: Then He denounced the disbelievers for mocking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying: "O you to whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad." So He, the Most High, said: "Indeed, it is We who sent down the message, meaning, We sent down that message which they denied and attributed to you madness because of it, and indeed, We will be its guardian," from everything that is not befitting of it, such as distortion, alteration, addition, subtraction, and the like. And in it is a severe warning to those who deny it and mock the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that the pronoun in "it" refers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but the former is more appropriate.
15:10: Then the Almighty mentioned that the custom of such infidels with their prophets was like that, as a consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so He said: 10- And We had sent before you meaning messengers, and the word was omitted to indicate sending: meaning messengers who came before you among the sects of the ancients among their nations, followers, and all their groups and factions. Al-Farra’ said: The sect is the nation that follows one another in what they agree upon, and its origin is from the word sha’a if it follows him, and adding it to the ancients is from adding the attribute to the described according to some grammarians, or from deleting the described according to others of them.
15:11: 11- And there came not to them a messenger but they mocked him. That is, there came not to them a messenger but they mocked him, as these infidels do with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The phrase but they mocked him is in the accusative case as a state, or in the nominative case as a description of the messenger, or in the genitive case as a description of him according to the wording, not the location.
15:12: 12- Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals meaning, like that which We caused to enter the hearts of those who mocked Our Messengers, We cause it meaning the Remembrance to enter the hearts of the criminals. So the reference is to what the previous statement indicated of the revelation being coupled with mockery, and the insertion is the insertion of something into something like a thread into a needle, as Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, as He did with the criminals who mocked, We cause misguidance to enter the hearts of the criminals.
15:13: And sentence 13 - They do not believe in it is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun We will send it down: meaning they do not believe in the message that We sent down. It is possible that it is a new sentence to explain what preceded it, so it has no place. It was said that the pronoun in We will send it down is for mockery, and in They do not believe in it is for the message, but this is far-fetched. It is better that the two pronouns are for the message. And the precedent of the ancients has passed meaning their method that God established in their destruction has passed, as they did what they did of denial and mockery. Al-Zajjaj said: And the precedent of God has passed with the ancients by instilling disbelief and misguidance in their hearts.
15:14: Then God the Almighty narrated their insistence on disbelief and their determination to deny and mock. He said: 14- And if We opened to them meaning to these stubborn opponents of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who denied him and mocked him, a gate from the heaven meaning one of its familiar gates and enabled them to ascend to it and they remained therein meaning in that gate ascending they ascended with or without a tool until they saw the wonders of the kingdom in the heaven which no denier can deny and no opponent can be stubborn when seeing them. It was said that the pronoun in they remained refers to the angels: meaning the angels ascended through that gate, and the disbelievers watched them and watched their ascension from that gate.
15:15: 15- They said meaning the infidels due to their extreme stubbornness and increased insolence Our eyes have only been dazzled Ibn Kathir read sakrat with a light pronunciation, and the rest read it with a heavy pronunciation, which is from the drunkenness of drink, or from drunkenness, which is blocking it from feeling. It is said that a river is drunk: if it is blocked and prevented from flowing, and the second reading is preferred with the light pronunciation. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala said: Sakrat means I covered and was covered, and from this is the saying of the poet: The sun rose over her helmet and made the camel's eyes water Abu Ubaid and Abu Ubaidah said the same. It was also narrated on the authority of Abu Amr that it is from the intoxication of drink: that is, what covered their sight covered them, just as the drunkard is covered by what covers his mind. It was said that the meaning of became drunk is became imprisoned as mentioned above. From this is the saying of Aws bin Hajar: So I spent a sleepless night, neither divorced nor drunk Al-Nahhas said: These statements are similar: Rather, we are a people bewitched. They rejected their statement that our eyes were intoxicated, then they claimed that they were bewitched: that is, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, bewitched them. This is a statement of their great stubbornness, from which nothing, whatever it may be, can stop them. For if they see a sign that requires them to believe in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers, they attribute to their eyes that their perception is not real due to the effect of intoxication, or that their minds have been bewitched so that their perception is incorrect. Whoever reaches this level of stubbornness, no admonition will benefit him, and no sign will guide him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: These are the verses of the Book, he said: The Torah and the Gospel. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on These are the verses of the Book, he said: The books that came before the Qur’an. And a clear Qur’an, he said: Clear, and God guided him, gave him the right path and gave him the best. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud and some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims, he said: The polytheists wished on the day of Badr when their necks were struck and they were presented to the Fire that they had believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding the verse, he said: This is about the people of Hell when they see them coming out of the Fire. Saeed bin Mansour, Hannad bin Al-Sarri in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Baath wa Al-Nashur narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: God will continue to intercede, admit, intercede and have mercy until He says: Whoever is a Muslim, let him enter Paradise. This is what He said: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. Ibn Al-Mubarak in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Baath narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Anas that they discussed this verse: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. They said: This is when God gathers the sinners from among the Muslims and the polytheists in the Fire, and the polytheists say: What benefit you have been given to you by what you used to worship? So God becomes angry on their behalf and brings them out by His grace and mercy. Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a chain of transmission that Al-Suyuti said is authentic on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Some people from my nation will be punished for their sins and will be in the Fire as long as God wills them to be. Then the polytheists will taunt them and say: ‘We do not think that your belief in them has benefited you.’ So there will not remain a monotheist except that God will take him out of the Fire. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims.’” Ibn Abi Asim narrated in Al-Sunnah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Hibban, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, also similarly. Hanad ibn Al-Sarri, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat and Abu Nu’aym narrated on the authority of Anas with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There are hadiths in this chapter that specify the reason for the revelation of this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves verse, he said: These are the infidels. He also narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: Leave them he said: Leave them alone. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Az-Zuhri regarding his statement: No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it verse, he said: We see that when its term comes, it is not delayed for an hour or advanced, but as for what its term has not come, God delays what He wills and advances what He wills. I said: This statement of Az-Zuhri has no result or meaning. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: O you upon whom the message has been revealed verse, he said: The Qur’an. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: We do not send down the angels except with the truth verse, he said: With the message and the punishment. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi regarding his statement: And they would not then have been given respite verse, he said: And if the angels had descended, they would not have been given respite from being punished. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in Mujahid, And indeed, We will be its guardians. He said: With Us. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Among the sects of the former peoples. He said: The nations of the former peoples. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Anas regarding his statement, Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals. He said: Polytheism is caused by us in the hearts of the polytheists. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada something similar. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar as well. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada something similar. And the precedent of the former peoples has already passed away. He said: The events of God among the nations that have passed away. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: And they continued therein ascending. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: And the angels continued to ascend, and when they looked at them, they would say, ‘Our eyes have been dazzled.’ He said: Quraysh said it. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas also regarding the verse, saying: And if We opened to them a door from the gates of heaven and the angels continued to ascend therein, differing therein, coming and going, the polytheists would say, ‘Our eyes have been taken away and made to appear to us as though we were bewitched.’ Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: Our eyes have been dazzled means: It has been blocked. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah, who said: Whoever reads sakarat with a lightened sakarat means bewitched.
15:16: When He, the Almighty, mentioned the disbelief of the disbelievers and their helplessness and the helplessness of their idols, He mentioned His dazzling power and His wondrous creation to prove His Oneness, so He said: 16- And We have certainly placed in the heaven constellations. If making means creating, then in the heaven is related to it, and if it means making, then in the heaven is its predicate. The constellations in the language are palaces and mansions, and what is meant by them here are the mansions of the sun, the moon, and the stars, which are the twelve famous ones, as indicated by experience. The Arabs consider knowledge of the positions of the stars and their mansions to be one of the most important sciences, and they use them as evidence of roads, times, fertility, and drought. They said that the universe is twelve constellations, and the names of these constellations are: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. Each three of them are based on the nature of one of the four elements that are engaged in this science. They call Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius a fiery triangle, Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn an earthly triangle, Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius an aerial triangle, and Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces an aquatic triangle. The origin of the zodiac signs is appearance, and from it a woman displays her adornment. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: The zodiac signs are the stars, and they were named thus because of their appearance and height. It was said: The seven moving ones among them, Abu Salih said. It was said: They are palaces and houses in the sky in which there are guards. The pronoun in And We adorned it refers to the sky: that is, We adorned the sky with the sun, the moon, the stars, and the zodiac signs for those who look at it: or for the contemplative, considerate, and inferential if it is from looking, which is inferring.
15:17: 17- And We have preserved it meaning the sky from every accursed devil. Abu Ubaidah said: The accursed is the one who is stoned by the stars, as in his saying: stones for the devils. Stones in the language are throwing stones, then cursing, expulsion, and banishment are called stoning, because the one who throws stones necessitates these meanings.
15:18: 18- Except for he who eavesdrops is a connected exception: that is, except for he who eavesdrops. It is also possible for it to be disconnected: that is, but for he who eavesdrops, then a clear meteor pursues him. The meaning is: We have protected the heaven from the devils from hearing anything of the revelation or anything else, except for he who eavesdrops, for meteors pursue him and kill him or confuse him. The meaning of then a clear meteor pursues him is: it follows him and catches up with him or overtakes him. A meteor is a star or a blazing, bright fire, as in his saying: With a meteor of lightning. Dhu al-Rummah said: Like a planet chasing a demon The planet was called a meteor because of its fire-like brightness, and al-Mubeen means the one who is visible to those who see it and is not confused by it. Al-Qurtubi said: There is disagreement about whether a meteor is to be killed or not. Ibn Abbas said: A meteor injures, burns and confuses, but it does not kill. Al-Hasan and a group said: It is to be killed. According to this statement, there are two opinions about killing them with meteors before they eavesdrop on the jinn: One of them is that they are killed before they eavesdrop on others, so that report from heaven does not reach anyone other than the prophets, and therefore divination is cut off. The second is that they are killed after they eavesdrop on others from the jinn. Al-Mawardi mentioned this, then he said: The first opinion is more correct. He said: There is disagreement about whether meteors were thrown before the mission. Most said yes, and it was said no, but that was after the mission. Al-Zajjaj said: Throwing meteors is one of the signs of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which happened after his birth, because the poets in ancient times did not mention it in their poems. Many scholars have said: We see the stars collapsing, so it is possible that it is as we see, then it becomes fire when it overtakes Satan, and it is possible to say that they throw a flame of fire into the air and it seems to us that it is a moving star.
