15:19: 19- And the earth We spread out meaning We expanded it and spread it out as in His statement: And the earth after that He spread out and in His statement: And the earth We spread out, how excellent are the levelers and in it is a response to those who claimed that it is like a ball And We cast therein firm mountains meaning fixed mountains so that it would not move with its inhabitants, and the explanation of that has been presented in Surat Ar-Ra’d And We caused to grow therein of every well-balanced thing meaning We caused to grow in the earth of every well-measured and known thing, so He expressed that with weight because it is a measure by which things are known, and from that is the saying of the poet: Before I met you, I had a balance for every opponent. It was said that the meaning of weighed is divided, and it was said that it is counted, and what is meant by affirmation is creation and existence, and it was said that the pronoun refers to the mountains: that is, We caused to grow in the mountains every balanced thing of gold, silver, copper, lead, and the like, and it was said that it is weighed with the scale of wisdom, and estimated according to the need, and it was said that what is weighed is what is judged to be good, just as it is said that speech is weighed, meaning good.
15:20: 20- And We have made for you therein means of livelihood that you live on from food and drink, the plural of livelihood, and it was said that it is clothing, and it was said that it is the disposal of the means of livelihood for the duration of life. Al-Mawardi said: And this is the apparent. I said: Rather, the first statement is more apparent, and from it is the statement of Jarir: The cost of living for the Al-Zaid family is on me, and who will provide me with the thin and the foggy? And those for whom you are not providers is in apposition to livelihoods: that is, We have made for you therein those for whom you are not providers: and they are the slaves, servants, and children whose provider in reality is God, even though some of the servants think that He is their provider in consideration of his independence in earning. It is permissible for it to be in apposition to the place of for you: that is, We have made for you therein livelihoods and We have made for those for whom you are not providers therein livelihoods, and they are those mentioned above. This includes animals of different kinds, and it is not permissible to make a apposition to the genitive pronoun in for you because it is not permissible according to most people except by repeating the preposition. It was said that he meant the wild beast.
15:21: 21- And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasures. In is the negative and min is added for emphasis. This construction is general because the indefinite noun falls within the realm of negation with the addition of min, and with the word thing which includes all existing things and is true for each individual of them. This indicates that all things have their treasures with God and nothing is taken out of them. The treasures are the plural of khazana treasury. It is the place where He keeps the most precious things. The mention of the treasures is an example of His power over everything that is possible. The meaning is that all possible things are possible and owned. He brings them out of nothingness into necessity in the amount He wills. The majority of commentators said: What is meant by what is in this verse is rain, because it is the cause of provisions and livelihoods. It was said that the treasuries are the keys: meaning there is nothing but that We have its keys in the sky. The first is what we mentioned of generality for every existing thing, rather a thing may be true of the non-existent according to the known disagreement in that. And We do not send it down except in a known measure. That is, what We send down from the sky to the earth or create for the servants except in a known measure, and the measure is the amount, and the meaning is: God Almighty does not create for the servants anything of those mentioned things except by engaging in that creation in a specific amount according to what His will requires according to the amount of the servants’ need for it, as He Almighty said: And if God were to extend provision to His servants, they would rebel throughout the earth, but He sends down in a measure as He wills. Sending down has been interpreted as giving and interpreted as creating, and interpreted as creating, and the meaning is close, and the phrase and We do not send it down is conjoined with an implied meaning: there is nothing but that We have its treasuries. We send it down and We do not send it down, or in the accusative case as a state.
15:22: 22- And We sent the winds as fertilizers is connected to And We made for you therein livelihood and what is between them is an interruption. Hamza read the wind in the singular. And those other than him read the winds in the plural, and according to Hamza's reading, the lam in the wind is for the genus. Al-Azhari said that the winds are fertilizers because they carry the clouds: that is, they carry them and direct them, then they pass by them and bring them down. God the Almighty said: Until, when they carry heavy clouds: that is, they become pregnant. And a fertile she-camel: if she carries the fetus in her belly, and Al-Farra and Ibn Qutaybah said the same, and it was said that fertilization means inseminated. Ibn Al-Anbari said: The Arabs say: the plant is green, so it is fertile: that is, green, and the meaning is that it fertilizes the tree: that is, with its strength, and it was said that the meaning of fertilization is: those that have insemination. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is and that which carries a pregnant camel, because it squeezes the clouds and produces them as a pregnant camel produces a pregnant camel. It is said: ramih meaning having a spear, laban meaning having milk, and tamir meaning having dates. Abu Ubaidah said: lawaqeh means malaaqeh, he went to the fact that it is the plural of malaqeh. In this verse, the winds that carry water are likened to a pregnant woman, and the pollen of the tree is like the pollen of a pregnant woman. And We sent down water from the sky meaning from the reckoning, and everything that rises above you and shades you is sky, and it was said from the direction of the sky, and what is meant by water here is rainwater and We made it to drink meaning We made that rain for you to drink and for your livestock and your land to drink. Abu Ali said: It is said that you gave him water if you gave him enough to quench his thirst, and you gave him a river: meaning you made it a drink for him. Based on this, Fawqaynakomuhu is more expressive than Saqynakomuhu. It was said that Saqqa and Asqa have the same meaning. And you are not its keepers meaning that its treasuries are not with you, rather its treasuries are with us, and we are its keepers. So He, the Exalted, negated from them what He affirmed for Himself in His statement: And there is nothing but that with Us are its treasuries. It was said that the meaning is: You are not its keepers after We sent it down to you meaning that you are not able to preserve it in wells, ponds, and springs, rather We are the ones who preserve it in them so that it may be a store for you when you need it.
15:23: 23- And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death meaning, We create life in creatures and take it away from them whenever We wish. The purpose of this is to prove with these matters the perfection of His power, the Almighty and Majestic, and that He is able to resurrect and reward His servants according to what they deserve and what His will requires. For this reason, He said: And We are the inheritors meaning of the earth and those on it, because He, glory be to Him, is the Everlasting after the annihilation of His creation, the Living Who does not die, the Eternal Whose existence does not cease, And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth.
15:24: 24- And We have certainly known those among you who have gone ahead. This lam is the one that introduces the oath, and so is the lam in And We have certainly known those who have come after. What is meant is those who have come before in birth and death, and those who have come after them. It has also been said that those who have come before in obedience and those who have come after it. It has also been said that those who have come before in the battlefield and those who have come after are meant. It has also been said that those who have come before are the dead, and those who have come after are the living. It has also been said that those who have come before are the nations who came before the nation of Muhammad, and those who have come after are the nation of Muhammad. It has also been said that those who have come before are those who were killed in jihad, and those who have come after are those who were not killed.
15:25: 25- And indeed, your Lord will gather them together meaning, He is the One who is in charge of that and is able to do it, and no one else is, as is indicated by the separating pronoun from the restriction. And in it is that He, glory be to Him, will reward the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil, because it is the matter intended by the gathering. Indeed, He is Wise He runs things according to what His perfect wisdom requires. Knowing His knowledge encompasses all things, nothing of them is hidden from Him, and whoever is like this has perfect power over everything that He has encompassed and known, and His judgment runs in it, glory be to Him, there is no god but Him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And We have certainly placed in the heaven great constellations, he said: planets. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, he said: the great planets. He also narrated on the authority of Atiyyah, he said: palaces in the heaven in which are guards. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah: the cursed one. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: except for one who steals a hearing, he meant to snatch a hearing, as in his statement: except for one who snatches a snatch. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say that meteors do not kill, but they burn, confuse and injure without killing. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And We have caused to grow therein of every well-balanced thing, he said: known. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: of every well-balanced thing, he said: in proportion. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, who said: things that are weighed. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The mountains do not produce anything like kohl and the like. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: {And for whom you are not providers}, he said: animals and livestock. These narrated on the authority of Mansur, who said: wild animals. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The treasures of God are speech. When He intends a thing, He says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: {But with Us are its treasures}, he said: rain in particular. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The rain has not decreased since God sent it down, but one land receives more rain than another. Then he recited: {And We do not send it down except in a known measure.} Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: No year brings rain more than another year, but God directs it as He wills. Then he recited: “And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories. And We do not send it down except according to a known measure.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: And We send the fertilizing winds, he said: God sends the wind and it carries water and fertilizes the clouds with it, so they produce rain as a she-camel produces rain, and then it rains. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ubayd Ibn Umair who said: God sends the bringer of good tidings and the earth rises up. Then He sends the stirrer and it stirs up the clouds and makes them into fragments. Then He sends the reconciler and it reconciles them and makes them into heaps. Then He sends the fertile winds and they fertilize it and it rains. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Daylami narrated with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: The south wind is from Paradise, and it is the fertilizing wind that God mentioned in His Book. Al-Tayalisi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, Al-Tabarani and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that authenticated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “A woman used to pray behind the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and she was one of the most beautiful women. Some of the people would move forward until they were in the first row so that they would not see her, and some of them would move back until they were in the last row. When he bowed, they would look from under their armpits. Then God revealed: ‘And We have certainly known those among you who went forward, and We have certainly known those who lagged behind. ’” This hadith is narrated by Abu Al-Jawza’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated it on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is more likely to be more authentic. Ibn Kathir said: There is a strong objection in this hadith. Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: Those who advance are the front rows, and those who lag behind are the back rows. Many hadiths have been narrated that the best rows for men are the first and the worst are the last, and the best rows for women are the last and the worst are the first. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ and Muqatil ibn Hibban that the verse is about the battle rows. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Those who advance are in obedience to God, and those who lag behind are in disobedience to God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He means by those who advance those who have died, and by those who lag behind those who are alive and have not died. These people also narrated on his authority, he said: Those who advance are Adam and those of his descendants who have passed away, and those who lag behind are in the loins of men. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada.
15:26: What is meant by man in His statement: 26- And We have certainly created man is Adam because he is the origin of this species, and clay, Abu Ubaidah said: is the mud mixed with sand that clinks when stirred, and when cooked in the fire it is pottery. This is the opinion of most commentators. Al-Kisa'i said: it is the stinking clay, taken from the Arabs' saying the meat became stinky and origin, if it stinks, whether cooked or raw. Al-Hutay'ah said: That is a young man who exerts himself with strength, and his meat is not spoiled by his sword. Hama: the black mud that has changed. Or black mud without specifying the changed. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: You say from it Hama’at Al-Bir Hama with a sukoon: if you removed its mud, and Hama’at Al-Bir Hama with a fat-ha: its mud became abundant, and Ahmaita Ihmaan: the mud was thrown into it. Abu Ubaidah said: Hama with a sukoon on the meem is like Hama’ah meaning with a fat-ha, and the plural is Hama’ like Tamra and Tamr, and Hama is a source like Al-Hala’ and Al-Jaza’, then it was named after it. Al-Minnun Al-Farra’ said: It is the changed, and its origin is from Sunnat Al-Hajar Al-A’la Al-Hajar: if you scraped it, and what comes out between the two stones is called Al-Sinanah and Al-Sinnin, and from it the saying of Abd Al-Rahman bin Hassan: Then I besieged her to the red dome, walking in marble and years. That is, rubbed. It is said: water has become stagnant if it has changed. From this comes his saying: It has not become stagnant and his saying: water that is not stagnant. Both derivations indicate change, because what comes out between the two stones can only be foul. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-masnun is al-masub, and it is from the Arabs’ saying: Sannanat al-ma’ ala al-wajh: if you poured it, and san is pouring. Sibawayh said: Al-masnun is “al-mawsur, taken from sanat al-wajh, which is its image. From this comes the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: You will see a smooth, flawless face with no blemishes or scars. Al-Akhfash said: “Al-Masnun is the accusative, standing, from their saying ‘a face that is long’: if it is long.” The result of these sayings is that when the soil is wet, it becomes clay, then when it stinks, it becomes blackened mud, then when it despairs, it becomes clay. So the root of salsal is blackened mud, and that is why it is described with both of them.
15:27: 27- And the jinn - We created them before from scorching fire. The jinn is the father of the jinn according to the majority of commentators. Ata', Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Muqatil said: He is Iblis. He was called a jinn because he hides himself from the eyes. It is said: He hid something if he covers it. So the jinn hides himself from the eyes of the children of Adam. The meaning of before is: before the creation of Adam. The scorching wind is the sharp wind that penetrates the pores, it occurs during the day and sometimes at night. This is what Abu Ubaidah said. The creation of man and the jinn is mentioned in this place to indicate the perfection of divine power, and to clarify that the One who is capable of the first creation is capable of the other creation.
15:28: 28- And when your Lord said to the angels The circumstance is in the accusative case with an implied verb: that is, remember. After mentioning the creation of man, the Almighty explained what happened when He created him. The explanation of that was presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. The word bashaar is derived from bashara, which is the outer part of the skin. The explanation of salsal and al-hama black mud was presented shortly and in full.
15:29: 29- Then when I have proportioned him meaning I have proportioned his creation and adjusted his human form and perfected his parts and breathed into him of My spirit Blowing: the passage of wind into the cavities of another body. Whoever says that the spirit is a subtle body like air, then its meaning is clear. Whoever says that it is an abstract essence that is not localized and has no state in a localized place. The meaning of blowing, according to him, is preparing the body for the speaking soul to attach to it. Al-Naysaburi said: There is no disagreement that the addition in my spirit is for honor and respect, like the she-camel of God and the House of God. Al-Qurtubi said: The spirit is a subtle body that God has made customary by creating life in the body with that body. Its reality is the addition of creation to the Creator. The spirit is a creation from His creation that He added to Himself as an honor and respect. He said: And similar to it is and a spirit from Him. It was mentioned previously in An-Nisa', So fall down before him in prostration the fa indicates that their prostration is obligatory upon them after the proportioning and blowing without delay, and it is an order to occur from the word to occur occurs. It is evidence that what is commanded is prostration, not just bowing, as has been said. This prostration is a prostration of greeting and honor, not a prostration of worship. God can honor whomever He wills of His creatures however He wills and with whatever He wills. It has been said that prostration was to God Almighty, and Adam was their qiblah.
15:30: 30- Then the angels prostrated, all of them together. God Almighty informed us that the angels prostrated together when God Almighty commanded them to do so without delay. Al-Mubarrad said: His saying, all of them, removed the possibility that some of the angels did not prostrate, and His saying, all of them, is an emphasis after an emphasis, and this was preferred by Al-Zajjaj. Al-Naysaburi said: This is because all of them is definite and does not occur as a state, and if it were correct for it to be a state, it would have been in the accusative case.
15:31: Then He excepted Iblis from the angels and said: 31- Except Iblis, he refused to be with those who prostrate. It was said that this exception is connected because he was from the same class as the angels, but he refused that out of arrogance and pride and envy of Adam, so the word of God was fulfilled against him. It was also said that he was not from the angels, but he was with them, so the name of the angels prevailed over him and he was commanded with what they were commanded, so the exception in this regard was connected. It was also said that the exception is separate based on his not being from them, and their not prevailing over him: that is, but Iblis refused to be with those who prostrate, and the discussion of this has been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. The phrase refused to be with those who prostrate is a resumption explaining how it contains the exception of not prostrating, because not prostrating may be with hesitation, so the Almighty explained that it was in the form of refusal.
15:32: And Julmah 32- He said, 'O Iblis, what is the matter with you that you are not with those who prostrate?' is also a new answer to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did God Almighty say to Iblis after he refused to prostrate? This address to him is not for the sake of honor and respect, but rather for the sake of rebuke and reprimand. The meaning is: What purpose do you have in refusing, and what reason led you to do it so that you would not be with those who prostrated to Adam with the angels, while they are in the same honor, high status, and closeness to God as you have learned.
15:33: And sentence 33 - He said, 'I would not prostrate to a human being whom You created from clay from altered black mud' is a new sentence like the one before it. He made the reason for not prostrating to be that Adam was a human being created from clay from altered black mud, claiming that he was created from a nobler element than Adam's element, and in it is a general indication that he was better than him. He stated this explicitly in another place. He said, I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay. And he said in another place, Should I prostrate to one whom You created from clay? The lam in I prostrate is to emphasize the negation: meaning that is not correct from me.
15:34: So God, the Almighty, answered him by saying: 34- He said, ‘Then get out of it, for you are expelled.’ The pronoun in from it, it was said, refers to Paradise. It was also said to the sky, and it was said to the group of angels: meaning, get out of the group of angels, for you are expelled, meaning stoned with meteors. It was also said that the meaning of expelled is cursed: meaning banished, because whoever is expelled is stoned.
15:35: And indeed upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment meaning that upon you is the expulsion and banishment from the mercy of God Almighty, which will continue upon you and will be binding upon you until the Day of Judgment, which is the Day of Resurrection. Making the Day of Judgment the end of the curse does not necessitate its cessation at that time, because what is meant is its continuity without interruption. The Day of Judgment is mentioned for emphasis, as in the Almighty's saying: As long as the heavens and the earth endure or what is meant is that on the Day of Judgment and after it, he will be punished with what is more severe than the curse, from the types of punishment, so it is as if he does not find for himself what he found before the punishment touched him.
15:36: 36- He said, 'My Lord, then give me respite' meaning, give me time and do not let me die until the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:meaning, Adam and his descendants. He asked to remain alive until that day. When he heard that, he knew that God had delayed his punishment until the Hereafter. It was as if he asked never to die, because if his death was delayed until that day, it would be a day in which there is no death. It was said that he did not ask never to die, but rather asked that his punishment be delayed until the Day of Resurrection and that he not be punished in this world.
15:37: 37- He said, ‘Then you are among those granted respite.’ When he asked for respite, God Almighty answered his request and informed him that he was among those He granted respite to among His creatures whose lives He had delayed, or among those whose punishment He had delayed for what they had committed.
15:38: Then the Almighty explained the end to which He gave him respite. He said: 38- Until the Day of the Appointed Time which is the Day of Resurrection. The Day of Judgment, the Day when they are resurrected, and the Day of the Appointed Time are all expressions about the Day of Resurrection. It was said that what is meant by the Appointed Time is the time close to the Resurrection, at which time he will die.
15:39: 39- He said, 'My Lord, because You have put me in error, I will surely make [things] attractive to them on the earth.' The letter ba is for swearing, and ma is a source. The answer to the oath is I will surely make [things] attractive to them on the earth. That is, I swear by Your tempting me to tempt me, I will surely make [things] attractive to them on the earth, that is, as long as they are in this world. The adornment of this is either by making sins seem good to them and causing them to fall into them, or by distracting them with the adornments of this world from doing what God has commanded them to do, so that they do not turn to anything else. His swearing here by God's tempting him does not contradict his swearing elsewhere by God's might, which is His authority and power, because tempting him is part of what might is true of. And I will surely mislead them all. That is, I will mislead them from the path of guidance and cause them to fall into the path of misguidance and carry them towards it.
15:40: 40- Except for Your sincere servants among them. The people of Medina and Kufa read it with a fatha on the lam: meaning those whom You have chosen from among the servants. The rest read it with a kasra on the lam: meaning those who devoted their worship to You and did not intend it for anyone other than You.
15:41: 41- He said, 'This is a straight path for Me' meaning a right that I must observe, which is that you have no authority over My servants. Al-Kisa'i said: This is a threat and a warning, like when you say to someone you threaten, 'Your path is upon Me and your destination is to Me', and like His saying, 'Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful', so the meaning of this statement is that this path returns to Me, so I reward everyone according to his deeds. It was said that 'upon' here means 'to', and it was said that the meaning is that the straight path is with clarification and argument, and it was said that it means success and guidance. Ibn Sirin, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Qays ibn 'Abbad, Abu Raja', Hamid and Ya'qub read This is a path for Me as an adjective, and its meaning is lofty.
15:42: 42- Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them. What is meant by the servants here are the sincere ones, and what is meant is that he has no authority over them by causing them to commit a sin that would destroy them and from which they do not repent. This does not contradict what happened with Adam and Eve and others like them, for it is a sin that is forgiven because they repented from it. Except for those who follow you of the deviators. God Almighty made an exception from His servants, and they are the followers of Satan from among the deviators from the path of truth who fall into misguidance. This is in agreement with what the accursed Satan said when he said: I will surely mislead them all, except for Your servants among them who are sincere. It can be said that there is a difference between the two statements, for God Almighty's statement negates Satan's authority over all of His servants except for those who follow him from among the deviants, so this includes the sincere ones and others who did not follow Satan from among the deviants. The statement of the accursed Satan includes misleading everyone except the sincere ones, so it includes those who were not sincere nor followers of Satan. A seducer. The result is that between the sincere and the seducers who follow Satan, there is a group that was neither sincere nor seduced by Satan. It has been said that the seducers who follow Satan are the polytheists, and this is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: His authority is only over those who take him as a friend and those who associate others with him.
15:43: Then God Almighty said, threatening the followers of Satan 43- And Hell is their promised place, all together. That is, the promised place for the misguided followers, and all together is an emphasis of the pronoun or a state.
15:44: 44- It has seven gates through which the people of Hell will enter. It was seven because of the large number of its people. For each gate there is a portion for them meaning for the misguided followers, a portion is allotted meaning a known amount distinct from the others. It was said that what is meant by the gates are layers, layer upon layer, and they are: Hell, then Laza, then Al-Hutama, then Al-Sa'ir, then Saqar, then Al-Jaheem, then Al-Haweeya. The highest of them is for the monotheists, the second is for the Jews, the third is for the Christians, the fourth is for the Sabians, the fifth is for the Magians, the sixth is for the polytheists, and the seventh is for the hypocrites. Hell is the highest layer, then what comes after it is below it, then likewise. This is what was said. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Man was created from three things: sticky clay, clay, and aged mud. Sticky clay is the good, fine clay is the fine clay from which pottery is made, and aged mud is the clay that contains mud. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority who said: Clay is water that falls on good earth, then it is removed from it and it cracks, then it becomes like thin pottery. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority who said: Clay is dry soil that gets wet after drying. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority who said: Clay is clay mixed with sand. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority who said: Clay is the clay that when you hit it, it cracks. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority who said: Clay is the clay that you squeeze with your hand and water comes out from between your fingers. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: from black mud, he said: from moist clay. These people also narrated from him: from black mud, he said: from stinking clay. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him: the jinn are the likeness of the jinn, like the monkeys and pigs are the likeness of humans. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, he said: the jinn is Iblis, who was created before Adam. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and the jinn We created before from scorching fire, he said: from the best of fire. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: the hot scorching fire that kills. Al-Tayalisi, Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim and he authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated from Ibn Mas’ud, he said: the scorching fire from which the jinn were created is one part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell. Then he recited: and the jinn We created before from scorching fire, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from him with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: “He said, ‘My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected. ’” He said: Iblis wanted not to taste death, but it was said: You are among those reprieved until the appointed time. He said: The first blast will be when Iblis will die, and between one blast and the next there will be forty years. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin: This is a straight path for me, meaning elevated. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: It has seven gates, the number of levels of Hell, as we mentioned earlier. Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Hunad, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Sifat al-Nar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Baath narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ali, who said: Hell has seven levels, one above the other. The first is filled, then the second, then the third, until it is all filled. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hell has seven gates: one of them is for those who draw the sword against my nation.” There are many hadiths and narrations about the description of Hell. Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib narrated in his history on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Regarding the words of God, ‘For each of their gates is a portion allotted,’ he said: A portion that associated partners with God, a portion that doubted God, and a portion that was heedless of God.”
15:45: His saying: 45- Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs meaning those who are righteous against associating partners with God as the majority of the Companions and Followers said. It was also said that they are those who are righteous against all sins in gardens, which are orchards, and springs, which are rivers. It was read with a damma on the 'ayn from 'ayn according to the original, and with a kasra to take into account the ya'. The construction may mean that all the righteous will have gardens and springs, or that each one of them will have gardens and springs, or that each one of them will have a garden and a spring.
15:46: 46- Enter it The majority read it in the imperative form, estimating the saying: that is, they were told to enter it. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah read it, and it was narrated from Ya'qub, with a damma on the hamza, disconnected, and a fatha on the kha', as a passive verb, meaning that God made them enter it. It has been said that if they were in gardens and springs, how would they be told after that to enter it according to the reading of the majority? For the command to enter indicates that they were not in it. It was answered that the meaning is that when they were in the gardens, and when they moved from one to another, they were told upon reaching the one they wanted to move to, to enter it. The meaning of "in peace, secure" is in safety from harm, and security from fears, or Muslims to each other, or Muslims to them from the angels, or from God the Almighty.
15:47: 47- And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment. Resentment means hatred and enmity. Its interpretation has already been mentioned in Al-A’raf. The accusative of brothers is in the state of being: meaning brothers in religion and sympathy. On thrones facing each other means in a state of being on thrones, and in a specific way, which is facing each other, looking at each other’s faces. Sirr is the plural of sirr - and it has been said that it is the high council prepared for pleasure, and from this their saying: The secret of the valley is for the best place in it.
15:48: 48- No fatigue or exhaustion will touch them therein meaning no weariness or exhaustion because there is nothing that would cause that in Paradise, because it is pure bliss and pure pleasure that they obtain easily, and their demands are met without gain or effort. Rather, as soon as the desire for something occurs to their hearts, that thing is obtained by them pure and innocent. And they will never be expelled from it ever. In this eternal eternity and their knowledge of it is the completion of pleasure and the perfection of bliss, because the knowledge of someone who is in bliss and pleasure that it will end and cease to exist after a while is a reason for his bliss to be spoiled and his pleasure to be disturbed.
15:49: Then He, the Most High, said after He told us what the righteous have with Him of great reward and abundant recompense 49- Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful. That is, inform them, O Muhammad, that I am the One who forgives their sins abundantly and has mercy upon them abundantly, as I have decreed for Myself that My mercy precedes My wrath. O God, make us among Your servants whom You have favored with forgiveness and brought under Your vast mercy.
15:50: Then, when He, glory be to Him, commanded His Messenger to inform His servants of this great good report, He commanded him to mention to them something that includes intimidation and warning so that hope and fear would come together, and good report and warning would meet so that they would be hopeful and fearful. He said: 50- And that My punishment is the painful punishment, meaning very painful. And when God combined for His servants these two matters of good report and warning, they became in a state of middle ground between despair and hope, and the best of things are their middle grounds, which is standing on the feet of hope and fear, and between the states of comfort and awe.
15:51: And the sentence 51- "And inform them about the guests of Abraham is connected to the sentence Inform My servants": that is, inform them about what happened to Abraham, the matter in which he combined hope and fear, and the good report that was mixed with a kind of fear, so that they would consider that and know that it is the way of God Almighty with His servants. Also, since the story included the salvation of the believers and the destruction of the wrongdoers, this was a confirmation of His being the Forgiving, the Most Merciful, and that His punishment is the painful punishment. The explanation of this story was mentioned in Surah Hud.
15:52: And the accusative 52- "When they entered upon him is an implied verb conjoined with Inform My servants" meaning and mention to them their entry upon him, or in the accusative case as a state, and the guest is originally a source, and for this reason it is singular even though they were a group, and it is called a guest because it is added to the host "And they said, Peace" meaning we greeted him with peace "He said, Indeed, we are afraid of you meaning terrified and afraid, and he only said this after he brought the calf to them and saw that they did not eat from it as mentioned previously in Surat Hud And when he saw that their hands did not reach it, he was dismayed at them and felt fear of them" and it was said that he disapproved of their peace because he was not in their country, and it was said that he disapproved of their entering upon him without permission.
15:53: 53- "They said, 'Do not be afraid.' That is, the angels said, Do not be afraid. It was read, Do not be afraid. And it was said, Do not be afraid. From awjalah, meaning I frightened him. And the phrase, Indeed, We give you good tidings of a learned boy," is a new sentence to explain the prohibition of fear. "Al-'Aleem" means one who has much knowledge. And it was said that he is the forbearing, as occurred in another place in the Qur'an. And this boy is Isaac, as mentioned previously in Hud. And he did not name him here, nor did he mention the good tidings of Jacob, being satisfied with what preceded.
15:54: 54- "He said, 'have you given me good report?' The majority read it with the interrogative alif. Al-A'mash read, have you given me good report without the alif, 'ala an al-kabar afflicted me in the accusative case as a state: i.e. with the state of old age and decrepitude. So with what do you give me good report? An interrogative of amazement, as if he was amazed at having a child with what he had reached of old age, which is the custom that no one who has reached that age has a child, and the meaning is: So with what do you give me good report? For giving good report of something that is not customary is not valid. Nafi' read tabashrun with a kasra on the noon and a lightened one, and keeping the kasra to indicate the deleted ya. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaisin read it with a kasra on the noon and stressed on the assimilation of the noon into the noon, and its original form is tabashrunni. The rest read tabashrun with a fatha on the noon.
15:55: 55- "They said, 'We have given you good tidings of truth'" meaning with certainty that cannot be broken, for that is the promise of God and He does not break His promise and nothing is impossible for Him, for He is capable of all things. "So do not be among the despairing." This is how the majority read it, with the alif. Al-A'mash and Yahya bin Waththab read from al-Qanteen without an alif, and this was narrated from Abu Amr: meaning among those who despair of that which We have given you good tidings of.
15:56: 56- "He said, 'And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those astray?' The word yaqantu was read with a fatha on the nun" and with a kasra on it, and these are two dialects. It was reported that the word "nun" was read with a damma: "And those astray are the deniers, or the mistaken ones who have strayed from the path of truth": meaning, I only excluded a child because of my old age, not because I have despaired of the mercy of my Lord.
15:57: Then he asked them why God Almighty had sent them 57- He said, ‘What is your business, O messengers?’ The business: the serious matter and the great affair: meaning, what is your business and what have you brought other than what you have given me glad tidings of? It is as if he understood that their coming was not merely for the sake of good tidings, but that they had another affair for which they were sent.
15:58: 58- They said, ‘Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals.’ That is, to a people who commit crimes, which includes polytheism and what is less than it. These people are the people of Lot.
15:59: Then He excepted from them those who are not criminals, saying: 59- Except the family of Lot, which is a connected exception, because it is from the pronoun in criminals, and if it was from a people, it would have been disconnected because they were described as criminals, and the family of Lot are not criminals. Then He mentioned what the family of Lot will be distinguished by in terms of honor because they did not enter with the people in their crime, so He said: Indeed, We will save them all meaning the family of Lot, and they are his followers and people of his religion, and this sentence is resumed on the assumption that the exception is disconnected, so it is report: meaning, but the family of Lot will be saved from Our punishment. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read We will save them with a light emphasis from Anja. The rest read with a heavy emphasis on Naja. Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim chose this last reading, and salvation and rescue are deliverance from what others fell into.
15:60: 60- Except his wife This exception from the pronoun in whom we will save is to exclude her from the salvation: that is, except for his wife, she is not among those we will save but rather among those we will destroy. It was said that the exception from the family of Lot is in consideration of what was decreed for them regarding salvation, and the meaning is: They said: We were sent to a people of criminals to destroy them except the family of Lot. We will save them except his wife, for she is among those who will perish. The meaning of We decreed that she is among those who will remain behind is that we decided and decreed that she is among those who remain in the punishment with the disbelievers, and the one who remains behind is the one who remains. The poet said: Don't sweep the shoal with its dust, you don't know the outcome Al-Ighbar: remains of milk. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of qadrana is dabrna and it is close to the meaning of qadina and the origin of qadrana is: making something according to the amount of sufficiency. Asim read from the narration of Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal qadrana with a light qadrana and the rest read it with a heavy qadda. Al-Harawi said: They are one and the same, and the qadr was attributed to the angels even though it is from the action of God, the Most High, because of their closeness to God.
15:61: 61- So when the messengers came to the family of Lot, this sentence is a resumption of the statement and destruction of those who deserve destruction and the salvation of those who deserve salvation.
15:62: 62- He said, ‘You are a people who are unknown.’ That is, Lot said to them, You are a people who are unknown. That is, I do not know you, but I do not know you.
15:63: 63- They said, ‘Rather, we have brought you that about which they were in doubt.’ That is, the punishment about which they were doubting. The interruption is about their bringing something that would deny it, as if they said: We have not brought you that which crossed your mind of dislike, rather we have brought you that which would please you, which is their punishment that you were warning them about, and they were lying to you.
15:64: 64- And We have brought you the truth meaning the certainty in which there is no doubt or hesitation, which is the punishment that will inevitably descend upon them. And indeed, We are truthful in that report that We have informed you.
15:65: The interpretation of His statement: 65- So set out with your family during a part of the night in Surat Hud and follow their backs meaning be behind them, driving them away so that none of them will differ and be punished and let none of you look back meaning do not look back, nor should any of them look back so that he sees what punishment has befallen them, so he is preoccupied with looking at that and slows down from the speed of travel and distance from the homes of the wrongdoers. It was said that the meaning of do not look back is: do not stay behind. And go where you are commanded meaning to the direction that God Almighty commanded you to go to, which is the direction of the Levant, and it was said Egypt, and it was said a village of the villages of Lot, and it was said the land of Abraham.
15:66: 66- And We decreed for him meaning We inspired Lot that matter which was the destruction of his people, then He explained it by saying: That the last of these people will be cut off. Al-Zajjaj said: The place of that is in the accusative case, and it is a substitute for that matter. And the last is the other: meaning that the last of them who remains will be destroyed at the time of dawn, and the accusative case of in the morning is in the state: meaning the state of their entering at the time of dawn, and similar to it is So He cut off the last of the people who did wrong. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: Safe he said: They are safe from death, so they will not die, nor grow old, nor become sick, nor go naked, nor become hungry. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ali: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment he said: Enmity. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri who said: Ali bin Abi Talib said: By God, it was revealed about us, the people of Paradise: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [while] they will be brothers, facing each other on thrones. Ibn Asakir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: It was revealed about three tribes of Arabs: Banu Hashim, Banu Taym, and Banu Adi, about Abu Bakr and Umar. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Kathir An-Nawa. He said: I said to Abu Ja`far that so-and-so told me on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn that this verse was revealed about Abu Bakr, Umar and Ali: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment. He said: By God, it was revealed about them, and about whom was it revealed except for them? I said: What resentment is it? He said: The resentment of the Age of Ignorance. There was among the Banu Taym, Banu `Adi and Banu Hashim in the Age of Ignorance. When these people embraced Islam, they loved one another. So I took Abu Bakr by the waist, and `Ali began to heat his hand and massage Abu Bakr’s waist with it, and this verse was revealed. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of `Ali through various chains of transmission that he said to Ibn Talhah: I hope that your father and I will be among those about whom God said: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts the verse. A man from Hamdan said: God is more just than that. `Ali shouted at him with a shout that shook the palace and said: Who then if we are not those? Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali who said: I hope that I, Uthman, Al-Zubayr and Talhah will be among those about whom God said: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment. Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: It was revealed about ten: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talhah, Al-Zubayr, Saad, Saeed, Abdur-Rahman bin Awf, and Abdullah bin Masoud. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Abu Salih, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: On thrones facing each other, he said: They will not see each other’s backs. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Abi Awfa who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to us and recited this verse: Brothers facing each other on thrones. He said: Those who love each other for the sake of God will be in Paradise, looking at each other. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding His statement: No fatigue will touch them therein. He said: Hardship and harm. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) looked out at us from the door through which Banu Shaibah enters and said: Do I not see you laughing? Then he turned away until he was at the Black Stone, then he retreated and said: When I went out, Gabriel came and said: O Muhammad, God the Almighty says: Why do you make My servants despair?” Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful * and that it is My punishment that is the painful punishment. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mus`ab ibn Thabit who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by some of his companions who were laughing and said: ‘Remember Paradise and remember Hell.’ Then the verse, ‘Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful,’ was revealed.” At-Tabarani, Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by and mentioned something similar. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God created mercy when He created it as one hundred mercies, then He kept ninety-nine mercies with Him and sent one mercy to all of His creation. If the disbeliever knew all that is with God of His mercy, he would not despair of mercy, and if the believer knew all that is with God of punishment, he would not feel safe from Hell.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of `Ikrimah: They said, ‘Do not be afraid.’ Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi: Of the despairing. He said: Those who despair. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah: Indeed, they are among those who remain behind, meaning those who remain in the punishment of God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Indeed, you are a people who deny, he said: Lot denied them. And regarding his statement: Because of what they were in doubt about, he said: About the punishment of the people of Lot. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada, Because of what they were in doubt about, he said: They doubted. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And follow their backs, he said: He was commanded to be behind his family, following their backs at the end of them when they walked. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, And go where you are commanded, he said: God brought them out to Ash-Sham. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, And We decreed that matter to him, he said: We revealed it to him. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Their backs will be cut off, meaning their destruction will be uprooted.
15:67: God Almighty mentioned what happened to the people of Lot when the angels arrived at their village, saying: 67- And the people of the city came, rejoicing. That is, the people of the city of the people of Lot, which is Saloum, as mentioned previously. The phrase rejoicing is in the accusative case as a state: that is, rejoicing at the guests of Lot, hoping that they would commit an immoral act.
15:68: F 68- Lot said to them Indeed, these are my guests and he made the guest singular because it is a source as mentioned above, and what is meant is my guests, and he called them guests because he saw them in the form of guests, and his people saw them as handsome men, so they coveted them so do not disgrace it is said: he disgraced him, he disgraces him, disgrace and disgrace if he revealed from his affair what would cause him shame by revealing it, and the meaning is: do not disgrace them by exposing them to immorality so that they know that I am unable to protect the one who came to me, or do not disgrace by disgracing my guest, for whoever does what disgraces the guest has done what disgraces the host.
15:69: 69- And fear God in their matter and do not be disgraced. It may be from khazi which means humiliation and disgrace, and it may be from khazayah which means shyness and shame. The explanation of this has been presented in Hud.
15:70: 70- "They said meaning the people of Lot, answering him, Did we not forbid you from the worlds?" The question is for denial, and the waw is for connecting to something understood: meaning, did we not come to you and forbid you from speaking to us about the matter of any of the people if we intended to commit an immorality against him? It was said that they forbade him from hosting people, and it is permissible to interpret what is in the verse as something more general than these two matters.
15:71: 71- “He said, ‘These are my daughters,’ so marry them. ‘If you are going to do,’ what you have decided to do of committing an immoral act with my guest, then these are my daughters. Marry them lawfully and do not commit an unlawful act.” It was said that he meant by his daughters the women of his people, because the Prophet is like a father to his people. The explanation of this has already been presented in Hud.
15:72: 72- By your life, indeed, in their intoxication, they are wandering blindly. Life and life with the fatha and damma are the same, but they specified the oath with the open one to prefer the lighter one because it is often used on their tongues. This was mentioned by Al-Zajjaj. Al-Qadi Iyad said: The people of interpretation agreed on this that it is an oath from God, the Most High, by the life of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi also narrated the consensus of the interpreters on this meaning, saying: The interpreters unanimously said: God, the Most High, swore here by the life of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to honor him. Ibn Al-Jawzaa said: God, the Most High, did not swear by the life of anyone other than Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is the most honorable of creation in His sight. Ibn al-Arabi said: What is it that prevents God, the Exalted, from swearing by the life of Lot and granting him whatever honor He wills, and all the grace that God, the Exalted, gives to Lot is given from his weakness of honor to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is more honorable to God than him? Do you not see that God, the Exalted, gave Abraham friendship and Moses speech, and gave that to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? So if God, the Exalted, swears by the life of Lot, then the life of Muhammad is higher. Al-Qurtubi said: What he said is good, because His swearing by the life of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is an interpolating statement in the story of Lot. If it is said that God, the Exalted, swore by the fig and the olive and Mount Sinai, and the like, then there is no grace in them. It is answered that there is nothing that God swears by except that there is evidence of its superiority over its kind. The author of al-Kashshaf and his followers mentioned that this is from the angels, meaning that the angels said to Lot, By your life, then he said: It was said that the address was to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he swore by the life of anyone as an honor to him. End quote. Many scholars disliked swearing by other than God Almighty, and authentic hadiths have come in this regard forbidding swearing by other than God, so His servants should not swear by other than Him, and He Almighty swears by whatever He wills of His creations, He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. It was said that swearing by Him Almighty by the fig and the olive and Mount Sinai and the star and the forenoon and the sun and the night and the like is based on the deletion of an adjective that is the object of the oath: that is, by the Creator of the fig, and likewise what comes after it. And in His saying: By your life that is, by the Creator of your life, and the meaning of Indeed, in their intoxication, they wander blindly: in their misguidance, they are confused. He made misguidance because it takes away the mind of its owner as wine takes away his intoxication, and the pronoun refers to the Quraysh, on the basis that the oath is by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to the people of Lot, on the basis that the oath is for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
15:73: 73- Then the great blast or Gabriel's blast took them while they were rising, that is, entering the time of sunrise. It is said that the sun rose: that is, it shone and shone when it rose. It was said that they are two languages with one meaning and the people shone when they entered the time of sunrise. It was said that he meant the rising of dawn, and it was said that the first punishment was at the rising of dawn and extended until sunrise. And the blast: the punishment.
15:74: 74- So We turned its upper part into its lower part meaning the upper part of the city into its lower part and We rained down upon them stones of hard clay of petrified clay. We have already discussed this in detail in Surat Hud.
15:75: 75- Indeed in that meaning in what was mentioned of their story and the explanation of what happened to them are signs for those who take signs” for those who think and consider the matter. From this is the saying of Zuhair: They are a place of entertainment for the friend and an elegant sight for the discerning observer. The other said: Or whenever a tribe came to Ukaz, they would send to their chief to look for Abu Ubaidah said: For those who have insight. Al-Tha’lab said: The one who looks at you from your horn to your feet. The meaning is similar. The origin of al-tawassum is verification and contemplation. It is taken from al-wasm, which is the effect of a sharp object on the camel’s skin.
15:76: 76- And it is on a fixed path meaning the villages of the people of Lot or their city on a fixed road, which is the road from Medina to Ash-Sham, as the traveler on this road passes through those villages.
15:77: 77- Indeed in that the city or villages mentioned is a sign for the believers to consider, for the believers among the servants are those who consider what they see of the signs. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And the people of the city came rejoicing, he said: They rejoiced at the guests of the Prophet of God, Lot, when they came to him because they wanted to come to them with evil. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Did We not forbid you from the worlds? he said: They say: Did We not forbid you from hosting anyone or sheltering him? “He said: These are my daughters, if you were to do so.” Lot ordered them to marry women and wanted to keep his guests with his daughters. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu’aym narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God did not create, nor did He sow, nor did He bring into being a soul more honorable to Him than Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. I have never heard God swear by the life of anyone other than him. He said: By your life, indeed, in their intoxication, they are wandering blindly, meaning: By your life, O Muhammad, and your life and your remaining in this world. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: By your life, he said: By your livelihood. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: God did not swear by the life of anyone except by the life of Muhammad. He said: By your life, the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i who said: They hated for a man to say By my life, seeing it as if he said By my life. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, Indeed, they are in their drunkenness, wandering blindly, meaning, they are playing in their error. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-A’mash regarding the verse, Indeed, in their heedlessness, they are wavering. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayh, The blast seized them like a thunderbolt, and everything that destroys a people is a thunderbolt and a blast. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, two sunrises, he said: When the sun rose. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed in that is a sign, he said: A sign. Do you not see a man sending his ring to his family, saying: Bring such and such, so when they see it they know that it is true? Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: For those who look, he said: For those who ponder. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Qatadah who said: For those who reflect. Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: For those who discern. Al-Bukhari narrated in At-Tarikh, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn As-Sunni, Abu Nu`aym, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Khatib on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of the discernment of the believer, for he sees with the light of God. Then he recited: Indeed in that are signs for those who look. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And indeed, it is on a straight path, meaning for destruction. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: A resident path. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: A clear path.
15:78: His saying: 78- And if the companions of the thicket "if" is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its name is the pronoun of the deleted matter: that is, and if the matter was the companions of the thicket. And the thicket is the thicket, and it is a group of trees, and the plural is a thicket. And it is narrated that their trees were always, and it is the dry, so the meaning is: And if the companions of the gathered trees, and it is said that the thicket is the name of the village in which they were. Abu Ubaidah said the thicket: The city of their city is like Mecca and Bakkah, and the companions of the thicket are the people of Shu'ayb, and their story has come before, and God Almighty limited himself here to describing them as unjust, and He has explained that injustice previously.
15:79: The pronoun in 79- And indeed, they are on a clear path refers to the city of the people of Lot, and the place of the people of the thicket: that is, indeed, the two places are on a clear path, and the path is the name of that which is followed, and among that is the path that is taken. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: The path is called a path because it is followed and followed. Ibn Qutaybah said because the traveler follows it until he reaches the place he wants, and it was said that the pronoun refers to the thicket and Madyan because Shu'ayb was attributed to them.
15:80: Then God the Almighty concluded the stories with the story of Thamud, saying: 80- And the companions of Al-Hijr denied the messengers. Al-Hijr is the name of the land of Thamud. Al-Azhari said that it is between Mecca and Tabuk. Ibn Jarir said: It is a land between Hijaz and Ash-Sham. He said that the messengers were not sent to them except Salih, because whoever denies one of the messengers has denied the rest because they agreed on calling to God. It was said that they denied Salih and the prophets who came before him, and it was said that they denied Salih and the believers who were with him.
15:81: 81- And We gave them Our signs, meaning the signs revealed to their Prophet, including the she-camel, which contained many signs, such as her emergence from the rock, the approach of her offspring when she emerged, her admonition to them, and the abundance of her milk. But they were turning away from them, meaning they did not pay attention. For this reason, they hamstrung the she-camel and disobeyed what their Prophet had commanded them to do.
15:82: 82- And they used to carve out of the mountains, houses. Carving in the speech of the Arabs means: the wild and the carved. He carved it, he carved it with the broken carving: meaning he made it. In the revelation: Do you worship what you carve? meaning you carve. And they used to make for themselves houses in the mountains: meaning they would carve them into the mountains. The accusative of safe is in the state. Al-Farra' said: safe from it falling upon them, and it was said safe from death, and it was said safe from punishment, relying on their strength and reliability.
15:83: 83- So the blast overtook them in the morning, meaning when they were entering the time of dawn. The blast was mentioned previously in Al-A’raf and in Hud, and it will also be mentioned soon.
15:84: 84- So what they were earning did not avail them. That is, what they were earning of money and fortresses in the mountains did not ward off any of God’s punishment from them.
15:85: 85- And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth meaning clothed in truth, which is what is in them of benefits and interests. It was said that what is meant by truth is the reward of the doer of good for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing, as in the saying of the Almighty: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, that He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good with goodness. It was said that what is meant by truth is transience because it is created and every created thing is transience. And the Hour is surely coming when it comes, God will take revenge on those who deserve punishment and will do good to those who deserve goodness. It contains a warning and a threat to the disobedient. Then the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to forgive his people, saying: So forgive with gracious forgiveness meaning overlook them and pardon with gracious forgiveness. It was said that he turned away from them with gracious turning and did not rush them, and treated them with the treatment of the forgiving and forbearing. It was said that this was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
15:86: 86- Indeed, your Lord is the Creator, the All-Knowing. That is, the Creator of all creation, the All-Knowing of their conditions and of the good and bad among them. Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Amr who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: Madyan and the People of the Thicket are two nations to whom God sent Shu`ayb. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The People of the Thicket are the people of Shu`ayb, and the thicket has thickets and trees in it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The thicket is the thicket. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority who said: The People of the Thicket are the people of Madyan, and the thicket is the intertwined trees. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority who said: The thicket is the gathering of something. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority who said regarding His statement: And indeed, they are at a clear front, an apparent chain of transmission. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the People of the Rock who said: The People of the Valley. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority who said: The People of the Rock were Thamud and the people of Salih. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the people of al-Hijr 15:‘Do not enter upon these people unless you are weeping. If you are not weeping, then do not enter upon them, lest the same thing happen to you as happened to them.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stopped at Al-Hijr near the houses of Thamud in the year of the Battle of Tabuk. The people drew water from the wells from which Thamud used to drink, kneaded dough from it and set up pots with meat. He ordered them to pour out the pots and feed the dough to the camels. Then he took them to the well from which the she-camel used to drink. He forbade them from entering upon the people who had been tortured, saying: ‘I fear that the same thing that happened to them might happen to you, so do not enter upon them.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sabra bin Ma’bad that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to his companions at al-Hijr 15:‘Whoever makes something from this water should throw it away.’ He said: ‘Some of them kneaded dough and some of them made hais.’” Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Ali regarding his statement: So pardon with gracious pardon, he said: Contentment without reproach. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab on the authority of Ibn Abbas similarly. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: This verse was before the fighting. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated similarly on the authority of Ikrimah.
15:87: Scholars differed about the seven Mathani, what are they? The majority of commentators said: It is Al-Fatihah. Al-Wahidi and most commentators said that it is the Opening of the Book, which is the opinion of Omar, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Al-Rabi' and Al-Kalbi. Al-Qurtubi added Abu Hurairah and Abu Aliyah, and Al-Naysaburi added Ad-Dahhak and Saeed bin Jubayr. It has been narrated from the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as will be explained, so it is necessary to refer to it. It has been said that they are the seven long ones: Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Ma'idah, Al-An'am, Al-A'raf, and the seventh is Al-Anfal and At-Tawbah, because they are like one Surah since there is no name between them. This opinion was narrated from Ibn Abbas. It has been said that what is meant by the seven Mathani are the Ahzab, for they are seven pages, and Mathani is the plural of Mathna from Tathniyyah or the plural of Mathna. Al-Zajjaj said: It is dual with what is recited after it with it. According to the first opinion, the reason for calling Al-Fatihah Mathani is that it is repeated: i.e. repeated in every prayer. According to the opinion that it is the seven long ones, the reason for calling it Mathani is that the lessons, rulings and punishments are repeated in it. According to the opinion that it is the seven confederates, the reason for calling it Mathani is the repetition of what is in the Qur’an of stories and the like. Ad-Dahhak, Tawus and Abu Malik went to the view that what is meant by the seven Mathani is the entire Qur’an, and it is a narration from Ibn Abbas. They used as evidence the statement of God Almighty: A Book similar and oft-repeated. It was said that what is meant by the seven Mathani are the sections of the Qur’an: which are commands, prohibitions, good tidings, warnings, giving examples, defining blessings, and report of past generations. It was said by Ziyad bin Abi Maryam, and it is not hidden from you that calling Al-Fatihah Mathani does not entail denying calling anything else by this name, and it has been established that it is what is meant by this verse, so the truth of the description of Mathani for anything else does not detract from that. And the Great Qur’an is conjoined with seven of the Mathani, and it is from the conjoining of the general with the specific because Al-Fatihah is part of the Qur’an, and likewise if what is meant by the seven Mathani is the seven long ones because they are part of the Qur’an, but if what is meant by it is the seven parties or all of the Qur’an or its sections, then it is from the category of conjoining one of the two descriptions with the other, as was said in the saying of the poet: To the venerable king and son of the hero What strengthens the fact that the seven oft-repeated verses are the Fatiha is that this surah is Meccan, and most of the seven long verses are Medinan, as is most of the Qur’an and most of its sections. The apparent meaning of His statement, And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses, is that the giving of the seven preceded the revelation of this verse. The of in of the oft-repeated verses is for partiality if you mean by the seven the Fatiha or the long verses, and for clarification if you mean saturation.
15:88: Then when he explained to his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, what he had bestowed upon him of this religious blessing, he turned him away from fleeting, transient pleasures, saying: 88- Do not stretch your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them. That is, do not aspire with your gaze to the adornments of this world, desiring and wishing for it. The categories are the kinds, as Ibn Qutaybah said. Al-Jawhari said: The couples are the companions. Al-Wahidi said: He only stretches his eyes toward something if he keeps looking at it, and keeping looking at it indicates his approval and desire for it. Some of them said: The meaning of the verse is: Do not envy anyone for what he has been given of this world. It was responded that envy is absolutely forbidden. Rather, He said in this Surah: Do not envy anyone for what he has been given of this world. It was responded that envy is forbidden absolutely. Rather, He said in this Surah: Do not envy anyone without a waw, because it was not preceded by a request, unlike what is in Surah Taha. Then, when He forbade him from looking at their wealth and possessions, He forbade him from looking at them, so He said: And do not grieve over them, since they did not believe and were determined to disbelieve and be stubborn. It was said that the meaning is: Do not grieve over what they enjoyed in this world, for the Hereafter is yours. The first is more appropriate. Then, when He forbade him from looking at the wealth of the infidels and not grieving over them. This would entail being lenient with them and with what is with them, He ordered him to be humble towards the believers, so He said: And lower your wing to the believers. Lowering the wing is a metaphor for humility and gentleness. From this is the saying of the Most High: And lower to them the wing of humility. And the saying of Al-Kumait: I lowered my wings of affection to them, to the protection of his kindness, and welcome Its origin is that when a bird folds its chick to itself, it spreads its wing, then holds it over the chick, so this was made a description of the humility of a person towards his followers. It is said that someone has lowered his wing: meaning dignified and calm.
