The wings of the son of Adam are his sides, and from this comes and fold your hand to your wing, and from this comes the saying of the poet: It is enough for you to be a trial for a leader of a people who extends a wing over my sick brother.
15:89: 89- And say, ‘I am the clear warner.’ That is, the warner who shows his people what will befall them of God’s punishment.
15:90: 90- As We sent down upon those who divided It was said that the object is omitted: that is, the object of We sent down, and the meaning is: As We sent down upon those who divided a punishment, so the meaning is: Indeed, I am the clear warner to you of a punishment like the punishment of those who divided that We sent down upon them, as in the saying of the Most High: I warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Aad and Thamud, and it was said that the kaf is redundant, and the meaning is: Indeed, I am the clear warner, I warned you of the punishment that We sent down upon those who divided, and it was said that it is related to His saying: And We have certainly given you meaning We sent down upon you like what We sent down upon the People of the Book, who are the ones who divided, and it is better to relate it to His saying: Indeed, I am the clear warner because it is in the force of a command to warn. And there is disagreement about who those who divided are? Al-Farra’ said: They are sixteen men sent by Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira during the season. They divided up the passes and valleys of Mecca, saying to whoever entered it: Do not be deceived by this one who has come among us, for he is crazy. And sometimes they said he is a magician, or they said he is a poet, or they said he is a soothsayer. So they were called dividers because they divided up these paths. And it was said that they were a people from Quraysh who divided up the Book of God, making some of it poetry, some of it magic, some of it soothsaying, and some of it legends of the ancients. This was said by Qatada. And it was said that they were the People of the Book, and they were called dividers because they used to divide up the Qur’an in mockery, so some of them would say, This surah is mine and this one is yours. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said that they divided their book, scattered it, dispersed it and distorted it. It was said that what is meant is the people of Salih who divided up to kill him, so they were called dividers, as God Almighty said: They divided up by God that we will surely kill him and his family. It was said that they divided up oaths that they swore to, as Al-Akhfash said. It was said that they were Al-Aas bin Wa’il, Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, Umayyah bin Khalaf and Munabbih bin Al-Hajjaj, as Al-Mawardi mentioned.
15:91: 91- Those who made the Qur'an into parts is the plural of 'Udhah, and its root is 'Udhah, a verb from 'Adhah, meaning to make it into parts. So the meaning according to this is: those who made the Qur'an into separate parts, some of it poetry, some of it magic, some of it divination and the like. It was said that it is taken from 'Adhahtuhu, meaning to slander him, so the omitted part is the ha', not the waw. The 'Udhah was pluralized for both meanings, according to the rational people, because of the omission that occurred to it, so they made that a substitute for the omission that occurred to it. It was said that the meaning of 'Udhah is their belief in some of the Book and their disbelief in some of it. What supports that the meaning of 'Udhah is separation is the saying of Ru'yah: God's religion is not limited to bits That is, in the separate parts. It was said that the word bite and biting in the language of the Quraysh means magic. They say to the magician bite him and to the witch bite her. From this comes the saying of the poet: I seek refuge in my Lord from those who blow on knots and bite. In the hadith, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who bites and the one who is asked to bite, and it was interpreted as the witch and the one who is asked to be bewitched. The meaning is that they frequently slandered the Qur’an, and called it magic, lies, and legends of the ancients. The equivalent of ‘udhah in deficiency is lip, and the root is lipha, and the same is sunnah, and the root is sanah. Al-Kisa’i said: ‘udhah means lying and slander, and its plural is ‘udhun. Al-Farra’ said: It is taken from ‘udah, which is a tree that harms and wounds like thorns. It is possible that what is meant by the Qur’an is the Torah and the Gospel because they are among what is read, and what is meant by the dividers are the Jews and Christians, meaning they made them into separate parts, and this is one of the previous sayings.
15:92: 92- By your Lord, We will surely question them all. That is, We will surely question all these infidels on the Day of Resurrection about the deeds they did in this world for which they will be held accountable and questioned. It was said that what is meant is that they will be asked about the word of monotheism.
15:93: And the generality in 93 - "about what they used to do", indicates what is broader than that, and it was said that those responsible here are all the believers, the sinners, and the disbelievers, and this is indicated by His saying: "Then you will surely be asked on that Day about the pleasure" and His saying: "Stop them, for they will be questioned", and His saying: "Indeed, to Us is their return. Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning", and it can be said: Limiting this question to those mentioned in the context and directing the generality to them does not contradict asking others.
15:94: 94- "So proclaim what you are commanded with." Al-Zajjaj said: He says, show what you are commanded with. It is taken from the word "sadi'" which means dawn. The root of "sadi'" is separation and splitting. It is said, "sada'tuhu I split it, fa-sada'u I split it, and tasada'u al-qawm the people split up, and from this is yawma' yasda'un" that day they split up, meaning they disperse. Al-Farra' said: He meant, "So proclaim the matter means, show your religion", so what is with the verb in this case is like a verbal noun. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The meaning of "sada'u bi-ma'mur is, intend. It was said, So proclaim what you are commanded with means, scatter their gathering and their word by calling them to monotheism, for they will disperse. The first is that sada'" means to show, as Al-Zajjaj, Al-Farra' and others said. The grammarians said: The meaning is "with what you are commanded with from the laws," and they allowed it to be a verbal noun: meaning, with your command and your affair. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: That is, declare the matter openly: that is, your matter after making the call public. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to conceal it until this verse was revealed. Then, after being commanded to make the call public, God Almighty commanded him to turn away and not pay attention to the polytheists, saying: And turn away from the polytheists, that is, do not pay attention to them and do not pay attention to them if they blame you for making the call public.
15:95: Then he confirmed this matter and strengthened the heart of his Messenger by saying: 95- Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers even though they were among the greatest of the disbelievers, and the people of power among them. So if God sufficed him with their command to suppress and destroy them, then the command of those who were lower than them would suffice him even more. These mockers were five of the leaders of the people of Mecca: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, Al-Aas bin Wa'il, Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib bin Al-Harith bin Zam'a, Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth, and Al-Harith bin Al-Talalatlah. This is what Al-Qurtubi said and other commentators agreed with him. And God destroyed them all and sufficed them with their command in one day.
15:96: Then He described those who mocked polytheism, saying: 96- Those who set up with God another god. Their sin was not just mockery, but they had another sin, which was polytheism with God Almighty. Then He threatened them, saying: Then they will know how He punished them in the Hereafter and what punishment God Almighty will inflict upon them.
15:97: Then he mentioned another consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the first consolation, that he would suffice them against their evil and repel their plotting, so he said: 97- And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say of the blasphemous statements that include slandering the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with magic, madness, soothsaying, and lying. This happened with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to human nature and human temperament.
15:98: Then He, the Almighty, commanded him to resort to praising and thanking God, the Almighty, to relieve the distress that had befallen him. He said: 98- So glorify the praises of your Lord meaning, while being immersed in His praise: meaning, do the glorification while being immersed in praise. And be among those who prostrate meaning, those who pray. If you do that, God will relieve your distress, remove your grief, and expand your chest.
15:99: Then He ordered him to worship his Lord: that is, to continue to do so until the end, which is His statement: until the certainty comes to you, meaning death. Al-Wahidi said, a group of commentators said: He means death because he is certain of it. Al-Zajjaj said, the meaning is worship your Lord forever, because if it was said worship your Lord without a specific time, it would be permissible for a person to worship once and be obedient. So if he said until the certainty comes to you, then He ordered him to remain in worship forever as long as he lives. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Umar regarding his statement: And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses, that he said: The seven oft-repeated verses are the Opening of the Book. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Daraqutni, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Ali with a similar chain of narration. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Ibn Masoud with a similar chain of narration and added: And the Great Qur’an is the rest of the Qur’an. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: The Opening of the Book was excepted by God for the nation of Muhammad, so He raised it in the Mother of the Book and saved it for them until He brought it out and no one before it was given it. It was said: So where is the seventh verse? He said: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Something similar to this was narrated on his authority through various chains of narration. Ibn Al-Durais, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The seven oft-repeated verses are the Opening of the Book. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b that he said: The seven oft-repeated verses are praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. A similar statement was narrated from a group of the Tabi’un. It was confirmed in Sahih al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abu Sa’id ibn al-Mu’alla that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, Shall I not teach you the best surah before I leave the mosque? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went to leave, but I remembered, so he said, Al-Hamdu Lillahi Rabbil ‘Alamin Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds, it is the seven oft-repeated and the great Qur’an. Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, The Mother of the Qur’an is the seven oft-repeated and the great Qur’an. Thus, it is obligatory for the people to agree that it is the Opening of the Book, but naming it thus does not contradict naming others as we have mentioned. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ‘Umar who said about the verse: They are the seven long ones. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Ibn Mas’ud. Al-Firyabi, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar from Ibn ‘Abbas who said about the verse: They are the seven long ones. Al-Darimi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from Ubayy ibn Ka’b. Something similar was narrated from a group of the Tabi’un. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It is the opening of the Book and the seven long ones. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: What I have repeated from the Qur’an, have you not heard the saying of God, God has sent down the best statement as a consistent Book, repeated. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: The repeated ones in the Qur’an are God mentioning the same story repeatedly. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ziyad bin Abi Maryam regarding the verse, he said: I have given you seven parts: Pass on, forbid, evil, warn, give examples, enumerate the blessings, and recite the report of the Qur’an. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Do not extend your eyes, he said: He forbade a man from wishing for his companion’s money. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Pairs among them, he said: The rich are like and similar. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah who said: Whoever is given the Qur’an and then looks at something that belittles the Qur’an has disobeyed the Qur’an. Has he not listened to His statement: And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses and to His statement: And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting? Ibn Uyaynah also explained the authentic hadith: He is not one of us who does not chant the Qur’an and said: The meaning is that he is content with it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr regarding His statement: And lower your wing he said: Submit. Al-Faryabi, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: As We sent down upon those who divided the verse, he said: They are the People of the Book who divided it into parts, so they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. Ibn Jarir narrated through the chain of narration of Ali ibn Abi Talhah from him who said: Divided into groups. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu`aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was revealed about a group of Quraysh who were preventing people from visiting the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), among them was Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira. Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Anas on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding his statement: By your Lord, We will surely question them all * About what they used to do. He said: About saying, There is no god but God. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Anas, without a chain of transmission ending with him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn `Umar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So proclaim what you are commanded, so carry it out. There is a well-known saying about Ali ibn Abi Talhah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) continued to hide until So proclaim what you are commanded was revealed, so he and his companions went out. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: This is a command from God to His Prophet to convey His message to his people and all to whom He was sent. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: So proclaim what you are commanded he said: Announce what you are commanded. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And turn away from the polytheists he said: It was abrogated by the statement of God the Almighty: Then kill the polytheists. At-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers he said: The mockers were Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth, Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib, Al-Harith bin Aytal As-Sahmi and Al-`As bin Wa’il, and he mentioned the story of their destruction. This has been narrated on the authority of a group of the Companions with some additions and some omissions in their number, over a long period of time. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim in At-Tarikh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Abu Muslim Al-Khawlani who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “It has not been revealed to me to accumulate wealth and be among the merchants, but it has been revealed to me to glorify the praises of your Lord and be among those who prostrate, and worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Masoud, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Daylami narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’. Al-Khatib narrated in Al-Muttafaq wa Al-Muftariq, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abaan bin Uthman bin Hudhayfah bin Aws At-Ta’ifi, who said: Abaan bin Uthman told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to the hadith of Abu Muslim Al-Khawlani. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah bin Umar, until the certainty comes to you, meaning death. Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Al-Hasan. Ibn Jarir narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Zayd.
16:1: Its verses are one hundred and twenty-eight verses. It is all Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata’ and Jabir. It was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ibn Abbas and on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr. An-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Surat An-Nahl was revealed in Mecca except for three verses at the end, which were revealed between Mecca and Medina on the return of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from Uhud. It was said that they are His statement: And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted 1:13, and His statement: And be patient, and your patience is not but through God 1:13 regarding the mutilation of Hamza and the people killed in Uhud, and His statement: Then indeed, your Lord is for those who emigrated 1:13. It was also said that the third is: And do not exchange the covenant of God for a small price 1:13 to His statement: in exchange for the best of what they used to do. This surah is called Surat An-Nahl because of what God enumerated in it. His saying: 1- The command of God has come meaning His punishment of the polytheists. A group of commentators said: The Resurrection. Al-Zajjaj said: It is what He promised them of retribution for their disbelief, and He expressed the future with the past tense to indicate the certainty of its occurrence. It was said that what is meant by the command of God is His judgment of that, and it has occurred and come, but as for what is judged, it has not come, because He, glory be to Him, has decreed that it will occur at a specific time, so before that time comes it does not come into existence. It was said that what is meant by its coming is the coming of its beginnings and preliminaries. So do not hasten it. He forbade them from hastening it: that is, do not seek its presence before that time. The polytheists used to hasten God’s punishment, as Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith said: O God, if this is the truth from You, the verse. The meaning is: God’s command is near, so do not hasten it. Their hastening it was in the manner of mockery, without hastening it in reality. In forbidding them from hastening, He mocked them. Glory be to Him and He is exalted above what they associate with Him. That is, He is transcendent and exalted above their associating partners with Him, or from having a partner with Him. Their associating partners here is what they did of hastening. The torment, or the occurrence of the Hour, is mockery and denial, as it includes their description of Him, glory be to Him, as not being able to do that, and that He is incapable of doing it, and incapacity and lack of ability are attributes of creatures, not attributes of the Creator, so that was polytheism.
16:2: 2- He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command. Al-Mufaddal read on the authority of Asim that the angels descend, and the original is that they descend, so the verb is attributed to the angels. Al-A'mash read that it descends in the passive form, and Al-Ja'fi read on the authority of Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim that we descend with the letter nun, and the subject is God Almighty. The rest read yanzil al-mala'ikah with a lower ya', except that Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr make the noon quiescent. The subject is God, the Most High. The connection of this sentence to what preceded it is that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them about God that He had brought His command near and forbade them from hastening, they hesitated about the way in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, learned of that. So he informed that he learned of it through revelation on the tongues of God's messengers from among His angels. The spirit is the revelation, and similar to it is He casts the spirit from His command upon whomever He wills of His servants. The revelation was called the spirit because it revives the hearts of the believers, for among the revelations is the Qur'an, and it descends from the religion as the spirit descends from the body. It was said that what is meant is the spirits of creation, and it was said that the spirit is mercy, and it was said that it is guidance because it revives the hearts as the bodies revive with spirits. Al-Zajjaj said: The spirit is that in which there is life from God through guidance to His command. Abu Ubaid said: The spirit here is Gabriel, and the ba’ in this case means with, and the min in from his command is explanatory: that is, with things or starting from his command or an attribute of the spirit, or related to descends, and the meaning of upon whomever He wills of His servants is upon whom He has chosen for that, and they are the prophets that they warn. Al-Zajjaj said: that they warn is a substitute for the spirit, that is, He sends them down so that they warn, and that is either an explanation because the revelation descends in it has the meaning of saying, or it is a lightened version of the heavy one and the pronoun of the matter is understood: that is, the matter is that I say to you warn: that is, inform the people that there is no god but Me, that is, command them to believe in My Oneness and inform them of that while frightening them, because in warning there is frightening and threatening, and the pronoun in that is for the matter fateken the address is to those who are impatient by way of turning away, and it is a warning to them against associating partners with God.
16:3: Then when God Almighty guided them to His Oneness, He mentioned the evidence of Oneness, saying: 3- He created the heavens and the earth in truth. That is, He brought them into existence in this state in which they are in truth: that is, to indicate His power and His Oneness. It was said that what is meant by truth here is annihilation and disappearance. Exalted is God “above what they associate with Him.” That is, He is exalted and sanctified above their association with Him or the association of the one they make a partner with Him.
16:4: Then since the human species is the most honorable of the lower creatures, He presented it and mentioned it specifically, saying: 4- He created man which is a name for the genus of this species from a sperm of an inanimate substance that comes out of an animal, which is semen, so He transferred it through stages until its form was completed, and He breathed the spirit into it and brought it out of its mother’s womb to this abode, so it lived in it. Then behold, he after his creation in this manner, is an opponent, meaning he frequently disputes and argues. The meaning is that he is like one who disputes with God Almighty in His power. The meaning of clear is the apparent and clear dispute. It was said that he clarifies about himself what he disputes with of falsehood, and the one who clarifies is the one who expresses what is in his conscience with his speech. Similar to this is the saying of God Almighty: Has man not seen that We created him from a sperm-drop? Then behold, he is a clear opponent.
16:5: Then, after mentioning the creation of man, he created livestock because of the benefit they bring to this species, so being grateful for them is more complete than being denied them otherwise. He said: And the livestock He created for you, which are camels, cows, and sheep. The word blessings and livestock are most often used for camels, but it is also used for the group, and it is not used for sheep alone. From this is the saying of Hassan: And there was still a companion in its meadows, yes and God willing. So the sheep was connected to the blessings, and here they are specifically camels. Al-Jawhari said: The blessings are the singular of the livestock, and this name is most often used for camels. Then when God the Almighty informed that He created them for the children of Adam, He explained the benefit that they have for them, saying: In them is warmth. Warmth is heat, which is what one warms himself with from their wool, fur, and hair. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. And benefits is connected to warmth, which are their milk, riding, offspring, farming with them, and the like. It has been said that warmth is offspring and milk. He said in As-Sahih: Warmth is the offspring of camels and their milk and what is benefited from them. Then he said: Warmth is also heat. Based on this, if the first meaning is intended by warmth, then the benefits must be applied to what is other than it that is benefited from them. If it is applied to the second meaning, then the interpretation of the benefits with what we mentioned is clear. It was said that what is meant by benefits is the offspring in particular. It was said that riding and from it you eat means from its meat and fat. He mentioned this benefit specifically despite it being included under the benefits because it is the greatest of them. It was said that he mentioned it specifically because benefiting from its meat and fat is lost to him in its essence, unlike other benefits that are in it. The presentation of the circumstance indicating the specificity is to indicate that eating from it is the origin, and other than that is rare.
16:6: 6- And for you therein is beauty meaning, for you therein, in addition to what was mentioned above, is beauty. Beauty is what is beautified and adorned, and beauty is goodness. The meaning here is: for you, so it is beautiful and adorned for those who look at it when you rest and when you set it out to pasture meaning at these two times, which are the time of returning it from its pastures, and the time of setting it out to pastures. So, the return is its return in the evening from the pastures, and the release is its journey to its pastures in the morning. It is said, I set the camels out to pasture, meaning, "I set them...
16:7: 7- And carry your burdens The burdens is the plural of thaqal, which is the traveler's provisions of food and other things. It is called thaqal because carrying it is difficult for a person. It was said that what is meant is their bodies. To a country which you could not have reached except with great difficulty meaning that you could not have reached it if they did not have camels to carry your burdens except with great difficulty due to its distance from you and the lack of anything to carry what you need on the journey. Its apparent meaning includes every distant country without specifying it. It was said that what is meant by the country is Mecca, and it was said that Yemen, Egypt and Syria are the Arabs' trade routes, and the difficulty of the soul is its hardship. The majority read it with a kasra on the sheen, and Abu Jaafar read it with a fatha on it. Al-Jawhari said: “And ‘shaq’ means hardship, and from this is his saying: ‘You would not have attained it except with great difficulty.’” Abu Ubaidah narrated it with the opening of the ‘shin’, and they have the same meaning. It is permissible for the open one to be a source of ‘shaqqatu ‘alayhi ashqa shaqan’, and the broken one means half. It is said ‘Akhdhuth sha’at’ and ‘shaqqat sha’at’, and the meaning according to this in the verse is: You would not have attained it except with the departure of the fatigue of the souls from the effort. And God Almighty has bestowed His favor upon His servants by creating livestock in general.
16:8: Then he mentioned camels specifically because of the blessing of carrying heavy loads, unlike cows and sheep, and the exception is from the most general of the general: that is, you would not have achieved it with anything except with great difficulty. 8- And horses, mules, and donkeys in the accusative case in apposition to livestock: that is, He created for you these three types, and Ibn Abi Ubla read in the nominative case in all of them, and horses were called horses because of their strut in their gait, and the singular of horses is kha’il like dha’in is the singular of sheep, and it was said that it does not have a singular. Then, the Almighty gave a reason for the creation of these three types by saying: that you may ride them. This reason is in consideration of most of their benefits, because benefiting from them other than riding is known, such as carrying loads on them. And the conjunction of adornment with the place of that you may ride them because it is in the accusative case as a reason for their creation. He did not say that you may adorn yourself with them so that it would match that you may ride them, because riding is the action of the addressees, and adornment is the action of the adorner, which is the Creator. The truth of this is that riding is what is considered in the intended meaning, unlike adornment, which is not paid attention to by people of high aspirations because it causes conceit. It is as if the Almighty said: I created them for you to ride them, so that you may ward off from yourselves by means of them the harm of fatigue and hardship. As for adorning yourself with them, this is achieved in the matter itself, but it is not intended in itself. Those who say that horse meat is forbidden have used this verse as evidence, saying that the reason for riding indicates that they were created for this benefit and not others. They said: This is supported by the singling out of these three types for mention and excluding them from livestock, which indicates the unity of their ruling in the prohibition of eating. They said: If eating horses was permissible, then mentioning it and being grateful for it would be more appropriate than mentioning riding, because it is of greater benefit. This is what Malik, Abu Hanifah and their companions, Al-Awza’i, Mujahid, Abu Ubaid and others held. The majority of jurists, hadith scholars and others held that horse meat is permissible, and the people of the first opinion have no argument in their justification with the words so that you may ride them because mentioning what is most beneficial does not contradict anything else. We do not accept that eating is of greater benefit than riding until it is mentioned and its mention comes before mentioning riding. Also, if this verse indicated the prohibition of horses, it would indicate the prohibition of domesticated donkeys, and then there would be no need to specify the prohibition for them in the year of Khaybar. We have already mentioned that this surah is Meccan. The result is that the correct evidence has indicated that eating horse meat is permissible. If we were to accept that this verse contains a basis for those who say that it is forbidden, then the established pure Sunnah would remove this possibility and repel this evidence. We have explained this issue in our books in a way that the one who looks into it will not need anything else. And He creates what you do not know means He creates what your knowledge of of creatures will not be nullified other than what He has enumerated here. It has been said that what is meant by the types of insects and vermin in the depths of the earth and in the sea are what humans have not seen or heard of. It has been said that it is what God has prepared for His servants in Paradise and in Hell that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. It has been said that it is the creation of worms in plants and worms in fruits. It has been said that it is a spring under the Throne. It has been said that it is a river of light. It has been said that it is a white earth. There is no reason to limit the interpretation of this verse to one of these types. Rather, what is meant is that He, glory be to Him, creates what His servants do not know, so it includes everything that their knowledge does not encompass. The expression here is in the future tense to evoke the image, because He, glory be to Him, has created. What people do not know.
16:9: 9- And upon God is the direction of the path The direction is a source meaning the agent, so the meaning is And upon God is the direction of the path: that is, the guidance of the one who intends the straight path according to His inevitable promise and His vast favor, and it was said that it is with the deletion of an added word, and the estimate is: And upon God is the clarification of the direction of the path, and the path is Islam, and its clarification is by sending messengers and establishing arguments and proofs, and the intention in the path is that it leads to the desired, so the meaning is: And upon God is the clarification of the path that leads to the desired, And among them is the unjust The pronoun in of them refers to the path in the sense of the road, because it is masculine and feminine, and it was said that it refers to it with the estimation of an added word: that is, and from the type of the path is permissible, deviating from the truth and deviating from it, so it is not guided by it, and from this is the saying of Imru' al-Qais: And from the way is the unjust and the guidance is the intention of the path and from it is the one with income It was said that the path is a metaphor for its owner, and the meaning is: And among them is he who deviates from the path of truth: that is, he who turns away from it, so he is not guided to it. It was said that they are the people of different desires, and it was said that they are the people of disbelieving religions. In the Mushaf of Abdullah it is And among them is he who deviates. And this is how Ali read it. And if He had willed, He could have guided you all. That is, if He had willed to guide you all to the correct path and the true method, He would have done that, but He did not will it. Rather, His will, glory be to Him, required that the path be shown and indicated: And We showed him the two ways. As for actually leading to it, that requires that there be no disbeliever among the servants, nor one of the Muslims who deserves Hell. And the divine will required that some be believers and some be disbelievers, as the Qur’an stated in more than one place. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “When the command of God has come was revealed, the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were terrified until ‘so do not hasten it’ was revealed, and they calmed down.” Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Hafs, who said: When the command of God has come was revealed, they stood up, and the ‘so do not hasten it’ was revealed. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so the command of God has come, meaning the emergence of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘The command of God has come,’ some of the hypocrites said to each other: ‘This man claims that the command of God has come, so hold back some of what you were doing until you see what will happen.’ When they saw that nothing was coming down, they said: ‘We do not think that anything has come down.’ So the verse was revealed: ‘The reckoning of the people has drawn near.’ They said: ‘This man also claims something similar.’ When they saw that nothing was coming down, they said: ‘We do not think that anything has come down.’ So the verse was revealed: ‘And if We should delay the punishment from them for a limited term,’ the verse was revealed.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: ‘The command of God has come,’ he said: ‘The rulings, the limits and the obligations.’ And these narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: ‘The angels descend with the spirit,’ he said: ‘With revelation.’” Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority that he said: The spirit is a command from God and a creation from God’s creation, and He formed them in the image of the sons of Adam, and no angel descends from the sky except that with him is one of the spirit, then he recited: On the Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan: The angels will descend with the spirit, he said: the Qur’an. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Therein is warmth for you, he said: clothing. And benefits, he said: what you benefit from of food and drink. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said: the offspring of every animal. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And carry your burdens to a land, meaning Mecca. You could not reach it except with great difficulty, he said: If you had undertaken it, you would not have been able to do it except with great effort. There are hadiths that permit eating horse meat, including those in the two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Asma’, who said: “We slaughtered a horse during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ate it.” Abu Ubaid, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fed us horse meat and forbade us from the meat of domestic donkeys.” Abu Dawud also narrated a similar hadith, and both meet the conditions of Muslim. It is also proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the meat of domestic donkeys and permitted horses.” As for what Abu Ubaid, Abu Dawud, and Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Khalid ibn Al-Walid, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade eating all fanged beasts of prey, and the meat of horses, mules, and donkeys,” its chain of transmission includes Salih ibn Yahya ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, and there is some criticism of him. Even if we assume that the hadith is authentic, it is not strong enough to contradict the hadiths of permissibility, as this hadith that explicitly prohibits it precedes the day of Khaybar, and thus it is abrogated. Al-Khatib and Ibn Asakir narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his statement: And He creates what you do not know, he said: the mules. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And peace be upon him: Among what God created is an earth of white pearls. Then he cited descriptions of it that indicate that the hadith is fabricated, then he said at the end of it: That is his saying: And He creates what you do not know. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And upon God is the direction of the way meaning: It is upon God to make clear guidance and misguidance. And among them are those who deviate he said: The scattered paths. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his saying: And upon God is the direction of the way he said: It is upon God to make clear what is lawful and what is unlawful, what is obedience to Him, and what is disobedience to Him. And among them are those who deviate he said: Among the paths is one who deviates from the truth. He said: And in the reading of Ibn Mas`ud: And among you is one who deviates. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn al-Anbari narrated in al-Masahif on the authority of Ali that he used to recite this verse: And among you is one who deviates.
16:10: When the Almighty demonstrated His existence, the perfection of His power, and the wonder of His creation through the wonders of the conditions of animals, He wanted to mention the demonstration of what is required through the strange conditions of plants, so He said: 10- It is He who sends down from the sky meaning from the direction of the sky, which is the clouds, water meaning a type of water, which is rain. From it you have a drink. It is possible that for you is related to sent down or it is an advanced predicate, and drink is a delayed subject, and the sentence is an attribute of what and from it is in the accusative case as a state, and drink is the name of what is drunk like food is the name of what is eaten, and the meaning is: The water that descends from the sky is of two types: a type that people drink, and among it is the water of wells and springs, because it is from the rain, according to His saying: And He causes it to flow as springs in the earth and a type from which trees are produced that livestock graze. Al-Zajjaj said: Everything that grows from the ground is a tree, because the structure indicates mixing, and from this, people quarreled when their voices mixed with each other, and the meaning of mixing is obtained in grass and pasture and in that which has a stem. Ibn Qutaybah said: What is meant by trees in the verse is pasture, and it was said that trees are everything that has a stem, like the Almighty’s saying: And the star and the tree prostrate and the conjunction requires difference, so since the star is that which has no stem, the tree must be that which has a stem, and it was answered that the conjunction of the genus to the species is permissible. In it you graze means in the trees you graze your livestock, it is said that the grazing livestock samata tasuma suma ra’at fawa saima, and I named it: meaning I took it out to graze, so I am musimam and it is musamam and rasima, and the origin of samam is to distance in the pasture. Al-Zajjaj said: It was taken from the mark, because it leaves marks on the ground by grazing.
16:11: 2- He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, the olives, the palm trees, and the grapes. Abu Bakr read from Asim, He causes to grow for you thereby the water that He sent down from the sky. The rest read it with the lower yaa: meaning, God causes to grow for you thereby the water that He sent down from the sky. He mentioned the crops because they are the origin of the foods that people live on, and followed it with the olives because they are a fruit in one respect and a condiment in another because of the abundance of fat in them. It is the plural of zaytouna, and the tree itself is called an zaytouna. Then he mentioned the palm trees because they are food and fruit, and they are, along with grapes, the most noble of fruits. He pluralized the grapes because they include different types. Then he referred to the rest of the fruits and said, And from all the fruits. He also summarized the animals that He did not mention previously by saying, And He creates what you do not know. Abi bin Ka'b read, He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, He raises the crops and what follows them. "Indeed in that, meaning the sending down and the growing, is a great sign, indicating the perfection of power and uniqueness in Lordship, for a people who reflect" on God's creations and do not neglect to look. In his products.
16:12: 12- And He has subjected to you the night and the day The meaning of subjecting them to people is making them beneficial to them according to what their interests require and their needs call for. They always alternate like a slave obedient to his master, not disobeying what he orders him to do, not going against his will, and not neglecting to strive for his benefit. The same applies to subjecting the sun, moon, and stars, as they proceed in a unified pattern by which the slaves infer the amounts of time, and are guided by them and know the parts of time. The meaning of subjected is tamed. Ibn Amir and the people of Ash-Sham read and the sun, moon, and stars are subjected in the nominative case as the subject and predicate. The rest read it in the accusative case in apposition to the night and the day. Hafs read from Asim with the nominative case of the stars as the subject and its predicate is subjugated by His command. And with the accusative reading in subjugated it is an emphatic state, because subjugation was understood from His saying and subjugated. Hafs read in a narration with the nominative case of subjugated with the accusative of what preceded it as the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, they are subjugated. Indeed in that the subjugation are signs for a people who reason that is, they use their minds in these effects indicating the existence of the Creator and His uniqueness and the absence of a partner for Him. And the signs were mentioned because the celestial effects are the most evident evidence of the dazzling power, and the clearest testimony to pride and greatness. And he pluralized them to match His saying subjugated. And it was said that the reason for the plural is that each of the subjugation of the night and the day and the sun and the moon and the stars is a sign in itself, unlike what came before about the vegetation, which is one sign. And all of this is not without difficulty, and it is better to say that these three places in which the verse was isolated in some and pluralized in some, each one of them is suitable. For the plural, with consideration, and for the singular, with consideration, so he did not make it in one way, as a temptation and to draw attention to the permissibility of both matters and the goodness of each one of them.
16:13: 13- And what He has dispersed for you on the earth meaning He created: it is said that God dispersed the creation, dispersing them, dispersing them: He created them: so he is a disperser, and from it comes the offspring, which is the offspring of the two heavy things, and the investigation of this has been presented, and it is conjoined with the stars in the nominative and accusative cases: meaning He has subjected to you what He has dispersed on the earth. The meaning is that He, glory be to Him, subjected to them those heavenly and earthly creatures, and the erection of different colors in the state, and its colors: its forms and views, for the scattering of these things in different colors and shapes with the equality of all in physical nature is a great sign indicating the existence of the Creator, glory be to Him, and His uniqueness. Indeed in that the subjection of these matters is a sign clear for a people who remember. For whoever remembers will consider, and whoever considers will infer what is required. It was said that the first station was only devoted to contemplation because of the possibility of presenting the aforementioned doubt, and the second station was devoted to reason because of its mention after removing the doubt and relieving the cause, so whoever does not acknowledge the Oneness after that has no reason, and the third station was devoted to remembrance for the sake of further indication, so whoever doubts after that has no sense, and in this there is an effort that is not hidden. It is better to say here as we said previously in the singularization of the verse in some cases and its pluralization in others, and its explanation is that each of these three places is suitable for mentioning contemplation, mentioning reasoning, and mentioning remembrance for apparent considerations that are not hidden, so in expressing in each place with one of them there was a good temptation that is not found in expressing with one of them in all three places.
16:14: 14- "And it is He who has subjected the sea" God Almighty has blessed us with the subjection of the sea with the ability to ride it and extract what is in it of catch and jewels, because it is among the blessings that God has bestowed upon His servants, along with what it contains of evidence of the Oneness of the Lord Almighty and the perfection of His power. God Almighty has combined for His servants in this position between reminding them of His earthly, heavenly and sea signs, so He guided them to look and reason with the various signs of different places to complete the argument, perfect the warning, clarify the disputes of reasoning, the basis of proof, and the places of consideration and consideration. Then He mentioned the reason for subjecting the sea, saying: "That you may eat from it tender meat meaning fish, and He described it as tender to indicate its tenderness, and to guide us to hasten to eat it because it is something that spoils quickly, and that you may extract from it ornaments which you may wear" meaning pearls and coral as in His Almighty saying: "From them emerge the pearls And the coral. The apparent meaning of his statement, you wear it, is that it is permissible for men to wear pearls and coral: that is, to make it an ornament for themselves, as it is permissible for women. There is no need for what a group of commentators have taken upon themselves to interpret his statement, you wear it, by saying that their women wear it, because they are part of them, or because they wear it for their sake. There is nothing in the pure Shari’ah that requires preventing men from adorning themselves with pearls and coral unless they use it in a manner that only women use it for, because that is forbidden because it is an imitation of them. The Shari’ah has prohibited it, not because it is an ornament of pearls or coral. And you see the ships plowing through it, that is, you see the ships yearning for the water, pushing it with their chests. The water splits the ship with its chest. Al-Jawhari said: The swimmer splits the water with his chest, and the earth splits it for cultivation. It was said that it is female slaves, and it was said that it is obstructed, and it was said that it goes and comes, and it was said that it is a raging ship. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Makhr in the language: the sound of the wind blowing, and it is not restricted to being in water. And that you may seek of His bounty is conjoined with you may extract, and what is between them is an objection, or a reason for an omitted word, the meaning of which is that you may benefit from that and that you may seek, or on the basis of the fact that he did that to seek: that is, to trade in it so that you may obtain profit from the bounty of God, the Most High. And that you may be grateful that is, if you find His bounty upon you and His kindness to you, you will acknowledge His favor upon you and thank Him for that with your tongue and limbs. It was said that perhaps the reason for specifying this favor with the follow-up of thanks is that it involves covering a long distance with heavy loads without engaging in the reasons for travel, rather without movement at all, although it is in the folds of dangers. It is possible to add to what was mentioned about covering the distance in the aforementioned manner what the sea includes of having in it the best food and the most beautiful clothing and the abundance of blessings with their preciousness and good location are among the greatest reasons that call for thanks and necessitate it.
16:15: Then he followed up these blessings that necessitate monotheism and are useful for proving what is required with another blessing and a major verse, saying: 15- And He cast into the earth firm mountains, meaning fixed mountains. It is said that he became firm and established, meaning he became steadfast and established. The poet said: So I was patient, knowing that I would be free to anchor if the coward's soul came out. "That it may sway with you" means that it is unwilling to sway with you, as the Basrans said, or lest it sway with you, as the Kufians said. Al-Mayd: is to sway right and left. Mada something sways, it moves, and the branches sway, and the man swaggers. "And rivers" means that He made rivers in it, because casting here means making and creating, as in His saying: "And I have cast upon you love from Me, and and paths" means that He made paths in it and made them apparent and clear so that you may be guided by them in your travels to your destinations. And the paths are the roads.
16:16: 16- "And signs" meaning He made signs in it, which are the landmarks of the roads. The meaning is that He, the Almighty, made signs for the roads by which they are guided. "And by the star they are guided." What is meant by the star is the genus: that is, they are guided by it in their night travels. Ibn Waththab read "And by the star with a damma on the noon and the jim, and what he meant was the stars, so he shortened it, or it is a plural like saqf and saqf". It was said that what is meant by the star here is Capricorn and Farqandan, as Al-Farra' said, and it was said Al-Thuraya, and it was said that the signs are the mountains, and it was said that they are the stars, because some stars are guided by, and some are signs that are not guided by. The majority of scholars held that what is meant in the verse is guidance in travels, and it was said that it is guidance to the qiblah, and there is nothing to prevent what is in the verse from being interpreted as more general than that. Al-Akhfash said: The discussion ended with His statement "And signs", and His statement: "And by the star they are guided" is a separate discussion from the first.
16:17: Then when he enumerated the verses indicating the Creator, His Oneness, and the perfection of His power, He wanted to rebuke the people of polytheism and stubbornness, so He said: 17- Is He who creates these great creations and does these wondrous deeds like He who does not create anything of them and is not able to bring into existence a single one of them, which are these idols that you worship and make partners with God Almighty, and He applied the term whoever to them, making them follow the path of the people of knowledge, following their claim that they are gods, or similar to His saying Is He who creates because they occur in His company, and in this question there is a rebuke and rebuke of the disbelievers that is not hidden, and how deserving they are of that, for they made some of the creatures partners with their Creator God is exalted above what they associate with Him “Do you not remember” God’s creations indicating His existence, His uniqueness in Lordship, and the wonder of His creation, so that you use them as evidence for that, for because of their clarity, merely remembering them is sufficient for using them as evidence.
16:18: Then when he finished enumerating the verses that are blessings for those who are accountable, he said: "And if you were to count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them." The explanation of this has already been mentioned in Surah Ibrahim. The wise people said: If the slightest defect or deficiency appeared in every part of the human being, it would spoil the blessings for the human being, and he would wish that he could spend the world if it were in his possession so that that defect would be removed from him. He, glory be to Him, directs the body of this human being in the manner that suits him, even though the human being has no knowledge of the existence of that. So how can he be able to count some of God's favors upon him or be able to count them, or be able to thank for the least of them? O our Lord, these are our forelocks in Your hand, submissive to Your great blessings, acknowledging our inability to even begin to thank You for any of them. We cannot count Your praises, for You are as You have praised Yourself, and we cannot express our thanks to You. So overlook our faults and forgive us and let the veil of Your covering fall over our faults, for if You do not do that, we will perish simply because of our failure to thank You for Your blessings. So how about what we have neglected in terms of our laxity in obeying Your commands and refraining from what You have forbidden? How beautiful is what was said by the one who said: Forgiveness is hoped for from the sons of Adam, so how can it not be hoped for from the Lord? So I said, concluding this verse, which is a well-built palace: He is more merciful to me than they are. He is enough for me, He is enough for me, He is enough for me. How beautiful is the way to conclude this gratitude that is not ambiguous to a human being, indicating the greatness of His forgiveness and the breadth of His mercy, saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. That is, He is abundant in forgiveness and mercy. He does not hold you accountable for neglecting to thank Him for His blessings, or for failing to count them, or for being unable to do even the smallest of them. And from His mercy is His continuity upon you and His bestowal of them at every moment and with every breath you take and every movement you make. O God, I thank You as much as the grateful have thanked You in every tongue at every time and as much as the grateful will thank You in every tongue at every time. You have singled me out with blessings that I have not seen in many of Your creation, and if I have seen some of them in some of Your creation, I have not seen the rest of them in them. So how can I be able to thank You? And how can I begin the slightest thanks for the lowest of them? So how can I be able to thank for the highest of them? So how can I be able to thank for any of their types?
16:19: Then He explained to His servants that He is All-Knowing of everything they do, nothing of it is hidden from Him. He said: 19- And God knows what you conceal meaning what you conceal of matters and what you declare meaning what you reveal of them. In it is a threat, an allusion, and a rebuke, and a warning that God must be All-Knowing of the secret and the public, not like the idols that they worship, for they are inanimate objects that have no awareness of anything outward, let alone the secrets, so how can they worship them? Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And what He has created for you on the earth, he said: What He has created for you on the earth of various kinds of animals, trees and fruits are blessings from God that are manifested, so thank God for them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: That you may eat from it fresh meat, meaning the whales in the sea, and extract from it ornaments which you wear, he said: These are pearls. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: And it is He who has subjected the sea that you may eat from it fresh meat, he said: These are the fish and the animals in it. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far who said: There is no zakat on jewelry, then he recited: and extract from it ornaments which you wear. I say: There is a problem with this evidence. What should be relied upon is that the basic principle is that one is free from zakat until evidence is presented that it is obligatory on some type of money, then it is obligatory. It has been reported regarding gold and silver and what is well-known, but there has been no report regarding jewels of various types that indicates that zakat is obligatory on them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mawaakhir, who said: Jawari. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Mawaakhir, who said: It splits the water with its chest. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, Mawaakhir, who said: Two ships sail with one wind, coming and going. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi, regarding His statement, And that you may seek of His bounty, that it is trade. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, firm mountains, that he means the mountains. So that they do not move with you, that is, until they do not move with you. They were on the earth, moving with them, not settling, then they woke up one morning and God had made the mountains, which are the firm mountains, pegs in the earth. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi, regarding His statement, And paths, that he means the paths between the mountains. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Khatib narrated on the authority of Qatada, And paths he said: roads, and signs he said: they are the stars. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: the signs of the day are the mountains. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Kalbi, And signs he said: the mountains. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And signs meaning the landmarks of the roads during the day, And by the stars they are guided meaning at night. And Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Is he who creates like he who does not create? he said: God is the Creator and Provider, and these idols that are worshipped instead of God create but do not create anything and do not possess any harm or benefit for their people.
16:20: God Almighty began to establish that the idols that He referred to in His saying: Like one who does not create are incapable of creating anything, so they do not deserve to be worshipped. He said: 20- And those who invoke besides God meaning the gods that the disbelievers invoke besides God Almighty have these mentioned attributes, which are that they do not create anything of the creations at all, neither great nor small, neither great nor insignificant, and they are created meaning that their attribute is that they create, so how can the created be able to create something other than Him? In this verse there is an additional explanation because He established for them the attribute of deficiency after He negated from them the attribute of perfection, unlike His saying: Is one who creates like one who does not create? If He limited Himself to merely negating the attribute of perfection. The reading of the majority and those whom you invoke with the superscript of the address is in agreement with what preceded it. Abu Bakr narrated from Asim, and Hubayrah narrated from Hafs they invoke with the greeting, which is the reading of Ya'qub.
16:21: Then he mentioned another of their attributes, saying 21- Dead, not alive. This means that the bodies of these idols are dead, with no life in them at all. The addition of not alive is to clarify that they are not like some bodies that die after life is established for them, but rather these have no life at all. So how can they worship them when they are better than them? Because they are alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected. The pronoun in they perceive refers to the gods, and in they are resurrected refers to the infidels who worship idols. The meaning is: these inanimate idols do not perceive when their infidel worshippers will be resurrected. This is done in a way that mocks them, because the perception of inanimate objects is impossible with regard to apparent matters, let alone matters that no one knows except God, the Most High. It was said that it is possible that the pronoun in they are resurrected refers to the gods, meaning that these idols do not perceive when they will be resurrected. This is supported by what was narrated that God resurrects the idols and creates for them spirits with their devils, and then He orders everyone to the Fire. This is indicated by His statement: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. It was said that the speech was completed when He said: And they are created. Then He began by describing the polytheists as dead, not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected. So the two pronouns in this case refer to the infidels. According to the statement that the two pronouns or one of them refers to the idols, the expression for them, despite their not having reason, is in accordance with the belief of rational beings. Whoever worships it, it is rational. Al-Salami read Iyan with a kasra over the hamza, and they are two languages, and it is in the accusative case with the verb that precedes it.
16:22: 22- Your God is one God. When He, glory be to Him, refuted the way of the idolaters, He stated what is the truth in the matter itself, which is His Oneness, glory be to Him. Then He mentioned why the infidels persisted in their polytheism, saying: As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial, of Oneness, and no admonition affects them nor does reminders work in them. And they are arrogant, about accepting the truth, too proud to submit to what is right, and persisting in denial.
16:23: 23- Indeed, God knows what they conceal and what they declare. Al-Khalil said: Indeed, God knows what they conceal of their words and actions and what they declare of them. The confirmation of the speech in Indeed, He does not love the arrogant. That is, He does not love those who are arrogant about the oneness of God and responding to His prophets. The sentence is an explanation of what the previous speech included.
16:24: 24- And when it is said to them, 'What has your Lord sent down?' That is, when someone says to these disbelieving, arrogant infidels, What has your Lord sent down? That is, what has your Lord sent down? Or what has He sent down? It was said that the speaker was Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, and the verse was revealed about him, so this statement from him was in the way of mockery. It was also said that the speaker was the one who came to them, and it was also said that the speaker was the Muslims, so the disbelieving, arrogant polytheists responded, They said, 'Legends of the ancients.' In the nominative case: That is, what you Muslims claim to have been sent down are legends of the ancients, or that the polytheists wanted to mock the Muslims, so they said that what was sent down to you are legends of the ancients. Therefore, what was said that this is not suitable to be an answer from the polytheists does not apply, otherwise the meaning would be that our Lord sent down legends of the ancients and the disbelievers do not acknowledge the sending down, and the reason for its not being mentioned is what we mentioned, and it was said that it is a new statement: that is, what you claim, O Muslims, was not sent down, but rather it is legends of the ancients, and it has been permitted according to the requirements of the science of grammar to put legends in the accusative even if it is not read in this way, and in the accusative it is necessary to have the interpretation that we mentioned: that is, He sent down in response to your claim the legends of the ancients, or they say that from themselves in a mocking manner. Legends are the falsehoods and nonsense that people talk about the first generations, and it is not from the speech of God in anything nor from what God sent down at all in their claim.
16:25: 25- So that they may bear their burdens in full meaning they said this statement so that they may bear their burdens in full. None of them were expiated because of their lack of Islam, which is a reason for expiating sins. It was said that the lam is the lam of consequence, because they did not describe the Qur’an as myths in order to bear the burdens, but since their consequence was that, it was good to explain it like His saying: So that he may be for them an enemy and a grief. It was said that it is the lam of command. And of the burdens of those who mislead them. That is, they bear some of the burdens of those who misled them, because whoever establishes a bad tradition bears its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it. It was said that from is for the genus, not for the partiality: that is, they bear all the burdens of those who mislead them. The location of without knowledge is the accusative case as a state of the subject of mislead them. That is, they mislead people ignorantly, not knowing what they are calling them to, nor knowing what sins are required of them. It was said that it is a state of the object: that is, they mislead those who have no knowledge. And like this verse: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens with their own burdens. In Al-An’am, we have already discussed the statement: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, “How evil is that which they bear,” meaning how evil is that which they bear. 61- And God will save those who fear Him meaning those who feared Him, and the ba in bi-mafazatihim is related to an omitted word which is a state of the relative pronoun: meaning those who are entangled in their bi-mafazatihim. The majority read bi-mafazatihim in the singular as a verbal noun with a mim, and al-fawz means achieving good and escaping evil. Al-Mubarrad said: al-mafaza is a verbal noun derived from al-fawz which means happiness, and if it is plural then it is good, like saying al-sa’adat and al-sa’adat. The meaning is that God will save them with their faz: meaning with their salvation from the Fire and their winning of Paradise. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and Abu Bakr read bi-mafazathimu as the plural of mufaza, and its plural, despite it being a source for the difference of types, and the phrase la maisahum al-sawwum is in the accusative case as a state of the relative pronoun, and likewise the phrase wa la hum yahjunu is in the accusative case as a state: meaning He negates evil and sadness from them. It is possible that the ba in bi-mafazathimu is for causality: meaning because of their victory with the negation of evil touching them and sadness not reaching their hearts because they were satisfied with God’s reward and were safe from His punishment. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that Al-Suyuti said with a sound chain of transmission and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed…’ the verse was revealed about the polytheists of Mecca. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “We used to say that there is no repentance for one who is tempted, and God will not accept anything from him. They knew God, believed in Him, and acknowledged His Messenger, then they turned back from that because of a calamity that befell them. They used to say that to themselves. When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came to Medina, God revealed about them: “O My servants who have transgressed…” the verses. Ibn Umar said: So I wrote it with my own hand and sent it to Hisham ibn Al-‘As. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed who said: When Wahshi converted to Islam, God revealed the verse: And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right, Wahshi and his companions said: We have committed all of this. Then God revealed: “Say: ‘O My servants who have transgressed…’” Al-Bukhari narrated in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to a group of his companions while they were laughing and talking. He said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much.’ Then he turned away and made the people cry, and God revealed to him: ‘O Muhammad, why have you made My servants despair?’ So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned and said: ‘Be of good cheer, strive straight, and come close to God.’” Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab that it was revealed about those who were tempted. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was revealed about the polytheists of Mecca when they said that God would not forgive them for what they had committed of polytheism, killing, and other things. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Thawban: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “I would not like to have the world and everything in it for the sake of this verse: ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves…’ until the end of the verse. A man said: ‘And who has associated others with God?’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was silent. He said: ‘And who has associated others with God?’” Three times. Ahmad, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it and Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Al-Anbari in Al-Masahif, Al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Asma’ bint Yazid: “I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recite: ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins and does not mind. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.’” Ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in Hasan Bil-Zan Billah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he passed by a judge who was reminding the people, so he said: O you who remind the people, do not make people despair. Then he recited: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves… Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin who said: Ali said: Which verse is more comprehensive? So they started mentioning verses from the Qur’an: Whoever does evil or wrongs himself and the like. Ali said: There is nothing in the Qur’an that is more comprehensive than the verse: O My servants. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, the verse: God has called to His forgiveness whoever claims that the Messiah is the son of God, whoever claims that Aziz is the son of God, whoever claims that God is poor, whoever claims that God’s hand is chained, and whoever claims that God is the third of three. He says to these al-Nas 114:Will they not then repent to God and seek His forgiveness? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. Then He called to His repentance whoever is greater in speech than these: whoever says: I am your Lord, the Most High and says: I know of no god for you other than Me. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever despairs of repentance after this has denied the Book of God, but a servant cannot repent until God repents to him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: that a soul should say, that he said: God informed what the servants would say before they said it, and He taught them before they knew.
16:26: Then the Almighty narrated the situation of their predecessors, saying: 26- Those before them plotted. Most commentators have said that what is meant by this is Nimrod bin Canaan, when he built a great building in Babylon, and he wanted to ascend to the sky to fight its people, but God blew the wind, and that building collapsed on him and his people, and they perished. The first is that the verse is general in all the false ones from before who tried to cause harm to those who were right, and the meaning of plotting here is the deceit and planning that does not conform to the truth, and in this there is a warning to the unbelievers who were contemporary with him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that their plotting will come back to them as the plotting of those before them came back to themselves. So God came to their building, meaning God's command came, which is the wind that destroyed their building. The commentators said: God sent a wind that threw the top of the edifice into the sea, and the rest of the foundations fell on them. Al-Zajjaj said: Of the pillars. The meaning is that God’s command came to them from the direction of their foundations, so He shook them. The roof fell on them from above them. Ibn Hurairah and Ibn Muhaisin read the roof with a fatha on the seen and a sukoon on the qaf. The meaning is that the roof fell on them, because after the foundations of the building fall, everything that is supported by them falls. Ibn al-A’rabi said: He only said from above them to let you know that they were under it. The Arabs say a roof fell on us or a wall fell on us if they owned it, even if it did not fall on them. So He came with His saying: from above them to remove this doubt in the speech of the Arabs. So He said: from above them meaning it fell on them, and they were under it, so they perished, but they did not escape. It was said that what is meant by the roof is the sky, meaning the punishment came to them from the sky above them.
