It was said that this verse is a metaphor for their destruction, and the meaning is: He destroyed them, so they were like someone whose building fell on him. There is a difference of opinion about those on whom the roof fell. Some say it was Nimrod, as mentioned above. Others say it was Bukhtanasr and his companions. Others say they were the oath-takers mentioned in Surat al-Hijr 15:And the punishment came to them meaning destruction from where they did not perceive it, but rather from where they were safe.
16:27: Then the Almighty made it clear that their punishment is not limited to the punishment of this world. He said: 27- Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them by sending them into the Fire, and He will disgrace them and humiliate them thereby, and it is connected to an implied meaning: this is their punishment in this world, then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them and say to them with that as a rebuke and reprimand Where are My partners as you claim and allege, Ibn Kathir read from the narration of Al-Bazzi my partners without a hamza, and the rest read with a hamza, then He described these partners by saying: those about whom you used to quarrel Nafi' read with a kasra on the noon as an addition, and the rest read with a fatha on it: meaning you quarreled with the prophets and believers about them, and according to the reading of Nafi' you quarrel with me about them and you are hostile to me: call upon them so that they may repel this punishment that has descended upon you. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: No crime, he said: Yes. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik: No crime, he said: It means the truth. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak who said: No lie. Muslim, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who has in his heart an atom’s weight of arrogance will not enter Paradise, and he who has in his heart an atom’s weight of faith will not enter Hell. A man said: O Messenger of God, a man must have nice clothes and nice shoes. He said: God is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.” There are many hadiths condemning arrogance and praising humility, and there are also many hadiths condemning the love of nice clothes and nice shoes, and similar forms of arrogance. The gist is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained the nature of arrogance, which is rejecting the truth and looking down on people. This is the blameworthy arrogance. The author of Al-Durr Al-Manthur, in his interpretation of this verse, I mean His statement, Indeed, He does not love the arrogant, cited many hadiths that this is not the place to cite, rather the place is to mention what is related to the interpretation of the Noble Book. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding His statement, They said, ‘Legends of the ancients,’ that some of the polytheists of Arabia used to sit on the path of those who came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they passed by, they would ask them and they would tell them what they had heard from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They would say, These are legends of the ancients. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, That they may bear their burdens, the verse, meaning that they will bear along with their sins the sins of those whom they misguide without knowledge. This is similar to His statement, And burdens along with their burdens. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid, and he added, This will not lighten the punishment of those who obey them at all. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Those before them plotted, he said: Nimrod bin Canaan when he built the palace. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam that it was also Nimrod. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Then God attacked their building from the foundations, he said: God’s command came to it from its roots. The roof fell upon them from above them, the roof is the tops of the houses, so their houses closed in on them, so God destroyed and ruined them. And the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, You quarrel about them, he said: You disagree with me. His statement: Those who were given knowledge said, it was said that they were the scholars, so they said it to their nations who used to preach to them but did not pay attention to their preaching. This statement was made by them in the way of gloating, and it was said that they were the prophets, and it was said that they were the angels, and the first is apparent because mentioning them with the description of knowledge indicates that, even though the prophets and angels are people of knowledge, rather they are more deeply rooted in it, but they have a description by which they are mentioned that is more honorable than this description, which is that they are prophets or that they are angels, and the permissibility of the generality does not detract from this, because what is meant is evidence of the appearance only, Indeed, disgrace today meaning humiliation, disgrace, and scandal on the Day of Resurrection and evil meaning torment for the disbelievers is specific to them.
16:28: 28- Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves its interpretation has been presented, and the relative pronoun is in the accusative case as an attribute of the disbelievers, or a substitute for it, or in the accusative case as a specification, or in the nominative case as a subject: meaning they are those whom the angels take in death, and the accusative of wronging themselves is in the state of "so cast down peace" is conjoined with and he will say, where are my partners? and what is between them is an interruption, meaning they acknowledged the Lordship, and submitted at death, and its meaning is submission, said Qatrub, and it was said that its meaning is peace: meaning they made peace and left the hardship, said Al-Akhfash, and it was said that its meaning is Islam, meaning they acknowledged Islam and left what they were doing of disbelief, and the phrase what we used to do of evil may be an interpretation of peace, so that what is meant by peace is the speech indicating it, and it is possible that what is meant by evil here is polytheism, and this statement from them is in the form of denial and lying, and whoever does not allow lying to the people of the Resurrection interpreted it as meaning that they meant that they did not do evil In their belief and according to their assumptions, and similar to it is their saying: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists. So when they said this, the people of knowledge responded to them by saying: Yes, God is Knowing of what you were doing. That is, yes, you were doing evil, and God is Knowing of what you were doing, so He will reward you for it, and this lie will not benefit you at all.
16:29: 29- So enter the gates of Hell meaning that will be said to them at death. The gates of Hell have been mentioned before and that Hell has levels, one above the other, and abiding therein is an implied state because their eternity is in the future. So evil is the abode of the arrogant the one specifically blamed is omitted, and the meaning is, evil is the abode of the arrogant - Hell. What is meant by their arrogance here is their arrogance regarding faith and worship, as in His statement: Indeed, when it was said to them, 'There is no god but God,' they were arrogant.
16:30: Then he followed the descriptions of the wretched with the descriptions of the happy, saying: 30- And it will be said to those who feared God, meaning the believers, What has your Lord sent down? They will say, Good, meaning He sent down good. Al-Tha'labi said: If it is said, why is the answer raised in his statement, Legends of the ancients and raised in his statement, good? The answer is that the polytheists did not believe in the revelation, so it is as if they said that what Muhammad says is legends of the ancients, and the believers believed in the revelation, so he said, Good has been revealed. "For those who do good in this world is good." It is said that this is from the speech of God Almighty, and it is said that it is a narration of the speech of those who feared God, so on this basis it is a substitute for good. On the first basis it is a renewed statement that is presented to praise the righteous, and the meaning is: For those who do good deeds in this world is good: that is, a good reward. "And the home of the Hereafter that is, its reward is better" than what they were given in this world. "And excellent is the home of the righteous the home of the Hereafter, so the specific praise was omitted because what preceded it indicates it.
16:31: And the elevation of 31- Gardens of Eden as a subject whose predicate is what comes after it, or the predicate of a deleted subject, and it was said that it is permissible for it to be the one specifically praised they enter it is either the predicate of the subject, or the predicate after the predicate, and if Eden is indefinite it is an attribute of gardens and likewise underneath which rivers flow and it was said that it is permissible for the two sentences to be in the accusative case as a state on the assumption that the word Eden is a proper noun, and the meaning of rivers flowing beneath the gardens has been presented for them therein whatever they wish meaning for them in the gardens whatever their will falls upon them, pure and easy, which they obtain simply by that thus does God reward the righteous meaning that He rewards them with such a reward, and what is meant by the righteous is everyone who avoids polytheism and what necessitates Hell from sins.
16:32: The relative pronoun in His statement: 32- Those whom the angels take in death, while they are good is in the accusative case as an attribute of the righteous mentioned before it. Al-A'mash and Hamza read takes them in death in this place and in the first place with the lower ya', and the rest read it with the upper tha', and Abu Ubaid chose the first reading, citing as evidence what was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The Quraysh claimed that the angels are females, so mention them. And good has several sayings: pure from polytheism, or righteous, or their actions and words are pure, or good in souls, trusting in what they will receive from the reward of God, or their souls are good in returning to God, or good in death: meaning it is easy for them and there is no difficulty in it, and the phrase "they say peace be upon you" is in the accusative case as a state of the angels: meaning saying peace be upon you, and its meaning has two possible meanings: one of them is that the peace is a warning to them of death. The second is that it is good report for them of Paradise, because peace is security. It was said that the angels say: Peace be upon you, O friend of God. God sends you peace. Enter Paradise for what you used to do, meaning because of your deeds. It was said that this has two possible meanings: The first is that it is good report of entering Paradise at death, and the second is that they say that to them in the Hereafter. This does not contradict entering Paradise through favor, as in the authentic hadith: Straighten your ways and come close, and know that no one will enter Paradise through his deeds. It was said: Not even you, O Messenger of God? He said: Not even me, unless God covers me with His mercy. We have already discussed this. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And it will be said to those who feared God, he said: These are the believers. It will be said to them: What has your Lord revealed? They will say: Good for those who do good, meaning they believed in God and His Books, were commanded to obey Him, urged God’s servants to do good and called them to it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Those whom the angels take in death [while] good, he said: Alive and dead, God has decreed that for them.
16:33: His statement: 33- Do they wait? This verse is an answer to another doubt of those who deny prophethood, for they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to send down to them an angel from heaven to testify to his truthfulness in claiming prophethood. He said: Do they wait to confirm your prophethood unless the angels come to them as witnesses to that? It is possible to say that when they attacked the Qur'an, claiming that it was legends of the ancients, God threatened them with His statement: Do they wait except that the angels come to them to take their souls or the command of your Lord comes meaning His punishment in this world that will uproot them, or what is meant by God's command is the Day of Resurrection. Al-A'mash, Ibn Waththab, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read except that the angels come to them with the lower ya', and the rest read it with the upper tha'. What is meant by them waiting is that they are waiting for the angels to come or for the command of God to come. According to the other interpretation, they have done the action of one who is obligated to be punished and is waiting for it. What is not meant is that they are actually waiting for it, for they do not believe in that or believe it. Thus did those before them, that is, like the action of these people of persisting in disbelief, denial and mockery, the action of those groups of disbelievers who came before them, so God's command came to them and they perished. And God did not wrong them by destroying them with the punishment, for He brought down upon them what they deserved for their disbelief. But they were wronging themselves by what they committed of ugly things. It indicates that their wrongdoing is limited to them in consideration of what it leads to.
16:34: And the sentence 34 - So the evil consequences of what they did befell them is connected to the actions of those before them, and what is between them is an interruption. It has been said that the speech is preceded and postponed, and the meaning is: Thus did those before them, so the evil consequences of what they did befell them, and God did not wrong them. The meaning is: So the recompense for the evil consequences of their actions befell them, or the recompense for their evil actions. And that which they used to mock encompassed them, meaning the punishment that they used to mock or the punishment for their mockery descended upon them in a comprehensive manner. "
16:35: 35- And those who associate others with God said This is another type of their disbelief that God related about them, and what is meant by those who associate others with God here are the people of Mecca If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him meaning if He had willed that we not worship anything other than Him, we would not have worshipped that nor our fathers who were on what we are on now of the religion of disbelief and association with God. Al-Zajjaj said: They said this in mockery, and if they had said it out of belief, they would have been believers. We have already discussed something similar in Surat al-An’am 6:Nor have We forbidden anything besides Him of the sa’iba and the bha’ir and the like. Their intention with this statement, which is linked to the will, is to cast aspersions on the message: that is, if what the Messenger said was true, regarding the prohibition of worshipping other than God, and the prohibition of forbidding what God did not forbid, narrating that from God, then nothing would have happened from us that contradicted what He wanted from us, for He willed that, and what He willed was and what He did not will was not. So when we worshipped other than Him and forbade what He did not forbid, that was evidence that that was what was in accordance with His will and in agreement with His desire, even though in reality they do not acknowledge that or admit it, but they intended what we mentioned of casting aspersions on the Messengers: Thus did those before them from the groups of disbelievers, for they associated partners with God and forbade what He did not forbid and argued with His Messengers falsely and mocked them. Then he said: Is there any duty upon the messengers whom God sends to His servants with what He has prescribed for them of His laws, the most important of which is His oneness and abandoning polytheism with Him, except to convey to those to whom they were sent what they were commanded to convey, a clear message that the recipients understand and that is not confusing to them?
16:36: Then He, the Almighty, confirmed this and made it more clear, saying: 36- And We have certainly sent to every nation a messenger, just as We sent to these people to establish the proof against them, and We never punish until We have sent a messenger, and that in His statement, that you worship God, is either a source: that is, We sent that you worship God, or it is an explanation because in sending there is the meaning of saying, and avoid false gods, that is, leave every deity other than God, such as Satan, the soothsayer, the idol, and everyone who calls to misguidance. And among them, that is, among these nations to which God sent His messengers, are those whom God guided, that is, He guided them to His religion, His oneness, His worship, and avoiding false gods. And among them are those upon whom misguidance is due, that is, it is obligatory and established due to their persistence in disbelief and stubbornness. Al-Zajjaj said: God knows that He sent the messengers with the command to worship, and that He is behind misguidance and guidance. An example of this verse is the Almighty’s saying: A party He guided, and a party upon whom error was due. In this verse is the explicit statement that God commanded all of His servants to worship Him, and to avoid Satan and everything that calls to misguidance, and that after that they are two groups, some of whom He guided and some of whom were due to misguidance. This was evidence that the command of God Almighty does not necessitate conformity with His will, for He commands everyone to believe, and He does not want guidance except for some, for if He wanted it for everyone, no one would disbelieve. This is the meaning of what we have narrated from Al-Zajjaj here: So travel through the land a journey of consideration and see how was the end of the deniers of the previous nations when you see their traces, such as ‘Aad and Thamud: that is, how their end came to be the destruction of their homes after the destruction of their bodies by punishment.
16:37: Then he dedicated the address to his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, confirming what came before, saying: 37- If you are eager for their guidance meaning you strive to do so then indeed, God does not guide whomever He leads astray. Ibn Mas'ud and the people of Kufa read La yahdi with a fat-ha on the letter of the present tense as a future verb attributed to God Almighty: meaning, indeed, God does not guide whomever He leads astray, and min is in the accusative case as the object. The rest read La yahdi with a damma on the letter of the present tense as a passive voice, and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this reading, meaning that no guide will guide him, whoever he may be, and min is in the nominative case as a substitute for the deleted subject, so this verse according to this reading is like his saying in the other verse He whom God leads astray, there is no guide for him and the pronoun in both readings is deleted: meaning, whomever He leads astray. Abu Ubaid narrated on the authority of Al-Farra’, according to the first reading, that the meaning of La yahdi is La yahdi is La yahdi like the Almighty’s saying: Or is there not one who guides unless he is guided meaning is guided. Abu Ubaid said: We do not know of anyone who narrated this other than Al-Farra’, and he is not accused of what he narrates. An-Nahhas said: It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Mubarrad, as if the meaning of La yahdi han yadhil is from his knowledge of that and he had previously known it, And they have no helpers who help them in guiding those whom God has led astray or help them by repelling the punishment from them.
16:38: Then he mentioned the stubbornness of the Quraysh and their denial of the resurrection, so he said 38- And they swore by God with their most fervent oaths a source in the place of the state: meaning striving that God will not resurrect those who die of His servants, they claimed that God, glory be to Him, is incapable of resurrecting the dead, so God responded to them by saying: Yes, a promise binding upon Him, true this is confirmation of what comes after the negation, meaning yes, He will resurrect them, and a promise is a source confirming what yes indicated, which is that He will resurrect them because the resurrection is a promise from God, a promise He promised to His servants with, and the estimate is the promise of the resurrection is a promise binding upon Him, true, in which there is no breach, and true is an attribute of a promise, and likewise upon Him, for it is an attribute of a promise: meaning existing upon Him, or the accusative of true as a source: meaning true truly but most people do not know that this is easy for Him, glory be to Him, not difficult.
16:39: And His statement: 39- To make clear to them meaning to make it apparent to them, and this is the ultimate goal of what is indicated by yes of the resurrection, and the pronoun in to them refers to the one who dies, and the relative pronoun in His statement: in which they differ is in the accusative case as the object of to make clear meaning the matter in which the disagreement occurred between them, and its clarification at that time will be with what the messengers brought to them, and what the books of God were revealed to them about, and it was said that to make clear is related to His statement: And We have certainly sent meaning We sent to every nation a messenger to make clear, and this is far-fetched and that those who disbelieved in God Almighty and denied the resurrection may know that they were liars in their argument and denial of the resurrection by saying: God does not resurrect the one who dies.
16:40: And sentence 40 - Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, 'Be,' and it is is a resumption of the explanation of how to create and repeat after explaining the ease of resurrection for Him, glory be to Him. Al-Zajjaj said: He informed them of the ease with which He created things, so He informed that whenever He wills a thing, it is. This is like His saying: And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is. Ibn 'Amir and Al-Kisa'i read so it is in the accusative case, in apposition to that We say. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as an answer to Be. The rest read it in the nominative case, meaning: so it is. Ibn Al-Anbari said: The word thing was applied to what was known to God before creation, because it is like what had already existed and been seen. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of for something is for the sake of something, so he made the lam causal. It was also said that it is the lam of notification, as in your saying, I told him to stand up, so he stood up. Our saying is the subject, that we say to him, ‘Be’ is its predicate. This statement is an example of the meaning: that nothing is impossible for Him, and that His existence when He wills it is like the existence of the command when the command of the obeyed commander comes to the obedient commanded one. There is no saying, nor is there anything said to it, nor a command, nor a commanded one, so that it can be said that one of two impossibilities necessitates from it: either addressing something that does not exist, or obtaining something that has already occurred. The explanation of that has already been given in full in Surat Al-Baqarah. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them? He said: With death. And he said in another verse: And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve and he is the Angel of Death, and he has messengers or the command of your Lord comes and that is on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: For God guides not whom He leads astray he said: Whoever God leads astray, no one guides. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah who said: A Muslim man owed a polytheist a debt, so he came to him to collect it, and among what he said was: And what I hope for after death is that it is such and such. So the polytheist said to him: You claim that you will be resurrected after death, so he swore by God with his most solemn oath that God will not resurrect anyone who dies, so God revealed: And they swear by God with their most solemn oaths that God will not resurrect anyone who dies the verse. Ibn Al-Aqeeli and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali regarding his statement: And they swear by God with their most solemn oaths that God will not raise up anyone who dies, he said: It was revealed about me. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: “God the Most High said: The son of Adam insulted Me, and it was not right for him to insult Me, and he lied about Me, and it was not right for him to lie about Me. As for his lying about Me, He said: “And they swear by God with their most solemn oaths that God will not raise up anyone who dies,” and I said: Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him. As for his insulting Me, he said: God is the third of three, and I said: He is God, the One, God, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.” This is how Abu Hurairah mentioned it as a mursal, and it is in the two Sahihs as a marfu’ with a different wording. Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: To make clear to them that over which they differ, he said: To all people in general.
16:41: The meaning of migration in Surat An-Nisa has already been investigated, which is leaving one's family and homeland, and the meaning of 41- They migrated for the sake of God is for the sake of God the Almighty and for His pleasure, and it was said for the sake of God is for the religion of God, and it was said that in means the letter lam: that is, for God after they were wronged that is, they were tortured and humiliated, for the people of Mecca tortured a group of Muslims until they said what they wanted from them, and when they left them, they migrated. There is disagreement about the reason for the revelation of the verse, and it was said that it was revealed about Suhaib, Bilal, Khabbab, and Ammar. It was objected that the Surah is Meccan, and that contradicts His statement: and those who migrated. It was answered that this verse could be one of the Medinan verses in this Surah as we mentioned in its title, and it was said that it was revealed about Abu Jandal bin Suhayl, and it was said that it was revealed about the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the polytheists in Mecca wronged them and forced them until a group of them fled to Abyssinia. We will surely grant them good in this world: There are different opinions about the meaning of this. It was said that what is meant is their settlement in Medina, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Al-Sha’bi and Qatadah. It was said that what is meant is good provision, as stated by Mujahid. It was said that it is victory over their enemy, as stated by Al-Dahhak. It was said that it is what they conquered of the lands and what they had in them of the provinces. It was said that it is what remained for them in it of praise and what became for their children of honor. There is no objection to interpreting the verse as referring to all of these matters. The meaning of We will surely grant them goodness in this world is We will grant them a good abode or a good abode. Goodness is an attribute of a deleted source. And the reward of the Hereafter means the reward for their deeds in the Hereafter is greater than anyone of God’s creation could know before seeing it. From this is the saying of God Almighty: And when you look, you will see pleasure and great dominion. “If they only knew” means if these oppressors knew that. It was said that the pronoun in they know refers to the believers: meaning if they saw the reward of the Hereafter and witnessed it, they would know that it is greater than the goodness of this world.
16:42: 42- Those who are patient the relative pronoun is in the accusative case as a compliment, or in the nominative case as a subject, or it is a substitute for the first relative pronoun, or for the pronoun in We will inform them, “and upon their Lord they rely” meaning upon their Lord in particular they rely in all their affairs, turning away from everything else, and the sentence is conjoined with the relative clause or in the accusative case as a state.
16:43: 43- And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed. Hafs read from Asim Nuhi with a nun, and the rest read yuhi with a ya below. This verse is a response to the Quraysh when they claimed that God, the Exalted, is too great to send a messenger from among humans. God responded to them by saying that this is His custom and His way, that He does not send except men from among humans to whom He reveals. Abu Ali al-Jubba'i claimed that the meaning of the verse is that God, the Exalted, did not send His revelation to the prophets except those who are in the form of men from among the angels. It is replied to him that Gabriel used to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in different forms, and since the infidels of Mecca acknowledged that the Jews and Christians were the people of knowledge of what God revealed in the Torah and the Gospel, He turned the address to them and ordered them to return to the People of the Book, so He said: So ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know, meaning, O polytheists, ask the believers of the People of the Book if you do not know, for they will tell you that all the prophets were human beings, or ask the People of the Book without restricting them to their believers, as is apparent, for they acknowledged that and did not conceal it. It was said that the meaning is: So ask the People of the Qur’an.
16:44: And 44- With clear proofs and scriptures is related to We sent, so it is included in the rule of exception with men, and Al-Farra' denied that. He said: The description of what comes before except is not delayed to what comes after it, because what is excepted from is the sum of what comes before except with its connection, as if it were said We sent except men with clear proofs, so since this sum was not mentioned in its entirety, it was not possible to include the exception in it, and it was said that there is an advancement and delay in the speech, and the meaning is: And We did not send before you with clear proofs and scriptures except men, and it was said that it is related to something omitted that was indicated by the mentioned: that is, We sent them with clear proofs and scriptures, and it is an answer to an implied question as if it was said Why did He send them? He said: We sent them with clear proofs and scriptures. It was said that it is related to you know as its object and the ba is redundant: meaning if you do not know with the clear proofs and scriptures. It was said that it is related to men: meaning men who are clothed with the clear proofs and scriptures. It was said that it is related to with my revelation: meaning We reveal to them the clear proofs and scriptures. It was said that it is accusative with the estimation of I mean, and the ba is redundant. The people of the remembrance are the people of the Book as mentioned above. Al-Zajjaj said: Ask everyone who remembers with knowledge. The clear proofs are the arguments and evidences, and the scriptures are the books. We have already discussed this in Al Imran. And We have sent down to you the Remembrance meaning the Qur’an. Then He explained the desired goal of sending it down and said: That you may make clear to the people all of them what was sent down to them in this remembrance of the legal rulings, promises and threats and that they may give thought meaning intending that they contemplate and apply their thoughts so that they may be admonished.
16:45: 45- Are those who plot evil deeds secure that God will cause the earth to swallow them up? It is possible that evil deeds are an attribute of a deleted source: that is, they plotted evil plots, and that it is the object of the mentioned verb, which includes the meaning of work: that is, they committed evil deeds, or an attribute of an implied object: that is, are those who plotted evil deeds secure that God will cause the earth to swallow them up? It is the object of secure, or a substitute for its object, according to the view that its object is deleted, and that evil deeds are an attribute of the deleted, and the question is for rebuke and rebuke, and the plotting of evil deeds: their efforts to harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to harm his companions in secret, and their trickery to invalidate Islam, and the plotting of its people that God will cause the earth to swallow them up as He caused Qarun to swallow up. It is said that the place was swallowed up, he went into the earth, and God caused the earth to swallow him up, meaning he disappeared into it, and from this is His saying: So We caused the earth to swallow up And the earth will swallow him and his home and he will be swallowed up in the earth and he will be swallowed up or the punishment will come to them from where they do not perceive in the event of their being heedless of it as was done to the people of Lot and others. It was said that he meant the Day of Badr, for they were destroyed on that day and it was not in their calculations.
16:46: 46- Or He takes them in their turning The commentators mentioned aspects of it. It was said that what is meant is in their travels and their trade, for He, glory be to Him, is able to destroy them in travel as He destroys them in the city, and they do not escape Him due to their traveling on the earth and their distance from their homelands. It was said that what is meant is in the state of their turning in the fulfillment of their desires due to the existence of tricks, so God prevents them from their goals and tricks. It was said that it is in the state of their turning in their beds at night. It was said that it is in the state of their coming and going, and their going and coming by night and by day. The heart in the first meaning is taken from His statement: Do not be deceived by the turning of those who disbelieve in the land, and in the second meaning it is taken from His statement: And they turned matters upside down for you. "So they will not escape," meaning they will not escape or be prevented.
16:47: 47- Or He seizes them in fear meaning a state of fear and anticipation of calamities, such that they are expecting the punishment and are wary of it, not heedless of it. This is contrary to what was previously stated in His statement, Or the punishment comes to them from where they do not perceive. It was said that the meaning of in fear is to diminish. Ibn al-A'rabi said: meaning to diminish money, lives, and fruits until He destroys them. Al-Wahidi said: The majority of commentators said: in fear, he said diminish: either by killing or by death, meaning by diminishing their extremities and sides, He takes them first and then the first until the taking comes upon all of them. He said, and fear is diminishing. It is said that he fears money: meaning it diminishes it, and takes from its extremities. End. It is said that time frightened him and betrayed him with the letter fa and the letter nun: diminished it. Dhu al-Rummah said: No, it is the longing from the house of fear, sometimes clouds and sometimes dust Labid said: Her fear is that I will come and go That is, its flesh and fat are reduced. Al-Haitham bin Adi said: Takhwāf with the letter fa’ means tanqāsāf in the language of Azd Shenouda, and he recited: Fear their enemy, Mali, and the most precious chains in their throats, which clang It was said: On fear: In haste, said Al-Layth bin Saad. It was said: On reprimand for the sins they committed, narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: On fear: that He will punish and overlook. Qatada said: Then your Lord is Kind and Merciful, He does not hasten, but rather He gives respite out of compassion and mercy for you, even though they deserve punishment.
16:48: 48- Or have they not seen what God has created of anything? When He, the Almighty, frightened the schemers with what He frightened, He followed it with mentioning what indicates the perfection of His power in managing the conditions of the upper and lower worlds and their place, and the question in Or have they not seen is for denial, and what is ambiguous and explained by His saying: of anything, and Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Yahya bin Waththab, and Al-A'mash read Tarawa with the upper thaa' as addressing all people, and the rest read it with the lower thaa' referring the pronoun to those who plotted evil deeds. Abu Amr and Ya'qub read Tatafya'u Shaylahu with the upper thaa'. The rest read it with the lower thaa' and Abu Ubaid chose it: meaning it leans from side to side, and is in one state at the beginning of the day and shrinks, then returns to another state at the end of the day. Al-Azhari said: The shadows return after midday, so the shadow does not occur except in the evening and that which the sun and moon have turned away from, and that which occurs in the morning is the shadow. Tha’lab said: I was told on the authority of Abu Ubaidah that Ru’bah said: Everything that the sun was on and then set from it is shadow, and that which the sun was not on is shadow. The meaning of from something is from something that has a shadow, and they are bodies, so it is general and what is meant by it is specific, and its shadows are the plural of shadow, and it is added to a singular because it is one and what is meant by it is many. From the right and the left means from the direction of their right and their left: meaning from the sides of each one of them. Al-Farra’ said: He made the right singular because he meant one of those with shadows, and the lefts plural because he meant all of them, because what God created is singular in word but its meaning is plural. Al-Wahidi said: The right hand is singular and what is meant by it is all, in brevity of expression, like his saying: And they turn their backs. The left hands indicate that what is meant by it is the plural. It was said that when the Arabs mentioned two plural forms, they expressed one of them with the singular form, like his saying: And He made the darkness and the light, and God set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing. It was said that what is meant by the right hand is the point that is the rising of the sun, and that it is one. The left hands are an expression for the deviation in the orbit of shadows after they fall on the ground, and they are many. The east is expressed by the right hand because the strongest side of a person is his right hand, and from it the strong movement appears. Prostrating to God is in the accusative case as a state: that is, the state of the shadows prostrating to God. Al-Zajjaj said: He means that these things are created to obey. He also said: The prostration of the body is its submission and what is seen of the effect of the craftsmanship. And they are humbled is in the accusative case as a state: that is, submissive and humiliated. And the humiliation is smallness and humiliation. It is said that the man is humbled, so he is humbled and God has humbled him. The poet said: There is nothing left but a buried treasure and a petrified place in a land other than yours, in a stone. Mukhis: the name of a prison in Iraq.
16:49: 49- And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures meaning to Him alone submits and obeys, not to anyone else, everything in the heavens, and whatever is on the earth of creatures that crawl on the earth, and what is meant by this is every creature. Al-Akhfash said: It is like you saying, No man like him has come to me, and No man like him has come to me. All things that exist in them are included in the generality of what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and He only mentioned creatures specifically because it is known from His statement, Have they not seen what God has created of anything, that inanimate objects submit, and the angels are linked to what came before them as an honor to them, and to magnify their inclusion in the linked, and they are not arrogant meaning that they are not arrogant about worshipping their Lord, and what is meant is the angels, and it is possible that the sentence is a new sentence. This is a response to the Quraysh, who claimed that the angels are daughters of God. It is possible that it is a state of the subject of prostrates and what is conjoined to it: that is, everything in the heavens and everything on the earth and the angels prostrate to God, and none of them are too proud to prostrate.
16:50: 50- They fear their Lord above them This sentence is in the accusative case as a state: that is, the state of their fearing their Lord above them, or a renewed sentence to clarify the negation of their arrogance, and one of the effects of fear is the absence of arrogance, and above them is related to they fear with the omission of an adjective: that is, they fear the punishment of their Lord above them, or it is a state of the Lord: that is, they fear their Lord while He is above them, and it was said that the meaning of they fear their Lord above them is they fear the angels, so it is with the omission of an adjective: that is, they fear the angels of their Lord being above them, and this is an unnecessary effort, and such far-fetched interpretations necessitated the defense of doctrines that have become firmly rooted in the minds and established in the hearts. It was said that this fear is the fear of reverence, and Al-Zajjaj chose it and said: they fear their Lord with reverent fear, and the correctness of this meaning is indicated by his saying: And He is the Dominant over His servants, and his saying as a statement About Pharaoh: And We are over them, dominant, “and they do what they are commanded,” meaning what they are commanded to do in obedience to God: meaning the angels, or all of those mentioned above. And applying these sentences to the angels is more appropriate, because among God’s creatures there are those who are too arrogant to worship Him, and do not fear Him and do not do what they are commanded to do, such as the infidels and the disobedient who do not have these characteristics and Satan and his soldiers. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And those who emigrated for the cause of God after they had been wronged, he said: They are people from the people of Mecca who emigrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after they had been wronged. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind who said: This verse was revealed about Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: And those who emigrated for the cause of God, he said: These are the companions of Muhammad who were wronged by the people of Mecca and were expelled from their homes until groups of them reached the land of Abyssinia, then God settled them in Medina after that and made it a place of migration for them, and He gave them supporters from among the believers. And the reward of the Hereafter is greater, he said: By God, what God will bestow upon them of His Paradise and blessings is greater, if they only knew. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Sha’bi regarding his statement: In this world is good, he said: Medina. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: We will provide them with a good provision in this world. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “When God sent Muhammad as a Messenger, the Arabs denied that, so God revealed: ‘And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed.’” Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding His statement: So ask the people of the message the verse, meaning the polytheists of Quraysh, that Muhammad is the Messenger of God in the Torah and the Gospel. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, he said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Salam and a group of the people of the Torah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: With clear proofs he said: The verses, and the scriptures he said: The books. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: Then do those who plot evil deeds feel secure? he said: Nimrod bin Canaan and his people. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: Meaning polytheism. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: Their denial of the messengers and their committing sins. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Or He seizes them in their turning, he said: In their disagreement. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: In their turning, he said: If you wish, I seize him in his travels. “Or He seizes them on fear,” he said: After the death of his companion. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: On fear, he said: It diminishes their deeds. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Umar that he asked them about this verse, Or He seizes them on fear, they said: We do not see anything except that it is when what is repeated from the verses is diminished. Umar said: I do not see anything except that it is due to what they diminish of the sins of God. A man who was with Umar went out and met a Bedouin and said: O so-and-so, what did your Lord do? He said: I have frightened him, meaning I have diminished him. So he went back to Umar and told him, he said: I have seen that. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Or He seizes them in fear, he said: He seizes them because of the shortcomings of some of them with others. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, He seeks shade, he said: He inclines. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And they are humbled, he said: Subdued. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And to God prostrates, the verse, he said: He did not leave any of His creation except that it worshipped Him willingly or unwillingly. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse, he said: Everyone in the heavens prostrates willingly and everyone on the earth prostrates willingly or unwillingly.
16:51: When He, the Almighty, made clear that His heavenly and earthly creatures are obedient to Him, subject to His Majesty, He followed that with a prohibition against polytheism, saying: 51- “And God said, ‘Do not take two gods. He is only one God.’” So He, the Almighty, prohibited taking two gods, then He established that divinity is limited to one God, who is God, the Almighty. It has been said that the duality in two gods indicates duality, and the singularity in one god indicates unity. So what is the reason for describing two gods as two, and describing one god? It was said in response: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: Do not take two gods, He is only one God. It was said that the repetition is for the sake of exaggeration in repelling from taking a partner. It was said that the benefit of adding two is to know that the prohibition refers to multiplicity, not to nationality. The benefit of adding one is to dispel the illusion that what is meant is to establish divinity without oneness, even though divinity is self-evident to Him, glory be to Him, and the difference between the polytheists is in oneness. Then He, glory be to Him, transferred the speech from the unseen to speaking in the manner of turning to increase the intimidation, so He said: So fear Me, meaning if you fear something, then fear Me and no one else. Something like this was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah.
16:52: Then when He, the Most High, established His Oneness, and that He is the One Whom one should be singled out for awe and desire, He mentioned that everything is in His kingdom and under His control, so He said: 52- And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. This sentence is established for those who came before in His statement: And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, to the end. The presentation of the report is to indicate the specificity. And to Him belongs the religion, everlasting, meaning fixed, obligatory, and permanent, and does not disappear. And the religion is obedience and sincerity. Al-Farra’ said: Persistent means always, and from this is the statement of Al-Du’ali: I do not seek praise that is short-lived, but rather blame that will last all of time. That is, always. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Farra’ that he said: The pure wasif, and the first is more appropriate. From this is the saying of the Almighty: And for them is a lasting punishment, meaning everlasting. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, His obedience is obligatory forever. So he interpreted wasif as obligatory. Ibn Qutaybah said in his interpretation of al-Wasib: That is, no one is obeyed except that this is cut off by the disappearance or destruction of other than God Almighty, for obedience to Him is permanent. So al-Wasib was interpreted as permanent, and if it is permanent for something and does not end, then it is obligatory and established. It is said that a person strives to do something, and he is persistent in it. And a man strives to do it, and it is said that wasab means fatigue and exhaustion, meaning that obedience to God Almighty is obligatory even if the servant is tired in it, and this is not appropriate for what is in the verse. The question in His statement: Do you then fear other than God? is for rebuke and rebuke, and it is connected to something understood as in its counterparts. The meaning is: If the religion, that is, obedience, is obligatory for Him permanently and does not end, then it is appropriate for that to specify piety to Him and not to do it to anyone else.
16:53: Then He, the Almighty, bestowed upon them the favor of all the blessings they are experiencing, which are from Him and not from anyone else, so He said: 53- And whatever blessings you have meaning whatever blessings you have of different types are from God: meaning they are from Him, so what is conditional, and it is permissible for it to be a relative pronoun that includes the meaning of a condition, and with you is its relative clause, and of blessings is a state of the pronoun in the preposition and noun, or an explanation of what. And his saying: Then from God is the report, and if what is a conditional, then the verb of the condition is omitted, i.e. whatever it is, and the blessing is either religious, which is knowing the truth for its own sake and knowing good for the sake of working with it, or worldly, psychological, or physical or external, such as financial happiness and others, and each one of these is a genus under which there are countless types, and all are from God, the Most High, so the wise person should thank none but Him, then he explained the change of a person after being immersed in the sea of blessings, saying: Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help, meaning when harm touches you, that is, to God, the Most High, and not to anyone else, you implore to remove it, for there is no one to remove it but Him, it is said that he cried out, crying out in supplication: if he raised his voice in supplication. Al-A’sha said, describing a cow: She circumambulated three times in a day and a night. It was objectionable that she circumambulated and traded. Harm: illness, affliction, need, famine, and everything that harms a person.
16:54: 54- Then when the hardship is removed from you, at once a party of you associate others with their Lord. That is, when the hardship that has befallen you is removed, at once a party, that is, a group of you, associate others with their Lord from whom the hardship has been removed, and they make with Him another god, such as an idol or something similar. The verse is intended to express astonishment at the actions of these people, as they place association with God, who has bestowed upon them the favor of removing the hardship that has befallen them, in place of thanking Him. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-An'am and Yunus, and will come in Subhan. Al-Zajjaj said: This is specific to deceit and thinking, and he opposed the removal of the hardship from him to denial and disbelief. Based on this, the min in minkum is for partiality, as the address was to all people, and the group is the disbelievers, even though the address was directed to the disbelievers, so min is for clarification.
16:55: And the lam in 55- So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them is the lam of ki: meaning so that they may disbelieve in what We have given them of the blessing of removing distress, so that it is as if this disbelief on their part, which occurs in the place of gratitude that is required of them, is a goal for them and an aim of their aims. This is the ultimate in stubbornness and obstinacy, with no end beyond it. It was said that the lam is for the consequence: meaning that the consequence of those supplications was nothing but this disbelief. Then the Almighty said by way of threat and intimidation, turning from the third person to the second person, So enjoy what you are in of that, for you will soon know the consequence of your affair and what will happen to you in this world and what you will become in the Hereafter.
16:56: Then the Almighty narrated another type of their ugly deeds, saying: 56- And they assign to that which they do not know a share of what We have provided for them. That is, this assignment occurs after they have sought refuge in God, the Almighty, to remove their distress and what follows His removal from them of disbelief in God and associating partners with Him. Despite that, they assign to that which they do not know the reality of, of inanimate objects and devils, a share of what We have provided for them from their wealth, by which they draw near to Him. It was said that the meaning is that they, the disbelievers, assign to idols, and they do not know anything about them, because they are inanimate objects. So the agent of they know according to this is the idols, and He made them like rational beings in their plural with the waw and the nun, following the belief of the disbelievers in them. The meaning is: These infidels give idols that do not understand anything a share of the wealth that God has provided them. By God, you will be asked about what you used to invent. This is a return from the third person to the second person, and this question is a question of rebuke and reproach. About what you used to invent. You fabricate lies about God Almighty in this world.
16:57: 57- And they attribute to God daughters This is another type of their scandals and ugliness. Khuza'ah and Kinanah used to say that the angels are daughters of God. Glory be to Him. He has exalted Himself from what these rude people who have no sound minds or straight understandings have attributed to Him. They are not except like livestock, nay, they are more astray. In this exaltation there is astonishment at their state. And they will have whatever they desire. That is, they attribute to themselves whatever they desire of sons, on the basis that what is in the accusative case with the implied verb, and it is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a subject. Al-Zajjaj denied the accusative case, saying: Because the Arabs do not say He made for him such-and-such and he means himself, but rather they say He made for himself such-and-such. If it were in the accusative case, He would have said And for themselves what they desire. Al-Farra' permitted the accusative case.
16:58: Then the Almighty mentioned their hatred of females which they attributed to God the Almighty, saying: 58- And when one of them is given the good report of a female meaning if one of them is informed of the birth of a girl to him his face remains dark meaning changed, and what is meant is not blackness which is the opposite of whiteness, but what is meant by blackness is a metaphor for brokenness and change due to what occurs from grief, and the Arabs say to anyone who encounters something bad, his face has turned black with grief and sadness, as Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Mawardi said: Rather what is meant is the blackness of the color in reality, he said: And this is the opinion of the majority, and the first is more appropriate, because what is known by conscience is that whoever is angry, sad and distressed does not experience in his color anything but a mere change and the appearance of depression and brokenness, not true blackness, and the phrase and he is suppressing his anger is in the accusative case as a state: meaning filled with grief, rage and anger. Al-Akhfash said: He is the one who suppresses his anger and does not show it. It was said that he is the one who is sad and closes his mouth from sadness. It is taken from the word kazamah, which means blocking the mouth of a well. This was said by Ali bin Issa, and it was mentioned previously in Surat Yusuf.
16:59: 59- He hides from the people meaning he disappears and disappears because of the bad report he has been given meaning because of the bad grief, shame and embarrassment that will befall him because of the girl he has given birth to. Should he keep her with humiliation? meaning he is still hesitant between the two options: keeping the girl he has been given humiliation with, or burying them both in the dirt. With humiliation meaning humiliation. This is how Isa Al-Thaqafi read it. Al-Yazidi said: Hun means humiliation in the language of Quraysh. This is how Abu Ubaid narrated it from Al-Kisa'i. It was narrated from Al-Kisa'i that it means affliction and hardship. Al-Khansa' said: We humiliate souls, and humiliating souls on the day of calamity is more lasting for them. Al-Farraa said: Al-Hun is a little in the language of Tamim. An-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Al-A’mash that he read ayyamsaquhu ‘ala su’ he holds her in su’ or am yadisahu fi al-drab he hides her in the dirt by burying her alive, meaning he hides her in the dirt by burying her alive as the Arabs used to do. The one who was given the good report of the birth of a female was still hesitating between these two matters. The masculine in yamsukahu he holds her in su’ and yadisahu he hides her in the dirt is used even though it refers to a female in order to preserve the wording. Al-Jahdari read am yadisahu fi al-drab he holds her in su’ and he must read ayyamsaquha he holds her in su’ and it was said that dasahu hiding her means hiding her from people so that she is not known, like madsoos hidden in order to hide it from sight. Are not evil what they judge? as they attributed the daughters they dislike to God, the Most High, and attributed the sons they love to themselves. An example of this is the saying of God, the Most High: Is it for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unfair division.
16:60: 60- For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the example of evil meaning for those whom God Almighty described with these terrible ugliness like evil: meaning the characteristic of evil from ignorance and disbelief in God, and it was said that it is their description of God Almighty with a companion and a son, and it was said that it is their need for a son to take their place and burying girls alive to remove shame and fear of poverty, and it was said that it is punishment and Hell And to God is the highest example and it is the opposites of the characteristic of the created beings from complete wealth and comprehensive generosity and vast knowledge, or monotheism and sincerity of worship, or that He is the Creator, Provider, Able, and a metaphor, and it was said that it is the testimony that there is no god but God, and it was said: "God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light", And He is the Exalted in Might who is not defeated, so it does not harm Him if they attribute to Him what is not befitting of Him, the Wise in His actions and words.
16:61: Then when He, the Almighty, narrated about the people the greatness of their disbelief, He showed the breadth of His generosity and forbearance, as He did not hasten to punish them and did not hold them accountable for their injustice, so He said: 61- And if God were to punish people for their injustice, and what is meant by people here are the disbelievers or all the sinners, He would not leave upon it, meaning on the earth, even if He did not mention it, the mention of people and the mention of the beast indicated it, for all are settled on the earth, and what is meant by the beast is the disbeliever, and it was said that it is everything that creeps, and it was said on this how can it be generalized by destruction even though among them are those who have no sin? And the answer is by destroying the oppressor as revenge against him, and destroying others if they are among those who are accountable, then for the sake of providing them with reward, and if they are not among them, then because of the evil of the oppression of the oppressors, and God has perfect wisdom He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned, and similar to this is His saying: And fear a trial that will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively. And in this meaning are the hadiths, including what is in Muslim and others from the hadith of Ibn Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When God intends to punish a people, the punishment afflicts whoever is among them, then they are resurrected according to their intentions. And likewise the hadith of the army who are swallowed up in the desert, and at the end of it: that they are resurrected according to their intentions. We have already presented when interpreting the words of God, the Most High: And fear a trial, the verse, a true confirmation of which should be reviewed. But He delays them for a specified term, known to Him, which is the end of their lives and the expiration of their ages, or the term of their punishment. In this delay there is great wisdom, including an excuse for them and loosening the reins with them, and including the occurrence of those of their children whom He has foreordained. So when their term comes, which He has named for them, the word of God, the Most High, will be fulfilled upon them at that time, without precedence or delay, and the hour is a short period, and this interpretation and confirmation of it have already been presented.
16:62: Then he mentioned another type of their ignorance and foolishness, saying: And they attribute to God that which they hate meaning they attribute to Him, glory be to Him, what they hate to attribute to themselves of daughters, and this is a repetition of what came before for the purpose of emphasis and confirmation and to increase the rebuke and reprimand. And their tongues describe falsehood This is from the other type that God, glory be to Him, mentioned of their ugliness, which is: meaning what their tongues describe of falsehood is their saying: That they will have the best meaning the best characteristic, or the best outcome. Al-Zajjaj said: They describe that they will have from God, along with the ugliness of their saying, a good reward. Al-Zajjaj also said and Al-Farraa: He replaced His saying And their tongues describe falsehood with His saying That they will have the best, and the lie is in the accusative case as the object of the verb describe. Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, and Ibn Muhaisin read the lie with the raising of the kaf, the dhal, and the ba' as an attribute of the tongues, which is the plural of lie, so the object according to this is that they will have the best. Then God, the Most High, responded to them by saying: Indeed, for them is the Fire. That is, they will truly have a place in the Fire that they have made for themselves. This has already been confirmed. And that they will be the forerunners. Ibn al-A’rabi and Abu Ubaidah said: That is, they will be left and forgotten in the Fire. Al-Kisa’i and al-Farra’ said the same, so it is derived from afrattu fulan khalfan meaning I left him behind and forgot him. Qatada and al-Hasan said: Hurrying to it, coming first in entering it, from “afrattuhu meaning I put him ahead in seeking water. Al-Fart is the one who goes first to the water, and al-Faraat are the ones who go first in seeking water, and al-Waraat are the ones who come late. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will be your forerunner at the Cistern. That is, I will be your leader. Al-Qatami said: They hastened us and they were among our companions, just as a camel hurried to its destination. Nafi' read in the narration of Warsh mufarritoon with a kasra on the ra' and a shaddah on it, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, and its meaning is: extravagant in sins and transgressions. It is said that someone was excessive towards someone: if he was arrogant towards him and said to him more evil than he said. Abu Ja'far al-Qari read mufarritoon with a kasra on the ra' and a shaddah on it: meaning, wasting the command of God, so it is from neglecting what is obligatory. The rest read mufarritoon with a fatha on the ra' and a shaddah on it, and its meaning is: brought to the fire. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And to Him is the religion, always, he said: The religion is sincerity, and is always constant. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, And to Him is the religion, always, he said: There is no god but God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And always, he said: Always. Al-Faryabi and Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: Obligatory. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, You cry out, he said: You implore in supplication. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: Then enjoy yourselves, and you will soon know, he said: A threat. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they assign to that which they do not know, the verse, he said: They know that God created them and that it harms them and benefits them, then they assign to that which they do not know that it harms them and does not benefit them, a share of what We have provided for them. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: They are the polytheists of the Arabs who made for their idols and devils from what God had provided for them and they divided a portion of their wealth and made it for their idols and devils. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the verse, he said: It is their saying, this is for God, according to their claim, and this is for our partners. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And they attribute to God daughters the verse, he said: They attribute to me daughters whom they like for me and do not like them for themselves, and that is because in the days of ignorance, if a male among them had a girl, he would keep her in contempt or bury her in the dirt while she was alive. And Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, And for them is what they desire, he said: He means sons. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Or bury him in the dirt, he said: He buried his daughter alive. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Suddi regarding his statement: How evil is that which they judge, he said: How evil is that which they judge, meaning: something that they would not accept for themselves, so how would they accept it for me. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: And to God belongs the highest similitude, he said: the testimony that there is no god but God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas: And to God belongs the highest similitude, he said: he means that there is nothing like Him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saeed Ibn Jubayr regarding his statement: He did not leave upon it any creature, he said: what the rain gave them to drink. He also narrated from Al-Suddi something similar. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Qatadah regarding the verse, he said: that was done in the time of Noah, God destroyed every creature on the face of the earth except what he carried in his ark. Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd from Ibn Masoud, he said: the sins of the sons of Adam killed the dung beetle in its hole, then he said: yes, by God, at the time of the drowning of the people of Noah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sha`b narrated on his authority that he said: The dung beetle was almost tortured in its hole because of the sin of Adam’s son. Then he recited: And if God were to punish people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon the earth a single creature. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated something similar on the authority of Anas. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sha`b narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he heard a man saying: The oppressor harms no one but himself. Abu Hurayrah said: Yes, by God, the houbara bustard dies emaciated in its nest because of the oppression of the oppressor. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak: And they attribute to God that which they dislike. He said: They attribute to me daughters and they dislike that for themselves. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And their tongues describe falsely that they will have the best, he said: The saying of the infidels of Quraysh 106:We have sons and He has daughters. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada something similar. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, And that they are excessive, he said: attributed. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair something similar. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada, he said: hastened. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar.
16:63: God Almighty explained that the same action of Quraysh had occurred among all nations, so He said, comforting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, 63- By God, We had sent to nations before you, meaning messengers, but Satan made their evil deeds pleasing to them, so he is their protector today. It is possible that today refers to the time of this world, in which case the meaning would be: He is their companion in this world. It is possible that today refers to the Day of Resurrection and what comes after it, in which case it would be for the coming situation, and protector would mean the helper, and what is meant is to deny the helper from them in the most eloquent way, because Satan cannot be imagined to be helped at all in the Hereafter, and if the helper is limited to him, then it is necessary that there is no help from anyone other than him. It is possible that today refers to some of the time of this world, and this is in two ways: The first is that it refers to some of what has passed, which is when Satan made the past nations look good, in which case it would be a narration of the past situation. The second is that it refers to some of the present, which is the time of the revelation of the verse. What is meant is that Satan made things seem good to the infidels of Quraysh, so the pronoun in their guardian refers to the infidels of Quraysh 106:meaning he is the guardian of these people today, or with the omission of an adjective: meaning he is the guardian of nations like those today. And for them is a painful punishment meaning in the Hereafter, which is the punishment of Hellfire.
16:64: Then the Almighty mentioned that no one perished except after the proof was established against them and the reason was removed from them, so He said: 64- And We have not sent down the Book to you except that you may make clear to them that in which they differed. This is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by the Book is the Qur’an, and the exception is devoid of the most general conditions: that is, We did not send it down to you for any condition or any reason except for the reason of making it clear to them: that is, for the people in which they differed regarding monotheism and the conditions of resurrection and all the other legal rulings, and the accusative of guidance and mercy is that they are the object of them, conjoined with the place of making it clear, and there is no need for the lam, because they are the verb of the subject of the reasoned verb, unlike making it clear, which is the verb of the one being addressed, not the verb of the one sending it down for a people who believe in God, the Almighty, and believe in what the messengers brought and the books were sent down.
16:65: Then He, glory be to Him, returned to confirming His existence and His uniqueness in divinity by mentioning His great signs, saying: 65- And God sends down water from the sky, meaning from the clouds, meaning from above as mentioned: meaning a type of water, and revives the earth with it after its lifelessness, meaning He revives it with vegetation after it had been dry and lifeless. Indeed in that, the sending down and revival, is a sign, meaning a sign indicating His oneness and His resurrection of creation and His reward for them, for a people who listen, the words of God and understand what it contains of lessons, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth.
16:66: 66- And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you. The livestock are camels, cows, and sheep, and goats are included in the sheep. The origin of the lesson is to represent one thing with another in order to know its reality through similarity, and from it So take heed, O you who have insight. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: The lesson in the livestock is their subjugation to their masters and their obedience to them. It appears that the lesson is His statement: We give you drink from what is in their bellies. So the sentence is resumed to explain the lesson. The people of Medina, Ibn Amir, and Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr read Nasqikm with the opening of the nun from saqā to water, yasqi. The rest and Hafs from Asim read it with the closing of the nun from asqa to water, yasqi. It was said that they are two languages. Labid said: He watered my people, Bani Majd, and watered Namir and the tribes from the crescent moon. It was read with the superscript ta’ so that the pronoun refers to the livestock, and it was read with the subscript so that the pronoun refers to God, the Most High. Both are weak, and all the reciters follow the first two readings. The fat-ha is the language of Quraysh, and the damma is the language of Himyar. It was said that there is a difference between saqa and asqa. If the drink is from the hand of the cupbearer to the mouth of the one being given the drink, it is said saqituhu, and if it is merely presented to him and prepared for him, it is said asqahu. The pronoun in his statement from what is in his bellies refers to the livestock. Sibawayh said: The Arabs describe livestock with the singular report. Al-Zajjaj said: Since the plural form is masculine and feminine, and it is said he is the livestock, and she is the livestock, it is permissible for the pronoun to refer to the masculine. Al-Kisa’i said that its meaning is from what is in the bellies of what we mentioned, so according to this it refers to what is mentioned. Al-Farra’ said: This is correct. Al-Mubarrad said: This is widespread in the Qur’an, such as His saying to the sun, This is my Lord, meaning this rising thing, and also, And I am sending to them a gift, then He said, So when Solomon came, and He did not say, It came, because the meaning is, the thing we mentioned came. End. And from that is His saying, Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: Like chickens, I have no crops He did not say its quotient, and the other said: The frankincense pollination was pleasant and cold He did not say and it cooled down.
