It was narrated from Al-Kisa’i that the meaning is from what is in the bellies of some of them, which are the females, because the males do not have milk. Abu Ubaidah said the same. It was narrated from Al-Farra’ that he said: The blessings and the cattle are one and the same, masculine and feminine. That is why the Arabs say: This is a blessing that has been mentioned. The pronoun refers to the word blessings, which means cattle. It is like what Al-Zajjaj said, and Ibn Al-Arabi preferred it and said: The masculinity refers to the meaning of the plural, and the feminization to the meaning of the group. So he mentioned it here in consideration of the plural word and feminized it in Surat Al-Mu’minun in consideration of the word of the group. From between excrement and blood. Excrement is the dung that goes down to the rumen, so when it comes out of it, it is not called excrement. It is said that the rumen excreted what was in it. The meaning is that the thing that you eat includes what is in the rumen, which is excrement, and blood is included in it. So the bottom of it is excrement, the top of it is blood, and the middle of it is milk. So the blood runs in the veins and the milk in the udders, and the excrement remains as it is. Pure means free from the redness of blood and the filth of excrement after they are combined in one vessel. Permissible to the drinkers meaning delicious and pleasant, and the one who drinks it does not choke on it. It is said that the drink is permissible, meaning that it enters the throat easily.
16:67: 67- And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines Ibn Jarir said: The meaning is, and from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines from what you take, so he deleted what and indicated its deletion by saying from it and it was said that it is conjoined with the livestock, and the meaning is: And for you from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines is a lesson, and it is permissible for it to be conjoined with what is in their bellies: that is, We give you to drink from what is in their bellies and from the fruits of the palm trees, and it is permissible for it to be related to what is omitted and indicated by what preceded it, its meaning is: And We give you to drink from the fruits of the palm trees, and on this basis you take from it intoxicant is an explanation of the giving to drink and a revelation of its reality, and it is permissible for it to be related to you take, its meaning is from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines is a fruit from which you take intoxicant, and the repetition of the circumstance, which is his saying from it, is for emphasis like your saying Zaid is in the house in it, and the pronoun was mentioned in from it because it refers to what is mentioned, or to the deleted addition: which is the juice as if it was said and from the juice of the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take from it, and the intoxicant is what Intoxication from wine, and good provision is everything that is eaten from these two trees, such as fruit, molasses, raisins, and vinegar. This verse was revealed before wine was forbidden. It was said that intoxication is vinegar in the Ethiopian language, and good provision is food from the two trees. It was said that sugar is the sweet, permissible juice, and it was called sugar because it may become intoxicating if it remains, and if it reaches intoxication it is forbidden. The first statement is more appropriate and is held by the majority. Linguists have stated that sugar is the name of wine, and no one disagreed with that except Abu Ubaidah, who said: sugar is the taste. What indicates what the majority of linguists have said is the saying of the poet: Bad company and bad drink is their drinking when they are delirious and drunk What indicates what Abu Ubaidah said is what he recited: I made the faults of the most generous people into sugar That is, he made their blame a taste, and Ibn Jarir preferred this and said: Intoxication is what is eaten from food and is permissible to drink from the fruits of palm trees and grapes, and it is good sustenance, so the wording is different but the meaning is the same like I only complain of my distress and my grief to God. Al-Zajjaj said: This statement of Abu Ubaidah is not known, and the people of interpretation are against it, and there is no proof in the verse that he recited because its meaning according to others is that he describes that she turns red with the faults of people, and a group of Hanafis attributed intoxication to what does not intoxicate from wines and to what two-thirds of them went with cooking, they said: God only bestows His favor upon His servants with what He has permitted them, not with what He has forbidden them, and this is rejected by the authentic, continuous hadiths assuming that it comes after the verse prohibiting alcohol. End quote. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason meaning, an indication for those who use reason and act according to what it requires when looking at the verses of creation.
16:68: 68- And your Lord inspired the bee We have already discussed revelation and that it means inspiration, which is what He creates in the heart from the beginning without any apparent reason. From this is His Almighty saying: And by the soul and He who proportioned it * And inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness. And from this is the inspiration of animals to do what benefits them and leave what harms them. Yahya bin Waththab read to the bees with the opening of the ha. Al-Zajjaj said: It was called a bee because God Almighty inspired it with the honey that comes out of it. Al-Jawhari said: “The bees and the bee-like word ‘dabr’ refers to both males and females. ‘That you take houses from the mountains’ means that you take, with ‘that’ being the source, and it is permissible for it to be explanatory because there is a meaning of saying in the suggestion, and the pronoun in ‘take’ is feminine because it is one of the two permissible words as mentioned above, or to carry the meaning or because bees are a collective noun, and the people of Hijaz feminize bees and those in the mountains houses. ‘And’ likewise in ‘of the trees’ and ‘of what they erect’ for the purpose of partiality: meaning dwellings that suit them and are appropriate for them in the niches of the mountains and the hollows of the trees, and in the thrones that the sons of Adam erect from wings and walls and other things, and it is most often used for what is made of wood, it is said ‘arsh ya’rsh’ with a kasra on the ra’ and a damma on it. Ibn ‘Amir and Shu’bah read it with a damma, and the rest read it with a kasra. It was also read ‘būyūtan’ with a kasra on the ba’ and a damma on it.
16:69: 69- Then eat of all the fruits from for the purpose of partiality because they eat the light from the trees, so if you eat them, then follow the ways of your Lord meaning the ways that God has made you understand and taught you, and attributed them to the Lord because He is their Creator and the Inspirator of the bees to follow them: meaning enter the ways of your Lord to seek sustenance in the mountains and through the trees, or follow what you have eaten in the ways of your Lord: meaning in His paths in which He transforms light into honey by His power, or if you eat the fruits in distant places, then follow to your homes, returning to the ways of your Lord, and do not go astray in them, and the erection of submissive is in the state of the ways, and it is the plural of submissive: meaning submissive and not rugged, and this was chosen by Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Jarir, and it was said that it is a state of the bees: meaning: obedient to subjugation and the extraction of honey from their bellies, and this was chosen by Ibn Qutaybah, and the phrase extracts from their bellies is a new sentence that he changed from addressing the bees, enumerating the blessings, and astonishing every listener, To alert others and guide them to the great signs that come from this fly-like animal, what is meant by drink in the verse is honey, and the meaning of of different colors is that some of it is white, some of it is red, some of it is blue, and some of it is yellow, depending on the bees’ nature, colors, and foods. The majority of commentators agree that honey comes out of the bees’ mouths, and it was said from below them, and it was said that it is not known from where it comes out of them, and the pronoun in His statement: in it is healing for people refers to the drink that comes out of the bees’ bellies, which is honey, and this is what the majority agreed with. Al-Farra’, Ibn Kaysan, and a group of the Salaf said: The pronoun refers to the Qur’an, and the estimation in what we have narrated to you of verses and proofs is healing for people, and there is no reason to deviate from the apparent meaning and contradict the clear reference and the obvious context. Scholars have differed as to whether this cure that God has made in honey is general for all diseases or specific to some diseases. A group said: It is general, and a group said: It is specific to some diseases. This is indicated by the fact that honey is indefinite in the context of affirmation, so it is not general. Its indefiniteness, if intended to express glorification, only indicates that it contains a great cure for one or more diseases, not for every disease. The indefiniteness of glorification does not indicate generality. The apparent meaning derived from experience and the laws of medical science is that if it is used alone, it is a cure for specific diseases, and if it is mixed with other foods such as pastes and the like, it is, along with whatever it is mixed with, a cure for many diseases. In short, it is one of the greatest foods and most beneficial medicines, and these two matters rarely come together in anything else. Indeed in that mentioned about the matter of the bee is a sign for a people who give thought meaning they use their thoughts when looking at the creation of God, the Most High, and the wonders of His creations, for the matter of the bee is one of the most amazing, strangest, most precise, and most wisest of them. Abdul Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Nahhas, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the statement: You take from it intoxicant and good provision. He said: Intoxicant is what is forbidden from their fruits, and good provision is what is permissible. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: The forbidden intoxicant is wine, and good provision is raisins, and vinegar, and grapes and their benefits. Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said: Intoxicant is wine, and good provision is raisins, but this verse abrogated it: Intoxicants and gambling are only. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi also narrated on his authority regarding the verse that he said: Then God forbade intoxicant after that, preventing the prohibition of wine because it is from it, then He said: and good provision. So it is the permissible vinegar, raisins, wine and the like, so God approved it and made it permissible for the Muslims. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he was asked about intoxication, and he said: It is wine itself. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: Intoxication is wine. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And your Lord inspired the bee, that is, He inspired it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, So follow the ways of your Lord submissively, that is, paths that do not make the place you have taken difficult. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, Submissive, that is, obedient. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, that he said: Submissive. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, There comes forth from their bellies a drink, that is, honey. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, that he said: It is honey, in it is healing and in the Qur’an. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: Honey is a cure for every illness, and the Qur’an is a cure for what is in the chests. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: You should use two cures: honey and the Qur’an. Ibn Majah, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab, Ibn as-Sunni, Abu Nu`aym and al-Khatib narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You should use two cures: honey and the Qur’an. There are hadiths that indicate that honey is a cure, including what al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: “Healing is in three things: a cupping incision, a drink of honey or cauterization with fire, and I forbid my nation from cauterization.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id that a man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, my brother has diarrhea. He said: Give him honey to drink. So he gave him honey. Then he came back and said: I gave him honey to drink, but it only made the diarrhea worse. He said: Go and give him honey to drink. So he went and gave him honey to drink. Then he came back and said: It only made the diarrhea worse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has spoken the truth and your brother’s diarrhea has lied. Go and give him honey to drink. So he went and gave him honey to drink and he was cured.
16:70: When the Almighty mentioned some of the conditions of animals and what they contain of amazing wonders of craftsmanship and characteristics of overwhelming power, He followed it with the wonders of human creation and what lessons it contains, saying: 70- And God created you when you were nothing then He takes you at the end of your appointed times and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age it is said radhal yardhala radhalah, and the most decrepit and decrepit are the worst and most base thing. Al-Naysaburi said: Know that the wise have defined the stages of human life into four: the first is the age of maturity. The second is the age of standing, which is the age of youth. The third is the age of slight decline, which is the age of middle age. The fourth is the age of apparent decline, which is the age of old age. It was said that the most decrepit age is when a person becomes senile, which is when he becomes like a child who has no mind. It was said that it is seventy-five years, and it was said that it is ninety years. Similar to this verse is the saying of the Most High: “Indeed, We created man in the best stature. Then We returned him to the lowest of the low.” Then the Most High explained the reason for returning the one who returns to the most decrepit age by saying: So that he may not know after knowledge he had acquired anything of knowledge, neither much nor little, or something of the information if knowledge here means the known. It was said that what is meant by knowledge here is the mind, and it was said that what is meant is so that he may not know more than the knowledge that he had acquired before that.
16:71: Then when He, the Almighty, explained the creation of man and his changes in the stages of life, He mentioned some of his conditions, so that he might remember at that time, and He said: 71- And God has favored some of you over others in provision. So He made you unequal in it, so He made it abundant for some of His servants until He made for them from provision what is sufficient for thousands of the sons of Adam, and He made it narrow for some of His servants until they could not find sustenance except by asking people and begging from them, and that is for a profound wisdom that the minds of the servants fall short of understanding and knowing the true causes of it. And just as He made the difference between His servants in wealth, He made it between them in intellect, knowledge, understanding, strength of body and weakness, beauty and ugliness, health and sickness, and other conditions. And it was said that the meaning of the verse is that God, the Almighty, gave the clients better than He gave their slaves, as evidenced by His statement: Then those whom God favored with abundant provision are not able to give back their provision to those whom their right hands possess. That is, those whom God favored with abundant provision over others are not able to give back their provision that God provided them with over What their right hands possess of slaves, “they are equal in it, meaning the owners and the slaves, in it, meaning in the provision, are equal, meaning they do not return it to them in a way that makes them equal to them. So the fa in this is to indicate that equality is a consequence of reciprocity: that is, they do not return it to them in a way that entails equality, but rather they return to them a small amount of it. This is an example that God Almighty gave to idol worshippers: that is, if your slaves are not equal to you and you are not satisfied with that, then how can you make My slaves equal to me when the situation is that your slaves are equal to you in humanity and creation? So when you do not make your slaves partners with you in your wealth, then how can you make some of God Almighty’s slaves partners with Him and worship them with Him, or how can you make some of His creations, such as idols, partners with Him in worship? Ibn Jarir mentioned the meaning of this. An example of this verse is the saying of God Almighty: “He has set forth for you an example from yourselves: Do you have among those your right hands possess partners in what We have provided for you?” It was said that the fa in they are equal in it means until. Do they then deny the favor of God? When you do what you do of polytheism, and the favor is that He, the Most High, made the owners preferable over the slaves, and they deny has been read with the lower and upper case. Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim said: The third-person reading is more appropriate because of the proximity of what is being reported, and because if it were an address, it would appear to be for the Muslims, and the question is for denial, and the fa is for conjoining with an implied meaning: that is, they associate partners with Him and thus deny His favor, and the meaning according to the address reading is that the owners are not the ones who give their sustenance to their slaves, rather I am the one who provides for them and them, so do not think that they give them anything, rather it is My sustenance that I make flow through their hands and they are all equal in that, they have no advantage over their slaves, so the implied conjoined to it is a verb that suits this meaning, as if it were said: they do not understand that and thus deny the favor of God.
16:72: Then He, the Almighty, mentioned the other state of man, saying: 72- And God has made for you mates from among yourselves. The commentators said: He means women, for He created Eve from Adam's rib, or the meaning is: He created for you mates from among your own kind so that you may be comforted by them, because a species is comforted by its own kind and is estranged from those other than its own kind, and because of this comfort, what occurs between men and women is the cause of offspring, which is the purpose of marriage. For this reason, He said: And He has made for you from among your mates sons and grandchildren. Grandchildren is the plural of Hafidh, it is said Hafid Yahfid Hafdan and Hafudan: if he hastens, so whoever hastens in service is a Hafidh. Abu Ubaid said: Hafid is work and service. Al-Khalil bin Ahmad said: Hafidh among the Arabs means servants, and from that is the saying of the poet, who is Al-A'sha: Our unknown was assigned Yemeni camels, while the camels on their shoulders were singing That is, servants and helpers. Al-Azhari said: It was said that the grandchildren are the children of the children, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it was said that they are the two sisters, as was said by Ibn Masoud, Alqamah, Abu Al-Dhaha, Saeed bin Jubair, and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and from it is the saying of the poet: If my soul had been willing, I would have become a great-grandchild for it, as it is known. But she is the same as Ali Abi Ayouf, and she is filthy towards her in-laws It was said that the grandchildren are the in-laws. Al-Asma’i said: The son-in-law is the one who was from the woman’s side, such as her son, brother, and the like, and the in-laws are all of them. It is said that so-and-so in-lawed to the Banu so-and-so and married. It was also said that they are the children of a man’s wife from someone other than him. It was also said that they are the children who serve him. It was also said that they are the daughters who serve their father. Many scholars have suggested that they are the sons of sons, because God Almighty has bestowed His favor upon His servants by giving them sons and grandchildren from among their wives. So the grandchildren are apparently connected to the sons, even though it is possible that the meaning is: He gave you sons from among your wives and gave you grandchildren. However, based on this apparent meaning, it is not impossible that the sons are meant to be those who do not serve, and the grandchildren are those who serve the father, or that the grandchildren are meant to be the daughters only. It does not benefit them to be the sons of sons unless the verse is understood to mean: And He gave you sons from among your wives, and grandchildren from among the sons. And He has provided you with good things that you enjoy and delight in. Min is for partiality because good things are not combined except in Paradise. Then God Almighty concluded the verse by saying: Do they then believe in falsehood? The question is for reproachful denial, and the fa is for connecting to something understood: that is, they disbelieve in God and believe in falsehood. Falsehood preceded the verb to indicate that they have no faith except in Him, and falsehood is their belief in their idols that they harm and benefit. It was said: Falsehood is what Satan has made attractive to them of prohibiting the bahīrah and the sā’ibah and the like. The majority of scholars read they believe with a sukoon, while Abu Bakr read it with a sukoon on the address and by the favor of God they are ungrateful meaning what He has bestowed upon them that is beyond description. In presenting the favor and placing the separating pronoun in the middle is evidence that their ungratefulness is specific to that and does not go beyond it for the purpose of exaggeration and emphasis.
16:73: 73- And they worship besides God is connected to they disbelieve and is included under the reproachful denial, a denial from Him, the Most High, against them, as they worship idols, which neither benefit nor harm. For this reason, He said, He who does not possess for them any provision from the heavens or the earth. Al-Akhfash said: Something is a substitute for provision. Al-Farra’ said: It is accusative because of the provision being bestowed upon it, so he made provision a verbal noun that works on something, and Al-Akhfash made it a name for provision. It was said that it is possible that it is an emphasis on his saying does not possess meaning that he does not possess anything of the kingdom, and the meaning is that these infidels worship deities that do not possess for them provision, meaning provision, and from the heavens and the earth is an attribute of provision, meaning being from them, and the pronoun in and they are not able refers to what, and the plural is the plural of rational beings based on their false claim, and the benefit in denying the ability from them is that the one who does not possess anything may be described as having the ability to possess in some way, so the Almighty made clear that it does not possess and is not able, and it was said that the pronoun in they are able is for the infidels: meaning that these infidels are not able, despite being alive and acting, so how about inanimate objects that have no life and are not able to act?
16:74: Then He, the Almighty, forbade them from likening Him to His creation. He said: 74- So do not make comparisons for God. For the one who makes comparisons compares one situation to another and one story to another. Al-Zajjaj said: Do not make comparisons for God because He is One and has no equal. They used to say: The God of the world is too great for one of us to worship Him. So they used to resort to idols and planets, just as the lowliest of people serve the most eminent of the king's presence, and those eminent ones serve the king. So they were forbidden from doing that, and the reason for the prohibition was His saying: Indeed, God is All-Knowing knows what you are to worship and you do not know what evil consequences there are in worshipping it, and exposing yourself to the punishment of God, the Almighty, or you do not know anything about that, and your action is based on a corrupt imagination, a false thought, and a distorted fantasy. It is possible that it is meant: Do not make comparisons for God, for God knows how comparisons are made and you do not know that. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ali regarding his statement: And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age, he said: Seventy-five years. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: It is senility. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: Whoever recites the Qur’an will not be returned to the most decrepit age, then he recited: So that he may know nothing after having known. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Tawus who said: The scholar does not become senile. It has been proven from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Sahih and other books that he used to seek refuge with God from being returned to the most decrepit age. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And God has favored some of you over others in provision, he said: They would not share their wealth and women with their slaves, so how can they share My slaves with Me in My authority? Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse who said: This is an example of false gods with God. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: {And God has made for you mates from among yourselves} that he said: He created Adam, then created his wife from him. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Bukhari in his history, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: {Sons and grandchildren} that he said: The grandchildren are the two sisters. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The grandchildren are the in-laws. And they narrated on his authority that he said: The grandchildren are the sons and the sons’ sons. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said: The grandchildren are the sons’ sons. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Hamza that Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement: {Sons and grandchildren} that he said: Whoever criticizes you has criticized you. Haven’t you heard the poet say: The grandchildren were surrounded by the camels and their hands were covered with the camels’ crisis. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said: The grandchildren are the sons of a man’s wife, they are not from him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, Then do they believe in falsehood? He said: Polytheism. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: It is Satan. And by the grace of God? He said: Muhammad. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding His statement, And they worship other than God the verse, he said: These idols that are worshipped other than God do not possess for those who worship them provision from the heavens and the earth nor goodness nor life nor resurrection. So do not make comparisons for God for He is One, Eternal Refuge, He did not beget nor was He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, the Most High, So do not make comparisons for God meaning their taking idols, he said: Do not make a god with Me other than Me, for there is no god other than Me.
16:75: His saying: 75- God sets forth a parable When He, the Most High, said that God knows: that is, with the information that includes how to set forth parables and you do not know, He, the Most High, taught them how to set forth parables, so He said: God sets forth a parable: that is, He mentioned something that can be used as evidence to show the contrast between the side of the Creator, the Most High, and what they made partners with Him from the idols, then He mentioned that and said: A slave owned and the parable in reality is a condition of the slave that occurs to him, which is ownership and inability to act, so His saying: A slave owned who is not able to do anything is an explanation of the parable and a substitute for it, and He described him as being owned because the slave and the free man share in the fact that each one of them is a slave of God, the Most High, and He described him as not being able to do anything because the mukatab and the mu'adhun are able to do some acts, so this description is to distinguish him from them, and whom We have provided is the relative, and it is conjoined with a slave: that is, and whom We have provided from Us That is, from our side, good provision from the free people who own money and dispose of it as they wish. What is meant by provision being good is that it is something that is good in the eyes of people, because it is a plentiful provision that includes desirable and valuable things that please those who look at it. The fa in His statement, so he spends from it is to arrange spending after provision: that is, he spends from it in ways of goodness and spends from it on types of righteousness and kindness. The accusative of secretly and openly is in the state: that is, he spends from it in the case of secret and in the case of publicity. What is meant is to clarify the generality of spending for times, and presenting secretly before publicity indicates its virtue over it, and that the reward for it is greater. It was said that from in and from whom We provided for him is described as if it was said: and a free man We provided for him, to match a slave. Are they equal? That is, the free man and the slave described by the aforementioned attributes. The plural of the pronoun is for the place of from, because it is an ambiguous noun in which one and two and the plural and the masculine and feminine are equal. It was said that what is meant by slave and the relative pronoun, which is an expression for the free man, is the gender: that is, whoever is characterized by those attributes. Of both sexes, and the question is for denial: that is, are slaves and free people described with those attributes equal, even though both groups are created by God Almighty from among mankind, and it is known that they are not equal in their view, so how can they make partners for God Almighty who do not possess any harm or benefit for them, and make them deserving of worship along with God Almighty? The meaning is that just as a slave who is owned and has no control over his own affairs is not the same to you as a free man whom God has provided with a good provision and from which he spends, so too the Lord, the Creator and Provider, is not the same as the inanimate objects of the idols that you worship, which do not see, hear, harm, or benefit. It was said that what is meant by the slave in the verse is the disbeliever who is deprived of obeying God and worshipping Him, and the other is the believer, and the point is that they are not the same in rank and honor. It was said that the slave is the idol, and the second is the worshipper of the idol, and the point is that they are not the same in ability and action, because the first is an inanimate object and the second is a human being. Praise be to God means all praise is due to God, because He is the Benefactor and no one else among His servants deserves anything from Him, so how can the idols deserve anything from Him or any blessing from Him at all, neither by origin nor by mediation? It was said that He meant praise be to God for the blessing of monotheism that He has bestowed upon His friends. It was also said that He meant say, Praise be to God, and the address is either to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to the one whom God has provided with a good provision. It was said that When he mentioned an example that was appropriate for the purpose and revealed the intended meaning, he said, Praise be to God, meaning for the strength of this argument, but most of them do not know, that is, until they worship the One to whom worship is due and recognize the One who bestowed great blessings upon them. And denying knowledge from them is either because they are so ignorant that they do not understand what is required of them, or because they abandon the truth out of stubbornness despite their knowledge of it, so they are like someone who has no knowledge. And he singled out the majority by denying knowledge, either because he meant all of creation, and most of them are polytheists, or he mentioned the majority while he meant all, or what is meant is most of the polytheists, because among them are those who know but do not act in accordance with knowledge.
16:76: Then the Almighty mentioned a second example that He gave for Himself, and for the religious and worldly blessings that He bestows upon His servants, and for the idols that are dead and do not harm or benefit, so He said: 76- And God sets forth an example, meaning another example that is clearer and more evident than the one before it, and two men is a substitute for an example and an explanation for it, and the mute is the one who is dumb and stunned, and it was said that he is the one who is cut off from the tongue and does not speak well, and Tha’lab narrated on the authority of Ibn al-A’rabi that he is the one who does not hear or see, then He described the mute and said: He is not able to do anything of the things related to himself or others due to his lack of understanding and inability to speak, and the meaning of each upon his master is a burden on his guardian and relatives and children upon the one who is in charge of his affairs and supports him and a burden upon his brothers, and the orphan may be called each because of his burden on the one who charges him, and from this is the saying of the poet: I eat everyone's money before my youth if everyone's bones are not strong This is a statement of his inability to provide for his own interests after mentioning his inability to do anything at all. Then he described him with a fourth attribute, saying, Wherever he directs him, he brings no good, meaning if he directs him in any direction, he brings no good at all, because he does not understand or comprehend what is said to him, and he cannot say it. Yahya ibn Waththāb read Wherever he directs in the passive form, and Ibn Mas‘ūd read Wherever he directs in the past tense, Is he equal in himself with these attributes that he has, and he who enjoins justice, meaning he enjoins people to be just, while he himself speaks what he wants to speak and understands, and is able to manage things, and he in himself is on a straight path, on a sound religion and a good conduct in which there is no inclination toward either side of excess or deficiency. He contrasted the attributes of the first with these two attributes mentioned for the other, because the sum of the attributes of the first is that he does not deserve anything, and the sum of my description of this is that he deserves the most complete deserving, and the purpose is to prove that these two mentioned are not equal to the impossibility of equality between Him, the Most High, and what they make a partner with Him. 43- The Day they emerge from the graves quickly Day is a substitute for their day, and quickly is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun they emerge. The majority read they emerge in the active form. As-Salami, Al-A'mash, Al-Mughirah, and Asim in one narration read it in the passive form, and Al-Ajdath is the plural of Jadth, which is the grave. As if they were hastening to a monument The majority read Nasb with a fatha on the noon and a sukoon on the sad. Ibn Amir and Halas read it with a damma on the noon and the sad, and Amr ibn Maymun and Abu Raja read it with a damma on the noon and a sukoon on the sad. It is said in As-Sahah: The nasb is what is erected so that it is worshipped instead of God, and so is the nasb with a damma, and it may be moved. Al-A'sha said: And do not worship this erected idol, nor worship Satan. But worship God. The plural is ansaab. Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra’ said: An-Nasb is the plural of an-Nasb, like Rahn and Rahn. Ansaab is the plural of an-Nasb, so it is the plural of plural. It was also said that an-Nasb is the plural of Nisab, which is a stone or an idol on which sacrifices are made. From this is His statement, And what is sacrificed on al-Ansaab. An-Nahhas said: Nasb and Nasb have the same meaning. It was also said that the meaning of to an-Nasab is to a limit, which is that which you direct your sight to. Al-Kalbi said: To something erected, a flag or a banner: meaning, as if they were calling to a flag, or a banner erected for them, they rush. Al-Hasan said: They would rush when the sun rose to their altars which they worshipped instead of God, not to hunt game there, for fear of it escaping. The meaning of yufaduun is they hasten, and ifyadh is to hasten. It is said that he hastened ifyadan, meaning he hastened quickly. From this is the saying of the poet: The knights of Dhubyan are under the iron, like jinn, who are being chased by genius. Ubaqar: a village of the jinn, as the Arabs claim. From this comes the saying of Labid: Old and young people are like the paradise of a genius
16:77: When He, the Almighty, finished mentioning the two examples, He praised Himself by saying: To God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, meaning that this is unique to Him, and no one else shares it with Him, nor is He independent of it. What is meant is knowledge of what is hidden from the servants in them, or He meant by their unseen the Day of Resurrection because His knowledge is hidden from the servants, and the meaning of the addition to them is attachment to them. Meaning: Rebuking and reprimanding the polytheists: that is, worship is only deserved by those who have this characteristic, not those who are ignorant and helpless, who neither harm nor benefit nor know any type of knowledge. And the matter of the Hour which is the greatest of the disputes that have occurred regarding the unseen matters specific to Him, the Most High, is but as the blink of an eye. A blink of an eye is quick, and there must be a time in which the pupil turns toward what is seen, and every time is divisible. Therefore, He said, Or it meaning their matter is nearer. This is not an exaggeration, rather it is a statement of the utmost truth, because the period between the address and the establishment of the Hour is finite, and from it to eternity there is no limit, and there is no relation between the finite and the infinite. Or it can be said: Since the Hour was coming and it must be, it was made as near as the blink of an eye. Al-Zajjaj said: It was not said that the Hour will come in the blink of an eye, but rather it is a description of the speed of the ability to bring it about, because He says to a thing, Be, and it is. It was said that the meaning is: It is like that with God, even if it is not like that with the created beings. Similar to it is His statement, the Most High: Indeed, they see it far away, but We see it near. The word or is it nearer is not for doubt, but for representation. It was said that it was included due to the doubt of the one being addressed. It was said that it is like rather, “Indeed, God is over all things competent,” and the speed of the Hour is among His abilities.
16:78: Then He, the Almighty, mentioned another state of man that indicates the utmost of His power and the ultimate of His compassion, saying 78- And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, not knowing a thing. This is connected to His statement: And God made for you mates from among yourselves, joining with it in the chain of evidence for monotheism: that is, He brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers as children, not knowing anything. The phrase you do not know anything is in the accusative case as a state. It was said that what is meant is that you do not know anything of the covenant that was taken from you. It was said that you do not know anything of what He decreed for you of happiness and misery. It was said that you do not know anything of your benefits. The first is the generalization so that the verse includes these matters and others, considering the generality of the wording, since something is an indefinite noun in the context of negation. Al-A'mash, Ibn Waththab, and Hamzah read your mothers with a kasra on the hamza and the meem here, and in An-Nur, Az-Zumar, and An-Najm. Al-Kisa'i read with a kasra on the hamza and a fatha on the meem. The rest read it with a damma on the hamza and a fatha on the meem, And He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts, meaning He placed these things in you, and it is conjoined with He brought you forth, and there is no indication in it that this making was delayed after bringing you forth, since the meaning of the waw is the absolute plural. The meaning is: He made for you these things so that you may obtain through them the knowledge that was taken away from you when you were brought forth from your mothers’ wombs, and so that you may act in accordance with that knowledge by thanking the Benefactor, worshipping Him, and fulfilling His rights. Hearts is the plural of fu’ad, which is the middle of the heart, located in it, like the heart in the chest. We have already mentioned the reason for singling out hearing, pluralizing sight, and hearts, which is that singling out hearing, since it is originally a source, includes both little and much. That you may be grateful, meaning so that you may use each instrument for what it was created for, and then you will know the extent of what God has bestowed upon you, so you may thank Him, or that this spending is the same as thanking.
16:79: Then the Almighty mentioned another proof of His perfect power. He said: 79- Have they not seen the birds subservient? That is, have they not looked at them while they are subservient: that is, made easy to fly by what God created for them of wings and all the other reasons that are conducive to that, such as the thinness of the air and His inspiration to spread and close the wing as a swimmer does in water in the atmosphere of the sky that is, in the air far from the earth in the direction of elevation, and adding it to the sky because it is on its side What holds them up in the atmosphere except God the Almighty with His dazzling power, for the weight of their bodies and the thinness of the air require that they fall, because they do not cling to anything above them nor rely on anything below them. Yahya ibn Waththab, Al-A'mash, Ibn Amir, Hamzah, and Ya'qub read Have you not seen with the superiority of the address, and Abu Ubaid chose this reading. The rest read with the letter ta’tiyah: Indeed, in that are signs, meaning that in that subjugation in that manner are clear signs that indicate the oneness of God Almighty and His dazzling power for a people who believe in God Almighty and in what His messengers brought of the laws that God legislated. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: “God sets forth a parable: a slave owned by someone who is not able to spend in the way of God.” And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision. “And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision.” And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision. “And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision.” And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision. “And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision.” And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision. “And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision.” And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision. “And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision.” And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision. “And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision.” And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision. “And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision.” And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision. “And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision.” And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision,... Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on his authority that he said: This verse, “God sets forth a parable: a slave owned by a man” was revealed about a man from Quraysh and Abdah ibn Hisham ibn Amr, who was the one who spent secretly and openly, and Abdah Abu al-Juza’ who used to forbid him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that regarding His statement, “God sets forth a parable: two men, one of them mute” the verse, he said: By the mute he means the one who is a burden on his disbelieving master, and one who enjoins justice the believer, and this parable is in deeds. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir also narrated on his authority that he said: This verse, “God sets forth a parable: two men” the verse was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan and his disbelieving slave, who was Asid ibn Abi al-Ays, who hated Islam. Uthman used to spend on him, provide for him and take care of his expenses, while the other used to forbid him from giving charity and doing good deeds, so it was revealed about them both. Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari in his History, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Dhiya' in Al-Mukhtara also narrated from him regarding his statement: And whoever enjoins justice, he said: Uthman ibn Affan. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: All, he said: All are the dependents. When they set out, they would carry him on a docile camel, and they would have a group of people with him to hold him down for fear that he would fall on them, which would be a burden and torment and a dependent on them. Is he equal to one who enjoins justice while he is on a straight path? meaning himself. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada regarding his statement: And the matter of the Hour is not but as the twinkling of an eye meaning that he says: Be, so it is as the twinkling of an eye or even nearer so the Hour is as the twinkling of an eye or even nearer. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, he said: From the womb. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada regarding his statement: In the atmosphere of the sky meaning in the middle of the sky.
16:80: His saying: 80- And God has made for you is connected to what preceded it, and this mentioned is from among the conditions of man, and from the enumeration of God's blessings upon him, and dwelling is a source that describes the singular and the plural, and it means inhabited: that is, you dwell in it and your limbs are calm from movement, and this is a blessing, for God Almighty had He willed, He would have created the servant always agitated like the heavens, and if He had willed, He would have created him forever still like the earth. And He has made for you from the hides of cattle, houses when He Almighty mentioned the houses of cities, which are those for long-term residence, then He mentioned the houses of the desert and the journey: that is, He made for you from the hides of cattle, which are the mats and leather, houses like tents and domes that you find light that is, it is easy for you to carry them on journeys and other things, and for this He said on the day of your departure and departure with the opening of the eye and its sukoon, and it was read with them: the travel of the people of the desert for migration and moving from one place to another, and from it is the saying of Antarah: The departure of those I expect to be separated, and the speckled crow runs among them The litter is also and from their wool and their hair and their furnishings is connected to He made meaning He made for you from the wool and their hair and their fur, and the livestock includes camels, cows and sheep as mentioned above, and the wool is for the sheep, the hair is for the camels, and the hair is for the goats, and they are among the sheep, so the mention of these three is for the purpose of variation, each one of them for one of the three, I mean the camels, the two types of sheep, and the furnishings are the household goods, and its origin is abundance and gathering, and from it is the poem athith meaning abundant and gathered, the poet said: A branch adorns the back, jet black, thick as the trunk of a palm tree. Al-Khalil said: Aththan means joined together, from ath if it increases. Al-Farra’ said: It has no singular. And the enjoyment is that which is enjoyed in various ways. And according to the saying of Abu Zaid Al-Ansari: The furniture is all money: camels, sheep, slaves, and the enjoyment. The conjunction of the enjoyment with the furniture is from the conjunction of the specific with the general. And it was said that the furniture is what a person wears and uses from the cover and the rug, and the enjoyment is what is spread out in the houses and adorned with. And the meaning of until a time is until you have satisfied your desires for it, or until it wears out and perishes, or until death, or until the Resurrection.
16:81: Then since man may not have tents or buildings to shelter under due to poverty or some other reason, and he needs to shelter under a tree, wall, cloud, or something similar, the Almighty pointed out that and said: 81- He made for you from what He created shades meaning things that you can shelter under, such as the things mentioned. The point is that shade includes things that provide shade. Then since the traveler may need a corner to take refuge in when he descends, and something that protects him from the harms of heat and cold, the Almighty pointed out that and said: And He made for you shelters in the mountains which is the plural of kan: which is what you shelter in from the rain, and here it is the caves in the mountains, God the Almighty made them a provision for creation to shelter in and fortify themselves in and isolate themselves from creation in them And He made for you garments plural of sarbal, which are shirts and clothes made of wool, cotton, linen, etc. Al-Zajjaj said: Everything you wear is a garment, and the meaning of protect you from the heat is to protect you from the harm of the heat. He specified the heat and did not mention the cold, as it was sufficient to mention one of the two opposites instead of mentioning the other, because what protects from the heat protects from the cold. The reason for specifying the heat is that protection from it was more important to them than protection from the cold, due to the prevalence of heat in their country. And garments to protect you from your violence are the armor and shields with which they protect themselves from stabbing, striking, and shooting. The meaning is that they prevent the violence that comes from some of you to others in war. Thus He completes His favor upon you meaning, like that perfect completion, His favor is completed upon you, for He, the Almighty, has bestowed upon His servants the various favors mentioned here and others, and by His grace and kindness He will complete for them the favor of religion and this world. That you may submit meaning that you may submit, for whoever ponders this matter, there is nothing left for him but Islam and submission to the truth. Ibn Muhaisin and Hamid read wa tamim ni’mah with two ta’s above it, meaning that the subject is ni’mah. The rest read it with ta’ below it, meaning that the subject is God, the Most High. Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah read taslamun with a fatha on the ta’ and lam from safety from wounds. The rest read it with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the lam from Islam. Abu Ubaid said: The preferred reading is the general reading, because what God has bestowed upon us of Islam is better than what He has bestowed of safety from wounds. It was said that the address is to the people of Mecca, meaning that you, O people of Mecca, may you sincerely devote your Lordship to God. The first is to carry it in general terms, and to single out the blessing here because what is meant by it is the source.
16:82: 82- But if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear conveyance. That is, if they turn away from you and do not accept what you have brought, then your excuse has been prepared, for upon you is only the clear conveyance of what you were sent to them with: that is, the obvious, and there is nothing else upon you. And directing the address to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is to console him.
16:83: And the sentence 83 - "They know the favor of God, then they deny it" is a resumption of explaining their turning away: that is, they know the favor of God, which He has enumerated, and they acknowledge that it is from God, the Most High, then they deny it with what occurs from their ugly actions of worshipping other than God and with their false words, where they say it is from God, but it is through the intercession of idols, and where they say that they inherited those favors from their fathers, and also because they do not use these favors to please the Lord, the Most High, and in the ways of goodness that God has commanded them to spend them in, and it was said that the favor of God is the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they knew him, then they denied his prophethood "and most of them are disbelievers", that is, those who deny the favors of God or those who disbelieve in God, and here He expressed the majority to mean all, or by the majority He meant the rational ones without children and the like, or He meant the disbelief of denial, and not all of them were disbelievers like that, rather the disbelief of some of them was the disbelief of ignorance, and the disbelief of some of them was due to denying the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, with Their recognition of God and their not denying His Lordship. An example of this verse is the Almighty’s saying: “And they denied it, while their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance. So see how was the end of the corrupters.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, sakana, meaning: you live in it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi something similar, saying: And He has made for you from the hides of the cattle, houses, which are the tents of the Arabs. You find them light, meaning: for carrying, and provision, meaning: for a time, for a time, meaning: until death. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, You find them light on the day of your departure, meaning: some of the houses of the car are built in an hour. In his statement, and their hair, he said: camels, and their hair, he said: sheep. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, in his statement, furniture, he said: furniture is provision. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority, he said: furniture is money, and provision for a time, meaning: you benefit from it for a time. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And God has made for you from what He has created shades, he said: from trees and other things, And has made for you shelters in the mountains, he said: from raids in which to dwell, And has made for you garments to protect you from the heat, he said: from cotton, linen and wool, and garments to protect you from your violence, from iron, Thus does He perfect His favor upon you that you may submit, and that is why this surah is called the Surah of Blessings. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Garments to protect you from the heat, he said: meaning the clothes, and garments to protect you from your violence, he said: meaning the armor and weapons, Thus does He perfect His favor upon you that you may submit, meaning from wounds. And Ibn Abbas used to read it as you submit, as we mentioned earlier, and its chain of transmission is weak.
16:84: When the Almighty explained the state of these people, that they recognized the blessing of God and then denied it, and that most of them are disbelievers, He followed it with types of threats on the Day of Resurrection, saying: 84- And the Day We will raise up from every nation a witness meaning, and remember the Day We will raise up, or the Day We will raise up they will fall into what they fell into, and the witness of every nation will be its prophet who will testify for them with faith and belief, and against them with disbelief, denial and falsification. Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved meaning to apologize, since they have no argument or excuse, as the Almighty said: And permission will not be given to them to make excuses or in the abundance of speech, or in returning to the worldly home, and the inclusion of then here is to indicate that their trial by being prevented from apologizing, which indicates total despair, is more severe than their trial by the testimony of the prophets. Nor will they be asked to repent because reprimand is only sought for the sake of returning to contentment, so if one is determined to be angry, then there is no benefit in reprimanding. Meaning: They are not appeased: that is, they are not required to please their Lord, because the Hereafter is not a place of obligation, nor are they left to the return of this world so that they may repent. The root of the word is from reproach, which is the one who finds fault. It is said that he reproached him, if he finds fault with him. So if he pours out on him what he reproached him for, it is said that he reproached him. So if he returns to his pleasure, it is said that he reproached him. The noun is reproach, which is the return of the reproached to what pleases the reproacher. This was said by Al-Harawi, and from it is the saying of Al-Nabigha: If you are wronged, then you are a servant whom you have wronged. If you are someone who is to be blamed, then someone like you is to be blamed.
16:85: 85- And when those who did wrong see the punishment, meaning, when those who associated others with God see the punishment they deserve for their association with God, which is the punishment of Hell, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved, meaning, they will not be given respite to repent, as there is no repentance there.
16:86: 86- And when those who associate others with God see their partners meaning their idols and statues that they worshipped, since it was established that they will be resurrected with the polytheists so that it will be said to them, whoever worshipped something, let him follow it, as was established in the Sahih from the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They will say, 'Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You' meaning those whom we used to worship besides You. Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: The polytheists' intention in this statement was to attribute the sin to those idols, making excuses for that and seeking comfort, even though they knew that the punishment would inevitably befall them, but the drowning person clings to whatever he can lay his hands on. So they cast down to them the word meaning those idols, statues, devils, and the like cast down to the polytheists the word Indeed, you are liars meaning they said to them that you, polytheists, are liars in what you claim of attributing the sin to us, which is what you intended by this statement. If it is said that the polytheists pointed to the idols and the like saying that these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You, and they were truthful in that, so how could the idols and the like have denied them that these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You, and they were truthful in that, so how could the idols and the like have denied them? The answer is that what they meant by their saying these are our partners is that these are partners of God in worship, so the idols denied them in their claim of this partnership. And even if the idols and statues are not able to speak, God Almighty makes them speak in that case to shame the polytheists and rebuke them. This is like what the angels said, Rather, they used to worship the jinn, meaning that the jinn were the ones who were satisfied with their worship of them.
16:87: 87- And they will cast their submission to God on that Day meaning that the polytheists will cast their submission and obedience to His punishment and submission to His might on the Day of Resurrection. It was said that the worshipper and the worshipped will submit and obey His judgment over them. And what they used to invent will be lost to them meaning that what they used to invent, that God Almighty has partners and what they used to claim about their intercession for them, and that their worship of them will bring them closer to God Almighty, will be lost and invalidated.
16:88: 88- Those who disbelieved in themselves and averted others from the path of God meaning from the path of truth, which is the path of Islam and faith, by preventing them from following it and leading them to disbelief. It was said that what is meant by averting from the path of God is averting from the Sacred Mosque, but the first is general. Then He informed about those who did this action by saying: We increased their punishment upon the punishment meaning that God increased their punishment for misleading others above the punishment that they deserved for their misguidance. It was said that the meaning is: We increased the leaders' punishment upon the punishment of their followers, meaning more severe than it. It was said that this increase is their removal from the Fire into the freezing cold, and other things were said.
16:89: 89- And the Day We shall raise up in every nation a witness over them meaning a prophet who will testify against them from among themselves from their own kind, completing the argument and cutting off the excuse. This is a repetition of what came before for the purpose of emphasis and threat. And We have brought you O Muhammad as a witness over these meaning you testify against these nations and bear witness for them, and it was said over your nation. Something similar to this has been mentioned in Al-Baqarah and An-Nisa. And We have sent down to you the Book meaning the Qur'an. The sentence is a new sentence or in the accusative case as a state with the estimation of had "explaining everything" meaning explaining it. The ta' is for emphasis, and its counterpart from the sources is the reciprocal, and nothing else has come. An example of this verse is the saying of the Most High: "We have neglected nothing in the Book", and the meaning of it being an explanation of everything is that it contains the explanation of many rulings, and the reference in what remains of it to the Sunnah, and He commanded them to follow His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he brings of rulings, and to obey him as in the Qur'anic verses indicating this. It has been authenticated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said: I have been given the Qur’an and something similar to it with it, and as guidance for the servants, as mercy for them, and as good tidings for the Muslims specifically, without others, or the guidance, mercy, and good tidings are specific to them, because they are the ones who benefit from that.
16:90: Then when God Almighty mentioned that the Qur’an explains everything, He followed it with a verse that includes all the principles of obligation, confirming that, and He said: God commands justice and doing good. Scholars have differed in their interpretation of justice and benevolence. Some have said that justice is there is no god but God, and benevolence is performing the obligatory duties. Others have said that justice is the obligatory duty, and benevolence is the voluntary act. Others have said that justice is the equality of what is done in public and in private, and benevolence is that what is done in private is better than what is done in public. Others have said that justice is fairness, and benevolence is favor. The first is to interpret justice in the linguistic sense, which is the middle ground between the two extremes of excess and negligence. The meaning of His, the Most High, command to be just is that His servants be in a middle state in religion, not leaning towards excess, which is the blameworthy extremism in religion, nor towards negligence, which is neglecting something that is part of religion. As for ihsan, its linguistic meaning indicates that it is a favor that is not obligatory, such as voluntary charity. And ihsan includes doing what the servant is rewarded for, which God has not obligated him to do in worship and other things. It has been authentically reported from the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he interpreted ihsan as the servant worshipping God as if he sees Him. He said in the hadith of Ibn Umar, which is proven in the two Sahihs, And ihsan is to worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. This is the meaning of ihsan in Islamic law. And giving to relatives, meaning giving relatives what their need calls for. The verse is guidance to maintain ties with relatives and encouragement to give them charity. It is a case of connecting the specific to the general, if giving to relatives is included under justice and ihsan. It was said that it is from the aspect of connecting the recommended to the obligatory, and like this verse is His saying: And give the relative his right. And He only singled out the relatives because their right is more important, for God derived the name of the womb from His name, and made its connection from His connection and its severing from His severing. And forbids immorality is the increasingly ugly trait of speech or action, and it was said that it is adultery, and it was said that it is miserliness, and wrongdoing is what the Shari’ah has rejected by forbidding it, and it includes all sins of different types, and it was said that it is polytheism. And as for oppression, it was said that it is arrogance, and it was said that it is injustice, and it was said that it is hatred, and it was said that it is transgression, and its reality is exceeding the limit, so it includes these mentioned and is included in all its categories under wrongdoing, and it was only mentioned specifically out of concern for it due to the severity of its harm and the terrible consequences of it, and it is one of the sins that return to its doer, as God the Almighty said: Your oppression is only against yourselves. And this verse is one of the verses indicating the obligation of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, then God the Almighty concluded This verse, with His saying: He admonishes you that you may remember, means He admonishes you with what He mentioned in this verse of what He commanded you to do and what He forbade you from doing. It is sufficient in the chapter of admonition and reminder, that you may remember, meaning that you may remember what should be remembered, so that you may be admonished by what God admonished you with. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And the Day We raise up from every nation a witness, he said: Its witness is its prophet, that he has conveyed the messages of his Lord. God said: And We have brought you as a witness over these, he said: It was mentioned to us that when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse, his eyes would overflow with tears. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: So cast the word to them, he said: Speak to them. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And they will cast to God that Day their submission, he said: They surrendered. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada. And Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad ibn al-Sarri, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba`th wa al-Nushur narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding the statement of God, We will increase their punishment over the punishment, that he said: We will increase scorpions with fangs like tall palm trees. Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib narrated on the authority of al-Baraa’ that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God, the Most High, “We will increase their punishment over the punishment,” that he said: Scorpions like tall palm trees will bite them in Hellfire. Abu Ya`la, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, the Most High, We will increase their punishment over the punishment, that he said: Five rivers of fire that God poured upon them, and they will be tormented with some of them at night and with some of them during the day. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Jabir from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The increase is five rivers flowing from beneath the Throne over the heads of the people of Hell: three rivers equal to the length of the night, and two rivers equal to the length of the day.” Hence his statement: We have increased their punishment over the punishment. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Masoud who said: God has sent down in this Book an explanation of everything, but our knowledge falls short of what He has explained to us in the Qur’an. Then he recited: And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of everything. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id al-Zuhd, Ibn al-Durais in Fadhail al-Qur’an, Muhammad ibn Nasr in Kitab al-Salat, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated from Ibn Masoud who said: Whoever seeks knowledge should study the Qur’an, for in it is the knowledge of the first and the last. Ahmad narrated from Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As who said: “I was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when his eyes fixed on him and he said: Gabriel came to me and ordered me to put this verse in this place in the surah: ‘Indeed, God commands justice and doing good’” the verse. In its chain of transmission is Shahr ibn Hawshab. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation: Its chain of transmission is acceptable. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in full on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Kathir classified its chain of transmission as good. Al-Bawardi, Ibn Al-Sakn, Ibn Mandah and Abu Nu`aym narrated in Ma`rifat Al-Sahaba on the authority of Abd Al-Malik ibn Umair that when this verse reached Aktham ibn Saifi, the wise man of the Arabs, he said: I think it commands him to have good morals and forbids him from those that are not appropriate for them. Then he said to his al-Nas 114:Be leaders in this matter and do not be tails, and be first in it and do not be last in it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: God commands justice, he said: Testifying that there is no god but God, and doing good is the fulfillment of obligations, and giving to kith and kin, he said: Giving your relatives the right that God has made obligatory upon you because of kinship and kinship, and forbids immorality, he said: adultery, and wrongdoing, he said: polytheism, and oppression, he said: arrogance and injustice, He admonishes you, he said: He advises you, that you may remember. Sa’id ibn Mansur, al-Bukhari in al-Adab, Muhammad ibn Nasr in al-Salah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and he authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated, he said: The greatest verse in the Book of God is God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and the most comprehensive verse in the Book of God for good and evil is the verse in al-Nahl, God commands justice and doing good, and the verse in the Book of God that entrusts the most, And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect, and the most severe A verse in the Book of God, please: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves the verse. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha’b on the authority of Al-Hasan that he recited this verse: Indeed, God commands justice and doing good to the end, then he said: Indeed, God, the Almighty, has gathered for you all good and all evil in one verse. By God, justice and doing good have not left anything from obedience to God without gathering it, nor have they left anything from indecency, wrongdoing, and transgression from disobedience to God without gathering it. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of his father who said: Ali bin Abi Talib passed by some people talking, so he said: What are you talking about? They said: We are discussing chivalry. He said: Isn’t that enough for you in God’s Book when He says: Indeed, God commands justice and doing good so justice, fairness, and doing good are favors, so what is left after this?
16:91: God Almighty singled out from the group of commands included in His statement: Indeed, God commands justice the fulfillment of the covenant, so He said: 91- And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant. Its apparent meaning is general for every covenant that occurs from a person, without differentiating between a covenant of allegiance and other than it. Some commentators have singled out this covenant mentioned in this verse to the covenant that exists in the pledge of allegiance of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Islam, which is contrary to what is indicated by the covenant added to the name of God Almighty, which is generality that includes all of God's covenants. Even if we assume that the reason is specific to a covenant, this would not require limiting it to the reason, so consideration is given to the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. Some of them have interpreted it as an oath, and it is refuted by mentioning the fulfillment of oaths after it, where God Almighty said: And do not break oaths after their confirmation, meaning after their emphasis, severity, and confirmation. What is meant is not that the prohibition of breaking is specific to confirmed oaths, not to other oaths that do not have confirmation, for the prohibition of breaking includes everyone, but In breaking an oath that is confirmed by a sin greater than the sin of breaking what is not confirmed, it is said that he confirmed and affirmed, and these are two languages. Al-Zajjaj said: The original is the waw and the hamza is a substitute for it. This generality is limited to what is proven in the authentic hadiths from the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him do what is better and expiate for his oath. He even went to extremes in that, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: By God, I will not swear an oath and then see something better than it, except that I do what is better and expiate for my oath. These words are proven in the two Sahihs and others. Also excluded from this generality is the oath of idle talk, as God Almighty says: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths. It is possible that the restriction of emphasis here is to exclude idle oaths. We have already discussed oaths in detail in Surat al-Baqarah 2:And you have made God a guarantor over you, meaning a witness. It was said that He is a protector, and it was said that He is a guarantor, and it was said that He is a watchman, because the guarantor takes into account the condition of the one guaranteed. It was said that the emphasis of an oath is a person swearing on the same thing repeatedly. Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar that the emphasis is to swear twice, and if he swears once, then there is no expiation upon him. Indeed, God knows what you do, so He will reward you accordingly, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. It contains encouragement and intimidation.
16:92: Then he emphasized the obligation of fulfillment and the prohibition of breaking it, saying: 92- And do not be like the one who untwisted her yarn meaning, do not be in what you do of untwisting after emphasising like the one who untwisted her yarn: meaning what she spun after it was strong meaning after they had made the yarn strong and perfect, and it is related to untwisted ankathan plural of nakath with a kasra on the noon, what breaks its thread. Al-Zajjaj said: Ankathan is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, because the meaning of nakath is nakhatta, and it was responded that ankathan is not a verbal noun, but rather a plural as we mentioned. Al-Wahidi said: It is in the accusative case as a second object, just as you say, I broke it into pieces and parts meaning I made it into pieces and parts, and it is possible that it is a state.
