Ibn Qutaybah said: This verse is related to what preceded it, and the meaning is: And fulfill the covenant of God and do not break your oaths, for if you did that, you would be like a woman who spun a spun thread and made it perfect, then made it into pieces. The phrase you take your oaths as a means of deception between you is in the accusative case as a state. Al-Jawhari said: Deception is trickery and deception. Abu Ubaidah said: Every matter that is not correct is deception. It was said that deception is what is introduced into something despite its corruption. Al-Zajjaj said: Deception and fraud that one nation is more numerous than another nation means that a group is more numerous than a group: that is, more numerous than it and more abundant in wealth. It is said that something grows if it increases. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is do not betray a people because of their small number and your large number, or because of your small number and their large number, and you have supported them with oaths. It was said that when the Quraysh saw a thorn in the side of their enemies, they would break their covenant and ally with their enemies. It was also said that it was a warning to the believers not to be deceived by the large number of Quraysh and the abundance of their wealth, so they would break their allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. God is only testing you with it, meaning He is testing you by your being more numerous and plentiful, to see whether you will hold fast to the rope of loyalty or break it out of deceit due to your large number. The pronoun in with it refers to the content of the sentence: that one nation is more numerous than another: meaning God is only testing you with that large number to know what you will do, or God is only testing you with what He commands you and forbids you. And He will make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ, so He will clarify the truth and those who are in the right and raise their ranks, and He will clarify falsehood and those who are false, so He will inflict upon them the punishment they deserve. In this there is a warning and caution against opposing the truth and leaning toward falsehood, or He will make clear to you that over which you used to differ, regarding the Resurrection, Paradise, and Hell.
16:93: Then the Almighty explained that He is able to unite the believers and the disbelievers in loyalty or in faith, so He said: 93- And if God had willed, He could have made you one nation in agreement on the truth. But by virtue of divinity He misguides whom He wills by abandoning them as justice from Him towards them and guides whom He wills by granting them success as a favor from Him towards them. He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. For this reason He said: And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do of deeds in this world. The lam in and He will make clear to you and in and you will surely be questioned are the two parts that introduce the oath.
16:94: Then when He, the Almighty, forbade them from breaking all oaths, He forbade them from breaking specific oaths, saying: 94- And do not use your oaths as a means of deception between you, which are the oaths of allegiance. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: This is in forbidding those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from breaking the covenant on Islam and supporting the religion, and they provided evidence for this specificity with what is in His statement: Then a foot will slip after it had been firmly established of exaggeration, and with what is in His statement: And taste evil for what you have turned away because if they broke the covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would have turned others away from entering Islam. And if we assume that these oaths with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are the reason for the revelation of this verse, then the consideration is in the generality of the wording, not in the specificity of the reason. A group of commentators said: This is a repetition of what came before it for the purpose of emphasis and confirmation. The meaning of then a foot slips after it has been firmly established is that the foot of the one who takes his right hand as a means of deception slips from the path of truth after it has been firmly established and firmly rooted in it. It was said that the foot was singled out to indicate that the slip of one foot, that is, a foot that was honored or insignificant, is a great danger, so how about many feet? This is a metaphor for the upright person who falls into great evil and falls into it, because if the foot slips, it transfers the person from a state of good to a state of evil. It is said of someone who makes a mistake in something that his foot slipped, and from this is the saying of the poet: You have both caught up with Abs, whose throne has fallen, and Dhubyan, whose sandals have slipped under her feet. And taste the evil because you turned away meaning taste the bad punishment in this world or in the Hereafter, or in both because you turned away from the path of God meaning because of your turning away from the path of God, which is Islam, or because you turned others away from Islam. For whoever breaks the pledge of allegiance and apostatizes, others will follow his example in that, so his action is a bad tradition upon him and he bears the burden of it and the burden of whoever acts upon it. For this reason He said: And for you is a great punishment meaning extremely great, and it is the punishment of the Hereafter if what was meant by what preceded it was the punishment of this world.
16:95: Then He, the Almighty, forbade them from leaning towards worldly gain and going back on the covenant for its sake, saying: 95- And do not exchange the covenant of God for a small price. That is, do not take a small, insignificant exchange in return for your covenant. Every worldly gain, even if it appears to be a lot, is because it is fleeting and insignificant. For this reason, the Almighty mentioned, after reducing the gain of this world, the goodness of what is with God, saying: Indeed, what is with God is best for you. That is, what He has of victory in this world, spoils, and abundant provision, and what He has in the Hereafter of the bliss of Paradise that will never end or cease, is better for them. Then He explained the prohibition against exchanging the covenant of God for a small price, and that what is with God is better for them, saying: If you only knew. That is, if you were people of knowledge and the ability to distinguish between things.
16:96: Then he mentioned a conclusive proof of the insignificance of the worldly life and the goodness of what is with God, saying: 96- Whatever is with you will be exhausted, but whatever is with God will remain. It is known to every rational person that whatever is exhausted and disappears, no matter how great its number is, is insignificant and insignificant, and whatever remains and does not disappear is abundant and great. As for the bliss of the Hereafter, it is apparent. As for the bliss of this world that God has bestowed upon the believers, even if it is fleeting, since it is connected to the bliss of the Hereafter, it is from this perspective in the ruling of what is permanent and does not cease. Then he said: And We will surely reward those who were patient with the best of what they used to do. The lam is the preamble: meaning, We will reward them because of their patience in the face of the hardships of the obligation and the struggle against the disbelievers and their patience in the face of the harm they suffer from them with the best of what they used to do of acts of obedience. It was said that He only specified their best deeds because everything else, which is good, is permissible, and the reward is only for obedience. It was also said that the meaning is: And We will reward them with a reward more noble and abundant than their work, like His statement: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof. Or We will reward them according to the best individual of their deeds, meaning that We will give them in return for the lower individual of their mentioned deeds what We give them in return for the higher individual of them of a great reward. Not that We give the reward according to their individuals that vary in degrees of goodness by rewarding the good among them with a good reward, and the better with the better. This is what was said. Asim and Ibn Kathir read lanajziyna with a nun. The rest read it with a ya below it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muzaydah ibn Jabir regarding his statement: And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant, he said: This verse was revealed regarding the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as if whoever converted to Islam pledged allegiance to Islam, and said: And fulfill the covenant of God, the verse, so do not let the small number of Muhammad and his companions and the large number of polytheists cause you to break the pledge of allegiance that you have pledged to Islam. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And do not break oaths after their confirmation, he said: after making them strong. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar from Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Saeed ibn Jubayr. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ata ibn Abi Rabah from Ibn Abbas that Sa’idah Al-Asadiyyah used to collect hair and fibers, so this verse was revealed regarding her: And do not be like the one who undoes the thread she has spun. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Abu Bakr ibn Hafs, and in both narrations it says that she was insane. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the reason for the revelation of the verse, he said: There was a woman in Mecca called Kharqa’ of Mecca. She used to spin, and when she finished her yarn, she would undo it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Kathir the same meaning. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, that one nation should be more numerous than another nation, he said: People more numerous than other people. They narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: They used to make alliances with allies and find that they were more numerous and more powerful than them, so they would break the alliance of these and make alliances with those who were more powerful, so they were forbidden from doing that.
16:97: This is a start to encourage every believer to do every good deed, and a generalization of the promise, and the meaning of 97- Whoever does righteousness whoever does a righteous deed, whatever the deed, and the increase in the distinction with male or female with the word whoever being inclusive of both for the purpose of emphasis and exaggeration in stating the promise, and it was said that the word whoever is apparent in males, so in specifying the male and female it was a statement of its inclusiveness of both types and the phrase and he is a believer in the accusative case as a state, the Almighty made faith a condition in the mentioned reward because the work of the disbeliever is not taken into account for His saying the Almighty: And We will present to them whatever deeds they have done and make them as scattered dust then He mentioned the reward for whoever does that righteous deed and said: Then We will cause him to live a good life and there was a disagreement about what the good life is? It was said with lawful provision, this was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ata' and Ad-Dahhak. It was said that it is contentment, said by Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Zaid bin Wahb, and Wahb bin Munabbih. It was also narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas. It was said that it is success in obedience, said by Al-Dahhak. It was said that the good life is the life in Paradise. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Qatadah, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: Life is not good for anyone except in Paradise. It was said that the good life is happiness, narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said that it is knowledge of God, narrated on the authority of Jaafar Al-Sadiq. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: It is the sweetness of obedience. Sahl bin Abdullah Al-Tustari said: It is that the servant is stripped of his self-control and his control is returned to the Truth. It was said that it is independence from creation and need for the truth, and most of the commentators are of the opinion that this good life is in this world and not in the hereafter, because the life of the hereafter has been mentioned in His saying: And We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do. We have already presented the interpretation of reward according to the best, and the pronoun is singular in We will revive him and plural in We will surely reward them based on the word from and its meaning.
16:98: Then when He, the Almighty, mentioned the righteous deed and the reward for it, He followed it with mentioning the seeking of refuge by which righteous deeds are freed from satanic whispers, saying: 98- So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed. The fa is for the order of seeking refuge from the righteous deed. It was said that this verse is connected to His saying: And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things. The meaning is: So when you begin to recite it, seek refuge. Al-Zajjaj and other linguists said: Its meaning is: If you want to recite the Qur’an, seek refuge, and it does not mean seek refuge after you recite the Qur’an. Similar to it is: If you eat, say, In the name of God. Al-Wahidi said: This is the consensus of the jurists that seeking refuge before recitation is required, except for what was narrated from Abu Hurairah, Ibn Sirin, Dawud, Malik and Hamzah among the reciters, who said: Seeking refuge after recitation. They took the apparent meaning of the verse, and the meaning of seek refuge with God is: ask Him, the Exalted, to protect you from the accursed Satan, meaning from his whisperings. And the specification of the recitation of the Qur’an from among the righteous deeds by seeking refuge when intending it is to draw attention to the fact that it is more important for all righteous deeds when intending it, because if the command to do so occurs when reciting the Qur’an, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it, then it is more appropriate when intending something other than it, as it was said. And directing the address to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is to indicate that others are more deserving of doing seeking refuge than him, because if he commanded it to repel the whisperings of Satan despite his infallibility, then how about the rest of his nation? The majority of scholars have said that the command in the verse is for encouragement. It was narrated from Ata’ that it is obligatory, taking the apparent meaning of the command. The discussion of seeking refuge has been presented in full at the beginning of this commentary.
16:99: The pronoun in 99- He has no authority for the matter or for Satan: meaning he has no power over the temptation of those who believe and upon their Lord rely. Al-Wahidi narrated from all the commentators that they interpreted authority as an argument. They said: The meaning is that he has no argument over the believers in tempting them and calling them to misguidance, and the meaning of and upon their Lord rely is that they entrust their affairs to Him in every word and action, for belief in God and reliance on Him prevent Satan from whispering to them, and if he whispers to one of them, his whispering does not affect him, and this sentence is an explanation for the command to seek refuge, and these are the ones who combine faith and reliance are those about whom Satan said: Except for Your chosen servants among them and God said about them: Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them except those who follow you of the deviators.
16:100: Then, glory be to Him, He limited the authority of Satan, saying 100- His authority meaning his power to seduce is only over those who take him as a friend meaning they take him as a friend and obey him in his whispers and those who associate others with Him the pronoun in with Him refers to God Almighty: meaning those who associate others with God, and it was said that it refers to Satan, and the meaning is: and those who, because of him and because of his whispers, associate others with God.
16:101: 101- And when We substitute a verse for another verse This is the beginning of His, glory be to Him, narrating a semblance of disbelief and repelling it. The meaning of substitution is: removing something while putting something else in its place. Substituting a verse is removing it with another verse other than it, which is abrogating it with another verse. We have already discussed abrogation in Surat Al-Baqarah. They said, meaning the ignorant infidels of Quraysh, regarding the wisdom of abrogation, You, O Muhammad, are only a liar, a fabricator, attributing to God what He did not say, as you claim that He commanded you to do something, then you claim that He commanded you to do something else. So God Almighty responded to them with what indicates their ignorance, saying: Rather, most of them do not know, anything of knowledge at all, or they do not know the wisdom of abrogation, as it is based on the interests that God Almighty knows. There may be a temporary interest in the law of this thing at one time, then the interest after that time may be in the law of another. If the cover was lifted from these infidels, they would know that this is the correct path and the method of justice, kindness, and gentleness.
16:102: Then the Almighty explained to those who object to the wisdom of abrogation, claiming that it was not from God, and that His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, invented it, saying: 102- “Say: It was sent down” meaning the Qur’an indicated by the mention of the verse by the Holy Spirit meaning Gabriel, and Holiness means purification, and the meaning is: The Spirit purified from the impurities of humanity sent it down, so it is from adding the described to the attribute from your Lord meaning the beginning of its revelation from Him, the Almighty, and with truth is in the accusative case as a state: meaning clothed in being a proven truth for a profound wisdom to establish those who believe in faith, so they say: Both the abrogator and the abrogated are from our Lord, and also because if they knew what interests there are in abrogation, their feet would be established in faith and their beliefs would be firm. It was read li-yathibt from i-thibt “and guidance and good report for the Muslims” and they are conjoined with the place of li-yathibt: meaning, to establish them and guide and good report, and in it is an allusion to the occurrence of the opposites of these qualities for others.
16:103: Then the Almighty mentioned another of their doubts, saying: 103- And We certainly know that they say, 'It is only a human being who teaches him' The lam is the preamble: meaning, We certainly know that these infidels say that Muhammad is taught the Qur'an by a human being from the children of Adam, not an angel. The people of knowledge differed in identifying this human being about whom they claimed what they claimed. It was said that he was the slave of Al-Fakih bin Al-Mughira, and his name was Jabr. He was a Christian who converted to Islam. When the infidels of Quraysh heard report from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the early generations, despite his being illiterate, they would say, 'It is only Jabr who teaches him.' It was also said that his name was Ya'ish, a slave of Banu Al-Hadrami, and he used to read foreign books. It was also said that he was a slave of Banu Amir bin Lu'ay. It was also said that they were two slaves: one of them was named Yasar, and the other was named Jabr. They were Sicilians who made swords, and they used to read a book of theirs. It was also said that they used to read the Torah and the Gospel. It was said that they meant Salman the Persian, and it was said that they meant a Christian in Mecca named Balaam, who used to read the Torah. It was also said that they meant a Christian man named Abu Maysarah who spoke Roman, and in another narration his name was Addas. An-Nahhas said: These statements are not contradictory, because it is possible that they claimed that they all knew him, but it is not possible to reconcile them based on the statement of the one who said that he was Salman, because this verse is Meccan, and he only came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina. Then God Almighty responded to their statement by saying: The tongue of the one they incline towards is foreign. Inclination means deviation. It is said to have deviated from the right path. This was mentioned previously in Al-A’raf, and Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read Yalhadun with the opening of the ya and ha. And those other than them read with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the ha: meaning the language of the one they incline towards and claim that he teaches you is foreign. It is said: a foreign man and a foreign woman: meaning they do not speak clearly. Foreignness is concealment, and it is the opposite of clarity. The Arabs call everyone who does not know their language and does not speak it a foreigner. Al-Farra’ said: The foreigner is the one whose tongue is foreign, even if he is from the Arabs. The foreigner is the foreigner whose origin is from the Persians. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: The foreigner attributed to the Persians is the one who does not speak clearly, whether he is from the Arabs or from the Persians. Likewise the foreigner, and the foreigner attributed to the Persians, even if he is eloquent. And this is a clear Arabic tongue, referring to the Qur’an. He called it a tongue because the Arabs say for the poem and the verse a tongue, and from this is the saying of the poet: The tongue of evil brings it to us, and you betrayed us, and I did not expect you to betray us Or he meant by the tongue eloquence, so it is as if he said: This Qur’an has Arabic eloquence and clear expression, so how do you claim that a non-Arab human being knows it? And you are unable to oppose a surah of it, and you are the people of the Arabic tongue, the men of eloquence, and the leaders of rhetoric. And these two sentences are new sentences that were brought to refute their criticism and repel their lies.
16:104: And when He, the Almighty, mentioned their answer, He rebuked and threatened them, saying: 104- Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of God meaning do not believe in them, God will not guide them to the truth, which is the path to salvation, a guidance that leads to what is sought, because He knows of their misery, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment because of what they are upon of disbelief and denial of the signs of God.
16:105: Then when they attributed slander to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he responded to them by saying: 105- Only those who do not believe in the verses of God invent lies. So how can slander come from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who is the head of those who believe in them and call to believe in them, and these disbelievers are the ones who do not believe in them, so they are the ones who invent lies. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that only those who invent lies are those who, when they see the verses that no one has power over except God, deny them. These are the worst of liars. Then he called them the liars, and said: Those meaning those who are described by that are the liars meaning that lying is a necessary description of them and a habit of theirs, so they are the perfect liars, since there is no lie greater than their denial of the verses of God. Abdul Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the good life mentioned in the verse, so he said: The good life is lawful provision in this worldly life, and when he reaches his Lord, He will reward him according to the best of what he used to do. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Good earnings and righteous deeds. Al-Askari narrated in Al-Amthal on the authority of Ali regarding the verse that he said: Contentment. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Contentment. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to supplicate: O God, make me content with what You have provided me and bless me in it, and replace for me everything that is absent of mine with something better. Ahmad, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Ibn Amr that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: He has succeeded who has accepted Islam, received sufficient provision, and God has made him content with what He has given him. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa'i narrated from Fadalah ibn Ubayd that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: He has succeeded who is guided to Islam, and his livelihood is sufficient and he is content with it. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated in Al-Musannaf and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ata’ who said: Seeking refuge is obligatory for every recitation in prayer and otherwise because of the statement of God interpretation of the meaning: So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed. There is a report on the permissibility of seeking refuge when reciting that which we have perhaps mentioned before. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God interpretation of the meaning: His authority is only over those who take him as an ally, meaning that the authority of Satan is over those who take Satan as an ally and commit disobedience to God. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And when We substitute one verse for another and his statement: Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted, he said: Abdullah bin Saad bin Abi Sarh used to write for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then Satan made him slip and he joined the disbelievers. The Messenger of God ordered him to be killed on the day of the conquest, so Uthman sought protection for him from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he granted him protection. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And when We substitute one verse for another, he said: It is like his statement: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated - Al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught a blacksmith in Mecca named Balaam, and he was a foreigner. The polytheists would see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entering and leaving his presence, so they said: Balaam is the one teaching him. So God revealed, And We certainly know that they say the verse. Al-Hakim narrated, who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman narrated on his authority regarding the verse. He said: They said: Muhammad is only taught by Abd Ibn Al-Hadrami, and he is the owner of the books. So God revealed this verse. Adam Ibn Abi Iyas, Sa’id Ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Muslim Al-Hadrami, who said: We had two slaves from the people of Ain Al-Tamr, one of whom was called Yasar and the other Jabr. They used to make swords in Mecca, and they used to recite the Gospel. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would sometimes pass by them while they were reciting, so he would stop and listen. So the polytheists said: He is only learning from them. So this verse was revealed.
16:106: His statement: 106- Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief The scholars have differed in its parsing. The majority have said that it is a substitute, either for those who do not believe in the signs of God and what is between them is an objection, and the meaning is: Only those who disbelieve invent lies, and he excluded from them the one who was forced, so he did not fall under the ruling of fabrication. Then he said: But whoever opens his heart to disbelief meaning he believes it and his soul is content with it and is reassured by it upon them is wrath and either from the subject which is those or from the predicate which is the liars. Al-Zajjaj went with the first and Al-Akhfash said: Min is a subject and its predicate is omitted and it is sufficient for it to be the predicate of the second Min like your saying: Whoever comes to us from you, we will honor him. And it was said that it is: that is, Min in Min Kafr is accusative of blame. And it was said that Min is a conditional and the answer is omitted because the answer to Min Sharh indicates it, and it is like what Al-Akhfash said. He only disagreed with him in applying the word of condition to Min and the answer to its predicate, so it is as if it was said on this: Whoever disbelieves in God, upon them is wrath except for whoever is forced. But whoever opens his heart to disbelief, upon them is wrath. And it is correct to exclude the one who is forced from the disbeliever even though he is not a disbeliever because what appears from him after faith is what only appears from a disbeliever were it not for the compulsion. Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars agreed that if someone is forced to disbelieve until he fears that he will be killed, then there is no sin upon him if he disbelieves while his heart is at peace with faith, and his wife will not be separated from him, and he will not be judged as a disbeliever. It was narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan that if he showed disbelief, he was an apostate in appearance, but between him and God he was a Muslim, and his wife was separated from him, and he was not prayed over if he died, and he did not inherit from his father if he died a Muslim. This statement is rejected by its speaker, and is refuted by the Book and the Sunnah. Al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Awza’i, al-Shafi’i, and Sahnun held that this permission mentioned in this verse only came in speech, but as for action, there is no permission, such as if he is forced to prostrate to someone other than God, and the apparent meaning of the verse refutes this, as it is general for those who are forced without differentiating between speech and action. There is no evidence for those who limit the verse to speech, and the specific reason is not taken into account with the generality of the wording, as is established in the science of principles. The phrase “and his heart is at peace with faith” is in the accusative case as a state of the exception: that is, except for the one who disbelieved under compulsion, and the fact is that his heart is at peace with faith and his belief has not changed. There is no greater threat after this, which is the combination of God’s wrath and His great punishment for the apostates.
16:107: And the reference in His saying: 107- That is to disbelief after belief, or to the threat of wrath and punishment, and the ba in because they preferred the life of this world is for causality: that is, because of their preference for the life of this world over the Hereafter and because God does not guide the disbelieving people is conjoined with that they preferred, that is, because they preferred, and because God does not guide the disbelieving people to belief in Him.
16:108: Then He described them by saying: 108- Those meaning those described with the ugly descriptions mentioned are those over whose hearts, hearing and sight God has sealed so they did not understand the sermons nor did they hear them, nor did they see the signs that are used as evidence for the truth. The confirmation of sealing was previously mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. Then He established for them a quality of deficiency other than the previous quality and said: And those are the heedless of what is intended for them, and the separating pronoun indicates that they are extremely heedless, as there is no heedlessness greater than this heedlessness of theirs.
16:109: 109- Indeed, they are the losers in the Hereafter. That is, they are the ones who are completely in loss and have reached an end beyond which there is no end. The meaning of indeed, they are the losers has already been investigated in several places, including what is in this surah.
16:111: 111- On the Day every soul will come disputing for itself. Al-Zajjaj said: The Day it will come is in the accusative case by His saying, Merciful, or by the implication of remember, or remind them, or warn them. The addition of the pronoun of the soul to the self has been questioned, and there must be a difference between the noun and the noun it is added to. It was answered that what is meant by the first soul is the entire human body, and by the second soul is the self, so it is as if it were said, On the Day every human being will come disputing for himself, not caring about anything else, and the meaning of disputing for it is apologizing for it, so he is disputing and arguing for himself, not having time for anything else on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to migrate to Medina, he said to his companions: Disperse from me. Whoever has the strength to stay until the end of the night, and whoever does not have the strength to go, let him go at the beginning of the night. When you hear that I have settled down, then join me. So Bilal, the muezzin, Khabbab, Ammar, and a girl from Quraysh who had become Muslim, came in the morning. The polytheists and Abu Jahl seized them and suggested that Bilal disbelieve, but he refused. So they began to place an iron shield in the sun and then put it on her. When they put it on her, he said: One, one. As for Khabbab, they began to drag him through the thorns. As for Ammar, he said a word that pleased them out of caution. As for the girl, Abu Jahl pegged her with four pegs, then stretched her out and thrust a spear into her vagina until he killed her. Then they left Bilal, Khabbab, and Ammar and they joined the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what had happened to them. Ammar, who had been He spoke, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to him, How was he before you when you said what you said? Was he pleased with what you said or not? He said, No. So God revealed, Except for one who is forced thereto and whose heart is at rest with faith. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar on the authority of his father who said: The polytheists seized Ammar ibn Yasir and did not leave him alone until he insulted the Prophet (peace be upon him) and spoke well of their gods. So they left him alone. When he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him), he said, What is behind you? He said, The worst thing you have left behind is that I have spoken ill of you and spoken well of their gods. He said, How do you find your heart? He said, At rest with faith. He said, If they return, then return. So the verse was revealed, Except for one who is forced thereto and whose heart is at rest with faith. He said, “That is Ammar ibn Yasir. But he who opens his breast to disbelief.” Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: Except for one who is forced and whose heart is at rest with faith, he said: It was revealed about Ammar bin Yasir. There are narrations on this topic that clearly state that it was revealed about Ammar bin Yasir. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin who said: This verse, Except for one who is forced and whose heart is at rest with faith, was revealed about Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: In Surat An-Nahl Upon them is wrath from God, and for them is a great punishment, then it was abrogated and an exception was made and he said: Then indeed, your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted, the verse. He said: He is Abdullah bin Abi Sarh who used to write for the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), then Satan made him slip and he joined the disbelievers, so the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ordered him to be killed on the day of the conquest of Mecca, so Uthman bin Affan sought protection for him and the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) granted him protection. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan something similar. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: This verse, Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted, was revealed about those who used to issue fatwas from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: There were people from Mecca who had converted to Islam but were hiding their Islam, so the verse, Then your Lord is for those who emigrated, was revealed about them. They wrote to them about that, God has made a way out for you, so leave. The polytheists caught up with them and fought them. Some of them escaped and some of them were killed. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that Musaylima’s spies captured two men from the Muslims and brought them to him. He said to one of them, Do you bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God? He said, Yes. He said, Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God? He reached for his ears and said, I am deaf. He ordered that he be killed. He said to the other, Do you bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God? He said, Yes. He said, Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God? He said: Yes, so he sent him and he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to him: As for your companion, he continued with his faith, but as for you, you took advantage of the concession. And he is a messenger.
16:112: His saying: 112- "And God sets forth a parable of a village. We have already mentioned that set forth implies the meaning of made so that village would be the first object and like" would be the second object. "Village" was only delayed so that there would be no separation between them and their attributes. We have also mentioned that it is possible for "set forth to be in its proper form without being implied and like would be its first object village" instead of it. The commentators have differed as to whether what is meant by this village is a specific village, or what is meant is an unspecified village, rather every people whom God has bestowed blessings upon and the blessings have made them arrogant? Most have gone with the first and stated that it is Mecca, and that is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplicated against them and said: "O God, make Your punishment severe upon Mudar and make them years like the years of Joseph," so they were afflicted with famine until they ate bones. The second is more likely because the indefiniteness of the village indicates that, and Mecca is included in this general substitution as a primary inclusion, and also the threat is more eloquent, and the example is more complete, and other than Mecca is like it, and assuming that it is intended, then in the example there is a warning for others of a similar outcome, then the village is described as safe not afraid reassured not disturbed, meaning its people are not afraid nor disturbed its provision comes to it meaning what its people are provided with in abundance and wide from every place of the places where what is in it is brought to it so it disbelieved meaning its people disbelieved in the favors of God that He bestowed upon them, and the favor is the plural of favor like the most severe is the plural of severity, and it was said that it is the plural of favor like misery and misery, and this disbelief on their part is their disbelief in God, the Most High, and their denial of His messengers so God made it taste meaning He made its people taste the garment of hunger and fear This was called a garment because it shows on them emaciation, paleness of color, and bad condition, which is like a garment, so its name was borrowed for it And he inflicted upon him the taste, and its origin is the taste with the mouth, then it was borrowed for the absolute connection with its informing of the intensity of the injury because of what it contains of the meeting of two perceptions: the perception of touch and the taste. It was narrated that Ibn al-Rawandi the heretic said to Ibn al-A'rabi, the imam of language and literature: Is clothing tasted? Ibn al-A'rabi said to him: There is no problem, you monkey, suppose that Muhammad was not a prophet, was he not an Arab? It is as if he challenged the verse by saying that it is appropriate to say: So God clothed her with the clothing of hunger or So God made her taste the taste of hunger. Ibn al-A'rabi responded to him. The scholars of rhetoric responded that this is from the abstraction of the metaphor, and that is that he borrowed the clothing for what overcame a person from some incidents such as hunger and fear because it includes them as clothing includes the wearer, then he mentioned the description in accordance with what was borrowed for, which is hunger and fear, because the use of taste to perceive hunger and fear was in their view the truth, so they say so-and-so tasted misery and hardship and someone else made him taste it, so the metaphor was abstract, and if he had said So He clothed her, it would have been a candidate. It was said that the nomination of metaphor, although it is desirable from the aspect of exaggeration, has a preference for abstraction in that the aspect of what is borrowed is taken into account, so the speech becomes clearer. It was said that the origin of taste is in the mouth, then it may be borrowed and placed in the position of recognition and testing, and from that is the saying of the poet: Whoever tastes the world, I have tasted it, and its torment and its punishment will be brought to us. Hafs bin Ghayath, Nasr bin Asim, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Abu Amr, as narrated by Abdul Warith, read the word fear with the accusative case in apposition to clothing. The rest read it with the damma case in apposition to hunger. Al-Farra’ said: All the attributes were applied to the village except for his saying: they make, indicating that what is meant in reality are its people.
16:113: 113- And there had certainly come to them meaning the people of Mecca a Messenger from among themselves from their own kind whom they knew and whose lineage they knew. He commanded them to do what would benefit them and forbade them from what would harm them. But they denied him in what he brought. So the punishment seized them from God Almighty. The fact is that when the punishment seized them, they were wronging themselves by causing them eternal punishment and others by harming them and preventing them from the path of God. This statement is part of the complete example given. It was said that what is meant by the punishment here is the hunger that afflicted them, and it was said that it was killing on the day of Badr.
16:114: Then when God the Almighty preached to them with what He mentioned about the condition of the people of the mentioned village, He ordered them to eat from what God had provided them of spoils and the like, and He used the letter fa to indicate that this was caused by abandoning disbelief. The meaning is: since you believed and abandoned disbelief, then eat the lawful and good, which is the spoils, and abandon the impure, which is the dead animal and blood. And be grateful for the favor of God that He bestowed upon you and recognize its right if it is Him that you worship and do not worship anyone other than Him, or if your claim is correct, that you mean by the worship of the deities that you claimed to worship God the Almighty. It was said that the letter fa in eat was included in the command to be grateful, and it was only included in the command to eat because eating is a means to gratitude.
16:115: 115- He has only forbidden you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God. God Almighty repeated the mention of these prohibitions in Al-Baqarah, Al-Ma’idah, Al-An’am, and in this Surah to eliminate excuses and remove doubt. Then He mentioned the permission to eat some of what was mentioned, saying: But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limits] - then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. We have already discussed all that was mentioned here in full.
16:116: Then he falsified the method of the infidels in adding to these prohibitions such as the bahīrah and the sa’ib and in subtracting from them such as permitting the dead and blood, so he said: 116- And do not say about what your tongues describe falsely. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Zajjaj said: Ma here is a source and the lie is in the accusative without taqlū: that is, do not say a lie because of the description of your tongues, and its meaning is: do not forbid or permit because of a statement that your tongues utter without proof. It is permissible for ma to be a relative pronoun and the lie is in the accusative with taqṣif: that is, do not say about what your tongues describe falsely this is permissible and this is forbidden. So a word was deleted in it because it is known, so his saying this is permissible and this is forbidden is a substitute for the lie. It is permissible for there to be an omission in the speech by estimating the saying: that is, do not say about what your tongues describe, so you say this is permissible and this is forbidden, or saying “this is permissible and this is forbidden. It is also permissible for taqṣif to be in the accusative with taqṣif and for ma to be a source: that is, do not say this is permissible. This is forbidden because your tongues describe lies. Lies are read with a damma on the kaf, dhal and ba’ as an attribute of tongues. Al-Hasan reads with a fatha on the kaf and a kasra on the dhal and ba’ as an attribute of what. It is said as a substitute for what: meaning, do not say the lie that your tongues describe, this is permissible and this is forbidden. The lam in that you may invent lies against God is the lam of consequence, not the lam of presentation: meaning, your inventing lies against God is followed by permitting and forbidding and attributing that to Him without it being from Him. Indeed, those who invent lies against God meaning any invention will not succeed in any type of success, which is attaining what is desired.
16:117: And height 117- A little enjoyment as a predicate of a deleted subject. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, their enjoyment is a little enjoyment, or it is a subject whose predicate is deleted: that is, they have a little enjoyment. And for them is a painful punishment to which they will be returned in the Hereafter.
16:118: Then He specifically mentioned the prohibitions of the Jews, saying: 118- And We have forbidden to those who are Jews meaning We have forbidden to them specifically and not to others what We have related to you by saying: We have forbidden to them every animal with claws, and of the cattle and the sheep We have forbidden to them their fat the verse, and before is related to Our stories or to Our prohibition and We did not wrong them by that prohibition, rather We punished them for their transgression but they were wronging themselves since they did the reasons for that, so We forbade them those things as a punishment for them.
16:119: Then the Almighty made it clear that slandering God Almighty and disobeying His command does not prevent them from repenting and obtaining forgiveness, so He said: 119- Then your Lord is for those who did evil in ignorance meaning those who committed it in ignorance. The interpretation of this verse was presented in Surat An-Nisa’ Then they repented after that meaning after they committed evil. This is an emphasis, because then indicates the aftermath, so He emphasised it by adding the mention of the aftermath and amended their deeds in which there was corruption due to the evil they committed. Then He repeated this as emphasis and confirmation, so He said: Indeed, your Lord after that meaning after repentance is Forgiving and Merciful abundant in forgiveness and vast in mercy. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And God sets forth an example of a city, he said: It means Mecca. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Atiyyah regarding the verse something similar, and he added: Do you not see that he said: And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among themselves, but they denied him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: The city of which God said: It was safe and secure, is Yathrib. I said: I do not know what evidence indicated this specification, nor what indication was established for him to support it, and when did the abode of migration and the dwelling place of the Ansar deny the blessings of God, and at what time did God make it taste the garment of hunger and fear, and it is that which removes its impurity as the bellows remove the impurity of iron, as is authentically reported from the Truthful, the Trusted. It is also authentically reported from him that he said: And Medina is better for them if they only knew. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And do not say about what your tongues describe as falsehood the verse, he said: In Al-Buhayrah and Al-Sa’ibah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Nadrah who said: I read this verse in Surat al-Nahl 16:And do not say about what your tongues describe as falsehood “This is lawful and this is unlawful” to the end of the verse, and I have not ceased to fear issuing fatwas to this day. I said: He is truthful, may God have mercy on him, for this verse includes in its general wording a fatwa from someone who issues a fatwa contrary to what is in the Book of God or in the Sunnah of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, as often happens with those who give precedence to their opinion over narration, or those who are ignorant of the knowledge of the Book and Sunnah, such as the imitators. They truly deserve to be prevented from issuing their fatwas and to be prevented from their ignorance, for they issued fatwas without knowledge from God, nor guidance, nor an enlightening Book, so they went astray and led others astray. They and those who seek their fatwas are like the one who said: Like a blind beast led by a blind man on the crooked and unjust road Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: Perhaps a man will say that God has commanded such-and-such or forbidden such-and-such, and God the Almighty will say to him: You have lied. Or he will say: God has forbidden such-and-such or permitted such-and-such, and God will say to him: You have lied. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding His statement: And We have forbidden to those who are Jews what We have related to you, he said: In Surat Al-An’am. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada, and he said where He says: And to those who are Jews up to His statement: And indeed, We are truthful.
16:120: When God finished repelling the doubts of the polytheists and invalidating their accusations, and Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was one of the monotheists and he was a role model for many of the prophets, God mentioned him at the end of this Surah and said: 120- Indeed, Ibrahim was a nation. Ibn al-A’rabi said: A learned man is called a nation, and a nation is a man who gathers goodness. Al-Wahidi said: Most of the commentators said: meaning a teacher of goodness. Based on this, the meaning of Ibrahim being a nation is that he was a teacher of goodness or a gatherer of good qualities or knowledgeable about what God taught him of the laws. It was said that a nation means one who is followed: meaning that people follow him to take goodness from him, as God, the Most High, said: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people. And the obedient is the one who obeys, and the meanings of qunut have been explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. And the Hanif is the one who turns away from false religions to the religion of truth. His statement was presented in al-An’am 6:And he was not among those who associate others with God as the infidels of Quraysh claimed that he was of their false religion.
16:121: 121- Grateful for His blessings which God bestowed upon him, even if they were few, as indicated by the plural of fewness, he is grateful for the many of them, all the more so. He chose him that is, He selected him for prophethood and singled him out for it. And guided him to a straight path, which is the religion of Islam and the true religion.
16:122: 122- And We gave him good in this world meaning a good characteristic or a good state, and it was said that it is a righteous son, and it was said that it is good praise, and it was said that it is prophethood, and it was said that it is our prayers upon him in the testimony of faith, and it was said that it is that all people of religions take charge of him, and there is no objection to what God gave him being comprehensive of all of that and what is besides it of good characteristics and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous according to what he asked his Lord when he said: And join me with the righteous * And grant me a reputation of truth among later generations * And make me one of the inheritors of the Garden of Delight.
16:123: 123- Then We revealed to you O Muhammad, despite your high rank and lofty status and your being the master of the children of Adam, to follow the religion of Abraham. The origin of the religion is the name for what God legislated for His servants through the tongue of one of His prophets. It was said that what is meant here is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, following the religion of Abraham in monotheism and calling to it. Ibn Jarir said: In disavowing idols and adhering to the religion of Islam. It was said in the rituals of Hajj. It was said in the fundamentals but not the branches. It was said in all of his law except what was abrogated from it, and this is what appears. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to follow the example of the prophets, even though he was their master. God Almighty said: Then follow their guidance. The accusative of hanif is a state of Abraham, and it is permissible for the state to come from it, because the religion is like a part of it. It has been established in the science of grammar that the state of the complement is permissible if the complement requires the work of the complement or is a part of it or like a part. And he was not of the polytheists, which is a repetition of what came before for the reason we mentioned.
16:124: 124- The Sabbath was only made for those who differed about it. That is, the consequences of the Sabbath, which is the transformation, were only made for those who differed about it, or the obligation to honor the Sabbath and refrain from hunting on it was only made for those who differed about it, not for other nations. Scholars have differed on how the difference between them occurred regarding the Sabbath. One group said: Moses commanded them to celebrate Friday and designated it for them and informed them of its superiority over others, but they disagreed with him and said that the Sabbath was better. So God said to him: Leave them to what they chose for themselves. It was also said that God Almighty commanded them to glorify a day of the week, but their interpretations differed regarding it. The Jews designated the Sabbath because God Almighty completed creation on that day, and the Christians designated Sunday because God began creation on that day. So God obligated each of them to do what his interpretation led to, and He designated Friday for this nation without leaving them to their interpretations, as a favor and blessing from Him. The connection between this verse and the one before it is that the Jews claimed that the Sabbath was one of the laws of Abraham, so God Almighty informed us that He only made the Sabbath obligatory for those who differed about it and did not make it obligatory for Abraham or anyone else. And your Lord will judge between them meaning between those who differed about it on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they differed and He will reward each person according to what he deserves in reward and punishment, just as He Almighty did in transforming a group of them and saving another.
16:125: Then God Almighty commanded His Messenger to call his nation to Islam, so He said: 125- Call to the way of your Lord. The object was omitted for the sake of generalization, since he was sent to all people, and the way of God is Islam. Wisdom, meaning with the sound, correct statement. It was said that it is the definitive arguments that provide certainty. And good preaching, which is the statement that includes good preaching that the listener approves of and is in itself good in consideration of the listener’s benefit from it. It was said that they are the conjectural and convincing arguments that necessitate belief in acceptable premises. It was said that there are only two methods for calling to Islam, but the caller may need to use opposition and contradiction with the most stubborn opponent and so on from argumentation. For this reason, the Almighty said: And argue with them in a way that is best, meaning in the way that is the best way of argumentation. The Almighty only commanded good argumentation because the caller is right and his purpose is correct, and his opponent is wrong and his purpose is corrupt. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way. When the Almighty urged calling to Islam through the mentioned methods, He made clear that guidance and right direction do not belong to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but rather to Him, the Most High, so He said: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing, meaning He knows who goes astray and who is guided. And He is most knowing of those who are guided, meaning who sees the truth and seeks it without being obstinate. The call was only prescribed for you and commanded you to do so to cut off the excuse, complete the argument, and remove doubt. There is nothing else upon you.
16:126: Then since the call included the obligation of those called to return to the truth, and if they refused, they would be fought, the caller was ordered to be just in the punishment, so he said: 126- And if you punish meaning if you wanted to punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted meaning with the equivalent of what was done to you, do not go beyond that. Ibn Jarir said: This verse was revealed regarding the one who was wronged, that he should not take from his oppressor if he was able to do so except the equivalent of his wrong, not extending it to anything else, and this is correct, because even if it is said that the verse has a specific reason as will come, consideration is given to the generality of the wording, and its generality conveys this meaning that he mentioned, and the Almighty called the first action, which is the action of the one who started the evil, punishment, even though the punishment is nothing but the action of the second, which is metaphorical for similarity, and it is a well-known chapter that occurred in many of the Noble Book. Then the Almighty urged forgiveness, saying: But if you are patient, it is better for the patient. That is, if you are patient and do not receive the same punishment, then patience is better for you than taking revenge. He put the patient in the place of the pronoun, as praise from God for them that they are patient in the face of hardships. The majority of scholars have said that this verse is decisive because it was revealed about patience and not receiving punishment and praising the patient in general. It was said that it was abrogated by the verses on fighting, but there is no basis for that.
16:127: Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to be patient, saying: 127- And be patient over the various types of harm that have befallen you. And your patience is not but through God, meaning through His guidance and support. The exception is devoid of the most general of things: meaning your patience is not accompanied by anything except through His guidance for you, and in it is consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He forbade him from grieving, saying: And do not grieve over them, meaning over the disbelievers in their turning away from you, or do not grieve over the dead of Uhud, for they have passed away to the mercy of God. And do not be in distress over what they are plotting, the majority read it with the fatha on the letter Ḍād, and Ibn Kathir read it with the kasra. Ibn al-Sikkit said: They are the same, meaning the fatha and the kasra. Al-Farra’ said: “Al-Daiq with the fat-ha is what your chest is too narrow for, and Al-Daiq with the kasra is what is in something that is spacious, such as a house or a garment. Al-Akhfash said the same. It is from the inverted speech, because Al-Daiq is a description of a person that he is in and the person is not in it. It is as if he wanted to describe the narrowness as great until it became like something surrounding the person from all sides. The meaning of “from what they plot” is: from their plotting against you in the future.
16:128: Then he concluded this surah with a verse that includes all the commands and prohibitions, saying: 128- Indeed, God is with those who fear Him meaning those who fear sins of all kinds and those who are doers of good by performing acts of obedience and doing what they are commanded to do. It was said that the meaning is: God is with those who fear the increase in punishment, and those who are doers of good in the origin of vengeance, so the first is a reference to His statement: Then punish with the like of that with which you were punished and the second is a reference to His statement: But if you are patient, it is better for the patient. It was said that those who fear Him is a reference to the glorification of God’s command and those who are doers of good is a reference to compassion for the servants of God the Most High. Abdul Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he was asked about the nation: What is it? He said: The one who teaches people good. They said: What is the obedient? He said: The one who obeys God and His Messenger. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, he said: He was a Muslim and there was no one from his people who was obedient to Islam at his time except him, and for that reason God said, He was a nation obedient to God. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding the statement of God, He was a nation, he said: An imam in good, obedient, he said: Obedient. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no servant for whom a nation bears witness except that God accepts their testimony. A nation is a man and above him, for God says, Indeed, Abraham was a nation, and a nation is a man and above him. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Amr that he said: Gabriel led Abraham in the noon and afternoon prayers at Arafat, then he stood until the sun set, then he moved him on. Then he prayed the sunset and evening prayers together, then he prayed the dawn prayer with him, as quickly as any of you among the Muslims prays. Then he stood with him until it was as slow as any of the Muslims prays, then he moved him on. Then he threw the pebbles, then he slaughtered, then he shaved his head, then he went with him to the House and circumambulated it. Then God said to His Prophet: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: The Sabbath was only made obligatory for those who differed therein, he said: He meant Friday, so they took the Sabbath in its place. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi on the authority of Abu Malik and Saeed Ibn Jubayr regarding the verse, he said: Because of their considering it permissible, Moses saw a man carrying firewood on the Sabbath, so he struck his neck. And in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, but they were given the Scripture before us and we were given it after them. Then this is their day which was enjoined upon them, meaning Friday, and they differed about it, then God guided us to it, so the people follow us in it, the Jews tomorrow and the Christians the day after tomorrow.” Muslim and others narrated something similar on the authority of Hudhayfah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And argue with them in a way that is best, he said: Turn away from their harm to you. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and authenticated it, and Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa’id al-Musnad, and al-Nasa’i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah in al-Fawa’id, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il, and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, who said: “On the day of Uhud, sixty-four men from the Ansar were killed, and from the Muhajireen, six of them were Hamzah, so they mutilated them. The Ansar said: If we ever kill them like this, we will slay them. On the day of the conquest of Mecca, God Almighty revealed: ‘And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient. ’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We will be patient and not punish. They refrained from the people except for four.” Ibn Sa'd, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Abu Nu'aym in Al-Ma'rifah, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood over Hamzah where he was martyred, and he looked at a sight that he had never seen before that was more painful to his heart, and he looked at him as he was mutilated, and he said: May God have mercy on you, for you were, as I know, one who maintained family ties and did good deeds. Were it not for the grief that will follow after you, I would be happy to leave you until God gathers you from various souls. By God, I will mutilate seventy of them in your place. Then Gabriel came down while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was standing, reciting the last verses of Surat al-Nahl 16:And if you punish, the verse, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) atoned for his oath and refrained from what he wanted and was patient. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a similar chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And if you punish the verse, he said: This was when God ordered His Prophet to fight whoever fought him, then Surat al-Bara’ah was revealed and the sacred months were over, so this is abrogated. Abd al-Razzaq, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement: Indeed, God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good, he said: They feared what was forbidden to them and did good in what was made obligatory upon them.
17:1: It has one hundred and eleven verses, and it is Meccan. Except for three verses, the Almighty said: And they almost provoked you, which was revealed when the delegation of Thaqeef came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and when the Jews said: This is not the land of the prophets. His saying: “And say: My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance.” His saying: Indeed, your Lord encompasses the people. Muqatil added: Indeed, those who were given knowledge before him. An-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Bani Israel was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Ad-Durais and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: In Bani Israel, Al-Kahf and Maryam, they are among the first to be freed and they are from my generation. Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it narrated on the authority of An-Nasa’i, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite Bani Israel and Az-Zumar every night. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Abu Amr Ash-Shaibani, who said: Abdullah led us in the dawn prayer and recited the last two of them, Bani Israel. His saying: 1- Glory be to Him Who took His servant by night is the source of sabaha, it is said sabaha yusbiha tasbihan and subhanan, like kufr al-yameen takfirun and kufrana, and its meaning is to sanctify and disavow God from all deficiency. Sibawayh said: The agent in it is a verb not from its wording, and the meaning is to sanctify God, sanctifying, so Subhanahu came in place of Tanzihan, so on this it is like qad al-qarfusaa and ishtalam al-sama’, and it was said that it is a name for glorification like Uthman for a man, and its erection is by an implied verb whose manifestation is left out, its meaning is I glorify God Subhan, then it was placed in the position of the verb and filled its place, and we have presented in his saying: Glory be to You, we have no knowledge except what You have taught us a part of the speech related to Subhan. And the Isra’ is said to be the night journey, it is said sara and asra: like saqaa and asqa are two languages, and the poet combined them in his saying: Al-Nadir neighborhood and the housewife whispered to me, but she did not whisper It was said that it is the journey at the beginning of the night in particular, and if the Isra’ only takes place at night, then there is no alternative to explicitly mentioning the night after it for any benefit. It was said that by his saying at night he meant to shorten the duration of the Isra’ and that he was taken on a journey in some of the night from Mecca to Syria, a distance of forty nights. The reason for indicating at night to shorten the duration is the indefinite article in it indicating some, unlike if you said I traveled the night which indicates that the journey encompasses all of it. The author of Al-Kashshaf provided evidence for indicating some by the night by the reading of Abdullah and Hudhayfah from the night. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of I took my servant by night is My servant’s journey meaning Muhammad by night. Based on this, the meaning of I took my servant by night is travel and there is a benefit in restricting it to the night. He said by His servant and did not say His Prophet or His Messenger or Muhammad as an honor to him, may God bless him and grant him peace. The scholars said: If another name was more honorable than this, God, the Exalted, would have named him by it in this great position and lofty state. Do not call me except by O Abdha, for it is the most honorable of my names. Claiming names that were mentioned in their tribes, as if some of their names had become my names. From the Sacred Mosque. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: It means the mosque itself, and this is the apparent meaning of the Qur’an. Most of the commentators said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on a night journey from the house of Umm Hani’, so they carried the Sacred Mosque to Mecca, or the Haram, because each of them surrounds the Sacred Mosque, or because the entire Haram is a mosque. Then God, the Almighty, mentioned the goal to which His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on a night journey, saying: To the Farthest Mosque, which is Jerusalem. It was called Al-Aqsa because of the great distance between it and the Sacred Mosque, and there was no mosque behind it at that time. Then He described the Farthest Mosque by saying: Which We have blessed around it, with fruits, rivers, prophets, and righteous people. God, the Almighty, blessed the surroundings of the Farthest Mosque with the blessings of this world and the Hereafter. In We have blessed after His saying they were taken on a night journey, there is a shift from the third person to the first person. Then he mentioned the reason for which he was taken on the Night Journey, saying: That We might show him some of Our signs, meaning what God Almighty showed him on that night of wonders, including covering this long distance in part of the night. He, Almighty, is the All-Hearing of everything heard, including the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the All-Seeing of everything seen, including the essence of His Messenger and his actions. Scholars have differed as to whether the Isra’ was with his body, peace and blessings be upon him, along with his soul, or with his soul only. Most of the early and later scholars held the former view. A group of scholars held the latter view, including Aisha, Muawiyah, Al-Hasan, Ibn Ishaq, and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Al-Yaman. A group went into detail and said: The Isra’ was with his body while awake to the Holy House and to the heavens with his soul. They provided evidence for this detail with his saying to the Al-Aqsa Mosque, so he made it the goal of the Isra’ with his person, may God bless him and grant him peace. If the Isra’ from the Holy House to the heavens had occurred with his person, he would have mentioned it. What is indicated by the many authentic hadiths is what most of the predecessors and successors went to, that the Isra’ was with his body and soul while awake to the Holy House, then to the heavens. There is no need for interpretation and diverting this Qur’anic arrangement and similar words of the hadiths to what contradicts the truth, and there is no reason for that to merely exclude and judge purely by the minds that are unable to understand what is known that nothing is impossible for Him, glory be to Him. If that was just a vision, as is said by those who claim that the Isra’ was with the soul only, and that the vision of the prophets is true, the disbelievers would not have denied the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he informed them of that, until those who apostatized from those who did not open their hearts to faith apostatized, because a person may see In his sleep, there is what is unlikely, rather what is impossible, and no one denies that. As for the adherence of those who said that this Isra’ was only by spirit in the form of a vision, by his saying, And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, if we assume that what is meant by this vision is this Isra’, then the explicit statement here in his saying, Glory be to Him who took His servant by night, and the explicit statement in the many authentic hadiths that he was taken by night do not fall short of being used as evidence for interpreting this vision that occurs in the verse as seeing with the eye, because it may be said that seeing with the eye is a vision, and how can it be correct to interpret this Isra’ as a vision with his, may God bless him and grant him peace, explicit statement that when he was taken by night, he was between sleeping and awake. There is also disagreement about the date of the Isra'. It was narrated that it was one year before the migration to Madinah, and it was narrated that the Isra' was years before the migration. The reason for that is that Khadija prayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she died five years before the migration, and it was said three years, and it was said four years, and prayer was not made obligatory until the night of the Isra'. Ibn Abd al-Barr used this as evidence for that, and the narrations from al-Zuhri differed. Among those who said that the Isra' was one year before the migration was al-Zuhri in a narration from him, and likewise al-Harbi, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey on the twenty-seventh night of Rabi' al-Awwal, one year before the migration. Ibn al-Qasim said in his history: The Isra' was eighteen months after his mission. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: I do not know of anyone among the biographers who said something like this. It was narrated from al-Zuhri that he was taken on the Night Journey seven years before his mission, and it was narrated from him that he said: It was five years before his mission. Yunus narrated from Urwah from Aisha that she said: Khadija died before prayer was made obligatory.
