17:2: 2- And We gave Moses the Book meaning the Torah. It was said that the meaning is: We honored Muhammad with the Ascension and honored Moses with the Book. And We made it meaning that Book, and it was said Moses a guidance for the Children of Israel to be guided by it that you do not take. Abu Amr read with the lower ya', and the rest read with the upper ya': meaning so that they do not take. The meaning is: We gave him the Book to guide the Children of Israel so that they do not take a guardian besides Me Al-Farra' said: meaning a guarantor of their affairs. It was narrated from him that he said sufficient. It was said that its meaning is: meaning they rely on Him in their affairs. It was said a partner. The meaning of the guardian in the language is someone to whom matters are entrusted.
17:3: 3- The descendants of those We carried with Noah is in the accusative case for specification or calling. He mentioned His favor upon them as part of saving their fathers from drowning. It is possible that the first object of His statement that you should not take, i.e. do not take the descendants of those We carried with Noah as a guardian other than Me, is like His statement: And He does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. It was read in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject or in place of the subject of you take. Mujahid read it with the opening of the dhal. Zayd ibn Thabit read it with a kasra, and what is meant by offspring here is all those on earth because they are from the offspring of those who were on the ship. It was said that Moses and his people were from the Children of Israel, and this is what is appropriate for reading the accusative as a vocative, the accusative as a specification, the nominative as a substitute, and the predicate, as they all refer back to the Children of Israel mentioned. As for making the accusative on the basis that offspring is the first object of his saying, Do not take, then it is better to interpret offspring as all those on earth from the Children of Adam. Indeed, he was a grateful servant, meaning Noah. God described him with much gratitude and made him like the cause of what came before it, indicating that gratitude is one of the greatest causes of goodness, and one of the best acts of obedience, urging his offspring to thank God, the Most High. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on a night journey on the seventeenth night of Rabi` al-Awwal, one year before the migration. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Ad-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on a night journey to Jerusalem, one year before he left for Madinah. Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar on the authority of Urwah. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated on the authority of As-Suddi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on a night journey sixteen months before his migration. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi, regarding the words of God, whose surroundings We have blessed, he said: We caused trees to grow around it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, regarding the words of God, And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, he said: God made it a guidance that would lead them out of darkness into the light and made it a mercy for them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God, that you do not take besides Me a protector, he said: a partner. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: The descendants of those We carried with Noah. He said: It is a call, O descendants of those We carried with Noah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abdullah bin Zaid Al-Ansari who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The descendants of those We carried with Noah. Noah had only four sons: Ham, Shem, Japheth, and Cush. So those are four sons who descended from this creation.” And know that many commentators, such as Ibn Kathir, Al-Suyuti, and others, have gone to lengths in this regard by mentioning the hadiths reported about the Night Journey with their different wordings, but there is not much benefit in that, as they are well-known in their place in the books of hadith. Likewise, they have gone to lengths in mentioning the virtues of the Sacred Mosque and the Al-Aqsa Mosque, which is another topic. The purpose of the books of interpretation is what relates to the interpretation of the words of the Noble Book, mentioning the reasons for revelation, and explaining what can be taken from it of legal issues. Other than that, it is its virtue and there is no need for it.
17:4: His saying: 4- And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book meaning We informed and informed, or We ruled and completed. The origin of the word qada is to make something right and to finish it. It was also said that We revealed. This is indicated by His saying to the Children of Israel. If it had the meaning of informing and reporting, He would have said We decreed to the Children of Israel. If it had the meaning of We ruled, He would have said upon the Children of Israel. If it had the meaning of We completed, He would have said to the Children of Israel. What is meant by the Book is the Torah, and sending it down to their Prophet Moses is like sending it down to them because they were his people. It was also said that what is meant by the Book is the Preserved Tablet. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Saeed bin Jubair read in the Books. Isa Al-Thaqafi read You will surely cause corruption on earth with the opening of the second letter. The meaning of this reading is close to the meaning of the reading of the majority, because if they cause corruption, they will cause corruption in their souls. What is meant by corruption is disobeying what God has prescribed for them in the Torah. What is meant by the land is the land of Ash-Sham and Jerusalem. It was also said that the land of Egypt. The lam in will surely cause corruption is the answer to an omitted oath. Al-Naysaburi said: Or he made the final judgment the course of an oath, as if it was said: And We swore that you will surely corrupt. And the accusative of twice is because it is a description of a deleted source, or because it is in itself a source in which something of a different kind was done. The first time was the killing of Isaiah or the imprisonment of Jeremiah or the violation of the rulings of the Torah, and the second was the killing of John the Baptist and the intention to kill Jesus. And that you will declare great haughtiness. This lam is like the lam that preceded it: that is, that you will be arrogant about obeying God and that you will declare injustice and oppression over the people, exceeding the limit in that.
17:5: 5- So when the first of the two times came to pass meaning the first of the two times mentioned We sent against you servants of Ours who were possessed of great might meaning strength in wars and violence in the encounter. It was said that it was Bukhtanasr and his soldiers, and it was said Goliath, and it was said that it was a Persian army, and it was said that it was a Babylonian army They roamed through the houses meaning they caused havoc and went back and forth, it is said that they roamed, hassaw, and trampled with the same meaning, mentioned by Ibn Ghurair and Al-Qutaybi. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is they roamed through the houses, is there anyone left whom they did not kill? He said: And roaming is seeking something thoroughly. Al-Jawhari said: Roaming is the source of your saying they roamed through the houses: meaning they went through them as a man roams for report: meaning he seeks it, and Abu Ubaidah said the same. And Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of roaming is they roamed through the houses seeking them and killing them going and coming. Al-Farra' said: Its meaning is they killed them between their houses, and he recited for Hassan: And among us is he who met the enemies with the sword of Muhammad, and with it he trampled the armies. Qatrib said: It means they descended, and he recited the poet’s words: We invaded their homes by force and bound their masters. Ibn Abbas read Fahasaw with a silent Ha. Abu Zaid said: Al-Haws, Al-Jaws, Al-Aws, and Al-Haws mean roaming at night. It was said that roaming at night is Al-Jawsan with a fat-ha. This is what Abu Ubaidah said. It was read as Khalal Al-Diyar and its meaning is the same as Khalal, which is the middle of the houses. And it was that wa’dan maf’ul means it will inevitably happen.
17:6: 6- Then We gave you back the upper hand over them meaning the state, victory and return, and that was when they repented. It was said that was when David killed Goliath, and it was said that was when he killed Nebuchadnezzar. And We reinforced you with wealth and children after plundering your wealth and taking your children captive until your situation returned to what it was. And We made you more numerous. Abu Ubaidah said: The number of men is the number of men, so the meaning is: more men than your enemy. The one who goes out with a man from his tribe is called nafir and nafir like qadir and qadir, and it is possible that nafir is the plural of nafir.
17:7: 7- If you do good: meaning your actions and words are in the manner required of you you have done good for yourselves because the reward for that will return to you and if you do evil your actions and words and you do them not in the manner required of you then it is for her meaning upon her. And similar to it is the saying of the poet: Proudly slain by the hands and mouth That is, on the hands and on the mouth. Ibn Jarir said: The lam means to: that is, to it the offense is returned, as in the saying of God the Almighty: Because your Lord has revealed to her meaning to her. It was also said that the meaning is: for her is the reward or punishment. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: for her is a Lord who forgives offenses. It was said that this address is to the Children of Israel who remained, as mentioned in these verses, and it was said to the Children of Israel who were in the time of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its meaning is: informing them of what happened to their predecessors, so they should await the same. It was also said that it is an address to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:So when the promise of the Hereafter comes meaning the time of the punishment they were promised the last time comes, and the last time is their killing of John, son of Zechariah, as mentioned previously, and the story of his killing is fully explained in the Gospel, and his name is John. He was killed by one of their kings because of a woman who urged him to kill him, and the name of the king was Lakht, as Ibn Qutaybah said. Ibn Jarir said: Herod, and the answer to if is omitted, its meaning is that we sent them because the answer to the first if indicates it, to make your faces ugly is related to this omitted answer: that is, to do to you what makes your faces ugly until the signs of harm appear on you and gloom is evident on your faces. It was said that what is meant by faces are the noble ones among them. Al-Kisa’i read lansu’u with a noon on the basis that the pronoun refers to God Almighty. Abi read lansu’un with a nun of emphasis. Abu Bakr, Al-A’mash, Ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Ibn ‘Amir read lisu’u with a tanween and singular. Al-Zajjaj said: Everything you break and crumble, you have acquitted it, and the pronoun refers to God or the promise. And let them enter the mosque is conjoined with let them make them ugly “as they entered it the first time and let them destroy” meaning they destroy and annihilate. Qutrub said: they demolish, and from this is the saying of the poet: People are only two workers: one worker builds what he builds and the other raises it. The rest read it with a damma on the hamza and a damma on the waw after it, on the basis that the subject is servants of ours “what they conquered” meaning what they overcame of your lands or the duration of their supremacy destruction meaning destruction. The source was mentioned to remove doubt and confirm the report.
17:8: 8- Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you O Children of Israel after taking revenge on you the second time and if you return the third time We will return to your punishment. The biographers said: Then they returned to what was not appropriate, which is denying Muhammad, peace be upon him, and concealing what was mentioned about his mission in the Torah and the Gospel, so God returned to punishing them at the hands of the Arabs, and what happened to Banu Qurayzah, Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa and Khaybar was done to them, killing, captivity, and deportation, and the imposition of the jizya on those who remained of them, and the imposition of humiliation and poverty And We have made Hell, for the disbelievers, a prison which is a confinement, so it is a fa'il with the meaning of fa'il or maf'il. The meaning is: They are confined in Hell and will never be released from it. Al-Jawhari said: He confined him, he confined him, he confined him, and it was said a bed and a cradle, and in this he meant by the mat that people spread out.
17:9: 9- Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright means that the Qur'an guides people to the path that is most upright than other paths, which is the religion of Islam. That which is most upright is an attribute of an omitted description, which is the path. Al-Zajjaj said: for the state that is most upright of states, which is the monotheism of God and belief in His Messengers. Al-Farra' said the same. And gives good tidings to the believers. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read yabshir with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the sheen. The rest read it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the sheen from at-tabsheer: meaning that it gives good tidings of what it includes of the promise of good in the hereafter and now for the believers who do righteous deeds which the Qur'an guides us to do that they will have a great reward meaning that they will have.
17:10: 10- And that those who do not believe in the Hereafter and its rulings explained in the Qur'an, We have prepared for them a painful punishment which is the punishment of the Fire. This sentence is connected to the sentence He gives glad tidings with the estimation of He informs: that is, and he informs that those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and it was said that it is connected to His statement that they will have a great reward and what is meant by the glad tidings is the absolute information, or what is meant by it is its real meaning, and the speech includes giving the believers glad tidings with two glad tidings: the first is what they will have of reward, and the second is what their enemies will have of punishment.
17:12: When He, the Almighty, mentioned the proofs of prophethood and monotheism, He confirmed them with another proof from the wonders of His creation and the wonders of His creation, saying: 12- And We have made the night and the day two signs. This is because of what they contain of darkness and light, along with their alternation and all the wonders they contain that are beyond human understanding to describe. The meaning of them being two signs is that they indicate the existence of the Creator and His power. He mentioned the night before the day because it is the origin. So We erased the sign of the night, meaning We obliterated its light. The moon was like the sun in illumination and light. It was said that one of the effects of obliteration is the blackness that is seen in the moon. It was also said that what is meant by its obliteration is that He, the Almighty, created it with its light erased and obliterated, and it is not that He erased it after it was not like that. And We made the sign of the day seeing, meaning He, the Almighty, made His sun shining so that things can be seen in it. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ and al-Kisa’i said: It is from the Arabs’ saying: Absara al-Nahar meaning he became in a state in which he could see. It was also said that it is mubbara al-nahar for people, from his saying absarahu fa’asaru. The first is a description of it according to the condition of its people, and the second is a description of it according to its condition itself. Adding a sign to the night and the day is explanatory: that is, We erased the sign, which is the night, and the sign, which is the day, like their saying the same thing and its essence, that you may seek bounty from your Lord, that is, so that you may access the whiteness of the day to manage aspects of livelihood. The lam is related to His saying, And We made the sign of the day visible, that is, We made it so that you may seek bounty from your Lord, that is, provision, since most of the acquisition of provisions and the fulfillment of needs occurs during the day. Here, rest at night is not mentioned, being satisfied with what He said elsewhere, It is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day as a seeing sign, then He mentioned another benefit in that making, saying, and that you may know the number of years and the account. This is related to both actions: I mean, We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible, not to one of them alone, like the first, since knowledge of the number of years and the account does not come about except by the difference between the two signs and knowledge of the days, months, and years. The difference between number and calculation is that number is the enumeration of something that has a quantity by repeating its likes without obtaining anything from it, and calculation is the enumeration of something that has a quantity by repeating its likes in terms of obtaining a specific group of them a specific limit of it that has a special name. So the year, for example, if it is looked at in terms of the number of its days, then that is the number. And if it is looked at in terms of its realization and its being obtained from several months, each month may be obtained from several days, each day may be obtained from several hours, each hour may be obtained from several minutes, then that is the calculation. And everything We have explained in detail, meaning everything that you need in the matter of your religion and your world, We have explained it in a clear explanation that is not ambiguous, and at that time the causes are removed and the excuses are eliminated.
17:13: So that he who is to perish will perish with clear evidence. That is why He said: 13- And every man's bird We have fastened to his neck. Abu Ubaidah said: The bird among the Arabs is luck, and it is called bakht. The bird is whatever happened to a person in eternity, as it is his portion of intellect, deeds, lifespan, provision, happiness, and misery, as if a bird flies to him from the nest of eternity and the darkness of the unseen world, a flight without end or destination, to that person at his allotted time, without salvation or escape. Al-Azhari said: The origin of this is that when God, the Exalted, created Adam, He knew who among his descendants would be obedient and who would be disobedient, so He wrote down what He knew of them all, and He decreed happiness for whomever He knew to be obedient and misery for whomever He knew to be disobedient, so each one of them would have what he would become when he was created and brought into existence. That is His statement: And every man We have fastened to his neck his bird, meaning whatever flew for him is in God's knowledge. On his neck is an expression for attachment, like the attachment of a necklace to the neck among what is worn. Al-Zajjaj said: The mention of the neck is an expression of adherence, just as a necklace adheres to the neck. And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread out. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Muhaisin, Abu Ja’far, and Ya’qub read it with a fatha on the second letter and a damma on the ra’, meaning and the bird will come forth for him. Kitab is in the accusative case as a state, and it is possible that the meaning is: the bird will come forth for her and it will become a book. Yahya ibn Waththab read it with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the ra’, meaning God will bring forth. Shaibah and Muhammad ibn al-Samife’ read it. It was also narrated from Abu Ja’far, it with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the ra’, in the passive form, meaning: the bird will bring forth for him a book. The rest read it with a nun, meaning that the bring forth is God Almighty, and Kitab is the direct object. Abu Amr supported this reading with the statement of God Almighty, We have made it binding upon him. Abu Ja’far, Al-Hasan, and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a damma on the ya’, a fatha on the lam, and a shaddah on the qaf. The rest read it with a fat-ha on the ya’, a sukoon on the lam, and a soft qaf. God Almighty said, He will find it spread out to hasten the good report and to rebuke the bad.
17:14: 14- Read your book meaning we say to him read your book, or saying to him, it was said that whoever is a reader will read that book, and whoever is not a reader Sufficient for yourself today as a reckoner against you the ba in yourself is redundant and haseeb is a distinguishing feature: meaning a reckoner. Sibawayh said: darīb al-qaddāh means its striker, and sareem means sharp, and it is possible for haseeb to mean sufficient, then it was put in place of witness so it was transitive with ala, and nafs means person, and it is possible for haseeb to mean accountable like partner and jalīs.
17:15: 15- Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself. God, the Almighty, made clear that the reward for a righteous deed and the punishment for its opposite are specific to the doer and do not extend from him to others. Whoever is guided by doing what God has commanded him to do and leaving what God has forbidden him to do, then the benefit of that returns to himself. And whoever goes astray from the path of truth and does not do what he has commanded or leave what he has forbidden, then he only goes astray to his own detriment. That is, the consequences of his misguidance fall upon himself and do not extend beyond him. Everyone is held accountable for himself, rewarded for his obedience and punished for his disobedience. Then He emphasized this statement with the most eloquent emphasis, saying: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. And burden is sin. It is said, wazara yuzra he bears a burden and wazra a sin. The plural is awzaar burdens, and wazr is a weight. And from it, They will bear their burdens on their backs, meaning the weight of their sins. The meaning of the verse is: No soul carrying a burden will bear the burden of another soul until the other is freed from its burden and the first is held accountable for it. Something similar to this has been mentioned in Al-An'am. Al-Zajjaj said in his interpretation of this verse: The sinner and the guilty will not be held accountable for the sin of another. And We never punish until We have sent a messenger. When God, the Almighty, mentioned that the one who is guided is singled out for His guidance and the one who goes astray is singled out for his misguidance, and that a person will not be held accountable for the crime of another, He mentioned that He does not punish His servants except after giving them an excuse by sending His messengers and revealing His books. So God, the Almighty, made clear that He did not leave them in vain, and He does not hold them accountable before establishing proof against them. It appears that He will not punish them, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter, except after giving them an excuse by sending messengers, and this is what a group of scholars said. The majority of scholars said that what is negated here is the punishment of this world, not the punishment of the Hereafter.
17:16: 16- And when We desire to destroy a city, We command The commentators differed in the meaning of Our command into two opinions: The first is that what is meant by it is the command that is the opposite of the prohibition, and based on this they differed in what is commanded, and most of them say that it is obedience and goodness. He said in Al-Kashaf: Its meaning is We commanded them to be immoral, so they were immoral. He spoke at length in explaining this, and those who are able to interpret it followed him, and what he mentioned from those who followed him is opposed by something like the saying of the speaker, I commanded him, so he disobeyed me, because everyone who knows the Arabic language understands from this that what is commanded is something other than disobedience, because disobedience contradicts and contradicts the command. Likewise, I commanded him, so he was immoral, which indicates that what is commanded is something other than immorality, because immorality is an expression for doing the opposite of what is commanded, so its being immoral contradicts and contradicts its being commanded. The second opinion is that the meaning of We commanded its affluent ones is We made them many, so they were immoral. Al-Wahidi said: The Arabs say the people commanded if they became many, and God commanded them if He made them many. Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, Abu Raja, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi’, Mujahid and Al-Hasan read amrana with a shaddah on the mim: meaning we made them powerful leaders. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Haywah Al-Shami, Ya’qub and Kharijah from Nafi’, Hammad bin Salamah from Ibn Kathir, Ali and Ibn Abbas also read amrana with a long and short vowel: meaning we increased its tyrants and leaders. Al-Kisa’i said. Abu Ubaidah said: Amartuhu with a long vowel and amrtuhu are two languages meaning I increased it. From this is the hadith: The best of wealth is a mare with a mammura, meaning one with many offspring and children. Ibn ‘Aziz also said this. Al-Hasan and Yahya bin Ya’mar also read amrana with a short vowel and a kasrah on the mim meaning we did. This reading was narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas. Qatadah and Al-Hasan said: The meaning is we increased it. Abu Zaid and Abu Ubaid narrated something similar, but Al-Kisa’i rejected it and said: It is not said of abundance except “amrana with a long vowel.” It is stated in As-Sahah: Abu Al-Hasan said amr malahu with a kasrah: meaning it increased, and amr al-qawm means they increased. From this is the saying of Labid: If they are envied, they will be brought down, and if they are commanded one day, it will be for destruction and ruin. The majority read our command from the command, and its meaning is what we presented in the first statement, and the meaning of its affluent ones is the pampered ones who have been spoiled by the blessing and the spaciousness of life, and the commentators say in the interpretation of the pampered ones: they are the tyrants, the oppressors and the unjust kings. He said: And they were specifically mentioned because those other than them are their followers, and the meaning of fasqa in it: they went out of obedience and rebelled in their disbelief because immorality is going out to what is more heinous. So the word came true upon it meaning it was established and the punishment was realized upon them after their immorality became apparent. So we destroyed it with a great destruction meaning a great destruction whose nature cannot be known due to its severity and the greatness of its impact. It has been said in the interpretation of our command that it is a metaphor for the command that led them to immorality, which is the bestowal of blessings upon them, and it has also been said that what is meant by we wanted to destroy a village is that the destruction of a village is close, and it is a deviation from the apparent meaning without resorting to it.
17:17: Then He, the Almighty, mentioned that this is His custom with past generations, so He said: 17- And how many generations have We destroyed meaning, many times have We destroyed from them, so how many is the object of the verb destroyed, and from generations is an explanation of how many and a distinction for it: meaning, how many people disbelieved after Noah, such as Aad and Thamud, so destruction befell them and the scourge of punishment descended upon them, and in it is a frightening for the disbelievers of Mecca. Then He addressed His Messenger with what is a deterrent to all people, so He said: And sufficient is your Lord, concerning the sins of His servants, as Knowing and Seeing Al-Farra' said: It is only permissible to insert the preposition ba in the subject if it is praising or blaming its owner, like you saying Kafaka, Akram bihi He honored a man with it, and Tabat bita'ik He made your food taste good, and you do not say Qama bi-khik when you mean Qama'ik brother He stood up. This verse contains great good report for the obedient and a severe warning for those who do not disobey, because complete knowledge, perfect experience, and penetrating insight require that the reward be delivered to the one who deserves it according to his deservingness, and this does not contradict further favoring those who are worthy of that. What is meant by His being All-Knowing and All-Seeing is that He encompasses the realities of things, both outwardly and inwardly, and nothing of them is hidden from Him. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dalā’il al-Nubuwwah and Ibn ‘Asakir narrated on the authority of Sa’id al-Maqburi that ‘Abdullah ibn Salam asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the blackness in the moon. He said: They were two suns. God said: And We have made the night and the day two signs, and We have erased the sign of the night. The blackness that you saw is the erasure. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a longer meaning than this. Al-Suyuti said: Its chain of transmission is weak. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Anbari narrated in al-Masahif on the authority of ‘Ali regarding his statement: And We have erased the sign of the night, he said: It is the blackness in the moon. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: And We have made the sign of the day visible, he said: Illuminating, that you may seek bounty from your Lord, he said: He made for you a long path. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas regarding his statement: We have explained it, he said: We have made it clear. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Jabir that he heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: The bird of every man is around his neck. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: We have fastened his bird to his neck, he said: His happiness and misery, and whatever God has decreed for him and upon him, he will be bound to it wherever he is. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Anas regarding his statement: His bird, he said: His book. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: His deeds. And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread out, he said: It is his deeds that were counted against him, so what was written for him of deeds will be brought forth for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will read it spread out. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: Read your book, he said: On that day, he who was not a reader in this world will read. Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated in al-Tamhid on the authority of Aisha regarding his statement: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, he said: I asked Khadija about the children of the polytheists and he said: They are from their fathers. Then I asked him after that and he said: God knows best what they used to do. Then I asked him after Islam had become firmly established and And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another was revealed and he said: They are upon the fitrah or he said: In Paradise. Al-Suyuti said: Its chain of transmission is weak. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others that “the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked and it was said to him: O Messenger of God, do we share in the nights from the offspring of the polytheists? He said: They are from them.” There are many hadiths and a long discussion on that. Ibn Kathir mentioned in his interpretation of this verse most of the hadiths reported about the children of the polytheists, then he quoted the words of the scholars on the issue, so let him refer to it. Ishaq bin Rahawayh, Ahmad, Ibn Hibban, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Ma`rifah, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Kitab Al-`I`tiqad narrated on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Sari` that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Four people will argue on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:a deaf man who does not hear anything, an insane man, an old man, and a man who died during the Fatrah interval between two periods of time. Then he said: God will take their covenants to obey Him and will send to them a messenger saying: Enter the Fire. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if they were to enter it, it would be cool and peaceful for them, and whoever does not enter it will be dragged to it.” Its chain of transmission is with Ahmad. This is how `Ali bin `Abdullah narrated to us: Mu`adh bin Hisham narrated to us: My father narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf bin Qais, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Sari`. Ishaq bin Rahawayh, Ahmad, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and it is with Ahmad with the aforementioned chain of transmission on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Rafi`, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Qasim bin Asbagh, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la and Ibn Abd Al-Barr in Al-Tamhid narrated on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, and he mentioned something similar, and he replaced the fool with the imbecile. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawader Al-Usul, and Al-Tabarani and Abu Nu’aym narrated on the authority of Mu’adh bin Jabal on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: On the Day of Resurrection, those who were permitted in reason, those who perished during the interregnum, and those who perished as children will be brought, and he mentioned its meaning at length. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayh on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, We commanded its affluent ones, he said: To obey God, but they disobeyed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say regarding the verse, We commanded its affluent ones, with truth, but they disobeyed Him, so destruction was due to them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on his authority regarding the verse, saying: We gave power to our wicked ones, so they rebelled. When they did that, We destroyed them with punishment. It is like His statement: And thus have We appointed in every city the greatest of its criminals to plot therein. Al-Bukhari and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: We used to say to a tribe when they became numerous in the pre-Islamic period, The sons of so-and-so have commanded.
17:18: His saying: 18- Whoever desires the immediate This is a confirmation of what came before regarding the group of every human being whom we have obligated, and regarding the group of those who are guided, and what is meant by the immediate is the immediate benefit or the immediate home. Meaning: Whoever wants that through righteous deeds or deeds of the Hereafter, which includes the infidels, the wicked, the hypocrites, and the hypocrites, We hasten for him meaning We hasten for that desirer in it meaning in that immediate life. Then He restricted the hastener with two restrictions: The first: His saying: what We will meaning whatever God the Almighty wills to hasten for him from it, not what that desirer wills. For this reason you see many of those who desire the immediate life want in this world what they cannot attain and wish for what they cannot attain. The second restriction is His saying: for whomever We will meaning for whomever We will hasten from them what Our will requires. The phrase for whomever We will is a substitute for the pronoun in for him by repeating the preposition instead of some of the whole, because the pronoun refers to whom and it is for generality. This verse restricts the extended verses such as His saying, the Almighty: Whoever desires the cultivation of this world, We give him thereof and His saying: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived. It has been said that whatever He wills was read with a ya’. The substratum, and we do not know who among the people of the anomalies read it that way, and according to this reading it was said that the pronoun refers to God Almighty: that is, whatever God wills, so its meaning is the meaning of the reading with the letter nun, and in it there is a distance because it contradicts what came before it: which is We hastened and what comes after it is for whomever We will, and it was said that the pronoun refers to whomever in His statement: whoever wanted, so that would be restricted by His statement for whomever We will: that is, We hastened for him what he wanted, but according to Our will, so whoever wanted the immediate will not get what he wanted unless God willed that for him. Then after all of this, behind these empty requests that have no effect except with the two mentioned restrictions is the eternal torment of the Hereafter, and for this reason He said: Then We made for him Hell, that is, We made for him because of his abandonment of what he was commanded to do of the Hereafter and his sincerity from impurities the torment of Hell in its various types, He will burn in it in the accusative case as a state: that is, he will enter it condemned and rejected, that is, expelled from the mercy of God and distanced from it, so this is his punishment in the Hereafter even though he will not get from this world except what God Almighty has decreed. For him, so where is the state of this wretched person compared to the state of the pious believer? He gets from this world what God has decreed for him and wanted for him without panic or worry, with his soul at peace, his heart at peace, and his trust in his Lord. He is, however, working for the Hereafter, awaiting the reward from God Almighty, which is Paradise.
17:19: That is why He said: 19- And whoever desires the Hereafter meaning, he desires the Hereafter with his actions and strives for it with the necessary effort meaning, the true effort for it that befits its seeker, which is to do what he is commanded to do and to leave what he is forbidden to do, purely for God, without any taint. And doing it according to the Islamic law without innovation or whims and he is a believer in God with a true faith, because the doer of a righteous deed does not deserve a reward for it unless he is a believer God only accepts from the righteous and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state, and the reference in His saying: Then those is to those who desire the Hereafter and strive for it with their necessary effort and its predicate their effort is ever appreciated with God: meaning, accepted and not rejected, and it was said that it is added to many times over, for God Almighty considered three matters in the effort being appreciated: The first is the desire for the Hereafter. The second is that he strives for it with the effort that is right for it. The third is that he is a believer.
17:20: Then He, the Almighty, explained the perfection of His compassion and the comprehensiveness of His mercy, saying: 20- To both We provide for these and those from the gift of your Lord. The tanween in both is a substitute for the complement, and the meaning is that each one of the two groups We provide: that is, We increase him from Our gift in succession without interruption. We provide for the believers and the unbelievers, the people of obedience and the people of disobedience. The disobedience of the disobedient does not affect the cutting off of his provision. What is provided for is what He hastened for those who want this world, and what He bestowed in the first and the last upon those who want the Hereafter. In His saying: from the gift of your Lord is an indication that this is purely by grace and it is related to to provide. "And the gift of your Lord is not forbidden," that is, prohibited. It is said that he prohibited it, he prohibited it: he forbade it, and everything that stands between you and something He has prohibited it from you. "From these is a substitute for both and these" is conjoined with the substitute. Al-Zajjaj said: God, the Almighty, knew that He would give to the Muslim and the unbeliever and that He would provide for them both, the two groups, so He said: These and those are from the bounty of your Lord.
17:21: 21- See how We have favored some of them over others The address is to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is possible that it is for anyone who has the capacity to look and consider, and this sentence confirms and explains what was mentioned above from the supply, and the meaning is: See how We have favored some servants over others in immediate gifts, so some are rich and some are poor, strong and some are weak, healthy and some are sick, some are wise and some are foolish, and this is for a profound wisdom that minds are unable to comprehend. And the Hereafter has greater degrees and greater preference This is because the ratio of the differentiation in the degrees of the Hereafter to the differentiation in the degrees of this world is like the ratio of the Hereafter to this world, and this world has no value in relation to the Hereafter, so the Hereafter has greater degrees and greater preference. It was said that what is meant is that the believers will enter Paradise and the disbelievers will enter Hell, so the superiority of the believers over the disbelievers will be apparent. The gist of the meaning is that the differentiation in the Hereafter and its degrees is above the differentiation in this world and the ranks of its people in it of expansion and contraction and the like.
17:22: Then when He, the Almighty, summarized the righteous deeds in His saying: And strive for it with the effort it deserves while he is a believer, He began to detail that, beginning with the most honorable of them, which is monotheism, so He said: 22- Do not make with God another god. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is his nation, as an agitation and incitement, or to every qualified person who is fit to direct him to it. It was said that it is on the implication of the statement, and the estimation is: Tell you, who is charged, do not make, and the accusative of sit is in response to the prohibition, and the estimation is: Do not make, then sit, and the meaning of sit is to become, from their saying: He sharpened the blade until it sat as if it were ruined, and what is meant is not the reality of sitting opposite to standing. It was said that it is a metaphor for the inability to obtain good deeds, for striving for it can only be achieved by standing, and the inability to do so requires him to be sitting from seeking, and it was said that it is the nature of the blameworthy and let down to sit regretting and atoning for what he has neglected, so sitting on this is the reality, and the accusative of blameworthy Disappointed is a noun phrase that is used to describe someone who is in a state of affairs, or a state of affairs: meaning that you become one who combines two matters: blame from God, His angels, and His righteous servants, and abandonment from Him, glory be to Him, or a state of being one who combines two matters.
17:23: Then when he mentioned what is the greatest pillar, which is monotheism, he followed it with all the rituals and laws, saying: 23- And your Lord has decreed And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them a word of contempt, nor repel them but speak to them a generous word. meaning He has commanded with a definite command, a decisive ruling, and a firm certainty that you not worship meaning that you should not worship, so an is a noun, and it is permissible for it to be an explanatory particle and not a prohibition. And it was read And your Lord has commanded meaning He has commanded His servants to worship Him alone, then He followed it up with the command to be dutiful to parents, saying: And to parents, good treatment meaning He has decreed that you be dutiful to your parents, or and be dutiful to them, and it is not permissible for it to be related to parents with good treatment, because the source is not preceded by what it is related to. It was said that the reason for mentioning kindness to parents after worshipping God the Almighty is that they are the apparent reason for the child being born between them, and in making kindness to parents a companion to the oneness of God and worshipping Him from the announcement of the confirmation of their right and the care for their affairs is not hidden, and thus the Almighty made in another verse thanking them coupled with thanking Him, so He said: That you be grateful to Me and to your parents. Then the Almighty specifically mentioned the state of old age because it is more in need of kindness from the child than others, so He said: Either one of them or both of them reach old age with you. Either is composed of the conditional in and the vague ma to emphasize the meaning of the condition, then the nun of emphasis was inserted in the verb to increase the confirmation as if it was said: This condition is something that will certainly happen in the usual way. The grammarians said: The condition is similar to the prohibition in terms of certainty and lack of proof, so this is why the introduction of the nun of emphasis into it is correct. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read yablaghna. Al-Farra’ said: It is dual because the parents were mentioned before it, so the verb was based on their number. Then he said: either one of them or both of them as a resumption. As for the reading yablaghna, one of them is the subject independently, and his saying or both of them is also the subject, but not independently, but rather as a consequence of the conjunction. It is better for one of them to be, according to the reading yablaghna, a substitute for the pronoun referring to the parents in the verb, and for both of them to be a conjunction of the substitute. It is not correct to make both of them an emphasis on the pronoun because the conjunction requires participation. The meaning of with you is in your protection and your care. The singularity of the pronoun in with you and do not say and what follows them is to indicate that each individual is forbidden by what is forbidden, and commanded by what is commanded. The meaning of do not say to them “uff is do not say to either of them in the two cases of meeting or being alone. What is meant is not the case of meeting only. In uff there are different ways: adding a damma to the hamza with the three vowels in the fa’, with or without tanween, and with a kasra to the hamza and the fa’ without tanween, and afy is a mamal, and af with the ha’. Al-Farra’ said: The Arabs say: So-and-so is disgusted by the smell he finds, meaning he says Uff, uf. Al-Asma’i said: “Uff is dirt from the ear, and thaff is dirt from the nails. It is said when something is disgusting, then it became common until they used it for everything that bothers them.” Tha’lab narrated on the authority of Ibn al-A’rabi that uf means boredom. Al-Qutaybi said: Its origin is that if dirt or the like falls on one, one blows into it to remove it, so the sound produced by that blow is the speaker saying Uff. Then they expanded and mentioned it for every unpleasant thing that reaches them. Al-Zajjaj said: It means stench. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: Uff is dirt between the nails, and thaff is their clippings. The result is that it is a verb that indicates annoyance and resentment, or wool that indicates that, so the son is forbidden from showing anything that indicates annoyance with his parents or resentment towards them, and from this prohibition is understood the prohibition of everything that hurts them by the content of the speech or its tone as is established in the principles. And do not scold them. Scolding means reprimanding and harshness. It is said that he scolded him and rebuked him: if he greeted him with words that reprimand him. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is do not speak to them with annoyance, shouting in their faces. And speak to them instead of groaning and scolding, a generous word, meaning softly and gently, the best expression of gentleness and dignity of speech with politeness, modesty, and decency.
17:24: 24- And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy. Al-Qaffal mentioned two aspects of the meaning of lowering the wing: The first is that when a bird wants to gather its chicks to itself for raising, it lowers its wing for them, so lowering the wing became a metaphor for good management, as if it said to the child, Protect your parents by gathering them to yourself as they did to you when you were young. The second is that when a bird wants to fly and rise, it spreads its wing, and when it wants to descend, it lowers its wing, so lowering the wing became a metaphor for humility and not rising. There are two aspects to adding the wing to humility: The first is like adding Hatim to generosity in your saying Hatim al-Joud, so the original meaning is the humiliated wing, and the second is following the path of metaphor as if he imagined a wing for humiliation and then established a lowering for that wing. The majority read humiliation with a damma on the dhal from dhala yadhil dhala wa dhala wa dhala fahuwa dhaleel. Saeed bin Jubair and Urwah bin Az-Zubayr read it with a kasra on the dhal, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Asim, from their saying a docile animal with the intention of humility: meaning obedient and easy, with no difficulty in it. And from the mercy in it is the meaning of al-Sharh 94:meaning because of the extreme compassion and sympathy for them due to their old age and their need today for the one who was the poorest of God’s creation to them yesterday. Then it is as if He said to him, Glory be to Him, And do not be satisfied with Your mercy that does not last “and” but Say, My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small. And the kaf is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source: meaning mercy like their bringing me up or like their mercy to me. And it was said that what is meant is not mercy like mercy, but the kaf is for their coupling in existence, so let this happen as that happened. And upbringing is development, and it is possible that the kaf is for al-Sharh 94:meaning because of their bringing me up like His saying: And remember Him as He guided you. And God, Glory be to Him, has exaggerated in recommending parents to an exaggeration that makes the skins of the disobedient shudder and their hair stand on end. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: Whoever desires the immediate he said: Whoever desires this world with his work, We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend that is his statement. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: No, We extend the verse he said: God provides for everyone in this world, the righteous and the wicked. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse he said: God provides for whoever desires this world and provides for whoever desires the Hereafter. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak he said: Prohibited is forbidden. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Zayd. Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilya narrated on the authority of Salman on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no servant who wants to rise a degree in this world and he rises by it, except that God will describe him in the Hereafter with a degree greater and longer than it. Then he recited: ‘And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference.’” This is narrated by Zadhan on the authority of Salman. It is proven in the two Sahihs that the people of the highest degrees will see the people of ‘Illiyyin as they see a distant star in the horizon of the sky. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: blameworthy, meaning blamed. Al-Firyabi, Sa`id Ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Al-Anbari narrated in Al-Masahif on the authority of Sa`id Ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited: And your Lord commanded, instead of and He decreed. He said: The waw and the sad were attached, and you read it as and your Lord decreed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on his authority something similar. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Mani’, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from Maymun Ibn Mihran, on his authority, something similar, and he added: If it had been revealed about the decree, no one would have associated partners with it. I say: This is only necessary if the decree means the completion of the matter, and even though it is one of the meanings of the absolute decree, as in His statement: The matter about which you two are asking has been decreed, and His statement: So when you have completed your rites, “So when you have completed the prayer,” but here it means the command, and it is one of the meanings of the decree, and the command does not entail that, for He, the Almighty, has commanded His servants with all that He has made obligatory, including singling Him out for worship and making Him One, and that does not entail that polytheists will not commit polytheism. Among the meanings of the absolute decree are other meanings besides these two, such as the decree meaning creation, from which is So He decreed them seven heavens. And in the meaning of will, as in His statement: When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. And in the meaning of the covenant, as in His statement: And you were not on the western side when We decreed the matter to Moses. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And your Lord has decreed, he said: He commanded. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse: He said: Your Lord has made a covenant. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: And to parents, good treatment, he said: Kindness. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: So say not to them a word of disrespect, when removing harm from them: toilet and urine, just as they did not say it when removing harm from you: toilet and urine. Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Ali, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, If God knew of anything less than disobedience to God, He would have forbidden it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad regarding his statement: And speak to them a generous word, he said: If they call upon you, say: At your service and may you be pleased. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse: He said: A gentle and easy word. Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Urwah regarding the statement of God, And lower to them the wing of humility, he said: Be gentle with them so that you do not refuse them anything they love. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding the verse, he said: Submit to your parents as a slave submits to his harsh and rough master. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, And say, ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them,’ then God revealed after this, It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives. Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated similarly. Many authentic hadiths have been narrated about honoring parents in the two Sahihs and elsewhere, and they are well-known in the books of hadith.
17:25: His saying: 25- Your Lord knows best what is in your souls meaning what is in your consciences of sincerity and lack thereof in all acts of obedience, and of repentance from the sin that you have neglected or persisting in it, and what is in the soul of righteousness and disobedience falls under this generality primarily, and it was said that the verse is specific to what is due to parents of righteousness, and what is forbidden for children of disobedience, and the first is more worthy of consideration due to the generality of the wording, so the context does not specify it nor restrict it if you are righteous intending righteousness, and repentance from sin and sincerity to obedience, then what has occurred of the sin that you have repented from will not harm you "for indeed He is ever, to those who turn back from sins to repentance, and from lack of sincerity to pure sincerity, forgiving what they have neglected of word, deed or belief, so whoever repents, God will accept his repentance, and whoever returns to God, God will return to him.
17:26: Then the Almighty mentioned the recommendation for relatives other than parents after recommending them, saying: 26- And give the near of kin his right and the address is either to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to incite and incite others from the nation, or to everyone who is fit for that from those who are accountable, as in His saying: And your Lord has decreed and what is meant by the near of kin is the relative, and their right is the kinship that God has commanded, and He repeated the recommendation in it, and the disagreement among the people of knowledge about the obligation of spending on relatives, or on some of them such as parents on children, and children on parents is well-known. What should be relied upon is the obligation of maintaining their ties to the best of one's ability and according to what the situation requires. And the needy is conjoined with the near of kin, and in this conjoining is evidence that what is meant by the right is the financial right. And the wayfarer is conjoined with the needy, and the meaning is: And give whoever is characterized by poverty, or is one of the wayfarers, his right. The reality of the poor and the wayfarer has been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah and in At-Tawbah. What is meant in this verse is to give them charity from whatever you can afford of voluntary charity, or from whatever God has prescribed for them of obligatory charity, because they are among the eight categories that are eligible for zakat. Then when God, the Almighty, commanded what He commanded here, He forbade extravagance, saying: And do not squander wastefully. Extravagance is distributing money as one scatters seeds, however they are, without intending to place them. It is the blameworthy extravagance for exceeding the permissible limit in spending according to the Shariah, or it is spending in an unlawful manner, even if it is small. Al-Shafi’i said: Extravagance is spending money in an unlawful manner, and there is no extravagance in doing good deeds. Al-Qurtubi said after narrating this statement of Al-Shafi’i: This is the opinion of the majority. Ashhab said on the authority of Malik: Extravagance is taking money from its rightful place and spending it in an unlawful place, and it is wastefulness.
17:27: And it is forbidden because He said: 27- Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils. This sentence is an explanation for the prohibition of wastefulness, and what is meant by brotherhood is complete similarity, and avoiding resembling the devil even in one of his characteristics is obligatory, so how about what is more general than that as indicated by the general similarity, and extravagance in spending is the work of the devil, so if one of the sons of Adam does it, then he has obeyed the devil and followed his example. And the devil is ever ungrateful to his Lord, meaning very ungrateful and greatly rebellious against the truth, because with his disbelief he only does evil, and only commands to do evil, and only whispers what is not good. In this verse there is a recording of the wasteful by resembling the devils, then a recording of the kind of devil that he is ungrateful, so this necessitates that the wasteful is similar to the devil, and everyone who is similar to the devil has the ruling of the devil, and every devil is ungrateful, so the wasteful is ungrateful.
17:28: 28- And if you turn away from them It was mentioned earlier that the origin of this either is composed of the conditional in and the vague ma, and that the introduction of the nun of emphasis to the condition is due to its resemblance to the prohibition: that is, if you turn away from the near of kin, the needy, and the wayfarer for a matter that compelled you to do so, seeking mercy from your Lord, that is, for the loss of provision from your Lord. However, he made the cause, which is seeking God's mercy, the place of the reason, which is the loss of provision, because the one who loses provision seeks it. The meaning is: And if you turn away from them for the loss of provision from your Lord, hoping that God will open it up for you, then speak to them a gentle word, that is, a gentle, easy word like a beautiful promise or an acceptable apology. Al-Kisa'i said: I made the speech easy for him, meaning I made it gentle. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of the verse is: If you turn away from the questioner due to his difficulty or inability, then speak to them a gentle word, and count them as a good number. It is also possible that the meaning is: And if you turn away from them and do not benefit them due to your inability, then speak to them a gentle word. What is meant here is not turning away in the face. In this verse is a discipline from God, the Exalted, to His servants if a questioner asks them something they do not have, how to say it and what to respond to. And the one who said it did well: If I am not a generous paper for those who ask, then I am soft Those who ask for good from my creation will not be deprived of either a gift or a good return.
17:29: When God the Almighty mentioned the etiquette of withholding after the prohibition of extravagance, He explained the etiquette of spending, saying: 29- And do not make your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it forth completely. This prohibition includes every accountable person, whether the address was to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an exposition to his nation and to teach them, or the address was to every accountable person who is suitable for it. What is meant is the prohibition for a person to withhold to the point of being tight-fisted with himself and his family, and not to be generous in spending to an extent that is not necessary, such that he becomes extravagant. It is a prohibition against both excess and deficiency. From this comes the legitimacy of moderation, which is the justice that God has urged: Do not be excessive or excessive in it, both sides of the intention of things are reprehensible In this verse, God Almighty likened the state of the miser to the state of someone whose hand is tied to his neck so that he cannot use it, and likened the state of someone who exceeds the limit in his use to the state of someone who extends his hand in an extension that has nothing to do with it that is held back by hands. This depiction is a great exaggeration. Then God Almighty explained the evil of the two prohibited extremes, saying: So you will sit blamed among the people because of your miserliness, regretful because of what you did of extravagance: meaning cut off from your goals because of poverty. Regretful in origin is the one who is cut off from traveling, from the word hasra travel when he reaches it. The hasir camel is the one whose strength has gone and he cannot rise again. From this is the saying of God Almighty: The sight will return to you, humbled and weary meaning weary and cut off. It was said that its meaning is regretful for what happened, so this speaker made it from the regret which is remorse, and there is a consideration in this because the doer of regret is hasran, and regret is only said to be blamed.
17:30: Then he comforted his Messenger and the believers that those who are burdened by the addition are not because they are insignificant to God, the Most High, but because of the will of the Creator, the Provider, so he said: 30- Indeed, your Lord expands the provision for whom He wills and restricts it. That is, He expands it for some and restricts it for others for a profound wisdom, not because the one for whom He expands his provision is honored by Him, and the one for whom He restricts it is content with Him. It was said that it is possible that what is meant is that expansion and restriction are from the command of God, whose treasuries are inexhaustible. As for His servants, they must be moderate. Then he explained what he mentioned about expansion for some and restriction for others by saying: Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Knowing and Seeing. That is, He knows what they conceal and what they declare. Nothing of that is hidden from Him, for He is the Knowing of their conditions and the Seeing of how they manage their provisions.
17:31: In this verse there is evidence that He is the One who provides for His servants, so He said after it 31- And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. A poor man has nothing left for him except the malqat: which are large, smooth stones. Al-Hudhali said, describing a hunter: She was given a very strong and powerful sword if she were to poison the poor. Al-Aqdar is the diminutive of Al-Aqdar, which is a short man. Al-Khashif of clothes means: creation. Samat passed by. It is said that he is poor if he is destitute and time has taken away what he has. Aws said: I am not flattered by the troubles that befall me God the Almighty forbade them from killing their children for fear of poverty, and they used to do that. Then He explained to them that their fear of poverty until they killed their children was baseless, because God the Almighty is the Provider for His servants, He provides for children as He provides for fathers, so He said: We provide for them and for you. And you are not their providers until you do this to them. A similar verse was mentioned in Al-An’am. Then God the Almighty explained the prohibition of killing children for that by saying: Indeed, killing them was a great mistake. The majority of scholars read it with a kasra on the kha’ and a sukoon on the ta’ and with a shortened hamza. Ibn ‘Amir read khata’an with a fatha on the kha’ and the ta’ and a shortened hamza. It is said that he committed a sin in his religion, khataan, if he sinned, and akhta’a: if he took a wrong path intentionally or unintentionally. Al-Azhari said, khata’a khataan is like athama ya’thamaan, if he intentionally made a mistake, and akhta’a: if he did not intentionally make mistakes and khita’a. The poet said: Leave me alone, it is only a mistake and a deception against me, and I have only wasted my money The noun khat is used to replace mistakes. There are two forms of khat: short, which is good, and long, which is rare. Ibn Kathir read it with a kasra on the kha, a fatha on the ta, and a long hamza. An-Nahhas said: I do not know of any basis for this reading. Abu Hatim also considered it a khat. Al-Hasan read khat with a fatha on the kha and the ta with a tanween without a hamza.
17:33: When he finished mentioning the prohibition of killing children in particular and the prohibition of adultery which leads to what killing children leads to in terms of mixing lineages and their instability, he prohibited killing innocent souls in general, saying: 33- And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. What is meant by what God has forbidden is the one whom He has made innocent by the inviolability of religion or the inviolability of the covenant, and what is meant by the right which He made an exception is what allows killing innocent souls in principle, such as apostasy and adultery by a married person, and retaliation for a murderer who intentionally kills out of aggression and what is connected to that, and the exception is empty: that is, do not kill her for any reason except for a reason that is involved in the right or except in those involved in the right, and the discussion of this has been presented in Al-An'am. Then He explained the ruling on some of those killed unjustly, saying: And whoever is killed unjustly, meaning not for a reason that justifies his killing according to the Shari’ah, We have given his heir authority, meaning for whoever is in charge of his affairs from his heirs if they are present, or whoever has authority if they are not present. Authority is the power over the killer: if he wishes, he may kill, if he wishes, he may pardon, and if he wishes, he may take blood money. Then, when He explained the permissibility of retaliation for whoever is entitled to the blood of the murdered person, or what is compensation for retaliation, He forbade him from exceeding the limit, saying: “So let him not exceed what God has permitted him to do, by killing two or a group for one person, or mutilating the killing or torturing him. The majority of scholars read “la yasrif” with a lower ya’, meaning the heir. Hamza and al-Kisa’i read tasrif with a higher ta’, which is addressed to the first murderer, and He forbade him from killing: meaning, do not be excessive, O murderer, in killing, for retaliation is due to you along with the punishment, wrath, and curse of God. Ibn Jarir said: The address is to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and to the Imams after him: i.e., do not kill, O Muhammad, other than the killer, and do not let the Imams after you do that. And in Abu’s reading: Do not be extravagant. Then he gave a reason for the prohibition of extravagance, saying: Indeed, he was supported, i.e., supported and aided: meaning the guardian, for God, the Exalted, aided him by establishing retaliation for him through the arguments he presented and the clearest evidence, and He ordered the people of authority to aid him and fulfill his right until he receives it. And it is possible that the pronoun refers to the one killed: i.e., God aided him through his guardian. It was said that this verse was among the first to be revealed in the Qur’an concerning killing because it was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: If you are righteous, he said: The initiative is from the son to the father, so God said: If you are righteous, if the intention is sincere, Then He is ever, to the frequently turning, Forgiving, for the initiative that he took. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Then He is ever, to the frequently turning, Forgiving, he said: Those who return to goodness. Saeed bin Mansour, Hannad, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding the verse, he said: Those who return from sin to repentance, and from bad deeds to good deeds. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The frequently turning, he said: Those who are obedient and do good. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on his authority in Al-Shu’ab, he said: Those who repent. Al-Bukhari in his history, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: And give the relative his right, he said: He ordered him to do the most deserving of rights, and taught him what to do if he had it, and what to do if he did not have it, so he said: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, he said: If they ask you and you do not have anything, you are waiting for provision from God. Then speak to them a gentle word, God willing, it will be like the waiting period. Sufyan said: The waiting period from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a debt. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: It is to maintain ties with relatives, feed the poor and treat the wayfarer well. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said to a man from the people of Ash-Sham: Have you recited the Qur’an? He said: Yes. He said: So what did you recite regarding the Children of Israel: And give the relative his right, he said: And you are the relatives whom God has commanded to be given their right? He said: Yes. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi regarding the verse. He said: The relatives are the relatives of Banu Abd al-Muttalib. I say: There is nothing in the context that indicates this specification, nor is there any evidence for that. The meaning of the Qur’anic system is clear if the address is to everyone from the nation who is suitable for it, because its meaning is a command to every responsible person who is able to maintain his kinship ties to give them their rights, which is the connection that God has commanded. If the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, if it is indirectly to his nation, then the command is the same as the first. If it is addressed to him without indirectly, then his nation is his example, so the command to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give his relatives their rights is a command to every individual from his nation. It appears that this address is not specific to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, based on what precedes this verse, which is His statement: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him and what follows it, which is His statement: “And do not spend wastefully. Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils.” There are many hadiths on the meaning of this verse indicating the obligation of maintaining kinship ties. Ahmad and Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Anas, “A man said: O Messenger of God, I have much wealth, a family, children and a city, so tell me how to spend it and what to do? He said: Pay the obligatory zakat, for it is a purification that purifies you, and maintain kinship ties, and recognize the rights of the beggar, the neighbor and the poor. He said: O Messenger of God, give me less? He said: Give the relative his right, and the poor and the wayfarer, and do not spend wastefully. He said: It is sufficient for me, O Messenger of God.” Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, who said: When this verse was revealed: And give the relative his right, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Fatimah and gave her Fadak. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse: And give the relative his right, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave Fadak to Fatimah. Ibn Kathir said after citing this hadith of Abu Saeed, word for word: This hadith is problematic even if its chain of transmission is authentic, because the verse is Meccan, and Fadak was conquered with Khaybar in the seventh year of the Hijra, so how can this be reconciled with this? End quote. Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding his statement, And do not be wasteful, he said: Wastefulness is spending money in ways other than its right. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: We, the companions of Muhammad, used to say that wastefulness is spending in ways other than its right. Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Indeed, the wasteful, he said: They are those who spend money in ways other than its right. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab on the authority of Ali, who said: Whatever you spend on yourself and your family except extravagance or wastefulness, and whatever you give in charity, is yours. And whatever you spend for show and reputation, that is the portion of Satan. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, So speak to them a gentle word, he said: The number. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Sayyar Abu Al-Hakam who said: A grain from Iraq came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was a generous giver, so he divided it among the people. report of that reached a group of Arabs, so they said: We will go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him, but they found that he had already finished with it, so God revealed: And do not make your hand chained to your neck, he said: Confined, “And do not stretch it forth completely and you will sit down blamed,” people will blame you, destitute, with nothing in your hand. I say: I do not know how this is? The verse is Meccan, and at that time there were no Arabs who would go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor were anything brought to him from Iraq or from what was closer to it, although the conquest of Iraq did not occur until after his death, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr: “A woman sent her son to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Tell him to give me a garment. He said: I do not have anything. She said: Go back to him and tell him to give me your shirt.
