So he went back to him and took off his shirt and gave it to her, and the verse, “And do not make your hand chained” was revealed.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Aisha and struck him with his hand: Spend what is on the back of my hand. She said: Then nothing will remain. He said that three times, and God revealed, “And do not make your hand chained” the verse.” What is detracted from this is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not marry Aisha until after the migration. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And do not make your hand chained he said: He meant miserliness. And they narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: This is about spending, he says: Do not make it shackled, do not expand it with good, and do not expand it completely, meaning extravagance, so that you sit blamed, blaming yourself for what he missed of his money, deprived, all of his money is gone. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Hasan regarding his statement: Indeed, your Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it, he said: He looks at him, if wealth is better for him, He enriches him, and if poverty is better for him, He impoverishes him. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Fear of poverty, he said: Fear of poverty and need. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding his statement: Mistake, he said: A sin. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And do not come near to adultery, he said: On the day this verse was revealed, there were no limits, then the limits came after that in Surat An-Nur. Abu Ya`la and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abi bin Ka`b that he recited, “And do not come near adultery. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and an evil way,” except for those who repent, for indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. This was mentioned to `Umar, so he went to him and asked him. He said, You took it from the mouth of the Messenger of God, and you have no other work to do except clapping in al-Baqi`. Many hadiths have been narrated to warn against the immorality of adultery. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding his statement: And do not kill the soul the verse, he said: This was in Mecca and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was there, and it is the first thing revealed in the Qur’an regarding killing. The polytheists of Mecca used to assassinate the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God said: Whoever kills you from among the polytheists, do not let his killing lead you to kill his father or brother or one of his relatives. And if they are polytheists, then do not kill anyone except your killer. This was before Bara’ah was revealed. It was said that he was commanded to fight the polytheists, so that is what his statement: “And do not exceed limits in killing. Indeed, he is to be supported.” He said: Do not kill anyone other than your killer. And today it is in that position with the Muslims, and it is not permissible for them to kill anyone other than their killer. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam that the people in the pre-Islamic era, if a man killed a man, they would not be satisfied until they killed a noble man. If their killer was not noble, they would not kill their killer and would kill someone else. They were admonished in this by the words of God, the Most High: And do not kill the soul until His words: And do not exceed limits in killing. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his words: And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, he said: Evidence from God revealed, which the heir of the murdered person seeks, retaliation or blood money, and that is the authority. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid on his authority: And do not exceed limits in killing, he said: He does not kill excessively. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on his authority as well: He does not fight except a killer of his kin.
17:34: When God the Almighty mentioned the prohibition of destroying lives, He followed it with the prohibition of destroying wealth, the most important of which is preserving and caring for the orphan's wealth, as He said: 34- And do not approach the wealth of the orphan. The prohibition of approaching it is an exaggeration in the prohibition of directly dealing with it and destroying it. Then God the Almighty explained that the prohibition of approaching it does not mean the prohibition of dealing directly with it in what improves or corrupts it, but rather it is permissible for the guardian of the orphan to do what improves the orphan's wealth, and that necessitates dealing with it. He said: Except in a way that is best, meaning except in the best of ways, which is preserving it, seeking profit from it, and striving to increase it. Then He mentioned the purpose of the prohibition of approaching the orphan's wealth, as He said: Until he reaches maturity, meaning do not approach it except in a way that is best until the orphan reaches maturity. When he reaches maturity, you may hand him over to him, or dispose of him with his permission. This has been discussed in detail in Al-An'am. And fulfill the covenant. This has been discussed in more than one place. Al-Zajjaj said: Everything that God has commanded and forbidden is a covenant, so that includes what is between the servant and his Lord, and what is between the servants of one another. Fulfilling the covenant means preserving it in the manner prescribed by the Shari'ah and the lawful and acceptable manner, unless there is specific evidence indicating that it is permissible to break it. The covenant was to be questioned about, meaning one is responsible for it. The one responsible here is its owner. It has been said that the covenant is to be questioned as a rebuke to the one who breaks it.
17:35: 35- And give full measure when you measure meaning complete the measure and do not lose it when you measure for people. And weigh with an even balance. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the balance of justice: any balance of dirhams and other things. There are two languages for it: with the qaf pronounced with a damma or with a kasra. It was said that it is the qaban called the qarstaun, and it was said that it is justice itself, which is the language of the Romans, and it was said that it is a Syriac language. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr read the balance with the qaf pronounced with a damma. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read with the qaf pronounced with a kasra. The reference in his saying: That is to giving full measure and weight. It is a subject and its predicate is good meaning good for you with God and with people, as it affects good reputation and encourages people to deal with those who are like that. And the best outcome meaning the best outcome, from aal if he returns.
17:36: Then God the Almighty ordered the correction of the tongue and the heart, saying: 36- And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge meaning do not follow what you do not know, from your saying qafut so-and-so if you follow his trace, and from it is the rhyme of poetry because it follows every verse, and from it is the tribe known as the qafah because they follow the traces of people's feet. Ibn Jarir narrated from a group that they said: quf waqaf like 'atha and 'atha. Mundhir bin Saeed al-Buti said: qafa and qaf, like jdhab and jabadh. Al-Kisa'i narrated from some of the reciters that he read taquf with a damma on the qaf and a sukoon on the fa. Al-Farra' read with a fatha on the qaf, which is the language of some Arabs, and Abu Hatim and others rejected it. The meaning of the verse: the prohibition of a person saying what he does not know or doing what he has no knowledge of, and this is a general issue, and a group of commentators made it specific to matters: it was said do not criticize someone for what you do not know, and it was said that it is in false testimony, and it was said that it is in slander. Al-Qatibi said: The meaning of the verse is: Do not follow intuition and assumptions. This is correct, because everything other than that is knowledge. It was said that what is meant by knowledge here is the preponderant belief derived from a source, whether definitive or conjectural. Abu Al-Su`ud said in his interpretation: Its use in this sense is something that cannot be denied as being widespread. I say: This verse has indicated that it is not permissible to act on what is not based on knowledge, but it is general and specific to the evidence that has been reported regarding the permissibility of acting on conjecture, such as acting on the general, on the report of a single person, acting on testimony, and ijtihad in the direction of the qiblah, in the penalty for hunting, and the like. So nothing is excluded from its generality and from the generality of Indeed, conjecture does not avail against the truth at all except what there is evidence for the permissibility of acting on. Acting on opinion in matters of the Shari’ah, if it is due to the absence of evidence in the Book and the Sunnah, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has permitted it, as in his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Mu’adh when he sent him as a judge, By what do you judge? He said, By the Book of God. He said, If you do not find it? He said, Then by the Sunnah of the Messenger of God. He said, If you do not find it? He said, I will exert my opinion. This is a hadith that is suitable for use as evidence, as we have explained in a separate discussion. As for jumping on an opinion when there is evidence in the Book or the Sunnah, but the one who has the opinion has refrained from research and has come up with his opinion, then he is included under this prohibition primarily, because it is purely an opinion in the law of God, and people are sufficient for it in the Book of God, the Most High, and the Sunnah of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there is no need for it. However, the permission to have an opinion when there is no evidence is only a permission for the mujtahid who is permitted to act upon it, and no evidence indicates that it is permissible for others to act upon it and treat it as a matter of the law. With this, it becomes clear to you in the most complete clarity and becomes clear to you in the most complete manner that these opinions recorded in the subsidiary books are not from the law at all, and the one who acts upon them is on the brink of a precipice. The mujtahid who has a lot of opinion has followed what he has no knowledge of, and the poor imitator who acts upon the opinion of that mujtahid has acted upon what he has no knowledge of, nor does the one who imitates him. Darknesses, one upon another. It has been said that this verse is specific to beliefs, and there is no evidence for that at all. Then the Almighty explained the prohibition of acting on what one does not know by saying: Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those one will be questioned, referring to the three organs, and they were treated like rational beings because they are responsible for their conditions and witness to their owners. Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs express what is rational and what is not rational by those, and Ibn Jarir recited, as evidence for the permissibility of this, the words of the poet: Blame the houses after the house of Al-Lawa and life after those days It was objected that the narration was after those people, and others followed him in this error, such as the author of Al-Kashshaf. The pronoun in kana in his saying: was responsible for it refers to all, and so does the pronoun in about it, and it was said that the pronoun in kana refers to the rhyme indicated by his saying: and do not stop. And his saying about it is in the nominative case because of the attribution of being responsible to it, and it was responded to by what Al-Nahhas narrated of the consensus on the impermissibility of presenting the one who takes the place of the subject if it is a preposition or a noun. It was said that it is better to say that it is the subject of the deleted responsible, and the mentioned is an explanation of it. The meaning of asking these limbs is that He asks their owner about what he used them for because they are tools, and what is used with them is the human soul. If he used them for good, he deserves reward, and if he used them for evil, he deserves punishment. It was said that God Almighty makes these limbs speak when they are asked, so they tell about what their owner did. 8- "Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure," meaning about the pleasures of this world that distracted you from working for the Hereafter. Qatada said: It means that the disbelievers of Mecca were in goodness and pleasure in this world, so they will be asked on the Day of Resurrection about their gratitude for what they had, and they did not thank the Lord of the blessings because they worshipped other than Him and associated others with Him. Al-Hasan said: None will be asked about pleasure except the people of Hellfire. Qatada said: God, the Exalted, will ask every person with a blessing about what He has bestowed upon him, and this is the apparent meaning. There is no reason to specify pleasure to an individual person or a type, because its definition is for a genus or an exhaustive list, and the mere question does not necessitate the punishment of the one being asked about the blessing he is being asked about. God may ask the believer about the blessings He has bestowed upon him, how he spent them, and what he did with them. To know his shortcomings and failure to do what is required of him in terms of gratitude. It was said that the question is about security and health, and it was said about health and leisure, and it was said about perception by the senses, and it was said about the pleasure of food and drink, and it was said about lunch and dinner, and it was said about the coolness of drink and the shade of dwellings, and it was said about moderation of character, and it was said about the pleasure of the letter nun, and the first is general as we mentioned. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Burdah regarding the verse {{You are distracted by multiplying [your worldly pursuits]}}, that he said: It was revealed about two tribes of the Ansar, Banu Haritha. Banu Harith boasted and multiplied, so one of them said: Among you are the likes of so-and-so and so-and-so. The others said the same, boasting about the living. Then they said: Let's go to the graves. One of the two groups began to say: Among you are the likes of so-and-so, pointing to the grave, and the likes of so-and-so, and the others did the same, so God revealed {{You are distracted by multiplying [your worldly pursuits] * Until you visit the graves}} Indeed, in what you visit there was for you a lesson and a distraction. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse {{You are distracted by multiplying [your worldly pursuits]}, that he said: In wealth and children. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of his father who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: Putting together in worship has distracted you meaning from obedience until you visit the graves meaning until death comes to you No! You will surely know meaning if you were to enter your graves Then no! You will surely know meaning if you were to emerge from your graves to the place of assembly No! If you were to stand before your Lord on account of your deeds “You would surely see Hell meaning the path is placed in the middle of Hell, so a Muslim will be saved and a Muslim will be scratched and a Muslim will be left scratched in the fire of Hell Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure meaning full bellies, cool drinks, shaded dwellings, moderate character, and the pleasure of sleep. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ayyad ibn Ghanam. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, "Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure, he said, It means the health of the body, hearing, and sight. And he is more knowledgeable about that than them, and it is His verse, Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart - about all those one will be questioned." Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa'id Al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, "Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure, he said, It means security and health. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ali bin Abi Talib, he said, Pleasure is well-being. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding the verse, he said, Whoever eats wheat bread and drinks cold water from the Euphrates, and has a house in which he lives, then that is from the pleasures about which he will be questioned. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Al-Darda', he said, The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said regarding the verse, 'Eating wheat bread, sleeping in the shade, and drinking cold water from the Euphrates.'" Perhaps the attribution of this to the Prophet is not correct, and it may have been from the words of Abu Al-Darda'. Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Abu Qilabah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the verse, he said: Some of my nation will combine ghee and honey with dates and eat it. This is a mursal narration. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: When this verse was revealed, the Companions said: O Messenger of God, what kind of comfort are we enjoying? We only eat barley bread halfway through our stomachs. God revealed to His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to say to them: Do you not wear sandals and drink cold water? This is from the comforts. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hanad, Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid who said: When the verse, Has multiplying [your worldly pursuits] distracted you? was revealed, he recited until he reached, Then you will surely be asked that Day about comfort, they said: “O Messenger of God, what comfort will we be asked about? They are only the two black things: water and dates, and our swords are over our necks, and the enemy is present, so what comfort will we be asked about?” He said: That will happen. It was narrated by ‘Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. It was narrated by Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam. It was narrated by Ahmad in al-Zuhd, by ‘Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The first thing that a servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection regarding blessings is that it will be said to him: ‘Did We not make your body healthy and give you cold water to drink?’” Ahmad, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Abu Bakr, and ‘Umar came to us, so we fed them dates and gave them water to drink. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘This is one of the blessings about which you are asking.’” A similar version was narrated by ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi from the hadith of Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah. Muslim, the Sunni scholars, and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that they said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out and found Abu Bakr and Umar. He said, ‘What brought you out of your homes just now?’ They said, ‘Hunger, O Messenger of God.’ He said, ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, what brought you out brought me out, so get up.’ So they got up with him. Then he came to a man from the Ansar, but he was not in his house. When the woman saw him, she said, ‘Welcome.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘Where is so-and-so?’ She said, ‘He went to get us fresh water. Then the Ansari came and looked at the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his two companions and said, ‘Praise be to God, no one has had more guests today than I.’ He went and brought a bunch of dates and said, ‘Eat some of this.’ He took the knife and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, ‘Beware of the milking ones.’ He slaughtered a sheep for them and they ate from the sheep and from that bunch and drank. When they were satisfied and had their fill, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Abu Bakr and Umar, ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, we will be asked about this luxury on the Day of Resurrection.’” There are hadiths on this topic.
17:37: 37- And do not walk on the earth exultantly. Exultation: It was said that it is intense joy. It was said that it is arrogance in walking, and it was said that a person exceeds his capacity, and it was said that it is conceit in walking, and it was said that it is insolence and wickedness, and it was said that it is activity. It appears that what is meant by it here is conceit and pride. Al-Zajjaj said in his interpretation of the verse: Do not walk on the earth exultantly and proudly. He mentioned the earth even though walking can only be done on it or on what is depended on it as an emphasis and confirmation. And he who said it did well: Do not walk on the earth except in humility, for there are many people beneath it who are more exalted than you. Even if you are in glory, protection and strength, how many people have died who were more powerful than you? Marah is a verbal noun that occurs in the state of being happy, and there is a kind of emphasis in placing the verbal noun in the place of the adjective. The majority read marah with the opening of the ra on the verbal noun. Yaqub narrated from a group that he broke it as an active participle, then the Almighty explained this prohibition by saying: You will never tear the earth. It is said that kharak al-thawb means he split it, and kharak al-ard means cutting it, and kharak al-ard is a wide part of the earth. The meaning is that you will never tear the earth by walking on it arrogantly, and in it is mockery of the arrogant and haughty person. And you will never reach the mountains in height, meaning that your power will never reach the level of the mountains until the size of your body carries you to arrogance and haughtiness, so you have no strength to tear the earth by walking on it, and no bone in your body to reach the level of the mountains. So what carries you in what you are in? Tall is a verbal noun in the place of a state, or a distinguishing feature, or an object for it. It was said that what is meant by kharak al-ard is to pierce it, not to cut it by distance. Al-Azhari said: kharak means to cut it. Al-Nahhas said: This is clearer, as if it is taken from the word kharak, which means a wide opening. It is said that someone is more akhrak than someone else, meaning he travels more.
17:38: And the reference in his saying: 38- "All of that" to all of what was mentioned previously of commands and prohibitions, or to what he prohibited only from his saying: "And do not stand And do not walk Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Masruq read his bad" with the addition of bad to the pronoun and this reading is supported by his saying: "disliked" because bad is disliked, and it is also supported by the reading of Abu: his bad deeds were, and Abu Ubaid chose this reading. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu Amr read "bad" as one of the bad deeds, and its accusative is on the predicate of was, and disliked is an attribute of bad according to the meaning, because it means bad, or it is a substitute for bad, and it was said that it is a second predicate for was based on the wording of all and Abu Ali Al-Farisi preferred the substitute, and it was said in explaining it in a way other than this which contains arbitrariness that is not hidden. Al-Zajjaj said: The addition is better, because the verses that preceded it contain bad and good, so the bad is the disliked, and this is strengthened by the reminder of the disliked. He said: And whoever reads with the tanween makes all of that encompass the forbidden without the good, meaning: Everything that God has forbidden is bad and disliked. He said: The disliked according to this reading is a substitute for the bad and not a description, and what is meant by the disliked in the sight of God is that which He hates and is not pleased with, not that it is not meant absolutely, because of the conclusive evidence that things happen by His will, glory be to Him. And mentioning absolute dislike even though in the things that preceded there are those that are major sins is an indication that mere dislike in the sight of God, glory be to Him, causes the listener to be repelled and avoid that. The result is that in the previous characteristics there is what is good, which is what is commanded, and what is disliked, which is what is forbidden. So according to the reading of the addition, there is a reference to the prohibitions, then the report about these prohibitions that they are bad and disliked in that case.
17:39: 39- This is from what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom The reference is to what was mentioned previously from His saying Do not make to this end and it rises to twenty-five duties, from what your Lord has revealed to you: that is, from its type or some of it, and it is called wisdom because it is a well-established statement, and it is what he taught of the laws or from the well-established rulings that are not subject to corruption. And according to the philosophers, wisdom is the knowledge of the truth for its own sake, and from wisdom is related to an omitted word that occurred as a state, that is, being from wisdom, or in place of the relative pronoun by repeating the preposition, or related to revealed And do not make with God another god The Almighty repeated the prohibition of polytheism as an emphasis, confirmation, and warning that it is the head of the characteristics of religion and its pillar. It was said that God Almighty took into consideration a minute in this emphasis, so He arranged for the first to be blamed and abandoned, and that is an indication of the state of polytheism in this world, and He arranged for the second to be thrown into Hell, blamed and rejected, and that is an indication of his state in the Hereafter, and in sitting there, and the throwing here is an indication that man in this world has a form of choice, unlike the Hereafter, and the explanation of blamed and rejected has been presented.
17:40: 40- Has your Lord chosen you with sons and taken for Himself daughters from among the angels? Abu Ubaidah said: He chose you, and Al-Fadl said: He made you pure. This is addressed to the infidels who say that the angels are daughters of God. It contains a severe rebuke and a severe rebuke for what these people who are like livestock, rather they are more astray, used to say. The fa is for conjunction with something understood, like its counterparts that we have repeated. Indeed, you say, meaning those who say that they have males and God has females, a tremendous statement, exceeding in magnitude and boldness towards God to a place whose magnitude cannot be measured.
17:41: 41- And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an meaning We have explained the types of sayings in it from examples and other things, or We have repeated it in it. It was said that in is redundant and the meaning is that We have certainly diversified this Qur'an. Diversification in origin means diversifying something from one direction to another. It was said that the meaning of diversification is contrast: meaning We have diversified between the sermons so that they may remember and consider. The majority read diversified with emphasis, and Al-Hasan read with emphasis. Then the Almighty explained that by saying: so that they may remember meaning so that they may learn a lesson and ponder with their minds and think about it until they realize the falsehood of what they say. Yahya ibn Waththab, Al-A’mash, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read li-dhakru with a light la, and the rest with a shaddah. Abu Ubaid chose it because it conveys the meaning of multiplication. The phrase wa ma yazidhum huwa nafaran is in the accusative case as a state: that is, while the fact is that this inflection and reminder only increases their distance from the truth and their neglect of looking at what is correct, because they have believed that the Qur’an is a trick, magic, divination and poetry, and they do not refrain from this misguidance and they have no deterrent that will incite them to guidance. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And do not approach the property of orphans, he said: They did not mix with them in wealth, food, or vehicles until the verse: But if you mix with them, then they are your brothers was revealed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: Indeed, the covenant will be questioned about, he said: God will ask the one who breaks the covenant about his breach. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding the verse: He will ask about his covenant from the one who gave it to him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: And give full measure when you measure, meaning to others, and weigh with an even balance, meaning the scales, and in the language of the Romans the scale is the qistas, that is better, meaning fulfilling the measure and the scale is better than deficiency, and better in outcome, the outcome. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Firyabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The qistas is justice in the Roman language. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: The qistas is the scale. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Iron. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not hesitate, he said: Do not say. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: Do not accuse anyone of what you have no knowledge of. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Hanafiyyah regarding the verse that he said: False testimony. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those one will be questioned, he said: His hearing, sight and heart will testify against him. Al-Faryabi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: About all those one will be questioned, he said: His hearing, sight and heart will testify against him. Al-Faryabi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: About all those one will be questioned, he said: On the Day of Resurrection, was it like that or not? Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And do not walk upon the earth exultantly, he said: Do not walk boastfully and haughtily, for that will not reach the mountains nor will you tear through the earth with your boasting and haughtiness. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Torah contains fifteen verses from the Children of Israel, then he recited: And do not make with God another god. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: repelled, he said: banished.
17:42: His saying: 42- "Say: If there were with Him other gods as they say" Ibn Kathir and Hafs read it with the lower yaa', and the rest read it with the upper yaa' as an address to those who say that there are other gods with God, and then it is an answer to their false statement and a reward for if "they would have sought to the Lord of the Throne who is God, the Most High, a way" a path to overcome and resist as kings do with each other by fighting and wrestling, and it was said that its meaning is: then the gods would have sought to draw near to God and be close to Him, because they are below Him, and the polytheists only believed that it would bring them closer to God. The first meaning is apparent, and similar to its meaning is His, the Most High's, saying: "If there were within them gods besides God, they both would have been ruined."
17:43: Then the Almighty exalted Himself, saying 43- Glory be to Him and glorification and sanctification, and and He is exalted has already been mentioned, far removed from what they say of heinous sayings and great slander exaltedly meaning exaltedly, but He placed exaltation in place of transcendence as in His saying: And God caused you to grow from the earth as plants then He described exaltation with greatness as an exaggeration of transcendence, and as a warning that between the necessary in itself and the possible in itself, and between the absolutely rich and the absolutely poor, there is a difference that cannot be increased.
17:44: Then, the Almighty, explained the majesty of His kingdom and the greatness of His authority, saying: 44- The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. It was read with the lower thana in yusbah and with the upper, and He said in them with the pronoun of rational beings because He attributed to them the glorification which is the action of rational beings. The Almighty informed about the heavens and the earth that they glorify Him, as well as whoever is in them of His creatures who have minds, and they are the angels, humans, jinn, and other things that do not have minds. Then He increased that in generalization and emphasis, saying: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, so it included everything that is called a thing, whatever it may be. It was said that His statement: and whoever is in them is interpreted as referring to the angels and the two heavy things, and and there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise is interpreted as referring to everything other than that of the creatures. Scholars have differed on this generality: is it specific or not? A group said: It is not specific, and they interpreted the glorification as glorification of proof because every creature bears witness to itself and guides others that God is the Creator and the Almighty. A group said: This glorification is in its true sense and the generality is in its apparent sense. What is meant is that all creatures glorify God, the Most High, with this glorification that means sanctification, even if humans do not hear that or understand it. This is supported by His statement, the Most High: But you do not understand their glorification, because if what was meant was glorification of proof, it would have been something that would be understood by everyone. It was answered that what is meant by His statement: You do not understand are the disbelievers who turn away from consideration. A group said: This generality is specific to the angels and the two heavy things, not to inanimate objects. It was said that it is specific to growing bodies, so plants are included, as this statement was narrated from Ikrimah and Al-Hasan. He specified the glorification of plants at the time of their growth, not after they are cut down. Evidence for this was provided by the hadith: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by two graves,” in which it says: “Then he called for a fresh stalk and split it in two, and said: It will lighten their burden as long as they do not dry up.” The interpretation of the verse as general is supported by his statement: Indeed, We subjected the mountains to him, glorifying God in the evening and at sunrise, and his statement: And among them are those that fall down for fear of God, and his statement: And the mountains fall down in utter ruin, and similar verses. It was established in the Sahih that they used to hear the glorification of food while they were eating with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Likewise, the hadith of Hanin al-Jad’, and the hadith that a stone in Mecca used to greet the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and all of them are in the Sahih, including the glorification of pebbles in his hand, may God bless him and grant him peace. And defending the generality of this verse with mere exclusions is not the habit of those who believe in God Almighty and believe in what came from Him. The meaning of except glorify Him with praise is except glorify Him while praising Him, but you do not understand their glorification. Al-Hasan, Abu Amr, Ya’qub, Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Khalaf read glorifies with the first letter of address, and the rest read it with the second letter of address. Abu Ubaid chose this reading: Indeed, He was Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving. So part of His forbearance is that He gives you respite and does not inflict His punishment upon you, and part of His forgiveness of you is that He does not punish those of you who repent.
17:45: When He finished with the divine matters, He began to mention some of the verses of the Qur’an and what happens to its listeners, so He said: 45- And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible veil. We place between you, O Muhammad, and the polytheists who do not believe in the Hereafter a veil: meaning that they, due to their turning away from your recitation and their neglect of you, are like someone between you and whom there is a veil; they pass by you but do not see you. Its meaning was mentioned by Al-Zajjaj and others. The meaning of hidden is concealer. Al-Akhfash said: He meant concealer. The subject may be in the form of the object, as you say: You are indeed ill-omened and auspicious. Rather, it is ill-omened and auspicious. It was said that the meaning of hidden is one who conceals, like their saying a flood, meaning one who is full. It was said that it is a veil that the eyes do not see, so it is hidden from them. It was said that a veil is beyond a veil, so it is hidden by something else. It was said that what is meant by the hidden veil is the nature and the seal.
17:46: 46- And We have placed over their hearts coverings. Al-Akna: the plural of Kinan. Its explanation has been presented in Al-An'am. It has been said that it is a narration of what they used to say, Our hearts are covered. "And in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a veil. That they may understand it" is an object for which: meaning, out of dislike for them to understand it, or lest they understand it, meaning that they comprehend what is in it of commands, prohibitions, wisdom, and meanings. "And in their ears is deafness" meaning, deafness and heaviness. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: that they may hear it. One of the ugly things about the polytheists is that they liked to have their gods mentioned as God Almighty is mentioned. So if they heard God mentioned without their gods mentioned, they would flee from the gathering. That is why God said: And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an, meaning as one, not accompanied by the mention of their gods. It is a verbal noun that takes the place of a state. They turned their backs in aversion is a verbal noun, and the meaning is: they fled in aversion, or they fled in aversion. It was said that the plural of nafir is like qa’id and qa’ud. The first is more appropriate. The verbal noun would be in the place of a state: meaning they turned away in aversion.
17:47: 47- We know best what they listen to meaning they listen to you while they are belittling you and the Qur'an and making idle mention of your Lord alone. It was said that the letter ba is redundant and the circumstance in when they listen to you is related to I know best: meaning We know best when they listen to you what they listen to, and it emphasizes the threat. His statement, and when they are whispering is also related to I know best: meaning We know best what they are whispering to each other at the time of their whispering, and they were whispering to each other with denial and mockery. He says instead of when they are whispering. You are following none but a man who has been bewitched meaning each of them says to the others when they are whispering: You are following none but a man who has been bewitched so his mind has become confused and he has deviated from the bounds of moderation. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The bewitched one is the one who has lost his mind and who has been corrupted by their words. Enchanted food if it spoils his work, and enchanted land that has been affected by more rain than it should have been so it has spoiled it. It was said that the bewitched is the deceived, because magic is a trick and deception, and that is because they claimed that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was learning from some people, and they were deceiving him with that teaching. Abu Ubaidah said: The meaning of bewitched is that he has magic: that is, a lung, so he cannot do without food and drink, so he is like you, and the Arabs say to the coward: his magic has blown up, and everyone who eats from a human or other is bewitched, and from that is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: He showed us two places for an unseen matter and we were enchanted by food and drink. That is, we feed and entertain. Ibn Qutaybah said: I do not know what led him to this abhorrent interpretation, although the predecessors interpreted it in clear ways.
17:48: 48- "Look how they have struck for you examples meaning they said sometimes that you are a soothsayer and sometimes a magician, sometimes a poet, and sometimes a madman they have gone astray from the right path in all of that so they cannot find a way" to guidance or to the criticism that the minds accept and that is believed, not the origin of the criticism, so they did what they were able to do of it, and it was said that they cannot find a way out due to the contradiction in their words like their saying: a mad magician. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr regarding his statement: "Then they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne" he said: to remove His kingdom. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu Nu`aym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma` wa al-Sifat narrated on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Qart that on the night of the Night Journey to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, Gabriel was on his right and Michael was on his left. He flew with him until he reached the highest heavens. When he returned, he said: I heard glorification from the highest heavens, along with much glorification. The highest heavens glorify the One of Majesty, fearing the One of Majesty in what is high. Glory be to the Most High, the Most High. Glory be to Him, the Most High. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was sitting with his companions when he heard a rumbling, and he said: The heavens groaned, and it has every right to groan. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, there is not a space in it the size of a handspan except that there is the forehead of an angel prostrating, glorifying Him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Shall I not tell you of something that Noah commanded his son to say? Noah said to his son: O my son, I command you to say Subhan God, for it is the prayer of creation, the glorification of creation, and by it creation is provided for.” God, the Most High, said: There is nothing but glorifies Him with praise. Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Ibn Umar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that he said: There is no servant who glorifies God except that everything that God has created glorifies Him. He said: There is nothing but glorifies Him with praise. Ibn Kathir said: Its chain of transmission is weak. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “An ant bit one of the prophets, so he ordered the ant colony to be burned, so God revealed to him: Because of a single ant, a nation of nations was burned while glorifying God.” Al-Nasa'i, Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Amr who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade killing frogs and said: ‘Its croaking is glorification of God.’” Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: There is nothing but glorifies God with praise, he said: The crop glorifies God and its reward is for its owner, and the garment glorifies God and the dirt says: ‘If you are a believer, then wash me.’” Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on his authority that he said: Everything glorifies God except the dog and the donkey. Ibn Rahawayh narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Al-Zuhri who said: A crow with abundant wings was brought to Abu Bakr, and it began to spread its wings and say: ‘No game was hunted or tree was cut except for what I lost of glorification.’ Ahmad narrated it in Az-Zuhd and Abu Al-Shaykh on the authority of Maymun bin Mihran who said: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq was brought and he mentioned it from his statement without a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Nu’aym narrated it in Al-Hilyah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in a similar manner on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud with some of the same meaning. Abu Al-Sheikh narrated from the hadith of Abu Al-Darda’ with a similar meaning. Ibn Asakir narrated from the hadith of Abu Ruhm something similar. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Al-Hasan who said: This verse in the Torah is like a thousand verses: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. He said: In the Torah, the mountains glorify Him and the trees glorify Him, and so-and-so glorifies Him, and so-and-so glorifies Him. Ahmad and Abu Al-Sheikh narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: David prayed one night until morning, and when morning came he found joy in himself, so a frog called out to him: O David, I was so persistent because of you, but I dozed off. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha’b from Sadaqah bin Yasar who said: David was in his prayer niche when he saw a small worm, so he thought about its creation and said: God does not care about the creation of this. So God made it speak, and it said: O David, do you marvel at yourself? Because I remember God and thank Him as much as God has given me, from you for what God has given you. God said: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. There are hadiths and narrations from the Salaf in which it is explicit that all creatures glorify God. Abu Ya`la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Na`im and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, who said: When the verse May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, was revealed, Umm Jameel, the one-eyed woman, came wailing and holding a stick in her hand, saying: We blame our father, despise his religion, and disobey his command. The Messenger of God was sitting and Abu Bakr was beside him. Abu Bakr said: This woman has come and I am afraid that she will see you. He said: She will not see me. He recited the Qur’an and held fast to it, as God the Almighty said: And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible veil. So she came and stood over Abu Bakr but did not see the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: O Abu Bakr, I have heard that your companion has satirized me. Abu Bakr said: No, by the Lord of this House, he has not satirized you. She left saying: Quraysh know that I am the daughter of their master. This story has been narrated with different wordings. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible veil. He said: The invisible veil is a covering over their hearts so that they do not understand it or benefit from it. They obeyed Satan and he took control of them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad regarding the verse, he said: That was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he recited the Qur’an to the polytheists in Mecca, they heard his recitation but did not see him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they turned their backs in aversion, he said: The devils. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: When they listened to you, he said: Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah and Al-As bin Wa’il.
17:49: When the Almighty finished narrating the people's doubts about the prophethoods, He narrated their doubts about the matter of the Resurrection, saying: 49- "And they said, 'When we are bones and dust?'" The question is for denunciation and rejection. The explanation of the doubt is that when a person dies, his bones dry up, scatter and disperse in the corners of the world, and their intermediate parts mix with their counterparts from the elements, so how can it be conceivable after that that they come together in their original form, then life returns to that group? The Almighty answered them by saying that returning the body of the dead to a state of life is possible, and if you suppose that his body has become the furthest thing from life and from the moisture of the living, such as stones and iron, it is like the saying of the speaker: Do you covet me while I am the son of so-and-so, so he says: Be the son of the sultan or the son of whomever you wish, and I will demand my right from you. The remains: what is broken and worn out of everything, such as crumbs, debris, and rubble. This was said by Abu Ubaidah, Al-Kisa’i, Al-Farra’, and Al-Akhfash. You say from it: Rafat Al-Shi’ Rafatan: meaning it was smashed, so it is marfut. It was said that the remains are dust, and it was said that the dirt. Shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation? The question indicating denunciation and exclusion was repeated for emphasis and confirmation. The factor in if is what lambu’athun indicated, not itself, because what comes after in and the hamza and the lam do not act on what comes before them. The meaning is: Shall we, if we are bones and remains, be resurrected? The accusative of khalaqan is on the source without its wording, or on the state: meaning created, and jadeedan is an attribute of it.
17:50: 50- "Say, 'Be you stones or iron, or some other creation' of that which is great in your hearts.'" Ibn Jarir said: Its meaning is that if you are amazed at God's creation of bones and flesh for you, then be stones or iron if you are able to do so. Ali ibn Isa said: Its meaning is that if you were stones or iron, He would restore you as He began you and would cause you to die and then bring you back to life. An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement, because they cannot be stones or iron. Rather, the meaning is that they have acknowledged their Creator and denied the resurrection, so it was said to them, 'Feel free to be whatever you wish. If you were stones or iron, you would be resurrected as you were created the first time.' I said: And in this manner we decided the answer to the doubt before this.
17:51: 51- "Or a creation that is great in your hearts" meaning that it is great in your eyes, which is greater than stones and iron, in contrast to life, for you will inevitably be resurrected. It was said that what is meant by it is the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, because of their greatness in the souls. A group of scholars and followers said: What is meant by it is death, because there is nothing greater in the soul of the son of Adam than it. The meaning is: If you were death, God would have killed you and then resurrected you. The remoteness of this is not hidden, for the meaning of the verse is the ascension from stones to iron, then from iron to what is greater in the hearts of the people than it, and death itself is not something that can be understood or sensed until the ascension from iron to it occurs. Then they will say, ‘Who will restore us?’ if we were bones and remains, or stones or iron with the difference between the two states. Say, ‘He who created you the first time.’ That is, He who created you and invented you at the beginning of your creation without a previous example or a preceding image. Then they will shake their heads at you, that is, they will move them in mockery. It is said, He shook his head, meaning he shakes and shakes, and he shakes a shake and a shake: meaning he moved, and he shook his head, he moved it as if astonished. From this is the saying of the rajaz poet: He lowered his head towards me and convinced me. And the other rajaz poet said: And she lowered her teeth Another said: When she saw me, she lowered her head. And they say, ‘When is it?’ meaning the resurrection and re-entry, mocking and ridiculing them. Say, ‘Perhaps it is near.’ That is, it is near, because perhaps in God’s speech is bound to happen. And similar to it is And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. And everything that is coming is near.
17:52: 52- "The Day He calls you" The circumstance is in the accusative case with an implied verb: i.e. remember, or in place of "soon", or the meaning is: The Day He calls you, whatever it was, the call is the call to the place of assembly with words that all creatures hear, and it was said that it is the shout that you hear, so it is a call to them to gather in the place of assembly "then you respond with His praise" i.e. submitting to Him, praising what He did to you, so it is in the accusative case as a state. It was said that the meaning is: then you respond and praise be to God as the poet said: Praise be to God, I do not wear fancy clothes, nor do I hide from treachery. It has been narrated that when the infidels emerge from their graves they say: Glory be to You and praise be to You. It has been said that what is meant by supplication here is the resurrection and the response is that they will be resurrected, so the meaning is: On the Day He resurrects you, you will be resurrected obediently. And you will think that you have remained only a little, meaning that you will think upon resurrection that you have remained in your graves only a little while. It has also been said that it is between the two blasts, and that is because the torment is withheld from those being tormented between the two blasts, and that is forty years in which they sleep. Therefore, They will say, ‘Woe to us! Who has raised us from our beds?’ It has been said that the world became insignificant in their eyes and became small when they saw the Day of Resurrection, so they said this statement.
17:53: 53- And tell My servants to say that which is best meaning, O Muhammad, tell My believing servants that they say when they converse with the polytheists the word that is best of all good speech, as in the words of the Almighty: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best and His words: And speak to him with gentle speech because being harsh with them may repel them from answering or lead to what the Almighty said: And do not insult those they invoke other than God, lest they insult God in enmity without knowledge and this was before the revelation of the verse of the sword, and it was said that the meaning is: Tell them to command what God commanded and forbid what He forbade, and it was said that this verse is for the believers among themselves in particular, and the first is more appropriate as is attested by the reason that we will mention, God willing, Indeed, Satan induces dissension among them meaning by corruption, sowing enmity and temptation. Al-Yazidi said: It is said that he induces dissension among us: meaning he corrupts. Another said: Nazagh means temptation. Indeed, Satan is ever a clear enemy to man, meaning he pretends to be hostile and reveals it. This is an explanation of what came before it, and something similar to this has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah.
17:54: 54- "Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy on you; or if He wills, He will punish you." It was said that this is addressed to the polytheists. The meaning is: If He wills, He will guide you to Islam and have mercy on you, or cause you to die from polytheism and punish you. It was also said that it is addressed to the believers: that is, if He wills, He will have mercy on you by protecting you from the disbelievers, or if He wills, He will punish you by giving them power over you. It was also said that this is an explanation of the word that is better: "And We have not sent you over them as a guardian." That is, We have not entrusted you with preventing them from disbelief and forcing them to believe. It was also said: We have not made you a guarantor for them to be taken by them. From this is the saying of the poet: I remembered Abu Arwa and spent the night as if I were the agent of the cold of past matters. Any sponsor.
17:55: 55- And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth He knows them best in essence, state and merit, and this is more general than His saying: Your Lord knows best about you because this includes everything in the heavens and the earth of His creations, and that is specific to the children of Adam or some of them, and this is like an introduction to His saying: And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others meaning that this preference is from His knowledge of who is higher in rank and who is lower than him, and who deserves more distinction by increasing his virtues and merits. This was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. And God took Abraham as a friend, and Moses as a speaker, and made Jesus His word and spirit, and gave Solomon a great kingdom, and forgave Muhammad his past and future sins, and made him the master of the children of Adam. In this verse, there is a refutation of what the infidels denied, regarding what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated about his high status with his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. Then he mentioned what David was given preference with, saying: And We gave David the Psalms, meaning a written book. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, do not deny the preference of Muhammad and his being given the Qur’an, for God gave David the Psalms. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and remains, he said: dust. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: and remains, he said: dust. And regarding his statement: Say, ‘Be you stones or iron,’ he said: Be whatever you wish, for God will restore you as you were. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdullah Ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement: or a creation of that which is great in your breasts, he said: death, if you were death, I would have brought you back to life. Abdullah Ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar as well. Abdullah Ibn Ahmad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr something similar, and he added: So be death if you are able, for death will die. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they will shake their heads at you, he said: They will move them in mockery. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And they will say, ‘When will it be?’ he said: The repetition. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali Ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And you will respond with His praise, he said: By His command. Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr regarding the verse: They will emerge from their graves saying: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada: And you will respond with His praise, he said: By knowing and obeying Him. And you will think that you have remained but a little, meaning that in this world, the world will be insignificant to them, and they will say when they see the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin regarding his statement: And tell My servants to say that which is best, he said: There is no god but God. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding the verse, he said: He pardons the bad. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, he said: He says to him, May God have mercy on you, may God forgive you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, he said: The devil’s incitement. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding His statement, And We gave David the Psalms, he said: We used to say that it was a supplication that David taught and praise and glorification of God, the Almighty, in which there is nothing permissible or forbidden, no obligations or limits. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, he said: The Psalms are praise, supplication and glorification of God. I said: The matter is as Qatada and Al-Rabi’ said, for we have come across the Psalms and found them to be sermons delivered by David, peace be upon him, addressing his Lord, the Exalted, when he entered the church. The total number of sermons is one hundred and fifty, each sermon is called a psalm with the first mīm open, the ḍay silent, the second mīm closed, and the last rā’. In some of these sermons, David complains to his Lord about his enemies and seeks His help against them, and in some of them he praises God, glorifies Him, and extols Him because of the victory and triumph that they had achieved over them. During the sermon, he would play the harp, which is an instrument of entertainment. Al-Suyuti mentioned here in Al-Durr Al-Manthur narrations from a group of the Salaf who mention expressions that they came across in the Psalms that do not have much benefit, for what the Qur’an contains of sermons and deterrents suffices them and others.
17:56: His statement: 56- "Say: Call upon those you claim are gods besides Him." This is a response to a group of polytheists who worshipped statues as images of angels, and to a group of the People of the Book who said that Jesus, Mary, and Ezra were divine. So God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them: Call upon those you claim are gods besides God. It was said that by those you claim, He meant a group of jinn who were among the Arabs. The verse was only specified for those we mentioned because of His statement: They seek a means of access to their Lord, for this is not appropriate for inanimate objects. They do not possess the power to remove harm from you, meaning they are not able to do so. The true worshipped One is the One who is able to remove harm and to transform it from one state to another and from one place to another. So it is necessary to be certain that these that you claim are gods are not gods.
17:57: Then He, the Almighty, confirmed their inability to do so by stating the extent of their need for God in bringing benefits and repelling harm, saying: 57- Those whom they call upon seek a means of approach to their Lord. Those is the subject and those whom they call upon is His attribute, and the relative pronoun is omitted: that is, they call upon them, and the predicate of the subject is they seek a means of approach to their Lord. It is possible that those whom they call upon is the predicate of the subject: that is, those who call upon His servants to worship them, and they seek is in the accusative case as a state. Ibn Mas'ud read it with the superlative as a direct address. The rest read it with the subjunctive as a predicate, and there is no disagreement that they seek with the subjunctive and the means of approach through obedience and worship: that is, they supplicate to God in seeking what brings them closer to their Lord, and the pronoun in their Lord refers to the worshippers or the worshipped. Which of them is nearest is the subject and predicate. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is which of them is closest to God in terms of means: that is, draws near to Him through righteous deeds. It is also possible that it is a substitute for the pronoun in they seek: that is, he seeks the means of means from those who are closest to Him, the Most High, so how about those who are less than Him? It was said that they seek implies the meaning of they are keen: that is, they are keen to see which of them is closest to Him, the Most High, through obedience and worship. And they hope for His mercy as others hope for it. And they fear His punishment as others fear it. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared. An explanation for his saying they fear His punishment: that is, His punishment, the Most High, is worthy of being feared by the servants, from the angels, prophets, and others.
17:58: Then the Almighty explained the outcome of this world and its people, saying: 58- And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection. "In is a negative, and min" is for comprehensiveness: meaning there is no city, meaning a city that was one of the cities of the infidels. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning there is no people of a city but that they will be destroyed, either by death or by a punishment that will eradicate them. So what is meant by the city is its people. It was only said before the Day of Resurrection because the destruction on the Day of Resurrection is not limited to the infidel cities, but rather it includes every city because the life of this world has come to an end. It was also said that the destruction is for the righteous and the torment is for the wicked, and the first is more appropriate because of His saying: "And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers. That mentioned of the destruction and torment was in the Book meaning the Preserved Tablet written" meaning written, and the line is the line and it is originally a source, and the line with the movement is like it. Jarir said: Whoever wants to, I will sell him my money and leave him until the team completes a line in its collection The successor, with the letter kha’ with a damma, is the best of the money. The line is the plural of lines, and the plural of line with a sukoon is lines.
17:59: 59- And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. The commentators said: The people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn Safa into gold for them and to remove the mountains of Mecca from them, so Gabriel came to him and said: If you wish, what your people asked for will happen, but if they do not believe, they will not be given respite, and if you wish, you can wait with them, so God revealed this verse. Meaning: And nothing prevented us from sending the signs they asked for except the denial of the former peoples. If we sent them and these people denied them, they would be hastened and not given respite, as is the way of God Almighty with His servants. So prevention is borrowed from abandonment, and the exception is devoid of the most general of things: that is, we did not abandon sending them for any reason except the denial of the former peoples. If these people denied them as those people denied them due to their sharing in disbelief and stubbornness, what happened to them would happen to them. And the first is in the accusative case due to the prevention being imposed on it, and the second is in the nominative case, and the ba’ in by the signs is redundant. The result is that the obstacle to sending the verses they proposed is that the proposal with denial leads to total destruction, which is extermination. We have resolved to postpone the matter of those to whom Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent until the Day of Resurrection. It was said that the meaning of the verse is that these infidels from Quraysh and others like them are imitators of their fathers, so they will not believe at all, just as those did not believe, so sending the verses will be wasted. Then, the Almighty cited as evidence for what was mentioned the story of Salih and his she-camel. When they suggested to him what they suggested about the she-camel and its description, which has been explained in another place, and God gave them what they suggested, but they did not believe, they were exterminated by punishment. Rather, the people of Salih were singled out for martyrdom because the effects of their destruction in the lands of the Arabs are close to Quraysh and their likes, and their visitors and visitors see it. So He said: And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a sighting sign, meaning one with sight that people perceive with their eyes, like His statement: And We made the sign of the day a sighting sign, or He attributed to it the state of the one who sees it metaphorically, or that He made them possessors of… Sight, and whoever sees him, He makes him see. It is read in the passive form. It is read with the opening of the meem and the sad and its accusative in the state. It was read with the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, and the sentence is connected to something deleted that is required by the context of the speech: that is, they denied it and We gave Thamud the she-camel. The meaning of they wronged it is that they wronged by denying it or by including wronged meaning they denied or disbelieved: that is, they denied it or disbelieved in it unjustly and were not satisfied with mere disbelief or denial. And We do not send the signs except as a warning. There are different interpretations of the verses in various ways: the first is that what is meant by them are the lessons and miracles that God made through the hands of the messengers as signs of warning to frighten the deniers. the second is that they are verses of vengeance to frighten against sins. the third is the change of conditions from childhood to youth then to middle age then to old age so that a person may consider the change of his conditions and fear the consequences of his actions. the fourth is the verses of the Qur’an. the fifth is the terrible death. What is appropriate for the situation is to interpret the aforementioned verses as the suggested verses: that is, We do not send the suggested verses except as a warning of the descent of the punishment, and if they do not fear, it will befall them. The sentence is a resumption and has no syntactic position. It may be in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun they wronged them with it: meaning, they wronged them with it and did not fear. The fact is that We do not send the signs that are part of it except as a warning. Ibn Qutaybah said: We do not send the suggested signs except as a warning of the immediate punishment.
17:60: And when the Almighty mentioned the refusal to send the proposed verses to His Messenger for the aforementioned reason, He strengthened his heart with the promise of victory and supremacy, so He said: 60- And when We said to you, ‘Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people.’ The circumstance is related to something omitted: that is, remember when We said to you: that is, they are in His grip and under His power, so they have no way out of what He wants for them because He encompasses them with His knowledge and power. It was said that what is meant by the people is the people of Mecca, and His encompassing them is His destruction of them: that is, God will destroy them. He used the past tense to indicate that it will happen, as happened on the day of Badr and on the day of the conquest. It was said that what is meant is that the Almighty protected him from the people killing him until he conveyed the message of his Lord. And We did not make the vision which We showed you except a trial for the people. When the Almighty explained that the sending down of the verses includes fear, He added to it the mention of the verse of the Night Journey, which is mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and He called it a vision because it happened at night, or because the infidels They said, Perhaps it was a vision. We have already mentioned at the beginning of the Surah another interpretation of this vision. The trial was the apostasy of a people who had converted to Islam when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them that he had been taken on a night journey. It was also said that it was a dream, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw that he was entering Mecca, so the Muslims were tempted by that. When God conquered Mecca, the Most High’s words were revealed: God has certainly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger in truth. This was followed by saying that this verse is Meccan, and the vision mentioned was in Medina. It was also said that this vision mentioned in this verse is that he saw the Banu Marwan jumping on his pulpit like monkeys, so that upset him. It was said that it was the world that they were given, so he was relieved. This is weak, because there is no trial for the people in this vision, unless what is meant by the people is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone, and what is meant by the trial is what happened of the offense to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or it is understood that he had informed the people of it, so they were tempted. It was said that God, the Almighty, showed him in a dream the place where the Quraysh will be killed, so he said: By God, it is as if I am looking at the place where the people will be killed, and he is pointing to the ground and saying: This is the place where so-and-so will be killed, this is the place where so-and-so will be killed. When the Quraysh heard that, they made his dream a mockery. And the cursed tree in the Qur’an is in apposition to the vision. It was said that there is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: And We did not make the vision that We showed you and the cursed tree in the Qur’an except as a trial for the people. The majority of commentators said that it is the tree of Zaqqum, and what is meant by cursing it is cursing the one who eats it, as God, the Almighty, said: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinful. Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs say that every hated food is cursed, and the meaning of the trial in it is that Abu Jahl and others said: Your companion claimed that the fire of Hell burns stones, then he says that trees grow in it, so God revealed this verse. It was narrated that Abu Jahl ordered a slave girl So he brought dates and butter and said to his companions: Zaqqum. Ibn Az-Zubayri said: May God increase the Zaqqum in your home, for it means dates with butter in the language of Yemen. It was said that the cursed tree is the tree that twists around the tree and kills it, and it is the Kashuth tree. It was also said that it is the devil, and it was said that it is the Jews, and it was said that it is the Umayyads. And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression. That is, We frighten them with signs, but the frightening only increases them in transgression, exceeding the limit and persisting to the utmost extent. The only benefit of sending signs to them is an increase in disbelief. Then We will do to them what We did to the disbelievers before them, which is the punishment of extermination, but We have decreed a delay in the punishment. Abdul Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud regarding his statement: "Say: Call upon those you claim besides Him, for they do not possess the power to remove harm from you, nor to change it." He said: A group of humans used to worship a group of jinn, so the group of jinn converted to Islam and the humans held on to their worship, so God revealed: Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of access to their Lord. Both of them mean the verbs with the letter yaa below it. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud through other chains of narration. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: The polytheists used to worship the angels, the Messiah and Ezra. It was narrated on his authority through another chain of narration with the wording of Jesus, his mother and Ezra. It was also narrated from him from another source with the wording: They are Jesus and Ezra, the sun and the moon. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ask God for me the means of intercession. They said: What is the means of intercession? He said: Closeness to God. Then he recited: They seek the means of intercession to their Lord - which of them is nearest? Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi regarding his statement: That was written in the Book, he said: In the Preserved Tablet. Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated on the authority of Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il, and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The people of Mecca asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn al-Safa into gold for them, and to remove the mountains from them so that they could farm.
