It was said to him: If you wish, you can take your time with them, or if you wish, We will give them what they asked for, but if they disbelieve, they will be destroyed as the nations before them were destroyed. He said: No, I will take my time with them. Then God revealed: And what prevented Us from sending signs? Ahmad and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from another chain of transmission on his authority something similar. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Ad-Dala’il on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas who said: “The people said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘Why don’t you bring us a sign like that brought by Salih and the prophets? ’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If you wish, I will call upon God and He will send it down upon you. If you disobey, you will perish. ’ They said: ‘We do not want it. ’” Ibn Al-Mundhir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We do not send the signs except as a warning, meaning death. Sa’id bin Mansour and Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: It is horrific death. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding His statement, And when We said to you, ‘Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people,’ he said: May God protect you from people. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: They are in His grasp. Abd al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ahmad, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We have not made the vision the verse, he said: It is a vision that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw on the night of his Isra’ to Jerusalem, and it is not a vision in a dream. And the accursed tree in the Qur’an he said: It is the tree of Zaqqum. Abu Saeed, Abu Ya’la and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Umm Hani’ that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on the Isra’, he began to speak to a group of Quraysh who were mocking him. They asked him for a sign, so he described Jerusalem to them and told them the story of the caravan. Al-Walid bin al-Mughirah said: This is a magician. So God revealed to him: And We have not made the vision the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the Banu So-and-so jumping on his pulpit like monkeys, and that upset him, and he could not stop laughing until he died. Then God revealed: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. Ibn Kathir said after citing its chain of transmission: This chain of transmission is very weak, and he mentioned among the men of the chain of transmission Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zaban is abandoned and his sheikh Abdul Muhaimin bin Abbas bin Sahl bin Saad is very weak. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Amr that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw the sons of Al-Hakam bin Abi Al-Aas on the pulpits like monkeys, so God revealed: ‘And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people and the accursed tree’,” meaning Al-Hakam and his son. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ya’la bin Murrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw the Umayyads on the pulpits of the earth and they will rule you and you will find them to be evil masters. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was concerned about that, so God revealed the verse. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Ali something similar to it, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, but it is mursal. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar to it, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, but it is mursal. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said to Marwan bin Al-Hakam: “I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) say to your father and grandfather that you are the cursed tree in the Qur’an.” This is an objection to her saying that he says to your father and grandfather, and perhaps Marwan’s grandfather did not live to see the time of the Prophethood. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) saw that he and his companions entered Mecca, and he was in Medina at that time, so he marched to Mecca before the appointed time, but the polytheists turned him back. Some people said: He has been turned back, and he had told us that he would enter it, so his return was a trial for them. These reasons conflicted and it was not possible to reconcile them, so it is necessary to resort to the most likely, and the most likely, in its abundance and correctness, is that the reason for the revelation of this verse is the story of the Night Journey, so that is necessary. Ibn Kathir narrated the consensus of the narrators of the dream, and in the interpretation of the tree, that it is the tree of Zaqqum, so no consideration should be given to others with them. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Baath narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Abu Jahl said when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned the tree of Zaqqum to frighten them: O people of Quraysh, do you know what the tree of Zaqqum is that Muhammad is frightening you with? They said: No. He said: Ajwa dates of Yathrib with butter. By God, if we get hold of it, we will surely make you vomit it in great quantities. God the Almighty said: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinful, and He revealed: And the accursed tree in the Qur’an the verse. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And the accursed tree, he said: Cursed, because he said: Its fruit is like the heads of devils, and devils are cursed.
17:61: When God the Almighty mentioned that the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in a great affliction from his people and a severe gift, He wanted to show that all the prophets were like that, to the extent that this is an old custom established by the accursed Satan. Also, when He mentioned that those who call upon God seek a means of approach to their Lord, which of them is closest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment, He mentioned here what confirms that, saying: 61- And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam.' This story was mentioned by God the Almighty in seven places: in Al-Baqarah, Al-A'raf, Al-Hijr, this Surah, Al-Kahf, Taha, and Sad. Its explanation has been presented in detail, so let us limit ourselves here to explaining what was not mentioned from the words. His saying, clay is in the accusative case by removing the preposition: meaning from clay, or in the state. Al-Zajjaj said that the meaning is for whom I created clay, and it is in the accusative case in the state.
17:62: 62- Have you seen me meaning tell me about this one whom you have favored over me, why have you favored him? You created me from fire and created him from clay so this was omitted because it was known so that I may seize his offspring meaning that I may take control of them by seducing and misleading. Al-Wahidi said: Its origin is from the locusts' seizing of crops, which means that you uproot it with their seizing and spoiling it. This is the origin, then seizing control of something and taking it all was called seizing it, and it was said that its meaning is: I will drive them wherever I want and lead them wherever I want, from their saying I seized the horse meaning I seized it, meaning I put the reins in its mouth, and the first meaning is more appropriate to the meaning of this verse, and from it is the saying of the poet: I complain to you about a year that has been unfair to us and has shocked us. Our money was seized and changed That is, our wealth has been uprooted. The lam in if you delay it is the prelude. The accursed one swore this oath that he would do to the descendants of Adam what he mentioned because of knowledge that had preceded him from those who had heard him stealthily, or he said it because he thought of the strength of his plot’s influence on the children of Adam, and that it runs through their bloodstreams, and that they are such that his plot is spread among them and his whisperings are carried out among them except for those whom God has protected, and they are the ones meant by His saying: except a few. And in the meaning of this exception is His, the Most High, saying: Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them. What we have mentioned is supported by His, the Most High, saying: And Iblis has certainly fulfilled his assumption about them, for it indicates that he said what he said here based on assumption. It was said that he derived that from the angels’ saying: Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein? It was said that he knew that from the nature of humans because of the desires that were inherent in them, or he thought that because he whispered to Adam, so he accepted that from him and did not find him determined, as was narrated from Al-Hasan.
17:63: 63- He said, ‘Go! And whoever follows you among them’ meaning obeys you then Hell is your recompense meaning Satan and whoever obeys him with a full recompense meaning abundant and complete. It is said: I provided it abundantly, and he provided money by himself, he flees abundantly, so it is abundant, so it is a source, and from it is the saying of Zuhair: Whoever does good without showing it will be rejected, and whoever does not fear insults will be insulted.
17:64: Then the Almighty repeated the respite for the accursed Iblis, saying: 64- And incite with your voice whomever you can among them meaning, disturb and belittle whomever you can from the sons of Adam. It is said that afzahu and istafzahu: meaning, disturb him and belittle him, and the meaning is: incite them with your voice, calling them to disobey God. It was said that it refers to singing, amusement, games, and flutes. And attack them with your cavalry and infantry Al-Farra and Abu Ubaidah said: ajlab is from noise and shouting: meaning, shout at them. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, gather against them all your tricks that you can. So, ijlab is the plural, and the ba in bikhaylik is redundant. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: ijlab means assistance, and khayal refers to horsemen, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O khayal of God, ride and it refers to horses, and rajul with a sukun on the jim is the plural of rajul like tajar and tajar, and sahib and sahab, and Hafs read it with a kasra on the jim as an adjective. Abu Zaid said: It is said, man and man, meaning pedo, so the horse and man are a metaphor for all the tricks of Satan, or what is meant is every rider and footman in disobeying God. And share with them in wealth and children. As for sharing in wealth, it is every disposition of it that contradicts the face of the Shari’ah, whether it is taking it unlawfully, or putting it unlawfully, such as usurpation, theft, and usury. This includes nicking the ears of livestock and making them free and free. Sharing in children is claiming a child without a legitimate reason, and obtaining it through fornication and naming them Abd al-Lat and Abd al-Uzza, and mistreating them in a way that makes them accustomed to evil traits and bad deeds. This includes what they killed of their children for fear of poverty, and burying their daughters alive and making their children follow the religion of disbelief that they are on. This includes sharing in sexual intercourse with Satan if he is not named. Then he said, He promised them. Al-Farra’ said: Tell them there is neither Paradise nor Hell. Al-Zajjaj said: He promised them that they would not be resurrected. And Satan promises them nothing but delusion, meaning falsehood. The origin of delusion is to beautify error with what gives the impression of correctness. It was said that its meaning is: He promised them victory over those who oppose them. These orders from Satan are a form of severe threat and warning. It was said that they are in the manner of belittling him and those who follow him.
17:65: 65- Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority means His believing servants, as in other places in the Noble Book, that the addition of servants to Him means the believers, because of the honor in the addition. It was said that what is meant is all the servants, as evidenced by the exception in His saying in other places, Except for those who follow you of the deviators, and what is meant by authority is domination. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs, they rely on Him, for He is the One who repels the plot of Satan from them and protects them from his seduction. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Iblis said: Adam was created from dust of clay and was created weak, and I was created from fire, and fire burns everything. I will surely seize his offspring except a few. So his assumption about them was confirmed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: I will surely seize his offspring, meaning: I will take control. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid: I will surely seize his offspring, meaning: I will contain them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd who said: I will lead them astray. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: in abundance, meaning: abundantly. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, he said: His voice is every caller who calls to disobey God. And attack them with your cavalry, he said: Every rider in disobedience to God. And your foot soldiers, he said: Every foot soldier in disobedience to God. And share with them in wealth, he said: Every wealth in disobedience to God. And children, he said: Everything they killed of their children and committed in them what was forbidden. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding the verse. He said: Every horse that travels in disobedience to God, and every wealth that was taken unlawfully, and every child of fornication. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse. He said: Wealth is what they used to forbid from their livestock. And children are the children of fornication. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority. He said: Wealth is the free, the free, and the wasilah for other than God. And children were named Abd Al-Harith and Abd Shams.
17:66: His saying: 66- Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you in the sea. Driving: driving, conducting, and directing, and from it is His Almighty saying: Have you not seen that God drives the clouds? And the poet’s saying: O rider, mixing his mount, ask the Banu Asad, what are these pictures? And the other said: Awadha leaves her children behind Meaning: God, the Almighty, moves the ship in the sea by the wind. The ship here is a plural. It was mentioned before, and the sea is a lot of water, whether fresh or salty. This name has become more common than the famous one, that you may seek of His bounty, meaning from His provision that He has bestowed upon His servants, or from the profit in trade. Min is redundant or for partiality. In this verse, there is a reminder to them of the blessings of God, the Almighty, upon them, so that they do not worship other than Him or associate anyone with Him. The phrase, Indeed, He was ever Merciful to you, is an explanation of what was mentioned before, meaning He was ever Merciful to you, so He guided you to your worldly interests.
17:67: 67- And when harm befalls you meaning the fear of drowning in the sea, those you call upon of the gods go astray and leave your thoughts, and there is no relief for you that which you used to call upon besides Him of idols, jinn, angels, or human beings except Him alone, for you place your hope in His mercy and relief, and the exception is disconnected, and the meaning of the verse is that the disbelievers only believe in their idols and all their other deities that they are beneficial to them in a situation other than this one, but in this situation each one of them knows by instinct, a knowledge that he is unable to refute, that idols and the like have no action. But when He delivered you to the land, you turned away from sincerity to God and His Oneness and returned to calling upon your idols and seeking aid from them. And man is ever ungrateful meaning very ungrateful for the blessing of God, and this is an explanation for what preceded, and the meaning is that when hardships occur, they cling to the mercy of God, and when prosperity occurs, they turn away from Him.
17:68: Then He, the Almighty, denounced their ill-treatment of them, saying: 68- Do you then feel secure that He will not cause a part of the land to swallow you up? The hamza is for denial and the fa is for connecting to an omitted word, meaning that you were saved and felt secure, so that made you turn away. So He explained to them that He is able to destroy them on land even if they were saved from the sea. And khasf is when the earth collapses with something. It is said that a well is khasif, meaning its foundation has collapsed. And a khasif spring means its pupil has sunk into the head. And the spring of water is khasf if its water has sunk. And the sun is khasf if it sets from the earth. And the land side is the side of the earth. And He called it a side because it becomes a side after the khasf. Also, the sea is a side of the earth and the land is a side. It was said that they were on the seashore, and its coast is on the land side, so they were safe from the fears of the sea. So what they were safe from on land warned them just as what they feared from the sea warned them, Or He sends upon you a hailstorm. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Qutaibi said: Al-Hasb is the throwing: meaning a strong hailstorm, which throws small pebbles. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Hasb is the dust that has pebbles in it, so the hailstone that has pebbles is like milk and dates. It was said that Al-Hasb is stones from the sky that pelt them as it did with the people of Lot. And the cloud that throws hail is called Hasb, and from this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: We are waiting for the mountains of Sham to hit us with hailstones like scattered cotton wool Then you will not find for yourselves a protector or supporter to protect you from the wrath of God.
17:69: 69- Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time? That is, to the sea once again, by strengthening your motives and providing for your needs to ride it. He used fi and did not say to the sea to indicate that they will settle in it. Then He will send upon you a violent wind. Al-Qasif is a strong wind that breaks violently, from qasaf al-shay' yuqsufhu: meaning he breaks it violently. Qasaf is breaking, or it is the wind that has a qasif: meaning a loud sound from their saying ra'd qasif: meaning a loud sound. Fughrakum. Abu Ja'far, Shaibah, Ruways and Mujahid read fataghrakum with the superscript ta' on the basis that its agent is the wind. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Wardan read Fughrakum with the subscript ta' and the shaddah on the ra'. Abu Ja'far also read al-riyyah. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read with the nun in all of these verbs. The rest read it with the lower yaa in all of them as well, and the baa in bima kafrtum is for causality: that is, because of your disbelief. Then you will not find for yourself against us a follower for it that is, a resentful person demanding what we did. Al-Zajjaj said: You will not find anyone who follows us in denying what has befallen you. Al-Nahhas said: It is from thaar, and this is also said for anyone who seeks revenge or something else, tabi’ and tabi’.
17:70: 70- And We have certainly honored the children of Adam. This is a summary of the blessing that God has bestowed upon the children of Adam: that is, We have honored them all, and this honor includes creating them in this beautiful form and distinguishing them with what He has distinguished them with of food, drink, and clothing in a way that is not found for any other species of animal. Ibn Jarir narrated from a group that this honor is that they eat with their hands, while all other animals eat with their mouths, and this is what An-Nahhas narrated. It was also said that He distinguished them with speech, reason, and discrimination, and it was also said that He honored men with beards and women with forelocks. Ibn Jarir said: He honored them by giving them control over all of creation and subjugating all of creation to them, and it was also said that it was with speech, writing, and understanding, and there is nothing to prevent the honor mentioned in the verse from being applied to all of these things. The greatest of the honorable qualities is the mind, for with it they have control over all other animals, and distinguish between good and bad, and expand in food and drink, and earn money that they use to obtain things that animals cannot obtain, and with it they are able to obtain buildings that protect them from what they fear, and to obtain clothing that protects them from heat and cold. It was said that their honor is that He made Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among them. And We carried them on land and sea. This is a specification of some types of honor. God Almighty carried them on land on beasts, and in the sea on ships. It was said that We carried them in both where We did not cause them to sink or drown. And We provided them with good things. That is, delicious food and drink and everything else that they enjoy and benefit from. And We preferred them over many of those We have created, with [definite] preference. God Almighty summarized this many and did not clarify its types, so this indicates that God Almighty preferred the children of Adam over many of His creations. Some scholars have made many here to mean all, which is an arbitrary and unnecessary statement. Many scholars have been occupied with something that was not needed and not related to benefit, which is the issue of the preference of the angels over the prophets or the prophets over the angels. Among the things that those who prefer the prophets over the angels have held onto is this verse, and it has no indication of what is required because of what is known about the ambiguity of the many and the lack of clarification of it. Fanaticism in this issue is what led some of the Ash'aris to interpret the many here as all so that he would be given preference over the angels. Some of the Mu'tazila held onto this verse to the preference of the angels over the prophets, and it has no indication of that, because there is no evidence that the angels are among the few that are outside this many. Even if we accept that, there is nothing in what is outside this many that indicates that he is better than the sons of Adam. Rather, the most that is in it is that man was not preferred over him, so it is possible that he is equal to man, and it is possible that he is better than him, and with the possibility the evidence is not complete, and the emphasis with his saying: preference indicates the greatness of this preference and that it is in a firm place, so the sons of Adam should receive it with gratitude and beware of denying it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Yazji, that he said: It flows. They narrated on the authority of Qatada, that he said: It makes it move in the sea. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Hasiban, that he said: A rain of stones. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, that he said: Stones from the sky. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Qasifan min al-Rih, that he said: That which drowns. Abu Ubaid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, that he said: The Qaseef and the Asif are in the sea. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Qasifan, that he said: Asif. And regarding the statement of God, Then you will not find for yourselves against Us a follower thereof, that he said: A supporter. Al-Tabarani, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b and Al-Khatib in his history narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Nothing is more honorable to God on the Day of Resurrection than the son of Adam. It was said: O Messenger of God, not even the angels? He said: “Not even the angels. The angels are compelled, just as the sun and the moon are compelled.” Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Amr, with a chain of transmission ending with him. He said: This is the correct view. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha’b on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The believer is more honorable to God than His angels. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Amr that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The angels said: O Lord, You have given the children of Adam the world in which they eat, drink and dress, while we glorify You and do not eat, drink or play. So just as You have given them the world, give us the Hereafter. He said: I will not make the righteous offspring of those I have created with My hands like those to whom I said, ‘Be,’ and they were.” Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam who said: The angels said: The chain of transmission of At-Tabarani is as follows: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sadaqa Al-Baghdadi told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Khalid Al-Masisi told us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad told us, Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Mutraf ibn Salim told us, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it. Ibn Asakir narrated from the path of Urwah ibn Ruwaym, who said: Anas ibn Malik told me, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar to the first hadith of Ibn Amr with an addition. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated something similar in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat from another chain of transmission on the authority of Urwah ibn Ruwaym, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned it. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated from various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We have certainly honored the children of Adam, he said: We made them eat with their hands, while the rest of creation eats with their mouths. Al-Hakim narrated in At-Tarikh and Al-Daylami from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Honor is eating with the fingers.
17:71: His saying: 71- On the Day We call every people with their leader. Al-Zajjaj said: It means the Day of Resurrection, and it is accusative in the meaning of remember the Day We call. It was read calls with the lower yaa in the active construction and is called in the passive construction, and the baa in with their leader is for attachment as you say: I call you by your name, and it is permissible for it to be related to something omitted which is a state, and the estimate is: We call every people wearing their leader, meaning they call and their leader is among them like rode with his soldiers, and the first is more appropriate and the leader in the language is everything that is followed from a prophet or a leader in religion or a book. The commentators differed in identifying the Imam to whom every people will be called. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said that it is the book of every person in which is his deeds, meaning that every person will be called by his book of deeds. This is supported by the statement: But as for him who is given his book 3:10. Ibn Zayd said that the Imam is the book revealed to them, so the people of the Torah will be called by the Torah, the people of the Gospel by the Gospel, and the people of the Qur’an by the Qur’an. It will be said: O people of the Torah, O people of the Gospel, O people of the Qur’an. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Their Imam is their Prophet, so it will be said: Bring the followers of Abraham, bring the followers of Moses, bring the followers of Jesus, bring the followers of Muhammad. Al-Zajjaj said the same. Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: What is meant by the Imam is the Imam of their time, so the people of every time will be called by their Imam whose commands they obeyed and whose prohibitions they refrained from. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: What is meant by their Imam is their deeds, so it will be said, for example: Where are the mujahidin, where are the patient ones, where are the fasting ones, where are the praying ones? And so on. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurairah. Abu Ubaidah said: What is meant by their Imam is the founder of their school of thought. For example, it is said: Where are the followers of the scholar so-and-so, son of so-and-so? This is very far-fetched. Muhammad bin Kaab said: Their Imam is with their mothers, since Imam is the plural of mother like Khuff and Khuff, and this is very far-fetched. It was said that the Imam is every good characteristic that appears in a person, such as knowledge, generosity, and bravery, or bad, such as their opposites. The one who calls for those actions is an inner characteristic, which is like the Imam. Al-Razi mentioned its meaning in his interpretation: So whoever is given his book in his right hand from those who are called, and the mention of the right hand specifically is for honor and good tidings. So those refers to whoever based on its meaning. It was said that the reason for the plural is to indicate that they are gathered for a great matter, or to indicate that their reading of their books is in a group and not individually. They read their book which they were given. And they will not be wronged a thread meaning that they will not be deducted from their rewards by the amount of a thread, which is the shell in the slit of the seed, or it is an expression for the least amount.
17:72: He did not mention the people of the left explicitly, but He, the Almighty, mentioned what indicates their ugly state, saying: 72- And whoever is blind in this world meaning whoever is among those called in this world is blind: meaning he lacks insight. Al-Naysaburi said: There is no disagreement that what is meant by this blindness is blindness of the heart. As for His statement: He is blind in the Hereafter, it is possible that it is meant blindness of sight, like His statement: "And We will gather him blind on the Day of Resurrection. He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind while I was seeing?" And in this there is an increase in punishment. It is possible that what is meant is blindness of the heart. It was said that what is meant by the Hereafter is the work of the Hereafter: meaning he is blind in work, or in the matter of the Hereafter. It was said that what is meant by the one who is blind to the blessings that God bestowed upon him in this world is blind to the blessings of the Hereafter. It was said that whoever is blind in the world in which repentance is accepted is blind in the Hereafter in which there is no repentance. It was said that whoever is blind to the proofs of God in this world is blind in the Hereafter. It has been said that his saying: So he will be blind in the Hereafter is a comparative adjective: meaning more blind. This is based on the fact that it is from blindness of the heart, as that is not said about blindness of the eye. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: Because He created it in the position of the hand and the foot, so it is not said what blinded him, just as it is not said what supported him. Al-Akhfash said: That is not said about it because it has more letters. Al-Farra’ narrated on the authority of some Arabs that he heard him say what blackened his hair, and from that is the saying of the poet: As for the kings, you are today the meanest of them all and the whitest of them is the cook’s robe. The research is complete in grammar. Abu Bakr, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Khalaf read blind with imala in both places, and Abu Amr, Ya’qub and the rest read them without imala. Abu Ubaid made the first inflected but not the second, and he is more astray than the blind man, meaning that the latter is more astray than the blind man because he cannot find a way to guidance, unlike the blind man who may be guided in some situations.
17:73: Then when He, the Most High, enumerated in the previous verses the types of blessings bestowed upon the children of Adam, He followed it with what runs the course of warning against being deceived by the whispers of the wretched, saying: 73- And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you “in” is the lightened form of the heavy form, and its subject is a deleted pronoun of matter, and the lam is the distinguishing feature between it and the negative, and the meaning is: Indeed, the matter is that they almost deceived you, tempting you. The origin of temptation is testing, and from it the goldsmith tempted gold, then it was used for anyone who removed something from its limit and direction, and that is because in giving them what they asked for there is a violation of the ruling of the Qur’an and a slander against God, the Most High, by changing the promise to a threat and other things about that which We revealed to you of the commands and prohibitions and the promise and threat so that you might invent something else about Us so that you might say something about Us other than that which We revealed to you from what the infidels of Quraysh suggested to you and then they would have taken you as a friend meaning if you had followed their desires they would have taken you as a friend To them: meaning, your guardian and your friend, taken from the word khalla with the letter kha open.
17:74: 74- And had We not established you on the truth and protected you from agreeing with them, you would have almost inclined towards them you would have come close to inclining towards them the slightest inclination, and inclination is a slight inclination, and for this reason he said: a little but infallibility overtook him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and prevented him from approaching the lowest levels of inclination towards them, let alone inclination itself, and this is evidence that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not intend to answer them, its meaning was mentioned by Al-Qushayri and others, and it was said that the meaning is: And they almost reported about you that you inclined towards their saying, so their action was attributed to him metaphorically and broadly, as you say to a man: You almost killed yourself: meaning people almost killed you because of what you did, its meaning was mentioned by Al-Mahdawi.
17:75: Then He, the Most High, threatened him with the most severe threat in that regard, saying: 75- Then We would have made you taste double the punishment in life and double the punishment in death, meaning if you were to come close to inclining towards them, meaning twice as much as others who do this action are punished with in both worlds. The meaning is: double the punishment in life and double the punishment in death: meaning doubled. Then the described was deleted and the adjective was used in its place and added, because the mistake of the great one is great, as He, the Most High, said: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her twofold. The double of something is its twofold, and the double may be the share, as in His saying: For each is double, meaning a share. Al-Razi said: The gist of the matter is that if you let the thoughts of Satan enter your heart and made your concern to be content, you would deserve to have your punishment doubled in this world and the next, and your punishment would be twice as great as the punishment of the polytheist in this world and twice as great as his punishment in the next world. Then you will not find for yourself against Us a helper who would help you and ward off this punishment from you. Al-Naysaburi said: Know that being close to a trial does not indicate falling into it, and being threatened with disobedience does not indicate committing it, so the verse does not necessarily imply a challenge to infallibility.
17:76: 76- And they almost provoked you The discussion of this is like the discussion of And they almost tempted you: meaning that the matter is that they almost disturbed you from the land of Mecca so that you would leave it, but they did not do that, rather God prevented them from it until he migrated by the command of his Lord and after they intended to do so, and it was said that he used the expulsion to mean expulsion as a permissibility. And then they will not remain behind you except a little is conjoined with to provoke you: meaning they will not remain after your expulsion except for a short time. Then they were punished with a punishment that would eradicate them all. Ata' ibn Abi Rabah read La yalbathu with a shaddah on the unified ba. It was read La yalbathu in the accusative case, acting on the fact that the sentence is conjoined with the sentence And they almost and not just the report. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, and Abu Amr read Khalafak and its meaning is after you. Ibn Amir, Hafs, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read Khilafak and its meaning is also after you. Ibn al-Anbari said: Khilafak means your opposition. Abu Hatim chose the second reading for his saying: Those who stayed behind rejoiced at their sitting in opposition to the Messenger of God. What indicates that Khilaf means after is the poet’s saying: The houses were covered with dirt, as if the sand dunes had been spread out between them as a mat. It is said that a woman split the palm frond to make a mat. Abu Ubaidah said: Then the splitter throws it to the mat.
17:77: 77- The way of those of Our messengers We sent before you Sunnah is in the accusative case as a source: meaning, God's way is a way. Al-Farra' said: meaning, they are punished as is the way of those We sent, so when the preposition was dropped, the verb worked. It was said that the meaning is: Our way is the way of those We sent. Al-Zajjaj said: He says that our way is the way of those to whom We sent before you, that if they expel their prophet from among them or kill him, the punishment will be brought down upon them. And you will not find any change in Our way meaning, what God has established as a habit, no one has been able to change it or is able to alter it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: On the Day We will call every people with their leader, he said: An leader of guidance and an leader of misguidance. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Khatib in his history narrated on the authority of Anas regarding the verse: Their prophet. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid similarly. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: With their book of deeds. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali regarding the verse: Every people will be called with the leader of their time, the book of their Lord and the Sunnah of their prophet. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and classified it as hasan, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim narrated it and classified it as saheeh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: On the Day when We will call every people with their leader, he said: “One of them will be called and given his book in his right hand, and his body will be stretched out to sixty cubits, his face will be whitened, and a crown of shining pearls will be placed on his head. He will go to his companions and they will see him from afar and say: O God, bring this to us and bless us in this, until he comes to them and says: Rejoice, for every man among you will have something like this. As for the disbeliever, his face will be blackened and his body will be stretched out to sixty cubits in the image of Adam, and he will wear a crown. His companions will see him and say: We seek refuge in God from the evil of this, O God, do not bring this to us. He said: So he will come to them and they will say: O God, disgrace him. He will say: May God distance you, for every man among you has something like this.” Al-Bazzar said after reporting it: It is not narrated except through this chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And whoever is blind in this world meaning whoever is blind in this world to what he sees of My power of creating the heavens, the earth, the mountains, the seas, the people, the beasts and the like he is from what I have described to him in the Hereafter and he did not see it blind and further astray meaning the furthest proof. Al-Firyabi and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on his authority something similar to this. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority saying whoever is blind to the power of God in this world is blind in the Hereafter. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority saying: “Umayyah bin Khalaf and Abu Jahl bin Hisham and men from Quraysh came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Come and anoint our gods and we will enter your religion with you. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was hard pressed by separation from his people and he loved their Islam so he felt sorry for them, so God revealed: “And they almost tempted you” until His saying: a supporter. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Yadhan on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was touching the Black Stone, and they said: We will not let you touch it until you touch it with our gods. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What would I have to do if I did, and God knows otherwise? Then God revealed: ‘And they almost tempted you’ verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Shihab. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Jubair bin Nufayr: “The Quraysh came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: If you have been sent to us, then expel those who followed you from the scum of the people and their clients so that we may be your companions. So he leaned towards them, and God revealed to him: ‘And they almost tempted you’ verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi who said: God revealed: “And the star when it goes down,” so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to them this verse: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? Then Satan suggested to him: Those are the exalted cranes, and where is their intercession that you may hope for? So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the rest of the surah and prostrated, then God revealed: And they almost tempted you away from that which We have revealed to you, the verse. He remained worried and distressed until God revealed: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he desired, the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “Thaqeef said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We have been given a year until what is being given to our gods is given, and when we take what is given to the gods, we will preserve it, then we will submit and defeat the gods, so they thought that they would be given a reprieve, so the verse: “And they almost tempted you,” the verse was revealed.” Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: The double of life and the double of death, meaning the double of the torment of this world and the hereafter. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding the verse, he said: It is the torment of the grave. He also narrated on the authority of Ata’ something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: The polytheists said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The prophets used to live in Ash-Sham, so what about Madinah? He thought about leaving, but God revealed: And they almost drove you away from the land Al-Bayhaqi 2:17. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Hadrami that he heard that some of the Jews mentioned something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala'il, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ghanem that the Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: If you are a prophet, then head to Ash-Sham, for Ash-Sham is the land of the gathering and the land of the prophets. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, believed what they said, so he set out for the Battle of Tabuk, intending nothing but Ash-Sham. When he reached Tabuk, God revealed to him verses from Surat Bani Israel after the surah had ended: And they almost incited you until His saying: A transfer. Then He ordered him to return to Madinah, and He said: In it is your life, and in it is your death, and from it you will be resurrected. Gabriel said to him: Ask your Lord, for every prophet has a question. He said: What do you command me to ask? He said: “Say: My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and let me exit a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.” So these were revealed to him on his return from Tabuk. Ibn Kathir said: There is some doubt about this chain of transmission, and it appears that it is not authentic, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not invade Tabuk because of what the Jews said, but rather he invaded it in compliance with the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you. He invaded it to exact retribution and take vengeance on those of his companions who killed the people of Mu’tah. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And they almost drove you away from the land, that they were the people of Makkah because they expelled the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from Makkah, and they did so after that, so God destroyed them on the Day of Badr, and they did not remain after that except for a short time until God destroyed them on the Day of Badr. This was the way of God with the Messengers when their people did something similar to them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And then they will not remain behind you except for a short time, that he said: By a short time he meant the day they were captured at Badr, so that was the short time they remained after that.
17:78: When God Almighty mentioned the divine, the afterlife, and the reward, He followed it up with mentioning the most honorable of acts of obedience, which is prayer, saying: 78- Establish prayer at the decline of the sun. The commentators have agreed that this verse includes the obligatory prayers. Scholars have differed about the decline mentioned in this verse into two opinions: One of them is that it is the sun’s demise from the middle of the sky, as stated by Omar and his son, Abu Hurairah, Abu Barzah, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Al-Sha’bi, Ata’, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Abu Ja’far Al-Baqir, and Ibn Jarir chose it. The second opinion is that it is the sunset, as stated by Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, and Ubayy ibn Ka’b, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Al-Farra’ said: The decline of the sun is from its decline until its setting. Al-Azhari said: The meaning of decline in the speech of the Arabs is the zenith, and that is why the sun is called Dalika when it declines in the middle of the day, and it is called Dalika when it sets, because in both cases it is declining. He said: The opinion in my opinion is that it is its decline in the middle of the day so that the verse includes the five prayers, and the meaning is: Establish prayer from the time of the sun’s decline until the darkness of the night, so it includes the noon and afternoon prayers and the two prayers of the darkness of the night, which are the two evening prayers, then he said and the Qur’an of Fajr, these are five prayers. Abu Ubaid said: Its setting is its sunset, and its setting is its setting: meaning al-Shams 91:that is, it set, and Qatrib recited on this the words of the poet: This is the place where Rabah's feet crawled until they were rubbed in the open space A name for the sun, similar to Hizam and Qatam. From this, Dhu al-Rummah said: Lamps that are not led by stars nor by the setting sun That is, the setting sun, and the dusk of the night is the gathering of darkness. Al-Farra and Al-Zajjaj said: It is said that the night has become dusk and has become dark: if it comes with its darkness. Abu Ubaid said: Dusk is the blackness of the night. Qais bin Al-Ruqayyat said: This night has darkened and worries and insomnia have subsided It was said that the dusk of the night is the disappearance of twilight, and from this is the saying of Zuhair: Her hands kept giving generously, while she was distracted, until darkness and dusk came. The root of the word is from the word sailan to flow, it is said: ghasqat if it flowed. Al-Farra’ narrated the words ghasaq al-layl and aghsaq, dhalam and adhlam, daja and adja and ghabash and aghbash. This purpose, I mean his saying: until the ghasaq al-layl, was used as evidence by those who said that the time for the noon prayer lasts from noon until sunset. This was narrated from Al-Awza’i and Abu Hanifa, and Malik and Al-Shafi’i permitted it in cases of necessity. There are authentic and continuous hadiths from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifying the times of prayers, so the general meaning of this verse must be understood according to what is explained by the Sunnah, so we will not prolong mentioning that. His saying: And the recitation of dawn is the accusative of quran because it is conjoined with the prayer: meaning, And establish the recitation of dawn, as Al-Farra’ said. Al-Zajjaj and the Basrans said: Its accusative is for enticement: meaning, you must recite the recitation of dawn. The commentators said: What is meant by the recitation of dawn is the dawn prayer. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a great benefit that indicates that prayer is not complete without recitation, so much so that prayer is called the Qur’an. The authentic hadiths indicate that there is no prayer without the Opening of the Book, and in some hadiths that have a good chain of transmission, the Qur’an is with it. What was mentioned indicates the obligation of the Opening of the Book in every rak’ah, and I have written it down in my books in a good manner. Then the Almighty explained that by saying: Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed, meaning that it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day, as was mentioned in the authentic hadith, and the majority of commentators said that.
17:79: 79- And during the night, then pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Min is for partiality, and its accusative is for circumstance with an implied word: meaning, get up some of the night and pray with it. The genitive pronoun refers to the Qur’an and what was said about it being accusative for enticement, and the estimation is upon you some of the night, so it is very far, and tahajjud is taken from hijood. Abu Ubaidah and Ibn al-A'rabi said: It is from the opposites, because it is said that a man hijood if he slept, and hijood if he stayed up late. Among its usage for staying up late is the saying of the poet: Did she not visit and the people of Mina are sleepless? I wish her shadow would return to Mina. It means alert, and another saying about its use in sleep: Did you not knock on our door while our companions were asleep? So, the burdens of generosity became more generous. Meaning asleep. Al-Azhari said: The origin of the word hajood is sleeping at night, but the verb ta’athim came to mean avoiding, and from it the verb ta’athim and taharraj means avoiding sin and embarrassment. So the one who prays at night is the one who avoids the hajood, so he gets up at night. It was also narrated from Al-Azhari that he said: The one who prays at night is the one who gets up to pray after sleeping. This is what Al-Wahidi narrated from him, so he restricted the tahajjud to getting up from sleep. This is what Mujahid, Alqamah and Al-Aswad said, and they said: Tahajjud after sleeping. Al-Layth said: “Pray at night when you wake up for prayer, ‘a voluntary prayer for you.’ The meaning of voluntary prayer in the language is an addition to the original. The meaning is that it was a voluntary prayer for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in addition to the obligatory prayers. Although the command to pray at night appears to be obligatory, the explicit statement that it is a voluntary prayer is a clear indication of the command. It was said that what is meant by voluntary prayer here is that it is an obligatory prayer in addition to the five obligatory prayers for him, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is refuted by the explicit statement of voluntary prayer. It was said that the night prayer was obligatory for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, then the obligation was abrogated and the night prayer became voluntary. Based on this, what was mentioned in the hadith is understood that it was obligatory for him, and voluntary for his nation. Al-Wahidi said: The night prayer was an addition for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically to raise his status, not for expiation, because he was forgiven for his sins, past and future. We do not have a voluntary prayer because of the abundance of our sins, we only work to expiate them. He said: This is the saying of all the commentators. The conclusion is that although the address in this verse is specific to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in his saying, “Establish prayer,” the command to him is a command to his nation, so it is a general law. This includes the encouragement to pray at night, as it includes the entire nation, and the explicit statement that it is a voluntary prayer indicates that it is not obligatory, as praying at night is recommended and prescribed for every accountable person. Then the Almighty promised him to perform the obligatory and voluntary prayers, saying: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station. We have mentioned in several places that perhaps from the Generous indicates the desires that must occur, and the accusative of a station is in the circumstance by implying a verb, or by including the resurrection with the meaning of residence. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case: that is, He will raise you to a praised station, and the meaning of the station being praised is that everyone who knows about it will praise it. There are different opinions about specifying this station: The first is that it is the station that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will stand to intercede for people on the Day of Resurrection so that their Lord, glory be to Him, may relieve them of what they are in. This opinion is what is indicated by the authentic evidence in the interpretation of the verse, and Ibn Jarir reported it from most of the people of interpretation. Al-Wahidi said: The consensus of the commentators is that the station of praise is the station of intercession. The second opinion: The station of praise is giving the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection. It can be said that this does not contradict the first opinion, as there is no contradiction between him standing in the place of intercession and holding the banner of praise. The third opinion: The station of praise is that God, glory be to Him, will seat Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with Him on His Throne. Ibn Jarir reported it from a group including Mujahid, and a hadeeth has been narrated about this. Al-Naqqash reported from Abu Dawud al-Sijistani that he said: Whoever denies this hadeeth is accused in our view. The people of knowledge continue to speak about this hadeeth. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: Even though Mujahid was one of the imams in interpretation, he has two opinions that are abandoned by the people of knowledge: one of them is this, and the second is in the interpretation of Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. He said: Its meaning is awaiting the reward, and it is not from looking. End quote. In any case, this opinion does not contradict the first opinion because it is possible that God, the Most High, will seat him in this seat and intercede with that intercession. The fourth opinion: It is absolute in every position that brings praise from the types of miracles. This was mentioned by the author of al-Kashshaf and those who follow him in interpretation. The response to this is that the authentic hadiths that were reported specifying this praiseworthy position are numerous, so the destination is determined, and there is no generality in the wording in the verse so that it can be said: The consideration is in the generality of the wording, not in the specificity of the reason. The meaning of his saying, And it is absolute in everything that brings praise, is that it is general in everything that is like that, but he expresses the general with the wording of the absolute, as he mentioned in the slaughter of the cow, and this is why he said here. It was said that what is meant is intercession, and it is one type of what the wording of the position includes. The difference between alternative generality and comprehensive generality is well-known, so we will not elaborate on it.
17:80: 80- "And say, 'My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and exit a truthful exit.' The majority of scholars read a truthful entrance and a truthful exit" with a damma on the two meems. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Nasr bin Asim read them with a fatha on them. They are two sources meaning entering and exiting. The addition to truth is for the sake of exaggeration, such as Hatim Al-Joud: meaning an entrance that deserves to be called an entrance, and in which there is nothing disliked. Al-Wahidi said: Adding them to truth is praise for them, and everything you add to truth is praise. The commentators differed on the meaning of the verse. It was said that it was revealed when he ordered the migration, meaning to enter Medina and to leave Mecca, and Ibn Jarir chose it. It was said that the meaning is: Cause me to die a death of truth and resurrect me on the Day of Resurrection as a source of truth. It was said that the meaning is: Cause me to enter what you have commanded me to do, and to leave what you have forbidden me to do. It was said that he was to enter a place of security and to leave him among the polytheists, and it is like the first statement. It was said that what is meant is to enter with honor and to leave with victory. It was said that the meaning is: Cause me to enter the grave at death with an entrance of truth, and to leave it at resurrection with an exit of truth. It was said that he was to enter me wherever you entered me with truth and to leave me with truth. It was said that the verse is general in all matters it includes, so it is a supplication, and its meaning is: O Lord, rectify my return in all matters and my outward appearance from them, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority, meaning a clear, overwhelming argument with which You grant me victory over all those who oppose me. It was said that he was to grant me from Yourself a kingdom and strong honor, as if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that he would not be able to do this matter without an authority, so he asked for an authority. A supporter. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Ibn Kathir said: It is the most likely, because with the truth there must be subjugation of those who oppose and oppose it. That is why God the Almighty says: “Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that people may maintain justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is mighty force and benefits for people, and that God may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen.” And in the hadith: Indeed, God restrains by authority what He does not restrain by the Qur’an. That is, He prevents by authority from committing indecencies and sins what He does not prevent many people by the Qur’an, and what is in it of strong warning and severe intimidation. And this is the reality. End quote.
17:81: 81- And say, 'The truth has come, and falsehood has perished.' What is meant by truth is Islam, and it was said the Qur'an, and it was said jihad. There is nothing wrong with interpreting the verse to mean all of that and to what is true, whatever it may be. What is meant by falsehood is polytheism, and it was said the devil. It is not far-fetched to interpret it to mean everything that is opposite to the truth, without differentiating between falsehood and falsehood. The meaning of perished is nullified and vanished. From this comes the vanishing of the soul, which is its nullification. Indeed, falsehood is bound to perish. That is, this is its nature, so it becomes nullified and does not remain, while the truth is always established.
17:82: 82- And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers. The majority read We send down with a noon. Abu Amr read it with a light pronunciation. Mujahid read it with a lower yaa and a light pronunciation. Al-Marwazi narrated it from Hafs. Min is for the beginning of the goal. It is correct that it is for clarifying the type. It was said that it is for partialization, but some commentators rejected it because it implies that some of it is not healing. Ibn Atiyyah rejected it by saying that the part is its revelation. Scholars differed on the meaning of it being a cure, with two opinions: The first is that it is a cure for the hearts by removing ignorance from them, dispelling doubt, and uncovering the matters that point to God, the Most High. The second opinion is that it is a cure for apparent diseases through incantations, seeking refuge, and the like. There is nothing to prevent the cure from being applied to both meanings based on the generality of the metaphor, or based on the common meaning being applied to both meanings. Then, the Almighty mentioned that it is a mercy for the believers because of the beneficial knowledge it contains, which includes what is good for religion and the world, and because of the great reward in reciting and contemplating it, which is a cause for the mercy, forgiveness, and pleasure of God, the Almighty. An example of this verse is the Almighty’s saying: “Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guide and a cure. But as for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is, upon them, blindness.’” Then, when the Almighty mentioned what is in the Qur’an of benefit for His believing servants, He mentioned what is in it of harm for those other than them, saying: And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss. That is, the Qur’an, as a whole or some of it, does not increase the wrongdoers who put denial in place of belief, and doubt and suspicion in place of certainty and reassurance, except in loss, meaning destruction, because listening to the Qur’an angers them and enrages them and calls them to increase the commission of shameful acts out of rebellion and stubbornness, and at that point they perish. It was said that loss is a decrease, like His saying: So it increased them in filth upon their filth.
17:83: Then the Almighty pointed out the opening of some of the blameworthy natures that man was created with, saying: 83- And when We bestow favor upon man, meaning upon this species, with blessings that require gratitude, such as health and wealth, he turns away from thanking God and remembering Him, and distances himself. Distance means distance, and the letter ba’ is for transitivity or companionship, and it is an emphasis on turning away, because turning away from something means turning one’s face toward it, meaning its side, and distancing oneself means turning one’s back on it. It is not far-fetched that what is meant by turning away here is turning away from the supplication and entreaty that he used to do when a calamity and trial befell him, and what is meant by distancing oneself is arrogance and distancing oneself from fulfilling the rights of blessings. Ibn ‘Amir read in the narration of Ibn Dhakwan and Abu Ja’far na’a like ba’a with delaying the hamza to the heart, and Hamza read na’ai with inclination of the two fathahs, and al-Kisa’i agreed with him, and Shu’bah and al-Susi inclined the hamza only. The rest read with the fat-ha in both of them: And when evil touches him from sickness or poverty he is hopeless very hopeless of God’s mercy. The meaning is that if he wins the worldly desire and attains the goal, he forgets the worshipped one, and if he misses something of that, regret takes hold of him and despair overcomes him. Both of these characteristics are ugly and reprehensible. What is in this verse does not contradict the statement of God Almighty: And when evil touches him, he is one of abundant supplication and its likes, for that is the case of some of them other than the some mentioned in this verse. It is not far-fetched to say that there is no contradiction between the two verses, for it may be that despite his intense despair and frequent hopelessness, he supplicates a lot with his tongue.
17:84: 84- "Say: Each one acts according to his own nature." Al-Shaklah, Al-Farra' said: The method, and it was said the side, and it was said the nature, and it was said the religion, and it was said the intention, and it was said the nature, and it was taken from the shape, it is said I am not according to my shape nor according to my nature, and the shape: is the example and the counterpart. The meaning: that each person acts according to what resembles the morals that he is accustomed to, and this is a condemnation of the disbeliever and praise of the believer. So your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided in the way, because He is your Creator, the Knower of the natures that you were created with and the ways in which you differ, so He is the One who distinguishes between the believer who does not show off when he is blessed and does not despair when he is tested, and the disbeliever whose habit is to be arrogant when blessed and despair when he is afflicted.
17:85: Then when the speech was completed to mentioning man and what he was created with, the Almighty mentioned the question of the questioners to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the soul, so He said: 85- And they ask you about the soul. People have differed about the soul that is being asked about, so it was said that it is the soul that manages the body and through which its life is formed, and this is what most of the commentators said. Al-Farra’ said: The spirit by which man lives, God Almighty did not inform any of His creation about it, and He did not give knowledge of it to any of His servants, so He said: “Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord,” meaning that you do not know it. It was said that the spirit that is asked about is Gabriel, and it was said that it is Jesus, and it was said that it is the Qur’an, and it was said that it is an angel of great creation, and it was said that it was created like the creation of the sons of Adam, and it was said that there is no benefit or advantage in mentioning it, and the first statement is apparent, and the reason for the revelation of this verse will be mentioned, and the explanation of those who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the spirit, then it is apparent that the question is about the reality of the spirit, because knowing the reality of a thing is more important and older than knowing one of its states, then He, Almighty, commanded him to answer those who asked him about the spirit, so He said: “Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord,” from is explanatory, and the matter is the matter and the addition is for exclusivity, meaning that it is from the same type of things that God has kept to Himself of which He did not teach His servants, and it was said that the meaning of from the command of my Lord is from His revelation and His speech, not from the speech of humans, and in this verse there is what He rebukes those who delve into the matter of the soul and who are pretentious in explaining its form and clarifying its reality with the most eloquent rebuke and deters them with the greatest deterrent. They have prolonged the discussion of this research to a point that is not sufficient for the purpose, and most of it, or rather all of it, is superfluous information that does not bring any benefit in religion or this world. Some investigators have reported that the statements of those who differed about the soul reached eighteen hundred statements. Look at this empty curiosity and useless effort, after they knew that God, the Exalted, has kept His knowledge to Himself and has not informed His prophets about it nor permitted them to ask about it or search for its truth, let alone their nations who follow their example. Oh, how amazing it is that the statements of the curious have reached this level that they have not reached, not even part of it, in any other issue that God has permitted speaking about and has not kept His knowledge to Himself. Then God, the Exalted, concluded this verse by saying, And you have been given only a little knowledge, meaning that your knowledge that God has taught you is only a small amount compared to the knowledge of the Creator, the Exalted, even if He has been given a great portion of knowledge. Rather, the knowledge of the prophets, peace be upon them, is not compared to the knowledge of God, the Exalted, except as a bird takes from the sea in its beak, as in the hadith of Moses and Al-Khidr, peace be upon them. Abdul Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: The sun’s decline means its setting. The Arabs say when the sun sets: The sun has declined. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali who said: Its decline means its setting. Abdul Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The sun’s decline means the sun’s zenith. Al-Bazzar, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘The sun’s decline means its zenith.’” Al-Suyuti declared its chain of transmission weak. Malik narrated it in Al-Muwatta’, Abdul Razzaq, Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Umar from his statement. Abdul Razzaq narrated on his authority who said: The sun’s decline is its setting after noon. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Its decline is its zenith. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: at the decline of the sun, he said: When the shadow has settled. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Mas’ud and Uqbah ibn Amr, they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Gabriel came to me at the decline of the sun when it had passed its zenith, and he prayed the noon prayer with me. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Barzah Al-Aslami, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer when the sun had passed its zenith, then he recited: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Anas. What is used as evidence that the decline of the sun is the middle of the day is what Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Jabir, he said: “I invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and whoever of his companions wanted to eat with me, then they went out when the sun had passed its zenith, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and said: Go out, O Abu Bakr, for this is when the sun has declined.” In its chain of transmission is an unknown man, but he narrated it on his authority through another chain of transmission on the authority of Sahl ibn Bakkar on the authority of Abu ‘Awanah on the authority of Al-Aswad ibn Qays on the authority of Nabih Al-‘Anbari on the authority of Jabir, so he mentioned something similar with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: Until the darkness of the night, he said: Until the last evening prayer. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The darkness of the night is the gathering of the night and its darkness. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: The darkness of the night is the beginning of the night. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The decline of the sun is when the sun passes its zenith, and the darkness of the night is the setting of the sun. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn, he said: The dawn prayer. Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding his statement: “And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed.” He said: The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it, they gather in it. It is in the two Sahihs from him, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, with the wording: The angels of the night and the angels of the day gather in the Fajr prayer. Then Abu Hurairah says: Recite if you wish, “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed.” Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Tabarani narrated from Ibn Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed. He said: The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: A voluntary act for you, meaning specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he was commanded to perform the night prayer and it was prescribed for him. At-Tabarani narrated in al-Awsat and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan from Aisha that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Three things are obligatory upon me and they are Sunnah for you: Witr, the siwak, and the night prayer.” Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah regarding his statement: A supererogatory prayer for you, he said: It was a supererogatory prayer for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a virtue for you. In another version: The supererogatory prayer was only for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station, and he was asked about it. He said: It is the praised station in which I will intercede for my Ummah. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ka’b ibn Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people will be raised on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my Ummah will be on a hill, and my Lord will clothe me in a green garment. Then I will be given permission to say whatever God wills me to say, and that will be the praised station.” Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “Every nation on the Day of Resurrection will follow its prophet, saying: ‘O so-and-so, intercede! O so-and-so, intercede!’ until intercession ends with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). On that day, God will raise him to a praiseworthy station.” And a similar hadith was narrated on his authority, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). There are many hadiths on this subject, which are authentic in the two Sahihs and elsewhere, so we will not prolong their mention. Whoever seeks to complete the details will look at the hadiths on intercession in the Ummah and elsewhere. At-Tabarani narrated regarding the statement: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station, that he will seat him between Himself and Gabriel and intercede for his nation, that is the praiseworthy station. Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station. He said: He will seat me with him on the Throne. The chain of transmission of these two hadiths should be investigated.
