Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym, Al-Bayhaqi and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in Mecca and then he was commanded to emigrate, so God revealed: And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and an exit a truthful exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.’ Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse: And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter’ that he said: God brought him out of Mecca a truthful exit and entered Medina a truthful entrance. He said: The Prophet of God knew that he would not be able to do this without a ruler, so he asked for a ruler who would support the Book of God, its limits and its obligations, and to establish the Book of God, because the ruler is a glory from God that He has placed among His servants, and were it not for that, some of them would raid others, and the strong among them would devour the weak. Al-Khatib narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab who said: By God, what God restrains with rulers is greater than what He restrains with the Qur’an. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Mecca and there were three hundred and sixty idols around the Ka`bah. He began to poke them with a stick in his hand and say: ‘The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Falsehood is bound to vanish.’ ‘The truth has come, and falsehood can neither begin nor bring back.’” There are hadiths on this topic. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And he distanced himself he said: He distanced himself. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He was despairing he said: Despairing. Regarding his statement: Everyone acts according to his nature he said: According to his side. Hannad and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Hasan who said: According to his nature, according to his intention. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: “I was walking with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the ruins of Medina, and he was leaning on a palm branch. He passed by some Jews, and some of them said to each other: Ask him about the soul. Some of them said: Do not ask him. They said: O Muhammad, what is the soul? He kept leaning on the palm branch, and I thought that revelation was being sent to him. He said: ‘And they ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is from the command of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.’” Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Quraysh said to the Jews: Give us something so we can ask this man. They said: Ask him about the soul. So the following was revealed: “They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is from the command of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.” They said: We have been given much knowledge. We have been given the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good. So God revealed: “Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.” There are hadiths and reports on this topic.
17:86: When He, the Almighty, made clear that He did not give them of knowledge except a little, He made clear that if He had willed to take this little from them, He would have done so, so He said: 86- And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you. The lam is the preamble, and We will surely take away is the answer to the oath and takes the place of the answer to the condition. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that if We willed, We could erase it from the hearts and from the books until no trace of it remains. End. He referred to the Qur’an with the relative pronoun to magnify its status. Then you will not find for yourself concerning it meaning the Qur’an against Us a protector meaning you will not find anyone who will rely on Us to return any of it after We have taken it away.
17:87: And the exception in His saying: 87- Except for the mercy of your Lord if it is connected then its meaning is unless your Lord has mercy on you, so we will not take him away, and if it is disconnected then its meaning is but He does not will that out of mercy from your Lord, or but the mercy of your Lord left him not taken away Indeed, His favor upon you was great as He made you a messenger and sent down the Book to you and made you the master of the children of Adam, and gave you the praised station and other than that which He bestowed upon him.
17:88: Then the Almighty argued with the polytheists with the miracle of the Qur’an, saying: 88- Say, ‘If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur’an’ revealed from God, described with the sublime attributes of perfect eloquence, beautiful composition, and eloquent expression, they could not produce the like of it. He made it clear in the context of the omission, and did not suffice to say they could not produce it, as the pronoun refers to the mentioned example, to dispel the notion that it has a specific example, and to indicate that what is meant is the negation of the example in any way, and it is the answer to an omitted oath as indicated by the preambulating lam, and it prevailed in the place of the answer to the condition, then the Almighty clarified their inability to oppose, whether the one who confronts it is each one of them individually, or the one who takes the lead with it is the group by support, so He said, And if some of them were to each other a backer, meaning a helper and supporter, and the answer to if is omitted, and the meaning is: And if some of them were to each other a backer, they would not produce the like of it, so it is proven that they would not produce the like of it on In any case, the miracle of the Qur’an was mentioned in the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. In this verse, there is a response to what the infidels said, If we had willed, we could have said the like of this, and a lie against them.
17:89: Then the Almighty explained that the disbelievers, despite their inability to oppose, continued in their disbelief and lack of faith, saying: 89- And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an every [kind of] example. That is, We repeated the statement in it with every example that requires consideration, from verses and lessons, encouragement and intimidation, commands and prohibitions, stories of the ancients, Paradise and Hell, and the Resurrection. But most of the people refused except disbelief. That is, from the people of Mecca, for they denied and rejected the Qur’an being the word of God after the proof was established against them, and they suggested verses that were not theirs. He made clear in the place of concealment where He said: But most of the people refused as an emphasis or clarification. Since refused is interpreted as negation, meaning that he did not accept or was not satisfied, the exception to it is valid in His saying: except disbelievers.
17:90: 90- And they said, 'We will not believe you' meaning the leaders of Mecca, such as Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi'ah, Abu Sufyan, and Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, said, then they linked their denial of faith to a goal they sought, so they said, Until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Asim read until you cause a spring to gush forth with a lightened vowel, like you kill. The rest read it with a shaddah, and they did not differ on so that the rivers gush forth being shaddah. Abu Hatim explained that by saying that the first is followed by yanbu' which is singular, and the second is followed by anhar which is plural. It was answered by saying that even though yanbu' is singular in wording, what is meant by it is plural, because yanbu' is springs that do not dry up. It is answered by saying that yanbu' is the water source, and the plural is yanabi', and the spring is only called yanbu' if it is abundant and its nature is to gush forth without interruption, and the ya is extra like ya'boob from 'ab al-ma'.
17:91: 91- Or you have a garden meaning an orchard whose trees cover its ground. The meaning is, suppose you do not cause rivers to gush forth for us, then cause them to gush forth for you by having a garden of palm trees and grapes, and causing rivers to gush forth meaning making them flow forcefully through it gushing forth meaning in its midst, gushing abundantly.
17:92: 92- Or the sky falls upon us in fragments as you have claimed. Mujahid read or it falls referring to the sky. Others read or it falls as a direct address. That is, or you, O Muhammad, fall on the sky. The word kasf with the fatha on the seen is the plural of kasfa: this is the reading of Nafi', Ibn Amir, and Asim. Kasfa is a piece. The rest read kasfan with the sukoon on the seen. Al-Akhfash said: Whoever reads with the sukoon on the seen makes it singular, and whoever reads with the fatha on it makes it plural. Al-Mahdawi said: It is permissible for it to be the plural of kasfa according to the reading of al-kun, and it is permissible for it to be a source. Al-Jawhari said: Kasfa is a piece of something. It is said: Give me a piece of your garment. The plural is kasfa and kusfa. It is also said that kasfa and kusfa are one. The accusative of kasfan is in the state of the case, and the kaf in kama za’ama is in the accusative case as a description of a deleted source: that is, a projection similar to what you claimed. They mean by that the statement of God, the Most High: If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them up or cause fragments from the sky to fall upon them. Abu Ali said: Kasfa with sukun. The cut thing is like grinding for the ground. Its derivation, according to what Abu Zaid said, is from katsafat al-thawb kasfan if you cut it. Al-Zajjaj said: From katsafat al-shay’ if you cover it, as if it was said or you drop it in layers upon us or you bring God and the angels face to face. The commentators differed about the meaning of qabilan. It was said that it means seeing, as said by Qatada and Ibn Jurayj. Abu Ali al-Farisi chose it and said: If you take it to mean seeing, then the tribe is a verbal noun like Nakir and al-Nadhir. It was also said that it means a guarantor, as said by al-Dahhak. It was also said that it means a witness, as said by Muqatil. It was also said that it is the plural of the tribe, meaning that you come with the various types of angels tribe by tribe, as said by Mujahid and Ata’. It was also said that it is implied, and it was also said that it is a counterpart, like the clan and the associates.
17:93: 93- Or you have a house of gold meaning gold, and Ibn Masoud read it this way. Its root is adornment, and adorned is decorated, and the decorations of water are its paths. Al-Zajjaj said: It is adornment, so he returned to the original meaning of decoration, and it is far-fetched because the meaning becomes: or you have a house of adornment or you ascend into the sky meaning you ascend its levels: it is said you ascended the ladder if you ascended and climbed like it and we will not believe in your ascension meaning for the sake of your ascension, and it is a source like he went on going and he fell “until you bring down to us a book that we can read” meaning until you bring down to us from the sky a book that confirms you and indicates your prophethood that we all read, or each one of us reads it, and it was said that its meaning is: a book from God to each one of us as in His statement: But each one of them wants to be given spread out pages so God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come with what expresses astonishment at their words, and to glorify the Lord, may He be glorified, from their ugly suggestions, so He said: “Say: Glory be to my Lord” meaning glorifying God from being incapable of anything. The people of Mecca and Syria read: Glory be to my Lord, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Was I anything but a human being? Not an angel, so that I could ascend to the heavens. A Messenger, commanded by God Almighty to convey to you. Have you heard, O you who propose these matters, that a human being was able to do anything about them? If you want me to ask God Almighty for that so that He may manifest it through my hand, then if the Messenger brings one miracle, that is sufficient for him, because through it his truthfulness is demonstrated, and there is no need to ask for more. I am a servant who is commanded, and I do not have the right to impose on my Lord what is not necessary, nor does a need call for it. If I were obliged to answer every stubborn person, then every stubborn person would suggest suggestions at every moment, and ask for himself to manifest signs. So God is far above what the wrongdoers say, far above their stubbornness, and sanctified above their suggestions. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: This Qur’an will be taken away. It was said: How will it be taken away when God has established it in our hearts and established it in the copies of the Qur’an? He said: It will be carried over in one night and not a single verse of it will be left in a heart or copy of the Qur’an except that it will be taken away. When you wake up, there will be nothing of it left in you. Then he recited: And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you. This has been narrated on his authority through various chains of transmission. Ibn Adi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), similar to this. Muhammad bin Nasr narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), similar to this. Al-Daylami narrated in Musnad Al-Firdaws on the authority of Mu’adh bin Jabal, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), similar to this. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), similar to this. Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), similar to this. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Mahmoud bin Shaikhan, Nu’ayman bin Asi, Bahri bin Amr, and Salam bin Mishkam came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: Tell us, O Muhammad.” What you have brought is more true than what God has brought. We do not see it as consistent as the Torah is consistent. He said to them: By God, you know that it is from God. They said: We will bring you something similar to what you bring. So God revealed: “Say: If mankind and the jinn were to gather together…” 3:100. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that Utbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabi’ah, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, a man from Banu Abd al-Dar, Abu al-Buhturi, the brother of Banu Asid, al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Rabi’ah ibn al-Aswad, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-‘As ibn Wa’il, Nabih and Munabbih, the sons of al-Hajjaj al-Sahmiyyah, gathered after sunset at the back of the Ka’bah. Some of them said to each other: Send for Muhammad and speak to him and argue with him. He mentioned a long hadith that included what they asked him about and were stubborn about, and that this was the reason for the revelation of His statement: “And they said: We will never believe in you…” until His statement: A human being, a messenger. Its chain of transmission according to Ibn Jarir is as follows: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us, Muhammad narrated to us. Ibn Ishaq narrated to me an old man from Egypt, who came forty-some years ago, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it, and it contains this unknown man. Saad bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And they said, ‘We will never believe you,’ that he said: It was revealed regarding the brother of Umm Salamah, Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: A spring, that he said: Springs. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, that he said: A spring is a river that flows from a spring. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Or you have a garden, that he said: An estate. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority: A rupture, that he said: Cutting off. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: A tribe, that he said: In plain sight. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority: Of adornment, that he said: Of gold. Abu Ubaid, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari and Abu Naim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: I did not know what Az-Zukhruf was until I heard it being recited by Abdullah: Or you will have a house of gold. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: A book which We read he said: From the Lord of the worlds to so-and-so, son of so-and-so. Every man will have a scroll placed at his head in the morning which he will read.
17:94: The Almighty narrated about them another doubt that was repeated in the Noble Book, and it was exposed to its presentation and rejection in more than one place, so He said: 94- And what prevented the people from believing? What is meant is the people in general, and it was said that what is meant is the people of Mecca in particular: that is, what prevented them from believing in the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is the second object of preventing, and the meaning of when the guidance came to them is that the revelation came to them from God Almighty to His Messenger, and He explained that to them and guided them to it, and it is an adverb of preventing or believing: that is, what prevented them at the time of the coming of the guidance from believing in the Qur'an and the prophethood except that they said that is, what prevented them except their saying, so it is in the nominative case as the subject of preventing, and the hamza in God sent a human being as a messenger is for their denial that the Messenger is a human being, and the meaning is: that this belief that is comprehensive to them, which is the denial that the Messenger is from the human race, is what prevented them from believing in the Book and the Messenger, and He expressed it with the saying to indicate that it is nothing but a mere saying that they said With their mouths.
17:95: Then he ordered his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer their doubt, saying: 95- "Say, 'If there were angels walking in peace and security on the earth,'" meaning, if it was found and proven that instead of the people on the earth, there were angels walking on foot as humans walk, reassured, settled in it and dwelling in it. Al-Zajjaj said: Reassured and settled on the earth, and the meaning of reassurance is stillness, so what is meant here is residence and settlement, for it is said that someone inhabited the country if he resided in it, even if he was walking and moving about in his needs, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger, so that he would be from their kind, and in it is information from God Almighty that the messengers should be from the kind of those to whom they are sent, so it is as if God Almighty considered two matters in sending down the messenger from the kind of angels: the first is that the inhabitants of the earth are angels. The second is that they are walking on foot and are unable to fly with their wings to the sky, because if they were able to do that they would have flown to it and heard from its people what must be known and heard, so there would be no benefit in sending angels to them. The accusative of human and angel is that they are the objects of the verbs, and messenger in both places is a description of them. The author of Al-Kashshaf allowed that they are states in both places of messenger in them, and the author of Al-Kashshaf strengthened this view. Perhaps the reason for that is that the denial is directed to the messenger who is described as human in the first place, so by virtue of the contrast it is necessary that the other be likewise.
17:96: Then he concluded the speech with what is considered a threat, saying: 96- "Say: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you." That is, say to them, O Muhammad, on your behalf: Sufficient is God alone as a witness to my conveying to you what He commanded me to do of the matters of the message. He said: "Between me and you," and he did not say: "Between us," to achieve the complete contradiction. It was said that the manifestation of the miracle according to the claim of the Prophet is a testimony from God to him of the truthfulness. Then he explained that He, the Most High, is a sufficient witness by saying: "Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Knowing and Seeing." That is, He is All-Knowing of all their conditions, encompassing their outward and inward aspects, and seeing what was of them and what will be.
17:97: Then the Almighty explained that the acknowledgment and denial are based on His will, saying: 97- He whom God guides is the one who is guided. That is, he whom God desires to guide is the one who is guided to the truth or to everything sought. And he whom He sends astray, that is, He desires to send him astray, you will not find for them protectors who will support them besides Him, meaning God, the Almighty, and guide them to the truth from which God has led them astray or to the path of salvation. His saying, he is the one who is guided, is based on the word who, and His saying, you will not find for them, is based on the meaning, and the address in His saying, you will not find is either to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone who is fit for him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces. This gathering on their faces has two aspects for the commentators: The first is that it is an expression of hastening them to Hell, from the saying of the Arabs: The people passed on their faces: if they hastened. The second is that they will be dragged on their faces on the Day of Resurrection in reality, as is done in this world to those who are excessively humiliated and tortured. This is correct, because God the Almighty says: The Day they will be dragged into the Fire on their faces, and because it is authentic in the Sunnah, as will come. The place of on their faces is the accusative case of the object pronoun, and blind is the accusative case of the state, and dumb and deaf are conjoined with it. The mute is the one who does not speak, and the deaf is the one who does not hear. This is the state in which they will be resurrected in the ugliest form and the most hideous sight. God has combined for them blindness of sight, inability to speak, and inability to hear, along with being dragged on their faces. Then, after that, their abode is Hell, meaning the place to which they will go. The sentence is in the accusative case of the state, or it is a new sentence with no place. Whenever it subsides, We will increase them in a Blaze, meaning whenever its flames subside. It is said that the fire subsides, it subside, if it is extinguished and its flames subside. Ibn Qutaybah said that the meaning of We will increase them in a Blaze is blazing, which is blazing. It has been said that the fading of the Fire will lighten the torment of its people. How can this be reconciled with His statement, The torment will not be lightened for them? It has been answered that what is meant by the lack of lightening is that there will be no perceptible time between the fading and the blazing. It has also been said that it will fade without lightening their torment.
17:98: 98- That meaning the punishment is their recompense which God has made obligatory for them and which they deserved from Him. The ba in His statement: because they disbelieved in Our signs is for causality: that is, because of their disbelief in them, so they did not believe in the signs of revelation nor did they ponder the signs of creation. The demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is their recompense, and because they disbelieved is another predicate. It is possible that their recompense is a second subject and its predicate is what comes after it, and the sentence is the predicate of the first subject. And they said, 'When we are bones and dust' The hamza is for denial. The interpretation of the verse has already been presented in this surah. And creation in His statement: Shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation is a source without its wording or a state: that is, created.
17:99: So God Almighty came with an argument that would prevent them from denying and turn them away from ingratitude. He said: 99- Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them? That is, whoever is able to create this, is more able to repeat what is less than it. It was said that what is meant is that He is able to annihilate them and bring into existence others. According to the first opinion, creation means repetition, and according to this opinion, it is in its true form. The phrase and has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt is in apposition to or they did not see. The meaning is: They have known by the evidence of reason that whoever is able to create the heavens and the earth is able to create the likes of them, because they are not more difficult to create than them, as He said: Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? “and has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt.” That is, death or the Resurrection. It is possible that the and is for resumption. It was said that the speech is an advancement and a delay: that is, or have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth and appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt, is able to create the likes of them? But the wrongdoers refused except to be ungrateful. That is, the polytheists refused except to deny. In this, the apparent is placed in place of the implied to judge them. By injustice and exceeding the limits.
17:100: Then when these infidels asked for rivers and springs to flow in their lands to expand their livelihoods, God the Almighty explained that they would not be satisfied, but would remain stingy and miserly, so He said: 100- "Say: If you possessed the treasures of my Lord's mercy" You is raised as the subject of a deleted verb that is explained by what follows: i.e. if you possessed, you possess, as the separate pronoun is replaced by the connected pronoun which is the waw, and the treasures of His mercy the Almighty: are the treasures of provisions. Al-Zajjaj said: God informed them that if they possessed the treasures of provisions, they would withhold them out of stinginess and miserliness, which is fear of spending: i.e. fear that they would spend and become poor, and in the deletion of the verb that you was raised by, and the presentation of the speech in the form of the subject and predicate, there is an indication that they are the ones who are specifically stingy. Linguists said: Anfas, A’ram, A’dam, and Aqtar mean that his wealth would be small. So the meaning would be: You would have withheld it for fear of a small amount of wealth. And man is ever Qatur means stingy and restrictive. It is said that he was stingy with his dependents, he is stingy and restrictive, meaning he was restrictive with regard to spending. It is possible that it is meant that man is Qatur, meaning he has little wealth. It appears that what is meant is an exaggeration in describing him as stingy, because man is not generally poor in wealth. Rather, some of them have much wealth, unless what is meant is that all of humanity has little wealth in comparison to the treasures of God and what is with Him. There are two opinions regarding this verse: One of them is that it was revealed specifically about the polytheists, and this is what Al-Hasan said, and the second is that it is general, which is the opinion of the majority, as narrated by Al-Mawardi. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “It was said, ‘O Messenger of God, how will people be gathered on their faces?’ He said: ‘The One Who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces.’” Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three categories: a category on foot, a category on horseback, and a category on their faces.” Then he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Anas. There are other hadiths on this topic. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement, Their abode is Hell, he said: He means that they are its fuel. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah on his authority regarding the statement, Whenever it subsides, he said: It becomes still. And these also narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: Whenever He burns them, He turns them into firewood. When He burns them and nothing remains of them, they become glowing embers, and that is their extinction. When they are replaced with a new creation, they return to them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ata’ regarding His statement, The treasures of the mercy of my Lord, he said: Provision. And he also narrated from Ikrimah regarding His statement, Then you would have withheld for fear of spending, he said: When you did not feed anyone anything. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, For fear of spending, he said: Poverty. And man is ever niggardly, he said: Stingy. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada, For fear of spending, he said: Fear of poverty. And man is ever niggardly, he said: Stingy and withholding.
17:101: His saying: 101- And We gave Moses nine signs meaning signs indicating his prophethood. It was said that the connection between this verse and the one before it is that the miracles mentioned are as if they were equal to those things that the infidels of Quraysh proposed, or even stronger than them. The failure to respond to the signs they requested was only because there was no interest in eradicating them. For those who believe in them, most of the commentators said: The nine signs are: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the staff, the hand, the years, and the loss of fruits. Al-Hasan replaced the years and the loss of fruits with the sea and the mountain. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: They are the five in Al-A'raf, the sea, the staff, the stone, and the obliteration of their wealth. We have already discussed these verses in detail, and the hadith of Safwan bin Assal will come in the enumeration of these nine verses. So ask the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Nahik read So ask as a statement: that is, Moses asked Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel and set them free and send them with him. The others read So ask as a command: that is, ask them, O Muhammad, when Moses came to them. The question is a question of testimony for greater reassurance and certainty, because when the evidence comes together, it is stronger, and those asked are the believers among the Children of Israel, such as Abdullah bin Salam and his companions. So Pharaoh said to him, ‘Indeed, I think, O Moses, that you are bewitched.’ The letter fa is the eloquent letter: that is, Moses showed Pharaoh the clear signs that We had given him and conveyed to him what he had been sent with, so Pharaoh said to him. The bewitched is the one who has been bewitched and whose mind has been confused. Abu Ubaidah and al-Farra’ said: It means the magician, so the object was placed in place of the subject.
17:102: F 102- "He said, 'You have certainly known what these have sent down' meaning the verses that He revealed, and 'sent down' means 'created' except the Lord of the heavens and the earth, insights meaning indications by which one can prove His power and oneness, and the accusative of 'insights' is in the state. Al-Kisa'i read with a damma on the ta' of 'I knew' as if it were for Moses, and this was narrated from 'Ali, and the rest read with a fatha on it as a reference to Pharaoh. The basis of the first reading is that Pharaoh did not know that, but Moses knew it. The basis of the reading of the majority is that Pharaoh knew that as God Almighty said: And they denied it, while their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance. Abu 'Ubaid said: What is taken from us is the fatha on the ta', and this is the most correct meaning, because Moses does not say, 'I knew' while he is the one calling, and something similar to this was narrated from Al-Zajjaj And indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed. Suspicion here means certainty, and doom is destruction and loss. Al-Kumait said: Quda'ah saw in the days a vision of a persevering and steadfast person. Meaning: lost and loser, and it was said: cursed and damned, and from this the poet said: O our people, do not seek out a sad person foolishly, for foolishness and oppression are both sinful. Any cursed one, woe to the one who is cursed, lacking in mind, and it was said that he is the one who is prevented from good, it is said what prevented you from such and such: what prevented you from it, as the linguists have said, and it was said that he is bewitched.
17:103: 103- So he wanted to expel them from the land meaning Pharaoh wanted to expel the Children of Israel and Moses and disturb them from the land, meaning the land of Egypt by removing them from it. It was said that he wanted to kill them, and based on this, the land is meant to be the entire land. The meaning of exhortation was mentioned earlier: So We drowned him and all those with him, so destruction by drowning befell him and them, and not one of them remained.
17:104: 104- And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land' meaning after drowning him and those with him. The land here means the land of Egypt from which He wanted to provoke them. Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes meaning the Hereafter, which is the Resurrection, or the Last Globe, or the Last Hour, We will bring you in droves. Al-Jawhari said: The droves are those who have gathered from different tribes. It is said that the people came in droves and droves: meaning with their mixtures. So what is meant here is that We have brought you from your graves mixed from every place, the believer has mixed with the disbeliever. Al-Asma'i said: The droves are a plural and it does not have a singular, and it is like the plural.
17:105: 105- And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended. The pronoun refers to the Qur'an, and the meaning of With the truth We sent it down is that We revealed it adorned with the truth, and the meaning of With the truth it descended is that it descended and in it was the truth. The rest was said that With the first truth means with: that is, with the truth We sent it down, like their saying The prince rode with his sword, that is, with his sword, and With the truth it descended: that is, with Muhammad, as you say I descended with Zayd. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: The ba in both places means with, and it was said that the meaning could be: And with the truth We determined that it should descend, and thus it descended, or We did not send it down from the sky except preserved, and it did not descend to the Messenger except preserved from the confusion of the devils, and the presentation in both places is for specialization. And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, that is, a bringer of good tidings to those who obey of Paradise and a warner who frightens those who disobey of the Fire.
17:106: 106- And a Qur'an which We have divided The Qur'an is in the accusative case with an implied verb that is explained by what follows it. Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Qatadah, Abu Raja' and Al-Sha'bi read We divided it with a shaddah: meaning We revealed it one after the other, not all at once. The majority read We divided it with a tafsir: meaning We explained it and clarified it, and We distinguished in it between truth and falsehood. Al-Zajjaj said: He divided it in the revelation so that people would understand it. Abu Ubaid said: I like the tafsir better, because its interpretation is We explained it, and the tafsir has no meaning except that it was revealed in parts. This is supported by what Tha'lab narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-A'rabi that he said: I divided the words with a shaddah, and I divided the bodies with a shaddah. Then the Almighty mentioned the reason for His statement: We did not divide it, so He said: So that you may recite it to the people in stages meaning in a long period of time, one after the other, according to the first reading, or We revealed it verse by verse, and surah by surah. Its meaning according to the second reading is on mukth: that is, on slowing down and taking one’s time in the recitation, as that is closer to understanding and easier to memorize. The reciters agreed to add a damma to the mim in mukth except for Ibn Muhaysin, who read it with a fatha on the mim “and We sent it down” as emphasis with the infinitive for emphasis, and the meaning is: We sent it down in stages, separated, because of the benefit in that, and if they were to undertake all the obligatory duties at one time, they would have been repelled and would not have been able to do it.
17:107: 107- "Say: Believe in it or do not believe." God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the disbelievers who proposed signs: Believe in it or do not believe. Whether you believe in it or refrain from it, it does not increase or decrease it. This is a severe warning for His command, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn away from them and despise them. Then He explained that by saying: Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it meaning the scholars who read the previous books before the revelation of the Qur'an and knew the truth of the revelation and the signs of prophethood, such as Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Waraqa ibn Nawfal, and Abdullah ibn Salam when it is recited to them meaning the Qur'an they fall upon their chins in prostration meaning they fall on their faces in prostration to God the Almighty. He restricted falling, which is falling, to being upon the chins: meaning upon it, because the chin, which is the meeting of the two jaws, is the first thing that touches the ground. Al-Zajjaj said: Because the chin is the meeting place of the two beards, and just as a person begins to prostrate himself, the first part of his face that touches the ground is the chin. It was said that what is meant is to cover the beard with dust, because that is the ultimate in submission. The preference of the lam in li-thiqanaan over indicates specificity, as if they singled out their chins for prostration, or singled out prostration with their chins. It was said that the pronoun in his statement: before him refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what we have mentioned about referring it to the Qur’an is preferable because the context indicates that, and in this there is consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The gist of it is that if these ignorant people who have no knowledge or understanding of the Books of God or His Prophets do not believe in it, then do not worry about that, because the people of knowledge believed in it and were humble before it and submitted to it when it was recited to them in submission, the great effect of which was evident in their prostrating on their chins to God.
17:108: 108- And they say, ‘Glory be to our Lord,’ meaning they say in their prostration, sanctifying our Lord from what the ignorant say of denial, or sanctifying Him from breaking His promise. Indeed, the promise of our Lord is fulfilled. This is the lightened form of the heavy form, and the lam is the distinguishing feature.
17:109: Then he mentioned that they fell on their chins weeping, so he said: 109- And they fall on their chins weeping. He repeated the mention of falling on their chins for a different reason, as the first is to glorify God Almighty and sanctify Him, and the second is to weep due to the effect of the Qur’an’s admonitions on their hearts and their increased humility. For this reason he said: And increases them, meaning hearing the Qur’an, or the Qur’an by their hearing it, in humility, meaning softening the heart and moistening the eye. Abdul Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: nine verses, and he mentioned what we mentioned on the authority of most of the commentators. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: His hand, his staff, his tongue, the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood. Al-Tayalisi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi and he authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Qani’, Al-Hakim and he authenticated it, Abu Nu’aym, Al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Safwan bin Assal that “two Jews said to each other: Let us go to this prophet and ask him. So they went to him and asked him about the statement of God: ‘And We gave Moses nine clear signs.’ He said: Do not associate anything with God, do not commit adultery, do not be extravagant, do not kill the soul which God has forbidden except by right, do not steal, do not practice magic, do not walk with an innocent person to the ruler so that he may kill him, do not consume usury, and do not accuse a chaste woman. Or he said: Do not flee from the battle. Shu’bah was not sure, and upon you is…” O Jews, especially do not transgress on the Sabbath. So they kissed his hands and feet and said: We bear witness that you are the Prophet of God. He said: What prevents you from submitting to Islam? They said: David prayed to God that there would always be a Prophet among his descendants, and we fear that if we submit to Islam, the Jews will kill us. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in Damm Al-Ghadab on the authority of Anas bin Malik that he was asked about his statement: And I think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed. He said: Disagreeing. He said: The prophets are too honorable to be cursed or insulted. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Mathboor meaning: cursed. Al-Shirazi narrated in Al-Alqab and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority: Little intellect. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority: Lafeef meaning: all together. An-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited, And a Qur’an We have divided into parts, in a heavy form. He said: The Qur’an was sent down to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree in Ramadan all at once. When the polytheists innovated something, God would create an answer for them, so God divided it into parts over twenty years. Something similar to this has been narrated on his authority through various chains of transmission. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority, We divided it, meaning, We separated it over a period of time. They fall upon their chins, meaning, upon their faces. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, When it is recited to them, meaning, their book.
17:110: God Almighty wanted to teach His servants how to supplicate and be humble, so He said: 110- "Say, 'Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious'. Its meaning is that they are equal in the permissibility of generalization and the goodness of supplication with them, and for this reason He said, Whichever you call upon, to Him belong the best names. The tanween in whatever is a substitute for the complement, and what is added to emphasize the ambiguity in whatever, and the pronoun in to Him" refers to the named, and the original statement was: Whatever you call upon, it is good, so it was placed in its place, to Him belong the best names for emphasis, and to indicate that if all of His names are good, these two names are good, and the meaning of the goodness of names is their independence with the attributes of majesty and honor. Al-Naysaburi mentioned the meaning of this and Abu Al-Su'ud followed him. Al-Zajjaj said: God informed them that their supplication to God and their supplication to the Most Gracious go back to one statement, and the reason for the revelation of the verse will be mentioned, and with it the meaning of it becomes clear. Then he mentioned another way of supplication and said: “And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice” meaning in the recitation of your prayer with the deletion of the complement because it is known that recitation aloud and in a low voice are attributes of the voice, not attributes of the actions of prayer, so it is from the generalization of the whole and the meaning of the part. It is said that his voice became low if his speech was cut off and weak and still, and the crops became low if they withered, and the man became low in his recitation: if he did not raise his voice with it. It was said that its meaning is: Do not recite your entire prayer aloud and do not recite it in a low voice, and the first is more appropriate. And seek between that meaning the loudness and in a low voice indicated by the two actions a way meaning a middle path between the two matters, so do not recite aloud or in a low voice. According to the second interpretation, the meaning of that is the prohibition of reciting all the prayers aloud, and the prohibition of reciting all the prayers in a low voice, and the command to make some of them. Some of them are loudly said, which is the night prayer, and quietly said during the day prayer. Some people said that this verse was abrogated by His saying: Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly.
17:111: And when He commanded that He should not be mentioned or called except by His beautiful names, He pointed out how to praise Him, saying: 111- “And say, ‘Praise be to God, who has not taken a son’” as the Jews and Christians say, and whoever among the polytheists says that the angels are daughters of God, He is far above that, and He has no partner in the kingdom meaning, anyone who shares with Him in His kingdom and lordship, as the dualists and other groups like them claim, who believe in multiple gods, and He has no protector out of humiliation meaning, He has no need of the support of anyone because of the humiliation that would befall him, so He is independent of a protector or a helper. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, he did not need to be victorious through anyone other than Him. In the mention of these sublime attributes during the praise, there is an indication that the one who deserves praise is the one who has these attributes, because he is able to bring into existence and bestow blessings, since a son is a coward and a miser, and because it also necessitates the father’s occurrence because he is born from one of his parts, and the originator is not able to complete the blessing, and partnership in ownership is only conceivable for one who is not able to be independent with it, and one who is not able to be independent is helpless, let alone the completion of what he has, let alone the system of what he is upon. Also, partnership causes conflict between the two partners, as the partner may prevent him from bestowing goodness on his guardians and leads to corruption. If there were within them gods besides God, they would have both been ruined. And the one who needs a guardian to prevent him from humiliation and support him against whoever wants to humiliate him is weak and is not able to do what the one who is self-sufficient is able to do. And glorify Him with great glorification, that is, magnify Him with great glorification, describing Him as greater than everything. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca one day and said in his supplication: ‘O God, O Most Merciful.’ The polytheists said: ‘Look at this Sabean forbidding us to call upon two gods, while he is calling upon two gods.’ So God revealed: ‘Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Merciful.’” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, who said: The Jews asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the Most Merciful, and they had a soothsayer in Yamamah whom they called the Most Merciful, so the verse was revealed, and it is mursal. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Makhul, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying in Mecca one night and saying in his prostration, ‘O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate.’ A polytheist heard him, and when morning came he said to his companions: ‘Ibn Abi Kabshah is calling tonight upon the Most Merciful who is in Yemen, and there was a man in Yemen called the Most Merciful, so the verse was revealed.” Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Nahshal bin Saeed on the authority of Al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God, ‘Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Merciful, whichever you call upon’ until the end of the verse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is protection from theft.” And a man from the emigrants, from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it when he went to bed, and a thief entered upon him, gathered what was in the house and carried it while the man was not asleep until he reached the door and found the door locked, so he put down the lever, and he did that three times, and the companion laughed and then said: I have fortified my house. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud the verse, he said: It was revealed while the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was hidden, so when he prayed with his companions, he would raise his voice with the Qur’an. When the polytheists heard that, they would curse the Qur’an, the One who revealed it and the One who brought it. So God said to His Prophet: And do not recite your prayer aloud, meaning your recitation, lest the polytheists hear and curse the Qur’an. And do not recite it in a low voice from your companions, so do not let them hear the Qur’an until they learn it from you. And seek a way between that, meaning between loudness and lowness. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that the Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would recite aloud in Mecca and would be disturbed, so God revealed: And do not recite your prayer aloud. Ibn Abi Shaybah also narrated something similar on his authority. Abu Dawud narrated something similar on his authority in his Naskh. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him that he said: Musaylimah the Liar had been called Ar-Rahman, so whenever the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed and recited In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful out loud, the polytheists would say: He is mentioning the God of Yamamah. So God revealed: And do not recite your prayer aloud. Sa’eed ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated from Muhammad ibn Sireen that he said: I was told that when Abu Bakr recited, he would lower his voice, and when ‘Umar recited, he would recite aloud. It was said to Abu Bakr, Why do you do this? He said: I am conversing with my Lord, and He knows my need. It was said to ‘Umar, Why do you do this? He said: I drive away Satan and wake up the sleepy ones. When And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice was revealed, it was said to Abu Bakr, Raise your voice a little, and it was said to ‘Umar, Lower your voice a little. Sa’eed ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from ‘Aa’ishah that she said: This verse, And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice was revealed in supplication. Ibn Jarir and Al-Hakim narrated on her authority that she said: It was revealed in the testimony of faith. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Mani’, Ibn Jarir, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar to the first hadith of Aisha. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi that he said: The Jews and Christians said: God has taken a son. The Arabs said: Here I am, You have no partner except a partner who is Yours, You own him and what he owns. The Sabians and Magians said: Were it not for the allies of God, He would have been humiliated. So God revealed this verse: “Say: Praise be to God” to the end of it. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And he had no protector out of humiliation that he said: He did not ally with anyone and did not seek anyone’s support. Ahmad and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Anas that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The verse of glory is: ‘Praise be to God, Who has not taken a son’ the entire verse.” Abu Ya`la and Ibn As-Sunni narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: “I went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his hand was in my hand, and a man of shabby appearance came to me and said: ‘O so-and-so, what has happened to you that I see?’ He said: ‘Illness and harm.’ He said: ‘Shall I not teach you some words that will remove from you illness and harm? I put my trust in the Ever-Living Who does not die, “Praise be to God who has not taken a son” to the end of the verse. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to him and his condition had improved and he said: ‘How are you?’ He said: ‘I have not ceased to say the words that you taught me.’” In another version, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) taught that to Abu Hurairah. Ibn Kathir said: Its chain of transmission is weak and there is something objectionable in its text. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah that he said: “It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to teach his family this verse: ‘Praise be to God who has not taken a son’ to the end of it, to the young and old among his family.” Abdul Razzaq narrated in Al-Musannaf on the authority of Abdul Karim bin Abi Umayya who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would teach a boy from Banu Hashim, if he pronounced it seven times, ‘Praise be to God who has not taken a son’ to the end of the surah.” Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf on the authority of Abdul Karim on the authority of Amr bin Shuayb and mentioned it. Ibn Al-Sunni narrated it in Amal Al-Yawm wa Al-Laylah on the authority of Amr bin Shuayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather.
18:1: It is one hundred and eleven verses. Al-Qurtubi said: It is Meccan according to all the commentators. It was narrated on the authority of Farqa that the beginning of the Surah was revealed in Madinah up to the words Jarzān, but the first is more correct. Among those who said that it is all Meccan is Ibn Abbas, narrated by An-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh, and among them is Ibn Az-Zubayr, narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. There are hadiths that have been narrated about its merits, including what was narrated by Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i and others on the authority of Abu Ad-Darda’ on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Antichrist. Ahmad, Muslim, An-Nasa’i and Ibn Hibban narrated on the authority of Abu Ad-Darda’ who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites the last ten verses of Surat Al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Antichrist. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’ who said: “A man was reciting Surat Al-Kahf while there was a beast in the house, and it began to scatter. He looked and saw that a mist or cloud had covered it. He mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘Recite, so-and-so, for tranquility has descended upon the Qur’an.’” This person who was reciting was Usaid ibn Hudayr, as explained by Al-Tabarani. Al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites three verses from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Antichrist. There are hadiths about reciting ten verses from the beginning or the end of it. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ali who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites Surat Al-Kahf on Friday will be protected for eight days from every trial that will happen. If the Antichrist emerges, he will be protected from him.” Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi and Al-Dhiya’ on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites Surat Al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his place of residence to Mecca. Whoever recites ten verses from the end of it and then the Antichrist emerges, it will not harm him.” Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abu Saeed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Surat Al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him from one Friday to the next. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it in Al-Sunan from this chain of transmission and from another chain of transmission. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites Surat Al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him from beneath his feet to the clouds of the sky, which will shine for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be forgiven between the two Fridays.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Shall I not tell you of a surah whose greatness fills what is between the heavens and the earth, and for its writer there is a reward similar to that? Whoever recites it on Friday will be forgiven for what is between that Friday and the next, plus three days. Whoever recites the last five of it before going to sleep, God will raise him up at whatever time of the night he wishes?” They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Surat Ashab al-Kahf. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The house in which Surat al-Kahf is recited, Satan will not enter it that night. There are hadiths and reports on this topic, and what we have mentioned is sufficient for Mughniyyah. He taught His servants how to praise Him for bestowing His blessings upon them, and describing it with a relative pronoun indicates the causality of what is in the realm of connection to what preceded it. The reason for the revelation of the Book, which is the Qur’an, being a blessing to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is that he learned through it the secrets of monotheism, the conditions of the angels and the prophets, and the manner of the legal rulings by which God and his nation worship Him. Likewise, the revelation of the Book to their Prophet was a blessing to the servants, similar to what we mentioned about the Prophet 1- And He has not made therein any crookedness meaning any kind of imbalance in the wording or meaning. Crookedness with the kasra is in meanings, and with the fatha in objects, is what was said. This is what is said in response to His, the Most High’s, statement: You will not see therein any crookedness or unevenness meaning the mountains, which are objects. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse is that He did not make any discrepancy in it, as He said: And if it had been from other than God, they would have found therein much discrepancy. The straight value that has no inclination, or the value of the religious and worldly interests of the servants, or the value of the heavenly books that preceded it, dominating them. According to the first, it is an emphasis on what is indicated by the negation of crookedness, for perhaps something that is straight in appearance is not free of the slightest crookedness in reality. The erection of the value by an implied word: that is, He made it straight. The author of Al-Kashshaf prevented it from being a state of the book, because his saying and did not make is conjoined with revealed so it is included in the scope of the relative clause, so making it a state of the book separates the state and the subject of the state by some of the relative clause. Al-Isfahani said: They are two successive states except that the first is a sentence and the second is singular, and this is correct because his saying and did not make was not conjoined with what preceded it, but the waw is for the state, so there is no separation between the state and the subject of the state by some of the relative clause.
18:2: It was said that 2- Qayman is a state of the pronoun lam ya'alhu, and it was said that there is an advancement and delay in the speech, and the estimate is: He sent down to His servant the Book as a straight one and does not make it crooked, then the Almighty wanted to detail what He summarized in His saying as a straight one, so He said: To warn of a severe punishment and He omitted the warner because of knowledge of it with the intention of generalization, and the meaning is to warn the disbelievers. And the punishment is the torment, and the meaning of from Him is issued from Him sent down from Him. Abu Bakr narrated from Asim that he read from Him with the damma of the dal, and with the kasra of the noon and the ha. This is the language of the Kalabiyyin. Abu Zaid narrated from all the reciters with the fatha of the lam and the damma of the dal and the sukoon of the noon And He gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds "Yabshar was read with emphasis and alleviation, and the relative pronoun was made to follow its aforementioned description, because the basis of the acceptance of deeds is faith that they will have a good reward which is Paradise.
18:3: The state of their being 3- remaining in it meaning in that reward forever meaning a permanent stay with no interruption, and the warning is presented before the good report to show the complete care in deterring the infidels.
18:4: Then He repeated the warning and mentioned the one who was warned specifically and omitted the one who was warned about, which is the severe punishment, because it was mentioned before, so He said: 4- And to warn those who say, ‘God has taken a son,’ and they are the Jews, Christians, and some of the infidels of Quraysh. Those who say that the angels are daughters of God, so the Almighty first mentioned a general issue, which is warning all infidels.
18:5: Then he connected a specific issue to it, which is some of the details of that whole, to draw attention to the fact that it is the greatest detail of that whole. This indicates that attributing a son to God, the Most High, is the ugliest type of disbelief. 5- They have no knowledge of it meaning of the son, or of God taking him, and of is added to emphasize the negation, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state or it is a new sentence, and the meaning is: They have no knowledge of that at all, nor did their fathers knowledge, rather they were in their claim on this misguidance, and their children imitated them and they all went astray. A great word that comes out of their mouths “word” is in the accusative case as a specification, and it was read in the nominative case as an agent. Al-Farra’ said: That word was a great word. Al-Zajjaj said: Their statement was a great word, and what is meant by this word is their saying that God has taken a son. Then he described the word by saying: It comes out of their mouths. The benefit of this description is to show how great their audacity in uttering it is, and what comes out of the mouth, even if it is merely desire, but since letters and sounds are qualities based on desire, he attributed to the state what is related to the place. Then he increased the ugliness of what they said by saying: They say nothing but a lie, meaning they say nothing but a lie in which there is no room for truth at all.
18:6: Then he consoled his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying: 6- "Perhaps you will kill yourself by following them." Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra' said: Bakh' means effort. Al-Kisa'i said: Bakh'at Al-Ard bil-Zira'at means making it weak due to continuous tillage, and a man Bakh'at Nafs means he exhausts it. Abu Ubaidah said: Its meaning is destroying yourself, and from it is the saying of Dhu Al-Rummah: Oh, you who are in great pain The meaning according to these sayings is that you may exhaust yourself or weaken or destroy yourself in their footsteps after their separation and after their turning away and turning away if they do not believe in this message meaning the Qur’an. The answer to the condition is omitted and is indicated by what precedes it. It was read with the opening of an: meaning because they did not believe with grief meaning anger and sorrow and it is an object for it or a source in the place of the state. This is what Al-Zajjaj said.
18:7: 7- Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it. This sentence is a resumption. The meaning is: We have made what is on the earth that is suitable to be an adornment for it from animals, plants, and inanimate objects, as in the saying of the Almighty: It is He who created for you all that is on the earth. The accusative of adornment is as a second object of made, and the lam in that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed is related to made, and it is either for the purpose or for the consequence, and what is meant by the test is that the Almighty treats them in a way that if that treatment were from someone other than Him, it would be from the category of a test and examination. Al-Zajjaj said: Which of them is raised as a subject, except that its wording is the word of a question, and the meaning is: to test whether this one is better in deed or that one? Al-Hasan said: Which of them is more ascetic, and Muqatil said: Which of them is more righteous in what he has been given of knowledge.
18:8: Then He, the Almighty, informed that He will destroy and annihilate all of that, so He said: 8- And indeed, We will make whatever is on it a barren plain. That is, We will make whatever is on it of these adornments, when the life of this world comes to an end, a barren plain. Abu Ubaidah said: The plain is the level part of the earth. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the path in which there is no vegetation. Al-Farra' said: Al-Jarz is the land in which there is no vegetation. And from their saying: A woman is Jarz if she is an eater, and a sword is Jarz if it is uprooted, and the locusts, sheep, and camels eat the land if they eat what is on it. Dhu al-Rummah said: The hump and the ribs folded what was in their bellies The meaning of the system is: Do not be sad, O Muhammad, about what these people have done in terms of denial, for We have made what is on the earth an adornment to test their deeds, and We will remove that at the end of the life of this world, so We will reward them, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Praise be to God, Who has sent down upon His Servant the Book the verse, he said: He sent down the Book as justice and upright, and has not made therein any crookedness ambiguous. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak, upright, he said: straight. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, from Him, meaning from Him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi: Hasan meaning Paradise, And to warn those who say, ‘God has taken a son’ he said: They are the Jews and Christians. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Shaibah bin Rabi’ah, Abu Jahl, Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, Umayyah bin Khalaf, Al-As bin Wa’il, Al-Aswad bin Abdul Muttalib, and Abu Al-Buhturi gathered with a group of Quraysh. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was grieved by what he saw of his people’s opposition to him and their denial of the advice he had brought, so it saddened him greatly, so God, the Exalted, revealed: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: Breaking yourself with grief meaning: Kill yourself. Abd bin Hamid narrated a similar narration on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated a similar narration on the authority of Al-Suddi. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid Asfan meaning: Impatience. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah: Asfan meaning: Grief. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth an adornment for it, he said: Men. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on his statement something similar. Abu Nasr al-Sajzi narrated in al-Ibanah on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: The scholars are the adornment of the earth. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan who said: They are the men who worship God and work for Him in obedience. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim in al-Tarikh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘To test them as to which of them is best in deed. ’ I said: What is the meaning of that, O Messenger of God? He said: To test you as to which of you is best in reason, most devout in avoiding the prohibitions of God, and quickest in obeying God.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: To test them as to which of them is best in deed. He said: Which of them is most perfect in reason. Al-Hasan narrated: Which of them is best in deeds? He said: The one who abandons the world the most. He also narrated: The one who is most ascetic in the world. Ibn Jarir narrated: Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We will make what is on it a barren plain. He said: Everything will perish and disappear. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Qatadah said: The plain is the dirt and mountains that have no crops. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Al-Hasan said: By barren he means the ruins.
18:9: His saying: 9- Or did you think "Or did you think is the disconnected or understood by bal and the hamza according to the majority, and bal" alone according to some of them and the estimation is: "Rather I thought, or Rather I thought, and its meaning is to move from one hadith to another, not to invalidate the first and ignore it as is the meaning of bal" in the original. The meaning is: When the people were amazed by the story of the People of the Cave and asked the Messenger about it as a test, the Almighty said: "Rather, did you think, O Muhammad, that they were only a wonder among Our signs?" Do not think so, for all of Our signs are a wonder, for He who was able to make what is on the earth an adornment for it for testing, then made what is on it a barren plain as if it had never flourished yesterday, do not rule out His power, protection, and mercy with respect to a specific group, even if their story was extraordinary, for the signs of God the Almighty are like that and above that. Amazingly is in the accusative case as the predicate of was: meaning, something amazing, or described as amazing as an exaggeration, and of Our signs is in the accusative case as a state.
18:10: And 10- When the young men took refuge is an adverb for I thought or for an implied verb, which is remember: meaning they went to it and made it their refuge. The young men are the people of the cave, and the cave is the wide cavern in the mountain. If it is small, it is called a cave. And the inscription, Kaab and Al-Suddi said: It is the name of the village from which the people of the cave came out. And Saeed bin Jubair and Mujahid said: It is a tablet of stones or lead on which their names were written, and it was placed on the door of the cave. Al-Farra' said: It is narrated that it was called the inscription because their names were written on it. And the inscription is writing. And something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas. And from it is the saying of Al-Ajjaj in his poem: And the settlers of the numbered Qur’an It was said that Ar-Raqim was the name of their dog, and it was said that it was the name of the valley in which they were, and it was said that it was the name of the mountain in which the cave was. Al-Zajjaj said: God, the Exalted, knows that the story of the People of the Cave is not a wondrous verse of God, because the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them is more wondrous than the story of the People of the Cave. And they said, ‘Our Lord, grant us mercy from You,’ meaning from You. Min is an introductory particle related to give us, or to an omitted word that was a state. The tanween in mercy is either for emphasis or for variety. Min is presented for specificity, meaning a mercy that is specific to being from the treasuries of Your mercy, which is forgiveness in the hereafter, security from enemies, and provision in this world. And prepare for us from our affair right guidance, meaning make it right for us, from your saying I prepared the affair so it was prepared. What is meant by their affair is the affair that they are upon, which is their separation from the disbelievers, and right guidance is the opposite of misguidance. Min is for the beginning, and it may be for the purpose of abstraction, as in your saying I saw right guidance from You. And presenting the two genitives is for the purpose of highlighting them.
18:11: 11- So We struck their ears. The commentators said: We put them to sleep. The meaning is: We blocked their ears with the sleep that overcomes hearing sounds. The object is omitted: that is, We struck the veil over their ears, likening the heavy sleep that prevents sounds from reaching the ears by striking the veil over them. In the cave is an adverb for We struck, and years is in the accusative case as an adverb, and number is an attribute of years: that is, having a number as a source or in the meaning of counted as in the meaning of the object. The abundance is derived from describing years as a number. Al-Zajjaj said: If something is small, its quantity is understood, so there is no need to count it. If it is large, it needs to be counted. It was said that it is derived from it to mean smallness because a large amount is small with God. And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.
18:12: 12- Then We sent them forth meaning We awakened them from that sleep to know meaning to make known what is known, and it was read with the letter ta'dah, built for the agent in the manner of turning, and which of the two parties is a subject from which knowledge is suspended due to what is in which of the interrogative, and its predicate is counted and it is a past tense verb. It was said that what is meant by the knowledge that was made a cause for the sending forth is the test metaphorically, so the meaning is that We sent them forth to treat them as someone who tests them, and what is better is what we mentioned that what is meant by it is the manifestation of what is known by God Almighty to His servants, and what is meant by the two parties are the two groups of believers and disbelievers from the People of the Cave who differed in the length of their stay. The meaning of ahsa is aqta I counted and it is as if there was a dispute between them about the length of their stay in the cave, so God sent them to make that clear to them, and to show who had counted correctly from who had not. What is in lamma labathu is a source: that is, He counted their stay. It was said that the lam is redundant, and ma means who, and amdan is a distinguishing feature, and al-amd is the limit. It was said that ahsa is a comparative form. It was responded that it is contrary to what is established in the science of grammar, and what was reported from the anomalous cannot be used as an analogy, such as their saying: aflas from Ibn al-Mudhlaq, and adda from scabies. It was responded that the comparative form from the additional form is an established analogy from Sibawayh and Ibn Asfour.
