It was said that the two parties are the People of the Cave who differed after they realized how long they had stayed. It was said that the People of the Cave were a party and their companions were a party. Al-Farra' said: Two groups of Muslims at the time of the People of the Cave differed about the length of their stay.
18:13: 13- We relate to you their story in truth. This is the beginning of detailing what was most beautiful in His statement: When the young men took shelter. That is, We inform you of their story in truth, that is, We related it to them in truth, or in the presence of truth. They were young men. That is, young men, and believed in their Lord. is an attribute of young men, and the sentence is resumed with the assumption of a question, and young men is a plural of paucity, and We increased them in guidance with confirmation and success, and in it is a shift from the third person to the second person.
18:14: 14- And We strengthened their hearts meaning We strengthened them with patience in abandoning family and homelands, and separation from friends and companions when they stood up the circumstance is in the accusative case because of We bound. The commentators differed about this standing up in sayings: It was said that they gathered behind the city without an appointment, and a man from them who was the eldest of the people said: I find something in myself, my Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, so they said: We also find it in ourselves, so they all stood up "and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth" said Mujahid. Most of the commentators said: They had a powerful king called Decius, who called people to worship tyrants. So God made these young men steadfast and protected them until they stood before Him. And they said, ‘Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth.’ Ata’ and Muqatil said that they said that when they woke up from sleep. We will never call upon any god besides Him, meaning we will never worship any other god besides God, neither as partners nor independently. Indeed, then we would have said an outrageous thing, meaning an outrageous statement, or a statement that is the same as outrageousness with the intention of exaggerating the description with the source, and the lam is the one that introduces the oath, and outrageousness is exaggeration and going beyond the limit. A’sha bin Qais said: You will stop, but those who are extravagant will not stop, like those who stab, in which the oil and the twist are lost.
18:15: 15- These are our people who have taken gods besides Him. These is the subject, and its predicate is they have taken, and our people is an explanatory apposition. In this statement there is a sense of denial, and in the reference to them there is a belittling of them. Why do they not bring against them a clear authority? That is, why do they not bring an apparent argument that is suitable for adhering to? Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God? So he claims that He has a partner in worship: that is, no one is more unjust than him.
18:16: 16- And when you withdrew from them meaning you left them and stepped aside from them: meaning from the idol worshippers. His statement: And they worship none but God is conjoined with the accusative pronoun, and ma is a relative pronoun or a source: meaning when you withdrew from them and withdrew from their deity or that which they worshipped. His statement: except God is an interrupted exception on the assumption that they did not worship anything but idols, or connected on the assumption that they associated them in worship with God Almighty. It was said that it is an interrupting statement, informing from God Almighty about the youths that they did not worship anyone but God, so ma is a negative in this case. So take refuge in the cave meaning go to it and make it your refuge. Al-Farra' said: It is the answer to idh, and its meaning is: Go to it and make it your refuge. It was said that it is evidence of its answer, that is, if you have isolated yourself from them in belief, then isolate yourself from them in physical isolation. If you want to isolate yourself from them, then do so by taking refuge in the cave. Your Lord will spread out for you from His mercy meaning He will expand and expand. And will prepare for you from your affair a relief meaning He will make easy and facilitate for you from the affair that you are dealing with. A relief. Al-Murfaq with the fatha or kasra of the m is two languages that are read with it. It is taken from irtifa' which means benefit. It was said that the fatha of the m is more correct, and the kasra of it is more common. Al-Farra' said: Most Arabs use the kasra of the m in the command and in the man's relief. Arabs may use the fatha of the m in both, so they understand that they are two languages. It is as if those who used the fatha wanted to differentiate between the relief of the command and the relief of the man. Al-Kisa’i said: The kasra is in the elbow of the hand. It was said that the elbow with the kasra is what you benefit from, and the elbow with the fatha is the accompanying matter. What is meant here is what they benefit from and benefit from obtaining it. The presentation in both places indicates specialization. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ar-Raqim is the Book. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on his authority, who said: Ar-Raqim is a valley in the middle of Palestine, close to Ayla. The two narrators on the authority of Ibn Abbas are weak. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on his authority, who also said: It is the mountain in which the cave is. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, who said: By God, I do not know whether Ar-Raqim is the Book or a building? In another narration on his authority, he said: I asked Ka’b and he said: The name of the village from which they came out. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: Ar-Raqim is the dog. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: They were among Our signs, a wonder, meaning: What I have given you of knowledge, the Sunnah, and the Book is better than the status of the People of the Cave and Ar-Raqim. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding His statement: Then We struck their ears, meaning: We put them to sleep. Then We sent them forth that We might know which of the two parties of the people of the youths, the people of guidance and the people of misguidance, had best accounted for how long they had remained, and that is because they wrote down the day on which they had gone out, the month, and the year. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, regarding His statement, And We increased them in guidance, he said: Sincerity. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His statement, And We strengthened their hearts, he said: With faith. And regarding His statement, Indeed, then we would have spoken an outrage, he said: A lie. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi, he said: Injustice. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, regarding His statement, And when you withdrew from them and what they worshipped except God, he said: The people of the youths worshipped God and worshipped various gods with Him, so the youths withdrew from the worship of those gods but did not withhold from the worship of God. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, saying: It is in the Mushaf of Ibn Masoud, and what they worship besides God, so this is its interpretation.
18:17: His saying: 17- And you see the sun when it rises His words began to describe their condition, after they had taken refuge in the cave tazarawwar The people of Kufa read without the taa' of ta'ifala, and Ibn Amir read tazwar. Al-Akhfash said: Azwarar is not used in this meaning, rather it is said he is mazwar 'ani: meaning he is withdrawn. The rest read with a shaddah on the zay and the assimilation of the taa' of ta'ifala into it after making it sukun. Tazarawwar is taken from zur with a fathah on the waw, which is inclination, and from it zaarahu if he leans towards him, and zur is inclination, so the meaning of the verse is that when the sun rises, it inclines and withdraws from their cave The rajaz poet Al-Kalbi said: Jab Al-Manda away from our love Azour Any inclined to the right meaning the right side, which is the side called the right, and the accusative of that is in the adverbial phrase, and when it sets, it ceders them ceding means cutting off. Al-Kisa'i, Al-Akhfash, Al-Zajjaj and Abu Ubaidah said: It turns away from them and leaves them, ceded the place: it turned away from it, you say to your friend: did you go to such and such place? He says: I only ceded it: if he passed by it and passed by it, and the meaning is: that when the sun rises, it slants away from their cave to the right: meaning the right of the cave, and when it sets, it passes to the left meaning the north of the cave, it does not hit it. Rather, it turns away from its direction to both directions, and the gap is the wide place, and the phrase and they are in a gap of it is in the accusative case as a state, and the commentators have two opinions in interpreting this phrase: the first is that despite being in a place that is wide open and in the shade of their entire day, the sun does not hit them at sunrise or sunset, because God, the Most High, has veiled it from them. The second is that the door of that cave was open on the north side, so when the sun rose it was to the right of the cave, and when it set it was to its left. The first statement is supported by his saying: That is one of the signs of God. For turning the sun away from them while the gap is directed to a place that it usually reaches is more appropriate in the sense that it is a sign. This is also supported by the generality of the gap and not restricting it to being in such and such a direction. What indicates that the gap is a wide place is the saying of the poet: You have clothed your people with shame and disgrace until they were permitted and left the gap of the house Then the Almighty praised them by saying: He whom God guides meaning to the truth is the one who is guided who attains guidance and attains righteousness and success and he whom He sends astray - you will find for him no protector to guide meaning no supporter to guide him to the truth like Decius and his companions.
18:18: Then the Almighty narrated another aspect of their strange conditions, saying: 18- And you think them awake plural of yaqiz with kasra or fatha of the qaf while they are asleep meaning asleep, and it is the plural of raqid like qa'ood in qa'id. It was said that the reason for this calculation is that their eyes were open while they were asleep. Al-Zajjaj said: Because of their frequent tossing and turning. And We turn them to the right and to the left meaning We turn them in their sleep to both sides so that the earth does not consume their bodies. And their dog stretched out his forelegs narrating a past state, because the active participle does not work if it has the meaning of the past, as is established in the science of grammar. Most of the commentators said: They fled from their king at night, and they passed by a shepherd with a dog who followed them. And the entrance. Abu Ubaid and Abu Ubaidah said that it is the courtyard of the door, and so did the commentators. It was said that it is the threshold. It was responded that the cave does not have a threshold or a door, but rather he meant that the dog is the place of the threshold in the house. If you had looked at them, you would have turned away from them in flight. Al-Zajjaj said: Farran is in the accusative case as a source meaning turning away, and farar is escaping. And you would have been filled it was read with a shaddah on the lam or a light from them with terror it was read with a sukoon on the ayn or a damma, meaning fear that fills the chest, and the accusative case of terror is in the specification, or that it is a second object, the cause of the terror is the awe that God clothed them with, and it was said that it was the length of their nails and hair and the greatness of their bodies and the wildness of their place, and this is refuted by the Almighty’s saying: We stayed a day or part of a day for that indicates that they did not deny anything about their condition, nor did they find in their nails or hair what indicates a long period.
18:19: 19- And thus We raised them up that they might question one another. The reference is to what was mentioned before it, i.e., just as We did to them what We did of miracles, We raised them up from their sleep. In it is a reminder of His ability to cause death and resurrection together. Then He mentioned the matter for which He raised them, saying: That they might question one another. That is, so that questioning might occur between them and differences and disputes over the duration of their stay would occur, due to what would result from that of the revelation of the situation and the appearance of the dazzling power. Limiting oneself to the reason for questioning does not negate anything else, but rather He singled it out because it follows all the effects. The phrase One of them said, 'How long did you remain?' explains what preceded it of questioning: i.e., how long did you remain in sleep? They said that because they saw in themselves something other than what they usually know. They said, ‘We have stayed a day or part of a day.’ That is, some of them said it in response to a question from one of them who asked. The commentators said that they entered the cave in the morning, and God Almighty sent them at the end of the day, so that is why they said a day. When they saw the sun, they said, Or part of a day, and there was still some of the day left. A similar answer was mentioned in the story of Uzair in Surat Al-Baqarah. They said, ‘Your Lord knows best how long you stayed.’ That is, some others said this statement, either by way of reasoning, or it was an inspiration to them from God Almighty: that is, you do not know how long you will stay, but God Almighty knows it. Then send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city. They turned away from the discussion of the length of the stay, and took up something else, as if the speaker among them said: Leave what you are in of the conversation, and take up something else that concerns you. The fa is for causality, and the silver coin is minted or not minted. Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs from Asim read it with a kasra on the ra’, and Abu Amr, Hamza, and Abu Bakr from Asim read it with a sukoon on it, and it was read with a kasra on the ra’ and the assimilation of the qaf into the kaf, and Ibn Muhaisin read it with a kasra on the waw and a sukoon on the ra’. And their carrying this paper with them is evidence that holding on to some of what a person needs does not contradict trust in God, and the city is Daqsus, which is their city that they lived in, and it is called Tarsus today, as Al-Wahidi said, So let him see which of them has the best food, meaning let him see which of its people has the best food, the most lawful earnings, or the cheapest price. It was said that it is permissible for the pronoun to refer to the foods indicated in the context, as it is said, Zayd tasted good father, meaning that the father is Zayd, and there is some error in that. The verse was used as evidence for the permissibility of slaughtering animals of the People of the Book, because most of the people of Medina were disbelievers, and among them were people who hid their faith. The evidence is that the food is eaten as one eats other things called food. And let him be gentle, meaning he should look carefully so that he does not know or is not cheated. The first is better. This is supported by and let no one perceive you, meaning they should not do anything that leads to perception or causes it. This prohibition includes emphasis on the command to be gentle.
18:20: Then he gave a reason for what preceded of the command and prohibition, saying: 20- If they gain the upper hand over you meaning if they find out about you and know where you are, meaning the people of Medina, they will stone you they will kill you by stoning, and this killing is the worst kind of killing, because that was their custom, and for this reason he singled it out from among the types of killing that occur or return you to their religion meaning they will return you to the religion that you were upon before God guided you, or what is meant by return here is becoming, assuming that they were not upon their religion, and the word in was preferred over the word to to indicate stability, and you will never succeed then in then has the meaning of a condition, as if he said: If you return to their religion, then you will never succeed then, neither in this world nor in the hereafter. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Tzawar he said: You incline towards it. And regarding his statement, Taqridhum he said: You scatter them. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Taqridhum he said: You leave them. “And they are in a recess thereof” he said: The inner place. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr he said: The recess is the empty part of the land, and by empty part he means the side of the land. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And We turn them over the verse he said: Six months on the right side, and six months on the left side. Saeed Ibn Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr regarding the verse he said: So that the earth does not consume their flesh. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid that the name of their dog is Qatmur. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan he said: His name is Qatmir. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, By the entrance he said: In the courtyard. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: On the chapter. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: The purest food he said: The most permissible slaughtering, and they used to slaughter for tyrants. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: The purest food meaning the cleanest, because they used to slaughter for tyrants.
18:21: His saying: 21- And thus We made them stumble meaning, just as We made them sleep and resurrected them, We made them stumble: meaning, We informed the people about them. And informing is called making them stumble, because whoever is unaware of something and stumbles over it, looks at it and recognizes it, so making them stumble was a reason for obtaining knowledge that they may know that the promise of God is true meaning that those whom God made them stumble over may know that the promise of God of resurrection is true. It was said that the king of that era was one of those who denied resurrection, so God showed him this verse. It was said that the reason for making them stumble was that the man whom they sent with the paper money, which was from the strike of Decius to the market, when the people of the market saw it, they accused him of finding a treasure, so they went with him to the king, and he said to him: Where did you find these dirhams? He said: Yesterday I sold some dates for it, so the king knew that he was telling the truth. Then he told him the story, so the king rode and his companions rode with him until they reached the cave. And that the Hour is certain, meaning, so that they may know that there is no doubt about the Resurrection, for whoever witnessed the state of the People of the Cave knows the truth of what God promised regarding the Resurrection. When they disputed among themselves about their affair, the circumstance is related to We made them stumble, meaning, We made them stumble at the time of the dispute and disagreement between those whom God made stumble regarding the matter of the Resurrection. It was said regarding the matter of the People of the Cave regarding the length of their stay, their number, and what they were doing after they had seen them. They said, ‘Build over them a structure,’ so that people would not be able to approach them. That is because when the king and his companions stood over them while they were alive, God killed the young men, so some of them said: Build over them a structure that will conceal them from the eyes of the people. Then the Almighty said, narrating the words of those disputing about them, their number, the length of their stay, and similar matters related to them: “Their Lord is more knowing of them than these disputing about them. They said that. Entrusting knowledge to God, the Most High. It was said that it is from the words of God, the Most High, in response to the words of those disputing about them: that is, leave what you are in of disputing, for I know them better than you. It was said that the circumstance in “when they dispute” is related to an omitted word, which is remember. This is supported by the fact that the stumbling was not at the time of the dispute, but before it. It can be said that those people continued to dispute among themselves century after century, from the time they took refuge in the cave until the time of the stumbling. This is supported by the fact that their story was written on the door of the cave, written by some of their contemporaries from the believers who were hiding their faith, as the commentators said: Those who prevailed in their affair said, ‘Let us build a mosque over them.’ Mentioning the building of a mosque indicates that those who prevailed in their affair are the Muslims. It was said that they are the people of authority and kingship from the mentioned people, for they are the ones who prevail over the affair of those other than them, and the first is more appropriate. Al-Zajjaj said: This indicates that when their affair became apparent, the believers prevailed in the resurrection and revival. Because mosques are for believers.
18:22: 22- They will say, 'Three, their dog is the fourth' These people who say that they are three, five, or seven, are the ones who disputed their number during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the People of the Book and the Muslims. It was said that they are the People of the Book in particular. In any case, it is not meant that they all said all of that, rather some of them said such and such, some of them said such and such, and some of them said such and such. Three, their dog is the fourth: meaning they are three people, and the phrase their dog is the fourth is in the accusative case as a state: meaning the state of their dog making them four by joining them. And they say, 'Five, their dog is the sixth' The speech about it is like the speech before it, and the accusative case of stoning by the unseen is in the state: meaning stoning or as a source, meaning they stone by stoning. Stoning by the unseen is saying by conjecture and guesswork without certainty, and those described as stoning by the unseen are both groups who say that they are three, and those who say that they are five. And they say, 'Seven, their dog is the eighth' as if the statement of this group is closer to being correct. Indicating that they are not included in the ranks of those who throw stones at the unseen. It was said that the appearance of the waw in this sentence indicates that it is intended in the first two sentences. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: His saying: Their fourth is their dog, and their sixth is their dog are two sentences in which the conjunction is dispensed with because they include the mention of the first sentence, which is His saying three, and the estimate: They are three, thus Al-Wahidi narrated it from Abu Ali, then he said: This is the meaning of Al-Zajjaj’s saying about the inclusion of the waw in their eighth and its exclusion from the first, and it was said that it is added for emphasis, and it was said that it is the waw of eight, and its mention is common on the tongues of the Arabs when they reach eight as in the saying of the Most High: And its gates were opened and His saying: Wives and virgins. Then God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform those who differed about their number in a way that would end the dispute between them, so He said: “Say: My Lord knows their number better than you, O you who differ.” Then He established knowledge of that for a few people, so He said: None knows them, meaning He knows their selves, let alone their number, or He does not know their number, deleting the added word, except a few of the people, then God Almighty forbade His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from arguing with the People of the Book regarding the People of the Cave, so He said: So do not… They argue about them in the language of argumentation: it is said that someone argues, argumentatively, and then the Almighty excepted from a person what was apparent and clear, so He said: Except for an apparent argument meaning not going into depth in it, which is that he tells them only what God revealed to him. Al-Razi said: It is that he does not lie to them in specifying that number, but rather says that this specification has no evidence, so it is necessary to stop, then the Almighty forbade him from asking a fatwa about their matter, so He said: And do not ask a fatwa about them from any of them meaning do not ask a fatwa about their matter from those who delve into them from any of them, because the one who gives a fatwa must be more knowledgeable than the one asking the fatwa, and here the matter is the opposite, especially in the incident of the People of the Cave, and in what God told you about that is what makes you independent of asking someone who has no knowledge.
18:23: 23- And never say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow.’ That is, for something you intend to do in the future, so He referred to it as tomorrow, and did not mean tomorrow specifically, so tomorrow is included in it primarily.
18:24: Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said when the Jews asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the report of the young men, he said: I will tell you tomorrow, and he did not say God willing, so the revelation was withheld from him until it was difficult for him, so God revealed this verse commanding him to make an exception with God’s will, saying: If you say about something that I will do that tomorrow, then say God willing. Al-Akhfash, Al-Mubarrad, Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said: Do not say of anything, I will do that tomorrow, unless you say, God willing. So the word say was implied, and when he deleted say he transferred it to the future tense. It was said that this exception is empty: that is, do not say that in any situation, except when it is connected to the will of God, which is that you say, God willing, or at any time except when God wills that you say it absolutely. It was said that the exception is in the course of support, as if it was said: Do not say it ever, like his statement: And it is not for us to return to it except that God wills, because their return to their religion is something that God does not will. And remember your Lord when you forget, the exception is by the will of God: that is, say, God willing, whether the period is short or long. Scholars have differed on the period in which it is permissible to add an exception after the thing excepted, according to well-known statements in their places. It was said that the meaning is And remember your Lord by seeking forgiveness if you forget and say, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer than this in right conduct’ referred to by His statement, Which of this is the report of the People of the Cave? meaning, say, O Muhammad, Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer than this report of the signs and evidence indicating my prophethood. Al-Zajjaj said: Perhaps my Lord will give me signs of prophethood that are nearer to right conduct and more indicative than the story of the People of the Cave. And God did that to him when He gave him knowledge of the unseen of the Messengers and their report that was clearer in argument and closer to right conduct than the report of the People of the Cave. It was said that the reference is to His statement, And remember your Lord when you forget, meaning, Perhaps my Lord will guide me at this time of forgetfulness to something else in place of this forgotten thing, and closer to right conduct and closer to good and benefit. The first is more appropriate.
18:25: 25- And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine. The majority of scholars read it with the tanween of one hundred and the accusative of years, so according to this reading, years is a substitute or an explanatory conjunction. Al-Farra, Abu Ubaidah, Al-Zajjaj and Al-Kisa'i said: There is an advancement and delay in it, and the estimate is three hundred years. Abu Ali Al-Farsi preferred the first. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read by adding one hundred to years, and according to this reading, years is a distinction by placing the plural in place of the singular in the distinction like the Almighty's saying: By the losers in their deeds. Al-Farra said: And some of the Arabs place years in place of year. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: These numbers that are added in the famous to the singular, about three hundred men and a garment, may be added to the plural, and in the Mushaf of Abdullah, three hundred years. Al-Akhfash said: The Arabs hardly say one hundred years. Ad-Dahhak read it as thalathma’un with a waw, and the majority read it as tisa’an with a kasra on the ta’, and Abu Amr read it with a fatha. This is a statement from God, the Exalted, about the length of their stay. Ibn Jarir said: The Children of Israel differed about the length of time that had passed for them after they were stumped. Some of them said: They stayed for three hundred and nine years, so God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that this length of time was while they were asleep, and that what came after that was unknown to mankind.
18:26: So God ordered that knowledge of that be returned to Him, so He said: 26- "Say: God knows best how long they stayed." Ibn Atiyyah said: His saying in this way that they stayed the first means on the Day of the Cave, and they stayed the second means after they were found until the time of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or until they died. Some of them said: When He said: And they increased by nine, the people did not know whether it was hours, days, weeks, months, or years, and the Children of Israel differed according to that, so God ordered that knowledge be returned to Him regarding the nine, so it is vague according to this. The first is more appropriate, because what appears from the speech of the Arabs, which is understood according to their language, is that nine years, as evidenced by the fact that the number in this speech is for years, not months, days, or hours. Al-Zajjaj said that what is meant is three hundred solar years and three hundred and nine lunar years, and this is only from Al-Zajjaj as an approximation. Then, the Almighty confirmed that He is the only One with knowledge of what they remained, by saying: To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, meaning that what is hidden in them and absent of their conditions is not known to anyone else. Then, He increased the exaggeration and emphasis, so He came with what indicates astonishment at His perception of what is seen and heard, so He said: I see and hear with it, so this astonishment indicates that His affair, the Almighty, in His knowledge of what is seen and heard is outside of what is perceived by those who perceive. And that in His knowledge the unseen and the present, the hidden and the apparent, the small and the great, the subtle and the dense are equal. It is as if its origin is what I see and what I hear, then it was transferred to the imperative form for the purpose of creation. The letter ba is redundant according to Sibawayh, and Al-Akhfash disagreed with him. The discussion is established in the science of grammar. They have no protector besides Him. The pronoun refers to the people of the heavens and the earth. It was also said to the people of the cave, and it was also said to the contemporaries of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the infidels: meaning they have no protector who would befriend them or take care of their affairs or support them. This is a statement of the extent of His power and that all are under His control. And He does not share in His rule with anyone. The majority of scholars read it with the kaf raised as a report on the authority of God Almighty. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Abu Raja’ and Qatadah read it with the ta’ above and the kaf being silent as a prohibition for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to make a partner for God in His rule. This reading was narrated on the authority of Ibn Amir. Mujahid read it with the ta’ and the jazm. Jacob said: I do not know its meaning. What is meant by God’s judgment is what He decrees, or knowledge of the unseen, and the first is more appropriate. Knowledge of the unseen is included in this primarily, for His knowledge, glory be to Him, is part of His judgment. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And thus We made them stumble upon, he said: We made them known. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Those who prevailed over their affair said, he said: The princes, or he said: The sultans. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding his statement: They will say three, he said: The Jews. And they will say five, he said: The Christians. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: A stab at the unseen, he said: Casting suspicion. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: None knows them except a few, he said: I am from those few, they were seven. At-Tabarani narrated in al-Awsat on the authority of Ibn Abbas. As-Suyuti said with a sound chain of transmission regarding his statement: None knows them except a few, he said: I am from those few, they were seven, then he mentioned their names. Ibn Kathir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the narration of Qatada, Ata’, and Ikrimah, then he said: These are sound chains of transmission back to Ibn Abbas that they were seven. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So do not dispute about them, he said: What I have told you is sufficient. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abasa regarding his statement: And do not consult anyone of them about them, he said: The Jews. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And do not say about anything, the verse, he said: If you forget to say about something, I will do it, and you forget to say, Insha God, then say, Insha God, when you remember. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he used to see the exception even after a year, then he recited, And remember your Lord when you forget. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: It is specific to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one has the right to make an exception except in connection with an oath. Saeed bin Mansour narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: Every exception that is connected does not commit perjury on its owner, but if it is not connected, then he commits perjury. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Solomon, son of David, said: ‘I will go around tonight to seventy women, and in another narration: ninety, each of whom will give birth to a boy who will fight in the cause of God.’ The angel said to him: ‘Say, ‘If God wills,’ but he did not say it. So he went around and only one of them gave birth to a boy who was half a human being. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if he had said, ‘If God wills,’ he would not have broken his oath, and his need would have been met.’” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ikrimah: If you forget, he said: If you get angry. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of al-Hasan: If you forget, he said: If you do not say, ‘If God wills.’ Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man interprets the verse and thinks that it is like this, then he falls as far as the distance between the heavens and the earth. Then he recited: And they remained in their cave, the verse, then he said: How long did the people remain? They said: Three hundred and nine years. He said: If they had stayed like that, God would not have said: “Say: God knows best how long they stayed,” but He related the statement of the people and said: “They will say: Three,” until His saying: Guessing at the unseen, so He informed that they did not know. Then He said: They will say: And they stayed in their cave for three hundred years and added nine. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah in the narration of Ibn Mas’ud, and they said: And they stayed in their cave the verse: meaning that the people said it. Do you not see that he said: “Say: God knows best how long they stayed?” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When this verse was revealed: And they stayed in their cave for three hundred, it was said: O Messenger of God: Days, months or years? So God revealed: Years, and added nine. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of al-Dahhak without mentioning Ibn Abbas. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: I see and hear it, he said: God says it.
18:27: His saying: 27- And recite what has been revealed to you God the Almighty commanded him to persevere in reciting the Book revealed to him. It was said that it is possible that the meaning of his saying: And recite and follow, is a command to recite, not to recite, and from the Book of your Lord is a clarification of what was revealed to him. There is no changing His words meaning there is no one able to change or alter them, and only He is able to do that. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning what God has informed and commanded, there is no changing it, and based on this the interpretation is: There is no changing the ruling of His words. And you will not find any refuge besides Him Al-Multahid: the refuge, and the root of the grave is: inclination. Al-Zajjaj said: You will not find anyone who turns away from His commands and prohibitions, and the meaning is: If you do not follow the Qur'an and recite it and act according to its rulings, you will not find anyone to turn to or a place to incline towards, and this verse is the last story of the People of the Cave.
18:28: Then the Almighty explained in another type as is the habit of the Noble Book, saying: 28- "And be patient with those who call upon their Lord." It was mentioned in Al-An'am that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade the poor believers from being driven away by his saying: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord." And the Almighty commanded him here to confine himself with them, so the patience of the soul is its confinement, and the mention of the morning and evening is a metaphor for continuing to supplicate at all times. It was said at the two ends of the day, and it was said that what is meant is the afternoon and dawn prayers. Nasr bin Asim, Malik bin Dinar, Abu Abd Al-Rahman and Ibn Amir read "Al-Ghadwah" with the letter waw, and they argued that it is written in the Qur'an as such with the letter waw. Al-Nahhas said: This does not necessarily mean that they wrote life and prayer with the letter waw, and the Arabs hardly say al-ghudwah. The meaning of they want His face is that they want the pleasure of God, the Most High, with their supplication. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. Then God, the Most High, commanded him to watch their conditions, saying: And let not your eyes pass beyond them, meaning let not your eyes pass beyond them to others. Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is do not turn your eyes away from them. Al-Zajjaj said: Do not turn your sight to others of those with appearances and adornments. Its use with an is to include the meaning of prophecy, from ‘adatuhu ‘an al-amr: meaning you turned it away from it. It was said that its meaning is do not despise them with your eyes. You want the adornments of the worldly life, meaning sitting with the people of honor and wealth. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state: meaning the state of your wanting that. This is if the subject of want is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If the subject is a pronoun referring to the eyes, then the meaning is: wanting the adornments of the worldly life. Attributing the will to the eyes is a metaphor, and the singularity of the pronoun is for the sake of connection, like the poet’s saying: Whose eyes slip and fall? And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance. That is, We have made him heedless by sealing it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade obeying one whose heart God has made heedless of His remembrance, such as those who asked him to remove the poor from his assembly. They asked to remove those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, while they are heedless of the remembrance of God. Despite this, they are among those who followed their desires and preferred them over the truth, so they chose polytheism over monotheism. And whose affair is excessive. That is, exceeding the limit of moderation, from their saying: a horse is excessive if it is ahead of the horses, so according to this it is from excess, and it was said that it is from negligence, which is shortcoming and waste. Al-Zajjaj said: And whoever is weak in his affair, it wastes him and destroys him.
18:29: Then the Almighty explained to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what He says to those heedless ones, saying: 29- And say, 'The truth is from your Lord' meaning, say to them: What was revealed to you and what you were commanded to recite is the truth that comes from God, not from anyone else, so that it can be changed or altered. It was said that what is meant by the truth is patience with the poor. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning what I have brought to you The truth is from your Lord meaning, I did not bring it to you from myself, rather I have brought it to you from God. So whoever wills - let him believe, and whoever wills - let him disbelieve. It was said that it is part of the statement that He commanded His Messenger to say, and the fa is to arrange what comes before it according to what comes after it. It is possible that it is from the words of God Almighty, not from the statement that He commanded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say, and it contains a severe threat, and the meaning is: Say to them, O Muhammad, the truth is from your Lord, and after you say this statement to them, whoever wills to believe in God and believe you - let him believe, and whoever wills to disbelieve in Him and belie you - let him disbelieve. Then he emphasized and intensified the threat, saying: Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers, meaning, We have prepared and made ready for the wrongdoers who chose to disbelieve in God, deny Him, and reject His prophets, a great fire, whose walls will surround them, meaning, it will encompass them. A canopy is one of the canopies. Al-Jawhari said: It is what is extended over the courtyard of the house, and every house made of a piece of wood is a canopy. From this is the saying of Ru’bah: Oh, Hakam bin Al-Mundhir bin Jarud, the canopy of glory is extended over you. The poet said: He is the entrance to the house of Al-Nu'man, whose name is Sadur Al-Fuel, after the house of Masradaq. Salam bin Jandal said it when the king of Persia killed the king of the Arabs, Al-Nu'man bin Al-Mundhir, under the feet of elephants. Ibn Al-A'rabi said: Its canopy is its wall. Al-Qutaybi said: The canopy is the room that surrounds the tent. The meaning is that the canopy of fire surrounded the infidels, likening what surrounds them of fire to the canopy surrounding those in it. And if they call for help from the heat of the fire, they will be helped with water like molten iron. Al-Zajjaj said: They will be helped with water like molten lead or brass. It was also said that it is the dregs of oil. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: It is everything that has been melted from the gems of the earth, such as iron, lead, and copper. It was also said that it is a type of tar. Then he described this water with which they were being given relief as burning faces if it was presented to them their faces would become burnt from its heat. What a bad drink is this drink of theirs, and what a bad fire is a resting place a reclining place. It is said I rested meaning I leaned on, and the root of Irtifaqa is the erection of the elbow, and it is said Irtifaqa is a man who sleeps on his elbow. Al-Qatibi said: it is the council, and it was said: the community.
18:30: 30- Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds This is the beginning of the promise to the believers after the threat to the disbelievers is over. The meaning is: Indeed, those who have believed in the truth that was revealed to you and done righteous deeds, Indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did good deeds. This is the report of those who believed, and the pronoun is omitted: meaning, whoever among them did good deeds.
18:31: And sentence 31 - "For them are the Gardens of Eden is a resumption of the explanation of the reward, and the reference to those who were mentioned before, and it was said that those may be the report of those who believed, and the sentence Indeed, We will not waste is an objection, and those may be report after report, and the discussion of the Gardens of Eden and how rivers flow beneath them has already been presented They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold" Al-Zajjaj said: bracelets is the plural of bracelet, and bracelet is the plural of bracelet, and it is an adornment worn on the forearm of the hand and it is from the adornment of kings, it was said that each one of them is adorned with three bracelets: one of silver, one of pearls, and one of gold, and the apparent meaning of the verse is that they are all of gold, and it is possible that the speaker's statement is a combination of the verses because God Almighty said in another verse: "Bracelets of silver" and because He said in another verse: "And pearls and from in His statement of bracelets is for the beginning, and in of gold" is for clarification. Al-Farra’ said: They will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade. Al-Kisa’i said: Fine silk is singular and brocade is thick. The commentators said the same. It was also said that brocade is silk, as the poet said: And the brocade was her dress It was said that it is woven with gold. Al-Qatibi said: It is Persianized. Al-Jawhari said: Its diminutive is Abiraq, and green was singled out because it is in harmony with the eyesight and because it is the best color. Reclining therein on couches. Al-Zajjaj said: Couches is the plural of arakeeh, which are the beds in bridal chambers. It was said that they are golden beds crowned with pearls and rubies. The root of atakka is taka’ or taka’, and the root of mutaka’een is mutaka’een, and reclining is leaning on something. Yes, the reward is that with which God rewarded them. And good are those couches. Reclining means reclining, and this was mentioned earlier. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Seeking refuge he said: Seeking refuge. Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym in Al-Hilyah and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated on the authority of Salman who said: Those whose hearts were to be reconciled came: Uyaynah bin Badr and Al-Aqra’ bin Habis. They said: O Messenger of God, if you would sit in the front of the gathering and be absent from these people and their cloaks, meaning Salman, Abu Dharr and the poor Muslims who were wearing wool cloaks, we would sit with you and talk to you and learn from you. Then God revealed: And recite what has been revealed to you until His statement: Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire. Abu Al-Shaykh added on the authority of Salman that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to look for them until he found them in the back of the mosque remembering God the Most High, so he said: Praise be to God who did not cause me to die until He commanded me to be patient with men from my nation, with you in life and death. Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Sahl bin Hanif who said: The verse And be patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was reciting one of his verses. He went out to look for them and found some people remembering God, including those with disheveled hair, bare skin and tattered clothing. When he saw them, he sat with them and said: Praise be to God who has placed among my nation those with whom I have been commanded to be patient. Al-Bazzar narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed and Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came and a man was reciting Surah Al-Hijr or Surah Al-Kahf and he remained silent. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is the gathering with whom I have been commanded to be patient. There are narrations on this topic. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Nafi’ who said: Abdullah bin Umar informed me regarding this verse And be patient with those who call upon their Lord that they are those who attend the five daily prayers. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Shuaib on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather regarding His statement: And be patient with yourself the verse, he said: It was revealed regarding the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Juwaybir on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance he said: It was revealed regarding Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and that was because he called the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to do something that God disliked, such as expelling the poor from him and bringing close the leaders of the people of Mecca, so God revealed this verse, meaning, whose heart We have sealed meaning monotheism and follows his desire meaning polytheism and whose affair is ever [in] neglect meaning neglect of the command of God and ignorance of God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Buraidah who said: Uyaynah ibn Hisn entered upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a hot day, and Salman was with him wearing a woolen cloak, and the smell of sweat from him spread on the wool. Uyaynah said: O Muhammad, when we come to you, send this man and his likes away from you so that they do not harm us. When we leave, you and they know best. So God revealed: And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless (al-Baqarah 2:17). It has been proven in Saheeh Muslim regarding the reason for the revelation of the verse that includes the meaning of this verse, which is the saying of God the Most High: And do not repel those who call upon their Lord morning and evening. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Waqqas who said: We were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), six men, and the polytheists said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Expel these people so that they do not dare to attack us. He said: “And it was me, Ibn Mas’ud, a man from Hudhayl, Bilal, and two men whose names I forgot. So what God willed to happen occurred to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he spoke to himself, and God revealed: “And do not repel those who call upon their Lord” (al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And his affair was in vain, he said: Wasted. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, And say the truth, he said: It is the Qur’an. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa Al-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So whoever wills - let him believe, and whoever wills - let him disbelieve, he said: Whoever God wills to believe - believes, and whoever God wills to disbelieve - disbelieves, and this is His statement: And you do not will except that God wills - Lord of the worlds. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: In this verse there is a threat and warning. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Its canopy will surround them, he said: A wall of fire. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The canopy of Hell has four walls, the thickness of each wall is a forty-year journey. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Baath narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding his statement: With water like molten metal, he said: Like turbid oil, so that when it is brought near to him, the scalp of his face falls into it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Like molten metal, he said: Black like turbid oil. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Atiyyah who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about molten metal and he said: Thick water like the dregs of oil. Hannad, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he was asked about molten metal, so he called for gold and silver and melted it, and when that was done he said: This is most similar to molten metal which is the drink of the people of Hell and its color is the color of the sky, except that the drink of the people of Hell is hotter than this. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: Do you know what molten metal is? Molten metal is the bottom of oil, meaning its end. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And wretched is the place to rest, he said: A gathering. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The adornment of the believer reaches where the ablution reaches. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu al-Khair Murthad ibn Abdullah, who said: In Paradise there is a tree from which brocade grows, which will be the clothing of the people of Paradise. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Istibraq is thick brocade. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Haytham ibn Malik al-Ta’i, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man may recline on a recliner for the length of forty years, never moving from it or getting tired of it. Whatever his soul desires and whatever delights his eyes comes to him.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The couches are the beds inside the curtains, upon which are the furnishings arranged in the sky a league apart. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Baath on his authority that he said: There is no couch unless the bed is in the chamber. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he was asked about couches and he said: They are chambers on the beds.
18:32: His saying: 32- And give them an example of two men. This example was given by God Almighty for those who are proud of the world and are reluctant to sit with the poor. Therefore, it is connected to His saying: And be patient with yourself. There is a difference of opinion about the two men: are they estimated or verified? Some commentators said the former, while others said the latter. They differed in identifying them. It was said that they were two brothers from the Children of Israel. It was said that they were two Makhzumi brothers from the people of Mecca: one of them was a believer and the other was an unbeliever. It was said that they were the two mentioned in Surat As-Saffat in His statement: A speaker from among them said, ‘Indeed, I had a companion.’ The accusative of for example and two men is that they are the objects of the verb strike. It was said that the first is the second and the second is the first. We made for one of them two gardens, he is the unbeliever, and of grapevines is an explanation of what is in the two gardens: that is, of various vineyards. And We surrounded them with palm trees. “Surrounding” means surrounding, and from it is surrounding the throne. It is said that the people surrounded someone with surrounding means they surrounded him. So the meaning of the verse is: And We made the palm trees surround the two gardens from all sides. “And We placed crops between them,” that is, between the two gardens, and it is their middle, so that each one of them would be a collector of food and fruits.
18:33: Then the Almighty informed about the two gardens that each one of them was giving its fruit and what was in it, so He said: 33- Both gardens produced their fruit. He informed about both with produced, because its wording is singular, so He took into account the aspect of the wording. The Basrans went to the view that both and both are singular nouns that are not dual. Al-Farra' said: It is dual, and it is taken from kull, so the lam was lightened and the alif was added for the dual. Sibawayh said: The alif of both is for the feminine, and the ta is a substitute for the lam of the verb, and it is a waw, and the original is kulwa. Abu Amr said: The ta is attached, and akalhuma means their fruit. And in it is an indication that it has become fit for eating. Abdullah bin Masoud read: All the two gardens produced their fruits, and did not deprive them of anything, meaning they did not reduce anything from their fruits. It is said that he deprived them of their right, meaning he reduced it. He described the two gardens with this description to indicate that they were unlike what is customary in other gardens, as they usually have many in one year and few in the next. And We caused a river to gush forth within them, meaning We caused a river to flow and split between the two gardens to water them constantly without interruption. Fajrna was read with emphasis for emphasis, and with a light emphasis according to the original.
18:34: 34- And he had meaning the owner of the two gardens fruits. Abu Ja`far, Shaibah, `Asim, Ya`qub, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read fruits with the tha' and the meem open, and they read it likewise in His statement, Its fruit was surrounded. Abu `Amr read with the tha' closed and the meem silent in both, and the rest read with the tha' closed in both places. Al-Jawhari said: The singular of fruit is fruit, and the plural of fruit is fruits like mountain and mountains. Al-Farra' said: The plural of fruits is fruits, like book and books, and the plural of fruits is fruits, like neck and necks. It was said that fruit is all wealth, gold, silver, animals, and other things. It was said that it is pure gold and silver. He said to his companion, meaning the owner of the two gardens, the unbeliever, said to his believing companion, while he was conversing with him, meaning the unbeliever was conversing with the believer, and the meaning is: he was reviewing the words and answering them. Conversation is reviewing, and dialogue is responding. I am more wealthy than you and more powerful in men. Men are the group, which is less than ten, and here he meant followers, servants, and children.
18:35: 35- And he entered his Paradise meaning the disbeliever entered his own Paradise. The commentators said: He took his Muslim brother by the hand and brought him into his Paradise, to walk around with him in it and show him its wonders. The singularity of Paradise here may be due to the fact that he did not bring his brother into except one of them, or because when they were connected they were like one, or because he brought him into one, then one, or because the purpose of mentioning them was not related. How far-fetched is what the author of Al-Kashshaf said, that he made Paradise singular to indicate that he has no share in the Paradise that the believers were promised. The phrase and he is unjust to himself is in the accusative case as a state: meaning that the disbeliever is unjust to himself with his disbelief and his conceit. He said, I do not think that this will ever perish meaning that the disbeliever said, due to his extreme heedlessness and long hope: I do not think that this Paradise that you see will perish.
18:36: 36- And I do not think that the Hour will come. He denied the resurrection after denying the passing of his paradise. Al-Zajjaj said: He informed his brother of his disbelief in the passing of the world and the occurrence of the Hour. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a return. The lam is the particle that introduces the oath, and the meaning is: that if he is returned to his Lord, it is obligatory and predestined, as his companion claimed, and the lam in I will surely find is the answer to the oath, and the condition: that is, I will surely find better than this paradise on that day, in the copies of the Qur'an of Mecca, Medina, and Syria, better than them, and in the copies of the Qur'an of the people of Basra and Kufa, better than it is singular, and returning is in the accusative case as a distinction: that is, a return and a consequence. He said this by comparing the absent to the present. And that since he was rich in this world, he will be rich in the hereafter, deceived by what he has become of wealth, which is a lure for him from God.
18:37: 37- His companion said to him meaning his believing companion said to the unbeliever while he was conversing with him, denying what he said: Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust by saying I do not think that the Hour will come and he said He created you from dust: meaning He made the origin of your creation from dust where He created your father Adam from it, and it is your origin, and the origin of mankind, so every individual has a share of that, and it was said that it is possible that he was a disbeliever in God, so he denied what he was upon of disbelief, and he did not mean that disbelief happened to him because of this statement Then from a sperm-drop which is the proximate substance Then He proportioned you to a man meaning He made you a male human being and adjusted your limbs and completed you, and in this there is an allusion to the evidence of resurrection, and that the One who is able to begin is able to return, and the erection of a man is in the state or the distinction.
18:38: 38- But we are God, my Lord This is how the majority read it, proving the alif after the doubled lakin. Its original form is lakin ana, the hamza was deleted and its vowel was placed on the silent noon before it, so it became lakin, then they found the coming together of the two noons too heavy, so the first was made silent and the second was assimilated, and the pronoun huwa is for the matter, and the sentence after it is its predicate and the whole is the predicate of ana, and the referent is the ya of the pronoun, and the meaning of the statement is: but I am the matter, God is my Lord. The Arabists said: Proving the alif of ana in the connection is weak. Al-Nahhas said: The doctrine of Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra' and Al-Mazini is that the original form is lakin ana, and he mentioned something similar to what we mentioned. It was narrated from Al-Kisa'i that the original form is lakin God huwa rabbi ana. Al-Zajjaj said: Proving the alif in lakana in the insertion is good because the alif was deleted from ana and they brought it instead. He said: And in the reading of Abu, lakana ana huwa God rabbi and Ibn Amir and Al-Muthanna from Nafi’ and Warsh from Ya’qub read lakana in the case of connection and stopping together by proving the alif, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: I am the sword of the tribe, so know me, for I have become a humpbacked warrior. And from it is the saying of Al-A’sha: How am I with the melodies of rhymes and after turning gray? That is enough of a disgrace There is no disagreement about proving it in the pause. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami and Abu al-Aaliyah read, and it was narrated from al-Kisa’i: But He is God, my Lord. Then he denied associating partners with God, saying: And I do not associate anyone with my Lord. This indicates that his brother was a polytheist.
18:39: Then he turned to him and blamed him, saying: 39- And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, 'What God wills'? "Why" is for encouragement: meaning, why did you not say this statement when you entered it? Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: "Ma" is in the nominative case with the meaning of a command: "What God wills meaning, why did you not say when you entered it, The matter is by the will of God, and What God wills will be, and it is possible for Ma" to be a subject and the predicate is understood: meaning, what God wills will be, and it is possible for "Ma" to be a conditional and the answer is omitted: meaning, whatever God wills will be "There is no power except with God meaning, why did you not say What God wills", there is no power except with God, to encourage him to acknowledge that it and what is in it is by the will of God, if He wills He wills it and if He wills He wills it, and to acknowledge his inability, and that what he was able to build it is only by the help of God and not by His strength and power. Al-Zajjaj said: No one has power over what is in his hand of dominion and blessings except with God, and nothing happens except what God wills. Then when He taught him faith and entrusting matters to God Almighty, He answered him about his boasting about wealth and children, saying, If you see that I am less than you in wealth and children. The first object is the ya of the pronoun, and I is a separating pronoun, and less is the second object for seeing if it is scientific, and if it is made visual, then less is in the accusative case as a state, and it is possible that I is an emphasis of the ya of the pronoun, and the accusative of wealth and children is in the distinction.
18:40: 40- Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden. This is the answer to the condition: that is, if you see me poorer than you, then I hope that God, the Exalted, will grant me a garden better than yours in this world or in the Hereafter or in both. And send down upon it a reckoning. That is, He sends down upon your garden a reckoning. Reckoning is a source, meaning reckoning, like forgiveness: that is, an amount that God has determined for it, and it falls into His reckoning, the Exalted, which is the judgment to destroy it. Al-Zajjaj said: Reckoning is from reckoning: that is, He sends down upon it the punishment of reckoning, which is the reckoning of what your hands have earned. Al-Akhfash said: Hisban: meaning goals from the sky. Its singular is Hisbanah, and Abu Ubaidah and Al-Qutaybi said the same. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Al-Hasbanah is a cloud, Al-Hasbanah is a pillow, and Al-Hasbanah is a thunderbolt. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Al-Hasban are arrows that a man shoots into the inside of a reed that is drawn from a bow, then he shoots twenty of them at once, and the meaning is: He sends upon them targets of His punishment: either hail, or stones, or whatever other types of punishment He wishes. And from this is the saying of Abu Ziyad al-Kalabi: The land was hit by a reckoning Any locusts and it becomes a slippery ground meaning the paradise of the unbeliever after God Almighty sends them upon it becomes a plain, meaning a land with no vegetation in it. Its explanation has been presented previously. Slippery: meaning feet slip in it because of its smoothness. It is said that a place is slippery with the fat-ha: meaning it is slipped, and it is originally the source of your saying his foot slipped, slipping, and someone else made it slip. The slippery place is the place where the foot cannot stay steady, and so is the slippery place. The description of the plain with the source is an exaggeration, or the effect is intended by it.
18:41: And sentence 41 - or its water becomes sunken is connected to the sentence before it: and the sunken is the sunken. Describing water with the source is an exaggeration, and the meaning is: that it becomes devoid of water after it had it, and during it that river was always watering it, and the sunken comes to mean sunset, and from it the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb: Is time anything but a night and a day, or the rising of the sun and its changing? You will not be able to seek it means you will not be able to seek deep water, let alone find it and return it, nor will you be able to obtain it by any trick. It was said that the meaning is: you will not be able to seek anything else in its place.
18:42: Then the Almighty informed about the occurrence of what that believer hoped for and expected of the destruction of the unbeliever's paradise, saying: 42- And its fruit is surrounded. We have already mentioned the differences of the reciters in this letter and its interpretation. The origin of the surround is from the enemy surrounding the person as mentioned in His statement: Unless you are surrounded. It is an expression of his destruction and annihilation, and it is connected to an implied meaning as if it was said, then what the believer expected happened and his fruit was surrounded. So he began to turn his hands over, meaning he strikes one hand against the other, which is a metaphor for regret, as if it was said, then he began to regret what he spent in it, meaning in its construction and repair from the money. It was said that the meaning is: his kingdom is turned over and he does not see in it a replacement for what he spent, because the kingdom may be expressed by the hand from their saying, In his hand is money, which is very far-fetched. The phrase And it is empty on its thrones is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, and the state is that that paradise is falling on its pillars that the vineyards are supported by, or some of that paradise has fallen. According to some, it is taken from the word khawwat an-nujum which means they are empty if it falls and does not rain during its period. Hence, the Almighty’s statement: Then those are their houses, desolate because of what they did wrong. It was said that mentioning what has trellises is specific to it, not palm trees and crops, because it is the origin. Also, its destruction is sufficient to mention the destruction of the rest. The phrase and he says, ‘Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord,’ is connected to turning his hands over, or a state of his pronoun: that is, while he is saying, he wished when he saw the destruction of his garden that he had not associated anyone with God so that his garden would be saved from destruction. Or this statement was from him in its true form, not because of the worldly purpose he missed, but with the intention of repenting from polytheism and regretting what he had neglected.
18:43: 43- And he had no party to aid him other than God. A party is the noun of was and its predicate is and they aid him, and they aid him is an attribute of a party, i.e. a supporting party. It is possible that they aid him is the predicate. The first was preferred by Sibawayh and the second was preferred by Al-Mubarrad, who provided evidence with his saying: And he had no equal. The meaning is that he had no party or group to which he could turn and with which he could be aided, and the group that he had boasted about previously did not benefit him. And he was not in his soul defender, i.e. he was not able, by his own strength, to prevent God from destroying His Paradise and taking revenge on him.
18:44: 44- There is the guardianship of God the Truth. Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read the Truth in the nominative case as an attribute of the guardianship, and the people of Medina, the people of Mecca, Asim and Hamza read the Truth in the genitive case as an attribute of God the Almighty. Al-Zajjaj said: The accusative case is permissible as a source and for emphasis, as you say this is yours truly. Al-A'mash, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read Al-Wilayah with a kasrah on the waw, and the rest read it with a fathah. They are two languages with the same meaning, and the meaning there is: that is, in that situation, victory is for God alone, and no one else has the power to do it. It was said that it is in the order of precedence and delay: that is, the guardianship is for God the Truth there. He is the best in reward and the best in consequence meaning, He, glory be to Him, is the best in reward for His friends in this world and the hereafter. And the best in consequence meaning, the outcome. Al-A'mash, Asim, and Hamzah read Aqban with a sukoon on the qaf, and the rest read it with a damma. They have the same meaning: that is, He is the best in consequence for whoever hopes in Him and believes in Him. He said, This is the outcome of so-and-so's matter, and its afterlife means its end. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And We made for one of them two gardens, he said: The garden is the orchard, so he had one garden and one wall, and there was a river between them, and that is why they were two gardens, and that is why he called it a garden because of the wall that was on it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Amr Al-Shaibani, who said: The river of Abi Qurtas is the river of the two gardens. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is a famous river in Ramla. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And you were not wronged in the least from it, he said: It was not diminished, every tree of Paradise is fertile. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah on his authority, And it had fruit, meaning money. Abu Ubaid and Ibn Jarir Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Ibn Abbas read it And it had fruit, with a dammah, and he said: It is types of money. Ibn Abi Shaybah Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, And it had fruit, he said: Gold and silver. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, And he is unjust to himself, meaning: ungrateful for the blessings of his Lord. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Asma bint Umays, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught me words to say when in distress: God, God is my Lord. I do not associate anything with Him. Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id al-Zuhd on the authority of Yahya bin Salim al-Ta’ifi on the authority of someone who mentioned it, who said: “Moses asked his Lord for a need, but He delayed him in coming to him. He said: ‘Whatever God wills.’ Then his need was before him, and he said: ‘O Lord, I have been asking for my need since such and such, and now I have granted it.’ Then God revealed to him: ‘O Moses, do you not know that saying ‘Whatever God wills’ is the most successful way to ask for needs?” Abu Ya`la, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God does not bestow a blessing on a servant in the form of family, wealth, or children, and he says, ‘What God wills, there is no power except with God,’ except that God wards off every calamity from him until his death comes.” And he recited: And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, ‘What God wills, there is no power except with God.’ In its chain of transmission is `Isa ibn `Awn on the authority of `Abd Al-Malik ibn Zararah on the authority of Anas. Abu Al-Fath Al-Azdi said: `Isa ibn `Awn on the authority of `Abd Al-Malik ibn Zararah on the authority of Anas, his hadith is not authentic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from another chain of transmission on the authority of Anas something similar to it, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar to it in Al-Shu`ab on his authority, with a chain of transmission ending with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ahmad narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise beneath the Throne? I said, Yes. He said: That you say, ‘There is no power except with God.’ It has been proven in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Musa that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Shall I not guide you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise? There is no power and no strength except with God. There are hadiths and narrations from the predecessors about the virtue of this statement.
