Ibn Jarir Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then it becomes a slippery ground, he said: Like a barren land. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada regarding his statement: A punishment from the sky, he said: A torment, then it becomes a slippery ground, meaning that what is in it has been harvested and nothing is left in it. Or its water becomes sunken, meaning gone and has sunk into the ground. And its fruit is surrounded, so he begins to wring his hands, he said: clapping over what he spent on it, yearning for what he missed.
18:45: Then the Almighty gave another example for the tyrants of Quraysh, saying: 45- And present to them the similitude of the life of this world, meaning, mention to them something that resembles the life of this world in its beauty, freshness, and quick passing, so that they do not rely on it. This example was presented in Surah Yunus, then the Almighty explained this example, saying: Like water which We have sent down from the sky. It is possible that this is the second object of His saying strike on the basis of making it in the sense of making so the vegetation of the earth mingled with it, meaning the vegetation of the earth mingled with the water until it became even. It was said that the meaning is that the vegetation mingled with each other when the water fell upon it, because the vegetation only mingles and increases with the rain, so the ba in because is causal. So it became the vegetation hasheem, the broken stubble, and it is from the vegetation that it breaks due to the water being cut off from it and it disintegrates. A man who is weak in body is weak, and someone was broken on him if he bent over, and what is in the udder of a camel was broken if he milked it, and he broke the porridge, he broke it. And his narration, and from it the saying of Ibn al-Zubayri: Amr who broke the tharid for his people and the men of Mecca were old and lean The winds scatter it scatters it. Abu Ubaidah and Ibn Qutaybah said: It blows it away. Ibn Kaysan said: It takes it and brings it back. The meanings are similar. Talhah ibn Musarraf read The wind scatters it. Al-Kisa'i said: In Abdullah's reading It scatters it, it is said The wind scatters it and I scatter it. Al-Farra' said: I scatter the man from his horse meaning I turned him over. And God is over all things competent. That is, He gives life to all things and destroys them with His power. He is not incapable of anything.
64:14: 46- Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world. This is a response to the leaders who were proud of their wealth, riches, and children. So God Almighty informed them that this is something that is adorned in this world, not something that will benefit them in the Hereafter, as He said in the other verse: Your wealth and children are only a trial. And He said: Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. That is why He followed this worldly adornment with His saying: And the lasting good deeds, meaning good deeds, which are what the poor Muslims used to do in terms of acts of obedience, are better in the sight of your Lord in reward, meaning better than this adornment of wealth and children in reward, and more beneficial and beneficial to its people. And better in hope, meaning that these good deeds for their people in terms of hope are better than what the people of wealth and children hope for, because they will attain better in the Hereafter than what these rich people hoped for in this world. There is no good in the adornment of this world for the Hereafter to be preferred over it, but this preference was taken out of the statement of God Almighty: The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be the best in settlement. It appears that the lasting good deeds are every good deed, so there is no reason to limit them to prayer as some have said, nor to limit them to a type of remembrance as some others have said, nor to what the poor immigrants used to do in consideration of the reason, because the point is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. And with this you will know that the interpretation of the lasting good deeds in the hadiths as will come does not contradict the application of this wording to what is a good deed other than that. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali who said: Wealth and children are the cultivation of this world, and righteous deeds are the cultivation of the Hereafter, and God has gathered them together for some people. Ibn Abi Shaybah Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and the lasting good deeds he said: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest. Saeed bin Mansour, Ahmad, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Increase the lasting good deeds. It was said: What are they, O Messenger of God? He said: Allahu Akbar God is Great, Tahlil There is No God but God, Tasbeeh Glory be to God, Tahmeed praise be to God, and there is no power and no strength except with God. At-Tabarani, Ibn Shaheen, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) with the wording: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest, and there is no power and no strength except with God, these are the lasting good deeds. An-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani in Al-Saghir, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Take your Paradise. It was said: O Messenger of God, from which enemy has he come? He said: “Rather, your Paradise from the Fire is the saying, ‘Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Great.’ For they will come on the Day of Resurrection in the forefront, behind, and behind, and they are the lasting good deeds.” Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of An-Nu’man ibn Bashir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Behold, Glory be to God, praise be to God, and there is no god but God are the lasting good deeds. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, but he added the takbir and called them the lasting good deeds. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Aishah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, but she added, There is no might nor power except with God. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Ali, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar to it without the phrase There is no power but from God. At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Junadah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a similar statement. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a similar statement. All of these hadiths explicitly state that they are the lasting good deeds. As for what was reported about the virtue of these words without specifying that they are the ones intended in the verse, then there are many hadiths that there is no benefit in mentioning here. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, who said: Everything that is from obedience to God is from the lasting good deeds. His saying: 14- O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you meaning that they are hostile to you and distract you from goodness, and the reason for revelation is included in that primarily, which is that some men from Mecca converted to Islam and wanted to emigrate, but their wives and children did not let them, so God Almighty commanded that they beware of them and not obey them in anything they wanted from them that was contrary to what God wants, and the pronoun in beware of them refers to the enemy, or to the wives and children, but not in general, rather to those among them who are characterized by hostility, and the pronoun is only permissible to pluralize in the first way, because the enemy is used to refer to one, two, and a group. Then God guided them to forgiveness, saying: {But if you pardon and overlook and forgive} meaning, pardon their sins that they committed and leave the blame for them and cover them up, {then indeed, God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful}, with the utmost forgiveness and mercy for you and them. It was said that the man whose wives and children discouraged him from emigrating, when he saw that people had preceded him to it and understood the religion, intended to punish his wives and children, so God revealed {But if you pardon} the verse. The verse is general even if the reason was specific, as we have told you more than once. Mujahid said: By God, he did not do it again in this world, but their love for them led them to take for themselves what is forbidden, so they gave it to them. that
18:47: And His statement: 47- And the Day We set the mountains in motion. Al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read tasir with a dammah on the second letter above and a fathah on the lower yaa' in the passive form, and raising the mountains as a substitute for the subject. Ibn Muhaisin and Mujahid read tasir with a fathah on the upper taa' and a light pronunciation on the basis that the mountains are the subject. The rest read Nasir with the letter nun, so that the subject is God, the Most High, and the mountains are in the accusative case as objects. The first reading is appropriate for the Almighty's saying: And when the mountains are set in motion. The second reading is appropriate for the Almighty's saying: And the mountains will move with a movement. Abu Ubaidah chose the third reading because it is appropriate for His saying: And We will gather them together. Some grammarians said: The estimate is that the lasting good deeds are better with your Lord on the Day We set the mountains in motion. It was said that the agent in the circumstance is a deleted verb, and the estimate is: And remember the Day We set the mountains in motion. The meaning of setting the mountains in motion is removing them from their places and setting them in motion as the clouds move. From this is the Almighty's saying: And they will pass as the clouds pass, then they will return to the earth after God made them as He said: And the mountains will be wiped clean * And they will be scattered dust. The address in His saying: And you will see the earth appearing is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone who is able to see. The meaning of its appearance is its appearance and the disappearance of what covers it from mountains, trees, and buildings. It was said that the meaning of its appearance is the appearance of what is in it of treasures and dead people. As the Almighty said: And it cast out what was in it and became empty, and He said: And the earth brought forth its burdens, so the meaning is: And you see the earth protruding what is in its interior, And We gathered them, meaning the creatures, and the meaning of gathering is gathering: that is, We gathered them to the place of assembly from every place, And We did not leave out a single one of them, so we did not leave out a single one of them. It is said that he left him and he betrayed him if he abandoned him. Antara said: I left him covered in dust, and the people were either wounded or maimed. That is, he left it, and from it comes treachery, because the traitor leaves loyalty to the one who was betrayed. They said: The pond was called a pond because the water went and he left it, and from it comes the woman’s braids because she leaves them behind her.
18:48: 48- And they will be presented before your Lord in ranks. The word rank is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, each nation and group in a row. It was also said that they were presented in one row as in His statement: Then come in a row meaning all together, and it was also said standing. In the verse, their condition is likened to the condition of an army that is presented to the ruler. You have come to Us as We created you the first time is an implied statement: meaning, We said to them, You have come to Us. The kaf in as We created you is an attribute of a deleted source: meaning, a coming like your coming when We created you the first time, or being as We created you the first time: meaning, barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, as mentioned in the hadith. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, We have resurrected you and brought you back as We created you, because His statement, You have come to Us, means, We have resurrected you. “Rather, you claimed that We would not make an appointment for you.” This is a transition and a transition from one statement to another for the purpose of rebuke and rebuke, and it is addressed to those who deny the al-Qiyamah 75:That is, you claimed in this world that you would not be resurrected, and that We would not make an appointment for you to reward you for your deeds and fulfill what We promised you of resurrection and punishment.
18:49: And the sentence 49 - And the book was placed is connected to they presented, and what is meant by the book are the records of deeds, and it was made singular because the definition in it is for the genus, and the placement is either physical, such that the record of each person is placed in his hand: the happy one in his right, and the wretched one in his left, or in the balance. Or rational: that is, He made manifest the deeds of each one, good and evil, in the reckoning that will take place on that Day. Then you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, that is, fearful and apprehensive of what is in the book that is placed because of what follows that of disgrace in that gathering, and the punishment with painful torment. And they will say, ‘Woe to us,’ calling upon themselves for woe for falling into destruction. The meaning of this call has already been explained in Surat Al-Ma’idah. What is this book that leaves out neither small nor great but that it has enumerated it? That is, what is it that does not leave out a small sin or a great sin but that it has contained it, recorded it, and established it. And they will find whatever they did, in this world of sins that warrant punishment, or they will find the reward for what they did, present, written and established. And your Lord does not wrong anyone, that is, He does not punish any of His servants without sin, nor does He diminish the reward that the doer of obedience deserves.
18:50: Then He, the Almighty, returned to responding to the arrogant masters of Quraysh, so He mentioned the story of Adam and the arrogance of Iblis towards him, saying: 50- And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ meaning, remember the time when We said to them, Prostrate, a prostration of greeting and honor, as was previously explained. So they prostrated, in obedience to the command of God and compliance with His request to prostrate, except Iblis, for he refused and was arrogant and did not prostrate. The phrase was of the jinn is a new sentence to explain the reason for his disobedience, that he was of the jinn and not of the angels, and that is why he disobeyed. The meaning of fasqa ‘an amr Rabbih is that he went against the command of his Lord. Al-Farra’ said: The Arabs say, fasqa ‘an amr Rabbih because it came out of it. Al-Nahhas said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of fasqa ‘an amr Rabbih in two opinions: The first is the view of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, that the meaning is: Disobedience came to him when he was commanded, so he disobeyed, and the reason for the disobedience was the command of his Lord. As you say, feed him when he is hungry. The other saying is the saying of Qatrub: that the meaning is with the deletion of the complement: that is, he became immoral in abandoning his command. Then He, the Almighty, was amazed at the state of the one who obeyed Satan in disbelief and sins and disobeyed the command of God, so He said: Then do you take him and his offspring as allies? As if He said: Following what He found from him of refusal and immorality, you take him and his offspring: that is, his children, and it was said that his followers are metaphorically allies other than Me, so you obey them instead of obeying Me and replace them with Me, while the fact is that they: that is, Satan and his offspring are your enemies, that is, enemies. He made it singular because it is a generic name, or because it is likened to sources as in His saying: For they are an enemy to Me, and His saying They are the enemy, that is, how do you do this and replace the One who created you and bestowed upon you all the blessings you have? With someone who has never benefited you, but is an enemy to you, waiting for something to harm you at all times. What an evil substitute for the wrongdoers. That is, those who put things in the wrong place and exchange obedience to their Lord for obedience to Satan. What an evil substitute they have exchanged for God Almighty.
18:51: 51- I did not make them witness to the creation of the heavens and the earth. Most of the commentators said: The pronoun refers to the partners, and the meaning is: If they were partners with Me in the creation of the heavens and the earth and in the creation of themselves, then they would have witnessed the creation of that and participated with Me in it, but they did not witness that, nor did I make them witness to it, so they are not partners with Me. This is evidence of the negation of the equal entailment on the negation of the necessary consequence. It was said that the pronoun refers to the polytheists who sought to expel the poor believers, and what is meant is that they were not partners with Me in managing the world, as evidenced by the fact that I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, and I did not support them, but rather they are like all other creation. It was said that the meaning is that these oppressors are ignorant of what the pen wrote in eternity, because they did not witness the creation of the world, so how can they judge their good condition with God? The first of these aspects is more appropriate because of what is required in the other two aspects of separating the two pronouns. This sentence is renewed to show that they do not deserve the aforementioned taking. Abu Ja`far read, I did not make them witness, and the rest read, I did not make them witness, and it is supported by and I would not have taken the misguiders as a support. The support is often used in the meaning of help, because the support is the pillar of the hand, and from this is His saying, We will strengthen your support with your brother, meaning, We will aid you and strengthen you with him. It is said, I supported someone with someone if you sought his help. The support was mentioned as a metaphor, and the misguiders were specifically mentioned for the sake of increase. Blame and rebuke. Meaning: I did not seek their help in creating the heavens and the earth, nor did I consult them, and I did not take the devils or the disbelievers as helpers. The word al-‘udhd is singular to agree with the pauses. Abu Ja’far al-Jahdari read wa ma kunt with a fatha on the ta’, meaning that the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: meaning, and you, O Muhammad, did not take them as helpers, nor is that correct for you. The rest read it with a damma on the ta’. There are eight dialects for ‘udhd, the most eloquent of which is with a fatha on the ‘ayn and a damma on the dad, and the majority read it this way. Al-Hasan read ‘udhdan with a damma on the ‘ayn and the dad, and Ikrimah read it with a damma on the ‘ayn and a sukoon on the dad, and al-Dahhak read it with a kasra on the ‘ayn and a fatha on the dad, and ‘Isa ibn ‘Umar read it with a fatha on both of them, and the dialect of Tamim is with a fatha on the ‘ayn and a sukoon on the dad.
18:52: Then he returned to frightening them with the conditions of the Day of Resurrection, saying: 52- And the Day when He will say, 'Call upon My partners whom you claimed' Hamzah, Yahya bin Waththab, and 'Isa bin 'Umar read 'We say' with a 'nun', and the rest read with a 'ya' with a 'sub': meaning, remember the Day when God Almighty will say to the disbelievers, rebuking and reprimanding them, 'Call upon My partners whom you claimed would benefit you and intercede for you', and He, glory be to Him, added them to Himself in accordance with what the polytheists believe, God is exalted above that. So call upon them meaning, they did what God commanded them to do of calling upon partners, but they did not respond to them at that time, meaning, they did not even respond to them, let alone benefit them or defend them. And We made between them a place of destruction meaning, We made between these polytheists and those whom they made partners with God a place of destruction. A group of commentators mentioned that it is the name of a deep valley through which God, glory be to Him, separated them, and based on this, it is the name of a place. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Every barrier between two things is a cause of destruction. Al-Farra' said: The destroyer is the ruiner. The meaning is: We made their connection in this world a cause of destruction for them in the Hereafter. It is said: Wabaqa yubqa, so he is wabaqa, this is how al-Farra' mentioned it in the sources. Al-Kisa'i narrated: Wabaqa yubqa and wabuqan, so he is wabaq. According to this, what is meant by the ruiner is the torment of the Fire in which they share. The first is more appropriate, because among the things they claimed that they were partners with God were the angels, Ezra, and the Messiah, so the destroyer is the place that separates them. Abu Ubaidah said: The destroyer here is the appointed time for destruction, and it has been established in the language that awbaqahu means devastated him, and from this is the saying of Zuhair: Whoever buys praise with his money will protect his honor from every ugly and deadly sin. But the first meaning is appropriate for the meaning of the verse.
18:53: 53- And the criminals will see the Fire and will think that they will fall into it. The criminals are the subject of the pronoun to indicate the increase in blame for them with this description recorded against them, and the thought here means certainty. And falling into it is mixing with falling into it, and it was said that the disbelievers will see the Fire from a far place and will think that, And they will find no way out from it, meaning a way out to which they can turn, or a departure, because the Fire has surrounded them from every side. Al-Wahidi said: The way out is the place to which one turns. Al-Qatibi said: meaning a way out to which they can turn, and it was said a refuge to which they can flee. The meaning is similar in all of them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And you will see the earth barren, he said: There are no buildings or trees on it. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Mujahid. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He leaves out neither a small nor a great sin, he said: The small is a smile, and the big is a laugh. Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Ibn Abi Hatim added on his authority: The small is a smile in mockery of the believers, and the big is a loud laugh. I say: Small and big are indefinite in the context of negation, so every sin that is described as small falls under that, and every sin that is described as big, so nothing remains of the sins except that God counts it. And whatever sin is ambiguous as being small or big, that is only in relation to the servants, not in relation to God, the Most High. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “Among the angels is a tribe called the jinn, and Iblis was one of them. He used to whisper whispers between the heaven and the earth, but he disobeyed, so God became angry with him, so He transformed him into a cursed devil.” Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: He was from the jinn, he said: He was the guardian of Paradise, so he was called the jinn. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority that Iblis was one of the most noble and honorable tribe of angels, and he was the guardian of Paradise. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: May God curse those people who claimed that Iblis was from the angels, and God says that he was from the jinn. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Anbari narrated on his authority that he said: “He was not from the angels for the blink of an eye. He is the origin of the jinn, just as Adam is the origin of mankind.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Al-Suddi regarding his statement: I did not make them witness to the creation of the heavens and the earth, he said: He says: I did not make the devils whom you took with me witness this. And I would not have taken the misguiders as supporters, he said: The devils as supporters. He said: Nor did I take them as supporters on anything they supported me on and helped me. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ali bin Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We placed between them a place of destruction, he said: a place of destruction. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid something similar. Abu Ubaid, Hannad and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from him that he said: A valley in Hell. Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th from Anas regarding the verse that he said: A valley in Hell of pus and blood. Ahmad narrated in Al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi from Ibn Amr that he said: It is a deep valley in Hell through which God will separate the people of guidance from the people of misguidance on the Day of Resurrection. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: They thought that they would fall into it, he said: They knew.
18:54: When the Almighty mentioned the disbelievers’ boasting over the poor Muslims with their wealth and clans and answered them about that and gave them clear examples, He narrated some of the horrors of the Hereafter and said: 54- And We have certainly diversified that is, We repeated and reiterated in this Qur’an for the people that is, for their sake and to care for their interests and benefit of every kind of examples, including the examples mentioned in this Surah. The interpretation of this verse was presented in Surah Bani Israel, and when the disbelievers did not abandon what they were doing of arguing falsely, He concluded the verse by saying: And man is most disputatious of anything. Al-Zajjaj said: What is meant by man is the disbeliever, and he provided evidence that what is meant by the disbeliever is the Almighty’s saying: And those who disbelieve argue with falsehood. It was said that what is meant by it in the verse is Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, and the apparent meaning is generality and that this type is the most disputatious of things, and this is supported by what is proven in the two Sahihs and others from the hadith of Ali “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knocked on his door.” And Fatima at night, and he said: Do you not pray? I said: O Messenger of God, our souls are in the hand of God. If He wills to resurrect us, He will resurrect us. So he turned away when I said that and did not return anything to me. Then I heard him slapping his thigh and saying: And man is most argumentative of anything. The word judgement is in the accusative case as a specification.
18:55: 55- "And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord except that the precedent of the former peoples should come to them. We have already discussed something similar in Surat Bani Israel, and we mentioned that the first an" is in the accusative case, and the second is in the nominative case, and the guidance is the Qur'an and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people here are the people of Mecca, and the meaning is that the added word is omitted: that is, what prevented the people from believing and asking forgiveness is seeking to come to the precedent of the former peoples, or waiting for the precedent of the former peoples to come, and asking forgiveness was added in this surah because what they had neglected of sins was mentioned here, including their arguing with falsehood, and the precedent of the former peoples is that if they did not believe, they would be punished with the punishment of extermination. Al-Zajjaj said: Their precedent is their saying: "If this is the truth from You the verse or the punishment should come to them meaning the punishment of the Hereafter precipitously." Al-Farra' said: "Precipitously is the plural of precipitously": that is, scattered, one after the other, and it was said clearly, and it was said suddenly. What Al-Farra’ said is consistent with the reading of Abu Ja`far, `Asim, Al-A`mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Yahya bin Waththab and Khalaf qablan with two dhammahs, as it is the plural of qabal, like sabil and subul, and what is meant is the types of punishment. The second interpretation is consistent with the reading of the rest with a kasrah on the qaf and a fathah on the ba’, meaning facing and witnessing. It was read with two fathahs with the meaning or the punishment will come to them in the future, and its accusative is in the state. So the meaning of the verse is that they will not believe and will not seek forgiveness except when the punishment of this world descends upon them that will eradicate them, or when the types of punishment of the Hereafter come or witness it.
18:56: 56- "And We do not send the messengers of Our messengers to the nations except while they are bringers of good tidings to the believers and warners" to the disbelievers, so the exception is emptied of the most general of the general, and the explanation of this has been presented. "And those who disbelieve argue with falsehood to refute thereby the truth" meaning to remove the truth by arguing with falsehood and invalidate it. The root of refutation is slipping: it is said that his foot slid, meaning it slipped, refuted, refutation, and refutation of the sun from the middle of the sky means it disappeared, and refutation of his argument means it became invalidated, and from that is the saying of Tarafa: Abu Munther, you sought loyalty, but you gave it up and you were stubborn as a camel strays from the right path. Among the false arguments of these infidels is their saying to the Messengers, You are only human beings like us, and the like. And they took My verses, meaning the Qur’an, and what they were warned of, of threats and intimidation, as a joke, meaning play and falsehood. This was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah.
18:57: 57- And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them meaning, no one is more unjust to himself than he who is admonished by the verses of his Lord, whether revealed or created, or both, but he takes them lightly and turns away from accepting them, and does not contemplate them properly and think about them properly and forgets what his hands have put forth of disbelief and sins, so he does not repent from them. It was said that forgetfulness here means abandonment, and it was said that it is in its true sense Indeed, We have placed coverings over their hearts, lest they understand it meaning covers. And coverings are the plural of kinan, and the sentence is an explanation for their turning away and forgetfulness. Al-Zajjaj said: God the Almighty informed us that these people have a seal on their hearts and in their ears is deafness meaning, We have placed a weight in their ears that prevents them from hearing it, and the explanation of this has been presented in Al-An'am And if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided then because God has sealed their hearts because of their disbelief and sins.
18:58: 58- "And your Lord is the Forgiving, the Possessor of Mercy meaning He is the One who forgives a lot, and the Possessor of mercy that encompasses everything, so He did not hasten to punish them, and for this reason He said, If He were to punish them for what they earned meaning because of what they earned of sins, including disbelief, argumentation, and turning away, He would have hastened the punishment for them" because they deserved it. "Rather He made for them an appointed time" meaning a set term for their punishment, it was said that it is the punishment of the Hereafter, and it was said that it was the day of Badr. "They will not find besides Him a refuge" meaning a shelter to which they can turn. Abu Ubaidah said, "Savement, and it was said, Escape", and from this is the saying of the poet: No, you left it to the Amiris and did not speak Al-A'sha said: I may make the master of the house forget me, and he may be wary of me, but he will not be able to do so. Anything that survives.
18:59: 59- "And those towns meaning the towns of Aad and Thamud and their likes We destroyed them" this is the predicate of the demonstrative pronoun and the towns are its description, and the discussion is about the deletion of an added word: meaning the people of the towns We destroyed them "when they wronged meaning the time when they wronged by disbelief and sins and We appointed for their destruction an appointed time meaning a specific time, and Asim read their destruction" with the opening of the meem and the lam, and it is the source of halaka, and Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' permitted the breaking of the lam and the opening of the meem, and Hafs read that way, and the majority read it with the closing of the meem and the opening of the lam. Al-Zajjaj said, "Muhalak" is a name for the time, and the meaning is: for the time of their destruction. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Unless there comes to them the punishment of the former peoples, he said: The punishment of the former peoples. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-A’mash regarding his statement: Openly, he said: Openly. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Suddenly. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And he forgot what his hands had put forth, he said: He forgot what had come before of the many sins. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Because of what they earned, he said: Because of what they did. Ibn Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, Rather, for them is an appointed time, he said: The appointed time is on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali Ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: A refuge, he said: A shelter. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, A refuge, he said: A place of protection.
18:60: The circumstance in His statement: 60- "And when he said is related to an omitted verb which is remember". It was said that the reason for mentioning this story in this surah is that when the Jews asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the story of the People of the Cave and said: If he tells you, then he is a prophet, otherwise he is not. God mentioned the story of Moses and Al-Khidr as a reminder that a prophet is not required to be knowledgeable about all stories and report. The scholars have agreed that the Moses mentioned is Moses bin Imran, the prophet sent to Pharaoh. A group, no attention should be paid to what Nawf Al-Bakali says, said: He is not the son of Imran, but rather he is Moses bin Mishi bin Yusuf bin Ya'qub, and he was a prophet before Moses bin Imran. This is false and has been rejected by the righteous predecessors from the Companions and those after them as in Sahih Al-Bukhari and others. What is meant by his young man here is Joshua bin Nun. Al-Wahidi said: They agreed that he was Joshua bin Nun, and his mention has already been mentioned in Al-Ma’idah and at the end of Surat Yusuf. Whoever said that Moses was the son of Misha said: This young man was not Joshua bin Nun. Al-Farra’ said: He was called the young man of Moses because he was close to him, taking knowledge from them and serving him. The meaning of I will not leave is I will not stop. From this is his saying: We will not stop being devoted to him. And from this is the saying of the poet: And may God keep my people, praise be to God, prosperous and glorious If the word "Barha means Zala, then it is an incomplete verb, and its predicate here is omitted based on the indication of what comes after it, which is until I reach the meeting of the two seas." Al-Zajjaj said: "La abhra means La azal, and the predicate was omitted because the state of travel indicates it, and because his saying until I reach" is a set limit, so it must have a limit, so the meaning is: I will not stop walking until I reach, and it is possible that it is meant that my journey will not depart until I reach, and it was said that the meaning of "La abhra" is: I will not leave you until I reach the meeting of the two seas, and it was said that it is possible that it is from the perfect "Barha, meaning Zala", and the meeting of the two seas is their meeting place. It was said that what is meant by "Bahrain" is the Persian and Roman seas, and it was said that the Jordan Sea and the Red Sea, and it was said that the meeting of the two seas is near Tangier, and it was said that it is in Africa. A group said that what is meant by "Bahrain is Moses and Al-Khidr, and this is very weak, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas and it is not correct or I spend a long time" meaning I travel for a long time. Al-Jawhari said: "Al-Haqb" with the dammah is eighty years. Al-Nahhas said: What the linguists know is that the era and the period are an indefinite and vague period of time, just as a group or a people from them are unlimited, and its plural is eras. The reason for this determination to travel from Moses, peace be upon him, is what was narrated that Moses was asked, who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said, I am, so God revealed to him: The one who is more knowledgeable than you is a servant of Mine at the confluence of the two seas.
18:61: 61- When they reached meaning Moses and his boy the place where they met meaning between the two seas. Meeting was added to the circumstance as an extension. It was said that the two seas means separation meaning that the two separated seas meet there. It was said that the pronoun refers to Moses and Al-Khidr, meaning that they reached the place where they met. The two seas according to this means connection because it is one of the opposites, and the first is more appropriate. They forgot their fish The commentators said that they had stocked up on a salted fish in a basket, and they would take from it when they needed food. God had made its loss a sign for them that they had found what they wanted. The meaning is that they forgot about his matter, and it was said that the one who forgot was Moses’ young man, because he entrusted the matter of the whale to him, and ordered him to inform him if he lost it. So when they reached the seashore, his young man put down the basket in which the whale was, and God revived it, so it moved and swayed in the basket, then it slipped into the sea. That is why He said: Then it took its way in the sea, a tunnel. The accusative of a tunnel is that it is the second object of took, meaning it took a tunnel, and a tunnel is a tunnel that is in the ground for the lizard and similar animals. That is because God, glory be to Him, held back the flow of water at the place where the whale slipped, so it became like an arch, so He likened the path of the whale in the sea while remaining and the water retreating from it to a tunnel, which is a hole dug in the ground. Al-Farra’ said: When he fell into the water, his path in the sea froze and was like a shoal. When they passed that place where the rock was and the whale had gone into it, they set off, and they were afflicted with what afflicts a traveler of fatigue and exhaustion, and they did not find fatigue until they passed the place where Al-Khidr was.
18:62: That is why the Almighty said: 62- So when they had passed meaning the meeting place of the two seas which was set as a meeting place, He said to his boy, ‘Bring us our lunch’ which is what is eaten in the morning, and Moses wanted to bring him the fish which they had carried with them. We have certainly encountered fatigue on this journey of ours meaning exhaustion and weariness. The commentators said: The reference in His saying this journey of ours is to the journey that would take place between them after passing the mentioned place, for they did not encounter fatigue except in that and not what came before it.
18:63: 63- He said, 'Have you seen when we took refuge at the rock?' That is, Moses' young man said to Moses. The meaning of the question is his astonishment at Moses for what happened to him of forgetfulness there, despite the fact that that matter is something that cannot be forgotten, because he had witnessed a great matter of God's dazzling power. The object of Have you seen is omitted because what he mentioned of forgetfulness indicates it, and the meaning is: Have you seen what happened to me, or befell me at that time and place? And that rock was at the junction of the two seas, which is the meeting place. Rather, he mentioned it without mentioning the junction of the two seas because it includes an additional specification of the place, because it is possible that the junction is a large place that includes the place of the rock and other things. He attributed forgetfulness to the fish, not to the food that was mentioned earlier, to clarify that that desired food is that fish that they made as provision for them, and a sign of finding what they wanted. Then he mentioned what is the reason for the occurrence of that forgetfulness, so he said: And nothing made me forget it except Satan, due to what he does of whispering, and that I should remember it is a substitute for inclusion from the pronoun in that I should forget it. In the Mushaf of Abdullah: And nothing made me forget to remember it except Satan. “And he took his way in the sea as a wonder.” The accusative of wonder is that it is the second object, as mentioned in a flock, and the adverb is in the accusative case as a state. It is possible that this is from the words of Joshua, who informed Moses that the whale took its way as a wonder to the people. The place of wonder is that a whale that had died and eaten its half comes back to life, then jumps into the sea and the trace of its running in the water remains, the trace of which is not erased by the running of the sea water. It is possible that it is from the words of God Almighty to explain another aspect of the matter of the whale, so what is between the two words is an interruption.
18:64: 64- He said, 'That is what we were seeking.' That is, Moses said to his servant, That which you mentioned about losing the fish in that place is what we were seeking, for the man we want is there. "So they returned, following their traces," That is, they returned on the path they came from, following their traces so that they would not lose their way. The accusative of "recordings" is as a source for a deleted verb, or as a state: that is, following or retaliating. "Recordings in the language means following the trace.
18:65: 65- "And they found one of Our servants" is Al-Khidr according to the majority of commentators, and the authentic hadiths indicate this, and those whose words are not taken into account disagreed with this, and said that he is not Al-Khidr but another scholar. It was said that he was called Al-Khidr because when he prayed, everything around him would turn green. It was said that his name was Balya bin Malkan, then God Almighty described him and said: "We gave him mercy from Us It was said that mercy is prophethood, and it was said that it was the blessing that God bestowed upon him And We taught him knowledge from Us" which is what God Almighty taught him of the knowledge of the unseen which He kept to Himself, and in His saying from Us there is an exaltation of the importance of that knowledge, and the journey in that is what indicates that no one should abandon the pursuit of knowledge even if he has reached its end, and that he should be humble before someone who is more knowledgeable than him.
18:66: Then God the Almighty narrated to us what happened between Moses and Al-Khidr after their meeting, saying: 66- Moses said to him, 'Shall I follow you so that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment?' In this question there is a gentleness and exaggeration in good manners, because he asked his permission to follow him so that he would teach him from what God had taught him of knowledge. And sound judgment is to stand on goodness and hit the mark, and its accusative is as a second object for you to teach me: meaning knowledge of sound judgment with which I guide, and it is read as rashdh with two fathahs, and they are two languages like bukhl and bukhl. And in the verse there is evidence that the learner is a follower of the scholar even if the ranks differ. And there is nothing in that to indicate that Al-Khidr is better than Moses, for the superior may take from the superior, and the superior may take from the inferior if one of them specializes in knowledge that the other does not know. Moses' knowledge was knowledge of the legal rulings and judging by their apparent meaning, while Al-Khidr's knowledge was knowledge of some of the unseen and knowledge of the inner meanings.
18:67: 67- He said, ‘You will never be able to have patience with me.’ That is, Al-Khidr said to Moses: You cannot be patient with what you see of my knowledge, because the phenomena that are your knowledge do not agree with that.
18:68: Then he confirmed that, pointing to the reason for the inability, and said: 68- And how can you be patient with that which you do not have knowledge of? That is, how can you be patient with knowledge that appears to be reprehensible, and you do not know, and someone like you, with your being a follower of the Shari’ah, is not permitted to remain silent about reprehensible things and acknowledge them, and report is in the accusative case of distinction: that is, your knowledge of it does not encompass it. And knowledge is knowledge of something, and the one who is knowledgeable about matters is the one who knows their secrets and what needs to be tested of them.
18:69: 69- He said, 'You will find me, if God wills, patient.' That is, Moses said to Al-Khidr: You will find me patient with you, committed to your obedience. And I will not disobey you in any matter. So the phrase and I will not disobey is conjoined with patient. Thus, the restriction by his saying, if God wills, includes patience and the negation of disobedience. It was said that the restriction by the will is specific to patience, because it is a future matter in which he does not know how his condition will be, and the negation of disobedience is determined at the present time. The answer to this is that patience and the negation of disobedience agree in that each one of them is determined at the present time. The answer to this is that patience and the negation of disobedience agree in that each one of them is determined at the present time, and in that each one of them does not know how his condition will be in the future.
18:70: He said: 70- If you follow me, do not ask me about anything of what you see of my actions that contradict what is required by the apparent meaning of the law with which God sent you until I mention it to you meaning until I am the one who initiates it for you, and explains its meaning and what it leads to. These sentences titled He said and He said are new, because they are answers to implied questions, each one of which the question arises from what preceded it. Ad-Daraqutni narrated in Al-Ifrad and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Muqatil bin Sulayman on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Al-Khidr is the son of Adam, and his life span will be extended until he denies the Dajjal. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: He was called Al-Khidr because he sat on a white fur, and behold, it began to shake green behind him. Ibn Asakir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he was called Al-Khidr because when he prayed, everything around him would turn green. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: I will not leave until I reach the junction of the two seas, he said: Until I finish. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: The junction of the two seas, he said: The Persian and Roman seas, which are towards the east and west. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab who said: The meeting place of the two seas is Africa. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab who said: Tangier. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Or shall I pass on for ages? He said: Seventy autumns. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: An age. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr regarding his statement: They forgot their fish. He said: It was salted and its belly was split. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: So it took its way in the sea, a path. He said: Its traces were dry in the sea as if it were on a rock. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: So they returned upon their traces, receding. He said: He returned them to their beginning. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: We gave him mercy from Us. He said: We gave him guidance and prophethood. Know that many hadiths have been narrated about the story of Al-Khidr with Moses mentioned in the Noble Book, and the most complete and perfect of them is what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, but they differed in some of the wording, and all of them were narrated by the path of Saeed bin Jubair from him, and some of them are in the two Sahihs and others, and some of them are in one of them, and some are outside of them. It was narrated by the path of Al-Awfi from him as narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim, and by the path of Harun bin Antara from his father from him according to Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Khatib and Ibn Asakir, so let us limit ourselves to the narration that is the most complete of the established narrations in the two Sahihs, for in it is what suffices without others, and it is: Saeed bin Jubair said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf Al-Bakali claims that Moses, the companion of Al-Khidr, is not Moses, the companion of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of God has lied. Abi bin Kaab narrated that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Moses stood up to give a sermon to the Children of Israel and was asked, ‘Who is the most knowledgeable of people? ’ He said, ‘I am. ’ So God rebuked him because he did not refer the knowledge to Him. Then God revealed to him, ‘I have a servant at the confluence of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. ’ Moses said, ‘O Lord, how can I deal with him? ’ He said, ‘Take a fish with you and put it in a basket. Wherever you lose the fish, it will be there. ’ So he took a fish and put it in a basket. Then he set out, and with him went his servant Joshua bin Nun until they reached the rock, where they put their heads down and slept. The fish stirred in the basket and came out of it and fell into the sea, making its way through the sea like a tunnel. God held back the flow of water from the fish, so it became like a vault over it. When he awoke, his companion forgot to tell him about the fish, so they set out for the rest of their day and night, until the next day Moses said to his servant, ‘Bring us our lunch. We have certainly encountered fatigue in this journey of ours. ’” Moses did not find the fatigue until he passed the place that God had commanded him to go, so he said, He said to his young man: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan, and it took its way into the sea, a wonder. He said: So the fish had a school, and Moses and his young man had a wonder. Moses said: That is what we were seeking. So they returned, following their footsteps. Sufyan said: Some people claim that there is a spring of life near that rock, and its water does not touch a dead person without it living. He said: The fish had eaten from it, and when the water dripped on it, it lived. He said: “So they returned, following their footsteps until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment. Moses greeted him, and Al-Khidr said: How can I bring peace to your land? He said: I am Moses. Moses said: The Children of Israel? He said, Yes. He said, I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said, "Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me. O Moses, I have knowledge from God which He has taught me and you do not know, and you have knowledge from God which God has taught you and I do not know." Moses said, If God wills, you will find me patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. Al-Khidr said to him, If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you. So they set off walking along the seashore, and a ship passed by them, so they spoke to them to carry them, and they recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried him without a plank. When they got on the ship, they were surprised to find Al-Khidr had torn off one of the ship's planks with an axe. Moses said to him, "People who carried us without a plank, and you deliberately attacked their ship and made a hole in it in order to drown its people. You have indeed done a terrible thing?" He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said, Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my affair with difficulty. He said, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The first was forgetfulness on the part of Moses. He said: A bird came and landed on the edge of the ship and made a peck in the sea. Al-Khidr said to him: My knowledge and your knowledge have not diminished from the knowledge of God except as much as this bird that landed on the edge of the ship has diminished from this sea. Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking on the shore, Al-Khidr saw a boy playing with the boys, so Al-Khidr took his head in his hand and tore it off with his hand and killed him. Moses said, Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done a horrible thing. He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said, And this is worse than the first. He said, "If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received an excuse from me." So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. They found therein a wall about to collapse, so he set it straight. "Ma'il said, 'So Al-Khidr said with his hand like this,' so he set it straight. Moses said, "A people we came to, but they did not feed us or offer us hospitality." If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it. He said, "This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, "We wish that Moses had been patient so that God could tell us of their story." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas used to recite and Before them was a king who seized every ship by force, and he was reciting: “As for the boy, he was a disbeliever, and his parents were believers.” The rest of the narrations of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b are in agreement with this narration in meaning, even if the wording differs in some of them, so there is no benefit in mentioning them at length. The same is true of narrations other than Saeed’s on his authority.
18:71: His saying: 71- So they set out meaning Moses and Al-Khidr on the seashore looking for the ship. A ship passed by them, so they spoke to them to carry them, so they carried them. Until when they boarded the ship, he tore it open. It was said that he tore off one of its planks, and it was said that it was two planks that were close to the water, and it was said that he tore open the ship’s wall to damage it and prevent its people from drowning quickly. He said Moses: “You tore it open to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing.” That is, you have done a great thing. It is said that the matter is great, and the noun is a matter. Abu Ubaidah said: The matter is the great disaster, and he recited: My peers have suffered a terrible and terrible punishment from me. Al-Qatibi said: The matter is strange. Al-Akhfash said: A matter is something he commands if it is intense, and the noun is the matter. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read to drown its people with a fatha on the lower ya’, and raised its people as the subject. The rest read it with a damma on the upper ya’, and lowered its people as the object.
18:72: 72- He said, meaning Al-Khidr, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? I remind him of what he had previously said to him, You would never be able to have patience with me.
18:73: F 73- Moses said to him, Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot. It is possible that ma is a source, meaning do not hold me accountable for my forgetting, or a relative pronoun, meaning do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, which is what Al-Khidr said, So do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you. Forgetting is either in its true sense, assuming that Moses forgot that, or in the sense of abandonment, assuming that he did not forget what he said to him, but he abandoned acting on it. And do not burden me with difficulty in my affair. Abu Zaid said: I burdened him with difficulty if I forced him to do that: and the meaning is treat me with ease, not with difficulty. It was read asran with two dammahs.
18:74: 74- So they set out until they met a boy, and he killed him meaning Al-Khidr. The word boy includes a young adult as well as a child. It was said that the boy was playing with the boys and Al-Khidr tore off his head. Moses said, Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Abu Ja'far and Uways read it with an alif after the zay and a light ya', active participle. The rest read it with a shaddah on the ya' without an alif. Az-Zakiya: is the one who is free from sins. Abu Amr said: Az-Zakiya is the one who did not sin, and Az-Zakiya is the one who sinned and then repented. Al-Kisa'i said: Az-Zakiya and Az-Zakiya are two dialects. Al-Farra' said: Az-Zakiya and Az-Zakiya are like Qasiya and Qasiya. The meaning of without a soul is without killing a forbidden soul so that killing this one would be retaliation. Indeed, you have done something monstrous meaning something terrible and reprehensible that is not known in the Sharia. It was said that its meaning is more denial than the first command because killing cannot be remedied, unlike removing the tablet from the ship, which can be remedied by returning it. It was also said that denial is less than the command, because killing one person is easier than drowning the people of the ship. It was said that Moses ruled out killing a person without a person, and he did not interpret to Al-Khidr that killing is permissible for other reasons.
18:75: 75- He said Al-Khidr Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? Here the word for you was added because the reason for the rebuke is greater and its justification is stronger. It was said that the word for you was added for the purpose of emphasis, as you say to someone you are rebuking: I say to you and I mean you.
18:76: 76- He said Moses If I ask you about anything after that meaning after this time, or after this murdered soul then do not keep me company meaning do not make me your companion, he forbade him from keeping company with him despite his eagerness to learn because his excuse was clear, and so he said: You have received an excuse from me meaning that you have been excused since I disobeyed you three times, and this is the speech of someone who is very remorseful, and the situation forced him to confess and take the path of justice. Al-A'raj read tasahabni with the opening of the ta' and the ba' and the shaddah of the nun. The majority read tasahabni and Ya'qub read tasahabni with the damma of the ta' and the kasrah of the ha' and Sahl narrated it from Abu Amr. Al-Kisa'i said: Its meaning is do not let me keep you company. The majority read la-dini with the damma of the dal except that Nafi' and Asim lightened the nun, and the rest stressed it. Abu Bakr read from Asim la-dini with the damma of the lam and the sukoon of the dal. Ibn Mujahid said: It is a mistake. Abu Ali said: This emphasis is perhaps due to the narration, but according to the standard Arabic, it is correct. The majority read adhran with a sukoon on the dhal. Isa bin Omar read it with a dammah on the dhal. Ad-Dani narrated that Abi narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a kasrah on the ra’ and a ya’ after it, adding the excuse to himself.
18:77: 77- So they set out until they came to the people of a village It was said that it was Ayla, and it was said that it was Antioch, and it was said that it was Barqa, and it was said that it was a village from the villages of Azerbaijan, and it was said that it was a village from the villages of the Romans and they asked for food from its people This sentence is in the accusative case as an attribute of the village, and the apparent was placed in place of the implicit for more emphasis, or because of the dislike of the two pronouns coming together in this word because of the difficulty involved, or to increase the ugliness of the people of the village by showing them but they refused to host them meaning they refused to give them what is rightfully their duty of hospitality, so whoever uses this verse as evidence for the permissibility of asking and the permissibility of begging has made a clear mistake, and from that is the saying of some of the writers who ask people: If I respond, then there is no shortcoming in responding to me. Moses and Al-Khidr responded before. It has been proven in the Sunnah that asking for something that cannot be refuted is forbidden, from many authentic hadiths: And they found therein meaning in the village a wall that was about to collapse. Attributing the will to the wall is metaphorical. Al-Zajjaj said: The wall does not have a real will, but the appearance of falling appeared in it, as the actions of those who desire and intend appear, so it was described as having a will. From this is the saying of Al-Ra’i: On a mission, he split their heads like axes when they want to cut them. The meaning of swooping is to fall quickly. It is said that a wall swooped down if it fell, and a bird swooped down if it descended from its flight and fell on something. The meaning of fa-qa-mahu is fa-s-taq-hu he straightened it because he found it leaning so he put it back as it was. It is also said that he demolished it and built it, and it is also said that he erected it with a column. It was mentioned in the authentic hadith that he wiped it with his hand. He said Moses If you wished, you could have taken a reward for it meaning for erecting it and fixing it, urging Moses to Al-Khidr to take a reward. Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is if you wished, you could not have straightened it until they had settled us, so it is the reward. Abu Amr, Ya’qub, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Al-Yazidi and Al-Hasan read latakhadht i.e., someone took it and straightened it like ikhtada. The rest read latakhadht i.e., someone took it and straightened it.
18:78: 78- He said Al-Khidr This is a parting between me and you adding parting to the circumstance for the sake of expansion: meaning this speech and your denial of abandoning the reward is the parting between us. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is this is a parting between us: meaning this is a parting of our connection, and he repeated between for emphasis, and when Al-Khidr said this to Moses, he began to explain the reason for which he did those actions that Moses denied, so he said: I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not have patience for and the interpretation is the return of something to its destination.
18:79: Then he began to explain to him, saying: 79- As for the ship, meaning the one he had breached, it belonged to poor people, weak people who were unable to repel those who wanted to oppress them, working at sea, and they had no money other than that ship, which they would rent out to those who sailed the sea and take wages. Al-Shafi’i used this verse as evidence that the poor are in a worse state than the needy. So I wanted to make it defective, meaning to make it defective by removing what I had removed from it. And behind them was a king, the commentators said: meaning in front of them, and behind can mean in front of them. We have already discussed this in His statement: Behind him is a severe punishment, and it was said that he meant behind them, and it was their way of returning to him, and they did not have any report that He seizes every ship by force, meaning every ship that was sound and not defective. It was read with the addition of sound, and this was narrated from Abi and Ibn Abbas. A group of people read it with emphasis on the seen from masakeen, and there was a difference of opinion regarding its meaning. It was said that they are the sailors of the ship, because masakeen is the one who holds the ship, and the most apparent reading is the majority’s reading with emphasis.
18:80: 80- And as for the boy meaning the one he killed, his parents were believers meaning he was not. So we feared that he would overwhelm them meaning that the boy would overwhelm his parents. It is said that he overwhelms him, and overwhelms him means he overwhelms him. The commentators said: Its meaning is we feared that his love would lead them to follow him in his religion, which is disbelief, and transgression is the object of overwhelms them and disbelief is conjoined with it. It was said that the meaning is: So we feared that he would overwhelm the parents by transgressing against them and being ungrateful for their blessings by his disobedience. It was said that it is possible that so we feared is from the words of God, and the meaning is that we hated the hatred of one who fears the bad consequences of his matter and changes it, and this is very weak, as the words are the words of Al-Khidr. Some scholars have questioned Al-Khidr’s killing of this boy for this reason. It was said that he was an adult and deserved it because of his disbelief. It was also said that he was cutting off the road and deserved to be killed for that. The meaning of We feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief is that Al-Khidr feared that his parents would defend him and be fanatical about him, and thus fall into sin, which could lead to disbelief and apostasy. In conclusion, there is no problem with Al-Khidr killing him if he was an adult, a disbeliever or a highway robber. This is according to what is required by Islamic law, and it is possible that Al-Khidr had a law from God the Almighty that permitted him to do that. However, if the boy was a young boy who had not yet reached puberty, it was said that Al-Khidr knew, through God’s knowledge, that if he had become an adult, he would have been a disbeliever whose disbelief would have led his parents astray and made them disbelievers. This is even though the apparent meaning of Islamic law forbids it. Killing someone who has no sin and who has not been subject to the pen of accountability for fear that he might do something after reaching puberty that would make it permissible to kill him is not permissible in Muhammadan law, but it is permissible in another law, so there is no problem. The majority of scholars have said that Al-Khidr was a prophet.
18:81: 81- So We desired that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him The majority of scholars read it with a fat-ha on the unified ba' and a shaddah on the dal. Asim, Ibn Amir, Abu Ja'far, and Ya'qub read it with a sukun on the ba' and a light dal. The meaning is: We desired that God should provide them with a better son instead of this child, purity meaning religion, righteousness, and purity from sins. And nearer in kinship Ibn Abbas, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Amir read it with a damma on the ha'. The rest read it with a sukun on it. The meaning of kinship is mercy. It is said, May God have mercy on him, the mercy of my mercy. The alif is for feminization.
18:82: 82- And as for the wall, meaning the one he repaired, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, which is the village mentioned previously, and it is permissible to use the name city for the village linguistically. And there was beneath it a treasure for them, it was said that it was a large sum of money, as the name treasure indicates, since it is the collected money. Al-Zajjaj said: It is known in the language that when the word treasure is singular, it means buried money. If it is not money, it is said: a treasure of knowledge and a treasure of understanding. It is said: a tablet of gold. It is said: written scrolls. And their father was righteous. So his righteousness required him to take care of his two sons and preserve their money. It is said: he is the one who buried him. It is said: he is the seventh father from the one who buried him. It is said: the tenth. So your Lord intended meaning: your owner and the manager of your affairs. The Lord added to the pronoun of Moses to honor him. That they should reach their maturity meaning: their perfection and full growth. And extract their treasure from that place where the wall was. If it had collapsed, the treasure would have come out from under it. A mercy from your Lord for them. It is a source in the place of the state: meaning: they were shown mercy by God Almighty. And I did not do it of my own accord meaning: of my effort and opinion. It is an emphasis on what came before it. It is known by His saying: So your Lord intended that Al-Khidr did not do it of his own accord. That is the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience meaning: that which was mentioned from those. The evidence that I have shown you and clarified its aspects is the interpretation of what you were impatient about and could not remain silent about. The meaning of interpretation here is the outcome to which those matters came, which is the clarification of what was unclear to Moses and the appearance of his face. The letter ta’ was deleted from tasata’a for the sake of lightness. Abdur-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: You have certainly done a bitter thing, meaning: something strange. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Mujahid. Abdullah Ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: a bitter thing, he said: something strange. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ubayy Ibn Ka’b regarding his statement: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, he said: He did not forget, but it is an indirect expression. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah who said: Al-Khidr was a slave whom no eyes could see, except for those whom God wanted to show him to. No one from the people saw him except Moses. If the people had seen him, they would have prevented him from tearing the ship and killing the boy. I say: It should be seen where he got this from? If his only proof is his saying: And if the people saw him, etc., then that is not in accordance with what he mentioned. Firstly, it is permissible for him to do that without the people of the ship and the boy’s family seeing him, not because the eyes do not see him, but because he did that without their knowledge. Secondly, it is possible that the people of the ship and the boy’s family knew him and knew that he would not do that except by the command of God, as the prophets do, so they submitted to the command of God. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: A pure soul, he said: A Muslim. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Saeed bin Jubayr, he said: The sins did not reach the level. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar from Al-Hasan. Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: Something strange, he said: Strangeness is more strange than wonder. Ahmad narrated from Ata’ who said: Najdah Al-Haruri wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about killing children, so he wrote to him: If you are Al-Khidr, you can tell the disbeliever from the believer, then kill them. Ibn Abi Shaybah added from another chain of transmission on his authority: But you do not know, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade killing them, so he kept away from them. Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa’id Al-Musnad, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: The boy whom Al-Khidr killed was born a disbeliever on the day he was born, and if he had lived to see it, he would have exhausted his parents with his transgression and disbelief. Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Abdullah bin Ahmad, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubayy that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited from me an excuse with a heavy an. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubayy that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited that they should host them with a heavy an. Ibn Al-Anbari in Al-Masahif and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he recited and they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he demolished it, then sat down to rebuild it. I say: The narration of the two Sahihs that we presented is more appropriate that he wiped it with his hand. Al-Faryabi in his Mu'jam, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abi that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: If you had willed, you could have taken payment for it in a lightened form. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “May the mercy of God be upon us and upon Moses. If he had been patient, God would have told us of his story.” But he said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. Sa’eed bin Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite: And before them was a king who seized every good ship by force. Ibn Al-Anbari narrated on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b that he recited it in this way. Abu Ubaid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abi Al-Zahariyyah who said: Uthman wrote: And behind them was a king who seized every ship by force. Abu Ubaid, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Anbari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite: As for the boy, he was a disbeliever, and his parents were believers. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said: It is in the Mushaf of Abdullah, so your Lord feared that He would overburden them through transgression and disbelief. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Better than him in purity, he said: Religion, and nearer in kinship, he said: Love, so they replaced it with a girl who gave birth to a prophet. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And beneath it was a treasure for them, he said: The treasure was for those before us and was forbidden to us, and the spoils were forbidden to those before us and were made lawful for us. So let no man be amazed and say: What is the matter with the treasure? It was made lawful for those before us and forbidden to us? Indeed, God makes lawful whatever He wills of His command and forbids whatever He wills, and these are the Sunnahs and obligations. He makes lawful for one nation and forbids another. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, and Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And beneath it was a treasure for them, he said: Gold and silver.
