Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ regarding his statement: And beneath it was a treasure for them, he said: Treasures were made lawful for them and spoils were forbidden to them, and spoils were made lawful for us and treasures were forbidden to us. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr who traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The treasure that God mentioned in His Book is a solid gold tablet on which are written: I am amazed at the one who is certain of destiny then becomes stubborn, I am amazed at the one who remembers Hell then laughs, I am amazed at the one who remembers death then becomes heedless, There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and there are many narrations similar to this, but there is no benefit in mentioning them. Ibn Al-Mubarak, Saeed bin Mansour, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Al-Hamid in his Musnad, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And their father was righteous, he said: They were preserved through the righteousness of their father. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Verily, God, the Almighty, the Majestic, corrects, through the righteousness of the righteous man, his children, his children’s children, the people of his household, and the people of the households around him. They will continue to be under the protection of God, the Almighty, as long as he is among them.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Verily, God, the Almighty, corrects, through the righteousness of the righteous man, his children, his children’s children, and protects him in his household and the households around him. They will continue to be covered by God and in well-being. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ammarah on the authority of his father who said: It was said to Ibn Abbas: We have not heard any mention of the servant of Moses, even though he was with him? Ibn Abbas said: He said, in what is mentioned in the hadith of the young man, that he drank from the water and became immortal, so the scholar took him and loaded him into a ship and then sent him into the sea, and it will continue to surge with him until the Day of Resurrection, and that is because he was not allowed to drink from it. Ibn Kathir said: Its chain of transmission is weak, al-Hasan is rejected and his father is unknown.
18:83: When God Almighty answered two of the Jews' questions, and the speech ended where it ended, God Almighty began with the third question and the answer to it. The questioners here are meant to be the Jews. They differed greatly about Dhul-Qarnayn. It was said that he was Alexander bin Philocoelhos, the Greek who ruled the entire world and built Alexandria. Ibn Ishaq said: He was a man from Egypt, his name was Marzban bin Marzuba the Greek, from the descendants of Yunan bin Japheth bin Noah. It was said that he was a king named Hermes, and it was said that he was a king named Herodes, and it was said that he was a young man from the Romans, and it was said that he was a prophet, and it was said that he was a righteous slave, and it was said that his name was Abdullah bin Al-Dahhak, and it was said that he was Mus`ab bin Abdullah, from the descendants of Kahlan bin Saba. Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Al-Suhayli that he said: What appears from the science of history is that they were two: one of them was during the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, and the other was close to Jesus, peace be upon him. It was said that he is Abu Karb Al-Himyari, and it was said that he is an angel king, and Al-Razi preferred the first statement, he said: Because the one whose kingdom reached the extent and power that the revelation spoke of is none other than Alexander the Greek as history books testify, he said: So it is necessary to be certain that Dhul-Qarnayn is Alexander, he said: And there is a problem with this because he was a student of the wise Aristotle, and he followed his school of thought, so God’s glorification of him necessitates the ruling that Aristotle’s school of thought is true and correct, and that is something that cannot be done. Al-Naysaburi said: I said that not everything that the philosophers went to is false, so perhaps he took from them what was clear and left what was cloudy, and God knows best. Ibn Kathir preferred what Al-Suhayli mentioned that they were two as we mentioned before, and he explained that the first circumambulated the House with Abraham when he first built it and believed in him and followed him and his minister was Al-Khidr. As for the second, he is Alexander the Macedonian Greek, and his minister was the famous philosopher Aristotle, and he was about three hundred years before Christ. As for the first mentioned in the Qur’an, it was during the time of Abraham. This is the meaning of what Ibn Kathir mentioned in his interpretation, narrating it from Al-Azraqi and others. Then he said: We have mentioned a good part of his stories in the book Al-Bidaya wa Al-Nihaya, which is sufficient. Abu Al-Su’ud narrated in his interpretation from Ibn Kathir that he said: We have only explained this, meaning that they are two, because many people believe that they are one, and that the one mentioned in the great Qur’an is this later one, and thus a great error and much corruption occurs. How could it not be, when the first was a righteous, believing slave, a just king, and his minister was Al-Khidr, and it has been said that he was a prophet. As for the second, he was an unbeliever, and his minister was the philosopher Aristotle, and there was more than two thousand years between them in time, so where is this in relation to that? End quote. I said: Perhaps he mentioned this in the book he mentioned previously, and called it The Beginning and the End, but he did not find it. What is learned from the history books is that they are two, as mentioned by Al-Suhayli, Al-Azraqi, Ibn Kathir, and others, not as mentioned by Al-Razi, who claimed that he is the one who is attested to in the history books. There was a dispute as to whether he was a prophet or not. What is learned from what is required will come at the end of this research, God willing. As for the reason for which he was called Dhul-Qarnayn, Al-Zajjaj and Al-Azhari said: He was called Dhul-Qarnayn because he reached the horn of the sun from its rising, and the horn of the sun from its setting. It was said that he had two braids of hair, and braids are called horns, and from this the poet said: I kissed her mouth, taking hold of her horns, and drank the bleeding with the cold water of the trough. Al-Hashraj is one of the waters of the Arabs. It was said that at the beginning of his reign he saw as if he was holding the two horns of the sun, so he was called that. It was also said that he had two horns under his turban. It was also said that he called to God, so his people wounded him on one horn. Then he called to God, so they wounded him on his other horn. It was said that he was called that because he was noble on both sides, from a house of honor on both sides of his father and mother. It was also said that two horns of people became extinct during his time while he was alive. It was also said that when he fought, he fought with both his hands and his stirrups. It was also said that he was given knowledge of the apparent and the hidden. It was also said that he entered the light and the darkness. It was also said that he was the king of Persia and Rome. It was also said that he was the king of Rome and Turkey. It was also said that his crown had two horns. His statement: Say, ‘I will recite to you from him a report.’ That is, I will recite to you, O questioners, report from Dhul-Qarnayn, by way of the recited revelation.
18:84: Then He, glory be to Him, proceeded to explain what He had commanded His Messenger to say to them, that he would recite to them a reminder of it, so He said: 84- Indeed, We established him upon the earth meaning, We empowered him with the means We paved for him, so We gave him the ability and capacity to dispose of it, and made it easy for him to travel in its places, and made its paths easy for him so that he could be able to do it wherever he wanted and however he wanted. And among the parts of his empowerment therein is that He made night and day equal in illumination, And We gave him of every thing of what is related to his request, a cause meaning a path by which he could reach what he wanted.
18:85: 85- So he followed a way from those ways. The commentators said: The meaning is a path that leads to the setting of the sun. Al-Zajjaj said: So he followed a way from the ways that he was given, and that is because he was given a way from everything, so he followed from those ways that he was given a way in traveling to the west. And it was said that he followed from everything knowledge that leads to what he wants, and it was said a way to where he wanted, and it was said from everything that creation needs, and it was said from everything that kings seek help from to conquer cities and subjugate enemies. The origin of the reason is the rope, so he sought help for everything that leads to something. Ibn Amir, the people of Kufa, Asim, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read So he followed with the hamza cut off, and the people of Medina, the people of Mecca, and Abu Amr read it with its connection. Al-Akhfash said: I followed him and I followed him with the same meaning, like I rode behind him and I rode behind him, and from this is His statement: So a piercing meteor followed him. An-Nahhas said: Abu Ubaidah chose the reading of the people of Kufa, he said because it is from the word sir. He and Al-Asma’i narrated that it is said: I followed him and I followed him if he walked but did not catch up with him, and I followed him if he caught up with him. Abu Ubaidah said: And similar to it is So they followed them from the east. An-Nahhas said: This is one of the differences, and even though Al-Asma’i narrated it, it is not accepted except with knowledge or evidence. The statement of God the Almighty: So they followed them from the east, does not say in the hadith that they caught up with them, but rather the hadith is that when Moses and his companions came out of the sea and Pharaoh and his companions were in the sea, the sea closed over them. The truth in this is that taba’a, “taba’a,” and taba’a are languages with the same meaning, which is the meaning of walking.
18:86: 86- Until he reached the setting of the sun meaning the end of the earth towards the west, because beyond this end is the ocean, and it is not possible to continue in it He found it setting in a hot spring Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read hot: meaning hot. The rest read Ham'ah meaning with a lot of sludge, which is black clay. You say: The well became hot with sukoon if its sludge was removed, and The well became hot with sukoon means its sludge became plentiful. It is also possible that it is hot from the sludge, so the hamzah was lightened and changed to a ya'. The two readings may be combined and it may be said that it was hot and with sludge. It was said that perhaps when Dhul-Qarnayn reached the shore of the ocean, he saw it thus in his vision. It is not far-fetched to say that there is no objection to God enabling him to cross the ocean until he reaches that spring where the sun sets. What is the objection to this after God narrated about him that he reached the setting of the sun, and enabled him on the land and the sea as a whole? The mere exclusion does not necessitate interpreting the Qur’an contrary to its apparent meaning: And he found near it a people The pronoun in by it refers either to the spring or to the sun. It was said that they were people who wore the skins of wild animals, and they were disbelievers, so God gave him the choice between punishing them or leaving them alone, so He said: Either you punish, or you take a good course with them meaning either you punish them by killing them from the beginning, or you take a good course with them, or a good course, an exaggeration by making the source a description of the command, and what is meant is calling them to the truth and teaching them the laws.
18:87: 87- He said Dhul-Qarnayn, choosing the call that is the last part of the hesitation As for he who wronged himself by insisting on polytheism and did not accept my call We will punish him by killing him in this world Then he will be returned to his Lord in the Hereafter And He will punish him therein with a terrible punishment meaning a terrible and terrible punishment. Al-Zajjaj said: God gave him the choice between the two matters. Al-Nahhas said: Ali bin Sulayman rejected his statement because it is not correct that Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet to be addressed with this, so how can he say to his Lord, the Almighty, Then he will be returned to his Lord and how can he say Then We will punish him and address him with the letter nun? He said: The meaning is We said, O Muhammad, they said, O Dhul-Qarnayn. Al-Nahhas said: What he mentioned is not necessary because it is possible that God, the Almighty, addressed him through the tongue of a prophet in his time, and it is as if Dhul-Qarnayn addressed those people, so what he mentioned is not necessary. It could be that he was addressing the prophet whom God spoke to through his tongue, or he was addressing his people who brought him to that place. Tha’lab said: In his saying: Either you punish or you take is in the accusative case, and if it had been raised it would have been correct in meaning as for it is like the saying of the poet: So go, either you will fulfill a need or you will find a good and friendly place to rest.
18:88: 88- And as for he who believes in God and believes in My call and does righteous work from what faith requires, he will have the best reward. The people of Medina, Abu Amr, Asim, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Amir read he will have the best reward" in the nominative case as a subject: meaning the reward for the best trait with God, or the best deed, which is Paradise, as Al-Farraa said. Adding the reward to the best, which is Paradise, is like adding the certainty of truth and the abode of the Hereafter. It is possible that this reward is from Dhul-Qarnayn: meaning I give it to him and bestow favor upon him. The rest of the Kufians read "he will have the best reward" with the accusative case of reward and its tanween. Al-Farraa said: Its accusative case is for the purpose of distinguishing. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a source in the place of the state, meaning rewarding it with a reward. Ibn Abbas and Masruq read "he will have the accusative case" without tanween. Abu Hatim said: It is with the deletion of the tanween due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Nahhas said: This is a mistake according to others because it is not the place for deleting the tanween due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. It was read with the nominative case of jaza’a with the tanween as a subject, and al-husna is a substitute for it, and the predicate is the preposition and the noun and we will say to him of our command with ease meaning from what we command with a word that is easy and not difficult or strenuous, or the source was used for it as an exaggeration.
18:89: 89- Then he followed a path meaning a path other than the first path, which is the one he took back from the west and traveled to the east.
18:90: 90- Until, when he reached the place of sunrise meaning the place where the sun rises first on the inhabited earth, or the place of its rising because there is no legal or rational impediment to its reaching it, as we explained previously, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made any covering against it to cover them, neither houses nor clothing, rather they were barefoot and naked and did not take refuge in any building. It was said because they were in a land where it was not possible to build on it.
18:91: 91- Likewise, and We have encompassed what he has with knowledge. That is, likewise the matter of Dhul-Qarnayn followed these causes until he reached it, and We knew when We gave him power what he had of suitability for that power and independence in it. It was said that the meaning is: We did not make for them a cover like that cover that We made for you of buildings and clothing. It was said that the meaning is: Likewise, the rising of the sun reached the same as it reached its setting. It was said that the meaning is: Likewise, it rose upon a people like that tribe upon which it set, so He decreed for these as He decreed for those of the punishment of the oppressors and kindness to the believers. The interpretation of encompassing what he has in these aspects is according to what suits that, as we said in the first aspect. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: The Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “O Muhammad, you only mention Abraham, Moses, Jesus and the prophets. You have heard us mention them, so tell us about a prophet whom God did not mention in the Torah except in one place.” He said: And who is he? They said: Dhul-Qarnayn. He said: I have not heard anything about him. So they left, happy and overcome by themselves, and they did not reach the door of the House until Gabriel came down with these verses: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not know whether Tubba’ was a prophet or not? I do not know whether Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet or not? I do not know whether the prescribed punishments are expiations for their people or not. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d who said: Ali was asked about Dhul-Qarnayn, is he a prophet? He said: I heard your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: He is a servant who advises God and He advises him. Ibn Abd al-Hakam in Futuh Misr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif, Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu al-Tayfil that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali ibn Abi Talib about Dhul-Qarnayn, was he a prophet or a king? He said: He was neither a prophet nor a king. Rather, he was a righteous servant who loved God, so God loved him. He advised God, so God advised him. God sent him to his people, so they struck him on one horn and he died. Then God revived him to fight them. Then God sent him to his people, so they struck him on the other horn and he died. Then God revived him to fight them. That is why he was called Dhul-Qarnayn, and there is someone like him among you. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Amr, who said: Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Akhras ibn Hakim, on the authority of his father, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about Dhul-Qarnayn, and he said: He is a king who wiped out the earth with means. Ibn Abd al-Hakam in Futuh Misr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azmah narrated on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma'dan al-Kila'i, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to this. Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari in Kitab al-Adad, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he heard a man calling out in Mina, O Dhul-Qarnayn. Umar said, You have heard the names of the prophets, so what about the names of the angels? There is more to the topic than what we have mentioned, which is sufficient for what we have mentioned. Ibn Abd al-Hakam in Futuh Misr, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani a hadith that includes that a group of Jews asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Dhul-Qarnayn, and he informed them of what they had come for in the beginning. Among what he informed them was that he was a young man from the Romans, and that he built Alexandria, and that a king ascended with him to the heavens, and that he went with him to the dam. Its chain of transmission is weak, and its text contains something strange, and most of what it contains is that it is from the stories of the Children of Israel. Ibn Kathir mentioned the meaning of this in his interpretation and attributed it to Ibn Jarir and Al-Umawi in his Maghazi, then he said after that: It is amazing that Abu Zar’ah Al-Dari, with his great status, included it in full in his book, Evidence of Prophethood. End quote. Al-Suyuti included it in full in Al-Durr Al-Manthur, and he also included a long report on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih and attributed it to Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Shirazi in Al-Alqab, and Abu Al-Shaykh, and it contains very strange things. He also mentioned a long report on the authority of Muhammad Al-Baqir, which was included by Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh. Perhaps these reports and similar ones were transmitted from the People of the Book, and we have been commanded not to believe them or disbelieve them in what they transmit to us. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And We gave him a reason for everything, he said: Knowledge. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal that Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan said to Kaab Al-Ahbar: You say that Dhul-Qarnayn used to tie his horses to the Pleiades. Kaab said to him: If you say that, then God said: And We gave him a means for everything. Abd Al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Abi Hasir that Ibn Abbas mentioned to him that Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan recited the verse in Surat al-Kahf 18:It sets in a hot spring. Ibn Abbas said: I said to Muawiyah: We do not recite it except as a hot spring. Muawiyah asked Abd bin Amr: How do you recite it? Abdullah said: As you read it. Ibn Abbas said: I said to Muawiyah: The Qur’an was revealed in my house. So he sent for Kaab and said to him: Where do you find the sun setting in the Torah? Kaab said to him: Ask the people of Arabic, for they are more knowledgeable about it. As for me, I find in the Torah: In water and mud, and he pointed with his hand to the west. Ibn Abi Hasir said: If I were with you, I would support you with words that would increase your insight into the scorching heat. Ibn Abbas said: What is it? I said: Among what we have attributed is the statement of Tubba’ in what he mentioned of Dhul-Qarnayn regarding his preoccupation with knowledge and his following it: Dhul-Qarnayn Omar was a Muslim king who made kings submit to him and mobilize. He came to the East and the West seeking the means of kingship from a wise guide. He saw the setting of the sun at sunset in the spring of Dhi Khalab and Thaat Kharmad. Ibn Abbas said: What is Khalab? I said: Mud, in their words. He said: What is Thaat? I said: Mud. He said: What is Kharmad? I said: Black. Ibn Abbas called a boy and said: Write down what this man says. At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite in a muddy spring. At-Tabarani, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
18:92: Then the Almighty narrated the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn to another region, which is the region of the northern country, after preparing its causes, saying: 92- Then he followed a way, meaning a third path crossing between the east and the west.
18:93: 93- Until he reached between the two barriers Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hafs, Ibn Muhaisin, Yahya Al-Yazidi and Abu Zaid from Al-Mufaddal read with the fat-ha on the seen. The rest read with the damma on it. Abu Ubaidah, Ibn Al-Anbari and Abu Amr Ibn Al-Ala said: If the dam is created by God, the Most High, then it is with the damma on the seen so that it has the meaning of a passive participle: that is, it is something that God did and created. If it is the work of the servants, then it is with the fat-ha so that it is an event. Ibn Al-A'rabi said: Everything that faces you and what is behind it is a dam and a dam is like weakness and weakness, and poverty and poverty. The two dams are two mountains on the side of Armenia and Azerbaijan. The accusative case of between is that it is a direct object, just as it was raised by the agent in His statement: It has been cut off between you. It was said that the place between the two dams is the land of the Turks towards the east, not the mountains of Armenia and Azerbaijan. Ibn Jarir narrated in his history that the ruler of Azerbaijan, during its conquest, sent a man from the direction of the islands and saw it. He described it as a tall building behind a strong, impregnable trench, and he found behind them meaning behind them, metaphorically referring to them. It was said that in front of them were a people who could hardly understand a word. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read yafqhoo with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the qaf from afqa if it makes clear: meaning they do not explain speech to others. The rest read with a fatha on the ya’ and the qaf: meaning they do not understand the speech of others. Both readings are correct, and their meaning is they do not understand from others and they do not understand others, because they do not know anything other than their own language.
18:94: 94- They said meaning these people who do not understand a word, it was said that Dhul-Qarnayn's understanding of their speech was among the reasons that God gave him, and it was said that they said that to their interpreter, so he said to Dhul-Qarnayn what they said to him: O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land. Gog and Magog are two foreign names as evidenced by the prohibition of their inflection, and the majority said the same. It was said that they are derived from the word aj for the gazelle in its gait when it runs, and ta'ajjat al-nar when it is blazing, the majority read them without a hamza, and Asim read them with a hamza. Ibn al-Anbari said: The reason for their hamza, even though its origin is not known, is that the Arabs have hamzatted letters in which the origin of the hamza is not known, like their saying: ba'ath, ra'atha, and istashta'a al-rih. Abu Ali said: It is possible that they are both Arabic. Whoever adds a hamza, it is on the pattern of yaf`ul, like yarbu`. Whoever does not add a hamza, it is possible that he lightened the hamza and changed it to an alif, like ra`s. As for Majuj, it is maf`ul from aj, and the two words are derived from the same root. He said: The inflection was left in them on the assumption that they are Arabic for the feminization and definiteness, as if it were the name of a tribe. There is disagreement about their lineage. It was said that they are from the descendants of Japheth, son of Noah. It was also said that Yajuj is from the Turks and Majuj is from the Gilan and Daylam. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Adam had a wet dream and his water mixed with the soil and they were created from that water. Al-Qurtubi said: This is questionable, because prophets do not have wet dreams, but rather they are from the descendants of Japheth. This is what Muqatil and others said. There has been disagreement about their description. Some people describe them as having small bodies and short stature, while others describe them as having large bodies and tall stature. Some say that they have claws like those of wild beasts, and that there is a type among them that spreads out one of its ears and covers itself with the other. The scholars of the past and those who came after them have different accounts about their descriptions and actions. There is a difference of opinion about their corruption on earth. Some say it is eating the children of Adam, and some say it is injustice, oppression, killing, and other forms of corruption. It is also said that they would go out to the land of those people who complained to Dhul-Qarnayn during the spring, and they would not leave anything green in it without eating it. Shall we then make for you a tribute? This question is an example of good manners with Dhul-Qarnayn. It was also read as Kharaj. Al-Azhari said: Kharaj refers to the tax, the spoils of war, the poll tax, and the yield. Kharaj is also the name for what is taken out of the obligatory duties on the wealth, and Kharaj is the source. Qatrib said: Kharaj is the poll tax and Kharaj is on the land. It was also said that Kharaj is what each person takes out of his money, and Kharaj is what the ruler answers. It was also said that they have the same meaning, On the condition that you make a dam between us and them, meaning a barrier between us and them. It was also read as Sadd with the seen open. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: The dam is the noun, and the “fatha is the source. Al-Kisa’i said: “Fath and Dammah are two dialects with one meaning. We have already mentioned earlier what we narrated from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’, Abu Ubaidah and Ibn al-Anbari about the difference between them.” Ibn Abi Ishaq said: “What your eyes see is Sad with Dammah, and what you do not see is Sad with Fathah. We have already explained who reads Sadin with Fathah and Dammah.
18:95: 95- He said, 'What my Lord has given me power over' meaning Dhul-Qarnayn said to them: What God has given me of power and dominion is better than your expulsion. Then he asked them to help him and said: So help me with strength meaning with men from among you who work with their hands, or help me with construction tools, or with both. Al-Zajjaj said: With work that you will do with me. Ibn Kathir alone read what my Lord has given me power over with two nuns, and the rest read with one shall I place between you and them a barrier? This is the answer to the command, and the barrier is what is placed one part on the other until it is connected. Al-Harawi said: It is said, I filled the breach ardhamahu with a kasra a broken word radam meaning I blocked it. Radam is also a noun, which is a dam. It was said that radam is more eloquent than sadd, since sadd is everything that is blocked with. Radam is placing something on something else, such as stones, dirt, or the like, until a strong veil is formed from that. From this comes the word radam he patched his garment: if he patched it with dense patches, one on top of the other. From this comes the saying of Antarah: Did the poets leave the ruins? Any statement that is compounded on top of each other.
18:96: 96- Atooni Zabar Al-Hadid means give it to me and hand it to me. Zabar Al-Hadid is the plural of Zabra, which is a piece. Al-Khalil said: Zabra is a large piece of iron. Al-Farra' said: The meaning of Atooni Zabar Al-Hadid is bring it to me. When the ya was dropped, an alif was added. Based on this, Zabar is in the accusative case by removing the preposition until he leveled between the two sides. The two sides of the mountain are called Sadfan if they are parallel to each other, meaning they meet. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Harawi said the same. The poet said: Both shells are blown away by her brilliance, lighting up like a lamp in the dark. Every great, tall building may be called a shell. This was stated by Abu Ubaidah. Nafi’, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Hafs read as-sadafayn with a fatha on the sad and the dal. Ibn Kathir, Ibn ‘Amir, Abu ‘Amr, Ya’qub, Al-Yazidi and Ibn Muhaisin read it with a damma on the sad and the dal. Asim read it in Abu Bakr’s narration with a damma on the sad and a sukoon on the dal. Ibn Al-Majshun read it with a fatha on the sad and a damma on the dal. Abu Ubaid chose the first reading because it is the most famous of the languages. The meaning of the verse is that they gave him iron blocks, so he placed them between the two mountains until he made them level. He said, ‘Blow.’ That is, he said to the workers, “Blow on these blocks with bellows. “Until, when he made it a fire.” That is, he made that which was blown into, which was the blocks, a fire: that is, like fire in its heat. Attributing the making to Dhul-Qarnayn is a metaphor for him being the one who ordered the blowing. It was said that he would order a pan of tiles and stones to be placed, then firewood and coal would be lit on it, and bellows would be used until it became hot. When iron is lit, it becomes like fire. Then molten copper would be brought and he would pour it on that pan, which is the meaning of his statement: He said, ‘Bring me molten copper, that I may pour over it.’ The linguists said: molten copper is molten copper, and pouring is pouring, and this is what most of the commentators said. A group said: molten iron is molten molten iron. Another group, including Ibn al-Anbari, said: it is molten lead.
18:97: 97-ُما إستأواits original form isابتداءوا, but when the two similar letters, which are the ta and the ta, came together, they lightened it by deletion. Ibn al-Sikkit said: It is said maابتداءوا, ma asti'a, and ma asti'a. The majority of people read it with lightening, and Hamza alone readُما إستأواwith a shaddah on the ta as if he meantابتداءوا, so he assimilated the ta into the ta, and it is a weak reading. Abu Ali al-Farsi said: It is not permissible. Al-A'mash readُما ابتداءواaccording to the original form, and the meaning ofأن ظهوروهis to ascend it: meaning, Gog and Magog were not able to ascend that barrier due to its height and smoothness. And they were not able to tunnel for it it is said naqabat al-ha'it: if you make a hole in it and reach what is behind it. Al-Zajjaj said: They were not able to ascend it due to its height and smoothness, and they were not able to tunnel from below it due to its strength and solidity.
18:98: 98- He said, 'This is a mercy from my Lord' meaning Dhul-Qarnayn said, pointing to the dam: This dam is a mercy from my Lord: meaning a trace of His mercy for those who crossed the dam and for those who came after them, for whom it is feared that they will be disgraced if that dam had not been there. It was said that it was a reference to enabling its construction. So when the promise of my Lord comes meaning my Lord has set a deadline for them to leave it. It was said that it is a source with the meaning of the object, and it is on the Day of Resurrection. He made it level meaning level with the ground. From this is His statement: No! When the earth is leveled. Al-Tirmidhi said: meaning level. It is said that a she-camel is leveled: if its hump is gone. Al-Qatibi said: meaning He made it leveled and stuck to the ground. Al-Hulaimi said: in pieces and broken. The poet said: Is it true that a cave was destroyed and collapsed? Al-Azhari said: Dakkattuhu means I crushed it. Whoever read Dakka with a long vowel, namely Asim, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i, wanted to liken it to a she-camel that has no hump, meaning like Dakka, because the dam is masculine and cannot be described as Dakka. The rest read Dakka with a tanween as a verbal noun, and its meaning is what was mentioned above. It is also permissible for it to be a verbal noun in the sense of a state, meaning crushed. And the promise of my Lord was true, meaning His promise of reward and punishment, or the customary promise is true and fixed and does not fail. This is the last statement of Dhul-Qarnayn. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Until, when he reaches between the two barriers, he said: The two mountains are Armenia and Azerbaijan. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: They can hardly understand a word, he said: The Turks. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Gog and Magog are a span and two spans, and the tallest of them is three spans, and they are from the descendants of Adam. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “Gog and Magog are from the descendants of Adam, and if they were sent forth, they would corrupt the livelihood of the people. Not a man of them dies except that he leaves behind a thousand or more of his descendants. And behind them are three nations: Tawil, Taris, and Mansak.” An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Aws on the authority of his father, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Not a man of them dies except that he leaves behind a thousand or more of his descendants. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba’th narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) who said: “Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the land. They dig the dam every day, until when they can almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: ‘Go back, you will conquer it tomorrow.’ So they return to it more intensely than ever, until when their time has come and God wants to send them against the people, they dig, until when they can almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: ‘Go back, you will conquer it tomorrow, God willing.’ And he makes an exception, so they return to it and it is as it was when they left it. They dig it and come out to the people to draw water, and the people fortify themselves against them in their forts. They shoot their arrows into the sky and they return stained with blood. They say: ‘We have subdued those on the earth and have overcome those in the sky by force and supremacy.’ So God sends upon them a flood in their horizons and they perish.” The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: “By the One Who Muhammad’s soul is in his hand. Indeed, the beasts of the earth grow fat, become arrogant, and become grateful for their flesh.” It was proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Zaynab bint Jahsh, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke up from his sleep with a red face and said: There is no god but God. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a hole has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this, and he shaved. I said: O Messenger of God, will we perish while there are righteous people among us?” He said: Yes, if the filth increases. They narrated something similar from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then shall We make for you a reward? He said: A great reward. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: A filling, he said: It is like the tightest barrier. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: Iron sheets, he said: Pieces of iron. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: Between the two mountainsides, he said: The two mountains. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid, he said: The tops of the two mountains. These narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: A drop, Al-Nahhas said: Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, And they were not able to ascend it, he said: To climb it. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Jurayj, he said: To ascend it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah regarding his statement: He made it level, he said: I do not know whether he meant the two mountains or between them.
18:99: His saying: 99- And We will leave some of them that Day surging against others. This is from the words of God Almighty after the end of the words of Dhul-Qarnayn, and the pronoun in some of them refers to Gog and Magog: meaning We will leave some of Gog and Magog on the day the promise comes, or on the day Gog and Magog emerge surging against some of them. It is said that people surged: if some of them enter into others, confused like waves of water. The meaning is that they will be disturbed and mixed up. It was said that the pronoun in some of them refers to creation, and today is the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:that is, We made some of creation from the jinn and mankind surge into others. It was said that the meaning is: We left Gog and Magog on the day the dam was completed and its construction was perfect, some of them surge into others. It was said that the meaning is: We left Gog and Magog on the day the dam was completed and its construction was perfect, some of them surge into others. The interpretation of and the trumpet is blown has been presented in Al-An’am. It was said that it is the second blast, based on His statement after then we gathered them together, for the fa indicates that, and the first blast was not mentioned because the purpose here is to mention the conditions of the Resurrection. The meaning is that We gathered the creatures after their bodies had disintegrated and turned into dust, in a complete gathering, in the most perfect form, most wonderful appearance, and most amazing style.
18:100: 100- “And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, presenting it.” What is meant by presenting here is showing it: that is, We will show them Hell so that they will see it on the day We gather them together. In that is a great threat to the disbelievers because of the terror and horror that will befall them when they see it.
18:101: Then He described the aforementioned disbelievers by saying: 101- "Those whose eyes were covered from My remembrance" meaning their eyes in this world were covered, which is what covers something and conceals it from all sides from My remembrance, from the reason for My remembrance, which is the verses that are seen by those who think and consider, so they remember God with monotheism and glorification. So He applied the cause to the cause, or to the Great Qur'an, and pondered its meanings and contemplated its benefits. Then when He, the Most High, described them as blind to the evidence of creation or revelation, or both of them, He wanted to describe them as deaf to hearing the truth, so He said: "And they were unable to hear" meaning they were unable to listen to what is true in the words of God and the words of His Messenger. This is more eloquent than if He had said and they were deaf, because the deaf person may be able to hear if he is called upon, but these people are completely unable to do so. In mentioning the covering of the eyes and the inability to hear, there is a representation of their blindness to seeing with their eyes and their turning away from the evidence of hearing.
18:102: 102- Do those who disbelieve think? Here, al-hisbān means assumption, and the question is for rebuke and rebuke, and the fa is for connecting to an implied meaning like its counterparts. The meaning is: Do they think that they will benefit from what they worship, despite their turning away from contemplating the signs of God and their rebellion against accepting the truth? The meaning of that they will take My servants besides Me is that they will take them besides God, and they are the angels, the Messiah, and the devils. As allies means worshipped. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: Do they think that this will benefit them? It was read af-hasab with a silent seen, and its meaning is that I will suffice them, and it is their thought that they will take them as allies, as it is a subject and predicate, meaning that this is not enough for them and will not benefit them with God, as they thought. Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a lodging meaning We have prepared it for them as a lodging that they will enjoy when they enter. Al-Zajjaj said: The inn is the shelter and the home. It was said that it is what is prepared for the guest, so it is a mockery of them, like his saying: “Then give them tidings of a painful punishment.” The meaning is: Hell is prepared for them with us, just as the inn is prepared for the guest.
18:103: 103- “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in respect of their deeds?” The word deeds is in the accusative case as a specification, and the plural is to indicate the intended types of them.
18:104: And the position of the relative pronoun, which is 104- Those whose effort is lost in worldly life is the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, as if it was said who are they? So it was said they are those whose effort is lost, and what is meant by the loss of effort is its invalidity and waste, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a blame. And the answer would be Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and it is permissible for it to be in the genitive case as an adjective for the losers or a substitute for it, and the answer would also be those and what comes after it, and the first of these aspects is the first, and the phrase and they think that they are doing well is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of went astray: meaning and the situation is that they think that they are doing well in that and benefiting from its effects.
18:105: And the sentence 105 - Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord is a new sentence introduced to complete the loss and explain its cause. This is according to the first and most likely view, not according to the other views, for they are the answer as we have presented, and the meaning of their disbelief in the signs of their Lord is their disbelief in the evidence of His Oneness from the verses of creation and revelation, and the meaning of their disbelief in meeting Him is their disbelief in the resurrection and what comes after it from the matters of the Hereafter, then He arranged on that like His saying: So their deeds have become worthless meaning what they did of what they thought was good, and it is loss and misguidance, then He ruled on them by His saying: So We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight meaning they will have no value with Us and we will not care about them, and it was said that no scale will be established for them to weigh their deeds, because that is only for the people of good and bad deeds from among the monotheists, and these have no good deeds. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The Arabs say, He has no weight with us, meaning he has no value due to his insignificance. A man is described as having no weight due to his lightness, quick recklessness, and lack of steadfastness. The meaning of this is that they are not taken into account and have no value or status with God. Mujahid read it with a yaa' below it, meaning God does not establish it. The rest read it with a noon.
18:106: Then the Almighty explained the consequence of these people and what their affair will lead to, saying: 106- That meaning what we mentioned of the types of threat is their recompense, and His saying: Hell is an apposition to the recompense, or the sentence Their recompense is Hell is a subject and predicate and the sentence is the predicate of that, and the reason for that is that they added to disbelief taking the signs of God and His messengers in mockery, so the ba in because of their disbelief is for causality, and the meaning of their being in mockery is that they are being mocked. The predecessors differed in identifying these greatest losers in their deeds, so it was said the Jews and Christians, and it was said the disbelievers of Mecca, and it was said the Khawarij, and it was said the monks who live in monasteries, and it is better to carry the verse in general for everyone who has the aforementioned characteristics.
18:107: Then, after this threat to these infidels, the Almighty mentioned the promise to the believers, saying: 107- Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds meaning, they combined them until they were in the opposite condition of those before them, for them will be Ibn al-Anbari said: It was in what was previously known by God, it was for the people of His obedience the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging. Al-Mubarrad said: Paradise, in what I heard from the speech of the Arabs, is a tangled tree, most commonly grapes. Al-Zajjaj chose what Mujahid said: Paradise is an orchard in the Roman language, and the explanation of the noun nuzul and its accusative as the predicate of kan has been presented. The meaning: The fruits of the Garden of Paradise will be for them as a lodging prepared for them, as an exaggeration of their honor.
18:108: And the accusative of 108- "They will abide therein is in the state, and likewise the sentence They do not seek to move away from it is in the accusative case in the state, and al-hawl" is a verbal noun: meaning they do not seek to move away from it because it is more precious than for them to seek anything else, or for their souls to yearn for anything else. Ibn al-A'rabi, Ibn Qutaybah, and al-Azhari said: "al-hawl is a noun meaning to move" that takes the place of the verbal noun. Abu Ubaidah and al-Farra' said: "al-hawl" is the transfer. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Harun bin Antara on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We left some of them the verse, he said: the jinn and mankind wavering some into one another. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: They are not able to hear he said: they do not understand hearing. Abu Ubaid, Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali that he read Do those who disbelieve think Abu Ubaidah said with the jazm of the seen and the damma of the ba. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he read it likewise. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d who said: I asked my father “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds” are they the Kharijites? He said: No, they are the Jews and Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and as for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise and said: There is no food or drink in it. The Kharijites are those who break the covenant of God after ratifying it. Sa`d used to call them the wicked. `Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Mus`ab that he said: I said to my father, “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?” Are they the Kharijites? He said: No, but they are the people of the monasteries. The Kharijites are a people who deviated, so God made their hearts deviate. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Humaysah `Abdullah ibn Qays that he heard `Ali ibn Abi Talib say: In this verse, “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?” They are the monks who confined themselves to the pillars. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl who said: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn al-Kawa asked him, saying: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in their deeds? He said: The wicked of Quraysh. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through two chains of narration on the authority of Ali that he was asked about this verse: “Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in their deeds?” He said: I do not think except that the Khawarij are among them. In the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A great, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection and he will not weigh as much as a mosquito’s wing in the sight of God. He said: Read if you wish: And We will not assign to them any weight on the Day of Resurrection. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Ask God about al-Firdaws, for it is the navel of Paradise, and the people of al-Firdaws will hear the creaking of the Throne. In the two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you ask God, ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it flow the rivers of Paradise. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim, Al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn As-Samit that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In Paradise there are one hundred levels, each level is as far as the distance between the heaven and the earth, and Al-Firdaws is the highest level, and above it is the Throne, and from it flow the four rivers of Paradise. So if you ask God, ask Him for Al-Firdaws.” There are many hadiths with this meaning. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Al-Firdaws is a garden in Roman. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of As-Suddi, who said: It is a vineyard in Nabataean. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Al-Harith that Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b about Al-Firdaws, and he said: It is the gardens of grapes in Syriac. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: They do not desire to change from it, he said: A change.
18:109: When the Almighty mentioned the types of evidence, He pointed out the perfection of the Qur’an, saying: 109- “Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord.” Ibn al-Anbari said: The ink was called ink because it supplies the writer, and its origin is from the increase and the coming of one thing after another, and the oil with which the lamp is lit is called ink, and what is meant by the sea here is the species. Meaning: If the words of God’s knowledge and wisdom were written, and it was assumed that the sea was the ink for them, the sea would be exhausted before the words were exhausted, and if we were to bring something like the sea as ink, it would also be exhausted. It was said in explaining the meaning that if the sea were the ink for the pen and the pen writes, The sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted. His saying, And if We were to bring the like of it as a supplement, is a statement from Him, glory be to Him, that is not included in His saying, Say, ‘If only’ and in it is an increase in exaggeration and emphasis. The waw is to connect what comes after it to an implied sentence indicated by what comes before it: that is, the sea would be exhausted before His words were exhausted if He did not bring the like of it as a supplement, and the supplement is the increase. It was said that He, glory be to Him, used the words to mean the ancient speech that has no end or limit, and even if it is one, it is permissible to express it with the plural form because of the benefits it contains. The Arabs expressed the individual with the plural form. Al-A’sha said: A pure, clear face adorned with good makeup and wrists So he used the word labbat to mean lubba. Al-Jubba’i said: His statement, Before the words of my Lord are exhausted indicates that His words may be exhausted in general, and that which is proven not to be so cannot be presented. It was answered that what is meant are the words indicating the objects of that eternal attribute. It was said in response that the exhaustion of one thing before the exhaustion of another does not indicate the exhaustion of the other thing, nor its non-exhaustion. So the only benefit from the verse is the abundance of the words of God such that human minds cannot comprehend them. As for their being finite or infinite, there is no evidence for that in the verse. The truth is that the words of God are subject to His knowledge, and they are infinite, so the words are infinite. Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin, and Hamid read even if we brought the like of it as ink and it is like that in the Mushaf of Ubayy. The rest read mudadan and Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read before it is exhausted with the ta’, and the rest read it with the fawq.
18:110: Then the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to follow the path of humility, saying: 110- Say, 'I am only a human being like you' meaning that my state is limited to humanity and does not go beyond it to kingship, and whoever is like this does not claim to have knowledge of the words of God, but he is distinguished from them by the revelation to him from God Almighty, so He said: It is revealed to me and this description is sufficient to differentiate him from all other types of humans, then He explained that what was revealed to him is His saying: Your God is only one God who has no partner in His divinity, and in this there is guidance to monotheism, then He commanded them to do good deeds and monotheism, saying: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord hope is the expectation of the arrival of good in the future, and the meaning is: whoever has this hope, which is the case of the believers, let him do righteous work which is what the Shari'ah indicates is a good deed for which the doer is rewarded and he does not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone from His creation whether he is good or bad, an animal or Inanimate, Al-Mawardi said: All the people of interpretation said in their interpretation of this verse: The meaning is that he does not show off his work to anyone. And I say: The inclusion of the obvious polytheism that the polytheists used to do under this verse is more important than the inclusion of the hidden polytheism which is showing off, and there is nothing preventing this hidden polytheism from being included under it, but what prevents it from being what is meant by this verse. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: for the words of my Lord, he said: the knowledge of my Lord. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the verse: he said: he says the water of the sea will be exhausted before the words and wisdom of God are exhausted. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, the verse: he said: it was revealed about the polytheists who worshipped a god other than God, and this is not about the believers. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: “A man said: O Prophet of God, I stand in the places of standing seeking the face of God, and I love for him to see my homeland, but no one responded to him until this verse was revealed: ‘And let him not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.’” Ibn Mandah, Abu Nu`aym in the Companions, and Ibn `Asakir narrated on the authority of al-Suddi al-Saghir on the authority of al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: When Jundub ibn Zuhair prayed, fasted, or gave charity, and he was mentioned with good, he felt relieved by it. He increased it because of the few people, but he did not intend God by it. So the verse, So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, was revealed. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: “A man said: O Messenger of God, I free slaves and I love to be seen, and I give charity and I love to be seen. So the verse, “So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord,” was revealed. It is a mursal. Hannad narrated it in al-Zuhd on his authority as well. Ibn Sa`d, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`b narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id ibn Abi Fadalah al-Ansari, who was one of the Companions, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When God gathers the first and last on a day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: Whoever has associated anyone in a deed he did for God, let him seek his reward from other than God, for God is the most independent of partners.” Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that a man said: O Messenger of God, what if a man strives in the cause of God seeking worldly gain? He said: There is no reward for him. The people were very upset about that, but the man returned and said: There is no reward for him. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in Al-Ikhlas, Ibn Jarir in his Tahdhib, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws who said: “We used to consider showing off during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be the lesser form of polytheism.” Al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi also narrated on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever prays to show off has committed polytheism, whoever fasts to show off has committed polytheism, and whoever gives charity to show off has committed polytheism.’ Then he recited: ‘So whoever hopes to meet his Lord…’” Al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym also narrated on the authority of Shaddad who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God says: ‘I am the best partner for he who associates partners with Me. And he who associates anything with Me, then his deeds, whether little or much, belong to his partner whom he associated with. I am independent of him.’” Ahmad, Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir in his Tahdhib, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you of what I fear for you more than the hidden shirk, that a man should stand up to pray in the place of another man. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: I fear for my nation polytheism and hidden desires. I said: Will your nation associate others with God after you? He said: Yes, for they do not worship the sun, the moon, a stone, or an idol, but they show off to people with their deeds. I said: O Messenger of God, what is hidden desire? He said: One of them is fasting in the morning and one of his desires is presented to him, so he abandons his fast and engages in his desire. Ahmad, Muslim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that his Lord said: I am the best of partners, so whoever does an action in which he associates someone other than Me, I am innocent of it, and it belongs to the one he associated. In another version: Whoever associates someone with Me, it is all his. In this chapter there are many hadiths warning against hypocrisy and that it is minor polytheism, and that God does not accept it. The author of Al-Durr Al-Manthur has exhaustively discussed them in this place, so let him refer to it. However, they do not indicate that this is what is meant by the verse. Rather, clear polytheism is included under it primarily. Assuming that the reason for revelation was hypocrisy, as indicated by what we have presented, then consideration is given to the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason, as is established in the science of principles. Regarding the virtues of this verse in particular, it was narrated by Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Abu Hakim who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If nothing was revealed to my nation except the end of Surat Al-Kahf, it would suffice them. Ibn Rahawayh, Al-Bazzar, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Al-Shirazi in Al-Alqab, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites at night ‘So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord’ the verse, will have a light from Aden Abin to Mecca, filled with angels. Ibn Kathir said after narrating it: Very strange. Ibn Al-Durais narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ who said: Whoever memorizes the end of Surat Al-Kahf will have a light on the Day of Resurrection from his head to his feet. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan that he recited this verse ‘So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord’ and said: It is the last verse revealed from the Qur’an. Ibn Kathir said: This is a problematic trace, because this verse is the last verse of Surat Al-Kahf, and the entirety of Surat Al-Kahf is Meccan. Perhaps Muawiyah meant that nothing was revealed after it to abrogate it or change its ruling, but rather it is confirmed and decisive, so some of the narrators were confused about that and narrated it according to the meaning as he understood it.
19:1: It is Meccan and has ninety-eight verses. An-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr that he said: Surah Maryam was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Aisha. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Ad-Dala’il on the authority of Umm Salamah that the Negus said to Ja’far ibn Abi Talib: Do you have with you anything of what he (meaning the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) brought from God? He said: Yes. So he recited to him the beginning of Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad. The Negus wept until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until their copies of the Qur’an were wet when they heard what he recited to them. Then the Negus said: This and what Moses brought came from the same lamp. Ibn Ishaq mentioned the story in full. His saying 1- Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad Abu Jaafar read these letters disconnected, and the rest connected them, and Abu Amr made the ha' inflected and the ba' opened, and Ibn Amir and Hamza were the opposite, and Al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr and Khalaf made them all inflected, and the people of Madinah read them between the two pronunciations and the rest opened them. And from Kharijah that Al-Hasan used to make the kaf inflected, and he narrated from others that he used to make the ha' inflected. Abu Hatim said: It is not permissible to make the kaf inflected, nor the ha', nor the ya'. Al-Nahhas said: The reading of the people of Madinah is among the best of this, and inflection is permissible in ha' and in ya'. A group objected to the reading of Al-Hasan. It was said in its interpretation that he only used to make the nominative case. And Nafi', Abu Jaafar, Ibn Kathir, Asim and Ya'qub made the dal clear from the spelling of the sad, and it is the choice of Abu Ubaidah, and the rest assimilated them. It has been said in explaining these readings that emphasis is the origin, and inclination is a branch of it. So whoever reads with emphasis on the ha’ and the ya’ has acted according to the origin, and whoever inclines them has acted according to the branch, and whoever inclines one of them and emphasises the other has acted according to both matters. The discussion of these letters that occur at the beginnings of the surah has been presented in full at the beginning of Surah Al-Baqarah. The place of this Fatihah, if it is made the name of the surah according to what most people do, is in the nominative case, as it is the subject and its predicate is what comes after it, as Al-Farra’ said. Al-Zajjaj objected to him and said: This is impossible because Kaha Ya Ain Sad is not what God the Almighty informed us about Zakariya, and God the Blessed and Exalted informed us about him and what he was given glad tidings of, and Kaha Ya Ain Sad is not from his story, or as it is the predicate of a deleted subject, even if it is listed in the manner of enumeration.
19:2: His saying: 2- Remember the mercy of your Lord is the predicate of an omitted subject, and if it is made listed in the manner of enumeration, then his saying: Remember the mercy of your Lord is the predicate of an omitted subject: that is, this is the remembrance of the mercy of your Lord. His servant Zachariah means his answer to him when he called upon him and asked him for a son, and the accusative of his servant is that it is a noun for mercy, as Al-Akhfash said. And it was said for the remembrance. And the meaning of the remembrance of mercy is its attainment and attainment, as it is said that someone mentioned me a favor: that is, it reached me. Yahya bin Ya'mar read remembered in the accusative, and Abu Al-Aaliyah read his servant in the nominative, so that the source is added to the object, and the subject of the remembrance is his servant, and Zachariah in both readings is an explanatory apposition for it or a substitute for it, and Al-Kalbi read remembered in the form of the past tense verb, stressed and unstressed, so that the subject is his servant, and Ibn Mu'ammar read it in the imperative, and mercy in this case is an expression of Zachariah, because every prophet is a mercy to his nation.
19:3: 3- When he called upon his Lord with a secret call. The agent in the circumstance is mercy, and it was said that it is mention, and it was said that it is a substitute for inclusion from Zachariah, and there is disagreement about the reason for his calling being secret, so it was said that it is further from hypocrisy, and it was said that he concealed it, so that he would not be blamed for seeking a child at the wrong time, and because it was from worldly matters, and it was said that he concealed it out of fear of his people, and it was said that it was from him because he had become weak and old and was not able to speak out loud.
19:4: 4- He said, 'My Lord, indeed my bones have grown feeble' This sentence explains his saying: He called upon his Lord. It is said that he became weak and feeble, and it was read with the three vowels. He meant that his bones became weak and his strength weakened. He mentioned the bone because it is the pillar of the body, and it is its foundation, and it is the origin of its construction. So if it weakens, it collapses and its strength falls. And because the strongest thing in a human being is his back, so if it weakens, what is behind it is weaker. He made the bone singular, intending the useful genus, because weakness includes every individual of the bones. And the head flared with gray hair. Abu Amr read it by assimilating the seen into the sheen, and the rest without it. Flaming originally means the spread of a ray of fire, so he likened it to the spread of the whiteness of the hair of the head in its blackness, by combining whiteness and illumination. Then he extracted it as a metaphor by means of a metonymy, by deleting the simile and the tool of comparison. This metaphor is one of the most creative and best metaphors. Al-Zajjaj said: When gray hair becomes very abundant, it is said that someone’s head is on fire. Al-Baid recited: If you see a head that has become clear, gray hair has spread over it and it has caught fire. The accusative of shiban is a specification, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. Al-Akhfash said: Its accusative is a verbal noun, because the meaning of ash-sha’ib is a young man. Al-Nahhas said: Al-Akhfash’s statement is more appropriate because it is derived from a verb, and the verbal noun is more apparent in what was like that. The original was ash-sha’ib ra’si my gray hairs were ignited, so the ignition was attributed to the head to indicate comprehensiveness. And I was never, in my supplication to You, my Lord, miserable, meaning I was never disappointed in my supplication to You at any time, but rather whenever I called upon You, You answered me. Scholars said: It is recommended that a person combine in his supplication submission with mentioning God’s blessings upon him, as Zachariah did here. In his saying: My bones have weakened and my head has turned white, there is the ultimate in submission and humility, showing weakness and inability to attain his demands and achieve his goals. In his saying: And I have never been, through my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy, there is mention of the blessings that God has accustomed him to by answering his supplications. It is said that he was unhappy with such-and-such, meaning he was tired out by it and did not achieve his goal.
19:6: 6- He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob The people of the two sanctuaries, Al-Hasan, Asim, Hamza, Ibn Muhaisin, and Yahya Ibn Al-Mubarak Al-Yazidi read both verbs in the nominative case as attributes of the guardian and not as an answer to the supplication. Yahya Ibn Ya'mar, Abu Amr, Yahya Ibn Wathab, Al-A'mash, and Al-Kisa'i read them in the accusative case as an answer to the supplication. Abu Ubaid preferred the first reading and said: It is more correct in meaning, because he asked for a guardian with this attribute and said: Grant me someone who will be my heir. Al-Nahhas preferred this and said: Because the answer to the command, according to grammarians, has the meaning of condition and reward. You say: Obey God and He will admit you to Paradise: meaning if you obey Him, He will admit you to Paradise. How can God, the Exalted, inform you of this, I mean that He will grant him a guardian who will inherit him, and He is more knowledgeable about that? And inheritance here is the inheritance of knowledge and prophethood according to what is preferable as mentioned above. Most commentators have said that the Jacob mentioned here is Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham. Some commentators have claimed that he is Jacob, son of Mathan, brother of Imran, son of Mathan. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil have said the same. The family of Jacob are his special people who are entrusted to him due to kinship, companionship, or agreement in religion. There were prophets and kings among them. It was read that he is an heir from the family of Jacob, as the subject of he is the agent...
19:7: 7- O Zachariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be Yahya. The majority of commentators said: This call is from God, the Exalted, and it was said that it is from the angels, based on His saying in Al Imran 3:Then the angels called to him, and there is an omission in the speech: meaning, He answered his prayer, so he said, O Zachariah. The reason for naming him Yahya and Zachariah has already been mentioned in Al Imran. Al-Zajjaj said: He was named Yahya because he was made alive by the knowledge and wisdom that was given to him. We have not made for him a namesake before. The majority of commentators said: Its meaning is that We have not named anyone before him Yahya. Mujahid and a group said: The meaning of We have not made for him a namesake before is that We have not made for him an example or a peer, so according to this it is taken from the name or the elevation, and this was rejected because it requires his preference over Abraham and Moses, and it was said that its meaning is: No barren woman has given birth to anyone like him, and the first is more appropriate. In His, glory be to Him, informing us that no one before Him had been given this name, there is a virtue for him in two respects: The first is that God, glory be to Him, is the One who took it upon Himself to name him with it, and did not leave it to the parents. The second respect is that naming him with a name that was not given to anyone else indicates his honor and glorification.
19:8: 8- He said, 'My Lord, how will I have a boy?' That is, how or from whom will I have a boy? The meaning of this question is not denial, but rather amazement at the power of God and the wonder of His creation, as He produces a son from a barren woman and an old man. We have already discussed something like this in Al Imran. And I have reached extreme old age. It is said that an old man has reached the end of his age and has grown old, and an old man has become dry and dehydrated. The original is 'atwān because it is from the words with a waw, so they replaced it with a ya' because it is lighter. An example of what is in the verse is the poet's saying: Only the newborn is excused, but not the one who was old in the time. Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Hafs and Al-A’mash read ‘atiya with a kasra on the ‘ayn, while the rest read it with a damma on the ‘ayn. These are two dialects. The position of the sentence and my wife was barren is in the accusative case as a state of the speaker’s pronoun, and the position of the sentence and she has reached old age is also in the accusative case as a state. Both sentences are to emphasize the exclusion and astonishment derived from his saying: How can I have a boy? That is, how can a child come between us now, when my wife was barren and did not give birth in her youth and my youth, and now she is an old woman, and I am a decrepit old man?
19:9: Then God the Almighty answered this question that expressed astonishment and exclusion by saying: 9- He said, thus said your Lord The Kaf is in the nominative case: meaning the matter is thus, and the reference is to what came before from the saying of Zachariah, then He began by saying: Your Lord said and it is possible that its place is in the accusative case as a source: meaning he said a statement like that, and the reference with that is to an ambiguous thing that is explained by his saying: It is easy for Me As for the first possibility, the sentence It is easy for Me is a new sentence introduced to remove the exclusion of Zachariah after his confirmation: meaning he said it is easy for Me despite its distance, and it is a verb from the verb hana yahun if it is not difficult and does not prevent the intended meaning. Al-Farraa said: meaning he created it easy for Me And I created you before, and you were nothing This sentence confirms what came before it. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, the creation of the child for you is like your creation. The meaning is that God, the Exalted, created him from the beginning and brought him into existence from pure nothingness. So bringing a child into existence for him through the usual way of procreation is easier and simpler than that. Rather, that was not attributed to Adam, peace be upon him, because he was truly created from nothingness, by saying: And I created your father Adam before, and he was nothing, to indicate that every individual among the human beings has a share in the creation of Adam from nothingness.
