The people of Medina, Mecca, Basra, Asim, and Ibn Amir read: And I have created you before, and the rest of the Kufians read: And I have created you before.
19:10: 10- He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign' meaning a sign that will show me that the question has occurred and been fulfilled and that pregnancy has occurred. The purpose of this question is to define it at the time of conception, as the good report was absolute regarding its specification. Ibn al-Anbari said: The reason for that is that his soul longed for the matter to be quick. So he asked God for a sign to prove the nearness of what He had bestowed upon him. It was said that he asked for a sign that would indicate that the good report was from God, the Exalted, not from Satan, because Satan made him think that. This is what al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said, and it is very far-fetched. He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, soundly.' The explanation of this has already been fully explained in Al-Imran, and soundly is in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is: Your sign is that you will not be able to speak, while you are sound in creation, with no defect that might prevent you from doing so. The mention of the nights here and the days in Al-Imran indicates that what is meant is three days and their nights.
19:11: 11- So he came out to his people from the sanctuary which is his place of prayer, and he recovered from the war, as if his companion was fighting the devil, and it was said from the war with a vowel, as if his companion was encountering war, fatigue and exhaustion. So he inspired them to glorify God morning and evening It was said that the meaning of inspired is: he hinted, as evidenced by his statement in Al Imran except by a sign It was said that he wrote for them on the earth and with the first said Al Kalbi, Al Qurzi, Qatadah and Ibn Munabbih, and with the second said Mujahid, and revelation may be applied to writing and from it the statement of Dhu Al Rummah: Except for the four dark ones, which are as if they were the remnants of revelation in the pages of the scrolls. Antara said: He revealed pages from the era of Khosrau and presented them to Ajam Tamtami. And in His saying: that they glorify is a source or an explanation, and the meaning is: So He inspired them to pray: or any pray, and the accusative of morning and evening is for the circumstance. Al-Farra’ said: Evening is feminine, and it is permissible to make it masculine if it is ambiguous. He said: Evening can also be said to be the plural of evening, and it was said that what is meant is the dawn and afternoon prayers, and it was said that what is meant by glorification is their saying Glory be to God at the two times: meaning glorify your Lord at the ends of the day. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat, and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Kaaf Ha Ya Ain Sad: Great, Guide, Trustworthy, Mighty, Truthful. In another version, Kaaf is used instead of Great. Abdul Razzaq, Adam bin Abi Iyas, Uthman bin Saeed Al-Darimi in Al-Tawhid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Kaaf in Karim, Ha in Guide, Ya in Wise, Ain in All-Knowing, and Sad in Truthful. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud and some of the Companions: Kaaf in Al-Mulk is the interrupted spelling, Kaf in Al-Mulk, Ha in God, Ya and Ain in Al-Azeez, and Sad in Al-Musawwar. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi that he was asked about Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad and he narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Umm Hani’ on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Ka Ha Hadi, Alam, and Sadiq. Uthman bin Saeed Al-Darimi, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Fatimah, the daughter of Ali, who said: “Ali used to say: ‘O Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad, forgive me.’” Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad, who said: The Kaf is sufficient, the Ha is the guide, the Ain is the knower, and the Sad is the truthful. Abu Ubaid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: Ibn Abbas used to say regarding Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad, Ha Mim, and Ya Sin and the like: It is the greatest name of God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It is an oath by which God swore, and it is one of the names of God. Just as there was disagreement about this and similar matters among the Companions, it also occurred among those who came after them, and nothing has been authenticated in this regard. If something has been narrated from the Companions about this, then something has been narrated from others that contradicts it. Different and contradictory interpretations of these opening chapters may be narrated from the same Companion, so none of that can be considered proof. Rather, the truth is to stop and refer knowledge of such matters to God, the Exalted. We have already presented an investigation of this in the opening chapter of Surat Al-Baqarah. Ahmad, Abu Ya`la, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) who said: Zachariah was a carpenter. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: The last of the prophets of the Children of Israel was Zachariah bin Azar bin Muslim from the descendants of Jacob. He called upon his Lord secretly, “He said: My Lord, indeed my bones have grown feeble” until His saying: I fear my relatives. He said: They are the clan. He will inherit me. He will inherit my prophethood and the prophethood of the family of Jacob. Then the angels, who was Gabriel, called out to him: God gives you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. When he heard the call, Satan came to him and said: O Zachariah, the voice that you heard is not from God, but from Satan, mocking you. So he doubted and said: How can I have a boy? He said: Where can he be when I have reached old age and my wife is barren? God said: And I created you before, while you were nothing. Al-Firyabi narrated on his authority that he said: Zachariah had no children, so he asked his Lord, and He said: Then grant me from Yourself an heir * Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. He said: He will inherit my wealth and inherit from the family of Jacob the prophethood. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: We have not made for him a namesake before, said: For example. Saeed ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim, who narrated with a chain of transmission that is authentic, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a chain of transmission that he said: “I do not know how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite this letter ‘Atiya or ‘Usayy.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with a chain of transmission that Ata’, regarding his statement: Atiya, said: He lived for a period of time in old age. He also narrated with a chain of transmission that is authentic: Decrepit. Ibn Jarir narrated with a chain of transmission that Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: That you shall not speak to the people for three nights without sound, said: His tongue was tied up without illness, and in another version, without being mute. Narrated by Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated with a chain of transmission that he said: Then He revealed to them, meaning: He wrote a book for them. Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission that is authentic, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: That they glorify God, said: He commanded them to pray in the morning and the evening.
19:12: His saying: 12- O Yahya here is an omission, and its meaning is: And God said to the newborn, O Yahya, or a child was born to him and he reached the age at which he can be addressed, so We said to him, O Yahya. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, We gave him and said to him, O Yahya. What is meant by the book is the Torah because it was known at that time, and it is possible that it was a book specific to him even if we do not know it now, and what is meant by taking is either the sensory taking or taking from the meaning, which is doing what is in it as it should be, and that is by acquiring a faculty that requires ease in proceeding with what is commanded, and refraining from what is forbidden, then he confirmed it by saying: With strength meaning with diligence, determination and effort And We gave him judgment while he was a boy what is meant by judgment is wisdom, which is understanding the book that he was commanded to take and understanding the religious rulings, and it was said that it is knowledge and memorizing it and acting upon it, and it was said that it is prophecy, and it was said that it is reason, and there is no objection to the judgment being suitable to be applied to all of what was mentioned. It was said that Yahya was two years old at the time of this speech, and it was said that he was three years old.
19:13: 13- "And compassion from Us" is connected to the ruling. The majority of commentators said: compassion is mercy, compassion, tenderness and love, and its origin is the longing of the soul, taken from the longing of a camel for her young. Abu Ubaidah said: You say "Your compassion, O Lord and Your compassion, O Lord" with the same meaning, meaning Your mercy. Tarafa said: Abu Munther, you have perished, so let some of us outlast your kindness. Some evil is less serious than others. Imru Al-Qais said: And the Banu Salkh bin Bakr give it to them, their tenderness, your tenderness Ibn al-A'rabi said: Hanan, with a shaddah, is one of the attributes of God, the Almighty, and Hanan, with a sukoon, means compassion and mercy. Hanan means provision and blessing. Ibn Atiyyah said: Hanan in the speech of the Arabs also means the great things in the essence of God, and from that is the saying of Zaid bin Amr bin Nufail, By God, if you kill this slave, I will make his grave a place of Hanan, meaning Bilal, when he passed by him while he was being tortured. It was said that the one who said that was Waraqa bin Nawfal. Al-Azhari said: The meaning of that is that I will have mercy on him and be compassionate towards him because he is one of the people of Paradise. Similar to that is the saying of al-Hutay'ah: Have mercy on that king, for every situation has its own words. The meaning of from Us is from Our side. It was said that it is possible that the meaning is that We gave him mercy from Us that is in his heart, with which he shows compassion to people, including his parents and relatives, until he saves them from disbelief. And zakat is in apposition to from before him. Zakat means purification, blessing, development, and righteousness, meaning that We made him blessed for people, guiding them to goodness. It was said that We purified him with good praise of him, like the purification of witnesses. It was said that it was charity that We gave him as charity to his parents. Ibn Qutaybah said this. And he was pious, meaning he avoided the sins of God and was obedient to Him. It was narrated that he never committed a sin.
19:14: 14- And dutiful to his parents is in apposition to pious. Dutifulness here means dutiful, a verb means an agent, and the meaning is: kind to them and good to them. And he was not a disobedient tyrant meaning he was not arrogant nor disobedient to his parents or his Lord, and this is a description of him, peace be upon him, as being gentle and humble.
19:15: 15- "And peace be upon him" Ibn Jarir and others said: Its meaning is security for him from God. Ibn Atiyyah said: What is more apparent to me is that it is the customary greeting, so it is more honorable and more prominent than security, because security is obtained by denying him disobedience, which is the least degree of it, and the honor is in God greeting him, and the meaning of the day he was born is that he was safe from Satan and others on that day, or that God revived him on that day, and this is the meaning of the day he dies and this is the meaning of the day he is raised alive. It was said that a person is most terrifying in three situations: the day he was born because he left what he was in, the day he dies because he sees a people he did not know and whose rulings he had no knowledge of, and the day he is raised because he sees the terror of the Day of Resurrection. So God, the Exalted, singled out Yahya for honor and safety in the three situations. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: O Yahya, take the Book with strength, he said: With seriousness, and We gave him judgment while yet a boy, he said: Understanding. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, he said: He says, ‘Do what is in it of obligations.’ Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Malik ibn Dinar, he said: The mind. Abu Nu`aym, al-Daylami and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And We gave him judgment while yet a boy, he said: He was given understanding and worship when he was seven years old. Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id al-Zuhd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah: Badala when he was three years old. Al-Hakim narrated in his history, through Nahshal, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The boys said to Yahya ibn Zakariya: ‘Let us go play.’ Yahya said: ‘We were not created for play. Go let us pray.’ This is the statement of God, ‘And We gave him judgment while yet a boy.’” Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites the Qur’an before reaching puberty is among those who were given wisdom as a child. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission ending with him. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And compassionate, he said: I do not know what it means except that I think that He is showing mercy to His servant, and a group of the Salaf interpreted it as mercy. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And purity, he said: A blessing. And regarding his statement: And was righteous, he said: He was pure and did not commit any sin.
19:16: His saying 16- And mention in the Book Mary This is the beginning of the creation of Jesus, and what is meant by the Book is this Surah: that is, mention, O Muhammad, to the people in this Surah the story of Mary. It is possible that what is meant by the Book is the genus of the Qur'an, and this Surah is part of it. And since mentioning is not related to objects, it was necessary to estimate an adjective to which mentioning is related, which is the story of Mary, or the report of Mary. When she withdrew The agent in the circumstance is that estimated adjective, and it is possible to make it a substitute for inclusion from Mary, because times include what is in them, and what is meant by Mary is her report, and in this substitution there is an indication of the magnification of the time for her amazing story to occur in it, and throwing is casting and throwing. God Almighty said: So they threw it behind their backs The meaning is: She moved away and distanced herself. Ibn Qutaybah said: She withdrew, and it was said that she separated, and the meanings are close. They differed about the reason for her seclusion. It was said that it was so that she might worship God Almighty, and it was said that it was so that she might purify herself from her menstruation. From her people is connected to seclusion, and the accusative of an eastern place is the object of the aforementioned verb: meaning a place on the eastern side. The east, with a sukoon on the ra’, is the place where the sun rises. The place was specifically named the east because they used to venerate the direction of the east because it is the place where the lights rise. Ibn Jarir narrated its meaning. People differed about the prophethood of Mary. It was said that she was a prophet simply because of this sending to her and her speaking to the angel. It was also said that she was not a prophet, because the angel spoke to her while he was in the form of a human being. This was discussed previously in Al Imran.
19:17: 17- So she took a veil to hide her from them meaning she took a veil to hide her from her family so that they would not see her during worship, or during purification from menstruation. The veil is the covering and the barrier So We sent to her Our Spirit which is Gabriel, peace be upon him, and it was said that it was the spirit of Jesus, because God Almighty created the spirits before the bodies, and the first is more appropriate because of His saying: So he appeared to her as a well-proportioned man meaning Gabriel appeared to her as a well-proportioned man who did not lose any of the characteristics of the sons of Adam. It was said that the reason for the angel appearing to her as a human being is that she could not bear to look at the angel while he was in his form.
19:18: When she saw him in the form of a handsome, perfect man who had torn the veil over her, she thought that he wanted to harm her, so she sought refuge in God from him. 18- She said, 'Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you should be righteous' meaning one who fears God and is in awe of Him. It was said that Taqi was the name of a righteous man, so she sought refuge from him out of amazement. It was also said that it was the name of a well-known wicked man at that time, but the first is more appropriate. The answer to the condition is omitted: meaning, do not interfere with me.
19:19: 19- "He said, 'I am only a messenger from your Lord'" meaning Gabriel said to her: I am only a messenger from your Lord who seeks pleasure in me, and you are not one of those from whom you expect what crosses your mind of evil will "to give you a pure boy" He made the gift from him because he was the cause of it from the aspect of the notification of it from him, or from the aspect of the blowing being carried out by him in appearance. Abu Amr, Ya'qub, and Warsh read from Nafi' "he gives" meaning he sent me to give you, and the rest read it with a hamza. The pure is the one who is clean from sins who grows on integrity and chastity, and it was said that what is meant by the pure is the prophet.
19:20: 20- She said, 'How can I have a boy when no man has touched me?' That is, no husband or anyone else has approached me. And I am not a prostitute. A prostitute is a prostitute who seeks out men. Al-Mubarrad said: Its root is baghwi on fa'ul, the waw was changed to a ya', then assimilated into the ya', and the ghayn was broken for the sake of suitability. Ibn Jinni said: It is fa'il. The addition of mentioning that she was not a prostitute, while her saying no man has touched me includes both lawful and unlawful, is intended to emphasize, to purify her from immorality. It was said that she did not exclude anything from the power of God, but she meant how the child would be, from a husband whom she would marry in the future, or would God create him from the beginning? It was said that touching refers to lawful marriage, and based on this, there is no need to explain the reason for her saying: And I was not a prostitute. What we have mentioned about its comprehensiveness is more appropriate to the usages of the people of language, and what is found in their conversations, which would take a long time to enumerate. End quote.
19:21: 21- And We will make him a sign for the people meaning, and We will make this boy or his creation without a father a sign for the people by which they will prove the perfection of power, and it is a cause for an omitted cause, and the meaning is, We created him to make him, or it is conjoined with another implied cause related to what is indicated by His statement, the Most High: It is easy for Me. And the phrase He said, thus said your Lord, it is easy for Me is a new sentence, and the speaker is the angel, and the discussion of it is like the discussion of what came before from the statement of Zechariah. And His statement, And a mercy from Us is conjoined with a sign: meaning, and We will make him a great mercy from Us for the people because of what they will attain of guidance and abundant good, because every prophet is a mercy for his nation And it was a matter decreed meaning, and what was mentioned was a matter decreed that God, the Most High, decreed and the pen has dried on it.
19:22: 22- So she carried him here is an incomplete statement, and the meaning is: So she was reassured by his words, so he approached her and blew into the pocket of her armor, and the blowing reached her stomach, so she carried him. It was said that the blowing was in her tail, and it was said in her mouth. It was said that her delivery was connected to this pregnancy without any period of pregnancy having passed, and this is indicated by his saying: So she withdrew with him to a remote place, meaning she moved aside and secluded herself to a distant place, and distant is far. It was said that this place was behind the mountain, and it was said the furthest place in that house, and it was said the farthest valley, and it was said that she carried him for six months, and it was said eight months, and it was said seven.
19:23: 23- Then the labor pains drove her to the trunk of the palm tree, meaning they forced her and compelled her. From this is the saying of Zuhair: Fear and hope came to him Shabl read faja’aha from al-jaf’ah surprise, and this reading was narrated from Asim. Al-Hasan read it without a hamza. In the Mushaf of Abi, Fal-ma aja’aha he said in Al-Kashshaf: Fal-ma aja’aha is transferred from ja’a, except that its use was determined after the transfer to the meaning of forcing, and there is some distance in it. It appears that each of the two verbs is placed in an independent position, and al-makhādh is the source of makhaddah al-ra’ah “tamkhadh” the woman gave birth to a child if her birth was near. The majority read it with a fathah on the mīm, and Ibn Kathir read it with a kasrah. The trunk is the dry stem of the palm tree, as if she sought something to lean on and cling to, as a pregnant woman clings to something she finds with her due to the severity of labor pain. The definition is either for the genus or the covenant. She said, ‘Oh, I wish I had died before this,’ meaning before this time. She wished for death because she feared that people would think badly of her in her religion, or so that people would not fall into slander because of her. And I was forgotten. Forgetfulness in the speech of the Arabs: the insignificant thing that is likely to be forgotten and not remembered and not pained by its loss, like a peg or a rope. From this is the saying of Al-Kumait: Would you make us a loss for a hungry dog, while we are not forgotten in Ma'ad and have no income? Al-Farra’ said: “An-Nasee is what a woman throws away from her illness, so Maryam says, ‘An-Naseeyan Mansiya’ meaning a menstrual period that has been thrown away. It has been read with a fatha on the ‘nun’ and a kasra on it, and they are two dialects like al-Hajar and al-Hajar, and al-Watr and al-Watr. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi read ‘Nisa’ with a hamza and a kasra on the ‘nun’. Nawf al-Bakali read it with a hamza and a fatha on the ‘nun’. Bakr ibn Habib read ‘An-Naseeyan’ with a fatha on the ‘nun’ and a shaddah on the ‘ya’ without a hamza. Al-Mansi is the one who is abandoned and is not mentioned or crosses anyone’s mind.”
19:24: 24- And he called to her from beneath her meaning Gabriel when he heard her words, and he was below her under the hill, and it was said under the palm tree, and it was said that the caller was Jesus. It was read with the opening of the meem from min and its breaking. And his saying: Do not grieve is an explanation of the call: meaning do not grieve or the meaning is that do not grieve as it is the source Your Lord has made a stream beneath you the majority of commentators said: The stream is the small river, and the meaning is: Your Lord has made a stream beneath your feet. It was said that it was a river from which the water had been cut off, so God sent water into it for Mary, and revived with it that dry trunk that she relied on until it grew leaves and bore fruit, and it was said that what is meant by the stream here is Jesus, and the stream is the great man, and from it their saying so-and-so is a stream: meaning great, and from the people of Sarat: meaning great.
19:25: 25- "And shake the trunk of the palm tree towards you" Shaking is movement: it is said shake it and shake, and the ba in the trunk of the palm tree is added for emphasis. Al-Farraa said: The Arabs say shake it and shake it, and the trunk is the bottom of the tree. Qatrib said: Every piece of wood at the base of a tree is a trunk, and the meaning of towards you is: towards you, and the root of tasaqat is tasaqatu, so the ta was assimilated into the seen. Hamza and Al-A'mash read tasaqatu with a lightened form. Asim read in the narration of Hafs and Al-Hasan with a damma on the ta with a lightened form and a kasra on the qaf, and it was read tasaqatu with the two na's pronounced. It was read with a tahtiya with a shaddah on the seen. It was read tasaqtu and yusqutu. The rest read with the assimilation of the ta in the seen, so whoever read with a fathah made the pronoun for the palm tree, and whoever read with a tahtiya made the pronoun for the trunk, and the accusative of "rutab" in some of these readings is for differentiation, and in some others it is the object of tasaqatu. Al-Mubarrad and Al-Akhfash said: It is permissible to make the word fresh in the accusative case, meaning shake fresh dates towards you, picked by the trunk of the palm tree, meaning on its trunk. Al-Zamakhshari considered it weak. Fresh is what is taken fresh, and it was said that it is what is requested and suitable for picking, and it is fa’il in the sense of maf’ul. Al-Farra’ said: Fresh and majni are one and the same, and it was said that it is fa’il in the sense of fa’il, meaning fresh, fresh and good.
19:26: 26- Eat and drink meaning from those dates and that water, or from the dates and their juice. He mentioned eating before the dates, even though the river was mentioned before the dates, because the need of the woman in childbirth to eat dates is greater than her need to drink water. Then he said, And be glad The majority read it with the opening of the qaf. Ibn Jarir narrated that it was read with the breaking of it. He said: It is the language of Najd. The meaning is: Be at ease and reject sadness. It is taken from qar and qarrah, which are cold. The happy person is cold-hearted and calm of the limbs. It was said that the meaning is: And be glad by seeing the child who was gifted to you. Al-Shaibani said: It means sleep. Abu Amr said: May God gladden his eye: meaning may He make his eyes sleep and remove his wakefulness. If you see from mankind anyone Its origin is tar'ayn: like tasma'in. The hamza was lightened and the nun was dropped for the jazm and the ya of the pronoun for the two quiescents after the addition of the nun of emphasis. Similar to this, with no intonations in the nun of emphasis, is the saying of Ibn Duraid: Don't you see that my head is the color of a morning's forehead under the covers of darkness? Talha and Shaiba read tarin with a sukoon on the yaa and a fatha on the noon, and lightened. Abu al-Fath said: It is anomalous, and the answer to the condition is Follow, I have vowed to the Most Gracious a fast meaning say if someone asks you to speak, I have vowed to the Most Gracious a fast meaning silence. It was said that what is meant by it is the legal fast, which is abstaining from things that break the fast, but the first is more appropriate. In Abu's reading, it is I have vowed to the Most Gracious a fast and silence by combining the two words. This is also narrated from Anas. It was narrated from him that he read sawm and samt with waw. The majority of commentators agree that fasting here means silence, and this is indicated by I will not speak to any human being today. The meaning of fasting in the language is broader than the two meanings. Abu Ubaidah said: Everyone who abstains from food, speech, or travel is fasting. Abu's reading indicates that what is meant by fasting here is silence, because it is an explanation of fasting. Anas’ reading indicates that fasting here is not silence, as the waw indicates. The meaning of I will not speak to any human today is that she will not speak to any human after informing them of this report. Rather, she will speak to the angels and commune with her Lord. It was said that she did not inform them here verbally, but rather with a gesture restricting the vow. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: She withdrew from her people to a place to the east, he said: A place where the sun shaded her so that none of them could see her. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The Christians took the east as a qiblah because Mary took a place to the east of her people, so they took his birth as a qiblah. The Jews prostrated on a ledge when the mountain rose above them, so they began to turn away while looking at it, fearing that it would fall on them, so they prostrated in a prostration that God was pleased with, so they took it as a Sunnah. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it, as did Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat, and Ibn Asakir, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abi Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. On the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, they said: Mary, daughter of Imran, went out to the side of the sanctuary because of her menses. When she became pure, there was a man with her, who appeared to her as a human being. She was startled and said, ‘Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you should be fearing God.’ So she went out wearing her cloak, and he took hold of her sleeve and blew into the side of her garment, which was torn in the front. The blow entered her chest and she became pregnant. Her sister, the wife of Zachariah, came to visit her one night. When she opened the door for her, she embraced her. The wife of Zachariah said, O Mary, do you feel that I am pregnant? Mary said, I feel that I am pregnant. The wife of Zachariah said, For I have found that which is in my womb prostrates to that which is in your womb. This is what God Almighty says: Confirming a word from God. So the wife of Zachariah gave birth to John. When Mary was about to give birth, she went out to the side of the sanctuary, “and the pangs of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, ‘Oh, I wish I had died before this.’” Then Gabriel called to her From beneath her, that you should not grieve. So when she gave birth to him, Satan went and informed the Children of Israel that Mary had given birth. When they wanted her to speak, she pointed to Jesus, so he spoke, and "He said, 'Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture.'" [The verses], and when he was born, there was not an idol on earth that did not fall on its face. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding Maryam, who said: When she became pregnant, she gave birth. Ibn Asakir narrated on his authority, who said: She gave birth after eight months. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Then We sent to her Our Spirit, he said: Gabriel. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abi bin Ka'b regarding the verse, who said: The spirit of Jesus appeared to her in the form of a human being, so she carried him. He said: She carried the one who spoke to her and entered her mouth. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, A distant place, he said: Far away. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: to the trunk of the palm tree, he said: It was a dry trunk. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him regarding his statement: and I was in oblivion, forgotten, he said: I was not created and I was nothing. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah, and I was in oblivion, forgotten, he said: A menstrual period that was cast away. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid something similar. Abd Ibn Humayd narrated from Nawf Al-Bakali and Ad-Dahhak something similar. Abd Ibn Humayd narrated from Ikrimah regarding his statement: and he called to her from beneath her, he said: The one who called to her was Gabriel. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, he said: The one who called to her from beneath her was Gabriel, and Jesus did not speak until she brought him to her people. There are different narrations from the predecessors, whether this caller was Gabriel or Jesus. And Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash who said: Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud read He called her from beneath her in the accusative case. He said: Asim said that whoever reads in the accusative case is Jesus, and whoever reads in the genitive case is Gabriel. And Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: The stream that God said to Mary, ‘Your Lord has provided a stream beneath you’ is a river that God brought forth for her to drink from. And in its chain of transmission is Ayoub bin Nahik Al-Jabali. Abu Hatim Al-Razi said about him: Weak. Abu Zur’ah said: His hadith is rejected. Abu Fath Al-Azdi said: His hadith is abandoned. And Al-Tabarani said after narrating this hadith: It is very strange. And Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Saghir and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding his statement: Your Lord has provided a stream beneath you, he said: The river. Abdul Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim who authenticated it, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’ who said regarding the verse: It is the stream, which is the small river. From this it is clear that the suspended verse is more correct. It has been narrated on the authority of a group of the followers that Al-Sarri is Jesus. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: fresh ripe dates he said: fresh. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his statement: Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast he said: silence. Abdul bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Anbari narrated on his authority that he recited a fast and silence.
19:27: When Mary, peace be upon her, was reassured by what she saw of the signs and she finished her childbirth 27- brought him meaning Jesus, and the phrase carried him is in the accusative case as a state, and her coming to them was from the remote place where she had secluded herself, and when they saw the child with her they were sad, and they were a righteous household, they said denying that, O Mary, you have certainly done meaning you have done a unique thing. Abu Ubaidah said: The unique is the strange and rare, and Al-Akhfash said the same. The unique is the definite, as if it is something that breaks the norm, or is definite as being strange and rare. Qatrab said: The new unique from the water skins: meaning you have come with a new and wonderful matter that has not been done before. Saeed bin Mas'adah said: The unique is the fabricated and contrived, it is said Farit and Afrit have the same meaning, and the child from fornication is like the fabricated bad, God Almighty said: And let them not come with a slander which they have invented between their hands and feet and Mujahid said: The unique is the great.
19:28: 28- O sister of Aaron. There has been a dispute over the meaning of this brotherhood, and who is the aforementioned Aaron? It has been said that he is Aaron, the brother of Moses, and the meaning is: how can someone we thought was like Aaron in worship come up with something like this? It has also been said that Mary was from the descendants of Aaron, the brother of Moses, so she was called O sister of Aaron, as is said to someone from the Arabs: O brother of the Arabs. It has also been said that she had a brother from her father whose name was Aaron. It has also been said that this Aaron was a righteous man at that time. It has also been said that there was at that time an immoral man whose name was Aaron, so they attributed her to him as an expression and a rebuke. Ibn Jarir narrated it, blaming its speaker, and he is weak: Your father was not a bad man, nor was your mother unchaste. This is a confirmation of what was mentioned above of the expression and rebuke, and a warning that immorality among the offspring of the righteous is something that should not happen.
19:29: 29- So she pointed to him meaning to Jesus, and she was satisfied with the pointing and did not order him to speak, because she had vowed to the Most Gracious to fast from speech as mentioned above, this is on the assumption that she was at that time in the days of her vow, and on the assumption that she had left the days of her vow, then it can be said that her limiting herself to the pointing was to exaggerate in showing the great sign, and that this newborn understands the pointing and is able to express the phrase They said, How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? This question is to express denial and astonishment at her pointing to that newborn to speak to them. Abu Ubaidah said: There is redundant padding in the speech. The meaning is: How can we speak to a child in the cradle, like the poet's saying: Our neighbors were generous. Al-Zajjaj said: It is better to have min in the sense of condition and consequence, and the meaning is: Whoever is a child in the cradle, how do we speak to him? Ibn al-Anbari preferred this and said: It is not permissible to say that it is redundant and it has made child the subject, and the answer to that is that whoever says it is redundant makes the subject the verb, which is we speak as previously estimated. It was said that here it is the complete one that means occurrence and existence, and it was responded that if it were complete it would dispense with the predicate, and the cradle is a well-known thing that is used to put a child to sleep. The meaning is how do we speak to him in order to put him to sleep in the cradle because of his smallness, and it was said here it is the mother’s lap, and it was said a bed like the cradle.
19:30: When Jesus heard their words 30- He said, 'I am the servant of God.' The first thing he said was the acknowledgment of his servitude to Him. He gave me the Book, meaning the Gospel: meaning He decreed that I would be given the Book and the Prophethood in eternity, even though it had not been revealed to him in that state nor had he become a Prophet. It was said that He gave him the Book and made him a Prophet in that state, which is far-fetched.
19:31: 31- And He has made me blessed wherever I may be meaning wherever you may be, and the origin of blessing is from the camel's kneeling, and the meaning is: He has made me steadfast in the religion of God, and it was said that blessing is increase and elevation, so it is as if he said: He has made me in all things increased, high and successful, and it was said that the meaning of blessed is benefit to the servants, and it was said that the teacher of good, and it was said that the one who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong And He has enjoined upon me prayer meaning that He commanded me to do it and zakat the zakat of money, or purifying the soul as long as I live meaning for the duration of my life, and these past actions are a case of placing what has not yet occurred in the position of reality, drawing attention to the certainty of its occurrence because it has already occurred in the final judgment.
19:32: 32- And dutiful to my mother is in apposition to blessed, and he limited it to dutifulness to his mother because he knew in that situation that he did not have a father, and it was read dutiful with a kasra on the ba' as a source of description with exaggeration And did not make me a wretched tyrant the arrogant tyrant who does not see anyone's right over him, and the wretched one who disobeys his Lord, and it was said the loser, and it was said the disobedient.
19:33: 33- "And peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I die and the day I am raised alive." The commentators said: Peace here means safety: that is, safety upon me the day I was born, so Satan did not harm me at that time, nor did he tempt me at death or at the resurrection. It was said that what is meant by it is greeting. It was said that the lam is for the genus, and it was said for the covenant: that is, that peace directed to John in these three places is directed to me. It was said that Christ did not speak after this speech until he reached the period in which children usually speak. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So she brought him to her people, carrying him, he said: After forty days after her confinement. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and others narrated on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to the people of Najran, and they said: ‘Have you seen what you read: “O sister of Aaron,” and Moses was before Jesus by such and such?’ He said: ‘So I returned and mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘Should you not tell them that they were called by the names of the prophets and righteous people before them?’” This prophetic interpretation suffices for all that has been narrated from the early generations regarding that. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Anas who said: Jesus had studied the Gospel and its rulings in his mother’s womb, so that is why he said: “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture.” Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement, He has given me the Book and the verse. He said: It was decreed that I should be thus. Al-Isma’ili narrated in his Mu’jam, Abu Nu’aym in al-Hilyah, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the statement of Jesus, “And has made me blessed wherever I may be,” that is, He has made me beneficial to people wherever I go.” Ibn ‘Adi and Ibn ‘Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, And has made me blessed, that is, a teacher and tutor. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas regarding his statement, And has not made me a wretched tyrant, that is, disobedient.
19:34: The reference in his saying: 34- That is to the one described by the previous descriptions. Al-Zajjaj said: That is the one who said, I am the servant of God, Jesus, son of Mary, not what the Christians say that he is the son of God and that he is a god. Ibn Amir, Asim, and Ya'qub read the saying of the truth in the accusative case, and the rest read it in the nominative case. The reason for the first reading is that it is in the accusative case for praise, or that it is a source of emphasis for I am the servant of God, as Al-Zajjaj said. The reason for the second reading is that it is an attribute of Jesus: that is, that Jesus, son of Mary, is the saying of the truth, as Al-Kisa'i said. And it is called the saying of the truth as it is called the word of God, and the truth is God Almighty. Abu Hatim said: The meaning is the saying of the truth. It was said that the estimate is: This is for the speech of the saying of the truth, and it is from the category of adding the described to the description like the truth of certainty. It was said that the addition is for clarification. It was read as the saying of the truth and it was narrated from Ibn Masoud. Al-Hasan read the saying of the truth with a damma on the qaf. The saying, the saying, the saying and the statement have the same meaning. about which they are in dispute is a description of Jesus: that is, that is Jesus, son of Mary, about whom they are in dispute, the saying of the truth. The meaning of they are in dispute is that they differ on the basis that it is from disputation, or they complain on the basis that it is from doubt. And the difference occurred regarding Jesus, so the Jews said he is a magician, and the Christians said he is the son of God.
19:35: 35- It is not for God to take a son meaning that it is not correct nor is it right, for an is in the nominative case as the subject of kana. Al-Zajjaj said: Min in min wold is an emphasis that indicates the negation of one and the group, then the Almighty cleared Himself and said: Glory be to Him meaning He is far removed and sanctified from what they say, then the Almighty stated what is His affair, exalted be His power, for He said: When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is meaning when He decrees a matter, it is at that time without delay. We have already discussed this in detail in Surat Al-Baqarah, and in presenting it in this place is a great rebuke to the Christians: that is, how can someone whose affair is like this imagine that he could have a son?
19:36: 36- Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. The people of Medina, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read it with a fat-ha on an. Ibn Amir and the people of Kufa read it with a kasra, and this is part of the words of Isa. Abu read Indeed, God without a waw. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: In explaining the reading of the accusative, the meaning is: Because God is my Lord and your Lord. Al-Farra' permitted it to be in the genitive case in apposition to the prayer. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' permitted it to be in apposition to a matter. This is a straight path, meaning that what I have mentioned to you, that He is my Lord and your Lord, is the straight path in which there is no crookedness and its follower does not go astray.
19:37: 37- "Then the parties differed among themselves" from the redundant particle for emphasis, and the parties are the Jews and Christians: meaning the groups of the People of the Book differed regarding the matter of Jesus, so the Jews said that he was a magician as mentioned above, and they said that he was the son of Joseph the carpenter, and the groups of the Christians differed regarding him, so the Nestorians among them said: He is the son of God, and the Malikis said: The third of three, and the Jacobites said: He is God Almighty, so the Christians went to extremes and went to extremes, and the Jews were negligent and fell short, "So woe to those who disbelieved and they are the ones who differed regarding his matter, from the scene of a tremendous day" meaning from witnessing the Day of Resurrection and what will happen in it of reckoning and punishment, or from the place of witnesses in it, or from the testimony of that day against them, and it was said that the meaning is: So woe to them from their attendance at the tremendous scene in which they gathered for consultation.
19:38: 38- I hear and see them. Abu Abbas said: The Arabs say this in a place of astonishment, so they say: I hear and I see it: meaning what I hear and see. So God Almighty was astonished at His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from them. On the Day they come to Us, meaning for the reckoning and punishment. But the wrongdoers today, meaning in this world, are in manifest error, meaning clear and apparent, but they neglected to think, consider, and look into the effects.
19:39: 39- And warn them of the Day of Regret meaning the day when they will all regret it, so the wrongdoer will regret his wrongdoing, and the good doer will regret not having done much good when the matter has been decided meaning the reckoning has been completed and the records have been folded, and the people of Paradise will be in Paradise and the people of Hell will be in Hell. The phrase and they are in heedlessness is in the accusative case as a state: meaning they are heedless of what is being done to them, and likewise the phrase and they do not believe is in the accusative case as a state.
19:40: 40- Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it. That is, We cause its inhabitants to die, so that no one remains to inherit the dead. It is as if He, glory be to Him, inherited the earth and whoever is on it, since He caused them all to die. And to Us they will be returned. That is, they will return to Us on the Day of Resurrection, and We will reward each one according to his deeds. Something similar to this has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Hijr. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: The word of truth, he said: God is the Truth, Almighty and Majestic. And Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: about which they have doubts, he said: The Children of Israel gathered and brought out from among them four men from each people, their scholar, and they doubted about Jesus when he was raised. One of them said: He is God, He descended to the earth and gave life to whom He gave life, and caused death to whom He caused death, then he ascended to the heavens. They were the Jacobites. The three said: You have lied. Then two of them said to the third: Say something about him. He said: He is the son of God. They were the Nestorians. Two of them said: You have lied. Then one of the two said to the other: Say something about him. He said: He is the third of three. God is God, and Jesus is God, and his mother is God. They were the Israelites, and they were the kings of the Christians. The fourth said: You have lied. He is the servant of God and His Messenger and His spirit from His word. They were the Muslims. So each man of them had followers for what he said, so they fought and were victorious over the Muslims. This is what God Almighty said: And they kill those who enjoin justice among the people. Qatada said: They are the ones about whom God said, Then the parties differed from among themselves. He said: They differed about it and became parties, and the people argued, and the Muslim said: I ask you by God, do you know that Jesus used to feed the poor and that God does not feed them? They said: By God, yes. He said: Do you know that Jesus used to sleep and that God does not sleep? They said: By God, yes. So the Muslims argued with them and the people fought, and it was mentioned to us that the Jacobites appeared on that day and the Muslims were afflicted, so God revealed: So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a tremendous Day. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, I hear them and I see them, the disbelievers say on that day: I hear something and I see it, but today they neither hear nor see. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada regarding His statement, The Day they come to Us, that he said: That is the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, death will be brought like a white ram and will be stopped between Paradise and Hell. It will be said: ‘O people of Paradise, do you recognize this? ’ They will look up and look at it and say: ‘Yes, this is death,’ and all of them have seen it. Then the people of Hell will be called out: ‘Do you recognize this? ’ They will look up and look and say: ‘Yes, this is death,’ and all of them have seen it. Then it will be ordered to be slaughtered and it will be said: ‘O people of Paradise, eternal life and no death, and O people of Hell, eternal life and no death. ’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And warn them of the Day of Regret’ and pointed with his hand and said: ‘The people of this world are heedless. ’” Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Day of Regret is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. He recited: That a soul will say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God.’ This is weak, and the verse that Ibn Abbas used as evidence does not indicate what is required, neither by conformity, nor by implication, nor by commitment.
19:41: His statement: 41- And remember is in apposition to and warn, and what is meant by the Messenger mentioning him in the Book is that he should recite that to the people, like his statement: And recite to them the report of Abraham, and the phrase Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet is an explanation of what preceded from the command to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to mention him, and it is an interjection between the substitute and what is being replaced, and the friend is very truthful, and the accusative of prophet is that it is another predicate of was: that is, mention Abraham, who combines these two descriptions.
19:42: And 42- When he said to his father is a substitute for inclusion from Abraham, and the mention is linked to the time although the intention is to remind him of the incidents that happened in him for the sake of exaggeration, and Abraham's father is Azar according to what was previously reported, and the ta' in Ya Abi is a substitute for the ya', and for this reason they do not come together, and the question in Why do you worship is for denial and rebuke that which does not hear what you say of praising Him and praying for Him nor sees what you do of worshipping Him and the actions that you do intending reward by them, and it is permissible to carry the negation of hearing and seeing to what is more general than that: that is, he does not hear anything of the things that are heard, nor does he see anything of the things that are seen nor does it avail you at all of the things, so it does not bring you benefit nor ward off harm from you, and they are the idols that Azar used to worship, Abraham, peace be upon him, brought evidence and advice to his father, and he began each of them with a call that included kindness and gentleness to win his heart and comply For the sake of his Lord.
19:43: Then he repeated his call to the truth and said: 43- O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you. So he informed that he had received a share of knowledge that had not reached his father, and that he had been granted a new acquisition of what would lead him to the truth and enable him to guide the lost. For this reason he ordered him to follow him and said: So follow me, I will guide you to a straight path, straight, leading to what is desired and saving from what is disliked.
19:44: Then he confirmed that with another piece of advice to deter him from what he was doing, saying: 44- "O my father, do not worship Satan" meaning do not obey him, because worshipping idols is obeying Satan. Then he explained that by saying: "Indeed, Satan was disobedient to the Most Merciful" when he left what he was commanded to do of prostrating to Adam. And whoever obeys someone who is disobedient to God, the Most High, is disobedient to God, and the disobedient deserves to have blessings taken away from him and punishments befall him. Al-Kisa'i said: Disobedient and disobedient have the same meaning.
19:45: Then he explained to him the motive for this advice, saying: 45- O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Gracious will afflict you. Al-Farra' said: The meaning of I fear here is I know. The majority said: The fear here is to be taken at face value, because Abraham was not certain that his father would die as a disbeliever, because if he had been certain of that, he would not have been busy advising him. The meaning of fear for others is that he thinks that harm will reach that other. Then you will be a friend of Satan, meaning that if you obey Satan, you will be with him in the Fire and the curse, so you will be a friend because of this, or you will be because of your friendliness in the punishment with him, and there is no true friendship, because of the Almighty's saying: Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another. It was said that friend means follower, and it was said that friend means close, meaning you will be close to Satan in the Fire.
19:46: When these beneficial pieces of advice and acceptable sermons reached the ears of Azar, he met them with harshness, rudeness and cruelty. 46- He said, 'Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham?' The question is for rebuke, rebuke and astonishment, and the meaning is: Are you turning away from that and turning to something else? Then he threatened him and said: If you do not desist, I will stone you, meaning with stones, and it was said the tongue, so its meaning is I will curse you, and it was said its meaning is I will beat you, and it was said I will expose your affair, and leave me for a long time, meaning a long time. Al-Kisa'i said: It is said I left him for a long time, and a long time, meaning the long time, and from it the saying of Muhalhil: The mountains cracked at his death and the widows wept for him. It was said that its meaning is: Stay away from harm, lest you be disgraced by me. Ibn Jarir chose this, so milia according to this is in the accusative case of the state of Ibrahim, and according to the first statement it is in the accusative case of the circumstance. So when Ibrahim saw his father’s insistence on stubbornness.
19:48: Then Al-Khalil stated what his greeting included of farewell and abandonment, saying: 48- And I will leave you and what you call upon besides God meaning I will migrate with my religion from you and from your deities since you did not accept my advice nor did my call to you work and I will call upon my Lord alone perhaps I will not be, in the call of my Lord, unhappy meaning disappointed, and it was said disobedient. It was said that he meant by this call: that God would grant him a son and a family with whom he would find comfort in his isolation and with whom he would feel reassured when he was lonely, and it was said that he meant his call for his father to be guided, and perhaps is for doubt because he did not know whether his call would be answered in it or not.
19:49: And the first is more appropriate, because of His statement: 49- So when he had withdrawn from them and what they worshipped besides God, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, meaning We made those who were given to him family and children in place of the family he had left. And each one of them We made a prophet, meaning each one of them. The accusative case of each one being the first object of We made is presented before it for specificity, but in relation to them themselves, not in relation to those other than them: meaning each one of them We made a prophet, not some of them without others.
19:50: 50- And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy by making them prophets. This was mentioned after explicitly making them prophets to show that prophethood is from the category of mercy. It was said that what is meant by mercy here is money, and it was said children, and it was said the Book, and it is not far-fetched that all of these matters are included under it. And We made for them a tongue of truthfulness, exalted. The tongue of truthfulness is good praise. It was expressed by the tongue because it is found in it, just as the hand was expressed by the gift. Adding it to truthfulness and describing it as exalted is to indicate that they are more deserving of what is said about them of praise on the tongues of the servants. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: I will stone you he said: I will curse you, and leave me alone for a while he said: for a while. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: and leave me alone for a while he said: avoid me completely. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse: he said: avoid me safely before a punishment befalls you from me. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah: for a long time a long time. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: safe. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, he was kind to me he said: gentle. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob he said: We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob his grandson. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And We made for them a tongue of truth, Ali, he said: Good praise.
19:51: God followed the story of Abraham with the story of Moses because he followed him in honor, and He put Ishmael before him so that there would be no separation between him and the mention of Jacob: that is, recite to them from the Qur’an the story of Moses 51- Indeed, he was sincere. The people of Kufa read it with the opening of the lam: that is, We made him chosen and made him sincere. The rest read it with the closing of it: that is, he sincerely worshipped and monotheized God without disputing with the servants. And he was a messenger and a prophet. That is, God sent him to His servants and he informed them from God about His laws that He legislated for them. This is the reason for mentioning the prophet after the messenger, even though the message entails prophethood. It is as if He intended by the messenger its linguistic meaning, not the legal meaning. And God knows best. Al-Naysaburi said: The messenger who has a book from the prophets, and the prophet who was informed from God Almighty even if he did not have a book. It would have been appropriate to mention the general before the specific, except that observing the separator required the opposite, like His saying in Ta-Ha 20:The Lord of Aaron and Moses. End quote.
19:52: 52- And We called him from the right side of the Mount meaning We spoke to him from the side of the Mount, which is a mountain between Egypt and Madyan called Zubayr. The meaning of right is that it was on the right side of Moses, because the tree was on that side and the call came from it, and it does not mean the right side of the mountain itself, because mountains have no right or left. It was said that the meaning of right is auspicious, and the meaning of the call is that the speech was presented to him from that side. And We brought him near in confidential conversation meaning We brought him near by bringing him near in a close position until We spoke to him. The meaning of the conversation is the one who is confiding, like the companion and the friend, so bringing near here is bringing near to honor and respect. His state was likened to the state of the one who is close to the angel to confide in him. Al-Zajjaj said: He brought him near to him in a close position until he heard his confide in him. It was said that God, the Most High, raised him until he heard the scratching of the pen. This was narrated from some of the predecessors.
19:53: 53- And We bestowed upon him of Our mercy meaning of Our grace, and it was said because of Our mercy, and Aaron is an explanatory apposition, and a prophet is a state of it, and that was when he asked his Lord, saying: Make for me a helper from my family * Aaron, my brother.
19:54: And God the Almighty described Ishmael as being true to his promise, although all the prophets were like that, because he was famous for that and exaggerated in it, and in addition to that he promised patience from himself for the slaughter and he fulfilled that, and he used to wait for those he promised with the promise of days and nights, until it was said that he waited for some of those he promised for a year. What is meant by Ishmael here is Ishmael, son of Abraham, and no one disagreed with that except those who are not respected, so they said: He is Ishmael, son of Ezekiel, God sent him to his people and they skinned the skin of his head, so God gave him the choice of whatever He wanted from their punishment, so he excused himself and was satisfied with his reward, and the Almighty’s saying in Ishmael 54- And he was a messenger and a prophet was used as evidence that the messenger does not have to be the bearer of a law because the sons of Abraham were his law, and it was said that he described him as a messenger because Abraham sent him to Jurhum.
19:55: 55- And he used to enjoin prayer and zakat upon his family. It was said that what is meant by his family here is his nation, and it was said that Jurhum, and it was said that it was his clan as in His statement: And warn your nearest relatives. What is meant by prayer and zakat here are the two legitimate acts of worship, and it is possible that their linguistic meaning is intended, And he was pleasing to his Lord, meaning pleasing, pure, and righteous. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: Whoever says mardi builds on raday, and they said: The people of Hijaz say mardu.
19:56: 56- And mention in the Book, Idris. The name of Idris is Enoch. It was said that he is the grandfather of Noah, for Noah is the son of Lamech, the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch. Based on this, he is the grandfather of Noah's father, as mentioned by Al-Tha'labi and others. It was said that this is a mistake, and that Idris is not allowed due to his foreignness and his lack of knowledge. He was the first to write with a pen, study the stars and arithmetic, and the first to sew clothes. It was said that he was the first of the sons of Adam to be given prophethood.
19:57: There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of his statement: 57- And We raised him to a high station. It was said that God raised him to the fourth heaven, and it was said to the sixth, and it was said to the second. Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of the Night Journey, and it says: And among them is Idris in the second, and this is a mistake in the narration of Sharik bin Abdullah bin Abi Namir. The correct view is that he is in the fourth heaven, as narrated by Muslim in his Sahih from the hadith of Anas bin Malik from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that what is meant by raising him to a high station is the honor of prophethood that he was given, and it was said that he was raised to Paradise.
19:58: 58- Those upon whom God has bestowed favor from among the prophets refers to those mentioned from the beginning of the surah to here, and the relative pronoun is its description, and from the prophets is an explanation of the relative pronoun, and from the descendants of Adam is a substitute for it by repeating the preposition, and it was said that from in from the descendants of Adam is for partiality, and and from those whom We carried with Noah meaning from the descendants of those whom We carried with him and they are those other than Idris, for Abraham was from the descendants of Sam, son of Noah, and and from the descendants of Abraham and they are the rest, and Israel meaning from the descendants of Israel, and among them are Moses, Aaron, John, and Jesus, and it was said that by his saying: from the descendants of Adam he meant Idris alone, and by his saying: and from those whom We carried with Noah he meant Abraham alone, and by his saying: and from the descendants of Abraham he meant Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob, and by his saying: and from the descendants of Abraham and Israel he meant Moses, Aaron, Zachariah, John, and Jesus, and and from those whom We guided meaning from A sentence from those whom we have guided to Islam and chosen with faith, when the verses of the Most Gracious are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping. This is report for those, and it is possible that the report is those upon whom God has bestowed His blessings. This is a resumption to explain their humility and fear of God. The meaning of they fell down in prostration has already been explained in Subhan: it is said, he cried, crying, and weeping. Al-Khalil said: If you shorten crying, it is like sadness: meaning there is no sound with it, and from this is the saying of the poet: My eyes cried and it was right to cry, but crying and wailing are of no use. And prostration is in the accusative case as a state. Al-Zajjaj said: God has made it clear that when the prophets heard God’s verses, they would cry and prostrate, and this verse was used as evidence for the legitimacy of prostration of recitation.
19:59: When these prophets were praised with these descriptions to encourage others to follow their example and adopt their path, he mentioned their opposites to repel people from their path, saying: 59- Then there came after them a successor meaning an evil successor. Linguists said: The successor of good is called a successor with a fat-ha on the lam, and the successor of evil is called a successor with a sukoon on the lam. We have already discussed this at the end of Al-A'raf. They wasted the prayer Most said: The meaning of this is that they delayed it from its time, and it was said that they wasted the time, and it was said that they disbelieved in it and denied its obligation, and it was said that they did not perform it in the prescribed manner. It appears that whoever delays the prayer from its time or leaves one of its obligations or one of its conditions or one of its pillars has wasted it, and the one who leaves it completely or denies it is included under wasting it in a primary sense. They differed about who this verse was revealed to. Some said it was about the Jews, some said it was about the Christians, and some said it was about a people from the nation of Muhammad (peace be upon him) who will come at the end of time. The meaning of and they followed desires is that they did what their souls desired and yearned for of forbidden things such as drinking alcohol and committing adultery. Then they will meet with error. Error means evil according to the linguists, just as good means guidance. The meaning is that they will meet evil, not good. It was said that error means misguidance, and it was said it is disappointment. It was said that it is the name of a valley in Hell. It was said that there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: they will meet the punishment of error. This is what Al-Zajjaj said. Similar to it is the saying of the Almighty: will meet sins, meaning the punishment of sins.
19:60: 60- Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds. That is, those who repent from what they have neglected, such as neglecting prayers and following desires, then return to obeying God, believe in Him, and do righteous deeds. This exception is evidence that the verse is about the infidels, not the Muslims. Then those will enter Paradise. Abu Ja`far, Shaibah, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Abu `Amr, Ya`qub, and Abu Bakr read they will enter with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the kha. The rest read it with a fatha on the ya and a damma on the kha. And they will not be wronged at all. That is, nothing will be reduced from their rewards, even if it is little, for God, the Exalted, will pay them their rewards in full.
19:61: And the accusative of 61- "Janāt Adn" is in apposition to Jannah, a apposition to some because Jannah Adn is part of Jannah. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible to say Jannah Adn in the nominative case as a subject, and it was also read. Abu Hatim said: And if it were not for the mistake, it would have been Jannah Adn: meaning in the singular instead of the plural, and this is nothing, for Jannah is the name of the group of Jannahs that are like species for the genus. And it was read in the accusative of Jannah as a compliment, and it was read in the singular "which the Most Gracious has promised His servants in the unseen" this sentence is an attribute of Jannah Adn, and in the unseen is in the accusative case as a state of Jannahs, or of His servants: meaning clothed, or clothed in the unseen, and it was read in the genus Adn, and from it as a name for the meaning of Adn, which is residence, or a name for the land of Jannah "Indeed, His promise was fulfilled" meaning His promise in general. So the Jannahs are included in it as a primary entry. Al-Farra' said: He did not say coming. Because everything that came to you, you have come to it, and so said Al-Zajjaj.
19:62: 62- They will not hear therein idle talk is idle talk that is useless and has no benefit, and it is a metaphor for not uttering idle talk from them, and it was said that idle talk is everything that does not include mention of God "except peace" is a discontinuous exception: meaning the peace of some of them to others, or the peace of the angels to them. Al-Zajjaj said: Peace is a comprehensive name for goodness, because it includes safety, and the meaning is: The people of Paradise will not hear what hurts them, but rather they will hear what keeps them safe. And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening The commentators said that there is no morning or evening in Paradise, but they will be given their provision according to the amount they know of lunch and dinner. Then the Almighty explained what He summarized of the evil of the torment, saying: 46- The Fire, they will be exposed to it morning and evening. So the Fire was raised as a substitute for the evil of the torment, and it was said that it is the predicate of a deleted subject, or a subject and its predicate are exposed, and the first is better and Al-Zajjaj preferred it. According to the last two interpretations, the sentence is renewed in answer to an implied question. And it was read in the accusative, assuming a verb that explains it is exposed in terms of meaning: that is, they will enter the Fire, they will be exposed to it, or as a specification, and Al-Farraa permitted the genitive as a substitute for the torment. The majority of scholars said that this exposure is in the Barzakh, and it was said that it is in the Hereafter. Al-Farra’ said: “There is an inversion in this verse: that is, admit the family of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment, the Fire, to which they will be exposed morning and evening. There is no resort to this exaggeration, for His statement, ‘And on the Day the Hour will appear, admit the family of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment,’ clearly indicates that this exposure will be in the Barzakh. His statement, ‘Enter,’ is in the sense of ‘say,’ that is, it will be said to the angels, ‘Enter the family of Pharaoh,’ and ‘the most severe punishment’ is the punishment of the Fire.” Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Nafi’, and Hafs read ‘adkhilu’ with a fat-ha on the hamzah and a kasra on the kha’, and it is in the sense of ‘say,’ as mentioned. The rest read ‘idkhulu’ with a hamzah wasl from yadkhul, commanding the family of Pharaoh to enter, in the sense of a letter of address: that is, enter, O family of Pharaoh, into the most severe punishment.”
19:63: 63- That is the Paradise which We give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were righteous. That is, this Paradise whose conditions We have described, We give as an inheritance to those who were righteous, just as an heir retains the wealth of his inheritance. Yaqub read nuthra with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the ra', while the rest read it with a sukoon. It was said that there is an advancement and delay in the speech, and the meaning is: We give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were righteous. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And he was a Messenger, a Prophet, he said: The Prophet is the one to whom revelation is sent and to whom he is not sent. The wording of Ibn Abi Hatim is: The Prophets who are not Messengers, to whom revelation is sent but to whom no one is sent. The Messengers are the Prophets to whom revelation is sent and who are sent. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: The right side of the Mount, he said: The right side of the mountain. And We brought him near for confidential conversation, he said: He was saved by his truthfulness. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah, he said: He brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of a group of the Followers. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: He said: Until he heard the scratching of the pen writing on the tablet. Al-Daylami narrated it on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We bestowed upon him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, that he said: Aaron was older than Moses, but He only bestowed upon him his prophethood. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We raised him to a high station, that he said: Idris was a tailor, and he would not sew a stitch without saying: Glory be to God. And he would go to bed every evening and there was no one on earth who did better work than him. So an angel from the angels asked permission from his Lord and said: O Lord, give me permission to descend to Idris. So He gave him permission, so he came to Idris and said: I have come to serve you.
