He said: How can you serve me when you are an angel and I am a human? Then Idris said: Is there anything between you and the Angel of Death? The angel said: That is my brother from the angels. He said: Can you benefit me? He said: He will neither delay nor advance anything, but I will speak to him for you and he will be gentle with you when you die. He said: Ride between my wings. So Idris rode and ascended to the highest heaven and met the Angel of Death with Idris between his wings. The angel said to him: I have a need of you. He said: I know your need, speak to me about Idris, and his name has been erased from the scroll, so only half the blink of an eye remained for him. So Idris died between the wings of the angel. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Masahif and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he asked Ka’b and he mentioned something similar. This is from the Isra’iliyyat that Ka’b narrated. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Idris was raised to the sixth heaven. At-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it, and Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated that Anas bin Malik told us on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When I was taken up, I saw Idris in the fourth heaven. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid. In the verse, He said that Idris was raised as Jesus was raised and he did not die. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: Idris is Elias. Al-Suyuti classified it as good. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding His statement: Those are the ones upon whom God has bestowed His favor to the end, he said: This is the name of the prophets whom He mentioned. As for the descendants of Adam: Idris and Noah. As for those who were carried with Noah, they were Abraham. As for the descendants of Abraham: Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob. As for the descendants of Israel: Moses, Aaron, Zachariah, John, and Jesus. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding His statement: Then there came after them a generation he said: They are the Jews and Christians. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: They are from this nation, they overlap on the roads as livestock overlap, they are not shy before people, and they do not fear God in the heavens. And Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: They neglected the prayer, he said: Its neglect does not mean abandoning it. A person may neglect something and not abandon it, but its neglect is if he does not pray it at its time. Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that he heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recite this verse: Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer and pursued desires, the verse. He said: There will be a generation after sixty years who neglected the prayer and pursued desires. Then they are going to meet with error, then there will be a generation who recite the Qur’an but it will not go beyond their collarbones, and three will recite the Qur’an: a believer, a hypocrite, and a wicked person. Ahmad and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the authority of ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Aamir: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: The People of the Book and the People of Milk will perish from among my nation. I said: O Messenger of God, who are the People of the Book? He said: People who learn the Book and argue with those who believe by it. I said: Who are the People of Milk? He said: People who follow their desires and neglect their prayers. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the authority of ‘Aa’ishah that she used to send charity to those who were given charity and say: “Do not give any of it to a Berber man or woman, for I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “They are the successors about whom God said: ‘Then there succeeded them a generation.’” Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to Ibn ‘Abbaas regarding His statement: Then they will meet with error, that he said: Loss. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Hannad, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Baath narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: Then they will meet Ghayyan, he said: Ghayyan is a river or valley in Hell of pus with a deep bottom and foul taste, into which those who follow their desires are thrown. Al-Bara bin Azib said that it is a valley in Hell. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Tabarani narrated that on his authority. Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a rock weighing ten ounces were thrown from the edge of Hell, it would not reach its bottom for seventy years, then it would end in Ghayy and Atham. I said: What are Ghayy and Atham? He said: “There are two rivers at the bottom of Hell in which the pus of the people of Hell flows. They are the ones mentioned by God in His Book: ‘Then they will meet Ghayyah’ and ‘And whoever does that will meet Atham.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ghayyah is a valley in Hell. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding His statement: They will not hear therein any idle talk, he said: Falsehood. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding His statement: morning and evening, he said: They will be given it in the Hereafter according to the amount they were given in this world. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawadir Al-Usul on the authority of Aban on the authority of Al-Hasan and Abu Qilabah, who said: “A man said: O Messenger of God, is there night in Paradise? He said: What made you do this? He said: I heard God mention in the Book, ‘And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening. ’ I said: The night is from the morning and evening. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no night there, but rather it is light and radiance. The morning comes after the evening and the evening comes after the morning. The best gifts from God come to them at the times of the prayers that they used to pray in the world, and the angels greet them.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no morning of the mornings of Paradise, and all of Paradise is mornings, until a wife from the houris of Paradise is brought to the friend of God therein, and the least of them is the one created from saffron.” He said: After narrating it, Abu Muhammad said: This is a rejected hadith.
19:64: His saying: 64- And we do not descend meaning God the Almighty said: Say, O Gabriel, and we do not descend, and that is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was slow in Gabriel's descent upon him, so he ordered Gabriel to inform him that the angels do not descend upon him except by the command of God. It was said that Gabriel was delayed from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for forty days, and it was said fifteen, and it was said twelve, and it was said three days, and it was said that this is a narration about the people of Paradise, and that they say upon entering it: And we do not descend to these gardens except by the command of your Lord and the first is more definite in meaning than what preceded it, and its meaning has two possible meanings: the first is and we do not descend upon you except by the command of your Lord to descend. The second is and we do not descend upon you except by the command of your Lord who commands you with what He has prescribed for you and your nation, and descending means descending slowly, and it may be applied to any descent in general. Then Gabriel confirmed what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had informed him of, saying: To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that, meaning of directions and places, or of the past and future crises, and what is between them of time or the place in which we are. We are not able to move from one direction to another, or from one time to another, except by the command and will of your Lord. It was said that the meaning is: To Him belongs what has passed of the worldly affairs and what will come of the Hereafter and what is between that, which is what is between the two blasts. It was also said that it is the earth that is before us when we descend, and the sky that is behind us and what is between the sky and the earth. It was also said that it is what has passed of our lives and what has changed of them and the state in which we are. According to all these sayings, the meaning is: God Almighty is the One who encompasses everything, nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing escapes His knowledge, even the weight of an atom. We do not undertake a matter except with His permission. He said: and what is between that, and did not say: and what is between those two, because what is meant is: and what is between what we mentioned, as in His Almighty saying: He is between that “And your Lord is not forgetful” meaning He does not forget even if the revelation is delayed from you. It was said that the meaning is: He is All-Knowing of all things and does not forget anything of them. It was said that the meaning is: and your Lord does not forget sending to you at the time when He sends His messengers.
19:65: 65- Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them meaning He is the Creator of what is between them, and the Owner of them and the Owner of what is between them, and whoever is like this, forgetfulness is impossible for him. Then God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to worship Him and be patient in it, so He said: So worship Him and be patient in His worship and the fa is for causality because His being the Lord of the worlds is a reason for Him to be worshipped, and the verb to be patient is transitive with the lam rather than ala which is transitive because it includes the meaning of steadfastness Do you know of anyone similar to Him? The question is for denial. Meaning: He has no equal or peer to share in worship with Him, so it is necessary that it is not purely for Him, glory be to Him. So when the partner is negated, God, glory be to Him, deserves to be singled out for worship and to be purely for Him. This is based on the fact that what is meant by the name is the partner in the named, and it was said that what is meant by it is: the partner in the name as is apparent from the language of the Arabs. So it was said that the meaning is: Nothing from the idols or others was ever named God, meaning after the introduction of the alif and lam that replaced the hamza and was necessary. And it was said that what is meant is: Do you know anyone whose name is the Most Gracious other than Him? Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation, and God knows best, is: Do you know anyone named for Him who deserves to be called Creator, Able, and Knower of what was and what will be? And based on this, there is no name for God in all of His names, because even if someone other than Him is named with one of His names, God, glory be to Him, has the reality of that description, and what is meant by the negation of knowledge derived from denial here is the negation of the known in the most eloquent and complete manner.
19:66: 66- And man says, 'When I die, will I then be brought back alive?' The majority of scholars read it as a question, while Ibn Dhakwan read it as a statement. What is meant by man here is the disbeliever, because this question here is for denial, mockery, and denial of the resurrection. It was said that the lam in man refers to the entire species, even though only some people said this statement, and they are the disbelievers. What one of them did may be attributed to the group. What is meant by his saying brought out: that is, from the grave, and the factor in the circumstance is a verb indicated by brought out, because what comes after the lam does not affect what comes before it.
19:67: 67- Or does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing? The hamza is for reproachful denial, and the waw is to connect the sentence that follows it to the sentence that precedes it. What is meant by remembering here is the application of thought: that is, does this denier not think about the beginning of his creation and deduce from the beginning the return? The beginning is more amazing and strange than the return, because the first creation is the bringing forth of these creatures from nothingness into existence as an innovation and invention, and nothing preceded it that would be like an example for it. As for the last creation, the first creation preceded it, so it was like an example for it. The meaning of before is before the state that he is in now. The sentence and he was nothing is in the accusative case as a state: that is, while he was not at that time anything at all, so returning him after he was something existing is easier and simpler. The people of Mecca, Abu Amr, Abu Ja`far, and the people of Kufa, except `Asim, read or does he not remember with emphasis, and its root is remembering. Shaiba, Nafi, Asim, and Ibn Amir read yadhkirr with a light pronunciation, and in Abu’s reading aw la yadhkirr.
19:68: Then when the Almighty came with this argument that the rational people agreed that there was no stronger argument than it among the arguments for resurrection, He confirmed it by swearing by His name, the Almighty, in addition to His Messenger, to honor and glorify him, and He said: 68- By your Lord, We will surely gather them. The meaning of We will surely gather them is: We will drive them to the place of assembly after bringing them out from their graves alive as they were, and the and in His statement: and the devils is to connect with the accusative, or in the sense of with. Meaning: That these deniers will be gathered by God with their devils who tempted them and led them astray. This is apparent from the fact that the lam in insan is for the covenant, which is the disbelieving human being. As for its being for the genus, it is because there is found in the genus someone who will be gathered with his devil. Then We will bring them around Hell on their knees. “Jathi” is the plural of jath, from their saying jathu ala rakatihi yajtu jathwanu, and it is in the accusative case as a state: meaning kneeling on their knees because of what will befall them of the horror of the situation and the terror of the reckoning, or because kneeling on the knees is the case of the people of the situation as in His saying, the Most High, And you will see every nation kneeling, and it was said that what is meant by His saying jathi is groups, and its origin is the plural of jathwa, and jathwa is a group of dirt or stones. Tarafa said: I see two bodies of dirt with deaf sheets of tin on them.
19:69: 69- Then We will surely extract from every sect The Shiites are the group that followed a religion, and Al-Zamakhshari specified that and said: It is the group that became widespread: that is, followed a misguided person from among the misguided people. God the Most High said: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects. The meaning of Which of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful is whoever disobeyed God and was most rebellious, then He will extract from every group of the groups of misguidance and corruption the most rebellious and rebellious of them, and when they gather, He will throw them into Hell. Al-'ati here is a source like 'atu, which is rebellion in disobedience. It was said that the meaning is: We will surely extract from the people of every religion their leaders and chiefs in evil. The reciters agreed to read Ayyum with the dammah except for Harun Al-Ghazi, who read it with the fathah. Al-Zajjaj said: There are three opinions regarding raising Ayyum: The first is the opinion of Al-Khalil bin Ahmad that it is raised based on the narration. Meaning: Then we will remove from every sect those who are asked, Which of them is the most severe? Al-Khalil recited the following words of the poet about this: I refused the girl's house and I refused, there is no blame and no one is deprived Any, so I refused, as if it were said to him, There is no harm nor is there any deprivation. An-Nahhas said: I saw Abu Ishaq, meaning Az-Zajjaj, choosing this statement and approving of it. The second statement is the statement of Yunus 10:That we will surely remove is like the verbs that are cancelled and suspended, so this verb, according to him, is suspended from the work in any, and Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and others specified the suspension with the verbs of doubt and the like, which have not been proven to occur. The third statement is the statement of Sibawayh, that ayyum here is built on the damma, because it differed from its sisters in deletion, and Sibawayh made a mistake in this statement by the majority of grammarians, so much so that Az-Zajjaj said: It did not become clear to me that Sibawayh made a mistake in his book except in two places, this is one of them, and the grammarians have a long discussion about the parsing of ayyum in this place.
19:70: 70- Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of it, burned. It is said, He burned, like something passed, passes, and Al-Jawhari said: It is said, I burned a man with fire, if you put him in the fire and made him burn in it. If you throw him as if you want to burn him, you say, I burned him, with the alif, and I prayed him, and you pray him. From this, and he burns in a blazing fire. And whoever lightens it, it is from their saying, So-and-so burned in the fire, with the kasra, he burns, burned. God Almighty said, Those who are most deserving of it, burned. Al-Ajjaj said: By God, if it weren't for the fire, you wouldn't be able to reach it The meaning of the verse: Those who are most rebellious against the Most Merciful are more deserving of its punishment or their punishment is more deserving of the Fire.
19:71: 71- And there is not one of you but will pass over it The address is to the people without turning away, or to the person mentioned, so it would be turning away: meaning there is not one of you but will pass over it: meaning he will reach it. People have differed about this arrival. It was said that arrival is entering and that it will be cool and safe for the believers as it was for Abraham. A group said: Arrival is passing over the bridge. It was said that arrival is not entering, but rather it is as one says: I arrived in Basra but I did not enter it. Many scholars have refrained from investigating this arrival and taking it at face value because of the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. They said: So he who God has guaranteed to remove from it will not enter the Fire. What indicates that arrival does not entail entering is the Almighty’s saying: And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, for what is meant is that he looked over it, not that he entered it. This is the saying of Zuhair. When they reached the water, the doves were blue, and they put down the sticks of the present camp. It is not hidden that the statement that the arrival is passing over the Sirat, or the arrival at Hell while it is still in it, combines the evidence from the Book and the Sunnah, so this verse should be interpreted in this way, because the combination has been achieved by interpreting the arrival as entering the Fire while the believer who enters is kept away from its punishment, or by interpreting it as passing over the bridge erected over it, which is the Sirat it was upon your Lord an inevitability decreed meaning their arrival mentioned was an inevitable matter that the Almighty had decreed that it must inevitably occur, and the Mu’tazila used this verse as evidence that punishment is obligatory upon God, and according to the Ash’aris this is similar to the obligatory in terms of the impossibility of the opposite approaching it.
19:72: 72- Then We will save those who feared meaning they feared what necessitates Hellfire, which is disbelief in God and His disobedience, and abandoning what He has legislated and made obligatory to act upon. Asim al-Jahdari and Muawiyah ibn Qurra read nanji with a light pronunciation of anja, and Hamid, Yaqub, and al-Kisa'i read it the same way, and the rest read it with a shaddah, and Ibn Abi Laila read wa nadhir with a fathah on the tha' from then, and what is meant by the wrongdoers is those who wronged themselves by doing what necessitates Hellfire, or wronged others by injustice to the soul, money, or honor, and al-jathi is the plural of jathi, and the explanation and parsing of al-jathi has been presented shortly. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel, What prevents you from visiting us more often than you do? Then the verse was revealed, And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord until the end of the verse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim added, and that was the answer given to Muhammad. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked, ‘Which place is most beloved to God and which is most hated to God?’ He said, ‘I do not know until I ask.’ Then Gabriel descended, and he had been slow to come to him. He said, ‘You have been so slow to come to me that I thought that my Lord was angry with me.’ He said, ‘We do not descend except by the command of your Lord.’” And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: “Gabriel was slow to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for forty days, then he came down. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘You did not come down until I longed for you.’ Gabriel said to him: ‘I was more eager to come to you, but I am commanded.’ So God revealed to Gabriel to say to him: ‘We do not descend except by the command of your Lord.’” And this is a mursal verse. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The messengers were slow to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then Gabriel came to him and said to him: ‘What kept you from me?’ He said: ‘How can we come to you when you do not cut your nails, clean your wombs, trim your moustaches, or use siwaks?’ And he recited: ‘We do not descend except by the command of your Lord.’” And this is also a mursal verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: To Him belongs what is before us, he said: of the affairs of the Hereafter. And what is behind us, he said: of the affairs of this world. And what is between that, he said: what is between this world and the Hereafter. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, And what is between that, he said: What is between the two blasts. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah. Al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Tabarani, al-Bayhaqi, and al-Hakim narrated something similar on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who traced the hadith back to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: Whatever God has permitted in His Book is permissible, whatever He has forbidden is forbidden, and whatever He has remained silent about is a blessing, so accept God’s blessing, for God does not forget anything. Then he recited, And your Lord is not forgetful. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Jabir. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Do you know of any other like Him? He said: Do you know of any likeness or similarity for the Lord? Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim narrated something similar on the authority of al-Bukhari, Do you know of any other like Him? He said: No one is called the Most Gracious except Him. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: O Muhammad, do you know of a son for your God? Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, And man will say, he said: Al-Aas bin Wa’il. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, kneeling, he said: sitting, and regarding his statement, obstinately, he said: disobedient. Ibn Jarir narrated from him regarding his statement, obstinately, he said: disobedient. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatada regarding his statement, Then We will surely extract, he said: We will extract from the people of every religion their leaders and chiefs in evil. Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba’th from Ibn Mas’ud, he said: We will gather the first upon the last until, when the number is complete, He will stir them all up, then He began with the greatest, then the greatest in crime, then He recited, By your Lord, We will surely gather them, until His statement, obstinately. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of it, burning, he said: He says that they are most deserving of eternal damnation in Hell. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Sumayyah who said: We differed about the arrivals. Some of us said that no believer will enter it, and some of us said that they will all enter it. Then We will save those who feared God. So I met Jabir ibn Abdullah and mentioned it to him. He said, pointing his finger to his ears, “I am silent if I had not heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘No righteous or wicked person will remain but will enter it. It will be cool and safe for the believer as it was for Abraham, until the Fire makes a roaring sound from its coldness. “Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.”’” And Abd al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Hannad, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Nafi’ bin al-Azraq argued with Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas said: Walking means entering. Nafi’ said: No. Ibn Abbas recited: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. You will be entering it.” And he said: Have they been entered or not? And he recited: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them into the Fire. Have they been entered or not? As for you and I, we will enter it, so see if we get out of it or not.” Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding the statement: And there is not one of you but will pass over it. He said: And there is not one of you but will enter it. Hannad and al-Tabarani narrated on his authority regarding the verse: And they will be entered by the path. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, al-Bayhaqi, Ibn al-Anbari and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement: There is none among you but will pass over it, that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “All people will pass over to the Fire, then they will depart from it because of their deeds. The first of them will be like the flash of lightning, then like the wind, then like the rush of a horse, then like a rider on his saddle, then like tightening his saddle, then like walking.” Something similar to this was narrated from the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud through various chains of transmission. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire. Hafsah said: Didn’t God say: There is none among you but will pass over it? She said: Didn’t you hear Him say: Then We will save those who feared God. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If three of a Muslim’s children die, he will enter the Fire, except by fulfilling the oath. Then Sufyan recited: There is none among you but will pass over it. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari in his history, Abu Ya’la, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Anas on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever guards behind the Muslims in the cause of God voluntarily, without being seized by a ruler, will not see the Fire with his own eyes, except by way of an oath, for God says: ‘There is not one of you but will pass over it.’” There are many hadiths explaining this verse. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: an inevitability decreed, he said: a decree from God. Al-Khatib narrated in Tali al-Takhlis on the authority of Ikrimah: an inevitability decreed, he said: an obligatory oath. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees, he said: remaining therein.
19:73: The pronoun in His statement 73- upon them refers to the infidels who were previously mentioned in His statement: When I die, will I then be brought forth alive? That is, when the Qur'an is recited to them, they will make excuses for the world and say: If you were on the truth and we were on falsehood, your situation in the world would be better than our situation. It is not the other way around, because it is not appropriate for the Wise One to humiliate His friends and honor His enemies. The meaning of the clear proofs is the ones whose meanings are not ambiguous. It was said that they are the apparent signs of the miracle, and it was said that they are arguments and proofs, but the first is more appropriate. This is a confirmed case because the verses of God are only clear, and the apparent was placed in place of the implicit in His statement: Those who disbelieved said to indicate that their disbelief is the reason for this statement coming from them. It was said that what is meant by those who disbelieved here are the rebellious and persistent ones among them, and the meaning of said to those who believed is they said for their sake. It was said that this lam is the lam of notification as in His statement: And their prophet said to them meaning they addressed them with that and conveyed the statement to them Which of the two parties is better in position? What is meant by the two parties are the believers and the disbelievers, as if they said, Is our group better or your group? Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, and Shibl ibn Abbad read maqam with a damma on the meem, which is the place of residence. It is permissible for it to be a source meaning residence. The rest read it with a fatha, meaning a home and a dwelling. It was said that the place is the place where great matters are held, and the meaning is: Which of the two parties is greater in status and has more supporters and helpers? The assembly and the club are the people’s council and their gathering, and from this is His statement, the Most High: “You come in Your club is the evil one. He called him: he sat in the club, and from it comes the word “Dar al-Nadwa”, because the polytheists used to consult in it about their affairs. From it also comes the saying of the poet: I call him Al Waleed and Jaafar
19:74: 74- And how many a generation have We destroyed before them The generation is the nation and the group who were better in furnishings and appearance Furnishings are all wealth: camels, sheep, cows, slaves and goods, and it was said that it is the furnishings of the house specifically, and it was said that it is the new furniture, and it was said that it is the clothing specifically. The readings differed in warthiya, so the people of Medina and Ibn Dhakwan read wariya with a double ya, and there are two views on that: One of them is that it is from ra'iya then the hamza was lightened and a ya was replaced with the ya and the ya was assimilated into the ya, and the meaning according to this reading: they are better in appearance and this is the opinion of the majority of commentators, and a good appearance is from the aspect of good clothing, or good bodies and their softness, or a combination of both. The people of Kufa and Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read wariya with a hamza, and Warsh narrated it from Nafi' and Hisham from Ibn Amir, and its meaning is the same as the first reading. Al-Jawhari said: Whoever hamzat it, he made it from the view of the verb I saw, which is what the eye saw of a good condition and apparent clothing. Abu Ubaidah recited for Muhammad bin Numayr Al-Thaqafi: The caravans missed you when they appeared with their beautiful furniture. And whoever does not pronounce the hamza: it is either from lightening the hamza, or from rawayt alwanuhum aw jalooduhum riyaan: meaning it became full and beautiful. Al-Zajjaj mentioned the meaning of this as Al-Wahidi narrated it from him. Yaqub narrated that Talha bin Masraf read with one light yaa, so it was said that this reading is a mistake, and some grammarians explained it by saying that its origin was the hamza, then it was changed to a yaa, then one of the two yaa was deleted. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he read with a zay instead of a raa, and the same was narrated from Ubay bin Kaab, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-A’sam Al-Makki, and Al-Yazidi. Al-Zay is the appearance and the beauty. It was said that it is possible that it is from zawayt: meaning I gathered, so its origin is zawayan, then the waw was changed to a yaa, and Al-Zay is collected beauties.
19:75: 75- "Say: Whoever is in error" God the Almighty and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded to respond to those who boast about their worldly fortunes: that is, whoever is settled in error, The Most Merciful will extend to him a respite. This is even though it is in the form of a command, and what is meant by it is good, and it was only issued in the form of a command to clarify the respite from Him the Almighty for the sinners, and that this will inevitably happen so that the excuses of the people of error will be cut off, and it will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection, Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember? Or to lure them in, as God the Almighty says, We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin. It was said that what is meant by the verse is a supplication with extension and relief. Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is that God made the punishment for his misguidance to be that He should leave him and extend it, because the wording of the command confirms the meaning of the report, as if the speaker is saying I will do that and command myself with it, until when they see what they are promised, meaning those who were extended in misguidance. And the group pronoun came in consideration of the meaning of who, just as his saying was in misguidance, so let him extend it is considered in its wording, and this is the limit of the extension, not for the saying of the boasters, since there is no extension in it, Either the punishment or the Hour. This is a detail of his saying what they are promised: meaning what you are promised is one of two things, either the punishment in this world by killing and captivity, or the Day of Resurrection and what will befall them then of the punishment in the Hereafter. Then they will know who is worse in position and weaker in soldiers. This is the answer to the condition, and it is an answer to the boasters: meaning those who say: Which of the two parties is better in position, if they see what they are promised of worldly punishment at the hands of the believers, or the Hereafter, then they will know at that time who is worse in position, not better in position, and weaker in soldiers, not stronger or stronger. Better than the group of believers. It is not meant that the boasters have weak soldiers there, but rather they have no soldiers at all, as in the Almighty’s saying: And he had no company to aid him other than God, nor was he victorious.
19:76: Then when the Almighty informed about the state of the people of misguidance, He wanted to clarify the state of the people of guidance, so He said: 76- And God increases those who are guided in guidance. This is because some guidance leads to some other guidance, and good calls to good. It was said that what is meant by increase is the worship of the believers, and the waw in and increases is for resumption, and the sentence is resumed to clarify the state of the guided. Say the waw is for conjunction with let him be extended, and it was said that it is for conjunction with the sentence of those who were in misguidance. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that God makes the reward of the believers to increase their certainty, just as He made the reward of the disbelievers to prolong their misguidance. And the lasting good deeds are better in the sight of your Lord as reward. These are the acts of obedience that lead to eternal happiness. The meaning of them being better in the sight of God as reward is that they are more beneficial in return than the worldly blessings that the disbelievers enjoy. And better in return. Here, return is a source like return. The meaning is and better in return for the reward for its doer, not like the deeds of the disbelievers in which they lost. Return is the reference, the consequence, and the favor to mock them, to cut short the fact that the deeds of the disbelievers have no good at all.
19:77: Then the Almighty followed up the statement of those boasters with another similar one by way of astonishment, saying: 77- Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs? That is, tell me the story of this disbeliever and mention his speech after the speech of those people. They used have you seen in the sense of informed because seeing something is one of the reasons for the authenticity of the report about it, and the signs include every sign, including the sign of resurrection. The fa is for connecting to an implied thing indicated by the context: that is, you looked and saw. The lam in I will be given wealth and children is the one that introduces the oath, as if he said: By God, I will be given wealth and children in the Hereafter: that is, look at the state of this disbeliever and be amazed at his speech and his deification of God, along with his disbelief in Him and his denial of His signs.
19:78: Then the Almighty answered the statement of this disbeliever with what repels and invalidates it, saying 78- I have knowledge of the unseen meaning I know what is hidden from him so that he knows that he is in Paradise or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful about that, for knowledge cannot be attained except by one of these two methods. It was said that the meaning is: Look in the Preserved Tablet? Or have I taken a covenant with the Most Merciful. It was said that the meaning is: Or have I taken a covenant with the Most Merciful? Or have I said there is no god but God, so have mercy on him with it? It was said that the meaning is: Or has he presented a righteous deed so he hopes for it? And I have looked at it is taken from their saying: He looked at the mountain, so he climbed to its top. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Yahya bin Waththab, and Al-A'mash read and a child with a damma on the waw, and the rest read it with a fatha on it. It was said that they are two languages with the same meaning. It is said that child and child are said just as non-existence and non-existence are said. Al-Harith bin Halzah said: I have seen people who have had wealth and children. Another said: I wish so-and-so was in his mother's womb, and I wish so-and-so was the son of a donkey It was said that the word child is with the damma for the plural and with the fatha for the singular. The majority of scholars have said that this infidel meant by his saying: I will be given wealth and children that he will be given that in this world. A group said: In Paradise. It was said that the meaning is: If I remained on the religion of my fathers, I will be given that. It was said that the meaning is: If I were on falsehood, I would not have been given wealth and children.
19:79: 79- No! We will record what he says. No! is a letter of deterrence and warning: meaning, the matter is not as this disbeliever said, that he will be given wealth and children. We will record what he says: meaning, We will record what he says, so We will punish him in the Hereafter, or We will reveal what he says, or We will take revenge on him with the revenge of one whose sin was recorded. And We will extend for him from the punishment an extension. Meaning, We will increase his punishment on top of his punishment in place of what he claims for himself of being provided with wealth and children, or We will extend for him from the punishment what he deserves, which is the punishment of one who combines disbelief and mockery.
19:80: And We shall inherit from him what he says meaning, We cause him to die, so We shall inherit from him the wealth and children that he says he will be given. The meaning is: the name of what he says and its verification. It was also said that the meaning is: We shall deprive him of what he desires and give him something else. And he will come to Us alone meaning, on the Day of Resurrection, he will have neither wealth nor children, rather, We will take that away from him, so how can he hope that We will give him what he desires? It was also said that what is meant by what he says is the statement itself, not its name. The meaning is: He will only say this statement as long as he is alive, so if We cause him to die, We will prevent him from saying it, and he will come to Us rejecting it and alone from it. The first is more appropriate. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: Which of the two parties is better in position? He said: Quraysh, we say it for them and for the companions of Muhammad. Al-Faryabi, Saeed Ibn Mansur, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Better in position, he said: Mansions. And better in company, he said: As-semblies. And regarding his statement: Best in furnishings, he said: Furniture and wealth. And in view, he said: The view. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: “Say: Whoever is in error, then let the Most Merciful extend for him a term,” so let God leave him in his transgression. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Habib Ibn Abi Thabit who said in the wording of Abi: Say: Whoever is in error, then God increases his error. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated in his statement, Have you seen the one who disbelieved? from the hadith of Khabbab bin Al-Arat, who said: I was a blacksmith, and Al-Aas bin Wa’il owed me a debt. I came to him to collect it, but he said: No, by God, I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad. So I said: By God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are resurrected. He said: I died and was resurrected, and you came to me with wealth and children, so I will give you. So God revealed this verse about him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in his statement, Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful? He said: There is no god but God, he hopes for it. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And We inherit from him what he says, he said: his wealth and his children.
19:81: God the Almighty narrated the situation of these infidels who wished for what they did not deserve, and swore to God the Almighty that they had taken gods besides God in order to be strengthened by that. Al-Harawi said: The meaning of 81- so that they may be a source of strength for them is to be their helpers. Al-Farra' said: Its meaning is so that they may be intercessors for them in the Hereafter. It was also said that its meaning is: so that they may be strengthened by them from the punishment of God and protect themselves by them.
19:82: 82- No, they will disbelieve in their worship meaning that the matter is not as they thought and imagined, and the pronoun in the verb either refers to the gods: meaning these idols will deny the disbelievers' worship of them on the day when God, the Most High, will speak, because when they worshipped them they were inanimate objects that did not understand that, or to the polytheists: meaning the polytheists will deny that they worshipped idols, and the first aspect is indicated by the Almighty's statement: They did not worship us and His statement: So throw to them the word, 'Indeed, you are liars' and the second aspect is indicated by the Almighty's statement: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists and Ibn Abi Nahik read No with the tanween, and it was narrated from him with the damma and fatha of the kaf, so with the damma it means all and its accusative is with an implied verb as if he said: They will disbelieve, no, they will disbelieve in their worshippers, and with the fatha it is a source for a deleted verb, the meaning of which is: All of this is the opinion, no, and the reading of the majority is correct, and it is a letter of deterrence and restraint And they will be against them meaning that these gods that they thought were their glory will be against them: that is, against glory, and the opposite of glory is humiliation. This is according to the first aspect. As for the second aspect, the polytheists will be against the gods and enemies who will disbelieve in them after they used to love them and believe in them.
19:83: 83- Have you not seen that We send the devils upon the disbelievers? Al-Zajjaj mentioned two aspects of the meaning of this: One of them is that its meaning is that we left the disbelievers to the devils, so we did not protect them from them or grant them refuge, unlike the believers about whom it was said, Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority. The second aspect is that they were sent upon them and decreed for them because of their disbelief. He said, And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious - We appoint for him a devil. So the meaning of sending here is domination, and from that is the saying of the Most High to Satan, And incite whomever you can among them with your voice. The second aspect is supported by the entire verse, which is, Incite them with incitement. For incitement, shaking, and incitement mean moving, agitating, and disturbing, so God, the Most High, informed us that the devils move the disbelievers, incite them, and mislead them, and that is their incitement upon them. It was said that the meaning of incitement is haste, and it is close to what we mentioned because haste is moving, agitating, inciting, and disturbing. The context of this verse is to astonish the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at their condition and to alert him that all of that is due to the misguidance and seduction of the devils. The sentence: It causes them distress in the accusative case as a state, or it is resumed as a question indicated by the situation, as if it was said: What do the devils do to them?
19:84: 84- So do not be impatient over them by asking God to destroy them because of their determination to disbelieve, their stubbornness towards the truth, and their rebellion against the call of God Almighty. Then God Almighty explained this prohibition by saying: We only count for them a [definite] count meaning We count the days, nights, months, and years of their lives until the end of their appointed times. It was said that We count their breaths, their steps, their moments, and the hours. Qatrub said: We count their deeds. It was said that the meaning is: Do not be impatient over them, for We only delay them so that they may increase in sin.
19:85: Then when He, the Most High, decided on the matter of the gathering and answered the doubts of those who denied it, He wanted to explain the state of those who are accountable at that time, so He said: 85- The Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation. The circumstance is accusative with an implied verb: that is, remember, O Muhammad, the Day of Gathering. It was said that it is accusative with the verb that follows it. The meaning of gathering them to the Most Merciful: gathering them to His Paradise and the abode of His honor, like His saying: Indeed, I am going to my Lord. And the delegation is the plural of a delegate, like the rider is the plural of a rider, and companions are the plural of a companion. It is said that he delegation is a delegation if he goes to a king or an important matter. This is what Al-Jawhari said.
19:86: 86- And We will drive the criminals to Hell in droves. The drive is the urging to walk, and the thirsty ones were said by Al-Akhfash and others. Al-Farra' and Ibn Al-A'rabi said: They are the pedestrians. Al-Azhari said: They are the thirsty pedestrians like camels that come to water. It was said: To go to water, like you say: I came to you to honor you, meaning to honor you. It was said: Individually. It was said: There is no contradiction between these sayings, as they are driven on thirsty walks, individually. The origin of the word ward is a group that comes to water, whether birds, camels, people, or other than that. The water that is brought is the water that is brought.
19:87: And the sentence 87- They do not possess intercession. is resumed to explain some of the matters that will occur on that Day, and the pronoun in they possess refers to the two groups, and it was said to the righteous specifically, and it was said to the criminals specifically, and the first is more appropriate. The meaning of they do not possess intercession is that they do not possess the right to intercede for others, and it was said that no one else possesses the right to intercede for them, and the first is more appropriate. Except for one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful. This exception is connected in the first way: that is, the two mentioned groups do not possess the right to intercede except for one who prepares for that by which he becomes one of the intercessors for others by being a believer and righteous, so this is the meaning of taking a covenant with God. It was said that the meaning of taking a covenant is that God commanded him to do so, like their saying: The prince made a covenant with so-and-so if he commanded him to do so. It was said that the meaning of taking a covenant is the testimony that there is no god but God, and other things were said. And in the connection in this exception, the position of min in min takhadh is nominative as a substitute, or accusative as per the original exception. As for the second aspect, the exception is disconnected because the meaning is: The criminals do not have the right to intercede except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, and they are the Muslims. It was said that it is connected in this aspect as well, and the meaning is: The criminals do not have the right to intercede except for those among them who are Muslims.
19:88: 88- And they said, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.' Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read son with a damma on the waw and a sukoon on the lam. The rest read in the four places mentioned in this surah with a fatha on the waw and the lam. We have already presented the difference between the two readings. The sentence is a new sentence to explain the statement of the Jews and Christians and those among the Arabs who claim that the angels are daughters of God.
19:89: And in His saying: 89- You have certainly done something terrible is a shift from the third person to the second person, and in it is a response to this heinous statement, and the id as Al-Jawhari said: the disaster and the terrible matter, and so is the addah, and the plural of addah is addad, it is said the disaster afflicted someone, it tu'adhu adaa with the fatha. Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami read addan with the fatha of the hamza, and the majority read it with the kasra, and Ibn Abbas and Abu Al-Aaliyah read addan like madan, and it is taken from heaviness, it is said the pregnancy made it heavy: if it weighed it down. Al-Wahidi said You have certainly done something terrible meaning great according to everyone, and the meaning of the verse: you said a great statement. It was said that id is astonishment, and idah is severity, and the meanings are close and the structure revolves around severity and heaviness.
19:90: 90- The heavens almost burst from it. Nafi', Al-Kisa'i, Hafs, and Yahya bin Waththab read yakad with a ta', and the rest read it with a ta'. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Hafs read yatafitarna with a ta', and Hamza, Ibn Amir, Abu Omar, Abu Bakr, and Al-Mufaddal read yatafitarna with a ta' from infitar. Abu Ubaid chose this reading because of his saying: When the sky is split and his saying The sky is split by it. Ibn Mas'ud read yatasha'an and infitar and tafitar are cracking. And the earth is split meaning the earth is almost split. The verb was repeated for emphasis because tatafitarna and tatashaq have the same meaning. And the mountains fall meaning they fall and collapse. The accusative of hada is because it is a source of emphasis because falling is in its meaning, or it is a source for an implied verb: meaning and it collapses, or in the state, meaning it is demolished, or as an object for it: meaning because it collapses. Al-Harawi said: It is said that the matter destroyed me and destroyed my pillar: meaning it broke me and affected me. Al-Jawhari said: The building destroyed, he broke it and weakened it, and the calamity destroyed it or weakened its pillar, and the mountain collapsed: meaning it was broken, and the collapse is the sound of a wall falling, as Ibn al-A’rabi said.
19:91: And the location of 91- "that they attributed to the Most Gracious a son" is the accusative instead of the pronoun in it. Al-Farra' said: In the accusative case meaning because they attributed. Al-Kisa'i said: It is in the genitive case with the preposition being assumed, and it was said that it is in the nominative case as the subject of guidance. And the supplication means naming: that is, they named the Most Gracious a son, or in the sense of attribution, that is, they attributed a son to Him.
19:92: 92- And it is not befitting for the Most Gracious to take a son meaning it is not suitable for Him nor is it appropriate for Him to do so, because a son requires both genus and occurrence. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state: meaning they said the Most Gracious has taken a son, or that they claimed that the Most Gracious had a son, and the state is that it is not befitting for Him, glory be to Him.
19:93: 93- Everyone in the heavens and the earth meaning, there is no one in the heavens and the earth except that he will come to God on the Day of Resurrection, acknowledging servitude, submissive and humiliated, as He said: And all will come to Him in humiliation meaning, humiliated. The meaning is: that all of creation are His servants, so how could one of them be His son? It was read coming according to the original.
19:94: 94- He has counted them meaning He has confined them and knows their number and counted them completely meaning He counted their persons after He confined them, so that not one of them is hidden from Him.
19:95: And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone. That is, each one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone, with no helper or wealth with him, as God Almighty said: The Day when neither wealth nor children will be of any benefit. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they will be against them he said: helpers. Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on his authority: Anti he said: regret. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: Taw’uzhum az’an means You lead them astray. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: Taw’uzhum az’an he said: You incite the polytheists against Muhammad and his companions. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse: You will incite them to disobey God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A delegation he said: riders. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: A delegation he said: on camels. In the two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three ways: those who desire and those who fear, two on a camel, three on a camel, four on a camel, and ten on a camel. The rest of them will be gathered in the Fire, resting with them where they said and spending the night with them where they spent the night.” There are many hadiths on this subject. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Wardan, he said: Thirsty. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Except for one who has made a covenant with the Most Merciful, he said: Testifying that there is no god but God, and disavowing any power or strength, and hoping for nothing but God. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: Whoever dies without associating anything with God will enter Paradise. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he recited, Except for he who has made a covenant with the Most Merciful. He said, “God will say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Whoever has made a covenant with Me, let him stand.’ No one will stand except he who said this in this world. Say, ‘O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, I entrust You in this worldly life that if You leave me to my own deeds, You will bring me closer to evil and distance me from good. I trust only in Your mercy, so make it a covenant with You that You will fulfill until the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail to fulfill Your promise.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, “Whoever brings joy to a believer has made me happy, and whoever makes me happy has made a covenant with the Most Merciful. And whoever makes a covenant with the Most Merciful, the Fire will not touch him, for God does not fail to fulfill His promise.” Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever comes to us with the five daily prayers on the Day of Resurrection, having maintained their ablution, their times, their bowing and prostration, without missing anything from them, will have a covenant with God that He will not punish him. Whoever comes having missed anything from them, will have no covenant with God. If He wills, He will have mercy on him, and if He wills, He will punish him.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, You have certainly done a terrible thing, he said: A tremendous statement. And regarding his statement, The heavens almost, he said: Polytheism has emptied the heavens, the earth, the mountains and all of creation except the two heavy things, and they almost disappeared because of the greatness of God, the Most High. Just as the good deeds of the polytheist are of no use with polytheism, so too one hopes that God will forgive the sins of the monotheists. And regarding his statement, And the mountains will collapse in ruins, he said: Destruction. Ibn Al-Mubarak, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated on the authority of Awn on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: The mountain calls out to the mountain by name, ‘O so-and-so, did anyone who mentioned God pass by you today? ’ So if he says yes, he is happy. Awn said: Do they hear falsehood when it is said and do not hear good? They listen to good. And he recited: “And they say, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son. ’” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
19:96: The Almighty mentioned some of the conditions of the believers that He has made special for them after mentioning the ugliness of the disbelievers, saying: 96- Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection meaning love in the hearts of His servants that He will appoint for them without them seeking it through the means that necessitate that, just as He casts terror into the hearts of their enemies. The seen in will be appointed is to indicate that this did not exist before and that it was appointed after the revelation of the verse. And wuddan was read with a kasra on the waw, and the majority of the seven and others with a damma.
19:97: Then the Almighty mentioned the glorification of the Qur’an, especially this Surah, because it includes monotheism and prophethood, and explains the state of the obstinate, saying: 97- Then We have only made it easy for your tongue meaning We have made the Qur’an easy by sending it down in your language, and We have explained it and made it easy. The ba means upon, and the fa is to explain a statement that the system is drawn to, as if it was said: convey this message or give good report of it or warn. Then We have only made it easy the verse. Then He explained what He mentioned about making it easy, saying: That you may give good tidings therewith to the righteous meaning those who are clothed in piety and characterized by it. And that you may warn therewith a people who are obstinate. Al-Lud is the plural of al-ald, which means the one who is very quarrelsome, and from this is the Almighty’s saying: The most stubborn of opponents. The poet said: I spend the night in seclusion from worries, as if I were arguing with people who are stubborn in their arguments. Abu Ubaidah said: The stubborn is the one who does not accept the truth and claims falsehood. It was said that the stubborn is the deaf, and it was said that he is the oppressor.
19:98: 98- And how many generations before them have We destroyed meaning a nation and a group of people. In this there is a promise to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the destruction of the disbelievers and a threat to them. Do you sense any of them? This sentence confirms the content of what preceded it: meaning do you sense any of them or see them or hear their thump? The thump is a low sound, and from it the thump of the spear is when its tip is hidden in the ground. Tarafa said: And I happened to hear the apprehension of a secret, of a hidden focus, or of a refuting voice. And Dhu al-Rummah said: If he senses a desolate place, he will sneak in the sound of what he hears as a lie. Meaning: He lied in his listening, but he is honest in his listening, and the clever one is the one who is sneaky, and the hidden voice is the one who is not heard. Al-Yazidi and Abu Ubaidah said: The focus is what is not understood from a sound or movement. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf that when he migrated to Madinah, he found himself separated from his companions in Makkah, including Shaibah ibn Rabi’ah, Utbah ibn Rabi’ah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf, so God revealed, Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds 1:13. Ibn Kathir said: This is a mistake, because the surah is Makkan in its entirety and no part of it was revealed after the migration, and its chain of transmission is not authentic. At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib, Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love 1:13. He said: Love in the hearts of the believers. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: “Say: O God, make for me a covenant with You, and make for me love with You, and place for me in the hearts of the believers affection”, so God revealed the verse about Ali. Abd al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Wod 1:13. He said: Love among people in this world. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali who said: “I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about His statement: ‘The Most Gracious will bestow love upon them’. What is it? He said: ‘The sincere love in the hearts of the believers.’” It is proven in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When God loves a servant, He calls Gabriel, ‘I love so-and-so, so love him.’ So he calls out in the heavens, then he sends down love for him among the people of the earth. This is what God says: ‘Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - the Most Gracious will bestow love upon them.’ And when God hates a servant, He calls Gabriel, ‘I hate so-and-so.’ So he calls out among the people of the heavens, then he sends down hatred for him on the earth.” There are many hadiths and reports on this subject. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And you warn thereby a hostile people, he said: Immoral. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Deaf. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement, Do you sense any of them? He said: Do you see any of them? Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, A sound. He said: A voice.
20:1: It is Meccan and has one hundred and thirty-five verses. Al-Qurtubi said: It was revealed in Mecca according to everyone. An-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Surah Ta-Ha was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Ad-Darimi and Ibn Khuzaymah narrated in At-Tawhid, Al-Uqayli in Ad-Du'afa, At-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Ibn 'Adi, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu'ab on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: "God, the Blessed and Exalted, recited Ta-Ha and Ya-Seen two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. When the angels heard the Qur'an, they said: Blessed is the nation upon which this is revealed, and blessed are the hearts that bear this, and blessed are the tongues that speak this." Ibn Khuzaymah said after narrating it: It is a strange hadith, and it contains something strange, and Ibrahim ibn Muhajir and his sheikh were criticized, meaning Ibrahim ibn Muhajir ibn Samar and his sheikh 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Dhakwan, and they are among the men in its chain of transmission. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given the surah in which cattle were mentioned from the first mention, and I was given Surah Taha and the Ta-Sin from the tablets of Moses, and I was given the opening verses of the Qur’an and the ending verses of Surah Al-Baqarah from beneath the Throne, and I was given Al-Mufassal as a supererogatory recitation.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Every Qur’an is placed away from the people of Paradise, and they do not recite anything from it except Surah Taha and Yasin, for they will recite them in Paradise. Ad-Daraqutni narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who mentioned the story of Umar ibn al-Khattab with his sister and Khabbab and their recitation of Taha, and that was because of Umar’s conversion to Islam, and the story is well-known in the books of biography. His saying: 1- Ta Ha was read with an inclination of the ha and a fatha on the ta by Abu Amr and Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Abu Bakr, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Al-A’mash inclined them both. Abu Ja’far, Shaiba and Nafi’ read them between the two pronunciations, and Abu Ubaid chose this reading. The rest read with emphasis. Al-Tha’labi said: They are all correct and eloquent languages. Al-Nahhas said: There is no reason for inclination according to most Arabists for two reasons: The first is that there is neither a ya’ nor a kasra here for inclination to occur, and the second reason is that the ta’ is one of the obstacles to inclination. Scholars have differed on the meaning of this word. The first is that it is ambiguous and its intended meaning is not understood. The second is that it means O man in the language of Ukl and in the language of Uk. Al-Kalbi said: If you said to a man from Uk O man he would not respond until you said Ta-Ha. Ibn Jarir recited the following in this regard: I called Taha to fight, but he did not answer, so I was afraid that he would be a traitor. It is narrated as Mazayilan, and it was said that in the language of Ak it means my beloved. Qatrib said: It is also in the language of Tayy: meaning, O man, and this is what Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said. It was also said that it is also in the Syriac language, as narrated by Al-Mahdawi. Ibn Jarir narrated that it is also in the Nabataean language, and Al-Suddi and Saeed bin Hubain said the same. Al-Tha’labi narrated from Ikrimah that it is also in the language of Abyssinia, and he narrated it from Ikrimah, and there is no objection to this word being used for that meaning in all of those languages if the transmission is correct. The third opinion: It is one of the names of God, the Most High. The fourth opinion: It is the name of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The fifth opinion: It is the name of the Surah. The sixth opinion: It is separate letters, each of which indicates a meaning. Then they differed regarding these meanings indicated by these letters, with all of them being forced and arbitrary. The seventh opinion is that its meaning is: Blessed is he who is guided. The eighth opinion is that its meaning is: Ta’ al-Ard, O Muhammad. Ibn al-Anbari said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to endure the hardship of prayer until his feet were about to swell and he needed to rest, so he was told to tab al-ard meaning do not tire yourself out until you need to rest. Al-Qadi Iyad narrated in Ash-Shifa’ on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed, he would stand on one leg and raise the other, so God revealed Ta Ha meaning tab al-ard, O Muhammad. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he read Ta Ha with the weight of da’a which means to trample, and the original is ta’a but the hamza was changed to a ha. Al-Wahidi narrated on the authority of most of the commentators that this word means O man, meaning the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: This is the saying of Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Mujahid, Ibn Abbas in the narration of Ata’ and Al-Kalbi, except that some of them say: It is in the language of Abyssinian, Nabataean, and Syriac. Al-Kalbi says: It is in the language of ‘Ak. Ibn Al-Anbari said: The language of Quraysh agreed with that language in this meaning, because God, the Exalted, did not address His Prophet in a language other than Quraysh. If it is determined that it has this meaning in one of the languages of the Arabs, then the meaning is apparent and the indication is clear, outside of the openings of the surahs, which we have previously explained as being among the ambiguous in the opening of Surat Al-Baqarah. And likewise if it has this meaning in one of the languages of the Persians and the Arabs use it in their speech in that meaning like all the Persian words that the Arabs used and that are found in the Noble Book, then with that use it becomes part of the language of the Arabs.
20:2: And the sentence 2- We did not send down the Qur'an to you to make you miserable is a new sentence introduced to console the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the fatigue he was suffering from the polytheists. Misery comes in the meaning of exhaustion. Ibn Kaysan said: The root of misery in the language is to suffer and toil, and from this the poet said: The wise man suffers in bliss with his wisdom, but the ignorant man enjoys misery. Meaning: We did not send down the Qur’an to you to tire you out with your excessive grief over them and their disbelief, and your regret that they believe. It is like His, the Most High, saying: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief. An-Nahhas said: Some grammarians say: This lam in li-mashqa is the lam of negation, and some of them say it is the lam of denial. Ibn Kaysan said: It is the lam of khifd. This interpretation of the verse is according to the opinion of those who said that Ta-Ha is like all the openings of the surahs that were mentioned to enumerate the names of the letters. If it were made the name of the surah, then His saying: We did not send down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable would be a predicate of it, and it is in the position of the subject. As for the opinion of those who said: Its meaning is O man, or it means the command to tread the earth, then the sentence is a new sentence to divert him, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his exaggeration in worship.
20:3: And the accusative of 3- except a reminder as an object for We revealed like your saying: I did not hit you for discipline except out of compassion for you. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a substitute for to make you miserable: meaning We revealed it only as a reminder. Abu Ali Al-Farisi denied it on the grounds that the reminder is not miserable, he said: Rather, it is accusative as a source: meaning We revealed it so that you may be reminded by it, a reminder, or as an object for it: meaning We did not reveal the Qur'an to you so that you may be miserable by it, We revealed it only as a reminder.
20:4: And the accusative of 4- A revelation from Him who created the earth and the high heavens is on the source: meaning We sent it down, and it was said instead of his saying a reminder, and it was said that it is accusative for praise, and it was said that it is accusative with he fears: meaning he fears a revelation from God as a direct object, and it was said that it is accusative as a state by interpreting it as an active participle. Abu Haywah al-Shami read a revelation in the nominative case on the meaning of this is a revelation, and from Him who created is related to a revelation, or to an omitted word that is an attribute of it, and the specification of the creation of the earth and the heavens because they are the greatest of what the servants see of His creations, the Almighty, and the high: the plural of the high: meaning the elevated like the plural of the great and the small on the great and the small. The meaning of the verse is informing the servants about the perfection of His greatness, glory be to Him, and the greatness of His majesty.
20:5: And the elevation of 5- the Most Gracious as the predicate of a deleted subject as Al-Akhfash said, and it is permissible for it to be raised for praise or for the beginning. And it was read in the accusative, Al-Zajjaj said as a substitute for whom, and Al-Nahhas allowed it to be raised as a substitute for the implied in creation, and the phrase on the throne He rose is in the place of raising as the predicate of a deleted subject, or as the predicate of the Most Gracious according to those who made it a subject. Ahmad bin Yahya said: Tha'lab said: The rising is turning towards something, and so said Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra. And it was said that it is a metaphor for the king and the authority, and the research into the verification of this is long, and the research on it has been presented in Al-A'raf. And what Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ash'ari went to is that He, the Most High, is established on His throne without limit or how, and to this statement he was preceded by the majority of the righteous predecessors who narrate the attributes as they were mentioned without distortion or interpretation.
20:6: 6- To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth meaning that He is the Owner and Manager of everything and whatever is between them of the existents and whatever is under the soil soil in the language means moist soil: meaning whatever is under the soil of anything. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators say that He, glory be to Him, meant the soil that is under the rock on which the bull is under the earth, and no one knows what is under the soil except God, glory be to Him.
20:7: 7- And if you speak aloud, then He knows the secret and what is even more hidden. Speaking aloud means raising one's voice, and the secret is what a person tells another person and confides in him, and what is more hidden than the secret is what a person tells himself and crosses his mind. The meaning is: If you speak aloud in the remembrance of God and invoke Him, then know that He is independent of that, for He knows the secret and what is even more hidden than the secret, so you have no need to speak aloud. This is the meaning of the prohibition of speaking aloud, as in His, the Most High, saying: And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear. It was said that the secret is what a person keeps secret in himself, and what is even more hidden than that is what the son of Adam is doing and he does not know it.
