And today he who prevailed has succeeded, meaning he who overcame, it is said that he prevailed over him if he overcame him, and all of this is from what the magicians said to each other, and it was said from what Pharaoh said to them.
20:65: And sentence 65 - They said, ‘O Moses, either you throw down’ is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did they do after they said among themselves what they said? It was said: They said, ‘O Moses, either you throw’ and that with what is in its scope is in the accusative case with an implied verb: that is, choose your throwing first or our throwing. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, that is, the matter is your throwing, or our throwing. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, that is, the matter is your throwing, or our throwing. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, that is, the matter is your throwing, or our throwing. The object of throw is deleted, and the estimate is: either you throw what you throw first or we “will be the first to throw” what he throws, or the first to do the throwing. What is meant is throwing the sticks on the ground, and the magicians had sticks with them, and Moses had thrown his stick on the day he entered upon Pharaoh, so when the magicians wanted to oppose him, they said this to him.
20:66: F 66- Moses said to them Rather, throw he ordered them to throw first so that his miracle would be more apparent if they threw what they had with them and then he threw his staff so that it would swallow it, and to show his indifference to their magic Then behold, their ropes and their staffs in the speech there is an omission, and the meaning is: So throw, then behold, their ropes, and the fa is eloquent, and if is for surprise or circumstantial. Meaning: So they threw, and Moses was surprised at the time when their ropes and staffs seemed to run. Al-Hasan read their staffs with a damma on the ‘ayn, which is the language of Banu Tamim. The rest read it with a kasra, following the kasra of the sad. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Dhakwan, and Ruh from Ya’qub read it with a doubled tha’ because the staffs and ropes are feminine, and that is because they smeared them with mercury, and when the heat of the sun struck them, they trembled and shook. Nakhil was read with a noon on the basis that God, the Most High, is the one who gave the impression of that. Yakhil was read with a ya’ underneath, built for the agent on the basis that the imagined is the plot. It was said that the imagined is that it runs, for it is in the nominative case: meaning that its running appears to him. Al-Zajjaj mentioned its meaning. Al-Farra’ said: It is in the accusative case: meaning that it then deleted the ba’. Al-Zajjaj said: And whoever read it with a ta’, meaning the upper case, made an in the accusative case: meaning that it appears to him running. He said: It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case instead of the pronoun in Imagine, and it refers back to the ropes and sticks, and the substitute includes inclusion. It is said that it appeared to him if it appeared to him and he introduced the beast and the resemblance to it.
20:67: 67- "So Moses felt fear within himself" meaning he sensed, and it was said he found, and it was said he concealed, and it was said he feared, and that is because of what appears from human nature when seeing what is feared, and it was said he feared that the people would be tempted before he threw down his staff, and it was said that the reason for his fear was that their magic was of the same type as what he showed them in the staff, so he feared that his matter would be confused for the people and they would not believe.
20:68: So God Almighty removed the fear that had befallen him by giving him good report of His words: 68- “We said, ‘Do not fear. Indeed, you are the superior.’” That is, the one who is superior to them in victory and triumph, and the sentence is an explanation for the prohibition of fear.
20:69: 69- "And throw what is in your right hand means the stick, but he made it ambiguous for the sake of glorification and emphasis, and talqaf ma sana'u" was made jussive as a response to the command. It was read with a shaddah on the qaf, and the original is tatalaqafa, so one of the two ta's was deleted, and talqaf was read with a kasrah on the lam from laqafa if he swallowed it quickly, and talqaf was read with the nominative case on the assumption that it is ttalaqafa, and the meaning of "ma sana'u" is what they made of ropes and sticks. Al-Zajjaj said: The reading with the jussive case is a response to the command, and the nominative case is permissible in the sense of the state, as if he said: throw it, grabbing it, and the phrase "inma sana'u kayd sahir" is an explanation for his saying talqaf, and the nominative case of kayd is the predicate of inna, and this is the reading of the Kufians except for Asim. And these read "magic" with a kasrah on the seen and a sukoon on the ha', and the addition of kayd meaning magic in the broad sense without estimation, or by estimating the possessor of magic. The rest read the trick of a magician and the magician will not succeed wherever he goes, meaning the magician will not succeed wherever he goes and wherever he goes, and this is a complete explanation.
20:70: 70- "So the magicians fell down in prostration." That is, the magicians fell down in prostration to God Almighty, which they witnessed from Moses and the staff. The confirmation of this was mentioned in Surat Al-A'raf. "They said, 'We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.'" Aaron was mentioned before Moses in the narration of their speech, taking into account the breaks in the verses and taking care to match their beginnings. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, He will destroy you with a punishment, he said: He will destroy you. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd Ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah, He will destroy you, he said: He will uproot you. Abd Ibn Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, he said: He will slaughter you. Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali, And they will take away your best way, he said: They will turn people’s faces towards them. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: He says the best of you, and they are the Children of Israel. Abd Ibn Hamid and Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on his statement, It swallows up what they have made, what they fabricate, on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Moses threw it and it turned into a snake that ate their ropes and what they had made. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that the magicians of Pharaoh were nine hundred. They said to Pharaoh: If these two are magicians, then we will defeat them, for there is no magician greater than us. And if they are from the Lord of the Worlds, then we have no power over the Lord of the Worlds. So when it came to their affair that they fell down in prostration, God showed them in their prostration the stations to which they would return. Then they said: We will not prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us. And God is better and more lasting.
20:71: His statement: 71- "He said, 'You believed in him.'" It is said that he believed in him and he believed in him. From the first, his statement: "So Lot believed in him." From the second, his statement in al-A’raf 7:"You believed in him before I gave you permission." It was said that the verb here includes the meaning of following, and it was read as a question of reproach: that is, how did you believe in him without my permission for that? "Indeed, he is your greatest who taught you magic." That is, Moses is your greatest: that is, he is your most enchanted and the highest in rank in the art of magic, or your teacher and master as indicated by his statement: "who taught you magic." Al-Kisa'i said: When a boy in the Hijaz comes from his teacher, he says: I came from my greatest. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He is a great magician. Al-Wahidi said: In the language, the greatest is the leader, and that is why the teacher is called the greatest. By this statement, Pharaoh wanted to cast doubt on the people so that they would not believe. Otherwise, he would have known that they had not learned from Moses, nor was he their leader, nor was there any connection between them. Then I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides. That is, by God, I will do that to you. Cutting off the hands and feet on opposite sides means cutting off the right hand and the left foot. Min is for beginning. And I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. That is, on their trunks, as he said: Or do they have a ladder by which they listen? That is, on it. From this is the saying of Suwaid ibn Abi Kahl: They crucified Al-Abdi on the trunk of a palm tree, and no old man sneezed except on his trunk. Rather, he preferred the word fi to indicate that they were settled on it, like the content of the envelope is settled in the envelope. And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting. He meant that you will surely know whether I am more severe in punishment for you or Moses? The meaning of more lasting is more lasting. And he meant by his words this to mock Moses, because Moses was not subject to any kind of punishment. It is possible that he meant the punishment that Moses threatened them with if they did not believe. It was said that he meant by Moses the Lord of Moses, with the omission of the complement.
20:72: 72- "They said, 'We will not prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs'" meaning, we will not choose you over what Moses brought us of clear proofs from God Almighty, such as the hand and the staff. It was said that by clear proofs they meant what they saw in their prostration of the houses prepared for them in Paradise. "And He Who created us" is conjoined with what has come to us, meaning, we will not choose you over what Moses brought us of clear proofs and over He Who created us: meaning, He created us. It was said that it is an oath: meaning, by God Who created us, we will not prefer you, or we will not prefer you. These two aspects of the interpretation of the verse were mentioned by Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj. "Then decide what you decide is their answer to Pharaoh when he said to them, I will cut off" etc. The meaning is: So do what you will do, and rule as you rule. The estimate is: what you will do. "You only decide this worldly life" meaning, your authority over us and the effect of your command over us is only in this world and you have no way over us in what comes after it. So the demonstrative pronoun is in the accusative case on Circumstantial or on the object and ma is comprehensive, and Al-Farra’ permitted the nominative case on the condition that ma means which: meaning that what this worldly life decrees, your decree and rule are limited to that.
20:73: 73- Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins which we have committed in the past of disbelief and other things and what you forced us to do of magic is conjoined with our sins: meaning and forgive us what you forced us to do of magic in opposition to Moses. So what is in the accusative case as a direct object, and it was said that it is negative. An-Nahhas said: The first is more appropriate. It was said that it is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a subject and the predicate is understood: meaning what you forced us to do of magic is placed on us. And God is better and more lasting meaning better than you in reward and more lasting than you in punishment, and this is the answer to his statement: And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting.
20:74: 74- Whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live. The criminal is the one who commits disbelief and sins. The meaning of will neither die therein nor live is that he will neither die and rest nor live a life that benefits him. Al-Mubarrad said: He will neither die a comfortable death nor live an enjoyable life. He feels pain as the living feel pain and he reaches the state of death in a state of distress, except that he does not cease to feel pain therein. The Arabs say: So-and-so is neither alive nor dead if he does not benefit from his life. Ibn al-Anbari recited in such a context: Is there no soul that does not die, so that its misery ends, and it does not live a life that has any taste? This verse is part of what God Almighty narrated of the magicians’ sayings. It was said that it is the beginning of a statement, and the pronoun in it is in this manner refers to the matter.
20:75: 75- And whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds meaning, and whoever comes to his Lord believing in Him has done righteous deeds: meaning acts of obedience, and the described is omitted, and the meaning is righteous deeds, and the phrase has done is in the accusative case as a state, and thus a believer is in the accusative case as a state, and the reference with those is to whom, considering its meaning, for them are the highest degrees meaning the lofty stations that the attributes fall short of.
20:76: 76- Gardens of Eden is an explanation of the degrees or a substitute for them, and Eden is the residence, and its explanation has been presented, and the phrase underneath which rivers flow is a state of the gardens, because it is added to Eden, and Eden is a name for residence as was presented, and the accusative of abiding therein is a state of the pronoun of the group in them: meaning staying permanently, and the reference with that is to what was presented to them of the reward, and it is a subject, and the reward of he who purifies himself is its predicate: meaning the reward of he who purifies himself from disbelief and the sins that necessitate Hell. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And what you forced us to do of magic, he said: Pharaoh took forty boys from the Children of Israel and ordered them to learn magic in Pelusium. He said: Teach them a teaching that no one on earth can defeat. Ibn Abbas said: They are among those who believed in Moses, and they are the ones who said: We believe in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you forced us to do of magic. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi regarding his statement: And God is better and more lasting, he said: Better than you if you obey and more lasting in punishment if you disobey. Ahmad, Muslim, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) delivered a sermon and recited this verse: Whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “As for its people who are its people, they will neither die therein nor live. As for those who are not its people, the Fire will kill them completely. Then the intercessors will arise and intercede, and they will be brought in groups on a river called Al-Hayat or Al-Hayawan, and they will grow like scum grows in the mud of a torrent.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The people of the highest ranks will be seen by those beneath them as you see a shining star in the horizon of the sky. Abu Bakr and Umar are among them, and they are blessed.” In the two Sahihs it is worded as: The people of the highest ranks will be seen by those above them as you see a setting star in the horizon of the sky.
20:77: This is the beginning of the rescue of the Children of Israel and the destruction of their enemy, and it was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, Al-A'raf, and Yunus. The lam in La qad is the one that introduces the oath, and in that there is an emphasis that is not hidden, and 77- An in An Tasbih bi-'Abadi is either explanatory because in revelation there is the meaning of saying, or it is a source: that is, that I will take them by storm, that is, by taking them by storm from Egypt. This was mentioned previously in full. So strike for them a dry path in the sea means make a path for them, and the meaning of dry is dry, and the subject was described with it as an exaggeration, and that is because God Almighty dried up that path for them until there was no water or mud in it. And it was read Yabsa with a sukoon on the ba' as a lightened form of Yabsa with a vowel, or the plural of Yabs like Sahib in Sahib, and the phrase Do not fear a dharkan is in the accusative case as a state: that is, we are safe from the enemy catching up with you, or another description of a path, and the dharkan is the catching up with them from Pharaoh and his soldiers. Hamza read do not fear as a response to the command, and the meaning is: if you strike, do not fear. Do not fear according to this reading is a new sentence: that is, you do not fear Pharaoh or the sea. The majority read do not fear and this is more likely because there is no jussive in do not fear. It is possible that this sentence according to the reading of the majority is another description of the path: that is, do not fear it and do not fear from it.
20:78: 78- "So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers. Here, follow is the passive form of follow. It is said that I followed them" if you follow them, and that is if you preceded you and caught up with them, so the meaning is: Pharaoh followed them with his soldiers. It was said that the "ba is redundant and the original is his soldiers followed them": that is, he ordered them to follow Moses and his people. It was read "so he followed them" with emphasis: that is, he caught up with his soldiers and he was with them, as it is said: the prince rode with his sword: that is, he had his sword with him. The place of "his soldiers" is the accusative case in the state of the state, that is, his soldiers preceded him. "So there covered them from the sea that which covered them" means that it rose above them and what rose above them and afflicted them, and the repetition is for glorification and intimidation as in His statement: "The Inevitable * What is the Inevitable?" It was said that what you heard of its story covered them. Ibn al-Anbari said: Some of what covered them covered them covered them, because not all of the sea water covered them, but what covered them was some of it. This phrase indicates that what drowned them was some water, and the first is more appropriate because of what it indicates of terror and glorification. It was read: And what covered them from the sea covered them: meaning what covered them covered them.
20:79: 79- And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them. That is, he led them astray from the right path, and did not guide them to the paths of salvation because he had decreed that Moses and those with him would not escape him because they were in front of him walking on a dry path, and the sea was in front of them. And in His saying: and did not guide, there is an emphasis on his misguidance, because the one who misguides may guide the one he misguides in some matters.
20:80: 80- "O Children of Israel, We have delivered you from your enemy." God Almighty mentioned what He bestowed upon the Children of Israel after their rescue, and the meaning is We said to them after their rescue: O Children of Israel. It is possible that it is addressed to the Jews who were contemporary with our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the blessing upon the fathers is counted among the blessings upon the sons, and what is meant by their enemy here is Pharaoh and his soldiers, by drowning him and his people in the sea in the sight of the Children of Israel. "And We made an appointment with you on the right side of the Mount. The accusative case of side" is as a direct object, not as a circumstantial case because it is a specific, non-vague place. Places are only accusative as a circumstantial case if they are vague. Makki said: This is a principle that is not disputed. An-Nahhas said: The meaning is that Moses commanded us to order you to go out with him so that we may speak to him in your presence and you may hear the speech. It was said that Moses promised after drowning Pharaoh that he would come to the side of the mountain, so the promise was to Moses, and they were only addressed by it because the promise was for them. Abu Amr, Abu Jaafar, and Yaqub read We promised you without an alif, and Abu Ubaidah chose it because the promise was from God specifically to Moses, and a promise can only be made by two people. We have already mentioned this meaning in Surat Al-Baqarah. The right hand is accusative as an attribute of the side, and what is meant is the right of the person, because the mountain has no right or left, so if it is said Take from the right of the mountain, it means from your right of the mountain. It was read with the right hand in the genitive case as an attribute of the complement to it. And We sent down upon you the manna and the quails. The interpretation of manna as taranjabin and the quails as samani has already been mentioned, and we have explained that in a way that cannot be added to it. And sending that down upon them was in the wilderness.
20:81: 81- Eat from the good things with which We have provided you meaning, We said to them, Eat, and what is meant by the good things are the pleasures, and it was said that it means the permissible according to the well-known disagreement on that. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Al-A’mash read: We have saved you from your enemy and made an appointment with you at the side of the mountain “Eat from the good things with which We have provided you” with the first-person pronoun ta in all three. The rest read it with the letter nūn of majesty in it and do not transgress therein. Transgression is transgression: that is, do not transgress what is permissible to what is not permissible. It was said that the meaning is: do not deny the blessing of God, lest you become transgressors. It was also said that do not be ungrateful for the blessing and do not forget to thank Him for it. It was also said that do not disobey the Benefactor: that is, do not let abundance and well-being lead you to disobedience. There is no objection to interpreting transgression as having all of these meanings, for each one of them is true of transgression. So My wrath will descend upon you is the answer to the prohibition: that is, My wrath will be upon you and will descend upon you. It is taken from the descent of the debt: that is, the time for its payment is present. And whoever My wrath descends upon has certainly perished. Al-A’mash, Yahya ibn Waththāb, and Al-Kisa’i read so that with a ḍamma on the ha’. They also read he will descend with a ḍamma on the first lam. The rest read it with a kasra in both of them, and they are two dialects. Al-Farra’ said: “I prefer the kasra to the damma because the damma is from the word ‘halul’ which means ‘occurring’, and ‘halul’ with the kasra means ‘occurring’. The interpretation came with the ‘obligation’ not ‘occurring’, and something similar to this was mentioned by Abu Ubaidah and others. The meaning of ‘he has fallen’ is ‘he has perished’.” Hawiya: Al-Zajjaj said, He fell meaning he went to the abyss, which is the bottom of Hell. From hawa yahwi hawiya: meaning he fell from a high place to a low place. And hawa so-and-so: meaning he died.
20:82: 82- And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, and does righteousness. That is, whoever repents from the sins, the greatest of which is associating partners with God, and believes in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and does righteous deeds that the Shari'ah encourages and approves of. Then is guided. That is, remains steadfast in that until he dies. This is what Al-Zajjaj and others said. It was said that he did not doubt his faith, and it was said that he adhered to the Sunnah and the Jama'ah, and it was said that he learned knowledge in order to be guided by it, and it was said that he knew that there is a reward for that and a punishment for abandoning it. The first is more likely than the following.
20:83: 83- And what made you leave your people in such a hurry, O Moses? This is a narration of what happened between God Almighty and Moses when he reached the appointed time. The commentators said: The appointment was that Moses and a group of the notables of his people would meet, so Moses set out with them, then he hurried away from them out of longing for his Lord, so God said to him: What made you leave in such a hurry? What made you leave your people and go out from among them?
20:84: So Moses answered that 84- He said, 'They are on my trail' meaning they are near me, following my trail and continuing after me. It was said that he did not mean that they were walking behind him, but rather he meant that they were near him waiting for him to return to them, then he said explicitly the reason for what God asked him about, saying: And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You might be pleased meaning that You might be pleased with me for my haste to obey Your command or that You might increase Your pleasure with me by that. Abu Hatim said: Isa bin Omar said: Banu Tamim say Oula shortened, and the people of Hijaz say Oula extended. Ibn Abi Ishaq, Nadr, and Ruways read on the authority of Ya'qub Ala'i with a kasra on the hamza and a sukoon on the tha', and the rest read it with a fatha, and they are two dialects. The meaning of I hastened to You is: I hastened to the place that You commanded me to go to so that You might be pleased with me. It is said: a man who is hasty, hasty, and hasty: between haste, and haste is the opposite of slowness.
20:85: And the sentence 85 - He said, 'We have indeed tested your people after you' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said, so what did God say to him? So it was said, He said, 'We have indeed tested your people after you': meaning, We tested them, tried them, and threw them into trial and tribulation. Ibn al-Anbari said: We made them tempted and wretched by worshipping the calf after you left among them, and they are the ones who left them with Aaron. And the Samaritan led them astray meaning, he called them to misguidance, and he was from a people who worshipped cows, so he entered the religion of the Children of Israel outwardly, but in his heart was what was in it of worshipping cows, and he was from a tribe known as the Samaria, and he said to those with him from the Children of Israel: Moses only differed from the appointment that was between you and him because of the jewelry that you had with you, and it was forbidden to you, and he ordered them to throw it into the fire, so what happened with the calf happened.
20:86: 86- "So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved." It was said that the return to his people was after he had completed forty days: Dhul-Qi'dah and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. Grief is intense anger, and it was said that it is sorrow. This has been explained in full in Al-A'raf. "He said, 'O my people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise?'" The question is for reproachful denial, and the good promise is his promise to them of Paradise if they remained obedient to Him. He promised them that He would let them hear His words in the Torah through the tongue of Moses so that they would act according to what is in it, and thus they would deserve the reward for their actions. It was said that he promised them victory and triumph. It was said that it is his statement: "And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents." The verse. "Has the covenant been prolonged upon you?" The fa' is for connecting to an implied meaning: that is, he promised you that, so the time was prolonged for you and you forgot. "Or did you want the wrath of your Lord to descend upon you?" That is, to befall you and descend upon you. Anger is punishment and vengeance. The meaning is: Or did you want to do an action that would be the cause of the wrath of God descending upon you? So you broke your appointment with me, meaning your appointment with me. The source is added to the object, because they promised him that they would remain obedient to God Almighty until he returned to them from Mount Tur. It was said that they promised him that they would follow him to the appointed time, so they stopped and answered him.
20:87: And 87- "They said, 'We did not break your appointment' which we promised you 'by our king'" with the opening of the meem, and this is the reading of Nafi', Abu Ja'far, Asim, and Isa bin Omar, and Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read with the breaking of the meem, and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this reading because it is in the high and eloquent language, and it is the source of the verb "malakat al-shay', I own it, and the source is added to the subject and the object is deleted: that is, by our kingship of our affairs, or by our kingship of the right, rather we made a mistake and did not control ourselves and we were forced to make a mistake, and Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read by our kingship with the damma of the meem, and the meaning is by our authority: that is, we did not have a king so we would break your appointment, and it was said that the opening, the breaking, and the damma in by our kingship are all languages in the source of malakat al-shay' "but we carried burdens of the ornaments of the people Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Hafs, Abu Ja'far, and Ruways read hamalna" with the damma of the ha' And the emphasis on the meem, and the rest read with the opening of the ha and the light meem, and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this reading because they carried the people’s ornaments with them by their choice, and they did not carry them by force, for they had borrowed them from them when they wanted to go out with Moses, and they made them think that they were meeting for a festival or a feast, and it was said that it is what they took from the people of Pharaoh when the sea threw them up to the shore, and it was called burdens: meaning sins, because it is not permissible for them to take it, and spoils are not permissible for them according to their law, and burdens are originally heavy as the linguists have stated, and what is meant by adornment here is the jewelry So we threw it meaning we threw it into the fire seeking to be freed from its sin, and it was said that the meaning is: we threw it to the Samaritan so that it would remain with him until Moses returned and he would consider it, So the Samaritan threw meaning the Samaritan threw it like that, before the Samaritan said to them when the people were slow in returning Moses: He was only held back from you because of the jewelry you have, so they gathered it and gave it to him, so he threw it into the fire He fashioned a calf for them from it, then threw a handful of the trace of the Messenger, who was Gabriel, on it.
20:88: So it became 88- a calf with a body that moos meaning it moos like a living calf, and moos is the sound of a cow. It was said that its mooing was due to the wind, because it had holes made in it, so when the wind entered its cavity it moos and there was no life in it. They said, 'This is your god and the god of Moses' meaning the Samaritan and those who agreed with him said this so he forgot meaning he preferred Moses and did not know the location of this god of his, and he went looking for him in the mountain. It was said that the meaning is: Moses forgot to mention to you that this is his god and your god. It was said that the people are the Samaritan: meaning the Samaritan left what Moses was commanded to do of faith and went astray. This is what Ibn al-A'rabi said.
20:89: 89- Do they not see that he does not return to them a word? That is, do they not consider and reflect that this calf does not return to them a word: that is, he does not respond to them, and does not speak to them if they speak to him? So how can they imagine that he is a god incapable of speaking? For in does he not return it is the lightened form of the heavy form, and in it there is an implied pronoun that refers to the calf, and for this reason the verb was raised after it, and from it is the saying of the poet: In the youth of the swords of India, they knew that whoever is barefoot and wears shoes will perish. That is, he is lost. And it was read with the verb in the accusative case, as if it were the accusative, and the sentence and he does not possess for them any harm or benefit is conjoined with the sentence he does not return: that is, do they not see that he is not able to ward off any harm from them or bring them any benefit?
20:90: 90- And Aaron had said to them before The lam is the one that introduces the oath, and the sentence confirms what the sentence before it included of denial and rebuke of them: that is, Aaron had said to them before Moses came and returned to them, O my people, you were only tempted by it that is, you fell into temptation because of the calf and were afflicted by it and went astray from the path of truth because of it. It was said that the meaning of the restriction derived from only is that the calf became a cause of their temptation, not for their guidance, and it does not mean that they were tempted by the calf and not by anything else, And your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command that is, your Lord is the Most Merciful, not the calf, and obey my command, not his command.
20:91: 91- They said, 'We will not cease to be devoted to it until Moses returns to us.' They answered Aaron about his previous statement with this answer that included his disobedience and his refusal to accept what he called them to of good and warned them against of evil: meaning, we will not cease to worship this calf until Moses returns to us, and we will see whether he will confirm our worship of it or forbid us from it. At that time, Aaron withdrew from them with twelve thousand who denied what the Samaritan had done. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab regarding his statement: dry, he said: dry, with no water or mud in it. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Do not fear being overtaken by the people of Pharaoh, nor fear drowning from the sea. They also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Then he has fallen, “has fallen,” has been miserable. They also narrated on his authority: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, he said from polytheism, and believes, he said: he believes in the Oneness of God, and does righteousness, he said: he performs the obligatory duties, and then is guided, he said: he did not doubt. Saeed bin Mansour and Al-Firyabi also narrated on his authority: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, he said: whoever repents from sin, believes from polytheism, and does righteousness between himself and his Lord, and then is guided, he knows that his work will be rewarded for it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Then he was guided. He said: Then he remained steadfast and adhered to the Sunnah and the Jama’ah. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th on the authority of Amr bin Maymun on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Moses hurried to his Lord, so God said: And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses? He said: Then he saw a man in the shade of the Throne and was amazed by him, so he said: Who is this, O Lord? He said: I will not tell you who he is, but I will tell you three things about him: He did not envy people for what God had given them of His grace, nor did he disobey his parents, nor did he spread gossip. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Ali, who said: When Moses hastened to his Lord, the Samaritan gathered what he could of the jewelry of the Children of Israel and made it into a calf. Then he threw a handful into its stomach, and behold, it was a calf with a body that bellowed. The Samaritan said to them: This is your god and the god of Moses. Aaron said to them: O people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise? When Moses returned, he took hold of his brother’s head, and Aaron said to him what he said. Moses said to the Samaritan: What is the matter with you? He said: I took a handful of the traces of the Messenger and threw it away, and thus my soul prompted me. Moses went to the calf, and Moses put the files on it and cut it with them while he was on the bank of a river. No one who worshipped that calf drank from that water except that his face turned yellow like gold. They said to Moses: What is our repentance? He said: Some of you will kill each other. So they took knives and a man would kill his brother, his father and his son, and he did not care who he killed until seventy thousand of them were killed. Then God revealed to Moses, Order them to raise their hands, for I have forgiven those who were killed and accepted the repentance of those who remained. There are many narrations of this story. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: By Our kingdom, he said: By Our command. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Qatadah: By Our kingdom, he said: By Our power. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi something similar. He also narrated from al-Hasan, he said: By Our authority. Al-Faryabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot, he said: Moses forgot to tell you that this was his god.
20:92: Sentence 92 - He said, O Aaron is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, and the meaning is: When Moses reached them, he took hold of the hair of his brother Aaron’s head and beard and said, What prevented you from following me and catching up with me when they fell into this misguidance and entered into the trial.
20:93: It was said that the meaning of 93-"What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me" is what prevented you from following me in denouncing them. It was said that its meaning is: Why did you not fight them, since you knew that if I were among them, I would fight them. It was also said that its meaning is: Why did you not leave them? "La in not following" is redundant, and it is in the accusative case as a second object of preventing: meaning, what prevented you, when you saw their going astray, from following me? The question in "did you disobey my command is for denial and rebuke, and the fa" is for conjunction with an implied word like its counterparts. The meaning is: How did you disobey my command to you by standing up for God and opposing those who disobeyed His religion and you stayed among those who took the calf as a god? It was said that what is meant by his saying "my command is his saying that God narrated about him Moses said to his brother Aaron, Take my place among my people and reform and do not follow the way of the corrupters. So when he stayed with them and did not exaggerate in denouncing them, he attributed it to His disobedience.
20:94: 94- "He said, O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head." It was read with the fat-ha and the kasra of the meem. We have already discussed this in Surat Al-A'raf. He attributed it to his mother, even though he was his brother from his father and mother, according to the majority, to gain sympathy for him and soften his heart. The meaning of "nor by my head and nor by the hair of my head" is: do not do this to me as a punishment from you to me, for I have an excuse, which is: "Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'I have divided the Children of Israel'," meaning I feared that if I went out from them and left them, they would disperse and you would say, 'I have divided their group.' This is because if Aaron had gone out, a group of them would have followed him and others would have stayed behind with the Samaritan at the calf, and perhaps this would have led to fighting between them. The meaning of "and you did not observe my word" and you did not act upon my advice to you regarding them, I feared that you would say, 'I have divided them' and you would say, 'You did not act upon my advice to you regarding them and preserve it.' What he meant by Moses' advice to him is his saying: "Take my place among my people and do good." Abu Ubaid said: The meaning of And you did not wait for my word and you did not wait for my covenant and my arrival because you ordered me to be with them, so Aaron apologized to Moses here with this, and he apologized to him in Al-A’raf with what God narrated about him there where he said: Indeed, the people weakened me and almost killed me.
20:95: Then he stopped talking to his brother and addressed the Samaritan, saying: 95- “He said: What is the matter with you, O Samaritan?” That is, what is the matter with you and what made you do what you did.
20:96: 96- He said, 'I saw what they did not see.' That is, the Samaritan said in response to Moses: I saw what they did not see, or I knew what they did not know, and I understood what they did not understand. What he meant by that was that he saw Gabriel in the prime of life, so it occurred to him to take a handful of the Messenger's trace, and that trace does not fall on an inanimate object except that it becomes alive. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Al-A'mash, and Khalaf read with what they did not see with the doubled letter above as a direct address. The rest read it with a lower syllable, which is better, because it is very unlikely that Moses would be addressed with this and claim for himself that he knew what Moses did not know. It was read with a damma on the sad in both cases, and with a kasra on the first and a fatha on the second. Abi bin Ka’b, Ibn Mas’ud, al-Hasan, and Qatadah read Fa-qabasat Qabsa with a silent sad in both cases, and the rest read it with a voiced dad in both cases. The difference between them is that qabd with a voiced sad means taking with the whole hand, and with a silent sad with the tips of the fingers, and qabdah with a damma on the qaf means the amount that is being grasped. Al-Jawhari said: It is what you have seized of something. He said: It may have come with the fat-ha, and it has been read as fist with the qaf with a damma or a fat-ha, and the meaning of the fat-ha is the time of seizing, then it was applied to what is seized, which is the meaning of fist with the qaf with a damma, and the meaning of from the trace of the Messenger is from the place on which the hoof of Gabriel’s horse fell, and the meaning of I threw it away is so I cast it into the molten jewelry cast in the form of a calf. And thus my soul tempted me Al-Akhfash said: meaning it adorned: meaning and like that temptation my soul tempted me, and it was said that the meaning of my soul tempted me.
20:97: 97- When Moses heard that from him, he said, Then go, for in life you will have the right to say, 'No touching' meaning, go from among us and leave us, for in life you will have the right to say, 'No touching'. Touching is taken from contact: meaning, no one touches you and you do not touch anyone, but not according to your choice, but rather according to the compulsion that forced you to do so, because God Almighty commanded Moses to banish the Samaritan from his people, and commanded the Children of Israel not to mix with him or come near him or speak to him as a punishment for him. It was said that when Moses said that to him, he fled, and began to wander in the wilderness with wild beasts and wild animals, not finding anyone to touch him until he became like someone who says, 'No touching' because of his distance from people and people being far from him, as the poet said: A flag bearer with a mask, until the Azd say, No, I will not be mocked. Sibawayh said: It is built on the kasra. Al-Zajjaj said: The seen was broken because the kasra is a sign of femininity. Al-Jawhari said in Al-Sahah: As for the Arabs saying La masaas like Qatam, it is built on the kasra because it is modified from the source, which is touch. Al-Nahhas said: I heard Ali bin Sulaiman say: I heard Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Mubarrad say: If something is defective in three ways, it must be built, and if it is defective in two ways, it must not be declined, because after declension there is nothing but construction. So Masaas Darak is defective in three ways: one of them is that it is modified, one of them is that it is feminine, and one of them is that it is definite. So when construction is required in it and the alif before the seen is silent, the seen was broken because of the meeting of two silent letters. I have seen Abu Ishaq, meaning Al-Zajjaj, who believed that this statement was wrong and he obliged Abu Al-Abbas if a woman is named Pharaoh to build it, and no one says this. Abu Haywah read the meem with a fatha and the rest with a kasra. The gist of what has been said about the meaning of no touching is threefold: The first is that it was forbidden for him to touch people, and if someone touched him, he would become a fever for the touched and the touched. That is why he would cry out if he saw someone no touching. The second is that what is meant is to prevent people from mixing with him. It has been objected that if a man is abandoned, he should not say no touching, but rather it is said to him. It has been answered that what is meant is the narration: that is, make you, O Samaritan, such that if you tell about your situation, you say no touching. The third opinion is that what is meant is the cessation of his offspring, and that he should tell that he will not be able to touch a woman. This was said by Abu Muslim, and it is very weak. Then he mentioned his situation in the Hereafter and said: And indeed, for you is an appointment that you will not fail to fulfill. That is, God will not fail you in that appointment, which is the Day of Resurrection. The appointment is a source: that is, for you is a promise for your punishment, and it will inevitably happen. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, God will reward you for what you did on the Day of Resurrection, and God does not fail in His promise. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Yaqub, Ibn Muhaisin, Al-Yazidi and Al-Hasan read lan takhlafhu with a kasra on the lam, and according to this reading it has two meanings: one is that you will come to him and will not find him left behind, as you say ahmadtuhu meaning you found him praised, and the second is a threat meaning you must go to him. Ibn Mas'ud read lan nakhlafhu with a noon meaning God will not leave him behind. The rest read it with a fatha on the lam and with a fatha on the fawqiyah in the passive form, meaning what we mentioned before. And look at your god to whom you have been devoted. The original form of dhala is dhalatu, so the first lam was deleted for ease, and the Arabs do that a lot. Al-A'mash read it with two lams according to the original form. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, dhalatu is with a kasra on the dhad. The meaning is: Look at your god to whom you have been devoted and established in His worship, and the devoted one is the one who is constant. Lahannahu The majority read it with a damma on the noon and a shaddah on the ra from harqahu yaharquhu. Al-Hasan read it with a damma on the noon, a sukoon on the ha’ and a light ra’ from ahraqahu yuharquhu. Ali, Ibn Abbas, Abu Ja’far, Ibn Muhaisin, Ashab and Al-Uqaili read lanharqunahu with a fatha on the noon and a damma on the ra’ and lightened from harqat al-shay’ aharqahu harqan if you cool it and rub some of it against others: that is, we will cool it with the files, and the file is called al-muharraq. The first reading is better, and its meaning is burning with fire, and so is the meaning of the second reading. These three readings were combined by saying that he burned, then cooled with the file. In the reading of Ibn Mas’ud, landhahbanhu thumma lanharqunahu, and the lam is the one that introduces the oath, Then we will blow it into the sea a blast. Blasting is shaking something so that the wind blows it away. Abu Raja’ read lannasfanhu with a damma on the seen, and the rest read it with a kasra, and they are two dialects. Mansaf is what food is used to blow away, and it is something that is straight and raised above the chest, and nasafat is what falls from it.
20:98: 98- Your god is only God, other than whom there is no god not this calf with which you were tempted by the Samaritan His knowledge encompasses all things The majority read Wasaa with a kasra on the seen and a lightened one. It is transitive with one object, which is everything, and the accusative of the word Wasaa is a specification transferred from the subject: meaning His knowledge encompasses all things. Mujahid and Qatadah read Wasaa with a shaddah on the seen and a fatha on it, so it is transitive with two objects, and the accusative of the word Wasaa is as the first object even though it is delayed, because it is originally the subject, and the meaning is: His knowledge encompasses all things, and something similar to this has been mentioned in Al-A'raf.
20:99: 99- Thus do We relate to you The kaf is in the accusative case as an adjective for a deleted source, meaning just as We related to you the story of Moses, so do We relate to you of the report of what has already occurred meaning of the report of past incidents in the past nations, to be a consolation for you and an indication of your truthfulness, and min is for partiality: meaning some of the report of that And We have given you from Ourselves a reminder what is meant by the reminder is the Qur'an, and it is called a reminder because of what it contains of reasons for remembrance and consideration, and it is said that what is meant by the reminder is honor, like His saying: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people.
20:100: Then He, the Most High, threatened those who turn away from this remembrance, saying: 100- Whoever turns away from it will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection. That is, he turned away from it and did not believe in it or act according to what was in it. It was said that he turned away from God, the Most High, for whoever turns away from it will bear a burden on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:that is, a great sin and a heavy punishment because of his turning away.
20:101: 101- They will abide in it meaning in the burden, and the meaning is: that they will abide in its punishment, and the accusative of they will abide is in the state of the state of "And evil for them on the Day of Resurrection is a burden" meaning evil is the burden on the Day of Resurrection, and the specific blame is omitted: meaning evil is the burden of their burden, and the lam is for clarification as in "Heet lak". Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: O Aaron, what prevented you? to his statement: Did you disobey my command? He said: Moses ordered him to reform and not follow the path of the corruptors. So part of his reform was to denounce the calf. He also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And you did not wait for My word. He said: You did not wait for My word to be said: What am I going to do? Ibn Abbas said: You did not wait for it means you did not keep My word. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Then you will have in this life that you will say, ‘No contact.’ He said: A punishment for it. And indeed, you have an appointment that you will not fail to fulfill. He said: You will not be absent from it. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And look at your god to whom you have been devoted. He said: I have established. We will surely burn him. He said: With fire. Then We will surely scatter him into the sea. He said: We will scatter him into the sea. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite lan harqanahu lightly and he would say: gold and silver are not burned in fire, rather they are ground with a file and then thrown into the fire and they turn to ash. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: al-yamm means the sea. He also narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: al-yamm means the river. He also narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: His knowledge encompasses all things he said: filled. He also narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: from Us is a reminder he said: the Qur’an. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid wazran he said: sin. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And evil for them on the Day of Resurrection is their burden he said: evil is what they have borne.
20:102: The circumstance is 102- "The Day it is blown" related to the implied word, which is remember. It was said that it is a substitute for the Day of Resurrection, but the first is more appropriate. The majority read "Yanfakh" with a damma on the lower yaa as a passive participle. Abu Amr and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a noon as an active participle. Abu Amr provided evidence for this reading by his saying, "And We will gather", for it is with a noon. Ibn Hormuz read "yanfakh" with a lower sukoon, in the passive voice, meaning that the subject is God, the Most High, or Israfil. Abu Ayyad read "fi al-Suwar with a fatha on the waw, plural of suwar", while the rest read it with a sukoon on the waw. Talha ibn Masraf and al-Hasan read "yahshar with a lower sukoon, in the passive voice, and al-mujrimin" was raised, which is contrary to the script of the Mushaf. The rest read it with a nun, and the explanation of this has been previously mentioned in Al-An'am. What is meant by the mujrimin are the polytheists and the disobedient who are seized with their sins that God has not forgiven them. What is meant by "that day" is the day of the blowing of the trumpet. The accusative of "zarqan is in the state of al-mujrimin", meaning the blue of the eyes. Blueness is the greenness of the eye like the eye of a cat, and the Arabs consider blueness of the eye to be a bad omen. Al-Farra' said "zarqan" means blind. Al-Azhari said: "thirsty", which is the opinion of Al-Zajjaj because the blackness of the eye changes to blue with thirst. It was said that he used his word blue to refer to false greed if disappointment follows it, and it was said that it is a metaphor for the eyes staring out from intense greed, and from it is the poet’s saying: Your eyes are blue, son of Ma'kabir, like every gazelle's eyes are blue from meanness. The first statement is more appropriate, and the combination between this verse and His statement: And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf is what was said that on the Day of Resurrection there are states and situations in which their characteristics differ and their punishment varies.
20:103: And the sentence 103 - "They whisper among themselves is in the accusative case as a state, or it is a new sentence to explain what they are in that day, and the word khaf in the language means stillness, then it was said to someone who lowered his voice, khaf". The meaning is that they whisper: that is, some of them say to each other secretly "You have not remained except ten" meaning you have not remained in this world except ten nights, and it was said in the graves, and it was said between the two blasts. The meaning is that they will shorten the duration of their stay in this world, or in the graves, or between the two blasts due to the severity of what they see of the horrors of the Resurrection. It was said that what is meant by "ten" is ten hours.
20:104: Then when they said this statement, God Almighty said 104- We know best what they say when the best of them in way says meaning the most just of them in speech, the most eloquent of them in opinion, and the most knowledgeable of them in his own eyes You have only remained a day meaning you have only remained a single day, and this statement is attributed to the best of them because it is more indicative of the intensity of the terror, not because it is closer to the truth.
20:105: 105- And they ask you about the mountains that is, about the state of the mountains on the Day of Resurrection. They had asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, so God Almighty commanded him to answer them, saying: Then say, 'My Lord will blow them away with a blast.' Ibn al-A'rabi and others said: By uprooting them from their roots, then turning them into sand that flows like a torrent. Then He makes them flow like patterned wool, blown by the winds like this and that, then like scattered dust. The fa in His statement, say is an implied condition, and the meaning is: If they ask you, then say, or to hasten to oblige the questioners.
20:106: The pronoun in his saying: 106- He leaves it refers to the mountains in terms of their locations: that is, He leaves their locations after blowing away what was on them of mountains a flat plain. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The flat plain is the smooth land in which there is no vegetation. Al-Jawhari said: The flat plain is the ground, and the plural is aqwa', aqwa', and qi'an. It is apparent from the language of the Arabs that the plain is the exposed place, and the flat plain is the smooth plain. Sibawayh recited: How many sand dunes and knots are there before your house? The word qa’an is in the accusative case as a second object of yadhar because it includes the meaning of making, or as a state, and safasafa is an attribute of it.
20:107: And location 107 - You will not see therein any crookedness The accusative case is as a second description of a valley, and the pronoun refers to the mountains in that regard, and the crooked with the kasra of the 'ayn is crookedness, Ibn al-A'rabi said. And the small hills, and the 'amt in the language is a high place, and it was said that the crooked is the inclination and the 'amt is the trace like the strap, and the crooked is said to be the valley, and the 'amt is the hill, and it was said that they are the height, and it was said that the crooked is for the cracks, and the 'amt is the hill, and the 'amt is the cracks in the ground, and the 'amt is said to be thick in one place and thin in another, and describing the places of the mountains with the crooked with the kasra of the 'ayn here refutes what is said: that the crooked with the kasra of the 'ayn is in the meanings and with the fatha of it in the objects, and the author of Al-Kashshaf took it upon himself to do so in this place with what is sufficient for him, and in others it is spacious.
20:108: 108- On that Day they will follow the Caller, with no crookedness in him. That is, on the Day when the mountains are blown away, people will follow the Caller of God to the place of assembly. Al-Farra' said: It means the sound of the assembly. It was also said that the Caller is Israfil when he blows the Trumpet, with no crookedness in him: that is, they will have no way of turning away from his call, so they will not be able to deviate from it or turn away from it, rather they will hasten to it. This is what most of the commentators said. It was also said that there is no crookedness in his call. And the voices will be humbled before the Most Merciful, that is, they will submit to His awe. It was also said that they will be humbled, and it was also said that they will be still. From this is the saying of the poet: When the report of Al-Zubayr came, the city walls and the mountains were humbled. You will hear nothing but a whisper. A whisper is a low voice. Most commentators said: It is the sound of the feet being carried to the place of resurrection. And from it the poet said: They walk with us whispering It means the sound of camel hooves. Ru'bah described himself as: A lion beats the lion's whispers, but is not afraid of the elephant or the buffalo. The lion is called whispering because it whispers in the darkness, meaning it treads lightly. It appears that what is meant here is every low sound, whether made by the foot, the mouth, or something else. This is supported by the reading of Abi bin Ka’b: They do not speak except in a whisper.
20:109: 109- "On that Day, no intercession will benefit meaning, on the Day that what was mentioned occurs, no intercession will benefit from any intercessor, whoever he may be, except for one to whom the Most Gracious has given permission meaning, except the intercession of one to whom the Most Gracious has given permission to intercede and whose word is acceptable" meaning, he is pleased with his word in the intercession or is pleased with the intercessor's word for him. The meaning is: Intercession will only benefit one to whom the Most Gracious has given permission to intercede, and who has a word that is acceptable. Similar to this verse is His statement: "They do not intercede except for one with whom He is pleased", and His statement: "They do not possess intercession except for one who has taken a covenant with the Most Gracious", and His statement: "So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them."
20:110: 110- He knows what is before them and what is behind them meaning what is before them of the matter of the Hour, and what is behind them of the matter of this world, and what is meant here is all of creation, and it was said that what is meant by them are those who follow the caller, and Ibn Jarir said: The pronoun refers to the angels, God has informed those who worship them that they do not know what is before them and what is behind them and they do not encompass Him in knowledge meaning God Almighty, their knowledge does not encompass His essence, nor His attributes, nor His information, and it was said that the pronoun refers to what is in the two places, for they do not know all of that.
20:111: 111- And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining meaning they will be submissive and humbled, as Ibn al-A'rabi said. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of anā in the language is submissive. It is said that someone is anā meaning he is submissive and from this the word an meaning he is submissive is used for a prisoner. From this is the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: A King on the throne of heaven, dominant, before whose glory faces bow and prostrate It was said that it is from the word ‘ana’, meaning fatigue. And he who bears injustice will fail, meaning he who bears some injustice will lose. It was also said that it is polytheism.
20:112: 112- And whoever does righteous deeds that is righteous deeds while he is a believer in God, because a deed is not accepted without faith, rather it is a condition for acceptance then he will not fear injustice that he will suffer from a reduction in reward in the Hereafter nor deprivation, deprivation means reduction and breaking. It is said I deprived you of my right: meaning I cut it off and left it, and this is digesting food: meaning its weight decreases, and a woman with a thin side: meaning a thin stomach, and Ibn Kathir and Mujahid read does not fear in the accusative case in response to his saying: And whoever does righteous deeds, and the rest read fears as a predicate. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man came to him and said: I saw his statement: And We shall gather the guilty on that Day blue-eyed and another time blind. He said: Indeed, on the Day of Resurrection there will be states in which they will be blue-eyed and in another state blind. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: They whisper among themselves, he said: They whisper. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd bin Hamid Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr regarding his statement: The best of them in way, he said: The most perfect of them in intellect. In another version he said: The most knowledgeable of them about himself. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: Quraysh said: How will your Lord deal with these mountains on the Day of Resurrection? So, And they ask you about the mountains, the verse was revealed. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He will leave it a level plain, he said: There is no vegetation in it. You will not see therein any crookedness, he said: A valley. Nor a hill, he said: A mound. And Abd bin Hamid bin Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he was asked about the statement of God, A level plain, wherein you will see no crookedness or unevenness, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say: It is the smooth land in which there is no high hill or depression. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Crookedness he said: Nor unevenness he said: Unevenness is the trace like a shoelace. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi who said: The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in a darkness that will envelop the sky and the stars will scatter and the sun and moon will disappear and a caller will call out and the people will follow the voice and believe in him. So that is the statement of God, On that Day they will follow the Caller, with no crookedness in him. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Salih regarding the verse: He said: There is no crookedness from him. And Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And the voices will be hushed, he said: They will be still, So you will hear nothing but a whisper, he said: A low voice. And Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement, But a whisper, he said: The sound of footsteps. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Hasan, similarly. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The low voice. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The secret of speech and the sound of feet. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the faces are humbled, meaning: They became submissive. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Qatadah, similarly. Abd bin Hamid Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They became humble. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abi Al-Aliyah, who said: They became submissive. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: And the faces are humbled, meaning bowing and prostrating. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And he who bears injustice has failed, meaning: Shirk. Abd al-Razzaq and Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Qatada, And he has failed who bears injustice, he said: polytheism, and fears neither injustice nor deprivation, he said: injustice: that his sins will be increased, nor deprivation, he said: that his good deeds will be decreased. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, he said: He does not fear that his sins will be wronged, nor his good deeds will be deprived. Al-Faryabi, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, nor deprivation, he said: by force.
20:113: His statement: 113- And thus We have sent it down is connected to His statement Thus do We relate to you. That is, We have sent down the like of that revelation: that is, the Qur'an while it is an Arabic Qur'an, that is, in the language of the Arabs so that they may understand it. And We have diversified therein some of the warnings, We have explained therein various types of warnings as a warning and intimidation, or We have repeated some of them in it, that they may fear God, that is, so that they may fear God and avoid His disobedience and beware of His punishment. Or that it may cause them to remember, that is, to consider and learn a lesson. It has been said that it is piety, or that it is honor, or that it is obedience and worship, because remembrance is applied to it. Al-Hasan read or that we may cause them to remember with a nun.
20:114: 114- So exalted is God, the True King When He explained to His servants the greatness of His favor upon them by sending down the Qur'an, He cleared Himself of resembling His creations in any way: meaning, God is exalted above the heresy of the heretics and from what the polytheists say about His attributes, for He is the King in whose hand is reward and punishment, and He is the Truth, meaning the Possessor of the Truth. And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you meaning its revelation is completed to you. The commentators said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would hasten to Gabriel and recite before Gabriel finished the revelation, out of his eagerness for what was being sent down to him, so God forbade him from doing so. Similar to this is His statement: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it as will come, God willing. It was said that the meaning is: And do not deliver it to the people before the explanation of its interpretation comes to you. Ibn Mas'ud, Ya'qub, Al-Hasan, and Al-A'mash read before you are completed with the letter nun and the accusative of His revelation. And say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge' that is, ask your Lord to increase knowledge of His Book.
20:115: 115- And We had already made a covenant with Adam The lam is the one that introduces the oath, and the renewed sentence confirms what preceded it from the conjugation of the threat. That is, We had commanded him and advised him, and the covenant is omitted, which is what will come from his prohibition from eating from the tree, and the meaning of before is before this time, so he forgot Al-A'mash read it with a sukoon on the ya', and what is meant by forgetfulness here is abandoning the work of what was covenanted with him and refraining from it, and this is what most of the commentators said, and it was said that forgetfulness in its true sense, and that he forgot what God had covenanted with him and refrained from it, and Adam was seized by forgetfulness at that time, even though forgetfulness was lifted from this nation, and what is meant by the verse is to console the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to the first opinion. That is, the obedience of the sons of Adam to Satan is an ancient matter, and that if these contemporaries of his broke the covenant, then their father Adam broke it, as Ibn Jarir and Al-Qushayri said. Ibn Atiyyah objected to him, saying that Adam being similar to the infidels who denied God is nothing. It was read fansa with a damma on the nun and a shaddah on the seen with a kasra, in the passive form: that is, Satan forgot him. And We found no determination in him. Determination in the language means the soul’s habituation to an action and determination to do it, and continuing with the belief in whatever it may be. Adam, peace be upon him, had habituated himself not to eat from the tree and was determined to do so, but when Satan whispered to him, his will softened and his determination weakened, and he was overcome by human weakness. It was said that determination is patience, that is, We found no patience in him to avoid eating from the tree. Al-Nahhas said: It is also the case in the language. It is said of someone that he was determined, meaning he was patient and steadfast in refraining from sins until he was saved from them. And from it is as the resolute messengers were patient. And it was said that the meaning is: And we did not find him determined to sin, and Ibn Kaysan said the same. And it was said that we did not find him an opinion that he was determined to do, and Ibn Qutaybah said the same.
20:116: Then the Almighty proceeded to explain how his forgetfulness and loss of resolve became apparent, and the factor in when is understood: i.e. 116- And remember when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam’ and connecting the mention to the time, even though the intended purpose is to mention the incidents in it, for the sake of exaggeration, because if the command to mention the time occurred, mentioning the incidents in it would be necessary by way of fortiori. The explanation of this story has been presented in full in Surat Al-Baqarah.
20:117: The meaning of 117- so you are miserable is that you are tired in obtaining what is necessary for a living, such as plowing and planting. He did not say so you are miserable, because the speech from the beginning of the story is with Adam alone.
20:118: Then he explained what this prohibition requires, including complete rest from fatigue and care, saying: 118- You will neither be hungry nor naked therein, meaning in Paradise. The meaning is that you will enjoy various types of livelihood and be luxuriant in various kinds of blessings, such as delicious food and beautiful clothing. For when hunger and nakedness were negated from him, it indicated that he would be full and clothed.
20:119: And thus His saying: 119- And that you will not be thirsty therein nor will you be exposed to the sun's heat. For the negation of thirst necessitates the attainment of quenching thirst and the existence of a dwelling that will relieve him of the hardship of the sun's heat. It is said that a man has been exposed to the sun's heat, so the Almighty mentioned here that He has relieved him of the preoccupation with the matter of livelihood and the fatigue of toiling to obtain it. There is no doubt that the origins of the hardships in this world are the attainment of satiety, quenching thirst, clothing, and shelter. What is other than these is leftovers without which survival is possible. It is an announcement from God Almighty to Adam that if he obeys Him, then he will have all of this in Paradise, and if he neglects his will and does not keep his covenant, He will expel him from Paradise to the world, and fatigue and toil will befall him, which will relieve hunger, nakedness, thirst, and the sun's heat. So what is meant by misery is the misery of this world, as many commentators have said, not the misery of the next. Al-Farra’ said: It means that he eats from the work of his own hands. Abu Amr and the Kufians, except for Asim, read and that you are not thirsty with the fatha on an, and the rest read it with the kasra on the basis of conjunction with that you have.
20:120: 120- Then Satan whispered to him has been explained in Al-A'raf in His statement: Then Satan whispered to them meaning he conveyed his whispering to him, and the phrase He said, O Adam to the end is either a substitute for whispered or a new sentence with the assumption of a question as if it was said: So what did he say to him in his whispering? The tree of immortality is the tree from which whoever eats will never die, and a kingdom that will not decay meaning it will not disappear or end.
20:121: 121- So they ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them. The explanation of this and what follows has been presented in Al-A'raf. Al-Farra' said: The meaning of began in Arabic is approached, and it was said that they began to stick fig leaves to themselves. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray, meaning he disobeyed Him by eating from the tree. So went astray deviated from the right path or from what he wanted, which was immortality by eating from that tree. It was said that his life was ruined by his descent into the world, and it was said that he was ignorant of his right path, and it was said that he was intoxicated from eating too much. Ibn Qutaybah said: Adam ate from the tree from which he was forbidden because of Satan's deception and trickery of him, and his oath to him by God that he was among his sincere advisors until he led him astray with deception, and his sin was not due to a previous belief and correct intention, so we say: Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. End quote. Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: It is not permissible for anyone to say that today about Adam. I said: There is no objection to this after God informed us in His Book that he disobeyed Him, and as it is said, the good deeds of the righteous are the bad deeds of those who are close to Him. Among what I said in this regard: Abu Al-Alam's stick, he is the one from the clay that God formed him And the angels prostrate for him, and Paradise becomes his abode. Satan tempted him, so who am I, the poor thing? Satan tempted him.
20:122: 122- Then his Lord chose him meaning He selected him and brought him close. Ibn Furak said: The sin of Adam was before the prophethood, as evidenced by what is in this verse, for He mentioned the selection and guidance after mentioning the sin. If the sin was before the prophethood, then the sins are permissible for them in one way, Then He turned to him and guided him meaning He turned to him from his sin and guided him to remain steadfast in repentance. It was said that God's repentance for him was before he and Eve repented, when they said, Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers. The reason for Adam being mentioned specifically and not Eve has already been mentioned. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, or it causes them to remember meaning the Qur’an, with great seriousness and piety. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, and do not hasten with the Qur’an, “do not hasten until We make it clear to you.” Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: A man slapped his wife, so she came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, seeking retaliation. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made retaliation between them, then God revealed, and do not hasten with the Qur’an, the verse, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, paused until men are the protectors and maintainers of women, the verse was revealed. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, and do not hasten the verse. He said: Do not recite it to anyone until We complete it for you. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mandah in al-Tawhid, and al-Tabarani in al-Saghir, who authenticated it, narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He was called human because He was given a covenant and he forgot.
