Abd al-Ghani and Ibn Sa’d narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We had already made a covenant with Adam, not to approach the tree, but he forgot, so he abandoned My covenant, and We found on his part no firm will, meaning: to preserve it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, but he forgot, so he abandoned and We found on his part no firm will, meaning: We did not give him firm will. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, that you will neither thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun, meaning: you will not be afflicted by thirst or heat therein. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In Paradise there is a tree in the shade of which a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it, and it is the tree of eternity. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Adam argued with Moses. Moses said to him: ‘You are the one who expelled the people from Paradise because of your sin and made them miserable because of your disobedience.’ Adam said: ‘O Moses, you are the one whom God chose with His message and His speech. Do you blame me for something that God wrote for me before He created me, or decreed for me before He created me?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘So Adam argued with Moses.’”
20:123: His statement: 123- "He said, 'Descend both of you.'" Its interpretation has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah 2:meaning, descend from Paradise to Earth. God, the Exalted, made them both an enemy of Himself by descending because they are the origin of mankind. Then He generalized the address to them and their offspring, saying: "Some of you are enemies to one another." The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. It is permissible to say that He addressed them in this and what follows as a collective address, because they are the origin of the children. The meaning of "Some of you are enemies to one another" is their hostility to one another in matters of livelihood and the like. As a result of that, fighting and quarreling occur. "But if there comes to you guidance from Me, by sending messengers and revealing books, then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer," meaning he will neither go astray in this world nor suffer in the Hereafter.
20:124: 124- And whoever turns away from My remembrance meaning from My religion, the recitation of My Book, and acting in accordance with what is in it, and does not follow My guidance then indeed he will have a depressed life meaning he will have a depressed life in this world: meaning a narrow life. It is said: a depressed home and a depressed life, a source in which the singular and what is above it, the masculine and the feminine are the same. Antara said: If fate could be represented, it would be represented by me when they descend into a difficult home. It is read as dhanki with a dhammah on the letter Ḍād on the basis of faʿlā. The meaning of the verse is that God the Almighty has made for those who follow His guidance and adhere to His religion to live a comfortable life in this world, without worry or grief or tiring themselves out, as He the Almighty said: We will surely cause him to live a good life. And He has made for those who do not follow His guidance and turn away from His religion to live a narrow life, with fatigue and hardship. In addition to the troubles that befall him in this world, he will be more tired, more distressed and more tired in the Hereafter. This is the meaning of And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind, meaning robbed of his sight. It has been said that what is meant by blindness is the proof, and it has been said that blindness is to the directions of goodness and he is not guided to any of them. It has also been said that what is meant by a narrow life is the torment of the grave, and what supports and strengthens this will come.
20:125: 125- He said, ‘My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I used to have sight?’ in this world.
20:126: 126- "He said, 'Likewise.' That is, you did the same thing. Then He explained it by saying, 'Our signs came to you, but you forgot them.' That is, you turned away from them, abandoned them, and did not look into them. 'And thus today you are forgotten.' That is, like that forgetfulness that you did in this world, you are forgotten: that is, you are left in blindness and torment in the Fire. Al-Farra' said: It is said that he comes out of his grave with sight, but he is blind when he is resurrected.
20:127: 127- And thus do We recompense him who transgresses meaning, We will recompense him in the same way: transgression is immersion in desires, and it was said that it means polytheism and does not believe in the signs of his Lord rather he denied them and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe meaning, more terrible than a difficult life and more lasting meaning, more permanent and more established because it does not end. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Tabarani, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever follows the Book of God, God will guide him from misguidance in this world and protect him from a bad reckoning on the Day of Resurrection. This is because God says: So whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer. Al-Faryabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, `Abd ibn Humayd, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God will protect the one who follows the Qur’an from going astray in this world or suffering in the Hereafter. Then he recited: So whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer. He said: He will neither go astray in this world nor suffer in the Hereafter. Abdul Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Musaddad in his Musnad, Abdul bin Hameed, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, regarding his statement, a straitened life, he said: The torment of the grave. The wording of Abdul Razzaq is: His grave will be constricted for him until his ribs overlap. It has also been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Kathir said: The chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet is more authentic. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, ‘Then he will have a straitened life,’ he said: A straitened life is when ninety-nine snakes are set loose upon him, gnawing at his flesh until the Hour comes.” Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, Then he will have a straitened life, he said: A straitened life is when ninety-nine snakes are set loose upon him, gnawing at his flesh until the Hour comes. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, but longer. Ibn Kathir said: Its chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet is very strange. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding his statement: For him will be a miserable life, he said: The torment of the grave. Ibn Kathir said after narrating it: The chain of transmission is good. Hannad, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding his statement: For him will be a miserable life, he said: The torment of the grave. The sum of what we have mentioned here goes back to the interpretation of a miserable life as the torment of the grave. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in the book of the torment of the grave, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he interpreted a miserable life as misery. Hannad, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: And We shall gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind, he said: Everything will be blind to him except Hell. In another version: He will not see anything except the Fire. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sufyan regarding his statement: And thus do We recompense him who transgresses, he said: Whoever associates partners with God.
20:128: His statement: 128- Have they not been guided? The question is for rebuke and reprimand, and the fa is for connecting to something understood, as was mentioned more than once, and the sentence is resumed to confirm what came before it, and the subject of guides is the sentence mentioned after it, and the object is omitted. The Basrans rejected such a thing because sentences do not take the form of a subject, but others permitted it. Al-Qaffal said: He made the large number of generations that were destroyed clear to them. Al-Nahhas said: This is a mistake because kam is an interrogative, so what came before it does not work on it. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, Or did the command to destroy those whom We destroyed not guide them? Its true meaning indicates guidance, so the subject is guidance. He said, How many is in the accusative case with we destroyed. It was said that the subject of guide is a pronoun for God or the Messenger, and the sentence after it explains it. The meaning of the verse, as it appears, is: Has not the report of those whom We destroyed before them of the generations become clear to the people of Mecca? while the generations walk in their dwellings and move about in their homes, or while these people walk in the dwellings of the generations whom We destroyed when they go out to trade and seek a living, so they see the lands of the past nations, and the past generations empty and warring from the people of Al-Hijr and Thamud and the villages of the people of Lot, for that is what necessitates their consideration lest what happened to those happen to them. Ibn Abbas and Al-Salami read Nahd with a nun, and the meaning according to this reading is clear. The sentence, Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding is an explanation for the denial and a confirmation of guidance, and the reference by His saying that is to the meaning of how many We destroyed and so on. Prohibition: the plural of prohibition, which is the mind: that is, for those with minds that prohibit their owners from doing what is ugly.
20:129: 129- And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord meaning, and had it not been for the previous word, which is the promise of God, the Most High, to delay the punishment of this nation until the Hereafter, the punishment for their sins would have been binding meaning, binding upon them, and would not be separated from them under any circumstances and would not be delayed. His statement, and a specified term is conjoined with the word, as stated by Al-Zajjaj and others, and the specified term is the Day of Resurrection, or the Day of Badr, and binding is a source of binding. It was said that it is permissible to conjoin and a specified term with the hidden pronoun in was referring to the urgent taking understood from the context, in order to reduce the separation by the report to the level of emphasis: meaning, the urgent taking and a specified term would have been binding upon them as they were binding upon 'Aad and Thamud, and in that there is clear arbitrariness.
20:130: Then when God the Almighty made clear that He would not destroy them with the punishment of extermination, He commanded him to be patient, saying: 130- So be patient over what they say that you are a lying magician, and similar false accusations of theirs. The meaning is: Do not celebrate them, for their punishment has a set time that is neither advanced nor delayed. It was said that this was abrogated by the verse on fighting. And glorify the praises of your Lord meaning, be clothed in His praise. Most of the commentators said: What is meant are the five daily prayers, as is indicated by His statement: Before the rising of the sun for it is a reference to the dawn prayer, and before its setting for it is a reference to the afternoon prayer, and during the hours of the night is darkness, and what is meant by the hours is the hours, which is the plural of inna with a kasra and shortening, and it is an hour, and the meaning of so glorify is to separate, and the ends of the day meaning sunset and noon because noon is at the end of the first end of the day, and the beginning of the end of the other day. It was said that the reference to the noon prayer is in His saying: and before its setting because it is the same as the afternoon prayer before sunset. It was also said that what is meant by the verse is the voluntary prayer. If it was said that there is no reference in the verse to prayer but rather what is meant is glorification at these times: that is, the one who says Subhan God, that would not be far from the truth. And glorification at these times: that is, the one who says Subhan God, that would not be far from the truth. And glorification, even though it is applied to prayer, is a metaphor, and the truth is more appropriate except for an indication that diverts it to the metaphorical meaning. And the phrase perhaps you will be satisfied is related to His saying so glorify: that is, glorify at these times in the hope that you will attain from God the Almighty what pleases your soul. This is according to the reading of the majority. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Bakr from Asim read trḍā with a ḍamma on the ta’ in the passive form: that is, your Lord will be satisfied with you.
20:131: 131- "And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them." The interpretation of this verse has already been presented in Al-Hijr. The meaning is: Do not let your eyes gaze long. "Groups is the object of We have given enjoyment, and flower" is in the accusative case as a state, or with an omitted verb: i.e. We made or gave. Al-Zajjaj mentioned the meaning of this. It was said that it is a substitute for the "ha in bih in consideration of its position, which is the accusative, not in consideration of its wording, as it is in the genitive case, as you say, I passed by your brother. Al-Farra' preferred the accusative case as a state, and it is permissible for it to be a substitute, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a source, such as Sabghat God and Abdullah and Zahrat al-Hayat al-Dunya" its adornment and delight with plants and other things. Isa bin Omar read Zahra with the opening of the ha’, and it is the light of the plant, and the lam in lanfitnahum is related to tamatna: that is, to make that a trial and misguidance for them, a test from us for them, like His saying: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it that We may test them. It was said that it was to punish them, and it was said that it was to make the task difficult for them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. That is, the reward of God, and what He has stored for the righteous of His servants in the Hereafter is better than what He has provided for them in this world in any case. Also, that does not cease, and this does cease, and it is the meaning of and more lasting. And before that, what is meant by this provision is what God opens up for the believers of spoils and the like. The first is more appropriate because the realized goodness and the uninterrupted permanence are only realized in the provision of the Hereafter, not the provision of this world, even if it is lawful and good. What is with you will be exhausted, but what is with God is lasting.
20:132: 132- And enjoin prayer upon your family God the Almighty commanded him to command his family to pray, and what is meant by them is his household, and it was said that it was all of his nation, and the command from God to him to pray was not mentioned here, but rather the command was limited to his family, either because his establishment of it is a known command, or because his command to it had been mentioned previously in His statement: And glorify the praises of your Lord to the end of the verse, or because his command to command his family was a command to him, and for this reason He said: And be steadfast in it that is, be steadfast in prayer, and do not be distracted from it by anything of worldly matters We do not ask you for provision that is, we do not ask you to provide for yourself or your family, and to be distracted by that from prayer We provide for you and provide for them and do not charge you with that and the final outcome is for righteousness that is, the praiseworthy outcome, and it is Paradise for the righteous, with the deletion of the complement as Al-Akhfash said, and in it is evidence that righteousness is the essence of the matter and upon it the circles of good revolve.
20:133: 133- And they said, 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?' That is, the infidels of Mecca said: Why does Muhammad not bring us a sign from his Lord as the prophets before him used to bring? This is like the she-camel and the staff. Or why does Muhammad not bring us a sign from his Lord as the prophets before him used to bring? This is like the she-camel and the staff. Or why does he not bring us a sign from the signs that we have suggested to him? So God Almighty answered them by saying: Did there not come to them a clear proof of what was in the former scriptures? He means by the former scriptures the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and all the revealed books, in which there is a clear statement of his prophethood and glad tidings of his being brought. This is sufficient, for they acknowledge the truthfulness and authenticity of these revealed books, and in them is what refutes their denial of his prophethood and invalidates their stubbornness and arbitrariness. It was said that the meaning is: Or did not Our destruction of the nations who disbelieved and proposed signs come to them? So what assures them that if the signs they proposed come to them, their condition will not be the same as their condition? It was said that what is meant is: Or did not come to them a sign that is the mother of signs and the greatest of them in the chapter of miracles, meaning the Qur’an, for it is a proof for what is in all the revealed books. Abu Ja’far, Shaibah, Nafi’, Abu Amr, Ya’qub, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Hafs read or did not come to them with the upper ta’, and the rest read it with the lower ta’ because the meaning of bayyinah is clarification and proof, so they mentioned the verb in consideration of the meaning of bayyinah, and this reading was chosen by Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. Al-Kisa’i said: Bayyinah with the tanween is permissible. Al-Nahhas said: If you put the tanween of bayyinah and raise it, you make ma a substitute for it, and if you put it in the accusative, it is in the state. The meaning is: Or did not come to them what is in the first scriptures made clear, and this is according to what grammatical permissibility requires, even if the reading is not done with it.
20:134: 134- And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it meaning before the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or before the evidence for the revelation of the Qur'an came, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection, Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger? meaning why did You not send us a messenger in this world so we could have followed Your signs that the messenger brings before we are humiliated by the punishment in this world and disgraced by entering the Fire. It was read humiliated and disgraced in the passive form, and God cut off the excuse of these disbelievers by sending the messenger to them before their destruction, and for this reason God narrated about them that they said, 'Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied and said, God has not sent down anything.'
20:135: 135- Say, 'Every one of you is waiting, so wait.' That is, say to them, O Muhammad, every one of us and you is waiting: that is, waiting for what will happen, so wait. Then you will know soon who are the companions of the straight path. That is, you will know by victory and the outcome who are the companions of the straight path. And who is guided from misguidance and removed from error. Min in both places is in the nominative case as a subject. An-Nahhas said: Al-Farra' believes that the meaning of of the companions of the straight path is he who has not gone astray, and that the meaning of who is guided is he who went astray and then was guided. It was said that Min in both places is in the accusative case, and this is what Al-Farra' said. It was narrated from Az-Zajjaj that he said: This is a mistake because what precedes it does not affect the question. Abu Rafi’ read you will know and Yahya bin Ya’mar and Asim al-Jahdari al-Suway read fa’ili. This reading was rejected because the feminine of sirat is irregular, and it was said that it means the middle and justice. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Have they not been guided “Have We not made clear to them” How many generations We destroyed before them who walked in their dwellings such as Aad and Thamud and whomever We destroyed of the nations” and regarding his statement, And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable and a term appointed he says this is from the introductions of speech, he says had it not been for a word and a term appointed, it would have been inevitable. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi something similar. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The term appointed is the word that preceded from your Lord. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas It would have been inevitable he said death. Al-Faryabi, Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And glorify the praises of your Lord the verse he said: It is the obligatory prayer. At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun, he said: Before the rising of the sun is the dawn prayer, and before its setting is the afternoon prayer. In the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Jarir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You will see your Lord as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able to avoid being overcome from praying before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so.” And he recited: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. In Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud and An-Nasa’i on the authority of ‘Ammarah ibn Ru’bah, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No one who prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will enter the Fire. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Rahawayh, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Kharaiti and Abu Na`im narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi` who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hosted a guest, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not have anything to provide for him, so he sent me to a Jewish man to sell or lend us flour until the crescent of Rajab. He said: ‘No, not unless we provide a pledge.’ So I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him, and he said: ‘By God, I am trustworthy in heaven and trustworthy on earth. If he lends me or sells me, I will pay him back. Go with my new armor.’ I did not leave him until this verse was revealed: ‘And do not extend your eyes. ’” As if he was consoling him about the world. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What I fear most for you is what God will open for you of the adornments of this world. They said: What are the adornments of this world, O Messenger of God? He said: The blessings of the earth. Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Asakir and Ibn Al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri who said: When the verse, And enjoin prayer upon your family, was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would come to Ali’s door for the morning prayer for eight months and say: Prayer, may God have mercy on you. God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Al-Hamra. Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu’ab on the authority of Thabit who said: “Whenever the Prophet’s family was afflicted with hardship, he would call out to them: ‘O my family, pray, pray.’” Thabit said: Whenever a matter befell the prophets, they would rush to prayer. Abu Ubaid, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, At-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Abu Nu’aym in Al-Hilyah and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu’ab narrated with a chain of transmission that As-Suyuti said is sound on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam who said: Whenever hardship or distress befell the Prophet’s family, he would command them to pray, and he would recite the verse, And enjoin prayer upon your family.
21:1: It is Meccan. Al-Qurtubi said in the opinion of everyone that it is one hundred and twelve verses. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: The Children of Israel, the Cave, Mary, and the Prophets are among the first to be freed, and they are from my lineage. Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym narrated in Al-Hilyah on the authority of `Amir ibn Rabi`ah that an Arab man stayed there, and `Amir treated him with great respect and spoke to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about him. The man came to him and said: I have given the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) a valley better than which there is no valley in Arabia, and I wanted to give you a piece of it for you and your descendants from your slave. `Amir said: I have no need of your piece of land. Today a surah was revealed that has made us forget the world. The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away. It is said that something is near and has drawn near, and the reckoning has drawn near: meaning the time in which they will be held accountable has drawn near. Al-Zajjaj said: Meaning 1- The time of their reckoning has drawn near for the people, meaning the Resurrection, as in His statement: The Hour has drawn near. The lam in for the people is related to the verb, and it and its object are brought before the subject to create awe. The meaning of the time of reckoning drawing near is its approach to them, because it is closer to them every hour than the hour before it. It was also said that everything that is coming is near, and the death of every person is the time of his resurrection, and the Resurrection is also near in comparison to what has passed of time, so what remains of this world is less than what has passed, and what is meant by the people is all. It was said that it is the polytheists in general, and it was said that it is the infidels of Mecca. Based on this, it was said that what is meant by the reckoning is their punishment on the Day of Badr, and the phrase and they are in heedlessness turning away is in the accusative case as a state: meaning that they are in heedlessness of this world turning away from the Hereafter, not prepared for what is required of them of faith in God, performing His obligations, and refraining from His prohibitions.
21:2: 2- "Whatever reminder comes to them from their Lord is newly created" from the beginning of the goal, and the description of the reminder as newly created has been used as evidence that the Qur'an is newly created, because the reminder here is the Qur'an. It was answered that there is no dispute about the occurrence of the combination of sounds and letters, because it is renewed in its revelation. So the meaning is that its revelation is newly created, and the dispute is in the psychological speech, and this issue: I mean the antiquity of the Qur'an and its occurrence has been afflicted by many people of knowledge and virtue in the Ma'mun, Mu'tasim and Wathiqiya states, and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal suffered what happened of severe beating and long imprisonment, and because of it Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Khuza'i was beheaded, and it became a great tribulation at that time and after, and the story is more famous than to mention, and whoever wants to know its truth should read the biography of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in the book of the nobles by the historian of Islam, al-Dhahabi. The Imams of the Sunnah were right in their refusal to answer those who say that the Qur’an is created and that it occurred, and God protected the nation of His Prophet from innovation through them. However, may God have mercy on them, they went beyond that to declaring as an unbeliever whoever says that the utterance of the Qur’an is created. Rather, they went beyond that to declaring as an unbeliever whoever stopped. I wish they had not gone beyond the limit of stopping and referring knowledge to the Knower of the Unseen, because nothing was heard from the righteous predecessors from the Companions and the Followers and those after them until the time of the ordeal and the emergence of the statement on this issue, nor was a word transmitted from them on that. So, refraining from answering what they called for, and adhering to the tails of stopping, and referring knowledge of that to its Knower is the best way, and in it is safety and freedom from declaring as unbelievers groups of God’s servants, and the matter is up to God, the Most High. His statement, except that they listen to it, is an empty exception in the accusative case as a state, and the phrase, while they are playing, is also in the accusative case as a state from the subject of listen to it.
21:3: And 3- Their hearts are distracted is also a state, and the meaning is: What comes to them of remembrance from their Lord is new in any state except in listening with play and mockery and the distraction of the hearts. And Lahia was read with the nominative case just as Muhaddith was read with the nominative case. And those who wronged whispered secretly. Whispering is a noun from whispering, and whispering can only be secret, so the meaning of whispering secretly is: exaggeration in concealment. There are different opinions about the position of the relative pronoun: It was said that it is in the nominative case as a substitute for the waw in asraw, as Al-Mubarrad and others said. It was said that it is in the nominative case as a blameworthy statement. It was said that it is the subject of a deleted verb, and the meaning is: Those who did wrong say, and Al-Nahhas chose this. It was said that it is in the accusative case with the meaning of I mean. It was said that it is in the genitive case as a substitute for people, as Al-Mubarrad mentioned. It was said that it is in the nominative case as the subject of asraw, according to the language of those who allow combining two subjects: like their saying the fleas ate me, as Al-Akhfash mentioned. Similar to it is then many of them became blind and deaf. From this is the saying of the poet: The mules were guided to the destinations. And the other said: But his father and mother came to Hauran, squeezing the blood of his relatives. Al-Kisa'i said: It has an inversion: that is, those who did wrong kept their secrets secret. Abu Ubaidah said: Here, they kept their secrets is one of the opposites: it may mean that they concealed their speech, and it may mean that they showed it and declared it. Is this anything but a human being like you? This sentence is estimated as the statement before it: that is, they said, Is this Messenger anything but a human being like you, who is not distinguished from you in anything? It is possible that this sentence is a substitute for the secret conversation, and is means negation: that is, they kept this conversation secret. The hamza in Do you then practice magic? is for denial, and the fa' is for conjunction with something estimated like its counterparts, and the sentence and you see is in the accusative case as a state. The meaning is: If he is a human being like you, and what he brought was magic, then how do you respond to him and follow him? So he informed his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what they were whispering about.
21:4: And God, the Most High, commanded him to answer them, so He said: 4- He said, ‘My Lord knows what is said in the heaven and the earth,’ meaning nothing that is said in them is hidden from Him. And in the copies of the Mushafs of the people of Kufa, My Lord said, meaning Muhammad said: My Lord knows what is said, so He is All-Knowing of what you whispered to Him. It was said that the first reading is better, because they kept this saying secret, so God informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that and commanded him to say this to them. An-Nahhas said: Both readings are correct, and they are like two verses, And He is the All-Hearing of everything that He hears, the All-Knowing of everything known, so what they kept secret is included in that primarily.
21:5: 5- Rather, they said, 'Confused dreams' Al-Zajjaj said: That is, they said that what he brings is confused dreams. Al-Qatibi said: Confused dreams are false visions. Al-Yazidi said: Confused dreams are what have no interpretation. This is a diversion from God, the Exalted, narrating what happened from them, and a transition from narrating their previous statement to narrating this statement. Then God, the Exalted, narrated their diversion from their statement: Confused dreams. He said: Rather, he invented it, that is, they said he invented it of his own accord without it having any basis. Then God, the Exalted, narrated from them that they diverted from this and said, Rather, he is a poet and what he brought is of the type of poetry. In this confusion from them, and their changing colors and hesitation is the greatest evidence that they are ignorant of the truth of what he brought. They do not know what it is nor do they understand its essence? Or they knew that it was true and that it was from God, but they wanted to push it away and throw every stone and mortar at it. This is the way of one who is overcome by argument and subdued by evidence. Then after all this, they said: Then let him bring us a sign. This is the answer to an omitted condition: that is, whoever is as we said: Then let him bring us a sign, just as the former ones were sent. That is, just as Moses was sent with the staff and other things, and Salih with the she-camel. The position of the kaf is the accusative as an attribute of the sign, and it is possible that it is an attribute of an omitted source. Their question was a question of stubbornness, because God, the Exalted, had given them enough signs, and if God, the Exalted, had known that they would believe if He gave them what they suggested, He would have given them that, as He said: “And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse.” Al-Zajjaj said: They proposed signs that do not require respite.
21:6: So God said in response to them 6- No city believed before them meaning before the polytheists of Mecca: The meaning of from a city is from the people of a city, and the description of the city by saying: We destroyed it means we destroyed its people, or we destroyed it by destroying its people, and in it is a statement that the law of God with the previous nations is that if the proposers were given what they proposed, and then did not believe, the punishment of extermination would inevitably descend upon them, and the from in from a city is added for emphasis. The meaning is: No city believed from the cities that we destroyed because of their proposal before these, so how can we give them what they propose, and they are an example for those before them, and the hamza in do they understand that they believe is for rebuke and rebuke, and the meaning is: If a nation from the destroyed nations did not believe when they were given what they proposed, then how will these people believe if they were given what they proposed.
21:7: Then the Almighty answered their saying: Is this anything but a human being like you by saying: 7- And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed meaning, We did not send before you to the previous nations except men from among the human beings, and We did not send angels to them as the Almighty said: Say, 'If there were on the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger' and the phrase inspired to them is a new sentence to explain the manner of sending, and it is possible that it is a description of men: meaning described by the quality of revelation to them. Hafs, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read inspired with a noon, and the rest read it with a ya below. Then God commanded them to ask the people of the Reminder if they were ignorant of this, so He said: So ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know and the people of the Reminder are the people of the two books: the Jews and the Christians, and the meaning of if you do not know: if you do not know that the messengers of God are from among the human beings, as most of the commentators said. The Jews and Christians were not ignorant of this nor did they deny it. The meaning of the statement is: If you do not know what has been mentioned, then ask the people of knowledge. The verse has been used as evidence that imitation is permissible, but it is a mistake. If it were accepted, the meaning would be to ask them about the texts from the Book and the Sunnah, not about pure opinion. Imitation is nothing but accepting the statement of another without his proof. We have explained this in a simple message: we called it The Useful Statement on the Ruling on Imitation.
21:8: Then when He finished answering their doubt, He confirmed that the messengers were from the human race, saying: 8- And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food meaning that the messengers are an example for all other individuals of the children of Adam in the rule of nature, they eat as they eat and drink, and the body is the human body. Al-Zajjaj said: It is one, meaning the body indicates a group: meaning, We did not make them with bodies that do not eat food, so the phrase do not eat food is an attribute of the body: meaning, We did not make them a body that does not need food, rather it is in need of that. And they were not immortal rather they die as other humans die, and they believed that the messengers do not die, so God answered them with this.
21:9: And the sentence 9- Then We fulfilled the promise to them is connected to a sentence indicated by the context, and the meaning is: We revealed to them what We revealed, then We fulfilled the promise to them: that is, We fulfilled the promise that We promised them by saving them and destroying those who denied them, and for this reason the Almighty said: Then We saved them and whomever We willed of Our believing servants, and what is meant is saving them from the punishment and destroying those who disbelieved in the worldly punishment, and what is meant by the extravagant are those who exceed the limit in disbelief and sins, and they are the polytheists. Al-Nasa'i narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And they are in heedlessness turning away, he said: In this world. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the verse, he said: Of the affairs of this world. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: Rather, they said, 'Confused dreams,' meaning, he did the dreaming, but it is a vision he saw. "Rather, he invented it. Rather, he is a poet." All of this was from him. Then let him bring us a sign as the former ones were sent, as Jesus and Moses came with clear proofs and messengers. No town we destroyed before them believed, meaning that when the messengers came to their people with clear proofs and they did not believe, they were not given respite. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: The people of Mecca said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If what you say is true and you are pleased for us to believe, then turn Safa into gold for us. Gabriel came to him and said: If you wish, what your people asked of you will happen, but if they do not believe, then they will not be given respite. If you wish, you may wait until your people arrive. He said: Rather, I will wait until my people arrive. Then God revealed: I did not believe before them 1:10. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, meaning: We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, rather We made them bodies that ate food.
21:10: He alerted His servants to His great blessing upon them by saying: 10- Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book meaning the Qur'an in which is your remembrance as an attribute of the Book, and what is meant by remembrance here is honor: that is, in it is your honor, as in His saying: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people and it was said: in it is your remembrance: that is, the remembrance of the matter of your religion, the rulings of your law, and what you will attain of reward or punishment, and it was said in it is your speech. This was said by Mujahid. And it was said in it is your noble morals and good deeds. And it was said in it is working with what is in your life. This was said by Sahl ibn Abdullah. And it was said in it is your admonition, and the question in His saying Do you not understand is for rebuke and reprimand: that is, do you not understand that the matter is thus, or do you not understand any of the things that include what was mentioned.
21:11: Then He threatened them and warned them about what happened to the nations that denied, saying: 11- And how many a city have We destroyed which was unjust. How much is in the accusative case as the object of we destroyed, and it is the report that indicates abundance. Qasam is the breaking and crushing of something. It is said: Qasam dahr so-and-so if you break it, and Aqtasam sinah if you break it. The meaning here is: destruction and torment. As for fasam with fa, it is the cracking in something without separation. The phrase was unjust is in the genitive case as an attribute of qaryah, and in the speech there is an omitted complement: that is, and for you, We destroyed from the people of a city which was unjust: that is, disbelieving in God and denying His signs. Injustice in origin is placing something in the wrong place, and they placed disbelief in the place of faith. And We brought forth after it another people, that is, We created and brought into being after the destruction of its people, a people who were not from it.
21:12: 12- When they sensed Our might meaning they realized or saw Our punishment. Al-Akhfash said: They feared and expected, or the might is the severe punishment. At once they were running from it. Running means fleeing, escaping, and being defeated. Its origin is from the man running the animal with his legs. It is said that the horse ran if he trampled them with their legs, then it became common until it was said that the horse ran if it galloped. From this, Run with your foot and the meaning is: that they flee from it running their animals.
21:13: It was said to them: 13- "Do not run" meaning do not flee. It was said that the angels called out to them when they fled. It was also said that those who said that to them were the believers there, mocking and ridiculing them. "And return to what you were enjoying in luxury" meaning to your blessings that were the cause of your arrogance and disbelief. The luxurious is the one who is pampered, it is said that someone was pampered: meaning he was given ample living "and your dwellings meaning return to the dwellings that you used to live in and boast about so that you may ask" meaning that you may go to ask, consult, and plan important matters, and this is in the way of mocking and rebuking them. It was also said that the meaning is: perhaps you will ask about the punishment that has befallen you so that you may be informed about it. It was also said that perhaps you will ask to believe as you used to ask before the punishment befell you. The commentators and historians said: What is meant by this verse are the people of Hadhur from Yemen, and God Almighty had sent to them a prophet named Shuaib bin Mahdam, and his grave is in a mountain in the mountains of Yemen called Dhain, and between it and Hadhur is about a distance. They said: He is not Shuaib, the owner of Madyan. I said: The traces of the grave are present in Jabal Dhain, and the common people of that area claim that it is the grave of Qadam bin Qadam.
21:14: 14- They said, ‘Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers.’ That is, when the angels said to them, Do not run! Woe to us! that is, by destroying us, we were wrongdoers to ourselves and deserved punishment for what we had done. So they admitted to themselves the wrongdoing that necessitated punishment.
21:15: 15- "And that was their call" meaning this word was still their call: meaning their call, and the word is their saying, "Oh woe to us meaning they call with it and repeat it until We made them a harvest meaning with swords as crops are harvested with a sickle, and the harvest here means the harvested, and the meaning of extinguished is that they are dead, from the word khamada" meaning the fire is extinguished, so he likened the extinction of life to the extinction of fire, as it is said of someone who has died, it has been extinguished.
21:16: 16- And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play. That is, We did not create them in vain or in vain, but rather to draw attention to the fact that they have a powerful Creator whose command must be obeyed. It contains a general reference to the creation of the world, and what is meant by what is between them is all the creatures existing between the heaven and the earth, with their different types and different kinds.
21:17: 17- If We had wanted to take a diversion. Diversion is that which is used for amusement. It was said that diversion is the wife and the child, and it was said that it is the wife only, and it was said that it is the child only. Al-Jawhari said: Diversion may be used as a metaphor for sexual intercourse, and what he said is indicated by the saying of Imru' al-Qais: Didn't you claim today that I have grown old and that people like me don't enjoy playing? And from it the other said: And there is a place for friends and a view The sentence is resumed to confirm the content of what preceded it, and the answer to if is his saying: We would have taken him from Our presence meaning from Our presence and from Our power, not from you. The commentators said: meaning from the houris, and in this there is a response to those who said that a companion and a son are attributed to God, may He be exalted far above that. It was said that he intended to respond to those who said: the idols or the angels are daughters of God. Ibn Qutaybah said: The verse is a response to the Christians If We were to do Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: We were not to do. Al-Farra’, Al-Mubarrad and Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that if is for negation as the commentators mentioned: meaning we did not do that and we did not take a companion or a son. It is also possible that it is for a condition: meaning if we were among those who would do that, We would have taken him from Our presence. Al-Farra’ said: This of the two interpretations is more similar to the Arabic language doctrine.
21:18: 18- Rather, We cast the truth upon falsehood. This is a refutation of taking amusement: that is, leave what they said, for it is a lie and falsehood. Rather, our way is to cast the truth upon falsehood. And for you is woe for what you describe. That is, the torment in the Hereafter because of your describing it with what is not permissible for it. It is said that woe is a valley in Hell, and it is a threat to the Quraysh that they will have the same torment as those people. Who is the causal particle.
21:19: 19- And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth as slaves and kings, and He is their Creator, Provider and Owner, so how is it permissible for some of His creations to have a partner who is worshipped as He is worshipped, and this sentence confirms what preceded it and from Him meaning the angels, and in it is a response to those who say that the angels are daughters of God, and in the expression of them being with is an indication of their honor and dignity, and that they are in the position of those brought near to kings, then He described them by saying: They are not too proud to worship Him meaning they are not arrogant nor are they disdainful of worshipping God Almighty and submitting to Him nor are they weary meaning they do not become exhausted, taken from the word hasir, which is a camel that is exhausted and tired, it is said: the camel became weary, it became weary and exhausted, and he became weary and weary like him and his weary I am weary, transitive and intransitive. Abu Zaid said: They do not tire. Ibn al-A'rabi said: They do not lose heart. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse is that those whom you mentioned are the sons of God, the servants of God, and they do not disdain to worship Him nor do they feel arrogant about it, like His saying: Indeed, those who are with your Lord are not too proud to worship Him. It was said that the meaning is: They do not cease from worshipping Him, and these meanings are close.
21:20: 20- They glorify God night and day, never slackening. That is, they always glorify God Almighty, never weakening or getting tired of that. It was also said that they pray day and night. Al-Zajjaj said: The flow of glorification from them is like the flow of the breath from us, nothing distracts us from the breath, so their glorification is constant. This sentence is either a new sentence in response to an implied question, or in the accusative case as a state.
21:21: 21- Or have they taken gods from the earth? Al-Mufaddal said: The purpose of this question is denial: that is, have they not taken gods who are able to bring back to life? And Am is the disconnected one, and the hamza is for denying the occurrence. Al-Mubarrad said: Am here means hal: that is, have these polytheists taken gods from the earth who bring the dead back to life? And Am here does not mean rather, because that would require them to create the dead unless Am is understood with the question, in which case Am is the disconnected one, so the meaning is correct. And from the earth is related to they took, or to an omitted word that is an attribute of the gods. The meaning of they resurrect is that they resurrect the dead, and the sentence is an attribute of the gods, and this sentence is the one that revolves around denial and ignorance, not the taking itself, because it will inevitably happen from them. The meaning is: Rather, they took gods from the earth, they in particular, despite their insignificance, who resurrect the dead, and this is not the case, because what they took as gods is separate from that. The majority read yanshrūn with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the sheen from anshrūhu: meaning he brought him back to life. Al-Hasan read it with a fatha on the ya’: meaning they bring him back to life and do not die.
21:22: Then He, the Almighty, established the proof of the invalidity of polytheism, saying: 22- If there were within them gods besides God, they both would have been ruined. That is, if there were in the heavens and the earth gods worshipped other than God, they would have been ruined: that is, they would have been nullified, meaning the heavens and the earth with what is in them of creatures. Al-Kisa'i, Sibawayh, Al-Akhfash, Al-Zajjaj, and the majority of grammarians said: Except here is not for exception, but rather means other as an attribute of gods. Therefore, the noun that follows it was raised and the i'rab of other that came with its meaning appeared in it. From this is the saying of the poet: Every brother who leaves his brother, by your father's life, except Al-Farqadhan Al-Farra’ said: Except here means other than, and the meaning is: If there were gods in them other than God, they would both be corrupted. The reason for the corruption is that having another god with God would necessitate that each one of them be able to control his actions, and then conflict and disagreement would occur, and corruption would result from that. So glory be to God, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe. The fa is to arrange what comes after it based on what comes before it of establishing oneness by proof: that is, He, the Almighty, is far removed from what is not befitting of Him, such as establishing a partner for Him. In it is guidance for the servants to purify the Lord, glory be to Him, from what is not befitting of Him.
21:23: 23- He is not questioned about what He does. This sentence is a resumption, explaining that due to the strength of His authority and the greatness of His majesty, none of His creation asks Him about anything of His judgment and destiny. And they, meaning the servants, are questioned about what they do, meaning God asks them about that because they are His servants. It was said that the meaning is that He, glory be to Him, is not held accountable for His actions, but they are held accountable. It was said that what is meant by this is that He, glory be to Him, explained to His servants that whoever is questioned about his actions, such as Christ and the angels, is not fit to be a god.
21:24: 24- "Or have they taken other gods besides Him?" That is, rather, they have taken, and in it there is a transition and a shift from showing the invalidity of their being gods with the previous proof to showing the invalidity of taking them as gods while rebuking them by asking them for proof. For this reason, He said, "Say, 'Bring your proof'" on the claim that they are gods, or on the permissibility of taking other gods besides God, and they have no way to anything of that, neither from reason nor transmission, because the proof of reason has been explained previously. As for the proof of transmission, He referred to it by saying, "This is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me," that is, this revelation that came regarding monotheism that includes the conclusive proof, the reminder of my nation and the reminder of the previous nations, and I have established it for you and made it clear to you, so establish your proof. It was said that the meaning is: This is the Qur'an and these books that were revealed before me, so look, is there in any of them that God commanded taking a god besides Him. Al-Zajjaj said: It was said to them: Bring your proof that a messenger from the messengers informed his nation that they have a god other than God. Is there any mention of those with me and those before me other than the oneness of God? It was said that the meaning of the statement is a threat and a warning: that is, do whatever you want, for soon the veil will be lifted. Abu Hatim narrated that Yahya bin Ya'mar and Talhah bin Musarraf read: "This is a mention of those with me and a mention of those before me" with the tanween and the kasra on the meem, and he claimed that there is no basis for this reading. Al-Zajjaj said in explaining this reading that the meaning is this is a mention of what was revealed to me and what is with me and a mention of those before me. It was said that a mention of those who were before me: that is, I came with what the prophets before me came with. Then when the proof was directed at them, He blamed them for their ignorance of the places of truth, so He said: "Rather, most of them do not know the truth." This is a digression from His side, glory be to Him, and a transition from rebuking them by demanding proof from them to explaining that establishing proof does not affect them because they are ignorant of the truth and cannot distinguish between it and falsehood. Ibn Muhaisin and Al-Hasan read Al-Haqq in the nominative case, meaning this is the truth, or it is the truth. The phrase they are turning away is an explanation of what came before it, that most of them do not know: that is, because of this ignorance that has taken hold of most of them, they are turning away from accepting the truth, continuing to turn away from monotheism and following the Messenger, so they do not contemplate an argument, nor do they ponder a proof, nor do they reflect on evidence.
21:25: 25- "And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him. Hafs, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read We revealed with a nun, and the rest read with a ya": meaning We revealed to him "that there is no god but Me." In this is a confirmation of the matter of monotheism and an emphasis on what came before in His statement: "This is a reminder of those with me. And He concluded the verse with the command to His servants to worship Him, so He said, So worship Me." So the evidence of reason and the evidence of transmission have become clear to you, and the proof of God has been established against you. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your mention, he said: Your honor. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding the verse: In it is your hadith. And in a narration on his authority: In it is your religion. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: God sent a prophet from Himyar called Shu`ayb, and a slave jumped up to him and struck him with a stick, then Bukhtanasr marched to them and fought them and killed them until nothing remained of them, and about them God revealed: And how many a town have We destroyed, up to His statement: inactive. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Kalbi regarding his statement: And how many a town have We destroyed, he said: They are the settlements of Banu Azd. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr regarding his statement: And return to that in which you were luxuriant, he said: Return to your homes and your wealth. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And that was their claim, he said: They were the people of Hadrat who had killed their prophet, so God sent Bukhtanasr upon them and killed them. And regarding his statement: We made them like a harvest harvested and extinguished, he said: The angels struck their faces with the sword until they returned to their dwellings. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Wahb who said: A man from Al-Jazari told me: Yemen had two villages, one of them was called Hadhur and the other Qalabah. They were arrogant and luxurious to the point that they would not close their doors. When they became luxurious, God sent a prophet to them and he called them, so they killed him. God put it in the heart of Nebuchadnezzar to attack them, so he prepared an army for them. They fought them and defeated his army, so they returned to him defeated. He prepared another army against them, larger than the first, and they also defeated them. When Nebuchadnezzar saw that, he attacked them himself. They fought them and defeated them until they ran out of it. They heard a caller saying: Do not run, but return to your luxurious life and your dwellings. So they returned, and they heard a voice calling out: Oh, revenge for the Prophet. So they were killed with the sword. It is the one about which God said: And how many a city have We destroyed until His saying extinct. I said: The villages of Hadhur are now well-known, between them and the city of Sana’a, about a mile to the west of it. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, A harvest that is extinguished, he said: Like the extinguishing of fire when it is extinguished. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement, If We had intended to take a diversion, he said: Diversion is children. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, If We had intended to take a diversion, he said: Women. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, nor will they regret, he said: They will not return. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement, He will not be questioned about what He does, he said: with His servants, and they will be questioned, he said: about their deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak something similar. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: There are no people on earth more hateful to me than the Qadarites, and that is only because they do not know the power of God. God says, He will not be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
21:26: His statement: 26- And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.' These people who said this are Khuza'ah, for they said that the angels are daughters of God. It was also said that they are the Jews. It is correct to apply the verse to anyone who attributes a son to God. The Jews said: Ezra is the son of God, and the Christians said: The Messiah is the son of God, and a group of Arabs said: The angels are daughters of God. Then God, the Almighty, cleared Himself of this and said: Glory be to Him, meaning, clearing Him of that, and it is said on the tongues of the servants. Then He struck out at their statement and invalidated it, saying, Rather, they are honored servants, meaning they are not as they said, rather they are servants of God, the Almighty, honored by His honoring them, brought near to Him. It was read with emphasis, and Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra' permitted the accusative of servants to mean: Rather, He has taken servants.
21:27: Then He described them with another attribute, saying: 27- They do not precede Him in speech meaning they do not say anything until He says it or commands them to do so. This is what Ibn Qutaybah and others said, and in this is evidence of the perfection of their obedience and submission. It was read They do not precede Him with a damma on the ba' from they preceded Him "and they do by His command" meaning they are the ones who do what God commands them to do, following Him and obeying their Lord.
21:28: 27- He knows what is before them and what is behind them. This sentence is an explanation of what preceded it: that is, He knows what they have done and what they will do, or He knows what is before them, which is the Hereafter, and what is behind them, which is this world. The reason for the explanation is that if they knew that He knows what they have done and what they have left behind, they would not do any action or say any word except by His command. And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased. That is, the intercessors intercede for him, which is the one with whom He is pleased. It was said that they are the people of There is no god but God. It has been proven in the Sahih that the angels intercede in the Hereafter. And they are fearful of His fear. That is, of their fear of Him. So the source is added to the object, and fear is fear of glorification, and fear is fear of expectation and caution: that is, they are not safe from the deception of God.
21:29: 29- And whoever among them says, 'I am a god besides Him' meaning whoever among the angels says, I am a god besides God. The commentators said: He meant Iblis by this, because none of the angels said, I am a god except Iblis. It was also said that the reference is to all the prophets. That one, We will recompense with Hell. That is, that one who said it, hypothetically and estimatingly: We will recompense him with Hell because of this statement that he said, just as We recompense other criminals. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers. That is, We recompense the wrongdoers with a similar terrible recompense, or just as We made the recompense of this one who said Hell, so also do We recompense the wrongdoers who place divinity and worship in the wrong place. What is meant by the wrongdoers are the polytheists.
21:30: 30- Have not those who disbelieved seen? The hamza is for denial, and the waw is for connecting to the implied, and the vision is the heart: that is, have they not thought or did they not know that the heavens and the earth were joined together? Al-Akhfash said: He only said were because they are two types, that is, the two groups of the heavens and the earths, as the Almighty said: Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist. Al-Zajjaj said: He only said were because he refers to the heavens with the singular word, because the heavens were one heaven, and so are the earths. And was is the opposite of was, it is said was the was of was, was, was, was, meaning it was joined together. And from this comes was for the joined space: meaning that they were one thing stuck together, then God separated them. And he said was and did not say was because it is a source, and the estimate is: they were two entities of was, and the meaning of was "was was, was", meaning we separated some of them from each other, so we raised The sky, and We kept the earth in its place. And We made from water every living thing. That is, We gave life with the water that We send down from the sky to every thing, including animals and plants. The meaning is that water is the cause of life for everything. It was said that what is meant by water here is sperm, and most of the commentators said the same. This is an argument against the polytheists with the power of God Almighty and the wonder of His creation. The interpretation of this verse has been presented, and the hamza in Will they not then believe? is to denounce them, since they did not believe despite the existence of what requires it from the divine signs.
21:31: 31- And We placed on the earth firm mountains meaning fixed mountains lest it should shift with them “moving” means moving and rotating, meaning so that it does not move and rotate with them, or because that is disliked. The explanation of that has already been given in full in An-Nahl. And We placed therein meaning on the firm mountains, or on the earth passes Abu Ubaidah said: They are paths. Al-Zajjaj said: Everything that passes between two mountains is a pass. Paths is an explanation of the passes, because a pass may not be a passable, well-traveled road so that they may be guided to the interests of their livelihood and what their needs call for.
21:32: 32- And We have made the sky a protected ceiling from falling and crashing to the ground, as in His statement: And He holds back the sky from falling to the earth. Al-Farra' said: Protected by the stars from Satan, as in His statement: And We have protected it from every outcast devil. It was said that protected does not need a pillar, and it was said that what is meant by protected here is the elevated one, and it was said that it is protected from polytheism and sins, and it was said that it is protected from destruction and demolition. And they turn away from its signs. He attributed the signs to the sky, because they are placed in it, and that is like the sun and the moon and the like, and the meaning of turning away is that they do not contemplate it, nor do they think about what it requires of faith.
21:33: 33- And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon This is a reminder to them of another blessing that He bestowed upon them, which is that He created for them the night to rest in, and the day to manage their livelihoods, and He created the sun and the moon, meaning He made the sun a sign of the day, and the moon a sign of the night, so that they would know the number of months and the reckoning as was explained previously in Subhan Each in an orbit is swimming meaning each one of the sun, moon and stars is in an orbit swimming: meaning they run in the middle of the orbit, and move quickly like a swimmer in water, and the plural in the verb is based on the rising places, Sibawayh said: Because He informed about them with the action of one who has reason, and made them in obedience like one who has reason, He made the pronoun about them the pronoun of rational beings, and He did not say they swim or she swims, and Al-Farra' said the same. Al-Kisa'i said: He only said they swim because it is the beginning of a sign, and the orbits of the stars, and the root of the word is from rotation, and from it the spindle's orbit for its rotation.
21:34: 34- And We have not granted to any human being before you immortality meaning perpetual life in this world. So if you die at your inevitable end, are they the immortals? meaning the immortals will understand: Al-Farra' said: The letter fa was used to indicate the condition because it is the answer to their saying He will die. He said: It is permissible to delete the letter fa or to imply it, and the meaning is: If you die, they will also die, so there is no gloating over death. Matt was read with a kasra or a damma on the mim in two dialects: The reason for the revelation of this verse was the saying of the polytheists, as God related from them: Or do they say, 'A poet, we are waiting for him to be struck by a misfortune of time?'
21:35: 35- Every soul will taste death meaning it will taste the separation from its body, so no created soul will remain, whoever it may be. And We test you with evil and good as trial meaning We test you with hardship and ease, to see how grateful and patient you are. What is meant is that He, the Almighty, treats them as those who test you, and trial is a source for We will test you without its wording. And to Us you will be returned not to anyone else, so We will reward you for your deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: The Jews said that God the Almighty had intermarried with the jinn and the angels were among them. God said, to disprove them, Rather, they are honored servants, meaning the angels are not as they said, rather they are servants whom He has honored with His worship. They do not precede Him in speech, praising them. Nor do they intercede, he said: The angels will not intercede on the Day of Resurrection. Except for him with whom He is pleased, he said: For the people of monotheism. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement, Except for him with whom He is pleased, he said: For the people of monotheism, for those with whom He is pleased. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding the verse, he said: Saying, There is no god but God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba’th on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: Those whom He is pleased with for their testimony that there is no god but God. Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba'th, on the authority of Jabir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the verse: {And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased} and said: {Indeed, my intercession is for the major sinners of my nation.} Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {They were joined together, then We split them}, he said: The sky split with rain, and the earth split with plants. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: {They were joined together}, he said: Nothing comes out of them, and he mentioned the same as mentioned above. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilyah also narrated it on his authority through another chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority: {They were joined together}, he said: stuck together. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah regarding his statement: {And We made from water every living thing}, he said: The sperm of a man. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We have made therein paths as roads, he said: between the mountains. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Each in an orbit, he said: revolving. Swimming, he said: they run. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on his authority, Each in an orbit, he said: an orbit like the spinning of a spindle. Swimming, he said: they revolve in the gates of heaven. Just as the spinning wheel revolves in the spindle. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, he said: it is the orbit of heaven. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Aisha, he said: Abu Bakr entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he had died, so he kissed him and said: And His prophets, His friends and His chosen ones, then he recited, And We have not granted to any human being before you immortality, the verse, and His statement, Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We test you with evil and with good as trial, he said: We test you with hardship and ease, health and sickness, wealth and poverty, lawful and unlawful, obedience and disobedience, guidance and misguidance.
21:36: His saying: 36- And when those who disbelieve see you meaning the mockers among the polytheists they take you only in ridicule meaning they take you only as a mockery, and mockery is derision, and these are the ones about whom God said Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers and the meaning is: they do not do anything to you except take you in ridicule Is this the one who mentions your gods is on the assumption of the saying: meaning they say is this the one, so on this it is the answer to if, and his saying: they take you only in ridicule is an objection between the condition and its answer, and the meaning of mentioning it is to find fault with it. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said that so-and-so mentions al-Nas 114:meaning he backbites them, and mentions their faults, and so-and-so mentions God: meaning he describes Him with greatness and praises Him, and what is understood from mention is only deleted with mention, and according to what they said, mention does not mean fault in the speech of the Arabs, and when it is intended to mean fault, the bad is deleted from it, it was said and from this is the saying of Antarah: Do not mention my dowry and what I fed him, lest your skin be like the skin of a mangy dog. That is, do not criticize my dowry. The phrase and they are disbelievers in the remembrance of the Most Gracious is in the accusative case as a state: that is, they are disbelievers in the Qur’an, or they are disbelievers in the remembrance of the Most Gracious who created them. The meaning is that they criticize the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for mentioning their gods that do not harm or benefit with evil, while the fact is that they are disbelievers in the remembrance of God Almighty in a manner befitting Him of monotheism or the Qur’an. They are more deserving of being criticised and denounced. The first pronoun is the subject and its predicate is disbelievers, and in the remembrance is related to the predicate, and the second pronoun is an emphasis.
21:37: 37- Man was created from haste meaning that due to his extreme haste he was made as if he was created from haste. Al-Farra' said: It is as if he is saying that he built and created him from haste and in haste. Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs were addressed with what they understand, and the Arabs say to someone who does something a lot, I was created from it, just as they say: You are from play, and you were created from play, meaning to exaggerate in describing him with that. This meaning is indicated by his saying: And man was hasty, and what is meant by man is the species. It was said that what is meant by man is Adam, because when God created him and breathed the spirit into him, the spirit was in his head, so he went to get up before the spirit reached his feet and he fell, so it was said Man was created from haste, this is what Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Suddi, Al-Kalbi and Mujahid said. Abu Ubaidah and many of the scholars of meaning said: The calf is clay in the language of Himyar. They recited: Palm trees grow between the water and the calf It was said that this verse was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, who said: O God, if this is the truth from You, and it was said that it was revealed about Quraysh because they hastened the punishment. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning of the creation of man from haste is that it was said to him, Be, and he was. It was said that this verse is from the reversed verse: that is, the creation of the calf from man. This was narrated from Abu Ubaidah and Al-Nahhas, and the first statement is more appropriate. I will show you My signs, meaning I will show you My punishments against you with the punishment of the Fire, so do not hasten it, meaning do not hasten Me to bring it, for it will inevitably befall you.
