It was said that what is meant by the signs is what indicates the truthfulness of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from miracles and what God has made for him of a praiseworthy outcome, and the first statement is more appropriate.
21:38: And this is indicated by their saying 38- "When will this promise come true, if you are truthful?" That is, when will this promise, which you threaten us with, of torment, come true? They said that in mockery and ridicule. It was said that what is meant by the promise here is the Resurrection, and the meaning of "if you are truthful" is if you, O group of Muslims, are truthful in your promise. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers who recite the Qur'anic verses warning of the coming of the Hour and the imminent arrival of the torment.
21:39: And the sentence 39- "If only those who disbelieved knew" what comes after it confirms what came before it: that is, if they knew that time, and the answer to "if" is omitted, and the meaning is: If only they knew the time when "they will not ward off the Fire from their faces nor from their backs, nor will they be aided" they would not hasten the threat. Al-Zajjaj said: In the estimation of the answer, so that they may know the truth of the promise, and it was said that if they knew it, they would not have persisted in disbelief. Al-Kisa'i said: It is a warning of the certainty of the occurrence of the Hour: that is, if they knew it with certainty, they would know that the Hour is coming, and this is indicated by his statement: "Rather, it will come upon them suddenly" and specifying the faces and backs in the mention in the sense of the front and the back because they are the most famous sides in requiring encompassing them to encompass the whole such that they are not able to repel it from any of their sides, and the location of "when they will not ward off is the accusative as it is the object of knowledge, and it is an expression of the promised time that they were hastening, and the meaning of nor will they be aided" is that no one among the servants will aid them and repel that from them.
21:40: And sentence 40- "Rather, it will come upon them suddenly is connected to they will not be able to ward it off": meaning, they will not ward it off, rather, the number, or the Fire, or the Hour will come upon them suddenly: meaning, suddenly, "and it will confuse them." Al-Jawhari said: It confounded him, it took him by surprise. Al-Farra' said: It will confuse them: meaning, it will bewilder them. It was also said: It will surprise them. "And they will not be able to repel it," meaning, to divert it from their faces or their backs, so the pronoun refers to the Fire. It was also said: It refers to the promise, interpreted as the number, and it was also said: It refers to the time, interpreted as the Hour. "Nor will they be given respite," meaning, they will be given respite and delayed for repentance and apology.
21:41: And the sentence 41 - And messengers before you were mocked is intended to console and comfort the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as if he said: If these people mocked you, then he did the same to the messengers before you, despite their large number and seriousness. So that which they mocked overtook them means that it surrounded and swept around, because of that, those who mocked those messengers and mocked them. That which they mocked is a relative pronoun, or a source: meaning that the matter which they mocked overtook them, or their mockery surrounded them: meaning that it is his punishment for placing the cause in place of the effect, or the mockery itself, if what is meant by it is the punishment in the Hereafter.
21:42: 42- “Say: Who guards you by night and by day from the Most Gracious?” That is, who guards you and preserves you. Guarding means guarding and preservation. It is said: God protected him, God protected him, meaning He preserved him and guarded him. Ibn Harmah said: Salma, may God protect her, was stingy with something that would have caused her misery. Say, O Muhammad, to those who mock by way of rebuke and rebuke: Who guards you and protects you by night and by day from the wrath and punishment of the Most Gracious, which you deserve to befall you and descend upon you? Al-Zajjaj said: It means who protects you from the wrath of the Most Gracious. Al-Farra’ said: It means who protects you from what the Most Gracious wants to bring down upon you of punishments in this world and the Hereafter. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ narrated: Who guards you from what the Most Gracious wants to bring down upon you of punishments in this world and the Hereafter? “Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord,” meaning from His remembrance, glory be to Him, so they do not remember Him nor does He cross their minds, rather they turn away from Him, or from the Qur’an, or from the admonitions of God, or from knowing Him.
21:43: 43- Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us? "Am is the disconnected particle that means rather," and the hamza is for interruption and transition from the previous statement that includes a statement of their ignorance of His, glory be to Him, protecting them to their rebuke and reprimand for their reliance on someone who is unable to benefit himself and defend himself. The meaning is: Rather, they are gods who can protect them from Our punishment. It was said that there is an inversion of it, and the estimate is: Or do they have gods other than Us who can protect them? Then He described these gods of theirs that they claimed would support them with what indicates weakness and inability, saying: "They cannot support themselves, nor can they be companions of Us." That is, they are unable to support themselves, so how can they be able to support others? Nor can they be companions of Us: that is, nor can they be protected from Our punishment. Ibn Qutaybah said: That is, no one can protect them from Us, because the protector is the companion of the neighbor, and the Arabs say "May God accompany you" meaning He protected you and protected you, and from this is the saying of the poet: He calls out at the top of his voice, seeking refuge, so that he may accompany us and the spears are in our hands. The Arabs say: I am your neighbor and friend from so-and-so. That is, I protect him. Al-Mazini said: It is from the verb ashabt to protect a man if you protect him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Abu Sufyan and Abu Jahl while they were talking. When Abu Jahl saw him, he laughed and said to Abu Sufyan: ‘This is the prophet of Banu Abd Manaf.’ Abu Sufyan became angry and said: ‘Why do you deny that Banu Abd Manaf has a prophet?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard this and went back to Abu Jahl, attacked him and frightened him and said: ‘I do not see you stopping until what happened to your uncle happens to you.’ He said to Abu Sufyan: ‘You only said what you said out of pride.’ Then this verse was revealed: ‘And when those who disbelieve see you.’” I said: Who is it that Al-Suddi narrated from? Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hameed and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: When the spirit was blown into Adam, it was in his head and he sneezed and said: Praise be to God. The angels said: May God have mercy on you. He went to get up before his feet could be shaken, but he fell. God said: He created man from haste. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar to this on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hameed, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah also narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated the same on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: “Say: Who guards you?” He said: Who protects you? And regarding His statement: Nor will they be companions of Us? He said: They will not be helped. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Nor will they be companions of Us? He said: They will not be protected. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding the verse: He said: They will not be protected.
21:44: When he nullified the fact that idols were beneficial, he turned away from that and moved on to explaining that what they were in of goodness and enjoyment of the immediate life was from God, not from a deterrent that would prevent them from destruction, nor from a supporter that would aid them in the causes of enjoyment. He said: 44- Rather, We provided for these and their fathers to enjoy meaning the people of Mecca. God provided for them with what He bestowed upon them until life was prolonged for them so they were deceived by that and thought that they would continue to be like that. So the Almighty responded to them saying: Do they not see meaning do they not look and see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders so we conquer it country after country and land after land. It was said that We reduce it by killing and capturing. The discussion of this has already been completed in Al-Ra'd. The question in His statement: Do they understand the victors is for denial, and the fa is for conjunction with an implied word like its counterparts: meaning how can they be victorious after We reduce their land from our borders? In this there is an indication that the victors are the Muslims.
21:45: 45- "Say, 'I only warn you by revelation' meaning I frighten you and warn you by the Qur'an, and that is my nature and what God has commanded me to do. His statement, "And the deaf do not hear the call" is either from the completion of the speech that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to say to them, or from the side of God the Most High. The meaning is that whoever God has deafened his hearing and sealed his heart and put a veil over his sight does not hear the call. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and Muhammad ibn al-Samife' read "and does not hear" with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the meem for what the agent is not named. Ibn Amir, Abu Haywah, and Yahya ibn al-Harith read with a damma on the ta' above and a kasra on the meem: meaning, you, O Muhammad, do not hear these people. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: If it were as Ibn Amir said, it would have been better to use "if you warn them" in the order of the speech. As for "if they warn", it is better to follow the reading of the common people, and the rest read it with a fatha on the ya' and a fatha on the meem and raise the deaf as the agent.
21:46: 46- And if a whiff of the punishment of your Lord touches them What is meant by a whiff is a little, taken from the whiff of musk, as Ibn Kaysan said, and from it the poet said: And Umrah is one of the noblest women, her garments are fragrant with musk. Al-Mubarrad said: “A blast is a small amount of something that is less than the majority of it. It is said that he struck it with a light blow with the sword, and it is also said that it is the erection, and it is also said that it is the edge.” The meaning is similar: that is, if the slightest bit of punishment touches them, they will surely say, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.’ That is, they will call down woe and destruction upon themselves and admit that they were wronged.
21:47: 47- And We shall set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection. The scales are the plural of scale, which indicates that there are scales, and it may be intended to mean one scale, expressed in the plural form. The Sunnah has mentioned what is sufficient about the description of the scale, and it has been mentioned in Al-A'raf and Al-Kahf in this regard, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. The scales are an attribute of the scales. Al-Zajjaj said: Qast is a verbal noun that is used to describe it. You say: a scale of justice and scales of justice. The meaning is: those who have justice, and justice is fairness. Al-Qast is read with the letters sad and ta, and the meaning of for the Day of Resurrection is for the people of the Day of Resurrection. It was said that the lam means in: that is, on the Day of Resurrection. So no soul will be wronged at all meaning that the good of a good person will not be diminished nor will the evil of a bad person be increased. Even if it is the weight of a mustard seed Nafi', Shaibah, and Abu Ja'far read Mithqal in the nominative case, as if it were complete, meaning if it occurred or was found to be the weight of a mustard seed. The rest read it with the accusative of the mithqal, on the assumption: And if the action indicated by placing the scales is the weight of a grain, as al-Zajjaj said. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: And if the injustice is the weight of a grain. Al-Wahidi said: This is better because of the previous statement: So let not a soul be wronged in the least, and the weight of something is its scale: meaning even if it is extremely light and insignificant, for the mustard seed is an example of smallness. We brought it The majority read it with the shortened form: meaning we brought it and brought it to recompense for it, it is said aati yu’ati mu’tatah: he recompensed. And sufficient for us are reckoners meaning sufficient for us as accountants, and the meaning of hasab in origin is counting, and it was said sufficient for us as knowers, because whoever has hasab something knows it and memorizes it, and it was said sufficient for us as recompense for what they have done of good and evil.
21:48: Then the Almighty proceeded to detail what He had previously summarized by saying: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed. He said: 48- And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous. What is meant by the Criterion here is the Torah, because it contains the distinction between what is lawful and what is unlawful. It has been said that the Criterion here is victory over enemies, as in His saying: And We did not send down to Our Servant on the Day of Criterion. Al-Tha'labi said: This statement is more similar to the apparent meaning of the verse, and the meaning of the Light is that they were illuminated by it in the darkness of ignorance and misguidance, and the meaning of the Reminder is the admonition: that is, they are admonished by what is in it, and He singled out the righteous because they are the ones who benefit from it.
21:49: And He described them by saying: 49- Those who fear their Lord unseen because this fear accompanies piety. Because this fear accompanies piety. And it is possible for the relative pronoun to be a substitute for the pious or an explanation of it, and the place of the unseen is the accusative case as a state: that is, they fear His punishment while He is absent from them, or they are absent from Him because they are in this world, and the punishment is in the Hereafter. And Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah read Diaa without a waw. Al-Farra' said that the waw was deleted and its occurrence is one, and Al-Zajjaj objected to him by saying that the waw comes for a meaning and is not added and they are fearful of the Hour that is, they are fearful and anxious of the Resurrection.
21:50: And the reference in his saying: 50- And this is a blessed reminder is to the Qur'an. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that this Qur'an is a reminder for those who remember it and an admonition for those who take heed from it, and the blessed is abundant in blessing and goodness. And his saying: We sent it down is a second description of the reminder, or a piece of report after a piece of report, and the question in his saying: Then will you deny it? is to deny what they did of denial: that is, how do you deny that it was sent down from God while you acknowledge that the Torah was sent down from Him.
21:51: 51- And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgment meaning the sound judgment befitting him and his likes among the messengers. The meaning of before is that He gave him his sound judgment before the Torah was given to Moses and Aaron. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is that We gave him his guidance before the prophecy: meaning We enabled him to see and reason when he was crazy about it, so he saw the sun, the moon, and the stars. This is what most of the commentators agree with, and the least of them agree with the first. And We were knowing of him is that it is a place for giving sound judgment, and that it is suitable for that.
21:52: The circumstance in his saying: 52- "When he said to his father is related to We have given" or to something omitted: that is, remember when he said: "And his father is Azar And his people" Nimrod and those who followed him, and the statues are idols, and the origin of the statue is the thing made similar to something from the creations of God Almighty, it is said that you make something similar to something, and the name of that representative is a statue, he denied their worship by saying: "What are these statues to which you are devoted?" And the devotion is an expression of adherence and continuity on the thing, and the lam in it is for specificity, and if it was for transitivity, the word on would have been brought: that is, what are these idols that you are devoted to worshipping? It was said that devotion includes the meaning of worship.
21:53: 53- They said, 'We found our fathers worshipping it.' They answered him with this answer, which is the stick that every weak person leans on, and the rope that every drowning person clings to, which is adherence to mere imitation of the fathers: that is, we found our fathers worshipping it, so we worshipped it, following their example and walking in their way. This is how these imitators from the people of this Islamic religion answer. If the scholar of the Book and the Sunnah denies them acting on the basis of mere opinion that is refuted by evidence, they say, This was said by our Imam, whom we found our fathers imitating and taking his opinion. Their answer is what Al-Khalil answered here.
21:54: 54- He said, 'Indeed, you and your fathers were in manifest error.' That is, in clear, obvious loss that is not hidden from anyone and is not confusing to anyone with reason. The people of Abraham worshipped idols that neither harm nor benefit, nor hear nor see. There is no error after this error, and no loss is equal to this loss. These imitators from among the people of Islam have replaced the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger with a book in which the efforts of a scholar of the scholars of Islam have been recorded. He claimed that he did not find any evidence that contradicts it, either due to his shortcomings or his negligence in research. So whoever finds that evidence finds it and presents it with a clear beacon. It's like a flag with fire in its head He said: This is the Book of God or this is the Sunnah of His Messenger, and he recited to them: Leave every word when Muhammad says, for he who believes in his religion is like a risk They said as the first one said: I am only from Ghazia, if it goes astray, I go astray, and if Ghazia is guided, I am guided He said it well: The young man refuses to follow anything but his desires, and the path of truth is clear to him.
21:55: Then when those people heard the statement of Al-Khalil 55- They said, ‘Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the players?’ That is, are you skilled in what you say, or are you a player who jokes? He said, striking out at what they based their statement on, which was imitation.
21:56: 56- Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them meaning, He created them and made them original. And I am, over that which I mentioned to you, that your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, without anything else, among the witnesses meaning, those who know it and prove it, for the witness to something is the one who knows it, proves it, and explains it to him. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir in his Tahdheeb, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated on the authority of Aisha that a man said: O Messenger of God, I have two slaves who lie to me, betray me, and disobey me, so I beat them and curse them, so what do I do to them? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Their betrayal, disobedience, and lying to you, and your reprimanding them, are considered a favor to you. If your punishment of them is less than their sins, then it is a favor for you. If your punishment of them is equal to their sins, then it is sufficient, neither for you nor against you. If your punishment of them is greater than their sins, then they have taken the favor from you. The man began to cry and shout, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you not read the Book of God: “And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all. And if there is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as reckoners.” The man said to him: O Messenger of God, I do not find anything better for myself and for them than to part with them. I bear witness to you that they are free. Ahmad narrated it as follows: Abu Noah Al-Aqrad, Laith bin Saad told us, on the authority of Malik bin Anas, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, and he mentioned it, and there are hadiths with the same meaning. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite, And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, he said: the Torah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada something similar. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zaid, he said: The Criterion is the truth. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, And this is a blessed message, meaning the Qur’an. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We gave Abraham his sound judgment, he said: We guided him when he was young. And regarding his statement, What are these statues? he said: idols.
21:57: His saying: 57- And by God, I will surely destroy your idols He informed them that he would move from arguing with words to changing evil with action, trusting in God the Almighty and defending His religion. And deception is trickery: it is said that he almost deceived him, and what is meant here is diligence. In breaking idols: It was said that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said that secretly, and it was said that a man from them heard him after they had turned their backs meaning after they had returned from worshipping them, going and departing. The commentators said: They had a festival every year in which they would gather, so they said to Ibrahim: If you went out with us to our festival, our religion would please you, so Ibrahim said this statement.
21:58: The Fa in His saying: 58- So He made them fragments is eloquent: that is, they turned away, so He made them fragments: fragmentation means cutting and breaking. It is said: I cut something apart and broke it, the singular is fragmentation, and fragmentation is what is broken from it. Al-Jawhari said: Al-Kisa'i said: And the gold stones are called fragments because they are broken. Al-Kisa'i, Al-A'mash and Ibn Muhaisin read Jathathan with a kasra on the jim: that is, breaking and cutting, the plural of fragmentation: which is dry straw, like light and light, and elegant and elegant. The poet said: Cutting down idols in their altar is for the sake of God, the Most High, the Almighty. The rest read it with the dammah, and this reading was chosen by Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim: meaning debris and chips, fa’al meaning maf’ul, and this is the plot that he promised them. Ibn Abbas and Abu al-Sammak read juthadh with the fathah on the jim, except a big one for them meaning for the idols, perhaps they will return to it meaning to Abraham, “so that he may argue with them about what will come and make them argue. And it was said that perhaps they will return to the big idol and ask it about the breaker, because it is the nature of the worshipped to return to it in important matters, and when they return to it they do not find any report with it, so they know then that it does not bring benefit nor ward off harm, and does not know good or evil, nor inform about the matter that befalls it. And it was said that perhaps they will return to God, and this is very far-fetched.
21:59: 59- They said, 'Who did this to our gods? He is indeed among the wrongdoers.' There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So when they returned from their festival and saw what had happened to their gods, they said this statement, and the question is for rebuke. It was said that who is not an interrogative, but rather it is a subject and its predicate is He is indeed among the wrongdoers: meaning the one who did this is a wrongdoer.
21:60: And the first is more appropriate for their saying: 60- We heard a young man etc., for some of them said this in response to their questioners, and this speaker is the one who heard Abraham say: By God, I will surely destroy your idols and the meaning of reminds them is to criticize them, and the investigation of such a phrase has been previously mentioned, and the phrase It is said to him, Abraham is a second description of a young man. Al-Zajjaj said: And Abraham was raised in the sense: It is said to him, he is Abraham, so according to this it is the predicate of a deleted subject, and it was said that it was raised as the object of what its agent was not named, and it was said that it was raised in the vocative. Among the strange grammatical refinements and the wonders of syntactic directions, is that Al-A’lam Al-Shantamari Al-Ashbili said: It is raised on neglect. Ibn Atiyah said: He went to raise it without anything. And the boy: is the young man, and the young girl: the young woman.
21:61: 61- They said, 'Bring him before the eyes of the people.' The questioners were the ones who asked. They ordered some of them to bring him openly in the sight of the people. It was said that when the report reached Nimrod and the nobles of his people, they were reluctant to take him without evidence, so they said this statement so that it would be an argument against him to make permissible what they had decided to do to him. The meaning of perhaps they will bear witness is that they may be present at his punishment so that others will be deterred from following his example in such a matter. It was also said that they may bear witness against him that they saw him break the idols, or that they may witness his stabbing their idols.
21:62: And sentence 62 - They said, 'Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, and in the speech there is an omission, the meaning of which is: So Abraham came when they brought him and asked him if he did that, to establish proof against him according to their claim.
21:63: 63- He said, 'Rather, their chief did it.' That is, Abraham said, establishing the argument against them and rebuking them, Rather, their chief did it, pointing to the idol that he had left and not broken. Then ask them if they speak. That is, if they are among those who can speak and are able to talk and understand what is given to them, then they will answer with what is appropriate, and it is not right in reason to call them a god. So he presented the speech in a way that would make them admit that the inanimate objects that they worshipped are not gods, because if they said that they do not speak, he would say to them: How do you worship someone who is unable to speak and is unable to know what is happening to him in the place where he is? This statement is a case of imposing falsehood on the opponent until the argument is binding on him and he acknowledges the truth, for that is more decisive in solving his doubts and repelling his stubbornness. It was said that Abraham, peace be upon him, intended by attributing the action to that great idol that he did that because he was jealous and angry that he and the small ones were worshipped with him, as guidance to them that the worship of these idols that do not hear, see, benefit or repel is not acceptable in reason with the existence of their Creator and their Creator, and the first is more appropriate. Ibn al-Sameefa’ read bala fa’ala with a shaddah on the lam, meaning bala, perhaps the doer is their great one.
21:64: 64- So they returned to themselves meaning some of them returned to each other as someone who is cut off from his argument and is aware of the soundness of his opponent's argument returns to his mind, and that is because they became aware and understood during this contract between them and Abraham that someone who is not able to repel harm from himself or to harm the one who did to him what Abraham did to those idols cannot possibly be worthy of worship, and for this reason they said, 'Indeed, you are the wrongdoers' meaning some of them said to each other: You are the wrongdoers to yourselves by worshipping these inanimate objects, and the wrongdoer is not the one to whom you attribute injustice by saying: He is among the wrongdoers.
21:65: 65- Then they lowered their heads meaning they returned to their ignorance and stubbornness. God Almighty likened their return to falsehood to the bottom of something becoming top. It was said that the meaning is that they lowered their heads in shame before Abraham, but this is weak because He did not say they lowered their heads with the opening of the kaf and attributing the action to them so that this interpretation would be correct. Rather, He said: they lowered their heads. It was read as they lowered their heads with emphasis. Then they said after they lowered their heads, addressing Abraham, You have certainly known that these do not speak meaning saying to Abraham, You have certainly known that speech is not the nature of these idols.
21:66: F 66- He said, Abraham, rebuking them and humiliating them, Do you then worship instead of God that which does not benefit you at all of benefit nor harm you in any way?
21:67: Then he, peace be upon him, became annoyed with them, and said 67- Fie upon you and upon what you worship besides God. In this is a humiliation of them and their deities, and the lam in lakum is to clarify what is being annoyed with: that is, upon you and your gods, and annoyance is a sound that indicates annoyance. Do you not understand? that is, you do not have minds with which to think, so that you know this ugly deed that you have done.
21:68: 68- They said, 'Burn him.' That is, some of them said to each other when they were exhausted in their efforts to repel Abraham, and were unable to argue with him, and the paths of debate became narrow for them, they burned Abraham, turning away from the path of injustice and oppression, and inclining to show victory in any way, and in any matter that happened. For this reason, they said, And support your gods, if you are going to do so. That is, support them by taking revenge on the one who did to them what he did, if you are going to do so for victory. It was said that this speaker was Nimrod, and it was said that he was a man from the Kurds.
21:69: 69- “We said, ‘O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham.’” There is an omission in the speech, the meaning of which is that they lit the fire and took Abraham to it. Then, we said, “O fire, be coolness and peace.” It was said that the accusative of “peace” is that it is a source for a deleted verb: that is, we gave him peace.
21:70: 70- And they intended to plot against him, meaning a scheme, but We made them the greatest losers, meaning the greatest losers of all losers. We turned their scheme back on them, so We made for them the worst outcome, just as We made for Abraham the best outcome. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: When the people of Abraham went out to their festival, they passed by him and said: O Abraham, will you not come out with us? He said: I am sick, and it was yesterday. He said: By God, I will surely destroy your idols after you have turned and departed. Some of them heard him, so when they went out he went to his family, took some food, then went to their gods and brought it to them, and said: Will you not eat? So he broke it except for their eldest, then he tied the hand with which he had broken their gods to his hand. When the people returned from their festival, they entered and found their gods broken, and their eldest was in his hand with the one with whom he had broken the idols. They said: Who did this to our gods? Those who heard Abraham say: By God, I will surely destroy your idols said: We heard a young man mentioning them. Then Abraham argued with them. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: in fragments, he said: debris. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: crumbs. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him: Rather, their greatest one did it. He said: The greatest of their gods. Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Abraham never lied about anything except in three cases, all of which were for the sake of God: his saying, ‘I am ill,’ when he was not ill; his saying to Sarah, my sister; and his saying, ‘Rather, their greatest one did it.’” This hadith is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, but it is longer than this. Abu Ya’la narrated something similar from the hadith of Abu Sa’d. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: When Abraham had collected what he had collected and was thrown into the fire, the rain keeper said: When will I be commanded to send rain? But God’s command was swift. God said, Be cool and safe, and there was no fire left on earth except that it was extinguished. Ahmad, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When Ibrahim was thrown into the fire, there was not a single creature that did not extinguish the fire for him, except for the gecko, which used to blow on Ibrahim. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered that it be killed.” Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The first words Ibrahim said when he was thrown into the fire were: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding His statement: O fire, be! He said: Gabriel was the one who called it. Al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If its coolness had not been followed by greetings, Ibrahim would have died from its coolness. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ali. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi on the authority of some of his companions who said: Gabriel came to Abraham while he was being bound to be thrown into the fire, and he said: O Abraham, do you have a need? He said: As for you, no. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ka'b who said: The fire did not burn anything of Abraham except his bonds. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Minhal ibn Amr who said: I was informed that Abraham was thrown into the fire, and he was in it for either fifty or forty. He said: I never lived a better life for days or nights when I was in it. I wished that my life and my entire life were like my life when I was in it.
21:71: It was mentioned earlier that Lot was the nephew of Abraham, so God Almighty narrated here that He saved Abraham and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds. The commentators said: It is the land of Ash-Sham, and they were in Iraq, and God Almighty called it blessed because of its abundant fertility, fruits, and rivers, and because it is the mines of the prophets. The origin of blessing is the continuity of goodness, and from it the camel kneels when it remains in its place and does not move. It was said that the blessed land is Mecca, and it was said that Jerusalem is the Holy Land because God sent most of the prophets from it, and it is also very fertile. The interpretation of the worlds was mentioned earlier.
21:72: 72- And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift. The additional gift is an addition. Abraham had asked God Almighty to bestow upon him a son, so He bestowed upon him Isaac, then He bestowed upon Isaac Jacob without supplication, so that was an additional gift: that is, an addition. It was said that what is meant by the additional gift here is the gift, as Al-Zajjaj said. It was also said that the additional gift here is the son of a son, because he is an addition to a son, and the accusative of the word an additional gift is in the state of the circumstance. Al-Farra' said: The additional gift is specifically Jacob, because he was the son of the father. And each of them We made righteous. That is, each one of these four: Abraham, Lot, Isaac, and Jacob, not some of them without others, We made him righteous, acting in obedience to God and abandoning His disobedience. It was said that what is meant by righteousness here is prophethood.
21:73: 73- And We made them leaders guiding by Our command meaning leaders who are followed in good deeds and acts of obedience. The meaning of by Our command is by Our command to them meaning by what We sent down to them of revelation. And We inspired them to do good deeds meaning that they should do acts of obedience. It was said that what is meant by good deeds are the laws of prophethood. And they were worshippers of Us meaning that they were obedient to Us alone, not to anyone else, doing what We commanded them to do and leaving what We forbade them from doing.
21:74: 74- "And to Lot We gave wisdom and knowledge." The accusative of Lot is an implied verb indicated by His saying We gave him: meaning, and We gave Lot We gave him. It was said that it is the same verb mentioned after it, and it was said that it is an omitted word, which is remember. The wisdom is the prophecy, and knowledge is the knowledge of the matter of religion. It was said that the wisdom is the settlement of disputes with truth. It was said that it is understanding. "And We saved him from the city that was doing evil." The city is Sodom, as mentioned above. The meaning of doing evil is that its people were doing evil. So He described the city with the description of its people, and the evils that they were doing were sodomy, farting, and throwing pebbles, as will come. Then the Almighty explained that by saying: "Indeed, they were an evil and wicked people." That is, they went outside of the obedience of God, and wickedness is going outside, as mentioned above.
21:75: 75- And We admitted him into Our mercy by saving him from the aforementioned people. The meaning of in Our mercy is: among the people of Our mercy. It was said that it was in prophethood, it was said that it was in Islam, and it was said that it was in Paradise. He is among the righteous for whom goodness from Us has preceded.
21:76: 76- And Noah, when he called out meaning, remember Noah, when he called out to his Lord before meaning before these mentioned prophets so We responded to him his call and saved him and his family from the great distress meaning from drowning in the flood, and distress is intense grief, and what is meant by his family are the believers among them.
21:77: 77- And We gave him victory over the people who denied Our signs meaning We gave him victory that entailed taking revenge on the aforementioned people. It was said that the meaning is: We prevented him from the people. Abu Ubaidah said: From means on, then the Almighty explained that by saying: Indeed, they were an evil people, so We drowned them all meaning We did not leave a single one of them alone, rather We drowned their great and small because of their insistence on sin. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab regarding his statement: to the land which We have blessed, he said: Ash-Sham. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Abi Malik something similar. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Lot was the nephew of Abraham. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority: And We bestowed upon him Isaac, he said: a son, and Jacob as an additional gift, he said: a son of a son. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatadah something similar. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Hakam something similar as well. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid: And We bestowed upon him Isaac, he said: We gave him, and Jacob as an additional gift, he said: a gift.
21:78: His statement: 78- And David is in apposition to Noah and is the object of its mentioned agent, or the implied one as mentioned before. And Solomon is in apposition to David, and the circumstance in when they judged is related to what he did with David: that is, remember them at the time of their judgment. What is meant by mentioning them is mentioning their report. The meaning of in the tillage is in the matter of the tillage, and it was said that it was a crop, and it was said that it was a vineyard, and the name of the tillage is applied to them. When the sheep of the people were scattered therein means that they were dispersed and spread out in it. Ibn al-Sikkit said: Nafsh with the movement is that the sheep are scattered at night without a shepherd. And We were witnesses to their judgment that is, to the judgment of the two judges, and in it is the permissibility of applying the plural to the two, and this is the doctrine of a group of the people of Arabic such as al-Zamakhshari and al-Radi, and al-Farra' preceded them in saying it. It was said that what is meant are the two judges and the one being judged, and the meaning of two witnesses is present, and the sentence is parenthetical.
21:79: And the sentence 79- So We made Solomon understand it is connected to when they judge, because it is in the past tense, and the pronoun in So We made it understand refers to the issue understood from the speech, or the government indicated by mentioning the judgment. The commentators said: Two men entered upon David, and his son Solomon was with him: one of them was a farmer, and the other was a sheep owner. The farmer said: This man's sheep got loose at night and fell into my field, leaving nothing of it. He said: You have the necks of the sheep. Solomon said: Or something else, the owners of the vineyard go with the sheep and take from their milk and benefits, and the owners of the sheep stand on the vineyard, until when it is dry and they have pecked in it, these give their sheep to those, and those give their vineyard to those. So David said: The judgment is what you have judged, and he ruled accordingly. An-Nahhas said: David ruled that the sheep belonged to the owner of the farm because their price was close to his. As for Solomon’s ruling, it has been said that the value of what he took from the sheep and the value of what the sheep spoiled were the same. A group of scholars said: David ruled by revelation, and Solomon ruled by revelation through which God abrogated David’s ruling, so the understanding of this was by way of revelation. The majority said: Their ruling was based on independent reasoning, and the scholars’ speech on the ruling on the independent reasoning of the prophets is well-known. This is also what the scholars have mentioned about the differences of opinion among those who make independent reasoning, and whether every independent reasoner is correct, or is the truth with one person? Those who cite this verse as evidence that every mujtahid is correct, but this verse and others do not indicate this. Rather, the agreed upon hadith in the two Sahihs and others clearly states that if a ruler exerts his ijtihad and is correct, he will have two rewards, and if he exerts his ijtihad and is wrong, he will have one reward. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called him wrong. So how can it be said that he is correct in the ruling of God and agrees with it? The ruling of God, the Exalted, is one and does not differ based on the differences of the mujtahids. Otherwise, His ruling, the Exalted, would be dependent on the ijtihads of the mujtahids, and the necessary consequence is invalid, so the necessary consequence is the same. It also requires that the particular thing in which the ijtihads of the mujtahids differed regarding what is permissible or forbidden is permissible according to the ruling of God, the Exalted. This is the necessary consequence of every mujtahid who has an ijtihad in that incident, and what God, the Exalted, wants in it does not cease except by the cessation of the mujtahids, and the necessary consequence is invalid, so the necessary consequence is the same. We have explained this issue in a way that cannot be added to in the two works that we called Al-Qawl Al-Mufid fi Hukm Al-Taqlid and fi Adab Al-Talab and Muntaha Al-Arab. So whoever wants to understand the truth should refer to them. If you say: What is the ruling on this incident in which David and Solomon ruled in this Muhammadan Sharia and the Islamic religion? I say: It has been proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hadith of Al-Baraa’ that he legislated for his nation that it is upon the owners of livestock to protect them at night, and upon the owners of fences to protect them during the day, and that whatever livestock destroys at night is guaranteed by its owners, and this guarantee is the amount lost in kind or value. The majority of scholars have adopted what is included in this hadith. Abu Hanifa and his companions and a group of Kufians have adopted the view that this ruling is abrogated, and that if animals destroy crops at night or during the day, their owner is not obligated to do anything, and they included their destruction in the generality of the Prophet’s statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, The wound of a dumb animal is compensated for, by analogy of all its actions to its wound. The response to this is that this analogy is invalid because it contradicts the text, and some scholars have adopted the view that the owner of livestock is responsible for what they destroy, regardless of whether it is night or day. The answer is given by the hadith of Al-Baraa’. What indicates that these two judgments of David and Solomon were by revelation from God, the Most High, and not by personal interpretation is his statement: And to each We gave judgment and knowledge. God, the Most High, informed us that He gave each of them these two matters, and if they were specific, then their truthfulness in this case that God, the Most High, narrated about them takes precedence over their truthfulness in other cases. And if they were general, then this individual judgment and knowledge, which is what each of them did in this case, is the most deserving of the individuals of that generality to be included under it and indicated by it. And what is learned from that is to repel what might be suggested by the specification of Solomon by understanding, that the judgment of David was not a legal judgment: that is, to each of them We gave much judgment and knowledge, not Solomon alone. And when David praised Solomon by way of sharing, he mentioned what was specific to each of them, so he began with David and said: And We subjected with David the mountains to glorify God. Glorification is either literal or metaphorical, and a group has said the first, and this is the apparent meaning. This is because when David glorified God, the mountains glorified God with him. It was also said that they prayed with him when he prayed, which is the meaning of glorification. Another group used metaphor, and interpreted glorification as the glorification of those who saw them in amazement at the greatness of their creation and the power of their Creator. It was also said that the mountains were moving with David, so whoever saw them moving with him glorified God. And the birds is in apposition to the mountains, and it was read in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is omitted: that is, the birds are subjected. It is not correct to link the pronoun in glorify due to the lack of emphasis and preference. And We were the Doer means what was mentioned of understanding, giving judgment and subjection.
21:80: 80- And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you. Coats among the Arabs mean all weapons, whether they are armor, shields, swords, or spears. Al-Hudhali said: I have a dress that looks like something like this. What is meant in the verse is armor specifically, and it means clothing, like riding and carrying, and the prepositional phrase I mean for you is related to Our knowledge to protect you from your violence. Al-Hasan, Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Amir, Hafs and Ruh read to protect you with the superscript ta’, referring the pronoun to the craft, or to the clothing with the interpretation of the armor. Shaibah, Abu Bakr, Al-Mufaddal and Ibn Abi Ishaq read to protect you with the nun, referring the pronoun to Him, the Most High. The rest read with the ya’, referring the pronoun to the clothing, or to David, or to God, the Most High. The meaning of from your violence is your war, or from the weapon falling on you. So are you grateful for this blessing that We have bestowed upon you, and the question is in the sense of a command.
21:81: Then the Almighty mentioned what He gave to Solomon. He said: 81- And to Solomon was the wind meaning We subjected to him the wind storming meaning blowing strongly. It is said that the wind blew strongly, so it is a stormy and violent wind, and the wind is in the accusative case as a state. Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, al-Salami and Abu Bakr read And to Solomon was the wind with the wind in the nominative case as a break from what preceded it, and it is the subject and its predicate is flowing. As for the accusative reading, the location of flowing by His command is also accusative as a state, or as a substitute to the land which We have blessed which is the land of Ash-Sham as mentioned previously And We are Knowing of all things meaning of the destruction of everything.
21:82: 82- And of the devils meaning, We subjected the devils there are those who dive for him in the seas and extract from them what he asks of them. It was said that min is the subject and its predicate is what precedes it, and diving is going under the water. It is said that he dived into the water, and the diver is the one who dives in the sea for pearls. And they do work less than that. Al-Farra' said: meaning other than that. It was said that he meant by that the shrines and statues and other things that he subjected them to. And We were their guardians, meaning their deeds. Al-Farra' said: Guarding them from escaping or resisting, or We protected them from going against his command. Al-Zajjaj said: He protected them from corrupting what they did, and it was their habit to corrupt at night what they did during the day.
21:83: 83- "And Job, when he called upon his Lord" is conjoined to what preceded it, and the factor in it is either mentioned or implied as mentioned above, and the factor in the circumstance, which is when he called upon his Lord, is the factor in Job "Indeed, harm has touched me" meaning that harm has touched me. And it is read with a kasra on "indi". There is a difference of opinion as to what the harm that befell him was. It was said that he stood up to pray but was unable to get up. It was said that he admitted his inability, so that is not contrary to patience. It was said that revelation was cut off from him for forty days. It was said that a worm fell from his flesh, so he took it and put it back in its place and it ate from him, so he cried out, Harm has befallen me. It was said that the worms took over his body and he was patient until they took over his heart. It was said that his harm was Satan’s saying to his wife, Prostrate to me, so he feared that her faith would go away. It was said that his people despised him. It was said that he meant by the harm to gloat, and other things were said. When he called upon his Lord, beseeching Him, He described Him with the utmost mercy, saying, And You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.
21:84: So God, the Most High, informed us of the response to his supplication, saying: So We responded to him and removed the affliction that was upon him meaning God healed him from what he was suffering from and compensated him for what he had lost. That is why God, the Most High, said: And We gave him his family and the like of them with them It was said that God, the Most High, left them to him and gave him the like of them in this world. An-Nahhas said: The chain of transmission for that is correct. All of his family had died except his wife, so God revived them in less than the blink of an eye and gave him the like of them with them. It was said that this was because he had children twice as many as those whom God had killed. So the meaning of the verse according to this is: We gave him the like of his family and the like of them with them. The accusative of a mercy from Us is based on the reason: that is, We gave him that because of Our mercy for him. And a reminder for the worshippers meaning and a reminder for other worshippers so that they may be patient as he was patient. There is disagreement about the duration of his stay in the affliction: some say it was seven years, seven months, seven days and seven nights, some say it was thirty years, and some say it was eighteen years.
21:85: 85- And Ishmael, and Idris, and Dhul-Kifl meaning, remember these, and Idris is Enoch, and Dhul-Kifl is Elijah, and it was said Joshua bin Nun, and it was said Zachariah. The correct view is that he is a man from the Children of Israel who did not refrain from any sin, so he repented and God forgave him. It was said that when Elisha grew old, he said: Who will guarantee me such and such of good qualities so that I may appoint him as my successor? A man said, I will, so he appointed him as my successor and he was called Dhul-Kifl. It was said that he was a man who would undertake the affairs of every person if he fell into something important, and other things were said. The majority of scholars have said that he was not a prophet. A group have said: He is a prophet. Then God, the Almighty, described these people as patient, saying: Every one of them is among the patient, meaning every one of them is among the patient in carrying out what God has charged them with.
21:86: 86- And We admitted them into Our mercy, meaning into Paradise, or into prophethood, or into protection in general. Then He explained that by saying: Indeed, they are among the righteous, meaning those who are perfect in righteousness.
21:87: 87- And Dhul-Nun meaning, remember Dhul-Nun, who is Yunus bin Matta, and he was given the nickname Dhul-Nun because the whale swallowed him, as nun is one of the names of whales. It was also said that he was called Dhul-Nun because he saw a handsome boy and said, Blacken his nun so that the evil eye would not strike him. Tha'lab narrated from Ibn al-A'rabi that the boy's nun is the hole in the chin of a young boy, and the meaning of blacken is that they blackened it. When he went away in anger means, remember Dhul-Nun when he went away in anger: that is, reluctantly. Al-Hasan, Al-Sha'bi, and Sa'd bin Jubayr said: He went away in anger for his Lord, and Ibn Jarir, Al-Qutaibi, and Al-Mahdawi chose this. It was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud: An-Nahhas said: This may be denied by someone who does not know the language, but it is a correct statement. The meaning is: In anger for the sake of his Lord, as you say, I became angry for you, meaning for your sake. Ad-Dahhak said: He went away in anger for his people. And he narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A group of them, Al-Akhfash, said: He only went out in anger at the king who was at his time and whose name was Hezekiah. And it was said that he did not anger his Lord, nor his people, nor the king, but it is taken from the word ghadab which means to be angry. And that is because when he promised his people punishment and he went out from them, they repented and God removed the punishment from them. So when he returned and knew that they had not perished, he was angry at that and went out from them. And from the use of anger in this meaning is the saying of the poet: I was angry that Tamim was called Amer That is, before, He thought that We would not have power over him. The majority read We will be able with a fatha on the nun and a kasra on the dal. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of the verse in this reading. It was said that its meaning is: that he thought that God Almighty is not able to punish him. This statement was reported from Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubair, and it is a rejected statement, because this thought about God is disbelief, and the like of that does not happen from the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. The majority of scholars said that its meaning is: so he thought that We will not make things difficult for him, like His statement: He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it meaning restricts it, and from this is His statement: And whoever has his provision restricted it is said qadr and qadara and qatar and qatar: meaning restrict, and it was said: it is from qadr which is the decree and ruling: meaning he thought that We will not decree the punishment on him: this was said by Qatadah and Mujahid, and it was chosen by Al-Farra and Al-Zajjaj, taken from qadr which is the ruling and not the ability and capability. Ahmad bin Yahya Tha’lab said: it is from qadr and not from power, it is said from it: God has decreed good for you, He has decreed it a measure, and Tha’lab recited: The evenings of Al-Lawa will never return to us, as long as the fresh peace is concluded. Nor will that time return, blessed be you, with what you can thank That is, what you estimate and decree. What supports what they said is the reading of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and al-Zuhri, who thought that naqdur with a damma on the nun and a shaddah on the dal comes from taqdir. Al-Mawardi narrated this reading on the authority of Ibn Abbas. This is also supported by the reading of Ubayd ibn Umair, Qatadah, and al-A’raj, that lan yaqdur with a damma on the ya and a shaddah on the dal in the passive voice. Ya’qub, Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq, and al-Hasan read yaqdur with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the dal in the passive voice. The scholars differed in interpreting the authentic hadith in which the man who had never done any good deeds said to his family that they should burn him if he died, then he said: By God, if God has power over me, the hadith is as they differed in interpreting this verse, and the discussion of this is long and we have mentioned here what the observer does not need to mention anything else, and the fa’ in his statement: Then he called out in the darkness is eloquent: that is, what happened was that the whale swallowed him, so he called out in the darkness, and what is meant by darkness is the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the whale, and his call was: his statement: There is no god except You, glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers, that is, that there is no god, etc., and the meaning of glory be to You is: to exalt You from anything that is beyond Your power, indeed I was among the wrongdoers who wrong themselves, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said that this statement from Yunus was an admission of his sin and repentance for his error, he said that while he was in the belly of the whale.
21:88: Then God the Almighty informed us that He responded to him, saying: 88- So We responded to him his supplication that he supplicated to Us with as part of his confession of sin in the most gentle manner and saved him from the distress by taking him out of the belly of the whale until it threw him up on the shore And thus do We save the believers meaning We deliver them from their distress with what they had done previously and what We have prepared for them of mercy, and this is the meaning of the other verse, which is His saying: And had he not been of those who glorify God, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected The majority read nanji with two noons. Ibn Amir read nanji with one noon and a doubled jim and a sukoon on the yaa for the past tense verb and the implied source, and thus salvation saved the believers as you say daraba Zaidan meaning the striking struck Zaid, and from this is the saying of the poet: If a poor woman gave birth to a puppy, the puppy would curse all dogs. This is what Al-Farra, Abu Ubaid and Tha'lab said in explaining this reading, but Abu Hatim and Al-Zajjaj made a mistake and said: It is a mistake because it is a noun in the accusative case without mentioning its agent, and it is said that the believers were saved. Abu Ubaidah has another opinion, which is to assimilate the nun into the jim, and Al-Qatibi said the same. Al-Nahhas objected to him and said: This opinion is not permissible according to any of the grammarians because the point of articulation of the nun is far from the point of articulation of the jim, so it is not assimilated into it. Then Al-Nahhas said: I have not heard anything better about this than what I heard from Ali bin Sulayman Al-Akhfash, who said: The original is nanji, so he deleted one of the two nuns because they came together, just as one of the two ta's is deleted because they came together, like the Almighty's saying: And do not separate, and the original is do not separate. I said: And likewise Al-Wahidi narrated from Abu Ali Al-Farsi that he said: The second noon is concealed with the jim, and it is not permissible to make it clear, so the listener was confused about concealment with assimilation, so he thought it was assimilation, and the evidence for this is his sukoon on the ya’ of naja and the accusative of the believers, and if it was on something whose agent was not named, he would not have made the ya’ sukoon and it would have been necessary to raise the believers. I said: And we do not accept his statement that it is not permissible to make it clear, for it has been made clear in the reading of the majority, and Muhammad bin Al-Sameefa’ and Abu Al-Aaliyah read likewise naja Al-Mu’minin on the active construction: meaning God saved the believers. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Marra regarding his statement: When they gave judgment concerning the field, he said: The field was vegetation and it was carved in it at night, so they disputed about it before David, so he ruled that the sheep belonged to the owners of the field. They passed by Solomon and mentioned that to him, so he said: No, the sheep will be given to them so they can take some of it and these people will take care of their field. When it was as it was, they will be returned to them, so And We gave Solomon understanding of it was revealed. This was narrated on the authority of Marra on the authority of Ibn Masoud. Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, he said: A vineyard had produced its clusters and the sheep spoiled it, so David ruled that the sheep belonged to the owner of the vineyard. So Solomon said: Other than that, O Prophet of God. He said: What is that? He said: The vineyard is given to the owner of the sheep, who takes care of it until it returns to how it was, and the sheep are given to the owner of the vineyard, who takes some of it, until when the vineyard returns to how it was, the vineyard is given to its owner and the sheep to their owners. This is what he said: And We gave it to Solomon. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Masruq. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas, but he did not mention the vineyard. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar in al-Musannaf, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from him, but longer. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated something similar from him, saying: Nafasht meaning: grazed. Abdul Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abdul bin Hamid, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Haram bin Muhaisah that a she-camel belonging to Al-Bara’ bin Azib entered a garden and caused damage to it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruled that the people who maintain the gardens must protect it during the day, and that the people who own them must bear the cost of what the livestock cause at night. He gave a reason for this hadith, and we have discussed it in detail in Sharh Al-Muntaqa. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Aishah. He added at the end of it, then he recited this verse: And David and Solomon. In the two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “While two women with two sons were with them, a wolf came and took one of the two. They took their case to David, and he ruled in favor of the elder. They went out, and Solomon called them and said: ‘Bring me a knife so I can cut him between them.’ The younger one said: ‘May God have mercy on you, he is her son, do not cut him.’ So he ruled in favor of the younger one.” Although this hadith is not included in what the verse has mentioned about their ruling, it is among what happened to them. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azmah narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And We subjected with David the mountains, to glorify God, and the birds, he said: They pray with David when he prayed. And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you, he said: They were plates, and the first to string and shave them was David, peace be upon him. Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Six hundred thousand chairs would be placed for Solomon, then the nobles of mankind would come and sit next to him, then the nobles of the jinn would come and sit next to the nobles of mankind, then he would call the birds and they would be dark, then he would call the wind and it would carry them, traveling a month’s journey in a single morning. Ibn Asakir, Al-Daylami and Ibn Al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God said to Job: Do you know what crime you committed against Me that I tested you? He said: No, O Lord. He said: Because you went to Pharaoh and were lenient with him in two words.” Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Job’s sin was that a poor man sought his help against an oppressor to protect him, but he did not help him, and he did not enjoin what is right, and he did not forbid the oppressor from oppressing the poor man, so God tested him. In its chain of transmission is Juwaybir. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair who said: One day, two brothers came to Ayoub and they could not get close to him because of his strong odor. So they stood from a distance and one of them said to the other: If God had known any good in Ayoub, He would not have afflicted him with this. Ayoub was so distressed by what they said that he had never been distressed by anything before. He said: O God, if You know that I have never spent a night full while I know where someone is hungry, then confirm it with me. So He confirmed it from the heavens while they were listening. Then he said: O God, if You know that I have never worn a shirt while I know where someone is naked, then confirm it with me. So He confirmed it from the heavens while they were listening. Then he fell down in prostration and said: O God, by Your glory, I will not raise my head until You uncover it. So when he raised his head, God uncovered it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another chain of transmission with a similar chain of transmission to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, he said: It was said to him, O Job, your family is yours in Paradise, so if you wish, We will give them to you, and if you wish, We will leave them for you in Paradise and compensate you with the like of them in this world. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: It reached Ibn Mas`ud that Marwan said regarding this verse: And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, he said: He was given a family other than his own, so Ibn Mas`ud said: Rather, he was given his family in person and the like of them with them. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Ruwayani, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: “Job’s affliction continued for eighteen years, and both his relatives and those far away rejected him, except for two men from his brothers who were among his closest friends. They used to come to him in the morning and in the evening. One of them said to his companion one day: ‘By God, you know that Job has committed a sin that no one else has committed. ’ He said: ‘What is that? ’ He said: ‘It has been eighteen years and God has not shown him mercy by removing what is wrong with him. ’ When they went to Job, the man could not wait until he mentioned it to him. Job said: ‘I do not know what he is saying, except that God knows that I will pass by two men who are arguing and mentioning God, so I will return to my house and expiate for them, disliking that God be mentioned except in a right way. ’ He used to go out to relieve himself, and when he had finished, his wife would hold his hand until he reached it. One day, when he was late with her, God revealed to Job in his place: ‘Strike with your foot, this is a cool place to wash. ’” And a drink.” So she was slow to receive him, and he came to her, and God had removed his affliction, and he was in the best condition he had ever been. When she saw him, she said: May God bless you! Have you seen the afflicted Prophet of God? By God, I have never seen a man more similar to him than you when he was healthy? He said: Then I am he. He said: “And he had two troughs: one for wheat and one for barley. So God sent two clouds, and when one of them was on the trough of wheat, it poured gold into it until it overflowed, and the other poured gold into the trough of barley until it overflowed.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And Dhul-Kifl, he said: A righteous man who was not a prophet, guaranteed to the prophet of his people that he would suffice him in the matter of his people, establish them through it, and judge between them with justice. So he did that, and he was called Dhul-Kifl. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There was a judge among the Children of Israel, and death came to him. He said: Who will take my place so that he will not get angry? A man said: I will. So he was called Dhul-Kifl. He spent the whole night praying, and in the morning he would stand and judge between the people. And he mentioned the story. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: Dhul-Kifl was not a prophet, but there was a righteous man among the Children of Israel who prayed one hundred prayers every day. Then he died, and Dhul-Kifl took care of him after him, so he prayed one hundred prayers every day, and he was called Dhul-Kifl. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman narrated it on the authority of Sa’d, the freed slave of Talhah, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Al-Kifl was from the Children of Israel and did not refrain from committing a sin. A woman came to him and he gave her sixty dinars on condition that he would have intercourse with her. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, she trembled and wept. He said: ‘What makes you weep? I force you?’ She said: ‘No, but he did something I have never done before, and nothing made me do it except need.’ He said: ‘You are doing this and I did not do it. Go, it is yours.’ He said: ‘By God, I will never disobey God after this.’ He died that night and in the morning it was written on his door: ‘God has forgiven Al-Kifl.’” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Sa’d, the freed slave of Talhah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn ‘Amr, who said: It includes Dhu Al-Kifl. Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And Dhul-Nun, when he went off in anger, meaning he was angry with his people, and he thought that We would not decree a punishment upon him, meaning that We would not inflict a punishment or affliction upon him for what he did to his people in his anger at them and his flight. He said: And his punishment was that Dhul-Nun took him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and he thought that We would not decree a punishment upon him, he said: He thought that the punishment that befell him would not overtake him. Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated - and he authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, And he called out in the darkness, he said: The darkness of the night, the darkness of the belly of the whale, and the darkness of the sea. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i, Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi in Nawader Al-Usul, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: "The supplication of Dhul-Nun when he was in the belly of the whale: 'There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers.' No Muslim ever supplicated to his Lord with it for anything but that He answered him." Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: "The name of God by which if He is supplicated with it He answers, and if He is asked with it He gives, is the supplication of Yunus ibn Matta. I said: O Messenger of God, is it specifically for Yunus or for all Muslims? He said: It is specifically for Yunus and for all believers if they supplicate with it. Have you not heard the statement of God: 'And thus do We save the believers'? This is a condition from God for whoever supplicates to Him." Al-Hakim also narrated something similar from his hadith. It is proven in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No one should say, 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.' It was also narrated in Sahih and other books on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and it was also narrated in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurairah.
21:89: His saying: 89- And Zachariah meaning, remember the story of Zachariah when he called upon his Lord. He said, My Lord, do not leave me alone, meaning isolated and alone, with no children. We have already discussed this verse in Al Imran. And You are the best of inheritors, meaning the best of those who remain after everyone who dies. So You are sufficient for me if You do not grant me a child, for I know that You will not let Your religion go to waste, and that one of Your servants will do that, whom You choose for it and are pleased with for conveying the message.
21:90: 90- So We answered his prayer and granted him John. This has been fully discussed in Surah Maryam. And We made his wife good for him. Most commentators said that she was barren so God made her fertile, and this is what is meant by making his wife good. It was also said that she was of bad character so God made her of good character. There is nothing wrong with intending both matters, and that is that God, the Almighty, makes her self good so she becomes fertile after she was barren, and makes her morals good so her morals become pleasing after she was unpleasing. The phrase Indeed, they used to hasten to do good deeds is an explanation for what preceded it of His, the Almighty's, kindness to His prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. The pronoun mentioned refers to them, and it was said that it refers to Zachariah, his wife, and John. Then God the Almighty described them as calling upon Him with desire and fear, meaning they would supplicate to Him in times of ease and hardship. It was said that desire is raising the palms of the hands to the sky, and fear is raising their backs. The accusative of desire and fear is on the source: meaning they desire with desire and they fear with fear, or on the cause: meaning for desire and fear, or on the state: meaning desiring and fearing. Talhah ibn Musarraf read and they call upon us with one nun, and Al-A’mash read with a damma on the ra in both of them and a sukun after it. Ibn Waththab read with a fatha on the ra in both of them and a fatha on what they worshipped in both of them. And they were humble before Us, meaning humble and supplicating.
