21:91: 91- And she who guarded her chastity meaning, mention her story, and she is Mary, for she guarded her chastity from what is lawful and unlawful and no man touched her, and she was only mentioned with the prophets even though she was not one of them in order to mention Jesus, and what is in mentioning her story of the dazzling sign So We breathed into her of Our spirit God Almighty added the spirit to him, and it is for the angel as an honor and glorification, and he means the spirit of Jesus And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds Al-Zajjaj said: The sign in it is one because she gave birth to him without a male, and it was said that the estimation according to the doctrine of Sibawayh: And We made her a sign and We made her son a sign like His saying, the Almighty, And God and His Messenger are more worthy that they should be pleased with Him, and the meaning is: God Almighty made their story a complete sign with the multiplication of the signs of each one of them, and it was said that He meant by the sign the comprehensive type, because of the signs of each one of them, and the meaning of guarded is chaste, so she refrained from indecency and other things, and it was said that what is meant by the vagina is the pocket The shirt: meaning that her clothes are pure. An explanation of something like this has already been given in Surat An-Nisa and Surat Maryam.
21:92: Then when He, the Almighty, mentioned the prophets, He explained that they were all united in monotheism, saying: 92- Indeed, this nation of yours is one nation. The nation that is as Ibn Qutaybah said. And similar to it is Indeed, we found our fathers upon a nation, meaning upon a religion, as if he said: Indeed, this religion of yours is one religion, there is no disagreement between the different nations in monotheism, and none deviates from that except the disbelievers who associate partners with God. And it was said that the meaning is: Indeed, this law that I have explained to you in your book is one law. And it was said that the meaning is: Indeed, this religion of yours is one religion, and it is the religion of Islam. And the accusative of one nation is in the state. That is, agreed upon and not different. And it was read that this is your nation with the accusative of your nation as a substitute for the name of in and the predicate is one nation. And the majority read with the nominative of your nation as the predicate and the accusative of nation as in the state as we mentioned. And Al-Farra' said: And Al-Zajjaj is on the cutting because of the coming of the indefinite after the completion of the statement And I am your Lord, so worship Me specifically, do not worship anyone other than Him, whoever He may be.
21:93: 93- And they divided their affair among themselves meaning they split into sects in religion until it became like scattered pieces. Al-Akhfash said: They differed about it, and it is like the first statement. Al-Azhari said: meaning they divided in their affair, so their affair was made accusative by deleting fi, and what is meant by the verse is the polytheists, God condemned them for opposing the truth and taking gods besides God, and it was said that what is meant is all of creation and that they made their affair in their religions into pieces and divided it among themselves, so this one is a monotheist, this one is a Jew, this one is a Christian, this one is a Zoroastrian, and this one is an idol worshipper. Then the Almighty informed that everyone will return to Him, so He said: To Us all will return meaning every one of these sects will return to Us by resurrection, not to anyone else.
21:94: 94- "So whoever does righteous deeds meaning whoever does some righteous deeds, not all of them, because no one is capable of that and he is a believer in God, His messengers, and the Last Day there is no denial for his effort" meaning there is no denial for his work, nor is his reward wasted, and denial is the opposite of faith, and denial is also denial of a blessing and is the opposite of gratitude, it is said he disbelieved ungratefully and ungratefully, and in the reading of Ibn Mas`ud there is no denial for his effort, "and indeed, We are its recorders" meaning We are its guardians, and similar to it is the saying of the Most High: "Never will I allow to be lost the work of any worker among you, whether male or female."
21:95: 95- "And it is forbidden for a town that we have destroyed. Zaid bin Thabit and the people of Medina read and it is forbidden, and the people of Kufa read and it is forbidden." Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose the first reading, and the second reading was narrated from Ali, Ibn Masoud, and Ibn Abbas: They are two dialects like hal and halal. Saeed bin Jubair read "and it is forbidden" with a fatha on the ha', a kasra on the ra', and a fatha on the meem. Ikrimah and Abu Al-Aaliyah read "it is forbidden" with a damma on the ra', a fatha on the ha' and the meem. The meaning of "we have destroyed it is we have decreed its destruction, and the phrase that they will not return" is in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is forbidden, or as an agent for it that takes the place of its predicate. Meaning: It is absolutely impossible for them not to return to Us for recompense. It was said that the la in la yaj’un is redundant: meaning it is forbidden for a village that We destroyed to return to the world after destruction. Abu Ubaidah chose this. It was said that the word haram here means obligatory: meaning it is obligatory for a village. From this is the saying of Al-Khansa’: It is forbidden that I do not see time crying over its sorrows except that I cry over a rock It was said that it is forbidden: meaning it is impossible for them to return to repentance, on the condition that la is redundant. An-Nahhas said: The verse is problematic, and among the best and most important things that have been said about it is what was narrated by Ibn Uyaynah, Ibn Ulayyah, Hisham, Ibn Idris, Muhammad Ibn Fadl, Salim Ibn Hibban, and Mu’alla on the authority of Dawud Ibn Abi Al-Hind on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the meaning of the verse. He said: It is obligatory that they do not return: meaning they do not repent. Az-Zajjaj and Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: There is an implication in the speech, meaning it is forbidden for a village that we have ruled to be exterminated, or to seal the hearts of its people, that any action be accepted from them because they do not return, meaning they do not repent.
21:96: 96- "Until when Gog and Magog are let loose" Until this is what the speech is narrated after, with the deletion of the complement, and it was said that Until this is the one for the purpose. The meaning is: that those mentioned previously will continue as they are until the Day of Resurrection, which is the day the dam of Gog and Magog is opened. "And they will rush from every mound The pronoun refers to Gog and Magog, and the mound is every elevated hill of land, and the plural is ahdab, taken from the hump of the earth, and the meaning of rush" is they hasten, and it was said that they go out. Al-Zajjaj said: And the gait of the wolf when it rushes. It is said that someone rushes in the enemy, rushing with the kasra and damma, naslan, nasulan, and nasalan: meaning that Gog and Magog walk quickly from every elevated place on the earth and disperse in the earth, and it was said that the pronoun in his saying: And they are for all of creation, and the meaning is that they will be gathered to the place of standing and they will rush from every elevated place on the earth. And it was read with the damma of the seen. Al-Mahdawi narrated this on the authority of Ibn Masoud. Al-Tha’labi also narrated this reading on the authority of Mujahid and Abu Al-Sahbaa.
21:97: 97- And the promise has drawn near is in apposition to I have opened, and what is meant is what comes after the opening of the reckoning. Al-Farra', Al-Kisa'i and others said: What is meant by the true promise is the Resurrection, and the waw is redundant, and the meaning is: until when Gog and Magog are opened, the true promise, which is the Resurrection, draws near. So drawn near is the answer to if, and Al-Farra' recited: When we passed the courtyard of the neighborhood and the people were gathered That is, he turned aside, and from this is the saying of the Most High: And he cast him down upon his forehead, and We called to him. Al-Farra’ permitted that the answer to if be then, behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved are staring. The Basrans said: The answer is omitted, and the meaning is: They said, Woe to us. Al-Zajjaj said the same, and the pronoun in then, behold is for the story, or is ambiguous and is explained by what follows, and if is for surprise, and it was said that the speech was completed when he said it, and the meaning is: then, the Resurrection is evident and occurring as if it is coming and present, then he began and said the eyes of those who disbelieved are staring, presenting the report before the subject: that is, the eyes of those who disbelieved are staring, and woe to us is based on the estimation of the saying: We were in heedlessness of this, that is, of this that befell us of futility and reckoning. Rather, we were wrongdoers, they refused to describe themselves as heedless: that is, we were not heedless, rather we were wrongdoers to ourselves by denying and not submitting to the messengers. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We made his wife good for him, he said: The tongue of Zachariah’s wife was long, so God made it good. Something similar was narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: He said: We gave him her son. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: She was barren, so He made her fertile and gave him John from her. Regarding his statement: And they were humble before Us, he said: Submissive. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: And they call upon Us in hope and fear, he said: In hope for the mercy of God and in fear of the punishment of God. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God, the Most High: And they call upon Us in hope and fear, he said: In hope like this and in fear like this, and he spread out his hands, meaning he put their backs to the ground in hope and the opposite in fear. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Ukaim who said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq addressed us and praised and thanked God, then he said: As for what follows, I advise you to fear God, and to praise Him as He deserves, and to mix desire with fear, for God praised Zachariah and his family when He said: Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Indeed, this community of yours is one community, that he said: Indeed, this is your religion, one religion. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Qatadah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding His statement: And they divided their affair among themselves, that he said: They divided their affair means they differed in religion. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed he said: It is obligatory to destroy it that they will not return he said: They will not repent. Sa`id Ibn Mansur, `Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite And it is forbidden for a town he said: It is obligatory to destroy it that they will not return as he said: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them that they would not return to them? `Abd Ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of `Ikrimah and Sa`id Ibn Jubayr. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: From every hill he said: A hill They rush forward he said: They approach. Many hadiths have been narrated describing Gog and Magog and the time of their emergence, but it is not necessary to mention them here, as they are of great benefit.
21:98: God the Almighty explained the state of their deity on the Day of Resurrection, saying: 98- Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hellfire. This is an address from Him the Almighty to the people of Mecca, and what is meant by His saying and what you worship is the idols that they used to worship. The majority read Hasab with a silent sad: meaning the fuel and firewood of Hellfire, and everything that you ignite the fire with or stir it up is hasab, as al-Jawhari said. Abu Ubaidah said: Everything that you throw into the fire, you have made it with, and similar to that is His statement the Almighty: So fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones. Ali ibn Abi Talib and Aisha read Hatab Jahannam with a ta, and Ibn Abbas read Hadhab with a voiced dad. Al-Farra’ said: “It was mentioned to us that in the language of the people of Yemen, hadhab means firewood. The reason for throwing idols into the fire, despite them being inanimate objects that do not understand or sense it, is to rebuke those who worship them, increase the rebuke for them, and multiply their regret. It was also said that they become heated and stick to them, increasing their torture. The phrase “you will enter it” is either a new sentence or a substitute for the firewood of Hell. The address is to them and to what they worship, as a predominance. The lam in laha is for emphasis due to the weakness of the function of the active participle. It was also said that it means upon, and what is meant by entering here is entering. Many scholars said: Jesus, Ezra, and the angels are not included in this verse, because ma is for those who do not understand. If he had intended generality, he would have said and those they worship. Al-Zajjaj said: Because those addressed in this verse are the polytheists of Mecca and no one else.
21:99: 99- If these were gods, they would not have entered it. That is, if these idols were gods as you claim, they would not have entered it: that is, the worshippers and the worshipped would not have entered the fire. It was said that only the worshippers entered, but they entered it and were not gods. In this there is a rebuke and severe rebuke to the worshippers of idols. And all therein are eternal. That is, all the worshippers and worshipped are in the fire eternally and will not leave it.
21:100: 100- Therein they will have sighing meaning for those who have entered the Fire, and sighing is the sound of the breath of one who is distressed, and what is meant here is groaning and heavy breathing, and this was explained previously in Hud. And therein they will not hear meaning some of them will not hear the sighing of others due to the intensity of the terror, and it was said that they will not hear anything, because they will be gathered deaf as the Almighty said, And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf, and they were only deprived of hearing because there is some comfort and comfort in it, and it was said that they will not hear what pleases them, rather they will hear what displeases them.
21:101: Then when the Almighty explained the state of these wretched people, He began to explain the state of the happy ones, saying: 101- Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us meaning the good characteristic which is the best characteristic, which is happiness, and it was said success, or the good report of Paradise, or Paradise itself they will be removed from it referring to those described with that characteristic from it meaning from Hell will be removed because they have become in Paradise.
21:102: 102- They do not hear its hissing sound. The sound and the hissing sound are the sounds you hear from something passing close to you. The meaning is: They do not hear the movement of the Fire and the movement of its people. This sentence is a substitute for expelled, or a state of its pronoun. And they will abide in what their souls desire. That is, they will be permanent. In Paradise, there is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in, as God Almighty said: And therein you will have whatever your souls desire, and therein you will have whatever you ask for.
21:103: 103- The greatest terror will not grieve them. Abu Ja`far and Ibn Muhaisin read will not grieve them with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the zay, and the rest read will not grieve them with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the zay. Al-Yazidi said: Hazana is the language of Quraysh, and ahzana is the language of Tamim. The greatest terror is the terrors of the Day of Resurrection, of resurrection, reckoning, and punishment. And the angels will meet them meaning they will receive them at the gates of Paradise, congratulating them and saying to them, This is your day which you were promised, meaning you were promised in this world and given good report on it. This is what a group of commentators said. What is meant by His statement, Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us up to this point are all those described as having faith and righteous deeds, not Christ, Ezra, and the angels. Most commentators said: When the verse, Indeed, you and what you worship was revealed, Ibn al-Zubayri came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, do you not claim that Aziz is a righteous man, and that Jesus is a righteous man, and that Mary is a righteous woman? He said, Yes. He said: The angels are Jesus, Ezra, and Mary, and they worship besides God, so these are in the Fire. Then God revealed, Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us, and an explanation of who brought this out will come soon, God willing.
21:104: 104- On the Day We fold the heaven like the folding of a scroll for books. Abu Ja`far ibn al-Qa`qa`, Shaibah, al-A`raj, and al-Zuhri read Natwi with a dammah on the first letter and raising the sky. Mujahid read Natwi with a fathah on the second letter, built for the agent, meaning that God folds the heaven. The rest read Natwi with the nun of majesty and the accusative of Yawm. His saying, We return it, means We return it on the Day We fold the heaven. It was said that it is a substitute for the deleted pronoun in You are promised, and the meaning is: those whom you promised on the Day We fold. It was said that it is based on His saying that fear will not grieve them, and it was said that it is based on His saying that you will meet them. It was said that it is related to something deleted, which is Remember, and this is clearer and more evident. Folding is the opposite of spreading, and it was said that it is erasure. What is meant by the sky is the genus, and the scroll is the page, meaning folding like the folding of a scroll. It was said that the scroll is the instrument, and it is derived from the argument, which is correspondence, and its origin is from the scroll, which is the bucket. It is said: I argued with the man. If you take out a bucket and he takes out a bucket, then it is borrowed for correspondence and review in speech, and from it is the saying of Al-Fadl bin Al-Abbas bin Utbah bin Abi Lahab: Whoever debates with me debates with a noble man who fills the bucket to the limit of distress. Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr and Ibn Jarir read As-Sajjil with a damma on the seen and the jim and a shaddah on the lam. Al-A'mash and Talhah read it with a fatha on the seen, a sukoon on the jim and a light lam. The folding in this verse has two possible meanings: one is folding, which is the opposite of spreading, as in His statement: And the heavens are rolled up in His right hand. The second is concealment, obscurity and erasure, because God, the Exalted, erases and obliterates their signs and clouds their stars. It was said that As-Sajjil is the name of an angel, who is the one who folds up the books of the sons of Adam. It was also said that it is the name of a scribe for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but the first is more correct. Al-A'mash, Hafs, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Yahya and Khalaf read it for all the books, while the rest read it for the book, and it is related to an omitted word in the state of the register: i.e. like the folding of the register, being for the books or an attribute of it: i.e. being for the books, because the books are the pages and what is written in them, so He recorded some of their parts, and folding is related to it in reality. As for the second reading, the book is a source, and the lam is for al-Sharh 94:that is, as the scroll is folded for writing: that is, to write in it, or for what is written in it of the many meanings, and this is on the assumption that what is meant by folding is the first meaning, which is the opposite of spreading. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it, that is, as We began them in the wombs of their mothers and brought them out to the earth barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, thus We will repeat them on the Day of Resurrection. So the first creation is the object of We will repeat, understood and explained by We will repeat it mentioned, or the object of We began, and what is a collective or relative pronoun, and the kaf is related to something omitted, that is, We will repeat like what We began, We will repeat it. In this way, the first is a circumstance of Our beginning, or a state, and the first of creation was specifically mentioned to depict creation from nothingness, and the purpose is to clarify the validity of the return by analogy to the beginning, due to the inclusion of the inherent possibility of both of them. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: We will destroy every soul as it was the first time, and on this basis the speech is connected to His saying: On the Day We will fold up the heaven, and it was said that the meaning is We will change the heaven, then We will return it once again after Folding it and disappearing, and the first is more appropriate, and it is like His statement: And you have certainly come to Us individually as We created you the first time, then the Almighty said: “A promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.” The word promise is in the accusative case as a source: meaning, We promised a promise binding upon Us to fulfill and fulfil. It is resurrection and re-establishment, then the Almighty confirmed that by saying: Indeed, We will do it. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of Indeed, We will do it is: We were able to do whatever We willed, and it was said that We will do what We promised you, and similar to it is His statement: His promise was to be fulfilled.
21:105: 105 And We have written in the Psalms The Psalms originally mean books. It is said that it was written, and based on this, it is correct to apply the Psalms to the Torah and the Gospel, and to the Book of David called the Psalms. It was said that what is meant here is the Book of David, and the meaning of after the remembrance is the Preserved Tablet. It was said that it is the Torah: meaning, by God, We have written in the Book of David after what We wrote in the Torah or after what We wrote in the Preserved Tablet that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants. Al-Zajjaj said: The Psalms are the plural of books: the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an, because the Psalms and the Book have the same meaning. It is said that you wrote and you wrote. What he said is supported by Hamza's reading of the Psalms with a damma on the zay, as it is the plural of zabar. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of My righteous servants will inherit it. It has been said that what is meant is the land of Paradise. Those who say this provide evidence for this with the words of God the Almighty: “And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, Who has fulfilled His promise to us and has given us the land as an inheritance. ’” It has also been said that it is the Holy Land. It has also been said that it is the land of the disbelieving nations, which our Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his nation will inherit by conquering it. It has also been said that what is meant by this is the Children of Israel, based on the words of God the Almighty: And We gave as an inheritance to the people who were oppressed the eastern regions of the earth and the western regions which We had blessed. It appears that this is good report for the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that they will inherit the land of the disbelievers, and most of the commentators agree with this. Hamzah read My servants with a sukoon on the ya’, while the rest read it with a fathah on it.
21:106: 106- Indeed in this is a message meaning that in what was mentioned in this surah of preaching and warning there is a message that is sufficient. It is said about this thing that there is a message, a language, and a message: meaning it is sufficient. It was said that the reference in His saying: Indeed in this is to the Qur'an for a people who worship meaning busy with the worship of God and concerned with it, and worship is submission and humility, and they are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the head of worship is prayer.
21:107: 107- And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds. That is, We have not sent you, O Muhammad, with the laws and rulings except as a mercy to all people. The exception is devoid of the most general conditions and reasons: that is, We have not sent you for any reason except for Our vast mercy, for what you were sent with is a cause for happiness in both worlds. It has been said that the meaning of it being a mercy to the disbelievers is that they were safe from being swallowed up, transformed, and exterminated. It has also been said that what is meant by the worlds are the believers in particular, and the former is more appropriate based on the evidence of His, the Most High, saying: And God would not punish them while you are among them.
21:108: Then the Almighty explained that the origin of that mercy is monotheism and innocence from polytheism, saying: 108- Say, 'I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your God is one God.' If ma is a relative pronoun, then the meaning is that what is revealed to me is that His description is limited to oneness and does not go beyond it to what contradicts or opposes it. If ma is a comprehensive pronoun, then the meaning is that the revelation to me is limited to God's monopolization of oneness. The reason for that is that restriction is always for what follows only. The first only is to restrict the description to the thing, like your saying only Zayd stands: meaning, none stands except Zayd. The second is to restrict the thing to the ruling, like your saying only Zayd stands: meaning, he has nothing but the attribute of standing. So are you Muslims? Submissive and sincere to worship and to the monotheism of God, the Almighty.
21:109: 109- "But if they turn away meaning, they turn away from Islam, say to them, I have warned you on equal terms" meaning, I have informed you and you of war, no peace between us, being on equal terms in the notification. I did not specify some of you over others, as in the saying of the Most High: "But if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them on equal terms" meaning, inform them that you have broken the covenant in a way that made them equal. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, I have informed you of what is revealed to me on an equal basis in knowledge of it, and I will not reveal to anyone anything that I have concealed from others. "And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far" meaning, I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far, and it is the victory of the people of Islam over the people of disbelief and its people. It was said that what you are promised is the Day of Resurrection, and it was said that I have warned you of war, but I do not know what I am being warned about in fighting you.
21:110: 110- He knows what you say openly and knows what you conceal. That is, He, glory be to Him, knows what you say openly of disbelief and slander against Islam and its people, and what you conceal and hide.
21:111: 111- And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you meaning, I do not know, perhaps the respite is a trial for you and a test to see how He has made you. And enjoyment for a time meaning, and enjoyment for a specified time required by His wisdom.
21:112: Then the Almighty narrated the supplication of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: 112- He said, 'My Lord, judge with truth' meaning, judge between me and these deniers with what is the truth with You, so He entrusted the matter to Him, may He be glorified. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa' and Ibn Muhaysin read Lord with a damma on the ba'. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake according to grammarians, as they do not accept a man coming until he says, O man. Ad-Dahhak, Talhah, and Ya'qub read Ahkam with a severing of the hamza, a fatha on the kaf, and a damma on the meem: meaning, Muhammad said, My Lord, judge with truth. It was read in the imperative form: meaning, say, O Muhammad. Lord is in the accusative case, because it is a vocative added to the pronoun, and the Almighty answered the supplication of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and punished them at Badr, then made the outcome, victory, and triumph for His believing servants, and all praise is due to God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Lord of the worlds. Then He, the Most High, said, completing that story: And our Lord, the Most Gracious, is the One sought for help against what you describe of disbelief and denial. So Our Lord is the subject and The Most Gracious is its predicate: meaning He is the One with the most mercy for His servants. The One sought for help is another predicate: meaning He is sought for help in matters that include what you describe, that you have power, and your saying: Is this anything but a human being like you? and your saying: The Most Gracious has taken a son. The description is often used in the Book of God to mean lying, like His saying: And for you is woe for what you describe, and His saying: He will repay them for their description. Al-Mufaddal and Al-Salami read what they describe with the lower ya’. The rest read it with the upper ya’ as an address. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse was revealed: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will surely enter it, the polytheists said: So the angels, Jesus, and Ezra are worshipping besides God. So the verse was revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it, Jesus, Ezra, and the angels. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on his authority that he said: Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayri came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: You claim that God revealed this verse to you: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will surely enter it. Ibn Al-Zubayri said: You have worshipped the sun, the moon, the angels, Ezra, and Jesus, son of Mary. All of these will be in Hell with our gods. Then the verse was revealed: “And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him. And they say, ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’ They only compare him to you out of argument. Indeed, they are a quarrelsome people.” Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. Abu Dawud in his Naskh, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Tabarani also narrated from another chain of transmission on his authority something similar but longer. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us, he said: Jesus, Ezra, and the angels. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: The pebbles of Hell, he said: The trees of Hell. In its chain of transmission is Al-Awfi. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority from another chain of transmission that the pebbles of Hell is its fuel. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority. He said: It is the firewood of Hell in Zanjiyah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: They do not hear its hissing sound, he said: Snakes on the path say, His, hiss. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi regarding his statement: They do not hear its hissing sound, he said: Snakes on the path sting them, and when they sting them they say, His, hiss. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hatib who said: Ali was asked about this verse: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us He said: It refers to Uthman and his companions. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: They will not hear its hissing sound He said: The people of Paradise will not hear the hissing sound of Hell when they descend to their abode in Paradise. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The greatest terror will not grieve them He said: The last blast. In its chain of transmission is al-Awfi. Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “There are three on the mounds of musk who will not be terrified by the greatest terror on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:a man who leads people while they are pleased with him, a man who calls to prayer every day and night, and a slave who fulfilled the rights of God and the rights of his masters.” Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Ali regarding his statement: Like the folding of a scroll He said: A king. The scroll is a king, so when he ascends with seeking forgiveness, he says: Write it down as light. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Baqir who said: The scroll is an angel. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa`i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah in al-Ma`rifah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, who authenticated it, narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas who said: The scroll is a scribe for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn `Adi and Ibn `Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a scribe called the scroll, and this is what God said: The Day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for books. He said: Just as the scroll rolls up the book, so will We roll up the heaven. Ibn Mandah, Abu Nu`aym in al-Ma`rifah, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib and Ibn `Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a scribe called the scroll, so God revealed: The Day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for books. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation after narrating this hadith: This is very strange from the hadith of Nafi` from Ibn `Umar and is not authentic at all. He said: Likewise, what was mentioned above from Ibn `Abbas from the narration of Abu Dawud and others is also not authentic. A group of hadith masters have stated that it is fabricated, although it is in Sunan Abi Dawood, among them is our great hadith master Abu Al-Hajjaj Al-Muzani, and I have devoted a separate section to this hadith, praise be to God. He said: Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir took it upon himself to denounce this hadith and rejected it completely, and said: We do not know of anyone among the Companions whose name was Sajjil, and the scribes of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) were well-known, and there was no one among them whose name was Sajjil. He was right, may God have mercy on him, in that, and it is one of the strongest pieces of evidence for the fabrication of this hadith. As for those who mentioned this among the names of the Companions, they relied on this hadith and nothing else, and God knows best. He said: What is correct from Ibn Abbas is that Sajjil is the document, as Ali bin Abi Talhah and Al-Awfi said from him. Mujahid, Qatadah and more than one person stated this explicitly, and Ibn Jarir chose it because it is well-known in the language. Based on this, the meaning of the statement: The Day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for a book: i.e. on the book, meaning what is written, like His statement: So when they had submitted and he laid it upon his forehead i.e. on the forehead, and there are similar examples in the language, and God knows best. I said: As for this being the correct view from Ibn Abbas, no, because Ali bin Abi Talha and Al-Awfi are weak, so it is better to rely on the linguistic meaning and to go with it. Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The record is the man, Ibn Mardawayh added in the Ethiopian dialect. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas in the interpretation of the verse, who said: Like folding the page over the book. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: As We began the first creation, We will repeat it, meaning: We will destroy everything as it was the first time. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, he said: the Qur’an, that the earth, he said: the land of Paradise. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him: And We had already written in the Psalms, he said: the books, after the remembrance, he said: the Torah. Al-Awfi is in his chain of transmission. Saeed bin Mansour also narrated from him, he said: the Psalms, the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an. The remembrance is the origin from which these books were copied, which is in the heaven, and the earth is the land of Paradise. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants, he said: The land of Paradise. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding the verse: God the Almighty informed in the Torah and the Psalms and His previous work before the heavens and the earth were created that He would inherit the earth for the nation of Muhammad and admit them to Paradise, and they are the righteous. Regarding his statement: A message for a people who worship, he said: Knowledgeable. In its chain of transmission is Ali ibn Abi Talhah. Saeed ibn Mansur and Ibn Mundhir narrated from Abu Hurairah: Indeed in this is a message for a people who worship, he said: The five daily prayers. Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym and Al-Daylami narrated from Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed in this is a message for a people who worship, he said: In the five daily prayers is a preoccupation for worship.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbasi that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this verse: To convey to a people who worship God. He said: It refers to the five daily prayers in congregation in the Sacred Mosque. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds. He said: “Whoever believes, mercy will be granted to him in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever does not believe will be spared from the torment that befalls nations in this world in the immediate world, such as sinking, transformation, and stoning.” Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: “It was said: O Messenger of God, invoke God against the polytheists. He said: I was not sent to curse, but rather I was sent as a mercy.” At-Tayalisi, Ahmad, al-Tabarani, and Abu Nu’aym narrated in al-Dala’il on the authority of Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God has sent me as a mercy to the worlds and a guide for the righteous. Ahmad and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Salman that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Any man of my nation whom I insult or curse in my anger, I am only a man from the children of Adam, I get angry as they get angry, and I was sent as a mercy to the worlds, so make it a blessing for him on the Day of Resurrection.” Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am only a mercy sent down. The meaning of this has been narrated in many ways. Ibn Abi Khathima and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he saw so-and-so, who was one of the Umayyads, on the pulpit delivering a sermon to the people, and this upset the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: {And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time} meaning: this is the angel. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: {And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you} meaning: what I have informed you of about the punishment and the Hour, perhaps delaying that from you is a trial for you. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: He said, ‘My Lord, judge with justice.’ He said: God only judges with justice, and he only hastens to do so in this world, asking his Lord.
22:1: It is seventy-eight verses. Scholars differed as to whether it was revealed in Mecca or Medina. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Hajj was revealed in Medina. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said: Surat Al-Hajj was revealed in Medina except for four Meccan verses of the Qur’an: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet to the torment of a barren day. Al-Qurtubi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was Meccan except for three verses, and it was said four verses to the torment of the burning fire. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Naqqash that ten verses of it were revealed in Medina. Al-Qurtubi said: The majority said: The surah is mixed, some of it is Meccan and some of it is Medinan. He said: This is the correct view. Al-Azizi said: It is one of the wonders of the surahs. It was revealed during the night and the day, during travel and at home, in Mecca and Medina, in peace and war, abrogating and abrogated, clear and ambiguous. Concerning its merits, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: “I said: O Messenger of God, is Surah Al-Hajj superior to the rest of the Qur’an because of its two prostrations?” He said: Yes, so whoever does not prostrate in them should not recite them. Al-Tirmidhi said: The chain of transmission of this hadith is not strong. Abu Dawud narrated in Al-Marasil and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Surah Al-Hajj is superior to the rest of the Qur’an because of its two prostrations. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Isma’ili, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umar that he used to prostrate twice during Hajj and said: This Surah is superior to the rest of the Qur’an because of its two prostrations. It has been narrated on the authority of many of the Companions that it contains two prostrations, and this is what Ibn Al-Mubarak, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq said. Some of them said: It contains one prostration, and this is the opinion of Sufyan Al-Thawri. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i. When the speech at the end of the previous Surah was drawn to mentioning the Resurrection and what came before and after it, the Almighty began in this Surah by mentioning the Resurrection and its terrors, urging piety, which is the most beneficial provision, so He said: 1- O mankind, fear your Lord, meaning beware of His punishment by doing what He has commanded you to do of obligations and leaving what He has forbidden you of forbidden things. The word people includes all those who are accountable, both those who are present and those who will be present, as has been established in its place. We have already presented some of the verification of that in Surah Al-Baqarah. The phrase Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing is an explanation of what came before it of the command to piety. The earthquake is a severe movement, and its origin is from zala ‘an al-ma’akun meaning he moved from it, and zala God qadamhu meaning he moved it. The repetition of the letter indicates emphasis of the meaning, and it is from adding the source to its subject, and according to this: the earthquake, which is one of the signs of the Hour that will occur in this world before the Day of Resurrection. This is the opinion of the majority, and it was said that it will occur in the middle of the month of Ramadan, and after it the rising of the sun. From the west, and it was said that the source here is added to the circumstance, which is the hour, making it a function of the object, or by estimating in as in his saying: Rather, the plotting of the night and the day and it is mentioned in his saying: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake. It was said that in expressing it with the thing there is an indication that the minds are incapable of comprehending its essence.
22:2: 2- On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed. The circumstance is in the accusative case with what follows it, and the pronoun refers to al-Zalzalah 99:that is, when you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from her infant and will be heedless of it. Qatrib said: She will be distracted and busy, and he recited the words of the poet: A blow that removes the inspiration from its place of rest and distracts the friend from his friend It was said that you forget, it was said that you play, and it was said that you amuse yourself, and these meanings are close. Al-Mubarrad said: “Ma fi ma ‘ra’ta’ means a source: i.e. she forgets about breastfeeding. He said: This indicates that this earthquake is in this world, since there is no pregnancy or breastfeeding after the Resurrection, unless it is said: Whoever dies pregnant will give birth to her pregnancy due to the terror, and whoever dies breastfeeding will be resurrected likewise. This is said as an example, just as it is said: “A day that will make children gray-haired.” It was said that it is from the first blast. He said: It is possible that the Hour is an expression for the terrors of the Day of Resurrection, as in His statement: Poverty and hardship will touch them, and they will be shaken. The meaning of and every pregnant woman will give birth to her pregnancy is that she will throw her fetus before it is fully formed due to the intensity of the terror, just as a breastfeeding woman leaves her child without breastfeeding. Therefore, and you will see the people drunk. The majority read it with the opening of the ta’ and the ra’, addressing each one: i.e. the one who sees them will see them as if they were drunk. But they are not drunk in reality. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read sakāra without an alif, and the rest read it with its confirmation, and they are two languages that pluralize sakrān, like kaslā. And lazy, and when the Almighty denied them drunkenness, He explained the reason for which they resembled drunkards, saying: But the punishment of God is severe. Because of this severity and great terror, their minds went astray, and their understandings were disturbed, so they became like drunkards, with the common denominator of the loss of perfect discrimination and sound perception. And it was read Watra with a damma on the ta’ and a fatha on the ra’, attributed to the addressee of ara’aytuka: meaning, do you think they are drunk? Al-Farra’ said: This reading has a good face in Arabic.
22:3: Then when He, the Almighty, wanted to argue with those who deny the resurrection, He presented before that an introduction that includes all those who argue, saying: 3- And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge. The parsing of such a structure has already been mentioned in His statement: And among the people is he who says, and the meaning of in God is about God and His power, and the location of without knowledge is the accusative case of state. The meaning is that he disputes about God's power and claims that He is not able to resurrect without knowledge that he knows, nor an argument that he presents. And follows in what he says, practices, argues with, and argues about every rebellious devil, meaning one who rebels against God, and he is the rebellious one, so called because he is devoid of all good, and what is meant is Satan and his soldiers or the leaders of the infidels who call their followers to disbelief. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: It was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, who was a frequent arguer, and he denied that God is able to revive the dead. It was said that it was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah and Utbah bin Rabi'ah.
22:4: 4- It was written for him that whoever takes him as a guardian meaning it was written for Satan, and the subject of it was written is that whoever takes him as a guardian, then he will mislead him meaning it is Satan's business to mislead him from the path of truth, so his saying that he will mislead him is the answer to the condition if you make it a conditional or the predicate of the relative pronoun if you make it a relative pronoun, so Satan was described with two descriptions: the first is that he is a willful one, and the second is what is indicated by the sentence It was written for him etc. And the sentence and guides him to the punishment of the Blaze is conjoined with the sentence misleads him: meaning it leads him to do what will cause him to be in the punishment of the Blaze.
22:5: Then the Almighty mentioned what is meant by the argument against the disbelievers after finishing that introduction, and He said: 5- O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection Al-Hasan read the Resurrection with the opening of the 'ayn, which is a language, and the majority read it with the sukoon, and their doubt may be about its occurrence or its possibility. The meaning is: If you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then look at the beginning of your creation, that is, the creation of your father Adam, so that doubt may be removed from you, suspicion may be lifted, and false suspicion may be refuted. For indeed, We created you from dust within the creation of your father Adam. Then We created you from a sperm-drop, that is, from semen. It is called a sperm-drop because of its smallness, and a sperm-drop is a small amount of water. It may be attributed to a lot of it, and the sperm: the drop, it is said Natuf Yantuf: meaning drop, and Lailat Natoof: meaning permanent drop Then from a clot and the clot: congealed blood, and the clot: the thick blood: meaning fresh or frozen, and it was said that it is very red and what is meant is the congealed blood formed from semen Then from a lump of flesh which is a piece of flesh the size of what the chewer chews, it is formed from the clot Mukhallaqa in the accusative case is an attribute of a lump: meaning clearly created and clearly depicted And not created meaning its creation has not become clear nor has its depiction appeared. Ibn al-A’rabi said: Mukhallaqa means that its creation has begun, and not created means it has not been depicted. Most said: What completed its creation by breathing the soul into it is the Mukhallaqa and it is the one who was born to completion, and what fell was not created, meaning not alive by completing its creation with the soul. Al-Farra’ said: Mukhallaqa is the one whose creation is complete, and not created: the miscarriage, and from it the saying of the poet: Is it okay to cry when you are not well-mannered? Where is the firmness and modesty? The lam in lanbayn lakum is related to our creation: that is, we created you in this manner to show you the perfection of our power by our management of the stages of your creation. And We place in the wombs whom We will. Abu Hatim narrated from Abu Zaid from al-Mufaddal from Asim that he read taqrur in the accusative case in apposition to nabayyun. The majority read naqr in the nominative case as a resumption: that is, and we place. Al-Zajjaj said: naqrur is in the nominative case only, because the meaning is not that we did that to place in the wombs whom We will. The meaning of the verse is: and we place in the wombs whom We will so that it will not be a miscarriage for a specified term, which is the time of birth. He said what We will and did not say whom We will, because it refers to the fetus when it is inanimate before the soul is breathed into it. It was read libayyun to make clear, wa-yaqrur to make clear, and yakhrajum to make clear with the dhammah in the three verbs. Ibn Abi Wathab read ma-nasha with the kasrah on the nun, "then We bring you forth as a child," that is, We bring you forth from the wombs of your mothers as a child: that is, children. He only made it singular to mean the genus that includes the one and the many. Al-Zajjaj said, A child means children, and the mention of the group indicates this: meaning, in our exodus. The Arabs often use the name one to refer to a group, and from this is the saying of the poet: He makes me yearn for her love and makes me realize that the critics are not my prince Al-Mubarrad said: It is a noun that is used as a verbal noun like contentment and justice, and it applies to both singular and plural. God the Almighty said: Or the child who has not yet appeared. Ibn Jarir said: It is in the accusative case as a specification like His saying: But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, and there is some distance in it. The apparent is that it is in the accusative case as a state with the aforementioned interpretation. The child is used for the young from the time of his separation until puberty. Then that you may reach your full strength. It was said that it is the reason for We will bring you out in apposition to another reason appropriate to it, as if it was said: We will bring you out so that you may grow up little by little, then that you may reach your full strength. It was said that then is redundant, and the meaning is that you may reach your full strength. It was said that it is in apposition to We will make you grow up little by little, then that you may reach your full strength. The most severe is the perfection of reason, strength, and discrimination. Fil is what is between thirty and forty. We have already discussed this in detail in Al-An’am. And among you is he who dies means before reaching his full strength. It was read yatawafa in the active form. The majority read "yutawafa in the passive form, And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit and lowest age", meaning the worst and lowest of it, which is old age and senility, so that he does not understand. For this reason, the Almighty said: "So that he may not know anything after knowledge", meaning anything of things, or something of knowledge. The meaning is that he becomes, after he had knowledge of things and understanding of them, without knowledge or understanding. Similar to this is His statement: "Indeed, We created man in the best of stature. Then We returned him to the lowest of the low", and His statement: "And whom We grant life to, We reverse him in creation, And you will see the earth lifeless", this is another argument for the resurrection, for the Almighty argued that the earth is revived by sending down water as evidence for the revival of the dead, and the lifeless is the dry that does not grow anything. Ibn Qutaybah said: meaning dead and dry like fire when it is extinguished. It was said that it is threshing, and threshing is the threshing. From this is the statement of Al-A'sha: A dead woman said, Why is your body so pale? I see your clothes are worn out and tired. It was said that it is the one from which the dew has gone, and it was said that it is lost, and the meaning of these sayings is close. So when We send down upon it water, it quivers and swells. What is meant by water here is rain, and the meaning of quivered is moved, and shaking is intense movement. It is said that I shook something and it quivered: meaning I moved it and it moved. The meaning is: it moved with the plant, because the plant does not come out of it until it removes some of it from the other in a real removal, so he called it shaking metaphorically. Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning is that its plant quivered, so he deleted the complement, and its shaking is intense movement, and shaking in plants is more apparent than in the ground, and the meaning of quivered is it rose, and it was said that it swelled. The meaning is one, and its origin is increase. It is said that something swelled if it increased, and from it comes riba and rabwah. Yazid bin Al-Qaqa’ and Khalid bin Ilyas read wa-rab’at meaning it rose until it became like a hill, which is what protects the people on a high place called rabi’, rabi’ah, and rabi’ah. wa-anbat meaning it brought forth of every beautiful pair meaning of every beautiful type and desirable color, and bahja means beauty.
22:6: And the sentence 6 - That is because God is the Truth is a resumption, after he mentioned the need of the existents for Him, the Most High, and their subjugation according to His will and power. He then said these articles, which are proof that He, the Most High, is the Truth, and that He is the One who is unique in bringing the dead back to life, and that He is capable of all things. The meaning is: He is the One who is unique in these matters and that it is His nature and no one else is claimed to be capable of any of them, so He, the Most High, indicated with this that He is the true, absolute, rich Truth, and that the existence of every existent is derived from Him, and the Truth is the existent that does not change or disappear, and it was said that He has the right over His servants, and it was said that He is the Truth in His actions. Al-Zajjaj said: That is in the nominative case: meaning the matter is what He described to you and explained that God is the Truth. He said: It is permissible for that to be in the accusative case.
22:7: Then the Almighty informed us that 7- The Hour is coming meaning in the future. It was said that a verb must be implied: meaning, and that you may know that the Hour is coming without a doubt meaning without a doubt or hesitation. The phrase without a doubt is a second predicate for the Hour, or in the accusative case as a state. Then the Almighty informed us about the resurrection, saying: And that God will resurrect those in the graves and will reward them for their deeds, if good then good and if evil then evil, and that this will inevitably happen. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, `Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa`i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of al-Hasan and others on the authority of `Imran ibn Husayn who said: “When the verse, ‘O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing,’ was revealed to him while he was on a journey. He said: ‘Do you know what day that is?’ They said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘That is the day when God will say to Adam, ‘Send those sent to Hell.’ He said: ‘O Lord, what are those sent to Hell?’ He said: ‘Out of every thousand, one hundred and ninety-nine will go to Hell, and one to Paradise.’ The Muslims began to cry. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘Come close, follow the right path, and be glad, for there has never been a prophethood except that there was ignorance before it. So the number of days is taken from ignorance. If it is complete, then it is completed from the hypocrites. And the example of you and the nations is like a mark on the arm of a beast, or like a mole on the face of a tree.’” The camel's side, then he said: I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, so they said Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise, so they said Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise, so they said Allahu Akbar. He said: I do not know whether he said two-thirds or not. At-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, with a similar chain of transmission, and he said at the end of it: "Work and be glad, for by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are with two creatures that were not with anything except that they multiplied it: Gog and Magog, and whoever died from the children of Adam and from the children of Iblis. So some of what they were feeling was relieved from the people, and he said: Work and be glad, for by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are among the people like a mole on the side of a camel, or like a mark on the arm of an animal." Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas, with a similar chain of transmission, from the Prophet, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas, with a similar hadith, in the Two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar, and at the end of it he said: “From Gog and Magog are a thousand and from you is one. Are you among the nations anything but like a black hair on a white bull, or like a white hair on a black bull?” Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd Bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, regarding his statement: It was written for him, he said: It was written for Satan. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid something similar: Whoever takes him as a guardian, he said: follows him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, the Sunan scholars and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) told us, and he is the truthful and the one who is believed: “The creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty days as a drop of semen, then he is a clot for a similar period, then he is a lump of flesh for a similar period, then God sends to him an angel who breathes the spirit into him, and he is commanded with four words to write down his provision, his life span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy. By the One besides Whom there is no god, one of you may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only an arm’s length between him and it, then the book is sent down to him and he does the deeds of the people of Hell and enters it. And one of you may do the deeds of the people of Hell until there is only an arm’s length between him and it, then the book overtakes him and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it.” There are many hadiths on this subject. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: created and uncreated, he said: Created is what was alive, and uncreated is what was aborted. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi`un. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Of every beautiful pair, he said: Good. Abdullah Ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd on the authority of Muadh Ibn Jabal who said: Whoever knows that God Almighty is true, and that the Hour will come to him without a doubt, and that God will resurrect those in the graves will enter Paradise.
22:8: 8- His saying And among mankind is he who disputes about God meaning about God, like the saying of the one who said: The angels are daughters of God, and the Messiah is the son of God, and Ezra is the son of God. It was said that it was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and it was said about Abu Jahl, and it was said that it is general for everyone who attempts to mislead and seduce people. In any case, the consideration is what the wording indicates, even if the reason is specific. The meaning of the wording is: And among mankind is a group who disputes about God, so this includes everyone who disputes about the essence of God, or His attributes, or His clear laws. Without knowledge is in the accusative case as a state: meaning being without knowledge. It was said that what is meant by knowledge is necessary knowledge, and by guidance is theoretical, inferential knowledge. It is better to interpret the action as general, and to interpret guidance as its linguistic meaning, which is direction. What is meant by the enlightening book is the Qur’an, and the enlightening is the clear, evident proof, and evident evidence. If it is included under His statement, without knowledge, then singling it out is like singling out Gabriel after mentioning the angels, because he is the perfect individual who excels over other individuals of knowledge. As for those who interpret knowledge as necessary and guidance as inferential, they interpret the book here as auditory evidence, so the verse includes the negation of rational evidence, whether necessary or inferential, and includes the negation of transmitted evidence in all its categories, and what we have mentioned is more appropriate. It was said that what is meant by this disputant in this verse is the disputant in the first verse, I mean His statement, And among mankind is he who disputes about God without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil, and many of the commentators said this, and the repetition is for exaggeration in the blame, as you say to a man, blaming and rebuking him, Did you do this, did you do that? It is possible that the repetition is because He described him in each verse with an increase in what He described him with in the other verse, so it is as if He said: And among the people is he who disputes about God and follows every rebellious devil without knowledge nor guidance nor an enlightening Book to mislead from the path of God. End quote. It was said that the first verse is about the imitators as an active participle. The second is about the imitators as a passive participle. The second is general in every misguidance and argument. The accusative of the second of his conjunction is in the state of the agent of the one who argues, and conjunction is the side, and the man's two sides are his right and left. There are two views in its interpretation: The first is that what is meant by it is he who twists his neck in joy and arrogance. Al-Zajjaj mentioned its meaning. He said: This is how the arrogant is described. The meaning is: And among the people is he who disputes about God arrogantly. Al-Mubarrad said: The conjunction is what is bent of the neck.
22:9: The second aspect is that what is meant by his saying: 9- The second of his affection is turning away: i.e. turning away from the remembrance, as Al-Farra' and Al-Mufaddal and others said, like the saying of God the Almighty: And he turned away arrogantly as if he did not hear it and His saying: They turned their heads, and His saying: He turned away and distanced himself, and the lam in to mislead from the path of God is related to to argue: i.e. his purpose is to mislead from the path even if he does not admit that, and it was read to mislead with the opening of the ya' so that the lam is the lam of the consequence as if he made his misguidance the goal of his argument, and the phrase for him in this world is disgrace is a new sentence explaining what will happen to him because of his argument of punishment. Disgrace is humiliation, and that is because of the punishment he will receive in this world of hastened torment and bad reputation on people's tongues. It was said that worldly disgrace is killing as happened on the day of Badr And We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the burning fire i.e. the punishment of the burning fire.
22:10: And the reference in His saying: 10- That is to what preceded of worldly and otherworldly torment, and it is a subject whose predicate is for what your hands have put forth. And the ba is for causality: meaning that torment that has descended upon you is because of what your hands have put forth of disbelief and sins, and the hand is used to refer to the whole body because directing sins usually occurs with it, and the place of an and what follows it in His saying: And that God is not unjust to His servants is the nominative case as it is the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning that the matter is that He, glory be to Him, does not torment His servants without sin. We have already discussed this verse at the end of Al Imran, so we will not repeat it.
22:11: 11- And among the people is he who worships God on the verge This is a statement of the dissension of the people of dissension. Al-Wahidi said: Most of the commentators said: The verge is doubt, and its origin is from the edge of something, which is its edge, like the edge of a mountain or a wall, for the one standing on it is not stable, and the one who worships God on the verge is restless in his religion, not steadfast and reassured, like the one who is on the edge of a mountain or the like, who is disturbed and his standing is weakened, so it was said to the one who doubts his religion that he worships God on the verge, because he is not certain of His promise and threat, unlike the believer because he worships Him with certainty and insight, so he is not on the verge. It was said that the conditional letter is: that is, among the people is he who worships God on a condition, and the condition is His statement: If good befalls him, he is reassured by it, meaning worldly good such as prosperity, health, fertility, and abundant wealth. The meaning of reassured by it is that he remains steadfast in his religion and continues in his worship, or his heart is reassured by that good that befell him. But if a trial befalls him, meaning something that befalls him of harm that befalls his family, wealth, or himself, he turns back on his face, meaning he apostatizes and returns to the face he was on of disbelief. Then He explained his state after turning back on his face, saying, He has lost this world and the Hereafter, meaning they are gone from him and he has lost them, so he has no mention of the spoils and good praise in this world, nor of the reward and what God has prepared for the righteous among His servants in the Hereafter. Mujahid, Humayd ibn Qays, Al-A’raj, Al-Zuhri, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read losing this world and the Hereafter in the form of an active participle in the accusative case as a state. It was read in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject. The reference in his saying: That is to the loss of this world and the Hereafter, and it is a subject and its predicate is That is the clear loss, meaning the clear and apparent, like which there is no loss.
22:12: 12- He calls upon besides God that which neither harms him nor benefits him. That is, this one who turned back on his face and returned to disbelief calls upon besides God: that is, he worships, going beyond the worship of God to the worship of idols, that which neither harms him if he abandons its worship, nor benefits him if he worships it, because that worshipped object is inanimate and has no power to harm or benefit. The reference in the words that is to the supplication understood from the verb he calls upon, and the demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is it is the distant misguidance, that is, from the truth and guidance, borrowed from the misguidance of the one who took a path other than the path and became distant from it through his misguidance. Al-Farra' said: The distant, the long.
22:13: 13- He calls upon one whose harm is closer than his benefit. Calls means says, and the sentence confirms what preceded it, that this supplication is a far-fetched misguidance. Idols have no benefit in any way, rather they are pure harm to the one who worships them, because he entered the Fire because of worshipping them. The use of the comparative form with no benefit at all is to exaggerate the ugliness of the state of that supplicant, or it is from the category of And either we or you are upon guidance or in manifest error. The lam is the one that introduces the oath, and from is a relative pronoun or a description, and his harm is the subject and its predicate is closer, and the sentence is the relative clause. The sentence What an evil master and what an evil companion is the answer to the oath, and the meaning is that that disbeliever will say on the Day of Resurrection to his idol whose harm is closer than his benefit: What an evil master and what an evil companion you are. The master is the supporter, and the clan is the companion, and like what is in this verse is the saying of Antara: They call Antar and the spears are like the shafts of a well in the frankincense of the dark-skinned man. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that yad’u is in the position of a state, and in it is a deleted ha’: meaning that is the distant misguidance that he calls upon. Based on this, it is stopped at yad’u, and his statement to him whose harm is nearer than his benefit is a renewed statement raised by the beginning, and its predicate is la ba’isa al-mawla. He said: This is because the lam is for the oath and emphasis, so it was made the beginning of the statement. Al-Zajjaj and al-Farra’ said: It is possible that yad’u is repeated on what preceded it in order to increase this action, which is the supplication: meaning he calls upon that which neither harms nor benefits him, he calls upon. Like I hit Zayd, I hit. Al-Farra’, al-Kisa’i and al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the statement is an oath, and the lam is presented in its position, and the estimate is: he calls upon the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit, so whoever is in the accusative position with yad’u, and the lam is the answer to the oath, and his harm is the subject, and closer is its predicate. Among the manipulations of the lam by advancing and delaying is the saying of the poet: My uncle is you and from Jarir, his uncle will attain glory and honor his uncles That is, you are my uncle. An-Nahhas said: Ali bin Sulaiman narrated to us on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid who said: There is an ellipsis in the speech, and the meaning is: He calls upon the one whose harm is closer than his benefit as a god. An-Nahhas said: I think this statement is a mistake on the part of Muhammad bin Yazid, and perhaps the reason for it is that what comes before this lam does not work on what comes after it. Al-Farra’ and Al-Qaffal also said: The lam is a connection, meaning it is redundant, and the meaning is: He calls upon the one whose harm is closer than his benefit, meaning he worships Him. And this is how it is in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud with the ellipsis of the lam, and the lam in Labi’sa al-Mawla and Labi’sa al-‘Asheer is, according to this, an introduction to the oath.
22:14: 14- Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. When He finished mentioning the state of the polytheists and those who worship God, He mentioned the state of the believers in the Hereafter, and He informed that He will admit them to these gardens with this description. The discussion of the flow of rivers beneath them has already been presented, and if what is meant by it is the earth, then it is necessary to estimate an added word: that is, from beneath its trees. Indeed, God does what He wills. This sentence is an explanation of what preceded it: that is, He does what He wills of actions. He is not questioned about what He does. He rewards whomever He wills and punishes whomever He wills.
22:15: 15- Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter An-Nahhas said: One of the best things that has been said about this verse is that the meaning is whoever thinks that God will not support Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that it is possible for him to cut off the victory that he has been given, let him stretch out a rope to the heaven meaning let him seek a trick to reach the heaven then let him cut off meaning let him cut off the victory if it is possible for him let him see whether his plot and his trick will vanish what enrages him from the victory of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that the meaning is: Whoever thinks that God will not support Muhammad until He makes him prevail over all religions, let him die of rage. Then he explained it by saying: let him stretch out a rope to the heaven meaning let him tie a rope to the ceiling of his house then let him cut off meaning let him stretch the rope until it breaks and he dies suffocated. The meaning is: let him suffocate with rage until he dies, for God is his supporter and victor, and his rage will not benefit him. The meaning of let him see Do they make his plot go away: meaning his actions and his tricks? What enrages: meaning his anger, and what is a source. It was said that the pronoun in yansuruhu refers to man, and the meaning is: whoever thinks that God will not provide for him, let him kill himself. Abu Ubaidah said the same.
