It was said that the pronoun refers to the religion: meaning whoever thinks that God will not support his religion. The Kufians read with a sukoon on the lam in thumma li-yaqta’. An-Nahhas said: This reading is far from Arabic.
22:16: 16- And thus We have sent it down as clear signs. That is, like that wondrous revelation, We have sent it down as clear signs, the meanings of which are apparent. And that God guides whom He wills. His guidance, either initially or in addition to it, for whoever was guided before. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the statement of God, the second of his curves, that he said: He twists his neck. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jurayj that it is the one who exposes himself. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the statement of God, the second of his curves, that he said: It was revealed about al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: He is a man from Banu Abd al-Dar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, And among mankind is he who worships God on the verge, that he said: A man would come to Madinah, and if his wife gave birth to a boy and his horses produced a child, he would say: This is a good religion. But if his wife did not give birth and his horses did not produce a child, he would say: This is a bad religion. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him with a sound chain of transmission that he said: A man would come to Madinah, and if his wife gave birth to a boy and his horses produced a child, he would say: This is a good religion. But if his wife did not give birth and his horses did not produce a child, he would say: This is a bad religion. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him with a sound chain of transmission that he said: Some Bedouins would come to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and convert to Islam. When they returned to their country, if they found a year of rain, a year of fertility, or a year of good children, they would say: This religion of ours is good, so adhere to it. But if they found a year of drought, a year of bad children, or a year of famine, they would say: There is no good in this religion of ours. So God revealed: {And among mankind is he who worships God upon an edge.} Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated something similar from him, and in its chain of transmission is Al-Awfi. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from his chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: “A Jewish man converted to Islam and lost his sight, wealth and children, so he took Islam as a bad omen. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Relieve me, forgive me.’ He said: ‘Islam is not to be excused.’ He said: ‘I have not gained any good from this religion of mine. I have lost my sight, wealth and children.’ He said: ‘O Jew, Islam melts men as fire melts the dross of iron, gold and silver.’ So the verse was revealed: ‘And among mankind is he who worships God on an edge.’” Al-Faryabi, ‘Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas regarding his statement: ‘Whoever thinks that God will not support him,’ he said: Whoever thinks that God will not support Muhammad in this world and the hereafter, ‘let him stretch out a rope,’ he said: let him tie it with a rope, ‘to the sky,’ he said: to the sky of his house, the roof, ‘then let him cut it,’ he said: then let him strangle himself with it until he dies.” And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Whoever thinks that God will not support him meaning that God will not provide for him, let him stretch out a rope to the sky so that he takes a rope and ties it to the sky of his house and chokes himself with it. Let him see whether his plan will remove that which enrages him he said: Let him see whether that will benefit him or bring him provision.
22:17: His statement: 17- Indeed, those who believed meaning in God and His Messenger, or in what was mentioned of the clear signs and those who were Jews are the Jews who claim to follow the religion of Moses and the Sabians are a people who worship the stars, and it was said that they are from the same kind as the Christians, but that is not correct, rather they are a well-known sect that does not go back to any of the religions that claim to follow the prophets and the Christians are those who claim to follow the religion of Jesus and the Magians are those who worship fire, and they say that the world has two origins: light and darkness. It was said that they worship the sun and the moon, and it was said that they use impurities, and it was said that they are a people from the Christians who isolated themselves from them and wore hair-cloth, and it was said that they took some of the religion of the Jews and some of the religion of the Christians and those who associated others with God who worship idols, and the investigation of this has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah, but He, the Almighty, put the Christians before the Sabians there, and put them after them here. It was said that the reason for presenting the Christians there is that they are People of the Book, not the Sabians, and the reason for presenting the Sabians here is that their time is over the time of the Christians, and the phrase God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection is in the nominative case as a predicate because of the preceding in, and the meaning of the separation is that He, the Exalted, will judge between them and admit the believers among them to Paradise and the disbelievers among them to Hell. It was said that the separation is to distinguish the truthful from the false by a sign by which each one of them is known, and the phrase God is Witness over all things is an explanation of what preceded it: that is, He, the Exalted, is Witness over all the actions and words of His creation, and nothing of them escapes Him. Al-Farra' denied that the phrase God will judge between them is a predicate because of the preceding in. He said that it is not permissible to say: Indeed, Zaid, his brother is leaving. Al-Zajjaj rejected what Al-Farra' said, and denied it and denied what he made similar to the verse, and there is no doubt in the permissibility of your saying: Indeed, Zaid has goodness with him, and Indeed, Zaid is leaving, and the like.
22:18: 18- Have you not seen that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth? The vision here is the vision of the heart, not the visual: that is, did you not know? The address is to everyone who is fit for it, and he is the one from whom vision is possible. What is meant by prostration here is complete submission, not the prostration of obedience specific to rational beings, whether the word of is made specific to rational beings, or general to them and others. For this reason, the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and the beasts is conjoined with of, for this indicates that prostration is submission, not obedience specific to rational beings. Rather, these matters were mentioned separately, even though they are included under of, on the assumption that they are general, because performing prostration with them is usually unlikely, and many people is raised by an implied verb indicated by the mentioned: that is, many people prostrate to Him. It was said that it is raised as a subject and its predicate is omitted, and its estimation is: and many people deserve the reward, and the first is more apparent. Rather, it was not raised by the conjunction with man, because the prostration of these many people is the prostration of obedience specific to rational people, and what is meant by the prostration that preceded is submission. If it were raised by the conjunction with man, then that would combine two different meanings in one word. And you are aware that there is no escape. To this, after carrying the prostration on submission, and there is no doubt that what is meant by the prostration of many people is their submission and not the specific prostration itself, then its being raised by the conjunction is fine, even if the author of Al-Kashshaf and his followers rejected that. As for his statement: And many upon whom the punishment is due, Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said: It is raised by the beginning and its predicate is what comes after it. It was said that it is conjoined with the first many, and the meaning is: And many of the people prostrate among them but refuse that. It was said that the meaning is: And many of the people are in Paradise, and many upon whom the punishment is due. This is how Ibn Al-Anbari narrated it. And he whom God humiliates, for him there is none to honor him, meaning, he whom God humiliates by making him a disbeliever and wretched, for him there is none to honor him so that he becomes happy and honorable. Al-Akhfash, Al-Kisa’i, and Al-Farra’ narrated that the meaning is: And he whom God humiliates, there is none to honor him meaning honor. God does what He wills of the things that include what was mentioned previously of misery and happiness, honor and humiliation.
22:19: 19- These are two opponents. The opponents are one of the most impure groups, the Jews, Christians, Sabians, Magians, and those who associate others with God. The other opponent is the Muslims. They are two quarreling groups. This was stated by Al-Farra and others. It was said that what is meant by the two opponents is Paradise and Hell. Paradise said: He created me for His mercy, and Hell said: He created me for His punishment. It was also said that what is meant by the two opponents are those who came out on the day of Badr. Among the believers were Hamza, Ali, and Ubaidah, and among the disbelievers were Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi'ah, and Al-Walid bin Utbah. Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him used to swear that this verse was revealed about these combatants, as was proven from him in Sahih. A group of the Companions said the same, and they are more knowledgeable than others about the reasons for revelation. This was also proven in Sahih from a group of the Companions, and they are more knowledgeable than others about the reasons for revelation. It was also proven in Sahih from Ali that he said: This verse was revealed about us. Ibn Kathir read these two with a shaddah on the nun. The Almighty said: They disputed and did not say they disputed. Al-Farra’ said: Because they are a plural, and if he had said they disputed, it would have been permissible. The meaning of in their Lord is in the matter of their Lord, meaning in His religion, or in His essence, or in His attributes, or in His law for His servants, or in all of that. Then the Almighty explained what He had summarized in His statement: He will judge between them, and said: Then those who disbelieved, garments of fire will be cut out for them. Al-Azhari said: That is, they will be smoothed out and made into clothing for them. The fire was likened to garments because it encompasses them as garments encompass, and the past tense was used to refer to the future to indicate that it will happen. It was said that these garments are made of copper that has been melted and has become like fire, and they are the garments mentioned in another verse. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: The fire surrounded them. It was read as qata’at with a light pronunciation. Then the Almighty said: He will pour boiling water over their heads. The boiling water is the hot water boiling in the fire of Hell. The sentence is a resumption or it is a second piece of report for the relative pronoun.
22:20: 20- With it will be melted what is in their bellies. Melting is dissolving, and molten metal is what has melted from it. It is said, I melted something and it melted, meaning, I melted it and it melted, so it is molten metal. The meaning is that with that boiling water, what is in their bellies of intestines and entrails will be melted. And the skins, is conjoined with what, meaning, and the skins will be melted by it. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. It has been said that the skins are not melted, but rather burned, so a verb is estimated that is appropriate for that, and it is said, And the skins will be burned by it, as in the poet's saying: I fed her straw and cold water. That is, I gave her water to drink. It is clear that there is no escape from this, because if boiling water dissolves what is in the stomach, then its dissolving of the visible skin is even more appropriate.
22:21: 21- And they will have maces of iron. Al-Maqami' is the plural of Maqama'ah, and Maqama' means I qamma'tuhu strike him with a mace, which is a piece of iron. The meaning is: They will have maces of iron with which they strike: that is, the infidels. The maces are called maces because they subdue the one being struck: that is, they humiliate him. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: I qamma't al-rajul 'anni iqma'an: if he attacked you, so I turned him away from you.
22:22: 22- Whenever they want to get out of it meaning from the fire they are returned to it meaning into the fire by being beaten with whips, and from grief is a substitute for the pronoun in from it by returning the preposition or an object for it: meaning because of a severe grief from the griefs of the fire and taste the punishment of the burning is by estimation of the saying: meaning they are returned to it, and it was said to them taste the punishment of the burning: meaning the burning punishment, and the origin of the burning is the name from burning, something is burned by fire and burned with burning and scorching, and tasting is contact with which the perception of taste is achieved, and here it is an expansion, and what is meant by it is the perception of pain. Al-Zajjaj said: This is for one of the two opponents. And he said about the other opponent, who are the believers.
22:23: 23- "Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow." So God, the Almighty, explained the state of the believers after explaining the state of the disbelievers. Then God, the Almighty, explained some of the bliss He has prepared for them after they enter Paradise, saying: "They will be adorned therein. The majority read they will be adorned" with emphasis and in the passive form, and it was read with a lightened form: meaning God or the angels will adorn them by His command. And the "min" in His statement: "of bracelets" is for partiality: meaning they will be adorned with some bracelets, or for clarification, or redundant, and the "min in of gold is for clarification, and bracelets is the plural of bracelet and the aswir" is the plural of bracelet, and there are two languages for bracelet: kasra and damma of the seen, and there is a third language, which is aswar. Nafi`, Ibn Kathir, `Asim and Shaibah read and pearls in the accusative case, in apposition to they will be adorned with pearls, or with a verb that is understood to be in the accusative case. This is how Ya`qub, Al-Jahdari and `Isa ibn `Umar read in the accusative case. This reading is in accordance with the script of the Qur’an, as this letter is written with an alif. The rest read in the genitive case, in apposition to the pearls, meaning they will be adorned with bracelets and pearls. It is not far-fetched that there will be bracelets of solid pearls in Paradise, just as there will be bracelets of gold in Paradise. And their clothing therein will be silk, meaning everything they will wear will be silk, as this addition indicates. It is possible that what is meant is that this type of clothing that was forbidden to them in this world will be permissible for them in the Hereafter, and that it is part of what they will wear therein, as therein is whatever their souls desire, and each one of them will be given what his soul desires and will attain what he wants.
22:24: 24- And they are guided to the good word meaning they are directed to it. It was said that it is There is no god but God and it was said that it is Praise be to God and it was said that it is the Qur'an, and it was said that it is the good tidings that come to them from God, the Most High. There is something in the Qur'an that indicates this general statement here, which is His, the Most High, saying: Praise be to God, Who has fulfilled His promise to us Praise be to God, Who has guided us to this Praise be to God, Who has removed from us sorrow and the meaning of and they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy is that they are guided to the path of praise, which is the path to Paradise, or the path of God, which is His straight religion, which is Islam. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And the Sabians, he said: They are a people who worship angels, pray towards the Qiblah, and recite the Psalms. And the Magians, the worshippers of the sun, moon, and fire. And those who associate others with God, the worshippers of idols. Indeed, God will judge between them, he said: There are six religions, five of which belong to Satan, and the religion of God Almighty. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the verse, he said: His judgment judged between them, making the five common and making this nation one. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Those who are Jews are the Jews, and the Sabians do not have a book, and the Magians are the people of idols, and the polytheists are the Arab Christians. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr that he used to swear that this verse, These two are opponents, was revealed about the three, and the three who fought on the day of Badr were Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, Ubaidah bin Al-Harith, Ali bin Abi Talib and Utbah, and Shaiba the sons of Rabi’ah and Al-Walid bin Utbah. Ali said: I will be the first to kneel before God on the Day of Resurrection in the dispute. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ali. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas in a similar manner, and it was narrated in this way on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his statement: Garments of fire will be cut out for them, he said: Of copper, and there is no vessel that is hotter than it when heated. And regarding his statement: Boiling water will be poured over their heads, he said: Copper will be melted on their heads. And his statement: What is in their bellies will be melted thereby, he said: Their intestines will flow, and their skins, he said: Their skins will be scattered. And Abd bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Abu Nu’aym in Al-Hilya and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he recited this verse: Boiling water will be poured over their heads, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Indeed, the boiling water will be poured over their heads and will penetrate their skulls until it reaches their stomachs, and what is in their stomachs will flow until it passes through their feet, and it will be melted, then it will be returned to how it was.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: With it will melt what is in their bellies, he said: They walk while their intestines and their skins fall out. And regarding his statement: And for them are maces of iron, he said: They will be struck with them, so every limb will fall on its own and they will cry out for woe and destruction. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse: They will be given water to drink that, if it enters their bellies, will melt them and their skins along with their bellies. Ahmad, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th wa Al-Nushur on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) who said: “If an iron mace were placed in the earth and the two heavy things came together, they would not lift it from the earth. And if a mountain were struck with an iron mace, it would shatter and then return to what it was.” Ibn Al-Mubarak, Saeed bin Mansour, Hannad, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Salman who said: The Fire is black and dark, its flames and embers do not give light. Then he recited: Whenever they want to get out of it, out of distress, they are returned to it. And in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Omar who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: He who does not wear silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter. There are hadiths on this topic. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And they are guided to the good word, he said: They were inspired. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah who said: They are guided to the good word in the dispute when they say: God is our protector and you have no protector. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid regarding the verse, he said: The Qur’an And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy, he said: Islam. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding the verse, he said: Islam. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd, who said: There is no god but God, and God is the greatest, and praise be to God who said, To Him ascends the good word.
22:25: His statement: 25- Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God is a conjunction of the present tense with the past, because what is meant by the present tense is the past of averting, and similar to this is his statement, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God, or what is meant by averting here is continuity and not just the future, so it is correct to conjoin it with the past, and it is permissible for the waw in and avert to be the waw of state: meaning they disbelieved and the state is that they avert. It was said that the waw is redundant and the present tense is the predicate of in and it is better to estimate the predicate of in after his statement, and the desert and that is like they lost or perished. Al-Zajjaj said: The predicate is and we will taste him of a painful punishment. It was said that if it was report, it would not have been made jussive. Also, if it was report, the condition would have remained, which is and whoever returns without an answer. So it is better that it is deleted, as we mentioned. What is meant by rejection is prevention. And the path of God is His religion: that is, they prevent whoever wants to enter the religion of God. And the Sacred Mosque is conjoined with the path of God. It was said that what is meant by it is the mosque itself, as is apparent from this Qur’anic arrangement. And it was said that it is the entire sanctuary, because the polytheists prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions on the day of Hudaybiyyah. And it was said that what is meant by it is Mecca, based on his statement: Which We have made for mankind, equal in it, the one who resides therein and the one who passes by, that is, We have made it for mankind in general, so that they pray in it and circumambulate it, equal in it, the one who resides therein and is constant in it, and the one who passes by, that is, the one who arrives from the desert. What is meant by it is the one who comes to it without any difference between being from the people of the desert or not. And the accusative of equal is that it is the second object of made it, and it means equal, and the one who resides is elevated in it. The Sacred Mosque was described with this to increase the rebuke and rebuke of those who prevent it. And it is possible that the accusative of equal is in the state. This is according to the accusative reading, and Hafs read it according to it from Asim, and it is the reading of Al-A’mash. The majority read it with the nominative case of sawa’a as a subject and its predicate is al-’akif or as an advanced predicate, and the subject is al-’akif meaning the one who is abiding in it and the one who comes from the desert are equal. It was read with the accusative case of sawa’a and the genitive case of al-’akif as an attribute of al-nas meaning We made it for the people, the one who is abiding and the one who comes from the desert, equal. Ibn Kathir confirmed the ya in al-badī in both connected and stopped words, and Abu Amr deleted it in stopping words, and Nafi’ deleted it in connected and stopped words. Al-Qurtubi said: The people agreed on the establishment of the Sacred Mosque itself. They differed about Mecca. Mujahid and Malik were of the opinion that the houses and dwellings of Mecca are the same for residents and visitors. Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Abbas and a group were of the opinion that the visitor may stay wherever he finds them, and the owner of the house must shelter him whether he likes it or not. The majority were of the opinion that the houses and dwellings of Mecca are not like the Sacred Mosque, and its people have the right to prevent visitors from staying there. The bottom line is that the discussion of this goes back to two principles: The first principle is what is in this verse: Is what is meant by the Sacred Mosque the mosque itself, or the entire sanctuary, or Mecca in particular? The second is: Was the conquest of Mecca by peace or by force? Assuming that it was by force, did the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) approve of it in the hands of its people in particular? Or did he make it for those who stayed there in general? We have explained this in our commentary on Al-Muntaqa in a way that does not require the reader to add anything more. And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice - We will make him taste a painful punishment. The object of return is omitted for the purpose of generalization. The meaning is: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice - meaning to deviate from the intention. In the language, inclination means deviation, except that He, the Most High, clarified here that it is deviation by injustice. There is a difference of opinion about what this injustice is. It has been said that it is polytheism, and it has been said that it is polytheism and murder, and it has been said that it is hunting its animals and cutting down its trees, and it has been said that it is swearing false oaths in it, and it has been said that what is meant is sins in it in general, and it has been said that what is meant by this verse is that one is punished merely for the intention to sin in that place. Ibn Masoud, Ibn Omar, Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and others have held this view, to the extent that they said that if a man intended to kill a man in the Sacred Sanctuary in Aden, God would punish him. The bottom line is that this verse indicates that whoever is in the Sacred House is held accountable for merely intending to commit injustice. It is specific to what was reported that God forgave this nation for what their souls spoke of, unless it is said that the will in it is more than just the speech of the soul. In short, researching this and establishing the truth in it in a way that combines the evidence and removes the ambiguity is very long. An example of this verse is the hadith, If two Muslims meet with their swords, then the killer and the killed will be in Hellfire. It was said, O Messenger of God, this is the killer, but what about the killed? He said, He was eager to kill his companion. So he entered Hellfire here because of his mere eagerness to kill his companion. We have devoted a separate thesis to this research. If the ba in his statement bi-ilhad is a deleted object as we mentioned, then it is not extra. It was said that it is extra here, like the poet’s saying: We are the Banu Ja'dah, the owners of the falaj. We strike with the sword and hope for relief. We hope for relief, and similar to it: Didn't the report reach you, spreading report of what happened to the camels of Banu Ziyad? That is, what it encountered. Among those who said that it is redundant is Al-Akhfash. The meaning according to him is: And whoever intends to commit an act of injustice therein. The Kufians said: The letter Baa’ was added because the meaning is to commit an act of injustice, and the letter Baa’ is included and deleted. It is possible that the estimation is: And whoever intends to commit an act of injustice therein. It was said that the word return contains the meaning of them, and the meaning is: And whoever intends to commit an act of injustice therein. As for the letter Baa’ in his statement with injustice, it is for causality, and the meaning is: And whoever intends to commit an act of injustice therein because of injustice. It is possible that with injustice is a substitute for with injustice by repeating the preposition, and it is possible that they are two synonymous states.
22:26: 26- And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House meaning, remember that time. It is said, I designated for him a home and I designated for him just as it is said, I made you dwelling and I made you dwelling. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is, We made the site of the House a dwelling place for Abraham, and the meaning of We designated is: We showed him the site of the House, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: How many noble brothers I have, I have given them my own hands to someone Al-Farra’ said: “The lam is redundant and the place is a circumstance: that is, We revealed it in it, “that you do not associate anything with Me.” It was said that this is an explanation of we have established because it includes the meaning of we worshipped because establishing is for worship. Abu Hatim said: It is a source: that is, because do not associate anything with Me. It was said that it is the lightened form of the heavy and and it was said that it is redundant. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: And We revealed to him that you should not worship other than Me. Al-Mubarrad said: It is as if it was said to him, Single Me in this house, because the meaning of do not associate anything with Me alone is and purify My house from polytheism and idol worship. In the verse, there is an attack on what the inhabitants of the house associated: that is, this was the condition on your father and those after him, and you did not fulfill it, but rather you associated. A group said: The address in His saying, do not associate anything is to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is very weak. The meaning of and purify My House is to purify it from disbelief, idols, blood, and all other impurities. It was said that it meant purification from idols only, because Jurhum and the Amalekites had idols in the place of the House. What was mentioned in Surat Bara’ah is sufficient in this meaning. What is meant by those who stand here are those who pray. And the mention of bowing and prostration after it is to clarify the pillars of prayer, indicating the great importance of this act of worship. He linked circumambulation with prayer because they are not prescribed except in the House, so circumambulation is near it and prayer is towards it.
22:27: 27- And proclaim to the people the Hajj. Al-Hasan and Ibn Muhaisin read and proclaim with a light dhal and a long dhal. The rest read with a heavy dhal. Adhan is notification, and it was mentioned previously in Bara'ah. Al-Wahidi said: A group of commentators said: When Abraham finished building the House, Gabriel came to him and ordered him to announce the Hajj to the people. He said: O Lord, who will convey my voice? God, the Exalted, said: Announce it and I will convey it. So he ascended the station and rose up until it became like the highest mountains. He put his fingers in his ears and turned his face to the right or left, east or west and said: O people, Hajj to the House has been prescribed for you, so respond to your Lord. So those who were in the loins of men and the wombs of women responded to him: Here I am, O God, here I am. It was said that the address was to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Meaning: Inform them, O Muhammad, of the obligation of Hajj upon them. Based on this, the address to Abraham ended with his saying: And bowing and prostration. It was said that his address ended with his saying: And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, and that his saying: That you do not associate with Me and what follows is an address to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The majority read with Hajj with a fat-ha on the ha’, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read in the entire Qur’an with a kasra on it: They will come to you on foot. This is the answer to the command. God promised that people would respond to Him to perform Hajj on foot and on horseback. So the meaning of on foot is the plural of on foot, and it was said that it is the plural of man. Ibn Abi Ishaq read rajalan with a damma on the ra and a light jeem. Mujahid read rajal with the weight of fa’ali like kasali. He mentioned rajal before rukban because of their increased fatigue in walking. He said: They come to you even though they come to the House, because whoever comes to the Kaaba as a pilgrim has come to Abraham, because he answered his call. And on every lean camel is in apposition to rajalan meaning and riders on every camel. A lean camel is one that is exhausted by travel. It is also said dhamar meaning dhamuran. He described a lean camel by saying they come considering the meaning, because dhamir is in the meaning of dhamir. The companions of Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abi ‘Ubla and Ad-Dahhak read yatu’ as an attribute of rijalan. Al-faj means a wide road, plural fajaj, and al-‘aamiq means the distant.
22:28: The lam in 28- that they may witness benefits for themselves is related to His saying, they come to you, and it was said to His saying, and permission, and the witnesses are the presence, and the benefits are the benefits of this world and the hereafter. It was said that what is meant by it are the rituals, and it was said forgiveness, and it was said trade as in His saying, There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord "and mention the name of God on the appointed days" meaning they mention the name of God when slaughtering the gifts and sacrifices, and it was said that this mention is a metaphor for slaughtering because it is inseparable from it. And the appointed days are the days of sacrifice as indicated by His saying, "for what He has provided for them of cattle" and it was said the tenth of Dhul-Hijjah. We have already discussed the known and numbered days in the cow, so we will not repeat it. The discussion of the time of slaughtering the sacrifice is well-known in the books of jurisprudence and commentaries on hadith. The meaning of: on what He has provided for them is on slaughtering what He has provided for them of the livestock, which are camels, cows, and sheep. The livestock are the livestock, so the addition in this is like the addition in their saying: the mosque of the congregation and the first prayer. Eat from it. The command here is for encouragement according to the majority, and a group went to the fact that the command is for obligation, and this is a shift from the third person to the second person. And feed the wretched, the needy. The wretched is the one with extreme poverty, so the poor were mentioned after him for further clarification, and the command here is for obligation, and it was said for encouragement.
22:29: 29- Then let them complete their untidiness. What is meant by utidiness here is performance: that is, let them complete the removal of their filth, because utidiness is dirt and filth from long hair and nails. The commentators have agreed on this, as narrated by Al-Naysaburi. Al-Zajjaj said: The linguists do not know utidiness. Abu Ubaidah said: There is nothing in poetry that can be used as evidence for the meaning of utidiness. Al-Mubarrad said: The root of utidiness in the language is every filth that befalls a person. It was said that its utidiness is its anointing because the pilgrim is dusty and disheveled and has not anointed himself or shaved his head. So when he completes his ritual and exits his state of ihram, he shaves his hair but not his clothes. This is the utidiness of utidiness. Al-Zajjaj said: It is as if it is a departure from ihram to the lawful state. And let them fulfill their vows meaning what they vow to do of righteousness during their Hajj. The command is for obligation. It was said that what is meant by vows here are the acts of Hajj. And let them go around the Ancient House This circumambulation is the circumambulation of Ifadah. Ibn Jarir said: There is no disagreement about that among the interpreters. The Ancient is the old, as is indicated by the saying of the Most High: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind (al-Ma’idah 10:1). It was called the Ancient because God freed it from being dominated by a tyrant. It was said because God frees the necks of sinners from punishment in it. It was said because it was freed from the drowning of the flood. It was said the Ancient, the Noble. Abd bin Hamid narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the Sacred Mosque he said: The entire sanctuary, which is the Sacred Mosque Alike for the one staying therein and the visitor he said: God’s creation is equal. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Saeed bin Jubair something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse he said: They are equal in the dwellings of Mecca, so the people of Mecca should make room for them so that they can complete their rituals. And the traveler and the people of Mecca said: They are equal, meaning in the home and the sanctuary. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Abdullah bin Amr who said: Whoever takes from the rent of the houses of Mecca is only eating fire in his stomach. Ibn Saad narrated from Umar bin Al-Khattab that a man said to him at Al-Marwah: O Commander of the Faithful, allocate me a place for me and my descendants, so Umar turned away from him and said: It is the sanctuary of God, equal for the one staying there and the visitor. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Ata’ who said: Umar used to prevent the people of Mecca from making doors for it so that the pilgrims could stay in the courtyards of the houses. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the statement of God, The one who stays therein is equal to the one who visits, he said: The one who stays there is equal to the one who enters. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Makkah is permissible, its houses are not to be rented out and its quarters are not to be sold. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Alqamah ibn Nadlah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr and Umar passed away and the quarters of Makkah were not called anything but the wandering places. Whoever needed a place to stay, they were given a place to stay, and whoever was independent, they were given a place to stay. It was narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah on the authority of Isa ibn Yunus on the authority of Umar ibn Saeed ibn Abi Hafra on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman on the authority of Alqamah, and he mentioned it. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever consumes the rent of the houses of Makkah will consume Hellfire. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Rahawayh, Ahmad, Abdul bin Hameed, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And whoever intends to commit an evil therein or commit an injustice, he said: If a man intends to commit an evil therein while he is in Aden Abyan, God will make him taste a painful torment. Ibn Kathir said: This chain of transmission is sound according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari, and its being a Mawqoof is more likely than its being a Marfu’, which is why Shu’bah insisted on its being a Mawqoof. Saeed bin Mansour and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding the verse: Whoever intends to commit a sin but does not commit it anywhere other than in the House, it will not be recorded against him until he commits it, and whoever intends to commit a sin in the House, God will not cause him to die in this world until he tastes a painful torment. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: This verse was revealed about Abdullah bin Unais: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent him with two men, one of whom was an emigrant and the other from the Ansar. They boasted about their lineage, so Abdullah bin Unais became angry and killed the Ansar, then he apostatized from Islam and fled to Mecca. So the verse was revealed about him: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice meaning whoever seeks refuge in the Sacred Sanctuary committing an act of injustice, meaning by turning away from Islam. Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the statement: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice he said: He associates partners with God. Abd bin Humayd, Al-Bukhari in his history, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ya’la bin Umayyah on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: Hoarding food in the Sacred Sanctuary is an act of injustice therein. Saeed bin Mansour, Al-Bukhari in his history and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Umar bin al-Khattab who said: Hoarding food in Mecca is an act of injustice. Abd bin Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: Selling food in Mecca is an act of injustice. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha`b on his authority that he heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: Hoarding food in Mecca is heresy. Ibn Jarir and Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to Ali that he said: When Ibrahim was commanded to build the Ka`bah, Ismail and Hajar went out with him, and that is when God says: And when We designated for Ibrahim the site of the House (Al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to Ata’, and those who stand he said: Those who pray near it. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to Qatadah with a similar meaning. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf, Ibn Mani`, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When Ibrahim finished building the Ka`bah, he said: My Lord, I have finished. He said: Proclaim to the people the Hajj. He said: My Lord, how can my voice reach them? He said: Proclaim and I am responsible for conveying it. He said: My Lord, how should I say it? He said: “Say: O mankind, Hajj to the Ancient House has been prescribed for you.” And whoever is in the heaven and the earth heard him. Do you not see that they come from the farthest parts of the earth responding to the call? There are narrations on this topic from a group of the Companions. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, So that they may witness benefits for themselves, he said: Markets that were for them. God did not mention any benefits except this world. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, he said: Benefits in this world and benefits in the Hereafter. As for the benefits of the Hereafter, they are the pleasure of God, and as for the benefits of this world, they are what they obtain of the meat of the animals on that day, the sacrifices and the trade. Abu Bakr Al-Marzouqi narrated from him in the Book of the Two Eids, he said: The known days: The Day of Sacrifice and the three days after it. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, he said: The known days: The Day of Sacrifice and the three days after it. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, he said: The Days of Tashreeq. Abd Ibn Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him in the known days, he said: The day before the Day of Tarwiyah, the Day of Tarwiyah and the Day of Arafah. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, he said: The wretched is the time. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Umar, he said: The rituals of the rituals are all. These narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas. Saeed bin Mansour, Abdul bin Hameed, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “Twisting the hair of the head, taking from the sideburns, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, standing at Arafat, walking between Safa and Marwah, throwing stones, cutting the nails, cutting the moustache and slaughtering.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: And let them circumambulate the Ancient House means the circumambulation of the visit on the Day of Sacrifice. There are reports from a group of the Companions about the reason for naming the House the Ancient House, and we have previously referred to that. There are hadiths about the virtue of circumambulation, but this is not the place to mention them.
22:30: Location 30- That is the nominative case as a predicate of a deleted subject: meaning the matter is that, or a subject whose predicate is deleted or in the accusative case with a deleted verb: meaning do that, and what is referred to is what preceded from the Hajj rituals, and this and similar things are used to separate between two statements or between two ends of one statement, and the prohibitions are the plural of prohibition. Al-Zajjaj said: The prohibition is what is obligatory to perform and it is forbidden to neglect it, and in this verse it is what is forbidden and from it from falling into it. What appears from the verse is the generality of every prohibition in Hajj and other than it as the wording indicates even if the reason is specific, and its glorification is leaving its association so it is better for him meaning glorification is the predicate for him with his Lord meaning in the hereafter than neglecting any of it. It was said that the comparative form here does not mean its real meaning, but rather what is meant is that this glorification is good that is benefited from, so it is a number of good things. And the livestock have been made lawful to you which are camels, cows and sheep except what is recited to you that is in the Noble Book of the forbidden things, which are dead animals and what is mentioned with them in Surat Al-Ma’idah. It was said in His statement except what is recited to you, other than the game that is lawful while you are in a state of ihram. “So avoid the uncleanness of idols” rajis means filth, and an idol is a statue, and its origin is from the word wathan something, meaning it remained in its place, and the cross was called an idol because it is set up and fixed in its place, so it does not move from it, and what is meant is avoiding the worship of idols, and He called it rajs because it is the cause of rajs, which is punishment. It was said that God, the Almighty, made it rajs by ruling, and rajs means impurity, and impurity is not an intrinsic description of it, but rather a legal description, so it does not go away except by faith, just as physical impurity does not go away except by water. Al-Zajjaj said: “From here, to summarize a type of types: that is, avoid the uncleanliness which is an idol, “and avoid false speech,” which is falsehood, and it is called falsehood because it deviates from the truth, and from that is the saying of the Most High: They turned away from their cave, and their saying, A city that is a slanted one, meaning, leaning, and what is meant here is false speech in general, and the worst of it is associating partners with God in any form. Al-Zajjaj said: What is meant by false speech here is their making some livestock permissible and their making others forbidden, and their saying, This is permissible and this is forbidden, and it was said that what is meant by it is false testimony.
22:31: And the accusative 31- Hanafa is in the state: meaning upright on the truth, or inclined towards the truth. The word Hanifa is one of the opposites, and it can be used for uprightness, and it can be used for inclination, and it was said that its meaning is pilgrims, but there is no basis for this. Not associating anything with Him is a state like the first: meaning not associating anything with Him, as the deletion indicates from the generality, and the phrase And whoever associates anything with God, it is as if he had fallen from the sky is a subject confirming what preceded it from the command to avoid, and the meaning of fell from the sky: fell to the ground: meaning he descended from the high level of faith to the depths of disbelief. Then the birds snatch him away, it is said that he snatched him away, if he robbed him, and from this is his saying: Snatching their sight, meaning they snatch his flesh and tear it apart with their claws. Abu Ja`far and Nafi` read it with a shaddah on the ta` and a fathah on the kha`. It was also read with a kasrah on the kha` and the ta` and with a kasrah on the ta` with both of them. Or the wind hurls him down means it tosses him and throws him in a distant place meaning far away. It is said, He crushed, crushed, crushed meaning he is crushed if he is far away. Al-Zajjaj said: God knows that the distance of the one who associates partners with Him from the throat is like the distance of what fell from the sky, so the birds carry him away or the wind hurls him down to a distant place.
22:32: 32- "That is it. And whoever honors the symbols of God" The discussion of this reference has already been presented. The symbols are the plural of ritual, and it is everything in which God the Most High has a symbol, and from it is the symbol of the people in war, which is their sign by which they recognize each other, and from it is the marking of the body, which is the stabbing in its right side, so the symbols of God are the signs of His religion, and the gifts are included in the Hajj primarily, and the pronoun in His statement: For it is from the piety of the hearts refers back to the symbols with the estimation of an omitted addition: that is, for honoring them is from the piety of the hearts: that is, from the actions of the hearts that are from piety, for this piety arises from piety.
22:33: 33- There are benefits for you in them meaning in the rituals in general, or in particular, and they are the body as the context indicates. Among their benefits are riding, milk, offspring, wool, and other things for a specified term which is the time of their slaughter then their place is at the Ancient House meaning where their slaughtering is permissible, and the meaning is: they end at the House and what is next to it from the Sanctuary, so their worldly benefits gained from them continue until the time of their slaughter, then their benefits after that are religious. It was said that their place here is taken from the permissibility of the forbidden, and the meaning is: all the rituals of Hajj from standing at Arafat, throwing the pebbles, and running end at the Tawaf al-Ifadah around the House, so the House in this case is intended in itself.
22:34: 34- And for every nation We have appointed a ritual. The ritual here is the source of the verb nasak which means to slaughter an offering. The sacrifice is nasikah, and its plural is nasak. Al-Azhari said: What is meant by the ritual in the verse is the place of slaughter. It is said mansak with a kasra on the seen and a fatha on it, two languages. The Kufians read it with a kasra except for Asim, and the rest read it with a fatha. Al-Farra' said: The ritual in the speech of the Arabs is: the usual place for good or evil. Ibn Arafa said: And for every nation We have appointed a ritual meaning a way of obeying God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Farra’ that the ritual is the Eid, and it was said that it is the Hajj, and the first is more appropriate because of his saying: That they may mention the name of God to the end, and the nation is the group gathered on one doctrine, and the meaning is: And We made for every people of religion a sacrifice that they slaughter and blood that they shed, or an act of worship or obedience or a festival or a Hajj that they perform, so that they may mention the name of God alone and make their ritual specific to Him on what He has provided for them of the livestock meaning on the slaughter of what He has provided for them from it, and in it is an indication that the sacrifice is only from the livestock and not others, and in the verse is evidence that what is meant by the mentioned sacrifice is the mention of the name of God over it. Then He, the Almighty, informed them of His uniqueness in divinity and that He has no partner. The fa is to arrange what comes after it based on what comes before it. Then He commanded them to submit to Him, and to obey and worship Him, and to place the prepositional phrase before the verb for the sake of restriction. The fa here is like the fa that came before it. Then He commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give good tidings to the humble among His servants: that is, the humble, submissive, and sincere. It is taken from al-Khabith, which is the low part of the earth. The meaning is: Give them good tidings, O Muhammad, of what God has prepared for them of His abundant reward and great bounty. It was said that the humble are those who do not wrong others, and if others wrong them, they do not take revenge.
22:35: Then the Almighty described these humble ones by saying: 35- Those whose hearts, when God is mentioned, become fearful meaning they fear and are wary of disobeying Him, and the fear they feel when God is mentioned is evidence of the perfection of their certainty and the strength of their faith. He described them as being patient for what befalls them of calamities and trials in obeying God. Then He described them as establishing prayer meaning performing it at its appointed times in a perfect manner. The majority read: and those who establish prayer in the accusative case as is apparent, and Abu Amr read it in the accusative case on the assumption that the nun remained, and Sibawayh recited on that the poet's saying: The protector of the clan's shame The house is in the accusative case of ‘awrah. It was said that Abu ‘Amr did not read it this way, and Ibn Muhaisin and the residents read it by proving the nun according to the original, and this reading was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud. Then the Almighty described them by saying: And from what We have provided them they spend. That is, they give it in charity and spend it in ways of righteousness, and put it in places of goodness. Similar to this verse is the saying of the Almighty: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith; and upon their Lord they rely. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: The sacred things of God, he said: The sacred things are Mecca, Hajj, Umrah and all the acts of disobedience that God has forbidden. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So avoid the uncleanness of idols, he said: Avoid obeying Satan in worshipping idols. And avoid false statement, meaning slandering God and denying Him. Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ayman ibn Huraym who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up to deliver a sermon and said: O people, false testimony is equal to associating partners with God three times. Then he recited: So avoid the uncleanness of idols and avoid false statement. Ahmad said: It is strange. We only know it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Zayd. There is a difference of opinion regarding the narration of this hadith, and we do not know that Ayman ibn Huraym heard it from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was narrated by Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab from the hadith of Hareem. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others from the hadith of Abu Bakrah who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins? We said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Associating partners with God, disobeying one’s parents. He was reclining, then he sat up and said: Beware of false speech, beware of false testimony. He kept repeating it until we said: If only he would stop. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, Hanifts for God, not associating partners with Him, that he said: Pilgrims to God, not associating partners with Him. This is because the people of ignorance used to perform Hajj as polytheists, but when God made Islam prevail, God said to the Muslims: Perform Hajj now, not associating partners with God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, And whoever honors the symbols of God, that he said: The sacrificial animals. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And whoever honors the symbols of God, he said: Appreciation, approval and reverence. Concerning His statement, Therein you have benefits for a specified term, he said: Until it is designated as a sacrificial animal. These people narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid, and in it he said: Therein you have benefits for a specified term, in their backs, milk, fur, hair and wool until it is designated as a sacrificial animal. When it is designated as a sacrificial animal, the benefits are gone. Then its place, he said: When it is designated, is to the Ancient House. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: When you enter the Sacred Sanctuary, you have reached its place. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And for every nation We have appointed a ritual, he said: A festival. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the verse, he said: Shedding blood. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Slaughtering. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam regarding the verse, he said: God has not made a ritual for any nation other than Mecca. There are hadiths about the sacrifice, but this is not the place to mention them. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And give good tidings to the humble ones, he said: The reassured ones. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in The Blame of Anger, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Amr bin Aws, he said: The humble ones in the verse are those who do not wrong people, and if they are wronged, they do not take revenge.
22:36: Ibn Abi Ishaq read 36- and the body with a damma on the ba and the dal, and the rest read it with a sukoon on the dal and they are two languages, and this name is specific to camels, and it is called badana because it is badana and fatana means fat. Abu Hanifa and Malik said: It is applied to other than camels, and the first is more appropriate because of the descriptions that will come that are apparent in camels, and because the books of language indicate that this name is specific to camels. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation: They differed about the validity of applying badana to cows with two opinions: The most correct of them is that it is applied to them in Sharia as is confirmed in the hadith We made it for you which is what was explained shortly There is good for you in it meaning religious and worldly benefits as mentioned So mention the name of God over it meaning in its manner and the meaning of Sawaf is that it is standing with its legs in line, because it is slaughtered standing and rational, and the origin of this description in horses is said: the horse is saffan so it is saffan if it stands on three legs and bends the fourth. Al-Hasan, Al-A'raj, Mujahid, Zaid bin Aslam and Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari read sawafi meaning purely for God, you do not associate anyone with Him in the name of God over its throat. The singular form is safa, which is the reading of the majority. The singular form is sawafi, and Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Abu Ja'far and Muhammad bin Ali read sawafin with a nun, the plural of safina. Safina is the one who has raised one of her hands with the reins so that she does not shake. From this is the saying of God Almighty: the purebred horses, and from this is the saying of Umar bin Kulthum: We left the horses devoted to him, imitating our leaders. The other said: The first row is like a broken row, and it is still like one of the three broken rows. And when its sides are obligated the obligation is to fall: that is, it falls after its slaughter, and that is when its soul leaves. Then eat from it the majority of scholars said that this command is recommended. And feed the contented and the needy it was said that this command is recommended like the first, and Mujahid, Al-Nakha’i, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Surayj said the same. Al-Shafi’i and a group said: It is obligatory. There is a difference of opinion about who is the contented one? Some say he is the questioner. It is said that a man is content with the opening of the letter nun and he is content with the breaking of the letter nun. From this comes the saying of Al-Shamakh: A man's wealth improves him and makes him rich, but his poverty is more honorable than his contentment. Any question, and it was said that it is the one who refrains from asking and is self-sufficient in language, Al-Khalil mentioned its meaning. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: Some Arabs mentioned Al-Qanoo’ in the meaning of contentment, which is satisfaction, self-restraint and leaving the question. Zaid bin Aslam and his son Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Hasan said the first, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Ikrimah and Qatadah said the second. As for Al-Mu’tarr, Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, Mujahid, Ibrahim, Al-Kalbi and Al-Hasan said that it is the one who approaches without asking. It was said that it is the one who approaches you and asks you. Malik said: The best thing I heard is that Al-Qani’ is the poor, and Al-Mu’tarr is the visitor. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: Both of them are the one who does not ask, but Al-Qani’ is the one who is satisfied with what he has and does not ask, and Al-Mu’tarr is the one who approaches you and does not ask you. Al-Hasan and Al-Mu’tarr read it and its meaning is like the meaning of Al-Mu’tarr, and from it is the saying of Zuhair: Those who are plentiful are provided with sustenance, while those who are few are given generosity and kindness. It is said that he exposed himself to something or sought it. An-Nahhas mentioned it: Thus have We subjected it to you. That is, like that wonderful subjection, We subjected it to you, so it became obedient to you to the places of its slaughter, so you slaughtered it and benefited from it after it had been subjected to carrying loads on it, riding on its back, milking it, and the like. Perhaps you will be grateful. This blessing that God bestowed upon you.
22:37: 37- Their meat and their blood will not reach God meaning the meat of these camels that you give in charity will not ascend to Him, nor will it reach His pleasure, nor will it be accepted by Him, since they are both meat and blood. But it will reach Him meaning the piety of your hearts will reach Him, and your sincerity to Him and your desire for His sake will reach Him, for that is what God accepts and rewards for. It was said that what is meant are the owners of the meat and blood: meaning those who sacrifice and draw near to their Lord will not be satisfied with the meat and blood, but with piety. Al-Zajjaj said: God knows that what reaches Him is His piety and obedience to what He commands. The true meaning of this statement is acceptance, because what a person accepts is said to have attained and reached. So God addressed the creation as is their custom when addressing them, Thus has He subjected them to you. He repeated this as a reminder. The meaning of that you may glorify God for that which He has guided you to is the saying of the one slaughtering: God is the Greatest when slaughtering. So He mentioned in the first verse the command to mention the name of God upon it, and He mentioned here the glorification to indicate the permissibility of combining the name and the glorification. It was said that what is meant by the glorification is His description, glory be to Him, with what indicates pride, and the meaning of for that which He has guided you to is for what He has guided you to of your knowledge of how to draw near to Him, and ma is a source or a relative pronoun. And give good tidings to the doers of good it was said that what is meant by them is the sincere ones, and it was said that the monotheists. It appears that what is meant by them is everyone who does good that justifies the name of doer of good being applied to him. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar who said: We do not know the badan except from camels and cows. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The badan is the one with a cavity. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The badan is only from camels. They narrated something similar from al-Hakam, and they narrated something similar from Ata’ to what Ibn Umar said. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated something similar from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from al-Hasan as well. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Yaqub al-Rabahi on the authority of his father who said: He bequeathed a badan, so I went to Ibn Abbas and said to him: A man bequeathed a badan to me and bequeathed a badan, will a cow suffice for me? He said: Yes. Then he said: Who are your companions? I said: From Banu Rabakh. He said: When did Banu Rabakh acquire cows in addition to camels? They are your companions, and cows are for al-Assad and Abd al-Qays. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in Al-Adahi, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Abu Thabyan who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God: And mention the name of God over it, standing in rows. He said: When you want to slaughter the sacrificial animal, make it stand on three legs, tied up, then say: In the name of God, and God is the greatest. Al-Faryabi, Abu Ubaid, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Standing in rows, he said: Standing tied up. And in the two Sahihs and others on his authority that he saw a man who had made his sacrificial animal kneel while he was slaughtering it, so he said: Send it standing tied up, the Sunnah of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And Abu Ubaidah, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Maymun bin Mihran who said: In Ibn Masoud’s reading, Sawafin means standing. And Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: And when it falls on its side. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Slaughtered. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said: The contented is the one who is self-sufficient, and the beggar is the one who asks. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: The contented is the one who is satisfied with what I have given him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The contented one is the one who is satisfied with what he has been given, and the objector is the one who objects. And he also narrated from him that he said: The contented one is the one who sits in his house. And Abd bin Hamid and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan from him that he was asked about this verse, and he said: As for the contented one, he is the one who is content with what you were sent to in his house, and the one who begs is the one who approaches you. And Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him that he said: The contented one is the one who asks, and the begs is the one who exposes himself and does not ask. And different sayings were narrated from the followers in the interpretation of this verse, and the reference is to the linguistic meaning, especially with the difference between the companions and those who came after them in the interpretation of that. And Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: When the polytheists slaughtered, they would face the Kaaba with the blood and sprinkle it towards the Kaaba, and the Muslims wanted to do that, so God revealed: Neither their meat nor their blood will reach God. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Ibn Jurayh.
22:38: Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read it as yadfa' and the rest read it as yadfa' and the form of the reciprocal verb here is devoid of its original meaning, which is the occurrence of the action from both sides as indicated by the other reading. This form may often be used without its original meaning being intended, such as aqabat al-las and the like, and we have already investigated it. It has been said that this form is used here for exaggeration and it has been said to indicate the repetition of the event. The meaning is: He defends the believers from the evils of the polytheists and it has been said that He strengthens their argument and it has been said that He guides them. The sentence is resumed to explain this advantage that the believers have obtained from the Lord of the Worlds, and that He is the One who is responsible for defending them. Sentence 38- Indeed, God does not love any traitorous ungrateful person confirms the inclusion of the first sentence, for God's defense of His believing servants is a complete indication that they are hated by God and not loved by Him. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever mentions a name other than God’s and draws near to idols with his sacrifice is a traitor and ungrateful. The two forms of exaggeration are used to indicate that they are like that in reality, not to exclude those who betrayed without their betrayal.
22:39: Or disbelief less than their disbelief 39- Permission is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged. Permission is read as active and passive, and so is they are fighting. It is read as active and passive, and in both readings, permission is given by God, the Exalted, to His believing servants that if they are fit for fighting, or the polytheists fight them, they should fight them. The commentators said: The polytheists of Mecca used to harm the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with their tongues and hands, so they would complain about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he would say to them: Be patient, for I have not been commanded to fight until he migrated, so God, the Exalted, revealed this verse in Medina, and it is the first verse revealed about fighting. This verse also confirms the meaning of His statement: Indeed, God defends. The permissibility of fighting them is part of God’s defense against them, and the ba in because they were wronged is for causality: that is, because they were wronged by what was inflicted upon them by the polytheists of cursing, beating, and expulsion. Then God Almighty promised them victory over the polytheists, saying: Indeed, God is able to give them victory. This also confirms what was mentioned about defense. 14- Tell those who have believed to forgive i.e. tell them to forgive, so they will be forgiven those who do not expect the days of God It was said that this is with the deletion of the lam, and the meaning is: tell them to forgive. The meaning is: tell them to overlook those who do not expect God’s punishment of His enemies: i.e. they do not anticipate it. The meaning of hope here is fear, and it was said that it has its literal meaning. The meaning is: they do not expect His reward at the times that God has set for the reward of the believers, and the first is more appropriate. Days are used to express events, as mentioned previously in the interpretation of His statement: and remind them of the days of God. Muqatil said: they do not fear the like of God’s punishment of the past nations, because they do not believe in Him, so they do not fear His punishment. It was said that the meaning is: they do not hope for God’s victory for His friends and His punishment of His enemies, and it was said that they do not fear the resurrection. It was said that the verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword: That He may reward a people for what they used to earn. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read linajzi with a noon, meaning that we may reward. The remaining seven read it with a lower case ending in the active voice: meaning that God may reward. Abu Ja’far, Shaiba, and Asim read it with a lower case ending in the passive voice with the accusative case of qawman. It was said that the representative of the subject is the source of the verb, meaning that God may reward a people. It was also said that the representative is the preposition and noun as in the saying of the poet: If a poor woman gave birth to a puppy, the puppy would curse all dogs. Al-Akhfash and the Kufians permitted this, but the Basrans forbade it. The sentence explains the command to forgive. What is meant by the people are the believers. They were commanded to forgive so that God may reward them on the Day of Resurrection for the good deeds they earned in this world, which include patience in the face of the harm caused by the disbelievers, overlooking them by suppressing anger, and enduring hardship. It was also said that the meaning is: so that He may reward the disbelievers for the evil deeds they did, as if he said: Do not reward them, so that we may reward them. The former is more appropriate.
22:40: Then he described these believers by saying: 40- Those who were expelled from their homes without right and it is possible that it is a substitute for those who fight, or in the accusative case for praise, or in the nominative case with an implied subject, and what is meant by the homes is Mecca except that they say, 'Our Lord is God' Sibawayh said: It is a discontinuous exception: meaning, but for their saying, 'Our Lord is God'. That is, they were expelled without right that necessitates their expulsion, but for their saying, 'Our Lord is God'. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: It is a connected exception, and the meaning is those who were expelled from their homes without right except that they say, 'Our Lord is God', so it is like His saying, the Most High: And you do not blame us for anything except that we believe and Al-Nabigha's saying: There is no fault in them except that their swords have dents from the clashing of the battalions. And had God not repelled the people Nafi' read And had He not repelled and the rest read And had He not repelled and the meaning is: had God not prescribed for the prophets and believers to fight the enemies, the polytheists would have taken control, and the places of worship would have been lost from the earth. The meaning of would have been destroyed is that it would have been ruined by the polytheists taking control of the people of other religions. So the monasteries are the monasteries of the monks, and it was said that they were the monasteries of the Sabians. The churches are the plural of church, which is the church of the Christians. The prayers are the churches of the Jews, and its name in Hebrew is Salutha with a triangle, which was Arabized. The mosques are the mosques of the Muslims. It was said that the meaning is: had it not been for this repelling, the churches would have been destroyed in the time of Moses, and the monasteries and churches in the time of Jesus, and the mosques in the time of Muhammad. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is the most correct interpretation of the verse. It was said that the meaning is: had God not repelled the oppression of the oppressors through the justice of the rulers, and it was said that God had not repelled the punishment through the supplication of the righteous, and other things were said. Monasteries: plural of silo, which is a tall building. It is said that the tharidah is sama’ if it raises its head, and the heart is sama’: meaning sharp-witted, and the sama’ of men means iron-spoken, and it is said that it means small-eared. Then it was used in the places where the call to prayer is made in Islam. Ibn Atiyyah mentioned in Salawat nine readings, and the reason for giving precedence to the places of worship of the people of religions over the place of worship of the Muslims is that they are older in construction and earlier in existence. The apparent meaning of the mentioned demolition is its real meaning as mentioned by Al-Zajjaj and others. It was said that what is meant by it is the metaphorical meaning, which is its being abandoned for worship. It was read to be demolished with emphasis, and the accusative of oft in his saying: The name of God is mentioned therein much is as an attribute of a deleted source: meaning much mention, or much time. The sentence is an attribute of the mosques.
