It was said that for all the mentioned things, And God will surely support whoever supports Him is the lam as an answer to a deleted oath: meaning, by God, God will support whoever supports Him. What is meant by whoever supports God is the one who supports His religion and His allies, and the strong one who is able to do something, and the mighty, majestic, noble, as Al-Zajjaj said. It was said that it is the one who is impregnable, who cannot be resisted, nor is he prevented.
22:41: The relative pronoun in His statement: 41- "Those whom We establish in the land is in the accusative case as an attribute of whom in His statement who will support him", as Al-Zajjaj said. And someone else said it is in the genitive case as an attribute of His statement "for those who fight". It was said that what is meant by them are the Muhajireen and Ansar and those who follow them in righteousness, and it was said that they are the people of the five daily prayers, and it was said that they are the rulers of justice, and it was said that they are other than that. And in it is the obligation of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong upon whomever God has established in the land and enabled to do that. The interpretation of the verse has been presented, and the meaning of "and to God belongs the outcome of matters" is that they refer to His judgment and management and no one else. Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was expelled from Makkah, Abu Bakr said: They expelled their Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so that the people would be destroyed. Then the verse was revealed: Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged. Ibn Abbas said: This is the first verse revealed about fighting. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good. It was narrated by more than one person on the authority of al-Thawri, but Ibn Abbas is not in it. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Those who were expelled from their homes meaning from Makkah to Madinah unjustly, meaning Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Affan who said: This verse was revealed about us: Those who were expelled from their homes without right and the verse after it: “We were expelled from our homes without right: then We established them in the land. We established prayer and gave zakah and enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong.” So it is for me and my companions. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib who said: This verse was revealed about the companions of Muhammad: And had God not repelled the people the verse: He said: Had God not repelled the followers through the companions of Muhammad, monasteries would have been demolished. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Monasteries would have been demolished the verse: He said: The monasteries in which the monks are, and the churches are the mosques of the Jews and the prayer places of the churches of the Christians, and the mosques are the mosques of the Muslims. And they narrated on his authority that he said: The churches are the churches of the Christians and the prayer places of the churches of the Jews. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam regarding his statement: Those who, if We establish them in the land, he said: the land of Medina, establish prayer, he said: the obligatory, and give zakat, he said: the obligatory, and enjoin what is right, he said: there is no god but God, and forbid what is wrong, he said: associating partners with God, and to God belongs the outcome of matters, he said: and with God is the reward for what they did.
22:42: His saying: 42- And if they deny you etc. This is a consolation and comfort to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, including a promise to him to destroy those who deny him, just as God Almighty destroyed those who denied those who came before him. It is guidance for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be patient with his people and to follow the example of the prophets who came before him in that.
22:43: 43- And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot. We have already mentioned these nations, what happened to them and their prophets, and what their fate was.
22:44: The only difference in the system is in his saying: 44- "And Moses denied", so the verb came in the passive form, because the people of Moses did not deny him, but rather others from the Copts denied him. "So I granted respite to the disbelievers, meaning I delayed the punishment from them and gave them respite, and the fa" is to arrange the respite after the denial. "Then I seized them", meaning I seized each group of the deniers with the punishment after the expiration of the period of respite. "So how was My denunciation?" This question is for confirmation: meaning, then look at how My denunciation was towards them and the change in what they were in of blessings and their destruction. Denunciation is a noun from munkar. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, then I seized them and denounced in the most eloquent denial. Al-Jawhari said: Denunciation and denunciation are changing the denunciation.
22:45: Then the Almighty mentioned how He punished the people of the lying towns, saying 45- How many a town have We destroyed meaning, We destroyed its people. We have already discussed this structure in Al Imran, and it was read I destroyed it, and the phrase while it was unjust is a circumstantial, and the phrase so it is empty is in apposition to We destroyed it, not to unjust because it is a circumstantial, and the punishment is not in the state of injustice, and what is meant by attributing injustice to it is attributing it to its al-Nas 114:and empty: in the sense of falling: meaning it is fallen on its thrones meaning on its roofs, and that is because of the idleness of its inhabitants until it collapsed and its walls fell on its roofs, and the interpretation of this verse has already been presented in Al Baqarah And a well that is not in use is in apposition to a town, and the meaning is: How many a town's people, and how many a well that is not in use, this is what Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Farra' said: It is in apposition to its thrones, and what is meant by the problem is the abandoned one. It was said that it is empty of its people due to their death, and it was said that it is sunken, and it was said that it is without buckets and ropes, and the constructed palace is the one with a high building, thus said Qatada and Ad-Dahhak, and it is indicated by the saying of Adi bin Zaid: It is built of marble and covered with lime, so that the birds can nest in its peaks and nests. Shada: meaning raised it. Saeed bin Jubair, Ata’, Ikrimah, and Mujahid said: What is meant by shada is plastered, taken from shid, which means plaster, and from it is the saying of the rajaz poet: Do not think that I am a man, like a water snake between mud and stone. It was said that the fortified is the one that Al-Kalbi said. Al-Jawhari said: The constructed is the one that is made with gypsum, and gypsum with the kasra is everything that a wall is covered with from plaster or tiles, and with the fatha it is the source, you say shada yashiduhu jassusa, and gypsum with the shaddah is the extended one. Al-Kisa’i said: For the singular of the Almighty’s saying: In fortified towers. The intended meaning is: How many fortified palaces are in disrepair like the inoperable well? The meaning of the inoperability of the palace is that it is inoperable of its people, or of its equipment, or something like that. Al-Qurtubi said in his interpretation: It is said that this well and the palace are well-known in Hadhramaut, for the palace overlooks the top of a mountain that cannot be climbed in any way, and the well is at its foot, and the wind does not leave anything that falls into it except that it brings it out, and the owners of the palace are the kings of the urbanites, and the owners of the well are the kings of the Bedouins. Al-Tha'labi and others narrated: The well was in Aden, Yemen, in a town called Hadhra'a. Four thousand of those who believed in Salih and were saved from the punishment descended there, along with Salih. Then Salih died, and the place was called Hadhramaut, because when Salih visited it, he died. So they built Hadhra'a and sat on this well and appointed a man over them. Then he mentioned a long story, and after that he said: As for the lofty palace, it was a palace built by Shaddad bin Aad bin Iram. Nothing like it has been built on earth, according to what they mentioned and claimed. Its condition was also like the condition of this well mentioned in its loneliness after familiarity, and its desertedness after civilization, and that no one could approach it for miles, because of what was heard in it of the jinn's singing and strange sounds after the bliss and comfortable life and the splendor of the kingdom, and the order of the people like a wire. So they hastened and did not return. So God Almighty mentioned them in this verse as a sermon and a lesson. He said: It was said that they were the ones who were destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar, as mentioned previously in Surat Al-Anbiya’ in His statement: And how many a city have We destroyed. Their well was destroyed and their palaces were ruined.
22:46: Then the Almighty denied the people of Mecca for not considering these traces, saying 46- Have they not traveled through the land? urging them to travel to see the fates of those nations and take heed. It is possible that they traveled and did not take heed, so that is why He denied them, as in His saying: "And indeed, you pass by them in the morning and at night. So will you not reason?" The meaning of so that they will have hearts with which to reason is that because of what they witnessed of the lessons, they will have hearts with which to reason what they must reason. Reasoning was attributed to the hearts because they are the seat of reason, just as the ears are the seat of hearing. It was said that the seat of reason is the brain, and there is no objection to that, for the heart is what prompts the mind to perceive, even if its seat is outside of it. The rationalists have differed greatly about the location of the mind and its nature, and there is no need to go into detail about it. Or ears with which they hear means what they should hear from what their prophets recited to them of the words of God, and what the people of report conveyed to them of the report of the destroyed nations. For indeed, the eyes are not blinded. Al-Farra’ said: The ha’ is a pillar. It is permissible to say: For indeed, which is the reading of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, and the meaning is the same, the masculine for the report, and the feminine for the eyes or the story: meaning, for the eyes are not blinded, or for the story, the eyes are not blinded: meaning the eyes of the eyes. But blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts means the defect is not in their feelings, but rather in their minds, meaning their minds do not perceive the places of truth and the places of consideration. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj said: His statement which are within the breasts is from the emphasis that the Arabs add to speech, like his statement: Ten complete, “They say with their mouths,” and Fly with its wings.
22:47: Then the Almighty narrated about these people what they were doing of denial and mockery, saying: 47- "And they urge you to hasten the punishment" because they were denying its coming with the utmost denial, so their hastening it was in the manner of mockery and ridicule, and it was as if they were saying that when they heard what the prophets were saying about God Almighty of His promise of its occurrence and its coming upon them, and for this reason He said: "And God will not fail in His promise" Al-Farra' said: In this verse there is a threat to them of punishment in this world and the hereafter. Al-Zajjaj mentioned another aspect, saying: I know that nothing escapes God, and that a day with Him and a thousand years in His power are one, and there is no difference between the occurrence of what they hasten of punishment and its delay in power, except that God has favored them with respite. The place of the sentence: And God will not fail in His promise is the accusative case in the state: that is, and the state is that He will never fail in His promise, and the promise has already come, so it must come inevitably, or it is an interjection explaining what came before it. According to the first, the sentence: And indeed a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count. According to the second, it is conjoined with the sentence before it, introduced to explain their state in hastening, and addressing them in that with a statement like His dream, because the short period with Him is like the long period with them, as in His statement: Indeed, they see it far off, but We see it near. Al-Farra’ said: This is a threat to them of the extension of their punishment in the Hereafter: that is, a day of their punishment in the Hereafter is like a thousand years. It was said that the meaning is: Indeed, a day of fear and severity in the Hereafter is like a thousand years of the years of this world in which there is fear and severity, and likewise the day of bliss by analogy. Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read ma ib’adunu with a lower case ending, and Abu Ubaid chose this reading because of his saying: and they hasten you. The rest read it with a higher case ending as a direct address, and Abu Hatim chose this reading.
22:48: 48- "And how many a town did I grant respite to while it was wrongdoing? Then I seized it, and to Me is the final destination." This is an announcement from Him, the Most High, that He seized a people after respite and delay. It was said that repeating this with its mention before it is for emphasis, and it is not a repetition in reality, because the first was cited to explain the destruction, appropriate to His statement: So how was My denial? And for this reason, it was connected with the letter fa instead of that. And the second was cited to explain the respite, appropriate to His statement: "And God will not fail in His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years." So it is as if it was said: And how many a town was like you, wrongdoers, whom I granted respite for a time, then seized them with punishment. And the reference of all is to My judgment. So the phrase: And to Me is the final destination is a conclusion to the confirmation of what came before it.
22:49: 49- Say, ‘O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you.’ Then God Almighty commanded him to inform the people that he is a warner to them before the Hour, explaining to them what was revealed to them.
22:50: 50- "So those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and noble provision." Whoever believes and does righteous deeds will win forgiveness and noble provision, which is Paradise.
22:51: 51- "And those who strive to outstrip Our verses - those are the companions of Hellfire." And whoever is contrary to that will be in Hellfire. They are those who strive to outstrip the verses of God. It is said that the one who outstrips the other, because each one of them is seeking to outstrip the other, so if he outstrips him, it is said that he outstripped him and outstripped him, said Al-Akhfash. And it is said that the meaning of "outstrip" is: thinking and desiring that they will outstrip God, the Exalted, and escape Him, so He will not punish them, said Al-Zajjaj. And it is said that they are obstinate, said Al-Farra'. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: So it is desolate on its roofs, he said: ruined with no one in it. And a well unused, its people abandoned it. And a lofty palace, he said: they built it and fortified it, so they perished and abandoned it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And a well unused, he said: the one that was left without people. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority. And a lofty palace, he said: it is plastered. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar from Mujahid. Abd al-Razzaq and Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar from Ata’. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And verily, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count, he said: of the six days in which God created the heavens and the earth. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, he said regarding the verse: it is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The world is a gathering of the gatherings of the Hereafter, seven thousand years, of which six thousand have passed. Ibn Adi and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Anas, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mu’ajizin meaning: Reluctant. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: Dissenters.
22:52: His saying: 52- "From a messenger or a prophet" It was said that the messenger is the one who was sent to the creation by sending Gabriel to him in person and conversing with him verbally, and the prophet is the one who is inspired or in a dream. It was said that the messenger is the one who was sent with a law and was commanded to convey it, and the prophet is the one who was commanded to call to a law before him, and no book was revealed to him, and both of them must have an apparent miracle "unless he desires, Satan casts into his desire" The meaning of desire is: he desires and prepares in his soul what he desires. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The meaning of desire is recitation. The group of commentators said about the reason for the revelation of this verse: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was distressed by his people’s turning away from him, he wished in his heart that nothing would be revealed to him that would turn them away from him, because of his keenness on their faith. One day, he was sitting in one of their clubs and Surah By the star when it goes down was revealed to him. He began to recite it to them until he reached the words: Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? That wish was in his heart, and it came to his tongue from what Satan had suggested to him: Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for. When Quraysh heard that, they rejoiced and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) continued reciting until he finished the surah. When he prostrated at the end of it, all those in the club, both Muslims and polytheists, prostrated with him. Quraysh dispersed, happy with that. They said: Muhammad has mentioned our gods in the best way. Gabriel came to him and said: What did you do? You recited to the people what I did not bring to you from God. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was saddened and feared greatly, so God revealed this verse. This is what they said. None of this is correct, nor has it been proven in any way. Despite its incorrectness, or rather its invalidity, the scholars have refuted it with the Book of God, the Most High. God says: And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta. And His statement: Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination. And His statement: And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them. So He denied the proximity of inclination, let alone inclination. Al-Bazzar said: This is a hadith that we do not know of, narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a continuous chain of transmission. Al-Bayhaqi said: This story is not proven in terms of transmission. Then he began to speak that the narrators of this story are questionable. The Imam of Imams, Ibn Khuzaymah, said: This story is a fabrication of the heretics. Al-Qadi Iyad said in Al-Shifa’: The nation has unanimously agreed, in terms of its transmission, that he is infallible in reporting something other than what he is, neither intentionally nor deliberately, nor by mistake nor inadvertently. Ibn Kathir said: Many commentators have mentioned here the story of the cranes, and the return of many of the emigrants to the land of Abyssinia, thinking that the polytheists of Quraysh had converted to Islam. However, all of these chains of narration are mursal, and I have not seen them attributed to a sound chain of narration. If you are certain that this is false, you will know that the meaning of tamanna is read and recited, as we have mentioned from al-Wahidi’s account of that from the commentators. Al-Baghawi also said: Most commentators said that the meaning of tamanna is read and recited the Book of God, and the meaning of Satan threw into his wish is in his recitation and reading. Ibn Jarir said: This statement is more like an interpretation of the speech, and this is supported by what was mentioned previously in the interpretation of His statement: They do not know the Book except in wishful thinking. It was said that the meaning of tamanna is an event, and the meaning of Satan threw into his wish is in his hadith. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was said that the meaning of tamanna is he said. The meaning of the verse is that Satan made the polytheists hear that without the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saying it or having it come out of his mouth. So this verse is a consolation for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), meaning that this should not frighten you or sadden you, for the same thing happened to the messengers and prophets before you. Assuming that the meaning of wish is that he spoke to himself, as Al-Farra’ and Al-Kisa’i narrated, for they said: he wished if he spoke to himself, then the meaning is that if he spoke to himself about something, Satan spoke it and cast it into the ears of the people without the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saying it or having it come out of his mouth. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: There is no disagreement that Satan’s casting is only for audible words that cause temptation. It has been said in the interpretation of the verse that what is meant by gharaneeq are the angels, and this is refuted by His statement: So God abrogates what Satan casts meaning He nullifies it, and the intercession of the angels is not invalid. It was said that this occurred on his tongue, may God bless him and grant him peace, inadvertently and forgetfully, and these are permissible for prophets. It is refuted by saying that forgetfulness and forgetfulness in the way of communication are not permissible, as is established in their contexts. Then when God Almighty consoled him with this consolation and that it had happened to those who came before him from the messengers and prophets, God Almighty explained that He would nullify it and not confirm it, and that Satan’s deception of him would not continue, so He said: Then God will nullify what Satan casts, meaning He will nullify it and make it go away and not be fixed. Then God will establish His verses, meaning He will confirm them. And God is Knowing and Wise, meaning He is full of knowledge and wisdom in all His words and actions.
22:53: And the sentence 53 - That He may make what Satan throws in a trial for the reason: that is, that throwing in which Satan throws in a trial: that is, a misguidance for those in whose hearts is disease that is, doubt and hypocrisy and those whose hearts are hardened they are the polytheists, for their hearts never soften towards the truth and never return to the right path, then the Almighty recorded for these two groups: and they are those in whose hearts is disease and those in whose hearts is hardness that they are wrongdoers and He said: And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme discord that is, intense enmity, and describing discord as being distant is an exaggeration, and the one described by it in reality is the one who committed it.
22:54: And when He, the Almighty, explained that this casting was a trial for the people of hypocrisy, doubt and polytheism, He explained that for the believers who know God and are aware of Him, it is a reason for them to gain knowledge that the Qur’an is true and honest, so He said: 54- And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, meaning the truth revealed from Him. It was said that the pronoun in that refers to enabling Satan to cast, because it is something that he usually does with his prophets, but this is rejected by His statement: So that they may believe in it, for what is meant by belief in the Qur’an is that they may remain steadfast in belief in it, so that their hearts may submit to it, meaning that they may be humbled, calmed and submissive. For belief in it and the submission of hearts to it cannot be enabling Satan, but rather to the Qur’an. And indeed, God is the Guide of those who believe, in matters of their religion, to a straight path, meaning a correct path with no crookedness. Abu Haywah read and indeed, God is the Guide of those who believe with the nunation.
22:55: 55- And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it meaning in doubt about the Qur'an, and it was said about the religion that indicates the mention of the straight path, and it was said about the devil's suggestion, so they say: Why did he mention idols with good and then go back on that? Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read in doubt with a damma on the meem until the Hour comes to them meaning the Resurrection suddenly meaning suddenly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day which is the Day of Resurrection because there is no day after it, so in this regard it was barren, and barren in the language is the one who does not have a child, and since the days follow one another it was made like the form of birth, and since there was no day after that day it was described as barren, and it was said that it was a day of war in which they were killed like the day of Badr, and it was said that the day was described as barren because there is no mercy or compassion in it, so it is as if it is barren of good, and from this is the saying of the Most High: When We sent upon them the barren wind meaning that which has no good in it and does not bring rain.
22:56: 56- The kingdom that Day will belong to God meaning the overwhelming authority and complete control: On the Day of Resurrection, God Almighty will be alone, with no one to dispute it or defend it. The phrase He will judge between them is a new sentence in response to an implied question. Then He explained this judgment by saying, So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the Gardens of Delight meaning they will be there, settled on its land, immersed in its delights.
22:57: 57- And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs meaning they combined disbelief in God and denial of His signs they will have a humiliating punishment meaning a punishment that is described as humiliating for those being punished, and it has reached a very great extent among them. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn al-Anbari narrated in al-Masahif on the authority of Amr bin Dinar who said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Sa`d bin Ibrahim bin Abd al-Rahman bin Awf, and he added: It was abrogated by a modernizer. He said: The modernizers are: the companion of Yasin, Luqman, the believer of the family of Pharaoh, and the companion of Moses. Al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Dhiya’ narrated in al-Mukhtara. Al-Suyuti said, with a chain of transmission whose men are trustworthy, Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza and Manat, the third, the other? These are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for.’ The polytheists rejoiced at that and said: ‘He has mentioned our gods.’ Then Gabriel came to him and said: ‘Recite to me what you have brought.’ So he recited: ‘Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza and Manat, the third, the other? These are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for.’ He said: ‘I have not brought you this, this is from Satan.’ Then God revealed: ‘And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished, he made a wish.’” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, and al-Suyuti said, with a sound chain of transmission, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited An-Najm in Mecca, and he mentioned something similar, but he did not mention Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah and al-Suddi on the authority of Saeed, without a chain of transmission. Abd bin Hamid narrated it on the authority of al-Suddi on the authority of Abu Salih, without a chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Shihab, without a chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, also without a chain of transmission. The result is that all the narrations in this chapter are either without a chain of transmission or without a chain of transmission, and none of them can be used as evidence. We have already mentioned enough from the hadith scholars at the beginning of this research. There are narrations in this chapter, and whoever wants to know all of them should look at them in al-Durr al-Manthur by al-Suyuti. There is no benefit in mentioning them here at length, as we have already told you that none of them can be used as evidence. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, If he wishes, Satan casts into his wish, meaning if he speaks, Satan casts into his speech. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Dahhak, who said: By wishing, he means recitation and reading. Satan casts into his wish: into his recitation. Then God abrogates, Gabriel abrogates, by God’s command, what Satan cast onto the tongue of the Prophet. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, If he wishes, he said: he spoke. In his wish, he said: his speech. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The punishment of a barren day, he said: the day of Badr. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr: The punishment of a barren day, he said: the day of Badr. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubay... Mujahid regarding the verse: the Day of Resurrection has no night. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ad-Dahhak.
22:58: God Almighty singled out the immigrants for mention, giving them more honor, saying: 58- And those who emigrated for the cause of God. Some commentators said: They are those who emigrated from Mecca to Medina. Some of them said: Those who emigrated from their homelands in a secret or military operation, and it is not far-fetched to carry that to both matters, and all of them are from the path of God Then they were killed or died meaning in the state of emigration, and the lam in So that God will provide them with a good provision is the answer to an omitted oath, and the sentence is the predicate of the relative pronoun with the estimation of the saying, and the accusative of provision is that it is a second noun: meaning provided with good provision, or that it is a source of emphasis, and good provision is the bliss of Paradise that does not cease, and it was said that it is the spoils because it is lawful, and it was said that it is knowledge and understanding like the saying of Shu’ayb And He provided me from it a good provision Ibn ‘Amir and the people of Ash-Sham read Then they were killed with emphasis for the multiplicity, and the rest read with alleviation And indeed, God is the best of providers for He, glory be to Him, provides without account, and every provision that flows through the hands of the servants to each other, it is from Him, glory be to Him, there is no provider other than Him and no giver other than Him, and the sentence is a conclusion confirming what came before it.
22:59: And the sentence 59- He will surely admit them to an entrance that will please them is a resumption, or a substitute for the sentence God will provide for them. The people of Medina read an entrance with a fat-ha on the meem, and the rest read it with a damma, and it is the name of a place that is intended for Paradise, and its accusative is as a second object or a verbal noun with a meem that confirms the mentioned verb, and we have already discussed something similar in Surat Subhan. And in this there is gratitude to them and good report for them that cannot be measured, for the entrance that they are pleased with is the most appropriate for their souls and closest to their desire, even though they see in Paradise what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, and that is what they are pleased with and above pleasure and indeed God is Knowing of the degrees of the workers and the levels of their deservingness Forbearing about the negligence of those who are negligent among them, and He does not hasten to punish them.
22:60: And the reference in his saying: 60- "that" is to what came before. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, the matter is what we have told you about fulfilling the promise to the immigrants, especially if they were killed or died. According to this, it is the predicate of a deleted subject. The meaning of and whoever punishes with the like of that with which he was punished is to repay the oppressor with the like of what he wronged him. The beginning is called the recompense in resemblance to the Almighty’s saying: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it and His saying: So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the like of that with which he transgressed against you. The punishment in origin only comes after an action, and it is a recompense for it. What is meant by the like is that it was limited to the amount with which he was wronged and did not increase it. The meaning of then he was wronged is that the oppressor against him in the beginning returned to the injustice after that first injustice. It was said that what is meant by this injustice is what happened from the polytheists of disturbing the Muslims from their homelands after they denied their prophet and harmed those who believed in him. The lam in God will surely support him is the answer to a deleted oath: that is, God will surely support the oppressed against the oppressor. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Forgiving meaning, He is abundant. Pardon and forgiveness for the believers for the sins they have committed. It has been said that pardon and forgiveness are for what the believers have committed of preferring revenge over forgiveness. It has also been said that the meaning of then he was wronged is then the metaphorical was wronged: that is, oppressed. The meaning of then is the difference in rank, because initiating the fight with him is a type of oppression, as is said in the proverbs of the Arabs: The one who starts is more unjust. It was said that this verse was revealed in Medina, and it is about retaliation and wounds.
22:61: And the reference in His saying: 61- That is because God causes the night to enter the day is to what came before of God's victory for the oppressed, and it is a subject and its predicate is the sentence that God causes it to enter, and the ba' is for causality: that is because He, the Almighty, is able, and from the perfection of His ability is causing the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night, and He expressed the increase by causing it, because the increase of one of them necessitates the decrease of the other, and what is meant is the acquisition of one of the two events in the place of the other. And the meaning of this causing it has already passed in Al Imran And that God is All-Hearing He hears everything that is heard, All-Seeing He sees everything that is seen, or Hears words and sees actions, so not even an atom escapes Him.
22:62: And the reference in His saying: 62- That is because God is the Truth to what came before of His being described as perfect, overwhelming power and perfect knowledge: that is, He is the Possessor of the Truth, so His religion is true, His worship is true, His victory for His friends over His enemies is true, and His promise is true, so He, the Almighty, is true in Himself, His actions and His attributes. And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir and Shu'bah read you call upon with the superlative, addressing the polytheists, and Abu Hatim chose this reading. The rest read it with the subjunctive, as a predicate, and Abu Ubaidah chose this reading. Meaning: Those whom you call gods, which are idols, are falsehood that has no proof or basis for being gods. And that God is the Most High, meaning the One who is high above everything by His power, the One who is sanctified above all likenesses and equals, the One who is free from what the wrongdoers say about attributes. The Great, meaning the One with pride, which is an expression of the perfection of His essence and His uniqueness in divinity.
22:63: Then the Almighty mentioned a clear proof of the perfection of His power, saying: 63- Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? The question is for confirmation, and the fa is for conjunction with anzala, and the verb was raised after the fa because it is a question of confirmation in the position of report, as Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said. Al-Khalil said: The meaning is that He sent down water from the sky, and it was such and such, as the poet said: Didn't you ask the strong quarter to speak? And will the desert of Samlaq tell you today? Meaning: I asked him and he spoke. Al-Farraa said: Haven’t you seen a report like you say in speech: God sends down water from the sky and the earth becomes green: meaning green as you say green and wild: meaning green with vegetables and beasts, and it is an expression of its hastening the effect of the water descending on the plants and its continuation in this way usually, and the future tense is to evoke the image of greening with the indication of the renewal of the descent and its continuation, and this meaning does not occur except in the future, and the nominative here is necessary because if it were to be accusative the intended meaning of the verse would be reversed and it would turn into negating the greening, and the intended meaning is to affirm it. Ibn Atiyyah said: This does not happen: meaning the greening on the morning of a rainy night except in Mecca and Tihamah. It appears that what is meant by greenness is the greening of the earth itself, not in terms of the plants in it, as in His statement: Then when We send down upon it water, it quivers and swells. What is meant by His statement: Indeed, God is Kind is that His knowledge reaches every minute and great thing. It was said that He is Kind with the provisions of His servants, and it was said that He is Kind with the extraction of plants. The meaning of All-Knowing is that He is knowledgeable in the management of His servants and what is good for them. It was said that He is All-Knowing of what they conceal of despair when the rain is delayed, and it was said that He is All-Knowing of their need and poverty.
22:64: 64- To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth in creation, ownership, and control, and all of them are in need of His provision. And indeed, God is the Free of need so He does not need anything. The Praiseworthy is the One who deserves praise in every situation.
22:65: 65- "Have you not seen that God has subjected to you whatever is on the earth?" This is another blessing that God Almighty mentioned, so He informed His servants that He has subjected to them what they need of animals, trees, and rivers and made it for their benefit. "And the ship is in apposition to what, or to the name of that": meaning, He has subjected to you the ship while it is sailing in the sea. Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj read "and the ship in the nominative case as the subject and what He has subjected to" is its predicate, and the rest read it in the accusative case. The meaning of it flows in the sea by His command is by His decree. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state according to the reading of the majority. And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth meaning He hates it to fall, because He created it in a manner that requires holding back. The sentence is conjoined with it flows “except by His permission” meaning by His will and desire, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God is to mankind Kind and Merciful meaning He is very kind and merciful, as He has subjected these matters to His servants and prepared for them the means of livelihood, and He has held back the sky from falling upon the earth and destroying them, as a favor from Him to His servants and as a blessing upon them.
22:66: Then the Almighty mentioned another blessing, saying: 66- And it is He who gave you life after you were inanimate then He will cause you to die when your lives come to an end then He will bring you to life when you are resurrected for the reckoning and punishment Indeed, man is ungrateful meaning he is very ungrateful for God’s blessings upon him, even though they are apparent and not hidden. This does not contradict some individuals being outside of this denial, because what is meant is to describe the entire species with the description of those individuals in whom that is found, as an exaggeration. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Salman al-Farsi that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever dies as a guard, God will reward him with the same reward, provide him with sustenance, and keep him safe from the afflictions. Read, if you wish, “And those who emigrated for the cause of God and were killed or died” until His saying: Forbearing. The chain of transmission of Ibn Abi Hatim is as follows: Al-Musayyab ibn Wadheeh narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Shuraih on the authority of Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith on the authority of Ibn Uqbah, meaning Abu Ubaydah ibn Uqbah, who said: Shurahbil ibn al-Simt said: Our guarding and staying at a fortress in the land of the Romans was prolonged, and Salman, meaning al-Farsi, passed by me and said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Fadala ibn Ubayd al-Ansari, the companion, that he was in Rhodes and they passed by two funerals, one of them was killed and the other was deceased, so the people turned away from the killed one, so Fadala said: Why do I see the people turning away from this one and leaving this one? They said: This is the one who was killed in the cause of God. He said: By God, I do not care from which of the two graves I am sent. Listen to the Book of God: And those who emigrated for the cause of God and were killed or died (al-Baqarah 2:170). Its chain of transmission with Ibn Abi Hatim is as follows: Abu Zur’ah told us on the authority of Zaid bin Bishr, who told me that Dhimam heard Abu Qabil and Rabi’ah bin Saif al-Maghafari say: We were in Rhodes and with us was Fadalah bin Ubayd al-Ansari, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned him. I said: This is supported by the statement of God, the Most High: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has become incumbent upon God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil regarding his statement: And whoever punishes with the like of that with which he was punished, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a detachment during the last two nights of Muharram and they encountered the polytheists. The polytheists said to each other: Fight the companions of Muhammad, for they forbid fighting in the sacred month. The companions of Muhammad urged them and reminded them by God to expose themselves to fighting them, for they do not consider fighting permissible in the sacred month except for those who initiate it. The polytheists initiated it and fought them, so the companions considered fighting them permissible at that time, so they fought them and God granted them victory over them. It is a mursal hadith. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement: And whoever punishes, the verse, he said: The polytheists cooperated against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions and expelled him, so God promised to grant him victory. It is also in retaliation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, And that which they invoke besides Him is falsehood, he said: The devil. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan regarding his statement: Indeed, man is ungrateful, he said: He counts the calamities and forgets the blessings.
22:67: God Almighty returned to explaining the matter of obligations while warning the contemporaries of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the people of religions against disputing with him, saying: 67- For every nation We have appointed a ritual. That is, for every century of the past centuries, We established a specific law, such that no nation of them would transgress its specific law for another. The phrase they are its worshippers is an attribute of a ritual, and the pronoun refers to every nation: that is, that nation is the one who practices it and no other. So the Torah was the ritual of the nation that existed from the mission of Moses to the mission of Jesus, and the Gospel was the ritual of the nation that existed from the mission of Jesus to the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an was the ritual of the Muslims. The ritual is a source, not a place name, as indicated by they are its worshippers, and He did not say the worshippers in it. It was said that the ritual is the place of performing obedience, and it was said that it is the sacrifices, and there is no reason for specificity, and no consideration for the specificity of the reason, and the fa in his saying: So let them not dispute with you in the matter is to arrange the prohibition on what preceded it, and the pronoun refers to the nations whose traces remain: that is, We have appointed for each nation a law, and among these nations is the Muhammadan nation, and that necessitates that those who remain from them not dispute with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and necessitates their obedience to him in the matter of religion, and the prohibition is either in its true sense, or a metaphor for his prohibition, may God bless him and grant him peace, of paying attention to their dispute with him. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a prohibition for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, from disputing with them: that is, do not dispute with them, just as you say, So-and-so does not dispute with you, meaning do not dispute with him, and just as you say, So-and-so does not dispute with you, meaning do not fight with him, and that is because the reciprocal verb implies the opposite, and it is not permissible for So-and-so does not strike you when you mean do not strike him. It was narrated from Al-Zajjaj that he said about the meaning of the verse: So let them not dispute with you, meaning do not argue with him. He said: This is indicated by And if they dispute with you and Abu Majlaz read Do not make you feel inferior or overcome you in your religion. The rest read They dispute with you from dispute. “And call to your Lord” meaning call these disputants or call people in general to the religion of God, His Oneness and belief in Him. Indeed, you are on a straight path meaning a straight path with no crookedness in it.
22:68: 68- And if they argue with you meaning if they refuse to argue except after the explanation and the proof has been made clear to them, “then say: God knows best what you do” meaning then all their affair is up to God and say to them this statement that includes the threat.
22:69: 69- God will judge between you meaning between the Muslims and the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ of religious matters. Then truth will be distinguished from falsehood. In this verse there is instruction for this nation on how they should respond to those who want to argue falsely. It was said that it was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
22:70: And the sentence 70 - Have you not known? is a resumption confirming the content of what preceded it, and the question is for confirmation: meaning you have known, O Muhammad, and you are certain that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and among that is what you differ about, that what is in the heavens and the earth of His information is in a book meaning it is written with Him in the Mother of the Book Indeed, that is easy for God meaning that the judgment from Him, glory be to Him, between His servants in what they differ about is easy for Him, not difficult, or that His knowledge encompassing what is in the heavens and the earth is easy for Him.
22:71: 71- And they worship besides God that for which He has not sent down any authority. This is a narration of some of their scandals: that is, they worship idols whose worship they have not adhered to with a clear proof from God Almighty. And that of which they have no knowledge. From rational evidence that indicates the permissibility of this in one way or another. And for the wrongdoers there is no helper. To support them and ward off God's punishment from them. We have already discussed this verse in Al Imran.
22:72: And the sentence 72- And when Our verses are recited to them as clear proofs is connected to they worship, and the accusative of clear proofs is in the state: that is, the state of their being clear and apparent in meaning. You recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve the evil, that is, the matter that is denied, which is their anger and frowning when they hear it, or what is meant by evil is denial: that is, you recognize in their faces the denial of it, and it was said that it is arrogance and haughtiness, and the sentence They almost assault those who recite to them Our verses is a new answer to an implied question as if it was said: What is that evil that is recognized in their faces? So it was said that they almost assault: that is, they strike, and assault is the severity of the assault. It is said that he assaulted him, he assaulted him by hitting, or cursing, or taking by the hand, and the root of assault is coercion. Thus you see the people of misguided innovations, when one of them hears what a scholar recites to them from the verses of the Noble Book, or from the authentic Sunnah, which contradicts what he believes to be falsehood and misguidance, you will see on his face such reprehensibility that if he were able to attack that scholar, he would do to him what he would not do to the polytheists. We have seen and heard from the people of innovations what cannot be described. And God is the supporter of the truth, the manifester of the religion, the refuter of falsehood, the destroyer of innovations, and the protector of the theologians with what He has taken from them, explaining to the people what was revealed to them. And He is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Then He ordered His Messenger to respond to them, saying: “Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that” which is in you of rage against those who recite to you the verses of God and your approach to attack them, which is the fire that God has prepared for you. The fire is raised as a predicate for an omitted subject, and the sentence is the answer to an implied question as if it was said: What is this matter that is worse than what we suffer and confront when we hear what you recite to us? So He said: The Fire which God has promised to those who disbelieve It was said that the fire is the subject and its predicate is the sentence God has promised to those who disbelieve. It was said that the meaning is: Shall I inform you of something worse than that which will befall those who recite the Qur’an among you of harm and threats to them and repentance against them? The fire was read in the accusative case, estimating I mean, and it was read in the genitive case instead of evil, “and evil is the destination” meaning the place to which you will go, which is the fire. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: They are its devotees, he said: meaning they are its slaughterers. So let them not dispute with you in the matter, meaning in the matter of slaughtering. Abd bin Hamid narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, he said: So let them not dispute with you in the matter is the saying of the polytheists: As for what God slaughtered with His right hand, do not eat it, but as for what you slaughtered with your own hands, it is permissible. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God created the Preserved Tablet a distance of one hundred years, and He said to the Pen before He created the creation while He was on the Throne: Write. It said: What should I write? He said: My knowledge is in my creation until the Day of Resurrection. So the pen wrote down what would be in the knowledge of God until the Day of Resurrection. That is what He said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? meaning what is in the seven heavens and the seven earths. Indeed, that knowledge is in a Book meaning in the Preserved Tablet written before He created the heavens and the earths. Indeed, that, for God, is easy meaning simple. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They almost assault means they strike.
22:73: His saying: 73- O people, a parable is made. This is connected to his saying: And they worship besides God that for which He has not sent down any authority. Al-Akhfash said: There is no parable, but the meaning is that they have made a parable for me, so listen to their saying, meaning that the disbelievers have made a parable for God by worshipping other than Him, so it is as if he said: They have made a likeness for me in my worship, so enjoy the report of this likeness. Al-Qatibi said: The meaning, O people, is the parable of someone who worships gods who cannot create a fly, and if you take something from them, they cannot extract it from them. Al-Nahhas said: The meaning is that God, the Almighty, has made a parable for what they worship besides Him. He said: This is one of the best things that has been said about it: meaning, God has made clear to you a likeness and for your object of worship. The origin of the proverb is a sentence of speech received with satisfaction and acceptance and is strange to people, and they make it an example for its source, then they may borrow it for a strange story, condition or characteristic because it is similar to it in strangeness like this story mentioned in this verse. What is meant by what they call upon besides God are the idols that were around the Kaaba and elsewhere. It was said that what is meant by them are the masters who turned them away from obeying God because they are the people of solution and contract among them. It was said that they are the devils who led them to disobey God, and the first is more appropriate to the situation and clearer in the example. Wolves are a name for the singular that is applied to both males and females, and the plural of paucity is adhbah, and the plural is dhabban like gharab, aghrabah, and ghuraban. Al-Jawhari said: The fly is well-known, and its singular is a fly. The meaning is: They will not be able to create it, even though it is small in body and insignificant in essence. The phrase even if they gathered together for it is connected to another conditional clause that has been deleted: that is, if they did not gather together for it, they would not create it, even if they gathered together for it. The answer is deleted, and the meaning is: They will not create it, and they are in the accusative case as a state: that is, they will not create it in any case. Then the Almighty explained the completeness of their helplessness and the weakness of their ability, saying: And if a fly should steal something from them, they cannot rescue it from it. That is, if a fly should steal something from them, they would not be able to rescue it from it due to their complete helplessness and extreme weakness. Rescue and rescue means getting rid of it, and if they are unable to create this weak animal, and to rescue it, and to rescue what it has taken from them, then they are more helpless and weaker than anything else that is greater in mass and stronger than it. Then the Almighty was amazed at the weakness of the idols and the flies, saying: The weakness of the seeker and the sought. The idol is like the seeker in that it seeks to create the fly or seeks to rescue what it has stolen from it, and the sought is the fly. It has been said that the seeker is the worshipper of the idol, and the sought is the idol. It has been said that the seeker is the fly and the sought are the gods.
22:74: Then the Almighty explained that the polytheists who worshipped gods other than God who were helpless to this extreme in helplessness did not know God as He should be known, so He said: 74- They did not appreciate God as He should be appreciated, meaning they did not glorify Him as He should be glorified, nor did they know Him as He should be known, since they made these idols partners with Him, despite their condition being this condition. It was mentioned previously in Al-An’am, Indeed, God is Powerful, over the creation of everything, Mighty, dominant, and no one can overcome Him, unlike the gods of the polytheists, for they are inanimate, without reason, nor do they benefit or harm, nor are they capable of anything.
22:75: Then the Almighty wanted to respond to them regarding what they believe in prophecies and divinities, so He said: 75- God chooses from among the angels messengers such as Gabriel, Israfil, Michael, and Azrael and He also chooses messengers from among the people who are the prophets, so He sends the angel to the prophet, and the prophet to the people, or He sends the angel to seize the souls of His creatures, or to obtain what will benefit you, or to bring down punishment upon them for God is Hearing of the words of His servants Seeing of whom He chooses from among His creation.
22:76: 76- He knows what is before them and what is behind them meaning what good and evil deeds they have done and what they have left behind, as God Almighty says: And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind “And to God are matters returned” not to anyone else.
40:60: And since what he mentioned about matters returning to Him includes warning His servants from disobeying Him and urging them to obey Him, he made clear what was intended and said: 77- O you who have believed, bow and prostrate meaning perform the prayer that God has prescribed for you, and he specified prayer because it is the most honorable of acts of worship. Then he generalized and said: And worship your Lord meaning do all types of worship that God has commanded you to do and do good meaning what is good, and they are more general than obligatory and recommended obedience, and it was said that what is meant by good here are recommended acts. Then he explained that by saying: Perhaps you will succeed meaning if you do all of these, you will hope for success. This verse is one of the places where prostration of recitation is prescribed according to Al-Shafi'i and those who agreed with him, not according to Abu Hanifah and those who said the same. It was previously mentioned that this Surah is preferred by having two prostrations, and this is evidence that prostration is established when reciting this verse. Then he ordered them to do what is the pinnacle of religion and its greatest deeds, saying: 78- And strive in the cause of God meaning in His essence and for His sake, and what is meant by it is the greater jihad, which is the invasion of the infidels and defending them if they invade the lands of the Muslims. It was said that what is meant by jihad here is compliance with what God commanded them to do in the previous verse, or compliance with everything that He commanded and prohibited in general, and the meaning of the right of His jihad is the exaggeration in the command to this jihad, because He added the right to jihad, and the original is to add jihad to the right: meaning a jihad purely for God, so He reversed that for the purpose of exaggeration, and jihad was added to the pronoun for the sake of expansion, or because it is specific to Him, the Most High, in terms of being the object of the verb and for His sake. It was said that what is meant by the right of His jihad is that you do not fear the blame of a blamer in God's cause, and it was said that what is meant by it is to exhaust all your ability in reviving the religion of God. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: The verse was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: So fear God as much as you are able, just as His saying: Fear God as He should be feared was abrogated by that. This was responded to by saying that the obligation is conditional upon ability, so there is no need to resort to abrogation. Then the Almighty glorified the status of those who are obligated by His saying: He has chosen you, meaning He has selected you for His religion, and in that is a great honor for them. Then since the obligation is difficult for the soul in some cases, He said: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty, meaning any narrowness and hardship. Scholars have differed about this hardship that God has lifted. It was said: It is what God has made permissible of women, two, three, four, and the right hand. It was also said that what is meant is shortening the prayer, breaking the fast for the traveler, praying by gesture for those who are unable to do otherwise, dropping jihad for the lame, the blind, and the sick, and forgiving the mistake of advancing or delaying fasting due to the difference in the crescent moons, as well as in the Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha. It was also said that the meaning is that He, glory be to Him, did not impose hardship on them by imposing what is difficult for them, but He imposed on them what they are able to do, and He lifted from them the obligations that are hard, so He did not make them obligated to do them as He made the children of Israel obligated to do them. It was also said that what is meant by this is that He made for them a way out of sin by opening the door of repentance, seeking forgiveness, and atonement for what He has prescribed for atonement and compensation, or retaliation in crimes, and returning the money or its equivalent or its value in the case of usurpation and the like. It appears that the verse is more general than all of this, as God Almighty has removed the burdensome obligations from His servants: either by dropping them from the beginning and not imposing them as He has imposed them on others, or by making it easier and allowing a change to an alternative that is not burdensome, or by making it permissible to get rid of sin in the manner prescribed by God. How beneficial this verse is, how sublime its position is, and how great its benefit is. Similar to it is the statement of God Almighty: So fear God as much as you are able, His statement: God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship, and His statement: “Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us. Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear.” And in the authentic hadith, He Almighty said: I have done so, as was previously explained in the interpretation of this verse, and there are many hadiths on this. The accusative of millah in the religion of your father Abraham is a source of a verb indicated by what preceded it: meaning He has made your religion easy for you as the religion of your father Abraham was easy. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is follow the religion of your father Abraham. Al-Farra’ said: It is in the accusative case on the assumption of deleting the kaf: meaning a word. It was said that the estimate is: And do good as your father Abraham did, so He established the religion in place of the verb. It was said that it was on the basis of enticement, and it was said that it was on the basis of specificity. And the Almighty made him their father because he is the father of the Arabs as a whole, and because he has great sanctity among the non-Arabs who were not from his descendants, like the sanctity of the father over the son because he is the father of their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He named you Muslims before meaning in the previous books. And in this meaning the Qur’an, and the pronoun refers to God Almighty. It was said that it refers to Abraham. The meaning is: that is, Abraham named you Muslims before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in this: meaning in his ruling that whoever follows Muhammad is a Muslim. Al-Nahhas said: This statement contradicts the statement of the scholars of the nation. Then the Almighty explained that by saying: So that the Messenger may be a witness over you meaning in conveying it to you. And you may be witnesses over the people that their messengers have conveyed it to them. The meaning of this verse has been explained previously in Al-Baqarah. Then he commanded them with what is the greatest of the Islamic pillars, saying: Establish prayer and give zakat. The two characteristics were specifically mentioned for their greater honor. And hold fast to God. That is, make Him your protection from what you fear, and turn to Him in all your affairs, and do not seek that from anyone but Him. He is your Protector. That is, your supporter and the One who takes care of your affairs, both minor and major. What an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper. That is, there is no one like Him in the guardianship of your affairs and victory over your enemies. It was said that what is meant by His saying, Hold fast to God is: hold fast to the religion of God. It was also said that you should trust in Him, the Most High. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: O people, a parable is made, he said: It was revealed about an idol. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: The weakness of the seeker and the sought, he said: The seeker is their gods, and the sought is the fly. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: They cannot rescue him from it, he said: The idols cannot rescue that thing from the fly. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on his authority also on the authority of Anas and authenticated it that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He chose Moses with speech, and Abraham with friendship. He also narrated on the authority of Anas and authenticated it that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Moses, son of Imran, is the chosen one of God. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf who said: Umar said to me: Didn’t we read among what we read: And strive for God with His striving at the end of time as you strived at its beginning? I said: Yes. Then when will this be, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: When the Umayyads are the princes and the Mughira are the ministers. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala'il on the authority of Al-Miswar bin Makhramah who said: Umar said to Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf and he mentioned it. Al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Askari in Al-Amthal on the authority of Fadalah bin Ubaid who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The mujahid is the one who strives against himself in obedience to God. Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty. He said: Difficulty. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad who said: Abu Hurairah said to Ibn Abbas: Is there no difficulty for us in religion if we steal or commit adultery? He said: Yes. He said: So And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty? He said: The burden that was a burden on the Children of Israel has been lifted from you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab that Ibn Abbas used to say: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty in expanding Islam, what God has placed of repentance and expiations. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Yasar on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty. He said: This is regarding the crescent of Ramadan if people are in doubt about it, and regarding Hajj if they are in doubt about Eid Al-Adha, and regarding Eid Al-Fitr and the like. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr that Ibn Abbas was asked about Al-Harq and he said: Call a man from Hudhayl for me. So he came to him and said: What is Al-Harq among you? He said: The hut is from the trees from which there is no exit. Ibn Abbas said: That which has no exit. Saeed bin Jubayr, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abi Yazid that Ibn Abbas was asked about Al-Harq and he said: Is there someone from Hudhayl here? A man said: I am. He said: What do you consider Al-Harq among you? He said: A narrow thing. He said: That is it. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Muhammad bin Zaid bin Abdullah bin Omar who said: Omar bin Al-Khattab recited this verse: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty then he said to me: Call for me a man from Banu Mudlij. Omar said: What is the difficulty for you? He said: Difficulty. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: The religion of your father. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He named you Muslims before, he said: God the Almighty: He named you. Something similar was narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un. Al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Al-Bukhari in his history, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, Al-Baghawi, Al-Barudi, Ibn Qani’, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Al-Harith Al-Ash’ari on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever supplicates with the supplication of the Age of Ignorance will be among the people of Hellfire. A man said: O Messenger of God, even if he fasts and prays? He said: Yes, so supplicate with the supplication of God by which He named you Muslims and believers, servants of God. Then, when He, the Almighty, made clear that the establishment of the Hour is true, without doubt or suspicion, He guided His servants to what is the means to happiness in the eternal home. He ordered His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to narrate from Him what He ordered him to convey, which is 60- And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you.’ Most of the commentators said that the meaning is: Believe in Me alone and worship Me; I will accept your worship and forgive you. It was also said that what is meant by supplication is asking to bring benefit and ward off harm. It was said that the first is more appropriate because supplication in most of its uses in the Noble Book is worship. I said: Rather, the second is more appropriate because the meaning of supplication, in reality and in the Shari’ah, is to request. If it is used for something other than that, then it is metaphorical. Moreover, supplication in itself, in its real meaning, is worship, indeed the essence of worship, as mentioned in the authentic hadith. So, God, the Almighty, has ordered His servants to supplicate to Him and has promised them that He will respond, and His promise is true, and He does not change His word, nor does He break His promise. Then the Almighty stated that this supplication, in its true meaning, which is asking, is from His worship, saying: Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell, humiliated. That is, humiliated and subdued. This is a severe threat to those who are too arrogant to call upon God, and in it is great kindness to His servants and great benevolence towards them, as He threatened with this severe threat those who abandon asking good from Him and warding off evil through Him and punished them with this great punishment. O servants of God, direct your desires and rely in all your requests on the One who ordered you to direct them to Him, guided you to rely on Him, and guaranteed that He will answer you by granting your request. He is the Absolutely Generous One who answers the call of the caller when he calls upon Him, and He becomes angry with the one who does not ask from His great bounty and vast kingdom for what he needs of worldly and religious matters. It was said that this promise of an answer is restricted to the will: that is, I will answer you if You will, as in His statement, the Most High: He will remove that which you call upon Him for, if God wills. The majority of scholars read they will enter with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the kha’, in the active form. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Warsh, and Abu Ja’far read it with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the kha’, in the passive form.
23:1: It is Meccan without dispute. Al-Qurtubi said: It is all Meccan according to everyone, and it has one hundred and nineteen verses. Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and others narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer in Mecca and began with Surat Al-Mu’minun, then when he mentioned Moses and Aaron, or Jesus, he was overcome with a cough and bowed. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Anas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: When God created Paradise, He said to it, ‘Speak.’ It said, ‘The believers have succeeded.’ It was also narrated by Ibn ‘Adi and Al-Hakim. At-Tabarani in As-Sunnah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas. The virtues of the first ten verses of this Surah have been mentioned, which will be mentioned shortly. His saying: 1- The believers have succeeded. Al-Farra’ said: Qad here may be an emphasis on the success of the believers, and it may be an approximation of the past from the present, because Qad brings the past close to the present until it is connected to its ruling. Do you not see them saying: The prayer has begun before the time of its establishment? The meaning of the verse is that success has been achieved for them, and that they are upon it at the present time. Success is achieving what is desired and escaping from what is disliked. It was said that it means remaining in goodness. Aflah means entering into success. It is said that aflah means making him succeed. The meaning of success has been explained previously at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. Talhah ibn Musarraf read Qad aflah with a damma on the hamza and the verb is in the passive form. It was narrated from him that he read aflahu al-mu’minun as an ambiguity and explanation, or in the language of the fleas ate me.
23:2: Then he described these believers by saying: 2- Those who are humble in their prayers and what is connected to it, and humility: some of them made it from the actions of the heart like fear and awe, and some of them made it from the actions of the limbs like stillness and not turning around and playing, and in the language it is stillness, humility, fear and submissiveness. People have differed about humility, is it one of the obligatory duties of prayer or one of its virtues? There are two opinions: It was said that the first is correct, and it was said that the second. Abdul Wahid bin Zaid claimed that the scholars agreed that the servant has nothing but what he understands from his prayer, as narrated by Al-Naysaburi in his interpretation. He said: What indicates the correctness of this opinion is the saying of God the Almighty: Do they not then reflect on the Qur’an? Reflection cannot be conceived without contemplating the meaning, and likewise His saying: Establish prayer for My remembrance. Heedlessness is the opposite of remembrance, and for this reason He said: And do not be among the heedless. His saying: Until you know what you are saying is a prohibition for the drunkard and the one immersed in worldly concerns, as is the case.
23:3: 3- And those who turn away from ill speech. Illusion, Al-Zajjaj said: is every falsehood, idle play, sin, and whatever is not acceptable in speech or action. Its explanation has been presented in Al-Baqarah. Ad-Dahhak said: Illusion here refers to polytheism. Al-Hasan said: it refers to all sins.
