The meaning of their turning away from it is their avoidance of it and not paying attention to it. Its apparent meaning is that they are characterized by the quality of turning away from ill speech at all times, so the time of prayer is included in that primarily as indicated by the nominal sentence and the construction of the ruling on the pronoun.
23:4: The meaning of their doing zakat is their paying it, so paying it was expressed with the verb because it is one of the things that can be described as a verb. What is meant by zakat here is the source because it is the one that comes from the doer. It was said that it is permissible to mean the essence of it on the assumption of an added word: i.e. 4- And those who are to pay zakat are doing.
23:5: 5- And those who guard their private parts The private parts refer to the private parts of men and women, and the meaning of guarding them is that they are keeping them chaste from what is not permissible for them. It was said that the subjects here are men in particular, not women, as evidenced by His statement: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, because there is consensus that it is not permissible for a woman to be penetrated by someone she owns.
23:6: Al-Farra' said: On in his statement: 6- Except for their wives means from. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that they are blamed for issuing what was forbidden to them, so they were ordered to preserve it except for their wives. The omitted part is indicated by the mention of blame at the end of the verse, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state. It was said that the exception to the negation of sending is understood from preservation: that is, they do not send it to anyone except for their wives. It was said that the meaning is: except for those who are guardians of their wives and maintainers of them, from their saying: So-and-so was married to so-and-so, then he died and so-and-so succeeded her. The meaning is: They guard their private parts in all circumstances except when they marry or are divorced. The phrase or what their right hands possess is in the accusative case in apposition to their wives, and what is a source, and what is meant by that are female slaves. He referred to them as what for non-rational people, because they combine femininity stemming from a deficiency in reason and the permissibility of buying and selling them like all other commodities. He treated them with these two matters in the same way as non-rational people. The phrase they are not to be blamed is an explanation of what came before, from which they are not obligated to guard their private parts.
23:7: 7- But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors. The reference is to wives and the right hand possessions, and the meaning of the transgressors is: those who go beyond what is not permissible for them, so God Almighty called whoever marries what is not permissible an 'aadi', and 'behind' here means other than and it is the object of 'sought'. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, whoever seeks what is beyond that, then the object of 'seek' is omitted, and 'behind' is a circumstance. This verse indicates the prohibition of temporary marriage, and some scholars have used it as evidence for the prohibition of masturbation because it is a form of sexual intercourse, as mentioned above. We have compiled a treatise on this subject, which we called Reaching Semen in the Ruling on Masturbation, and in it we have mentioned the evidence for prohibition and permissibility, and the preference for the more correct of the two.
23:8: 8- And those who are to their trusts and covenants attentive. The majority of scholars read their trusts in the plural. Ibn Kathir read it in the singular. A trust is what they are entrusted with, and a covenant is what they promise to do on behalf of God Almighty or on behalf of His servants. The covenant and the trust have combined everything that a person bears in matters of religion and the world. A trust is more general than a covenant, so every covenant is a trust, and the meaning of attentive is: guardians.
23:9: 9- And those who are constant in their prayers. The majority of scholars read their prayers in the plural. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read their prayers in the singular. Whoever reads in the singular means the generic noun, which has the same meaning as the plural. Constantly performing the prayer means performing it and maintaining it at its appointed times, completing its bowing, prostration, recitation, and the prescribed remembrances of it.
23:10: Then God Almighty praised these people and said: 10- Those are the inheritors, meaning they are the most deserving of being called by this name, and no one else.
23:11: Then he explained the inheritance by saying: 11- Those who inherit Paradise which is the middle of Paradise, as it was interpreted correctly from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning is: whoever acts according to what is mentioned in these verses is the inheritor who inherits that place from Paradise, and in it is a metaphor for their deserving Paradise by their deeds. It was said that the meaning is: that they inherit from the disbelievers their homes which they distributed among themselves, because God, the Almighty, created for every person a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. The word Paradise is a Roman language that was Arabized, and it was said that it is Persian, and it was said that it is Ethiopian, and it was said that it is Arabic, and the phrase they will abide therein eternally is in the accusative case as a presumed state, or it is a new sentence with no position, and the meaning of eternity is that they will remain there, they will not leave it nor will they die therein, and the feminine pronoun is used even though it refers to Paradise because it means Paradise. Abdul Razzaq, Ahmad, Abdul bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Uqaili, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab who said: “Whenever revelation was sent down to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), the sound of bees could be heard near his face. God sent it down to him one day and we waited for an hour, then he was relieved and faced the qiblah and said: O God, increase us and do not decrease us, honor us and do not humiliate us, give us and do not deprive us, prefer us and do not prefer others over us, satisfy us and be satisfied with us. Then he said: Ten verses have been sent down to me, whoever recites them will enter Paradise. Then he recited: ‘The believers have succeeded’ until he finished the ten.” In its chain of transmission is Yunus bin Salim Al-Aili. Al-Nasa’i said: We do not know anyone who narrated it on the authority of Ibn Shihab except Yunus bin Salim, and we do not know Yunus. Al-Bukhari narrated in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Yazid bin Babnous, who said: We said to Aisha: How was the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? She said: His character was the Qur’an. Then she said: Do you recite Surat Al-Mu’minun? So he recited The believers have succeeded until he reached ten. She said: This is how the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was. Sa’id bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Muhammad bin Sireen said: I was informed that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed, he would raise his eyes to the sky, so the verse, Those who are humble in their prayers was revealed. Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from him, and he added: So he ordered him to be humble, so he cast his eyes towards his mosque. Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in al-Marasil, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan also narrated it from him with the wording: When he stood up to pray, he would look this way and that, right and left, so the verse, Those who are humble in their prayers was revealed, so he bowed his head. It was narrated from him through various chains of transmission in a mursal manner like this. Al-Hakim narrated it, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan from him on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed, he would raise his eyes to the sky, so the verse, Those who are humble in their prayers was revealed, so he bowed his head. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin with the wording: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would raise their heads and eyes to the sky in prayer and turn right and left. Then God revealed, “Indeed, the believers have succeeded. Those who are humble in their prayers.” So they turned their heads and did not raise their eyes after that in prayer, nor did they turn right and left. And Ibn al-Mubarak narrated in Az-Zuhd, Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abu Hatim, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ali that he was asked about the statement: Those who are humble in their prayers, he said: Humility is in the heart and that you soften your shoulder for the Muslim man, and that you do not turn around in your prayer. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Those who are humble in their prayers, he said: Fearful and calm. There are well-known hadiths in the books of hadith that indicate the permissibility of humility in prayer and the prohibition of turning around and raising the eyes to the sky. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And those who turn away from ill speech, he said: Falsehood. Abd Al-Razzaq and Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh on the authority of Al-Qasim Ibn Muhammad that he was asked about Mut’ah and he said: I see that it is forbidden in the Qur’an, then he recited: And those who guard their private parts * Except from their wives or those their right hands possess. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that it was said to him: God mentions prayer frequently in the Qur’an: Those who are constant in their prayers. “And those who maintain their prayers.” He said: That is at their appointed times. They said: We did not see that except as abandoning them. He said: Abandoning them is disbelief. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Abu Hurairah regarding his statement: Those are the inheritors. He said: They will inherit their dwellings and the dwellings of their brothers that were prepared for them if they had obeyed God. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Baath on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is none among you but that he has two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in Hell. When he dies and enters Hell, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling. That is what God says: “Those are the inheritors.” And Abd bin Hamid and Al-Tirmidhi narrated, and he said: It is good and authentic and strange, on the authority of Anas, who mentioned a story in which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Al-Firdaws is the highest part of Paradise, its middle and its best part. And what indicates this inheritance mentioned here is the words of God Almighty: That is Paradise which We give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were righteous, and His words: That is Paradise which you have inherited for what you used to do. And what supports this hadith of Abu Hurayrah is what is in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Musa on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, some Muslims will come with sins as great as mountains, and God will forgive them and some of them will be for the Jews and Christians. And in another version of his, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will hand over to every Muslim a Jew or a Christian, and he will say: This is your release from the Fire.”
23:12: When God Almighty urged His servants to worship and promised them Paradise for doing so, He returned to stating the duration and the resurrection so that this could be established in the souls of those who are accountable, so He said: 12- And We have certainly created man to the end, and the lam is the answer to an omitted oath, and the sentence is a subject, and it was said that it is conjoined with what preceded it, and what is meant by man is the species because they were created within the creation of their father Adam, and it was said that what is meant by it is Adam. And the lineage is effective from the extraction of something from something, it is said that the hair was extracted from the dough, and the sword from its sheath was pulled, so the sperm is a lineage, and the child is a descendant, and a lineage also, and from it the saying of the poet: Then he came with a fierce lion, a strong and powerful beast, who was not immune. And the other said: Is Hind anything but an Arabian mare, a purebred stallion, who was sired by a mule? The word min in min sala is an introductory particle related to our creation, and in min tīn it is an explanatory particle related to something omitted, which is an attribute of salalah: meaning being from clay. The meaning is that He, glory be to Him, created the essence of man first from clay, because the origin is Adam, who is from pure clay, and his children are from clay and semen. It was said that salalah means that if you squeeze clay, it slips out from between your fingers, so what comes out is the salalah, as Al-Kalbi said.
23:13: 13- Then We made him meaning the race in terms of its individuals who are the children of Adam, or We made his offspring by deleting an added word if what is meant by man is Adam, a drop of semen. The explanation of the drop of semen has already been presented in Surat Al-Hajj, as well as the explanation of the clot and the lump of flesh. What is meant by the firm settlement is the womb, and it is expressed by the settlement which is a source of exaggeration.
23:14: The meaning of 14- Then We created the sperm-drop into a clot means that He, the Almighty, transformed the white sperm into a red clot. Then We created the clot into a lump of flesh meaning an unformed piece of flesh. Then We created the lump of flesh into bones meaning that God, the Almighty, made it solid to be a pillar of the body in specific shapes. Then We clothed the bones with flesh meaning that God, the Almighty, caused flesh to grow on every bone in the amount that was appropriate and suitable for it. Then We produced it as another creation meaning that We breathed life into it after it was inanimate. It was said that We brought it out into the world. It was said that it was the growth of hair, and it was said that the teeth came out, and it was said that it was the completion of the powers created in it. There is no objection to intending all of them, and bringing then to complete the difference between the two creations. So blessed be God, the best of creators meaning that He deserved glorification and praise. It was said that it is taken from barakah, meaning that his goodness and blessings increased. And creation in the language means estimation. It is said that you created the leather, meaning you measured it to cut something from it. So the meaning of the best of creators is the most perfect of the estimating craftsmen. And from this is the saying of the poet: Because you create what you have created, and some people create and then do not create.
23:15: 15- Then after that you will surely die. The reference in His saying: that is to the previous matters: meaning, then after those matters you will surely die, destined for death inevitably.
23:16: 16- Then on the Day of Resurrection you will be resurrected from your graves to the place of assembly for reckoning and punishment.
23:17: And the lam in 17- And We have certainly created above you seven paths is an answer to an omitted oath, and the sentence is a subject including a statement of the creation of what they need after the statement of their creation, and the paths are the heavens. Al-Khalili, Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said, and they were called paths because some of them were knocked on top of others like the knocking of a sandal. Abu Ubaidah said: To knock on something means to make some of it above others, and the Arabs call everything above something a path. It was said because they are the paths of the angels, and it was said because they are the paths of the planets. And We were not unaware of creation What is meant by creation here is the created: that is, We were not unaware of these full paths and their preservation from falling on the earth. Most of the commentators said: What is meant is that all of creation is heedless. Rather, We have preserved the heavens from falling, and We have preserved those on the earth from the heaven falling upon them and destroying them, or the earth shaking with them, or they perishing due to one of the causes that eradicate them. It is possible that what is meant is the negation of heedlessness in taking care of their interests and what they live on, and the negation of heedlessness in preserving them.
23:18: 18- And We sent down water from the sky This is among the blessings that God the Almighty has bestowed upon His creation. What is meant by water is rainwater, for it provides life for the earth and its animals. Among that is the water of rivers descending from the sky, springs, and wells extracted from the earth, for their origin is the water of the sky. It has been said that God the Almighty meant in this verse the four rivers: Seyhan, Ceyhan, Euphrates, and the Nile, but there is no basis for this specification. It was said that what is meant by it is fresh water, and there is no basis for that either, as there is no water on earth except that it comes from the sky. The meaning of in measure is by Our estimation or in a quantity that is sufficient for the crops and fruits, because if it were to be abundant, it would lead to their destruction. Similar to this is the saying of the Most High: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in a known measure. The meaning of So We settled it in the earth is that We made it stable in it so that they may benefit from it when they need it, like the water that remains in swamps and ponds and the like. And indeed, We are Able to take it away, meaning just as We were able to send it down, we are able to take it away in some way. This indefiniteness has a good position that is not hidden, and in this is a severe threat because of what it indicates of His ability, the Most High, to take it away and submerge it until people perish with thirst and their livestock perish. Similar to this is His saying: “Say, Have you considered: if your water were to become sunken, then who could bring you flowing water?”
23:19: Then the Almighty explained what results from sending down water, saying: 19- And We produced for you thereby gardens of palm trees and grapevines meaning, We created with that water gardens of the two types mentioned for you therein meaning in these gardens are many fruits that you enjoy and covet. It was said that the meaning is: And from these gardens are aspects of your provisions and livelihood, like his saying: So-and-so eats from such-and-such craft, and this is far-fetched. The Almighty limited it to palm trees and grapevines, because they are found in Taif and Madinah and what is connected to that. This is what Ibn Jarir said. It was said that they are the most noble of trees in terms of fruit and the most delicious in terms of benefit, taste and pleasure. It was said that the meaning of his saying: for you therein are fruits is that you have fruits in these gardens other than date palms and palm trees. It was said that the meaning is that you have fruits in these two types in particular, because they have different types that vary in taste and color. Scholars of jurisprudence have differed greatly about what the term fruit refers to. The best that has been said is that it refers to fruits that people eat, but are not their sustenance, food, or condiment. There has been a difference of opinion about whether legumes are included as fruit or not.
23:20: And the tree is in the accusative case in apposition to gardens, and Al-Farra' permitted the nominative case on the assumption: And there is a tree, so it is raised as a subject and its predicate is omitted and assumed before it, which is the mentioned circumstance. Al-Wahidi said: And all the commentators say: What is meant by this tree is the olive tree, and it was specifically mentioned because no one tends to water it, and it is the one from which oil comes out, so God Almighty mentioned it as a favor from Him to His servants with it, and because it is the most honorable of trees and the most beneficial and the most blessed, then God Almighty described this tree as 20- coming out of Mount Sinai which is a mountain in Jerusalem, and Mount is the mountain in the speech of the Arabs, and it was said that it is the blessed, and the majority went to that it is the name of the mountain as you say Mount Uhud. And it was said that Sinai is a specific stone to which the mountain was added because it is near it, and it was said that it is every mountain that bears fruits. The Kufians read Sinai with a fatha on the seen, while the rest read it with a kasra on the seen. It was not declined because it was made a name for the area, and Al-Akhfash claimed that it was foreign. The majority read tanbat bi-dahn with a fatha on the second letter and a damma on the unified ba. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a damma on the second letter and a kasra on the unified ba. The meaning according to the first reading is that it grows in itself covered with oil. According to the second reading, the ba means with, so it is for companionship. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: The meaning is: its wing grows and with it the oil. It was said that the ba is redundant. Abu Ubaidah said this, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: They are free women, not red-eyed, black-eyed women who do not recite the Surahs. Another said: We strike with the sword and hope for relief Al-Farra and Al-Zajjaj said: Nabt and Anbat have the same meaning. Al-Asma’i denies Anbat, and Zuhair’s statement is refuted by him: I saw the needy people around their homes, and I brought them some cotton, until I brought the vegetables. Any plant. Az-Zuhri, Al-Hasan and Al-A'raj read it as Tanbat with a damma on the second letter and a fatha on the first letter. Az-Zajjaj and Ibn Jinni said: That it grows and with it oil. Ibn Mas'ud read it comes out with oil. Zur ibn Hubaysh read Tanbat Al-Dahn without the preposition. Sulayman ibn Abd Al-Malik and Al-Ashhab read it as Dahan and and a dye for the eaters in apposition to Al-Dahn: meaning it grows with something that combines being an oil that is applied as a smear and a dye that is used as a condiment. The majority read it as Sabgh and some people read Sabbagh like Labsa and Lubsa. Every condiment that is used as a condiment is a dye and a sabbagh. The root of dye is that with which a garment is colored, and the condiment is likened to it because bread is dyed with a condiment like that which is dyed with it.
23:21: 21- And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you. This is one of the blessings that God has bestowed upon them. The interpretation of livestock has already been mentioned in Surat An-Nahl. Al-Naysaburi said in his interpretation: Perhaps what is meant by livestock here is camels in particular because they are usually carried on them, and because He linked them to the ark, which is the ships of the land, just as the ark is the ships of the sea. And the Almighty explained that they are a lesson, because they are among the things that indicate the greatness of the Divine power through their creation and actions. Then the Almighty detailed what is in these livestock of blessings after what He mentioned of the lesson in them for the servants, saying: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies. He, the Almighty, means: the milk that forms in their bellies and flows into their udders, for in the formation of what they eat of fodder and its transformation into this delicious food and precious drink is the greatest lesson for those who reflect, and the greatest admonition for those who are admonished. Nasiqikum was read with a nun to indicate that the agent is God Almighty, and it was read with a ta above it to indicate that the agent is the livestock. Then he mentioned the benefits in them in general, saying: And for you therein are many benefits, meaning in their backs, milk, offspring, wool, and hair. Then he mentioned a specific benefit, saying: And from them you eat, because there is great benefit for them in eating.
23:22: He also mentioned riding on them because of the great benefit in it, so He said: And on them and on the ships you are carried meaning on the livestock. If what is meant by livestock is camels, cows and sheep, then what is meant is on some livestock, namely camels in particular. If what is meant by livestock is camels in particular, then the meaning is clear. Then since livestock are what is mostly ridden on land, He added to them what is ridden on the sea, so He said: And on the ships you are carried to complete the blessing and perfect the favor. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The lineage is the thin, clear water from which the child is formed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: When the sperm falls into the womb, it flies in the hair and nails and remains for forty days, then descends into the womb and becomes a clot. The followers have different interpretations of the lineage, which we have already referred to. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then We produced him as another creation, he said: hair and teeth. Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, Then We produced him as another creation, he said: breathed the soul into him. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Rabi’ said on the authority of Anas, Al-Suddi, Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Then We produced him as another creation, he said: when youth reached maturity. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Salih Abu Al-Khalil who said: When this verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, up to His saying: Then We produced him as another creation, Umar said: So blessed be God, the best of creators. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it has been sealed with what you have spoken, O Umar. Al-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Anas who said: Umar said: I agreed with my Lord in four matters. I said: O Messenger of God, what if we prayed behind the Maqam? Then God revealed, And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. I said, O Messenger of God, if you were to take a veil over your wives, then the righteous and the wicked would enter upon you. Then God revealed, And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition. I said to the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Either you stop or God will substitute for you wives better than you. Then, Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, was revealed. Then, And We have certainly created man from a lineage, until His saying, Then We developed him into another creation, was revealed. Then I said, So blessed is God, the best of creators. Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit that he said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dictated this verse, “And We have certainly created man,” until His saying, Another creation, and Muadh ibn Jabal said, So blessed is God, the best of creators. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed. Muadh said to him, Why are you laughing, O Messenger of God? He said: With it I concluded, So blessed be God, the best of creators. In its chain of transmission is Jabir al-Ju’fi, who is very weak. Ibn Kathir said: In this report of his is a great oddity, because this surah is Meccan, and Zayd ibn Thabit only wrote the revelation in Medina, and likewise the conversion to Islam of Muadh ibn Jabal only took place in Medina, and God knows best. Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib narrated, al-Suyuti said, with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God sent down five rivers from Paradise to Earth. The Sihon, which is the river of India, and the Jihon, which is the river of Balkh, and the Tigris and Euphrates, which are the rivers of Iraq, and the Nile, which is the river of Egypt, He sent it down from one spring of the springs of Paradise from the lowest degree of its degrees on the wings of Gabriel, so He deposited it in the mountains and made it flow in the earth, and made it beneficial for people in the idols of their livelihood, so that is His saying: And We sent down from the sky water in measure and settled it in the earth. So when Gog and Magog came out, God sent Gabriel, and he lifted from the earth the Qur'an and knowledge, and the stone from the corner of the House, and the station of Abraham, and the Ark of Moses with what was in it, and these five rivers, and he lifted all of that to the sky, so that is His saying: And indeed, We are Able to take it away. So when these things were lifted from the earth, its people would have the best of this world and the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Mount Sinai is the mountain from which Moses was called. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding His saying: It produces oil, he said: It is oil that is eaten and used as a anointing.
23:23: When God Almighty mentioned the ark, He followed it with the mention of Noah, because he was the first to make it, and He mentioned what Noah’s people did with him because of their neglect to contemplate God Almighty’s creations and remember His blessings upon them, so He said: 23- And We sent Noah to his people. In that is a consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a consolation for him by explaining that other people of the prophets did with their prophets what his people did with him, and the lam is the answer to an omitted oath. So he said, ‘O my people, worship God,’ meaning worship Him alone and do not associate anything with Him, as is understood from the other verses. The phrase You have no god other than Him is in the position of explaining what preceded it, and the elevation of other than Him because it is a description of a god in the place, because it is a subject whose predicate is for you, meaning you have no god in existence other than Him, glory be to Him. It was read in the accusative case in consideration of the word god. Do you not then fear? meaning do you not fear that you will abandon the worship of Your Lord, the only One worthy of worship, and you have no god but Him. It was said that the meaning is: Will you not protect yourselves from His punishment that your sins require?
23:24: 24- Then the leaders of his people who disbelieved said meaning the leaders of his people who disbelieved in him said This is only a human being like you meaning of your kind in humanity, there is no difference between you and him Wanting to dominate you meaning he seeks superiority over you by dominating you so that you would be his followers and obedient to his command, then they stated that humans cannot be messengers and said: And if God had willed, He would have sent down angels meaning if God had willed to send a messenger, He would have sent angels, and He only used the word sending down to mean sending because sending them to the servants necessitates their descent to them We have not heard of this among our forefathers meaning a claim like this claimant to prophethood from among humans, or a statement like his, which is the command to worship God alone, or we have not heard of a human being making this claim among our forefathers: meaning among the nations that came before this. It was said that the ba in this is redundant: meaning we have not heard this being in the past, they said this relying on tradition and holding fast to its rope.
23:25: And they were not satisfied with that until they added to it a pure lie and blatant slander, so they said: 25- He is only a man possessed by madness meaning madness who does not know what he is saying: So wait for him for a time meaning wait for him until his matter becomes clear, that is, he recovers from his madness and abandons this claim, or until he dies and you are relieved of him. Al-Farra' said: He does not mean by a time here a specific time, rather it is like their saying: Leave him until a certain day. So when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, heard their words and knew their persistence in disbelief and their insistence on it.
23:26: 26- He said, ‘My Lord, support me’ against them, so take revenge on them as You wish and however You wish. The ba in because they denied is for causality: that is, because of their denial of me.
23:27: 27- So We inspired him at that time, meaning We sent to him a messenger from heaven, to build the ark and that it is an explanation of what is in the inspiration of the meaning of saying under Our eyes meaning clothed in Our protection and care, and this was explained previously in Hud. The meaning of and Our inspiration is Our command to you and Our teaching of you how to build it, and the fa in His statement: So when Our command comes is to arrange what comes after it according to what came before it of building the ark, and what is meant by the command is the torment and the oven overflows is conjoined to the sentence before it by a conjunction of sequence, and it was said that the conjunction of al-Sharh 94:meaning that the coming of the command is the overflow of the oven: meaning the oven of Adam that will go to Nuh 71:meaning when that happens, then enter therein from every kind two meaning enter it, it is said that he entered it in such-and-such, and I entered it. Hafs read min kul with tanween, and the rest read with addition. The meaning of the first reading is min kulli from every nation is two pairs, and the meaning of the second is min kulli from every pair, and they are the nation of males and females, two. Ahlak was replaced by a verb conjoined with fasalak so follow, not by conjoining zawwain two pairs, or ithnayyin two people according to the two readings, in order to convey a difference in meaning: that is, and follow your people “except for those against whom the word has already passed among them” meaning the word of their destruction among them and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged by praying for their salvation. The phrase indeed, they are drowned is an explanation for the prohibition of addressing: that is, they are destined to be drowned for their wrongdoing, and whoever is like this does not deserve to be prayed for.
23:28: 28- So when you have ascended that is, ascended you and those with you of your family and followers on the ship riding on it "then say: Praise be to God, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people" that is, He came between us and them, and delivered us from them, as He said: "So He cut off the root of the people who did wrong. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." The explanation of this story has already been presented in Surat Hud in full and complete, and He only made their ascension on the ship a means of salvation from drowning, for He knew beforehand that this was the reason for their salvation from the oppressors, and their safety from being afflicted with the punishment that afflicted them.
23:29: Then he ordered him to ask his Lord what is most beneficial and most useful for him, so he said: 29- And say, 'My Lord, alight me at a blessed landing place.' That is, alight me in the ship. The majority read a landing place with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the zay as a verbal noun. Zur ibn Hubaish and Abu Bakr from Asim and al-Mufaddal read with a fatha on the meem and a kasra on the zay as a place name. According to the first reading: anzalni inzal mubarak a blessed landing, and according to the second reading: anzalni makan mubarak a blessed landing. Al-Jawhari said: A landing place with a fatha on the meem and zay is the descent, which is the settlement. You say, I descended a descent and a place. The poet said: If the house reminds you of its home, you will cry, and the tears will flow down your cheeks. By erecting her home, because it is a source, it was said that God Almighty commanded him to say this statement when he entered the ship, and it was said when he exited it, and the verse is a teaching from God to His servants when they board and then disembark to say this statement And You are the best of those who provide a place to stay. This is praise from Him to God Almighty after his supplication to Him. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: He was commanded to say when he was seated on the ship: Praise be to God, and when he disembarked from it: My Lord, let me alight at a blessed place.
23:30: And the reference in His saying: 30- Indeed in that to what came before of what God told us about the matter of Noah, peace be upon him: and the verses are the indications of the perfection of His power, glory be to Him, and the signs by which the greatness of His status is proven. And indeed We were to test meaning to test them by sending messengers to them, to show the obedient and the disobedient to the people or the angels. And it was said that the meaning is: He, glory be to Him, treats them as one who tests their conditions, sometimes by sending, and sometimes by punishing.
23:31: 31- Then We produced after them another generation meaning after their destruction. Most of the commentators said: Those whom God produced after them were the people of Aad, the people of Hud, because their story came after the story of Noah in a place other than this, and because of His saying in Al-A'raf And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and it was said that they were Thamud because they were the ones who were destroyed by the blast. And God the Almighty said in this story So the blast seized them and it was said that they were the people of Madyan, the people of Shu'ayb because they were among those who were destroyed by the blast.
23:32: 32- So We sent among them a Messenger. The verb of sending is transitive with yafi, although it is transitive with ila, to indicate that this Messenger sent to them grew up among them, and they knew his place and birth, so that their repose in what he said would be more than their repose in what someone came to them from a place other than theirs. It was said that the reason for the transitive nature of the aforementioned verb with fi is that it included the meaning of saying: that is, We said to them on the tongue of the Messenger, Worship God. This is why the explanatory an was brought. The first is more appropriate, as we included in sent the meaning of said, which does not necessitate its transitivity with fi. The phrase you have no god other than Him is an explanation of the command to worship. Will you not then fear His punishment, which your polytheism requires.
23:33: 33- And the chiefs of his people said meaning their nobles and leaders. Then he described the chiefs as disbelievers and deniers, saying: Those who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter meaning they denied what is in the Hereafter of reckoning and punishment, or they denied the resurrection and We provided them with luxury meaning We made the worldly blessings abundant for them, so they became arrogant because of what they had become in the life of this world of abundant wealth and comfortable living This is only a human being like you meaning the chiefs said this to their people, describing him as being equal to them in humanity, and in eating from what you eat and drinking from what you drink, and this necessitates for them that he has no superiority over them. Al-Farra' said: The meaning of and drinks from what you drink is omitted from it: meaning from what you drink, and it was said that ma is a source, so it does not need a reference.
23:34: 34- And if you obey human beings like yourselves, in what was mentioned of the descriptions, then you will be losers, meaning you will be deceived by abandoning your gods and following him without any favor from him over you.
23:35: The question in his saying: 35- Does He promise you that when you die? is for denial, and the sentence is a resumption confirming what came before it of the ugliness of their following Him. It was read with a kasra on the meem from matam, from mata yamāt like khafā yakhāf. It was read with a damma from mata yamūt: like qāla yaqūl And you were dust and bones meaning some of your parts were dust, and some of them were rotten bones with no flesh in them or nerves on them. It was said that the dust was brought forward because it is further from their minds. It was said that the meaning is: your predecessors were dust, and your successors were bones that you will be brought out meaning from your graves alive as you were. Sibawayh said: The first is in the accusative case due to the occurrence of ayyadkum on it, and the second is a substitute for it. Al-Farra', Al-Jarmi and Al-Mubarrad said: The second an is repeated for emphasis, and its repetition is good due to the length of the speech, and Al-Zajjaj said something similar. Al-Akhfash said: The second is in the nominative case with an implied verb: meaning your expulsion will occur, just as you say: Today the fighting will occur. So the meaning is: Today the fighting will occur.
23:36: 36- Hihat Hihat lmaa ta'wa'idun meaning after what you are promised, or far from what you are promised, and the repetition is for emphasis. Ibn al-Anbari said: And in Hihat there are ten languages and then he listed them, and they are explained in the science of grammar. And some of them were read, and the lam in lmaa ta'wa'idun is to clarify the excluded as in his saying: Hait lak as if it was said why this exclusion? So it was said lmaa ta'wa'idun. The meaning is: after you bring out the promise that you are promised, this is on the basis that Hihat is a verb. Al-Zajjaj said: It is in the estimation of the source: meaning far from what you are promised, or far from what you are promised according to a reading with a nun, so it is on this basis a subject whose predicate is lmaa ta'wa'idun.
23:37: Then the Almighty explained their extravagance, as they said: 37- It is only our worldly life, meaning that life is nothing but our worldly life, not the afterlife that you promise us, and the phrase we die and we live explains what they claimed of limiting their lives to the life of this world.
23:38: Then they explicitly denied the resurrection, and that the promise of it from him was a fabrication against God, so they said: 38- “And we will not be resurrected. He is only a man who has fabricated a lie against God.” That is, he is only fabricating a lie against God in what he claims. And we will not believe him. That is, we will not believe what he says.
23:39: 39- He said, ‘My Lord, support me.’ That is, their prophet said when he knew that they would not believe him at all: My Lord, support me against them and take revenge for me from them because they denied me.
23:40: 40- He said, 'In a little while they will surely become regretful.' That is, God Almighty said, answering his prayer and promising him acceptance of what he prayed for: In a little while they will surely become regretful for what they did of denial, stubbornness, and persistence in disbelief. What is in in a little while is an additional word between the preposition and the noun to emphasize the shortness of time, as in His statement: Then by the mercy of God.
23:41: Then the Almighty informed us that it was 41- the blast seized them and His punishment overtook them and His wrath descended upon them. The commentators said: Gabriel shouted at them with one shout along with the wind with which God destroyed them, so they all died. It was said that the blast is the same punishment that descended upon them, and from this the poet said: Time shouted at the Barmak family with a shout that caused them to fall on their chins because of its intensity. The letter ba in bi-haqq is related to taking. Then the Almighty informed us about what they became after the punishment that descended upon them. He said: So We made them scum. That is, like the scum that a flood carries. Scum is what a flood carries of decayed trees, grass, reeds, and the like that it carries on the surface of the water. The meaning is: He made them perish, so they dried up as scum dries up. So away with the wrongdoing people. The word ba’dan is in the accusative case as a source, and it is one of the sources whose verb is not mentioned with it, that is, they went away, far away. The lam is to clarify who was told that. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: So walk therein, meaning: take with you on the ship of every kind two. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, “And say: My Lord, alight me at a blessed landing place,” he said to Noah when he was disembarked from the ship. These narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, he said: He teaches you, glory be to Him, what to say when you embark, and what to say when you disembark. As for embarking, then: “Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return,” and: “In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful,” and upon disembarking, My Lord, alight me at a blessed landing place, and You are the best to give a landing place. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement: A generation, he said: A nation. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Far, far, he said: Far, far away. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: So We made them scum, he said: They were made like a dead, decaying tree.
23:42: And His statement: 42- Then We produced after them meaning after their destruction other generations It was said that they were the people of Salih, Lot, and Shuaib, as their story was mentioned in this order in Al-A’raf and Hud, and it was said that they were the Children of Israel. And generations are nations, and perhaps the reason for the plural here for generations and the singular in what came before shortly is that He meant here multiple and there one nation.
23:43: Then the Almighty explained the perfection of His knowledge and power regarding His servants, saying: 43- No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it. That is, no group of people together in a century can precede their destined terms of destruction, nor can they delay it. Similar to that is the Almighty’s saying: So when their term comes, they will not delay an hour, nor will they advance it.
23:44: Then the Almighty explained that His messengers were successive after these centuries, and that the affair of their nations was one in denying them, so He said: 44- Then We sent Our messengers in succession. The sentence is connected to the sentence before it, meaning that the sending of each messenger was later than the establishment of the century to which he was sent, not in the sense that the sending of all the messengers was later than the establishment of all those centuries. The meaning of successively is successively one after the other and they follow each other, from witr, which means individual. Al-Asma'i said: I sent my books to him in succession: I followed one another, except that there was a period of time between each one of them and the next. Another said: successive is consecutive without a period. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amr read successively with tanween as a source. Al-Nahhas said: According to this, it is permissible to say successively with a kasra on the first ta'. Because the meaning of Then We sent is: We sent in succession. It is possible that it is in the position of a state: that is, successively. Whenever there came to a nation their messenger, they denied him. This sentence is a resumption explaining the coming of each messenger to his nation, on the condition that what is meant by coming is to convey. So We made some of them follow others that is, in the destruction by the torment that befell them. And We made them stories. Stories is the plural of hadith, which is what people talk about, like wonders is the plural of ajjubah, which is what people marvel at. Al-Akhfash said: It is only said that We made them stories in evil and not in good, as it is said that someone became a story: that is, a lesson, and as the Almighty said in another verse: So We made them stories and tore them apart, all of them. I said: This generality is not accepted, as it may be said that someone became a good story, and from this is the saying of Ibn Duraid in his book Al-Maqsura: A person is only a story after his death, so be a good story for the one who narrated it. So away with a people who do not believe. He described them here as not believing, and previously as being unjust, because each of the two descriptions came from each of the two groups, or because these people did nothing but disbelief, and those people added to it those heinous statements that are among the most severe and horrific forms of injustice.
23:45: Then the Almighty narrated what happened with Pharaoh and his people when He sent Moses and Aaron to them, saying: 45- Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs are the nine previously mentioned more than once, and it is not correct to count the splitting of the sea among them here. Because what is meant are the signs that they denied and were arrogant about. What is meant by the clear authority is the clear and evident proof. It was said that they are the nine signs themselves, and the conjunction is from the category of. To the venerable king and son of the hero It was said that he meant the staff because it is the mother of signs, so it is a case of Gabriel’s connection to the angels. It was said that what is meant by the signs is what they had, and by the authority is the clear evidence: the nine signs.
23:46: And what is meant by the chiefs in His statement: 46- To Pharaoh and his chiefs are the nobles among them, as was previously explained more than once. But they were arrogant meaning they sought arrogance and assumed it, so they did not submit to the truth. And they were a haughty people oppressing the people through oppression and injustice, looking down on them, haughty with arrogance, stubbornness, and rebellion.
23:47: And sentence 47- And they said, 'Shall we believe in two human beings like us?' is connected to the sentence they were arrogant. What is between them is an interjection, and the question is for denial: that is, how can we believe in someone who is like us in humanity? Humans are used for the singular, as in His saying: A normal human being, and they are also used for the plural, as in His saying: If you see from among mankind one, so its dual here is in consideration of the first meaning, and the example is singular because it is in the ruling of the source, and the meaning of and their people are worshippers of us is that they are obedient to them and submit to what they command them to do, like the submission of slaves. Al-Mubarrad said: The worshipper is the obedient, the submissive. Abu Ubaidah said: The Arabs call everyone who submits to a king a worshipper of him, and it was said that it is possible that he claimed divinity, so he called the people to worship him and they obeyed him, and the lam in us is related to worshippers, it was brought before it to take care of the pauses, and the sentence is a circumstantial.
23:48: 48- So they denied them meaning they insisted on denying them and were among those destroyed by drowning in the sea.
23:49: Then the Almighty narrated what happened to the people of Moses after the destruction of their enemy, saying: 49- And We certainly gave Moses the Book meaning the Torah, and Moses was specifically mentioned because the Torah was revealed to him on Mount Tur, and Aaron was his successor among his people so that they may be guided meaning that perhaps the people of Moses would be guided by it to the truth, and act according to what is in it of laws, so the Almighty made giving it to Moses a giving to his people, because even though it was revealed to Moses, it was for the guidance of his people. It was said that there is an omitted complement and the complement to it was established in its place: meaning that We gave the people of Moses the Book. It was said that the pronoun in so that they may refers to Pharaoh and his people, and this is an error because Moses was not given the Torah until after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, as the Almighty said: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations.
23:50: Then the Almighty referred to the story of Jesus in general, saying: 50- And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign meaning a sign indicating the greatness of Our power and the wonder of Our creation. We have already discussed this at the end of Surat Al-Anbiya in the interpretation of His Almighty's saying: And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds and the meaning of His saying: And We sheltered them on a high ground to a high place: meaning We made them take refuge there. It was said that it is the land of Damascus, and Abdullah bin Salam, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Muqatil said the same. It was also said that it is Jerusalem, said Qatadah and Kaab, and it was also said that it is the land of Palestine, said Al-Suddi. With a place of settlement meaning that it has a place where its inhabitants settle. And a spring meaning a spring of water. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the running water in the springs, so the mim in this case is an extra letter like its extra letter in manba', and it was said that it is fa'il with the meaning of maf'ul. Ali bin Sulayman Al-Akhfash said that the meaning of water is when it flows, then it is a spring and a flowing water. Ibn Al-A'rabi said the same. It was said that it is taken from the word ma’un, which means benefit, and Al-Farra’ said the same as Al-Zajjaj said.
23:51: 51- O messengers, eat from the good things. Al-Zajjaj said: This address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the plural indicates that all the messengers were commanded thus. It was said that this statement was addressed to every prophet, because this was their way of being, which they should follow, so the meaning is: And We said, O messengers, addressing each one individually due to the difference in their times. Ibn Jarir said: The address was to Jesus. Al-Farraa said: It is like saying to one man, Stop from us. The good things are what is desirable and enjoyable, and it was said that they are the permissible, and it was said that they are what combines the two mentioned descriptions. Then after He commanded them to eat from the good things, He commanded them to do righteous deeds, saying: And do righteous deeds, meaning righteous deeds, which are those that are in accordance with the Shari'ah. Then He explained this command by saying: Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do, nothing of it is hidden from Me, and I will reward you according to your deeds, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.
23:52: 52- And this nation of yours is one nation. This is among the things that the prophets were addressed with, and the meaning is: This is your religion and your law, O messengers, one religion, and a unified law united by a principle that is the greatest thing with which God sent His prophets and revealed His books, which is the call of all the prophets to worship God with no partner. It was said that the meaning is: This that was mentioned above is your religion and your nation, so adhere to it, on the basis that what is meant by the nation here is religion, as in His statement: Indeed, we found our fathers upon a nation. And from this is the statement of Al-Nabigha: I swore and left no doubt for you. Can a slave be held accountable while he is obedient? It was read with a kasra on the resumption of what preceded it, and it was read with a fatha and a shaddah. Al-Khalil said: It is in the accusative case because the preposition has not yet been applied: meaning, I know that this is your religion that I have commanded you to believe in. Al-Farra’ said: In is related to an implied verb, and its meaning is: And know that this is your nation. Sibawayh said: It is related to fear God, and the meaning is: fear God because your nation is one nation, and the fa in fear God is to arrange the command to fear God on what preceded it from His being your Lord who is special in lordship: meaning, do not do what would necessitate punishment from Me by associating others with Me, or disobeying what I have commanded you to do or forbidden you from doing.
23:53: Then the Almighty mentioned what happened from the nations of their disobedience to what the messengers commanded them to do, so He said: 53- So they divided their affair among themselves into sects. The fa is to arrange their disobedience to what preceded from the command to be pious, and the pronoun refers to what the word nation indicates, and the meaning is: that they made their religion, despite its unity, into separate, different pieces. Al-Mubarrad said: Zabran means sects and different pieces, the singular of which is Zabur, which is the group and sect, and the same is the case with zubra and its plural is zubar, so the Almighty described the nations as having differed, so a group followed the Torah, a group followed the Zabur, and a group followed the Gospel, then they distorted and changed, and a group of polytheists followed what their fathers had prescribed for them of misguidance: Zabran is read with a damma on the ba', the plural of Zabur, and it is read with a fatha: meaning pieces like pieces of iron. Every party rejoices in what they have meaning every group of these different ones rejoices in what they have: meaning in what they have of religion: meaning they are pleased with it.
23:54: 54- So leave them in their ignorance for a time meaning leave them in their ignorance, for they are not worthy of guidance, and do not be distressed by delaying the punishment for them, for everything has its time. The Almighty likened their state of ignorance to water that immerses whoever enters it. The immersion is originally what immerses you and rises above you, and its origin is covering, and the immersion is a lot of water because it covers the earth, and the burden of the cloak is what includes people with gifts, and hatred is called the immersion, and what is meant here is: confusion, heedlessness and misguidance, and the verse is out of the context of threatening them, not of ordering him, may God bless him and grant him peace, to refrain from them, and the meaning of until a time is until the time of their punishment by killing comes, or until they die in disbelief and are punished in the Fire.
23:55: 55- Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children? That is, do they think that what We give them in this world of wealth and children?
23:56: 56- Nasara'i with it for them in what is good for them and honors them, and the hamza is for denial, and the answer to this is understood and indicated by his saying: Rather, they do not perceive because it is a conjunction to an understood word to which the speech extends: meaning, no, we do not do that, rather they do not perceive anything at all like the animals that do not understand or reason, for what We have granted them of blessings and what We have extended to them of good things is only a lure for them to increase in sin as the Almighty said: We only grant them respite so that they may increase in sin. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that We hasten with it for them in good things, so it was deleted with it, and what in anma is a relative pronoun, and the link is this deleted one. Al-Kisa'i said: Anma here is one letter so it does not need to estimate a link. It was said that it is permissible to stop at Banin, and it was said that it is not good because yahsabun needs two objects, so the two objects are complete in good things. Ibn Al-Anbari said: This is a mistake because ma is a plural. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra read yasara’a with a ya underneath, on the basis that its subject is what is indicated by amdadna, which is the supply. It is also possible that the meaning is: God hastens to them. The rest read nasara’a with a nun. Al-Tha’labi said: This reading is the correct one, because of his saying namdhum. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then We sent Our messengers in succession, he said: One after the other. In another version he said: One after the other. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, he said: She gave birth to him without a father. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ Ibn Anas: A sign, he said: A lesson. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We settled them on a high ground, he said: A level hill. Al-Ma’in is the flowing water, and it is the river about which God said: Your Lord has provided beneath you a stream. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: And We settled them on a high ground, he said: It is the elevated place on the earth, and it is the best place for plants to grow, of stability, of fertility, and Al-Ma’in is the apparent water. Wakee’, Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Tamam Al-Razi and Ibn Asakir narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: to a hill, he said: We were informed that it is Damascus. Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it likewise on his authority. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this, but its chain of transmission is weak. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Murrah Al-Nahzi: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The hill is the sand. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim in Al-Kuna, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: It is the sand in Palestine. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from his hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this. Al-Tabarani, Ibn Al-Sakn, Ibn Mandah, Abu Nu’aym, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Aqra’ bin Shafi Al-Akki, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similar to this. Ahmad, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O people, God is good and accepts only that which is good. God has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, saying: ‘O messengers, eat from the good things and work righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing.’ Or he said: ‘O you who believe, eat from the good things which We have provided for you.’ Then he mentioned a man who travels a long way, disheveled and dusty, whose food is unlawful, whose drink is unlawful, whose clothing is unlawful, and who is nourished with unlawful things, and he stretches out his hands to the sky, saying: ‘O Lord, O Lord.’ How can that be answered?” Sa’id ibn Mansur narrated on the authority of Hafs al-Fazari, regarding his statement: ‘O messengers, eat from the good things,’ he said: That is Jesus, son of Mary, eating from his mother’s spinning. Abdun narrated it in the Companions on the authority of Hafs, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and it is mursal because Hafs was a Tabi’i.
23:57: When He, the Almighty, denied the true goodness of the infidels who live in luxury, He followed that by mentioning those who are deserving of goodness, both soon and in the hereafter, and He described them with four attributes: The first is His statement: 57- Indeed, those who, for fear of their Lord, are apprehensive. Apprehension means fear. You say, I am apprehensive about this matter, meaning, I am afraid. It was said that apprehension means fear, so the apparent meaning of the verse is repetition. It was answered by interpreting fear as punishment: meaning, they are afraid of the punishment of their Lord. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said the same. It was also answered by interpreting apprehension as what is an effect of it: which is constant obedience: meaning, those who, for fear of their Lord, are constant in obeying Him. It was also answered that apprehension is the perfection of fear, so there is no repetition. It was also said that repetition is for emphasis.
23:58: And the second attribute is his saying: 58- And those who believe in the signs of their Lord. It was said that what is meant by the signs is the revelation, and it was said that it is the creation, and it was said that it is the combination of both. It was said that what is meant by belief in them is not the belief that they are proofs and that their meaning is true.
23:59: The third attribute is His statement: 59- And those who do not associate anything with their Lord meaning they completely abandon association, both outwardly and inwardly.
23:60: The fourth attribute is His statement: 60- And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful because they will be returning to their Lord. That is, they give what they give while their hearts are fearful because of that giving, thinking that it will not save them from the punishment of God. The phrase and their hearts are fearful is in the accusative case as a state: that is, while their hearts are fearful with the greatest fear. Al-Zajjaj said: Their hearts are fearful because they will be returning to their Lord, and the reason for the fear is that they fear that it will not be accepted from them in the desired manner, not just their return to Him, glory be to Him. It was said that the meaning is: Whoever believes in returning to the reward and reckoning and knows that the rewarder and the reckoner is the Lord from whom nothing is hidden, is not free from fear. Aisha, Ibn Abbas, and Al-Nakha'i read they give what they give shortened from coming. Al-Farra' said: Even if this reading is correct, it does not contradict the reading of the group because some Arabs require the alif in the hamza in all cases. Al-Nahhas said: The meaning of this reading is that they do what they do.
23:61: And the reference in his saying: 61- those is to those who are described by these qualities, and the meaning of they hasten in good deeds is they initiate them. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: they compete in them, and it was said they race, and it was read they hasten "and they are foremost in it" the lam is for emphasis, and the meaning is: they are foremost in it, and it was said that the lam is to as in his saying: "that your Lord inspired it" meaning inspired it, and Sibawayh recited the words of the poet: Stay away from the people of Yamamah, young man, and I did not seek anyone from its people except you. That is, to your liking. It was said that the object is omitted, and the meaning is: And they are ahead of the people for its sake.
23:62: Then when the speech moved to mentioning the actions of those charged, he mentioned two rulings for them: The first is His statement: 62- And We charge no soul except [with that within] its capacity. Capacity is the ability, and this was explained at the end of Surat Al-Baqarah. There are two opinions regarding the interpretation of capacity: The first is that it is the ability, as the linguists have explained it. The second is that it is less than the ability, and this is what Muqatil, Ad-Dahhak, and Al-Kalbi said. The Mu'tazila said: Because capacity is only called that because its action is spacious for the doer and not tight for him, so whoever is unable to sit, then he should nod for a day, and whoever is unable to fast, then he should break his fast. This sentence is a resumption of the incitement to what the predecessors described of doing acts of obedience that lead to attaining honors by explaining its ease and that it is not beyond the limits of one’s ability and capacity, and that this is the habit of God, the Most High, in charging His servants. The sentence And with Us is a Book that speaks the truth is a completion of what preceded it of denying charging with what is beyond one’s capacity. What is meant by the Book are the records of deeds: that is, with Us is a Book in which He has recorded the deeds of each one of those charged as they are. The meaning of speaks the truth is that the truth that corresponds to reality is revealed in it without addition or subtraction. Similar to this is His, the Most High’s, statement: “This is Our Book that speaks against you with the truth. Indeed, We were transcribing what you used to do.” In this is a threat to the disobedient and a comfort to the obedient from injustice and oppression. It was said that what is meant by the Book is the Preserved Tablet, for everything was written in it. It was also said that what is meant by the Book is the Qur’an, and the former is more appropriate. In this verse there is a comparison of the Book to the one from whom the statement is issued by speaking with his tongue, for the Book expresses what is in it as the true speaker expresses it, and His statement: with the truth. It is related to speaking, or to an omitted word that is a state of its subject: that is, speaking in a way that is ambiguous with the truth. The phrase and they are not wronged explains what preceded it of His favor and justice in rewarding His servants: they are not wronged by reducing reward or increasing punishment. Similar to it is the statement of the Almighty: And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone.
23:63: Then He, the Most High, struck out from this and said: 63- Rather, their hearts are in a state of overwhelming darkness over this and the pronoun refers to the disbelievers: meaning, rather, the hearts of the disbelievers are in a state of overwhelming darkness over this Book that speaks the truth, or over the matter that the believers are upon. It is said that the water covered him: if it covered him, and a river covered: it covered whoever entered it, and what is meant by it here is covering and heedlessness or confusion and blindness, and the discussion of the darkness came before recently. And they have deeds other than that Qatada and Mujahid said: meaning, they have sins that they must commit other than the truth. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is that they have evil deeds that they did not do, other than what they are upon, and they must do them and enter the Fire because of them. So the reference in His statement, that, is either to the deeds of the believers, or to the deeds of the disbelievers: that is, they have deeds other than the deeds of the believers that God mentioned, or other than the deeds of the disbelievers that were mentioned earlier, because their hearts are in great heedlessness of what was mentioned, and they are the types of their disbelief and their sins, including what will come of their criticism of the Qur’an. Al-Wahidi said: The consensus of the commentators and the scholars of meaning is that this is a statement about what they will do of their evil deeds that were written for them, and they must do them. The phrase they are doing them confirms what came before it: that is, it is obligatory upon them to do them and enter the Fire because of what preceded them of misery, and they have no escape from that.
23:64: Then the Almighty returned to describing the disbelievers and said: 64- Until, when We seized their affluent ones with punishment. Until this is what the speech begins after, and the speech is the conditional sentence mentioned, and this sentence explains what came before it, and the pronoun in their affluent ones refers to those previously mentioned from the disbelievers, and what is meant by the affluent ones are those who live in luxury among them, and the pronoun in their affluent ones refers to those previously mentioned from the disbelievers, and what is meant by the affluent ones are those who live in luxury among them, and they are those whom God provided with what was mentioned above of wealth and children, or what is meant by them are the leaders among them. What is meant by the punishment is their punishment with the sword on the day of Badr, or with hunger by the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said: O God, intensify Your wrath upon Mudar and make it years for them like the years of Joseph. It was said that what is meant by the punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is preferred because what they do of rebellion only happens at the time of the punishment of the Hereafter, because it is a call for help from God and they did not do that on the day of Badr nor in the years of famine. The answer to this is that in the language, jawar means screaming and shouting. Al-Jawhari said: Jawar is like khowar. It is said that a bull roared, meaning it shouted. This happened to them, their families, and their children when they were tortured with the sword on the day of Badr, and with hunger during the years of famine. Here, jawar is not restricted to jawar, which is supplication in prayer, until what the speaker mentioned is fulfilled. The phrase if they roar is the answer to the condition, and if is the suddenness, and the meaning is: until when We seized their affluent ones with the punishment, they roared and shouted.
23:65: Then the Almighty informed that it will be said to them then, as a form of rebuke 65- Do not cry out in distress today so the statement is implied, and the sentence is intended to rebuke them, make them despair, and cut off their desires. The Almighty singled out the luxurious ones, even though the punishment will befall them all, befalling both the luxurious and the non-luxurious ones, to show that after the blessing they were in, they became in a state that is different and contrasting from it, so they moved from complete bliss to pure misery. The Today was singled out for mention for the purpose of intimidation, and the sentence You will not be helped by Us is an explanation for the prohibition of crying out in distress, and the meaning is: You will not be protected from Our punishment, and your distress will not benefit you. It was said that the meaning is: You will not be helped by Us to prevent you from the punishment that has befallen you.
23:66: Then the Almighty enumerated their ugliness as a rebuke to them, saying: 66- My verses were recited to you, meaning in this world, and they are the verses of the Qur’an, but you turned back on your heels, meaning you went back behind you. The root of backsliding is to go backwards, and from this is the saying of the poet: They claimed to be on the right path, but I turned back. Here it is a metaphor for turning away from the truth. Ali bin Abi Talib read ala adbarkum instead of ala tankasoona with a damma on the kaf. ala tankasoona is related to tankasoona or related to an omitted word that was a state of the subject of tankasoona.
23:67: 67- arrogant to it The pronoun in it refers to the ancient house, and it was said to the sanctuary, and what justified the omission before mentioning it is their fame for arrogance towards it and their pride in its guardianship and performing it, and they used to say: No one will prevail over us because we are the people of the sanctuary and its servants. And this is what the majority of commentators agreed with. And it was said that the pronoun refers to the Qur’an. And the meaning is: that listening to it causes them arrogance and tyranny so they do not believe in it. Ibn Atiyah said: This is a good statement. And An-Nahhas said: The first statement is more appropriate and it is explained by what we mentioned. So according to the first statement, it would be related to arrogant, and according to the second, it would be related to staying up late because they used to gather around the house at night to stay up late, and most of their staying up late was to mention the Qur’an and criticize it, and the night owl is like the one present in the application of the plural. Al-Wahidi said: As-Sāmir is a group who chat at night: that is, they talk. It is possible that it is related to his saying: You chatter. And hajar with the fathah is idhyan: that is, you chatter idly about the Qur’an. It is possible that it is from hajar with the damma, which is obscenity. Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, and Abu Haywah read samran with the damma of the seen and the fathah of the doubled meem. Zaid bin Ali and Abu Raja read samārān, and this reading was narrated from Ibn Abbas. The accusative of sāmiran is in the state either from the agent of tankasūn, or from the pronoun in mustakbireen. It was said that it is a source that came in the form of the agent. It is said the people of sāmir, and from it the saying of the poet: As if there was no companion between Al-Hujun and Al-Safa, and no one spent the evening in Mecca Al-Raghib said: It is also said Samer and Samar, Samar and Samaroon. The majority read tahjaroon with a fatha on the double taa’ from above and a damma on the jim. Nafi’ and Ibn Muhaisin read with a damma on the taa’ and a kasra on the jim from ahjar: meaning he spoke obscenely. Zaid bin Ali, Ibn Muhaisin and Abu Nahik read with a damma on the taa’ and a fatha on the haa’ and a kasra on the jim with a shaddah, the present tense of hajar with a shaddah.
