Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, regarding His statement, And their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance, that he said, Out of arrogance, and their souls were convinced thereof. This is an example of bringing things forward and backward.
27:15: When He, glory be to Him, finished the story of Moses in the story of David and his son Solomon, and these stories and those before and after them are like an explanation and confirmation of His saying: And indeed, you receive the Qur’an from One Who is Wise and Knowing. The tanween in 15- knowledge is either for the type: that is, a group of knowledge, or for glorification: that is, a great deal of knowledge. So the waw in His saying: And they said, ‘Praise be to God’ is for conjunction with something omitted, because this is the position of the fa’, so the meaning is: And indeed, We gave them knowledge, so they acted upon it and said, ‘Praise be to God.’ This is supported by the fact that thanks with the tongue are only good if it is preceded by an action of the heart, which is the resolve to do obedience and leave disobedience. Who has favored us over many of His believing servants, that is, He favored us with knowledge, prophethood, and the subjugation of birds, jinn, and mankind, and they did not favor themselves over everyone out of humility on their part. This verse is evidence of the honor and high status of knowledge, and that the blessing of knowledge is one of the greatest blessings that God bestows upon His servants, and that whoever is given it has been given superiority over many of His servants and granted great honor.
27:16: 16- And Solomon inherited David meaning he inherited knowledge and prophethood from him. Qatada and Al-Kalbi said: David had nineteen sons, and Solomon inherited his prophethood from among them. If what was meant was the inheritor of wealth, Solomon would not have been mentioned specifically because all of his sons were equal in that regard. This is what the majority of commentators said. This inheritor is a metaphorical inheritor, as in the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The scholars are the inheritors of the prophets and And he said, 'O people, teach us the language of the birds.' Solomon said this statement addressing the people, speaking of what God had bestowed upon him and thanking Him for the blessing with which He had singled him out. He mentioned the language of the birds because it was a blessing specific to him and no one else shared it. Al-Farra' said: The language of the birds is the speech of the birds, so he made it like the speech of a man. He recited the words of Humayd ibn Thawr: It is strange that her singing is eloquent and her speech is not forgiven. The meaning of the verse is that we understand what the birds say. A group of commentators said that he learned the speech of all animals, and he only mentioned the birds because they were one of his soldiers who would travel with him to shade him from the sun. Qatadah and Ash-Sha'bi said that he only learned the speech of birds, and this does not apply to the ant, because it is one of the birds, and often grows wings to fly. This was also the case with this ant whose speech he heard and understood. The meaning of And We have been given of all things is everything that is needed, such as knowledge, prophecy, wisdom, wealth, and the subjugation of the jinn, mankind, birds, winds, wild animals, beasts, and everything between the heavens and the earth. Solomon used the letter nun to denote greatness, but what is meant is himself, explaining his state of being obeyed and not disobeyed, not out of arrogance or self-aggrandizement. The reference in his statement, Indeed, this to what was mentioned above of teaching and giving, is the manifest bounty means the apparent and obvious that is not hidden from anyone, or the manifestation of our virtue.
27:17: 17- And there were gathered for Solomon his soldiers from the jinn, mankind, and birds. Hashr is the plural: that is, he gathered for him his soldiers from these kinds. The commentators have gone into great detail in mentioning the number of his soldiers, and many of them have gone to extremes that are beyond the reach of reason and are not authentic in terms of transmission. If it were authentic, then there would be something greater and more numerous in the divine power. So they are distributed that is, for each group of them there is a distribution that returns the first of them to the last of them, so they stand in their ranks. It is said that he distributed him, he distributes him, he distributes him: he restrains him. The deterrent in war who is assigned to the ranks deters those who come forward from them: that is, he returns them. From this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: While I blamed gray hair for my youth and said, Why don’t I wake up while gray hair is a deterrent? And the other said: He who is not deterred by his mind and modesty will have no deterrent in his gray hair. And the other said: Only a person of perfect reason can deter a stubborn soul from its desires. It is said that distribution means separation. It is said: The people are groups, meaning sects.
27:18: 18- "Until they came upon the Valley of the Ants" Until is the word that follows it and is the end of what precedes it. The meaning is that they are distributed until they reach this end, which is their coming upon the Valley of the Ants: that is, they are walking, prevented from separating from one another, until they come, etc. And upon the Valley of the Ants is related to they came, and it is transitive with the preposition 'ala' because they were carried by the wind, so they are high. The meaning is that they crossed the valley and reached its end. All the reciters stopped at Wadi without the Ya' following the orthography, as it was not deleted due to the meeting of two sukoon letters, like his saying: "those who hewed the rocks in the valley" except Al-Kisa'i, who stopped with the Ya'. He said: Because what caused the deletion is only the meeting of two sukoon letters in the connection. Ka'b said: Wadi Al-Naml is in Taif. Qatada and Muqatil said: It is in Ash-Sham. An ant said, this is the answer to if, as if when it saw them heading towards the valley it ran away and alerted the rest of the ants, calling out to them and saying: O ants, enter your dwellings. He made the ants’ address like the address of rational beings so that they would understand that address, and the dwellings are the places where the ants live. It was said that this ant that Solomon heard was female, as evidenced by the feminization of the verb attributed to it. Abu Hayyan responded by saying: The addition of the taa’ in qalaat does not indicate that the ant is feminine. Rather, it is correct to say qalat for the masculine, because namlah, even if it has the taa’, is one of those in which the masculine is not distinguished from the feminine by the masculine or feminine of the verb, but rather by stating that it is male or female. There is no much benefit in relating to such a thing, nor in discussing the name of the ant and the fabricated stories and false hadiths that have been mentioned. Al-Hasan, Talhah, and Muammar ibn Sulayman read namlah and an-naml with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the noon, with the same weight as rajul and samrah. Sulayman at-Taymi read it with two dhammahs, in which there is la yuḥathamanukum Solomon and his soldiers al-rajul wa-samrah. It is said hamatuhu hataman I broke it, meaning I broke it a breaking, and shatara is taksar I broke. This prohibition apparently refers to the ant, but in reality to Solomon. It is from the same category as I do not see you here. It may be a substitute for the command, and it is possible that it is an answer to the command. Abu Hayyan said: As for its interpretation as a response to a command, it can only be according to the reading of Al-A’mash, as he read la yuḥtaḥimkum in the jussive mood without the nun of emphasis. However, with the presence of the nun of emphasis, this is only permissible in poetry. Sibawayh said: It is rare in poetry, they likened it to a prohibition when it is in the jussive mood. Abi read adkhulu masakinukun and Shahr ibn Hawshab read maskankum and Al-Hasan, Abu Raja’, Qatadah and Isa Al-Hamadani read la yuḥtamankum with a damma on the ya’, a fatha on the ha’ and a shaddah on the ta’. Ibn Ishaq, Ya’qub and Abu Amr, in one narration, read it with a sukun on the nun of emphasis. The phrase and they do not feel is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of yaḥtamankum: meaning they do not feel that they have crushed you and they do not know where you are. It was said that the meaning is: and the ants do not feel that Solomon understands what they say, but this is far-fetched.
27:19: 19- So he smiled, laughing at her statement. Ibn al-Samīfā' read it as laughing. According to the majority reading, laughing is an emphatic adverbial because laughter was understood from smiling. It was also said that it is an implied adverbial because smiling is the beginning of laughter. It was also said that since smiling can be for anger, laughter was a clear explanation of it. It was also said that the laughter of the prophets was smiling only. According to Ibn al-Samīfā' reading, laughter is a verbal noun governed by a deleted verb or in the adverbial position. Solomon's laughter was in amazement at her statement, her understanding, and her being guided to warn the ants. And he said, 'My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents.' The meaning of inspire me was explained shortly in His statement, so they are evaluating. He said in al-Kashāf: The true meaning of inspire me is: Make me evade and be grateful for Your favors, and I will restrain myself and bind it so that it does not slip away from me until I do not stop being grateful to You. End quote. Al-Wahidi said: Awza’ni means inspire me to be grateful for the blessings that You have bestowed upon me. It is said that someone is mowza’i for something, meaning he is obsessed with it. Al-Qurtubi said: Its origin is from waza’a, so it is as if he said: Keep me away from that which angers You. The second object of awza’ni is: to be grateful for the blessings that You have bestowed upon me. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of and grant me is: Prevent me from being ungrateful for Your blessings, which is an interpretation based on the necessary meaning. The meaning of upon my parents is a supplication from him that God distributes gratitude for His blessings to his parents as He distributed gratitude for His blessings upon him, for bestowing blessings upon them is a blessing upon him, and that requires him to thank God Almighty. Then he asked that God add to him the consequences of His blessings to the previous ones, especially the religious blessings, so he said: And that I do righteousness that pleases You, meaning righteous work that pleases You from me. Then he supplicated that God Almighty make him in the Hereafter among the group of the righteous, for that is the goal to which the supplication is related, so he said: And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants, meaning: admit me among their group, establish my name among their names, and gather me in their group to the abode of the righteous, which is Paradise. O God, I supplicate to You with what this noble Prophet supplicated to You with, so accept that from me and bestow it upon me, for even if I have been negligent in my work, Your favor is the reason for winning good. This verse is a call with the loudest voice and the clearest statement. That entering Paradise, which is the abode of the believers, is through Your bounty, not through their deeds, as Your truthful Messenger said in what was authenticated from him in the Sahih: Straighten your ways and come close, and know that no one will enter Paradise through his deeds. They said: Not even you, O Messenger of God? He said: Not even me, unless God covers me with His mercy. So if there is nothing but Your abundant bounty, then abandoning seeking it from You is a failure, and neglecting to beseech You to lead him to it is a waste. Then the Almighty proceeded to mention the story of Bilqis and what happened between them and Solomon, and that was through the guidance of the hoopoe.
27:20: He said: 20- And check the birds. Checking means seeking out what is missing from you and knowing its condition. The bird is a generic name for everything that flies, and the meaning is that you seek out what is missing from the birds and know the condition of what is absent from them. The birds used to accompany him on his travels and shade him with their wings. He said, 'Why do I not see the hoopoe, or is he among the absent?' That is, what is wrong with the hoopoe that I do not see him? This is one of the inverted expressions that the Arabs use a lot. It was said that there is no need to claim the inversion, rather it is a question about what prevents him from seeing the hoopoe, as if he said, Why do I not see him? Is that because of a screen that conceals him from me, or because of something else? Then it appeared to him that he was absent, so he said: Or was he among the absent ones? And am is the disconnected one that means interruption. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Hisham, and Ayoub read mali with a fatha on the ya’, and they also read in Yasin And why should I not worship He who created me? with a fatha on the ya’. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read it with a sukoon in both places, and the rest read it with a fatha on the one in Yasin and a sukoon on the one here. Abu Amr said: Because this one here is an interrogative, and the one in Yasin is a negation. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid chose the sukoon.
27:21: 21- I will surely punish him severely or slaughter him. They differed about what this severe punishment is. Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: It is that all his feathers are plucked. Yazid ibn Rumaan said: It is that the feathers of his wings are plucked. It was also said that it is that he is imprisoned with his enemies, and it was also said that it is that he is prevented from serving them. This is evidence that the punishment is according to the sin, not according to the body. His statement, punishment, is a verbal noun or a verbal noun with the omission of the extra letters, like his statement, He caused you to grow from the earth like a plant, “Or that he should bring me clear authority.” Ibn Kathir alone read it with the doubled nun of emphasis followed by the nun of protection. The rest read it with only a doubled nun, which is the nun of emphasis. Isa ibn Umar read it with a doubled open nun not connected to the ya’. The clear authority is the clear proof in his occultation.
27:22: 22- Famakt not far away meaning the hoopoe stayed for a period of time not far away. The majority read makath with a damma on the kaf, while Asim alone read it with a fatha. In both readings, its meaning is: stay for a period of time not far away. Sibawayh said: mukath yamktihu mukhuthan like qa'ada yaqudu qu'udan. It was said that the pronoun in mukath refers to Solomon. The meaning is: Solomon stayed for a period of time not long after the inspection and threat. The first is more appropriate. Fala said, I have encompassed that which you have not encompassed meaning I knew what you did not know about the matter. Encompassing is knowing something from all sides. Perhaps there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: so the hoopoe stayed not after me, so he came and was reprimanded for his absence, so he said, apologizing for that, I have encompassed that which you have not encompassed. Al-Farra’ said: It is permissible to assimilate the letter ta’ into the letter ta’, so it is said ‘aht’, and to assimilate the letter ta’ into the letter ta’, so it is said ‘aht’. And I have come to you from Sheba with certain report. The majority read from Sheba in the genitive case, as if it were the name of a man, to whom a people were attributed. From this is the saying of the poet: The visitors and Taym in the heights of Saba, their necks are covered with buffalo skin. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a fat-ha on the hamza and did not decline it, believing it to be the name of a city. Az-Zajjaj denied that it is the name of a man and said: Saba is the name of a city known as Ma'rib in Yemen, between them and Sana'a, three days away. It was also said that it is the name of a woman after whom the city was named. Al-Qurtubi said: The correct view is that it is the name of a man, as in the book of At-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Urwah ibn Masik Al-Muradi. Ibn Atiyyah said: This was not clear to Az-Zajjaj, so he rambled blindly. Al-Farra' claimed that Ar-Ru'asi asked Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala' about Saba, saying: I do not know what it is. An-Nahhas said: Abu Amr is too noble to say this. He said: The statement about Saba, as it was reported, is that it was originally the name of a man. If you decline it, it is because it has become the name of a tribe. If you do not decline it, you make it the name of a tribe like Thamud. However, according to Sibawayh, the preferred form is the decline. I say: There is no doubt that Saba is the name of a city in Yemen where Bilqis was located, and it is also the name of a man from Qahtan, namely Saba bin Yashjub bin Ya’rub bin Qahtan bin Hud. But what is meant here is that the hoopoe came to Solomon from this city with certain report, and report is serious report of a serious nature. So when the hoopoe said to Solomon what he said, Solomon said to him: What is that?
27:23: He said: I have found a woman ruling them. She is Bilqis bint Shurahbil, whose grandfather was the hoopoe, ruling the people of Sheba. This sentence is like a statement and explanation of the sentence before it: that is, the certain report is that this woman rules these people. And she has been given of everything. There is an exaggeration in this, meaning that she has been given of everything that she needs. It was also said that the meaning is: she has been given something of everything in her time, so something was omitted because the speech had already indicated it. And she has a mighty throne, meaning a great bed. He described it as great because, as was said, it was made of gold, eighty cubits long, forty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high in the sky, crowned with pearls, red rubies, and green chrysolite. It was also said that what is meant by the throne here is the kingdom, and the former is more appropriate because of His saying: Which of you will bring me her throne? Ibn Atiyyah said: What is necessary from the verse is that she was a woman who was queen over the cities of Yemen, with a great kingdom and a great bed, and she was an unbeliever from an unbeliever people.
27:24: 24- I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God meaning they worshipped it, transgressing the worship of God Almighty. It was said that they were Magians, and it was said that they were heretics. And Satan made their deeds pleasing to them that they were doing, which was worshipping the sun and all other acts of disbelief. So he averted them from the way meaning that Satan averted them because of that beautification from the clear path, which is belief in God and His Oneness. So they are not guided to that.
27:25: 25- that they should not prostrate themselves. The majority of reciters read the word with a shaddah on ala. Ibn al-Anbari said: The pause at fahm la yahtidun is incomplete according to those who stress ala, because the meaning is: And Satan made it seem good to them that they should not prostrate themselves. An-Nahhas said: It is if la is added to it, and it is in the accusative case. Al-Akhfash said: That is, he made it seem good to them that they should not prostrate themselves to God, meaning lest they prostrate themselves to God. Al-Kisa'i said: It is in the accusative case due to sadahum: that is, he prevented them from prostrating themselves, meaning lest they prostrate themselves, so in both cases it is an object for it. Al-Yazidi said: It is a substitute for their actions in the accusative case. Abu Amr said: It is in the genitive case as a substitute for as-sabil. It was said that the factor in it is they are not guided: meaning they are not guided to prostrate to God, and la in this case is redundant like his saying: What prevented you from prostrating? According to the reading of the majority, this verse is not a place for prostration, because that is informing about them leaving al-Sajdah 32:either by beautification or by being turned away, or by being prevented from being guided. Al-Zajjaj preferred that it be the reason for turning away, and Al-Farra’ preferred that it be the reason for zayd, as he said: Their deeds were made beautiful for them so that they would not prostrate, then the lam was deleted. Al-Zuhri and Al-Kisa’i read ala with a light ala sound. Al-Kisa’i said: I did not hear the elders recite it except with a light emphasis on the intention of command, so ala in this reading is a letter of warning and opening, and what follows it is a letter of calling, and asjuddu is a verb of command. The correct writing in this reading should have been like this: ala ya isjuddu, but the companions, may God be pleased with them, dropped the alif from ya and the hamzat al-wasl from asjuddu by mistake and connected the ya’ to the seen of asjuddu, so the written form became ala yasjuddu, and the called out is deleted, and its interpretation is: ala ya ha’alihu’i isjuddu. The Arabs have often deleted the called out in their speech, and from this is the saying of the poet: Oh Aslami, oh Darami, despite the decay, the rain still flows from your necks. And the other said: Oh, Islam, then Islam, then Islam, three times. Greetings, even if you do not speak. And another said: Oh, Aslami, oh Hind, Hind of Bani Bakr It is common in their poetry. Al-Zajjaj said: The takfif reading requires prostration, while the tadkif reading does not. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid preferred the tadkif reading. Al-Zajjaj said: The takfif reading has a good aspect, except that it interrupts the story of Sheba and then returns to mentioning them. The tadkif reading is a piece of report that follows one another with no interruption in the middle. An-Nahhas said the same thing: According to this reading, the phrase would you not prostrate is an interruption from the words of the hoopoe, or from the words of Solomon, or from the words of God, the Most High. In this reading, Abdullah ibn Masoud reads would you not prostrate with the tafsir, and in Abu’s reading, would you not prostrate with the tafsir also Who brings forth the hidden in the heavens and the earth meaning He reveals what is hidden and concealed in them. It is said: I hid the thing, I hid it, and the hidden is what I concealed. Al-Zajjaj said: It was mentioned in the interpretation that the hidden here means rain from the sky and plants from the earth. It was said that the hidden of the earth is its treasures and plants. Qatada said: The hidden is the secret. An-Nahhas said: It means what is hidden in the heavens and the earth. Abi and Isa bin Omar read al-Khab with a fat-ha on the ba’ without a hamza for ease. Abdullah, Ikrimah and Malik bin Dinar read al-Khaba with an alif. Abu Hatim said: This is not permissible in Arabic. He was refuted by the fact that Sibawayh narrated from the Arabs that the alif is replaced by a hamza if it is preceded by a sukoon. In Abdullah’s reading, al-Khaba comes out of the heavens and the earth. Al-Farra’ said: Min and wa alternate, and the relative pronoun may be in the genitive case as an attribute of God, the Most High, or as a substitute for Him, or as an explanation of Him. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a praise, or it is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject. The phrase And He knows what you conceal and what you declare is conjoined with He brings forth. The majority of scholars read the two verbs with the subjunctive ending, while Al-Jahdary, Isa ibn Umar, Hafs, and Al-Kisa’i read them with the superjunctive ending for address. As for the first reading, it is because the preceding pronouns are absent pronouns. As for the second reading, it is because the reading of Al-Zuhri and Al-Kisa’i contains the command to prostrate and addresses them with that. This, according to them, is part of that address. The meaning is that God, the Exalted, brings forth what is hidden in this human world with His knowledge of it, just as He brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth. Then, after describing the Lord, the Exalted, with what came before, which indicates His great power and sublime authority, and the necessity of making Him One and dedicating worship to Him alone.
27:26: He said: 26- God, there is no god but He, Lord of the Mighty Throne. The majority of scholars read the Mighty in the accusative case as a description of the Throne, and Ibn Muhaisin read it in the nominative case as a description of the Lord, and he specifically mentioned the Throne because it is the greatest of creations, as is proven in the hadith attributed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz that he wrote: “If God bestows a blessing upon a servant and he praises God for it, his praise will be better than the blessing, if only you knew that from the revealed Book of God. God the Almighty said: ‘And We had certainly given knowledge to David and Solomon, and they said, ‘Praise be to God, who has favored us over many of His believing servants.’” What blessing could be better than what was given to David and Solomon? I say: There is nothing in the verse that indicates what he may God have mercy on him understood. What it indicates is that they praised God, the Exalted, for the blessings He bestowed upon them. So how do you indicate that His praise is better than His blessings? Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatadah, regarding the statement, And Solomon inherited David, that he said: He inherited his prophethood, his kingdom, and his knowledge. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Siddiq al-Naji, who said: Solomon, son of David, went out to pray for rain with the people. He passed by an ant lying on its back, raising its legs to the sky and saying, “O God, we are one of Your creations and we are not independent of Your provision. Either You give us rain or You destroy us.” Solomon said to the people, Go back, for you have been given rain because of the supplication of someone other than you. Al-Hakim narrated in Al-Mustadrak on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad who said: Solomon was given the kingdom of the East and the West. Solomon ruled for seven hundred years and six months. He ruled over all the people of the world, from the jinn, humans, animals, birds, and wild beasts. He was given everything and the ability to speak everything. During his time, amazing deeds were done, until when God wanted to take him, He revealed to him to entrust God's knowledge and wisdom to his brother. The sons of David were four hundred and eighty men, prophets without a message. Al-Dhahabi said: This is false. Stories have been narrated about the greatness of Solomon's kingdom, and mentioning any of them is not pleasing to the soul, so refraining from mentioning them is better. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: And they are distributed, he said: They are pushed. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the statement: And they are distributed, he said: He made for each group a distribution, the first of which returns to the last so that it would not precede him in the march as kings do. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, regarding the statement of God, and inspire me, that he said: Inspire me. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar from al-Hasan. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated through various chains of narration from Ibn Abbas that he was asked, How did Solomon miss the hoopoe among the birds? He said, “Solomon stopped at a place and did not know where the water was. The hoopoe used to guide Solomon to the water, so he wanted to ask it about it but missed it.” It was said, How could that be when the hoopoe sets traps for him, throwing dirt over them, and a boy sets a snare for him, hiding it and catching him? He said, When the decree comes, his sight is lost. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, that he said: I will pluck out all his feathers. Something similar was narrated from a group of the Successors. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan, who said: The name of Solomon’s hoopoe was Ghabar. And I say: Where did Al-Hasan may God have mercy on him get this knowledge? And so what Ibn Asakir narrated from him that the ant's name was Haras, that it was from a tribe called Banu Shaytan, that it was lame, and that it was the size of a wolf? And he may God have mercy on him is the most pious of people when it comes to narrating lies. And we know that nothing has been authenticated from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) concerning this matter, and we know that Al-Hasan has no chain of transmission that goes back to Solomon or any of his companions. So this knowledge was taken from the People of the Book, and we have been commanded neither to believe them nor to disbelieve them. If someone permits himself to narrate from them something like what he narrated, then narrate from the Children of Israel and there is no blame. This is not in relation to the interpretation of the Book of God, the Exalted, without a doubt, but rather in relation to the stories that happened to them. We have repeatedly drawn attention to such matters when discussing strange interpretations. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Or let him bring me clear authority, he said: It is clear, truthful report of the truth. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: Ibn Abbas said: Every authority in the Qur’an is a proof. He mentioned this verse and then said: What kind of authority did the hoopoe have? Meaning that what is meant by authority is the proof, not the authority that is the king. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the statement: I have encompassed that which you have not encompassed, he said: I have seen that which you have not seen. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: And I have come to you from Sheba, he said: Sheba is in the land of Yemen, it is called Ma’rib, between it and Sana’a is a journey of three nights. With certain report, he said: With true report. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority: Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them, he said: Her name was Bilqis bint Sharaheel, and the Sulaymans were poets. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Zuhair bin Muhammad that she was Bilqis bint Sharaheel, and on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that she was the daughter of Dhi Sharh. Ibn Jarir, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: One of the parents of Bilqis was a jinn. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And she will have a mighty throne, that he said: A noble throne of gold, its legs made of precious jewels and pearls, beautifully crafted and very expensive. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, He brings forth what is hidden, that he said: He knows every hidden thing in the heavens and the earth.
27:27: Sentence 27 - He said, 'We will see' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question: that is, Solomon said to the hoopoe: We will see what you have told us of this story. Have you told the truth in what you said, or were you among the liars? This interrogative sentence is in the accusative case as the object of We will see, and or is the connected particle. His saying, Or were you among the liars is more eloquent than his saying or did you lie, because the meaning is: among those who are characterized by lying and it has become their nature. Looking is contemplation and examination, and in it is guidance to search for report and uncover the truths, and not to accept the report of informants by imitating them or relying on them if that is possible in any way. Then Solomon explained this looking that he promised.
27:28: He said: 28- Go with this letter of mine and throw it to them meaning to the people of Saba'. Al-Zajjaj said: There are five aspects to throwing it: proving the ya' in the pronunciation and deleting it, proving the kasra to indicate it, pronouncing the ha' with a damma and pronouncing the waw, deleting the waw and pronouncing the damma to indicate it, and pronouncing the ha' with a sukoon. Abu Amr, Hamzah, and Abu Bakr recited with this fifth language. Qalun recited with a kasra on the ha' only without a ya'. Two aspects were narrated from Hisham: pronouncing the ya' in the pronunciation and deleting it with a kasra on the ha'. The rest read it by confirming the ya’ in the wording. His saying with this letter of mine could be a demonstrative pronoun describing the letter, or a substitute for it, or an explanation of it. He singled out the hoopoe for sending him the letter because he was the one who informed of the story and because he saw in him signs of understanding and knowledge that required him to be worthy of the message. Then turn away from them means move away from them. He ordered him to do that because moving away after delivering the letter is one of the best manners with which messengers of kings are taught. What is meant is moving away to a place where he hears their conversation until he informs Solomon of what he heard. It was said that the meaning of turning away is returning to it, and the first is more appropriate because of his saying: Then see what they return meaning order and think about what some of them return to each other in terms of saying and what they exchange among themselves in terms of speech.
27:29: 29- She said, meaning Bilqis, O assembly, indeed a noble letter has been thrown to me. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So the hoopoe went and threw it to them, and he heard her say: O assembly, etc., and she described the letter as noble because it was from someone great in her soul, out of reverence for Solomon. It was said that she described it thus because it contained beautiful words, and it was said that she described it thus because it reached her sealed with the seal of Solomon, and the nobleness of the letter is its seal, as was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Then she explained what this letter contained.
27:30: She said: 30- It is from Solomon and it is in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. That is, what it contained of speech and what it included of saying began with the name of God and after the name of God.
27:31: 31- That you do not be arrogant towards me meaning do not be arrogant as the tyrants of kings do, and that is the explanatory particle, and it was said that it is a verbal noun, and not is a prohibitive particle, and it was said that it is a negative particle, and the location of the sentence is the nominative case as a substitute for book or the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning that it is that you do not be arrogant. The majority read it is from Solomon and it is with a kasra on both of them as a resumption, and Ikrimah and Ibn Abi Ubla read it with a fatha on it, dropping the preposition, and Abi read it is from Solomon and it is in the name of God by deleting the two pronouns and sukoon on the two noons as they are explanatory, and Abdullah Ibn Masoud read it is not exaggerating with the voiced ghayn from exaggeration, which is exceeding the limit in arrogance, and come to me as Muslims meaning opposing the religion and believing in what I have brought.
27:32: 32- She said, ‘O assembly, advise me in my affair.’ The assembly is the nobles of the people, and the meaning is, O assembly, advise me and show me what is right in this affair and answer me with what is required by prudence. She expressed the advice with the fatwa because that would solve what was unclear to her in the affair, and there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So when Bilqis read the letter, she gathered the nobles of her people and said to them: “O assembly, I have been given a ruling. O assembly, advise me.” She repeated said to further pay attention to what she said to them, then she increased her politeness and attracted their thoughts so that they would give her sincere advice and advise her to what is right, so she said: I have not decided on a matter until you witness it. That is, I have not decided on a matter until you are present with me and advise me.
27:33: F 33- They said in response to her We are men of strength in numbers and equipment and men of great might in war and confrontation. We have the courage and bravery with which we can protect ourselves, our country and our kingdom. Then they entrusted the matter to her, knowing the soundness of her opinion and the strength of her mind, so they said: And the matter is up to you meaning it is entrusted to your opinion and your consideration so see what you command meaning consider what you command us to do, for we are listening to your command and obeying it. As
27:34: When she heard that they had delegated the matter to her, 34- “She said, ‘When kings enter a town, they ruin it’ meaning, when they enter a town, they destroy its buildings, change its places of worship, destroy its wealth, and scatter its people. ‘And make the most honored of its people humiliated’ meaning, they humiliate its nobles and lower their ranks, so that they become humiliated. They only do that in order for the kingdom to be complete for them, for their control to be established, and for awe to be established in their hearts.’ Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, if they enter it by force, not by fighting or defeat. The purpose of her statement was to warn her people against Solomon’s march toward them and his entry into their land. God, the Exalted, confirmed what she said, as He, the Exalted, said, ‘And thus they do’ meaning they do the same action. Ibn al-Anbari said: The pause at the verse, “and they made the most honorable of its people humiliated” is a complete pause. So God Almighty said, in confirmation of her statement, And thus they do. It was said that this sentence is a new sentence and has no syntactic position. Then, when she presented this introduction to them and explained to them the corruption that would result from kings entering their land, she clarified to them the direction of her opinion and declared it to be correct.
27:35: She said: 35- And I am sending to them a gift meaning I am testing this man by sending my messengers to him with a gift containing precious wealth. If he is a king, we will satisfy him with that and take care of his matter. But if he is a prophet, that will not satisfy him, because the ultimate goal of his request and the ultimate desire is to call to the religion, and nothing will save us from it except answering him, following him, adopting his religion, and following his path. For this reason, she said: Then I will see what the messengers will return with. The fa is in conjunction with sent, and with what is related to will return, and the meaning is: I am looking at what my messengers, the ones sent with the gift, will return with, whether acceptance or rejection, so I will act according to what that requires. The commentators have spoken at length about this gift, and at the end of the research, there will be an explanation of what is closest to what has been said to being correct and sound.
27:36: 36- "When Solomon came" meaning when her messenger came with the gift, Solomon, and what is meant by this implied pronoun is the gender, so it does not contradict their being a group, as indicated by her saying: "With what do the messengers return? Abdullah read When Solomon came meaning the messengers, and the phrase He said, 'Do you provide me with wealth?'" is a new sentence in response to an implied question, and the question is for denunciation: meaning he said, denying their providing him with wealth despite his high authority and abundant wealth. Hamzah read it by assimilating the noon of i'rab into the noon of protection, and the rest read it with two noons without assimilating. As for the ya', Nafi', Abu Amr, and Hamzah keep it in connection and delete it when stopping, and Ibn Kathir keeps it in both cases, and the rest delete it in both cases. It was narrated on the authority of Nafi’ that he would read it with one noon, “So what God has given me is better than what He has given you,” meaning what He has given me of prophethood, great kingdom, and abundant wealth is better than what He has given you of wealth, which this gift is part of. Abu Amr, Nafi’, and Hafs read God has given me with an open ya’, and Ya’qub read it with it when pausing and deleting it when connecting. The rest read it without a ya’, both when connecting and stopping. Then he reversed the previous denial and said: Rather, you rejoice in your gift, rebuking them for their joy over this gift with a joy of pride and arrogance. As for me, I do not rejoice over it, and this world is not among my needs, because God, the Exalted, has given me from it what He has not given to anyone else in the worlds, and despite that, He honored me with prophethood. The purpose of this reversal by Solomon was to explain the reason that prompted them to receive the gift, while belittling and degrading them.
27:37: 37- “Return to them, for We will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot resist.” That is, Solomon said to the messenger: Return to them, meaning to Bilqis and her people. He addressed a singular person here after addressing the group previously, either because the one who will return is the Messenger alone, or he singled out the Commander of the Messengers for address here and addressed them along with him previously, to create temptation in speech. Abdullah ibn Abbas read Return, and it was said that the pronoun refers to the hoopoe, and the lām in We will surely come to them is the answer to an omitted oath. An-Nahhas said: I heard Ibn Kaysan say: It is a lam of emphasis, a lam of command, and a lam of khufd. This is the opinion of the most skilled grammarians because they return a thing to its origin, and this is only possible for someone who is trained in Arabic. The meaning of they have no power is that they have no strength or ability to do so. The sentence is in the genitive case as an attribute of the soldiers. And We will surely expel them is in apposition to the answer to the oath, meaning: We will expel them from their land in which they are humiliated, meaning in a state of humiliation after they had been honored. The sentence and they are humiliated is in the accusative case as a state of circumstance. It was said that it is a state of emphasis because humiliation is subjugation. It was also said that what is meant by humiliation here is captivity and exile. It was also said that humiliation is the humiliation that results from humiliation. When the messenger returned to Bilqis, she prepared to go to Solomon, and Gabriel informed Solomon of that.
27:38: 38- Solomon said, ‘O eminent ones, which of you will bring me her throne’ meaning the throne of Bilqis, which was previously described as enormous, before they come to me in submission meaning before she and her people come to me in submission. It was said that Solomon wanted to take her throne before they reached it and submitted to it, because if she submitted and her people did, it would not be permissible to take their wealth without their consent. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: The apparent meaning of the narrations is that this statement by Solomon occurred after her gift had arrived, after he had returned it to her, and after he had sent the hoopoe with the letter. This is the view of the majority of interpreters. It was also said that he summoned the throne before her arrival to show her the power that comes from God and make it a proof of his prophethood. It was also said that he wanted to test her intelligence, and for this reason He said, ‘Disguise her throne for her’ etc. It was also said that he wanted to test the truthfulness of the hoopoe in describing the throne as enormous, and the first view is the one that most agree with.
27:39: 39- An 'Afreet from among the jinn said, 'I will bring it to you before you rise from your place.' The majority of reciters read it with a kasra on the 'ayn, a sukoon on the fa', a kasra on the ra', a sukoon on the second thaa', and a ta'. Abu Raja', 'Isa al-Thaqafi, Ibn al-Samee', and Abu al-Samal read 'Afreet with a fatha on the lower thaa' followed by a feminine ta' marbuta that became a ha'. This recitation was narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. Abu Hayyan read it with a fatha on the 'ayn. 'Afreet is the rough, strong rebel. An-Nahhas said: If a strong person is accompanied by malice and cunning, it is said that he is 'Afreet, 'Afreet, and 'Afreet. Qatada said: He is the cunning one, and it was said that he is the chief of the jinn. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: A group of 'Afar read it with a kasra on the 'ayn, pluralizing it to 'Affar. Among the Arab poetry that matches the recitation of the majority of the scholars is what al-Kisa'i recited: Then Satan, an Ifrit, said to them: Why do you have no stay or night? What was mentioned in the second reading is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: Like a planet following a demon, directed in the blackness of the night The meaning of the Ifrit’s saying that he will bring the throne to Solomon before he rises from the seat in which he sits to govern among the people, And indeed, I am for it strong and trustworthy. Indeed, I am strong in carrying it and trustworthy with what is in it. It was said that the name of this Ifrit is Kudan, mentioned by An-Nahhas on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih. Al-Suhayli said Dhakwan, and it was said that his name is Dawan, and it was said that he is Sakhr. His saying, I will bring you is a present tense verb, and its root is a’teek with two hamzas, but the second was replaced with an alif, and it was said that it is an active participle.
27:40: 40- He who had knowledge of the Scripture said, ‘I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.’ Most commentators said: The name of the one who had knowledge of the Scripture was Asaf bin Barkhiya, and he was from the Children of Israel. He was a minister to Solomon, and he knew the Greatest Name of God, by which if He is called upon, He answers, and if He is asked by it, He gives. Ibn Atiyyah said: A group said it was Solomon himself, and in this case the address is to the ‘ifrit: as if Solomon was impatient for what the ‘ifrit said, so he said to him, in contempt, ‘I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.’ It was also said that it was Gabriel, or Al-Khidr, but the first is more appropriate. Other statements have been made that have no basis. What is meant by blinking is the moving of the eyelids and opening them to look, and its returning is its closing. It was also said that it is the meaning of ‘al-Matroof’: that is, the thing that looks at them. It was also said that it is the eyelid itself, and it was used to express the speed of a matter, as when you say to your companion: Do that in a moment. This was said by Mujahid. Saeed bin Jubair said: He said to Solomon: Look at the sky and he did not blink until he brought it and placed it in front of him. The meaning is: until your glance returns to you after extending it to the sky, and the first is the most correct of these sayings. Then the third: And when he saw it settled near him, it was said that there was an omission in the verse, and the meaning is: So Solomon gave him permission, so he called upon God and brought it. When Solomon saw it settled near him: meaning he saw the throne present before him, “he said: This is from the bounty of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful.” The reference in his saying this is to the presence of the throne, to test me: meaning to test me whether I will thank Him for that and acknowledge that it is from His bounty without any power or strength from me, or whether I will be ungrateful by leaving gratitude and not performing it. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is to see whether I am grateful or ungrateful. Another said: The meaning of to test me is for him to worship Me. This is a metaphor, and the origin of testing is examination. And whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself because he deserves through gratitude the completion and continuity of the blessing. The meaning is that the benefit of that does not return except to the grateful one. And whoever is ungrateful by not being grateful, then indeed, my Lord is free of need of His gratitude, generous in not hastening punishment by taking away His blessings from him and depriving him of what He gave him of them. The umm in umm akfar is the connected particle. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Go with this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then turn away from them, meaning: Be close to them, and see what they return. So he set off with the letter until he was in the middle of her throne, and he delivered the letter to her. It was read to her and it said: “It is from Solomon and it says: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority: A noble letter, meaning sealed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Maymun ibn Mihran that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to write: In your name, O God, until the verse: “It is from Solomon and it says: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful” was revealed. Abu Dawud narrated in his Marasils on the authority of Abu Malik, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Advise me in my affair. He said: She gathered the leaders of her kingdom and consulted them about her opinion, and their opinion and her opinion were unanimous that he should invade him. So she set out until she was close by and said: Send him a gift. If he accepts it, then he is a king whom I will fight, and if he rejects it, I will follow him, and he is a prophet. When her messengers approached Solomon, he learned their report, so he ordered the devils to fake a thousand palaces of gold and silver. When her messengers saw the palaces of gold, they said: What will this man do with our gift while his palaces are gold and silver? When they entered upon him with her gift, he said: Do you provide me with wealth? Then Solomon said: Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission? So Solomon’s scribe said: Lift your eyes. So he raised his eyes, and when he looked back at him, he saw a throne. He said: Disguise her throne for her. So he removed its jewels, its accessories, and whatever was on it. So it was said to her: Is this your throne? She said: It is as if it is. And he ordered the devils to make a palace for her. Stretched out of glass and made in it statues of fish, then it was said to her, Enter the palace, so she uncovered her legs and found hair in them. Then he ordered that lime be made, so it was made, and it was said to her, It is a palace smooth of glass. She said, My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement, Indeed, when kings enter a city, they ruin it, that he said: If they take it by force, they destroy it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, that he said: The Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, says: And thus they do. Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement, And indeed, I am sending to them a gift, that he said: I sent a brick of gold, and when they arrived, the walls of the city were made of gold. This is what he said, Do you provide me with wealth? Thabit al-Bunani said: Gold plates in brocade vessels were presented to him as a gift. Mujahid said: The clothing of slave girls is like that of young boys, and the clothing of young boys is like that of slave girls. Ikrimah said: Two hundred horses were given as a gift, with each horse having a male and female slave, and each horse had a different color than the other. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: The gift was jewels. Other things were said, which there is no benefit in mentioning at length. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Before they come to me in submission, he said, Obeying. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, he said, The name of the Ifrit is Sakhr. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, Before you rise from your place, he said, From your seat. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, He who had knowledge of the Scripture said, he said, He is Asif ibn Barkhiya, and he was a truthful person who knew the Greatest Name. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said regarding the recitation of Ibn Masoud: “He who had knowledge of the Book said: ‘I will look into the Book of my Lord, then I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.’” So that scholar spoke words that caused the throne to enter a tunnel under the earth until it came out to them. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement, before your glance returns to you, that he said: He said to Solomon, Look at the sky. So he did not blink until he brought it to him and placed it before him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The throne of the Lady of Sheba did not move between the earth and the sky, but the earth split open with it, so it moved under the earth until it appeared before Solomon.
27:41: His statement: 41- They disguised her throne for her. Disguise means change. He says they changed her bed to a state that she would disguise when she saw it. It was said that he made its top its bottom and its bottom its top, and it was also said that it was changed by adding and subtracting. Al-Farra’ and others said: He ordered it to be disguised because the devils told him that there was something wrong with her mind, so he wanted to test her. It was also said that the jinn feared that Solomon would marry her and that she would bear him a child and that they would remain subservient to the family of Solomon forever, so they told Solomon that she was weak of mind and her leg was like a donkey’s leg. His statement, We will see is in the jussive mood as an answer to the mother, and the majority read it in the jussive mood. Abu Hayyan read it in the nominative case as a resumption, Will you be guided to knowing Him, or to believing in God, Or will you be among those who are not guided to that.
27:42: 42- So when she came meaning Bilqis to Solomon, it was said to her, and the speaker was Solomon, or someone else, by his command, Is this your throne? He did not say This is your throne lest that be a prompting to her and thus her mind would not be tested. She said, ‘It is as if it were him.’ Mujahid said: She began to recognize and deny it and to be amazed by his presence with Solomon, so she said: It is as if it were him. Muqatil said: She recognized it, but she pretended to them as they pretended to her. If she had been told: Is this your throne, she would have said: Yes. Ikrimah said: She was wise, she said: If I say, ‘It is,’ I fear that I will lie, and if I say, ‘No,’ I fear that I will lie. So she said: It is as if it were him. It was said that Solomon wanted to show her that the jinn were subservient to him. And we were given knowledge before her, and we were Muslims. It was said that this is from the words of Bilqis, meaning we were given knowledge of the truth of Solomon’s prophethood before this sign in the throne, and we were Muslims, disobeying his command. It was said that it is from the words of Solomon, meaning that we were given knowledge of God's power before Bilqis. It was also said that we were given knowledge of her Islam and her willingness to come before her, meaning before her arrival. It was also said that it is from the words of Solomon's people. The second statement is more reliable than the other statements.
27:43: 43- "And what she used to worship besides God prevented her." This is from the words of God, the Most High, explaining what prevented her from manifesting what she claimed of Islam. The agent of "prevented is what she used to worship": that is, what prevented her from manifesting her faith was what she used to worship, which was the sun. An-Nahhas said: that is, what prevented her from worshipping other than God. It was also said that the agent of "prevented" is God: that is, God prevented her from what she used to worship besides Him, so "ma" is in the accusative case. It was also said that the agent was Solomon: that is, and Solomon prevented her from what she used to worship. The first is more appropriate, and the sentence is a new statement as we mentioned. The sentence "Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people" is an explanation of the first sentence: that is, the reason for her delay in worshipping God, and preventing what she used to worship from that is that she was from a people characterized by disbelief. The majority read "indeed" with a kasra. Abu Hayyan read it with a fatha. There are two views on this reading: One is that the sentence is a substitute for what she used to worship. The second is that the interpretation is: because she used to worship, so the letter of explanation was dropped.
27:44: 44- She was told to enter the palace. Abu Ubaidah said: The palace is the palace. Al-Zajjaj said: The palace is the fortress. It is said that this is the palace of Al-Ar and its hall. Ibn Qutaybah said: The palace is a floor made for her from glass and placed water and fish underneath it. Abu Ubaid narrated in Al-Gharib that the sarj is every tall, elevated building, and that the tall, When she saw it, she thought it was a deep sea and uncovered her shins, meaning when she saw the palace in front of her, she thought it was a deep sea, and a deep sea is most of the water, so she uncovered her shins to wade through the water. When she did that, Sulayman said, ‘It is a palace smoothed from glass.’ Al-Murrad is the smoothed, polished one, and from it comes the word Amrad. A man rebels if his beard does not grow, as Al-Farra’ said. And from it comes the tree that has no leaves. Al-Murrad is also the tall one, and from it is said that the fortress is called Marid, and from it comes the saying of the poet: I went early in the morning and found them before noon in the desert. That is, the wide, broad, long shields. When Bilqis heard that, she submitted and surrendered, and said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself,’ that is, by what I was doing in worshipping other than You. It was also said that it was based on the suspicion she had about Solomon, because she thought that he wanted to drown her in the abyss, but the first is more appropriate. And I submitted with Solomon, following him and entering into his religion, to God, Lord of the worlds. She turned from addressing him to the third person. It was said that it was to show her knowledge of God, and it is more appropriate that she turned because of what this noble name indicates of all the names and because it is a name for the Self. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, They denied her throne to her, he said: It was added to and subtracted from because of let us see if she will be guided, he said: so that we may see her mind, and she was found to have firm reason. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement, And We were given knowledge before her, he said: from the words of Sulayman. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, But when she saw him, she thought he was a sea, he said: an ocean. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him in a long narration that Sulayman married her after that. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: What a beautiful hadith. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir after narrating the statement of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah: Rather, it is very strange, and perhaps it is from the delusions of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib regarding Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. What is most likely in such contexts is that it was received from the People of the Book, as found in their scriptures, such as the narrations of Ka’b and Wahb, may God forgive them, regarding what they transmitted to this nation from the Children of Israel of the eternal, strange and wondrous things, what was and what was not, what was distorted, changed and abrogated. This statement of his is a branch of what we have repeated in this interpretation and pointed out in several places, and I thought that no one had pointed it out except me. Praise be to God for agreeing with such a fair-minded hafiz. Al-Bukhari included in his Tarikh and Al-Uqaili on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The first for whom baths were made was Solomon. It was narrated from him with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by another chain of transmission narrated by Al-Tabarani, Ibn ‘Adi in Al-Kamil and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab with the wording: “The first to enter the bathhouse was Solomon. When he experienced its heat, he said: ‘Oh, the punishment of God.’”
27:45: His statement: 45- And We have certainly sent is in apposition to His statement, And We have certainly given David and the lam is the particle that introduces the oath, and this story is part of the explanation of His statement, And indeed, you receive the Qur'an from One Who is Wise and Knowing and righteous is an apposition, and that you worship God is an explanation of the message, and that is the explanatory, and it is permissible for it to be a source: that is, that you worship God, and if in then they are two parties is the suddenness: that is, then they were surprised by the division and the quarrel, and what is meant by the two parties are the believers and the disbelievers among them, and the meaning of the quarrel is that each party disputes over what it has and claims that it is right with it, and it was said that the dispute between them is over whether Saleh was sent or not? And it was said that one of the two parties is Saleh, and the other party is all of his people, and this is weak.
27:46: 46- He said, ‘O my people, why do you hasten the evil before the good?’ That is, Salih said to the disbelieving group among them, denouncing them: Why do you hasten the evil before the good? Mujahid said: The punishment before mercy. The meaning is: Why do you delay the faith that brings you reward and bring forward the disbelief that brings you punishment? And because of their extreme disbelief, they used to say: O Salih, bring us the punishment. “Why do you not ask forgiveness of God?” Why do you not ask forgiveness of God and repent to Him for polytheism? That you may receive mercy? Hoping that you will be shown mercy or so that you may be shown mercy and not be punished? Hastening good is better than hastening evil. And describing punishment as evil is a metaphor, either because punishment is a necessary consequence of it, or because it is similar to it in being disliked.
27:47: So their answer to him after this correct guidance and gentle speech was that they 47- They said, ‘We consider you and those with you to be an ill omen.’ Its root is tatātana, and it has been read as such. Tatātana means pessimism: that is, we consider you and those with you to be an ill omen, who responded to you and entered your religion. This is because a drought struck them, so they considered Salih to be an ill omen. The Arabs were the people who had the most bad omen and the most miserable because of it. When they wanted to travel or do something, they would scare a bird from its nest. If it flew to the right, they would go and do what they had intended to do, but if it flew to the left, they would leave it. So when they said that, Salih said to them, Your bad omen is with God. That is, it is not because of the bird that you consider an ill omen, rather the reason for that is with God, it is what He has decreed for you. The meaning is that the bad omen that has befallen you is from God because of your disbelief. This is like the Almighty’s saying, “They consider Moses and those with him to be an ill omen. Unquestionably, their bad omen is with God.” Then He explained to them the reason for what they were in with the clearest statement. He said: Rather, you are a people who are being tested, meaning you are being tried and examined. It was also said that you are being tormented for your sins. It was also said that others tempt you, and it was also said that Satan tempts you with what you fall into of superstition or what you are superstitious for. So he turned away from mentioning the bird to what is the reason that calls for it.
27:48: 48- “And there were in the city” which is in Salih, which is the stone, nine men meaning nine men from the sons of the nobles, and the group is the name of the group, so it is as if they were leaders, each one of whom had a group following him, and the plural is group and groups, and these nine are the companions of Qadar, the barren she-camel, then he described these by saying: They cause corruption in the land and do not reform meaning their affair and their work is corruption in the land that is not mixed with reform, and there is much disagreement regarding the names of these nine, there is no need to prolong the mention of it.
27:49: 49- “They said, ‘Swear by God.’” That is, some of them said to each other, Swear by God. This is on the basis that swear by God is an imperative verb, and it is possible that it is a past tense verb explaining they said, as if what they said was said. He said, They divided, or it could be a state of the omission of had, meaning they said that dividing. Ibn Mas’ud read, They corrupt the earth and do not reform. They divided by God, and there is no word in it. The lam in We will surely come to him and his family is the answer to the oath: meaning, we will come to him suddenly at the time of the night, and kill him and his family. Then we will surely say to his heir. The majority read with the nun for the speaker in We will surely spend the night and in We will surely say. Abu Hatim chose this reading, and Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read with the fa in both of them, as if they were addressing each other. Abu Ubaid chose this reading, and Mujahid and Hamid read with the da in both of them. What is meant by the heir of Salih is his people. We did not witness the destruction of his family, meaning, we did not attend their killing, and we do not know who killed him or killed his family. Their denial of their witnessing the place of destruction indicates the denial of their witnessing the killing itself, a fortiori. It was said that muhlak means destruction, and Hafs and Al-Sulami read muhlak with the mim and lam open. Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read with the mim open and the kasra broken. The lam and we are truthful in what we said. Al-Zajjaj said: These people had made an alliance to spend the night with Salih and his family, then deny to his friends that they had not done that or seen him. This was a plot on their part.
27:50: That is why God Almighty said 50- “And they planned a plan,” meaning with this alliance, and We planned a plan, We punished them for their actions and destroyed them, while they did not perceive God’s plan against them.
27:51: 51- “Then see how was the outcome of their plot.” That is, see what happened to their affair, which they built on plotting, and what befell them because of it. Indeed, We destroyed them and their people, all together. The majority of scholars read the word with a kasra over the hamza of inna. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Al-A’mash, Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Asim read it with a fatha. Whoever reads it with a kasra makes it a new sentence. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads it with a kasra starts a new sentence, and explains what came before it, as if he made it dependent on the outcome, as if he said: The outcome is that We destroyed them. According to the fatha reading, the interpretation would be that We destroyed them or because We destroyed them. Kan is complete and Aqib is its subject, or it could be a substitute for Aqib, or it could be the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, We destroyed them. It is permissible for Kan to be incomplete and kaif to be its predicate, or it could be that its predicate is I destroyed. Abu Hatim said: In the letter of Abi it is that We destroyed them. The meaning of the verse is that God destroyed the nine groups mentioned, and destroyed their people who were not with them when they committed this. The meaning of the emphasis on all of them is that not one of them was excluded, and not one of them was spared from punishment.
27:52: Sentence 52- those are their houses empty confirms what preceded it. The majority read khawiya in the accusative case as a state. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, look at their houses as they are empty. Al-Farra' and An-Nahhas said the same: that is, empty of their people, ruined, with no inhabitants in them. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Ubaidah said: Khawiya is in the accusative case as a severance, and the original is those are their houses empty. When the alif and lam were cut off from it, it was made accusative like his saying: And to Him is the religion, complete. Asim bin Umar, Nasr bin Asim, Al-Jahdary, and Isa bin Umar read it in the nominative case as the predicate of the demonstrative pronoun, and their houses are a substitute, or an apposition, or the predicate of the demonstrative pronoun, and khawiya is another predicate. The ba' in because of what they wronged is for causality: that is, because of their wrongdoing. Indeed in that the destruction and rehabilitation is a sign a great for a people who know that is, who are characterized by knowledge of things.
27:53: 53- “And We saved those who believed” - and they are Salih and those who believed in him - and were fearful of God and dreaded His punishment. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Your bird, meaning your misfortunes. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, And there were in the city nine men, saying, “They are the ones who hamstrung the she-camel and said when they hamstrung it: ‘Let us spend the night with Salih and his family.’ So we carried them off, and then we said to the followers of Salih: ‘We did not witness any of this and we have no knowledge of it.’ So God destroyed them all.”
27:54: Lot is in the accusative case: by an implied verb conjoined with We sent: meaning, We sent Lot, and 54- when he said is an adverbial phrase for the implied verb, and it is permissible to imply mention, and the meaning is: and We sent Lot at the time of his saying: to his people, do you commit immorality? meaning the act of extreme ugliness and heinousness, and they are the people of Sodom, and the phrase and you are seeing is in the accusative case as a state, including an emphasis of denial: meaning, and you know that it is an immorality. And that is greater for your sins, on the basis that you see with the sight of the heart, which is knowledge, or in the sense of looking, because they did not conceal themselves when committing the immorality out of transgression and rebellion, and the explanation of this story has been presented in full in Al-A'raf.
27:55: 55- Do you indeed approach men with desire? This is a repetition of the rebuke, while stating that this indecency is sodomy. The word desire is in the accusative case as a reason: meaning for desire, or as a description of a deleted source: meaning coming with desire, or as a condition: meaning desiring them without women meaning going beyond women who are the subject of that. Rather, you are a people who are ignorant of the prohibition or punishment for this sin. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh chose to lighten the hamza of that you aankum.
27:56: 56- “And the only answer of his people was that they said, ‘Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure.’” The majority of scholars read the answer in the accusative case as the predicate of kana, and its subject is except that they said, meaning, except for their saying. Ibn Abi Ishaq read the answer in the nominative case as the subject of kana, and its predicate is what follows it. Then they explained what they ordered each other to do of expelling by saying, Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure, meaning, they keep away from the backsides of men. They said that as a mockery of them.
27:57: So We saved him and his family from the punishment, "except for his wife. We destined her to be among those who remained behind." That is, We destined her to be among those who remained in the punishment. The meaning of We destined is We decided. The majority of scholars read We destined with a shaddah, while Asim read it with a tafsir. The meaning is the same, although the additional construction indicates an additional meaning.
27:58: 58- And We rained down upon them a rain. This emphasis indicates the intensity of the rain and that it is unusual. So evil was the rain of those who were warned. The specific word for blame is omitted: that is, evil was the rain of those who were warned. What is meant by those who were warned are those who were warned but did not accept it. All of this has been explained in Al-A’raf and Ash-Shu’ara.
27:59: 59- “Say: Praise be to God, and peace be upon His servants.” Al-Farra’ said: The scholars of semantics said: It was said to Lot: Say: Praise be to God for their destruction. A group disagreed with him and said: This is addressed to our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. That is, it was said: Praise be to God for the destruction of the disbelievers of the past nations, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen. An-Nahhas said: This is more appropriate because the Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and everything in it is addressed to him except what its meaning is not valid except for others. It was said that what is meant by His servants whom He has chosen is the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. It is better to interpret it in a general way, so that it includes the prophets and their followers. Is God better or what they associate? That is, God, whose actions and attributes have been mentioned, which indicate His great power, is better or what they associate with Him from idols. This goodness is not in its original meaning, but rather it is like the saying of the poet: I satirize him, but I am not his equal. May God sacrifice my life for you both. So what is in the verse is a mockery of them, as there is no good in them at all. Sibawayh narrated that the Arabs say: Happiness is more beloved to you than misery, but there is no good in misery at all. It was said that the meaning is: Are the rewards of God better, or the punishment of what you associate with Him? It was also said that he said that to them in accordance with their belief, because they believed that there was good in worshipping idols. It was also said that what is meant by this question is the report. The majority read associate with the superlative before the address, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. Abu Amr, Asim, and Ya'qub read associate with the subjunctive, and the am in ama yashrikun is the attached one.
27:60: 60- "From the One who created the heavens and the earth" is the disconnected one. Abu Hatim said: Its meaning is: Are your gods better, or is He who created the heavens and the earth and was able to create them? It was also said that the meaning is: Is the worship of your idols better, or the worship of He who created the heavens and the earth? So, in this case, "am" is connected and contains the meaning of rebuke and mockery as in the first sentence. Al-A'mash read "amn with a lightened meem, And sent down for you from the sky water meaning a type of water, which is rain, And We caused to grow thereby gardens" the plural of garden. Al-Farra' said: A garden is an orchard that has a wall around it. If there is no wall around it, then it is an orchard and not a garden. Qatada and Ikrimah said: Gardens are palm trees "of delight" meaning of beauty and splendor. And joy: is the beauty that delights whoever sees it, and He did not say those with joy in the plural, and the meaning of this negation is prohibition, and the meaning of doing this: that is, it was not for humans, nor is it possible for them to do that, nor is it within their ability due to their inability to bring something from nonexistence into existence. Then the Almighty said, rebuking and censuring them, Is there a god with God? That is, is there a deity with God, who has previously done some of these actions, such that He would be paired with Him and made a partner with Him in worship? And it was read Is there a god with God in the accusative case, estimating: Do you call upon a god? Then He turned away from rebuking and rebuking them with what was mentioned above and moved to explaining their bad state, while shifting from direct address to the third person, so He said, Rather, they are a people who equate others with God, that is, they equate others with God, or they deviate from the truth to falsehood. Then He began to provide evidence from the conditions of the earth and what is on it.
27:61: He said: 61- Is He Who has made the earth a resting place? The settled resting place: that is, He spread it out and leveled it so that it is possible to settle on it. It was said that this sentence and the three sentences following it are a substitute for His statement, Is He Who created the heavens and the earth? There is no recourse to that, rather it and what follows it are a diversion and a transition from the rebuke and reprimand with what came before it to the rebuke and reprimand with something else. And made within them rivers. Al-Khalal: the middle.
