Its investigation has already been presented in His statement, And We caused a river to gush forth within them, "And placed for them firm mountains," that is, fixed mountains that hold them up and prevent them from moving. "And placed between the two seas a barrier." The barrier: the preventer: that is, He placed between the two seas, by His power, a barrier. The two seas are the fresh and the salty, so one does not mix with the other, neither one changes the other, nor does the other enter into this. Its explanation has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Furqan. "Is there a god with God?" That is, if it is proven that no one has the power to do that except God, then is there a god in existence who makes what He makes and creates His creation? How can they associate with Him what neither harms nor benefits? But most of them do not know the Oneness of their Lord and the power of His might.
27:62: 62- Is there anyone who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him? This is an indication from Him, glory be to Him, of the need of man in general. The distressed is a passive participle from the verb to be forced, which means someone who is distressed and exhausted and has no power or strength. It has also been said that it refers to the sinner, or it has been said that it refers to the one who has been afflicted by hardship, such as poverty or illness, which has forced him to supplicate to God. The lam in the word al-Muddhir is for the genus, not for exhaustiveness. The supplication of some of those in need may not be answered due to an obstacle that prevents that because of something that the servant creates that prevents him from having his supplication answered. Otherwise, God, the Exalted, has guaranteed that the supplication of the one in need will be answered if he calls upon Him, and He has informed us of that about Himself. The reason for answering the supplication of the one in need is that the compulsion that occurs to him results in sincerity and shunning all else but God. God, the Exalted, has informed us that He answers the supplication of those who are sincere in their religion to Him, even if they are disbelievers. He said: “Until, when you were in the ships and they sailed with them with a good wind and they rejoiced in it, there came a stormy wind and the waves came upon them from every side and they thought that they were surrounded, they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion, ‘If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful. ’” And He said: But when He delivered them to the land, at once they associated others with Him. So He answered them when they were in need and sincere, even though He knew that they would return to their polytheism. And remove the evil, meaning that which harms the servant, without specifying. It was said that it is harm, and it was said that it is injustice. And make you successors on the earth. "That is, each generation among you will be succeeded by the generation before it after their extinction. The meaning is: He will destroy a generation and create others. It was also said that He will make your children succeed you, and it was also said that He will make the Muslims succeed the unbelievers, settling in their land and dwellings. "Is there a god with God who gives you these great blessings? You remember little." That is, you remember little. The majority read it with the superlative as an address. Abu Amr, Hisham, and Ya'qub read it with the subjunctive as a statement in response to his statement: "Rather, most of them do not know." Abu Hatim chose this reading.
27:63: 63- Who guides you through the darkness of the land and sea? That is, who guides you during the dark nights when you travel by land or sea. It was said that what is meant is the deserts of the land that have no landmarks and the depths of the seas, and He likened them to darkness because of the lack of guidance therein. And who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? What is meant by mercy here is the rain: that is, He sends the winds before the rain, and before it falls. Is there a deity with God? Who does that and brings it into existence. Exalted is God above what they associate with Him. That is, He is pure and sanctified from the existence of anything that they associate with Him.
27:64: 64- Is He who begins creation and then repeats it? They used to acknowledge that God Almighty is the Creator, so He obligated them to repeat it: meaning if He is able to begin, He is able to repeat it. And who provides for you from the sky and the earth with rain and plants: meaning is He better, or what you make a partner with Him who is not able to do any of that? Is there a god with God so that you make Him a partner with Him. Say, 'Produce your proof, if you should be truthful' meaning your argument that God Almighty has a partner, or bring your argument that there is a Maker who makes as He makes, and in this there is a rebuke and mockery of them.
27:65: 65- Say, ‘None in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except God.’ That is, none of the creatures in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen, the knowledge of which God has kept to Himself. The exception in His saying, except God, is disjunctive: that is, but God knows that. The raising of what comes after except with the exception being disjunctive is according to the Tamimi language, as in their saying: Except for the jackals and the camels It was said that the agent of ya’lam is ma after illa, and min fi al-samaw is its object, and al-ghayb is a substitute for min. Al-Zajjaj said: Except God is a substitute for min. Al-Farra’ said: Ma after illa is raised because what comes after it is a predicate, like their saying No one has gone except your father, which is like what al-Zajjaj said. Al-Zajjaj said: “And whoever puts the accusative in the accusative case is an exception. “And they do not feel when they will be resurrected,” meaning they do not feel when they will be raised from the graves. Ayyan is composed of ayn and in. Its explanation has already been given, and the pronoun refers to the disbelievers. Al-Sulami read ayyan with a kasra over the hamza, which is the language of Banu Salim, and it is in the accusative case with yabay’thun and attached to yasha’run, so it and what comes after it are in the accusative case by removing the preposition: meaning they do not feel when they will be resurrected, and the meaning of ayyan is the meaning of when.
27:66: 66- Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter. The majority of scholars read it as idarakka translated as adarak. The root of idarakka is tadrak translated as to overtake, the ta' was assimilated into the dal, and a hamzat al-wasl was added to enable the beginning with a consonant. Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Hamid read bal idrak from idrak. Ata' ibn Yasar, Sulayman ibn Yasar, and al-A'mash read bal idrak with a fatha on the lam of bal and a shaddah on the dal. Ibn Muhaisin read bal idrak as a question. Ibn Abbas, Abu Raja', Shaibah, al-A'mash, and al-A'raj read bala adarak by adding the ya' to bal and a hamzat al-qata' translated as to overtake and a shaddah on the dal. Abu Bakr read bal tadarak translated as to overtake, and the meaning of the verse is: Rather, their knowledge will be perfected in the Hereafter, because they will see and witness everything they were promised. It was also said that it means: Their knowledge will continue in the Hereafter, and the second reading means all of their knowledge will be in the Hereafter with witnessing, and that will be when knowledge will not benefit them, because they were deniers in this world. Al-Zajjaj said: It means denial, and he provided evidence for that with his statement later: Rather, they are blind to it, meaning their knowledge did not reach the knowledge of the Hereafter. It was said that the meaning is: Rather, their knowledge of the Hereafter has gone astray and is absent, so they have no knowledge. The meaning of the third reading is like the meaning of the first reading, so ifta’ala and tafa’ala may come for one meaning, and the fourth reading is in the meaning of denial. Al-Farra' said: "This is a good interpretation, as if he directed it to the deniers as a way of mocking them. There are other readings in the verse that should not be occupied with mentioning and explaining them. "Rather, they are in doubt about it," meaning, they are today in doubt in this world about the Hereafter. Then he turned away from that to what is more severe, saying: "Rather, they are blind to it," so they do not perceive any of its evidence due to the disorder in their insight by which perception occurs. Blind is the plural of "Amm," which is someone who is blind of heart. The intention is to explain their ignorance of it to the point that they are not guided to anything that leads to knowledge of it. So whoever says that the meaning of the first verse, I mean, "Rather, their knowledge will be realized in the Hereafter, is that their knowledge will be perfected and completed with seeing it, then his statement, Rather, they are in doubt," etc. must be interpreted as referring to what they were doing in this world. Whoever says that the meaning of the first verse is to mock them and rebuke them, does not need to restrict his statement, "Rather, they are in doubt," etc., to what they were doing in this world. Thus, the meaning of these verses becomes clear and evident." Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, “And peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen,” that he said: They are the Companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom God chose for His Prophet. A similar narration was narrated on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri. The generalization we have already mentioned is preferable, so the Companions of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are included in this primarily. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, An-Nasa’i and At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of a man from Baljum who said: “I said, ‘O Messenger of God, what do you call upon?’ He said: ‘Call upon God alone, for if harm afflicts you and you call upon Him, He will remove it from you.’” This is part of a longer hadith. Ahmad narrated it from another chain of transmission, in which he named the Companion and said: ‘Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, Ubayd ibn Ubaydah Al-Hujaymi narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Tamimah Al-Hujaymi, on the authority of Jabir ibn Salim Al-Hujaymi. This hadith has chains of transmission according to Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Aisha that she said: “There are three, whoever speaks of one of them has greatly slandered God. God the Almighty says: ‘Say, “None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except God.”’” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter. He said: When knowledge will be of no benefit. Abu Ubaid narrated in his Fada’il, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humaid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him that he recited, Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter. He said: He did not overtake their knowledge. Abu Ubaid said: He meant that he recited it as a question. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter. He said: Their knowledge will be hidden.
27:67: When the Almighty mentioned that the doubters are in doubt about the resurrection and that they are blind to considering its evidence, He wanted to clarify the extent of their doubt, which is merely the exclusion of reviving the dead after they have become dust, so He said: 67- And those who disbelieve say, ‘When we have become dust and our fathers, will we indeed be brought forth?’ The factor in if is omitted, and is indicated by mukhrijun those who will be brought forth, meaning will we be resurrected or brought forth if we are. The reason for it not being acted upon is because the interrogative hamza and the lam of initiation are in between them. Abu Amr recited with two interrogatives, except that he lightened the hamza. Asim and Hamza recited with two interrogatives, except that they pronounced both hamzas with emphasis. Nafi` read it with a hamza, and Ibn `Amir, Warsh, and Ya`qub read `Idhā with two hamzas, and inna with two noons as a statement. Abu `Ubaid preferred Nafi`’s reading and responded to those who combined two interrogative pronouns. The meaning of the verse is that they were astonished and thought it unlikely that they would emerge from their graves alive after they had turned to dust.
27:68: Then they confirmed this exclusion with what is a denial of the resurrection, so they said: This has been promised to us meaning the resurrection we and our fathers before meaning before Muhammad’s promise to us, and the sentence is a new sentence introduced to confirm the denial, beginning with an oath to increase the confirmation This the promise of the resurrection is nothing but legends of the ancients their fabricated hadiths and lies, and the meaning of legends has been explained in Surat Al-Mu’minun. Then the Almighty threatened them with not accepting what the prophets brought of report of the resurrection, so He ordered them to look into the conditions of the previous nations that denied the prophets and what they were punished with and what their end was.
27:69: He said: 69- Say, ‘Travel through the land and observe what was the end of those who denied the messengers.’ With what the prophets brought of report of the resurrection, the meaning of observing is seeing their traces with the eyes, for in observing there is an increase in consideration. It was said that the meaning is: So look with your hearts and your insights at what was the end of those who denied their messengers, and the first is more appropriate for their command to travel through the land.
27:70: 70- And do not grieve over them for their persistence in disbelief. And do not be in distress. Distress means embarrassment. It is said that something became narrow, with the kasra, and it was read with both of them. They are two languages. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: It is said that someone has distress and constriction in his chest, which means that the chests are constricted by it. The interpretation of this verse was presented at the end of Surat An-Nahl.
27:71: 71- And they say, ‘When will this promise come to pass?’ That is, the punishment with which you promise us, if you should be truthful in that.
27:72: 72- “Say: Perhaps there will be a punishment behind you.” It is said that you rode behind a man and rode him if you rode behind him, and that you followed him if you followed him and came in his footsteps. The meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, to these unbelievers, perhaps this punishment that you are promised will follow you and catch up with you. So the lam is redundant for emphasis, or in the sense that it has come close to you and drawn near to you, so it is not redundant. Ibn Shajarah said: The meaning of radfa lakum is taba’akum. He said: And from this is the woman’s radfa, because it follows her from behind, and from this is the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb: The blackness has returned to whiteness in his partings. No welcome to the whiteness of gray hair when it follows. Al-Jawhari said: And he rode behind him is a linguistic term for he rode behind him, just as he followed him and he followed him have the same meaning. Khuzaymah ibn Malik ibn Nahd said: If Gemini follows the Pleiades, I will have bad thoughts about the family of Fatima. Al-Farra’ said: Radfa lakum means came near to you, and that is why it was said lakum. Al-A’raj read radfa lakum with a fatha on the dal, which is a dialect, and the kasra is more common. Ibn Abbas read azfa lakum and arafa’ “some of which you are hastening” meaning that he is the subject of radfa, and what is meant is some of the punishment that you are hastening meaning that it may have drawn near and had drawn near. It was said that it refers to their punishment by being killed on the day of Badr, and it was also said that it refers to the punishment of the grave.
27:73: Then the Almighty mentioned His favor in delaying the punishment, saying: 73- And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty to mankind in delaying the punishment. It is better to understand the verse in general terms, and to have the delay of the punishment included among His favors and blessings, but most of them are not grateful for His favor and blessings, and they do not recognize the right of His benevolence. Then He explained that He is aware of what is in their hearts.
27:74: He said: 74- And indeed, your Lord knows what their hearts conceal meaning what they hide. The majority read it with a damma on the ta’ from akana. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn al-Samifa’ and Hamid read it with a fatha on the ta’ and a damma on the kaf. It is said kanannatuhu meaning I concealed him and his trace was hidden. And what they declare means what they reveal of their words and actions.
27:75: 75- And there is nothing hidden in the heaven or earth except that it is in a clear book. The commentators said: There is nothing hidden or hidden from creation in the heaven or earth except that it is in a clear book, except that it is made clear in the Preserved Tablet. Ghayyat is one of the attributes, and the ta’ is for emphasis. Al-Hasan said: Ghayyat here is the Resurrection. Muqatil said: He knows what they are hastening of the punishment, and it is clear to God, even if it is hidden from creation. Ibn Shajarah said: “Ghayyat here is everything that God has concealed from His creation and hidden from them, and it is made clear in the Mother of the Book. So how could any of that be hidden from Him, and among that is what they is hastening before its appointed time?”
27:76: 76- Indeed, this Qur’an narrates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ. This is because the People of the Book were divided and formed into parties, some of them slandering others and some of them disowning others. So the Qur’an was revealed clarifying the truth over which they differed. If they had taken it, they would have found in it what would remove their differences and prevent their division.
27:77: 77- And indeed, it is guidance and mercy for the believers. That is, the Qur’an is guidance and mercy for those who believe in God and follow His Messenger. He singled out the believers because they are the ones who benefit from it, and among them are those who believed from the Children of Israel.
27:78: 78- Indeed, your Lord will judge between them with His judgment. That is, He will judge between the disputing parties among the Children of Israel according to what He rules in truth, rewarding those who are right and punishing those who are wrong. It was also said that He will judge between them in this world and reveal what they had distorted. The majority of scholars read it as bi-hukmihi with a damma on the ha' and a sukoon on the kaf. Janah read it with a kasra on it and a fatha on the kaf, the plural of hikmah. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. The Exalted in Might Who cannot be defeated, and the Knowing of what He rules, or the One with abundant knowledge.
27:79: Then the Almighty commanded him to put his trust in God and not to be concerned, saying: 79- So put your trust in God. The fa indicates the order of the matter as mentioned above, and the meaning is: Entrust your matter to Him and rely on Him, for He is your supporter. Then He gave two reasons for that: The first is His saying: Indeed, you are upon the clear truth, meaning the apparent, and it was said the manifest.
27:80: The second reason is his statement: 80- You cannot make the dead hear because if it is known that their state is like the state of the dead in that hearing is useless, or like the state of the deaf who do not hear, understand, or find guidance, this becomes a strong reason for not attacking them. He likened the disbelievers to the dead who have no sense or mind, and to the deaf who do not hear admonitions or respond to supplications to God. Then he mentioned a sentence to complete and emphasize the simile, saying: When they turn their backs meaning when they completely turn away from the truth. The deaf person does not hear supplication when he is facing it, so how about when he is turning away from it, turning his back and retreating. The apparent meaning of denying the dead hearing is general, so only what is mentioned with evidence is specific to it, as is proven in the Sahih that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) addressed those killed in the well of Badr, and it was said to him, O Messenger of God, only bodies with souls speak. Likewise, what was mentioned that the dead hear the flapping of the sandals of those who are mourning him when they depart. Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Abi Ishaq readل َذميغعwith a fatha on the taa' and a fatha on the meem, and its subject is the deaf. The rest readتَميمwith a damma on the taa' and a kasra on the meem from asma'. Qatada said: When the deaf person turns his back and you call him, he does not hear. The same is true for the unbeliever, he does not hear what he is called to of faith.
27:81: Then He struck the blind man as an example for them, saying: 81- And you cannot guide the blind from their misguidance meaning, you cannot guide the one whom God has blinded from the truth, guiding him to what is required of him, which is faith, and that is not within your power. Similar to this is His statement: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love. The majority of scholars read it by adding Hadi to Al-Ammi. Yahya bin Al-Harith and Abu Hayyan read Bahād Al-Ammi with the tanween Hād. Hamzah read tahdī as a present tense verb. In the wording of Abdullah, And you cannot guide the blind "You only hear those who believe in Our verses" meaning, you only hear those who believe, not those who disbelieve. What is meant by those who believe in the verses is those who believe in the Quran, and the phrase "they are Muslims" is an explanation of faith: meaning, they are sincere and devoted opponents. Then He threatened the servants by mentioning some of the signs of the Hour and its horrors.
27:82: He said: 82- And when the word falls upon them. There is disagreement about the meaning of the statement being made against them. Qatada said: Wrath is obligatory upon them. Mujahid said: The statement is due upon them that they do not believe. It is also said that the punishment is due upon them, and it is also said that wrath is obligatory, and the meanings are close. It is also said that what is meant by the statement is what the Qur’an has spoken about the coming of the Hour and the various horrors it contains that they were hastening. It is also said that the statement is due to the death of the scholars and the loss of knowledge. It is also said that it is if they do not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. The gist of the meaning of occurred is obligatory, and what is meant by the statement is its content, or the infinitive is used for the object: that is, what is said, and the answer to the condition is We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them. There are different opinions about this beast. Some say it is a righteous young camel that will emerge near the Day of Resurrection and will be one of the portents of the Last Hour. Others say it is a hairy beast with long legs called Al-Jassasah. Others say it is a beast in the form of human beings that is in the clouds with its legs on the ground. Others say its head is the head of a bull, its eye the eye of a pig, its ear the ear of an elephant, its horn the horn of a deer, its neck the neck of an ostrich, its chest the chest of a lion, its color the color of a tiger, its flank the flank of a cat, its tail the tail of a ram, its legs the legs of a camel, and between each joint there are twelve cubits. Others say it is the snake overlooking the wall of the Kaaba that was uprooted by an eagle when the Quraysh wanted to rebuild the Kaaba. What is meant is that it is the one that will emerge at the end of time. Others say it is a tailless beast with a beard. Others say it is a speaking human who debates the heretics and argues with the infidels. Others say other things that there is no point in going into detail about. Al-Qurtubi preferred the first opinion in his commentary. There is a difference of opinion about the place from which it will emerge. Some say it will emerge from Mount Safa in Mecca, and some say it will emerge from Mount Abu Qubais. It is also said that it will emerge three times: an emergence in some of the deserts until people fight over it and much blood is shed, then it will lie in wait. It will emerge in the villages, then emerge from the greatest, most honorable and most noble of mosques. It is also said that it will emerge from between the corner and the station. It is also said that it will emerge in Tihamah. It is also said that it will emerge from the mosque of Kufa from where the oven bubbled. It is also said that it will emerge from the land of Taif. It is also said that it will emerge from a rock in the valley of Ajyad, and it is also said that it will emerge from a crack in the Kaaba. There is a difference of opinion about the meaning of His statement talk to them. Some say: He spoke to them about the invalidity of religions other than the religion of Islam. Others say: He spoke to them with what would upset them. Others say: He spoke to them with the words of God the Almighty: That people were not certain of Our signs, meaning of their coming out, because their coming out is one of the signs. The majority read talk to them from talking. This is indicated by the reading of Abu Tanbi’hum. Ibn Abbas, Abu Zur’ah, Abu Raja’ and Al-Hasan read: talk to them with a fatha on the first letter and a sukoon on the kaf from kalam, which means wounding. Ikrimah said: That is, you brand them with a branding. Others say: You wound them. Others say: The reading of the majority is taken from kalam with a fatha on the kaf and a sukoon on the lam, which means wounding, and the emphasis is for emphasis, as Abu Hatim said. The majority read: That people were not certain of Our signs, with a kasra on in as a new sentence. The Kufians and Ibn Abi Ishaq read an with a fatha. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning according to the fatha reading is that the people. Ibn Mas’ud also read that people with a ba’. Abu Ubaid said: Its position is in the accusative case because the verb falls upon it, meaning that it informs them that the people. According to this reading, what the people spoke about is His statement: that the people were not certain of Our signs, as we have previously indicated. As for the kasr reading, the sentence is a new sentence, as we have previously stated, and it is not from the speech of the beast. A group of commentators have stated this explicitly, and Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ were certain of it. Al-Akhfash said: The kasr of in is on the assumption of the statement, meaning that it tells them that the people, etc. So the meaning of the first reading, according to this, returns to the meaning of the second reading. What is meant by people in the verse is: people in general, so it includes every accountable person. It was said that what is meant is the disbelievers specifically, and it was said that it is the disbelievers of Mecca, but the first is more appropriate. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, Perhaps there will be a successor to you, he said: Come closer to you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, And indeed, your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare, he said: He knows what they did during the night and the day. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, And there is nothing hidden, the verse, meaning: There is nothing in the heavens or the earth, secret or public, but He knows it. Ibn Al-Mubarak in Az-Zuhd, Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Nu’aym Ibn Hammad, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, regarding the verse, And when the word comes to pass against them, he said: If they do not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on his authority, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah that he interpreted and the word comes to pass against them as meaning what was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, {A creature from the earth will speak to them}, that he said: It talks to them. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: Its speech informs them that people were not certain of Our signs. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Dawud Nafi’ al-Ama, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His statement, {It will speak to them}, meaning is it from speaking with the tongue or from speaking, which is wounding? He said: By God, it does all of that. It speaks to the believer and speaks to the disbeliever, meaning it wounds him. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, regarding the verse, that he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “That is not speech or talk, but it is a mark that marks whomever God has commanded it to do. So its exit from al-Safa will be on the night of Mina, and they will be between its head and its tail, neither one can push it aside nor one can wound it. Then, when it has finished what God has commanded it to do, those who are destroyed will perish and those who are saved will be saved. The first step it takes will be in Antioch.” Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The beast has fur and feathers of all colors, and it has four legs that emerge from the heel of the pilgrims. Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Umamah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The beast will emerge and be branded on their snouts, then they will live among you until a man buys the beast and it will be said to him, ‘From whom did you buy it?’ He will say, ‘From the man with the snout.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that the beast will emerge three times, and he mentioned something similar to what we mentioned. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Hudhayfah ibn Asid that he said: The beast will emerge from one of the most sacred mosques. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Nu’aym ibn Hammad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: It will emerge from one of the valleys of Tihamah. At-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Nu’aym ibn Hammad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: It will emerge from one of the valleys of Tihamah. Al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Nu'aym ibn Hammad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba'th narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The Beast of the Earth will emerge, carrying with it the staff of Moses and the ring of Solomon. It will polish the face of the believer with the ring and cut off the nose of the disbeliever with the staff, until the people gather at the table and the believer will be known from the disbeliever." Al-Tayalisi, Nu'aym ibn Hammad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba'th narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid Al-Ghifari who said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned the Beast and said: 'It will emerge three times during this world.'" He mentioned something similar to what we mentioned in a long hadith. There are many hadiths about its description, the place where it emerges, what it will do, and when it emerges, some of which are sahih, some hasan, and some da'if. As for its emergence and its being one of the signs of the Hour, the hadiths that have been narrated concerning that are sahih. And among them is what is proven in Sahih, such as the hadith of Hudhayfah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, The Hour will not come until you see ten signs, and he mentioned among them the Beast, as it is in Sahih Muslim and in the Four Sunans. And like the hadith, Hasten to do good deeds before the sun rises from the west, the Antichrist, and the Beast, as it is also in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, and like the hadith of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, The first of the signs to appear will be the rising of the sun from the west, and the emergence of the Beast among the people at noon, as it is also in Sahih Muslim.
27:83: Then the Almighty mentioned a general aspect of the horrors of the Day of Resurrection, saying: 83- And the Day We shall gather from every nation a company. The agent in the adverbial phrase is an omitted verb addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and gathering is the plural. It was said that what is meant by this gathering is the gathering of the torment after the comprehensive gathering that includes all creation. Min is for the beginning of the goal, and Fuj is the group like the group, and Min in of those who deny Our signs is explanatory. So they will be distributed meaning the first of them will be detained by the last of them, and its full investigation was presented in this surah. It was said that its meaning is: they will be pushed, and from this is the saying of Al-Shamakh: We distributed his name from five legions The meaning of the verse: And remember, O Muhammad, the Day when We will gather from every nation a group who denied Our signs. At that gathering, the first of them will be returned to the last of them or they will be driven away. That is, remind them of this or explain it to them as a warning and intimidation to them.
27:84: 84- Until, when they come to the place of reckoning, God will say to them, as a rebuke and a reprimand, Did you deny My signs that I sent down to My messengers, and commanded them to convey them to you, while the fact is that you did not encompass them with knowledge, but rather you denied them from the beginning, ignorant of them, not looking into them or proving their validity or invalidity, out of rebellion, stubbornness, and audacity towards God and His messengers. In this there is more rebuke and reprimand, because whoever denies something without encompassing knowledge of it has lied in his denial, and has called himself ignorant, unfair, misunderstood, and deficient in perception. This is similar to someone who has taken it upon himself to criticize a science of the religious sciences, or to criticize a science that is an introduction to them, and a means by which one can reach them, and that provides increased insight into their knowledge, and understanding of their meanings, like the sciences of the Arabic language as a whole, and they are twelve sciences, and the science of the principles of jurisprudence, because by it one can reach the deduction of…” The legal rulings on their detailed evidence, while including an explanation of the general rules of language, and so is every science that has further benefit in understanding the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, then he has called out against himself in the loudest voice that he is an ignorant, arguing with falsehood, attacking the legal sciences, deserving of a severe punishment that will deter him from his ignorance, misguidance, and attacking what he does not know, is not aware of, and does not comprehend the essence of, so that he will become a lesson to others, and an admonition from which those like him, the weak-minded, the weak-religious, and the rabble who falsely and mendaciously claim knowledge, will learn. And in His statement: What were you doing? it is the disconnected particle, and the meaning is: Or what were you doing that distracted you from looking into it and contemplating its meanings? This question is by way of rebuking them.
27:85: 85- And the word will be fulfilled upon them has been explained previously. The ba in because of what they did wrong is for causality: meaning, the word was fulfilled upon them because of the wrong, the worst kind of which is associating partners with God. So they will not speak when the word will be fulfilled upon them: meaning, they will have no excuse to speak, or they will not be able to speak because of the great terror they will see. Most of the commentators said: Their mouths will be sealed so they will not speak. Then, after frightening them with the horrors of the Day of Resurrection, the Almighty mentioned what could be evidence of monotheism, the gathering, and prophethood, as an exaggeration of guidance and a demonstration of the excuse.
27:86: He said: 86- Have they not seen that We have made the night for them to rest therein and the day to see? That is, We made the night for rest, stability, and sleep, because of the darkness in it, for they do not strive for a livelihood therein, and the day to see so that they may see what they strive for of the livelihood that they need. The description of the day as seeing is a description of people to exaggerate its illumination as if it sees what is in it. It was said that there was an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: And We made the night dark so that they may rest, and dark was omitted because of the indication of seeing it, and its investigation was presented previously in Al-Isra and in Yunus. Indeed in that mentioned are signs meaning signs and indications for a people who believe in God, the Most High. Then He, the Most High, mentioned another sign of the Resurrection, saying: And the Day the Trumpet is blown is in apposition to And the Day We are gathered and is accusative with its previous accusative. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is: And that is the Day the Trumpet is blown, and the first is more appropriate. The images: a horn that Israfil will blow, and its investigation was presented in Al-Isra and Yunus. Indeed in that mentioned are signs meaning signs and indications for a people who believe in God Almighty.
27:87: Then the Almighty mentioned another sign of the Resurrection, saying: 87- And the Day the Trumpet is blown is in apposition to And the Day We are gathered and is in the accusative case with its previous accusative. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is: And that is the Day the Trumpet is blown, and the first is more appropriate. The Trumpet is a horn into which Israfil will blow, and we have already discussed it in detail in Al-An'am. The Trumpet will be blown three times: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of unconsciousness, and the third is the blast of resurrection. It was said that there will be two blasts, and that the blast of terror may refer either to the blast of unconsciousness or to the blast of resurrection. This was the opinion of Al-Qushayri, Al-Qurtubi, and others. Al-Mawardi said: This blast mentioned here is on the Day of Resurrection from the graves, So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, meaning they will be afraid and disturbed by the intensity of what they heard. It was said that what is meant by fright here is: hastening and responding to the call, as in their saying I hastened to respond to you, but the first meaning is more appropriate for the verse. The past tense was expressed in conjunction with a present tense verb to indicate that it will happen, as stated by the scholars of rhetoric. Al-Farra’ said: It is interpreted in this sense because the meaning is, If the blast is blown, ‘except what God wills,’ meaning, except for whomever God wills to be terrified at that blast. There is a difference of opinion as to who is excluded from the verse. Some say they are the martyrs and prophets, others say they are the angels, others say they are Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death, others say they are the houris virgin black maidens, and others say they are all believers, based on the verses that follow: Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be secure. The exception could be comprehensive of all those mentioned, so there is no objection to that. And all will come to Him in humility. The majority of scholars read they came to Him in the form of an active participle with a pronoun referring to God, the Exalted. Al-A’mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Hafs on the authority of Asim read they came to Him as a past tense verb, as did Ibn Mas’ud. Qatadah read and all will come to Him. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads the verb as a past tense verb has unified it with the word kull, and whoever reads it as a present participle has pluralized it with its meaning, which is a clear mistake, because there is no unification in either of the two readings. Rather, the unification is only in the reading of Qatadah, and the meaning of dakhreen is saghreen dhaleen, and it is in the accusative case as a state. The majority read dakhreen, and Al-A’raj read dakhreen without an alif. The explanation of this has already been mentioned in Surat An-Nahl.
27:88: 88- And you will see the mountains and think them rigid is in apposition to Blows. The address is to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) or to anyone who is able to see. And you will think them rigid is in the accusative case as a hal of the pronoun you see or its object, because seeing is visual. It was also said that it is a substitute for the first clause, but this is weak. This is the third sign of the Hour. The meaning of you will think them rigid is: standing and still. The clause and they will pass like clouds is in the accusative case as a hal: meaning, they will move quickly like the clouds that are moved by the winds. Al-Qatibi said: This is because the mountains are gathered and move, but in the sight of the eye they are like standing ones while they are moving. Al-Qushayri said: This is the Day of Resurrection. Similar to it is the statement of God the Almighty: And the mountains will be set in motion and will become a mirage. The people of Kufa read you think it with a fatha on the seen, while the rest read it with a kasra. The creation of God, Who perfected everything. The accusative case of created is a source according to Al-Khalil, Sibawayh and others: meaning God made that creation. It was also said that it is a source emphasizing His statement: And the Day the Trumpet is blown. It was also said that it is accusative to induce: meaning look at the creation of God. The meaning of Who perfected everything is who made it perfect. It is said that a man is perfect: meaning he is skilled at things. The phrase He is All-Aware of what you do is an explanation of what preceded it, that He, the Almighty, made what He made and perfected everything. The All-Aware is the One who is aware of the outward and inward aspects. The majority read it with the superscript ta’ as an address, while Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Hisham read it with the subscript as a declarative.
27:89: 89- Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it. The definite article denotes the type: whoever brings a good deed will have a reward from God that is better than it: meaning better and more than it. It was also said that it is better obtained from its side, but the former is more appropriate. It was also said that what is meant by good here is: there is no god but God. It was also said that it is sincerity, and it was also said that it is performing the obligatory duties. Generalization is more appropriate and there is no basis for specification, even though some of the early Muslims said so. It was also said that this sentence is an explanation of His statement that He is All-Knowing of what you do. It was also said that it is an explanation of His statement that all will come to Him humbled. 'Asim, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read and they are from fear with the tanween and the fatha on the meem of that day. Nafi' read it with the fatha without the tanween. The rest read it with the addition of fear to that day. Abu 'Ubaid said: This is more pleasing to me because it is the more general of the two interpretations, because its meaning is: security from the fear of all of that Day, and with the tanween there is security from fear but not fear. It was said that it is a source that includes a lot, so what was mentioned is not preferred, so the two readings have the same meaning. It was said that what is meant by terror here is the greater terror mentioned in His statement: The greatest terror will not grieve them. The reason for Nafi’s reading is that he put day in the accusative case as a circumstantial word because its parsing is not established, and since terror is added to an established adverbial phrase, a full discussion of this has been presented in Surah Hud.
27:90: 90- And whoever brings evil - their faces will be thrown down into the Fire. A group of the Companions and those who came after them, and it was even said that it is agreed upon by the people of interpretation, said that what is meant by evil here is polytheism, and the point of specificity is his statement: so their faces will be thrown down into the Fire, so this recompense will only be for a similar evil of polytheism. The meaning of so their faces will be thrown down into the Fire is that they will be thrown down on their faces into it, and thrown down and thrown upon it. It is said that you threw a man on his face, so he fell down and prostrated. The phrase Are you recompensed except for what you used to do? is understood as saying: that is, that is said, and the one who says it is the keepers of Hell: meaning you will not be recompensed except for your deeds.
27:91: 91- I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred. When He, the Almighty, finished explaining the conditions of the beginning and the end, He commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them this statement: Say, O Muhammad, I have only been commanded to single out God alone for worship, with no partner for Him. What is meant by city is Mecca, and He singled it out from among all the other cities, but in it is the Sacred House of God, and because it is the most beloved city to His Messenger. The relative pronoun is a connection to the city, and the meaning of making it sacred is making it a safe sanctuary in which no blood is shed, no one is wronged, no game is hunted, and no one is alone within it. To Him belongs everything, of things, creation, ownership, and disposition: meaning, everything belongs to God. And I have been commanded to be of the Muslims, that is, those who oppose God’s command and submit to Him in obedience, complying with His command, and avoiding what He has forbidden. What is meant by His saying to be is that I remain as I am.
27:92: 92- And that I recite the Qur'an means that I recite it regularly and persevere in it. It has been said that what is meant by reciting the Qur'an here is nothing but the recitation of the call to faith. The first is more appropriate: So whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself because the benefit of that returns to him: that is, whoever is guided in general, or whoever is guided by what I recite to him and acts according to what is in it of faith in God, and acting according to His laws. The majority read And that I recite by adding the waw after the lam, as if it is from recitation, which is reading, or from recitation, which is following. Abdullah read And that I recite by deleting the waw as a command to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is how Al-Farra' explained it. An-Nahhas said: We do not know of anyone who recited this reading, and it contradicts all the copies of the Qur’an. And whoever goes astray, say, ‘I am only one of the warners.’ That is, whoever goes astray through disbelief and turns away from guidance, say to him, I am only one of the warners. I have done so by conveying that to you, and I have no other responsibility. It was also said that the answer is omitted: that is, the consequences of his misguidance will be upon him. I put I am only one of the warners in its place because it is like a cause for it.
27:93: 93- And say, 'Praise be to God,' for the blessings He has bestowed upon me, such as prophethood, knowledge, and other things. His statement, He will show you His signs, is part of what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was commanded to say: meaning, God will show you His signs in yourselves and in others. Then you will recognize them, meaning, you will recognize His signs and the evidence of His power and Oneness. This knowledge will not benefit the disbelievers, because they will recognize them when faith will not be accepted from them, which is when death approaches. Then He concluded the Surah by saying, And your Lord is not unaware of what you do. These are statements from Him, the Exalted, that are not included in the statements that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was commanded to say, and they contain severe intimidation and a tremendous threat. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham, and Hafs from Asim, read tam'alumun with the superlative as an addressee, while the rest read it with the subjunctive. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, dakhreen humbled, he said: humbled. These people narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And you will see the mountains and think them rigid, he said: upright. The creation of God, who perfected all things, he said: perfected. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding his statement, The creation of God, who perfected all things, he said: He perfected and strengthened everything He created. And Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, meaning: There is no god but God, “and whoever brings an evil deed, their faces will be thrown into the Fire,” meaning: It is polytheism. If this is authentically reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then it is necessary to refer to it in interpreting the words of God Almighty. It is understood that what is meant is: There is no god but God in its right and what is due to it, so every act of obedience is included under that. This is supported by what al-Hakim reported in al-Kuna on the authority of Safwan ibn Assal, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, faith and polytheism will come, kneeling before God Almighty. God will say to faith: Go, you and your family, to Paradise, and He will say to polytheism: Go, you and your family, to the Fire. “Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it,” meaning His statement: There is no god but God, “and whoever brings an evil deed,” meaning polytheism, will be thrown into the Fire. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Anas, and others, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), on the authority of Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever brings a good deed - meaning the testimony that there is no god but God - will have better than it - meaning Paradise - and whoever brings an evil deed - meaning polytheism - will throw them face down into the Fire and say: This saves and this destroys. ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat, and al-Khara’iti in Makarim al-Akhlaq narrated from Ibn Mas’ud: Whoever brings a good deed - he said: There is no god but God. “And whoever brings an evil deed” - he said: Polytheism. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Ibn ‘Abbas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: For him is better than it - he said: He has better than it, meaning from its direction. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him: For him is better than it - he said: A reward. He also narrated from him: The town is Makkah.
28:1: Its verses are eighty-eight, and it is all Meccan according to Al-Hasan and Ikrimah Ata’ Ibn Ad-Durais, Ibn An-Najjar, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Qasas was revealed in Makkah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Al-Qurtubi said: Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: It was revealed between Makkah and Madinah. Ibn Salam said: It was in Al-Juhfa at the time of the migration of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). It is the verse of God the Almighty: Indeed, He who enjoined upon you the Qur’an will surely bring you back to a place of return. Muqatil said: It contains from Madinah: Those to whom We gave the Scripture until His saying: We seek not the ignorant. Ahmad, At-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated: As-Suyuti said: Its chain of transmission is good on the authority of Ma’d Yakrib, who said: We came to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud and asked him to recite to us Surat Ta-Sin-Min. He said: I do not have it, but you should go to the one who took it from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): Khabbab ibn Al-Arat. So I went to Khabbab and said: How did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recite Ta-Sin-Min or Ta-Sin? He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite either. 1- Ta-Sin-Mim The word Ta-Sin-Mim in the opening of the Surah has already been mentioned in the opening of Al-Shu’ara’ and others, so we will not repeat it.
28:2: And likewise the speech passed on his saying: 2- These are the verses of the clear Book so the demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is what comes after it, or the predicate of a deleted subject and verses is a substitute for the demonstrative pronoun, and it is permissible for those to be in the accusative case of we recite, and the clear includes clarifying the truth from falsehood, and the lawful from the unlawful, and it is from abaan meaning made apparent.
28:3: 3- We recite to you, [O Muhammad], from the report of Moses and Pharaoh, in truth, for a people who believe. That is, We reveal to you their story mixed with the truth. He specified the believers because the recitation only benefits the believer. It was said that the object of we recite is omitted, and the meaning is: We recite to you something of their report. It is possible that from is an addition according to the opinion of Al-Akhfash: that is, We recite to you the report of Moses and Pharaoh. It is better for it to be for clarification based on the estimation of the object as mentioned, or for partiality, and there is no need to rule with its addition, and the truth is honesty.
28:4: And the fourth sentence - Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and what follows it is a new sentence brought forward to explain the general story. The commentators said: The meaning of exalted is to be arrogant and tyrannical with his power, and what is meant by the land is the land of Egypt. It was said that the meaning of ala is: he claimed divinity, and it was said that he rose above the worship of his Lord. And made its people into sects, meaning groups and classes in his service, who support him in whatever he wants and obey him. The phrase He oppresses a group of them is a new sentence introduced to explain the state of the people whom he made into groups and classes. It is possible that it is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of made: meaning, he made them into sects while a group of them was oppressed. It is possible that it is an attribute of a group, and the group is the Children of Israel. The phrase He slaughters their sons and keeps their women alive is a substitute for the first sentence. It is possible that it is a new sentence for explanation, or a state, or an attribute like the one before it, assuming that it is not a substitute for it. Rather, Pharaoh used to slaughter their sons and leave the women, because the astrologers of that era informed him that his kingdom would be lost at the hands of a child born from the Children of Israel. Al-Zajjaj said: It is surprising how foolish Pharaoh was. If the priest who told him this was telling the truth, then killing him would be of no use. If he was lying, then killing him would be meaningless. He was among the corrupters on earth through his sins and tyranny. This shows that killing is the work of the corrupters.
28:5: 5- And We desire to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land came in the present tense to narrate the past situation, and to evoke its images: that is, We desire to bestow a favor upon them after they were oppressed, and what is meant by these are the Children of Israel, and the and in and We desire is to connect with the clause Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself even though the connected clause is nominal, because there is a connection between them in that each one of them is for explanation and clarification, and it is permissible for it to be a state of the subject of weakens with the assumption of a subject: that is, We desire to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land as in the saying of the poet: I escaped and mortgaged them a kingdom The first is more appropriate: And We will make them leaders, meaning leaders in goodness and callers to it, and rulers over the people and kings among them. And We will make them inheritors of Pharaoh’s kingdom and the dwellings and possessions of the Copts. So Pharaoh’s kingdom will be among them and they will live in his dwellings and the dwellings of his people, and they will benefit from his possessions and their possessions.
28:6: 6- And We will establish them in the land meaning We will make them powerful over it and its people, and will have control over it, disposing of it as they wish. The majority of scholars read naamkun without lam, and Al-A'mash read linamkun with lam al-illah. And We will show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers The majority of scholars read naar with dammah on the noon and kasrah on the ra', with the subject being God, the Exalted. Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read wa yara with fathah on the ya' and the ra', with the subject being Pharaoh. The first reading is more in line with the context because before it is nareeda and naja'ala and wamkun with nun. Al-Farra’ permitted the word wa yari Fir’awn with a damma on the lower ya’ and a kasra on the ra’, meaning that God will show Fir’awn. The meaning of from them is from those weak ones, what they were wary of. The relative pronoun is the second object according to the first reading, and the first object according to the second reading. The meaning is that God will show them, or they will see, what they were wary of and striving to prevent, the loss of their kingdom and their destruction at the hands of the one born from the weak Children of Israel.
28:7: 7- And We inspired the mother of Moses, saying, ‘Suckle him.’ That is, We inspired her and put it in her heart. This is not the same revelation that is revealed to the messengers. It was said that this was a vision in her sleep, and it was said that this was through an angel whom God sent to inform her of this. The scholars have agreed that she was not a prophet, but rather the angel’s sending to her, according to those who said so, was in a manner similar to the angel speaking to a bald, leprous, or blind person, as in the authentic hadith in the two Sahihs and others. The angels greeted Imran bin Husayn, as in the authentic hadith in the Sahih, so he was not a prophet. And in breastfeed him is the explanation, because in revelation there is the meaning of saying, and it is possible that it is a source: that is, that I breastfeed him. Omar bin Abdul Aziz read with a kasra on the noon of an, and connected the hamza of breastfeed him, so the kasra is because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the hamza of connection was deleted contrary to the norm. So when you fear for him from Pharaoh that report of him would reach him, cast him into the river, which is the Nile. The explanation of the manner in which she was cast into the river has been presented in Surat Taha. And do not fear and do not grieve, meaning do not fear for him drowning or being lost, and do not grieve over his separation. Indeed, We will return him to you, soon in a way that will save him. And We will make him one of the messengers, whom We send to the servants.
28:8: The Fa in His saying 8- So the family of Pharaoh picked him up is the eloquent one, and picking up is finding something without asking for it, and what is meant by the family of Pharaoh are those who took the chest containing Moses from the sea, and there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is so she threw it into the sea after she put it in the chest, and whoever of the family of Pharaoh found it picked it up, and the Lam in so that he would be to them an enemy and a grief is the Lam of consequence, and the reason for that is that they took him so that he would be to them a son and a comfort to their eye, not so that he would be an enemy, so the consequence of that was that he was to them an enemy and a grief, and since this enmity was a result of their action and a fruit of it, it was likened to the motive for which the doer does the action, and from this is the poet’s Qazul: They were born for death and built for destruction Another saying: And for the fates, every wet nurse raises us, and our homes are built for the destruction of time. The majority read Wa Hazanan with a fat-ha on the ha' and the zay. Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read Wa Hazanan with a damma on the ha' and a sukun on the zay. Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim chose the first reading, and they are two dialects like Adam and Adam, Rushd and Rushd, and Saqm and Saqm. The phrase Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were sinners is to explain what preceded it, or to interrupt with the intention of emphasis. The meaning of Khaatiyyin is: disobedient and sinful in all their actions and words. It is taken from Khata which is the opposite of Rahta. Khaatiyyin is read with a ya without a hamza, so it is possible that the meaning of this reading is the meaning of the majority reading, but it was lightened by deleting the hamza. It is possible that it is from Khata yakhtu which means to go beyond what is correct.
28:9: 9- And the wife of Pharaoh said, 'A comfort of the eye for me and for you.' That is, the wife of Pharaoh said to Pharaoh. The raising of coolness is as predicate of a deleted subject, as stated by Al-Kisa'i and others. It was also said that it is as subject and predicate do not kill him, as stated by Al-Zajjaj, but the first is more appropriate. Her saying this was when she saw him when he reached her and she took him out of the chest and she addressed Pharaoh and those of his people who were with him with her saying, do not kill him, or Pharaoh alone as a way of glorifying him. Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited, And the wife of Pharaoh said, 'Do not kill him, a comfort of the eye for me and for you.' It is permissible to place coolness in the accusative case with his saying, do not kill him, as a preoccupation. It was said that she said, Do not kill him, for God brought him from a distant land and he is not from the Children of Israel. Then she explained what she said by hoping that they would benefit from him, or adopt him, so she said: Perhaps he will benefit us so that we may attain good from him or that we may adopt him as a son. She had not given birth, so she asked Pharaoh for him as a gift, and he gave him to her. The phrase and they perceive not is in the accusative case as a state: that is, they do not perceive that they were wrong in finding him, nor do they perceive that their destruction is at his hand, so it is a state of Pharaoh’s family, and it is from the words of God, the Most High. It was said that it is from the woman’s words: that is, and the Children of Israel do not know that we found him without realizing it. Al-Kalbi said this, but it is very far-fetched. Al-Farra’ narrated from Al-Suddi from Al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas that his saying Do not kill him was from the words of Pharaoh, and he interrupted it with words that refer to the wording.
28:10: And it is sufficient to refute it because of the weakness of its chain of transmission. 10- "And the heart of Moses' mother became empty." The commentators said: The meaning of this was that it was empty of everything except the matter of Moses, as if she did not care about anything else. Abu Ubaidah said: Empty of the remembrance of everything in this world except the remembrance of Moses. Al-Hasan, Ibn Ishaq, and Ibn Zayd said: Empty of what was revealed to her from His saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve," and that was because Satan tempted her to drown and destroy him. Al-Akhfash said: Empty of fear and sorrow because she knew that he did not drown because of what had been revealed to her. A similar narration was also narrated from Abu Ubaidah. Al-Kisa'i said: Forgetful and absent-minded. Al-Ala' ibn Ziyad said: Aversion. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Distracted, she almost said, "Oh, my son," from the intensity of her grief. Muqatil said: She almost cried out in pity for him from drowning. It was also said that the meaning is that when she heard of his falling into the hands of Pharaoh, her mind was blown from extreme grief and astonishment. Al-Nahhas said: The most correct of these sayings is the first, and those who said it are more knowledgeable about the Book of God. So if it is empty of everything except the mention of Moses, then it is empty of revelation. The saying of the one who said empty of worry is an ugly mistake because after it is She would have almost disclosed it, had We not strengthened her heart. Fadalah ibn Ubayd al-Nasari, Muhammad ibn al-Samifa’, al-Aliyah and Ibn Muhaisin read faz’an with a fa’, zay and ayn from faz’a, meaning afraid and terrified. Ibn Abbas read qara’an with a fatha qaf, a kasra ra’ and ayn from qara’ ra’s, meaning when its price subsided. The meaning of wa-asbaha is: and it became, as the poet said: The caliphs followed Rashid's orders and the city became Al-Walid's. "She would have almost disclosed it, had We not strengthened her heart. An" is the lightened form of the heavy form, and its subject is a deleted pronoun of matter: meaning, she almost disclosed the matter of Moses and that he was her son, due to the extreme astonishment, fear, and grief that had overwhelmed her. From the root word "bada to appear, yadda to show, and abada" to reveal. It was said that the pronoun in "bih" refers to the revelation that was revealed to her, but the former is more appropriate. Al-Farra' said: She would have disclosed his name due to the constriction of her chest, had We not strengthened her heart. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of "consolidating" the heart is inspiring and strengthening patience. The answer to "lawla" is deleted: meaning, had We not strengthened her heart, she would have disclosed. The "lam in li-tawkun min al-mu'minin is related to rabtna" to fasten, and the meaning is: We strengthened her mind so that she would be among those who believe in the promise of God, which is His statement, "Indeed, We will return him to you. It was said that the ba in li-tawkun bih" is redundant for emphasis. The meaning is: so that she would disclose it, as you say, "I took a rope to a rope."
28:11: And it was said that the meaning is: to express the saying about it 11- And she said to his sister, ‘Follow him.’ That is, Moses’ mother said to Moses’ sister, who was Mary, ‘Follow him.’ That is, follow his traces and know his report and see where he fell and to whom he went. It is said that you followed something: if you followed its traces, getting to know its condition. Then I saw it from afar, that is, I saw it from afar. Its root is from a place on the side, and from it comes the foreigner. The poet said: Do not deprive me of what I have gained due to my impurity, for I am a stranger in the midst of a land. It was said that what is meant by his saying from the side is from the side, and the meaning is that she looked at him, turning away and deceiving him. This is supported by the reading of Al-Nu’man bin Salim from the side. The place of from the side is the accusative case as a state, either from the agent: meaning she looked at him secretly, being from the side, or from the genitive: meaning far from her. The majority read I saw him with a fatha on the ba’ and a damma on the sad. Qatadah read it with a fatha on the sad and ‘Isa bin ‘Umar read it with a kasra. Al-Mubarrad said: I saw him and I saw him have the same meaning. The majority read from the side with two dhammah. Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Al-A’raj and Zaid bin ‘Ali read it with a fatha on the jim and a sukoon on the noon. Abu ‘Umar bin Al-‘Ala’ said: The meaning of from the side is from longing. He said: It is the language of Jutham, they say I yearned for you meaning I missed you, and they do not realize that she is telling him stories and following his report and that she is his sister.
28:12: 12- "And We forbade him from wet nurses" Wet nurses are the plural of wet nurse: meaning we forbade him from being breastfed by wet nurses. It is also said that wet nurses are the plural of wet nurse, with the letter ḍād open, and it means breastfeeding or its place, which is the breast. The meaning of "before" is before we return him to his mother, or before his mother comes to him, or before she traces his traces. Pharaoh's wife had sought wet nurses for Moses to breastfeed him, but he did not breastfeed from any of them. Then she said, meaning his sister, when she saw his refusal to breastfeed, "Shall I direct you to a household who will take care of him for you?" That is, they will guarantee that they will take care of him and breastfeed him. "And who are sincere to him?" That is, compassionate toward him and will not fall short in breastfeeding and raising him. There is an ellipsis in the speech, and the meaning is: So they said to her, who are they? She said, "My mother." So she was asked: Does your mother have milk? She said, "Yes, the milk of my brother Aaron." So she directed them to Moses' mother, and they gave him to her. He kissed her breast and suckled from it.
28:13: And this is the meaning of His Almighty saying: 13- So We restored him to his mother that her eye might be refreshed with her son and not grieve over his separation and that she might know that the promise of God meaning all of His promises, including what He promised her when He said, We will surely return him to you “is true” and will inevitably happen but most of them do not know meaning most of Pharaoh’s people did not know that, rather they were unaware of the fate and the secret of the decree, or most people do not know that or they do not know that God promised her that He would return him to her. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, And He made its people into sects, meaning He separated them. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah, And He made its people into sects, meaning He enslaved a group of them and left a group alone, killed a group and kept a group alive. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding His statement, And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders, meaning the rulers, and make them heirs, meaning those who inherit the land after Pharaoh and his people, and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they had feared, he said, that which the people had feared. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And We inspired the mother of Moses, meaning We inspired her with what she did to Moses. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-A’mash who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding His statement, And when you fear for him, he said: That your neighbors may hear his voice. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding His statement, And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty, he said: It was emptied of all worldly matters except for the mention of Moses. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated it – and he authenticated it – from various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty, he said: Empty of everything except the mention of Moses. And regarding His statement, She was about to disclose him, he said: She would say, O my son. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated it – and he authenticated it – from him regarding His statement, And she said to his sister, ‘Follow him,’ meaning, follow his traces. So she saw him from afar, he said: from afar. At-Tabarani and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Khadija: Did you not know that God married me to Mary, daughter of Imran, and Kulthum, the sister of Moses, and the wife of Pharaoh? She said: Congratulations, O Messenger of God. Ibn Asakir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Rawad, with a longer chain of transmission than this, and at the end of it she said: With comfort and children. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated it - and authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, And We had forbidden him wet nurses before, he said: A wet nurse should not be brought to him so that he could kiss her.
28:14: His saying: 14- And when he reaches maturity He presented the discussion of reaching maturity in livestock. Rabi'ah and Malik said: It is puberty, based on the Almighty's saying: Until, when they reach the age of marriage, if you perceive in them sound judgment (al-Quran 2:14). The maximum is thirty-four years, as Mujahid, Sufyan al-Thawri and others said. It was said that maturity is between eighteen and thirty, and maturity is from thirty to forty. It was said that maturity is reaching forty. It was said that maturity is a reference to the perfection of creation. It was said that it has one meaning, but it is weak because the conjunction indicates difference. We gave him judgment and knowledge. Judgment is wisdom in general. It was said that it is prophethood. It was said that it is understanding in religion. Knowledge is understanding, as al-Suddi said. Mujahid said that it is jurisprudence. Ibn Ishaq said: Knowledge of his religion and the religion of his fathers. It was said that this was before the prophethood. The meaning of this was explained in Surat al-Baqarah 2:And thus do We reward the doers of good. That is, like the reward that We rewarded the mother of Moses when she submitted to the command of God and threw her son into the sea and believed in God’s promise. We reward the doers of good for their goodness. What is meant is generality.
28:15: 15- "And he entered the city meaning Moses entered the great city of Egypt, or it was said that it was another city from the cities of Egypt, and the place of his saying while its people were unaware" is the accusative case as a state: either from the subject: meaning in secret, or from the object. It was said that when Moses knew what he was upon of the truth in his religion, he criticized what Pharaoh's people were upon and that spread about him, so they frightened him and he feared them, so he did not enter the city except in secret. It was said that his entry was between the evening and night prayers, and it was said that it was during the midday meal. Ad-Dahhak said: He asked to enter the city when its people were not paying attention, so he entered when he knew about them, and what happened was what God narrated in His saying: And he found therein two men fighting, one of his own party meaning of those who supported him in his religion, and they were the Children of Israel and this one of his enemy meaning of those who were hostile to him in his religion, and they were the people of Pharaoh. Then the one of his own party sought aid from him meaning he asked him to support him and aid him against his opponent against the one of his enemy and he aided him because supporting the oppressed is obligatory in all religions. It was said that Al-Qutbi wanted to force the Israelite to carry firewood to Pharaoh’s kitchen, but he refused, so he sought aid from Moses. So Moses prodded him. Prod is by pluralizing the palm, and similarly, the pronunciation of laz and lahz. It was also said that prodding is on the beard, and prodding is on the heart. It was also said that he struck him with his staff. Ibn Mas’ud read fa-lazhu. Al-Tha’labi narrated that in the copy of Uthman, fa-nazhu with a nun nun is nazhu nun meaning he struck him and pushed him. Al-Asma’i said: Nazhu with a nun means he struck him and pushed him. Al-Jawhari said: Lakaz is striking on the chest. Abu Zaid said: On the entire body, meaning that it is called Lakaz. Lahz is striking with both hands on the chest. Similar to it is reported by Abu Ubaidah: He killed him, meaning he killed him. And everything you have done and finished with: you have finished with it. From this is the saying of the poet: He bit him, so Ashja' killed him. It was said that Moses did not intend to kill the Copt, but rather intended to push him away, but that led to his own downfall. That is why he said, This is the work of Satan. He only said this statement even though the one killed was an infidel who deserved to be killed, because at that time he was not commanded to kill infidels. It was also said that this situation was one of refraining from fighting because he was considered safe by them, so he did not have the right to assassinate them. Then he described Satan by saying, Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy, meaning an enemy of man who seeks to mislead him, clearly hostile and misleading. It was also said that the reference in his statement was to the action of the one killed because he was an infidel, which was contrary to what God wants. It was also said that it was a reference to the one killed himself, meaning that he was from the soldiers and party of Satan. Then he asked God, the Almighty, to forgive him for what he had done.
28:16: 16- He said, My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me. So God forgave him that. He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
