The reason for his seeking forgiveness is that no prophet could kill until he was commanded to do so. It was said that he sought forgiveness for leaving the first one, as is the way of the messengers, or he meant that I have wronged myself by killing this infidel, because if Pharaoh had known of that, he would have killed me because of it. The meaning of so forgive me is: conceal that from me so that Pharaoh does not find out about it. This is contrary to what appears, because Moses, peace be upon him, continued to regret that and fear punishment because of it, to the point that on the Day of Resurrection, when people asked him for intercession, he would say, I killed a soul that I was not commanded to kill, as was proven in the authentic hadith of intercession. It has been said that this was before the prophethood, and it was said that it was before he reached the age of accountability and that he was at that time twelve years old. All of these far-fetched interpretations preserve what has been established regarding the infallibility of the prophets, and there is no doubt that they are infallible from major sins. The killing that he committed was not intentional, so it is not a major sin, because a stab does not usually kill. Then when God answered his question and forgave him, he did not ask for His forgiveness.
28:17: 17- "He said, 'My Lord, because You have bestowed favor upon me,' This preposition by" could be the preposition of an oath, and the answer is understood: i.e., I swear by Your favor upon me that I will repent. The sentence "I will never be a supporter of the criminals" could be an explanation of the answer, as if he swore by the favor God had bestowed upon him that he would not support a criminal. It is also possible that this preposition "by" is the preposition of causality related to something omitted: i.e., protect me because of the favor You have bestowed upon me, and his saying "I will never be a supporter of the criminals" could be a consequence of it, and in that there would be an appeal to God the Most High and a means of attaining His favor through His favor. What is in His saying "by the favor You have bestowed" is either a relative pronoun or a verbal noun. What is meant by "by the favor He bestowed upon him" is what He gave him of wisdom and knowledge, or forgiveness, or all of them. What is meant by supporting the criminals is either the company of Pharaoh and being a member of his group, apparently, or supporting him in something that is sinful. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: His statement, "I will never be a supporter of the criminals" is not a statement, but rather a supplication: "So do not make me, O Lord, a supporter of them." Al-Kisa'i said: In Abdullah's reading, it is: "So do not make me, O Lord, a supporter of the criminals." Al-Farra' said: The meaning is, O God, I will never be a supporter of the criminals." Al-Nahhas said: Making it a statement is more complete and more consistent with the flow of speech.
28:18: 18- So he entered the city, fearful and anticipating meaning he entered the city in which the Copt was killed in the morning. Fearful is the predicate of became, and it is possible that it is a state, and the predicate is in the city, and anticipating may be a second predicate, or a second state, or a substitute for fearful, and the object of anticipates is omitted, and the meaning is: anticipating the misfortune or anticipating the joy. Then he who had sought his aid yesterday cried out to him If is the suddenness, and the relative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is crying out to him: meaning, then his Israelite companion who had sought his aid yesterday was fighting another Copt whom he wanted to mock and oppress, just as he wanted the Copt whom Moses had killed yesterday. And crying out is seeking help, and it is from screaming, and that is because the one seeking help makes a sound and screams in request for help, and from it the poet said: Whenever a screaming person came to us in panic, our response was the banging of pipes. Moses said to him, You are clearly misguided. That is, you are clearly misguided, because you are fighting someone you cannot fight and cannot stand. It was said that he said this to him because he had caused the death of a man the day before and wanted to cause the death of another today.
28:19: 19- So when he intended to seize the one who was an enemy to them both meaning to seize the Copt who was an enemy to Moses and the Israelite since he was not of their religion. The meaning of seizing and the differences of the reciters in it have already been mentioned. He said, ‘O Moses, do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday?’ The one speaking was the Israelite when he heard Moses say to him: You are clearly a liar and saw him intending to seize the Copt, he thought that he wanted to seize him, so he said to Moses: Do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? When the Copt heard that, he revealed it. None of Pharaoh’s companions knew that Moses was the one who killed the Copt yesterday until the Israelite revealed it to him. This is what the majority of commentators said. It was said that the one who said, Do you want to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? was the Copt. He had heard the report from the Israelite, and this is what appears to be the case. The Copt was mentioned before without separation because he is the one meant by his saying, An enemy of both of them. There is no reason to contradict the apparent meaning, so as to necessitate that the believer in Moses was the one who sought his help the first time, and the second time he was the one who disclosed it to him. Also, his saying, You only want to be a tyrant on earth is only befitting of an unbeliever, and in his saying, If you want is the negative, meaning you only want to be a tyrant on earth. Al-Zajjaj said: In the language, a tyrant is one who does not humble himself before the command of God, and the unjust killer is a tyrant. It was said that a tyrant is one who does whatever he wants of hitting and killing without considering the consequences and does not repel with what is best. And you do not want to be of the reformers means those who reconcile between people.
28:20: 20- And a man came running from the farthest part of the city. It was said that this man is Ezekiel, the believer of the family of Pharaoh, and he was the cousin of Moses. It was also said that his name was Shimon, or it was said that he was Talut, or it was said that Shaman. What is meant by the farthest part of the city is its last and furthest part. Running may be in the nominative case as an attribute of a man, or it may be in the accusative case as a state, because the word man, even though it is indefinite, is made specific by His statement: from the farthest part of the city. He said, 'O Moses, indeed the eminent ones are taking counsel together about you to kill you,' meaning they are consulting each other about killing you and plotting because of you. Al-Zajjaj said: They are ordering each other to kill you. Abu Ubaid said: They are taking counsel together about you to kill you, meaning the most prominent people of Pharaoh. Al-Azhari said: The people took counsel together and conspired, meaning they ordered each other. Similar to His statement: And consult among yourselves in what is right. Al-Nimr ibn Talib said: I see that people have created a habit and in every incident they are ordered Then go out, for I am among your sincere advisors, in the command to go out. The lam is for clarification because the object of the genitive does not precede it.
28:21: 21- So he went out from it, fearful and waiting. So Moses went out from the city while he was afraid of the oppressors, waiting for them to catch up with him and overtake him. Then he called upon his Lord to save him from what he feared, saying: My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people. That is, save me from the disbelieving people and repel them from me, and stand between me and them.
28:22: 22- And when he turned toward Madyan meaning toward Madyan intending it. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning he took the road toward Madyan and ended up there. It is said that his house was opposite the house of so-and-so, and its origin is from the word meeting. This village was not under the authority of Pharaoh, and that is why he went out to it. He said, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way' meaning that He will direct me toward the straight road to Madyan.
28:23: 23- And when he came to the water of Madyan meaning he reached it, which is the water from which they draw water, he found there a group of people watering their livestock meaning he found there a large group of people watering their livestock. The word arriving may refer to entering a watering place, or it may refer to reaching it even if he does not enter it, and this is what is meant here. From this is the saying of Zuhair: When we reached the water, the doves were blue. The meaning of al-wurud has already been investigated in His statement: And there is not one of you but will pass by it. It has been said that Madyan is the name of the tribe, and it is not declined in both cases. And he found, besides them, meaning, besides the people who water what is between them and the direction from which he came. It has also been said that its meaning is: in a place lower than them. Two women who are holding back, meaning, they are holding back their sheep from the water until the people have finished and it is clear between them and the water. The meaning of al-wurud is pushing and holding back. From this is the saying of the poet: I spend the night at the door of rhymes as if I am fending off a swarm of wild beasts with it. That is, I detain and prevent. The word ward means to expel, and from this comes the poet’s saying: Your stick was taken away by Banu Tamim, so you do not know which stick to use to defend yourself. Any expulsion He said, What is the matter with you two?" That is, Moses said to the two women: What is the matter with you that you do not water your sheep with the people? And the matter is the matter, it was said that it is only said, "What is the matter with you" to someone who is afflicted, or persecuted, or to someone who commits an evil. "They said, We do not water [their flocks] until the shepherds depart. That is, it is our custom to wait until the people depart from the water and leave it, for fear of mixing with them, or for being unable to water their flocks with them. The majority read yusdur with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the dal, the present tense of asdara transitive with a hamza. Ibn Amir, Abu Amr, and Abu Ja'far read it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the dal from sadra yasdur intransitive. So the object in the first reading is deleted: that is, they return their livestock. The shepherds are the plural of ra'a. The majority read al-ri'a with a kasra on the ra'. Abu Amr read it in a narration from him with a fatha. Abu al-Fadl said: It is a verbal noun that replaces an adjective, and therefore the singular and plural are the same in it. Al-ri'a was read with a damma as a plural noun. Talha bin Musarf read Nasqi with a damma on the nun from asqa “and our father is a great old man,” and this is part of their statement: meaning he is unable to water his livestock due to his old age, so we, two weak women, needed to water the sheep because there was no man to do that for us. So when Moses heard their statement.
28:24: 24- He watered for them out of mercy for them: meaning he watered their sheep for their sake. Then when he finished watering for them, he turned to the shade meaning he went to it and sat in it. It was said that this shade was the shade of a samura tree there. Then he said, due to the effort and fatigue that had befallen him, calling out to his Lord, Indeed, I am, for whatever good You send down to me meaning good. He was poor meaning in need of that. It was said that he meant food by that, and the lam in lamma anzalta means to. Al-Akhfash said: It is said that he is poor in it and towards it. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Muhammadi in his Amali narrated on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, And when he reached his full strength, he said: thirty-three years, and and reached full strength, he said: forty years. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Long-Long Lives on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abi Saleh on his authority that he said: Full strength is between eighteen and thirty years, and full strength is between thirty and forty years, and when it exceeds forty it begins to decrease. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority on the statement of God, and he entered the city at a time when its people were unaware, he said: midday. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani, on his authority also regarding the verse that he said: between sunset and night prayers. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, This one is from his party, he said: an Israelite, and this one is from his enemy, he said: a Copt. So the one from his party, the Israelite, sought help from him against the one from his enemy, the Copt. So Moses struck him and killed him, he said: So he died. He said: That was a great burden on Moses. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, regarding his statement, Then he who had sought his aid the day before cried out to him, he said: He is the companion of Moses who had sought his aid the day before. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah, he said: The one who sought his aid is the one who cried out to him. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from al-Sha’bi, he said: Whoever kills two men is a tyrant, then he recited this verse, You only desire to be a tyrant on the earth. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from al-Sha’bi, he said: Whoever kills two men is a tyrant, then he recited this verse, You only desire to be a tyrant on the earth. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah, he said: A man is not a tyrant until he kills two people. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Moses went out in fear, watching for a hungry person who had no provisions with him until he reached the water of Madyan, and there was a group of people watering their flocks and two women were sitting with their sheep. He asked them, What is the matter with you? They said, We will not water our flocks until the shepherds depart, and our father is a very old man. He said, Is there water near you? They said: No, except a well with a rock covered over it, so that no group could bear it. He said: So they set out and showed it to me, and they set out with him. He took the rock in his hand and moved it, then drew a bucket for them and watered the sheep, then he returned the rock to its place. Then he turned to the shade and said: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need. So they heard. He said: So they returned to their father, and he was astonished at their quick arrival, so he asked them, and they told him. He said to one of them: Go and call him. So she came and said: My father calls you to reward you for having watered our sheep. So she walked in front of him, and he said to her: Walk behind me, for I am a man from the lineage of Abraham, and I cannot bear to see from you what God has forbidden me. So he showed me the way. So when he came to him and related to him the story, he said: Fear not; you have been saved from the wrongdoing people. One of them said: O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy. Her father said to her: What did you see of his strength and trustworthiness? So she told him what had happened. She said, "As for his strength, he turned the stone by himself, and no one could turn it over except a few. As for his trustworthiness, he said, 'Walk behind me and show me the way, for I am a man from the lineage of Abraham. What God has forbidden is not permissible for me from you.'" Ibn Abbas was asked, Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said, The more righteous and fulfilled of the two. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah in Al-Musannaf, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, who said, "When Moses arrived at the well of Madyan, he was surprised by two women. He said, 'What is the matter with you?' They told him. He went to the stone and lifted it by himself. Then he drew water, but he drew water only once until the sheep were satisfied. The two women returned to their father and told him, and Moses turned away to take shelter. 'My Lord, indeed I, for whatever good You may send down to me, am in need.'" He said: One of them came to him walking shyly, putting her garment over her face, not like the women who go out and come in. She said, ‘My father invites you that he may reward you for having watered our land for us.’ So Moses stood with her and said to her, Walk behind me and describe the way to me, for I hate for the wind to catch your clothes and for you to describe your body to me. When he reached her father, he told him what he told her. One of them said, O my father, hire him, for the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy. He said, O my daughter, how do you know that he is trustworthy and strong? She said, “As for his strength, he can lift a stone, and only ten men can lift it. As for his trustworthiness, he said to her, ‘Walk behind me and describe the way to me, for I hate for the wind to catch your clothes and for it to describe your body to me.’” When he reached her father, he told her what he told her. One of them said, O my father, hire him, for the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy. He said, O my daughter, how do you know that he is trustworthy and strong? She said: As for his strength, he could lift a stone, and only ten men could do it. As for his trustworthiness, he said, Walk behind me and describe the way to me, for I hate for the wind to catch your clothes and describe your body to me. This increased his desire for him. Then, He said, ‘Indeed, I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine,’ until His saying, You will find me, if God wills, among the righteous, meaning in good company and fulfilling what I said. He said, Moses, “That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms you fulfill, there will be no aggression against me.” He said, Yes. He said, And God is Witness over what we say. So, he married him to him and he stayed with him, providing for him and working to tend to his sheep and whatever he needed. He married Safoor and her sister Sharf, and they were the ones who used to drive them away. Ibn Kathir said, after citing various chains of narration for this hadith: Its chain of narration is sound. As-Salfa’ was a bold and sharp woman. Ahmad reported in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And when he reached the water of Madyan, he said: He reached the water wherever he reached, and the greenery of the plants could be seen in his belly due to his emaciation. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that Moses left Egypt for Madyan, and the distance between them was eight nights. He had no food except tree leaves. He left barefoot, and as soon as he reached it, his sole fell off. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority that he said: They kept back means they kept their sheep back until the people left and the well was clear for them. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara also narrated on his authority that Moses said: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need. And he was the most honorable of His creation to Him, and he was in need of even half a date, and his stomach clung to his back from the severity of hunger. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said: He asked for nothing but food. Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id al-Zuhd and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he asked for a piece of bread to strengthen his back from hunger.
28:25: His statement: 25- Then one of the two came to him walking shyly. There is an omission in the speech indicated by the context. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that they went to their father quickly, as it was their custom to be slow in watering their flocks. They told him what had happened to the man who had watered their flocks. He ordered the elder of his two daughters, or it was said the younger, to call him for him, so she came to him. Most of the commentators said that they were the daughters of Shu'ayb, and it was said that they were the daughters of Shu'ayb's brother, and that Shu'ayb had died. The first is more likely. This is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. The place of walking is the accusative case of the subject of came, and on shyness is another case: that is, being on shyness in the states of walking and coming only, and the phrase She said, my father invites you is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said what did she say to him when she came to him so that he may reward you for having watered for us that is, the reward for your watering for us So when he came to him and related to him the story the story is a source named after the object: that is, the one related, meaning he told him everything that happened to him from when he killed the Copt until when he arrived at the water of Midian He said Shuaib Do not fear, you have escaped from the wrongdoing people that is, Pharaoh and his companions, because Pharaoh had no authority over Midian, and Al-Razi has very cold problems in this place that do not deserve to be mentioned in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty, and the answer to them is clear to the negligent, let alone the complete, and the most clear thing he came with is how Moses answered the invitation that was explained by the reward for what he did of watering. The answer is that he followed God’s law in answering the call of one of God’s prophets, and that answer was not for the sake of receiving a reward for this work. That is why it was reported that when food was presented to him, he said: We are a family who will not sell our religion for an earth full of gold.
28:26: 26- One of the two women said, 'O my father, hire him.' The one who said this is the one who came to him: meaning, hire him to tend our sheep. This is evidence that hiring was permissible for them. All Islamic scholars have agreed on its permissibility and legitimacy except for al-Asamm, who was deaf to hearing its evidence. The phrase Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy is an explanation for what she did in guiding her father to hire Moses: meaning, he is worthy of your hiring him because he combines the two qualities of strength and trustworthiness. It was mentioned previously in al-Mardawi on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Umar that her father asked her about her description of him as strong and trustworthy, so she answered him as mentioned earlier.
28:27: 27- He said, 'I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine.' This indicates the legitimacy of a woman's guardian offering her to a man, and this is an established tradition in Islam, as has been proven from Umar offering his daughter Hafsa to Abu Bakr and Uthman, and the story is well-known, and other things that happened during the days of the Companions and the days of the Prophethood. Likewise, what happened when a woman offered herself to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the condition that you hire me for eight years meaning that you will be my employee for eight years. Al-Farra' said: He is saying, on the condition that you make my reward to be that you tend my sheep for eight years. The place of on the condition that you hire me is the accusative case of state, and it is the present tense of I hired him, and its second object is omitted: meaning yourself, and eight years is an adverbial phrase. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said: I rented my house and my slave, whether extended or extended, and the former is more. If you complete ten, then it is from you, meaning if you complete what I hired you for of herding for ten years, then it is from you, meaning as a favor from you, not as an obligation from me to you. He made what is in excess of eight years to complete ten years. It is entrusted to chivalry, and the place of then it is from you is the nominative case, assuming the subject: meaning it is from you. And I do not want to make it difficult for you by obligating you to complete the ten years. The derivation of difficulty comes from the word shaq: meaning he split his thought in half, so sometimes he says I can, and sometimes he says I cannot. Then he encouraged him to accept the hire, so he said: You will find me, God willing, among the righteous, in good company and loyalty. It was said that he meant righteousness in general, so righteousness in dealings with that hire is included under the verse as a primary entry, and he restricted that to the will, delegating the matter to God’s success and assistance.
28:28: Then when Shuaib finished speaking, Moses decided, so 28- "He said, 'That is between me and you.'" The demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is what he worshipped, and the reference is to what they agreed upon. The clause "Whichever of the two terms you fulfill is conditional and its answer is there is no aggression against me." What is meant by the two terms is eight years and ten years. The meaning of fulfilled is I fulfilled it and completed it. The two terms are in the genitive case by adding "to it, and ma" is redundant. Ibn Kaysan said: "ma is in the genitive case by adding any to it, and the two terms" is a substitute for it. Al-Hasan read "whatever with a sukoon on the yaa, and Ibn Mas'ud read whichever of the two terms you fulfill. The meaning of there is no aggression against me" is that there is no injustice against me by demanding more than what I have fulfilled of the two terms: that is, just as I do not demand more than eight years, I do not accept less than ten. It was said that the meaning is: just as I do not demand more than eight years, I do not accept more than eight years, and this is more evident. The root of aggression is exceeding the limit in something other than what is necessary. Al-Mubarrad said: Moses knew that there would be no aggression against him if he fulfilled them, but he combined them to make the first like the most complete in fulfillment. The majority read aggression with a damma on the ‘ayn. Abu Haywah read it with a kasra, And God is a witness to what we say, meaning, over what we say of these conditions that are in effect between us, He is a witness and a guardian, so none of us can deviate from any of that. It was said that it is from the words of Moses, and it was said that it is from the words of Shu’ayb, but the first is more appropriate because it occurs within the group of Moses’ words.
28:29: 29- And when Moses had fulfilled the term - the most complete and perfect of them, which is ten years, as will be mentioned at the end of the discussion. The fa is eloquent. And he traveled with his family to Egypt, and in it is evidence that a man can go with his family wherever he wants. He perceived a fire from the side of the Mount - that is, he saw a fire from the side facing the Mount. The explanation of this has already been presented in full in Surah Taha. He said to his family, ‘Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you information from it.’ The explanation of this has also been presented in Surah Taha and in Surah An-Naml. Or a burning ember. The majority of scholars read it with a kasra on the jim, while Hamzah and Yahya ibn Waththab read it with a damma. Asim, As-Sulami, and Dhar ibn Hubaysh read it with a fatha. Al-Jawhari said: Al-jadhwa, al-jadhwa, and al-jadhwa are embers, and the plural is jathan, jathan, and jatha. Mujahid said: In the verse, the burning ember is a piece of coal in the language of all Arabs. Abu Ubaidah said: It is a thick piece of wood as if there is fire at its end, but there is none. What supports the idea that the ember is a coal is the statement of Al-Salami: And after the musk and frankincense, the misery of the smoke of the firewood was replaced by the head of a pale, disheveled man. Perhaps you may warm yourself by the fire.
28:30: 30- When he came to it meaning he came to the fire that he saw. It was also said that he came to the tree, but the former is more appropriate because the tree was not mentioned earlier. He was called from the right bank of the valley “from” indicates the beginning of the limit, and right is an attribute of the bank, and it is from Yemen, which is the blessing, or from the right side of the graves to the left in relation to Moses: meaning what is next to his right, not his left. The bank of the valley is its edge, and so is its shore. Al-Raghib said: The plural of shore is shores, and his saying: in the blessed spot is related to he was called, or to an omitted word as a state of the bank, and from the tree is an inclusionary alternative to the bank of the valley, because the tree was growing on the bank. Al-Jawhari said: He says the bank of the valleys and it is not pluralized. The majority read in the spot with a damma on the ba', while Abu Salamah and Al-Ashhab Al-Uqayli read it with a fatha, which is a dialect narrated by Abu Zayd. O Moses, I am God. "An" is the explanatory word, and it is possible that it is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its subject is the pronoun of the matter, and the vocative sentence means it. It was also read with a fatha, which is a weak reading.
28:31: And His statement: 31- And throw down your staff is connected to O Moses. The explanation of this and what follows it has already been presented in Taha and An-Naml. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So he threw it down and it became a snake and shook. And when he saw it shaking as if it were a genie in the speed of its movement with the size of its body, he turned back in flight, meaning defeated. The accusative of turning back is in the state of circumstance, and His statement: And he did not return is also in the accusative position as a state of circumstance: meaning he did not return. “O Moses, come forward and do not fear. Indeed, you are among those who are safe.” The explanation of all that was mentioned here has already been presented in full, so we will not repeat it.
28:32: And also His saying: 32- "Put your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease. And draw your wing toward you." The wing of a person is his arm, and the entire hand is called a wing: that is, draw your two outstretched hands toward you to protect yourself with them from a snake like someone who is frightened. This meaning has been expressed in three phrases: the first is put your hand into your bosom, the second: and draw your wing toward you, and the third: and put your hand into your bosom. It is possible that by drawing close is meant endurance and steadfastness when the stick turns into a snake, and the meaning of from fear is from fear, which is fear. The majority read fear with a fatha on the ra' and the ha', and this reading was chosen by Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim, and Hafs, As-Salami, Isa ibn Umar and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a fatha on the ra' and a sukoon on the ha'. Ibn Amir and the Kufians except Hafs read it with a damma on the ra' and a sukoon on the ha'. Al-Farra’ said: By the wing he meant his staff. Some of the scholars of semantics said: The monk is the sleeve in the language of Himyar and Banu Hanifa. Al-Asma’i said: I heard a Bedouin say to another: Give me what is in your monk, so I asked him about the monk, so I asked him about the monk, and he said: The sleeve. Based on this, its meaning would be: Bring your hand closer to you and take it out of the sleeve. Fadhanak is a reference to the staff and the hand. Two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs meaning two bright arguments and two clear proofs. The majority read Fadhanak with a light nun, while Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a shaddah. It was said that shaddah is the language of the Quraysh. Ibn Mas`ud, `Isa ibn `Umar, Shibl, and Abu Nawfal read it with a sukoon on the ba` after a kasra on the noon, and the ya` is a substitute for one of the two noons. This is the language of Hudhayl, and it was said that it is the language of Tamim. His statement, From your Lord, is connected to something omitted: that is, two beings from Him. Likewise, His statement, To Pharaoh and his chiefs, is connected to something omitted: that is, two messengers, or two people who reached them. Indeed, they were a wicked people, exceeding the limit in injustice, going beyond obedience in the most eloquent departure. The sentence is an explanation of what came before it. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl on the authority of `Umar ibn Al-Khattab, regarding the statement of God, walking modestly, that he said: She came concealed by the sleeve of her armor over her face. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated it on the authority of Abi Al-Hudhayl, with a chain of transmission traceable back to him. Ibn `Asakir narrated on the authority of Abi Hazim, who said: When Moses entered upon Shu`ayb, he saw dinner being served. Shu`ayb said to him, Eat. Moses said, I seek refuge in God. He said, Why? Are you not hungry? He said, “Yes, but I fear that this might be in exchange for what I provided for them. I am from a household that does not sell any of the deeds of the Hereafter for the earth full of gold.” He said, “No, by God, but that is my custom and the custom of my forefathers. We honor guests and feed people.” So Moses sat and ate. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Malik ibn Anas that he had heard that Shu`ayb was the one who told him the story. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The companion of Moses was Athrun, the nephew of the Prophet Shu`ayb. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: The one who hired Moses was Yathrib, the ruler of Madyan. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, who said: The name of Moses’ son-in-law was Yathrib. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: Some people say that he was Shu`ayb, but he was not Shu`ayb, but he was the master of the waters at that time. Ibn Majah, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Utbah ibn Al-Mundhir Al-Sulami, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he recited Surah Ta-Sin-Mim until he reached the story of Moses. He said: ‘Moses hired himself for eight or ten years in exchange for his chastity and food. When the term was fulfilled…’ It was said: ‘O Messenger of God, which of the two terms did Moses fulfill?’ He said: ‘The more righteous and fulfilled of the two. When he wanted to leave Shu’ayb, he ordered his wife to ask her father to give her from his sheep what they would live on, so he gave her what his sheep bore.” The hadith in full. In its chain of transmission is Muslimah ibn ‘Ali Al-Hasani Al-Dimashqi Al-Balati, who was declared weak by the imams. It has been narrated from another chain of transmission, but there is some doubt about it. Its chain of transmission according to Ibn Abi Hatim is as follows: Abu Zur’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Bakir, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Yazid Al-Hadrami, on the authority of ‘Ali ibn Rabah Al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard ‘Utbah ibn Al-Mundhir Al-Sulami, the companion of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he mentioned it. Ibn Lahi'ah is weak, and the rest of the chain of narrators should be examined. Ibn Jarir narrated a part of it on the authority of Anas, with a chain of narration ending with him. Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on his authority. His statement that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said he did something is questionable, because Moses did not say that he would fulfill the larger of the two terms, but rather he said: Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no aggression against me. It has been narrated from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) that Moses fulfilled the larger of the two terms through various chains of narration. Al-Khatib narrated in his history on the authority of Abu Dharr that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: "If you are asked which of the two terms Moses fulfilled, say the better and more righteous of them. And if you are asked which of the two women did he marry, say the younger of the two, which is the one who came and said: 'O my father, hire him.'" Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Gabriel said to me: O Muhammad, if the Jews ask you which of the two terms Moses fulfilled, say the fuller of the two. And if they ask you which of the two he married, say the younger of the two." Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Dharr, “The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked which of the two terms Moses fulfilled. He said, ‘The more righteous and fulfilling of the two.’ He said, ‘And if you are asked which of the two women he married, say the younger of the two.’” Al-Bazzar said, “We do not know of any narration on the authority of Abu Dharr except with this chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Uwaid ibn Abi Imran, and he is weak. As for the narrations that he fulfilled the two terms, they have chains of transmission that strengthen each other. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: Ibn Abbas said: When Moses fulfilled the term, he traveled with his family. He lost his way. It was winter, and a fire was raised up for him. When he saw it, he thought it was fire, but it was from the light of God. “So he said to his family, ‘Wait here. I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch from it.’ But if I cannot find any information, I will bring you a burning flame, ‘perhaps you may warm yourselves’ from the cold.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: Perhaps I will bring you report from it, so that I may find someone who can show me the way. They had lost their way. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Or a burning ember, he said: A meteor. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: He was called from the shore of the valley, he said: The call was from the lowest heaven. The apparent meaning of the Qur’an contradicts what he said, may God be pleased with him. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud who said: The tree to which Moses sought refuge was mentioned to me, so I went to it day and night until morning. It was a green, tamarisk tree, luxuriant. I invoked blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and gave him my salutations. My camel went towards it while it was hungry, and took a full mouthful of it and chewed it, but could not swallow it, so he spat it out. I invoked blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and gave him my salutations, then I left. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And draw your wing towards you, he said: Your hand.
28:33: When Moses heard God Almighty’s words: These are two proofs to Pharaoh, God Almighty asked him to strengthen his heart, so 33- He said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have killed a person among them,’ meaning the Copt who had struck him and killed him, ‘and I fear that they will kill me’ because of it.
28:34: 34- And my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I in speech because Moses's tongue was a plaster cast as explained above. Eloquence is the language of purity. It is said that the milk became clear and eloquent, so he is eloquent: meaning it was free of foam. From this, a man became eloquent: his language became good. He spoke in Arabic. It is said that the eloquent is the one who speaks, and the foreigner is the one who does not speak. As for the terminology of the people of rhetoric, eloquence is: the purity of the word from the dissonance of letters, strangeness, and contradiction of analogy. Eloquence of speech is: its purity from weak composition and complexity. The accusative of rad'an is in the state, and the appointed rad'a is from arad'atu meaning I helped him. It is said that so-and-so supported so-and-so: if he supports him and strengthens his back. From this, the poet said: Haven't you seen that Asram was bad and the best of people were in heart and money? The hamza was deleted for ease of reading in Nafi’ and Abu Ja’far. It is possible that the hamza was omitted from their saying arda’a ‘ala al-mi’ah meaning he increased it, so the meaning was that he sent him with me to increase my belief. From this is the saying of the poet: And dark-skinned, his heels are like the pits of reeds, and he has lost an arm's length by ten. The verse is narrated in Al-Sahah with the wording has grown, and the hard qasb, which is the dry fruit that crumbles in the mouth, and it is the hard seed yasdiqni Asim and Haza read yasdiqni in the nominative case as a resumption, or as an attribute of ra’dan, or as a state of the object of arsalahu, and the rest read it in the jussive case as an answer to the command, and Abi and Zaid bin Ali read yasdiqun meaning Pharaoh and his people I fear that they will lie if Aaron is not with me due to my tongue not being able to speak fluently in argument.
28:35: 35- He said, We will strengthen you with your brother, meaning, We will fortify you with him. Strengthening the arm is a metaphor for strengthening. It is said in a supplication for good: May God strengthen your arm, and in its opposite: May God weaken your arm. The majority of scholars read your arm with a fatha on the 'ayn. Al-Husayn and Zayd ibn 'Ali read it with a damma. It was also narrated from Al-Hasan that he read it with a damma and a sukoon. 'Isa ibn 'Umar read it with a fatha on both of them. And We will make for you both an authority, meaning, an argument and proof. Or authority over him and his people. So that they will not reach you with harm, nor will they be able to overcome you with an argument. With Our signs is connected to something omitted: meaning, you will protect yourself from them with Our signs, or go with Our signs. It was said that the ba' is for an oath, and its answer is they will reach. How weak this statement is. Al-Akhfash and Ibn Jarir said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is You and those who follow you will be the victors with Our signs, and the beginning of this affection is the first of them, and in You and those who follow you will be the victors there is good report for them and strengthening of their hearts.
28:36: 36- So when Moses came to them with Our clear signs the clear signs that are clear in meaning, and the reason for using the word signs in Surat Taha has already been mentioned, and it is the plural of stick and hand in Surat Taha, they said, ‘This is nothing but invented magic’ meaning, a fabrication that you have invented yourself, and we have not heard of this that you have brought of the claim of prophethood, or we have not heard of this magic among our forefathers meaning, that it existed or occurred among our forefathers.
28:37: 37- And Moses said, ‘My Lord knows best who has brought guidance from Him.’ He meant himself, and he only used this phrase so that he would not explicitly state what he wanted before explaining the proof to them, and God knows best. The majority read And Moses said with a waw, while Mujahid, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Muhaisin read Moses said without a waw, and this is how it is in the Qur’an copies of the people of Mecca. The Kufians, except for Asim, read Whoever has the final home with a tanween, on the basis that the noun the home is the home of the Hereafter. The masculine form is due to the separation and because it is a metaphorical feminine. The rest read will be with a tanween, which is clearer than the first reading. What is meant by home here is this world, and its final outcome is the Hereafter. The meaning is: whoever has the praiseworthy outcome. The pronoun in Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed is for the matter: that is, the matter is that the wrongdoers will not succeed: that is, they will not attain any good goal. It is possible that what is meant by the home of the Hereafter is the conclusion of good.
28:38: 38- Pharaoh said, O eminent ones, I know of no god for you other than me. The accursed one held on to the mere false claim to deceive his people, even though he knew that his Lord was God Almighty. Then he returned to his arrogance and haughtiness and deluded his people into believing that he was completely powerful, so he said, Then kindle for me, O Haman, the clay, meaning cook the clay for me until it becomes bricks, and make for me a tower, meaning make for me from this clay that you lit until it becomes bricks a tower: meaning a high castle, that I may look up to the God of Moses, meaning ascend to Him. And indeed, I think he is one of the liars. Rising and looking up are the same. It is said that the mountain has risen and it has looked up.
28:39: 39- And he and his soldiers were arrogant upon the land without right. What is meant by land is the land of Egypt, and arrogance is undeserved glorification, rather with aggression because he had no argument to refute what Moses had brought, nor any doubt to present in response to the miracles he had shown. And they thought that they would not return to Us. That is, Pharaoh and his soldiers. What is meant by return is resurrection and the Hereafter. Nafi', Shaibah, Ibn Muhaysin, Hamid, Ya'qub, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read they would not return with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the jim, in the active voice. The rest read it with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the jim, in the passive voice. Abu Ubaid chose the second reading.
28:40: 40- So We seized him and his soldiers after they had rebelled in their disbelief and transgressed the limits therein and cast them into the sea meaning We threw them into the sea. The explanation of this has already been presented. Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers The address is to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: meaning, see, O Muhammad, how was the end of the disbelievers when they were brought to destruction.
28:41: 41- And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire. That is, We made them leaders who are followed and obeyed among the disbelievers. It is as if, by their insistence on disbelief and persistence in it, they are inviting their followers to the Fire because they imitated and followed their path, mimicking them. It was also said that the meaning is: He did not follow their example, that is, whoever came after them would take heed from them and learn a lesson from what they were made to do. The first is more appropriate. And on the Day of Resurrection they will not be aided. That is, no one will aid them and nothing will prevent them from the punishment of God.
28:42: 42- And We pursued them in this world with a curse, meaning expulsion and banishment, or We ordered the servants to curse them, so whoever mentioned them, He cursed them, and the first is more appropriate. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will be among the despised, the despised, the banished, the banished. Abu Ubaidah and Ibn Kaysan said: It means among the destroyed and hated. Abu Zaid said: May God make so-and-so ugly, ugliness, and distance him from all good. Abu Amr said: I made his face ugly with the light vowel meaning I made it ugly with the heavy vowel, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: May God make ugly all the joints, and may God make ugly Yarboa and Darma It was said that it is the ugly one with a deformed creation, and the agent in the deleted day explains it from the ugly ones, and the estimate is: and they were made ugly on the Day of Resurrection, or it is connected to a place in this world: that is, and we followed them with a curse on the Day of Resurrection, or it is connected to a curse on the deletion of an added word: that is, and the curse on the Day of Resurrection.
28:43: 43- And We gave Moses the Scripture meaning the Torah after We destroyed the former generations meaning the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and others. It was also said that it was after We destroyed Pharaoh and his people and caused the earth to swallow Qarun. The accusative case of insights for the people is as an object of the verb or a state: meaning We gave him the Scripture so that people would see the truth through it, or as a state of it being insights for the people so that they would see the truth through it and be guided to it and save themselves through it from misguidance by being guided by it. And as mercy for them from God, He had mercy on them through it, that they might remember these blessings and thank God and believe and answer His call to what is best for them. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, A support that would confirm me, so that he would confirm me. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: When Pharaoh said, O eminent ones, I know of no god for you other than Me, Gabriel said, O Lord, your servant has transgressed, so permit Me to destroy him. Gabriel said, “O Gabriel, he is My servant and he will not precede Me. He has a term that will come. When he said, “I am your Lord, the Most High,” God said, O Gabriel, Your supplication concerning My servant has preceded, and the time of his destruction has come. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Two words were said by Pharaoh, ‘I know of no god for you other than Me,’ and his saying, ‘I am your Lord, the Most High.’ He said: There were forty years between them. Then God seized him as a punishment for the Hereafter and this world.” Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said, I have been informed that Pharaoh was the first to bake bricks. It was narrated by Ibn al-Mundhir on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa’id who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “God has not destroyed a people, a generation, a nation or a village with a punishment from the sky since He sent down the Torah to the face of the earth, except for the village that was transformed into a monkey.” Have you not seen the words of God: And We gave Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations? Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Sa’id, with a chain of transmission ending with him.
28:44: His statement: 44- And you were not on the western side This is a start to explaining the revelation of the Qur'an: that is, and you, O Muhammad, were not on the western side of the mountain, so it is from the deletion of the described and the replacement of the adjective with it, and this is what Al-Zajjaj preferred. Al-Kalbi said: On the western side of the valley: that is, where Moses spoke to his Lord When We decreed to Moses the matter that is, We entrusted him and made the matter firm with him with the message to Pharaoh and his people and you were not among the witnesses to that until you understand its reality and relate it from your own perspective. If it is established that knowing the details of those circumstances could not have been done by being present at them with our Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and witnessing them from him, and it is denied by sound evidence that he did not receive that from anyone other than human beings nor was it taught to him by a teacher from them as we have previously stated, it is clear that it was from God, the Exalted, by revelation from Him to His Messenger by means of the angel who descended with that, then this statement is in the manner of And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary. And it was said that the meaning of When We decreed the matter to Moses is that We charged him and obliged him. And it was said that We informed him that the nation of Muhammad is the best of nations. And the fact that he was on the western side does not necessitate denying his being one of the witnesses, because it is possible for him to be present but not to witness. It was said that what is meant by the seventy witnesses are those whom Moses chose for the meeting.
28:45: 45- But We created generations meaning, We created nations between your time, O Muhammad, and the time of Moses. And life was prolonged for them their respite was prolonged and time was prolonged, so the laws and rulings changed and religions were forgotten, so they abandoned the command of God and forgot His covenant. Similar to this is the saying of the Most High: And the period was prolonged for them, so their hearts hardened. This statement was used as evidence that God, the Most High, had made covenants with Moses regarding Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and regarding belief in him. But when their life was prolonged and centuries after centuries passed, they forgot those covenants and abandoned fulfilling them. And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan meaning, residing among them as Moses did, so that you would read to the people of Mecca their story and relate to them from your own perspective. It is said, thawa, “yathawi,” thawwa, and thawwa, so he is thaw. Dhu al-Rummah said: He was in a state of rest, his clothes were spent in the evenings, and he was bored and tired. Al-Ajaj said: So he stayed where the host entered It means the resident guest, and another said: The Messenger of the House has been waiting for a long time You recite to them Our verses meaning you read to the people of Madyan Our verses and learn from them. It was also said that you reminded them of the promise and the threat. The clause is in the accusative case as a state or a second predicate. It is possible that this clause is the predicate and the subjunctive as a state. Al-Farra' considered it a new sentence as if it was said: And here you are, reciting to your nation. But We were messengers meaning We sent you to the people of Makkah and revealed this report to you, and had it not been for that you would not have known it. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that you did not witness the stories of the prophets nor were they recited to you, but We revealed them to you and related them to you.
28:46: 46- "And you were not by the side of the Mount when We called out" meaning, and you, O Muhammad, were not by the side of the mountain called Mount Tur when We called out to Moses when he came to the appointed time with the seventy. It was also said that the one calling out was the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Wahb said: That is because when God mentioned to Moses the superiority of Muhammad and his nation, he said: "O Lord, show them to me." God said: "You will not reach them, and if you wish, I will call out to them and make you hear their voice." He said: "Yes, O Lord." God said: "O nation of Muhammad." And they responded from the loins of their fathers. So the meaning of the verse according to this is: You, O Muhammad, were not by the side of the Mount when We spoke to Moses and called out to your nation. What indicates this, strengthens it, and makes it more likely will come at the end of the discussion, God willing. "But as a mercy from your Lord," meaning, but We did that as a mercy from Us to you. It was also said that We sent the Qur'an as a mercy to you, and it was also said that We taught you, and it was also said that We made you known. Al-Akhfash said: It is accusative, meaning mercy, based on the source: meaning, but We had mercy on you as a mercy. Al-Zajjaj said: It is an object for which: meaning, We did that to you for the sake of mercy. An-Nahhas said: Meaning, you did not witness the stories of the prophets, nor were they recited to you, but We sent you and revealed them to you for mercy. Al-Kisa’i said: It is the predicate of the understood kana: meaning, but that was mercy. Isa bin Omar and Abu Haywah read rahmah in the nominative case, estimating: but you are mercy. Al-Kisa’i said: The nominative case is that it is the subject of the understood kana, and this is far-fetched unless it is assumed that it is complete. The lam in to warn a people to whom no warner came before you is related to the understood verb, although its estimation is disputed. The people are the people of Mecca, for no warner came to warn them before him, peace and blessings be upon him. The phrase what came to them etc. is an attribute of a people, that they may remember means that they may take heed from your warning.
28:47: 47- And had it not been that a disaster should befall them for what their hands have put forth. “Had it not been” is the prohibition, and that and what is within its scope are in the nominative case as a subject, and its answer is omitted. Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is that We did not send messengers to them: meaning that the motive for sending messengers is to remove their excuses, so it is like His, the Most High, saying: So that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers. Ibn Atiyyah interpreted it as We would have hastened the punishment upon them. Al-Wahidi agreed with him on this interpretation and said: The meaning is that if they had not argued that sending them was not an argument, We would have hastened the punishment upon them because of their disbelief. His saying, and they would say is in apposition to they would be afflicted and among what is within the scope of if only: meaning, they would say, Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger? This second if only is the preparatory one: meaning, why did You not send us a messenger from You? The answer to it is so that we would follow Your signs, and it is in the accusative case with the omission of that because it is an answer to the preparatory one. What is meant by signs are the clear, apparent, revealed signs. The statement is only in apposition to they would be afflicted because it is the reason for sending, but since the punishment was the reason for the statement, and its existence was due to its existence, it is as if it were the reason for sending messengers by means of the statement, and we would be among the believers in these signs. The meaning of the verse is: I and We had punished them because they would have said, The time without messengers has been so long, and God has not sent us a messenger. They thought that this was an excuse for them, but they had no excuse after the report of the messengers had reached them. But We have completed the argument, removed the defect, and perfected the statement by sending you, O Muhammad, to them.
28:48: 48- So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, ‘Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?’ That is, when the truth came to the people of Mecca from God, namely Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and what was revealed to him of the Qur’an, they said, out of stubbornness and false argument: Why was this Messenger not given the like of what was given to Moses, including the Torah revealed to him as a whole? So God answered them by saying: Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? That is, before this statement, or before the appearance of Muhammad. The meaning is that they had disbelieved in the signs of Moses as they had disbelieved in the signs of Muhammad. The phrase They said, ‘Two magicians who cooperated’ is a new sentence intended to confirm their disbelief and stubbornness. What is meant by their saying are two magicians, Moses and Muhammad, and cooperation is cooperation: that is, they cooperated in magic. The pronoun in His statement, or did they not disbelieve refers to the disbelievers of Quraysh, and it was said that it refers to the Jews. The first is more appropriate, because the Jews do not describe Moses as a magician, but rather the infidels of Quraysh and their likes describe him that way, unless what is meant is those who denied the prophethood of Moses, such as Pharaoh and his people, for they described Moses and Aaron as magicians, but they were not Jews. The pronoun could refer to those who disbelieved in Moses and those who disbelieved in Muhammad, because those who disbelieved in Moses described him as a magician, and those who disbelieved in Muhammad also described him as a magician. It was also said that the meaning is: Did the Jews not disbelieve in the time of Muhammad in what Moses was given before him, the good report of Jesus and Muhammad? The majority read it as two magicians, while the Kufians read it as two magicians, meaning the Torah and the Qur’an, or it was said the Gospel and the Qur’an. Al-Farra’ said the first. Abu Zayd said the second. It has been said that the pronoun in Did they not disbelieve refers to the Jews, and that what they meant by their statement two magicians was Jesus and Muhammad. And they said, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in both of them.’ That is, in both Moses and Muhammad, or in Moses and Aaron, or in Moses and Jesus, according to the different opinions. This is according to the majority reading. As for the second reading, what is meant is the Torah and the Qur’an, or the Gospel and the Qur’an. This sentence confirms what preceded it, describing the prophets as magicians, or describing the two books as magicians, and emphasizes that.
28:49: Then God the Almighty commanded His Prophet to say to them a statement that would reveal their helplessness, saying: 49- Say, ‘Then bring a Book from God that is better guidance than both of them, I will follow it.’ That is, say to them, O Muhammad, so bring a Book that is better guidance than the Torah and the Quran. At-Tabba is the answer to the command, and the majority of reciters have made it definitive for that reason. Zayd ibn Ali read at-Tabbahu in the nominative case as a resumption: meaning, then I will follow it. Al-Farra’ said: According to this reading, it is an attribute of the Book, and in this statement there is mockery of it. This also indicates that the reading of the Kufians is stronger than the reading of the majority, because the statement refers to the two Books, not the two Messengers, and the meaning of if you are truthful is if you are truthful in what you described the two Messengers or the two Books with.
28:50: 50- If they do not respond to you meaning they do not do what you have ordered them to do of bringing a book that is better guidance than the two books, and the answer to the condition is know that they only follow their own desires meaning their deviant opinions and false approvals without argument or proof. It was said that the meaning is: If they do not respond to you by believing in what you have brought, and the transitive use of yattajibu with lam is one of the two possibilities. And who is more astray than he who follows his own desires without guidance from God? meaning no one is more astray than him, rather he is the perfect individual in misguidance. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people against themselves by disbelief, denying the prophets, and turning away from the signs of God.
28:51: 51- And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word The majority read Wasalna with emphasis on the sad, while Al-Hasan read it without emphasis. The meaning of the verse is: We made some of it follow others, and We sent messenger after messenger. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: It means We completed. Ibn Uyaynah and Al-Suddi said: We made clear. Ibn Zayd said: We conveyed to them the best of this world with the best of the Hereafter, until it was as if they had seen the Hereafter in this world, and the first is more appropriate. It is taken from joining ropes together, and from it the poet said: So tell the Banu Marwan, why is my covenant bound by a weak rope that keeps on being tied? Imru' al-Qais said: He flips his hands with a conductive thread The pronoun in them refers to the Quraysh, and it was said to the Jews, and it was said to all of them, Perhaps they will remember, so remembering is a reason for their faith, for fear that what happened to those before them will happen to them.
28:52: 52- Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it meaning before the Qur’an, and the relative pronoun is the subject and predicate they believe in it. God Almighty informed us that a group of the Children of Israel believed in the Qur’an, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and the rest of the People of the Scripture who converted to Islam. It was said that the pronoun in those before it refers to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but the first view is more appropriate. The pronoun in it refers to the Qur’an according to the first view, and to Muhammad according to the second view.
28:53: 53- And when it is recited to them, they say, ‘We believe in it.’ That is, when the Qur’an is recited to them, they say, “We believe in it. It is the truth from our Lord.” That is, the truth that we know was revealed from our Lord. Indeed, we were, before it, Muslims. That is, sincere to God through monotheism, or believing in Muhammad and what he brought, based on what we know of his mention in the Torah and the Gospel of the good tidings of him, and that he will be sent at the end of time and the Qur’an will be revealed to him.
28:54: And the reference in His saying: 54- Those will be given their reward twice is to those described with those attributes, and the ba in because they patiently endured is for causality: that is, because of their patience and steadfastness in believing in the first book and the last book, and in the first prophet and the last prophet. And they repel evil with good repelling means repelling: that is, they repel with patience and good speech the harm they encounter. It was said that they repel disobedience with obedience, and it was said that it is with repentance and seeking forgiveness for sins, and it was said that it is with the testimony that there is no god but God against polytheism. And from what We have provided them they spend that is, they spend their money in acts of obedience and in what the Shari'ah has commanded.
28:55: Then He, the Almighty, praised them for turning away from idle talk, saying: 55- And when they hear ill talk, they turn away from it out of honor, purity, and good manners according to the etiquette of the Shari'ah. Similar to this is His statement, the Almighty: And when they pass by ill talk, they pass by with dignity, idle talk here refers to what they hear from the polytheists, who insult them and their religion and mock them. And they say, To us our deeds, and to you your deeds", none of the harm of your disbelief will befall us, and none of the benefit of our faith will befall you. "Peace be upon you", this peace is not meant as a greeting, but rather as a greeting of estrangement, and its meaning is security for you from us and safety. We will not compete with you or respond to what you are doing. Al-Zajjaj said: This was before the command to fight. "We do not seek the ignorant", meaning we do not seek their company. Muqatil said: We do not want to be among the people of ignorance and foolishness. Al-Kalbi said: We do not like the religion that you are following.
28:56: 56- Indeed, you do not guide whom you love of people, and that is not up to you, but God guides whom He wills, His guidance, and He is most knowing of the guided, meaning those who are receptive to guidance and prepared for it. This verse was revealed about Abu Talib, as is proven in the two Sahihs and others. This was previously mentioned in Bara’ah. Al-Zajjaj said: The commentators agreed that it was revealed about Abu Talib, and it has been established in the fundamental principles that consideration is given to the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the cause, so Abu Talib is included in this primarily.
28:57: 57- And they said, 'If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land.' That is, the polytheists of Quraysh and those who followed them said, If we enter your religion, O Muhammad, we will be snatched away from our land. That is, the Arabs will snatch us away from our land, meaning Mecca, and we will have no power over them. This is just one of their false excuses and meaningless pretexts. Snatching basically means to be taken away quickly. The majority of scholars read snatching in the subjunctive mood as a response to the condition, while Al-Manqari read it in the nominative case as a resumption. Then God responded to them with a response that included a question of rebuke and reprimand, saying, Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary? That is, have We not made for them a secure sanctuary? Abu Al-Baqa' said: He made it transitive because it means to make, as He clearly stated in His statement, Have they not seen that We have made a sanctuary? Then He described this sanctuary by saying, To it are gathered the fruits of all things. That is, the fruits of different kinds are gathered to it from the various lands and carried to it. The majority read yubba with a ta'i'ah, considering the masculine nature of everything and the presence of a barrier between the verb and thamarat. Also, the feminization of thamarat is not real. Abu Ubaid chose the reading of the majority for what we mentioned, and Nafi' read it with a ta'i'ah, considering thamarat. The majority also read thamarat with two fathahs, and Abaan read it with two dhammahs, the plural of thamaar with two dhammahs. It was read with a fathah on the tha' and a sukoon on the meem, rizqan min laduna in the accusative case as a verbal noun because the meaning of yubba is: We provide for them. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as an object for a deleted verb, meaning We send it to them as a provision from Us. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a state, meaning providers. But most of them do not know due to their extreme ignorance, increased heedlessness, and lack of contemplation regarding their afterlife and guidance, because they are among those whose hearts God has sealed and whose vision has placed a veil. Al-Faryabi, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym, and Al-Bayhaqi together in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah regarding his statement, And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called, that he said: They were called, O nation of Muhammad, I gave to you before you asked Me, and I responded to you before you called upon Me. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Asakir narrated it from him through another chain of transmission with a similar wording. Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Dala’il, Abu Nasr Al-Sajzi in Al-Ibanah, and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Abasa that he said: “I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the statement, ‘And you were not by the Mount when We called,’ what was the call and what was the mercy? He said: ‘God wrote it two thousand years before He created His creation, then He placed him on His Throne, then He called: ‘O nation of Muhammad, My mercy preceded My wrath. I gave to you before you asked Me, and I forgave you before you sought My forgiveness. So whoever among you meets Me and testifies that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is My servant and Messenger, truthful, I will admit him into Paradise.’” Al-Khatli narrated in Al-Dibaj on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d Al-Sa`idi, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah regarding the statement, ‘And you were not by the Mount when We called,’ with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that they called: ‘O nation of Muhammad, you did not call upon Us when We responded to you, nor did you ask Us when We gave to you.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “God called out: ‘O nation of Muhammad, answer your Lord.’ They answered while they were in the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers until the Day of Resurrection, and they said: ‘At your service, you are truly our Lord, and we are truly your servants.’ He said: ‘You have spoken the truth. I am your Lord, and you are truly my servants. I pardoned you before you called upon me, and I gave to you before you asked me. So whoever among you meets me bearing witness that there is no god but God will enter Paradise.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The one who perished during the interval will say: ‘O Lord, no book or messenger came to me.’ Then he recited this verse: ‘Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger?’” Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: They said, ‘Two magicians who support each other…’ etc., that they are the People of the Book. Indeed, we disbelieve in all of them, meaning in the two Books: the Torah and the Criterion. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, al-Bawardi, and Ibn Qani’ narrated the three in their dictionaries of the Companions. At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Rifa’ah al-Qurazi who said: “The verse, ‘And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word that perhaps they will be reminded’ up to the verse, ‘Those will be given their reward twice’ was revealed regarding ten men, of whom I am one. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, ‘Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it’. He said: This means those of the People of the Scripture who believed in Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There are three who will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Scripture who believed in the first and the last Scripture; a man who had a female slave whom he educated and taught her well, then he freed her and married her; and a slave who worshipped his Lord well and was sincere to his master.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Al-Musayyab, and Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that his statement, Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, was revealed about Abu Talib when he refused to convert to Islam. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that some people from Quraysh said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, If we follow you, the people will snatch us away. So the verse, And they said, ‘If we follow the guidance with you,’ was revealed. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, The fruits of all things are brought to Him, meaning the fruits of the earth.
28:58: His statement: 58- And how many a city have We destroyed meaning, of the people of a city who lived in ease, comfort, and prosperity, then they became arrogant and were destroyed. Al-Zajjaj said: Arrogance is transgression when one is in comfort. Ata' said: They lived in arrogance, consuming God's provisions and worshipping idols. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Mazini said: The meaning of her livelihood became arrogant is she became arrogant in her livelihood. So when it was deleted in a transitive verb like in His statement: And Moses chose his people, Al-Farra' said: It is in the accusative case for explanation, just as you say: Malik and his arrogance made you arrogant. Its equivalent is in His statement: Except for he who makes a fool of himself, and the accusative case of definite nouns for differentiation is not permissible according to the Basrans, because the meaning of explanation is for the indefinite noun to indicate the genus. It was said that its livelihood is in the accusative case because it includes the meaning of ignorance. Those were their dwellings, which were not inhabited after them except for a little while. That is, no one inhabited them after them except for a short time, like someone who passes by it as a traveler, as he stays there for a day or part of a day, or no one remained to inhabit it except for a few days due to the evil of what happened in it of their sins. It was said that the exception refers to the dwellings: that is, no one was inhabited after the death of its people except a few of the dwellings, and most of them are in ruins. This is what Al-Farra’ said, and it is a weak opinion. And We were the inheritors from them because they did not leave an heir to inherit their homes and wealth. The location of the clause was not inhabited is the nominative case as a second predicate of the demonstrative pronoun. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a state.
28:59: 59- And your Lord would not destroy the cities until He had sent to their mother a Messenger reciting to them Our verses. That is, it is not correct nor right that God would destroy the disbelieving cities - that is, the disbelieving people - until He had sent to their mother a Messenger to warn them and recite to them the verses of God speaking of what God has enjoined upon them and what He has prepared of reward for the obedient and punishment for the disobedient. The meaning of their mother is: the largest and greatest of them. He singled out the greatest of them for being sent to because in it were the nobles of the people, the people of understanding and opinion, and in it were the kings and nobles. Thus, in this regard, it became like the mother of the cities around it. Al-Hasan said: The Mother of Villages is the first of them.
