It was said that what is meant by Umm al-Qura here is Mecca, as in His statement: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind 12:13. The explanation of what this verse includes has already been presented at the end of Surat Yusuf. The phrase reciting to them Our verses is in the accusative case as a state: that is, reciting to them and informing them that the punishment will descend upon them if they do not believe. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers 12:13. This phrase is conjoined with the previous phrase, and the exception is devoid of the most general of conditions: that is, We would not destroy the people of the cities after We sent to their mother a messenger calling them to the truth except while they were wrongdoers and deserved to be destroyed for their persistence in disbelief after they had been excused and the argument had been confirmed against them, as in His statement: And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly while their people were righteous.
28:60: Then He, the Most High, said: 60- And whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment. The address is to the disbelievers of Mecca: meaning, whatever you have been given of things is the enjoyment of worldly life, which you enjoy for the duration of your life or some of your life, then you are removed from it or it is removed from you. In any case, that will come to an end and pass away. And what is with God of His reward and recompense is better than that transient and fleeting because it is pure pleasure devoid of any turbidity. And more enduring because it lasts forever, and this passes quickly. Do you not understand? That what is enduring is better than what is fleeting, and that which contains pure, unmixed pleasure is better than pleasures tainted with turbidity that are marred by ailments of the body and heart. It was read with the accusative of enjoyment as a source: meaning, then you enjoy the enjoyment of life. Abu Amr read they understand with the subjunctive, and the rest read it with the subjunctive as an address, and their reading is more preferable because of His saying: And what you have been given.
28:61: 61- Is he to whom We have promised a good promise which he will surely attain? That is, We have promised him Paradise and the countless blessings it contains, which he will attain, that is, he will inevitably attain, for God does not break His promise. Like one whom We have given enjoyment of the enjoyment of worldly life, so he was given some of what he wanted, even though it quickly vanished and was spoiled. Then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth. This is connected to His statement We have given enjoyment, and is included with it in the scope of the relative clause, emphasizing the denial of similarity and establishing it. The meaning is: Then on the Day of Resurrection he whom We have given enjoyment will be among those brought forth by the Fire. The specification of those brought forth to those who were brought forth by the punishment is required by the situation, and the question is for denial, that is, their situation is not the same, for the one promised Paradise will inevitably attain what he was promised, even though he will not miss out on his share of this world. This is the situation of the believer. As for the state of the disbeliever, he is only subject to enjoyment of some worldly things in which he and the believer are equal, and each one of them gets his share of it, while he is heading to the Fire. Are they equal? The majority of scholars read then with a damma on the ha’. Al-Kisa’i and Qalun read it with a sukoon on the ha’, making lathum follow the rules of waw and fa’.
28:62: And the nominative case of day in His statement: 62- And the Day He will call to them in conjunction with the Day of Resurrection or by implying remember: meaning the day God Almighty will call to these polytheists and say to them Where are My partners whom you claimed would support you and intercede for you? And the two objects of they claim are omitted: meaning you claim them to be My partners because the statement indicates them.
28:63: 63- Those upon whom the word has come into effect will say, meaning the word of punishment has come into effect upon them, and they are the leaders of misguidance who took lords other than God. This is what Al-Kalbi said. Qatadah said: They are the devils. Our Lord, these are those whom we led astray, meaning we invited them to misguidance, meaning the followers. We led them astray as we were led astray, meaning we led them astray as we were led astray. We disavow them to You, meaning that the leaders of misguidance, or the devils, disavowed those who obeyed them. Al-Zajjaj said: They disavowed each other and became enemies, as God the Most High said: Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another. “These” is the subject, and those whom we led astray is its description. The pronoun is omitted: meaning we led them astray. The predicate is we led them astray, and as we led them astray is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun. It was said that the report of these is that we were led astray, and as for We led them astray as we were led astray, then it is a new statement to confirm what came before it. Abu Ali al-Farsi preferred this, and the first view was objected to, and Abu al-Baqa’ responded to his objection, They did not worship us, but rather they worshipped their desires. It was said that what in what they were is a source: that is, we disavow to you their worship of us, and the first is more appropriate.
28:64: 64- And it will be said, ‘Call upon your partners.’ That is, this was said to the unbelievers among the children of Adam, meaning: Seek aid from your gods whom you used to worship besides God in this world, so that they may aid you and protect you. So they called upon them, at that time, but they did not respond to them, nor did they benefit them in any way. And they saw the punishment, that is, the one who follows and the one followed, for it had overtaken them. If only they were guided. Al-Zajjaj said: The answer to if is omitted, and the meaning is: If only they were guided, that would have saved them, and they would not have seen the punishment. It was also said that the meaning is: If only they were guided, they would not have called upon them. It was also said that the meaning is: If only they were guided by some means, they would have warded off the punishment. It was also said that the time has come for them to be guided, if only they were guided. Others said otherwise. The first is more appropriate.
28:65: And the Day in His statement: 65- And the Day He will call to them and say, ‘What was your answer to the messengers?’ is connected to what preceded it: What was your answer to those prophets sent to you when they conveyed My messages to you?
28:66: 66- So the report was hidden from them that Day meaning the arguments were hidden from them until they became like the blind who cannot be guided. The original is they were blind to the report, but it was reversed for emphasis. report is information. He called their arguments report because they were not evidence at all, but rather stories and tales. So they will not ask each other they will not ask each other, nor will they utter an argument, nor will they know how to answer, because God had excused them in this world, so they will have no excuse or argument on the Day of Resurrection. The majority of scholars read Amayt with a fatha on the 'ayn and a soft 'mim'. Al-A'mash and Janah ibn Hubaysh read it with a damma on the 'ayn and a shaddah on the 'mim.
28:67: 67- But as for he who repents, believes, and does righteousness, he may be among the successful. If he repents from polytheism, believes in what the messengers brought, performs the obligatory duties, and avoids sins, then perhaps he will be among the successful: that is, those who achieve their aspirations for happiness in both abodes. And perhaps if it originally refers to hope, then it is obligatory from God, as is the custom of the honorable. It has been said that the hope is from the aforementioned repentant person, not from God, the Most High.
28:68: 68- And your Lord creates what He wills meaning He creates it and chooses what He wills to choose. He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. This is connected to the mention of the partners whom they worshipped and chose: meaning the choice is up to God. They had no choice meaning the right to choose. It was said that what is meant by the verse is that no one among God’s creation has the right to choose, rather the choice is up to God Almighty. It was said that this verse is an answer to their saying: Why was this Qur’an not sent down to some great man from the two cities? It was also said that this verse is an answer to the Jews when they said: If the messenger to Muhammad had been other than Gabriel, we would have believed in him. Al-Zajjaj said: The pause at and he chooses is complete, as ma is a negative. He said: It is possible for ma to be in the accusative case of he chooses, and the meaning is: and he chooses the one in whom they have the best choice. The first is correct due to their consensus on the pause. Ibn Jarir said: The interpretation of the verse is: and he chooses for his guardianship the best of his creation, and this is extremely weak. Ibn Atiyyah permitted that it was is complete, and they have the best is a renewed sentence. This is also very far-fetched. It was said that ma is a source: that is, he chooses their choice, and the source is in the position of the direct object: that is, and he chooses their choice, and this is like an explanation of Ibn Jarir’s words. The first of these interpretations is the most correct, and similar to it is the statement of the Most High: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option. “Option” means choice, just as ominous omens means superstition. These are two nouns that are used as a source. Then the Most High declared Himself pure and said: Glory be to God, meaning He is pure in a way that is specific to Him, without anyone disputing with Him or sharing with Him. And exalted is He above what they associate with Him, meaning above those whom they make partners with Him, or above associating others with Him.
28:69: 69- And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal meaning what they hide of polytheism, or enmity towards the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), or everything they conceal that contradicts the truth, and what they declare meaning what they reveal of that. The majority of scholars read takun with a damma on the ta’ above and a kasra on the kaf. Ibn Muhaisin and Hamid read it with a fatha on the ta’ above and a damma on the kaf.
28:70: Then He, glory be to Him, praised Him for His Oneness and His uniqueness in deserving praise, saying: 70- “And He is God, there is no god but Him. To Him is due praise in the first [world] and the Hereafter,” meaning the Hereafter. And His is the judgment, He judges between His servants as He wills, without any partner. And to Him you will be returned, by resurrection. He will reward the doer of good for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. You will not return to anyone other than Him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, And We would not destroy cities except while their people were wrongdoers, that he said: God said, “We did not destroy a city because of faith, but He destroyed cities because of wrongdoing when its people were wrongdoers. If Mecca had believed, they would not have been destroyed with those who were destroyed, but they lied and were wrongdoers, and that is why they were destroyed.” Muslim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, God, the Almighty, says, ‘O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me.’ The hadith in full. Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id az-Zuhd on the authority of Abd bin Ubayd bin Umair, who said, “People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection hungrier than ever, thirstier than ever, and nakeder than ever. So whoever feeds for the sake of God, God will feed him. Whoever clothes for the sake of God, God will clothe him. Whoever gives drink for the sake of God, God will give him drink. Whoever is pleasing to God, God will be pleased with him.” Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, And the report was hidden from them, meaning the proofs. So they did not ask about one another, meaning about lineages. It has been proven in Sahih that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught the prayer of istikharah, how to pray it and supplicate for it, so we will not prolong the mention of it.
28:71: His saying: 71- Say, ‘Have you considered’ meaning, tell me, if God made the night continuous for you. Continuous is permanent and ongoing, from the root word sarad, which means following, so the mim is an extra letter, and from it is the saying of Tarafa: By your life, my days and nights are not filled with sorrow, nor are my sorrows with you eternal. It was said that its meem is original and its weight is fa`lal, not fa`mal, and this is what is apparent. He, the Most High, explained to them that He had provided them with the means of livelihood so that they would be grateful for the blessing. If the time in which they live were always night until the Day of Resurrection, they would not be able to move around and seek what they need to sustain life, such as food, drink, and clothing. Then He bestowed His favor upon them by saying: Is there a god other than God who can bring you light? That is, do you have a god among the gods that you worship who is able to lift this permanent darkness from you with light? That is, a light in which you seek livelihood, see what you need, improve your fruits, grow your crops, and live. Do you not hear? This speech, hearing understanding, acceptance, contemplation, and reflection.
28:72: Then when He finished thanking them for the existence of the day, He thanked them for the existence of the night, saying: 72- “Say, ‘Have you considered: if God made the day continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection?’” That is, He made the entirety of your life day until the Day of Resurrection. What god other than God could bring you a night in which to rest? That is, in which you would rest from fatigue and exhaustion and rest from what you are engaged in of seeking a livelihood and earning. Do you not see? This great benefit is a vision of admonition so that you may turn away from what you are doing of worshipping other than God. And if they acknowledge that no one is able to do that except God, the Almighty, then the proof is binding on them and the fallen doubts they cling to are invalidated. Rather, the Almighty linked the statement Do you not hear with the light because hearing perceives what sight does not perceive of perceiving its benefits and describing its benefits. And He linked the statement Do you not see with the night because sight perceives what hearing does not perceive of that.
28:73: 73- And out of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein meaning at night and that you may seek of His bounty meaning during the day by striving to earn money and that you may be grateful meaning so that you may be grateful for God’s blessing upon you. This verse is from the category of twisting and spreading as in the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: As if the hearts of birds are moist and dry, jujubes and old straw near their nest. Know that even if it is possible to rest during the day and to seek sustenance at night, when the moon rises above the earth, or when illuminated by something that has light, such as a lamp, this is rare and inconsistent with what people are accustomed to, so it is not to be taken into account.
28:74: 74- And the Day He will call to them and say, ‘Where are My partners whom you used to claim?’ God Almighty repeated this because the two situations are different, because they will be called one time and call upon the idols, and they will be called another time and they will be silent. In this repetition also there is rebuke after rebuke and reprimand after rebuke.
28:75: And His statement: 75- And We will extract from every nation a witness is in apposition to calls, and it came in the past tense to indicate verification, and the meaning is: And We will extract from every nation a witness who will testify against them. Mujahid said: They are the prophets, and it was said: The just ones of every nation, but the first is more appropriate. Similar to this is His statement, the Most High: How will it be then when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? Then the Most High explained what He says to each of these nations by His statement: "Then We said: Produce your proof" meaning your argument and evidence that I have partners, so at that point they acknowledged and were silent about establishing the proof, and thus He said: And they knew that the truth belongs to God in divinity and that He alone has no partner, and what they were inventing was lost to them meaning what they were inventing of lies in this world, that God had partners who deserved to be worshipped, was nullified and gone.
28:76: Then the Almighty followed the speech of the people of misguidance with the story of Qarun, because of what it contained of wondrous power and amazing creation, saying: 76- Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses. Qarun, on the weight of Fa’ool, is a foreign name that is not Arabic due to its foreignness and proper noun nature. It is not Arabic and is derived from Qaranta. Al-Zajjaj said: If Qarun was from Qaranta something, it would have been declined. Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah and others said: He was the son of Imran bin Qahath. Ibn Ishaq said: He was the paternal uncle of Moses from his father and mother, so he made him a brother to Imran, and they were the sons of Al-Samiri, and he rebelled against the obedience of Moses. This is the meaning of His statement: Then he transgressed against them, meaning he exceeded the limit in his tyranny and arrogance towards them, and rebelled against them and rebelled against the obedience of Moses and disbelieved in God. Ad-Dahhak said: His transgression against the Children of Israel was his belittling of them due to his great wealth and children. Qatada said: His transgression was due to his attributing the wealth that God had given him to himself due to his knowledge and cunning. It was also said that he was an agent for Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, so he transgressed against them and oppressed them. It was also said that his transgression was for something other than that, which does not fit the meaning of the verse. And We gave him of the treasures is the plural of kanz which is saved money. Ata’ said: He acquired a treasure from the treasures of Joseph. It was also said that he was an alchemist. What is in His statement its keys is a relative pronoun, its clause is in and what is within its scope, and that is why it was broken. Al-Akhfash Al-Saghir reported from the Kufians who forbade making the broken word and what is within its scope a relative clause for alladhina and they found that ugly because it occurs in the Noble Book in this place. The keys are the plural of miftaha with a broken vowel, which is that with which one opens. It was also said that what is meant by miftaha are the treasuries, so its singular is miftaha with a fatha on the mim. Al-Wahidi said: Most of the commentators say that the keys are the treasuries, like His statement: And with Him are the keys of the unseen. He said: This is the choice of Al-Zajjaj, who said: What is most likely in the interpretation is that his keys are the treasuries of his wealth. Others said: It is the plural of key, which is what opens a door. This is the saying of Qatada and Mujahid: That a band of strong men may bear it. This sentence is the predicate of in and it and its subject and predicate are the relative clause of ma. It is said: Na’a bi-hamluhu if he carried it heavily, and it is said: Na’a bi-al-haml if it weighed me down. The meaning is: Carrying keys weighs them down. Abu Ubaidah said: This is from the inverted form, and the meaning is: So that a band of strong men may bear it meaning that they may carry it. Abu Zaid said: Na’utu bi-al-haml if you carried it. The poet said: We have found a successor, a miserable successor, a slave who, when he is unable to bear the burden, stops. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of natu’a bil-‘asaba is to make them sway with its weight, as one says: he goes away with misery and misery goes away, and dhahabtu bih I went away with it and dhahabtuhu I brought it and aja’tuhu I came with it and natu’a bih I brought it and ana’tuhu... Al-Farra’ said: It is Musa, and it is a plural meaning one. The meaning of do not rejoice is: do not be arrogant and do not be vain. God does not like the arrogant, the arrogant and wicked who do not thank God for what He has given them. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is do not rejoice over money, because rejoicing over money does not fulfill its right. It was said that the meaning is: do not spoil it, as the poet said: If you continue to perform a trust and carry another, the deposits will make you happy. That is, I have spoiled you. Al-Zajjaj said: The happy ones and the joyful ones are the same. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of the happy ones is those who are in a state of joy, and the joyful ones are those who will rejoice in the future. Mujahid said: The meaning of do not rejoice is do not seek to be miserly, for God does not like the happy ones who seek to be miserly. It was also said that it means: do not be miserly, for God does not like the miserly.
28:77: 77- And seek, through that which God has given you, the home of the Hereafter. That is, seek the home of the Hereafter through the wealth God has given you, and spend it in that which pleases God, not in arrogance and transgression. It was also read and followed by and do not forget your share of this world. The majority of commentators said: It means that one works in this world for his hereafter, and a person’s share is his lifespan and righteous deeds. Al-Zajjaj said: It means do not forget to work for your hereafter, because the true share of a person in this world is what he works for for his hereafter. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: It means do not waste your share of this world in enjoying what is lawful and seeking it. This is more closely aligned with the meaning of the Qur’anic verse. And do good as God has done good to you. That is, do good to God’s servants as God has done good to you with the blessings of this world that He has bestowed upon you. It was also said: Obey God and worship Him as He has bestowed blessings upon you. This is supported by what was proven in the two Sahihs and others: “Gabriel asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about ihsan, and he said: It is that you worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you.” And do not seek to cause corruption on earth, meaning do not commit sins against God. Indeed, God does not like corrupters on earth.
28:78: 77- He said, It was only given to me because of knowledge I have." Qarun said: This statement is in response to those who advised him as mentioned above: that is, I was only given the money because of my knowledge. His statement "for knowledge is in the accusative case as a state, and with me is either an adverbial phrase for I was given it" or a relative clause of the knowledge. This knowledge which he made the cause of what he attained in this world. It was said that it is the knowledge of the Torah, and it was said that it is his knowledge of the various forms of earnings and trade, and it was said that it is knowledge of treasures and buried treasures, and it was said that it is the knowledge of alchemy, and it was said that the meaning is: God gave me these treasures because of His knowledge that I deserved them due to the superiority of His knowledge over me. Al-Zajjaj chose this and rejected the rest. Then God responded to his statement by saying: "Did he not know that God destroyed before him generations who were mightier than him in strength and greater in accumulation? What is meant by generations are previous nations, and the meaning of greater in accumulation" is greater in accumulation of wealth than him. If wealth or strength indicated virtue, God would not have destroyed them. It was also said that strength refers to tools, and the plural is helpers. This statement is not intended to rebuke and reprimand Qarun, because he had read the Torah and learned the knowledge of the earlier generations and God’s destruction of them. And the criminals will not be asked about their sins, meaning they will not be asked to seek forgiveness, as in His statement, nor will they be asked to repent. “They will not be among those who are forgiven.” Rather, they will be asked to rebuke and reprimand, as in His statement, By your Lord, We will surely question them all. Mujahid said: The angels will not be asked about the criminals tomorrow, because they will be known by their appearance, as they will be gathered with black faces and blue eyes. Qatadah said: The criminals will not be asked about their sins because they are obvious and numerous, rather they will enter the Fire. It was also said that the criminals of this nation will not be asked about the sins of previous nations.
28:79: 79- So he came out to his people in his finery. The fa is for conjunction with qala and what is between them is an interruption. In his finery is related to came out, or to an omitted word which is a state of the subject of came out. The commentators have mentioned different narrations about this finery in which he came out. What is meant is that he came out in a finery that dazzled those who saw it, and for this reason those who looked at him wished that they had the same as what God said about them in His saying: Those who desire the life of this world and its finery said, “Oh, would that we had like that which Qarun has been given. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.” That is, an abundant share of this world. There is a difference of opinion about those who said this statement. Some say they were believers at that time, and others say they were infidels.
28:80: 80- And those who were given knowledge said, and they were the rabbis of the Children of Israel, they said to those who wished, Woe to you! The reward of God is better, meaning God’s reward is better than what you wish for, for whoever believes and does righteousness, so do not wish for the fleeting worldly goods that do not last, nor will he attain it, meaning this is the word that the rabbis spoke. It was said that the pronoun refers to righteous deeds, and it was said that it refers to Paradise, except the patient, in obeying God and those who are patient with themselves from desires.
28:81: 81- So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. It is said: The place was swallowed up means it went into the earth. The earth swallowed him up means it disappeared into it. The meaning is that God Almighty hid him and hid his home in the earth. So he had no company to help him other than God. That is, he had no group to repel that from him. Nor was he in himself among the victors among those who resisted the swallowing up that which befell him.
28:82: 82- And those who had wished for his place yesterday meaning a short time ago began to say, ‘It is as if God expands provision for whom He wills among His servants or restricts it’ meaning each one of them says it regretting what he had wished for. An-Nahhas said: The best thing that has been said about this is what Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, Yunus, and Al-Kisa’i said, that the people became aware and said, Woe. And the regretful Arab says during his regret, Woe. Al-Jawhari said: Woe is a word of amazement, and it is also said, Woe. “Wa” may also be used with ka’ana the lightened or stressed ka’ana and ka’ana God. Al-Khalil said: It is separated, so you say wa, then you begin and say ka’ana. Al-Farra’ said: It is a word of confirmation, like you say, Do you not see the creation and kindness of God? It was said that it is a word of warning like ala. Qatrib said: It is only woe to you, so its lam was dropped. From this is the saying of Antarah: The saying of the knights, Woe to Antar, has healed my soul and cured its illness. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The meaning of "Waykaan God" is: I know that God. Al-Qutaybi said: Its meaning in the Himyarite language is mercy, and it was said that it means "Have you not seen?" It was narrated on the authority of al-Kisa'i that he said: It is a word that expresses grief, "Had it not been that God had bestowed His mercy upon us and protected us from the same arrogance and transgression that Qarun was subject to, and had not punished us for our desires, and He would have swallowed us up" as He swallowed him up. Hafs read "lakhsaf indicating the subject, while the rest read it in the passive form, Waykaanhu la yaflah al-kafirun" meaning they would not succeed in any of their demands.
28:84: 84- Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it meaning that God will reward him ten times as much as it to seven hundred times as much. And whoever brings an evil deed - those who do evil will not be recompensed except for what they used to do meaning except like what they used to do. So the noun was omitted and the noun to which it was added was used in its place. The meaning of this verse was explained previously in Surat An-Naml.
28:85: 85- Indeed, He Who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an The commentators said: meaning, He revealed the Qur’an to you. Al-Zajjaj said: He has enjoined upon you to act in accordance with what the Qur’an requires. The meaning of the statement is: He has enjoined upon you the rulings and obligations of the Qur’an. He will bring you back to a place of return The majority of commentators said: meaning, to Mecca. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Zuhri and Al-Hasan said: The meaning is: He will bring you back to the Day of Resurrection, and this is the preferred choice of Al-Zajjaj. It is said, Between you and me is the return: meaning, the Day of Resurrection, because people return to it alive. Abu Malik and Abu Salih said: He will bring you back to a place of return, to Paradise. Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri said the same, and it was narrated from Mujahid. It was said about the return to death: Say, ‘My Lord knows best who has brought guidance and who is in clear error.’ This is an answer to the infidels of Mecca when they said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, You are in error. What is meant by who has brought guidance is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and who is in clear error is the polytheists. It is better to interpret the verse in a general way, and that God Almighty knows the condition of each of these two groups and will reward them according to what they deserve of good and evil.
28:86: 86- And you did not expect that the Book would be revealed to you meaning, you did not expect that We would send you to the servants and send down the Qur’an to you. It was also said, You did not expect that the Book would be revealed to you by returning you to your place of return. The exception in His statement, except as a mercy from your Lord is disconnected, meaning, but its revelation to you is a mercy from your Lord. It is also permissible for it to be connected based on the meaning, as if it was said, And the Book was not revealed to you except for the sake of mercy from your Lord. The first is more appropriate, and Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ affirmed it. So do not be an auxiliary to the disbelievers meaning, an assistant to them, and in it is an allusion to others from the nation. It was also said that what is meant is, Do not be an auxiliary to them by being accommodating to them.
28:87: 87- “And let not the disbelievers, their sayings, their lies, and their harm turn you away, O Muhammad, from reciting the verses of God and acting upon them after they have been revealed to you and made obligatory upon you.” The majority of scholars read the verse with a fatha on the ya’ and a kasra on the sad, from asdahu, meaning to prevent. And call to your Lord, meaning call people to God and to His Oneness, to act upon His obligations, and to avoid sins. And do not be among those who associate others with God. This is an allusion to someone other than Him, as mentioned above, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was never among those who associate others with God under any circumstances.
29:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Ankabut, it consists of sixty-nine verses There is a difference of opinion as to whether it is Meccan or Medinan, or part of it is Meccan and part of it Medinan. There are three opinions: The first is that it is all Meccan. This was reported by Ibn Ad-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh also reported it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr, and this is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata’, and Jabir ibn Zayd. The second opinion is that it is all Medinan. Al-Qurtubi said: This is one of the two opinions of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. The third opinion is that it is Meccan except for ten verses from the beginning. Al-Qurtubi said: This is one of the two opinions of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, and it is the opinion of Yahya ibn Salam. It was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib that it was revealed between Mecca and Medina, and this is a fourth opinion. Ad-Daraqutni reported in As-Sunan on the authority of Aishah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pray during a solar or lunar eclipse with four rak’ahs and four prostrations, reciting in the first rak’ah Surah Al-Ankaboot or Ar-Rum, and in the second Surah Ya-Seen. 1- Alif, Lam, Meem. The opening of this Surah was discussed in detail in Surah Al-Baqarah.
29:2: And the question in his saying: 2- Do people think is for reprimand and rebuke, and that they will be left is in the accusative case according to, and it and what it enters into take the place of the two objects according to the saying of Sibawayh and the majority, and that they say is in the accusative case on the assumption: that they say, or that they say, or that they say, and it was said that it is a substitute for that they will be left, and the meaning of the verse: that people will not be left without testing or trial that they say, 'We believe,' and they will not be tested meaning that they will not be tested in their wealth and themselves, and the matter is not as they thought, rather He must test them until the sincere is distinguished from the hypocrite, and the truthful from the liar, so the verse is intended to deny that calculation and exclude it, and to clarify that testing with various types of obligations and other things is necessary. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, Do they think that we will be satisfied with them saying, ‘We are believers’ only, and that they will not be tested with that which will reveal the truth of their faith? This is His statement, that they should be left to say, ‘We believe’ and they will not be tested. Al-Suddi, Qatadah, and Mujahid said: That is, that they will not be tested in their wealth and lives by being killed and tortured. A discussion of the reason for the revelation of these verses will clarify the meaning of what we have mentioned. Its apparent meaning is that it includes all people of faith. Even if the reason is specific, then the generality of the wording should be taken into consideration, as we have stated more than once. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: Even though this verse was revealed for a specific reason, it will remain with regard to the ummah of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and its ruling will remain in effect for the rest of time. This is because the trial from God will remain in the borders of the Muslims through captivity, harming the enemy, and other things.”
29:3: 3- And We have certainly tried those before them meaning this is God’s way with His servants and that He tests the believers of this nation as He tested the nations before them, as the Quran has mentioned in more than one instance in the stories of the prophets and the trials that befell their people and the things with which God tested their followers and those who believed in them. So God will surely make evident those who are truthful in their statement, We believe, “and He will surely make evident the liars” among them in that. The majority of scholars read So He will surely make evident with a fat-ha on the ya’ and the lam in both instances, meaning that God will make evident the truthful and the liar in their statement and distinguish between them. Ali ibn Abi Talib read it with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the lam in both instances. The meaning is that He will make evident the two groups in the Hereafter by their stations, or He will make evident the people’s truthfulness of those who are truthful and expose the liars with their lies, or He will set for each group a mark by which it will be known and distinguished from others.
29:4: 4- Or do those who do evil deeds think that they will outstrip Us? That is, that they will escape Us and be unable to do so before We hold them accountable for what they do? This is the main object of hasaba and am is the disjunctive particle. Evil is that which they judge. That is, evil is the judgment they make. Al-Zajjaj said: Ma is in the accusative case meaning evil is a thing or judgment they judge. He said: It is permissible for ma to be in the nominative case meaning evil is a thing or judgment, their judgment. Ibn Kaysan made it a verbal noun meaning evil is their judgment.
29:5: 5- Whoever hopes to meet God means whoever is hopeful, and hope means greed. This was said by Saeed bin Jubair. It was also said that hope here means fear. Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars of interpretation agreed that the meaning is: whoever fears death. And from this is the saying of Al-Hudhali: If a wasp stings him, he will not feel its sting. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of whoever hopes for the meeting with God is: whoever hopes for the reward of meeting God, meaning the reward of arriving at Him. So hope in this sense means expectation. For indeed, God’s term will surely come meaning the appointed time for resurrection will inevitably come. Muqatil said: It means the Day of Resurrection, and the meaning is: Let him work for that day as in His statement: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work. The whom in the verse here may be conditional and the reward is For indeed, God’s term will surely come. It may also be relative and the fa entered into its answer to liken it to the conditional. In the verse there is promise, threat, intimidation and encouragement that is not hidden. And He is the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, The All-Knowing of what they conceal and what they declare.
29:6: 6- And whoever strives, strives only for himself meaning, whoever strives against the disbelievers and strives against himself by being patient in performing acts of obedience, then he strives only for himself: meaning, the reward for that is for him and not for anyone else, and none of the benefit of that returns to God, the Exalted. Indeed, God is free from need of the worlds so he has no need of their obedience, just as their disobedience does not harm Him. It was said that the meaning is: And whoever strives against his enemy for himself, not seeking thereby the face of God, so God has no need of his striving, but the first is more appropriate.
29:7: 7- And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds meaning, We will cover them with forgiveness because of the righteous deeds they did, and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do meaning, with the best reward for their deeds. It was also said, with the best reward for their deeds. What is meant by best is merely a description, not a preference, so that their reward for good is not something that is kept silent about. It was also said that He will give them more than they did and better than it, as in His statement: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof.
29:8: 8- And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, goodness. The word good is in the accusative case as an adjective for a deleted verbal noun: meaning, enjoining goodness as an exaggeration, or as an omission of the complement: meaning, of goodness. This is the doctrine of the Basrans, while the Kufians said: Its meaning is, And We have enjoined upon man to do good, so it is the object of an implied verb. From this comes the saying of the poet: I was amazed at Dahma when he complained about us and at Abu Dahma when he advised us Good for them, as if they feared us That is, he advises us to do good to it. Similar to this is the saying of Al-Hutay’ah: I have recommended from the outside a free heart to treat dogs well and mud badly. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is, And We have enjoined upon man: to do to his parents what is good. It was said that it is an adjective for a deleted noun, meaning, And We enjoined upon him a good thing. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a direct object by implication, meaning, We obligated him to do good. It was said that it is in the accusative case by removing the preposition, meaning, And We enjoined upon him to do good. It was said that it is a verbal noun for a deleted verb, meaning, to do good. The meaning of the verse is: recommending that man be kind to his parents and be compassionate to them. The majority read good with a damma on the ha’ and a sukoon on the meem. Abu al-Raja’, Abu al-Aliyah, and al-Dahhak read them with a fatha. Al-Jahdary read ihsanan and so is in the copy of Abu Talib. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, meaning, they demand of you and oblige you to associate with Me a god that you have no knowledge of being a god, so do not obey them, because there is no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator. The negation of knowledge is expressed as the negation of god because what is not known to be true is not permissible to follow, so how about what is known to be false? If it is not permissible to obey one’s parents in this matter while striving to do so, then it is more appropriate that it is not permissible to do so merely without striving to do so. And the same applies to all other acts of disobedience to God Almighty, so there is no obedience to them in what is a disobedience to God, as was authenticated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do, meaning I will inform you of your good and bad deeds, and I will reward each of you according to what he deserves.
29:9: The relative pronoun in His statement: 9- And those who have believed and done righteous deeds is in the nominative case as the subject and its predicate is We will surely admit them among the righteous, meaning among the group of those firmly rooted in righteousness. It is also possible that it is in the accusative case as an object of preoccupation, and it is possible that the meaning is: We will surely admit them into the entrance of the righteous, which is Paradise, as it has been said, and the first is more appropriate.
29:10: 10- And among the people is he who says, ‘We believe in God,’ but when he is harmed for the sake of God, that is, for the sake of God and for His sake, as the unbelievers do to the people of faith, and as the sinners do to the people of obedience, by inflicting harm on them for the sake of their faith in God and doing what He has commanded, he considers the trial of the people, which is the harm they inflict on him, to be like the punishment of God, that is, he is impatient with those who harm them, so he does not have patience, and makes it as severe and severe as the punishment of God, so he obeys the people as he obeys God. It was said that he is the hypocrite who, when harmed for the sake of God, turns away from the religion and disbelieves. Al-Zajjaj said: The believer should be patient in the face of harm for the sake of God. And if victory comes from your Lord, that is, victory from God for the believers, and a conquest and victory over the enemies, and spoils they seize from them, he will surely say, ‘Indeed, we were with you,’ that is, entering with you into your religion and assisting you against your enemy, so God denied them. He said: Is not God most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds? That is, He, glory be to Him, knows best what is in their breasts, both good and evil, so how can they make this false claim? These are people whose faith was weak. When they were harmed by the disbelievers, they agreed with them. But when the strength of Islam became apparent and God granted victory to the believers in some situation, they would say, ‘Indeed, we were with you.’ It was said that what is meant by this and the previous verses are the hypocrites. Mujahid said: This was revealed about people who believed in God with their tongues, but when a calamity or misfortune befell them from God, they were tempted. Ad-Dahhak said: This was revealed about some hypocrites in Makkah who used to believe, but when they were harmed, they reverted to polytheism. It appears that this verse, from His statement: And among the people is he who says to His statement: And those who disbelieved say, was revealed about the hypocrites, as is evident from the context.
29:11: And His statement: 11- And that God will surely make evident those who believe and that He will surely make evident the hypocrites is to confirm and emphasize what came before it: that is, that God will distinguish between the two groups and reveal the sincerity of the sincere and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites. So the sincere one is the one who does not waver due to the harm that befalls him and is patient for God's sake as he should be, and does not treat the trial of the people as equivalent to the punishment of God. And the hypocrite is the one who inclines thus and thus, if harm befalls him from the disbelievers, he agrees with them and follows them and disbelieves in God the Almighty, and if the wind of Islam blows and its victory rises and its conquest becomes apparent, he returns to Islam and claims that he is a Muslim.
29:12: 12- And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, ‘Follow our way.’ The lam in for those who believed is the lam of notification: meaning they said, addressing them as previously explained in more than one place: meaning they said to them, Follow our way and enter our religion. “And We will bear your sins.” Meaning, if following our way is a sin for which you will be held accountable on the Day of Resurrection, as you say, then We will bear that for you and be held accountable for it without you. The lam in for us to bear is the lam of command, as if they ordered themselves to do that. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj said: It is a command in the interpretation of condition and consequence: meaning, if you follow our way, We will bear your sins. Then God responded to them by saying: And they will not bear any of their sins. The first part is explanatory. The second is for emphasis: that is, they will not bear any of the sins they committed to and were guaranteed to bear. Then God the Almighty described them as liars in this bearing, saying: Indeed, they are liars in what they guaranteed of bearing your sins. Al-Mahdawi said, this denial of them by God the Almighty was interpreted in terms of the meaning, because the meaning is: If you follow our path, we will bear your sins. So since the matter goes back in meaning to the report, the denial was applied to it just as it is applied to the report.
29:13: 13- And they will surely bear their burdens meaning the sins they committed. The expression burdens indicates that they are great sins. And burdens with their burdens meaning burdens with their burdens. They are the sins of those whom they led astray and led them away from guidance to misguidance. Similar to this is the statement of God, the Most High: They will surely bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection and also some of the sins of those whom they led astray without knowledge. Similar to this is the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever establishes a bad practice will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it, as in the authentic hadith of Abu Hurayrah in Sahih Muslim and others. And they will surely be asked on the Day of Resurrection as a rebuke and rebuke about what they used to invent meaning the lies they used to invent in this world. Muqatil said: This means their statement: We are responsible for every consequence that befalls you from God. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated regarding the verse {{... Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaidullah bin Umair who said: “This verse was revealed about Ammar bin Yasir when he was being tortured for the sake of God: ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left alone?’” Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud who said: “The first to whom God declared their Islam were seven: the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Abu Bakr, Sumayyah, the mother of Ammar, Ammar, Suhayb, Bilal, and Miqdad. As for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), God protected him by means of his uncle Abu Talib. As for Abu Bakr, God protected him by means of his people. As for the rest of them, the polytheists seized them, dressed them in iron armor, and melted them in the sun. Not one of them did what they wanted except Bilal, who considered himself insignificant for the sake of God and he considered himself insignificant in the eyes of his people. They seized him and gave him to the children who paraded him around the valleys of Mecca while he was saying, ‘One, one.’” Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, that they should outstrip Us, that he said, that they should outstrip Us. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: My mother said, I will not eat food or drink until you disbelieve in Muhammad. So she abstained from food and drink until they began to hit her mouth with a stick. Then this verse was revealed: “And We have enjoined upon man, to be dutiful and kind to his parents. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them.” At-Tirmidhi also narrated it from his hadith, and he said: It was revealed concerning four verses. He mentioned a similar story, and he said: It is hasan saheeh. Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i also narrated this hadith. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Hibban, Abu Nu’aym, al-Bayhaqi and al-Dhiya’ narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I have been harmed for the sake of God, as no one else is harmed. I have been afraid for the sake of God, as no one else is afraid. A third time has passed while Bilal and I had no food that a living being would eat, except what Bilal’s armpit covered.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement, He has made the trial of the people like the punishment of God, that he said: He turns away from the religion of God if he is harmed for the sake of God.
29:14: God Almighty made the story of Noah beautiful, confirming His statement at the beginning of the Surah, And We certainly tried those before them. In it is a confirmation for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as if it was said to him: Noah remained for a thousand years minus fifty years calling his people, and none of them believed except a few. So you are more deserving of patience because of the short duration of your stay and the large number of your nation. It was said that it was mentioned in the system minus fifty years and did not say nine hundred and fifty years, because the exception confirms the number, unlike the second, which may be used for something close to it. There is disagreement regarding the amount of Noah's lifespan. This will come at the end of the discussion. The verse only says that he remained among them for this period, and it does not indicate that it was his entire lifespan. It may have remained with others before it remained with them, and it may have remained on the earth after their destruction by the flood. The fa in 14- The flood overtook them is for subsequent purposes: that is, it took them after the completion of the aforementioned period. The flood is said for everything abundant and encompassing them, whether it be a delay, killing, or death, as Al-Nahhas said. Saeed bin Jubayr, Qatadah, and Al-Suddi said: It is rain. Ad-Dahhak said: It is drowning, and it was said: Death. From this comes the saying of the poet: A devastating flood of death swept them away. The phrase and they are wrongdoers is in the accusative case as a state: that is, they persisted in their wrongdoing, and what Noah admonished them with and reminded them of this long period did not work on them.
29:15: 15- So We saved him and the companions of the ship meaning, We saved Noah and those with him in the ship from his children and followers. There are different opinions about their number. And We made it meaning the ship a sign for the worlds meaning a great lesson for them. There are several aspects to it being a sign: First, it remained on Al-Judi for a long time. Second, God saved the ship from the turbulent winds. Third, the water subsided before the provisions were exhausted. This is not appropriate to describe the ship as a sign. It has been said that the pronoun in We made it refers to the event, or to the salvation, or to the punishment by drowning.
29:16: 16- And Abraham, when he said to his people Abraham is in the accusative case in apposition to Noah. An-Nasa'i said: It is in apposition to the ha' in We made it, and it was said that it is in the accusative case with an implied meaning: that is, remember Abraham. And when he said is in the accusative case in apposition to the circumstantial case: that is, and We sent Abraham at the time when he said to his people, Worship God, or We made Abraham a sign at the time when he said this: or remember Abraham at the time when he said, with the circumstantial case being a substitute for inclusion from Abraham. Worship God and fear Him, that is, single Him out in worship and specialize in it and fear Him lest you associate anything with Him. That is better for you, that is, worshipping God and fearing Him is better for you than polytheism, and there is no good in polytheism ever. However, He addressed them in consideration of their belief, if you should know something of knowledge, or you should know a knowledge by which you can distinguish between what is good and what is evil. The majority of scholars read it and Abraham in the accusative case, and the reason for that is what we have presented. Al-Nakha’i, Abu Ja’far, and Abu Hanifa read it with the nominative case as the subject and the predicate is understood: that is, among the messengers was Abraham.
29:17: 17- You only worship idols besides God. Abraham explained to them that they worship things that neither benefit nor harm, nor hear nor see, and idols are statues. Abu Ubaid said: An idol is what is made of gold, silver, or copper, and an idol is what is made of plaster or stone. Al-Jawhari said: An idol is a statue, and the plural is awthan. And you create falsehood, meaning you lie, based on the meaning of you create being you lie. It is also possible that it means: you work and you carve, meaning you teach them and you carve them for falsehood. Al-Hasan said: The meaning of you create being you carve is: you only worship idols and you make them. The majority read you create with a fatha on the first letter, a sukoon on the kha, and a damma on the lam, the present tense of create, and falsehood with a kasra on the hamza and a sukoon on the fa. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Zaid ibn Ali, Al-Salami, and Qatadah read it with a fatha on the kha and a shaddah on the lam, and the original is you create. It was narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Ali that he read it with a damma on the ta’ and a shaddah on the lam, but with a kasra. Ibn al-Zubayr and Fudayl ibn Warqan read it with a fatha on the hamza and a kasra on the fa’. It is a verbal noun like kadhbah, or an adjective for a deleted verbal noun, meaning a fabricated creation. Indeed, those you worship other than God do not possess for you any provision meaning they are not able to provide you with any provision. So seek provision from God meaning direct your desire for your provisions to God, for He is the One with whom all provision is, so ask Him from His bounty and affirm His Oneness alone. And be grateful to Him meaning for His blessings, for gratitude causes them to continue and is a reason for more of them. It is said, I thanked Him and I thanked Him “To Him you will return” through death and then by resurrection, not to anyone else.
29:18: 18- And if you deny, then nations before you have denied. It was said that this is from the words of Abraham: That is, if you deny me, then that has happened to others before you. And it was said that it is from the words of God Almighty: That is, if you deny Muhammad, then that was the custom of the disbelievers with those who came before. And the Messenger has no duty except to convey clearly to his people to whom he was sent, and he is not responsible for guiding them, and that is not within his power.
29:19: 19- Have they not seen how God originates creation and then repeats it? The majority read or have they not seen with a fat-ha as report, and this reading was chosen by Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. Abu Ubaid said: It is as if he said: Or have they not seen the nations. Abu Bakr, Al-A'mash, Ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read it with a fat-ha as an address from Ibrahim to the Quraysh, and it was said that it is an address from God to the Quraysh. The majority read how does he begin with a nas-ha of the lower form from abda yabda'. Al-Zubayri, Isa bin Umar, and Abu Amr read it with a fat-ha from bada yabda'. Al-Zuhri read How He began and the meaning is “Have they not seen how God creates them initially as a drop of semen, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then He breathes the spirit into him, then brings him out into the world, then He takes him after that?” And so it is with all the animals and all the plants. So if you see the ability of God Almighty to begin and bring into existence, then He is able to bring them back. The hamza is to deny their not being seen, and the waw is to connect to something understood, Indeed, that is easy for God, because if He wants something, He says to it, Be, and it is.
29:20: Then God, the Almighty, commanded Abraham to command his people to travel through the earth so that they might reflect and take heed. He said: 20- Say, 'Travel through the earth and observe how He began creation.' Despite their great multitude and the diversity of their colors, natures, and languages, and observe the dwellings of past generations and bygone nations and their traces, so that you may learn thereby the perfection of God's power. It was said that the meaning is: Say to them, O Muhammad, travel. The meaning of His statement, Then God will produce the final creation, is that God, who began the first creation and created it in that manner, will produce it a second creation at the resurrection. The sentence is in apposition to the sentence Travel through the earth, included with it in the scope of the statement. The sentence, Indeed, God has power over all things, is an explanation of what preceded it. The majority read the creation with a short vowel and a sukoon on the sheen. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a long vowel and a fatha on the sheen, and they are two dialects like ra'fah and ra'fah. It is a verbal noun with the deletion of the extra letters, and the original is construction.
29:21: 21- He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills. That is, after the Hereafter, He, glory be to Him, punishes whom He wills, and they are the disbelievers and sinners, and He has mercy on whom He wills, and they are the believers in Him, those who believe in His messengers and act according to His commands and prohibitions. And to Him you will return. That is, you will return and be returned, not to anyone else.
29:22: 22- And you will not be able to frustrate God on earth or in heaven. Al-Farra’ said: Nor will those in heaven frustrate God therein. He said: It is as in the saying of Hassan: So whoever among you satirizes the Messenger of God, praises him, and supports him, it is the same. Anyone who praises Him and supports Him is the same. Similar to this is the statement of God the Almighty: And there is not one of us but has a known station meaning, except for he who has a known station. The meaning is that He, glory be to Him, is not defeated by the people of the earth or the people of the heavens in the heavens if they disobey Him. Qatrab said: The meaning of the verse is: nor in the heaven if you were in it, just as you say: So-and-so would not escape me here, nor in Basra,” meaning, not in Basra if he went there. Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning is nor anyone in the heaven, based on the fact that man is not a relative pronoun but rather an indefinite noun, and in the heaven is an adjective for it, so the adjective was used in place of the noun. Ali bin Sulayman rejected this and said: It is not permissible, and he preferred what Qatrab said: And you have not besides God any protector or helper as an additional emphasis: meaning, you have no protector to support you nor any helper to aid you and ward off God’s punishment from you.
29:23: 23- And those who disbelieve in the signs of God and the meeting with Him means the signs of revelation or of creation, or both. And they disbelieved in the meeting with God: that is, they denied the resurrection and what comes after it and did not act upon what the Messengers of God, the Most High, informed them of. The reference in His statement, Those is to the disbelievers in the signs and the meeting, and it is the subject and predicate have despaired of My mercy meaning that in this world they are hopeless of God’s mercy. What was revealed of God’s Books and what His Messengers informed them of did not work on them. It was said that the meaning is that they will despair on the Day of Resurrection of God’s mercy, which is Paradise. The meaning is that they have lost hope of mercy. And those will have a painful punishment. God, the Most High, repeated the reference for emphasis, and described the punishment as being painful to indicate that it is extremely severe.
29:24: 24- And the answer of his people was only that they said, ‘Kill him or burn him.’ This is a return to the address of Abraham after the objection to what preceded from the address of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to the opinion of those who said: His saying, Say, ‘Travel through the land,’ is an address to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for the opinion of those who said: It is an address to Abraham, peace be upon him, the speech is in its context, previously and subsequently: that is, some of them said to each other when consulting among themselves: Do one of the two mentioned things to Abraham, then they agreed to burn him. So God saved him from the Fire and made it cool and safe for him. Indeed in that, that is, in God’s saving of Abraham, are clear signs, that is, clear indications and apparent signs of the greatness of God’s power and the wonder of His creation: since they lit that great fire and threw him into it, and it did not burn him or affect him at all, but rather it became in a state contrary to what is the nature of its element of heat and burning. Rather, the believers were singled out, because they are the ones who consider the signs of God. Glory be to Him. As for those other than them, they are unaware of that. The majority of scholars read the answer to his people in the accusative case as the predicate of kana and what follows it is its subject. Salim al-Aftas, Amr ibn Dinar, and al-Hasan read it in the nominative case as the subject of kana and what follows it is in the accusative case as the predicate.
29:25: 25- And he said, 'You have only taken, besides God, idols out of affection among you in worldly life.' That is, Ibrahim said to his al-Nas 114:that is, to foster affection among you and to maintain contact by worshipping them, and for fear that affection would be lost if you abandoned worshipping them. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Al-Kisa'i read mawaddah baynakum in the nominative case, mawaddah baynakum without a tanween, and adding it to baynakum. Al-A'mash and Ibn Wathab read mawaddah in the nominative case, but with a tanween. Nafi', Ibn Amir, and Abu Bakr read mawaddah in the accusative case, but with a tanween, and baynakum in the accusative case, as an adverbial phrase. Hamzah and Hafs read it in the accusative case, adding mawaddah baynakum to baynakum. As for the nominative reading, Al-Zajjaj mentioned two interpretations for it: The first is that it is in the nominative case as a predicate of inna in inna takhadhum and made ma its description, and the meaning is: Indeed, what you have taken, besides God, are idols out of affection among you. The second interpretation is that it is an implied subject: that is, it is affection or that is affection. Meaning: It is the affection that brought you together to worship idols and take them. It was said that it is possible for affection to be raised by the subject and its predicate is in the worldly life. Whoever reads with the affection raised with a tanween, then his interpretation is like the first reading, and he puts the accusative between you as a circumstantial word. Whoever reads with the affection lowered and does not put a tanween on it makes it you took them and makes innama a single letter for the sake of limitation, and so on for whoever puts it in the accusative and its nun. It is permissible for the accusative in these two readings to be on the basis that affection is the cause, so it is the object for the sake of which, and on the reading of the nominative, the second object of you have taken is omitted: that is, idols as gods, and on the assumption that what is in his saying you have only taken is a relative pronoun, the first object is its pronoun: that is, you have taken it, and the second object is idols. Then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disbelieve in others that is, some of those who took idols and worshipped them will disbelieve in others of them, so the leaders will disown the followers and the followers will disown the leaders. It was said that the meaning is that the idol worshippers will disown the idols and the idols will disown those who worshipped them. And some of you will curse one another that is, each group will curse the Hereafter according to the two mentioned interpretations. And your refuge is the Fire that is, the disbelievers. It was said that the idols are included in that: that is, it is your home to which you take refuge. And you will have no helpers to save you from it by their support for you.
29:26: 26- So Lot believed him meaning Abraham believed Lot and confirmed everything he brought. It was said that he did not believe in him until he saw that the fire would not burn him, and Lot was Abraham’s nephew. And he said, ‘Indeed, I will emigrate to my Lord.’ Al-Nakha’i and Qatadah said: The one who said, I will emigrate to my Lord is Abraham. Qatadah said: He emigrated from Kutha, which is a village in the plains of Kufa, to Harran, then to Ash-Sham, with his nephew Lot and his wife Sarah. The meaning is: I am emigrating in accordance with wisdom.
29:27: It was said that the one who said, I am emigrating to my Lord was Lot, and the first is more appropriate because the pronoun in his saying, And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob refers to Abraham, and likewise in his saying, And We placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book, and likewise in his saying, And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. All of these pronouns refer to Abraham without dispute: that is, God bestowed upon him children, so He bestowed upon him Isaac as a son for him and Jacob as a son for his son Isaac, and He placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book, so God did not send a prophet after Abraham except from his loins. The Book was made singular because the alif and lam in it denote the genus that includes the books, and what is meant is the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Qur'an. The meaning of And We gave him his reward in this world is that he was given children in this world, and God informed him that prophethood would continue among them, and that is what would please his eye and increase his joy. It was said that his reward in this world is that the people of all religions claim him and say that he is one of them. It was said that He gave him righteous deeds in this world and a good outcome. And indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. That is, those who are perfect in righteousness and are deserving of abundant reward and gifts from the Lord, the Most High. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God sent Noah when he was forty years old. He remained among his people for one thousand years less fifty, calling them to God. He lived sixty years after the flood until people had multiplied and spread. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Noah’s age before he was sent to his people and after he was sent was one thousand seven hundred years. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Awf ibn Abi Shaddad, who said: God sent Noah to his people when he was three hundred and fifty years old. He remained among them for one thousand and fifty years, then he lived three hundred and fifty years after that. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in his book, The Blame of the World, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Angel of Death came to Noah and said: O you who lived the longest, how did you find the world and its pleasures? He said: Like a man who entered a house with two doors, stood in the middle of the house for a while, then left through the other door. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the verse, And We made it a sign for the worlds, that he said: God left it as a sign, so it is on Mount Judi. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, And you invent falsehood, that he said: You tell lies. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, The Hereafter, that he said: It is life after death, which is the Resurrection. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, So Lot believed in him, that he said: Lot believed Abraham. Abu Ya'la and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas who said: "The first of the Muslims to migrate to Abyssinia with his family was Uthman ibn Affan. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: 'May God be with them both. Uthman was the first to migrate to God with his family after Lot." Ibn Mandah and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Asma' bint Abi Bakr who said: "Uthman migrated to Abyssinia and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: 'He was the first to migrate after Abraham and Lot.'" Ibn Asakir, Al-Tabarani and Al-Hakim in Al-Kuna narrated on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There was no migration between Uthman, Ruqayyah and Lot. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The first to migrate to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was Uthman ibn Affan just as Lot migrated to Abraham. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, {And We gave him Isaac and Jacob}, that he said: They are the sons of Abraham. And regarding his statement, {And We gave him his reward in this world}, he said: God commanded the people of religions to follow His religion, so there is no people of religions of any religion except that they say Abraham and are pleased with him. And these also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, {And We gave him his reward in this world}, that he said: Good remembrance. And Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority, that he said: The righteous son and praise. And the statement of Ibn Abbas, {They are the sons of Abraham}, perhaps he means his son and his son’s son, because the son of a son is like a son, and something like this is not hidden from the likes of Ibn Abbas, for he is the scholar of this nation. And this narration on his authority is from the narration of Al-Awfi. And in the two Sahihs, The noble one is the son of the noble one, the son of the noble one, the son of the noble one, is Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Ishaq, son of Abraham.
29:28: His statement: 28- "And Lot is in the accusative case in apposition to Noah, or to Abraham, or by estimating mention". Al-Kisa'i said: The meaning is, "And We saved Lot, or And We sent Lot When he said to his people is an adverbial phrase for the agent in Lot Indeed, you commit an immorality Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr read A'lnko" with the interrogative form. The rest read it without the interrogative form. The immorality is the most hideous trait, and the phrase "No one among the worlds has preceded you in it" confirms the complete ugliness of this trait, and that they are unique in that, no one among the people, regardless of their race, has preceded them in doing it.
29:29: Then the Almighty explained this indecency, saying: 29- Do you indeed approach men meaning, sodomize them and block the way It was said that they used to commit indecency with the travelers who passed by them, so when they did that, people stopped passing by them, and thus they blocked the way. Al-Farra’ said: They used to intercept people on the roads with their evil deeds. It was also said that they used to block the way of passersby by killing and robbing them. It appears that they used to do whatever would cause them to block the way without being restricted to a specific reason. It was said that the meaning of blocking the way is to block offspring by switching from women to men. And you commit evil in your gatherings The club, assembly, and forum are the gatherings of the people and their speakers. There is a difference of opinion regarding the evil they used to do. Some say they used to throw pebbles at people, and hide from strangers. Some say they used to fart in their gatherings. Some say they used to come to men in their gatherings, and they could see each other. Some say they used to play with pigeons. Some say they used to dye their fingers with henna. Some say they used to compete with roosters and butt heads with rams. Some say they used to play dice and chess and wear dyed clothes. There is no objection to the fact that they used to do all of these evil deeds. Al-Zajjaj said: This indicates that people should not associate with one another in evil and should not gather to mock and forbid. When Lot denied what they were doing, they responded with what God said about them: And the only answer of his people was that they said, ‘Bring us the punishment of God, if you should be of the truthful.’ That is, they did not respond with anything except this statement, returning to denial, obstinacy, and stubbornness. We have already discussed this verse, and we have already mentioned in Surat al-Naml 27:And the only answer of his people was that they said, ‘Expel the family of Lot from your city.’ And we have already mentioned in Surat al-A’raf 7:And the only answer of his people was that they said, ‘Expel them from your city.’ These three places are combined in that Lot was steadfast in his guidance and repeatedly forbade them and threatened them. So they said to him first: Bring us the punishment of God, as in this verse. Then, when he did that a lot and did not remain silent, they said: Expel them, as in Al-A’raf and An-Naml. It was said that they said first: Expel them from your city, then they said a second time: Bring us the punishment of God.
29:30: Then, when Lot despaired of them, he asked God Almighty for victory over them, so 30- He said, ‘My Lord, help me against the corrupting people’ by sending down Your punishment upon them, and their corruption was due to what had previously happened of men coming to him and doing evil in their gathering, so God Almighty responded and sent His angels to punish them and commanded them to give Abraham good tidings before their punishment.
29:31: And for this reason He said: 31- And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, meaning the good tidings of a son, who was Isaac, and of a son’s son, who was Jacob, they said, ‘Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city,’ meaning they said this statement to Abraham, and the city was the city of Sodom, in which the people of Lot were, and the phrase Indeed, its people were wrongdoers is an explanation for the destruction: meaning that We destroyed them for this reason.
29:32: 32- He said, ‘Indeed, in it is Lot.’ That is, Abraham said to them: Indeed, in this city that you are about to destroy is Lot, so how will you destroy it? “They said, ‘We know best who is in it,’ of the good and the evil, and We know better than anyone else where Lot is, ‘We will surely save him and his family’ from the punishment.” Al-A’mash, Hamzah, Ya’qub, and Al-Kisa’i read We will surely save him with a light pronunciation, while the rest read it with a heavy pronunciation, Except his wife, she was among those who remained behind, meaning those who remained in the punishment. This is a word shared between the past and the future, and its investigation has been presented above. It has also been said that the meaning is: among those who remain in the city upon which the punishment will descend, so she will be punished among them and not be saved among those who are saved.
