29:33: 33- And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed by them meaning when the messengers came to Lot after they had left Abraham, he was distressed by them: meaning something happened to him that upset him and he feared it, because he thought they were human beings, so he feared for them from his people because they were in the best human form, and the word that in that is an additional word for emphasis. And he felt constricted by them meaning he was unable to manage them and he was sad and his chest felt constricted, and the constriction of the arm is a metaphor for inability, as is said in the metaphor for poverty: his hand felt constricted, and the explanation of this has been presented in full in Surat Hud. When the angels witnessed the grief and distress that had befallen him, they said, Do not fear or grieve. That is, do not fear for us from your people and do not grieve, for they cannot defeat us. Indeed, We will save you and your family, from the punishment that God has commanded us to inflict upon them. Except for your wife; she will be among those who remain behind. They informed Lot of what they had done of destroying his people and saving him and his family except for his wife, just as they had informed Abraham. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Shu'bah, Ya'qub, and Al-A'mash read manjuk with a light sukoon. The rest read it with a shaddah. Al-Mubarrad said: The kaf in manjuk is in the genitive case, and it is not permissible to connect the apparent noun to the pronoun in the genitive case, so the second was taken to mean the meaning, and the interpretation became: And We will save your family.
29:34: 34- Indeed, We are going to send down upon the people of this city a punishment from the sky. This sentence is a resumption of explaining their destruction, which is understood from the specificity of salvation to him and his people. The punishment is torment, meaning torment from the sky, and it is the stoning. It was also said that it is their burning with a fire descending from the sky. It was also said that it is the subsidence and stones as in other places. The meaning of subsidence being from the sky is that the command for it was sent down from the sky. Ibn Amir read manzilun with a shaddah. Ibn Abbas read it the same way. The rest read it with a tafsir. The ba’ in because they were sinning is for a reason: that is, because of their sinning.
29:35: 35- And We left from it a clear sign. That is, We left from the city a clear sign and indication, which are the traces of the stones they stoned and the ruins of the homes. Mujahid said: It is the black water remaining on the surface of their land. There is nothing wrong with interpreting the verse to refer to all of what was mentioned, but it was specifically for those who have reason, because they are the ones who understand that those traces are a lesson for whoever sees them to consider.
29:36: 36- And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu`ayb meaning, We sent him to them. He, his lineage, and his people were mentioned previously in Surat Al-A`raf and Surat Hud. He said, ‘O my people, worship God’ meaning, single Him out in worship and single Him out for it. And hope for the Last Day meaning, anticipate it and do deeds today that will repel His punishment from you. Yunus the grammarian said: Its meaning is, fear the Hereafter in which is the recompense for deeds. And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption. Al-`athu, `athu, is the most severe form of corruption. Its explanation has been mentioned above.
29:37: 37- So the earthquake seized them meaning the earthquake. It was mentioned in Surat Hud And the shriek seized those who did wrong meaning the shriek of Gabriel, which was the cause of the earthquake. So they became in their homes, prostrate meaning they became in their country or homes, prostrate on their knees, dead.
29:38: 38- And 'Aad and Thamud. Al-Kisa'i said: Some of them said that it refers to the beginning of the surah: meaning, We certainly tried those before them, and We tried 'Aad and Thamud. He said: I would prefer it to be: And the earthquake seized them, meaning, and seized 'Aad and Thamud. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: And We destroyed 'Aad and Thamud. It was also said that the meaning is: And remember 'Aad and Thamud when We sent to them Hud and Salih. And it has become clear to you from their dwellings, meaning, it has become clear to you, O community of disbelievers, from their dwellings in Al-Hijr and Al-Ahqaf, signs from which you may be admonished and reflect. The subject of has become clear is omitted. And Satan made their deeds pleasing to them, which they do of disbelief and disobedience to God, and averted them, with this beautification, from the path, meaning the clear path leading to the truth. And they were perceptive, meaning people of insight by which they are able to know the truth through substitution. Al-Farra’ said: They were wise men with insight, but their insight did not benefit them. It was said that the meaning is: They were insightful about their disbelief and misguidance, and were impressed by it, thinking that they were on the right path and seeing that their matter was right. So he described them as having insight in this regard, considering what was in their souls.
29:39: 39- And Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman. Al-Kisa'i said: If you wish, it can be attributed to 'Aad and it would have what it had. If you wish, it can be attributed to their being prevented from the path, meaning Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman were prevented. It was also said that the meaning is: And We destroyed these people after the messengers came to them. So they were arrogant in the land from worshipping God. And they were not forerunners, meaning they would not have missed out. It is said that his seeker missed out: if he missed him. It was also said that they were not forerunners in disbelief, but many centuries had preceded them in it.
29:40: 40- So each We seized for his sin meaning, We punished him for his disbelief and denial. Al-Kisa’i said: So each We seized meaning, We seized each one for his sin. And among them were those upon whom We sent a violent storm meaning, a wind that brought small pebbles and pelted them with them, and they were the people of Lot. And among them were those whom the blast seized meaning, the people of Thamud and the people of Madyan. And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow meaning, Qarun and his companions. And among them were those whom We drowned meaning, the people of Noah and the people of Pharaoh. And God would not wrong them for what He did to them, because He had sent His messengers to them and sent down His books to them. But they were wronging themselves by continuing to disbelieve, deny the messengers, and commit sins against God. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, the Exalted, {and you commit evil in your assemblies}, that he said: Your gathering. Al-Faryabi, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in Kitab Al-Mustam, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, about the statement of God, the Exalted, {and you commit evil in your assemblies}. He said: They used to sit on the road and throw fun at wayfarers and ridicule them.” Al-Tirmidhi said, after narrating it and classing it as good: We do not know it except from the hadith of Hatim ibn Abi Saghira on the authority of Samak. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade throwing fun, which is the statement of God, the Exalted, {and you commit evil in your assemblies}. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding the verse, saying: It is throwing fun. Abd ibn Humayd narrated a similar statement on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Aisha regarding the verse, she said: flatulence. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated regarding His statement, Then the earthquake seized them, he said: the blast. And regarding His statement, and they were seeing, he said: in misguidance. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, And among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, he said: the people of Lot. And among them were those whom the blast seized, he said: Thamud. And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, he said: Qarun. And among them were those We drowned, he said: the people of Noah.
29:41: His statement: 41- The parable of those who take protectors other than God who befriend them and speak to them regarding their needs instead of God, whether they are inanimate or animal, living or dead, is like the parable of the spider who takes a home Its home does not benefit it at all, neither in heat nor cold nor rain. Likewise, what they take as protectors other than God will not benefit them in any way and will not benefit them at all. Al-Farra’ said: It is a parable that God gave for those who take gods other than Him who neither benefit them nor harm them, just as the spider’s home does not protect it from heat nor cold. He said: It is not appropriate to stop at the spider because when it was intended to be likened to its home that does not protect it from anything, it was likened to the gods that do not benefit or harm it. It is permissible to stop at the spider that has made a home, so it is not appropriate to stop at the relative clause without the relative pronoun. The spider occurs in the singular and plural, masculine and feminine, and its plural is anakab and ankabutat. It is the small creature that weaves a fine web. It may also be called anakabat, and from this is the saying of the poet: As if a house of thorns falls from its mines on its reins And indeed, the flimsiest of houses is the spider’s house. There is no house weaker than that which vermin take as a home, and nothing comes close to it in fragility and frailty. If they only knew that taking allies other than God is like taking a spider’s home, or if they had any knowledge, they would have known this.
29:42: 42- Indeed, God knows whatever they invoke besides Him. "Ma is an interrogative, negative, or relative pronoun, and min" is for partialization or additional emphasis. It is said that this sentence is implied to say: that is, say to the disbelievers that God knows what they invoke besides Him. Abu Ali al-Farisi asserted that it is an interrogative, and if it is assumed to be negative, it is as if it was said: "Indeed, God knows that you do not invoke besides Him" meaning that what you invoke is nothing. And if it is assumed to be a relative pronoun, it is as if God knows those whom you invoke besides Him. It is possible that "ma is a source, and min" is an expression for the source. Asim, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read "yad'un" with the subjunctive ending. Abu Ubaid chose this reading because of the mention of the nations before this verse. The rest read it with the superlative ending as an address. "And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise" is the predominant source, whose actions are extremely precise and perfect.
29:43: 43- And these examples We present to the people meaning this example and other examples in the Qur’an We present to the people to alert them and bring what is beyond their understanding closer. And none will grasp them meaning they will understand them and comprehend the matter for which we presented them except those of knowledge of God, those firmly grounded in knowledge, who reflect and ponder what is recited to them and what they witness.
29:44: 44- God created the heavens and the earth in truth, meaning with justice and equity, taking into account the interests of His servants in their creation. It has been said that what is meant by truth is His speech and His power, and the place of truth is the accusative case of circumstance. Indeed in that is a sign for the believers, meaning a great indication and a clear sign of His power and His uniqueness in divinity. He singled out the believers because they are the ones who benefit from that.
29:45: 45- Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book meaning the Qur’an, which commands us to recite the Qur’an regularly while contemplating its verses and reflecting on its meanings. “And establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing.” That is, persevere in establishing it and continue performing it as it has been commanded. The phrase Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing explains what preceded it. Immorality is what is ugly in action, and wrongdoing is what is not known in the Shari’ah, meaning it prevents one from disobeying God and distances one from it. The meaning of its prohibition is that performing it is a reason for abstaining. What is meant here are the obligatory prayers. And the remembrance of God is greater meaning greater than everything, meaning better than all acts of worship without remembrance. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: I believe that the meaning is that the remembrance of God is greater in absolute terms, meaning that it is what prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. The part of it that is in prayer does that, and the part that is not in prayer does the same, because abstaining can only happen to someone who remembers God and is mindful of Him. It was said that the remembrance of God is greater than the remembrance in the verse of glorification and praise, meaning it is greater and more deserving of forbidding indecency and wrongdoing. It was also said that what is meant by remembrance here is prayer, meaning that prayer is greater than all other acts of obedience, and it was expressed with remembrance as in His statement: So hasten to the remembrance of God to indicate that the remembrance in it is the main reason for giving it precedence over all other acts of obedience. It was also said that the meaning is: And God’s remembrance of you with reward and praise from Him is greater than your remembrance of Him in your worship and prayers. Ibn Jarir preferred this view, and it is supported by the hadith: Whoever remembers Me to himself, I will remember him to Myself, and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I will remember him in an assembly better than them. “And God knows what you do,” nothing of that is hidden from Him, so He will reward you for good with good and for evil with evil.
29:46: 46- And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best meaning, except in the best manner, by way of calling to God Almighty for them and alerting them to His arguments and proofs in the hope that they will accept Islam, not by way of harshness and roughness except for those who commit injustice among them by going to extremes in the argument and not being polite with the Muslims. There is nothing wrong with being harsh and rough in arguing with them. This is how most of the commentators have interpreted the verse, meaning that what is meant by the People of the Scripture are the Jews and Christians. It was also said that the meaning of the verse is: Do not argue with those who believed in Muhammad from the People of the Scripture, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and all the others who believed among them, except in a way that is best, meaning by agreeing with what they narrated to you of the stories of the People of the Scripture. According to this statement, what is meant by those who committed injustice are those who remained in their disbelief. It was also said that this verse was abrogated by the verses on fighting, and this is what Qatadah and Muqatil said. An-Nahhas said: Whoever says it was abrogated argued that the verse was revealed in Mecca and that at that time there was no obligatory fighting, no demand for jizyah, or anything else. Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: “Those who did wrong among them are those who set out to fight the Muslims, arguing with them with the sword until they submitted or paid the jizyah. ‘And say, “We believe in that which has been revealed to us” of the Qur’an and revealed to you of the Torah and the Gospel, meaning, we believe that they were revealed from God and that they are an established law until the establishment of Islamic law and the mission of Muhammad. This does not include what they have distorted and changed. ‘And our God and your God is one’, with no partner, opposite, or equal. ‘And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him’, meaning, we, the community of Muhammad, are obedient to Him in particular. We did not say that Ezra was the son of God or that the Messiah was the son of God, nor did we take our rabbis and monks as lords besides God. It is possible that what is meant is that we are all submissive to Him, and this does not invalidate this viewpoint because the Muslims’ submission is more complete than that of the People of the Book and their obedience is more eloquent than theirs.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: The parable of those who take protectors other than God 2:176, he said: That is a parable that God has set forth for those who worship other than Him, that their parable is like that of a spider’s web. Abu Dawud narrated in his Marasil on the authority of Yazid ibn Murthad who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The spider is a devil that God transformed, so whoever finds it should kill it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muzayd ibn Maysarah who said: The spider is a devil. Al-Khatib narrated on the authority of Ali who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Abu Bakr and I entered the cave and the spiders gathered and wove a web around the door, so do not kill them. Al-Qurtubi narrated in his Tafsir on the authority of Ali as well that he said: Purify your homes from the spider’s web, for leaving it in the house leads to poverty. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani who said: The spider spun its web twice, once for David and the second time for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, that he said: In prayer there is a limit and deterrent from sins. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about the statement of God, Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, so he said: Whoever’s prayer does not prohibit immorality and wrongdoing, then there is no prayer for him. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever’s prayer does not prohibit immorality and wrongdoing, then it only increases his distance from God. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever’s prayer does not prohibit immorality and wrongdoing, then there is no prayer for him. In another version: It only increases his distance from God. Al-Khatib narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Umar. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud. As-Suyuti said: Its chain of transmission is weak. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and At-Tabarani in Ash-Shu'ab narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-A'mash and others. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, And the remembrance of God is greater, he said: And the remembrance of God of His servants when they remember Him is greater than their remembrance of Him. Al-Faryabi, Sa'd ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rabi'ah who said: Ibn Abbas asked me about the statement of God, And the remembrance of God is greater, so I said: The remembrance of God by glorifying God, declaring His oneness, and declaring His greatness. He said: The remembrance of God of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. Then He said: Remember Me and I will remember you. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa'id az-Zuhd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, And the remembrance of God is greater. He said: The servant's remembrance of God is greater than the servant's remembrance of God. Ibn as-Sunni, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami narrated something similar from Ibn Umar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, saying: It has two interpretations: The remembrance of God is greater than anything else. In another version: The remembrance of God when He has forbidden it, and God's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. Ahmad narrated in az-Zuhd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mu'adh bin Jabal, who said: No human being has done any deed that saves him from the punishment of God more than the remembrance of God. They said: Not even jihad in the way of God? He said: Not even striking with his sword until it breaks, because God says in His Noble Book, And the remembrance of God is greater. Sa'id bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim in al-Kuna and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'b narrated from Antara, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas, Which deed is best? He said: The remembrance of God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, he said: With ‘There is no god but God.’ Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The People of the Scripture used to recite the Torah in Hebrew and explain it to the Muslims in Arabic. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Neither believe the People of the Scripture nor disbelieve them, but say: ‘We believe in that which was revealed to us and revealed to you. Our God and your God is One, and we are Muslims in submission to Him.’” Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab, Al-Daylami, and Abu Nasr Al-Sajzi in Al-Ibanah on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not ask the People of the Scripture about anything, for they will never guide you, and they have gone astray. Either you believe in falsehood or you disbelieve in the truth. By God, if Moses were alive among you, he would have no choice but to follow me.” Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: Do not ask the People of the Book, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Jabir. Then he said: If you must ask them, then look for what is in accordance with the Book of God and take it, and what contradicts the Book of God and leave it.
29:47: His saying: 47- And thus We have sent down to you the Book. This is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the reference is to the source of the verb as we have explained in many places. And similar to that wondrous revelation, We have sent down to you the Book, which is the Qur’an. It has been said that the meaning is: Just as We sent down the Book to them, We have sent down the Qur’an to you. Those to whom We have given the Scripture believe in it, meaning the believers among the People of the Scripture, such as Abdullah ibn Salam. He singled them out by giving the Scripture because they acted according to it, as if others had not been given it due to their lack of acting according to what was in it and their denial of the attributes of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned in it. And among these are those who believe in it, referring to the people of Mecca, and what is meant is that among them, and that is, those who have converted to Islam, are those who believe in it, meaning the Qur’an. It has also been said that the reference is to all Arabs. And none reject Our verses, meaning the verses of the Qur’an, except the disbelievers, those who are determined in their disbelief among the polytheists and People of the Scripture. And none reject Our verses, meaning the verses of the Qur’an, except the disbelievers, those who are determined in their disbelief among the polytheists and People of the Scripture.
29:48: 48- And you did not recite before it any Scripture The pronoun in before refers to the Qur’an because what is meant by We have sent down to you the Book is that you, O Muhammad, did not recite a book before the Qur’an, nor were you able to do so because you were illiterate and could neither read nor write. Nor did you inscribe it with your right hand means you did not write it because you were not able to write. Mujahid said that the People of the Book found in their books that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, could neither write nor read, so this verse was revealed. Al-Nahhas said: This is evidence of his prophethood because he did not write nor did he mix with the People of the Book, and there were no People of the Book in Mecca, so he came to them with report of the prophets and nations. Then the falsifiers would have had doubts. That is, if you had been one of those who were able to recite and write, they would have said, Perhaps he found what he could recite to us from the previous books of God or from the books recorded in the report of the nations. But since you were illiterate and could neither read nor write, there was no room for doubt or suspicion at all. Rather, the denial of those who denied and disbelieved was mere stubbornness and ingratitude without any doubt. He called them falsifiers because their doubt, assuming that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, could read and write, was an injustice on their part, due to the clarity of his purity and the obviousness of his miracles.
29:49: 49- Rather, they are clear signs meaning the Qur’an in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge meaning the believers who memorized the Qur’an during his time (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and memorized it after him. Qatada and Muqatil said: The pronoun refers to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): meaning, Rather, Muhammad is clear signs meaning, possessor of signs. Ibn Mas’ud read: Rather, they are clear signs. Al-Farra’ said that the meaning of this reading is: Rather, the verses of the Qur’an are clear signs. Ibn Jarir chose what Qatada and Muqatil said, and he supported what they said with the reading of Ibn as-Sameefa’: Rather, these are clear signs. There is no evidence for that in this reading, because the reference may be to the Qur’an just as it is possible for it to be to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Rather, its referring to the Qur’an is more evident because that does not require interpretation. The meaning is: And none reject Our verses except the wrongdoers meaning those who transgress the limits in wrongdoing.
29:50: 50- And they said, ‘Why were no signs sent down to him from his Lord?’ That is, the polytheists said this statement, and the meaning is: Why were no signs sent down to him like the signs of the prophets, such as the signs of Moses, the she-camel of Saleh, and Jesus’ reviving the dead? Then God, the Exalted, commanded him to answer them, saying: Say, ‘The signs are only with God,’ He sends them down to whomever He wills of His servants, and no one has the power to do that. And I am only a clear warner,’ I warn you as I have been commanded and I make clear to you as it should be. I have no other power. Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read Why were no signs sent down to him? in the singular. The rest read it in the plural, and Abu Ubaid chose this reading because of the statement, Say, ‘The signs are only with God.’
29:51: 51- Was it not sufficient for them that We sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book which is recited to them? This sentence is a resumption of the response to their suggestion and to demonstrate its invalidity: that is, was this miraculous Book which you challenged them to produce something like it or a surah from it not sufficient for the polytheists from the signs they suggested, and they failed? And if you had brought them the signs of Moses and the signs of other prophets, they would not have believed, just as they did not believe in the Qur’an which is recited to them at all times and in all places. Indeed in that refers to the Book described by what was mentioned is a great mercy in this world and the hereafter and a reminder in this world by which they remember and which guides them to the truth for a people who believe that is, for a people who believe in what you have brought from God, for they are the ones who benefit from that.
29:52: 52- Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a Witness between me and you.’ That is, say to the deniers, “Sufficient is God as a Witness for what happened between me and you. ‘He knows what is in the heavens and the earth.’ Nothing of that is hidden from Him, including what occurred between you and His Messenger. ‘And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in God - it is they who are the losers.’” That is, they believe in what they worship other than God and disbelieve in the truth, which is God, the Exalted. They are the ones who combine loss in this world and the Hereafter.
29:53: 53- And they ask you to hasten the punishment in mockery and denial, as in their saying, Rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. “And were it not for a specified term” that God has set for their punishment and specified it, which is the Resurrection. Ad-Dahhak said: The term is the duration of their lives because when they die they will be subjected to the punishment. The punishment would have come to them meaning were it not for that specified term, the punishment that they deserved for their sins would have come to them. It was said that what is meant by the specified term is the first Trumpet blast, and it was said that it is the time that God has decreed for their punishment in this world by killing and captivity on the Day of Badr. The result is that every punishment has a term that cannot be preceded or delayed, as in the words of the Most High: For every matter there is a term appointed. The phrase and it will come to them suddenly is a new sentence explaining the coming of the punishment mentioned before it, and the meaning of suddenly is sudden. The phrase and they do not perceive is in the place of a predicate of state: that is, the state of their not knowing that it will come.
29:54: Then the Almighty mentioned that the appointed time for their punishment is Hell, saying: 54- They ask you to hasten the punishment, while Hell is encompassing the disbelievers. That is, they ask you to hasten their punishment, while the place of punishment is surrounding them, that is, it will surround them soon, for what is coming is near. What is meant by the disbelievers is their kind, so these hasteners are included in it primarily. So His saying, and they ask you to hasten the punishment, is informing about them, and His saying a second time, they ask you to hasten the punishment, is an expression of amazement at them. It was said that the repetition is for emphasis.
29:55: Then the Almighty mentioned how the punishment will surround them, saying: 55- The Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet meaning from all sides of them. Then when the punishment covers them in this manner, Hell will have surrounded them. And He will say, ‘Taste what you used to do.’ The speaker is God, the Almighty, or one of His angels, commanding him: meaning, taste the recompense for what you used to do of disbelief and sins. The people of Medina and Kufa read naqul with a noon. The rest read it with a tahtiya. Abu Ubaid chose the last reading, because of His saying: Say, ‘Sufficient is God.’ Ibn Mas’ud and Ibn Abi Ubla read it, and it is said, Taste. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Ismaili in his Mu'jam narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, the Almighty, {And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand}, that he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, could neither read nor write; he was illiterate. And regarding the statement of God, the Almighty, {Rather, they are clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge}, that he said: God had revealed the status of Muhammad in the Torah and the Gospel to the people of knowledge, and taught it to them and made him a sign for them, so He said to them: The sign of his prophethood is that when he emerges he will neither know a book nor inscribe it with his right hand, and these are the clear signs of which God, the Almighty, said. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, regarding the statement of God, the Almighty, {And you did not recite before it any book}, that he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, could neither read nor write. Al-Faryabi, Al-Darimi, Abu Dawud in his Marasil, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Ja'dah who said: “Some Muslims came with books they had written in which were some of what they had heard from the Jews. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘It is enough foolishness and misguidance for a people to turn away from what their Prophet brought to them and to instead follow what others brought to others.’ So the verse, ‘Was it not sufficient for them?’ was revealed.” Al-Ismaili narrated it in his Mu’jam and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Yahya bin Ja'dah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and he mentioned it with the same meaning. Abd Al-Razzaq in Al-Musannaf and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri that Hafsah came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with a book of the stories of Joseph in a shoulder strap. She began to read it and the Prophet’s face changed color. He said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if Joseph came to you while I was your prophet and you were to follow him and abandon me, you would go astray.’” Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn al-Durais, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith al-Ansari that he said: "Umar ibn al-Khattab entered upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with a book containing passages from the Torah. He said: 'I have found these with a man from the People of the Book. I will show them to you.' The face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) changed so drastically that I had never seen anything like it. Abdullah ibn al-Harith said to Umar: 'Do you not see the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)?' Umar said: 'We are pleased with God and Islam as our religion and with Muhammad as our Prophet.' The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) felt better and said: 'If Moses had come down and you were to follow him and abandon me, you would have gone astray. I am your portion among the prophets, and you are my portion among the nations.'" A similar narration was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq and al-Bayhaqi via Abu Qilabah on the authority of Umar. Al-Bayhaqi narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: "I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about learning the Torah. He said: 'Do not learn it, but believe in it. Learn what has been revealed to you and believe in it.'" Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers, he said: Hell is this green sea in which the stars are scattered and in which the sun and moon are, then it is kindled and becomes Hell. There is great objection to this, for many authentic hadiths clearly state that Hell exists and was created with the characteristics mentioned in the Book and the Sunnah.
29:56: When God, the Almighty, mentioned the state of the disbelievers from among the People of the Book and the polytheists, and gathered them in the warning and made them among the people of Hell, their stubbornness intensified, their corruption increased, and they sought to harm the Muslims in every way. So God, the Almighty, said: 56- O My servants who have believed, He added them to Himself after addressing them as an honor and a tribute. Those who believed is a clear or distinctive description. Indeed, My earth is spacious. If you are in difficulty in showing faith in Mecca, and in a plot against the disbelievers, then leave it so that worshipping Me alone may be made easy for you and facilitated for you. Al-Zajjaj said: They were commanded to migrate from a place where they could not worship God. Likewise, whoever is in a land where they commit sins and cannot change that must migrate to a place where he can worship God as He should be worshipped. Mutraf ibn Ash-Shakheer said: The meaning is that My mercy is vast and My provision is abundant for you, so seek it on earth. It was also said that the meaning is: My earth, which is the land of Paradise, is vast, so worship Me until I inherit it for you. And the subject of I is the subject of an implied verb: that is, worship Me.
29:57: Then He, glory be to Him, frightened them with death to make the matter of migration easy for them, so He said: 57- Every soul will taste death, then to Us you will be returned. That is, every soul will inevitably experience the bitterness of death, so it will not be difficult for you to leave your homelands and part from your brothers and friends. Then to God is the return through death and resurrection, and not to anything else. Every living being is on a journey to the abode of permanence, even if his stay in this abode is long.
29:58: 58- And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely assign them lofty chambers of Paradise. This encourages emigration, and that the reward of those who emigrate is to be in the lofty chambers of Paradise. The meaning of We will surely assign them is We will surely place them in the lofty chambers of Paradise, which are its upper levels. So the accusative of lofty chambers is the second object, as their prophethood implies the meaning of We will surely place them, or it is a circumstantial noun without implied meaning, because their prophethood only extends to one object. Or it is accusative by removing the preposition for expansion: meaning in the lofty chambers of Paradise, and it is taken from maba'ah, which means to descend. Abu Amr, Ya'qub, Al-Jahdary, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Muhaysin, Al-A'mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read O My servants, with a sukoon on the ya', while the rest read it with a fatha. Ibn 'Amir read Indeed, my land, with a fatha on the ya', while the rest read it with a sukoon. As-Sulami and Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim, read they return with a ta'iyyah, while the rest read it with a fawqiyah. Ibn Mas'ud, Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i readلنِبوينهمwith a triple tha' instead of a unified ba', while the rest read it with a unified ba'. The meaning ofلنثاوينهمwith a triple tha' is: We will give them rooms to reside in, from thawa, which means to stay. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said that a man thawa stays if he resides, and athwaytuhu give him a place to stay if he puts him in a home to reside in. Al-Akhfash said: I do not like this reading because you do not say athwaytuhu al-dar I reside in the house, but rather you say fi al-dar in the house, and there is no preposition in the verse as the second object. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: It is intended as a preposition, then it was deleted, just as you say I have commanded you with goodness, meaning with goodness. Then God, the Almighty, described those rooms and said: Underneath which rivers flow meaning from under the rooms, abiding therein meaning in the rooms, they will never die, or in Paradise. The first is more appropriate. Yes, the reward of the workers which is specifically praised is deleted, meaning yes, the reward of the workers is their reward. The meaning is: the workers for righteous deeds.
29:59: Then he described these workers, saying: 59- Those who were patient in the face of the hardships of the obligation and the harm done to them by the polytheists. It is possible that it is in the accusative case for praise. And upon their Lord they rely meaning they entrust their affairs to Him in every step forward and every retreat.
29:60: Then the Almighty mentioned what helps in patience and trust, which is looking at the condition of the beasts, saying: 60- "And how many a creature carries not its own provision! God provides for it and for you." We have already discussed Ka'in, and that its origin is that the letter Kaf of comparison was added to it and it took on the meaning of Kam, as stated by Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, and they estimate it as a large number of beasts. It was also said that the meaning is: And how many a creature. The meaning of "does not carry its own provision" is that it is not able to carry its provision due to its weakness and does not store it. Rather, God provides for it from His bounty and provides for you. So how can they not trust in God, with their strength and ability to provide for the means of livelihood, as God trusts in God, with its weakness and inability? Al-Hasan said: It eats at its appointed time, not storing anything. Mujahid said: He means the birds and beasts that eat with their mouths and do not carry anything. "And He is the All-Hearing is the One who hears everything that is heard, The All-Knowing is of everything known.
29:61: Then He, the Almighty, mentioned the state of the polytheists from among the people of Mecca and others, and the listener was amazed at the fact that they acknowledged that there is a Creator and Provider for them, but they did not believe in His Oneness and abandoned the worship of anyone other than Him. He said: 61- And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ That is, He created them. They will not be able to deny that, nor will they be able to disavow Him. So how are they deluded? That is, how are they turned away from acknowledging His uniqueness in divinity, and that He alone has no partner? The question is for denial and exclusion.
29:62: And when the polytheists said to some of the believers: If you were on the truth, you would not be poor, God Almighty repelled that by saying: 62- God expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for whom He wills. That is, the expansion of provision and its restriction are from God, the Expander and the Constrictor. He expands it for whom He wills and restricts it for whom He wills according to what His wisdom requires and what is appropriate for the condition of His servants of restriction and expansion. For this reason He said: Indeed, God is Knowing of all things, He knows what is good for His servants and what is corrupt for them.
29:63: 63- And if you ask them, ‘Who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ That is, it is God who sent it down and gave life thereby to the earth. They acknowledge this and find no way to deny it. Then, when they acknowledged this in these verses, which necessitates the invalidity of their polytheism and their failure to single out God Almighty for worship, He commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to praise God for their acknowledgment and not denying it despite their stubbornness and their severity in rejecting everything that the Messenger of God brought regarding monotheism. He said, Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ But most of them do not reason. That is, I praise God for making the truth with you and revealing Your prohibition over them. Then He blamed them, saying, But most of them do not reason. These are the things that rational people would rely on. Therefore, they do not act in accordance with what they acknowledged, which necessitates the invalidity of their practice in the eyes of every rational person.
29:64: Then the Almighty indicated the insignificance of this world and that it is of the same kind as play and amusement: and that the abode in reality is the abode of the Hereafter, so He said: 64- And this worldly life is not but diversion and amusement of the same kind as what children play and amuse themselves with. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the life. Ibn Qutaybah and Abu Ubaidah said: The life is life. Al-Wahidi said: This is the opinion of all the commentators, they went to the meaning of the life here is life, and that it is a source in the position of life, so it is like ecstasy and boiling, and the interpretation would be: And indeed, the home of the Hereafter is the home of the life, or the essence of the life: that is, the home of the everlasting life that does not pass away and is not diminished by death or sickness, nor by worry or grief. If they had known anything of knowledge, they would not have preferred over it the transient, bitter abode.
29:65: Then the Almighty made it clear that the only thing preventing them from believing is the mere influence of life, as He said: 65- So when they embark on a ship, they supplicate God, devoting their religion to Him sincerely. That is, when their hope in life is cut off and they fear drowning, they return to their natural disposition, so they supplicate God alone, being in the image of those who are sincerely devoting their religion to Him through the sincerity of their intentions, and they abandon supplication to idols because they know that no one can relieve this great hardship that has befallen them except God, the Almighty. But when He delivers them to land, at once they associate others with Him. That is, they are suddenly forced back to polytheism and supplicate to other than God, the Almighty. Riding means superiority, and it is transitive in and of itself, but it is transitive with the word fi to indicate that the thing ridden in itself is a type of place.
29:66: The lam in 66- that they may disbelieve in what We have given them and in His saying: and that they may enjoy themselves is for the purpose of al-Sharh 94:that is, surprise them with polytheism with God so that they may disbelieve in the blessing of God and enjoy them, so in both verbs there is a lam of ki, and it was said that they are the lams of command, threatening and warning: that is, disbelieve in what We have given you of blessings and enjoy yourself, and this reading is indicated by the reading of Abu and enjoy yourself, and this possibility of the two matters is only according to the reading of Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Asim and Warsh with the kasra of the lam, and as for the reading of the majority with its sukoon, there is no disagreement that it is the lam of command, and in His saying: they will soon know is a great threat to them: that is, they will know the consequences of that and the calamity in it for them.
29:67: 67- Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary? That is, have they not considered, meaning the infidels of Quraysh, that We have made this sanctuary of theirs a secure sanctuary in which its inhabitants are safe from raids, killing, captivity, and plunder? So they have become safe and sound from what has become of other Arabs, for they are constantly attacked, their property is swept away by invaders, their blood is shed by soldiers, and their sanctuary and property are violated by the clever Arabs and their devils. The phrase and people are snatched away from all around them is in the accusative case as a state: that is, they steal away from all around them by killing, captivity, and plunder. Snatching means taking quickly, and the meaning of this has already been explained in Surat Al-Qasas. Then do they believe in falsehood, which is polytheism, after the proof of God has been made clear to them and their acknowledgment of what requires monotheism. And they are ungrateful for the favor of God, they make their ingratitude a substitute for their gratitude. This question contains an immeasurable amount of rebuke and rebuke.
29:68: 68- And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God meaning no one is more unjust than him, which is the one who claims that God has a partner or denies the truth when it has come to him meaning he denies the Messenger who was sent to him and the Book that He revealed to His Messenger. Al-Suddi said: He denied monotheism, and it appears that it includes everything that is true to be true. Then He threatened the deniers and warned them by saying: Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers? meaning a place where they will settle. The question is for confirmation, and the meaning is: Do they not deserve to settle there after they did what they did?
29:69: Then when he mentioned the state of the polytheists who denied monotheism and disbelieved in the blessings of God, he followed it up with the state of His righteous servants, saying: {And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways} meaning, they strive for God's sake, seeking His pleasure and hoping for the good that is with Him - We will surely guide them to Our ways: meaning the path that leads to Us. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is a Meccan verse that was revealed before the customary jihad was made obligatory. Rather, it is a general jihad in the religion of God and seeking His pleasure. It was also said that this verse was revealed about the servants. Ibrahim ibn Adham said: It is about those who do what they know. {And indeed, God is with the doers of good} with victory and support, and whoever is with Him will not be let down. The lam of emphasis was added to with with the understanding that it is a noun, or that it is a particle, and it was added to it to convey the meaning of stability, as you say: Indeed, Zaid is in the house. This discussion is established in the science of grammar. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When this verse was revealed, Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die, I said, O Lord, will all of creation die while only the prophets remain? So the verse, Every soul will taste death, then to Us you will be returned, was revealed. It should be seen how correct this is, for after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hears God’s words, Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die, he knows that he will die, and he also knows that the prophets before him had died, and that he is the Seal of the Prophets. So how can this verse lead to what Ali, may God be pleased with him, asked about, namely, Will all of creation die while only the prophets remain? Perhaps this narration is not authentic, whether it is attributed to the Prophet or not. And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir narrated - Al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission - on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “I went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) until he entered some of the walls of Madinah. He began to pick up dates and eat them. He said to me: Why don’t you eat? I said: I don’t desire them, O Messenger of God. He said: But I desire them, and this is the fourth morning since I have tasted food and I have not found any. If I wished, I could have called upon my Lord to give me a kingdom like that of Chosroes and Caesar. So what will you do, O Ibn Umar, if you remain among a people who love their yearly provision and whose faith is weak?” He said: By God, we did not leave or throw stones until the verse And how many a creature carries not its own provision was revealed. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: God did not command me to hoard the worldly wealth or to follow desires. Beware, I do not hoard dinars or dirhams, nor do I store provision for tomorrow.” This hadith is very objectionable because it contradicts the practice of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). He used to give his wives their food for the year, as is proven in the reliable books of hadith. In its chain of transmission is Abu al-Atouf al-Jawzi, who is weak. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the life, meaning: eternal. Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Shu’ab on the authority of Abu Ja’far, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How strange it is for someone to believe in the home of life while he strives for the home of delusion. And it is mursal.
30:1: It is sixty verses. Al-Qurtubi said that they are all Meccan without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala'il narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah Ar-Rum was revealed in Makkah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ahmad narrated something similar. As-Suyuti said with a good chain of narration on the authority of a man from the Companions: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) led them in the Fajr prayer and recited Surah Ar-Rum in it. Al-Bazzar narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Ighar Al-Madani. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar ibn Abd Al-Malik ibn Umair that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) recited Surah Ar-Rum in Fajr on Friday. Ibn Abi Shaybah in Al-Musannaf, Ahmad, and Ibn Qani' narrated through Abd Al-Malik ibn Umair something similar to the hadith of the Companions, but he added: He hesitated in it, and when he finished, he said: Our prayer is only confounded by people who attend the prayer without purification. Whoever attends the prayer should purify himself properly. 1- Alif, Lam, Meem The opening of the surah was discussed in the opening of Surah Al-Baqarah, and its grammatical position and the position of similar letters were discussed in more than one place in the openings of the surahs.
30:2: The majority read it. 2- Ghalbat ar-Rum with a damma on the ghayn and a kasra on the lam indicating the object. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Saeed al-Khudri, Muawiyah ibn Qurra, Ibn Umar and the people of Ash-Sham read it with a fatha on the ghayn and the lam, forming the subject. An-Nahhas said: The reading of most people is Ghalbat with a damma on the ghayn and a kasra on the lam. The people of interpretation said: Persia defeated the Romans, so the infidels of Mecca rejoiced at that and said: Those who do not have a book defeated those who have a book, and they boasted over the Muslims and said: We will also defeat you as Persia defeated the Romans, and the Muslims loved for the Romans to prevail over the Persians because they were people of the book.
30:3: The meaning of 4- in the lowest land is in the land closest to their land from the land of the Arabs, or in the land closest to the Arabs. It was said that it is the land of Al-Jazira, and it was said Adhra'at, and it was said Kaskar, and it was said Jordan, and it was said Palestine. These places are closer to the land of the Arabs than others, and the land was attributed to the land of the Arabs because it is known in their languages that when they use the word land they mean the Arabian Peninsula. It was also said that the definite article replaces the noun, and the interpretation is: in the lowest land of their land, so the pronoun refers to the Romans, and the meaning is: in the land of the Romans closest to the Arabs. Ibn Atiyyah said: If the battle took place in Adhra'at, then it is in the lowest land compared to Mecca. If the battle took place in Al-Jazira, then it is closer compared to the land of Kisra. If it took place in Jordan, then it is closer to the land of the Romans. And they, after their defeat, will overcome. That is, the Romans, after the defeat of Persia, will overcome the people of Persia. Ghalb and ghalba are two languages, and the infinitive is added to the object according to the reading of the majority, and to the subject according to the reading of others. The majority read it as and to the agent according to the reading of others. The majority read they will be defeated as an agent, while Ali, Abu Saeed, Muawiyah bin Qurra, Ibn Omar, and the people of Ash-Sham read it as a passive voice, and Ibn As-Samee’ read it as after they were defeated with a silent lām.
30:4: 4- In a few years is related to what preceded it. The explanation of a few and its derivation were presented in Surah Yusuf. What is meant by it here is between three and ten. To God belongs the command before and after. That is, He is the One alone in power and in saving the rulings at the time of their defeat and the time of their predominance. All of that is by the command and decree of God, the Most High. The majority read before and after with a damma because they are separated from the addition. The meaning is: before the defeat and after it, or before every matter and after it. Al-Kisa'i narrated before and after with a kasra on the first and with a tanween, and a damma on the second without a tanween. Al-Farra' narrated before and after with a kasra on both of them without a tanween, and Al-Nahhas made a mistake. Shihab Al-Din said: It has been read with a kasra on both of them with a tanween. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse: Who is earlier and who is later And on that day the believers will rejoice * In God’s victory meaning, on the day that the Romans defeat the Persians in a few years, the believers will rejoice in God’s victory for the Romans because they are people of the Book, just as the Muslims are people of the Book, unlike the Persians who do not have a book. This is why the polytheists were delighted with their victory over the Romans. It was said that God’s victory is to demonstrate the truth of the believers in what they told the polytheists about the Romans’ victory over the Persians, but the former is more appropriate. Al-Zajjaj said: This verse is one of the verses that indicate that the Qur’an is from God because it is a prediction of what will happen, and no one knows this except God, the Most High.
30:5: 5- He supports whom He wills to support, and He is the Exalted in Might the Victorious, the Subduer, the Merciful the One with abundant mercy for His believing servants. It was said that what is meant by mercy here is worldly, and it includes both Muslims and disbelievers.
30:6: 6- God’s promise - God never breaks His promise meaning God made a promise that He never breaks, which is the victory of the Romans over Persia. But most people do not know that God never breaks His promise, and they are the infidels, and it was said that they are the infidels of Mecca in particular.
30:7: 7- They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world meaning they know the outward appearance of what they see of the world’s adornments and pleasures, the matter of their livelihood and the reasons for obtaining their worldly benefits. It was said that it is what the devils throw at them of worldly matters when they eavesdrop, and it was said that it is the outward falsehood. And they are heedless of the Hereafter which is the permanent blessing and pure pleasure. They are heedless they do not pay attention to it and do not prepare for it what is needed, or they are heedless of belief in it and confirmation of its coming.
30:8: 8- Have they not considered within themselves what God has created the heavens and the earth and what is between them? The hamza is for denial of them and the waw is for linking to an implied word as in similar verses. In themselves is an adverbial phrase for contemplation and not an object of contemplation. The meaning is that the causes of contemplation are available to them, and they are themselves. If they contemplated them as they should, they would know the Oneness of God and the truth of His prophets. It was also said that it is an object of contemplation. The meaning is: Or have they not contemplated God's creation of them while they were nothing? Ma in Ma Khalaqa God is a negative: meaning He did not create them except with the established truth that must be established. Or it is a noun in the accusative case by dropping the preposition: meaning with what God created. The operator in it is either the knowledge that contemplation leads to. Al-Zajjaj said in Al-Kalam that it was deleted: meaning so that they know. So he made Ma the object of the implied verb, not the knowledge indicated by it. The Ba in Except with the truth is either for causality, or it and its object are in the accusative case as a state: meaning mixed with the truth. Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is except for the truth: i.e., for reward and punishment. It was also said that the truth means justice, and it was also said that the truth means justice, and it was also said that the truth means that He is the Truth and for the truth He created them. And a specified term is in apposition to the truth: i.e., and for a specified term for the heavens and the earth and what is between them, they will all come to it, which is the Day of Resurrection. This is an indication of annihilation, and that every created being has a term that it will not exceed. It was also said that the meaning of and a specified term is that He created what He created at a time He named for the creation of that thing. And indeed, many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers i.e., they disbelieve in the resurrection after death. The lam is for emphasis, and what is meant by these are disbelievers in general, or the disbelievers of Mecca.
30:9: 9- Have they not traveled through the land? The question is for rebuke and reprimand for not thinking about the effects and contemplating the places of consideration. The fa in yanzaru is for conjunction with yasriru and is included under what the question includes of rebuke and reprimand. The meaning is that they have traveled and witnessed how was the end of those before them from the groups of disbelievers whom God destroyed because of their disbelief in God, their denial of the truth, and their rejection of the messengers. The phrase were stronger than them in strength explains the state they were in, and that they were more capable than the disbelievers of Mecca and those who followed them in worldly matters. The meaning of and tilled the land is they plowed it and turned it over for cultivation and took up the means of that, and the people of Mecca were not people of cultivation. and cultivated it more than they cultivated it meaning they cultivated it more than these people did, because those people lived longer than them, were stronger in body, and had more access to the means of livelihood. So they populated the land with buildings, agriculture and planting. And their messengers came to them with clear proofs, meaning miracles, and it was said with legal rulings. So God would not wrong them by punishing them for no sin, but they were wronging themselves by disbelief and denial.
30:10: 10- Then the end of those who did evil was meaning they committed evil deeds of polytheism and transgressions. The worst is a noun from the root word saw, the feminine form of aswa, which is the ugliest: meaning their end was the punishment that is the worst of punishments. It was said that it is a name for Hell, just as al-husna is a name for Paradise. It is possible that it is a verbal noun like al-bushra and al-dhikr. The punishment was described with it as an exaggeration. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read the end in the nominative case as the noun of kana, and the masculinity of the verb is due to its feminine being metaphorical. The worst report: meaning the deed, characteristic, or bad punishment or the report that they lied meaning the end of their matter was denial. The end of those who did evil, and the worst is a verbal noun from asa'u or an attribute of something omitted. Al-Kisa’i said: His statement, because they denied is in the accusative case as a reason, meaning because they denied the verses of God that He sent down to His messengers, or because they denied. Among those who say that the worst is Hell are Al-Farra’, Al-Zajjaj, Ibn Qutaybah and most of the commentators. It is called the worst because it makes its inhabitant feel bad. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, Then the end of those who associated partners with God was the Fire because of their denial of the verses of God and their mockery. The phrase and they used to mock at them is in apposition to they denied and is included with it in the rule of causality according to one of the two opinions, or in the rule of being a noun because of kana, or as a report item according to the other opinion. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Kabir, Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il, and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated,” that he said: “The polytheists loved for Persia to prevail over the Romans, because they were idolaters, and the Muslims loved for the Romans to prevail over the Persians because they were People of the Book. They mentioned it to Abu Bakr, who mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Indeed, they will be defeated.’ Abu Bakr mentioned it to them, and they said: ‘Set a time limit between us and you. If we are victorious, then such-and-such will be ours, and if you are victorious, then such-and-such will be yours.’ So he set a time limit between them of five years, but they did not prevail. Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘Why did you not make it?’ I think he said less than ten years. Then the Romans prevailed after that, and that is what His statement, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated,” so they prevailed, then they were defeated after that, by the statement of God, ‘To God belongs the command before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice.’” By the help of God. Sufyan said: I heard that they were victorious over them on the day of Badr. Abu Ya’la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, who added that when the time limit had passed and the Romans had not defeated Persia, the Prophet was displeased with the time limit that Abu Bakr had set and disliked it. He said: What prompted you to do this? He said: In confirmation of God and His Messenger. So he said: Expose yourself to them and make the greatest effort and extend it to a few years. So Abu Bakr came to them and said: Would you like to return, for returning is better? They said: Yes. But those years had not passed until the Romans defeated Persia and they tied up their horses in Al-Madain and built Rome. Abu Bakr was defeated and brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: This is ill-gotten gain, give it in charity. Al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it, as did Al-Daraqutni in Al-Afrad, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Dala’il, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab, on the authority of Niyyar ibn Mukram Al-Aslami, who said: When the verse, Alif, Lam, Meem, The Romans have been defeated was revealed, the Persians had been victorious over the Romans on the day this verse was revealed. The Muslims loved the Romans’ victory over them because they and they were the People of the Book. Concerning this, God says, And on that Day the believers will rejoice in God’s victory. The Quraysh loved the Persians’ victory because they and they were not the People of the Book and did not believe in the Resurrection. When God revealed this verse, Abu Bakr went out shouting in the outskirts of Makkah, “Alif, Lam, Meem, The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land. But after their defeat they will overcome. Within a few years.” Some of the Quraysh said to Abu Bakr, “That is between us and you. Your companion claims that the Romans will defeat the Persians in a few years. Shall we not bet on that with you?” He said, Yes, and that was before betting was forbidden. So Abu Bakr and the polytheists took a bet and agreed on a wager. They said to Abu Bakr, Why did you not make the 'ba'dah' range from three to nine years? So name a middle ground between us and you. So they named six years between them. The six years passed before they were victorious, so the polytheists took Abu Bakr's pledge. When the seventh year began, the Romans emerged. The Muslims criticized Abu Bakr for naming it six years because God said, in a few years. At that point, many people embraced Islam. At-Tirmidhi narrated - and he authenticated it - Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Abu Bakr, Why did you not take precautions, O Abu Bakr? The 'ba'dah' ranges from three to nine. Al-Bukhari narrated something similar on his authority in his history. Al-Firyabi, Al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id that he said: When the Day of Badr occurred, the Romans were victorious over the Persians, and that pleased the believers. So, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated.” He recited it in the accusative case, meaning with the ghayn in the active form, until the verse, The believers rejoice * in the victory of God. He said: So the believers rejoiced at the victory of the Romans over the Persians. This narration explains the reading of Abu Sa’id and those who were with him. Al-Hakim narrated, who authenticated it, on the authority of Abu Darda’, who said: There will come people who will recite “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated,” meaning with the fatha on the ghayn. However, it is ghalabat, meaning with the damma on its ghayn. There are narrations on this topic, and what we have mentioned suffices. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world, meaning their livelihoods, when to plant, when to sow, and when to harvest. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, regarding the verse, They were mightier than them in strength, he said: A man of those who came before you had a distance between his shoulders, a mile apart.
30:11: His statement: 11- God begins creation, then repeats it meaning He creates them first, then returns them after death alive as they were. Then to Him you will be returned to the place of reckoning, so He rewards the doer of good for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. The singular pronoun in He returns is based on the word creation, and the plural in you will return is based on its meaning. Abu Bakr and Abu Amr read they will return with the sub-ta’i. The rest read it with the superlative, indicating the address and the shifting that indicates exaggeration.
30:12: 12- And on the Day the Hour appears, the criminals will be in despair. The majority of scholars read in despair in the active form. As-Salami read it in the passive form. It is said that a man is in despair: if he is silent and his argument is cut off. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: The one who is in despair is the one who is silent and cut off in his argument and who has despaired of being guided to it. From this is the saying of Al-Ajjaj: Hey friend, do you know a consecrated drawing? He said yes, I know it and Abelsa Al-Kalbi said: That is, the polytheists despaired of all good when they witnessed the punishment. We have already explained the meaning of desolation in His statement: Then they are in despair.
30:13: 13- And they will have no intercessors from among their partners meaning, on the Day of Resurrection, the polytheists will have no intercessors from among their partners whom they worshipped besides God to protect them from God’s punishment. And they will be at that time disbelievers in their partners meaning, in their gods whom they made partners with God. Disbelievers in their being gods meaning, denying that they were gods because they knew at that time that they could neither benefit nor harm. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: They were disbelievers in this world because of their worship, but the first is more appropriate.
30:14: 14- And on the Day the Hour comes, on that Day they will be separated. That is, all of creation referred to in His statement, God begins creation. What is meant by separation is that each group will separate itself, so the believers will go to Paradise, and the disbelievers to Hell. What is not meant is that each individual will separate from the other. Similar to this is His statement, the Most High, A group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze, and that is after the reckoning is complete, so they will never come together again.
30:15: Then the Almighty explained how they will disperse, saying: 15- But as for those who have believed and done righteous deeds, they will be in a garden, rejoicing. An-Nahhas said: I heard Az-Zajjaj say that the meaning of as for is to leave what we were doing and take something else. Sibawayh said the same: Its meaning is: Whatever the thing is, take something other than what we were doing. A garden is any land with vegetation. The commentators said: What is meant by it here is Paradise, and the meaning of they will be happy is they will be pleased, and the joy and the happiness are delights: that is, they will be in the gardens of Paradise, enjoying themselves. Abu Ubaid said: A garden is what is at the bottom, but if it is elevated, then it is a canal. Another said: A garden is best when it is in an elevated place, and from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: What a garden of the gardens of sadness, lush and green, upon which pouring rain pours It was said that the meaning of yahibrūn is yakaramimun. An-Nahhas said: Al-Kisa'i narrated that yahibrūn means I honored him and blessed him. The first interpretation is to interpret yahibrūn as joy as is the Arabic meaning, and entering Paradise itself entails honor and joy, and in joy there is more to that. It was said that tahbīr means beautification so the meaning of yahibrūn is beautification towards them. It was also said that it is the hearing that they hear in Paradise, and other things were said.
30:16: 16- And as for those who disbelieved in God and denied Our signs and denied and the meeting of the Hereafter meaning the resurrection, Paradise, and Hellfire, and the reference in His saying: Then those is to those who are described by these attributes, and it is the subject and its predicate will be brought into the punishment meaning they will reside in it, and it was said they will be gathered, and it was said they will be descending, and it was said they will be tormented, and the meanings are close, and what is meant is the permanence of their punishment. Then, after explaining the outcome for the group of believers and the group of disbelievers, He guided the believers to that which contains abundant reward and general good.
30:17: He said: 17- So glorify God when you go to bed and when you wake up. The fa is to arrange what comes after it according to what came before it, meaning, when you know that, then glorify God: that is, praise Him for what befits Him in the morning and evening, in the evening, and at noon. It was said that what is meant by glorification here are the five daily prayers. So His statement, when you go to bed, is the Maghrib and Isha prayers. His statement, when you wake up, is the Fajr prayer. His statement, and in the evening, is the Asr prayer. His statement, when you reach the noon prayer, is the Dhuhr prayer. This is what Ad-Dahhak, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others said. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The meaning of glory be to God is pray to God. An-Nahhas said: The commentators agree that this verse is about the prayers. He said: I heard Muhammad ibn Zayd say: In my opinion, its true meaning is glorify God in the prayers, because glorification occurs in prayer.
30:18: And the sentence 18- And to Him be praise in the heavens and the earth is parenthetical and intended to guide to praise and to indicate the permissibility of combining it with glorification as in His saying, the Most High: So glorify the praises of your Lord and His saying: And we glorify Your praise. It was said that the meaning of To Him be praise is that the prayer in which praise is recited is reserved for Him, but the first is more appropriate. Ikrimah read sometimes you spend the evening and sometimes you rise, meaning: sometime you spend the evening and sometime you rise. And the 'ishi' is from the sunset prayer until the darkness. Al-Jawhari said this. Some people said: It is from the time of the sun's decline until the break of dawn. From this is the saying of the poet: We went out at dawn, at night, in the evening after noon His saying: in the evening is connected to while, and in the heavens is related to the praise itself: that is, praise to Him will be in the heavens and the earth.
30:19: 19- He brings forth the living from the dead, like a human being from a sperm-drop and a bird from an egg. And He brings forth the dead from the living, like a sperm-drop and an egg from an animal. This has been previously explained in Surah Al Imran. It has been said that the connection between this verse and the one before it is that in the morning a human being emerges from a semblance of death, which is sleep, to a semblance of existence, which is wakefulness, and at nightfall he emerges from wakefulness to sleep. And He revives the earth after its lifelessness, that is, He revives it with vegetation after its death by dryness. This is similar to bringing forth the living from the dead. And thus you will emerge, that is, and like this bringing forth you will emerge from your graves. The majority of scholars read you emerge in the passive form. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it in the active form, and so the emergence is attributed to them, as in His statement, The Day they emerge from the graves.
30:20: 20- And among His signs is that He created you from dust meaning that His dazzling signs indicating resurrection are that He created you: that is, He created your father Adam from dust and created you within His creation, because the branch is derived from the root and taken from it.
