The explanation of this has already been mentioned in Al-An’am. An is in the nominative case as a subject, and among His signs is its predicate. Then, behold, you are human beings dispersing in the earth. If is the suddenness: meaning, then you were surprised after that time when you were human beings, dispersing in the earth. If is the suddenness, although it most often comes after fa, but here it came after thumma in relation to what is appropriate for this special state, which is the stages of man as God has related in places: from his being a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then a bone covered with flesh, He surprised humanity and dispersal. The meaning of disperse is: you go about what is the basis of your livelihood.
30:21: 21- And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves meaning, among His signs and indications of the resurrection is that He created for you mates from among yourselves: that is, from your kind in humanity. It was said that what is meant is Eve, for He created her from Adam’s rib. That you may dwell in tranquility with them meaning, that you may be at peace with her and incline toward her, for two different kinds of being cannot dwell in tranquility with each other, nor incline toward each other. And He placed between you affection and mercy meaning, love and compassion because of the inviolability of marriage, by which you are kind to one another without there having been any prior acquaintance between you, let alone affection and mercy. Mujahid said: Affection is sexual intercourse, and mercy is children, and al-Hasan said the same. Al-Suddi said: Affection is love, and mercy is compassion. It was said that affection is the love of a man for his wife, and mercy is his mercy towards her from harming her. His saying that He created for you is in the nominative case as a subject, and among His signs is its predicate, Indeed in that mentioned previously, are signs of great importance, wonderful in expression, and clear indicative of His ability, glory be to Him, to resurrect and revive for a people who give thought because they are the ones who are able to deduce evidence, since thinking is a source of it, and as for those who are heedless of thinking, they are nothing but like livestock.
30:22: 22- And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth. For He who created these great bodies, which are the bodies of the heavens and the earth, and made them eternal as long as this world exists, and created in them such wondrous creations and marvels of formation as a lesson for those who reflect, is able to create you after your death and resurrect you from your graves. And the diversity of your tongues, that is, your languages, from Arabs and Persians, and Turkish, and Romans and other languages, and your colors, from white, black, red, yellow, blue, and green, despite you being the children of one man and one mother, and you are united by one kind, which is humanity, and one distinction, which is speaking, until you became distinct in your essence, and this is not confused with that. Rather, each individual among you has that which distinguishes him from other individuals. In this is from the wonder of power what only the knowledgeable can comprehend, and only the thoughtful can understand. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge, who are of the same kind as this world, with no difference between righteous and wicked. The majority read with the opening of the lam of the knowledgeable. Hafs alone read it with a kasra. Al-Farra’ said: This has a good interpretation because he said: Signs for a people who understand, “Signs for those of understanding,” and None will understand them except those of knowledge.
30:23: 23- And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day and your seeking of His bounty. It has been said that there is an inversion of this intonation, meaning: And among His signs is your sleep by night and your seeking of His bounty by day. It has also been said that the meaning is correct without this inversion: that is, among His great signs is that you sleep at night and during the day in some cases to rest, such as during the siesta, and to seek of His bounty in both. This occurs in each of them, even though seeking bounty during the day is more common. The first is more appropriate for the rest of the verses that mention this meaning, and the second is more appropriate to the Qur'anic structure here. The reason for mentioning sleep and seeking here and making them among the proofs for the resurrection is that sleep is similar to death, and dealing with needs and striving for earnings is similar to life after death. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen. That is, they listen to the verses and admonitions with thoughtful, contemplative listening, and thus they deduce from that the resurrection.
30:24: 24- And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, causing fear and hope. The meaning is: that He shows you, so the that was omitted because the speech indicates it, as Tarafa said: Oh you who blame me, I attend the battle and witness the pleasures, will you make me immortal? The estimation: to attend, so when the letter was deleted in the verse and the house, its function was invalidated, and from it the famous proverb hearing about Al-Mu’idi is better than seeing him and it was said that it is on the advancement and delay: that is, and He shows you lightning as one of His signs, so it is from the conjunction of a verbal sentence with a nominal sentence, and it is possible that He shows you is an attribute of a deleted described: that is, and among His signs is a sign with which He shows you and in it is lightning, and it was said that the estimation: and among His signs He shows you lightning, fear and hope of His signs. Al-Zajjaj said: so it is from the conjunction of a sentence with the cause of a sentence. Qatada said: fear for the traveler and hope for the resident. Al-Dahhak said: fear of lightning and hope for rain. Yahya bin Salam said: fear of the cold that it will destroy the crops, and hope for rain that it will revive the crops. Ibn Bahr said: fear that the lightning will be a deceptive lightning that does not rain, and hope that it will be a rainmaker, and he recited: Let not your lightning be a deceptive lightning, for the best lightning is that which is accompanied by rain. And the object is erected out of fear and hope for the reason And He sends down water from the sky and revives the earth with it after its lifelessness meaning He revives it with vegetation after its death by dryness Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason for whoever has a share of reason knows that this is a sign by which he proves the dazzling power.
30:25: 25- And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command meaning that they stand and hold fast by His will and power without any pillars that He supports them, nor any stable place for them to rest on. Al-Farra’ said: He means that they will remain standing by His command. Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will emerge meaning, after your death and destiny in the graves, if He calls you with a single call, you will suddenly emerge from it quickly, without delay or hesitation, just as the called and obedient one answers the call of the caller who is obeyed. And from the earth is connected to he called: that is, he called you from the land you are in, just as one says, I called him from the bottom of the valley, so he came up to me. Or it is connected to something omitted, which is an attribute of calling. Or it is connected to something omitted, which is an indication of you come out: that is, you came out of the earth. It is not permissible for it to be connected to you come out, because what comes after if does not affect what comes before it. This call is the final blowing of the trumpet by Israfil, as was explained above. The reciters agreed to open the ta in you come out here, and whoever said that it was read here with a damma on the passive form was mistaken. Rather, it was read with a damma in Al-A’raf.
30:26: 26- And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth of all creatures in dominion, control, and creation. No one else has any of that. All are devoutly obedient to Him meaning they are obedient in submission and submission. It was said that they are committed to servitude, and it was said that they are praying, and it was said that they will stand on the Day of Resurrection, as He said: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds meaning for the reckoning. It was said that they testify that they are His servants, and it was said that they are sincere.
30:27: 27- And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it after death, giving it life eternally. And that is easier for Him. That is, it is easy for Him, He does not find it difficult, or it is easier for Him in relation to your ability and what some of you say to one another. Otherwise, there is nothing in His ability, some of which is easier than others. Rather, all things are equal. He brings them into existence by saying, Be, and they are. Abu Ubaid said: Whoever makes easier an expression for preferring one thing over another, his statement is refuted by his statement, And that is easy for God, and by his statement, And their preservation does not burden Him. The Arabs often interpret af’al as fa’il, as in the saying of Al-Farazdaq: He who raised the sky built for us a house whose pillars are stronger and taller. Any tall, dear one, and Ahmad bin Yahya Tha’lab recited on that: Men wished that I would die, and if I die, then that is a path in which I am not alone. That is, I am not one, and similarly, another said: By your life, Al-Zubayr is generous with his good deeds over the years and better Any and excellent, and Abdullah bin Masoud read it and it is easy for him. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: Indeed, the return is easier for Him - meaning for God - than the beginning - meaning easier even though all of it was easy. It was said that what is meant is that the return among creation is easier than the beginning. It was said that the pronoun in for Him refers to creation - meaning, it is easier for creation because they will be shouted at once and they will stand and it will be said to them, Be and they will be. That is easier for them than being a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, and so on until the end of creation. And His is the highest example - Al-Khalil said: The example is the description - meaning, His is the highest description in the heavens and the earth as He said: The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised - meaning, its description. Mujahid said: The highest example is the statement, There is no god but God, and Qatadah said the same. Az-Zajjaj said: And His is the highest example in the heavens and the earth - meaning, His statement, And it is easier for Him - He has given you an example of what is difficult and what is easy. It was said that the highest example is that there is nothing like Him, and it was said that what He intended was by saying Be, and in the heavens and the earth is related to the content of the previous sentence, and the meaning is that He, glory be to Him, is known by the highest example, and described by it in the heavens and the earth, and it is permissible for it to be related to something omitted as a state of the highest, or of the pronoun in the highest, and He is the Exalted in Might in His kingdom, the Able who cannot be overcome, the Wise in His words and actions. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement,يبلس, that he said:يبتئس. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement,ينِهبُروَن, that he said:يبتئس. Al-Iblas also narrated on the authority of Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir, that he said:ينِهبُروَن, that he said: They are honored. Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Jabir, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will say: 'Where are those who kept their ears and eyes clear of the flutes of Satan?' They will be distinguished, and they will be distinguished in the closets of musk and ambergris. Then He will say to the angels: 'Let them hear My glorification, praise and exaltation.' He said: 'They will glorify Him with voices the like of which the listeners have never heard before.'" Al-Daynuri narrated in Al-Majalisah on the authority of Mujahid, who said: A crier will call out on the Day of Resurrection, and he mentioned something similar, but he did not name the one who narrated it to him on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated something similar in Dham Al-Malahi and Al-Asbahani in Al-Targheeb on the authority of Muhammad ibn Al-Munkadir. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi both narrated in their description of Paradise. Al-Suyuti said with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “In Paradise there is a tree with a trunk the length of which a diligent rider would travel in its shade for a hundred years. The people of Paradise, the people of the upper rooms and others, will come out and converse in its shade. Some of them will yearn and remember the amusements of this world. Then God will send a wind from Paradise that will stir up every amusement that was in this world.” Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawader Al-Usul on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a similar hadith. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: Nafi’ bin Al-Azraq came to Ibn Abbas and said: Do you find the five daily prayers in the Qur’an? He said: Yes. So he recited: So glory be to God when you reach the evening [the Maghrib prayer], and when you rise [the Fajr prayer], and in the afternoon [the Asr prayer], and when you appear [the Dhuhr prayer], and he recited: and after the ‘Isha’ prayer. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: This verse includes the times of prayer: So glory be to God when you reach the evening meaning the sunset and the night. And when you rise meaning the dawn, And in the afternoon meaning the afternoon, And when you appear meaning the noon prayer. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn as-Sunni in Amal Yawm wa Layla, and al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Da’wa narrated on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Anas that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Shall I not tell you why God called Ibrahim His faithful friend? Because he used to say every morning and evening: Glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you rise, and to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the evening and when you appear” meaning the noon prayer. Ibn Lahi’ah is in its chain of transmission. Abu Dawud, Al-Tabarani, Ibn As-Sunni and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Whoever says in the morning: ‘Glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. To Him be praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the evening and when you rise,’ He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and gives life to the earth after its lifelessness, and thus you will be brought out,’ will make up for what he missed during that day. And whoever says it in the evening will make up for what he missed during that night.” Its chain of transmission is weak. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: All are devoutly obedient to Him, meaning obedient to Him, meaning life, resurrection and death, and they are disobedient to Him in all other forms of worship. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And it is easier for Him, he said: Easier. Ibn Al-Anbari also narrated on his authority, regarding His statement: And it is easier for Him, he said: “Recurrence is easier for the created being, because on the Day of Resurrection He will say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. And He began creation from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And to Him belongs the highest example, meaning: There is nothing like Him.
30:28: His statement: 28- He has given you an example. The meaning of the example has already been explained, and the min in from yourselves is for the beginning of the goal, and it and its object are in the accusative case as an attribute of the example: that is, an example extracted and taken from yourselves, for it is the closest thing to you, and clearer than anything else to you. So if He gave you an example with it of the invalidity of polytheism, it would be more evident and more clear. Then he explained the aforementioned example, saying: Do you have, from among those your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided you? The min in mamma malkat indicates some, and the min sharika in min is redundant for emphasis. The meaning is: Do you have partners in what We have provided you who are of the same type as those your right hands possess, and they are the male and female slaves? The question is for denial, and the phrase you are equal therein is an answer to the question that has the meaning of negation, and it confirms the meaning of partnership between them and the male and female slaves who are owned by them in their wealth: that is, would you be satisfied for yourselves, while your male and female slaves are like you in humanity, that they be equal to you in disposing of what We have provided you of wealth, and share it with you without any difference between you and them? Fear them as you fear yourselves The kaf is an adjective of a deleted source: that is, you fear the free people who are similar to you in freedom, ownership of wealth, and the permissibility of disposing of it. The intended meaning is to deny the three things: partnership between them and the owned, equality with them, and their fear of them. The intended meaning is not to establish partnership and negate istiwa' and fear, as was said in their statement: You do not come to us to speak to us. What is intended is to establish proof against the polytheists, for they will inevitably say, We are not satisfied with that. It will be said to them, How can you absolve yourselves from sharing with your slaves, who are like you in humanity, and make the slaves of God partners with Him? Thus, if the partnership between slaves and their masters in what the masters own is nullified, then the partnership between God and any of His creation is nullified. All creation is the slaves of God, and nothing remains except that He is the Lord alone, with no partner. The majority of scholars read yourselves in the accusative case as the object of the verbal noun added to its subject. Ibn Abi Ubla read it in the nominative case as the verbal noun added to its object. Thus do We detail the verses in clear detail and explicit explanation for a people who understand because they are the ones who benefit from the revealed and cosmic verses by using their minds to contemplate and reflect upon them.
30:29: Then He, glory be to Him, turned away from addressing the polytheists and guiding them to the truth with the example He gave them, saying: 29- Rather, those who do wrong follow their own desires without knowledge. That is, they did not understand the verses, but rather followed their own deviant desires and their corrupt, false opinions. The place of without knowledge is the accusative case of circumstance: that is, ignorant that they are astray. Then who can guide one whom God has led astray? That is, no one is able to guide him, because right guidance and direction are by the decree and will of God. And they will have no helpers. That is, those whom God has led astray will have no helpers to aid them and stand between them and the punishment of God, glory be to Him.
30:30: Then He commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to worship Him alone and to worship Him as He commanded him, saying: 30- So direct your face toward the religion, inclining toward it. He likened turning toward the religion to straightening your face toward it and devoting oneself to it. The accusative case of inclining toward it is in the state of the subject of aqama or its object, meaning inclined toward it, upright toward it, not turning to any other false religion. The fitrah of God upon which He has created mankind. Fitrah originally means creation, and what is meant by it here is religion, which is Islam and monotheism. Al-Wahidi said: This is the saying of the commentators regarding the victory of God, and what is meant by the people here are those whom God created upon Islam, because the polytheist did not start his fast upon Islam. Even though this address is specific to the Messenger of God, his nation is included with him in it. Al-Qurtubi said, with the agreement of the scholars of interpretation: It is preferable to interpret the Qur’an in general terms, without differentiating between Muslims and disbelievers, and that they are all created in this way, were it not for the obstacles that befall them that cause them to remain in disbelief, as in the authentic hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Every child is born in a state of fitrah. In another narration: “In this religion, but his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as an animal gives birth to a whole animal. Do you see any among them whose tails are mutilated?” Then Abu Hurayrah said: “And read, if you wish, ‘The fitrah of God in which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God.’” In another narration: Until you yourselves mutilate it. We will come at the end of this discussion with what has been reported to support this hadith of Abu Hurayrah. Every individual among people is created in a state of Islam, but innate faith and Islam are not taken into account. Rather, what is considered is the legal faith and Islam. This is the opinion of a group of the Companions and those who came after them, and the opinion of a group of commentators, and it is the truth. The statement that what is meant by fitrah here is Islam is the doctrine of the majority of the early Muslims. Others said: It is the beginning with which God began them, for He began them for life and death, happiness and misery. In Arabic, fatir is the one who initiates. Those who believe in this tend to adopt the linguistic meaning of fitrah and neglect its legal meaning. The legal meaning takes precedence over the linguistic meaning by consensus among the scholars of Islamic law. This does not contradict the fact that fitrah is mentioned in the Qur’an or Sunnah in some places with the linguistic meaning intended, such as in the statement of God, the Most High: Praise be to God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, meaning their Creator and Originator. And in His statement: And why should I not worship He who created me? There is no dispute that this is the linguistic meaning. However, the dispute is over the legal meaning of fitrah, which is what the early scholars mentioned, as we have explained, and the accusative of fitrah as a verbal noun emphasizing the sentence before it. Al-Zajjaj said: fitrah is accusative meaning follow the fitrah of God. He said: Because the meaning of direct your face toward the religion is follow the religion and follow the fitrah of God. Ibn Jarir said: It is a verbal noun derived from the word fa-’ujha wa-’ah direct your face because its meaning is that God has created people upon the religion. It was also said that it is in the accusative case as an inducement, meaning adhere to God’s nature, or upon you is God’s nature. Abu Hayyan rejected this interpretation and said: The word inducement is not implied since it is a substitute for the verb, so if it were deleted, the substitute and what is being replaced would be deleted, which would be unfair. It was responded to by saying that this is the opinion of the Basrans, but Al-Kisa’i and his followers permit it. The phrase there is no changing of the creation of God is an explanation of what precedes it of the command to adhere to the fitrah: meaning this fitrah that God created people upon cannot be changed by the Creator, glory be to Him. It was also said that it is a negation whose meaning is a prohibition: do not change the creation of God. Mujahid and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: Its meaning is there is no changing of the religion of God. Qatadah, Ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: This is regarding beliefs. Ikrimah said: The meaning is that there is no change in the creation of animals by castrating their males. That is the right religion, meaning that the religion that we are commanded to establish is the right religion, or the adherence to the fitrah is the right religion. But most people do not know, that until they do it and act upon it.
30:31: 31- Repenting to Him means returning to Him in repentance and sincerity, and obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions. From this is the saying of Abu Qais ibn al-Aslat: If they repent, then Banu Salim and their people Hawazin have repented. Al-Jawhari said: Anaba ila God means he turned and repented. Its accusative case is in the state of the agent of aqama. Al-Mubarrad said: Because the meaning of “aqama waja is: Turn your faces up. Al-Farra’ said: “The meaning is: Turn your face and those with you, turning back.” Al-Zajjaj said the same. He said that its meaning is: Turn your face and your nation up, so the state is for all of them. It is permissible to delete the conjoined word because turning back indicates it. It was said that it is in the accusative case for severance, and it was said that it is the predicate of the deleted kan: meaning, turn back to Him because and do not be among the polytheists indicates that. Then the Almighty commanded them to fear Him after commanding them to turn back, so He said: And fear Him meaning by avoiding His disobedience, and it is conjoined with the understood verb, making turn back the subject. And establish prayer which you have been commanded with, and do not be among those who associate others with God.
30:32: And His statement: 32- of those who divided their religion and became sects is a substitute for what came before it by repeating the preposition, and sects are groups: meaning do not be among those who divided into sects in religion, following one another from the people of innovations and whims. It was said that what is meant by those who divided their religion into sects are the Jews and Christians. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read divided their religion and this reading was narrated from Ali bin Abi Talib: meaning they abandoned their religion that must be followed, which is monotheism. The interpretation of this verse has been presented at the end of Surat Al-An'am Every faction rejoices in what it has meaning every group is happy and joyful with what they have of the religion that is built on incorrectness, thinking that they are on the right path but they do not have any of it in their hands. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for His statement of those who divided their religion and became sects to be a new sentence, just as it is permissible for it to be connected to what came before it.
30:33: 33- And when harm touches people meaning drought and hardship they call upon their Lord to lift that from them and they seek help from Him turning to Him meaning returning to Him, seeking refuge in Him, not relying on anyone other than Him. It was also said that they turned to Him with all their hearts. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him by answering their call and lifting those hardships from them, at once a party of them associate others with their Lord “when” is the suddenness that comes in response to the condition because it is like the fa in indicating immediate consequence: meaning, associating others with God was taken by surprise by a party of them, and they were the ones who called upon Him, so He delivered them from what they were in. This statement is intended to express amazement at their state and what they have become of acknowledging the Oneness of God Almighty when hardships befall them and then returning to polytheism when that is lifted from them.
30:34: The lam in 34- that they may disbelieve in what We have given them" is the lam of ki, and it was said that it is the lam of command for the purpose of threat and intimidation, and it was said that it is the lam of consequence. Then the Almighty addressed those from whom what happened happened, saying: "Then enjoy yourselves, for you will soon come to know" what painful torment follows this fleeting enjoyment. The majority read "Fatamatu" as addressing. Abu Al-Aaliyah read it with the subjunctive mood in the passive form, and in the copy of Ibn Mas'ud it is li-laytamta'u.
30:35: 35- Or have We sent down upon them authority? Or" is the disjunctive form, and the interrogative is for denial, and authority is the apparent proof. "So it speaks" means it indicates, as in His statement: "This is Our Book that speaks against you with the truth." Al-Farra' said: The Arabs feminize authority, they say: The authority decreed it against you. As for the Basrans, the masculine is more eloquent for them, and the Qur'an came with it, and the feminine is permissible for them because it means proof. It was said that what is meant by authority here is the king "because of what they used to associate" meaning he speaks of their association with God, the Most High. It is possible for the preposition "with" to be causal: that is, because of the matter because of which they associate.
30:36: 36- And when We give people a taste of mercy, meaning fertility, blessings, abundance, and well-being, they rejoice therein, a joy of arrogance and malice, not a joy of gratitude and exultation at its arrival to them. Say, ‘In the bounty of God and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice.’ Then the Almighty said: But if evil befalls them, any kind of hardship, for what their hands have put forth, meaning because of their sins, at once they despair, despair is hopelessness of mercy, as the majority said. Al-Hasan said: Despair is abandoning the obligations of God, the Almighty. The majority read yaquntuun with a damma on the nun, while Abu Amr, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read yaquntuun with a kasra on it.
30:37: 37- Have they not seen that God expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and expands for him and restricts that is, He restricts for whom He wills for the benefit of expanding for whom He expands and restricting for whom He restricts Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe so they deduce the truth because of its indication of the perfection of power, the marvelous creation, and the strangeness of creation. At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The polytheists would chant: “Here I am, You have no partner except a partner who is Yours. You own him and what he owns.” Then God revealed: Do you have partners among those whom your right hands possess? The verse. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse that he said: It refers to the gods, and in it He says: You fear that they will inherit you as you inherit one another. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding His statement: There is no change in the creation of God, that he said: The religion of God. That is the right religion, that he said: The right judgment. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari’ that “the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent an expedition to Khaybar and they fought the polytheists. The killing ended with the offspring. When they arrived, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What made you kill the offspring? They said: O Messenger of God, they were only the children of the polytheists. He said: Are the best of you except the children of the polytheists? By the One in Whose hand is my soul, no soul is born except in a state of fitrah natural disposition until its tongue expresses it.” Ahmad narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Every child is born in a state of fitrah natural disposition until his tongue expresses it. When his tongue expresses it, he is either grateful or ungrateful.” Narrated by Ahmad from al-Rabi’ ibn Anas from al-Hasan from Jabir. Imam Ahmad said in al-Musnad: Yahya ibn Sa’id told us, Hisham told us, Qatadah told us, Mutraf told us, ‘Ayad ibn Hammad said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) delivered a sermon one day and said in his sermon, narrating from God the Almighty: ‘Indeed, I created My servants all as monotheists. However, the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion and prohibited for them what I had permitted for them.’”
30:38: When God, the Almighty, explained how to glorify God's command, He indicated what is appropriate in terms of consoling relatives and those in need whom God has provided abundantly, saying: 38- Give the relative his right. The address is to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his nation as an example, or to every accountable person who has wealth that God has provided for him. He mentioned doing good to relatives because the best charity is that which is given to a relative, so it is a doubled charity and a desirable way of maintaining family ties. What is meant is doing good to them through charity, maintaining family ties, and being kind to them. And the needy and the traveler. That is, give the needy and the traveler their right that they deserve. The reason for mentioning these three categories specifically is that they are more deserving of doing good than all the other categories, and because it is obligatory for them from everyone who has wealth in excess of what suffices him and those he supports. There is a difference of opinion as to whether this verse is decisive or abrogated. Some say it was abrogated by the verse on inheritance. Others say it is decisive and a relative has a right to the wealth of his rich relative, and this is the view of Mujahid and Qatadah. Mujahid said: Charity is not accepted from anyone whose womb is in need. Muqatil said: The right of the poor is that charity be given to him, and the right of the wayfarer is hospitality. It was also said that what is meant by relatives is the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Qurtubi said: The first view is more correct, as their right is stated clearly in the Book of God, the Almighty, in His saying: Then for God is a fifth of it, and for the Messenger and for near relatives. Al-Hasan said: The command to give to relatives is an encouragement. That is best for those who desire the countenance of God meaning that giving is better than withholding for those who seek to draw closer to God, the Almighty. And those are the successful, meaning those who achieve what they seek, as they spend for the sake of God, in compliance with His command.
30:39: 39- And whatever you give in interest The majority of scholars read ataytum with a long vowel, meaning you have given. Mujahid, Hamid, and Ibn Kathir read it with a short vowel, meaning what you did. They unanimously agreed to read it with a long vowel in the statement And whatever you give in zakat. The root of interest is increase, and the shortened reading can be interpreted as a long vowel reading, because it means what you did as a gift, just as you say, I gave something wrong and I gave something right. The meaning of the verse is: whatever you give in increase without compensation so that it may increase in the wealth of the people meaning so that their wealth may increase and be purified will not increase with God meaning that God will not bless it. As-Suddi said: Interest in this context is a gift that a man gives to his brother seeking a reward, because that does not increase with God, and its giver is not rewarded for it, nor is there any sin on him. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said the same. Al-Wahidi said: This is the opinion of a group of commentators. Al-Zajjaj said: It means that a person gives something in order to receive more in return. This is not forbidden, but there is no reward for it, because the one who gives it is asking for something more in return. Al-Sha'bi said: The meaning of the verse is that whatever a person serves someone in order for them to benefit from it in this world, that benefit for which the service is rewarded does not increase with God. It was said that this was forbidden for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in particular, because God, the Most High, said: And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return. Its meaning is: to give and then take more in return. It was also said that this verse was revealed regarding the gift of reward. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: And what is similar to it of what a person does in order to be rewarded for it. 'Ikrimah said: Usury is of two types: lawful usury and unlawful usury. As for lawful usury, it is that which guides seeking what is better than it, meaning as in this verse. It was said that what is in this verse is forbidden usury, so the meaning of does not increase with God according to this statement is not ruled by it, but rather applies to the one from whom it is taken. Al-Muhallab said: The scholars differed regarding someone who gives a gift seeking reward from it. Malik said: It should be looked into. If someone like him seeks reward from the one to whom it is given, then he is entitled to it, such as a gift from a poor person to a rich person, a gift from a servant to his master, or a gift from a man to his leader. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi’i. Abu Hanifa said: He is not entitled to reward if he did not stipulate it. This is the other opinion of al-Shafi’i. The majority of scholars read li-yaribu with a dhammah on the basis that the verb is attributed to the pronoun of usury. Nafi’ and Ya’qub read it with a damma over the letter, addressing the group, meaning that you will have extras. Abu Malik read it as tarbooha, and the meaning of the verse is that it will not be purified by God nor will He reward it because He only accepts that which is done sincerely for Him. And whatever you give in zakat, desiring the countenance of God meaning, and whatever you give in charity not seeking a reward, but rather intending by it what is with God, those are the ones who will receive multiples. The multiple is less than the multiples of good deeds, and they are given for a good deed ten times its value up to seven hundred times. Al-Farra’ said: It is similar to their saying: fat, thirsty, and weak, if he has fat, thirsty, or weak camels. Abu Al-Mudha’foon read it with a fatha on the ‘ayn, the passive participle.
30:40: 40- “God is He who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life. Is there any of your partners who does any of that?” The Almighty returned to the argument against the polytheists, and that He is the Creator, the Provider, the One who causes death and gives life. Then He said in the form of a question, Is there any of your partners who does any of that? It is known that they say that there is no one among them who does any of that, so the argument is established against them. Then the Almighty cleared Himself and said, Glory be to Him and He is exalted above what they associate with Him. That is, clear Himself of all that is, and He is exalted above anything of that being permissible for Him. His saying, of your partners is an advanced predicate, and of is for partiality, and the subject is the relative pronoun: I mean whoever does, and of that is related to something omitted because it is a state of thing mentioned after it, and of in of something is an additional emphasis. He added the partners to them because they called them gods and assigned them a share of their wealth.
30:41: 41- Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned. God Almighty has made it clear that polytheism and sins are the reason for the appearance of corruption in the world. There is disagreement over the meaning of the aforementioned appearance of corruption. Some say it refers to drought, lack of vegetation, decreased sustenance, increased fear, and the like. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: Corruption on land is the killing of a son of Adam by his brother, meaning Cain's killing of Abel. And on the sea, it refers to the king who used to seize every ship by force. I wonder what evidence led them to this far-fetched specification and strange designation? The verse was revealed to Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the definite article in corruption refers to the genus, so it includes all corruption that occurs on land and at sea. Al-Suddi said: Corruption is polytheism, and it is the greatest corruption. It could be said that although polytheism is the perfect individual in the types of sins, there is no evidence that it is meant specifically. It was also said that corruption is the stagnation of prices and the scarcity of livelihood. It was also said that corruption is blocking roads and injustice. Others were said that are specific and for which there is no evidence. What is apparent from the verse is the emergence of what can be called corruption, whether it is related to the actions of the children of Adam, such as their sins and commission of evil deeds, their estrangement, injustice and fighting, or it is related to what is from God, the Most High, due to their sins, such as drought, frequent fear, death, loss of crops and loss of fruits. The land and sea are the two well-known and famous ones. It was said that the land is the wilderness, and the sea is the villages that are on water, as was said by Ikrimah. The Arabs call cities seas. Mujahid said: The land is what is of the cities and villages that are not on a river, and the sea is what is on the bank of a river. The first is more appropriate. The meaning of the land is the cities of the land, and the meaning of the sea is the cities of the sea, and what is connected to the cities of their farms and pastures. The ba in bi-ma kasabt is for causality, and ma is either a relative pronoun or a verbal noun that He may make them taste some of what they have done. The lam is related to dahr and it is the lam of cause: meaning that He may make them taste the punishment of some of their work or the recompense for their work that they may return from their sins and repent to God.
30:42: 42- Say, ‘Travel through the land and observe what was the end of those before.’ When God Almighty explained the appearance of corruption due to what the hands of the polytheists and sinners had earned, He explained to them the misguidance of their peers from the people of the earlier times, and He commanded them to travel to observe their traces and see what their end was, for their homes were empty and their lands were desolate and desolate, like the ‘Aad and Thamud and similar groups of disbelievers. The phrase most of them were polytheists is a new sentence to explain the state they were in and to clarify the reason why their end came to be what it came to be.
30:43: 43- So direct your face toward the upright religion before there comes a Day from which there is no averting. This is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation, as his example in it, as if the meaning is that if corruption has become apparent due to the aforementioned reason, then direct your face, O Muhammad, etc. Al-Zajjaj said: Make your direction toward following the upright religion, which is the straight Islam, before there comes a Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection, from which there is no averting, no one can turn it back. Al-Mard is the source of Radda. It was said that the meaning is: make the truth clear and go to great lengths in making excuses. From God is related to comes, or to an omitted word indicated by the source: that is, no one from God can turn it back. It was said that the meaning may be that God will not turn it back, because His eternal will is related to its coming. It contains weakness and bad manners towards God that is not hidden. On that Day they will be split apart. Its root is they will be split apart, and splitting apart means dispersing. It is said: The people split apart if they disperse. From this comes the saying of the poet: We were like Juthayma’s companions for a while, until it was said that they would never split apart. What is meant by their dispersion here is that the people of Paradise will go to Paradise, and the people of Hell will go to Hell.
30:44: 44- Whoever disbelieves, upon him shall be his disbelief meaning the penalty for his disbelief, which is Hellfire. And whoever does righteousness, then they prepare for themselves meaning they prepare for themselves homes in Paradise through righteous deeds. A mattress is a bedding. You have spread out a mattress: you have laid it out and made it smooth. So righteous deeds, which are a reason for entering Paradise, are like building homes in Paradise and furnishing them. It has also been said that the meaning is: then they fear for themselves, from their saying about someone who fears: Or have I spread out my mattress and slept? The adverbial phrase is brought forward in both instances to indicate specificity. Mujahid said: then they prepare for themselves in the grave.
30:45: The lam in 45- to reward those who have believed is related to they split apart, or they prepare: that is, they disperse so that God may reward the believers with what they deserve from His grace or they prepare themselves with righteous deeds so that He may reward them. And it was said that it is related to something omitted. Ibn Atiyyah said: Its meaning is that it is so that He may reward, and the reference is to what came before from His statement: whoever works and whoever disbelieves. Abu Hayyan made the division of His statement those who believe and do righteous deeds omitted because of the indication of His statement: Indeed He does not love the disbelievers on it, because it is a metaphor for His hatred of them, which necessitates His anger, glory be to Him, and His anger entails His punishment.
30:46: 46- And among His signs is that He sends the winds as good tidings. That is, among the signs of His wondrous power is sending the winds as good tidings of rain, because they precede it, as in His Almighty’s statement: As good tidings before His mercy. The majority of scholars read winds. Al-A’mash read wind in the singular, intending the genus, because He said good tidings. The lam in His statement: And that He may make you taste of His mercy is connected to sends. That is, He sends the winds as good tidings, and He sends them to send you a taste of His mercy. That is, He sends them as sends. It was said that it is connected to something omitted: that is, And that He may make you taste of His mercy. It was said that the waw is an addition, according to the opinion of those who allow that, so the lam is connected to sends. “And that the ships may sail by His command.” It is conjoined with That He may make you taste of His mercy. That is, He sends the winds so that the ships may sail in the sea when they blow. And when He attributed the sailing to the ships, He followed it with His statement by His command. “And that you may seek of His bounty.” That is, seek provision through the trade carried by the ships. And perhaps you will be grateful. These blessings make you worship God alone and increase your obedience. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse {And whatever you give in interest}, that he said: Usury is of two types: permissible interest and impermissible interest. As for permissible interest, it is a gift from one man to another, wanting more or multiples of it. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from him, that he said: This is permissible interest, that he gives a gift, wanting more than it, and there is no reward or sin for him. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, specifically forbade it, saying: {And do not bestow favors, expecting more.} Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, {And whatever you give in zakat}, that he said: It is charity. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, regarding the verse {Corruption has appeared on land and sea}, that he said: Land is the wilderness that has no river near it, and sea is the towns and villages on the banks of a river. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, regarding the verse, that he said: The decrease in blessings is due to the deeds of the servants so that they may repent. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him, {Perhaps they will return}, that he said: From sins. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: They split apart. He said: They disperse.
30:47: His statement: 47- And We had certainly sent before you messengers to their people just as We sent you to your people and they came to them with clear proofs meaning with miracles and clear arguments, so We took revenge on them: meaning they disbelieved, and We took revenge on those who committed crimes meaning they committed crimes, which are sins, and it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers This is information from God, the Most High, that His support for His believing servants is incumbent upon Him, and He is true to His promise and does not break His promise, and in it is an honor for the believers and further honor for His righteous servants, and some of the reciters stopped at haqq and made the subject of kana a pronoun in it and its predicate haqq: meaning, the vengeance was incumbent. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is weak, and what is correct is that support the believers is its subject and haqq is its predicate, and upon Us is related to haqq or to an omitted word that is an attribute of it.
30:48: 28- God is He Who sends the winds. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Muhaisin read He sends “the wind” in the singular. The rest read the winds. Abu Amr said: Everything that has the meaning of mercy is plural, and whatever has the meaning of torment is singular. This sentence is a new sentence introduced to explain what preceded about the states of the winds. Thus, the sentence And We have sent is interrupted by His statement, And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers. “Then it stirs up a cloud,” that is, it disturbs it from where it is. Then He spreads it out in the sky however He wills, sometimes moving, sometimes standing, sometimes closed, sometimes not closed, sometimes to a far distance, and sometimes to a short distance. The explanation of this verse has been presented previously in Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat An-Nur. And He makes it into fragments, another time, or He makes it after spreading it out into separate pieces. A fragment is the plural of a fragment, and a fragment is a piece of the cloud. The interpretation and difference of reading of it were presented above: Then you will see the rain emerging from within it. The rain is the rain, and from within it is from its middle. Abu Al-Aliyah and Al-Dahhak read it emerging from its middle. Then when He sends down with it meaning rain whoever He wills of His servants meaning their countries and lands. At once they rejoice. “At once” is the suddenness: meaning they are surprised by the rejoicing at the coming of the rain, and rejoicing is happiness.
30:49: 49- And if they were before it descended upon them meaning before the rain descended upon them. And is the lightened form and contains a pronoun of matter understood as its subject: meaning, and the matter was before it descended upon them. His saying, before it is a repetition for emphasis, as stated by Al-Akhfash and most of the grammarians as reported by An-Nahhas. Qatrib said: The pronoun in before it refers to the rain: meaning, and if they were before the descent, before the rain. It was also said that the meaning is: before the rain was sent down upon them, before the crops and the rain. It was also said that it descended upon them, before the clouds: meaning before seeing it, and An-Nahhas chose this. It was also said that the pronoun refers to the eclipse, and it was said to the sending, and it was said to the good report. The first face is more correct, and what follows from all of these faces is extremely forced and arbitrary, and the predicate of was is in despair meaning hopeless or miserable. An investigation of this has already been presented.
30:50: 50- So look at the traces of God’s mercy resulting from the sending down of rain in the form of plants, fruits, and crops through which comes fertility and ease of living: that is, look with consideration and insight so that you may conclude from this the Oneness of God and His uniqueness in this wondrous creation. The majority read Athar in the singular form. Ibn Amir, Hafs, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read Athar in the plural form. How He revives the earth after its death? The subject of Revival is a pronoun referring to God, the Most High. It was also said that it is a pronoun referring to the trace. This sentence is in the accusative case with Look at: that is, look at the manner of this wondrous revival of the earth. Al-Jahdary and Abu Haywah read it with the fathah, meaning that its subject is a pronoun referring to mercy or to the effects, according to the reading of those who read it with the plural. The reference in his saying: That is to God Almighty: meaning that God, the Great in status, the Inventor of these mentioned things, is the Giver of Life to the dead, meaning that He is able to give them life in the Hereafter, raise them up, and reward them, just as He gave life to the dead earth with rain. And He is over all things competent, meaning that He is of great and abundant power.
30:51: 51- And if We send a wind and they see it yellow The pronoun in they see it refers to the crops and vegetation that were the result of God's mercy: that is, they see it yellow from the cold caused by the wind that God sent after it had turned green. It was also said that it refers to the wind, and it is permissible to make it masculine or feminine. It was also said that it refers to the effect indicated by the effects. It was also said that it refers to the clouds because if they were yellow, they would not rain, but the former is more appropriate. The lam is the introductory particle, and the answer to the oath they would have continued to disbelieve after that fulfills the role of the answer to the condition. The meaning is: And if We send a hot or cold wind, and it strikes their crops with yellow, they would have continued to disbelieve in God and deny His blessings. This is evidence of their quick changeability, lack of patience, and weak hearts, and this is not the case with the people of faith.
30:52: Then he likened them to the dead and the deaf, saying: 52- For indeed, you cannot make the dead hear if you call them, so it is the same for these people due to their lack of understanding of the truths and their lack of knowledge of what is correct. And the deaf cannot hear the call if you call them to the truth and admonish them with the admonitions of God, and remind them of the Hereafter and what is in it. And His saying: When they turn away, departing is a statement of their turning away from the truth after stating that they are like the dead and that they are deaf-eared. The explanation of this has already been presented in Surat An-Naml.
30:53: Then he described them as blind, saying: 53- And you cannot guide the blind from their misguidance because they cannot benefit from their sight as they should, or because they cannot gain insight. You only hear those who believe in Our signs meaning you only hear these people because they are people of contemplation, reflection, and reasoning based on the effects of the effect. So they are Muslims meaning they oppose the truth and follow it.
30:54: 54- God is He Who created you from weakness. God the Almighty mentioned another proof of His perfect power, which is the creation of man himself in different stages, and the meaning of from weakness is from a sperm-drop. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: from a sperm-drop, and the meaning is from a weak person. It was said that what is meant is the state of childhood and youth. Then He made, after weakness, strength. This is the strength of youth, for at that time the strength is strengthened and the creation is strengthened until it reaches its peak. Then He made, after strength, weakness. This means in old age and decrepitude. And gray hair. Gray hair is the completion of weakness and the end of old age. The majority of scholars read difference with a damma on the letter Ḍād in these instances. Asim and Hamzah read it with a fatha. Al-Jahdary read it with a fatha in the first two and a damma in the third. Al-Farra' said: Damm is the language of Quraysh and fatha is the language of Tamim. Al-Jawhari said: Weakness and weakness are the opposite of strength. It was said that it is with the fat-ha in opinion, and with the damma in body. He creates what He wills, meaning from all things, including strength and weakness in the children of Adam. And He is the All-Knowing of His management. The All-Powerful to create what He wants. The Kufians permitted weakness with the fat-ha on the dad and the ayn.
30:55: 55- And on the Day the Hour is established meaning the Resurrection. It is called an hour because it will occur in the last hour of the worldly life. The criminals will swear that they had not remained more than an hour meaning they will swear that they had not remained in this world, or in their graves, more than an hour. It is possible that they had assumed that the length of their stay was insignificant and that this had settled in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking that their oaths were in accordance with reality. Ibn Qutaybah said: They lied at this time just as they had lied before, and this is what is apparent because if they had intended that they would remain in this world, then each one of them knew the amount of time that would have passed, and if they had intended that they would remain in their graves, then they swore out of ignorance if they did not know the times in the intermediate realm. Thus were they led astray It is said that a man was akka meaning he was diverted from the truth. The meaning is: they were diverted in a similar manner. It was also said that what was meant was that they would be diverted from the truth, and it was also said that they would be diverted from goodness. The first is more appropriate and is evidence that their oaths were lies.
30:56: 56- And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, ‘You have remained in the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection.’ There is disagreement about identifying those who were given knowledge. Some say they are the angels, others the prophets, others the scholars of the nations, and others the believers of this nation. There is nothing wrong with applying it to all of them. The meaning of ‘in the Book of God’ is in His knowledge and judgment. Al-Zajjaj said: In the knowledge of God established in the Preserved Tablet. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators interpreted this as an inversion, estimating: And those who were given knowledge said in the Book of God. The response of those who were given knowledge was an oath for emphasis, or to counter an oath with an oath. Then they alerted them in a way of rebuke that this time in which they had become is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know that it was true. Rather, you were hastening it in denial and mockery.
30:57: 57- On that Day, no excuse will benefit those who did wrong. That is, their apologies will not benefit them on that Day, nor will their knowledge of the Resurrection benefit them. It was said that when the believers responded to them, they asked to return to the world and apologized, but they were not excused. The majority of scholars read will not benefit with a fat-ha, while Asim, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read it with a dhamma. Nor will they be asked to repent. It is said, I sought his repentance, so he repented to me, meaning, I sought his satisfaction, so he satisfied me. This applies if you have wronged him. The true meaning of I sought his repentance is to remove a rebuke. The meaning is that they will not be called to remove their repentance and obedience as they were called to do in this world.
30:58: 58- And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an from every [kind of] example meaning from every example of the examples that guide them to the Oneness of God and the truthfulness of His Messengers, and We have presented to them every argument that indicates the invalidity of polytheism. And if you bring them a sign from the verses of the Qur’an that speak of that, or if you bring them a sign like the staff and the hand, those who disbelieve will surely say, ‘You are not but falsifiers’ meaning, you, O Muhammad, and your companions, are nothing but falsifiers, followers of falsehoods who follow magic and what is similar to it in falsehood.
30:59: 59- Thus does God set a seal upon the hearts of those who do not know. That is, God sets a seal like that upon the hearts of those who lack beneficial knowledge by which they are guided to the truth and saved from falsehood.
30:60: Then God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be patient, explaining that by the truth of God's promise and the impossibility of breaking it. He said: 60- So be patient with what you hear from them of harm and what you see of disbelieving acts, for God has promised you victory over them, the elevation of your argument and the manifestation of your call, and His promise is true and there is no breach in it. And do not let those who have no certainty impress you meaning, do not let those who do not have certainty in God, nor believe in His prophets nor in His books, make you frivolous and provoke you away from your religion and what you are following. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is said that someone impresses someone else, meaning he makes him follow him in error. The majority read istakhfanakkanak with a voiced kha and a fa, while Ya'qub and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a silent ha and a qaf from al-istihaaq. The prohibition in the verse is from the principle: I do not see you here. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Darda’ who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: There is no Muslim who defends the honor of his brother except that it is a right upon God to defend him from the fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: And it is incumbent upon Us to support the believers. This is on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab on the authority of Umm Al-Darda’ on the authority of Abu Darda’. Abu Ya’la and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding His statement: And He will make it into fragments, he said: pieces one on top of the other. Then you will see the rain, he said: rain. Emerging from within it, he said: from between it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: This verse: Indeed, You cannot make the dead hear, nor can the deaf hear the call, was revealed regarding the supplication of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for the people of Badr. The chain of transmission is weak. It is well-known in the two Sahihs and elsewhere that Aisha used this verse as evidence to reject the narration of the Companions who narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out to the people of the well of Badr. This is an example of using a general term to reject a specific term, as “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when it was said to him: ‘You are calling out to decaying bodies. You do not hear what I say any better than they do.’” In Muslim, from the hadith of Anas, “When Umar ibn al-Khattab heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, calling out to them, he said: ‘O Messenger of God, you are calling out to them after three days, and do they hear? God says: You do not hear the dead.’ He said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you do not hear any better than they, but they are not able to respond.’”
31:1: It has thirty-four verses. It is Meccan except for three verses, which are His statement: And if all the trees on the earth were pens until the end of the three verses. Ibn Abbas said this, as narrated by An-Nahhas from him. Ibn Ad-Durais, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated from him that it is Meccan and he did not make any exception. Al-Qurtubi narrated from Qatadah that it is Meccan except for two verses. An-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated from Al-Baraa’ who said: We used to pray Dhuhr behind the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and we would hear from him verse after verse from Surat Luqman and Surat Adh-Dhariyat. His saying: 1- Alif, Lam, Meem. We have already discussed examples of the opening of this surah, and its grammatical position is complete, so we will not repeat it. The reference to the allusion is also explained.
31:2: 2- These are the verses of the Book. We have already discussed examples of the opening of this surah, and their syntactic position is complete, so we will not repeat it. The reference of the allusion will also be explained. The Wise can either mean the active participle, the active participle, or the possessor of wisdom or the wise one who said it.
31:3: 3- Guidance and mercy are in the accusative case as a state according to the reading of the majority. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that these are the verses of the Book in the state of guidance and mercy. Hamzah read and mercy in the nominative case as predicate of a deleted subject: i.e. it is guidance and mercy. It is also permissible for them to be predicate of those. The doer of good is the one who does good deeds, or the one who worships God as if he sees Him, as was proven from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Sahih when Gabriel asked him about ihsan, so he said: It is to worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you.
31:4: Then he explained the actions of the righteous, saying: 4- Those who establish prayer and give zakat and are certain of the Hereafter. The word muwasil is in the accusative case as a description of the righteous, or in the nominative case, or in the accusative case as praise or emphasis. He singled out these three acts of worship because they are the mainstay of acts of worship.
31:5: 5- Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful. The explanation of this was presented at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. The meaning here is that those who are characterized by doing good and performing those acts of obedience, which are the mothers of worship, are on the path of guidance. They are the ones who achieve their goals and are victorious in the best of both worlds.
31:6: 6- And among the people is he who buys the amusement of speech The place of of the people is in the nominative case as explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah, and its predicate is who buys the amusement of speech and who is either a relative pronoun or a description. Ambiguity of speech is everything that distracts from goodness such as singing, entertainment, fabricated hadiths, and everything that is reprehensible, and the addition is explanatory. It was said that what is meant is buying female singers and singers, so the interpretation would be: and who buys the people of ambiguous speech? Al-Hasan said: Ambiguity of speech is musical instruments and singing. It was narrated from him that he said: it is disbelief and polytheism. Al-Qurtubi said: The first thing that was said in this chapter is to explain ambiguous speech as singing. He said: It is the saying of the Companions and the Followers, and the lam in to lead astray from the path of God is for explanation. The majority read it with a damma on the ya of to lead astray meaning to lead others astray from the path of guidance and the method of truth, and if he leads others astray, then he has gone astray himself. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Warsh and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a fatha on the ya’, meaning that he may go astray in his own mind. Az-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads it with a damma on the ya’, its meaning is that he may lead others astray. So if he leads others astray, then he himself has gone astray. Whoever reads it with a fatha on the ya’, its meaning is that his affair may lead to misguidance. Even if he does not buy to go astray, his affair may lead to that. This explanation indicates that only the one who buys idle talk for this purpose deserves to be blamed. This is supported by the reason for revelation of the verse, which will be discussed later. Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars of all regions have unanimously agreed that singing is disliked and forbidden. Only Ibrahim ibn Sa’d and Abdullah al-Anbari differed from the group. Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: It is permissible for a man to listen to his female slave singing, since nothing of her outward or inward nature is forbidden to him, so how can he be prevented from enjoying her voice? I said: I have compiled a treatise containing the statements of the scholars on singing and the evidence used by those who permit it and those who prohibit it. I have verified this position in such a way that whoever examines it and ponders its meanings will not need to look at anything else. I have called it [Invalidating the Claim of Consensus on the Prohibition of Absolute Listening], so whoever wants to verify the position as it should be should refer to it. The place of his statement without knowledge is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, the state of his being unaware of the state of what he is buying, or the state of what is beneficial and what is harmful in trade. For this reason, he substituted good for what is pure evil. And takes it in ridicule. The majority of scholars read with the nominative case as an apposition to buys, so it is part of the relative clause. Some say that it is in the nominative case as a resumption, and the accusative pronoun in takes it refers to the verses mentioned previously, but the former is more appropriate. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Al-A’mash read and takes it in the accusative case as an apposition to leads astray. The accusative pronoun refers to the path, so according to this reading, it is part of the explanation for the prohibition. The meaning is that he buys idle talk to mislead [people] from the path of God and takes the path in ridicule: that is, mocked at. The path is masculine and feminine. The reference in his statement Those will have a humiliating punishment is to whom. The plural is in consideration of its meaning, just as the singular in both verbs is in consideration of their wording. The humiliating punishment is the severe one by which the one who it strikes becomes humiliated.
31:7: 7- And when Our verses are recited to him, meaning when the verses of the Qur’an are recited to this mocker, he turns away in arrogance, meaning he turns away from them while being extremely arrogant. The phrase as if he did not hear them is in the accusative case as a reference to the one who did not hear, and the phrase as if there was deafness in his ears is a second state, or in place of the one before it, or a state of the pronoun hears them, and it is possible that it is a new sentence. Deafness is heaviness, and its explanation has been presented, and in it is an exaggeration in the turning away of that one who turns away. Then give him tidings of a painful punishment, meaning inform him that he will have a severe punishment in terms of pain.
31:8: Then, when He, the Almighty, explained the state of those who turn away from the signs, He explained the state of those who accept them, saying: 8- Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds meaning, they believe in God and His signs and do not turn away from them, but rather accept them and act upon them for them are gardens of pleasure meaning the pleasures of the gardens, so He reversed it for emphasis. He made for them gardens of pleasure, just as He made for the first group the humiliating punishment.
31:9: And the accusative of 9- abiding therein is in the state. Zabad bin Ali read abiding therein as a second predicate because the promise of God is true is two sources, the first confirms itself: meaning God promised a promise, and the second confirms something other than it, and it is the content of the first sentence and its estimation is true that is true. The meaning is that His promise will inevitably come to pass and there is no breach in it. And He is the Exalted in Might who is not overcome by anyone, the Wise in all His actions and words.
31:10: Then the Almighty explained His glory and wisdom by saying: 10- He created the heavens without any pillars that you can see. Pillars is the plural of pillar, and we have already discussed this in Surat Ar-Ra’d. You can see them in the genitive case as an attribute of pillars, so it could be then pillars, but not seen. It could also be in the accusative case as a state: meaning, not pillars at all. Al-Nahhas said: I heard Ali bin Sulaiman say: It is better to have it as a new sentence: that is, and no pillars. Then And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains meaning fixed mountains lest it should move with you is in the accusative case as a reason: that is, to avoid it moving with you. The Kufians understand it as lest it should move. The meaning is that it was created and He made it stable and fixed so that it does not move with mountains that He placed on it and anchored it on its back. And He dispersed therein of every kind of creature meaning every kind of creature. The meaning of dispersing has already been explained. And We sent down water from the sky and caused to grow therein of every noble pair meaning We sent down rain from the sky and caused to grow therein of every kind because of its sending down: that is, of every kind. He described it as being noble because of its beautiful color and many benefits. It was said that what is meant by this is people, so the noble among them is he who goes to Paradise, and the ignoble is he who goes to Hell. Al-Sha’bi and others said this, but the first is more appropriate.
31:11: And the reference in His saying: 11- "This to what was mentioned in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and it is the subject and its predicate is God's creation" meaning His creation. "So show me what those other than Him have created" of your gods that you worship, and the question is for rebuke and rebuke, and the meaning is: So show me what thing they have created that imitates God's creation or comes close to it, and this command to them is for the purpose of incapacitating and rebuking. Then He turns away from rebuking them with what was mentioned to judging them with apparent misguidance, so He says, "Rather, the wrongdoers are in error," so He established their injustice first and their misguidance second, and He described their misguidance as clear and obvious, and whoever is like this does not understand the argument nor is guided to the truth. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu'ab from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, "And among mankind is he who buys idle talk," meaning false talk. He is Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith bin Alqamah who bought the hadiths of the non-Arabs and their practices in their time. He used to write books from Al-Hirah to Ash-Sham and lied about the Qur'an. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated regarding the verse, saying: False talk. It is singing and the like. "To mislead [people] from the way of God," he said: Reciting the Qur'an and remembering God. This verse was revealed about a man from Quraysh who bought a female singer. Al-Bukhari narrated in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sunan also from him regarding the verse, saying: It refers to singing and the like. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding the verse, saying: Female drummers. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated from Abu Al-Sahba' who said: I asked Abdullah bin Mas'ud about his statement, "And among mankind is he who buys idle talk," he said: By God, it refers to singing. Ibn Jarir’s wording: It is singing, and God is the One besides Whom there is no god, he repeats it three times. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Umaah that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Do not sell female singers, nor buy them, and there is no good in trading in them, and their price is unlawful. Concerning such matters, this verse was revealed: And among mankind is he who buys the amusement of speech al-Ma’idah 2:17. In its chain of transmission is ‘Ubayd ibn Zuhr on the authority of ‘Ali ibn Zayd on the authority of al-Qasim ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, and there is some weakness in them. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “God has forbidden the singing girl, her sale, her price, her teaching, and listening to her. Then he recited: ‘And among mankind is he who buys the idleness of speech.’” Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sunan on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Singing sprouts hypocrisy just as water sprouts herbs. They both narrated it from him as a complete narration. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: No one raises his voice in singing except that God sends to him two devils who sit on his shoulders, striking his chest with their heels until he stops. There are ahaadeeth on this topic, each of which has its own discussion. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding his statement: And among mankind is he who buys the idleness of speech, he said: A man buys a slave girl who sings night and day.
