Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say, regarding the verse: And among the people is he who buys idle talk, “That is a man’s purchase of play and falsehood.” Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Nafi’ who said: “I was walking with Abdullah ibn Umar on a road. He heard a flute, so he put his fingers in his ears, then turned from the road. Nafi’ kept saying: ‘O Nafi’, can you hear?’ I said: ‘No.’ So he took his fingers out of his ears and said: ‘This is what I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) do.’” Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I have only been forbidden from two foolish, wicked sounds: a sound at the sound of idle talk and the flutes of Satan, and a sound at the sound of a calamity: scratching faces, rending garments, and the wailing of Satan.”
31:12: There is a difference of opinion about Luqman, was he a foreigner or an Arab? It is derived from the word luqm morsel. Those who said he was a foreigner denied it due to the definite article and foreignness, and those who said he was an Arab denied it due to the definite article and the addition of the alif and the nun. They also differed over whether he was a prophet or a righteous man. Most scholars held that he was not a prophet. Al-Wahidi narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Al-Suddi and Al-Sha'bi that he was a prophet, and the former is more likely, as will be mentioned at the end of the research. It was also said that only Ikrimah acknowledged his prophethood, although the one who narrated it on his authority was Jabir Al-Ja'fi, and he is very weak. He is Luqman bin Ba'oura bin Nahor bin Tarikh, who is Azar, the father of Ibrahim. It was also said that he is Luqman bin Anqa bin Marwan, and he was a Nubian from the people of Ayla, mentioned by Al-Suhayli. Wahb said: He is the nephew of Job. Muqatil said: He is his maternal cousin. He lived for a thousand years and took knowledge from him. He used to issue fatwas before the mission of David, but when David was sent, he stopped issuing fatwas. It was said to him: Isn't it enough for me since I have already been sufficient? Al-Waqidi said: He was a judge among the Children of Israel, and the wisdom that God gave him is jurisprudence, reason, and accuracy in speech. Wisdom was explained by those who say that his prophethood is prophethood. 1- “That you be grateful to Me” is the interpreter, because in giving wisdom there is the meaning of speech. It was said that the meaning is We told him to thank Me. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: We gave Luqman wisdom so that he would be grateful to Me. It was said: That he would be grateful to Me, so he was grateful and was wise in his gratitude. Thanks to God are praises to Him in return for the blessing and obedience to Him in what He commanded. Then God, the Almighty, made it clear that thanks are of no benefit except to the grateful one, as He said: And whoever is grateful is only grateful for his own soul, because the benefit of that returns to him and its advantage is attained by him, as through it the blessing is preserved and because of it more of it is brought to him from God, the Almighty. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy, meaning whoever makes ingratitude a substitute for gratitude for blessings, then God is Free of need of thanks, not in need of them, Praiseworthy and deserving of praise from His creation for bestowing upon them His blessings whose extent cannot be encompassed and whose number cannot be counted, even if none of His creation praises Him, because every existing being speaks His praise with the tongue of its state. Yahya ibn Salam said: He is Free of need of His creation and Praiseworthy in His actions.
31:13: 13- And when Luqman said to his son, Al-Suhayli said: His son’s name was Tharan according to Ibn Jarir and Al-Qutaibi. Al-Kalbi said: Mishkam. Al-Naqqash said: An’am. It was also said that they were both dead. Al-Qushayri said: His son and wife were disbelievers, and he continued to admonish them until they became Muslim. This sentence is connected to what came before, and the meaning is: We gave Luqman wisdom when we made him grateful in himself, and when we made him an admonisher to others. Al-Zajjaj said: When is in the accusative case with we gave. The meaning is: We certainly gave Luqman wisdom when he said. Al-Nahhas said: I think it is a mistake because there is a waw in the sentence, and it prevents that. The meaning of and he admonishes him is that he addresses him with admonitions that encourage him to monotheism and deter him from polytheism. O my son, do not associate partners with God. The majority of scholars read it with a kasra over the yaa. Ibn Kathir read it with a sukoon. Hafs read it with a fat-ha, and his prohibition of polytheism indicates that he was a disbeliever, as mentioned above. The phrase Indeed, polytheism is a great injustice explains what came before it. He began his sermon by prohibiting polytheism because it is more important than anything else. There is a difference of opinion regarding this sentence. Some say it is from the words of Luqman, and others say it is from the words of God, so it is separate from what preceded it. This is supported by what is proven in the authentic hadith that when the verse, and they do not mix their faith with injustice, was revealed, it was difficult for the Companions, and they said, Who among us has not wronged himself? So God revealed, Indeed, associating others with God is a great wrong, and their souls were at ease.
31:14: 14- And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents. This commandment concerning the parents and what follows it until His saying: because of what you used to do is an interruption between Luqman’s words with the intention of emphasizing what came before it of the prohibition of associating partners with God, and the interpretation of the commandment is His saying: That you be grateful to Me and to your parents. What is between them is an interruption between the interpreter and the interpreted, and in making gratitude to them linked to gratitude to God there is an indication that their right is one of the greatest rights over the child and the largest and most obligatory. The meaning of his mother bore him with weakness upon weakness is that she bore him in her womb and she increased in weakness every day. It was said that the meaning is that the woman is weak in creation, then pregnancy weakens her. The accusative of weakness is in the source. An-Nahhas said that it is a second object by dropping the letter: meaning she carried him weakly upon weakly. Al-Zajjaj said that the meaning is that she was obliged by her carrying him to become weak time after time. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a state of his mother and on weakness as an attribute of weakness, meaning weakness being upon weakness. The majority read it with a sukoon on the ha’ in both places. Isa Al-Thaqafi read it, and it is a narration from Abu Amr, with a fatha on them, and they are two languages. Qanab said: Is there anyone who can stop the critics and admonish them? Critics are weak and feeble. And his weaning is in two years. Weaning is weaning, which is to separate the child from his mother. It is the subject and its predicate is the circumstance. Al-Jahdary, Qatadah, Abu Raja’, Al-Hasan, and Ya’qub read it as wa-fasalahu and they are two dialects. It is said infasala ‘an kada meaning it was distinguished, and the young camel is named after it. We have already mentioned that his mother in His statement, So be grateful to Me and to your parents is the explanatory word. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a verbal noun. The meaning is: So be grateful to Me. Al-Nahhas said: Better than that is for an to be explanatory, and the phrase To Me is the destination is an explanation of the obligation to obey the command: meaning to return to Me and to no one else.
31:15: 15- And if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, meaning that which you have no knowledge of associating, do not obey them in that. We have already presented the interpretation of the verse and the reason for its revelation in Surat Al-Ankaboot, and the accusative of well-known as an attribute of a deleted source: meaning, and keep them with well-known companions. It was said that it is accusative by removing the preposition, and the meaning is with well-known. And follow the way of those who turn back to Me, meaning, follow the way of those of My righteous servants who return to Me with repentance and sincerity. Then to Me is your return, all of you, not to anyone else. Then I will inform you, meaning, I will inform you when you return, about what you used to do, of good and evil, so I will reward every worker according to his work. It was said that this context from His saying, And We have enjoined on man up to here is from the speech of Luqman, so it is not an objection and there is some distance in it.
31:16: Then the Almighty proceeded to narrate the rest of Luqman's words in his admonition to his son, saying: 16- O my son, if it be the weight of a mustard seed The pronoun in it refers to the sin, as it was narrated that Luqman's son said to his father: O my father, if I commit a sin where no one sees me, will God know about it? He said: It is: meaning the sin, and the conditional clause explains the pronoun: meaning if the sin is the weight of a mustard seed. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that what you asked me about is the weight of a mustard seed, and he used the word mustard to refer to the smallest of grains, and its weight cannot be perceived by the senses and it does not tip the scales. It was said that the pronoun in it refers to the characteristic of wrongdoing or good deeds: that is, if the characteristic of wrongdoing or good deeds is the weight of a grain, etc. Then he added to clarify the invisibility of the grain despite its lightness, saying: and it is in a rock, for its being in a rock means it has become in the most hidden and protected place. Or in the heavens or on the earth, that is, or wherever it is in the regions of the heavens or among the groceries of the earth. God will bring it forth, that is, He will bring it forth and hold its doer accountable for it. Indeed, God is Subtle, nothing is hidden from Him; rather, His knowledge reaches all that is hidden. Aware of everything; nothing is hidden from Him. The majority read in tek with the fathah, meaning if it is the sin, the issue, the characteristic, or the story. They read mithqal with the accusative case as the predicate of kana, and asma'a is one of those implied words. Nafi' read mithqal with the nominative case as the subject of kana, which is complete. The verb is feminine in this reading due to adding mithqal to the feminine. The majority of scholars read it as fatakun with a damma on the kaf. Al-Jahdary read it with a kasra and a shaddah on the noon. It is from kan which means something that is covered. Al-Suddi said: This rock is a rock that is neither in the heavens nor on the earth. Then God, the Almighty, narrated about Luqman that he commanded his son to establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient in the face of calamity. The reason for specifying these acts of obedience is that they are the mothers of worship and the foundation of all good.
31:17: And the reference in his saying: 17- That is to the acts of obedience mentioned. And the predicate of that: his saying: From the resolve of matters Al-Mubarrad said: The 'ayn is replaced by a ha', so it is said resolve and firmness. Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that he means that that is from the noble deeds of the people of good character and the resolve of the people of firmness who take the path of salvation, and Al-Qurtubi approved this.
31:18: 18- And do not turn your cheek away from people The majority read it as tas’ar while Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Asim read it as tas’aar. The meanings are similar, and sa’r is inclination. It is said sa’ar khuda or sa’ar khuda if he inclined his face and turned away out of arrogance. The meaning is do not turn away from people out of arrogance towards them. From this is the saying of the poet: When the tyrant turned his cheek, we would walk towards him with swords and scold him. Ibn Jarir narrated it like this: And when the tyrant turned his cheek, we would stand up for him from his leaning, and they would stand up. Al-Harawi said: And do not turn your cheek away from people meaning do not turn away from them out of arrogance. It is said that a camel is afflicted with a disease that twists its neck. It is also said that the meaning is: Do not turn your jaw when a man is mentioned in your presence as if you despise him. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: It is as if he forbade a person to humiliate himself unnecessarily, and perhaps he understood from ta’sir to mean humiliation. And do not walk on the earth exultantly meaning with pride and joy. The meaning is the prohibition of arrogance and haughtiness. The swaggerer walks exultantly. It is a verbal noun in the place of a circumstantial noun, and its explanation has been given above. The phrase Indeed, God does not like every arrogant boaster is an explanation for the prohibition. Arrogance means exultation, and the boaster is the one who boasts to people about his money, honor, power, etc. It does not include speaking of God’s blessings, as God says: And as for the favor of your Lord, speak of it.
31:19: 19- And be moderate in your walk means be moderate in it, and moderation is between speed and slowness. It is said that someone walked moderately, if he walked straight, not creeping like the dead, nor jumping like the jumping of devils. It has been proven that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to walk quickly, so moderation here must be understood to mean what exceeds the limit in speed. Muqatil said: Its meaning is do not be inconsistent in your walk. Ata’ said: Walk with dignity and tranquility. Like His statement: They walk on the earth humbly. “And lower your voice” means reduce it and lower it, and do not strain to raise it, because speaking louder than necessary annoys the listener. The phrase Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the braying of donkeys is an explanation for the command to lower the voice: meaning the most terrifying and ugly of them. Qatada said: The ugliest of sounds is the braying of donkeys, the beginning of which is a sigh and the end of which is a sob. Al-Mubarrad said: Its interpretation is that raising the voice is not praiseworthy and that it falls under the category of reprehensible voices. The lam in al-sawt is for emphasis, and the word al-sawt is singular despite it being added to the plural because it is a verbal noun, and it indicates abundance, and it is a verbal noun from sat he makes a sound, so it is a voiced noun. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Do you know what Luqman was like? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: He was an Abyssinian. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Ad-Dunya in Kitab Al-Mamlukun, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Luqman was an Abyssinian slave and carpenter. At-Tabarani, Ibn Hibban in Ad-Du’afa and Ibn Asakir narrated on his authority that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Take over black people, for three of them will be the leaders of the people of Paradise: Luqman the Wise, the Negus, and Bilal the Mu’adhdhin.” At-Tabarani said: He meant the Abyssinians. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding the statement: And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom, meaning reason, understanding and cleverness, but not as a prophet. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he was a prophet. We have already mentioned that the narrator on his authority was Jabir Al-Ju’fi, and he is very weak. Ahmad, Al-Hakim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim in Al-Kuna and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Verily, Luqman the Wise used to say: ‘When God entrusts something to Him, He preserves it.’” A group of the scholars of Hadeeth have mentioned narrations from a group of the Companions and Successors that include words of advice and wisdom from Luqman. However, nothing of this kind has been authentically reported from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), nor has a sound chain of transmission going back to Luqman been established for us to accept it. God, the Exalted, has narrated from His advice to His son what He narrated in this hadeeth and in Al-Kifayah. As for other than that which is not soundly reported, mentioning it is nothing but a distraction and a waste of time. He was not a prophet for what has been transmitted from him to be part of the Sharia of those before us, nor is the chain of transmission of what has been transmitted from him sound enough for mentioning that to be part of the writing down of words of wisdom, which is the lost property of the believer. Abu Ya'la, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi that Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said: This verse, But if they endeavor to make you associate others with Me, was revealed, and this has already been mentioned. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: This verse was revealed about Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, and here upon weakness, that he said: Hardship after hardship and success after success. Al-Tabarani, Ibn 'Adi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ayyub Al-Ansari that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about the verse, and do not turn your cheek [in contempt] to people, that he said: Do not be arrogant, despising God's servants and turning away from them when they speak to you. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, that he said: It is he who, when greeted, turns his neck like someone who is arrogant.
31:20: When God finished the story of Luqman, He returned to rebuking and reprimanding the polytheists and establishing proofs against them, saying: 20- Do you not see that God has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of subjecting them to humans is to benefit from them. End quote. Among the creations of the heavens that have been subjected to the children of Adam: that is, those from which they benefit are the sun, the moon, the stars, and so on. Among these are the angels, for they are guardians for the children of Adam by the command of God, the Most High. Among the creations of the earth that have been subjected to the children of Adam are stones, dirt, crops, trees, fruits, animals from which they benefit, the grass in which they graze their animals, and other countless things. What is meant by subjecting is making the subjected such that the one to whom it is subjected benefits from it, whether it is obedient to Him and under His control or not. And He has completed and perfected His blessings upon you, both apparent and hidden. Meaning, He has completed and perfected His blessings upon you. It is said that a blessing has been completed and perfected. The majority read asbagha with a seen, while Ibn Abbas and Yahya bin Ammarah read asbagha with a sad instead of a seen. Na'am is the plural of na'mah according to the readings of Nafi', Abu Amr, and Hafs. The rest read na'man with a sukoon on the 'ayn, singular, and tanween, as a generic noun meaning plural and indicating abundance, like the statement: And if you were to count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]. This is the reading of Ibn Abbas. What is meant by apparent blessings is what is perceived by the mind or the senses and recognized by those who recognize them. What is meant by hidden blessings is what is not perceived by people and is hidden from them. It is said that the apparent is health and perfect character, while the hidden is knowledge and the mind. It is said that the apparent is what is seen with the eyes of wealth, status, beauty, and acts of obedience, while the hidden is what a person finds within himself of knowledge of God, good faith, and what God wards off from distance of calamities. It is said that the apparent is the blessings of this world, and the hidden is the blessings of the Hereafter. It was said that the outward meaning is Islam and beauty, and the inward meaning is what God conceals from the servant of bad deeds. And of mankind is he who disputes about God that is, about God, the Exalted, in His Oneness and His attributes, out of stubbornness and obstinacy after the truth has become clear to him and the proof has been established against him. For this reason, He said: without knowledge of reason or transmission nor guidance by which he is guided to the right path nor an enlightening Book that God, the Exalted, has revealed. Rather, it is merely obstinacy and sheer obstinacy. The interpretation of this verse has been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah.
31:21: 21- And when it is said to them, ‘Follow what God has revealed,’ meaning, if it is said to these disputants, and the plural is based on the meaning of who, follow what God has revealed to His Messenger of the Book, they cling to mere imitation. They say, ‘Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing,’ so we worship what they used to worship of idols, and we walk in the way they used to walk in their religion. Then He says, in the way of questioning to exclude and rebuke, Or even if Satan were inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze, meaning he was inviting their fathers whom they followed in their religion: that is, they followed them in polytheism. Even if Satan were inviting them to what they are doing of polytheism, it is permissible to mean that he is inviting these followers to the punishment of the Blaze, because he has made following their fathers and adhering to their religion seem attractive to them. It is permissible to mean that he is inviting all followers and those being followed to the punishment, so his calling to those being followed is by making polytheism seem attractive to them, and his calling to the followers is by making the religion of their fathers seem attractive to them. The answer to…” If the word law is omitted: meaning he calls them and they follow him. The position of the sentence is in the accusative case as a state. How ugly is imitation, how harmful it is to its doer, how dire its consequences, and how ominous its return is to those who fall into it. Indeed, the one who calls to what God revealed to His Messenger is like someone who wants to protect a moth from the flames of a fire lest it be burned, but it refuses and falls into the burning fire and the torment of the Blaze.
31:22: 22- And whoever submits his face to God meaning, entrusts his affair to Him, devotes his worship to Him completely, and is a doer of good in his actions, because worship without doing good for Him or knowing what is needed for it does not meet the criteria by which the worship of the doers of good is met. It has been authentically reported from the Truthful, the Trusted One, that when Gabriel asked him about ihsan, he said to him, It is to worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you. “He has grasped the most trustworthy handhold” meaning, he has held fast to the most trustworthy covenant and clung to it. This is a metaphor for the state of the one who submits his face to God, like the state of someone who wants to climb a high mountain, so he holds fast to the most trustworthy rope hanging from it. And to God is the outcome of all matters meaning, their destination is to Him and no one else. Ali ibn Abi Talib, as-Sulami, and Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Yasar recited and whoever submits with a shaddah. An-Nahhas said, The lightening in this is more well-known, as God, the Almighty, said, “Say, ‘I have submitted my face to God.’
31:23: 23- And whoever disbelieves - let not his disbelief grieve you meaning, do not be sad about it, for his disbelief will not harm you. The Almighty explained the state of the disbelievers after He finished explaining the state of the believers, then He threatened them with His saying: To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did meaning, We will inform them of the evils of their deeds and will punish them for them. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts meaning, what their breasts conceal; nothing of it is hidden from Him. So, what is secret to Him is like what is public.
31:24: 24- We will grant them enjoyment for a little meaning, We will keep them in this world for a short period of time to enjoy. For transient bliss is very little compared to eternal bliss. The word little is in the accusative case as an adjective for a deleted verbal noun: meaning, a little enjoyment. Then We will compel them to a severe punishment meaning, We will force them to the punishment of the Fire. For there is nothing heavier than this for the one who falls into it and is afflicted by it. That is why severity was used metaphorically for it.
31:25: 25- And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ That is, they will acknowledge God as the Creator of that, as the matter is clear to them. This is an acknowledgment from them that indicates monotheism and the invalidity of polytheism. For this reason, He said, Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ That is, say, O Muhammad, ‘Praise be to God for your acknowledgment. How can you worship other than Him and make them partners with Him?’ Or the meaning is: So say, ‘Praise be to God for the religion He has guided us to, and there is no limit to otherness.’ Then He turned away from that and said, Rather, most of them do not know. That is, they do not consider or reflect until they know that the Creator of these things is the One to whom worship is due, and no one else.
31:26: 26- To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth in dominion and creation, so no one deserves to be worshipped but Him. Indeed, God is the Rich in need of others. The Praiseworthy meaning the One who deserves praise or is praised by His servants in word or deed.
31:27: Then when He, the Most High, mentioned that He owns what is in the heavens and the earth, He followed it with what indicates that He has beyond that what is beyond number and beyond limit, so He said: 27- And if all the trees on the earth were pens, meaning if all the trees on the earth were pens. He used the singular form of tree because it has been established in the science of semantics that the comprehensiveness of the singular is more comprehensive. It is as if He said: Every tree is a tree until not a single tree species remains except that it has been sharpened into pens. He used the plural of pens for the purpose of emphasis: meaning if He counted every tree as pens. Abu Hayyan said: This is from the singular being used in the place of the plural and the indefinite noun in the place of the definite noun, like His statement: We do not abrogate a verse, then He, the Most High, said: And the sea, after it, will be replenished by seven more seas, meaning after it is exhausted, He will replenish it by seven more seas. The majority read "and the sea in the nominative case as the subject, and and it increases" as its predicate, and the sentence is in the position of a circumstantial adverbial: that is, the circumstantial sea, with its vastness, is increased by the seven seas in an endless increase, as Sibawayh said. Al-Mubarrad said: The sea is raised by an implied action, the estimation of which is that if the sea were to remain in a state of being, it would be increased by seven seas after it. It was also said: It is raised by being in apposition to "that" and what is within its scope. Abu Amr and Ibn Abi Ishaq read "and the sea in the accusative case in apposition to the name of that, or by an implied verb that explains it and it increases". Ibn Hurmuz and Al-Hasan read "and it increases with a damma on the letter of the present tense and a kasra on the meem, from and it increases". Ja'far ibn Muhammad read "and the sea is its ink, and the answer to if is the words of God had not been exhausted" means His words, which are an expression of His knowledge. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: What is meant by the words - and God knows best - is what is in the possible, not what came into existence from it. Al-Qaffal agreed with him and said: The meaning is that if trees were pens and the seas were ink, and he wrote with them the wonders of God’s creation, proving His power and oneness, those wonders would not be exhausted. Al-Qushayri said: Al-Qaffal attributed the meaning of the words to the possible, and it is more appropriate to interpret the verse as referring to the eternal speech. Al-Nahhas said: It has been made clear that the words here refer to knowledge and the realities of things, because He, glory be to Him, knew before He created creation what He would create in the heavens and the earth of anything, and He knew what was in them of the weight of an atom, and He knew all species and what they contain of hair and limb, and what leaf is in a tree and what kinds of creation it contains. It was said that the Quraysh said: How much Muhammad speaks! So this was revealed, as Al-Suddi said. It was also said that when the verse, And of knowledge you have been given only a little was revealed about the Jews, they said, How can we, when we have been given the Torah, in which is the speech of God and His rulings? So this was revealed. Abu Ubaidah said: What is meant by the sea here is the fresh water that produces the pens, as for salt water, it does not produce the pens. I said: What is missing in this statement and what is less useful is Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise meaning He is the Victorious, nothing is beyond His power, and not a single individual among His creations is beyond His wisdom and knowledge.
31:28: 28- He created you and resurrected you only as a single soul meaning, except as the creation of a single soul and its resurrection. An-Nahhas said: This is how the grammarians estimated it, like the creation of a soul, like His statement: And ask the town. Az-Zajjaj said: Meaning, God’s ability to resurrect all of creation and to create them is like His ability to create a single soul and resurrect a single soul. Indeed, God is All-Hearing of everything he hears, All-Seeing of everything he sees. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu'ab on the authority of Ata' who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the verse: "And bestowed His blessings upon you" Al-A'raf 2:17. He said: This is one of the treasures of my knowledge. I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) about it and he said: "As for the outward, it is everything other than your creation. As for the inward, it is what conceals your private parts, and if He were to reveal them, your family would reject you. So who else would be besides them?" Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab, Al-Daylami and Ibn Al-Najjar narrated on his authority that he said: "I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) about the verse: And bestowed His blessings upon you, outward and inward. He said: As for the outward, it is Islam, everything other than your creation and what He bestowed upon you of His provision. As for the inward, it is what He conceals of your shortcomings." Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: The outward blessing is Islam, and the inward blessing is everything that He conceals from you of sins, faults and legal punishments. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said in his interpretation of the verse: It is: There is no god but God. Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, And even if all that is on the earth verse, that the Jewish rabbis said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina: O Muhammad, what do you think of your statement, ‘And of knowledge you have been given only a little,’ do you mean us or your people? He said, No. They said, Do you not recite in what has come to you that we have been given the Torah, and in it is the clarification of all things? He said, It is little in the knowledge of God. And God revealed, And even if all that is on the earth verse. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on his authority, but at a longer length. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud.
31:29: The address in His saying: 29- "Have you not seen" to everyone who is fit for that or to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, "that God merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night" meaning He inserts each one of them into the other, and its explanation has been presented in Surat Al-Hajj and Surat Al-An'am. "And He has subjected the sun and the moon" meaning He has subdued them and made them obedient to rising and setting, determining the terms and completing the benefits. The sentence is conjoined to what preceded them, although they are different. "Each runs to a specified term." There is disagreement about what the specified term is. Some say it is the Day of Resurrection, and some say the time of rising and setting, but the first is more appropriate. The sentence "And that God, with what you do, is Acquainted is conjoined to God merges": meaning He is Acquainted with what you do of deeds, nothing of which is hidden from Him, because He who has the power to do such great matters has the power to know what you do more than anything else. The majority read you work with a fat-ha, while Al-Salami, Nasr bin Aamer, and Al-Duri, on the authority of Abu Amr, read it with a dhammah as a predicate.
31:30: And the reference in His saying: 30- "That is to what was mentioned previously, and the ba in because God" is for causality: that is, because He, glory be to Him, "is the Truth" and everything else is false, or it is related to something omitted: that is, He did that so that they would know that He is the Truth. "And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood." Mujahid said: What they call upon besides Him is Satan, and it was said that what they associated with Him of an idol or something else, and this is more appropriate. "And that God is the Most High, the Grand is connected to the phrase that God is the Truth." The meaning is: That the wondrous creation that He described in the previous verses to prove the truth of God, the falsehood of everything else, and His loftiness and majesty: He is the Most High in His position, the Possessor of majesty in His Lordship and His authority.
31:31: Then He mentioned another type of His wondrous creation and marvelous power, saying: 31- Have you not seen that the ships sail through the sea by the grace of God? That is, by His kindness and mercy to you, and that is one of His greatest blessings upon you because it saves you from drowning when you travel at sea in search of sustenance. Ibn Hormuz read by the graces of God as the plural of grace. “To show you some of His signs.” Min is for partiality: that is, to show you some of His signs. Yahya bin Salam said: It is the sailing of ships in the sea by the wind. Ibn Shajarah said: What is meant by His saying of His signs is what they see of God’s power. Al-Naqqash said: What God provides for them in the sea. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful. This sentence explains what came before it: that is, in what was mentioned are great signs for everyone who has extreme patience and much gratitude, who is patient about the sins of God and is grateful for His blessings.
31:32: 32- And when a wave covers them like shadows. The wave is likened, due to its size, to that which shades a person, such as a mountain, cloud, or other things. The wave, which is singular, is likened to shadows. It is plural because death comes one thing after another, and some things pile up on top of others. It has been said that the wave has the meaning of plural because it is a verbal noun, and the root of the word wave is movement and crowding, and from it is said that the sea surged and the people surged. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah read waves like shadows as the plural of shadow. “Call upon God, sincerely devoting religion to Him,” meaning, they should call upon God alone, not relying on anyone else for their salvation, because they know that nothing can harm or benefit except Him. However, their natures are overcome by customs and the imitation of the dead. When they find themselves in such a situation, they acknowledge the Oneness of God and dedicate their religion to Him, seeking salvation and safety from what they have fallen into. Then when He delivered them to land, they are divided into two groups: One group is moderate, meaning, one who fulfilled the covenant they made with God at sea to be sincere in their religion to Him, remaining in that state after God delivered them from the terrors of the sea and brought them out to land safely. Al-Hasan said: The meaning of moderate is a believer who adheres to monotheism and obedience. Mujahid said: Moderate in speech implies disbelief. The first is what we have mentioned, and there is an ellipsis in the speech, meaning, Some of them are moderate and some are disbelievers. This ellipsis is indicated by His statement, And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous, ungrateful person. “Khatr” is the worst and ugliest form of treachery, and from this is the saying of al-A’sha: Al-Bablaq Al-Fard from Tayma, his home is a strong fortress and his neighbor is not a traitor Al-Jawhari said: “Khatr is treachery. It is said that he betrayed him, so he is a treachery.” Al-Mawardi said: This is the opinion of the majority. Ibn Atiyyah said: “It refers to the denier. Denying the verses means rejecting them, and the ungrateful person is the one who is extremely ungrateful for the blessings of God, the Most High.”
31:33: 33- O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his son at all. That is, no father will avail his son at all, nor will he benefit him in any way, because he will be preoccupied with himself. The meaning of this has already been explained in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Nor a son can avail his father at all. God Almighty mentioned two individuals from among the relatives, which are the father and the son, and they are the ultimate in compassion and mercy for one another. Any other relative other than them cannot avail, let alone strangers. O God, make us among those who hope for none but You and depend on none but You. Indeed, the promise of God is truth It will not fail. Whatever He has promised of good and threatened with of evil will inevitably come to pass. So let not the worldly life and its adornments deceive you, for it is fleeting and gone. And let not the Deceiver deceive you about God. The majority of scholars read al-Ghurur with a fatha on the voiced ghain. The deceiver is Satan, because it is his nature to deceive people and give them false hopes, distract them from the Hereafter, and turn them away from the path of truth. Simak bin Harb, Abu Haywah, and Ibn as-Sameefa’ read it with a damma on the ghain, as a verbal noun for gharra yaghra ghururan. It may be a verbal noun describing Satan as an exaggeration.
31:34: 34- Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour meaning the time when it will occur. Al-Farra' said: The meaning of this statement is negation: that is, no one knows it except God, the Almighty. An-Nahhas said: The meaning of negation came about because of what was narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said in his statement: "And with Him are the keys of the unseen. None knows them except Him," that it is this. And He sends down the rain at the times He has set for sending it down, and no one else knows that. And He knows what is in the wombs of males and females, goodness and corruption. And no soul perceives of souls, whatever they may be, with no distinction between angels, prophets, jinn, and humans, what it will earn tomorrow of earning religious or worldly gain. And no soul perceives in what land it will die meaning in what place God decrees death for it. The majority of scholars read and He sends down the rain with a shaddah. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read it with a light shaddah. The majority of scholars read it as in any land, while Abi bin Ka'b and Musa Al-Ahwazi read it as in a verse. Al-Farra' permitted this, although it is a weak dialect. Al-Akhfash said: It is permissible to say I passed by a slave girl, meaning a slave girl. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever claims to know any of these five has disbelieved in the Quran because he contradicted it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: khatār he said: ungrateful. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And let not the Deceiver deceive you about God he said: It is the devil. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah and Qatadah said. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: A man from the desert came and said: My wife is pregnant, so tell me what she will give birth to. Our land is barren, so tell me when the rain will fall. I know when I gave birth, so tell me when I will die. So God revealed: Indeed, with God is knowledge of the Hour (al-Baqarah 2:170). Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah something similar, but he added: I know what I have earned today, so what will I earn tomorrow? He also added that he asked him about the Hour. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The keys of the unseen are five, and none knows them but God: none knows what will happen tomorrow but God, and none knows when the Hour will come but God, and none knows what is in the wombs but God, and none knows when the rain will fall but God, and no soul knows in what land it will die but God.” In the two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah in the hadith of his question about the Hour and his answer with its signs, then he said: There are five, and none knows them but God. Then he recited this verse, and there are hadiths on this topic.
32:1: It is thirty verses It is a Meccan verse, as narrated by Ibn Ad-Durais, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Ibn An-Najjar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is a Meccan verse except for three verses: Then he who is a believer... until the end of the three verses. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said the same. It was also said that it was except for five verses, from His saying: Their sides forsake each other... until His saying: that which you used to deny. It was proven by Muslim and the Sunan scholars from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite in the Fajr prayer on al-Jumuah 62:Alif, Lam, Meem, Tanzil As-Sajdah and Has there not come upon man a period of time? Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others also narrated it from his hadith. Abu Ubaidah narrated in his Fada'il, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ad-Darimi, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would not sleep until he had recited Alif, Lam, Meem, Tanzil As-Sajdah and Tabarak Al-ladhi Bidhi Al-Mulk. Abu Nasr, Al-Tabarani, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, tracing it back to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: “Whoever prays four rak’ahs after the last ‘Isha’ prayer, reciting in the first two ‘Say, ‘O you disbelievers’ and ‘Say, ‘He is God, the One’, and in the last two ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion’ and ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. Tanzeel’ as-Sajdah, it will be recorded for him as if he had prayed four rak’ahs of the Night of Decree.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Whoever recites ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. Tanzeel’ as-Sajdah, ‘Ya Sin,’ ‘The Hour has drawn near’, and ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion’ as-Sajdah, between Maghrib and the last ‘Isha’ prayer, it will be as if he had prayed during the Night of Decree.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of ‘Aishah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Whoever recites at night ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. Tanzeel’ as-Sajdah, ‘Ya Sin,’ ‘The Hour has drawn near’, and ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion’, it will be a light for him and a protection from Satan, and he will be raised in status until the Day of Resurrection.” Ibn Al-Durais narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’ that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Alif, Lam, Meem is a revelation. On the Day of Resurrection, two wings will come to it, shading its owner and saying: ‘There is no way against him, there is no way against him.’” His saying: 1- Alif, Lam, Meem. We have already discussed the opening of this surah and its grammatical position in Surah Al-Baqarah and in many places in the openings of the surahs.
32:2: And the elevation of 2- Tanzil as a predicate for a deleted subject or predicate after predicate on the assumption that Alif, Laam, Meem is in the nominative case as predicate for a deleted subject, or predicate for His saying Alif, Laam, Meem on the assumption that it is the name of the surah, and La rham is in the accusative case as a state, and it is permissible for the elevation of Tanzil as a subject and its predicate La rham, and Min Rabb al-'Alamin is in the accusative case as a state, and it is permissible for all of these to be predicates for the subject understood before Tanzil, or for His saying Alif, Laam, Meem on the assumption that it is a subject, not on the assumption that they are letters listed in a list in the manner of enumeration. Al-Makki said: The best way is for La rham to be in the state, and Min Rabb al-'Alamin is the predicate, and the meaning according to these ways is: There is no doubt or suspicion in the revelation of the recited Book, and that it was sent down from the Lord of the Worlds, and that it is not a lie, nor magic, nor divination, nor myths of the ancients.
32:3: And Umm in 3- Or do they say he invented it? is the disconnected one that means rather and the hamza: meaning rather do they say it is invented? So he diverted from the first statement to what is the belief of the disbelievers with the question that includes rebuke and rebuke, and the meaning of he invented it is he fabricated it and made it up. Then he diverted from their belief to explain what is the truth regarding the Book and said: Rather it is the truth from your Lord so He belied them in their claim of fabrication, then he explained the reason for which the revelation was made and said: That you may warn a people to whom no warner came before you and they are the Arabs and they were an illiterate nation to whom no messenger came, and it was said the Quraysh in particular, and the second object of to warn is omitted: meaning that you may warn a people of punishment, and the phrase that no warner came to them is in the accusative case on the ha and before you is an attribute of warner. Abu Hayyan allowed that ma could be a relative pronoun, and the meaning is: to warn a people of the punishment that came to them from a warner before you. This is very weak, because what is meant is the explanation of the sending down of the warning to a people to whom no warner came before him, not its explanation of the warning to a people who had been warned of what he warned them of. It was said that what is meant by the people are the people of the period between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they may be guided, hoping that they will be guided or so that they will be guided.
32:4: 4- God is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself on the Throne. The interpretation of this verse has been presented in Surat Al-A’raf, and the purpose of mentioning it here is to inform them of the perfection of His power and the greatness of His creation so that they may listen to the Qur’an and contemplate it. The meaning of created: I would And he created. Al-Hasan said: The days here are from the days of this world, and it was said that the length of a day is a thousand years of the years of this world, as Ad-Dahhak said. So based on this, what is meant by the days here are from the days of the Hereafter, not from the days of this world, and there is no then for the order in His statement: Then He established Himself on the Throne and the explanation of this has been presented in full. You have not besides Him any protector or intercessor meaning you have not besides God or besides His punishment any protector to protect you and protect you from His punishment, nor an intercessor to intercede for you with Him. So will you not remember? Remember, ponder, and think, and listen to these sermons as one who understands and reasons, so that you may benefit from them.
32:5: 5- He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth because He, glory be to Him, explained the creation of the heavens and the earth, meaning: His command descends from the highest heavens to the furthest borders of the seventh earth, as He, glory be to Him, said: "God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them. The command descends between them." The distance between the lowest heaven and the earth beneath it, in descent and ascent, is a thousand worldly years. It was said that what is meant by the commanded deeds is: that He sends them down as a director from the heaven to the earth. It was also said that He directs the affair of this world by heavenly means from the angels and others, sending down their rulings and effects to the earth. It was also said that the revelation descends with Gabriel. It was also said that the Throne is the place of direction, just as what is below the Throne is the place of detail, as in His statement: "Then He established Himself upon the Throne and subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. He directs the affair, He details the verses." What is below the heavens is the place of control. God said: And We have certainly distributed it among them that they may remember. Then, when He, the Exalted, mentioned the management of the affair, He said: Then it will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count. That is, then that affair and that management will return to Him, the Exalted, during a Day the extent of which is a thousand years of the days of this world. This is based on the distance of descent from the heaven and ascension from the earth, as we have mentioned. It was also said that what is meant is that it will ascend to Him on the Day of Resurrection, the extent of which is a thousand years of the days of this world, and that is when the affairs of this world come to an end and those in it die. It was also said that it is the report of the people of the earth ascending to Him with whomever He sends to it from the angels. The meaning is that He records that with Him and writes in the scrolls of His angels what the people of the earth have done at every moment until the end of the life of this world. It was also said that the meaning of ascends to Him is that it is recorded in His knowledge as actually existing for a period of time, the extent of a thousand years. The marid is the length of time between the management of events and their occurrence. It was said that He manages the daily events by recording them in the Preserved Tablet, and the angels descend with them, then they ascend to Him in a time that is like a thousand worldly years. It was also said that a thousand years are decreed, and the angels descend with them, then they ascend after the thousand to another thousand. It was also said that what is meant is that the deeds that are acts of obedience are managed by God the Almighty and His angels descend with them, then none of them ascend to Him except the pure after a long period of time due to the fewness of His sincere servants. It was also said that the pronoun in ascends refers to except the pure after a long period of time due to the fewness of His sincere servants. It was also said that the pronoun in ascends refers to the angel even though he is not mentioned because it is understood from the context. It was stated explicitly in His statement: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him. The pronoun in to Him refers to the heaven in the language of those who mention it, or to the place of the angel to whom he returns, which is the one in which God has confirmed him. It was said that the meaning is: He manages the affair of the sun in its rising, setting, and return to God in a time whose duration, if it were managed by someone other than an angel, would be a thousand years. This is because the distance between the heaven and the earth is five hundred years, so the distance of the descent from the heaven to the earth and the return from the earth to the heaven is a thousand years. This was preferred by a group of commentators, including Ibn Jarir. It was said that the distance of the descent is a thousand years and the distance of the rising is a thousand years. This was narrated from Ad-Dahhak. This day is an expression for a time that is estimated at a thousand years, and it does not mean the term day, which is the length of a day between two nights. The Arabs may express the duration with a day, as the poet said: Two days, one day of gatherings and clubs, and one day of marching to the enemies to discipline them. The poet did not mean two specific days, but rather that their time is divided into two halves, so he expressed each of the two halves with a day. The majority read ya’rju in the active form. Ibn Abi ‘Ubaidah read it in the passive form, and the original is ya’rju bih, then the preposition was deleted and the pronoun was hidden. A group appreciated the combination of this verse with the saying of God, the Most High: The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. It was said in response that the Day of Resurrection is the extent of a thousand worldly years, but considering its difficulty and the severity of its horrors for the disbelievers, it is like fifty thousand years. The Arabs often describe the day of adversity as long as they describe the day of joy as short, as the poet said: And a day like the shadow of a spear, its length was shortened, the blood of the wineskin was cut short for us, and the flowers lined up And the other said: And a day like a cat's thumb cut off It was said that on the Day of Resurrection there are days, some of which are a thousand years long, and some of which are fifty thousand years long. It was also said that these are different times, during which the unbeliever will be punished with one type of punishment for a thousand years, then he will be transferred to another type, and punished with it for fifty thousand years. It was also said that the stations of the Resurrection will be fifty stations, each station a thousand years long. So the meaning of he will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is a thousand years is that he will ascend to Him at one of those times or stations. Al-Tha’labi narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Qatadah and Al-Dahhak that in His statement, The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years, what God meant by His statement, The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years, is the distance from the earth to the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is the station of Gabriel. What is meant is that Gabriel and the angels who are with him will travel to the earth at that station a distance of fifty thousand years, in the amount of one worldly day. What He meant by His statement, on a Day the extent of which is a thousand years, is the distance between the earth and the lowest heaven, descending and ascending, for it is the amount of one thousand worldly years. It was said that this is an indication of the extension of the implementation of the command, because the one whose command is fully implemented in a day or two and is then interrupted is not like the one whose command is implemented over many years. So his statement, in a day the measure of which is a thousand years means that the command is managed in the time of a day of which a thousand years. So how much of it is a month? And how much of it is a year? Based on this, there is no difference between a thousand years and fifty thousand years. Other than that was said. The scholar of this nation, Ibn Abbas, when asked about the two verses, stopped, as will come at the end of the research, God willing. The majority read of what you count with the superlative as addressing, while Al-Hasan, As-Salami, Ibn Waththab, and Al-A’mash read it with the subjunctive as addressing.
32:6: And the reference in His saying: 6- That is to God, the Most High, in consideration of His being described with those attributes, and it is the subject and its predicate is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed meaning the Knower of what is hidden from creation and what is present to them. And in this there is a sense of threat because if He, the Most High, knows what is hidden and what is present, then it is a metaphor for every worker according to his work. Or He manages the matter according to what His wisdom requires, the Almighty, the Dominant, the Victorious, the Merciful to His servants, and these are predicates of that subject.
32:7: Likewise, his statement: 7- Who has perfected everything which He created is another piece of report. The majority read created it with a fat-ha on the lam. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read it with a sukoon on it. According to the first reading, it is a past tense verb describing something, so it is in the genitive case. Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim chose the reading of the majority. It is also permissible for it to be an adjective for the construct, so it is in the accusative case. As for the second reading, there are aspects to its accusative: The first is that it is a substitute for everything, a substitute of inclusion, and the pronoun refers to everything, and this is the well-known aspect among grammarians. The second is that it is a substitute for everything, and the pronoun refers to God, the Most High. The meaning of best is good, because there is nothing except that it is created according to what wisdom dictates, so all creation is good. The third is that everything is the first object, and its creation is the second object, implying the meaning of best, which means gave, and the meaning is: He gave everything its creation with which He distinguished it. It was said that it implied the meaning of inspired. Al-Farraa said: He inspired His creation with everything they need. The fourth is that it is accusative as a verbal noun emphasizing the meaning of the sentence: i.e. He created it a creation like his saying: God made. This is the opinion of Sibawayh, and the pronoun refers to God, the Most High. The fifth is that it is accusative by removing the preposition, and the meaning is that He made everything good in His creation. The meaning of the verse is that He perfected and perfected the creation of His creatures, so some of the creatures, even if they are not good in themselves, are perfected and established. So the meaning of this verse is the same as He gave each thing its creation, i.e. He did not create man in the creation of an animal, nor did He create the animal in the creation of man. It was said that it is general in wording but specific in meaning: i.e. He created everything good. And He began the creation of man from clay, meaning Adam, He created him from clay, so he became in a beautiful form and beautiful shape.
32:8: 8- He made his offspring meaning his progeny from a lineage. Offspring are called a lineage because they are derived from the root and separated from it. Its explanation was presented in Surat Al-Mu’minun. The meaning of from despised water is from despised water that is not dangerous to people, which is semen. Al-Zajjaj said: from weak water.
32:9: 9- Then He proportioned him meaning the human being whose creation began from clay, which is Adam, or the entire species, and what is meant is that He made his creation even and proportioned his form and made his limbs proportionate, and breathed into him of His spirit the addition is for honour and respect, and this addition strengthens that the speech is about Adam and not about his offspring, even if it can be directed in relation to everyone. Then He addressed all of mankind, saying: And He has given you hearing, sight, and hearts. That is, He created these things for you as a completion of His blessings upon you and as a perfecting of His perfecting of your creation, so that blessings may be gathered for you, so that you may hear everything that is heard, see everything that is seen, reason everything that is reasoned, and understand everything that is understood. He singled out hearing because it is a source that includes little and much, and He singled out hearing by mentioning the source without sight and the heart, so He mentioned them by name, and for this reason they were combined, because hearing is a single faculty and has a single location, which is the ear, and it has no choice in it. Sound reaches it and it is not able to reject it, nor to specify hearing for some things that are heard and not others. This is in contrast to sight, whose location is the eye, and it has a choice in it. It moves to the side of the visible and not to the other, and closes its eyelids if it does not want to see something. Likewise, the heart has a kind of choice in its perception, so it reasoned this and not that, and understands this and not that. The majority of the readers read it and began with a hamza, while Al-Zuhri read it with a pure alif without a hamza. The accusative of how little you thank is that it is a deleted verbal noun, meaning a little thanks, or an adjective of a deleted time, meaning a short time. This shows their ingratitude for God's blessings and their abandonment of thanking Him except in rare circumstances.
32:10: 10- And they said, 'Shall we, when we are lost in the earth?' The difference of opinion among the reciters has already been mentioned regarding this hamza and the hamza that follows it. Loss is disappearance. It is said: The dead person was lost in the dust if he disappeared and vanished. The Arabs say of something that is overcome by something else until its trace is hidden, it has been lost. From this is the saying of Al-Akhtal: I was the speck in a turbid, foaming wave, the one who brought it threw it away as a misguidance Qatrib said: The meaning of dalalana fi al-ardh is: we disappeared into the earth. The majority of scholars read dalalana with a fatha on the dhad and a fatha on the lam, meaning we went, lay down, became dust, and disappeared from sight. Yahya ibn Ya'mar, Ibn Muhaisin, and Abu Raja' read dalalana with a kasra on the lam, which is the dialect of Aliyah in Najd. Al-Jawhari said: The people of Aliyah say dalalta with a kasra. He said: and adahaluhu: meaning he lost him and destroyed him. It is said that the dead person is lost if he is buried. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Al-Hasan, Al-A'mash, and Aban ibn Sa'id read dalalana with a silent sad and a fatha on the lam, meaning you are lost. An-Nahhas said: It is not known in the language that we say salalan, but it is said sala al-lahm if it rots. Al-Jawhari said: sala al-lahm yasalun with a kasra, salulan if it rots, whether cooked or raw. From this comes the saying of Al-Hutay'ah: That is a young man who exerts his effort, and his meat does not spoil. Shall we indeed be in a new creation? That is, will we be resurrected and become alive? The question is one of astonishment. This is the statement of the disbelievers who deny the resurrection, so God, the Exalted, shifted from explaining their disbelief by denying the resurrection to explaining something more eloquent than it, which is their disbelief in meeting God. He said: Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord. That is, they deny Him out of stubbornness and obstinacy, because their acknowledgment that He is the Initiator of creation necessitates their acknowledgment that He is Able to bring about resurrection.
32:11: Then the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to explain to them the truth and refute their false claims, saying: 11- Say, ‘The Angel of Death who has been appointed over you will take you.’ It is said: God takes him and takes his soul if He takes him to Himself, and the Angel of Death is Azrael, and the meaning of assigned to you is: He is assigned to take your souls when your appointed times come. Then to your Lord you will be returned, meaning you will become alive to Him through resurrection and revival, not to anyone else, and He will reward you for your deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: He directs the affair verse, he said: This is in this world, the angels ascend in a day the length of which is a thousand years. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on his authority regarding the verse: In a day the length of which is a thousand years. He said: One of the six days in which God created the heavens and the earth. Abd Al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Al-Anbari in Al-Masahif, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Malekah who said: I entered upon Abdullah bin Abbas, I and Abdullah bin Fayruz, the client of Uthman bin Affan, and Ibn Fayruz said to him: O Abu Abbas, his statement: He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth, then it ascends to Him in a Day the length of which is a thousand years, so it was as if Ibn Abbas suspected him and said: What is a day the length of which is fifty thousand years? He said: I only asked you to tell me. Ibn Abbas said: They are two days that God mentioned in His Book. God knows best about them, and I hate to say about God’s Book what I do not know. Time dealt its blows until I sat with Ibn Al-Musayyab. A person asked him about them, but he did not tell him and did not know. I said: Shall I not tell you what I remembered from Ibn Abbas? He said: Yes. So I told him, and he said to the questioner: This Ibn Abbas has refused to say anything about it, and he is more knowledgeable than me. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: {its length is a thousand years} that he said: The day will not be halfway through the length of a day in this world on that day until judgment is passed between the servants, so the people of the jinn will descend to Paradise and the people of Hell will descend to Hell. If it were to be done elsewhere, it would not have been finished in fifty thousand years. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him regarding His statement: {then it will ascend to Him in a Day} of your days, and the journey between the heaven and the lowest heaven is five hundred years. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi in Nawader Al-Usul, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite, Who has perfected everything which He created, and he said, I have never seen a monkey that is not beautiful, but He perfected their creation. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse that he said, As for the monkeys, they are not beautiful, but He perfected their creation. He said, His creation means his form. He said, He has perfected everything, meaning the ugly and the beautiful, scorpions, snakes and everything that He created, and other than that, none of that is beautiful. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that he said, “While we were with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, we met Amr ibn Zurarah Al-Ansari wearing a garment that had let its garment hang down. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, took hold of the hem of his garment and said, ‘O Messenger of God, I have hairy legs.’ The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said, ‘O Amr ibn Zurarah, God has perfected everything that He created. O Amr ibn Zurarah, God does not like those who let their garments hang down.” Ahmad and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Al-Sharid bin Suwaid who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man who had let his garment hang down, so he said: ‘Lift your garment.’ The man said: ‘O Messenger of God, I have a humpbacked face and my knees knock.’ He said: ‘Lift your garment, all of God’s creation is beautiful.’”
32:12: His statement: 12- And if you could but see when the criminals will lower their heads before their Lord. What is meant by the criminals are those who say, If we have gone astray. The address here is to everyone who is suitable for it, or to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is possible that what is meant by the criminals is every criminal, and those who say it are primarily included in it. The meaning of they will lower their heads is that they will lower them out of shame and regret for what they have neglected in this world of associating partners with God and disobeying Him. The meaning of before their Lord is when He calls them to account. Al-Zajjaj said: Addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is addressing his nation. The meaning is: If you could see, O Muhammad, those who deny the resurrection on the Day of Resurrection, you would see the wonder. Our Lord, we have seen and heard, meaning they will say: Our Lord, we have now seen what we used to deny and we have heard what we used to deny. It was also said: We have seen the truth of Your threat and we have heard the confirmation of Your messengers. These people saw when sight did not benefit them and heard when hearing did not benefit them. So send us back to the world so that we may do righteous work as You commanded us. Indeed, we are certain, meaning, we believe. It was also said that we believe in what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. They described themselves as certain now, hoping for what they asked for of being returned to the world. How can they do that when the word of God has come true upon them? If they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars. It was also said that the meaning of indeed, we are certain is that the doubts that had been plaguing them in the world have been removed from them when they saw and heard what they heard. It is permissible The meaning of we saw and heard is that we became among those who hear and see, so there is no need to estimate an object. It is permissible for it to be a suitable object for us to work, just as it is permissible for it to be an adjective for a deleted source, and the answer to if is deleted: that is, you would have seen a terrible matter and a tremendous terror.
32:13: 13- And if We willed, We could have given every soul its guidance. This is a response to them when they asked to return: that is, if We willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, so We guided all of mankind, and none of them would have disbelieved. An-Nahhas said: There are two sayings regarding the meaning of this: One of them is that it is in this world, and the other is that it is in the Hereafter: meaning, if We willed, We could have returned them to this world, “but the word from Me will come true: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.” The phrase If We willed is understood by a saying that is connected to the understood word before His saying We saw, meaning, And We say, if We willed, and the meaning of but the word from Me will come true is that My judgment and decree have been carried out and My words have preceded, I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together. This is the statement that is required of God and is true upon His servants, and His judgment has been carried out in it. So the implication of this statement is that He does not give every soul its guidance, but rather He decreed this upon them because He, glory be to Him, knew that they were among the people of misery, and that they were among those who choose misguidance over guidance.
32:14: The letter fa in His statement: 14- Then taste for having forgotten the meeting of this Day of yours is to arrange the command to taste after what came before it, and the letter ba in for having forgotten is for causality, and in it is an indication that their punishment is not just because of the previous statement, but because of that and this. There is a difference of opinion about the forgetfulness mentioned here. Some say it is the true forgetfulness, which is when the remembrance disappears. Others say it is abandonment. The meaning according to the first is that they did not work for that day, so they were like those who forget it and do not remember it. According to the second, it is necessary to estimate an addition before the meeting: that is, because of your abandoning what I commanded you, taste the punishment of meeting this day of yours. Al-Mubarrad preferred the second and recited: As if a skewer was coming out of the side of his page, and they forgot to drink from it at Muftah. That is, they abandoned it. Ad-Dahhak and Yahya ibn Salam said the same: Forgetting here means abandonment. Yahya ibn Salam said: The meaning is: Because you abandoned belief in the Resurrection on this Day, We abandoned you from goodness. As-Suddi said the same. Mujahid said: We abandoned you in torment. Muqatil said: When they enter the Fire, the guards will say to them: Taste the torment for what you forgot. Taste is a metaphor for feeling, and from this is the saying of Tufail: So taste as we tasted on the morning of the Hajj, the rage in our hearts and the resentment. His statement, And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do, is repeated for emphasis: that is, taste the eternal punishment that will never cease for what you used to do in this world of disbelief and sins. Al-Razi said in his interpretation: The demonstrative pronoun in His statement, for you have forgotten the meeting of this Day of yours, has three possible interpretations: it may refer to the meeting, it may refer to the Day, or it may refer to the punishment.
32:15: And the sentence 15- Only he who believes in Our verses is a new sentence to explain who deserves guidance to faith, and who does not deserve it. The meaning is: Only those who believe in Our verses and benefit from them are those who, when they are reminded by them, fall down in prostration and no one else who is reminded by them: that is, he is admonished by them but does not remember or believe in them. The meaning of fall down in prostration is that they fell on their faces in prostration in reverence for the verses of God and in fear of His wrath and punishment. And glorify the praises of their Lord that is, they declared Him free from everything that is not befitting of Him, immersed in praise of Him for His blessings, the greatest and most perfect of which is guidance to faith. The meaning is: They said in their al-Sajdah 32:Glory be to God and His praise, or Glory be to my Most High Lord and His praise. Sufyan said: The meaning is to pray in praise of their Lord, and the phrase and they are not arrogant is in the accusative case as a state: that is, in a state of being submissive to God, humbled before Him, not arrogant toward Him.
32:16: 16- "Their sides forsake their beds" meaning they are raised and turned away. It is said: something jafā ‘anhu wa jafāwā ‘anhu: if it does not adhere to it and turns away from it. The plural of mudhājī is the place in which one lies down. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Rummani said: turning away and forsake are towards an upward direction, and likewise it is in forgiving someone who has made a mistake in cursing or the like. The plural of janub is janub, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state: meaning their sides forsake their beds. They are the ones who stay up at night and get up from their beds to pray. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata’ and the majority said the same. What is meant by prayer is the voluntary prayer at night without restriction. Qatadah and Ikrimah said: It is the voluntary prayer between Maghrib and Isha’. It was also said that it is the Isha’ prayer only, and this is a narration from Al-Hasan and Ata’. Ad-Dahhak said: The Isha and Fajr prayers are performed in congregation. It was also said that they are those who stand to remember God, whether in prayer or otherwise. They call upon their Lord in fear and hope. This sentence is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in their sides, so it is a state after a state. It is possible that the first sentence is a new sentence to explain a type of their acts of obedience. The meaning is: Their sides forsake each other while they are calling upon their Lord in fear of His punishment and hope for His mercy. And from what We have provided them they spend. That is, from what We have provided them or from their provision, and that is the obligatory charity. It was also said that it is voluntary charity. The first is to carry it as a generality, and the accusative of in fear and hope is based on the reason. It is possible that it is two nouns accusative with an implied meaning.
32:17: 17- No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort to their eyes. The indefinite noun in the context of negation indicates generality: that is, no soul, of any soul, knows what God the Almighty has hidden for those mentioned above that will comfort their eyes. The majority of scholars read comfort in the singular. Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurairah, and Abu Darda' read from qaraat in the plural. Hamzah read ma akhfa with a sukoon on the ya' as a present tense verb attributed to God the Almighty. The rest read it with a fatha as a past tense passive verb. Ibn Mas'ud read ma nakhfi with a damma on the noon, and Al-A'mash read yakhfi with a damma on the ta'. Al-Zajjaj said about the meaning of Hamzah's reading: that is, from it what God has hidden for them, and it is the reading of Muhammad ibn Ka'b, and ma is in the accusative case.
