Then God Almighty explained that this was because of their righteous deeds, saying: A reward for what they used to do, meaning because of the reward for what they used to do in this world, or they were rewarded for that.
32:18: 18- Is he who is a believer like he who is a sinner? The question is for denial: that is, the believer is not like the sinner, for the difference between them has become clear. For this reason, He said: They are not equal. This is because it further expresses the denial conveyed by the question. Al-Zajjaj said: He made the two a group when He said: They are not equal for the sake of the meaning of who. It was also said that it is because two is the smallest group. The reason for its revelation will be explained at the end of the research.
32:19: Then the Almighty explained the outcome of the two groups, starting with the believers, saying: 19- As for those who have believed and done righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge. The majority of scholars read Gardens in the plural, while Talhah ibn Musarraf read Jannat al-Ma’aim in the singular. Refuge is that to which they will take refuge. He added Gardens to it because it is the true refuge. It was also said that refuge is a garden from the gardens, and this has been discussed previously. The meaning of nuzlan is that it is prepared for them when they descend, and it is basically what is prepared for the one who descends of food and drink, as we explained in Al-Imran. Its accusative is in the state. Abu Haywah read nuzlan with a sukoon on the zay, and the ba’ in bima kana yam’om is for causality: that is, because of what they used to do, or because of their work.
32:20: Then he mentioned the other group and said: 20- And as for those who disobeyed, meaning they went out of obedience to God and rebelled against Him and His messengers, their refuge is the Fire, meaning their home to which they will go and in which they will settle is the Fire. Whenever they wish to leave it, they will be returned to it, meaning if they wish to leave it, they will be returned to it, reluctantly and unwillingly. And it was said that when the flames pushed them to the top of it, they were returned to their places. And it will be said to them, ‘Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.’ And the one who said this to them was the guardians of Hell from the angels, or the one who said it to them was God Almighty, and in this saying to them while they were in the Fire there is an irritation to them that is not hidden.
32:21: 21- And We will make them taste of the lesser punishment, which is the punishment of this world. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ad-Dahhak, and An-Nakha'i said: It is the calamities and ailments of this world, and it was said that it refers to the prescribed punishments, and it was said that it refers to being killed by the sword on the Day of Badr, and it was said that it refers to years of famine in Mecca, and it was said that it refers to the punishment of the grave. There is nothing wrong with applying it to all of them, less than the greater punishment, which is the punishment of the Hereafter, that they may return from their state of polytheism and sins because of the punishment that befalls them, to faith and obedience, and repent for what they were doing. This explanation is evidence of the weakness of the statement of those who say that the lesser punishment is the punishment of the grave.
32:22: 22- And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them? That is, no one is more unjust than him because he heard from the verses of God what necessitates turning to faith and obedience, so turning away was made in place of that, and the use of then is to indicate the exclusion of that, and that it is not something that should be Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals. That is, from the people of crime in general, so it includes those who turn away from the verses of God primarily. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, Indeed, We have forgotten you, that he said: We have abandoned you. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu’ab from him, that he said: This verse was revealed regarding the five daily prayers: Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded by them, fall down in prostration, that is, they come to them, and glorify, that is, they pray at the command of their Lord, and they are not arrogant, about performing the prayer in congregation. Al-Tirmidhi narrated who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Muhammad ibn Nasr in the Book of Prayer, from Anas ibn Malik that this verse, Their sides forsake their beds, was revealed regarding awaiting the prayer called ‘Isha’. Al-Bukhari narrated in his Tarikh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, that he said: It was revealed regarding the ‘Isha’ prayer. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from Ibn Mardawayh regarding the verse: They would not sleep until they prayed ‘Isha’. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from him, that he said: We used to avoid sleeping before the ‘Isha’ prayer. Abd al-Razzaq narrated in al-Musannaf and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him that he said: I never saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sleeping before the Isha’ prayer, nor speaking after it, because this verse was revealed regarding that: Their sides forsake their beds. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Their sides forsake their beds. He said: They are those who do not sleep before the Isha’ prayer, and he praised them. When he mentioned that, a man would keep away from his bed for fear that sleep would overcome him, so he would do that before the young sleep and the old become lazy. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Bala that he said: We used to sit in the mosque and some of the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would pray the Isha’ prayer after the Maghrib prayer, and their sides would forsake their beds. Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated something similar in Zawa’id al-Zuhd, Ibn Adi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Anas, regarding the verse, Their sides forsake their beds, that he said: They used to wait for the time between sunset and night prayers to pray. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, regarding the verse, Their sides forsake their beds, that he said: The servant’s standing at night. Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Nasr in the Book of Prayer, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He mentioned a hadith in which he guided to various types of acts of obedience, and said in it, And the prayer of a man in the depths of the night, then he recited, Their sides forsake their beds. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas, regarding the verse, that he said: Not a night would pass without them taking from it. Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa'id az-Zuhd, on the authority of Abu Abdullah al-Jadali, on the authority of Ubadah bin as-Samit, on the authority of Ka'b, who said: "When the people are gathered, a crier will call out: 'This is the Day of Judgment. Where are those who forsake their beds?'" The hadith. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: "Forsake for the remembrance of God. Whenever they wake up, they remember God, either in prayer, or standing or sitting, or lying on their sides, they do not cease remembering God." Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Muhammad bin Nasr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Throne of God was over the water, then He created a garden for Himself, then He created another beneath it, then He covered them with a single pearl, then He said: And beneath them are two gardens, the creation did not know what was in them. It is this that God said: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes, from which a gift comes to them every day. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: It is written in the Torah: God has prepared for those who forsake their beds that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has ever conceived, and no angel brought near or prophet has ever known. And it is also in the Qur’an: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “On the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), who said: God the Most High said: ‘I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has ever conceived.’” Abu Hurayrah said: “And if you wish, recite: ‘No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes.’” There are hadiths on this topic from a group of the Companions, and they are well-known, so we will not go on mentioning them at length. Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani in Kitab al-Aghani, al-Wahidi, Ibn Adi, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib and Ibn Asakir narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Al-Walid ibn Uqba said to Ali ibn Abi Talib: I have a sharper spear than you, I am more eloquent than you, and I fill the army better than you. Ali said to him: Be quiet, for you are a sinner. Then the verse was revealed: Is he who is a believer like he who is a sinner? They are not equal. He meant Ali as a believer and Al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu’it as a sinner. Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib and Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on his authority regarding the verse. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, al-Suddi and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Mani’, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding his statement: And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment, he said: on the day of Badr. Below the greater punishment, he said: on the Day of Resurrection. Perhaps they will return, he said: Perhaps those who remain among them will repent and return. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud regarding the verse, he said: The lesser punishment is years that befall them, perhaps they will return, he said: They will repent. Muslim, Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa'id Al-Musnad, Abu 'Awanah in his Sahih, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka'b regarding the verse, And We will surely make them taste of the lesser punishment, he said: The calamities of this world, the Romans, the fistfight and the smoke. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: The day of Badr. Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, of the lesser punishment, he said: The prescribed punishments, perhaps they will return, he said: They will repent. Ibn Mani', Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said, with a weak chain of transmission, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There are three things, whoever does them has committed a sin: whoever ties a banner unjustly, or disobeys his parents, or walks with an oppressor to support him, has committed a sin.” God says: Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals. Ibn Kathir said after transmitting it: This is a strange hadith.
32:23: His statement: 23- And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture meaning the Torah so be not O Muhammad in doubt meaning in doubt and suspicion about meeting Him. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was promised that he would meet Moses before he died, then he met him in heaven or in Jerusalem when he was taken on the Night Journey. This is the opinion of Mujahid, Al-Kalbi, and Al-Suddi. It was also said: So do not be in doubt about meeting Moses on the Day of Resurrection, and you will meet him therein. It was also said: So do not be in doubt about Moses meeting the Scripture. This was said by Al-Zajjaj. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, and he was denied and harmed. So do not be in doubt that he will meet you with what he encountered of denial and harm. So the pronoun in meeting Him in this case refers to something omitted, and the meaning is: from meeting what Moses encountered. Al-Nahhas said: This is a strange opinion. It was said that the speech is an estimation and a delay, and the meaning is: Say, The Angel of Death who is assigned to you will take you, so do not be in doubt about meeting him. So it came as an objection between And We gave Moses the Scripture and And made it a guidance for the Children of Israel. And it was said that the pronoun refers to the Scripture, which is the Criterion, like His saying: And indeed, you are receiving the Qur’an. The meaning is: Indeed, We gave Moses the same as We gave you of the Scripture, and We met him with the same revelation as We met you with, so do not be in doubt that you have met the like of it and its equivalent. How far-fetched this is! Perhaps the one who said it was prompted by His saying: And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, because the pronoun refers to the Scripture. It was said that the pronoun in meeting him refers to the return understood from His saying: Then to your Lord you will be returned, meaning do not be in doubt about meeting the return, and this is also far-fetched. There is a difference of opinion regarding the pronoun in His statement, And We made it. Some say it refers to the Book, meaning, We made the Torah a guidance for the Children of Israel. This was said by Al-Hasan and others. Qatada said, It refers to Moses, meaning, We made Moses a guidance for the Children of Israel.
32:24: 24- And We made from among them leaders meaning leaders to be followed in their religion. The Kufians read it as ai’immah. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake according to all grammarians, because it combines two hamzas in one word. The meaning of they guide by Our command is that they call them to guidance by what we convey to them of the rulings of the Torah and its sermons by Our command: meaning by Our command to them to do so, or for the sake of Our command. Qatada said: What is meant by the imams are the prophets among them. It was said by the scholars, When they were patient, the majority read when with a fat-ha on the lam and a shaddah on the meem, meaning, We made them leaders for their patience. Abu Ubaid chose this reading, citing as evidence the reading of Ibn Masoud, when they were patient with a ba’. This patience is their patience in the hardships of the obligation and guidance for the people. It was said that they were patient about the world, and they were certain of Our signs, the revelation, meaning they believed in them and knew that they were true and that they were from God, due to their increased thinking and frequent contemplation.
32:25: 25- Indeed, your Lord will judge between them meaning He will judge between them and rule between the believers and the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ. It was also said that He will judge between the prophets and their nations, as narrated by Al-Naqqash.
32:26: 26- Or was it not shown to them? meaning, or was it not made clear to them? The hamza is for denial, and the subject is what is indicated by How many generations We destroyed before them? meaning, or did we not make clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them? Al-Farra' said: Kam is in the nominative case with byahed. Al-Mubarrad said: The subject is the guidance indicated by byahed: meaning, or was the guidance not shown to them? Al-Zajjaj said: Kam is in the accusative case with byahakna. The majority of scholars read or was not guided with a lower case ending, while As-Salami, Qatadah, and Abu Zaid from Ya'qub read it with a nun, and this reading is clear. An-Nahhas said: There is a problem with the reading with a lower case ending with a ya" because it is said: A verb is not devoid of a subject, so where is the subject of "li-yahed"? The answer to this is that the subject is what we have mentioned previously, and what is meant by the generations are: Aad, Thamud, and the like, and the phrase they walk in their dwellings is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun for them: that is, while the situation is that they walk in the dwellings of the destroyed and see them, and look at what lessons and traces of punishment are in them, and they do not take heed of that. It was said that it refers back to the destroyed, and the meaning is: We destroyed them while they were walking in their dwellings, and the first is more appropriate. Indeed in that mentioned are signs great so will they not hear from them and take heed from them.
32:27: 27- Have they not seen that We drive water to the barren land? That is, do they not know that We drive water to the land that does not grow except by driving water to it? It was said that it is the dry land, and its origin is from jarz which means to cut: that is, the one whose vegetation is cut off due to the lack of water. And that which does not grow at all like the salt marshes is not called jarz because of His saying: And We bring forth thereby crops. It was said that it is the land of Yemen, and it was said that it is the land of Aden. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the thirsty land. Al-Farra' said: It is the land in which there is no vegetation. Al-Asma'i said: It is the land that does not grow anything. Al-Mubarrad said: It is far-fetched that it is the land itself due to the introduction of the definite article. It was said that it is derived from their saying a man who is jarooz: if he does not leave anything except eating it, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: He is a young bird, he cries when he is hungry, he eats dates but does not throw away the pits And also the she-camel of Jaruz: if she eats everything she finds. Mujahid said: It is the land of the Nile, because water comes to it every year. And We bring forth with it meaning with the water crops from which their livestock eat meaning from the crops such as straw, leaves and the like of what people do not eat and themselves meaning they eat the grains that come out of the crops from which they live. The phrase from which their livestock eat is in the accusative case as a state. Do they not see these blessings and thank the Bestower and declare His Oneness because He is the only One who brings that about.
32:28: 28- And they say, ‘When will this conquest be, if you should be truthful?’ Those who say this are the disbelievers in general, or the disbelievers of Mecca in particular: that is, when will be the conquest that you promise us? By conquest they mean judgment and separation between the servants, which is the Day of Resurrection when God will judge between His servants, as stated by Mujahid and others. Al-Farra’ and Al-Qutaybi said: It is the conquest of Mecca. Qatada said: The companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the disbelievers: We have a day when we will enjoy ourselves and rest, and God will judge between us and you, meaning the Day of Resurrection. The disbelievers said: When will be this conquest? Al-Suddi said: It is the Day of Badr, because the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say to the disbelievers: God will support us and make us victorious over you. The word when in his statement, When will this conquest be? is in the nominative case, or in the accusative case as a circumstantial particle.
32:29: Then God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer them, saying: 29- Say, ‘On the Day of Conquest, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved.’ This is evidence that the Day of Conquest is the Day of Resurrection, because the Day of the Conquest of Mecca and the Day of Badr are two of the days on which faith benefits. The people of Mecca converted to Islam on the Day of the Conquest, and before that, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had converted to Islam. The meaning of nor will they be reprieved is that they will not be given respite or delay. Day in the Day of the Conquest is in the accusative case as a circumstantial particle, and Al-Farra’ permitted the nominative case.
32:30: 30- So turn away from them meaning from their foolishness and denial, and do not respond to them except with what you have been commanded to do. And wait, for they are waiting. That is, wait for the Day of Conquest, which is the Day of Resurrection, or the Day of their destruction by killing. They are waiting for you for the events of time, such as death, killing, or victory, as in His statement: Then wait, for we are with you waiting. It is possible that what is meant is that they are waiting for their destruction, and the verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword. It was also said that it was not abrogated, since turning away may occur with the command to fight. Ibn al-Samīf' read innahu muntaṣar with a fatḥah on the ḍāl, in the passive form. This reading was narrated from Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin. al-Farra' said: This is not correct except by implying: that is, they are waiting for them. Abu Hatim said: The correct one is the kasrah: that is, wait for their punishment, for they are waiting for your destruction. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the night of my Night Journey, I saw Moses, son of Imran, a tall, curly-haired man as if he were one of the men of Shanu’ah. I saw Jesus, son of Mary, with a medium build, reddish and white, and a smooth head. I saw Malik, the keeper of Hell, and the Antichrist, with signs that God showed him.” He said: So be in no doubt about meeting him. Qatadah interpreted it as meaning that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had met Moses. And We made him a guidance for the Children of Israel. He said: God made Moses a guidance for the Children of Israel. At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Ad-Diya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated with a chain of transmission. As-Suyuti said: It is authentic on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, So be in no doubt about meeting him. He said: About meeting Moses. It was said: Or did he meet Moses? He said: “Yes. Don’t you see His saying: “And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers?” Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, {Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land?} He said: Barren land is the land that receives nothing but rain that does not benefit it at all except what comes to it from torrents. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement, {to the barren land.} He said: The land of Yemen. Al-Qurtubi said in his commentary: The chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas is sound and there is no objection to it. Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il, who authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, {And they say, When will this conquest be, if you should be truthful?} He said: On the day of Badr, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) conquered, and their faith did not benefit those who disbelieved after death.
33:1: It is seventy-three verses, and it is Medinan Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Ahzab was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Abd Al-Razzaq in Al-Musannaf, At-Tayalisi, Saeed bin Mansour, Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa’id Al-Musnad, Ibn Mani’, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Al-Anbari in Al-Masahif, Ad-Daraqutni in Al-Ifrad, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ad-Diya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Zur, who said: Ubayy bin Ka’b said to me: How do you recite Surat Al-Ahzab or how do you count it? I said: Seventy-three verses. He said: I have seen it and it is equal to Surat Al-Baqarah, or more than Surat Al-Baqarah. We recite in it: “The old man and the old woman, if they commit adultery, stone them both. It is a punishment from God, and God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” So he raised it, among other things. Ibn Kathir said: Its chain of transmission is good. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up, praised and thanked God, and then said: “O people, God sent Muhammad with the truth and revealed to him the Book. Among the things that were revealed to him was the verse of stoning. We recited it and memorized it: ‘If an old man or an old woman commits adultery, stone them both.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stoned, and we stoned after him. I fear that a long time may pass before the people say, ‘We do not find the verse of stoning in God’s Book,’ and they will go astray by abandoning an obligation that God had revealed.” Similar to this has been narrated from him through various chains of narration. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah that Umar ibn al-Khattab said to me, How many verses do you count in Surat al-Ahsaab? I said, Seventy-two or seventy-three. He said, It is close to the number of verses in Surat al-Baqarah, and it contains the verse of stoning. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history that he said: “I recited Surat al-Ahzab to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and I forgot seventy verses of it that I did not find.” Abu Ubaid, in Al-Fada’il, Ibn Al-Anbari, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: Surat Al-Ahzab was recited in the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as two hundred verses. When Uthman wrote the copies of the Qur’an, he did not confirm any of it except what it is now. His statement: 1- O Prophet, fear God meaning continue in that and increase it and do not obey the disbelievers from the people of Mecca and those who are on the same disbelief as them and the hypocrites meaning those who outwardly show Islam but inwardly disbelieve. Al-Wahidi said: What God, the Almighty, meant by the disbelievers were Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah, and Abu Al-A’war Al-Sulami. This is because they said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Refuse to mention our gods, and say that they have the power of intercession for those who worship them. He said: And the hypocrites were Abdullah bin Ubayy and Abdullah bin Sa’d bin Abi Sarh. The reason for the revelation of the verse Indeed, God is All-Knowing, All-Wise will come at the end of the research, meaning He is All-Knowing and All-Wise, meaning He is All-Knowing and All-Wise. An-Nahhas said: “And by His saying, ‘Indeed, God is All-Knowing and All-Wise,’ He indicated that He was inclined towards them, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in order to call them to Islam. The meaning is that if God Almighty had known that there would be benefit in your inclination towards them, He would not have forbidden you from them, because He is All-Wise. The distance of this alleged evidence is not hidden, but this sentence is an explanation for the sentence of the command to piety and the prohibition against obeying the disbelievers and hypocrites. The meaning is that He does not command you or forbid you except with what He knows is good or bad, due to the abundance of His knowledge and the breadth of His wisdom.”
33:2: 2- And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord from the Qur’an: meaning follow the revelation in all your affairs and do not follow anything other than it from the advice of the disbelievers and hypocrites, nor from pure opinion, for in what has been revealed to you there is enough for you to do so. The phrase Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Knowing is a justification for his command to follow what has been revealed to you, and the command to him, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is a command to his nation, so they are commanded to follow the Qur’an as he is commanded to follow it. That is why he came addressing him and them in his statement: with what you do according to the reading of the majority with the superior letter of the address, and this reading was chosen by Abu Ubaidah and Abu Hatim. Abu Amr, As-Salami and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with the subjunctive letter.
33:3: 3- And put your trust in God, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs. That is, depend on Him and entrust your affairs to Him, and He is sufficient as a protector who protects those who put their trust in Him.
33:4: Then the Almighty mentioned an example to prepare and pave the way for what follows it of the Qur’anic rulings that are from the revelation that God commanded him to follow, saying: 4- God has not made for any man two hearts within him. There is disagreement about the reason for the revelation of this verse, as will be mentioned. It was said that it is a parable that God gave for the liar: just as a man cannot have two hearts, so the wife of the liar cannot be his mother so that he can be protected, and likewise an adopted son cannot be the son of two men. It was also said that one of the hypocrites would say: I have a heart that commands me to do such and such and a heart to do such and such. So the verse was revealed to refute hypocrisy and to clarify that it cannot coexist with Islam, just as two hearts cannot coexist. The heart is a small piece in the shape of a pine tree, created by God and made it a place of knowledge. And He has not made your wives of whom you declare yourselves to be your mothers. The Kufians and Ibn Amir read al-la’i with a silent ya’ after a hamza. Abu Amr and al-Bazzi read it with a silent ya’ after a pure alif. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: It is the language of the Quraysh that people were commanded to recite. Qanbal and Warsh read it with a broken hamza without a ya’. Asim read Tathaaroon with a damma on the first letter and a kasra on the ha' after an alif, present tense verb. Ibn Amir read it with a fatha on the first letter and the ha' and a shaddah on the dhad, present tense verb Tathaaroon. The original is Tathaaroon, while the rest read it with a fatha on the first letter without the dhad and without an alif, and the original is Tathaaroon. Zihar is derived from back, and its origin is that a man says to his wife: You are to me like the back of my mother, and the meaning is: And God has not made your women, to whom you say this, like your mothers in prohibition, but it is a reprehensible and false statement. And likewise He has not made the pretenders whom you claim are your sons your sons, and the pretenders are the plural of dai, which is the one who claims a son for someone other than his father. Discussion of Zihar will come in Surat Al-Mujadilah, and the reference in his saying: That is to what came before from mentioning Zihar and claiming, and it is a subject and its predicate is your saying with your mouths meaning that it is nothing but a mere saying with the mouths and has no effect, so the woman does not become a mother because of it nor does the son of someone else become a son because of it, and nothing results from that. Of the rulings on motherhood and sonship. It was said that the reference is to the claim: that is, your claim that the children of others are your children has no basis in truth, but is merely a verbal statement And God speaks the truth which must be followed because it is true in itself and not falsehood. So the supplication of children for their fathers falls under this And He guides to the way meaning He points out the path that leads to the truth. In this there is guidance for the servants to speak the truth and abandon falsehood and lies.
33:5: Then the Almighty stated what is obligatory for the servants of God to call their children after their fathers, saying: 5- Call them by their fathers by bloodline and trace their lineage back to them and do not call them by anyone else. The phrase it is more just in the sight of God is an explanation for the command to call children after their fathers. The pronoun refers to the source of call them. The meaning of more just is more just: that is, more just than any statement related to that. So the addition was left for the sake of generality, like saying God is Great. The complement to it may be understood as specific: that is, more just than saying he is the son of so-and-so when he is not his son by bloodline. Then the Almighty completed the guidance for the servants of God, saying: But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients. That is, they are your brothers in religion and they are your clients, so say: my brother and my client, and do not say the son of so-and-so, since you do not know their fathers in a true sense. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for your clients to be your clients in religion. It was said that the meaning is: If they were freed but not free, then say, the clients of so-and-so. “And there is no blame upon you for that in which you erred,” meaning there is no sin upon you for what you did by mistake, unintentionally, but the sin is in what your hearts intended, which is what you said intentionally by attributing children to other than their fathers, knowing that. Qatada said: If you called a man by a name other than his father, and you believed that he was his father, there would be no blame upon you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, He forgives the one who makes a mistake, has mercy on him, and overlooks him, or is Forgiving of sins, Merciful to His servants. Among those whom He forgives and has mercy upon is the one who calls a man by a name other than his father by mistake. Or before the prohibition of that.
33:6: Then God, the Almighty, mentioned to His Messenger a great advantage and a sublime distinction that no other servant shares with him, saying: 6- The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves. That is, he is more entitled to them in all matters of religion and life, and is closer to them than they are to themselves, let alone being closer to them than anyone else. Therefore, it is obligatory for them to give him priority in whatever he wants from their wealth, even if they are in need of it. It is obligatory for them to love him more than they love themselves, and it is obligatory for them to give precedence to his judgment over their judgment for themselves. In short, if the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, calls them to something and their souls call them to something else, it is obligatory for them to give precedence to what he called them to and postpone what their souls call them to. It is obligatory for them to obey him more than they obey themselves, and to give precedence to his obedience over what their souls incline toward and what their desires demand. It is said that what is meant by themselves in this verse is some of them, so the meaning is that the Prophet is closer to the believers than some of them to others. It is also said that it is specific to judgment, meaning that he is closer to them than they are to themselves in what he judges between them. It was said that they are more deserving of jihad before him and sacrificing their lives for him, and the first is more deserving. And his wives are their mothers, meaning like their mothers in the ruling of prohibition and the status of their status in deserving of respect. It is not permissible for anyone to marry one of them, just as it is not permissible for him to marry his mother. This motherhood is specific to the prohibition of marriage for them and to the respect due to their position. The specification of the believers indicates that they are not the mothers of the women of the believers, nor are their daughters the sisters of the believers, nor are their brothers the maternal uncles of the believers. Al-Qurtubi said: What appears to me is that they are the mothers of men and women, out of necessity to magnify their right over men and women. He said: Then in the Mushaf of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and his wives are their mothers, and he is their father. Ibn Abbas read: He is closer to the believers than they are to themselves, and he is a father, and his wives are their mothers. Then God, the Exalted, made it clear that kinship is closer to one another, saying: And those of kinship are closer to one another. What is meant by those of kinship is kinship: that is, they are more entitled to inheritance from one another. The interpretation of this verse was presented at the end of Surat al-Anfal, and it abrogates what was in the early days of Islam regarding inheritance by migration and loyalty. Qatadah said: When God, the Exalted, said in Surat al-Anfal 8:And those who believed but did not emigrate - you have no right to them as allies until they emigrate, the Muslims inherited from one another by migration, then this was abrogated by this verse. And others said the same. It was said that this verse abrogates inheritance by oath and brotherhood in religion. In the Book of God may be related to the comparative adjective in His statement: more worthy of one another because it works in the circumstance. It may be related to something omitted which is a state of the pronoun: that is, existing in the Book of God. What is meant by the Book is the Preserved Tablet or the Qur’an or the verse of inheritance. His statement: Of the believers may be an explanation of those with kinship ties, meaning that those with kinship ties among the believers and the emigrants are more worthy of one another. It... related to those with kinship ties, meaning that those with kinship ties among the believers and the emigrants are more worthy of one another. It may be related to those with kinship ties, meaning that those with kinship ties among the believers and the emigrants who are strangers. It was said that the meaning of the verse: And those with kinship ties are more worthy of one another is not that it is permissible for the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be like mothers in the prohibition of marriage. There is a weakness in this that is not hidden. Unless you do good to your relatives. This exception is either connected to the generality of the general, The interpretation is: And those of kinship are closer to one another in everything of inheritance and other things, except that you do to your relatives a good deed such as charity or a will, for that is permissible. This was stated by Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Ata’ and Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah. Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah said: It was revealed regarding the permission of making a will for a Jew or a Christian. The unbeliever is a guardian in lineage but not in religion, so making a will for him is permissible, and it is permissible for it to be temporary. The meaning is: But doing good to relatives is permissible. The meaning of the verse is that when God the Almighty abrogated inheritance by oath and migration, He permitted making a will to them. Mujahid said: What is meant by good is supporting and preserving the sanctity by virtue of faith and migration. The reference in His saying: That was is to what was mentioned above: that is, the abrogation of inheritance by migration, alliance and contract, and its return to the relatives from among the relatives was written in the Book meaning in the Preserved Tablet, or written in the Quran. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Ad-Diya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: One day the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up to pray and a thought occurred to him. The hypocrites who were praying with him said: Don’t you see that he has two hearts, one with you and one with them? Then this verse was revealed: God has not made for any man two hearts in his chest. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority through another chain of transmission with the wording: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a prayer and forgot during it, and a word occurred to him and the hypocrites heard it and said: He has two hearts. So this verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: There was a man from Quraysh who was called ‘the two-hearted’ because of his cunning, so God revealed this verse about him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that Zayd ibn Haritha, the freed slave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), “We never used to call him anything but Zayd ibn Muhammad until the verse was revealed: ‘Call them by the names of their fathers’…’ Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You are Zayd ibn Haritha ibn Sharaheel.” Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There is no believer but that I am closer to him in this world and the Hereafter. Read, if you wish, ‘The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves.’ So any believer who leaves behind wealth, let his relatives inherit it. But if he leaves behind debt or property, let him come to me, for I am his protector.” Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith from Jabir. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad and al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Buraydah that he said: “I went on a military expedition with ‘Ali to Yemen and I saw some coldness in him. When I came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I mentioned ‘Ali and disparaged him. I saw the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) change, and he said: ‘O Buraydah, am I not closer to the believers than they are to themselves?’ I said: ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Whoever I am the protector of, then ‘Ali is his protector.’” It has been proven in Sahih that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, none of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his own self, his wealth, his children and all of mankind. Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Aisha that a woman said to her: O mother! She said: I am the mother of your men, not the mother of your women. Ibn Sa'd narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah who said: I am the mother of your men and women. Abd Al-Razzaq, Sa'id bin Mansour, Ishaq bin Rahawayh, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Dalail narrated on the authority of Bajalah who said: “Umar bin Al-Khattab passed by a boy who was reciting the Qur’an: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them. He said: Boy, scratch it. He said: This is my father’s Qur’an. He went to him and asked him. He said: “The Qur’an distracted me, and bargaining in the markets distracted you.” Al-Firyabi, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and he is a father to them, and his wives are their mothers.”
33:7: His statement: 7- And when We took from the prophets their covenant The agent in the circumstance is omitted: meaning, remember, as if he said: O Prophet, fear God and remember that God took a covenant from the prophets. Qatada said: God took a covenant from the prophets specifically that they would believe in one another and follow one another. Muqatil said: He took a covenant from them that they would worship God, call to the worship of God, believe in one another, and advise their people. The covenant is the oath, and it was said that it is the acknowledgment of God, but the first is more appropriate, and its investigation has been mentioned previously. Then the Almighty singled out some of the prophets for mention after making a comprehensive generalization for them and others, saying: And from you, and from Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary. The reason for singling them out for mention is to inform them that they have more honor and merit because they are among the bearers of the well-known religious laws and among the messengers of resolve. The mention of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, first, despite his later time, is a way of honoring and glorifying him that is not hidden. Al-Zajjaj said: And the covenant was taken when they were extracted from the loins of Adam like atoms. Then He confirmed the covenant He took from the prophets by repeatedly mentioning it and describing it as being firm, saying: And We took from them a firm covenant, meaning a strong pledge to fulfill what they were charged with and what God took from them. It is possible that God took the covenant from them twice, so He took from them the first time just a covenant without making it more severe or harsh, then He took it from them a second time, more severe and harsh. Similar to this verse is His saying: “And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘Whatever I have given you of the Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall believe in him and support him.’”
33:8: The lam in His statement: 8- So that He may question the truthful about their truthfulness may be the lam of ki: meaning so that He may question the truthful among the prophets about their truthfulness in conveying the message to their people, and in this there is a warning to others, because if they are asked about that, then how would others? And it was said that He may question the prophets about what their people answered them, as in His statement: Then We will surely question those to whom messages were sent, and We will surely question the messengers. And it is permissible for it to be connected to something omitted: meaning He did that in order to ask, And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment in apposition to what is indicated by In order that He may question the truthful, since the meaning is: He rewarded the truthful and prepared for the disbelievers. And it is permissible for it to be in apposition to Our taking, because the meaning is: He emphasized on the prophets the call to His religion in order to reward the believers and prepared for the disbelievers. It was said that what was proven in the first was deleted from the second, and what was proven in the second from the first, and the meaning is: To ask the truthful about their truthfulness, so He rewarded them, and to ask the disbelievers about what they answered their messengers, and He has prepared for them a painful punishment. It was said that it is conjoined with the understood, acting on To ask, as we mentioned, and it is possible that the speech was completed when He said: To ask the truthful about their truthfulness, and the phrase And He prepared for them is a new sentence to explain what He has prepared for the disbelievers.
33:9: 9- O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you. This is a fulfillment of what was previously commanded to fear God so that there is no fear of anyone with it. His saying upon you is related to the favor if it is a source or to an omitted word that is a state: that is, it is upon you. The meaning of when there came to you soldiers is when there came to you soldiers, which is a circumstance of the favor, or to the understood working in upon you, or to an omitted word which is remember. What is meant by the soldiers are the soldiers of the parties who formed parties against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and invaded Medina. It is the invasion called the Battle of the Trench, and they are: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb from Quraysh and those with him from the thousands, and Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari and those with him from his people Ghatafan, Banu Qurayzah, and Banu al-Nadir. They oppressed the Muslims severely as God the Almighty described in these verses. This invasion took place in Shawwal of the year five after the Hijra. This was said by Ibn Ishaq. Ibn Wahb and Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik: It was in the year four. The biographers have elaborated on this incident in what is well known, so we will not prolong the discussion. So We sent upon them a wind is in apposition to came to you. Mujahid said: It is the north wind, sent upon the Confederates on the Day of the Trench until it overturned their pots and tore down their tents. This is indicated by what was proven from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said: I was aided by the north wind, and the ‘Ad were destroyed by the west wind. What is meant by his saying: and hosts you did not see is the angels. The commentators said: God sent angels against them, so they pulled out the pegs, cut the tent ropes, extinguished the fires, overturned the pots, and the horses lashed out at each other. God sent terror upon them, and the angels’ takbir increased in the sides of the army until the leader of each people would say to his al-Nas 114:O sons of so-and-so, come to me. And when they gathered together, he would say to them: Escape, escape. And God is Seeing of what you do. The majority read you do with the upper vowel: meaning, what you do, O Muslims, of arranging the war, digging the trench, seeking His aid, and putting your trust in Him. Abu Amr read it with the lower vowel: meaning, what the disbelievers do of stubbornness against God and His Messenger, and forming parties against the Muslims and gathering against them from every side.
33:10: 10- When they came to you from above you This idh and what follows it are a substitute for the first idh, and the agent in this is the agent in that, and it was said that it is accusative with an omitted word, which is remember. The meaning of from above you is from the top of the valley, which is from the direction of the east, and those who came from this direction are Ghatafan and their master Uyaynah ibn Husayn, and Hawazin and their master Awf ibn Malik, and the people of Najd and their master Tulaiha ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadi, and Awf ibn Malik and Banu al-Nadir joined them, and the meaning of and from below you is from the bottom of the valley from the direction of the west from the direction of Mecca, and they are Quraysh and those with them from the Abyssinians, and their master is Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Abu al-A’war al-Sulami came with Huyayy ibn Akhtab the Jew among the Jews of Banu Qurayza from the direction of the Trench, and with them was Amir ibn al-Tufayl, and the phrase and when the eyes turned away is connected to what preceded it: that is, they turned away from everything and did not look Except towards her enemy coming from every side. It was said that she stared in amazement from the extreme terror and confusion. And the hearts reached the throats - the plural of hanjarah, which is the hollow of the throat. That is, the hearts rose from their place, and reached from the terror and fear to the throats. Had the throat not become too narrow for them, which ends at the throat, they would have come out. This is what Qatada said. It was said that it is in the manner of exaggeration known in all Arabs, even if the hearts did not rise to that place nor move from their place, but it is an example of their disturbance and their estrangement. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is that they were cowardly and most of them were alarmed. The path of the coward when his fear is intense is that his lungs swell. When the lungs swell, the heart rises to the throat. That is why it is said of the coward: his magic swelled. And you think about God various thoughts - that is, different thoughts. Some of them thought of victory and hoped for triumph, and some of them thought otherwise. Al-Hasan said: The hypocrites thought that Muhammad and his companions would be eradicated, and the believers thought that he would be victorious. It has been said that the verse is addressed to hypocrites, but the first view is that of Al-Hasan. Thus, the address is to anyone who outwardly professes Islam, rather than to someone who is a true believer or a hypocrite. The reciters differed regarding this alif in al-Zununa: Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, and Abu Bakr confirmed it in both connected and paused readings. This reading was narrated from Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i. They held to the omission of the Uthmanic codex and all copies of the Qur'an in all countries, as the alif is fixed in all of them. Abu 'Ubaydah chose this reading, except that he said: The reciter should not insert the recitation after them, but rather stop at them. They also held to what is in Arabic poetry of this kind. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, al-Jahdary, and Ya'qub recited by deleting it in both connected and paused readings. They said: It is from the additions in writing, so it was written thus, and it should not be pronounced. As for poetry, what is not permissible in other poetry is permissible in it due to necessity. Ibn Kathir, Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Muhaisin recited it with it in the pause and omitted it in the connection. This reading is the most likely in light of the Arabic language. This alif is what grammarians call the alif of generalization, and the discussion of it is well-known in the science of grammar. Thus, the reciters differed regarding the alif in His statement the messenger and the way, as will come at the end of this surah.
33:11: 11- There the believers were tested. The adverbial phrase is in the accusative case because of the verb that follows it. It was also said that it is you think, but Ibn Atiyyah considered it weak. It is an adverbial phrase of place, used for a distant place there, just as it is used for a nearby place here, or for a medium-sized place there. It may also be an adverbial phrase of time, meaning that at that time the believers were tested. From this, the poet said: And if things get worse and worse, then they will admit where the alarm is. That is, at that time, and the meaning is: that in that place or time the believers were tested with fear, fighting, hunger, siege and combat to distinguish the believer from the hypocrite. And they were shaken with a severe shaking. The majority of scholars read Zalzalu with a damma on the first zay and a kasra on the second, as is the norm in the passive voice. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr that he read it with a kasra on the first zay, and Al-Zamakhshari narrated on his authority that he read it with a kasra on the ishmām. The majority of scholars read Zalzalan with a kasra on the first zay, and Asim, Al-Jahdary and Isa bin Omar read it with a fatha. Al-Zajjaj said: Every verbal noun of the doubled form fa’lāl allows for kasra or fatha, such as qalqaltu qalqālān and zalzalu zalzālan, and the kasra is better. Ibn Salam said: the meaning of zalzalu is: they were moved with fear with a severe movement. Ad-Dahhak said: it is their removal from their places until they had nothing but the place of the trench. It was also said that the meaning is that they were shaken in varying degrees, some of them were shaken in themselves, and some of them were shaken in their religion.
33:12: 12- And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said is connected to when the eyes turned away. Disease in the hearts is doubt and suspicion. What is meant by the hypocrites is Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions, and what is meant by those in whose hearts is disease are the people of doubt and confusion. God and His Messenger have promised us nothing of victory and triumph except delusion, meaning falsehood in speech. The ones who said this statement were about seventy men of hypocrisy and doubt. This statement attributed to them is like an explanation of the aforementioned suspicions: that is, the suspicion of these people was this suspicion, just as the believers suspected victory and the elevation of the word of God.
33:13: 13- And when a party of them said meaning of the hypocrites. Muqatil said: They are Banu Salim of the hypocrites. Al-Suddi said: They are Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions. It was also said: They are Aws bin Qibti and his companions. The word party refers to one person or more. The statement made by this group is: O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you to stay meaning there is no place for you to reside, or there is no residence for you here in the army. Abu Ubaid said: Yathrib is the name of the land, and the city of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is in a part of it. Al-Suhayli said: It was named Yathrib because the one who settled there from the Amalekites was called Yathrib bin Ameel. The majority of scholars read You have no place to stay with a fat-ha on the meem, while Hafs, As-Sulami, Al-Jahdary and Abu Haywah read it with a damma, as it is a verbal noun from the root word aqama to establish oneself. According to the first reading, it is a place name. Farja’u return, meaning to your homes. They were ordered to flee from the army of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This was because the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims went out in the year of the Trench until they turned their backs to Sala’ and the trench was between them and the people. These hypocrites said: There is no place to stay here, and they ordered the people to return to their homes in Madinah. And a party of them will ask permission of the Prophet is in apposition to A party of them said, meaning they will ask permission to return to their homes, and they are Banu Haritha and Banu Salamah. The phrase they say is a substitute for he asks permission, or a condition, or a new chapter in response to an implied question. The statement that they said, which is their statement: Our homes are vulnerable, means lost and unsafe, not fortified or immune from the enemy. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said that the place is vulnerable, meaning it is vulnerable, and houses are vulnerable and vulnerable, and it is a verbal noun. Mujahid, Muqatil, and Al-Hasan said: They said our houses are lost and we fear thieves for them. Qatada said: They said our houses are near the enemy and we do not feel safe for our families. Al-Harawi said: Every place that is not forbidden or covered is vulnerable. In origin, vulnerability means a defect, so it was applied to the disturbed, and what is meant is: one with vulnerability. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Abu Raja Al-Attardi read it as ‘urwah with a kasra on the waw, meaning short walls. Al-Jawhari said: Vulnerability is every situation that is feared in a border or war. An-Nahhas said: It is said that a place is one-eyed if a defect is evident in it, and that a knight is one-eyed if the place of the defect is evident from him. Then the Almighty responded to them by saying: And it is not a defect, so God the Almighty denied them in what they said, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state. Then He explained the reason for their asking permission and what they wanted from him, saying: They want nothing but flight, meaning they want nothing but to flee from the fighting. It was said that what is meant is: they want nothing but to flee from the religion.
33:14: 14- And if it had entered upon them from its regions meaning their homes or the city. Regions are the directions, the plural of country, which is the side and the region. The meaning is: If it had entered upon them from all its regions, not from some of them, this severe calamity would have befallen them, their homes would have been violated, and their sanctity and homes would have been violated. Then they were asked for the trial from another side when this severe calamity befell them. They would have come to it meaning they would have resorted to it or given it. The meaning of trial here is either fighting for tribalism, as Ad-Dahhak said, or associating partners with God and returning to the disbelief that they conceal and show the opposite of, as Al-Hasan said. The majority read they would have come to it with a long vowel, meaning they would have given it from themselves. Nafi’ and Ibn Kathir read it with a short vowel, meaning they would have sought it. And they would not have stayed there except a little while meaning in the city after the trial had come, except a little while until they were destroyed. This is what Al-Hasan, As-Suddi, Al-Farra’ and Al-Qutaybi said. Most of the commentators said: The meaning is: They were not held back from the temptation of polytheism except for a short time, rather they were hastening towards it, desiring it, and they did not stop except as soon as they were asked, and they did not make excuses for answering the Messenger by saying that their houses were in this state of disgrace, even though they had become disgraceful in reality, just as they made excuses for answering the Messenger and fighting with him by saying that they were disgraceful, even though they were not disgraceful at that time.
33:15: Then the Almighty narrated about them what had happened from them before of the covenant with God and His Messenger to remain steadfast in war and not flee from it, so He said: 15- And they had already made a covenant with God before that they would not turn their backs meaning before the Battle of the Trench and after Badr. Qatada said: This is because they were absent from Badr and saw what God had given the people of Badr of honor and victory, so they said: If God makes us witness to a fight, we will fight, and they were Banu Haritha and Banu Salamah. And the covenant with God is to be questioned about meaning one is responsible for it, and its owner is required to fulfill it, and one is rewarded for not fulfilling it.
33:16: 16- Say, 'Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing.' For whoever's time has come to die or be killed, whether he flees or does not flee. And then you will not enjoy yourself except for a little. That is, a little enjoyment or a short time after they flee until their time limits expire, and everything that is coming is near. The majority read You will enjoy yourself with the superlative, and Ya'qub Al-Hadrami read it in Al-Saji's narration from him with the sublative. In some narrations, do not enjoy yourself by deleting the nun, applying permission, and according to the reading of the majority, it is cancelled.
33:17: 17- Say, ‘Who is it that can protect you from God if He intends for you evil?’ That is, destruction, or a decrease in wealth, drought, or disease, or intends for you mercy, that He may have mercy on you with fertility, victory, and well-being. And they will not find for themselves besides God a protector or a helper, who will support them and defend them, or a helper, who will protect them from God’s punishment. Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Abu Maryam Al-Ghassani that a Bedouin said: O Messenger of God, what was the first thing in your prophethood? He said: God took a covenant from me as He took a covenant from the prophets. Then he recited: {And when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary, and We took from them a firm covenant} and the supplication of Abraham: {And send among them a messenger from themselves}, and the good report of Jesus, the son of Mary. The mother of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) saw in a dream that a lamp emerged from between her legs that illuminated the palaces of Ash-Sham. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was said: O Messenger of God, when did you take your covenant? He said: While Adam was between the soul and the body. Al-Bazzar, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, and Abu Nu'aym in Al-Dala'il narrated on his authority: It was said: O Messenger of God, when were you a prophet? He said: While Adam was between the soul and the body.} There are hadiths on this topic, some of which have been authenticated. Al-Hasan bin Sufyan, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Dala’il, Al-Daylami and Ibn `Asakir narrated on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the statement of God, And when We took from the prophets their covenant (10:11), he said: You were the first of the prophets in creation and the last of them in resurrection, so He began with him before them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Their covenant is their promise. `Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and At-Tabarani narrated with a saheeh chain of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when We took from the prophets their covenant (10:11), he said: God only took the covenant of the prophets from their people. Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym, and Al-Bayhaqi, both of them in Al-Dala’il, and Ibn `Asakir, through various chains of transmission, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: “I saw us on the Night of the Confederates, sitting in rows, with Abu Sufyan and those of the Confederates with him above us, and the Qurayzah Jews below us. We feared them for our children. There has never been a night more dark or more foul-smelling than us, with sounds of its wind like thunderbolts, and it was so dark that none of us could see his finger. So the hypocrites began to ask permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said, ‘Our houses are exposed, but they are not exposed.’ None of them asked permission except that he gave him permission. They would sneak away, and we were three hundred, or that was us, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met us, man by man, until he passed me, and I had no protection from the enemy or from the cold except a cloak for my wife that did not go beyond my knees. He came to me while I was kneeling on my knees and said, ‘Who is this?’ I said, ‘Hudhayfah.’ Hudhayfah said, ‘So I lowered myself to the ground and said, ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’” He said: I hated to get up. He said: Get up. So I got up. He said: There is report among the people, so bring me report of the people. He said: I am the most frightened of the people and the most anxious. So I went out and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, protect him from before him and behind him and from his right and from his left and from above him and from below him. He said: By God, God did not create fear or anxiety in my stomach except that it came out of my stomach, and I did not feel anything of it. So when I turned away, he said: O Hudhayfah, do not tell anything about the people until you come to me. So I went out and when I approached the camp of the people, I looked into the light of their fire being lit, and there was a huge, dark man pointing with his hand at the fire and moving his side and saying: Departure, departure. Then I entered the camp, and the people closest to me were Banu Amir, saying: O family of Amir, departure, departure, you have no place to stay. And the wind was in their camp, not going beyond a handspan. By God, I could hear the sound of stones in their tents and their mattresses, the wind hitting them. Then I went out towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when I was halfway there on the road, when I saw about twenty horsemen wearing turban. They said, Tell your companion that God has sufficed him against the people. So I went back to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him. He was wrapped in a cloak praying, and whenever something worried him, he would pray. So I told him about the people, that I had left them to depart, and God revealed, O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when there came to you armies (al-Madinah 4:17). Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, when there came to you armies, that he said: The day of Abu Sufyan was the day of the Confederates. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim in Al-Kuna, Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu`aym in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “When the Night of the Confederates came, the north came to the south and said: ‘Go and support God and His Messenger.’ The south said: ‘A free woman does not travel at night.’ So God became angry with her and made her barren. He sent upon them a north wind, which extinguished their fires and cut their ropes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘I was aided by the north wind, and ‘Ad was destroyed by the west wind.’ This is what God said in the verse: ‘So We sent upon them a wind and soldiers you did not see.’” Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I was aided by the north wind, and ‘Ad was destroyed by the west wind. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Aisha, regarding God’s statement: ‘When they came upon you from above you…’ that she said: That was on the Day of the Trench. There are hadiths on this topic describing this battle and what happened in it, and they are included in the books of battles and biographies. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I have been commanded to create a town that will eat all towns. They call it Yathrib, but it is Madinah. It drives away harm as the bellows drive away the impurities from iron.” Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever calls Madinah Yathrib, let him seek forgiveness from God. It is Taybah, it is Taybah, it is Taybah.” Ahmad’s wording is: It is Taybah. But its chain of transmission is weak. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, regarding the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): And a party of them will ask permission of the Prophet, that they are Banu Haritha. They said: Our houses are exposed, meaning they are uninhabited and we fear theft. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Jabir. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The interpretation of this verse came at the beginning of sixty years, And if it had entered upon them from its regions and they were asked for the trial, they would have come to it. He said: They would have been given it, meaning the entry of the Banu Haritha, the people of Ash-Sham, into Medina.
33:18: His saying: 18- God knows those among you who hinder him. It is said that He hindered him, set him free, and obstructed him: if He diverted him from the path he wanted. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: These were a group of hypocrites who were discouraging the supporters of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they said to them: Muhammad and his companions are nothing but a morsel of food, and if they were meat, Abu Sufyan and his party would have devoured them, so leave them and come to us. It was said that the one who said this was the Jews who said to their brothers from al-Munafiqun 63:Come to us. The meaning of come is to approach and attend. The people of Hijaz use the same word for singular and plural, masculine and feminine, while other Arabs say: come for a singular masculine, come for a feminine, come for two, and come for a group. This has been discussed in Surat Al-An’am. And they do not come to battle meaning war except a little for fear of death. It was said that the meaning is: they do not attend the battle except for show and reputation without expectation.
33:19: 19- Stingy with you meaning miserly with you, they do not help you in digging the trench or in spending in the way of God, as stated by Mujahid and Qatadah. It was also said that they are stingy with fighting with you, and it was also said with spending on your poor and needy, and it was also said that they are stingy with the spoils if they acquire them. As-Suddi said. Its accusative is in the state of the agent of they come, or of the hindering ones. Al-Farra' said: There are four possible ways for its accusative: one of them is the accusative of blame, and one of them is by estimating an omitted verb: meaning they come to him stingy. Al-Nahhas said: It is not permissible for the agent to be for the disabled or the speakers, lest there be a difference between the relative clause and the relative pronoun. So when fear comes, you will see them looking at you, their eyes rolling that is, rolling right and left, and this is the way of the coward when he sees what he fears. Like one who faints from death that is, like the eye of one who faints from death, and he is the one upon whom death has descended and its causes have overwhelmed him, so he is astounded and his mind is lost and his sight is fixed and he does not blink. Likewise, the sight of these people is fixed because of the fear that befalls them. And it is said of the dead when his sight is fixed: his eyes rolled, and the eyebrows of his eyes rolled. The kaf is an adjective for a deleted source. So when the fear is gone, they slap you with sharp tongues it is said that someone slapped someone with his tongue: if he spoke harshly to him openly. Al-Farra’ said: That is, they hurt you by speaking about security with sharp, sharp tongues. And it is said: a slapped orator orator if he is eloquent. From this is the saying of Al-A’sha: They have glory, generosity, and help, and they have the right suitor. Al-Qatibi said: The meaning is that they hurt you with harsh words, and salq means harm, and from this is the poet’s saying: I climbed the Hawazin Bani Ahl until we bent down Qatada said: The meaning of the verse is: They stretched out their tongues against you at the time of dividing the spoils, saying: Give us, for we have testified with you. So, at the time of the spoils, the most miserly and most outspoken people are, and at the time of battle, they are the most cowardly and fearful people. An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement. The accusative of ash-shah-ala al-khair is a circumstantial case of the subject of salaqukum, and it is permissible for it to be accusative as a criticism. Ibn Abi Ubla read it with the nominative case of ash-shah, and what is meant here is that they are miserly with the spoils and quarrel with the Muslims at the division, as Yahya ibn Salam said. It was said that they spend their money in the way of God, as al-Suddi said. It could be said that its meaning is: They do not do good without being restricted to any type of it, and the reference in His statement: those is to those described with those attributes. They did not believe with pure faith, rather they are hypocrites: they show faith but conceal disbelief. So God rendered their deeds worthless means He invalidated them, meaning He revealed their invalidity, because they did not have deeds that warranted reward until God invalidated them. Muqatil said: Their jihad was invalidated because it was not based on faith. And that was easy for God. That is, the nullification of their deeds, or their hypocrisy, was easy for God.
33:20: 20- They think that the confederates have not gone away meaning that these hypocrites, due to their cowardice, think that the confederates are remaining in their camp and have not gone home, because of the evil and terror that has befallen them. But if the confederates should come again after this time, they would wish that they were in the desert among the bedouins meaning that they wish that they were in the desert of the bedouins because of the terror that has befallen them. The deserter is the opposite of the one who is present. It is said: he went out to the desert, asking about your report meaning about your report and what has happened to you, each one coming to them from your direction, or some of them asking each other about the report that has reached him from the report of the confederates and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Meaning: They wish they were far away from you, asking about your report without witnessing the fighting, due to their extreme cowardice and weak intentions. And if they had been among you, they would not have fought except a little. That is, if they had been with you in this raid, witnessing the fighting, due to their extreme cowardice and weak intentions. And if they had been among you, they would not have fought except a little. That is, if they had been with you in this raid, witnessing the fighting, they would not have fought with you except a little, out of fear of disgrace and out of zeal for their homeland.
33:21: 21- There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern meaning a righteous example. It is said that I have a good example in so-and-so, meaning I have a good example in him. The example comes from the verb to imitate, just as the example comes from the verb to follow. It is a noun that replaces the verbal noun. Al-Jawhari said: The example and the model are with the damma and kasra, and the plural is asa and isa. The majority read aswa with the damma because of the hamza, and Asim read it with the kasra, and they are two dialects as Al-Farra and others said. This verse is a rebuke to those who stayed behind from fighting with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): meaning, you have an example in the Messenger of God, as he sacrificed himself to fight and went out to the Trench to support the religion of God. Although the reason for this verse is specific, it is general in everything. Similar to it is: Whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from.
