And His statement: “Say: If you should love God, then follow me, and God will love you.” The lām in for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day is related to good deed or to an omitted word that is an attribute of good deed: meaning, it will be for whoever hopes in God. It was said that the sentence is a substitute for the kāf in for you, but Abu Hayyan rejected this and said that the pronoun for the person addressed cannot be substituted by repeating the preposition. The answer to this is that the Kufians and Al-Akhfash permitted it, but the Basrans forbade it. What is meant by whoever hopes in God are the believers, for they are the ones who hope in God and fear His punishment. The meaning of hope in God is that they hope for His reward or to meet Him. The meaning of hope in the Last Day is that they hope for God’s mercy in it or believe in its occurrence and that it will inevitably happen. This sentence is a specification after the generalization in the first sentence, and remember God often, in apposition to was, meaning, for whoever remembers God often in all his circumstances, and combines hope in God and remembrance of Him, then by that the good example of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is achieved.
33:22: Then the Almighty explained what happened from the sincere believers when they saw the confederates and witnessed those armies that surrounded them like a raging sea, saying: 22- And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, ‘This is what God and His Messenger promised us.’ The reference in His saying this is to what they saw of the armies, or to the calamity that befell and the affliction that befell. They said this statement in anticipation of the occurrence of what God and His Messenger promised them of the coming of these soldiers, and that their coming to them will be followed by the descent of victory and triumph from God. The word ma in what God promised us is the relative pronoun or the verbal noun. Then they followed up what they said by saying: And God and His Messenger spoke the truth, meaning the truth of the report of God and His Messenger became clear. And it only increased them in faith and submission, meaning what they saw only increased their faith in God and submission to His command. Al-Farra’ said: Looking at the confederates only increased their faith and submission. Ali bin Sulayman said: Seeing indicates seeing and The feminine of the word vision is not real, and the meaning is: The vision only increased their faith in God and their submission to fate. If he had said it only increased them, it would have been permissible.
33:23: 23- Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to God. That is, among the sincere believers are men who have been true to what they promised God. From sadaqni if he says the truth. The place of ma khattak God is the accusative by removing the preposition. The meaning is that they fulfilled what they pledged to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of Aqaba, to remain steadfast with him and fight whoever fought him, unlike those who lied in their pledge and betrayed God and His Messenger, and they are the hypocrites. It was said that they are those who vowed that if they encountered war with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would remain steadfast for him and not flee. The reason for showing the noble name and the Messenger in his saying: God and His Messenger have spoken the truth after his saying: what God and His Messenger promised us is to show glorification, as in the saying of the poet: I see death, nothing precedes death Also, if he had implied both of them, he would have combined the pronoun of God and the pronoun of His Messenger in one word. And he said, Truly, and the prohibition of combining them has been reported, as in the hadith, What a bad orator you are to the people! He said, And whoever disobeys them has certainly gone astray. Then the Almighty detailed the state of those who were truthful in what they promised God and His Messenger, and divided them into two groups, saying, And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is he who awaits. The word naḥīf means what a person has committed to and believes in fulfilling, and from it is the saying of the poet: On the eve of the Harithians' escape after he met his death at the meeting place of the people, Huber The other said: With a light fist, the kings fought us, and our horses, in the evening, were green on the ground. Anything great. Nahaab is used to mean a vow, killing, or death. Ibn Qutaybah said: He fulfilled his vow: meaning he was killed. The root of nahaab is a vow. On the day of Badr, they vowed that if they met the enemy, they would fight until they were killed or God granted them victory. So they were killed, so it was said that so-and-so fulfilled his vow: meaning he was killed. Nahaab is also a need and the fulfillment of a wish. One of them says: I have no vow with them. Nahaab is a covenant. From this comes the saying of the poet: Dog has cried over people that they are more deserving of the crown of the glorious and generous Another said: We may love glory more than we love Among the expressions of lamentation about need and the fulfillment of desire is the poet’s saying: Should I weep and die, or should I be misled and false? The meaning of the verse is: Among the believers are men who have achieved their wish, fulfilled their need, and fulfilled their vows, so they fought until they were killed, and that was on the day of Uhud, such as Hamza, Mus’ab ibn ‘Umair, and Anas ibn al-Nadr. And among them are those who await the fulfillment of their vow until their time comes, such as ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, Talha, al-Zubayr, and their likes. They continue to fulfill what they pledged to God to do, to remain steadfast with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to fight his enemy, and they await the fulfillment of their need and the fulfillment of their wish by being killed and attaining the virtue of martyrdom. The phrase and they have not changed at all is connected to they have been truthful, meaning they have not changed their pledge to God as the hypocrites changed their pledge, rather they have remained steadfast in it. As for those who have fulfilled their vows, this is clear. As for those who await the fulfillment of their vows, they have continued in that until they departed this world, and they have not changed or altered.
33:24: The lam in His statement: 24- That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness may be related to their truthfulness, or to their provisions, or to what they changed, or to something omitted, as if it were said: everything that happened occurred so that God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness, and punish the hypocrites if He wills for what they did of change and alteration, making the hypocrites as if they intended the bad outcome and wanted it because of their change and alteration, just as the truthful intended the outcome of truthfulness through their loyalty, so each of the two groups is driven to its outcome of reward and punishment, so it is as if they are equal in seeking it and striving to obtain it, and the object of if He wills and its answer are omitted: meaning if He wills to punish them, He will punish them, and that is if they persist in hypocrisy and do not abandon it and repent from it. And God is Forgiving and Merciful meaning to whoever among them repents and desists from the hypocrisy that they were upon.
33:25: Then the Almighty returned to narrating the rest of the story and the blessings He bestowed upon His Messenger and the believers, saying: 25- And God turned back those who disbelieved, meaning the parties. The sentence is connected to So We sent upon them a wind, or to the implied factor in so that God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness, as if it was said: What happened of the incidents happened, and God turned back those who disbelieved. The place of in their fury is the accusative case of state, and the ba’ is for accompaniment: that is, the state of their being engulfed in their fury and accompanying it. It is permissible for it to be for causality, and the sentence they did not attain any good is in the accusative case of state also of the relative pronoun, or of the first state of succession, or overlap. Meaning: That God returned them with their anger, their hearts were not satisfied, nor did they attain any good in their belief, which was victory over the Muslims, or they did not attain any good, rather they returned as losers, they gained nothing except the trouble of travel and the cost of expenses. And God sufficed the believers in fighting with what He sent of the wind and the soldiers of angels. And God is Powerful and Exalted over everything He wants, if He says to it, Be, it is. Exalted, Victorious, Dominant, no one among His creation can overcome Him, and no one can oppose Him in His authority and might. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated regarding the statement of God, They slapped you, that he said: They faced you. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, And that was easy for God, that he said: Easy. Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib, Ibn Asakir and Ibn al-Najjar narrated from Umar regarding the statement of God, Indeed, you have in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern, that he said: In the hunger of the Messenger of God. A group of the Companions used this verse as evidence in many matters included in the books of Sunnah, but they are outside the scope of our discussion. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Dala’il from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, And when the believers saw the confederates, to the end of the verse, that God said to them in Surat al-Baqarah, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [affliction] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? They were touched by poverty and hardship. So when the affliction befell them when they joined the confederates in the trench, They said, ‘This is what God and His Messenger promised us.’ The Muslims interpreted that, but it only increased them in faith and submission. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Anas who said: We see that this verse was revealed about Anas ibn An-Nadr: Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. Ibn Sa’d, Ahmad, Muslim, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i, Al-Baghawi in his Mu’jam, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Anas who said: My uncle Anas ibn An-Nadr was absent from the Battle of Badr and he was distressed and said: “I was absent from the first battle that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) witnessed. If God lets me witness another battle with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) after that, God will see what I will do.” So he was present at the Battle of Uhud. Sa’d ibn Mu’adh met him and said: O Abu Amr, where? He said: Wow, the fragrance of Paradise I smell before Uhud. He fought until he was killed and eighty-odd wounds were found on his body, between blows, stab wounds and arrow wounds. Then this verse was revealed: Men true to what they pledged to God. They believed that it was revealed about him and his companions. A similar narration was narrated from him through another chain of narration by At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, as was An-Nasa’i and others. Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) returned from Uhud, he passed by Mus'ab ibn 'Umair who had been killed. He stopped over him and supplicated for him, then recited, ‘Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God…’ [Al-Bukhari and Muslim], and then said, ‘I bear witness that these are witnesses with God, so go to them and visit them. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one will greet them until the Day of Resurrection without them greeting him back.’” Al-Hakim commented on this in his authentication of Al-Dhahabi, as mentioned by Al-Suyuti, but Al-Hakim narrated another hadith and authenticated it. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it in Al-Dala'il on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said, “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had finished the day of Uhud, he passed by Mus'ab ibn 'Umair who had been killed on his way, and recited, ‘Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God…’ [Al-Bukhari and Muslim].” Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith from Khabbab, and they both bear witness to the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. At-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Talhah that the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to an ignorant Bedouin: Ask him about someone who has fulfilled his vow and who he is. They did not dare to ask him because they respected and feared him. The Bedouin asked him, but he turned away. Then he asked him again, but he turned away. Then I looked out of the door of the mosque and he said: Where is the one who asked about someone who has fulfilled his vow? The Bedouin said: I am. He said: This is one of those who have fulfilled his vow. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith. At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Mu'awiyah that he said: “I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: Talhah is one of those who have fulfilled his vow.” Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abu Ya'la, Abu Nu'aym, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aishah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever would like to see a man walking on the earth who has fulfilled his vow, let him look at Talhah. Abu Al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ali that this verse was revealed about Talhah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, meaning dying while they had pledged to God, and among them are those who await death while they were still in that covenant. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sulayman ibn Sard, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said on the Day of the Confederates: ‘Now we will attack them, and they will not attack us.’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, regarding his statement, And among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, he said: dying while they were in that state of belief and faith. And among them are those who await that. And they have not changed by any change, they did not change as the hypocrites changed.
33:26: His saying: 26- And He sent down those who supported them from among the People of the Scripture meaning they supported and aided them against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and they were Banu Qurayzah, for they aided the Confederates and broke the covenant that was between them and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and they became one hand with the Confederates. And the word siyasi is the plural of saysiyyah which means fortresses, and everything that you fortify yourself with is called saysiyyah, and from this comes the word saysiyyah of a rooster, which is the thorn in its leg, and the horns of cows because they protect themselves with it, and the weaver’s thorn with which he straightens the warp and weft is called saysiyyah, and from this comes the saying of Duraid bin Al-Summah: I came to him and the spears were hitting him like the sound of spears hitting a fabric. And from its application to fortresses, the poet said: The bulls fell down and the women of Tamim started racing to catch the bulls. And He cast terror into their hearts meaning intense fear until they surrendered themselves to be killed and their women and children to be taken captive. This is the meaning of His statement, A party you kill and a party you take captive. The first party is the men, and the second party is the women and children. This sentence explains and confirms the casting of terror into their hearts. The majority of scholars read you kill with a superlative as an addressee, and they also read you take captive. Ibn Dhakwan, in a narration from him, read it with a sub-diacritical mark in both. Al-Yamani read it with a superlative in the first and a sub-diacritical mark in the second. Abu Haywah read you take captive with a damma on the seen. Al-Farra' reported that the seen is pronounced with a kasra or a damma, as they are two dialects. The reason for bringing the direct object of the verb forward and the direct object of the second verb back is that since men were the people of power, and the more severe of the two matters that befell them was killed, so mentioning them first was more appropriate for the situation. There is disagreement about the number of those killed and captured. Some say the number killed was between six and seven hundred. Others say six hundred, seven hundred, eight hundred, and nine hundred. The number of those captured was seven hundred, seven hundred and fifty, and nine hundred.
33:27: 27- And He caused you to inherit their land, their houses, and their wealth. What is meant by land is real estate and palm trees, and by houses is houses and fortresses, and by wealth is jewelry, furniture, livestock, weapons, dirhams, and dinars. And a land which you have not trodden. That is, He caused you to inherit a land which you have not trodden, and the phrase you have not trodden is an adjective for land. The majority of scholars read lam tatawuha with a damma on the hamza and then a silent waw. Zayd ibn Ali read tatawuha with a fatha on the ta' and a silent waw. The commentators differed in identifying the mentioned land. Yazid ibn Ruman, Ibn Zayd and Muqatil said: It was Khaybar, and at that time they had not yet obtained it, so God promised it to them. Qatada said: We used to think it was Mecca. Al-Hasan said: Persia and Rome. Ikrimah said: Every land will be conquered until the Day of Resurrection. And God is over all things competent, meaning He, glory be to Him, is capable of everything He wills of good and evil, blessing and punishment, and of fulfilling what He promised of conquest to the Muslims. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: From their fortresses, he said: Their strongholds. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: “I went out on the day of the Trench to follow the people, and there I saw Sa`d ibn Mu`adh. A man from Quraysh called Ibn al-Farqadah shot him with an arrow that struck his ankle and cut it off. Sa`d called upon God and said: ‘O God, do not let me die until you have relieved my eyes from the Qurayzah.’ So God sent a wind upon the polytheists, and ‘God spared the believers the fighting.’ Abu Sufyan and those with him went to Tihamah, and `Uyaynah ibn Badr and those with him went to Najd. Banu Qurayzah returned and fortified themselves in their fortresses. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned to Medina and ordered that a leather tent be erected over Sa`d in the mosque. She said: ‘Then Gabriel came, and dust had fallen on his front teeth, and he said: ‘Have you laid down your weapons? No, by God, the angels have not laid down their weapons after that. Go out to Banu Qurayzah and fight them.’ So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) dressed for his nation and gave the people permission to leave, so he besieged them.” Twenty-five nights, and when the siege intensified and the affliction intensified upon them, it was said to them: Come down according to the judgment of the Messenger of God. They said: We will come down according to the judgment of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh. So they came down and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for Sa`d ibn Mu`adh and he was brought to him on a donkey. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Judge regarding them. He said: Then I judge regarding them that their fighters be killed, their children be taken captive and their wealth be divided. He said: You have judged regarding them according to the judgment of God and the judgment of His Messenger.
33:28: His saying: 28- O Prophet, tell your wives It was said that this verse is connected to the meaning of what preceded it regarding the prohibition of harming the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had been harmed by some of his wives. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him for something of worldly goods and requested an increase in their spending and harmed him with the jealousy of some of them towards others, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore an oath to be away from them for a month, and God revealed this verse of choice, and they were nine at that time: Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Salamah, Umm Habiba, and Sawda. These were from the women of Quraysh, and Safiyya al-Khaibariyya, Maymunah al-Hilaliyya, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyya, and Juwayriyya bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqya. The meaning of the life of this world and its adornment is its spaciousness, freshness, luxury and enjoyment therein. So come means come to me. I will provide for you in the jussive mood as an answer to the command: meaning, give the provision. And likewise, I will set you free in the jussive mood: meaning, I will divorce you. The majority of scholars have read both verbs in the jussive mood, while Hamid al-Kharraz has read both verbs in the nominative mood as a new resumption. What is meant by beautiful release is that which occurs without causing harm, according to the Sunnah. It has been said that the jussive mood of the two verbs indicates that they are an answer to the condition. Based on this, his statement So come is an interruption between the condition and the consequence.
33:29: 29- And if you desire God and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter meaning Paradise and its delights then indeed God has prepared for the good-doers among you meaning those who do righteous deeds a great reward that cannot be described and whose value cannot be measured, because of their good deeds and in return for their righteous deeds. Scholars differed on how the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave his wives the choice. There are two opinions: The first opinion is that he gave them the choice, by God’s permission, to remain married to each other or to divorce them, and they chose to remain married. This is what Aisha, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ash-Sha’bi, Az-Zuhri, and Rabi’ah said. The second opinion is that he gave them the choice between this world, in which case he could divorce them, and the Hereafter, in which case he could keep them. He did not give them the choice of divorce. This is what Ali, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah said, but the first opinion is more correct. They also differed on the woman who is given the choice if she chooses her husband. Does this mere choice count as one divorce from the husband or not? The majority of the early and later scholars held the view that if a woman chooses her husband, there is no divorce, not one or more. Ali and Zayd ibn Thabit said: If she chooses her husband, then it is one irrevocable divorce. This is what Al-Hasan and Al-Layth said. Al-Khattabi and Al-Naqqash narrated it from Malik. The first and most correct opinion is based on the hadith of Aisha, which is proven in the two Sahihs. She said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave us a choice, and we chose him. He did not consider it a divorce. There is no basis for considering the mere fact of giving us a choice to be a divorce. The claim that it is a euphemism for divorce is refuted by the fact that the one who gave the choice did not intend separation simply for the sake of choice, rather he intended to delegate the matter to the woman and put her in her own hands. If she chose to remain, she would remain in the state of marriage, and if she chose separation, she would be divorced. They differed regarding her choosing herself, whether that would be a revocable or irrevocable divorce. The former was held by Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Abi Layla, al-Thawri, and al-Shafi'i. The latter was held by Ali, Abu Hanifa, and his companions, and it was also narrated from Malik. The former is more correct, because it is very unlikely that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would divorce his wives contrary to what God had commanded him to do, as He had commanded him by saying: When you divorce women, divorce them during their waiting period. It was narrated from Zayd ibn Thabit that if she chooses herself, then it is three divorces, but this opinion is baseless. It was narrated from Ali that if she chooses herself, then it is nothing, but if she chooses her husband, then it is one revocable divorce.
33:30: Then when the wives of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) chose the Messenger of God, He revealed these verses regarding them to honor them and magnify their rights, saying: 30- O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality meaning something that is clearly ugly and obvious indecency, and God has protected them from that and has cleared and purified them the punishment will be doubled for her meaning He will punish them twice as much as other women if they commit such an immorality, and that is due to their honor, high status, and lofty position. It has been established in this Shari'ah in more than one place that the doubling of honor and elevation of status necessitates that the punishments be doubled for its doer if he disobeys. Abu Amr read yuda'if in the passive form, and he and Abu Ubaid differentiated between yuda'if and said: it could be yuda'if as three punishments and yuda'if as two punishments. An-Nahhas said: This distinction that he brought is not known to any linguist, and the meaning of He multiplies and He weakens is one: that is, He makes it double, and thus He doubled is what Ibn Jarir said, And that was easy for God, He does not find it too great or difficult.
33:31: 31- And whoever among you is obedient to God and His Messenger and does righteousness The majority of scholars read yaqunt with a dhammah, and they also read yu’ta minkuna based on the word min in both instances. Al-Jahdary, Ya’qub, and Ibn ‘Amir in one narration, and Abu Ja’far read it with a dhammah based on the meaning, and the meaning of whoever is obedient is whoever obeys. The reciters differed in mubayyinah. Some of them read it with a kasrah, and some of them read it with a fathah on the ya’, as mentioned previously in An-Nisa’. Ibn Kathir and Ibn ‘Amir read yuddaa’ib with a noon and al-‘adhaab with a nasb. Yudha’tiha ‘ajrha murtayn was also read with a kasrah on the ‘ayn, based on the active participle nu’tuha ‘ajrha murtayn Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a dhammah, and they also read ya’mal with a dhammah, and the rest read ya’mal with a dhammah, and nu’tu with a noon. The meaning of they will receive the reward twice is that they will have a reward for obedience, for example, what other women would receive if they did that act of obedience. This is strong evidence that the meaning of her punishment will be doubled for her is that the punishment will be twice, not three times, because the intent is to demonstrate their honor and distinction in obedience and disobedience by making their good deed like two good deeds and their bad deed like two bad deeds. If their bad deed were like three bad deeds, it would not be appropriate for their good deed to be like two good deeds, because God is more just than to double the punishment for them in a way that exceeds the doubling of their reward. And We have prepared for her in addition to the reward twice, a noble provision. The commentators said: The noble provision is the bliss of Paradise, as An-Nahhas reported from them.
33:32: Then God, the Almighty, clearly demonstrated their superiority over all other women. He said: 32- O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. Al-Zajjaj said: He did not say like any of the women, because one is a general negation for masculine and feminine, singular and plural. It may also be said of something that is not human, as one says: There is no one among them, neither a sheep nor a camel. The meaning is: You are not like any single group of women in virtue and honor. Then He qualified this great honor by saying: If you fear God. Thus, God, the Almighty, made clear that this virtue for them is only due to their adherence to fear of God, not merely their connection to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And, praise be to God, they demonstrated clear fear of God, pure faith, and followed the path of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his life and after his death. The answer to the condition is omitted because what preceded it indicates it: that is, if you fear God, then you are not like any of the women. It was said that the answer to it is: Then do not be submissive, but the former is more appropriate. The meaning of do not speak softly is do not be soft in speech when addressing people as suspicious women do, because that causes great corruption, which is His statement, lest he in whose heart is disease covet meaning immorality, doubt and hypocrisy. The word yatama' is in the accusative case because it is the answer to the prohibition. This is how the majority of scholars read it. Abu Hatim narrated that Al-A'raj read yatama' with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the meem. An-Nahhas said: I think this is a mistake. This reading was narrated on the authority of Abu As-Sama'al, 'Isa ibn 'Umar and Ibn Muhaisin, and it was narrated on their authority that they read it with a jazm in apposition to the place of the verb of prohibition. And speak a word that is appropriate among people, far from suspicion, in accordance with the ways of the Sharee'ah, so that the hearer does not disapprove of anything from it, and the people of immorality and immorality do not covet them because of it.
33:33: 33- And stay in your houses The majority read it as wa-qarān with a kasra on the qaf from wa-qār yaqrū wa-qārān: meaning to dwell, and the imperative form of it is qār with a kasra on the qaf, and for women qarn is like ‘Adan in weight. Al-Mubarrad said: It is from qārār, not from waqār. You say qarārat bi-l-makān with a fatha on the ra’, and the original is iqrārna with a kasra on the ra’, so the first ra’ was deleted for ease of speech as they said in Ḍilt ḍalta, and we quote its movement to the qaf, and the alif of connection was dispensed with by moving the qāl. Abu Ali al-Farsi said: It was replaced by it, and the meaning is iqirna, then the movement of the ya’ is transferred to the qaf due to the dislike of moving the ya’ with a kasra, so the ya’ is dropped due to the meeting of two sukūn letters, and the hamzat al-wasl is dropped due to the movement of what follows it, so it becomes qarn. Nafi' and Asim read it with a fatha on the qaf. Its original form is qarara bil-makan i.e., you reside in it with a kasra on the ra'. Aqarra with a fatha on the qaf like hamd yahmad praise, and it is the dialect of the people of Hijaz. This was mentioned by Abu Ubaid on the authority of Al-Kisa'i, and it was also mentioned by Al-Zajjaj and others. Al-Farra' said: It is like saying hal hasat sahibak did you feel his companion meaning did you feel him? Abu Ubaid said: Our elders among the Arab scholars used to reject the reading with a fatha on the qaf, because qarara bil-makan i.e., you resided in it is not permitted by many Arab scholars. The correct form is qarara qarra with a kasra, and its meaning is: an order to them to be respectful and to remain in their homes and not to go out. This contradicts what we mentioned here on the authority of Al-Kisa'i, who was one of his most prominent sheikhs. Abu Hatim agreed with him in rejecting this reading, saying: There is no school of thought in the speech of the Arabs that uses qarra with a fatha on the qaf. An-Nahhas said: Abu Hatim was contradicted in his statement that it is his school of thought in the speech of the Arabs. Rather, there are two schools of thought: One of them was narrated by Al-Kisa’i, and the other is from Ali bin Sulayman. As for the school of thought that Al-Kisa’i narrated, it is what we presented from the narration of Abu Ubayd from him. As for the school of thought that Ali bin Sulayman narrated, he said: It is from qararah bih ayn, meaning: And acknowledge it with an eye in your homes. An-Nahhas said: This is a good interpretation. I say: It is not good and it is not the meaning of the verse, because what is meant by it is an order to them to be calm and settled in their homes, and it is not from the delight of the eye. Ibn Abi Ubla read Wa-aqarna with an alif wasl and two ra’s, the first one is kasra according to the original and do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance. Tabarruj is for a woman to show off her adornment and charms that which she should cover, in order to arouse the desire of a man. The meaning of Tabarruj has been mentioned previously in Surat An-Nur. Al-Mubarrad said: It is taken from the word burj wideness, it is said about his teeth burj if they are spread out. It has been said that Tabarruj is swaggering in walking, but this is very weak. There is disagreement about what is meant by the first Jahiliyyah. Some say it is between Adam and Noah, or between Noah and Idris, or between Noah and Abraham, or between Moses and Jesus, or between Jesus and Muhammad. Al-Mubarrad said: The first Jahiliyyah is as the ignorant Jahiliyyah say. He said: The women of the Jahiliyyah used to show what was shameful to show, to the point that a woman would sit with her husband and her lover, and her lover would be alone with what was above the lower garment upwards, and her husband would be alone with what was below the lower garment downwards, and one of them might ask the other for a change. Ibn Atiyyah said: What appears to me is that he referred to the Jahiliyyah that they had fallen into, so they were ordered to change from their way of life therein, which was the way of the disbelievers before the Shari’ah, because they had no jealousy among them. The meaning does not mean that there was another Jahiliyyah, as he said, and it is a good statement. The other ignorance could be what occurs in Islam of imitating the people of ignorance in word or deed, so the meaning would be: And do not, O Muslim women, display yourselves after your conversion to Islam in a manner like the display of ignorance that you were upon, and that was done by those before you. That is, do not create with your actions and words an ignorance that resembles the ignorance that came before. And establish prayer and give zakat and obey God and His Messenger. He specified prayer and zakat because they are the foundation of physical and financial obedience. Then he generalized and ordered them to obey God and His Messenger in all that is permissible. God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the Household. That is, God has only enjoined upon you what He has enjoined upon you of piety, not to be submissive in speech, to speak well of others, to be quiet in your homes, not to be ostentatious, to establish prayer, to give zakat, and to obey, so that He may keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the Household. What is meant by uncleanness is the sin and wrongdoing that defiles the reputations that result from abandoning what God has commanded and doing what He has forbidden. This includes everything that does not please God. The nominative case of people of the household is for praise, as Az-Zajjaj said. He said: If you like, it is for substitution. He said: The nominative and genitive cases are permissible. An-Nahhas said: If it is in the genitive case, it is because it is a substitution for the kaf and the mim. Al-Mubarrad objected to him by saying that it is not permissible to substitute the one being addressed, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a call. And purify you with a thorough purification. That is, He purifies you from uncleanness and filth with a complete purification. The metaphor of filth for sin and the recommendation for purification are strong warnings against it and a severe reprimand for its perpetrator. Scholars have differed regarding the people of the house mentioned in the verse. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Ata’, Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and Saeed bin Jubair said: The people of the house mentioned in the verse are the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically.
33:34: They said: What is meant by the house is the house of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the dwellings of his wives, as God says: 34- And remember what is recited in your houses. Also, the context of wives begins with His saying: O Prophet, tell your wives until His saying: “And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom. Indeed, God is ever Kind and Aware.” Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Al-Kalbi said that the people of the house mentioned in the verse are Ali, Fatima, Al-Hasan, and Al-Hussein specifically. Among their arguments is the address in the verse in a way that is appropriate for males and not for females, which is His saying: from you and that He may purify you. If it were for women specifically, He would have said from you and that He may purify you. The first scholars responded to this by saying that the reminder is based on the word family, as God the Almighty said: Do you wonder at the command of God? May the mercy and blessings of God be upon you, O people of the house. And as when a man says to his friend: How is your family? meaning his wife or wives, and he says: They are fine. Let us mention here what each group held on to: As for the first, they held on to the context, for it is about wives, as we mentioned, and what Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the House. He said: It was revealed specifically about the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ikrimah said: Whoever wishes to marry his wife, that it was revealed about the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ikrimah. Ibn Saad narrated something similar on the authority of Urwah. As for what others have held fast to, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and authenticated it, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, through various chains of transmission, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: “In my house, the verse ‘God only desires to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House’ was revealed. In the house were Fatimah, Ali, Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, covered them with a cloak that he was wearing, then he said: These are my family, so remove impurity from them and purify them with a thorough purification.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in her house, sleeping, wearing a Khaybari cloak. Fatimah brought a pot of stew, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Call your husband and your two sons, Hasan and Husayn. So she called them. While they were eating, the following verse was revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the Household, and to purify you with a thorough purification. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took the remainder of his cloak and covered them with it. Then he took his hand out of the cloak and waved it toward the sky, then said: O God, these are my family and my special ones, so keep away uncleanness from them and purify them with a thorough purification. He said it three times. Umm Salamah said: “So I put my head into the curtain and said: O Messenger of God, am I with you?” He said: You will be in goodness twice. Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of her. He said: Abdullah ibn Numayr told us. Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulaiman narrated to us on the authority of Ata bin Abi Riyah, he told me that someone heard Umm Salamah mentioning that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned it. In its chain of transmission is an unknown narrator, and he is the sheikh of Ata, but the rest of its men are trustworthy. At-Tabarani narrated it on her authority through two chains of transmission similar to it. Ibn Kathir mentioned in his commentary on the hadith of Umm Salamah many chains of transmission in Musnad Ahmad and others. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Khatib narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri. At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh, At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umar bin Abi Salamah, the foster son of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: When this verse was revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Umm Salamah. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Muslim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out one morning wearing a black hair cloak. Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn came to him, so he brought them in with him. Then Fatimah came, so he brought her in with him. Then Ali came, so he brought him in with him. Then he said: God only desires to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came to Fatimah, accompanied by Ali, Hasan, and Husayn, until he entered. He brought Ali and Fatimah close and seated them in front of him, and seated Hasan and Husayn, each one of them on his thigh. Then he wrapped his garment around them, and I was behind them. Then he recited this verse: ‘God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the Household.’ And he said: ‘O God, these are my family. O God, keep away the uncleanness from them and purify them with a thorough purification.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, am I one of your family?’ He said: ‘And you are one of my family.’” Wathilah said: This is the most hopeful thing I hope for. And it has various chains of narration in Musnad Ahmad. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would pass by Fatimah’s door when he went out to the dawn prayer, saying: “Prayer, O people of the house, prayer. God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the house, and to purify you with a thorough purification.” Muslim narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I remind you of God by regard to the people of my house. It was said to Zayd: And who are the people of his house? Are not his women among the people of his house? He said: “His women are among the people of his house, but the people of his house are those for whom charity is forbidden after him: the family of Ali, the family of Aqeel, the family of Ja’far, and the family of Abbas.” Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God divided creation into two parts, and He made me in the better part of them. This is what He said: ‘And the companions of the right’ and ‘And the companions of the left.’ So I am one of the companions of the right, and I am the best of the companions of the right. Then He divided the two parts into thirds, and He made me in the better part of them. This is what He said: ‘And the companions of the right,’ ‘And the companions of the left,’ ‘And the foremost, the foremost.’ So I am one of the foremost, and I am the best of the foremost. Then He divided the thirds into tribes, and He made me in the best tribe. This is what He said: ‘And We have made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Verily, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you.’ And I am the most righteous of the children of Adam and the most honoured of them in the sight of God, and I do not boast. Then He divided the tribes into houses, and He made me in the best house. This is what He said: ‘God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the Household, and to purify you with a thorough purification.’ So I and my household are purified from sins.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu al-Hamra’ who said: I stayed in Medina for seven months during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: “I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when dawn came, coming to the door of Ali and Fatima and saying: ‘Prayer, prayer. God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.’” In its chain of transmission is Abu Dawud al-Ama, who is a fabricator and a liar. There are hadiths and narrations on this topic, and we have mentioned here what is suitable to adhere to and not what is not. A third group mediated between the two groups, making this verse inclusive of the wives, Ali, Fatima, Hassan and Hussein. As for the wives, this is because they are the ones meant in the context of these verses, as we mentioned, and because they are the ones who resided in his houses, may God bless him and grant him peace, and stayed in his dwellings. This is supported by what was mentioned previously from Ibn Abbas and others. As for the inclusion of Ali, Fatima, Hassan and Hussein, this is because they are his relatives and members of his household in lineage. This is supported by what we mentioned from the hadiths that clearly state that they are the reason for revelation. Whoever makes the verse specific to one of the two kin has implemented some of what must be implemented and neglected what cannot be neglected. This opinion has been favored by a group of scholars, including Al-Qurtubi, Ibn Kathir and others. A group said: They are Banu Hashim, and they based their evidence on the hadith of Ibn Abbas mentioned above and the words of Zaid bin Arqam mentioned above where he said: But his family after whom charity was forbidden: the family of Ali, the family of Aqeel, the family of Jaafar, and the family of Abbas. These people went to the view that what is meant by the house is the house of lineage. His statement: {And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom} meaning remember the place of blessing when God placed you in houses in which the verses of God and wisdom are recited. Remember them and reflect on them so that you may be admonished by God’s admonitions, or remind them to the people so that they may be admonished by them and be guided by their guidance, or remember them by reciting them so that you may memorize them and do not abandon frequent recitation. Al-Qurtubi said: The people of interpretation said that the verses of God are the Qur’an, and the wisdom is the Sunnah. Muqatil said that what is meant by the verses and wisdom are His commands and prohibitions in the Qur’an. It has been said that the Qur’an combines being clear verses indicating monotheism and the truth of prophethood with being wisdom encompassing various types of sciences and laws. Indeed, God is Kind and All-Aware. That is, He is kind to His friends and All-Aware of all His creation and everything that comes from them of good and evil, obedience and disobedience. He rewards the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil. Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir who said: Abu Bakr came to ask permission to see the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) while the people were sitting at his door and the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was sitting, but he was not given permission. Then ‘Umar came and asked permission but he was not given permission. Then Abu Bakr and ‘Umar were given permission and they entered while the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was sitting with his wives around him and he was silent. ‘Umar said: I will tell the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) so that he may laugh. ‘Umar said: O Messenger of God, if you had seen the daughter of Zayd, the wife of ‘Umar, who asked for a living just now and I struck her on the neck. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) laughed until his molars were visible and said: They are around me asking me for a living. Abu Bakr went to ‘Aisha to hit her, and ‘Umar went to Hafsa, both of them saying: You are asking the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) for something he does not have. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) forbade them. His wives said: By God, we will not ask the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) for something he does not have after this gathering. God revealed the choice. So he called to ‘Aisha and said: I am going to mention something to you. I do not like you to rush into it until you consult your parents. She said: What is it? So he recited to her: O Prophet, tell your wives the verse. Aisha said: Is it you who I consult my parents about? Rather, God chose His Messenger. And I ask you not to mention to your wives what I have chosen. He said: God did not send me to be strict, but He sent me as a teacher and bringer of good tidings. Let no woman among them ask me about what I have chosen except that I inform her. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to her when God commanded him to give his wives a choice. She said: He started with me and said: I am going to mention to you a matter, so do not be hasty until you consult your parents. He knew that my parents would not command me to leave him. He said: God said: O Prophet, tell your wives, if you should desire the life of this world the verse continues. I said to him: So about which of these should I consult my parents? I desire God, His Messenger and the Hereafter. The wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did as I did. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse {And whoever among you is obedient to God and His Messenger and does righteousness}, he said: He means whoever among you obeys God and works for the sake of God and His Messenger by obeying Him. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding the verse {And do not be soft in speech}, he said: He means do not be soft in speech and do not speak softly. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority regarding the verse {And do not be soft in speech}, he said: Comparing men in speech until the one in whose heart is a disease is filled with desire. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said: I was told that it was said to Sawdah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Why do you not perform Hajj or Umrah as your sisters do? She said: I have performed Hajj and Umrah, and God has commanded me to remain in my house, so by God I will not leave my house until I die. He said: By God, she did not leave the door of her room until her funeral procession was brought out. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Sa'd, Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Zuhd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Masruq who said: When Aisha would recite And abide in your houses Qur'an 1:17, she would weep until her veil was soaked. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated that he said: The first Jahiliyyah was between Noah and Idris and lasted for a thousand years. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Umar bin al-Khattab asked him, "What do you think of the statement of God to the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), 'And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the first ignorance'? Was there more than one Jahiliyyah? Ibn Abbas said, "I have never heard of a first one that does not have an end. Umar said to him, Bring me something from the Book of God that confirms that. He said, God says, 'And strive in God's cause with the striving due to Him. He chose you the first time.' Umar said, Who commanded us to strive in God's cause? He said, Makhzum and Abd Shams. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said, The first Jahiliyyah was between Jesus and Muhammad. We have already mentioned the narrations that have been reported about the reason for the revelation of the verse: God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom, that he said: The Qur’an and Sunnah praise them for that. Ibn Sa’d narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah on the authority of Sahl regarding his statement: And remember what is recited in your houses, that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pray voluntary prayers in the houses of his wives, day and night.
33:35: His saying: 35- The Muslims God Almighty began by mentioning Islam, which is merely entering into the religion and submitting to it with action, as was established in the authentic hadith “that when Gabriel asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Islam, he said: It is to testify that there is no god but God, to establish prayer, to pay zakat, to make the pilgrimage to the House, and to fast Ramadan.” Then He mentioned the Muslim men and women as an honor to them by mentioning them. And so it is in what follows, even though they are included in the expressions of Muslims and believers and the like. The masculine gender is to give precedence to males over females, as in all that is mentioned in the Noble Book regarding this. Then He mentioned the believing men and believing women, who are those who believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and in destiny, both good and bad, as is proven in the authentic hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The obedient man is the worshipper who obeys, and so is the obedient woman. It was also said that they are those who are constant in worship and obedience. The truthful man and truthful woman are those who speak the truth, avoid lying, and fulfill their covenant. The patient man and patient woman are those who are patient in avoiding desires and the hardships of obligation. The humble man and humble woman are those who are humble before God, fear Him, and submit in their worship of God. The charitable man and charitable woman are those who give charity from their wealth as God has made it obligatory for them. It was said that this is more general than obligatory and voluntary charity, and the same applies to the fasting man and woman. It was said that this is specific to the obligatory, and it was said that it is more general. The man and woman who guard their private parts from the forbidden by being chaste, abstaining from what is permissible, and the man and woman who remember are those who remember God in their states. The mention of abundance is evidence of the permissibility of frequently remembering God, the Most High, in the heart and on the tongue. In the case of the female guardians, what was mentioned previously in the case of the male guardians was sufficient, with the meaning: and the male guardians of their private parts, and the same applies to the female guardians, with the meaning: and the male guardians of their private parts, and the same applies to the female guardians, with the meaning: and the male and female guardians of their private parts. The report of all of what was mentioned is His statement: God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward, meaning forgiveness for their sins that they committed and a great reward for their acts of obedience that they performed of Islam, faith, piety, truthfulness, patience, humility, charity, fasting, chastity, and remembrance. The description of the reward as great is to indicate that it is extremely great, and there is nothing greater than the reward of Paradise and its everlasting bliss that does not cease nor It is running out, O God, forgive our sins and grant us the greatest reward.
33:36: 36- And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision. That is, it is not right or proper for a believing man or woman. The words what was and what should be and similar mean the prohibition and ban of something and informing that it is not permissible for it to be legally permissible. It may also refer to something that is rationally forbidden, as in His statement: It is not for you to cause its trees to grow. The meaning of the verse is that it is not permissible for someone who believes in God, when God has decided a matter, to choose whatever they want in their own affairs. Rather, they must submit to the decree and submit to what God has decided and chosen for them. The two pronouns are combined in His statement: for them and of their affair because a believing man and a believing woman are in the context of negation, so they include every believing man and woman. The Kufians read an yakun with a sukoon on the lower case, and Abu Ubaid chose this reading because he differentiated between the verb and its feminine subject by saying to them, even though the femininity is not real. The rest read it with a sukoon on the upper case because it is attributed to the choice, which is feminine in form, and the choice is a source meaning choice. Ibn al-Sameefa' read al-khayra with a sukoon on the lower case, and the rest read it with a sukoon on it. Then the Almighty threatened the one who does not submit to the will and destiny of God, saying: And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger in any matter, including dissatisfaction with the decree, has certainly gone astray with clear error. He has gone astray from the path of truth with a clear, obvious error that is not hidden. Ahmad, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah who said: I said, O Messenger of God, why are we not mentioned in the Qur'an as men are? I was startled one day by him calling out from the pulpit, saying, God says, 'Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...' to the end of the verse. Something similar to this was narrated on her authority through another chain of transmission narrated by Al-Faryabi, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh. Al-Faryabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Tirmidhi who classed it as hasan, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umm 'Amara Al-Ansariyya that she came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said, I do not see that everything is for men, and I do not see that women are mentioned at all. Then this verse was revealed, Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women. Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a chain of transmission - Al-Suyuti said: Hasan - on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas who said: The women said, O Messenger of God, why does He mention the believing men and not the believing women? Then this verse, Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women... was revealed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went to propose marriage to the daughter of Zayd ibn Haritha. He entered upon Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah and proposed marriage to her. She said: I am not willing to marry him. He said: Yes, marry him. She said: O Messenger of God, I am consulting myself. While they were talking, God revealed this verse to His Messenger: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman 4:17. She said: I have approved him for myself, O Messenger of God. He said: Yes. She said: Then I will not disobey the Messenger of God, I have married myself to him. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on his authority from another chain of narration. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Zaynab: ‘I want to marry you to Zayd ibn Haritha, for I am pleased with him for you.’ She said: ‘O Messenger of God, but I would not accept him for myself, as I am the leader of my people and the daughter of your paternal aunt, so I would not do that.’ Then this verse was revealed: ‘And it is not for a believing man’ meaning Zayd, ‘or a believing woman’ meaning Zaynab, ‘when God and His Messenger have decided a matter’ meaning marriage in this case, ‘that they should have any option in their decision’ meaning: they have no option in their decision other than what God has commanded. ‘And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.’ She said: ‘I have obeyed you, so do as you wish.’ So he married her to Zayd and consummated the marriage with her.’ Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Zayd that he said: This was revealed concerning Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, who was the first woman to emigrate and offer herself to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he married her to Zayd ibn Haritha. She and her brother were displeased and said: ‘We only wanted the Messenger of God, so we married him to his slave.’”
33:37: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married Zayd ibn Haritha to Zaynab bint Jahsh, as mentioned in the interpretation of the verse before this, God, the Exalted, revealed 37- And when you said to him whom God had bestowed favor upon and whom you had bestowed favor. That is, remember when you said to the one whom God had bestowed favor upon, namely Zayd ibn Haritha, “God had bestowed Islam upon him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had bestowed favor upon him by freeing him from slavery.” He was one of the captives of the Age of Ignorance, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had bought him during the Age of Ignorance, freed him, and adopted him. The reason for the revelation of the verse will come at the end of the research, which will clarify what is meant by it. Al-Qurtubi said: There has been a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of this verse. Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and a group of commentators, including Ibn Jarir al-Tabari and others, held that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, expressed his approval of Zaynab bint Jahsh while she was under the guardianship of Zayd, and he was keen for Zayd to divorce her so that he could marry her. Then, when Zayd informed him that he wanted to separate from her and complained about her harsh speech, disobedience to orders, verbal abuse, and pride in honor, he said to him: Fear God in what you say about her and keep your wife. He was concealing his eagerness for Zayd to divorce her. This is what he was concealing in his soul, but he adhered to what was required of enjoining what is right. Keep your wife means Zaynab. And fear God in her matter and do not hasten to divorce her. And conceal in yourself what God is to bring to light, which is marrying her if Zayd divorces her. It was also said that he loved her. And you fear the people, meaning you are shy of them, or you fear their reproach, that they might say that his master ordered his wife to be divorced and then he married her. And God is more deserving that you should fear Him in every situation, and be afraid of Him and feel ashamed of Him. The and is for the situation: that is, you conceal that matter in your soul for fear of people. So when Zaid had satisfied his need for it. Satisfying one’s need in the language means reaching the utmost limit of what is in the soul regarding something. It is said that he has satisfied his need for it: if he has reached what he wanted of his need for it. From this is the saying of Omar bin Abi Rabi’ah: O glorious fragrant invention, which has been spent from the Tihama of the strings That is, he completed the Hajj rituals and achieved what he wanted from it. What is meant here is that he satisfied his desire for her by marrying her and consummating the marriage, such that he no longer had any need for her. It was said that what is meant by it is divorce, and that a man only divorces his wife if he no longer had any need for her. Al-Mubarrad said: Desire is lust and love, and he recited: How will I stay in the city after Jameel bin Muammar has had his fill of it? Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Watar means the desire and need, and he recited the words of Al-Fazari: We bid farewell before we bid farewell to him, for he spent much of our youth and his desire for it The majority of scholars read "We have married you to her, while Ali and his sons, Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein, read We have married you to her". When God informed him of that, he consummated the marriage with her without permission, a contract, a dowry, or anything that is considered valid in marriage for his female slave. It was also said that what was meant by it was an order for him to marry her. The first is more appropriate, and this is what the authentic narrations came with. Then God, the Almighty, explained that by saying: "So that there will not be upon the believers any difficulty meaning hardship and difficulty concerning the wives of their adopted sons" meaning in marrying the wives of those they consider their sons, as the Arabs used to do, for they would adopt whomever they wanted. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had adopted Zayd ibn Haritha, so he was called Zayd ibn Muhammad until the Almighty's saying was revealed: "Call them by the names of their fathers" and the Arabs used to believe that the wives of those they adopted were forbidden to him just as the wives of their real sons were forbidden to him. And the adopted sons are permissible for them if they have satisfied their desire with them, unlike the son of the loins, whose wife makes his father forbidden to him by the same contract he made with her. And the command of God is to be fulfilled, meaning that God’s command regarding Zaynab, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, should marry her, was a past command that would inevitably be fulfilled.
33:38: Then God, the Almighty, made it clear that there was no blame on the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, for this marriage, saying: 38- There is no blame upon the Prophet for what God has ordained for him meaning in what God has permitted him, decreed, and ordained. It is said that such and such has been ordained for him: meaning it has been decreed for him. It is the way of God with those who passed on before meaning that this is the oldest way with the prophets and past nations, that they would attain what God had permitted them of marriage and other matters. And the command of God is a decree decreed meaning a decree that was decreed. Muqatil said: God informed that the matter of Zaynab was from the decree and predestination of God. The accusative of sunnah is in the source: meaning the way of God is the way of God, or a noun in the place of the source or in the accusative by making or by temptation. Abu Hibban rejected this by saying that the factor of temptation is not deleted.
33:39: Then the Almighty mentioned the past prophets and praised them, saying: 39- Those who convey the messages of God. The relative pronoun is in the genitive case as an attribute of those who passed away, or in the accusative case as an expression of praise. He praised them, the Almighty, for conveying what He sent them with to His servants and for fearing Him in every action and word, and they do not fear anyone other than Him, and they do not care about what people say or their expressions. Rather, their fear is limited to God, the Almighty. And sufficient is God as Accountant. He is present in every place, sufficient for His servants in everything they fear, or He is their accountant in everything. When the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, married Zaynab, the people said: He married his son’s wife.
33:40: So God revealed 40- Muhammad is not the father of any of your men meaning he is not the father of Zayd ibn Haritha in reality such that his wife would be forbidden to him, nor is he the father of anyone he did not father. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: He was not the father of anyone he did not father. He had sons, Ibrahim, Al-Qasim, Al-Tayyib, and Al-Mutahhar. Al-Qurtubi said: But he did not have a son who lived to become a man. He said: As for Al-Hasan and Al-Hussein, they were children and not men contemporaries of him. But the Messenger of God Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra' said: But he was the Messenger of God and they allowed the nominative case. Ibn Abi Ubla also read it in the nominative case in Rasool and in Khatam, meaning: But he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets. The majority of scholars read it with a light lakin and the accusative case in Rasool and Khatam. The accusative case is based on the predicate of kan, which is understood, as mentioned above. It is also permissible for it to be in conjunction with Abu Ahad. Abu Amr, in a narration from him, read it with a heavy lakin and the accusative case in Rasool as its name and its predicate is omitted: meaning, but he is the Messenger of God. The majority read khatam with a kasra on the ta'. Asim read it with a fatha. The meaning of the first reading is that he sealed them, meaning he came last among them. The meaning of the second reading is that he became like a seal to them, which they wear and adorn themselves with because he is one of them. It was said that the kasra and fatha of the ta' are two dialects. Abu Ubaid said: The correct reading is kasra because the interpretation is that he sealed them, so he is their seal, and that he said: I am the Seal of the Prophets. The seal of something is its last part. This is why they say: His seal is musk. Al-Hasan said: The seal is that with which one seals. And God is Knowing of all things. His knowledge encompasses all things, and among His knowledge are the rulings mentioned here. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi and others narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “Zaid ibn Haritha came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) complaining about Zainab. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept saying, ‘Fear God and keep your wife.’ Then the verse, ‘And you concealed within yourself that which God is to bring to light,’ was revealed.” Anas said: If the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had been able to conceal anything, he would have concealed this verse. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married her, and he never held a feast day for any of his wives as he did for her. He slaughtered a sheep. ‘And when Zaid had no longer any need for her, We married her to you.’ She used to boast to the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), saying, ‘Your families married you, but God married me from above the seven heavens.’” Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa’i and others narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “When Zaynab’s waiting period had ended, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said to Zayd: ‘Go and mention her to me.’ So he went. He said: ‘When I visited her, she became very strong in my heart, so I said: ‘O Zaynab, be glad, the Messenger of God has sent me to mention you.’ She said: ‘I will not do anything until I consult my Lord.’ So she got up to go to her place of prayer and the Qur’an was revealed. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came and entered upon her without permission. I saw us when she entered upon the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and we fed her bread and meat. Then the people went out and some men remained talking in the house after the meal. Then the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) went out.” I followed him, and he kept following his wives’ rooms, greeting them and saying: O Messenger of God, how did you find your family? I do not know whether I told him that the people had left or he told me. He went until he entered the house, so I went to enter with him. He threw a curtain between me and him, and the veil was revealed. He admonished the people as they had been admonished: Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you verse. Sa’id ibn Mansur, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: “If the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) had concealed anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse: “And when you said to him upon whom God had bestowed favor” meaning with Islam and whom you had bestowed favor meaning with emancipation Keep your wife to yourself until His saying: And the command of God is to be carried out. And when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) married her, they said: He married the wife of his son. So God revealed: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) had adopted him when he was young, and he lived until he became a man called Zayd ibn Muhammad. So God revealed: Call them by the names of their fathers; it is more just in the sight of God. God means more just with God. Ibn Sa'd narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi regarding his statement, The way of God with those who passed on before, he said: It means that he marries as many women as he wishes. This is an obligation. This was the way of the prophets before. Solomon, son of David, had a thousand wives, and David had a hundred wives. Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, The way of God with those who passed on before, David said: The woman whom he married and whose husband was named Elias, so this is the way of Muhammad and Zaynab. And the command of God is a decree decreed, similarly to his way with David, the woman, the Prophet, and Zaynab. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, he said: It was revealed about Zayd ibn Haritha. Ahmad and Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "My example and that of the prophets is like that of a man who built a house. All was finished except for one brick, so I came and completed that brick." Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “My example and that of the prophets is like that of a man who built a house, completing it and making it beautiful except for the place of one brick. Whoever entered it and looked at it would say, ‘How beautiful it is except for the place of the brick.’ So I am the place of the brick until the prophets were sealed with me.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated a similar hadith from Abu Hurayrah. Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi narrated a similar hadith, which he authenticated, from Ubayy ibn Ka’b.
33:41: His saying: 41- O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance. God, the Almighty, commanded His servants to remember Him often by glorifying, praising, extolling, and extolling Him, and everything that is a remembrance of God, the Most High. Mujahid said: It means never forgetting Him. Al-Kalbi said: It is also said to remember Him often through the five daily prayers. Muqatil said: It is glorifying, praising, extolling, and extolling God in every situation.
33:42: 42- And glorify Him in the morning and the evening. That is, declare Him free from what is not befitting of Him during the morning and the evening, which are the beginning and end of the day. They are specifically mentioned for the greater reward of glorifying Him in them. Glorification was specifically mentioned after it came under the generality of His statement, Remember God, to draw attention to its greater honor and the superiority of its reward over other remembrances. It was said that what is meant by glorifying Him in the morning is the Fajr prayer, and by glorifying Him in the evening is the Maghrib prayer. Qatada and Ibn Jarir said: What is meant are the Fajr and Asr prayers. Al-Kalbi said: As for the morning, it is the Fajr prayer, and as for the evening, it is the Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha prayers. Al-Mubarrad said: Asil is the evening, and its plural is asa’il.
33:43: 43- It is He who sends blessings upon you, and so do His angels. And the blessings from God upon His servants are His mercy and blessings upon them, and from the angels is supplication for them and seeking forgiveness, as He said, And they ask forgiveness for those who have believed. Muqatil ibn Sulayman and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The meaning is, And He orders His angels to seek forgiveness for you. The sentence is a new sentence, as an explanation for what preceded it, which is the command to remember and glorify God.
