It was said that the blessings from God upon the servant are the spreading of good remembrance of Him among His servants, and it was said that it is praise of Him, and His angels were joined to the pronoun implied in sallala because of the separation by His saying upon you, so this made it unnecessary to emphasize the pronoun with the meaning of supplication, lest a literal and a metaphorical meaning be combined in one word. The lam in to bring you out of darkness into the light is connected to sallala: that is, He and His angels take care of your affairs to bring you out of the darkness of guidance and to constantly be upon it, because they were upon guidance at the time of the address. Then God Almighty informed us of His mercy for the believers, to comfort and strengthen them, saying: And He is Most Merciful to the believers. This sentence confirms the meaning of what preceded it.
33:44: Then God, the Almighty, made it clear that this mercy from Him is not limited to the listeners at the time of the address, but rather it is general for them and for those who come after them and in the Hereafter. He said: 44- "Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, 'Peace.'" That is, the greeting of the believers from God, the Almighty, on the Day they meet Him at death, or at the resurrection, or upon entering Paradise will be His greeting them with peace from Him. It was said that what is meant is their greeting to one another on the Day they meet their Lord, "Peace." This is because He was Most Merciful to the believers, and when His mercy encompassed them, they were safe from His punishment, and they greeted one another with joy and good tidings. The meaning is: Safety for us from the torment of the Fire. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that God will keep them safe from calamities and give them good tidings of safety from fears on the Day they meet Him. It was said that the pronoun in they meet Him refers to the Angel of Death, who is the one who brings them to life, as was reported that He does not take the soul of a believer except that He greets him with peace. Muqatil said: It is the angels’ greeting of them on the day they meet their Lord, as in His statement: “And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], ‘Peace be upon you.’” And He has prepared for them a noble reward, meaning He has prepared for them in Paradise a good provision, whatever their souls desire and their eyes delight in.
33:45: Then the Almighty mentioned the attributes of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for which He sent him, saying: 45- O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness meaning over his nation, testifying for those who believed in him and had faith in him, and against those who denied him and disbelieved in him. Mujahid said: A witness over his nation by conveying the message to them, and over all other nations by conveying the message of their prophets to them, and a bringer of good tidings to the believers of God’s mercy and what He has prepared for them of abundant reward and great recompense, and a warner to the disbelievers and sinners of the Fire, and of what God has prepared for them of great punishment.
33:46: 46- And a caller to God calls God’s servants to monotheism and belief in what He has brought, and to act in accordance with what He has prescribed for them. The meaning of with His permission is with His command to him to do so and His decree, and it was said with His glad tidings. And an illuminating lamp meaning one is illuminated by it in the darkness of misguidance, just as one is illuminated by a lamp in the darkness. Al-Zajjaj said: And a lamp means one with an illuminating lamp, meaning a shining book. The accusative case of witness and what follows it is in the state of circumstance.
33:47: 47- And give good tidings to the believers is an appositive to something implied by the situation, as if he said, Bear witness and give good tidings, or Manage the affairs of the people. "And give good tidings to the believers," or it is an appositive of one sentence to another, which is what was mentioned previously. This is not prevented by the difference between the two sentences in terms of declaring and performing the command. He, the Most High, commanded him to give them good tidings that they will have from God a great bounty over all other nations. He, the Most High, made this clear by saying: "And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in gardens of Paradise, having whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.
33:48: Then the Almighty forbade him from obeying the enemies of religion, saying: 48- And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites meaning do not obey them in what they advise you to do regarding flattery in religion. The verse is an allusion to others from his nation because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is protected from obeying them in anything they want or advise him to do. The interpretation of this verse was presented at the beginning of the surah. And leave their harm meaning do not care about the harm they do to you because of the harm that befalls you in the religion of God and your severity against His enemies, or leave them alone as a recompense for the harm they do to you. The first is the verbal noun added to the subject. The second is the object added to the object. It was abrogated by the verse of the sword. And put your trust in God in all your affairs. And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs matters are entrusted to Him and affairs are delegated to Him. Whoever entrusts his affairs to Him, He will suffice him, and whoever entrusts his affairs to Him will not need anyone else. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Remember God with much remembrance, he said: He does not impose an obligation on His servants except that He has set a known term for it. Then He excused those who do it in the state of time other than remembrance, for God did not set a limit for it to reach and did not excuse anyone for abandoning it except one who is overcome by his mind. So He said: Remember God standing, sitting, and lying on your sides, by night and by day, on land and by sea, while traveling and at home, in wealth and poverty, in health and sickness, in secret and in public, and in every situation. And He said: And glorify Him morning and evening, if you do that, He and His angels will pray for you. God said: It is He who sends blessings on you, and so do His angels. There are many hadiths that have been narrated about the virtue of remembrance and frequent remembrance. A group of imams, such as al-Nasa’i, al-Nawawi, al-Jazari, and others, have compiled books on the remembrances related to the night and day. The Qur’anic verses have spoken of the virtue of those who remember God and the virtue of remembrance: And the remembrance of God is greater. It has been narrated that it is better than jihad, as in the hadith of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, narrated by Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Bayhaqi: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Which of the servants will have the highest degree before God on the Day of Resurrection? He said: ‘Those who remember God frequently.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, and who is the fighter in the cause of God?’ He said: ‘If he were to strike with his sword against the infidels and polytheists until it breaks and his blood is stained, then those who remember God would be higher in degree than him.” Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Darda’ who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest in the sight of your Lord, the highest in your degrees, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemies and striking their necks while they strike yours?” They said: What is that, O Messenger of God? He said: Remembrance of God, the Almighty and Majestic. It was also narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. In Sahih Muslim and elsewhere on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Those who are alone have outstripped others. They said: Who are the alone, O Messenger of God? He said: Those who remember God often. Ahmad, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Remember God often until they say you are crazy. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Remember God until the hypocrites say you are hypocrites. There are authentic hadiths about the merits of tasbih specifically in the two Sahihs and others. Among them is the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever says ‘Subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi’ one hundred times a day, his sins will be forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea. Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and others narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he said: ‘Is one of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds in a day?’ A man said: ‘How can one of us earn a thousand good deeds?’ He said: ‘He glorifies God one hundred times, and a thousand good deeds will be recorded for him and a thousand sins will be erased from him.’” Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Dhikr al-Mawt, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, regarding the statement, “Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, ‘Peace,’” he said: On the Day they meet the Angel of Death, there will be no believer whose soul is taken but that he will greet him. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Khatib and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “When the verse, ‘O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner’ was revealed, and Ali and Muadh had been ordered to go to Yemen, he said: ‘Go and give good tidings and do not repel, and make things easy and do not make them difficult, for the verse, ‘O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner’ was revealed to me. He said: A witness over your nation, and a bringer of good tidings of Paradise, and a warner from the Fire, and an inviter to testify that there is no god but God, ‘by His permission, and an illuminating lamp’ with the Qur’an.” Ahmad, Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar who said: I met Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-As and said: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the Torah. He said: Yes, by God, he is described in the Torah with some of the qualities that are mentioned in the Quran. O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and a protection for the unlettered. You are My servant and Messenger. I have named you Al-Mutawakkil the trustworthy. He is not rude, nor harsh, nor a loudmouth in the markets. And do not repay evil for evil, but pardon and overlook. Ahmad added: And God will not take his soul until he establishes the crooked religion, so that they say, There is no god but God, and thereby he opens blind eyes, deaf ears and sealed hearts. Al-Bukhari mentioned this hadith in his Sahih, in the chapter on sales, and he said: Sa’id narrated on the authority of Hilal, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam. He did not say Abdullah ibn Amr, and this is more appropriate, because Abdullah ibn Salam was the one who was asked about the Torah and he would inform him of what was in it.
33:49: When God Almighty mentioned the story of Zayd and his divorce of Zaynab, and he had consummated the marriage with her and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had proposed to her after her waiting period had expired as mentioned above, He addressed the believers, explaining to them the ruling on the wife if her husband divorces her before consummating the marriage, saying: 49- O you who have believed, when you marry believing women meaning you conclude a marriage contract with them. The word marriage is not mentioned in the Book of God except in the sense of a contract, as stated by the author of Al-Kashaf, Al-Qurtubi, and others. There is disagreement over the word nikah as to whether it actually refers to intercourse, or to the contract, or to both in a shared manner. The words of the author of Al-Kashshaf in this passage indicate that it actually refers to intercourse, as he said: Nikah is intercourse. The contract is called nikah because it is closely related to it, as it is a path to it. Similar to this is calling wine a sin because it is a cause of committing sin. before you touch them means before you have intercourse with them. So he used the word touch as a metaphor for that. Then you have no waiting period to count for them. This is agreed upon as Al-Qurtubi and Ibn Kathir reported. The meaning of you count for them is that you complete their number, from I counted the dirhams, so I count them. Attributing this to men is to indicate that the waiting period is a right for them, as is indicated by then you have no waiting period to count for them. The majority of scholars read you count for them with a shaddah on the dal, while Ibn Kathir, in a narration from him, and the people of Mecca, read it with a light da. There are two interpretations of this reading: One of them is that it means the first, taken from the word I’tidda you complete the number of days, but they left out the addition in order to make it easier. Al-Razi said: If it was from aggression which is injustice, it would be weak, because aggression is transitive with ala. It was said that it is permissible for it to be from I’tidda by deleting the preposition: meaning you transgress against it, meaning against the number of days metaphorically. Similar to this is his saying: She yearns and shows her longing, but I hide what would have killed me if it weren't for grief. That is, he would have decreed it upon me. The second meaning is that you transgress therein, and what is meant by transgression is what is in His statement: And do not keep them, to cause them harm, in order to transgress. So the meaning of the verse according to the other reading is: So when you have a waiting period over them, you transgress against them by causing them harm. Ibn Atiyyah denied the correctness of this reading from Ibn Kathir and said: Al-Bazzi made a mistake on his part, and this verse is specific to the generality of His statement: Divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods and His statement: And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you doubt, their period is three months. The Mut’ah mentioned here has been discussed previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Saeed bin Jubair said: This pleasure mentioned here is abrogated by the verse in Surat Al-Baqarah, which is His saying: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have specified for them a dowry, then half of what you specified. It was said that the pleasure here is more general than being half the dowry, or the pleasure specifically if it was not specified for her. So if the dowry was specified, she is entitled to half of the specified amount, in accordance with His saying: then half of what you specified. And if it was not specified, she is entitled to the pleasure, in accordance with this verse. This is supported by the saying of God Almighty: “There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them a dowry. And give them a provision, the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability.” This combination is necessary, and it takes precedence over the preference and the claim of abrogation. This verse specifies the woman whose husband has died, because if he dies after the marriage contract and before consummation of the marriage, then the death is like consummation, so she observes a waiting period of four months and ten days. Ibn Kathir said: By consensus, so the specification is the consensus. This verse has been used as evidence by those who say that there is no divorce before marriage. They are the majority. Malik and Abu Hanifa held that divorce before marriage is valid if a person says: If I marry so-and-so, she is divorced, so she is divorced if he marries her. The basis for using the verse as evidence for what the majority said is that it says: If you marry believing women and then divorce them, so he followed the divorce with marriage by saying then which indicates order and neglected and release them with gracious release, meaning take them out of your homes, since you have no waiting period for them. The gracious release here is a euphemism for divorce, but this is far-fetched because divorce has been mentioned previously and enjoyment is arranged according to it and gracious release is conjoined with it, so it must be intended to mean something other than divorce.
33:50: 50- O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their dowries. In this verse, the Almighty mentioned the types of marriages that He made lawful for His Messenger, and He began with the wives to whom He had given their dowries: that is, their bride-prices, for the dowries are the wages for giving, and giving them is either handing them over immediately or naming them in the contract. There is a difference of opinion as to the meaning of His statement, We have made lawful to you your wives. Ibn Zayd and Ad-Dahhak said: God has made it lawful for him to marry any woman to whom he gives her dowry, so the verse permits all women except those who are mahrams. The majority said: What is meant is that We have made lawful to you your wives who are with you because they chose you over this world and its adornments. This is the apparent meaning, because His sayings, We have made lawful and You have given are past tense. The restriction of making lawful to the payment of wages is not because making lawful depends on it, because the contract is valid without naming it, and a dowry equivalent to that of the wife must be paid with intercourse and a dowry equivalent to that of the wife without it. So it is as if the intention is to guide to what is better. And those whom your right hand possesses from what God has bestowed upon you, meaning the concubines who entered into his possession through spoils. The meaning of from what God has bestowed upon you is what God has returned to you from the infidels as spoils of war for their women who were taken by force and coercion. What is meant by this restriction is not that he should take out what he owned other than spoils, for it is permissible for him to have a concubine who was bought or given as a gift and the like, but it is an indication of what is better, like the first restriction which explicitly states the giving of wages. And thus the restriction of the emigrant woman in His statement: and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, for it is an indication of what is better, and to indicate the honor of emigration and the honor of the one who emigrated. What is meant by companionship here is participation in emigration, not companionship in it. It was said that this restriction, I mean the emigrant woman, is valid and that it is not permissible for him to have a woman who did not emigrate from among them, as in His statement: And those who believed and did not emigrate - you have no guardianship over them until they emigrate. This is supported by the hadith of Umm Hani’, and we will come at the end of this discussion, God willing. The reason for singling out the paternal uncle and maternal uncle and pluralizing the paternal aunt and maternal aunt is what Al-Qurtubi mentioned, that the paternal uncle and maternal uncle in general are the generic names for poets and rajaz poets, but the same is not true for the paternal aunt and maternal aunt. He said: This is a linguistic convention, so the discussion of it came with the utmost clarity. He narrated it from Ibn Al-Arabi. Ibn Kathir said: He used the singular form for the male because of its nobility, and the plural for the female, as in His statement: on the right and the left, and His statement: He brings them out from darkness into the light, and He made darkness and light. And there are many similar examples. Al-Naysaburi said: Rather, the paternal uncle and maternal uncle were not included because their nationality is sufficient, although the inclusion of daughters is indicative of that, since two sisters under one parent are not permitted. This abbreviation in the case of the paternal aunt and maternal aunt is not appropriate because a misconception may have preceded that the ta’ in both of them indicates unity. End quote. Each of these aspects is open to discussion and opposition, the best of which is the justification for the inclusion of the paternal aunt and maternal aunt by the misconception that the ta’ indicates unity. There is nothing in the case of the paternal uncle and maternal uncle that would precede the misconception that they are intended to mean unity except the mere singular form, which does not necessitate that after its addition to what is established from the generality of the nouns of the added genders. However, this better aspect is not free from the taint of discussion. And a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet is conjoined with the object of We have made lawful: that is, We have made lawful for you a woman who believes in monotheism if she gives herself to you without a dowry. As for the one who is not a believer, she is not lawful for you merely by virtue of her gift. For this reason, He said, If the Prophet wishes to marry her, meaning to make her his wife and take possession of her private parts by that gift without a dowry. It has been said that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not marry any of those who offered themselves as a gift and he did not have any of them. It has also been said that he had one of them, Khawlah bint Hakim, as in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Aisha. Qatadah said: She is Maymunah bint Al-Harith. Al-Sha’bi said: She is Zaynab bint Khuzaymah Al-Ansariyyah, the mother of the poor. Ali bin Al-Hussein, Al-Dahhak, and Muqatil said: She is Umm Sharik bint Jabir Al-Asadiyyah. Urwah bin Al-Zubayr said: She is Umm Hakim bint Al-Awqas Al-Sulamiyyah. Then God, the Almighty, made it clear that this type of marriage was specific to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and was not permissible for anyone else from his nation, as He said: Purely for you, not for the believers. That is, this pure permissibility is specific to you and not for any other believer. The word purely is either a description of woman, as Al-Zajjaj said. Or it is a confirmed source like God’s promise, meaning purely for you. The majority of scholars read and woman in the accusative case. Abu Haywah read it in the nominative case as a subject. The majority of scholars read if you give with a kasra on in. Abu, Al-Hasan, and Isa bin Omar read it with a fat-ha as a subject. The majority read khalisah in the accusative case, and it was read in the nominative case as an attribute of a woman, according to the reading of those who read woman in the nominative case. The scholars have agreed that this is specific to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and that it is not permissible for anyone else. We do not contract marriage by a woman gifting herself, except what was narrated from Abu Hanifa that this is specific to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. For this reason, he said: We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives, meaning what God, the Exalted, has enjoined upon the believers concerning their wives of the conditions and rights of the marriage contract. This is a right imposed upon them and it is not permissible for them to fail in it, nor to follow the example of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, in what God has made specific to him as an expansion and honor for him. They may not marry except four with a dowry, a witness, and a guardian. and those whom your right hands possess, meaning, We have known what We have enjoined upon them concerning those whom their right hands possess, such that they are among those who may be taken captive or free, not those who may not be taken captive or who have a covenant with the Muslims, so that there will be no blame upon you. The commentators said: This goes back to the beginning of the verse: i.e., We have made lawful to you your wives, and those your right hand possesses, and those gifted, so that there will be no difficulty for you. So the lam is related to We have made lawful. It was said that it is related to pure. The first is more appropriate, and difficulty means narrowness: i.e., We have made it easy for you in making it lawful for you so that your chest will not be constricted, and you will think that you have sinned in some of the wives. And God is Forgiving and Merciful. He forgives sins and has mercy on His servants. Therefore, He made the matter broad and did not make it narrow.
33:51: 51- "You may postpone whomever you wish of them. Tarja" is read with a hamza and without a hamza, and they are two dialects. Irja' means delay. It is said: "I postponed the matter and Irajtuhu": if you postponed it. "And you may take whomever you wish" means you may take her with you. It is said: "Awahu ilayhi" with a long vowel: he took her with him, and "Awa" without a short vowel: meaning he took her with him. The meaning is that God has given His Messenger plenty of space and given him the choice regarding his wives. He may delay whomever he wishes of them, delay her turn, leave her, and not have intercourse with her without a divorce. He may take with him whomever he wishes of them, sleep with her, and spend the night with her. The division of time was obligatory upon him until this verse was revealed, so the obligation was lifted and the choice became his. Among those whom he gave refuge to were Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Salama, and Zaynab. Among those whom he postponed were Sawda, Juwayriyya, Umm Habiba, Maymunah, and Safiyya. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) treated equally among those whom he gave refuge in the division, and he would divide what he wished for those whom he postponed. This is the opinion of the majority of commentators concerning the meaning of the verse, and it is what is indicated by the established evidence in Sahih al-Bukhari and other sources. It was said that this verse refers to women who give themselves as wives, not to other wives. This was said by al-Sha'bi and others. It was also said that the meaning of the verse is about al-Talaq 65:that is, you may divorce whomever you wish of them and keep whomever you wish. Al-Hasan said: The meaning is: you may marry whomever you wish of the women of your community and refrain from marrying whomever you wish of them. It was also said that this verse abrogates the statement: "It is not lawful for you Others after that" 10:17, and we will explain that later: "And if you seek of those whom you have set aside, there is no blame upon you." Seeking means seeking, and setting aside means removing. The meaning is that if someone wants to take in another woman from those whom he has set aside from the division of the marriage and take her into his care, there is no blame on him for that. The gist is that God, the Exalted, delegated the matter to His Messenger to do with his wives as he wished, by advancing or delaying, separating or keeping, taking into care those whom he postponed, and postponing those whom he took into care. He did whatever he wished in their matter, making things easier for him and removing any hardship from him. Its root is jinnah inclination, it is said that the ship slanted: if it tilted. The meaning is: there is no blame or reproach upon you for what you did, and the reference in His saying: that is to what came before of delegating it to His will, and it is the subject and its predicate is that their eyes may be comforted, meaning that the delegation that We delegated to you is closer to their satisfaction because it is the decree of God, the Most High. Qatada said: meaning that the choice that We gave you in their company is closer to their satisfaction because it is from Us, because if they knew that it is from God, their eyes will be comforted. The majority read tagrur in the active form, attributed to ayhinna. Ibn Muhaisin read tagrur with a damma on the ta’ of aqrara and its subject is the pronoun for the second person addressee and the accusative of ayhinna as the object, and some read it in the passive form. The meaning of "coolness of the eye" has already been explained in Surah Maryam. "And the meaning of not grieve" is not to be affected by sadness with them because of your influencing some of them over others. "And be satisfied with what You have given them all" meaning they are all satisfied with what You have given them of closeness, postponement, isolation, and shelter. The majority of scholars read "all of them in the nominative case to emphasize the agent of are satisfied. Abu Iyas read it in the accusative case to emphasize the object pronoun in you have given them. And God knows what is in your hearts" of everything that you conceal, including what you conceal regarding women's affairs. "And God is Knowing" of everything; nothing is hidden from Him. "Forbearing" He does not hasten punishment for the disobedient.
33:52: 52- It is not lawful for you to have women after this. The majority read it is not lawful with a subjunctive ending to separate the verb from its feminine subject, while Ibn Kathir read it with a superjunctive ending. Scholars have differed in their interpretation of this verse, with several opinions: The first is that it is definitive, and that it was forbidden for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to marry other wives besides his own as a reward for what they did, by the choice of God and His Messenger and the Hereafter, when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gave them the choice by God’s command to do so. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Ubayy ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn Hisham, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Jarir. Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunaif said: When God forbade them from marrying after him, it was also forbidden for him to marry anyone other than them. Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Ikrimah, and Abu Razin said: The meaning is: It is not permissible for you to marry other women after the categories that God has named. Al-Qurtubi said: This is the preferred opinion of Ibn Jarir. It was also said that it is not permissible for you to marry Jewish or Christian women because they cannot be described as the Mothers of the Believers. This opinion is flawed because the meaning would be: It is not permissible for you to marry other women after the Muslim women, and it is not permissible for Muslim women to be mentioned. It was said that this verse was abrogated by the Sunnah and by the Almighty’s saying: You may defer from them whom you wish and take to yourself whom you wish. This is what Aisha, Umm Salamah, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ali ibn al-Husayn and others said, and this is the most correct opinion. Evidence to support this will come at the end of the research: nor that you exchange them for other wives, meaning that you may be exchanged. So one of the two ta’s was deleted, meaning that you do not have the right to divorce one or more of them and marry another woman instead of the one you divorced. The min in the phrase of other wives is added for emphasis. Ibn Zayd said: This is something the Arabs used to do, saying: Take my wife and give me your wife. An-Nahhas and Ibn Jarir denied what Ibn Zayd mentioned. Ibn Jarir said: The Arabs never did this. This denial is refuted by what Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The exchange in the pre-Islamic era was for a man to say to another: Give me your wife and I will give you my wife. So God, the Almighty, revealed: nor that you exchange them for other wives. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from him. The phrase even if their beauty pleases you is in the accusative case as a state of the agent of the verb to change. The meaning is that it is not permissible to change your wives even if you are pleased with the beauty of someone other than them whom you want to replace with one of them. This change is also among the things that God abrogated with regard to His Messenger according to the most correct opinion. His statement, except what your right hand possesses, is an exception from women because it includes free women and slave women. Scholars have differed regarding the permissibility of marrying a non-Muslim woman. The first opinion is that it is permissible for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) due to the generality of this verse. This is the view of Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ata' and Al-Hakam. The second opinion is that it is not permissible for him, as he is too high to be intimate with a non-Muslim woman. The first opinion is preferred due to the generality of this verse. The justification for prohibiting marriage based on being pure is weak, as one cannot be pure from what God has permitted. What He has permitted is good, not impure, with regard to matters of marriage, not anything else. Polytheists are impure according to the text of the Qur'an. The second opinion can be supported by the statement of God swt: And do not hold fast to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women, as this is a general prohibition. And God is ever, over all things, a Watcher, meaning He is Watchful, Preserving, and Dominating. Nothing is hidden from Him and nothing escapes Him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, the Most High, When you marry believing women, he said: This is about a man who marries a woman, then divorces her before touching her. If he divorces her once, she is separated from him and there is no waiting period for her to marry whomever she wants. Then He said, Then provide for them and set them free with gracious freedom, meaning: If he specified a dowry for her, then she is only entitled to half. If he did not specify a dowry, then he should provide for her according to his ease or difficulty, and this is a gracious freedom. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: When you marry believing women and then divorce them, is abrogated by the abrogation in Surat al-Baqarah, then give half of what you specified. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab. Abdur-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: It reached Ibn Abbas that Ibn Masoud said: If a man divorces a woman before marrying her, it is permissible. Ibn Abbas said: He made a mistake in this, for God says: If you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, and He did not say: If you divorce believing women and then marry them. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited this verse and said: There is no divorce until there is marriage. There are hadiths that state there is no divorce except after marriage, and they are well known. Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it narrated it and he authenticated it, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated it on the authority of Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) proposed marriage to me, so I apologized to him and he excused me. Then God revealed, O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to His saying, They emigrated with you. She said, I was not lawful to him because I did not emigrate with him; I was among those who were freed. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from another chain of transmission on her authority that she said, "This verse was revealed concerning, 'And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you.'" The Prophet wanted to marry me, but he was forbidden from marrying me because I did not emigrate. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying, Indeed, We have made lawful to you your wives to His saying, Purely for you, he said, "So God forbade him other women. Before that, he would marry any women he wanted, but that was not forbidden to him. His wives found that very difficult to marry any women he liked. But when the verse, "I have forbidden you [to marry] other women, other than what I have related to you," was revealed, his wives were amazed at that. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sunan narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The one who offered herself to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was Khawlah bint Hakim. Abd Al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Urwah that Khawlah bint Hakim was among those who offered themselves to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, Umar bin Al-Hakam, and Abdullah bin Ubaydah that they said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married thirteen women: six from Quraysh, two from Banu Hilal bin Amir: Maymunah bint Al-Harith, who offered herself to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Zaynab Umm Al-Masakin, Al-Amiriya, who chose this world, a woman from Banu Al-Jun, who sought refuge from him, Zaynab bint Jahsh Al-Asadiyya, and the two captives: Safiyya bint Huyayy, and Juwayriya bint Al-Harith Al-Khuza’iyya. Al-Bukhari and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: A woman came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Prophet of God, do you have a need? Anas’ daughter said: How modest she was! He said: She is better than you. She desired the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and offered herself to him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d al-Sa’idi that a woman came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and offered herself to him, but they remained silent in full. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding the statement: We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives, that he said: God enjoined upon them that there is no marriage except with a guardian and two witnesses. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar and added: and a dowry. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade having intercourse with a pregnant woman until she gives birth, and with a menstruating woman until she has been cleansed by one menstrual cycle. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: You may delay [the marriage of] any of them you wish, that he said: You may delay. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him regarding the statement: You may delay whomever you wish of them, meaning: You may release whomever you wish of them, and keep whomever you like. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Aisha who said: “I used to be jealous of those who offered themselves to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and I used to say: ‘A woman may offer herself.’ But when God revealed the verse: “You may delay whomever you wish of them,” I said: I see that your Lord is quick to fulfill your desires. Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Razin who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wanted to divorce some of their wives, but when they saw that, they came to him and said: ‘He will not let us go while you are free of what is between us and you. Assign to us whatever you wish of yourself and your wealth.’ So God revealed: “You may delay whomever you wish of them,” meaning: You may remove whomever you wish. So he delayed some of them and took in some women. Among those who deferred marriage were Maymunah, Juwayriyyah, Umm Habibah, Safiyyah and Sawdah, and he would divide among them whatever he wished of himself and his wealth. He was among those who sheltered Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Salamah and Zainab, and he would divide his wealth and his wealth equally among them. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to ask permission from us on Women’s Day after the verse was revealed: You may defer whomever you wish of them. I said to her: What did you say? She said: “I used to say: ‘If that is up to me, then I do not want to favor anyone over you.’” Al-Ruwayani, Al-Darimi, Ibn Sa’d, Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id Al-Musnad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ziyad, a man from the Ansar, who said: “I said to Ubayy ibn Ka’b: ‘Do you think that if the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) died, would it not be permissible for him to marry again?’ He said: “What prevents him from doing that?” I said: His statement: It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that. He said: He only made lawful for him a type of women and described their validity to him, saying: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives until His saying: and a believing woman. Then He said: It is not lawful for you to marry other women after this description. Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade all kinds of women except believing emigrant women. He said: It is not lawful for you to marry other wives after that, even if their beauty pleases you, except those whom your right hand possesses. So he made lawful for him believing girls, and a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet, and he forbade every woman of a religion other than Islam, and he said: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives until His saying: Privately for you, not for the believers, and he forbade all kinds of women other than that. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) intended to marry any after his first wives. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, saying: God kept him from them as He kept them from him. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan on the authority of Anas, who said: When he gave them the choice and they chose God and His Messenger, he restricted it to them and said: It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that. Ibn Sa’d and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not die until God made it lawful for him to marry as many women as he wished, except a mahram. This is due to the statement of God, You may delay whomever you wish of them and take to yourself whomever you wish. ’ ‘Abd Al-Razzaq, Sa’id bin Mansur, Ibn Sa’d, Ahmad, ‘Abd bin Humaid, Abu Dawud in his Naskh, At-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of ‘Ata’ on the authority of ‘Aishah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not die until God made it lawful for him to marry as many women as he wished, except a mahram, due to the statement, You may delay whomever you wish of them and take to yourself whomever you wish. Ibn Sa'd narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Razin, It is not lawful for you to have women after that. He said: Of the companies, except those that are taken captive and are your right hand’s possession. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The exchange in the pre-Islamic era was for a man to say to another man: ‘Exchange your wife for me and I will exchange my wife for you’, meaning, ‘Give me your wife and I will give you my wife.’ So God revealed: ‘Nor that you exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty should please you. ’” He said: “So ‘Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ‘Aishah was with him. He entered without permission, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Where is the permission?’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, I have not asked permission to enter upon a man from the Ansar since I became an adult.’ Then he said: ‘Who is this red-skinned woman next to you?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘This is ‘Aishah, the Mother of the Believers.’ He said: ‘Shall I not give you my wife, the best of God’s creation?’ He said: ‘O ‘Uyaynah, God has forbidden that.’ When he left, ‘Aishah said: ‘Who is this?’ He said: ‘An obeyed fool, and as you see, he is the master of his people.’”
33:53: His statement: 53- O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet This is a general prohibition for every believer to enter the houses of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) except with his permission. The reason for the prohibition was what happened from some of the Companions at Zaynab's wedding feast, and we will explain that at the end of the discussion, God willing. His statement, Unless permission is given to you is an exception devoid of the most general conditions: that is, do not enter it under any circumstances unless you are given permission. It is in the accusative case as a state: that is, unless accompanied by permission, or by removing the preposition: that is, unless permission is given to you, or it is accusative as a circumstantial case: that is, except when permission is given to you. His statement, To food is connected to is given permission to include the meaning of a supplication: that is, enter without waiting. The meaning of waiting is awaiting. It is ripe is its maturity and maturity. It is said, Anna yanna anna if it is ready and ripe. The majority read Ghayr nadhireen in the accusative case. Ibn Abi Ubla read ghayr in the genitive case as an adjective for food. Grammarians deemed this reading weak due to the lack of a pronoun, as it is governed by something other than the one it belongs to. Therefore, it should have been said ghayrihin anha anta. Then God, the Exalted, explained to them what is appropriate in that regard, saying: {But when you are invited, then enter.} This emphasizes the prohibition and explains the time when entry should occur, which is upon permission. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The meaning of the statement is: But if you are invited and given permission, then enter. Otherwise, the invitation itself is not sufficient permission to enter. It was said that this clearly indicates that what is meant by permission to eat is the invitation to it. {So when you have eaten, then disperse.} God, the Exalted, commanded them to disperse after eating, which is to separate. What is meant is the obligation to leave the house to which they were invited after the purpose of eating has been completed. {Nor seeking entertainment for conversation.} This is in apposition to His statement ghayrihin, or to something implied: that is, do not enter and do not stay enjoying themselves. The meaning is to forbid them from sitting after eating, talking and enjoying themselves. Al-Razi said about his statement, Unless permission is given to you for a meal, either there is an order of precedence or delay in which case it means: Do not enter unless permission is given to you for a meal. In this case, permission is conditional on it being for a meal. If permission is not given to a meal, then entry is not permissible. So if someone is given permission to enter to listen to a conversation, not to eat, then it is not permissible. We say that the second is meant, so that the prohibition against entering is general. As for it being not permissible except with permission for a meal, this is because it is mentioned in the reason for revelation that the address was to a people who used to wait for the time of the meal and enter without permission, so they were prevented from entering during their time without permission. Ibn Adil said: It is better to say that the second is meant, because precedence and delay are contrary to the original principle, and his statement, for a meal is a matter of specifying the mention, so it does not indicate the negation of anything else, especially if something similar is known, since whoever is permitted to enter with his permission for something other than food ends. The first way to express this meaning that he intended is to say: The evidence has shown that it is permissible to enter his houses, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his permission for anything other than food. This is known and there is no doubt about it, as the Companions and others would ask permission to enter for anything other than food, and he would give them permission. This is known and there is no doubt about it, as the Companions and others would ask permission to enter for anything other than food, and he would give them permission. This necessitates limiting this verse to the reason for which it was revealed, which is the people who used to wait for the food of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they would enter and sit waiting to catch up with him and their likes. It does not indicate the prohibition of entering with permission for anything other than food. Otherwise, it would not be permissible for anyone to enter his houses with his permission for anything other than food. The necessary consequence is invalid, so the necessary consequence is like it. Ibn Atiyyah said: The custom of the people, when they had a feast or something similar, was for whoever wanted to come early to the invitation, waiting for the food to be cooked and ready, and likewise when they finished, they would sit like that. So God forbade the believers from doing that in the house of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the intention included all the believers, and the people adhered to God’s etiquette for them in that, so He forbade them from entering except with permission when eating, not before, in order to wait for the food to be cooked. The reference in His saying, That is you is to waiting and seeking familiarity with the conversation, and they were indicated by what is indicated to one by interpreting them with what was mentioned, as in His saying, Among those two things, meaning that what was mentioned of the two matters was bothering the Prophet because they were making the house too cramped for him and his family and talking about what he did not want. Al-Zajjaj said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would tolerate their prolonged waiting out of his generosity, and he would be patient with the harm caused by that. So God taught those who were present to behave, and it became a manner for them and for those who came after them. He would be shy of you meaning he would be shy to tell you to get up or go out. And God is not shy of the truth meaning he would not fail to explain to you what the truth is, nor would he refrain from explaining it, revealing it, and expressing it with a lack of shyness in order to be consistent. The majority of scholars read istahhaya with two ya’s. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Kathir that he read it with one ya’, and it is the language of Tamim, and they say istahha yasthay like istaqaa yastuqaa. Then God, the Almighty, mentioned another answer related to the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), saying: And when you ask them for something meaning something to enjoy, such as provisions or other things. Ask them from behind a partition meaning from behind a curtain between you and them. The word mat’a refers to everything that is enjoyed, so there is no basis for what was said that what is meant by it is a loan, a fatwa, or a copy of the Qur’an. The reference in his saying, that is to asking for the goods from behind a veil. It was said that the reference is to all that was mentioned, such as not entering without permission, and not seeking familiarity with the conversation when entering and asking for the goods. The first is better, and the demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is purer for your hearts and their hearts, meaning more purifying them from suspicion and bad thoughts that occur to men in the matter of women, and to women in the matter of men. This is good manners for every believer and a warning to him against trusting himself with seclusion with someone he is not permitted to, and speaking behind a veil to someone he is not permitted to. And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God meaning it is not right or proper for you to harm him in any way, whatever it may be, including entering his houses without his permission, staying in them in a manner other than the way he wanted, and speaking to his wives without a veil. Nor to marry his wives after him, ever meaning it is not for you to do that after his death because they are the mothers of the believers, and it is not permissible for children to marry their mothers. The reference in His statement: Indeed, that to marrying his wives after him is in the sight of God tremendous meaning a great sin and a very serious and horrific matter. The reason for the revelation of this verse was that someone said: If Muhammad were to die, we would marry his wives, and an explanation of that will come.
33:54: 54- Whether you reveal anything or conceal it, then indeed, God is Ever-Knowing of all things. He knows everything, including what you reveal about the wives of His Messenger, and what you conceal in your hearts. This is a severe warning, because His comprehensiveness of all information necessitates retribution for both good and evil.
33:55: Then the Almighty explained who is not required to cover up from, saying: 55- There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their brothers’ sons, or their sisters’ sons. So the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and other women are not required to cover up from them. He did not mention the paternal uncle and maternal uncle because they are considered to be like parents. Al-Zajjaj said: The paternal uncle and maternal uncle may describe a woman to their sons, because a woman is permissible for a paternal uncle and maternal uncle, so he thought they could see her. This is very weak, because permitting a woman to be described to someone for whom it is permissible is possible for others who are permitted to look at her, especially the sons of brothers and the sons of sisters. The implication is false, so the implication is the same. Thus, it is necessary that it is not permissible for foreign women to look at her because they describe her. The implication is false, so the implication is the same. Thus, there is no basis for what Al-Sha’bi and Ikrimah said, that it is disliked for a woman to remove her veil in front of her paternal uncle or maternal uncle. It is better to say that the Almighty limited himself here to some of what He mentioned of mahrams in Surat An-Nur, being satisfied with what came before. nor their women This addition necessitates that what is meant by women are the believers, because the disbelieving women are not to be trusted with regard to their private parts, and all women are private parts. nor those whom their right hands possess of male and female slaves. It was said that it refers specifically to female slaves, and to those slaves who have not yet reached puberty. The disagreement on this is well-known. What is sufficient has been mentioned in Surat An-Nur. Then He, the Almighty, commanded them to be pious, which is the essence of the whole matter. And the meaning is fear God in all matters, including what is mentioned here. Indeed, God is ever, over all things, a witness. Nothing is hidden from Him, whatever it may be. So He rewards the doer of good for his goodness and the doer of evil for his evil. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: O Messenger of God, both righteous and wicked men may enter upon your women, so why don’t you veil them? So God revealed the verse of hijab. In another version, Umar said: O Messenger of God, both righteous and wicked men may enter upon you, so why don’t you order the Mothers of the Believers to veil themselves? So God revealed the verse of hijab. Al-Bukhari and Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married Zaynab bint Jahsh, he invited the people and they ate, then they sat talking. It was as if he was getting ready to get up, but they did not get up. When he saw that, he got up. When some of them got up and three of them sat, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to enter and found the people sitting. Then they got up, so I went and informed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that they had left. He came and entered, and I went to enter, but he threw a veil between me and him. So God revealed the verse: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet [al-Bukhari and Muslim]. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Aisha that the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would go out at night when they wanted to defecate to the open plains, and Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Veiling your women, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would not do so. One night, Sawdah bint Zam’ah, who was a tall woman, went out to her. Umar called out to her in his loudest voice, We know you, Sawdah, out of eagerness for the veil to be revealed. So God revealed the veil, saying, O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet, [this verse]. Ibn Sa’d narrated on the authority of Anas, who said, “The veil was revealed when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married Zaynab bint Jahsh, and that was in the fifth year of the Hijra. He veiled his women from that day on, and I was fifteen years old.” Ibn Sa’d also narrated on the authority of Salih ibn Kaysan, who said, The veil was revealed for his women in Dhul-Qa’dah in the fifth year of the Hijra. Qatada and al-Waqidi also said the same. Abu Ubaidah and Khalifah ibn Khayyat claimed that it was in the third year. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God, that he said: It was revealed about a man who intended to marry one of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after his death. Sufyan said: They mentioned that it was Aisha. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: It reached us that Talhah ibn Ubaydullah said: Will Muhammad make us neglect our paternal cousins and marry our women after us? If something happens to him, we will marry his women after him. So this verse was revealed. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Eid, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah, who said: Talhah ibn Ubaydullah said: If the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were to die, I would marry Aisha. So it was revealed. Ibn Sa’d narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, who said: It was revealed about Talhah because he said: If the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) dies, I will marry Aisha. Ibn Atiyyah said: In my opinion, this is not authentic regarding Talhah ibn Ubaydullah. Al-Qurtubi said: Our Sheikh, Imam Abu al-Abbas, said: This statement has been narrated from some of the virtuous Companions, and may they never say such a thing. Rather, it is a lie in its transmission, and such a statement is only befitting of ignorant hypocrites. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from among the Companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had died, I would have married Aisha or Umm Salamah. Then God revealed: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God 2:170. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that “a man came to one of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and spoke to her, even though he was her cousin. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Do not stand in this position after today.’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, she is my cousin, and by God, I did not say anything reprehensible to her and she did not say anything to me.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘I know that, for no one is more jealous than God, and no one is more jealous than me.’ He went on and said: ‘He prevents me from speaking to my cousin so that I may marry her after him.’ So God revealed this verse, and that man freed a slave, carried ten camels in the way of God, and performed Hajj on foot, repenting for what he had said.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Asma’ bint Umays, who said: ‘Ali proposed to me, but report of that reached Fatimah, so she came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘Asma’ is married to Ali.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to her: ‘She should not harm God and His Messenger.’” Ibn Sa'd narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunaif, regarding the statement of God, Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, he said: If you speak about it, saying, "So-and-so is marrying one of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), or you conceal it to yourselves and do not utter it, God knows about it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, "There is no blame upon them," to the end of the verse, he said: This was revealed about the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "The wives of the Prophet, meaning the Muslim women, and those their right hands possess," of male and female slaves, and they were given permission to see them after the veil was imposed on them.
33:56: The majority of scholars read 56- and His angels with the angels in the accusative case, in apposition to the word that. Ibn Abbas read and His angels in the nominative case, in apposition to the place of the name that, and the pronoun in His statement, they pray refers to God and the angels. This is a great honor for the angels, as the pronoun refers to them and to God, the Most High, in one. The objection is not invalidated by what was proven from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, "When he heard the orator say: Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray, he said: You are a bad orator to the people. Say: And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger," and the reason for that is that it is not more virtuous to mention God, the Most High, with something else in one pronoun. This hadith is proven in Sahih. It is also proven in Sahih that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered a crier to call out on the day of Khaybar: God and His Messenger forbid you from the meat of domestic donkeys. Scholars have discussed reconciling the two hadiths, but this is not the place to discuss them. The verse supports the permissibility of using the pronoun for God and His angels as one. The same reasoning regarding the honor of the angels is said about the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The blame for that preacher who combined them is interpreted as meaning that he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) understood from him the intention to make God, the Exalted, and His Messenger equal, so the prohibition is specific to such a thing. This is the best that has been said about combining them. A group said: There is an ellipsis in this, and the meaning is: God prays and His angels pray. According to this opinion, the verse is not one in which the mention of God and someone other than Him is combined in one pronoun. It also does not refute what was said that prayer from God is mercy and from His angels is supplication, so how can these two different meanings be reconciled in the wording they pray? According to the first opinion, it is said that what is meant by they pray is a metaphorical meaning that includes both meanings, in that what is meant by they pray is that they are concerned with showing His honor, or they magnify His status, or they are concerned with His affairs. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah that the prayer of God, the Most High, is His praise of him before His angels, and the prayer of the angels is supplication. At-Tirmidhi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri and more than one of the people of knowledge that they said: The prayer of the Lord is mercy, and the prayer of the angels is seeking forgiveness. Al-Wahidi narrated on the authority of Muqatil that he said: As for the prayer of the Lord, it is forgiveness, and as for the prayer of the angels, it is seeking forgiveness. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said: His prayer, may He be blessed and exalted, is Subuh, Wa-Haddus, My mercy has preceded My wrath. The meaning of this verse is that God, the Most High, informed His servants of the status of His Prophet with Him in the highest assembly, that He praises him before His angels and that the angels send blessings upon him. He commanded His servants to follow that example and send blessings upon him. Scholars have differed over whether sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) is obligatory or recommended. They have agreed that sending blessings upon him is obligatory once in a lifetime. Al-Qurtubi mentioned this consensus in his interpretation. Some scholars said that it is obligatory whenever he is mentioned, while others said that it is obligatory in every gathering. There are hadiths that clearly criticize those who hear the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned and do not send blessings upon him. Scholars differed regarding whether sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) during the tashahhud of obligatory prayers is obligatory or not. The majority of scholars are of the view that it includes a confirmed Sunnah that is not obligatory. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It is recommended that no one prays a prayer without sending blessings upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). If someone omits that, then his prayer is valid according to the school of Malik, the people of Medina, Sufyan al-Thawri, the people of Kufa who follow the opinion, and others. This is the view of the majority of scholars. Al-Shafi'i held an anomaly and made it obligatory for the one who omits it to repeat it, even if he intentionally omitted it, not out of forgetfulness. This view of al-Shafi'i was not narrated from him except by Harmalah ibn Yahya, and it is not found from al-Shafi'i except through his narration. Al-Tahawi said: No scholar except al-Shafi'i held this view. Al-Khattabi, who was one of the Shafi'is, said: It is not obligatory in prayer. He said: This is the view of the majority of scholars except al-Shafi'i, and I do not know of any example for him in this regard. A group of scholars have agreed with Al-Shafi’i’s opinion, including Al-Sha’bi, Al-Baqir, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Ahmad ibn Hanbal finally agreed with him, as Abu Zur’ah Al-Dimashqi narrated. Ibn Rahawayh and Ibn Al-Mawaz from the Malikis also said the same. I have compiled a separate treatise on this issue in which I mentioned the arguments used by those who require it and the responses of the majority. The most clear evidence for the obligation is the authentic hadith with the wording: “God has commanded us to pray for you, so how should we pray for you in our prayer? He said: Say…” The hadith. This command can be used as evidence for the obligation. As for the invalidity of the prayer by leaving it and the obligation to repeat it, no, because the absence of obligatory acts does not necessitate their absence as the conditions and pillars do. Know that there are many hadiths that have been narrated about the virtue of sending blessings upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). If they were collected, they would be included in an independent book, even if the only hadiths that were authenticated in the Sahih were his statement (peace and blessings be upon him): Whoever sends blessings upon me, God will send blessings upon him tenfold. This sublime virtue and noble honor suffices. As for the description of sending blessings upon him (peace and blessings be upon him), many descriptions have been narrated in authentic hadiths in the two Sahihs and other sources. Some of these are restricted to the description of sending blessings upon him in prayer, and some are general, and they are well-known in the books of hadith, so we will not prolong the discussion. What is achieved by complying with the general command in this verse is for the speaker to say: “O God, send blessings and peace upon Your Messenger, or upon Muhammad, or upon the Prophet, or O God, send blessings and peace upon Muhammad.” And whoever wants to send blessings upon him and greet him with one of the descriptions that have been taught and guided to, that is more complete. There are many descriptions that are included in the books of the pure Sunnah, some of which will be mentioned at the end of this research, and we will discuss sending blessings upon the family of God (peace and blessings be upon him). The apparent meaning of this command to send blessings and peace was mentioned in this research, and we will discuss sending blessings upon the family of God (peace and blessings be upon him). The apparent meaning of this command to pray and greet in the verse is that the speaker would say: I prayed for him and greeted him, or praying and greeting him, or praying and greeting him, because God, the Exalted, has commanded us to pray for him and greet him. Obedience means that this should be as we have mentioned. So how could it be that we obey God’s command to say: O God, pray and greet him, by responding to God’s command to us with our command to pray for him and greet him? The response to this has been that these prayers and greetings were a great symbol of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and a noble honor, and we entrust that to God, the Exalted, and refer it to Him. This response is very weak. The best response is to say: The prayers and greetings commanded in the verse are to say: O God, pray and greet him, or something similar that conveys its meaning, as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) explained to us. This explanation in many hadiths necessitates that this is the prescribed prayer. Know that this prayer from God upon His Messenger, even though its meaning is mercy, has become a slogan for him that is specific to him and not to anyone else. Therefore, it is not permissible for us to pray upon anyone other than him from his nation, just as it is permissible for us to say, O God, have mercy upon so-and-so, or May God have mercy upon so-and-so. This is what the majority of scholars said, although they differed as to whether it is forbidden, strongly disliked, or disliked with a sense of purity, according to three opinions. Ibn Abbas said, as narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab, “It is not permissible to pray upon anyone except the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but it is permissible to supplicate for forgiveness for the Muslim men and women.” Some people said: This is permissible based on the words of God the Almighty: “And pray for them. Indeed, your prayers are a reassurance for them.” And His words: Upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And His words: It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels do. And the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, which is authentic in the Two Sahihs and elsewhere, in which he said: “Whenever people came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) with their charity, he would say: ‘O God, send blessings upon them.’ So my father came to him with his charity and he said: ‘O God, send blessings upon the family of Abi Awfa.’” The response to this is that this is an authentic slogan of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and he may specify it for whomever he wishes, and we do not have the right to apply it to anyone else. As for the words of God the Almighty: It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels do, and His words: Upon them are blessings from their Lord, this only indicates that God the Almighty sends blessings upon groups of His servants, just as He sends blessings upon those who send blessings upon His Messenger once ten times. There is no command in this regard for us, nor has God prescribed it for us. Rather, He has prescribed for us nothing but prayers and peace upon His Messenger. Just as the phrase "blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of God" is a symbol of his slogan, so is the phrase "peace be upon him". It has been the custom of the majority of this nation and the great majority of its predecessors and successors to pray for the satisfaction of the Companions, to have mercy on those who came after them, and to supplicate for God's forgiveness and pardon for them, as He has guided us to do in His saying, the Most High: And those who came after them say, Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] hatred toward those who have believed."
33:57: Then when God, the Almighty, mentioned the reverence due to His Messenger, He mentioned the severe threat to those who harm him, saying: 57- Indeed, those who harm God and His Messenger - God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter. It was said that what is meant by harm here is doing the sins they hate, because it is impossible for God, the Almighty, to be harmed. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said that they are the polytheists, Jews, and Christians who described God as having a son, so they said: Aziz is the son of God, the Messiah is the son of God, and the angels are the daughters of God. They lied about the Messenger of God, and they cut his face and broke his front tooth, and they said: He is a madman, a lying poet, and a magician. Al-Qurtubi said: This is what the majority of scholars said. Ikrimah said: Harming God, the Almighty, is by making pictures and exposing oneself to doing what only God does by carving pictures and other things. A group said: The verse has an omitted noun, and the meaning is that those who harm the friends of God, and as for harming His Messenger, it is everything that harms him from words and actions, and the meaning of the curse is expulsion and banishment from His mercy, and He made that in this world and the hereafter so that the curse includes them in both of them such that there will not remain a time of their lives or deaths except that the curse will befall them and accompany them. And He has prepared for them along with that curse a humiliating punishment by which they will be humiliated in the hereafter, because the meaning of preparation indicates that it is in the hereafter.
33:58: Then when he finished blaming those who harm God and His Messenger, he mentioned harming the righteous servants of God, saying: 58- And those who harm believing men and believing women in any way, whether by word or deed. The meaning of for other than what they have earned is that it was not for a reason they did that would require them to be harmed and that they deserved it. As for harming a believing man and woman for what they have earned that requires a prescribed punishment or discretionary punishment or something similar, that is a right established by the Shari’ah and a matter that God has commanded us to do and urged us to do. And so it is if a believing man and woman initiates cursing or harming a believing man or woman, then retaliation against the perpetrator is not among the forbidden harms in any way, as long as it does not exceed what God has legislated. Then He informed us about what will happen to those who harm believing men and women for no reason, saying: They have borne the burden of slander and a manifest sin. That is, it is clear and obvious, and there is no doubt that it is slander and sin. The reality of slander and sin has been explained previously. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They send blessings upon the Prophet. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Dhammah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Children of Israel said to Moses, Does your Lord send blessings upon you? So his Lord called out to him, “O Moses, they have asked you, ‘Does your Lord send blessings upon you?’ Say, ‘Yes, I send blessings upon you, and so do My angels for My prophets and messengers.’ Then God revealed to His Prophet, “Indeed, God sends blessings upon the Prophet, and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said, “God’s sending blessings upon the Prophet is forgiveness. God does not send blessings upon him, but He forgives.
