As for people’s sending blessings upon the Prophet, it is asking forgiveness for him.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited, “Pray for him as God sent blessings upon him, and greet him with peace.” Sa`id ibn Mansur, `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ka`b ibn `Ujrah who said: “When the verse, ‘Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet’ was revealed, we said: ‘O Messenger of God, we have learned how to send blessings on you, but how should we send blessings on you?’ He said: ‘Say: O God, send blessings on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings on Abraham and the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.’” Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated it from his hadith with the wording: “A man said: O Messenger of God, as for the blessings on you, we have learned how to send blessings on you. He said: ‘Say: O God, send blessings on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings on the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. O God, send blessings on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings on the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ahmad and al-Nasa'i narrated from the hadith of Talhah ibn Ubaydullah who said: “I said, ‘O Messenger of God, how should we send blessings upon you?’ He said, ‘Say, “O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings upon Abraham and the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Most Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Most Glorious.”’ There are differences in the hadiths. Some say it is only for Abraham, some say it is only for the family of Abraham, and some say it is both, like this hadith of Talhah. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa’idi that they said, O Messenger of God, how should we send blessings upon you? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Say, ‘O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and his wives and his offspring as You sent blessings upon the family of Abraham. And bless Muhammad and his wives and his offspring as You blessed the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Most Glorious.’” There are many hadiths on this topic, and some of them limit it to prayer, as in the hadith of Abu Mas`ud, narrated by Ibn Khuzaymah and al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan: A man said: O Messenger of God, we know how to greet you with peace, but how should we send blessings upon you if we send blessings upon you in our prayers? The hadith. Al-Shafi`i included a similar hadith in his Musnad from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. All the instructions narrated from him (peace and blessings be upon him) regarding sending blessings upon him include sending blessings upon his family, except for a few rare hadiths. Therefore, the one sending blessings upon him should include his family in his prayers. This has been stated by a group of people, and Imam al-Haramayn and al-Ghazali narrated it from al-Shafi’i, as Ibn Kathir narrated it from them in his Tafsir. There is no need to adhere to the opinion of any person in such a matter, given that the authentic hadiths clearly state this. There is no basis for the opinion of those who say that these instructions narrated from him (peace and blessings be upon him) regarding sending blessings upon him are restricted to sending blessings upon prayer, based on the general hadiths that are restricted by that restriction, because in the hadith of Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah and others, that question of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) occurred when the verse was revealed. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Pray upon the prophets and messengers of God, for God sent them as He sent me. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, those who abuse God and His Messenger the verse, he said: It was revealed regarding those who slandered the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he took Safiyyah bint Huyayy as his wife. It was narrated on his authority that it was revealed regarding those who slandered Aisha.
33:59: When God finished warning those who harm His Messenger and His believing men and women, He commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to order some of those who were harmed to do something to repel the harm inflicted upon them, saying: 59- O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. “Min” is for partiality, and Jilbabs is the plural of Jilbab, which is a garment larger than a khimar. Al-Jawhari said that Jilbab is a covering, and it was also said that it is a veil, or it was also said that it is a garment that covers a woman’s entire body, as was proven in the Sahih from the hadith of Umm Atiyyah, “that she said: O Messenger of God, one of us does not have a jilbab. He said: Let her sister dress her in one of her jilbabs.” Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said that they cover their faces and heads except for one eye, so that it is known that they are free and so that they are not harmed. Al-Hasan said: She covers half of her face. Qatada said: She twists it over the forehead and tightens it, then folds it over the nose, even if her eyes are visible, but it covers the chest and most of the face. The reference in his saying: That is to bringing the jilbabs closer, and it is the subject and its predicate is more likely that they will be known meaning it is more likely that they will be known and distinguished from the slave women and it will appear to the people that they are free so that they will not be harmed from the side of the people of suspicion by exposing them to them, watching them and their families. What is meant by his saying: That is more likely that they will be known is not that one of them will be known who she is, but rather what is meant is that they will be known that they are free women and not slave women because they have worn clothing that is specific to free women. And God is Forgiving for what they did in the past of not bringing the jilbabs closer, Merciful to them or Forgiving of the sins of the sinners, Merciful to them, so they are included in that as a primary inclusion.
33:60: Then the Almighty threatened the people of hypocrisy and slander, saying: 60- If the hypocrites do not desist from their hypocrisy, and those in whose hearts is a disease meaning doubt and suspicion about their disorder, and the slanderers in the city from the slander they issue by mentioning false report that includes weakening the side of the Muslims and the victory of the polytheists over them. Al-Qurtubi said: The people of interpretation agree that the three descriptions refer to one thing, and the meaning is that the hypocrites have combined hypocrisy, disease of the hearts, and slander against the Muslims. So, according to this, it is from the category of His saying: To the noble king, son of the hero, and lion of the battalion in the crowded place That is, to the honorable king, Ibn Al-Hammam, the lion of the battalion. Ikrimah and Shahr Ibn Hawshab said: Those in whose hearts is disease are the adulterers. Irjaf in the language: is the spreading of lies and falsehood. It is said: he irjaf bi-kadha: if he reported something without the truth, because it is unstable and unstable report, from rajfa which is an earthquake. It is said: the earth raged: meaning it moved and shook, trembling trembling. Irjafan: is severe turmoil. The sea is called rajaf because of its turmoil, and from it the poet said: The meat is eaten every evening until sunset in Rajaf. Irjaf is the same as arajif, and they circulated something and talked about it. From this comes the saying of a poet: Even if you accuse us of being few and slandering Islam, we are a rebel and an envious person. And the other said: O son of blame, you threaten me with rumours, while in rumours you find meanness and weakness. This is because these rumour-mongers were reporting that the Muslim armies had been defeated, killed, and conquered, and other similar stories that would break the hearts of Muslims. So God, the Exalted, threatened them by saying: We will surely tempt you against them, meaning, We will give you power over them by killing and displacing them by Our command to do so. Al-Mubarrad said: God tempted him against them in His statement after this verse.
33:61: 61- Cursed are they, wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed with a utter slaughter. This implies an order to kill them and seize them: that is, this is their judgment if they persist in hypocrisy and spreading rumors. An-Nahhas said: This is one of the best things said about the verse. I say that this is neither good nor better, because his saying cursed etc. is merely a supplication against them, not an order to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) to fight them nor does he give him authority over them. It has been said that after this verse was revealed they stopped spreading rumors and God did not tempt him with them. The phrase We will surely tempt you with them is the answer to the oath, and the phrase then they will not be your neighbors therein except for a little while is conjoined with the phrase in response to the oath: that is, they will not be your neighbors therein except for a little while until they perish. The accusative of cursed is in the state of the adverbial as al-Mubarrad and others said, and the meaning is expelled wherever they are found and overtaken, taken and killed is a supplication against them that they be taken and killed a complete slaughter. It has been said that this is the ruling concerning them and not a supplication against them, but the first is more appropriate. It has also been said that the meaning of the verse is that they persisted in their hypocrisy and they had no place in Madinah except that they were expelled.
33:62: 62- It is the way of God with those who passed on before meaning that God’s way was with the past nations, which is cursing the hypocrites, seizing them, and killing them, and likewise the ruling on those who spread rumors, and it is in the accusative case as a source. Al-Zajjaj said: God made clear that those who are hypocrites towards the prophets and spread rumors about them are to be killed wherever they are found. And you will not find any change in the way of God meaning any transformation or alteration, rather it is constant and permanent with the likes of these people among the past and present.
33:63: 63- People ask you about the Hour, that is, about the time of its occurrence. It was said that those who ask about the Hour are the hypocrites and alarmists who, when threatened with punishment, asked about the Hour to deny it. And what makes you know? O Muhammad: that is, what informs you and tells you? Perhaps the Hour will be near. That is, in the near future. The word near is in the accusative case as a circumstantial word. The word is masculine because the Hour has the meaning of day or time, while the feminine gender of hour is not real. The address is to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to clarify that if it is hidden from him, he does not know its time, and he is the Messenger of God, so how about anyone else among the people? In this there is a great threat to them.
33:64: 64- Indeed, God has cursed the disbelievers meaning He has expelled them and removed them from His mercy and has prepared for them in the Hereafter, along with His curse on them in this world, a Blaze meaning a blazing fire.
33:65: 65- They will abide therein forever without interruption. They will find no protector to befriend them and protect them from its torment nor any helper to aid them and deliver them from it.
33:66: And the Day in His statement: 66- The Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire is an adverbial phrase for His statement they will not find, and it was said for eternal life, and it was said for a helper, and it was said for an implied verb, which is I remember. The majority read taqalaba with a damma on the ta' and a fatha on the lam in the passive form. Isa al-Hamadani and Ibn Abi Ishaq read yaqalaba with a noon and a kasra on the lam in the active form, which is God, the Most High. Isa also read with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the lam meaning the Blaze will turn their faces over. Abu Haywah, Abu Ja'far and Shaibah read it with a fatha on the ta' and the lam meaning it will turn over, and the meaning of this turning over mentioned in the verse is: it will turn over sometimes on one side and sometimes on another side, back to back, or their colors will change with the scorching of the Fire, so it will blacken sometimes and become white the next, or their skins will be replaced with other skins, so then they will say, 'Oh, if only we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger.' The sentence is a new chapter as if it was said, so what is their state? It was said that they say, and it is possible that the meaning is that they will say on the Day when their faces will be turned over in the Fire, Oh, would that we had… They wished that they had obeyed God and the Messenger and believed in what he brought so that they could be saved from the torment they are in, just as the believers were saved. This alif in ar-Rusula and the alif that will come in as-Sabila are the alif that occurs in pauses and grammarians call it the alif of insight, and this was explained previously at the beginning of this surah.
33:67: 67- And they said, 'Our Lord, indeed we have obeyed our masters and our dignitaries.' This sentence is connected to the first sentence. What is meant by masters and dignitaries are the leaders and commanders whose orders people obeyed in this world and followed their example. This is a strong warning against imitation, and the Noble Book contains many reminders of this, warnings against it, and warnings against it. However, this is for those who understand the meaning of God's words, follow their example, and are fair to themselves, not for those who are like cattle, who have poor understanding, increased stupidity, and extreme fanaticism. Al-Hasan and Ibn 'Amir read our masters with a kasra on the ta', the plural of masters, so it is the plural of the plural. Muqatil said: They are the ones who were fed in the Battle of Badr, and the first is more appropriate. There is no reason to specify a specific group. So they led us astray from the path, meaning from the path with what they made attractive to us of disbelief in God and their Messenger, and the path is monotheism.
33:68: Then they invoked against them in that situation and said: 68- Our Lord, give them double the punishment meaning twice the same as our punishment. Qatada said: The punishment of this world and the hereafter, and it was said: The punishment of disbelief and the punishment of misguidance. And curse them with a great curse The majority read much with a triangle: meaning a curse in great numbers, great in measure, and very effective. Abu Hatim, Abu Ubaid, and An-Nahhas chose this reading. Ibn Masoud and his companions, Yahya bin Waththab, and Asim read it with a unified ba: meaning great in itself, severe upon them, and heavy in effect. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: “Sawda went out after the veil was imposed to relieve herself. She was a large woman who was not hidden from those who knew her. Umar saw her and said: ‘O Sawda, by God, you are not hidden from us. Look how you go out.’ So I turned back and found the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in my house. He was eating dinner and had a vessel in his hand. She entered and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I went out for some of my needs and Umar said to me such and such.’ Then a revelation was revealed to him and then he was lifted from him, and the vessel was still in his hand. He said: ‘You have been given permission to go out for your needs.’” Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa’d, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Malik that he said: The wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would go out for their needs, and some of the hypocrites would approach them and cause them harm. This was said to the hypocrites and they said: ‘We only do that to the female slaves.’ Then this verse was revealed: ‘O Prophet, tell your wives…’ Ibn Sa'd narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: There was a man from the hypocrites who would harass the believing women and harm them. When someone said to him, I thought she was a slave girl, he would say, I thought she was a slave girl. So God commanded them to differ from the dress of slave girls and to draw their outer garments over themselves and to cover their faces except for one of their eyes. That is more suitable that they will be known. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, who said: God commanded the believing women, when they went out of their homes for some need, to cover their faces from above their heads with their outer garments and to show one eye. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: When this verse, And draw their cloaks over their bosoms, was revealed, the women of the Ansar came out as if their heads were like crows due to tranquility, and they were wearing black cloaks. This is how it is in al-Zawa’id with the wording from tranquility, but it has no meaning. The intention is to liken the black cloaks to crows, not to describe them as tranquility, as one says, As if birds were on their heads. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: May God have mercy on the women of the Ansar, when the verse, O Prophet, tell your wives, was revealed, they tore their cloaks and flaunted them, and prayed behind the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) as if crows were on their heads. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, who said: A free woman used to wear the clothing of a slave woman, so God commanded the believing women to draw their cloaks over their bosoms. Drawing the cloak under one’s cloak means covering one’s face and tying it over one’s forehead. Ibn Sa'd narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b, regarding his statement, If the hypocrites do not desist, meaning the hypocrites themselves, and those in whose hearts is disease, doubt: meaning the hypocrites as well. Ibn Sa'd also narrated on the authority of Ubayd ibn Jubayr, who said, Those in whose hearts is disease and the agitators in the city, they are all the hypocrites. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, We will surely tempt you against them, he said, We will give you power over them.
33:69: His saying: 69- Do not be like those who harmed Moses is their saying: He had leprosy or leprosy or some other defect, and the explanation of that will come at the end of the research, and in it is discipline for the believers and a warning to them from entering into any of the matters that harm the Messenger of God. Muqatil said: God admonished the believers not to harm Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as the Children of Israel harmed Moses. And there was disagreement about what harmed our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, until this verse was revealed. Al-Naqqash related that their harming of Muhammad was their saying Zayd ibn Muhammad. Abu Wa'il said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) divided an oath, and a man from the Ansar said: This division was not made for the sake of God. It was also said that it was revealed regarding the story of Zayd ibn Haritha and Zaynab bint Jahsh and what was heard from the people therein. The meaning of and he was esteemed in the sight of God is that he was great and esteemed in the sight of God. The esteemed person in the sight of God is the one who is of great status and high position. It was said in the interpretation of esteem that it means that God spoke to him directly. The majority of scholars read and he was in the sight of God with a noon as a metaphorical adverbial phrase. Ibn Mas'ud, Al-A'mash, and Abu Haywah read Abdullah with a unified ba' from servitude. What is in His statement: So God cleared him of what they said is the relative pronoun or the verbal noun: meaning from what they said.
33:70: Or from His saying: 70- O you who have believed, fear God meaning in every matter and speak words of appropriate justice meaning words that are correct and true. Qatada and Muqatil said: It means say words of appropriate justice regarding Zayd and Zaynab, and do not attribute to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) what is impermissible. Ikrimah said: The appropriate statement is There is no god but God. It was said that it is that which appears to be in agreement with its inner meaning, and it was said that it is that which is intended for the sake of God alone, and it was said that it is reconciliation between people. The appropriate statement is derived from aiming an arrow so that it hits its target, and it appears from the verse that He commanded them to say words of appropriate justice in all that they do and leave, so He did not specify one type over another, even if there is nothing in the wording that requires generality, the context conveys this meaning, because He, glory be to Him, guided His servants to say words that differ from the words of those who cause harm.
33:71: Then he mentioned the reward for those who obeyed the command to be pious and to speak the truth, saying: 71- He will amend for you your deeds meaning He will make them righteous, not corrupt, by what He guides them to and gives them understanding in it, and forgive you your sins meaning He will make them expiated and forgiven, and whoever obeys God and His Messenger in doing what is obedience and avoiding what is disobedience, has certainly achieved a great victory meaning he has achieved goodness with a great victory, and has attained the good of this world and the hereafter. This sentence is a new sentence confirming what came before it.
33:72: Then when He, glory be to Him, finished explaining the good that comes to the people of obedience after explaining the punishment that comes to the people of disobedience, He explained the greatness of the legal obligations and the difficulty of their matter, saying: 72- Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it. There is disagreement over the interpretation of the trust mentioned here. Al-Wahidi said, The meaning of trust here, according to all commentators, is obedience and obligations, the fulfillment of which brings reward and the failure to perform which brings punishment. Al-Qurtubi said, Trust encompasses all aspects of religion, according to the most correct opinion, which is the view of the majority. There is disagreement over the details of some of them. Ibn Masoud said: It is in the trust of money, such as deposits and others. It was narrated from him that it is in all obligatory duties, and the most important of them is the trust of money. Ubayy ibn Kaab said: It is from the trust that a woman is entrusted with her private parts. Abu Darda’ said: Covering ritual impurity is a trust, and God did not trust the son of Adam with anything of his religion except it. Ibn Umar said: The first thing that God created of man was his private parts, and He said: This is a trust that I entrust to you, so do not wear it except with right, and if you guard it, I will guard you. So the private parts are a trust, the ear is a trust, the eye is a trust, the tongue is a trust, the stomach is a trust, the hand is a trust, and the foot is a trust. He who has no trust has no faith. Al-Suddi said: It is Adam’s trust of his son Cain with his son Abel and his betrayal of him by killing him. How far-fetched this statement is! I wonder what justified al-Suddi’s interpretation of this verse. If it was due to evidence that led him to that, then there is no evidence. This verse is not a narration of past servants, so that he would have a hold on it that is more distant than anything distant and weaker than a spider’s web. If this interpretation is based on what the Arabic language requires, then there is nothing in the Arabic language that requires this and requires that this absolute trust be carried out on something that was at the beginning of this world. If this is an interpretation from him based on pure opinion, then the Noble Book is not subject to the manipulation of men’s opinions. For this reason, a warning was issued to whoever interprets the Qur’an based on his opinion. So beware, O seeker of truth, of accepting such interpretations and strengthen your hands in interpreting the Book of God according to what the Arabic language requires. It is an Arabic Qur’an as God described it. If the interpretation comes to you from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then do not pay attention to anything else. If the river of God comes, then the river of Ma’qil is invalidated. The same is true of what the Companions, may God be pleased with them, narrated from them, for they are among the Arabs, among the people of the language, and among those who combined it with the Arabic language. So you must add to what the Companion mentioned what the language of the Arabs requires. And its secrets, take this as a whole and benefit from it. We have mentioned in the introduction to this interpretation what will guide you to this. Al-Hasan said: The Trust was presented to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains. They said: What is in them? He said to them: If you do well, I will reward you, and if you do wrong, I will punish you. They said: No. Mujahid said: When God created Adam, He presented it to him, and he was asked that, and he said: I have undertaken it. Something similar to this was narrated from people other than Hasan and Mujahid. Al-Nahhas said: This is the opinion of the people of interpretation. It was said that this Trust is what God deposited in the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and all other creatures as evidence of His Lordship, that they should manifest it, so they did, except for man, who concealed it and denied it. This is what some of the theologians said, interpreting the Quran according to his false opinion. According to this, the meaning of We presented, we manifested would be. A group of scholars said: It is known that inanimate objects do not understand or respond, so life must be assumed within them. This presentation in the verse is a presentation of choice, not one of obligation. Al-Qaffal and others said: The presentation in this verse is an example: that is, the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, despite their large bodies, if they were to be made to bear a burden, it would be too heavy for them to bear the burden of the laws that contain reward and punishment. That is, the burden is a tremendous matter that the heavens, the earth, and the mountains are truly incapable of bearing. Man has been charged with it, and he is unjust and ignorant, had he been rational. This is like His statement, If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain. It was said that presented means we opposed: that is, we opposed the Trust with the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, so these things would have been too weak to bear the Trust, and the Trust would have been too heavy for them. It was also said that the Trust was presented to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains by Adam, peace be upon him, and that God commanded him to present it to them. This is also a distortion, not an explanation. The meaning of and man bore it is that he committed himself to its right, and in doing so he is unjust to himself and ignorant of what is required of him, or ignorant of the extent of what he has entered into, as Sa’id ibn Jubayr said, or ignorant of his Lord, as al-Hasan said. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of bearing it is that he betrayed it, and made the verse about the infidels, the immoral, and the disobedient. It was said that the meaning of bearing it is: he charged it and made it obligatory, or he became prepared for it by nature, or he bore it when it was presented to him in the world of atoms when the offspring of Adam emerged from his back and he took the covenant from them.
33:73: The lam in 73- That God may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women is related to carrying it, meaning that man carried it so that God may punish the disobedient and reward the obedient. Based on this, the phrase Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant is parenthetical between the sentence and its purpose to indicate that he did not fulfill his responsibility. Muqatil ibn Sulayman and Muqatil ibn Hibban said: To punish them for their betrayal of the trust, their denial of the messengers, and their violation of the covenant that they acknowledged when they were brought forth from the loins of Adam. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: These who will be punished are those who betrayed it, and these whom God will forgive are those who fulfilled it. Ibn Qutaybah said: “We have presented this to reveal the hypocrisy of the hypocrite and the polytheism of the polytheist, so that God may punish them. And to reveal the faith of the believer, so that God may accept his repentance.” That is, He will return to him with forgiveness and mercy if he fell short in some acts of obedience. That is why the word repentance was mentioned, indicating that the disobedient believer will be saved from punishment. And God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. That is, He will forgive and have mercy upon the believers among His servants if they fall short in something that is required of them. It has been said that what is meant by trustworthiness is the mind, and the most correct opinion is what we have presented from the majority. Anything other than that is not without weakness, because it does not have the Arabic meaning, nor does it apply to what the Shari’ah requires, nor does it agree with what the definition of trustworthiness requires. Al-Bukhari and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Moses was a modest, discreet man. Nothing of his skin was visible out of shyness. He was harmed by those among the Children of Israel who said that he only covered himself this way because of a defect in his skin, either leprosy, or a disease, or some other illness. God, the Almighty, wanted to clear Moses of what they said, so he was alone one day and took off his clothes at the Stone and washed himself. When he had finished, he went to get his clothes but the Stone ran after him with his clothes. Moses took his staff and asked the Stone and said: ‘My clothes, Stone! My clothes, Stone!’ until he reached a group of the Children of Israel. They saw him naked, the most handsome man God had created, and he cleared him of what they said. The Stone stood up, took his clothes, put them on, and began striking the Stone with his staff. By God, there were scars on the Stone from the marks of his striking it three, four, or five times.” Al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Anbari, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Anas. Ibn Abi Shaybah in Al-Musannaf, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Do not be like those who harmed Moses, he said: His people were upset with him because he was afflicted with diarrhoea. So one day he went out to bathe and placed his clothes on a rock. The rock came out, grabbing his clothes. Moses went out following it naked until it reached the gathering of the Children of Israel. They saw that he was not afflicted with diarrhoea. This is what he said: So God cleared him of what they said, and he was esteemed in the sight of God. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it through the chain of transmission of Al-Suddi on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Ibn Abbas and on the authority of Marra on the authority of Ibn Masoud and some of the Companions: That God revealed to Moses, I am going to take Aaron, so bring him to such-and-such a mountain. So they set off towards the mountain and there they saw a tree and a house in which there was a bed with a mattress on it and a pleasant scent. When Aaron looked at that mountain and the house and what was in it, he was pleased and said, O Moses, I would like to sleep on this bed. He said, Sleep on it. He said, Sleep with me. So when they slept, death overtook Aaron. When he died, that house was lifted up and the tree was gone and the bed was lifted up to the sky. When Moses returned to the Children of Israel, they said, He killed Aaron, and he envied him because of the Children of Israel's love for him. Aaron was the most kind and gentle with them, but Moses was somewhat harsh with them. When that reached him, he said, "Woe to you! He was my brother. Do you think I would kill him?" So when they complained against him, he stood up and prayed two rak'ahs, then he supplicated to God, and the bed descended until they saw it between the sky and the earth and believed him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: “One day the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divided a portion. A man said: ‘This is a portion not intended for the sake of God.’ This was mentioned to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and his face turned red. Then he said: ‘May God have mercy on Moses. He was harmed more than this, but he was patient.’” Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash`ari who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) led us in the noon prayer, then he said: ‘Stay where you are.’ Then he went to the men and said: ‘God has commanded me to command you to fear God and to speak words of appropriate justice.’ Then he went to the women and said: ‘God has commanded me to command you to fear God and to speak words of appropriate justice.’” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Anbari narrated in Kitab Al-Adadh on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: {Indeed, We offered the Trust} (Surah Al-Adadh: 1), he said: The Trust is the obligations that God offered to the heavens and the earth and the mountains. If they fulfilled it, He would reward them, and if they neglected it, He would punish them. They disliked that and feared it, not as a sin, but out of respect for the religion of God, they would not fulfill it. Then He offered it to Adam, and he accepted it with what was in it, which is His statement: {And man undertook it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant}, meaning, he was deceived by the command of God. Sa`id Ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Anbari narrated in Kitab Al-Adadh and Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - on his authority regarding the verse: He said: It was offered to Adam and it was said: Take it with what is in it. If you obey, I will forgive you, and if you disobey, I will punish you. He said: I accepted it with what is in it. It was only between the afternoon and nightfall on that day until he committed the sin. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir also narrated something similar from him through another chain of narration.
34:1: It is fifty-four verses It is a Meccan verse. Al-Qurtubi said that everyone said the same except for one verse about which there was a difference of opinion, which is His statement: And those who were given knowledge will see. One group said it was a Meccan verse, and another group said it was a Medinan verse. The disagreement over the meaning of this verse and about whom it was revealed will come later, God willing. Ibn al-Durais, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah Saba’ was revealed in Mecca. His saying: 1- Praise be to God. The definition of praise with the lam of specificity indicates that all individuals of praise are specific to God, the Most High, as was previously stated in the opening chapter of the Book. The relative pronoun is in the genitive case as an adjective, or a substitute, or an accusative case as a specification, or a nominative case as a subject. The meaning of To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is that everything in them is in His possession and under His control. He does with it what He wills and rules over it as He wants. Every blessing that reaches the servant is from what He created for him and bestowed upon him. So, His praise for what is in the heavens and the earth is praise for the blessings that He bestowed upon His creation from what He created for them. And when He made clear that worldly praise from His servants who praise Him is specific to Him, He made clear that the praise of the Hereafter is specific to Him as well, so He said: To Him be praise in the Hereafter. And His saying: To Him is related to the praise itself, or to what the predicate of praise is related to, I mean in the Hereafter, for it is related to a general related matter which is stability or something similar. The meaning is that to Him, glory be to Him, is the specific praise of His servants who praise Him in the Hereafter when they enter Paradise, as in His saying: “And they will say: ‘Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us,’” and His saying: Praise be to God, who has guided us to this, and His saying: Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow, and His saying: Praise be to God, who has settled us in the home of eternity out of His grace, and His saying: “And their final cry will be: ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’” So He, glory be to Him, is the One to be praised in the Hereafter just as He is the One to be praised in this world, and He is the Owner of the Hereafter just as He is the Owner of this world, and He is the Wise, who perfected the matter of the two abodes, the All-Aware of the matter of His creation in them. It was said that the difference between the two praises is that praise in this world is Worship, and in the Hereafter there is pleasure and joy, because the obligation has been ended there.
34:2: Then the Almighty mentioned some of the matters of the heavens and the earth that His knowledge encompasses, saying: 2- He knows what enters into the earth meaning what enters it of rain, treasure, or something buried in it, and what comes forth from it of crops, plants, and animals, and what descends from the sky of rain, snow, hail, lightning, and blessings, including what His angels and books send down to His prophets, and what ascends therein of the angels and the deeds of His servants. The majority of scholars read yanzil with a fatha on the ya’ and a light zay, attributed to ma. Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Sulami read it with a damma on the ya’ and a shaddah on the zay, attributed to God the Almighty, and He is the Most Merciful to His servants, the Forgiving of their sins.
34:3: 3- And those who disbelieve say, ‘The Hour will not come to us.’ What is meant by these speakers is all disbelievers, or the disbelievers of Mecca in particular. The meaning of The Hour will not come to us is that it will not come under any circumstances, denying its existence, not just its coming when they speak or when they live, with its existence being realized later on. So God responded to them and ordered His Messenger to say to them, Say, ‘Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.’ This section is to confirm the coming. The majority read for it to come to you with the superlative, meaning the Hour. Talq al-Mu’allim read it with the subordinate, interpreting the Hour as the day or time. Talq said: I heard our sheikhs read it with the letter ya’, meaning the lower one, with the meaning, as if he said: The resurrection will come to you or his command, as he said: Do they await except that the angels come to them or your Lord comes? Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read ‘Knower of the Unseen’ in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is La ya’zeb, or with the assumption of a subject. ‘Asim, Ibn Kathir, and Abu ‘Amr read it in the genitive case as an adjective for my Lord. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read ‘Allam in the genitive case with the intensive form. The meaning of La ya’zeb is that nothing is hidden from Him, nor concealed from Him, nor is anything far from Him, even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller than that “nor greater” than it except in a clear book, which is the Preserved Tablet. The meaning is: except that it is established in the Preserved Tablet, which contains the information of God, the Most High, so it emphasizes the negation of celibacy. The majority read Ya’zeb with the damma on the zay, and Yahya ibn Waththab read it with the kasra. Al-Farra’ said: “I prefer the kasra, and they are two dialects. It is said ‘azaba ya’zib with the damma, and ya’zib with the kasra if he is far and absent.” The majority read nor younger nor greater in the nominative case as the subject and the predicate except in a book, or in apposition to mithqal. Qatada and Al-A’mash read them in the accusative case as apposition to dhara, or that la is the la of exoneration whose name is built on the fatha.
34:4: The lam in 4- That He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds is for the explanation of His saying that the Hour will come to you meaning the coming of the Hour. Its benefit is that the believers will be rewarded and the unbelievers will be punished. The reference in His saying: those is to the relative pronoun: meaning those who have believed and done righteous deeds. For them is forgiveness for their sins and a noble provision which is Paradise because of their faith and righteous deeds along with the favor bestowed upon them by God Almighty.
34:5: Then he mentioned the group of disbelievers who will be punished when the Hour comes, saying: 5- And those who strive to frustrate Our verses, meaning they strive to invalidate Our verses revealed to the messengers, and they cast aspersions on them and turned people away from them. The meaning of frustrating is racing who think that they will escape Us and will not catch up, and that is because they believe that they will not be resurrected. It is said ‘ajzahu or ‘ajazuhu if he overpowers someone and outstrips him. The majority read it as mu’ajziyin incapable, while Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Mujahid, and Abu Amr read it as mu’ajziyin incapable, meaning discouraging people from believing in the verses. Those meaning those who sought it. For them is a punishment of a torment. The torment is the punishment, so min is for clarification. It was said that the torment is the worst and most severe torment, but the first is more appropriate. From that is His statement: So We sent down upon those who wronged a punishment from the sky. The majority read it as alim painful in the accusative as an attribute of rajz. Ibn Kathir and Hafs on the authority of Asim read it in the nominative as an attribute of punishment, and alim means severe pain.
34:6: 6- And those who have been given knowledge will see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth. When He mentioned those who sought to invalidate the verses of God, He mentioned those who believe in them. The meaning of And those who have been given knowledge will see is that they know, and they are the Companions. Muqatil said: They are the believers among the People of the Book. It was also said that they are all Muslims. The relative pronoun is the first object of yarā to see, and the second object is the truth, and the pronoun is the separating pronoun. The majority of scholars read it in the accusative case, and Ibn Abi Ubla read it in the nominative case as the predicate of the pronoun. The sentence is in the accusative case as the second object, and this is the language of Tamim, as they know what comes after the separating pronoun. Al-Farra' claimed that the preferred choice is the nominative case, but others disagreed with him and said that the accusative is more common. It was said that his saying: He sees is connected to to reward, and this is what Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farraa said: It was objected to that by saying: to reward is connected to his saying: It will come to you and it is not said: The Hour will come to you, for those who have been given knowledge, that the Qur'an is true. And it is better that it is a new statement to refute what those who strive in the verses say: that is, that from them indicates their ignorance because they are contradicting what the people of knowledge know regarding the Qur'an. To guide to a straight path is connected to the truth, the connection of a verb to a noun, because in its interpretation it is as in his saying: They line up and grasp meaning and grasping, as if it was said and a guide. And it was said that it is a new statement and its subject is a pronoun that refers to the subject of revealed, which is the Qur'an, and the path is the road: that is, and guides to the path of the Mighty in His kingdom the Praiseworthy with His creation, and what is meant is that it guides to the religion of God, which is monotheism.
34:7: Then the Almighty mentioned another type of speech of those who deny the resurrection, saying: 7- And those who disbelieved said, meaning some said to one another, Shall we direct you to a man? meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, who will inform you? meaning, will we guide you to a man who will tell you? meaning, will he inform you of an amazing matter and strange report, which is that when you are torn apart in every way, meaning, you are dispersed in every way and cut apart in every way, and after your death, you become ashes and dust, indeed, you will be in a new creation, meaning, you will be created in a new way, and you will be resurrected from your graves alive and will return to the forms you were in. Some of them said this to one another in mockery of what God promised them through His Messenger regarding the resurrection, and they made the speech out of amusement and laughter at what he was saying about that. If is in the accusative case with his saying you are torn apart. An-Nahhas said: It is not permissible for the agent in it to be informs you because he will not inform them at that time, and it is not permissible for the agent in it to be what comes after in because it does not work on what precedes it. Al-Zajjaj allowed the operator to be omitted, and the meaning is: If you tear everything apart, you will be resurrected or you will be informed that you will be resurrected if you tear it apart. Al-Mahdawi said: It is not permissible for you tore to work on it because it is a noun in the genitive case and the noun in the genitive case does not work on the noun in the genitive case. The root of torn is the tearing of something. It is said that a garment is torn, torn, torn, and ripped.
34:8: Then the Almighty narrated about these disbelievers that they rejected what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had promised them regarding the resurrection between two matters, so they said: 8- Does he invent a lie against God, or is he mad? That is, is he lying in what he said, or is he mad such that he does not understand what he says? The hamza in invented is the hamza of interrogation, and the hamza of connection was deleted because of it, as mentioned previously in His statement: He knows the unseen. Then the Almighty responded to what they said about His Messenger, saying: Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in torment and extreme error. That is, the matter is not as they claimed, rather they are the ones who have gone astray from understanding and comprehending the truths, so they disbelieved in the Hereafter and did not believe in what he brought them, so because of that they became in eternal torment in the Hereafter, and today they are in error, extremely far from the truth. Then, Glory be to Him, He rebuked them for their bold denial, explaining to them that this only came from them due to their lack of contemplation and reflection on the creation of the heavens and the earth, and that He who is capable of this great creation is not unable to resurrect from His creations what is less than that and return it to what it was in terms of essence and attributes.
34:9: The meaning of 9- to what is before them and what is behind them is that if they look, they will see the sky behind them and in front of them, and likewise if they look at the earth, they will see it behind them and in front of them. The sky and the earth surround them, and He is able to send down upon them whatever punishment He wills because of their disbelief, their denial of His Messenger, and their denial of the Resurrection. This verse includes two matters: One of them is that the creation that God created of the sky and the earth indicates the perfection of His ability over what is less than Him in the Resurrection, as in His statement: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? The other matter is the threat to them that He who created the sky and the earth in this form that encompasses all of the creatures in them is able to hasten the punishment for them. If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them up as He caused the earth to swallow up Korah, or cause a fragment meaning pieces to fall upon them from the sky as He caused it to fall upon the Companions of the Thicket. So how can they feel safe from that? The majority of scholars readإن َنْشعwith the letter nūn of majesty, as didَْشُفْشَنandُفَشَنُف. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read with the letter ya below the letter ya in the three verbs, meaning If God wills. Al-Kisa'i alone read with the assimilation of the fa into the ba inَْشُفْشِهِه ِهِهم. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: This is not permissible because the fa is from the lining of the lower lip and the edges of the upper incisors, unlike the ba. The majority of scholars readْشْنُانwith a sukoon on the seen. Hafs and Al-Sulami read it with a fathah. Indeed in that mentioned about the creation of the heaven and the earth is a sign that is clear and evident for every penitent servant that is, one who returns to his Lord with repentance and sincerity. He singled out the penitent because he is the one who benefits from contemplation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding His statement, He knows what penetrates into the earth, he said: of rain, and what emerges from it, he said: of plants, and what descends from the sky, he said: of the angels, and what ascends therein, he said: the angels. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, of a painful punishment, he said: the punishment is the painful, hurtful torment. And regarding His statement, and those who were given knowledge will see, he said: the companions of Muhammad. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding the verse, he said: he means the believers from among the People of the Book. And Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And those who disbelieve say, ‘Shall we guide you to a man?’ He said: The polytheists of Quraysh said that. When you are torn apart, completely. He said: When the earth consumes you and you become dust and bones and wild beasts and birds tear you apart. Indeed, you will be in a new creation. You will be brought back to life and resurrected. They said that as a denial of him. Does he invent a lie against God, or is there madness in him? He said: They said: Either he is lying about God or he is crazy. Have they not seen what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? They said: If you look to your right and to your left and what is before you and behind you, you will see the heaven and the earth. If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them up, just as We caused those who came before them to swallow up. Or cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon them. That is, pieces of the sky. If He wills to punish with His heaven, He does so, and if He wills to punish with His earth, He does so, and all His creation has an army. “Indeed, in that A verse for every penitent servant. He said: A repentant servant who turns to God.
34:10: Then the Almighty mentioned among His servants who turned to Him, David and Solomon, as He said about David, So he sought forgiveness from his Lord and fell down bowing and repented, and He said about Solomon, And We placed on his throne a body, then he repented, and He said: 10- And We had certainly given David bounty from Us, meaning that We gave him, because of his repentance, bounty from Us over all the other prophets. There are different opinions about this virtue: Some say it is prophethood, some say it is the Psalms, some say it is knowledge, some say it is strength as in His statement, And remember Our servant David, the possessor of strength, and some say it is the subjection of the mountains as in His statement, O mountains, echo with him, and some say it is repentance, and some say it is judging with justice as in His statement, O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people with justice, and some say it is the softening of iron as in His statement, And We softened the iron for him, and some say it is a beautiful voice. The first is to say that what is mentioned is what God mentioned after it from His statement, O mountains, to the end of the verse. The phrase O mountains, echo with him is understood by saying: that is, We said, O mountains. And the repentance is glorification as in His statement, Indeed, We subjected the mountains with him, to glorify God. Abu Maysarah said: It is glorification in the Ethiopian dialect. And when David glorified God, they glorified God with him. The meaning of the mountains glorifying God is that God made them capable of that, or created glorification in them as a miracle for David. It was said that the meaning of Obei is: Go with him, from ta’weeb, which means going all day long. From this is the saying of Ibn Muqbil: We caught up with the Oboa neighborhood after the sunbeam and the winged tip pushed us The majority of scholars read "Obi with a fatha on the hamza and a shaddah on the waw in the imperative form, from ta'wīb" which means to return, glorify, walk, or wail. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read "Obi with a damma on the hamza as a command from aba ya'ūb" if he returns, meaning return with him. The majority of scholars read "wal-tayr in the accusative case in apposition to fadlān" meaning: And We subjected the birds to him, because giving them to him means making them subservient to him, or in apposition to the position of "ya jibal" because it is accusative by implication, since the meaning is: We called out to the mountains and the birds. Sibawayh and Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' said: Its accusative case is based on an implied verb meaning: And We subjected the birds to him. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Nahhas said: It is permissible for it to be an accusative with it, as you say: The water and the wood were level. Al-Kisa'i said that it is in apposition to "fadlān" but with an implied omitted complement, meaning: We gave him fadl and the glorification of the birds. As-Salami, Al-A'raj, Ya'qub, Abu Nawfal, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Nasr ibn Asim, Ibn Hurmuz, and Maslama ibn Abd al-Malik read it in the nominative case, in apposition to the word "mountains, or to the implied word in obi," due to the separation between the conjoined and the word it is conjoined to. "And We made the iron soft for him, is in apposition to we gave him," meaning, We made it soft so that he could do with it as he wished. Al-Hasan said: The iron became like wax, which he could work with without fire. Al-Suddi said: The iron in his hand was like wet clay, dough, or wax, which he could use as he wished, without fire or striking with a hammer. Muqatil said the same. He would finish making the armor in part of a day.
34:11: 11- "To make long coats of mail" This has two aspects: One of them is that it is a verbal noun with the preposition omitted: that is, to work, and the second is that it is the explanation for His statement: "And We gave" and there is a problem with it because it only comes after the statement or what is similar in meaning. Some of them estimated a verb with the meaning of the statement and said the estimate is and we ordered him to work. His statement: "long coats of mail" is an attribute of a deleted description: that is, long coats of mail, and the long coats of mail are the complete and wide ones. It is said that the armor, garment, and other things are covered: if they cover everything they are on and there is a surplus of it. "And he estimated in the narrative", the narrative is the weaving of armor, and it is said sard and zard as it is said sirad and zarad for the armor maker, and the narrative also is beads, it is said sarda yasrd: if he beads, and from it the narrative of speech: if he came with it consecutively, and from the hadith of Aisha: the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not narrate the hadith as you narrate. Sibawayh said: And from it is sarid, meaning running, and the meaning of sardi armor is its tightness, and that the order of its rings is uniform and not different, and from it is the saying of Labid: He doubled his armor to live a long life, without any regrets. And the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb al-Hudhali: And upon them are two chains of command, which David made when he made the coats of mail. Qatada said: Shields before David were heavy, so he commanded that they be measured in terms of what combines lightness and strength: that is, measure what you take from these two meanings in equal measure, so do not aim for strength, for it will be heavy, nor for lightness, for it will remove strength. Ibn Zayd said: The measure that he commanded is in the size of the ring: that is, do not make it small, for it will weaken and the shield will not be able to defend itself, and do not make it large, for it will be heavy on the wearer. It was said that the measure is in the nail: that is, do not make the nail of the shield thin, for it will become loose, nor thick, for it will break the ring. Then He addressed David and his family, saying: And work righteousness, meaning righteous deeds, as in His statement: Work, O family of David, in gratitude. Then He explained the command to do righteous deeds by saying: Indeed, I, of what you do, am Seeing, meaning nothing of that is hidden from Me.
34:12: 12- And to Solomon was the wind The majority of scholars read the wind in the accusative case, assuming: And We subjected to Solomon the wind, as Al-Zajjaj said. Asim read it in the narration of Abu Bakr from him in the nominative case as subject and predicate: meaning, and to Solomon was the wind, fixed or subjected. The majority of scholars read the wind, while Al-Hasan, Abu Haywah, and Khalid bin Ilyas read the winds in the plural. Its morning is a month and its evening is a month meaning it travels in the morning a month's journey and in the evening a month like Kaaf. The sentence is either a new sentence to explain the subjection of the wind, or in the accusative case as a state. The meaning is: it travels in one day a month's journey. Al-Hasan said: He would go from Damascus in the morning and take a nap in Istakhr, and between them is a month's journey for the one who is fast. Then he would go back from Istakhr and spend the night in Kabul, and between them is a month's journey. And We made a spring of molten copper flow for him. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The yellow spring flowed for him for three days and nights like running water, and people today only work with what Solomon was given. The meaning is: We made a spring of copper flow for him as We softened iron for David. Qatada said: I ask God for him a spring that he can use as he wishes. And among the jinn were those who worked before him by permission of his Lord Min is the subject and works is its predicate, and of the jinn is related to it or to an omitted word as a state, or whoever works is conjoined with the wind and of the jinn is a state. The meaning is: And We subjected to him those who worked before him while he was from the jinn by permission of his Lord: that is, by his command. Permission is a verbal noun added to its subject, and the preposition and noun are in the accusative case as a state: that is, subjected or facilitated by the command of his Lord. And whoever among them deviates from Our command Min meaning, and whoever among the jinn deviates from the command that we commanded him with, which is obeying Solomon, We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze. Most of the commentators said: And that is in the Hereafter, and it was said that it is in this world. Al-Suddi said: God appointed an angel over the jinn who had a whip of fire in his hand. Whoever deviated from Solomon’s command, he would strike him with that whip, burning him.
34:13: Then the Almighty mentioned what the jinn did for Solomon, saying: 13- They work for him whatever he wishes. The min in His statement: of sanctuaries is for clarification. Sanctuaries in the language are any elevated place, and they are tall buildings and high palaces. Al-Mubarrad said: A sanctuary cannot be reached unless one ascends it by stairs. From this, the place where one prays is called a sanctuary because it is elevated and glorified. Mujahid said: Sanctuaries are less than palaces. Abu Ubaidah said: The sanctuary is the most honorable of the houses in the house. From this, the poet said: What if I mentioned people like sand gazelles in the shrines of kings? Ad-Dahhak said: What is meant by the niches here are the mosques, and the statues are the plural of statue, which is anything that you have likened to something: i.e., you have depicted it in its image, whether it is copper, glass, marble, or other. It was said that the statues were pictures of the prophets, angels, scholars, and righteous people, and they used to make pictures of them in the mosques for people to see and increase their worship and diligence. It was also said that they are statues of things that are not animals. This has been used as evidence that making pictures was permitted in the law of Solomon, and that was abrogated by the law of our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. The jifan is the plural of janfah, which is a large bowl. The answer is the plural of jabiyyah, which is a hole like a basin. It was also said that it is a large basin that collects water. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: It means large bowls like camel basins, in which a thousand men gather around a single bowl and eat from it. Al-Nahhas said: It is better to add the ya’ in the jawabi. Whoever deletes the ya’ says that the way of the alif and lam is to enter it with an indefinite noun and does not change it from its state. So when it was said jawabi and the alif and lam entered, it remained as it was and the ya’ was deleted. Al-Kisa’i said: It is said jabut al-ma’ and jabbatihu in the basin, meaning I gathered it. The jabbiya is the basin in which water is collected for camels. Al-Nahhas said: The jabbiya is the great pot and the great, large basin in which something is collected, meaning it is gathered. From this comes the words jabayt al-kharaj and jabayt al-jarad: I gathered them in the cloak. And qadur rasayyat Qatadah said: They are the copper pots that are found in Persia. Ad-Dahhak said: They are pots carved from solid mountains, made by the devils. The meaning of rasayyat is: fixed and cannot be carried or moved due to their size. Then, the Almighty commanded righteous deeds in general: meaning Solomon and his family. He said: Work, O family of David, in gratitude. That is, We said to them: Work in obedience to God, O family of David, in gratitude to Him for what He has given you. Or do a deed in gratitude, as it is an adjective of a deleted source. Or work for gratitude, as it is an object for it or a state: meaning grateful or a direct object. Obedience is called gratitude because it is one of its types. Or it is accusative as a source by an implied verb of the same type: meaning, give thanks in gratitude. Then, after commanding them to give thanks, He explained that those who are grateful to Him from among His servants are not many, so He said: And few of My servants are grateful. That is, those who work in My obedience and are grateful for My blessings are few. And the raising of few is as it is an advanced predicate. And of My servants is an adjective for it. And the grateful is the subject.
34:14: 14- And when We decreed death for him meaning We sentenced him to it and imposed it on him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth meaning the termite. The earth is also read with a fatha on the ra': meaning eating. It is said that the wood was eaten by the termite. The meaning of eat his staff: it eats his stick that he was leaning on. The staff is the stick in the Ethiopian dialect, or it is taken from the verb nas'at al-ghanim meaning to drive the sheep away. Al-Zajjaj said: The staff with which one drives sheep away: meaning to drive them away. The majority of recited mans'atu with an open hamza. Ibn Dhakwan recited with a silent hamza. Nafi' and Abu Amr recited with a pure alif. Al-Mubarrad said: Some Arabs replace its hamza with an alif, and he recited: If you crawl on the fork out of old age, then fun and flirting will be far from you And like the audience reading the poet’s saying: We struck him with a blow on his face, and he became humiliated and disgraced. And the same: For the sake of a rope that is not your father, you struck him with a whip, and he dragged your rope with ropes. What indicates Ibn Dhakwan’s reading is the saying of Tarafa: Amon is like the tablets of the rabbits, I forgot them on the back of a tower When he fell down, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. That is, if what they claim about knowing the unseen were true, they would have known of his death and would not have remained for long after his death in the humiliating punishment for doing the work he had commanded them to do and obeying him, while he was dead at that time. Muqatil said: The humiliating punishment is misery and hardship in work. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: In the time of Solomon, people used to say that the jinn knew the unseen. So when Solomon remained standing on his staff for a whole year, dead, and the jinn were doing those terrible deeds that they had been doing during Solomon’s lifetime, they did not notice his death until the termites ate away at his staff and he fell dead. They then knew of his death and the people learned that the jinn do not know the unseen. It is possible that the jinn became apparent from the word tabayyuna the word the thing or from the word tabayyuna the word the thing: meaning it became apparent and manifest. And an and what is within its scope are a badal ishtimal exhaustive clause from the jinn with an implied omission: meaning the matter of the jinn became apparent to the people that if they knew the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating torment. Or it became apparent that if the jinn knew the unseen, etc. The majority of scholars read tabayyuna in the active form, attributed to the jinn. Ibn Abbas and Ya’qub read tabayyuna in the passive form, and the meaning of the two readings is known from what we have mentioned. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Reply with him, he said: Pray with him. A similar narration was narrated from Abu Maysarah, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We softened the iron for him, he said: Like dough. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated, through various chains, from him, regarding his statement, And measure out the chains, he said: The iron rings. Abd Al-Razzaq and Al-Hakim also narrated from him, And measure out the chains, he said: Do not hammer the nails and widen the rings so that they become smooth, and do not make the nails thick and narrow the rings so that they break. Make it a measure. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated, through various chains, from him, regarding his statement, And We poured out for him a spring of molten copper, Al-Nahhas said: Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him, he said: Copper molten copper was not attained by anyone after Solomon, and people after him only worked on what Solomon had been given. Abd Ibn Humayd narrated from Mujahid, he said: Yellow molten copper. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawader Al-Usul on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And statues, he said: Solomon made statues of copper and said: O Lord, breathe life into them, for they are more capable of service. So God breathed life into them, and they served him. Isfandiyar was among their remnants, so it was said to David and Solomon: “Work, O family of David, in gratitude. But few of My servants are grateful.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement, like a well, he said: like a well in the ground. and firm pots, he said: its fire places are made of it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement, and few of My servants are grateful, he said: few of My servants are monotheists in their monotheism. These also narrated from him that he said: Solomon stayed on his staff for a year after he died, then he fell down at the beginning of the year, so the jinn took a staff like his staff and a beast like his beast and let it devour it for a year. Ibn Abbas used to recite, And when he fell down, the jinn became clear to him, the verse. Sufyan said: And in Ibn Masoud’s recitation, they were trotting around him for a year. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn al-Sunni, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When Solomon prayed, he would see a tree growing in front of him. He would say to it, ‘What is your name?’ It would say, ‘This and that.’ He would say, ‘What are you for?’ It would say, ‘This and that.’ If it was for planting, it would be planted, and if it was for medicine, it would be written down.” One day, he prayed and saw a tree growing in front of him. He asked it, ‘What is your name?’ It said, ‘The carob tree.’ He said, ‘What are you for?’ It said, ‘To destroy this house.’ So Solomon said, ‘O God, blind the jinn to my death so that mankind will know that the jinn…’ They do not know the unseen, so he prepared a staff and leaned on it, and God took him while he was leaning on it, and he remained dead for a year while the jinn were working, and the termites ate it and it fell, and at that point they knew of his death, and the people realized that if the jinn had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. Ibn Abbas used to recite it like this, so the jinn thanked the termites, and wherever they were, they would bring them water. Al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it from Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Al-Daylami narrated from Zaid bin Arqam, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, “God, the Almighty, says: ‘I have favored My servants with three things: I cast the beast upon the grain, and were it not for that, the kings would have hoarded it as they hoard gold and silver. I cast stench upon the body, and were it not for that, the beloved of his beloved would not have been buried. I took away grief, and were it not for that, the offspring would have been lost.’”
34:15: When the Almighty mentioned the state of some of those who are grateful for His blessings, He followed it with the state of some of those who are ungrateful for them, saying: 15- Indeed, there was for Sheba What is meant by Sheba is the tribe that is from the children of Sheba, and it is Saba bin Yashjub bin Ya’rub bin Qahtan bin Hud. The majority read for Sheba with the accusative and tanween as the name of a tribe: meaning the tribe who are the children of Sheba. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read for Sheba indeclinable with the interpretation of the tribe, and this reading was chosen by Abu Ubaid. The first reading is strengthened by his saying: in their dwellings. If it was with the interpretation of the tribe, he would have said in their dwellings. What was mentioned in the first reading is the saying of the poet: The visitors and Taym in the heights of Saba, their necks were bitten by buffalo hides. What was mentioned in the second reading is the poet’s saying: From Saba, the people of Ma'rib, who built without the flood waters of Al-Arma. Qanbal, Abu Haywah, and Al-Jahdary read "Saba" with a sukoon on the hamza, and it was also read with an alif. The majority read "fi masakinhim" in the plural, and this reading was preferred by Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. The reason for this choice is that they had many mansions and multiple dwellings. Hamzah and Hafs read it in the singular with a fatha on the kaf. Al-Kisa’i read it in the singular with a kasra, and Yahya bin Waththab and Al-A’mash read it with this reading. The reason for the singular is that it is a verbal noun that includes little and much, or a place name with the meaning of the plural intended. These dwellings that they had are what is now called Ma’rib, and between it and Sana’a is a journey of three nights. The meaning of his saying: a sign is a mark indicating the perfection of God’s power and the wonder of His creation. Then he explained this sign and said: Two gardens. Their being raised as a substitute for a sign, as Al-Farra’ said, or as the predicate of a deleted subject, as Al-Zajjaj said, or as the subject and its predicate, to the right and left. Ibn Atiyyah chose this view, and in it is that it is not permissible to begin with an indefinite noun without justification. Ibn Abi Ubla read two gardens in the accusative as a second predicate and its name is a sign. These two gardens were to the right and left of their valley, surrounding it from both sides, and their dwellings were in the valley, and the sign is the two gardens. A woman would walk in them with lumps on her head, and it would be filled with various kinds of… Fruits that fall without being touched by hand. Abdur Rahman bin Zaid said: The sign that the people of Sheba had in their dwellings was that they did not see in them a mosquito, a fly, a flea, a louse, a scorpion, a snake, or any other pest. And if a caravan came to them wearing lice, they would die when they saw their homes. Al-Qushayri said: He did not mean two gardens, but rather he meant on both sides, right and left, in each direction there are many orchards. Eat from the provision of your Lord, meaning that was said to them and there was no command, but what was meant was that they would be able to have those blessings. It was said that the angels said to them, and what was meant by provision was the fruits of the two gardens. It was said that they were addressed with that through their prophet. And be grateful to Him for the blessings He has provided you with, and work in obedience to Him and avoid disobedience to Him. The phrase a good land and a Forgiving Lord is a new sentence to explain the reason for being grateful. The meaning is: This is a good land because of the abundance of its trees and the goodness of its fruits. It was said that the meaning of its being good is that it is not salty, and it was said that it has no vermin. Mujahid said: It is Sana'a. The meaning of "And a Forgiving Lord" is that the one who bestowed blessings upon them is a Lord who is Forgiving of their sins. Muqatil said: The meaning is: And your Lord, if you are grateful therein, He will provide for you. A Lord who is Forgiving of sins. It was said that the combination of the goodness of the town and forgiveness was used to indicate that the provision may be unlawful. Warsh read "town and lord in the accusative case as an expression of praise, or as an interpretation of dwell in a town and be grateful to a Lord."
34:16: Then the Almighty mentioned what happened to them after this blessing that He bestowed upon them, saying: 16- So they turned away from gratitude, disbelieved in God, and denied their prophets. Al-Suddi said: God sent thirteen prophets to the people of Sheba, but they denied them. Wahb said the same. Then, when they turned away from being grateful for the blessing, God sent a punishment upon them, stripping them of what He had bestowed upon them. He said: {So We sent upon them the flood of the dam.} That is because the water used to come to the land of Sheba from the valleys of Yemen. They built a barrier between two mountains and held back the water. They made three gates in that barrier, one above the other. They used to water themselves from the upper gate, then from the second gate, then from the third. Thus, their wealth became abundant and increased. But when they denied their messengers, God sent a rat that tore open that barrier until it collapsed. The water entered their garden and flooded it, and the flood buried their houses. This is the flood of the dam, which is the plural of `armah, which is the dam that holds back water. Qatada and others said the same. Al-Suddi said: Al-`arm is the name of the dam. The meaning is: We sent upon them the flood of the dam, Al-`arm. Ata’ said: Al-`arm is the name of the valley. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-`arm is the name of the rat that burrowed into the dam on them. It is the one called the mole. So the flood was attributed to it because it was the cause of its flow. Ibn Al-A`rabi said: Al-`arm is one of the names of the mouse. Mujahid and Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Al-Aram is red water that God sent into the dam, splitting it and demolishing it. It was said that Al-Aram is the name of heavy rain, and it was also said that it is the name of a heavy flood. Al-Aramah originally means severity, ferocity and difficulty. It is said that someone is Aram if he became intense and difficult. It was narrated that Ibn Al-A’rabi said: Al-Aram is an unbearable flood. Al-Mubarrad said: Al-Aram is anything that is a barrier between two things.
