And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens meaning, We destroyed their two gardens that contained those delicious fruits and good kinds, and We gave them in their place two gardens in which there was no good and no benefit to them from what grew in them. For this reason, He said: of bitter food. The majority of scholars read it with the nunation of akal and without adding it to khamat. Abu Amr read it with the addition. Al-Khalil said: Al-Khamat is the arak tree, and many of the commentators said the same. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Khamat is every bitter tree with thorns. Al-Zajjaj said: Every plant that has a bitter taste that cannot be eaten. Al-Mubarrad said: Everything that changes into something undesirable is called khamat, and from this comes milk when it changes. The reading of the majority is more correct than the reading of Abu Amr. Khamat is an adjective for food or a substitute for it, because eating is khamat itself. Al-Akhfash said: The addition is better in the speech of the Arabs: such as a silk garment and a brick house. It is better to explain khamat as mentioned by Al-Khalil and others. Al-Jawhari said: Khamat is a type of arak tree that has an edible fruit. The naming of the substitute as two gardens is to imitate or mock them. Athl is the well-known tree similar to the tamarisk. This is what Al-Farra and others said. He said: Except that it is taller than the tamarisk. The singular is atlah, and the plural is athlāt. Al-Hasan said: Athl is wood. Abu Ubaidah said: It is the tree of the natar, but the first is more correct, and tamarisk has no fruit. Sidr is a well-known tree. Al-Farra said: It is the samr. Al-Azhari said: Sidrān is a wild tree that is not beneficial and not suitable for washing. It has a tarry fruit that is not eaten, and it is called the dal. The second is the lote tree that grows on water and the fruit of the jujube tree, and its leaves are a kind of lote tree similar to the jujube tree. It was said that the lote tree was described as few because there is a type of it that is delicious to eat, and this is the second type mentioned by Al-Azhari. Qatada said: While their tree was from the best of trees, God made it from the worst of trees because of their deeds, so He destroyed their fruitful trees and in their place grew the arak, tamarisk, and lote tree. It is possible that his saying few refers to all of what was mentioned from the khamt, tamarisk, and lote tree.
34:17: And the reference in His saying: 17- That is to what came before of the change, or to the source of We recompensed them and the ba in because they disbelieved is for causality: that is, that change, or that recompense is because of their disbelief in the blessing by their turning away from being grateful for it. And do We recompense except the ungrateful? That is, do We recompense with this retribution of taking away the blessing and sending down the punishment except for the extreme ungrateful who exaggerates in it? The majority read Najaazi with a damma on the lower letter and a fatha on the zay in the passive form. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Ya’qub, and Hafs read it with a noon and a kasra on the zay, indicating the active participle, which is God. Al-kufr the ungrateful according to the first reading is nominative, and according to the second reading it is accusative. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred the second reading. They said: Because before it is We recompensed them, and the apparent meaning of the verse is that only the ungrateful are recompensed, even though the people who commit sins are recompensed. Some people said: The meaning of the verse is that only the one who disbelieves is recompensed with this recompense, which is crushing and destruction. Mujahid said: The believer’s sins are expiated, and the disbeliever is recompensed for every deed he has done. Tawus said: It is the discussion in the reckoning, but the believer will not be discussed. Al-Hasan said: The meaning is that the disbeliever will be recompensed like for like, and this answer was preferred by An-Nahhas.
34:18: 18- And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed" This is connected to His statement: "Indeed, there was for Sheba" meaning, and it was part of their story: We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed with water and trees, which are the towns of Ash-Sham, "visible towns" meaning continuous. Their trade was from their land, which is Ma'rib, to Ash-Sham. They would spend the night in one town and take a rest in another until they returned. They did not need provisions to carry from their land to Ash-Sham. This is part of the story of what God had bestowed upon them. Al-Hasan said: These towns are between Yemen and Ash-Sham. It was said that they were 4,700 towns, and it was said that they were between Madinah and Ash-Sham. Al-Mubarrad said: The apparent towns are the well-known ones, and they were called apparent because they were visible. If you leave one, the others will appear to you, so they were apparent towns, meaning well-known. It is said that this is an apparent matter, meaning well-known. "And We measured the journey therein" meaning We made the journey from one town to another a specific amount, which is half a day, as the commentators said. Al-Farra' said: "That is, We made between every two villages half a day so that the afternoon nap would be in one village and the night would be in another until one reaches Ash-Sham. A person only travels excessively due to the lack of provisions and water and the fear of the road. When he finds provisions and safety, he does not burden himself with hardship, but rather stops wherever he wants. The gist is that God, the Exalted, enumerated their blessings, then mentioned the calamities that befell them, then returned to enumerating the rest of the blessings He bestowed upon them that were outside their country, such as the villages connected between them and the place they wanted to travel to. Then He mentioned replacing it with deserts and wildernesses, as will come later. His statement, Travel therein, is based on the estimation of the statement, that is, We told them to travel in those connected villages. It is a command to enable them, that is, We enabled them to travel therein whenever they wanted. Nights and days, secure, from what they feared. The accusative of nights and days is a circumstantial, and the accusative of safe is a state. Qatada said: They would travel without fear, nor hungry, nor thirsty. They would travel a distance of four months in security, not disturbing one another. If a man encountered his father's killer, he would not disturb him.
34:19: Then the Almighty mentioned that they did not thank the blessing, but rather asked for fatigue and toil 19- And they said, ‘Our Lord, extend our journeys.’ This statement from them was arrogance and tyranny because they were tired of the blessing and could not be patient with well-being, so they wished for long journeys and distance between the homes, and they asked God Almighty to make between them and the Levant a place for those connected villages with abundant water and trees, security, deserts, wastelands, and wildernesses far apart in the regions. So God answered their request and destroyed those connected villages and took away what was in them of goodness, water, and trees. So their supplication was like the supplication of the Children of Israel when they said, Call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us from what the earth grows of its green plants verse instead of manna and quails, and like the saying of Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky verse. The majority read Our Lord in the accusative case as a vocative with a genitive complement. They also read Bā'id distance. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Muhaisin, and Hisham on the authority of Ibn Amir read Ba'd with a shaddah on the 'ayn. Abu Salih, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, Abu al-'Aliyah, Nasr ibn 'Asim, and Ya'qub read Our Lord in the nominative case as Bā'id with a fathah on the 'ayn as a past tense verb in the subject and predicate. The meaning is: Our Lord has distanced our journeys. This reading was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Abu Hatim chose it. He said that because they did not seek distance, rather they sought something closer than that closeness that existed between them and Ash-Sham with the connected villages, out of arrogance, wickedness, and ingratitude. Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Isa ibn Umar read Rabbana in the nominative case with a shaddah on the 'ayn. The meaning of this reading is a complaint that their Lord has made their journeys far apart, despite them being close and connected to villages, trees, and water. This is part of their arrogance. The brother of al-Hasan al-Basri read it like the previous reading of Ibn as-Samee', raising bayna as the subject, as was said in the statement, Indeed, it has been severed between you. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj reported a reading similar to this but with the accusative of bayna as an adverbial phrase, meaning: after our journey between our journeys. An-Nahhas said: If the meanings of these readings differ, it is not permissible to say that one of them is better than the other, just as this is not said in individual narrations if their meanings differ. Rather, He informed us that they supplicated to their Lord to make their journeys far apart, and when He did that to them, they complained and were harmed. For this reason, God, the Most High, said, And they wronged themselves, as they disbelieved in God, were arrogant toward His blessings, and exposed themselves to His wrath. So We made them stories, for people to talk about their stories. Meaning: We made them stories that would be talked about after them, in amazement at their actions and consideration of their condition and fate. And We tore them apart completely. That is, We scattered them in every direction in the country completely. This sentence explains why they were made stories. When God, the Exalted, destroyed their place and took away their paradise, they dispersed throughout the country, and the Arabs began to make proverbs about them, saying: They were scattered like the hands of Saba. Al-Sha’bi said: So the Ansar went to Yathrib, Ghassan to Ash-Sham, Azd to Oman, and Khuza’ah to Tihamah. Indeed in that are signs, that is, in what is mentioned of their story and what God did to them, there are clear signs and evident indications. For every patient, grateful person. That is, for everyone who is very patient and grateful. He specifically mentioned the patient and grateful people because they are the ones who benefit from the sermons and signs.
34:20: 20- "And Satan proved true about them his assumption. The majority of scholars read he proved true with a light stress on the letter saddaqa and Iblis with a fatha, and he thought" with a fatha. Al-Zajjaj said: It is on the source: that is, he proved true about them his assumption, or he was true in his assumption, or on the adverbial. The meaning is that he thought about them that if he led them astray, they would follow him, and he found them to be so. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a direct object, or by dropping the preposition. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Yahya ibn Waththab, Al-A'mash, and Asim read "he proved true with a shaddah, and he thought" with a fatha as a direct object. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: That is, the assumption he made was true. Mujahid said: He thought a supposition, and his assumption was proven true, so it was as he thought. Abu Ja'far, Abu Al-Hajja', Al-Zuhri, and Zaid ibn Ali read "he proved true with the assumption that he thought was a substitute for he smelled" from Satan. It was said that this verse is specific to the people of Saba'. Meaning: That they changed and altered after they had believed in what their messengers brought. It was said that it is general, meaning that Iblis confirmed his assumption about all people except those who obeyed God. This was said by Mujahid and Al-Hasan. Al-Kalbi said: He thought that if he misled them, they would answer him, and if he led them astray, they would obey him, so his assumption was confirmed, so they followed him. Al-Hasan said: He did not strike them with a whip, nor some of them, but he only thought a thought due to his whispers. The accusative of except a party of the believers indicates an exception, and there are two views on this: One of them is that it refers to some of the believers, because many of the believers sin and follow Iblis in some transgressions, and no one is safe from him except a group, and they are those about whom He said, Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority. It was said that what is meant by a party of the believers is all the believers, so that the min is explanatory.
34:21: 21- And he had no authority over them meaning he had no power over them: that is, he did not force them to disbelieve, but rather he used to supplicate, whisper, and adorn them. It was also said that it meant authority and power, and it was also said that it meant proof. The exception in His statement, Except that We may know who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it is disjointed, and the meaning is: He had no authority over them, but We tested them with his whispering so that We may know. It was also said that it is connected and devoid of the most general: that is, he had no power over them under any circumstances or for any reason except to distinguish who believes from who does not believe, because He, the Most High, knew that with eternal knowledge. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is: Except that We may know that from you. It was also said: Except that you may know. It was also said: So that our allies and the angels may know. Al-Zuhri said: Except that He may know is in the passive form, and it is better to understand knowledge here as differentiation and manifestation, as we mentioned. And your Lord is Guardian over all things meaning He protects it. Muqatil said: He knew everything from faith and doubt. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi - who authenticated it - Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and others narrated on the authority of Farwah ibn Masik Al-Muradi, who said: “I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, should I not fight those of my people who have turned back with those of them who have come forward?’ He gave me permission to fight them and commanded me. When I left him, he sent after me and sent me back, saying: ‘Call the people. Whoever among them has accepted Islam, accept him, but whoever has not accepted Islam, do not hasten until I tell you.’ And what was revealed about Saba was revealed. A man said: ‘O Messenger of God, what is Saba? Is it a land or a woman?’ He said: ‘It is neither a land nor a woman, but rather a man who gave birth to ten Arabs. Six of them were considered to be on the right and four were considered to be on the wrong. As for those who were considered to be on the right, they were Al-Azd, Al-Ash’ariyyun, Himyar, Kinda, Madhhij, and Anmar.’ A man said: ‘O Messenger of God, who are Anmar?’ He said: ‘The ones among them are Khatham and Bajila.’” Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani, Ibn Adi, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas something similar but shorter. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement, the flood of al-‘Arim, that he said: The severe one. Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said: the flood of al-‘Arim is a valley in Yemen that used to flow to Mecca. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding the statement, the bitter vine, that he said: the arak tree. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him regarding the statement, And shall We reward anyone but the ungrateful? that he said: That is the discussion. Ishaq ibn Bishr and Ibn Asakir also narrated from him regarding the statement, And We placed between them, that is, between their dwellings, and between the towns which We have blessed, that is, the Holy Land, towns prominent, that is, prosperous and fertile. And We appointed therein the journey, that is, between their dwellings and the land of Syria. Travel therein, when you set out from your homes to the land of Syria from the Holy Land. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And Iblis proved true his assumption about them, Iblis said: Adam was created from dust, clay, and aged black mud, a weak creation, and I was created from fire, and fire burns everything, so I will consume his offspring except a few. He said, So his assumption about them proved true, ‘So they followed him, except for a party of the believers,’ he said, They are all the believers.
34:22: His statement: 22- "Say, 'Call upon those you claim besides God.'" This is a command to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say this to the infidels of Quraysh, or to the infidels in general. The objects of "claim" are omitted: that is, you claimed them to be gods, as the context indicates them. Muqatil said: He says, "Call upon them to remove from you the harm that befell you during the years of famine. Then God, the Exalted, answered about them, saying, They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth." That is, they have no power to do good or evil, nor to bring benefit or ward off harm in any matter. He mentioned the heavens and the earth for the purpose of generalization, as they are a container for external beings. "And they have no share in them." That is, the gods in the heavens and the earth have no share in creation, ownership, or control. "And He has no supporter among them." That is, God, the Exalted, does not have among those gods any helper to assist Him in any matter of the affairs of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them.
34:23: 23- "And no intercession will avail with Him" meaning the intercession of those who intercede with Him from among the angels and others. His statement, "except for him for whom He permits" is an exception devoid of the most general of conditions: meaning, no intercession will avail in any situation except for those who He permits to intercede from among the angels, prophets, and similar people of knowledge and action. It is known that these do not intercede except for those who deserve intercession, not for the disbelievers. It is also possible that the meaning is: no intercession from intercessors who are qualified for it will avail in any situation except for those for whom He permits: meaning for him and regarding him from among those who deserve intercession for them, not for others who are not deserving of it. The lam in "for whom" may relate to the intercession itself. Abu al-Baqa' said: Just as you say "I interceded for him, and it is possible for it to relate to benefit", but it is preferable that it relates to the omitted word as we mentioned. It was said that what is meant by his saying: Intercession is of no benefit is that it does not exist at all except for the one who is given permission, and the negation is linked to its benefit and not to its occurrence, explicitly denying what their purpose in its occurrence is. The majority of scholars read "adhan" with a fatha on the hamza, meaning that God, the Most High, gave him permission, because His name, Subhanahu, was mentioned before this. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read it with a damma on the hamza, in the passive voice, and the one who gives permission is God, the Most High. An example of this verse is the saying of God, the Most High: "Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission?" and His saying: "And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased." Then God, the Most High, informed about the fear of these intercessors and those for whom intercession is made, saying: "Until, when fear is banished from their hearts. The majority of scholars read faza'a" in the passive voice, and the subject is God, and what takes the place of the subject is the preposition and noun. Ibn 'Amir read "faza'a" clarifying the subject, and its subject is a pronoun referring to God, the Most High. Both readings are with a shaddah on the zay, and the meaning of fa'l negation, so tafze'a means removing fear. Al-Hasan read it like the majority of scholars, except that he lightened the zay. Qatrab said: The meaning of faza'a 'an qulubhim their hearts is that he removed the fear that was in them, which is fear. Mujahid said: The veil will be removed from their hearts on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning is that intercession will not be from any of those worshipped by God, from the angels, prophets, and idols, except that God, the Exalted, gives permission to the angels, prophets, and those like them to intercede for those who deserve it, and they are extremely terrified before God, as He, the Most High, says: And they, out of fear of Him, are fearful. So when He gives them permission to intercede, they are terrified because of the terrible matter and intense fear that something of God’s decrees might occur. So when the revelation descends upon them, they will say to the angels above them, who are the ones who bring them revelation with permission, What did your Lord say? That is, what did He command? They will say to them, “He said: The word is ‘the truth,’ which is the acceptance of your intercession for those who deserve it and no one else. And He is the Most High, the Grand.” So He has the power to rule regarding His servants as He wishes and to do as He wishes. It was said that this fear is for the angels in every matter that the Lord commands. Meaning: Intercession will not benefit except from the angels who are terrified today and obedient to God, excluding inanimate objects and devils. It was said that those who say: What did your Lord say? They are the ones whose intercession will be made, and those who answer them: They are the intercessors from among the angels and prophets. Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd and Mujahid said: The meaning of the verse is: Until, when the fear is removed from the hearts of the polytheists in the Hereafter, the angels will say to them: What did your Lord say in this world? They will say the truth, so they acknowledged it when acknowledgment would not benefit them. Ibn Umar and Qatadah read: faragh with a dhammah ra and ghayn from the word faragh. The meaning is: God emptied their hearts, meaning He removed the fear from them. Ibn Mas`ud read afraqa` after the fa’ with a dhammah ra, then a nun, then a qaf, then ayn from afranaqa` which means scattering.
34:24: Then God, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger to rebuke and rebuke the polytheists, saying: 24- “Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?” That is, who bestows upon you these provisions that you enjoy? Your gods do not possess even the weight of an atom. Provision from the sky is rain and what is beneficial from it, such as the sun, moon, and stars. Provision from the earth is plants, minerals, and the like. Since the disbelievers were unable to answer this question, and their minds did not accept attributing this provision to their gods, and they might hesitate to attribute it to God, fearing that the argument would be established against them, God, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger to answer this, saying: “Say: God,” that is, He is the One who provides for you from the heavens and the earth. Then God, the Exalted, commanded him to inform them that they are astray, but in a fair manner in the argument after what preceded the establishment of who is on guidance and who is on misguidance, He said: And indeed, we or you are upon guidance or in error. Mubeen meaning: that one of the two groups of those who believe in the Oneness of God, the Creator and Provider, and single Him out for worship, and those who worship inanimate objects that are not able to create, provide sustenance, benefit, or harm, is on one of two paths of guidance or misguidance. It is known to every rational person that whoever worships the One who creates, provides, benefits, and harms is the one who is on the right path, and whoever worships the One who is not able to create, provide sustenance, benefit, or harm is the one who is on the misguidance. This statement includes a clear statement of the group of guidance, which are the Muslims, and the group of misguidance, which are the polytheists, in a way that is more eloquent than explicitly stated. Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning of this statement is the meaning of the one who has insight into the argument saying to his companion: One of us is a liar. And it is known that he is the truthful one who is right, and his companion is the liar who is mistaken. He said: "And or, according to the Basrans, is in its proper place and is not for doubt, but it is what the Arabs use in such a case if the informant does not want to clarify and he is knowledgeable of the meaning." Abu Ubaidah and Al-Farra’ said: It has the meaning of and, and its interpretation is: And we are on guidance, and you are in clear error. From this is the saying of Jarir: Ath'alaba of the knights or Rabah, they were equal to Tahya and Rababa Any fox and alopecia, and so is the saying of the other: When the war became intense among us, we hoped for profit or gain. That is, and firmly. His saying: or you is conjoined with the subject of in and its predicate is the one mentioned, and the predicate of the second was deleted to indicate it: that is, we are upon guidance or in clear error, and you are upon guidance or in clear error. The opposite is permissible: that is, the mentioned is the predicate of the second, and the predicate of the first is deleted, as was mentioned previously in His saying: And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should be pleased.
34:25: Then the Almighty followed up this fair statement with words more eloquent in fairness, and further from argument and quarrel, saying: 25- Say, ‘You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you do.’ That is, I only call you to what is best and beneficial for you, and no harm will come to me from your disbelief and your failure to answer me. This is like His Almighty saying: To you be your religion, and to me mine. And in attributing the crime to the Muslims and attributing the absolute work to those addressed, with the actions of the Muslims being pure righteousness and utter obedience, and the actions of the disbelievers being clear disobedience and obvious sin, there is a fairness that cannot be measured. What is meant is: appeasement and forbearance. This verse and others like it were abrogated by the verse of the sword.
34:26: Then He, the Almighty, commanded him to threaten them with the punishment of the Hereafter, but in a way that was not explicitly stated, as He said: 26- Say, ‘Our Lord will gather us together’ meaning on the Day of Resurrection then He will judge between us in truth meaning He will judge and decide between us in truth, rewarding the obedient and punishing the disobedient. And He is the Opener meaning the Judge with truth and the Judge with what is right. The Knower of what is related to His judgment and decision of interests. This too was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
34:27: Then He, the Almighty, commanded him to present to them another argument to demonstrate their error, saying: 27- Say, 'Show me those whom you have associated with Him as partners.' That is, show me those whom you have associated with God as partners. This is the third object, because the verb is transitive with the hamza to three. The first is the ya' in 'aruni', the second is the relative pronoun, and the third is partners. The pronoun of the relative pronoun is omitted: that is, you have associated them. It is also possible that it is the Basran one, and the verb is transitive with the hamza to two: the first is the ya', and the second is the relative pronoun, and partners is in the accusative case as a state. Then He responded to their claim of partners and invalidated it, saying: No! Rather, He is God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. That is, be deterred from claiming to have partners. Rather, the One Who is unique in divinity is God, the Exalted in power and victory, the Wise in dazzling wisdom. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, He removed fear from their hearts, saying, Jali. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: When the Almighty revealed to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, he called the Messenger from the angels to send him with the revelation. The angels heard the voice of the Almighty speaking with the revelation. When He uncovered their hearts, they asked Him about what God had said. They said, The truth, and they knew that God only says the truth. Ibn Abbas said: The sound of the revelation was like the sound of iron on a rock. When they heard it, they fell down in prostration. When they raised their heads, they said, What did your Lord say? They said, The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said: The command descends to the lowest heaven with a sound like the sound of a chain on a rock. All the inhabitants of the heavens are startled by it and say, What did your Lord say? Then they come to their senses and say, The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand. Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, as if it were a chain beating a rock. But when fear departs from their hearts, they say, ‘What did your Lord say?’ They say, ‘To He who spoke the truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.’” The hadith and there are other similar hadiths. Sa’id ibn Mansur, ‘Abd ibn Humayd ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of ‘Ikrimah, regarding the statement of God, And indeed, either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error, he said: We are upon right guidance, and indeed, you are in manifest error. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Fattah means the judge.
34:28: 28- All of you has several aspects. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a state of the kaf in Arslanaka. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, We have not sent you except as a gatherer of people to warn and convey. Kafah means gatherer, and the ha' in it is for emphasis as a mark. Abu Hayyan said: As for Al-Zajjaj's saying that kafah means gatherer, and the ha' in it is for emphasis, the language does not support it because kaf does not mean gathering, rather it means preventing. It is said that kaf yakfu: meaning to prevent, prevents. The meaning is: except preventing them from disbelief, and from this comes the word kaf because it prevents the exit of what is in it. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a source and the ha' is for emphasis like the consequence and well-being, and what is meant is that it is an attribute of a deleted source: that is, except a comprehensive message. It was said that it is a state of people and the interpretation is: We have not sent you except to all of people. It was said that it is a state of women and the interpretation is: We have not sent you except to all of people. It was responded that the state precedes the genitive as is established in the science of grammar. The answer to this is that Abu Ali Al-Farsi, Ibn Kaysan, and Ibn Burhan permitted it, and from this is the saying of the poet: If a person is tired of sovereignty as a young person, then seeking it as an old person will be difficult for him. And the other said: I consoled myself with your memories, as if you were with me. And the other said: Heedless of the fact that death is exposed to a person, he is called there is no time for refusal Among those who preferred that it be a state of the majrur after it is Ibn Atiyyah, and he said: It was presented for emphasis and piety. It was said that the meaning is except for the comprehensive one: that is, the one who prevents, so the complement was deleted. It was said that the lam in for mankind means to: that is, We did not send you to mankind except to gather them with warning and notification, or to prevent them from disbelief and sins. The accusative of bearing good tidings and warning is in the state: that is, bringing them good tidings of Paradise and warning them of the Fire, but most people do not know what benefit is with God in sending messengers.
34:29: 29- And they say, ‘When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?’ That is, when will this promise that you are promising us, which is the establishment of the Hour, tell us about it if you are truthful.
34:30: They said this as a way to mock the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the believers who were with him. So God commanded His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to respond to them, saying: 30- Say to you, 'An appointed time has come for you on a Day.' That is, an appointed time has come for you on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that it was the time of approaching death, and it was also said that it meant the Day of Badr because it was the day of their punishment in this world. In any case, this addition is for clarification. It is permissible for Ma'ad to be a verbal noun meaning promise, or it may be a noun of time. Abu Ubaidah said: The promise, the threat, and the appointed time have the same meaning. Ibn Abi Ubla recited the Quran with the tanween of Mi'ad and the nominative case, and the accusative case of Day so that Mi'ad is the subject, and Day is an adverbial phrase, and the predicate is for you. Isa ibn Umar recited the Quran with the nominative case of Mi'ad and the accusative case of Day as an addition to the sentence after it. Grammarians have permitted the word meeting day to be raised with both nouns, with the definite article on the basis that meeting day is the subject and day is a substitute for it. The phrase do not delay from it an hour, nor do you advance it is an attribute of meeting day, meaning that you will not delay from this appointed time, nor advance from it, but it will inevitably be at the time that God has decreed for it to occur.
34:31: Then the Almighty mentioned some of the ugly deeds of the disbelievers and a type of their disbelief, saying: 31- And those who disbelieve say, ‘We will never believe in this Qur’an or in that which was before it.’ These are the ancient scriptures, such as the Torah, the Gospel, and the previous messengers. It was said that what is meant by that which is before it is the Hereafter. Then the Almighty informed about their state in the Hereafter, saying: And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord. The address is to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, or to everyone who is fit for it. The meaning of made to stand before their Lord is detained in the place of reckoning. They will return to each other’s words, meaning they will exchange words with each other, blaming and rebuking each other after they were hostile, supportive, and loving each other in this world.
34:32: Then the Almighty explained that review, saying: 32- Those who were oppressed will say - meaning the followers - to those who were arrogant - meaning the leaders who were followed, If it were not for you - who prevented us from believing in God and following His Messenger, we would have been believers in God, believing in His Messenger and His Book. Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed - responding to them, denouncing what they said, Did we prevent you from guidance - meaning we prevented you from believing after it had come to you - guidance? They said this, denying what they claimed against them of preventing them, and rejecting what they attributed to them of that. Then they explained to them that they were the ones who prevented themselves, who refused guidance after it had come to them, so they said: Rather, you were criminals - meaning persisting in disbelief, committing many crimes, and committing great sins.
34:33: 33- And those who were oppressed said to those who were arrogant, in response to their answer and to refute what they attributed to them of their own aversion to themselves, Rather, it is your plotting by night and by day. The root of plotting in Arabic speech is deception and trickery. It is said, He plotted against him if he deceived him and schemed against him. The meaning is, Rather, your plotting against us by night and by day. So the complement to it was omitted, and the adverbial phrase was used instead for the sake of expansion. Al-Akhfash said, On this estimation, it is your plotting by night and by day. Al-Nahhas said, The meaning, and God knows best, is, rather, your plotting by night and by day, and your calling us to disbelief is what drove us to this. Sufyan al-Thawri said, Rather, your work by night and by day. It is permissible to make night and day plotting by metaphorical attribution, as is established in the science of semantics. Al-Mubarrad said, as the Arabs say, He fasts during the day and stands in prayer at night. And he recited the words of Jarir: You blamed us, O mother of Ghilan, in the night, and you slept, while the mounts were asleep. And Sibawayh recited: Night prayers and the relief of my worries Qatada and Yahya ibn Ya'mar read the word by raising makr with a tanween, and by placing al-llil and al-nahar in the accusative case. The meaning is: Rather, it is a plot that occurs at night and during the day. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu Razin read it with a fatha on the kaf and a shaddah on the ra', adding the meaning of kurur, from kar yakkar if it comes and goes. The raising of makr according to these readings is as a subject and its predicate is omitted: i.e., the plot of night and day turned us away, or as an agent of a omitted verb: i.e., the plot of night and day turned us away, or as a predicate of a omitted subject as previously reported by al-Akhfash. Talhah ibn Rashid read as Sa'id ibn Jubayr did, but he placed makr in the accusative case as a verbal noun: i.e., you repeatedly tempt us with a constant plot that you never cease, and the raising of idh ta'amruna as an adverbial phrase for the plot: i.e., rather, your plot against us at the time of your command to us is that we disbelieve in God and make equals to Him i.e., similar and similar. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said that someone is like someone, meaning he is like him. And he recited: You make me a rival, but I have no rival to Him. The pronoun in His statement, And they concealed their regret when they saw the punishment, refers to both groups. That is, both groups concealed their regret for what they had done of disbelief and hid it from others, or each of them hid it from the other for fear of gloating. It was said that what is meant by concealed here is shown because it is an opposite that can sometimes mean concealment and sometimes show. From this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: I have overcome the guards and the horrors of the Ali clan, who are guards to conceal my death. It was said that the meaning of they concealed their regret is: regret was evident in the depths of their faces. And We placed shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Shackles is the plural of shackle. It is said, There is a shackle of iron on his neck, meaning, the shackles of iron were placed on the throats of these people in the Fire. What is meant by those who disbelieved are those mentioned previously, and the expression is for further censure or for the disbelievers in general, so these are included among them in a primary inclusion. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do? That is, except for the recompense for what they used to do of associating partners with God, or except for what they used to do, with the deletion of the preposition. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, {And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to mankind}, that he said: To all of mankind. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: God sent Muhammad to the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and the most honorable of them in the sight of God were those who were most obedient to Him. These people narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, {And those who disbelieved said, We will not believe in this Qur'an}, that he said: This is the statement of the polytheist Arabs who disbelieved in the Qur'an and what came before it of books and prophets.
34:34: When the Almighty narrated the situation of the disbelievers who came before, He exhausted His Messenger with what was consoling and clarifying that the disbelief of the previous nations in the Messengers He sent to them was a continuous occurrence in the early ages, so He said: 34- And We did not send to any city of the cities a warner to warn them and caution them of God’s punishment but its affluent ones said meaning its leaders, rich people, tyrants, and leaders of evil to their messengers Indeed, we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent meaning in what you have been sent with of monotheism and faith, and the phrase but its affluent ones said is in the accusative case as a state.
34:35: Then he mentioned what they boasted about of wealth and children and compared their condition in the Hereafter to their condition in this world, based on the estimation of what the messengers had warned them about. He said: 35- And they said, ‘We are more in wealth and children, and we will not be punished.’ The meaning is that God has favored us over you with wealth and children in this world, and this indicates that He is pleased with what we are upon of religion and that we will not be punished in the Hereafter after His kindness to us in this world and His pleasure with us.
34:36: So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer them and said: 36- Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills’ that He expands it for him and restricts it’ that is, He restricts it for whom He wills. So He, glory be to Him, may provide for the unbeliever and the sinner to lure him in, and He may test the obedient believer by restricting it to save him his reward. The mere fact that He expands provision for whom He expands it for does not indicate that He is pleased with him and his work, nor does His withholding it from whom He withholds it indicate that He is not pleased and his work is not pleased. So comparing the Hereafter to the first abode in such a case is a clear error or obvious fallacy. But most people do not know. This, and among these are most of those who compare the matter of the Hereafter to the first abode, then this answer is further supported and confirmed.
34:37: 37- And neither your wealth nor your children are the things that bring you near to Us meaning they are not the trait that brings you near to Us. Mujahid said: Zulfi means kinship and zalfah means nearness. Al-Akhfash said: Zulfi is a verbal noun, as if he said with that which brings you near to Us, so zulfi is in the accusative case. Al-Farra' said: That which applies to both wealth and children. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: It is not your wealth that brings you near to Us, nor are your children the thing that brings you near to Us. Then the predicate of the first was deleted because the second indicates it, and he recited: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs It is permissible in places other than the Qur’an to use the words allatti which, allatti which, allatti which, and alladhi which for children specifically: meaning, wealth will not increase you in degree or eminence with Us, nor will it bring you closer to Us. Except for he who believes and does righteousness is a disjunctive exception, so its place is in the accusative: meaning, but for he who believes and does righteousness, or in the place of the genitive as a substitute for the pronoun in taqarabukum drawing closer to Us, this is what Al-Zajjaj said. An-Nahhas said: This statement is wrong, because the kaf and the meem are for the addressee, so a substitute is not permissible. If this were permissible, then I saw you Zayd would have been permissible. The answer to this is that Al-Akhfash and the Kufians permit this. He said something similar to what Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra’ said. Al-Farra’ permitted it to be in the nominative case meaning except for those who believe. The reference in his statement, those is to those, and the plural is in consideration of its meaning, which is the subject and predicate. For them is a double reward, meaning an increase in reward. This is the comparison with his statement, Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof. This is from adding the source to the object, meaning the double reward for good deeds. It was said to them, The reward of doubling because doubleness is in the plural sense, and the ba in because of what they did is for causality. And they will be in the chambers, secure from everything they dislike, meaning the chambers of Paradise. The majority read the reward of double with the addition, while Al-Zuhri, Ya’qub, Nasr ibn ‘Asim and Qatadah read them in the nominative case, on the basis that doubleness is a substitute for reward. It was narrated from Ya’qub that he read reward in the accusative case with a tanween, and doubleness in the nominative case, assuming: For them is double as a reward, meaning the state of it being a reward. The majority read in the rooms in the plural, and Abu Ubaid chose this reading because of his saying: We will surely assign them rooms in Paradise. Al-A’mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamza, and Khalaf read they will be rewarded with the room in the singular because of his saying: Those will be rewarded with the room.
34:38: And when He, the Almighty, mentioned the state of the believers, He mentioned the state of the disbelievers, saying: 38- And those who strive against Our signs by rejecting them and challenging them while they are unable to do so racing against Us, claiming that they can outsmart Us themselves, or opposing Us with their disbelief, those will be brought to the punishment meaning in the punishment of Hell, the guards will bring them to it and they will find no escape from it.
34:39: Then the Almighty repeated what was mentioned before in order to emphasize the argument and refute what the disbelievers said, saying: 39- “Say: Verily, my Lord enlarges the provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for whom He wills.” That is, He expands it for whom He wills and restricts it for whom He wills. There is no indication in that of happiness or misery. And whatever you spend, He will replace it. That is, He will replace it for you. It is said, He will replace it for him or He will replace it for him if He gives him his compensation and substitute, and that substitute is either in this world or in the Hereafter. And He is the Best of Providers. For the provision of the servants to one another is only by God’s facilitation and decree, and they are not providers in reality but rather by way of metaphor, as it is said of a man that he provides for his family, and of a prince that he provides for his soldiers. The Provider of the prince and the one who is commanded, the great and the small, is their Creator. And whoever among the servants gives to another something of what God has provided for him, he has only disposed of God’s provision for him, so he deserves, by what he gives from it, the double reward for it, by the command of God. And spend it on what God has commanded.
34:40: 40- And the Day We gather them all together The circumstance is in the accusative case with an implied verb such as remember, or it is connected to His statement: And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are stopped meaning if you could also see them on the Day We gather them all together for the reckoning, the worshipper and the worshipped, the arrogant and the weak, Then He will say to the angels, Was it these you that they used to worship? As a rebuke to the polytheists and a rebuke to those who worshipped other than God, the Almighty, as in His statement to Jesus, Did you tell the people to take me and my mother as deities besides God?" He only mentioned the angels specifically even though some of the disbelievers worshipped other than them from the devils and idols because they are the most honorable of the idols worshipped by the polytheists. An-Nahhas said: The meaning is that if the angels disbelieved them, then in that there was a rebuke to the polytheists.
34:41: The phrase They said, 'Glory be to You! You are our protector rather than them' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question: that is, to glorify You! You are the one we protect, obey, and worship rather than them. We did not take them as our protectors, nor did we protect them, and we have no protector other than You. Then they stated what the polytheists worshipped, saying, Rather, they used to worship the jinn, meaning the devils, who are Iblis and his soldiers, and they claimed that they could see them and that they were angels and that they were the daughters of God. It was said that they used to enter the idols' chambers and gather them from them. Most of them are believers in them, meaning that most of the polytheists believe in the jinn and confirm them. It was said that the majority are in the meaning of all.
34:42: 42- So today none of you has power to benefit or harm others meaning the worshippers and the worshipped do not have power to benefit or harm others, and they are the worshippers benefit meaning intercession and salvation nor harm meaning torment and destruction. Rather, this statement was made to them to show their inability and shortcomings and to rebuke their worshippers. His statement: nor harm is an omitted addition: meaning they do not have power to ward off harm. His statement: And We will say to those who wronged is in apposition to His statement: He will say to the angels meaning to those who wronged themselves by worshipping other than God Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny in this world. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Razin who said: “Two men were partners. One of them went to the coast and the other stayed behind. When God sent the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he wrote to his companion asking him what he had done. He wrote to him that no one from Quraysh followed him except the dregs and poor people. So he abandoned his business and went to his companion who said: ‘Guide me to him.’ He used to read books. So he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘What do you call to?’ He said: ‘To such and such.’ He said: ‘I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘And how do you know that?’ He said: ‘No prophet was sent except that the dregs and poor people followed him.’ Then these verses were revealed: ‘And We did not send to a city a warner but its affluent ones said…’ [The following verses were revealed]. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent him word that God had revealed confirmation of what you had said.” Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: ‘The reward of double’: he said: ‘The doubling of a good deed.’ Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi in Nawader Al-Usul, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab who said: If a man is rich and pious, God will give him his reward twice over, and he recites this verse: And neither your wealth nor your children until His saying: For those is a double reward. He said: The doubling of a good deed. Sa’id bin Mansour, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And whatever you spend, He will replace it. He said: Not in extravagance nor miserliness. A similar narration was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, and a similar narration on the authority of Al-Hasan. Al-Daraqutni and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab on the authority of Jabir that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whenever a servant spends, God will replace it, except for spending in a clear way or in a sin. Ibn ‘Adi narrated something similar in Al-Kamil and Al-Bayhaqi from another chain of transmission on his authority, with a longer chain of transmission. It has been proven in Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “God the Almighty said: Spend, O son of Adam, and I will spend on you.” It has also been proven in Sahih from his hadith that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is no day on which the servants arise except that two angels descend, and one of them says: ‘O God, replace the one who spends,’ and the other says: ‘O God, destroy the one who withholds.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: Every day has an unlucky fate, so repel the unlucky fate of that day with charity. Then he said: “Read the places where there is a chance of replacement, for I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: ‘Whatever you spend, He will replace it.’” If you do not spend, how will He replace it? Al-Hakim at-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawadir al-Usul from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Indeed, assistance descends from the heavens according to the amount of your support.
34:43: Then the Almighty mentioned another type of their disbelief, saying: 43- And when Our verses are recited to them, meaning the Qur’anic verses while they are clear, with clear indications and obvious meanings, they say, ‘This is nothing but a man who wants to avert you from what your fathers used to worship,’ meaning your ancestors of the idols they used to worship. And they said, Secondly, “This is nothing but a fabricated lie,” meaning a lie that was invented. And those who disbelieved said, Thirdly, about the truth when it came to them, meaning the matter of the religion that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought them, This is nothing but obvious magic. This denial from them is specific to monotheism. As for denying the Qur’an and the miracle, it was agreed upon between the People of the Book and the polytheists. It was said that what was meant by the first, which is their saying, Except a fabricated lie, is its meaning, and by the second, which is their saying, This is nothing but magic. Mubeen is a miraculous system. It was said that a group of them said: It is a lie, and a group said: It is magic. It was said that they all said sometimes that it is a lie, and sometimes that it is magic, and the first is more appropriate.
34:44: 44- And We did not give them any books to study meaning, We did not send down to the Arabs any heavenly books for them to study, nor did We send to them before you any warner calling them to the truth and warning them of the punishment. So, their denial of the Qur’an and the Messenger has no basis, nor is there any doubt to cling to. Qatada said: God did not send down a book to the Arabs before the Qur’an, nor did He send to them a prophet before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Farra’ said: Meaning, how did they deny you, when no book or warner came to them about what they did?
34:45: Then He, the Almighty, granted them power and informed them of their end and the end of those who came before them, saying: 45- And those before them denied of the past generations and they did not reach even a tenth of what We gave them meaning the polytheists of Quraysh and other Arabs did not reach a tenth of what We gave those before them of strength, abundant wealth, and long life, so God destroyed them, like Aad, Thamud, and their likes. A tenth is a tenth. Al-Jawhari said: A tenth of something is a tenth. It was also said that a tenth is a tenth of a tenth, but the first is more appropriate. It was also said that the meaning is: Those before them did not reach a tenth of what We gave these people of clear proofs and guidance. It was also said that those before them did not reach a tenth of gratitude for what We gave them. It was also said that God did not give those before them a tenth of what He gave them of knowledge, explanation, argument, and proof, but the first is more appropriate. It was also said that a tenth is a tenth of a tenth, and a tenth is a tenth of a tenth, so it would be one part of a thousand parts. Al-Mawardi said: This is more apparent because what is meant by it is exaggeration in minimization. I said that taking into account exaggeration in minimization does not allow for it to deviate from the Arabic meaning. His statement, So they denied My messengers is in apposition to those before them denied in the manner of interpretation, like His statement, The people of Noah denied before them, so they denied Our servant verse. It is better for it to be in apposition to the specific in general, because the first denial, when it was deleted from the object of the denial, indicated generality. So its meaning is: They denied the revealed books, the sent messengers, and the clear miracles. Denying the messengers is more specific than it, even though it entails it. The verbal meaning was taken into account, not the implied meaning. So how was My denial? That is, how was My denial of them with torment and punishment? So let these people beware of such a thing. It was said that there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So We destroyed them, so how was My denial? And denial is a noun meaning denial.
34:46: Then the Almighty commanded the Messenger to establish an argument against them that would stop them, so He said: 46- “Say, ‘I only admonish you of one thing,’ meaning I warn you and caution you of the evil consequences of what you are in, and I command you of one characteristic, which is, ‘that you stand up for God in pairs and individually.’ This is an explanation of the one characteristic, or a substitute for it: meaning it is your standing up and rolling up your sleeves in seeking the truth with sincere thought, separated two by two, and one by one, because gathering confuses the mind. What is meant is not standing up on two men, but what is meant is standing up in seeking the truth and being sincere in thinking about it, as it is said, ‘So-and-so did such-and-such a thing,’ ‘then you reflect.’ This is because they used to say, ‘Muhammad is crazy.’ So God Almighty said, ‘Say to them, consider my command with one thing, which is that you stand up for God and in His essence together.’ So a man says to his companion, ‘Come, let us be friends. Have we seen in this man any madness?’ meaning madness, or have we experienced him lying?’ Then each one separates himself from his companion. So he thinks and considers, for in that is evidence that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is truthful and that he is a messenger from God, and that he is not a liar, a magician, or a madman. This is the meaning of His statement: “He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment,” meaning that he is only a warner to you before the Hour. It was said that the phrase there is no madness in your companion is a new statement from God Almighty, intended to draw attention to the method of looking and contemplating, that this great matter and great claim would not be exposed to anyone except a madman who does not care about what is said about him or what lies are attributed to him. They knew that he was the most rational of people, so it was necessary for them to believe his claim, especially with the addition of the clear miracle and their consensus that he was not one of those who fabricated lies, nor had they experienced lying from him during his life and theirs. It was said that the word "ma bisahibkum" may be an interrogative, meaning then think about what is wrong with him of the effects of madness. It was also said that what is meant by his saying, "I only admonish you with one thing is La ilaha illa God", as Mujahid and As-Suddi said. It was also said that it is the Qur'an because it encompasses all admonitions, and what we mentioned first is preferable. Al-Zajjaj said: The "an in his saying, that you stand up" is in the accusative case meaning that you stand up. As-Suddi said: The meaning of "muthanna and al-wādī" is: alone in his opinion and consulting others. Al-Qutaybi said: debating with his clan and thinking about himself. It was also said that "al-muhanna refers to the work of the day and al-wādī" refers to the work of the night. Al-Qutaybi said: debating with his clan and thinking about himself. It was also said that "al-muhanna refers to the work of the day and al-wādī" refers to the work of the night, as Al-Mawardi said. How cool and ineffective this statement is. Abu Hatim and Ibn al-Anbari chose to pause at the statement: Then you reflect. Based on this, the sentence There is no madness in your companion is a new sentence, as we mentioned earlier. It was said that it is not a pause, because the meaning is: Then you reflect: Have you experienced him lying, or have you seen madness, or corruption in his conditions?
34:47: Then God, the Almighty, commanded them to inform them that he had no purpose in this world nor any desire for it, so that their doubts would be removed and their suspicions would be lifted. He said: 47- Say, ‘Whatever reward I have asked of you is yours.’ That is, whatever reward I have asked of you in return for the message, it is yours if you ask it of him. The rebellious one denies the question completely, as someone says: Whatever I own in this, I have given it to you, meaning that he has no ownership of it at all. Similar to this verse are His saying: Say, ‘I do not ask of you for it any reward except love for the relatives.’ And His saying: I do not ask of you for it any reward except that whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.’ Then He explained to them that his reward is with God, the Almighty, and He said: My reward is only from God. That is, my reward is only from God, not from anyone else. And He is, over all things, Witness. That is, He is All-Knowing, and nothing is hidden from Him.
34:48: 48- Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord casts the truth.’ Casting is throwing an arrow, pebbles, or speech. Al-Kalbi said: He throws means he brings it. Muqatil said: He speaks the truth, which is the Qur’an and the revelation, meaning he conveys it to his prophets. Qatada said: With the truth means with revelation, and the meaning is that he clarifies the argument and makes it apparent to the people through the tongues of his messengers. It was also said that he throws falsehood with the truth and destroys it. Knower of the unseen. The majority of scholars read Knower in the nominative case as a second predicate for in, or predicate of a deleted subject, or a substitute for the pronoun in yadhdhfi, or in apposition to the position of the noun of in. Al-Zajjaj said: The nominative case has two aspects: position, because the position is a position of raising, or as a substitute. Zayd ibn Ali, Isa ibn Umar, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it in the accusative case as an attribute of the noun of in, or as a substitute for it, or as a praise. Al-Farra’ said: The nominative case is more common in such a case, as in his saying: “Indeed, that is the truth. The dispute of the people of Hellfire will occur.” Al-Ghayub was read with the three vowel marks on the letter ghayn, and it is the plural of ghayb, and ghayb is the matter that is hidden and very concealed.
34:49: 49- “Say, ‘The truth has come,’ meaning Islam and monotheism. Qatada said, ‘The Qur’an.’ Al-Nahhas said, ‘The estimation is the possessor of the truth,’ meaning the book that contains proofs and arguments. I say: There is no justification for estimating the complement, as the Qur’an came as its author did: “And falsehood does not originate nor does it restore.” That is, falsehood has gone away, and there remains of it no coming or going, no emergence or restoration. Qatada said: Falsehood is Satan, that is, Satan does not create in the first place nor does he resurrect. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said the same. It was said that it is permissible for ma to be an interrogative: that is, what does it originate and what does it restore? The first is more appropriate.
34:50: 50- “Say: If I go astray” from the clear, true path I only go astray to my own detriment meaning the sin of my going astray is upon myself, and that is because the disbelievers said to him: I have abandoned the religion of your fathers and have gone astray. So God commanded him to say this to them: And if I am guided, then it is by what my Lord reveals to me of wisdom, admonition, and explanation in the Qur’an. He is All-Hearing, Near to me and you. He knows guidance and misguidance. The majority read go astray with a fat-ha on the lam, and Al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Waththab read it with a kasra on the lam, and this is the language of the people of Aliyah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, And they have not attained even a tenth of what We have given them, meaning: of strength in this world. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar from Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Muhammad Ibn Ka'b Al-Qurazi regarding the verse, saying: A man stands with another man or alone and thinks about what madness is in his companion. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, There is no madness in your companion, meaning: He is not mad. These people also narrated from him regarding his statement, I have not asked you for any reward, meaning: whoever makes it, it is yours. He said: I have not asked you for a reward for Islam. And regarding his statement, "Say: Indeed, my Lord casts the truth," he said: by revelation. And regarding his statement, And falsehood does not originate, nor does it restore, he said: Satan does not originate or restore if he perishes. These people also narrated from him regarding his statement, And falsehood does not originate, nor does it restore, he said: Iblis does not create anything nor resurrect it. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Omar bin Saad regarding his statement: If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment, he said: I will only be held accountable for my crime.
34:51: Then the Almighty mentioned one of the states of the disbelievers, saying: 51- And if you could but see when they are terrified. The address is to the Messenger of God, or to anyone who is suitable for him. It was said that what is meant is their terrification when death descends upon them. Al-Hasan said: It is their terrification in the graves from the shout. Qatadah said: It is their terrification when they emerge from their graves. Al-Suddi said: It is their terrification on the day of Badr when their necks were struck by the swords of the angels, so they were unable to flee or return to repentance. Ibn Mughaffal said: It is their terrification when they witness God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the sinking that will swallow them up in the desert, and one of them will remain and tell the people what happened to his companions, so they will be terrified. The answer to if is omitted: i.e. you would have seen a terrifying matter. The meaning of so there is no escape is that none of them will escape me, and none of them will be saved. Mujahed said: There is no escape. And they were seized from a place nearby from the surface of the earth, or from the graves, or from the place of judgment. It was also said: From wherever they were. So they are close to God, they are not far from Him nor do they miss Him. It was also said: It is permissible that this fear is the fear that means answer. It is said that a man was frightened if he answered the one crying out to them for help, like their fear of war on the Day of Badr.
34:52: 52- "And they said, 'We believe in him,' meaning in Muhammad, as Qatada said, or in the Qur'an. Mujahid said: In God Almighty. Al-Hasan said: In the resurrection. "And how can they grasp?" Grasping means taking, and it is an interchange of tanawush which is taking, and the meaning is: How can they grasp faith from afar, meaning in the hereafter when they abandoned it in this world, and this is the meaning of "from a distant place" and it is a metaphor for their state in seeking salvation after what they missed. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: It is said to a man when he grabs a man to take hold of his head or beard, "naasheh", grabbing him, and he recited: It touches the basin with a high touch, crossing the borders of the desert. That is, to drink the water of the basin from above, and from it comes the skirmish in combat, and it was said that the skirmish is the return: that is, how can they return to the world to believe? And from it comes the saying of the poet: I wish you would come back to me and not argue with me
34:53: And sentence 53 - And they had disbelieved in it before is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, the situation is that they had disbelieved in what they believed in now before this time, and that was while they were in this world. Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Al-A'mash read Al-Tanawush with a hamza, and the rest read it with a waw. Abu Ubaid and Al-Nahhas ruled out the first reading, and there is no reason to rule it out, as it has been established in the Arabic language and poetry, including the saying of the poet: You have been away from your students for a long time, and you have come back as a liar after the good has passed you by. And you finally came. Al-Farra’ said: The hamza and omission of the hamza are similar. And they cast aspersions on the unseen meaning they cast aspersions, saying: There is no resurrection, no revival, no Paradise, and no Hellfire. From a distant place meaning from a distant direction where there is no basis for their false assumptions. It was also said that the meaning is: They say false things about the Qur’an: that it is magic, poetry, and the legends of the ancients. It was also said that they say about Muhammad that he is a magician, poet, soothsayer, and madman. Abu Haywah, Mujahid, and Mahbub read on the authority of Abu Amr they cast aspersions in the passive form: meaning they throw what hurts them as a result of their actions from where they do not expect. It represents their state as someone who throws something he cannot see from a distant place where there is no room for illusion in its catching up. The sentence is either conjoined with And they disbelieved in it as a narration of the past state and a recall of its image, or it is a new sentence to explain the representation of their state.
34:54: 54- And they will be prevented from what they desire of salvation from the punishment and they will be prevented from that. It was said that they will be prevented from what they desire in this world of their wealth and families, or they will be prevented from what they desire of returning to this world as was done to their followers before meaning their likes and counterparts from the disbelievers of the past nations. Religious followers is the plural of sects, and shi’a is the plural of shi’a. The phrase they were in disquieting doubt is an explanation of what came before it: meaning in doubt that leads to suspicion or has doubts about the matter of the messengers, the resurrection, Paradise and Hell, or about monotheism and what the messengers brought them of religion. It is said that a man is arab if he becomes suspicious, so he is suspicious. It was said that it is from doubt, which is doubt, so it is like what is said strange wonder and poet’s poetry. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: There is no escape, he said: There is no escape. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And if you could but see when they are terrified, there is no escape and they are seized from a place nearby, he said: It refers to the army of al-Sufyani. It was said: From where were they seized? He said: From beneath their feet. It has been proven in the Sahih that an army will be swallowed up in the desert from the hadith of Hafsah and Aishah. Outside the Sahih, it is from the hadith of Umm Salamah, Safiyyah, Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Mas`ud. There is nothing in them that states that this was the reason for the revelation of this verse. But Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah bin al-Yaman the story of this swallowing up with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said at the end of it: That is what God Almighty said in Surat Saba’: And if you could but see when they are terrified, there is no escape, the verse. Al-Faryabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And how can they approach? He said: How can they be repelled? From a place far away? He said: They ask for a response, but there is no time for response. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Taymi who said: I came to Ibn Abbas and said: What is tanaws? He said: Taking hold of something, but that is not the time for that.
35:1: It is forty-five verses. It is a Meccan surah. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Al-Durais, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah Fatir was revealed in Mecca. Fatar: to split something. It is said that he split it and it split. From this comes the word fatar to split a camel’s fang if it comes out, so it is a fatir camel. The thing is split and cracked. Fatar is the beginning and invention, which is what is meant here. The meaning is 1- Praise be to God, the Creator and Inventor of the heavens and the earth. The intended meaning is that He who was able to begin this great creation is able to repeat it. The majority read fatir in the active participle form, while az-Zuhri and ad-Dahhak read fatar in the past tense. According to the first reading, it is an attribute of God because its addition is mixed with its meaning in the past tense. If it is not pure, it is a substitute. The same applies to Ja’il al-Mala’ikah rasul making the angels messengers. Both interpretations are permissible. Rasul is in the accusative case with an implied verb according to the first interpretation, because the active participle does not function if it has a past tense meaning. Al-Kisa’i allowed it to function. According to the second interpretation, it is in the accusative case with ja’il making the angels messengers. Al-Hasan read it with the nominative case, while Khalil ibn Nasheet and Yahya ibn Ya'mar read it with the past tense. Al-Hasan and Hamid read it with a sukoon on the seen, which is the language of Tamim. Ole Wings is an adjective for rusulan. Wings is the plural of wing. Mithna wa thalatha wa raaba’ is an adjective for jinn. We have already discussed Mithna wa thalatha wa raaba’ in An-Nisa’. Qatadah said: Some of them have two wings, some three, and some four, with which they descend from the sky to the earth and ascend from the earth to the sky. Yahya ibn Salam said: God sends them to the prophets. Al-Suddi said: To His servants with His blessings or punishments. The phrase He increases in creation as He wills is a new sentence confirming what preceded it about the varying states of the angels. The meaning is that He increases in the creation of the angels as He wills, which is the opinion of most of the commentators, and was chosen by Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj. It was said that this increase in creation is not specific to the angels, so Al-Zuhri and Ibn Jurayj said: It refers to the beauty of the voice. Qatada said: Beauty is in the eyes, beauty is in the nose, sweetness is in the mouth, and it was said a beautiful face, and it was said a beautiful handwriting, and it was said curly hair, and it was said the mind and discrimination, and it was said the sciences and crafts. There is no reason to limit that to a specific type, rather it includes every increase, and the phrase Indeed, God is over all things competent is an explanation for what preceded it, that He increases in creation what He wills.
35:2: 2- Whatever mercy God opens to mankind, no one can withhold it. That is, whatever God gives them of rain and provision, no one can withhold it. And whatever He withholds of that, no one can send after withholding it. It was said that the meaning is: The messengers were sent as a mercy to mankind, and no one can send them except God. It was also said that it refers to supplication, repentance, and success and guidance. There is no basis for this specification, rather the meaning is: Everything God opens to mankind from the treasuries of His mercy includes every blessing that He bestows upon His creation. Similarly, withholding includes everything that God withholds from His blessings. He, glory be to Him, is the Giver, the Withholder, the Constrictor, the Expander. There is no giver or bestower other than Him. Then God, glory be to Him, commanded His servants to remember His abundant blessings upon them, which are countless and innumerable. And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them. The meaning of this command to them to remember is to guide them to be grateful for its continuity and to ask for more of it.
35:3: 3- Is there a creator other than God? "Min is redundant, Khaliq is the subject, and other than God" is an adjective. Al-Zajjaj said: Raising "Ghayr means Is there a creator other than God? because Min is a redundant word, and lowering Ghayr" makes it an adjective based on the word. The majority of scholars read "Ghayr" in the nominative case, while Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it in the genitive case. Al-Fadl ibn Ibrahim read it in the accusative case as an exception. The phrase "He provides for you from the sky and the earth" is the predicate of the subject, or a renewed sentence or another adjective for the Creator, and its predicate is omitted. Provision is from the sky in the form of rain, and from the earth in the form of plants and other things. The phrase "There is no god but He is renewed to confirm the negation derived from the question Fana tu'afkun from afk" with a fatha, which means to deflect. It is said "ma afkaka 'an kadha": meaning "what diverted you": meaning "how do you deflect? It is also said that it is taken from ifk" with a kasra, which means to lie because it is diverted from the truth. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, how can you slander and deny the Oneness of God and the Resurrection, while you acknowledge that God created you and provided for you?
