35:4: Then God, the Almighty, consoled His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: 4- And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], [other] messengers were denied before you, so that he might take an example from the prophets before him and console himself for the denial of the Arab disbelievers. And to God are returned all matters, not to anyone else, so that He may reward each one according to what he deserves. Al-Hasan, Al-A’raj, Ya’qub, Ibn ‘Amir, Abu Haywah, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Al-A’mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Khalaf read tarja’ with a fatha on the first letter as an active participle, while the rest read it with a damma on the second letter as a passive participle.
35:5: 3- "O mankind, indeed the promise of God is true" meaning His promise of resurrection, judgment, punishment, Paradise and Hellfire, as indicated by His saying: "And to God all matters will return. So let not the worldly life with its adornments and pleasures deceive you.* Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The deception of worldly life is that a person becomes preoccupied with its pleasures and delights so much that he says, Oh, if only I had sent forth [more] for my life. "And let not the Deceiver deceive you about God." The majority of scholars read it with a fat-ha on the ghayn: meaning the one who goes to extremes in deception, which is Satan. Ibn al-Sikkit and Abu Hatim said: Deceiver is Satan, and it may be a verbal noun, but al-Zajjaj ruled it out, because gharara bihi is transitive, and the verbal noun of a transitive verb is usually in the pattern of fa'l, like darabahu darban, except in simple, well-known matters that cannot be used as an analogy. The meaning of the verse is: Do not let Satan deceive you about God and say to you: God overlooks you and forgives you because of your virtue or the vastness of His mercy to you. Abu Haywah, Abu Al-Samak and Muhammad ibn Al-Samee' read it with a damma on the ghayn, which means falsehood. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: Ghurur with a damma is that which deceives of the worldly pleasures. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that ghurur is the plural of ghar, like qa'id and qa'ud. It is also said that it is possible that it is the verbal noun of ghara, like lazum and an-nahuk, and what Al-Zajjaj mentioned about the improbability is in it.
35:6: Then God, the Almighty, warned His servants against Satan, saying: 4- Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. That is, be hostile to him by obeying God and do not obey him in disobeying God. Then He explained to His servants how Satan is hostile to them, saying: He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze. That is, he only invites his followers, his supporters, and those who obey him to disobey God, the Almighty, so that they will be among the people of the Fire.
35:7: The position of the relative pronoun in His statement: 5- For those who disbelieve is a severe punishment is the nominative case as the subject, and For them is a severe punishment is its predicate, or the nominative case as a substitute for the subject of they will be, or the accusative case as a substitute for his party, or an attribute of it, or the omission of a verb that indicates blame, because after mentioning the enmity of Satan and his supplication to his party, He mentioned the state of the two groups of those who obey him and those who disobey him. So He said to the first group, For them is a severe punishment, and to the other group, He said, And those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is forgiveness and a great reward, meaning that God forgives them because of their faith and righteous deeds, and gives them a great reward, which is Paradise.
35:8: 6- "Is he who has had his evil deeds made attractive so he regards them as good?" This sentence is a resumption of what was previously mentioned about the difference between the two groups. "Min" is in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is omitted. Al-Kisa'i said: The meaning is "your soul has perished over them in grief." He said: This is indicated by his statement: "So do not let yourself perish over them in grief." He said: This is elegant Arabic speech that only a few know. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is like someone who has been guided, while others have considered it like someone who has not had their evil deeds made attractive. This is more appropriate as it agrees with the wording and meaning. The author of Al-Kashshaf made a mistake and narrated from Al-Zajjaj what Al-Kisa'i said. Al-Nahhas said: What Al-Kisa’i said is the best thing said about the verse, because of what he mentioned of its indication of what was omitted. The meaning is that God the Almighty forbade His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from being excessively aggrieved by them and grieving over them, as He said: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them. The phrase For God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills confirms what came before it: that is, He leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not consume yourself over them in regret. The majority of reciters read it with a fat-ha on the first letter and the ha’, referring to the self, so it would be from the same root as La arinikka ha’nuka. Abu Ja’far, Shaibah, Ibn Muhaysin, and Al-Ashhab recited it with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ha’, and the accusative of your self and the nominative of regrets as a reason: that is, for the regrets. It is permissible for it to be accusative as a state as if it had all become regrets due to the intensity of regret, as narrated from Sibawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: Inna is a distinguishing feature. Regret is intense sadness over what has passed. Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what they do. Nothing of their actions or words is hidden from Him. The sentence explains what preceded it, along with the severe threat it contains. Abu Ubaid, in his Fadhail, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: I did not know what Fatir al-samawāt wa’l-ard was until two Bedouins came to me disputing about a well. One of them said: I created it, meaning I began it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Fatir al-samawāt means Originator of the heavens. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority regarding His statement: He increases in creation what He wills, he said: A beautiful voice. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding His statement: Whatever mercy God opens for mankind... the verse, he said: Whatever God opens for mankind by way of repentance, there is none to withhold it, they repent whether they wish or refuse. And whatever He withholds by way of repentance, there is none to release it after Him, they do not repent. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the verse, he said: He says, You have no part in the matter. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding his statement, For them is forgiveness and a great reward, he said: Everything in the Qur’an is for them forgiveness, a great reward, and generous provision, which is Paradise. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Qatada and al-Hasan regarding his statement, Then is he to whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive, he said: Satan has made misguidance attractive to them, by God. So let not yourself perish over them in regret, meaning do not grieve over them.
35:9: Then the Almighty informed us about a type of His wonderful creation and great power, so that they might reflect on that and take heed from it, so He said: 9- And God is He who sends the winds. The majority read: the winds. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Al-A’mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read the wind in the singular. So it stirs up a cloud. He used the present tense after the past tense to evoke the image, because that is more relevant to the consideration of those who consider. The meaning of it stirring up the clouds is that it disturbs it from where it is. So We drove it to a dead land. Abu Ubaidah said: Its path, so it drives it, because he said: So it stirs up a cloud. It was said that the point of using the past tense after the present tense is to indicate realization. Al-Mubarrad said: Dead and dead are one. He said: This is the saying of the Basrans, and he recited: Not everyone who dies and finds rest is dead, but the dead are the dead of the living. Then We revived the earth thereby meaning, We revived the earth with rain by causing whatever grows in it to grow. Even if the mention of rain is not mentioned before, the clouds indicate it, or We revived with the clouds, because it is the cause of the rain. After its death meaning, after its dryness. He used the metaphor of revival for plants and death for dryness. Likewise is the resurrection meaning, likewise God revives the servants after their death, just as He revived the earth after its death. Resurrection means resurrection, from to resurrect man, and the kaf is in the nominative case as a predicate: meaning, like the revival of the dead earth is the revival of the dead. So how can you deny it when you have witnessed, more than once, what is like it and similar to it.
35:11: Then the Almighty mentioned another proof of resurrection and revival, saying: 11- And God created you from dust, meaning He created you initially within the creation of your father Adam from dust. Qatada said: It means Adam. The meaning of this is: The Creator of your first father, and your origin to whom you will return from dust. Then from a sperm-drop He brought it forth from the loins of your fathers. Then He made you in pairs meaning He paired some of you with others, so the male is the partner of the female, or He made you into types, males and females. And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge meaning there is no pregnancy or birth except with God’s knowledge, so nothing is outside His knowledge and planning. And no one is granted a long life, nor is his lifespan shortened except in a book meaning no one’s lifespan is prolonged, nor is his lifespan shortened except in a book, meaning in the Preserved Tablet. Al-Farra’ said: He means another other than the first, so He used a pronoun to refer to it as if it were the first, because if the wording of the second had been made clear, it would have been like the first, as if he had said: And no one’s lifespan is shortened. So the pronoun in his lifespan refers to another other than the first. Similar to this is your saying, I have a dirham and a half of it meaning another half. It was said that he was called long-lived in consideration of his destination. Meaning: No one's life is extended or reduced, but not in the sense that his life is not reduced after it was increased, but rather in the sense that nothing from the beginning is made deficient except that it is in a book. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: No one lives long except that his life is written down: how many years, how many months, how many days, how many hours, then it is written in another book: how much an hour is missing from his life, how much a day is missing from his life, how much a month is missing from his life, how much a year is missing from his life, until he completes his term. So whatever has passed is what is missing, and whatever is to come is what makes him live long. Qatada said: The one who has a long life is the one who reaches sixty years of age, and the one whose life is missing is the one who dies before sixty years. It was said that the meaning is: God has decreed the lifespan of a person so-and-so if he obeys, and less than that if he disobeys, so whichever of them he reaches is in a book, and the pronoun in this case refers to the one who lives long. It was said that the meaning is: No one lives long until old age, and no one decreases the lifespan of old age except in a book: that is, by God's decree. This was said by Ad-Dahhak, and chosen by An-Nahhas. He said: It is most similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation, and it is better to say that the apparent meaning of the Qur’anic system is that the lengthening and shortening of life are by the decree and predestination of God for reasons that necessitate lengthening and reasons that necessitate shortening. Among the reasons for lengthening the lifespan are what was reported from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about maintaining kinship ties and the like. Among the reasons for shortening it is committing many sins against God Almighty. For example, if a man's allotted lifespan is seventy years, God may add to it if he does the reasons for increasing it, and He may subtract from it if he does the reasons for decreasing it. All of this is in a clear book, so there is no contradiction between this verse and the statement of God, the Most High: So when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it. This is supported by the statement of God, the Most High: God blots out whatever He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. We have already presented in its interpretation what adds clarity and eloquence to what we have mentioned here. The majority of scholars read yanqṣas in the passive voice. Ya'qub, Salam, and it was narrated from Abu Amr read yanqṣas in the active voice. The majority of scholars read min 'umrah with a ḍammah on the meem. Al-Hasan, Al-A’raj, and Al-Zuhri read it with a sukoon. The reference in his saying, That to what came before of creation and what will come after it, is easy for God is that nothing is difficult for Him, and nothing is too much or little, big or small, hidden from Him.
35:12: Then the Almighty mentioned another type of His wondrous creation and amazing power, saying: 12- "And the two seas are not alike. This is fresh and sweet, pleasant to drink, and this is salty and bitter." What is meant by the two seas is fresh and salty. The fresh is sweet, while the bitter is bitter. What is meant by plain to drink is that which goes down easily in the throat due to its sweetness. Isa bin Omar read sayyigh with a shaddah on the yaa, and it was narrated from him that it was sukoon. Talhah and Abu Nahik read malh with a fathah on the mim. "And from each of them you eat tender meat," which is what is hunted from their edible animals. "And you extract from them ornaments which you wear." The apparent meaning is: "And you extract from them ornaments which you wear." Al-Mubarrad said: "The trick is only extracted from the salty." It was narrated from Al-Zajjaj that he said: "The ornaments are only extracted from them when they mix, not from each one of them separately." An-Nahhas preferred Al-Mubarrad's statement. The meaning of "you wear it" is that you wear each item of it according to its size, such as a ring on the finger, a bracelet on the arm, a necklace on the neck, an anklet on the foot, and what is worn as an ornament for the weapon carried such as a sword, shield, and the like. "And you see the ships therein" means in each of the two seas. An-Nahhas said: The pronoun refers specifically to the salt water. If that were the case, he would have said: "Therein are the ships that pass through the water. It is said that the ship passes through" mukhārta safa'ih tamkhār: if it splits the water. So the meaning is: And you see the ships in the two seas, waterways, some coming and some going, with a single wind. This has already been discussed in Surat An-Nahl. The "lām in that you may seek of His bounty" is related to what is indicated by the previous statement: that is, He did that for you to seek or for a way out. Mujahid said: Seeking bounty is trade by sea to distant countries in a short period of time, as mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. "And perhaps you will be grateful" to God for what He has bestowed upon you of that. Most commentators said: The verse is intended to provide an example of the believer and the unbeliever, and unbelief and faith. Just as two seas are not the same, so too the believer and the unbeliever, and unbelief and faith are not the same.
35:13: 13- He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night meaning He adds some of their parts to each other, increasing one by decreasing the other. This has been explained in Al Imran and in other places in the Noble Book. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term which God has determined for their running, which is the Day of Resurrection. It has also been said that it is the period of time in which they travel an orbit, which is a year for the sun and a month for the moon. It has also been said that what is meant by it is the running of the sun in a day and the moon in a night. This has been fully explained in Surah Luqman. The reference in His statement, That is to the doer of these actions, and He is the Most High. The demonstrative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is God, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. That is, this one whose creation is what was mentioned above: He is the Creator, the Determiner, the Able, the Powerful, the Owner of the world and the One who controls it. It is permissible for His statement, To Him belongs the dominion to be an independent clause in opposition to His statement, And those you invoke besides Him do not possess even a date stone. That is, they have no power over Him or His creation. The date stone is the thin shell that is between the date and the stone and wraps around the stone like a wrapper. Al-Mubarrad said: It is the split in the stone. Qatadah said: It is the cone on top of the stone. Al-Jawhari said: It is said that it is the white dot on the back of the stone from which the palm tree grows.
35:14: Then the Almighty explained the state of those whom they call upon other than God, that they can neither benefit nor harm, saying: 14- If you call upon them, they do not hear your call meaning, if you seek their aid in times of calamity, they do not hear your call, because they are inanimate objects that do not perceive anything. And if they heard in the manner of supposition, and the meaning is they would not respond to you because of their inability to do so. Qatada said: The meaning is, And if they heard, they would not benefit you. It was also said that the meaning is: If We gave them hearing and life, so they heard your call, they would be more obedient to God than you, and they would not respond to you in what you called them to of disbelief. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association meaning, they will disavow your worship, and they will say: It was not us you used to worship. It is permissible for and those you call upon other than Him and what follows it to refer to those who have reason among those whom the disbelievers worshipped, and they are the angels, jinn, and devils. Meaning: They deny that what you did is true, and they deny that they ordered you to worship them. And none can inform you like the One who is All-Knowing. That is, none can inform you like the One who is All-Knowing and All-Aware of things, and He is God Almighty. No one is more knowledgeable about His creation, their sayings, and their actions than He Almighty, and He is the All-Knowing of the essence and truth of things. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: An angel will stand between the heaven and the earth with the Trumpet and blow it, and no creation of God will remain in the heavens or the earth except whom God wills, except that he will die. Then God will send from beneath the Throne semen like the semen of men, and their bodies and flesh will grow from that water as the earth grows from the dust. Then Abdullah recited: It is God who sends the winds (the verse). Abu Dawud, al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma` wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Abu Razin al-`Uqayli who said: “I said, O Messenger of God, how does God bring the dead back to life? He said: Have you not passed by a barren land and then passed by one that was fertile, shaking and green? I said: Yes. He said: Thus does God bring the dead back to life, and thus is the Resurrection.” Abd bin Humaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat The Names of God and the Attributes narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: “When we narrate to you a hadith, we will bring you confirmation of that from the Book of God. When a Muslim slave says: ‘Glory be to God and praise be to Him, and praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest, and blessed be God,’ an angel seizes them and takes them under his wing, then ascends with them to the heavens. No group of angels passes by them except that they ask forgiveness for the one who said them until they bring them to the Face of the Most Merciful. Then he recites: ‘To Him ascends good speech, and righteous action raises it. ’ He said: ‘Performing the obligatory duties. So whoever remembers God in performing his obligatory duties, his deeds will be more deserving of being carried out. ’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And no one will be granted a long life… 1:176, he said: “He says, ‘There is no one for whom I have decreed a long life except that he reaches the age that I have decreed for him, and I have decreed that for him. ’ So he only reaches the book that was decreed for him. ’ This is what His statement: ‘And nothing will be diminished from his lifespan except that it is in a book. ’” He said: All of that is in a book with Him. Ahmad, Muslim, Abu 'Awanah, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "The angel enters upon the sperm-drop after it has settled in the womb for forty or forty-five nights and says: 'O Lord, will I be wretched or happy? Male or female?' God says and they write. Then his deeds, provision, lifespan, legacy, and calamity are written down. Then the scroll is folded and nothing is added to it or taken away." Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, al-Nasa'i, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that Umm Habibah said: God granted me enjoyment through my husband the Prophet, my father Abu Sufyan, and my brother Mu'awiyah. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "You have asked God for fixed terms, numbered days, and allotted provisions. God will not hasten anything before its time or delay anything. If you had asked God to protect you from punishment in the Fire or punishment in the grave, that would have been better and more excellent." These hadiths are specific to what was reported about the acceptance of supplication, and that it is intertwined with divine decree, and to what was reported about maintaining kinship ties increasing one's lifespan. Thus, there is no contradiction between the evidences, as we have mentioned. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, what they possess of even a husk, he said: The husk is the peel, and in another version: the skin that is on the back of the date pit.
35:15: Then the Almighty mentioned the need of His creation for Him, and their increasing need for His grace, saying: 15- O mankind, you are those in need of God, meaning those in need of Him in all matters of religion and this world. They are the ones in need of Him absolutely, and He is the Rich absolutely, the Praiseworthy, meaning the One deserving of praise from His servants for His kindness to them.
35:16: Then the Almighty mentioned a type of the types at which their need for Him and His independence from them are realized, so He said: 16- If He wills, He can take you away and bring forth a new creation. That is, if He wills, He can annihilate you and replace you with a new creation that will obey Him and not disobey Him, or He can bring forth a type of creation and a world other than what you know.
35:17: 17- And that is nothing but your going away and bringing others is difficult for God meaning impossible and not difficult. The explanation of this has already been mentioned in Surat Ibrahim.
35:18: 18- And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another meaning a bearer of burdens. The noun was omitted because it is known. The meaning of bears is carries. The meaning is: no soul shall bear the burden of another soul, meaning its sin. Rather, every soul shall bear its own burden. This verse does not contradict His statement: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens in addition to their own burdens, because they only bore the burdens of their misguidance in addition to the burdens of their misguidance, and all of this is from their own burdens, not from the burdens of others. An example of this is the hadith: Whoever establishes a bad practice will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection. The one who establishes a bad practice will bear the burden of his bad practice. We have already discussed this verse in full. And if a heavily laden soul calls upon another to carry it, Al-Farra’ said: meaning a heavily laden soul. He said: This applies to both males and females. Al-Akhfash said: That is, if a soul burdened with sins calls another soul to bear its burden, which is its sins, “he will not bear any of it that is, of its burden even if he is a close relative. That is, even if the one it calls is a relative, it will not bear any of its burden. The meaning of the verse is: “And if a soul burdened with sins calls another soul to bear any of its sins with it, that soul called will not bear any of those sins, even if it were a close relative to it, so how about others who have no relation to the one calling it?” Those of kin was read as complete, like His statement: And if he is in hardship. The phrase You only warn those who fear their Lord unseen is a new sentence intended to clarify who is admonished by the warning. The meaning of they fear their Lord unseen is that they fear Him while they are absent from His punishment, or they fear His punishment while He is absent from them, or they fear Him when they are alone with people. Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is that your warning only benefits those who fear their Lord, so it is as if you are warning them and not others who are not benefited by the warning, like His statement: You are only a warner of those who fear it and His statement: You only warn those who follow the message and fear the Most Merciful unseen. The meaning of and establish prayer is that they focused on its matter and did not distract themselves from it with anything that would distract them. And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for the sake of his own soul. Purification is cleansing from the filth of polytheism and immorality. The meaning is that whoever purifies himself by abandoning sins and increasing righteous deeds only purifies himself, because the benefit of that is specific to him, just as the burden of someone who becomes defiled is only on him and not on anyone else. The majority read, And whoever purifies himself, only purifies himself. Abu Amr read, Purifies himself, by assimilat- ing the ta’ into the zay. Ibn Mas’ud and Talhah read, And whoever purifies himself, only purifies himself. “And to God is the final destination,” not to anyone else. God Almighty mentioned first that no one bears any of his sins that He does not bear. Then He mentioned thirdly that the reward for obedience is specific to its doer, and no one else has any of it.
35:19: Then he gave an example of the believer and the disbeliever, saying: 19- The blind are not equal meaning the one who is deprived of the sense of sight and the seeing who has the faculty of sight. So he likened the disbeliever to the blind, and likened the believer to the seeing.
35:20: 20- Nor darkness nor light meaning darkness and light are not the same, so he likened falsehood to darkness and truth to light. Al-Akhfash said: Nor in his statement 'nor light'.
35:21: 21- nor heat is redundant, and the meaning is: darkness and light are not the same, nor shade and heat. Heat is the intense heat of the sun. Al-Akhfash said: Heat only occurs during the daytime sun, and the toxic winds occur at night, and it was said the opposite. Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajaj said: Heat only occurs at night, and the toxic winds occur during the day. Al-Farra' said: The toxic winds only occur during the day, and heat occurs in both. An-Nahhas said: This is more correct. Qatrib said: Heat is heat, and heat is cold, and the meaning is: shade that has neither heat nor harm is not the same, and heat that harms. It was said that he meant reward and punishment, and heat was called heat to exaggerate the intense heat, because the increase in the structure indicates an increase in meaning. Al-Kalbi said: By shade he meant Paradise, and by heat he meant Hell. Ata' said: He means the shade of the night and the sun of the day. It was said that darkness was pluralized and light was singular due to the multiplicity of types of falsehood and the unity of truth.
35:22: Then the Almighty mentioned another example of the believer and the disbeliever, saying: 22- And not equal are the living and the dead. So He likened the believers to the living, and likened the disbelievers to the dead. It was said that He meant to liken the scholars to the ignorant. Ibn Qutaybah said: The living are the rational ones, and the dead are the ignorant ones. Qatada said: All of these are examples, meaning just as these things are not equal, so too the disbeliever and the believer are not equal. Indeed, God makes hear whom He wills to make hear from His friends whom He created for His Paradise and guided them to His obedience. And you cannot make hear those in the graves meaning the disbelievers whose hearts have been killed by disbelief. Meaning, just as you cannot make hear those who have died, you cannot make hear those who died before them. The majority read musam' with a tanween, separating it from the addition.
35:23: Al-Hasan, Isa Al-Thaqafi, and Amr bin Maymun read it with the addition of You are only a warner, meaning you are only a messenger and warner. You are only responsible for warning and conveying the message, and guidance and misguidance are in the hand of God Almighty.
35:24: 23- Indeed, We have sent you with the truth. It is possible that with the truth is in the accusative case as a state of the subject: meaning the truthful, or of the object: meaning the truthful, or an adjective for a deleted verbal noun: meaning a sending mixed with the truth, or it is related to good tidings: meaning a bringer of good tidings of the true promise and a warner of the true promise. It is better for it to be an adjective for the deleted verbal noun, and the meaning of good tidings is: a bringer of good tidings to the people of obedience and a warner to the people of disobedience. And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them meaning that there is no nation from the past nations but that a warner from the prophets has passed among them to warn them. The mention of the warner is limited to the mention of the bearer of good tidings, not the bearer of good tidings, because it is more appropriate to the situation.
35:25: Then he consoled and comforted his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: 24- And if they deny you, then those before them denied meaning those before them from the past nations denied their prophets Their messengers came to them with clear proofs meaning with clear miracles and apparent evidence and with the scriptures meaning the written books like the scrolls of Abraham and with the enlightening book like the Torah and the Gospel. It was said that the enlightening book is included under the scriptures and under the clear proofs and the conjunction is due to the difference in concepts, even though they are united in truth. It is better to specify the clear proofs with the miracles, and the scriptures with the books that contain sermons, and the book with what it contains of laws and rulings.
35:26: 25- Then I seized those who disbelieved. The placement of the apparent in place of the pronoun indicates the explicit condemnation of them with what is in the scope of the relative clause, and indicates the reason for seizing. How was my censure? That is, how was my censure and punishment of them? Warsh read on the authority of Nafi’ and Shaibah with the addition of the ya’ in my reminder in connection, not in pause. The meaning of this was explained shortly. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Al-Ahwas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: “No sinner shall sin except against himself. No father shall sin against his child, nor shall a child sin against his father.” Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Abu Rimtha who said: “I set out with my father towards the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). When I saw him, he said to my father: ‘Is this your son?’ He said: ‘Yes, by the Lord of the Ka'bah.’ He said: ‘He will not sin against you, and you will not sin against him.’ Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: ‘And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: And if you call a heavily laden one to carry it, nothing of it will be borne, that he said: He will be burdened with a burden, and he will not find anyone to carry any of it for him.
35:27: Then the Almighty mentioned a type of His dazzling power and one of His wondrous creations, saying: 27- Have you not seen - the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to whoever is suitable for it - that God sends down water from the sky This vision is the heart-felt one: that is, do you not know? And that and its subject and predicate take the place of the two objects then We brought forth thereby - that is, with water. The point in this shift is to show the complete care given to the action because of the wondrous creation in it, and the accusative of of varying colors is in description of fruits, and what is meant by colors are the kinds and types: that is, some of them are white, some are red, some are yellow, some are green, and some are black. And among the mountains are new - report is the plural of report, which is the road. Al-Akhfash said: If it were the plural of new he would have said report with a damma on the jim and the dal, like bedir and surrir. Zuhair said: As if he had dark cheeks and new hair, he flew away and grazes himself after the summer sometimes. It is said that the new ones are pieces, taken from the word jaddat something, meaning to cut it, as narrated by Ibn Bahr. Al-Jawhari said: The newness is the line on the back of a donkey that differs from its color, and the newness is the method, and the plural is jadid and jadaid, and from that is the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb: John the Serpent has four braids. Al-Mubarrad said: Jadid: paths and lines. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said something similar to this in the interpretation of al-Jadid. Al-Farra’ said: They are the paths that are in the mountains like veins, white, black, and red, and the singular is Jadda. The meaning is that God the Almighty informed us about the Jadid of the mountains, which are their paths, or the lines in them, that the color of some of them is white and the color of others is red, and this is the meaning of His statement: white and red, of varying colors. The majority of scholars read Jadad with a damma on the jim and a fatha on the dal. Al-Zuhri read it with a damma on both of them, the plural of Jadidah. It was narrated from him that he read it with a fatha on both of them, and Abu Hatim rejected it and others authenticated it. He said: al-Jadid means the clear and evident path. And black ravens means intense blackness whose color resembles the color of a crow. Al-Jawhari said: You say: This is black gharib, meaning intense black, and when you say black ravens, you make aswad a substitute for ghurabib. Al-Farra’ said: There is an inversion in the speech, the meaning of which is and black crows, because it is said black crows, and it is rarely said black crows. His statement, of different colors, is an attribute of jadda, and his statement, and crows is connected to jadda in the sense of: And among the mountains are white and reddish jades, and among the mountains are crows of one color, which is black, or of red in the sense of: And among the mountains are white, red, and black jades. It was said that it is connected to white, and it is necessary to estimate a deleted complement before jadda: that is, and among the mountains are those with jades, because jadda is only in the colors of each other.
35:28: 28- And among mankind, beasts, and grazing livestock are of varying colors. His statement, various, is an attribute of an omitted noun: that is, among them is a class, or a kind, or some whose colors vary in red, black, white, green, and yellow. Al-Farra’ said: That is, He created them in varying colors like the variation of fruits and mountains. God, the Almighty, only mentioned the variation of colors in these things because this variation is one of the greatest proofs of God’s power and the wonder of His creation. The meaning of like that is different like that variation, and it is an attribute of an omitted source, and the interpretation is that its colors vary in a variation that is like that: that is, like the variation of mountains and fruits. Al-Zuhri read and beasts with a light ba’. Ibn as-Samee’ read their colors. It was said that his statement like that is related to what comes after it: that is, like that rain. Considering God’s creations and their varying colors makes those of His servants who have knowledge fear God. This is the preferred choice of Ibn ‘Atiyyah, but it is rejected because what comes after only affects what comes before it. The first interpretation is more correct, and stopping at like that is complete. Then the speech was resumed and He, the Almighty, informed us by saying: Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge. Or it is a continuation of His saying: You only warn those who fear their Lord unseen. Meaning that only those who fear Him, the Almighty, unseen, fear Him, and those who have knowledge of Him and of His sublime attributes and beautiful actions that befit Him. In any case, He, the Almighty, has specified in this verse those who fear Him, and they are those who have knowledge of Him and glorify His power. Mujahid said: The knowledgeable one is he who fears God, the Almighty. Masruq said: “Fearing God is sufficient as knowledge, and being deceived is sufficient as ignorance. So whoever knows God best is the one who fears Him most.” Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Whoever does not fear God is not a scholar. Ash-Sha’bi said: The scholar is he who fears God. The reason for presenting the object is that the situation is one of limiting the agent, and if it were delayed, the matter would be reversed. Omar bin Abdul Aziz read it by raising the noble name and putting the scholars in the accusative. This reading was narrated on the authority of Abu Hanifa, who said in Al-Kashaf: The fear in this reading is a metaphor, and the meaning is that He respects and venerates them as He respects and honors the awe-inspiring man among the people. The phrase Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Forgiving is an explanation for the necessity of fear, as it indicates that He will punish for His disobedience and forgive whoever among His servants repents.
35:29: 29- Those who recite the Book of God means they continue to recite it and are consistent with it. The Book is the Holy Quran, and there is no basis for what was said that it refers to the entirety of the Books of God. And establish prayer means they perform it at its appointed times with the completion of its pillars and remembrances. And spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly. This is an urging to spend however one is prepared. If it is prepared secretly, then it is better, otherwise it should be done publicly. It does not prevent him from thinking that it is showing off. It is possible that secret refers to voluntary charity, and public refers to obligatory charity. The phrase they hope for a trade that will never fail is in the nominative case as a predicate of in as Tha’lab and others said. What is meant by trade is the reward for obedience, and the meaning of will never fail is that it will not be lost or destroyed. It is an attribute of trade, and informing us of their hope for the reward for what they have done is like a promise that their hope will come true.
35:30: The lam in 30- to pay them their wages is connected to will not be lost, meaning: it will not be lost so that He will pay them their wages for their righteous deeds. Similar to this verse is the saying of the Almighty: But as for those who have believed and done righteous deeds, He will pay them their wages in full and increase them from His bounty. It was said that the lam is connected to something omitted that the context indicates: that is, they did that so that He would pay them in full. The meaning of and increase them from His bounty is that He bestows upon them an increase in their wages, which are the reward for their deeds. The phrase He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative is an explanation of what was mentioned about paying them in full and increasing: that is, He is Oft-Forgiving of their sins, Most Appreciative of their obedience. It was said that this phrase is the predicate of in, and the phrase they hope is in the place of a preposition as a state, but the first is more appropriate.
35:31: 31- And that which We have revealed to you of the Book meaning the Qur’an, and it was said that it is the Preserved Tablet, with min being a partial or introductory particle, and the phrase It is the truth is the predicate of the relative pronoun, and confirming what was before it is in the accusative case as a state: meaning in agreement with what came before it of the books, Indeed, God is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of His servants meaning He encompasses all their affairs.
35:32: 32- Then We caused to inherit the Book those We chose of Our servants. The first object of We caused to inherit is the relative pronoun, and the second object is the Book. The second object was brought forward to honor and glorify the Book. The meaning is: Then We caused to inherit the Book, which is the Qur’an, those whom We chose of Our servants. We decreed and predestined that the scholars of your nation, O Muhammad, should inherit this Book which We sent down to you. The meaning of choosing them is that they were selected and chosen. There is no doubt that the scholars of this nation, from the Companions and those who came after them, were honored by God over all other servants and made them a middle nation so that they would be witnesses over the people. He honored them by making them the nation of the best of the prophets and the master of the children of Adam. Muqatil said: It means the Qur’an of Muhammad, which We made reach those whom We chose of Our servants. It was said that the meaning is: We caused it to inherit from the previous nations, meaning We delayed it from them and gave it to those whom We chose, but the first is more appropriate. Then, the Almighty divided those whom He inherited His Book and chose from among His servants into three categories, saying: Among them are those who wrong themselves. Many scholars have questioned the meaning of this verse, because the Almighty made this category of those who wrong themselves part of that division, which is among those He chose from among His servants. So how could those whom God chose be wronging themselves? It was said that the division refers to the servants: that is, among Our servants are those who wrong themselves, which is the disbeliever, and the pronoun they enter refers to the moderate and the foremost. It was also said that what is meant by those who wrong themselves is the one who falls short in acting upon it, and he is the one who postpones the command of God, and it is not necessary for the inheritors of the Book to observe it with due observance, because He said: Then there came after them generations who inherited the Scripture. This is questionable, because wronging oneself does not fit with being chosen. It was said that the one who wrongs himself is the one who commits minor sins. This statement was narrated on the authority of Umar, Uthman, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Darda' and Aisha. This is the most correct view, because committing minor sins does not contradict being chosen, nor does it prevent its doer from entering Paradise with those who will be adorned with bracelets of gold and so on. The reason for him being unjust to himself is that he has diminished his reward by committing minor sins that have been forgiven. If he had done acts of obedience instead of those minor sins, he would have had a great reward for himself in them. It was said that the one who wrongs himself is the one who commits major sins. The early Muslims differed in their interpretation of the foremost and the moderate. Ikrimah, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak said: The moderate is the disobedient believer, and the foremost is the pious in general. Al-Farra’ also said this. Mujahid said in his interpretation of the verse: “Among them are those who are unjust to themselves, such as the people on the left. “And among them are those who are moderate” are the people on the right. And among them are those who are foremost in good deeds are the foremost among all people. Al-Mubarrad said: The moderate is the one who gives this world its due and the Hereafter its due. Al-Hasan said: The unjust is the one whose bad deeds outweigh his good deeds. The moderate is the one whose good and bad deeds are equal. The foremost is the one whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds. Muqatil said: The one who is unjust to himself is the one who commits major sins among the people of Tawhid. The moderate is the one who has not committed a major sin. The foremost is the one who is first in righteous deeds. An-Nahhas related that the unjust is the one who commits major sins, and the moderate is the one who does not deserve Paradise because his good deeds exceed his bad deeds. So the Gardens of Eden will be entered by those who are foremost in good deeds and no one else. He said: This is the opinion of a group of people of insight, because the pronoun in insight is more deserving of what follows it. Ad-Dahhak said: Among them is he who wrongs himself: that is, from their offspring he is wronged by himself. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: The foremost is the one who knows, the moderate is the one who learns, and the wrongdoer by himself is the ignorant. Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: The wrongdoer by himself is the one who remembers God with his tongue only, the moderate is the one who remembers Him with his heart, and the foremost is the one who does not forget Him. Al-Antaki said: The wrongdoer is the one who speaks, the moderate is the one who does, and the foremost is the one who states. Ibn Ata’ said: The wrongdoer is the one who loves God for the sake of this world, the moderate is the one who loves God for the sake of the Hereafter, and the foremost is the one who abandons his desire for the desire of the Truth. It was also said: The wrongdoer is the one who worships God out of fear of Hellfire, the moderate is the one who worships Him in the hope of Paradise, and the foremost is the one who worships Him for no reason. It was also said: The wrongdoer is the one who loves himself, the moderate is the one who loves his religion, and the foremost is the one who loves his Lord. It was also said: The wrongdoer is the one who is fair but does not get fair, the moderate is the one who gets fair and gets fair, and the foremost is the one who gets fair but does not get fair. Al-Tha’labi and others have mentioned many sayings, and there is no doubt that the linguistic meanings of the oppressor, “the moderate,” and the foremost are well-known. It applies to oppression of the self merely by depriving it of its good fortune and missing out on what is better. So, the one who abandons the multiplication of acts of obedience has wronged himself in view of the reward he has missed, even if he is doing what God has enjoined upon him and leaving what God has forbidden him. From this standpoint, he is among those whom God has chosen and among the people of Paradise, so there is no problem with the verse. From this is the saying of Adam, Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and the saying of Yunus, Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers. The meaning of the moderate is the one who is moderate in matters of religion and does not lean toward excess or neglect, and this is one of the people of Paradise. As for the foremost, he is the one who is ahead of others in matters of religion, and he is the best of the three. It has been questioned why the oppressor should be given precedence over the moderate person and both of them should be given precedence over the one who is foremost, given that the moderate person is better than the one who is foremost in the world, while the one who is foremost in the world is better than the one who is foremost in the world. It has been said that precedence does not necessitate honor, as in His statement, The companions of the Fire are not equal to the companions of Paradise, and similar verses of the Qur’an which give precedence to the evil people over the good people and the less favored over the virtuous. It has also been said that the reason for precedence here is that the moderate people are few in relation to the sinners, and the foremost in relation to both groups are even fewer, so He gave precedence to the more numerous over the less numerous. The former is more appropriate, since the majority alone does not necessitate precedence in mention. Other reasons for precedence have been given other than what we have mentioned, which there is no need to elaborate on. The reference in His statement, that, is to the inheritance of the Book and selection, and it has been said to the precedence in good deeds, but the former is more appropriate. It is the subject and predicate, He is the great bounty, meaning the bounty whose value cannot be measured.
35:33: And the elevation of 33- Gardens of Eden as a subject and what is worshipped is its predicate, or as a substitute for the grace because since it is the reason for attaining the reward, it is placed in the position of the causer, and on this basis the sentence they enter it is a resumption and we have already mentioned that the pronoun in they enter it refers to the three categories, so there is no reason to limit it to the last category, and Zur ibn Hubaysh and al-Tirmidhi read garden in the singular, and al-Jahdari read gardens in the accusative case due to the preoccupation, and Abu al-Baqa’ allowed that gardens be a second predicate of the demonstrative pronoun, and Abu Amr read they enter it in the passive form, and his saying: they are adorned is a second predicate of the Gardens of Eden, or an implied state, and it is from the woman is adorned so it is a state, and in it is an indication of the speed of entry, for in their adornment outside of Paradise there is a delay in entry, so when he said they are adorned in it he indicated that their entry is quickly of bracelets of gold from the first being partial, and the second being explanatory: that is, they are adorned with some bracelets of gold, Bracelets are the plural of bracelet, the plural of bracelet, and the accusative of pearls is in apposition to the place of of bracelets and it was read in the genitive case in apposition to gold. And their clothing therein will be silk. The explanation of the verse has been presented in full in Surat Al-Hajj.
35:34: 34- And they will say, 'Praise be to God, Who has taken away from us sorrow.' The majority of scholars read sorrow with two fat-has. Janah ibn Hubaysh read it with a damma on the ha' and a sukoon on the zay. The meaning is that they will say this statement when they enter Paradise. Qatadah said: The sorrow of death. Ikrimah said: The sorrow of bad deeds and sins and fear of the rejection of good deeds. Al-Qasim said: The sorrow of the loss of blessings and fear of the consequences. It was also said: The sorrow of the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. Al-Kalbi said: What saddened them in this world about the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They are the bread in this world. It was also said: They are the livelihood. Al-Zajjaj said: God will take away from the people of Paradise all sorrows, whether for livelihood or the afterlife. This is the most correct of the opinions, because even if the pleasures of this world are great, it is not free of impurities and calamities that cause much sorrow, especially for the people of faith, for they will always be fearful of God's punishment, afraid of His retribution, and their hearts will be troubled at all times. Will their deeds be accepted or rejected? Warned of the evil consequences and the evil ending, then their worries and sorrows will continue until they enter Paradise. As for the disobedient, even if their strangulation is relieved for a little while in the life of this world, which is the abode of delusion, and they forget the abode of permanence one day of their lives, their fear will inevitably intensify and their calamity will be great, and the cauldrons of their sorrows will boil when they approach death and approach the dwellings of the Hereafter. Then when their souls are taken and what will upset them from the recompense for their deeds becomes clear to them, their grief and sorrow will increase. If God favors them with forgiveness and admits them to Paradise, then He has removed their sorrows and removed their grief and worries. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative. That is, Forgiving of those who disobey Him. Appreciative of those who obey Him.
35:35: 35- Who has settled us in the home of permanence out of His bounty meaning the home of permanent residence in which one will remain forever and not move from it out of His bounty and mercy therein no fatigue will touch us meaning no toil, fatigue, or hardship will befall us in Paradise nor will weariness touch us therein meaning exhaustion from fatigue, and weariness from fatigue. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, {Fruits of varying colors}, that he said: white, red, and black. And regarding His statement, {And among the mountains are streaks}, that he said: Paths of white meaning colors. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, that he said: The intense black raven. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Malik, regarding His statement, {And among the mountains are streaks}, that he said: Paths that are white in the mountain. And red and those are the streaks. And black raven he said: black mountains. And among people and beasts and livestock he said: Likewise the variation of people, beasts, and livestock is like the variation of mountains. Then He said, {Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge}, that he said: A chapter on what preceded it. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, {Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge}, that he said: Those who have knowledge of God are those who fear Him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, regarding the verse, that he said: Those who know that God has power over all things. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Adi narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: Knowledge does not come from many hadiths, but knowledge comes from fear of God. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Abd bin Hamid and At-Tabarani narrated on his authority that he said: Fear of God is sufficient as knowledge, and being deceived by God is sufficient as ignorance. Ahmad also narrated in Az-Zuhd on his authority that he said: Knowledge does not come from many narrations, but knowledge comes from fear of God. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah who said: Knowledge is sufficient for the believer that he fears God. Abd Al-Ghani bin Saeed Ath-Thaqafi narrated in his Tafsir on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the verse Indeed, those who recite the Book of God and establish prayer was revealed about Husayn bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib bin Abdul Manaf. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We have chosen of Our servants, that he said: They are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God gave them as an inheritance every Book that was revealed. The wrongdoer among them is forgiven, the moderate among them is given an easy reckoning, and the foremost among them enters Paradise without being held to account. At-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, at-Tirmidhi who classed it as hasan, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said regarding this verse, “Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds,” that he said: All of these are of one status, and all of them will enter Paradise. In its chain of narration are two unknown men. Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Shu’bah told us on the authority of al-Walid ibn al-’Aizar, that he heard a man from Thaqeef It was narrated on the authority of a man from Kinanah, on the authority of Abu Saeed. Al-Faryabi, Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Baath narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God said: ‘Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by God’s permission. As for those who are foremost, they are the ones who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. As for those who are moderate, they will be brought to an easy account. As for those who wronged themselves, they will be detained in the ruins of the place of assembly. Then they are the ones whom God will cover with His mercy. They are the ones who will say: ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.’ to the end of the verse.” Al-Bayhaqi said: If there are many narrations about a hadith, it becomes clear that the hadith has a basis. End quote. In Ahmad’s chain of transmission is Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and in Ibn Abi Hatim’s chain of transmission is an unknown man, because he narrated it via Al-A’mash on the authority of a man on the authority of Abu Thabit on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: Abu Thabit mentioned. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Awf ibn Malik on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “My nation is divided into three parts: a third will enter Paradise without being brought to account, a third will be brought to a light account, then…” They will enter Paradise, and a third will be tested and uncovered. Then the angels will come and say, We found them saying, ‘There is no god but God alone.’ God will say, Enter them into Paradise because they said, ‘There is no god but God alone.’ And carry their sins on the people of disbelief. This is what God said, And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens in addition to their own burdens. This is confirmation of what was mentioned about the angels. God the Most High said, Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We have chosen of Our servants. He divided them into three groups. Among them is he who wrongs himself, so this is the one who is tested and uncovered. Among them is he who is moderate, and he is the one who will be held to an easy account. And among them is he who is foremost in good deeds, and he is the one who will enter Paradise without account or punishment, by God’s permission, they will all enter it.” Ibn Kathir said after mentioning this hadith: It is very strange. End quote. These hadiths strengthen each other and must be adhered to, and they refute the statement of those who attribute the wrongdoer to themselves to the disbeliever. They are supported by what was narrated by al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd: And among them is he who is unjust to himself (al-Baqarah 2:17), who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All of them are from this nation, and all of them are in Paradise. And what was narrated by al-Tayalisi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Uqbah ibn Sahban, who said: I said to Aisha, “What do you think of God’s statement: ‘Then We caused the Book to be inherited’ (al-Baqarah 2:17)?” She said: “As for the foremost, he is the one who passed away during the lifetime of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he testified that he would be in Paradise. As for the moderate, he is the one who follows their footsteps and acts like they did until he joins them. As for the one who is unjust to himself, he is like me and you and those who follow us, and all of them are in Paradise.” And he narrated Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Mas'ud who said: This nation will be divided into three thirds on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:one third will enter Paradise without being held to account, one third will be held to a light reckoning, and one third will come with great sins except that they did not associate partners with God. So the Lord will say: Admit these people into the breadth of My mercy. Then he recited: Then We caused the Book to be inherited verse. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that when he recited this verse: Then We caused the Book to be inherited, he would say: Verily, the foremost among us will be forerunners, the moderate among us will be saved, and the wrongdoer among us will be forgiven. Al-'Uqaili, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Ba'th from another chain of narration from him, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn al-Najjar narrated it from the hadith of Anas with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). al-Tabarani narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The one who is foremost in good deeds will enter Paradise without being held to account, the moderate among us will enter Paradise by the mercy of God, and the wrongdoer and the companions of the A'raf will enter Paradise by the intercession of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Uthman ibn Affan that he recited this verse, then said: Surely those who outstrip us are those who strive hard, those who are moderate are those who live here, and those who wrong us are those who live in poverty. Sa'id ibn Mansur and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba'th on the authority of al-Bara' ibn Azib regarding the verse: And among them is he who wrongs himself al-Baqarah 2:17, he said: I bear witness that God will admit them all into Paradise. Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this verse: Then We gave inheritance to those We have chosen of Our servants al-Baqarah 2:17. He said: All of them will be saved, and it is this nation. Al-Firyabi and Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: “It is like the one in al-Waqi'ah: the companions of the right and the companions of the left.” And the forerunners: two types will be saved, and one type will perish.” Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Humaid, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from him regarding his statement: {And among them is he who wrongs himself}, that he said: He is the disbeliever, and the moderate one is the companions of the right hand. This narration from him may God be pleased with him does not conform to the apparent meaning of the Qur’anic order, nor does it agree with the narrations we have previously mentioned from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and a group of the Companions. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Humaid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Abdullah bin Al-Harith that Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b about this verse, and he said: They were all saved. Then he said: Their shoulders were touching, by the Lord of the Ka’bah, then they were given the reward for their deeds. We have previously mentioned from Ibn Abbas what indicates that the one who wrongs himself is among those who are saved, but the opinions about him conflict. Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba’th narrated from Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited the statement of God: {Gardens of Eden which they will enter, adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls}, and he said: They will wear crowns, the smallest pearl of which will illuminate what is between the east and the west. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: “And they said: Praise be to God” 1:177, he said: They are people in this world who fear God and strive to worship Him secretly and openly, but in their hearts is sadness because of past sins they have committed, so they are afraid that this striving for the sins they have committed will not be accepted from them. So, “They said: Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.” He forgave us the great and appreciated our few deeds. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated - and he authenticated it - on his authority regarding the verse: He said: Sorrow of the Fire.
35:36: Then when He, the Almighty, finished mentioning the reward of His righteous servants, He mentioned the reward of His righteous servants, saying: 36- “And those who disbelieve will have the fire of Hell. They will not be decreed to die, nor will their punishment be lightened for them.” Rather, Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. This verse is similar to His, the Almighty’s, statement: He will neither die therein nor live. The majority of scholars read he will die in the accusative case as an answer to the negation, and Isa bin Omar and Al-Hasan read it with the nun. Al-Mazini said: in apposition to he will die. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is a weak reading and there is no basis for this weakening. Rather, it is like his saying: And they will not be given permission to make excuses, “Thus do We recompense every ungrateful person,” meaning, with such a terrible recompense, We recompense everyone who is excessive in disbelief. Abu Amr read yajza’i in the passive form.
35:37: 37- And they cry out therein from the word sarāk which means shouting, meaning they cry out for help in the fire, raising their voices. The one who cries out is the one who seeks help, and from this the poet said: Whenever a frightened person came to us, the screaming was like the beating of pipes. Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do. That is, while they are therein crying out, saying: Our Lord, etc. Muqatil said: It means that they will call out: Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do, of polytheism and sins. So we replace the disbelief we were upon with faith, and obedience with sin. The accusative case of righteous is an attribute of a deleted verbal noun, meaning righteous action, or an attribute of a deleted described noun, meaning we do something righteous. It was said that the addition of his statement: other than what we used to do is to express regret for what they did of other than righteous deeds, while admitting that their deeds in this world were not righteous. So God, the Exalted, answered them by saying: Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember? The question is for rebuke and rebuke, and the and is for conjunction with an implied word as in similar words. Ma is an indefinite noun described, meaning, Or did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember to remember? It was said that it was sixty years, and it was said that it was forty, and it was said that it was eighteen years. The first was stated by a group of companions, the second by Al-Hasan, Masruq and others. The third was stated by Ata' and Qatadah. Al-A'mash recited what is mentioned with idgham: "And the warner has come to you." Al-Wahidi said: The majority of commentators said: It refers to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Ikrimah, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, Waki', Al-Hasan ibn Al-Fadl, Al-Farra' and Ibn Jarir said: It refers to gray hair. According to this statement, its meaning would be: Did We not grant you life until you became gray hair? It was also said that it refers to the Qur'an, or to fever. Al-Azhari said: Its meaning is that fever is a messenger of death, as if it senses its arrival and warns of its coming. Gray hair is also a harbinger because it comes at the age of maturity and is a sign of leaving the age of youth, which is the age of play and amusement. It was also said that it refers to the death of family and relatives. It was also said that it refers to the completion of reason, or to puberty. So taste [the punishment], for the wrongdoers will have no helper. That is, taste the torment of Hell, because you did not take heed and learn a lesson. You have no helper to protect you from God’s torment and stand between you and Him. Muqatil said: So taste the torment, for the polytheists will have no protector to protect them.
35:38: 38- Indeed, God is Knowing of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. The majority of scholars read the verse by adding knowing to unseen. Janah ibn Hubaysh read it with the tanween and the accusative case of unseen. The meaning is that He is Knowing of everything, including deeds that are not hidden from Him. If He were to return you to this world, you would not do righteous deeds, as the Most High said: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. “Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts” is an explanation of what preceded it, because if He knows what is concealed in the breasts, which are more hidden than anything, He knows what is above them a fortiori. It was said that this sentence explains the first sentence.
35:39: 39- It is He who has made you successors upon the earth meaning He made you a nation succeeding those before them. Qatada said: successor after successor and generation after generation. The successor is the one who follows the one who came before. It was also said that He made you His successors on His earth. So whoever among you disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief meaning the harm of his disbelief will be upon him and will not extend to anyone else. And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers in the sight of their Lord except hatred meaning anger and hatred. And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers except in loss meaning decrease and destruction. The meaning is that disbelief does not benefit them in the sight of God since it only increases them in hatred, and it does not benefit them in themselves since it only increases them in loss.
35:40: Then He, the Almighty, commanded him to rebuke and rebuke them, saying: 40- Say, 'Have you seen your partners whom you invoke besides God?' That is, tell me about the partners whom you have taken as gods and worshipped besides God. The phrase Show me what they have created from the earth is a substitute for the inclusion of have you seen? The meaning is: Tell me about your partners, show me what they have created from the earth. It was said that the two verbs, have you seen and show me are from the category of conflict. The second one was applied according to what is preferred by the Basrans, Or have they a share in the heavens? That is, do they have a partnership with God in creating them, owning them, or disposing of them, such that they deserve to share in divinity? Or have We given them a scripture? That is, or have We sent down to them a scripture about partnership. So they have clear evidence from it? That is, a clear and evident proof from that scripture. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamzah, and Hafs from Asim read bayyinah in the singular, while the rest read it in the plural. Muqatil said: He says, Did We give the disbelievers of Mecca a book, so that they would accept a clear statement from it that there is a partner with God? Then the Almighty turned away from this to something else, saying, Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion. That is, the wrongdoers do not promise one another, as leaders and chiefs do, except delusion with which they tempt their followers and make it seem attractive to them. These are falsehoods that deceive but have no reality. This is their saying: These deities benefit them, bring them closer to God, and intercede for them before Him. It was said that the devils promise the polytheists this, and it was said that what is meant by the promise that some of them promise one another is that they will be victorious over the Muslims and overcome them.
35:41: And the sentence 41- Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist is a new statement to explain the power of God, the Most High, and the wonder of His creation after explaining the weakness of the idols and their inability to do anything. It was said that the meaning is that their polytheism necessitates the cessation of the heavens and the earth, as in His statement: The heavens almost burst from it and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation * Because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son "And if they were to cease, no one could hold them back after Him" meaning no one could hold them back after His holding them back, or after their cessation. The sentence is a mainstay in the place of the answer to the oath and the condition, and the meaning of "lest they cease to exist" is lest they cease to exist, or out of aversion for them to cease to exist. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that God prevents the heavens and the earth from disappearing, so there is no need for an estimation. Al-Farra’ said: That is, even if they were to disappear, no one would hold them back. He said: It is similar to His statement: And if We send a wind and they see it yellow, they will continue to disbelieve after that. It was said that what is meant is their disappearance on the Day of Resurrection, and the phrase Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving is an explanation of what preceded it about His, the Most High, holding back the heavens and the earth.
35:42: 42- And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that if a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the nations. The Quraish are meant. They swore this oath before God sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, when the People of the Book rejected their messengers. The meaning of of any of the nations is those who rejected the messengers. The warner is the prophet, and guidance is righteousness. The Arabs wished that there would be a messenger from among them, just as there were messengers among the Children of Israel. But when there came to them what they wished for, which was the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, who is the most honorable warner and the most honorable messenger, and he was from among themselves, his coming only increased them in aversion from him and their distancing from answering him.
35:43: 43- Arrogance in the land meaning for the sake of arrogance and insolence and for the sake of and the plotting of evil meaning the plotting of evil action, or they plotted the evil plot, and the plot is the deception, trickery and ugly action, and it is added to its description like his saying: the mosque of the congregation, and the first prayer and the feminine of one because a nation is a burden as Al-Akhfash said. And it was said that the meaning is: from one of the nations in general, and it was said from the nations that are called one of the nations as a preference for them. The majority read and the plotting of evil with the hamza of the bad in the genitive case, and Al-A'mash and Hamza read it with a sukoon in connection. Many grammarians made a mistake in this reading, and they acquitted Al-A'mash, despite his greatness, from reading it. They said: He only stopped with the sukoon, so whoever narrated from him that he used to read with the sukoon in connection was mistaken. The explanation of this reading is possible, because whoever reads it treats the connection as a pause as in the saying of the poet: Today I drink without committing any sin against God or being excessive. With a sukoon on the ba’ from ashrab, and similar to it is the reading of those who read wa ma yasha’rkum with a sukoon on the ra’, and similar to that is the reading of Abu Amr ila barikum with a sukoon on the hamza, and many others. Abu Ali al-Farsi said: This is on the basis of connecting the same as stopping, and Ibn Mas’ud read wa makran sye’i “And the evil plotting will not encompass except its own people” meaning that the evil consequence will not befall except those who do evil. Al-Kalbi said: yahiq means yahuq, and hawq is to encompass, it is said haqqa bihu if it has encompassed it, and this is the apparent meaning of yahiq in the Arabic language, but Qatrab interpreted it here as yazanal, and he recited: They lifted the death, so it became an arm's length after it had been looming over it. That is, do they await anything but the way of the former peoples? That is, do they await anything but the way of the former peoples? That is, the way of God with them, that He sends down upon these peoples the punishment as He sent down upon those peoples?
