You will not find any change in the way of God That is, no one is able to change the way of God that He established with the nations who denied, of sending down His punishment upon them, by replacing it with something else instead. And you will not find any change in the way of God by changing what God’s way of punishment has brought about, by pushing it away from them and placing it on someone else. The negation of finding change and transformation is an expression of the negation of their existence.
35:44: 44- Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? This sentence is intended to confirm and emphasize the meaning of what preceded it: that is, have they not traveled through the land and observed what We sent down upon ‘Aad, Thamad, Madyan, and their likes of punishment when they denied the Messengers? For that is from the law of God with those who deny, which does not change or alter. The traces of their punishment and what God sent down upon them are present in their dwellings, evident in their homes. And the fact is that those were mightier than them in strength, longer-lived, more wealthy, and stronger in body. And nothing in the heavens or on the earth could escape God, that is, nothing in the heavens or on the earth could overtake Him or escape Him. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent, that is, He is of great knowledge and great power. Nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing is difficult for Him.
35:45: 45- And if God were to punish people for what they have earned of sins and wrongdoings, He would not leave upon its surface meaning the earth a single creature of all the creeping creatures that move, whatever they may be. As for the children of Adam, it is for their sins, and as for others, it is for the evil of the sins of the children of Adam. It was said that what is meant is whatever creeping creatures from the children of Adam and the jinn were left upon the surface of the earth. Ibn Mas`ud and Qatadah said the former, while Al-Kalbi said the latter. Ibn Jurayj, Al-Akhfash, and Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said: What is meant by creatures here is people alone, not others. But He delays them for a specified term, which is the Day of Resurrection. So when their term comes, then indeed, God is ever, of His servants, Seeing, meaning who among them deserves reward and who among them deserves punishment. The agent in if is: He came to me, Seeing. In this there is consolation for the believers and a threat to the disbelievers. Abdur-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Abu Al-Shaykh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, {And have We not given you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember?}, he said: Sixty years. Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi in Nawader Al-Usul, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on his authority that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said, ‘Where are the sixty-year-olds?’ This is the age of which God said, ‘And have We not given you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember?’” In its chain of transmission is Ibrahim bin Al-Fadl Al-Makhzumi, who is criticized. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari, An-Nasa’i, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God excuses a man who prolongs his life until he reaches the age of sixty. Abd ibn Hamid, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa'd. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The age with which God has reproached them is sixty years. At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Hakim, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The lifespans of my ummah will be between sixty and seventy, and the fewest of them will exceed that. At-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: It is a hasan ghareeb hadith, we do not know it except from this chain of narration. Then he narrated it in another place in the Book of Asceticism and said: This is a hasan ghareeb hadith on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and it has been narrated from him through other chains of narration. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: It is forty-six years. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority: The age with which God has excused the son of Adam, when He said: Have We not given you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember? is forty years. Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ad-Daraqutni in Al-Ifrad, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat, and Al-Khatib in his Tarikh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say on the pulpit: "It occurred to Moses, 'Does God, the Almighty, sleep?' So God sent an angel to him who kept him awake for three days and gave him two bottles, one in each hand, and ordered him to guard them. So he would sleep with his hands almost meeting, then he would wake up and hold one over the other until he fell asleep and his hands clapped and the two bottles broke. He said: God set forth an example for him: If God, the Blessed and Exalted, were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would not hold together." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam that Moses said: O Gabriel, does your Lord sleep? He narrated something similar. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-'Azmah and Al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah on the authority of his father that Moses narrated something similar. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani and Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: The dung beetle was almost tortured in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam. Then he recited: And if God were to punish people for their wrongdoing verse.
36:1: It is eighty-three verses. It is a Meccan surah. Al-Qurtubi said: There is consensus, except for a group that said, ‘And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind.’ This verse was revealed about Banu Salamah of the Ansar when they wanted to leave their homes and move near the Mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). This will be explained later. Ibn Ad-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah Yaseen was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar narration on the authority of Aishah. Ad-Darimi, At-Tirmidhi, Muhammad ibn Nasr, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur’an is Yaseen. Whoever recites Yaseen, God will record for him, by reciting it, the recitation of the Qur’an ten times.” At-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: This is a strange hadith that we do not know of except through the hadith of Humayd ibn Abd ar-Rahman. In its chain of transmission is Harun or Muhammad, who is an unknown sheikh. There is a hadith on this topic on the authority of Abu Bakr, but it is not authentic due to the weakness of its chain of transmission. Al-Bazzar narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur’an is Yaseen. Then he said after narrating it: We do not know of anyone who narrated it except Zayd from Humayd, meaning Zayd ibn al-Hubab from Humayd al-Makki, the client of the family of Alqamah. Al-Darimi, Abu Ya’la, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever recites Yaseen at night, seeking the pleasure of God, will be forgiven that night. Ibn Kathir said: Its chain of transmission is good. Ibn Hibban and al-Diya’ narrated from Jundub ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites Yaseen at night, seeking the pleasure of God, will be forgiven. Its chain of transmission in Sahih Ibn Hibban is as follows: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, a freed slave of Thaqeef, narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Shuja’ ibn al-Walid al-Kubi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Khaithama narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Juhadah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Jundub ibn ‘Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood up and mentioned it. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated to us from Muqal ibn Yasar that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Sura Yasin is the heart of the Qur’an. No servant recites it, desiring God and the Hereafter, will be forgiven for his previous sins, so recite it over your dead.” Ahmad mentioned two chains of transmission for it: one of them has an unknown narrator, and the other mentions it from Abu ‘Uthman, who he said is not al-Nahdi, from his father, from Muqal. Sa’id ibn Mansur and al-Bayhaqi narrated to us from Hassan ibn ‘Atiyyah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever recites Yasin, it is as if he recited the Qur’an ten times. Ibn Al-Durais, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Khatib, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Surat Yasin is called in the Torah the ‘generous one’. It grants its reciter the good of this world and the next, protects him from the trials of this world and the next, wards off from him the terrors of the hereafter, and repels all evil from its reciter and fulfills his every need. Whoever recites it, it will be equal to twenty Hajj pilgrimages. Whoever hears it, it will be equal to a thousand dinars in the way of God. Whoever writes it and then drinks it, it will put into his body a thousand medicines, a thousand lights, a thousand certainties, a thousand blessings, and a thousand mercies, and it will remove from him every rancor and disease.” Al-Bayhaqi said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Abu Bakr Al-Judaani sought it as a means of seeking closeness to God, on the authority of Sulayman bin Rafi’ Al-Jundi, and it is rejected. I said: This is the hadith that Al-Tirmidhi previously indicated was weak in its chain of transmission, and it is not unlikely that it is fabricated, as all of these wordings are objectionable and far removed from the speech of one who has been given concise speech. Al-Tha’labi mentioned it from the hadith of Aisha, and Al-Khatib mentioned it from the hadith of Anas, and Al-Khatib mentioned something similar from the hadith of Ali, but in a shorter version. Al-Bazzar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said about Surat Ya-Sin 36:I wish it were in the heart of every person of my nation. And its chain of transmission is as follows: He said: Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Al-Hakam ibn Abaan narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said…” And Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever persists in reciting Yaseen every night and then dies, dies a martyr. Al-Darimi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Whoever recites Yaseen in the morning will be given ease for his night until evening, and whoever recites it at the beginning of the night will be given ease for his night until morning. His statement: 1- Ya Seen The majority read it with a sukoon on the noon, while Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamzah, Hafs, Qaloon, and Warsh read it with the assimilation of the noon into the waw that follows it. Isa bin Omar read with a fatha on the noon, while Ibn Abbas, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Nasr bin Asim read it with a kasra. The fatha is based on the construction or that it is the object of an implied verb, which is: Atal Ya Seen. The kasra is also based on the construction like jir, and it was said that the fatha and kasra are to avoid the meeting of two quiescent letters. As for the reason for the majority reading it with a sukoon on the noon, it is because it is listed in a list, so it has no role in parsing. Harun Al-A'war, Muhammad bin Al-Sameefa', and Al-Kalbi read it with a damma on the noon based on the construction like mandh, wahayt, and qat, and it was said that it is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning this is Ya Seen, and it was prevented from being declined due to the operation and feminization. There is a difference of opinion about the meaning of this word. Some say it means O man or O human being. Ibn al-Anbari said: “Pausing at Ya Seen is good for those who say it is the opening of the surah. However, those who say it means “O man” do not pause at it.” Sa’id ibn Jubayr and others said: “It is one of the names of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. The evidence for this is “Indeed, you are one of the messengers.” And from this is the saying of al-Sa’d al-Himyari: O soul, do not give sincere advice, striving for love except to the family of Yasin. And from this is His statement: “Peace be upon the family of Yasin,” meaning upon the family of Muhammad. What is meant by the family of Yasin will come in As-Saffat. Al-Wahidi said: Ibn Abbas and the commentators said: He means O human being, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: It means O master of mankind. Malik said: It is one of the names of God Almighty, and Ashab narrated that from him. Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami narrated from Ja’far Al-Sadiq that it means O master. Ka’b said: It is an oath by which God swore. Al-Zajjaj preferred that it means O Muhammad. They differed as to whether it is Arabic or non-Arabic. Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah said: It is Abyssinian. Al-Kalbi said: It is Syriac, spoken by the Arabs, and it became part of their language. Al-Sha'bi said: It is in the language of Tayy. Al-Hasan said: It is in the language of Kalb. We have already mentioned in Taha and in the opening of Surat Al-Baqarah what makes the discussion unnecessary here.
36:2: 2- And the Wise Qur'an in the accusative case as it is the object of the oath initially. It was also said that it is conjoined with Ya Seen, assuming it is in the accusative case due to the oath being implied. Al-Naqqash said: God did not swear to any of His prophets by the message in His book except to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a sign of his greatness and glorification. The Wise is the perfect one who does not contradict or conflict, or the Wise is the one who said it.
36:3: The answer to section 3 - You are indeed one of the messengers. This is a response to those infidels who denied his message by saying: You are not a messenger.
36:4: And his saying: 4- On a straight path is another piece of report for in: meaning that you are on a straight path, and the straight path is the worthy path that leads to what is sought. Al-Zajjaj said: On the path of the prophets who came before you, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a state.
36:5: 5- A Revelation of the Almighty, the Most Merciful Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Abu Bakr read Tanzil in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning it is a revelation. It is also permissible for it to be the predicate of the statement of Ya Seen if it is made the name of the surah. The rest read it in the accusative case as a source: meaning God sent down this revelation of the Almighty, the Most Merciful. The meaning is: You, O Muhammad, are a revelation of the Almighty, the Most Merciful, and the first is more appropriate. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a praise according to the reading of those who read it in the accusative case. The Almighty expressed the revealed with the source as an emphasis so that it is as if it is the revelation itself. Abu Haywah, Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ja'far Yazid bin Al-Qa'qa', and Shaibah read Tanzil in the genitive case as an attribute of the Quran or a substitute for it.
36:6: The lam in 6- to warn a people whose fathers were not warned may be related to the revelation, or to an implied verb that indicates it from the messengers: i.e. We sent you to warn, and what is in what their fathers were not warned is the negative: i.e. their fathers were not warned, and it may be a relative or a description: i.e. to warn a people whom their fathers warned, or to warn them of a punishment their fathers warned, and it may be a source: i.e. warning their fathers, and according to the saying that it is negative the meaning is: their fathers were not warned of a messenger from themselves, and it may be intended what their closest fathers were warned of due to the long period, and his saying: they are heedless is related to the negation of the warning in the first way: i.e. their fathers were not warned so they are heedless because of that, and according to the other ways it is related to his saying to warn: i.e. they are heedless of what we warned their fathers with, and most of the people of interpretation have gone to the meaning on Negation, which is apparent from the system to arrange the understanding of the heedless on what came before it.
36:7: The lam in His statement: 7- The word has come true upon most of them is the particle that introduces the oath, meaning, by God, the word has come true upon most of them. The meaning of has come true is: it has been established and the word has become obligatory: meaning, the punishment is upon most of them: meaning, most of the people of Mecca, or most of the disbelievers in general, or most of the disbelievers of the Arabs, and they are those who died in disbelief and persisted in it throughout their lives. So His statement: They do not believe branches off from what came before it in this regard: meaning, because God Almighty knew of their persistence in what they were in of disbelief and dying in it. It was said that what is meant by the statement mentioned here is His statement, the Almighty: Then the truth, and the truth I say, * I will fill Hell with you and those who follow you.
36:8: And the sentence 8- Indeed, We have placed shackles around their necks is a confirmation of what came before it. It likened their state to the state of those whose necks are shackled. So they meaning the shackles reach to their chins so they are not able to turn around at that time nor are they able to bend them, and this is the meaning of His statement: So they are with their heads down meaning they are raising their heads and lowering their gaze. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Muqamih is the one who lowers his gaze after raising his head, and the meaning of iqmah is raising the head and lowering the gaze. It is said that a camel has aqmah a head that is lowered and qahmah a head that is lowered if it raises its head and does not drink water. Al-Azhari said: God meant that when their hands were chained around their necks, the chains were raised to their chins and their heads were raised, so their heads were raised by the chains being raised. Qatada said: The meaning of muqhimoon is shackled, but the first is more appropriate, and from this is the saying of the poet: We sit on its sides, biting our ends like camels in the sun. Al-Zajjaj said: The two months of Kanun are called Qamaah, because when camels come to the water, they raise their heads due to the severe cold. He recited the words of Abu Zaid Al-Hudhali: A young man, what a son of the noble one, if we are equal, the provisions are required in the two months of Qamaah Abu Ubaidah said: The camel dries up when it raises its head from the water tank and does not drink. Abu Ubaidah also said: It is a metaphor that God gave them regarding their refusal to follow guidance, like the refusal of one who is chained, just as it is said that someone is a donkey, meaning he does not see guidance, and as the poet said: They are shackled and chained to the right path. Al-Farra’ said: This is a parable: meaning, We prevented them from spending in the way of God, and it is like His statement: And do not make your hand chained to your neck and Ad-Dahhak said the same. It was also said that the verse is a reference to what will be done to people in the Fire by placing shackles on their necks as God the Most High said: When the shackles are on their necks and Ibn Abbas read: Indeed, We have placed shackles on their right hands. Az-Zajjaj said: meaning, on their hands. An-Nahhas said: This reading is an explanation, and one should not recite in a way that contradicts the Qur’an. He said: There is an omission in the speech according to the reading of the group, the meaning is: Indeed, We have placed on their necks and on their hands shackles, so they reach the chins. So the word it is a metaphor for the hands, not the necks. The Arabs omit such a thing, and similar to it is garments that protect you from the heat, and its meaning is: and garments that protect you from the cold, because that which protects from the heat protects from the cold, because if the shackles are on the neck, then there is no alternative for them to be on the hand, especially since God said so they reach the chins, so it is known that what is meant by it is the hands, so they are muḥammahun meaning raising their heads, unable to lower their heads, because whoever has his hands shackled to his chin, his head is raised. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he read: Indeed, We have placed on their hands shackles, and on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he read: Indeed, We have placed on their right hands shackles, as was narrated from the reading of Ibn Abbas.
36:9: 9- And We placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them meaning We prevented them from believing with obstacles, so they are unable to move from disbelief to belief, like someone who has barriers placed in front of him and behind him. The word barrier with the seen pronounced with a damma or a fatha is two languages. From this meaning in the verse is the poet’s saying: And from the accidents, I don't care that I was hit on the ground with axes I cannot find my way to the place of a hill between Al-Udhaib and the land of Murad. "Then We covered them means We covered their sight so they because of that do not see" meaning they are unable to see anything. Al-Farra' said: "Then We covered their sight with a covering" meaning they were blinded so they do not see the path of guidance. Qatadah said the same, meaning they do not see guidance. Al-Suddi said: They do not see Muhammad when they conspired to kill him. Ad-Dahhak said: "And We placed before them a barrier meaning this world and behind them a barrier" meaning the Hereafter. "Then We covered them so they do not see" meaning they are blind to the resurrection and blind to accepting the laws in this world. It was said that what is before them is the Hereafter and what is behind them is this world. The majority of scholars read it with the voiced ghayn, meaning We covered their sight, so it is with the omission of an adjective. Ibn Abbas, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Hasan, Yahya ibn Ya'mar, Abu Raja', and Ikrimah read it with the silent ghayn from "asha" which means weak eyesight. And from it is "and whoever is blind from the remembrance of the Most Gracious".
36:10: 10- And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. That is, whether you warn them or not is the same. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, whoever God misguides in this way, the warning will not benefit him.
36:11: Warning is only of benefit to him who is reminded in His statement: 11- You can only warn him who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful in secret. That is, he follows the Qur’an and fears God in this world. The phrase they will not believe is a new sentence explaining what came before it regarding being equal. Or it is in the accusative case as a state, or as a substitute. In secret is in the accusative case as a state of the subject or the object. Then give him good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward. That is, give good tidings to this one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful in secret of great forgiveness and a noble reward: that is, good, which is Paradise.
36:12: Then God, the Almighty, informed us of His resurrection of the dead, saying: 12- Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, meaning, We will resurrect them after death. Al-Hasan and Ad-Dahhak said: meaning, We will revive them with faith after ignorance, but the former is more appropriate. Then He threatened them with recording their traces, saying: And We will record what they have put forth, meaning, what they have put forth of good and evil deeds, and their traces, meaning, what they left behind of good deeds whose benefit continues after death, such as someone who sets a good precedent or the like, or the bad deeds that remain after the death of their doer, such as someone who sets a bad precedent. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: Similar to this is His statement: A soul will know what it has put forth and what it has left behind, and His statement: On that Day man will be informed of what he put forth and what he left behind. It was said that what is meant by the verse is the traces of those who walk to the mosques, and this is what a group of the Companions and Followers said. An-Nahhas said: This is the most appropriate statement about the verse because it was revealed for that reason. The answer to this is that consideration is based on the generality of the verse, not the specificity of its cause. Its generality requires that all the effects of good and evil be recorded. Among the good is teaching the knowledgeable and classifying them, endowing charity for the sake of God, and building mosques and bridges. Among the evil is innovating injustices and doing what harms people, which the unjust will follow and practice, such as taxation and other things. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: And everything We have recorded in a clear register. That is, everything, from the deeds of the servants and others, whatever they may be, is in a clear register, i.e., a book followed and explained to everyone. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said: He meant the Preserved Tablet. A group said: He meant the scrolls of deeds. The majority of scholars read and We record in the active form. Zur and Masruq read it in the passive form. The majority of scholars read everything We have recorded with every in the accusative case, indicating the preoccupation. Abu al-Samal read it in the nominative case, indicating the beginning. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, Ya Seen, that they said: O Muhammad. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, through various chains of narration, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, Ya Seen, that he said: O human being. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and Ikrimah. Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite in the mosque, and he would recite loudly, until some of the Quraysh were bothered by it, so they got up to grab him, and there they saw their hands tied to their necks, and they were blind and could not see. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘We ask you by God and by kinship, O Muhammad.’ He said: ‘There was no clan of the Quraysh except that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a kinship with them.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed until that was removed from them, and then ‘Ya Seen * By the Wise Qur’an’ was revealed until His saying: ‘Or did you not warn them that they would not believe?’ He said: ‘Not one of that group believed.’” There are narrations on this topic about the reason for its revelation, and this narration is the best and closest to the truth. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The shackles are between the chest and the chin, ‘so they are bound head-first’ as an animal is bound by a bridle. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: {And We placed before them a barrier} the verse, he said: They would pass by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) but could not see him. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: The Quraysh gathered at the door of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) waiting for him to come out so that they could harm him, and that was difficult for him, so Gabriel came to him with Surah Yasin and ordered him to go out to them, so he took a handful of dirt and went out reciting it and throwing dirt on their heads, but they did not see him until he passed by, and one of them started touching his head and found dirt, and one of them came and said: What is making you sit here? They said: We are looking for Muhammad, so he said: I saw him entering the mosque, so he said: Get up, for he has bewitched you. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that he said: Banu Salamah were in a part of Madinah and wanted to move closer to the mosque. Then God revealed: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have put forth and what they left behind. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called them and said: He records your footsteps. Then he recited the verse to them and they left. Al-Firyabi, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. In Sahih Muslim and elsewhere, it is narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: “Banu Salamah wanted to sell their homes and move closer to the mosque. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: O Banu Salamah, your homes record your footsteps.”
36:13: His statement: 13- And present to them an example of the people of the city. We have already discussed something similar to this in Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat An-Naml. The meaning is: Present an example for them, or present an example for yourself of the people of the city: that is, compare them to yourself as the people of the city. So based on the first, when God Almighty said: Indeed, you are among the messengers and said: To warn a people, He said, “Say to them: I am not an innovation among the messengers, for shortly before me came the people of the city as messengers, and they warned them with what I warned you, and they mentioned monotheism, and they feared the Resurrection, and they were given good tidings of the bliss of the eternal home.” And regarding the second, when he said: Indeed, warning does not benefit him whom God has led astray and decreed that he will not believe, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Give yourself and your people an example. That is, give them an example in your opinion of the people of the village, to whom three messengers came and they did not believe, and the messengers were patient in the face of the harm, and you came to them as one, and your people are more than the people of the three, for they came to the people of the village, and you were sent to all of mankind. The meaning is: Give them an example like the people of the village. That is, tell them a strange story, the story of the people of the village. So the example was omitted, and the people of the village was used in its place in the grammar. It was said that there was no need for the omission, rather the meaning is: Make the people of the village an example for them, so that example and the people of the village are the objects of strike, or the people of the village is a substitute for example. We have already discussed the first of these two objects, whether it is example or the people of the village. It has been said that the use of parables is sometimes used to describe a strange situation with another similar situation, as in His statement: “God presents an example to those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot.” And it is used at other times to describe a strange situation and explain it to people without intending to apply it to its counterpart, as in His statement: And We have presented to you examples, meaning, We have explained to you wonderful and strange situations: they are like examples in their strangeness. So His statement here, And present to them an example, can be considered both ways. Al-Qurtubi said: This village is Antioch according to all commentators, and His statement, When there came to it the messengers, is a substitute for inclusion from the people of the village, and the messengers are the companions of Jesus, whom He sent to the people of Antioch to call people to God.
36:14: God the Almighty attributed the sending to Himself in His saying: 14- When We sent to them two because Jesus sent them by the command of God the Almighty, and it is possible that God sent them after Jesus was raised to heaven, so they denied their message, and it was said that they beat them and imprisoned them. It was said that the names of the two were John and Simon. It was also said that the names of the three were Sadiq, Masadduq, and Salmum, as Ibn Jarir and others said. It was also said that they were Simon, John, and Paul. So We reinforced with a third The majority read it with a shaddah, and Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim, read it with a light zay. Al-Jawhari said that So We reinforced means that we strengthened and intensified, so the two readings on this have the same meaning. It was said that the light meaning means we overcame and subdued, and from this And He strengthened me in speech and the shaddah meaning we strengthened and multiplied. It was said that this third was Simon. And others said that So they said, Indeed, we are messengers to you" means that all three of them said, and they came with this statement of theirs to confirm the previous denial of the two. Denying them both is denying the third, because they were all sent with one thing, which is to call to God Almighty. This sentence is a new answer to an implied question, as if it was said: What did these messengers say after they were reinforced with a third?
36:15: Likewise, sentence 15 - They said, 'You are only human beings like us,' is a new answer to an implied question: as if it was said, So what did the people of Antioch say to them? It was said: They said, You are only human beings like us, meaning you share with us in humanity, so you have no special advantage over us. Then they explicitly denied the sending down of the heavenly books, saying, And the Most Gracious has not sent down anything, of what you and others before you claim from the messengers and their followers, you are only lying, meaning you are only lying in your claim of that, so He answered them by proving their messengership with words that strongly confirm the repeated denial from the people of Antioch.
36:16: And it is their saying: 16- Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you. So they confirmed the answer with the oath that is understood from their saying: Our Lord knows, and with that, and with lam.
36:17: 17- And our duty is only to convey the clear message. That is, what is required of us from our Lord is to convey His message clearly and clearly, and we are not required to do anything else. This sentence is a new sentence like the one before it.
36:18: Likewise, sentence 18 - "They said, 'Indeed, we consider you a bad omen.'" It is a new sentence in response to an implied question: "We consider you a bad omen. You could not find an answer to respond to the messengers with it." Muqatil said: The rain was withheld from them for three years. It was said that they continued to warn them for ten years, then they returned to their arrogance and haughtiness when their chests became constricted and their reasons exhausted them. They said: "If you do not desist, we will surely stone you." That is, if you do not abandon this call and turn away from this statement, we will stone you. "And a painful punishment will touch you from Us." That is, severe and horrific. Al-Farra' said: Most of what is mentioned in the Qur'an about stoning means killing. Qatadah said: It is similar to stoning. It was said that the meaning of painful punishment is killing, and it was said that it means cursing, and it was said that it is painful torture without being restricted to a specific type, and this is what appears to be the case.
36:19: Then the messengers answered them, refuting their claim that they were being seen as omens. 19- "They said, 'Your bad omen is with you,' meaning your bad omen is with you from yourselves, it is incumbent upon you, and it is not from our bad omen." Al-Farra' said: Your bad omen is with you: meaning your livelihood and your deeds, and Qatada said the same. The majority read "your bad omen" as an active participle, meaning whatever good or evil has flown to you. Al-Hasan read "your bad omen, meaning your bad omen if you remember. The majority of the seven and others read it with an interrogative hamza followed by the conditional in," according to the difference of opinion among them regarding facilitation and emphasis, and inserting an alif between the two hamzas or not. Abu Ja'far, Zur ibn Hubaish, Ibn al-Samee', and Talhah read it with two open hamzas. Al-A'mash, 'Isa ibn 'Umar, and al-Hasan read "ayn" with a fatha on the hamza and a sukoon on the ba' in the adverbial form. Sibawayh and Yunus differed over which of the two is answered when a question and a conditional sentence come together. Sibawayh held that the question is answered, while Yunus held that the condition is answered. According to both opinions, the answer here is omitted: If you mention your pastries with you, as indicated by what preceded it. Al-Majshun read that you mentioned with an open hamza: because you mentioned. Then they turned away from what the question and condition imply, that the reminder is a cause of bad luck, and said: Rather, you are a people who are extravagant, meaning that is not the case. Rather, you are a people whose habit is to be extravagant in sin. Qatadah said: Extravagant in your superstition. Yahya ibn Salam said: Extravagant in your disbelief. Ibn Bahr said: Extravagance here means corruption, and extravagance in origin means exceeding the limit in opposing the truth.
36:20: 20- And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running. He was Habib bin Israel the carpenter. He was a carpenter, and it was said a cobbler, and it was said a plasterer. Mujahid and Muqatil said: He was Habib bin Israel the carpenter, and he used to carve idols. Qatada said: He used to worship God in a cave, and when he heard the report of the messengers, he came running. The phrase He said, ‘O my people, follow the messengers’ is a new answer to an implied question: as if it was said, So what did he say to them upon his arrival? So it was said: “O my people, follow the messengers. These are the ones who were sent to you, for they have come with the truth.”
36:21: Then he confirmed that and repeated it, saying: 21- Follow those who do not ask you for a reward meaning they do not ask you for a reward for the guidance they brought you and they are guided meaning the messengers.
36:22: Then he highlighted the speech in the context of advising himself, wanting to advise his people, so he said: 22- And why should I not worship He who created me? That is, what obstacle on my part prevents me from worshipping the One who created me. Then he returned to addressing them to clarify that he did not mean himself, but rather he meant them with his speech, so he said: And to Him you will be returned, and he did not say to Him I will return, and in it is an exaggeration in the threat.
36:23: Then he returned to the first course for the purpose of emphasis and further clarification, saying: 23- Shall I take other gods besides Him? So he made the denial directed at himself, and they are the ones meant by it: that is, I will not take other gods besides God and worship them, and abandon the worship of the One who deserves to be worshipped and He is the One who created me. Then he explained the state of these idols that they worship besides God, the Most High, as a denial of them, and a clarification of the misguidance of their minds and the deficiency of their perception, so he said: If the Most Gracious intends me harm, their intercession will not avail me at all, meaning at least any benefit, nor will they save me from that harm that the Most Gracious intends me. This sentence is an attribute of the gods, or a new sentence to explain their state in the lack of benefit and defense, and his saying: will not avail is the answer to the condition, and Talhah bin Musarraf read if He intends me with a fat-ha on the ya’.
36:24: He said: 24- Then I would be in clear error. That is, if I were to take gods besides Him, I would be in clear and obvious error. This is an allusion to them, as mentioned previously, and error is loss.
36:25: Then he declared his faith in a clear statement that left no doubt, saying: 25- Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen. With these words he addressed the messengers. The commentators said: The people wanted to kill him, so he turned to the messengers and said: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, O messengers, so listen. That is, listen to my faith and bear witness to it for me. It was also said that he addressed his people with these words when they wanted to kill him due to his stubbornness in religion and his severity in adhering to the truth. So when he said this and declared his faith, they pounced on him and killed him. It was also said that they trampled him underfoot. It was also said that they burned him. It was also said that they dug a hole for him and threw him in it. It was also said that they did not kill him, but that God raised him to the sky, so he is in Paradise. Al-Hasan said the same. It was also said that they sawed him apart.
36:26: 26- It was said, ‘Enter Paradise’ meaning that it was said to him as an honor for him by entering it after he was killed, as is the way of God with the martyrs of His servants. According to the saying of those who say that he was raised to the sky and was not killed, the meaning is: When they wanted to kill him, God saved him from being killed, and it was said to him, ‘Enter Paradise’. So when he entered it and saw it, He said, ‘Oh, would that my people knew * That my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored ones’. The sentence is a new answer to an implied question: What did he say after it was said to him, ‘Enter Paradise’, and he entered it? So it was said, ‘Oh, would that my people knew,’ etc.
36:27: And what is in 27- By what He forgave me is the verbal noun: meaning by the forgiveness of my Lord, and it was said that it is the relative pronoun: meaning by the one who forgave me my Lord, and the pronoun is omitted: meaning my Lord forgave, and this was deemed weak because there is no meaning to his wishing that his people would know about his forgiven sins, and what is meant is only his wish that his people would know about his Lord's forgiveness of him. Al-Farra' said: It is an interrogative with the meaning of astonishment, as if he said: By what did my Lord forgive me? Al-Kisa'i said: If this was correct, he would have said by whom without an alif. The response to this is that it has been proven in the Arabic language even if it is broken in relation to its omission, and from this is the saying of the poet: Why did he insult me like a pig wallowing in filth? There are two opinions regarding the meaning of his wish: One is that he wished they knew about his condition so that they would know his good end and praiseworthy outcome, in order to spite them. Another said that he wished they knew about that so that they would believe like his belief and reach the same state as him. Al-Faryabi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {And present to them an example of the companions of the city}. He said: It is Antioch. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Buraydah. Ibn Saad and Ibn Asakir narrated from Al-Kalbi from Abi Salih from Ibn Abbas who said: There were 1900 years between Moses, son of Imran, and Jesus, son of Mary, and there was no gap between them. He sent 1000 prophets from the Children of Israel between them, in addition to those who were sent from other than them. There were 569 years between the birth of Jesus and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. In the first of these, He sent three prophets, which is His statement: {When We sent to them two, but they denied them, so We reinforced them with a third}. The one who was reinforced was Simon, who was one of the disciples. The period in which God did not send a messenger was 434 years. Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him regarding his statement: {Your bad omen is with you}. He said: Your bad luck is with you. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: {And there came from the farthest part of the city a man}. He said: He was Habib Al-Najjar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him from another chain of transmission, he said: The name of the companion of Yasin was Habib, and leprosy had spread rapidly in him. Al-Hakim narrated from Ibn Masoud, he said: When the companion of Yasin said: O my people, follow the messengers, they strangled him to death. Then he turned to the prophets and said: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen, meaning bear witness to me.
36:28: When they did this to Habib Al-Najjar, God became angry with him and hastened their vengeance and destroyed them with the blast. The meaning of 28- And We did not send down upon his people after him meaning upon the people of Habib Al-Najjar after they killed him, or after God raised him to the heavens according to the previous difference any army from the heaven to destroy them and take revenge on them: meaning We did not need to send soldiers from the heaven to destroy them as happened to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Badr when the angels were sent to aid him and fight his enemies. And We would not have sent down meaning it is not correct in Our judgment and wisdom to send down an army to destroy them because Our judgment and decree had preceded that their destruction would be with the blast, not by sending down an army. Qatada, Mujahid and Al-Hasan said: meaning We did not send down upon them any message from the heavens nor any prophet after he was killed. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: They are the angels who descend with revelation to the prophets. It appears that the meaning of the Qur’anic system is to belittle their status and diminish their matter: that is, they are not worthy of us sending down an army from heaven to destroy them.
36:29: Rather, We destroyed them with a single blast, as is indicated by His statement: 29- It was only a single blast meaning that the punishment, vengeance, or punishment was only a single blast that Gabriel shouted at them and destroyed them. The commentators said: Gabriel took hold of the doorposts of the city, then shouted at them, and behold, they were dead, no sound could be heard from them, like a fire when it is extinguished. This is the meaning of His statement: And behold, they were extinguished meaning a people who were extinguished and dead. He likened them to a fire when it is extinguished, because life is like a bright fire, and death is like its extinction. The majority read a blast in the accusative case, as if it were incomplete, and its subject is a pronoun that refers to what is understood from the context, as we mentioned previously. Abu Ja`far, Shaiba, Al-A`raj, Mu`adh, and Al-Qari read it with the nominative case, on the basis that kan is complete, meaning it occurred and happened. Abu Hatim and many grammarians rejected this reading because of the feminine ending in his statement, if it was. Abu Hatim said: If it were as Abu Ja`far read it, he would have said, If it was only a blast. Al-Zajjaj estimated this reading by saying, If there was only a blast upon them, only a single blast, while others estimated it as, It did not fall upon them except a single blast. Abdullah bin Mas`ud read, If it was only a single wineskin, and the wineskin is the blast. An-Nahhas said: This is contrary to the Mushaf. Also, the well-known language is Zaqan yazaqu if it shouts, and from it is the proverb heavier than Al-Zawaqi, so based on this, it should be Zaqwa. The answer to this is what Al-Jawhari mentioned: Al-Zaqqu and Al-Zaqqi are verbal nouns, and Al-Sada yazaqu zaqqan” means it shouted, and every shouter shouts, and the wineskin is the blast.
36:30: 30- "O grief for the servants The majority read it with the accusative case of hasrah" as an indefinite vocative as if he called out to the grief and said to it: This is your time, so come. It was said that it is the accusative case as a source, and the vocative is omitted, and the meaning is: O these people, grieve with grief. Qatada and Abi, in a narration from him, read with the damma of "hasrah" as a vocative. Al-Farra' said: In explaining this reading: The preferred reading is the accusative case, and if it had raised the indefinite noun, it would have been correct. He cited as evidence things that he transmitted from the Arabs, including that he heard from the Arabs, "O you who are concerned with our affair, do not be concerned," and he recited: Oh house, the decay has changed it An-Nahhas said: “This invalidates most of the vocative case. What he mentioned could mean: ‘O you who are concerned, do not worry about our affairs.’ The verse could mean: ‘O home.’ The true meaning of regret is that a person is overcome by remorse that makes him feel regretful. Ibn Jarir said: “The meaning is: ‘O regret of the servants for themselves, and remorse and longing for their mockery of the Messengers of God.’ This is supported by the reading of Ibn Abbas and Ali bin Al-Hussein: ‘O regret of the servants’ with the addition. This reading was narrated from Abu. Ad-Dahhak said: “It is the regret of the angels for the disbelievers when they denied the Messengers.” It was also said that it is from the words of the man who came from the farthest part of the city. It was said that the one who said: Oh, what a pity for the servants is the disbelieving disbelievers, and the servants are the messengers, because when they saw the punishment they regretted their killing and wished to believe. This was said by Abu Al-Aaliyah and Mujahid. It was also said that the pity for them is from God Almighty by way of metaphor to magnify what they had done. Ibn Hurmuz, Muslim bin Jundub, Ikrimah and Abu Al-Zinad read Oh, what a pity with a silent ha to make the connection like a pause. It was read Oh, what a pity as it was read in Surat Az-Zumar. The phrase There came not to them a messenger but they used to mock him is a new sentence introduced to explain what they were doing of denying the messengers and mocking them, and that this is the reason for the pity for them.
36:31: Then He, the Almighty, was amazed at their condition, as they did not consider their peers from the past nations, so He said: 31- Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them? That is, do they not know the number of generations We destroyed before them from the past nations? The phrase to them they will not return is a substitute for how many We have destroyed according to the meaning. Sibawayh said: An is a substitute for how many, which is a report sentence, and that is why it was used to substitute something that is not an interrogative, and the meaning is: Have they not seen that the generations We destroyed will not return to them? Al-Farra’ said: How many is in the accusative case for two reasons: One of them is birowa, and he cited as evidence for this the fact that in the reading of Ibn Mas’ud, did they not see those We destroyed? The other reason is that how many is in the accusative case with ahlakana. An-Nahhas said: The first statement is impossible, because kam does not affect what precedes it because it is an interrogative, and it is impossible for an interrogative to be included in the scope of what precedes it. The same applies to it if it is a predicate, even though Sibawayh had hinted at some of this and made them a substitute for kam, and Al-Mubarrad vehemently rejected that.
36:32: 32- "And verily, all who are brought before Us will be brought forth." That is, they will be brought before Us on the Day of Resurrection for recompense. Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamzah read "lama" with a shaddah, while the rest read it without a shaddah. Al-Farra' said: Whoever makes "lama with a shaddah makes illah mean illah and inna mean ma": that is, "nothing but all" will be brought before Us. The meaning of "all is gathered, so it is a fa'il with the meaning of maf'ul, and with Us" is an adverbial phrase for it. As for the lightened reading, it is the lightened version of the heavy one, and what follows it is raised by the subject, and the tanween of "kull" replaces the complement ilaihi and what follows it is the predicate, and the lam is the distinguishing mark between the lightened and the negative. Abu Ubaidah said: "Ma" in this reading is redundant, and according to him, the interpretation is: and verily, all will be brought before Us. It was also said that the meaning of "muhajirun is mu'tadhabun," but it is preferable that it has its literal meaning of being brought to account.
36:33: Then the Almighty mentioned the proof of monotheism and the gathering, along with enumerating and reminding of the blessings, saying: 33- And a sign for them is the dead land. So a sign is the predicate that comes first, and its indefiniteness is for emphasis, and for them is its description, or it is related to a sign because it means a mark, and the land is the subject. It is possible for a sign to be the subject because it is specialized by the description, and what follows it is the predicate. The people of Medina read the dead with emphasis, while the rest did not. The phrase We revived it is a new sentence explaining how it is a sign. It was said that it is a description of the land, so God alerted them with this to the revival of the dead and reminded them of His blessings and the perfection of His power, for He, the Almighty, revived the land with vegetation: and brought forth from it the grains that they eat and are nourished by, and this is the meaning of His statement: And We brought forth from it grain and from it they eat. It is the grains that they eat, and the introduction of it is to indicate that grain is most of what is eaten and most of what is used for livelihood.
36:34: 34- And We placed therein gardens of date palms and grapevines meaning We placed on the earth gardens of various types of date palms and grapes, and He mentioned them specifically because they contain fruits and are the most beneficial to the servants. And We made springs gush forth therein meaning We made some springs gush forth in the earth, so the described was deleted and the adjective was used in its place, or the object is the springs, and from is an addition according to the opinion of those who allow its addition in the affirmation, which is Al-Akhfash and those who agreed with him, and what is meant by springs are springs of water. The majority read fajrna with a shaddah, and Janah ibn Hubaysh read it with a tafsir, and fajr and tafjir are like fath and taftih in wording and meaning.
36:35: The lam in 35- that they may eat from its fruit is connected to We made, and the pronoun in from its fruit refers to the mentioned gardens and palm trees. It was also said that it refers to the water of the springs because the fruit is from it, Al-Jurjani said. The majority read its fruit with a fatha on the tha' and the meem, while Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read them with a damma on both, and Al-A'mash read it with a damma on the tha' and a sukoon on the meem. This has already been discussed in Al-An'am. His statement, and what their hands have made is in apposition to its fruit: meaning that they may eat from its fruit and eat what their hands have made, such as juice, molasses, and the like. Likewise, what they planted and dug, with ma being a relative pronoun. It was also said that it is a negative, and the meaning is: they did not make it, but rather the one who made it is God: meaning they found it made and they had no hand in it, and this is the statement of Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil. The public read it as worked and the Kufians read it as worked without the pronoun, and the question in his saying: Do they not then give thanks? is to rebuke and reprimand them for not being grateful for the blessings.
36:36: And the sentence 36 - Glory be to Him who created all pairs is a new sentence introduced to declare Him, glory be to Him, free from what they have done in terms of not being grateful for His aforementioned blessings and expressing their astonishment at their failure to do so. We have already discussed in detail the meaning of Glory be to Him, which is in the estimation of the command to the servants to declare Him free from what is not befitting of Him. Pairs are the types and kinds, because each kind has different colors, tastes, and shapes. From what the earth grows is an explanation of the pairs, meaning everything that grows in it from the aforementioned things and others. And from themselves, meaning He created the pairs from themselves, and they are the males and females. And from what they do not know from the kinds of His creation on land, sea, sky, and earth.
36:37: 37- "And a sign for them is the night. We strip thereof the day." The discussion of this is as we have already mentioned in His statement: "And a sign for them is the dead earth. We have given life to it." The meaning is that this is a sign indicating the Oneness of God, His power, and the necessity of His divinity. Stripping means scraping and pulling. It is said, God stripped him from his body. Then it is used to mean bringing out. So He, the Most High, made the disappearance of light and the coming of darkness like stripping something. This is a powerful metaphor. Then they are in darkness. That is, they enter darkness suddenly and unexpectedly. It is said, We became dark, meaning we entered the darkness of the night. We appeared, meaning we entered at noon. Likewise, We became morning and We became evening. It is also said that it means from it, and the meaning is, We strip it of the light of the day. Al-Farra' said: The day is thrown onto the night, so darkness comes. This is because the root is darkness and the day enters it. So when the sun sets, the day is stripped from the night, meaning it is scraped and removed, so darkness appears.
36:38: 38- And the sun runs to its resting place. The waw may be used in conjunction with the night, and the meaning is: And a sign for them is the sun. It is also possible that the waw is introductory, and the sun is the subject, and what follows it is the predicate, and the statement would be renewed and include a mention of an independent sign. It was said that there is an ellipsis in the statement, and the meaning is: It runs to its resting place, so the lam is for the reason: that is, for the sake of a resting place. It was also said that the lam means to and it was read that way. It was said that what is meant by resting place is the Day of Resurrection, for there it will rest and no longer move. It was also said that its resting place is the furthest point it reaches and does not go beyond. It was also said that it ends when it rises in the summer and ends when it sets in the winter. It was also said that its resting place is under the throne, because it goes there and prostrates, then asks permission to return, and it is given permission. This is the most correct opinion. Al-Hasan said: The sun has three hundred and sixty places of rising in one year, and it descends to one place every day and does not descend for a year. So it runs in those stations, and that is its resting place. Other opinions were said. Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Zain Al-Abidin, his son Al-Baqir, and Al-Sadiq Ibn Al-Baqir read: La Mustaqar Laha with the letter La that to negate the genus, and the construction of Mustaqar with the fat-ha. Ibn Abi Ubaidah read: La Mustaqar Laha with the letter La that to mean not, and Mustaqar is its subject, and Laha is its predicate. The reference in His statement: that is to the running of the sun, meaning that running. The Decree of the Almighty, meaning the Victorious, the Dominant. The All-Knowing, meaning His knowledge encompasses everything. It is possible that the reference is to the settled place, meaning that settled place: the decree of God.
36:39: 39- And the moon - We have determined for it phases. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read al-Qamar in the nominative case as the subject. The rest read it in the accusative case as a preoccupation, and the accusative case of manazil as a second object, because qadarna means we made, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a state: that is, We determined its movement while it has phases, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a circumstantial case: that is, in phases. Abu Ubaid preferred the accusative case for al-Qamar, saying: Because before it is a verb, which is naslakh, and after it is a verb, which is qadarna. Al-Nahhas said: All the Arab scholars, as far as I know, disagree with what he said. Among them is Al-Farra', who said: The nominative case is more pleasing to me. He said: The nominative case was more appropriate for them because it is conjoined with what preceded it, and its meaning is: And a sign for them is the moon. Abu Hatim said: “Raising the voice is more appropriate because you used the pronoun to distract the verb from it, so you raised it as the subject. The mansions are the twenty-eight in which the moon descends every night. They are well-known and will be mentioned later. When the moon is at the end of them, it returns to the beginning, traversing the heavens in twenty-eight nights. Then it disappears for two nights, then it rises as a crescent moon, and it returns to traversing those mansions in the heavens “until it returns like an old cluster of clusters.” Al-Zajjaj said: The cluster of clusters is the stem of the cluster, which has the branches. It is a verb from in’rij, which means turning, meaning it traveled through its mansions. When it is at the end of them, it becomes thin, curved, and small until it becomes like an old cluster of clusters. Based on this, the nun is redundant. Qatadah said: It is the dry, curved cluster of the palm tree. Tha’lab said: The cluster of clusters is what remains in the palm tree when it is cut, and the old one is the worn one. Al-Khalil said: The ‘arjoon’ is the base of the ‘uthq and it is yellow and wide, and it resembles the crescent moon when it is bent. Al-Jawhari said the same: It is the base of the ‘uthq that becomes crescent and the clusters are cut from it, leaving the palm tree dry. ‘Arjoontuhu’ means: I struck it with the ‘uthqon’. Based on this, the ‘nun’ is original. The majority read al-‘arjoon with a damma on the ‘ayn and the ‘jeem. Sulayman al-Taymi read it with a kasra on the ‘ayn and a fatha on the ‘jeem, and they are two dialects. ‘Al-Qadeem’ means: the ancient.
36:40: 40- The sun shall not overtake the moon. The word sun is in the nominative case, because it is not permissible for it to act not in knowledge: that is, it is not correct and it is not possible for the sun to overtake the moon quickly and descend in the same house as the moon, because each of them has authority on its own, so neither can enter upon the other, and its authority is lost until God permits the Day of Resurrection, and the sun rises from the West. Ad-Dahhak said: Its meaning is that when the sun rises, the moon will have no light, and when the moon rises, the sun will have no light. Mujahid said: That is, the light of one of them does not resemble the light of the other. Al-Hasan said: They do not meet in the sky on the night of the crescent moon in particular, and Yahya ibn Salam said the same. It was also said that its meaning is: When they meet in the sky, one of them is in front of the other in a house that they do not share. It was also said that the moon is in the lowest heaven, and the sun is in the fourth heaven. This was mentioned by An-Nahhas and Al-Mahdawi. An-Nahhas said: The best and clearest thing that has been said about its meaning is that the moon's movement is fast, and the sun does not overtake it in its movement. As for His statement, And the joining of the sun and the moon, this is when the sun is prevented from rising, as was explained previously in Al-An’am, and it will also appear in Surat Al-Qiyamah. Their joining together is a sign of the end of this world and the establishment of the Hour. Nor does the night outstrip the day, meaning it does not outstrip it and miss it, but rather it follows it, and each one of them comes in its time and does not outstrip the other. It was said that what is meant by night and day are their two signs, which are the sun and the moon, so it is the opposite of His statement, Nor shall the sun overtake the moon, meaning, nor shall the moon outstrip the sun. The introduction of precedence instead of overtaking is due to the speed of the moon’s movement. Each in an orbit floats, the tanween in each replaces the complement to it, meaning, each one of them. The orbit is the round body, the round surface, or the circle. The disagreement over whether the sky is spread out or round is well-known. Swimming means moving with expansion and ease. The joining together in His statement, they swim is in consideration of the difference in their risings, so it is as if they are multiple due to their multiplicity, or what is meant is the sun, the moon, and the planets. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding the verse: {And We did not send down upon his people after him}, he said: We did not suffer them with multitudes: meaning the matter was easier for us than that. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: {O regret for the servants}, he said: Woe to the servants. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse: {O regret for the servants}, he said: Regret is for the servants who {There came not to them a messenger but they used to ridicule him}, he said: Regret is for them on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse: {And what their hands had made}, he said: They found it made, their hands had not made it: meaning the Euphrates, Tigris, Balkh River and the like. {So will they not be grateful?} for this. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr who said: I asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about the statement, And the sun runs to its resting place. He said, Its resting place is beneath the Throne. In a version of his hadith narrated by al-Bukhari and others, he said: I was with the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in the mosque at sunset, and he said, O Abu Dharr, do you know where the sun sets? I said, God and His Messenger know best. He said, It goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne. This is what God said, And the sun runs to its resting place. In a version of his hadith also narrated by Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and others, he said, O Abu Dharr, do you know where it goes? I said, God and His Messenger know best. He said, “It goes until it prostrates before its Lord, then it asks permission to return, and He gives it permission. It is as if it has been told, ‘Up from where you came,’ and it rises from its setting place.” Then he recited, Upon its resting place. This is the reading of Abdullah. Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and others narrated a similar statement from Ibn Umar. Al-Khatib narrated in his book, The Stars, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: And the moon - We have determined for it mansions 13:28, he said: They are twenty-eight mansions that the moon enters every month: fourteen of them are in the Levant, and fourteen of them are in the Yemenite. The first of them are Ash-Shartayn, Al-Batin, Thuraya, Al-Dabran, Al-Haq’ah, Al-Hana’ah, Al-Dhira’, Al-Nathra, Al-Taraf, Al-Jabha, Al-Dabrah, Al-Sarfah, Al-Aw’a, and Al-Samak, which is the last of the Levantine, and Al-Ghafr, Al-Zabana, Al-Iklil, Al-Qalb, Al-Shula, Al-Na’aim, Al-Baldah, Sa’d Al-Dhabih, Sa’d Baligh, Sa’d Al-Su’ud, Sa’d Al-Akhbiyyah, Muqaddam Al-Dali, Naakhil Al-Dali, and Al-Hout, which is the last of the Yemenite. When it has traveled these twenty-eight mansions, it returns like an old cluster of dates, as it was at the beginning of the month. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, regarding his statement: like an old cluster of dates, meaning the base of the old cluster.
36:41: Then God Almighty mentioned another type of blessings He bestowed upon His servants, saying: 41- And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship. That is, an indication and a sign. It was said that the meaning of sign here is a lesson, a blessing, or a warning. There is a difference of opinion as to the meaning of We carried their offspring and to whom the pronoun refers. The first pronoun, and a sign for them, refers to the people of Mecca, or to the disbelievers of the Arabs, or to all disbelievers existing at the time of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him). Some say the pronoun refers to past generations, and the meaning is that God carried the offspring of past generations in the laden ark. So the two pronouns are different. This was related by An-Nahhas on the authority of Ali ibn Sulayman Al-Akhfash. Others say the two pronouns refer to the disbelievers of Mecca and others like them. The meaning is that God carried their offspring, including their children and the weak among them, on the ark. God bestowed this favor upon them, meaning that they carry them with them on ships when they travel, or they send their children to trade for them in them. Offspring refers to fathers and grandfathers, and the ark refers to Noah's Ark, meaning that God carried the fathers and grandfathers of these people in Noah's Ark. Al-Wahidi said: Offspring refers to fathers as well as children. Abu Uthman said: “The fathers were called offspring because offspring of sons are from them. It was also said that offspring is the sperm found in the wombs of women. The wombs were likened to a laden ark. The second opinion is more correct, then the first, then the third. As for the fourth, it is extremely remote and strange. We have already discussed offspring and its derivation in Surat Al-Baqarah in full. Laden means filled and replenished. Ark is used for both singular and plural as mentioned in Yunus. The nominative case of ‘aayah’ is that it is an advanced predicate, and the subject is ‘ana hamala’ or vice versa as we mentioned earlier. It was also said that the pronoun in His statement, “And a sign for them” refers to the servants mentioned in His statement, O grief for the servants, because He said after that, And a sign for them is the dead land, and He said, And a sign for them is the night. Then He said, And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring, so it is as if He said, And a sign for the servants is that We carried the offspring of the servants. It is not necessary for one of the two pronouns to mean some of them, and the other pronoun to mean the other, and this is a good statement.
36:42: 42- And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride. That is, We created for them something similar to the ark on which they ride, based on the fact that ma is the relative pronoun. Mujahid, Qatadah, and a group of commentators said: They are camels that He created for them to ride on land, like ships that they ride. This was stated by Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, and Abu Malik. An-Nahhas said: This is more authentic because it has a continuous chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was also said: They are the ships that were built after Noah’s Ark.
36:43: 43- And if We will, We could drown them, and there will be no one to cry out to them, nor will they be saved. This is part of the verse with which God bestowed His favor upon them. The reason for this favor is that He did not drown them in the depths of the seas, despite His ability to do so. The pronoun refers either to the owners of the offspring, or to the offspring, or to all of them, according to the different opinions. The cry means the one who cries out, and the one who cries out is the helper: that is, there is no one to help them who can save them if We will to drown them. It was said: it means protection. The meaning of they save is that they are saved. It is said that He saved him and rescued him, if He freed him from a harm.
36:44: 44- Except by mercy from Us is an exception devoid of the most general causes: that is, they have no cry for help, nor are they saved for anything except by mercy from Us. This is what Al-Kisa'i, Al-Zajjaj and others said. It was also said that it is a disjunctive exception: that is, but by mercy from Us. It was also said that it is accusative as a source by an implied verb. And the accusative of enjoyment is in apposition to mercy: that is, We grant them enjoyment in worldly life for a time which is death, as Qatada said. Yahya bin Salam said: until the Resurrection.
36:45: 45- And when it is said to them, ‘Fear what is before you and what is behind you,’ meaning, what is before you of calamities and misfortunes, for they encompass you, and what is behind you of them. Qatadah said that the meaning of Fear what is before you is what happened to the nations who came before you, and what is behind you in the Hereafter. Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said, What is before you is what has passed of sins, and what is behind you is what remains of them. It was also said, What is before you is this world, and what is behind you is the Hereafter, as Sufyan said. Al-Tha’labi reported the opposite of this statement from Ibn Abbas. It was also said, What is before you is what is apparent to you, and what is behind you is what is hidden from you. The answer to if is omitted, and the meaning is: If that is said to them, they turn away, as indicated by unless they turn away from it “that you may receive mercy,” meaning hoping to receive mercy, or so that you may receive mercy, or hoping that you may receive mercy.
36:46: 46- And there never comes to them a sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it. What is the negative particle ma, and the present tense indicates renewal, and the first is added for emphasis, and the second is for partiality. The meaning is: There never comes to them a sign proving the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the truth of the monotheism he called for under any circumstances except that they turn away from it. Its apparent meaning includes the verses of revelation and the verses of creation, and the phrase except that they turn away from it is in the accusative case as a state, as was previously explained in more than one place. What is meant by turning away is not paying attention to it, and abandoning the correct consideration of it. This verse is related to His statement: Oh, how great is the grief for the servants! There comes not a messenger to them except that they ridicule him. That is, when the messengers come to them, they deny them, and when they are brought verses, they turn away from them.
36:47: 47- And when it is said to them, ‘Spend from what God has provided for you,’ meaning, give charity to the poor from what God has given you and bestowed upon you of wealth. Al-Hasan said: meaning, the Jews were commanded to feed the poor. Muqatil said: The believers said to the infidels of Quraysh 106:Spend on the poor from what you claim belongs to God from your wealth of crops and livestock, as in the words of God Almighty: And they have assigned to God a share of what He created of crops and livestock. So their response was what God related about them in His words: Those who disbelieved said to those who believed, mocking them and mocking their saying, Should we feed those whom God would feed if He willed? That is, those whom God would provide for if He willed. They had heard the Muslims say: God is the Provider, and He enriches whomever He wills and impoverishes whomever He wills. So it was as if they were trying to force the Muslims with this statement and said: We agree with God’s will and do not feed those whom God has not fed. This is a mistake on their part, stubbornness and a false argument, because God Almighty enriched some of His creation and impoverished others, and He commanded the rich to feed the poor and tested him with it in what He had prescribed for him from his wealth as charity. Their statement, Whosoever, if God willed, He would feed is, although it is a correct statement in itself, since they intended thereby to deny the power of God, or to deny the permissibility of the command to spend when God has power, their argument from this perspective is invalid. His statement, You are nothing but in manifest error is a complete statement of the disbelievers. The meaning is: You, O Muslims, in asking for money, and our command to feed the poor, are in a most clear and obvious error. It was said that it is from the words of God, the Exalted, in response to this statement made by the disbelievers. Al-Qushayri and Al-Mawardi said: The verse was revealed about a group of heretics. There were some infidels among the Quraysh and others from among the Arabs who were heretics and did not believe in the Creator, so they said this statement to mock the Muslims and contradict them. Al-Qurtubi narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas.
36:48: 48- And they say, When will this promise come to pass? which you promise us of torment, resurrection, and the destination of Paradise or Hell, if you should be truthful in what you say and write down. They say this to mock and ridicule the believers. Their intention is to deny this completely, to deny its fulfillment, and to reject its occurrence.
