36:49: So God Almighty answered them by saying: 49- They await nothing but a single blast meaning they await nothing but a single blast, which is Israfil’s blowing of the trumpet which will seize them while they are disputing meaning they are disputing among themselves about buying and selling and other worldly matters, and this is the first blast, which is the blast of the thunderbolt. There are different readings for yakhḍasmūn. Hamzah read it with a sukun on the kha and a soft sad from khaḍās yakhḍasmūn, meaning: they dispute with each other, so the object is omitted. Abu ʿAmr and Qalun read it with a sukun on the kha and a doubled sad. Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir and Hisham read it likewise, except that they made the fathah on the khaʿ clear. The rest read it with a kasrah on the khaʿ and a doubled sad. The original in the three readings is yakhḍasmūn, so the taʿ was assimilated into the sad. Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir and Hisham completely transferred the fathah on the taʿ to the consonant before it. Abu ʿAmr and Qalun stole its vowel to indicate that the sukun corrected the khaʿ. The rest omitted its vowel, so two consonants met, so they kasrahed the first one. It was narrated from Abu ʿAmr and Qalun that they read with a sukun on the khaʿ and a doubled sad. This is a problematic reading due to the meeting of two consonants in it. Abu ʿAmr read yakhḍasmūn according to the original.
36:50: 50- They will not be able to make a will meaning some of them will not bequeath to others their money or what they owe, or they will not be able to recommend to others repentance and abandonment of sins, rather they will die in their markets and places nor will they return to their families meaning to the homes they died outside of. It was said that the meaning is: they will not return to their families with a word, and this is report of what will befall them at the first blast.
36:51: Then the Almighty informed about what will befall them at the second blast, saying: 51- And the Trumpet will be blown, which is the blast that will raise them from their graves. That is why He said: Then at once they will hasten from the graves to their Lord, meaning they will hasten. And between the two blasts there will be forty years. And He expressed the future with the past tense when He said and will be blown, indicating that it will happen, as the people of eloquence have mentioned. They made this verse an example of it. The Trumpet, with a sukoon on the waw, is the horn that Israfil will blow into, as mentioned in the Sunnah. And giving this name to the horn is well-known in the Arabic language, and from it is the saying of the poet: We butted them on the day of the two Ghorins with a severe butting, not like the butting of two Tyrians. Which of the two horns. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-An’am. Qatada said: The trumpets are the plural of trumpet, meaning He blew the souls into the trumpet. The ajdaths are the plural of jadtha, which is the grave. The ajdaf are read with a fa’, which is a language, and the eloquent language with a tha’. An-Nasl and An-Naslaan: to hasten in walking. It is said nasla yansal, like daraba yadrubu, and it is said yansal with a damma, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: So separate my clothes from your clothes and they will fall off And the other said: The wolf's lions became cold at night, so they fled.
36:52: And they said: 52- "Woe to us! Who has raised us from our beds? That is, they said when they were raised from the graves by the blast, Woe to us! They cried out, Woe to them! As if they were saying to him, Come, for this is the time for you to come!" And those who rise are the disbelievers. Ibn al-Anbari said: Stopping at "Woe to us" is a good stop. Then the speech begins with the words, "Who has raised us from our beds?" They thought, due to the confusion of their minds over what they witnessed of the horror and the fear that had entered them, that they were asleep. The majority read "Woe to us. Ibn Abi Layla read Woe to us" and added the ta'. The majority read "Who has raised us? with a fat-ha on the m of min" as a question mark. Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Abu Nahik read it with a kasra on the m as a preposition. This reading was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib. According to this reading, "min is related to woe, and the majority read min ba'athna." In Abi’s reading, Man ahbana man haba min nawmihu means: if he wakes up, and Tha’lab recited in this reading: A critic came at night to blame me, and no critic had ever relied on me before. It was said that they say this when they see Hell. Abu Salih said: When the first blast is blown, the punishment will be lifted from the people of the graves and they will sleep until the second blast. The phrase This is what the Most Gracious has promised and the messengers have spoken the truth is an answer to them from the angels, or from the believers. It was also said that it is from the speech of the disbelievers, answering each other. Al-Farra’ said the first, and Mujahid said the second. Qatada said: It is from the statement of God, the Most High, and what is in His statement, What the Most Gracious has promised is a relative pronoun and its antecedent is omitted, and the meaning is: This which the Most Gracious has promised and the messengers have spoken the truth about has come true for them and has descended upon you. The objects of the promise and the truth are omitted: that is, the Most Gracious promised it to you and the messengers spoke the truth about it. The original is The Most Gracious promised it to you and spoke the truth about it, or The Most Gracious promised us and the messengers spoke the truth about it, meaning that this is from the statement of the believers or from the statement of the disbelievers.
36:53: 53- It will be only a single blast meaning that the aforementioned blast was only a single blast that Israfil made by blowing the trumpet and at once they will all be brought before Us meaning they will be gathered and brought before Us quickly for the reckoning and punishment.
36:54: 54- So today no soul will be wronged from among the souls in anything of what it deserves: that is, nothing will be reduced from the reward for its deeds, nor will it be wronged in any way. And you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do that is, except for the recompense for what you used to do in this world, or except for what you used to do: that is, because of it, or in exchange for it. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Malik regarding his statement, Indeed, We carried their offspring (1:11), that he said: In Noah’s ark, in which he carried two of each pair. And We created for them from the like thereof that which they ride (1:11), that he said: The ships in the sea and rivers in which people ride. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar from Abu Salih. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And We created for them from the like thereof that which they ride (1:11), that he said: These are the ships that were made after Noah’s ark. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding the verse, that he said: He means camels. God created them as you have seen, so they are the ships on land that they ride and ride. The same was narrated from al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Abdullah ibn Shaddad and Mujahid. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, regarding the verse, they will not be able to make bequests, that he said: The Hour will come while people are in their markets, trading, shearing garments, milking camels, and attending to their needs, and they will not be able to make bequests, nor will they return to their families. Abd ibn Humayd, Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id al-Zuhd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, who said: The Hour will come while a man is shearing garments and a man is milking a she-camel. Then he recited, they will not be able to make bequests, that is, the verse. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Hour will come while two men have spread out their garments, neither trading with them nor folding them up. The Hour will come while a man is cleaning his trough, but he will not water his camel from it. The Hour will come while a man has taken the milk of his she-camel away, but he will not eat it. The Hour will come while a man has raised his food to his mouth, but he will not eat it. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab regarding his statement: Who has raised us from our place of sleep? He said: They sleep a sleep before the resurrection.
36:55: When God, the Exalted, mentioned the state of the disbelievers, He followed it with a narration of the state of His righteous servants, and made it part of what will be said to the disbelievers on that Day, to increase their regret, complete their grief, and complete the affliction that has befallen them and the misery they have witnessed. So when they see the various types of torment that God has prepared for them and the various types of bliss that He has prepared for His friends, it will reach their hearts to a great extent and increase the constriction of their chests to an extent that cannot be measured. The meaning 55- Indeed, the companions of Paradise on that Day will be busy with the pleasures they are experiencing, which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, to avoid caring about the matter of the disbelievers and their destiny in Hell, even if they are related to them. It is better not to specify the busyness with a specific thing. Qatadah and Mujahid said: Their busyness that day will be with the deflowering of virgins. Waki' said: Their busyness will be with listening to... Ibn Kaysan said: By adding some of them to each other. It was said that their preoccupation was that they were in the hospitality of God that day. The Kufians and Ibn Amir read shaghal with two dhammahs. The rest read it with a dhammah on the sheen and a sukoon on the ghain. They are two dialects as Al-Farra’ said. Mujahid and Abu Al-Sammak read it with two fathahs. Yazid Al-Nahwi and Ibn Hubayrah read it with a fathah on the sheen and a sukoon on the ghain. The majority read fakihoon in the nominative case as the predicate of in, and fi shaghal is related to it, or in the accusative case as a hal. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as the predicate of in, and fakihoon is a second predicate. Al-A’mash and Talhah ibn Musarraf read fakiheen in the accusative case as a hal, and fi shaghal is the predicate. Al-Hasan, Abu Ja’far, Abu Haywah, Abu Raja’, Shaybah, Qatadah and Mujahid read fakahoon. Al-Farra’ said: They are two dialects like farah and farah, and al-hazir and al-hazir. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Fakih is the possessor of fruits like tamer and laban, and al-fakkah is the one who enjoys and indulges. Qatada said: Al-Fakkahun are the admiring ones. Abu Zaid said: It is said of a man who is funny: if he is of a good nature and laughs. Mujahid and Al-Dahhak said as Qatada said. Al-Suddi said as Al-Kisa’i said.
36:56: 56- They and their spouses, reclining on couches in shades. This sentence is a new sentence introduced to explain how they were occupied and amused and to complete it with what increased their happiness and joy from their spouses being with them in this manner of reclining on couches. The pronoun, they, is the subject and their spouses is conjoined to it, and the predicate is reclining. It is possible that they is an emphasis of the pronoun in enjoying and their spouses is conjoined to that pronoun, and the raising of reclining is because it is the predicate of a deleted subject, and in shades is related to it or a state, and likewise on couches. Abu al-Baqa’ allowed that in shades is the predicate and on couches is a new sentence. The majority read in shades with a kasra on the dhaal and with an alif, which is the plural of shade. Ibn Masoud, Abd ibn Umair, Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read fi dhillal with a damma on the dhal without an alif, the plural of dhallah. According to both readings, what is meant are the furnishings and curtains that shade them like tents and partitions. Ar'eeq is the plural of ariqah, like safaa'in is the plural of ship, and what is meant by it are the beds in partitions. Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha'lab said: A couch can only be a bed in a dome. Muqatil said: What is meant by shade is the shelters of palaces.
36:57: And sentence 57 - For them therein is fruit explains what they will enjoy in Paradise of food, drink, etc. What is meant is an abundant fruit of every kind. And for them is whatever they request. "What - this is the relative pronoun and the pronoun is omitted, or it is a description or a source, and they request is the present tense of adda'a." Abu Ubaidah said: "They request by wishing." The Arabs say: "Pray for me whatever you wish," meaning wish for it. So-and-so is in the best of what he requests, meaning whatever he wishes for. Al-Zajjaj said: It is from the supplication, meaning whatever the people of Paradise request will come to them, from "I called my servant. Thus, ifti'al can mean the action, like importance means carrying, and travel" means saddlery. It has also been said that ifti'al can mean "tafa'ala, meaning what they request, like their saying artamamu and tartamamu." It was said that the meaning is: whoever among them claims something, it is his, because God has created them in a way that none of them claims something unless it is good and fitting for him to claim it. And ma is the subject and its predicate is lahum and the sentence is conjoined to what preceded it. And it was read yad’un with a lightened pronunciation and its meaning is clear. Ibn al-Anbari said: Stopping at yad’un is a good stop.
36:58: Then it begins 58- "Peace" meaning to them is peace. It was said that peace is the predicate of what: meaning a pure Muslim or one of peace. Al-Zajjaj said: Peace is raised as a substitute for what: meaning and for them is that God greets them, and this is the wish of the people of Paradise. It is better to take his statement: "and for them is what they call for" as a generality, and this peace falls under it primarily, and there is no reason to limit it to a specific type, even though it is the most honorable of its types to achieve the meaning of generality, and to observe what the Qur’anic system requires. It was said that peace is raised as a predicate of a deleted subject: meaning peace is said to them "a word." It was said that peace is a subject, and its predicate is the accusative of a word: meaning peace is said to them a word. It was said that its predicate is from the Lord of the Worlds. It was said that the estimate is: Peace be upon you. This is according to the reading of the majority. Ubayy, Ibn Mas`ud, and `Isa read peace in the accusative case, either as a source or as a circumstantial meaning pure. Peace: either from greeting or from safety. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi read "peace as if he said peace be upon them so that they will not dispute over it. The word saying" is in the accusative case as a source of a deleted verb meaning: God said that to them with a word, or He says it to them with a word, or it is said to them with a word "from a Merciful Lord" meaning from His direction. It was said that God sends a cloud to them with peace. Muqatil said: The angels enter upon the people of Paradise from every gate saying: Peace be upon you, O people of Paradise, from a Merciful Lord.
36:59: 59- And separate yourselves today, O criminals. This is on the basis of the omission of the word, in contrast to what was said to the believers. That is, it is said to the criminals, See them separate, meaning, Isolate yourselves, from māzahu ghayrihu. It is said, māzat ash-shay’ min ash-shay’, meaning, I isolate one thing from another and set it aside. Muqatil said, Its meaning isolate yourselves today, meaning, in the Hereafter, from the righteous. As-Suddi said, Be separate. Az-Zajjaj said, They were isolated from the believers. Qatadah said, They were isolated from every good thing. Ad-Dahhak said, “The criminals will be separated from one another, so the Jews will be separated into a group, the Christians into a group, the Magians into a group, the Sabians into a group, and the idol worshippers into a group.” Dawud ibn al-Jarrah said, The Muslims will be separated from the criminals, except for the people of desires, for they will be with the criminals.
36:60: Then God the Almighty rebuked and admonished them by saying: 60- Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? This is among the things that are said to them. A covenant is a command: that is, did I not command you and convey to you through the tongues of My messengers that you not worship Satan, meaning do not obey him. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, did I not present to you through the tongues of the messengers, O children of Adam? Muqatil said: He means those who were ordered to isolate themselves. Al-Kisa'ik said: No for the prohibition. It was said that what is meant by the covenant here is the pledge taken from them when they were brought forth from the loins of Adam. It was also said that it is the rational proofs that God established for them in the heavens and the earth. The phrase Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy is an explanation for what preceded it of the prohibition against obeying Satan and accepting his whispers.
36:61: And sentence 61 - And that you worship Me is in apposition to that you do not worship, and that in both instances is the explanation of the covenant in which the meaning of the statement is, and it is permissible for it to be a source in them: that is, I did not covenant with you that you should not worship but that you worship Me, or did I not covenant with you to abandon the worship of Satan and to worship Me This is a straight path that is, the worship of God and His Oneness, or the reference to the religion of Islam.
36:62: Then the Almighty mentioned Satan's enmity towards the children of Adam, saying: 62- And he has certainly led astray many a mountain from among you. The lam is the particle used to introduce the oath, and the sentence is a resumption of rebuke and rebuke, meaning, By God, he has certainly led astray, etc. Nafi' and Asim read a mountain with a kasra on the jim and ba' and a shaddah on the lam. Ibn Abi Ishaq, al-Zuhri, and Ibn Hurmuz read it with two dhammahs and a shaddah on the lam. This is also the reading of al-Hasan, 'Isa ibn 'Umar, and al-Nadr ibn Anas. Abu Yahya, Hammad ibn Salamah, and al-Ashhab al-'Uqaili read it with a kasra on the jim, a sukoon on the ba', and a softened lam. An-Nahhas said: The first reading is clearer. The evidence for this is that they all read and the first mountain with a kasra on the jim and ba' and a shaddah on the lam. So, mount is the plural of jabalah, and the derivation of all of them is from Jabal God al-Khalq, meaning He created them. The meaning of the verse is that Satan has led astray many people, as Mujahid said. Qatada said: Many crowds. Al-Kalbi said: Many nations. Al-Tha’labi said: All readings have the meaning of creation. It was read as generation with a jeem and a yaa below it. Ad-Dahhak said: One generation is ten thousand, and a large number is that which only God the Almighty can count. This reading was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib. The hamza in the verse, Did you not understand? is for rebuke and rebuke, and the fa is for conjunction with an understood word required by the situation as mentioned previously in similar verses: Do you see the effects of the punishments? Did you not understand? or Did you not understand the enmity of Satan towards you? or Did you not understand anything at all? The majority read Did you not understand? as a direct address. Talhah and Isa read it in the absence.
36:63: 63- This is the Hell which you were promised. That is, when they come close to the Fire, it will be said to them: This is the Hell which you were promised in this world, on the tongues of the Messengers, and the one who says this to them is the angels.
36:64: Then they will say to them: 64- Enter it today for what you used to disbelieve. That is, endure its heat today and enter it and taste the various types of torment in it for what you used to disbelieve: that is, because of your disbelief in God in this world and your obedience to Satan and your worship of idols. This matter is a matter of punishment and humiliation, like His saying: Taste, for you are the honored, the noble.
36:65: 65- Today We will seal up their mouths. Today is an adverbial phrase for what follows it. It was also read yakhatam in the passive voice, and the noun and preposition after it. The commentators said: They deny polytheism and believism of the messengers, as in their statement: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists. So God will seal their mouths with a seal that prevents them from speaking. This is a shift from being directly addressed to being absent, to indicate that their ugly deeds warrant us ignoring them. Then He said: And their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn. That is, their hands will speak about what they used to do, and their feet will testify against them about what they used to do. The majority of scholars read kallamna and tashahud. Talhah ibn Musarraf read wal taklamna and waltashahud with the lam of kay. It was said that the reason for sealing their mouths was so that the people standing at the gathering would recognize them. It was also said that their mouths were sealed so that the confession would come from their limbs, because the testimony of a non-speaking person is more eloquent in proof than the testimony of a speaking person, since it is a miraculous occurrence. It was also said that it was so that they would know that their limbs, which were their helpers in committing the sins of God, became witnesses against them. And what the hands utter was made speech and confession because they were directly involved in most of the sins. And the speech of the feet was made testimony because they are present at every event, and the speech of the doer is a confession, and the speech of the one present is testimony. This is a consideration of the majority, otherwise the feet may be directly involved in the sin just as the hands are directly involved in it.
36:66: 66- And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes meaning, We could have taken away their eyes and made them so that no slit or eyelid could be seen in them. Al-Kisa'i said: tamās, yatmūs, and tamīs, according to the linguists, is the one who has no slit in his eyes, as in the statement: And if God had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. The object of the will is omitted: meaning, if We willed to obliterate their eyes, We would have obliterated them. Al-Suddi and Al-Hasan said: The meaning is, We would have left them blind, wandering about, not seeing the path of guidance. Ibn Jarir preferred this view. So race to the path is in apposition to We obliterated meaning, they hastened to the path to cross it and continue on it. The path is in the accusative case with the removal of the preposition: meaning, they raced to it. Ata', Muqatil, and Qatadah said: The meaning is, if We willed, We could have gouged out their eyes and blinded them from their error. And We turned their sight from error to guidance, so they saw their right path, were guided, and hastened to the path of the Hereafter. The meaning of how can they see is how can they see the path and follow it well when they have no sight? Isa ibn Umar recited Fastabiqu in the imperative form, meaning it will be said to them, Race ahead. This is a threat to them.
36:67: Then He repeated the threat to them, saying: 67- And if We willed, We could have transformed them in their places. Transformation is changing the creation to stone or other inanimate objects or animals, and place is place: that is, if We willed, We could have changed their creation to the place they are in. It was said that place is more specific than place, like residence and standing. Al-Hasan said: that is, We would have made them sit down. So they could neither proceed nor return. That is, they could neither go nor come. Al-Hasan said: They could neither proceed in front of them nor return behind them, and likewise inanimate objects cannot advance nor fall behind. It was also said that the meaning is: If We willed, We could have destroyed them in their dwellings. It was also said that We would have transformed them in the place where they committed the sin. Yahya ibn Salam said: All of this will be on the Day of Resurrection. The majority of scholars read in their places in the singular. Al-Hasan, Al-Sulami, Zur ibn Hubaish, and Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim read their places in the plural. The majority of scholars read it with a damma on the meem, while Abu Haywah read it with a fatha. It was narrated from him that he read it with a kasra, and this reading was narrated from Al-Kisa’i. It was said that the meaning is: and they are not able to return, so the verb was placed in the position of the infinitive to maintain the separation. It is said that he went on the earth and returned, he returns, he returns from where he came.
36:68: 68- And whomsoever We prolong his life, We reverse him in creation. The majority of scholars read nankasahu with a fatha on the first noon, a sukoon on the second, and a damma on the kaf with a shaddah. Asim and Hamzah read it with a damma on the first noon, a fatha on the second, and a kasra on the kaf with a shaddah. The meaning is: Whoever We prolong his life, We change his creation, and make him the opposite of how he was at first in terms of strength and freshness. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: Whoever We prolong his life, We reverse his creation, so strength becomes weakness, and youth becomes old age. Similar to this verse are the words of God, the Most High: And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age so that he does not know a thing, after having known anything. And His statement: Then We return him to the lowest of the low. The meaning of Do you not then reason? is: Do you not know with your minds that He who is able to do that is able to resurrect and be raised? The majority of scholars read ya'qaloon with a ta' marbutah. Nafi' and Ibn Dhakwan read it with a ta' marbutah, indicating address.
36:69: And when the infidels of Mecca said: The Qur’an is poetry, and Muhammad is a poet, God responded to them by saying: 69- And We did not teach him poetry. The meaning is: He denied that the Qur’an is poetry, then He denied that the Prophet was a poet, so He said: And it is not befitting for him, meaning that poetry is not right for him, nor is it possible for him, nor is it easy for him if he sought it and wanted to say it. Rather, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to recite a verse that a poet had said, reciting it, he would break its meter. So when he recited the famous verse of Tarafa bin al-Abd, which is his saying: Days will show you what you were ignorant of, and report will come to you from someone you did not know. He said: And someone comes to you whom you did not provide with report. And he recited again the words of Al-Abbas bin Mirdas Al-Salami: Do you make my loot and the loot of the slaves between Uyaynah and Al-Aqra’? He said: Between Al-Aqra’ and Uyaynah, and he also recited: Islam and gray hair are enough to deter a person Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, the poet said: Gray hair and Islam are enough to prevent a person He said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. God the Almighty says: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for it. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) did much of this. Al-Khalil said: Poetry was more beloved to the Messenger of God than much speech, but it was not possible for him to master it. The reason for not teaching him poetry and not being able to do it is to complete the argument and refute the doubt, just as God made him illiterate, unable to read or write. As for what was narrated from him (peace and blessings be upon him) in his saying: Are you nothing but a bloody finger, and in the way of God I have not found And he said: I am the prophet, no lie, I am the son of Abdul Muttalib And so on, from the unintended coincidence that comes, as it comes in some verses of the Qur’an, and it is not poetry nor is it intended to be poetry, but it happened by coincidence as occurs in much of people’s speech, for they may speak in a way that if someone considered it would be in the meter of poetry and they do not consider it poetry, and that is like the saying of the Most High: You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love and His saying: And basins like jugs and pots firmly planted although Al-Akhfash said that his saying: I am the prophet, no lie It is not poetry. Al-Khalil said in Kitab Al-Ayn: What came from the rhyme in two parts is not poetry. Ibn Al-Arabi said: What is most apparent from his situation is that he said no lie with the raising of the ba from lie, and with the lowering of it from Abdul Muttalib. Al-Nahhas said, some of them said: The narration is by the syntax, and if it is by syntax it is not poetry, because if the ba of the first is opened or both of them are closed or its nun is opened and the ba of the second is broken, it is out of the meter of poetry. It was said that the pronoun in lahu refers back to the Qur’an, meaning the Qur’an should not be poetry. It is only a reminder meaning the Qur’an is only a reminder from the remembrances and an exhortation from the exhortations and a clear Qur’an meaning a book from the heavenly books of God that includes the legal rulings.
36:70: 70- To warn whoever is alive meaning that the Qur'an may warn whoever is alive: meaning that his heart is sound, accepting the truth and rejecting falsehood, or that the Messenger may warn whoever is alive. The majority of scholars read it with the sub-ya', while Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with the sub-ya'. According to the first reading, what is meant is the Qur'an, and according to the second reading, what is meant is the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. And the word will come into effect upon the disbelievers meaning that the word of punishment will be inflicted upon those who persist in disbelief and refuse to believe in God and His Messengers. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through various chains of narration, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, in their busy pursuits, that he said: in deflowering virgins. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding the verse, that he said: their preoccupation was the deflowering of virgins. Abd ibn Humayd narrated a similar narration on the authority of Ikrimah and Qatadah. Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he said: whenever a believer desires a wife, he finds her a virgin. A similar narration has been narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id, with a chain of narration traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, by Al-Tabarani in Al-Saghir and Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah. A similar narration has also been narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of narration traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, by Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi in Sifat Al-Jannah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, in their busy pursuits, that he said: playing the strings. Abu Hatim said: This is perhaps a mistake by the listener, and it refers to the deflowering of virgins. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: Feasting means rejoicing. Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in Sifat Al-Jannah, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Ajurri in Al-Ru’yah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “While the people of Paradise are enjoying their pleasures, a light will shine for them. They will raise their heads and behold, the Lord has looked down upon them from above and said: ‘Peace be upon you, O people of Paradise.’ This is the word of God: ‘Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord.’ He said: ‘So He will look at them and they will look at Him, and they will not turn back to any of the pleasures as long as they are looking at Him until He is veiled from them and His light and blessings remain upon them in their homes.’” Ibn Kathir said: In its chain of transmission on their authority. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: Indeed, God is the One who greets them. Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in al-Tawbah repentance, and the wording is his, and Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat the names of the people narrated on the authority of Anas regarding his statement, This Day We shall seal their mouths, that he said: “We were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he laughed until his molars were visible. He said, ‘Do you know why you laughed?’ We said, ‘No, O Messenger of God.’ He said, ‘It is from the servant addressing his Lord, saying, ‘O Lord, did you not save me from injustice?’ He says, ‘Yes.’ He says, ‘I will not accept against me anyone except a witness from me.’ He says, ‘Your own self is sufficient as a witness against you this Day, and the noble scribes are witnesses.’ So his mouth is sealed. His limbs are told, ‘Speak,’ and they speak of his deeds. Then he is left alone to speak, and he says, ‘Away with you and ruin! It was for you that I struggled.’” Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id and Abu Hurayrah that they said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “A servant will meet his Lord, and God will say: ‘Say, “Did I not honor you, make you a leader, give you a wife, and subject the horses and camels to you, and let you rule and graze your flocks?” He will say: Yes, O Lord. God will say: Did you think that you would meet Me? He will say: No. God will say: I will forget you as you forgot Me. Then he will meet a second person and say the same. Then he will meet a third person and say the same. He will say: I have believed in You, Your Book, and Your Messenger, and I have prayed, fasted, and given charity, and I have praised You as much as I can. God will say: Shall We not send our witness against you? He will think within himself about who will testify against me, and his mouth will be sealed, and his thigh will be told: Speak, and his thigh, mouth, and bones will speak of his deeds. This is so that he may excuse himself. This is the hypocrite, and this is the one with whom God is angry.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from the hadith of Abu Musa. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “And if We willed, We could have blinded them and led them astray from guidance. “Then how can they see?” He said: How can they be guided? Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, regarding his statement: And if We willed, We could have transformed them. He said: We could have destroyed them. In their places He said: In their dwellings. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was reported to me that it was said to Aisha: Was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Do you recite some poetry? She said: “It was the most hated speech to him, except that he would recite the verse of the brother of Banu Qais, making its beginning and end: ‘And there comes to you one whom you have not provided with report.’ Abu Bakr said: ‘It is not like this.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘By God, I am not a poet, and it is not appropriate for me to do so.’” This refutes what we previously reported from Al-Khalil, that poetry was more beloved to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than much speech. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ahmad narrated from her that she said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to hear a story, he would recite the verse of Tarafa: And he brings you report from someone you did not provide. Al-Bayhaqi included in his Sunan on the authority of Aisha, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never collected a verse of poetry except one verse: Be optimistic about what you desire, for it is rare for something to be said to have happened but it has come true. Aisha said: He did not say it in verification lest he should parse it and it would become poetry. Its chain of transmission is as follows: He said: Abu Ubaidullah al-Hafiz informed us - meaning al-Hakim - Abu Hafs ibn Ahmad ibn Na’im informed us - Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Hilal al-Nahwi al-Dharee’ informed us - Ali ibn Amr al-Ansari informed us - Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us - on the authority of al-Zuhri - on the authority of Urwah - on the authority of Aisha - and he mentioned it. Al-Mizzi was asked about this hadith and he said: It is rejected and neither al-Hakim’s sheikh nor al-Dharee’ were known.
36:71: Then He, the Most High, mentioned His great power, His blessings upon His servants, and the ingratitude of the disbelievers for His blessings, saying: 71- Have they not seen that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, livestock? The hamza is for denial and amazement at their condition, and the waw is for connecting to something understood, as in similar examples. And seeing is the heart’s: that is, or have they not known through contemplation and consideration, that We have created for them: that is, for their sake, from what Our hands have made: that is, from what We have created and made without an intermediary or partner. Attributing work to hands is an exaggeration of exclusivity and uniqueness in creation, as one of us says: I made it with my hands to indicate His uniqueness in His work. Ma means which, and the pronoun was omitted due to the length of the connection. It is permissible for it to be a source, and livestock is the plural of na’am, which are cows, sheep, and camels, and we have already discussed it in detail. Then the Almighty mentioned the benefits resulting from the creation of livestock, saying: They are their owners, meaning they are controlling and dominating them, disposing of them as they wish. If We had created them wild, they would have been repelled by them and they would not have been able to control them. It is possible that what is meant is that they became part of their possessions and are counted among their wealth, which is attributed to them by virtue of ownership.
36:72: 72- And We have subjected it to them meaning, We have made it subservient to them, not refusing to do whatever they want with it of benefits, even slaughter. The boy leads it and it obeys him, and he urges it on and it refrains. The fa in His statement, and from it is their riding is to rebuke the rulings of taming it: meaning, from it is their mount that they ride, as it is said, a milking camel, meaning milked. The majority read rakubhum with a fat-ha on the ra. Al-A'mash, Al-Hasan and Ibn Al-Samee' with a damma on the ra as a verbal noun. Abu and Aisha read rakubhum, and rakub and rakubah are the same, like al-haluub and al-halubah, and al-hamul and al-hamulah. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-rakubah can be for one person or a group, while rakub can only be for a group. Abu Hatim claimed that it is not permissible, famhum with a damma on the ra because it is a verbal noun, and rakub is that which is ridden. Al-Farra' permitted this, as it is said: famhum akalhum and famhum dharbihum, and the meaning of and from it they eat is what they eat of its meat, and min is for partialization.
36:73: 73- And they have benefits from them meaning they have benefits from livestock other than riding them and eating from them, which is what they benefit from of their wool, fur, and hair, and what they make of fat from their fat, as well as carrying loads and ploughing with them. And drinks meaning they have drinks from what is obtained from their milk. So will they not then be grateful to God for these blessings and unify Him and single Him out for worship.
36:74: Then the Almighty mentioned their ignorance, their deception, and their placing ingratitude for blessings in place of gratitude for them, saying: 74- And they have taken besides God gods of idols and the like, which they worship, but which have no power over anything, and from which they have gained no benefit, nor has any benefit been gained from their worship, so that they may be aided meaning in the hope that they may be aided by them if a punishment befalls them or something befalls them.
36:75: And the sentence 75- They cannot help them is a new sentence to clarify the invalidity of what they hoped for and desired from it in terms of benefit. The plural of them with the waw and the nun is the plural of rational beings based on the polytheists' claim that they can benefit, harm, and reason. And they are an army prepared for them. That is, the disbelievers are an army prepared for the idols: that is, they attend them in this world. Al-Hasan said: They prevent them and defend them. Qatadah said: That is, they become angry on their behalf in this world. Al-Zajjaj said: They take revenge on the idols, although they are unable to help them. It was also said that the meaning is: They worship the gods and stand up for them, so they are like an army to them. These sayings are based on making the pronoun they refer to the polytheists, and the pronoun them refers to the gods. It was also said that they means the gods are for them: that is, the polytheists are an army prepared with them in the fire, so they cannot defend one another. It was also said that its meaning is: And these idols are for these disbelievers, God's army against them in hell, because they curse them and disown them. It was said that the meaning is: The infidels believe that the idols are their soldiers who will be present on the Day of Resurrection to help them.
36:76: Then the Almighty consoled His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) by saying: 76- So let not their statement grieve you. This statement is what is indicated by His statement: And they have taken other gods besides God. For they would inevitably say, These are our gods, and that they are partners with God in worship, and the like. This is a prohibition against the one being addressed from being present with Him. It is not a prohibition against seeing Him. This is far-fetched, but the former is more appropriate, and the statement is for the sake of consolation, as we have mentioned. It is possible that what is meant by the statement mentioned is their saying that he is a magician, a poet, and a madman. The phrase Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare is to explain the previous prohibition. His knowledge of what they reveal and conceal necessitates that He reward them for it. And everything they do is not hidden from Him, whether it is hidden or apparent, secret or public, apparent or implied. The secret is mentioned before the public to emphasize the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all information.
36:77: And the sentence 77- Does not man see that We created him from a sperm-drop? is a new sentence introduced to demonstrate the proof against those who deny the resurrection and to express astonishment at their ignorance, for witnessing their creation in themselves in this manner from beginning to end necessitates acknowledging the ability of the All-Powerful, All-Wise to do what is less than that of resurrecting bodies and returning them to the state they were. The human being mentioned in the verse refers to the human race as in His statement: Does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing? There is no justification for specifying it as a specific human being, as it was said that it was Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and that it was said to him because he denied the resurrection. Al-Hasan said: It is Umayyah ibn Khalaf. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: It is Al-As ibn Wa'il Al-Sahmi. Qatada and Mujahid said: He is Abi bin Khalaf Al-Jumahi. Even though one of these was a cause for revelation, the meaning of the verse is addressing the human being as such, not a specific human being. Whoever was a cause for revelation is included under the human race primarily. The sperm is a small amount of water, and we have already explained its meaning. Then behold, he is a clear adversary. This sentence is connected to the negative sentence before it, entering with it into the realm of denial understood from the question. Then behold is suddenness: Didn’t man see that We created him from the weakest of things, so Our adversary suddenly came to him in a matter in which God’s proofs and evidence had been established against him? The adversary is one who is very argumentative and debates a lot. The meaning of the clear is the one who makes clear what the one explaining to him says with the strength of his argument and fluency of his tongue.
36:78: And thus, sentence 78 - And he presented to us an example and forgot his creation is connected to the negative sentence and falls within the scope of denial understood from the question. It is a completion of the astonishment at the state of man and a demonstration of his ignorance of the truths and his neglect of thinking about himself, let alone thinking about all of God's creations. It is possible that the sentence Then he is an opponent is connected to Our creation, and this is connected to it: that is, he mentioned a strange story about us like an example: which is his denial sometimes of the bones, and he forgot his creation: that is, We created him. This sentence is connected to strike, or in the accusative case as a state with the estimation of may, and the sentence He said, 'Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?' is a resumption of the answer to an assumed question, as if it were said, What is this example that he presented? It was said that he said: Who gives life to the bones when they have decayed? This question is for denial because he equated the power of God to the power of the servant, so he denied that God gives life to decayed bones since that was not within the power of humans. It is said that the bone has decayed, if it has rotted, then it is decayed and ashes. He only said decayed and not rotten, even though it is the predicate of the feminine because it is a noun for the decayed bones, not an adjective like decay and ashes. It was also said that it is because it was modified from its agent, and everything that is modified from its face is diverted from its syntax, as in His statement: {And your mother was not a harlot} because it is diverted from harlot, this is what Al-Baghawi and Al-Qurtubi said, and the author of Al-Kashshaf said the former. It is better to say that it is fa’il with the meaning of fa’il or maf’ul, and it applies to both masculine and feminine, as was said in Jareeh and Saboor.
36:79: Then the Almighty answered the one who made this example, saying: 79- Say, ‘He will give life to it who produced it the first time.’ That is, He began it and created it the first time from nothing. He who was able to create the first creation was also able to create the second. And He is Knowing of all things. Nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing escapes His knowledge, whatever it may be. Abu Hanifa and some of the followers of al-Shafi’i used this verse as evidence that bones are among those that are permeated by life. Al-Shafi’i said: Life does not permeate them, and what is meant by His statement, Who will give life to the bones? is Who will give life to the owners of the bones? based on the assumption of an omitted complement. It was responded that this assumption is contrary to the apparent meaning.
36:80: 80- Who made for you fire from the green tree. This is a return from Him, glory be to Him, to the confirmation of what preceded from repelling their exclusion. So He, glory be to Him, drew attention to His Oneness and indicated His ability to revive the dead by what they witness of the burning fire coming out of the moist, moist wood. This is because the tree known as Marakh and the tree known as Afar, if two branches are cut from them and one of them is struck against the other, fire will ignite from them while they are both green. It was said that Marakh is the male and the Aqar is the female, and the first is called the Zand and the second the Zandah. He said Al-Akhdar and did not say Al-Khadhra in consideration of the wording. Al-Khidr was read in consideration of the meaning. It has been established that the generic noun may be masculine or feminine as in His statement: palm trees hollowed out and His statement: palm trees empty. So Banu Tamim and Najd mention it in the masculine form, while the people of Al-Hijaz feminize it except rarely. The relative pronoun is a substitute for the first relative pronoun. Then you kindle from it means you kindle from it a fire and light it from that green tree.
36:81: Then the Almighty mentioned what is greater in creation than man, saying: 81- Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? The hamza is for denial, and the waw is for linking something understood like its counterparts. The meaning of the verse is that He who was able to create the heavens and the earth, which are extremely great and large in parts, is able to recreate human beings, who are small in gratitude and weak in strength. The Almighty did not say: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. The majority of scholars read Qadir in the active participle form. Al-Jahdary, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Al-A’raj, Salam ibn Al-Mundhir, and Abu Ya’qub Al-Hadhmari read Yaqdir in the present tense. Then the Almighty answered what the question indicated of denial and confirmation by saying: Yes, and He is the Creator, the All-Knowing. That is, yes, He is able to do that, and He is the most perfect and complete in creation and knowledge. Al-Hasan, Al-Jahdary, and Malik ibn Dinar read He is the Creator.
36:82: Then the Almighty mentioned what indicates the perfection of His power and the ease with which He can begin and repeat. He said: 82- His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. That is, when His will is connected to something, the Almighty’s affair is only that He says to it, ‘Bring it about,’ and it comes about, without depending on anything else at all. The explanation of this has been presented previously in Surat An-Nahl and in Surat Al-Baqarah. The majority of scholars read be in the nominative case as a new sentence. Al-Kisa’i read it in the accusative case as an apposition to says.
36:83: 83- So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things. In Arabic, malakut is an expression used to exaggerate dominion, like jabrūt and rahmūt. It is as if He said, So glory be to Him in whose hand is the ownership of all things. Qatadah said, The dominion of all things means the keys to everything. The majority of scholars read it as malakut, while Al-A'mash, Talhah ibn Musarraf, and Ibrahim Al-Taymi read it as malakah with the same weight as shajarah. It was also read as malakah with the same weight as maf'ala. It was also read as malak, and malak is more expressive than all of them. The majority of scholars read and to Him you will return with the superior vowel as direct address, in the passive voice. As-Sulami, Zur ibn Jahsh, and the companions of Ibn Mas'ud read it with the superior vowel as absent, also in the passive voice. Zayd ibn Ali read it with the active voice: meaning you will return to Him, not to anyone else, and that will be in the Hereafter after the resurrection. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim in his Mu'jam, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: "Al-'As ibn Wa'il came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with a decayed bone. He crumbled it in his hand and said: 'O Muhammad, will God bring this back to life after what I see?' He said: 'Yes, God will resurrect this, then cause you to die, then bring you back to life, then cause you to enter the fire of Hell.' Then the verses were revealed from the end of Ya Sin: 'Does man not see that We created him from a sperm-drop?' until the end of the Surah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that Abdullah ibn Ubayy came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with a decayed bone in his hand and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Ibn Kathir said: This is strange because the Surah was revealed in Mecca and Abdullah ibn Ubayy was only in Medina. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi came and mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above.
37:1: It is one hundred and eighty-two verses It is a Meccan surah. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion. Ibn al-Durais, Ibn al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was revealed in Mecca. An-Nasa’i and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to command us to make it brief and he would say Alamin as-Saffat. Ibn Kathir said: It was narrated only by al-Nasa’i. Ibn Abi Dawud narrated in Fada’il al-Qur’an and Ibn al-Najjar in his Tarikh, on the authority of Nahshal ibn Sa’d al-Wardani, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever recites Ya-Seen and as-Saffat on Friday and then asks God, He will grant him what he asks for. Abu Nu’aym narrated in al-Dala’il and al-Salfi in al-Tayouriyat, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “When the kings of Hadhramaut asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) upon their arrival to recite to them something of what God revealed, he recited ‘As-Saffat in rows’ until he reached ‘Lord of the Easts and the Wests’” the hadith. His saying: 1- And those who rank up in ranks Abu Amr and Hamzah, and it was said Hamzah only, read it by assimilating the taa of as-saffat into the sad of saffan, and assimilating the taa of as-zajirat into the zay of zajran, and assimilating the taa of as-taliyyat into the dhal of dhikran. This reading was rejected by Ahmad ibn Hanbal when he heard it. An-Nahhas said: It is far-fetched in Arabic for three reasons: The first is that the taa is not from the point of articulation of the letter sad, nor from the point of articulation of the letter zay, nor from the point of articulation of the letter dal, nor from their sisters. The second reason is that the taa in one word and what follows it is in another word. The third is that when you assimilate, you combine two quiescent letters from two words. It is only permissible to combine two quiescent letters in such a case if they are in one word. Al-Wahidi said: Assimilation of the taa into the sad is good because of the similarity of the two letters. Don't you see that they are from the tip of the tongue? The rest read it with all of that made clear, and the waw is for the oath, and what is sworn by are the angels: those who line up, those who repel, and those who follow. What is meant by those who line up are those angels who line up in the sky like the rows of creation in this world, as stated by Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah. It was also said that they line up their wings in the air, standing in it until God commands them as He wills. Al-Hasan said: Line up like their rows before their Lord in their prayer. It was also said that what is meant by those who line up here are the birds, as in His statement: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading out? The first is more correct, and a line is the arrangement of the group on a line like the row in prayer. The first is more correct, and a line is the arrangement of the group on a line like the row in prayer. It was said that those who line up are the group of believers when they stand in a line in prayer or in jihad, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri.
37:2: 2- The ones who forbid are the angels who do the forbidding, either because they forbid the clouds as al-Suddi said, or because they forbid sins with sermons and advice. Qatada said: What is meant by the ones who forbid are the deterrents from the Qur'an, which are everything that forbids and forbids from evil. The first is more appropriate. The accusative of Safa and zajran is as a source to emphasize what precedes them. It was said that what is meant by the ones who forbid are the scholars, because they are the ones who forbid the people of sins. And forbidding in origin means pushing with force, and here it is the force of the voice, and from it the saying of the poet: Abu Urwa's reprimand of wild animals if he feared they would mix with the sheep From this, you say: you frighten camels and sheep with your voice.
37:3: 3- those who recite the remembrance refers to the angels who recite the Quran, as stated by Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, and Al-Suddi. It is also said that it refers to Gabriel alone, so it was mentioned in the plural form to glorify him, although he is not devoid of followers from the angels. Qatada said: It refers to everyone who recites the remembrance of God and His books. It is also said that it refers to the verses of the Quran, and He described them as being recited, even though they are recited, as in His statement: Indeed, this Quran relates to the Children of Israel. It is also said that it is because some of them recite to others and are followed by them. Al-Mawardi mentioned that the ones who recite are the prophets who recite the remembrance to their nations. The accusative of remembrance is as a direct object, and it is permissible for it to be a verbal noun, as before it in His statement describing and reprimanding. It is said that this fa in His statement those who reprimand, so the ones who recite are either to arrange the attributes themselves in ecstasy or to arrange their descriptions in virtue, and each is subject to consideration.
37:4: And His statement: 4- Indeed, your God is One is the answer to the oath: meaning that God swore by these oaths that He is One and has no partner. Al-Kisa'i permitted opening the in that occurs in the answer to the oath.
37:5: 5- Lord of the heavens and the earth may be a second predicate, a substitute for one, or a predicate of a deleted subject. Ibn al-Anbari said: Stopping at one is a good stop, then starting with Lord of the heavens and the earth with the meaning He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. An-Nahhas said: It may also be a substitute for one. The meaning of the verse is that the existence of these creatures in this wonderful form is one of the clearest proofs of the existence of the Creator and His power, and that He is the Lord of all of it: that is, its Creator and Owner. What is meant by between is what is between the heavens and the earth of creatures. What is meant by the risings is the risings of the sun. It was said that God, the Exalted, created for the sun a rising and a setting place every day, corresponding to the number of days in the year. Every day it rises from one of them and sets from one of them. This is what Ibn al-Anbari and Ibn Abd al-Barr said. As for His statement in Surah Ar-Rahman, Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests, what is meant by the two Easts is the furthest point from which the sun rises during long days and the shortest point during short days, and likewise for the two Wests. As for mentioning the East and the West in the singular, what is meant by them is the direction from which the sun rises and the direction from which it sets. Perhaps we have previously discussed this in more detail.
37:6: 6- Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with an adornment of the stars. The intended meaning of the lowest heaven is the one closest to the earth, from ad-danu which means near, so it is the closest of the heavens to the earth. The majority of scholars read with the adornment of the stars by adding adornment to the stars. The meaning is: We adorned it with the adornment of the stars: that is, with their beauty. Masruq, Al-A'mash, Al-Nakha'i, and Hamzah read it with the tanween of adornment and the kawkab in the genitive case as a substitute for adornment, and the intended meaning of adornment is the noun and not the verbal noun. The interpretation after subtracting the substituted one is: Indeed, We adorned the heaven with the stars, for the stars in themselves are a great adornment, for in the eyes of those who look at them they are like glittering jewels. Asim read in the narration of Abu Bakr from him with the tanween of adornment and the accusative of the planets, on the basis that adornment is a source and its agent is deleted, and the meaning is: that God adorned the planets by them being bright and beautiful in themselves, or the planets are accusative by the implication of I mean, or as a substitute for the sky as a substitute for inclusion, and the accusative of preservation as a source by the implication of a verb: that is, we preserved it preservation, or as an object for the sake of it: that is, we adorned it with the planets for preservation, or by devoting it to the place of adornment as if he said: Indeed, we created the planets as an adornment for the sky.
37:7: 7- To protect from every rebellious devil meaning a rebellious one who disobeys and throws stars, as in His saying: And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them missiles to drive away the devils.
37:8: 8- The phrase they do not hear the highest assembly is a new sentence to explain their condition after the heaven was protected from them. Abu Hatim said: That is, so that they do not hear. Then he deleted in and raised the verb. Al-Kalbi said the same. The highest assembly: the people of the lowest heaven and what is above it. Each of them was called the highest by adding it to the assembly of the earth. The pronoun in they hear refers to the devils. It was said that the phrase they do not hear is an attribute of every devil. It was also said that it is an answer to an implied question, as if it was said: What was their condition after the heaven was protected from them? He said: they do not hear the highest assembly. The majority read they hear with a silent seen and a light mim. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and Asim, in the narration of Hafs from him, read it with a shaddah on the meem and the seen. The original is yastasma’u they listen, but the ta’ was assimilated into the seen. The first reading indicates the negation of their hearing but not their listening, and the second reading indicates the negation of both. Consisting of the meaning of the first reading is the statement of God Almighty: {Indeed, from hearing they are removed.} Mujahid said: They used to listen but did not hear. Abu Ubaidah preferred the second reading. He said: Because the Arabs hardly ever say: I listened to him, but they say: I listened to him.
37:9: 9- And they throw from every side * Dahwran meaning they throw meteors from every side of the sky if they want to ascend to eavesdrop. The accusative of Dahwran is as an object for which purpose and Dahwran is expulsion. You say dahratuhu dahwran and Dahwran: I expelled him. The majority read Dahwran with a damma on the dal, while Ali, As-Salami, Ya'qub Al-Hadrami and Ibn Abi Ubla read it with a fatha. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr that he read yadhqithuna as an active participle, which is a reading that does not conform to what is intended by the Qur'anic structure. It was said that the accusative of Dahwran is in the state of: meaning expelled. It was also said that it is the plural of Dahir like qa'id and qa'ud, so it is also a state of. It was said that it is a verbal noun for an implied verb: meaning they throw Dahwran. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is that they throw with that which drives them away: meaning with a defeat, then the ba' was deleted and it was accusative by removing the preposition. There is a difference of opinion as to whether this shooting of meteors was before or after the mission. Some held the former, others the latter. A group combined the two opinions, saying that the devils were not shot before the mission in a way that would cut them off from hearing, but they were shot at one time and not at another, and they were shot from one side and not from another. Then after the mission they were shot at all times and from every side until they were unable to eavesdrop except for someone who snatched a snatch, and a piercing meteor followed him. The meaning of and for them is a lasting torment is that they will have a permanent torment that will not cease. What is meant by it is the torment in the Hereafter, other than the torment they will have in this world from being shot with meteors. Muqatil said: It means always until the first blast, but the former is more appropriate. The majority of commentators have said that the lasting wasab is permanent. Al-Suddi, Abu Salih and Al-Kalbi said: It is the painful one whose pain reaches the heart. It is taken from wasab, which means illness, and it was said that it means severe.
37:10: The exception in His statement: 10- Except for he who snatches a snatch is from His statement they do not hear or from His statement and they throw. It was said that the exception refers to other than revelation, as He said: Indeed, they are removed from hearing, but rather one of them snatches a snatch of what the angels negotiate about and what goes on among them of what will happen in the world before the people of the earth know about it. And snatching is theft and taking something quickly. The majority read khalaf with a fatha on the kha and a kasra on the ta, with a light sukoon. Qatadah and Al-Hasan read it with a kasra on both of them and a shaddah on the ta, and it is the language of Tamim bin Murr and Bakr bin Wa'il. Isa bin Omar read it with a fatha on the kha and a kasra on the ta, with a shaddah. Ibn Abbas read it with a kasra on both of them and a soft taa. It was said that the exception is disjunctive. Fata’ahu Shihab Thaqib means that a piercing meteor followed him, meaning a piercing meteor caught up with him: a bright star that burns him, and sometimes it does not burn him, so it throws to its brothers what it snatched. The meteors that are thrown are not from the reward planets, but rather from the non-fixed ones. The origin of holes is illumination. Al-Kisa’i said: The fire pierced, pierced, and ignited: if it ignited. This verse is like His saying: Except for he who steals a hearing, then a clear flaming fire pursues him.
37:11: 11- So ask them, are they stronger in creation, or those We created? That is, ask the unbelievers who deny the resurrection, are they stronger in creation, have stronger bodies, and have larger limbs, or those We created from the heavens, the earth, and the angels? Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, then ask them a question of confirmation, are they stronger in creation: that is, whose creation is more perfect, or those of the previous nations We created before them? He means that they are not more perfect in creation than other nations, and We destroyed them for their denial, so what will protect them from the punishment? Then He mentioned the creation of man, saying: Indeed, We created them from sticky clay. That is, We created them within the creation of their father Adam from sticky clay, meaning that it adheres. It is said that lazb literally, sticks means that it sticks. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: lazb means sticky. "Ikrimah said: "lazb" means sticky. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "lazb" is good that sticks to the hand. Mujahid said: It is the intransitive, and the Arabs say: sticky clay, and it is necessary to replace the b with the m, and the intransitive is the fixed, as it is said: the thing became a sticky blow, and from it is the saying of Al-Nabigha: Do not think that good will bring about evil, and do not think that evil will bring about a lasting blow. Al-Farra' narrated on the authority of the Arabs: "Latib clay means inseparable, and latib" is constant. Al-Asma'i said: "Latib is sticky like lazib. The meaning of the verse is: How can these people enslave the afterlife while they were created from this weak creation, and no one who was created stronger, greater, more perfect and complete than them denied it. It was said that lazib is the stinking one, as said by Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak. The majority read Am man khalaqna with a shaddah on the mim, which is the connected umm, and Al-A'mash read it without a shaddah, which is a second question according to his reading. It was said that lazim and la-atib were also read, but I do not know who read it that way.
37:12: Then the Almighty turned away from the previous statement and said: 12- Rather, I am amazed O Muhammad, at the power of God the Almighty, and they mock you because of your amazement, or they mock you for what you say about proving the resurrection. The majority of scholars read the word amazed with a fat-ha, addressing the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a damma, and this reading was reported from Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, and Ibn Abbas, and Abu Ubaid and Al-Farra' chose it. Al-Farra' said: People read it with the ta' in the accusative and nominative cases, but I prefer the nominative case because it was narrated from Ali, Abdullah, and Ibn Abbas. He said: What is amazed is that it is attributed to God, so its meaning from God is not like its meaning from the servants. Al-Harawi said: Some of the imams said: The meaning of his saying: Rather, I am amazed is Rather, I rewarded them for their amazement, because God has spoken about them in more than one place with amazement at creation, as He said: And they are amazed that a warner has come to them from among themselves. And they said: Indeed, this is a strange thing. “Is it a wonder to the people that We have revealed to a man from among themselves?” Ali bin Sulayman said: The meaning of the two readings is the same, and the interpretation is: Say, O Muhammad, rather I am amazed, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is being addressed by the Qur’an. An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement, and the omission of the statement is common. It was said that the meaning of God’s statement about Himself with amazement is that He has made apparent from His command and His wrath upon those who disbelieve in Him what takes the place of amazement at created beings. Al-Harawi said: It is said that the meaning of your Lord is amazed: Your Lord is pleased and rewarded, so He called it amazement, but it is not amazement in reality, so the meaning of amazement here is the greatness of their action in my opinion. Al-Naqqash related that the meaning of rather, I am amazed is Rather, I denied. Al-Hasan bin Al-Fadl said: Wonder at God is denying something and glorifying it, and it is the language of the Arabs. It was said that its meaning is: He reached the point in the perfection of His power and the multitude of His creations to the point where I was amazed by them, and these people, due to their ignorance, mock them. The waw in and they mock is for the state: that is, rather I was amazed and the state is that they mock. It is possible that it is for resumption.
37:13: 13- And when they are reminded, they do not remember. That is, when they are admonished with an admonition from God or His Messenger, they do not remember: that is, they do not learn from it nor benefit from what is in it. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: That is, when what happened to the disbelievers who came before them is mentioned to them, they turn away from it and do not reflect.
37:14: 14- And when they see a sign, meaning one of the miracles of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they mock, meaning they go to extremes in their mockery. Qatada said: They mock and say that it is mockery. It is said that sakhar and istakhar mean the same thing, like qarra and iqara, ajab and istajab. The first is more appropriate, because the additional structure indicates an additional meaning. It was said that the meaning of istakharoon is that they invoke mockery from others. Mujahid said: They mock.
37:15: 15- And they said, ‘This is nothing but obvious magic.’ That is, what you are bringing us is nothing but obvious, clear magic.
37:16: 16- When we die and become dust and bones The question is for denial: that is, will we be resurrected when we die? The factor in when is what is indicated by Will we indeed be resurrected which is will we be resurrected, not will we be resurrected because of something that prevents its action in it. This denial of resurrection on their part is the reason why they denied the messengers and what was revealed to them and mocked the miracles they brought. The interpretation of the meaning of this verse has been presented previously in other places.
37:17: 17- Or our forefathers is a subject and its predicate is omitted: that is, or our forefathers are resurrected. It was said that it is conjoined to the place of in and its noun, and it was said that it is conjoined to the pronoun in resurrected because of the separation between them and the hamza is for denial and is included in the conjunction, and for this reason the majority read it with the fatha on the waw, and Ibn Amir read it and said with its sukoon on the basis that or is the conjunction, and the hamza is not for interrogation.
37:18: Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to respond to them, as a rebuke to them, saying: 18- Say, ‘Yes, while you are humbled.’ That is, yes, you will be resurrected while you are humiliated and disgraced. Al-Wahidi said: Dakhur is the most severe form of humiliation, and the phrase while you are humbled is in the accusative case as a state.
37:19: Then the Almighty mentioned that their resurrection will take place with a single blast, saying: 19- It will be only a single blast. The pronoun refers to the story or the resurrection understood from what preceded it: meaning, the story of the resurrection or the resurrection will be a single blast: meaning, a single blast from Israfil when he blows the trumpet at the resurrection. Then they will look on, meaning they will see what punishment God will do to them. Al-Hasan said: It is the second blast, and the blast was called a blast because its intended purpose is a warning. It was also said that the meaning of they will look on is that they are waiting for what will be done to them, but the first is more appropriate. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim - who authenticated it - narrated from various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud: And those who rank up in ranks, he said: the angels. And those who drive away a driving away, he said: the angels. And those who recite the Reminder, he said: the angels. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Athmah narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he used to recite: They do not listen to the highest assembly, with a lightened vowel. He said: They used to listen but did not hear. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: A persistent torment, he said: Permanent. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Athmah also narrated on his authority: And a piercing flame pursued him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority: And a piercing flame pursued him, he said: they will not be killed by the flame, nor will they die. But it burns, disables, and wounds without killing. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement, from sticky clay, he said: stuck together. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him, from sticky clay, he said: good sticky. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, he said: sticky, mud, and clay are one and the same: it was first dust, then it became stinking mud, then it became sticky clay, and from it God created Adam. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Masoud, he said: sticky is that which sticks together. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it from Ibn Masoud that he used to recite, Rather, I am amazed and they mock, raising the ta’ from amazed.
37:20: His saying: 20- And they said, ‘Woe to us!’ That is, those resurrected ones said, when they witnessed the resurrection that they used to deny in this world, ‘Woe to us!’ They called for woe upon themselves. Al-Zajjaj said: Woe is a word that someone says at the time of destruction. Al-Farra’ said: Its origin is ‘Woe to us!’ and ‘Woe’ means sorrow, as if he said: ‘Oh sorrow to us!’ Al-Nahhas said: If it were as he said, it would have been separate. In the Qur’an, it is connected, and we do not know of anyone who writes it except connected. The phrase ‘This is the Day of Judgment’ is an explanation for their calling for woe upon themselves, and Judgment is the recompense, so it is as if they said, ‘This is the day on which we will be recompensed for our deeds of disbelief and denial of the messengers,’ so the angels responded to them with their words.
37:21: 21- This is the Day of Judgment which you used to deny. It is possible that this is what some of them said to each other, and the Judgment is the judgment and ruling because it is the Day of Judgment between the good and the bad.
37:22: And His statement: 22- Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses is a command from God the Almighty to the angels to gather together the polytheists and their spouses, who are similar to them in polytheism, who follow them in disbelief, and who support them in denying the messengers. This is what Qatada and Abu Al-Aaliyah said. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: What is meant by their spouses are their polytheist women who agree with them in disbelief and injustice. Ad-Dahhak said: Their spouses are their companions from the devils, and every disbeliever will be gathered together from his devil. This is what Muqatil said.
