Muqatil said: “So He made it springs and wells in the earth. ‘Then He brings forth thereby crops of varying colors.’” That is, by that water He brings forth from the earth crops of varying colors, such as yellow, green, white, and red, or wheat, barley, and others, if what is meant by colors is the variety. Then it dries up. It is said that the plant dries up completely. Al-Jawhari said: It is said that the plant dries up completely, and a turbulent land dries up with its greenery or turns yellow. The wind dries up the plants, meaning it dries them up. Al-Mubarrad said: Al-Asma’i said: It is said that the land dries up if its plants turn away and turn back. He said: Likewise, the vegetation trembles. And you see it yellow, meaning you see it after its greenness, freshness and beautiful lustre, yellow, its greenness and freshness gone. Then He makes it into debris, meaning crumbled and broken, from the shattering of a stick when it crumbles from dryness. Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding, meaning in what was mentioned above there is a reminder for the people of sound minds, for they are the ones who understand things according to their true nature, so they reflect, consider and know that the state of this worldly life is like the state of this plant in its swift passing, the nearness of its end, the loss of its joy and the disappearance of its lustre and freshness. So if reflection and consideration produce knowledge of that for them, they will not be deceived by it or inclined towards it and prefer it over the abode of eternal bliss, continuous life and pure pleasure, and they will not have any doubt that God is Able to resurrect and gather, because He who has power over this is able to do that. It was said that it is an example that God made for the Qur’an and for the hearts of those on earth. Meaning: He sent down a Qur'an from the sky and made it linger in the hearts of the believers, then He brought it forth as a religion, some of which is better than the other. As for the believer, his faith and certainty increase, while as for the one in whose heart is disease, he will be stirred up like the crops stir up. This is more like a change than an explanation. The majority read then He makes it in the nominative case in apposition to what preceded it. Abu Bishr read it in the accusative case, implying that, but there is no basis for that.
39:22: Then when He, the Almighty, mentioned that in that is a reminder for those of understanding, He mentioned expanding the heart to Islam, because complete benefit is not attained except through it, so He said: 22- Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam? That is, He has made it spacious to accept the truth and opened it to be guided to the path of goodness. Al-Suddi said: He has expanded his breast to Islam to rejoice in it and feel reassured by it. The discussion of the hamza and the fa' is as previously mentioned in Is he upon whom the word of punishment has come into effect? "Min" is the subject and its predicate is omitted, meaning how hardened his heart and wounded his breast. This omitted predicate is indicated by His statement: "So woe to those whose hearts are hardened." The meaning is: Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam, so his heart and he are guided by its guidance "so because of that expansion is upon a light from his Lord" that flows upon him like he whose heart has hardened due to his bad choices, so he finds himself in the darkness of misguidance and the calamities of ignorance. Qatada said: The light is the Book of God, by which one is led and to which one ends. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse is: Is he whose breast God has expanded like he whose heart has been sealed so he is not guided because of its hardness? So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj said: It means against the remembrance of God, just as you say you are full from the food you ate or from the food you ate. The meaning is that his heart has hardened and become cold towards accepting the remembrance of God. It is said that the heart is hardened if it is rigid, and a hard heart means rigid, not tender or soft. It was said that the meaning of whoever remembers God is for the sake of His remembrance, which is right for breasts to expand and hearts to find peace. The meaning is that when God is remembered, they feel disgusted. The first is more appropriate, and this is supported by the reading of those who read from the remembrance of God. The reference in His statement: those is to those whose hearts are hardened, and it is the subject and predicate, in manifest error, meaning apparent and clear.
39:23: Then the Almighty mentioned some descriptions of His Noble Book, saying: 23- God has sent down the best statement, meaning the Qur’an. He called it a statement because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to tell his people about it and inform them of what was revealed to him from it. This shows that the best statement mentioned previously is the Qur’an, and the accusative case of a book is in apposition to the best statement, and it is possible that it is a state of it. Mutashabih is an attribute of a book: meaning that some of it resembles others in beauty, perfection, soundness of meanings, and strength of construction. It was said that it resembles the books of God revealed to His prophets. Mathani is another attribute of a book: meaning that the stories are repeated in it and the sermons and rulings are repeated in it. It was said that it is recited in recitation so that its listener does not get bored nor its reader get tired. The majority read Mathani with a fat-ha on the ya', and Hisham read it on the authority of Ibn Amir and Bishr with a sukoon on it to make it easier and heavier to move it, or as the predicate of a deleted subject: i.e. it is mathani. Al-Razi said in Tabyeen Mathaniyyah that most of the things mentioned in the Quran are repeated in pairs, such as commands and prohibitions, the general and the specific, the general and the detailed, the conditions of the heavens and the earth, Paradise and Hell, light and darkness, the tablet and the pen, the angels and the devils, the throne and the chair, the promise and the threat, hope and fear. The purpose of this is to clarify that everything other than the truth is a pair, and that the unique, one and only truth is God. It is not hidden what is in his words of affectation and distance from the purpose of the revelation The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it This sentence may be an attribute of the book, or it may be a state of it, because even if it is indefinite it has been made specific by the attribute, or it may be renewed to clarify what happens when hearing it of the effect on its listeners, and shivering is contraction, it is said that his skin shivered: if it contracts and gathers from fear. Meaning: It makes them shiver. Al-Zajjaj said: When the verses of torment are mentioned, the skins of those who fear God shiver. Then their skins and their hearts soften when the verses of mercy are mentioned. Al-Wahidi said: This is the opinion of all the commentators, including the statement of Imru’ al-Qais: So I spent the whole night suffering, my heart trembling with fear. It was said that the meaning is: Since the Qur’an was at the peak of eloquence and rhetoric, when they saw their inability to oppose it, their skins would shudder in awe of it and in wonder at its beauty and eloquence. Then their skins and hearts would soften to the remembrance of God. “softens” is transitive with to because it includes a verb that is transitive with it, as if it was said: it calmed down and was reassured by the remembrance of God, soft and not contracted. The object of the remembrance of God is omitted, and the meaning is: to the remembrance of God, His mercy, His reward, and His Paradise, and it was omitted because of knowledge of it. Qatada said: This is a description of the friends of God, a description that makes their skin shudder and their hearts find reassurance in the remembrance of God. He did not describe them as having lost their minds or fainting, rather it was mentioned about the people of innovations, which is from Satan. The reference in His statement, that, is to the Book described with those attributes, and it is the subject, and the guidance of God is its predicate: that is, that Book is God. He guides with it whom He wills, that is, He guides him of His servants. It was said that the reference in His statement, that is to what God has given to these people of fear of His punishment and hope of His reward. And he whom God sends astray, that is, He makes whose heart hard and dark, unable to accept the truth, for him there is no guide, who will guide him to the truth and save him from misguidance. The majority of scholars read man had without the yaa’. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaysin read it with the yaa’.
39:24: Then when He judged those whose hearts were hardened with a judgment in this world, which is misguidance, He judged them with another judgment in the Hereafter, which is torment. He said: 24- Is he who will protect himself with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection? The question is for denial, and we have already discussed this and this fa that comes before min in His statement: Is he who has the word of torment justified against him? "Min" is the subject and its predicate is omitted because the context indicates it. The meaning is: Is it he who is meant to protect himself with his face, which is the most honorable of his limbs, from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, since his hand has become shackled to his neck? How safe he is, not affected by any of that and not in need of protection? Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: Is he who protects himself with his face from the evil of the punishment like he who enters Paradise? Ata' and Ibn Zayd said: He will be thrown bound into the Fire, and the first thing that will touch him will be his face. Mujahid said: He will be dragged on his face in the Fire. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is: Is he who protects himself with his face from the evil of the punishment better or Sa'ad? Such as His statement: Is he who is thrown into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Then the Almighty informed about what the keepers will say to the disbelievers, saying: And it will be said to the wrongdoers, ‘Taste what you used to earn.’ This is in apposition to taste: meaning, it will be said to them. The past tense is used to indicate certainty. Ata’ said: meaning, the recompense for what you used to do. Similar to this verse is His statement: This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard. We have already discussed the meaning of tasting in more than one place.
39:25: Then the Almighty informed us about the state of the disbelievers who came before them, saying: 25- Those before them denied meaning the disbelievers who were contemporaries of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning is that they denied their messengers so the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive meaning from a direction from which they did not expect the punishment to come, and that was when they felt secure and were heedless of God’s punishment for their denial.
39:26: 26- So God made them taste disgrace meaning humiliation and degradation in the life of this world by being transformed, swallowed up, killed, captured, and other things. But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater because it is extremely severe and lasting. If they only knew meaning if they were among those who know things, reflect on them, and act in accordance with their knowledge. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said to you that whatever a limb has tasted has reached it: meaning it has reached it just as sweetness and bitterness reach the one who tastes them. He said: And disgrace is the hated thing. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky?} [Al-Bukhari and Muslim], he said: There is no water on earth except that it comes down from the sky, but the veins in the earth change it. This is what His statement: {And springs flow through the earth.} So whoever is pleased that the salt should return to sweetness, let him ascend it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding his statement: {Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam?} [Al-Bukhari and Muslim], he said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: {Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam?} We said: O Prophet of God, how is his breast expanded? He said: When light enters the heart, it expands and becomes spacious. We said: What is the sign of that, O Messenger of God? He said: Returning to the eternal home, turning away from the home of delusion, and preparing for death before death descends.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawader Al-Usul on the authority of Ibn Umar, “A man said: O Prophet of God, which of the believers is the most intelligent? He said: The one who remembers death most often and prepares best for it. When light enters the heart, it expands and becomes spacious. They said: What is the sign of that, O Prophet of God? He said: Returning to the eternal home and turning away from the home of delusion, and preparing for death before death descends.” And he narrated it on the authority of Abu Ja’far Abdullah ibn Al-Miswar on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner, with additions. Then he recited: Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam so that he is upon light from his Lord? Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Shaheen in Al-Targheeb fi’l-Dhikr, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not speak excessively except in remembrance of God, for excessive speech without remembrance of God hardens the heart, and the people furthest from God are those who are hard-hearted. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “They said: O Messenger of God, why don’t you tell us something?” Then the verse was revealed: God has revealed the best of statements. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him regarding his statement: Mathani that he said: The entire Qur’an is mathani. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding the verses that he said: The Qur’an resembles parts to others and relates some parts to others. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding the verse that he said: The Book of God is mathani, the matter is repeated in it repeatedly. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Abdullah ibn Urwah ibn al-Zubayr that he said: I said to my grandmother Asma’: What did the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) do when they recited the Qur’an? She said: They were as God described them, their eyes would tear up and their skin would shudder. I said: What if some people here hear that and a faintness seizes them? She said: I seek refuge in God from Satan. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then is he who will protect himself from the evil of the punishment with his face? He said: He will be taken to the Fire bound and then thrown into it, and the Fire will not touch his face.
39:27: His statement: 27- And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an from every [kind of] example. We have already explained the definition of the example and how to present it in more than one place. The meaning of from every [kind of] example is what they need, and what is meant is not something more general than that. Here it is as in His statement: We have not neglected anything in the Book, meaning anything they need in the matter of their religion. It has been said that the meaning is: What We mentioned of the destruction of previous nations is an example for these people so that they may remember, so that they may be amazed and take heed.
39:28: And the accusative of 28- an Arabic Qur'an is in the state of this, and it is a confirmatory state, and this is called an introductory state, because the state in reality is Arabic, and the Qur'an is an introduction to it, like Zayd came to me, a righteous man: this is what Al-Akhfash said, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative of praise. Al-Zajjaj said: Arabic is in the accusative of the state, and the Qur'an is an emphasis, and the meaning of without crookedness is not disputed in any way. Al-Dahhak said: meaning not different. An-Nahhas said: The best that has been said about its meaning is the saying of Al-Dahhak, and it was said not contradictory. And it was said not ambiguity, and it was said not a mistake, and it was said not a doubt as the poet said: And there has come to you an oath from God without crookedness and a word that is not false. Perhaps they will fear God is another reason after the first reason. It is Perhaps they will remember, meaning so that they may fear disbelief and falsehood.
39:29: Then the Almighty mentioned a parable from the parables of the Qur’an to remind and awaken, saying: 29- God sets forth a parable, meaning He likened one strange situation to another like it. Then He explained the parable, saying: A man among whom are partners at odds with one another. Al-Kisa’i said: He put man in the accusative case because it is an explanation of the parable. It was also said that man is the first object, and like is the second object, and He put the first object last to connect to what completes it. This was previously explained in Surah Yasin. The phrase among whom are partners is in the accusative case as an attribute of man. Tashakkul means disagreement. Al-Farra’ said: That is, different. Al-Mubarrad said: That is, difficult to deal with, from shakas shakas, shakasan, “shakas,” like ‘usar, “ya’sur,” ‘usar, and ‘usar. Al-Jawhari said: Tashakkul means disagreement. He said: It is also said that a man is shakas with a sukun, meaning he is difficult to create. This is an example of someone who associates partners with God and worships many tools. Then he said: "And a man at peace for a man" meaning purely for Him. This is an example of someone who worships God alone. The majority read Salam with a fatha on the seen and the lam. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, and Abu Al-Aaliyah read it with a kasra on the seen and a sukoon on the lam. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Jahdary, Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, and Ya'qub read Salam with an alif and a kasra on the lam, an active participle from Salam lahu so he is safe. Abu Ubayd chose this reading, saying: Because pure safety is the opposite of shared, and peace is the opposite of war, and there is no place for war here. It was answered by saying that if a letter has two meanings, it is only to be interpreted according to the first of them. So peace, even if it is the opposite of war, has another meaning meaning safe, from Salam lahu means: if it is purely for him. Also, what he is obligated to do with Salam is obligatory for him, because he said something is safe meaning it has no defect. Abu Hatim chose the first reading. The result is that the majority read it as a description with a source for emphasis, or a doubling omission: meaning of safe. Similar to it is the reading of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and those with him. Then the Almighty came with what indicates the difference between the two men, saying: Are they equal, for example? This question is for denial and exclusion. The meaning is: Is this one who serves a group of partners with different morals and diverse intentions equal, each of whom uses him, causing him fatigue and exhaustion, while each of them is dissatisfied with his service? And this one who serves one person, with no one else disputing with him? If he obeys him, he is pleased with him, and if he disobeys him, he pardons him. Indeed, between these two there is such an apparent and clear difference that no sane person would be able to pronounce them equal, because one of them is at the highest station, and the other is at the lowest. The word for example is in the accusative case as a specification transferred from the subject, because the original is: Are their two likes equal? The specification is singular and not dual, because the original is singular because it explains the genus. The phrase Praise be to God is a confirmation of what preceded it of negating equality, and to inform the monotheists of the great blessing in their monotheism for God, which deserves to be praised specifically for Him. Then, Suhaana turned away from the negation of istiwa’ understood from the rhetorical question to explaining that most people do not know, saying: Rather, most of them do not know, meaning the polytheists, for they do not know that despite its being clear and obvious. Al-Wahidi and Al-Baghawi said: “What is meant by ‘most’ is all, and what appears is the opposite of what they said, for the believers in God know the exalted status and lofty position of monotheism, and that polytheism is not comparable to it in any way, nor is it equal to it in any description. They know that God, the Exalted, deserves praise for this blessing, and that praise is specific to Him.”
39:30: Then God, the Almighty, informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that death would inevitably overtake him and them, saying: 30- Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die. The majority of scholars read dead and deadly with a shaddah. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Abi Ubla, Isa bin Umar, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Al-Yamani read may'it wa ma'itun, and Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr read it this way. Some commentators approved of this reading because his death and their death are in the future, but there is no basis for favoring it, as the reading of the majority conveys this meaning. Al-Farra' and Al-Kisa'i said: Dead with a shaddah is the one who has not yet died and will die, and dead with a fathah is from qadamat and the soul departed from him. Qatada said: The report of his death was conveyed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the report of their souls was conveyed to them. The reason for this choice was to inform the Companions that he would die.
39:31: Some of them believed that he would not die, even though it was a prelude and preparation for what came after, as he said: 31- Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord. That is, you will dispute with them, O Muhammad, and argue with them that you have conveyed the message to them and warned them, and they will dispute with you, or the believer will dispute with the unbeliever, the oppressor, and the oppressed.
39:32: Then the Almighty explained the situation of each group of disputants, saying: 32- "Then who is more unjust than he who lies about God meaning no one is more unjust than he who lies about God, claiming that He has a son, partner, or wife and denies the truth when it comes to him" which is what the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, came with, calling people to monotheism, commanding them to perform the obligations of the Shari'ah, forbidding them from what is forbidden, and informing them of the resurrection and the Hereafter, and what God has prepared for the obedient and the disobedient. Then the Almighty asked a question to clarify, saying: "Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?" meaning is there not for these slanderers who deny the truth? Abode is the place, and it is derived from thawa in a place if he resided there, he resides there, a residency and a garment, like mada' muda'an and mada'an. Abu Ubaid narrated that it is said athwa, and he recited the words of Al-A'sha: He stayed and shortened the night for Rhodes, so she went and broke the appointment with the tribe Al-Asma'i denied this and said: We do not know Athwa.
39:33: Then the Almighty mentioned the group of believing and confirming believers, saying: 33- And he who brought the truth and believed in it The relative pronoun is in the nominative case as a subject, and it refers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who followed him and his predicate, Those are the righteous. It was said that the one who brought the truth was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the one who confirmed it was Abu Bakr. Mujahid said: The one who brought the truth was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the one who confirmed it was Ali ibn Abi Talib. Al-Suddi said: The one who brought the truth was Gabriel, and the one who confirmed it was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Qatadah, Muqatil, and Ibn Zayd said: The one who brought the truth was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the one who confirmed it were the believers. Al-Nakha'i said: The one who brought the truth and believed in it are the believers who will bring the Qur'an on the Day of Resurrection. It was said that this is general for everyone who called to the Oneness of God and guided to what He legislated for His servants. Ibn Jarir chose this, and he is the one who chose it from these sayings. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: And those who brought the truth and believed in it. The wording as it appears in the majority readings, even if it is singular, has a plural meaning, because it refers to the genus, as indicated by the statement: Those are the righteous, meaning those who are characterized by righteousness, which is the sign of salvation. Abu Saleh read it as and believed in it in a lightened form, meaning the people believed in it.
39:34: Then the Almighty mentioned what these truthful and believing people will have in the Hereafter: 34- They will have whatever they wish with their Lord meaning they will have everything they wish of raising their status, warding off harm, and expiating their sins. This is a great encouragement and intense suspense. The reference in His saying: that is to what was mentioned previously about their reward, and it is the subject, and its predicate is His saying: the reward of the doers of good meaning those who did good in their deeds. It has been proven in the Sahih from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that doing good is to worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you.
39:35: Then the Almighty explained the ultimate goal of what they have with their Lord, saying: 35- That God may remove from them the worst of what they have done. This is the greatest thing they hope to do in terms of warding off harm from them, because if God, the Almighty, forgives them what is worse than that, He will forgive them what is less than that, in a more appropriate way. The lam is related to they wish or to the good-doers or to something omitted. The majority read worse as a comparative. It was also said that it is not for comparison, but rather means the evil of what they did. Ibn Kathir, in a narration from him, read aswa with an alif between the hamza and the waw, with the weight of ajmal, the plural of saw, and will reward them with the best of what they used to do. When God, the Almighty, mentioned what indicates the harm from them, He mentioned what indicates bringing them the greatest benefits. Adding better to what comes after it is not an addition of a preference to a preference, but rather an addition of a thing to some of it with the intention of clarifying without considering preference. Muqatil said: He will reward them with the good deeds they did, but He will not reward them with the bad. Al-Ajurri and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, without any crookedness, that he said: Uncreated. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement, “God presents an example: a man” [verse], that he said: A man worships various gods, so this is an example that God presented for the idolaters. “And a peaceful man” [verse] who worships one God, setting an example for himself. They also narrated from him regarding his statement, “And a peaceful man” [verse], that he said: No one has anything to do with him. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Umar, that he said: “We remained for a period of our time, and we still believed that this verse was revealed about us and the People of the Book before us: ‘Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die’ [verse], until I saw some of us striking each other’s faces with the sword, so I knew that it was revealed about us.” Nu’aym bin Hammad narrated a similar version in Al-Fitan, and Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him a longer version. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: The verse, Then on the Day of Resurrection you will surely dispute before your Lord, was revealed to us and we did not know its meaning until the tribulation occurred, so we said, This is what our Lord promised us that we would dispute about. Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, Ibn Mani’, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym in al-Hilyah and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th al-Nushur narrated on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam that he said: “When the verse, ‘Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will surely dispute before your Lord,’ was revealed, I said, ‘O Messenger of God, will what happened between us in this world be repeated for us along with our special sins?’ He said, ‘Yes, it will be repeated for you until everyone who has a right is given his right.’ Al-Zubayr said, ‘By God, the matter is very difficult.’” Sa'id bin Mansour narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri who said: When the verse, Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord, was revealed, we used to say, Our Lord is one, our religion is one, and our Prophet is one, so what is this dispute? But when the Day of Siffin came and we attacked each other with swords, we said, Yes, this is it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And he who brought the truth meaning, There is no god but God "and believed in it" meaning, in the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), "Those are the righteous" meaning, they avoided polytheism. Ibn Jarir, Al-Bawardi in Ma'rifat Al-Sahaba, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Asid bin Safwan - who was a companion of the Prophet - on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib who said, "The one who brought the truth is Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Abu Bakr believed in it." Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar narration on the authority of Abu Hurayrah.
39:36: His statement: 36- Is not God sufficient for His servant? The majority of scholars read His servant in the singular. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read His servants in the plural. According to the first reading, what is meant is the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) or the genus, with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) being included as a primary inclusion. According to the other reading, what is meant are the prophets or the believers or all of them. Abu Ubaid preferred the reading of the majority of scholars because of the statement after it and they frighten you and the questioning for denial of His lack of sufficiency, glory be to Him, in the most eloquent way, as if it is in a place of manifestation that is not easy for anyone to deny. It was said that what is meant by the servant and the servants is what includes the Muslim and the disbeliever. Al-Jurjani said: God is sufficient for His believing servant and His disbelieving servant, this one with reward, and this one with punishment. It was read as Kafi ‘Ibadah with the addition, and it was read as Yakafi in the present tense. His statement, And they frighten you with those besides Him may be in the accusative case as a state, since the meaning is, Is it not sufficient for you when they frighten you? It may be a new sentence, and those besides Him refers to the deities that they worship. And he whom God sends astray, for him there is no guide, meaning, he upon whom the judgment of his misguidance is due, for him there is no guide to guide him to the right path and bring him out of misguidance.
39:37: 37- And whomsoever God guides, there is for him no misguider who takes him away from guidance and causes him to fall into misguidance. Is not God Exalted in Might? That is, Overpowering and overpowering all things. Possessor of Retribution? He takes revenge on His disobedient ones by inflicting upon them His punishment and by sending down upon them the lash of His punishment.
39:38: 38- And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ God, the Almighty, mentioned their admission, when asked about the Creator, that it was God, the Almighty, despite their worship of idols and their taking of deities other than God. This is the greatest proof that they were in extreme heedlessness and ignorance, because if they knew that the Creator of them and of what they worship other than God is God, the Almighty, then how could their minds accept the worship of other than the Creator of everything and the association of a creation with its Creator in worship? They were mentioned with good minds, perfect perception and complete intelligence, but when they imitated their forefathers and thought well of them, they abandoned what reason required and acted on what was pure ignorance. Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to rebuke them after this confession and to rebuke them, saying: Say, ‘Have you considered what you invoke besides God? If God should intend me harm, can they remove His harm?’ That is, tell me about these gods of yours, are they able to remove the harm that God intends for me? Harm is severity or worse. Or if He intends me mercy, can they withhold His mercy? from me so that it does not reach me? Mercy is grace and ease. The majority of scholars read withholding and revealing in both instances with the addition of a tanween. Abu ‘Umar read them with the tanween. Muqatil said: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) asked them and they remained silent. Another narrator said: They said: It does not repel anything of God’s decree, but it does intercede. So, Say, ‘God is sufficient for me’ was revealed in all my affairs, in bringing benefit and warding off harm. Upon Him do the trustful rely, that is, on Him, not on anyone else. Abu ‘Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose Abu ‘Umar’s reading. Because Kashfat is an active participle in the sense of receiving, and if it is like that, then its tanween is better, and this is how Al-Hasan and Asim read it.
39:39: Then God commanded him to threaten and warn them, so He said: 39- “Say, ‘O my people, work according to your position,’ meaning according to the state you are in and have been able to achieve. ‘I am working,’ meaning according to the state I am in and have been able to achieve. This was omitted because it was known from what preceded it.
39:40: 40- Then you will know who will be afflicted with a punishment that will disgrace him. That is, humiliate and degrade him in this world. Then it will be revealed that he is the one who is wrong and his opponent is the one who is right. What is meant by this punishment is the punishment of this world and what befell them of killing, capture, subjugation and humiliation. Then He mentioned the punishment of the Hereafter, saying: And a lasting punishment will befall him. That is, permanent and ongoing in the Hereafter, and it is the punishment of the Fire.
39:41: Then, when the harm they caused to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was too great for him to bear, he informed him that he was only charged with explaining, not with guiding those who had gone astray, so he said: 41- Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for the people, meaning for their sake and to explain what they were charged with. With the truth is a state of the subject or the object: meaning those who are rightly guided or engaged in the truth. So whoever is guided to the path of truth and follows it, “does so for [the benefit of] his own soul. And whoever goes astray” from it, only goes astray to its detriment, meaning to his own soul, so the harm that this causes to him does not extend to anyone else. And you are not a guardian over them, meaning you are charged with guiding them and are addressed by it. Rather, your only duty is to convey the message, and you have done so. These verses were abrogated by the verse of the sword, for God commanded His Messenger after this to fight them until they say, There is no god but God and implement the rulings of Islam.
39:42: Then the Almighty mentioned a type of His great power and wondrous creation, saying: 42- God takes the souls at the time of their death meaning He takes them when their time comes and takes them out of the bodies and those that do not die during their sleep meaning He takes the souls that do not die: meaning their time has not come during their sleep. There is a difference of opinion on this. Some say that He takes it away from action while the soul remains in the body. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is that He takes away the one that did not die when its appointed time expires. He said: It could be that her sleep takes her, in which case the meaning would be: and the one that did not die has passed away in her sleep. Al-Zajjaj said: Every human being has two souls: one is the soul of discernment, which leaves him when he sleeps so he is unable to reason, and the other is the soul of life: if it ceases, the breath ceases with it, and the sleeper breathes. Al-Qushayri said: There is some ambiguity in this, since the concept of the verse is that the soul taken in both cases is one thing. For this reason, he said: Then He keeps that for which He has decreed death and sends the other, meaning the sleeping one, until a specified term, which is the time set for his death. Ibn Al-Anbari said something similar to what Al-Zajjaj said. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "God takes the souls of the dead when they die and the souls of the living when they sleep, and they get to know each other as long as God wills them to get to know each other. 'He keeps those for whom He has decreed death and sends the other back', returning them. It is more appropriate to say that He takes the souls during sleep by removing sensation and causing a affliction in the place of sensation. He keeps those for whom death has decreed death and does not return them to the body they were in, and sends the other back by restoring their sensation." It was said that the meaning of He takes the souls at the time of their death is with the omission of an adjective: that is, at the death of their bodies. Rational scholars have differed about the soul and the spirit: are they one thing or two? Discussing this would take a long time, and it is well-known in the books written for this purpose. The majority read Qada in the active form, meaning that God decreed death for them. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Al-A'mash, and Yahya ibn Waththab read it in the passive form. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading because it is in agreement with the statement, God takes the souls and the allusion in the statement, Indeed in that to what came before of the taking, retaining, and sending back of souls, are signs, meaning wondrous, amazing signs indicating the dazzling power. However, these are not signs that everyone will understand, rather for a people who reflect on that, ponder it, and use it as evidence of the Oneness of God and the perfection of His power. Indeed, in this taking, retaining, and sending back, there is an admonition for those who take admonition and a reminder for those who remember. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, God takes the souls at the time of their death, that he said: A soul and a spirit between them are like the rays of the sun. So God takes the soul during its sleep and leaves the spirit inside it to turn over and live. If He wishes to take it, He takes the soul and it dies. If He delays its appointed time, He returns the soul to its place in its body. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azmah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Dhiya in al-Mukhtara narrated from him regarding the verse, that he said: The souls of the living and the souls of the dead meet in dreams and ask each other what God wills. Then God holds back the souls of the dead and sends the souls of the living back into their bodies for an appointed term, without making any error in any of them. This is what He said, Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought. Abd ibn Humayd also narrated from him regarding the verse, that he said: Every soul has a cause by which it runs, so when death is decreed for it, it sleeps until the cause is cut off, and the one that did not die in its sleep is left. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you goes to bed, let him shake it out with the inside of his garment, for he does not know what has come upon him afterward. Then let him say: ‘In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and in Your name I raise it. If You should take my soul, then have mercy upon it, and if You should release it, then protect it as You protect Your righteous servants.’”
39:43: His statement: 43- Or have they taken intercessors besides God? “Or” is the detached particle understood by bal and the hamza: meaning, rather, they have taken intercessor gods besides God who intercede for them with God. Say, ‘Even if they did not possess anything nor reason?’ The hamza is for denial and rebuke, and the waw is for conjunction with an implied omitted word: meaning, would they intercede even if they did, etc., and the answer to law is implied, its meaning is you take them: meaning, even if they were of this quality, you take them. The meaning of they do not possess anything is that they do not possess anything, and intercession enters into that as a primary entry, or they reason about something because they are inanimate and have no reason. And their plural with the waw and the nun is because the disbelievers believe that they reason.
39:44: Then He, the Most High, commanded him to inform them that intercession belongs to God alone, so He said: 44- “Say: ‘To God belongs all intercession.’” No one has any of it except by His permission for whomever He is pleased with, as in His statement: Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? and His statement: And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased. The accusative of both is in the state of the state, and intercession is only emphasized by what two or more are emphasized by because it is a verbal noun that is used for one, two, or a group. Then He described His vast kingdom, saying: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, meaning He owns them and owns what is in them and disposes of that as He wishes and does what He wants. Then to Him you will be returned, not to anyone else, and that is after the resurrection.
39:45: 45- And when God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter are filled with disgust. The word alone is in the accusative case as a state according to Yunus, and as a verbal noun according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh. In the language, disgust means aversion. Abu Ubaidah said: ashmaazat means to be repelled. Al-Mubarrad said: it contracted. Qatadah said the first, and Mujahid said the second, and the meanings are close. Al-Mu'raj said: I denied it. Abu Zaid said: The man became frightened from panic. The interpretation of ashmaazat is appropriate for the situation, meaning he contracted, and it is originally azrar. When the polytheists were told, There is no god but God, they would contract, as God related about them in His statement: And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn back in aversion. Then the Almighty mentioned their good tidings at the mention of their idols, saying: And when those other than Him are mentioned, at once they rejoice, meaning they rejoice at that and are delighted by it. The agent of if in His statement, And when God is mentioned is the verb that comes after it, which is ashmaazat, and the agent of if in His statement, And when those other than Him are mentioned is the verb that acts as a sudden factor in if, and the meaning is: They were surprised by the good tidings at the mention of those other than Him.
39:46: And when the rebellious infidels did not accept what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought them of the call to goodness and persisted in their disbelief, God the Almighty commanded him to reject the command, saying: 46- “Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ.” The explanation of Creator of the heavens and the explanation of Knower of the unseen and the witnessed have already been presented, and they are both in the accusative case as a call. The meaning of You will judge between Your servants is that You reward the doer of good for his goodness and punish the doer of evil for his evil. Thus, He reveals who is right and who is wrong, and the disagreement of those who differ and the quarrel of those who quarrel are resolved by Him.
39:47: Then, when he narrated about the disbelievers what he narrated of disgust at the mention of God and joy at the mention of idols, he mentioned what indicates the severity of their torment and the enormity of their punishment, saying: 47- And if those who did wrong had all that is in the earth meaning all that is in the world of wealth and treasures and the like thereof with it meaning added to it they would offer it as ransom from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection meaning from the evil of the punishment of that Day. The explanation of this has already been mentioned in Al Imran. And there will appear to them from God that which they had never reckoned with meaning there will appear to them of God’s punishments, wrath, and severe torment that which they had not reckoned with. In this there is a great threat and a severe warning. Mujahid said: They did deeds that they thought were good deeds, but they turned out to be bad deeds. Al-Suddi said the same. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Woe to the hypocrites, woe to the hypocrites, woe to the hypocrites. This is their sign and their story. Akrima ibn Ammar said: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir was extremely distressed when he was dying. He was asked, What is this distress? He said, “I fear a verse from the Book of God: ‘And there will appear to them from God that which they had never reckoned with.’ So I fear that what I had never reckoned with will appear to me.”
39:48: 48- And the evils of what they had earned will become apparent to them meaning the evils of their actions of polytheism and oppression of God’s friends. It is possible that it is a source: meaning the evils of what they earned, and that it is a relative pronoun: meaning the evils of what they earned. And that which they used to ridicule will encompass them meaning that what they used to ridicule of the warning that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to warn them with will befall them. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: And when God alone is mentioned, they recoil he said: The hearts of these four who do not believe in the Hereafter harden and are repelled Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Al-Walid ibn Uqbah, Sufyan, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf and when those besides Him are mentioned Al-Lat and Al-Uzza behold, they rejoice. Muslim, Abu Dawud, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Aisha who said: “When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) got up at night, he would begin his prayer by saying: O God, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. Guide me to the truth concerning that over which they differ, by Your permission. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.”
39:49: His statement: 49- "So when a human being is touched What is meant by human" here is the species, considering some of its individuals or most of them. It was also said that it refers to the disbelievers only, but the former is more appropriate. The specific reason for its cause does not prevent it from being applied to the species, because considering the generality of the wording fulfills the right of the Qur’anic system and fulfills its meaning. The meaning is that the nature of most of the human species is that if harm touches them, such as sickness, poverty, or something else, they call upon God and implore Him to lift them up and repel them. "Then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, meaning We give him a favor coming from Us, he says, 'I was given it only because of knowledge'" from Me regarding the types of earnings, or because of goodness with Me, or because of knowledge from God regarding My favor. Al-Hasan said: Because of knowledge that God taught me. It was also said that I knew that if I was given this in this world, I would have a status with God. The pronoun in "I was given it" is masculine, even though it refers to the favor because it means a blessing. It was said that the pronoun refers to ma, and it is a relative pronoun, and the first is more appropriate. Rather, it is a trial. This is a response to what he said, meaning that what We gave you is not what you mentioned, rather it is a trial for you and a test of your condition. Will you be grateful or ungrateful? Al-Farra’ said: The pronoun was made feminine in his statement it to make the trial feminine. If he had said, Rather, it is a trial, it would have been permissible. An-Nahhas said: Rather, I gave him a trial. It was said that the pronoun was made feminine in consideration of the word trial, and the first was made masculine in his statement I was given it in consideration of its meaning. But most of them do not know, that this is a luring of them from God and a test of what they have of gratitude or ingratitude.
39:50: 50- Those before them had said it meaning that they said this word which they said, which is their saying: I was only given it because of the knowledge of those before them, like Qarun and others, for Qarun said: I was only given it because of knowledge I have, “so what they were earning did not avail them at all” It is possible for this ma to be negative: meaning what they earned of worldly pleasures did not avail them at all, or for it to be interrogative: meaning what did that avail them at all?
39:51: 51- So the evil consequences of what they earned befell them, meaning the recompense for the evil consequences of their earnings, or they were afflicted with evil consequences that were the recompense for what they earned. The recompense is called evil consequences because it occurs in response to their evil consequences, so this is a case of analogy, like His statement: And the recompense for an evil is an evil consequence like it. Then the Almighty threatened the disbelievers of His time, saying: And those who did wrong among these, the existing disbelievers, will be afflicted by the evil consequences of what they earned, just as those before them were afflicted. And what afflicted them in this world was what afflicted them of famine, killing, captivity, and oppression. And they will not escape, meaning they will be able to escape from God, rather their return is to Him, and He will do with them whatever punishment He wills.
39:52: 52- Do they not know that God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it? That is, He expands provision for whom He wills to expand it. And restricts it. That is, He withholds it for whom He wills to restrict it or restricts it for whom He wills. Muqatil said: God admonished them so that they would consider His Oneness, and that was when they received rain after seven years, and He said: Do they not know that God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it for whom He wills? Indeed in that are signs. That is, in what is mentioned are great indications and signs of the threat, followed by mentioning the breadth of His mercy and the greatness of His forgiveness.
39:53: And he ordered his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give them good tidings of that, saying: 53- Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ What is meant by transgression is going too far in sins and committing many of them. The meaning of do not despair is: do not lose hope in God’s mercy and forgiveness. Then, after he forbade them from despairing, he informed them of what would remove that, raise it, and replace despair with hope, saying: Indeed, God forgives all sins. Know that this verse is the most hopeful verse in the Book of God, the Exalted, because it contains the greatest good report. First, He added the servants to Himself with the intention of honoring them and giving them further good report. Then He described them as being excessive in sins and committing many sins. Then He followed that with the prohibition against despairing of mercy for those who commit many sins. So the prohibition against despairing for sinners who are not excessive is more appropriate and based on the meaning of the address. Then He came with what leaves no doubt after it and no suspicion enters the heart upon hearing it. He said: Indeed, God forgives sins. The definite article has made the plural that it entered into a genus that necessitates the inclusion of its individuals. It is as strong as Indeed, God forgives every sin, whatever it may be, except what the Qur’anic text excludes, which is polytheism. Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. Then He was not satisfied with what He informed His servants of regarding the forgiveness of every sin, but rather confirmed that by saying: all of them. What good report that comforts the hearts of the believing doers of good.” Their belief in their Lord is true, in their hope in Him. They cast off the garments of despair, rejecting bad thoughts about Him Who is not considered too great by any sin, nor is He stingy with His forgiveness and mercy towards His servants who turn to Him seeking pardon and who turn to Him for forgiveness of their sins. How beautiful is the justification with which the Almighty explained this statement, saying that He is the Forgiving, the Most Merciful. That is, He is abundant in forgiveness and mercy, great, eloquent, and vast. So whoever rejects this great favor and abundant gift, and thinks that making God’s servants despair and losing hope in His mercy is more appropriate for them than what God has given them glad tidings of, has committed the greatest excess and the ugliest mistake. For giving good tidings and not causing despair is what God’s promises came with in His Noble Book, and is the path taken by His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as is authentically reported from him in his saying: Make things easy and do not make them difficult, and give good tidings and do not repel. If this is established for you, then know that the combination of this verse and His statement, Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills is that every sin, whatever it may be, except for associating partners with God, is forgiven for whomever God wills to forgive. However, it can be said that His informing us that He forgives all sins indicates that He wills to forgive them all, and that necessitates that He wills to forgive all sinners among the Muslims, so there remains no contradiction between the two verses from this standpoint. As for what a group of commentators claim about restricting this verse to repentance and that it only forgives the sins of those who repent, they claim that they said this to reconcile the verses. It is a combination of the lizard and the nun, and the sailor and the guide, and a lion that reaps its rewards. If this great glad tidings were restricted to repentance, it would not have had much effect, because the repentance of the polytheist will forgive him for what he did of polytheism by starving the Muslims. He said, Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. If repentance was a restriction on forgiveness, then the explicit mention of polytheism would not have been useful. He, the Most High, said, And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for mankind, despite their wrongdoing. Al-Wahidi said, “All the commentators said that this verse is about a people who feared that if they became Muslims, they would not be forgiven for the great sins they committed, such as polytheism, killing a soul, and hostility towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.” I said: Suppose it was for these people, so what would happen? The consideration is what it contains of generality, not the specificity of the cause, as is agreed upon among the people of knowledge. If the Qur’anic verses and the Prophetic hadiths were restricted by their causes and did not go beyond them, then most of the obligations would be lifted from the ummah, if not all of them. The necessary consequence is invalid by consensus, so the required consequence is the same. In the pure Sunnah, there are authentic hadiths in the two Sahihs and others on this subject, which, if the one who studies them truly knows them and appreciates them truly, he will know the correctness of what we have mentioned and recognize the truth of what we have explained. The majority of scholars read O My servants with the ya’ in both connected and paused speech. Abu Bakr narrated from Asim that he pauses without the ya’. The majority of scholars read Taqantu with the noon fatha, while Abu Amr and Al-Kisa’i read it with the noon kasra.
39:54: 54- And turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you and then you will not be helped. That is, return to Him in obedience to what He, glory be to Him, gave them good tidings that He forgives all sins. He commanded them to return to Him by performing acts of obedience and avoiding transgressions. There is nothing in this that indicates that the first verse is restricted to repentance, neither by conformity, nor by implication, nor by commitment. Rather, the most that is in it is that He gave them good tidings of that great glad tiding, then called them to good and frightened them from evil. However, it can be said that this sentence is a new address to the infidels who did not submit, as evidenced by His saying: And submit to Him. He brought it to warn the infidels and warn them after encouraging the Muslims with the first verse and giving them good tidings. Although this is far-fetched, it can be said that it is. The meaning, as it appears, is that God combined for His servants the great glad tidings, the command to turn to Him, be sincere to Him, submit to His command, and submit to His rule. And His saying: before the punishment comes upon you, meaning the punishment of this world, as His statement, before it comes to you, is useful to him. There is nothing in that that indicates what the claimants have claimed and what the despairing and hopeless have held fast to. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.
39:55: 55- And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord, meaning the Qur’an. He says: Perform what He has permitted and forbid what He has forbidden, and the entire Qur’an is good. Al-Hasan said: Commit to obeying Him and avoiding what He has disobeyed. Al-Suddi said: The best is what God has commanded in His Book. Ibn Zayd said: It means the clear verses, and entrust the knowledge of the ambiguous verses to its Knower. It was also said that it refers to the abrogating verse, not the abrogated verses. It was also said that it refers to forgiveness, not to retaliation, in a way that justifies retaliation. It was also said that it refers to the best of what has been revealed to you from the report of past nations: Before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you perceive not. That is, before the punishment surprises you while you are unaware of it and do not perceive it. It was also said that it means that they will die suddenly and fall into the punishment. The first is more appropriate because what comes upon them suddenly is the punishment in this world, with killing, capture, subjugation, fear, and drought, not the punishment of the Hereafter or death, because its coming is not attributed to Him.
39:56: 56- That a soul should say, 'Oh, how I regret what I neglected in relation to God.' The Basrans said: That is, out of caution lest it say. The Kufians said: Lest it say. Al-Mubarrad said: Hasten for fear that it might say, or out of caution lest a soul say. Al-Zajjaj said: For fear that you will reach a state in which you say, 'Oh, how I regret what I neglected in relation to God.' It was said that what is meant by 'soul' here is the disbelieving soul, and it was also said that it means repetition as in His statement, A soul knows what it has brought forth. The majority read Oh, how I regret with an alif instead of the ya' added to it, and the original is Oh, how I regret. Ibn Kathir read Oh, how I regret with a silent ha' as a pause, and Abu Ja'far read Oh, how I regret with a ya' as the original. Regret is remorse, and the meaning of Oh, how I neglected in relation to God is Oh, how I neglected in obeying God, as Al-Hasan said. Ad-Dahhak said: Oh, how I neglected in remembrance of God, meaning the Quran and acting upon it. Abu Ubaidah said, In the side of God, meaning in the reward of God. Al-Farra’ said, The side is nearness and neighborhood, meaning in the nearness and neighborhood of God. From this is his statement, and the companion is by the side. The meaning according to this statement is, because you neglected seeking the side of God, meaning in seeking His neighborhood and closeness, which is Paradise. Ibn al-A’rabi said the same. Al-Zajjaj said, “That is, you neglected the path which is the path of God, in His Oneness and the acknowledgment of the prophethood of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Based on this, the side means the side, meaning you fell short in the side that leads to the pleasure of God. From this is the statement of the poet: People are on one side and the prince is on the other People on one side and the ruler on the other. And if you were among the mockers. That is, you were nothing but one of those who mocked the religion of God in this world. The accusative case of the sentence is in the state of circumstance. Qatada said: It was not enough for him to neglect the obedience of God, so he mocked its people.
39:57: 57- Or you say, ‘If God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.’ That is, if God had guided me to His religion, I would have been among those who avoid polytheism and sins. This is among the false arguments that the polytheists use, and the invalid reasons they use, as in His statement: Those who associate others with God will say, ‘If God had willed, we would not have associated others with Him.’ It is a true statement with which they intend falsehood.
39:58: Then the Almighty mentioned another statement of what they said, saying: 58- Or you will say when you see the punishment, ‘If only I had another chance’ meaning a return to the world so I could be among the doers of good, the believers in God, those who believe in Him alone, those who do good in their deeds. The accusative of I could be is either because it is conjoined with karah, which is a verbal noun, and I could be is interpreted as a verbal noun, as in the poet’s saying: Wearing an abaya and having my eyes comforted is more beloved to me than wearing something transparent. Al-Farra recited on this: You have nothing from it but remembrance and fear, and you ask about its riders, where they headed. Or because it is the answer to the wish understood from his saying: If I had a chance.
39:59: Then the Almighty mentioned His answer to these wishful souls who make excuses without a reason, saying: 59- Yes, My signs did come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers. What is meant by the signs are the revealed verses, which is the Qur'an. The meaning of denying them is that they are not from God, and you were too arrogant to believe in them. Along with that, there was denial and arrogance from the disbelievers in God. The Almighty addressed the masculine gender in His statement: They came to you, and you denied and were arrogant, because the self nafs is used to refer to both the male and the believer. Al-Mubarrad said: The Arabs say one self nafs wahid, meaning one person. The majority of people read it with a fat-ha on the ta' in these instances. Al-Jahdary, Abu Haywah, and Yahya ibn Ya'mar read it with a kasra in all of them, and this is the reading of Abu Bakr, his daughter Aisha, and Umm Salamah, and it was narrated from Ibn Kathir.
39:60: 60- And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces will be blackened. That is, you will see those who lied about God, that He had partners, a wife, and a son, their faces will be blackened because of the torment that surrounded them and the wrath and punishment that they witnessed. The phrase their faces will be blackened is in the accusative case as a state. Al-Akhfash said: You will see is not an agent in their faces will be blackened. Rather, it is the subject and predicate. The first is that you see if it is from visual vision, so the phrase their faces will be blackened is a state. But if it is from the heart, then it is in the accusative case as the second object of you will see. The question in His statement, Is there not in Hell a residence for the arrogant? is for confirmation: that is, there is no place in it for those who are too arrogant to obey God. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people, as proven in the authentic hadith.
39:62: His saying: 62- God is the Creator of all things of the things that exist in this world and the hereafter, whatever they may be, without any difference between one thing and another. The interpretation of this verse has been presented in Al-An’am And He is Disposer of all things meaning that all things are entrusted to Him, so He is the One who preserves and manages them without anyone sharing with Him.
39:63: 63- To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. The singular of al-maqallad is maqallad or it has no singular form from the same word as asateer. They are the keys of the heavens and the earth, sustenance, and mercy. This was said by Muqatil, Qatadah, and others. Al-Layth said: Al-maqallad is the treasury. The meaning of the verse is To Him belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, sustenance, and mercy. This was said by Muqatil, Qatadah, and others. Al-Layth said: Al-maqallad is the treasury. The meaning of the verse is To Him belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said the same. It was said that the treasuries of the heavens are the rain, and the treasuries of the earth are the plants. It was said that it is an expression of His power and His preservation of it, but the former is more appropriate. Al-Jawhari said: Al-maqallad is the key. Then he said: The plural is al-maqallad. It was said that it is There is no god but God, and God is the Greatest, “Glory be to God and His praise,” I seek forgiveness from God, and There is no might nor power except with God. And it was said otherwise: And those who disbelieve in the signs of God - it is they who are the losers, meaning the Qur’an and all the other signs that indicate God Almighty and His Oneness. The meaning of losers is: those who are complete in loss because they have gone to Hell by this disbelief.
39:64: 64- Say, 'Is it other than God that you command me to worship, O ignorant ones?' The interrogative is for censure and criticism, and the fa is for conjunction with an implied word like its counterparts, and ghair is in the accusative case with ibdu, and abdu is the object of ta'amruoni based on the assumption that the verbal noun, but when it was deleted its function was lost. The original form is: Do you command me to worship other than God? Al-Kisa'i and others said: It is permissible for ghair to be in the accusative case with ta'amruoni, and abdu is a substitute for it, a substitute of inclusion, and an is also implied with it. It is permissible for ghair to be in the accusative case with an implied verb: i.e., do you compel me to worship other than God? i.e., to worship other than God or to worship other than God, I worship. He, the Almighty, commanded him to say this to the disbelievers when they called him to what they were upon of idol worship and said, This is the religion of your fathers. The majority read ta'amruna by assimilating the noun of raising with the noun of protection, with a difference of opinion among them regarding opening or sukoon on the ya'. Nafi’ read ta’muruni with a light nun and a fatha on the yaa, and Ibn ‘Amir read ta’muruni with a fatha and a sukoon on the yaa.
39:65: 65- And it has already been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and to those before you meaning, of the messengers, that if you associate [anything] with God, your work will surely become worthless, and you will surely be among the losers. This statement is an allusion to other than the messengers, because God, the Exalted, has protected them from associating partners with God. The reason for bringing it up in this manner is to warn and caution the servants against associating partners with God, because if it were to render the work of the prophets worthless, then the estimation would be that it would render the work of other nations worthless, even more so. It has been said that there is an inversion in the statement, and the estimation is: A son has revealed to you, If you associate partners with God, and the same was revealed to those before you. Muqatil said: That is, He revealed to you and to the prophets before you the monotheism, and monotheism is omitted. Then He said: If you associate partners with God, O Muhammad, your work will surely become worthless, and this is addressed specifically to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that the address in His statement, If you associate, is singular, considering each one of the prophets: as if it was said, This speech was revealed to you and to each one of the prophets, which is ‘if you associate,’ and this verse is restricted to death in polytheism as in the other verse, And whoever among you turns back from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless. And say that this is exclusive to the prophets because polytheism among them is a greater sin than polytheism among others, and the first is more appropriate.
39:66: Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to worship Him alone, saying: 66- Rather, worship God alone. This is a refutation of the polytheists who ordered him to worship idols, and the point of the refutation is what is indicated by the precedence of restriction. Al-Zajjaj said: The wording of the name God is accusative with worship. He said: There is no disagreement on this between the Basrans and Kufians. Al-Farra' said: It is accusative with an implied verb, and a similar narration was reported from Al-Kisa'i, but the former is more appropriate. Al-Zajjaj said: The fa in worship is for recompense. Al-Akhfash said: It is redundant. Ata' and Muqatil said the meaning of worship alone is because His worship is not valid except by His aloneness. And be among the grateful for His favor upon you in guiding you to monotheism and calling to His religion and choosing you for the message.
39:67: 67- And they did not appraise God with His true appraisal. Al-Mubarrad said: meaning, they did not glorify Him with His true greatness, like when you say that so-and-so is of great stature. He only described them thus because they worshipped other than God and ordered His Messenger to be like them in polytheism. Al-Hasan, Abu Haywah, and Isa bin Umar read qadru with emphasis. And the earth entirely will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection. In the language, a fist is what you grasp with your entire hand. So, the Almighty informed us of the greatness of His power, that the entire earth, with its vastness and density, is within His grasp, like something that someone grasps with their hand, as they say: it is in the hand of so-and-so, and in his grasp is something that is easy for him to dispose of even if he does not grasp it. Similarly, His statement: And the heavens are folded in His right hand. The mention of the right hand is to exaggerate the perfection of His power, just as one of us folds something that is destined for him with his right hand. The right hand in the speech of the Arabs may mean power and possession. Al-Akhfash said, By his right hand, meaning in his ability, like his saying: Or what your right hands possess, meaning what you have the ability to do. The right hand does not possess power over you, rather than the left and the rest of the body. From this is His, the Most High, saying: We would have seized him by the right hand, meaning by force and ability. From this is the saying of the poet: If a banner is raised for glory, Araba will receive it with her right hand. And the other said: When I saw the sun shining, I took what I needed from it with my right hand. And the other said: I sneezed with a raised nose and reached for the chandelier with my hands, sitting upright. The phrase and the earth entirely in His grasp is in the accusative case as a state of circumstance, meaning that they did not glorify it with the glorification He deserves, and the fact is that He is described by this attribute that indicates complete power. The majority of scholars read his grasp in the nominative case as the predicate of the subject, while Al-Hasan read it in the accusative case. Ibn Khalawayh argued that it is a circumstantial case, meaning in His grasp. The majority read folded in the nominative case as the predicate of the subject, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state like the one before it, and with his right hand is related to folded or a state of the pronoun in folded on the earth, and his grip is the predicate on the earth and the heavens, and folded is a state, or folded is accusative with an implied verb, and with his right hand is the predicate, and he mentioned the Day of Resurrection specifically even though his power is comprehensive, because claims are cut off on it as the Almighty said The kingdom on that Day belongs to God and said Owner of the Day of Judgment then the Almighty cleared himself of saying: Glory be to Him and He is exalted above what they associate with Him of the deities that they make partners with Him despite this great power and dazzling wisdom.
39:68: 68- And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will be stunned. This is the first blast. The Trumpet is the horn that Israfil will blow, and it has been mentioned more than once. The meaning of stunned is that their minds will be lost, so they will fall unconscious. It was also said that they will die. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said that the people of the heavens and the earth died from the terror and the loudness of the sound. The majority read the Trumpets with a sukoon on the waw, while Qatada and Zayd ibn Ali read it with a fatha, the plural of sawrah. The exception in His statement, except whom God wills, is connected, and the exception is Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil. It was also said that it is Ridwan, the bearers of the Throne, and the keepers of Paradise and Hell. Then He will blow into it again. It is permissible for another to be in the nominative case as a substitute, and it is an attribute of a deleted source: that is, another blast. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case, and the one standing in the place of the subject. Then at once they will be standing, looking. This means that all of creation will be standing on their feet, looking at what will be said to them, or waiting for that. The majority read it as a nominative case as predicate, and they look forward to reading it as an accusative case as a state. Zayd ibn Ali read it as a accusative case as a state, and the predicate is they look forward to reading it, and the factor in the state is what the factor in the sudden idha does. Al-Kisa’i said, Like saying, ‘I went out and saw Zayd sitting.’
39:69: 69- And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord. Shining means illumination. It is said that the sun shone, meaning it illuminated, and rose, meaning that it rose. The meaning of with the light of its Lord is with the justice of its Lord, as stated by Al-Hasan and others. Ad-Dahhak said: with the decree of its Lord, and the meaning is that the earth was illuminated and lit up by what God established of justice among its people, and what He decreed of truth among them. Justice is light and injustice is darkness. It was also said that God will create a light on the Day of Resurrection that will cover the face of the earth, so it will shine with it, other than the light of the sun and the moon. There is nothing wrong with interpreting it according to its literal meaning, for God Almighty is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The majority of scholars read shine in the active form, while Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Jawza’, and Ubaid bin Umair read it in the passive form. It was said that the Book was placed in the Preserved Tablet. Qatadah said: “It means the books and scrolls in which are the deeds of the children of Adam. So I will take him with my right hand and I will take him with my left,” and Muqatil said the same. It was said that it is from the accountant who placed the book of accounting in his hands: that is, the book was placed for the account. And the prophets will be brought that is, they will be brought to the place of standing and they will be asked about the answers of their nations. And the witnesses who testify against the nations from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as in His statement: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people.
