It was said that what is meant by the martyrs are those who were martyred in the cause of God, so they will testify on the Day of Resurrection for those who defended the religion of God. It was said that they are the guardians, as God Almighty said: And every soul will come with a driver and a witness “And it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged” that is, the servants will be protected by justice and honesty, and the fact is that they will not be wronged: that is, their reward will not be reduced nor will it be increased beyond what they deserve of punishment.
39:70: 70- And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has done of good and evil and He is most knowing of what they do in this world. He does not need a scribe, a calculator, or a witness. Rather, the book was placed and the prophets and witnesses were brought to complete the argument and eliminate the excuse.
39:71: Then the Almighty mentioned the details of what He mentioned about every soul being fully compensated for what it earned, saying: 71- And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups. That is, the disbelievers will be driven to the Fire while they are in groups: that is, scattered groups, one following the other. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said, groups, scattered groups, one following the other. And from this is the saying of the poet: You see people coming to his doors in groups, one after the other. It is derived from az-Zumar, which means sound, as a group is never without it. Until, when they come to it, its gates are opened meaning the gates of Hell are opened for them to enter it, and there are seven gates. This has been explained in Surat al-Hijr. And its keepers will say to them the plural of khazin is like sadanah and sadaan Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves meaning from among yourselves reciting to you the verses of your Lord which He sent down to them and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours meaning frightening you of the meeting of this day in which you have become? They said this to them as a rebuke and a rebuke, so they responded by confessing and were unable to engage in the argument they used in this world because the matter had been exposed and made clear. For this reason, they said, ‘Yes’ meaning the messengers have come to us with the verses of God and they warned us of what we will encounter. But the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers which is I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.
39:72: So when they confessed this confession 72- It was said, ‘Enter the gates of Hell’ which have been opened for you to enter, and the accusative of eternally is in the state: meaning destined for eternity. So wretched is the abode of the arrogant the one specifically condemned is omitted: meaning wretched is their abode, Hell. The explanation of the abode has been presented in more than one place. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, The keys of the heavens and the earth, that he said: Their keys. Abu Ya’la, Yusuf al-Qadi, Abu al-Hasan al-Qattan, Ibn as-Sunni, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Uthman ibn Affan, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the statement of God, ‘To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth.’ He said to me: ‘O Uthman, you have asked me about a matter that no one before you has asked me about. The keys of the heavens and the earth are: There is no god but God, and God is the Greatest, and Glory be to God, and Praise be to God, and I seek forgiveness from God, other than whom there is no god, and the First and the Last, and the Evident and the Immanent, He gives life and causes death, and He is Alive and does not die, in His Hand is good, and He has power over all things.’ Then he mentioned the merit of these words.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Uthman, who said: He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: ‘Tell me about the keys of the heavens and the earth.’ So he mentioned them. Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of Uthman. Al-Aqili and Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of Uthman. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Quraysh invited the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to give him money so that he would be the richest man in Mecca and they would marry him to any women he wanted and they would have intercourse with his heels. They said to him: This is for you, O Muhammad, and refrain from cursing our gods and not speaking ill of them. He said: Until I see what comes to me from my Lord. So the revelation came: “Say: O you disbelievers” to the end of the Surah, and God revealed to him: “Say: Is it other than God that you order me to worship, O you ignorant ones?” to His saying: of the losers. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: A rabbi came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: “O Muhammad, we find that on the Day of Resurrection God will carry the heavens on a finger, the trees on a finger, the water and the soil on a finger, and the rest of creation on a finger, and He will say, ‘I am the King.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed and said: “O Muhammad, we find that on the Day of Resurrection God will carry the heavens on a finger, the trees on a finger, the water and the soil on a finger, and the rest of creation on a finger, and He will say, ‘I am the King.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed until his molars were visible in confirmation of what the rabbi had said. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: ‘And they have not appraised God with true appraisal, and the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection.’” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “God will grasp the earth on the Day of Resurrection and roll up the heavens with His right hand, then He will say, ‘I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?’” There are hadiths and reports on this topic that indicate that carrying The verse should be taken literally, without any interpretation or arbitrary interpretation. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: “A Jewish man in the marketplace of Medina said: ‘By Him Who chose Moses over all mankind.’ A man from the Ansar raised his hand and slapped him. He said: ‘Do you say this while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is among us?’ I mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: ‘God says: “And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.’ So I will be the first to raise his head, and suddenly I will see Moses holding onto one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether his head was raised before me or whether he was one of those whom God excepted.” Abu Ya’la, al-Daraqutni in al-Ifrad, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said regarding His statement: ‘except whom God wills,’ he said: ‘They are the martyrs, wearing their swords around His Throne, and the angels will meet them on the Day of Resurrection.’” It was narrated by Saeed bin Mansour and Abd bin Hamid from the sayings of Abu Hurairah. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Abu Nasr Al-Sajzi in Al-Ibanah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his statement: Except whom God wills. He said: Gabriel, Michael, the Angel of Death, and Israfil. And the bearers of the Throne. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Jabir regarding his statement: Except whom God wills, he said: Moses, because he had been struck dead before. There are many hadiths that have been narrated about how the trumpet will be blown. Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, he said: The prophets are the messengers, and the witnesses are those who testify that they conveyed the message, and there is no slander or cursing among them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: They testify that the message was conveyed and that the nations denied them.
39:73: After He mentioned previously the state of those who disbelieved and their being driven to Hell, He mentioned here the state of the righteous and their being driven to Paradise, saying 73- And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups. That is, the angels will drive them in a drive of honor, respect, and glorification. The meaning of groups has been explained previously. Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, is the answer to the omitted if. Al-Mubarrad said that it means: they were happy and it was opened. He recited the words of the poet: Even if it were a soul that would all die, it would be a soul that sheds souls So the answer to law was deleted, and the meaning is: I would have gone. Al-Zajjaj said: My opinion is that the answer is deleted based on the estimation: until they came to it, and these things that I mentioned entered it, so the answer is they entered it, and it was deleted because there is evidence for that in the speech. Al-Akhfash and the Kufians said: The answer is opened and the waw is redundant, which is a mistake according to the Basrans, because the waw is one of the letters of meaning and is not added. It was said that the addition of the waw is evidence that the gates were opened for them before they came due to their honor with God, and the estimation is: until they came to it and its gates are open, based on His statement: Gardens of Eden, their gates open for them. The waw was deleted in the story of the people of Hell because they stood before Hell and it was opened after they stood as a humiliation and intimidation. An-Nahhas mentioned its meaning, attributing it to some of the people of knowledge. He said: I do not know that anyone preceded him in that. According to this statement, the waw is the waw of state with the estimation of qad: meaning they came to it and the gates were opened for them. It was said that it is the waw of the eight, because it was the custom of the Arabs to say in numbers: five, six, seven, and eight. This has been fully discussed in Surah Bara’ah and in Surah Al-Kahf as well. Then God the Almighty informed that the keepers of Paradise greet the believers, saying: “And its keepers will say to them, ‘Peace be upon you.’” That is, peace be upon you from every affliction. You were good in this world, and you were not defiled by polytheism and sins. Mujahid said: You were good by obeying God. It was also said that it was by doing good deeds, but the meaning is the same. Muqatil said: “When they cross the bridge of Hell, they will be detained on a bridge between Paradise and Hell, and retribution will be taken from each other for the wrongs that were committed between them. Then, when they are refined and refined, Ridwan and his companions will say to them, “Peace be upon you,” the verse. So enter it, that is, enter Paradise. Abiding eternally, that is, destined for eternity.
39:74: At that point the people of Paradise will say 74- Praise be to God, Who has fulfilled His promise to us of resurrection and reward in Paradise and has given us inheritance of the earth meaning the land of Paradise as if it had come from someone other than them to them so they could take possession of it and dispose of it. It has also been said that they inherited the land that had belonged to the people of Hell if they had been believers. This is what most of the commentators have said. It has also been said that it is the land of this world, and there is an inversion in the speech. We will settle in Paradise wherever we will meaning we will take in it whatever homes we will wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers the one specifically praised is omitted: meaning how excellent is the reward of the workers in Paradise. This is part of what the people of Paradise have said.
39:75: It was said that it is from the saying of God Almighty 75- And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne meaning surrounding it and enveloping it. It is said that the people surrounded someone if they went around him, and it is an additional word said by Al-Akhfash, or for the beginning, and the meaning is: that the one who sees will see them in this state on that day. The phrase glorifying with praise of their Lord is in the accusative case as a state: meaning in the state of their being glorifying God and engulfed in His praise. It was said that the meaning of glorifying is that they pray around the Throne in thanks to their Lord, and al-hafeen is the plural of haaf, said by Al-Akhfash. Al-Farra’ said: It has no singular, as this name does not apply to them except together. And it was judged between them in truth, meaning between the servants by admitting some of them into Paradise and some into Hell. It was also said that it was between the prophets who were brought with the martyrs and their nations with the truth. It was also said that it was between the angels by establishing them in their homes according to their degrees, but the first is more appropriate. And it was said, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds,’ the speakers are the believers who praised God for His judgment between them and the people of Hell with the truth. It was also said that the speakers are the angels who praised God Almighty for His justice in judgment and His judgment between His servants with the truth. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The first group to enter Paradise will be like the moon on a full moon night, and those who follow them will be like the brightest shining star in the sky. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Paradise has eight gates, one of which is called the Gate of Rayyan, which none will enter except those who fast. There are hadiths in the two Sahihs and others that indicate that Paradise has eight gates. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatadah, regarding the verse, And We have inherited the earth, he said: The land of Paradise. Hannad narrated a similar narration on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah.
40:1: It is Surat Al-Mu'min, and it is called Surat Al-Tul. It is Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ata’, Ikrimah, and Jabir. Al-Hasan said: Except for the verse: And glorify the praises of your Lord, because the prayers were revealed in Medina. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: Except for two verses that were revealed in Medina, which are: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the verses of God and the one after it, which are eighty-five verses, and it was said eighty-two verses. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Ha Mim al-Mu’min was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar narration from Ibn al-Zubayr. Ibn al-Durais, al-Nahhas, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The seven Ha Mim surahs were revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami narrated from Samurah ibn Jundub that he said: All the Ha Mim surahs were revealed in Mecca. Muhammad bin Nasr and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “God gave me the seven Ha-Mim surahs in place of the Torah, and He gave me the Ra’s to the Ta-Sin surahs in place of the Gospel, and He gave me what is between the Ta-Sin and the Ha-Mim surahs in place of the Psalms. He favored me with the Ha-Mim surahs and the Mufassal surahs. No prophet before me recited them.” Abu Ubaid narrated in his Fada’il on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Everything has a core, and the core of the Qur’an is Al-Ha-Mim. Abu Ubaid, Ibn Ad-Durais, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Ha-Mim surahs are the brocade of delicate gardens in which I adorn myself. Abu Al-Shaykh, Abu Nu’aym and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The Ha-Mim surahs are the brocade of the Qur’an. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha’b on the authority of Khalil ibn Murrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Ha-Mim surahs are seven, and the gates of Hellfire are seven. Each Ha-Mim surah comes and stands at one of these gates, saying: ‘O God, do not let anyone who believes in me and recites me enter through this gate.’” Abu Ubaid, Ibn Sa’d, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha’b on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites Ha-Mim al-Mu’min until ‘To Him is the final destination’ and Ayat al-Kursi in the morning will be protected by them until the evening, and whoever recites them in the evening will be protected by them until the morning.” His statement: 1- "Ha Mim" The majority of people read it with a full fatha on the haas, while Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with a pure imala. Abu Amr read it with a half-way imala, and the majority read Ha Mim with a sukoon on the meem like the rest of the disconnected letters. Al-Zuhri read it with a damma as the predicate of an implied subject or a subject and the predicate is what follows it. Isa bin Omar Al-Thaqafi read it with a fatha as it is accusative by an implied verb or as a constructional vowel not a grammatical vowel. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abu Al-Samak read it with a kasra due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, or by estimating an oath. The majority of people read it by connecting the haa to the meem. Abu Ja'far read it with a qata'. There is a difference of opinion regarding its meaning. Some say it is one of the names of God, and others say it is one of the names of the Quran. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kisa’i said it means He has decided, and they made it mean Ha Meem, meaning He has decided and happened. Others say it means Ha Meem, the command of God, meaning His victory is near for His friends and His vengeance for His enemies. All of this is unnecessary and unnecessary and arbitrary. The truth is that this opening to this and others like it are among the ambiguous verses whose meaning God has kept to Himself, as we have already explained in the opening verse of Surat Al-Baqarah.
40:2: 2- The revelation of the Book is the predicate of Lahm on the assumption that it is a subject, or a predicate of an implied subject, or it is a subject and its predicate is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. Al-Razi said: What is meant by revealed is the one who revealed, and the meaning is: that the Qur'an was revealed from God and is not a lie against Him. The Exalted in Might is the Victorious, the Dominant, and the Knowing is the One who has abundant knowledge of His creation and what they say and do.
40:3: 3- Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment Al Farraa' said: He made it like an adjective for a definite noun, and it is indefinite. The reason for his statement is that its addition is verbal, but it is permissible to make its addition semantic as Sibawayh said that everything that is not purely added can be made pure and used to describe definite nouns except for the adjective. As for the Kufians, they did not exclude anything, but rather made the adjective like the active participle in the permissibility of making it a pure addition, and that is when it does not mean a specific time, so they allow for the word severe here to be a pure addition. According to Sibawayh, it must be interpreted as mushadd. Al-Zajjaj said: These three adjectives are in the accusative case as a substitute. It was narrated that he made Ghafir and Qaabil in the genitive case as a description, and Shadid in the genitive case as a substitute. The meaning is: Forgiver of the sin of His friends and Accepter of their repentance, and Severe in punishment of His enemies. Tawb is a verbal noun meaning repentance from taaba yatoob tawbah wa tawban. It was also said that it is the plural of tawbah. It was also said that Ghafir is the sinner of those who say la ilaha illa God, and Accepter of repentance from polytheism, and Severe in punishment of those who do not believe in His Oneness. His statement, Owner of Tow may be an adjective, because it is a definite noun, or it may be a substitute. The root of tow is blessings and favor: meaning, the One who bestows blessings upon His servants and bestows favors upon them. Mujahid said: the One of richness and spaciousness. From this is His statement, And whoever among you cannot afford to have enough, meaning riches and spaciousness. Ikrimah said: the One of tow is the One who bestows favors. Al-Jawhari said: Tow with a fat-ha means to be long upon him and to be long upon him if he bestows favors upon him. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: the One of tow is the One of favors. Al-Mawardi said: The difference between man and favors is that man is forgiveness for a sin, while favors are undeserved kindness. Then he mentioned what indicates His Oneness and that He is the One worthy of worship, saying: “There is no god but Him. To Him is the final destination,” not to anyone else, and that will be on the Last Day.
40:4: Then when he mentioned that the Qur’an is the Book of God, which He revealed to guide people in religion, he mentioned the conditions of those who dispute about it with the intention of invalidating it, so he said: 4- None dispute about the verses of God except those who disbelieve. That is, none dispute about refuting and denying the verses of God except those who disbelieve. What is meant is arguing with falsehood and intending to refute the truth, as in His statement: And they dispute with falsehood to refute thereby the truth. As for arguing to clarify the truth, remove ambiguity, search for the stronger and weaker, the decisive and ambiguous, and repel the ambiguous verses of the Qur’an that the falsifiers cling to, and return them through argument to the decisive, then this is one of the greatest ways for those who seek to draw near. With this, God took a covenant from those who were given the Book, so he said: “And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, ‘You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it. ’” And He said: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear to the people in the Scripture—those are cursed by God and cursed by those who curse. And He said: And do not… “Dispute with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best.” So let not their moving about in the land deceive you. When God, the Almighty, ruled that those who disputed about God’s verses were disbelievers, He forbade His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, from being deceived by any of their worldly fortunes, saying: “So let not what they do of trade in the land, or the profits they obtain and the wealth they accumulate, deceive you, for they will be punished soon, and if they are given respite, then indeed they will not be neglected.” Al-Zajjaj said: Do not be deceived by their safety after their disbelief, for their outcome is destruction. The majority of scholars read la yughirrak without assimilation. Zayd ibn Ali and Ubayd ibn Umair read it with assimilation.
40:5: Then he explained the condition of those who came before them, and that these people followed the same path as those people in denial, so he said: 5- Before them, the people of Noah denied, and so did the parties after them. The pronoun in after them refers to the people of Noah, meaning, the parties who formed parties against the messengers after the people of Noah, such as Aad and Thamud, denied. And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him. That is, every nation of those nations that denied their messenger who was sent to them plotted to seize him, so that they could seize him, imprison him, torture him, and do whatever they wanted to him. Qatada and As-Suddi said: to kill him. Seizing may also mean destroying, like his statement: Then I seized them, so how was My punishment. The Arabs call a prisoner a captive. “And they argued with falsehood to refute thereby the truth.” That is, they argued with their messenger with falsehood to refute thereby the truth and remove it. From this comes the word dahdha, meaning a slippery slope and a slippery slope. Falsehood is dahdha because it slips and disappears, so it does not settle. Yahya bin Salam said: They argued with the prophets about polytheism in order to invalidate faith. So I seized them, so how was My punishment? That is, I seized these people who argued with falsehood, so how was My punishment with which I punished them? The first-person ya’ was deleted from punishment in order to replace it with a kasra in both connected and paused speech because it is the beginning of a verse.
40:6: 6- And thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who disbelieve. That is, it has become necessary, established, and binding. It is said that something is haqq true if it is binding and established. The meaning is: Just as the word of punishment came into effect upon the nations who denied their messengers, it has come into effect upon those who disbelieved in it, argued falsely, and formed parties against you. The phrase that they are the companions of the Fire is for the purpose of al-Sharh 94:that is, because they deserve the Fire. Al-Akhfash said: that is, because they, or because they. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case instead of word. The majority read word in the singular form, while Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read words in the plural form.
40:7: Then he mentioned the referents of the bearers of the Throne and those around it, saying: 7- Those who carry the Throne and those around it. The relative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is they glorify the praises of their Lord. The sentence is a new sentence intended to console the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) by explaining that this type of angels, who are of the highest ranks, add to their glorification of God and belief in Him the seeking of forgiveness for those who believed in God and His Messenger and were truthful. What is meant by those around the Throne are the angels who circle around it, glorifying and magnifying God. It is in the nominative case in apposition to those who carry the Throne, and this is the apparent meaning. It was also said that it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case in apposition to the Throne, but the former is more appropriate. The meaning is that the angels who carry the Throne, as well as the angels who are around the Throne, glorify God, immersed in His praise for His blessings, and they believe in God and seek forgiveness from God for His believing servants. Then, the Almighty explained how they seek forgiveness for the believers, saying, narrating from them, Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge. This is by estimating the saying: that is, they say, Our Lord, or saying, Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge. The word mercy and knowledge are in the accusative case as a distinguishing feature transferred from the subject. The original is Your mercy and knowledge have encompassed all things. “So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way,” that is, they have repented from sins and followed the way of God, which is the religion of Islam. And protect them from the punishment of Hellfire, that is, save them from it.
40:8: 8- Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eden. And admit them is in apposition to His statement: Say goodbye to them. It is in the middle of the vocative sentence to emphasize the repetition, and He described the Gardens of Eden as which You have promised them "and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring." That is, admit whoever was righteous. What is meant by righteousness here is belief in God and doing what God has prescribed. Whoever does that is righteous to enter Paradise. It is permissible to connect "and whoever was righteous to the pronoun in Wa'adathum" I promised them: that is, I promised whoever was righteous. It is better to connect it to the first pronoun in "Wa'adathum" And admit them. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: It is accusative from two places: if you wish, on the pronoun in "Adhkaalhum I admitted them, and if you wish, on the pronoun in Wa'adathum" I promised them. The majority of scholars read it with a fat-ha on the lam of "salih" righteousness. Ibn Abi Ubla read it with a damma. The majority of scholars read "and their offspring" in the plural. Isa ibn Umar read it in the singular: "Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise" (i.e., the Victorious, the Subduer, the Abundant, the Dazzling.
40:9: 9- And protect them from evil deeds meaning the punishments, or the recompense for evil deeds, based on the estimation of an omitted complement. Qatada said: Protect them from the torment that will distress them. And whomsoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection, You have had mercy on him. It is said, He protected him means, He preserved him. The meaning of You have had mercy on him is, You have had mercy on him from Your punishment and admitted him into Your Paradise. The reference in His statement, And that is to what came before of their being admitted into Paradise and their being protected from evil deeds. This is the subject and its predicate. It is the great triumph meaning, the victory like which no other triumph is equal, and the salvation like which no other salvation is equal. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: Ha Meem is one of the names of God. Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, Abu Ubaid, Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Muhallab ibn Abi Sufrah who said: “Someone who heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say on the night of the Battle of the Trench told me: ‘If you come tonight, say, “Ha Meem, they will not be helped.”’” Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Nasa’i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When you meet your enemy, let your slogan be, ‘Ha Meem, they will not be helped.’ Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Possessor of abundance, he said: Possessor of plenty and wealth. At-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement: Forgiver of sin in the verse, he said: Forgiver of sin for the one who says there is no god but God. Acceptor of repentance for the one who says there is no god but God. Severe in penalty for the one who does not say there is no god but God. Possessor of bounty for the one who is rich. There is no god but Him the infidels of Quraysh did not believe in His Oneness, so He believed in Himself. To Him is the destination for the one who says there is no god but God, which will admit him to Paradise, and the destination for the one who does not say there is no god but God, which will admit him to Hell. Abd bin Humaid narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Disputing about the Qur’an is disbelief. Abd bin Humaid and Abu Dawud narrated on his authority that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Disputing about the Qur’an is disbelief.
40:10: When God, the Almighty, mentioned the state of the people of the Fire, and that the word of punishment has come true upon them, and that they are the people of the Fire, He mentioned their state after entering the Fire, saying: 10- Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: When they saw their deeds and looked into their record and were admitted to the Fire and hated themselves for their evil deeds, a caller called out to them when they witnessed God’s punishment: God’s hatred for you in this world when you were called to faith but you disbelieved is greater than your hatred of yourselves today. Al-Akhfash said: This lam in lamqat is the lam of initiation that came after they will be called out because its meaning is it will be said to them, and the call is a statement. Al-Kalbi said: Every person from the people of the Fire will say to himself: Your hatred, O soul, so the angels will say to them while they are in the Fire: God’s hatred for you in this world is more intense than your hatred of yourselves today. Al-Hasan said: They will be given their book, and when they look at their sins, they will hate themselves. Then they will call out: God’s hatred for you in this world when you were called to faith is greater than your hatred for yourselves when you saw the Fire. The adverbial phrase when you were called is in the accusative case due to an implied omitted word indicated by the mentioned word: that is, your hatred at the time of your call. It was also said that it was due to an omitted word, which is remember, and it was also said that it was due to the mentioned hatred, and hatred is the most intense hatred.
40:12: Then God Almighty responded to their statement by saying: 12- That is because when God alone is called upon, you disbelieve meaning that which you are in of torment because if God alone is called upon in this world without anyone else, you disbelieve in Him and abandon His Oneness and if others are associated with Him from idols or other you believe in associating others with Him and respond to the one who calls to Him. So God Almighty explained to them the reason that prompted them not to respond to their exit from the Fire, which is what they were in of abandoning the Oneness of God and associating others with Him in the worship whose head is supplication, and the place of that torment that you are in for that reason. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: so respond that there is no way to respond, and that is because when God is called upon, etc. The judgment is God’s alone without anyone else, and He is the one who ruled that you will remain in the Fire forever and not exit from it. The Most High is the one who is far above having a likeness in His essence or attributes, and The Great is the one who is too great to have a likeness or a companion or Son or partner.
40:13: 13- It is He who shows you His signs meaning the proofs of His Oneness and the signs of His power and sends down for you provision from the sky meaning rain, for it is the cause of provisions. God, the Almighty, combined the manifestation of signs with the sending down of provisions, because the religions are founded on the manifestation of signs, and the bodies are founded on provisions. These are the signs of creation that God, the Almighty, has placed in His heavens and earth and whatever is in them and between them. The majority of scholars read yanzil with a shaddah. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a khafdah, and none will remember except he who turns back meaning none will remember and be admonished by those dazzling signs, and use them as evidence for the Oneness of God and the truth of the promise and threat, except he who turns back: meaning none will return to obedience to God through what he benefits from contemplating God’s signs.
40:14: Then when He, the Most High, mentioned the evidence He had established for monotheism, He commanded His servants to call upon Him and to dedicate their religion to Him, saying: 14- So call upon God, making your religion sincere to Him. That is, if the matter is as He mentioned, then call upon God alone, devoting to Him the worship that He has commanded you, even though the disbelievers hate it. So do not pay attention to their hatred, and let them die in their rage and perish in their regret.
40:15: 15- Exalted in degrees and the elevation of the Exalted in degrees as another predicate of the subject that preceded it: meaning He is the One who shows you His signs, and He is Exalted in degrees. Likewise, Possessor of the Throne is a third predicate. It is possible that Exalted in degrees is the subject, and its predicate is Possessor of the Throne, and it is possible that they are two predicates of a deleted subject, and Exalted is an adjective. The meaning is Exalted in attributes, or Exalted in degrees of His angels: meaning their ascensions, or Exalted in degrees of His prophets and saints in Paradise. Al-Kalbi and Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: He is the Exalted of the seven heavens. According to this meaning, exalted means raiser. The meaning of the Possessor of the Throne is its Owner, Creator, and Controller. This necessitates the exaltation of His status and the greatness of His power. Whoever is thus is the One to whom worship is due and to whom sincerity is due. The phrase He casts the Spirit by His command is in the nominative case as another predicate of the subject that precedes it or the implied one. The meaning of that is that He, glory be to Him, casts the revelation upon whomever He wills of His servants. The revelation is called a spirit because people are revived by it from the death of disbelief, just as bodies are revived by spirits. His statement, by His command is connected to He casts, and from is for the beginning of the goal. It is possible for it to be connected to something omitted as a state of the spirit. An example of this verse is the statement of God Almighty: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit by Our command. It was said that the spirit is Gabriel, as in His statement: The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, and His statement: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth, and His statement: upon whomever He wills of His servants are the prophets. The meaning of from whomever He wills is… His command from His judgment to warn of the Day of Meeting. The majority of scholars read linadhir as the active voice and the accusative of yawm." The subject is God, the Exalted, or the Messenger, or whomever He wills, and the one being warned is omitted, meaning: to warn of the punishment on the Day of Meeting. Abi and a group read it likewise, except that he raised "yawm" as the active voice, metaphorically. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Ibn Al-Sameefa' read "linadhir" as the superlative voice, with the subject being the pronoun for the second person, which is the Messenger, or a pronoun referring to the soul because it is permissible to feminize it. Al-Yamani read "linadhir as the passive voice, raising yawm" as a deputy. The meaning of "the Day of Meeting" is the day when the people of the heavens and the earth meet at the gathering place, and Qatada said the same. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Muqatil said: The day the worshippers and the worshipped will meet, and it was said the oppressor and the oppressed, and it was said the first and the last, and it was said the reward of deeds and the workers.
40:16: And His statement: 16- The Day they will emerge instead of the Day of Meeting. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is in the accusative case due to His statement: Nothing is hidden from God. It was also said that it is in the accusative case due to the implication of remember, but the first is more appropriate. The meaning of emergent is: coming out of their graves, nothing covering them. The phrase nothing of them is hidden from God is a new sentence explaining their emergence. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun of emergent, and it is permissible for it to be a second predicate for the subject: meaning, nothing of them or of the deeds they did in this world is hidden from Him, glory be to Him. The phrase To whom belongs the kingdom today is a new sentence answering an implied question, as if it was said: So what is said about the emergence of the creation on that day? So it was said: To whom is the kingdom today? The commentators said: When everyone in the heavens and the earth perishes, the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, will say: Whose is the kingdom today? meaning the Day of Resurrection, and no one will answer Him, so He will answer Himself. And the statement, To God, the One, the Prevailing, Al-Hasan said: He is the questioner, the Exalted, and He is the One who answers when no one answers Him, so He answers Himself. And it was said that He, Glory be to Him, will command a crier to call out with that, and the people of the gathering, their believers and disbelievers, will say, To God, the One, the Prevailing. And it was said that the people of Paradise will answer the crier with this answer, not the people of Hell. And it was said that it is a narration of what the tongue of the state will utter on that day, when the claims of the falsifiers will be cut off, as in the words of God, the Exalted: “And what will make you know what is the Day of Recompense? * Then what will make you know what is the Day of Recompense? * The Day when no soul will possess anything for another, and the command that Day will be God’s.”
40:17: And His saying: 17- “This day every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed, God is swift in account.” This is a complete answer to the view that the Responder is God, the Exalted. As for the view that the Responder is all or some of the servants, it is a new chapter to explain what God, the Exalted, says after their answer: That is, today every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned of good and evil. There is no injustice today upon any of them by reducing their reward or increasing their punishment. Indeed, God is swift in account. That is, He is swift in account because He, the Exalted, does not need to think about that as others do, because His knowledge encompasses everything, and not even the weight of an atom escapes Him.
40:18: Then God Almighty commanded His Messenger to warn His servants, saying 18- And warn them of the approaching Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection. It was named thus because of its nearness. It is said that someone has approached, meaning he is close, approaching, and from this is Al-Nabigha: The departure has come, but our passengers are still with us, as if they had already left. And from this is the saying of God the Most High: The approaching hour has drawn near meaning the hour has drawn near. It was said that the approaching day is the day of the presence of death, but the former is more appropriate. Al-Zajjaj said: It was called approaching because it is near even if people consider it unlikely, and what is to come is near. When the hearts will be at the throats, stifling that is because they move from their places out of fear until they reach the throat, as in His statement: And the hearts will reach the throats "suppressing" is sorrowful, distressed, and filled with grief. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is when people's hearts are at the throats in a state of stifling. Qatadah said: Their hearts fell into the throats out of fear, so they do not leave or return to their places. It was said that it is describing the end of panic, and he said "suppressing" in consideration of the people of hearts, because the meaning is: when people's hearts are at their throats, so it is a state of them. It was said that it is a state of the hearts, and the plural of state from it is the plural of rational beings because it is attributed to it what is attributed to rational beings, so it was pluralized in its plural. Then the Almighty made clear that no one will benefit the disbelievers on that Day, saying: The wrongdoers will have no close friend meaning no relative who will benefit them, nor an intercessor whose intercession is obeyed in his intercession for them. The place of whom one obeys is the accusative as an attribute of intercessor.
40:19: Then God, the Almighty, described the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of everything, even if it is extremely hidden, saying: 19- He knows the deceitful eyes, which is a stealthy glance at what is not permissible to look at. The sentence is another predicate of His statement, It is He who shows you. Al-Mu’arraj said: There is an inversion of the treachery of the eyes. Qatada said: The deceitful eyes is the pronoun ayn in what God does not like. Ad-Dahhak said: It is a person saying I did not see when he has seen, and I saw when he did not see. Sufyan said: It is a glance after a glance. The first is more appropriate, and Mujahid said the same, and what the hearts conceal of the pronouns and what they conceal of the sins of God.
40:20: 20- And God judges with truth, so He rewards everyone according to what he deserves of good and evil. And those whom you invoke besides Him, that is, whom you worship besides God, do not judge at all, because they do not know anything and are not able to do anything. The majority read they invoke with a d under the letter, meaning the wrongdoers. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this reading. Nafi’, Shaibah, and Hisham read it with a d over the letter, addressing them. Indeed, God is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, so nothing of what is heard or seen is hidden from Him. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding the statement of God, We caused you to die twice and We gave you life twice, that he said: It is like the statement in Al-Baqarah, You were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die, then He will give you life. They were dead in the loins of their fathers, then He brought them forth and gave them life, then He caused them to die, then He will give them life after death. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: You were dust before He created you, so this is death. Then He gave you life and created you, so this is life. Then He will cause you to die and you will return to the graves, so this is another death. Then He will raise you on the Day of Resurrection, so this is life. So they are two deaths and two lives, like His statement, How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life? Al-Baqarah 2:27. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, The Day of Meeting, that he said: On the Day of Resurrection, Adam and the last of his children will meet. It was also narrated from him that he said: The Day of Meeting is the approaching day, and similar names for the Day of Resurrection. May God magnify it and warn His servants about it. Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa’id az-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Abu Nu’aym in al-Hilyah also narrated from him that he said: “At the time of the Hour, a caller will call out: ‘O people, the Hour has come to you.’ The living and the dead will hear it, and God will descend to the lowest heaven and say: ‘To whom belongs dominion today? To God, the One, the Prevailing.’” Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in al-Ba’th and al-Daylami narrated a similar hadith from Abu Sa’d from the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Abd bin Hamid narrated from Ibn Mas’ud that he said: “God will gather all creation on the Day of Resurrection on a single plain, on a white land like a silver ingot in which God has never been disobeyed. The first thing that will be spoken will be a caller calling out: ‘To whom belongs dominion today? To God, the One, the Prevailing.’ ‘Today every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. There will be no injustice today. Indeed, God is swift in account.’ The first of the disputes that He will initiate will be bloodshed.” Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: {He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal}, he said: A man is among people and a woman passes by them, so he shows them that he lowers his gaze from her, but if they are not paying attention, he glances at her, and if they look, he lowers his gaze from her, and God has seen in his heart that he wishes to look at her private parts. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`b narrated on his authority regarding the verse: If he looks at her, does he intend to betray her or not? And what the breasts conceal He said: If He has power over her, will he commit adultery with her or not? Shall I not tell you of what follows it? And God judges with truth He is able to reward good with good and bad with bad. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa’d who said: “On the day of the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave security to the people except for four men and two women. He said: ‘Kill them even if you find them clinging to the curtains of the Ka’bah.’ Among them was ‘Abdullah ibn Sa’d ibn Abi Sarh. He hid with ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called the people to pledge allegiance, he brought him and said: ‘O Messenger of God, pledge allegiance to Abdullah.’ He raised his head and looked at him three times, each time refusing to pledge allegiance. Then he turned to his companions and said: ‘Was there not a wise man among you who would say to this man when he saw me refraining from pledging allegiance to him and kill him?’ They said: ‘O Messenger of God, what was in your mind? Why didn’t you signal to us with your eye?’ He said: ‘It is not appropriate for a prophet to have treacherous eyes.’”
40:21: When He, the Almighty, frightened them with the conditions of the Hereafter, He followed it up with a statement of frightening them with the conditions of this world, saying: 21- Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? He, the Almighty, guided them to consider others, for those who disbelieved from among the disbelievers who passed away were stronger than them in strength than these disbelievers who are present and stronger and left traces in the land with what they built in it of fortresses and palaces and with what they had of numbers and equipment, so when they denied their messengers, God destroyed them. His statement, so they may observe is either in the subjunctive mood in apposition to travel, or in the accusative case in response to the question. His statement, were stronger than them in strength is a statement of the difference between the state of these and those, and His statement, and traces is in apposition to strength. The majority read more severe than them, while Ibn Amir read more severe than you with the shifting of emphasis. So God seized them for their sins, meaning because of their sins. And they had no protector from God, meaning no one to protect them from the punishment. The interpretation of this verse has been mentioned in other places.
40:22: And the reference in His saying: 22- That is to what came before about taking because their messengers came to them with clear proofs meaning with clear arguments but they disbelieved in what they brought them “so God seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful” He does everything He wants, nothing is beyond His power Severe in penalty for whoever disobeys Him and does not return to Him.
40:23: Then the Almighty mentioned the story of Moses and Pharaoh so that they might take heed, saying: 23- And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs meaning the nine signs that were mentioned earlier in more than one place and a clear authority meaning a clear and evident argument, which is the Torah.
40:24: 24- To Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah, and they said, ‘He is a lying magician,’ meaning regarding what he brought. He mentioned them specifically because they were the leaders of those who denied Moses, so Pharaoh was the king, Haman was the minister, and Korah was the owner of the money and treasures.
40:25: 25- So when he brought them the truth from Us, which are his clear and evident miracles, they said, ‘Kill the sons of those who believed with him and keep their women alive.’ Qatada said: This is a killing other than the first killing, because Pharaoh had refrained from killing children at the time of Moses’ birth, but when God sent Moses, he renewed the killing of the Children of Israel, ordering the killing of the males and leaving the women. Similar to this is Pharaoh’s saying, We will kill their sons and keep their women alive. “And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error,” meaning in loss and disaster, because it goes in vain and what God Almighty wants befalls them.
40:26: 26- And Pharaoh said, 'Let me kill Moses.' He only said this because there were those among his elite who prevented him from killing Moses, fearing that punishment would befall them. The meaning is: Leave me to kill him. And let him call upon his Lord, whom he claims sent him to us, to prevent him from being killed if he is able to do so. That is, do not be alarmed by that, for he has no true Lord. Rather, I am your Supreme Lord. Then he mentioned the reason why he wanted to kill him, saying: I fear that he will change your religion, which you are following, which is the worship of other than God, and bring them into his religion, which is the worship of God alone. Or that corruption will appear on earth. That is, that he will cause discord and strife among the people. The accursed one made the appearance of what Moses called to, its spread on earth, and people being guided by it, corruption. Corruption is nothing but what he himself, who followed him, is doing. The Kufians and Ya'qub read or that it will appear with the or for ambiguity. The meaning is that one of the two things must occur. The rest read and it appears without an alif, meaning that both things happen. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read it with a fatha on the ya’ of inni akhaf. Nafi’, Abu Amr, and Hafs read it with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the ha’ from adhar, and its subject is the pronoun Musa, and corruption is in the accusative case as a direct object. The rest read it with a fatha on the ya’ and the ha’, and corruption is in the nominative case as the subject.
40:27: 27- And Moses said, ‘Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account.’ Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read I have sought refuge with the assimilation of the dhal, while the rest read it with the idhhar. When Pharaoh threatened him with death, he sought refuge in God Almighty from every one who is too arrogant to believe in God and does not believe in the Resurrection and the Hereafter. Pharaoh is included in this generality primarily.
40:28: 28- And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said. Al-Hasan, Muqatil, and As-Suddi said: He was a Copt and a cousin of Pharaoh, and he was the one who escaped with Moses, and he is the one meant by His statement: And a man came running from the farthest part of the city and said, ‘O Moses!’ (Al-Baqarah 2:17). It was also said that he was from the Children of Israel and not from the family of Pharaoh, which is contrary to what is in the verse. This was made possible by the fact that there is an inversion in the verse, and the meaning is: And a believing man from the Children of Israel, who concealed his faith from the family of Pharaoh, said. Al-Qushayri said: Whoever considers him to be an Israelite, then there is a deviation in that, because it is said that he concealed such and such a matter, but it is not said that he concealed it from him, as God, the Most High, said: And they do not conceal from God a statement. Also, Pharaoh would not have tolerated such a statement from the Children of Israel. There is a difference of opinion about the name of this man. Some say Habib, some say Ezekiel, and others say something else. The majority read rajul with a damma on the jim, while Al-A’mash and Abd Al-Warith read it with a sukoon on it, and it is the language of Tamim and Najd. The first is the eloquent one. It was read with a kasra on the jim, and mu’min is an attribute of a man, and min ahl Pharaoh is another attribute, and ya takhtis conceals his faith is a third attribute. The interrogative in Do you kill a man is for denial, and that he says, ‘My Lord is God’ is in the accusative case with the preposition removed: that is, because he says or he dislikes saying it. The phrase and he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord is in the accusative case as a state: that is, while the situation is that he has come to you with clear miracles and apparent evidence of his prophethood and the truth of his message, then he was gentle with them in defending him by saying: And if he is a liar, upon him is his lie, but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you. His statement was not due to doubt on his part, for he was a believer as God described him, and a believer does not doubt. The meaning of Some of what He promises you will befall you means that if it does not all of it befall you, then at least some of it will befall you. The nun was omitted from yakan in both places to make it easier due to frequent use, as Sibawayh said. Abu Ubaidah and Abu al-Haytham said: some here means all of it, meaning that all of what He promises you will befall you. Abu Ubaidah recited on this the saying of Labid: There are places where if I do not like them or some souls are attached to their bathroom That is, all souls. This was objected to, and it was answered that some may be used in the Arabic language to mean all, as in the poet’s saying: The patient may realize some of his need, while the hasty may make mistakes. And the other said: If things are managed by the youth rather than the elders, you will see some flaws in some of them. There is nothing in the two couplets that indicates what they claimed. As for the couplet of Labid, it was said that by some souls he meant himself, and there is no necessity that compels us to interpret what is in the verse in that way, because he wanted to be condescending with them and make them think that he did not believe in the truth of his prophethood, as is indicated by his saying: He conceals his faith. The people of meaning said: This is based on the demonstration of Al-Hajjaj, as if he said to them: The least that can happen in his truthfulness is that some of what he promises you will befall you, and in some of that your destruction, so it is as if what is obtained by some is what is obtained by all. Al-Layth said: “Some here is a connection, meaning: what he promises you will befall you. It was said that this torment that he says will befall you in this world, and it is some of what he threatens you with of torment. It was said that he promised them reward and punishment, so if they disbelieved, the punishment will befall them, and it is some of what he promised them. “Indeed, God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.” This is from the completion of the words of the believing man, and it is another argument with two aspects: One of them is that if he were a transgressor and a liar, God would not have guided him to clear proofs nor supported him with miracles. The second is that if he was like that. May God let him down and destroy him, so you have no need to kill him. He is a profligate who persists in sins and does a lot of them, and a lying slanderer.
40:29: 29- O my people, yours is the kingdom this Day, dominant in the land. That believing man reminded them of their kingdom so that they would thank God and not persist in their disbelief. The meaning of dominant is: dominance over people, victory over them, and superiority over them. The land is the land of Egypt. The accusative of dominant is in the state of so who will protect us from the wrath of God if it comes to us? That is, who will prevent us from His punishment and stand between us and Him when He comes? This is a warning from Him to them of God’s vengeance upon them and the infliction of His punishment upon them. When Pharaoh heard what this man said of sound advice, he came up with a deception to make his people think that he had a firm place of advice and care for them, and that he would only treat them in a way that would bring them benefit and ward off harm. For this reason, he said: I only show you what I see. Ibn Zayd said: That is, I only advise you with what I see for myself. Ad-Dahhak said: I teach you nothing but what I know. The seeing here is the seeing of the heart, not the sight. The second object is except what I see. "And I guide you only to the path of right guidance." That is, I guide you with this opinion only to the path of truth. The majority of scholars read "ar-rashad with a soft sh on the letter shin. Muadh ibn Jabal read it with a shaddah on it, as it is an exaggerated form like darrab." An-Nahhas said: "It is a mistake, but there is no basis for it." Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh said, that he said: There was no believer from the family of Pharaoh other than him, the wife of Pharaoh, and the believer who warned Moses, who said, The eminent ones are plotting against you to kill you. Ibn al-Mundhir said: I was told that his name was Ezekiel. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: His name was Habib. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Urwah, who said: It was said to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, “Tell us about the worst thing the polytheists did to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” He said: While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was praying in the courtyard of the Kaaba, Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt came, seized the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) by the shoulder, twisted his garment around his neck, and strangled him violently. Abu Bakr came, seized his shoulders, and pushed him away from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and then said: Do you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God,’ while he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord? Abu Nu`aym narrated in Fadhail al-Sahaba and al-Bazzar on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: O people, tell me who is the bravest of people? They said: You. He said: I have never fought anyone without taking my revenge on him, but tell me who is the bravest of people? They said: We do not know, so who? Abu Bakr said: I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Quraysh seized him. One of them was avoiding him and another was throwing himself at him, and they were saying: You are the one who made the gods into one god. By God, no one approached us except Abu Bakr. He was hitting this one, and another was coming, and another was throwing himself at him, and he was saying: Woe to you! Do you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God?’ Then he raised his cloak and wept until his beard was wet, then he said: Who is the toughest of you, is the believer from the family of Pharaoh better or Abu Bakr? The people were silent. He said: Will you not answer? By God, an hour with Abu Bakr is better than a believer from the family of Pharaoh. That one was a man who concealed his faith and that one was a man who declared his faith.
40:30: Then that believing man repeated his reminder to them, and warned them that what happened to those before them would happen to them, so God said, narrating from him: 30- And the one who believed said, ‘O my people, indeed I fear for you something like the Day of the Confederates.’ That is, something like the day of the punishment of the past nations who formed parties against their prophets. He used the singular form of day because the plural of confederates is sufficient to suffice with the plural of confederates.
40:31: Then he explained the confederates and said: 31- Like the way of the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and those after them meaning like their condition in the punishment, or like their habit of continuing to deny, or like the punishment for what they were upon of disbelief and denial And God does not intend injustice for the servants meaning He does not punish them without sin, and negating the intention to be unjust necessitates negating injustice by the implication of the address.
40:32: Then he increased the preaching and reminding, saying: 32- "And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling. The majority of scholars read tanad" by softening the dal and deleting the ya'. The original form is "tanadi, which is the reflexive verb from nada". It is said "tanada al-qawm" meaning they called out to one another. Al-Hasan, Ibn al-Samee', Ya'qub, Ibn Kathir, and Mujahid read it by keeping the ya' as per the original form. Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Ikrimah read it by doubling the dal. Some linguists said that it is a mistake, because it is from "nada yanda" meaning to run away. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake, and the reading is good due to the meaning of "tanafani". Ad-Dahhak said: Its meaning is that when they hear the roar of Hell, they will call out in flight, and they will not come to any part of the earth except that they will find rows of angels, so they will return to the place they were in. This is what He said: The Day of Calling. According to the reading of the majority, the meaning is: The day when some of them will call out to others, or the people of Hell will call out to the people of Paradise and the people of Paradise will call out to the people of Hell, or the happiness of the happy will be called out and the misery of the miserable will be called out, or the day when every people will call out to their leader. There is nothing to prevent it from being interpreted in all of these meanings.
40:33: And His statement: 33- The Day you turn back in flight is a substitute for the Day of Calling: meaning turning away from the situation to the Fire, or fleeing from it. Qatada and Muqatil said: The meaning is to the Fire after the reckoning, and the phrase you have no protector from God is in the accusative case as a state: meaning you have no one to protect you from God's punishment and prevent you from it. And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide to guide him to the path of righteousness.
40:34: Then he increased his admonition and reminder to them, saying: 34- And indeed, Joseph had come to you before with clear proofs, meaning Joseph, son of Jacob. The meaning is that Joseph, son of Jacob, came to them with clear miracles and signs before Moses came to them: that is, he came to your fathers, so he made the coming to the fathers a coming to the sons. It was said that what is meant by Joseph here is Joseph, son of Ephraim, son of Joseph, son of Jacob, and he had stayed among them as a prophet for twenty years. Al-Naqqash narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak that God sent to them a messenger from the jinn called Joseph, but the first is more appropriate. It has been said that the Pharaoh of Moses lived during the days of Joseph, son of Jacob, because of his long life. And you did not cease to be in doubt about what he brought you of clear proofs and you did not believe in him until when he died Joseph you said, ‘God will never send after him a messenger’ So they disbelieved in him during his life and disbelieved in the messengers who came after him after his death. Thus does God send astray he who is a transgressor and doubter meaning, like this clear misguidance, God sends astray he who is a transgressor and a great deal of sinner, doubting God’s religion and doubting His Oneness, His promise and His threat.
40:35: The relative pronoun in His statement: 35- Those who dispute concerning the verses of God is a substitute for whom and the plural is in consideration of its meaning, or an explanation of it, or an attribute, or in the accusative case with the omitted I mean, or the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, they are the ones, or a subject and its predicate are printed without authority related to they dispute: that is, they dispute concerning the verses of God without a clear argument, and came to them is an attribute of authority great hatred in the sight of God and in the sight of those who believe it is possible that it is intended to express amazement, or that it is intended to express blame like bad, and the subject of great is a pronoun that refers back to the argument understood from they dispute, and it was said that its subject is a pronoun that refers back to whom in whom is extravagant, and the first is more appropriate. His saying: with God is connected to arrogance, and likewise with those who believe it was said that this is from the words of the believing man, and it was said that it is the beginning of a speech from God the Most High, Thus does God set a seal upon every arrogant, tyrannical heart meaning just as He set a seal upon the hearts of these disputants, so He sets a seal upon every arrogant, tyrannical heart. The majority of scholars read it by adding heart to arrogant, so the second part was deleted because the first part indicates it, and the meaning is that He the Most High sets a seal upon the hearts of all the arrogant, tyrants. Abu Amr, Ibn Muhaysin, and Ibn Dhakwan, from the people of Ash-Sham, read it with the tanween on heart on the basis that arrogant is an attribute of it, so the heart is meant by it in the whole, because the heart is the seat of arrogance and the rest of the organs follow it in that. Ibn Masoud read it on the heart of every arrogant person.
40:36: Then when Pharaoh heard this, he returned to his arrogance and haughtiness, turning away from the sermon and averse to accepting it. He said, O Haman, build me a tower, meaning a lofty castle, as explained above, that I may reach the paths, meaning the roads. Qatada, Al-Zuhri, Al-Suddi, and Al-Akhfash said: They are the doors.
40:37: And his saying: 37- The causes of the heavens is an explanation of the causes, because if something is made vague and then explained, it is more effective in people’s hearts. Al-Akhfash recited, when explaining the verse, the verse of Zuhair: Whoever fears the causes of death will be overtaken by it, even if he seeks the causes of heaven with a ladder. It was said that the causes of the heavens are the matters to which one clings. So I looked up to the God of Moses. The majority of scholars read it in the nominative case, in apposition to abgh, and on this basis it falls within the scope of hope. Al-A’raj, Al-Sammali, Isa bin Omar, and Hafs read it in the accusative case, in response to the command in His statement, Build for me, or in response to hope, as Abu Ubaidah and others said. Al-Nahhas said: The meaning of the accusative case is different from the meaning of the nominative case, because the meaning of the accusative case is: When I reach the causes, I looked up, and the meaning of the nominative case is: Perhaps I will reach the causes, and perhaps I will look up after that. This is evidence that Pharaoh was in a state of great ignorance, and at a very low level of understanding the true nature of things. And indeed, I think he is a liar, meaning, I think Moses was a liar in his claim that he had a god, or in what he claimed of being a messenger. And thus was made fair-seeming to Pharaoh his evil deeds, meaning, and similar to this beautification, Satan made fair-seeming to Pharaoh his evil deeds of polytheism and denial, so he persisted in error and continued in his transgression. And he was turned away from the path, meaning the path of right guidance. The majority read wasd with a fatha on the sad and the dal: meaning Pharaoh turned people away from the path. The Kufians read wasd with a damma on the sad, in the passive form. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this reading, and perhaps the reason for choosing it from them is that it is consistent with what they agreed upon in zayna in the passive form. Yahya ibn Waththab and Alqamah read sad with a kasra on the sad. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra read it with a fatha on the sad and a damma on the dal, with a tanween, as a verbal noun in apposition to his evil deeds: meaning Satan made his evil deeds and turning people away seem attractive to him. And the plot of Pharaoh was only in ruin. Ruin: loss and destruction. From this comes Perish the hands of Abu Lahab.
40:38: Then that believing man repeated the reminder and warning as God narrated about him in His saying: 38- And he who believed said, ‘O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the path of right conduct.’ That is, follow my example in religion and I will guide you to the path of right conduct, which is Paradise. It was also said that this was from the saying of Moses, but the first is more appropriate. Muadh bin Jabal read ar-rashad with a shaddah on the shin as mentioned earlier in the saying of Pharaoh. It appears in the Mushaf as ‘follow’ without a ya’. Likewise, Abu ‘Amr and Nafi’ read it by deleting it when stopping and keeping it in the original. Ya’qub and Ibn Kathir read it by keeping it in both connected and stopped, and the rest read it by deleting it when connected and stopped. Those who kept it did so as is the original, and those who deleted it did so because it was deleted in the Mushaf.
40:39: 39- O my people, this worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment which is enjoyed for a few days, then it ends and disappears. And indeed, the Hereafter is the home of settlement meaning stability, because it is permanent and does not end and is continuous and does not disappear.
40:40: 40- Whoever does evil will not be recompensed except with the like thereof. That is, whoever commits a sin in this world, will not be recompensed except with the like thereof and will not be punished except in proportion to it. The apparent meaning of this verse is that it includes everything that is called evil. It was said that it is specific to polytheism, but there is no basis for that. And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer. That is, whoever does a righteous deed while believing in God and what His Messengers brought, they - those who combine righteous deeds with faith will enter Paradise and will be provided for therein without account." That is, without measure or accountability. Muqatil said: He is saying that they will not be held accountable for what they are given in Paradise of good. It was said that righteous deeds are "there is no god but God. The majority of scholars read they enter" with a fat-ha on the first letter, in the active form. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Abu Amr, Ya'qub, and Abu Bakr, from Asim, read it with a damma on the second letter, in the passive form. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, Like a habit, he said: Like a state. Abd al-Razzaq and Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Qatadah, Like the habit of the people of Noah, he said: They are the Confederates: the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Jurayj, regarding the verse, And Joseph had already come to you before with clear proofs, he said: The vision of Joseph. Regarding the verse, Those who dispute concerning the verses of God, he said: The Jews. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, Except in ruin, he said: Loss. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar from Mujahid. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, This worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment, he said: This world is a gathering of the gatherings of the Hereafter, seven thousand years. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The life of this world is a temporary enjoyment, and there is nothing better than a righteous woman, whom you look at and she pleases you, and if you are away from her, she protects you with regard to herself and her wealth.”
40:41: That believing man repeated their call to God and declared his faith, and did not follow the previous paths of making them think that he was one of them, and that he was only reminding them out of aversion that some of what Moses had threatened them with would happen to them, as a man who loves his people would say in warning against falling into what he fears they would fall into, so he said: 41- And O my people, why do I call you to salvation and you call me to the Fire? That is, tell me about you, how is this situation: I call you to salvation from the Fire and entering Paradise by believing in God and responding to His messengers, and you call me to the Fire with what you want from me of polytheism. It was said that the meaning of Why do I call you is Why do I call you? Just as you say: Why do I see you sad? That is, what is wrong with you?
40:42: Then he explained the two calls, saying: 42- You call me to disbelieve in God and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge. So his saying you call me is a substitute for the first you call me or a clarification to them that of which I have no knowledge meaning that I have no knowledge of him being a partner to God. And I call you to the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving meaning to the Exalted in Might in His vengeance on whoever disbelieves in the Forgiving for the sin of whoever believes in Him.
40:43: 43- "La Jarm" The explanation of this has already been mentioned in Surah Hud. Jarm is a past tense verb meaning right, and the "la" that comes before it negates what they claim and rejects what they alleged. The subject of this verb is His statement: "That to which you call me has no claim in this world or in the Hereafter" meaning right and his claim must be invalidated. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that no beneficial call will be answered. It was also said that he has no claim that would make him divinity in this world or in the Hereafter. Al-Kalbi said: He has no intercession. "And that our return is to God" meaning our return and destination is to Him through death first and resurrection at the end, so each person will be rewarded according to what he deserves of good and evil. "And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire" meaning those who commit many sins against God. Qatadah and Ibn Sirin said: It means the polytheists. Mujahid and Ash-Sha'bi said: They are the fools who shed blood unjustly. Ikrimah said: The tyrants and the arrogant.
