It was said that they are those who transgressed the limits of God, and that in both places there is an apposition to that in His statement: that you only call me to it, and the meaning is: It is true that we will return to God, and it is true that the transgressors, etc.
40:44: 44- Then you will remember what I say to you if the punishment descends upon you, and you know that I have gone to great lengths in advising you and reminding you. This vagueness contains intimidation and threats that are not hidden. And I entrust my affair to God meaning I put my trust in Him and submit my affair to Him. It was said that he said this when they wanted to trap him. Muqatil said: This believer fled to the mountain and they could not catch him. It was also said that the one who said it was Moses, but the first is more appropriate.
40:45: 45- So God saved him from the evil of their plotting. That is, God saved him from the evil plotting they intended to do to him, and the evil they intended for him. Qatada said: God saved him along with the Children of Israel. And the evil of the punishment encompassed Pharaoh's people. That is, it surrounded them and the evil of the punishment descended upon them. Al-Kisa'i said: It is said haqqa yahiq hayqan it descended and stuck: meaning it descended and stuck. Al-Kalbi said: They scooped up the sea and were thrown into the fire. What is meant by the people of Pharaoh is Pharaoh and his people. It was not stated explicitly because mentioning them does not mean mentioning him, as he is more deserving of that than them. Or what is meant by the people of Pharaoh is Pharaoh himself. The first is more deserving because they were all tormented in this world by drowning, and they will be tormented in the Hereafter by the Fire.
40:47: 47- And when they dispute in the Fire The adverbial phrase is in the accusative case because of the verb remember. The meaning is: Remind your people of the time of their dispute in the Fire. Then the Almighty explained this dispute, saying: Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant about submitting to the prophets and following them, and they are the leaders of disbelief, Indeed, we were your followers The plural of follower, like servant and servant, or a verbal noun in the position of an active participle: i.e. followers, or with the deletion of an added noun: i.e. those with followers. The Basrans said: Followers can be singular or plural. The Kufians said that it is a plural with no singular. So can you relieve us of a portion of the Fire? i.e., can you repel a portion of it from us or carry it with us? The accusative case of nassib is an implied verb indicated by maghnun: i.e., can you repel a portion from us or prevent it, implying that it includes the meaning of carriers: i.e., can you carry a portion with us? Or with the verbal noun.
40:48: 48- Those who were arrogant said, ‘Indeed, we are all in it.’ This sentence is a new answer to an implied question, and the meaning is: We and you are both in Hell, so how can we avail you? The majority of scholars read all in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is in it, and the sentence is the predicate of in, as Al-Akhfash said. Ibn As-Samee’ and Isa bin Omar read all in the accusative case. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said that it is to emphasize the noun in in the sense of all of us, and its tanween replaces the complement. It was also said that it is in the state, and Ibn Malik preferred this. Indeed, God has judged between the servants, meaning that He ruled that a group will be in Paradise and a group will be in the Blaze.
40:49: 49- And those in the Fire will say from the disbelieving nations, the arrogant and the weak among them to the keepers of Hell plural of khazin, who is the one who is responsible for torturing the people of Hell: Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment. “A day” is an adverbial phrase for to lighten, and the object of to lighten is omitted: that is, to lighten for us some of the punishment for the duration of a day or in a day.
40:50: And the sentence 50- They said, ‘Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?’ is a new answer to an implied question, and the question is for rebuke and reprimand. They said, ‘Yes,’ meaning they brought them to us, but we denied them and did not believe in them or in the clear proofs they brought. So when they confessed, They said, meaning the angels who are the guardians of Hell said to them, Then call, meaning if the matter is like this, then call yourselves, for we do not call upon those who disbelieved in God and denied His messengers after they came with clear proofs. Then they informed them that their call is of no benefit, so they said, And the call of the disbelievers is only in error, meaning in loss, invalidity, ruin, and destruction.
40:51: And the sentence 51- Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe is a new sentence from Him, glory be to Him: meaning, We will make them the victors over their enemies who subjugate them. The relative pronoun is in the accusative case in apposition to Our messengers: meaning, We will support Our messengers and those who believed with them in the life of this world with what God has promised them of vengeance against them through killing, plunder, capture, and subjugation. And on the Day when the witnesses will stand which is the Day of Resurrection. Zayd ibn Aslam said: The witnesses are the angels and the prophets. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: The witnesses are the angels who testify for the prophets that they conveyed the message, and against the nations that they denied it. Al-Zajjaj said: The word witnesses is the plural of witness like companion and companions. An-Nahhas said: The root fa’il is not pluralized as af’al nor can it be used as an analogy. Rather, what comes from it is heard and performed according to what is heard, so on this basis it is the plural of shahid, like sharif and ashraaf. The meaning of their victory on the Day when the witnesses stand is that God will reward them for their deeds and admit them into Paradise and honor them with His honors, and He will reward the infidels for their deeds and curse them and admit them into Hell.
40:52: This is the meaning of His statement: 52- The Day when the wrongdoers’ excuses will not benefit them, and for them is the curse meaning far from mercy and for them is the worst home meaning the Fire. The Day is a substitute for The Day when the witnesses will stand. The reason for their excuses not being of any use to them is because they are false excuses, baseless pretexts, and misleading doubts. The majority of scholars read tanfa` with a fathah. Nafi` and the Kufians read it with a tanfa`, and all are permissible in the language. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, regarding his statement: And the transgressors are the companions of the Fire, he said: Those who shed blood unjustly. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening. If he is among the people of Paradise, then he is among the people of Paradise, and if he is among the people of the Fire, then he is among the people of the Fire. It is said to him, ‘This is your seat until God raises you to it on the Day of Resurrection.’” Ibn Mardawayh added. Then he recited: The Fire is shown to them morning and evening. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No one who does good, Muslim or disbeliever, does it without God rewarding him. We said: O Messenger of God, what is the reward of the disbeliever? He said: Wealth, children, health and the like. We said: And what is his reward in the Hereafter? He said: A punishment less severe than this punishment. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: Enter the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever defends the honor of his brother, God will defend his face from the fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar verse from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.
40:53: His statement: 53- And We gave Moses guidance. This is part of what God Almighty related recently regarding His support for His Messengers: that is, We gave him the Torah and prophethood, as in His statement, Almighty: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. Muqatil said: Guidance from misguidance: meaning the Torah.
40:54: 54- And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture, * as a guidance and a reminder for those of understanding. What is meant by the Scripture is the Torah, and the meaning of We caused to inherit is that when God, the Exalted, sent down the Torah to Moses, it remained among them after him and they inherited it from generation to generation. It was said that what is meant by the Scripture is all the books sent down to the prophets of the Children of Israel after the death of Moses. Guidance and Reminder are in the accusative case as objects for which: that is, for the sake of guidance and reminder, or as sources in the place of circumstance, that is, a guide and a reminder. What is meant by those of understanding are the people of sound minds.
40:55: Then God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be patient in the face of harm, saying: 55- “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth.” That is, be patient in the face of the harm of the polytheists, as the messengers before you were patient. Indeed, the promise of God that He promised to His messengers is true, with no breach in it and no doubt in its fulfillment, as in His statement: Indeed, We will support Our messengers. And His statement: “And Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they will be the ones who are aided. And indeed, Our soldiers will be the predominant.” Al-Kalbi said: This was abrogated by the verse of the sword. Then God the Almighty commanded him to seek forgiveness for his sin, saying: And seek forgiveness for your sin. It was said that what is meant is the sin of your nation, so this is with an omitted complement. It was also said that what is meant is minor sins according to those who allow it for the prophets. It was also said that it is merely an act of worship for him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) by seeking forgiveness to increase the reward, and God has forgiven him his past and future sins. And glorify the praises of your Lord in the evening and the morning. That is, continue to glorify God, praising Him. It was also said that what is meant is to pray at the two times, the Asr prayer and the Fajr prayer. This was said by Al-Hasan and Qatadah. It was also said that they are two prayers, two rak’ahs in the morning and two rak’ahs in the evening, and that was before the five daily prayers were made obligatory.
40:56: 56- Indeed, those who dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority that has come to them meaning, without any clear and evident proof that has come to them from God, there is nothing in their breasts except arrogance meaning, there is nothing in their hearts except arrogance towards the truth that drives them to deny you. The phrase they will never attain it is an attribute of arrogance. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except arrogance; they will never attain their desire for it, so he omitted the complement. Another narrator said: They will never attain arrogance. Ibn Qutaybah said: The meaning is, there is nothing in their breasts except arrogance: meaning, arrogance towards Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the desire to defeat him, but they will never attain that. It was said that what is meant by arrogance is the great matter: that is, they seek prophethood, or they seek a great matter by which they can reach you, such as killing and the like, but they do not attain that. Mujahid said: The meaning is, there is greatness in their breasts which they will never attain. What is meant by this verse is the polytheists, and it was said that it refers to the Jews, as will be explained at the end of the research, God willing. Then God Almighty commanded him to seek refuge in God from their evils, saying: So seek refuge in God, for He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. That is, seek refuge in Him from their evil, their plotting, and their aggression against you, for He is the All-Hearing of their words and the All-Seeing of their actions. Nothing of that is hidden from Him.
40:57: Then the Almighty explained His great power, saying: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. That is, greater in people’s hearts and more sublime in their minds, due to the greatness of their bodies and their stability without pillars, and the orbits running with the planets without cause. So how can they deny the resurrection and the revival of what is less than them in every respect, as in His statement: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The meaning is that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Antichrist when the Jews glorified him. Yahya bin Salam said: This is an argument against those who deny the al-Qiyamah 75:that is, they are greater than the re-creation of mankind. But most people do not know about the greatness of God’s power and that nothing is beyond His power.
40:58: Then when He, the Most High, mentioned arguing with falsehood, He mentioned an example of falsehood and truth, and that they are not equal, so He said: And not equal are the blind and the seeing, meaning the one who argues with falsehood and the one who argues with truth. And those who believe and do righteous deeds, nor the evildoer, meaning the one who does good through faith and righteous deeds is not equal to the one who does evil through disbelief and sins. The addition of la in nor the evildoer is for emphasis. Little do you remember. The majority read yattadhakaroon with a sub-dhammah indicating absence, and this reading was chosen by Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim, because before and after it are indicating absence, not address. The Kufians read it with a super-dhammah indicating address, in the manner of turning away: meaning, remembering, little do you remember.
40:59: 59- The Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it meaning there is no doubt about its coming and occurrence but most people do not believe in that and do not believe it because their understanding is limited and their minds are too weak to comprehend the proof. What is meant by most people are the disbelievers who deny the Resurrection.
40:61: Then the Almighty mentioned some of the blessings He bestowed upon His servants, saying: 61- It is God who has made for you the night that you may rest therein from the movements in seeking earnings, because He made it dark and cold, suitable for comfort through stillness and sleep, and the day to see meaning bright so that you may see your needs and manage your livelihoods. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind He bestows upon them His countless blessings, but most people are not grateful for the blessings and do not acknowledge them, either because they are ungrateful for them and disbelieve in them, as is the case with the disbelievers, or because they neglect to consider and ignore what is required of thanking the benefactor, and they are the ignorant.
40:62: 62- “That is God, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no god but Him.” In this, the Almighty made clear the perfection of His power, which necessitates the obligation of His Oneness. The majority read Creator in the nominative case as a predicate after the first predicate of the subject. Zayd ibn Ali read it in the accusative case as a specification. So how are you turned away? That is, how do you turn away from His worship and turn away from His Oneness?
40:63: 63- Thus are those who used to deny the signs of God deluded. That is, just as those who deny the signs of God and reject His Oneness are deluded.
40:64: Then He, the Almighty, mentioned to them another type of His blessings that He bestowed upon them, along with what that contains of evidence of the perfection of His power and His uniqueness in divinity, saying: 64- God is He who made for you the earth a resting place and the heaven a canopy meaning a place of rest in which you live and in which you die. And the heaven a canopy meaning a fixed, standing ceiling. Then He explained some of His blessings related to the souls of His servants, saying: And He formed you and perfected your forms meaning He created you in the best form. Al-Zajjaj said: He created you in the best of all living things. The majority of scholars read Suwarakum with a damma on the sad, while Al-A’mash and Abu Razin read it with a kasra. Al-Jawhari said: Suwar with a kasra on the sad is a language for Suwar with a damma. And He has provided for you of the good things meaning the pleasures. That the one sent with these sublime attributes “is God, your Lord. So blessed be God, Lord of the worlds” meaning the abundance of His goodness and blessings.
40:65: 65- He is the Ever-Living, there is no god but Him meaning the Everlasting, the One who does not perish, the One who is unique in divinity. So call upon Him, devoting to Him your religion meaning obedience and worship. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. Al-Farra’ said: It is a statement that contains an implied command: meaning, praise Him. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated. As-Suyuti said with a saheeh isnad on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah who said: The Jews came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: The Dajjal will be from among us at the end of time, and he will be in charge of his affair. They magnified his affair and said: We will do such and such. Then God revealed: {Indeed, those who dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority that has come to them - there is in their hearts nothing but pride. They will never attain it.} He said: The one who says, Seek refuge in God will not attain it. So He ordered His Prophet to seek refuge from the trial of the Dajjal, because the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of the Dajjal. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar regarding the verse, he said: They are the Jews. It was revealed about them in what they were awaiting regarding the matter of the Dajjal. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding His statement: {There is in their hearts nothing but pride.} He said: The greatness of the Quraysh. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilyah, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Supplication is worship. Then he recited: "And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship' - he said: "of My supplication - will enter Hell in humiliation." Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Khatib narrated on the authority of Al-Bara' that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Supplication is worship. 'Your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'" Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-'Azmah on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the verse: "Call upon Me; I will respond to you," he said: "Seek Me alone; I will forgive you." Al-Hakim narrated - he authenticated it - on the authority of Jarir ibn 'Abdullah, regarding the verse: "Worship Me." Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Supplication is seeking forgiveness. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Hakim and Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever does not supplicate to God, God will be angry with him. Ahmad, Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya’la and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Caution does not benefit against destiny, but supplication benefits against what has happened and what has not happened, so you should supplicate. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawader Al-Usul on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Supplication is the core of worship. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The best form of worship is supplication. He recited: “And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you. ’” (Surah Al-Adab: 10) Al-Bukhari narrated in Al-Adab on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked, Which form of worship is best? He said: A person’s supplication for himself. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever says There is no god but God should immediately say Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. This is what He said: “So call upon Him, devoting your religion to Him alone. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.”
40:66: God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to inform the polytheists that God had forbidden him from worshipping anyone other than Him and had commanded him to believe in the Oneness of God. He said: 66- Say, ‘Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides God,’ meaning idols. Then He explained the reason for the prohibition, saying: When clear proofs came to me from my Lord, meaning rational and transmitted evidence, as they necessitate belief in the Oneness of God. And I was commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds, meaning to surrender to Him in obedience and submission.
40:67: Then he followed this by mentioning evidence of monotheism, saying: It is He who created you from dust, meaning He created your first father, who is Adam, and his creation from dust necessitates the creation of his offspring from him. Then from a sperm-drop, then from a clot. The explanation of this has already been presented in more than one place. Then He brings you forth as a child, meaning children. He made it singular because it is a generic name, or in the sense that each one of you is brought forth as a child. Then that you may reach your full strength, which is the state in which strength and reason are combined. The full explanation of full strength has already been fully explained in Al-An’am. The causal lam in that you may reach the pinnacle of perfection. His statement: Then that you may be elders is conjoined with that you may reach. Nafi’, Hafs, Abu Amr, Ibn Muhaisin, and Hisham read shuyukhan with a damma on the shin, and the rest read it with a kasra. Shaykhan was read in the singular because of his saying child, and a shaykh is someone who has passed forty years. And among you is he who dies before, meaning before old age. And that you may reach… A specified term” meaning the time of death or the Day of Resurrection, and the lam is the lam of consequence. So that you may understand meaning so that you may understand the Oneness of your Lord and His infinite power in creating you in these different stages.
40:68: 68- It is He who gives life and causes death. That is, He has the power to give life and cause death. So when He decrees a matter, of the matters that He wants, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is, without hesitation. This is a representation of the effect of His power on the possible when His will is attached to them. The meaning of this has been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah and what follows it.
40:69: Then God, the Almighty, was amazed at the state of those who dispute about the verses of God, saying: 69- Have you not seen those who dispute about the verses of God? The meaning of dispute has already been explained. How are they turned away? That is, how are they turned away from them, despite the evidence proving their authenticity and that they themselves are a reason for monotheism. Ibn Zayd said: They are the polytheists, as evidenced by His statement: Those who denied the Scripture and that with which We sent Our messengers. Al-Qurtubi said: Most of the commentators said that it was revealed about the Qadarites. Ibn Sirin said: If this verse was not revealed about the Qadarites, then I do not know about whom it was revealed.
40:70: The answer to this is that God Almighty described these people with a description that indicates something other than what they said, so He said: Those who denied the Book, meaning the Qur’an. This is a description that cannot be applied to a sect of Islam. The relative pronoun is either in the genitive case as an adjective to the first relative pronoun, or in place of it, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a censure. What is meant by the Book is either the Qur’an or the generality of books revealed from God. His statement: and what We sent Our messengers with, is conjoined with His statement by the Book, and what is meant by it is what is revealed to the messengers other than a Book, if the lam in the Book is for a generality, or all the books, if what is meant by the Book is the Qur’an. Then they will know the outcome of their matter and the consequences of their disbelief, and in this there is a severe warning.
40:71: The circumstance in His statement: When the shackles are on their necks is related to they will know: meaning, they will know when the shackles will be on their necks. And the chains is conjoined with the shackles, and the interpretation is: When the shackles and chains are on their necks. It is permissible for the chains to be raised as a subject and its predicate omitted because on their necks indicates it. It is permissible for its predicate to be they will be dragged * in the boiling water with the pronoun omitted: meaning, they will be dragged with it in the boiling water. This is according to the reading of the majority with the chains raised. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, Ikrimah, and Abu al-Jawza' read it with the accusative. They read they will be dragged with the fatha on the ya' as an active participle, so the chains will be the advanced object. Some of them read the chains with the genitive. Al-Farra' said: This reading is based on the meaning, as the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and chains. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning according to this reading is: And in chains they are dragged. Ibn al-Anbari objected to him, saying that this is not permissible in Arabic. The place of they are dragged is if the chains are conjoined with the shackles. And if it is assumed to be the subject and its predicate is in their necks, it is the accusative case in the state of circumstance, or it has no place, rather it is a new sentence in response to an implied question.
40:72: And the boiling water is the extreme heat, and it was said that it is pus, and its interpretation was mentioned above. 72- Then into the Fire they will be lit. It is said that you lit the oven, meaning you lit it, and you lit it, meaning you filled it with fuel. And from this comes and the sea is lit, meaning filled. So the meaning is that the Fire will be lit with them, or filled with them. Mujahid and Muqatil said: The Fire will be lit with them, and they will become its fuel.
40:73: 73- And it will be said to them, ‘Where are those you used to worship * besides God?’ This is a rebuke and a rebuke to them: that is, where are the partners you used to worship besides God?
40:74: 74- “They said, ‘They have strayed from us,’ meaning they have gone away and are missing so we cannot see them. Then they turned away from that and moved on to informing us of their nonexistence and nonexistence, saying, ‘Rather, we did not call upon anything before,’ meaning we did not worship anything. They said this when we showed them the misguidance and ignorance they were in, and that they were worshipping things that neither saw nor heard nor harmed nor benefited. This is not a denial on their part of the existence of the idols they were worshipping, rather it is an admission on their part that their worship of them was false. ‘Thus does God misguide the disbelievers,’ meaning, in the same way God misguides the disbelievers, as they worshipped these idols that led them to the Fire.
40:75: And the reference in His saying: 75- That is to the misguidance indicated by the verb: that is, that misguidance is due to what you used to rejoice on the earth that is, what you used to show in this world of joy in disobeying God and delight in disobeying His messengers and books. And it was said that it was with what you used to rejoice in of money, followers and health. And it was said that it was with what you used to rejoice in of denying the resurrection. And it was said that what is meant by joy here is insolence and arrogance, and by merriment is an increase in insolence. Mujahid and others said: merriment means: you act insolently and show off. Ad-Dahhak said: Joy is pleasure, and merriment is aggression. And Muqatil said: merriment means insolence and pride.
40:76: 76- Enter the gates of Hell while you are eternally therein meaning destined to remain there forever. Evil is the abode of the arrogant about accepting the truth: Hell.
40:77: Then God, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be patient, saying: 77- “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is true.” That is, His promise to take revenge on them will inevitably happen, either in this world or in the Hereafter. For this reason, He said: Then either We show you some of what We promise them of the punishment in this world by killing, captivity, and subjugation. The word either in then is redundant according to the view of Al-Mubarrad and Al-Zajjaj. The original is then We show you. The letter nun of emphasis was added to the verb. His saying: Or We cause you to die is in apposition to We cause you to die, meaning, “Or We cause you to die before the punishment is brought down upon them. “To Us they will be returned” on the Day of Resurrection, so We will punish them.
40:78: 78- And We had certainly sent messengers before you, among them were those We have related to you meaning, We informed you of their report and what they encountered from their people, and among them were those We have not related to you nor did We convey to you knowledge of what happened between them and their people. And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God not from himself. What is meant by the sign is the miracle indicating his prophethood. So when the command of God comes meaning, when the appointed time for their punishment in this world or in the Hereafter comes, it will be judged between them in truth between them, so God will save through His just judgment upon His righteous servants. And there will be loss meaning at that time the falsifiers who follow falsehood and act upon it.
40:79: Then the Almighty bestowed upon His servants a type of His countless blessings, saying: 79- God is He who has made for you the grazing livestock meaning He created them for your sake. Al-Zajjaj said: The grazing livestock here are the camels, and it was said that the eight pairs that you may ride from them “from” is for partiality, and likewise in His statement: and from them you eat. It is permissible for it to be for the beginning of the goal in both instances, and its meaning is the beginning of riding and the beginning of eating, but the first is more appropriate. The meaning is: that you may ride some of them and eat some of them.
40:80: 80- And for you therein are other benefits besides riding and eating fur, wool, hair, butter, ghee, cheese, and other things. And that you may achieve thereby a need in your hearts. Mujahid, Muqatil, and Qatadah said: They carry your burdens from one land to another. This has been fully explained in Surat An-Nahl. And upon them and upon ships you are carried. That is, on camels on land and on ships at sea. It was said that what is meant by carrying livestock here is carrying children and women in litters.
40:81: 81- And He shows you His signs meaning His indications that point to the perfection of His power and His oneness. Then which of the signs of God do you deny? They are all so obvious and not hidden that no one can deny them and no one can reject them. In it is a rebuke and a great rebuke to them, and the accusative is you will deny. It was brought forward before the agent in it because it is the beginning of the speech.
40:82: Then the Almighty guided them to consider and reflect on the signs of God, saying: 82- Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? Of the nations who disobeyed God and denied His messengers, for the traces found in their homes indicate the punishment that befell them and the evil end they met. Then the Almighty explained that those nations were superior to these in number and strength, saying: They were more numerous than them and stronger in strength, meaning more numerous than them, stronger in body, and more abundant in wealth, and more evident than them traces in the land in buildings, factories, and crops, so what they used to earn availed them not. The first ma may be an interrogative: meaning what availed them not, or negative: meaning it did not avail them, and the second ma may be a relative pronoun or a verbal noun.
40:83: 83- So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs meaning with clear arguments and apparent miracles they rejoiced in what they had of knowledge meaning they showed joy in what they claimed to be knowledge of the false doubts and false claims. He called it knowledge to mock them, or what they believed. Mujahid said: They said, “We know more than them. We will never be punished or resurrected.” It was said that what is meant by knowledge is the conditions of this world, not religion, as in His statement, They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world. It was said that those who rejoiced in what they had of knowledge were the messengers, because when their people denied them, God informed them that He would destroy the disbelievers and save the believers, so they rejoiced at that. And that which they used to ridicule encompassed them meaning, the recompense for their mockery encompassed them.
40:84: 84- So when they saw Our punishment, meaning they witnessed Our torment descending upon them, they said, ‘We believe in God alone and disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him,’ meaning the idols that they used to worship.
40:85: 85- So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment meaning when they witnessed Our punishment, because that faith is not the kind of faith that benefits its possessor, for only voluntary faith benefits, not forced faith. The way of God that has passed among His servants meaning that which has already occurred among His servants. The meaning is that God, the Exalted, has established this way for all nations, that faith will not benefit them when they see the punishment. This has been explained previously in Surat An-Nisa and Surat At-Tawbah. The accusative of sunnah is used as a verbal noun emphasizing a deleted verb, similar to God's promise and similar emphatic verbal nouns. It has also been said that it is used as a warning: meaning, O people of Makkah, beware of God's way with past nations. The former is more appropriate. And there the disbelievers lost meaning when they saw God's punishment and witnessed His punishment. Al-Zajjaj said: The disbeliever is a loser at all times, but their loss will become clear to them when they see the punishment. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba'th wa Al-Nushur narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited: ‘When the shackles are on their necks’ until the verse: ‘are set ablaze.’ He said: ‘If a bullet the size of this’ – and he pointed to a skull – were sent down from the sky to the earth, a distance of five hundred years, it would reach the earth before nightfall. If it were sent down from the top of the chain, it would travel for forty years, day and night, before reaching its base, or he said its bottom.’” Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in Sifat Al-Nahar on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: They will swim in the boiling water, and everything on them will be sloughed off – skin, flesh, and veins – until it reaches his heels, until his flesh is the size of his height, and his height is sixty cubits. Then he will be covered with another skin, then he will be set ablaze in the boiling water. Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib regarding the verse: ‘And among them are those whose history We have not told you’ – that he said: God sent an Abyssinian slave, and he is one of those whose history We have not told Muhammad.
41:1: It is called Surat Ha Mim As-Sajdah and it has fifty-four verses, and some say fifty-three. Al-Qurtubi said: It was revealed in Mecca according to everyone. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that it was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Ya’la, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym, and al-Bayhaqi, both of them in al-Dala’il, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: “The Quraysh gathered one day and said: ‘Look for the most knowledgeable among you in magic, divination, and poetry. Let this man, who has divided our community, scattered our affairs, and criticized our religion, come and speak to him and see what he will say in response.’ They said: ‘We do not know anyone other than Utbah ibn Rabi’ah.’ They said: ‘Come, Abu al-Walid.’ So he came to him and said: ‘O Muhammad, are you better or Abdullah? Are you better or Abdul Muttalib?’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) remained silent. He said: ‘If you claim that these people are better than you, then they have worshipped the gods you criticized. If you claim that you are better than them, then speak so that we may hear your words. By God, we have never seen a more ominous calf for your people than you. You have divided our community, scattered our affairs, criticized our religion, and disgraced us among the Arabs. It has even spread among them that there is a magician among the Quraysh and a soothsayer among the Quraysh. By God, you only expect the like of…’” The cry of the pregnant woman is that some of us will rise up to one another with swords, O man, if what you have is only need, we will gather for you until you are the richest man of Quraysh, and if what you have is only misfortune, then choose any women of Quraysh you wish and we will marry you to ten. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Are you done? He said: Yes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Ha Meem. * A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. * A Book whose verses are detailed.” Until he reached: “But if they turn away, then say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ‘Aad and Thamud.” Utbah said: Enough, enough, you have nothing else? He said: No. So he returned to Quraysh and they said: What is behind you? He said: I have not left anything that I think you would speak to him about without speaking to him. They said: Did he answer you? He said: By the One who set it up with a intention, I did not understand anything of what he said except that he warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ‘Aad and Thamud. They said: Woe to you, the man speaks to you in Arabic and you do not know what he said? He said: No, by God, I did not understand anything he said except the mention of the thunderbolt. Abu Nu`aym and Al-Bayhaqi both narrated in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: “When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited to `Utbah ibn Rabi`ah, ‘Ha Meem, a revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,’ he came to his companions and said: ‘O my people, obey me on this day and disobey me after it. By God, I have heard from this man words the like of which I have never heard before, and I did not know what he intended by it.’” In this regard, there are narrations that indicate that the Quraysh gathered and sent `Utbah ibn Rabi`ah and that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited the beginning of this surah to him. His saying: 1- Ha Mim - we have already discussed its parsing and meaning in the surah before this one, so we will not repeat it.
41:2: And likewise we have discussed the meaning of 2- Tanzil and its parsing. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Akhfash said: Tanzil is raised as a subject and its predicate is The Book detailed. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for this to be omitted and it is permissible to say Book instead of Tanzil, and from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful is related to Tanzil.
41:3: Meaning 3- His verses are explained in detail means that they are clarified or made in different ways. Qatada said: They are explained by clarifying what is lawful and what is unlawful, and what is obedience to Him and what is disobedience to Him. Al-Hasan said: With promise and threat. Sufyan said: With reward and punishment, and there is no objection to applying it to all. The sentence is in the accusative case as an attribute of the Book. It was read Fussilat with a light vowel: meaning, I distinguished between truth and falsehood. The accusative of an Arabic Quran is in the state of description, meaning, its verses are explained while it is an Arabic Quran. Al-Akhfash said: It is in the accusative case for praise, and it was said that it is in the source: meaning, he recites it as a Quran, and it was said that it is a second object of Fussilat, and it was said that it is in the form of an implied verb that indicates it. Fussilat 41:meaning, we explained it as an Arabic Quran for a people who know meaning, they know its meanings and understand them: and they are the people of the Arabic language. Ad-Dahhak said: meaning, they know, meaning, they know its meanings and understand them: and they are the people of the Arabic language. Ad-Dahhak said: That is, they know that the Qur’an was revealed from God. Mujahid said: That is, they know that He is one God in the Torah and the Gospel. The lam is related to something omitted, another description of the Qur’an: that is, existing for a people, or it is related to Fussilat, but the former is more appropriate.
41:4: And also 4- Bringing good tidings and a warner are two other attributes of the Qur'an or two conditions of the Book, and the meaning is a bringer of good tidings to the friends of God and a warner to His enemies. Bashir and Nadhir were read in the nominative case as an attribute of the Book or the predicate of a deleted subject. So most of them turned away What is meant by most here are the disbelievers: that is, so the disbelievers turned away from what it contained of warning. So they do not hear a hearing from which they would benefit because they turned away from it.
41:5: 5- "And they said, 'Our hearts are within coverings,' meaning, in covers like quivers in which arrows are placed, so they do not understand what you say and your words do not reach them. 'Qunan' is the plural of 'kinaan,' which is a cover. Mujahid said: 'Qunan' is to the heart as paradise is to arrows.' This has been explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. 'And in our ears is deafness,' meaning, deafness. The root of 'waqar' is heaviness. Talhah ibn Musarraf read 'waqar' with a kasra on the 'waw'. It was also read with a fatha on the 'waw' and 'qaf'. 'Min' in 'And between us and you is a veil' indicates the beginning of the goal. The meaning is that the veil began with us and began with you. The intermediate distance between our direction and your direction is encompassed by the veil, with no space in it. These are examples of their hearts' aversion to perceiving the truth and hearing it, and the inability to connect between them and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). 'So work, for we are working,' meaning, work on your religion, for we are working on our religion. Al-Kalbi said: Work for our destruction, for we are working for your destruction. Muqatil said: Work for your God who sent you, for we work for our gods whom we worship. And it was said: Work for your afterlife, for we work for our worldly life.
41:6: Then God the Almighty commanded him to respond to their statement, saying: 6- "Say, 'I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is one God.'" That is, I am only like one of you, were it not for the revelation. I would not be of a different race from you, so that your hearts would be covered from what I call you to, and in your ears would be deafness, and between me and you would be a veil. I do not call you to what contradicts reason, but I call you to monotheism. The majority of scholars read "is revealed" in the passive form. Al-A'mash and Al-Nakha'i read it in the active form, meaning, God reveals to me. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: I am not able to force you to believe, for I am a man like you, and I have no distinction over you except that monotheism and the command to follow it have been revealed to me. So, my duty is to convey the message alone, so if you accept, you will be guided, and if you refuse, you will be destroyed. It was said that the meaning is: I am not an angel, but rather a human being like you, and revelation has been sent to me, not to you. So, through revelation, I became a prophet and it is obligatory for you to follow me. Al-Hasan said about the meaning of the verse: God, the Exalted, taught His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, how to be humble. So be upright toward Him, He made it transitive with to because it includes the meaning of direct yourself, and the meaning is: Direct your uprightness toward Him through obedience and do not deviate from His path. And seek His forgiveness for the sins you have committed. Then He threatened the polytheists and warned them, saying: And woe to the polytheists.
41:7: Then he described them by saying: 7- Those who do not give zakat meaning they prevent it and do not give it to the poor. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They do not acknowledge its obligation. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: They do not give charity nor spend in obedience. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: they do not testify that there is no god but God because it is the zakat and purification of the souls. Al-Farra’ said: The polytheists used to spend on expenses and provide water and food to the pilgrims, so they forbade that to those who believed in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. So this verse was revealed about them: And they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers. It is connected to do not give and is included with it in the scope of the relative clause: meaning they deny the Hereafter and reject it. The use of the separating pronoun is for the purpose of limitation.
41:8: 8- Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have a reward uninterrupted. That is, it will not be cut off from them. It is said that you cut the rope, meaning you cut it. From this is the saying of Al-Asbagh Al-Awdi: By your life, I do not accept anything that is attached to a friend, nor do I accept any good from anyone. It was said that it is the deficient one, as Qatrib said, and he recited the words of Zuhair: The superiority of the horse over the horses of the pack gives thanks and no weakness Al-Jawhari said: “Mann means cutting off, and it is also said that it means deficiency. From this is the saying of God Almighty: “For them is a reward uninterrupted.” Labid said: A stubborn, unproductive woman whose food is not good Mujahid said: Not counted means not counted. It was said that the meaning of the verse is that He does not bestow it upon them, because He only bestows it as a favor. As for the reward, it must be given. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed regarding the sick, the chronically ill, and the senile, if they become too weak to obey, a reward will be written for them equivalent to the best of what they used to do.
41:9: Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to rebuke and rebuke them, saying: 9- Say, 'Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days?' That is, do you indeed disbelieve in the One whose affair is this great affair and whose power is this amazing power? It was said that the two days are Sunday and Monday, and it was also said that what is meant is the length of two days because the real day only comes into existence after the existence of the earth and the heavens. The majority read A'inkum with two hamzas, the second of which is between, and Ibn Kathir read with a hamza followed by a light ya', and you make rivals for Him, meaning opposites and partners. The clause is conjoined with you disbelieve and is under the question, and the reference by His saying: That is to the relative pronoun described by what was mentioned, and it is the subject and predicate Lord of the worlds. And among the worlds are those that you make rivals to God, so how do you make some of His creations partners with Him in His worship?
41:10: 10- And His statement: "And placed therein firm mountains" is connected to creation: that is, how can you disbelieve in He who created the earth and placed therein firm mountains: that is, fixed mountains above it. And it was said that the sentence "And placed therein firm mountains" is a new sentence and not connected to creation because of the separation between them by a foreign word. The first is better because the separating sentence confirms the meaning of what preceded it, so it is in the position of emphasis. The meaning of "above it" is that it is elevated above it because it is a part of the earth, and it differs from it in terms of elevation, so from this standpoint it is as if it is different from it. "And blessed it" means He made it blessed and abundant in goodness through the benefits He created in it for the servants. Al-Suddi said: “He caused its trees to grow therein and determined therein its sustenance.” Qatadah and Mujahid said: He created therein its rivers, trees, and animals. Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and Ad-Dahhak said: “He determined therein the provisions of its people and what is suitable for their livelihood of trade, trees, and benefits. He made in each land what He did not make in another, so that some of them might live off one another through trade and travel from one land to another.” The meaning of in four days is in the completion of four days with the two days that preceded it. This was stated by Az-Zajjaj and others. Ibn Al-Anbari said: An example of this is the saying of someone who says, ‘I left Basra for Baghdad in ten days, and to Kufa in fifteen days,’ meaning in the completion of fifteen days. So the meaning is that the occurrence of all that came before of the creation of the earth and what comes after it occurred in four days.” Equally was substituted. Zayd ibn Ali, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa, Ya’qub, and Amr ibn Ubayd read it in the accusative case as a predicate of days. Abu Ja’far read it in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject. Al-Hasan said: The meaning is in four perfectly level days. His statement, for those who ask is related to equally: meaning, level for those who ask, or to something omitted, as if it was said: This limitation for those who ask is in how much time was the earth and what is in it created? Or it is related to measured: meaning, He determined therein its sustenance for those who seek it and are in need of it. Al-Farra’ said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: And He determined therein its sustenance equally for those in need in four days, and Ibn Jarir chose this option.
41:11: Then when He, the Most High, mentioned the creation of the earth and what is in it, He mentioned how He created the heavens, saying: 11- Then He directed Himself to the heaven, meaning He directed and aimed towards it with a straight aim. Al-Razi said: It is from their saying: He directed Himself to such and such a place, meaning He turned towards it without paying attention to any other action. It is from istawa which is the opposite of istawa straightness. Similar to it is their saying He straightened towards it, and from it is His statement, the Most High: So be straight towards it. The meaning is: Then the caller of wisdom called Him to create the heavens after creating the earth and what is in it. Al-Hasan said: The meaning of the verse is that His command ascended to the heaven and it was smoke. Smoke is what rises from the flames of fire, and it is a metaphor for what is seen from the steam of the earth. The commentators said: This smoke is water vapor. The Almighty specified the ascension to the sky, although the resulting address was directed to it and to the earth, as indicated by His statement: “Then He said to it and to the earth, ‘Come both of you, willingly or by compulsion,’” dispensing with what was mentioned previously about its estimation and the estimation of what is in it. The meaning of come is: Do what I command you and bring it, just as one says come what is best meaning do it. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: God, the Almighty, said: “As for you, O sky, rise your sun, moon, and stars. As for you, O earth, split your rivers and bring forth your fruits and plants.” The majority read come as a command from coming. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr and Mujahid read atayya qaltuna ataina with a long vowel in both of them. It is either from muwata which means agreement, meaning that each of you agrees with the other, or from itaa which means giving. So according to the first, its weight is fa’il like qatilun, and according to the second, if’ala like akrama. Willingly or by force are two verbal nouns in the place of the adverbial: meaning obediently or by force. Al-A’mash read karhan with a damma. Al-Zajjaj said: They obeyed obedience or you both hate it. It was said that the meaning of this command to them is subjugation: meaning be, and they were, as God Almighty said: Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. So the speech is by way of illustration of the effect of His power and the impossibility of its refusal. They said, ‘We have come willingly,’ meaning we came to your command obediently. The plural of both of them is the plural of those who have a mind because they are addressed in a way that addresses rational beings. Al-Qurtubi said: Most scholars said that God Almighty created speech in them, so they spoke as He Almighty wanted. It was also said that this is a representation of the appearance of obedience from them and the influence of divine power in them.
41:12: 12- “And He ordained them as seven heavens,” meaning He created them, perfected them, and finished them, as in the poet’s saying: And upon them are two chains of command, which David made when he dyed the long garments. The pronoun in qada'hinna either refers to the heavens in meaning because they are seven heavens, or it is ambiguous and explained by seven heavens. The accusative of seven heavens is for explanation or as a substitute for the pronoun. It was said that its accusative is as the second object of qada'hinna because it includes the meaning of sabarinha. It was said that it is in the state: that is, He decreed them while they were counted as seven, and qada' could mean made. It was said that it is a specification. The meaning of in two days is as previously mentioned in His statement: He created the earth in two days. So the sentence is six days, as in His statement: He created the heavens and the earth in six days, which was explained previously in Surat Al-A'raf. Mujahid said: And one day of the six days is like a thousand years of those which you count. Abdullah ibn Salam said: He created the earth on Sunday and Monday, and in it were its sustenance on Tuesday and Wednesday, and He created the heavens on Thursday and Friday. His statement: And He inspired in each heaven its command is in apposition to qada'hinna. Qatada and Al-Suddi said: That is, He created in it its sun, moon, stars, orbits, and what is in it of angels, seas, hail, and snow. It was also said that the meaning is: He revealed in it what He wanted and what He commanded. Inspiration may mean a command, as in His statement: That your Lord revealed and His statement: And when I revealed to the disciples, meaning I commanded them. It has been questioned whether this verse can be reconciled with His statement, And the earth after that He spread out. For what is in this verse of His statement, Then He directed Himself to the heaven, indicates that its creation came after the creation of the earth, and its apparent meaning contradicts His statement, And the earth after that He spread out. So it has been said that the then in Then He directed Himself to the heaven does not indicate a temporal delay, but rather a hierarchical delay, so the problem is removed from its origin. Assuming that it indicates a temporal delay, then the combination is possible, since the creation of the earth preceded the creation of the heaven, and spreading it out, in the sense of spreading it out, is something additional to its mere creation, so it was created earlier but spread out later. This is clear, and perhaps it will come in our interpretation of His statement, And the earth after that He spread out, to further clarify the situation, God willing. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps, that is, with shining stars that twinkle on it like the twinkling of lamps. And the accusative of preservation is as a verbal noun emphasizing an omitted verb, that is, and We preserved it with preservation, or as an object for which, on the assumption: And We created the lamps as adornment and preservation, and the first is more appropriate. Abu Hayyan said: In the second aspect, it is a burden and a deviation from the clear and easy meaning. What is meant by preservation is preserving it from the devils who eavesdrop. The reference in his saying: That to what was mentioned previously is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing, meaning the One with eloquent power and abundant knowledge.
41:13: 13- But if they turn away from contemplating and reflecting on these creations, then say, 'I have warned you' meaning, say, O Muhammad, I have warned you and frightened you with a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Aad and Thamud meaning a punishment like their punishment. What is meant by thunderbolt is the destructive punishment of everything. Al-Mubarrad said: The bitter, destructive thunderbolt for whatever it may be. The majority of scholars read thunderbolt as a thunderbolt in both instances. The meaning of thunderbolt and lightning has already been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah.
41:14: And His statement: 14- When the messengers came to them is an adverbial phrase for I warned you, or for a thunderbolt, because it means torment: i.e. I warned you of the torment that would occur at the time of the messengers' arrival, or a state of the thunderbolt of 'Aad. This is more appropriate than the first two, because the warning did not occur at the time of the messengers' arrival, so it cannot be a state of it, and likewise the thunderbolt cannot be a state of time. And His statement: from before them and from behind them is connected to came to them: i.e. it came to them from all their sides. And it was said that the meaning is that the messengers came to them, both before and after, based on the interpretation of the arrival of their speech on the same level as their arrival themselves, so it is as if the messengers came to them and addressed them with their saying: That you worship none but God i.e. that you worship not, based on it being a source, and it is permissible for it to be explanatory or a lightened version of the heavy one, and its subject is a deleted pronoun of state. Then He, the Almighty, mentioned their response to the messengers, saying: They said, ‘If our Lord had willed, He could have sent down angels.’ That is, He could have sent them to us, and He would not have sent to us human beings from our kind. Then they openly declared their disbelief and did not hesitate, saying, Then we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers. That is, we are disbelievers in what you claim, that God sent you to us, because you are human beings like us, with no superiority over us. So how could He have singled you out for His message, rather than us? The refutation of this baseless argument that they brought up has already been presented in more than one place. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa al-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And woe to the polytheists * Who do not give zakat, he said: They do not testify that there is no god but God. And regarding his statement: For them is a reward uninterrupted, he said: Undiminished. Ibn Jarir, An-Nahhas in his Naskh, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on his authority that the Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about the creation of the heavens and the earth. He said: God created the earth on Sunday and Monday, and created the mountains and all the benefits in them on Tuesday, and on Wednesday He created the trees, stones, water, cities, built-up areas, and ruins. So these are four days. Then God Almighty said: “Say, ‘Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed therein firm mountains from above it and blessed it and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask.’” On Thursday He created the heavens, and on Friday He created the stars, the sun, the moon, and the angels, until three hours remained of it. From the first of these three hours He created the terms when whoever dies, and in the second He cast into it everything that is beneficial, and in the third He created Adam and settled him in Paradise and commanded Iblis to prostrate to him and expelled him from it. At the last hour, the Jews said: What next, Muhammad? He said: Then He established Himself on the Throne. They said: You have done well, if only you had completed it. They said: Then He rested. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became extremely angry, so the following verse was revealed: {And We certainly created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us. So be patient over what they say.} Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding His statement: {And determined therein their sustenance} that he said: He split the rivers, planted the trees, placed the mountains, and made the seas flow, and made in these what is not in these and in these what is not in these. Abu al-Shaykh also narrated from him that he said: God, the Most High, created a day and named it Sunday, then He created a second and named it Monday, then He created a third and named it Tuesday, then He created a fourth and named it Wednesday, then He created a fifth and named it Thursday, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Umar from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: God completed His creation in six days and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Bakr something similar to what was mentioned above from Ibn Abbas. Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat from Ibn Abbas in He said: Then he said to it and to the earth, ‘Come, willingly or by compulsion.’ He said: He said to the sky, ‘Bring forth your sun, moon, and stars,’ and to the earth, ‘Divide your rivers and bring forth your fruits.’ They said, ‘We have come willingly.’ Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement, Come, that he said, We were given. And regarding his statement, They said, ‘We have come,’ he said, We were given.
41:15: When God Almighty mentioned ‘Aad and Thamud in general, He mentioned what was specific to each of the two groups in detail, saying: 15- As for ‘Aad, they were arrogant upon the earth without right. That is, they were arrogant about believing in God and confirming His messengers and they acted haughtily over those on the earth without right: that is, without deserving of the arrogance and tyranny that they did. Then, the Almighty mentioned some of the statements they made that indicated their arrogance, saying: And they said, ‘Who is stronger than us in strength?’ They were tall and had great strength, so they were deceived by their bodies when Hud threatened them with punishment. What they meant by this statement was that they were able to ward off the punishment that would befall them. So, God responded to them by saying: Do they not see that God, who created them, is stronger than them in strength? The question is to denounce and rebuke them, meaning, did they not know that God is stronger than them in strength, so He is able to bring down upon them whatever types of punishment He wills by saying, Be, and it is? And they used to deny Our signs, meaning, the miracles of the messengers that God singled them out with and made them evidence of their prophethood, or Our signs that We sent down to Our messengers, or Our signs of creation that We set up for them and made them an argument against them, or all of that.
41:16: Then the Almighty mentioned the punishment He sent down upon them, saying: 16- So We sent upon them a furious wind. Fursal is a very loud wind from the word sarra, which means a shout. Abu Ubaidah said: The meaning of fursal is very violent and stormy. Al-Farra’ said: It is cold and burns as fire burns. Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Qatadah said: It is cold. Qatrib recited the words of Al-Hutay’ah: Those who feed themselves when a storm blows, and those who carry it when they are entrusted with the responsibility of the people. That is, if they were asked for blood money. Mujahid said: It is a very poisonous thing, and it is better to interpret it as cold, because in Arabic language, sar means cold. From this comes the saying of the poet: She has treachery like the horns of women who ride on a day of wind and rain. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: Sarsar may be from as-sar, which means cold, and it may be from rasar al-bab, and from al-sarra, which means a shout, and from it, ‘Fajjat wal-husna sara’ his wife came in a shout. Then the Almighty explained the time of the descent of that punishment upon them, saying: On unlucky days, meaning ominous and unlucky. Mujahid and Qatadah said: The end of Shawwal was from Wednesday to Wednesday, and that is seven nights and eight days in succession. It was also said that they were unlucky and cold, and it was said that they were consecutive, and it was said that they were intense, and it was said that they were full of dust. Nafi`, Ibn Kathir and Abu `Amr read nhasat with a sukoon on the ha' as the plural of nahas, while the rest read it with a kasra. Abu Hatim chose the first reading because of his statement: On a day of continuous misfortune. Abu `Ubaid chose the second reading: That We may make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, meaning that We may make them taste it. Disgrace is humiliation and disgrace because of that arrogance. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful, meaning more severe in humiliation and disgrace. He described the punishment with that, and it is in fact a description of those being punished, because they are the ones who have become characterized by disgrace. And they will not be aided, meaning they will not be prevented from the punishment that has befallen them, and no one will repel it from them.
41:17: Then he mentioned the situation of the other group, saying: 17- And as for Thamud, We guided them meaning, We showed them the path of salvation and showed them the path of truth by sending messengers to them, and setting up proofs for them from among God’s creations, as this obligates every rational person to believe in God and accept His messengers. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of the verse is, We showed them the path of goodness by sending messengers. The majority of scholars read And as for Thamud in the nominative case and without the accusative case. Al-A’mash and Ibn Waththab read it with the nominative and declinable forms. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Asim, in one narration, read it with the accusative and declinable forms. Al-Hasan, Ibn Hurmuz, and Asim, in one narration, read it with the accusative and declinable forms. The nominative case indicates the subject and the sentence after it is the predicate. The accusative case indicates preoccupation. The declinable form indicates the interpretation of the noun as father or tribe. The declinable form indicates its interpretation as tribe. So they preferred blindness to guidance means they chose disbelief over faith. Abu Al-Aliyah said they chose blindness over clarification. Al-Suddi said they chose disobedience over obedience. So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them. It has already been mentioned that thunderbolt is the name for something destructive, whatever it may be. Hun is humiliation and disgrace, so it is as if he said they were struck by the destructive punishment of humiliation or disgrace. It is said that a humiliating punishment means humiliating, like his saying, They did not remain in the humiliating punishment. The ba’ in because of what they used to earn is for causality, meaning because of what they used to earn, or because of their earnings.
41:18: 18- And We saved those who believed and were righteous - and they are Salih and the believers with him - for God saved them from that punishment.
41:19: Then when He, the Most High, mentioned how He punished them in this world, He mentioned how He would punish them in the Hereafter, saying: 19- And the Day when the enemies of God will be gathered to the Fire. Describing them as enemies of God is an exaggeration in their condemnation, and the agent in the adverbial phrase is omitted and indicated by what follows it, meaning: People will be driven on the Day when they are gathered, or by mentioning: meaning, mention the Day when they are gathered. The majority of scholars read yahshur with a damma on the under-tone and raising enemies as a substitute. Nafi' read nahshur with a noon and placing enemies in the accusative case. The meaning of gathering them to the Fire is driving them to it or to the place of reckoning, because the group from Paradise and the group from Hell will be distinguished there. So they will be distributed, meaning the first of them will be detained behind the last of them so that they may catch up and gather together. This is what Qatada, al-Suddi, and others said, and a full explanation of its meaning has already been given in Surat al-Naml.
41:20: 20- Until, when they come to it meaning, when they come to the Fire to which they will be herded, or the place of reckoning. What is for emphasis. Their hearing and their sight and their skins will testify against them as to what they used to do in this world of sins. Muqatil said: Their limbs will speak of what their tongues have concealed of their actions of polytheism. What is meant by skins is their well-known skins, according to most commentators. Al-Suddi, Ubayd God ibn Abi Ja`far, and Al-Farra’ said: What is meant by skins is the private parts, but the former is more appropriate.
41:21: 21- And they will say to their skins, ‘Why have you testified against us?’ The reason for singling out the three as witnesses is what Al-Razi mentioned, that the five senses are: hearing, sight, smell, taste, and touch, and the instrument of touch is the skin. So God Almighty mentioned here three types of senses, which are hearing, sight, and touch, and neglected to mention two types, which are taste and smell. Taste is included in touch in some ways, because the perception of taste is only achieved when the skin of the tongue comes into contact with the mass of food, and likewise smell is not achieved until the skin of the palate comes into contact with the mass of smell, so they are included in the type of touch. And if you know from his words the reason for singling out the three for mention, you will know from it the reason for singling out the skins for questioning because they include three senses, so sin comes from them more. As for the saying of those who interpreted the skins as the private parts, the reason for singling them out for questioning is clear, because what the private parts testify to of adultery is more hideous and brings shame and punishment. We have already presented the reason for singling out hearing and combining The eyes said, God has made us speak, He who makes everything speak. That is, He made every speaking thing of His creation speak, so we testify against you regarding what you did of the shameful deeds. It was also said that the meaning is: We did not speak by our own choice, rather God made us speak. The first is more appropriate. And He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. It was said that this is from the completion of Al-Julud’s speech, and it was said that it is a new chapter in the speech of God, and the meaning is that He who was able to create you and bring you into being from the beginning was able to bring you back and return you to Him.
41:22: 22- And you were not concealing yourself, lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins should testify against you. This is a rebuke and rebuke from God, the Most High, or from the words of the skins: that is, you were not concealing your ugly deeds, fearing the testimony of your limbs against you. Since a person is not able to conceal his limbs when committing a sin, the meaning of concealing here is to abandon the sin. It was said that the meaning of concealing is to guard against: that is, you were not wary in this world of your limbs testifying against you in the Hereafter, so you abandoned sins for fear of this testimony. And in His statement: that you should testify is in the accusative case as a reason: that is, in order for you to testify, or fearing that you should testify. It was said that it is accusative by removing the preposition, which is with, or about, or from. It was said that concealment includes the meaning of suspicion: that is, you did not think that you would witness, and this is far-fetched. But you thought that God did not know much of what you do of sins, so you dared to do them. It was said that the disbelievers used to say: God does not know what is in our souls, but He knows what we reveal, not what we conceal. Qatada said: Suspicion here means knowledge. It was also said that what is intended by suspicion is a metaphorical meaning that includes its literal meaning and what is above it of knowledge.
41:23: 23- And the reference in His saying: That is to what was mentioned of their assumption, and it is the subject and its predicate is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord and His saying: He ruined you is another predicate for the subject. It was said that He ruined you is in the accusative case as a predicate of the implied state. It was said that your assumption is a substitute for That, and What you assumed is its predicate, and He ruined you is another predicate, or a state. It was said that your assumption is the predicate of the first, and the relative pronoun and its clause are the second predicate, and He ruined you is the third predicate, and the meaning is: that your assumption that God does not know much of what you do destroyed you and threw you into the fire so you became among the losers meaning complete in loss.
41:24: Then He informed about their condition, saying: 24- If they are patient, then the Fire will be their abode. That is, if they are patient with the Fire, then the Fire will be their abode: that is, their place of settlement and residence, from which they will not escape. It was also said that the meaning is: If they are patient in this world with the deeds of the people of the Fire, then the Fire will be their abode. But if they seek repentance, they will not be of those who are repented. It is said that someone repented to me: meaning he satisfied me after he had angered me, and I asked him to repent, I asked him to be pleased. The meaning is that if they ask him to return them to what they love, he will not do so because they do not deserve that. Al-Khalil said: You say I asked him to repent, so he repented to me: meaning I appeased him, so he appeased me. The meaning of the verse is: If they seek satisfaction, then satisfaction will not come to them, rather they will inevitably go to the Fire. The majority read yasta'tabawu with a fatha on the lower letter and a kasra on the second upper ta', in the active form. They read from the repenters with the fat-ha on the first letter, as a passive participle. Al-Hasan, Ubayd ibn Umair, and Abu al-Aaliyah read they repenter as a passive participle, so they are not from the repenters is an active participle: meaning that if God pardons them and returns them to the world, they will not work in obedience to Him, as in His Almighty’s saying: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. At-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And they are distributed, he said: The first of them is detained for the last of them. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: They are pushed. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: I was hidden behind the curtains of the Ka`bah when three men came: a Qurayshite and two Thaqifites, or a Thaqif and two Qurayshites, with much flesh on their bellies but little understanding in their hearts. They said words that I did not hear. One of them said: Do you think that God hears what we are saying? The other two said: If we raise our voices, He hears it, but if we do not raise our voices, He does not hear it. The other two said: If He hears any of it, He hears all of it.
