I mentioned that to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and God revealed: {And you were not covering yourselves, lest your ears should bear witness against you} until His saying: {of the losers.} Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated on the authority of Mu'awiyah ibn Haidah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You will be gathered here - and he pointed with his hand to Syria - "on foot and riding, on your faces, and you will be presented to God with blood on your mouths. The first parts of you to be revealed will be your thigh and your shoulder." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: And you were not covering yourself lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins should testify against you. Ahmad, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Let none of you die except while having good thoughts about God, for some people were ruined by their bad thoughts about God. God said: "And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord that has ruined you, and you have become among the losers."
41:25: His saying: 25- "And We appointed for them companions" meaning We prepared companions from among the devils. Al-Zajjaj said: We caused them to have companions until they led them astray. It was also said that We empowered them with companions, and it was also said that We decreed. The meanings are close, and the root of "appointment" is making things easy and making things easy. "Quarana is the plural of qareen", and they are the devils. He made them like their friends. It was also said that God appointed for them companions in the Fire, but it is more appropriate that this is in this world, based on His statement: "And they made attractive to them what is before them and what is behind them." The meaning is: They made attractive to them what is before them of worldly matters and desires, and they led them to fall into disobeying God by their immersion in it. They made attractive to them what is behind them of the matters of the Hereafter, so they said: There is no resurrection, no reckoning, no Paradise, and no Hell. Al-Zajjaj said: What is before them is what they did, and what is behind them is what they resolved to do. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Zajjaj that he said: What is before them of the matter of the Hereafter is that there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Hellfire, and what is behind them of the matter of this world and the word has come into effect upon them means that the punishment has become obligatory and established upon them, and it is the saying of the Most High: I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you among them, all together. And among nations is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in upon them, and the meaning is: existing among nations. And it was said that in means with: that is, with nations of the disbelieving nations that had passed away and passed away before them of the jinn and mankind in disbelief, and the phrase they were losers is an explanation of why they deserved the punishment.
41:26: 26- And those who disbelieved said, ‘Do not listen to this Qur’an,’ meaning some of them said to one another, Do not listen to it and do not pay attention to it. It was said that the meaning of do not listen is do not obey, as it is said, I listened to you, meaning, I obeyed you. “And speak noisily therein,” meaning, obstruct it with idle talk and falsehood, or raise your voices so that the reader would be confused. Mujahid said, Be noisy therein with bleating, clapping, and mixing up your speech until it becomes idle talk. Ad-Dahhak said, Speak a lot so that what he says will be confused. Abu Al-Aaliyah said, Fall into it and criticize it. The majority of scholars read and speak noisily with a fatha on the ghain, from laghā if someone speaks idle talk, which is something that is of no benefit, or from lagha with a fatha, also with a fatha, as narrated by Al-Akhfash. Isa bin Umar, Al-Jahdary, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Abu Haywah, Bakr bin Habib As-Sahmi, Qatadah, As-Sammak, and Az-Za’farani read it with a damma on the ghain. We have already discussed the use of idle talk in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Perhaps you will prevail, meaning that you will prevail over them and make them remain silent.
41:27: Then He, the Most High, threatened them for that, saying: 27- Then We will surely make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment. This is a threat to all disbelievers, and those with whom the context primarily applies to them are included in it. And We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do. That is, We will recompense them in the Hereafter for the worst of the deeds they did in this world. Muqatil said: It is polytheism. It was also said that the meaning is that He will recompense them for the evils of their deeds, not for the good ones, as they do when it comes to maintaining kinship ties and honoring guests, because that is invalid and there is no reward for it given their disbelief.
41:28: And the reference in His saying: 28- That is to what came before, and it is a subject and its predicate is the recompense of the enemies of God, or the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning that is the matter, and the phrase the recompense of the enemies of God is the Fire explains the sentence before it, and the first is better and the Fire is an apposition to the recompense, or a substitute for it, or the predicate of a deleted subject, or a subject and the predicate for them therein is the home of eternity. According to the first three interpretations, the phrase for them therein is the home of eternity is a resumption confirming what came before it, and the meaning of the home of eternity is the permanent abode that has no interruption as recompense for what they used to deny Our verses meaning they are recompensed as a recompense for their denial of the verses of God. Muqatil said: He means that they deny that the Qur'an is from God, and based on this the expression of the meaning of denial is because it is the cause of it, establishing the cause in the place of the effect.
41:29: 29- And those who disbelieved will say, ‘Our Lord, show us those who led us astray among the jinn and mankind.’ They said this while they were in the Fire. The past tense is mentioned to indicate that it will definitely happen. What is meant is that they asked God, the Exalted, to show them who had led them astray from among the jinn and mankind, from the devils who used to tempt them and urge them to commit sins, and from the leaders who used to make disbelief seem attractive to them. It was said that what was meant was Iblis and Cain because they were the ones who legislated sin for the children of Adam. The majority of scholars read arna with a kasra on the ra’. Ibn Muhaysin and Al-Susi, on the authority of Abu Amr and Ibn Amir, read it with a sukoon on the ra’. Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read it the same way, and they are two dialects with the same meaning. Al-Khalil said: If you say, Show me your garment, with the kasra, it means, Show it to me, and with the sukoon, Give it to me. “We will put them under our feet,” meaning, we will trample them with our feet to get rid of them. It was also said, We will put them below us in the fire, “so that they will be among the lowest,” in a place there, or so that they will be among the most humiliated and disgraced. It was also said, so that their punishment will be more severe than ours.
41:30: Then, after mentioning the punishment of the disbelievers and what He has prepared for them, He mentioned the state of the believers and what He has bestowed upon them, saying: 30- Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ meaning, He is One, with no partner, and then remain steadfast in monotheism and do not pay attention to any god other than God. A group of the Companions and Followers said: The meaning of steadfastness is to do deeds sincerely for God. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: Then they remain steadfast in obeying God. Al-Hasan said: They remained steadfast in the commands of God, so they acted in obedience to Him and avoided disobeying Him. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: They remained steadfast in testifying that there is no god but God until they died. Al-Thawri said: They acted in accordance with what they said. Al-Rabi’ said: They turned away from everything other than God. Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad said: They renounced the transient and desired the everlasting. The angels descend upon them from God, the Exalted, with the good tidings they seek, such as bringing benefit, warding off harm, or lifting sorrow. Ibn Zayd and Mujahid said: They descend upon them at death. Muqatil and Qatada said: When they rise from their graves for the resurrection. Wakee' said: The good tidings are given in three situations: at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection. A and Do not fear and do not grieve "an" is the mitigating, explanatory, or accusative particle. "La" in the first two meanings is prohibitive, and in the third it is negative. The meaning is: Do not fear what you are about to do of the affairs of the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have missed of the affairs of this world of family, children, and wealth. Mujahid said: Do not fear death and do not grieve over your children, for God is your successor over them. "Ata' said: Do not fear the rejection of your reward, for it is accepted, and do not grieve over your sins, for I will forgive them. What appears is that the angels do not descend upon them at a specific time, and the negation of fear and grief is not restricted to a specific situation, as is indicated by the deletion of the related word in all of them. And receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised in this world, for you will reach it, settle there, and abide in its delights.
41:31: Then He, the Almighty, gave them glad tidings of something even greater than all of that, saying: 31- We are your allies in this world and in the Hereafter. That is, We are the ones who will protect you and help you in the affairs of this world and the hereafter. Whoever has God as his guardian will attain every goal and be saved from every fear. It was said that this is from the words of the angels. Mujahid said: They will say to them, "We are your companions who were with you in this world. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, they will say, 'We will not leave you until you enter Paradise.'" Al-Suddi said: We are the guardians of your deeds in this world and your allies in the hereafter. It was said that they will intercede for them in the Hereafter and receive them with honor. And for you therein will be whatever your souls desire, of various kinds of pleasures and blessings. And for you therein will be whatever you ask for, meaning whatever you wish for. The active participle of the verb to pray means to ask. The meaning of this has been explained in detail in His statement, And for them will be whatever they ask for, and the difference between the two sentences is that the first is in consideration of their souls’ desires, and the second is in consideration of what they ask for, which is more general than it being what their souls desire in the first place. Al-Razi said: What is most likely to me is that His statement, And for you therein will be whatever your souls desire, is a reference to the spiritual paradise mentioned in His statement, Their call therein will be, ‘Glory be to You, O God,’ verse.
41:32: And the accusative of 32- A lodging from the Forgiving, Most Merciful is in the state of the relative pronoun, or of its pronoun, or of the subject of you call upon, or it is a source emphasizing a deleted verb: i.e., We sent it down as a lodging. The lodging: what is prepared for them when they descend of provisions and hospitality, and its investigation was presented previously in Surat Al Imran.
41:33: 33- And who is better in speech than one who invites to God i.e. to the Oneness of God and His obedience. Al-Hasan said: He is the believer whose call God has answered and who invites people to the obedience God has answered, and does righteousness in answering him, and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims' to my Lord. Ibn Sirin, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said: He is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was also narrated by Al-Hasan. Ikrimah, Qays ibn Abi Hazim, and Mujahid said: It was revealed about the muezzins. The response to this is that the verse is Meccan, and the call to prayer was only legislated in Medina. It is better to interpret the verse generally, as the wording requires, and to include in it whoever was a primary cause of its revelation. So, everyone who combines calling people to what God has prescribed and doing righteous deeds, which is fulfilling what God has enjoined upon him while avoiding what He has forbidden, and is a Muslim in religion and not a non-Muslim. There is nothing better than him, nor clearer than his method, nor more rewarding than his work.
41:34: Then God, the Almighty, explained the difference between good deeds and bad ones, saying: 34- Not equal are the good deed and the bad meaning, the good deed that God is pleased with and rewards for is not equal to the bad deed that God dislikes and punishes for. There is no justification for specifying a good deed with a type of obedience, and specifying a bad deed with a type of sin, as the wording is broader than that. It was said that a good deed is monotheism and a bad deed is polytheism. It was also said that a good deed is moderation and a bad deed is a mistake. It was also said that a good deed is forgiveness and a bad deed is victory. It was also said that a good deed is knowledge and a bad deed is obscenity. Al-Farra' said, "There is no redundancy in His statement, 'nor the bad deed'. "Repel evil with that which is better" meaning, repel the evil deed if it comes to you from the wrongdoer with the best possible way to repel it from good deeds, and this includes responding to wrongdoing with kindness, to sin with forgiveness, to anger with patience, to overlook mistakes, and tolerating unpleasant things. Mujahid and Ata' said: "In a way that is best" means by greeting someone with peace, or it was said that it means shaking hands when meeting. "Then he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend." This is the benefit derived from repelling enemies in a way that is best. The meaning is that if you do that repelling, the enemy will become like a friend, and the one who is far from you will become like the one who is close to you. Muqatil said: This was revealed about Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, who was an enemy of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but he became his friend through the marriage that occurred between them. Then he converted to Islam and became a close friend in Islam through marriage. Other sayings have been made, but it is better to interpret the verse in a general sense.
41:35: 35- And none shall receive it except those who are patient. Al-Zajjaj said: This action and state, which is repelling evil with good, is not received except by those who are patient in suppressing anger and enduring hardship. And none shall receive it except one with a great portion in reward and goodness. Qatada said: The great portion in Paradise means none shall receive it except he for whom Paradise is obligatory. It was said that the pronoun in yaleqaha refers to Paradise, and it was said that it refers to the word of monotheism. The majority of scholars read yaleqaha from talqiqa, and Talhah ibn Musarraf and Ibn Kathir, in a narration from him, read yaleqaha from milaaqah.
41:36: Then He, the Most High, commanded him to seek refuge from Satan, saying: 36- And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. An evil suggestion is similar to a nudge, and it is likened to a whisper because it leads to evil. The meaning is: And if Satan diverts you from something that God has prescribed for you, or from repelling evil with that which is better, then seek refuge in God from his evil. He made the evil suggestion an evil suggestion as a mental metaphor, like their saying: very serious. The phrase Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing is an explanation of what preceded it: that is, the All-Hearing of everything that he hears, and the All-Knowing of everything that he knows. And whoever is like this, then he protects whoever seeks refuge in Him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in Mecca reciting the Qur’an, he would raise his voice. The polytheists would drive people away from him and say, Do not listen to this Qur’an and speak noisily during it that you may prevail. But if he lowered his voice, those who wanted to hear the Qur’an would not be able to hear him. So God revealed: Do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice. Abdur-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that he was asked about the statement of God, Our Lord, show us those who led us astray among the jinn and mankind. He said, It refers to the son of Adam who killed his brother and Satan. At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn ‘Adi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited this verse to us: ‘Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast…’ He said: ‘Some people said it, then most of them disbelieved. So whoever says it when he dies is among those who remained steadfast in it.’” Ibn Al-Mubarak, ‘Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Musaddad, Ibn Sa’d, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn ‘Imran on the authority of Abu Bakr As-Siddiq regarding His statement: ‘Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast…’ He said: Steadfastness means that they do not associate anything with God. Ibn Rahawayh and Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilyah narrated on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Hilal on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq that he said: What do you say about these two verses: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, and those who have believed and not mixed their belief with injustice, they said: Those who say, Our Lord is God, then acted according to it and remained steadfast in His command, so they did not sin, and did not mix their belief with injustice, they did not sin. He said: You have burdened them with a severe matter. Those who have believed and not mixed their belief with injustice, means polytheism, and those who say, Our Lord is God, then remained steadfast and did not return to the worship of idols. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of some of the Companions: Then they remained steadfast in the obligations of God. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then they remained steadfast, he said: on the testimony that there is no god but God. Ibn al-Mubarak, Saeed ibn Mansur, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: They remained steadfast in obeying God and did not swerve like a fox. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Darimi, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban narrated on the authority of Sufyan al-Thaqafi, “A man said: ‘O Messenger of God, command me to do something in Islam that I will not ask anyone about after you.’ He said: ‘Say, ‘I believe in God,’ and then remain steadfast.’ I said: ‘What should I avoid?’ He turned to his tongue.” al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha, regarding the statement: And who is better in speech than one who invites to God, she said: The muezzin and does righteousness, she said: Two rak’ahs between the adhan and the iqama. Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from another chain of narration on her authority that she said: I do not think that this verse was revealed except regarding the muezzins. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, “Not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel evil by that which is better,” that he said: The Muslims were commanded to be patient when angry, to be forbearing when ignorant, and to forgive when offended. If they do that, God will protect them from Satan and their enemy will submit to them as if he were a devoted friend. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, Repel evil by that which is better, that he said: Greet him with peace and he will be as if he were a devoted friend. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Anas, regarding the verse, And none are granted it except those who are patient, that he said: A man is insulted by his brother, and he says, If you are truthful, then may God forgive me, and if you are lying, then may God forgive you. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Sulayman ibn Sard, who said: “Two men were quarreling in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and one of them became very angry. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I know a word that, if he said it, his anger would go away: I seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed.’ The man said: ‘Am I crazy?’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing.’”
41:37: The Almighty began to explain some of His wonderful signs that indicate the perfection of His power and the strength of His control to prove His Oneness. He said: 37- And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Then, when He explained that these are among His signs, He forbade them from worshipping the sun and the moon, and commanded them to prostrate to God Almighty, saying, Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, because they are two of His creations, and it is not right for them to be partners with Him in His Lordship. And prostrate to God, who created them, meaning He created these four mentioned, because the plural of what is not rational has the same ruling as the plural of females, or signs, or the sun and the moon, because two are plural according to a group of imams. If you worship Him. It was said that some people used to prostrate to the sun and the moon, like the Sabians in their worship of the planets, and they claimed that by prostrating to them they intended to prostrate to God, so they were forbidden from that. This is the reason for specifying the mention of prostration without disagreement. They only differed about the places of prostration. It was said that its place is with His saying: If you worship Him is because it is connected to the command. It was said when he said: And they do not get tired because it is the completion of the statement.
41:38: 38- But if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they never tire. That is, if these people are arrogant about obeying, then the angels continue to glorify God Almighty night and day, and they never tire or cease.
41:39: 39- And among His signs is that you see the earth barren. The address here is to everyone who is suitable for Him or for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Barren means dry and barren. It was also said that it means dusty and does not grow plants. Al-Azhari said: If the earth dries up and does not rain, it is said that it has become barren. But when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells, meaning rainwater. The meaning of quiver is that it moves with plants. It is said that a person quivers if he moves, and from this is the saying of the poet: You see him like the blade of a sword shaking with dew if you do not find food with a bad man The meaning of rabat is to swell and rise before it sprouts. This was said by Mujahid and others. Based on this, the speech has an inversion, and its interpretation is: it swelled and shook. It was said that shaking and swelling may occur before the emergence of the plant or after it. The meaning of rabat in the language is elevation, as a high place is called rabwah or rabiyah. The explanation of this verse has been presented in full in Surat Al-Hajj. It was said that it shook and was pleased with the rain, and rabat means it swelled with plants. Abu Ja`far and Khalid read and rabat “Indeed, He who gave it life will revive the dead” with resurrection and revival Indeed, He is over all things competent nothing is beyond His power, whatever it may be.
41:40: 40- Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses means deviate from the truth. Deviation means inclination and deviation, and from it is the word lahd in the grave, because it leans to one side of it. It is said lahd in the religion of God, meaning he deviated and turned away from it. It is also said lahd. The explanation of deviance has already been presented. Mujahid said: The meaning of they deviate from belief in the Qur’an. Mujahid said: They deviate when reciting the Qur’an by whistling, clapping, idle talk, and singing. Qatadah said: They lie about Our verses. Al-Suddi said: They are stubborn and oppose. Ibn Zayd said: They associate partners with God. They are not hidden from Us, rather, We know them, so We reward them for what they do. Then He explained the nature of the reward and the difference between the believer and the disbeliever, saying: Is he who is thrown into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? This question is for confirmation, and its purpose is to point out that those who deviate concerning the verses will be thrown into the Fire, and that the believers will come secure on the Day of Resurrection. The apparent meaning of the verse is general, taking into account the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. It was said that the one who is meant by the one who will be thrown into the Fire is Abu Jahl, and the one who comes safely is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said that it is Hamza, and it was said that it is Umar ibn al-Khattab, and it was also said that it is Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi. Do whatever you will, for He is Seeing of what you do. This is a threatening command: that is, do whatever you will of the deeds that will throw you into the Fire, for He is Seeing of what you do, and He will reward you for everything you do. Al-Zajjaj said: Its wording is that of a command, but its meaning is a threat.
41:41: 41- Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message when it came to them is a new sentence confirming what came before it, and the predicate of inna is omitted: that is, those who disbelieved in the Qur’an when it came to them will be punished for their disbelief, or will perish, or will be tormented. It was also said that it is His statement: They will be called from a distant place. This is far-fetched, although Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ preferred it. Al-Kisa’i said: It replaced the previous statement, which is They are not hidden from Us. It was also said that the sentence is a substitute for the first statement, which is: Those who err concerning Our verses. The predicate of inna is the previous statement, And indeed, it is a noble Book, meaning the Qur’an about which they erred: that is, noble enough to be challenged or attacked by those who attack it, immune from every flaw.
41:42: Then He described it as the Truth that falsehood has no way to reach in any way, saying: 42- Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it. Al-Zajjaj said: This means that it is protected from being diminished so that falsehood could approach it from before it, or from being added to so that falsehood could approach it from behind it. This is what Qatada and Al-Suddi said. According to this, the meaning of falsehood is: addition and diminution. Muqatil said: No denial can come to it from the books that came before it, and no book can come after it to invalidate it. This is what Al-Kalbi and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said. It was said that falsehood refers to Satan, meaning he cannot add to it or subtract from it. It was also said that nothing can be added to it or subtracted from it, neither from Gabriel nor from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. A revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy is the predicate of an omitted subject or another description of the Book, according to those who permit presenting non-explicit descriptions before explicit ones. It was also said that it is the description of the Book, and the phrase cannot come to it is an interjection between the described and the description.
68:48: Then the Almighty consoled His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the harm he was experiencing from the disbelievers, saying: 43- Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. That is, what is said to you from these disbelievers, describing you as a magician, a liar, or a madman, is except what was said to the messengers before you, for their people used to say to them the same as these people say to you. It was said that the meaning is: What is said to you about monotheism and sincere worship of God is except what was said to the messengers before you, for all the religions agree on that. It was said that it is a question: What is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you? Indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness to those who deserve His forgiveness from among the monotheists who pledged allegiance to you and to the prophets who pledged allegiance before you. And the Possessor of painful punishment for the disbelievers who denied and were hostile to the messengers of God. It was said that He is the Possessor of forgiveness for the prophets, and the Possessor of punishment for their enemies. 48- So be patient for the decision of your Lord meaning for His judgment that He had decreed in His foreknowledge. It was said that the judgment here is to give them respite and delay the victory of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, over them. It was also said that it is what He decreed upon him regarding the delivery of the message. It was said that this was abrogated by the verse of the sword. And do not be like the companion of the fish meaning Jonah, peace be upon him: do not be like him in anger, annoyance and haste. The adverbial phrase when he called is in the accusative case with an omitted complement: meaning do not be in the same state as he was at the time of his call. The phrase while he was filled with grief is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of called, and the one filled with grief and distress is the one who is filled with anger and distress. Qatada said: God consoles his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and orders him to be patient and not to be hasty as the one who was afflicted with the fish was hasty. His story has already been explained in Surat Al-Anbiya, Yunus, and As-Saffat. He called out with his words: “There is no god but You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.” It was said that the one who is suppressed is the one who is seized by his suppression, which is the passageway of the breath. Al-Mubarrad said this. It was also said that it is the one who is imprisoned, but the first is more appropriate. From this is the saying of Dhu Al-Rummah: And you, from the love of Mai, concealed sadness, my heart suffered, my heart ached and oppressed
41:44: 44- And if We had made it a foreign Qur'an meaning, if We had made the Qur'an that you recite to the people in a language other than the Arabic language, they would have said, 'Why were its verses not explained in detail?' meaning, were they explained in our language, for we are Arabs and do not understand the language of the non-Arabs. The interrogative in His statement, a foreigner and an Arab, is for denial, and it is part of the saying of the polytheists: meaning, they would have said, The speech of a foreigner and the Messenger is an Arab. A foreigner is the one who does not articulate, whether he is an Arab or a non-Arab. A foreigner is the opposite of eloquent; he is the one who does not articulate his speech, and a non-speaking animal is called a foreigner. Abu Bakr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read a foreigner with two definite hamzas. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aliyah, Nasr ibn Asim, and Hisham read it with one hamza as a statement, while the rest read it by making the second easy and in between. It was said that what is meant is: Why were its verses not explained in detail, so that some of them were made foreign to make the non-Arabs understandable and some of them Arabic to make the Arabs understandable. Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer them, saying: Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a healing.’ That is, they are guided by it to the truth and are healed by it from every doubt and suspicion, and from illness and pain. And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, that is, a deafness to hearing it and understanding its meanings. That is why they advised each other to engage in idle talk about it. And it is, for them, blindness. Qatadah said: They became blind to the Quran and deaf to it. Al-Suddi said: Their hearts became blind to it. The meaning is: It is, for them, blind. Or it was described with a verbal noun for emphasis. The relative pronoun in His statement: And those who do not believe is a subject and predicate. In their ears is a deafness, or the second relative pronoun is in apposition to the first relative pronoun. And it is deaf is in apposition to guidance according to those who permit the apposition of two different operators. The interpretation is: For the former, it is guidance and healing, and for the latter, it is deafness in their ears. The majority read Amma with a fatha on the meem with a tanween as a verbal noun. Ibn Abbas, Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, Amr bin Al-Aas and Ibn Umar read it with a kasra on the meem with a tanween as a defective noun, describing it as a metaphor. Amr bin Dinar read it with a kasra on the meem and a fatha on the ya as a past tense verb. Abu Ubaidah chose the first reading because he said firstly guidance and healing and did not say guide and healer. It was said that the meaning is: and the burden on them is blindness. The reference in his saying those is to those who do not believe and what is within its scope, and its predicate is they are called from a distant place like their situation considering their lack of understanding of the Quran, the situation of someone who is called from a great distance from which he cannot hear the voice of the one calling him. Al-Farra' said: You say to the man who does not understand your speech, you are calling from a distant place. Ad-Dahhak said: They will be called on the Day of Resurrection by their ugliest names from a distant place. Mujahid said: From a place far from their hearts. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas that he used to prostrate at the last two verses of Al-Sajdah, and Ibn Masoud used to prostrate at the first of them. Ibn Saad and Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar that he used to prostrate at the first. Saeed bin Mansur narrated from him that he used to prostrate at the last verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement, Indeed, those who err concerning Our verses, that he said: It means putting words in the wrong place. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him regarding the statement, Then is he who is thrown into the Fire? He said: Abu Jahl bin Hisham. Or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq. Abd Al-Razzaq, Abd bin Humaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Asakir narrated from Bashir bin Tamim that he said: This verse was revealed about Abu Jahl and Ammar bin Yasir. Ibn Asakir narrated a similar verse from Ikrimah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Do whatever you will, he said: This is specifically for the people of Badr. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And if We had made it a foreign Qur’an, the verse, he said: If We had made the Qur’an a foreign language and your language, O Muhammad, was Arabic, they would have said: It is foreign and Arabic, and you bring it to us in a different or mixed form. Why are its verses not explained in detail? Why are its verses not made clear so that the Qur’an is like the language? He said: So we did not do that lest they say: It would have been an argument against them.
41:45: His statement: 45- And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but there was disagreement over it. This is a new statement that includes consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what he was experiencing of distress due to the disbelief of his people and their criticism of the Qur’an. So God informed him that this was an old custom among the nations of the messengers, as they would differ over the books revealed to them. What is meant by the book is the Torah, and the pronoun in His statement therein refers to it. It was also said that it refers to Moses, but the former is more appropriate. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord regarding delaying the punishment for the disbelievers among your nation, as in His statement: But He defers them for a specified term, "it would have been decided between them" regarding hastening the punishment for those among them who disbelieved. "And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it," meaning about Your book revealed to you, which is the Qur’an. The meaning of disquieting doubt is: one who is in doubt, or one who is extremely doubtful. It was also said that what is meant is the Jews, and that they are in disquieting doubt about the Torah, but the former is more appropriate.
41:46: 46- Whoever does righteousness, it is for [the benefit of] his own soul, meaning whoever obeys God and believes in His Messenger and does not deny them, then the reward for that will return to him and its benefit will be specific to him. And whoever does evil, it is against himself, meaning the punishment for his evil will be against him and not against anyone else. And your Lord is not unjust to His servants, so He does not punish anyone except for his sin, and He does not wrong anyone, as in His statement, the Most High: Indeed, God does not wrong the people at all. We have already discussed the meaning of this verse in Surat Al Imran when He says: And that God is not unjust to His servants, and in Surat Al Anfal as well.
41:47: Then the Almighty informed that no one knows the knowledge of the Resurrection and its time except Him, so He said: 47- To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. So if the question is asked about it, the one being asked must refer its knowledge to Him and not to anyone else. It has been narrated that the polytheists said: O Muhammad, if you are a prophet, then tell us when the Hour will come? So it was revealed. And what is in His statement: And no fruits emerge from their coverings is negative. The first is for comprehensiveness, and the second is for the beginning of the goal. It was said that it is a relative pronoun in the genitive case in apposition to the Hour: meaning the knowledge of the Hour and the knowledge of what will emerge, and the first is more appropriate. And the coverings are the plural of kam with a kasra on the kaf, and it is the container of the fruit and is applied to every container for money or other things. Abu Ubaidah said: Its coverings are its vessels, and they are what the fruit is in, and its singular is kam and kummah. Al-Raghib said: The sleeve is what covers the hand from the shirt, and what covers the fruit, and the plural is sleeves. This indicates that the sleeve is with a damma on the kaf because he made it common between the sleeve of the shirt and the sleeve of the fruit. There is no disagreement that the sleeve of the shirt is with a damma. It can be said that there are two languages regarding the sleeve, which is the container of the fruit. The majority read from fruit in the singular, while Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs read it in the plural. And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. That is, no female carries a pregnancy in her womb or gives birth except with the knowledge of God, the Most High. The exception is devoid of the most general conditions: that is, nothing happens, such as the emergence of a fruit, pregnancy, or giving birth, under any circumstances, except with the knowledge of God. To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour, just as to Him is referred the knowledge of these matters. And the Day He will call them, that is, God, the Most High, will call the polytheists, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say to them: Where are My partners? Those whom you claimed were My partners in this world, from idols and other things, so call upon them now so that they may intercede for you or avert the punishment from you. This is in the manner of mocking them. The majority read partners, with a sukoon on the ya', while Ibn Kathir read it with a fatha. The factor in day is omitted: that is, remember. They said, 'We have given you notice, there is not one witness among us.' It is said, adhan means to inform. And from this is the saying of the poet: She let us know the names of a Lord who is constant and from whom constant repose is never tired. Meaning: We have informed you that none of us will testify that you have a partner. This is because when they witnessed the Resurrection, they disavowed their partners, and the idols they used to worship disavowed them. It was said that the one who said this was the deities they used to worship: that is, none of us will testify that they were right, but the former is more appropriate.
41:48: 48- And what they used to call upon before has vanished from them meaning that what they used to worship in this world, such as idols and the like, will vanish and remain in the Hereafter. And they thought that there was no escape for them meaning they were certain and knew that there was no escape for them. It is said that haas yahyais haysan means he fled. It was said that thought has its real meaning because they still had a thought and hope in those circumstances, but the first is more appropriate.
41:49: Then God the Almighty mentioned some of the conditions of man, saying: 49- "Man does not grow weary of praying for good" meaning he does not grow weary of praying for good for himself and to bring it to him, and good here is: money, health, power and elevation. Al-Suddi said: "Man here refers to the disbeliever, and it was also said to be Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, and it was also said to be Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi'ah and Umayyah bin Khalaf. The first interpretation is to interpret the verse in general terms based on the majority, and it does not contradict the exclusion of the most sincere servants. Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited: Man does not grow weary of praying for money, But if evil touches him, he despairs of [his] hopelessness meaning if affliction, hardship, poverty or sickness touches him, he despairs of God's mercy, despairing of His mercy. It was also said that he despairs of his prayer being answered, despairing due to bad thoughts about his Lord. It was also said that he despairs of the removal of what he is suffering from of hardship, despairing due to what he gets from his assumption of its permanence, and these are two exaggerated forms that indicate that he is extremely hopeless and greatly despairing.
41:50: 50- And if We let him taste mercy from Us after an adversity had befallen him meaning, if We gave him goodness, well-being, and wealth after hardship, sickness, and poverty, he will surely say, ‘This is for me.’ meaning, this is something I deserve from God because of His pleasure with my actions. So he thought that the blessing he had attained came to him because he deserved it, and he did not know that God tests His servants with good and evil so that He may distinguish between the grateful and the ungrateful, and the patient and the impatient. Mujahid said: Its meaning is this, with my actions, and I am entitled to them. And I do not think that the Hour will come, meaning I do not think that it will come as the prophets tell us, or I am not certain of the Resurrection. This is specific to the disbelievers and hypocrites. So what is meant by the human being mentioned at the beginning of the verse is the species, considering the majority of its individuals, because despair of God’s mercy, hopelessness from His goodness, and doubt in the Resurrection only comes from the disbelievers or those who waver in religion, who outwardly pretend to be Muslims but inwardly are disbelievers. And if I were to return to my Lord, assuming the truth of what the prophets tell us about the establishment of the Hour and the occurrence of the Resurrection and the Hereafter, I will have with Him the best, meaning the best state of honor. So he thought that he deserved the good of this world because of the good in it, and he deserved the best of the Hereafter because of what he believed in himself and established for himself, and this is a false belief and a corrupt assumption. Then We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did, meaning We will surely inform them of it on the Day of Resurrection. And We will make them taste a severe punishment, severe because of their sins. This lam and the one before it are…” Introduction to the section.
41:51: 51- And when We bestow favor upon man, meaning upon this species, considering the majority of its individuals, he turns away from giving thanks, and distances himself, meaning he is too proud to submit to the truth and becomes arrogant and haughty. The side here is a metaphor for the soul. It is said, I distanced myself and I became distant, meaning I became distant and distant. The remote place is the faraway place. From this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: You are like the night that overtakes me, even if I think that the distance from you is vast. Yazid ibn al-Qaqa’ read and he distanced himself from his side with an alif before the hamza, and if evil touches him meaning affliction, hardship, poverty, or sickness, then he has a wide supplication meaning much. The Arabs use length and breadth to mean abundance metaphorically. It is said that someone prolonged his speech and was broad in supplication, meaning he multiplied. The meaning is that if evil touches him, he supplicates to God and seeks His help to remove what has befallen him and increases that, so he remembers Him in times of hardship and forgets Him in times of ease, and seeks His help when a calamity descends and abandons Him when a blessing occurs. This is the action of the disbelievers and those Muslims who are not firm in their stance.
41:52: Then the Almighty returned to addressing the disbelievers and arguing with them, saying 52- “Say, ‘Have you considered,’ meaning, inform me, ‘if it is from God,’ meaning, the Qur’an, ‘and then you disbelieved in it,’ meaning, you denied it and did not accept it or act according to what is in it, ‘who is more astray than he who is in extreme dissension?’” Meaning, no one is more astray than you due to the intensity of your mischief and the severity of your enmity. The original is, ‘what is more astray than you?’ So, He placed ‘who is in dissension’ in place of the pronoun to explain their state of dissension, and that it is the greatest reason for their misguidance.
41:53: 53- We will show them Our signs in the horizons meaning, We will show them the evidence of the truth of the Qur’an and the signs that it is from God in the horizons and in their own selves. Horizons is the plural of horizon, which means direction. Horizon is pronounced with a damma on the hamza and the fa’, and this is what the linguists said. Al-Raghib reported that it is also said afaq with a fatha on both of them, and the meaning is: We will show them Our signs in the directions, and in their own selves are the events of the earth. Mujahid said: In the horizons is the conquest of the cities that God facilitated for His Messenger and the caliphs after him and the supporters of His religion in the horizons of the world, east and west, and the victory over the tyrants and the Chosroes. In their selves is the conquest of Mecca, and Ibn Jarir favored this view. Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said: In the horizons are the events of God with the nations, and in their selves on the Day of Badr. Ata' said: In the horizons means the regions of the heavens and the earth, from the sun, moon, stars, night, day, winds, rain, thunder, lightning, thunderbolts, plants, trees, mountains, seas, and other things. And in themselves there is a subtle creation and wondrous wisdom, as in His statement: And in yourselves - will you not see? "Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth?" The pronoun refers to the Qur'an. It was also said that it refers to Islam brought to them by the Messenger of God. It was also said that it refers to what God shows them and does of that. It was also said that it refers to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that he is the true Messenger from God. The first is more appropriate. "Is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?" The sentence is intended to rebuke and rebuke them. "And your Lord is in the nominative case, with the subject li-yakfa to suffice, and the ba is redundant, and it is a substitute for your Lord", and the hamza is for denial. The meaning is: Has it not satisfied them about the promised verses that demonstrate the truth of the Qur'an that He, glory be to Him, is a Witness over all things. It was also said that it means: Or is it not sufficient for your Lord, O Muhammad, that He is a Witness to the deeds of the disbelievers. It was said, "Is your Lord not sufficient as a witness that the Qur'an was revealed from Him?" The witness means the one who knows, or it means the testimony which is presence. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the metaphor here is that God, the Almighty, has made clear to them what is sufficient in evidence, and the meaning is: Is your Lord not sufficient that He is a Witness and Watcher over all things and that nothing is hidden from Him?
41:54: 54- Indeed, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. That is, in doubt about the resurrection, the reckoning, the reward, and the punishment. Indeed, He encompasses all things. His knowledge encompasses all information, and His power encompasses all that is possible. It is said, He encompasses, “He encompasses,” He encompasses, and in this is a severe threat, because He who encompasses all things such that nothing is hidden from Him will reward the doer of good for his good, and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Qatada who said: Concerning the statement, {And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord}, there had been a time and a term that they would have attained from God. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid concerning the statement, {And no fruits emerge from their coverings}, he said: When they appear. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning the statement, {We have informed you}, he said: We have informed you. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ikrimah concerning the statement, {Man will not grow weary}, he said: He will not get tired. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid concerning the statement, {We will show them Our signs in the horizons}, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him concerning the verse, he said: What God opens of towns, and in themselves, he said: The conquest of Mecca. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Jurayj concerning the verse, he said: He withheld the rain from the entire earth, and in themselves, he said: The afflictions that befall their bodies. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, saying: They used to travel and see the traces of Aad and Thamud, and they would say: By God, Muhammad has spoken the truth. But what I see in them is illness.
42:1: It has fifty-three verses, and they are all Meccan. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Al-Sura Ha Mim Ain Sin Qaf was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from Ibn Az-Zubayr, and this is what Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata’ and Jabir said. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah that it was revealed in Mecca except for four verses that were revealed in Medina: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for this but love for the relatives” to the end. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Nu’aym ibn Hammad and Al-Khatib narrated from Arta’ah ibn Al-Mundhir that he said: A man came to Ibn Abbas while Hudhayfah ibn Al-Yaman was with him and said: Tell me the interpretation of Al-Sura Ha Mim Ain Sin Qaf. He ignored him. Then he repeated his statement and he ignored him and repeated his statement. Then he repeated it a third time but he did not answer him, so Hudhayfah said to him: Shall I tell you about it? Why did he dislike it? It was revealed about a man from his family called Abd-Ellah or Abdullah, who will camp by a river in the East and build two cities there. The river will split between them, and every obstinate tyrant will gather in them. Then, when God permits the end of their kingdom and the end of their state and their period, God will send a fire at night upon one of them, and it will become black and dark, burned as if it had never been in its place. Its companion will wake up wondering how it escaped. It will be no sooner that day than every obstinate tyrant among them will gather in it. Then God will cause the earth to swallow it and them all up. This is what His statement, {Ha Meem * Ain Sin Qaf} means a determination from God, a trial and a decree. {Gathering} means justice from Him. {Sin} means it will be. {Qaf} for these two cities. I say: This hadith is not authentic and cannot be proven, and I think it is nothing but fabricated lies. The reason for the one who fabricated it is the same as the enmity of nations, the belittling of their status and the disparagement of them. Abu Ya'la and Ibn Asakir narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission: I said: Rather, with a fabricated chain of transmission and a false text on the authority of Abu Mu'awiyah who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab ascended the pulpit and said: O people, has any of you heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) explain Ha Mim Ain Sin Qaf? Ibn Abbas jumped up and said: Indeed, Ha Mim is one of the names of God. He said: Fa 'Ayn. He said: The one mentioned saw the punishment on the Day of Badr. He said: Fa 'Sin. He said: And those who do wrong will come to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned. He said: So he stood up and was silent. Then Abu Dharr stood up and explained as Ibn Abbas had said and said: Qaf is a calamity from the sky that strikes the people. Ibn Kathir said concerning the first hadith: It is strange, astonishing and reprehensible. And concerning the second hadith: It is stranger than the first hadith. In my opinion, they are both fabricated and false. His saying: 1- Ha Mim.
42:2: 2- "Ha Meem * Ain Sin Qaf" We have already discussed similar openings. Al-Hasan bin Al-Fadl was asked why he separated Ha Meem Ain Sin Qaf and not Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad. He said: Because they are surahs that begin with Ha Meem, so they are like their counterparts, so it is as if Ha Meem is the subject and Ain Sin Qaf is its predicate. Also because they are two verses, and their sisters, such as Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad, Al-Ra and Al-Mas, are one verse. It was also said that the people of interpretation did not differ regarding Ka Ha Ya Ain Sin and its sisters, that they are merely letters of spelling. They differed regarding Ha Meem, so it was said that its meaning is Ha Meem: that is, He decreed, as mentioned above. It was also said that Ha is His forbearance, M His glory, A His knowledge, and Qawra, by which God swore. Other things were said that are forced and contrived, for which there is no evidence, no argument, and no semblance of an argument. We have already mentioned before what was narrated in this regard that has no basis, and the truth is what we presented to you in the opening of Surat Al-Baqarah. It was said that they are two names for the surah, and it was said that they are one name for it. According to the first, they are two predicates for a deleted subject, and according to the second, they are the predicate for that deleted subject. Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas read Ha Mim Saq.
42:3: 3- Thus does God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, inspire you and those before you. This is a new statement not related to what preceded it: that is, like that inspiration that was inspired to all the prophets from the books God revealed to them, which included the call to monotheism and resurrection, is inspired to you, O Muhammad, in this surah. It was said that Ha Mim Ain Sin Qaf was inspired to the prophets before it, so the reference in His saying thus is to it. The majority read is inspired with a kasra on the ha’, in the active form, which is God. Mujahid, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Muhaysin read it with a fatha on it, in the passive form, and the subject is a hidden pronoun referring to thus, and the meaning is: like that inspiration, He inspires you, or the subject is inspired to you, or the mentioned sentence: that is, this word, or the Qur’an, or the source of inspires is inspired to you, and the noun is raised as the subject of a deleted verb, as if it was said: Who inspires? So it was said: God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. As for the reading of the majority, it is clear in wording and meaning, and something like this has been mentioned before in His statement: Men glorify Him therein in the mornings and the evenings. Abu Haywah, Al-A’mash, and Aban read Nawee with a nun, so his statement: God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise is in the accusative case, and the meaning is: We reveal this wording to you.
42:4: 4- To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great. God Almighty mentioned this description of Himself, while He is the King of everything in the heavens and the earth, to indicate the perfection of His power and the influence of His control over all of His creation.
42:5: 5- The heavens almost burst from above them. The majority of scholars read takad with a fat-ha, and likewise yatafitarna with a fat-ha and a shaddah on the ta'. Nafi', al-Kisa'i, and Ibn Wathab read takad al-samawat yatafitarna with a thamada in both of them. Abu 'Amr, al-Mufaddal, Abu Bakr, and Abu 'Ubaid read yatafitarna with a thamada and the noon from infitar, like His statement When the sky is split. Splitting means to crack. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: They burst, they crack from the greatness and majesty of God from above them. It was also said that the meaning is: Each one of them almost bursts above the one below it, from the saying of the polytheists, God has taken a son. It was also said that from above them means from above the earths, but the first is more appropriate. The word min in from above them indicates the beginning of the limit: meaning the splitting begins from above. Al-Akhfash Al-Saghir said: The pronoun refers to the groups of unbelievers, meaning from above the groups of unbelievers, which is very far-fetched. The reason for specifying the direction above is that it is closer to the great signs and dazzling creations, or by way of exaggeration, as if the word unbelievers, although it came from below, affected the direction above, so its effect on the direction below is more appropriate. And the angels exalt [God] with praise of their Lord, meaning they declare Him free from what is not befitting of Him and is not permissible for Him, clothed in His praise. It was said that glorification is the subject of amazement, meaning they are amazed at the audacity of the polytheists towards God. It was said that the meaning of by the command of their Lord was said by Al-Suddi. And they ask forgiveness for those on the earth of the believing servants of God. As in His statement, And they seek forgiveness for those who have believed. It has been said that seeking forgiveness for them means striving for what calls for forgiveness for them and delaying their punishment, hoping for the faith of the disbeliever and the repentance of the sinner, so the verse is general, as is apparent from the wording, and not specific to the believers, even though they are included in it primarily. Unquestionably, it is God who is the Forgiving, the Merciful. That is, He is abundant in forgiveness and mercy for the people of His obedience and His allies, or for all of His servants, for delaying the punishment of the disbelievers and sinners is a type of His forgiveness and mercy.
42:6: 6- And those who have taken as protectors besides Him meaning idols that they worship God is a Guardian over them meaning He preserves their deeds to reward them for them and you are not a guardian over them meaning He has not entrusted you with them so that you may be held accountable for their sins, nor has He entrusted you with guiding them, but rather your duty is to convey the message. It was said that this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
42:7: 7- And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur’an meaning, We have revealed to you like that revelation, and Qur’an is the object of We have revealed, and the meaning is: We have sent down to you an Arabic Qur’an in the language of your people, just as We sent every messenger in the language of his people, so that you may warn the Mother of Towns, which is Mecca, and what is meant is its people, and those around it, of the people, and the second object is omitted: meaning, to warn them of the punishment, and warn of the Day of Assembly, meaning, to warn of the Day of Assembly, which is the Day of Resurrection because it is the gathering place of creation. It was said that what is meant is the gathering of souls with bodies, and it was said that the oppressor and the oppressed are gathered, and it was said that it is the gathering of the agent and the action there is no doubt about it meaning there is no suspicion about it, and the clause is an interjection confirming what preceded it or an attribute of the Day of Gathering or a state of it A group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze. The majority of scholars read a group in the nominative case in both instances, either as a subject and its predicate is a preposition and a noun, and it was common to begin with an indefinite noun because the situation is one of detail, or as a subject and its predicate is a preposition and a noun, and it was common to begin with an indefinite noun because the situation is one of detail, or as a predicate understood before it: that is, a group of them in Paradise and a group of them in the Blaze, or as the predicate of a deleted subject, which is a pronoun referring back to the two groups indicated by the mention of the gathering: that is, they are a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze. Zayd ibn Ali read a group in the accusative case in both instances as a state of a deleted clause: that is, they separated while they were like that. Al-Farra’ and Al-Kisa’i permitted the accusative case on the assumption that you warn a group.
42:8: 8- And if God had willed, He could have made them one nation. Ad-Dahhak said: People of one religion, either on guidance or misguidance, but they split into different religions by the eternal will, and this is the meaning of His statement: But He admits whom He wills into His mercy in the true religion: which is Islam. And the wrongdoers will have neither protector nor helper. That is, the polytheists will have no protector to ward off punishment from them, nor any helper to aid them in that situation. Similar to this is His statement: And if God had willed, He could have gathered them upon guidance and His statement: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance. Here there are disputes between adherents of the doctrines who advocate for what their predecessors followed and which those after them followed. There is no benefit in mentioning any of that, as is our custom in interpreting it. This is a Salafist interpretation that goes with the truth and revolves around the implications of the noble system, and this is only known by the one who is firmly rooted and whose heart, flesh, and blood are free from fanaticism.
42:9: And the sentence 9- Or have they taken besides Him protectors? is a resumption confirming what came before it, which is that the wrongdoers do not have a protector and helper. This am is the disjunctive particle understood by bal which indicates transition and by the hamza which indicates denial: that is, rather, have the disbelievers taken besides God protectors from among the idols that they worship? Then God is the Protector that is, He is the One truly worthy of being taken as a protector, for He is the Creator, the Provider, the Harmer, and the Benefactor. It was said that the fa is the answer to an omitted condition: that is, if they wanted to take a protector in reality, then God is the Protector. And He that is, and it is His nature that He gives life to the dead, and that He is over all things competent that is, He is able to do all that is possible, so He is the One truly worthy of being singled out for divinity and worshipped alone.
42:10: 10- And whatever you differ over, its ruling is with God. This is general and applies to everything in which the servants differ regarding matters of religion. Its ruling and referral is to God, who will judge it on the Day of Resurrection with His ruling and settle the dispute of those who dispute over it. At that time, the truthful will be distinguished from the false, and the group of Paradise and the group of Hell will be distinguished. Al-Kalbi said: And whatever you differ over: meaning, regarding matters of religion, its ruling is with God, who will decide it. Muqatil said: Some of the people of Mecca disbelieved in the Qur'an and some of them believed in it, so this verse was revealed. The consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the cause. It can be said: The meaning of His judgment is to God: that it is referred back to His Book, for it includes the judgment between His servants in what they differ about, so the verse is general in every difference related to the matter of religion, that it is referred back to the Book of God. Similar to this is His saying: But if you disagree about anything, refer it to God and the Messenger. God Almighty has ruled that the religion is Islam, and that the Qur’an is true, and that the believers are in Paradise and the disbelievers are in Hell. However, since the disbelievers will not acknowledge that this is true except in the Hereafter, God promised them that on the Day of Resurrection. That is the judge with this judgment. “God is my Lord. In Him I have relied” I have relied on Him in all my affairs, not on anyone else, and I have entrusted Him with all my matters. And to Him I turn meaning I return in everything that befalls me, not to anyone else. Creator of the heavens and the earth. The majority read it in the nominative case as another predicate of that, or predicate of a deleted subject, or a subject and its predicate is what follows it, or an attribute of my Lord because the addition is pure, and In Him I have relied and to Him I turn is an interjection. Between the adjective and the noun it describes. Zayd ibn Ali read Fatir in the accusative case as an adjective for the noble noun in his statement, To God, and what is between them is an objection or a substitute for the ha’ in upon him or to him. Al-Kisa’i permitted the accusative case as a vocative, and others permitted it as an expression of praise. Fatir is the Creator, the Innovator, and its investigation has been presented above.
42:11: 11- He made for you mates from among yourselves meaning He created for you women from your own kind, or what is meant is Eve because she was created from Adam's rib. Mujahid said: offspring after offspring. And of the livestock, mates meaning He created for the livestock females from their own kind, or He created for you from the livestock types of males and females, and they are the eight that He mentioned in the livestock. He multiplies you therein meaning He spreads you out therein, from dhar' which means spreading, or He creates you and brings you into being. The pronoun in He multiplies you therein refers to the addressees and the livestock, except that it is mostly used for rational beings. The pronoun in therein refers to the making indicated by the verb, and it was said that it refers to what was mentioned about management. Al-Farra', Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Kaysan said: The meaning of He multiplies you therein is "He multiplies you by making you mates because that is the cause of offspring. Ibn Qutaybah said: He creates you therein: meaning in the spouse. It was also said: In the womb. It was also said: There is nothing like Him. What is meant by mentioning the like here is the exaggeration of the negation by way of allusion, for if it is negated from someone who is suitable for it, then it is more appropriate to negate it from him: like their saying: The like of you is not stingy, and others than you are not generous. It was also said that the kaf is an additional letter for emphasis: meaning, There is nothing like Him. It was also said that the like is an additional letter, as Tha’lab and others said, as in his saying: If they believe in the like of what you believe in, meaning in what you believe in. From this is the saying of Aws ibn Hajar: And the dead are like palm trunks covered by pouring rain Like trunks, and the first is better, because metaphor is a door that is well-trodden by the Arabs and a familiar path to them. From this comes the poet’s saying: There is no one like the young man Zuhair who can match his virtues. Another said: A man kills himself for the sake of Layla, even if he spends the night in despair because of Layla. Another said: Saad bin Zaid: If you see their virtue, there is no one like them among the people. Ibn Qutaybah said: The Arabs use proverbs to replace the self, so they say: Someone like me cannot be called this, meaning that I cannot be called that. Abu al-Baqa’ said, favoring the addition of the kaf: If it were not an addition, it would lead to the impossible, since the meaning would be: He has a likeness and there is no likeness for Him. There is a contradiction in that, because if He has a likeness, then there is a likeness for Him, and He is He, even though attributing a likeness to God Almighty is impossible. This is a good statement, but what he mentioned is refuted by what we mentioned about the speech being an external metaphor. Whoever understands this noble verse with the right understanding and contemplates it with the right contemplation will proceed with it when those who differ about the attributes differ in a clear, pure way. And his insight will increase if he contemplates the meaning of His statement: And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. For this affirmation, after that negation of the likeness, includes the coolness of certainty, the healing of the chests, and the quenching of the hearts. So, O seeker of truth, appreciate the value of this luminous argument and strong proof, for with it you destroy many innovations and smash the heads of misguidance, and humiliate groups of those who are pretentious, especially if you add to it the statement of God Almighty: And they do not encompass Him in knowledge. For then you have taken hold of both ends of the rope. What they call theology and theology: Leave the loot that was shouted at in its rooms, but what is the talk of the camels?
42:12: 12- To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth meaning their treasuries or keys. This has been explained previously in Surat Az-Zumar, which is the plural of iqlid, which is the plural of meftah contrary to the norm. An-Nahhas said: He who owns the keys owns the treasuries. Then, when He, the Most High, mentioned that in His hand are the keys of the heavens, He mentioned expansion and contraction after that, saying: He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it meaning He expands it for whom He wills of His creation and restricts it for whom He wills. Indeed, He is Knowing of all things of things. Nothing is hidden from Him. His encompassing knowledge of everything includes His knowledge of the obedience of the obedient and the disobedience of the disobedient. He rewards each according to what he deserves of good and evil. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to us with two books in his hand and said: ‘Do you know what these two books are?’ We said: ‘No, unless you tell us, O Messenger of God.’ He said to the one in his right hand: ‘This is a book from the Lord of the Worlds with the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and their tribes. Then he made it complete for the last of them, so nothing will be added to them or taken away from them ever.’ Then he said to the one in his left: ‘This is a book from the Lord of the Worlds with the names of the people of Hellfire, the names of their fathers and their tribes. Then he made it complete for the last of them, so nothing will be added to them or taken away from them ever.’ His companions said: ‘Then what is the point of working, O Messenger of God, if a matter has already been completed?’ He said: ‘Make yourselves steadfast and come close, for the one in Paradise will have his final deeds done by the people of Paradise, even if he did whatever he did. And the one in Hellfire will have his final deeds done by the people of Hellfire, even if he did whatever he did.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) put his hands together and threw them down, then said: ‘Your Lord has completed His servants; a group will be in Paradise and a group will be in the Blaze.’” Al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: A good, authentic, rare hadith. Ibn Jarir narrated part of it on the authority of Ibn Amr, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Ibn Jarir said: This chain of transmission ending with him is more likely to be correct. I say: Rather, the chain of transmission ending with him is more likely to be correct, because a trustworthy person narrated it in the Prophet’s Mosque, and he also narrated it with an authentic addition from a sahih chain of transmission. The chain of transmission ending with him is strengthened by what Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to us with a book in his hand, looking into it. We said: Look at him, how can he be, while he is illiterate and cannot read? So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) taught it to us and said: This is a book from the Lord of the Worlds with the names of the people of Paradise and the names of their tribes, with no additions or subtractions from them. He said: A group will be in Paradise and a group will be in the Blaze. Your Lord has finished with the deeds of His servants.”
42:13: The address in His statement: 13- He has ordained for you of religion for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: meaning, He has made clear and explained to you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah of monotheism, the religion of Islam, and the fundamentals of the Sharia on which the messengers did not differ and which the books agreed upon, and that which We have revealed to you of the Qur’an, the Sharia of Islam, and disavowal of polytheism. The expression for it is with the relative pronoun to magnify its importance, and He specified what He legislated for our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by revelation, even though what comes after it and before it is mentioned as a recommendation to clearly state his message, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus of what the Sharia agreed upon. Then He explained what He enjoined upon these people, saying: and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus of what the Sharia agreed upon. Then he explained what He commanded them to do, saying: Establish the religion, meaning the Oneness of God, belief in Him, obedience to His messengers, and acceptance of His laws. An is the verbal noun, and it and what follows it are in the nominative case as report of a deleted subject, as if it were said: What is that which God has prescribed? So it was said: It is the establishment of the religion. Or it is in the accusative case as a substitute for the relative pronoun, or in the genitive case as a substitute for the religion, or it is the explanatory particle, because the meaning of said precedes it. Muqatil said: It means monotheism. Mujahid said: God never sent a prophet except that He commanded him to establish prayer, pay zakat, and acknowledge obedience to God. This is His religion that He prescribed for them. Qatadah said: It means making permissible what is permissible and forbidding what is forbidden. He specifically mentioned Abraham, Moses, and Jesus with our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon them, because they are the masters of the laws. Then, when He, the Almighty, commanded them to establish the religion, He forbade them from differing therein, saying: {And do not be divided therein}, meaning, do not differ in monotheism, belief in God, obedience to His messengers, and acceptance of His laws. These are matters on which the laws are agreed upon and the religions are in agreement, so it is not appropriate to differ in such matters. This does not include the branches of issues in which evidence differs, indications conflict, and understandings diverge, as these are areas of independent reasoning and disagreement. Then, the Almighty mentioned that what He legislated of the religion was difficult for the polytheists, saying: {Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you invite them}, meaning, what you invite them to of monotheism and rejection of idols was great and difficult for them.
