Qatadah said: The testimony that there is no god but God alone was difficult and hard for the polytheists, and Satan and his soldiers were fed up with it, but God refused except to support it, elevate it, make it prevail, and grant it victory over those who opposed it. Then He singled out His saints, saying: God chooses for Himself whom He wills. That is, He selects. Choosing means choosing, and the meaning is: He chooses for His unification and entry into His religion whomever He wills from among His servants. And guides to Himself whoever turns back. That is, He guides to His religion and selects for His worship whoever returns to His obedience and accepts His worship.
42:14: Then when He, the Most High, mentioned what He had prescribed for them of establishing the religion and not dividing it, He mentioned what had occurred in the division and disagreement, saying: 14- And they did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them. That is, they did not become divided except out of knowledge that division was misguidance, so they did that division out of transgression among themselves, seeking leadership and intense zeal. It was said that what was meant was the Quraysh, who became divided after knowledge had come to them, which was Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of transgression against him. They used to say what God related about them in His saying: And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that if a warner came to them verse, and in His saying: But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. It was said that what was meant was the nations of the previous prophets, and that they differed among themselves when the period had passed, so some people believed and some people disbelieved. It was said that it was the Jews and Christians in particular, as in His saying: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after there came to them clear evidence, “And had it not been for a word that preceded from the Your Lord which is delaying the punishment until a specified term which is the Day of Resurrection as in His statement: Rather, the Hour is their appointed time It was also said that it refers to the term that God had decreed for their punishment in this world with killing, captivity, humiliation and subjugation for it would have been decided between them meaning that it would have been decided between them with the punishment being brought down upon them immediately. It was also said that it would have been decided between those among them who believed and those who disbelieved with the punishment being brought down upon the disbelievers and the believers being saved And indeed, those who were given the Scripture of the Jews and Christians after them after those before them of the Jews and Christians are in doubt about it meaning about the Qur’an, or about Muhammad disturbing placing them in doubt, that is why they did not believe. Mujahid said: The meaning of after them is before them meaning before the polytheists of Mecca, who are the Jews and Christians. It was also said that what is meant are the disbelieving polytheists among the Arabs who were given the Qur’an after the People of the Scripture were given their Scripture, describing them as being in doubt about the Qur’an disturbing. The majority read they inherited and Zayd ibn Ali read they inherited with a shaddah.
42:15: 15- Therefore, call and be steadfast. That is, because of what was mentioned about division and doubt, or because He legislated what He legislated of the religion, then call and be steadfast. That is, call as you say: I called to so-and-so and so-and-so. This is a reference to what the prophets recommended of monotheism. It was said that there is an inversion of the order of the words, and the meaning is: What we call them to is difficult for the polytheists, so call. Qatadah said: Be steadfast in the command of God. Sufyan said: Be steadfast in the Qur’an. Ad-Dahhak said: “Be steadfast in conveying the message ‘as you have been commanded’ by God, ‘and do not follow their desires’ and their deviant fanaticism, and do not look at the disagreement of those who disagree with you in the remembrance of God, ‘and say, “I have believed in what God has revealed of the Book,” meaning in all the books that God revealed to His messengers, not like those who believed in some of them and disbelieved in others, and I have been commanded to be just between you, in God’s rulings when you bring your cases before me, and I will not wrong you by adding to or subtracting from what God has prescribed, and I will convey to you what God has commanded me to convey as it is.” The lam is the lam of ki: meaning I was commanded to do what I was commanded to do in order to be just between you. It was said that it is redundant, and the meaning is: I was commanded to be just. The first is more appropriate. Abu Al-Aliyah said: I was commanded to be just between you in religion, so I believe in every book and every messenger. It appears that the verse is general in its application to everything, and the meaning is: I have been commanded to be just between you in everything. God is our Lord and your Lord, meaning our God and your God, our Creator and your Creator. For us are our deeds, meaning their reward and punishment are specific to us. And for you are your deeds, meaning their reward and punishment are specific to you. There is no argument between us and you, meaning there is no dispute between us and you, because the truth has been made clear. God will gather us together, at the gathering place. And to Him is the final destination, meaning the return on the Day of Resurrection, when He will reward each one according to his deeds. This was abrogated by the verse of the sword. It was said that the address was to the Jews, and it was said that it was to the disbelievers in general.
42:16: 16- And those who dispute about God after it has been responded to meaning, they dispute about the religion of God after people have responded to it and entered into it. Mujahid said: After people have submitted to Islam. He said: These are people who imagine that ignorance will return. Qatada said: They are the Jews and Christians, and their argument is their saying: Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book came before your book. They saw for themselves the virtue of being people of the book and the children of the prophets, while the polytheists used to say, Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company? So this verse was revealed, and the relative pronoun is the subject, and its predicate is the sentence after it, which is Their argument is invalid before their Lord, meaning it has no stability, like something that moves from its place. It is said: His argument was invalidated, meaning it became invalidated. Refutation means slipping, and the place of Ḥadhād means slipping, and his foot slipped means it slipped. It was said that the pronoun in lahu refers to God. It was also said that it refers to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The former is more appropriate. And upon them is wrath meaning great wrath from God for their false argument. And for them is a severe punishment in the Hereafter.
42:17: 17- God is He Who sent down the Book with the truth. What is meant by the Book is the genus, so it includes all the books revealed to the Messengers. It was said that it refers to the Qur’an specifically, and that by the truth is related to something omitted: that is, mixed with the truth, which is honesty. And what is meant by the balance is justice, as most of the commentators said. They said that justice was called a balance because the balance is the instrument of fairness and equality among creation. It was said: The balance is what was explained in the revealed books of what every person must act upon. It was said: It is the reward for obedience and reward, and for disobedience, punishment. It was said that it is the balance itself, God sent it down from the heavens and taught the servants to weigh with it so that there would be no injustice or shortcoming between them, as in His statement: Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that people may maintain justice. It was said that it refers to Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him. And what can make you know that the Hour is near? Meaning, what is something that will make you aware of it? Knowing its time, perhaps it is something near, or its coming is near, or something that is near. He said qareeb and did not say qareeb because its feminine form is not real. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is perhaps the resurrection or perhaps the coming of the Hour is near. Al-Kisa’i said: qareeb is an adjective used to describe both the feminine and the masculine, as in his saying: Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good. And from this is the saying of the poet: We were close, but the houses were far away. When we arrived, we disappeared right in front of their eyes. It was said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the Hour while some polytheists were with him. They said, When will the Hour be? as a denial of it, so God revealed the verse.
42:18: This is indicated by His statement: 18- Those who do not believe in it urge it on They urge it on in mockery and denial of its coming. And those who believe are fearful of it meaning they are afraid and apprehensive of its coming. Muqatil said: Because they do not know what they are attacking. Al-Zajjaj said: Because they know that they will be held accountable and rewarded. And they know that it is the truth meaning that it will come, there is no doubt about it. Similar to this is His statement: And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful because they will be returning to their Lord. Then He explained the misguidance of those who doubt it, saying: Indeed, those who dispute about the Hour - that is, they dispute about it with a dispute of doubt and suspicion, from mumāra which is argument and debate, or from murriya which is doubt and suspicion - are in extreme error from the truth, because they did not reflect on the reasons for believing in it from the evidence that is visible to them, set up before their eyes, and understandable to their minds. And if they reflected, they would know that the One who created them in the beginning is able to bring them back. Ibn Jarir narrated from Al-Suddi, Establish the religion, meaning: Practice it. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Qatadah, regarding his statement, Establish the religion and do not be divided therein, he said: Do you not know that division leads to destruction and unity leads to affliction? Grue to the polytheists is that to which you invite them, he said: The polytheists were arrogant when it was said to them: There is no god but God. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid, God chooses for Himself whom He wills, he said: He chooses for Himself whom He wills. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And those who dispute about God after He has been responded to, he said: They are the People of the Book who used to dispute with the Muslims and turn them away from guidance after they had responded to God. He said: They are a people of misguidance who used to wait for ignorance to come to them. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the statement of God, And those who dispute about God (al-Baqarah 2:17). He said: They are the Jews and Christians. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of al-Hasan. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: When the verse, When there comes the help of God and the conquest, was revealed, the polytheists said to the believers among them, People have entered God’s religion in multitudes, so leave us. Then the verse, And those who dispute about God (al-Baqarah 2:17) was revealed.
42:19: His statement: 19- God is Kind to His servants meaning He is very kind to them and extremely compassionate towards them. Muqatil said: Kind to the righteous and the wicked, as He does not starve them to death because of their sins. Ikrimah said: Kind to them. As-Suddi said: Gentle with them, and it was also said that He is compassionate towards them. Al-Qurtubi said: Kind to them in presentation and accountability, and other statements were made. The meaning is that His kindness extends to His servants in all their affairs, and among that is the provision by which they live in this world, and this is the meaning of His statement: He provides for whom He wills of them however He wills, so He expands for this one and restricts for that one. And He is the Strong the Great, the dazzling, powerful the Almighty the One who overcomes all things and nothing overcomes Him.
42:20: 20- Whoever desires the tillage of the Hereafter - We increase for him in his tillage. Harth in the language means earning. It is said that he plows for his family and he plows, meaning he earns. From this, a man is called Harith. The original meaning of Harth is to sow seeds in the ground, and it was applied to the fruits and benefits of deeds by way of metaphor. The meaning is: Whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter through his deeds and earnings, God will multiply that good deed for him by ten to seven hundred times. It was also said that it means He will increase his success, assistance, and facilitating the paths of good for him. And whoever desires the tillage of this world - We will give him thereof. That is, whoever desires the reward of this world through his deeds and earnings, We will give him thereof, which is its enjoyment, and whatever God provides for His servants from it, We will give him from it what Our will has decreed and what We have allotted for him in Our judgment. Qatadah also said: God gives whatever He wills of worldly matters based on the intention of the Hereafter, and He does not give anything based on the intention of this world except this world. Al-Qushayri said: It appears that the verse is about the disbeliever, and it is a specification without a specification. Then God Almighty made it clear that the one who seeks worldly gain through his actions will have no share in the Hereafter, saying: And he will have no share in the Hereafter, because he did not work for the Hereafter, so he will have no share in it. The interpretation of this verse was presented in Surat Al-Isra.
42:21: 21- Or have they partners who have instituted for them in religion that which God has not permitted? When God, the Almighty, explained the law in this world and the Hereafter, He followed it with an explanation of the great sin that necessitates Hellfire. The hamza is for questioning and rebuke, and the pronoun they instituted refers to the partners, and the pronoun them refers to the disbelievers. It was also said that the opposite is true, but the former is more appropriate. The meaning of that which God has not permitted is what He has not permitted of polytheism and sins. And were it not for the decisive word which is the delay of their punishment where He said, Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, "it would have been judged between them" in this world, so they would have been hastened with the punishment. The pronoun in "between them" refers to the believers and the polytheists, or to the polytheists and their partners. "And indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment" meaning, the polytheists and deniers will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. The majority of scholars read "and indeed, the wrongdoers" with a kasra over the hamza as a new sentence. Muslim, Al-A'raj, and Ibn Hurmuz read it with a fatha over it as an apposition to the decisive word.
42:22: 22- You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned meaning afraid and terrified of the evil deeds they have earned, and that fear and terrification will be on the Day of Resurrection and it will befall them The pronoun refers to what they have earned, with the assumption of an added word. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, the recompense for what they have earned will inevitably befall them, whether they fear or not. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. And when He mentioned the state of the wrongdoers, He mentioned the state of the believers, saying, And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise Gardens is the plural of garden. Abu Hayyan said: The language of Katheer is to sukoon the waw, and the language of Hudhayl is to open it. The garden is a pleasant place with much greenery. This has been explained in Surat Ar-Rum. The garden of Paradise is the best of its dwellings, as it is the best of its places in this world. For them is whatever they wish with their Lord from the kinds of blessings and types of pleasures. The agent in with their Lord is they wish, or the agent in the gardens of Paradise is stability. The reference in His saying: that is to what was mentioned to the believers before it, and its predicate is the sentence mentioned after it, which is He is the Great Bounty, meaning that which cannot be described and minds are not guided to knowing its reality.
42:23: And the reference in His statement: 23- That is the one about whom God gives good tidings to His servants to the great bounty: that is, He gives them good tidings of it. Then He described the servants by saying: Those who have believed and done righteous deeds So these are the ones who combine faith and doing what God has commanded and abstaining from what He has forbidden, they are the ones who will receive that good tidings. The majority read yabshar with a shaddah from basharah. Mujahid and Hamid bin Qais read it with a damma on the taa, a sukoon on the unified letter, and a kasra on the shin from abshar. Some of the seven read it with a fatha on the taa and a damma on the shin. The readings for this word have already been explained. Then, when He, the Exalted, mentioned what He had informed His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of of these noble rulings contained in His Book, He commanded him to inform them that he would not ask them for any reward for conveying this message, so He said: Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it.’ That is, say, O Muhammad: I do not ask of you any reward or benefit for conveying the message, except love for my relatives. This exception may be connected: that is, unless you love me for my kinship among you, or you love my relatives. Or it may be disjunctive. Al-Zajjaj said: Except love is an exception not from the first: that is, unless you love me for my kinship and protect me.” The addressee is Quraysh. This is the opinion of Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Malik, and Al-Sha’bi. So, the meaning, based on the disjunctive, is: I do not ask of you any reward at all, but I ask you for love for the kinship that is between me and you. Watch over me in it and do not rush to me, and leave me and the people. Qatadah, Muqatil, Al-Suddi, Al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and others said the same. It is also proven from Ibn Abbas, as will be mentioned. Saeed bin Jubair and others said: They are the family of Muhammad, and the evidence used by those who say this will come later. Al-Hasan and others said: The meaning of the verse is: Except for being friendly to God Almighty and drawing closer to Him by obeying Him. Al-Hasan bin Al-Fadl said: Ibn Jarir narrated from Ad-Dahhak that this verse was abrogated, and it was revealed in Mecca, and the polytheists were harming the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so God commanded them to be friendly to him. When he migrated, the Ansar came to him and supported him, so God revealed to him: {And I do not ask you for it any reward. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.} And He revealed to him: {Say, "What I have asked of you for it is yours. My reward is only from God."} And what will become clear at the end of this research will clarify the reward and make clear the meaning of the verse, God willing: {And whoever does a good deed - We will increase for him good therein.} The root of qarf is earning. It is said to someone for his family: meaning he earns. Al-iqtiraf is earning, taken from their saying a man of division: if he is a swindler. The meaning is: Whoever does a good deed - We will increase for him good by doubling its reward. Muqatil said: The meaning is, Whoever earns a single good deed, We will increase for him [in reward] another good deed, multiplying it by ten or more. It was said that what is meant by this good deed is the love of relatives, but interpreting it generally is more appropriate, and the love of relatives is primarily included under it. Indeed, God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative, meaning, He forgives sinners greatly and is most appreciative of the obedient. Qatada said: Forgiving of sins, grateful for good deeds. As-Suddi said: Forgiving of the sins of the family of Muhammad.
42:24: 24- Or do they say, 'He has fabricated a lie against God?' Or is it the disconnected version: meaning, do they say, Muhammad fabricated a lie against God by claiming prophethood and denying the rebuke? The meaning of fabricating a lie is to invent it. Then the Almighty responded to their claim by saying, If God wills, He can seal your heart. Meaning, if he fabricated a lie against God, He would have willed that it would not come from him and would have sealed his heart so that nothing he lied about would ever cross his mind, as you claim. Qatada said, He will seal your heart and make you forget the Quran. So He informed them that if he fabricated a lie against Him, He would have done to him what He informed them of in this verse. Mujahid and Muqatil said, If He wills, He will strengthen your heart by making you patient with their harm so that your heart will not feel hardship because of what they say. It was also said that the addressee is him, and what is meant by the disbelievers is, if He wills, He will seal the hearts of the disbelievers and hasten their punishment. Al-Qushayri mentioned this. It was said that the meaning is: If your soul tempted you to invent a lie against God, He would seal your heart, for no one would dare to lie except one whose heart is sealed, and the former is more appropriate. His statement, And God blots out falsehood is a resumption confirming what preceded it of negating the fabrication. Ibn al-Anbari said: He will seal your heart completely, meaning that what follows is a new verse. Al-Kisa'i said: There is an inversion: that is, God blots out falsehood. Al-Zajjaj said: Or do they say, He has fabricated a complete lie against God? His statement, And God blots out falsehood is an argument against those who deny what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought: that is, if what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought was false, He would have blotted it out, as is His custom with those who fabricate falsehoods. And establishes the truth, that is, Islam, and makes it clear. With His words, that is, with what He revealed of the Quran. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts, that is, Knowing what is in the hearts of His servants. The waw was omitted from and blots out in some copies of the Qur'an, as Al-Kisa'i related.
42:25: 25- And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants meaning He accepts the repentance of the sinners among His servants for the sins they have committed and the evil deeds they have perpetrated. Repentance is regret for the sin and the resolve not to repeat it. It was also said that He accepts the repentance of His allies and those who obey Him. The former is more appropriate, because repentance is accepted from all servants, Muslims and disbelievers, if it is sincere and stems from a pure intention and correct resolve. And He pardons misdeeds in general for those who repent from their misdeeds. And He knows what you do of good and evil, so He rewards each one according to what he deserves. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Hafs, and Khalaf read ta-fa’alun with the superlative as an address. The rest read it with the subjunctive as a predicate. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred the second reading because this verb occurs between two predicates.
42:26: 26- "And those who believe and do righteous deeds will respond." The relative pronoun is in the accusative case: meaning, God responds to those who believe and gives them what they ask of Him. It is said that He responded and responded to means the same. It was also said that the meaning is He accepts the worship of the sincere ones. It was also said that the estimate is He responds to them, so the statement was omitted as was omitted in His statement, "And when they measure out to them," meaning they measure out to them. It was also said that the relative pronoun is in the nominative case: meaning, they respond to their Lord when He calls them, like His statement, "Respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you." Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning of "And those who believe will respond" is that those who believe demand an answer. This is the true meaning of "istaf'ala," so those is in the nominative case, and the former is more appropriate. "And increase them from His bounty," meaning He will increase them over what they asked of Him, or over what they deserve of reward as a favor from Him. It was also said that He will allow them to intercede for their brothers. "And for the disbelievers is a severe punishment." This is for the disbelievers, in contrast to what He mentioned for the believers previously.
42:27: 27- And if God were to expand the provision for His servants, they would surely rebel upon the earth. That is, if God were to expand their provision for them, they would rebel upon the earth, they would disobey therein, be insolent and arrogant, and seek what they have no right to seek. It was also said that the meaning is: If He made them equal in provision, they would not submit to one another, and they would strive for what is not theirs. The former is more appropriate. What appears to be the generality of the types of provision, and it was said that it refers specifically to rain. But He sends down in due measure as He wills. That is, He sends down from the provision to His servants by measure according to His will and what His perfect wisdom dictates. Indeed, He is All-Aware of His servants of their conditions. All-Seeing of what is best for them in terms of expanding or restricting provision. So He measures for each one of them what is best for him and prevents him from spreading corruption through transgression upon the earth.
42:28: 28- And it is He who sends down the rain meaning rain, which is the most beneficial and useful type of provision, after they have despaired meaning after they have lost hope of that. Thus, by sending down the rain after despairing, they know the extent of His mercy towards them, and they thank Him as they should be thanked. And He is the Protector of the righteous among His servants by being kind to them, bringing them benefits, and warding off evil from them. The Praiseworthy is the One deserving of praise from them for His blessings in particular and in general. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, he said: “The life of the Hereafter. We increase for him in his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him thereof,” [al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab] said: Whoever gives priority to his worldly life over his Hereafter, God will not grant him any share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and he will not gain anything from this world except provision that has been allocated to him. Ahmad, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Hibban narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka’b that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Give this nation good tidings of glory, elevation, victory and empowerment on earth, as long as they do not seek this world by working for the Hereafter. Whoever works for the Hereafter for the sake of this world will have no share in the Hereafter.” Al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited the verse, Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, then said: “God says: Son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship and I will fill your chest with contentment and satisfy your poverty. But if you do not, I will fill your chest with preoccupation and will not satisfy your poverty.” Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ali who said: “Cultivation is of two types. The cultivation of this world is wealth and children, and the cultivation of the Hereafter is the lasting righteous deeds.” Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Tawus on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the statement of God, Except for the love of kinship, Saeed bin Jubair said: The kinship of the family of Muhammad. Ibn Abbas said: “I was hasty in saying that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had no clan of Quraysh except that he had kinship among them.” He said: Except that you maintain the kinship that is between me and you. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: I do not ask you for any reward for it except that you love me for my sake because of my kinship and preserve the kinship that is between me and you. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa`d, `Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala`il narrated on the authority of al-Sha`bi who said: Most people are against us regarding this verse, Say, ‘I do not ask of you for it any reward except love for my relatives.’ So we wrote to Ibn `Abbas asking him about that, and he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was of intermediate lineage among the Quraysh, and there was no clan among them that did not have a kinship with him. So God said, Say, ‘I do not ask of you for it any reward’ for what I call you to, except love for my relatives, that you love me for my kinship to you and protect me for it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of `Ali ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn `Abbas regarding the verse, he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had kinship from among the Quraysh, and when they denied him…” And they refused to pledge allegiance to him. He said: O my people, if you refuse to pledge allegiance to me, then preserve my kinship to you, and no one else from the Arabs is more deserving of my protection and support than you. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from him. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated something similar from him. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated something similar from him. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated something similar from him from another chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Muqsim from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Ansar said: We did this and that, and it was as if they were boasting. Al-Abbas said: We have the advantage over you. report of that reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he came to them in their gatherings and said: O group of Ansar, were you not humble and then God honored you? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Will you not answer? They said: What should we say, O Messenger of God? He said: Will you not say: Didn’t your people expel you and we gave you shelter? Didn’t they deny you and we believed you? Didn’t they abandon you and we gave you support? He kept saying this until they knelt on their knees and said: Our wealth and what is in our hands belong to God and His Messenger. Then the verse was revealed: “Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward but love for the relatives.” In its chain of transmission is Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, and he is weak. It is better that the verse is Meccan, not Medinan. We have pointed out at the beginning of the surah the statement of those who said that this verse and what follows it are Medinan, and this is their basis. Abu Nu`aym and al-Daylami transmitted through the path of Mujahid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Say: I do not ask of you for this any reward but love for my relatives,’ meaning that you should protect me in my family and love them through me.” Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it. Al-Suyuti said: With a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘Say: I do not ask of you for this any reward but love for my relatives,’ they said: O Messenger of God, who are these relatives of yours whose love is obligatory upon us? He said: Ali, Fatima and her children.” Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed in Mecca, and the polytheists loved the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God revealed: “Say to them, O Muhammad: ‘I do not ask of you for it’ meaning for what I call you to, ‘any reward’ in this world, ‘except love for my relatives’ except for the protection of my kinship among you.’ So when he migrated to Medina, he wanted to join his brothers among the prophets, so he said: ‘Say: “I have not asked you for any reward - it is yours. My reward is only from God’ meaning His reward and honor in the Hereafter, just as Noah said: ‘And I do not ask of you for it any reward. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds’ and just as Hud, Salih, and Shuaib said: They did not except a reward, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did, so he returned it to them. And it is abrogated. Ahmad narrated Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh, through Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), regarding the verse: “Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for what I have brought you of clear proofs and guidance, except that you love God and draw near to Him by obeying Him.’” This is the gist of what was narrated from the scholar of this nation, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, in his interpretation of this verse. The first meaning is what is authentically reported from him, and was narrated from him by a large group of his students and those who came after them. It is not contradicted by what has been reported from him of abrogation. There is nothing to prevent the Qur’an from being revealed in Mecca, so that the infidels of Quraysh would love it because of the kinship between them and him, and they would memorize it there. Then that would be abrogated and this exception would be removed from its origin, as is indicated by what we have mentioned, which indicates that he did not ask for a reward for conveying it at all. What has been reported about it being attributed to the family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, cannot be used to oppose what has been authentically reported from Ibn Abbas through those many chains of transmission. God has made the family of Muhammad independent of this because of their great virtues and beautiful merits. We have explained some of that when we interpreted his statement: God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the House. Just as this cannot be used to oppose it, so too does what has been reported from him that what is meant by love for kinship is that they love God and draw near to Him by obeying Him, but what strengthens this is that he said: An explanation traced back to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and its chain of transmission is found in Ahmad’s Musnad as follows: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Qaz’ah ibn Suwayd narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muslim ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Qaz’ah, on his authority. Ibn al-Mubarak, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab also narrated it. Al-Suyuti said with a sahih chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hani’ al-Khawlani, who said: I heard ‘Umar ibn Harith and others say: This verse was revealed about the people of the Suffa: And if God were to extend provision to His servants, they would transgress upon the earth. That is because they said, If only we had it, and they desired this world. Al-Hakim narrated a similar verse, which he authenticated, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated it on the authority of ‘Ali.
42:29: The Almighty mentioned some of His signs that indicate the perfection of His power, which necessitates His Oneness and the truth of His promise of resurrection. He said: 29- And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth meaning He created them in this wondrous manner and strange craftsmanship. And what He has dispersed throughout them of living creatures It is permissible to connect it to creation, or it is permissible to connect it to the heavens. The creature is the name for everything that moves. Al-Farra’ said: He meant what He dispersed throughout the earth, not the heavens, like His statement: From them come forth pearls and coral. Rather, it comes forth from the salt, not from the torment. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: Its meaning is what He dispersed throughout one of them, so the complement was deleted. Mujahid said: This includes the angels and people, and the Almighty said: And He creates what you do not know. “And He is Able to gather them” meaning to gather them on the Day of Resurrection. When He wills, He is Able. The adverbial phrase is related to gathering them, not to Able. Abu Al-Baqa’ said: This is because that conveys, and He is Able to gather them when He wills, so the ability is related to the will, which is impossible. Shihab al-Din said: I do not know why it is impossible according to the doctrine of the Sunnis. If he says what the Mu’tazila say, which is that power is related to what God does not will, then his words are valid, but it is a bad doctrine that it is not permissible to believe.
42:30: 30- And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned meaning whatever disasters befall you, whatever they may be, it is because of what your hands have earned of sins. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read for what you have earned without fa, while the rest read it with fa. Ma in what you have earned is the conditional particle, and for this reason fa was included in its answer according to the reading of the majority, and it is not permissible to delete it according to Sibawayh and the majority. Al-Akhfash permitted deletion as in his saying: And if you obey them, then indeed, you are polytheists and the saying of the poet: Whoever does good deeds, God will reward them, and evil is recompensed for evil in the sight of God. It was said that it is the relative pronoun, so deletion or confirmation are both permissible, but the former is better. Al-Zajjaj said: Proving the fa’ is better because fa’ is a reward for the answer to the condition, and whoever deletes fa’ does so because ma has the meaning of alluding to, and the meaning is: What befell you befell what your hands have earned. Al-Hasan said: The calamity here is the hudud set limits for sins, and it is better to take it in general terms, as is indicated by the occurrence of the indefinite noun in the context of negation and the inclusion of the comprehensive man in it. And He pardons many of the sins that people commit, so He does not punish them for them. So the meaning of the verse is that He expiates for the servant for the calamities that befall him and pardons many sins. Authentic evidence has proven that everything that befalls a person in this world, he will be rewarded for it or his sins will be expiated. It was said that this verse is specific to what befalls a person in this world, he will be rewarded for it or his sins will be expiated. It has been said that this verse is specific to the disbelievers, meaning that what they suffer because of their sins, without that being an expiation for their sin or a result of righteousness, and by leaving their punishment for many of their sins, He does not hasten them in this world, but rather gives them respite until the Hereafter. It is better to interpret the verse in a general sense, and forgiveness applies to delaying punishment, just as it applies to erasing sin and removing the address due to it. Al-Wahidi said: This is the most hopeful verse in the Book of God, because He divided the sins of the believers into two categories: a category that He expiated for them through calamities, and a category that He pardoned in this world, and He is Generous and does not go back on His pardon. This is God’s way with the believers. As for the disbeliever, He will not hasten his punishment for his sin until he meets it on the Day of Resurrection. 8- So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it. That is, the weight of an ant, which is the smallest of ants. Muqatil said: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good in this world will see it in his book on the Day of Resurrection and be happy about it.
42:31: 31- And you will not escape Him on the earth meaning you will not escape Him by escaping on the earth or in the heavens if they were in it, rather what He has decreed for them of calamities will befall them. And you have besides God no protector who will befriend you and prevent from you what God has decreed nor helper who will help you from God’s punishment in this world or in the Hereafter.
42:32: Then He, the Most High, mentioned another of His great signs indicating His Oneness and the truth of His promise, saying: 32- And among His signs are the ships. Nafi’ and Abu Amr read the word al-jawari with the ya’ in the connected form, but in the pause, it is proven according to the original and deleted for the sake of alleviation. They are ships, the singular of which is jariya: meaning moving. In the sea like the flags meaning the mountains, the plural of alam which is the mountain. From this is the saying of al-Khansa’: And Sakhr is the one whom the guides follow, as if he were a flag with fire on its head. Al-Khalil said: Everything that is elevated among the Arabs is a flag. Mujahid said: Flags are palaces, the singular of which is flag.
42:33: 33- If He wills, He stills the wind. The majority read it with a hamza for yasha, and Warsh read it from Nafi' without a hamza. The majority read al-rih in the singular, and Nafi' read al-riyyah in the plural: meaning He stills the wind that carries the ships. fayzillan meaning the ships rawaakid meaning stationary and fixed on his back the sea. It is said that water became stagnant: it became still, and likewise the wind became stagnant and the ship became stagnant, and everything that is fixed in a place is stagnant. The majority read fayzillan with a fatha on the first lam, and Qatada read it with a kasra, which is a rare language. Indeed in that what was mentioned about the ships are signs great indications for every patient, grateful meaning for every one who is very patient in the face of affliction and very grateful for blessings. Qatrab said: The patient, grateful person is the one who is grateful when given something and is patient when tested. Awn ibn Abdullah said: How many are blessed but not grateful, and how many are afflicted but not patient.
42:34: 34- Or He destroys them for what they have earned is in apposition to He inhabits: meaning He destroys them by drowning, and what is meant is their people for what they have earned of sins. It was also said: For what they associated with God. The former is more appropriate, because both polytheists and non-polytheists perish at sea. It is said: He destroyed him: meaning He destroyed him. And He pardons many of its people by overlooking their sins and saving them from drowning. The majority of scholars read He pardons in the jussive mood as an apposition to the answer to the condition. Al-Qushayri said: There is a problem with this reading because the meaning is: If He wills, He can still the wind so those ships remain motionless, or He can destroy them for the sins of their people. It is not appropriate to connect He pardons to this, because the meaning becomes: If He wills, He pardons, and that is not the meaning. Rather, the meaning is to inform about the pardon without the condition of will. So it is in apposition to the jussive mood in terms of wording, not meaning. Some people read He pardons in the nominative case, and it is good in meaning. Abu Hayyan said: What he said is not good, because the meaning of the construction was not understood, and the meaning is: except that the Almighty destroyed some people and saved others by way of forgiving them. Al-A’mash read wa ya’fu in the nominative case, and some of the people of Medina read it in the accusative case, implying an after the waw as in the saying of Al-Nabigha: If Abu Qaboos perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred month will perish. And then you take the tail of a life that has no hump Install and take.
42:35: 35- "And those who dispute about Our verses know that they have no escape. The majority of reciters read ya'lam" in the accusative case. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a derivation. He said: The meaning of derivation is to change the conjunction of the word to the meaning. He said: This is because when it is not appropriate to conjoin "wa'lam" in the jussive mood with what precedes it, since the meaning would be: if He wills with knowledge, He shifted to conjoining the verbal noun of the verb that precedes it. This is only possible by implying "an" so that it is with the verb in the interpretation of a noun. From this are the two couplets of Al-Nabigha mentioned earlier. As Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Mubarrad and Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: This interpretation was objected to with something that is pointless. It was said that the accusative is in conjunction with an omitted explanation, and the meaning is: so that He may take revenge on them and he may know. Abu Hayyan objected to it by saying that it is an arrangement based on the condition of the destruction of a people and the salvation of a people, so it is not appropriate to estimate "so that He may take revenge on them. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read ya'lam" in the nominative case as a resumption, and this is a reading that is clear in meaning and clear in wording. It was read in the jussive mood in apposition to the jussive mood before it, meaning: And if He wills, He can bring together destruction, salvation, and warning. The meaning of there is no escape for them is that they have no escape or escaping, as stated by Qatrub. Al-Suddi said: they have no refuge, and it is taken from their saying the camel threw it hasa bihi haysa, meaning that it was thrown at him. And from this is their saying so-and-so turns away from the truth, meaning he deviates from it.
42:36: 36- Whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of worldly life. When God, the Almighty, mentioned the proofs of monotheism, He mentioned the aversion to this world: that is, whatever you have been given of wealth and abundance in provision is only a brief enjoyment lasting a few days, which will pass and vanish. Then He encouraged them to seek the reward of the Hereafter and the everlasting bliss that is with God, saying: And what is with God is better and more lasting. That is, what is with God of reward for acts of obedience and the recompense for them in Paradise is better and more lasting than the enjoyment of this world, because it is permanent and never ends, while the enjoyment of this world quickly ends. Then God, the Almighty, explained to whom this is for, saying: For those who have believed, that is, who were truthful and did what faith requires. And upon their Lord they rely. That is, they entrust their affairs to Him and rely on Him in all their affairs, and not on anyone else.
42:37: 37- And those who avoid the major sins and immoralities The relative pronoun is in the genitive case in apposition to those who believe or in place of it or in the accusative case with the omission: I mean, and the first is more deserving, and the meaning is: What is with God is better and more lasting for those who believe and for those who avoid it. What is meant by major sins are the major sins, and we have already explained its explanation in Surat An-Nisa. The majority of scholars read major sins in the plural, while Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read major in the singular, which conveys the meaning of major sins, because the addition to the genus is like the lam. Immoralities are among the major sins, but despite being described as immoral, it is as if they are above them, such as murder, adultery, and the like. Muqatil said: Immoralities are those that warrant the prescribed punishments. Al-Suddi said: It is adultery. And when they become angry, they forgive. That is, they overlook the sin that angered them, and they suppress their anger and attack the one who wronged them. Anger is singled out for forgiveness because its control over a person’s nature and its dominance over him is strong. According to Surat Al-Ghasb, no one forgives except the one whose breast God has expanded and whom He has singled out with the virtue of patience. For this reason, God, the Exalted, praised them by saying in Al Imran 3:And those who restrain anger. Ibn Zayd said: God divided the believers into two types: a type that forgives their oppressor, so He began by mentioning them, and a type that takes revenge on their oppressor, and they are the ones who will be mentioned.
42:38: 38- And those who responded to their Lord and established prayer meaning they responded to what He called them to and performed the obligatory prayer that He enjoined upon them. Ibn Zayd said: They are the Ansar in Medina who responded to the belief in the Messenger when he sent twelve leaders from among them before the migration, and they performed the prayer at its appointed times with its conditions and procedures. And their affair is by consultation among themselves meaning they consult among themselves and do not rush or take sides in their affairs. Shura is the source of consulting him like good report and remembrance. Ad-Dahhak said: It is their consultation when they heard of the appearance of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the arrival of the leaders to them when they agreed in the house of Abu Ayyub on belief in him and support for him. It was said that what is meant is their consultation in every matter that arises to them, so that none of them monopolizes an opinion over the other. How beautiful is what Bashar ibn Burd said: If the opinion reaches the level of advice, then seek the opinion of a sincere advisor or the advice of a firm person. Do not let consultation be a source of shame for you. The freshness of the edges is a source of strength for the coming ones. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to consult his companions in his affairs, and God Almighty commanded him to do so, saying, And consult them in the matter. We have already discussed consultation in Al Imran. And from what We have provided them they spend. That is, they spend it in the way of goodness and give it in charity to the needy.
42:39: Then the Almighty mentioned the group that takes revenge on those who wronged them, saying: 39- And those who, when they are wronged, defend themselves. That is, they are wronged by those who wronged them unjustly. The Almighty mentioned these victorious ones in a context of praise, just as He mentioned forgiveness in times of anger in a context of praise, because humiliation to those who wrong is not among the characteristics of those to whom God has given honor, as He said: To God belongs honor and to His Messenger and to the believers. So, taking revenge in times of wrong is a virtue, just as forgiveness in times of anger is a virtue. Al-Nakha’i said: They hated to humiliate themselves, lest the foolish ones become bold toward them.
42:40: But this waiting is conditional upon limiting oneself to what God has made for him and not exceeding it, as God the Almighty explained after this by saying: 40- And the recompense for an evil act is an evil act like it. Thus God the Almighty explained that justice in revenge is limiting oneself to equality, and this appears to be general. Muqatil, Al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa, and Sufyan said: This is specific to the one who has been wounded, who takes revenge on the one who wounded him by means of retaliation, and no one else. Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: It is the response to the ugly one, if someone says, May God disgrace you, he says, May God disgrace you, without transgressing. Calling the recompense an evil act is either because it harms the one it befalls or by way of similarity due to their similarity in form. Then, when God, the Almighty, made clear that the recompense for evil is a just and permissible reward, He explained the virtue of forgiveness, saying: But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation - his reward is due from God. That is, whoever pardons the one who wronged him and reconciles between him and his oppressor through forgiveness, that is, God, the Almighty, will reward him for that. He left the reward vague to magnify His status and draw attention to His majesty. Muqatil said: So pardon is one of the righteous deeds, and we have already explained this in Surah Al Imran. Then God, the Almighty, mentioned the oppressors’ abandonment of His love, which is the reason for victory and salvation, saying: Indeed, He does not like the wrongdoers, that is, those who initiate injustice. Muqatil said: “He means the one who initiates injustice, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said the same. It was also said that He does not like the one who transgresses in retaliation and oversteps the bounds, because overstepping the bounds is injustice.”
42:41: 41- And for him who retaliates after being wronged is a verbal noun added to the object: meaning after the oppressor has wronged him, and the lam is the lam of initiation. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is the lam of the oath, and the first is more appropriate. And min is the conditional and its answer for those there is no way with regard to accountability and punishment, and it is permissible for min to be the relative and the fa' entered into its answer to liken the relative to the conditional, and the first is more appropriate.
42:42: When God, the Almighty, denied the path to those who retaliated after being wronged, He explained who the path is against, saying: 42- The path is only against those who wrong people meaning, they transgress against them from the beginning. This is what most people said. Ibn Jurayj said: This is what they wrong them with polytheism that is contrary to their religion. And commit transgressions upon the earth without right meaning, they act with people and wealth without right. This is what most people said. Muqatil said: Their work with sins has made them miserable. It was also said that they act arrogantly and tyrannically. Abu Malik said: It is what the people of Mecca hope will be in Mecca other than Islam as a religion. The reference in His statement: Those is to those who wrong people, and it is the subject, and its predicate is For them is a painful punishment meaning, for them because of this, they will have a very painful punishment.
42:43: Then the Almighty encouraged patience and forgiveness, saying: 43- And for him who is patient and forgives meaning he is patient with the harm and forgives the one who wronged him and does not retaliate. The discussion of this lam and min is like the discussion of and for him who retaliates, that patience and forgiveness is for him who has resolved upon matters meaning that that is from him, so it was deleted because it is clear, as in their saying: Butter is one dirham Muqatil said: It is one of the things that God has commanded. Al-Zajjaj said: The patient will be rewarded for his patience, so the desire for reward is a more perfect resolve. Ibn Zayd said: All of this was abrogated by jihad and that it is specific to the polytheists. Qatada said: It is general, and it is apparent from the Qur’anic structure: And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no protector after Him meaning, he has no one to follow his guidance and support him. The apparent meaning of the verse is general. It was said that it is specific to the one who turned away from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and did not act upon what he called him to of belief in God and acting upon what he legislated, but the first is more appropriate. Ahmad, Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Mani', Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: Shall I not tell you of the best verse in the Book of God, which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) narrated to us: "And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much." And I will explain it to you, Ali: Whatever strikes you of sickness, punishment or affliction in this world - it is for what your hands have earned. And God is too generous to repeat the punishment upon you in the Hereafter. And whatever God pardons in this world - God is too generous to return it after His pardon. Abd ibn Humayd and At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Musa that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "No servant is afflicted with a calamity, or something greater or lesser than that, except due to a sin. And what God pardons is more." And he recited: And whatever strikes you the verse. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in al-Kafarāt, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn that some of his companions came to him and he had been afflicted with some physical ailment. He said, We are saddened by what we see in you. He said, Do not be sad about what you see, for what you see is a sin, and what God pardons is greater. Then he recited this verse, And whatever strikes you of disaster until the end. Ahmad narrated on the authority of Mu`awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say, Nothing befalls a believer in his body that harms him but that God expiates his misdeeds because of it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Bara’ that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, There is no stumble of the foot, no twitching of a vein, and no scratch of a stick except for what your hands have put forth, and what God pardons is greater. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement, and they will remain motionless on its back, he said, They will move and not flow in the sea. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, regarding his statement: {stagnant}, he said: standing, or destroys them he said: destroys them. An-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: “Zainab entered upon me while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was with me. She came to me and cursed me, but the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) stopped her, but she did not stop. He said to me: Curse her. So I cursed her until her saliva dried in her mouth, and the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) beamed with joy.” Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The two who curse each other, whatever they say, is at fault until the one who started it transgresses. Then he recited: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “When it is the Day of Resurrection, God will command a crier to call out: ‘Let those who have a reward from God stand up.’ None will stand up except those who pardoned in this world.” This is His statement: But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is due from God. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A crier will call out, ‘Whoever has a reward from God, let him enter Paradise’ twice. Then the one who pardoned his brother will stand up and God will say, ‘But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is due from God.’”
42:44: His statement: 44- And you will see the wrongdoers meaning the polytheists who denied the resurrection when they see the punishment meaning when they see the fire, and it was said that they see what God has prepared for them at death saying, ‘Is there any way to return?’ meaning is there a way to return to the world?
42:45: 45- And you will see them presented before it, humiliated by humiliation. That is, they are calm and humble when they are presented before the Fire because of the humiliation and disgrace that has befallen them. The pronoun in upon it refers to the torment and makes it feminine because the torment is the Fire. His statement they are presented is in the accusative case as a state because seeing is visual, and so is humiliated. “From humiliation” is related to humiliated, that is, because of it. They look from a hidden corner. “From” is the word that indicates the beginning of the goal: that is, their gaze will begin at the Fire. It is permissible for it to be a partial, and the hidden corner that hides its gaze is like the one who is patiently looking at a sword because of the humiliation, fear, and dread that have befallen them. Mujahid said: From a hidden corner means humbled. He said: They only look with their hearts because they will be gathered blind, and the eye of the heart is a hidden corner. Qatadah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, As-Suddi, and Al-Qurazi said: They steal glances from the intensity of fear. Yunus said: “The word ‘min’ in ‘min taraf’ has the same meaning as the preposition ‘ba’, meaning they look with a weak eye out of humiliation and fear. Al-Akhfash said the same: “And those who have believed will say, ‘Indeed, the losers are those who will have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.’” That is, those who are complete in loss are those who have combined the loss of themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. As for their loss of themselves, it is because they will be in the Fire, tormented by it. As for their loss of their families, it is because if they are with them in the Fire, they will not benefit from them, and if they are in Paradise, a barrier will separate them from them. It was said that the loss of families is that if they had believed, they would have family in Paradise from the wide-eyed houris. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers will be in a lasting punishment. This may be part of the words of the believers, or it may be part of the words of God, the Most High, meaning they will be in a permanent punishment that will not cease.
42:46: 46- And they had no protectors to aid them other than God meaning they had no helpers to ward off punishment from them, nor supporters to aid them in that situation other than God. Rather, He is the One who disposes of whatever He wills, and whatever He does not will, does not happen. And he whom God sends astray has no way meaning no path to take to salvation.
42:47: Then God, the Almighty, commanded His servants to respond to Him and warned them, saying: 47- Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from God which no one can repel. That is, respond to His call to you to believe in Him, His books, and His messengers before a day comes which no one can repel or repel. This means: before a day comes from God which no one can repel, or God does not repel it after He has decreed it for His servants and promised it to them. What is meant by this is the Day of Resurrection, or the Day of Death. You will have no refuge that Day to which you can resort, and you will have no denial, meaning denial. The meaning is: you will have no denial that Day, rather you will confess your sins. Mujahid said: And you will have no denier, meaning a supporter who will aid you. It was said that denier means denier, like pain means painful: that is, you will not find on that Day anyone to denounce the torment that will befall you. This was said by Al-Kalbi and others, but the first is more appropriate. Al-Zajjaj said: It means that they are not able to deny the sins that they are accused of.
42:48: 48- But if they turn away, then We have not sent you over them as a guardian meaning as a guardian who records their deeds until you hold them accountable for them, nor as an overseer over them. Upon you is only the conveyance meaning you are only responsible for conveying what you were commanded to convey, and nothing else is upon you. This was abrogated by the verse of the sword. And indeed, when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it meaning if We give him ease, health, and wealth and he rejoices in it out of arrogance. What is meant by mankind is the human race. For this reason, He said: And if evil befalls them meaning affliction, hardship, or sickness for what their hands have put forth of sins then indeed, man is ungrateful meaning he is very ungrateful for the blessings He bestowed upon him, not thankful for them. This is in consideration of the majority of the human race.
42:49: Then the Almighty mentioned the vastness of His kingdom and the effectiveness of His control, saying: 49- To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. That is, He has the right to dispose of them as He wills. There is none who can prevent what He gives, nor give what He prevents. He creates what He wills. “He gives to whom He wills female [children], and He gives to whom He wills males.” Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Malik, and Abu Ubaidah said: He gives to whom He wills females, but not males, and He gives to whom He wills males, but not females. It has been said that the definite article males is used to indicate their superiority over females. It could also be said that the precedence of females contradicts this, so the verse does not indicate any preference, but rather it is intended for another meaning. The honor of males is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: Men are in charge of women by [right of] what God has given them and other evidence indicating the honor of males over females. It has been said that females are given priority because of their large number in relation to males, and it has been said to please the hearts of their fathers, and it has been said for other reasons that there is no need to elaborate on.
42:50: 50- Or He pairs them, males and females meaning He brings together the females and the males and makes them mates, thus giving them both to some of His creation. Mujahid said: It is that a woman gives birth to a boy, then gives birth to a girl, then gives birth to a boy, then gives birth to a girl. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: It is that she gives birth to twins, a boy and a girl. Al-Qatibi said: Marriage here is combining sons and daughters. The Arabs say: I paired my camels, meaning I brought together the young and the old. The meaning of the verse is clearer than to differ on its like, for He, the Almighty, informed us that He gives females to some of His creation, and gives males to others, and brings together males and females. And He makes whom He wills barren meaning that neither a male nor a female is born to him. Barren is the one who does not give birth to children. It is said that a man is barren and a woman is barren. A woman is barren, and its root is to cut off. It is also said that women are barren, and from this is the saying of the poet: Women are barren, and they do not give birth to anything similar to it. Women are barren like it. He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful meaning He is All-Knowing and All-Powerful.
42:51: 51- And it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation meaning that it is not right for any human being to speak to God in any way except by revelation to him, inspiring him and casting that into his heart. Mujahid said: A whisper that He whispers into his heart. So it is an inspiration from Him, as He inspired the mother of Moses and Abraham in slaughtering his son. Or from behind a veil as He spoke to Moses, meaning that His speech is heard from where He cannot be seen. This is a metaphor for the state of a hidden angel who speaks to his confidants from behind a veil. Or He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, whatever He wills. That is, He sends an angel, and that angel inspires the messenger from among the humans by God’s command and facilitates whatever He wills to reveal to him. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that God’s speech to humans is either by inspiration that He inspires them, or He speaks to them from behind a veil as He spoke to Moses, or by an angel’s message to them. The meaning of the statement is: It is not for a human being that God should speak to him except that He reveals a revelation, or that He speaks to him from behind a veil, or that He sends a messenger. Whoever reads yursul in the nominative case means that He sends, so it is a beginning and a resumption. The majority read or yursul in the accusative case and fuyuhi in the accusative case, assuming that, and that and what it precedes are conjoined with wuhyan, and wuhyan is in the place of the adverbial, and the meaning is: except that he reveals or is sent. It is not correct to conjoin or yursul with that He speaks to him because the meaning becomes: It is not for a human being that God should send a messenger, which is corrupt in form and meaning. Other than this has been said to explain the reading of the majority, which is not without weakness. Nafi' read or yursul in the nominative case, and likewise fuyuhi with a sukoon on the ya' as the predicate of a deleted subject, and the meaning is: or that He sends, as al-Zajjaj and others said. The phrase Indeed, He is Most High, Most Wise is an explanation of what preceded it: that is, He is exalted above the attributes of imperfection, Wise in all His judgments. The commentators said: The reason for the revelation of this verse is that the Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why don’t you speak to God and look at Him if you are a prophet as Moses spoke to Him? So it was revealed.
42:52: 52- And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. That is, just as We revealed to the prophets before you, We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. What is meant by this is the Qur’an, and it was also said that it means prophethood. Muqatil said: It means revelation by Our command, and its meaning is the Qur’an, because one is guided by it, and in it is life from the death of disbelief. Then God, the Exalted, mentioned the description of His Messenger before He revealed it to him, saying: You did not know what the Book was, meaning what it was, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was illiterate and could neither read nor write. This is more miraculous and more indicative of the authenticity of his prophethood. The meaning of nor faith is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not know the details of the religious laws nor was he guided to their features. He specified faith as its head and foundation. It was also said that what is meant by faith here is prayer. This was held by a group of scholars, including the Imam of Imams Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah. He provided evidence for this by the words of God, the Exalted: And God would never let your faith go to waste, meaning prayer, so He called it faith. A group went to that God the Almighty did not send a prophet except that he believed in Him, and they said the meaning of the verse is: You did not know before the revelation how to recite the Qur’an nor how to call people to faith, and it was said that this was before puberty when he was a child in the cradle. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: It is with the deletion of an adjective: meaning, nor the people of faith, and it was said that what is meant by faith is the religion of Islam, and it was said that faith here is an expression of acknowledgment of everything that God has charged the servants with, But We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will meaning, but We made the spirit that We have revealed to you a light and a proof of monotheism and faith by which We guide whom We will of Our servants, and We direct them to the true religion, And indeed, you guide to a straight path. Qatada, Al-Suddi and Muqatil said: And indeed, you call to Islam, so it is the straight path. The majority read to guide in the active form, and Ibn Hawshab read it in the passive form. Ibn Al-Samifi’ read it with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the dal from ahda, and in the reading of Abi: And indeed, you call. 38- The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows. The adverbial phrase is in the accusative case without they speak, or without they own, and the description is in the accusative case as a state: meaning lined up, or as a source: meaning they will stand in rows. His saying they will not speak is in the accusative case as a state, or a resumption to confirm what came before it. There is a difference of opinion about the Ruh. Some say it is an angel greater than the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the mountains. It is also said that it is Gabriel, as stated by Al-Sha’bi, Ad-Dahhak, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr. It is also said that the Ruh is an army of God’s soldiers that are not angels, as stated by Abu Salih and Mujahid. It is also said that they are the noblest of the angels, as stated by Muqatil ibn Hayyan. It is also said that they are guardians over the angels, as stated by Ibn Abi Nujayh. It is also said that they are the sons of Adam, as stated by Al-Hasan and Qatadah. It is also said that they are the souls of the sons of Adam, standing in a row, and the angels standing in a row, and that is between the two blasts before they return to the bodies, as stated by Atiyyah Al-Awfi. It is also said that it is the Qur’an, as stated by Zayd ibn Aslam. His statement, except for he to whom the Most Gracious has given permission, may be a substitute for the pronoun they speak, or it may be in the accusative case based on the original exception. The meaning is: they do not intercede for anyone except for he to whom the Most Gracious has given permission to intercede, or they do not speak except for the right of he to whom the Most Gracious has given permission. And that person was among those who said correctly, as Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid said: correctly means truly. Abu Saleh said: There is no god but God. The root of correctness is correctness in speech and action. It was said that they do not speak: meaning the angels and the spirit who stood in a row in awe and reverence, except for those among them whom the Most Gracious has given permission to intercede, and they have spoken the truth. Al-Hasan said: The spirit will stand on the Day of Resurrection, and no one will enter Paradise except through the spirit, and no one will enter Hell except through deeds. Al-Wahidi said: They do not speak: meaning all of creation, except for those whom the Most Gracious has given permission, and they are the believers and the angels. He said: In this world, it is correct: meaning, he bore witness to the Oneness of God.
42:53: Then He explained the straight path by saying: 53- The path of God to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. This addition of the path to the noble name is a glorification of Him and an exaltation of His status that is not hidden. The meaning of To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is that He is the Owner of that and the One who controls it. Unquestionably, to God do all matters return, meaning that all the matters of creation will return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, not to anyone else. It contains a threat of resurrection that necessitates recompense. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, They look from a hidden corner, that he said: “Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid something similar. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka’b, that he said: “They steal glances at the Fire.” Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated from Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Among the blessings of a woman is her inception with a female child, because God said, ‘He grants to whom He wills female children and He grants to whom He wills males.’ Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, And He renders whom He wills barren, that he said: One who does not have children. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, regarding the verse, And it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation, that he said: Unless He sends an angel to reveal to him from Him, or inspires him and casts inspiration into his heart, or speaks to him from behind a veil. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, regarding the verse, And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command, that he said: The Qur’an. Abu Naim narrated in Al-Dala’il and Ibn Asakir on the authority of Ali who said: “It was said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Have you ever worshipped an idol?’ He said: ‘No.’ They said: ‘Have you ever drunk alcohol?’ He said: ‘No.’ I always knew that what they were doing was disbelief, but I did not know what the Book or faith was. And the Qur’an was revealed about this: ‘You did not know what the Book or faith was.’”
43:1: It is eighty-nine verses. Al-Qurtubi said: It is Meccan by consensus. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Surat Ha Mim Az-Zukhruf was revealed in Mecca. Muqatil said: Except for the words: And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers, meaning that it was revealed in Medina. His saying: 1- Ha Mim.
43:2: His saying: 2- “Ha-Mim. By the clear Book.” The discussion here in terms of grammar is like the discussion we presented in “Ya-Sin. By the Wise Qur’an.” If you make Ha-Mim an oath, then the waw is a conjunction, and if you do not make it an oath, then the waw is for the oath.
43:3: The answer to section 3 - Indeed, We made it.
