Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever makes the answer to and the book Ha Mim, as you say: It was revealed, by God, it is obligatory to stop at the clear book. The meaning of We made it is: We named it and described it, and for this reason it is transitive with two objects. Al-Suddi said: The meaning is that We sent it down as a Quran. Mujahid said: We said it. Sufyan al-Thawri said: We explained it in Arabic. Al-Zajjaj said the same: meaning it was sent down in the language of the Arabs, because every prophet sent down his book in the language of his people. Muqatil said: Because the language of the people of Paradise is Arabic. That you may understand, meaning We made that book an Arabic Quran so that you may understand it, comprehend its meanings, and encompass what is in it. Ibn Zayd said: So that you may reflect.
43:4: 4- And it is in the Mother of the Book meaning the Qur’an is in the Preserved Tablet with Us meaning with Us sublimely Wise high in status, perfectly composed, with no discrepancy or contradiction in it. The clause is in apposition to the clause being sworn by, and is included under the meaning of an oath, or it is a new sentence confirming what came before it. Al-Zajjaj said: The Mother of the Book is the origin of the book, and the origin of everything is its mother, and the Qur’an is established with God in the Preserved Tablet as He said: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an * in a Preserved Tablet. Ibn Jurayj said: What is meant by His statement and it is are the deeds of creation, such as faith and disbelief, obedience and disobedience. Qatadah said: He informed about its status, nobility and excellence: meaning if you deny it, O people of Mecca, then it is with Us, noble, lofty and perfectly composed, free from falsehood.
43:5: 5- Shall We then turn away from you the Reminder completely? It is said, I turned away from it and I harmed from it: if you left it and refrained from it, as said by Al-Farra', Al-Zajjaj and others. The accusative of safhan is a verbal noun, and it is said that it is a state, meaning: Shall We then turn away from you the Reminder completely? And safhan is the source of their saying: I turned away from it if you turned away from it, and that is because you turn your face and neck to it. What is meant by dhikr here is the Qur'an, and the question is for denial and rebuke. Al-Kisa'i said: The meaning is: Shall We then turn away from you the Reminder completely, so that you are neither admonished nor commanded? Mujahid, Abu Salih and Al-Suddi said: Shall We turn away the punishment from you and not punish you for your extravagance and disbelief? Qatadah said: The meaning is: Shall We destroy you and neither command you nor forbid you. It was narrated from him that he said: The meaning is: Shall We then withhold from sending down the Qur'an because you do not believe in it. It was said that the dhikr is the reminder, as if he said: Shall we leave your reminder ‘if you are a people who are extravagant?’ Nafi’, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read if you are with a kasra on in as a conditional and the consequence is omitted due to the indication of what preceded it. The rest read it with a fatha as a justification: that is, because you were a people immersed in extravagance and persisting in it. Abu Ubaid chose the fatha reading.
43:6: Then God Almighty consoled His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: 6- And how many prophets We sent among the former peoples. “How many” is a piece of information that means many, and the meaning is: How many prophets We sent among the previous nations.
43:7: 7- And no prophet came to them except that they mocked him like your people mocked you.
43:8: 8- So We destroyed those stronger than them in force. That is, We destroyed a people stronger than these people. The word forceful is in the accusative case as a specification or a state: that is, forceful. "And the example of the former peoples has passed." That is, they were mentioned in the Qur'an more than once. Qatada said: their punishment. It was also said: their description. The example is the description and the report. This is a severe threat because it implies that the former peoples were destroyed by denying the messengers, and these, if they continue to deny you and disbelieve in what you have brought, will perish like them.
43:9: 9- And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘The Exalted in Might, the Knowing created them.’ That is, if you ask these disbelievers from your people, who created these celestial and celestial bodies, they will acknowledge that God is their Creator and will not deny it. This is worse for their situation and more severe for their punishment, because they worshipped some of God’s creations and made them partners with Him. Rather, they turned to that which does not hear, see, benefit, or harm from among the creations, namely idols, and made them partners with God.
43:10: Then He, the Almighty, described Himself with what indicates the greatness of His blessings upon His servants and the perfection of His power over His creations, saying: 10- Who has made the earth a cradle for you. This is a new statement that is not connected to what preceded it. If it had been connected to what preceded it from the group of statements made by the disbelievers, they would have said Who has made the earth a cradle for us. A cradle is a mattress or a carpet, and its explanation has been presented. The majority read a cradle, while the Kufians read a cradle. “And He has made for you therein paths,” meaning roads that you take to wherever you want. It was said that it is a livelihood that you live by, that you may be guided by taking it to your goals and benefits.
43:11: 11- And He who sends down water from the sky in due measure meaning, according to need and as the public interest dictates. He does not send down more than you need, so that it destroys your crops, demolishes your homes, or drowns you, nor less than that, so that you need more. And according to what His will dictates regarding the provisions of His servants, by sometimes being generous and at other times being stingy. Then We revived thereby a dead land meaning, We revived thereby a land barren of vegetation. The majority of scholars read dead with a light double suffix. Isa and Abu Ja`far read it with a heavy double suffix. Thus will you emerge from your graves: meaning, like that revival of the earth by bringing forth its vegetation after it had been devoid of vegetation, you will be resurrected from your graves alive. Whoever is able to do this is able to do that. This has been explained previously in Al-`Imran and Al-`A`raf. The majority of scholars read you emerge in the passive form, while Al-A`mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, Al-Kisa`i, and Ibn Dhakwan, on the authority of Ibn `Amir, read it in the active form.
43:12: 12- And He who created in pairs all things What is meant by pairs here are the species. Saeed bin Jubair said: All species. Al-Hasan said: Winter and summer, night and day, the heavens and the earth, Paradise and Hell. It was also said: The pairs of animals, male and female. It was also said: The pairs of plants, like His statement: And We caused to grow therein of every beautiful pair and of every noble pair. It was also said: What man experiences of good and evil, faith and disbelief. The first is more appropriate. And He made for you of the ships and the grazing livestock that which you ride in the sea and on land: meaning that which you ride.
43:13: 13- That you may mount on their backs. The pronoun refers to what Abu Ubaid said. Al-Farra' said: He added the appearance to one because what is meant is the appearance of this type and the mount is the dominance: that is, that you may mount on the backs of the ships and livestock that you ride. Then remember the favor of your Lord when you are mounted on them, that is, this favor that He bestowed upon you of making that ship subservient to you on the sea and land. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: It is to say, Praise be to God who has provided me with this and carried me on it. "And say, 'Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us,'" that is, He has made this ship subservient to us. Ali ibn Abi Talib recited, "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us." Qatada said: He has taught you how to say when you ride. The meaning of "And we were not able to subdue it" is that we were not able to bear it. It is said, "He subdued this camel," if it could bear it. Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubaidah said: Muqarnayn ad-Da’ib two pairs of two equals, and it was said that they are similar to him in strength, from their saying he is the horn of so-and-so if he is similar to him in strength. Qatrib recited the words of Amr ibn Ma’di Karib: The tribes knew what was said to us in the calamities of our two horns Another said: You have ridden my difficult path, you are cowardly and wicked, but you are not able to face difficulties. What is meant by livestock here is camels in particular, and it was said that it means camels and cows, but the first is more appropriate.
43:14: 14- And indeed, to our Lord we will return. That is, we will return to Him. This is the complete statement to be said when riding an animal or a ship.
43:15: Then the Almighty returned to mentioning the disbelievers who were mentioned previously, and said: 15- And they assigned to Him a portion of His servants. Qatada said: That is, equal to Him, meaning what was worshipped besides God. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Mubarrad said: The portion here refers to daughters, and the portion among the Arabs refers to daughters. It is said that a woman has given birth to daughters, and from this is the saying of the poet: If a free woman is sufficient one day, it is no wonder that a free woman may be sufficient sometimes. The author of Al-Kashshaf considered the interpretation of the part as daughters to be an innovation in interpretation, and stated that it is a lie against the Arabs. The response to this is that it was narrated by Al-Zajjaj and Al-Mubarrad, who are the masters of the Arabic language and its preservers, and those who came after them are the ultimate in its knowledge. The interpretation of the part as daughters is supported by what will come in His statement: Or has He taken from what He creates daughters? and His statement: And when one of them is given the good report of what is set forth for the Most Merciful and His statement: And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females. It was said that what is meant by the recompense here are the angels, for they made them the sons of God, the Most High, as stated by Mujahid and Al-Hasan. Al-Azhari said: The meaning of the verse is that they have made for God an exaggerated portion of His servants. It was said that what is meant by ghansan here is the disbeliever, for he is the one who clearly denies the blessings of God upon him.
43:16: Then He denied this to them, saying: 16- Or has He taken for Himself daughters from among what He creates? This is a question of rebuke and rebuke. Or is the detached particle, and the meaning is: Has your Lord taken for Himself daughters and purified you with sons? So He made for Himself the preferred of the two types and for you the superior of them. It is said I purified him with such-and-such: meaning I preferred him with it, and I purified him with love: I made it pure for him. Similar to this verse is His statement: For you are the males and for Him are the females? * That is indeed an unfair division. And His statement, Then has your Lord purified you with sons? The phrase and purified you is conjoined with has taken and included with it under the denial.
43:17: Then he increased his rebuke and rebuke of them, saying: 17- And when one of them is given the good report of that which is presented to the Most Merciful as an example, meaning that what He made for the Most Merciful, glory be to Him, of Him having given Himself daughters. The meaning is that if one of them is given the good report that a daughter has been born to him, he becomes distressed and its effects are evident on him, which is the meaning of His statement: his face remains black, meaning his face becomes black because of the birth of a female, as there was no male birth in her place. and he is filled with grief, meaning he is very sad, full of grief, filled with it. Qatada said: Sad. Ikrimah said: Distressed, and it was said: silent. The phrase and he is filled with grief is in the accusative case as a state.
43:18: Then he increased his rebuke and reprimand of them, saying: 18- Or one who grows up in adornment and is not clear in dispute? The meaning of is raised is is brought up. Raising is nurturing, and adornment is decoration. Min is in the accusative case, with an implied meaning, conjoined with made. The meaning is: Or they made it for Him, glory be to Him, that he be brought up in adornment, while he is unable to take care of his own affairs, and when he is disputed, he is unable to establish his argument and refute what his opponent argues with due to his deficient mind and weak opinion. Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning of the verse is: Or they make for him one who grows up in adornment: meaning, grows up in adornment. The majority of scholars read yansha with a fatha on the ya' and a sukoon on the noon. Ibn Abbas, Al-Dahhak, Ibn Waththab, Hafs, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read it with a damma on the ya', a fatha on the noon, and a shaddah on the sheen. Abu Hatim preferred the first reading, and Abu Ubaid preferred the second. Al-Harawi said: The verb according to the first reading is intransitive, and according to the second, transitive. Meaning: He is raised and grows up in adornment. Qatada said: A woman rarely speaks with her argument without being spoken with an argument against her. Ibn Zayd and Al-Dahhak said: What grows up in adornment are their idols that they fashioned from gold and silver.
43:19: 19- And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females. Making here means saying and judging something, as you would say: I made Zayd the best of people, meaning I said that and judged him accordingly. The Kufians read servants in the plural, and Ibn Abbas read it the same way. The rest read with the Most Merciful with a silent nun. Abu Ubaid preferred the first reading because the chain of transmission is higher in it, and because God denied them when He said that they are the daughters of God, so He informed them that they are His servants. This reading is supported by His statement: Rather, they are honored servants. Abu Hatim preferred the second reading, and said: “The confirmation of this reading is His statement: ‘Indeed, those who are with your Lord…’” Then He rebuked and admonished them, saying: Bring them to witness their creation, meaning bring them to witness God’s creation of them. This is from witnessing, which means presence. This is a mockery and a mockery of them. The majority read ash-hadu as a question without waw. Nafi’ read ash-hadu. The majority read their testimony will be written with a damma on the superscript ta’, the passive voice of the verb, and the nominative case of their testimony. As-Salami, Ibn as-Sameefa’, and Hibaira on the authority of Hafs read it with a noon, the active voice of the verb, and the accusative case of their testimony. Abu Raja’ read their testimony in the plural, and the meaning is: We will write this testimony that they testified with in the register of their deeds so that we may reward them for it, and they will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection.
43:20: 20- And they say, 'If the Most Gracious had willed, we would not have worshipped them.' This is another form of their disbelief in God, which they used to mock and ridicule. Its meaning is: If the Most Gracious had willed, as you claim, we would not have worshipped these angels. This is a true statement intended to be false, and its explanation has already been mentioned in Al-An'am. So God, the Exalted, made clear their ignorance by saying, They have no knowledge of that. That is, they have no knowledge of what they said, that if God had willed that they not worship the angels, He would not have worshipped them. Rather, they spoke of that out of ignorance, and intended what they portrayed as true to be false, and they claimed that if He willed, He would be pleased. Then He made clear their lack of knowledge by saying, They are only guessing. That is, they are only lying in what they said and pretending to be false. It has been said that the reference in His saying, that, is to His saying, and they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Gracious, females. Qatada, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said it. Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: That is, they have no knowledge of worshipping idols. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that God created was the pen, and He commanded it to write down everything that will happen until the Day of Resurrection, and the Book is with it. Then he recited: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, sublime and wise. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar, on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: Shall We turn away from you the Reminder? He said: You would have liked to be forgiven, but you did not do what you were commanded to do. Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: “When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) traveled, he would mount his mount, then say: ‘Allahu Akbar’ three times, then say: ‘Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, for we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return.’” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: and we could not have subdued it, He said: With the ability to do so. And Abd bin Hamid narrated on his authority, Or one who grows up in adornment, he said: It refers to women. He distinguished between their attire and the attire of men and reduced them in inheritance and testimony and ordered them to sit and called them the ones who remained. And Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: I used to recite this letter, Who are the female servants of the Most Merciful, so I asked Ibn Abbas and he said: Servants of the Most Merciful? I said: It is in my copy of the Qur’an with the Most Merciful. He said: Erase it and write, Servants of the Most Merciful.
43:21: His statement: 21- Or did We give them a scripture before it? “Or is it the disconnected one?” That is, rather, did We give them a scripture before the Qur’an that they should worship other than God? So they hold fast to it. They take what is in it and use it as evidence and make it their proof. It is possible that Or is repeated for His statement, Bring them witness, so it is connected, and the meaning is, did they bring their creation to bear witness, or did We give them a scripture, etc. It was said that the pronoun in before it refers to their claim: That is, or did We give them a scripture before their claim that speaks of the truth of what they claim? The first is more appropriate.
43:22: Then the Almighty made it clear that they had no argument or doubt, but they followed their fathers in misguidance, so He said: 22- Rather, they said, ‘Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and we are, following in their footsteps.’ So they admitted that they had no basis except imitating their fathers, and the meaning of ‘upon a nation’ is ‘upon a way and a doctrine.’ Abu Ubaid said: It is the method and religion, and Qatada and others said the same. Al-Jawhari said: ‘Ummah means method and religion. It is said that someone has no nation, meaning he has no religion or sect. From this is the saying of Qays ibn al-Khatim: We were on the nation of our fathers and we follow the example of the first of the first And the other said: Are the nation and the unbelievers equal? Al-Farra and Qatrib said: In the direction of the Qiblah. Al-Akhfash said: In a straight line. He recited the words of Al-Nabigha: I swore and left no doubt for you. Can a slave be sinned if he is obedient? The majority read ummah with a dammah over the hamza, while Mujahid, Qatadah, and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz read it with a kasrah over it. Al-Jawhari said: "Ummah with a kasrah means blessing, and ummah is also a dialect for nation, and from it, Uday ibn Zayd said: Then after the farmer, the king and the nation, she showed them graves there.
43:23: Then the Almighty informed that other disbelievers had preceded them in this statement and said it, saying: 23- And thus We did not send before you a warner to any city except that its affluent said, ‘Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and we will certainly follow in their footsteps.’ Its affluent people are its rich and its leaders. Qatada said: Followers and followers. The meaning of guidance and imitation are close, and He singled out the affluent people to draw attention to the fact that luxury is the reason for neglecting consideration.
43:24: Then God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to respond to them, saying: 24- He said, ‘Even if I came to you with better guidance than what you found your fathers following.’ That is, would you follow your fathers even if I came to you with a religion better guided than the religion of your fathers? Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, say to them, Will you follow what you found your fathers following, even if I came to you with better guidance than it? The majority read, He said, ‘Or if I came to you,’ while Ibn ‘Amir and Hafs read, He said, ‘Or if I came to you,’ which is a narration of what happened between the warners and their al-Nas 114:that is, each of those warners said to his nation. It was said that both readings are a narration of what happened between the prophets and their people, as if he said: To every prophet say, as evidenced by his saying: They said, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent.’ This is one of the greatest proofs indicating the invalidity and ugliness of imitation, for these imitators in Islam only act upon the words of their ancestors and follow their traces and imitate them. So if the caller to the truth seeks to bring them out of misguidance or to prevent them from an innovation that they have held fast to and inherited from their ancestors without clear evidence or clear proof, but rather with mere ‘he said and it was said’ for a refuted doubt, a false proof and a false statement, they say what the affluent of these religions said: Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion and we are following in their footsteps, or with something that has a similar meaning. So if he says to them, The caller to the truth: The Islamic faith has united us and this Muhammadan religion encompasses us. God, and you, and your fathers before you, have not commanded us to worship except by His Book which He revealed to His Messenger and by what has been authenticated from His Messenger. It is the clarifier of the Book of God, the explainer of its meanings, the distinguisher between its clear and ambiguous verses. So come, let us refer what we dispute over to the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, as God has commanded us to do in His Book, in His saying: And if you disagree over anything, refer it to God and the Messenger. For referring to them is more guiding for us and you than referring to what your ancestors said and your fathers followed. They fled like wild beasts, and threw every stone and mortar at the one calling them to that, as if they had not heard the saying of God, the Most High: “The only statement of the believers, when they are called to God and His Messenger to judge between them, is to say, ‘We hear and we obey. ’” Nor His saying: “But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.” For The speaker said to them: This scholar whom you follow and whose sayings you follow is like you in that he worships according to the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and what is required of him is what is required of you. If he acts according to his opinion when he does not find evidence, then that is a concession for him and it is not permissible for anyone else to follow him in it, nor is it permissible for him to act according to it. They have found the evidence that he did not find, and here I am finding it for you in the Book of God, or in what is authentic from the Sunnah of His Messenger, and that is better guidance for you than what you found your fathers upon. They said: We will not act according to this and we will not listen to you or obey you. They found in their hearts the greatest difficulty in the ruling of the Book and the Sunnah, and they did not submit to that nor yield to it. Satan has given them a stick to lean on when they hear someone calling them to the Book and the Sunnah, and that is that they say: Our Imam whom we imitate and follow is more knowledgeable than you about the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger. This is because their minds have imagined someone they follow with a great imagination due to the advancement of the age and the large number of followers, and they did not know that this is refuted against them and pushed in their faces. If it were said to them that among the followers there is one who is greater in stature and older in age than your companion, then if the advancement of age and greatness of stature has an advantage that requires emulation, then come so that I may show you one who is older in age and more exalted in stature. If you refuse that, then here I am directing you to one who is greater in stature, more important, has more followers, and is older in age, and he is Muhammad ibn Abdullah, our Prophet and your Prophet, the Messenger of God to us and to you. So come, for this is his Sunnah present in the books of Islam and its records that all of this nation has received century after century and age after age. This is the Book of our Lord, the Creator of all, the Provider of all, and the Originator of all among us, present in every home and in the hand of every Muslim. It has not been subjected to change or alteration, addition or subtraction, distortion or falsification. We and you are among those who understand its words and comprehend its meanings. So come, let us take the truth from its source and drink the pure water from its spring, for it is more guidance than what you found your fathers upon. They said: Neither hearing nor obedience, either by the tongue of speech or by the tongue of The situation, so ponder and reflect on this if there remains in you any remnant of fairness, a branch of goodness, a shred of modesty, or a portion of religion. There is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty. I have explained this to the utmost in my book which I entitled The Etiquette of Request and the Ultimate Goal, so refer to it if you desire to dispel the darkness of fanaticism and for the clouds of imitation to dissipate for you.
43:25: 25- So We took vengeance upon them. That vengeance was what God inflicted upon the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud. So see how was the end of the deniers of those nations, for their traces are still present.
43:26: 26- And when Abraham said to his father and his people meaning, remember to them the time when he said to his father and his people who imitated their fathers and worshipped idols, Indeed, I am disassociated from what you worship. Disassociation is a verbal noun used to describe exaggeration, and it is used for singular, dual, plural, masculine, and feminine. Al-Jawhari said: And I disassociate myself from such-and-such, and I am disassociated from it and empty. It is not dual or plural because it is originally a verbal noun.
43:27: Then He excepted his Creator from innocence, saying: 27- Except He who created me, meaning He created me, for He will guide me, He will guide me to His religion and make me steadfast in the truth. The exception is either disconnected: meaning but He who created me, or connected from the generality of what, because they were worshipping God and idols, and His informing him that He will guide him is certainty due to his trust in God Almighty and the strength of his certainty.
43:28: 28- And made it a word lasting among his descendants. The pronoun in made it refers to His statement, except He who created me. It means monotheism, as if He said: And made the word of monotheism lasting among the descendants of Abraham, who are his offspring, so there will always be among them those who believe in the Oneness of God Almighty. The subject of made it is Abraham, as He commanded them to believe in monotheism and ordered them to adhere to it, as in His statement, And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons, and [so did] Jacob. It was also said that the subject is God Almighty, meaning that God Almighty made the word of monotheism lasting among the descendants of Abraham, and the descendants after him. Mujahid and Qatadah said: The word there is no god but God will remain among his descendants who worship God until the Day of Resurrection. Ikrimah said: It is Islam. Ibn Zayd said: The word is His statement, I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds. The phrase that they may return is an explanation for making it: that is, He made it lasting in the hope that those among them who associate others with God will return to it through the supplication of those who believe in the Oneness of God. It was said that the pronoun in perhaps they refers to the people of Mecca, meaning perhaps the people of Mecca will return to your religion, which is the religion of Abraham. It was also said that there is an inversion of the text, and the meaning is: for He will guide them, perhaps they will return, and He made it, etc. Al-Suddi said: perhaps they will repent, so they will return from what they are doing to the worship of God.
43:29: Then the Almighty mentioned His blessing upon the Quraysh and those who agreed with them from the disbelievers who were contemporary with them, saying: 29- Rather, You gave enjoyment to these and their fathers He moved away from the first statement to mention what He gave them enjoyment with of souls, families, wealth, and various blessings, and what He gave enjoyment to their fathers, and He did not hasten to punish them, so they were deceived by the respite and devoted themselves to desires until there came to them the truth meaning the Qur’an and a clear Messenger meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning of clear is the apparent and clear message, or one who made clear to them what they needed regarding the matter of religion, but they did not respond to him and did not act upon what was revealed to him.
43:30: Then the Almighty explained what they did when the truth came, saying: 30- And when the truth came to them, they said, ‘This is magic, and indeed, we are disbelievers in it.’ That is, they denied it. So they called the Qur’an magic and denied it. They looked down on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
43:31: 31- And they said, 'Why was this Qur'an not sent down to some great man from the two cities?' What is meant by the two cities is Makkah and Ta'if, and by the two men is Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah from Makkah, and Urwah ibn Mas'ud Al-Thaqafi from Ta'if. This is what Qatada and others said. Mujahid and others said: Utbah ibn Rabi'ah from Makkah, and Umair ibn Abd Yalil Al-Thaqafi from Ta'if. Other than that was said. The apparent meaning of the verse is that what is meant is a man from one of the two cities who was of great status, wealthy, and a leader among his people. The meaning is that if it were the Qur'an, it would have been sent down to some great man from the leaders of the two cities.
43:32: So God, the Exalted, answered them by saying: 32- Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? Meaning prophethood or something more general than it, and the question is for denial. Then He explained that He, the Exalted, is the One Who apportioned among them what they need to live on in worldly matters, saying: We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We did not delegate that to them, and no one among the servants has the right to control anything, rather the judgment belongs to God alone. And if God, the Exalted, is the One Who apportioned their provisions among them and raised the ranks of some over others, then how can they not be content with His apportionment in the matter of prophethood and delegating it to whomever He wills from among His creation? Muqatil said: He says, Do they have in their hands the keys to the message so they can place them wherever they wish? The majority of people read their livelihood in the singular, while Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ibn Muhaisin read their livelihood in the plural. And the meaning of We raised some of them above others in degrees is that He distinguished between them, making some better than others in this world in terms of provision, leadership, strength, freedom, intellect, and knowledge. Then He mentioned the reason for raising the degrees of some in this world in terms of provision, leadership, strength, freedom, intellect, and knowledge. Then He mentioned the reason for raising the degrees of some over others, saying: That some of them may take others for service, meaning that some of them may use others, so the rich may use the poor, the leader the subordinate, the strong the weak, the free the slave, the intelligent the one who is below him in intellect, and the learned the ignorant. This is the case in most of the conditions of the people of this world, and through it their interests are fulfilled, their livelihood is regulated, and each of them reaches what he wants, for every worldly craft is excelled by some people and not others, so He made some people need others in order to achieve sympathy between them in worldly pleasures, and this one needs this one, this one makes this one, and this one gives this one. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: We subjected Our slaves and servants so that the rich subject the poor, so that some of them would be a means of livelihood for others. Qatada and Al-Dahhak said: So that some of them would own others. It was also said that it is mockery which means ridicule. Although this is in accordance with the linguistic meaning, it is far from the meaning of the Qur’an and contradicts what is intended by the context. And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate. What is meant by mercy is what God has prepared for His righteous servants in the Hereafter. It was also said that it refers to prophethood because it is what is meant by the mercy mentioned earlier in His statement: Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? There is nothing to prevent the meaning of everything that is called mercy, either comprehensively or as an alternative. The meaning of what they accumulate is what they accumulate of money and other worldly goods.
43:33: Then the Almighty explained how insignificant this world is to Him, saying: 33- And had it not been that mankind would be one community meaning, had it not been that they would unite in disbelief out of inclination towards this world and its adornments, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver. The pronoun in their houses is plural and in yakfir is singular, considering the meaning and wording of min, and for their houses is a badal ishtiml from the relative pronoun, and saqf is the plural of saqf. The majority of scholars read it with a damma on the seen and the qaf, like karhan and rahn. Abu Ubaidah said: There is no third option for them. Al-Farra’ said: It is the plural of saqif, like katheer and katheer, and ragheef and raghaf. It was said that it is the plural of suqoof, so it is a plural of a plural. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a fatha on the seen and a sukoon on the qaf, singular, and its meaning is plural because it is for the genus. Al-Hasan said: The meaning of the verse is: Had it not been that people would all disbelieve because of their inclination towards this world and their abandonment of the Hereafter, We would have given them in this world what We have described, because this world is insignificant to God. Most of the commentators said: Ibn Zayd said: Had it not been that people were one nation in seeking this world and choosing it over the Hereafter. Al-Kisa’i said: “The meaning is, had it not been that there were rich and poor among the disbelievers, and the same among the Muslims, We would have given the disbelievers this worldly life because of its insignificance. “And stairways by which they ascend.” Stairways are the plural of mi’raj, and mi’raj is a ladder. Al-Akhfash said: “If you wish, you can make the singular mi’raj and mi’raj like marqah and marqah. The meaning is: So We made for them stairways of silver by which they ascend.” That is, they ascend and climb the stairs. It is said, I ascended the roof of the house, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: We have reached the sky in glory, pride and supremacy, and we hope for more glory than that. Any elevator.
43:34: 34- And for their houses, doors and couches. That is, We made for their houses doors of silver and couches of silver. Upon them they will recline. That is, on couches, which is the plural of bed. It was also said that it is the plural of family, so it is the plural of plural. Reclining and leaning on something means leaning on something. From this, I lean on it and he leaned on something, so he is leaning. The place is a place to lean on. Decoration is gold. It was also said that adornment is more general than it being gold or something else. Ibn Zayd said: It is what people have in their homes of furnishings and furnishings. Al-Hasan said: Engravings and its origin is adornment. It is said that the house was decorated, meaning that I adorned it.
43:35: 35- And the accusative of Zukhruf is by an implied verb: meaning, And We made for them, along with that, an adornment, or by removing the preposition: meaning, doors and thrones of silver and gold, so when the preposition was deleted, it became accusative. Then the Almighty informed that all of that is only enjoyed in this world, so He said: And all of that is but the enjoyment of worldly life. The majority of scholars read Lamma with a light Lamma, while Asim, Hamza, and Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Amir, read it with a heavy Lamma. According to the first reading, Inna is the light Inna from the heavy Lamma. According to the second reading, it is the negative Lamma and in the meaning of illa: meaning, all of that is nothing but something enjoyed in this world. Abu Raja' read it with a kasra on the Lamma from Lamma, on the basis that the Lamma is for the reason and Ma is a relative pronoun and the pronoun is deleted: meaning, for that which is enjoyment. And the Hereafter is with your Lord for the righteous meaning, for those who avoid polytheism and sins and believe in God alone and do what He commands, for it is everlasting and does not perish and its bliss is everlasting and does not disappear. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, he said: upon a religion. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on his authority, and made it an enduring word, he said: There is no god but God. In his descendants, he said: the descendants of his son Ibrahim. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he was asked about the statement of God, Why was this Qur’an not sent down to a great man from the two cities? What were the two cities? He said: At-Ta’if and Mecca. It was said: Who were the two men? He said: Umair ibn Mas’ud and the best of Quraysh. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority, he said: By the two cities he means Mecca and At-Ta’if, and the great ones are Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah Al-Qurashi and Habib ibn Umair Al-Thaqafi. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: They mean more noble than Muhammad, for Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah from the people of Mecca and Mas’ud ibn Amr Al-Thaqafi from the people of At-Ta’if. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: Had it not been that mankind would be one community 10:17, meaning: Had it not been that We would make all of mankind disbelievers, I would have made the houses of the disbelievers have roofs of silver, and stairways of silver, which are stairs on which they ascend to the rooms, and beds of silver, and decorations: which are gold. At-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it, and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: If the world weighed in the sight of God the wing of a mosquito, He would not have given a disbeliever a sip of water from it.
43:36: His saying: 36- And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious It is said I went to the Fire: I intended to go to it, and I turned away from it: I turned away from it, just as you say: I turned to so-and-so and turned away from him, and I inclined towards him and turned away from him. This is what Al-Farra’, Al-Zajjaj, Abu Al-Haytham, and Al-Azhari said. So the meaning is: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse is that whoever turns away from the Qur’an and the wisdom in it to the falsehoods of the misguiders, God will punish him with a devil whom He will appoint for him until he misguides him and stays with him like a companion, so he will not be guided, as a recompense for his preference for falsehood over the clear truth. Al-Khalil said: “Blindness is weak vision, and from it: What a fine young man he is, who has dinner by the light of his fire when the wind blows and the place is barren. It appears that the meaning of the verse is the intention to go to the fire, not to look at it with weak eyesight, as Al-Khalil said. This is evidence of what we mentioned before, that it comes with the meaning of intention and with the meaning of turning away. This is what Al-Khalil recited, citing it as evidence for what he said about Al-Hutay’ah’s saying: When you come to him and dine by the light of his fire, you will find the best fire with him and the best stove. It appears that its meaning is: aim for the light of his fire, do not look at it with weak eyesight. It can be said that the meaning of this couplet is the exaggeration in the light of the fire and its brightness, such that the viewer does not see it except as someone whose eyesight is blind looks due to the weakness that befalls his eyes when he sees it due to the greatness of its fuel. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: The meaning of “and whoever lives” is whoever whose eye is darkened, which is similar to what Al-Khalil said, and this is according to the reading of the majority, and whoever lives with a damma on the shin from asha ya’shu. Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah read and whoever lives with a fatha on the shin, it is said that a man is blind, ya’shu, if he goes blind, and from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: She saw a man who was absent-minded, of different appearance, blind and deaf. Al-Jawhari said: Al-‘Asha is a shortened verbal noun derived from Al-A’sha, which means the one who cannot see at night and sees during the day, and a woman is blind. It was read as Ya’sha with a waw, as min is a relative pronoun that does not include the meaning of a condition. The majority read Naqid Lahu Shaytan with a noon, and Al-Salami, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ya’qub, and Asmah from Asim, and Al-A’mash read it with a lower form as an active participle. Ibn Abbas read it with a lower form as a passive participle, and raised Shaytan as a deputy. So he is his companion, meaning he is constantly with him and does not leave him, or he is constantly with Satan and does not leave him, rather he follows him in all his affairs and obeys him in everything he whispers to him.
43:37: 37- And indeed, they avert them from the path. That is, the devils whom God appoints for everyone who is blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, as is the meaning of avert them. That is, they stand between them and the path of truth and prevent them from it, and they whisper to them that they are on the right path until they think that what they whisper is true. This is the meaning of His statement, And they think that they are guided. That is, the disbelievers think that the devils are guided, so they obey them, or the disbelievers think, because of that whispering, that they are guided in themselves.
43:38: 38- Until when he comes to Us The majority read it in the dual form: meaning the disbeliever and the devil who is accompanying him. Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it in the singular: meaning the disbeliever or each one of them came. The disbeliever said addressing the devil Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts meaning the distance between the east and the west, so the east was preferred over the west. Muqatil said: The disbeliever wishes that there was between them the distance of the east of the longest day of the year than the east of the shortest day of the year, but the former is more appropriate, and Al-Farra' said the same. Then what an evil companion the one specifically blamed is omitted, meaning you, O devil.
43:39: 39- And nothing will benefit you today This is a narration of what will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection for you were unjust meaning because of your wronging yourselves in this world. It was said that if is a substitute for today because it becomes clear on that day that they were unjust to themselves in this world. The majority of scholars read that you will share in the punishment with a fatha on an as it and what follows it are in the nominative case as subject: meaning, your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you today. The commentators said: Nothing of the punishment will be lightened for them because of their sharing, because each of the disbelievers and devils has the greater share of it. It was said that it is an explanation for the denial of benefit: meaning, because it is your right to share, you and your peers, in the punishment, just as you shared in its cause in this world. This meaning is strengthened by the reading of Ibn Amir, with a kasra on in, despite his disagreement.
43:40: Then the Almighty mentioned that the call and preaching do not benefit the one who has already been doomed to misery, so He said: 40- Then can you make the deaf hear or guide the blind? The hamza is to negate the amazement: meaning, you cannot do that, so do not be distressed if they disbelieve. In it is consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informing him that no one is able to do that except God Almighty. His statement: And whoever is in manifest error is in apposition to the blind: meaning, you do not guide the one who is like that. The meaning of the verse is that these disbelievers are like the deaf who do not understand what you have brought, and like the blind who do not see it, so their excess in misguidance and their ability to be ignorant.
43:41: 41- If We take you away with death before the punishment descends upon them, then We will take retribution from them either in this world or in the Hereafter. It was said that the meaning is: We will expel you from Mecca.
43:42: 42- Or We show you that which We have promised them of the punishment before your death for indeed, We are over them with power whenever We will We will punish them. Many of the commentators said: God showed him that on the Day of Badr. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: It is regarding the people of Islam, meaning the trials that occurred after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There was a severe trial after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God honored His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He did not show him anything of that in his nation, but the first is more appropriate.
43:43: 43- So hold fast to what has been revealed to you meaning the Qur’an, even if someone denies it. Indeed, you are on a straight path meaning a clear path. The sentence is an explanation for his saying: So hold fast.
43:44: 44- And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people. That is, the Qur’an is an honor for you and your people from Quraysh, as it was revealed to you while you were one of them, in your language and theirs. Similar to this is His statement: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance. It was said that it is an explanation for you and your nation regarding what you have a need for. It was said that it is a reminder by which you remember the matter of religion and learn by it. And you will be questioned. About the honor that God has given you. This is what Az-Zajjaj, Al-Kalbi, and others said. It was said that they will be questioned about what they are required to do in it and act upon it.
43:45: 45- “And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: ‘Did We appoint other gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?’” Az-Zuhri, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Zayd said: Gabriel said that to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when he was taken on the Night Journey al-Isra. The intended meaning was to ask the prophets at that time when he met them, and this is what a group of the early Muslims said. Al-Mubarrad, Az-Zajjaj, and a group of scholars said: The meaning is: Ask the nations We have sent. This is what Mujahid, As-Suddi, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ata’, and Al-Hasan said. The meaning of the verse, according to both opinions, is to ask them: Did God permit the worship of idols in any religion, and did He permit that for any of them? The intended meaning is to rebuke the polytheists of Quraysh, saying that what they were doing was not mentioned in any of the religious laws. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Makhzumi that the Quraysh said: Allocate a man for each of the companions of Muhammad. So they allocated Talha ibn Ubaydullah to Abu Bakr. Talha came to him while he was among the people and Abu Bakr said: What do you call me to? He said: I call you to the worship of al-Lat and al-Uzza. Abu Bakr asked: And what is al-Lat? He said: The sons of God. He said: And what is al-Uzza? He said: The daughters of God. Abu Bakr said: And who is their mother? Talha remained silent and did not answer him. So he said to his companions: Answer the man. The people remained silent. Talha said: Get up, Abu Bakr, I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Then God revealed: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful… [al-Bukhari and Muslim] It is proven in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere that with every human being there is a companion from the jinn. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali regarding the words: But if We take you away, he said: His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has gone and his vengeance against his enemy remains. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {Or We shall show you that which We promised them}, he said: On the Day of Badr. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated through various chains of narration on his authority regarding his statement: {And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people}, he said: An honor for you and your people. Ibn Adi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas, they said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to present himself to the tribes in Mecca and promise them victory. When they said: Who will rule after you? He would hold back and not answer them because he was not commanded to do anything about that until the verse {And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people} was revealed. So after that, whenever he was asked, he would say to the Quraysh, but they would not answer him until the Ansar accepted him on that basis. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers}, he said: Ask those to whom We sent before you of Our messengers.
43:46: When God Almighty informed His Prophet that He would take revenge on his enemy and mentioned the agreement of the prophets on monotheism, He followed it by mentioning the story of Moses and Pharaoh and explaining the punishment that befell Pharaoh and his people, saying: 46- And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs - the nine of which were explained above - to Pharaoh and his chiefs - the chiefs: the nobles and he said, ‘Indeed, I am the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds’ - He has sent me to you.
43:47: 47- So when he brought them Our signs, at once they laughed at them in mockery and derision, and in response to the sudden if, because the meaning is: surprise them at the time of their laughter.
43:48: 48- And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its sister, meaning that each of the signs of Moses was greater than the one before it, and greater in value, while the one before it was great in itself. It was said that the meaning is that the first requires knowledge and the second requires knowledge, so if the second is added to the first, the clarity increases. The meaning of brotherhood between the signs is that they are similar and proportionate in their indication of the truth of Moses’ prophethood, as it is said that this is the companion of this, meaning that they are two companions in meaning. The phrase except that it is greater than its sister is in the genitive case as an attribute of the sign. It was said that the meaning is that each of the signs, if it is alone, the one who thinks will think that it is greater than all the other signs. Similar to this is the saying of the one who says: Whoever receives from them, say, I have met their master, like the stars that a traveler carries. And We seized them with punishment that perhaps they would return, meaning because of their denial of those verses. The punishment is what is mentioned in His statement: And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and loss of fruits, and the Almighty explained that the reason for His seizing them with punishment was the hope that they would return.
43:49: And when they witnessed the clear signs and evident proofs that he had brought to them, they thought that it was a kind of magic. 49- "And they said, 'O magician!'" They used to call scholars magicians and they would revere and honor magicians. Magic was not considered a derogatory term among them. Al-Zajjaj said: They addressed him with the same name they had previously called him a magician. "Call upon your Lord for us according to what He has covenanted with you." That is, according to what you have told us of His covenant with you. "If we believe, the punishment will be removed from us." It was said that what is meant by the covenant is prophecy, and it was said that the call is answered in general. "Indeed, we are [rightly] guided." That is, if the punishment that has befallen us is removed from us, then we are guided in the future and believe in what you have brought.
43:50: 50- So when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their covenant. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So Moses called upon his Lord, and We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their covenant. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So Moses called upon his Lord, and He removed the punishment from them. So when the punishment was removed from them, they were surprised at the time of their breaking the covenant that they had made upon themselves of guidance. Breaking: violating.
43:51: 51- And Pharaoh called out to his people, It was said that when he saw those signs, he feared that the people would turn to Moses. So he gathered them and called out in his voice among them, or ordered a crier to call out, saying: O my people, is not mine the kingdom of Egypt? No one would dispute it with me and no one would oppose me? And these rivers flow beneath me, meaning from beneath my palace, meaning the Nile. Qatada said: The meaning is: They flow before me. Al-Hasan said: They flow at my command: meaning they flow under my command. Ad-Dahhak said: By the rivers he meant the leaders, chiefs, and tyrants, and that they march under his banner. It was also said that by the rivers he meant wealth, but the first is more appropriate. The waw in this is a conjunction to the kingdom of Egypt, and it flows in the accusative case as a state, or it is the waw of state. The demonstrative pronoun is the subject, and the rivers are its description, and flows is its predicate. The sentence is in the accusative case, Do you not see that and use it as evidence of the strength of my kingdom, the greatness of my power, and the weakness of Moses in resisting me.
43:52: 52- "Or am I better than this who is humiliated? Am is the disconnected particle understood by bal" which indicates confusion without the hamza which indicates denial: that is, rather, I am better. Abu Ubaidah said: Am means "rather," and the meaning is: Pharaoh said to his al-Nas 114:Rather, I am better. Al-Farra' said: If you wish, you can make it from the interrogative particle that is made by "am" because of its connection to a statement before it. It was said that it is redundant. Abu Zaid narrated from the Arabs that they make "am" redundant, and the meaning is: I am better than this. Al-Akhfash said: There is an ellipsis in the statement, and the meaning is: Do you not see or do you not see? Then he began and said "I am better." It was narrated from Al-Khalil and Sibawayh similar to what Al-Akhfash said. This is supported by the fact that Isa Al-Thaqafi and Ya'qub Al-Hadrami stopped at "am with the understanding of am tabsiroun," so it was deleted because the first indicates it. Based on this, "am" is connected, not disconnected, and the first is more appropriate. Similar to it is the saying of the poet whom Al-Farra' recited: She looked like the sun's horn in the splendor of the morning, and her image, or are you more beautiful in the eye? Rather, you are. Al-Farra’ narrated that some of the reciters read, Am I not better than this one who is humiliated? meaning, weak, contemptible, and humiliated in his own right, with no honor. “And he can hardly articulate” the words because of the knot in his tongue, and this was explained previously in Surah Taha.
43:53: 53- Why were not bracelets of gold bestowed upon him? That is, why was he not adorned with bracelets of gold if he was of high standing? When a man among them was blackened, they would adorn him with a bracelet of gold and put a necklace of gold around his neck. The majority of scholars read aswarah as the plural of aswarah, the plural of swar. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' said: The singular of asawarah, asawair, and asawir is aswar, which is a variant of swar. Hafs read asawir as the plural of swar, Abu read asawir, and Ibn Mas'ud read asawir. Mujahid said: When they blackened a man, they would adorn him with two bracelets and put a necklace of gold around him as a sign of his high standing. Or the angels came with him in pairs is in apposition to was thrown, and the meaning is: Why did not the angels come with him one after the other, in pairs, if he was truthful, to aid him in his affairs and bear witness to his prophethood? So the accursed one made his people believe that the messengers must be in the form of giants and surrounded by angels.
43:54: 54- So he made his people foolish, so they obeyed him. That is, he made them obey him out of ignorance and foolishness with his words, his trickery, and his deception. They obeyed him in what he commanded them, and they accepted and denied Moses. Indeed, they were a wicked people. That is, they disobeyed God. Ibn al-A’rabi said: The meaning is, So he made his people foolish, so they obeyed him out of their foolishness and weak minds. It is said, Farah made him foolish, meaning it disturbed him. Istighah made him foolish means it made him angry. And from this is the verse, And do not let those who have no certainty make you foolish. It is also said, He made his people foolish, meaning he found them to be weak-minded. He made his people foolish and subdued them until they followed him.
43:55: 55- So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them. The commentators said: They angered Us, and retribution means anger. It was also said that it means intense anger, and it was also said that it means wrath. It was also said that it means: They angered Our messengers. Then He explained the punishment by which the retribution was inflicted, saying: So We drowned them all in the sea.
43:56: 56- So We made them predecessors meaning an example for those who do what they do among the disbelievers, deserving of punishment. The majority of scholars read salfan with a fatha on the seen and the lam, the plural of salif like khidam and khadam, rasad and rasid, haras and haris. It is said salaf yaslaf if he advances and goes ahead. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj said: We made them predecessors so that others would take heed from them. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read salfan with a damma on the seen and the lam. Al-Farra’ said: It is the plural of salif, like surar and sarir. Abu Hatim said: It is the plural of salaf like khashab and khashab. Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Alqama, Abu Wa’il, Al-Nakha’i, and Hamid ibn Qays read it with a damma on the seen and a fatha on the lam, the plural of salfa, which is the advanced group like ghurf and ghurfa. This is what Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said. And an example for others meaning a lesson and admonition for those who come after them, or a strange story that is used as proverbs. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, {and he could hardly make it clear}, that he said: Moses had a lisp in his tongue. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, {And when they angered Us}, that he said: They angered Us. They also narrated on his authority, {And when they angered Us}, that he said: They angered Us. And regarding the statement of God, {And before}, he said: Different desires. Ahmad, al-Tabarani, al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you see God giving a servant whatever He wills while he persists in his sins, then that is only to lure him in. And he recited, {And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all.} Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: I was with Abdullah and he mentioned sudden death, so he said: It is a relief for the believer and a grief for the disbeliever. {And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them.}
43:57: When God the Almighty said: "And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: 'Did We make gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?'" The polytheists clung to the matter of Jesus and said: Muhammad only wants us to take him as a god as the Christians took Jesus, son of Mary. So God revealed 57- And when the son of Mary is cited as an example. This is what Qatada and Mujahid said. Al-Wahidi said: Most of the commentators agree that this verse was revealed during the argument of Ibn Al-Za'bari with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when the verse was revealed: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hellfire. Ibn Al-Za'bari said: I have argued with you, by the Lord of the Ka'ba. Didn't the Christians worship Christ, the Jews worship Ezra, and the sons of Malih worship the angels? So he rejoiced at what he said, so God the Almighty revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. And this verse mentioned here was revealed. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Anbiya. It is no secret that what Ibn Al-Zubayri said is fundamentally invalid and completely false. God the Almighty said: You and what you worship, and He did not say and whom you worship so that rational beings such as the Messiah, Ezra, and the angels would be included in that. When your people, O Muhammad, turn away from that parable, meaning they make a commotion and shout out in joy at that parable. What is meant by his people here are the infidels of Quraysh. The majority of scholars read yasdun with a kasra on the sad, while Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, and Al-Kisa'i read it with a damma. Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra', Al-Zajjaj, and Al-Akhfash said: They are two dialects and their meanings are: they make a commotion. Al-Jawhari said: Sadda yasdud sadidan means to make a commotion. It was also said that with a damma it means turning away and with a kasra from noise, as stated by Qatrab. Abu Ubaid said: If it was from turning away from the truth, He would have said: When your people turn away from it. Al-Farra' said: They are the same from it and from it. Abu Ubaidah said: Whoever says Damma means they are just, and whoever says Kasra means they are noisy.
43:58: 58- And they said, 'Are our gods better, or is he?' That is, are our gods better, or is the Messiah? As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: They argued with him and said, 'If everyone who worships other than God is in the Fire, then we are satisfied that our gods are with Jesus, Ezra, and the angels.' Qatada, meaning Muhammad, said, 'Are our gods better, or is Muhammad?' This is strengthened by Ibn Mas'ud's reading: 'Are our gods better, or is he?' The majority of reciters read it with a simplified second hamza, while the Kufians and Ya'qub read it with a full hamza. They only set forth this example for you about Jesus to argue with you, meaning they set forth this example for you about Jesus only to argue with you, with jiddān being in the accusative case as a cause, or mujadīlin as a verbal noun in the place of a circumstantial adverbial. Ibn Muqsim read jiddāl, Rather, they are a quarrelsome people, meaning they are very quarrelsome, very stubborn, and very argumentative.
43:59: Then the Almighty made clear that Jesus is not a Lord, but rather a servant of His servants whom He chose for His prophethood, saying: 59- He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor with what We honored him with and made him an example for the Children of Israel meaning a sign and a lesson for them through whom they would know the power of God Almighty, for he was without a father, and he would bring the dead back to life, and heal the blind and the leper, and every sick person.
43:60: 60- And if We willed, We could have made from you angels on the earth, succeeding you. That is, if We willed, We could have destroyed you and made in your place angels on the earth, succeeding you. Al-Azhari said: And from can be used for a substitute, as in His statement, We would have made from you, meaning in place of you. It was also said that the meaning is: If We willed, We could have made angels from among the children of Adam. The first is more appropriate. The meaning of the verse is: If We willed, We could have settled the angels on the earth, and there is no honor in Our settling them in the heavens so that they would be worshipped. It was also said that the meaning of succeed is that they succeed one another.
43:61: 61- And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour. Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Qatadah said: What is meant is the Messiah, and his emergence is one of the signs that indicate the arrival of the Hour, as he is one of its portents, because God, the Exalted, will send him down from the sky shortly before the Hour is complete, just as the emergence of the Antichrist is one of the signs of the Hour. Al-Hasan and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: What is meant is the Qur’an, because it indicates the nearness of the Hour, and through it its time, horrors, and conditions are known. It was also said that the meaning is that the emergence of the Messiah without a father and his reviving the dead is evidence of the truth of the Resurrection. It was also said that the pronoun refers to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, but the former is more appropriate. The majority of scholars read it as a verbal noun, making the Messiah a scholar, as an exaggeration of the knowledge that will come about when he descends. Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Abu Malik al-Ghifari, Qatadah, Malik ibn Dinar, al-Dahhak, and Zayd ibn Ali read it with the fat-ha on the ‘ayn and the lam, meaning the sign by which the Hour will be known. So have no doubt about it, meaning do not doubt its occurrence and do not deny it, for it will inevitably happen. And follow me - this is a straight path, meaning follow me in what I command you of Tawhid and the invalidity of polytheism, and the obligations that God has imposed upon you. This is what I command you to do of Tawhid and the invalidity of polytheism, and the obligations that God has imposed upon you. This is what I command you to do and call you to - a straight path that leads to the truth. The majority of scholars read it by deleting the ya’ from atabi’un when connected and when stopping. They also read it by deleting it in both cases in ata’iyun. Ya’qub read it by affirming it when connected and when stopping in both. Abu Amr read it, and this is a narration from Nafi’, by deleting it when connected but not when stopping.
43:62: 62- And let not Satan turn you away meaning, do not be deceived by his whisperings and doubts that he plants in your hearts, so that they prevent you from following me, for that which I have called you to is the religion of God upon which His Messengers and Books agreed. Then He explained His prohibition against Satan turning them away by making clear his enmity towards them, saying: Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy meaning, he is harmful because of his enmity towards you, not avoiding that nor concealing it, as is indicated by what occurred between him and Adam and what he committed himself to of misleading all of the children of Adam except the sincere servants of God.
43:63: 63- And when Jesus came with clear proofs, meaning he came to the Children of Israel with clear miracles and laws. Qatada said: The clear proofs here are the Gospel. “He said, ‘I have come to you with wisdom,’ meaning prophecy. It was also said to be the Gospel, or what encourages beauty and refrains from evil. ‘And that I may make clear to you some of that over which you differ,’ of the rulings of the Torah. Qatada said: It means the differences between the sects who formed parties regarding the matter of Jesus. Al-Zajjaj said: What Jesus brought in the Gospel is only some of that over which they differed, so he explained to them in places other than the Gospel what they needed. It was also said that the Children of Israel differed after the death of Moses regarding some aspects of their religion. Abu Ubaidah said that “some” here means all, as in His statement, Some of what He promises you will befall you. Muqatil said, It is like His statement, “And to make lawful to you some of what was forbidden to you, meaning what was made lawful in the Gospel of what was forbidden in the Torah, such as camel meat, the fat of every animal, and hunting fish on the Sabbath. The lam in and to make clear to you is conjoined to something understood, as if he said, I have come to you with wisdom to teach you and to make clear to you. Then he commanded them to be pious and obedient, saying, So fear God, meaning fear His disobedience, and obey in what I command you of monotheism and the laws.
43:64: 64- Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is an explanation of what He commanded them to obey Him in. This is a straight path, meaning worshipping God alone and acting according to His laws.
43:65: 65- Then the parties differed among themselves. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: The parties are the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: They are the Christian groups who differed about the matter of Jesus. Qatada said: The meaning of among them is that they differed among themselves. It was also said that they differed among those to whom he was sent from the Jews and Christians, and the parties are the factionalized groups. So woe to those who did wrong from among those who stayed behind, and they are those who associated partners with God and did not abide by His laws from the punishment of a painful Day meaning His punishment is painful, which is the Day of Resurrection.
43:66: 66- Do they await anything but the Hour? That is, do these parties anticipate and wait for anything but the Hour that it should come upon them suddenly that is, suddenly while they do not perceive that is, they do not realize it? It was said that what is meant by the parties are those who formed parties against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denied him, and they are the ones meant by His saying: Do they await anything but the Hour? The first is more appropriate.
43:67: 67- Friends, that Day, will be enemies to one another. That is, friends in this world who loved one another on the Day the Hour comes to them will be enemies to one another. That is, they will be hostile to one another, because the ties between them have been severed and each one of them will be preoccupied with himself, and they will find those things in which they were friends to be causes of punishment, so they will become enemies. Then He excepted the righteous, saying: Except the righteous. For they will be friends in this world and the Hereafter, because they found that friendship that was between them to be a cause of goodness and reward, so their friendship will remain as it was.
43:68: 68- O My servants, there is no fear concerning you today, nor shall you grieve. That is, this statement will be said to these pious people who love one another for the sake of God, and their fear will then go away and their grief will be lifted.
43:69: 69- Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims. The relative pronoun may be an adjective for My servants, a substitute for it, an explanatory apposition for it, or separated from it in the accusative case of praise, or in the nominative case as the subject and predicate of Enter Paradise, assuming: It will be said to them, Enter Paradise. The first is more appropriate, and this is what Al-Zajjaj said. Muqatil said: When fear occurs on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will call out, O My servants, there is no fear concerning you. When they hear the call, the creation will raise their heads, and it will be said, Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims. Then the idolaters, the non-Muslims, will lower their heads. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and Abu ‘Amr recited O My servants with the sukoon on the ya’ in both connected and paused sentences. Abu Bakr and Zur ibn Hubaish recited it with the sukoon on the ya’ and the fatha on the ya’ in both cases. The rest recited it without the ya’ in both cases.
43:70: 70- Enter Paradise, you and your spouses. What is meant by spouses are their believing wives, and it was said that they are their companions from among the believers, and it was said that they are their wives from among the houris. You will be delighted is that you will be honored, and it was said that you will be blessed, and it was said that you will be happy, and it was said that you will be pleased, and it was said that you will be amazed, and it was said that you will take pleasure in hearing it. The first interpretation of that is the joy and happiness arising from honor and blessing.
43:71: 71- And they will be served with golden plates. Sahaf is the plural of sahfah, which is a wide, broad bowl. Al-Kisa’i said: The largest of the bowls is the basin, then the qas’ah, which feeds ten, then the sahfah, which is similar to five, then the makilah, which is similar to two or three men. The meaning is: They will have foods in Paradise that will be served to them in golden plates, and drinks that will be served to them in kawab, which is the plural of kub. Al-Jawhari said: A kub is a jug without a handle, and the plural is akwab. Al-A’sha said: A delicious, creamy dish with a hint of butter between its cup and ear Another said: Reclining, its doors slamming, the servant rushes towards it with a cup Qatada said: The round cup with a short neck and a short handle, and the rectangular pitcher with a long neck and a long handle. Al-Akhfash said: The cups are the pitchers without spouts. Qatrib said: They are the pitchers without handles. And in them is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in. The majority of scholars read desires. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and Hafs read desires it with the pronoun referring to the relative pronoun. The meaning is: Whatever the souls of the people of Paradise desire of all kinds of foods and drinks and the like, which the soul seeks and craves, whatever it may be. The eyes delight in all the delights that they take pleasure in and seek to see. You say “laḍa’ yalḍa...
43:72: 72- And that is Paradise which you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do. That is, this statement will be said to them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:That is, it has become yours as an inheritance becomes the heir because of what you used to do in the world of righteous deeds. The demonstrative pronoun is the subject, Paradise is its description, and what you have been made to inherit is a description of Paradise, and the predicate is what you used to do. It was said that it is the relative predicate with its clause, and the first is more appropriate.
43:73: 73- For you therein are many fruits. Fruit is a well-known term, and it refers to all fruits, both fresh and dry. That is, in addition to food and drink, they will have many types and kinds of fruit in Paradise. From it you will eat. “From” is a partial or introductory particle, and the preposition was brought forward for the sake of separation. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the Quraysh 106:There is no one who is worshipped other than God in whom there is good. They said: Do you not claim that Jesus was a prophet and a righteous servant of God, yet the Christians worshipped him? If you are truthful, then he is like their gods. Then God revealed: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him. I said: And what do they turn away from? He said: They make noise. “And with Him is knowledge of the Hour.” He said: The emergence of Jesus, son of Mary, before the Day of Resurrection.
