Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No people went astray after they were guided except that they were given argument. Then he recited this verse: They do not present it to you except to argue. Many hadiths have been narrated condemning argument based on falsehood. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “The polytheists came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘Tell me, what do you think of what we worship besides God? Where are they?’ He said: ‘In the Fire.’ They said: ‘And the sun and the moon?’ He said: ‘And the sun and the moon.’ They said: ‘And Jesus, son of Mary?’ He said: ‘God said: “He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and made him an example for the Children of Israel.’” Al-Firyabi, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Musaddad, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Tabarani narrated, through various chains of transmission, on his authority, regarding His statement: And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour, that he said: The emergence of Jesus will come before the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). ‘Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Mu’adh, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, kinship ties will be severed, lineages will diminish, and brotherhood will disappear, except for brotherhood in God. This is His statement: ‘Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except for the righteous.’” And Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh in his Targhīb, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sha`b narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding his statement: Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except for the righteous, he said: Two believing friends and two disbelieving friends. One of the believers died and was given the good report of Paradise, so he mentioned his friend and said: O God, my friend so-and-so used to command me to obey You and obey Your Messenger, and he commanded me to do good and forbade me from evil, and he informed me that I would meet You. O God, do not lead him astray after me until You show him what You have shown me and are pleased with him as You are pleased with me. Then it is said to him: Go, for if you knew what I have given him, you would laugh a lot and cry a little. Then the other dies and their souls are brought together and it is said: Let each of you praise the other. Then each of them says to the other: What a good brother, what a good friend, and what a good confidant. And when one of the disbelievers dies, he is given the good report of Hell, so he mentions his friend and says: O God, my friend so-and-so used to command me to disobey You. And disobeying Your Messenger, and he orders me to do evil and forbids me from good and informs me that I will not meet You. O God, do not guide him after me until You show him what You have shown me and are angry with him as You were angry with me. Then the other dies and their souls are joined together and it is said: Let each of you praise the other. Then each of them says to the other: What a bad brother, what a bad companion, and what a bad friend. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abasa who said: The goblets are made of silver. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There is no one but that he has a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. The disbeliever inherits the believer’s home in Hell, and the believer inherits the disbeliever’s home in Paradise. This is His statement: ‘And that is Paradise which you have been made to inherit.’”
43:74: His statement: 74- The criminals meaning the people of criminal disbelief, as is indicated by their being mentioned in contrast to the believers who have what God Almighty mentioned before this are in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally the punishment will never cease from them.
43:75: 75- It will not be lightened for them meaning that the torment will not be lightened for them. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. And they are therein in despair meaning that they have lost hope of salvation. It was said that they are silent in a state of despair. The meaning of this has already been explained in Al-An’am.
43:76: 76- And We did not wrong them meaning We did not punish them without guilt or more than they deserved, but it was they who were the wrongdoers to themselves because of the sins they committed. The majority of scholars read al-zalimin in the accusative case as the predicate of kana, and the pronoun is a disjunctive pronoun. Abu Zayd the grammarian read al-zalimin in the nominative case as the pronoun is the subject and what follows is its predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of kana.
43:77: 77- And they will call, 'O Malik!' meaning the criminals will call out this call, and Malik is the keeper of the Hellfire. The majority of scholars read O Malik without softening. Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Yahya ibn Waththab, and Al-A'mash read O Mal with softening. That your Lord may decree upon us with death. They sought intercession through Malik to God, the Exalted, to ask Him to decree death upon them so that they may be relieved from the torment. He said, 'Indeed, you will remain.' Meaning, you will remain in the torment. It was said that He remained silent for eighty years, then He answered them with this answer. It was also said that He remained silent for a thousand years, and it was said for a hundred years, and it was said for forty years.
43:78: 78- Indeed, We have brought you the truth. This may be from the words of God, the Most High, or from the words of Malik, but the former is more evident. The meaning is: Indeed, We sent to you the messengers and sent down to them the books, but they called upon you, but you did not accept them or believe them. This is the meaning of His statement: But most of you are averse to the truth, they do not accept it. What is meant by the truth is everything that God has commanded through His messengers and sent down in His books. It is said that it is specific to the Qur’an. It is said that the meaning of most of them is: all of you. It is also said that he meant the leaders and chiefs, and those other than them who follow them.
43:79: 79- Or have they plotted a plan, then We are plotting. "Am is the disconnected particle that means rather," and the hamza means: "Rather, they have plotted a plan." In that there is a transition from the anguish of the people of Hell to the narration of what will happen from them. Ibram means perfection and mastery. It is said that Ibrammat al-Shi' means I perfected and mastered it. Ibram al-Habl means if you twist it tightly. The meaning is: Rather, they have plotted a plan against the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, then We are plotting a plan for them. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd. Similar to this is the saying of God the Almighty: "Or do they intend a plan? Then it is those who disbelieve who are the plotters." It was said that the meaning is: Or have they decided a plan, then We are the ones who will decide upon them. We have commanded them with the punishment.
43:80: Al-Kalbi said: 80- Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? That is, do they think that We do not hear what they whisper to themselves, or what they talk about secretly in a private place, or what they whisper among themselves? Yes, We hear that and we act upon it. And Our messengers are with them, writing down, that is, the guardians with them write down everything that comes from them of words or actions. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state, or it is conjoined with the sentence that indicates Yes.
43:81: Then God, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the infidels a statement that would bind them to the proof and would cut off the doubts they presented. He said: 81- “Say: ‘If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of his worshippers.’” That is, if He had a son, as you say and as you claim, then I would be the first to worship God alone, because whoever worships God alone has denied that He had a son. This is what Ibn Qutaybah said. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: The meaning is that the Most Gracious did not have a son, and His statement: Then I would be the first of his worshippers is the beginning of a statement. It was also said that the meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, if it is proven that God has a son, then I would be the first to worship this son that you claim has been proven, but it is impossible for Him to have a son. It denies the existence of a son in the most eloquent, complete, and elegant manner. This is what is apparent from the Qur’anic system. An example of this is the saying of the Most High: Indeed, we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. An example of this is when a man says to someone who is debating him: If you prove what you say with evidence, then I am the first to believe it and say it. So, in in if is a conditional particle. This was preferred by Ibn Jarir and others. It was said that the meaning of al-‘abideen is those who are averse to worship, which is a forced and unavoidable matter. However, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Yamani read al-‘abideen without an alif. It is said that ‘abd ya’budan ‘abdan with a fat-ha: if he is averse and angry, then he is ‘abd. The noun ‘abdah is like anfah. Perhaps the one who read this strange and far-fetched reading is rejecting the meaning of I am the first of the worshippers, and he is neither prepared nor surprised. Al-Jawhari narrated on the authority of Abu ‘Amr regarding his saying: I am the first of the worshippers, that it is from averseness and anger. Al-Mawardi narrated it on the authority of al-Kisa’i and al-Qutaybi, and al-Farra’ said the same. Ibn al-A'rabi also said: The meaning of the worshippers is the angry and the rude. Abu Ubaidah said: It means the deniers. It was said that 'Abdani Haqqi' means 'he denied me'. They recited the following words of al-Farazdaq in support of the meaning they said: Those are my companions, so bring me someone like them, and I will hate to satirize Kulayb with a sword. He also said: These are people who, if they satirized me, I would satirize them. I would rather not satirize Kulayb in Daram. There is no doubt that the word 'abd' and 'a'bad, meaning 'to be angry' or 'to be angry', are well-established in the Arabic language. The transmission of these imams is sufficient as proof. However, making what is in the Qur'an of this is a forced and unavoidable exaggeration and a clear arbitrariness. Ibn 'Arafah refuted what they said, saying: It is only said 'abd ya'budu worshipper, so he is 'abd, and it is rarely said 'aabid' worshipper, and the Qur'an does not come with the little of the language or the unusual. The majority read walad in the singular, and the people of Kufa, except 'Asim, read walad with a damma on the waw and a sukoon on the lam.
43:82: 82- Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the Throne, from what they describe. That is, He is glorified and sanctified from what they say of the lie that He has a son and they invent about Him, glory be to Him, what is not befitting of His status. If this is from the words of God, glory be to Him, then He has glorified Himself from what they said. If it is from the complete words of His Messenger that He commanded him to say, then He commanded him to add to what he narrated from them, according to their false claim, the glorification and sanctification of his Lord.
43:83: 83- So leave them to plunge into falsehood and play meaning leave the disbelievers where you have not guided them to that which you have guided them with nor have responded to what you have called them to, to plunge into their falsehoods and play in their worldly life until they meet their Day which they are promised which is the Day of Resurrection, and it was said that it is the torment in this world. It was said that this was abrogated by the verse of the sword, and it was said that it was not abrogated and was only stated as a threat. The majority of scholars read it as yalaghu they will meet, and Mujahid, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, and Ibn al-Samife’ read it hatta yalaghu until they will meet with a fat-ha on the ya’ and a sukoon on the lam without an alif. This reading was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr. 84- And He is God in the heaven and God on the earth. The preposition and its object in both instances are related to god because it means worshipped or deserving of worship. The meaning is: He is the one worshipped in the heaven and worshipped on earth, or deserving of worship in the heaven and worship on earth. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: God in both instances is nominative as the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, He who is in the heaven is God and on earth is God. It is appropriate to omit it due to the length of the statement. He said: The meaning is to inform about His divinity, not about His existence in them. Qatada said: He is worshipped in the heaven and on earth. It was said that in means over: that is, He is able to have power over the heaven and earth as in His statement: And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. Umar ibn Al-Khattab, Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ibn Mas'ud read He who is in the heaven is God and on the earth is God, implying that knowledge has the meaning of a derivative, so the preposition and its object are related to it from this perspective. And He is the Wise, the Knowing, that is, the eloquent in wisdom and abundant in knowledge.
43:85: 85- And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. Tabarak is a verbal noun derived from barakah, which means abundant goodness. What is meant by between them is the air and the animals in it. And with Him is knowledge of the Hour, meaning knowledge of the time when it will occur. And to Him you will be returned. Everyone will be rewarded according to what he deserves of good and evil, and in it is a severe threat. The majority of scholars read tarja’oonu with a fathah, while Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, and al-Kisa’i read it with a tah.
43:86: 86- And those they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession meaning, those they invoke besides God, such as idols and the like, do not possess intercession with God, as they claim that they intercede for them. The majority of scholars read they invoke with a lower vowel, while As-Sulami and Ibn Waththab read it with a higher vowel. Except for those who bear witness to the truth, i.e., monotheism. And they know, i.e., they have knowledge and insight into what they have testified to. The exception may be connected, meaning: except for those who bear witness to the truth, namely, the Messiah, Ezra, and the angels, for they possess the power of intercession for whoever deserves it. It was also said that it is disconnected, meaning: but for those who bear witness to the truth, these will intercede for them. It is possible that the exception is omitted, meaning they do not possess the power of intercession for anyone except for those who bear witness to the truth. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said: The meaning of the verse is that these do not possess the power of intercession except for those who bear witness to the truth and believe with knowledge and insight. Qatada said: They do not intercede for their worshippers, but rather they intercede for those who testify to God's Oneness. It has been said that the connection in this exception is based on making those they call upon general for everything worshipped besides God, and the disconnection is based on making it specific to idols.
43:87: 87- And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ The lām is the particle used to initiate an oath. The meaning is: If you ask these idol-worshipping polytheists, who created them, they will acknowledge and confess that God is their Creator, and they will not be able to deny it, nor will they be able to reject it, since the matter has been made clear and evident. How then are they deluded? That is, how can they turn away from the worship of God to the worship of someone other than Him and turn away from it, despite this acknowledgment? If someone acknowledges that God is his Creator, and worships an idol or an animal along with God or worships it alone, then he has worshipped one of God’s creations. This shows an immeasurable amount of ignorance. It is said that afkahu ya’fukahu ifkān means to turn something away or divert it. It is also said that the meaning is: If you ask the Messiah, Ezra, and the angels, who created them, they will surely say God. How then are these disbelievers deluded in taking them as gods? It is also said that the meaning is: If you ask all the worshippers and the worshipped.
43:88: 88- The majority read and his saying in the accusative case in apposition to the place of the hour, as if it was said: He knows the hour and knows what is said, or in apposition to their secret and their private conversations: meaning He knows their secret and their private conversations and knows what is said, or in apposition to the deleted object of they write: meaning they write that and they write what is said, or in apposition to the deleted object of they know: meaning they know that and they know what is said, or it is a verbal noun: meaning He said what is said, or in the accusative case with an implied verb: meaning God knows what His Messenger said, or it is in apposition to the place of the truth: meaning He bore witness to the truth and to what is said, or in the accusative case with the omission of the letter of the oath. Among those who permit the first interpretation are Al-Mubarrad and Ibn Al-Anbari, and among those who permit the second are Al-Farra’ and Al-Akhfash, and among those who permit the accusative case as a verbal noun are Al-Farra’ and Al-Akhfash as well. Hamzah and Asim read and his saying in the accusative case in apposition to the word the Hour: meaning, with him is the knowledge of the Hour and the knowledge of its saying. The saying, the saying, and the saying have the same meaning, or on the basis that the and is for an oath. Qatadah, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Abu Qilabah, Al-A'raj, Ibn Hurmuz, Muslim ibn Jundub, and his saying in the nominative case in apposition to the knowledge of the Hour: meaning, with him is the knowledge of the Hour and with him is his saying. Or on the basis of the subject, and its predicate is the sentence mentioned after it, or its predicate is omitted, its estimated meaning is and his saying is such and such, or his saying is heard. Abu Ubaid said: It is said, I said a saying and a saying and a saying, and the pronoun in his saying refers to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. Qatadah said: This is your Prophet complaining to his Lord about his people. It was also said that the pronoun refers to the Messiah. In both versions, the meaning is that he said, calling out to his Lord, O Lord, these to whom You sent me are a people who do not believe.
43:89: Then when he called upon his Lord with this, He answered him by saying: 89- So pardon them meaning turn away from their call "and say, 'Peace'" meaning My command is submission from you and I leave you alone. Ata' said: He means to be lenient until My judgment is revealed, and its meaning is to leave alone, like His saying: "Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant." Qatada said: He ordered him to pardon them, then he ordered him to fight them, so the pardon was abrogated by the sword. It was said that it is a decisive statement that was not abrogated. You will soon know contains a severe threat and a great warning from God, the Almighty. The majority read they know with a lower vowel, while Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with a higher vowel. Al-Farra' said: Indeed, "Peace" is raised by the omission of upon you. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th wa al-Nushur narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, And they will call, 'O Malik!' He said, He will remain away from them for a thousand years, then He will answer them, 'Indeed, you will remain.' Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said, "While three were between the Ka'bah and its curtains, two from Quraysh and one from Thaqafi, or two from Thaqafi and one from Quraysh, one of them said, 'Do you think that God hears our speech?' One of them said, 'If you speak aloud, He hears, but if you speak in secret, He does not hear.' So the verse, "Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations?" was revealed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, "If the Most Gracious had a son, he said, If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers, he said, The witnesses. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding the verse, If the Most Gracious had a son, he said, This is well-known from the speech of the Arabs: 'If this matter ever happened,'" meaning, it never happened. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Qatada.
44:1: It is fifty-nine, and it was said fifty-seven verses. Al-Qurtubi said: It is unanimously agreed that it was revealed in Mecca, except for the saying: Indeed, We will remove the punishment. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr that Surat Ad-Dukhan was revealed in Mecca. At-Tirmidhi and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever recites Ha-Mim Ad-Dukhan at night, seventy thousand angels will seek forgiveness for him in the morning. At-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: It is strange; we do not know it except from this source. Amr ibn Abi Khath’am is weak. Al-Bukhari said: His hadith is rejected. At-Tirmidhi, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever recites Ha-Mim Ad-Dukhan on a Friday night, will wake up forgiven. Al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: It is strange and we do not know it except from this source. Hisham bin Al-Miqdam is considered weak, and Al-Hasan did not hear it from Abu Hurayrah. This is what Ayoub, Yunus bin Ubaid and Ali bin Zaid said. What supports this is what Ibn Al-Durais and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, and he mentioned it. And what Ibn Al-Durais narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, with a similar chain of transmission, but it is mursal. And what Al-Darimi and Muhammad bin Nasr narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi’, who said: Whoever recites Surat Ad-Dukhan on the night of Friday will wake up forgiven and married to the houris. And Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites Surat Ha Mim Ad-Dukhan on the night of Friday or on the day of Friday, God will build for him a house in Paradise because of it. His saying: 1- Ha Mim.
44:2: His saying: 2- Ha Meem * By the clear Book. The meaning and syntax of this had been discussed in the two surahs that preceded this surah.
44:3: And his saying: 3- Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night is the answer to the oath. If you make the answer Ha Mim, then this sentence would be a new sentence. Some grammarians have denied that this sentence is an answer to the oath because it is an adjective for the thing sworn by, and the adjective for the thing sworn by is not an answer to the oath. He said the answer is Indeed, We were warners and Ibn Atiyyah chose this. It was said that his saying: Indeed, We were warners is a second answer, or a new sentence confirming the sending down, and it is like the reason for it as if he said: We sent it down because it is Our business to warn. The pronoun in We sent it down refers to the clear book, which is the Qur'an. It was said that what is meant by the book is all the revealed books, and the pronoun in We sent it down refers to the Qur'an, meaning that He, the Most High, swore by all the revealed books that He sent down the Qur'an, and the first is more appropriate. The blessed night is the Night of Decree, as stated in the verse: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. It has four names: the Blessed Night, the Night of Bara’ah, the Night of the Deed, and the Night of Decree. Ikrimah said: The blessed night here refers to the middle of Sha’ban. Qatada said: The entire Qur’an was revealed on the Night of Decree from the Mother of the Book, which is the Preserved Tablet, to the House of Honour in the lowest heaven. Then God, the Exalted, revealed it to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the nights and days over a period of twenty-three years. A detailed explanation of this has already been presented in Surah Al-Baqarah, when God, the Exalted, says: The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was revealed. Muqatil said: Every night, a portion of revelation would descend from the Tablet, equal to what Gabriel descends in a similar year. God, the Exalted, described this night as blessed because the Qur’an was revealed in it, encompassing religious and worldly interests, and because the angels and the Spirit descend in it, as will be mentioned in Surah Al-Qadr.
44:4: Among its blessings is what God the Almighty mentioned here in His saying: 4- Therein is ordained every wise matter. The meaning of distinguishes is: separates and clarifies, from their saying: I separated something means I separated it into parts. The wise matter is the well-established, because God the Almighty writes in it what will happen in the year of life and death, expansion and contraction, good and evil, and other things. This is what Mujahid, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, and others said. This sentence is either another description of the night and what is between them is an interruption, or it is a new chapter to confirm what came before it. The majority read yafreq with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the ra', and it was lightened. Al-Hasan, Al-A'mash, and Al-A'raj read it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the ra', and they put every matter in the accusative case and raised Hakeem as the subject. The truth is what the majority of scholars have stated, that this blessed night is the Night of Decree, not the fifteenth night of Sha’ban, because God Almighty has made it general here and explained it in Surat Al-Baqarah, saying: The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was revealed, and in Surat Al-Qadr, saying: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. So after this clear explanation, there is nothing left that would require disagreement or confusion.
44:5: 5- A command from Us Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farraa said: The accusative of a command that separates means that it separates, because a command means separation. The meaning is: We command that this be made clear and copied from the Preserved Tablet, so on this basis it is accusative as a verbal noun like your saying yadriba darban. Al-Mubarrad said: A command is in the position of a verbal noun, and the meaning is that we sent it down. Al-Akhfash said: Its accusative is in the state of description: that is, commanding. It was said that it is accusative of specificity: that is, by this command I mean a command that has come from Us, and in it is the glorification and magnification of the Qur’an. Some scholars have mentioned twelve aspects for the accusative of a command, the most evident of which is what we have mentioned. Zayd ibn Ali read a command in the nominative case: that is, it is a command. Indeed, We were messengers. This sentence is either a replacement for his saying Indeed, We were warners or a third answer to the oath or a new sentence. Al-Razi said: The meaning is that we did that warning because we were sending prophets.
44:6: 6- A mercy from your Lord The word mercy is in the accusative case as a reason: meaning, We sent it down as mercy, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. Al-Mubarrad said: It is in the accusative case as an object of messengers: meaning, We were messengers of mercy. It was also said that it is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial noun: meaning, merciful, as stated by Al-Akhfash. Al-Hasan read mercy in the nominative case, assuming it is mercy, Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing for whoever calls upon Him, the All-Knowing of everything.
44:7: Then He, the Almighty, described Himself with what indicates His great and dazzling power, saying: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. The majority of scholars read Lord in the nominative case, in apposition to The All-Hearing, All-Knowing, or as a subject and predicate, There is no god but He, or as a predicate of a deleted subject: that is, He is Lord. The Kufians read Lord in the accusative case, as a substitute for your Lord, or as a clarification of it, or as a description of if you are certain that He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and they acknowledged that, as God related from them in more than one place.
44:8: And the sentence 8- There is no god but He is a new sentence confirming what came before it, or the predicate of the Lord of the heavens as mentioned, and likewise the sentence He gives life and causes death is a new sentence confirming what came before it Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old. The majority of scholars read it in the nominative case as a new sentence with an assumed subject: that is, He is your Lord, or as a substitute for the Lord of the heavens, or a clarification or description of it. Al-Kisa'i, in the narration of Al-Shirazi from him, and Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Abu Haywah, and Al-Hasan read it in the genitive case, and the reason for the genitive case is what we mentioned in the reading of those who read in the genitive case in the Lord of the heavens.
44:9: 9- Rather, they are in doubt, playing. I am striking out at their being certain, at their being in doubt about monotheism and resurrection, and at their acknowledgment that God is their Creator and the Creator of all creation, and that this is from them in the manner of playing and joking. The place of playing is the nominative case as a second predicate or the accusative case as a state.
44:10: 10- Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. The fa is for arranging what comes after it based on what came before it, because their being in doubt and play requires that. The meaning is: So await for them, O Muhammad, the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. It was also said that the meaning is: Memorize their statement so that you may bear witness against them on the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. There is a difference of opinion about this smoke mentioned in the verse: When will it come? Some say it is one of the signs of the Hour, and that it will remain on earth for forty days. It has been proven in Sahih that it is one of the ten signs that will occur before the Hour begins. Others say it is something that had already been decreed, and it is what happened to the Quraysh because of the supplication of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), until a man would see smoke between the sky and the earth. This is proven in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim and others. This was when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) supplicated against them for years like the years of Joseph, and they were afflicted with drought and famine until they ate their bones. A man would look at the sky and see what was between him and it like smoke from the effort. It has also been said that it was on the day of the conquest of Mecca. A statement of what indicates these opinions will come at the end of this research.
44:11: And His saying: 11- It covers the people is a second description of al-Dukhan 44:that is, it encompasses them and surrounds them. This is a painful torment means they say, This is a painful torment, or they say that, or God says that to them.
44:12: 12- Our Lord, remove the punishment from us, indeed we are believers. That is, they say that. It has been narrated that they came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: If God removes this punishment from us, we will submit. What is meant by the punishment is the hunger that caused what they saw of the smoke, or what they say when they see the smoke, which is one of the signs of the Hour, or when they see it on the day of the conquest of Mecca, according to the different opinions. The most correct of them is that it is the smoke that they imagined because of the hardship and severe hunger that befell them. This preference does not contradict what was reported that the smoke is one of the signs of the Hour, as that is another smoke. It also does not contradict what was said that it was what happened on the day of the conquest of Mecca, as it was another smoke, assuming that it happened.
44:13: 13- How can they be reminded? That is, how can they remember and learn from what happened to them, when the situation is that a clear Messenger has come to them, explaining to them everything they need regarding religious and worldly matters.
44:14: 14- Then they turned away from him meaning they turned away from the Messenger who came to them and they were not satisfied with merely turning away from him, but they went beyond him and said, ‘A madman is being taught’ meaning they said: Only a human being is teaching him the Qur’an and they said he is mad. So how can these people remember and how can they be reminded?
44:15: Then when they called upon God to remove the punishment from them and that if He removed it from them they would believe, He, the Most High, answered them by saying: 15- Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little while, meaning that We will remove it from them for a little while or for a little while. Then God, the Most High, informed about them that they would not desist from what they were doing of polytheism, and they would not fulfill what they promised Him of faith, so He said: Indeed, you will return, meaning to what you were doing of polytheism. And the matter was thus, for when God, the Most High, removed that punishment from them, they returned to what they were doing of disbelief and obstinacy. It was said that the meaning is: You will return to Us with the resurrection and the revival, and the first is more appropriate.
44:16: 16- The Day We strike with the Greater Bash The adverbial phrase is in the accusative case due to the omission of remember, and it is said that it is a substitute for The Day the sky comes, and it is said that it is related to Muntaqimun, and it is said that it is indicated by Muntaqimun which is Muntaqim. The Greater Bash is the Day of Badr, as stated by most. The meaning is that when they returned to denial and disbelief after the punishment was lifted from them, God took revenge on them with the Battle of Badr. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: What is meant by it is the punishment of the Fire. Al-Zajjaj chose this opinion: The first is more appropriate. The majority read Nabtash with a fatha on the noon and a kasra on the ta', meaning We strike them. Al-Hasan and Abu Ja'far read it with a damma on the ta', which is a dialect. Abu Raja' and Talhah read it with a damma on the noon and a kasra on the ta'. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On a blessed night, he said: The Qur’an was revealed on the Night of Decree, and Gabriel brought it down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in stars to answer the people. Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, Therein is distinguished every precise matter, he said: It is written from the Mother of the Book on the Night of Decree what will happen in the year of livelihood and death, life and rain, until it is written for the pilgrim: So-and-so will perform Hajj, and so-and-so will perform Hajj. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Therein is distinguished every precise matter, he said: The matter of one year is next to the next except misery and happiness, for that is in the Book of God and cannot be changed or altered. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated that he said: You will see a man walking in the markets and his name has been included among the dead, then he recites: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, meaning the Night of Decree. He said: On that night, worldly affairs are divided into a similar one for the next, whether death, life, or provision. Every worldly affair is divided into a similar one for the next. Ibn Zanjawayh and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Deaths are cut off from one Sha'ban to the next, to the extent that a man marries and has a child born to him while his name has been included among the dead. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Mughirah ibn Al-Akhnas. This is a mursal hadith and it cannot be used as evidence, nor does it contradict the clear verses of the Qur'an. What has been narrated concerning this is either mursal or not authentic. The author of Al-Durr Al-Manthur mentioned this, as well as what was narrated about the virtue of the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, but that does not necessarily mean that it is meant by on a blessed night. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that when the Quraysh resisted the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and were slow to convert to Islam, he said, O God, help them against seven days like the seven days of Joseph. Then a drought and famine struck them until they ate their bones. A man looked at the sky and saw what was between him and it like smoke because of hunger. Then God revealed, Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was approached and it was said, O Messenger of God, ask God to send down rain for Mudar. So he asked God to send down rain for them and they were given rain. Then God revealed, Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little; indeed, you will return. When they were granted ease, they returned to their previous state. Then God revealed, On the Day We will strike with the greatest strike; indeed, We will take retribution. So God took retribution from them on the Day of Badr. The strike, smoke and oppression had passed. Something similar to this has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud from more than one source, and something similar to it has been narrated on the authority of a group of the Successors. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah who said: I entered upon Ibn Abbas and he said: I did not sleep last night. I said: Why? He said: The star rose and I was afraid that smoke would come down. Ibn Kathir said: This is a saheeh isnad. As-Suyuti authenticated it as well, but it does not state that it is the reason for the revelation of the verse. We have already told you that there is no contradiction between this verse being revealed about the smoke that appeared to the Quraysh due to hunger, and the smoke being one of the signs, portents and portents of the Hour. There are authentic, good, and weak hadiths that speak of this, but they do not mention the reason for the revelation of the verse, so there is no need for us to elaborate on it. What is obligatory is to adhere to what is proven in the two Sahihs and others, that the smoke of the Quraysh at times of hardship and hunger was the reason for the revelation. This refutes the view of those who preferred that the smoke is one of the signs of the Hour, such as Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir and others. Similarly, the view of those who said that it was the smoke that occurred on the day of the conquest of Mecca is refuted, adhering to what Ibn Sa’d narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: On the day of the conquest of Mecca there was smoke, and this is the saying of God, the Most High, ‘Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke.’ This does not contradict what is in the two Sahihs, assuming its chain of transmission is sound, although it is possible that Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him thought that the occurrence of that smoke on the day of the conquest was what was meant by the verse, and that is why he did not state it explicitly as the reason for its revelation. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: Ibn Mas’ud said: The great strike was on the Day of Badr, and I say that it is on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Kathir said: This chain of transmission is sound. Ibn Kathir said before this: Ibn Masoud interpreted it as referring to the Day of Badr. This is the opinion of a group of those who agreed with Ibn Masoud on his interpretation of smoke as mentioned above. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Al-Awfi, on his authority, and on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b and a group, and this is possible. What appears to be the case is that it refers to the Day of Resurrection, even though the Day of Badr was also a day of great destruction. I said: Rather, it appears that it is the Day of Badr, even though the Day of Resurrection is a day of greater affliction than any other affliction. The context is with the Quraysh, so interpreting it as their specific affliction is more appropriate than interpreting it as the affliction that will be on the Day of Resurrection for every sinner among mankind and jinn.
44:17: His saying: 17- And We had certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh meaning We tried them. The meaning of the trial here is that God, the Exalted, sent His messengers to them and they commanded them with what He had prescribed for them, but they denied them, or He gave them abundant provisions, but they transgressed and rebelled. Al-Zajjaj said: We tried them, and the meaning is: We treated them as someone who is being tested by sending messengers to them. It was read fitna with the emphasis. And there came to them a noble Messenger meaning noble to God, noble among his people. Muqatil said: Good character through forgiveness and pardon. Al-Farra’ said: Noble to his Lord if He chose him for prophethood.
44:18: 18- That you deliver to me the servants of God This is the explanation for what came before what is in the sense of saying, and it is permissible for it to be the lightened form of the heavy form, and the meaning is: that the matter and the conversation were delivered to the servants of God, and it is permissible for it to be a source: that they delivered, and the meaning is: that he asked them to hand over the Children of Israel to him. Mujahid said: The meaning is send with me the servants of God and release them from the punishment, so the servants of God according to this is the object. It was said that the meaning is: deliver to me the servants of God what is required of you of the rights of God, so it is accusative as a vocative with an addition. It was said: lend me your hearing so that I may convey to you the message of your Lord Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger is an explanation of what came before: that is, a messenger from God to you who is trustworthy with regard to the message and is not accused.
44:19: 19- And that you do not exalt yourselves over God meaning do not act arrogantly and haughtily towards Him by refusing to obey Him and follow His messengers. It was also said that you should not transgress against God, and it was also said that you should not fabricate lies against Him. The first is better, and this is what Ibn Jurayj and Yahya ibn Salam said. The phrase Indeed, I bring you clear authority is an explanation for the prohibition before it: meaning, with a clear argument that cannot be denied. Qatada said: with a clear excuse. The first is better, and this is what Yahya ibn Salam said. The majority of scholars read it with a kasra on the hamza of inna, and it was also read with a fatha, estimating the lam.
44:20: 20- And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me. He sought refuge in God Almighty when they threatened to kill him, meaning: from being stoned. Qatada said: Stone me with stones, and it was said: Curse me, and it was said: Kill me.
44:21: 21- And if you do not believe in me, then leave me alone. That is, if you do not believe in me and acknowledge my prophethood, then leave me alone and do not harm me. Muqatil said: Leave me alone, neither against me nor for me. It was also said: Stay away from me and I will stay away from you until God judges between us. It was also said: Let me go, and the meanings are close. Then, when they did not believe him and did not answer his call.
44:22: He returned to his Lord with supplication as God related about him in His saying: 22- So he called upon his Lord, ‘These are a criminal people.’ The majority of scholars read it with a fat-ha on the hamza, implying the preposition: meaning he called upon Him, saying: These are the ones. Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Isa bin Umar read it with a kasra on it, implying the statement. There is an omission in the speech: meaning they disbelieved, so he called upon his Lord, and the criminals are the disbelievers. He called it a supplication even though he only mentioned that they were criminals, because they deserved to be supplicated against because of that.
44:23: 23- So take My servants by night. God Almighty answered his prayer, and ordered that the Children of Israel be taken by night. It is said traveled and traveled are two dialects. The majority read so traveled with the disconnection, and the people of Hijaz read it with the connection, and Ibn Kathir agreed with them. The first reading is from traveled and the second is from traveled. The sentence is understood as saying: that is, God said to Moses, Take My servants by night. “You will be pursued,” that is, Pharaoh and his soldiers will follow you. And it has been mentioned in more than one place that Pharaoh left after them.
44:24: 24- And leave the sea calm meaning still. It is said raha yarhu rahwan if it is calm and does not move. Al-Jawhari said: It is said do that calmly meaning calmly as you are. And aysh raha means calm. And raha al-bahr means calm. Al-Harawi and others said the same, and it is well-known in the language. From this comes the saying of the poet: And the horses frolic freely in their reins like birds escaping from the hairy grove. And the horses gait calmly in their reins. The meaning is: Leave the sea calm as it was after you struck it with your staff, and do not order it to return as it was, lest the people of Pharaoh enter it after you and the Children of Israel, and it close on them and they drown. Abu Ubaidah said: He opened between his legs, meaning he opened... He said: And from this is His statement: And leave the sea calmly, meaning: Leave it open as it was after you entered it. This is what Abu Ubaid said, and Mujahid and others said the same. Ibn Arafa said: They both go back to one meaning, even though their wording differs, because when the sea calms down, it opens up. Al-Harawi said: It is permissible for rahwān to be an adjective for Moses, meaning: Walk calmly as you were. Ka’b and Al-Hasan said: rahwān means a path. Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ said: Easy. Akrima said: Dryness is like his saying: Then strike for them a dry path through the sea. In any case, the meaning is leave it alone or leave it alone, as an exaggeration in the description with the source Indeed, they are a drowned army, meaning that Pharaoh and his people will be drowned. The Almighty informed Moses of that to calm his heart and reassure him. The majority read it with a kasra on inna as a resumption with the intention of informing him of that, and it was read with a fatha on the assumption that they are.
44:25: 25- How much is the informative particle that indicates abundance. We have already discussed the meaning of the verse in Surat Ash-Shu’ara’.
44:26: The majority read 26- and a place with a fat-ha on the meem as the name of a place to stand. Ibn Hurmuz, Qatadah, and al-Samifi’ read it, and it was narrated on the authority of Nafi’ with a damma as the name of a place of residence.
44:27: 27- And they were enjoying comfort in it Comfort with the first letter fatha: enjoyment: it is said that God has blessed him and made him happy, and with the kasra it is the favor, and what He has bestowed upon you, and someone is abundant in comfort: meaning abundant in wealth. Al-Jawhari mentioned the meaning of this: The majority read fakihin with an alif. Abu Raja', Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Ashhab, Al-A'raj, Abu Ja'far and Shaibah read fakihin without an alif, and the meaning according to the first reading: enjoying themselves in good health and in the second reading: arrogant and haughty. Al-Jawhari said: A man is fakaha with the kasra, so he is fakaha if he is in good health and joking, and fakaha is also: the arrogant and haughty. He said: Fakaheen: meaning comfortable. Al-Tha'labi said: They are two languages like al-haadhir and al-hadar and al-farah and al-farah. It was said that al-faka is the one who enjoys various types of pleasure as a man enjoys various types of fruit.
44:28: 28- Likewise, We gave it as an inheritance to another people. The kaf is in the nominative case as predicate of a deleted subject. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, the matter is thus, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, and the reference is to the source of the verb indicated by left: that is, We took it from them in the same way as that plunder, and it was said that We expelled them from it in the same way as that expulsion, and it was said that We destroyed them in the same way as that destruction. So, according to the first interpretation, His statement And We gave it as an inheritance to another people is in apposition to left and according to the other interpretations, it is in apposition to the implied verb. What is meant by the other people are the Children of Israel, for God Almighty made them kings of the land of Egypt after they had been enslaved there, so they became its heirs: that is, it reached them as an inheritance reaches an heir. Similar to this is His statement: And We gave inheritance to the people who had been oppressed the eastern and western parts of the earth.
44:29: 29- So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them. This is a statement of the lack of concern for their destruction. The commentators said: That is, they did not perform any righteous deeds on earth for which they would be wept over, and no good deed ascended for them to heaven for which they would be wept over. The meaning is that no one from the people of heaven or earth was afflicted by their loss and destruction. The Arabs used to say when a master among them died: The heavens and the earth wept for him, meaning his affliction was widespread. An example of this is the saying of Jarir: When Al-Zubayr came, the city walls and the mountains were humbled. And from it is the saying of Al-Nabigha: Harith Al-Jolan cried for the loss of his Lord, and Hawran was humble and humbled before him. Al-Hasan said: There is an omitted complement in the speech: that is, the people and angels of the heavens and the earth did not weep over them. Mujahid said: The heavens and the earth weep over the believer for forty mornings. It was also said that the places of his prayers and the ascents of his deeds weep over the believer. And they were not given respite meaning, they were given respite until another time, but rather they were hastened to be punished due to the intensity of their disbelief and the severity of their stubbornness.
44:30: 30- And We saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment. That is, We delivered them by destroying their enemy from the slavery they were in, the killing of their children, the enslavement of their women, and the imposition of hard labor on them.
44:31: And His statement: 31- From Pharaoh is a substitute for the punishment, either by deleting an adjective: meaning from the punishment of Pharaoh, or by exaggeration as if it were the punishment itself, so it was substituted for it, or as a state of the punishment, meaning it came from Pharaoh. Ibn Abbas read From Pharaoh with a fat-ha on the meem as a question of contempt, as is said to someone who boasts about his lineage or ancestry: Who are you? Then the Almighty explained his state, saying: Indeed, he was exalted among the transgressors meaning exalted in arrogance and haughtiness among the transgressors in disbelief in God and committing His sins, as in His statement: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land.
44:32: And when He, the Most High, explained how He averted harm from the Children of Israel, He explained how He honored them, saying: 32- And We chose them, with knowledge, over the worlds. That is, God chose them over the worlds of their time, with knowledge of their deserving of that. It is not meant that He chose them over all the worlds, as evidenced by His statement about this nation, You are the best nation produced for mankind. And it was said over all the worlds because of the large number of prophets among them. The place of with knowledge is the accusative case of the subject of We chose them, meaning the case of Our choosing them with knowledge from Us, and over the worlds is related to We chose them.
44:33: 33- And We gave them of the signs meaning the miracles of Moses that which was a clear trial meaning a clear test and examination to see how they would act. Qatada said: The signs were saving them from drowning, splitting the sea for them, shading them with clouds, and sending down manna and quails for them. Ibn Zayd said: The signs are the evil that He kept them from, and the good that He commanded them to do. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: The clear trial is the apparent blessing as in His statement: And that He might test the believers through Him with a good trial and from this is the saying of Zuhair: So he gave them the best test that can be given.
44:34: And the reference in his saying: 34- Indeed, these is to the infidels of Quraysh, because the speech is about them, and the story of Pharaoh is presented to indicate their equality in their insistence on disbelief.
44:35: 35- They will say, ‘It is only our first death.’ That is, it is only our first death, which we die in this world, and there is no life after it or resurrection. This is the meaning of His statement, And we will not be resurrected. That is, we will not be resurrected. The speech does not intend to prove another death, but rather what is meant is that the outcome and the end of the matter is only the first death that removes worldly life. Al-Razi said: The meaning is that nothing comes to us from the severe conditions except the first death.
44:36: Then they brought against those who promised them resurrection what they thought was proof, but it is a refuted argument, and they said: 36- Bring our fathers meaning return them after their death to the world if you are truthful in what you say and tell us about the resurrection.
44:37: Then God, the Exalted, responded to them by saying: 37- Are they better or the people of Tubba'? That is, who is better in strength and power: or the people of Tubba' al-Himyari who roamed the world with his armies and defeated and subjugated its people? And in that is a severe threat. And it was said that what is meant by the people of Tubba is all of his followers and not one in particular. Al-Farra' said: The address in His statement: Bring our fathers is to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, alone, like His statement: My Lord, send us back. But it is more appropriate that it is an address to him and his followers from among the Muslims. And what is meant by those before them are Aad, Thamud, and the like. And His statement: We destroyed them is a new clause to explain their condition and the outcome of their affair, and the phrase Indeed, they were criminals is an explanation of their destruction. The meaning is that God, the Exalted, destroyed these people because they were criminals, so His destruction of those who are less than them because they were criminals, despite their weakness and lack of power, is more appropriate. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We certainly tried he said: We tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger he said: He is Moses that you deliver to me the servants of God send with me the Children of Israel and that you do not exalt yourselves above God he said: Do not commit evil I have come to you with clear authority he said: A clear excuse and I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, that you should stone he said: with stones and if you do not believe me then leave that is, leave my way. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, that you deliver to me the servants of God he said: He means follow me to the truth that I call you to. And regarding his statement, and that you do not exalt yourselves above God he said: Do not invent lies. And regarding his statement, that you should stone he said: You should curse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, a sign he said: A mark. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him: Rahwan He said: As it appears and goes. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him that he asked Ka’b about his statement: And leave the sea at ease He said: A path. Ibn Jarir also narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: Rahwan means to leave it as it was. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: And a noble station He said: The pulpits. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jabir something similar. At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym in Al-Hilyah and Al-Khatib narrated from Anas who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: There is no servant but that he has two doors: a door from which his deeds ascend, and a door from which his provision descends. When he dies, they miss him and weep over him. He recited this verse: So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them and mentioned that they did not do any righteous deeds on earth for them to weep over, and no righteous words from their words or deeds ascended to the heavens for them to miss them and to weep over them. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas. Abu al-Shaykh narrated from him that he said: It is said that the earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings. Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Ibn Jarir narrated from Shuraih ibn Ubayd al-Hadrami, with a mursal chain of transmission, that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange as it began. There is no strangeness for a believer. No believer dies in a strange land in which his mourners are absent from him, except that the heavens and the earth weep for him." Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: So neither the heavens nor the earth wept for them, and said: They do not weep for a disbeliever. Ibn al-Mubarak, Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated from al-Musayyab ibn Rafi' that Ali ibn Abi Talib said: When a believer dies, his place of prayer on earth and the place of ascent of his deeds from the sky weep for him. Then he recited the verse. Ibn al-Mubarak, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The earth weeps for the son of Adam for forty mornings. Then he recited the verse. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not insult Tubba’, for he has become a Muslim. Ahmad, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d Al-Sa’idi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said something similar. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of others among the Companions and Followers.
44:38: His statement: 38- And We did not create the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them meaning between the two types of heaven and earth in play meaning without a valid purpose. Muqatil said: We did not create them playing around for no reason. Al-Kalbi said: Heedless, and it was said: Heedless. The majority of scholars read and whatever is between them and Amr ibn Ubayd read and whatever is between them because the heavens and the earth are plural, and players is in the accusative case as a state.
44:39: 39- We did not create them meaning what is between them except with the truth meaning except with the true command, and the exception is devoid of the most general of conditions. Al-Kalbi said: except for the truth, and so did Al-Hasan, and it was said: except to establish the truth and make it manifest. But most of them do not know that the matter is thus, and they are the polytheists.
44:40: 40- The Day of Judgment is their appointed time, all of them. That is, the Day of Resurrection, on which truth will be separated from falsehood, is their appointed time: that is, the time set to distinguish the good-doers from the bad, the truthful from the false, all of them, no one is excluded from that. The reciters of the Qur’an agreed to raise their appointed time as the predicate of in and its subject is the Day of Judgment. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' permitted it to be lowered as its subject and the Day of Judgment as its predicate.
44:41: Then the Almighty described that Day, saying: 41- The Day when no protector will avail another at all. “The Day” is a substitute for The Day of Separation, or it is governed by an implied verb indicated by the separation: that is, a Day will separate them on which there is no benefit. It is not permissible for it to be the object of the separation because the separation between them has been caused by something foreign. The meaning is that on that Day no relative will benefit another relative, nor will anything be repelled from him. Nor will they be helped. The pronoun refers to the protector based on the meaning, because it is an indefinite noun in the context of negation, and it is one of the forms of generality: that is, nor will they be prevented from the punishment of God.
44:42: 42- Except for he upon whom God has mercy. Al-Kisa’i said: The exception is disjunctive, meaning, but for he upon whom God has mercy. Al-Farra’ said the same. It was also said that it is connected, and the meaning is: No relative can avail another relative except the believers, for they will be given permission to intercede and they will intercede. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a substitute for the master of the first, or for the pronoun in they will be helped. “Indeed, it is He who is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful,” meaning the Victorious Who does not help whomever He intends to punish, the Merciful, for His believing servants.
44:43: Then when he described the day, he mentioned after it the threat to the infidels, saying 43- Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum.
44:44: 44- Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * is the food of the sinful. The tree of Zaqqum is the tree that God created in Hell and called it the accursed tree. When the people of Hell are hungry, they take refuge in it and eat from it. We have already discussed the tree of Zaqqum in Surah As-Saffat. The sinful person has much filth. It is stated in As-Sahah: A man commits a sin by breaking it, ithman and ma’athman: if he falls into sin, then he is a sinner, atheem and athum. So the meaning of the food of the sinner is the sinful.
44:45: 45- Kalmahl which is the dregs of oil and the cloudy tar. It was also said that it refers to molten copper. It was also said that everything that melts in fire boils in bellies * like the boiling of scalding water The majority read yajili with the fatha on the basis that the subject is a pronoun referring to the tree, and the sentence is a second predicate or a state, or the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, it boils violently like the boiling of scalding water, which is extremely hot water. Ibn Kathir, Hafs, Ibn Muhaisin, and Warsh on the authority of Yaqub read yajili with the ta' marbuta on the basis that the subject is a pronoun referring to the food, which is in the meaning of a tree, and it is not correct for the pronoun to refer to al-mahl because it is likened to it, but rather what resembles al-mahl boils.
44:46: And his saying: 46- Like the boiling of scalding water is an adjective of a deleted source: meaning boiling like the boiling of scalding water.
44:47: 47- Take him and ride him to the heights of Hellfire. That is, it will be said to the angels who are the guardians of Hellfire: Take him, meaning the sinner, and ride him. Atal means force through violence. It is said that Atalah ya’taluh means he dragged him and took him to something bad. It is also said that Atal means that he takes hold of a man’s collar and genitals and drags him. From this comes the saying of the poet describing a horse: We knock on it, but we do not ride it And from it is the saying of Al-Farazdaq, satirizing Jarir: Until you return to Atiya, you are sick The majority read fa'ataluhu with a kasra on the ta'. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Ibn 'Amir read it with a damma, and these are two dialects. ila sawa'u jahilliya means to its middle, like his saying: Fara'ah wa sawahu wa jahilliya Hellfire.
44:48: 48- Then they poured over his head some of the torment of scalding water. “Min” is the partitive: meaning they poured over his head some of this type, and adding the torment to the scalding water is for clarification: meaning the torment is the scalding water, which is extremely hot water as mentioned above.
44:49: 49- Taste, for you are the honorable, the generous. That is, say to him mockingly, rebukingly, and rebukingly: Taste the torment, for you are the honorable, the generous. It was said that Abu Jahl used to claim that he was the most honorable and generous of the people of the valley, so they would say to him: Taste the torment, you who are arrogant and generous in your claim and in what you used to say. The majority of scholars read inka with a kasra over the hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read it and it was narrated from Ali with a fatha over it, meaning because you. Al-Farra' said: That is, with this statement that you said in this world.
44:50: And the reference in his saying: 50- This to the punishment is what you were in doubt about meaning you were doubting it when you were in this world, and the plural is in consideration of the type of sinner.
44:51: Then the Almighty mentioned the resting place of the righteous, saying: 51- Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure position. That is, those who feared disbelief and sins. The majority of scholars read maqam with a fatha on the meem, while Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a damma. According to the first reading, it is the place of standing, and according to the second reading, it is the place of residence. This was stated by Al-Kisa’i and others. Al-Jawhari said: Each of them may mean residence, or it may mean the place of standing.
44:52: Then he described the station as being safe, ensuring that its owner is safe from all fears. 52- In gardens and springs is a substitute for the station of a trustworthy person, or a statement of it, or a second piece of report.
44:53: 53- They will wear fine silk and heavy brocade is a second or third piece of report or a state of the pronoun implied in the preposition and noun. Fine silk is the finer type of brocade, and heavy brocade is the thicker type. Its explanation was presented in Surat Al-Kahf. The accusative of facing each other is in the state of the subject of they will wear: meaning facing each other in their gatherings, looking at each other.
44:54: The kaf in His statement: 54- Thus is either an adjective of a deleted verbal noun: meaning We deal with the righteous in this manner. Or it is raised as a predicate for a deleted subject: meaning the matter is thus. And We married them to beautiful women with wide, beautiful eyes. Meaning, We honored them by marrying them to beautiful women with wide, beautiful eyes. Hoor is the plural of hawra', which means white, and ayn is the plural of ayna', which means wide-eyed. Mujahid said: The reason for the name hawra' is because the eye is dazzled by her beauty. It was also said that it is from hoor al-'ayn, which is the intense whiteness of the eye in contrast to its intense blackness. This is what Abu Ubaidah said. Al-Asma'i said: I do not know what hoor al-'ayn is. Abu Amr said: Hoor is when the entire eye is black like the eyes of gazelles and cows. He said: "There are no houris among the children of Adam. Women are only called houris because they resemble gazelles and cows." It was also said that what is meant by His statement, We married them is that We paired them and it is not from the marriage contract, because it is not said that he married him to a woman. Abu Ubaidah said: And We made them husbands for them as a husband marries another husband: that is, We made them two by two, and Al-Akhfash said the same.
44:55: 55- Therein they will call for every kind of fruit, secure. That is, they will be commanded to bring whatever fruits they desire while they are safe from harm, illness, and pain. Qatada said: Safe from death, illness, and Satan. It was also said that the bliss they are enjoying will be cut off.
44:56: 56- They will not taste death therein except the first death. That is, they will never die therein except the death they tasted in this world. The exception is disconnected, meaning, but the death they tasted in this world. This is what Az-Zajjaj, Al-Farra’ and others said. Similar to this verse is His statement, And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred. It was said that except means after, like your saying, I did not speak to a man today except a man with you, meaning after a man with you. It was also said that it means except, meaning except for the first death. Ibn Qutaybah said, “The reason for excluding the first death, which is in this world, is because when the happy ones die, by God’s grace and power, they are transported to the causes of Paradise. They encounter the spirit and basil, and they see their homes in Paradise, and its doors are opened for them. So when they die in this world, it is as if they died in Paradise due to their connection to its causes and their witnessing of it. So, in this case, the exception is connected.” Ibn Jarir chose that illa means after, and Ibn Atiyyah chose that it means except, “and He protected them from the torment of Hellfire.” The majority read waqahum with a light waqahum, while Abu Haywah read it with a heavy waqahum for emphasis.
44:57: 57- A favor from your Lord meaning because of His favor, or He gave them that as a gift from Him. That is the great triumph meaning that what was mentioned above is the triumph after which there is no triumph, which is infinitely great.
44:58: Then when the Almighty explained the evidence and mentioned the promise and the threat, He said: 58- We have only made it easy in your language that they may remember. That is, We have only sent down the Qur’an in your language so that your people may understand it, remember, consider, and act upon what is in it, or We have made it easy in your language for you and for those who read it that they may remember.
44:59: 59- So wait, for they are waiting. That is, wait for what We promised you of victory over them and their destruction at your hand, for they are waiting for whatever death or other thing will befall you. It was also said: Wait for God to judge between you and them, for they are waiting for you to face the calamities of time. The meaning is similar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Taste, for indeed, you are the mighty, the generous, meaning: I am neither mighty nor generous. Al-Umawi narrated in his book, Al-Maghazi, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met Abu Jahl and said: God has commanded me to say to you: ‘It is better for you, then better, then better, then better,’ so he took his hand away from him and said: You and your companion cannot do anything to me. You know that I can protect the people of Batha’, and I am the mighty, the generous. So God killed him on the day of Badr, humiliated him, and reproached him with His word, and revealed: ‘Taste, for indeed, you are the mighty, the generous.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * is the food of the sinner, he said: The molten metal. He also narrated on his authority: Taste, for indeed, you are the mighty, the generous, he said: He is Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. Praise be to God Almighty, the fourth part has been printed, followed by: the fifth part The first: Interpretation of Surat Al-Jathiya.
45:1: It is thirty-seven verses, and some say thirty-six. It is all Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Jabir, and Ikrimah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Al-Zubayr that it was revealed in Mecca. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah that they both said: except for one verse, which is the verse: for those who believe until the days of God, for it was revealed in Medina about Umar ibn Al-Khattab, as will be mentioned. 1- His saying: Ha Meem. We have already discussed this opening and its parsing in the opening of Surat Ghafir and what follows it. If it is made a name for the surah, then its place is in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject or a subject. If it is made into letters listed in the manner of enumeration, then it has no place.
45:2: And his saying: The revelation of the Book in the first version is a second predicate, and in the second version it is a predicate of the subject, and in the third version it is a predicate of a deleted subject, or a subject and its predicate from God, the Almighty, the Wise.
45:3: 3- Then the Almighty informed us of what indicates His dazzling power, saying: Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers, meaning in themselves, for they are among the types of signs, or in their creation.
45:4: 4- Al-Zajjaj said: What indicates that the meaning is in the creation of the heavens and the earth is his statement: And in your creation meaning in your creation of yourselves in different stages. Muqatil said: From dust then from a sperm-drop until he becomes a human. And what He disperses of moving creatures are signs meaning in the creation of what He disperses of moving creatures. The raising of signs is as a delayed subject and its predicate is the circumstantial adverbial phrase before it. The majority of scholars read it in the nominative case, and Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read signs in the accusative case in apposition to the name of inna. The predicate is his statement: And in your creation as if it was said: And indeed in your creation and what He disperses of moving creatures are signs, or as an emphasis on the first signs. The majority also read Signs for a people who know in the nominative case, while Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it in the accusative case, while agreeing on the genitive case in ikhtilaf. As for the genitive case of ikhtilaf, it is based on the assumption of the preposition, i.e. and in the difference between night and day are verses. So whoever raises ayat, it is based on the fact that it is the subject, and its predicate is fi ikhtilaf. As for the accusative case, it is a case of conjunction with the objects of two different operators. Al-Farra' said: The nominative case is for resumption after in. The Arabs say: Indeed I owe you wealth, and Your brother owes wealth. They place the second in the accusative case and the nominative case, and grammarians have discussed this issue at length. The discussion of the issue of conjunction with the objects of two different operators, the arguments of those who permit it, and the answers of those who forbid it, is established in the science of grammar and explained in detail in its long volumes. The meaning of what He spreads of a creature is that which He disperses and spreads.
45:5: 5- And the alternation of night and day is their succession or their difference in length and shortness. His statement: And what God has sent down from the sky of provision is connected to the difference. Provision is rain, because it is the cause of everything with which God provides His servants. The revival of the earth: the production of its vegetation, and its death: its being devoid of vegetation. And the meaning of the changing of the winds is that they blow sometimes from one direction and sometimes from another, sometimes it is hot and sometimes it is cold, sometimes it is beneficial and sometimes it is harmful.
45:6: 6- These are the verses of God which We recite to you meaning these verses mentioned are God's proofs and evidence. The place of We recite them to you is the accusative case of state, and it is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as the predicate of the demonstrative pronoun, and the verses of God are an explanation of it or a substitute for it. His saying: with the truth is a state of the subject of we recite, or of its object: meaning, truthful, or mixed with the truth. It is possible that the preposition with is for causality, so it is related to the verb itself. Then in what statement after God and His verses will they believe? meaning after the speech of God and after His verses. It was said that what is meant is: Then in what statement after the verses of God? And the mention of the noble name is only for the purpose of glorifying the verses, so it is from the category of: I admire Zayd and his generosity. It was said that what is meant is after the speech of God, which is the Qur'an, as in His saying: God has sent down the best statement, which is what is meant by the verses, and the conjunction is for the sake of the difference in title. The majority read you believe with the superlative, while Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with the subjunctive.
