Meaning: They believe in any hadith, but it was presented before it because the question is at the beginning of the speech.
45:7: 7- Woe to every slanderer and sinner meaning every liar who commits many sins and does what is required of him, and woe is a valley in Hell.
45:8: 8- Then he described this liar with another attribute, saying: He hears the verses of God recited to him. It was said that hears is in the accusative case as a state, and it was said that it is a resumption, but the first is better. His saying: are recited to him is in the accusative case as a state, then he persists in his disbelief and remains as he was while he was arrogant, meaning he persists in his disbelief, feeling too proud to submit to the truth. Persistence is taken from the donkey’s persistence on the pubis, which is when it bends over it, bending its ears. Muqatil said: If it hears something from the verses of the Qur’an, it takes it as a joke. The phrase as if it had not heard it is in the accusative case as a state, or is a resumption. An is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its subject is a deleted pronoun of matter. Then give him tidings of a painful punishment. This is from the category of mockery: meaning, give him tidings of a very painful punishment for his persistence, arrogance, and refusal to listen to the verses.
45:9: 9- And if he learns something of Our signs, the majority read it as knows with a fatha on the ‘ayn and a kasra on the lam, lightened, in the active form. Qatadah and Matar al-Warraq read it as a passive form. The meaning is that if he learns something of God’s signs, he takes it meaning the signs in ridicule. It was said that the pronoun in takes it refers to something, because it refers to the signs, but the former is more appropriate. The reference in His statement, those is to every liar who is described by those characteristics. For them is a humiliating punishment because of what they did of persisting and being arrogant about hearing God’s signs and taking them in ridicule. A humiliating punishment is one that includes humiliation and disgrace.
45:10: 10- Behind them is Hell meaning behind what they are in of being arrogant about the world and being haughty about the truth is Hell, for it is in front of them because they are facing it, and He used the expression behind to mean in front, like His saying: Behind him is Hell and the saying of the poet: Isn't he behind me if my death is delayed? It was said that it was made in consideration of their turning away from it as if it were behind them. And what they have earned will not avail them at all meaning that what they have earned of their wealth and children will not ward off from them anything of God’s punishment, nor will it benefit them in any way. And what they have taken besides God as protectors is conjoined with what they have earned: meaning that what they have taken besides God as protectors from the idols will not avail them at all. Ma in both places is either a source or a relative pronoun, and the addition of la in the second sentence is for emphasis. And for them is a great punishment in Hell, which is behind them.
45:11: 11- This is guidance is a renewed sentence consisting of a subject and a predicate, meaning this Qur'an is guidance for those who are guided by it. And those who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord of the Qur'an, for them is a punishment of a painful punishment. A punishment is the most severe punishment. The majority of scholars read painful in the accusative case as an attribute of a punishment. Ibn Kathir, Hafs, and Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative case as an attribute of a punishment.
45:12: 12- God is He who has subjected the sea to you meaning He made it in a way that enables you to ride it so that ships may sail therein by His command meaning with His permission and decree for you and that you may seek of His bounty sometimes by trade, diving for pearls, processing fish, and other things and that you may be grateful meaning so that you may be grateful for the blessings that you obtain because of this subjecting of the sea.
45:13: 13- And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him. That is, He has subjected to His servants whatever He created in His heavens and earth, which is related to their interests and through which their livelihoods are sustained. Among the heavenly creations He has subjected to them are the sun, the moon, the bright stars, the rain, the clouds, and the winds. The accusative case of all is in the hal of what is in the heavens and what is on the earth or to emphasize it. His statement: from Him may be related to something omitted which is an attribute of all: that is, created from Him. It may also be related to subjugated, or it may be a hal of what is in the heavens, or a predicate of an omitted subject. The meaning is that all of that is a mercy from Him to His servants. Indeed in that mentioned of subjection are signs for a people who give thought. He specified those who give thought because only those who give thought will benefit from them, as they move from thought to using them as evidence for monotheism.
45:15: Then he mentioned the believers and their deeds and the polytheists and their deeds, saying: 15- Whoever does righteousness does so for his own soul, and whoever does evil does so against it. The meaning is that the deeds of each group, whether good or evil, done to the one who does them will not extend to others, and in it there is encouragement and threat. Then to your Lord you will be returned. He will reward each one for his deeds, if they were good then good, and if they were evil then evil. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azmah narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, All of it is from Him, that he said: From Him is the light, the sun, and the moon. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse, that he said: Everything is from God. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Tawus that he said: A man came to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As and asked him, From what He created creation? He said, From water, light, darkness, wind, and dust. He said, Then from what He created these? He said, I do not know. Then the man came to Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr and asked him, and he said the same as Abdullah ibn Amr. Then he came to Ibn Abbas and asked him, From what He created creation? He said, From water, light, darkness, wind, and dust. He said, Then from what He created these? Ibn Abbas recited, And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth—all from Him. The man said, “No one could have done this except a man from the family of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Tell those who believe to forgive verse 11, that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would turn away from the polytheists when they harmed him, and they would mock him and call him a liar. Then God commanded him to fight all the polytheists, and this was one of the abrogated verses.
45:16: 16- His statement: And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood. What is meant by the Scripture is the Torah, and by wisdom is the understanding and comprehension by which judgment is made between people and the settlement of their disputes, and by prophethood is the one whom God sent among the prophets among them. And We provided them with good things, meaning the pleasures that God made lawful for them, including manna and quails. And We preferred them over the worlds, of the people of their time, as We gave them what We did not give to anyone other than them, such as the splitting of the sea and the like.
45:17: This was explained in Surah Ad-Dukhan 17 - And We gave them clear proofs of the matter meaning clear laws regarding what is permissible and what is forbidden, or apparent miracles. It was said that it meant knowledge of the mission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the evidence of his prophethood, and the specification of his migration. But they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them meaning that they did not differ about that matter except after knowledge had come to them, explaining it and clarifying its meaning. So they made what necessitates the removal of the difference a reason for its establishment. It was said that what is meant by knowledge is Joshua bin Nun, for some of them believed in him and some of them disbelieved. It was also said that it was the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they differed about it out of envy and malice. It was also said that it was malice from some of them against each other in seeking leadership. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ regarding the matter of religion. He will reward the doer of good for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing.
45:18: 18- Then We placed you, O Muhammad, upon a clear way of religion Sharia in the language means doctrine, religion, and method. It is said: for a water source which is a place where its drinkers come to drink, Sharia, and from this comes the word street because it is a path to the destination. So what is meant by Sharia here is what God has legislated for His servants of religion, and the plural is Shara’i’: meaning We placed you, O Muhammad, upon a clear way of religion which leads you to the truth. So follow it So implement its rulings in your nation. And do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know the Oneness of God and His laws for His servants, and they are the disbelievers of Quraysh and those who agreed with them.
45:19: 19- They will never avail you against God at all meaning they will not ward off from you anything that God wants for you if you follow their desires. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another meaning supporters who support one another. Ibn Zayd said: The hypocrites are the allies of the Jews. And God is the ally of the righteous meaning He is their supporter. What is meant by the righteous are those who avoid polytheism and sins.
45:20: And the reference in his saying: 20- This is to the Qur’an or to following the Shari’ah, and it is a subject and its predicate is insights for the people meaning proofs and evidence for them regarding what they need of the rulings of religion. He made that like insights in the hearts and it was read This is insights: meaning these verses, because the Qur’an has the same meaning as the poet said: Question Bani Asad, what is this sound? Because the voice means a shout, and guidance means right guidance and a path that leads to Paradise for whoever acts upon it, and mercy from God in the Hereafter, for a people who are certain meaning that it is their nature to be certain and not to doubt or waver in doubt.
45:21: 21- Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who have believed and done righteous deeds - meaning, We will make them equal, despite their committing evil deeds, and the people of good deeds, their life and their death are the same in this world and in the Hereafter. No, they are not equal, for the state of the people of happiness in both is not the state of the people of misery. It was said that what is meant is denying that they will be equal in death as they were equal in life. The majority read equal in the nominative case as an advanced predicate, and the subject is their life and death, and the meaning is denying that they will be equal in death. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and Hafs read sawa’u in the accusative case as a state of the hidden pronoun in the prepositional phrase like those who believed or as a second object of hasaba. Abu Ubaid chose the accusative reading and said that it means: We will make them equal. Al-A’mash and Isa bin Umar read mamatuhum in the accusative case, meaning equal in their life and death. When the preposition was dropped, it was made accusative, or as a substitute for the object of naja’alhum as a substitute for inclusion. Sa’a ma juhkimuhum means evil is this judgment that they made.
45:22: 22- And God created the heavens and the earth in truth meaning in truth that requires justice among the servants. The place of in truth is in the accusative case as a state of the subject, or of the object, or the preposition with is for causality. His statement, And that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned may be in the case of truth, because each of them is a cause, so the cause is conjoined with the cause. It may also be conjoined with something omitted, and the meaning is: God created the heavens and the earth to demonstrate His power and to recompense. It may be that the preposition with is for becoming. And they are not wronged meaning the souls indicated by every soul are not wronged by a reduction in reward or an increase in punishment. Then He, the Most High, is amazed at the state of the disbelievers.
45:23: 23- He said: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his own desire? Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: That is the disbeliever who has taken as his religion what he desires, so he does not desire anything except that he does it. Ikrimah said: He worships what he desires or finds good, and if he finds something good and what he desires good, he takes it as a god. Saeed bin Jubair said: One of them used to worship a stone, and if he saw something better than it, he would throw it away and worship another. And God led him astray, knowingly, meaning, knowing that He knew it. It was also said that the meaning is: He led him astray from the reward, knowing that he did not deserve it. Muqatil said: Knowingly, he was astray because he knew that an idol could neither benefit nor harm. Al-Zajjaj said: He had bad knowledge that he was astray before God created him. The place of on knowledge is in the accusative case as a state of the subject or the object. And He set a seal upon his hearing and his heart means He imprinted upon his hearing so that he would not hear the sermon, and He imprinted upon his heart so that he would not understand the guidance. And He placed over his vision a covering meaning a veil so that he would not see the right path. The majority read a covering with an alif and a kasra on the ghain. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read a covering without an alif and with a fatha on the ghain. From this is the saying of the poet: If you have clothed me in a veil, I have listened to you affectionately for a while. Ibn Masoud and Al-A'mash read it as the majority did, with a fat-ha on the ghain, which is the dialect of Rabi'ah. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah read some of them, which is the dialect of Ikl, So who will guide him after God? meaning after God has led him astray. Will you not then remember? Remembering is considering so that you may know the true state of affairs.
45:24: Then God, the Almighty, explained some of their ignorance and misguidance, saying: 24- And they say, 'There is nothing but our worldly life.' That is, what is life except the life we are in? We die and we live. That is, death and life befall us in it, and there is no life beyond that. It was also said that we die and our children live in it, and it was also said that we are dead sperm and then we become alive. It was said that there is an inversion of the verse: that is, we live and we die. Ibn Mas'ud recited it this way. In any case, what they meant by this statement was to deny the resurrection and to belie the afterlife. And nothing destroys us except time. That is, nothing destroys us except the passing of days and nights. Mujahid said: He means years and days. Qatadah said: Except lifespan, and the meaning is the same. Qatrab said: The meaning is, nothing destroys us except death. Ikrimah said: Nothing destroys us except God. And they have no knowledge of that. That is, they said this statement only out of doubt and lack of knowledge of the truth. Then he explained that this was done by them and not based on knowledge, saying: They only conjecture, meaning that they are only a people whose only conjecture is conjecture, so they only speak about it and rely on it.
45:25: 25- And when Our clear verses are recited to them meaning when the verses of the Qur’an are recited to the polytheists while they are clear and evident in meaning and indication of the resurrection their only argument is that they say, ‘Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful’ We will be resurrected after death: meaning they had no argument or hold on to anything except this false statement which has no basis in any argument, and He only called it an argument to mock them. The majority of scholars read the word their argument in the accusative case as the predicate of was, and its subject is except that they said. Zayd ibn Ali, Amr ibn Ubayd, and Ubayd ibn Umar read the word their argument in the nominative case as the subject of was.
45:26: Then God, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to respond to them, saying: 26- “Say: God gives you life,” meaning in this world, then causes you to die, when your appointed times have come to an end, then He will assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, with resurrection and revival, there is no doubt about it, meaning about your assembly, because He who was able to initiate creation was able to bring it back, but most people do not know, of that. For this reason, they had doubts about the resurrection, and they came to refute it with something weaker than a spider’s web. If they had looked with the right eye, they would have attained certain knowledge, doubt would have been removed from them, and they would have relieved themselves of the predicament of doubt and confusion. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, {Then We put you on a way of religion}, meaning: on guidance regarding the matter of His religion. Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid regarding his statement, {Their life and their death are the same}, he said: The believer in this world and the hereafter is a believer, and the disbeliever in this world and the hereafter is a disbeliever. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, {Have you seen he who takes as his god his own desire}, he said: That disbeliever took his religion without guidance from God or proof. {And God has sent him astray due to knowledge}, meaning: He sent him astray due to His foreknowledge. An-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him that he said: A man from the Arabs would worship a stone, and if he found a better one he would take it and throw away the other, so God revealed: {Have you seen he who takes as his god his own desire}. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The people of the Jahiliyyah used to say, ‘It is only the night and the day that destroy us.’ So God said in His Book, ‘And they say, “There is nothing but our worldly life. We die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.” God said, ‘The son of Adam insults time, and I am time. In My hand is the command. I alternate night and day.’” Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, ‘God said, Almighty God said: “The son of Adam harms Me by cursing time, and I am time. In My hand is the matter. I alternate night and day.”
45:27: When the Almighty mentioned the argument that the polytheists used and how He answered them, He mentioned that He is the only One with dominion, saying: 27- And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, meaning that He alone is the One who controls them, and none of His servants share with Him. Then He threatened the people of falsehood, saying: And on the Day the Hour arises, that Day the falsifiers will lose, meaning that the disbelieving disbelievers who cling to the false ones will see their loss on that Day because they will go to the Fire. The agent in on the Day is he who loses, and on that Day is a substitute for it, and the tanween is to replace the complement indicated by what the complement is added to, so the meaning is: and on the Day the Hour arises, so it is a confirmatory substitute. It is better for the agent in on the Day to be is dominion, meaning that to God belongs dominion on the Day the Hour arises, and on that Day will be the object of to lose.
45:28: 28- And you will see every nation kneeling The address is to everyone who is fit for it, or to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The nation is the religion. The meaning of kneeling is prostrated, and the one who is provoked is the one from whom nothing touches the ground except his knees and the tips of his fingers, and that is at the time of judgment. It was said that the meaning of kneeling is gathered. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is and you will see the people of every religion gathered. Ikrimah said: distinct from the others. Mu'ajj said: its meaning in the language of Quraysh is: submissive. Al-Hasan said: kneeling on the knees. And kneeling is sitting on the knees. You say jatha yajtuhu and yajtihi jathuwan and jathuan: if he sat on his knees, and the first is more appropriate. This is not contradicted by the occurrence of this word for another meaning in the Arabic language. The term jathwa has been used to refer to a group of everything in the Arabic language, such as the saying of Tarafa describing two graves: You see two bodies of dirt, on which are solid sheets of arranged sheets. The apparent meaning of the verse is that this attribute applies to every nation, without any difference between the followers of the religions that follow the messengers and other polytheists. Yahya ibn Salam said: It is specific to the disbelievers, but the former is more appropriate. This is supported by His statement: Every nation will be called to its book, and His statement later: As for those who have believed, and the meaning of to its book is to the book revealed to it. It was also said: to its record of deeds, or to its accounting, or to the Preserved Tablet, but the former is more appropriate. The majority of scholars read every nation in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is: will be called. Ya’qub al-Hadrami read it in the accusative case as a substitute for every nation. “This Day you will be recompensed for what you used to do,” meaning that it will be said to them: This Day you will be recompensed for what you used to do, both good and evil.
45:29: 29- This is Our Book that speaks against you with the truth. This is part of what is said to them, and the one who says this is the angels. It has also been said that it is from the statement of God, the Most High: meaning, it bears witness against you, and it is a metaphor. It is said that the Book speaks of such-and-such: meaning, it makes clear. It has also been said that they read it and remember what they did, so it is as if it speaks against them with the truth that has no addition or subtraction. The place of speaks is the accusative as a state, or the nominative as another predicate of the demonstrative pronoun. The phrase Indeed, We were transcribing what you used to do is an explanation for speaking the truth, meaning, We command the angels to transcribe your deeds: that is, to write them down and record them for you. Al-Wahidi said: Most of the commentators agree that this transcribing is from the Preserved Tablet, for the angels write from it every year what is of the children of Adam and they find that in agreement with what they do. They said: Because transcribing can only be from an original. It has also been said that the meaning is: We command the angels to transcribe what you used to do. It is said that the angels write down the deeds of the servant every day. When they return to their places, they delete the good and bad deeds and leave out the permissible deeds. It is also said that when the angels present the deeds of the servants to God, the Almighty, He orders that those deeds that contain reward and punishment be recorded with Him, and those that contain neither reward nor punishment are dropped.
45:30: 30- As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is, admit them into His mercy. That is the clear attainment. That is, the apparent and clear.
45:31: 31- And as for those who disbelieved, were not My verses recited to you? That is, were they not told that, and it is a question of rebuke, because the messengers had come to them and the verses of God were recited to them, but they denied them and did not act upon them. Then you were arrogant and were a criminal people. That is, you were too arrogant to accept them or believe in them, and you were among the people of ihram, which is sins, and ijatram is acquisition. It is said that someone is the crime of his al-Nas 114:if he is their earner, so the criminal is the one who acquires sins by doing transgressions.
45:32: 32- And when it is said, ‘The promise of God is true’ meaning His promise of resurrection and judgment, or that He will gather together what He promised of future matters, will inevitably happen. And the Hour meaning the Resurrection there is no doubt about it meaning about its occurrence. The majority of scholars read and the Hour in the nominative case as a subject, or in apposition to the position of the subject of in. Hamzah read it in the accusative case in apposition to the subject of in. “You say, ‘We do not know what the Hour is’” meaning what it is? We only think an assumption meaning we surmise and imagine an illusion. Al-Mubarrad said: Its meaning is: We only think a thought. It was said that the meaning is: We only think that you think a thought. It was said that we think includes the meaning of we believe: that is, we only believe a thought, not knowledge. It was said that thought has an implied quality: that is, except a clear thought. It was said that thought can mean knowledge and doubt, so it is as if they said: We have no belief except doubt. And we are not certain, that is, we had no certainty in that, and we had nothing with us except a mere thought that the Hour was coming.
45:33: 33- And the evils of what they did will become apparent to them meaning the evils of their actions will appear to them as they are and that which they used to ridicule will encompass them meaning it will surround them and the punishment for their actions will descend upon them by making them enter the Fire.
45:34: 34- And it will be said, ‘Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours.’ That is, We will leave you in the Fire as you left off working for this Day. He added the meeting to the Day as an expansion, because he added to the thing what it is in. And your refuge is the Fire, that is, your dwelling and your abode to which you will take refuge. And you will have no helpers, to help you and prevent the punishment from you.
45:35: 35- That is because you took the verses of God in jest meaning that this punishment is because you took the Qur’an in jest and play and the worldly life deceived you meaning it tricked you with its decorations and falsehoods, so you thought that there is no home other than it, no resurrection or revival. So today they will not come out of it meaning from the Fire. The majority read yujruju with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the ra’, in the passive voice, in the third person to belittle them. Nor will they be asked to repent meaning that they will not be appeased and asked to return to the obedience of God, because on that day no repentance will be accepted and no excuse will be of any use.
45:36: 36- So praise be to God, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds. None deserves praise except Him. The majority of scholars read Lord in the three instances in the genitive case as an adjective for the noble name. Mujahid, Hamid, and Ibn Muhaisin read it in the nominative case in the three instances, assuming it is a subject: meaning, He is the Lord of the heavens, etc.
45:37: 37- And to Him belongs pride in the heavens and the earth meaning majesty, greatness, and authority. He specified the heavens and the earth because this is evident in them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise meaning the Exalted in His power. No one can overcome Him. He is Wise in all His actions, words, and all His judgments. Saeed bin Mansour, Abdullah bin Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba'th narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Babaah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is as if I see you kneeling on a mound before Hellfire. Then Sufyan recited: And He will see every nation kneeling. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding His statement: And you will see every nation kneeling, that he said: Every nation will be with its Prophet until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) comes on a mound that has risen above all creation, and that is the praised station. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: This is Our Book that speaks against you with truth, that he said: It is the Mother of the Book in which are the deeds of the children of Adam. Indeed, We were recording what you used to do, that he said: They are the angels who record the deeds of the children of Adam. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated a similar narration at length from him. A man stood up and said: O Ibn Abbas, we did not see the angels writing this down every day and night. Ibn Abbas said: You are not an Arab people. Indeed, We used to record what you did. Can something be recorded except from a book? Ibn Jarir also narrated something similar from him. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: God has angels who descend every day with something in which they record the deeds of the children of Adam. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Umar something similar to what was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: The angels record from the Mother of the Book what the children of Adam do. Man only does what the angel records from the Mother of the Book. Al-Hakim narrated something similar from him and authenticated it. At-Tabarani also narrated from him regarding the verse: “God and all His angels copy from that year in Ramadan, on the Night of Decree, whatever happens on earth, to a similar one in the following year. Then the guardians of God, may He be exalted, will compare it with the servants on the eve of every Thursday, and they will find that what the guardians have lifted agrees with what is in their book, with no addition or subtraction.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding His statement: This Day We will forget you as you forgot the meeting with this Day of yours, he said: We will abandon you. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: Pride is My cloak and greatness is My garment. Whoever disputes with Me over one of them, I will throw him into the Fire.”
46:1: It is thirty-four verses, and it was said thirty-five It is a Meccan verse. Al-Qurtubi said: According to the saying of all of them: Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr, they said: Surat Ha Mim al-Ahqaf was revealed in Mecca. Ibn al-Durais and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) taught me Surat al-Ahqaf, and another recited it but he differed from his recitation. I said: ‘Who taught you it?’ He said: ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).’ I said: ‘By God, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) taught me something different.’ So we came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and I said: ‘O Messenger of God, did you not teach me such and such?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ The other said: ‘Did you not teach me such and such?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ The face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) became red, and he said: ‘Let each of you recite what he heard, for those who came before you were destroyed only because of differences.’” His saying: 1- Ha Meem We have already discussed this in Surah Ghafir and what follows it in full, and we have mentioned the reason for the grammatical analysis and clarified what is true, that the openings of the surahs are among the ambiguous, the knowledge of which must be entrusted to the One who revealed it.
46:2: 2- The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. We have already discussed this in detail in Surah Ghafir and what follows it, and we have mentioned the reason for the grammatical analysis and clarified what is true, that the openings of the surahs are among the ambiguous, the knowledge of which must be entrusted to the One who revealed it.
46:3: 2- We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them of all the creations except with the truth is an exception devoid of the most knowledgeable conditions, that is, except a creation mixed with the truth required by the Divine Will. His statement, and a specified term is conjoined with the truth: that is, except with the truth, and with a specified term is based on the assumption of a deleted complement: that is, and with the assumption of a specified term, and this term is the Day of Resurrection, for on that day the heavens and the earth and what is between them will come to an end and the earth will be replaced by something other than the earth and the heavens. It was said that what is meant by the specified term is the end of the term of each individual of the creations, and the first was for something else, rather it was created for reward and punishment. And those who disbelieve - from that of which they are warned - are turning away that is, from that of which they are warned and frightened in the Qur’an of resurrection, judgment, and recompense, they are turning away from it, not believing in it. What is in His statement, they were not warned may be the relative pronoun, or it may be the source.
46:4: 3- “Say: Have you seen what you call upon besides God?” That is, tell me what you worship besides God of idols. Show me what they have created from the earth. That is, what thing they have created from it. His saying, Show me may be an emphasis on his saying, Have you seen? That is, tell me, Show me. The second object is have you seen “what they have created.” It may also be that it is not an emphasis, but rather this is a case of dispute, because Have you seen requires a second object, and Show me is likewise. Or do they have a share in the heavens? This is the disjunctive particle understood by bal and the hamza, and the meaning is: Rather, He has inspired a share with God in it. The question is for rebuke and reprimand. Bring me a book before this. This is a rebuke to them and a demonstration of their inability and inability to produce that. The reference in his saying this is to the Qur’an, for it has clearly stated the invalidity of polytheism, that God is One without partner, and that the Hour is true, there is no doubt about it. So do the polytheists have a book that contradicts this book? Or an argument that contradicts this argument, or a trace of knowledge. It is said in As-Sahah: Or a trace of knowledge, a remainder of it, and so is Athara with the fat-ha. Ibn Qutaybah said: Meaning a remainder of the knowledge of the ancients. Al-Farra’ and Al-Mubarrad said: It means what is transmitted from the books of the ancients. Al-Wahidi said: This is the meaning of the commentators’ statement. Ata’ said: Or something you transmitted from a prophet who came before Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Muqatil said: Or a narration from knowledge from the prophets. Al-Zajjaj said: Or Athara: It is said I transmitted the hadith, Athara, Athara, and Athara: if you mentioned it from someone other than you. The majority read Athhara as a verbal noun, like Samahah and Al-Ghawayah. Ibn Abbas, Zaid bin Ali, Ikrimah, As-Sulami, Al-Hasan, and Abu Raja’ read it with the fat-ha on the hamza and the tha’ without an alif. Al-Kisa’i read Athara with a damma on the hamza and a sukoon on the tha’ if you are truthful in your claim that you are making, which is your saying that God has a partner and you did not bring anything of that, so the invalidity of their statement is clear due to the establishment of rational and textual proof to the contrary.
46:5: 4- And who is more astray than he who invokes besides God those who do not respond to him? That is, no one is more astray or more ignorant than him, for he invokes one who does not hear, so how can he hope for an answer, let alone bringing benefit or warding off harm? Thus, it is clear that he is the most ignorant of the ignorant and the most astray of the misguided. The question is for correction and rebuke. His statement, until the Day of Resurrection is the limit for the lack of response. And they, of their invocation, are unaware. The first pronoun refers to the idols, and the second refers to their worshippers. The meaning is: And the idols that they invoke are unaware of their invocation to them. They do not hear nor do they understand, because they are inanimate. The plural in the two pronouns is based on the meaning of who. He applied to the idols what is for rational beings, because the polytheists believed that they had reason.
46:6: 5- And when mankind is gathered together, they will be enemies to them. That is, when the idol worshippers are gathered together, the idols will be enemies to them, disowning each other and cursing each other. It has been said that God creates life in idols, so they deny them. It has also been said that what is meant is that they deny them and are hostile to them in their actions, not in their words. As for the angels, the Messiah, Ezra, and the devils, they will disown those who worshipped them on the Day of Resurrection, as in the saying of God the Almighty: We declare our disavowal to You that they used to worship us. “And they were disbelievers in their worship.” That is, the worshipped ones were disbelievers in the worship of the polytheists, meaning they denied and rejected them. It has been said that the pronoun in were refers to the worshippers, as in His saying: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists. The first is more appropriate.
46:7: 6- And when Our verses are recited to them, meaning the verses of the Qur’an, when they are clear, with clear meanings and obvious indications, those who disbelieve say about the truth, meaning because of it and regarding it, which is the verses, when it has come to them, meaning at the time it came to them, this is obvious magic, meaning obvious magic.
46:8: 7- Or do they say, 'He invented it'? "Umm" is the disconnected form: meaning, rather, do they say, "He invented it? The question is for denial and astonishment at their actions, and rather, to shift from calling their verses magic to their saying, The Messenger of God invented what he brought," and in that there is a rebuke and rebuke that is not hidden. Then God Almighty commanded him to answer them, saying, "Say, 'If I invented it, then you do not possess for me anything from God.' That is, say, If I invented it, hypothetically and estimatingly, as you claim, then you are not able to ward off God's punishment from me. So how can I invent it against God for your sake, while you are not able to ward off His punishment from me? He knows best what you indulge in, that is, what you indulge in of denial and indulgence in something, delving into it and rushing into it. It is said, They indulged in the hadith, meaning they rushed into it, and the camel indulged: if it pushed its water from its stomach. Meaning: God knows best what you say about the Qur’an and what you engage in regarding it, denying it and claiming that it is magic and divination. That is sufficient as a witness between me and you, for He bears witness for me that the Qur’an is from Him and that I have conveyed it to you, and He bears witness against you regarding your denial and rejection. In this is a severe threat. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, for whoever repents, believes, acknowledges the Qur’an, and acts according to what is in it: meaning, He is abundant in forgiveness and mercy and is eloquent in them.
46:9: 8- Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers.’ Innovations in everything are the beginning: meaning I am not the first messenger, God had sent many messengers before me. It has been said that innovations mean the innovated, like light and light, and innovation is that which has no equal, from innovation, which is invention, and something is innovation with the kasra: meaning innovative, and so-and-so is an innovator in this matter: meaning innovative, thus said Al-Akhfash, and Qutrub recited: I am not an exception to the incidents that befall men who became happier after Moses. Ikrimah, Abu Haywah and Ibn Abi Ubla read "Bid'aan" with a fat-ha on the dal, assuming the omission of the complement: i.e. I was not a person of innovations. Mujahid read it with a fat-ha on the door and a kasra on the dal, describing it as "and I do not know what will be done to me or to you", i.e. what will be done to me in the future: will I remain in Mecca or leave it? Will I die or be killed? Will the punishment be hastened for you or will you be given respite? This only applies to this world. As for the Hereafter, it is known that he and his nation are in Paradise and that the disbelievers are in Hell. It was said that the meaning is: I do not know what will be done to me or to you on the Day of Resurrection. When this verse was revealed, the polytheists rejoiced and said: How can we follow a prophet who does not know what will be done to him or to us, and who has no superiority over us? Then the Almighty’s saying was revealed: That God may forgive you your sins, past and future. The first is more appropriate: I only follow what is revealed to me. The majority read is revealed, clarifying the object: that is, I only follow the Qur’an and I do not innovate anything of my own. The meaning is: He limited his actions, may God bless him and grant him peace, to revelation, not limited his following to revelation. And I am only a clear warner, that is, I warn you of God’s punishment and frighten you with His torment, in a clear manner. Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or a trace of knowledge. He said: Handwriting. Sufyan said: “I do not know of any hadith except from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), meaning that the hadith is attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), not to Ibn Abbas. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “There was a prophet among the prophets who used to write, so whoever came across something like his handwriting would know.” The meaning of this is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, but scholars have different interpretations of it. How can we know that these lines in the sand correspond to that writing? And where is the authentic chain of transmission back to that prophet, or to our Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that this writing is of such and such form? What the people of sand do is nothing but ignorance and misguidance. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Or a trace of knowledge. He said: Good handwriting. al-Tabarani narrated in al-Awsat and al-Hakim on the authority of al-Sha’bi on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or a trace of knowledge. He said: A line that the Arabs used to write on the ground. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Or a trace of knowledge, meaning: a clear indication of the matter. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding his statement, Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers,’ meaning I am not the first of the messengers. And I do not know what will be done with me or with you. Then after this, God revealed, That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come, and His statement, That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens, the verse. So God, the Exalted, informed His Prophet what He would do with him and with all the believers. Abu Dawud also narrated in his Naskh from him that this verse was abrogated by the statement: So that God may forgive you. It has been proven in Sahih al-Bukhari and other books from the hadith of Umm al-Ala’ who said: “When Uthman ibn Maz’un died, I said: May God have mercy on you, Abu al-Sa’ib, I bear witness that God has honored you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How do you know that God has honored him? As for him, certainty has come to him from his Lord, and I hope good for him. By God, I do not know, and I am the Messenger of God, what will be done to me or to you. Umm al-Ala’ said: By God, I will not vouch for anyone after him.”
46:10: 9- “Say: Have you considered” meaning tell me if it is from God meaning what was revealed to him of the Qur’an, and it was said that what is meant is Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the meaning is: if it was sent from other than God, and His statement: and you disbelieved in it is in the accusative case as a state with the estimation of had, and likewise His statement: and a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it meaning: tell me if that was in fact from God and the fact is that you disbelieved in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel who knew what God revealed in the Torah testified to the like of it: meaning the Qur’an from the meanings found in the Torah that are identical to it such as proving monotheism, resurrection, and other things. This similarity is due to the identity of the meanings even if the wording differs. Al-Jurjani said: It is like a relative clause, and the meaning is: And a witness testified that it is from God. Al-Wahidi said the same: So he believed is the witness in the Quran when it became clear to him that it is the speech of God and of the same type as what He sends down to His messengers. This witness from the Children of Israel is Abdullah ibn Salam, as Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ikrimah and others said. There is a problem with this, as the Surah is Meccan by consensus, and Abdullah ibn Salam converted to Islam after the Hijrah. So what is meant by the witness is a man from the People of the Book who believed in the Quran in Mecca and confirmed it. This was the choice of Ibn Jarir, and we will come at the end of the discussion with what indicates the most likely meaning that he is Abdullah ibn Salam and that this verse is Medinan, not Meccan. It was narrated from Masruq that what is meant by the man is Moses, peace be upon him. His statement, And you were arrogant is connected to testified: meaning the witness believed, and you were arrogant about believing. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people. So God, the Exalted, denied them guidance because of their wrongdoing to themselves through disbelief after the clear proof of the obligation of belief had been established. And whoever loses God’s guidance goes astray. There is a difference of opinion as to what the answer to the condition is. Al-Zajjaj said: It is omitted, meaning: Do you believe? It was said that His statement: So he believed, and you were arrogant. It was also said that it is omitted, meaning: You have wronged, as indicated by Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people. It was also said that it is omitted, meaning: Who among you is more astray? As in His statement: Have you considered, if it is from God and then you disbelieve in it, who is more astray? Al-Farisi 3:17. Or Ali Al-Farisi said that it is omitted, meaning: Do you feel secure from the punishment of God? It was also said that it is omitted, meaning: Are you not wrongdoers?
46:11: Then the Almighty mentioned another type of their false sayings, saying: 10- And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, meaning for their sake. It is possible that this lam is the lam of notification, If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it, meaning if what Muhammad brought of the Qur’an and prophethood had been good, they would not have preceded us to it because they, in their own eyes, are the ones who deserve to be preceded to every honor. They did not know that God, the Almighty, singles out for His mercy whomever He wills, honors whomever He wills, humiliates whomever He wills, and chooses for His religion whomever He wills. And when they are not guided by it, meaning by the Qur’an, and it was said by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said by faith, they will say, ‘This is an ancient falsehood.’ So they went beyond denying the goodness of the Qur’an to claiming that it is an ancient lie, as they said, legends of the ancients. The factor in idh is understood: meaning their stubbornness became apparent, and it is not permissible for it to work in it, they will say, because of the contrast between the two times: I mean the past and the future, and also because of the fa’. It was said The agent in it is an implied verb of the same type as the mentioned one: that is, they were not guided by it.
46:12: And if they are not guided by it, they will say: 11- And before it was the Book of Moses. The majority of scholars read it with a kasra on the meem of min as a preposition, and it and its object are the predicate, and the Book of Moses is a delayed subject, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state, or it is a new sentence, and the speech is intended to refute their statement This is an ancient lie. The fact that the Book of Moses, which is the Torah, preceded the Qur'an and they agreed on the fundamentals of the Sharia indicates that it is true and from God, and requires the invalidity of their statement. It was read with a fatha on the meem of min as a relative pronoun and the accusative of book: meaning, and We gave before it the Book of Moses. This reading was narrated from Al-Kalbi, an imam and a mercy, meaning that he is followed in religion and a mercy from God for whoever believes in him, and they are in the accusative case as a state. This was said by Al-Zajjaj and others. Al-Akhfash said: It is definite, and Abu Ubaidah said: That is, We made it an Imam and a mercy. And this is a confirming Book, meaning the Qur’an, for it confirms the Book of Moses, which is an Imam and a mercy, and other Books of God. The restriction of confirming is for the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. The accusative of an Arabic tongue is in the accusative case, and its owner is the pronoun in confirming, referring to the Book. Abu al-Baqa’ allowed it to be the object of confirming, but the first is more appropriate. It was said that it is with the deletion of an adjective: that is, of an Arabic tongue, and he is the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. To warn those who have wronged. The majority of scholars read linadhir with a fat-ha on the basis that its subject is a pronoun referring to the Book: that is, to warn the Book who have wronged. It was said that the pronoun refers to God, and it was said to the Messenger, but the first is more appropriate. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and al-Bazzi read it with a fat-ha on the basis that its subject is the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. Abu Hatim and Abu ‘Ubaid chose this reading. His statement: And good tidings for the doers of good is in the accusative case in apposition to the place of linadhir. Al-Zajjaj said: It is better to have it in the nominative case: meaning, it is good report. It was said that it is a source for a deleted verb: meaning, and you are given good report. His saying: for the doers of good is related to good report.
46:13: 12- Indeed, those who have said, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remained steadfast meaning, they combined monotheism with steadfastness in the Shari’ah. The explanation of this has been presented in Surat As-Sajdah. There will be no fear concerning them the fa is redundant in the predicate of the relative pronoun because it contains the meaning of a condition. Nor will they grieve meaning: they will not fear that something bad will befall them, nor will they grieve over the loss of something beloved, and that this will continue and be permanent.
46:14: 13- Those are the companions of Paradise meaning those described as the companions of Paradise, which is the abode of the believers, while they are abiding therein eternally. In this verse there is a great matter of encouragement, for the denial of fear and sorrow forever and the settlement in Paradise forever is something that souls do not seek anything else and do not long for anything other than it. As a reward for what they used to do meaning they will be rewarded for the deeds they did of obedience to God and abandoning His disobedience.
46:15: 14- And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, good treatment. The majority of reciters read good treatment with a damma on the ha' and a sukoon on the seen. Ali and As-Salami read them with a fatha on both. Ibn Abbas and the Kufians read ihsanan. It was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Ankabut. And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, good treatment, with no difference between the reciters. It was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-An'am and Surat Bani Isra'il. And to parents, good treatment. Perhaps this is the reason for the difference of opinion among the reciters in this verse. According to all of these readings, the accusative is a verbal noun: i.e. We enjoined upon him to treat them well, or with kindness. It was said that it is a direct object, as the word wasina includes the meaning we obliged. It was also said that it is a direct object, as his mother bore him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship. The majority of reciters read karhan in both instances with a damma on the kaf. Abu 'Umar and the people of Hijaz read it with a fatha. Al-Kisa'i said: They are two dialects with the same meaning. Abu Hatim said: “Karah with the fat-ha is not good because it means anger and overpowering. Abu Ubaid preferred the reading of the fat-ha. He said: “Because the word ‘karah’ in the entire Quran is with the fat-ha except in Surat Al-Baqarah, ‘Fighting is prescribed for you while it is hateful to you.’” It was said that ‘karah with the damma’ is what a person forces upon himself, and with the fat-ha’ is what he forces upon someone else. God mentioned the mother’s pregnancy and delivery to emphasize the obligation of treating her kindly, which God has commanded. The meaning is that she carried him with hatred and gave birth to him with hatred. Then God explained the period of his pregnancy and weaning, saying: His gestation and weaning is thirty months, meaning their period is this period from the beginning of his pregnancy until he is weaned from breastfeeding. This verse has been used as evidence that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, because the period of breastfeeding is two years, meaning the period of complete breastfeeding, as in His statement: Two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the suckling. So God mentioned in this verse the minimum period of pregnancy and the maximum period of breastfeeding. This verse indicates that the mother's right is more important than the father's right because she carried him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty, and breastfed him during this period with fatigue and exhaustion, and the father did not share in any of that with her. The majority of scholars readوَفيُّسُه وَفيُّسُهwith an alif, while al-Hasan, Ya'qub, Qatadah, and al-Jahdi readوَفيُّسُه with a fat-ha on the fa' and a sukoon on the sad without an alif. Fasl and fisal have the same meaning as weaning, weaning, picking, and harvesting. Until he reaches his prime means he reaches the full maturity of his strength and mind. The full explanation of ash-had has already been given, but it is necessary to estimate a sentence that is until its limit: that is, he lived and his life continued until he reached his prime. It was said that he reached his prime eighteen years of age, and it was said that ash-had is maturity, as was said by al-Sha'bi and Ibn Zayd. al-Hasan said: It is reaching forty, and the first is more appropriate because of his statement: and reached forty years, which indicates that reaching forty is something beyond reaching prime. The commentators said: God never sent a prophet except after forty years. He said, 'My Lord, inspire me' means inspire me. Al-Jawhari said: I sought God’s help, so He inspired me meaning I sought His inspiration, so He inspired me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents meaning inspire me to be grateful for the guidance You have bestowed upon me, and for the compassion You showed me when they raised me as a child. It was also said that You bestowed health and well-being upon me, and wealth and riches upon my parents. However, it is better not to restrict the blessing upon him and his parents to a specific blessing. And to do righteousness that pleases You meaning, and inspire me to do righteous deeds that please You from me. And make righteous for me my offspring meaning, make my offspring righteous, firmly rooted in righteousness, and able to do it. This verse is evidence that whoever reaches the age of forty should say these supplications often. It has been narrated that it was revealed about Abu Bakr, as will be mentioned at the end of this discussion. Indeed, I repent to You from my sins. And indeed, I am of the Muslims meaning those who submit to You, obey You, and are sincere in their belief in Your Oneness.
46:16: And the reference in His statement: 15- those is to the mentioned human being, and the plural is because it refers to the species and it is the subject, and its predicate is those from whom We accept the best of what they did of good deeds in this world, and what is meant by best is good like His statement: And follow the best of what was revealed to you. It was said that the comparative has its meaning, and what is meant by it is what the servant is rewarded for of deeds, not what he is not rewarded for like what is permissible, for it is good but not better. And We overlook their misdeeds so We do not punish them for them. The majority read accept and overlook in the passive form of the two verbs. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read them with a noon in both of them, attributing them to God, the Most High, and transgression means forgiveness. Its origin is from the verb jazat which means you did not stop at it. The meaning of among the companions of Paradise is that they will be among them, organized in their ranks. The preposition and its noun are in the accusative case as in the state of the prince honored me among his companions, meaning being among their group. It was said that fi has the meaning of ma’, meaning with the companions of Paradise. It was also said that they are the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning they are among the companions of Paradise. The promise of truth which they were promised. The promise of truth is a source emphasizing the content of the previous sentence, because His statement, Those are the ones from whom We accept, etc., means the promise of acceptance and transgression. It is possible that the source of the verb is deleted, meaning God promised them the promise of truth which they were promised through the tongues of the messengers in this world. Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani, and Al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, on the authority of Awf bin Malik Al-Ashja`i, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I went with him until we entered the church of the Jews on their feast day. They disliked our entering upon them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: ‘O group of Jews, show me twelve men from among you who bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. God, the Most High, will remove the wrath that is upon every Jew under their hands, the heavens beneath their feet.’ They remained silent, but none of them answered him. Then he turned to them, but none of them answered him three times. Then he said: ‘If you refuse, by God, I am the gatherer, the last, and the last, whether you believe or lie.’ Then he turned away, and I was with him until we were about to leave, when a man of his creation said: ‘As you are, O Muhammad.’ So he came forward. That man said: ‘Which man do you know among you, O group of Jews?’ They said: ‘By God, we do not know among us a man more knowledgeable of the Book of God or more understanding than you, nor your father, nor your grandfather.’ He said: ‘Then I bear witness by God that he is the Prophet you find written about in the Torah and the Gospel.’ They said: ‘You have lied.’ Then they turned back.” And they said evil things about him, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You have lied, your word will not be accepted from you. So we went out, three of us: the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), myself, and Ibn Salam. Then God revealed: {Say, Have you considered, if it is from God? until His saying: He does not guide the wrongdoing people.} And Al-Suyuti authenticated it. Al-Bukhari and Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas who said: I never heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say to anyone walking on the face of the earth that he is from the people of Paradise except for Abdullah ibn Salam. And regarding him was revealed the verse: {And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it.} At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam who said: It was revealed concerning verses from the Book of God, which were revealed concerning And a witness from among the Children of Israel and concerning Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.’ Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness, he said: Abdullah ibn Salam. Something similar to this was narrated from a group of the Successors. This is evidence that this verse is Madani, so it specifies the generality of their statement that the entire Surah Al-Ahqaf is Makkan. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah who said: Some of the polytheists said, “We are more honorable, we, we, we. If it had been good, so-and-so would not have preceded us to it.” So the verse, And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.’ was revealed. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Awn ibn Abi Shaddad who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab had a female slave who had converted to Islam before him, called Zunayrah. Umar used to beat her for accepting Islam, and the disbelievers of Quraysh used to say, If it had been good, Zunayrah would not have preceded us to it. So God revealed concerning her, And those who disbelieved say, the verse. At-Tabarani narrated from Samurah ibn Jundub that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Banu Ghifar and Aslam were a trial for many people. They said, ‘If it had been good, God would not have made them the first people to it.’” Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The verse: And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents up to the verse: the promise of truth which they were promised was revealed about Abu Bakr As-Siddiq. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Nafi’ bin Jubayr that Ibn Abbas told him that he was the companion of the woman who was brought to Umar and she gave birth after six months and the people disapproved of that. So I said to Umar: Why are you being unjust? He said: How? I said: Recite: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months and And mothers shall nurse their children two complete years. How long is a year? He said: One year. I said: How long is a year? He said: Twelve months. I said: Then twenty-four months are two complete years, and God delays of the pregnancy what He wills and advances what He wills. Umar was satisfied with my saying. Saeed bin Mansour, Abdul bin Hameed and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he used to say: If a woman gives birth after nine months, then twenty-one months of breastfeeding is sufficient for her. If she gives birth after seven months, then twenty-three months of breastfeeding is sufficient for her. If she gives birth after six months, then two complete years, because God says: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: This verse was revealed about Abu Bakr As-Siddiq: Until, when he attained his full strength and reached forty years, he said, ‘My Lord, enable me to succeed.’ The verse was revealed about him. God answered his prayer and all of his father, brothers and children became Muslims. The verse was also revealed about him: But as for him who gives and fears God, to the end of the surah.
46:17: When God the Almighty mentioned being grateful for the blessings of God the Almighty upon him and his parents, He mentioned someone who said to them a word that indicated annoyance with them when they called him to faith, so He said: 16- And he who said to his parents, 'Uff to you both.' The relative pronoun refers to the gender that said that word, and that is why He mentioned it in the plural. Uff is a word that is said by someone who says it when he is annoyed by something that comes to him. Nafi' and Hafs read Uff with a kasra on the fa' and with tanween. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Ibn Muhaisin read it with a fatha without tanween. The rest read it with a kasra without tanween, and these are dialects. The explanation of this has already been explained in Surah Bani Isra'il. The lam in His statement lakum for you both is to indicate anguish: that is, anguish for you both, as in His statement, Heyt lak. The majority read ata'adhani do you promise me with two light noons. The people of Madinah and Makkah opened the ya', while the rest closed it. Abu Haywah, Al-Mughira, and Hisham read the word by assimilating one of the two noons into the other. This reading was narrated from Nafi’. Al-Hasan, Shaiba, Abu Ja’far, and Abd Al-Warith, on the authority of Abu Amr, read it with a fatha on the first noon, as if they were fleeing from two consecutive kasra-like words. The majority read that I should go out with a damma on the hamza and a fatha on the ra’, indicating the object. Al-Hasan, Nasr, Abu Al-Aliyah, Al-A’mash, and Abu Mu’ammar read it with a fatha on the hamza and a damma on the ra’, indicating the subject. The meaning is: Do you promise me that I will be resurrected after death? The phrase and generations before me have passed is in the accusative case as a state of description: while the generations before me have passed and died, and none of them were resurrected. Similarly, the phrase and they are seeking help from God is in the accusative case as a state of description: while the two of them are seeking help from God and asking Him to guide them to faith. He sought help is transitive with itself and with the preposition with: it is said he sought help from God and he sought help from Him. Al-Razi said: Its meaning is that they seek help from God against their disbelief. So when the preposition was deleted, the verb was connected. It was said that seeking help is a supplication, so there is no need for the preposition bi. Al-Farra’ said: It is said that God answered his supplication and helped him. His saying, Woe to you is by estimation of the saying: that is, they say to him, Woe to you. It is not meant by it to supplicate against him, but rather to urge him to believe. For this reason, they said to him, Believe, for the promise of God is true, meaning believe in the resurrection, for the promise of God is true and there is no breach in it. Then he says, then denying what they said, This is nothing but legends of the ancients, meaning, what you are saying about the resurrection is nothing but the stories of the ancients and their falsehoods that they have written in their books. The majority read Indeed, the promise of God with a kasra over in as a new sentence or explanation. Umar ibn Fayed and Al-A’raj read it with a fatha over it as the object of believe with an estimation of the preposition bi. That is, believe that God’s promise of the resurrection is true.
46:18: 17- Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect meaning those who say these statements are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect: meaning the punishment has become obligatory upon them by the words of the Almighty to Iblis: I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you among them, all together as is indicated by His words: among nations that have passed on before them of jinn and mankind, and the phrase they were losers is an explanation of what preceded it, and this refutes the fact that the reason for the revelation of the verse was Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr and that he was the one who said to his parents what he said, for he was one of the best of the believers, and not one upon whom the word of punishment came into effect. The explanation of the revelation will come at the end of the research, God willing.
46:19: 18- And for all are degrees according to what they have done meaning, for each group of the two groups, the believers and the disbelievers, from among the jinn and mankind, there are ranks with God on the Day of Resurrection, according to their deeds. Ibn Zayd said: The degrees of the people of Hellfire in this verse go down, and the degrees of the people of Paradise go up. And that He may fully recompense them for their deeds meaning, the reward for their deeds. The majority of scholars read to fully recompense them with a nun nun. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Asim, Abu Amr, and Ya’qub read it with a ya subject to the lower ya. Abu Ubaid chose the first reading, while Abu Hatim chose the second. And they will not be wronged meaning, no wrongdoer will be given more, nor will a good-doer be deprived. Rather, each group will be fully recompensed for what they deserve of good and evil. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state, or it is a new sentence confirming what came before it.
46:20: 19- And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire The circumstance is related to an omitted word: that is, remind them, O Muhammad, of the Day when the cover will be removed and they will look at the Fire and be drawn near it. It was said that the meaning of are exposed is are tormented from their saying: He exposed him to the sword. It was also said that the speech is inverted. The meaning is: The Fire will be exposed to them. Have you spent your good things in your worldly life? That is, it will be said to them. It was said that this amount is what makes the circumstance accusative, and the first is more appropriate. The majority of scholars read: Have you spent with one hamza. Al-Hasan, Nasr, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ya'qub, and Ibn Kathir read it with two light hamzas. The meaning of the question is rebuke and reprimand. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs reprimand with questions and other means, so reprimanding applies to both readings. Al-Kalbi said: What is meant by good things are the pleasures and livelihoods they enjoyed. And you enjoyed them means the good things. The meaning is that they followed the desires and pleasures that are in disobeying God, the Most High, and they did not care about the sin, as a denial of what the messengers brought of the promise of accountability, punishment and reward. So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation means the punishment in which there is humiliation and disgrace for you. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Hun means disgrace in the language of the Quraysh. Because you were arrogant upon the earth without right meaning because of your arrogance regarding the worship of God, belief in Him and His Oneness. And because you were wicked meaning [you went out] from obeying God and committing sins. So He made the reason for their punishment two things: arrogance regarding following the truth and committing sins against God, the Most High. This is the way of the disbelievers, for they combined both. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Yusuf bin Mahak who said: Marwan was in charge of the Hijaz and Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan had appointed him. He gave a sermon and mentioned Yazid bin Muawiyah so that people would pledge allegiance to him after his father. Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr said something, so he said, Take him. So he entered Aisha’s house and they could not find him. Marwan said, Indeed, the verse ‘And he who said to his parents, ‘Fie upon you both’ was revealed about him. Aisha said, God did not reveal anything about us in the Qur’an except that God revealed my excuse. Abd bin Hamid, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad who said: When Mu'awiyah pledged allegiance to his son, Marwan said: It is the way of Abu Bakr and Umar. Abd Al-Rahman said: It is the way of Heraclius and Caesar. Marwan said: This is the one about whom God said: And he who said to his parents, 'Fie upon you both' The Verse. report of that reached Aisha and she said: Marwan lied, by God, it is not about him. If I wanted to name the one about whom it was revealed, I would have named him. But the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) cursed Abu Marwan and Marwan was in his loins, so Marwan is one whom God cursed. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: He said: This is a son of Abu Bakr. Abu Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Suddi, but this is not authentic, as we have mentioned previously.
46:21: His statement: 20- And mention the brother of Aad meaning, O Muhammad, mention to your people the brother of Aad, who is Hud bin Abdullah bin Rabah, he was their brother in lineage, not in religion. His statement, When he warned his people is a substitute for inclusion from him: meaning the time when he warned them in Al-Ahqaf which is the land of Aad, the plural of Haqf, which is the great, oblong, curved sand, as Al-Khalil and others said, and they had subdued the people of the earth with their strength. The meaning is that God, the Exalted, commanded him to mention their story to his people so that they would be admonished and fear. It was also said that He commanded him to remember to himself their story with Hud so that he would follow his example and his people's denial would be easy for him. Ata' said: Al-Ahqaf is the sands of the land of Ash-Shihr. Muqatil said: It is on the right in Hadhramaut. Ibn Zayd said: It is flat, rectangular sand like mountains, but it has not reached the level of being mountains. And the messengers have passed away before him and after him meaning the messengers have passed away before him and after him. This is what Al-Farra’ and others said. And in Ibn Masoud’s reading: before him and after him. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state, and it may be parenthetical between Hud’s warning and his statement to his al-Nas 114:Indeed, I fear for you, but the former is more appropriate. The meaning is: He informed them that the messengers who were sent before him and those who will be sent after him are all warners, similar to his warning. Then he returned to Hud’s statement to his people, and said, narrating it from him: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day. It was said that making that sentence parenthetical is more appropriate for the situation and more in line with the meaning.
46:22: 21- They said, ‘Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?’ That is, to turn us away from worshipping them. It was also said, To remove us, and it was also said, To prevent us. The meanings are similar, and from this is the saying of Urwah ibn Udaynah: If you are slandered about good deeds, then others have slandered you. He says: If you are not successful in doing good, then you are among a people who have been turned away from that. Then bring us what you promise us of great punishment if you should be of the truthful in your promise to us.
46:23: 22- He said, ‘Knowledge is only with God’ meaning that knowledge of the time of its coming is only with God, not with me. And I convey to you what I have been sent with to you from your Lord of warning and excuse. As for knowledge of the time of the coming of the punishment, it was not revealed to me. But I see you as a people behaving ignorantly since you remained insistent on your disbelief and were not guided by what I brought you. Rather, you suggested to me what is not among the duties of messengers.
46:24: 23- When they saw it as a cloud The pronoun refers to what is in His statement, with what You promised us. Al-Mubarrad and Al-Zajjaj said: The pronoun in they saw it refers to something unmentioned, and this is explained by His statement, a cloud, so the pronoun refers to the clouds: that is, when they saw the clouds as a cloud, so a cloud is in the accusative case for repetition, meaning for explanation, and the cloud is called a cloud because it appears across the sky. Al-Jawhari said: The cloud that appears across the horizon, and from this is His statement, This cloud that brings us rain. The accusative case of a cloud is in the state of state or specification, facing their valleys meaning heading towards their valleys. The commentators said: The rain had been withheld from Aad for days, so God sent a black cloud towards them, and it came out upon them from their valley called Al-Mu’tab. When they saw it approaching their valleys, they were filled with good tidings, and they said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain,’ meaning there was no rain in it. His statement, facing their valleys, is an attribute of a cloud because its addition is verbal, not semantic, so it is correct to describe an indefinite noun with it, and thus bring us rain.
