When they said that, Hud answered them, saying, Rather, it is what you hastened, meaning of the punishment when they said, Then bring us what you promise us. His statement, a wind, is a substitute for what, or the predicate of a deleted subject, and the phrase, in which is a painful punishment, is an attribute of a wind, and the wind with which they were punished arose from that cloud that they saw.
46:25: 24- Destroys everything by the command of its Lord. This sentence is a second description of the wind: meaning it destroyed everything it passed through from the lives and wealth of the people of Aad. Destruction means annihilation, and so does destruction. It is read Yadmur with a fatha over the letter dāl and a sukūn over the letter mīm and a damma over the letter mīm and raising kulli as an active participle from dammāra damanan. The meaning of by the command of its Lord is that it is by His judgment and decree. So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings meaning that you, O Muhammad, or anyone who is fit to see, could only see their dwellings after their lives and wealth were gone. The majority of scholars read La ta'ara with a fathah over the letter dāl as an addressee, and masakinākim as a noun. Hamzah and Asim read it with a fathah over the letter dāl as a passive participle and raised masakinākim. Sibawayh said: Its meaning is that nothing could be seen of their persons except their dwellings. Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose the second reading. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that nothing is seen except their dwellings, so it is interpreted in this sense, just as you say: No one said except Hind, and the meaning is: No one stood up except Hind. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: Then the wind came to them and destroyed them, so nothing was seen except their dwellings. “Thus do We recompense the criminal people,” meaning, like that recompense, We recompense these people. The explanation of this story has already been mentioned in Surat Al-A’raf.
46:26: 25- And We have empowered them in that in which We have empowered you. Al-Mubarrad said: Ma in his statement in what is like that and if is like what: meaning the negative, and its interpretation is: And We have empowered them in that in which We have not empowered you of wealth, long life, and strength of body. It was said that it is redundant and its interpretation is: And We have empowered them in that in which We have empowered you. Al-Qatibi said the same, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: As soon as we applied cheese, but our desires and the state of others The first is more appropriate because it is more effective in rebuking the disbelievers of Quraysh and their likes. And We gave them hearing, sight, and hearts means that they turned away from accepting the argument and remembering, despite what God had given them of senses by which to perceive evidence. That is why He said: So their hearing, their sight, and their hearts availed them nothing meaning that what God had given them of that did not benefit them at all, since they did not attain through it the monotheism and the truth of the promise and the threat. We have already discussed the singular form of hearing and the plural form of sight, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. The min in min shay’a is redundant, and the meaning is: So nothing availed them nor did it benefit them in any way since they denied the signs of God the circumstance is related to aghna, and in it is the meaning of justification: that is, because they denied and that which they mocked encompassed them meaning that the punishment that they were hastening by way of mockery encompassed them when they said, Then bring us what you promise us.
46:27: 26- And We destroyed the towns around you The address is to the people of Mecca, and what is meant by the towns around them are the towns of Thamud, the towns of Lot, and others similar to them that were adjacent to the land of Hijaz, and their stories were well-known to them. And We diversified the signs that perhaps they would return That is, We explained the arguments and diversified them so that they would return from their disbelief, but they did not return.
46:28: Then the Almighty mentioned that no one would help them against God’s punishment, so He said: 27- Why did not those whom they took as deities besides God help them? That is, why did not their deities, through whom they claimed to draw near to God, help them so that they would intercede for them when they said, These are our intercessors with God, and prevent them from the destruction that befell them? Al-Kisa’i said: “Qurban is everything that is done to draw closer to God, such as obedience and ritual sacrifice. The plural is qurābin, like ḥubān and ḥubābin. One of the two objects of ‘takhḍawu’ is a pronoun referring to the relative pronoun, and the second is ‘ilāhī,’ and ‘qurbanan’ is a circumstantial verb. It is not correct for ‘qurban’ to be the second object, and ‘ilāhī’ to be a substitute for it, because the meaning is corrupted. It was also said that it is correct and the meaning is not corrupted, and Ibn ‘Atiyyah, Abu al-Baqa’ and Abu Hayyan preferred this view. It was denied that the meaning would be corrupted in this way. “Rather, they went astray from them” means they were absent from their support and were not present when they were needed. It was also said that they perished. It was also said that the pronoun in ‘going astray’ refers to the disbelievers, meaning they abandoned the idols and disavowed them. The first view is more appropriate. The reference in His statement, and that is to the misguidance of their gods. The meaning is that misguidance and loss is the result of their slander, which is their taking them as gods and their claim that they bring them closer to God. The majority read ifkahum with a kasra on the hamza and a sukoon on the fa', the infinitive of afka ya'fak ifkan: meaning their lie. Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr and Mujahid read it with a fatha on the hamza, fa' and kaf as a verb: meaning that saying turned them away from monotheism. Ikrimah read it with a fatha on the hamza and a shaddah on the fa': meaning he made them afkeen. Abu Hatim said: meaning he turned them away from the pleasures they were experiencing. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he read it with a long vowel and a kasra on the fa' meaning that he turned them away. And what they used to invent is in apposition to ifkahum: meaning and the effect of their invention or the effect of what they used to invent. The meaning is: that is their ifkahum: meaning their lie that they used to say that it would bring them closer to God and intercede for them. And what they used to invent means they used to lie that they were gods. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Ahqaf is a mountain in Ash-Sham. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of narration on his authority regarding his statement: This is a cloud that will bring us rain, that he said: It is the clouds. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: “I never saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiling or relaxing until I could see his uvula. He would only smile, and whenever he saw a cloud or a wind, you could tell from his face. I said: O Messenger of God, when people see a cloud, they rejoice that it will rain. But when I see it, I can tell from your face that it is disliked. He said: O Aisha, what assures me that it will not be a punishment? Some people were punished by wind, and some people saw the punishment, so they said: ‘This is a cloud that will bring us rain.’” Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated on her authority that she said: “Whenever the wind blew, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would say: ‘O God, I ask You for its good and the good within it and the good for which You sent it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil within it and the evil for which You sent it.’ Then when I imagined the sky, his color would change, and he would go out and come in, come and go, and when it rained, he would be relieved. I asked him and he said: ‘I do not know. Perhaps it is as the people of ‘Aad said: “This is a cloud bringing us rain.”’” Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in his book Al-Sahab and Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, It is a cloud with rain in it. The first thing they knew that it was a punishment was that they saw what was coming out of their men and livestock flying between the sky and the earth like feathers. They entered their homes and closed their doors. Then the wind came and opened their doors and covered them with sand. They were under the sand for seven nights and eight days, groaning. Then God commanded the wind to remove the sand from them and throw them into the sea. So his statement, So in the morning nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Al-Hakim narrated - and he authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said, God did not send upon ‘Aad any wind except the size of this ring of mine. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And We had certainly established them in that in which We had not established you, meaning, We had not established you. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, saying: The people of Aad were empowered in the land better than this nation was, and they were stronger, had more wealth, and lived longer.
46:29: When He, the Almighty, made clear that among mankind are those who believe and those who disbelieve, He also made clear that this is also the case among the jinn, saying: 28- And remember when We directed to you a company of the jinn The agent in the circumstance is understood: meaning, remember when We directed, meaning, We directed to you a company of the jinn and sent them to you. His statement, listening to the Qur’an is in the accusative case as a second description of a company or a state because the indefinite noun is made specific by the first description. So when they attended it meaning, they attended the Qur’an when it was recited. It was said that they attended the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There is a shift in the speech from direct address to third person, but the first is more appropriate. They said, ‘Listen’ meaning, some of them said to one another, Be quiet. They ordered each other to do that in order to listen. So when it was concluded The majority read it was concluded in the passive form: meaning, its recitation was completed. Habib bin Ubaidullah bin Az-Zubayr, Lahiq bin Humaid and Abu Majlaz read it in the active form, meaning the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished reciting it. The first reading supports that the pronoun in his presence refers to the Qur’an. The second reading supports that it refers to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And they turned back to their people as warners, meaning they turned away intending to go to their people behind them, warning them against disobeying the Qur’an and cautioning them. The accusative of warners is in the implied state, meaning they were able to warn. This indicates that they believed in the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and an explanation of that will come at the end of the research.
46:30: 29- They said, ‘O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses,’ meaning the Qur’an, but there is an ellipsis in the text, meaning: So they reached their people and said, O our people. Ata’ said: They were Jews who converted to Islam. Confirming what was before it, meaning what came before it of the revealed books. Guiding to the truth, meaning to the true religion. And to a straight path, meaning to the straight path of God. Muqatil said: God did not send a prophet to the jinn and mankind before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
46:31: 30- "O our people, respond to the caller of God and believe in him" meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, or the Quran "He will forgive you some of your sins" meaning some of them, which is everything except the rights of the servants. It was said that the word "min" here is for the beginning of the goal. The meaning is that forgiveness begins with sins and ends with forgiveness for leaving what is more important. It was said that it is redundant. "And will save you from a painful punishment" which is the punishment of the Fire. This verse is evidence that the ruling on the jinn is the ruling on humans in reward and punishment and obedience to the commands and prohibitions. Al-Hasan said that the believing jinn have no reward other than their salvation from the Fire. Abu Hanifa said the same. The first is more appropriate, and it was said by Malik, Al-Shafi'i, and Ibn Abi Layla. According to the first opinion, those who say it say that after their salvation from the Fire, it will be said to them: Become dust, as it is said to animals, but the second is more correct. God the Almighty said, addressing the jinn and mankind: “And for him who fears standing before his Lord are two Gardens. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?” Thus, God the Almighty bestowed His favor upon the two races by making the reward of their good-doers Paradise. This does not contradict the fact that it is limited here to mentioning their protection from a painful torment. What supports this is that God the Almighty has rewarded their disbelievers with Hellfire, which is a position of justice, so how could He not reward their good-doers with Paradise, which is a position of grace? What also supports this is what is in the Noble Qur’an in more than one place that the reward of the believers is Paradise, the reward of those who do righteous deeds is Paradise, the reward of those who say there is no god but God is Paradise, and there are many other things in the Book and Sunnah. Scholars have differed as to whether God sent messengers from among themselves to the jinn or not. The apparent meaning of the Qur’anic verses is that the messengers were only from humans, as in His statement: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], any but men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns. And He also said: And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And God the Almighty said about Abraham the Friend of God: And We placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book. So every prophet whom God sent after Abraham was from his descendants. As for His statement in Surat al-An’am 6:O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you? It was said that what is meant is from the two genders and is true for one of them, which are humans, as in His statement: From them come pearls and coral, meaning from one of them.
46:32: 31- And whoever does not respond to the caller of God will not escape Him on earth. That is, God will not escape him nor will He outrun him nor will he be able to escape from Him, because even if he fled with every means of escape, He is on earth with no way out of it. This is a severe intimidation and he has no protectors besides Him, that is, supporters who will prevent him from the punishment of God. The Almighty made clear, after the impossibility of his salvation by himself, the impossibility of his salvation by means of someone else. The reference in His saying, those, is to those who do not respond to the caller of God, and He informed that they are in manifest error, that is, apparent and clear.
46:33: Then the Almighty mentioned evidence for the resurrection, saying: 32- Have they not seen that it is God who created the heavens and the earth? Here, the vision is the heart, which means knowledge, and the hamza is for denial, and the waw is for connecting to something understood: that is, have they not thought and not known that the One who created these great bodies of the heavens and the earth from the beginning and was not weary of their creation? that is, He was not incapable of that nor weak from it. It is said that someone is weary of a matter and is weary: if he is not guided to its direction, and from this is the saying of the poet: They were blinded by their order, just as the dove was blinded by its egg. The majority read "wa la yaa" with a sukoon on the 'ayn and a fatha on the yaa, the present tense of 'ayyi. Al-Hasan read with a kasra on the 'ayn and a sukoon on the yaa, "bi qadir 'ala an yahya al-mawtad." Abu 'Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: The baa is redundant for emphasis, as in His statement, "And sufficient is God as a witness." Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farraa, and Al-Zajjaj said: The Arabs add the baa with denial and interrogation, so you say, "Ma thannakan bi-qaim, and the preposition and noun are in the nominative case as the predicate of lan. Ibn Mas'ud, 'Isa ibn 'Umar, Al-A'raj, Al-Jahdi, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ya'qub, and Zaid ibn 'Ali read yaqdir" in the present tense. Abu 'Ubaidah chose the first reading, and Abu Hatim chose the second reading. He said: Because the introduction of the baa in the predicate of "an is ugly, By God, He is Able to do all things," nothing is beyond His power.
46:34: 33- And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire The circumstance is related to an implied statement: that is, it will be said to those who disbelieved on that Day, Is this not the truth? This sentence is the decisive statement, and the reference here is to what they will witness on the Day they are exposed to the Fire. And in being satisfied with a mere reference there is a great deal of terror in what is being referred to and a great magnification of its importance that is not hidden, as if it is a matter that cannot be expressed with a word that indicates it. They said, ‘Yes, by our Lord.’ They confessed when confession would not benefit them, and they confirmed this confession with an oath, because witnessing is the certain truth that cannot be denied or rejected. He said, ‘Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.’ That is, because of your disbelief in this in this world and your denial of it. And in this command to them to taste the punishment there is a severe rebuke and great mockery.
46:35: When God, the Almighty, established the evidence for prophethood, monotheism, and resurrection, He commanded His Messenger to be patient, saying: 34- "So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will. The fa" is the answer to an omitted condition: that is, when you have come to know that and the proofs are established for it, and it does not work with the disbelievers, then be patient as were patient the messengers of strong will: that is, the masters of steadfastness and resolve, for you are one of them. Mujahid said: The messengers of strong will are five: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, peace be upon him. They are the bearers of the religious laws. Abu Al-Aliyah said: They are Noah, Hud, and Abraham, so God commanded His Messenger to be the fourth of them. Al-Suddi said: They are six: Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, Jesus, and Muhammad, peace be upon him. It was also said that they were Noah, Hud, Salih, Shuaib, Lot, and Moses. Ibn Jurayj said: Among them were Ishmael, Jacob, and Job, but not Jonah. Al-Sha'bi and Al-Kalbi said: They are the ones who were ordered to fight, so they revealed their faith and fought the infidels. It was also said that they are the noble messengers mentioned in Surat Al-An'am, and they are eighteen: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Noah, David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Zachariah, John, Jesus, Elias, Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot. Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl chose this because of his saying after mentioning them: "Those are the ones whom God has guided, so follow their guidance." It was also said that all the messengers were those of strong will. It was also said that they are twelve prophets to the Children of Israel. Al-Hasan said: They are four: Abraham, Moses, David, and Jesus. "And do not hasten them" means, O Muhammad, do not hasten the punishment for the infidels. When God, the Almighty, commanded him to be patient and forbade him from hastening the punishment for his people, hoping that they would believe, He said: It will be as if, on the Day they see what they are promised of the punishment, they had not remained [in the world] except for an hour of a day. That is, it will be as if, on the Day they witness it in the Hereafter, they had not remained in this world except for the length of an hour of the days because of what they will witness of the great terror and lasting affliction. The majority of scholars read balagha in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, this that you admonished them with is a message, or that hour is a message, or this Qur’an is a message, or it is a subject, and the predicate is for them, which comes after His statement: and do not hasten it, meaning it is a message for them. Al-Hasan, Isa bin Omar, and Zaid bin Ali read balagha in the accusative case as a verbal noun: that is, convey a message. Abu Majlaz read balagha in the imperative form. Balagha was read in the past tense: Then will none perish except the defiantly disobedient people? The majority of scholars read fa-l-yahlak in the passive form. Ibn Muhaisin recited it in the active voice, meaning: None perish by God's punishment except those who disobey God and commit sins. Qatada said: None perishes by God's punishment except a polytheist. It was said that this verse is the strongest verse on hope. Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is: None perish with God's mercy and grace except the wicked people. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Mani' and Al-Hakim narrated - Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym and Al-Bayhaqi both authenticated it in Al-Dala'il - on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud who said: They, meaning the jinn, descended upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was reciting the Qur'an in Batn Nakhl. When they heard him, they said, "Listen! They said, Shh!" They were nine, one of them being a whirlwind. Then God revealed: "And when We directed towards you a company of the jinn..." until His saying: "manifest error." Ahmad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Az-Zubayr: "And when We directed towards you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an..." He said: In Nakhl while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was praying the last 'Isha' prayer. "They were almost over him in crowds." Ibn Jarir, At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated: "And when We directed towards you a company of the jinn..." He said: They were nine people from the people of Nasibin, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) appointed them as messengers to their people. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu`aym also narrated something similar. He said: The jinn were sent to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) twice, and they were the chieftains of the jinn in Nasibin. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Masruq, who said: I asked Ibn Mas`ud, “Who informed the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) of the jinn on the night when they listened to the Qur’an?” He said: A tree informed him of them. Abd ibn Humayd, Ahmad, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Alqamah, who said: I said to Ibn Mas`ud, “Did any of you accompany the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) on the night of the jinn?” He said: “None of us accompanied him, but we missed him one night, so we said: ‘He was assassinated or taken away, what happened?’ He said: “So we spent the worst night ever spent by a people. When it was near dawn, we saw him coming from the direction of Hira’. We informed him, and he said: ‘A caller of the jinn came to me, so I went to them and recited the Qur’an to them. He then went and showed us their tracks and the traces of their fires.” Ahmad narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: “I was with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) on the night of the jinn.” Similar to this has been narrated through various chains of narration. Reconciling the narrations by basing them on two stories that happened between him (peace be upon him) and the jinn, Ibn Masoud was present in one of them and he was not present in the other. Many hadiths have been reported that the jinn after this came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) time after time and learned the laws from him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Those of strong resolve among the messengers are the Prophet (peace be upon him), Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: They are the ones who were ordered to fight until they continued with that: Noah, Hud, Salih, Moses, David, and Solomon. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: I was informed that those of strong resolve among the messengers were three hundred and thirteen. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fasted for a long time, then he continued fasting for a long time, then he continued fasting for a long time, then he continued fasting. He said: O Aisha, the religion is not appropriate for Muhammad or the family of Muhammad. O Aisha, God was not pleased with any of the messengers of resolve except with patience in the face of what is disliked and patience in refraining from what is beloved. Then He was not pleased with me except to charge me with what He charged them with. He said: So be patient as the messengers of resolve were patient. And by God, I will be patient as they were patient to the best of my ability, and there is no strength except with God.
47:1: It is called Surat Al-Qital and Surat Al-Dhin Kafiru. It has thirty-nine verses, and some say thirty-eight. It is Madani. Al-Mawardi said: According to everyone’s opinion, except for Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, who said: Except for one verse that was revealed after the Farewell Pilgrimage when he left Makkah and began to look at the Kaaba and he was crying out of grief over it, then the verse was revealed: And how many a city was mightier in power than your city! Al-Tha’labi said: It is Makani. Ibn Hibatullah narrated it on the authority of Ad-Dahhak and Sa’id ibn Jubayr, but this is a mistake in the statement, as the Surah is Madani, as is clear. Ibn Ad-Durais narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surah Al-Qital was revealed in Madinah. An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated on his authority that he said: Surah Muhammad was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr, who said: Surah Al-Dhinkafiru was revealed in Madinah. At-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat on the authority of Ibn Imran that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to recite to them in the Maghrib prayer: Those who disbelieved and averted from the way of God. His statement: 1- Those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God are the disbelievers of Quraysh who disbelieved in God and averted themselves and others from the way of God, which is the religion of Islam, by forbidding them from entering it. This is what Mujahid and As-Suddi said. Ad-Dahhak said: The meaning of from the way of God is: from the House of God by preventing those who visit it. It was also said that they are the People of the Book, and the relative pronoun is the subject and predicate. He rendered their deeds worthless means He rendered them worthless and in vain. Ad-Dahhak said: The meaning of He rendered their deeds worthless is that He rendered their plot and deceit against the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and turned their disbelief against them. It was also said that He rendered worthless what they did in disbelief, which they called noble morals, such as maintaining kinship ties, freeing captives, and hosting guests. Although these are essentially invalid, the meaning is that God, the Almighty, has decreed their invalidity.
47:2: And when He mentioned the group of disbelievers, He followed them by mentioning the group of believers, saying: 2- And those who believed and did righteous deeds and believed in what was revealed to Muhammad. This generality appears to include every believer among the believers who do righteous deeds, and its specific reason does not prevent that. It has been said that it was revealed about the Ansar, and it has been said about some of the Quraysh, and it has been said about the believers among the People of the Book. However, the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. God Almighty singled out belief in what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for mention, even though it is included under the generality of belief mentioned before it, to draw attention to its honor and high status. The phrase And it is the truth from their Lord is an interjection between the subject, which is His statement: And those who believed, and its predicate, which is His statement: He removed from them their misdeeds. The meaning of it being the truth is that it abrogates what came before it, and His statement: from their Lord is in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning of He removed from them their misdeeds: that is, the misdeeds that they committed in the past, for He forgave them through faith and action. Al-Salih And set right their condition meaning their affair and their state. Mujahid said: their condition. Qatadah said: their condition. It was also said: their affair, and the meanings are close. Al-Mubarrad said: The condition here is the condition. It was said that the meaning is that He protected them from sins in their lives and guided them to good deeds, and it is not meant to set right their worldly condition by giving them money and the like. Al-Naqqash said: The meaning is that He set right their intentions, and from this is the saying of the poet: If you accept my kindness, I will accept the same, but if you turn away, I will go to a bad state.
47:3: And the reference in His saying: 3- That is a reference to what was mentioned previously of what He promised the disbelievers and promised the believers, and it is a subject whose predicate is what comes after it. It was said that it is the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, the matter is that because that those who disbelieved followed falsehood and that those who believed followed the truth from their Lord so falsehood is polytheism, and the truth is monotheism and faith, and the meaning is: that this misguidance of the deeds of the disbelievers is because of their following falsehood of associating partners with God and committing sins against Him, and that expiation of the sins of the believers and the reform of their condition is because of their following the truth that God has commanded us to follow of monotheism, faith, and performing acts of obedience Thus does God set forth for the people their examples meaning that the example of that example is shown to the people their examples: that is, the conditions of the two groups that are like examples in strangeness. Al-Zajjaj said: Thus does God set forth for the people the examples of the good deeds of the believers and the misguidance of the deeds of the disbelievers: meaning that whoever was a disbeliever, God would cause his deeds to go astray, and whoever was a believer, God would expiate his bad deeds.
47:4: 4- So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike [their] necks. When God, the Almighty, explained the state of the two groups, He ordered jihad against the disbelievers. What is meant by those who disbelieve are the grateful ones and those from the People of the Book who were not bound by a covenant. The word strike is in the accusative case as a verbal noun for a deleted verb. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, strike the necks, and he mentioned necks specifically because killing is most often done by severing them. It was also said that it is in the accusative case as an inducement. Abu Ubaidah said: It is like their saying: O soul, be patient. It was also said that the meaning is: Aim to strike the necks. It was said that the striking of necks was specified because the expression for it contains harshness and severity that is not in killing itself, which is slitting the neck and severing the limb which is the head of the body and its top and best part. Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, that is, you have gone to extremes in killing them and killed many of them. This is the ultimate goal of the command to strike necks, not to explain the ultimate goal of killing. It is taken from something thick, meaning coarse, and the meaning of it has already been explained in Surat Al-Anfal. So bind the bonds firmly. Al-Wathaq, with the fatha, and it can be pronounced with the kasra: the name of the thing that is tied down, like a ribat. Al-Jawhari said: And he bound him in the bonds means he tightened him. He said: Wathaq, with the kasra of the waw, is a dialectal term for it. The majority read fa-shadu with the damma on the shin, and As-Salami read it with the kasra on it. Rather, God the Almighty commanded that the bonds be tightened so that they do not escape. The meaning is: If you go to extremes in killing them, then take them captive and surround them with bonds. Either a favor from us after the capture, or a ransom. That is, either you bestow a favor upon them after the capture, from us, or you ransom them. Mann means release without compensation, and ransom is what a captive redeems himself with from captivity. Killing was not mentioned here, as what preceded was sufficient. The majority read Fidaa with a long vowel. Ibn Kathir read Fahda with a short vowel. He only mentioned Mann before Fidaa because it is one of the noble morals, and for this reason the Arabs used to boast about it, as their poet said: We do not kill prisoners, but we release them if the burden of debts becomes too heavy for them. Then the Almighty mentioned the goal for that, saying: until the war lays down its burdens. The burdens of war that cannot be sustained except by peace and truce, the laying down is attributed to it and it is for its people by way of metaphor, and the meaning is: The Muslims have a choice between those matters until there is no war with the disbelievers. Mujahid said: The meaning is: until there is no religion other than the religion of Islam, and this is what Al-Hasan and Al-Kalbi said. Al-Kisa’i said: Until people submit. Al-Farra’ said: Until they believe and disbelief is gone. It was said that the meaning is: Until the warring enemies lay down their burdens, which is their weapon by defeat or truce. It was narrated from Al-Hasan and Ata’ that they said: This verse is an inversion, and the meaning is: So strike the necks until the war lays down its burdens, and when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then tighten the bonds. Scholars have differed as to whether this verse is definitive or abrogated. Some say that it was abrogated with regard to the idolaters and that it is not permissible to ransom them or to bestow favors upon them. What abrogated it is the verse in which God says interpretation of the meaning: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and His saying: But if you come upon them in war, scatter with them those who are behind them, and His saying: And fight the polytheists altogether. This is the view of Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and many of the Kufians. They said: Al-Ma’idah was the last to be revealed, so it is obligatory to kill every polytheist except for those who can be spared, such as women, children, and those from whom the jizyah is taken. This is the well-known view of the Hanafi school. It was also said that this verse abrogates the verse in which God says: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. This was narrated from ‘Ata’ and others. Many scholars said: The verse is definitive and the imam has the choice between killing or taking them prisoner, and after taking them prisoner, he has the choice between giving them a favor and ransoming them. This is the view of Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Ath-Thawri, Al-Awza’i, Abu ‘Ubaid, and others. This is the most likely opinion because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Rightly-Guided Caliphs after him did that. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: There is no ransom or captivity except after the slaughter and killing by the sword, based on His saying: It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a great slaughter in the land. So if he is taken captive after that, then the imam can rule according to what he saw of killing or other things. That is, and if God had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them. The place of that is in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning the matter is that. It was said that it is in the accusative case as the object with the estimation of a verb: meaning do that. It is permissible for it to be a subject and its predicate deleted as indicated by what came before: meaning that is the ruling of the disbelievers. The meaning of If God had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them is that He is able to take vengeance upon them by taking revenge on them, destroying them, and tormenting them with whatever types of torment He wills. But He commanded you to fight them that He might test some of you by means of others, meaning that He might choose some of you by means of others, so that He might know those who strive in His cause and those who are patient in His trial, and He might make their reward abundant and torment the disbelievers by their hands. And those who are killed in the cause of God the majority read fought in the active form, and Abu Amr and Hafs read killed in the passive form, while Al-Hasan read it with emphasis and also in the passive form. Al-Jahdi, Isa bin Omar, and Abu Haywah read killed in the active form with a light vowel without an alif. The meaning according to the first and fourth readings is that the reward of those who strive in the cause of God will not be lost. According to the second and third readings, the reward of those who are killed in the cause of God will not be diminished. Qatada said: We were told that this verse was revealed on the Day of Uhud.
47:5: Then God, the Almighty, mentioned the great reward they will have with Him, saying: 5- He will guide them meaning God, the Almighty, will guide them to the right path in this world and give them the reward in the Hereafter. And set right their condition meaning their state, their affairs, and their situation. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Guidance may be used, and what is meant by it is guiding the believers to the paths of Paradise and the road leading to it. Ibn Ziyad said: He will guide them to argue with Munkar and Nakir.
47:6: 6- "And He will admit them to Paradise. He has made it known to them." That is, He has made it clear to them so that they know it without any proof. This is because when they enter Paradise, they will disperse to their homes. Al-Wahidi said: This is the opinion of most of the commentators. Al-Hasan said: God described Paradise to them in this world, so when they entered it, they knew it by its description. It was also said that there was an omission: that is, they knew its paths, dwellings, and houses. It was also said that this definition is by a proof that guides them to it, which is the angel assigned to the guardian who walks before him until he enters his home. This is what Muqatil said. It was also said that the meaning of He made it known to them is that He made it fragrant with various types of pleasures, taken from arf, which means scent.
47:7: Then He, the Almighty, promised them that His religion would be victorious, saying: 7- O you who have believed, if you support God, He will support you. That is, if you support the religion of God, He will support you against the disbelievers and grant you victory. Similar to this is His saying: And God will surely support those who support Him. Qatrib said: If you support the Prophet of God, He will support you. And plant firmly your feet. That is, when fighting, and plant firmly your feet is an expression of victory and assistance in battlefields. It was said that it was for Islam, and it was said that it was for the path.
47:8: 8- And those who disbelieve - woe to them The relative pronoun is in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is omitted, its meaning is woe to them as evidenced by what follows it, and the fa was added to liken the subject to the condition, and the ta'san is in the accusative case as a source for the verb understood as a predicate. Al-Farra' said: Like providing them with water to drink and grazing, and the origin of ta'san is falling and stumbling. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: Ta'san means to be dragged on one's face, and naks means to be dragged on one's head. He said: Ta'san also means destruction. Al-Jawhari said: Its origin is kab which is the opposite of naji'ah, and from it is the saying of Majma' bin Hilal: She says, after she has separated her from her husband, I am miserable, just as you have made me miserable, O Majma’. Al-Mubarrad said: That is, they are hated. Ibn Jurayj said: Away with them. Al-Suddi said: Disgrace for them. Ibn Zayd said: Misery for them. Al-Hasan said: An insult to them. Tha’lab said: Destruction for them. Al-Dahhak said: Disappointment for them. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Misery for them, as narrated by Al-Naqqash. Al-Dahhak said: Despite them. Tha’lab also said: Evil for them. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Misery for them. The lam in for them is for clarification, as in His statement: He is for you and His statement: And He rendered their deeds worthless, is conjoined with what precedes it and is included with it in the predicate of the relative pronoun.
47:9: And the reference in His saying: 9- That is to what was mentioned previously by God regarding misery and misguidance: meaning that matter, or that matter because they hated what God sent down to His Messenger from the Qur’an, or what He sent down to His Messengers from His books because they included what is in the Qur’an regarding monotheism and resurrection, so God rendered worthless their deeds for that reason, and what is meant by deeds are the good deeds they did in form even if they were invalid in origin, because the deeds of the disbeliever are not accepted before his conversion to Islam.
47:10: Then the Almighty frightened the disbelievers and guided them to consider the condition of those before them, saying: 10- Have they not traveled through the land? That is, did they not travel through the land of Aad, Thamut, the people of Lot, and others, to take a lesson and see how was the end of those before them? That is, the end of the disbelievers before them, for the traces of the punishment in their lands remain. Then the Almighty explained what He did to those before them, saying: God destroyed them. The sentence is a new chapter in response to an implied question. Destruction and annihilation mean He annihilated and uprooted them. It is said, He destroyed him and He destroyed him have the same meaning. Then He threatened the polytheists of Mecca, saying: And for the disbelievers is the like thereof. That is, for these disbelievers is the like of the end of the disbelieving nations before them. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Jarir said: The pronoun in like them refers to the consequences of those who came before them. It is pluralized because the consequences are multiple according to the number of nations punished. It was said that it is like the punishment, and it was said that it is destruction, and it was said that it is devastation. The first is more appropriate because the pronoun refers to what is mentioned before it.
47:11: And the reference in his saying: 11- That is to what was mentioned about the disbelievers having similar things because God is the Protector of those who believe meaning because God is their supporter and that the disbelievers have no protector meaning no supporter to defend them. Ibn Masoud read it as meaning that God is the Protector of those who believe. Qatada said: It was revealed on the Day of Uhud.
47:12: 12- Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. The explanation of the verse has been presented in more than one place, and the manner in which rivers flow beneath the gardens has been presented. The sentence is intended to explain God’s guardianship over the believers. And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as livestock eat. That is, they enjoy the pleasures of this world and benefit from them as if they were livestock with no concern other than their stomachs and their private parts, heedless of the outcome and distracted by what they are in. And the Fire will be their abode. That is, a place where they will reside, and a home where they will descend and settle. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state or a new sentence. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated and Ibn Mardawayh authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, Those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God, he said: They are the people of Mecca, the Quraysh, regarding whom the verse, And those who believed and did righteous deeds, was revealed. He said: They are the people of Medina, the Ansar. And set right their condition, he said: Their affairs. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, regarding the verse, He rendered worthless their deeds, he said: They had virtuous deeds, and God does not accept any deeds that are accompanied by disbelief. An-Nahhas also narrated on his authority, regarding the verse, Then either as a favor afterwards or ransom, he said: So God gave the Prophet and the believers the choice regarding the captives; if they wished, they could kill them, or enslave them, or ransom them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority, regarding the verse, he said: This is abrogated by the verse, So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Al-Hajjaj was brought prisoners, so he handed over a man to Ibn Umar to kill. Ibn Umar said: This is not our command. Rather, God said: “Until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure their bonds. Then either grant them favor or ransom them.” And Abd al-Razzaq narrated in al-Musannaf, and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Layth who said: I said to Mujahid: I have heard that Ibn Abbas said: It is not permissible to kill captives, because God said: Then either [take] a favor afterwards or ransom [them]. Mujahid said: Do not pay any attention to this. I met the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and they all denied this and said: This had been abrogated and that it had only been during the truce that was between the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the polytheists, but not today. God says: Kill the polytheists wherever you find them and He says: But when you meet those who disbelieve, strike [their] necks. If they are from the polytheists of the Arabs, nothing will be accepted from them except Islam. If they do not convert, then killing is permissible. As for others, if they are taken captive, the Muslims have a choice regarding them: they can kill them, or they can spare them, or they can ransom them if they do not abandon their religion. If they profess Islam, then ransom is not permissible. And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade the killing of children, women, and the elderly. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Soon, whoever among you lives will meet Jesus, son of Mary, as a guided Imam and just judge. He will break the cross, kill the pigs, abolish the jizyah, and war will lay down its burdens.” Ibn Sa’d, Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, al-Baghawi, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Salamah ibn Nufayl that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: War will not lay down its burdens until Gog and Magog emerge. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And for the disbelievers is the like of it. He said: For the disbelievers of your people, O Muhammad, is the same as the villages were destroyed by the sword.
47:13: The fear of God Almighty of the infidels is that He has destroyed those who were stronger than them, so He said: 13- And how many a town was stronger than your town which expelled you, We destroyed them. We have already mentioned that how many is composed of the letter kaf and the letter ay, and that it has the meaning of the report how many: that is, how many a town, and Al-Akhfash recited the words of Al-Walid: How many kings and commoners have we seen, and a key to the shackles of the bound prisoner? The meaning of the verse is: And how many a town was there that was stronger than the town from which they expelled you? We destroyed them, “so they had no helper. So it is even more appropriate for those who are weaker than them, namely the Quraysh, who are the people of the town of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is Mecca. So the discussion is about deleting the complement, as in His statement: And ask the town. Muqatil said: That is, We destroyed them with punishment when they denied their Messenger.
47:14: Then the Almighty mentioned the difference between the state of the believer and the state of the disbeliever, saying: 14- Is he who is upon clear evidence from his Lord? The hamza is for denial, and the fa is for connecting to an implied word like its counterparts, and min is the subject, and the predicate is like he to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive. And He made this singular in consideration of the word min, and plural in His saying: and followed their desires, in consideration of its meaning, and the meaning is: He who is certain of his Lord is not the same as he who is not like he to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive, which is the worship of idols, associating partners with God, and committing sins against God, and they followed their desires in their worship, and they became immersed in various types of misguidance without a doubt that necessitates doubt, let alone a clear proof.
47:15: Then when he distinguished between the two groups in guidance and misguidance, he distinguished between the two groups in their reference and their family, so he said: 15- The example of Paradise which has been promised to the righteous. The sentence confirms the explanation of the beauties of Paradise and what is stated in it, and the meaning of the example of Paradise is its description of the wondrous and important matter, and it is a subject and its predicate is omitted. Al-Nadr ibn Shammi said: Its estimation is what they hear, and Sibawayh estimated it in what is recited to you like Paradise. He said: The example is the description and its meaning is the description of Paradise, and the sentence in it is of water that is not stagnant is the explanation of the example. It was said that like is redundant, and it was said that like Paradise is a subject, and the predicate is in it rivers, and it was said that its predicate is like someone who is eternal, and stagnant is changing, so stagnant, stagnant: if its smell changes, and like it is putrid, and from it is the saying of Zuhair: I may leave the horn with yellow fingers, swaying in the spear like the stale salt sway. The public reading is Aasen with a long vowel. Hamid read it with a short vowel, and they are two dialects like Hadher and Hadhar. Al-Akhfash said: The long vowel refers to a new person, and the intended meaning is the present state. And rivers of milk whose taste is not consumed means it has not turned sour as the milk of this world has changed. Today it has not yet emerged from the udders of camels, sheep, and cows. And rivers of pleasure for the drinkers means beautiful to drink and the drinkers do not hate it. A hidden drink is a pungent drink and it has pleasure in the same meaning. An example of this famous verse: White, a pleasure for the drinkers I read pleasure in the accusative case as a description of wine, and ra is confirmed as a source or an object of the verb. It was read with the nominative case as a clear description. And rivers of purified honey meaning purified from what removes wax, dirt, turbidity and mud. And for them therein is every kind of fruit meaning, for the people of Paradise in Paradise with what was mentioned of drinks from every kind of fruit: meaning, from every type of its dishes. And forgiveness from their Lord for their sins. The indefiniteness of forgiveness for the great: meaning, for them is ignorance of the great: meaning, for them is forgiveness for the great, greenery from their Lord. Like one who is in eternal life is the predicate of the Fire for a deleted subject. Alberta: Or is he who is in the bliss of Paradise in this manner, eternally in it, as he is eternally in the Fire? Or predicate of his saying like Paradise as mentioned above. The first one was increased and said: Desiring is he who is in this bliss as he is eternally in the Fire. Al-Zajjaj said: Is one who has clear evidence from his Lord and has been given these things like one to whom his evil deeds have been made attractive while he is abiding eternally in the Fire? So his saying like is a substitute for the verse Is one to whom his evil deeds have been made attractive? Ibn Khaisan said: The likeness of Paradise in which are fruits and rivers is not like the likeness of Hell in which are scalding water and Zaqqum, and the likeness of the people of Paradise in bliss is not like the likeness of the people of Hell in severe torment, as in: And they will be given water to drink, blazing hot is an apposition to apposition, as you know, verbal to nominal, but the wording was taken into consideration in the center. From, and in the second its meaning, and the intense thanks for the boiling, but they drank it and it cut their intestines, and this is the meaning of saying: So it cut their intestines to resist its heat. And the intestines is the plural of with, and it is the contents in the stomachs.
47:16: 16- And among them are those who enjoy themselves with you meaning among those infidels who boast and eat as cattle eat those who enjoy themselves with you and they are the hypocrites. The pronoun was made singular in consideration of the word from, which specifies it and continues: until they leave you with consideration of its meaning, and the meaning is: that the hypocrites had accused and stopped the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the places where he dictated his sermons to the urine until they left him. They said to those who were given knowledge they are the scholars, and it was said Abdullah bin Abbas, and it was said Abdullah bin Masoud, and it was said Abu Darda, and the first: that is, they asked the people and said to them What did he say anfan that is, what did the prophet say just now in a mocking way, and the meaning: we did not pay attention to the companions, and anfan means knowledge of the hour is the nearest time, and from it is a matter anfan: that is, recognized, and a meadow anfan: that is, no one has pastured it, and its accusative case is circumstantial: at any time, affected, or a state of the pronoun in said. Al-Zajjaj said: it is from lam bida’a something: if you start it, and its origin is to ask from anfan something for what it has reached, abbreviated from the wound, and from it the poet says: Their neighbor's secret is forbidden to them, and their neighbor eats the tip of the bowl. The specific reference to that is: Those to the righteous hypocrites whose hearts God has sealed so they did not believe and their hearts were directed towards any good and they followed their desires in disbelief and stubbornness.
47:17: Then he mentioned the state of their opposites, saying: 17- "And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance." That is, those who are guided to the path of goodness, so they believe in God and do what He has commanded them, He increases them in guidance through success. It was also said that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, increased them, and it was also said that the Qur'an increased them. Al-Farra' said: The hypocrites' turning away and mocking increased their guidance. It was also said that the revelation of the abrogating verse increased their guidance. In any case, the evidence is that it increased their faith, knowledge, and insight in the religion. "And gave them their piety," that is, He inspired them with it and aided them in it. Piety, Al-Rabi' said: It is fear of God. Al-Suddi said: It is the reward of the Hereafter. Muqatil said: It is success in doing the work that pleases Him. It was also said that it means acting according to the abrogating verse and abandoning the abrogated verse. It was also said that it means abandoning concessions and adopting the obligatory verses.

47:19: 19- "Know that there is no god but God" meaning if you know that the basis of good is monotheism and obedience, and the basis of evil is polytheism and committing sins against God, then know that there is no god but Him and no Lord but Him. The meaning is: Be steadfast in that and continue on it, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knew that there is no god but God before this. It was said that whatever you know by deduction, know it by certainty. It was also said that the meaning is: Remember that there is no god but God, so remembrance was expressed as knowledge. "And seek forgiveness for your sin" meaning seek forgiveness from God that you should commit a sin, or seek forgiveness from God to protect you, or seek forgiveness from Him for what you might do by abandoning what is best. It was said that the address is to him, and what is meant is the nation. This is refuted by his statement: And for the believing men and believing women, for what is meant by it is his seeking forgiveness for the sins of his nation by praying for them to be forgiven for what they have neglected of their sins. And God knows your [place of] movement in your deeds and your resting place in the Hereafter. It was also said that it is your movement in your deeds during the day and your resting place during the night while you are asleep. It was also said that it is your movement in the loins of your fathers to the wombs of your mothers and your resting place on the earth: meaning your standing therein. Ibn Kaysan said that it is your movement from back to belly in this world, and your resting place is in the graves. Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, "When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left Mecca for the cave, he turned to Mecca and said, 'You are the most beloved land of God to me. Had your people not expelled me from you, I would not have left.' The most stubborn of enemies is he who rebels against God in His sanctuary, or kills someone other than his killer, or kills by entering the Age of Ignorance. So God revealed, And how many a town..." [verse]. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, "Rivers of water unpolluted," meaning unchanging. Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated on the authority of Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah, "I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say, 'In Paradise there is a sea of milk, a sea of water, a sea of honey, and a sea of wine. Then rivers will spring forth from them.' Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah narrated in his Musnad and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ka'b, who said, The Nile River is the river of honey in Paradise, the Tigris River is the river of milk in Paradise, the Euphrates River is the river of wine in Paradise, and the Sayhan River is the river of water in Paradise." Ibn Jarir and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - from the path of Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, the Almighty, {Until, when they go out from you, they say to those who have been given knowledge, What did he say just now?} He said: I was among those who were asked. Abd bin Hamid narrated from another chain of narration from him regarding the verse, he said: I am one of them. In this there is a great virtue for Ibn Abbas because at that time he was a boy who had not yet reached puberty, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) died while he was at the age of puberty. So the people asking him about the meanings of the Quran during the life of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and God’s description of those asked as those who have been given knowledge, and he being one of them, is one of the greatest proofs of the breadth of his knowledge and his deep understanding of the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, despite the fact that his peers and people of his age at that time were playing with boys. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ikrimah who said: They used to enter upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and when they left him they would say to Ibn Abbas, What did he say just now? He said such and such, and Ibn Abbas was the youngest of the people, so God revealed the verse, and Ibn Abbas was among those who were given knowledge. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ibn Buraydah regarding the verse, he said: He is Abdullah bin Masoud. Ibn Asakir narrated from Al-Kalbi from Abi Saleh from Ibn Abbas, he said: He is Abdullah bin Masoud. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, {And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness}, he said: When the Quran was revealed, they believed in it, so it was guidance. Then when the abrogating verse was distinguished from the abrogated, He increased them in guidance. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from him, And its portents have come, he said: The first of the hours. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others from the hadith of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: I and the Hour have been sent like these two, and he pointed with his middle and index fingers. A similar narration is reported by Al-Bukhari from the hadith of Sahl bin Sa’d. There are many hadiths on this topic that explain the signs of the Hour, what has happened and what has not. They will be discussed in a separate book, so we will not prolong their mention. At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The best remembrance is ‘There is no god but God,’ and the best supplication is ‘seeking forgiveness.’ Then he recited, ‘Know that there is no god but God. And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women.’” Abdur-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah regarding his statement, ‘And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women,’ the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I ask God for forgiveness seventy times a day. Ahmad, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sarjis who said: “I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and ate some food with him. I said: ‘May God forgive you, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘And for you.’ It was said: ‘Do you seek forgiveness for yourself, O Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)?’ He said: ‘Yes, and for you.’ And he recited: ‘And seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women.’” There are hadiths about the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) seeking forgiveness for himself and his Ummah and encouraging people to seek forgiveness. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And God knows your movements in this world and your resting place in the Hereafter.
47:20: The believers asked their Lord, the Almighty, to send down to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, a surah in which he would command them to fight the disbelievers, inciting them to jihad and attaining the abundant reward that God has prepared for the mujahideen. God spoke about that on their authority, saying: 20- And those who believe say, ‘Why was a surah not sent down?’ But when a surah is sent down that is decisive, that is, not abrogated, and fighting is mentioned therein, that is, the obligation of jihad, Qatada said: Every surah in which jihad is mentioned is decisive, and it is the harshest of the Quran on the hypocrites. According to the reading of Ibn Masoud, When a newly revealed surah is sent down, that is, its revelation was newly revealed. The majority read When a surah is sent down, and mentioned in the passive form of the two verbs. Zayd ibn Ali and Ibn Umair read it as revealed and mentioned in the structure of the two verbs for the agent and the accusative of fighting. I saw those in whose hearts is disease meaning doubt, and they are the hypocrites looking at you with the look of one fainting from death meaning they look at you with the look of one who has lost his sight at death due to their cowardice in fighting and their inclination towards the disbelievers. Ibn Qutaybah and Al-Zajjaj said: He means that they stare at you with intense gaze as one who stares at death looks. So it is more fitting for them Al-Jawhari said: Their saying It is more fitting for you is a threat and warning, and this is what Muqatil, Al-Kalbi and Qatadah said. Al-Asma’i said: The meaning of their saying in the threat is It is more fitting for you meaning your guardian and what you dislike is close to you. He recited the words of the poet: He was divided between two of them, and it is better to exceed three. Anything that is close to increasing. Tha'lab said: And no one has said anything better than what Al-Asma'i said. Al-Mubarrad said: For those who are about to get angry and then it gets away, it is better for you: meaning you are close to getting angry. Al-Jarhani said: It is taken from woe, meaning woe to them, and this is what he said in Al-Kashaf. Qatada also said: It is as if he said punishment is better for them.
47:21: And His statement: 21- Obedience and appropriate speech is a new statement: meaning, their command is obedience, or obedience and appropriate speech is better for you. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: The estimation is obedience and appropriate speech is better and more appropriate for you than anything else. It was said that obedience is the predicate of the first, and it was said that obedience is an attribute of the surah, and it was said that they have an advanced predicate and obedience is a delayed subject, and the first is better. So when the matter is decided the matter is decided, the matter becomes serious: meaning the fighting becomes serious, obligatory and mandatory, and the determination is attributed to the matter and it is metaphorically for its people, and the answer to if it is said is So if they were truthful with God and it was said that it is omitted, its estimation is that they hated it. The commentators said that its meaning is that when the matter becomes serious and the obligation of fighting becomes obligatory, they disobey and stay behind. So if they were truthful with God in showing faith and obedience it would have been better for them than disobedience and disobedience.
47:22: 22- If you were given authority, would you then cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? This is addressed to those in whose hearts is disease, by way of turning to further rebuke and reprimand. Al-Kalbi said: That is, if you were given authority over this nation, would you then cause corruption in the land through injustice? Ka’b said: If you were given authority, would you then cause corruption in the land meaning by killing one another. Qatada said: If you turned away from obeying the Book of God, the Almighty, would you then cause corruption in the land through shedding blood and severing your ties of kinship? Ibn Jurayj said: If you turned away from obedience, and it was said that you turned away from fighting and abandoned its rulings. The majority of scholars read tawlaytum as an active verb, while Ali ibn Abi Talib read it with a damma on the ta' and waw and a kasra on the lam as a passive verb. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Warsh read it this way on the authority of Ya'qub. Its meaning is, So, if unjust rulers rule over you, will you revolt against them in sedition, fight them, and sever your family ties through oppression, injustice, and killing? The majority of scholars read wa-taqat'aw with a shaddah indicating abundance. Abu 'Amr, in a narration from him, and Salam, 'Isa, and Ya'qub read it with a light saq'at. It is said, 'I may that I do such-and-such. 'I may with a fatha and a kasra are two dialects, mentioned by al-Jawhari and others. The predicate of 'Imaytum is that you will corrupt, and the conditional clause between them is an interjection.
47:23: And the reference in His saying: 23- Those is to those addressed by what preceded, and it is the subject and predicate: those whom God has cursed: that is, He has distanced them from His mercy and expelled them from it. So He has made them deaf from hearing the truth and blinded their sight from seeing what they use as evidence for monotheism, resurrection, and the truth of all that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to.
47:24: The question in His statement: 24- Do they not then consider the Qur'an? is for denial, and the meaning is: Do they not understand it and know what it contains of admonitions and clear arguments and conclusive proofs that are sufficient for those who have understanding and reason and deter them from disbelieving in God, associating partners with Him, and committing sins? Or are there locks upon their hearts? Or are they the closed ones: meaning, rather, the hearts have locks, so they do not understand or reason. Muqatil said: He means the seal on the hearts and the locks are a metaphor for the heart being closed to knowing the truth. Adding the locks to the hearts is to indicate that what is meant by them is what is for the hearts, like locks for doors. The meaning of the verse is that faith will not enter their hearts nor will disbelief and polytheism exit from them, because God, the Exalted, has sealed them, and what is meant by these hearts are the hearts of those addressed. The majority read its locks in the plural, and its locks was read with a kasra on the hamza as a verbal noun like approach.
47:25: 25- Indeed, those who turned back on their heels means they returned to being disbelievers as they were. Qatada said: They are the disbelievers of the People of the Book who disbelieved in the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after they recognized his description among themselves. Ibn Jarir said the same. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: They are the hypocrites who sat back from fighting. This is more appropriate because the context is about the hypocrites after guidance had become clear to them with what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought to them of apparent miracles and clear proofs. Satan enticed them means he made their sins seem attractive to them and made it easy for them to fall into them. This sentence is the predicate of inna, and the meaning of and granted them respite is that Satan extended their hope and promised them a long life. It was said that the one who granted them respite was God, meaning that He did not hasten their punishment. The majority read amla in the active form, while Abu Amr, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa ibn Umar, Abu Ja`far, and Shaibah read it in the passive form. It was said that according to this reading, the agent is God or Satan, as in the first reading. Al-Farra and Al-Mufaddal chose to say that the agent is God, but it is better to choose that it is Satan, as he was mentioned soon.
47:26: And the reference in His saying: 26- That is to what preceded their apostasy, and it is the subject and predicate because they said to those who hated what God revealed - and they are the polytheists - We will obey you in some of the matter and this some is the enmity of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and opposition to what he brought. And it was said that the meaning is: The hypocrites said to the Jews: We will obey you in some of the matter, and it was said that the speakers were the Jews and those who hated what God revealed: the hypocrites, and it was said that the reference in His saying that is to dictation, and it was said to incitement, and the first is more appropriate. This is supported by the fact that the speakers, the hypocrites and the haters, are the Jews, and God the Almighty said: Have you not seen those who are hypocrites saying to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you and we will never obey anyone concerning you, and if you are fought, we will surely aid you" And since their aforementioned saying was to those who hated what God revealed in secret among themselves. God the Almighty said: And God knows their secrets. The majority of scholars read it with a fat-ha over the hamza, the plural of secret. This reading was favored by Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. The Kufians, Hamzah, al-Nasa’i, and Hafs on the authority of Asim, Ibn Waththab, and al-A’mash read it with a kasra over the hamzah, as a source meaning their concealment.
47:27: 27- How will it be when the angels take their souls? The fa indicates the order of what comes after it based on what comes before it. How is in the nominative case as a predicate that comes before it. The meaning is: How will He know their secrets when the angels take them? Or it is in the accusative case with an omitted verb: meaning how do they act? Or it is in the accusative case with an implied verb: meaning how are they? Or it is the predicate of kana which is understood: meaning how are they? And the adverbial phrase is the object of the understood one. The majority of scholars read tawathum while Al-A'mash read tawathum and the phrase yadhibun fawjuhum wa adbarhum is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of tawathum or its object: meaning striking their faces and striking their backs. The speech is intimidating and emphatic, and the meaning is that if the punishment is delayed for them, their condition will be like this, which is a depiction of their death in the ugliest and most hideous condition. It was said that this was during the battle as support from the angels for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and it was said that this was on the Day of Resurrection, but the first is more appropriate.
47:28: And the reference in His saying: 28- That is to the mentioned death in the mentioned manner, and it is a subject and its predicate is because they followed what angered God meaning because of their following what angered God of disbelief and sins, and it was said that it was their concealment of what was in the Torah of the description of a prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the first is more appropriate because of the generality in the formula and they hated His pleasure meaning they hated what pleased God of faith, monotheism and obedience so God rendered null “their deeds” for this reason, and what is meant by their deeds are the deeds that took the form of obedience, otherwise there is no deed for a disbeliever, or what they had done of good before the apostasy.
47:29: 29- Or do those in whose hearts is disease think meaning the hypocrites mentioned previously, and am is the disconnected form: that is, the hypocrites think that God will not bring to light their hatred. Bringing to light means making known, and hatred is the plural of daghn, which is what is concealed of hatred. There is disagreement over its meaning, some say it is deceit, some say it is envy, and some say it is rancor. Al-Jawhari said: Rancor and rancor are hatred. Qatrib said: In the verse it is enmity, and an is the lightened form of the heavy form, and its subject is a pronoun of matter that is understood.
47:30: 30- And if We willed, We could have shown them to you meaning, We could have taught you and recognized them by their faces, a recognition that takes the place of seeing. The Arabs say: I will show you what I do, meaning I will teach you. Then you would have known them by their mark, meaning by their special mark that distinguishes them. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, if We willed, We could have made a mark on the hypocrites, which is the mark, so I would have known them by that mark. The fa is to make knowledge follow showing, and what follows it is conjoined to the answer to law and it was repeated in the conjoined word for emphasis. As for the lam in His statement: And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech, it is the answer to an omitted oath. The commentators said: The tone of speech is its gist, purpose, and meaning, and what they offer of satirizing you and the Muslims. After this, no hypocrite would speak in his presence except that he recognized it. Abu Zayd said: You made him speak the tone of the speech: if you said something to him that he would understand from you but that was hidden from others. From this is the saying of the poet: Sound logic, sometimes you make mistakes, but the best speech is that which is good The best of it is that which is an allusion to the mind of the addressee and is not understood by anyone else due to his intelligence and cleverness. The origin of the mistake is to incline the speech to a certain direction for a certain purpose. And God knows your deeds, nothing of them is hidden from Him, so He will reward you for them. And in it is a severe warning.
47:31: 31- And We will surely test you until We make evident those among you who strive [for the cause of God] and the patient. That is, We will treat you as one who is tested, by ordering you to fight until We make evident those who have complied with the command to fight and have been patient in their religion and the hardships of what they have been charged with. The majority of scholars read the three verbs with a nun, while Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim, read them all with a ta under the letter kh in them.
