The meaning of And We will test your report is that We will reveal it and expose it as a test for you so that it may become clear to the people who have obeyed God’s command, and who has disobeyed, and who has not. The majority of scholars read And We will test with a waw in the accusative case, in apposition to the statement until We make evident. Warsh narrated on the authority of Ya’qub that it is sukoon as a break from what preceded it. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God created the creation, and when He finished with them, the womb stood in line with the Most Merciful. He said: ‘No!’ She said: ‘This is the station of one who seeks refuge in You from being severing ties.’ He said: ‘Yes, would you be pleased that I should maintain ties with those who maintain ties with you and sever ties with those who sever ties with you?’ She said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then that is yours.’ Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Recite if you wish, “Then will you…” from the verse to the words, Or are there locks upon their hearts? There are many hadiths about maintaining ties of kinship. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, Indeed, those who turn back on their heels, that he said: They are the hypocrites. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding His statement, Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that God will not bring to light their hatred? He said: Their deeds are their malice and the envy in their hearts. Then God, the Most High, guided the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to the hypocrites, so he would call by the name of a hypocrite. Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri regarding his statement: And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech, he said: By their hatred of Ali bin Abi Talib.
47:32: His statement: 32- Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God refers to the hypocrites, and it was said that they are the People of the Book, and it was said that they are the polytheists who were coveted on the Day of Badr. The meaning of averting people from the way of God is that they prevented people from Islam and following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the meaning of opposed the Messenger is that they opposed him and opposed him after guidance had become clear to them meaning that they knew that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a prophet from God through what they witnessed of clear miracles and conclusive proofs. They will never harm God at all by abandoning faith and persisting in disbelief. They have only harmed themselves. And He will render their deeds worthless meaning He will nullify them. What is meant by these deeds is what is portrayed as good deeds such as feeding the poor, maintaining family ties, and all the other good deeds they used to do, even if they were invalid from the beginning because disbelief is an obstacle. It was said that what is meant by deeds are the plots they set up to invalidate the religion of God and the calamities they sought to harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
47:33: Then God, the Almighty, commanded His believing servants to obey Him and His Messenger, saying: 33- O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger in what you have been commanded to do of the laws mentioned in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger. Then He forbade them from invalidating their deeds as the disbelievers invalidated their deeds by persisting in disbelief, saying: And do not invalidate your deeds. Al-Hasan said: That is, do not invalidate your good deeds by committing sins. Al-Zuhri said: By major sins. Al-Kalbi and Ibn Jurayj said: By showing off and seeking fame. Muqatil said: By showing off. What appears to be the prohibition of every cause that leads to the invalidation of deeds, whatever it may be, without specifying a particular type.
47:34: Then the Almighty made it clear that He will not forgive those who persist in disbelief and avert people from the path of God, saying: 34- Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert people from the way of God and then die while they are disbelievers - never will God forgive them. The Almighty restricted the lack of forgiveness to death in disbelief, because the door of repentance and the path to forgiveness are not closed to those who are alive, and the apparent meaning of the verse is general, even if the reason is specific.
47:35: Then the Almighty forbade the believers from weakness and feebleness, saying: 35- So do not weaken meaning, be too weak to fight, and weakness means weakness. “And call for peace” meaning, do not call the disbelievers to peace on your own initiative, because that only happens when you are weak. Al-Zajjaj said: God forbade the Muslims from calling the disbelievers to peace and ordered them to fight them until they submit. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read wa tadda’u with a shaddah on the dal from ada’da’ al-qawm and tadda’u. Qatada said: The meaning of the verse is: Do not be the first of the two parties to supplicate to the other. Scholars differed as to whether this verse is definitive or abrogated. Some said it is definitive and that it abrogates the statement: “But if they incline to peace, then incline to it.” Others said it was abrogated by this verse. It is clear that there is no justification for the view of abrogation, as God, the Exalted, forbade the Muslims in this verse from calling for peace in the first place, but He did not forbid accepting peace if the polytheists incline towards it. Thus, the two verses are definitive and did not occur in the same place, to the point of requiring a claim of abrogation or specification. The phrase and you are superior is in the accusative case as a state, or it is a new sentence confirming the prohibition before it: that is, you are the victors by the sword and argument. Al-Kalbi said: “That is, in the end, your affair will be, even if they defeat you at times. Likewise, the phrase “And God is with you” is in the accusative case as a state: that is, with you in victory and assistance over them. And He will not deprive you of your deeds that is, He will not deprive you of anything from the reward for your deeds. It is said that he diminished his right, and its origin is from the word watartu killing a relative of his or stealing his money. It is also said that someone is ma’tur deprived of his blood money if someone killed someone for him and his blood money was not punished. Al-Jawhari said: That is, He will not diminish your deeds, just as you say, ‘I entered the house’, meaning ‘in the house’. Al-Farra’ said: It is derived from “watar entering which means entering, and it was also said that it is derived from watar spreading, so the meaning is: a color that singles you out without reward.”
47:36: 36- The life of this world is only play and amusement. That is, it is falsehood and delusion, there is no basis for any of it, no stability, and no transgression against it. But if you believe and fear God, He will give you your rewards. That is, if you believe in God and fear disbelief and sins, He will give you the reward for that in the Hereafter, and the reward is for obedience. And He does not ask of you your wealth. That is, He does not command you to give all of it in zakat and other forms of obedience, rather He commands you to give a small amount of it, which is zakat. It was said that the meaning is: He does not ask of you for your wealth, rather He asks of you His wealth because He owns it, and He is the One who bestows it upon you. It was also said that He does not ask of you your wealth as a reward for conveying the message, as in His statement: I do not ask of you for it any reward. The former is more appropriate.
47:37: 37- "If they ask you for it meaning all of your wealth, He will force you" The commentators said: He will exhaust you and insist upon you by asking you all of it. It is said that he is persistent in asking, and he is persistent and insistent, meaning they all have the same meaning. Al-Muhaffa is the one who asks thoroughly, and Ihfaa is the thoroughness in speech, and from this comes the word Ihfaa al-Shaar exterminating the drinker: meaning he will eradicate it. The answer to the condition is His statement: "Be miserly" meaning if He orders you to give away all of your wealth, you will be miserly with it and refuse to comply. "And He will bring forth your grudges" is in apposition to the answer to the condition. For this reason, the majority read "He will bring forth" in the jussive mood. It was narrated from Abu Amr that he read it in the nominative case as a resumption. It was narrated from him that he read with the fatha on the yaa and the damma on the raa and raised your grudges. It was narrated from Yaqub al-Hadrami that he read with the nun. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ibn Muhaisin and Hamid read it with the fatha over the raa and the damma on the raa. According to the reading of the majority, the subject is a pronoun that refers to God, the Most High, or to the miserliness indicated by "Tabkhalu". Grudges: hatreds, meaning that they appear at that time. Qatada said: God knows that asking for money brings out grudges.
47:38: 38- Here you are, being called upon to spend in the cause of God meaning, here you are, O believers, being called upon to spend in jihad and in the path of goodness. But among you is he who is stingy with what is asked of him and called upon to spend in the cause of God. If there are those among you who are stingy with a little money, how would you not be stingy with a lot, which is all money? Then the Almighty made clear that the harm of stinginess returns to the self, saying: And whoever is stingy is only stingy with himself meaning he prevents himself from reward and recompense through his stinginess, and stinginess is transitive with ala sometimes and ban other times. It was said that its origin is transitive with 'ala and not with 'an unless it includes the meaning of withholding. And God is the Rich the Absolute, the One free from need for your money. And you are the poor to God and to what is with Him of goodness and mercy. The phrase And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people is conjoined with the previous conditional, which is and if you believe. The meaning is: If you turn away from faith and piety, He will replace you with another people who will be more obedient to God than you. Then they will not be the likes of you in turning away from faith and piety. 'Ikrimah said: They are the Persians and the Romans. Al-Hasan said: They are the Persians. Shuraih ibn 'Ubaid said: They are the people of Yemen. It was also said: They are the Ansar, the angels, and the followers. Mujahid said: They are whomever God wills from among the rest of the people. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning is: Then they will not be the likes of you in stinginess in spending in the way of God. Abd ibn Humayd, Muhammad ibn Nasr in his book on prayer, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah who said: The companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to think that no sin could harm one who proclaims La ilaha illa God just as no deed could benefit one who professes polytheism until the verse, Obey God and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds was revealed. They feared that sin would invalidate the deeds. The wording of Abd ibn Humayd is: They feared that major sins would render their deeds worthless. Ibn Nasr, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: We, the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), used to think that no good deed would be accepted until the verse, Obey God and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds was revealed. When this verse was revealed, we said: What is this that invalidates our deeds? So we said: The major sins that commit sins and the indecencies. So if we saw someone committing any of these, we would say he is doomed, until this verse was revealed: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. When this verse was revealed, we stopped speaking about it. When we saw someone committing any of these, we feared for him, but if he did not commit any of them, we hoped for him. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: He will leave you, he said: When the verse: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people was revealed, they said: Who are these? And Salman was beside the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He said: They are the Persians, this one and his people. In its chain of transmission is Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanj, and he is the only one who transmitted it, and there is a well-known criticism of him. He 'will replace you with another people.' They said: 'O Messenger of God, who are these people who, if we turn away, will replace us and will not be the likes of us?' The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck Salman on the shoulder and said: 'This one and his people.' By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if faith were suspended from the Pleiades, men from Persia would attain it.”” Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanj also is in its chain of transmission. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Jabir.
48:1: It has twenty-nine verses, and it is Medinan. Al-Qurtubi said: By consensus. Ibn Al-Durais, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Fath was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr. Ibn Ishaq and Al-Hakim narrated - and Al-Bayhaqi authenticated it in Al-Dala’il - on the authority of Al-Miswar bin Makhrama and Marwan, who said: Surat Al-Fath was revealed between Makkah and Madinah regarding Al-Hudaybiyyah from beginning to end. This does not contradict the consensus that it was revealed in Madinah, because what is meant by a Madinan surah is the one revealed after the migration from Makkah. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Mughaffal, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited Surat Al-Fath on his mount in the year of the conquest, while he was traveling, and then he returned in it. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was traveling on one of his journeys, and Umar ibn al-Khattab was traveling with him at night. Umar asked him about something, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not answer him. Then he asked him, but he did not answer him. Then he asked him, but he did not answer him. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: ‘Umar’s mother has perished. I called upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, three times, and each time he did not answer you.’ Umar said: ‘So I spurred my camel on, then I went ahead of the people, and I was afraid that something had been revealed about the Qur’an. I had not waited long before I heard someone shouting at me. I said: ‘I was afraid that something had been revealed about the Qur’an. So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him. He said: ‘A surah has been revealed to me, and it is more beloved to me than anything upon which the sun rises.’ Then he recited, ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory.’” In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Qatadah, that Anas ibn Malik told them: When the verse, ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory,’ was revealed, up to His saying, ‘a great victory.’ He was returning from al-Hudaybiyyah. They were filled with sadness and depression, and they had slaughtered the sacrificial animals at Al-Hudaybiyah. He said: A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the entire world. His saying: 1- Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. There is a difference of opinion regarding the specificity of this conquest. The majority say that it is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and a treaty may be called a conquest. Al-Farra' said: A conquest may also be a peace treaty. The meaning of conquest in language is: to open something that is closed. The treaty that was with the polytheists at Hudaybiyyah was blocked and impossible until God granted it a victory. Al-Zuhri said: There was no conquest greater than the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. This was because the polytheists mingled with the Muslims and listened to their words, so Islam took root in their hearts. In three years, many people converted to Islam, and the majority of Muslims increased through them. Al-Sha'bi said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) achieved in Hudaybiyyah what he had never achieved in any other battle. God forgave him his past and future sins. The Pledge of Ridwan was given, the palm trees of Khaybar were fed, the sacrificial animals reached their destination, and the Romans defeated the Persians. The believers rejoiced at the victory of the People of the Book over the Magians. Some people said: It was the Conquest of Mecca. Others said: It was the Conquest of Khaybar. The first is more likely, and is supported by what we mentioned before, that the Surah was revealed regarding Al-Hudaybiyyah. It was said that it refers to all the conquests that God opened for His Messenger, and it was said that it refers to the prophethood and the call to Islam, and it was said that it refers to the conquest of the Romans, and it was said that what is meant by conquest in this verse is judgment and judgment, as in His statement: Judge between us and our people in truth, so it is as if He said: Indeed, We have decreed for you a clear judgment, meaning apparent, clear, and obvious.
48:2: 2- That God may forgive you your sins, past and future The lam is connected to fathaana opening, not the cause. Ibn al-Anbari said: I asked Abu al-Abbas meaning al-Mubarrad about the lam in His statement, That God may forgive you, and he said: It is the lam of ki, meaning: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, so that the completion of the blessing may be combined for you with forgiveness in the conquest. So when something new and real is combined with the forgiveness, the meaning of ki is good, and whoever says that the conquest is not the cause of forgiveness is wrong. The author of al-Kashshaf said: The lam was not the cause of forgiveness, but rather the combination of a number of four things, which are: forgiveness, completion of the blessing, guidance to the straight path, and the glorious victory. It is as if it was said: We facilitated for you the conquest of Mecca and granted you victory over your enemy, so that we may combine for you the glory of both abodes, and the blessings of this world and the hereafter. This is not a good statement, because the lam is included in forgiveness, so it is the cause of the conquest, so how can it be the cause? Al-Razi said in explaining the reason: What is meant by His statement, So that God may forgive you, is the definition of forgiveness, meaning: We have granted you victory so that you may know that you are forgiven and protected. Ibn Atiyyah said: What is meant is that God granted you victory in order to make the victory a sign of His forgiveness of you, so it is as if it is the lam of becoming. Abu Hatim said: It is the lam of an oath, which is a mistake, because the lam of an oath is not broken or placed in the accusative case. There is a difference of opinion as to the meaning of the statement of God, Whatever of your sins have come before and whatever is to come after them. Some say that it refers to your sins that came before the message and those that came after it. This was said by Mujahid, Sufyan, Ath-Thawri, Ibn Jarir, Al-Wahidi and others. Ata’ said: Whatever of your sins have come before means the sin of your parents Adam and Eve, and what are to come of the sins of your nation. This is very far from the meaning of the Quran. It was also said that it refers to the sins of your father Abraham, and the sins of the prophets who came after him. This is like the previous statement. It was also said that it refers to the sins that came before on the day of Badr and the sins that came after on the day of Hunayn. This is similar to the first two statements in being far-fetched. It was also said that if it had been an old or new sin, we would have deceived you. Another statement was made that this is baseless, but the first is more appropriate. What is meant by sin after the message is abandoning what is best, and it is called a sin in his right due to his great status even if it is not a sin in the right of anyone else. And He completes His favor upon you by making your religion prevail over all other religions. It was also said that it was Paradise, and it was also said that it was prophethood and wisdom, and it was also said that it was the conquest of Mecca, Taif, and Khaybar. The first is that the meaning is: So that the conquest may bring together for you the completion of the favor with forgiveness and guidance to the straight path, which is Islam. The meaning of He guides you is that He makes you steadfast on guidance until He takes you to Him.
48:3: 3- And God will grant you a mighty victory meaning a victorious and powerful victory that is not followed by humiliation.
48:4: 4- It is He who has sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers meaning peace and reassurance through the victory He has made easy for them so that their souls will not be disturbed by what befalls them that they may increase in faith along with their faith meaning that because of that tranquility they may increase in faith, adding to the faith they already have. Al-Kalbi said: Whenever a verse is sent down from the heaven and they believe in it, their belief increases with their belief. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Fear along with their fear. Ad-Dahhak said: Certainty along with their certainty And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth meaning the angels, mankind, jinn and devils. He manages their affairs as He wills, giving some of them power over others and surrounding some of them with others And God is Ever-Knowing of abundant knowledge, eloquent Wise in His actions and words.
48:5: 4- That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow. This lam is related to an omitted word indicated by what precedes it, which is that He tests with those soldiers whomever He wills, so He accepts good from its people and evil from whomever He has decreed for it, so that he may enter and be punished. It was also said that it is related to His saying: Indeed, We have opened, as if He said: Indeed, We have opened for you what We have opened so that he may enter and be punished. It was also said that it is related to He will give you victory, meaning that God will give you victory with the believers so that he may enter and be punished. It was also said that it is related to They will increase, meaning that they will increase so that he may enter and be punished. The first is more appropriate. And He will cover up their misdeeds, meaning that He will conceal them and not reveal them and will not punish them for them. He presented the introduction before the expiation, even though the command is the opposite, in order to hasten to explain what is the highest goal and the most sublime purpose. And that is with God a great triumph, meaning that it is a triumph of everything desired and salvation from every sorrow and bringing about every benefit and repelling every harm. His saying: With God is related to an omitted word as a state of triumph, because Originally an adjective, but when it was presented it became a state: that is, existing with God. The sentence is parenthetical between the reward of the believers and the reward of the hypocrites and polytheists.
48:6: Then when He finished what He promised His righteous servants, He mentioned what others deserve, saying: 6- And He will punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women. This is connected to enters. That is, He will punish them in this world with the worries and sorrows that they will experience because of what they will witness of the emergence of the word of Islam and the subjugation of those who oppose it, and with the subjugation, killing, and imprisonment that they will suffer. And in the Hereafter, He will punish them with the torment of Hell. Giving precedence to the hypocrites over the polytheists indicates that they will be more severely punished than them and more deserving of what God has promised them. Then He described the two groups, saying: Those who think evil of God. This is their belief that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will prevail and that the word of disbelief will prevail over the word of Islam. Among what they thought was what God related about them in His saying: Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families “upon them is a circle of evil” meaning that what they thought and waited for the believers will circle around them and surround them. The meaning is that the torment and destruction that they expect for the believers will befall them. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: Evil here means corruption. The majority read evil with a fatha on the seen. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a damma. And God has become angry with them and has cursed them and has prepared Hell for them, and evil it is as a destination because God Almighty made it clear that the circle of evil will be upon them in this world and what they deserve in addition to that of wrath, curse, and torment in Hell.
48:7: 7- And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth of angels, humans, jinn, and devils and God is Knowing and Wise. This verse was repeated for the purpose of emphasis. It was said that what is meant by the soldiers here are the soldiers of torment, as is indicated by the expression of glory here instead of knowledge there. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Majma’ ibn Haritha al-Ansari who said: “We witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah. When we turned back and reached Kura’ al-Ghamim, the people were urging their camels on. The people said to one another: ‘What is wrong with the people?’ They said: ‘Revelation has been sent down to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so we went out with the people urging their camels on. Then we saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on his mount at Kura’ al-Ghamim. The people gathered around him and he recited to them: ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest.’ A man said: ‘Yes, Messenger of God, or is it a conquest?’ He said: ‘Yes, by the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, it is a conquest.’ Khaybar was divided among the people of al-Hudaybiyyah. No one entered it with them except those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divided it into eighteen shares. The army numbered one thousand five hundred, including three hundred horsemen. He gave the horsemen two shares and the infantry one share.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Bukhari in his History, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: We came from Al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). While we were walking, the revelation came to him. Whenever it came to him, he would be overwhelmed with emotion, but he was relieved and filled with as much joy as God willed. Then He informed us that the following had been revealed to him: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Anas regarding His statement: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, he said: Al-Hudaybiyyah. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’ who said: You consider the conquest to be the conquest of Mecca, but the conquest of Mecca was a conquest, and we consider the conquest to be the Pledge of Ridwan on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. He said: The conquest of Mecca. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah that he said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pray until his feet swelled. Then it was said: Has God not forgiven you your past and future sins? He said: Should I not then be a grateful servant?” There are hadiths on this topic. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: It is He who has sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers, that he said: Tranquility means mercy. Concerning His statement: that they may increase in faith along with their present faith, he said: God sent His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with the testimony that there is no god but God. When the believers believed in it, He increased them in prayer. When they rejected it, He increased them in fasting. When they believed in it, He increased them in zakat. When they believed in it, He increased them in Hajj. When they believed in it, He increased them in jihad. Then He perfected their religion for them, saying: This day I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as religion. Ibn Abbas said: The strongest, most truthful, and most complete faith of the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth is the testimony that there is no god but God. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud: That they may increase in faith along with their faith. He said: Belief along with their belief. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: When the verse, So that God may forgive you your sins, past and future, was revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he returned from Al-Hudaybiyyah. He said: A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than anything on the earth. Then he recited it to them. They said: Congratulations and good report, O Messenger of God! God has made clear to you what He will do with you, so what will He do with us? Then the verse, So that He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, was revealed to him until he reached a great attainment.
48:8: His saying: 8- Indeed, We have sent you as a witness meaning over your nation by conveying the message to them and a bringer of good tidings of Paradise to the obedient and a warner to the disobedient.
48:9: 9- That you may believe in God and His Messenger. The majority of reciters read that you may believe with a superlative. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a sublative. According to the first reading, the addressee is the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his Ummah. According to the second reading, the intended recipients of good tidings and the warners are the witnesses, bearers of good tidings, and warners. The accusatives of witness, bearers of good tidings, and warner are in the nominative case. And you support him, honor him, and glorify him. The disagreement among the reciters regarding these three and the verbs is like the disagreement regarding that you may believe, as mentioned previously. The meaning of that you support him is to glorify and magnify him. This was stated by Al-Hasan and Al-Kalbi. Honoring means to glorify and respect him. Qatada said: to support him and protect yourself from him. Ikrimah said: fight with him with the sword. The meaning of that you honor him is to venerate him. Al-Suddi said: Tasbihhu You praise Him. It was said that the two pronouns in the two verbs refer to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Here there is a complete pause, then he begins, Tasbihhu and glorify Him: meaning glorify God the Almighty morning and evening meaning in the morning and evening. It was also said that all the pronouns are in the three verbs, the Almighty, so the meaning of Ta’zirhu you honor and respect Him: you affirm His Oneness and deny Him partners. It was also said that you support His religion and strive alongside His Messenger. There are two aspects to glorifying Him: one of them is to sanctify Him, the Almighty, from all that is ugly, and the second is prayer.
48:10: 10- Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you meaning the Pledge of Ridwan at Hudaybiyyah, for they pledged allegiance under the tree to fight Quraysh are only pledging allegiance to God God the Almighty informed us that this pledge of allegiance to His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is a pledge of allegiance to Him, as He said: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God because they have sold themselves to God for Paradise. The phrase the Hand of God is over their hands is a new sentence to confirm what came before it by way of imagination in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is that the covenant with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is like his covenant with God the Almighty, without any difference. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is that the blessing of God upon them in guidance is above what they did in the pledge of allegiance. And it was said that His hand in reward is above their hands in fulfilling it. Ibn Kisyan said: God’s power and victory are greater than their power and victory. But whoever breaks his oath, he only breaks it to the detriment of his own soul. That is, whoever breaks the pledge he has made, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself, because the harm of that will be attributed to him and not to anyone else. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God. That is, he remains steadfast in fulfilling what he pledged to God in the pledge of allegiance to His Messenger. The majority of scholars read to him with a kasra on the ha’, while Hafs and Az-Zuhri read it with a damma. Then He will give him a great reward, which is Paradise. The majority of scholars read they will give him with a tā’, and Nafi’ and Kathir and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a noon. Abu ‘Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading, while Al-Farra’ preferred the second reading.
48:11: 11- The bedouins who stayed behind will say to you They are those whom God left behind from accompanying His Messenger when he departed in the year of Hudaybiyyah. Mujahid and others said: He means the bedouins of Ghifar, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, and Ashja’ ad-Dail, and they are the bedouins who lived around Madinah. It was said that they stayed behind when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) traveled to Mecca in the year of the conquest, after he had summoned them to go out with him. The one who stays behind is the one who is left behind. Our wealth and our families have preoccupied us means that our wealth, women and children have prevented us from going out with you, and we have no one to take care of them or take care of them. So ask forgiveness for us so that God may forgive us for what we did in staying behind you for this reason. Since asking forgiveness from them was not based on belief but rather in a mocking manner, and their inner selves were different from their outward appearance, God, the Exalted, exposed them with His saying: They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. This is the action of the hypocrites. The sentence is a new sentence to explain what their inner selves conceal, and it may be a substitute for the first sentence. Then God, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to answer them, saying: Say, ‘Then who can prevent you from God at all?’ Meaning, who can prevent you from what God intends for you of good or evil? Then He clarified that by saying: If He intends for you harm, meaning to bring down what will harm you, such as the loss of wealth and the destruction of families. The majority read Dharan with a fatha on the Ḍad and it is the source of the verb ḍarātuhu to harm. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a ḍammah and it is the noun of what harms. It was said that they are two dialects. Or He intended for you some benefit meaning victory and booty. This is a response to them when they thought that staying behind the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would ward off harm from him and bring them benefit. Then God, the Most High, turned away from that and said: Rather, God is All-Aware of what you do. Meaning, your staying behind was not because of what you claimed, rather God was All-Aware of all the deeds that you did, including your staying behind. He knew that your staying behind was not because of that, but rather because of doubt, hypocrisy and the corrupt suspicions that occurred to you arising from a lack of trust in God.
48:12: 12- Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families. This sentence explains His statement: Rather, God is All-Aware of what you do, because of the ambiguity in it: that is, rather, you thought that the enemy would eradicate the believers completely, so that not one of them would return to his family. Therefore, for that reason you stayed behind, not because of the false excuses you mentioned. And that was made attractive in your hearts, that is, Satan made that assumption attractive in your hearts, so you accepted it. The majority read ًََوزas an explanation of the object, and it was read as an explanation of the subject.وجَنَجاْهْم َجُإَْه اََسفمَهْمand you thought an evil thought that God, the Almighty, would not support His Messenger. This thought is either the first thought, and the repetition is for emphasis and rebuke, or what is meant by it is something more general than the first, so the first thought is included under it as a primary entry.وجَنَجاْهْم رجَةا and you were a people who were ruined means who were destroyed. Al-Zajjaj said: who are ruined in the sight of God. Mujahid said the same. Al-Jawhari said: a ruined man is a corrupt, ruined man in whom there is no good. Abu Ubaid said: A people who are ruined means who are ruined, and it is the plural of َََج, like ْحجائإand ُْهوجa head of hair. So-and-so has been ruined: meaning he has perished, and God has made him ruined.
48:13: 13- And whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger, then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze. This statement is renewed from God Almighty and is not included in what God Almighty commanded His Messenger to say: that is, whoever does not believe in them as these laggards did, then their recompense is what God has prepared of the punishment of the Blaze.
48:14: 14- And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth He disposes of it as He wishes. He does not need anyone behind Him. Rather, He worships them as they worship Him, so that He may reward those who do good and punish those who do evil. For this reason, He said: He forgives whom He wills to forgive him, and He punishes whom He wills to punish him. He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. “And God is Forgiving and Merciful” meaning He is abundant in forgiveness and mercy, and He singles out with His forgiveness and mercy whomever He wills of His servants.
48:15: 15- Those who stayed behind will say, ‘When you set out to take the spoils,’ those who stayed behind are the ones mentioned previously. The adverbial phrase will say is related to the phrase will say, and the meaning is: They will say when you set out, O Muslims, to take the spoils, meaning the spoils of Khaybar, to take them, to possess them, Leave us to follow you, meaning let us follow you and witness the Battle of Khaybar with you. The origin of the story is that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims who were with him returned from Hudaybiyyah, God promised them the conquest of Khaybar, and He allocated its spoils to those who had witnessed Hudaybiyyah. So when they set out to it, those who stayed behind said: Leave us to follow you. God, the Exalted, said: They want to alter the Word of God, meaning to change the Word of God. What is meant by this word that they wanted to change is the promises God had made to the people of Hudaybiyyah, specifically regarding the spoils of Khaybar. Muqatil said: It means God’s command to His Messenger that none of them should go with him. Ibn Zayd said: It is the saying of God the Almighty: “And they asked your permission to go out. Say, ‘You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy.’” Ibn Jarir and others objected to this by saying that the Battle of Tabuk took place after the conquest of Khaybar and after the conquest of Mecca, but the former is more appropriate. This is what Mujahid and Qatadah said, and Ibn Jarir and others preferred it. The majority read it as the speech of God, while Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it as the word of God. Al-Jawhari said: Speech is a generic noun that can be used for both little and much, and a word cannot be less than three words because it is the plural of a word like nabqah and nabq. Then God, the Almighty, commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to prevent them from going out with him, saying: Say, ‘You will not follow us.’ This negation is in the sense of a prohibition, and the meaning is: Do not follow us. Likewise, God said before, that is, before our return from Hudaybiyyah, that the spoils of Khaybar were exclusively for those who witnessed Hudaybiyyah, and no one else would have a share in it. Then they will say, meaning the hypocrites, upon hearing this statement, which is His saying, You will not follow us, “Rather, you envy us,” meaning, what prevents you from going out with us is envy lest we share in the spoils with you. This is not the word of God as you claim. Then God, the Almighty, responded to them by saying, Rather, they did not understand except a little, meaning, they did not know except a little knowledge, which is their knowledge of worldly matters. It was said that they did not understand except a little of religious matters, which is what they did outwardly outwardly but not inwardly. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and honor him, meaning revere him, and and respect him, meaning glorify him, referring to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, and honor him, that he said: Strike in front of him with the sword. Ibn Adi, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Khatib and Ibn Asakir narrated in his history on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: “When this verse, ‘and honor him,’ was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said to his companions: What is that? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: To support him.” Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit who said: “We took a pledge from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to hear and obey in times of activity and laziness, to spend in times of difficulty and ease, to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, to speak about God and not be deterred by the blame of any blamer, and to support him when he comes to us in Yathrib, and to protect him from what we protect ourselves, our wives and our children, and Paradise will be ours. Whoever fulfills his pledge, God will fulfill his pledge for him, and whoever breaks his pledge only breaks it to the detriment of himself.” In the two Sahihs, it is narrated on the authority of Jabir that they were fifteen hundred in the Pledge of Ridwan. In the two Sahihs, it is narrated on his authority that they were fourteen hundred. In al-Bukhari, it is narrated on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab that he asked him, How many were there in the Pledge of Ridwan? He said, Fifteen hundred. Sa’id said to him, Jabir said they were fourteen hundred. He may God have mercy on him said, And he Jaabir told me that they were fifteen hundred.
48:16: His statement: 16- Say to those who stayed behind from the bedouins they are those mentioned previously You will be called to fight a people of great strength Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, Mujahid, Ibn Abi Laila and Ata’ al-Khurasani said: They are the Persians. Ka’b and al-Hasan said: They are the Romans. It was also narrated from al-Hasan that he said: They are the Persians and the Romans. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: They are Hawazin and Thaqif. Ikrimah said: Hawazin. Qatada said: Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn. Al-Zuhri and Muqatil said: They are Banu Hanifa, the people of Yamamah, the companions of Musaylimah. Al-Wahidi reported this statement from most of the commentators: You fight them or they submit meaning it will be one of two things: either fighting, or submitting to Islam, there is no third option, and this is the ruling on the disbelievers from whom the jizyah is not taken. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, or they submit, and in Abu’s reading, or they submit, meaning until they submit. If you obey, God will give you a good reward, which is the spoils of war in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. But if you turn away, meaning you expose yourself, as you turned away before, and that was in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. He will punish you with a painful punishment, by killing, captivity, and oppression in this world and by the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter, to double your crime.
48:17: 17- There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the ill meaning there is no blame upon those who are excused for not participating in the conquest due to their inability. Muqatil said: God excused the people of the time who stayed behind from the march to Hudaybiyyah with this verse, and blame means sin. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger in what they commanded and prohibited, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow The majority of scholars read he will admit him with a tā’, and Abu Hatim and Abu Ubayd preferred this reading. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a noon. And whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment meaning whoever turns away from obedience - God will punish him with a very painful punishment.
48:18: Then the Almighty mentioned those who were sincere in their intentions and witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan, saying: 18- God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree meaning God was pleased with them at the time of that pledge, which was the Pledge of Ridwan, which took place at Hudaybiyyah. The verb under is either they pledged allegiance to you or is omitted as a condition of the object. This tree mentioned is a tree that was at Hudaybiyyah, and it was said to be a lote tree. The pledge was to fight the Quraysh and not flee. It was narrated that he pledged allegiance to them to die. The number of those who took part in this pledge was mentioned earlier, and the story is explained in detail in the books of Hadith and biography. Then He knew what was in their hearts is in apposition to they pledged allegiance to you. Al-Farra' said: meaning He knew what was in their hearts of sincerity and loyalty. Qatada and Ibn Jurayj said: from being pleased with the matter of the pledge of allegiance on the condition that they not flee. Muqatil said: “From the dislike of pledging allegiance to death, ‘So He sent down tranquility upon them’ is in apposition to ‘pleased’. Tranquility means reassurance and peace of mind as mentioned above. It was also said to mean patience. ‘And He rewarded them with an imminent conquest’, which is the conquest of Khaybar upon their return from Hudaybiyyah. This was said by Qatada, Ibn Abi Layla, and others. It was also said to mean the conquest of Mecca, but the former is more appropriate.”
48:19: 19- And they will take many spoils meaning, He will reward you with many spoils, or He will give you, which are the spoils of Khaybar, and the shift is to honor them by addressing them And God is Exalted in Might and Wise meaning, He often uses the style of wisdom in His actions and words.
48:20: 20- God has promised you many spoils that you will take. This is a promise from Him, glory be to Him, to His believing servants regarding the spoils that He will open for them until the Day of Resurrection, and that they will take them at the times He has decreed for them. So He hastened this for you, meaning the spoils of Khaybar, as Mujahid and others said. It was also said that it was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. And He restrained the hands of the people from you, meaning that He restrained the hands of the Quraysh from you on the day of Hudaybiyyah through the treaty. It was also said that it was restraining the hands of the people of Khaybar and their supporters from fighting you, and He cast terror into their hearts. Qatada said: The Jews were restrained from Madinah after the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left for Hudaybiyyah and Khaybar. Ibn Jarir preferred this view, saying: Because restraining the people’s hands at Hudaybiyyah is mentioned in His statement: And it is He who restrained their hands from you. It was also said that restraining the people’s hands from you means ‘Uyaynah between the fortress of al-Fazari and ‘Awf ibn Malik al-Nadri and those who were with them, when they came to aid the people of Khaybar when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) besieged them. And that it may be a sign to the believers. The lam may be related to an omitted verb that is understood after it: that is, he did what he did of hastening and restraining so that it would be a sign, or it may be based on an omitted reason, the meaning of which is that he promised, so he hastened and restrained so that you may benefit from that and so that it would be a sign. It was also said that the waw is an additional particle and the lam is to explain what came before it: that is, and restrained so that it would be, and the meaning is: That restraint is a sign by which the truthfulness of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in fulfilling what he promised you will be known. And guide you to a straight path. That is, by that sign He increases your guidance, or He establishes you on guidance to the true path.
48:21: 21- And others which you were not able to obtain is in apposition to these: meaning, He hastened for you these spoils, and other spoils which you were not able to obtain, and they are the conquests which God granted to the Muslims after them, such as Persia, Rome and the like. This is what Al-Hasan, Muqatil and Ibn Abi Layla said. Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and Ibn Abi Ishaq said: It is Khaybar which God promised to His Prophet before he conquered it, and they were not hoping for it. Qatada said: The conquest of Mecca. Ikrimah said: Hunayn, and the first is more appropriate. God has encompassed it is a second description of the other. Al-Farra’ said: God has surrounded it for you so that you may conquer it and take it. The meaning is that He has prepared it for them and made it like something that has been surrounded from all sides, so it is confined and nothing of it is lost. Even if they are not able to control it at the moment, it is reserved for them and will not be lost to them. It was said that the meaning of surrounded is that He knew that it would be for them. And God is over all things competent. Nothing is beyond His power, and His power is not limited to some things that are possible and not others.
48:22: 22- And if those who disbelieve should fight you, they would turn their backs. Qatada said that it means the disbelievers of Quraysh at Al-Hudaibiyah, and it was said that it means Asad and Ghatafan who wanted to support the people of Khaybar, but the first is more appropriate. Then they will not find a protector who would support them in fighting you nor a helper who would support them against you.
48:23: 23- The way of God that has passed before meaning His method and custom that has been in effect among nations of granting victory to His friends over His enemies. The word sunnah is in the accusative case as a source of a deleted verb: meaning God explained the way of God, or it is a source that confirms the content of the previous sentence And you will not find any change in the way of God meaning you will not find any change in it, rather it is continuous and constant.
48:24: 24- And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them. That is, He restrained the hands of the polytheists from the Muslims and the hands of the Muslims from the polytheists when they came to confirm the truth about the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and those with him from the House in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and this is what is meant by the valley of Mecca. It was said that eighty men from the people of Mecca descended upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from Mount At-Tan'im, armed, intending to surprise the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so the Muslims captured them and then left them. In another narration there is a difference of opinion, which will be explained at the end of this research, God willing. And God is Seeing of what you do. Nothing of it is hidden from Him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Of great strength, he said: Persians. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that they are the Kurds. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Persians and the Romans. Al-Faryabi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, who said: Hawazin and Banu Hanifa. Al-Tabarani narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: I was writing for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was holding the pen to my ear when he ordered the fighting, when a blind man came and said: How can I, when I have lost my sight? Then the verse was revealed: There is no blame upon the blind al-Ma'arij. He said this regarding jihad, and jihad is not required of them if they are unable to do so. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Salamah ibn al-Akwa’ who said: “While we were saying something, a crier called out to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): ‘O people, pledge allegiance! The Holy Spirit has descended.’ So we rushed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) while he was under a samura tree and pledged allegiance to him. This is what God, the Most High, said: ‘God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree.’ So he pledged allegiance to Uthman with one hand over the other. The people said: ‘Congratulations to Ibn Affan, he is circumambulating the House while we are here.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘If he had stayed for so many years, he would not have circumambulated until I did.’” Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in al-Musannaf on the authority of Nafi’ who said: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab heard that people were coming to the tree under which the pledge of allegiance was taken, so he ordered that it be cut down.’ Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Salamah ibn al-Akwa’ who said: ‘I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) under the tree.’ It was said: ‘For what were you pledging allegiance to him that day?’ He said: ‘For death.’” Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: We pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee, but we did not pledge allegiance to him to die. Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No one who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire. Muslim narrated a similar hadith from him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then He sent down tranquility upon them, meaning tranquility was only sent down to those from whom He knew they would fulfill their vows. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, Then He hastened this for you, meaning the conquest. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority, Then He hastened this for you, meaning Khaybar, And restrained the hands of the people from you, meaning the people of Mecca, lest they violate the sanctity of God and violate your sanctity while you were in a sanctuary, and that it may be a sign to the believers, meaning a way for those who come after you. And Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il also narrated from him regarding his statement: And others which you have not been able to conquer, he said: These are the conquests that have been conquered until today. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him: And others which you have not been able to conquer, he said: It is Khaybar. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated from Anas that he said: On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, eighty men from the people of Makkah, armed with weapons, descended upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions from the direction of the mountains of al-Tan’im, intending to surprise the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He invoked a curse upon them and they were seized, but he pardoned them. Then this verse was revealed: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah after He had given you victory over them. And in Sahih Muslim and others it is stated that it was revealed regarding a group that Salamah ibn al-Akwa’ had taken prisoner on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah. Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu al-Na'im in al-Dala'il narrated regarding the reason for the revelation of this verse: “Thirty young men from the polytheists came out against the Muslims on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, armed, and they rebelled against them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) invoked curses against them, and God took away their hearing, while al-Hakim took away their sight. The Muslims rose up against them and seized them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: ‘Have you come under the covenant of anyone, or has anyone given you security?’ They said: ‘No.’ So he let them go, and this verse was revealed.”
48:25: His saying: 25- They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, and the meaning of preventing them from the Sacred Mosque is that they prevented them from circumambulating it and from completing their Umrah. And the sacrificial animals are besieged. The majority of scholars read the sacrificial animals with the accusative case in apposition to the accusative pronoun in they prevented you. Abu Amr, in a narration from him, read it with the genitive case in apposition to the mosque, and it is necessary to estimate an added word: that is, from slaughtering the sacrificial animals. It was read with the nominative case, assuming the sacrificial animals were besieged. The majority of scholars read with the fatha on the ha’ of the sacrificial animals and the sukoon on the dal. It was narrated from Abu Amr Asim with the kasra on the dal and the shaddah on the ya’: and the accusative case of besieged as a state of the sacrificial animals: that is, imprisoned. Al-Jawhari said, He confined him means he detained him and stopped him, and from this comes and the sacrificial animals are besieged. From this comes seclusion in the mosque, which means confinement. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: “It is a connected and collected particle, and his saying: ‘that it reaches its place’ means that it does not reach its place, or it is an action for its sake, and the meaning is: they turned away the sacrificial animal, hating that it would reach its place, or it is a substitute for the sacrificial animal, a substitute for inclusion, and its place is its slaughtering place, and it is where it is permissible to slaughter it in the sanctuary, and the sacrificial animal was seventy camels, and God Almighty permitted them to make that place which they reached, which is al-Hudaybiyah, a place for slaughtering.” Scholars have a well-known statement on this in the books of branches of knowledge. And had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, meaning the weak believers in Mecca. The meaning of you did not know them is that you did not recognize them. It was also said that you did not know that they were believers. That you trample them could be a substitute for men and women, but it is predominantly males. It could also be a substitute for the object of you learned them, and the meaning is that you trample them by killing and striking them. It is said that you trampled the people, meaning you struck them. This is because if they had conquered Mecca and taken it by force with the sword, the believers who were in it would not be distinguished from the disbelievers. At that point, they would not be safe from killing the believers, so expiation would be required of them and a disgrace would befall them. This is the meaning of His statement, Then a disgrace would befall you from them, meaning from their side, “that is, hardship due to what is required of them in killing them of expiation and blemish. The root of “disgrace” is blemish, taken from arr, which is scabies. This is because the polytheists would say: The Muslims have killed the people of their religion. Al-Zajjaj said: Had it not been that you kill believing men and believing women and a disgrace befalls you because of them: meaning, a sin. Al-Jawhari said the same, and Ibn Zayd said the same. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and others said: Disgrace is the expiation for accidental killing, as in His statement: But if he is from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave (10:11). Ibn Ishaq said: Disgrace is the payment of blood money. Qatrub said: Disgrace is severity, and it was said that it means grief. Without knowledge is connected to that you trample them: meaning, without knowing. The answer to had it not is omitted, and the meaning is: God would have given you permission, or He would not have restrained your hands from them. The lam in that God may admit into His mercy whom He wills is connected to what is indicated by the implied answer, meaning, but He did not give you permission, or He restrained your hands so that God may admit into His mercy whom He wills of His servants, and they are the believing men and women who were in Mecca. So He completes their reward by bringing them out from among the disbelievers and frees their captivity, and removes the torment that had been descending upon them. It was said that the lam is related to an omitted word other than what was mentioned, and its interpretation is: If you had said them, God would have admitted them into His mercy, and the first is more appropriate. It was said that whoever He wills of His servants who desire Islam from the polytheists If they were to separate, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment. At-tazeel means distinction: that is, if those who believed were to separate from those who disbelieved among them, We would have punished those who disbelieved. It was also said that at-tazeel means separation: that is, if these were to separate from those. It was also said that if the believers were to disappear from among them, and the meanings are close, and the painful punishment is killing, capture, and subjugation.
48:26: The adverbial phrase in His statement: 26- When those who disbelieved made is in the accusative case with an implied verb: that is, remember the time when those who disbelieved made in their hearts the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance. It was also said that it is related to We punished, and fanaticism means arrogance. It is said that someone is fanatic, meaning he has arrogance and anger: that is, they made it firmly established in their hearts. Making means throwing, and the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance is a substitute for fanaticism. Muqatil ibn Sulayman and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said, the people of Mecca said: They have killed our sons and brothers and are now entering our homes, so the Arabs say that they have entered upon us against our will, but they would not let Al-Lat and Al-Uzza enter upon us. So this fanaticism is the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance that has entered their hearts. Al-Zuhri said, their fanaticism is their aversion to acknowledging the Prophet's message, may God bless him and grant him peace. The majority read it as law taza'ilu while Ibn Abi Ubla, Abu Haywah and Ibn 'Awn read it as law taza'ilu and taza'il is the difference. Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers meaning He sent down tranquility and dignity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, as He did not let them enter into what the unbelievers entered into of fanaticism. It was also said that He made them steadfast in contentment and submission. And He bound them to the word of piety which is There is no god but God as was said by the majority. Some of them added Muhammad is the Messenger of God and some of them added He is alone, with no partner. Az-Zuhri said in the treaty of peace that took place between them and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as is proven in the books of Hadeeth and Seerah, God singled out the believers with this word and bound them to it. The former is more appropriate because the word of monotheism is that by which one protects against associating partners with God. It was also said that the word of piety is keeping one's covenant and adhering to it. And they were more deserving of it and worthy of it meaning that the believers were more deserving of this word than the unbelievers and were less deserving of it because God, the Exalted, made them worthy of His religion and the company of His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him).
48:27: 27- God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: God, the Exalted, saw His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina before he went out to Al-Hudaybiyyah, as if he and his companions had shaved and cut their hair. He informed his companions of that, so they rejoiced and thought that they would enter Mecca that year. But when they returned from Al-Hudaybiyyah and had not entered Mecca, the hypocrites said: By God, we have neither shaved nor cut our hair nor entered the Sacred Mosque. So God revealed this verse. It was said that the vision was at Al-Hudaybiyyah, and His saying in truth is an attribute of a deleted source: that is, a truth mixed with the truth. The answer to the deleted oath indicated by the preamble is His saying: You will enter the Sacred Mosque, that is, in the following year. His saying: If God wills is a condition for the number based on the will to teach the servants what they should say, as in His saying: And never say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow,’ except [if God wills]. Tha’lab said: God made an exception in what He knows to exempt creation from what they do not know. It was also said that God Almighty knew that some of those who were with Him at Hudaybiyyah would die, so the exception was made for this meaning, as stated by Al-Hasan ibn Al-Fadl. It was also said that the meaning of God willing is as God wills. Abu Ubaidah said: “Inna means ‘when’ meaning if God wills, when I see His Messenger that. The accusative of ‘safe’ is in the state of the agent of ‘you will certainly enter’. Likewise, ‘shaving your heads and cutting your hair’ means safe from the enemy. Shaving some of you and cutting your hair. Shaving and cutting your hair are specific to men, and shaving is better than cutting your hair, as indicated by the authentic hadith in which the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked forgiveness for those who shaved their heads the first and second times. The speaker says to him and to those who cut their hair, so he said the third time and to those who cut their hair. His saying, ‘do not fear’ is in the accusative case as a state or a new sentence, and it further emphasizes what has been understood from his saying ‘safe’. ‘Then He knew what you did not know’ meaning what you did not know of the benefit of the treaty because of the harm that would be in your entering in the year of Hudaybiyyah for the weak believers. It is conjoined with ‘truth’ meaning His Messenger’s vision was true, so He knew what you did not know. ‘Then He ordained for you a near victory’ meaning He ordained for you a near victory before entering Mecca, as I see His Messenger. Most of the commentators said: It is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Zayd and Al-Dahhak said: The conquest of Khaybar. Al-Zuhri said: There was no conquest in Islam greater than the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. And in those two years, as many as had entered Islam before that, or even more. The Muslims in the sixth year, which was the year of Hudaybiyyah, were 1,400, and in the eighth year, they were 18,000.
48:28: 28- It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance meaning a sending mixed with guidance and the religion of truth which is Islam to make it prevail over all religions meaning to make it superior to all religions as is indicated by the emphasis on the genus. It was also said to make His Messenger prevail, but the former is more appropriate. And that happened, praise be to God, for the religion of Islam prevailed over all religions and all people of religions were subdued by it. And sufficient is God as Witness the ba is redundant as mentioned previously in more than one place: meaning sufficient is God as a witness to this manifestation that He promised the Muslims and to the truth of the prophethood of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
48:29: 29- Muhammad is the Messenger of God Muhammad is the subject and the Messenger of God is its predicate, or it is the predicate of a deleted subject and the Messenger of God is its substitute. It was also said that Muhammad is the subject and the Messenger of God is its attribute. And those with him is conjoined to the subject and what follows is the predicate. The former is more appropriate, and the sentence is constructed for what is part of the group of what is testified to. Those with him were said to be the companions of Hudaybiyyah. The latter is more appropriate, in general. Severe against the disbelievers means harsh with them as a lion is harsh with its prey, which is a severe plural. Compassionate among themselves means loving and compassionate, which is a merciful plural. The meaning is that they show severity and firmness to those who oppose their religion, and mercy and compassion to those who agree with it. The majority read severe and compassionate in the nominative case as predicate of the relative pronoun, or predicate of Muhammad and what is conjoined to it as mentioned above. Al-Hasan read them in the accusative case as a state or as praise. According to this reading, the predicate is You will see them bowing and prostrating, meaning you will see them while bowing and prostrating. According to the majority reading, it is another predicate or a resumption: I mean His statement, You will see them, “seek bounty from God and His pleasure,” meaning they seek God’s reward and pleasure for them. This sentence is a third predicate according to the majority reading or in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun you will see them. Likewise, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. The mark is the sign, and there are two dialects for it: lengthening and shortening: meaning their mark appears on their foreheads from the traces of prostration in prayer and much worship during the day and night. Ad-Dahhak said: If a man stays up late, he becomes yellow, so he made this the mark. Az-Zuhri said: The places of prostration will be the whitest of their faces on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: It refers to humility and modesty. According to the first reading, I mean that it is what appears on the foreheads from much prostration, as Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Malik said. Ibn Jarir said: It refers to dignity. Al-Hasan said: If you see them sick, but they are not sick. It was said that it is the radiance in the face and the appearance of lights on it. Sufyan al-Thawri said the same. The reference in his saying: That is to what preceded from these sublime attributes. It is the subject and its predicate is his saying: Their likeness in the Torah, meaning their description with which they were described in the Torah and their description with which they were described in the Gospel. The repetition of the mention of the example is to increase its confirmation and to draw attention to its strangeness and that it is similar to examples in strangeness. Like a seed that sends forth its shoot, etc. His statement is renewed: meaning they are like a seed, etc. It was said that it is an explanation of that as an ambiguous indication that did not mean what preceded from the descriptions. It was said that it is the predicate of his saying: And their likeness in the Gospel, meaning their likeness in the Gospel is like a seed. Al-Farra’ said: There are two aspects to it: If you wish, you can say that their likeness is in the Torah and their likeness in the Gospel: meaning, their likeness in the Qur’an, so the pause would be at the Gospel. If you wish, you can say that their likeness is in the Torah, then you begin and their likeness in the Gospel is like a seed. The majority read shta'ahu with a sukoon on the ta', while Ibn Kathir and Ibn Dhakwan read it with a fatha. Anas Nasr ibn Asim and Yahya ibn Wathab read it shattah like his stick. Al-Jahdi and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it shattah without a hamza, and all of them are dialects. Al-Akhfash and Al-Kisa'i said: shata'ahu means its edge. Al-Farra' said: The crop shata'a is thick and smooth if it comes out. Al-Zajjaj said: Akhraj shata'ahu: meaning its plants. Qatrib said: The shata' is the length of the ear of corn. It was also narrated from Al-Farra' that he said: It is the ear of corn. Al-Jawhari said: The crop and the plant have become thick and even, and the plural is ashta'a. He has made the crop shata'a thick and he strengthened it, aided it, and supported it. It was said that the meaning is that the shata'a made the crop strong, and it was said that the crop has a strong root. What indicates that the shata' is the emergence of the plant. The poet said: He brought forth the shore on the face of the earth and the branches of fruit from the trees. The majority read fa’azzura with a long vowel. Ibn Dhakwan, Abu Haywah, and Hamid ibn Qays read it with a short vowel. The majority read it with the saying of Imru’ al-Qays: In a curve, the struggle has supported its plants by bringing armies of victors and losers. Al-Farra’ said: Azarat Fulan Azran means you strengthened him. Fa-ta-ghalth means that the crop became thick after it was thin. Fa-stawa ‘ala-sawquhu means it stood straight on its stalks. Sawq is the plural of saq. Qunbul read sawquhu with a silent hamza. Yajib al-Zar’ means that this crop impresses its planter with its strength and beautiful appearance. This is a metaphor that God the Almighty made for the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that they would be few at first, then increase and multiply and become strong like a crop, which would be weak at first then become stronger, one condition after another, until its stem becomes thick. Qatada said: The metaphor of the companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the Gospel is that there will emerge from a people who will grow like crops, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. Then the Almighty mentioned the reason for His increasing the number of companions of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and strengthening them, saying: To enrage the disbelievers through them. That is, He increased their number and strengthened them so that they would be an enrage to the disbelievers. The lam is related to something omitted: that is, He did that to enrage. God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward. That is, the Almighty promised those who are with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He will forgive their sins and grant them a great reward by admitting them into Paradise, which is the greatest blessing and most important favor. Ahmad and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala'il on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: On the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, they slaughtered seventy camels. When they were prevented from reaching the House, they moaned as one moans for their young. Al-Hasan bin Sufyan, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Qani', Al-Baroudi, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of narration on the authority of Abu Jumah Hunayth bin Sab' who said: "I met the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) at the beginning of the day as an unbeliever, and at the end of the day I met him as a Muslim. It was about us that the verse 'And had it not been for believing men and believing women' was revealed. We were nine people, seven men and two women." In a narration by Ibn Abi Hatim: We were three men and nine women. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, he said when they turned back the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had you not trampled them down, by your killing of them, had you removed, he said, had you removed the disbelievers from the believers, God would have punished them with a painful punishment because of your killing of them. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Hunayf that he said: On the day of Siffin, accuse yourselves. You saw us on the day of Hudaybiyyah,” meaning the peace treaty that was between the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the polytheists. If we had seen fighting, we would have fought. Then Umar came to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: O Messenger of God, are we not upon the truth and they upon falsehood?
