Aren’t our dead in Paradise and their dead in Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Then why should we give up our religion and go back before God has yet to judge between us and them? He said: O Ibn Al-Khattab, I am the Messenger of God, and God has never let me down. He returned furious, and could not be patient until he came to Abu Bakr and said: O Abu Bakr, are we not on the truth and they on falsehood? He said: Yes. He said: Aren't our dead in Paradise and their dead in Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Then why should we give up our religion? He said: O Ibn Al-Khattab, he is the Messenger of God, and God has never let him down. So Surah Al-Fath was revealed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for Umar and recited it to him. He said: O Messenger of God, is it a conquest? He said: Yes. At-Tirmidhi, Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id Al-Musnad, Ibn Jarir, Ad-Daraqutni in Al-Ifrad, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, And make them adhere to the word of piety, he said: There is no god but God. In its chain of transmission is Al-Hasan ibn Qaz'ah. At-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: A strange hadith, we do not know it except from his hadith. Abu Zur'ah said the same. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith from Salamah ibn Al-Akwa'. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Daraqutni in al-Afrad narrated something similar on the authority of al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan. Something similar was also narrated on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger. He said: It refers to Muhammad entering the House while the believers were with their heads shaved or shortened. There are a number of hadiths in the supplication for those with their heads shaved or shortened in the two Sahihs and elsewhere, including what we have mentioned above. It is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibn Umar, and in both of them from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah as well. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Their mark is on their faces, he said: It is not what they see, but it is the mark of Islam, its mark and humility. Muhammad ibn Nasr narrated in the Book of Prayer, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, he said: It refers to a good mark. At-Tabarani narrated in al-Awsat and al-Saghir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said regarding the verse, Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration, that he said: The light on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari narrated in his history and Ibn Nasr on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: A whiteness that will cover their faces on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, That is their description in the Torah, meaning their description was written in the Torah and the Gospel before God created the heavens and the earth. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Anas, Like a seed that sends forth its shoot, that is, its plants are its young.
49:1: It is eighteen verses, and it is Medinan Al-Qurtubi said: By consensus. Ibn Al-Durais, Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Al-Zubayr that it was revealed in Medina. His saying: 1- O you who have believed, do not precede God and His Messenger. The majority of scholars read Taqaddamu with a damma on the second letter and a shaddah on the dal with a kasra. There are two interpretations: First, it is transitive and its object was omitted to indicate generalization, or the object was left out to indicate the action itself, as in their saying He gives and He prevents. The second is that it is intransitive, such as face and treat. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Abbas, Al-Dahhak, and Ya’qub, with a fatha on the ta’, qaf, and dal. Al-Wahidi said: Qad here means precede, and it is intransitive. Abu Ubaidah said: The Arabs say La taqaddum bayna yada al-imam and bayna yada al-father, meaning do not rush into a command or prohibition without them, because the meaning is: Do not precede their command or prohibition. Before the imam refers to the imam, not what is before a person. The meaning of the verse is: Do not decide on a matter without God and His Messenger, and do not rush into it. It was said that what is meant is in the presence of someone, because whatever a person attends is in his presence. And fear God in all your affairs, and this includes abandoning it in order to advance before God and His Messenger as a primary entry. Then He explained the piety He commanded by saying: Indeed, God is Hearing of everything that is heard, Knowing of everything that is known.
49:2: 2- "O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet." It is possible that what is meant is actually raising the voice, because that indicates a lack of modesty and disrespect, because lowering the voice and not raising it are requirements of glorification and reverence. It is also possible that what is meant is to prevent excessive talking and excessive chatter, but the former is better. The meaning is do not raise your voices to a level that is higher than the voice of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The commentators said: What is meant by the verse is to glorify and revere the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and not to address him as some address one another. "And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another." That is, do not speak loudly when you speak to him as you are accustomed to speaking loudly when speaking to one another. Al-Zajjaj said: God commanded them to revere His Prophet, to lower their voices, and to address him with tranquility and dignity. It was said that what is meant by His statement, And do not speak loudly to him, is not to say, O Muhammad or O Ahmad, but rather, O Prophet of God or O Messenger of God, out of respect for him. The kaf is in the accusative case as an adjective for a deleted verbal noun, meaning, loudly, like the loudness of some of you to others. Raising the voice and speaking loudly is not meant to be taken in a contemptuous manner, for that is disbelief. Rather, what is meant is that the voice in itself should be inappropriate for situations in which one is respected and honored. The point is that the prohibition here concerns a number of things: First, advancing in front of him with speech that is not permitted. Second, raising one’s voice to a level that is above his own, whether in addressing him or someone else. Third, avoiding harshness in addressing him and adhering to good manners in his vicinity, because speaking loudly can only occur between equals who do not have an advantage over each other that warrants respect and reverence. Then, the Almighty gave a reason for what He mentioned by saying: {lest your deeds be rendered worthless}. Al-Zajjaj said: lest your deeds be rendered worthless means that your deeds be rendered worthless. The understood lam is not the matter that becomes it. This is what he said. This reason could be for the prohibition: that is, God forbade you from speaking out loud for fear that it might be rendered worthless, or for disliking that it might be rendered worthless. Or it could be a reason for the prohibition: that is, do not speak out loud for it leads to it being rendered worthless. Al-Zajjaj’s words refer to the second aspect, not the first. The phrase while you perceive not is in the accusative case as a state, and it contains a severe warning and a great threat. Al-Zajjaj said: And while you perceive not does not mean that a person disbelieves without knowing. Just as a disbeliever does not become a believer unless he chooses belief over refraining, so too a disbeliever does not become a disbeliever without knowing.
49:3: Then the Almighty encouraged us to comply with what He commanded, saying: 3- Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God The root of al-ghadd is to decrease anything, including decreasing the voice. Those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety. Al-Farra’ said: He purified their hearts for piety just as gold is tested by fire, so its good is extracted from its bad and its bad is dropped. Muqatil, Mujahid, and Qatadah said the same. Al-Akhfash said: He singled it out for piety, and it was also said that He purified it from all that is ugly, and it was also said that He made it spacious and spread it, from manhat al-adaim: if you made it spacious. Abu Amr said: Everything that you have striven for, you have been granted. The lam in for piety is related to something omitted: that is, suitable for piety, like when you say, You are suitable for such-and-such. Or it is for the explanation that runs in the manner of explaining the reason, like when you say, I came to you to perform the duty. That is, so that my coming would be a reason for performing the duty. For them is forgiveness and a great reward. That is, for those, it is another predicate for the demonstrative pronoun. It is permissible for it to be renewed to explain what God has prepared for them in the hereafter.
49:4: 4- Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason. They are the rude ones of Banu Tamim, as will be explained. And behind the chambers is outside and behind it: and chambers is the plural of room, just as rooms is the plural of room, and darkness is the plural of darkness, and it was said that rooms is the plural of room, and stone is the plural of room, so it is the plural of plural: and room is the patch of land enclosed by a wall around it, and it is a fa'ilah with the meaning of maf'ulah. The majority read al-Hujurat with a damma on the jim. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa' and Shaiba read it with a fatha for ease, and Ibn Abi Ubla read it with a sukoon, and these are languages, and min in min behind it for its beginning of the end, and there is no reason to prevent making it for this meaning most of them do not reason because of the prevalence of ignorance among them and the abundance of rudeness in their nature.
49:5: 5- And if only they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. That is, if they had waited for you to come out and not hastened to announce it, it would have been better for them in their religion and their worldly life, because that would include observing good manners with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and observing his noble side and doing what he deserves of respect and reverence. It was said that they came as intercessors for the captives, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) freed half of them and ransomed the other half, and if they had been patient, he would have freed all of them. Muqatil mentioned its meaning. And God is Forgiving and Merciful. He is abundant in forgiveness and mercy, and He is eloquent in them. He does not hold such people accountable for any ill-mannered behavior they commit.
49:6: 6- O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, verify it. The majority of scholars read fatabayyinu from tabayyin, while Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read fatabayyinu from tattaqit. What is meant by tabayyin is to identify and investigate, while what is meant by tattaqit is to be patient and not hasty, and to consider the reality and the report received until it becomes clear and evident. The commentators said: This verse was revealed about Al-Wayd bin Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ayt, as will be explained, God willing. His statement: lest you harm a people out of ignorance is an object: meaning, out of dislike for harming them, or lest you harm them, or lest you harm them, because mistakes are made by those who have not verified the matter or established it, and it is ignorance, because it did not come from knowledge. The meaning is: confused in ignorance of their condition, so that you may become, over what you did to them of harming them by mistake, regretful about it and concerned about it.
49:7: Then God the Almighty admonished them and said: 7- And know that among you is the Messenger of God, so do not say a false statement and do not rush when the report reaches you without clarifying, and that and what is within its scope are the two objects of know, and the phrase If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in trouble is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in you or is a new sentence, and the meaning is: If he were to obey you in much of the false report that you tell him and the opinions that are not correct that you suggest to him, you would be in trouble, which is fatigue and effort. And sin and destruction, but he does not obey you in most of what you want before his face is clear to him, and he does not hasten to do what he is told before looking into it. But God has endeared faith to you meaning He made it the most beloved thing to you, or beloved to you, so you do nothing from you except what is in accordance with it and what is required of it from the good deeds, and leaving haste in report and not verifying it. It was said that what is meant by these are those other than the first ones to demonstrate their innocence from the descriptions of the first ones, and it appears that it is a reminder to everyone of what faith requires and what is required by its love which God placed in their hearts. And He has beautified it in your hearts meaning it has made it beautiful by His guidance so that they acted according to what it requires in words and deeds. And He has made disbelief, wickedness and disobedience hateful to you meaning He has made everything that is of the type of wickedness and disobedience hateful to you. The root of wickedness is disobedience, and disobedience is the type of thing by which God is disobeyed. It was said that He meant by that lying specifically, but the first is more appropriate. Those are the rightly guided meaning those described by what the rightly guided ones mentioned. Righteousness: steadfastness on the path of truth with firmness, with guidance: which is the rock.
49:8: 8- Blessings and favors from God meaning because of His favor and blessings. The meaning is that He made you love what He loved and hate what He hated because of His favor and blessings, or He made you rightly guided because of that. It was said that the accusative is with the estimation of a verb: meaning you seek favor and blessings. And God is Knowing of everything known. Wise in everything that He decrees between His servants and decrees for them. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: “A group of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Bakr said: ‘He commanded al-Qa’qa’ ibn Ma’bad.’ ‘Umar said: ‘Rather, he commanded al-Aqra’ ibn Habis.’ Abu Bakr said: ‘You only wanted to contradict me.’ ‘Umar said: ‘I did not want to contradict you.’ They argued until their voices rose, and God revealed: ‘O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger,’ until the verse was completed.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: ‘Do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger,’ that they were forbidden to speak before His speech. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha, regarding the verse: ‘Do not fast before your Prophet fasts.’ Al-Bukhari narrated in his history on her authority that she said: ‘Some people used to fast before Ramadan, meaning one or two days, so God revealed: ‘O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger.’” At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from her that some people used to anticipate the month and fast before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so God revealed: O you who have believed the verse. Al-Bazzar, Ibn ‘Adi, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Bakr As-Siddeeq who said: This verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet. I said: O Messenger of God, by God I will not speak to you except as a confidential brother. In its chain of narration is Husayn ibn ‘Umar, who is weak, but it is supported by what ‘Abd ibn Humayd and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: When the verse Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God was revealed, Abu Bakr said: By Him Who sent down the Book to you, O Messenger of God, I will not speak to you except as a confidential brother until I meet God. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “When the verse, ‘O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet’ until His saying, ‘while you perceive not,’ was revealed, Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas had a loud voice. He said, ‘I am the one who raised my voice to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). My deeds have been in vain. I am one of the people of Hellfire.’ He sat in his house grieving. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) missed him, so some people went to him and said, ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has lost you. What is the matter with you?’ He said, ‘I am the one who raised my voice above the voice of the Prophet and spoke loudly to him. My deeds have been in vain. I am one of the people of Hellfire.’ They went to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him of that. He said, ‘No, rather he is one of the people of Paradise.’ On the day of Yamamah, he was killed.” There are hadiths with the same meaning on this topic. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet the verse: He said: It was revealed about Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah regarding his statement: Those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Among them is Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Qasim, al-Ghawi, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said: With a saheeh isnad on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of al-Aqra’ ibn Habis “that he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Muhammad, my praise is an adornment and my blame is a disgrace. He said: That is God. Then God revealed: “Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers…” Ibn Mani’ said: I do not know of any isnad that al-Aqra’ narrated other than this. At-Tirmidhi narrated with a hasan chain of narration, along with Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh, on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, regarding the verse, Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, that he said: A man came and said, O Muhammad, my praise is an adornment and my blame is a disgrace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, That is God. Ibn Rahawayh, Musaddad, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said, with a hasan chain of narration, on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, that he said: Some Arabs gathered and said, Go to this man, for if he is a prophet, we will be the happiest people because of him, and if he is a king, we will ride on his wings. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of what they had said. They came to his chamber and began to call out to him, O Muhammad, O Muhammad. Then God revealed, Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not use reason. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took hold of my ear and began to say, “God has truly fulfilled your statement, O Zayd. God has truly fulfilled your statement, O Zayd.” There are ahaadeeth on this topic. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said, with a good chain of transmission, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Dirar Al-Khuza’i, who said: “I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he invited me to Islam, so I entered it and acknowledged it. He invited me to pay zakat, so I acknowledged it. I said: ‘O Messenger of God, I will return to my people and invite them to Islam and pay zakat. Whoever responds to me, I will collect his zakat, and you, O Messenger of God, will send me a messenger for such and such a time so that what I have collected of zakat may come to you.’ When Al-Harith collected the zakat from those who responded to him and the time that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to send to them reached, the messenger was delayed and did not come. Al-Harith thought that the wrath of God and His Messenger had occurred with him, so he called the leaders of his people and said to them: ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set a time for me when he would send his messenger to whoever he was displeased with. So go and go to the Messenger of God.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Walid ibn Uqbah to Al-Harith to collect what he had of the zakat that he had collected. When he left…’ Al-Walid went on until he reached some point on the road, so he got separated and returned and came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Al-Harith refused me the zakat and wanted to kill me. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent a detachment to Al-Harith. Al-Harith came with his companions until the detachment was separated and left Madinah. Al-Harith met them and they said: This is Al-Harith? When he approached them, he said: To whom have you been sent? They said: To you. He said: Why? They said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Al-Walid ibn Uqbah to you. He claimed that you refused him the zakat and wanted to kill him. He said: No, by the One Who sent Muhammad with the truth, I have never seen him, nor did he come to me. When Al-Harith entered upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said: You refused the zakat and wanted to kill My messenger? He said: No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I did not see him, nor did he see me. I did not come back until the messenger of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delayed. I feared that it was because of the wrath of God and His Messenger. Then the verse was revealed: “O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information” to his al-Nas 114:Wise. Ibn Kathir said: This is one of the best reports about the reason for the revelation of the verse. Many reports have been reported that agree that it is the reason for the revelation of the verse, and that it is what is meant by it, even though the stories differ.
49:9: His statement: 9- And if two parties among the believers should fight The majority read they fought considering each individual from the two parties, like his statement these are two adversaries who have disputed and the pronoun in his statement between them refers to the two parties considering the wording. Ibn Abi Ubla read they fought considering the wording of two parties, and Zaid bin Ali and Ubaid bin Umair read they fought and the verb is masculine in this reading considering the two groups or parties. Al-Baghy transgression means transgression without right and refusal to make peace that is in accordance with what is right. Al-Fay' return means returning. The meaning is that if two groups of Muslims fight, it is upon the Muslims to seek peace between them and call them to the rule of God. If, after that, transgression occurs from one group against the other and they do not accept peace or enter into it, it is upon the Muslims to fight this transgressing group until it returns to the command and rule of God. If that transgressing group turns away from its transgression and responds to the call to the Book of God and His rule, then it is upon the Muslims to judge justly between the two groups, seek what is right in accordance with the rule of God, and restrain the [unjust] group until it abandons injustice and fulfills its obligations to the other. Then God the Almighty commanded the Muslims to be just in all their affairs after commanding them with this specific justice towards the two warring groups, saying: "And act justly. Indeed, God loves those who act justly." That is, act justly, for God loves the just, and His love for them necessitates rewarding them with the best reward. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Al-Suddi said, “Then make peace between them” by calling for the rule of the Book of God and being satisfied with what is in it for and against them. But if one of them transgresses and seeks what is not hers and does not return to peace, then fight against the one who transgresses until she returns to obedience to God and the peace that God has commanded.
49:10: Phrase 10- The believers are but brothers is a resumption of the command to reconcile, and the meaning is that they go back to one origin, which is faith. Al-Zajjaj said: Religion unites them, so they are brothers if they agree on their religion, so they go back by agreement in religion to the origin of lineage because they are from Adam and Eve. "So make peace between your two brothers" means every Muslim who has quarreled and fought. The mention of two specifically is to prove the obligation of reconciling with those above them a fortiori. The majority of scholars read between your two brothers in the dual form, while Zayd ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Al-Hasan, Hammad ibn Salamah and Ibn Sirin read your brothers in the plural form. It was narrated from Abu Umar, Nasr ibn Asim, Abu Al-Aliyah, Al-Jahdary and Ya'qub that they also read your sisters' houses in the superlative form in the plural form. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said in explaining the reading of the majority of scholars: He meant by the two brothers the two groups, because the dual form may be used to mean many. Abu Ubaidah said: Meet between two brothers, and fear God in all your affairs, that you may receive mercy, because of piety. Hope, in consideration of those being addressed, means hoping that you will receive mercy. This verse indicates fighting the rebellious group if it is established that they have rebelled against the Imam or any of the Muslims, and it indicates the invalidity of the statement of those who say that it is not permissible, citing as evidence the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Fighting a Muslim is disbelief. What is meant by this hadith and others similar to it is fighting a Muslim who has not committed rebellion. Ibn Jarir said: “If it were obligatory in every disagreement between two groups of Muslims to flee from it and remain at home, then no right would be established, no falsehood would be nullified, and the hypocrites and immoral people would find a reason to consider permissible everything that God has forbidden them, such as the wealth of the Muslims, the captivity of their women, and the shedding of their blood, by forming a group against them, and the Muslims would refrain from attacking them. This contradicts the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “Take control of your fools.” Ibn al-Arabi said: This verse is the basis for fighting Muslims, and a pillar in the war against those who interpret things. The Companions relied on it, and the notables of the people of the faith resorted to it. It is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meant when he said: The rebellious group will kill Ammar, and when he said, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the Khawarij: They will emerge at a time when a group of people will be killed by the one of the two groups who is more entitled to the truth.
49:11: 11- O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them. Ridicule: mockery: Abu Zaid narrated: I ridiculed him, laughed at him, and mocked him. Al-Akhfash said: I mocked him and made fun of him, I laughed at him and made fun of him, I mocked him and made fun of him, all of that is said, and the noun is mockery and mockery, and it was read with both of them in that some of them may take others in mockery, and the meaning of the verse: the prohibition of the believers from mocking each other, and the reason for this prohibition is his saying: perhaps they will be better than them meaning that the one mocked by God will be better in the sight of God than those mocking them, and since the word people is specific to men, because they are the people over women, he mentioned women alone and said: nor women from women meaning and women should not be mocked by women perhaps they the one mocked by better than them meaning better than those mocked by them, and it was said that he mentioned women alone because mockery of them is more common, and do not find fault with one another slander is a defect, and its investigation was mentioned in Surat Bara’ah when he said: and among them is he who finds fault with you concerning the charities Ibn Jarir said: slander is with the hand, the eye, the tongue, and the gesture, and the nudge It can only be done by the tongue, and the meaning of Do not insult one another is that you should not insult one another, as in His statement: And do not kill yourselves and His statement: So greet yourselves. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Sa`id ibn Jubayr said:: Do not backbite one another. Ad-Dahhak said: Do not curse one another. And do not insult one another with nicknames. Insulting is the verbal noun derived from nabaz with a sukoon, which is the verbal noun. Nabz with a sukoon is the title, the plural is anbaaz, and titles is the plural of title, which is a name other than the one by which a person is called. What is meant here is a bad nickname. Insulting is calling one another by nicknames. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: It is to say to one’s Muslim brother, You sinner, you hypocrite, or to one who has converted to Islam, You Jew, you Christian. Ata’ said: It is anything by which you expelled your brother from Islam, such as saying, You dog, you donkey, you pig. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: A man would be taunted for his disbelief, and it would be said to him, You Jew, you Christian, so this was revealed. Qatadah, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Ikrimah said the same. How evil is the name of immorality after faith, meaning how evil is the name by which people are mentioned with immorality after they have entered into faith. The name here means mention. Ibn Zayd said: How bad it is for a man to be called an infidel or an adulterer after his conversion to Islam and repentance. It was also said that the meaning is that whoever does what is forbidden of mockery, backbiting, and slander is a sinner. Al-Qurtubi said: “An exception is made for someone who is often used to such as the lame or the hunchbacked, and he has no reason to feel sorry for him, so the imams permitted it and the linguists agreed on his statement.” End quote. And whoever does not repent from what God has forbidden, then those are the wrongdoers because they have committed what God has forbidden and refused to repent, so they wronged the one they called them by, and they wronged themselves because of the sin that befell them.
49:12: 12- O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Suspicion here means simply an unfounded accusation, such as someone who accuses another of something immoral even though nothing appears to warrant that. God swt has commanded us to avoid much [negative] assumption so that the believer may examine every suspicion he has until he knows its validity, because there are types of assumptions that must be followed. Most of the Islamic rulings are based on assumption, such as analogy, a single report, and the meaning of general principles. However, this assumption, which must be acted upon, has been strengthened in one of the ways that requires acting upon it, and is thus free from doubt and suspicion. Al-Zajjaj said: It means to think the same of the good people. As for the evil and immoral people, we may think of them as they appear. Muqatil ibn Sulayman and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It means to think ill of one's Muslim brother, and there is nothing wrong with that as long as one does not utter it. But if one speaks about that assumption and expresses it, then he has sinned. Al-Qurtubi narrated from most scholars that it is impermissible to have bad thoughts about someone who appears to be good, and that there is no harm in having bad thoughts about someone who appears to be bad. The phrase Indeed, some suspicion is sin explains what preceded it regarding the command to avoid many suspicions. This kind of suspicion is thinking badly of good people, and sin is the punishment that the suspect deserves. What indicates that this suspicion that one is commanded to avoid is based on bad thoughts is the verse in which God the Almighty says: And you thought evil thoughts and you were a people who were ruined. The suspicion that one is commanded to avoid does not include any of the suspicion that one is commanded to follow in matters of religion, because God has commanded His servants to follow it, and the majority of scholars have made it obligatory to act upon it. This was only denied by some groups of innovators out of spite for the religion and their deviation from the majority of Muslims. The command to follow suspicion is mentioned in many parts of the pure Shari’ah, indeed in most of it. Then when God the Almighty commanded them to avoid a lot of suspicion, He forbade them from spying, saying: And do not spy. Spying means searching for what is concealed from you of the faults and shortcomings of Muslims. God the Almighty forbade them from searching for the faults and shortcomings of people. The majority read Tajassu with a jim, and its meaning is what we mentioned. Al-Hasan, Abu Raja’, and Ibn Sirin read it with a ha. Al-Akhfash said: They are not far from each other, because Tajassu with a jim means searching for what is concealed from you, and Istassu with a ha means seeking and searching for report. It was said that Tajassu with a jim means searching, and from it is said that a man is a spy, if he searches for matters, and Ha is what a person perceives with some of his senses. It was said that it is with the letter Ha in what a person seeks for himself, and with the letter Jeem to be a messenger to others. Tha’lab said: And do not backbite each other meaning do not speak ill of each other behind their backs. Backbiting is to mention a man in a way that he dislikes, as in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, which is proven in Sahih, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Do you know what backbiting is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It is mentioning your brother in a way that he dislikes. It was said: What if what I say is true in my brother? He said: If what you say is true, then you have backbitten him, and if it is not true, then you have slandered him. “Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?” God, the Almighty, likened backbiting to eating carrion, because the dead person does not know that his flesh is being eaten, just as the living person does not know that the one who backbites him is backbiting. Al-Zajjaj mentioned its meaning. It indicates that a person's honor is like his flesh, and that just as it is forbidden to eat his flesh, it is also forbidden to insult his honor. This is a clear indication of the aversion to backbiting, the rebuke of the one who does it, and the condemnation of him for it. Human flesh is something that human nature rejects and is abhorred by the human nature, in addition to it being forbidden by Islamic law. And you would have hated it. Al-Farra' said: Its meaning is: You would have hated it, so do not do it. The meaning is: Just as you hate this, avoid mentioning him badly in his absence. Al-Razi said: The fa is in the sense of an answer to a statement. It is as if he said: None of you likes to eat the flesh of his brother, so you would have hated it. Abu al-Baqa' said: It is conjoined with an omitted word, the meaning being: This was offered to you, and you hated it. And fear God by abandoning what He has commanded you to avoid. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful to whoever fears Him for what he has committed of sin and disobedience to His command. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Anas who said: It was said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Why don’t you go to Abdullah ibn Ubayy? So he went to him and rode a donkey, and the Muslims set off walking, and it was marshy land. When he went to him, he said: Go away from me, for by God, the smell of your donkey has bothered me. A man from the Ansar said: “By God, the smell of the Messenger of God’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) donkey is better than yours.” Some men from his people became angry on behalf of Abdullah, and each of their companions became angry, and there was fighting between them with palm branches, hands and sandals. Then the verse: And if two parties among the believers should fight was revealed about them. Something similar to this was narrated from other sources. Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi, on the authority of Ibn Umar, said: “I did not feel anything in myself as I felt in myself about this verse. I did not fight this rebellious group as God had commanded me.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, saying: “God commanded the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers, if a group of believers quarrel, to call them to the judgment of God and to be just with each other. If they respond, he should judge them according to the judgment of the Book of God until justice is served to the oppressed. Whoever among them refuses to respond is a transgressor, and it is the duty of the leader of the believers and the believers to fight them until they return to the command of God and acknowledge His judgment.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas And if two parties among the believers should fight the verse. He said: It was a fight with sandals and sticks, so He ordered them to make peace between them. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Aisha who said: I have not seen anything like what this nation has rejected in this verse: "And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil regarding His statement: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people, he said: It was revealed about a group of Banu Tamim who mocked Bilal, Sulayman, Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb, Ibn Fuhayrah, and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah. Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in Dhamm Al-Ghibah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And do not insult one another, he said: Do not slander one another. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab, the four Sunans, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Jubayrah ibn Ad-Dahhak who said: “The verse, ‘And do not insult one another by nicknames,’ was revealed about us, Banu Salamah. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came and there was not a man among us who did not have two or three names. So if he called one of them by one of those names, they would say, ‘O Messenger of God, he dislikes it.’ So the verse, ‘And do not insult one another by nicknames,’ was revealed.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “Insulting one another by nicknames is when a man commits evil deeds and then repents and returns to the truth. God forbade taunting one another for his past deeds.” Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding the verse: If a man was Jewish and then converted to Islam, he would say, ‘O Jew, O Christian, O Magian,’ and he would say to a Muslim man, ‘O sinner.’ Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab Al-Iman narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption, that he said: God has forbidden the believer from having bad thoughts about another believer. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the falsest of speech. Do not spy, do not look for faults in one another, do not compete, do not envy, do not hate one another, and be, O servants of God, brothers. A man should not propose marriage to a woman whom his brother has already proposed to until he either marries her or leaves her alone." Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, and do not spy, that he said: God has forbidden the believer from pursuing the faults of another believer. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Wahb who said: Ibn Mas'ud was visited and it was said, This is so-and-so whose beard is dyed with wine. Ibn Mas'ud said, We have been forbidden from spying, but if something is revealed to us, we will seize it. There are ahaadeeth that forbid searching for the faults of Muslims and spying on their defects. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, And do not backbite one another, that he said, God has forbidden backbiting a believer about anything, just as He has forbidden dead meat. There are many ahaadeeth that forbid backbiting and are well-known in the books of hadeeth.
49:13: His saying: 13- O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female They are Adam and Eve, and the meaning is that they are equal because they are connected by one lineage and are united by one father and one mother, and that there is no place for boasting among them in lineages. It was said that the meaning is: Each one of you is from a father and a mother, so all are equal. And We made you peoples and tribes People is the plural of people with a fatha on the sheen, and it is the great neighborhood: like Mudar and Rabi'ah, and the tribes are below them like Bani Bakr from Rabi'ah, and Bani Tamim from Mudar. Al-Wahidi said: This is the saying of a group of commentators, they called people because of their branching out and gathering like the branches of a tree, and people are from the names of opposites: it is said that he gathered it, and he separated it if he dispersed it, and from this death was called peoples because it disperses, as for the people with a kasra, it is the path in the mountain. Al-Jawhari said: A people is what branched out from the tribes of the Arabs and the Persians, and the plural is peoples. Mujahed said: Peoples are distant relatives, and tribes are less so. Qatada said: Peoples are relatives and closer. It was said that the peoples are the Arabs of Yemen from Qahtan, and the tribes are from Rabi’ah, Mudar, and the rest of Adnan. It was also said that the peoples are the clans of the Persians, and the tribes are the clans of the Arabs. Abu Ubaid narrated that the people are more numerous than the tribe, then the tribe, then the building, then the clan, then the thigh, then the faction, then the clan. What supports what the majority said, that the people are more numerous than the tribe, is the saying of the poet: Tribes of peoples who do not have a generous or noble person among them The majority of scholars readََعارفواto know one another with a soft ta', while its original form isََعارفواto know one another, so one of the two ta's was deleted. Al-Bazzi read it with a shaddah on it due to assimilation. Al-A'mash read it with two ta's and the lam is related toخجلجَجَجْهْهwe created you thus so that you may know one another. Ibn Abbas readََعارفواas the present tense ofَجَجفهto know one another. The benefit of knowing one another is that each one of them is traced back to his lineage and does not trace it back to anyone else. The point of this is that God, the Exalted, created them this way for this benefit, not to boast about their lineages and claim that this people are better than that people, this tribe is more honorable than that tribe, or this clan is more noble than that clan. Then, the Almighty gave a reason for what the words indicate of the prohibition of boasting, saying: Indeed, the most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. That is, the distinction between you is only by righteousness, so whoever is immersed in it is the one who deserves to be more honorable, more noble, and more excellent than the one who is not immersed in it. So, abandon what you are doing of boasting about lineage, because that does not necessitate nobility, nor does it establish honor, nor does it necessitate superiority. The majority of scholars read indeed, the most honorable of you with a kasra on in. Ibn Abbas read it with a fatha, meaning because the most honorable of you. Indeed, God is Knowing of everything known, including your deeds. Aware of what you conceal and what you declare. Nothing of that is hidden from Him.
49:14: And when He, the Almighty, mentioned that the most honorable of people in the sight of God is the one who is most pious to Him, and that the basis of piety is faith, He mentioned what the Arabs used to say in claiming faith to prove to them honor and virtue, so He said: 14- The desert Arabs said, ‘We believe,’ meaning Banu Asad, who showed Islam in a year of famine, wanting charity. So God, the Almighty, commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to respond to them, saying: Say, ‘You have not believed,’ meaning you have not believed with true belief from the heart, sincere intention, and reassurance, “but say, ‘We have submitted,’ meaning we have surrendered for fear of being killed and taken captive, or for the sake of greed for charity. This is a characteristic of the hypocrites, because they submitted outwardly, but their hearts did not believe. For this reason, the Almighty said, And faith has not yet entered your hearts, meaning what you showed with your tongues was not in agreement with your hearts, but rather just a saying with the tongue without true belief or sincere intention. The sentence is either a new sentence to confirm what came before it, or in the accusative case as a state, and in when Meaning of expectation. Al-Zajjaj said: Islam is to show submission and acceptance of what the Prophet came with, and by doing so, blood is spared. If that showing is accompanied by belief and affirmation in the heart, then that is faith and its companion is a believer. These people were excluded from faith by His statement: And faith has not yet entered your hearts, meaning you have not believed, but rather you have submitted to seek refuge from being killed. And if you obey God and His Messenger, true obedience emanating from sincere intentions and hearts that believe, not hypocritically. He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds. It is said la yaltu if it is reduced, and walata yalitu if it is diminished. The meaning is: He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds. The majority read yaltkom from lata yalitu like ba’a yabi’u. Abu Amr read la yaltkom with a hamza from alata ya’altu with a fatha in the past tense and a kasra in the present tense. He preferred the reading of Abu Amr and Abu Hatim because of His statement: And We did not deprive them of anything of their work. And based on this, the poet said: Convey to Bani Asad on my behalf, loudly and clearly, without hesitation or falsehood. Abu Ubaidah chose the reading of the majority, and based on it, Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj said: And a dewy night I walked, and it did not turn me away from its secret. I wish They are two eloquent languages: God is Forgiving, meaning He is the most forgiving of those who have committed a sin. Merciful, meaning He is the most merciful to them.
49:15: Then when He, the Most High, mentioned that those who said, We believe, to those who believe, but faith did not enter their hearts, are among the believers who deserve to be called believers, He said: 15- The believers are only those who have believed in God and His Messenger, meaning a true faith, purely free of the agreement of the heart and tongue, and then have not doubted, meaning, no doubt has entered their hearts, nor has any doubt mixed with them, and strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God, meaning in obeying Him and seeking His pleasure. Jihad includes the righteous deeds that God has commanded, for they are among the things that a person strives with himself until he performs it and supports it, as God, the Most High, has commanded. The reference in His saying, those, is to those who combine the aforementioned matters, and it is the subject, and its predicate is His saying, They are the truthful, meaning those who are truthful in being characterized by the quality of faith and being among its people, not those other than them who have manifested Islam with their tongues. He claimed to be a believer, but his heart was not reassured by faith, nor did he understand its meaning, nor did he act according to the deeds of its people, who are the Bedouins mentioned above and the rest of the hypocrites.
49:16: Then God, the Most High, commanded His Messenger to say to those Bedouins and their likes something else when they claimed that they were believers. He said: 16- Say, ‘Do you teach God about your religion?’ Teaching here means informing, and that is why the preposition ba was included in your religion: that is, inform Him about that when you said, We believe. “And God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth.” So how could the falsehood of what you claim of faith be hidden from Him? The sentence is in the accusative case as a state of the object of you teach. “And God is Knowing of all things.” Nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He knows what you conceal of disbelief and what you show of Islam out of fear of harm and hope of benefit.
49:17: Then God, the Exalted, informed His Messenger of what He would say to them when they bestowed upon him a favor for what they claimed of Islam, saying: 17- They consider their Islam a favor to you because they have submitted, meaning they consider their Islam a favor to you, as they said, We have come to you with our burdens and children, and we did not fight you as the Banu so-and-so and the Banu so-and-so fought you. “Say, ‘Do not consider your Islam a favor to me,’ meaning do not consider it a favor to me, for Islam is a favor for which the one who bestows it does not seek a reward for the one who bestows it upon him. For this reason, He said, Rather, God bestows a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith, meaning He has guided you to it and shown you its path, whether you reach the destination or not. The accusative of your Islam is either as a direct object, as they consider the meaning of they consider, or by removing the preposition: that is, because they submitted. And likewise His saying, that He has guided you to faith, for it is possible to interpret it in both ways, if you are truthful in what you claim, and the answer is omitted, indicated by what precedes it: that is, if you are truthful. So God has bestowed His favor upon you. The majority of scholars read that He has guided you with a fatha on an, while Asim read it with a kasra.
49:18: 18- Indeed, God knows the unseen (unseen) of the heavens and the earth meaning everything that is hidden in them. And God is Seeing of what you do. Nothing of it is hidden from Him. He will reward you for good with good and for evil with evil. The majority of scholars read you do as addressing others, while Ibn Kathir read it as addressing others. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah who said: On the day of the conquest, Bilal ascended the Kaaba and called the adhan call to prayer. Some of the people said: Is this black slave calling the adhan on the roof of the Kaaba? Some of them said: If God is displeased with this, He will change him. So the verse, O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female was revealed. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. Abu Dawud narrated in his Marasil, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan on the authority of al-Zuhri who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) ordered the Banu Bayada to marry Abu Hind, a woman from among them. They said: O Messenger of God, should we marry our daughters to our clients? So this verse was revealed. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that this verse, O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female, was revealed in Mecca, and it is specifically for the Arab clients: any tribe or region. And His statement, The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you, he said: The most righteous of you in shirk. Al-Bukhari and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Shu’ub are the great tribes, and tribes are the clans. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that: Shu’ub are the group, and tribes are the branches by which people recognize one another. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked: ‘Which people are the most honorable?’ He said: ‘The most honorable of them in the sight of God is the most righteous of them.’ They said: ‘We are not asking you about this.’ He said: ‘The most honorable of people is Joseph, the Prophet of God, the son of the Prophet of God, the son of the Prophet of God, the son of the Friend of God.’ They said: ‘We are not asking you about this.’ He said: ‘Then are you asking me about the origins of the Arabs?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Their best in the pre-Islamic period are the best in Islam, if they attain understanding.’” There are hadiths in Sahih al-Bukhari and other collections that piety is what distinguishes people. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: The desert Arabs said, ‘We believe,’ he meant the desert Arabs of Banu Asad and Khuzaymah. And regarding his statement: But say, ‘We have submitted,’ he meant the desert Arabs of Banu Asad and Banu Khuzaymah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada that it was revealed about Banu Asad. Ibn al-Mundhir al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa: Some Arabs said: O Messenger of God, we have become Muslims and the Banu so-and-so did not fight you. So God revealed: They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. An-Nasa’i, al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He mentioned that they were Banu Asad.
50:1: It is forty-five verses. It is all Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata', and Jabir. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah that it is Meccan except for one verse, which is: "And We certainly created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us." It is the beginning of Al-Mufassal according to the correct view, and it was also said that it is from Al-Hujurat. Ibn Ad-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Qaf was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar narration on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Qutbah ibn Malik that he said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite in the first rak'ah of Fajr Surah 'Qaf. By the Glorious Qur'an.'" Ahmad, Muslim, and the Sunan scholars narrated on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laythi that he said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite Qaf and 'Aqrabtutu' on Eid." Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umm Hisham bint Haritha that she said: "I did not take Qaf and the Glorious Qur'an except from the mouth of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He used to recite it every Friday on the pulpit when delivering the sermon to the people." It is also in Sahih Muslim. His statement: 1- "Qaf. By the Glorious Qur'an." The discussion of the grammatical analysis of this is like the discussion that we have previously discussed in His statement: "Sad. By the Qur'an full of remembrance" and in His statement: "Ha Meem. And the clear Book." There is disagreement over the meaning of Qaf. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: It is the name of a mountain made of emerald that surrounds the world and the sky is domed over it and it is behind the veil behind which the sun sets at a year's journey. Al-Farra' said: Based on this, the grammatical analysis of Qaf should have been made clear because it is a noun and not a spelling. He said: Perhaps the Qaf alone was mentioned in its name like the saying of the speaker: I said to it stop, and it said Qaf, meaning I am standing. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj narrated that some people said that the meaning of Qaf is: The matter has been decreed and what is to come has been decreed, as it was said about Ha Meem: Ha Meem the matter. It was also said that it is one of the names of God by which He swore. Qatadah said: It is one of the names of the Qur'an. Al-Sha'bi said: It is the opening of the surah. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said that it means: Stop at Our command and prohibition and do not transgress them. Other weaker statements were made. In fact, it is one of the ambiguous verses whose knowledge God has kept to Himself, as we have established in the opening verse of Surat Al-Baqarah. The meaning of Al-Majid is that He has glory and honor over all other revealed books. Al-Hasan said: It is the generous. It was also said: the one of high status. It was also said: the great status. The answer to the oath, according to the Kufians, is His statement: Rather, they were amazed. Al-Akhfash said: Its answer is omitted, as if he said: Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an, you will surely be resurrected. It is indicated by: Will we, when we have died and become dust? Ibn Kaysan said: Its answer is: What is uttered of a word. It was also said: We have known what the earth takes of them, with the estimation of the lam, meaning: We have known. It was also said that it is omitted and its interpretation is: We have sent it down to you so that you may warn, as if it was said: Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an, we have sent it down to you so that you may warn the people. The majority read Qaf with a sukoon. Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Nasr ibn Asim read it with a kasra over the fa. Isa Al-Thaqafi read it with a fatha over the fa. Harun and Muhammad ibn Al-Samifi read it with a damma.
50:2: 2- Rather, they were amazed that a warner had come to them from among themselves. “Rather” is used to negate the answer, according to the different opinions, and that is in the accusative case, assuming: because he came to them. The meaning is: Rather, the disbelievers were amazed that a warner had come to them from among themselves, namely Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. They were not satisfied with mere doubt and rejection, but rather they considered it one of the amazing things. It was said that it is a negation of the description of the Qur’an as being glorious, and the explanation of this was presented in Surat Sad. Then he explained what he narrated about their amazement by saying: Then the disbelievers said, ‘This is an amazing thing.’ This contains additional clarification and explanation. Qatadah said: They were amazed that they were called to one God, and it was said that they were amazed by the resurrection.
50:3: So this is an indication of something ambiguous that is explained by what follows it, such as his saying: If we die, etc., and the first is more appropriate. Al-Razi said: It appears that their statement is an indication of the coming of the warner. Then they said: Will we die? Also, there is found here after the exclusion by question something that conveys the meaning of astonishment, which is their statement: That is a distant return. For it is an exclusion and it is like astonishment. So if the astonishment in their statement: This is something amazing was referring back to their statement: Will it then? then it would be like repetition. If it is said that explicit repetition necessitates that your statement This is something amazing refers back to the coming of the warner. If their astonishment at it is known from their statement: And they were amazed that he came to them, then his statement: This is something amazing is a repetition. So we say that it is not a repetition but rather a confirmation because when he said: Rather, they were amazed in the verb form. It is permissible for a person to be amazed at something that is not amazing, like his statement: Do you wonder at the command of God? And it is said in common parlance: There is no reason for your astonishment at something that is not amazing. So it is as if when they were amazed, it was said to them: There is no point in your astonishment, so they said: This is something amazing. So how can we not be amazed at it? And this is indicated by his statement: Here, The disbelievers said with the letter fa, as it indicates that it is a consequence of what came before. The majority read When we die as a question. Ibn Amir, in a narration from him, Abu Ja`far, Al-A`mash and Al-A`raj read it with one hamza, so it could be a question like the reading of the majority, and the hamza of the question is understood, and it could also mean a statement. The agent in the adverbial phrase is understood: i.e., will He resurrect us, or will we return if we die, because what comes after it indicates it. This is according to the reading of the majority. As for the second reading, the answer to when is omitted: i.e., we returned. It was said that this is a return, and the meaning is: their denial of the resurrection after their death and their turning to dust. Then they were certain of their remoteness of the resurrection, so they said: That, i.e., the resurrection, is a distant return, i.e., far from minds, understandings, custom or possibility. It is said that I returned him, I returned him a return, and he returned, he returns a return.
50:4: Then the Almighty responded to what they said, saying: 4- We know what the earth takes from them meaning what it consumes from their bodies, so nothing of that escapes us. And He whose knowledge encompasses everything, even reaching the knowledge of what goes from the bodies of the dead in the graves, does not find resurrection difficult for Him nor does it seem remote from Him. Al-Suddi said: The decrease here is death. He says: We know who among them will die and who will remain, because whoever dies is buried, so it is as if the earth decreases the dead. And it was said that the meaning is: who among the polytheists enters Islam, and the first is more appropriate. And with Us is a Preserving Book meaning it preserves their number and their names and everything, and it is the Preserved Tablet: meaning it is preserved from the devils, or everything is preserved in it.
50:5: Then the Almighty turned away from their first statement and moved to what is more heinous than it, saying: 5- Rather, they denied the truth. This is an explicit statement from them of denial after what came before from them of enslavement, and what is meant by the truth here is the Qur’an. Al-Mawardi said in the opinion of all, and it was said it is Islam, and it was said Muhammad, and it was said the prophethood established by miracles, when it came to them, meaning the time of his coming to them without contemplation, thinking, or deep consideration. The majority read it with a fatha on the lam and a shaddah on the meem. Al-Jahdary read it with a kasra on the lam and a soft meem, they are in a confused state, meaning mixed and disturbed. They say sometimes a magician, sometimes a poet, and sometimes a soothsayer. This was said by Al-Zajjaj and others. Qatada said it is different. Al-Hasan said it is ambiguous, and the meaning is close, and it was said it is corrupt, and the meanings are close. From this is their saying: Marjab, the trusts of the people, meaning they are corrupted, and the religion is confused and the matter is mixed.
50:6: 6- Have they not looked at the sky above them? The question is for rebuke and rebuke: that is, how did they neglect to look at the sky above them? How We constructed it and made it in this manner, raised without a pillar to lean on. And adorned it with what We placed in it of lamps. And it has no rifts meaning cracks, fissures, and fissures. It is the plural of faraj, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: It closes the anus Al-Kisa’i said: There is no discrepancy, difference, or gap in it.
50:7: 7- And the earth We have spread out meaning We have expanded it and placed therein firm mountains meaning fixed mountains. The explanation of this has already been presented in Surat Ar-Ra’d. And We have caused to grow therein of every beautiful kind meaning of every beautiful kind. The explanation of this has already been presented in Surat Al-Hajj.
50:8: 8- An insight and a reminder for every penitent servant are two reasons for what came before, and they are in the accusative case with the last verb, or with an implied meaning: We did what we did to provide insight and a reminder, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. Abu Hatim said: They are in the accusative case as a source, meaning we made that an insight and a reminder. The penitent is the one who returns to God in repentance, contemplating the wonders of His creation and the wonders of His creation. In the context of this verse, there is a reminder to those who deny the resurrection and awakening them from their state of heedlessness, and a clarification of the possibility of that and its impossibility, for the One who is capable of such matters is capable of it.
50:9: And thus his statement: 9- And We sent down from the sky blessed water meaning We sent down from the clouds abundant water for people to benefit from in most of their affairs And We caused gardens to grow thereby meaning We caused many orchards to grow thereby and grain for harvest meaning what is eaten and harvested from the grains, and the meaning is: and the grain for the crop is the harvest, and the grain was specified because it is what is intended, this is what the Basrans said. The Kufians said: it is from the category of adding something to itself like the congregational mosque, Al-Farra’ narrated it: Ad-Dahhak said: The grain for the harvest is wheat and barley, and it was said that it is every grain that is harvested, stored and eaten.
50:10: 10- And tall palm trees with clusters of date palms is in apposition to gardens: that is, and We caused the date palms to grow therein. The mention of them specifically with their inclusion in the gardens is to indicate their superiority over all other trees. The accusative of tall is in the state of the adverbial phrase, and it is an implied state because at the time of growing they were not tall. Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Qatadah said: tall and lofty. Saeed bin Jubayr said: level. Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and Al-Farra' said: abundant and pregnant. It is said of a sheep that when it gives birth it gives birth. The first is more common in the Arabic language. It is said that the palm tree has grown tall: if it has become tall. From this comes the saying of the poet: We have wine, not vineyard wine, but the fruit of tall trees. Generous ones in heaven have gone long and their fruits have reached the hands of the gardens. The phrase Its date palms are arranged in rows is in the accusative case as a state of the palm tree. The date palm is the first fruit to emerge from the date palm. It is said that the date palm has emerged. The overlapping date palm is the fruit that has been arranged one on top of the other, before it opens. It is arranged in rows in its sleeves. But if it emerges from its sleeves, it is not arranged in rows.
50:11: 11- Provision for the servants is in the accusative case as a source: meaning we provided them with provision, or as a cause: meaning we caused these things to grow for provision. And We revived thereby a dead land meaning we revived with that water a barren land in which there were no fruits or crops. The phrase Likewise the emergence is a new sentence to explain that emerging from the graves at the resurrection is like this revival with which God revived the dead land. The majority read dead with a light pronunciation, while Abu Ja`far and Khalid read it with a heavy pronunciation.
50:12: Then the Almighty mentioned the nations that denied, saying 12- The people of Noah and the companions of the Messenger denied before them. They are the people of Shuaib, as previously explained. It was also said that they were the ones to whom a man came running from the farthest part of the city. They were from the people of Jesus, and it was also said that they were the companions of the trench. The messengers are either a place to which they are attributed, or an action, which is digging a well. It is said that Ras means digging a well.
50:13: 13- Noah, Aad, and Pharaoh meaning Pharaoh and his people, and the brothers of Lot he made them his brothers because they were his in-laws, and it was said that they were from the people of Abraham and were acquaintances of Lot.
50:14: 14- And the companions of the thicket The discussion of the thicket and the differences in the reciters of it has been fully discussed in Surat Ash-Shu'ara', and their prophet whom God sent to them was Shu'ayb. And the people of Tubba' is Tubba' Al-Himyari who was mentioned previously in His statement: Are they better or the people of Tubba'? His name is Sa'd Abu Karb, and it was said As'ad? Qatada said: God condemned the people of Tubba’, but He did not condemn Him. Everyone denied the messengers. The tanween replaces the complement: that is, every one of these people denied the Messenger whom God sent to them, and denied the law that he brought. The lam in the messengers can be for a covenant, and it is possible that it is for a type: that is, every group of these groups denied all of the messengers. The singular pronoun in lie is in consideration of the word everyone. In this there is consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as if it was said to him: Do not be sad and do not worry about your grief because these people denied you, for this was the case with the prophets who came before you, for their people denied them and only a few of them believed them. So My threat came into effect, that is, My threat became necessary for them, and the word of punishment came into effect upon them, and what God had decreed for them of sinking, transformation, and destruction with the types of punishment that God sent down upon them.
50:15: 15- Are We weary with the first creation? The interrogative is for rebuke and rebuke. The sentence is a resumption of the matter of resurrection that the nations denied: that is, were We unable to create when We created them first and they were nothing, so how can We be unable to resurrect them? It is said, I am weary with the matter: if I am unable to do it and do not know its meaning. The majority read it with a kasra on the first yaa followed by a silent yaa. Ibn Abi Ubla read it with a shaddah on the yaa without a full vowel. Then he mentioned that they are in doubt about the resurrection, so he said: Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation, that is, in doubt, bewilderment and confusion about a renewed creation, which is the resurrection of the dead. The meaning of the reversal is that they do not deny God's ability to create the first rather, they are in doubt about a new creation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Qaf, that he said: It is one of the names of God. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: God created beyond this earth an encompassing sea. Then He created beyond that a mountain called Qaf, the lowest heaven hovering over it. Then He created beyond that mountain an earth seven times the size of that earth. Then He created beyond that an ocean encompassing it. Then He created beyond that a mountain called Qaf, the second heaven hovering over it, until He counted seven earths, seven seas, seven mountains, and seven heavens. He said: This is His statement, And the sea, replenished thereafter by seven other seas. Ibn Kathir said: Its chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas is not sound. He also said: There is an interruption in it. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya and Abu Al-Shaykh also narrated on his authority that he said: It is a mountain and its veins reach the rock on which the earth is located. So when God wants to shake a village, He commands that mountain to move that vein next to that village, so it shakes and moves it, and from there He moves the village without the village. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: And the Glorious Qur’an, he said: The Noble Qur’an. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him that he said: There is nothing better or more excellent than the Glorious Qur’an. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him that: {We know what the earth takes of them} He said: Their bodies and what is lost from them. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him regarding the verse that he said: What it eats of their flesh, bones and hair. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him that he said: Al-Murij is something that changes. Al-Hakim narrated - who authenticated it - and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Qutba that he said: “I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recite in the morning prayer Qaf. When he came to this verse: {And the tall palm trees} I kept saying: What is their stalks? He said: Their height.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of narration from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {And the tall palm trees} He said: Height. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: {And they have clusters of dates} He said: Stacked one on top of the other. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: Have We tired of the first creation? He said: The first creation has not tired us. And regarding his statement: Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation, he said: There is doubt about the resurrection.
50:16: His saying: 16- And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him. This is a new statement, some of which includes mention of the divine power. What is meant by man is the species, and it was said that it is Adam, and the whispering is originally the hidden voice, and what is meant by it here is what is stirred in his secret, heart, and conscience: that is, We know what is hidden and concealed in his soul. Among the uses of the whispering in the hidden voice is the saying of Al-A’sha: You hear whispers about jewelry when you leave So he used for what was hidden from the inner self And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein which is the jugular vein, which extends from the side of his throat to his shoulder, and they are two veins on the right and left. Al-Hasan said: The jugular vein, which is a vein attached to the heart. It is a metaphor for the closeness of that vein to the person: meaning We are nearer to him than his jugular vein, and the addition is explanatory: which rope is the jugular vein. And it was said that the rope is the jugular vein itself, so it is from the door of the congregational mosque.
50:17: Then the Almighty mentioned that with His knowledge of it, He assigned two angels to write down and record his deeds, as a binding proof, so He said: 17- When the two receivers receive The adverbial phrase is in the accusative case with what is closer in meaning to the verb, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with an understood noun, which is remember. The meaning is that He is closer to him than his jugular vein when the two receivers, who are the two angels assigned to him, receive what he says and what he does: that is, they take that and record it. Receiving means taking: that is, We are most knowledgeable about his conditions and have no need of the guardians assigned to him. We only made that as a binding proof and to confirm the matter. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Mujahid said: The two receivers are two angels who receive your deeds, one of them on your right writes down your good deeds, and the other on your left writes down your bad deeds. Mujahid also said: God has assigned to man two angels at night and two angels during the day to record his deeds and write down his traces. On the right and on the left is a seated one. He said sitted and did not say two seated ones when they are two, because what is meant is on the right is a seated one and on the left is a seated one. So the first was omitted because the second indicates it. This is what Sibawayh said, like the poet’s saying: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs And Al-Farazdaq said: He came and happened, and I had no excuses That is, he was inexcusable and I was inexcusable. Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra’ said: The word qa’id is suitable for one, two, and a plural, and does not require an estimation in the first. Al-Jawhari and other imams of language and grammar said: Fa’il and fa’ul are among the forms that apply to one, two, and a plural. Qa’id is the seated type like jalis in the sense of gatherings.
50:18: 18- Not a word does he utter but there is by him an observer ready to record.
