That is, no word is spoken, and no one utters it or throws it out except that there is a watcher by him: that is, the one who speaks has a watcher: that is, an angel who watches his words and writes them down. The watcher is the keeper who follows up on a person’s affairs and writes down what he says, good or bad. The writer of good is the angel on the right, and the writer of evil is the angel on the left. Prepared means present and prepared. Al-Jawhari said: Prepared means present and prepared. It is said, I prepared it and I prepared it meaning I made it ready. From this comes And I prepared for them a reclining place. What is meant here is that it is prepared and ready for writing.
50:19: 19- And the intoxication of death will come in truth. After the Almighty made clear that all of His deeds are preserved and written down, He mentioned after that what will befall them of death. What is meant by the intoxication of death is its severity and overwhelming force that overwhelms a person and overcomes his mind. The meaning of in truth is that at death, the truth will become clear to him and the truth of what the messengers brought of information about the resurrection, the promise, and the threat will become clear to him. It was said that the truth is death. It was also said that there is an inversion of the statement: that is, the intoxication of truth will come with death. This is how Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Ibn Mas`ud read it. The intoxication is the truth, so it was added to itself due to the difference in the two words. It was also said that the ba’ is for association, like in His statement: It grows with oil, meaning entwined with the truth, meaning with the reality of the situation. The reference in His statement: That is to death, and the deviant inclination: that is, that death from which you were turning away and fleeing. It is said that he deviated from something, he deviated, he deviated, he turned away from it and deviated. From this is the saying of Tarafa: Abu Munther: I threw away loyalty, but I gave it up and I was stubborn as a camel strays from the edge Al-Hassan said: If you avoid, you will run away.
50:20: 20- And the Trumpet will be blown This is expressed in the past tense to indicate that it will happen, and this is the final blast of the Resurrection. That is the Day of Threat meaning that is the time when the Trumpet will be blown, the Day of Threat with which God has threatened the disbelievers. Muqatil said: What is meant by the threat is the torment in the Hereafter, and the threat was specified even though today is the Day of both promise and threat to horrify it.
50:21: 21- And every soul will come with a driver and a witness. That is, every soul will come with someone to drive it and someone to testify for it or against it. There is a difference of opinion about the driver and the witness. Ad-Dahhak said: The driver is from the angels, and the witness is from themselves, meaning the hands and feet. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: A driver drives them and a witness testifies to their actions. Ibn Muslim said: The driver is their companion from the devils. He is called a driver because he follows them even if he does not urge them on. Mujahid said: The driver and the witness are two angels. It is said that the driver is the angel and the witness is the action. It is also said that the driver is the writer of bad deeds, and the witness is the writer of good deeds. The location of the sentence is the accusative case as a state.
50:22: 22- Indeed, you were heedless of this. That is, it will be said to him: You were heedless of this. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state of nafs or a new sentence as if it was said: What is said to him? Ad-Dahhak said: What is meant by this are the polytheists because they were heedless of the consequences of their actions. Ibn Zayd said: The address is to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): That is, O Muhammad, you were heedless of the message. Most of the commentators said: What is meant by it is all of creation, both the righteous and the wicked. Ibn Jarir preferred this. The majority read it with a fatha on the ta' of kunt and a fatha on the kaf in ghita'uka and basaraka based on the masculine nature of the wording of each. Al-Jahdary and Talha bin Musarraf read them all with a kasra, meaning that what is meant is the soul. So We removed from you your covering which was in this world: meaning, We lifted the veil that was between you and the matters of the Hereafter, and We lifted what you were in of heedlessness about that. So your sight today is sharp, meaning penetrating, with which you see what was hidden from you of this world. Al-Suddi said: What is meant by the covering is that it was in his mother’s womb and was lowered. It was also said that it was in the grave and was resurrected, but the first is more appropriate. It was said that sight is the sight of the heart, and it was also said that it is the sight of the eye. Mujahid said: Your sight is towards the tongue of your scale when your good and bad deeds are weighed, and Ad-Dahhak said the same.
50:23: 23- And his companion said, ‘This is what I have ready.’ That is, the angel assigned to him said, “This is what I have of your record of deeds ready and present. I have prepared it.” This is what Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak said. Mujahid said, The angel says to the Lord, glory be to Him, ‘This is what You have assigned to me from the sons of Adam, I have brought it and the record of its deeds.’ It was narrated from him that he said, His companion is from the devils, and he says that, ‘This is what I have prepared for you by my seduction and misguidance.’ Ibn Zayd said, “What is meant here is his companion from among mankind, and ‘ready’ is raised as an attribute of what is described, and if it is a relative pronoun, then it is a predicate after a predicate, or a predicate of a deleted subject.”
50:24: 24- Throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever. This is an address from God Almighty to the driver and the witness. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a command to the two angels assigned to him, namely the driver and the witness: Every stubborn ungrateful person who rejects the blessings and rejects the faith.
50:25: 25- "Hinderer of good does not do good Aggressor is an oppressor who does not acknowledge the Oneness of God Suspicious is a doubter of the truth, from their saying arab arajul": if he becomes suspicious. It was said that it is addressed to the two angels from the keepers of Hell. It was said that it is addressed to one person, by reducing the dual subject to the same level as the dual and repetitive verb. Al-Khalil and Al-Akhfash said: This is the correct speech of the Arabs, to address one person in the dual form. They say: irhalaha wa ajraha, and take him and release him for one person. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say to one person "people from us". The origin of that is that the minimum helpers of a man in his camels, sheep, and companions on his journey are two, so the speech of a man to one person is based on that, and from it is their saying to one person in poetry, as Imru' al-Qais said: My friend, I passed by Umm Jundub, and the tears fell on my tormented heart. And he said: Stop and let us weep over the memory of a beloved and a home in the valley between Dakhul and Hawmal. And the other said: If you rebuke me, O son of Affan, I will rebuke, and if you call me, I will be an impregnable presence. Al-Mazini said: His saying: al-qayā indicates al-qa the one that casts a glance. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a dual form for emphasis, so al-qayā replaces al-qa the one that casts a glance. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: The stubborn one who opposes the truth, and it was said: the one who turns away from the truth. It is said when ya’nad with a kasra is anūd obstinate: if he opposes the truth.
50:26: 26- He who has set up another god with God may be a substitute for all or an accusative of blame, or a substitute for disbelievers, or a subject or a predicate. So throw him into the severe punishment is an emphasis on the first command or a substitute for it.
50:27: 27- His companion said, ‘Our Lord, I did not make him transgress.’ This sentence is a new chapter to explain what the companion says. What is meant by the companion here is the devil who was appointed for this disbeliever. He denied that he had made him transgress, then he said, But he was far astray, meaning from the truth. So I called upon him and he responded to me. Had he been one of Your sincere servants, I would not have attacked him. It was said that his companion was the angel who wrote down his bad deeds, and that the disbeliever says, My Lord, he hastened me, and He answers him with this. This is what Muqatil and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said. But the first is more appropriate.
50:28: And the majority said the same: 28- He said, ‘Do not dispute in My Presence’ This sentence is a new answer to an implied question, as if it was said, so what did God say? So it was said: He said, ‘Do not dispute in My Presence’ meaning the disbelievers and their peers, He, the Most High, forbade them from disputing in the place of judgment, and the sentence And I have already presented to you the threat is in the accusative case as a state: that is, and the state is that I have presented to you the threat of sending messengers and revealing books, and the ba in in the threat is added for emphasis or to imply that present has the meaning of presented.
50:29: 29- My word cannot be changed meaning there is no breaking of My promise, rather it will inevitably happen, and I have decreed punishment for you, so there is no changing it. It was said that this statement is His saying: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof.
50:30: 30- The Day We will say to Hell, ‘Are you filled?’ and it will say, ‘Are there any more?’ The majority of scholars recited We say with a nun. Nafi’ and Abu Bakr recited it with a ya. Al-Hasan recited I say. Al-A’mash recited It is said, and the agent in the circumstance is what the saying changes or is omitted, i.e., remind or warn them. This speech is by way of representation and imagination, with no question or answer. This is what was said. It is more appropriate that it is by way of investigation, and neither reason nor religion prevents that. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: God showed it the confirmation of His statement, I will surely fill Hell. So when it was filled, He said to it, Are you filled?’ and it will say, ‘Are there any more?’ Meaning, it has been filled and there is no place left that has not been filled. This is what Ata’, Mujahid, and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said. It was said that this question means asking for more, i.e., it is asking for more for those who have already entered it. It was said: The meaning is that she asked for more of her wealth because she was in distress with her family. More is either a source like al-Muhaid or a passive participle like al-Mani’. The first means Is there an increase? and the second means Is there something you can increase?
50:31: Then when he finished explaining the state of the disbelievers, he began explaining the state of the believers, saying: 31- And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far away. That is, Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far away, or a place not far from them, such that they will see it in the gathering place, and see what is in it that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. It is possible that the accusative of not far is in the state of circumstance. It was said that the meaning is that their hearts were adorned in this world with encouragement and intimidation, so it became close to their hearts, but the first is more appropriate.
50:32: And the reference in His saying: 32- This is what you are promised to Paradise is by estimating the saying: that is, and it will be said to them, This is what you are promised. The majority read you are promised with the superlative. Ibn Kathir read it with the subjunctive. For every frequently turning back, a Guardian. It is a substitute for for the righteous by repeating the preposition or related to an omitted saying that is a state: that is, said to them for every frequently turning back. The frequently turning back is the one who returns to God in repentance from sin. It was also said that it is the one who glorifies God, and it was also said that it is the one who remembers God in private. Al-Sha'bi and Mujahid said: It is the one who remembers his sins in private and seeks God's forgiveness for them. Ubayd ibn Umair said: It is the one who does not sit in a gathering until he seeks God's forgiveness in it. The Guardian is the one who guards his sins until he repents from them. Qatadah said: He is the guardian of what God has entrusted to him of His rights and blessings, as Mujahid said. It was also said that it is the guardian of God's command. Ad-Dahhak said: He is the guardian of God's command to him to accept.
50:33: 33- "Whoever fears the Most Gracious in secret" the relative pronoun is in the genitive case as a substitute or clarification for every one who turns back to God. It was also said that it is permissible for it to be a substitute after a substitute for "al-muttaqeen" the pious, and there is a problem with that because the substitute and what it is substituted for are not repeated. It is also permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a resumption and the predicate is "enter it with the estimation that it is said to them, enter it." Fear in secret means that one fears God even though he has not seen Him. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: It means seclusion where no one can see him. Al-Hasan said: If he lowers the curtain and closes the door. And in secret is related to an omitted word which is a state or description of the source of fear. "And he came with a heart turning in repentance" meaning he returned to God, sincere in his obedience to Him. It was also said that the one who turns in repentance is the one who is ready to obey Him, and it was also said that he is the one who is sound.

50:40: 40- And during part of the night glorify Him. "Min" is for partiality: meaning glorify Him some of the night. It was said that it refers to the night prayer, and it was said that it refers to the two rak'ahs of Fajr, and it was said that it refers to the Isha prayer, and the first is better. "And the ends of prostration" meaning glorify Him after the prayers. The majority read "Adbar" with a fatha on the hamza, plural of dabr. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Hamzah read it with a kasra on it as a verbal noun, from adbara al-shay' idbaran: if it turned away. A group of the Companions and Followers said: The ends of prostration are the two rak'ahs after Maghrib, and the turning away of the stars are the two rak'ahs before Fajr. The seven reciters agreed that "Idbar al-Nujum" is with a kasra on the hamza, as will come.
50:41: 41- And listen on the Day when the Caller will call from a place nearby. That is, listen to what is revealed to you regarding the circumstances of the al-Qiyamah 75:On the Day when the Caller will call, and he is Israfil or Gabriel. It was also said that he will listen to the call, or the voice, or the shout, which is the shout of the al-Qiyamah 75:I mean the second blowing of the Trumpet by Israfil. It was also said that Israfil will blow, and Gabriel will call the people of the place of assembly, saying: Come for the reckoning. So the call, according to this, will be at the place of assembly. Muqatil said: It is Israfil calling for the gathering, saying: O people, come for the reckoning “from a place nearby,” such that the call will reach every individual of the people of the place of assembly. Qatada said: We used to narrate that he would call from the rock of Jerusalem. Al-Kalbi said: It is the closest land to the heavens by twelve miles. Ka’b said: Eighteen miles.
50:42: 42- The Day they hear the Shout in truth is a substitute for The Day He calls out meaning the Shout of Resurrection, and in truth is related to the Shout. That is the Day of Resurrection meaning the Day of Resurrection from the graves. Al-Kalbi said: In truth means Resurrection. Muqatil said: It means that it will truly happen.
50:43: 43- Indeed, it is We who bring to life and cause to die. That is, We bring to life in the Hereafter and cause to die in this world. No one shares in that with Us. The sentence is a resumption of the matter of resurrection. And to Us is the final destination. So We reward every worker according to his work.
50:44: 44- "The Day the earth will split open about them" The majority of reciters read it by assimilating the taa' into the sheen. The Kufians read it by softening the sheen, deleting one of the two taa's for ease. Zayd ibn Ali read: tatashaqqaf by affirming the two taa's as per the original, and it was recited in the passive form, and the accusative of "sira'an as a state of the pronoun in about them", and the agent in the state is tashaqqaf, and it was said that the agent in the state is the same as the agent in the day: meaning hurrying to the crier who called them "That is a gathering meaning resurrection and the plural of for us is easy" is hayn.
50:45: Then God, the Exalted, consoled His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: 45- We know best what they say, meaning their denial of what you have come with and their denial of resurrection and monotheism. And you are not a compeller over them, meaning in your path of forcing and compelling them to believe. The verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword. So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat, meaning whoever fears My threat of punishment to My disobedient ones. As for those other than them, do not concern yourself with them. Then God, the Exalted, commanded him after that to fight. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And no fatigue touched us, he said: from fatigue. At-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat and Ibn Asakir on the authority of Jarir ibn Abdullah on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding his statement, And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun, the dawn prayer, and before its setting, the afternoon prayer. At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “I spent the night with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he prayed two short rak’ahs before the dawn prayer, then he went out to pray and said: O Ibn Abbas, two rak’ahs before the dawn prayer after the stars have set, and two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer after prostration.” Musaddad narrated in his Musnad, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, about the setting of the stars and the ending of prostration, and he said: The ending of prostration is two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer, and the setting of the stars is the two rak’ahs before the morning prayer.” Muhammad bin Nasr narrated in As-Salah and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Umar bin Al-Khattab: The end of prostration is two rak’ahs after Maghrib, and the end of the stars is two rak’ahs before Fajr. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Nasr, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Asma’ wa’l-Sifat from Ali bin Abi Talib, something similar. Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: He ordered him to glorify God at the end of all prayers. Ibn Jarir narrated from him: And listen on the Day when the crier will call out, he said: It is the shout. Al-Wasiti also narrated from him: From a place nearby, he said: From the rock of Jerusalem. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him: That is the Day of Resurrection, he said: The day when they will emerge from the graves for resurrection. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him: “They said: O Messenger of God, if you had frightened us,” so this verse was revealed: So remind by the Qur’an whoever fears My threat.
51:1: It has sixty verses, and it is Meccan. Al-Qurtubi said in the opinion of everyone Ibn Al-Dharis, Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Adh-Dhariyat was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar statement on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr. His saying: 1- And the scatterers scatter It is said that the wind scatter the dust, scattering it, and that it scatters it, scattering it, the Almighty swears by the winds that scatter the dust. The victory of dharwān is on the source, and the agent in it is the active participle and the passive participle is omitted. Abu Amr and Hamzah read it by assimilating the ta’ of dharwān into the dhal of dharwān. The rest read it without assimilation. It was said that the one sworn by is understood and He is the Lord of dharwān and what comes after it, but the first is more appropriate.
51:2: 2- "The ones that carry water" are the clouds that carry water, just as quadrupeds carry heavy loads. The accusative case of "waqran is that it is the direct object, just as one says, So-and-so carried a heavy load. The majority of scholars read waqran" with a kasra on the waw, as the name of what is carried, and it was read with a fatha on it as a verbal noun, and the factor in it is the active participle, or as the noun being named as a verbal noun out of emphasis.
51:3: 3- "The ships that sail easily" are the ships that sail the sea with the wind easily. The word "yasra" is in the accusative case as a source, or as an attribute of a deleted source, or as a state: meaning, running easily. It was said that it refers to the winds. It was also said that it refers to the clouds, but the first is more appropriate. Ease: easy in everything.
51:4: 4- "Those who divide a matter" are the angels who divide matters. Al-Farra' said: They come with different commands: Gabriel with harshness, Michael with mercy, and the Angel of Death comes with death. It was also said that they come with different commands of drought, fertility, rain, death, and accidents. It was also said that they are the clouds by which God divides the affairs of His servants. It was also said that what is meant by the scatterers, carriers, movers, and dividers are the winds, for they are described with all of these because they scatter the dust, carry the clouds, run in the air, and divide the rain. This is very weak. The accusative of "amrana" is the direct object, and it was also said that it is in the state of command, meaning commanded, but the first is more appropriate.
51:5: 5- "You are promised something true." This is the answer to the oath: that is, you are promised reward and punishment for something that will inevitably happen. It is permissible for the word to be a relative pronoun with the pronoun omitted, or for it to be a verbal noun. The reason for singling out these matters for swearing by them is that they are novelties that go against the dictates of custom, so whoever is able to do them is also able to bring about the promised resurrection.
51:7: 7- "And the sky of intertwined things. The majority read intertwined things" with a damma on the ha' and the ba'. It was also read with a damma on the ha' and a sukoon on the ba', with a kasra on the ha' and a fatha on the ba', and with a kasra on the ha' and a damma on the ba'. Ibn Atiyyah said: These are languages, and what is meant by the sky here is the well-known one, and it was said that what is meant by it are the clouds, but the first is more appropriate. The commentators differed in the interpretation of Al-Habbak. Mujahid, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ and others said: It means the one with a good, even character. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: Everything that you perfect and make well, you have woven and intertwined. Al-Hasan and Sa’id bin Jubayr said: The one with adornment. It was also narrated from Al-Hasan that he said: The one with the stars. Al-Dahhak said: The one with the paths. Al-Farra’ said the same. What you see of water and sand when the wind hits it is called Habbak. Al-Farra’ said: Al-Habbak with a kasra is everything like sand when a still wind passes over it, and water when the wind passes over it. An iron shield is called Habbak, and from this is the saying of the poet: As if the weaver had covered her with a rug, and woven it with silk Any way, and it was said that the word habak means intensity, and the meaning is: the sky is intense, and the mahbuk is the one with strong creation, whether a horse or other, and from it the poet said: He may carry me in his nose, following the path of the two woven paths The other said: Marj al-Din, so I prepared for him the supervisor of the Harak, the knitted Al-Katd Al-Wahidi said after narrating the first opinion: This is the opinion of the majority.
51:8: 8- "Indeed, you are of a different opinion." This is the answer to the oath by the heaven with its interwoven fabric. That is, you, O people of Mecca, are of a different and contradictory opinion about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of you say he is a poet; some of you say he is a magician; and some of you say he is insane. The reason for specifying the oath by the heaven with that description is that their different opinions are likened to the different paths of the heaven. The use of interwoven fabric in paths is what the linguists agree with, even though most of the commentators disagree. However, it is possible that these statements in the interpretation of the interwoven fabric can be traced back to this, by saying: The paths in the heaven could be a reason for its increased beauty, the evenness of its creation, the presence of adornment in it, and its increased strength. It has been said that what is meant by their having a different opinion is that some of them deny the resurrection and some of them doubt it. It has also been said that they acknowledge that God is their Creator and worship idols.
51:9: 9- "He who afka is turned away from it" means he is turned away from believing in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought, or from the truth, which is resurrection and monotheism, from the verb "sarfa". It was also said that he is turned away from that difference from the one who God turned him away from it with protection and success. It is said that he afkahu ya'fuquhu ifkān: meaning he accepted him from the thing and turned him away from it. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: "They said, 'Have you come to us to turn us away?'" Mujahid said: He is turned away from it from afan, and afan is the corruption of the mind. It was also said that he is deprived from it from haraam. Qatrib said: He is cut off from it from jada'. Al-Yazidi said: He is repelled from it from repelled.
51:10: 10- The liars were killed. This is a supplication against them. Al-Wahidi narrated from all the commentators that the meaning is: Cursed are the liars. Ibn Al-Anbari said: If killing is reported on behalf of God, it means cursing, because whoever is cursed by God is in the same position as someone who has been killed and destroyed. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of killing is cursing. The liars are the liars who guess what they do not know, saying: Muhammad is a madman, a liar, a poet, and a magician. Al-Zajjaj said: The liars are the liars. Al-Khars is the storage of fresh dates on palm trees, and Al-Kharras is the one who estimates them, but he is not the intended meaning here.
51:11: Then he said: 11- Those who are in a state of heedlessness meaning in a state of heedlessness, blindness, and ignorance of the affairs of the Hereafter. The meaning of heedless is careless and negligent. Forgetfulness is heedlessness of something and its disappearance from the heart. The root of ghamrah is what conceals and covers something, and from it are the ghamarat al-mawt.
51:12: 12- They ask, ‘When is the Day of Judgment?’ That is, they say, When is the Day of Judgment? as a denial and mockery.
51:13: Then the Almighty informed us about that Day, saying: 13- "The Day they will be tested by the Fire" meaning they will be burned and tormented. It is said that you have tested gold, meaning you burned it to test it. The root of "test" is to test. Ikrimah said: Haven't you seen that when gold is put into the Fire, it is said that it is tested? The accusative of "Day" is implied: meaning the recompense: the Day they will be tested by the Fire. It is permissible for it to be a substitute for the Day of Judgment, and the fat-ha is for construction because it is added to the sentence. It was said that it is accusative by estimating "I mean". Ibn Abi Ubla read it by raising "Day" as a substitute for the Day of Judgment.
51:14: And the sentence 14- "Taste your trial" is by the power of the saying: that is, it will be said to them: Taste your punishment, as Ibn Zayd said. Mujahid said: Your burning, and Al-Farra' preferred the first. And the sentence "This is what you were hastening" is from what is narrated by the saying: that is, this is what you were asking to hasten in mockery of you, and it was said that it is a substitute for your trial.
51:15: 15- Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs. When God Almighty mentioned the state of the people of Hell, He mentioned the state of the people of Paradise: that is, they will be in gardens with flowing springs that no describer can describe.
51:16: 16- taking what their Lord has given them meaning accepting what their Lord has given them of goodness and honor. The phrase they were before that doers of good is an explanation of what preceded it: meaning because they were doers of good deeds in this world, doing what they were commanded to do and leaving what they were forbidden to do.
51:17: Then he explained their goodness with which he described them, saying: 17- They slept but little of the night. Sleeping: sleeping at night rather than during the day, and the meaning is: they slept little of the night, and ma is redundant, and it is possible for it to be a source or a relative pronoun: meaning they slept little of the night or what they slept in, and from that is the saying of Abu Qais bin Al-Aslat: The egg has been laid on my head, so I do not eat sleep except for sleeplessness Sleep deprivation: a little sleep, including the saying of Amr ibn Ma’di Karib: Amen, Rayhana, the All-Hearing, the Supplicant arouses me while my companions are asleep It was said that ma is a negative particle, meaning they did not sleep a little at night, so how about a lot of it? This is very weak. This is the opinion of those who said that the meaning was that their number was small. Then he began by saying: they did not sleep, and Ibn al-Anbari said the same, but it is weaker than what came before it. Qatadah said in his interpretation of this verse: they used to pray between the two evening prayers, and Abu al-Aaliyah and Ibn Wahb said the same. 18- And in the hours of the pre-dawn hours they would seek forgiveness meaning they would ask God, the Almighty, to forgive their sins during the hours of the pre-dawn hours. Al-Hasan said: They extended the prayer until the hours of the pre-dawn hours, then they began seeking forgiveness during the hours of the pre-dawn hours. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and Mujahid said: They sought forgiveness during the hours of the pre-dawn hours. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and Mujahid said: They prayed during the hours of the pre-dawn hours, because their prayer was a request for forgiveness. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the dawn prayer.God
51:19: Then God, the Almighty, mentioned their charity, saying: 19- And in their wealth is a right for the beggar and the deprived. That is, they make a right in their wealth for the beggar and the deprived as a way of drawing closer to God, the Almighty. Muhammad ibn Sirin and Qatadah said: The right here is the obligatory zakat, but the first is more appropriate, so it is interpreted as voluntary charity, maintaining kinship ties, and hosting guests, because the Surah was revealed in Mecca, and zakat was only made obligatory in Medina. And we will see in Surah A beggar asked, In their wealth is a known right * For the beggar and the deprived. With the addition of known, and the beggar is the one who asks people because of his need. There is disagreement over the interpretation of mahrum deprived. Some say it refers to someone who refrains from asking, so people think he is rich and do not give him charity. This is what Qatada and Az-Zuhri said. Al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah said: He is the one who has no share in the spoils of war and no share of the spoils of war is given to him. Zayd ibn Aslam said: He is the one whose fruit, crops, or livestock have been destroyed. Al-Qurtubi said: He is the one who has been struck by a catastrophe. It is also said that he is the one who does not earn a living. It is also said that he is the one who does not find wealth that will make him self-sufficient. It is also said that he is the one who seeks this world and it turns away from it. It is also said that he is a slave. It is also said that he is a dog, and other sayings have been made. Al-Sha'bi said: It has been seventy years since I had a wet dream and I have been asking about mahrum deprived. I am no more knowledgeable about it today than I was then. What should be relied upon is what the linguistic meaning indicates. Mahrum deprived in the language means forbidden, from deprivation, which means prevention. This includes those who have been deprived of sustenance from the ground up, those whose wealth has been stricken by a catastrophe that has taken it away, those who have been deprived of gifts, and those who have been deprived of charity because of their self-respect.
51:20: Then the Almighty mentioned the evidence He established to indicate His Oneness and the truth of His promise and threat, saying: 20- And on the earth are signs for those of certain faith. That is, clear evidence and visible signs from the mountains, the land, the sea, the trees, the rivers, and the fruits, and in them are signs of destruction for the disbelieving nations who denied what the Messengers of God brought and called them to. He singled out those of certain faith in God because they are the ones who acknowledge that and reflect on it, thus benefiting from it.
51:21: 21- And in yourselves, will you not see? That is, in yourselves are signs that indicate the Oneness of God and the truth of what the Messengers brought. He created them as a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then a bone until He breathed the soul into them. Then after that, their forms, colors, natures, and tongues changed. Then He created them in this wondrous state of flesh, blood, bones, limbs, senses, ducts, and organs. The meaning of will you not see is: will you not look with the eye of insight, and thereby deduce the Creator, the Provider, who is unique in divinity, and that He has no partner, opposite, or equal, and that His promise is true, and His word is true, and that what His Messengers brought to you is the truth about which there is no doubt or suspicion. It was said that what is meant by souls are spirits: that is, in your souls, by which you live, are signs.
51:22: 22- And in the sky is your provision meaning the cause of your provision, which is rain, for it is the cause of provisions. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ad-Dahhak said: Provision here is what descends from the sky of rain and snow. It was said that what is meant by the sky are the clouds: meaning, and in the clouds is your provision. It was also said that what is meant by the sky is the rain, and it was called sky because it descends from its direction. From this is the saying of the poet: If the sky descends upon the land of a people, we will take care of them, even if they are angry. Ibn Kaysan said: It means, And upon the Lord of the heaven is your provision. Similar to it is, And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, which is far-fetched. Sufyan al-Thawri said: It means, With God in the heaven is your provision. It was also said that the meaning is, And in the heaven is the decree of your provision. The majority of scholars read your provision in the singular, while Ya’qub, Ibn Muhaisin, and Mujahid read your provisions in the plural. And what you are promised of Paradise and Hell, as Mujahid said. Ata’ said: Of reward and punishment. Al-Kalbi said: Of good and evil. Ibn Sirin said: What you are promised of the Hour. Al-Rabi’ said the same. It is better to interpret it in a more general way than these statements, because the reward for deeds is written in the heaven, and fate and destiny descend from it, and Paradise and Hell are in it.
51:23: Then He, the Most High, swore by Himself, saying: 23- "By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth." That is, what He has informed you of in these verses. Al-Zajjaj said: It is what was mentioned about the matter of provision and the signs. Al-Kalbi said: It means what was narrated in the Book. Muqatil said: It means about the matter of the Hour. It was said that what is in His statement, "And what you are promised, is the subject and its predicate is By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth. So the pronoun refers to what." Then He, the Most High, said: "Like what you speak. The majority of scholars read like" in the accusative case, assuming: like your speech. "Ma" is redundant. This is how some of the Kufians said that it is in the accusative case by removing the preposition. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case for emphasis: that is, it is the truth like your speech." Al-Mazini said: Like and ma are like one thing, so it is built on the fat-ha. Sibawayh said: It is in the accusative case because it is added to something that is not established. This reading was chosen by Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Abu Bakr and Al-A’mash read mithl in the nominative case as an attribute of haqq, because mithl is an indefinite noun, and even if it is added to a noun it is not definite with an addition like ghair. Abu Ali Al-Farisi preferred Al-Mazini’s statement, and he said, “And similar to it is the statement of Hamid: Woe to those who do not know what they are and what they protect So, Bani Waih with what was not followed by the tanween, and the meaning of the verse is likening the realization of what God has informed about to the realization of human speech and existence, and this is like what you say: It is true just as you are here, and it is true just as you speak, and the meaning is: that in its truthfulness and existence, and this is like what you say: It is true just as you are here, and it is true just as you speak, and the meaning is: that in its truthfulness and existence it is like what you know by necessity. Abdul Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Al-Anbari, Al-Daraqutni in Al-Afrad, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab have narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, regarding his statement, “By the scatterers,” he said: The winds. By those carrying heavy loads, he said: The clouds. By those running smoothly, he said: The ships. By those distributing a matter, he said: The angels. Al-Bazzar, Al-Daraqutni in Al-Ifrad, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir have narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, tracing it back to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). In its chain of narration is Abu Bakr bin Sabra, who is weak in hadith, and Saeed bin Salam, who is not among the scholars of hadith. This is what Al-Bazzar said. Ibn Kathir said: This hadith is weak in its attribution to the Prophet, and the most likely explanation for it is that it stops at Umar. Al-Firyabi and Ibn Mardawayh have narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar to what Ali said. Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh have narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, By the sky of constellations, he said: Its beauty and its evenness. Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: Of splendor and beauty, and its structure is like a chained cloak. Ibn Jarir and Abu Al-Shaykh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar. Ibn Mani’ narrated on the authority of Ali, he said: Its is the seventh heaven. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, He who is led astray from it will be turned away from it, he said: He who is led astray will be led astray from it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, The liars were killed, he said: The doubters are cursed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, he said: They are the soothsayers, “who are in heedlessness, he said: In heedlessness and inattentiveness. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, he said: Ghumrah is disbelief and doubt. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, he said: In their misguidance they will persist. Concerning His statement, The Day they will be tested over the Fire, he said: They will be tormented. These people also narrated from him regarding his statement, taking what their Lord has given them, he said: the obligatory duties. Indeed, they were before that doers of good, he said: before the obligatory duties were revealed, they used to do good. These people also narrated from him, and al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat, also narrated from him: They used to sleep but little of the night, he said: There would not come a night in which they slept until morning except that they would pray during it. Ibn Nasr, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: They used to sleep but little. Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Anas regarding the verse, he said: They used to pray between sunset and night prayers. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Umar: And in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness, he said: They would pray. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, There is a right in their wealth, meaning, other than zakat, which is used to maintain kinship ties, entertain a guest, or help the deprived. Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, saying: The beggar is the one who asks people, and the deprived is the one who does not have a share of the spoils of the Muslims. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, saying: The deprived is the one who seeks this world and turns away from it and does not ask people, so God commanded the believers to support him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Aisha regarding the verse. She said: He is the one who is deprived and cannot find a way to earn a living. At-Tirmidhi and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Fatimah bint Qais, “She asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about this verse. He said: There is a right in wealth other than zakat, and he recited this verse: ‘Righteousness is not that you turn your faces…’ until His saying: ‘and in freeing slaves…’ and establishing prayer and giving zakat.” Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr regarding his statement: And in yourselves, then will you not see? He said: The path of defecation and urination.
51:24: His statement: 24- Has there come to you the story of the honored guests of Abraham? God the Almighty mentioned the story of Abraham to clarify that he was destroyed due to the denial of his family. The question is an indication that this story is not something that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knew, and that he only learned it through revelation. It was said that hal means qad, as in His statement: Has there not been over man a period of time? "Guys" is a noun that refers to one, two, or a group. We have previously discussed the story of Abraham's guests in Surah Hud and Surah Al-Hijr. What is meant by them being honored is that they are honored by God the Almighty because they were angels who came to him in the form of human beings, as God the Almighty said in describing them in another verse: "Rather, they are honored servants." It was also said that they were Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil. Muqatil and Mujahid said: Abraham honored them, treated them well, and stood over them, although he would not stand over a guest. He ordered his wife to serve them. Al-Kalbi said: He honored them with the calf.
51:25: 25- When they entered upon him The agent in the circumstance is hadith: that is, did you hear their story that occurred at the time of their entering upon him? Or the agent in it is guest because it is a verbal noun, or the agent in it is the honored ones, or the agent in it is an implied verb: that is, remember. They said, Peace"" meaning, we greet you with peace. He said, Peace means, Ibrahim said, Peace". The majority of scholars read the first "Peace" in the accusative case and the second in the nominative case. The first is in the accusative case as a verbal noun with the verb assumed as we mentioned, and what is meant by it is the subjunctive. It is possible that the meaning is: So they said good words because it is a statement with which the speaker was safe from idle talk, so in this case it would be a direct object. As for the second, it is in the nominative case as a subject with the predicate omitted: that is, peace be upon you. It was changed to the nominative case in order to indicate that the nominal sentence is permanent and stable, unlike the verbal noun which is for mere renewal and occurrence. For this reason, the scholars of semantics said: Ibrahim's peace is more eloquent than the angels' peace. The nominative case was read in both cases, and the accusative case was read in both. The people of Kufa, except for Asim, read it with a kasra on the seen, and Salam read it in both of them, a people who are ungrateful. The word people is raised as if it were the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning, you are a people who are ungrateful. It was said that he said this to himself and did not address them with it, because that would be contrary to honor. It was said that he disapproved of them because they initiated the greeting, and that was not customary among his people. It was said that it was because he saw in them something that differed from some human forms. It was said that it was because he saw them in a form other than the angels that he knew. Others said otherwise.
51:26: 26- "He went to his family" Al-Zajjaj said: meaning he went to his family secretly from his guests, and it was said that he went to them secretly from his guests, and the meaning is close and its explanation was presented in Surah As-Saffat. It is said that ragha and irtaha mean to seek, and what does yariga: meaning he wants and seeks, and aragha ila such-and-such: he inclined towards it secretly and deviated from it. "So he brought a fattened calf meaning so his guest brought a calf that he had roasted for them as in Surah Hud with a roasted calf" and there is an omission in the speech indicated by the eloquent fa: meaning so he slaughtered a calf and roasted it and brought it.
51:27: 27- So he brought it near to them meaning he brought the calf near to them and placed it in their hands, then he said, 'Will you not eat?' The question is for denial, because when he brought it near to them, when he brought it near to them, they did not eat from it. It is stated in As-Sahah: The calf is the offspring of a sheep, and the calves are similar, and the plural is 'ajajil, and the female is a ewela. In some languages, the calf is said to be the sheep.
51:28: 28- So he felt fear of them meaning he felt a deep fear of them because they did not eat what he had brought near to them. It is also said that the meaning of he felt fear is he concealed it, and that this only happened to him because they did not observe the prohibition of his food. It is human nature to eat someone's food and feel safe from them, so Abraham thought that they came to do evil and not to do good. It is also said that it occurred to him that they were angels, but when they saw the signs of fear that appeared on him, they said, 'Do not fear' and informed him that they were angels sent to him by God, the Exalted. And they gave him good tidings of a learned boy meaning they gave him good tidings of a boy who would be born to him with much knowledge when he reached adulthood. The one given good tidings, according to the majority of scholars, was Isaac. Mujahid alone said that it was Ishmael, but this is refuted by the statement, And We gave him good tidings of Isaac. We have already explained this matter in detail, so the reader will not need to read anything else.
51:29: 29- So his wife came in a shriek. This coming was not from one place to another, but rather it is like you saying: He came to insult me, meaning he began to insult me, this is what Al-Farra and others said. And the shriek is the shout and the commotion, and it was said that it is a group of people. Al-Jawhari said: The shriek is the shout and the shout, and the shriek is the group, and the shriek is the severity of distress or other, and the meaning is: that she came in a shout, or in a commotion, or in a group of people listening to the words of the angels, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: So he attached it to the guides and dragged it in a bundle that did not leave. His saying: in a bundle is in the accusative case as a state. So she slapped her face means she slapped her face with her hand, as is the custom of women when expressing amazement. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: She gathered her fingers together and slapped her forehead in amazement. The meaning of slapping is to hit something with something wide. It is said sakahu meaning he struck it. And a barren old woman said meaning how can I give birth when I am an old barren woman? She considered that unlikely due to her old age and the fact that she is barren and cannot give birth.
51:30: 30- They said, ‘Thus said your Lord.’ That is, just as we told you and informed you, your Lord said, so do not doubt that and do not be surprised by it, for whatever God wills will inevitably happen, and we did not say that on our own authority. At that time, she was ninety-nine years old, and Abraham was one hundred years old. This has been fully explained previously. The phrase, Indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing, is an explanation of what preceded it: that is, He is Wise in His actions and words, and He knows everything.
51:31: And sentence 31 - He said, 'What is the matter with you, O messengers?' is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did Abraham say after this statement from the angels? The matter is the affair and the story, and the meaning is: What is the matter with you and what is your story, O messengers, from God's side, and what is that matter for which He sent you other than this good report.
51:32: 32- They said, ‘Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals.’ They meant the people of Lot.
51:33: 33- To send upon them stones of clay meaning to pelt them with stones of petrified clay. The accusative of marked is an adjective for stones or as a state of the pronoun implied in the prepositional phrase or of stones because it is an adjective with a prepositional phrase.
51:34: 34- The meaning of marked is marked with signs by which it is known. It was said that it was striped in black and white, and it was said that it was black and red, and it was said that it was known that they were stones of torment, and it was said that it was written on each stone who would be destroyed by them. His statement, with your Lord is an adverbial phrase for marked, meaning: marked with Him. For the transgressors, those who persist in misguidance and exceed the limit in immorality. Muqatil said: For the polytheists. Polytheism is the most transgressive and greatest of sins.
51:35: 35- So We brought out whoever was there of the believers. This is a statement from God Almighty: that is, when We wanted to destroy the people of Lot, We brought out whoever was in the villages of the people of Lot from his people who believed in him.
51:36: 36- We did not find in it except one house of Muslims meaning other than one household. It is said that it is a noble house and its people are meant by it. It is said that they are the people of the house of Lot. Islam is submission and surrender to the command of God, the Most High. Every believer is a Muslim. From this is his saying: The Bedouins said, ‘We believe.’ Say, ‘You have not believed, but say, ‘We have submitted.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, clarified the difference between Islam and faith in the hadith in the two Sahihs and others that are proven through various chains of transmission that “He was asked about Islam and he said: To testify that there is no god but God, to establish prayer, to pay zakat, to make pilgrimage to the House, and to fast Ramadan. He was asked about faith and he said: To believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and in destiny, both its good and its bad.” So the reference in the difference between them is what was said by the truthful and the believed, and no attention should be paid to what other scholars have said about the description of each one of them with confused, different, confused, and contradictory descriptions. As for what is in the Noble Book of the difference in the places of use of Islam and faith, that is based on linguistic meanings and Arabic usages. It is obligatory to give precedence to the legal truth over the linguistic, and the legal truth is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us about, and he answered The questioner asked him about it.
51:37: 37- And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment. That is, We left in those towns a sign and indication of the punishment that befell them, for everyone who feared the punishment of God and was in awe of it from the people of that time and those who came after them. This sign is the traces of the punishment in those towns, for they are clear and obvious. It was said that they are the stones that were thrown at them. Those who fear the painful punishment were singled out because they are the ones who take heed from the sermons and reflect on the signs, unlike others who do not fear that, and they are the polytheists who deny the resurrection, the promise, and the threat. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: in a bundle, he said: in a shout. So she slapped her face, he said: she slapped it. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And we found therein not but one house of Muslims, he said: Lot and his two daughters. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said: they were thirteen.
51:38: His statement: 38- And in Moses is connected to his statement in it by repeating the preposition, and the meaning is: And We left in the story of Moses a sign or connected to and in the earth and the meaning is: And in the earth and in Moses are signs, said Al-Farra’, Ibn Atiyyah and Al-Zamakhshari. Abu Hayyan said: It is very far-fetched, the Qur’an is far removed from something like it, and it is possible that it is related to making it understood for the purpose of indicating and We left upon him It was said and it is possible that it is connected to and We left in the manner of the saying of the one who says: I fed her straw and cold water. The interpretation is: And We left therein a sign, and We made in Moses a sign. Abu Hayyan said: There is no need to omit and We made because it is possible for the agent to be in the genitive and We left. The first aspect is preferable, and anything other than it is forced and arbitrary, and no need or necessity called for it. When We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority. The adverbial phrase is related to something omitted, which is the description of the sign: that is, existing at the time We sent him, or to the sign itself, and the first is preferable. And the clear authority is the apparent and evident proof, which is the staff and the signs with it.
51:39: 39- So he turned away with his corner. Turning away means turning away, and the corner means the side. Al-Akhfash said. The meaning is: he turned away from his side as in his saying: He turned away and moved away from his side. Al-Jawhari said: The corner of something is its stronger side, and it takes refuge in a strong corner: meaning honor and strength. Ibn Zayd, Mujahid, and others said: The corner is its plural and its soldiers who strengthened him, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: Or take refuge in a strong corner, meaning a clan and strength. It was said that the corner is the strength itself, and Qatada and others said the same, and from this is the saying of Antarah: How weak is my support in war, but how old is my time And he said, 'A magician or a madman' means Pharaoh said about Moses, He is a magician or a madman. So he wavered in what he saw of Moses' condition, between him being a magician or a madman. This is from the accursed one, a deception and a deception to his people, because he knew that the miracles he saw could not be done by a magician or by someone suffering from madness. It was said that or has the meaning of and, because he said all of that and did not hesitate. This was said by Al-Muraji and Al-Farra', like his saying, And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate.
51:40: 40- So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. That is, We threw them into the sea. The phrase and he was blameworthy is in the accusative case as a state: that is, he did what he was blameworthy for when he claimed divinity, disbelieved in God, and transgressed in his disobedience.
51:41: 41- And in Aad meaning that we left out in the story of Aad the verse when We sent upon them the barren wind which is the one in which there is no good or blessing, it does not pollinate the trees nor does it carry rain, rather it is a wind of destruction and torment.
51:42: Then the Almighty described this wind, saying: 42- It leaves nothing it comes upon except that it turns it into chaff. That is, it leaves nothing it comes upon of their lives, livestock, or wealth except that it turns it into something perishing and decaying. The poet said: You left me when time had taken away my sight, and I remained like the decayed bone of a palm tree. Qatada said: It is the dry plant that has been trampled on. Al-Suddi and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is the crushed dirt. Qatrib said: It is the ashes. The root of the word is from rama al-azm: if it has worn away, then it is ramaym, and rama means the decayed bones.
51:43: 43- And in Thamud, when it was said to them, ‘Enjoy yourselves for a time.’ That is, We left in the story of Thamud a verse about when We said to them, Live enjoying yourselves in this world for a time until the time of destruction, which was three days, as in His statement, Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days.
51:44: 44- They rebelled against the command of their Lord meaning they were too arrogant to obey God’s command. So the thunderbolt seized them. This refers to any devastating punishment. The majority of scholars read it as the thunderbolt. Umar ibn al-Khattab, Hamid, Ibn Muhaisin, Mujahid, and al-Kisa’i read it as the thunderbolt. We have already discussed the subject of the thunderbolt in Surat al-Baqarah, and in other places, while they are looking meaning they are seeing it with their own eyes. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state of description. It has also been said that the meaning is: they are awaiting the punishment they were promised, but the former is more appropriate.
51:45: 45- So they were unable to rise meaning they were not able to rise. Qatada said: From rising means they did not rise from that struggle, and the meaning is that they were unable to rise, let alone flee. Similar to this is His statement: So they became within their homes, prostrate “and they were not able to defend themselves” meaning they were not able to protect themselves from the punishment of God through anyone other than themselves.
51:46: 46- And the people of Noah before meaning before these destroyed ones, for their time preceded the time of Pharaoh, Aad, and Thamud. Indeed, they were a wicked people meaning they disobeyed God. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Amr read people in the accusative case, meaning that in the people of Noah there is a sign. The rest read it in the accusative case: meaning, and We destroyed the people of Noah, or it is conjoined with the object of the thunderbolt seized them, or with the object of we cast them out: meaning, we cast them out and cast out the people of Noah, or the factor in it is remember.
51:47: 47- And the heaven We constructed with power meaning with strength and ability. The majority of scholars read the sky with the accusative case as an izifah occurrence, and the meaning is: And We constructed the sky, We constructed it. Abu Al-Sammak and Ibn Muqsim read it with the nominative case as an introductory sentence. And indeed, We are expanding The expander is the one who has expansion and spaciousness, and the meaning is: Indeed, We have spaciousness by creating it and creating other things. We are not unable to do that. It was also said that We are Able, from was meaning energy and ability. It was also said that We are provided with provision by rain. Al-Jawhari said: And the man became spacious: he became wealthy and rich.
51:48: 48- And the earth We have spread out. The majority of scholars read the earth in the accusative case, indicating the preoccupation. Abu Al-Sammak and Ibn Muqsim read it in the nominative case, as mentioned previously in His statement: And the heaven We have constructed. The meaning of We have spread out is: We have extended it like a bed. So excellent are We, the spreaders. It is said, I spread out the bed: I have laid it out and smoothed it. To prepare matters means to level them and fix them.
51:49: 49- And of everything We have created pairs meaning two kinds and two types of male and female, land and sea, sun and moon, sweet and bitter, sky and earth, night and day, light and darkness, jinn and humans, good and evil that you may remember meaning We created it this way so that you may remember and know that He is the Creator of everything and thus prove His Oneness and the truth of His promise and threat.
51:50: 50- "So flee to God. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner." That is, say to them, O Muhammad: So flee to God by repenting from your sins of disbelief and transgressions. The phrase Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner is an explanation for the command to flee. It was said that the meaning of So flee to God is leave Mecca. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Beware of everything other than God, for whoever flees to anything other than Him cannot avoid it. It was said that they fled from obeying Satan to obeying the Most Merciful, and it was said that they fled from ignorance to knowledge. The meaning of Indeed, I am to you from Him is that from Him, a clear warner.
51:51: 51- And do not associate with God another god. He forbade them from associating partners with God after commanding them to flee to God. The phrase Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner is an explanation for the prohibition.
51:52: 52- Likewise, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, ‘A magician or a madman.’ This is a consolation for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), explaining that this was the way of previous nations, and that what happened from the Arabs of denying the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and describing him as magic or madness had happened to those who came before them with their messengers. Likewise is in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning, the matter is thus. Then he explained what he summarized by saying: What came etc., or it is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source: meaning, I warn you with a warning like the warning of the messengers who came before me who warned their people, and the first is more appropriate.
51:53: 53- They enjoined it upon one another The question is for rebuke, rebuke and astonishment at their state: that is, did the first of them enjoin the last of them to deny and did they follow suit? Rather, they are a transgressing people A diversion from the enjoining to what brought them together in transgression: that is, they did not enjoin it upon one another, rather transgression brought them together, which is exceeding the limit in disbelief.
51:54: Then God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn away from them, saying: 54- Then turn away from them, meaning turn away from them and refrain from arguing with them and calling them to the truth, for you have done what God commanded you to do and conveyed His message. So you will not be blamed before God after this, because you have done what was required of you. This was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
51:55: Then when He ordered him to turn away from them, He ordered him not to abandon the reminder and the admonition in the best way, saying: 55- And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is, admonish with the Qur'an whoever among your people has believed, for the reminder benefits them. Muqatil said: Admonish the disbelievers of Mecca, for the reminder benefits whoever God knows will believe. It was also said that He reminded them of the punishment and the days of God, and He singled out the believers for the reminder because they are the ones who will benefit from it.
51:56: Paragraph 56 - "And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me" is a resumption of what preceded it, because their creation merely for worship is something that motivates the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to remind and motivates them to respond. It was said that this is specific to those whom God, the Exalted, knew would worship Him previously, so it is a generality intended to be specific. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: This is specific to those who obey Him, meaning from the people of both groups. He said: This is the opinion of Al-Kalbi and Al-Dahhak and the choice of Al-Farra' and Ibn Qutaybah. Al-Qushayri said: The verse is made specific by certainty, because the insane were not commanded to worship Me, nor were they deterred from it. He said: "And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind." And whoever was created for Hell is not among those created for worship. So the verse is interpreted to include the believers among them, and this is indicated by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And I did not create the jinn and mankind from among the believers except to worship Me." Mujahid said: The meaning is: except that they might know Me. Al-Tha'labi said: This is a good statement, because if He had not created them, then His existence and Oneness would not have been known. It was narrated from Mujahid that he said: The meaning is, "Except to command them and forbid them. This is indicated by His statement, And they were commanded no more than to worship One God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him." Az-Zajjaj preferred this view. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is what they were created with of happiness and misery. So He created the happy ones among the jinn and mankind for worship, and He created the miserable ones for disobedience. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is, "Except to unify Him. As for the believer, he unifies Him in times of hardship and ease, and as for the disbeliever, he unifies Him in times of hardship but not in times of ease, as in His statement, And when waves cover them like canopies, they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion." A group said: Except to submit to Me and humble themselves. The meaning of worship in the language is humiliation, submission, and obedience. Every creature among mankind and jinn is subject to the decree of God, humbled to His will, and obedient to what He has decreed for them. He created them as He willed and provided for them as He decreed. None of them possesses the power to benefit or harm himself. The reason for the jinn being presented before humans here is the precedence of their existence.
51:57: 57- I do not desire from them any provision, nor do I desire that they feed me. This sentence clarifies His independence from His servants, and that He does not desire any benefit from them as masters desire from their slaves. Rather, He is the Absolute Free, the Provider, the Giver. It has been said that the meaning is: I do not desire from them to provide for any of My creation, nor to provide for themselves, nor to feed any of My creation, nor to feed themselves. Rather, He attributed the feeding to Himself because creation is God’s dependents. So whoever feeds God’s dependents is as if He fed Him. This is as mentioned in the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): God says, ‘My servant, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me.’ Meaning, you did not feed My servants. The min in His saying, of provision is redundant to emphasize the generality.
51:58: Then the Almighty made it clear that He is the Provider and no one else, saying: 58- Indeed, it is God who is the Provider. There is no provider other than Him and no giver other than Him. He is the One who provides for His creation and does what is best for them, so they do not occupy themselves with anything other than the worship for which they were created. The Possessor of Strength, the Firm. The raising of al-Mutin is as a description of the Provider, or of the Possessor, or as a predicate of a deleted subject, or as a predicate after a predicate. The majority read al-Razzaq, while Ibn Muhaisin read al-Razzaq. The majority read al-Mutin in the nominative case. Yahya ibn Waththab and al-A’mash read it in the genitive case as a description of strength. The masculine gender is due to its feminine gender not being real. Al-Farra’ said: His right was al-Mutinah, so He mentioned it because he went with it to something twisted and tightly woven. It is said a strong rope, meaning tightly woven. The meaning of al-Mutin here is: very strong.
51:59: 59- For those who have wronged will be sins like the sins of their companions meaning they wronged themselves through disbelief and sins, so they will have sins: meaning long-lasting evil that will not end. The root of sins in the language is the great bucket, and from the use of sins to mean a share of something is the poet’s saying: By your life, death knocks on every son of a father, and among them are sins. What is in the verse is taken from the sharers of water with the big bucket, so it is a metaphor, making sins a substitute for luck and portion. Ibn Qutaybah said, So let them not be impatient meaning let them not ask me to hasten the punishment for them, as in their saying, Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful.
51:60: 60- So woe to those who disbelieve from the Day they are promised. It was said that it is the Day of Resurrection, and it was said that it is the Day of Badr. The fa is to arrange what comes after it based on what comes before it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: With his people. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on his authority, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: With his people. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated it - and he authenticated it - on his authority, on the authority of, The barren wind, he said: The strong wind that does not fertilize anything. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority, he said: It does not fertilize the trees nor stir up the clouds. And on the authority of, Except it makes them like ashes, he said: Like a perishing thing. Al-Faryabi and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The barren, catastrophic wind. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of, And the heaven We constructed with power, he said: With strength. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh and Ibn Al-Mundhir on his authority, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of, Then turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed, he said: God commanded him to turn away from them in order to punish them, and he excused Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, then He said: And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers, so it abrogated it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement, And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me, he said: To acknowledge servitude willingly or unwillingly. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: According to what I created them upon of My obedience and disobedience, My misery and My happiness. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat also narrated from him regarding his statement, al-Muttin, he said: The strong. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement, sins, he said: A bucket.
52:1: It is forty-nine verses, and it was said forty-eight It was revealed in Mecca. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion, Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Tur was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Jubayr ibn Mut’im, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite Surat Al-Tur in the Maghrib prayer.” Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, “She heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying beside the House, Surat Al-Tur, and a written book.” His saying: 1- And the Mount Al-Jawhari said: It is the mountain on which God spoke to Moses. Mujahid Al-Suddi said: The Mount in Syriac means mountain, and what is meant by it is Mount Sinai. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: They are two Mounts: One of them is called Mount Sinai, and the other is called Mount Zeitan, because figs and olives grow on them. It was said that it is Mount Madyan, and it was said that the Mount is every mountain that grows, and that which does not grow is not a Mount. God Almighty swore by this mountain to honor and glorify it.
52:2: 2- And a written book. The written book means the one written. What is meant by the book is the Qur’an. It was also said that it is the Preserved Tablet. It was also said that it is all the revealed books. It was also said that it is the Tablets of Moses. It was also said that it is what the guardians write. This was said by Al-Farra’ and others. Similar to it is And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread out. And His statement: And when the pages are spread out.
52:3: 3- On spread parchment is related to mustawur: meaning written on parchment. The majority read on parchment with a fatha on the ra', while Abu Al-Sammak read it with a kasra. Al-Jawhari said: Parchment with a fatha is what is written on, and it is thin leather. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: On spread parchment. Al-Mubarrad said: Parchment is what is thin of leather for writing on, and spread out. Abu Ubaidah said: Its plural is raquq. From this is the saying of Al-Mutalammiss: It is as if she is from the past, and her book is written As for slavery with the kasra, it refers to the slave. It is said, Abd Raq and Abd Marquq.
52:4: 4- And the Frequented House is in the seventh heaven. It was said that it is in the lowest heaven, and it was said that it is the Kaaba. According to the first two opinions, its description as being inhabited is based on the angels who enter it and worship God there. According to the third opinion, its description as being inhabited is literal or metaphorical based on the large number of people who worship there.
52:5: 5- And the raised ceiling means the sky. He called it a ceiling because it is like the ceiling of the earth. From this is His saying, And We made the sky a protected ceiling. It was said that it is the throne.
52:6: 6- And the sea which is set ablaze means lit, from the root word sajar which means igniting fire in the light, and from it His statement: And when the seas are set ablaze It has been narrated that the seas will be set ablaze on the Day of Resurrection and will be fire, and it has been said that masjur means filled, and it has been said that it is one of the names of opposites, it is said sajur sea means full, and sajur sea means empty, and it has been said that masjur is held, and from it is the word sajur al-dog, because it holds it. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: masjur is the one whose water has gone, and it has been said that masjur is the one which is set ablaze, and from it and when the seas are set ablaze", and Al-Rabi' bin Anas said: It is the one in which fresh water is mixed with salty water. The first is more appropriate, and this is what Mujahid, Al-Dahhak, Muhammad bin Ka'b, Al-Akhfash and others said.
52:7: 7- The punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. This is the answer to the oath: that is, it will inevitably happen to whoever deserves it.
52:8: 8- There is none to repel him that repels him and turns him away from the people of Hellfire. This sentence is a second predicate of in, or an attribute of a reality, and min is an additional word for emphasis. The reason for singling out these matters for oaths is that they are great and indicate the perfection of divine power.
52:9: 9- The Day the sky will sway violently The agent in the circumstance is actual: meaning that it will happen on this day, and the agent in it may be driver. And al-mawr: disturbance and movement. Linguists said: Mara yamu'ran means that something moved, came and went. Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubaidah said this: And he recited the verse of Al-A'sha: Her walk from her neighbor's house was like the walk of a cloud, neither slowing down nor hurrying up. There is nothing in the verse that indicates what they said, unless this gait mentioned in the verse is called al-mur in the language. Ad-Dahhak said: Some of it surges into others. Mujahid said: It revolves around. It was also said that it runs. From this is the saying of the poet: The blood of the dead is still flowing in the Tigris until the water of the Tigris becomes cloudy.
