The word mawr means wave, and from this comes the word mawwara al-yad, meaning a fast-moving camel that glides like waves. The meaning of the verse is that the punishment will befall the disobedient and nothing will avert it from them on this day when the sky will be like this, which is the Day of Resurrection. It has also been said that the sky here refers to the heavens, and mawra means the disorder of its systems and the unevenness of its path.
52:10: 10- And the mountains will move meaning they will move from their places and depart from their locations like the movement of clouds and will become scattered dust. It has been said that the reason for emphasizing the two verbs with the infinitive that indicates their strangeness and departure from the norm, and the explanation of this has been presented in Surat Al-Kahf.
52:11: 11- So woe on that Day to the deniers. Woe is a word said to someone who is doomed, and it is the name of a valley in Hell. The letter fa was added because the statement has the meaning of retribution: that is, if what was mentioned about the rising of the sky and the movement of the mountains occurs, then woe to them.
52:12: Then He described the deniers by saying: 12- Those who are engaged in idle talk and playing. That is, they are hesitating about falsehood and rushing into it, playing around, not remembering to be accounted for nor fearing punishment. The meaning is that they are engaging in the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by denying and mocking him. It was also said that they are engaging in worldly matters and turning away from the Hereafter.
52:13: 13- The Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, summoned. To summon means to push violently and harshly: it is said, I called him, I called him, I pushed him, meaning, they will be pushed into the Fire with a violent and severe push. Muqatil said: Their hands will be chained to their necks and their forelocks will be gathered to their feet, then they will be pushed into Hell on their faces. The majority of recited the Quran with a fatha on the dal and a shaddah on the 'ayn. Ali, As-Salami, Abu Raja', Zayd ibn Ali and Ibn As-Samee' recited it with a sukoon on the dal and a light, open 'ayn: meaning, they will be called to the Fire from the supplication. And Day is either a substitute for Day of Dates, or related to the implied statement in the sentence after this one.
52:14: And it is 14- This is the fire which you used to deny. That is, they will be told that on the day when they are summoned to the fire of Hell. That is, this fire which you see is the fire which you used to deny in this world, and the one who says this to them are the keepers of the fire.
52:15: Then He, glory be to Him, rebuked them or commanded His angels to rebuke them, saying: 15- Is this that you see and witness bewitched, as you used to say about God’s sent messengers and His revealed books. The report here precedes the subject because it is the one about whom the question was made and to whom the rebuke was directed. Or do you not see? That is, are you blind to this as you were blind to the truth in this world?
52:16: 16- "Enter it and be patient or do not be patient" meaning if you cannot deny it and you are certain that it is not magic and there is no defect in your eyesight, then now enter it and experience its severity and be patient with the punishment or do not be patient and do what you want, for both matters are "the same for you" in that they are of no benefit. It was also said that the angels say this to them, and "whether" is the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning the two matters are the same, and it is possible for it to be a subject and the predicate deleted: meaning it is the same for you whether you are patient or not, and the phrase "You are only recompensed for what you used to do" is an explanation for the equality, for if the recompense for the work is inevitable then patience and lack thereof are the same.
52:17: 17- Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and bliss. When God Almighty finished mentioning the state of the criminals, He mentioned the state of the righteous. This sentence may be a new sentence, or it may be part of what is said to the disbelievers to increase their grief and regret. The tanween in gardens and bliss is for emphasis.
52:18: 18- Enjoying what their Lord has given them. It is said that a man is fakih, meaning he has fruits, as was said about Ibn Watamir. The meaning is that they are people of fruits from the fruits of Paradise, and it was said that they are people of comfort and enjoyment with what they have of what God Almighty has given them, which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. The meaning of this has been explained previously. The majority read fakihin with an alif and the accusative as a state. Khalid read fakihun in the nominative case as a predicate after a predicate. Ibn Abbas read fakihin without an alif. Fakah means good-naturedness, as mentioned previously in ad-Dukhan, and it is said of evil and arrogance. It is not appropriate to interpret it this way here. And their Lord saved them from the punishment of Hellfire is conjoined with gave them, or as a predicate of in, or the sentence is in the accusative case as a state with the omission of qad.
52:19: 19- Eat and drink at ease meaning that will be said to them. Enjoyment is that which is not marred by bitterness, sorrow, or turbidity. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, may you be happy with what you have reached at ease. The meaning is: Eat at ease and drink at ease. The explanation of enjoyment has already been given in Surat An-Nisa. It has also been said that the meaning of enjoyment is that you will not die.
52:20: 20- Reclining on lined-up couches is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of eat, or of the object of ataathahum, or of the object of waqahum, or of the passive participle implied in the adverbial phrase, or of the pronoun in fakihin. The majority read on couches with a damma on the first ra'. Abu al-Sammak read it with a fatha. The couches are the plural of bed. The lined-up ones are the ones connected to each other until they become a row. And We married them to beautiful, wide-eyed maidens means We coupled them with them. Yunus ibn Habib said: The Arabs say He married him to a woman and He married him to a woman, but it is not in the speech of the Arabs to marry him to a woman. He said: And the statement of God the Most High: And We married them to beautiful, wide-eyed maidens means We coupled them with them. Al-Farra' said: Married him to a woman is the language of Azdashnu'ah. The interpretation of beautiful, wide-eyed maidens has been presented in Surat al-Dukhan. The majority read beautiful, wide-eyed maidens without an addition. Ikrimah read it by adding beautiful maidens to wide-eyed maidens. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And Al-Tur he said: A mountain. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Kathir ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Awf, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: At-Tur is a mountain among the mountains of Paradise. Kathir is very weak. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On an unrolled scroll, he said: In the book. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The Frequented House is in the seventh heaven. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day and do not return to it until you say the Hour.” In the two Sahihs and others, it is stated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the hadith of the Night Journey after passing through the seventh heaven: Then he was taken up to the Frequented House, and behold, seventy thousand angels enter it every day and do not return to it. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn al-Anbari narrated in al-Masahif on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about the Ka'ba al-Ma'ma'. He said: "That is a house above the seven heavens, beneath the sky. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and they never return to it again until the Day of Resurrection." Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: "The Ka'ba al-Ma'ma' is opposite the Ka'ba. If anything were to fall from it, it would fall on top of it. Seventy thousand pray in it every day, and they would never return to it again." At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas, but al-Suyuti deemed its chain of transmission weak. Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azmah, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding His statement: And the raised ceiling, he said: The sky. Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding His statement: And the sealed sea, he said: A sea in the sky beneath the Throne. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Ibn Umar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The imprisoned is the one who is detained. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him, who said: The imprisoned is the one who is sent. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, On the Day the sky will shake with a shake, he said: It will move. Concerning His statement, On the Day they are summoned, he said: They will be pushed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, On the Day they are summoned, ‘To the Fire of Hell will it be pushed around their necks until they return to the Fire.’ Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, regarding His statement, Eat and drink at ease, meaning: You will not die in it. Then they said: Then will we not die * Except our first death, and we will not be punished?
52:21: When the Almighty finished mentioning the people of Paradise in general, He mentioned the state of a group of them in particular, saying: 21- And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring. The relative pronoun is the subject, and its predicate is We will join with them their offspring. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case by an implied verb: i.e., We honored those who believed, and We will join could be an explanation of this implied verb. The majority of scholars read and We followed them by attributing the action to the offspring. Abu Amr read we followed them by attributing the action to the speaker, like His saying we joined. The majority of scholars read their offspring in the singular. Ibn Amir, Abu Amr, and Ya’qub read it in the plural, except that Abu Amr read it in the accusative case as the object because he read and We followed them. This plural reading was reported from Nafi’, and the well-known one from him is like the reading of the majority of scholars. The majority of scholars read we joined with them their offspring in the singular. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, Abu 'Umur, and Ya'qub read it in the plural, and the phrase and their offspring followed them is conjoined with believed or parenthetical, and with faith is related to following. The meaning of this verse is that God, the Exalted, raises the offspring of the believer to Himself, even if they are lower than him in deeds, so that His eyes may be comforted and His soul may be content, on the condition that they are believers. This is specific to those offspring who are characterized by faith, and they are the adults, not the children. Even if they are related to their fathers, it is based on evidence other than this verse. It was said that offspring refers to adults and children, as is the linguistic meaning. Thus, the young and old offspring of the believers are related to the believing fathers. His statement, with faith is in the accusative case as a state, meaning, with the faith of the fathers. It was said that the pronoun in with them refers to the offspring mentioned first, meaning, We included them with the offspring who follow their fathers through the faith of their offspring. It was said that those who believed are only the Muhajireen and Ansar, and the apparent meaning of the verse is general, and it does not necessitate that it be limited to the Muhajireen and Ansar, since they were the reason for its revelation, if that is correct. Rather, the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds. The majority of scholars read the verse with a fat-ha on the lam of alatna, while Ibn Kathir read it with a kasra: meaning, And We did not deprive the fathers of anything of the reward for their deeds by including their offspring with them. The pronoun of the object refers to those who believed. It was also said that the meaning is: And We did not deprive the offspring of anything of their deeds due to their short lives. The former is more appropriate, and we have already explained the meaning of alatah and alatuhu in Surat Al-Hujurat. Ibn Hurmuz read alatnahum with a long vowel, which is linguistically. He said in As-Sahah: It is said that he did not deprive him of a year, and that every person is mortgaged by his deeds. If he does them in the manner commanded by God, He will release him, otherwise He will destroy him. It was also said that it means between, and the meaning is: Every person is permanently and permanently responsible for what he has earned. It was also said that this is specific to the disbelievers, based on the verse: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right hand.
52:22: Then the Almighty mentioned the goodness He provided them with, saying: 22- And We provided them with fruits and meat of whatever they desired. That is, We increased the bliss they had with various fruits and meat of whatever their souls desired and found delicious.
52:23: 23- They will dispute over a cup therein meaning they will share and take a cup. A cup is a vessel of wine, and it is applied to any vessel filled with wine or other things. When it is empty, it is no longer called a cup. There is no idle talk therein and no sin therein. Al-Zajjaj said: Nothing idle will occur between them and there is no sin in them, as occurs between those who drink wine in this world. Sin is a verbal noun from sin, and the pronoun in therein refers to the cup. It was also said: There is no idle talk therein: meaning in Paradise and nothing sinful will occur therein, but the former is more correct. Ibn Qutaybah said: Their minds will not be taken away, so they will engage in idle talk, as occurs with the wine of this world, and nothing will occur from them that will cause them sin. Ad-Dahhak said: There is no sin: meaning no lying. The majority of scholars read There is no idle talk therein and no sin with the nominative case and the tanween in both. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaisin read them with the fat-ha without the tanween. Qatadah said: Idle talk is falsehood. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: There is no excess therein. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: There is no obscenity in it. Ibn Zayd said: There is no cursing or quarreling in it. The sentence is in the accusative case as a description of a cup.
52:24: 24- And there will circulate among them their young boys meaning they will circulate among them with cups, fruits, food, and other things as their servants. It was also said that their children are as if in beauty and splendor they were hidden pearls meaning hidden and protected in shells, untouched by hands. Al-Kisa’i said: Kannat al-shay’ means to cover and safeguard it from the sun, and akannatuhu means to put it in a kanaan shelter, and from this comes kanaantu the girl and kanaantuhu hermit, so she is kanaan hidden.
52:25: 25- And some of them will turn to others, asking one another. That is, some of them will ask one another in Paradise about their condition, and what they were in of worldly toil and fear of the consequences. They will praise God who removed from them sadness, fear, and worry, and the toil and misery they were in while seeking a living and obtaining the necessary provisions. It was said that some of them will say to one another: How did you reach this exalted station? It was also said that the questioning among them will be upon the resurrection from the graves. The first is more appropriate, as the context indicates that they have reached Paradise.
52:26: The sentence: 26- They said, ‘Indeed, we were before among our families, fearful’ is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said: What did some of them say to each other when questioning? So it was said: They said, ‘Indeed, we were before’: meaning before the Hereafter, and that was in this world among our families, fearful and apprehensive of God’s punishment, or we were afraid of disobeying God.
52:27: 27- So God bestowed His favor upon us with forgiveness and mercy or with success in obeying Him and saved us from the punishment of the poisonous winds meaning the punishment of Hell. Poisons are one of the names of Hell, as al-Hasan and Muqatil said. Al-Kalbi and Abu Ubaidah said: It is the punishment of the Fire. Al-Zajjaj said: The poisonous winds of Hell are what is found of its heat. Abu Ubaidah said: The poisonous winds are during the day, and it may be at night, and the heat is during the night, and it may be during the day. Poisons are sometimes used to mean the scorching cold, and the scorching sun and heat more, and from this is the saying of the poet: Today is a cold day, its poisons are from the panic of the day, so I do not blame him It is said that the wind is called poison because it enters the pores.
52:28: 28- Indeed, before, we used to call upon Him meaning we used to worship God alone and ask Him: or we used to ask Him to bestow upon us forgiveness and mercy Indeed, He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful. The majority of scholars read it with a kasra over the hamza as a new sentence, while Nafi’ and Al-Kisa’i read it with a fatha over it: meaning because He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful, and it was said that He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful to His servants.
52:29: 29- So remember, for you are not, by the grace of your Lord, a soothsayer or a madman. That is, persist in your preaching and reminding. The preposition ba is related to an omitted word, which is the state: that is, you are not mingled with the grace of your Lord that He bestowed upon you of sound mind and prophethood as a soothsayer or a madman. It was also said that it is related to an omitted word indicated by the speech: that is, you are not, when you remember the grace of your Lord, as a soothsayer or a madman. It was also said that the preposition ba is causal and related to the content of the negative sentence, and the meaning is: soothsaying and madness were removed from you because of the grace of God upon you, just as you say, I am not in difficulty, by the praise of God. It was also said that the preposition ba is for the oath, between the name of ma and its predicate, and the meaning is: you are not, by the grace of God, a soothsayer or a madman. The soothsayer is the one who gives the impression that he knows the unseen without revelation: that is, what you say is not like a soothsayer, for you only speak the revelation that God has commanded you to convey. The purpose of the verse is to refute what the polytheists were saying: that he was a soothsayer or a madman.
52:30: 30- Or do they say, 'A poet, we are waiting for him to be struck by a calamity of fate'? Or is it the disconnected form, and the dispute has already been presented as to whether it is understood by bal and the hamza, or by bal alone. Al-Khalil said: It is here for questioning. Sibawayh said: The servants were addressed with what happened in their speech. Al-Nahhas said: Sibawayh means that am in the speech of the Arabs is to move from one speech to another, and we are waiting is in the nominative case as an attribute of poet, and the calamity of fate is the vicissitudes of time, and the meaning is: We await for him the events of the days so that he dies as others died, or perishes as those before him perished, and al-manun can mean time, and it can mean fate. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is we are waiting for the calamity of fate, so he deleted the preposition, as you say: I intended Zayd and I intended Zayd, and from this is the saying of the poet: Death is waiting for her, perhaps she will divorce him one day or her lover will die And the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb al-Hudhali: Death and its uncertainties are painful, and time does not forgive those who are impatient. Al-Asma'i said: Al-Manun is singular and has no plural. Al-Farra' said: It can be singular or plural. Al-Akhfash said: It is plural and has no singular.
52:31: Then the Almighty commanded him to answer them, saying: 31- Say, ‘Wait, for I am with you among those who wait.’ That is, await my death or destruction, for I am with you among those who wait for your death or destruction. The majority of scholars read we wait by attributing the verb to a group of speakers. Zayd ibn Ali read it in the passive form.
52:32: 32- Or do their dreams command them to do this? That is, rather, do their minds command them to say this contradictory statement, that the soothsayer is the one who is excessively shrewd and intelligent, and the madman is the one who has lost his mind, let alone being shrewd and intelligent. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said that the leaders of Quraysh were described as having dreams and intelligence, so God destroyed their dreams when they did not bear fruit in distinguishing truth from falsehood. Or are they a transgressing people? That is, rather, they transgressed and exceeded the limit in stubbornness, so they said what they said. These changes from one thing to another with the question, as is the meaning of the disjunctive am, indicate that what follows it is more heinous than what preceded it, and more audacious and stubborn.
52:33: 33- Or do they say that you fabricate it? That is, he fabricated the Qur’an on his own and made it up. The word taqawul is usually only used to mean lying, even though its root is to force a statement. From this comes the word iqtala he fought against him, and it is said iqtala he fought against him, meaning to judge him. From this comes the poet’s saying: And a position in the house of truth and happiness, and he did not fight in the judgment of Ali, the doctor Then He, glory be to Him, stopped saying: You say it and moved on to what is more heinous to them, saying: Rather, they do not believe. That is, the reason for these contradictory statements coming from them is that they are infidels who do not believe in God and do not believe in what His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought.
52:34: Then He, the Most High, challenged them and obligated them to present the proof, saying: 34- Then let them produce a statement like it, meaning like the Qur’an in its organization, beautiful expression, and wonderful style, if they are truthful, in what they claimed of their saying that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it and brought it from his own side, even though it is Arabic speech, and they are the leaders of the Arabs and their most eloquent and the practitioners of all Arabic styles of poetry and prose. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Hannad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God will raise the offspring of the believer with him in his rank in Paradise, even if they are below him in deeds, so that his eyes may be comforted by them. Then he recited: And those who have believed and whose offspring follow them 1:17. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "When a man enters Paradise, he will be asked about his parents, his wife, and his children. It will be said that they have not reached your rank and deeds. He will say: 'O Lord, you have worked for me and for them.' He will be ordered to join them with him." Ibn Abbas recited: And those who have believed and whose offspring follow them 1:17. Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa'id al-Musnad on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The believers and their children will be in Paradise, and the polytheists and their children will be in Hellfire. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: And those who have believed 1:17. Its chain of transmission is as follows. Abdullah bin Ahmad said: Uthman bin Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Muhammad bin Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Uthman, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, who said: “Khadijah asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about two of her sons who died during the pre-Islamic era. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘They are in Hell.’ When he saw the dislike on her face, he said: ‘If you saw where they were, you would hate them.’ She said: ‘O Messenger of God, my sons are from you.’ He said: ‘In Paradise.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The believers and their children are in Paradise, and the polytheists and their children are in Hell.’ Then he recited: ‘And those who believe’” the verse. Imam Ahmad said in Al-Musnad: Yazid narrated to us, Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najud, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God raises the status of a righteous servant in Paradise, and he says: ‘O Lord, from where did I get this?’ He says: ‘Because of your son’s supplication for forgiveness for you.’” Its chain of transmission is authentic. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We did not deprive them, meaning, We did not diminish them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, There is no idle talk therein, meaning, falsehood, nor sin, meaning, a lie. Al-Bazzar narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they will yearn for their brothers. Then one of them will come to the bed of another and they will talk, one of them will lean on his back and the other will lean on his back, and they will talk about what they did in the world. Then one of them will say: O so-and-so, do you know what day God forgave us? The day we were in such-and-such a place, and we supplicated to God, and He forgave us.” Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: If God opened upon the people of the earth a poisonous torment the size of a fingertip, He would burn the earth and everyone on it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Indeed, He is the Most Barrier, he said: The Most Kind. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that when the Quraysh gathered at Dar al-Nadwa regarding the matter of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), one of them said, “Keep him in chains and await his death until he perishes as the poets before him perished, such as Zuhair and al-Nabigha. He is like one of them.” So God revealed concerning that, Or do they say, ‘He is a poet; we await for him a misfortune of fate.’ Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, The misfortune of fate, he said, Death.
52:35: His saying: 35- "Or were they created from nothing? This am" is the disjunctive particle, as mentioned before it, and as will come in what follows it: meaning, rather, they were created in this wondrous manner and amazing craftsmanship without a Creator for them. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, they were created in vain for nothing, they are not held accountable, nor are they commanded or forbidden, and he made "min in the sense of lam". Ibn Kaysan said: Or were they created in vain and left aimlessly, they are not commanded or forbidden. It was said that the meaning is: Or were they created without a father or mother, so they are like inanimate objects, they do not understand, and no proof can be established against them. "Or are they the creators?" meaning, do they say that they are the creators of themselves, so they are not commanded or forbidden, even though they acknowledge that God is their Creator, and if they acknowledge it, then the proof is binding on them.
52:36: 36- Or did they create the heavens and the earth? and they do not claim that, so the argument is binding on them. For this reason, he turned away from this and said, Rather, they are not certain, meaning they are not certain of the matter, rather they stumble in the darkness of doubt regarding God’s promise and threat.
52:37: 37- Or do they have the treasures of your Lord? That is, the treasures of the provisions of His servants. It was also said that it means the keys to His mercy. Muqatil said: He says: Do they have the keys to Your Lord with the message, so that they can place them wherever they wish? And this is what Ikrimah said. Al-Kalbi said: The treasures of rain and provisions. Or are they the ones in control? That is, the ones who are in control and the tyrants. It is said in As-Sahah: “The one who is in control is the one who has control over something to supervise it, oversee its affairs, and record its deeds. Its origin is from “satra” because the writer writes. Abu Ubaidah said: You have taken me as your servant. The majority of scholars read Al-Musaytarun with a pure sad. Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Mujahid, Qanbal, and Hisham read it with a pure sin. This reading was narrated from Hafs. Khallad read it with a sad with a zaya.
52:38: 38- Or do they have a ladder by which they listen? That is, do they say that they have a ladder erected to the heaven by which they ascend and listen to the speech of the angels and what is revealed to them and by which they attain knowledge of the unseen, just as Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, attained it through revelation? His statement therein is an attribute of ladder, and it is a circumstantial noun in its proper form. It was also said that it means on, meaning that they listen on it, like His statement, And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, as Al-Akhfash said. Abu Ubaidah said: They listen to it. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that they are like Gabriel who brings revelation to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said that it is in the accusative case as a state, meaning that they ascend on it. Then let their listener bring, if he claims that, a clear authority, meaning a clear and apparent argument.
52:39: 39- Or does He have daughters and you have sons? That is, do you say that God has daughters and you have sons? He, glory be to Him, has made their dreams foolish, led their minds astray and rebuked them. That is, do they attribute daughters to God, even though they are the weaker of the two categories, and attribute sons to themselves, even though they are the superior of the two? This indicates that whoever holds this opinion is in a lowly position in terms of understanding and reason, so it is not unlikely that he will deny the resurrection and reject monotheism.
52:40: Then the Almighty returned to the words of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: 40- Or do you ask them for a reward? That is, rather, do you ask them for a reward that they should pay you for conveying the message? They are burdened with a heavy fine. That is, from the obligation of a fine that you demand of them, they are burdened with the burden of that heavy fine. Qatada said: He is saying: Did you ask these people for a reward that would exhaust them so that they are unable to accept Islam?
52:41: 41- Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write. That is, do they claim to have knowledge of the unseen, which is what is in the Preserved Tablet, so they write down for people whatever they want of knowledge of the unseen? Qatada said: This is an answer to their saying: We await for him a misfortune of time. God says: Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, such that they know that Muhammad will die before them, so they write? Ibn Qutaybah said: The meaning of they write is that they rule by what they say.
52:42: 42- Or do they intend a plan meaning a plot against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they destroy him with that plot. Then those who disbelieve are the ones who are plotted against meaning the ones who are plotted against and who will be rewarded for their plot, so the harm of their plot will come back to them. And the evil plan does not encompass except its own people God killed them on the Day of Badr and humiliated them in more than one place, and He, glory be to Him, plotted against them. And they plotted, and God plotted, and God is the best of planners.
52:43: 43- Or do they have a god other than God? That is, they claim that they have a god other than God who protects them, provides for them, and grants them victory. Then, the Almighty cleared Himself of this heinous statement, saying: Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him. That is, above their association with Him, or above those whom they make partners with Him.
52:44: Then the Almighty mentioned some of their ignorance, saying: 44- And if they see a fragment of the sky falling upon them, they say, ‘It is a piled-up cloud.’ Kasf is the plural of kusfa, which is a piece of something. The word saqatan is in the accusative case as a state, or as the second object. Markum is that which is placed one on top of the other. The meaning is that if they see a fragment of the sky falling upon them as a punishment for them, they will not desist from their disbelief, but rather they will say, ‘It is a piled-up cloud, one on top of the other.’ The difference of the reciters regarding kusfān has already been mentioned. Al-Akhfash said: Whoever reads kasfan, meaning with a kasra on the kaf and a sukoon on the seen, makes it singular. Whoever reads kasfan, meaning with a kasra on the kaf and a fatha on the seen, makes it plural.
52:45: Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to leave them alone, saying: 45- So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck dead. That is, leave them alone and let them alone until they meet the day of their death, or the day they will be killed at Badr, or the Day of Resurrection. The majority of scholars read they will meet, while Abu Haywah read they will throw down, and the majority of scholars read they will be struck dead in the active form. Ibn Amir and Asim read it in the passive form, and the shock means destruction, as explained above.
52:46: 46- The Day when their plot will not avail them at all is a substitute for their day: meaning that their plot with which they plotted against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this world will not benefit them on that day, nor will they be aided meaning that nothing will prevent the punishment that will befall them, rather it will inevitably befall them.
52:47: 47- And indeed, for those who have wronged is a punishment less than that. That is, for those who wronged themselves through disbelief and sins, there is a punishment in this world less than the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, meaning before it, which is their being killed on the Day of Badr. Ibn Zayd said: It is the calamities of this world, such as pain, illness, and disasters, and the loss of wealth and children. Mujahid said: It is hunger and hardship for seven years. It was also said that it is the punishment of the grave. It was also said that what is meant by the punishment is famine, and by the punishment that comes after it is their being killed on the Day of Badr. But most of them do not know what they will face of God’s punishment and what He has prepared for them in this world and the Hereafter.
52:48: 48- And be patient over the decision of your Lord until the punishment We have promised them befalls them. For indeed, you are before Our eyes meaning, in Our sight and view, and under Our protection and care, so do not worry about them. Al-Zajjaj said: You are where We see you, protect you, and watch over you, but they cannot reach it. And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise meaning, declare your Lord pure from what is not befitting of Him, and praise your Lord for His blessings upon you when you rise from your seat. Ata’, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Sufyan al-Thawri, and Abu al-Ahwas said: He glorifies God when he rises from his seat, saying: Glory be to Him, God, and His praise, or Glory be to You, God, and Your praise when he rises from every seat he sits in. Muhammad ibn Ka’b, al-Dahhak, and al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: When you rise for prayer. Ad-Dahhak said: He says: God is the Greatest, the Greatest, and praise be to God abundantly, and glory be to God morning and evening. This is questionable because the takbir should be said after standing, not while standing, and the tasbih should be said after the takbir, and this is not the meaning of the verse, so the first is more appropriate. It was said that the meaning is: Pray to God when you wake up from your sleep, and Abu al-Jawza’ and Hassan ibn Atiyyah said the same. Al-Kalbi said: And remember God with the tongue when you get up from your bed until the prayer begins, which is the dawn prayer.
52:49: 49- And during part of the night, glorify Him. God, the Exalted, commanded him to glorify Him during some of the night. Muqatil said: That is, pray the Maghrib and Isha prayers. It was also said: the two Rak’ahs of Fajr. And at the setting of the stars. That is, at the time of their setting at the end of the night. It was also said: the Fajr prayer. Ibn Jarir chose this, and it was also said: it is glorification at the end of the prayers. The majority read idbar with a kasra over the hamza as a verbal noun. Salim bin Abi al-Ja’d, Muhammad bin al-Samife’, Ya’qub, and al-Minhal bin Umar read it with a fatha over it as a plural: that is, the ends and ends of the stars: when they set. And dabar al-amr: its end. We have already discussed this in Surah Qaf. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Or are they the ones who control [them]? He said: The ones who are given power. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: Or are they the ones who are sent down? They also narrated on his authority: A punishment less than that? He said: The punishment of the grave before the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Barzah al-Aslami, who said: “When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) stood up from a gathering, he would say: ‘Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.’ A man said: ‘O Messenger of God, you are saying something that you did not say in the past.’ He said: ‘It is expiation for what happens in the gathering.’” Al-Nasa’i and al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-‘Aliyah, on the authority of Rafi’ ibn Khadij, on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever sits in a gathering and engages in idle talk, and says before leaving his seat: ‘Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You,’ whatever happened in that gathering will be forgiven.” Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. There are both isnad and mursal hadiths on this topic. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: And glorify the praises of your Lord when you arise, he said: When you get up from your bed until you enter the prayer. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), regarding the verse: And during part of the night glorify Him, he said: The two rak’ahs before the dawn prayer. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when the stars have set, he said: The two rak’ahs of dawn prayer.
53:1: It is sixty-one verses, and it was said sixty-two verses All of its surahs were revealed in Mecca according to the majority of scholars. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah that it was revealed in Mecca except for one verse, which is the verse: Those who avoid major sins and immoralities. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat An-Najm was revealed in Mecca. He also narrated a similar verse from Ibn Az-Zubayr. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Masoud that he said: Or a surah in which prostration was revealed is An-Najm. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prostrated and all the people prostrated except for a man whom I saw take a handful of dirt and prostrate on it. I later saw him killed as a disbeliever, and he was Umayyah ibn Khalaf. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Masoud that he said: The first surah in which the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited openly was An-Najm. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan that Ibn Umar said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) led us in prayer and recited An-Najm, then he prostrated with us and prolonged his prostration.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited Surat An-Najm and when he reached the verse of prostration, he prostrated therein.” At-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i, At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit who said: I recited Surat An-Najm in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he did not prostrate therein. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to prostrate during Surat An-Najm in Mecca, but when he migrated to Medina, he abandoned it. He also narrated on his authority that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not prostrate during any part of Surat Al-Mufassal since he moved to Medina. His saying 1- And the star when it falls is the definition of the genus, and what is meant is the genus of stars, and this is what a group of commentators said, and from it is the saying of Omar bin Abi Rabi’ah: The best star in the sky is the Pleiades, and the Pleiades on earth are the most beautiful of women. It was said: What is meant by it is the Pleiades. It is a name that is prevalent in it. The Arabs say the star meaning the Pleiades. Mujahid and others said the same. Al-Suddi said: The star here is Venus, because some Arabs used to worship it. It was also said that the star here is the plant that has no stem, as in His statement: And the star and the tree prostrate, as Al-Akhfash said. It was also said that the star is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and it was also said that the star is the Qur’an. It was called a star because it was revealed in stages and in parts. The Arabs call the stages as astrology, and the separated is the astrologer. Mujahid, Al-Farra’ and others said the same, but the first is more appropriate. Al-Hasan said: What is meant by the star is the stars if they fall on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that what is meant by it is the stars by which the devils were stoned. The meaning of its descent is its fall from a height. It is said that the star fell, it falls from a height to a bottom. It was also said that it is its setting, and it was also said that it is its rising. The first is more appropriate, and this is what Al-Asma’i and others said. From it is the saying of Zuhair: Camels walk by it, and it falls like a bucket. The bribe is given to it. It is said that he went on his way, and from this the poet said: While we are in the blackness, the camels are falling fast A thought crossed my heart from remembering you, and I felt weak, so I could not move on. The meaning of al-hawa according to those who interpret the star as the Qur’an is that it descended from above to below. However, according to those who say it is a tree without a stem, or Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the correct meaning of al-hawa does not appear, and the factor in the circumstance is the implied oath verb.
53:2: 2- Your companion has neither strayed nor gone astray. That is, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, has neither strayed from the truth and guidance nor deviated from it. Rich is the opposite of right guidance, that is, he has not gone astray, nor has he spoken falsehood. It has also been said that he has not been disappointed in what he sought. Rich is disappointment, and from this is the saying of the poet: Whoever finds good, people praise him for his actions, and whoever goes astray will not lack someone to blame him for his error. In his saying: Your companion, there is an indication that they are the ones who know the truth about his situation, and the address is to the Quraysh.
53:3: 3- And he does not speak from [his own] inclination meaning that he does not speak from his own desire, neither by the Quran nor anything else. So, the word 'an is in its proper form. Abu Ubaidah said: 'an has the same meaning as the preposition baa, meaning from desire. Qatada said: It means that he does not speak by reading from his own desire.
53:4: 4- It is only a revelation revealed meaning that what he utters is nothing but a revelation from God revealed to him. His saying, revealed is an attribute of revelation that indicates continuous renewal and negates metaphor: that it is a revelation in reality and not just a name.
53:5: 5- He was taught by One of Mighty Power. Powerful is the plural of strength, and the meaning is that he was taught by Gabriel, who is of Mighty Power. This is what most commentators have said, meaning Gabriel. Al-Hasan said: It is God Almighty, but the first is more appropriate and is a case of adding an attribute to the described.
53:6: 6- Of a lifetime and established Al-Mara: strength and intensity in creation, and it was said that he has a healthy body and is free from diseases, and from this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Charity is not permissible for the rich, nor for the one of a healthy lifetime. And it was said that he has a sound mind and a firm opinion. Qatrib said: The Arabs say for everyone who is of sound mind and sound opinion, Of a lifetime, and from this is the saying of the poet: Before I met you, I had a balance for every opponent. The interpretation of the word time is more appropriate, because strength and intensity are indicated by His statement: strong in strength. Al-Jawhari said: Time is one of the four natures, and time is strength and intensity of the mind, and the fa in His statement: He rose up is to connect with His knowledge, meaning Gabriel: that is, He rose and returned to his place in the sky after he had taught Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was said by Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Saeed bin Jubayr. It was said that the meaning of He rose up is that he stood in the form in which God created him, because he used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the form of a human. It was also said that the meaning is that the Qur’an rose up in his chest, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hasan said: He rose up means God Almighty on the Throne.
53:7: 7- And he was on the highest horizon This sentence is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, Gabriel stood up while he was on the highest horizon. What is meant by the highest horizon is the eastern side, which is above the western side. It was also said that it means: He stood up high. The horizon is the side of the sky and its plural is horizons. Qatada and Mujahid said: It is the place from which the sun rises. It was also said that he means Gabriel and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were on the highest horizon on the night of the Ascension. It is possible that this sentence is a new sentence.
53:8: 8- Then he drew near and descended meaning Gabriel drew near after he was at the highest horizon: that is, he came close to the earth, so he descended and came down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the revelation. It has been said that there is a difference in the order of precedence and delay in speech, and the meaning is: Then he descended and drew near, as Ibn al-Anbari and others said. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of drawn near and drawn near is the same: that is, he drew near and increased in nearness, as you say, So-and-so drew near to me and drew near. If you had said, he drew near to me and drew near, it would have been permissible. Al-Farra' said: The fa in fatadala has the same meaning as the waw, and the meaning is: Then Gabriel descended and drew near. However, it is permissible if the meaning of the two verbs is the same, so you can bring whichever one you wish forward. The majority said: The one who drew near and descended is Gabriel. It has also been said that it is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning: His command and judgment drew near to him, but the first is more appropriate. It was said: Whoever said that the one who rose up was Gabriel and Muhammad, then the meaning according to him is: Then Muhammad drew near to his Lord with a dignified drawing near, so he descended: that is, he bowed down in prostration. Ad-Dahhak said the same.
53:9: 9- "So it was two bow lengths or nearer" meaning it was the distance between Gabriel and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Or the distance between Muhammad and his Lord was two bow lengths: meaning the distance of two Arabic bows. Qabb and Qayb, Qad and Qayd: the amount, their meaning is mentioned in As-Sahih. Az-Zajjaj said: meaning according to what you estimate, and God, the Almighty, knows the measures of things, but He addresses us according to what is customary among us. It was said that or has the meaning of waw: meaning and nearer, and it was said that it means rather: meaning rather closer. Saeed bin Jubair, Ata', Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani and Abu Wa'il Shaqiq bin Salamah said, "So it was two bow lengths" means two cubits, and the qaw is the cubit by which everything is measured, and it is the language of some of the Hijazis, and it was said that it is the language of Azd Shanu'a. Al-Kisa'i said: So it was two bow lengths meaning one bow.
53:10: 10- Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed meaning, Gabriel revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, what He revealed. This emphasizes the revelation that was revealed to him. Revelation means throwing something quickly, and from it comes the word waha which means speed. The pronoun in his servant refers to God, as in His statement, He did not leave on its back any creature. It was also said that the meaning is: Then God revealed to His servant Gabriel what He revealed. Al-Rabi', Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd, and Qatadah said the first. It was also said that God revealed to His servant Muhammad. It was said that God Almighty has made vague what Gabriel revealed to Muhammad, or what God revealed to His servant Gabriel or to Muhammad, and He did not make it clear to us, so it is not for us to attempt to interpret it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: What was revealed to him is, Have We not expanded your breast for you? etc., and Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? etc. It was said that God revealed to him that Paradise is forbidden to the prophets until you enter it, and to the nations until your nation enters it. It was said that the word ma indicates generality, not vagueness, and that what is meant is everything that was revealed to him, and interpreting it as vague is more appropriate because of the glorification it contains. The heart did not lie about what it saw meaning the heart of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not lie about what his eyes saw on the Night of Ascension. It is said that he lied to him if he told him a lie and the person did not believe him. Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning of the verse is that he saw something and believed it.
53:11: The majority read 11- Ma Kadhdhab with a lightened vowel. Hisham and Abu Jaafar read it with a shaddah. Ma in Ma Ra'a is a relative pronoun or a verbal noun in the accusative case with Khadhb with a lightened and shaddah.
53:12: 12- Do you find him arguing with you about what he sees? The majority read Aftamarunuh with an alif from mumaraat, which means argument and debate. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read Aftamarunuh with a fatha on the ta' and a sukoon on the meem, meaning do you find him? Abu Ubaid chose the second reading. He said: Because they did not argue with him, but rather denied him. It is said: He showed him his right, meaning he denied it. And I showed him my right: I denied it. He said: And from this is the saying of the poet: Because I satirized a brother who was honest and generous. I passed by a brother who was not generous. That is, you denied it. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said that he denied his right or his morals, meaning if he prevented him from it and pushed him away from it. It is said that upon means from. Ibn Mas’ud, Al-Sha’bi, Mujahid, and Al-A’raj read it with a damma on the ta’ of amrayt, meaning do you doubt him and suspect him? A group of commentators said: The meaning, according to the reading of the majority, is do you argue with him? This is because they argued with him when he was taken on the Night Journey and they said: Describe to us the mosque of Jerusalem, meaning do you argue with him with an argument that aims to push him away from what he saw and knew?
53:13: The lam in His statement: 13- And he saw him on another descent is the particle that introduces the oath: meaning, by God, he saw him on another descent. The descent is a time from the descent, so its accusative is in the adverbial case or in the accusative case as a verbal noun in the position of a state: meaning, he saw Gabriel descending on another descent, or as an attribute of a deleted confirmed verbal noun: meaning, he saw him on another vision. The majority of commentators said: The meaning is that Muhammad saw Gabriel on another time, and it was said that Muhammad saw his Lord on another time with his heart.
53:14: 14- At the Lote Tree of the Limit The adverbial phrase is in the accusative case, and the Lote Tree is the Nabq tree. This Lote Tree is in the sixth heaven as in the Sahih. It was narrated that it is in the seventh heaven. The Limit is the place of ending, or it is a verbal noun with a mim, and what is meant by it is ending itself. It was said that the knowledge of creation ends at it and none of them knows what is beyond it. It was also said that what ascends from the earth ends at it. It was also said that the knowledge of creation ends and none of them knows what is beyond it. It was also said that what ascends from the earth ends at it. It was also said that the souls of the martyrs end at it. Others were said. Adding the tree to the Limit is like adding something to its place.
53:15: 15- Near it is the Garden of Refuge meaning near that lote tree there is a garden known as the Garden of Refuge, and it was called the Garden of Refuge because Adam was the first to go to it, and it was said that it is where the souls of the believers take refuge. The majority read Jannah by raising Jannah as the subject and its predicate as the adverbial phrase that precedes it. Ali, Abu Darda, Abu Hurairah, Ibn Az-Zubayr, Anas, Zar bin Hubaish, Muhammad bin Kaab, Mujahid and Abu Sabra Al-Juhani read Jannah as a past tense verb from jannah yajnun, meaning he was sheltered by God during the night, or the covering of God's sheltering him. Al-Akhfash said: He overtook him as you say the night covered him, meaning it covered him and overtook him. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state.
53:16: 16- "When that which covers the lote tree covers" The verb in the adverbial phrase also saw it, and it is an adverbial of time, and what preceded it is an adverbial of place, and covering means covering and concealing, and it means coming, it is said: So-and-so covers me every time, meaning he came to me, and in the ambiguity in his saying: "that which covers" there is an emphasis that is not hidden, and it was said that locusts of gold cover it, and it was said that it was groups of angels. Mujahid said: A green flutter, and it was said that it was a flutter of green birds, and it was said that it was covered by the command of God, and the use of the present tense to narrate the past situation is to evoke the beautiful image, or to indicate the continuous renewal.
53:17: 17- The sight did not swerve meaning the sight of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not deviate from what he saw. And it did not go beyond meaning it did not go beyond what he saw. This describes the Prophet’s etiquette, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that situation, as he did not turn around, did not swerve his sight, and did not extend it to anything other than what he saw. It was said that he did not go beyond what he was commanded to do.
53:18: 18- He saw of the greatest signs of his Lord meaning, by God, he saw that night of the great signs of his Lord that cannot be described. It was said that he saw a fluttering cloud that filled the horizon, and it was said that he saw Gabriel in a green garment that filled the space between the heaven and the earth, and he had six hundred wings, as is stated in Sahih Muslim and others. Ad-Dahhak said: He saw the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and it was said that it is everything that he saw that night during his journey and his return, and min is for partiality and is the object of saw the greatest, and it is possible that the object is omitted, meaning that he saw something great of the signs of his Lord, and it is possible that min is redundant.
53:19: 19- Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza?
53:20: 20- Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? When God, the Exalted, related these stories, He said to the polytheists, rebuking and censuring them, Have you considered? That is, tell me about the deities that you worship besides God. Do they have any power that can be described? Have they revealed anything to you as God revealed to Muhammad, or are they inanimate objects that do not reason or benefit? Then He mentioned these three idols that were famous among the Arabs and their great belief in them. Al-Wahidi and others said: They derived names for them from the names of God, so they said Al-Lat, and Al-Uzza, which is the feminine of Al-Azz, meaning the honored, and Manat is from Manna the word for God if God decreed something. The majority of scholars read Al-Lat with a soft taa'. It was said that it is derived from the name of God, the Most High, as mentioned above. It was also said that its origin is laat yalita, so the taa' is original. It was also said that it is extra and its origin is lawa yalwa because they used to twist their necks towards it or twist around it and circumambulate around it. The reciters differed over whether to stop on it with taa' or haa'. The majority of scholars stopped on it with taa', while Al-Kisa'i stopped on it with haa'. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra' chose to stop on taa' to follow the orthography of the Qur'an, as it is written with taa'. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Mansur bin Al-Mu'tamir, Abu Al-Jawza', Abu Saleh and Hamid read Al-Lat with a stressed taa'. This reading was narrated from Ibn Kathir. It was said that it is the name of a man who used to knead gruel and feed it to the pilgrims. When he was a man on top of a mountain, he used to make hais from its milk and butter and feed it to the pilgrims. He was in Batn Nakhal, and when he died, they worshipped him. Al-Kalbi said: He was a man from Thaqif who had a flock of sheep. It was said that he was Amer bin Al-Dharb Al-Adwani, and this idol belonged to Thaqif, and the poet said about him: Do not support Al-Lat, for God will destroy her. How can he support you who does not support himself? It is stated in As-Sahah: Al-Lat is the name of an idol belonging to Thaqeef, and it was in At-Taif. Some Arabs stop on it with a ta’, and some with a ha’. Al-Uzza is the idol of Quraysh and Banu Kinanah. Mujahid said: It is a tree that was in Ghatafan, and they used to worship it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Khalid ibn Al-Walid to it, and he cut it down. It was also said that it was a female demon who used to visit three tamarisk trees in Batn Nakhl. Sa’eed ibn Jubayr said: Al-Uzza is a white stone that they used to worship. Qatada said: It is a house that was in Batn Nakhl. Manat is the idol of Banu Hilal. Ibn Hisham said: It is the idol of Hudhayl and Khuza’ah. Qatada said: It belonged to the Ansar. The majority read Manat with an alif without a hamza, while Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Hamid, Mujahid, and As-Sulami read it with a long vowel and a hamza. As for the reading of the majority, it is derived from Muna which means to pour, because the blood of women used to be poured there to draw closer to it. As for the second reading, it is derived from the word naw’, which means rain, because they used to ask for rain from the anwa’, and it was said that they are two languages of the Arabs. What came according to the first reading is what Jarir said: Azid Manat threatens Ibn Taym. Where did the threat take you? And what came in the other reading is what Al-Harithi said: Did Tamim ibn Abd Mana’ah come to us secretly? The majority of reciters stopped on it with a ta’ in accordance with the orthography of the Qur’an, while Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaisin stopped on it with a ha’. It is stated in As-Sahah: “Manat was the name of an idol that existed between Mecca and Medina. The ha’ is for the feminine and it is paused with a ta’, as is the case with linguistics.” His statement, the third and other is a description of Manat, describing it as third and other, and third can only be other. Abu Al-Baqa’ said: The description with the other is for emphasis, and describing the third with the other is problematic, as the Arabs only describe the second with it. Al-Khalil said: He only said that to agree with the beginnings of the verse, like his statement, other aims. Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said: There is an inversion, and the meaning is: Have you seen Al-Lat and Al-Uzza the other, and Manat the third? It was said that describing it with the other was for the purpose of glorification because it was great among the polytheists. It was also said that it was for the purpose of humiliation and blame, and that what is meant is the later and lowly one, as in his statement, The last of them said to the first of them, meaning their lowest ones to their leaders.
53:21: Then the Almighty repeated His rebuke and reprimand of them with a heinous statement they said, saying: 21- Do you have males and He has females? That is, how do you attribute to God what you hate of females and attribute to yourself what you love of males? It was said that this is His statement that the angels are daughters of God, and it was said that what is meant is how do you attribute to Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat, who are females in your opinion, partners with God, and it is their nature to despise females.
53:22: Then the Almighty mentioned that this naming and the division understood from the question is an unfair division, so He said: 22- That, then, is an unfair division. The majority read unfair with a silent ya’ without a hamza, and Ibn Kathir read it with a silent hamza, and the meaning is: that it is a division that is outside of the right, unjust, and deviating from justice. Al-Akhfash said: It is said that he was unjust in the ruling, meaning he was unfair, and he reduced and stinted on his right. He said: And it is sometimes added with a hamza, and he recited: If you distance yourself from us, we will disparage you, and if you are absent, we will annihilate you and make you angry. Al-Kisa’i said: Daaz yadhiz dayzan, and Daaz yadhuz dawz means to transgress, oppress, cheat, and diminish. From this comes the poet’s saying: Banu Asad have gone astray with their rule, as they make the head like the tail. Al-Farra’ said: “Some Arabs say ‘Dhizay’ with a hamza. Abu Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Zayd that he heard the Arabs pronounce the hamza in ‘Dayzay’. Al-Baghawi said: “There is no ‘Fala’ with a kasra on the ‘fa’ in adjectives in Arabic. It is only used in nouns like ‘Dhikra’.” Al-Mu’arraj said: “They disliked the damma of the ‘Dhad’ in ‘Dayzay’ and feared the ya’ would change to a waw, which is one of the derivatives of ‘waw’. So they broke the ‘Dhad’ for this reason, just as they said in the plural of ‘abyad’ ‘baydh’. Al-Zajjaj said the same. It was also said that it is a verbal noun like ‘dhikra’, so the meaning would be: an unjust and oppressive division.”
53:23: Then the Almighty responded to them by saying: 23- They are only names which you have named, you and your fathers. That is, the idols or statues, in terms of what you claim as gods, are only mere names, devoid of any of the meaning of the divinity which you claim, because they neither see nor hear, nor reason nor understand, nor harm nor benefit. They are nothing but names which you and your fathers have named, with the latter imitating the former in this, and the sons following the fathers in that. And in this there is a belittling of their status which is not hidden, just as you say in belittling a man: He is only a name if it does not include a valid description. And similar to this verse is the saying of the Almighty: You do not worship besides Him except names which you have named. It is said: I named him Zayd and I named him Zayd. So His saying you have named them is an attribute of idols, and the pronoun refers to the names, not to the idols: that is, you made them names, not gave them names. It was said that his statement they refers to the three names mentioned, and the first is more appropriate. God has not sent down any authority for them means He has not sent down any proof or evidence for them. Muqatil said: He has not sent down to us a book for you in which there is proof as you say that they are gods. Then He informed about them by saying: They follow nothing but assumption meaning that they follow, in what was mentioned of naming and acting according to it, nothing but assumption that is of no avail against the truth. He shifted from direct address to third person, ignoring them and belittling them, so He said: and what the souls desire meaning that they incline towards and desire without paying attention to what is the truth that must be followed. The majority read yataba'un with a lower case ending in the third person, while 'Isa ibn 'Umar, Ayyub and Ibn al-Samee' read it with a higher case ending in the second person. This reading was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Talhah and Ibn Wathab. And there has certainly come to them from their Lord guidance meaning a clear and apparent explanation that they are not gods. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of yataba'un, and it is permissible for it to be an interruption, but the first is more appropriate. Meaning: How can they follow that when there has come to them guidance from God through the tongue of His Messenger whom God sent among them and made him one of their own?
53:24: 24- Or does man have whatever he desires? “Am” is the detached particle understood by bal and the hamza is for denial. So he struck out their following of conjecture, which is merely imagination, and their following of the desires of the souls and what they incline toward. He moved on to denying that they will have what they desire, that idols will benefit them and intercede for them.
53:25: Then he explained the reason for the person not having what he wished for by saying: 25- To God belongs the Hereafter and the first life. That is, the affairs of the Hereafter and the world in their entirety belong to God Almighty, so they have no affair with Him, including their vain wishes and empty ambitions.
53:26: Then He confirmed that and increased the invalidation of what they wish for, saying: 26- And how many are there angels in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all. “How many” here is the informative particle indicating abundance, and its place is in the nominative case as a subject, and the sentence after it is its predicate. Because how many has the meaning of abundance, the pronoun is plural in their intercession with the singular of the angel. The meaning is: to rebuke them for what they wish for and desire from the intercession of idols, while the angels, despite their great worship and honor with God, do not intercede except for whom He has given permission to intercede for. So how about these inanimate objects that lack reason and understanding? This is the meaning of His statement: Except after God has given permission for them to intercede for whomever He wills to intercede for them and is pleased with intercession for him because he is one of the people of monotheism. The polytheists have no share in that, and God does not give permission for intercession for them nor is pleased with it because they are not among those who deserve it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the star when it sets, meaning when it is set. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, saying: It is the Pleiades when they hang down. He also narrated on his authority, saying: God swears that Muhammad has neither gone astray nor erred. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding His statement, Of good character, he said: Of good character. Ahmad ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azmah narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not see Gabriel in his true form except twice. The first time, he asked him to see him in his true form, so he showed him his form and the horizon was blocked. The second time, he was with him wherever he ascended, so that is what God says, “And he is on the highest horizon,” He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord, meaning the creation of Gabriel. Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated on his authority that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Gabriel at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and he had six hundred wings. Ahmad also narrated on his authority. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And he is on the highest horizon, meaning the rising of the sun. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement: He was two bow lengths away or even nearer, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel with six hundred wings.” Al-Faryabi, `Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi - who authenticated it - Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and Abu al-Shaykh also narrated it. In Al-Azmah, Al-Hakim authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from him regarding his statement, The heart did not lie about what it saw, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel wearing a fluttering green ring that filled the space between the heaven and the earth.” Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Then he drew near and descended, he said: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He drew near and descended to his Lord. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, he said: His Lord drew near and descended. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement, Then he was two bow lengths away, he said: Gabriel drew near to him until he was only a cubit or two. Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara narrated from Ibn Abbas, he said: Qabb is the chain, and qawsin are the arms. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he drew near to his Lord. He was two bow lengths away or even nearer. Have you not seen the bow, how close it is to the string? Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed, meaning His servant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muslim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat narrated on his authority regarding His statement, The heart did not deny what it saw. And he saw Him on another occasion. He said: Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart twice. Similar narrations were reported from him by Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh. Ibn Mardawayh reported from Anas, who said: Muhammad saw his Lord. Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) saw his Lord with his eyes. al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him, who said: Muhammad saw his Lord twice, once with his sight and once with his heart. al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi also reported from him, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) saw his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh also reported from him, who said: Do you wonder that friendship was for Abraham, speech was for Moses, and the vision was for Muhammad? Similar narrations have been reported from him through various chains of narration. Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), Did you see your Lord? He said: "Light. How can I see Him?" Muslim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), Did you see your Lord? He said, I saw a light. Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa’i, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he said, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) saw his Lord with his heart, but did not see Him with his sight.” Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah regarding his statement: And he saw him on another occasion, said Gabriel. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is in the sixth heaven. The souls that ascend from it end and are taken from it, and the souls that descend from above it end and are taken from it.” When that which covers the Lote Tree covers it, he said: A carpet of gold. Abu al-Shaykh narrated in al-Azmah on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: Paradise is in the seventh highest heaven, and Hellfire is in the seventh lowest earth. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Lat was a man who kneaded gruel for the pilgrims. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that al-Uzza was in Batn Nakhl, that al-Lat was in Taif, and that Manat was made of dried meat. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Dhaizi, who said: An oppressor who has no right to it.
53:27: 27- Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels female names. That is, those who do not believe in the Resurrection and what comes after it in the Hereafter, and they are the disbelievers, add to their disbelief a heinous statement and ignorant ignorance, which is that they name the angels, who are free from all shortcomings, female names. This is because they claimed that they are the daughters of God, so they made them females and called them daughters.
53:28: 28- And they have no knowledge of it. This sentence is in the place of a noun in the state of context: meaning, they call them by this name, while they do not know what they are saying. They have not known them, nor seen them, nor has it reached them through any of the sources that informants narrate. Rather, they said that out of ignorance, misguidance, and boldness. It was read, They have no knowledge of it, meaning the angels or the name. They follow nothing but conjecture, meaning they follow nothing in this statement except mere conjecture and imagination. Then Silhana spoke about conjecture and its ruling, saying, Indeed, conjecture is of no avail against the truth at all, meaning that conjecture is of no avail against the truth at all, and the truth here is knowledge. This is evidence that mere conjecture does not replace knowledge and that the conjecturer is not knowledgeable. This applies to matters that require knowledge, which are scholarly issues, not to matters in which conjecture is sufficient, which are scholarly issues. We have already explained this. This specialization is necessary, because the meaning of generality, analogy, a single report, and the like are conjectural, so acting upon them is acting upon conjecture. We are obligated to act upon it in such matters, so the evidence for the obligation to act upon it in them is specific to this generality, and what was reported in its meaning of censure of those who act upon conjecture and the prohibition against following it.
53:29: 29- So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance. That is, turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance. What is meant by remembrance here is the Qur’an, or the remembrance of the Hereafter, or the remembrance of God in general. It was also said that what is meant by remembrance here is faith, and the meaning is: Leave arguing with them, for you have conveyed to them what you were commanded to do, and you are only required to convey it. This was abrogated by the verse of the sword. And he did not desire anything but the life of this world.
