That is, he did not desire anything other than it, nor did he seek anything other than it, but rather he limited his sight to it, for he is not qualified for good nor does he deserve to have his affairs taken care of.
53:30: Then, the Almighty, belittled their status and insignificant their matter, saying: 30- That is the extent of their knowledge. That is, this turning away and limiting one’s will to this worldly life is the extent of their knowledge; they have nothing else, and they do not pay attention to anything else in the matter of religion. Al-Farra’ said: That is, the extent of their minds and the limit of their knowledge is that they preferred this world over the Hereafter. It was said that the reference in His statement, That, is to their making the angels daughters of God and calling them female names, but the first is more appropriate. What is meant by knowledge here is absolute perception which includes false suspicion. The sentence is a new sentence to confirm their ignorance and their following mere suspicion. It was said that it is an interruption between the reason and the cause, which is His statement: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who has been guided. This is a reason for the command to turn away, and the meaning is that He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of who has deviated from the truth, turned away from it and was not guided to it, and He is most knowing of who has been guided, accepted the truth, turned towards it and acted upon it. So He will reward every doer according to his action, if good then good, and if evil then evil. In it is consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and guidance for him not to tire himself in calling those who persist in misguidance and are destined for misery, for God knows the state of this misguided group just as He knows the state of the rightly guided group.
53:31: Then the Almighty informed about the vastness of His power and the greatness of His kingdom, saying: 31- And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, meaning He is the owner of that and the one who controls it, no one shares it with Him. The lam in that He may recompense those who do evil for what they have done is related to what the speech indicates, as if He said He is the owner of that, He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills, to recompense the evildoer for his evil and the doer of good for his good. It was said that His statement, And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is parenthetical, and the meaning is: Your Lord knows best who has strayed from His path and He knows best who has been guided, so that He may recompense. It was also said that it is the lam of consequence, meaning that the consequence of the matter of creation, among whom are the good-doers and the evil-doers, is that God will recompense each of them for his deeds. Makki said: The lam is related to His statement, Their intercession will be of no avail, which is far-fetched in terms of wording and meaning. The majority read to recompense with a dhammah. Zayd bin Ali read it with the letter nun, and the meaning of with goodness is with the good reward, which is Paradise, or because of their good deeds.
53:32: Then he described these doers of good, saying: 32- "Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities." This relative pronoun is in the accusative case as an adjective to the first relative pronoun in His statement: "Those who do good. It was also said that it is a substitute for it, and it was also said that it is an explanation of it, and it was also said that it is in the accusative case for praise by the omitted I mean," or in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, they avoid the major sins. The majority of scholars read "major" in the plural. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Al-A'mash, and Yahya ibn Waththab read "major" in the singular. Major sins are every sin for which God has threatened Hellfire, or severely condemned its perpetrator. The scholars have discussed the definition of major sins at length. Just as they differed in defining their meaning and nature, they also differed in their number. Immoralities are the plural of "fahishah," which is the major sin that is immoral, such as adultery and the like. Muqatil said: Major sins are any sin that is sealed with Hellfire, and immoralities are any sin for which a hadd has been prescribed. It has been said that major sins are polytheism and immoralities are adultery. We have already mentioned in Surat An-Nisa something simpler and more beneficial than this. The exception in His statement: except for lamma is disjunctive. The root of lamma in the language is what is little and small, and from this: someone who is accustomed to a place means he stayed there for a short time, and someone who is accustomed to food means he rarely ate from it. Al-Mubarrad said: The root of lamma is to touch something without riding it. It is said that he touched such and such if he approached it and did not mix with it. Al-Azhari said: The Arabs use ilmaam to mean nearness and proximity, and from this is the saying of Jarir: I myself avoid him, he is dear to me, and I avoid visiting him for a long time And the other said: When you come to visit us in our homes, you will find abundant firewood and a blazing fire. Al-Zajjaj said: The root of al-mam and ilma is what a person learns time after time without delving into it or continuing with it. It is said I visited it if you visited it and left it. It is also said I did it only occasionally or ilmaman meaning from time to time. From this comes the learning of the imagination. Al-A’mash said: Pain of imagination from a tribe after it has severed its rope from our rope and then severed it He said in Al-Sahah: A man’s pain comes from alamma, which refers to minor sins. It is also said that it refers to approaching a sin without committing it. Another recited: Come to Zainab before the caravan departs and say that you will tire us out, for the heart does not own anything. The sayings of the people of action differed in interpreting this touch mentioned in the verse. The majority are of the opinion that it is minor sins. It was said that it is what is less than adultery, such as kissing, winking, and looking. It was said that it is a man who touches upon a sin and then repents, and this is what Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Al-Zuhri, and others said. Among them: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a lot, and which servant of yours is there but pain? This statement was chosen by Al-Zajjaj and Al-Nahhas. It was said that it refers to the sins of the Age of Ignorance, for God does not hold one accountable for them in Islam. Naftawayh said: It is to commit a sin that is not usually done. He said: The Arabs say: It only comes to us occasionally, meaning from time to time. He said: It is not possible for him to touch us but not do it, because the Arabs do not say He touched us except if he did, not if he intended to do it but did not do it. The first is more correct. The phrase Indeed, your Lord is Vast in forgiveness is an explanation of what the exception includes: that is, even if that is outside the ruling of accountability, it is not devoid of being a sin that requires God’s forgiveness and mercy. It was said that He, glory be to Him, forgives whoever repents from his sin. Then He, the Almighty, mentioned that His work encompasses the conditions of His servants, saying: He knows you best when He produced you from the earth, meaning He created you from it as part of the creation of your father Adam. It was also said that it refers to Adam, for He created him from clay. And when you were fetuses, meaning He knows your conditions while you were fetuses. Fetuses is the plural of fetus, which is the child as long as it is in the womb. It was called thus because of its concealment. For this reason, He said: in the wombs of your mothers, so the one who comes out of the womb is not called a fetus. The sentence is a new sentence to confirm what came before it. So do not praise yourselves, meaning do not exonerate them from sins or speak ill of them. For abandoning the purification of the soul is further from ostentation and closer to humility. The sentence He knows best who fears God is a new sentence to confirm the prohibition, meaning He knows best who fears God’s punishment and works sincerely for Him. Al-Hasan said: And God, the Almighty, knows of every soul what it does, what it makes, and what it will become.
53:33: Then, when God Almighty explained the ignorance of the polytheists in general, He singled out some of them for blame, saying: 33- Have you seen the one who turned away? That is, turned away from goodness and refused to follow the truth.
53:34: 34- And he gave a little and then he was akada meaning he gave a little gift or he gave a little thing and stopped it and held back from it. The origin of akada is from the word kadda, which means hardness. It is said of someone who dug a well and then reached a rock in which he could not dig, he has akada. Then the Arabs used it for someone who gave but did not complete it, and for someone who asked for something but did not reach the end of it. From this is the saying of Al-Hutay’ah: He gave a little, then he was ungrateful. And whoever does good to people will be praised. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Zaid said: It is said that his fingers became devoid of digging, and his hand became tired and did nothing, and the land became sparse, and its vegetation became sparse, and the land became sparse, and its vegetation became sparse, and the man became sparsely supplied with something, and his goodness became scarce. Al-Farra' said: The meaning of the verse is: He withheld a gift and cut off. Al-Mubarrad said: He withheld strongly. Mujahid, Ibn Zaid, and Muqatil said: This was revealed about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, who had followed the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) for his religion, but some of the polytheists reviled him, so he abandoned it and returned to his polytheism. Muqatil said: Al-Walid praised the Qur'an, then he refrained from it and gave a little of his tongue goodness, then he cut it off. Ad-Dahhak said: This was revealed about An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith. Muhammad ibn Ka'b Al-Qurazi said: This was revealed about Abu Jahl.
53:35: 35- Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees? The question is for rebuke and rebuke, and the meaning is: Does this beggar have knowledge of what he has hidden from him regarding the matter of the punishment, so that he knows it?
53:36: 36- Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses?
53:37: 37- Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses * and Abraham who fulfilled That is, has he not been informed and not narrated what is in the scriptures of Moses: meaning his books, which is the Torah, and what is in the scriptures of Abraham who fulfilled: meaning he completed and perfected what he was commanded to do. The commentators said: That is, he conveyed to his people what he was commanded to do and delivered it to them, and it was said that he went to great lengths to fulfill what he had promised God.
53:38: Then the Almighty explained what is in their scrolls, saying: 38- No soul shall bear the burden of another meaning no soul shall bear the burden of another soul, and its meaning is: no soul shall be taken for the sin of another, and that is the light form of the heavy form, and its subject is a pronoun of an implied matter, and its predicate is the sentence after it, and the position of the sentence is the accusative as a substitute for the scrolls of Moses and the scrolls of Abraham, or the nominative as the predicate of a deleted subject, and the interpretation of this verse has already been explained in Surat Al-An’am.
53:39: 39- And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for is in apposition to His statement: You shall not sin. This is also from what is in the scriptures of Moses, and the meaning is: He shall have no reward for his striving or recompense for his work, and no one’s work will benefit anyone. This generality is made specific by the words of the Most High: We will join with them their offspring, and by what was mentioned about the intercession of the prophets and angels for the servants and the permissibility of the living praying for the dead and the like. Whoever said: This verse is abrogated by such matters is not correct, because the specific does not abrogate the general, rather it specifies it. So everything that there is evidence that a person benefits from without his striving is a specification of what is in this verse of generality.
53:40: 40- And that his effort will be seen meaning it will be presented to him and revealed to him on the Day of Resurrection.
53:41: 41- Then He will reward him meaning He will reward the person for his efforts. It is said that God rewarded him for his work and rewarded him for his work. The nominative pronoun refers to the person and the accusative to his efforts. It was said that the accusative pronoun refers to the reward that comes after it, which is His statement: the fullest reward. So the pronoun refers to something that comes after it and explains it. It is possible that the accusative pronoun refers to the reward, which is the source of he will reward him, and the fullest reward is made an explanation of the reward indicated by the verb, as in His statement: Be just, that is nearer. Al-Akhfash said: It is said that I rewarded him with the reward and I rewarded him with a reward other than it, there is no difference between them.
53:42: 42- And that to your Lord is the final destination meaning the return and destination is to Him, glory be to Him, and not to anyone else, so He will reward them for their deeds. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, he said: The major sins are those for which God has named Hellfire, and the immoralities are those for which there is worldly punishment. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: I have not seen anything more similar to licking than what Abu Hurairah said that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God has decreed for the son of Adam his share of zina, which he will inevitably attain. The zina of the eye is looking, the zina of the tongue is speaking, the soul desires and longs, and the private parts confirm that or deny it.” Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding the statement, except for a touch, that he said: The zina of the eyes is looking, the zina of the lips is kissing, the zina of the hands is touching, and the zina of the feet is walking. The private parts confirm that or deny it. If he comes forward with his private parts, then he has committed zina, otherwise it is licking. Musaddad, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he was asked about the statement, except for a touch, that he said: It refers to a look, a wink, a kiss, and direct contact. If circumcised parts touch circumcised parts, then ritual ablution is required, and that is zina. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said regarding the statement, except for a minor sin, it refers to a man who commits an immoral act and then repents from it. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If you forgive God, you forgive a lot, and which servant of yours does not have pain? Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: except for a small amount he said: except for what has already happened. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah regarding his statement: except for a small amount he said: The small amount of adultery, then he repents and does not return to it, and the small amount of drinking alcohol, then he repents and does not return to it, that is the small amount. Abd bin Humaid and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The small amount is everything between the two limits, the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter, which is expiated by prayer, and it is less than every obligatory sin. As for the limit of this world, it is every limit whose punishment God has imposed in this world, and as for the limit of the Hereafter, it is everything that God has sealed with Hell and postponed its punishment until the Hereafter. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu`aym in al-Ma`rifah narrated on the authority of Thabit ibn al-Harith al-Ansari, who said: “Whenever a young boy died among the Jews, they would say, ‘He is a truthful person.’ When report of that reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said, ‘The Jews have lied. There is no soul created in its mother’s womb except that it is either wretched or blessed.’ Then God revealed, ‘He knows best about you when He created you from the earth,’ the entire verse.” Ahmad, Muslim, and Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Zaynab bint Abi Salamah that she was named Barra, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘Do not praise yourselves. God knows best who are the righteous among you. Name her Zaynab.’ Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, ‘And he gave little and was straitened,’ he said, ‘He stopped.’ It was revealed about al-`As ibn Wa’il. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said, ‘He obeyed for a little, then stopped.’” Sa`id ibn Mansur, `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Shirazi in Al-Alqab, and Al-Daylami narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Umamah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: “Do you know what is meant by His statement: ‘And Abraham who fulfilled,’” They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: And in his daily deeds, he used to pray four rak`ahs, and he claimed that it was the Duha prayer. In its chain of transmission is Ja`far ibn Al-Zubayr, and he is weak. Al-Hakim narrated, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The arrows of Islam are thirty arrows, and no one completed them before Abraham, peace be upon him. God said: And Abraham who fulfilled. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse: Abraham who completed obedience in what he did with his son when he saw the vision, and what is in the scrolls of Moses, No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, to the end of the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Muadh ibn Anas, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Shall I not tell you why God called Abraham His faithful friend? He used to say every morning and evening: ‘Glory be to God when you go to bed at night and when you come to bed at morning,’ to the end of the verse.” Ibn Lahi’ah’s chain of transmission includes it. Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When By the star was revealed, it reached And Abraham who fulfilled, and he said: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, to the words: of the first vow. Abu Dawud and al-Nahhas, both of them in al-Nasikh, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for. Then God revealed after that: And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring, so God admitted the children into Paradise because of the righteousness of the fathers. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: “Whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would recite, ‘And that man can have nothing but what he strives for, and that his striving will soon be seen, and then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense,’ he would seek refuge in God and submit.” Ad-Daraqutni narrated in Al-Ifrad and Al-Baghawi in his Tafsir on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, “On the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), regarding His statement, ‘And that to your Lord is the final destination,’ he said, ‘There is no thought about the Lord.’”
53:43: His saying: 43- And that it is He who makes laugh and cry meaning He is the Creator of that and the Judge because of it. Al-Hasan and Al-Kalbi said: He makes the people of Paradise laugh in Paradise and makes the people of Hell cry in Hell. Ad-Dahhak said: He makes the earth laugh with plants and makes the sky cry with rain. It was also said that He makes whomever He wills laugh in this world by making him happy and makes whomever He wills cry by making him sad. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: He makes the obedient laugh with mercy and makes the disobedient cry with wrath.
53:44: 44- And that it is He who causes death and brings to life meaning He decreed the causes of death and life, and no one else has the power to do that. It was also said that He created death and life itself, as in His statement, He created death and life. It was also said that He caused the fathers to die and gave life to the sons. It was also said that He caused death in this world and gave life for the resurrection. It was also said that what is meant by them is sleep and wakefulness. Ata’ said, He caused death by His justice and gave life by His grace. It was also said that He caused the disbeliever to die and the believer to give life, as in His statement, Or he who was dead and We gave him life.
53:45: 45- And that He created the two mates, the male and the female.
53:46: 46- And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, * From a sperm-drop when it emitted. What is meant by the two mates is the male and female of every animal, and Adam and Eve are not included in that, for they did not come from a sperm-drop. The sperm-drop is a small amount of water, and the meaning of when it emitted is when it is poured into the womb and flows into it, as said by Al-Kalbi, Ad-Dahhak, Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, and others. It is said that a man ejaculated and emanate, meaning he poured semen. Abu Ubaidah said, when it ejaculated means that he estimated it: it is said that you estimated something, and he estimated it for him, and from this is the saying of the poet: Until you find what you want, German Meaning: He is able to have a child from her.
53:47: 47- And that upon Him is the other creation meaning the return of souls to bodies upon resurrection in fulfillment of His promise. The majority of scholars read the creation with a shortened form, with the weight of a strike, while Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a long form, with the weight of a guarantee. According to both readings, they are two sources.
53:48: 48- And that He is the Most Enriching and the Most Satisfied meaning He enriches whomever He wills and impoverishes whomever He wills. Similar to this is His statement: He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it and His statement: He withholds and expands it Ibn Zayd said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Al-Hasan said: Aghna means to provide for, and aqna means to serve. It was said that the meaning of aqna is to give qaniya, which is what is stored up from wealth. It was also said that the meaning of aqna is to be pleased with what He gave: that is, He enriched him, then made him satisfied with what He gave him. Al-Jawhari said: Qana means to make a man qana, like ghana means to give him what he acquires. Aqna means to satisfy him, and aqna means to be satisfied. Abu Zayd said: The Arabs say, Whoever is given one hundred cows has given qaniya, and whoever is given one hundred sheep has given wealth, and whoever is given one hundred camels has given desire.” Al-Akhfash and Ibn Kaysan said: Aqna means to impoverish, and this supports the first statement.
53:49: 49- And that He is the Lord of Sirius is a planet behind Gemini that Khuza'ah used to worship. What is meant by it is Sirius which is called Al-Obour, and it is brighter than Sirius which is called Al-Ghumaisa. God Almighty mentioned that He is the Lord of Sirius along with being the Lord of all things in order to refute those who used to worship it. The first to worship it was Abu Kabsha, who was one of the nobles of the Arabs. The Quraysh used to call the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Ibn Abi Kabsha, likening him to him because he opposed their religion as Abu Kabsha opposed them. An example of this is what Abu Sufyan said on the day of the conquest: The matter of Ibn Abi Kabsha has been decreed.
53:50: 50- And that He destroyed the former 'Aad He described the 'Aad as the first because they were before Thamud. Ibn Zayd said: They were called the first 'Aad because they were the first nation to be destroyed after Noah. Ibn Ishaq said: They are two 'Aad, the first was destroyed by the Chirping, and the other by the Blast. It was said that the first 'Aad were the people of Hud and the second 'Aad were Iram. The majority read the first 'Aad with the tanween and the hamza, while Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaisin read it by transferring the vowel of the hamza to the lam and assimilating the tanween into it.
53:51: 51- And Thamud, and He left none of them alive. That is, He destroyed Thamud just as He destroyed Aad, and He left none alive from either group. Thamud were the people of Noah before the destruction of Aad and Thamud.
53:52: 52- Indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious. That is, more unjust and more rebellious than Aad and Thamud, or more unjust and more rebellious than all the disbelieving sects, or more unjust and more rebellious than the polytheists of the Arabs. They were thus because they transgressed against God with their sins despite the long period of Noah’s call to them, as in His statement: So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years.
53:53: 53- And the overturned city, I fall Al-Itifaak means to overturn: Al-Mu'tafikah is the city of the people of Lot, and it was called Al-Mu'tafikah because it was overturned with them and its top became its bottom. You say afakatuhu if you turn it upside down. The meaning of ahwa is to drop: that is, Gabriel made it fall after he raised it. Al-Mubarrad said: he made it fall.
53:54: 54- So that which covered it covered it meaning that it was covered with what covered them from the stones that fell upon it, as in His statement: So We turned it upside down and rained down upon them stones of baked clay. In this phrase there is an emphasis on the matter that covered it and a glorification of it. It was said that the pronoun refers to all the nations mentioned: meaning that that which covered it covered them from the punishment of different types.
53:55: 55- Then which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute? This is addressed to the disbelieving human being: that is, which of the favors of your Lord, O disbelieving human being, do you doubt and dispute? It was also said that the address was to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as an allusion to someone other than him, and it was also said that it was to everyone who is suitable for it. The action of disputing is attributed to one person considering its multiplicity according to the multiplicity of its object. And these mentioned matters are called favors: that is, blessings, even though some of them are punishments and not blessings, because they contain lessons and admonitions, and because they contain vengeance against the disobedient, and in that is victory for the prophets and the righteous. The majority read yatamāra without assimilation, while Ya'qub and Ibn Muhaysin read it by assimilation of one of the two ta's into the other.
53:56: 56- This is a warner among the first warners. That is, this Muhammad is a messenger to you from among the messengers who came before him. He has warned you as they warned their people. This is what Ibn Jurayj, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, and others said. Qatada said: He means the Qur’an, and that he has warned with what the previous scriptures warned with. It was also said that what he has informed us about the report of the nations is to frighten this nation lest what happened to those people happen to them. This is what Abu Malik said. Abu Salih said: The reference in his statement: This is to what is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham. But the first is more appropriate.
53:57: 57- "The Hour has drawn near" means the Hour has drawn near. He called it "Azfah" because it is close to coming, and it was said because it is close to the people. As in his saying: "The Hour has drawn near" He informed them of that so that they would prepare for it. It is said in Al-Sahah: "Azfah Al-Azfah" means the Resurrection. A man hastened, and from this is the saying of the poet: The departure time has come, but our passengers have not yet left our saddlebags, as if they had
53:58: 58- There is none who can uncover it besides God meaning that there is no soul capable of uncovering it when it befalls except God, the Most High. It was said that Kashifah means uncovering, and the ha in it is like the ha in al-‘aqibah and al-dahiyah. It was also said that Kashifah means revealer, and the ha is for emphasis, as in the narration, but the first is more appropriate. Kashifah is an adjective for a deleted noun, as we mentioned, and the meaning is that no one is able to uncover it when it overwhelms creation with its hardships and horrors except God. This is what Ata’, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others said.
53:59: Then God Almighty rebuked them and said: 59- Do you then marvel at this narration? What is meant by the narration is the Qur’an: that is, how do you marvel at it in denial?
53:60: 60- And you laugh at it in mockery, even though it is not a place for denial or mockery, and you do not cry in fear and aversion because of the severe threat it contains.
53:61: And sentence 61 - "And you are samudun" is in the accusative case as a state, and it is possible that it is a new sentence to confirm what is in it, and samud: is heedlessness and forgetfulness of something. And it is said in Al-Sahah: samud samud means raising his head in arrogance, so he is samud. The poet said: The stillness of the night is light Ibn al-A'rabi said: As-samud is amusement, and as-samid is the playful one. It is said of a female singer: Asmadinā, meaning, he distracted us with singing. Al-Mubarrad said: Samidun, Khamidun. The poet said: The two events threw the women of the Al Amr family with a measure of gratitude to him. He turned their black hair white and turned their white faces black
53:62: 62- So prostrate to God and worship Him. When God, the Almighty, rebuked the polytheists for mocking the Qur’an, laughing at it, ridiculing it, and not benefiting from its admonitions and warnings, He ordered His believing servants to prostrate to God and worship Him. The fa is the answer to an omitted condition: that is, if the command from the disbelievers is like this, then prostrate to God and worship Him, for He is the One who deserves that from you. It was mentioned in the opening of the surah that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, prostrated when reciting this verse, and the disbelievers prostrated with him, so what is meant by it is the prostration of recitation, and it was said that it is the prostration of obligation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And that He is the Most Enriched and the Most Satisfied, that he said: He gave and satisfied. Ibn Jarir narrated from him, And that He is the Lord of Sirius, that he said: It is the star called Sirius. Al-Fakihi also narrated from him, that he said: This verse was revealed about Khuza’ah, and they used to worship Sirius, which is the star that follows Gemini. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, regarding his statement, This is a warner among the first warners, that he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, that he said: The approaching one is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Hannad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Salih Abu Al-Khalil, that he said: When this verse was revealed, Is it at this statement that you marvel * And laugh and do not weep? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, never laughed after that except by smiling. The wording of Abd ibn Humayd is: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was never seen laughing or smiling until he departed from this world. Abdul Razzaq, Al-Faryabi, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, samidoon, that he said: They are distracted and turning away from it. Al-Faryabi, Abu Ubaid in his Fadhail, Abdul bin Hamid, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in Dhamm Al-Malahi, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from him: And you are samidoon, that he said: Singing is in Yemeni; when they heard the Quran, they would sing and play. Al-Faryabi, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding the statement of God, samidoon, that he said: They used to pass by the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, high-stepping their feet. Haven’t you seen how a camel struts high? Abdul Razzaq, Abdul bin Hamid and Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Khalid Al-Walibi who said: Ali bin Abi Talib came out to us after the call to prayer had been made and we were standing waiting for him to come forward. He said: Why are you samidoon? You are neither praying nor sitting waiting.
54:1: It is called Surat Al-Aqrabat, and it has fifty-five verses. It is all Meccan according to the majority of scholars. Muqatil said: It is Meccan except for three verses from the verse, Or do they say, “We are all victorious?” to the verse, And the Hour is more grievous and bitter. Al-Qurtubi said: It is not authentic. Ibn Ad-Durais, Ibn Mardawayh, An-Nahhas, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar verse on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Ash-Shu’ab on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It has drawn near and is called in the Torah Al-Mubiyadah the whitening one. It will whiten the face of its companion on the day when faces will be whitened. Al-Bayhaqi said: It is unknown. Ibn Ad-Durais narrated on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Farwah that he said: Whoever recites ‘The Hour has drawn near’ every two nights, God will raise him on the Day of Resurrection with a face like the moon on the night when it is full. Ibn Ad-Durais narrated a similar verse on the authority of Layth ibn Ma’n, on the authority of a sheikh from Hamdan that he said: It has drawn near. It was previously mentioned that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite Qaf and The Hour has drawn near on the two Eids of Sacrifice and Fitr. His saying: 1- The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. That is, it has drawn near. There is no doubt that it has become close, considering the relation of what remains after the establishment of the Prophethood of Muhammad to what has passed of this world. It can be said that since it was bound to occur, it was close, for everything that is coming is close. And the moon has split. That is, the moon has split. Hudhayfah read it this way with the addition of qad. What is meant is the splitting that occurred during the days of the Prophethood, a miracle of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is the view of the majority of the early and later scholars. Al-Wahidi said: “The majority of the commentators are of the same opinion, except for what Uthman ibn Ata’ narrated from his father, who said: The meaning is that the moon will split. All scholars disagree with him.” He said: “The approach of the Hour was mentioned along with the splitting of the moon, because its splitting is one of the signs of the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and his prophethood and his time are portents of the approaching Hour.” Ibn Kaysan said: “There is an inversion in the speech: that is, the moon split, and the Hour is drawing near.” Al-Qurtubi narrated from Al-Hasan something similar to what Ata’ said, referring to the splitting that will occur on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that the meaning of and the moon split is that the matter became clear and apparent, and the Arabs use the moon as an example of what becomes clear. It was also said that the splitting of the moon is the splitting of darkness from it and its rising during it, just as dawn is called after the splitting of darkness from it. Ibn Kathir said: The splitting occurred during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as proven in the numerous hadiths with authentic chains of transmission. He said: This is a matter agreed upon among scholars, that the splitting of the moon occurred during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and that it was one of the dazzling miracles. Al-Zajjaj said: Some people, who deviated from the correct viewpoint and what the scholars agree upon, claimed that its interpretation is that the moon will split on the Day of Resurrection.
54:2: The matter is clear in the ambiguity and the consensus of the scholars, because His statement: 2- And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, 'Persistent magic' indicates that this was in this world, not on the Day of Resurrection. And no one came who disagreed with the majority and said that the split will occur on the Day of Resurrection except by mere exclusion, saying: Because if the split had occurred during the time of the Prophethood, no one would have remained who did not see it because it is a sign, and people are equal with regard to signs. The response to that is that it is not necessary for everyone to see it, neither rationally, nor religiously, nor customarily. Despite this, it has been transmitted to us by way of continuous narration, and this in and of itself eliminates the exclusion and strikes the one who says it in the face. In conclusion, if we look at the Book of God, it has informed us that it split, but it has not informed us that it will split. If we look at the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it has been proven in the Sahih and other mutawatir chains that this happened during the days of the Prophet. If we look at the statements of the people of knowledge, they have agreed on this, and no attention should be paid to the anomaly of those who anomaly and the exclusion of those who exclude. We will mention some of what was reported on this, God willing. And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, ‘Persistent magic.’ Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: When the moon split, the polytheists said, Muhammad has bewitched us. So God said, And if they see a sign, meaning the splitting of the moon, they turn away from believing in it and saying, Strong, intense magic that surpasses all magic. This is from the saying, Something continues if it becomes strong and solid. A group of people of knowledge have said that the meaning of persistent is strong, intense. Al-Akhfash said: It is taken from passing a rope, which means twisting it tightly. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Dahhak said the same, and An-Nahhas chose it. From this is the saying of Laqit: Until he continued with evil that is not outweighed by the sincerity of his resolve, neither by pity nor by supplication Al-Farra’, Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaidah said: Mashar mursul means going away, from their saying mara something passed by and continued if it went away. Qatada, Mujahid and others said the same, and Al-Nahhas chose it. It was also said that the meaning of mursul is permanent and constant, and from this is the saying of the poet: The world is nothing but nights and ages, and nothing eternal is permanent. That is, permanent and everlasting. It was also said that it is continuous and false. This was also narrated from Abu Ubaidah. It was also said that some parts resemble each other. It was also said that it passed from the earth to the sky. It was also said that it is from bitterness: it is said that something has become bitter, meaning that it is abhorrent to them. And in this verse is the greatest evidence that the split occurred as we have stated previously.
54:3: Then the Almighty mentioned their denial, saying: 3- And they denied and followed their desires meaning, they denied the Messenger of God, and what they witnessed of God's power, and they followed their desires and what the accursed Satan made attractive to them. The phrase and every matter is settled is a new sentence to confirm the invalidity of what they said about denial and following desires: meaning, every matter has an end, so good is settled with the good people, and evil is settled with the evil people. Al-Farra' said: He says, the decision of their denial and the decision of the believers will be settled until they know its reality through reward and punishment. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is that every matter has a reality, what was of it in this world will be made clear, and what was of it in the Hereafter will be known. The majority read steadfast with a kasra on the qaf, and it is raised as the predicate of the subject, which is all. Abu Ja'far and Zayd ibn Ali read it with a genitive, steadfast as an attribute of a matter. Shaybah read it with a fatha on the qaf, and this reading was narrated from Nafi'. Abu Hatim said: It has no basis, and it was said that it has a basis in the omitted noun taddir: meaning, every matter that has stability, or a time of stability, or a place of stability, as a source, or a time adverb, or a place adverb.
54:4: 4- And there has certainly come to them of the report that which is a deterrent meaning, there has certainly come to the unbelievers of Mecca, or the unbelievers in general, of report, which is the report of the lying nations narrated to us in the Qur’an, that which is a deterrent meaning a deterrent, as it is a verbal noun with a mim, it is said: I warned him: if you forbade him from evil and admonished him, and it is possible that it is a place name, and the meaning is: there has come to them that which is a place for a deterrent: meaning that it is in itself a place for that, and its origin is muztajar, and the taa’ of the ifti’al is changed to a dal with the zay, the dal, and the dhal as is established in its place, and Zayd ibn Ali read muzjajar by changing the taa’ of the ifti’al to a zay and adding the zay to the zay, and the min in his saying: of the report is for partiality and it is what it entered into in the place of the accusative case as a state.
54:5: And the elevation of 5- a profound wisdom as a predicate of a deleted subject or a substitute for what each substituted for each, or a substitute of inclusion, and the meaning: that the Qur’an is wisdom that has reached the goal, in which there is no deficiency or defect, and it was read in the accusative as a state of what: that is, the state of what is in it being a deterrent of profound wisdom so what good are vows what may be interrogative and negative: that is, what good are vows or what good are vows at all, and the fa is to arrange the absence of the vessel on the coming of the profound wisdom, and the vow is the plural of a warner meaning the warner, or meaning the warning as a source.
54:6: Then He, the Most High, commanded him to turn away from them, saying: 6- Then turn away from them, meaning turn away from them since the warning did not affect them. This abrogated the verse of the sword, The Day the caller will call to a thing reprehensible. The circumstance was made accusative either by an implied verb: i.e., remember, or they will expel the mentioned after it, or by His saying: Then it will not benefit you, and His saying: Then turn away from them is an interjection, or by His saying: The disbelievers will say.
54:7: Or by saying: 7- Khashai'an and the waw was dropped from yad'u to follow the pronunciation, and it was written like this in the script and the ya' was deleted from da'i to make it easier and the kasra was sufficient, and the da'i is Israfil, and the thing that is unknown: the terrible thing that they deny because they do not know anything like it before. The majority read it with a damma on the kaf. Ibn Kathir read it with a sukoon to make it easier. Mujahid and Qatadah read it with a kasra on the kaf and a fatha on the ra' in the passive form khashai'an absarhim The majority read khashai'an as the plural of khashi'an. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Amr read khashai'an in the singular, and from it the saying of the poet: And young men of good face from Iyad bin Nizar bin Ma'ad Ibn Masoud read it as Khashi’a. Al-Farra’ said: When an adjective precedes a group, it is permissible to be masculine, feminine, or plural: meaning the broken plural, not the sound plural, because it comes from combining two subjects. An example of the reading of the majority is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: My companions stood there on their mounts and said, Do not perish in sorrow and be patient. The word khashu’an is in the accusative case as a state of the agent of they come out or of the pronoun in about them. In sight, khushu’ means submission and humiliation. He added submission and humiliation, and he added khushu’ to sight because honor and humiliation are evident in them. They come out of the graves as if they were locusts spread out meaning they come out of the graves, and the singular of ajdath is jadhth which is the grave, as if they were, due to their large number and the intermingling of some with others, locusts spread out: meaning scattered in the regions, mixed with each other.
54:8: 8- Rushing to the caller Ihta’a means to hasten, meaning he said that they were rushing to the caller, who is Israfil, and from this the poet said: Their home is in the Tigris. I saw them rushing to listen to the Tigris. That is, hastening towards it. Ad-Dahhak said: Coming towards it. Qatadah said: Intending. Ikrimah said: Opening their ears to the sound. The first is more appropriate, and Abu Ubaidah and others said the same. The phrase The disbelievers say, ‘This is a hard day’ is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun rushing towards it. The conjunction is understood or it is a new sentence in response to an understood question, as if it was said, So what will it be then? Hardship means something very difficult. Attributing this statement to the disbelievers is evidence that today is not difficult for the believers.
54:9: Then the Almighty mentioned the details of some of the general report that preceded it, saying: 9- The people of Noah denied before them, meaning they denied their prophet, and in this there is consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. His saying: So they denied Our servant, is an explanation of what came before it of the ambiguous denial, and in it is further confirmation and emphasis: meaning they denied Our servant Noah. It was said that the meaning is: The people of Noah denied the messengers, so they denied Our servant Noah by their denial of the messengers, for he is one of them. Then, the Almighty made it clear that they did not limit themselves to mere denial, saying: And they said, ‘He is mad.’ That is, they accused Noah of madness. His statement, and he was rebuked, is connected to they said, meaning he was rebuked against claiming prophethood and conveying what he was sent with through various forms of rebuke. The letter dal... first is more correct. Mujahid said: It is from the words of God, the Almighty, in which He informed us that he was rebuked and rebuked with insults and various forms of harm. Al-Razi said: This is more correct, because the purpose was to strengthen the heart of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by mentioning those who came before him.
54:10: 10- So he called upon his Lord, 'Indeed, I have been overcome, so help me.' That is, he called upon his Lord against his people, saying, I have been overcome by my people because of their rebellion against obedience and their forbidding me from conveying the message, so help me. That is, take revenge on them for me. He asked his Lord, the Exalted, for victory over them when he despaired of their response and knew of their rebellion, arrogance, and insistence on their misguidance. The majority of scholars read ani with a fat-ha over the hamza, meaning that I. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Al-A'mash read it with a kasra over the hamza. This reading was narrated from Asim, assuming that the statement was omitted: that is, he said.
54:11: Then the Almighty mentioned what He punished them with, saying: 11- So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water, meaning pouring down heavily. Pouring down means pouring abundantly. It is said: the water poured down and the tears flowed abundantly, and from this the poet said: My eyes are filled with tears of joy for the sake of the good of those who came before and after them. And from it is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais describing an eye: The morning will pass by it, then it will turn towards it with a pouring southern wind. The majority read fathana with a light fathaana, while Ibn Amir and Ya'qub read it with a shaddah.
54:12: 12- And We made springs gush forth from the earth meaning We made the entire earth full of gushing springs. The original is We caused the springs of the earth to gush forth. The majority of scholars read fajrna with a shaddah. Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Haywah, and Asim, in one narration from him, read it with a tahfidah. Ubayd ibn Umair said: God inspired the earth to release its water, so springs gushed forth. Then the waters met according to a decree already decreed meaning the water from the sky and the water from the earth met according to a decree that had been decreed for them: that is, in a state that God had decreed and predestined. Ibn Qutaybah related that the meaning is according to a measure, one did not precede the other, rather the water from the sky and the water from the earth were equal. Qatada said: It was decreed for them, when they disbelieved, that they would be drowned. Al-Jahdary read Then the two waters met and Al-Hasan read Then the two waters met. This reading was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib and Muhammad ibn Ka'b.
54:13: 13- And We carried him on planks and nails. That is, We carried Noah on a ship with planks, which are wide pieces of wood. And nails Az-Zajjaj said: They are the nails that hold the planks together, the singular of which is dasar. Anything that is inserted into something to hold it together is a dasr. Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Ibn Zayd, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and others said the same. Al-Hasan, Shahr ibn Hawshab, and Ikrimah said: The dasr is the back of the ship that is hit by waves. It was named thus because it pushes back the water, meaning it repels it. Al-Layth said: The dasar is a thread that holds the planks together. It is said in As-Sahah: The dasar is the singular of dasr, which are threads that hold the planks together, and they are also said to be nails.
54:14: 14- "It runs under Our eyes" meaning under Our sight and vision and protection, as in His statement: "And construct the ark under Our eyes" and it was said by Our command, and it was said by Our revelation, and it was said by the springs springing from the earth, and it was said by the eyes of Our guardian angels charged with guarding it. "A reward for he who disbelieved" Al-Farra' said: We did to him and them what We did of saving him and drowning them as a reward for he who disbelieved in him and rejected his command, and he is Noah, peace be upon him, for he had a blessing that they were ungrateful for, so the word "reward" is in the accusative case as a cause, and it was said as a source with an implied verb: meaning We rewarded them with a reward. The majority of scholars read "disbelieved" in the passive form, and what is meant by it is Noah. It was also said that it refers to God, the Most High, for they disbelieved in him and rejected his blessing. Yazidi bin Ruman, Qatadah, Mujahid, Hamid, and Isa read "disbelieved" with a fat-ha on the kaf and the fa, in the active form: meaning a reward and punishment for he who disbelieved in God.
54:15: 15- And We have certainly left it as a sign meaning that God left the ship as a lesson for those who reflect. It was said that the meaning is: And We have certainly left this action that We did to them as a lesson and admonition. So is there anyone who will remember? Its original form is Mudhtakar, so the ta’ was replaced with a dhal, then the voiced letter was replaced with a dhal because they are close together, and the dhal was assimilated into the dhal. The meaning is: Is there anyone who will take heed and reflect, who will be admonished by this verse and learn from it.
54:16: 16- So how was My punishment and My warning? That is, My warning. Al-Farra' said: Warning and warning are two sources, and the question is for intimidation and amazement: that is, they were in a terrible and wondrous manner that cannot be described. It was said that warning is the plural of warner, and warner means warning like denial means denial.
54:17: 17- And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy to remember meaning, We have made it easy to memorize, and We have helped whoever wants to memorize it. It was also said that We prepared it for remembrance and admonition. So is there any who will remember? meaning, one who will take heed from its admonitions and reflect on its lessons. This verse encourages studying the Qur’an, reciting it frequently, and hastening to learn it. The root of muddkar is muddakar as mentioned earlier. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Anas that “the people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to show them a sign, and he showed them the moon in two halves until they saw Hira’ between them.” It was narrated from him through another chain of transmission by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and others that he said: Then the verse, ‘The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split’ was revealed. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: “The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) into two parts: one part above the mountain and one part below it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘Bear witness.’” ‘Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala’il narrated on his authority that he said: “I saw the moon split into two halves twice: once in Mecca, before the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) left: one part over Abu Qubays and one over as-Suwayda’.” He stated that this was the reason for the revelation of the verse. Ahmad, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu’aym also narrated on his authority that he said: “I saw the moon split. And I saw the mountain between the two halves of the moon.” There are other chains of transmission from him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. He said: That was during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It split into two parts: one part in front of the mountain and the other part behind it. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O God, bear witness. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Jubayr ibn Mut`im, on the authority of Abu, regarding the words: And the moon has split. He said: The moon split while we were in Makkah during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until one part was on this mountain and one part on that mountain. Then the people said: Muhammad has bewitched us. A man said: If he has bewitched you, then he cannot bewitch all of the people. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu’aym narrated on the authority of Abd ar-Rahman as-Sulami who said: “Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman delivered a sermon to us in al-Mada’in, and he praised and glorified God, then he said: ‘The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split.’ Beware, the Hour has drawn near, and beware, the moon split during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Beware, the world has given notice of parting. Today is the racecourse, and tomorrow is the race.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: rushing forward, he said: watching. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: Then We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water. Kathir said: The sky did not rain before or after that day except from clouds, and the gates of heaven were opened with water from other than clouds that day, and the two waters met. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority: on planks and nails. He said: The planks are the planks of the ship, and the nails are its supports with which the ship is tied down. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: and nails, he said: nails. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: nails are like the top of a ship. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi also narrated on his authority regarding his statement: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, he said: If God had not made it easy for the tongue of humans, no one among creation would have been able to speak the words of God. Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Anas, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a similar hadith. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Is there anyone who will remember? He said: Is there anyone who will remember?
54:18: His saying: 18- Aad denied they are the people of Aad so how was My punishment and My warnings meaning listen to how was My punishment and My warnings to them, and warner is a source meaning warning as was explained previously, and the question is for intimidation and glorification.
54:19: 19- Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind. This sentence explains what was summarized previously about the torment. The furious wind is intense cold: that is, an extremely cold wind. It was also said that the furious wind is an intense sound. This was previously explained in Surah Ha Mim As-Sajdah. On a continuous ill-omened day. That is, a day of constant bad luck that continued upon them with its bad luck. They used to consider that day a bad omen. Al-Zajjaj said: It was said that it was on a Wednesday at the end of the month. The majority of scholars read On an ill-omened day by adding day to unlucky with a sukoon on the ha, which is from adding the described to the attribute, or on the assumption of an added word, that is, on a day of ill-omened torment. Al-Hasan read it with the tanween of day so that unlucky is an attribute of it. Harun read it with a kasra on the ha. Ad-Dahhak said: That day was bitter for them. Likewise, Al-Kisa’i narrated on the authority of some people that they said: It is from bitterness, and it was said that it is from marra meaning strength: that is, on a day of strong, steadfast misfortune like something tightly twisted that cannot be broken. And it appears that it is from continuity, not from bitterness nor from marra: that is, the torment continued upon them until it destroyed them, and its destruction included their great and small.
54:20: And sentence 20 - It uproots people is in the accusative case as an attribute of the wind or a state of it. It may be a new sentence: that is, it uproots them from the ground from under their feet as a palm tree is uprooted from its roots. Mujahid said: It would uproot them from the ground and throw them on their heads, breaking their necks and separating their heads from their bodies. It was also said that it would pull people from their houses, and it was also said that it would pull people from their graves because they dug holes and entered them. As if they were hollowed-out trunks of palm trees. “A’jaz” is the plural of ajz, which is the back of something. Munqar means that which is cut off and uprooted from its root. It is said that you uprooted the palm tree: if you uprooted it from its root until it falls. He likened their height when the wind tossed them and threw them on their faces to palm trees that have fallen to the ground without heads. This is because the wind first uprooted their heads and then wrote them on their faces. Munqar is masculine, although it is an attribute of A’jaz of palm trees, and it is feminine based on the wording. It is permissible to feminize it based on the meaning, as he said, Empty palm tree trunks. Al-Mubarrad said: Everything that comes to you from this chapter, if you wish, you can return it to the wording as masculine or to the meaning as feminine. It has been said that the date palm and the palm trees are mentioned in this chapter, if you wish, you can return it to the masculine form of the word or to the feminine form of the word. It has also been said that the date palm and the palm trees are both masculine and feminine.
54:21: 21- How was My punishment and My warnings? Its interpretation was presented shortly.
54:22: And likewise His saying: 22- And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
54:23: Then when He, the Most High, mentioned the denial of Aad, He followed it with the denial of Thamud, saying: 23- Thamud denied the warnings. It is possible that it is the plural of nadhir, meaning they denied the messengers sent to them. It is possible that it is a source meaning warning, meaning they denied the warning with which they were warned. Their denial of their messenger, who was righteous, was a denial of the messengers, because whoever denies one of the prophets with whom they were warned, their denial of their messenger, who was righteous, was a denial of the messengers, because whoever denies one of the prophets has denied all of them, because they agreed in calling to the generalities of the laws.
54:24: 24- "They said, 'Is it a human being from among us that we should follow?' The question is for denial: how can we follow a human being who is from our kind, isolated and alone, with no one to follow him in what he calls for? The majority of scholars read the verse with the accusative case of basharan as an emphasis on preoccupation: that is, should we follow a single human being? Abu as-Samak, ad-Dani, Abu as-Ashab, and Ibn as-Samee' read it with the nominative case as the subject, with wahid as its adjective, and natabuhu as its predicate. It was narrated from Abu as-Samak that he read with the nominative case of basharan and the accusative case of wahid as a state. Indeed, then we would be in error, meaning if we follow him, we would be in error and straying from the truth. And a blaze, meaning torment, hardship, and severity. This is what al-Farra' and others said. Abu Ubaidah said: It is the plural of sa'eer, which is the flame of fire, and sa'ar means madness that goes thus and thus due to the intensity with which it is inflamed. Mujahid said: And blaze and distance from the truth. Al-Saddī said: In burning. It was said that what is meant by it here is madness, from their saying: A mad camel, meaning that it is as if it is mad from the intensity of its activity. From this comes the saying of the poet describing a camel: You think it is a price, but the price shakes it and the rhythm of walking is tiring
54:25: Then they repeated their denial and exclusion, saying: 25- Was the Reminder sent down to him from among us? That is, how was he singled out from among us for revelation and prophethood, while there is one among us who is more deserving of that than him? Then they stopped their denial and moved on to asserting that he was a wicked liar, saying: Rather, he is a wicked liar. Ashr means joy and activity, or arrogance and haughtiness, and interpreting it as arrogance and haughtiness is more appropriate to the situation, and from this is the saying of the poet: You mentioned wearing silk when you wore it, and before that you do not know who conquered the villages. The majority read ashr as farah. Abu Qilabah and Abu Ja'far read it with a fatha on the shin and a shaddah on the ra', as if it were a comparative form. Al-Kisa'i narrated from Mujahid that he read it with a damma on the shin and a fatha on the hamza.
54:26: Then the Almighty answered them by saying: 26- They will know tomorrow who is the most evil liar. What is meant by His saying tomorrow is the time when the punishment will descend upon them in this world, or on the Day of Resurrection, following the people’s custom of expressing tomorrow in reference to the future of a matter, even if it is far away, as in their saying: There is tomorrow with today, and as in the saying of Al-Hutay’ah: Death has arrows that do not miss. He who is not dead today will die tomorrow. And from it is the saying of Abu Al-Tammah: O cure me before the wailing of the mourners, and it was said that the soul is disturbed between the sides And the day before tomorrow, how I long for a tomorrow when my friends have left and I am not going The majority of scholars read they will know with a sub-domain, as God informing Salih of the punishment that would befall them after a period of time. Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Hamzah read it with a sub-domain, as if it were a speech from Salih to his people.
54:27: And the sentence 27 - Indeed, We will send the she-camel is a resumption of the statement of what was previously summarized of the threat: that is, We will bring her out of the rock according to what they suggested as a trial for them meaning a test and trial, and the word trial is in the accusative case as a reason so watch them meaning wait for what they do and be patient with whatever harm befalls you from them.
54:28: 28- And inform them that the water is to be divided between them, that is, between Thamud and the she-camel. She has a day and they have a day, as in His statement: She has a drink and you have a drink on a known day. And He said: Inform them using the pronoun of rational beings, to emphasize every drink is to be divided. Drinking, with a kasra on the sheen, is the water. The meaning of divided is that whoever owns it brings it, so the she-camel brings it one day and they bring it one day. Mujahid said: Thamud brings the water on their turn, so they drink and they bring it on the day of her turn, so they milk it. The majority read divided with a kasra on the qaf, meaning divided. Abu Amr read it in a narration from him with a fatha.
54:29: 29- So they called their companion meaning Thamud called their companion, who was Qidar bin Salaf, who had hamstrung the she-camel, urging him to hamstring them. So he took it upon himself and hamstrung it meaning he took the she-camel by hamstringing it, or he dared to take the means of hamstringing it, so he hamstrung it. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: He ambushed it at the base of a tree on its way, so he shot it with an arrow, which pierced its calf muscle. Then he attacked it with the sword, breaking its Achilles tendon, then he slaughtered it. To take something with effort is to take it upon oneself.
54:30: 30- How will be My punishment and My warnings? An explanation of this has been presented in this Surah.
54:31: Then he explained the torment in general, saying: 31- Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast. Ata’ said: He means the blast of Gabriel. This has been explained previously in Surah Hud and in Al-A’raf. And they were like chaff from a garden. The majority of scholars read it with a kasra on the Dhad. Chaff is the debris and dry remains of trees. Al-Mutahazar is the owner of a pen, and he is the one who makes a pen for his sheep to protect them from the cold wind. It is said that he made a pen for his sheep: if he gathered the trees and placed some on top of others. It is said in Al-Sahah: Al-Mutahazar is the one who makes the pen. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Abu Al-Aaliyah read it with a fatha on the Dhad: meaning like the chaff from a garden. So who is the one who makes the pen? Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Abu Al-Aaliyah read it with a fatha on the dhal: meaning like dry stubble in a pen. Whoever reads it with a kasra means the agent of the enclosure, and whoever reads it with a fatha means the enclosure. It is a fa’ila with the meaning of maf’ula. The meaning of the verse is that they became like trees when they dry up in the pen and the sheep trample them after they fall. From this is the saying of the poet: They raised a fume like the smoke of a fire that ignites a scorched dry stubble. Qatada said: It is the rotten, burnt bones. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the dust scattered from the walls on a windy day. Sufyan al-Thawri said: It is what scatters from the enclosure if you hit it with a stick. Ibn Zayd said: The Arabs call everything that was wet and then dries straw, and from this the poet said: He saw the carcasses of the camels lying beside him, as if their bones were dry wood.
54:32: 32- And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? An explanation of this has already been presented in this Surah.
54:33: Then God Almighty informed us about the people of Lot, that they denied the messengers of God, just as others denied them, and He said: 33- The people of Lot denied the warning. The interpretation of the warning was presented shortly.
54:34: Then the Almighty explained how He punished them, saying: 34- Indeed, We sent upon them a hurricane, meaning a wind that pelted them with pebbles, which are gravel. Abu Ubaidah and Andar ibn Shumayl said: Hasib means stones in the wind. It is stated in As-Sahah: “Hasib is a strong wind that stirs up pebbles, and from this is the saying of Ar-Razdaq: We are receiving report from the north of Syria that it will be hit by hailstones like cotton wool. "Except the family of Lot. We saved them by dawn" meaning Lot and those who followed him. The dawn is the last part of the night. It was also said that in Arabic it means the mixing of the blackness of the night with the whiteness of the early morning. The word "dark" was declined because it is an indefinite noun and was not intended to refer to the dark of a specific night. If it had been intended to refer to a specific person, it would have been impossible. This is what Az-Zajjaj, Al-Akhfash and others said.
54:35: And the accusative of 35- A blessing from Us is based on the cause, or on the source: meaning a blessing from Us upon Lot and those who followed him. Thus do We reward whoever is grateful. Meaning, in this way do We reward whoever is grateful for Our blessing and does not deny it.
54:36: 36- And he had warned them of Our punishment meaning Lot warned his people of God’s punishment upon them, which is His severe torment and ultimate punishment. But they disputed about the warning meaning they doubted the warning and did not believe it. It is derived from the verb mariyah, which means doubt.
54:37: 37- And they had already sought to seduce him from his guest meaning they wanted him to enable the angels who had come to him to commit adultery with them, as is their custom. It is said, I sought him from something in a sedative or a provocative way: meaning I wanted him. The verb to seek means to ask for something. The explanation of seeking has already been given in full in Surah Hud. Then We blinded their eyes meaning We made their eyes obliterated so that no slit could be seen, just as the wind blinds landmarks with the dust it blows over them. It has also been said that God took away the light of their sight while the eyes remained as they were. Ad-Dahhak said, “God blinded their sight, so they did not see the messengers, so they returned. “Then taste My punishment and My warning” has already been given in this surah.
54:38: 38- And indeed, early in the morning, a lasting torment overtook them. That is, an established torment came to them early in the morning, descending upon them that would never leave them or cease. Muqatil said: The torment came to them early in the morning. The word early in the morning refers to the fact that it did not refer to a specific time, as previously mentioned in at dawn.
54:39: 39- So taste my torment and my warning.
54:40: 40- “So taste My punishment and My warning. And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?” The explanation of this has already been presented in this surah. Perhaps the reason for repeating the Qur’an’s making it easy for remembrance in this surah is to indicate that it is a great blessing for which no one should neglect to be grateful. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: {Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind}, he said: cold, on an unlucky day, he said: days of hardship. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Wednesday is a day of continuous unluckiness. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on his authority from another chain of transmission, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Ali, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), in which it says: “It was said: How is that, O Messenger of God? He said: God drowned Pharaoh and his people on it, and destroyed ‘Aad and Thamud on it.” Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Al-Suyuti said: It is weak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The last Wednesday of the month is a day of continuous unluckiness. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on their authority: As if they were trunks of palm trees, he said: The roots of the palm trees, Dug out, he said: Uprooted. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: The black trunks of date palms. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority: And a price he said: Misery. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority, he said: Like the dry stubble of a burning tree he said: Like the burnt enclosures of trees. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: Like the burnt bones. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority, he said: Like the grass that sheep eat.
54:41: 41- The vow may be the plural of nadhir, or it may be a source meaning warning, as mentioned above, and they are the signs with which Moses warned them.
54:42: This is more appropriate for His statement: 42- They denied all Our signs, for it is an explanation of that, and what is meant by it are the nine signs that were mentioned previously, So We seized them with the grip of the Almighty, the Powerful, meaning We seized them with punishment with the grip of the Almighty in His vengeance, the One capable of destroying them, and nothing is beyond His power.
54:43: Then the Almighty frightened the disbelievers of Mecca, saying: 43- Your disbelievers are better than those? The question is for denial, and the meaning is negation: that is, your disbelievers, O people of Mecca, or O group of Arabs, are not better than the disbelievers of Mecca from the nations that came before you who were destroyed because of their disbelief, so how can you hope to be safe from the punishment when you are worse than them. Then the Almighty turned away from that and moved to rebuke them in another way that is more severe than the rebuke in the first way, so He said: Or do you have immunity in the scriptures? The scriptures are the books revealed to the prophets, and the meaning is: denying that they have immunity from the punishment of God in any of the scriptures of the prophets.
54:44: Then he turned away from this rebuke and moved on to rebuke them in another way, saying: 44- Or do they say, ‘We are all victorious’? That is, a group that cannot be tolerated due to our large numbers and strength, or our matter is one and we cannot be defeated. He used the singular word victory in consideration of the word all. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is that we are all victorious over our enemies.
54:45: God responded to them by saying: 45- The assembly will be defeated meaning the assembly of the infidels of Mecca, or the infidels of the Arabs in general. The majority read Sayyahma with a lower case passive voice. Warsh, on the authority of Ya'qub, read Sayyahma with a noon and a kasra on the zay and the plural was accusative. Abu Haywah and Ibn Abi Ubla read it with a lower case active voice. It was also read with a higher case active voice. And they will turn their backs The majority read Yulun with a lower case. Isa, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Warsh, on the authority of Ya'qub, read it with a higher case in the direct address form. What is meant by Dabr is the genus, and it means retreat. God defeated them on the day of Badr and they turned their backs, and the leaders of polytheism and the legends of disbelief were killed. So praise be to God.
54:46: 46- Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, meaning the appointed time for their punishment in the Hereafter. This punishment in this world, in the form of killing, captivity, and oppression, is not the full measure of the punishment they were promised, but rather it is an introduction to it and a vanguard of its signs. For this reason, He said: And the Hour is more terrible and bitter, meaning the punishment of the Hour is more severe and more horrific. It is taken from dahaan, which means monstrousness and horror. The meaning of amr is more bitter than the punishment of this world. It is said that something bad befell him, meaning that something bad and terrible befell him.
54:47: 47- Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness. That is, they are straying from the truth and far from it. The explanation of madness has already been presented in this surah, so we will not repeat it.
54:48: 48- The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces.
