Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: Except for one verse that was revealed in Medina, which is the verse: And you make your provision that you lie. Al-Kalbi said: It is Meccan except for four verses, which are: Is it then that you are in vain? And you make your provision that you lie. And His saying: A group of the former peoples * And a few of the latter ones. Ibn Ad-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Waqi'ah was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from Ibn Az-Zubayr. Abu Ubaid in his Fada'il, Ibn Ad-Durais, Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu'b narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: Whoever recites Surat Al-Waqi'ah at night will never be afflicted with poverty. Ibn Asakir narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Surat Al-Waqi'ah is the Surat of wealth, so recite it and teach it to your children. Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Teach your women Surat Al-Waqi’ah, for it is the Surat of wealth. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hud Al-Waqi’ah has made my hair turn grey. End quote. His saying: 1- If the event occurs. The event is the name of the Resurrection, like the approaching and others. It is called an event because it will inevitably occur, or because its occurrence is close, or because of the many hardships that will occur in it. The accusative of if is with an implied pronoun: that is, I remember the occurrence of the event.
56:2: Or by the negation implied by his saying: 2- Its occurrence will not be a lie meaning there will be no denial when it occurs, and the liar is a verbal noun like the consequence: meaning there is no lie in its coming and appearance at all, and it was said that if it is conditional and its answer is understood: meaning if it occurs then such and such, and this answer is the factor in it, and it was said that it is conditional, and the factor in it is the verb that comes after it, and Abu Hayyan chose this, and Makki preceded him in this and said: and the factor is occurred. The commentators said: The occurrence here is the last blast, and the meaning of the verse is that if the last blast occurs at the resurrection there will be no denial of it at all, or there will be no soul that lies about God and denies what He has informed about the matters of the afterlife. Al-Zajjaj said: Its occurrence will not be a lie: meaning nothing will repel it, and Al-Hasan and Qatadah said the same. Al-Nawawi said: No one will deny its occurrence. Al-Kisa’i said: It cannot be denied: meaning, no one should deny it.
56:3: 3- Khafidah Rafi'ah The majority of scholars read them in the nominative case, implying a subject: i.e. it is a khafidah raf'ah. Al-Hasan and Isa Al-Thaqafi read them in the accusative case, as a state. Ikrimah, Al-Suddi and Muqatil said: I lowered my voice and made those near hear, and I raised my voice and made those far hear: i.e. I made those near and far hear. Qatada said: I lowered some people to the torment of God, and I raised some people to the obedience of God. Muhammad bin Ka'b said: I lowered some people who were exalted in this world, and I raised some people who were humbled in this world. The Arabs use khafidah and raf' to denote place, position, honor and humiliation, and the khafidah and raf' are attributed to them metaphorically, and the one who lowers and raises in reality is God, the Most High.
56:4: 4- When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking meaning if it is moved with a violent movement. It is said that he shook it, shaking it, if he moved it. The shaking is the disturbance, and the sea was shaken and turbulent. The commentators said: It shakes as a baby shakes in its cradle until everything on it collapses and everything is broken, from the mountains and other things. Qatada, Muqatil and Mujahid said: The meaning of shaken is quake-quake, and the adverbial phrase is related to His statement lowering and raising meaning it is lowered and raised at the time of the earth's shaking and the mountains' shaking, because at that time what is low is raised and what is high is lowered. It was said that it is a substitute for the adverbial phrase, and the first was mentioned by Al-Zajjaj, so the meaning of the occurrence of the event is the earth's shaking and the mountains' shaking.
56:5: 5- And the mountains were dried up Al-Basa means to break. It is said: Basa means to break something up until it becomes crumbs. It is also said: Bas al-Sawiq means to knead it with ghee or oil. Mujahid and Muqatil said: The meaning is that the mountains were crushed into crumbs. Al-Suddi said: It was broken into pieces. Al-Hasan said: It was split from its roots. Mujahid also said: Basa as flour is dried with ghee or oil. The meaning is: It was mixed and became like twisted flour. Abu Zaid said: Al-Basa al-Souq, and the meaning according to this is: The mountains were driven in a market. Abu Ubaid said: Bas al-Ibil and Absaha are two languages: if he urged the camels on. Ikrimah said: The meaning is: It led them on.
56:6: 6- So it was scattered dust meaning scattered dust. Mujahid said: Scattered dust is the ray that is in a niche like dust. It was also said that it is the lightning that shines from the hooves of beasts and then goes away. It was also said that it is what flies from the fire when it is blazing, according to Surat Al-Sharrar, and when it falls it is nothing. Its explanation was presented in Al-Furqan when explaining His statement: So We made it scattered dust. The majority of scholars read scattered with the dot on the letter taa'. Masruq, An-Nakha'i, and Abu Haywah read it with the dot on the letter taa' above: meaning cut off, from their saying Batahu God meaning He cut it off.
56:7: Then the Almighty mentioned the conditions of people and their differences, saying: 7- And you were three groups. The address is to all people or to the present nation, and the groups are the classes, and the meaning is: And you were on that day three groups.
56:8: Then the Almighty explained these categories and said: 8- Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? That is, the companions of the right, and they are the ones who take their books in their right hands, or those who are taken to the right to Paradise. The companions of the right is the subject, and its predicate is: what are the companions of the right? That is, what are they in their state and description? The question is for glorification and emphasis, and repeating the subject here with its emphasis is sufficient for the connecting pronoun, as in His saying: The Inevitable * What is the Inevitable? “The Calamity * What is the Calamity?” Such a thing is not permissible except in situations of glorification and emphasis.
56:9: 9- The discussion of the companions of the left, who are the companions of the left? is like the discussion of the companions of the right, who are the companions of the right. What is meant is those who will be taken to the left to the Fire or who will take their records of deeds in their left hands. The intended meaning is to astonish the listener at the state of the two groups in terms of grandeur and horror, as if it were said: The companions of the right are in the ultimate state of happiness and goodness, and the companions of the left are in the ultimate state of misery and badness. Al-Suddi said: The companions of the right are those who were on Adam’s right when the offspring were taken from his loins, and the companions of the left are those who were on his left. Zayd ibn Aslam said: The companions of the right are those who were taken from Adam’s right side, and the companions of the left are those who were taken from his left side. Ibn Jurayj said: The companions of the right are the people of good deeds, and the companions of the left are the people of bad deeds. Al-Hasan and Al-Rabi’ said: The companions of the right are those who are auspicious to themselves with good deeds, and the companions of the left are those who are ominous to themselves with ugly deeds. Al-Mubarrad said: The people of the right are the ones who are ahead, and the people of the left are the ones who are behind. The Arabs say: Put me on your right and do not put me on your left, meaning put me among those who are ahead and do not put me among those who are behind. From this is the saying of Ibn al-Damina: My daughters, have you placed me in your right hand so that I may rejoice, or have you placed me in your left?
56:10: Then the Almighty mentioned the third category, saying: 10- And the foremost, the foremost. The repetition in this is for emphasis and glorification, as mentioned in the first two sections, just as you say you, you and Zayd, Zayd. The foremost is the subject, and its predicate is the foremost. There are two interpretations for this: One is that it means the foremost are those who are the first to faith, the first to Paradise. The first is more appropriate because it indicates emphasis and glorification. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They are the first to faith from his words. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: They are the prophets. Ibn Sirin said: They are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs. Mujahid said: They are those who were the first to jihad, and Ad-Dahhak said the same. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They are the first to repentance and righteous deeds. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: And the first to obey God are the first to receive God's mercy.
56:12: It has been said that the reason for delaying this third category, despite it being more honorable than the first two, is that it is coupled with what comes after it, which is His statement: 12- Those are the ones brought near * in the gardens of delight. The reference is to them: that is, those brought near to the abundant reward of God and the greatness of His honor, or those whose degrees have been brought near and whose positions have been elevated with God. His statement in the gardens of delight is related to those brought near: that is, those brought near to God in the gardens of delight. It is permissible for it to be a second predicate for those, or to be a state of the pronoun in those brought near: that is, being in them. The majority of scholars read in gardens in the plural, while Talhah ibn Musarraf read in a garden in the singular. Adding gardens to blessings is like adding a place to what is in it, just as one says: the house of hospitality, the house of da’wah, and the house of justice.
56:13: And the height of 13- A group of the ancients as a predicate of a deleted subject: meaning they are a group, and a group whose number is not limited. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of a group is a division, from thallalat something: if you cut it up, and what is meant by the ancients are the previous nations from Adam to our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
56:14: 14- And a few of the others meaning from this nation. They were called few in relation to those who came before them, but they are many because of the large number of prophets among them and the large number of those who answered them. Al-Hasan said: The forerunners of those who came before are more numerous than our forerunners. Al-Zajjaj said: “Those who saw all the prophets and believed in them are more than those who saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This does not contradict what is proven in the Sahih from his saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): ‘I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise. ’ Then he said: ‘A third of the people of Paradise. ’ Then he said: ‘Half of the people of Paradise.’” This is because his saying: A group of the first and a few of the last is only a preference for the forerunners, as will come in the mention of the people of the right hand, that they are a group of the first and a group of the last. So it is not impossible that among the people of the right hand of this nation there are those who are more numerous than the people of the right hand than others, so from the few of the forerunners of this nation and from the group of the people of the right hand there are those who will constitute half of the people of Paradise. The comparison between the two thirds of the people of the right hand does not necessitate their equality, as it is permissible to say: This group is more than this group, and this group is more than this group, and this group is more than this group, and this group is more than this group. Thus you will know that those who said that this verse was abrogated by the aforementioned hadith were not correct.
56:15: Then the Almighty mentioned another state of the foremost and the close ones, saying: 15- On lined couches. The majority read couches with a damma on the seen and the first ra’, while Abu Al-Sammak and Zaid bin Ali read it with a fatha on the ra’, and it is a language as mentioned above. Mowdoo’a means woven, and Wadhan means doubled weaving. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: Woven with gold bars, and it was said: Interlaced with pearls, rubies, and emeralds, and it was said that Mowdoo is arranged in rows. Mujahid said: Mowdoo is that which is lined with gold.”
56:16: 16- reclining on them is in the accusative case, and so is the accusative case of facing each other and the meaning is: settling on couches reclining on them facing each other, not looking at each other’s backs.
56:17: 17- And there will circulate around them immortal youths. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state of those brought near, or it is a new sentence to explain some of the bliss that God has prepared for them. The meaning is that there will circulate around them to serve them, young boys who will neither grow old nor change, but will always look like young boys. Mujahid said: The meaning is they will never die. Al-Hasan and Al-Kalbi said: They will neither grow old nor change. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say about a man who has grown old and has not combed his hair that he is immortal. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Immortal and well-earned. Al-Farra' said: It is also said: Immortal and well-earned. It is said that he adorned his slave girl with immortality, which is an earring. Ikrimah said: Immortal and well-off. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qais: And who enjoys nothing but the eternally happy, the carefree, the one who does not go to bed in distress? It was said that they were covered with ornaments, and something similar was narrated on the authority of Al-Farra’, and from it is the saying of the poet: And immortalized in silver, as if their buttocks were the highest of the dunes. It was said that they are immortal and logical. It was said that they are the children of Muslims who die young and have no good or bad deeds. It was also said that they are the children of polytheists, and it is not far-fetched that they were created in Paradise to perform this service. The cups are the round-mouthed goblets that have no ears or handles. The meaning of this has been explained in Surat Az-Zukhruf. The pitchers are those with handles and spouts. The singular is a pitcher, which is the one whose color shines from its clarity.
56:18: 18- And a cup from a spring meaning from running wine or flowing water. What is meant here is the wine flowing from springs. The meaning of the cup has been explained previously in Surat As-Saffat.
56:19: 19- They will not have a headache from it meaning their heads will not have a headache from drinking it as they do from drinking worldly wine. Headache is the well-known disease that afflicts a person's head. It was said that the meaning of they will not have a headache is that they will not scatter as wine scatters. This meaning is strengthened by Mujahid's reading of they will not have a headache with a fat-ha on the yaa and a shaddah on the saad. The original is yatasda'du meaning they will scatter. The sentence is resumed to explain what God has prepared for them of bliss, or in the accusative case as a state. The sentence and they will not be intoxicated is conjoined with the sentence before it. The differences of the reciters regarding this letter of Surat As-Saffat have already been mentioned, and its explanation has also been mentioned: meaning they will not become intoxicated so that their minds go away, from anzaf the drinker: if his mind or drink runs out. From this is the saying of the poet: By my life, whether you bleed or wake up, you, the family of Abjara, will be bad companions.
56:20: 20- And fruits from what they choose meaning what they select. It is said: I chose something if you took the best of it. The majority of scholars read and fruits in the accusative case.
56:21: 21- And and meat in apposition to cups: meaning they will be served these things that are eaten, drunk, and enjoyed. Zayd ibn Ali, Abu Ali, and Abu Abd al-Rahman read it with the subject in the nominative case, and the predicate is understood: meaning they will have fruit and meat, and the meaning of of what they desire is of what they wish for and what their souls desire.
56:23: 23- And wide-eyed houris * Like hidden pearls. The majority of scholars read wide-eyed houris in the nominative case in apposition to boys or as a subject: meaning their women are wide-eyed houris, or as a predicate: meaning they will have wide-eyed houris. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read them in the genitive case in apposition to cups. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for it to be in apposition to gardens: meaning they are in gardens and among wide-eyed houris, estimating a deleted noun: meaning and in the company of wide-eyed houris. Al-Farra' said: Regarding explaining the apposition to cups, it is permissible to use the genitive case in accordance with the wording, even if they differ in meaning, because the wide-eyed houris are not to be walked around, as in the poet's saying: If the prostitutes appear one day and raise their eyebrows and eyes The eye is not glazed, but is lined with kohl. This is why the poet said: I fed her straw and cold water. And the other said: Armed with a sword and a spear Qatrib said: It is connected to the cups and pitchers without being based on the meaning. He said: It is not objectionable that they will be served with wide-eyed houris: and they will have pleasure in that. Al-Ashab Al-Uqaili, Al-Nakha’li, and Isa bin Omar read it in the accusative case, estimating an implied verb, as if it were said: And they will be married to wide-eyed houris, or they will be given. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred the reading of the majority. Then the Almighty likened them to hidden pearls, which are those that have not been touched by hands nor dust has fallen on them, so they are extremely pure.
56:24: The object of the word jaza'a in His statement: 24- A recompense for what they used to do" is the object of the verb: meaning that all of that will be done to them as a recompense for their deeds. It may also be a verbal noun emphasizing a deleted verb: meaning that they will be recompensed with a recompense. The explanation of the wide-eyed houris has been presented previously in Surat At-Tur and elsewhere.
56:25: 25- They will hear therein no idle talk or sinful speech. Idle talk is false speech, and sinful speech is the relation to sin. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: They will not blame one another. Mujahid said: They will hear no cursing or sinful speech. The meaning is that they will not say to one another, You have sinned, because they will not speak about anything that is sinful.
56:26: 26- "Except for the word 'Peace, peace'" The word 'saying' is the saying, and the exception is disjunctive: meaning but they say a word, or they hear a word, and the accusative of 'Peace, peace' is on the basis that it is a substitute for 'saying', or an attribute of it, or it is the object of 'saying': meaning except that they say 'Peace, peace'. Al-Zajjaj chose this: or on the basis that it is accusative with a verb that is narrated by 'saying': meaning except that they say 'peace, peace', and the meaning of the verse is that they do not hear anything except the greeting of one another. 'Ata' said: They greet one another with 'peace'. It was said that the exception is connected, which is far-fetched, because the greeting is not among what falls under idle talk and sin. 'Peace, peace' was read in the nominative case. Maki said: The nominative case is permissible in the sense of 'peace be upon you' as a subject and predicate. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, When the Event occurs, he said: on the Day of Resurrection. There is no denier of its occurrence, he said: it can never be averted. Having lowered and raised, he said: it lowers some people and raises others. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, Having lowered and raised, he said: it makes the near and the far hear. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Umar ibn Al-Khattab, Having lowered and raised, he said: the Hour will lower the enemies of God to the Fire and raise the friends of God to Paradise. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, When the earth is shaken with a mighty shaking, he said: it is quaked. And the mountains are crushed, he said: they are shattered. And they are like scattered dust, he said: the rays of the sun. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, And they are like scattered dust, he said: the dust that flies from the fire when it is lit, sparks fly from it, but when it falls, it is nothing. Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him that he said: Dust is what stirs up with the sun’s rays, and its scattering is its dispersion. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ali bin Abi Talib that he said: The scattered dust is the tumult of the beasts, and the scattered dust is the sun’s dust that you see in the rays of a window. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, And you were pairs, he said: types. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement, And you were three pairs, he said: It is the one in Surat Al-Mala’ikah, “Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds.” Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding his statement, And the foremost are the foremost, he said: Joshua bin Nun preceded Moses, the believer of the family of Yasin preceded Jesus, and Ali bin Abi Talib preceded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, saying: It was revealed about Ezekiel, the believer of the family of Pharaoh, and Habib the carpenter who was mentioned in Yasin, and Ali ibn Abi Talib. Each of them was foremost in his nation, and Ali was the best of them in foremost. Ahmad narrated on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘And the companions of the right’ and ‘The companions of the left’. He took two handfuls of food and said: ‘This one is in Paradise and I do not care, and this one is in Hell and I do not care.’” Ahmad also narrated on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Do you know who will be the first to enter the shade of God on the Day of Resurrection? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Those who, when given what is due, accept it, and when asked, give generously, and judge for the people as they judge for themselves. Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: When the verse, A group of the former peoples and a few of the latter ones, was revealed, the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were distressed, so the verse, A group of the former peoples and a group of the latter ones, was revealed. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of Paradise. Rather, you are half of the people of Paradise, or half of the people of Paradise, and you will share the other half with them.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba’th on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On lined couches, meaning: arranged in rows. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Hanad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba’th on his authority. He said: lined with gold. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in Sifat al-Jannah, al-Bazzar, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba’th on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me, You look at a bird in Paradise and desire it, and it falls down roasted before you. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Dhiya’ narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The birds of Paradise are like camels grazing among the trees of Paradise. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, these birds are soft. He said: I eat them softer than them, and I hope that you will be among those who eat from them. There are hadiths on this topic. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement: like hidden pearls, he said: those in shells. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: They will not hear therein any idle talk, he said: falsehood, nor sinful talk, he said: lying.
56:27: When God Almighty finished mentioning the conditions of those who came before and what He had prepared for them of eternal bliss, He mentioned the conditions of the people of the right hand, saying: 27- And the people of the right hand - what are the people of the right hand? We have already presented the parsing of this statement and what is in this interrogative sentence of glorification and magnification, and it is the predicate of the subject, which is the people of the right hand.
56:28: And His statement: 28- In thornless lote trees is a second predicate or predicate of a deleted subject: meaning they are in thornless lote trees, and the lote tree is a type of tree, and thornless is that which has its thorns cut off: meaning it has been cut off so it has no thorns. Umayyah ibn al-Salt said, describing Paradise: The gardens in Paradise are shady, with young maidens, whose lote trees are adorned with green leaves. Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: The green, venerated lote tree is a burden.
56:29: 29- And Talh, arranged in layers. Most commentators said: The Talh in the verse refers to the banana tree. A group said: It is not the banana tree, but the well-known Talh, which is the greatest tree of the Arabs. Al-Farra' and Abu Ubaidah said: It is a large tree with thorns. Al-Zajjaj said: The Talh refers to Umm Ghailan, and she has a pleasant light, so they were addressed and promised what they loved, except that its superiority over what is in this world is like the superiority of everything else in Paradise over what is in this world. He said: It is possible that it is in Paradise with its thorns removed. Al-Suddi said: The Talh of Paradise is similar to the Talh of this world, but its fruit is sweeter than honey. And the arranged: is the overlapping that has been arranged from beginning to end with the fruit and has no prominent stems. Masruq said: The trees of Paradise, from their roots to their branches, are all arranged in layers of fruit. Whenever they take a fruit, something better returns to its place.
56:30: 30- And an extended shade meaning permanent and everlasting, that does not disappear or become undone by the sun. Abu Ubaidah said: The Arabs say for everything long and uninterrupted extended, and from this is His statement: Have you not seen how your Lord extended the shade? And Paradise is all shade with no sun beside it. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: He means the shade of the throne. Among the Arabs' usage of extended to mean permanent and uninterrupted is the statement of Labid: The invasion was victorious, but it was not victorious, a long, permanent, extended period
56:31: 31- And poured water meaning that it flows day and night wherever they want, without stopping from them. It is poured, and God pours it into its channels. The root of pouring is pouring. It is said that he poured it, meaning he poured it.
56:32: 32- And many fruits meaning many and varied colors.
56:33: 33- It is not cut off at any time, just as the fruits of this world are cut off at certain times, nor forbidden, meaning it is not prevented from whoever wants it at any time or in any way. Rather, it is prepared for whoever wants it, with nothing standing between them and it. Ibn Qutaybah said: This means that it is not forbidden to them, just as it is forbidden to the orchards of this world.
56:34: 34- And raised couches meaning raised one above the other, or raised on beds. It has been said that the couches here are a metaphor for the women in Paradise, and their height is because they are on couches, or because they are of high status in beauty and perfection.
56:35: 35- Indeed, We created them a new creation meaning We created them a new creation without procreation. It was said that what is meant is the women of the children of Adam, and the meaning is that God Almighty returned them after death to a state of youth. Even if no mention was made of women, they have entered into the companions of the right hand. As for the saying of those who said that the raised couches are the women, then the reference of the pronoun is clear.
56:36: 36- So We made them virgins “whom no human or jinn had touched before them.”
56:37: 37- Araban atrab Arab is the plural of ‘arub, which means the woman who is beloved by her husband. Al-Mubarrad said: She is the woman who is in love with her husband, and from this is the saying of Labid: In the tent is a pure, not obscene bride, with beautiful rumps, whose light blinds the eyes. Zayd ibn Aslam said: She is the one who speaks well. The majority of readers read it with a damma on the ‘ayn and the ra’. Hamzah and Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim read it with a sukoon on the ra’ and they are two languages in the plural of fa’ul. Atrab are those who are of the same birth and age. Mujahid said: Atrab are examples and shapes. Al-Suddi said: Atrab in morals, there is no hatred or envy between them.
56:38: His statement: 38- For the companions of the right hand is related to We created them or We made or of equal age, and the meaning is: that God created them for them or created them for them or they are equal in age to the companions of the right hand, or it is report for a deleted subject: that is, they are for the companions of the right hand.
56:39: 39- A group of the first ones.
56:40: 40- A group from the first and a group from the last. This refers to His statement: And the companions of the right hand - what are the companions of the right hand? That is, they are a group from the first and a group from the last. The explanation of a group was presented when mentioning the first, and the meaning is: that they are a group or nation or sect or segment from the first, and they are from Adam to our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And a group or nation or sect or segment from the last, and they are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, and Ad-Dahhak said: A group from the first. Meaning, from the first of this nation, and a group from the last of this nation from its end.
56:41: Then when He, glory be to Him, finished what He had prepared for the people of the right, He began to mention the people of the left and what He had prepared for them, saying: 41- And the people of the left - what are the people of the left? The discussion is about the grammatical analysis of this and what it contains of glorification, as was previously mentioned in the case of the people of the right.
56:42: His statement: 42- "In scorching winds and scalding water" is either a second piece of report for the people on the left or a predicate of a deleted subject. The scorching winds are the heat of fire and the scalding water is extremely hot water. Its meaning has been explained previously. It has also been said that the scorching winds are the hot wind that enters the pores of the body.
56:43: 43- And a shade of black smoke Al-Yahmum is a noun derived from aham, which means black. The Arabs say aswad yahmum if it is very black, and the meaning is that they are startled by the shade and find it a shade of the smoke of Hell, very black. It is also said that it is derived from ham, which is fat blackened by burning in fire. It is also said that it is derived from hamam, which is coal. Ad-Dahhak said: Fire is black and everything in it is black.
56:44: Then he described this shade by saying: 44- Neither cool nor generous meaning it is not like other shades that are cool, rather it is hot because it is from the smoke of the fire of Hell. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Nor generous: meaning it does not have a good appearance. And everything that has no good in it is not generous. Ad-Dahhak said: Nor generous nor torment. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs make generous an adjunct to everything that they negate a description of with the intention of criticizing it. They say: He is neither fat nor generous, and this house is neither spacious nor generous.
56:45: Then the Almighty mentioned their deeds for which they deserved the punishment, saying: 45- Indeed, before that, they were in luxury. This sentence explains what preceded it: that is, before this punishment that had befallen them, they were in luxury in this world: that is, enjoying what was not permissible for them. The luxurious is the one who is pampered. Al-Suddi said: polytheists, and it was said: arrogant, but the first is more appropriate.
56:46: 46- And they persisted in the great perjury. Perjury is a sin: that is, they persisted in the great sin. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: It means polytheism, meaning they did not repent from polytheism. Al-Hasan, Al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said the same. Qatadah and Mujahid said: It is the great sin from which they did not repent. Al-Sha'bi said: It is a false oath.
56:47: 47- And they used to say, ‘When we die and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?’ The hamza in both cases is for denial and exclusion. We have already discussed this in Surat As-Saffat and in Surat Ar-Ra’d. The meaning is that they denied and excluded the possibility of being resurrected after death, as they have become bones and dust. What is meant is that their flesh and skin have become dust and their bones have become decayed and rotten. The factor in the adverbial phrase is what is indicated by resurrected, because what comes after the question does not affect what comes before it: i.e., will we be resurrected when we die? etc.
56:48: 48- Or our forefathers is connected to the pronoun in the resurrected because of the separation between them with the hamza, and the meaning is: that the resurrection of their forefathers is more distant because of their earlier death, and it was read and our forefathers.
56:49: Then God Almighty commanded His Messenger to answer them and reject their rejection, saying: 49- “Say: The first and the last will be gathered together.” That is, say to them, O Muhammad, that the first of the nations and the last of them, of whom you are a part, will be gathered together after the resurrection.
56:50: 50- Until the appointed time of a known day which is the Day of Resurrection.
56:51: 51- Then you, O you who are astray and deny This and what follows it are part of what is included under the statement, and it is connected to the first ones and His description of them, glory be to Him, with two ugly descriptions, which are straying from the truth and denying it.
56:52: 52- They will eat from the tree of Zaqqum meaning they will eat in the Hereafter from a tree that is unpleasant to look at and unpleasant to taste. Its interpretation was presented in Surat As-Saffat. The first is for the beginning of the goal, and the second is explanatory. It is possible for the first to be additional, and the second to be explanatory, or for the second to be additional, and the first to be for the beginning.
56:53: 53- And you will fill your bellies with it meaning you will fill your bellies with the tree of Zaqqum because of the severe hunger that will befall you.
56:54: 54- And they will drink from it scalding water. The pronoun in from it refers to Zaqqum, and scalding water is the water that has reached its peak. The meaning is: And they will drink from Zaqqum after eating from the scalding water. The pronoun may refer to the tree because it is both masculine and feminine. It may also refer to the acres indicated by the statement: They will eat. And it was read from a tree in the singular.
56:55: 55- Fa Sharboon Sharb Al-Haym The majority read Sharb Al-Haym with a fatha on the sheen, and Nafi', Asim, and Hamza read it with a damma, and Mujahid and Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi read it with a kasra, and these are dialects. Abu Zayd said: I heard the Arabs say with a damma, a fatha, and a kasra on the sheen. Al-Mubarrad said: The fatha is on the basis of the infinitive and the damma is the name of the infinitive. Al-Haym are the thirsty camels that are not quenched due to an illness that afflicts them. This sentence is an explanation of what came before it: that is, your drinking will not be a regular drinking, but rather it will be like the drinking of a camel that is thirsty and is not quenched by drinking water. The singular of Al-Haym is Ahaym, and the female is Hayma'. Qays ibn Al-Mulawwah said: It is said that he was afflicted with the disease of infatuation, and I knew myself the place of his recovery. Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Uyaynah, Al-Akhfash and Ibn Kaysan said: Al-Haym is the flat, sandy land. The meaning is that they drink as this land drinks water, but no trace of it appears in it. In As-Sahah it says: Al-Hiyam with the dammah is the most severe thirst. Al-Hiyam is like madness from love. Al-Hiyam is a disease that afflicts camels, they wander the land and do not graze. It is said that a she-camel is Haima. Al-Hayma is also a desert without water. Al-Hiyam with the fathah is the sand that does not hold together in the hand because of its softness. The plural is Haim like Qadhal and Qadhal. Al-Hiyam with the kasrah is the thirsty camels.
56:56: 56- This is their lodging on the Day of Judgment. The majority read nuzulhum with two dammahs, and it was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr and Ibn Muhaisin with a dammah and a sukoon. It was previously mentioned that the nozul is what is prepared for the guest, and is the first thing he eats, and the Day of Judgment is the Day of Recompense, which is the Day of Resurrection. The meaning is that what was mentioned about the tree of Zaqqum and the drink of boiling water is what is prepared for them and that they will eat on the Day of Resurrection. In this there is mockery of it, because the nozul is what is prepared for guests as an honor to them, and similar to this is His statement: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: God benefits us through the Bedouins and their questions. One day a Bedouin came and said: O Messenger of God, a harmful tree is mentioned in the Qur’an, but I have never seen a tree in Paradise that would harm its inhabitant. He said: What is it? He said: The lote tree, for it has thorns. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did God not say: In thornless lote trees? God shakes its thorns and replaces each thorn with a fruit, and it produces fruit from which seventy-two types of food spring forth, none of which resembles the other. Ibn Abi Dawud, Al-Tabarani, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Uyaynah ibn Abd Al-Salami who said: “I was sitting with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when a Bedouin came and said: ‘O Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), have you heard mention of a tree in Paradise? I do not know of a tree with more thorns than it,’ meaning the talh tree. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Indeed, God will place in place of every thorn a fruit like the testicle of a castrated goat,’ meaning the castrated one. In it are seventy types of food, no other type is similar.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: Tufty lote trees, he said: Its twigs are its udder and its heavy load. ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated through various chains of narration on his authority that: The twiggy is that which has no thorns. ‘Abd ibn Humayd also narrated on his authority that: The twiggy is the one that has no thorns. ‘Abd al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Hanad, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding the verse: And twiggy lote trees, he said: It refers to bananas. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib that he recited and it came out arranged. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Anbari narrated in Al-Masahif on the authority of Qays bin Ibad that he recited to Ali bin Abi Talib and the banana trees arranged in layers. Ali said: What is the matter with the banana trees? Don’t you read and it came out? Then he said: It came out arranged in layers. It was said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, should I scratch it in the Mushaf? He said: The Qur’an is not disputed today. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement arranged, he said: Some of it on top of others. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “In Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Recite if you wish: “and an extended shade.” Al-Bukhari and others narrated something similar on the authority of Anas. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated a similar hadith from Abu Saeed. Ahmad narrated it as well. At-Tirmidhi – who authenticated it – and An-Nasa’i and others narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri that the Prophet – may God bless him and grant him peace – spoke about his statement, And raised couches, saying: Their height is like the distance between the heaven and the earth, and the journey between them is five hundred years. At-Tirmidhi said after transmitting it: This is a strange hadith that we do not know of except through the hadith of Rashdin ibn Sa’d. End quote. Rashdin is weak. Al-Firyabi, Hanad, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba’th transmitted it on the authority of Anas who said: “The Messenger of God – may God bless him and grant him peace – spoke about his statement, ‘Indeed, We created them a special creation,’ saying: Indeed, those created in this world were old women, blind and lame.” At-Tirmidhi said: After transmitting it: It is strange. Musa and Yazid are weak. Al-Tayalisi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Qani’, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba’th narrated on the authority of Salamah ibn Yazid Al-Ju’fi that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say, regarding the verse, Indeed, We created them a special creation, that he said: The previously married women and the virgins who were in the world. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, that he said: He created them other than their first creation. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, Virgins, that he said: Virgins. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, Arab, that he said: Loving ones of equal age, “Atraban,” that he said: Equal in age. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, Arab, that he said: Loving ones for their husbands and their husbands are lovers for them, “Atraban,” that he said: Of the same age, that he said: Of the same age, thirty-three years. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, that he said: The single woman is the one who is fond of her husband. Musaddad in his Musnad, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a good chain of narration on the authority of Abu Bakra, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding His statement: {A group from the former peoples * And a group from the latter ones}, he said: “Both of them are from this nation.” Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, Musaddad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Bakra, regarding His statement: {A group from the former peoples * And a group from the latter ones}, he said: Both of them are from this nation. Al-Faryabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Adi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of narration: “On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: {A group from the former peoples * And a group from the latter ones}, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Both of them are from my nation.” Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Both of them are from this nation. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated - and he authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and a shade of scorching heat, he said: of black smoke, and in another version: of the smoke of Hellfire. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, a drink of boiling water, he said: thirsty camels.
56:57: His statement: 57- We created you, so why do you not believe? The Almighty turned to address the disbelievers, rebuking them and making the argument binding: That is, why do you not believe in the resurrection or in creation? Muqatil said: We created you when you were nothing, and you know that, so why do you not believe in the resurrection?
56:58: 58- Have you seen what you wish for? That is, what you ejaculate and pour into the wombs of women of semen. The meaning of Have you seen is: Tell me.
56:59: And its first object is what you wish for, and the second is the interrogative sentence, which is 59- Do you create it, or are We the creators? That is, do you estimate it and form it as a human being, or are We the ones who estimate and form it? Am is the connected word, and it was said that it is the disjunctive one, but the first is more appropriate. The majority read tamnoon with a damma on the first letter from amana yamani. They are two languages, and it was said that their meanings are different. It is said that amani means that one ejaculates from sexual intercourse, and the meaning is that one ejaculates from a wet dream. Semen is called semen because it is yamani, meaning that it is shed.
56:60: 60- We have decreed death among you, and We will not be outdone. The majority of scholars read We have decreed with emphasis, while Mujahid, Hamid, Ibn Muhaisin, and Ibn Kathir read it with emphasis. These are two dialects. It is said We have decreed or We have decreed meaning we have divided something among you and set a time for each one of you. It is also said We have decided, or We have written, and the meanings are close. Muqatil said: Some of you will die old, and some of you will die young. Ad-Dahhak said: “Its meaning is that He made the people of the heavens and the people of the earth equal in it. “And We will not be outdone,” overpowered, but rather, able.
56:61: 61- That We may replace your likes means that We will bring forth a creation like you. Al-Zajjaj said: If We wanted to create a creation other than you, no one would have preceded Us or missed Us. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning is that We have decreed death among you so that We may replace your likes after your death with others of your kind, and We will not be outdone in your appointed times: that is, no one will precede or delay. And We will create you in that which you do not know of forms and shapes. Al-Hasan said: That is, We will make you apes and pigs as We did with peoples before you. It was also said that the meaning is: We will create you on the Day of Resurrection in forms other than your worldly forms. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: In that which you do not know means in the crops of black birds that are in Barhout like swallows. Barhout is a valley in Yemen. Mujahid said: In that which you do not know means in any creation We will, and whoever is capable of this is capable of resurrection.
56:62: 62- And you have certainly known the first creation, which is the beginning of creation from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh. Before that, you were nothing. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: It means the creation of Adam from dust. Then why do you not remember? That is, why do you not remember God’s power over the final creation and compare it to the first creation? The majority of scholars read the creation with a shortened form, while Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read it with a long vowel. The explanation of this has already been explained in Surat Al-Ankaboot.
56:63: 63- Have you seen what you till? That is, tell me what you till from your land and sow seeds in it.
56:64: 64- Do you plant it? That is, do you grow it and make it into a crop so that the ear of grain is in it? Or are We the planter? That is, the ones who grow it and make it into a crop, not you. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said that God planted it, meaning He made it grow. So if you acknowledge this, how can you deny the resurrection?
56:65: 65- If We willed, We could have made it debris. That is, if We willed, We could have made what you till debris: that is, shattered and broken. The debris is the broken pieces that are not useful and from which no grain or anything required for cultivation is obtained. So you remained in amazement. Al-Farra’ said: You were in amazement means you were amazed at what happened to your crops. It is said in As-Sahah: And to be amazed means to be filled with amazement, it is said to be regretful. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said: The meaning of the verse is: You are amazed at its passing and you regret what happened to you. Ikrimah said: You blame and regret what you did in the past of disobeying God. Abu Amr and Al-Kisa’i said: It is yearning for what is gone. The majority read So you remained with a fatha on the dhad and one lam. Abu Haywah and Abu Bakr, in a narration from him, read it with a kasra on the dhad. Ibn Abbas and Al-Jahdary read it with two lams: the first with a kasra according to the original, and it was narrated from Al-Jahdary with a fatha, which is a dialect. The majority read it tafakahuun, and Abu Hazam Al-Ukali read tafkanun with a noon instead of a ha, meaning you regret. Ibn Khalawayh said: tafaka means to be amazed, and tafkan means to regret. In As-Sahah, tafkan means to regret.
56:66: 66- Indeed, we are in debt. The majority read it with one hamza as a statement, while Abu Bakr, Al-Mufaddal, and Zur ibn Hubaysh read it with two hamzas as a question, and the janlah is estimated to say: that is, you say, Indeed, we are in debt, meaning we are obligated to pay for what our crops have lost. The indebted person is the one whose money has been lost without compensation, as Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said. It was said that [its meaning] is, Indeed, we are being punished, as Qatadah and others said. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: He is indebted to us, and from this is the saying of An-Namir ibn Talib: He kept it a secret and was obsessed with it. It is said that someone is infatuated with someone, meaning he is obsessed with them. Muqatil said: They are doomed. An-Nahhas said: It is taken from gharam, which means destruction, and from it the poet said: And the Day of the Eagles and the Day of the Jabbar will be a lasting torment upon you. The first meaning appears from the context: that is, we are infatuated with the loss of what we have cultivated and its becoming rubble.
56:67: Then they turned away from their statement and moved on to say: 67- Rather, we are deprived, meaning we were deprived of our sustenance due to the destruction of our crops. The deprived one is the one who is prevented from sustenance and has no share in it, and he is the one who is forbidden.
56:68: 68- Have you seen the water that you drink? with which you assuage the thirst that afflicts you and ward off the afflictions that befall you. God Almighty limited His mention of drinking to the point of mentioning the many benefits of water, because it is the greatest and most important of its benefits.
56:69: 69- Did you bring it down from the clouds? meaning the clouds. It is stated in Al-Sahah: Abu Zaid said: The cloud is the white cloud, and the plural is mizn, and mizna is rain. The poet said: Have you not seen that God sent down rain and poured down the gazelles’ dust in the churches? What indicates that it is the clouds is the poet’s saying: We are like rainwater, there is no one who is generous to us, and no one who is miserly to us And the other said: Neither rain nor thunder nor rain nor land that is as green as it Or are We the ones who send it down to him by Our power and no one else? If you know that, then how can you not acknowledge monotheism and believe in the resurrection?
56:70: Then He, glory be to Him, explained to them that if He had willed, He could have taken this blessing away from them, saying: 70- If We willed, We could have made it brackish. Brackish water is very salty water that cannot be drunk. Al-Hasan said: It is bitter water that they do not benefit from in drinking, planting, or anything else. Then why are you not grateful? That is, why do you not thank God for the blessing that He created for you fresh water from which you can drink and benefit from.
56:71: 71- Have you seen the fire that you kindle? That is, tell me about it. The meaning of you kindle is that you extract it by striking it from the wet tree. It is said, you kindle the fire if you strike it.
56:72: 72- Did you create its tree from which the arms are made, which are the marakh and the afar. The Arabs say: In every tree there is fire, and the marakh and the afar are glorified. Or are We the creators of it with Our power without you? The meaning of creation is creation, and it is expressed by the word ghansha to indicate what is in that of the wondrous craftsmanship and amazing power.
56:73: 73- And We have made it a reminder meaning We have made this fire in this world a reminder of the greater fire of Hell. Mujahid and Qatadah said: insight for the people in the darkness. Ata’ said: an admonition for the believer to take heed from. And provision for the needy meaning a benefit for those who stay in quwa’, which is a barren land like travelers and desert dwellers who stay in a desolate place. It is said that a quwa’ land with a long vowel and a sr means a desolate place. From this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: Oh, house of Mayya in the highlands, the Sind is strong and the past has been long upon it Antara said: I came back from the ruins of an ancient era, stronger and more established after Umm Al-Haytham And the other said: Didn't you ask the strong quarter to speak? And will the desert of Samlaq tell you today? It is said that he traveled, meaning he stayed strong. Mujahid said that the strong ones are those who enjoy it from all people in cooking, baking, warming themselves, and lighting, and it reminds us of the fire of Hell. Ibn Zayd said: For the hungry in preparing their food, it is said: I have been strong since such and such, meaning I did not eat anything, and so-and-so spent the night strong, meaning he spent the night hungry, and from this is the saying of the poet: I choose the strong, full of heart, who is careful not to be called mean. Qatrib said: [Al-Qawwa] is one of the opposites. It can mean poverty or wealth. It is said that a man is strong if he has no provisions, and strong if his animals are strong and his wealth is abundant. Al-Tha’labi reported the first opinion from most commentators, and this is the apparent one.
56:74: 74- So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great. The fa is for the order of what follows it of mentioning God Almighty, and His glorification of what preceded it of the blessings He bestowed upon His servants and the polytheists’ denial and rejection of them. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab, and he declared it weak, narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let none of you say, ‘I sowed,’ but say, ‘I plowed.’ Abu Hurayrah said: Have you not heard God say, ‘Have you seen that which you plow? Is it you who sow it, or are We the sower?’ Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, You are joking, meaning, you are amazed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, saying, Al-Muzan means the clouds. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, We have made it a reminder, meaning, a reminder of the Great Fire. And provision for the travelers, meaning, for the travelers.
56:75: His saying: 75- "So I swear The majority of commentators held that la" is for emphasis, and the meaning is: So I swear, and this is supported by his statement after that: "And it is an oath." A group of commentators said: It is for negation, and that what is negated by it is omitted, and it is the speech of the deniers who deny. Al-Farra' said: It is a negation, and the meaning is: The matter is not as you say. Then he resumed and said "I swear, and this is weakened by the fact that deleting the subject of la" and its predicate is not permissible, as Abu Hayyan and others said. It was said that it is the lam of initiation, and the original is "so I swear," so the fatha was cast and an alif was generated from it, like the saying of the poet: I seek refuge in God from the scorpion Al-Hasan, Hamid, and Isa ibn Umar read it thus: Fala-Islam without the alif. According to this statement, and this reading, a deleted subject is understood, and the meaning is: Fala-I swear by that. It was said that La here means ala which is for emphasis, but this is far-fetched. It was also said that La here is to be taken literally, and that it is for negating the oath: that is, I do not swear by this because the matter is clearer than that.
56:76: This is refuted by His statement: 76- "And indeed, it is a great oath, if you but knew," specifying the thing sworn by and the thing sworn to. The meaning of His statement, "By the positions of the stars," is their places of setting, which are their places of setting. This is what Qatada and others said. Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: Their stations. Al-Hasan said: Their setting and scattering on the Day of Resurrection. Ad-Dahhak said: They are the stars about which the people of the Jahiliyyah used to say, "It rained because of such-and-such a star." It was said that what is meant by the positions of the stars is the revelation of the Qur'an in stages from the Preserved Tablet. As-Suddi and others said the same. Al-Farra' narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that the positions of the stars are the decisive parts of the Qur'an. The majority of scholars read "positions in the plural, while Ibn Mas'ud, An-Nakha'i, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Ibn Muhaisin, and Warsh from Ya'qub read position" in the singular. Al-Mubarrad said: Position here is a verbal noun, so it is valid for both singular and plural. Then the Almighty informed us about the greatness and magnificence of this oath, saying: And indeed, it is a great oath, if you but knew. This clause is parenthetical between the thing sworn by and the thing sworn upon. His statement, If you but knew, is a parenthetical clause between the two parts of the parenthetical clause, so it is a parenthesis within a parenthesis. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj said: This indicates that what is meant by the positions of the stars is the revelation of the Qur’an, and the pronoun in it refers to the oath indicated by I swear. The meaning is that swearing by the positions of the stars is a great oath, if you but knew.
56:77: Then the Almighty mentioned what the oath was sworn to by, saying: 77- Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an, meaning that God has honored it, glorified it, and raised its status above all other books. He has honored it above being magic, divination, or lies. It has been said that it is noble because it contains noble morals and lofty matters, and it has also been said because it honors the one who memorizes it and glorifies the one who recites it. Al-Wahidi narrated from the scholars of semantics that the Qur’an was described as noble because it is capable of providing much good through evidence that leads to the truth in religion. Al-Azhari said: Noble is a comprehensive name for what is praised, and the Qur’an is noble and praised because of what it contains of guidance, clarification, knowledge, and wisdom.
56:78: 78- In a Protected Book meaning concealed and protected. It was also said that it is preserved from falsehood. It is the Preserved Tablet, as stated by a group. It was also said that it is a book. Ikrimah said: It is the Torah and the Gospel, in which the Qur’an is mentioned and who it was revealed to. Al-Suddi said: It is the Psalms. Mujahid and Qatadah said: It is the Qur’an that is in our hands.
56:79: 79- "None shall touch it except the purified." Al-Wahidi said: Most commentators agree that the pronoun refers to the Concealed Book, meaning that none shall touch the Concealed Book except the purified, who are the angels. It was also said that they are the angels and the messengers from among the children of Adam. The meaning of "None shall touch it" is the literal touch. It was also said that it means that none shall bring it down except the purified. It was also said that it means that none shall recite it. Based on the fact that what is meant by the Concealed Book is the Qur'an, it was said that "None shall touch it except the purified" from ritual impurities and impurities. This is what Qatada and others said. Al-Kalbi said that it refers to those purified from polytheism. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: Those purified from sins and faults. Muhammad ibn al-Fadl and others said: The meaning of "None shall touch it" is the believers. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Its interpretation and explanation can only be known to those whom God has purified from polytheism and hypocrisy. The majority of scholars have prohibited someone in a state of minor ritual impurity muḥarrah from touching the Qur’an. This is the view held by Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, Sa’id ibn Zayd, Ata’, al-Zuhri, al-Nakha’i, al-Hakam, Hammad and a group of jurists, including Malik and al-Shafi’i. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, al-Sha’bi and a group, including Abu Hanifa, that it is permissible for someone in a state of minor ritual impurity to touch it. We have explained the correct interpretation of this in our commentary on al-Muntaqa, so please refer to it. The majority of scholars have read al-mutahahhirun the purifiers with a soft ta’ and a stressed ha’, as a passive participle. Salman al-Farsi read it with a kasra on the ha’ as an active participle, meaning the purifiers themselves. Nafi’ ibn ‘Amr, in a narration from them both, read it: ‘Isa ibn ‘Umar with a sukoon on the ta’ and a fatha on the ha’, as a passive participle from at-tahar purely pure. Al-Hasan, Zayd ibn ‘Ali and ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Awf read it with a stressed ta’ and a kasra on the ha’, as a passive participle from at-tahar purely pure.
56:80: 80- A revelation from the Lord of the Worlds. The majority of people read it in the nominative case, and some read it in the accusative case. The nominative case is because it is another description of the Qur’an, or the predicate of a deleted subject, and the accusative case is in the state.
56:81: 81- "Is it this narration that you are in denial of?" The reference is to the Qur'an, which is described with the previous descriptions. The in denial and the in denial are hypocrites. This is what Az-Zajjaj and others said. Ata' and others said: He is the liar. Muqatil ibn Sulayman and Qatadah said: In denial are disbelievers, as in His statement: "They wish that you would be in denial so they would be in denial." Ad-Dahhak said: In denial are those who turn away. Mujahid said: Those who side with the infidels in their disbelief. Abu Kaysan said: The in denial is the one who does not understand God's right over him and repels it with excuses. The first is more appropriate because the origin of the in denial is that its outward appearance is contrary to its inward appearance, as if it resembles oil in its ease. Al-Mu'arraj said: The in denial is the hypocrite who softens up to hide his disbelief. In denial and in denial mean lying, disbelief, and hypocrisy. Its origin is softness, and to be easy going contrary to what appears. In Al-Kashaf, it says: Madhanoon means those who are lax about it, like someone who is soft in a matter: that is, he is soft and does not stiffen in it out of laxity. Al-Raghib said: “Idhan in origin is like tadheen, but it was made an expression for tact and gentleness, and seriousness was left out: just as taqreed, which is removing ticks, was made an expression for that. What he mentioned is supported by the saying of Abu Qais bin Al-Aslat: Firmness and strength are better than indolence, idiocy and fear.
56:82: 82- "And you make your provision that you deny." There is an omitted complement in the statement, as Al-Wahidi reported from the commentators: That is, you make your gratitude for your provision that you deny the blessing of God, so you substitute denial for gratitude. Al-Haytham said: The Azdashnu'a say, "Ma rizq so-and-so means he did not thank." According to this language, there is no omitted complement in the verse, but rather the meaning of provision is gratitude. The way provision is expressed in the sense of gratitude is that gratitude overflows with an increase in provision, so gratitude is provision, expressing the cause for the effect. What falls under this verse is the saying of the disbelievers when God provides them with water and sends down rain: "We were given water by such-and-such a star, and We were given rain by such-and-such a star." Al-Azhari said: The meaning of the verse is, "And you make your provision that God has provided you a denial that it is from God, the Provider." Ali and Ibn Abbas read it as you make your thanks. The majority read it as that you lie with emphasis from denying. Ali and Asim, in a narration from him, read it with emphasis from lie.
56:83: 83- Why then, when it reaches the throat meaning why then, when the soul or spirit reaches the throat at death, and it is not mentioned before, because the meaning is understood by them if they use such an expression, and from it is the saying of Hatim Tayy: Amawi, wealth is of no use to a young man if he chokes one day and his chest becomes tight
56:84: 84- And you will then be watching what the person is in, the one whose soul or spirit has reached the throat. Al-Zajjaj said: And you, O family of the deceased, will be in that state seeing the deceased until his soul leaves it. The meaning is that in that state they will be unable to defend him, nor will they be able to do anything to benefit him or alleviate what he is in.
56:85: 85- And We are nearer to him than you meaning in knowledge, power, and vision. It was also said that He meant that Our messengers who are responsible for taking him are nearer to him than you. But you do not see meaning you do not realize that because of your ignorance that God is nearer to His servant than the jugular vein, or you do not see the angels of death who attend the dead person and are responsible for taking him.
56:86: 86- Why, if you are not indebted, do not return it? It is said that the sultan subjugated his subjects: if he ruled them and enslaved them. Al-Farra’ said: I subjugated him, and it is more severe for Al-Hutay’ah: You have brought your sons so close that you have left them finer than flour. That is, he owned it. It is also said that he humiliated him and enslaved him. It is also said that the meaning is indebted and accountable, and it is also said that it means rewarding. From this comes the poet’s saying: Nothing remains but the enemy, we approach them as they approach The first meaning is more accurate to the meaning of the verse: that is, if you are not being raised or controlled, why do you not return it? That is, the soul that has reached the throat to the place where it was.
56:87: 87- If you are truthful and you will not return it, then your claim that you are not nurtured or owned is invalid. The factor in his statement if it reaches is his statement that you return it, and were it not for the second, it would confirm the first. Al-Farra’ said: And perhaps the Arabs repeated the two letters, and their meaning is the same.
56:88: Then the Almighty mentioned the classes of creation at death and after it, saying: 88- But if he is among those brought near meaning those who are foremost among the three categories whose conditions were detailed previously.
56:89: 89- Farooh, basil, and a garden of delights. The majority of scholars read it as Rooh with a fat-ha on the ra', and it means rest from the world and relief from their conditions. Al-Hasan said: The spirit is mercy. Mujahid said: The spirit is joy. Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Nasr ibn Asim, and Al-Jahdary read Farouh with a damma on the ra'. This reading was narrated from Ya'qub, it was said, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Muqatil. Muqatil said: It is provision in the language of Himyar. It is said, I went out seeking the basil of God, meaning His provision. From this is the saying of Al-Nimr ibn Talib. God's peace, his fragrance, his mercy, and a sky of pearls Qatada said: It is Paradise. Ad-Dahhak said: It is mercy. Al-Hasan said: It is the well-known fragrant basil. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: This is at death, and Paradise is hidden for him until he is resurrected. Abu Al-Jawza’ and Abu Al-Aaliyah said the same. The meaning of Paradise of Delight is that it is full of delight and an elevated spirit. What comes after it is in the beginning, and the predicate is omitted: that is, he has a spirit.
56:90: 90- And if that deceased was one of the companions of the right hand and the details of their conditions and what God has prepared for them as a reward have been mentioned and detailed previously.
56:91: 91- “So peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand.” That is, you will not see in them anything but what you would like of safety, so do not worry about them, for they will be safe from the punishment of God. It was said that the meaning is: Peace be upon you from them, that is, you will be safe from worrying about them. It was said that the meaning is: They will pray for you and greet you. It was said that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, greets with peace out of respect. It was said that it is report from God, the Exalted, of some of them greeting one another. It was said that the meaning is: Peace be upon you, O companion of the right hand, from your brothers, the companions of the right hand.
56:92: 92- And if he is among the deniers who have gone astray, meaning those who deny the resurrection and have gone astray from guidance, and they are the people of the left mentioned above, and their conditions were detailed.
56:93: 93- Then he will descend from scalding water meaning that he will descend from scalding water, which is water that has reached extreme heat, after he eats from Zaqqum, as explained above.
56:94: 94- And a scorching fire It is said that he scorched him from the fire and scorched him: meaning if he put him in the fire, and it is from adding the source to the object, or to the place. Al-Mubarrad said: The answer to the condition in these three places is omitted and the meaning is: whatever it is of a thing, then it goes away, etc. Al-Akhfash said: The fa in the three places is the answer to amma and the answer to the letter of the condition. The majority read and a scorching fire in the nominative case in apposition to then it descended. Abu Amr, in a narration from him, read it in the genitive case in apposition to hot water: meaning then he descended from hot water and from a scorching fire.
56:95: 95- Indeed, this is the certainty of truth. The reference is to what is mentioned in this surah, or to what is mentioned close to the states of the dispersed. It is the certainty of truth: meaning pure and unadulterated certainty. Adding truth to certainty is like adding something to itself. Al-Mubarrad said: It is like your saying about certainty and pure certainty. This is according to the Kufians, and they permitted that due to the difference in wording. As for the Basrans, they omit the complement to it, and the meaning is: the certainty of the matter or the certainty of the report.
56:96: The fa in 96- So glorify the name of your Lord, the Great is to arrange what comes after it on what comes before it: that is, purify Him from what is not befitting of His status, and the ba' is related to something omitted: that is, so glorify while mixing it with the name of your Lord to seek His blessing. It was said that the meaning is: separate by mentioning your Lord, and it was said that the ba' is redundant, and the name means the essence. It was said that it is for transitivity because glorify is transitive by itself sometimes and transitive by a preposition at other times, and the first is more appropriate. An-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Qur'an was revealed on the Night of Decree from the highest heaven to the lowest heaven all at once, then it was distributed over the years. In another version: Then it descended from the lowest heaven to the earth in stars. Then he recited: So I swear by the positions of the stars. 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Muhammad ibn Nasr, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, At-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority: So I swear by the positions of the stars, he said: The Qur'an: And indeed, it is a tremendous oath, if you but knew, he said: The Qur'an. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding the verse: He said: The stars of the Qur'an when it is revealed. 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ma'rifah also narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas: None shall touch it except the purified, he said: The Book revealed in the heaven is not touched except by the angels. Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Anas: None shall touch it except the purified, he said: The angels. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Alqamah who said: We came to Salman al-Farisi and he came out to us from the toilet. We said to him: O Abdullah, why don’t you perform ablution and then recite to us such-and-such a surah? He said: God said: “It is in a well-guarded Book. None touch it except the purified.” This is the one in the heavens which none touch except the angels. Then he recited to us from the Qur’an whatever we wished. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Dawud and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm on the authority of his father who said in the letter of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Amr ibn Hazm: Do not touch the Qur’an except when you are pure. Malik narrated it in al-Muwatta’ on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr. Abu Dawud narrated it in al-Marasil on the authority of al-Zuhri who said: He read in the scroll of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: None may touch the Qur’an except one who is pure. Ad-Daraqutni narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Hazm, Abdullah ibn Amr and Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As, but there is some doubt about their chains of transmission. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he would not touch the Qur’an except in a state of ritual purity. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, who said: We were with Salman when he went to relieve himself, then he hid from us and then came out to us. We said: Why don’t you perform ritual purity so we can ask you about some things from the Qur’an? He said: Ask me, for I will not touch it, for only the purified touch it. Then he recited: None shall touch it except the purified. At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: None shall touch the Qur’an except the pure. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal that when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) sent him to Yemen, he wrote to him in his covenant: None shall touch the Qur’an except the pure. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement: You are doubtful, he said: You are liars. Muslim, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Rain fell on the people during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Among the people are grateful and among them are disbelievers.’ They said: ‘This is a mercy that God has bestowed.’ Some of them said: ‘The occurrence of such and such a star has come true.’ Then this verse was revealed: ‘So I swear by the positions of the stars…’ until it reached: ‘And you consider your provision to be that you deny.’” The origin of the hadith, without mentioning that it was the reason for the revelation of the verse, is established in the two Sahihs from a hadith. The meaning of this verse is mercy because it is like life for the one who has received mercy. ‘Rayhan’ is provision in Paradise, as Mujahid said, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani. It is from the hadith of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri. There are other hadiths on this topic.
