Ahmad, Ibn Mani’, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it narrated it, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of ‘Ali, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding his statement: ‘And you consider your provision to be that you deny.’ He said: ‘Your gratitude. You say our rain was due to such and such a star and such and such a star.’” Ibn Asakir narrated in his history on the authority of Aisha who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did not interpret from the Quran except a few verses. His statement, And you make your provision that you deny, said: Your gratitude. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recited, And you make your provision. Abu Ubaid in his Fadhail, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Humaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite, And you make your gratitude, meaning the stars. No people received rain except that they became disbelievers. They used to say, We received rain because of such and such a star, so God revealed, And you make your provision that you deny. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami on the authority of Ali that he recited, And you make your gratitude, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recite it like this. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, Not being held accountable, he said: Not being held accountable. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in Az-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham, But if he should be of those brought near the verse, he said: This is for him at death. And a Garden of Delight Paradise is stored up for him until the Day of Resurrection. But if he should be of the deniers and those who have gone astray, * then he will be given scalding water the verse, he said: This is at death. And burning in Hellfire the verse, he said: Hellfire is stored up for him until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And a fragrance the verse, he said: A scent, And basil the verse, he said: Rest. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: By basil he means rest from this world. And a Garden of Delight the verse, he said: Forgiveness and mercy. Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority, he said: Basil is provision. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority, regarding His statement, “So peace to you from the companions of the right,” the verse, he said: The angels will come to him with peace from God, greeting him and informing him that he is among the companions of the right. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, Indeed, this is the certain truth. He said: What we have narrated to you in this surah. He also narrated on his authority, So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great. He said: Pray to your Lord. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir Al-Juhani, who said: “When ‘So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great’ was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Include it in your bowing. When ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ was revealed, he said: Include it in your prostration.”
57:1: It is twenty-nine verses. It was revealed in Madinah. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion. Ibn Al-Durais, Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Hadid was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Surat Al-Hadid was revealed on a Tuesday, and God created iron on a Tuesday, and the son of Adam killed his brother on a Tuesday, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade cupping on Tuesday.” Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): Do not have cupping done on a Tuesday, for Surat Al-Hadid was revealed to me on a Tuesday. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Al-Arbadh ibn Sariyah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite the Tasbihat before going to sleep and said: In them there is a verse better than a thousand verses. In its chain of transmission is Baqiyyah ibn Al-Walid, about whom there is a well-known criticism. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not mention Al-Arbad bin Sariyah, so it is mursal. Ibn Al-Durais narrated it on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not sleep until he had recited the Tasbihat, and he would say: In them is a verse better than a thousand verses. Yahya said: We see it as the verse at the end of Al-Hashr. Ibn Kathir said in his interpretation: “The verse referred to, and God knows best, is His statement: ‘He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent.’” The verse and the glorifying verses mentioned are: Al-Hadid, Al-Hashr, Al-Saff, Al-Jumu’ah, and Al-Taghabun. His statement: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts God meaning glorifies Him and magnifies Him. Al-Muqatilaneen said: It means everything with a soul or without. We have already discussed the glorification of inanimate objects when explaining His statement: There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification. What is meant by glorification attributed to everything in the heavens and the earth, of rational beings and others, animals and inanimate objects, is that which includes glorification by speech, such as the glorification of the angels, humans and jinn, and by action, such as the glorification of others, because every existing thing points to the Creator. Al-Zajjaj denied that the glorification of non-rational beings is the glorification of indication and said: If this were the glorification of indication and the appearance of the effects of craftsmanship, it would have been understood. So why did he say: But you do not understand their glorification? Rather, it is the glorification of speech. He provided evidence with his saying: And We subjected the mountains with David to glorify? If this glorification from the mountains was the glorification of indication, there would be no benefit in singling out David. The verb glorification may be transitive in and of itself sometimes, as in his saying: And glorify Him and with the lam at other times like this verse. Its origin is that it is transitive in and of itself, because the meaning of glorifying Him is His distance from evil. So if the lam is used, it is either an additional emphasis as in I thanked him and I thanked him or it is for al-Sharh 94:that is, do the glorification for the sake of God, the Most High, purely for Him. This verb came in some openings in the past tense like this opening, and in some in the present tense, and in some as a command to indicate that these things glorify at all times, their glorification is not specific to one time rather than another, rather they glorify forever in the past and will glorify forever in the future. The future and He is the Exalted in Might meaning the All-Powerful, the Victorious, whom no one disputes and whom no one can oppose, whoever he may be. The Wise is the One who does actions of wisdom and right.
57:2: 2- To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He alone disposes of them and nothing is carried out except His disposition and command. It was said that He meant the treasuries of rain, plants, and all other provisions. He gives life and causes death. The two verbs are in the nominative case as predicate for a deleted subject, or in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun to Him, or a renewed statement to explain some of the rulings of the dominion. The meaning is that He gives life in this world and causes death to the living. It was said that He gives life to the sperm, which is dead, and causes death to the living. It was said that He gives life to the dead for resurrection. And He is over all things competent. Nothing is beyond His power, whatever it may be.
57:3: 3- He is the First before everything and the Last after everything: meaning the One who remains after the annihilation of His creation and the Manifest the High who dominates over everything, or the One whose existence is apparent through clear evidence and the Hidden meaning the One who knows what is hidden, and from their saying so-and-so hides the affair of so-and-so meaning he knows the inner meaning of his affair, and it is possible that the meaning is hidden from sight and mind, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained these four names as will come, so it is necessary to arrive at that and He is Knowing of all things nothing of the information escapes His knowledge.
57:4: 4- It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days. This is a statement of some of His dominion over the heavens and the earth. Its explanation has already been presented in detail in Surat Al-A’raf and elsewhere. He knows what penetrates into the earth meaning what enters it of rain and other things and what emerges from it of plants and other things and what descends from the sky of rain and other things and what ascends therein meaning what ascends to it of the angels and the deeds of the servants. The explanation of this has already been presented in Surat Saba’. And He is with you wherever you are meaning by His power, authority and knowledge. This is an illustration of His comprehensiveness of what they issue wherever they go on earth, on land and at sea. And God is Seeing of what you do. Nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him.
57:5: 5- To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. This repetition is for emphasis. And to God all matters return, not to anyone else. The majority of scholars read will return, indicating the object. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Ibn 'Amir read it in the active form.
57:6: 6- He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night. The explanation of this has already been presented in Surat Al Imran, and in places And He is Knowing of that within the breasts, meaning of the innermost thoughts of the breasts and their hidden contents. Nothing of that is hidden from Him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: Fatimah came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asking him for a servant. He said: “Say: ‘O God, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, Cleaver of the grain and the date stone, I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything You hold by its forelock. You are the First and there is nothing before You, and You are the Last and there is nothing after You, and You are the Manifest and there is nothing above You, and You are the Hidden and there is nothing beneath You. Pay off our debt and enrich us from poverty.’” Ahmad, Muslim and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah through another chain of transmission, with a similar chain of transmission, regarding the four names mentioned and their explanation. Abu Al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Ibn Umar and Abu Saeed on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “People will continue to ask about everything until they say, ‘This is God who was before everything, so what was before God?’ If they say that to you, then say, ‘He is the First before everything, and the Last, and there is nothing after Him. He is the Manifest above everything, and the Hidden below everything, and He is All-Knowing of everything.’” Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Zumail who said: “I asked Ibn Abbas, ‘What is that I find in my chest?’ He said, ‘What is it?’ I said, ‘By God, I will not speak about it.’ He said, ‘Is it some doubt?’ He laughed. He said, ‘No one was saved from that.’ He said, ‘Until God revealed, “So if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you…’” He said, And He said to me, ‘If you find something in your soul, then say, ‘He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is All-Knowing of everything.’ Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Abbas regarding His statement, And He is with you wherever you are, he said, He is All-Knowing of you wherever you are.
57:7: 7- His saying, Believe in God and His Messenger, meaning, believe in monotheism and the truth of the message. This is addressed to the infidel Arabs, but it is possible that it is addressed to everyone, and what is meant by the command to believe for the Muslims is to continue in it, or to increase it. Then, when He commanded them to believe, He commanded them to spend in the way of God, saying, And spend from that over which He has made you successors, meaning, He made you successors in disposing of it without actually owning it, for money is God’s money and the servants are God’s successors over His money, so they must spend it in a way that pleases Him. It was also said that He made you successors to those who came before you from whom you inherit, and it will pass to others who inherit from you, so do not be stingy with it. This is what Al-Hasan and others said. It encourages spending in the way of goodness before it is transferred from them to others. It appears that the meaning of the verse is the encouragement to spend in the way of goodness and what God is pleased with in general. It was said that it is specific to the obligatory zakat, but there is no basis for this specificity. Then God Almighty mentioned the reward of whoever spends in the way of God, saying: So those among you who have believed and spent - for them is a great reward. That is, those who combined belief in God and His Messenger, and spending in the way of God - for them is a great reward, which is Paradise.
57:8: 8- And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in God? This question is for rebuke and reprimand: meaning, what excuse do you have, and what obstacle prevents you from believing? The reasons have been removed from you. Ma is the subject and la laka is its predicate, and la la ba'minun is in the accusative case as a hal of the pronoun in la laka, and the agent is ma which has the meaning of stability. It was said that the meaning is: what reward will there be for you in the Hereafter if you do not believe? The phrase and the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord is in the accusative case as a hal of the pronoun la la ba'minun due to overlap, and la la ba'minun is related to invites you: that is, he invites you to believe. The meaning is: what excuse do you have for abandoning belief while the Messenger invites you to it and alerts you to it? The phrase and He has taken your covenant is in the accusative case as a hal of the subject of invites you due to overlap as well: meaning, and the situation is that God took your covenant when He informed you from the loins of your father Adam, or with what He set up for you of evidence indicating monotheism and the obligation of belief. The majority of scholars read and He has taken as an active participle, which refers to God Almighty, as He has been mentioned previously. Abu Amr read it as a passive participle, if you are believers, in what He took from you of the covenant, or in the arguments and evidence, or if you are believers for some reason, as this is one of the greatest reasons and most obvious of its requirements.
57:9: 9- It is He who sends down to His Servant clear signs meaning clear and evident, and they are the Qur’anic signs, and it has been said that miracles are the greatest of them, that He may bring you out from darkness into the light meaning that God may bring you out with those signs from the darkness of polytheism into the light of faith, or that the Messenger may bring you out with those signs, or with the call, and indeed, God is to you Kind and Merciful meaning that He is very compassionate and merciful, and He is very eloquent in their compassion and mercy, as He sent down His books and sent His messengers to guide His servants, so there is no compassion or mercy more eloquent than this.
57:10: The question in His statement: 10- And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of God? is for rebuke and reprimand. The discussion of the parsing of this is like the discussion of the parsing of His statement: And what is [the matter] with you that you do not believe in God? In this verse is evidence that the spending commanded in His statement: And spend from that in which He has made you successors is spending in the cause of God, as we have explained. The meaning is: What excuse do you have and what is preventing you from that? The original is that you should not spend. It was said that an is redundant, and the phrase And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of you should not spend or its object. The meaning is: What is preventing you from spending in that way, while the situation is that everything in the heavens and the earth returns to God, glory be to Him, with the extinction of the world, like the return of inheritance to the heir, and nothing of it remains for them? This is more in the way of rebuke and more complete in reprimand, because that money is taken from its people and becomes for God, glory be to Him, and no one remains From its owners, it is stronger in requiring spending on them than it is for God in reality, and they are His successors in disposing of it. Then the Almighty explained the virtue of those who were the first to spend in the way of God, saying: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest. It was said that what is meant by the conquest is the conquest of Mecca. This is what most of the commentators said. Al-Sha’bi and Al-Zuhri said: The conquest of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Qatadah said: There were two fightings, one of which was better than the other, and two spendings, one of which was better than the other. Fighting and spending before the conquest of Mecca were better than fighting and spending after that. This is what Muqatil and others said, and there is an omission in the statement, and the meaning is: Not equal are those who spent before the conquest and fought and those who spent after the conquest and fought. So it was omitted for its clarity and the indication of what will follow. Spending and fighting before the conquest were better than spending and fighting after the conquest, because people’s need was greater at that time while they were fewer and weaker. Spending was mentioned before fighting to indicate the virtue of spending due to their need, as they were generous with themselves but did not find money to be generous with. Generosity with one’s soul is the ultimate in generosity. The reference in His statement, Those is to whom in consideration of its meaning, and it is the subject and predicate. are greater in degree than those who spent afterwards and fought, meaning they have a higher status and rank than those who spent their wealth in the way of God after the conquest and fought alongside the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ata’ said: The degrees of Paradise vary, so those who spent before the conquest are in the best of them. Al-Zajjaj said: Because those who came before experienced more hardship than those who came after them. And their insight was also more penetrating. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, guided us to this virtue by saying in what was authentically reported from him: If one of you spent the equivalent of Mount Uhud in gold, it would not amount to… One of them extended it, but not half of it.” This is an address from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the later generations and his companions, as it indicates that reason. In which this hadith was mentioned: And to both of them God promised the best, meaning that to each of the two groups God promised the best reward. It is Paradise, with their degrees varying in it. The majority read and all in the accusative case as the object of the delayed verb. Ibn Aamer is in the nominative case as a subject, and the sentence after it is its predicate and the antecedent is omitted, or as a predicate of an omitted word, and something like this is said The poet: Umm Al-Khayar has come to accuse me of a sin I did not commit. And God is All-Knowing of what you do. Nothing of it is hidden from Him.
57:11: Then He, the Almighty, encouraged charity, saying: 11- Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? That is, who is it that would spend his money in the way of God? It is as if he were lending it. The Arabs say to everyone who does a good deed, He has lent. And from this is the saying of the poet: If you give a loan, give it, for only the young man gives, not the camel. Al-Kalbi said: A loan means charity. Good means rewarded from the heart, without favor or harm. Muqatil said: Good means content with his soul. The interpretation of the verse in Surat Al-Baqarah has already been presented. He will multiply it for him. Ibn Amir and Ibn Kathir read it He will multiply it for him by dropping the alif, except that Ibn Amir and Ya’qub put the fa’ in the accusative case. Nafi’ and the people of Kufa and Basra read it He will multiply it for him with the alif and soften the ‘ayn, except that Asim put the fa’ in the accusative case and the rest raised it. Ibn Atiyyah said: The nominative is in apposition to He lends, or it is a new sentence and the accusative is because the fa’ is in the answer to the question. Abu Ali Al-Farisi weakened the accusative case. He said that the question was not about the loan, but rather about the doer of the loan. The fa’ is only used in the accusative case as a verb rejected by a question about an action. However, this group interpreted it to mean the same thing, as if his statement, Who is it that would loan God? is like his statement, Would God loan anyone? “And for him is a noble reward,” which is Paradise. The multiplication here means that the good deed is multiplied tenfold to seven hundredfold, depending on the circumstances, people, and times. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu`aym in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, who said: “We went out with the Messenger of God in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah until we reached Usfan. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Soon there will come a people who will burn your deeds along with their deeds.’ We said: ‘Who are they, O Messenger of God? The Quraysh?’ He said: ‘No, but they are the people of Yemen, and they are the most tender-hearted and soft-hearted.’ We said: ‘Are they better than us, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘If one of them had a mountain of gold, it would not reach the level of one of you or even half of it. However, this is the distinction between us and the al-Nas 114:‘Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought…’ [The verse].” Ibn Kathir said about this hadith: It is strange with this chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated it without mentioning Al-Hudaybiyyah in it. Ahmad narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “There was a discussion between Khalid ibn al-Walid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Khalid said to Abd al-Rahman: ‘Do you think you are superior to us because of the days you have outpaced us?’ When this report reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said: ‘Leave my companions alone, for by the One in Whose hand is my soul, even if you spent gold equal to Mount Uhud or mountains in gold, you would not reach their deeds.’” What is in the Sahih on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is worded: Do not revile my companions, for by the One in Whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend gold equal to Mount Uhud, he would not reach one of them, or even half of it. The wording is: He would not reach the level of one of them, or even half of it. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated this hadith on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “Do not revile the companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), for one hour of standing with one of them is better than the deeds of one of you for a lifetime.”
57:12: His statement: 12- The Day you see the believing men and believing women The agent in the circumstance is implied, which is mentioner, or generous, or He multiplies it, or the agent in for them which is stability, and the address is to everyone who is suitable for it, and His statement, Their light will proceed is in the accusative case as a state of the object of you will see, and the light is the radiance that is seen before them and on their right and that is on the Sirat on the Day of Resurrection, and it is their guide to Paradise. Qatada said: A light will shine for the believer as is between Aden and Sana'a, until there are among the believers there is one whose light will not shine for him except the place where his feet are. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: And on their right are their books that they were given, so their books are in their right hands, and their light is before them. Al-Farra' said: The ba' has the meaning of in: that is, in their right hands, or it has the meaning of about. Ad-Dahhak also said: Their light guided them, and by their right hands He wrote them down. Ibn Jarir At-Tabari preferred this view: meaning, their right hands and righteous deeds are before them, and in their right hands are written down their deeds. The majority read by their right hands as the plural of right hand. Sahl bin Sa’d As-Sa’idi and Abu Haywah read by their right hands with a kasra on the hamza, meaning that what is meant by faith is the opposite of disbelief. It was also said that it refers to the Qur’an, and the preposition and noun in both cases are in the accusative case as a hal of their light, meaning, being before them and by their right hands. Your good tidings this day are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein you will abide eternally.... are” is the subject, and its predicate is gardens, as an implied noun: meaning, entering gardens. The sentence is the statement of an implied statement: meaning, this is said to them, and the one who says this to them are the angels. Al-Makki said: Al-Farra’ permitted the accusative case of Jannat as a state, and today would be the predicate of your good report, and this is very unlikely. They will abide therein is a predicate that is understood, and the reference in his saying: that is to the light and good report, and it is a subject and its predicate is it is the great victory, meaning its value cannot be estimated, as if there is no victory other than it, and no consideration is given to what is other than it.
57:13: 13- The Day the hypocrites, men and women, will say A day instead of the first day, and it is possible that the factor in it is the great victory, and it is possible that it is accusative with an implied verb: i.e., remind to those who have believed The lam is for notification like its counterparts. The majority read Anzuruna as a command by connecting the hamza and damma the fa from anzur meaning to wait: i.e., wait for us, they say that when they see the believers being hastened to Paradise. Al-A'mash, Hamza, and Yahya ibn Waththab read it by cutting off the hamza and kasra the dhaal from inzur: i.e., give us time and inform us. It is said, Anzurtuhu wa istanzaruhu I gave him time and asked him to give me time: i.e., I gave him time and asked him to give me time. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say anzurni I give me time: i.e., wait for me. And he recited the words of Amr ibn Kulthum: Abu Hind, do not rush us and wait for us to tell you for sure. It was said that the meaning of look at us is look at us, because when they look at them, they face them and are illuminated by their light. We take from your light, meaning we are illuminated by it. The flame is the torch from the fire and the lamp. When they said that, It was said, ‘Go back behind you,’ meaning the believers or the angels said to them, as a rebuke and mockery: Go back behind you to the place from which we took the light, ‘and seek light,’ meaning seek light there for yourselves, because it is from there that light is taken. It was also said that the meaning is: Go back to this world and seek the light with what we sought of faith and righteous deeds. It was also said that by light they meant the darkness behind them, mocking them. Then He placed between them a wall, a wall is a barrier between two things, and what is meant by it here is the barrier between Paradise and Hell, or between the people of Paradise and the people of light. Al-Kisa’i said: The ba’ in ‘wall’ is redundant. Then God described the aforementioned wall, saying: It has a door, within it is mercy, meaning the interior of that wall. It is the side that follows the people of Paradise, in which there is mercy, which is Paradise. And its exterior is the side that follows the people of Hell. Before it is the torment, meaning from its side is the torment of Hell. It was said that the believers will precede them and enter Paradise. The hypocrites will be in the torment, and between them is the wall. It was said that the mercy within it is the light of the believers, and the torment on its exterior is the darkness of the hypocrites.
57:14: And when the wall was set up between the believers and the hypocrites, God the Almighty informed us of what the hypocrites said at that time, saying: 14- They will call out to them, ‘Were we not with you?’ That is, we were in agreement with you outwardly, praying as you pray in your mosques and doing the deeds of Islam like you. The sentence is a new sentence, as if it was said: So what did the hypocrites say after the wall was set up between them and the believers? He said: They will call out to them. Then God the Almighty informed us of what the believers answered them, saying: They said, ‘Yes,’ That is, you were with us outwardly, but you tempted yourselves with hypocrisy and concealing disbelief. Mujahid said: You destroyed it with hypocrisy, and it was said: with desires and pleasures. And you waited for Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the believers with him for the events of time. It was also said: You waited for repentance, but the former is more appropriate. And you doubted means you doubted the matter of religion and did not believe in what was revealed of the Qur’an or in the apparent miracles. And you were deluded by wishful thinking, the false ones, including what you were in of waiting. It was also said: it is the length of hope, and it was also said: what they were wishing for due to the weakness of the believers. Qatada said: The wishful thinking here is the deception of Satan, and it was also said: the world, and it was also said: it is their greed for forgiveness, and all of these things are included in the term wishful thinking. Until the command of God came, which is death, and it was also said: His victory for His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Qatada said: it is their being thrown into the Fire. And the Deceiver deceived you about God. The majority of scholars read the Deceiver with a fat-ha on the ghayn, and it is an adjective on the form fa’ul, and what is meant by it is Satan: that is, Satan deceived you with God’s forbearance and His respite. Abu Haywah, Muhammad ibn al-Samīf’ and Samāk ibn Harb read it with a ḍammah, and it is a verbal noun.
57:15: 15- So today no ransom will be taken from you by which you could ransom yourselves from the Fire, O hypocrites, nor from those who disbelieved in God outwardly and inwardly. Your refuge is the Fire meaning your home to which you will flee. It is your protector meaning it is more deserving of you. The protector is originally the one who takes care of a person’s interests, then it was used to refer to the one who stays with him. It was said that the meaning of your protector is: your place close by, from the word guardian which means closeness. It was said that God [places] life and reason in the Fire, so it is distinguished by its wrath against the disbelievers. It was said that the meaning is: it is your supporter, in the manner of the poet’s saying: Greetings between them are a painful blow "And what an evil destination" you will end up in, which is Hellfire. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, Their light will proceed before them. He said: They will be given their light according to the extent of their deeds. They will pass over the Sirat. Some of them will have light like a mountain, and some of them will have light like a palm tree. The light nearest to them will be on their thumb; it will be extinguished at one time and rekindled at another. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba`th on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: While the people were in darkness, God sent a light. When the believers saw the light, they headed towards it, and the light was their guide from God to Paradise. When the hypocrites saw the believers heading towards the light, they followed them, and God cast darkness upon the hypocrites. They then said, Wait for us to borrow from your light, for we were with you in the world. The believers said, Go back behind you, from where you came from the darkness, and seek the light there. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will call people on the Day of Resurrection by their mothers as a screen from Him for His servants. As for at the Bridge, God will give every believer a light and every hypocrite a light. When they are all lined up on the Bridge, God will take away the light of the hypocrites, both men and women. The hypocrites will say, ‘Wait for us so that we may take from your light.’ The believers will say, ‘Our Lord, perfect our light for us.’” No one mentions anyone at that time. There are hadiths and narrations on this topic. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit: He was on the wall of Jerusalem and he cried, so he was asked, What makes you cry? He said: Here the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us that he saw Hell. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin al-As, who said: The wall that God mentioned in the Qur’an, And He placed between them a wall, is the wall in Jerusalem’s eastern part. Inside it is mercy, meaning the mosque. And outside it is torment, meaning the Valley of Hell and what is next to it. It is no secret that interpreting the chapters mentioned in the Qur’an in this verse as this chapter located in Jerusalem contains a problem that cannot be refuted by any discussion, especially after adding the statement: its interior is in mercy, the mosque. This is not what the verse was intended for and other than what it indicated. Where is Jerusalem or its wall located in relation to the wall separating the two groups of believers and hypocrites? What is the meaning of mentioning the mosque of Jerusalem here? If what is meant is that God, the Exalted, will remove the wall of Jerusalem and make it in the Hereafter a wall pitched between the believers and the hypocrites, then what is the meaning of interpreting the interior of the wall and what is in it of mercy as the mosque? And if what is meant is that God will lead the two groups of believers and hypocrites to Jerusalem and will place the believers inside the wall in the mosque, and will place the hypocrites outside it, then they will then be on the Sirat and on the way to Paradise and not to Jerusalem. If such an interpretation is proven from the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, then we accept it and believe in it; otherwise, there is no honor or acceptance. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Sha`b on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: But you tempted yourselves he said: with desires and pleasures and you waited he said: with repentance and wishful thinking deceived you until the command of God came he said: death and the Deceiver deceived you about God he said: Satan.
57:16: His saying: 16- Has not the time come for those who have believed? It is said Ana laka yanna anna: if it has come. The majority read Alma ya’na and Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Samak read Alma ya’na and Ibn Al-Sikkit recited: Is it not time for my blindness to be revealed and for me to stop being with Layla? Yes, it is time for me And that their hearts should be humbled is the subject of groaning: meaning that the time for their hearts to be humbled is coming, and from this comes the poet’s saying: Is it not time for my heart to leave the ignorant and for the enlightened gray hair to give us reason? This verse was revealed about the believers. Al-Hasan said: He finds them impatient, even though they are the most beloved of His creation to Him. It was also said that the address was to those who believed in Moses and Jesus, but not Muhammad. Al-Zajjaj said: It was revealed about a group of believers who were urged to be gentle and humble. As for those whom God described as gentle and humble, they are a class above these. Al-Suddi and others said: The meaning is: Has not the time come for those who have believed outwardly but concealed their disbelief, that their hearts should humble themselves at the remembrance of God? We will come at the end of the discussion with evidence that supports the view of those who said that it was revealed about the Muslims, and humbleness is the softness and tenderness of the heart. The meaning is: The remembrance should instill in them humbleness and tenderness, and they should not be like those whose hearts do not soften at the remembrance and do not humble themselves at it. And what has come down of the truth is in apposition to the remembrance of God, and what is meant by what has come down of the truth is the Qur’an. Thus, the remembrance conjoined to it may be interpreted as referring to everything else that contains the remembrance of God with the tongue or what comes to mind. It was also said that what is meant by the remembrance is the Qur’an, so this apposition is an explanatory apposition, or it takes into consideration the change in the two concepts. The majority readنزل with a shaddah and in the active voice. Nafi' and Hafs read it with a tafsir and in the active voice. Ibn Mas'ud readأنزلas in the active voice. And do not be like those who were given the Scripture before. The majority read it with a tadhiyyah for the third person, in accordance with what was mentioned above. Abu Haywah and Ibn Abi 'Ubla read it with a tadhiyyah for the second person, shifting the attention. 'Isa and Ibn Ishaq read it this way. The sentence is conjoined with َختخزare humbled: meaning, is it not time for their hearts to be humbled and not to be? The meaning is: the prohibition against them following the path of the Jews and Christians who were given the Torah and the Gospel before the revelation of the Qur'an. So the period was prolonged for them, meaning the time between them and their prophets was prolonged. The majority read al-amad with a soft dal, and Ibn Kathir read it with a shaddah in a narration from him: meaning a long time. It was said that what is meant by al-amad according to the first reading is the term and the goal. It is said that someone extended such-and-such, meaning his goal. Their hearts hardened because of that, and for that reason they distorted and changed. So God, the Exalted, congratulated the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they are like them. And many of them are wicked, meaning they are outside the obedience of God because they abandoned working with what was revealed to them, and they distorted and changed and did not believe in what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that they are those who abandoned belief in Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said that they are those who turned away from monasticism, and they are the people of monasteries.
57:17: 17- Know that God revives the earth after its death. He is able to resurrect bodies after their death, and soften hearts after their hardness. We have made clear to you the signs, which include these verses, so that you may understand. That is, so that you may understand the sermons they contain and learn accordingly.
57:18: 18- Indeed, the men and women who give charity The majority of scholars read it with a shaddah on the sad in both instances of sadaqah charity, and its original form is al-mutasadiqin wa al-mutasadiqat charitable men and women, so the ta was assimilated into the sad. Abi Al-Muttasadiqin wa al-mutasadiqat charitable women with the ta as per the original form. Ibn Kathir read it with a light sad in both instances of tasadiq believing: meaning, they believed in what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought. And loan God a goodly loan is conjoined with the active participle in al-musadiqin the men who give charity and loan, because when it is a relative clause for the relative definite article, it replaces the verb, so it is as if he said: Indeed, those who give charity and loan, so-and-so said Abu Ali Al-Farisi and others. It is said that the phrase and loan is an interjection between the subject of in and its predicate, which is yudib multazibal. It is also said that it is a relative clause for an omitted relative pronoun: meaning, those who lend. A goodly loan is an expression for giving charity and spending in the way of God with a sincere intention, a sound purpose, and seeking reward. The majority of scholars read it as yuddhifa'uhu with a fatha on the 'ayn in the passive voice, and the subject is either a preposition and a noun in the genitive case or a pronoun referring to the believers with the omission of an adjective: i.e. their reward. Al-A'mash read it as yuddhifa'uhu with a kasra on the 'ayn and an addition of the ha'. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir, and Ya'qub read it as yuddhifa'u with a shaddah on the 'ayn and a fatha, and for them is a generous reward which is Paradise. The multiplication here means that a good deed is multiplied by ten to seven hundred times its like.
57:19: 19- And those who believed in God and His messengers, all of them. The reference in His statement, those, is to the relative pronoun, and its predicate is His statement, They are the truthful and the martyrs, and the clause is the predicate of the relative pronoun. Mujahid said: Everyone who believes in God and His messengers is a truthful one. Al-Muqatilani said: They are those who did not doubt the messengers when they informed them and did not deny them. Mujahid said: This verse is specifically for the martyrs, and they are the prophets who testify for the matter and against them. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj chose this view. Muqatil bin Sulayman said: They are those who were martyred in the cause of God. Ibn Jarir said the same. It was also said that they are the nations of the messengers who will testify on the Day of Resurrection for their prophets’ conveyance. The apparent meaning of the verse is: Those who believed in God and His messengers all are in the same position as the truthful ones and the martyrs, who are known for their high status with God. It was also said that the truthful ones are those who exaggerate in truthfulness, as they believed in God and believed in all His messengers, and they stand up for God, the Most High, in monotheism. Then, the Almighty explained what good they will have because of their belief in God and His Messengers, saying: For them is their reward and their light. The first pronoun refers to the relative pronoun, and the last two pronouns refer to the truthful and the martyrs. So, all three pronouns refer to one thing, and the meaning is: For them is the promised reward and light. Then, after He mentioned the state of the believers and their reward, He mentioned the state of the disbelievers and their punishment. He said: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, meaning they combined disbelief with denial of the signs. The reference in His statement, those, is to the relative pronoun, considering what is in its connection of their being characterized by disbelief and denial. This is a subject and its predicate is the companions of Hellfire, who will be tormented there and will have no reward or light. Rather, it is an enduring torment and eternal darkness. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God felt impatient with the hearts of the emigrants after seventeen years of the revelation of the Qur’an, so He revealed: ‘Has not the time come for those who have believed?’” The verse. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to a group of his companions in the mosque and they were laughing. He pulled his cloak, making his face red, and said: ‘Are you laughing while you have not received security from your Lord that He has forgiven you? And a verse was revealed to me concerning your laughter: ‘Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God?’ They said: ‘O Messenger of God, what is the expiation for that?’ He said: ‘You will cry as much as you laughed.’” Muslim, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: “Between our conversion to Islam and when God admonished us with this verse: ‘Has not the time come for those who have believed?’” The verse. Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim narrated something similar on his authority, and he authenticated it. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through a different chain of narration. Abu Ya'la and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him that he said: When this verse was revealed, some of us turned to one another and said: What have we done? What have we done? Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that God felt the hearts of the emigrants were slow, so He rebuked them thirteen years after the revelation of the Quran, reciting: Has not the time come for those who have believed? Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf from Abdul Aziz ibn Abi Rawad that joking and laughter appeared among the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so this verse was revealed: Has not the time come for those who have believed? Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated from Ibn Abbas that: Know that God gives life to the earth after its death. He said: Meaning, He softens hearts after their hardness. Ibn Jarir narrated from Al-Bara' ibn Azib that he heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: The believers of my nation are martyrs. Then the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited: And those who have believed in God and His messengers - those are the truthful and the martyrs in the sight of their Lord. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: Every believer is a truthful and a martyr. Al-Hakim narrated with a saheeh hadith on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: A man may die in his bed as a martyr, then he recited this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And those who believe in God and His messengers - those are the truthful. He said: This is separate. And the martyrs are with their Lord, for they will have their reward and their light. Ibn Hibban narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah al-Juhani: He said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, tell me, if I testify that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God, and I pray the five daily prayers, and pay the zakat, and fast and pray during Ramadan, then who am I? He said: Among the truthful and the martyrs.”
57:20: His statement: 20- Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement. When the Almighty mentioned the state of the second group and what they committed of disbelief and denial, which was because of their inclination towards this world and its influence, He showed them their insignificance and that it is too insignificant to have any influence on the Hereafter. Play is falsehood. Amusement is anything that one is amused by and then it goes away. Qatada said: Play and amusement. Eating and drinking. Mujahid said: All play is amusement. It was said that play is what gives desire to this world, and amusement is what distracts from the Hereafter and occupies it. It was said that play is acquisition, and amusement is women. The confirmation of this was presented in Surat Al-An’am. Adornment is adorning oneself with worldly pleasures without working for the Hereafter. And boast among yourselves The majority read it with the tanween of boast and the adverbial phrase is an adjective for it, or its object. Al-Salami read it with the addition: that is, some of you boast about it to others. It was said that they boast about their creation and strength, and it was said about lineage and pedigree as the Arabs were. And multiply in wealth and children that is, they multiply with their wealth and children and are arrogant to the poor. Then the Almighty explained this life with a likeness and gave it an example, saying: Like the example of rain whose growth pleases the disbelievers that is, like the example of rain whose growth pleases the farmers. What is meant by the disbelievers here are the farmers because they cover the seed: that is, they cover it with dirt, and the meaning of its growth is the growth produced by it. Then it withers that is, it dries up after it has turned green. And it dries up. You will see it yellow meaning it has changed from its green color, and the luster has turned to a yellowish color and withered. Then it becomes debris meaning shattered, broken, and shattered crumbs after it dries. The explanation of this example has been presented in Surah Yunus and Surah Al-Kahf. The meaning is that the life of this world is like a crop that delights those who look at it because of its greenery and abundant freshness. Then it does not take long for it to become shattered straw as if it had never existed. It was read as yellowed, and the kaf is in the accusative case as a state, or in the nominative case as a predicate after a predicate or a predicate of a deleted subject. Then, when God, the Exalted, mentioned the insignificance of this world and the speed of its disappearance, He mentioned what He has prepared for the disobedient in the Hereafter, saying: And in the Hereafter is a severe punishment. He followed it with what He has prepared for the obedient, saying: And forgiveness from God and approval. The indefiniteness in both is for emphasis. Qatadah said: A severe punishment for the enemies of God. And forgiveness from God and approval for His allies and the obedient. Al-Farra' said: The estimation is a severe punishment for the enemies of God. And forgiveness and pleasure from God for His friends and those who obey Him. Al-Farra' said: The estimation in the verse is either severe punishment or forgiveness, so do not stop at severe. Then, after the intimidation and encouragement, God the Almighty mentioned the insignificance of this world, saying: And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion for those who are deceived by it and do not work for the Hereafter. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The enjoyment of delusion is for those who do not occupy themselves with seeking the Hereafter, but whoever is occupied with seeking it will have the enjoyment of reaching what is better than it. This sentence confirms and emphasizes the previous example.
57:21: Then He urged His servants to compete in what necessitates forgiveness, such as repentance and righteous deeds, because that is a path to Paradise. He said: 21- Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord meaning, hasten like those who race one another in righteous deeds that necessitate forgiveness from your Lord, and repent for the sins you have committed. It was said that what is meant by the verse is the first takbir with the imam, as Makhul said. It was also said that what is meant is the first row. There is no reason to specify what is in the verse with something like this, rather it is part of what is true in a comprehensive or alternative sense. And a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth meaning like their width. If this is the extent of its width, then what do you think of its length? Al-Hasan said: It means all of the heavens and the earth spread out, each one towards its companion. It was said that what is meant by the Paradise whose width is this width is the Paradise of each one of the people of Paradise. Ibn Kaysan said: He meant by it one of the gardens, and the width is less than the length. It is the custom of the Arabs to express something by its width rather than its length, and from that is the saying of the poet: As if the lands of God, which are wide, are like a rope to the fearful and sought after. This has been explained in Surah Al Imran, then God the Almighty described Paradise with another attribute, saying: It has been prepared for those who have believed in God and His messengers. This sentence may be a new sentence. This is evidence that Paradise is deserved merely by believing in God and His messengers. However, this is restricted by the evidence that no one deserves it except the one who does what God has enjoined upon him and avoids what God has forbidden. There is much evidence for this in the Qur’an and Sunnah. The reference in His statement: that is to what God the Almighty has promised of forgiveness and Paradise. It is a subject and predicate. The bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills means that He gives it to whom He wills, as a favor and kindness. And God is the possessor of great bounty, so He bestows upon whom He wills whatever He wills. There is no one who can withhold what He gives, nor can He give what He withholds. All good is in His hand, and He is the Absolutely Generous and Bountiful Who does not withhold.
57:22: Then the Almighty made clear that whatever calamities befall His servants has been predestined and decreed and recorded in the Mother of the Book, saying: 22- Whatever disaster strikes upon the earth from drought, poor vegetation, and lack of fruits. Muqatil said: drought and lack of vegetation and fruits, and it was said: catastrophes in crops. nor within yourselves Qatadah said: with afflictions and diseases. Muqatil said: the implementation of the prescribed punishments. Ibn Jurayj said: the narrowness of livelihood except in a Book is in the accusative case as a state of calamity: that is, except when it is written in a Book, which is the Preserved Tablet. The phrase before We bring it into being is in the genitive case as an attribute of Book, and the pronoun in we bring it into being refers to the calamity, or to the souls, or to the earth, or to all of that. The meaning of we bring it into being is we create it. “Indeed, that, for God, is easy,” that is, establishing it in the Book, despite its abundance, is easy for God, not difficult.
57:23: 23- So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you meaning, We tested you with that so that you may not grieve over what has escaped you of this world. And do not rejoice over what He has given you of it: meaning, what He has given you of it, because that will soon disappear, and everything that disappears soon does not deserve to be rejoiced over its attainment or grieved over its loss. And although everything is by the decree and predestination of God, no one will go beyond what has been written for him, and whatever will inevitably occur, he does not deserve to be rejoiced over its attainment or grieved over its loss. It was said that the grief and joy that are forbidden are those in which one transgresses into what is not permissible, otherwise there is no one who does not grieve and rejoice. The majority of scholars read By what He has given you with a long vowel, meaning He gave you. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Nasr ibn Asim, and Abu Amr read it with a short vowel, meaning He brought it to you. Abu Hatim preferred the first reading, and Abu Ubaid preferred the second reading. And God does not like anyone who is arrogant and boastful, meaning He does not like anyone who has these two characteristics: arrogance and boasting. It was said that this is a criticism of the joy in which a person is arrogant and haughty. It was also said that whoever rejoices in worldly fortunes and feels great in his soul will be arrogant and boastful about them. It was also said that the arrogant is the one who looks at himself, and the proud is the one who looks at people with contempt. It is better to interpret these two characteristics with their legal meaning and then their linguistic meaning. Whoever has them is the one whom God does not love.
57:24: 24- "Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness on people" The relative pronoun is in the nominative case as a subject, and it is a new statement with no connection to what precedes it. The predicate is understood: those who are miserly, then God is independent of them. This is indicated by His statement: "And whoever turns away - then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy. It was also said that the relative pronoun is in the genitive case as a substitute for arrogant," but this is far-fetched, because this miser who is miserly with what is in his hand and enjoins miserliness on people is not the same as the arrogant and proud one, neither linguistically nor religiously. It was also said that it is in the genitive case as an attribute of it, but this is also far-fetched. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Those who are miserly with knowledge and enjoin miserliness on people with it so that they do not teach people anything. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is miserliness in fulfilling God’s duty. It was also said that it is miserliness in giving charity. Tawus said: It is miserliness with what one has. It was also said that he meant the Jewish leaders who were miserly in describing Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) in their books lest people believe in him and their food would be lost. As-Suddi and Al-Kalbi said: The majority read by miserliness with a damma on the ba’ and a sukoon on the kha’. Anas, Ubayd ibn Umair, Yahya ibn Ya’mar, Mujahid, Hamid, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read it with two fathahs, which is the dialect of the Ansar. Abu Al-Aliyah and Ibn As-Samee’ read it with a fathah on the ba’ and a sukoon on the kha’. Nasr ibn Asim read it with a damma on both of them, and all of them are dialects. And whoever turns away, then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy. That is, whoever turns away from spending, then indeed, God is Free of need of him and is praised by His creation, and it will not harm Him. The majority read He is the Rich by affirming the separating pronoun. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy without the pronoun. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves meaning in religion and this world except that it is in a register before We bring it into being meaning We create it, so that you may not grieve over what has escaped you of this world, nor rejoice over what He has given you of it. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: It is something that has been completed before the souls are brought into being. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’b also narrated on his authority regarding the verse, so that you may not grieve over what has escaped you he said: There is no one who does not grieve and rejoice, but whoever is afflicted with a calamity turns it into patience, and whoever is afflicted with good turns it into gratitude. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding the verse, saying: He means the calamities of livelihood, not the calamities of religion. He said: So that you will not grieve over what has escaped you and not rejoice over what He has given you. This is not from the calamities of religion. He commanded them to grieve over the bad and rejoice over the good.
57:25: His statement: 25- Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs meaning with clear miracles and manifest laws and sent down with them the Scripture meaning the genus, so it includes the book of every messenger and the balance that people may maintain justice Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The balance is justice, and the meaning is: We commanded them to be just as in His statement: And the heaven He raised and placed the balance and His statement: It is God who sent down the Book with the truth and the balance Ibn Zayd said: It is what is weighed and dealt with, and the meaning of that people may maintain justice is that they may follow what they were commanded to do of justice and deal with one another fairly, and justice is justice, and it indicates that what is meant by the balance is justice, and the meaning of sending it down is sending down its causes and requirements. According to the view that what is meant by it is the instrument with which weighing is done, then sending it down means guiding people to it and inspiring them to weigh with it, and the speech is of the type - I fed them straw and cold water. “And We sent down iron” means We created it, as in His statement: And He sent down for you from the livestock eight mates. The meaning is that He created it from minerals and taught people how to make it. It was also said that it was sent down with Adam. Therein is great force because weapons of war are made from it. Al-Zajjaj said: It is used to protect oneself and to fight. The meaning is that a tool for pushing and a tool for striking is made from it. Mujahid said: It contains a shield and weapons. The meaning of and benefits for people is that they benefit from it in many of their needs, such as knives, axes, needles, and agricultural, carpentry, and building tools. And that God may know who will support Him and His messengers unseen is conjoined with His statement: That people may establish a position. That is, We have sent Our messengers and done such and such so that people may establish a position and so that He may know. It was also said that it is conjoined with an implied reason, as if it was said so that they may practice it and that God may know, but the first is more appropriate. Meaning: God has commanded in the Book that He revealed to support His religion and His messengers. So whoever supports His religion and His messengers, He knows that he will support them, and whoever disobeys, He knows that he will be the opposite. And unseen is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of supports or its object: meaning absent from them or absent from Him. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might meaning capable of everything, dominant over everything, and He has no need for any of His servants to support Him and His messengers. Rather, He charged them with that so that they may benefit from it if they comply and so that what He promised His obedient servants may be obtained for them.
57:26: 26- And We sent Noah and Abraham. When God Almighty mentioned sending the messengers in general, He indicated here a type of detail, so He mentioned His message to Noah and Abraham, and repeated the oath for emphasis. And We placed among their descendants prophethood and the Scripture. That is, We placed among them prophethood and the Scriptures revealed to the prophets among them. It was said that He made some of them prophets and some of them recite the Scripture. And among them is he who is guided. That is, among the descendants is he who is guided by the guidance of Noah and Abraham. It was said that the meaning is: Among those to whom the prophets were sent from the people of the prophets is he who is guided by what the prophets brought of guidance. And many of them are wicked. Those who disobey.
57:27: 27- Then We followed up their footsteps with Our messengers meaning We followed up the footsteps of the offspring or the footsteps of Noah and Abraham with Our messengers whom We sent to the nations, such as Moses, Elijah, David, Solomon, and others. And We followed up with Jesus, the son of Mary meaning We sent messenger after messenger until we reached Jesus, the son of Mary, who is from the offspring of Abraham on his mother’s side. And We gave him the Gospel which is the book that God revealed to him, and the mention of its derivation was mentioned previously in Surat Al Imran. The majority read the Gospel with a kasra on the hamza, while Al-Hasan read it with a fatha on it. And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy. Those who followed him are the disciples. God placed in their hearts affection for one another, and mercy with which they show mercy to one another, unlike the Jews, who are not like that. The root of compassion is gentleness, and mercy is pity. It was said that compassion is the most intense mercy. And monasticism which they invented. Monasticism is in the accusative case due to the preoccupation: that is, and they invented monasticism which they invented, and it is not conjoined with what preceded it. It was said that it is conjoined with what preceded it: that is, and We placed in their hearts compassion and mercy, and monasticism which they invented from themselves. The first is more appropriate, and Abu Ali Al-Farisi and others preferred it. The phrase We did not prescribe it for them is a second description of monasticism, or a new sentence confirming that it was an innovation from their own side. The meaning is: We did not impose it on them. Monasticism, with the fatha or damma of the ra’, has been read with both. With the fatha it means fear of monasticism, and with the damma it is attributed to the monks. This is because they went to extremes in worship and imposed hardships on themselves by abstaining from food, drink and sex, and they clung to caves and monasteries, because their kings changed and altered, and only a few of them remained, so they became monastics and ascetics. Its meaning was mentioned by Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and others: Except seeking the pleasure of God. The exception is disjunctive: that is, We did not prescribe it for them at all, but they innovated it seeking the pleasure of God. Al-Zajjaj said: We did not prescribe it for them means that We did not prescribe anything for them at all. He said: Except seeking the pleasure of God is a substitute for the ha’ and the alif in We wrote it, and the meaning is: We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God. But they did not observe it with its right observance, that is, they did not observe this monasticism that they innovated on their own, but rather they distorted it and disbelieved in the religion of Jesus, and entered into the religion of the kings that they changed and altered and abandoned monasticism. Only a few of them remained on the religion of Jesus, and they are the ones meant by His statement: So We gave those who believed among them their reward, which they deserved for their faith, because they believed in Jesus and remained steadfast in his religion until they believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when God sent him. And many of them are wicked, outside of the faith in what they were commanded to believe in. The reason for blaming them, assuming that the exception is discontinuous, is that they had obligated themselves to monasticism believing that it was obedience and that God was pleased with it, so abandoning it and not observing it with its right observance was It indicates their indifference to what they believe to be religious. As for the view that the exception is connected, and that the meaning is: We did not prescribe it for them for any reason except that they might seek thereby the pleasure of God after We had guided them to invent it, then the reason for the blame is clear.
57:28: Then the Almighty commanded the believers in the previous messengers to fear God and to have faith in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: 28- O you who have believed, fear God by abandoning what He has forbidden you, and believe in His Messenger, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He will give you a double portion of His mercy, meaning two shares of His mercy because of your belief in His Messenger after your belief in the messengers who came before him. The root of a portion is a share and a portion. We have already discussed its interpretation in Surat An-Nisa’. And He will make for you a light by which you will walk, meaning on the path, as He said: Their light will proceed before them. It has also been said that the meaning is: And He will make for you a clear path in the religion by which you will be guided, “and He will forgive you,” your previous sins, and God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning He is eloquent in forgiveness and mercy.
57:29: 29- So that the People of the Book may not know The lam is related to what preceded the command to believe and fear God. The meaning is: Be pious and believe, and He will give you such and such, so that those among the People of the Book who did not fear God nor believe may know that they have no power over anything of God’s bounty. The la in His statement: so that they may not have power is redundant for emphasis, as stated by Al-Farra’, Al-Akhfash, and others. The an in His statement: that they may not have power is the lightened form of the heavy form, and its subject is a deleted pronoun of a matter, and its predicate is what follows it. The sentence is in the accusative case as the object of knows. The meaning is: So that the People of the Book may know that they are not able to attain anything of God’s bounty that He bestowed upon those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are not able to repel that bounty that God bestowed upon those who deserved it. The sentence and that bounty is in God’s hand is conjoined with the sentence before it: that is, so that they may know that they are not able and so that they may know that bounty is in God’s hand, glory be to Him. His statement: He gives it to whomever He wills is a second predicate. Because, or it is the predicate, and the preposition and noun in the accusative case are in the state of circumstance. And God is the possessor of great bounty. This sentence confirms the content of what preceded it, and what is meant by bounty here is what He bestowed upon those who feared Him and believed in His Messenger of a double reward. Al-Kalbi said: It is God’s provision, and it was said that God’s blessings are countless, and it was said that it is Islam, and it was also said that the la in la’ala is not redundant, and the pronoun they are not able to refers to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his companions, and the meaning is: so that the People of the Book do not think that the Prophet and the believers are not able to have anything from God’s bounty, which is an expression for what they were given, and the first is more appropriate. Ibn Mas’ud read so that he may not know, and Khattab ibn Abdullah read because he knows, and Ikrimah read so that he may know, and it was read layla by changing the hamza to a ya, and it was read with a fatha on the lam. Abd bin Hamid and Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi in Nawader Al-Usul, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it and authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha`b, through the chains of transmission of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Abdullah! I said, ‘At your service, O Messenger of God,’ three times. He said: ‘Do you know which lineage of Islam is the most trustworthy?’ I said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘The best of people are those who do best in deeds if they understand their religion. O Abdullah! Do you know which of the people are the most knowledgeable?’ I said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘The most knowledgeable of people is the one who sees the truth when people differ, even if he is negligent in deeds and even if he crawls on his backside. And those who came before us differed into seventy-two sects, three of which were saved and the rest were destroyed: A sect supported the kings and fought them for the religion of God and Jesus, son of Mary. A sect did not have the strength to support the kings, so they stayed among their people and called them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, so the kings killed them and sawed them through with saws... By supporting the kings and not staying with them, they wandered in the mountains and practiced monasticism there, and they are the ones about whom God said: “And monasticism they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its right observance. So We gave those among them who believed their reward” they are those who believed in Me and confirmed Me and many of them are wicked those who denied Me and disbelieved in Me.” Al-Nasa’i, Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi in Nawader Al-Usul, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were kings after Jesus who changed the Torah and the Gospel. There were believers among them who read the Torah and the Gospel. It was said to their kings: They have not been saved from anything more severe than the insults that these people insult us with. They read: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the disbelievers “And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the wrongdoers” These are they who are the wicked in addition to what they criticize us for regarding our actions in their reading. So call them to read as we read and believe as we believe. So he called them and gathered them and offered them to be killed, or to abandon reading the Torah and the Gospel except what they changed from them. They said: What do you want to do with that? So a group of them said: Build us a pillar and raise us up to it, then give us something to raise our food and drink with and we will not turn back to you. A group said: Let us roam the earth and wander and eat what the wild beasts eat and drink what they drink. If you gain control over us in your land, kill us. A group said: Build us houses in the deserts and we will dig wells and cultivate vegetables and we will not turn back to you or pass by you. There is no one among the tribes who does not have a kinsman among them. So they did that, and God revealed: “Monasticism, which they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its right observance.” The others, from among the polytheists who worshipped and those who died out, said: We will worship as so-and-so worshipped and wander as so-and-so wandered and take houses as so-and-so did while they were still polytheists. They have no knowledge of the faith of those who followed their example. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent and only a few of them remained, the hermit descended from his hermitage, the traveler returned from his travels, and the monastery owner returned from his monastery. They believed in him and confirmed his belief. God said, "O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy." They were rewarded for their belief in Jesus and their establishment of the Torah and the Gospel, and for their belief in Muhammad and their confirmation. And He will make for you a light by which you will walk. They followed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ahmad, al-Hakim at-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Anas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Every nation has monasticism, and the monasticism of this nation is jihad in the cause of God. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari regarding his statement, two portions, he said, twice, and it is in the Ethiopian dialect. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement: He will give you two parts of His mercy, that he said: The two parts are three hundred and fifty parts of God’s mercy.
58:1: It is twenty-two verses. It is Madani. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion, except for a narration from Ata’, the first ten of it were Madani and the rest were Makki. Al-Kalbi said: All of it was revealed in Madinah except for the statement: There are not three who converse privately but He is the fourth of them, which was revealed in Makkah. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Mujadilah was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar statement on the authority of Az-Zubayr. His saying: 1- "God has heard" Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read it by assimilation of the dal into the seen, and the rest read it by idhhar. Al-Kisa'i said: From the dal when it comes to the seen, his tongue is foreign and not Arabic. "The statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband" means she argues with you about him. "And complains to God" is in apposition to arguing with you. This argument that she had with the Messenger of God was that whenever he said something to her, she would become angry with him. She said: By God, he did not mention divorce. Then she would say: I complain to God of my poverty and loneliness, and that I have young children. If I take them with him, they will be lost, and if I take them with me, they will starve.
