She would raise her head to the sky and say: O God, I complain to You. This is the meaning of His saying: "And complains to God." Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: This verse was revealed about Khawlah bint Tha'labah and her husband Aws ibn al-Samit. He had a affliction, and one day his affliction intensified, so he declared dhihar repentance from her, then he regretted it. Dhihar was considered a divorce in the pre-Islamic era. It was said that she is Khawlah bint Hakim, and it was said that her name is Jamila, and the first is more correct, and it was said that she is the daughter of Khuwaylid. Al-Mawardi said: She was sometimes named after her father, and sometimes after her grandfather, and one of them is her father and the other is her grandfather, so she is Khawlah bint Tha’laba bin Khuwaylid. The phrase And God hears your dialogue is in the accusative case as a state, or it is a new sentence that runs in the course of explaining what came before it: meaning, God knows that you both return to each other in speech. Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. He hears everything that is heard and sees everything that is seen, and among that is what this woman argued with you about.
58:2: Then God, the Almighty, explained the status of zihar in itself and mentioned its ruling, saying: 2- Those of you who swear an oath of divorce against their wives. The majority of scholars read yuziharun with a shaddah and a fathah on the present tense letter. Ibn Amir, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read yuziharun with a fathah on the ya’, a shaddah on the dha’, and an additional alif. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Asim, and Zar ibn Hubaish read yuziharun with a damma on the ya’, a softened dha’, and a kasrah on the ha’. A similar example has been presented in Surat Al-Ahzab. Abu Al-Awza’arun read yuziharun without assimilation. The meaning of zihar is to say to his wife: You are to me like the back of my mother: meaning, there is no disagreement that this is zihar. They differed about if he says: You are to me like the back of my daughter or sister, or any other mahram. A group of them, including Abu Hanifah and Malik, held that it is zihar. Al-Hasan, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Zuhri, Al-Awza’i, and Al-Thawri said the same. A group of scholars, including Qatada and Al-Sha'bi, said that it is not considered zihar, but rather zihar applies only to the mother. There are different narrations from Al-Shafi'i. Some narrations are similar to the first statement, and others are similar to the second. The root of zihar is derived from back. They differed if someone says to his wife, You are to me like my mother’s head, hand, leg, or something similar. Is this considered zihar or not? Similarly, if someone says, You are to me like my mother, but does not mention the back. It appears that if he intends zihar by that, then it is zihar. It was narrated from Abu Hanifa that if he likens her to a part of his mother’s body, it is permissible for him to look at it, but it is not zihar. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i that zihar only applies to the back. They differed over whether he compares his wife to a foreign woman. Some said it is considered zihar and others said it is not. The discussion of this is explained in detail in the books of branches. The phrase their mothers are not is in the nominative case as it is the predicate of the relative pronoun. That is, their women are not their mothers. This is a lie from them, and in this there is a rebuke and reprimand for those who make zihar. The majority read their mothers in the accusative case in the Hijazi dialect in which ma acts as laysa. Abu Amr and As-Salami read it in the nominative case without acting on it, and it is the language of Najd and Banu Asad. Then God the Almighty explained to them their mothers in reality, saying: Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them meaning their mothers are none but the women who gave birth to them. Then the Almighty increased His rebuke and rebuke of them, saying: And indeed, they say an abominable statement and a lie. That is, indeed, those who support it say what they say, an abominable statement: that is, a terrible statement that is rejected by the Shari’ah. Falsehood is a lie. The accusative of abominable and falsehood is that they are descriptions of a deleted source: that is, an abominable statement and a lie. And indeed, God is Forgiving and Pardoning. That is, He is most eloquent in His forgiveness and pardon, as He made the expiation upon them to free them from this abominable statement.
58:3: 3- And those who swear an oath of divorce from their wives and then go back on what they said When God, the Almighty, mentioned zihar in general terms and rebuked its doers, He proceeded to detail its rulings. The meaning is: And those who say that reprehensible, false statement, then go back on what they said: meaning to what they said by making up for it and making amends, as in His statement: that you return to the like of it meaning to the like of it. Al-Akhfash said: When they said and to what they said, they alternate. He said: And they said, ‘Praise be to God, who has guided us to this’ and He said: So guide them to the path of Hellfire and He said: Because your Lord inspired her and He said: And it was inspired to Noah Al-Farra’ said: The lam means [about], and the meaning is: Then they go back on what they said and want to have intercourse. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: Then they return to wanting to have intercourse because of what they said. Al-Akhfash also said: The verse contains an inversion, and the meaning is: And those who abstain from their wives and then return to what they were doing of intercourse, the freeing of a slave for what they said: meaning, it is upon them to free a slave for what they said. So the preposition in His statement: for what they said is related to the omitted word which is the predicate of the subject, which is upon them. Scholars differed in interpreting the aforementioned repetition into several opinions: The first is that it is the intention to have intercourse. This is what the Iraqis, Abu Hanifa and his companions, said. It was also narrated from Malik. It was also said that it is the intercourse itself. This is what al-Hasan said, and it was also narrated from Malik. It was also said that the one who kept her as a wife after the zihar, while being able to divorce her. This is what al-Shafi’i said. It was also said that it is expiation, meaning that he does not consider intercourse with her permissible except with expiation. This is what al-Layth ibn Sa’d said, and it was narrated from Abu Hanifa. It was also said that it is repeating the zihar with its wording, and this is what the scholars of the apparent meaning said. It was narrated from Bakir ibn al-Ashja, Abu al-Aliyah, and al-Farra’. The meaning is: Then they return to what they said. The relative clause is the subject and its predicate is freeing a slave, assuming that they are obligated to free a slave as mentioned above, or that it is obligatory upon them to free a slave. It is said that I freed him, meaning I made him free. It appears that any slave is sufficient. It was also said that it is required that she be a believer, like a slave in the expiation for murder. Abu Hanifa and his companions said the first, and Malik and Al-Shafi’i said the second. They also stipulated that she be free from every defect. Before they touch each other. What is meant by touching here is sexual intercourse. This is what the majority said. It is not permissible for the one who has pronounced zihar to have intercourse until he expiates. It was also said that what is meant by it is enjoyment of sexual intercourse, touching, or looking at the vagina with lust. This is what Malik said, and it is one of the opinions of Al-Shafi’i. The reference in his saying that is to the aforementioned ruling, which is the subject and its predicate. You are admonished by it, meaning you are commanded to do it, or warned by it against committing zihar. This explains what is intended by the law of expiation. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse is that the severity of the expiation is an admonition to you: that is, the severity of the expiation is an admonition to you so that you abandon zihar. And God is All-Aware of what you do. Nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him, so He will reward you for them.
58:4: Then the Almighty mentioned the ruling for the one who is unable to make expiation, saying: 4- But whoever cannot find a slave, then a fast of two consecutive months before they touch each other. That is, whoever does not find a slave in his possession and is not able to obtain her value, then he must fast two consecutive months without breaking the fast. If he breaks the fast, he must start over if he broke the fast without an excuse. But if it was for an excuse such as travel or sickness, then Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, ‘Amr ibn Dinar, al-Sha’bi, al-Shafi’i and Malik said that he should continue and not start over. Abu Hanifah said that he should start over, and this was narrated from al-Shafi’i. The meaning of before they touch each other is what was mentioned earlier. So if he has intercourse at night or during the day, intentionally or by mistake, he must start over, and Abu Hanifah and Malik said the same. Al-Shafi’i said: He does not have to start over if he has intercourse at night because it is not a time for fasting. The first is better. And whoever is unable meaning fasting for two consecutive months then feed sixty poor persons meaning he must feed sixty poor persons, each poor person two mudds, which are half a sa’. Abu Hanifa and his companions said the same. Al-Shafi’i and others said: For each poor person, there is one mudd. What is apparent from the verse is that he should feed them until they are satisfied once, or give them what will satisfy them. He is not obligated to gather them all at once, rather it is permissible for him to feed some of the sixty on one day, and some of them on another day. The reference in his saying: that is to what was mentioned previously of the rulings, and it is the subject and its predicate is understood: that is, that is, that you may believe in God and His Messenger. It is permissible for the demonstrative pronoun to be in the accusative case, and the meaning is: We did that so that you may believe: that is, so that you may believe that God commanded it and legislated it: or that you may obey God and His Messenger in the commands and prohibitions, and stop at the limits of the law and not transgress them and do not return to zihar, which is an evil and false statement. The reference in his saying: and those is to the mentioned rulings, and it is the subject, and its predicate is the limits of God, so do not transgress the limits that He has set for you, for He has made clear to you that zihar is a sin, and that its expiation mentioned requires pardon and forgiveness. And for the disbelievers who do not… They stop at the limits of God and do not act according to what God has set for His servants. A painful punishment, which is the punishment of Hell. He called it disbelief to emphasize and intensify it. Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: Blessed be He whose hearing encompasses all things. I hear the words of Khawlah bint Tha’labah, some of which are hidden from me, as she complains about her husband to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and she says: O Messenger of God, he has consumed my youth and made my belly swell for him, until now I have grown old and my children have ceased to be children, and he has become apparent to me. O God, I complain to You. She said: I did not stop until Gabriel came down with these verses: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband - and he is Aws ibn As-Samit. Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first person to pronounce zihar in Islam was Aws, and he was married to his cousin Khawlah bint Khuwaylid. He pronounced zihar from her, but he was disappointed and said: I see that you are forbidden to me, so go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him. So she went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found his hairdresser with him, so she told him. He said: O Khawlah, we have not been commanded to do anything about your matter. So God revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O Khawlah, be of good cheer. She said: Good. He said: Good. So he recited to her: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband [verses]. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Yusuf ibn Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: “Khawlah bint Tha’labah told me: By God, and about Aws ibn al-Samit, God revealed the beginning of Surat al-Mujadilah. She said: I was with him, and he was a very old man whose character had become bad. One day, he came to me, and I argued with him about something, so he became angry and said: ‘You are to me like my mother’s back.’ Then he went back and sat in the gathering of his people for a while, then he came to me and he wanted to talk to me about myself. I said: ‘No, by the One in Whose hand is Khawlah’s soul, you will not get to me, and you have said what you have said, until God and His Messenger have judged us.’ Then I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him. I did not leave until the Qur’an was revealed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was overcome by what had always overwhelmed him, then he was relieved, and he said to me: ‘O Khawlah, God has revealed about you and your companion.’ Then he recited to me: ‘God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you’ until His saying: ‘A painful punishment.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Tell him to free a slave.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, he has nothing to say about me.’” He said: Then let him fast for two consecutive months. I said: By God, he is very old and he has no time for fasting. He said: Then let him feed sixty poor people a wasq of dates. I said: By God, he does not have that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then I will help him with a bushel of dates. I said: And I, O Messenger of God, will help him with another bushel. He said: You have done well and done well, so go and give it in charity on his behalf, then treat your cousin well. She said: So I did. There are hadiths on this topic. Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated In his Sunan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then they return to what they said, he said: It is the man who says to his wife: You are to me like my mother’s back. If he says that, it is not permissible for him to approach her by marriage or otherwise until he expiates by freeing a slave. Then whoever… If he cannot find [that], then he should fast for two consecutive months before they touch each other. And touching is marriage. Then whoever… If “he cannot, then he should feed sixty poor people. And if he says to her: You are to me like my mother’s back if I do such and such, then there is no zihar pronouncement of divorce for that until he breaks his oath. If he is persistent, then he should not approach her until he expiates, and zihar does not constitute divorce. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: There are three things in which there is a mudd: expiation for an oath, expiation for zihar, and expiation for fasting. Al-Bazzar, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘I divorced my wife by zihar, and I saw the whiteness of her anklet in the moonlight, and I had intercourse with her before I made atonement.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Did not God say before they touch each other?’ He said: ‘I have done it, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Refrain from her until you make atonement.’” Abd Al-Razzaq, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Al-Hakim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man said: ‘O Messenger of God, I divorced my wife by zihar, and I had intercourse with her before I made atonement.’ He said: ‘What made you do that?’ He said: ‘I saw…’” Her anklet in the moonlight, he said: Do not approach her until you do what God has commanded you. Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, Abd ibn Hamid, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, al-Tabarani, al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, and al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated on the authority of Salamah ibn Sakhr al-Ansari, who said: “I was a man who had been given intercourse with women in a way that no one else had been given. When Ramadan came, I renounced intercourse with my wife until Ramadan had passed, fearing that I might have intercourse with her at night, and I would continue to do that and not be able to stop until morning came. While she was serving me one night, something of her uncovered itself to me, so I jumped on her. When morning came, I went out to my people and told them what had happened.” So I said: Come with me to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and inform him of my situation. They said: No, by God, we will not do that, for we fear that the Qur’an might be revealed about us, or that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) might say something about us that would leave us with shame. But go and do what you want. So I went out and came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him of my situation. He said: Are you doing this? I said: I am doing this. He said: Are you doing this? I said: I am doing this. He said: Are you doing this? I said: I am doing this, and here I am. So carry out God’s judgment, for I will be patient. He said: Free a slave. I struck my neck with my hand and said: No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I do not own anything else this day. He said: Fast two consecutive months. I said: Did what happened to me happen only because of fasting? He said: Then feed sixty poor people. I said: By Him Who sent you with the truth, we spent this night hungry and without any supper. He said: Go to the charity collector of Banu Zuraiq and tell him to give it to him and feed sixty poor people from it a wasq on your behalf, then use the rest of it to help you and your family. I returned to my people and said: I found hardship and bad opinion among you, but I found plenty and blessing with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He has ordered your charity for me, so give it to me. So they gave it to him.
58:5: His statement: 5- Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger When God, the Exalted, mentioned the believers who abide by His limits, He mentioned the opponents. Opposition is quarrel, enmity, and opposition. Similar to this is His statement: Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger Al-Zajjaj said: Opposition is to be in a limit that contradicts your companion, and its root is resistance, and from it is iron, and from it is the blacksmith for the doorman. They were subdued as those before them were subdued meaning they were humiliated and disgraced. It is said: God subdued so-and-so if He humiliated him, and the one who is returned with humiliation is called Makboot. Al-Muqatilan said: They were disgraced as those before them from the polytheists were. Qatadah said the same. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: They were destroyed. Ibn Zayd said: They were tormented. Al-Suddi said: They were cursed. Al-Farra’ said: They enraged them. What is meant by those before them are the disbelievers of the past nations who were hostile to the messengers of God. The future is expressed in the past tense to indicate that it will happen. It is also said that the meaning is: in the past, and that is what happened to the polytheists on the day of Badr, for God subdued them with killing, capture, and subjugation. The phrase And We have sent down clear signs is in the accusative case as a state of the waw in they subdued: meaning, and the state is that We have sent down clear signs to those who opposed God and His messengers from the previous nations. It is also said that what is meant are the obligations that God, the Most High, sent down, and it is also said that they are the miracles. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment, meaning for the disbelievers in everything that must be believed in, so the signs mentioned here are included as a primary inclusion. And the humiliating punishment is that which humiliates and degrades its doer and takes away his honor.
58:6: 6- The Day God will resurrect them all The adverbial phrase is in the accusative case due to the implied verb remember, or to humiliate, or to what the preposition lam is attached to of stability, or to He counted mentioned after it, and the accusative case of all is in the state of: that is, gathered together in one state, or He will resurrect them all, not one of them will remain except that he is resurrected. Then He will inform them of what they did meaning He will inform them of what they did of the ugly deeds they did in this world as a rebuke and reprimand to them and to complete the argument against them. The phrase God has counted it, and they have forgotten it is a new answer to an implied question, as if it was said, How will He inform them of that with its multitude and different types? So it was said, God has counted it all, and nothing of it has escaped Him? The fact is that they have forgotten it and did not memorize it, rather they found it present and written in their scrolls. And God is Witness over all things. Nothing is hidden from Him, rather He is All-Knowing and All-Watching.
58:7: Then the Almighty confirmed the statement that He knows everything. He said: 7- Do you not see that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? That is, do you not know that His knowledge encompasses what is in them, such that nothing in them is hidden from Him? The phrase whatever happens of a secret conversation between three etc. is a new sentence to confirm the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and its encompassing of all information. The majority read be with a lower vowel. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa', al-A'raj, and Abu Haywah read it with a higher vowel. In both readings, it is complete. Min is added for emphasis. Najwa is the subject of kan, and Najwa is a secret. It is said: Qawm Najwa, meaning those who whisper, and it is a verbal noun. The meaning is: what happens of three people whispering or of those who whisper. Najwa may be applied to people whispering. In the first reading, the word three is lowered by adding Najwa to it. In the other two readings, the lowered word is a substitute for Najwa or an attribute of it. Al-Farra’ said: “Three are descriptions of the secret conversation, so it is in the accusative case, and if you wish, you can add secret conversation to it. If it is in the accusative case with an implied verb, it is permissible, and this is the reading of Ibn Abi Ubla. It is permissible to raise three as a substitute for the place of secret conversation. “Except He is their fourth.” This sentence is in the accusative case as a state, and likewise his statement: Except He is their sixth. “Except He is with them.” That is, none of these things exists except in one of these states, so the exception is devoid of the most general states. The meaning of their fourth is that He makes them four, and likewise their sixth is that He makes them six, in that He shares with them in knowing that secret conversation. Nor five. That is, nor is there a secret conversation between five. The two numbers were specifically mentioned because most of the customs of those who are secretly talking are for them to be three or five, or the incident that is the reason for revelation was about those who were secretly talking, three in one place and five in another. Al-Farra’ said: “The number is not intended because He, glory be to Him, is with every number, whether little or much. He knows the secret and the public. Nothing is hidden from Him. “Nor less than that nor more but that He is with them.” That is, nor less than the mentioned number, such as one or two, nor more than it, such as six or seven, but that He is with them. He knows what they whisper to each other about, nothing of it is hidden from Him. The majority of scholars read nor more in the accusative case with a fatha, in apposition to the word confidential conversation. Al-Hasan, Al-A’mash, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Abu Haywah, Ya’qub, Abu Al-Aliyah, Nasr, Isa ibn Umar, and Salam read it in the nominative case, in apposition to the location of confidential conversation. The majority of scholars read nor more with a triangle. Al-Zuhri and Ikrimah read it with a unified letter. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The hypocrites and the Jews used to whisper among themselves and make the believers think that they were whispering about things that would upset them, so they would be saddened by that. When that went on for a long time and became frequent, they complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered them not to whisper to each other without the Muslims. But they did not stop doing that and returned to their whispering, so God revealed these verses. The meaning of wherever they are is that His action encompasses every whispering that they may have in any place. Then He will inform them that is, He will tell them what they did on the Day of Resurrection as a rebuke and reprimand to them and to make the argument binding. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things nothing is hidden from Him, whatever it may be.
58:8: 8- Have you not considered those who were forbidden from secret conversation, then they return to that which they were forbidden? These people who were forbidden, then they return to that which they were forbidden, are the hypocrites and the Jews mentioned above. Muqatil said: There was an appointment between the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Jews. When a believer passed by them, they would whisper among themselves until the believer would think evil. God forbade them, but they did not desist, so this verse was revealed. Ibn Zayd said: A man would come to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ask him for a need and whisper to him, while the land at that time was at war. They would imagine that he was whispering to him about a war, a calamity, or an important matter, so they would be startled by that. And they whisper about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger. The majority read yatanaju with the weight of tafa'alun.
58:9: Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this reading because of what he said later: 9- "If you whisper, do not whisper. Hamzah, Khalaf, and Warsh read on the authority of Ya'qub and they whisper with the weight of yafta'alun," which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and his companions. Sibawayh narrated that "tafa'alu and ifta'alu have the same meaning, such as takhasamau and ikhasamau and taqatala and iqtalawa. The meaning of sin" is that which is sinful in itself, such as lying and injustice, and aggression is that which includes aggression against the believers, and disobedience to the Messenger is opposing him. The majority read "and and disobedience" in the singular. Ad-Dahhak, Hamid, Mujahid, and "disobedience" in the plural. "And when they come to you and greet you with that with which God has not greeted you," Al-Qurtubi said: What is meant by it is the Jews who would come to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and say "As-samu 'alayka, outwardly meaning peace, but inwardly meaning death," so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say: "And upon you." In another narration, And upon you “And they say within themselves” meaning among themselves Why does God not punish us for what we say? meaning why does He not punish us for that? If Muhammad were a prophet, He would punish us for what our saying implies of belittling him. It was said that the meaning is: If he were a prophet, he would have been answered regarding us when he says And upon you, and death would have befallen us at that time. Sufficient for them is Hell as a punishment. They will burn in it they will enter it. How evil is the destination meaning the return, which is Hell. O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger. When He, glory be to Him, finished forbidding the Jews and hypocrites from private conversation, He guided the believers, if they confer privately among themselves, not to confer about what contains sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger of God, as the Jews and hypocrites do. Then He explained to them what they whisper to each other about in their gatherings and in private, saying: And whisper to each other about righteousness and piety, meaning about obedience and abandoning sin. It was said that the address was to the hypocrites, and the meaning is: O you who have believed outwardly or by their claim. This was chosen by Al-Zajjaj. It was said that the address was to the Jews, and the meaning is: O you who have believed in Moses, and the first is more appropriate. Then He, glory be to Him, frightened them and said: And fear God, to whom you will be gathered, and He will reward you with your deeds.
58:10: Then the Almighty made clear that what the Jews and hypocrites do of whispering is from Satan, so He said: 10- The secret conversation meaning with regard to sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger is only from Satan not from anyone else: that is, from his embellishment and instigation that he may grieve those who believe that is, in order to make them feel sad by what they get from the thought that they are in a trap that they are being plotted against and it will not harm them at all or neither Satan nor the secret conversation that Satan embellishes with harming the believers at all except by permission of God that is, by His will, and it was said with His knowledge and in God let the believers put their trust that is, they entrust their affair to Him and delegate all their matters to Him and they seek refuge in God from Satan and they do not care about what he embellishes of secret conversation. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Sha’b narrated it. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Umar: The Jews used to say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, As-Samu ‘Alaikum, meaning to insult him. Then they would say to themselves, Why does God not punish us for what we say? So this verse was revealed: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you. Ahmad, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, and al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, narrated on the authority of Anas, “A Jew came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions and said, ‘As-Samu ‘Alaikum.’ The people responded to him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Do you know what he said?’ They said, ‘God knows best. He greeted me, O Prophet of God.’ He said, ‘No, but he said such and such.’ They responded to him. He said, ‘Did you say As-Samu ‘Alaikum?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ At that point, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘If one of the People of the Book greets you, then say, ‘Alaikum.’ He said, ‘Alaikum, what you said.’ He said, ‘And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you.’” Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said, “The Jews entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘As-Samu ‘Alaikum, O Abu al-Qasim.’ Aisha said: “Death and the curse be upon you.” He said: O Aisha, God loves obscenity and not the obscene. I said: Don’t you hear them say ‘Death’? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Did you not hear me say ‘And upon you’? Then God revealed: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: The hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when they greeted him: Death be upon you. So this verse was revealed. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: “When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent out an expedition and engaged in it, the hypocrites would meet and lower their heads to the Muslims and say, ‘These people have been killed.’ But when they saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), they would whisper to each other and show grief. report of this reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims, so God revealed: “O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: If you are three, two should not whisper to the third, for that will make him sad. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id who said: “We used to take turns telling the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) about something, and many of the people who were there and those who were waiting increased in number one night until we were all talking. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came out to us in the middle of the night and said: ‘What is this whispering? Were you not forbidden from whispering?’ We said: ‘O Messenger of God, we were mentioning the Messiah out of fear of him.’ He said: ‘Shall I not tell you of something that I fear for you more than him?’ We said: ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Hidden polytheism is when a man stands up and does something in place of another.’” Ibn Kathir said: This chain of transmission is strange, and it contains some weak narrators.
58:11: His statement: 11- O you who have believed, when you are told, ‘Space yourselves in assemblies,’ it is said, He made space for you, meaning, He made room for you. And from this is their saying, a spacious town. God, the Exalted, commanded us to have good manners with one another by making room in the assembly and not being cramped in it. Qatada, Mujahid, and Ad-Dahhak said: They used to compete in the assembly of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so they were commanded to make room for one another. Al-Hasan and Yazid ibn Abi Habib said: It is the assembly for battle when they lined up for war. They used to quarrel over who should be in the first row, so they would not make room for one another out of a desire to fight to attain martyrdom. So make room, and God will make room for you, meaning, make room, and God will make room for you in Paradise, or in whatever you want to make room in, such as space, provision, etc. The majority read tafasahaw fi assemblies. As-Salami, Zur ibn Hubaysh, and Asim read fi assemblies in the plural, because each one of them had an assemblage. Qatada, Al-Hasan, Dawud ibn Abi Hind, and Isa ibn Umar read tafasahaw. Al-Wahidi said: The correct interpretation is the singular form in al-majlis, because he meant by it the assembly of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qurtubi said: The correct interpretation of this verse is that it is general and applies to every gathering in which Muslims gather for good and reward, whether it is a gathering of war, remembrance, or on Friday, and that each person has more right to the place he reached first, but room should be made for his brother as long as he is not harmed by that and the cramped space does not force him out of his place. This is supported by the hadith of Ibn Umar, as recorded by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: A man should not make another man get up from his seat and then sit in it, but make room and make room. “And when it is said to rise, rise.” The majority of scholars read it with a kasra on the shin, while Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and ‘Aasim read it with a damma on the shin in both of them. These are two dialects with the same meaning. It is said that nashaza means to rise, yanshaz, yanshaz, like ‘akif, ya’kif, and ya’kif. The meaning is: when it is said to you, rise, rise. The majority of commentators said: that is, rise for prayer, jihad, and doing good deeds. Mujahid, Al-Dahhak, and Ikrimah said: There were men who were reluctant to pray, so it was said to them, when the call to prayer is made, rise. Al-Hasan said: Rise up to fight. Ibn Zayd said: This was in the house of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There was a man among them who wanted his last meeting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be his last. So God Almighty said: And when it is said to rise up, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then rise up, for he has needs, so do not delay. Qatada said: The meaning is: Answer if you are called to a matter of good. The apparent meaning is to carry the verse in a general sense, and the meaning is: If you are told to rise up to a matter of religious matters, then rise up and do not be slow. The reason for carrying it in a general sense is not prevented by the fact that it is specific, for consideration is given to the generality of the wording, not to the specificity of the reason, as is the truth. What is the reason for revelation is included in it primarily, and thus what is in the context, which is making room in the assembly, is included primarily. We have already mentioned that the meaning of nashaz is to rise, and thus it is said nashaz yanshiz: if he moves away from his place, and from this a woman nashiz: meaning one who withdraws from her husband, and its origin is taken from nashaz, which is what rose from the ground and moved away. An-Nahhas mentioned its meaning: God raises those who believe among you in this world and the hereafter by providing them with a share in them. And those who have been given knowledge by degrees meaning He raises those who have been given knowledge by high degrees in honor in this world and reward in the hereafter. The meaning of the verse is that He raises those who believe by degrees over those who do not believe and He raises those who have been given knowledge by degrees. Those who believe will have degrees. So whoever combines faith and knowledge, God will raise him by degrees through his faith, and then raise him by degrees through his knowledge. It was said that those who believe are meant to be the Companions, as well as those who were given knowledge. It was also said that those who were given knowledge are those who recited the Qur’an. It is better to interpret the verse in general terms, referring to every believer and every person with knowledge of the religious sciences from all the people of this religion. There is no evidence to indicate that the verse is specific to some people and not others. In this verse there is a great virtue for knowledge and its people, and its virtue and their virtue are indicated by Qur’anic verses and prophetic hadiths: And God is Acquainted with what you do. Nothing of your deeds, good or evil, is hidden from Him, so He will reward you for good with good and for evil with evil.
58:12: 12- O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an act of charity. Conversation is private talk, and the meaning is: If you want to confide in the Messenger about any of your affairs, present an act of charity before your private conversation with him. Al-Hasan said: This was revealed because some Muslims used to confide in the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so some Muslims thought that they were belittling them in their private conversation, and this upset them, so God commanded them to give charity when they conferred privately to prevent them from seeking his privacy. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It was revealed because the hypocrites and the Jews were whispering to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and saying that he was an ear that heard everything that was said to him, and he did not prevent anyone from whispering to him. This was difficult for the Muslims, because Satan was making them think that they were whispering to him about groups that had gathered to fight him. So God revealed: O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer privately about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger. But they did not stop, so God revealed this verse, and the people of falsehood stopped whispering because they did not offer charity before their whispering. This was difficult for the people of faith, and they refrained from whispering because many of them were too weak to give charity, so God lightened the burden for them with the verse after this. The reference in His saying: that is to what came before, offering charity before the whispering, and it is the subject and its predicate. It is better for you and purer because it involves obedience to God. The restriction of the command to compliance being better for them than not complying and purer for their souls indicates that it is a recommended command, not an obligatory command. But if you do not find [anything], then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful means that whoever among them does not find the charity commanded before the secret conversation, then there is no blame upon him for the secret conversation without giving charity.
58:13: 13- Did you fear to offer alms before your private conversation? That is, did you fear poverty and destitution so that you would offer that? Fear is the fear of something unpleasant, and the question is for confirmation. It was also said that the meaning is: you were stingy, and the plural of alms here is in consideration of those being addressed. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was only for ten nights, then it was abrogated. Al-Kalbi said: It was only for one night. Qatada said: It was only an hour of the day. So when you did not do what you were commanded to do of charity before the secret conversation. This is addressed to those who found what to give in charity and did not do it. As for those who did not find anything, permission was given to them in His saying: But if you do not find anything, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. “And God has turned to you” by giving you permission to leave it. When is in its proper context in indicating continuity. It was said that it means if, and it was said that it means if. “And turned to you” is conjoined with you did not do: that is, if you did not do it and when He turned to you then establish prayer and give zakat. The meaning is: If you are reluctant to comply with the command to give charity before the secret conversation, then persevere in establishing prayer, giving zakat, and obeying God and His Messenger in what you are commanded to do and forbidden from doing. And God is Acquainted with what you do. Nothing of that is hidden from Him, so He will reward you. There is nothing in the verse that indicates the believers’ negligence in complying with this command. As for the poor among them, the matter is clear. As for the believers other than them, they did not… They were not required to engage in private conversation until charity became obligatory upon them. Rather, they were commanded to give charity if they wanted to engage in private conversation. So, whoever neglected private conversation is not negligent in complying with the command to give charity. However, the verse indicates that the mother is for encouragement, as we mentioned earlier. These verses were used as evidence by those who said that abrogation is permissible before the act is possible. This evidence is not correct, as abrogation did not occur until after the act was possible. Also, some did that, and gave charity before engaging in private conversation, as will be mentioned. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Muqatil ibn Hayyan who said: This verse, When you are told to make room in the assemblies, was revealed on a Friday while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in the Suffah, and the place was narrow. He was honoring the people of Badr from among the Muhajirun and Ansar. Some people from the people of Badr came and had reached the assemblies first, so they stood in front of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: “Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of God and His blessings.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) responded to them. Then they greeted the people after that and they responded to them. They stood on their feet waiting for space to be made for them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knew what was causing them to stand, so he did not make room for them. This upset him, so he said to those around him from the Muhajirun and Ansar who were not from Badr: Stand up, so-and-so, and you, so-and-so. He continued to make them stand according to the number of people who were standing from among the people of Badr. This upset those who were made to stand from their seats, so this verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: This is in the battle council. And when it is said to rise up, he said: To goodness and prayer. Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi in al-Madkhal narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees, he said: God will raise those who have been given knowledge among the believers above those who have not believed, by degrees. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud in their interpretation of this verse, he said: God will raise those who have believed among you and have been given knowledge above those who have believed but have not been given knowledge. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: God did not specify the scholars in any part of the Quran as He specified them in this verse. God preferred those who believed and were given knowledge over those who believed but were not given knowledge. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, When you confer privately with the Messenger, the verse, that he said: The Muslims asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, many questions until they became difficult for him. God wanted to make things easier for His Prophet, but when he said that, many people became suspicious and stopped asking questions. Then God revealed after that, Did you fear? the verse, so God made things easy for them and did not make things difficult. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: “When the verse, ‘O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation a charity,’ was revealed, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me, ‘What do you think of a dinar?’ I said, ‘They cannot afford it.’ He said, ‘What about half a dinar?’ I said, ‘They cannot afford it.’ He said, ‘What about how much?’ I said, ‘A barley grain.’ He said, ‘You are indeed insignificant.’ Then the verse, ‘Did you fear to present before your private conversation a charity?’ was revealed, and through me God lightened the burden on this nation.” What is meant by barley here is the weight of a barley grain of gold, not one barley grain. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said, ‘No one acted upon it except me until it was abrogated, and it was only an hour ago’ - meaning the verse about the private conversation. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Abi Shaybah, `Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: There is a verse in the Book of God which no one before me acted upon, and no one will act upon after me. It is the verse of confidential conversation: O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an amount of charity. I had a dinar which I sold for ten dirhams. Every time I conferred privately with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I would present before my private conversation a dirham. Then it was abrogated and no one acted upon it. Then the verse was revealed: Do you fear to present before your private conversation an amount of charity? At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. Al-Suyuti said: With a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: “The verse, ‘O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an act of charity,’ was revealed. So I presented a grain of barley, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘You are indeed an ascetic.’ Then the other verse was revealed: ‘Do you fear to present before your private conversation an act of charity?’”
58:14: His statement: 14- Have you not considered those who took a people as allies? That is, took an illusion as allies. Qatadah said: They are the hypocrites who took the Jews as allies. As-Suddi and Muqatil said: They are the Jews who took the hypocrites as allies. The first is indicated by His statement: God’s wrath is upon them, for those who incur His wrath are the Jews. The second is indicated by His statement: They are neither of you nor of them, for this is a description of the hypocrites, as God said about them: Wavering between that, neither with these nor with those. The phrase they are neither of you nor of them is in the accusative case as a state of affairs, or it is a new sentence. And they swear to a lie, that is, they swear that they are Muslims, or they swear that they did not transmit the report to the Jews. The phrase and they know is in the accusative case as a state of affairs, meaning that they know the invalidity of what they swore to, and that it is a lie with no truth to it.
58:15: 15- God has prepared for them a severe punishment because of this turning away and swearing falsely. Evil indeed is what they have been doing of ugly deeds.
58:16: 16- They took their oaths as a shield. The majority read their oaths with a fat-ha on the hamza, the plural of oath, which is what they swore falsely that they were Muslims to avoid being killed. So they made these oaths a shield and a protection against their blood, just as a fighter makes heaven a shield for himself from being struck by a sword, spear, or arrow. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah read their belief with a kasra on the hamza, meaning they made their belief a shield from being killed. Their tongues felt safe out of fear of being killed, but their hearts did not feel safe. So they turned people away from the path of God means they prevented people from Islam because of what they did of discouraging and belittling the Muslims and weakening their power. It was said that the meaning is: So they turned the Muslims away from fighting them because of their outward display of Islam. So for them is a humiliating punishment, meaning it humiliates and disgraces them. It was said that it is a repetition of His statement, God has prepared for them a severe punishment for emphasis. It was said that the first is the punishment of the grave, and this is the punishment of the Hereafter. There is no basis for saying that there is repetition, because the punishment described as severe is not the punishment described as humiliation.
58:17: 17- Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God meaning, they will not avail them at all against His punishment. Muqatil said: The hypocrites said: Muhammad claims that he will be victorious on the Day of Resurrection. Then we will be wretched. By God, we will be victorious on the Day of Resurrection with ourselves, our wealth and our children, if there is to be a Resurrection. Then the verse was revealed: Those are described as mentioned, are the companions of the Fire they will not leave it, they will abide therein eternally they will not emerge from it.
58:18: 18- On the Day when God will resurrect them all The circumstance is in the accusative case due to His saying: humiliating, or due to what is understood: that is, remember. And they will swear to Him as they swear to you that is, they will swear to God on the Day of Resurrection falsely as they swore to you in this world. This is due to the severity of their misery and the increased sealing on their hearts, for on the Day of Resurrection the truths will be revealed and matters will be known by necessity of witnessing. So how can they dare to lie in that situation and swear falsely and they think that they are on something that is, they think in the Hereafter that with those false oaths they are on something that brings benefit or wards off harm as they thought that in this world. Unquestionably, they are the liars that is, they are complete in lying, immersed in it, and have reached a level that no one else has reached by their committing it and their false oaths in the situation of Resurrection before the Most Merciful.
58:19: 19- Satan took control of them meaning he overcame them, became arrogant and took control. Al-Mubarrad said: To take possession of something means to encompass it and surround it. It was also said to be strong over them, or to gather them together. It is said to gather something, meaning to gather it and join some parts to others. The meanings are close because if he gathers them together, he has overpowered them, overcome them, become arrogant to them, dominate them, and surround them. So He made them forget the remembrance of God, meaning His commands and the work of obeying Him, so they did not remember any of that. It was also said His prohibitions in forbidding His disobedience. It was also said that they did not remember Him in their hearts or with their tongues. The reference in His statement, Those, is to those mentioned who are described with those attributes. It is the subject and predicate, the party of Satan, meaning his soldiers, followers, and group. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers, meaning those who are complete in loss, so that it is as if the loss of others in comparison to their loss is not a loss, because they sold Paradise and guidance for misguidance, and lied about God and His Prophet and swore false oaths in this world and the hereafter.
58:20: 20- Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger The meaning of opposition to God and His Messenger was presented at the beginning of this Surah, and the sentence explains what came before it. Those are among the most humiliated meaning those who oppose God and His Messenger and are characterized by the aforementioned characteristics are among the bearers of those whom God has humiliated from among the previous and subsequent nations, because when they opposed God and His Messenger, they became humiliated in this place. Ata’ said: He means humiliation in this world and disgrace in the hereafter.
58:21: 21- God has decreed, ‘I will surely prevail, I and My messengers.’ The sentence is a resumption of what came before it, even though they are among the most humiliated. That is, He has decreed in the Preserved Tablet and decreed in His foreknowledge: I and My messengers will surely prevail, by argument and sword. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the victory of the messengers is of two types: Whoever is sent for war will prevail in war, and whoever is sent for something other than war will prevail by argument. Al-Farra’ said: Written means said, and his saying I is an emphasis. Then he mentioned something like Al-Zajjaj’s statement: Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might. So He is Powerful in granting victory to His allies, He is Victorious over His enemies, and no one can prevail over Him.
58:22: 22- You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day having friendship with those who oppose God and His Messenger. The address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone who is suitable for him: that is, they love and befriend those who oppose God and His Messenger and oppose them. The phrase have friendship is in the accusative case as the second object of you will find if it is transitive to two objects, or in the accusative case as a state if it is transitive to one object, or another description of a al-Nas 114:that is, those who combine faith and friendship with those who oppose God and His Messenger. Even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred that is, even if those who oppose God and His Messenger were the fathers of those who are friendly, etc., for faith deters from that and prevents it, and its protection is stronger than the protection of fatherhood, sonship, brotherhood, or kindred. Those - He has decreed in their hearts faith means those who do not have friendship with those who oppose God and His Messenger. The meaning of He has decreed in their hearts faith is that He created it, and it was said that He established it, and it was said that He made it, and it was said that He Collected it, and the meanings are close. And supported them with a spirit from Him meaning He strengthened them with victory from Him over their enemy in this world. He called His victory for them a spirit because through it their matter is revived. It was also said that it is the light of the heart. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: with the Qur’an and the proof. It was also said that it was with Gabriel. It was also said that it was with faith. It was also said that it was with mercy. The majority read wrote as the active voice and put faith in the accusative case as the direct object. Zur ibn Hubaish and Al-Mufaddal on the authority of Asim read it as the passive voice and raised faith as the subordinate. Zur ibn Hubaish read their clans in the plural, and this reading was narrated from Asim: And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally forever. God is pleased with them meaning He accepts their deeds and bestows upon them the effects of His immediate and deferred mercy. And they are pleased with Him meaning they rejoice in what He has given them in this life and the next. Those are the party of God meaning His soldiers who obey His commands, fight His enemies, and support His friends. In their being added to God, the Exalted, there is a great honor and a magnificent glorification for them. Unquestionably, the party of God are the successful ones meaning those who win the happiness of this world and the next, the complete ones in success, whose success has become the complete individual, until the success of others in comparison to their success is like every success. Ahmad, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting in the shade of a room with a group of Muslims. He said: ‘A man will come to you and look at you with the eye of a devil. When he comes to you, do not speak to him.’ They had not waited long before a blue-eyed man appeared. When he saw him, he said: ‘Why are you cursing me, you and your companions?’ He said: ‘Leave me to bring them to you.’ They swore and apologized, and God revealed, ‘The Day God will resurrect them all and they will swear to Him as they swear to you’ and the verse after it.” Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim, Abu Nu’aym in Al-Hilyah, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Shawdhab, who said: The father of Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah kept targeting Abu Ubaidah on the day of Badr, and Abu Ubaidah kept avoiding him. When Abu Ubaidah targeted him more and more, he killed him, and then this verse was revealed: ‘You will not find a people who believe in God…’”
59:1: It is twenty-four verses. It is Madani. Al-Qurtubi said in the opinion of all. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Surat Al-Hashr was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Surat Al-Hashr? He said: Surat An-Nadir, meaning that it was revealed about Banu An-Nadir as stated clearly in some of the narrations. His saying: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. The explanation of this was presented in Surat Al-Hadid.
59:2: 2- It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. They are Banu Nadir, a group of Jews from the descendants of Aaron, who settled in Madinah during the persecutions of the Children of Israel, waiting for Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. They betrayed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, after they had made a covenant with him, and they sided with the polytheists against him. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, besieged them until they agreed to be expelled. Al-Kalbi said: They were the first of the People of the Covenant to be expelled from the Arabian Peninsula, then the last of them were expelled during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab. Their expulsion was the first gathering from Madinah, and the last gathering was Umar's expulsion of them. It was said that the first gathering was their expulsion from their fortresses to Khaybar, and the last gathering was their expulsion from Khaybar to Syria. It was also said that the last gathering was the gathering of all people to the place of assembly, which is Syria. Ikrimah said: Whoever doubts that the gathering place on the Day of Resurrection will be in Ash-Sham, let him read this verse, and that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to them: Go out. They said: Where to? He said: To the place of gathering. Ibn al-Arabi said: The gathering place has a beginning, a middle, and a end. The first is the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir, the middle is the expulsion of the people of Khaybar, and the last is the Day of Resurrection. The commentators have unanimously agreed that those mentioned in the verse are Banu Nadir, and only Al-Hasan Al-Basri disagreed with that, saying: They are Banu Qurayzah, which is a mistake. Banu Qurayzah were not gathered together, but were killed by the judgment of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh when they accepted his ruling. He ruled that their fighters should be killed, their children should be taken captive, and their wealth should be taken as booty. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Sa`d: You have judged with the judgment of God from above seven heavens. The lam in the word first of the gathering is connected to brought out, and it is the lam of timing, like His statement: due to the decline of the sun. You did not think that they would leave This is addressed to the Muslims: that is, you Muslims did not think that Banu Nadir would leave their homes due to their strength and power, as they were people of fortified fortresses, vast estates and palm trees, and were people of numbers and equipment. And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God That is, Banu Nadir thought that their fortresses would protect them from the wrath of God. The phrase protected them is the predicate, and their fortresses is the subject that comes after. The sentence is the predicate of that they they. It is also possible that protected them is the predicate of that they and their fortresses is the subject of protected them. Abu Hayyan preferred the second opinion. The first is more appropriate. So God came to them from where they did not expect That is, God's command came to them from a place they had never imagined that His command would come to them from that direction. That is, God, the Almighty, commanded His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to fight them and expel them, although they did not think so. It was said that it was the killing of their leader Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, as stated by Ibn Jurayj, al-Suddi, and Abu Salih. Killing him weakened their power. It was said that the pronoun in It came to them without expecting refers to the believers: meaning, God’s victory came to them from where they did not expect. The former is more appropriate, based on His statement, And He cast terror into their hearts. The casting of terror was in the hearts of Banu Nadir, not in the hearts of the Muslims. Linguists say: Terror is the fear that terrifies the chest, meaning it fills it, and casting it refers to that. It was also said that the casting of terror into their hearts was due to the killing of their master Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf, but it is more appropriate not to restrict it to that and explain it by that. Rather, what is meant by the terror that God cast into their hearts is what is established in the Sahih from the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I was aided by terror, a distance of a month’s journey, “destroying their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers.” This is because when they were certain of the expulsion, they envied the Muslims for living in their homes, so they began to destroy them from within, and the Muslims from outside. Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said: The believers were destroying from outside in order to enter, and the Jews from inside to rebuild what had been destroyed of their fortress. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of its destruction by the hands of the believers is that they exposed it to that. The majority of scholars read yukharibun with a light pronunciation. Al-Hasan, As-Salami, Nasr ibn Asim, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Abu Amr read it with a shaddah. Abu Amr said: I chose the reading with a shaddah because ikhrab is leaving something in ruins, and they only destroyed it by demolishing it. What he said is not authentic, because destruction and ikhrab, according to the linguists, have the same meaning. Sibawayh said: The meanings of fa'ala and af'alta alternate, such as akhrabtuhu, kharabtuhu, afarahtuhu, and farahtuhu. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading. Al-Zuhri, Ibn Zayd, and Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made peace with them on the condition that they would have what the camels carried, they preferred a piece of wood or a column, so they would demolish their houses and load them on their camels, and the believers would destroy the rest of them. Al-Zuhri also said: They destroy their homes by breaking the treaty and the hands of the believers by fighting. Abu Amr said: With their hands in abandoning them and with the hands of the believers in expelling them. The sentence is either a new sentence explaining what they did, or in the accusative case as a state. So take heed, you who have vision, meaning take heed, reflect and consider what has befallen them, you people of reason and insight. Al-Wahidi said: The meaning of taking heed is looking into matters to know something else of the same kind.
59:3: 3- And had it not been that God had decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world. That is, had it not been that God had decreed for them to leave their homelands in that manner and decreed it for them, He would have punished them by killing and captivity in this world, as He did with Banu Qurayzah. Exile is leaving one's homeland. It is said that it is exile itself, but he expelled it without evacuation. The difference between exile and expulsion, even though they have the same meaning in terms of banishment, is in two aspects: First, exile is not with family and children, while expulsion can be with family and children remaining. Second, exile is only for a group. Expulsion can be for a group or for an individual. This is what Al-Mawardi said: And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire. This sentence is a new sentence, not connected to the answer to had it not, and it includes an explanation of what punishment will befall them in the Hereafter, even if they are saved from the punishment of this world.
59:4: And the reference in his saying: 4- That to what was mentioned previously about exile in this world and punishment in the hereafter because they opposed God and His Messenger meaning because of their opposition to God and His Messenger by not obeying and leaning towards the disbelievers and breaking the covenant And whoever opposes God - then indeed, God is severe in penalty Here he restricted himself to opposition to God. Because his opposition is opposition to His Messenger. The majority read yashaq with idgham. Talhah bin Masraf and Muhammad bin al-Samif'a read yashaq with separation.
59:5: 5- Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was done by permission of God. Mujahid said: Some of the emigrants fell into cutting down palm trees, but some of them forbade them, saying: These are spoils for the Muslims. Those who cut them down said: Rather, it is a source of anger for the enemy. So the Qur'an was revealed to confirm those who forbade cutting down palm trees and to excuse those who cut them down from sin. It said: Whatever palm trees you cut down. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: They cut down some of their palm trees and burned six. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They cut down one palm tree and burned another. Banu Nadir, who were people of the Book, said: O Muhammad, do you not claim that you are a prophet who seeks reform? Is cutting down palm trees and burning trees considered reform? And have you found in what was revealed to you permission to spread corruption on earth? This upset the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims felt uncomfortable, so the verse was revealed. The meaning of the verse: Whatever you cut off or leave of that, it is by God’s permission. The pronoun in you left it refers back to what to explain it with softness. The same is true of His statement: standing on its roots. The meaning of on its roots is that it remains as it is. The commentators differed in the interpretation of layna. Az-Zuhri, Malik, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, and Al-Khalil said: It refers to all date palms except ajwa. Mujahid said: It refers to all date palms, without excluding ajwa or others. Ath-Thawri said: It refers to the most noble date palms. Abu Ulaida said: It refers to all types of dates except ajwa and barni. Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: It refers specifically to ajwa. It was also said that it refers to a type of palm tree whose dates are called colorful, and its dates are the best of dates. Al-Asma'i said: It refers to date palms. The root of layna is lawna, but the waw was changed to a ya because of the kasra of the letter before it. The plural of layna is layn, and it was also said that it refers to layyan. Ibn Mas'ud read: You did not cut down any layna nor did you leave a people on their roots, meaning standing on their stalks. It was also read on its root, standing on its roots, and to disgrace the wicked, meaning to humiliate those who disobeyed God, who are the Jews. And He angers them by cutting it down and leaving it because when they see the believers controlling their wealth as they wish, from cutting it down to leaving it, their anger increases. Al-Zajjaj said: And to disgrace the wicked, He permitted that. The omitted part is indicated by His statement: Then by God’s permission. This verse has been used as evidence for the permissibility of ijtihad and for the approval of the mujtahids. The discussion is complete in the books of Usul.
59:6: 6- And what God bestowed upon His Messenger from them meaning what He returned to him from the wealth of the infidels. It is said that he may return if he returns, and the pronoun in from them refers to Banu Nadir. You did not urge upon it any horses or camels. It is said that the horse and the camel became dry, the horse and the camel become dry and dry: which is the speed of the blazing fire, and his owner urged him: if he made him walk quickly, the saying of Tamim bin Muqbil: Since [or beginning] with the iron eggs, it polishes it from the knees sometimes if the knees are tired Naseeb said: Oh, how many a caravan has been cut off and their corpses are coming to you. Were it not for you, the caravan would not have moved on. The word "ma in fa-ma awjaftum is negative, and the fa is the answer to the condition if the ma in his statement, what God has given as booty is conditional, and if it is a relative pronoun, then the fa is redundant, and the min in his statement, of horses" is redundant for emphasis, and the riders are what are ridden from camels specifically, and the meaning is: that what God returned to His Messenger from the wealth of Banu Nadir you did not ride horses or camels to obtain it, nor did you make the effort to obtain it, nor did you encounter war or hardship with it, but it was two miles from Madinah, so God, the Exalted, made the wealth of Banu Nadir specifically for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, for this reason. He conquered it by peace and took its wealth. The Muslims had asked him to divide it among them, so the verse was revealed: But God gives power to His messengers over whomever He wills of His enemies. This shows that this wealth was specifically for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and not for his companions, because they did not attack it with horses or camels, but rather walked to it on foot, and did not suffer any of the hardships of war. And God is over all things competent, He gives power to whomever He wills over whomever He wants, and He gives to whomever He wills and prevents whomever He wills. He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned.
59:7: 7- What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns. This is a clarification of the uses of the spoils of war after stating that they are specifically for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The repetition is for the purpose of confirmation and emphasis. The people of the towns were placed in place of the phrase from them, meaning from Banu Nadir, to indicate that this ruling does not apply only to Banu Nadir, but rather it applies to every town that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) conquered through peace and against which the Muslims did not attack with cavalry or camels. It was said that what is meant by the towns are: Banu Nadir, Qurayzah, Fadak, and Khaybar. Scholars have discussed this verse and the one before it. Are their meanings the same or different? It was said that their meanings are the same, as we mentioned, and it was said that they differ. Scholars have discussed this at length. Ibn al-Arabi said: There is no doubt that they have three meanings in three verses. As for the first verse, which is His statement: And what God has bestowed upon His Messenger from them, it is specific to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and it is the wealth of Banu Nadir and similar things. As for the second verse, which is His statement: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, this is a statement that begins differently from the first, with a claimant different from the first, although it and the first share the same fact that each includes something that God has bestowed upon His Messenger. The first verse requires that it was obtained without fighting, and the verse of Al-Anfal, which is the third verse, requires that it was obtained through fighting. The second verse, which is His statement: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, is devoid of any mention of whether it was obtained through fighting or without fighting. This is where the disagreement arose. A group said that it is attached to the first verse, which is the property of the peace treaty. A group said that it is attached to the third, which is the verse of Al-Anfal. Those who said that it is attached to the verse of Al-Anfal differed as to whether it was abrogated or final. This is the gist of his statement. Malik said that the first verse of this surah is specific to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the second verse is about Banu Qurayzah, meaning that its meaning goes back to the verse of Al-Anfal. The Shafi'i school of thought states that one-fifth of the spoils of war is to be taken, and that four-fifths of it belonged to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and after his death, it is for the benefit of the Muslims. It belongs to God, to the Messenger, to near relatives, to orphans, to the needy, and to the wayfarer. What is meant by the statement, It belongs to God, is that He decides regarding it as He wills. The Messenger belongs to him, and to near relatives, namely Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib, because they were prevented from giving zakat, so He gave them a right to the spoils of war. It was said that the division of this wealth is such that four-fifths of it goes to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and one-fifth is divided into fifths. One-fifth goes to the Messenger, one-fifth goes to each of the four categories mentioned, and another said that it is divided into sixths. The sixth is the share of God, the Most High, and is spent on causes of worship, such as building mosques and the like. So that it will not be a circulating spoils among the rich among you meaning so that the spoils of war will not be a circulating spoils among the rich to the exclusion of the poor. Dawlah is the name for something that people circulate among themselves, sometimes for this person and sometimes for that person. Muqatil said: The meaning is that the rich will prevail over the poor, so they divide it among themselves. The majority of scholars read yakun with a fat-ha, dawlah in the accusative case, meaning so that the spoils of war will not be a circulating spoils. Abu Ja`far, Al-A`raj, Hisham, and Abu Hayyan read takun with a fat-ha, dawlah in the nominative case, meaning so that a circulating spoils of war will not occur or exist. And kan is complete. The majority of scholars read dawlah with a damma on the dal. Abu Haywah and As-Sulami read it with a fat-ha. Isa ibn `Umar, Yunus, and Al-Asma`i said that they are two dialects with the same meaning.
