Abu `Amr ibn Al-`Ala` said: Dawlah with a fat-ha is that which is circulated of wealth, and with a damma it is the action. Abu `Ubaidah said the same. Then, when God, the Almighty, explained to them the uses of this wealth, He commanded them to follow the example of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), saying: {And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from.} Meaning, whatever he has given you from the spoils of war - take it. And whatever he has forbidden you from taking - refrain from it and do not take it. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: Whatever he has given you from the spoils of war - accept it, and whatever he has withheld from you - do not seek it. Ibn Jurayj said: Whatever he has given you of my obedience - do it, and whatever he has forbidden you of my disobedience - avoid it. The truth is that this verse is general and includes everything that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) brought, whether it be a command or prohibition, a statement or an action. Even if the reason is specific, then the consideration is the general meaning, not the specific reason. Everything that he brought us from the Sharia, he gave it to us and conveyed to us. How beneficial and useful is this verse. Then, when He commanded them to take what the Messenger has commanded them to do and to abandon what he has forbidden them to do, He commanded them to fear Him and to warn them of the severity of His punishment. He said: And fear God, for God is severe in punishment. He will punish whoever does not take what the Messenger gave him and does not abandon what he forbade him from. Al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Aisha who said: The Battle of Banu Nadir, a group of Jews, took place six months after the Battle of Badr. Their homes and palm trees were on the outskirts of Medina. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) besieged them until they agreed to exile, and that they would have whatever goods and money the camels carried except for their weapons. God revealed about them: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God until His saying: For the first gathering, you did not think they would come forth. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fought them until he made peace with them on the basis of exile, and he exiled them to Ash-Sham. They were from a tribe that had not been exiled before, and God had decreed that for them, and if it had not been for that, He would have punished them in this world with killing and captivity. As for His saying: For the first gathering, their exile was the first gathering in this world to Ash-Sham. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba’th narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Whoever doubts that the place of assembly will be in Ash-Sham, let him read this verse: ‘It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. ’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them on that day: ‘Go out.’ They said: ‘To where?’ He said: ‘To the place of assembly.’” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had besieged them until he had reached every limit with them, so they gave him whatever he wanted from them. So he made peace with them on the condition that he spare their bloodshed, expel them from their land and homeland, and march to Adhra’at Ash-Sham. He gave every three of them a camel and a water skin. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burned and cut down the palm trees of Banu An-Nadir, which is Al-Buwayrah, and Hassan said about it: A fire is raging in Bouira, it is spreading to the leaders of Bani Luay Then God revealed: “Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by God’s permission, and that He may disgrace the defiantly disobedient.” At-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, saying: The palm tree is the date palm. “And that He may disgrace the defiantly disobedient” means: They brought them down from their fortresses and ordered the palm trees to be cut down, so they felt a pang in their hearts. The Muslims said: We have cut down some and left others, so let us ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, will we receive a reward for what we have cut down, and will we bear a sin for what we have left behind? Then God revealed: Whatever palm trees you cut down [al-Bayhaqi], the verse. There are hadiths on this topic, and the discussion of the peace treaty of Banu Nadir is detailed in the books of biography. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, who said: The wealth of Banu Nadir was among what God bestowed upon His Messenger, and what the Muslims had not fought over with horses or camels. It was exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he would spend from it on his family for a year’s expenses, then he would put what remained in weapons and mounts, equipment for the path of God. God. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: {And you did not urge upon it cavalry or camels}, so he made what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had taken be ruled as he wanted, and at that time there were no cavalry or camels to urge upon. He said: And the urge is to put down the saddles, and it belonged to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and from that came Khaybar, Fadak, and the villages of Uraynah. And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) ordered that Yanbu be dug, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came to it and took possession of it all, so some people said: Why did not God divide it? So God revealed His excuse and said: {And what God bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns} the verse. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: What God bestowed upon His Messenger from Khaybar was half for God and His Messenger, and the other half for the Muslims. What God and His Messenger had of that was Al-Kathiba, Al-Watih, Salalam, and [Wahdhu], and what the Muslims had was Al-Shaq, and Al-Shaq was thirteen shares, and Nata was five shares. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not divide Khaybar among any of the Muslims except for those who witnessed Al-Hudaybiyyah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not permit any of the Muslims who had stayed behind when he left for Al-Hudaybiyyah to witness Khaybar with him except Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram Al-Ansari. Abu Dawud and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had spoils of war in Banu al-Nadir, Khaybar and Fadak. As for Banu al-Nadir, it was reserved for his needs, Fadak was for wayfarers, and Khaybar, he divided it into three parts: he divided two parts among the Muslims, and kept one part for himself and his family’s expenses. Whatever was left over from his family’s expenses, he gave it to the poor emigrants. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Zanjawayh in al-Amwal, Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: There is no Muslim on the face of the earth who does not have a right to this booty, except for those whom your right hands possess. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: “May God curse the tattooers and the tattooed, the pluckers and the filers for the sake of beauty, changing the creation of God. report of that reached a woman from Banu Asad called Umm Ya`qub, so she came to Ibn Mas`ud and said: ‘I have heard that you cursed such and such.’ He said: ‘Why should I not curse those whom the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) cursed, and it is in the Book of God?’ She said: ‘I have read between the covers and I did not find anything like this in it.’ He said: ‘If you had read it, you would have found it. Have you not read: “Whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and whatever he has forbidden you - refrain from.”’ She said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘He has forbidden it.’”
59:8: His saying: 8- For the poor It was said that it is a substitute for those of kin and what is conjoined to it, and it is not correct for it to be a substitute for the Messenger and what follows it lest it entails describing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as poor. It was said that the meaning is so that it is not a state but rather it is for the poor. It was said that the meaning is: be amazed at the poor. It was said that the meaning is: And God is severe in punishment for the poor: meaning severe in punishment for the disbelievers because of the poor. It was said that it is a conjoined to what has passed by estimating the and just as you say the money is for Zaid for Umar and for Bakr. What is meant by the emigrants are those who emigrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, desiring the religion and supporting it. Qatada said: These emigrants are those who left their homes, wealth and families. The meaning of were expelled from their homes is that the infidels of Mecca expelled them from it and forced them to leave. They were one hundred men seeking bounty from God and approval meaning they asked Him to bestow provision upon them in this world and approval in the Hereafter and to support God and His Messenger by jihad against the infidels. This clause is conjoined with seek, and the position of the two clauses is in the accusative case as a state. The first is comparative, and the second is understood: meaning intending that. It is permissible for it to be a comparative state because their leaving in that manner was to support God and His Messenger. The reference in His statement: those is to them in terms of their being described by those characteristics. It is a subject and its predicate is they are the truthful, meaning perfect in truthfulness and firmly rooted in it.
59:9: Then when he finished praising the Muhajireen, he praised the Ansar, saying: 9- And those who had established themselves in the home and in faith before them. What is meant by the home is Medina, which is the home of the migration, and the meaning of their establishing themselves in the home and in faith is that they took it as a place of residence: that is, they were firmly established in it. And establishing themselves in the original is only for a place, but He made faith like it because of their establishment in it, reducing the situation to the status of a place. And it was said that faith is accusative by a verb other than the mentioned verb, and the meaning is: and they believed in faith or they were sincere in faith. This is what Abu Ali al-Farsi said. It is possible that the complement is omitted: that is, they settled in the home and place of faith. It is possible that the meaning of they settled is implied by the meaning of they adhered, and the estimate is: they adhered to the disease and faith. The meaning of before them is: before the migration of the emigrants. Therefore, it is necessary to estimate the complement, because the Ansar only believed after the emigrants believed. The relative pronoun is the subject and its predicate is they love those who emigrated to them, because they treated the emigrants well and shared their wealth and homes with them. and they find no need in their hearts, that is, the Ansar do not find in their hearts any envy, resentment, or bitterness. for what they were given, that is, for what the emigrants were given without them of the spoils. Rather, their souls were content with that. There is an omitted complement in the speech: that is, they do not find in their hearts any need or trace of need. Whatever a person finds in his heart of what he needs is a need. The Muhajireen were living in the homes of the Ansar. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) captured Banu Nadir, he called the Ansar and thanked them for what they had done for the Muhajireen, by hosting them in their homes and sharing their wealth with them. Then he said: If you like, I will divide what God has bestowed upon me from Banu Nadir between you and the Muhajireen. The Muhajireen will remain as they are, living in your homes and sharing your wealth with you. If you like, I will give them that and they will leave your homes. They were satisfied with dividing that among the Muhajireen and were pleased. And they give preference over themselves, even though they are in need. Al-Ittihad is its specificity, and the meaning is: They give preference to the Muhajireen over themselves in worldly goods. Even though they are in need, meaning need and poverty. Khasasah is taken from khisas privilege of a house, which is the space in which it is located. The phrase if they were in need is in the accusative case as a state. It was said that khisasah is taken from ikhtisas, which means to be alone in a matter. So khisasah means to be alone in need. From this is the saying of the poet: If spring is scarce, the sick will live in it and the poor will become rich. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. The majority of scholars read yuqi with a sukoon on the waw and a soft qaf from wiqayah. Ibn Abi Ubla and Abu Haywah read it with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the qaf. The majority of scholars read shah nafsah with a damma on the sheen. Ibn Umar and Ibn Abi Ubla read it with a kasra. Stinginess means miserliness combined with greed, as is stated in As-Sahah. It is also said that stinginess is more severe than miserliness. Muqatil said: Shah nafs means he was greedy. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: Stinginess of the soul is taking what is forbidden and withholding zakat. Ibn Zayd said: Whoever does not take something that God has forbidden and does not withhold what God has commanded him to pay has been protected from the stinginess of his soul. Tawus said: Stinginess is when a person is miserly with what he has, and stinginess is when he is miserly with what is in people's hands, wanting to have what is in their hands through lawful means not being satisfied with what is forbidden. Ibn Uyaynah said: Stinginess is injustice. Al-Layth said: It is abandoning obligatory duties and violating the prohibitions. It is apparent from the verse that success is dependent on not being stingy with regard to any of the things that are considered reprehensible by Islamic law, such as zakat, charity, maintaining family ties, and the like, as is indicated by the addition of stinginess to the self, and the reference in His saying: Those to those in consideration of its meaning, which is the subject and its predicate is they are the successful ones. Success is winning and attaining everything desired.
59:10: Then, when He, the Almighty, finished praising the Muhajireen and Ansar, He mentioned what those who came after them should say, saying: 10- And those who came after them and they are those who followed them in goodness until the Day of Resurrection. It was said that they are those who migrated after Islam had become strong. The apparent meaning of the verse is that it includes those who came after the early Companions who converted to Islam late in the era of the Prophet, and those Muslims who followed them after the era of the Prophet until the Day of Resurrection, because it is true of all of them that they came after the first Muhajireen and Ansar. The relative pronoun is the subject and predicate: They say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith.’ It is permissible for the relative pronoun to be conjoined with His statement: And those who were established in the home and in faith, in which case they say would be in the accusative case as a state, or it would be a new sentence with no position. What is meant by brotherhood here is brotherhood in religion. God commanded them to seek forgiveness for themselves and for those who came before them from the Muhajireen and Ansar. And do not put in our hearts any rancor toward those who have believed, meaning any deception. Hatred and envy. God the Almighty commanded them, after seeking forgiveness for the Muhajireen and Ansar, to ask God the Almighty to remove from their hearts any rancor toward those who believed in general. The Companions are included in this primarily because they are the most honorable of believers, and because the context is about them. Whoever does not seek forgiveness for the Companions in general and does not seek God’s pleasure for them has disobeyed what God has commanded him to do in this verse. If he finds rancor toward them in his heart, then he has been afflicted by a temptation from Satan and has been afflicted with a large share of disobedience to God through enmity toward His friends and the best nation of His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. A door of failure has been opened for him, leading him to the fire of Hell if he does not remedy himself by resorting to God the Almighty and seeking His aid, by removing from his heart the rancor toward the best of generations and the most honorable of this nation. If he goes beyond what he finds of rancor to insulting one of them, then he has followed the reins of Satan and fallen into the wrath and anger of God. This incurable disease only afflicts the one who is afflicted with a teacher from The Rafidah or his companions are among the enemies of the best of this nation who have been manipulated by Satan, who has beautified for them various lies, fabricated stories and made-up myths, and diverted them from the Book of God, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, and from the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) which has been transmitted to us through the narrations of the great Imams in every era. So they have bought misguidance for guidance, and exchanged great loss for abundant profit. The accursed Satan has continued to move them from one station to another and from one rank to another until they became enemies of the Book of God, the Sunnah of His Messenger, the best of His nation, the righteous of His servants and all the believers. They have neglected the obligations of God, abandoned the rituals of the religion, and strove to plot against Islam and its people with all their might, and have thrown every stone and mortar at the religion and its people. God is behind them, encompassing them. Our Lord, You are indeed Kind and Merciful, meaning abundant in compassion and mercy, and eloquent in their praise of those of Your servants who deserve it. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: I advise the Caliph after me regarding the first Muhajirun, that he recognize their rights and preserve their sanctity. And I advise him regarding the Ansar who had settled in the land and faith before them, that he accept their good deeds and overlook their wrongdoers. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God? I was overcome by hardship, so he sent to his wives but did not find anything with them. He said: Is there no man who will host this man tonight? May God have mercy on him. A man from the Ansar said, and in another narration Abu Talha al-Ansari said: I will, O Messenger of God. So he took him to his family and said to his wife: Honor the guest of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and do not withhold anything from him. She said: By God, I have nothing but food for the children. He said: When the children want dinner, put them to sleep and come and extinguish the lamp, and we will fill up our stomachs tonight for the guest of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So I did, and then the guest went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: God was pleased tonight with so-and-so and so-and-so, and He revealed about them: {And they give preference over themselves, even though they were in need.} Al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab on the authority of Ibn 'Umar who said: A man from among the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was given the head of a sheep as a gift. He said: 'My brother so-and-so and his family are in greater need of this than us.' So he sent it to him. He kept sending it from one person to another until it had been passed around to seven households until it returned to the first one. Then the verse, "and give others preference over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation," was revealed about them. Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud that a man said: "I fear that I may be ruined." He said: "What is that?" He said: "I heard God say: 'And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. I am a stingy man who hardly gives anything. Ibn Mas'ud said to him: "That is not stinginess, but rather miserliness, and there is no good in miserliness. The stinginess mentioned by God in the Qur'an is that you unjustly consume your brother's wealth." Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding the verse, saying: “Greed does not mean that a man withholds his wealth, but it is miserliness, and that is evil. Greed is when a man aspires to what does not belong to him.” Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: Whoever pays the zakat on his wealth has protected himself from the greed of his soul. Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya’la, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Nothing has ever wiped out Islam as greed has wiped out. Ahmad, al-Bukhari in al-Adab, Muslim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Beware of oppression, for oppression will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection. Beware of greed, for greed destroyed those who came before you. It led them to shed each other’s blood and make permissible what was forbidden.” Many hadiths have been narrated that condemn greed. Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: People are of three ranks. Two of them have passed and one remains. The best thing for you to be in is to be in this remaining rank. Then he recited: And those who came after them al-Masahif. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: They were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but they reviled them. Then he recited this verse: And those who came after them al-Masahif. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn `Umar that he heard a man addressing some of the Muhajireen, so he recited to him: For the poor Muhajireen al-Masahif, then he said: These are the Muhajireen, are you one of them? He said: No. Then he recited to him: And those who were settled in the home and in faith al-Masahif. Then he said: These are the Ansar, are you one of them? He said: No. Then he recited to him: And those who came after them al-Masahif, then he said: Are you one of these? He said: I hope. He said: Those who reviled these are not one of these.
59:11: When the Almighty finished mentioning the three classes of believers, He mentioned what happened between the hypocrites and the Jews in terms of the contract to astonish the believers at their condition, so He said: 11- Have you not seen those who are hypocrites? The address is to the Messenger of God, or to everyone who is suitable for him, and those who are hypocrites are Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions. The phrase they say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture is a new sentence to explain what is astonished at, and the expression is in the present tense to bring to mind the image or to indicate continuity, and He made them brothers to them because disbelief brought them together, even if the type of their disbelief differed, so they are brothers in disbelief, and the lam in to their brothers is the lam of notification, and it was said that it is from the saying of Banu Nadir to Banu Qurayza, and the first is more appropriate, because Banu Nadir and Banu Qurayza are Jews, and the hypocrites are not them, and the lam in His saying: If you are expelled is the one that introduces the oath: meaning, by God, if you are expelled from Your homes. We will surely go out with you. This is the answer to the oath: that is, we will go out from our homes in your company. And we will not obey concerning you, that is, concerning you and for your sake, anyone who wants to prevent us from going out with you, even if it takes a long time. This is the meaning of His statement: Never. Then when they promised them that they would go out with them, they promised them victory for them, and they said: And if you are fought, we will surely aid you against your enemy. Then He, the Most High, denied them and said: And God bears witness that they are liars, regarding what they promised them of going out with them and giving them victory.
59:12: Then when he summarized their lie in what they promised, he detailed what they lied about, saying: 12- If they are expelled, they will not go out with them, and if they are fought, they will not aid them. And the matter was thus, for the hypocrites did not go out with those who were expelled from the Jews, namely Banu al-Nadir and those with them, and they did not aid those who were fought from the Jews, namely Banu Qurayza and the people of Khaybar. And if they aid them, that is, if it were possible for their aid to exist, because what God has denied cannot exist. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is, if they intended to aid the Jews, they would turn their backs in defeat and then they would not be aided. That is, the Jews would not be aided if their aid was defeated, and they are the hypocrites. It was also said that it means the hypocrites would not be aided after that, rather God would humiliate them and their hypocrisy would not benefit them. It was also said that the meaning of the verse is: They would not aid them willingly, and if they aided them unwillingly, they would turn their backs. It was also said that the meaning of they would not aid them is: They would not continue to aid them. The first is more appropriate, and it is similar to His statement: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden.
59:13: 13- "Indeed, you are more fearful in their hearts than God" meaning, you, O Muslims, are more fearful and dreadful in the hearts of the hypocrites, or the hearts of the Jews, or the hearts of everyone than God: meaning, from the fear of God, and fear here means being terrified, because it is a source of the passive voice, and its accusative is a specification. "That is because they are a people who do not understand" meaning what was mentioned of the described fear due to their lack of understanding of any of the things, and if they had understanding, they would have known that God, the Exalted, is the one who gave you power over them, so He is more deserving of being feared than you.
59:14: Then the Almighty informed us of their further failure and the weakness of their intimidate, saying: 14- "They will not fight you all together meaning the Jews and the hypocrites will not come out together to fight you and they will not be able to do so except within fortified villages with paths and houses or from behind walls" meaning from behind walls behind which they hide due to their cowardice and fear. The majority read "walls in the plural, while Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read jidar" in the singular. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading because it is in agreement with the statement "fortified villages". Some of the Meccans read "jidar with a fatha on the jim and a sukoon on the dal, which is a dialect for wall". "Their violence among themselves is severe" meaning some of them are harsh and rude to others, their hearts are different and their intentions are diverse. Al-Suddi said: What is meant is the difference in their hearts to the point that they do not agree on a single matter. Mujahid said: Their violence among themselves is severe in speech and threats so that they will do such and such. Meaning: When they are alone, they attribute to themselves strength and might, but when they encounter an enemy, they are humiliated, submissive, and defeated. It is said that the meaning is that their might in comparison to their peers is great, but their weakness in comparison to you is due to the terror God has cast into their hearts. The former is more appropriate, because of His statement: You think they are united, but their hearts are diverse, as it indicates that their unity is only in appearance, while their hearts differ inwardly. This difference is the might that is described as strength between them. The meaning of diverse is scattered. Mujahid said: He means the Jews and the hypocrites; you think they are united, but their hearts are diverse. It was also narrated from him that he said: What is meant are the hypocrites. Ath-Thawri said: They are the polytheists and the People of the Book. Qatadah said: You think they are united: meaning united on a matter and an opinion, but their hearts are diverse and scattered. So the people of falsehood have different opinions, different testimonies, and different desires, and they are united in enmity towards the people of truth. Ibn Masoud read: And their hearts are divided meaning they are more divided. That is because they are a people who do not understand. That is, this difference and division is because they are a people who do not understand anything. If they understood, they would have known the truth and followed it.
59:15: 15- Like those before them meaning their example is like those before them. The meaning is that the example of the hypocrites and the Jews is like those before them from the disbelieving polytheists. Nearly means in a near time. The accusative of nearly is a circumstantial word meaning they will resemble them in a near time. It was also said that the agent in it is they tasted meaning they tasted in a near time. The meaning of they tasted the evil consequences of their deed is the bad consequences of their disbelief in this world by being killed on the day of Badr. This was six months before the Battle of Banu Nadir, as stated by Mujahid and others. It was also said that what is meant is Banu Nadir since God had given them power over them, as stated by Qatadah. It was also said that it refers to the killing of Banu Qurayzah, as stated by Ad-Dahhak. It was also said that it is general and applies to everyone whom God takes revenge on because of his disbelief, but the first is more appropriate. And for them is a painful punishment meaning in the Hereafter.
59:16: Then he gave another example of the Jews and the hypocrites, saying: 16- Like the example of Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ That is, their example in their failure to support one another. It is either the predicate of a deleted subject, or another predicate of the implied subject before his saying: Like those before them, assuming the deletion of the conjunction, as you say: You are wise, you are working, you are generous. It was said that the first example is specific to the Jews, and the second is specific to the hypocrites, and it was said that the second example is an explanation of the first example. Then the Almighty explained the similarity, saying: {When He said to man, Disbelieve.} That is, He tempted him to disbelieve, made it attractive to him, and urged him to do it. What is meant by man here is a type of man who obeyed Satan. It was said that he was a worshipper among the Children of Israel whom Satan urged to disbelieve, so he obeyed him. {Then when he disbelieved, he said, Indeed, I am disassociated from you.} That is, when man disbelieved, obeying Satan and accepting his embellishments, Satan said, I am disassociated from you. This will happen to him on the Day of Resurrection. The phrase, {Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds} is an explanation of His disassociation from man after his disbelief. It was said that what is meant by man here is either ignorance or ignorance, but the former is more appropriate. Mujahid said: What is meant by man here is all people in Satan's deception of them. It was said that Satan's saying, I fear God, is not its literal meaning, but rather it is to disassociate himself from man, so it is an emphasis on his saying, Indeed, I am disassociated from you. The majority read it as inni with a sukoon on the yaa. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read it with a fatha on it.
59:17: 17- "So the outcome of them was that they were both in the Fire. The majority of scholars read their outcome in the accusative case as if it were the subject of was," and its noun is that they are in the Fire. Al-Hasan and Amr ibn Ubayd read it in the nominative case as if it were the subject of "was," and the predicate is what follows it, and the meaning was that the outcome of Satan and that person who disbelieved was that they would go to the Fire. "Eternally therein. The majority of scholars read Eternally in the accusative case as a state, and Ibn Mas'ud, Al-A'mash, Zayd ibn Ali, and Ibn Abi Ubla read Eternally therein, as if it were the predicate of that," and the adverbial phrase is related to it. "And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers," meaning eternally in the Fire is the recompense of the wrongdoers, and these are included among them as a primary inclusion.
59:18: Then the Almighty returned to addressing the believers with good admonition, saying: 18- O you who have believed, fear God meaning fear His punishment by doing what He has commanded you to do and leaving what He has forbidden you from. And let a soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow meaning let it look to what it has put forth of deeds for the Day of Resurrection. The Arabs suffice from the future with tomorrow, and it was said that mentioning tomorrow is an indication of the nearness of the Hour. And fear God He repeated the command to fear God for emphasis. Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do nothing is hidden from Him, so He will reward you for your deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil.
59:19: 19- And do not be like those who forgot God meaning they abandoned His command, or did not value Him as He should be valued, or did not fear Him, or all of the above. So He made them forget themselves meaning He made them forget themselves because of their forgetting Him. So they did not occupy themselves with the deeds that would save them from the punishment, and they did not refrain from the sins that would cause them to fall into it. So there is an omitted complement in the speech: meaning He made them forget their own interests. Sufyan said: They forgot the right of God, so He made them forget the right of themselves. It was also said that they forgot God in times of ease, so He made them forget themselves in times of hardship. Those are the wicked meaning those who are complete in disobeying God.
59:20: 20- The companions of the Fire are not equal to the companions of Paradise in merit and rank, and what is meant is both groups in general. Those whom God has forgotten are included in the group of the people of the Fire as a primary entry, and those who were righteous are included in the group of the people of Paradise as a primary entry because the context is about them. We have previously discussed the meaning of such a verse in Surat Al-Ma’idah, Surat As-Sajdah, and Surat Sad. Then God the Almighty informed us about the companions of Paradise after denying their equality with the people of the Fire, saying: The companions of Paradise are the successful ones, meaning the ones who are victorious in everything they seek and saved from every harm. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Have you not seen those who are hypocrites? He said: Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, Rifa’ah bin Tabut, Abdullah bin Nabtal, Aws bin Qayzi, and their brothers Banu Nadir. Ibn Ishaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu Nu’aym in al-Dala’il narrated on his authority that a group of Banu Auf bin al-Harith, including Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, Wadi’ah bin Malik, Suwayd, and Da’is, sent to Banu al-Nadir saying, “Stand firm and resist, for we will not surrender you. If you are fought, we will fight with you, and if you are expelled, we will go out with you.” They waited for that to help them, but they did not. God cast terror into their hearts, so they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to expel them and refrain from shedding their blood, on the condition that they would be entitled to whatever camels could carry except a ring. He did so, and a man among them would demolish his house, place it on the back of a camel, and set off with it. So they went out to Khaybar, and some of them went to Syria. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding his statement, You think they are united, but their hearts are diverse, that he said: They are the polytheists. Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Rahawayh, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Hamid, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that a man was worshipping in a monastery and a woman had brothers. Something happened to her, so they brought her to him and she made things look good to him. He plucked pricks on her and she became pregnant. Then Satan came to him and said, Kill her, for if they defeat you, you will be disgraced. So he killed her and buried her. Then they came and took him and took him away. While they were walking, Satan came to him and said, I am the one who made things look good to you, so prostrate to me a prostration and I will save you. So he prostrated to him. This is what God said, Like Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ [al-Bukhari and Muslim], the verse. I say: This does not indicate that this man is the one meant by the verse, but rather it indicates that he was among those to whom God bestowed charity. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a longer version than this, but it does not contain anything that indicates that this is the intended meaning of the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated it in a similar manner on the authority of Ibn Masoud. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding his statement, like Satan, he said: God gave the example of the disbelievers and hypocrites who were at the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, like Satan when he said to man, Disbelieve.
59:21: When He, the Almighty, finished mentioning the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, and showed that they are not equal in any of the matters, He mentioned the greatness of His noble Book, and informed of its majesty, and that it is worthy of hearts being humbled by it and souls being softened by it, so He said: 21- If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God. That is, because of its status, greatness, the quality of its words, the strength of its structures, its eloquence, and its inclusion of sermons that soften hearts, if it had been sent down upon a mountain of the mountains on earth, you would have seen it, despite it being extremely hard, extremely solid, and massive, humbled and coming apart: that is, coming apart from fear of God, the Almighty, out of caution against His punishment and fear that it would not fulfill what is required of it in glorifying the words of God. This is a representation and imagination that necessitates the high status of the Qur’an and the strength of its effect on hearts, and this is indicated by His statement: And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will… They reflect on what they should reflect on so that you may be admonished by admonitions and deterred by warnings. It contains a rebuke and rebuke to the disbelievers because they did not humble themselves before the Qur’an, nor take heed of its admonitions, nor take heed of its warnings. The humble is the submissive and humble. It was said that the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: That is, if We had sent down this Qur’an, O Muhammad, upon a mountain, it would not have remained stable and would have cracked from its descent upon it. We have sent it down to you and made you firm and strengthened for it. So, on this basis, it is from the aspect of gratitude to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because God Almighty made him firm when the firmly established mountains cannot remain firm.
59:22: Then He, the Most High, informed us of His Lordship and Greatness, saying: 22- He is God, other than whom there is no god. This is a confirmation of monotheism and a rejection of polytheism. The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, meaning the Knower of what is absent of perception and what is present. It was also said that He is the Knower of the secret and the open. It was also said that He is the Knower of what was and what will be. It was also said that He is the Hereafter and this world. He presented the unseen before the witnessed because it precedes in existence. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The explanation of these two names has already been presented.
59:23: 23- He is God, other than whom there is no god He repeated it to emphasize and confirm that monotheism is truly that the Holy King meaning pure from every defect and free from every imperfection. In the dialect of the people of Hijaz, al-Quds with a fatha on the letter qaf means a bucket, because one purifies oneself with it. From this comes the word qadus for one of the vessels used to extract water. The majority read al-Quddus with a damma on the qaf. Abu Dharr and Abu al-Sammak read it with a fatha, and Sibawayh used to say Subuh Quddus with a fatha on the first letter. Abu Hatim narrated on the authority of Ya'qub that he heard an eloquent Bedouin reading al-Quddus with a fatha on the qaf. Tha’lab said: Every noun on the pattern of fa’ul has a fatha at the beginning except al-Sabbuh and al-Quddus, as the damma is more common in them. They may also have a fatha. As-Salam means the one who is safe from every deficiency and defect. It was said that the Muslim is upon his servants in Paradise, as he said: “Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord.” It was also said that he is the one who is safe from his injustice, and this is what most people said. It was also said that he is the one who is safe for his servants, and it is a source of description for emphasis. Al-Mu’min means the one who has granted his servants security from his punishment. It was also said that he is the one who believes in his messengers to show miracles. It was also said that he is the one who believes in the believers with what he promised them of reward, and the one who believes in the disbelievers with what he promised them of punishment. It is said that he granted him security from security, and it is the opposite of fear. From this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: The faithful birds are touched by the riders of Mecca between Ghayl and Sind. Mujahid said: The believer is the one who found himself by saying: God bears witness that there is no god but He. The majority read al-mu’min with a kasra on the meem, an active participle from aman meaning to feel secure. Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn read it with a fatha, meaning to believe in Him, with the deletion like his saying: And Moses chose his people. Abu Hatim said: This reading is not permissible because its meaning is that he was afraid, but someone else reassured him. al-Muhaymin means the witness over his servants by their deeds, the watcher over them. This is what Mujahid, Qatadah, and Muqatil said: It is said hayman he dominates, he dominates, so he is muhaymin he dominates, if he is a watcher over something. Al-Wahidi said: “Many of the commentators have said that its root is ‘mu’amin’ from ‘aman ya’min,’ so it has the meaning of ‘believer’, and the first is more appropriate. We have already discussed Al-Muhaymin in Surat al-Ma’idah 5:“The Mighty” who has no equal. It was also said: The Conqueror, and it was also said: The Victorious, the Unconquered. It was also said: The Strong “The Compeller” means the might of God and His greatness. The Arabs call a king Al-Jabbar. It may be from jabar if he enriches the poor, and its root is kasir. It may also be from jabaru ala kada if he compelled him to do what he wanted. So, He is the One who compelled His creation to do what He wanted from them. Al-Suddi and Muqatil said the same, and Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra’ chose it. He said: It is from ajbaruhu ala amar meaning he subdued him. He said: I did not hear a fa’al from “af’al except in jabar from ajbara and diraka from idraka. It was also said: The Compeller whose power is unbearable is Al-Mutakabbir meaning the One who is too proud to do any deficiency and is too haughty to do anything that is not befitting of Him. The root of arrogance is abstention and non-submission. From this is the saying of Humayd ibn Thawr: She forgave as a young camel forgives, so she became proud of the tough, yet she was submissive. Arrogance in the attributes of God is praiseworthy, and in the attributes of created beings it is blameworthy. Qatada said: He is the One who is too proud to bear any evil. Ibn al-Anbari said: The arrogant is the One with pride, and He is the King. Then God, the Exalted, absolved Himself from the polytheism of the polytheists, saying: Glory be to God from what they associate with Him, meaning from what they associate with Him or from their associating partners with Him.
59:24: 24- He is God, the Creator meaning the One who determines things according to His will and desire the Maker meaning the Originator and Inventor of things and brings them into existence. And it was said that He is the One who distinguishes some from others the Fashioner meaning the One who brings into existence the images composed of them in different forms. So fashioning is dependent on creation and fashioning and follows them, and the meaning of fashioning is planning and shaping. Al-Nabigha said: The Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner, creates water in the wombs until it becomes blood. Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah, the companion of the artist, read it with a fat-ha on the waw and a nasb on the ra’, as a direct object of al-Bari’, meaning the one who created the artist, meaning he distinguished him. To Him belong the best names. This has already been explained and discussed in the interpretation of his statement: To God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. “Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him,” meaning everything in them speaks of His sanctity with the tongue of action or speech. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, meaning He is the Victorious over the One Who is not defeated by anyone, the Wise in all matters that He decrees. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, {If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain}, he said: He means, if I had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain and I carried it, it would have split and humbled itself from its weight and from fear of God. So God commanded the people when the Qur’an was sent down to them to take it with intense fear and humility. He said: Thus God sets forth examples for the people that perhaps they will reflect. Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud and Ali, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, regarding the statement of God, {If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain} to the end of the surah, he said: It is a cure for headaches. Al-Daylami narrated it with two chains of transmission, but we do not know the status of their men. Al-Khatib narrated in his history with his chain of transmission on the authority of Idris bin Abdul Karim Al-Haddad, who said: I recited to Khalaf, and when I reached this verse, he said: Place your hand on your head, for I recited to Hamza, and when I reached this verse, he said: Place your hand on your head, for I recited to Al-A’mash. Then he narrated the chain of transmission in a continuous manner in this way to Ibn Mas’ud, who said: I recited to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and when I reached this verse, he said to me: Place my hand on your head, for when Gabriel revealed it, he said to me: Place your hand on your head, for it is a cure for every disease except death, and death is death. Al-Dhahabi said: It is false. Ibn As-Sunni narrated it in his ‘Amal Yawm Wa Layla’ and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded a man, when he went to bed, to recite the end of Surat Al-Hashr and said: If you die, you will die a martyr. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Whoever seeks refuge in God from Satan three times, then recites the last verses of Surat al-Hashr, God will send seventy angels to drive away the devils of mankind and jinn from him, whether at night or during the day, until the evening.” Ahmad, al-Darami, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Tabarani, Ibn al-Durais, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ma’qil ibn Yasar that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Whoever says three times in the morning, ‘I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the accursed,’ then recites the three verses from the end of Surat al-Hashr, God will assign seventy thousand angels to pray for him until the evening. If he dies that day, he will die a martyr. Whoever says it in the evening will have the same status.” Al-Tirmidhi said after transmitting it: It is strange; we do not know it except from this source. Ibn Adi, Ibn Mardawayh, Al-Khatib, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites the last verses of Surat Al-Hashr during the night or day and dies that day or night, God will make Paradise obligatory for him. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, he said: The secret and the public. Regarding the statement, The believer, he said: The believer is created from being wronged. Regarding the statement, The Guardian, he said: The Witness.
60:1: It is thirteen verses It is Madani. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion. Ibn Al-Durais, Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Mumtahanah was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr. Al-Mumtahanah, with a kasra on the ha, is an active participle to which the verb is metaphorically attributed, just as Surat Bara’ah was named Al-Fadihah because it revealed the faults of the hypocrites. It was also said that Al-Mumtahanah, with a fatha on the ha, is a passive participle attributed to the woman about whom it was revealed, and she is Umm Kulthum bint Uqba ibn Abi Mu’ayt, because God the Almighty said: “So test them. God knows best about their faith.” The commentators said: The verse: 1- O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies was revealed about Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah when he wrote to the polytheists of Quraysh about the Prophet’s march to them. The story will be mentioned at the end of the research, God willing. His saying: My enemy is the first object, and your enemy is conjoined to it, and the second object is allies. God Almighty added the enemy to Himself to magnify their crime. The enemy is a verbal noun that refers to one, two, or a group. The verse indicates the prohibition of befriending the infidels in any way. You extend to them affection means you extend affection to them, although the ba is redundant or causal. The meaning is: You extend to them report of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, because of the affection between you and them. Al-Zajjaj said: “You convey to them the report of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his secret through the love that is between you and them.” The sentence is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun you take. It may be a new sentence to inform about what it includes or to explain their allegiance to them. It may be in the accusative case as a description of friends. The sentence and they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of you receive, or of the subject of do not take. It may be a new sentence to explain the state of the disbelievers. The majority read with what has come to you with a unified ba. Al-Jahdary and Asim, in a narration from him, read when it came to you with the letter lam: meaning, because of what came to you of the truth, deleting the object of disbelief: meaning, they disbelieved in God and the Messenger because of what came to you of the truth, or making what is a cause of belief a cause of disbelief as a rebuke to them. They expel the Messenger and you is a new sentence to explain their disbelief, or in the accusative case as a state. His saying: That you believe in God, your Lord is an explanation of the expulsion: meaning, they expel you because of your belief, or out of dislike for you to believe. If you have come out in jihad in My cause and seeking My pleasure is the answer to the condition, omitted, meaning, if you are like that, then do not extend your affection to them, or if you are like that, then do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies. The accusative of jihad and seeking is based on the reason: meaning, if you have come out for the sake of jihad in My cause and for the sake of seeking My pleasure. The sentence You secretly convey to them affection is a new sentence for rebuke and rebuke: meaning, you convey to them the report because of affection. It was said that it is a substitute for His statement: You receive: Then He, the Most High, informed that nothing of their conditions is hidden from Him, so He said: And I know what you conceal and what you declare. The clause is in the accusative case as a state: that is, what you concealed and what you declared. The ba in by is redundant: it is said, I knew such-and-such and I knew of such-and-such. This is on the basis that I know is a present tense verb. It was also said that it is a comparative adjective: that is, I know better than anyone what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever does that among you has certainly strayed from the right path. That is, whoever does that, taking My enemy and your enemy as allies and expressing love towards them, has strayed from the path of truth and righteousness and has strayed from the intended path.
60:2: 2- If they encounter you, they will be your enemies. That is, if they meet you and encounter you, they will show you the enmity in their hearts. This is derived from the term muthaqafah, which means seeking to catch the offender in a race. It was also said that the meaning is: if they get the better of you and are able to dominate you, and the two meanings are close. And they stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil. That is, they stretch out their hands and tongues against you with beating and the like, and their tongues with cursing and the like. And they wish that you would disbelieve. This is connected to the answer to the condition, or to the sentence of the condition and the consequence. Abu Hayyan preferred this. The meaning is that they wished for their apostasy and wished that they would return to disbelief.
60:3: 3- Never will your kinship ties or your children benefit you meaning, neither kinship ties in general nor children will benefit you. They were specifically mentioned even though they are included in the kinship ties to increase love and compassion for them. The meaning is that these people will not benefit you unless you befriend the disbelievers for their sake, as happened in the story of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. Rather, what will benefit you is what God has commanded you to do, which is to be hostile to the disbelievers and abandon their friendship. The phrase On the Day of Resurrection He will judge between you is a new sentence to clarify the lack of benefit of kinship ties and children on that Day. The meaning of He will judge between you is that He will separate you, so the people who obey Him will enter Paradise, and the people who disobey Him will enter Hell. It was said that what is meant by the judgement between them is that each one of them will flee from the other due to the intensity of the terror, as in His statement, The Day a man will flee from his brother (al-Baqarah 2:17). It was said that it is permissible for the Day of Resurrection to be connected to what preceded it, meaning, neither your kinship ties nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection, so it is stopped at. It begins with the statement: He will judge between you. It is preferable to relate it to what comes after it, as we mentioned. And God is Seeing of what you do. Nothing of your words and deeds is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for that. The majority read yufasil with a damma on the ya', a soft fa', and a fatha on the sad, in the passive voice. Abu Ubaid chose this reading. Asim read it with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the sad, in the active voice. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma on the ya', a fatha on the fa', and a doubled kasra on the sad. Alqamah read it with a noon. Qatadah and Abu Haywah read it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the sad, lightened. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me, Az-Zubayr, and Al-Miqdad. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman there with a letter. Take it from her and bring it to me.’ So we went out until we reached the garden, and there we saw the woman. We said: ‘Bring out the letter.’ She said: ‘I have no letter with me.’ We said: ‘Bring out the letter or throw away your clothes.’ So she took it out of her tie, and we brought it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It said: ‘From Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah to some of the polytheists in Mecca, informing them of some of the affairs of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘What is this, Hatib?’ He said: ‘Do not rush me, O Messenger of God. I was a man attached to the Quraysh, but I was not one of them. Those of the Muhajireen who were with you had relatives with whom they protected their families and property in Mecca. So, since I missed that in terms of kinship with them, I wanted to do them a favor with which they could protect them.’” My kinship, and I did not do that out of disbelief or apostasy from my religion. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: He is truthful. Umar said: Let me strike off his head. He said: He was present at Badr. How do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you. And the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection. There are hadiths with chains of transmission and with mursal on this topic that include an explanation of this story, and that these verses up to His saying: There has certainly been for you a good example in Abraham were revealed regarding that.
60:4: When God finished forbidding friendship with polytheists and blaming whoever did that, He set for them an example of Abraham when he disowned his people, saying: 4- "There has already been for you an excellent pattern" meaning a praiseworthy trait for you to follow: It is said to me that he is an example in this matter: meaning an imitation. So God guided them to follow his example in that except for his seeking forgiveness for his father. The majority read "aswah" with a kasrah on the hamza, while Asim read it with a damma, and they are two dialects. The root of aswah with a damma and a kasrah is qudwah. It is said that he is your example: meaning like you and you are like him. His statement about Abraham and those with him is related to an example, or to a good deed, or it is an attribute of an example, or a state of the hidden pronoun in good deed, or the predicate of "kan, and lakum" is for clarification, and those with him are his believing companions. Ibn Zayd said: They are the prophets. Al-Farra’ said: He says: Why don’t you, Hatib, take Abraham as an example and disown your family as Abraham disowned his father and his people? The circumstance in His statement: When they said to their people is the predicate of kana or is related to it: that is, the time when they said to their disbelieving al-Nas 114:Indeed, we are innocent of you. The plural of bari’ is bari’, like sharika and sharika, and dharifa’ and dharif. The majority read bara’ with a damma on the ba’, a fatha on the ra’, and an alif between two hamzas, like karmaa’ in kareem. Isa ibn ‘Umar and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a kasra on the ba’ and one hamza after an alif, like karmaa’ in the plural of kareem. Abu Ja’far read it with a damma on the ba’ and a hamza after an alif. And of what you worship besides God, which are idols, we have disbelieved in you, meaning in what you believed in of idols, or in your religion, or in your actions, and there has appeared between us and you, enmity and hatred forever, meaning this is our way with you as long as you are in your disbelief, until you believe in God alone, and abandon what you are upon of polytheism. If you do that, that enmity will turn into friendship and hatred into love. Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, ‘I will surely ask forgiveness for you,’ is a connected exception from His saying about Abraham, by estimating an added word that was deleted to make the exception valid: meaning, you have had a good example in the words of Abraham except for his saying to his father, or from a good example, and that is correct because the saying is part of the example, as if it was said: There was a good example in Abraham in all of his sayings and actions except for his saying to his father, or from the disavowal and severance that was mentioned: meaning, he did not support him except for his saying. This was mentioned by Ibn Atiyyah, or it is disconnected: meaning, but Abraham’s saying to his father, ‘I will surely ask forgiveness for you,’ so do not…” Or that he only did that because he thought that he had become Muslim. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him. The explanation of this has already been presented in Surat At-Tawbah. And I have not for you anything against God. This is from the complete group of people who are excepted: meaning, I cannot avail you, nor can I avert anything from you of the punishment of God. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of I will surely ask forgiveness. So the exception is directed to the seeking of forgiveness, not to this restriction, as it is a manifestation of helplessness and entrusting the matter to God, and that is from the characteristics of goodness. Our Lord, in You we have put our trust, and to You we turn, and to You is the final destination. This is from the supplication of Abraham and his companions, and it contains a good example to be followed. It has been said that it is a teaching for the believers to say this statement, and trust is entrusting matters to God, and turning means returning, and the final destination is the reference. The preposition and its object are estimated to limit trust, turning, and final destination to God.
60:5: 5- Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve. Al-Zajjaj said: Do not make them prevail over us, lest they think that they are right and be tempted by that. Mujahid said: Do not punish us by their hands or by a punishment from You, lest they say, If these people had been right, this would not have happened to them. “And forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might,” meaning the Victorious One who cannot be defeated. The Wise, the Possessor of perfect wisdom.
60:6: 6- There has certainly been for you in them an excellent pattern. That is, there has certainly been for you in Abraham and those with him an excellent example. This was repeated for emphasis and emphasis. It was said that this was revealed some time after the first verse. For whoever hopes in God and the Last Day. This was instead of saying for you instead of some for all. The meaning is that this example is only for whoever fears God and fears the punishment of the Hereafter, or hopes for good from God in this world and the Hereafter. And whoever turns away - then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy. This means that he turns away from that, for God is the Free of need of His creation and is Praiseworthy towards His friends.
60:7: 7- Perhaps God will establish affection between you and those among you with whom you are at enmity by them becoming Muslim and becoming of the people of your religion. Some of them did become Muslim after the conquest of Mecca, and their Islam was good, and affection arose between them and those who preceded them in Islam, and they fought and did deeds that bring them closer to God. It was said that what is meant by affection here is the marriage of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Umm Habibah bint Abu Sufyan. There is no basis for this specification, even though it was among the things that became a cause for affection. Abu Sufyan later abandoned his enmity towards the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but affection did not come about except through his conversion to Islam on the day of the conquest and after it. And God is All-Powerful meaning His power is abundant and great. And God is Forgiving and Merciful meaning His power is abundant and great.
60:8: Then, when He, the Almighty, mentioned what is appropriate for the believers in terms of antagonizing the disbelievers and abandoning friendship with them, He distinguished between those among them whom it is permissible to be kind to and those whom it is not, saying: 8- God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes meaning He does not forbid you from these people from being kind to them this is a substitute for the relative pronoun, a substitute of inclusion. And similarly His statement: and be just to them it is said I was just to a man if you treat him justly. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is and be just between you and them in fulfilling the covenant for God loves those who are just meaning the just. The meaning of the verse is that God, the Almighty, does not forbid being kind to the people of the covenant from the disbelievers who made a covenant with the believers to refrain from fighting and not to support the disbelievers against them. Nor does He forbid treating them justly. Ibn Zayd said: This was in the beginning of Islam when the truce was made and the command to use force was abandoned, then it was abrogated. Qatada said: It was abrogated by Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. It was also said that this ruling was established in the peace treaty between the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Quraysh, but when the peace treaty was ended with the conquest of Mecca, the ruling was abrogated. It was also said that it applies specifically to the allies of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and those between whom he had a covenant. This was said by Al-Hasan. Al-Kalbi said: They are Khuza’ah and Banu Al-Harith ibn Abd Manaf. Mujahid said: It applies specifically to those who believed but did not emigrate. It was also said that it applies specifically to women and children. Al-Qurtubi narrated from most of the commentators that it is decisive.
60:9: Then the Almighty explained who it is not permissible to be kind to him or to treat him justly, saying: 9- God only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes and they are the leaders of disbelief from Quraysh and aided in your expulsion meaning they aided those who fought you in that, and they are all the people of Mecca and those who entered into their covenant with them, and His saying: that you take them as allies is a substitute for inclusion from the relative pronoun as mentioned previously, and whoever takes them as allies - then those are the wrongdoers meaning those who are complete in wrongdoing because they took as allies someone who deserved enmity because he was an enemy of God, His Messenger, and His Book, and they made them their allies. Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Except for the saying of Abraham to his father. He said: They were forbidden to take as an example Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father, and his saying, Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, “Do not punish us by their hands or with a punishment from You,” so they would say, If these people had been on the truth, this would not have happened to them. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on his authority, Indeed, in them you have a good example to follow, he said: In all of Abraham’s actions except his seeking forgiveness for his father, who was a polytheist. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding his saying, Do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, he said: Do not give them power over us so that they would tempt us. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The first to fight the apostates for the sake of establishing the religion of God was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and this verse was revealed about him: Perhaps God will establish between you and those among them with whom you have been hostile, affection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) appointed Abu Sufyan ibn Harb over some of Yemen. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) died, Dhu al-Khimar came as an apostate. He was the first to fight in the apostasy and struggle for the religion. He said: He is among those about whom God said: Perhaps God will establish between you and those among you with whom you have been at enmity, affection. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Adi ibn Mardawayh, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: The affection that was established between them was the marriage of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, so she became the Mother of the Believers, and Muawiyah became the maternal uncle of the believers. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “Abu Sufyan said: ‘O Messenger of God, give me three things.’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Will you command me to fight the infidels as I used to fight the Muslims?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘And Muawiyah, make him your scribe?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘And I have with me the most handsome and beautiful of the Arabs, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, I will marry her to you.’” Al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Al-Bazzar, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, An-Nahhas in his Naskh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr, who said: Qutaylah bint Abd Al-Uzza came to her daughter Asma’ bint Abi Bakr with gifts of: dried yogurt, ghee, and butter, while she was a polytheist. Asma’ refused to accept her gift or let her into her house until she sent word to Aisha, ‘Ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about this.’ She asked him. Then God revealed: God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion 1:17, and He ordered her to accept her gift and bring it into her house. Ibn Abi Hatim added to the period of time that existed between the Quraysh and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). In Bukhari and others, on the authority of Asma bint Abi Bakr, she said: “My mother came to me, desiring to be with her, while she was a polytheist during the time of the Quraysh when they made a treaty with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Should I maintain ties with her? Then God revealed: “God does not forbid you” 1:17, and he said: Yes, maintain ties with your mother.”
60:10: When God Almighty mentioned the ruling on the two groups of disbelievers regarding the permissibility of kindness and fairness to the first group but not to the second group, He mentioned the ruling on the one who shows faith, saying: 10- O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants from among the disbelievers. This is because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with the Quraysh on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah on the condition that he would return to them the Muslims who had come to them, but when the women emigrated to him, God refused to return them to the polytheists, and He ordered that they be tested, saying: Then test them, meaning put them to the test. There is a difference of opinion about what they were tested with. It was said that they would swear by God that they did not leave out of hatred for their husbands, nor out of desire for a new land, nor out of worldly gain, but out of love for God and His Messenger and desire for His religion. If she swore thus, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would give her husband her dowry and what he spent on her, and would not return it to him. It was also said that the test was for her to testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. It was also said that the test was only for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to recite to them the verse, which is: O Prophet, when believing women come to you to the end of it. Scholars differed over whether women were included in the truce or not. There are two opinions. According to the opinion that women were included, this verse is specific to that covenant, and this is what the majority said. According to the opinion that it was not, there is no abrogation or specification. God knows best about their faith. This sentence is an interjection to clarify that the reality of their situation is only known to God, the Most High. He did not command you to do that, but rather commanded you to test them until what indicates the truth of their claim to desire Islam becomes clear to you. Then if you ascertain that they are believers, that is, if you ascertain that based on the outward appearance after the test that you commanded him to do, then do not return them to the disbelievers, that is, to their disbelieving husbands. The sentence They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them is an explanation for the prohibition against returning them. And in it is evidence that a believing woman is not permissible for a non-Muslim, and that a woman’s conversion to Islam necessitates her separation from her husband, not merely her emigrating. The repetition is to emphasize the sanctity, or the first to show the annulment of the marriage, and the second to prevent a new marriage. And give them what they spent meaning, give the husbands of those who emigrated and converted to Islam the same as what they spent on them in dowries. Al-Shafi’i said: If someone other than the husband among her relatives demands it, he is prevented from it without compensation. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them because they have become people of your religion. When you have given them their due compensation meaning their dowries, and that is after the expiration of their waiting period, as is indicated by the evidence for the obligation of the waiting period. And do not hold on to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women. The majority of scholars read Tasmakwa with a light Imsak absak pronunciation of Imsak. Abu Ubaid chose this reading, based on the statement, Then keep them in acceptable terms. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Abu Amr read it with a heavy Tamasmak pronunciation of Ismah, which is what one holds on to. What is meant here is the marriage bond of a contract. The meaning is that whoever has a disbelieving wife, she is not his wife because her marriage bond is severed due to a difference in religion. Al-Nakha'i said: She is a Muslim woman who goes to the land of war and becomes a disbeliever. Disbelievers used to marry Muslims, and Muslims used to marry polytheistic women, but this was abrogated by this verse. This is specific to disbelieving polytheistic women and not disbelieving People of the Book. It was said that it is general and applies to all disbelieving women, except for the exclusion of the People of the Book. The majority of scholars are of the view that if a pagan or People of the Book converts to Islam, they should not be separated until their waiting period has expired. Some scholars said: They are separated merely by the husband’s conversion to Islam. This only applies if the woman has been consummated with. However, if she has not been consummated with, there is no disagreement among scholars that the bond between them is severed by Islam, as she does not have to observe the waiting period. And ask for what you have spent means ask for the dowries of your wives who have gone on to marry the infidels.
