And let them ask for what they have spent means the commentators said: If a Muslim woman who had apostatized went to the infidels among the people of the covenant had her dowry, it would be said to the infidels: Bring her dowry. And it would be said to the Muslims: If a woman from the infidels came to the Muslims and converted to Islam, they would return her dowry to her infidel husband. That is the judgment of God means that what was mentioned about returning the dowries from both sides is the judgment of God. His statement: He will judge between you is in the accusative case as a state, or it is a new sentence. And God is Knowing and Wise means He is eloquent in knowledge; nothing is hidden from Him. He is eloquent in wisdom in His words and actions.
60:11: Al-Qurtubi said: This was specific to that time and to that particular calamity by the consensus of the Muslims. And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers When the previous verse was revealed, the Muslims said: We are satisfied with God’s judgment, and they wrote to the polytheists, but they refused. Then the following verse was revealed: And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers from what you had paid to them of the dowries of the Muslim women. It was said that the meaning is: And if one of your women escapes from you to the disbelievers, such that a Muslim woman apostatizes, and you punish Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: So you punished and gained spoils. Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is: And the final outcome was yours: meaning the spoils were yours until you gained spoils. Then give those whose wives have passed away the equivalent of what they spent of the dowry of the emigrant woman whom they married, and give it to the disbelievers, but do not give it to her disbelieving husband. Qatada and Mujahid said: They were only commanded to give those whose wives had died an equivalent to what they had spent from the spoils of war. This verse was abrogated and its ruling was discontinued after the conquest. The gist of it is that of your wives may be related to your loss, i.e., from your wives, and what is meant by something is the dowry that the husband paid. It may also be related to something omitted as a description of something. Then, it is possible for something to mean the dowry, but in this case, there must be an omitted complement: i.e., from the dowry of your wives, so that the described and its description are consistent. It may be meant by something to refer to women: There is a type and category of them, and this is apparent from His statement: of your wives and His statement: then give to those whose wives have gone meaning: that they give to the one whose wife went to the polytheists and disbelieved and the polytheists did not return her dowry as God had ruled, like the dowry that he spent on her from the spoils. And fear God in whom you are believers meaning beware of exposing yourselves to something that would necessitate punishment upon you, because the faith that you are characterized by necessitates that of its owner.
60:12: 12- O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you meaning intending to pledge allegiance to you on Islam, that they will not associate anything with God of any kind, this was on the day of the conquest of Mecca, as the women of Mecca came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pledge allegiance to him, so God commanded him to take from them that they would not associate anything with God nor steal nor commit adultery nor kill their children which is what the pre-Islamic era used to do when they buried their daughters alive nor bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and feet meaning that they would not attribute to their husbands a child who was not theirs. Al-Farra' said: The woman would pick up the newborn and say to her husband: This is my child from you. That is the slander fabricated between their hands and feet, because when the mother gives birth to the child, he falls between her hands and feet. The meaning here is not that she attributes her child from adultery to her husband, because that is included in the prohibition of adultery. And let them not disobey you in what is right meaning in every matter that is obedience to God. Ata' said: In every righteousness and piety. Al-Muqatilani said: What is meant by what is right is the prohibition of wailing, tearing clothes, cutting hair, tearing garments, scratching faces, and praying for woe. Qatadah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib, and Zayd ibn Aslam said the same. The meaning of the Qur'an or hear from what they said. It was said that the reason for restricting it to what is good, even though the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only commanded it, is to point out that it is not permissible to obey a created being in disobeying the Creator. Then take their pledge of allegiance. This is the answer to if. The meaning is: If they take your pledge of allegiance to you on these matters, then take their pledge of allegiance. Prayer, zakat, fasting, and Hajj were not mentioned in their pledge of allegiance because it is clear that these matters and the like are among the pillars of religion and the rituals of Islam. Rather, the matters mentioned were specified because of the frequency with which they occur among women. And ask God for forgiveness for them. That is, ask God to forgive them after this pledge of allegiance from you to them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. That is, He is eloquent in forgiveness and mercy for His servants.
60:13: 13- O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry. They are all sects of disbelief, and it was said that they are the Jews in particular, and it was said that they are the hypocrites in particular. Al-Hasan said: The Jews and Christians. The first is more appropriate, because all sects of disbelief are characterized by God being angry with them. They have despaired of the Hereafter. “They have despaired of the Hereafter.” Min is the beginning of the goal: meaning that they do not have any certainty in the Hereafter because of their disbelief. Just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves. That is, just as they have despaired of the resurrection of their dead because of their belief in the lack of resurrection. It was said that they have despaired of the Hereafter among the disbelievers who died, because they have witnessed the truth and known that they have no share in the Hereafter. So, Min is introductory according to the first aspect, and explanatory according to the second, and the first is more appropriate. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Miswar bin Makhramah and Marwan bin Al-Hakam that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a treaty with the infidels of Quraysh on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah, Muslim women came to him, so God revealed: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants until he reached and do not hold on to the bonds of disbelieving women, so Omar divorced on that day two of his wives who had been polytheists. He also narrated from their hadith, with a longer version than this, in which it says that Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt was among those who went out to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and she was a widow. Her family came asking the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to return her to them until God revealed what He revealed about the believing women. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: Then test them, he said: Their test was that they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger. If they knew that this was true from them, they would not return to the disbelievers. Her husband, among the disbelievers with whom the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had made a contract, gave her the dowry that he had given her, and they were lawful for the believers if they gave them their dues. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, he said: Surah Al-Mumtahanah was revealed after that peace treaty, and some of their women converted to Islam. I was asked: What made you come out? If she left fleeing from her husband or not wanting him, she is to be returned. If she left hoping to become a Muslim, she is to be kept and her husband is to be returned what he spent. Ibn Abi Usamah, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani in Al-Kabir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a good chain of transmission, as Al-Suyuti said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, When believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them, he said: When a woman came to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Umar ibn Al-Khattab would make her swear by God that she had not left desiring one land for another, and by God that she had not left out of hatred for her husband, and by God that she had not left seeking worldly gain, and by God that she had not left except out of love for God and His Messenger. Ibn Mani’ narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab embraced Islam and his wife remained among the polytheists, so God revealed: And do not hold on to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would test the believing women who migrated to him with this verse: O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you until His saying: Forgiving, Most Merciful. So whoever of the believing women accepted this condition, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would say to her: I have pledged allegiance to you verbally. By God, his hand never touched the hand of any of the women who had pledged allegiance. He did not pledge allegiance to them except by saying: I have pledged allegiance to you on that. It was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa`id, Ahmad, `Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Umaimah bint Ruqayqah who said: “I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with some women to pledge allegiance to him. He took from us what is in the Qur’an that we would not associate anything with God until he reached ‘nor disobey you in what is right’. He said: ‘To the best of your ability and capacity.’ We said: God and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves, O Messenger of God. Will you not shake hands with us?’ He said: ‘I do not shake hands with women. My words to a hundred women are like my words to one woman.’” There are hadiths on this topic. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn as-Samit who said: We were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: Give me your pledge that you will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery. Then he recited the verse of An-Nisa’ The Women. “Whoever fulfills it, his reward is with God. And whoever commits any of that and is punished in this world, it will be an expiation for him. And whoever commits any of that and God conceals it, it is up to God. If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him.” Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, nor shall they bring forth a slander they have invented, that he said: A free woman would give birth to a slave girl and she would replace her with a boy. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding the verse, “They shall not attribute to their husbands anyone other than their own children. And they shall not disobey you in what is right.” He said: This is a condition that God has stipulated for women. Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah al-Ansariyyah, who said: "A woman among the women said: 'What is this kindness in which we should not disobey you?' He said: 'Do not wail.' I said: 'O Messenger of God, the sons of so-and-so have made me happy on behalf of my uncle, and I must repay them.' But he refused, so I repeated this request several times, and he gave me permission to repay them. I have not yet wailed, and none of the women remained who did not wail except me.'" Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Umm 'Atiyyah, who said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and he recited to us that we should not associate anything with God, and he forbade us from wailing. One of our women withdrew her hand and said: 'O Messenger of God, so-and-so has made me happy, and I want to repay her.' But he did not say anything to her. So she went away and then came back and said: 'No woman among us has fulfilled her obligation except Umm Sulaym, Umm al-'Ala', and the daughter of Abu Sabra, the wife of Mu'adh, or the daughter of Abu Sabra and the wife of Muadh. Many hadiths have been narrated prohibiting wailing. Abu Ishaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Abdullah bin Amr and Zaid bin Al-Harith were fond of a Jewish man, so God revealed: O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding His statement: They have despaired of the Hereafter, that they neither believe in it nor hope for it, just as a disbeliever despairs when he dies and sees his reward and learns about it. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that they are the disbelievers in graves who have despaired of the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse that he said: Whoever dies from among those who disbelieve, then the living among those who disbelieved have despaired that they will return to them or that God will resurrect them.
61:1: It is fourteen verses It is Madani. Al-Mawardi said: According to the group’s statement. Ibn Al-Durais, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Saff was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr. An-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Saff was revealed in Makkah, but perhaps this is not authentic from him. What supports it being Madani is what Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam who said: We were discussing which of you should go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and ask him which deeds are most beloved to God? None of us got up, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent a man to us and gathered us together. He recited to us this Surah, meaning the entire Surah Al-Saff. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, and he said at the end of it: So this Surah was revealed about them. It was also narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Hibban, and Al-Hakim, who said: It is authentic according to the criteria of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab and Al-Sunan. His saying: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God. We have already discussed this, and the way of expressing it in some surahs using the present tense, and in some of them using the imperative, is to guide us to the permissibility of glorifying God at all times, past, future, and present. We have already mentioned something similar to this at the beginning of Surah Al-Hadid. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, meaning the Victorious Who is not defeated: the Wise in His actions and words.
61:2: 2- O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? This question is for rebuke and reprimand: that is, why do you say of the good that which you do not do? Lam is composed of the preposition lam and the interrogative ma, and its alif was deleted to make it easier due to its frequent use, as in similar words.
61:3: Then He, the Almighty, blamed them for that, saying: 3- It is most hateful to God that you say what you do not do meaning that it is very hateful, which is hatred, and hatred and maqtah are two verbal nouns. It is said that a man is hated and hated: if people do not like him. Al-Kisa'i said: that you say is in the nominative case, because kabar is a verb meaning bad, and maqtan is in the accusative case as a specification. Based on this, there is an indefinite pronoun in kabar explained by the indefinite article, and that you say is the one specifically blamed. There is disagreement about whether it is raised by the subject, and its predicate is the predicate of the sentence that precedes it, or its predicate is deleted, or it is the predicate of a deleted subject. If it is said that he intended by his saying kabar to express astonishment, and Ibn Asfour counted it among the verbs of astonishment. It is also said that it is not among the verbs of blame nor among the verbs of astonishment, but rather it is attributed to that you say, and maqtah is a specification transferred from the subject.
61:4: 4- Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks. The commentators said: The believers said: We wish that God would inform us of the most beloved deeds to Him so that we would do them even if it cost us our wealth and lives. So God revealed: Indeed, God loves those who fight Al-Mawrid 2:17. The accusative of safān is a verbal noun, and the object is omitted: that is, they arrange themselves in ranks. It was said that it is a verbal noun in the place of a state: that is, in rows or lined up. The majority of scholars read yaqatīluun in the active form. Zayd ibn Ali read it in the passive form, and yaqatluun was read with a shaddah. The phrase as if they were a solid structure is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of yaqatīluun, or of the pronoun in safān on the assumption that it is interpreted as in rows or lined up. The meaning of marsūn is: stuck together. It is said that you stacked the building in rows, meaning you joined some of it to others. Al-Farra' said: stacked with lead. Al-Mubarrad said: It is taken from the word rasasat which means to put things together, but they are not close together until they become like a single piece. It is also said that it is from rasees, which means to put things together, and tarass means to stick together.
61:5: 5- And when Moses said to his people When God Almighty mentioned that He loves those who fight in His cause, He made clear that Moses and Jesus were commanded to follow monotheism and fought in the cause of God, and that punishment was imposed on those who opposed them. The circumstance is related to something omitted, which is remember: that is, remember, O Muhammad, to these people who turned away at the time of Moses's statement. It is possible that the reason for mentioning the story of Moses and Jesus after loving those who fight in the cause of God was to warn the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, not to do to their prophet what the people of Moses and Jesus did to them. O my people, why do you harm me? This is what is said: that is, why do you harm me by disobeying what [I command you] of the laws that God has imposed upon you, or why do you harm me with cursing and disparagement, including throwing stones at him? This was explained in Surat Al-Ahzab. The phrase and you know that I am the Messenger of God to you is in the accusative case as a state. Has is to confirm knowledge or to emphasize it. The present tense is to indicate continuity. The meaning is: How do you harm me while you know that I am the Messenger of God, and the Messenger is respected and glorified, and you have no doubt about the message because of the miracles you have witnessed that require you to acknowledge my message, and the knowledge of it is beneficial to you with certainty. But when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate meaning when they persisted in their deviation and continued upon it, God caused their hearts to deviate from righteousness and turned them away from accepting the truth. It was also said: When they deviated from faith, God caused their hearts to deviate from the reward. Muqatil said: When they turned away from the truth, God turned their hearts away from it, meaning that when they abandoned the truth by harming their prophet, God turned their hearts away from the truth as a punishment for what they had done. And God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people This sentence confirms the meaning of what preceded it. Al-Zajjaj said: He does not guide those who He knows will be defiantly disobedient, meaning that He does not guide everyone who is characterized by immorality, and these are among them.
61:6: 6- And when Jesus, son of Mary, said is in apposition to And when Moses said, the object of its agent, or the object of an implied agent in apposition to the agent of the first circumstance, O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what was before me of the Torah meaning that I am the Messenger of God to you with the Gospel, confirming what was before me of the Torah, because I did not bring you anything that contradicts the Torah, rather it includes good tidings of me, so how can you turn away from me and oppose me? The accusative of confirming is in the state, and likewise bringing good tidings, and the agent in them is what is in the messenger of the meaning of sending, and the meaning is: I was sent to you while I was confirming what was before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of those who will come after me, and if I am like that in confirming and bringing good tidings, then there is no reason to deny me, and Ahmad is the name of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is a proper noun derived from the attribute, and it is possible that it is an exaggeration of the agent, so its meaning is that he praises God more than others, or than The passive participle means that he is praised for his good qualities more than anyone else. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Abu ‘Amr, as-Sulami, Zur ibn Hubaish and Abu Bakr from ‘Aasim read min ‘adī with a fat-ha on the ya’. The rest read it with a sukun on the ya’. So when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, ‘This is obvious magic.’ That is, when Jesus came to them with miracles, they said, This that he has brought to us is clear, apparent magic. It was also said that what was meant was Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning that when he brought them this, they said this statement. The first interpretation is more appropriate. The majority read it as magic, while Hamzah and al-Kisa’i read it as sahir.
61:7: 7- And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God while he is being invited to Islam? That is, no one is more unjust than him who invents a lie against God, while he is being invited to the religion of Islam, which is the best and most honorable religion, because whoever is like that has the right not to invent a lie against others, so how can he invent a lie against his Lord? The majority of scholars read and he is being called from the supplication in the passive form. Talhah ibn Musarraf read he is called with a fat-ha on the ya and a shaddah on the dal from the claim in the active form. It is transitive with to because it includes the meaning of belonging and affiliation. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. This sentence confirms the content of what preceded it. The meaning is: He does not guide those who are characterized by injustice, and those mentioned are among them.
61:8: 8- They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths. Extinguishing means putting out. Its root is fire, and it is used metaphorically for something similar to it, such as appearance. What is meant by the light of God is the Qur’an, meaning they want to invalidate and deny it by word, or Islam, or Muhammad (peace be upon him), or arguments and proofs, or all of the above. The meaning of with their mouths is: with the words that come out of their mouths that include insults. And God will perfect His light by making it appear in the horizons and raising it above other things. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs from Asim read it as perfecting His light with the addition, and the rest read it with the tanween of mutam, even if the disbelievers dislike that, as it will inevitably happen. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. Ibn Atiyyah said: The lam in li-ya-tif’u is a lam of emphasis that precedes the object, because the meaning is: they want to extinguish, and this lam mostly adheres to the object when it comes before it, like when you say: I hit Zayd, or I intended to see you. It was also said that it is the lam of reason, and the object is omitted: that is, they want to invalidate the Qur’an or repel Islam or destroy the Messenger in order to extinguish. It was also said that it has the meaning of an that is the accusative and that it is accusative in itself. Al-Farra’ said: The Arabs place the lam of ki in the place of an in aradah and amr, and Al-Kisa’i agreed with this view. An example of this is his statement: God wants to make clear to you.
61:9: And the sentence 9- It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions, even though the polytheists hate that is a new sentence confirming what came before it. Guidance is the Quran or the miracles, and the meaning of the religion of truth is the true religion, which is the religion of Islam. The meaning of to make it prevail is to make it prevail over all religions, high above them and dominant over them, even though the polytheists hate that, for that will inevitably happen. Mujahid said: That is, when Jesus descended, there would be no religion on earth except the religion of Islam. Religion is a verbal noun used to express multiple religions, and the answer to if in both cases is omitted, and the meaning is that he completed it and made it prevail. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Before jihad was made obligatory, some of the believers would say: We wish that God would tell us what the most beloved deeds are so that we could do them. But God delayed telling His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that the most beloved deeds are faith in God without doubt, and jihad against those who disobey Him, who contradicted faith and did not acknowledge it. When jihad was revealed, some of the believers disliked that and found it difficult to do so, so God said: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding His statement: It is most hateful to God that you say what you do not do, that he said: This verse is only about fighting. They were people who would come to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and a man would say: I fought and struck with my sword, but they did not do so, so this verse was revealed. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him that he said: They said, If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, we would do them. So God informed them and said, Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks as if they were a solid structure. They disliked that, so God revealed, O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? Great is hatefulness in the sight of God that you say that which you do not do. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, as if they were a solid structure. He said: It is fixed and cannot be removed, stuck together. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Jubayr bin Mut’im that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, “I have names: I am Muhammad, and I am Ahmad, and I am al-Hashir upon whose feet God will gather the people, and I am al-Mahi through whom God will wipe out disbelief, and I am al-Aqib, and the Aqib is the one after whom there will be no prophet.”
61:10: His statement: 10- O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? He made the aforementioned business equivalent to [trade] because they profit from it just as they profit from it, and that is by entering Paradise and being saved from the Fire. The majority read tanjikum with a light pronunciation of injaa. Al-Hasan, Ibn Amir, and Abu Haywah read it with a heavy pronunciation of tanjih.
61:11: Then the Almighty explained this trade which He indicated, saying: 11- You believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives. This is a statement in the sense of a command to indicate the obligation of compliance, so it is as if it had already happened, so He informed of its occurrence. He mentioned wealth before lives because it is what one begins with in spending and preparing for jihad. The majority read it as you believe, and Ibn Mas'ud read it as they believed and strived for the matter. Al-Akhfash said: You believe is an explanatory apposition to trade. It would be better for the sentence to be renewed, explaining what preceded it. The reference in His saying that is to what was mentioned of faith and jihad, which is the subject and predicate. It is better for you, meaning this action is better for you than your wealth and your lives. If you only knew, meaning if you were among those who know, then you know that it is better for you, not if you were among the ignorant, for you do not know that.
61:12: 12- "He will forgive you your sins." This is the answer to the command indicated by the wording of the declarative, and that is why it is in the jussive mood. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Mubarrad said: His statement "you believe means believe. That is why He will forgive you" is in the jussive mood. Al-Farra' said: "He will forgive you" is the answer to the question, so he made it in the jussive mood because it is the answer to the question. The scholars made a mistake in this view. Al-Zajjaj said: They are not forgiven if He guides them to what will benefit them, but rather they are forgiven if they believe and strive in jihad. Al-Razi said, explaining Al-Farra's statement: "Have I guided you? has the meaning of a command, for him it is said Have you been silent? meaning be quiet. The explanation is that hall" has the meaning of a question, then it gradually becomes an offer and an urging, and urging is like enticement, and enticement is a command. Zayd ibn Ali read "you believe and you strive in jihad" with the omitted lam of the command. And before you are forgiven is in the jussive mood with an implied condition: that is, if you believe, He will forgive you. Some of them read it with assimilation in He forgives you. The first one left out assimilation because the ra’ is a repeated letter, so it is not good to assimilate it with the lam. And He will admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. The explanation of how the rivers flow beneath the gardens has already been presented. And goodly dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is, in gardens of residence. That is the great attainment. That is, that which is mentioned in forgiveness. And entering the gardens described with what was mentioned is the conquest after which there is no victory, and the triumph that has no equal.
61:13: 13- "And another which you love." Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra' said: "Another is conjoined with trade," so it is in the accusative case: meaning, "Shall I guide you to another salvation which you love in this life along with the reward of the Hereafter?" It was also said that it is in the nominative case: meaning, "And you have another characteristic." It was also said that it is in the accusative case: meaning, "And He will give you another characteristic." Then the Almighty explained this Hereafter and said: "Victory from God and an imminent conquest." Meaning, it is a victory from God for you, and an imminent conquest. Al-Kalbi said: It means the victory over Quraysh and the conquest of Mecca. Ata' said: He means the conquest of Persia and Rome. "And give good tidings to the believers" is conjoined with something omitted: meaning, "Say, 'O you who believe, and give good tidings,' or you believe," because it is in the sense of a command. The meaning is: And give good tidings, O Muhammad, to the believers of victory and conquest, or give them good tidings of victory in this world and conquest, and of Paradise in the Hereafter, or give them good tidings of Paradise in the Hereafter.
61:14: Then the Almighty urged the believers to support His religion, saying: 14- O you who have believed, be supporters of God meaning, continue in what you are doing of supporting the religion. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Nafi' read Ansar God with the tanween and left the addition. The rest read it with the addition, and the orthography accepts both readings together. Abu Eid chose the addition reading because of His statement, We are supporters of God with the addition as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, Who are my supporters to God? meaning, support the religion of God like the support of the disciples when Jesus said to them, Who are my supporters to God? They said, We are the supporters of God. The kaf in as he said" is an attributive attribute of a deleted source, meaning: Be as he said. It was said that the kaf is in the accusative case due to the implied verb, and it was said that it is a statement based on its meaning without its wording, and the meaning is: Be supporters of God as the disciples were supporters of Jesus when he said to them, "Who are my supporters to God?" His saying: to God It was said that to means with: that is, from my supporters with God. It was also said that the meaning is: from my supporters in what brings one closer to God. It was also said that the meaning is: from my supporters who are directed to the support of God. This was discussed previously in Surat Al Imran. The disciples are the supporters of Christ and his sincere companions, and the first to believe in him. Their statement was previously mentioned. So a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved that is, a party believed in Jesus and a party disbelieved in him. This is because when they differed after his ascension, they dispersed and fought. So We supported those who believed against their enemy that is, We strengthened those who were right among them against those who were wrong. So they became dominant that is, high and victorious. It was also said that the meaning is: So now We have supported the Muslims against both groups altogether. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: They said: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, then this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? They disliked it, so it was revealed: O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? until His saying: a solid structure. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding His statement: O you who have believed, be supporters of God, that he said: That happened, praise be to God. Seventy men came to him and pledged allegiance to him at al-‘Aqabah, and they sheltered him and supported him until God made his religion prevail. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Sa’d narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the group who met him at al-‘Aqabah: Bring out to him twelve of you who will be responsible for their people, just as the disciples were responsible for Jesus, son of Mary.” Ibn Sa'd narrated on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the leaders: 'You are responsible for your people as the disciples were responsible for Jesus, son of Mary, and I am responsible for my people.' They said: 'Yes.'" Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "Then We supported those who believed," meaning: "We strengthened those who believed." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: "We supported those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation against their enemy, and today they have become victorious."
62:1: It is eleven verses It was revealed in Madinah. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Jumu’ah was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr. Muslim and the Sunan scholars narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recite on Friday Surat Al-Jumu’ah and When the hypocrites come to you. Muslim and the Sunan scholars narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Hibban and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite in the Maghrib prayer on Friday night “Say: O disbelievers” and “Say: He is God, the One.” He used to recite in the last ‘Isha’ prayer on Friday night Surat Al-Jumu’ah and Surat Al-Munafiqun. His statement: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God. The explanation of this has already been presented at the beginning of Surat Al-Hadid, and what follows it of the glorifications: The King, the Holy, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. The majority of scholars read these four attributes in the accusative case as an adjective for God, and it was also said that it was a substitute, but the first is more appropriate. Abu Wa’il ibn Muharib, Abu Al-Aliyah, Nasr ibn Asim, and Ru’bah read it in the nominative case as an implied subject, and the majority of scholars read Al-Quddus with a damma on the qaf, and Zayd ibn Ali read it with a fatha, and the explanation of this has already been presented.
62:2: 2- It is He who sent among the unlettered ones a Messenger from among themselves. What is meant by the unlettered ones are the Arabs, those among them who could write and those who could not, because they were not People of the Book. The unlettered one is originally the one who does not write or read what is written, and most of the Arabs were like that. The meaning of the unlettered one has already been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. The meaning of from among them is from among themselves, from their kind, and from among them. There was no tribe among the Arab tribes except that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a kinship with them. The reason for being grateful for him being from them is that this is closer to agreement because the kind is more inclined to his kind and closer to him. He recites to them His verses meaning the Qur’an, even though he was an unlettered one who could neither read nor write, and he did not learn that from anyone. The sentence is an attribute of a Messenger, and so is His statement: And purifies them. Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil said: meaning, he cleanses them from the filth of disbelief and sins. Al-Suddi said: He takes the zakat of their money. It was also said that He makes them pure of heart through faith. And teaches them the Book and wisdom. This is a third attribute of a Messenger. What is meant by the Book is The Qur’an and the Sunnah with wisdom, as al-Hasan said. It was also said that the Book is writing with a pen, and wisdom is understanding the religion, as Malik ibn Anas said, And they were before in clear error, meaning that they were before his mission among them in polytheism and straying from the truth.
62:3: 3- And others among them is in apposition to the illiterate: meaning He was sent among the illiterate, and He was sent among others among them before they had yet joined them at that time, and they will join them later, or it is in apposition to the first object in He teaches them, meaning and He teaches others, or to the object of He purifies them: meaning He purifies them and He purifies others among them, and what is meant by the others are those who came after the Companions until the Day of Resurrection, and it was said that what is meant by them are those who converted to Islam from outside the Arabs. Ikrimah said: They are the Followers. Mujahid said: They are all people. Ibn Zayd and Al-Suddi said the same. The phrase until they join them is an attribute of others, and the pronoun in among them and for them refers to the illiterate. This supports the fact that what is meant by others are those who will come after the Companions from among the Arabs specifically on the Day of Resurrection. Even though he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to all of mankind, the specification of the Arabs here is to show gratitude to them, and that does not contradict the generality of the message. It is permissible for what is meant by others to be the non-Arabs because even though they are not Arabs, they have become from them through Islam, and all Muslims are one nation, even if their races differ. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, meaning He is eloquent in might and wisdom.
62:4: And the reference in his saying: 4- that is to what was mentioned above. Al-Kalbi said: It means Islam. Qatada said: It means revelation and prophethood. And it was said that it refers to the inclusion of the non-Arabs with the Arabs, and it is a subject and its predicate is The bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills meaning He gives it to whomever He wills of His servants and God is the possessor of great bounty which no bounty is equal to or comparable to.
62:5: 5- The parable of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not uphold it God Almighty set an example for the Jews who abandoned acting in accordance with the Torah, saying: The parable of those who were entrusted with the Torah meaning they were charged with carrying it out and acting in accordance with it and then did not uphold it meaning they did not act in accordance with it nor obey what they were commanded to do in it is like the parable of a donkey who carries volumes which is the plural of book which is the large book because it reveals the meaning when it is read. Maimun ibn Mihran said: The donkey does not know whether it has dung on its back or is dung? This is how it is with the Jews. Al-Jarhani said: He means they carried from the word carry meaning guarantee: meaning they guaranteed the rulings of the Torah. His saying carries is in the accusative case as a state, or as an attribute of the donkey since it is not meant to be a specific donkey, so it is considered an indefinite noun as in the saying of the poet: The mean man came and insulted me, so I went and said, It doesn’t concern me. “How evil is the example of the people who denied the signs of God.” That is, how evil is the example of the people who denied the signs of God, with the specification omitted, and the subject explained by it is implied, and the like of the people is the one specifically blamed, or the like of the people is the subject of how evil is the example, and the one specifically blamed is the relative pronoun after it with the omission of an adjective: that is, the like of those who denied. It is possible for the relative pronoun to be an attribute of the people, in which case it would be in the genitive case, and the one specifically blamed is omitted, and the meaning is: How evil is the example of the people who deny the signs of God, and God does not guide the wrongdoing people, meaning in general, so the Jews are included among them as a primary inclusion.
62:6: 6- Say, ‘O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of mankind…’ What is meant by those who are Jews is that they have become Jews. This is because the Jews claimed superiority over mankind, and that they are allies of God to the exclusion of mankind, as in their saying, We are the children of God and His beloved, and their saying, None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian. So God, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger to say to them when they made this false claim, Then wish for death, so that you may attain the honor you claim to attain, if you should be truthful in this claim. For whoever knows that he is among the people of Paradise loves to be free from this abode. The majority read fatamu with a damma on the waw, and Ibn as-Samīf’ read it with a fathah for ease. Al-Kisa’i narrated that the waw was replaced with a hamzah.
62:7: Then God Almighty informed us that they will never do that because of their sins, saying: 7- And they will never desire it because of what their hands have put forth, meaning because of what they have done of disbelief, sins, distortion, and alteration. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers, meaning in general, and these Jews are included among them in a primary way.
62:8: Then God, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger to tell them that fleeing from death will not save them and that it will come upon them. He said: 8- “Say: ‘The death from which you flee will surely meet you.’” It will inevitably and will come upon you without a doubt. The fa in His statement for it is included to include the meaning of the condition in the noun. Al-Zajjaj said: It is not said that Zayd is leaving, and here He said: For it will meet you because of the meaning of that of condition and consequence: that is, if you flee from it, then it will meet you. This is an exaggeration in indicating that fleeing from it will be of no use. It was said that it is an additional particle, and it was said that the speech was completed when He said you flee from it, then He began by saying For it will meet you. “Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed,” and that is on the Day of Resurrection. Then He will inform you of what you used to do, of ugly deeds and will reward you for them. Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib on the authority of Maysarah that this verse is written in the Torah with seven hundred verses: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. This is the beginning of Surat al-Jumu'ah. Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn 'Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: We are an illiterate nation; we neither write nor calculate. Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: "We were sitting with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when Surat al-Jumu'ah was revealed and he recited it. When he reached: "And others among them who have not yet joined them," a man said to him: "O Messenger of God, who are these who have not yet joined us?" So he placed his hand on Salman al-Farisi and said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if faith were at the Pleiades, men from these would have attained it." Muslim also narrated it from his two hadiths with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with the wording: "If faith were at the Pleiades, men from Persia, or he said: from the sons of Persia, would have taken it." Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Qays ibn Sa'd ibn Ubadah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "If faith were the Pleiades, some people from Persia would attain it." At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Ad-Diya' narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa'd that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "In the loins of the loins of the loins of men from among my companions are men and women from my nation who will enter Paradise without account." Then he recited: "And others from among them have not yet joined them, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise." Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: "That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills," he said: religion. Abd ibn Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on his authority: "The parable of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not uphold it," he said: the Jews. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding His statement: "journals," he said: books.
62:9: His saying: 9- O you who have believed, when the call to prayer is made meaning the call to prayer has been made, and what is meant by it is the call to prayer when the imam sits on the pulpit on Friday, because there was no other call during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). His saying, on the day of Friday is an explanation of when and an interpretation of it. Abu al-Baqa' said: Min means in as in His saying: Show me what they have created from the earth meaning on the earth. The majority of scholars read al-Jumu'ah with a damma on the meem. Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr and al-A'mash read it with a sukoon on it for the sake of alleviation. They are two dialects and their plural is jammu' and jummu'ah. Al-Farra' said: It is said al-Jumu'ah with a sukoon on the meem, a fatha on it, or a damma on it. It is an attribute of the day: meaning the day on which people are gathered. Al-Farra' also said and Abu Ubaid: The alleviation is easier and more appropriate, like: ghurfah and ghurf, tarfa and tarf, hurjah and hujr. The fatha on the meem is the dialect of Uqayl. It was said that it was called Friday because God gathered the creation of Adam in it. It was also said that God finished creating everything in it, so all creation gathered in it. It was also said that it was because people gathered in it for prayer. So hasten to the remembrance of God. Ata’ said: It means going and walking to the prayer. Al-Farra’ said: Going, striving, and going have one meaning, and this is indicated by the reading of Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn Mas’ud: So hasten to the remembrance of God. It was also said that what is meant is intention. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is not striving on foot, but rather it is intending with the hearts and intentions. It was also said that it is action, like His statement: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer, and His statement: Indeed, your striving is diverse, and His statement: And that man can have nothing but what he strives for. Al-Qurtubi said: This is the statement of the majority, and from it is the statement of Zuhair: People came after them to catch up with them. He also said: He sought to avenge the anger of Bin Murrah after the blood feud between the clan So work on remembering God and engage in His causes, such as washing, ablution, and turning to Him. This statement is supported by the poet’s saying: I strive for the sake of the majority of Bani Malik, each person striving for his own cause And leave off trading means abandon dealing in it, and all other transactions are included in it. Al-Hasan said: When the muezzin calls to prayer on Friday, buying and selling are not permitted. The reference in his saying, That is to striving to remember God and abandoning trading, and it is the subject and predicate. That is better for you means better for you than doing the trading and abandoning the striving, because of the reward and recompense in complying. And in not doing that, if it does not lead to punishment. If you only knew means if you are people of knowledge, then it is not hidden from you that that is better for you.
62:10: 10- So when you have completed the prayer meaning when you have performed the prayer, completed it, and finished it, disperse within the land for trade and to do whatever you need for your livelihood, and seek from the bounty of God meaning from His provision with which He bestows upon His servants what they obtain of profits in transactions and earnings. It was said that what is meant by it is seeking the reward from God through doing acts of obedience and avoiding what is not permissible. And remember God often meaning remember Him often by thanking Him for the good in this world and the hereafter that He has guided you to. Likewise, remember Him with what brings you closer to Him of remembrances, such as praise, glorification, magnification, seeking forgiveness, and the like, that you may succeed meaning so that you may win the good of both abodes and attain it.
62:11: 11- And when they see a trade or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing. The reason for the revelation of this verse is that the people of Medina were in poverty and need, so a caravan came from Syria while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was delivering the Friday sermon, so the people turned to him until only twelve men remained in the mosque. The meaning of disperse to it is that they dispersed and went out to it. Al-Mubarrad said: They inclined towards it, and the pronoun refers to trade, and it was specifically referred to by the pronoun rather than amusement because it was more important to them. It was said that the meaning is: And when they see a trade, they disperse to it, or amusement, they disperse to it, so the second was deleted because the first indicates it, as in the saying of the poet: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs It was said that he limited it to the pronoun of trade, because if dispersing to it is reprehensible with the need for it, then how about dispersing to amusement? And it was said otherwise, And they left you standing, meaning on the pulpit. Then God, the Exalted, commanded him to inform them that working for the Hereafter is better than working for this world, so He said, Say, ‘What is with God,’ meaning of the great reward, which is Paradise, is better than amusement and trade, which you went to and for which you left staying in the mosque and listening to the sermon of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And God is the Best of Providers, so from Him you should seek provision, and to Him you should send your acts of obedience, for that is one of the reasons for obtaining provision and the greatest thing it brings. Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: "I said, 'O Messenger of God, why is Friday so named?' He said: 'Because on it the clay of your father Adam was gathered together, and on it the blast and the resurrection will take place, and at the end of it are three hours, one of which is an hour in which whoever supplicates to God with a supplication will have his supplication answered.'" Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Salman who said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me: 'Do you know what Friday is?' I said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said it three times, then on the third time he said: 'It is the day on which God gathered your father Adam together. Shall I not tell you about Friday?'" Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he entered Paradise, and on it he was expelled from it. The Hour will not come except on a Friday." There are hadiths on this topic which clearly state that Adam was created on it. There are many hadiths about the merits of Friday, as well as about the merits of the Friday prayer and its great reward, and the time it is held, and that supplications are answered on it. I have explained this in my explanation of Al-Muntaqa in a way that no one needs to read anything else. Abu Ubaid in his Fadhail, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Al-Anbari in Al-Masahif narrated on the authority of Kharshah bin Al-Har who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab saw with me a tablet on which was written: When the call to prayer is made on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of God. He said: Who dictated this to you? I said: Ubayy bin Ka’b. He said: “Ubayy taught us the abrogated verses: ‘Recite it, then proceed to the remembrance of God.’” These narrators, except for Abu Ubaid, narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed away, and we do not recite this verse in Surat Al-Jumu’ah except: ‘Proceed to the remembrance of God.’” Al-Shafi’i also narrated it on his authority in Al-Umm, as did Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. They all narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he used to recite, Then proceed to the remembrance of God. He said, If it were so, then listen, I would have hastened until my cloak fell off. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b that he recited it likewise. Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then proceed to the remembrance of God. He said, Then proceed. Abd bin Hamid narrated on his authority that striving is action. Abd bin Hamid narrated On the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b: “Two men from among the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to go to Ash-Sham for business. They might come on a Friday while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was delivering the sermon, so they would leave him and stand up. Then the verse, ‘And abandon business,’ was revealed, and what had happened before that was forbidden to them.” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said regarding the verse, ‘So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God,’ that he said: ‘It is not for seeking worldly gain, but rather to visit the sick, attend a funeral, and visit a brother for the sake of God.’” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: You have not been commanded to do anything for the sake of worldly gain; it is only to visit the sick, attend a funeral, and visit a brother for the sake of God. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: “While the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing delivering the Friday sermon, a caravan arrived in Medina. The Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rushed to it until there were only twelve men left, including myself, Abu Bakr, and Umar. Then God revealed: ‘And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it’ to the end of the surah. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: The caravan of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came carrying food, and they left the Friday prayer, some of them wanting to buy, and some of them wanting to look at Dihya, and they left the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing on the pulpit. Twelve men and seven women remained in the mosque. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If they were to all leave, the mosque would be engulfed in fire around them.’” There are narrations on this topic that include this meaning from a group of the Companions and others.
63:1: It is eleven verses It was revealed in Madinah. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Munafiqun was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Saeed bin Mansour and At-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat, and As-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recite Surat Al-Jumu’ah in the Friday prayer, inciting people against the believers with it, and in the second prayer he would recite Surat Al-Munafiqun with it, rebuking the hypocrites.” Al-Bazzar and At-Tabarani narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Unayyah Al-Khawlani. His saying: 1- If the hypocrites come to you meaning if they reach you and attend your gathering, and the answer to the condition is they said, and it was said that it is omitted, and they said is a state, and the meaning is: they came to you saying such and such, so do not [accept] from them.
63:2: And it was said that the answer is 2- They took their oaths as a shield and this is far-fetched. They said, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God’ They confirmed their testimony with that and lam to indicate that it came from the depths of their hearts from the sincerity of their belief. What is meant by the hypocrites is Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions. The meaning of we bear witness is that we swear, so it runs in the manner of an oath, and therefore it meets with what an oath meets with. From this is the saying of Qays bin Dharih: I bear witness before God that I love her, so this is for her with me, as she has for me And like we testify we know, it is like an oath as in the poet’s saying: I knew that my death would come, for the arrows of fate do not miss. The sentence And God knows that you are indeed His Messenger is parenthetical, confirming the content of what preceded it, which is the testimony they made public, even though their inner selves were contrary to that. And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars that is, in their testimony which they claimed was from the bottom of their hearts and sincere belief, not in what they actually said, which was the testimony to the Messengership, for that is true. The meaning is, And God bears witness that they are liars in what their words contain of emphasis indicating that their testimony to that is issued from sincere belief, reassurance of heart, and that their inner selves agree with their outward appearance. They have taken their oaths as a shield that is, they made their oath which they swore to you that they are from you and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, a protection to protect them from you and a screen to conceal themselves behind from being killed and captured. The sentence is a new sentence to explain their lie and their oath to him. The statement of those who said that it is the answer to the condition has already been made. The majority of scholars read their oaths with a fat-ha on the hamza, while al-Hasan read it with a kasra. The explanation of this has already been mentioned in Surat al-Mujadilah. So they barred people from the path of God means they prevented people from believing, striving, and performing acts of obedience because of their doubts and criticism of the Prophethood. This is the meaning of sadd which means turning away, and it may be from sudd which means they turned away from entering the path of God and implementing His laws. Indeed, evil was what they used to do of hypocrisy and barring.
63:3: And in Sa'a there is a meaning of astonishment and allusion in His saying: 3- That is to what was mentioned previously of lying, turning away and the ugliness of deeds, and it is the subject and its predicate is because they believed meaning because they believed outwardly as hypocrisy then disbelieved inwardly, or they showed belief to the believers and showed disbelief to the disbelievers, and this is explicit in the disbelief of the hypocrites, and it was said that the verse was revealed about a people who believed then apostatized. The first is more appropriate as the context indicates So He sealed their hearts meaning He sealed them because of their disbelief. The majority read So He sealed in the passive voice, and the preposition and noun that follow it replace the subject. Zayd ibn Ali read it in the active voice, and the subject is a pronoun that refers to God, the Most High, and this is indicated by the reading of Al-A'mash, So God sealed their hearts, so they do not understand" what is in it of their goodness and guidance, which is faith.
63:4: 4- And when you see them, their bodies impress you meaning their appearance and looks, meaning that they have bodies that impress whoever sees them because of the freshness and beauty in them. And if they speak, you listen to their speech so you think that their speech is true and honest because of their eloquence and smooth tongues. Abdullah bin Ubayy was the leader of the hypocrites, eloquent, large and handsome, and he used to attend the gathering of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when he spoke, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would hear his speech. Al-Kalbi said: What is meant is Abdullah bin Abi, Jad bin Qais, and Mu’tab bin Qais. They had good bodies, good looks, and eloquence. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said to be for anyone who was suitable for him. This is indicated by the reading of those who read yasma’ in the passive voice. The phrase as if they were propped up wood is a new sentence to confirm what came before, that their bodies delight the observer and delight the viewer. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject. They were likened in their sitting in the gatherings of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, leaning on them to propped up wood leaning against a wall that does not understand or know. They are like that because they are devoid of beneficial understanding and knowledge that benefits its owner. Al-Zajjaj said: He described them with perfect images, then he informed that they are in their lack of understanding and insight like wood. The majority read khashab with two dhammahs, while Abu Amr, Al-Kisa'i, and Qunbal read it with a sukoon on the sheen. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib also read it this way. Abu 'Ubaid chose it because its singular is khashbah like badanah and badan. Abu Hatim chose the first reading. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Sa'id ibn Al-Musayyab read it with two fathahs. The meaning of musnadah is that it was attributed to something else, from their saying: I attributed such-and-such to such-and-such, and the emphasis is for emphasis. Then God, the Exalted, criticized them for their cowardice, saying: They think that every shout is against them, meaning that they think that every shout they hear is a real and devastating blow to them, due to their extreme cowardice and the fear in their hearts. There are two interpretations of the second object of calculation: One is that it is against them, and His statement, They are the enemy, is a new sentence to clarify that they are the ones who are perfect in their enmity, since they show something other than what they conceal. The second interpretation is that the second object of calculation is His statement, They are the enemy, and His statement, Against them, is connected to a shout. It came with the collective pronoun because of the predicate, and it should have been said, He is the enemy, but the first interpretation is more appropriate. Muqatil and al-Suddi said: That is, if a crier calls out in the army, or an animal gets loose, or a lost animal is reported, they think that they are the ones meant because of the fear in their hearts. An example of this is the saying of the poet: You still think that everything after them is just horses charging at them and men It was said that the hypocrites were afraid that something would be revealed about them that would expose their secrets and permit the shedding of their blood and property. Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger to be on his guard against them, saying: Beware of them, lest they seize an opportunity from you or find out any of your secrets, because they are spies for your enemies among the disbelievers. Then He cursed them, saying: May God curse them, how they are deluded. The Arabs sometimes say this phrase to express astonishment, like saying: May God curse him, what a poet he is, or What a poet he is. This is not what is meant here, rather what is meant is to rebuke and rebuke them. It is a request from God the Almighty, a request from Himself to curse and disgrace them, or it is a teaching to the believers to say that. The meaning of how they are deluded is how they are diverted from the truth and inclined towards disbelief. Qatadah said: It means they deviate from the truth. Al-Hasan said: It means they are diverted from the right path.
63:5: 5- And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ meaning, if a believer says to them, What was revealed concerning you of the Quran has been revealed, so repent to God and His Messenger and come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you, they turn their heads away, meaning, they move them in mockery of that. Muqatil said: They turned their heads away from seeking forgiveness. The majority read turn away with a shaddah, while Nafi’ read it with a tafsir, and Abu Ubaid preferred the first reading. And you saw them turning away, meaning, they turned away from the words of the one who said to them, Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you, or they turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The phrase while they were arrogant is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of the first state, which is turn away, because seeing is visual, so they turn away is in the accusative case as a state of the subject, and the meaning is: And you saw them turning away, arrogant.
63:6: 6- "It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them" meaning asking forgiveness or not is the same, it will not benefit them because of their insistence on hypocrisy and persistence in disbelief. The majority read "I ask forgiveness with an open hamza without a long vowel, and deleted the question hamza, trusting in the evidence of am" on it. Yazid ibn al-Qaqa' read "God will not forgive them" meaning as long as they are in hypocrisy. "Indeed, God does not guide the wicked people meaning those who are complete in disobeying God and immersed in disobeying God, and the hypocrites are included among them primarily.
63:7: Then the Almighty mentioned some of their evil deeds, saying: 7- They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse.’ That is, until they disperse from him, meaning the poor emigrants. The sentence is a new chapter, explaining their immorality or God’s lack of forgiveness for them. The majority of scholars read yanfadhu from infidhad, which means dispersal. Al-Fadl ibn Isa al-Ruqashi read yanfadhu from anfad al-qawm, meaning when their provisions run out. It is said that a man shook out his vessel of provisions and it dispersed. Then the Almighty informed of the vastness of His kingdom, saying: And to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, meaning that He is the Provider of these emigrants, because the treasures of provisions belong to Him, so He gives to whomever He wills whatever He wills and withholds whatever He wills. But the hypocrites do not understand, that, and they do not know that the treasures of provisions are in God’s hand, the Almighty, and that He is the Expander, the Withholder, the Giver, and the Withholder.
63:8: Then the Almighty mentioned a heinous statement they said, saying: 8- They say, ‘If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble.’ The one who said this statement was Abdullah bin Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites. By more honorable, he meant himself and those with him, and by more humble, he meant the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and those with him. What he meant by return was their return from that battle. The statement was attributed to the hypocrites, even though the one who said it was an individual among those who listened to him and obeyed him. Then God, the Almighty, responded to the one who said that statement, saying: To God belongs honor and to His Messenger and to the believers. Meaning, power and victory belong to God alone and to those upon whom He bestowed it from among His Messengers and righteous servants, and not to anyone else. O God, just as You have given honor to the believers over the hypocrites, give honor to the just among Your servants, and send humiliation down upon the unjust and oppressive ones. But the hypocrites do not know what is beneficial so they do it, and what is harmful so they avoid it. Rather, they are like livestock due to their extreme ignorance, their increased confusion, and the seal on their hearts. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Zaid ibn Arqam, who said: “We set out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a journey and hardship befell the people. Abdullah ibn Ubayy said to his companions, ‘Do not spend on those with the Messenger of God until they disperse’ from around him. He also said, ‘If we return to Madinah, the more honorable will expel the more humble.’ So I went to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him of that. He sent for Abdullah ibn Ubayy and asked him. He swore an oath to tell him what to do. They said, ‘Zaid lied about the Messenger of God.’ I was deeply troubled by what they said until God revealed my confirmation in ‘When the hypocrites come to you.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called them and asked God to forgive them, but they turned their heads. This is His saying: ‘As if they were propped up pieces of wood.’ He said, ‘They were men, the most beautiful of things.’” A longer version of this narration was narrated on his authority by Ibn Sa’d, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God called them hypocrites because they concealed their polytheism and displayed faith. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: They took their oaths as a shield, meaning: Their oath by God that they were from you, and they avoided killing and war with their oaths. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: As if they were propped up wood, meaning upright palm trees. Ibn Mardawayh and al-Dhiya’ in al-Mukhtara also narrated on his authority: This verse was revealed: They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse,’ concerning a palm grove belonging to Umar ibn al-Khattab. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam and Ibn Mas’ud that they both recited: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: “We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a military expedition. Sufyan said: They thought it was the Battle of Banu al-Mustaliq, and a man from the Muhajirun kicked a man from the Ansar. The Muhajir said: ‘O Muhajirun,’ and the Ansar said: ‘O Ansar.’ When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard that, ‘What is this call of the Age of Ignorance?’ They said: ‘A man from the Muhajirun kicked a man from the Ansar.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Leave it, for it is rotten.’ Abdullah ibn Ubayy heard that and said: ‘Have they done it? By God, if we return to Madinah, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humiliated.’ report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so Umar stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, let me chop off the head of this hypocrite.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Leave him, lest people say that Muhammad kills his companions.’” Al-Tirmidhi added: “Then his son Abdullah said to him: ‘By God, you will not escape until you admit that you are the humiliated one, and the Messenger of God is the honorable one.’ So he did.”
63:9: When God the Almighty mentioned the ugliness of the hypocrites, He returned to addressing the believers, urging them to remember Him, saying: 9- O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. So He warned them against the morals of the hypocrites, whose wealth and children distracted them from the remembrance of God. The meaning of let them not distract you is let them not preoccupy you. What is meant by remembrance are the obligatory duties of Islam, as stated by Al-Hasan. Ad-Dahhak said: The five daily prayers. It was also said that it refers to reading the Quran. It was also said that it is addressing the hypocrites. He described them as believers because they outwardly believed, but the first is more appropriate. And whoever does that meaning is distracted by this world from religion, then it is those who are the losers meaning those who are complete in loss.
63:10: 10- And spend from what We have provided you. It appears that what is meant is spending in the Hereafter in general, and min is for partiality, meaning spend some of what We have provided you in the way of goodness. It was also said that what is meant is the obligatory zakat. Before death comes to one of you, that is, when its causes befall him and he witnesses its signs, the object is placed before the subject to emphasize the importance of the verb. Then he will say, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term.' That is, when what has befallen him comes, he says, calling out to his Lord, Why do you not give me respite and delay my death for a short term? "So I will give charity," meaning I will give charity with my wealth. "And be among the righteous. The majority of scholars read so I will give charity," with the assimilation of the ta' into the sad, and its accusative case as an answer to the wish. It was also said that the la in "lawla is redundant, and the original is law aakhrtanī. Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ūd, and Sa'īd ibn Jubayr read fa'atsādiq" without assimilation, according to the original. The majority of scholars read "wa-akun in the jussive mood, in the place of fa-sādiq, because it means, If You delay me, I will give charity and be." This is what Abu Ali al-Farsi, Ibn Atiyyah, and others said. Sibawayh, quoting al-Khalil, said: He made the jussive on the assumption of the condition indicated by the wish. Sibawayh considered this similar to the statement of Zuhair: It seemed to me that I was not aware of what had happened, nor had I preceded anything if it was a current one. So, the word wa-l-sabiq was lowered and was in apposition to mudrik which is the predicate of la based on the assumption that the letter ba was added to it.
