Abu Amr, Ibn Muhaisin and Mujahid read wa-akun in the accusative case in apposition to fa-sadaq, and the meaning of this is clear. However, Abu Ubaid said: I saw in the copy of Uthman wa-akun without the letter waw, and Ubaid ibn Umair read wa-akun in the nominative case as a new sentence: meaning, And I am. Ad-Dahhak said: Death does not befall anyone who has not performed Hajj or paid zakat except that he will ask to be returned to him, and he recited this verse.
63:11: Then God, the Almighty, answered this wisher, saying: 11- And God will not delay a soul when its term has come meaning when its term has come and its lifespan has come to an end. And God is Acquainted with what you do nothing is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for your deeds. The majority of scholars read you do with the superlative as an address, and Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim and As-Salami, read it with the subjunctive as a statement. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said about the verse, O you who have believed, let not the Qur’an he said: “They are righteous servants from my nation. Neither trade nor sale diverts them from the remembrance of God and the five obligatory prayers.” Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Whoever has wealth sufficient to perform Hajj to the House of God, or on which zakat is due, and does not do so, should ask to be returned to God upon death. A man said: O Ibn Abbas, fear God, for only the disbeliever asks to be returned to God. He said: I will recite to you a Qur’an regarding that: “O you who have believed” to the end of the surah.” Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So give charity and be among the righteous, he said: Perform Hajj.
64:1: It is eighteen verses. It is Madani according to the majority opinion. Ad-Dahhak said: It is Makkan. Al-Kalbi said: It is both Madani and Makkan. Ibn Ad-Durais, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah At-Taghabun was revealed in Madinah. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from Ibn Az-Zubayr. An-Nahhas narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah At-Taghabun was revealed in Makkah except for a few verses at the end which were revealed in Madinah about Awf ibn Malik Al-Ashja'i. He complained to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) about the coldness of his family and children, so God revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them to the end of the Surah. Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Ata' ibn Yasar. Ibn Hibban narrated in Ad-Du'afa, At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: No child is born except that five verses from Surah At-Taghabun are written on the crown of his head. Ibn Kathir said: This is very strange, indeed it is objectionable. Al-Bukhari included in his history on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: No child is born without five verses from the beginning of Surat Al-Taghabun written on the temple of his head. His saying: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God meaning that all of His creations in His heavens and His earth declare Him free from every deficiency or defect. To Him belongs the kingdom and to Him belongs praise They are unique to Him, and no one else has anything of them. Whatever is for His servants of them is from His abundance and returns to Him. And He is over all things competent Nothing is beyond His power.
64:2: 2- It is He who created you, and among you are disbelievers and among you are believers. That is, some of you are disbelievers and some of you are believers. Ad-Dahhak said: "Some of you are disbelievers in secret but believers in public, like the hypocrite. Some of you are believers in secret but disbelievers in public, like Ammar ibn Yasir and others like him who were forced to disbelieve." Ata' said: "Some of you are disbelievers in God but believers in the stars. Some of you are believers in God but disbelievers in the stars." Az-Zajjaj said: "God created the disbeliever, and his disbelief is an action for him and an acquisition, even though God is the Creator of disbelief. He created the believer and his faith is an action for him and an acquisition, even though God is the Creator of faith. The disbeliever disbelieves and chooses disbelief after God created him, because God has decreed that for him and knew it from him, because the existence of something contrary to what has been decreed is inability, and the existence of something contrary to what is known is ignorance." Al-Qurtubi said: This is the best of the sayings and it is what the majority of the nation agree upon. The disbeliever is mentioned before the believer because this is the most common occurrence when the Qur’an was revealed. And God is Seeing of what you do. Nothing of that is hidden from Him, so He will reward you according to your deeds.
64:3: Then when He, the Almighty, mentioned the creation of the microcosm, He followed it with the creation of the macrocosm, saying: 3- He created the heavens and the earth in truth, meaning with perfect wisdom. It was said that He created that with certainty, without doubt. It was also said that the ba’ has the same meaning as the lam, meaning that He created that to reveal the truth, which is that He rewards the doer of good with good and the wrongdoer with his wrongdoing. Then the Almighty returned to the creation of the microcosm, saying: And He shaped you and perfected your shapes. It was said that what is meant is Adam, whom He created with His own hand as an honor to him, as said by Muqatil. It was also said that what is meant is all of creation, and this is what is apparent: that He, the Almighty, created them in the most perfect shape, the best form, and the most beautiful shape. And framing means planning and shaping. The majority read and perfected your shapes with a damma on the sad, while Zayd ibn Ali, Al-A’mash, and Abu Zayd read it with a kasra, and to Him is the destination in the Hereafter, not to anything else.
64:4: 4- He knows what is in the heavens and the earth Nothing of it is hidden from Him. And He knows what you conceal and what you declare meaning what you conceal and what you reveal. The statement of it, along with its inclusion [in what] precedes it, is for further emphasis in the promise and threat. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts. This sentence confirms what preceded it, that His knowledge includes all that is known, and it is a conclusion.
64:5: 5- Did there not come to you the report of those who disbelieved before? They are the disbelievers of the past nations, such as the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud. The address is to the disbelievers of the Arabs. So they tasted the consequences of their affair because of their disbelief. Consequence means heaviness and severity. What is meant by their affair here is the disbelief and sins they committed, and consequence is the punishment they suffered in this world. And for them is a painful punishment in the Hereafter, which is the punishment of the Fire.
64:6: And the reference in His saying: 6- That is to what was mentioned of the torment in the two abodes, and it is a subject and its predicate is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs meaning because the messengers sent to them used to come to them with apparent miracles so they said, ‘Are human beings guiding us?’ meaning each group of them said this statement to their messenger, denying that the messenger was of the human race and astonished by that, and by human beings He meant the race, and for this reason He said, Guide us. “So they disbelieved and turned away,” meaning they disbelieved in the messengers and what they brought and turned away from them and did not reflect on what they brought. It was said that they disbelieved in this statement that they said to the messengers and God was independent of their faith and worship. Muqatil said: God is self-sufficient with the proof He showed them and the clearest miracles. It was also said that He is self-sufficient with His authority and does not need the obedience of His servants. And God is Rich and Praiseworthy, meaning He has no need of the world or their worship of Him. He is praised by all His creatures in word and deed. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When the semen remains in the womb for forty nights, the Angel of Souls comes to it and ascends with it to the Lord. He says: ‘O Lord, is it male or female?’ God decrees as He decrees, and He says: ‘Wretched or happy?’ Then He writes what will befall it.” Abu Dharr recited five verses from the opening chapter of al-Taghabun up to the verse: And He formed you and perfected your forms, and to Him is the final destination. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “A person is born a believer, lives as a believer, and dies as a believer. A person is born a disbeliever, lives as a disbeliever, and dies as a disbeliever. A person acts happily for a period of his life, then what is written for him overtakes him and he dies miserable. A person acts miserably for a period of his life, then what is written for him overtakes him and he dies happy.”
64:7: His saying: 7- Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Allegation: is a statement based on conjecture and is used to refer to lying. Shuraih said: Everything has a definite article, and the definite article of lying is they claimed, and that they will never be resurrected is the object of claimed, and that is the lightened form of the heavy form, not the verbal noun, so that no accusative is added to accusative, and what is meant by the disbelievers are the disbelievers of the Arabs, and the meaning is: The disbelievers of the Arabs claimed that they will never be resurrected. Then the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to respond to them and invalidate their claim, so He said: Say, ‘Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed.’ Nay is the word for affirming the negation, so the meaning is: Rather, you will be resurrected. Then he swore to that, and the answer to the oath is that you will be resurrected: that is, you will emerge from your graves to be punished for what you did that is, you will be destroyed by that to establish proof against you, then you will be rewarded for it. And that the resurrection and the reward is easy for God since the return is easier than the beginning.
64:8: 8- So believe in God and His Messenger The fa is the eloquent letter that indicates an implied condition: that is, if the matter is thus, then believe in God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the light which We have sent down which is the Qur’an because it is a light by which one is guided from the [darkness] of misguidance. And God is Acquainted with what you do Nothing of your words and actions is hidden from Him, so He will reward you for that.
64:9: 9- The Day He will gather you for the Day of Assembly The factor in the adverbial phrase is to inform you, as An-Nahhas said. Another said: The factor in it is Khabir, and it was said that the factor in it is omitted, which is remember. Abu Al-Baqa' said: The factor in it is what the speech indicates: that is, you will differ on the Day He will gather you. The majority read Yajma'kum with a fat-ha on the ya' and a damma on the 'ayn, and it was narrated from Abu Amr with a sukoon on it, and there is no reason for that except for alleviation, even though this is not the place for it, as it was read in And what makes you feel with a sukoon on the ra', and like the saying of the poet: Today I drink without committing any sin against God or being excessive. By sukun Baa’ of Ashrab, Zayd ibn Ali, Ash-Sha’bi, Ya’qub, Nasr, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Al-Jahdary read it with a noon. The meaning of Liyyum Al-Jam’um is the Day of Resurrection, for on that day the people of the gathering will be gathered for recompense, and on that day every worker will be gathered with his work, and every prophet with his nation, and every oppressed person with his oppressor. That is the Day of Mutual Loss means that the Day of Resurrection is the Day of Mutual Loss, and that is because on that day some of the people of the gathering will be cheated by others, so the people of truth will be cheated by the people of falsehood, and the people of faith will be cheated by the people of disbelief, and the people of obedience will be cheated by the people of disobedience. There is no greater cheating than the cheating of the people of Paradise by the people of Hell when these people enter Paradise and those enter Hell. They will be placed in the same positions they would have been in had they not done what necessitated Hell. It is as if the people of Hell exchanged good for evil, good for bad, and bliss for torment, while the people of Paradise are the opposite of that. It is said that you cheated someone: if you sold or bought from him and the deficiency was on him and he was overpowered, this is what the commentators said, so the one who is cheated is the one whose family and homes in Paradise are cheated. And whoever believes in God and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds. That is, whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds deserves to have his misdeeds removed. The majority read he will remove and he will enter it with a dot, and Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read them with a noon in both, and the accusative of abiding therein forever is that it is an implied state, and the reference in his saying: that is to what was mentioned of the expiation and the entry, and it is the subject and its predicate is the great victory, meaning the victory that no victory can equal.
64:10: 10- And those who disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of the Fire, abiding eternally therein, and wretched is the destination. What is meant by the verses is either revelation or something more general than them. God Almighty mentioned the state of the happy and the wretched here to clarify what was mentioned previously about the loss, and that it will be due to thinking and the first group entering Paradise, and due to the second group entering Hell and remaining there eternally.
64:11: 11- No disaster strikes except by God's permission meaning, no disaster strikes anyone except by God's permission: that is, by His decree and predestination. Al-Farra' said, Except by God's permission meaning, by God's command. It was also said, Except by God's knowledge. It was said that the reason for its revelation was that the disbelievers said, If what the Muslims are doing were true, God would have protected them from disasters in this world. "And whoever believes in God - He will guide his heart" meaning, whoever believes and knows that nothing befalls him except what God has decreed for him, He will guide his heart to patience and acceptance of His decree. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said, "His heart is guided when a disaster strikes, so he knows that it is from God, so he submits to His decree and seeks refuge in Him. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, His heart is guided when a disaster strikes, so he says, 'Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return.' Al-Kalbi said, When afflicted, he is patient, when blessed, he is grateful, and when wronged, he forgives. The majority read yahdhu" with a fatha on the yaa and a kasra on the dal, meaning God guides him. Qatada, As-Sulami, Ad-Dahhak, and Abu Abd Al-Rahman read it with a damma on the yaa and a fatha on the dal in the passive form. Talha bin Masraf, Al-A'raj, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ibn Hurmuz, and Al-Azraq read "nahd" with a noon. Malik bin Dinar, Amr bin Dinar, and Ikrimah read "yahdhu" with a silent hamza and raising his heart, meaning he is reassured and calmed. "And God is All-Knowing," meaning He is eloquent in knowledge, nothing of it is hidden from Him.
64:12: 12- And obey God and obey the Messenger meaning, make the calamities easy for yourselves and occupy yourselves with obeying God and obeying His Messenger. But if you turn away meaning, you turn away from obedience, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification He has no other duty than that, and he did. The answer to the condition is omitted, and the meaning is that there is no harm upon the Messenger. The phrase then upon Our Messenger is only is an explanation for the omitted answer.
64:13: Then he guided us to monotheism and trust, saying: 13- God, there is no god but He meaning He is the One who deserves to be worshipped alone, so worship Him alone and do not associate partners with Him. And in God let the believers put their trust meaning let them entrust their affairs to Him and rely on Him, not on anyone else. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas`ud that it was said to him: What did you hear the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say about what they claim? He said: I heard him say: What a wretched mount a man is. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from him that he disliked what they claim. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The Day of Loss is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding the statement: That is the Day of Loss, that he said: The people of Paradise will be deceived by the people of Hell. Sa`id ibn Mansur narrated from Ibn Mas`ud regarding the statement: Whatever strikes of disaster, that he said: These are the calamities that befall a man and he knows that they are from God, so he submits to them and is content with them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: He guides his heart, that he said: meaning He guides his heart to certainty, so he knows that what befell him could not have missed him, and what missed him could not have befallen him.
64:15: Then God Almighty informed us that wealth and children are a trial, saying: 15- Your wealth and your children are but a trial, meaning a test, trial, and ordeal that will lead you to earn unlawful income and prevent God’s right, so do not obey them in disobeying God. And God has with Him a great reward, for whoever chooses to obey God and abandon disobeying Him out of love for his wealth and children.
64:16: Then the Almighty commanded them to fear God and obey Him, saying: 16- So fear God as much as you are able meaning as much as you are capable and as much as you can. A group of scholars have stated that this verse abrogates the statement of the Almighty: Fear God as He should be feared including Qatada, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. We have already explained the statement of the Almighty: Fear God as He should be feared and the meaning of and listen and obey meaning listen to what you are commanded to do and obey the commands. Muqatil said: Listen: Accept what you hear because there is no benefit in merely hearing. And spend that which is good for yourselves meaning spend from the money that God has provided you in ways of goodness and do not be miserly with it. His statement: that which is good for yourselves is in the accusative case due to an implied verb indicated by spend, as if he said: Give in spending that which is good for yourselves, or present good for it, this is what Sibawayh said. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said: It is an adjective for a deleted source: meaning, a good spending. Abu Ubaidah said: It is the predicate of the understood kan: meaning, let spending be good for you. The Kufians said: It is in the accusative case as a state, and it was said that it is the object of that which is spent: meaning, then spend that which is good. Apparently, in the verse, spending is general, without restriction to the obligatory zakat. It was said that what is meant is the obligatory zakat, and it was said that it is the voluntary zakat, and it was said that it is spending in jihad. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. That is, whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul and does what he is commanded to spend and that does not prevent him from it, it is those who are victorious in every good and successful in every goal. The interpretation of this verse has been presented above.
64:17: 17- If you lend God a good loan, spending your money on charitable causes with sincere intention and a good heart, He will multiply it for you, making the good deed tenfold to seven hundredfold. The interpretation of this verse and the differences in the readings of it in Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat Al-Hadid have been presented. And forgive you, meaning He will add to that multiplication the forgiveness of your sins. And God is Most Appreciative and Forbearing, He rewards those who obey Him with many times over, and He does not hasten to punish those who disobey Him.
64:18: 18- The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed meaning that which is unseen and what is present, nothing is hidden from Him. He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise meaning the Victorious, the Dominant, the Possessor of dazzling wisdom. Ibn al-Anbari said: The Wise is He who perfects the creation of things. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse, O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them, was revealed about a group of people from Mecca who had embraced Islam and wanted to come to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but their wives and children refused to let them. When they came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and saw that the people had understood the religion, they intended to punish them, but the verse was revealed up to His saying, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Buraydah who said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was delivering a sermon when Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn came forward wearing red shirts, walking and stumbling. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came down from the pulpit and carried them, one by one side and the other by the other. Then he ascended the pulpit and said: ‘God has spoken the truth: “Your wealth and your children are but a trial.” When I saw these two boys walking and stumbling, I could not resist interrupting my speech and going down to them.” Ibn Jarir and Al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God says: ‘I borrowed from My servant and he refused to lend Me. My servant reviled Me without realizing it. He says: ‘Woe to him, woe to him, while I am Time.’ Then Abu Hurayrah recited: ‘If you lend God a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you.’”
65:1: It is eleven verses, and it was said twelve It was revealed in Medina. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone. Ibn Al-Durais, Ibn Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat At-Talaq was revealed in Medina. His saying: 1- O Prophet, when you divorce women, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called them first as an honor to him, then he addressed them with his nation, or the address was to him specifically, and the plural is for glorification, and his nation is his example in that, and the meaning is: If you want to divorce them and are determined to do so, then divorce them during their waiting period, meaning when they are due to complete their waiting period or during the preceding period, or before their waiting period. Al-Jurjani said: The lam in li’datihinna has the meaning of fi: meaning during their waiting period. Abu Hayyan said: It is on the deletion of an adjective: that is, to begin their waiting period, and the lam is for timing, like I met him on the remaining night of such-and-such a month, and what is meant is that they divorce them during a period of purity in which intercourse has not occurred, then leave them until their waiting period expires. So if they divorce them, thus they have divorced them for their waiting period, and an explanation of this from the Sunnah will come at the end of the research, God willing. And count the waiting period means memorize it and memorize the time in which the divorce occurred until the waiting period is complete: which is three menstrual periods. The address is to the husbands, and it was said to the wives, and it was said to the Muslims in general, and the first is more appropriate because all the pronouns refer to them. And fear God, your Lord so do not disobey Him in what He has commanded you and do not harm them. Do not turn them out of their houses meaning the one we were in at the time of the divorce as long as they are in their waiting period. He added the houses to them, which are for their husbands, to emphasize the prohibition and to clarify their complete entitlement to residence during the waiting period. And likewise His saying: And remember what is recited in your houses and His saying: And abide in your houses then when He forbade the husbands Regarding their expulsion from the houses in which the divorce took place, he also forbade the wives from leaving, saying: nor should they leave meaning they should not leave those houses as long as they are in their waiting period except for a necessary matter, as will be explained later. It was also said that what is meant is that they should not leave on their own unless their husbands give them permission, in which case there is no problem, but the first is more appropriate: unless they commit a clear immorality. This exception is from the first clause, meaning do not expel them from their homes, not from the second clause. Al-Wahidi said: Most of the commentators agree that what is meant by immorality here is adultery, that is, if she commits adultery and is taken out to have the prescribed punishment carried out on her. Al-Shafi’i and others said: It is vulgarity in the tongue and being rude to those who live with her in that house. This is supported by what Ikrimah said: “In the Mushaf of my father, it says: ‘Unless they commit indecency with you.’” It was said that the meaning is: Unless they go out transgressing, because their going out in this manner is an indecency, and this is far-fetched. The reference in his saying: And those is to what was mentioned of the rulings, and it is the subject and predicate the limits of God. The meaning is: These rulings that He made clear to His servants are the limits that He set for them, and it is not permissible for them to transgress them to anything else. And whoever transgresses the limits of God, that is, he transgresses them to something else or neglects any of them, has wronged himself by bringing it to a place of destruction and causing it to fall into places of harm by God’s punishment of him for his transgression of His limits and transgression of His decree. The phrase You do not know, perhaps God will bring about after that something new is a new sentence to confirm the content of what came before it and to explain it. Al-Qurtubi said: All the commentators said: What is meant by the command here is the desire to take her back, and the meaning is: the incitement to divorce once and the prohibition of divorce three times, because if he divorces three times, he will harm himself when he regrets the separation and desires to take her back, so he will not find a way to take her back. Muqatil said after that: meaning after one or two divorces, a command to take her back. Al-Wahidi said: The thing that happens is that love for her return is placed in the man’s heart after one or two divorces. Al-Zajjaj said: If he divorces her three times at the same time, there is no meaning to his saying: Perhaps God will bring about something after that.
65:2: 2- And when they have reached their term i.e., they have almost reached the end of their waiting period and are approaching its end then keep them according to acceptable terms i.e., take them back with good treatment and desire for them without intending to harm them or part from them according to acceptable terms i.e., leave them until their waiting period is over so that you may have their souls while fulfilling their rights over you and not harming them and bring to witness two just men from among you to the taking back, and it was said to the divorce, and it was said to it to cut off disputes and resolve the source of the dispute, and the command is for encouragement as in His statement: And bring to witness when you make a sale and it was said that it is for obligation, and this is what Al-Shafi’i went with. He said: Witnessing is obligatory in the case of taking back and is recommended in the case of separation, and this is what Ahmad ibn Hanbal went with. Al-Shafi’i said: Return does not require witnesses like other rights. Something similar to this was narrated from Abu Hanifa and Ahmad. And establish the testimony for God. This is a command to the witnesses to come with what they have witnessed in order to draw closer to God. We have already presented an explanation of this in Surat Al-Baqarah. It has been said that the command is for spouses to establish the testimony, meaning, to bear witness upon return. Thus, His statement, And bring to witness two just men among you, is a command to bear witness itself, and His statement, And establish the testimony, is a command that it be purely for God. The reference in His statement, That is to what was previously mentioned of the command to bear witness and establish the testimony for God, and it is the subject and predicate. He who believes in God and the Last Day is admonished by it. He specified the believer in God and the Last Day because he is the one who benefits from it and no one else. And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. That is, whoever fears God’s punishment by obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions and adhering to the limits He has set for His servants and not transgressing them, He will make for him a way out from the hardships and trials he has fallen into.
65:3: 3- And will provide for him from where he does not expect meaning from a source that does not occur to him and is not in his calculations. Al-Sha'bi and Al-Dahhak said: This is specifically about al-Talaq 65:meaning, whoever divorces as God has commanded him, will have a way out in taking her back during the waiting period, and he will be like one of those who propose marriage after the waiting period. Al-Kalbi said: And whoever fears God by being patient at the time of calamity, He will make for him a way out from the Fire to Paradise. Al-Hasan said: A way out from what God has forbidden. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: A way out from everything that is difficult for people. Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said: And whoever fears God in performing the obligatory duties, He will make for him a way out from the punishment and will provide him with reward from where he does not expect: meaning, He will bless him for what he has done. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: And whoever fears God in following the Sunnah, He will make for him a way out from the punishment of the people of innovation and will provide him with Paradise from where he does not expect. And other sayings have been said. The apparent meaning of the verse is general, and there is no basis for specifying a particular type. What is included in the context is primarily included. And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him. That is, whoever puts his trust in God regarding what befalls him, He will suffice him regarding what concerns him. Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose. The majority of scholars read baligh amruhu with the tanween of baigh and the accusative of amruhu. Hafs read it with the addition, and Ibn Abi Ubla, Dawud ibn Abi Hind, and Abu Amr, in one narration from him, read it with the tanween of baigh and the nominative of amruhu as the subject of baigh, or that amruhu is a delayed subject and baigh is better brought forward. Al-Farraa’ said, explaining this reading: That is, His purpose is complete. The meaning according to the first and second readings is that God, glory be to Him, will accomplish whatever He wants of the matter; nothing escapes Him and nothing that is sought is beyond His power. According to the second reading, God’s purpose is enforceable and nothing can prevent Him. Al-Mufaddal read baighan in the accusative case as a state, and it is the predicate of indeed. His statement, God has set for everything a measure, means a determination, timing, or amount. God, glory be to Him, has set a term for hardship and a term for ease. Al-Suddi said: It is the amount of menstruation and waiting period.
65:4: 4- "And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation" They are the adults whose menstruation has stopped and have despaired of it. "If you are in doubt That is, you are suspicious and do not know how to complete their waiting period, Their waiting period is three months. And those who have not menstruated" Because they are young and have not reached the age of menstruation. That is, their waiting period is three months. This was omitted because the preceding statement indicated it. "And those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth" That is, their waiting period ends with the delivery of the pregnancy. The apparent meaning of the verse is that the waiting period of pregnant women is until they give birth, whether they are divorced or have had their husbands die. We have discussed this in detail in Surat Al-Baqarah. We have already discussed this verse and the other verse. "And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days. It was said that the meaning of If you are in doubt" is if you are certain. Ibn Jarir preferred that it means doubt, and this is the apparent meaning. Al-Zajjaj said: If you are in doubt about her menstruation, and her menstruation has stopped and she is one of those who menstruate like her. Mujahid said: If you are in doubt: meaning you do not know the waiting period of the woman who has reached menopause or the one who has not menstruated, then the waiting period is this. It was said that the meaning is: If you are in doubt about the blood that appears from her, whether it is menstruation or not, or istihadah, then the waiting period is three months. And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out meaning whoever fears God in obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, his matter will be made easy for him in this world and the hereafter. Ad-Dahhak said: Whoever fears God, let him follow the Sunnah, and He will make his matter easy for him in returning to her. Muqatil said: Whoever fears God in avoiding His disobedience, He will make his matter easy for him in enabling him to obey Him.
65:5: And the reference in his saying: 5- That is to what was mentioned of the rulings: that is, what was mentioned of the rulings is the command of God which He has sent down to you that is, His ruling by which He ruled between His servants and His law which He has legislated for them, and the meaning of He has sent it down to you is that He sent it down in His Book to His Messenger and made it clear to you and detailed its rulings and clarified what is permissible and what is forbidden. And whoever fears God by abandoning what He is not pleased with, He will remove from him his misdeeds that he committed, because piety is one of the reasons for forgiveness of sins. And He will make great for him a reward that is, He will give him a great reward in the Hereafter, which is Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced Hafsa, so she went to her family. Then God revealed: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their prescribed waiting period. It was said to him, Take her back, for she fasts and prays, and she is one of your wives in Paradise. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Qatadah, as a mursal. Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Abd Yazid and Abu Rukanah divorced Umm Rukanah, then he married a woman from the Muzaynah tribe. She came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, nothing will avail me more than this hair for a hair I took from her head.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became furious at that, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slept with Rukanah and his brothers, then he said to those sitting with him: ‘Do you think such and such is better than such and such?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abd Yazid: ‘Divorce her,’ so he did. Then he said to Abu Rukanah: ‘Take her back.’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, I divorced her.’ He said: ‘I know that,’ so he took her back. Then this verse was revealed: ‘O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period.’” Al-Dhahabi said: Its chain of transmission is weak, and the report is an error, because Abd Yazid did not live to see Islam. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry and then said: Let him take her back, then keep her until… She becomes pure, then menstruates and becomes pure. If he decides to divorce her, he should divorce her while she is pure before touching her. This is the waiting period for which God has commanded women to be divorced. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them during their waiting period. Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Divorce them during their waiting period. Ibn al-Anbari narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he recited: Divorce them during their waiting period. Ibn al-Anbari, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he recited it like this. Abd al-Razzaq, Abu Ubayd in his Fada’il, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited it like this. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: Whoever wants to divorce according to the Sunnah as God has commanded him, let him divorce her while she is pure, without intercourse. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh, through various chains of narration, narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, "Divorce them during their prescribed waiting period," that he said: "While they are pure and have not had intercourse with each other." There are narrations on this topic. Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, "And count the waiting period," that he said: "Divorce while they are pure and have not had intercourse with each other. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn Umar, regarding his statement, And they should not leave their houses unless they commit a clear immorality," that he said: "Her leaving her house before the expiry of her waiting period is a clear immorality. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, Unless they commit a clear immorality," that he said: "Adultery." And Abd al-Razzaq, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The clear indecency is when a woman speaks ill of a man’s family. If she speaks ill of them verbally, it is permissible for them to expel her.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Fatimah bint Qays, regarding His statement, Perhaps God will bring about after that something new, that she said: It is taking her back. Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin that a man asked Imran ibn Husayn about a man who divorced his wife and no one witnessed it. He said: “What a bad thing he did! He divorced her based on innovation and took her back based on something other than the Sunnah. So let him have witnesses to his divorce and to taking her back, and ask God for forgiveness.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, regarding His statement, And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out, that he said: His way out is to know that it is from God, and that God is the One who gives to him and withholds from him, who tests him, who heals him, and who defends him. And regarding His statement, And provides for him from where he does not expect, he said: From where he does not expect. He does not know. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out, that he said: He will save him from every distress in this world and the Hereafter. Al-Hakim narrated, who authenticated it, and al-Dhahabi declared it weak, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “This verse, ‘And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out,’ was revealed about a man from the Ashja’ tribe who was poor, had little money, and had many dependents. He came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Fear God and be patient. It was not long before his son brought back some sheep that the enemy had captured. He came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about them and told him their story. He said: Eat them. Then the verse, ‘And whoever fears God’ was revealed.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “Awf bin Malik Al-Ashja’i came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, my son has been captured by the enemy and his mother is distressed, so what do you command me?’ He said: ‘I command you and her to say frequently, “There is no power or strength except with God.”’ The woman said: ‘Yes, what you command.’ So they began to say it frequently, but the enemy neglected him, so he drove away their sheep and brought them to his father. Then this verse was revealed: ‘And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out’…’” (Surah Al-Baqara: 10) There are narrations on this topic that testify to this. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Aisha regarding the verse: ‘It will suffice him for the worries and sorrows of this world.’ Ahmad narrated…” And Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in Al-Ma`rifah, and Al-Bayhaqi authenticated it on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite this verse: ‘And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect. ’ He kept repeating it until he fell asleep, then he said: O Abu Dharr, if all of mankind were to take it, it would suffice them.” There are hadiths on this topic. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, regarding the statement: ‘And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him,’ that he said: The one who relies is not the one who says, ‘My need will be fulfilled,’ and not everyone who relies upon God will have his concerns sufficed for him, repel what he dislikes, and fulfill his need. Rather, God has made the superiority of the one who relies upon God over the one who does not relies upon Him: that He will expiate his sins and grant him a great reward. Concerning His statement: ‘Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose,’ he said: He says that He will judge the one who relies upon God and the one who does not relies upon Him, but He will expiate his sins and grant him a great reward. Concerning His statement: ‘God has already set for everything a [decreed] extent,’ he said: It means a term and an end to which it will reach. Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Abu Ya’la, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: If you were to put your trust in God as He should be trusted, you would be provided for as the birds are provided for; they go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening with full crops. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b that when this verse in Surat al-Baqarah about the waiting period of women was revealed, some people from Madinah said: There remains a number of waiting periods for women that are not mentioned in the Qur’an: the young, the old, those whose menstruation has stopped, and those who are pregnant. Then God revealed: And those who have despaired of menstruation al-Baqarah 2:17. Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa'id al-Musnad, Abu Ya'la, al-Dhiya' in al-Mukhtara, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka'b who said: "I said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): 'And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth.' Does this refer to the woman who has been divorced three times, or the woman whose husband has died? He said: 'It refers to the woman who has been divorced three times, or the woman whose husband has died.'" A similar hadith was narrated from him with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) by Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Daraqutni from another chain of transmission. Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id bin Mansur, Abd bin Hamid, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud that he heard that Ali said: She should observe the waiting period of the later of the two periods. He said: Whoever wishes, I may imprecate him. The verse in Surat al-Qasra was revealed after Surat al-Baqarah 2:'And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth.' It is so-and-so many months. Every divorced woman or woman whose husband has died, her term is until she gives birth. Something similar to this was narrated from him through various chains of transmission, some of which are in Sahih al-Bukhari. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and other books of hadith from Umm Salamah that Subai'ah al-Aslamiyah's husband died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth forty nights after his death. She proposed marriage and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married her. There are other hadiths on this topic.
65:6: His statement: 6- Lodge them where you live This is a new statement that includes an explanation of what women are entitled to in terms of housing. Min is for partiality: meaning some of the place where you live. It was said that it is redundant. From your means means from your means and energy. Lodge means ability. Al-Farra' said: He says according to what he finds. If he is well-off, he should be generous with her in terms of housing and expenses. If he is poor, then according to that. Qatada said: If you can only find a corner of your house, then let her live in it. Scholars have differed regarding a woman who has been divorced three times: is she entitled to housing and maintenance or not? Malik and al-Shafi'i held that she is entitled to housing but not maintenance. Abu Hanifa and his companions held that she is entitled to housing and maintenance. Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr held that she is not entitled to maintenance or housing. This is the correct view, and I have stated it in my commentary on al-Muntaqa, in a manner that no one needs to read otherwise. And do not harm them in order to restrict them. God, the Exalted, forbade harming them by restricting their housing and maintenance. Mujahid said: In housing. Muqatil said: In maintenance. Abu al-Dhaha said: It means that he divorces her, and when two days remain of her waiting period, he takes her back, then divorces her. And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. That is, until the end of their pregnancy. There is no disagreement among scholars about the obligation of maintenance and housing for a pregnant divorced woman. As for a pregnant woman whose husband has died, Ali, Ibn Umar, Ibn Mas`ud, Shuraih, Al-Nakha`i, Al-Sha`bi, Hammad, Ibn Abi Laila, Sufyan and his companions said: She should be supported from all of the wealth until she gives birth. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Jabir ibn Abdullah, Malik, Al-Shafi`i, Abu Hanifah and his companions said: She should not be supported except from her share. This is the correct view based on the evidence from the Sunnah. But if they breastfeed for you your children after that, then give them their payment meaning the payment for breastfeeding. The meaning is that if divorced women breastfeed the children of their divorced husbands, they are entitled to their payment for that. And consult together in what is acceptable is addressed to husbands and wives, meaning, consult among yourselves about what is acceptable and not reprehensible, and let some of you accept what is acceptable and good from others. The original meaning is to command some of you to do what is customary among the people and not reprehensible to them. Muqatil said: The meaning is that the father and the mother should agree on a specified wage. It was said that the good and beautiful thing from the husband is that he provides her with the wage, and the good and beautiful thing from her is that she does not ask for the wage that the husband finds difficult. And if you disagree meaning regarding the wage for breastfeeding, and the husband refuses to give the mother the wage and the mother refuses to breastfeed him except for the wage she wants, then another wet nurse shall breastfeed him meaning he may hire another wet nurse to breastfeed his child. He is not obligated to give what the wife asks for, and it is not permissible for him to force her to breastfeed for the wage he wants. Ad-Dahhak said: If the wife refuses to breastfeed, he may hire another woman for his child. If she does not accept, his mother may be forced to breastfeed for a wage.
65:7: 7- Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance This is an order to the people of abundance to be generous to their breastfeeding women according to their ability. And whoever is restricted in his provision meaning his provision is sufficient for sustenance, or is restricted but not generous, let him spend from what God has given him meaning from what He has given him of provision, he is not required to do anything else. God does not charge a soul except [with that within] what He has given it meaning what He has given it of provision, so He does not charge the poor person to spend what is not within his ability, rather he is required to do what he is able to do and what he can reach from what God has given him of provision. God will bring about, after hardship, ease meaning after hardship and difficulty, ease and wealth. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Whoever you have, he said, From your abundance, “and do not harm them in order to constrain them,” he said, with regard to housing. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, and if they are pregnant, the verse. He said, “This is about a woman whose husband divorces her while she is pregnant. So God commands him to provide for her and support her until she gives birth, and if she breastfeeds until she is weaned. If he announces her divorce and she is not pregnant, then she is entitled to housing until her waiting period is over, and she is not entitled to support.” Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Abu Sinan, who said, “Umar ibn al-Khattab asked about Abu Ubaydah, and it was said that he wears coarse clothing and eats the coarsest food. So he sent him a thousand dinars and said to the Messenger, ‘Look what he will do with them when he takes them.’ He immediately began to wear the softest clothes and eat the best food. Then the Messenger came and informed him, and he said, ‘May God have mercy on him, interpret this verse as, ‘Let the one with an abundance spend according to his abundance, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend according to what God has given him.’”
65:8: When the Almighty mentioned the aforementioned rulings, He warned against disobeying them, and mentioned the obstinacy of a people who disobeyed His commands, so He inflicted His punishment upon them, saying: 8- And how many a city was insolent toward the command of its Lord and His messengers. That is, it disobeyed, and what is meant is its people, and the meaning is: How many a city’s people disobeyed the command of God and His messengers, or turned away from the command of God and His messengers, with insolent including the meaning of turned away. We have already discussed how many in Surat Al Imran and others. So We brought it to a severe account. That is, We made its people severely accountable for what they did. Muqatil said: God held her accountable for her deeds in this world and punished her with a torment. This is the meaning of His statement: And We punished her with a terrible torment. That is, We punished her people with a great and terrible torment in the Hereafter. It was said that there is an inversion of the original meaning: We punished her people with a terrible torment in this world with hunger, famine, sword, sinkhole, and transformation, and We held them accountable in the Hereafter with a severe accounting. Nakar means the reprehensible.
65:9: 9- So she tasted the evil consequences of her deed meaning the consequences of her disbelief and the outcome of her deed was loss meaning destruction in this world and torment in the hereafter.
65:10: 10- God has prepared for them a severe punishment in the Hereafter, which is the punishment of the Fire. The repetition is for emphasis. So fear God, O you of understanding, meaning, O you of sound minds. His statement, who have believed, is in the accusative case, with the meaning: I mean an explanation of the one being addressed by His statement, O you of understanding, or an explanation apposition to it, or an attribute. God has sent down to you a Reminder * A Messenger. Al-Zajjaj said: The sending down of the Reminder is evidence of the omission of He sent down: meaning, He sent down to you a Qur'an and sent to you a Messenger. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: A Messenger is in the accusative case with the verbal noun, which is a Reminder, because the verbal noun with the definite article works. The meaning is: He sent down to you the Reminder of the Messenger. It was said that a Messenger is a substitute for a Reminder, as if it made the Messenger the Reminder itself as an exaggeration. It was said that it is a substitute for it by deleting an adjective from the first, the meaning being: He sent down that Reminder as a Messenger, or the companion of that Reminder as a Messenger. It was said that Messenger is an adjective with an omitted noun: i.e. a male with a Messenger, so this Messenger is an adjective for the male. It was also said that Messenger is in the accusative case as an inducement, as if he said: Stick to the Messenger. It was also said that the remembrance here means honor, as in His statement: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance and His statement: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people.
65:11: Then He explained this honor by saying: 11- A Messenger. Most of the scholars have stated that what is meant by Messenger here is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Al-Kalbi said: It is Gabriel, and what is meant by mention is the Qur’an, and the meaning differs according to the previous grammatical aspects, as is clear. Then the Almighty described the mentioned Messenger by saying: He recites to you the clear verses of God, meaning that they are clear. The majority read clear in the form of the active participle: meaning the verses clarify to people the rulings they need. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid preferred the first reading, based on the statement: We have made clear to you the verses, ‘that He may bring forth those who have believed and done righteous deeds from darkness into the light.’ The lam is related to recite, meaning that the Messenger who recites the verses may bring forth those who have believed and done righteous deeds from the darkness of misguidance into the light of guidance. It is permissible for the lam to be related to revealed, in which case the one who brings forth would be God, the Exalted. And whoever believes in God and does righteousness, meaning that he combines belief and doing what God has enjoined upon him while avoiding what He has forbidden, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. The majority of scholars read enter him with a dhammah, while Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a nun. The plural of the pronoun in abiding therein forever is based on the meaning of from, and the singular of enters is based on its wording. The phrase God has given him a good provision is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in khaalideen due to overlap, or of the object of enters due to synonymy. The meaning of God has given him a good provision is that He has expanded his provision in Paradise.
65:12: 12- God is He who created seven heavens The noble name is the subject and its predicate is the relative clause with its clause and from the earth the like of them meaning He created from the earth the like of them, meaning seven. There is disagreement about the nature of the layers of the earth. Al-Qatrbi said in his interpretation: There are disagreements about them in two opinions: One of them, which is the opinion of the majority, is that they are seven earths, one above the other, between each earth a distance like that between the heaven and the earth, and in each earth there are inhabitants of God’s creation. Ad-Dahhak said: They are layered over each other without any gap, unlike the heavens. The first is more correct, because the hadiths indicate it in At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i and others. This has been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. He said: And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Zayd, he said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: Whoever takes a handspan of land unjustly, it will be hung around his neck on the Day of Resurrection from seven earths, and so on. What strengthens the opinion of the majority will come at the end of the discussion. The majority read like them in the accusative case in apposition to seven heavens, or in the sense of a verb: that is, and He created from the earth the like of them. Asim, in a narration from him, read it with the nominative case as the subject, and the preposition and noun before it are its predicate. The command descends between them. The sentence is a resumption, and it is possible that it is an attribute of what preceded it, and the command is revelation. Mujahid said: The command descends from the seven heavens to the seven earths. Al-Hasan said: Between each heaven and the earth. Qatada said: In every earth of His earth and heaven of His heavens there is a creation from His creation and a command from His command and a decree from His decree. It was said that between them refers to what is between the lowest earth, which is the lowest, and the seventh heaven, which is the highest. It was said that it is what He manages in them of His wondrous management, so He sends down rain and produces plants, brings about night and day, summer and winter, and creates animals with their different types and forms, transferring them from one state to another. Ibn Kaysan said: This is the scope and breadth of the language, just as death is called the command of God, and the wind and clouds and the like. The majority read the command descends from tanzall and raised the command as the subject. Abu Amr read in a narration from him that it is derived from sending down, and the imperative is in the accusative case as a direct object and the subject is God, the Most High, and the lam in that you may know that God is over all things competent is related to creation, or to descend, or to something that is determined: that is, He did that so that you may know the perfection of His power and His encompassing of things, and this is the meaning of and that God has encompassed all things with knowledge, so nothing of them is outside His knowledge, whatever it may be. The accusative case of knowledge is in the source, because hatat means knew, or it is a preposition for a deleted source: that is, He encompassed with a encompassing knowledge, and it is possible for it to be a distinguishing feature. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: {So We brought them to a severe account}, meaning: They showed no mercy. {And We punished them with a terrible punishment}, meaning: A great and terrible punishment. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority: {God has sent down to you a reminder * A Messenger}, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man said to him: {God is He Who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them} to the end of the surah. Ibn Abbas said: What assures you that I will not tell you about it and you will disbelieve? Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu al-Duha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: {And of the earth the like of them}, he said: Seven earths, in each earth a prophet like your prophet, and an Adam like Adam, and a Noah like Noah, and a Abraham like Abraham, and a Jesus like Jesus. Al-Bayhaqi said: This is a sound chain of transmission, but it is somewhat anomalous. I do not know of anyone who corroborates Abu al-Duha’s report on it. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The two lands, between each land and the one next to it, are a journey of five hundred years. The upper one is on the back of a whale whose two ends meet in the sky, and the whale is on a rock, and the rock is in the hand of an angel. The second is the prison of the wind. When God wanted to destroy ‘Ad, He ordered the keeper of the wind to send a wind upon them to destroy ‘Ad. The keeper of the wind said: ‘O Lord, send upon them a wind the size of a bull’s nostril.’ The tyrant said to him: ‘Then the earth and all that is on it will be overturned. But send upon them the size of a ring. It is the one about which God said in His Book: ‘It does not leave anything it comes upon except that it reduces it to ashes. ’ The third one contains the chamber of Hell, and the fourth one contains the sulfur of Hell. They said: O Messenger of God, does Hell have sulfur? He said: ‘Yes, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, there are valleys in it of sulfur. If He sent firm mountains into them, they would melt. ’” To the end of the hadith. Al-Dhahabi said, commenting on Al-Hakim: It is a rejected hadith. Uthman bin Saeed Al-Darimi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The master of the heavens is the heaven in which the Throne is located, and the master of the earths is the earth in which we are.
66:1: It is twelve verses It was revealed in Medina. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion, it is called Surat Al-Nabi. Ibn Al-Durais, Al-Nahhas, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat At-Tahrim was revealed in Medina. Ibn Mardawayh’s wording is Surat Al-Muharram. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr that he said: Surat An-Nisa was revealed in Medina: O Prophet, why do you prohibit yourself? His saying: 1- O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? There are different opinions about the reason for the revelation of this verse: The first opinion is that of most of the commentators. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in Hafsah’s house when she visited her father. When she returned, she saw Mariah in her house with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She did not enter until Mariah left and then came back in. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw jealousy and sadness on Hafsah’s face, he said to her: Do not tell Aishah, and I promise that I will never come near her again. So Hafsah told Aishah, and they had been on good terms. Aishah became angry and kept nagging the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until he swore that he would not come near Mariah. Then God revealed this Surah. Al-Qurtubi said: Most of the commentators agree that the verse was revealed about Hafsah, and he mentioned the story. It was said that the reason was that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was drinking honey at Zainab bint Jahsh’s house, so Aisha and Hafsa conspired to say to him when he entered upon them, We smell the odor of maghāfir a type of saffron. It was also said that the reason was the woman who offered herself to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The evidence for these sayings will come at the end of the research, God willing, and you will understand how to reconcile them. The phrase seek[ing] the pleasure of your wives is a new sentence, or it explains the saying you forbid, or it is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of you forbid, meaning seeking thereby the pleasure of your wives. Murdāt is a verbal noun, which means contentment, and its root is mardūwah, and it is added to the object, meaning that you please your wives, or to the subject, meaning that they be pleased. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning He is most forgiving and merciful for what you neglected in forbidding what God had made lawful for you. It was said that this was a minor sin, and that is why God rebuked him for it. It was also said that it was a rebuke for abandoning what was better.
66:2: 2- "God has ordained for you the expiation of your oaths" meaning He has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths and made that clear to you. The root of "halala is tahlila" but it was assimilated. It is a verbal noun derived from the verb "ta'ila like tasyadah and tasmiyah", so it is as if an oath is a contract, and expiation is a solution, because it makes permissible for the one who swears to do what he has forbidden to himself. Muqatil said: The meaning is that God has explained the expiation of your oaths in Surat Al-Ma'idah. God commanded His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to expiate his oath and take back his female slave, so he freed a slave. Al-Zajjaj said: No one has the right to forbid what God has permitted. I said: This is the truth, that prohibiting what God has permitted is not binding and is not binding upon its doer. What is permissible and what is forbidden is up to God, the Exalted, and no one else. His rebuke to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this Surah is the most eloquent proof of that. The discussion is lengthy, the schools of thought regarding it are many, and the articles on it are lengthy. We have examined it in our books to satisfactory effect. Scholars differed as to whether merely forbidding something constitutes an oath that requires expiation or not. There is disagreement on this point, and there is nothing in the verse to indicate that it is an oath, because God, the Exalted, rebuked him for forbidding something that He had made permissible for him, then He said: God has already prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths. It was mentioned in the story that most commentators believe was the reason for the revelation of the verse that he first forbade something, then swore a second time, as we mentioned. And God is your Protector, meaning your Guardian, Supporter, and the One in charge of your affairs. And He is the Knowing, of what is best for you and your success. The Wise in His actions and words.
66:3: 3- And when the Prophet confided in one of his wives a statement. Most of the commentators said: It was Hafsah, as mentioned previously, and the statement was about the prohibition of Maria, or honey, or the prohibition of the one who offered herself to him, and the agent in the circumstance is an implied verb: that is, mention when he confided. Al-Kalbi said: He confided in her that your father and Aisha’s father would be my successors over my nation after me. So when she informed of it that is, she told others about it and God made it manifest to him that is, God informed His Prophet of that fact from her of informing others about it. He knew some of it that is, Hafsah knew some of what she had informed him about. The majority read "arfa" with a shaddah from the definite article, while Ali, Talha bin Musarraf, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Kisa'i read it with a tafsir. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose the first reading because of his statement, "And he turned away from some," meaning he did not make it known to her. If it had been with a tafsir, he would have said the opposite: "And he denied some. And he turned away from some," meaning he turned away from defining some of it, not wanting it to spread among the people. It was said that what he turned away from was the hadith of Maria. The commentators have made some confusion and ambiguity here, and each group of them interpreted the definite article and turning away in a way that matches some of what was mentioned in the reason for revelation. We will explain that to you, God willing. "So when He informed her of it, meaning He informed her of what she had divulged of the hadith, She said, 'Who informed you of this?'" meaning who informed you of it. "He said, 'The Knowing, the Aware informed me,'" meaning He from whom nothing is hidden.
66:4: 4- "If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed inclined" The address is to Aisha and Hafsa: that is, if you both repent to God, then He has found in you that which necessitates repentance. The meaning of "inclined" is that they deviated and turned away from the truth, which is that they loved what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) hated, which was spreading talk. It was also said that the meaning is: if you both repent to God, then your hearts have indeed inclined toward repentance. He said "your hearts and did not say your two hearts" because the Arabs dislike combining two dual words in one word. "And if you both support each other against it" means you support each other. The majority read "tathahara" by deleting one of the two ta's for ease. Ikrimah read "tathahara" according to the original. Al-Hasan, Abu Raja’, Nafi’ and Asim, in a narration from them, read it with emphasis on the dhaal and the ha’ without an alif. What is meant by tadhahar is mutual support and cooperation, and the meaning is: If you support and cooperate in being jealous for him and divulging his secret, then indeed, God is his Protector and [so will be] Gabriel and the righteous believers meaning, God will take care of his support, as will Gabriel. And whoever among His believing servants is righteous will not lack a supporter to support him. And the angels after that meaning, after God’s support for him and the support of Gabriel and the righteous believers. A supporter meaning helpers who support him. The angels are the subject and its predicate is supporter. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: Fa’il has been used for pluralism, as in His statement: And no intimate friend will ask a intimate friend. Al-Wahidi said: This is from the singular form that is derived from the plural, as in His statement: And excellent are those as companions. It has been established in the science of grammar that words such as Jareeh wounded, Saboor patient and Dhaheer supporter are used to describe singular, dual and plural. It was said that the dispute between Aisha and Hafsa was about controlling the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in terms of spending.
66:5: 5- Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you all, will give him in exchange wives better than you. That is, He will give him in your place wives better than you. God the Almighty knows that he will not divorce them, but He has informed them of His power that if he divorces them, He will replace them with better ones to frighten them. This is like His statement: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people. This is a statement of His power and a frightening measure for them. Then God the Almighty described the wives by saying: Muslims, believers. That is, those who fulfill the obligations of Islam and believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and in destiny, both the good and the bad. Saeed bin Jubair said: Muslims means sincere. It has also been said that its meaning is: those who submit to the command of God and His Messenger. Obedient means obedient to God. Qanāt means obedience. It has also been said that they pray: Repentant means from sins. Worshipping God and submitting to Him. Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubair said: Women who worship a lot are “saihat meaning fasting. Zaid bin Aslam said: They are emigrants. There is no travel in the nation of Muhammad (peace be upon him) except emigration. Ibn Qutaybah, Al-Farra’ and others said: Fasting was called saihat because the traveler has no provisions with him. It was also said that the meaning is: They go in the obedience of God, from sahah if the water goes. The origin of saihat is roaming on the earth. We have already discussed saihat in Surah At-Tawbah. Thybat and abkaran virgins are separated from each other because of their contradiction. Thybat is the plural of thayyib, which is a woman who has been married and then divorced, so she returns to being as she was, not having a husband. Abkar is the plural of bakr, which means virgin. She was called this because she was in the first state in which she was created. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to stay with Zainab bint Jahsh and drink milk or honey at her place. Hafsa and I advised each other that if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, enters upon any of us, she should say, I detect the odor of maghāfir on you. So he entered upon one of them and she said that to him. He said, No, rather I drank honey at the house of Zainab bint Jahsh and I will not do it again. Then this verse was revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? until His saying: If you both repent to God for Aisha and Hafsa. And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives for his saying: Rather, I drank honey. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. Al-Suyuti said, with a saheeh chain of narration, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) drank a drink of honey at Sawdah’s, and he went to Aisha, and she said: ‘I smell a foul odor from you.’ He went to Hafsa, and she said: ‘I smell a foul odor from you.’ He said: ‘I think it is from a drink I drank at Sawdah’s, and by God, I will never drink it again.’ Then God revealed the verse, ‘O Prophet, why have you forbidden?’” Ibn Sa’d narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rafi’ who said: I asked Umm Salamah about this verse, O Prophet, why have you forbidden? She said: I had a bowl of white honey with me, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to lick some of it and he loved it. Aisha said to him: ‘We have honey that has a strong scent,’ so he forbade it. Then the verse was revealed.” Al-Nasa’i, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had a female slave whom he would have intercourse with. They kept on having intercourse with Aisha and Hafsa until he made her forbidden to him. Then God revealed this verse: ‘O Prophet, why do you forbid?’” Al-Bazzar Al-Tabarani narrated. Al-Suyuti said: With a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I said to Umar ibn Al-Khattab: Who are the two women who declared their divorce? He said: Aisha and Hafsa. The beginning of the hadith was about Mariyah Al-Qibtiyyah, the mother of Ibrahim, whom the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had intercourse with in Hafsa’s house on her day. She found Hafsa and said: O Messenger of God, you have brought me something that you have not brought to any of your husbands on my day or in my turn on my bed. He said: Are you not satisfied that I make her forbidden and never approach her again? She said: Yes. So he forbade her and said: Do not mention that to anyone. So I mentioned it to Aisha and God revealed it to him. Then God revealed: {O Prophet, why do you forbid} all the verses. We have been informed that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) atoned for his oath and had intercourse with Maria. Ibn Sa’d and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from him in a longer version than this. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from another chain of transmission from him in a shorter version. Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from him in an abbreviated version with the wording: He forbade his concubine and made that the reason for revelation in all that was narrated from him through these chains of transmission. Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb narrated in his Musnad and al-Dhiya’ al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtara from the chain of transmission of Nafi’ from Ibn ‘Umar who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Hafsah: Do not tell anyone, for the mother of Ibrahim is forbidden to me.
