She said: Do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? He said: By God, I will not approach her. So he did not approach her until Aisha informed him. Then God revealed: {God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths.} At-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the reason for the revelation of the verse was the prohibition of Maria as mentioned above, but its chain of transmission is weak. So these are two correct reasons for the revelation of the verse, and reconciling them is possible due to the occurrence of the two al-Qasas 28:the story of the honey and the story of Maria, and that the Qur’an was revealed regarding both of them, and in each of them that he confided the conversation to some of his wives. As for what was said that the reason was the prohibition of the woman who offered herself, there is no difference in that except what Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: This verse: {O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?} was revealed regarding the woman who offered herself to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). As-Suyuti said: Its chain of transmission is weak. This also applies to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who did not accept that woman who offered herself to him. How can it be said that the verse O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you was revealed about her? Because if someone rejects what was given to him, it cannot be said that he forbade it for himself. Also, the saying And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives and so on, as God narrated, does not apply to this reason. As for what is proven in the two Sahihs and others, that Ibn Abbas asked Omar bin Al-Khattab about the two women who conspired against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he told him that they were Aisha and Hafsa, then he mentioned the story of the oath as in the long hadith, this does not negate the fact that the reason was what we mentioned about the story of the honey and the story of the concubine, because he only told him about the two women who conspired, and he mentioned in it that the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would return to him and one of them would abandon him day and night, and that this was the reason for seclusion and not the reason for the revelation of O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? This is supported by what we mentioned about Ibn Abbas, who said to Omar, Who were the two women who conspired? So he told him that they were Hafsa and Aisha, and explained to him that the reason was the story of Maria. This is what was possible to summarize the reason for the revelation of the verse, and to remove the differences concerning it, so be firm on it to save yourself from the confusion and mess that occurred to the commentators. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Bukhari, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Indeed, in the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) there is an excellent pattern for you.” Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that a man came to him and said: I have made my wife forbidden to me. He said: You have lied; she is not forbidden to you. Then he recited: Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? He said: Upon you is the most severe expiation, which is the freeing of a slave. Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: When Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend on Mistah, God revealed: God has already prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths, so he absolved his oath and spent on him. Ibn Adi and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Aisha regarding his statement, And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives, she said: He confided in her that Abu Bakr would be my successor after me. Ibn Adi and Abu Nu`aym in Wa al-Sahaba, and al-`Ash`ari in Fada’il as-Siddiq, and Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas who said: By God, the leadership of Abu Bakr and `Umar is in the Book. “And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives,” he said to Hafsah: Your father and the father of Aisha are the rulers of the people after me, so beware of telling anyone about this. I said: This does not indicate that it was the reason for the revelation of his statement, O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? Rather, it indicates that the statement that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) confided was this. Even if we assume that it has a chain of narration that is valid for consideration, it contradicts what was previously mentioned from those authentic narrations, which take precedence over it and are preferred to it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, But your hearts have already deviated, he said: They have deviated and sinned. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: They have deviated. Ibn Asakir narrated from God ibn Buraydah on the authority of his father, regarding His statement: And the righteous believers, he said: Abu Bakr and Umar. Ibn Asakir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Masud. At-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu`aym narrated something similar in Fadhail al-Sahaba from another chain of transmission on his authority. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas. Al-Hakim narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar. As-Suyuti said, with a weak chain of transmission, on the authority of Ali, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, he said: He is Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Asma’ bint Umays, “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘And the righteous believers,’ he said: He is Ali ibn Abi Talib.” Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And the righteous believers, he said: He is Ali ibn Abi Talib. At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Buraydah, regarding His statement: Wives and virgins, he said: God promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this regard that He would marry him to a widow, Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, and to a virgin, Mary, daughter of Imran.
66:6: His statement: 6- O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones by commanding them to obey God and forbidding them from disobeying Him. A Fire whose fuel is people and stones i.e. a great Fire that is kindled by people and stones just as others are kindled by wood. This has been explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: The meaning is protect yourselves and your families from the Fire in the Hereafter with good manners. Muqatil and Mujahid said: Protect yourselves with your actions, and protect your families with your advice. Ibn Jarir said: “We must teach our children religion, goodness, and the indispensable manners. From this is His statement: ‘And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant therein,’ and His statement: ‘And warn your nearest relatives,’ ‘Over it are angels, stern and severe,’ meaning over the Fire are guardians of angels who oversee its affairs and the torture of its people, stern and severe upon the people of the Fire, who do not have mercy on them if they ask for mercy from them, because God Almighty created them from His wrath and made them love the torture of His creation. It was said that what is meant are those who are stern of heart and strong of body, and it was said that they are stern of speech and strong of action, and it was said that the stern are those who are large of body, and the strong are the strong. ‘They do not disobey God in what He commands them,’ meaning they do not [disobey Him] in His command. What is in ‘what He commands them’ may be a relative pronoun with the pronoun omitted: meaning they do not disobey God in what He commanded them to do, and it may be a source: meaning they do not disobey God in His command, provided that what He commanded them is a substitute for inclusion from the noble name, or on the assumption that it is removed.” Al-Khafidh: meaning they do not disobey God in His command. And they do what they are commanded, meaning they perform it on time without delay, neither delaying it nor bringing it forward.
66:7: 7- O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses today meaning this will be said to them when they are brought into the Fire [to make them despair] and to cut off their ambitions You will only be recompensed for what you used to do of deeds in this world. Similar to this is His statement: So on that Day, no excuse will benefit those who did wrong, nor will they be asked to repent.
66:8: 8- O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance. That is, advise its doer to refrain from returning to what he repented from. It is described in this way with a metaphorical attribution, and it is originally a description of the repentant ones to advise themselves to repent by resolving to abandon the sin and refrain from repeating it. Repentance is an obligation on everyone. Qatada said: Sincere repentance is honest, and it was said: pure. Al-Hasan said: Sincere repentance is to hate the sin that one loved and seek forgiveness for it when he remembers it. Al-Kalbi said: Sincere repentance is regret in the heart, seeking forgiveness with the tongue, ceasing with the body, and reassurance that one will not return to it. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the accepted repentance. The majority read Nasoohan with a fatha on the nun as a description of repentance: meaning a repentance that is utterly sincere. Al-Hasan, Kharijah, and Abu Bakr from Asim read it with a damma: meaning a sincere repentance for yourselves. It is permissible for it to be the plural of Naseh or a verbal noun: it is said Nasah praise and Nasoohan sincere. Al-Mubarrad said: He meant sincere repentance, Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, because of that repentance. Although perhaps originally meant to express desire, it is obligatory from God, because the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin. And admits you is conjoined with excuses and is accusative with its accusative, and the majority read it in the accusative. It was read in the jussive mood in conjunction with the place of perhaps, as if he said: Repent, it will require the expiation of your misdeeds and admit you on the Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet. The adverbial phrase is related to enters you: that is, He will admit you on the Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believe with him, and the relative pronoun is conjoined with the Prophet. It was said that the relative pronoun is a subject and its predicate is their light proceeds before them and on their right, and the first is more appropriate, and the phrase their light proceeds would be in the accusative case as a state or renewed to explain their state. It was mentioned in Surat Al-Hadid that the light will be with them when they walk on the bridge. The phrase “They say, ‘Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things able. ’” Something powerful” is also in the accusative case as a state, and on the other hand it is another piece of report. This is the supplication of the believers when God extinguished the light of the hypocrites, as was previously explained and detailed. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding the statement of God, "Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire," that he said: Teach yourselves and your families goodness and discipline them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, that he said: Do what God commands and avoid what God commands and enjoin remembrance upon your families, and God will save you from the Fire. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on his authority, regarding the verse, that he said: Discipline your families. Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa'id al-Zuhd on the authority of Abu Imran al-Joni, that he said: It has reached us that the keepers of the Fire are nineteen, and between the shoulder of one of them is a distance of one hundred autumns' journey. There is no mercy in their hearts, but they were created for punishment. The angel among them will strike a man from the people of the Fire with a single blow, leaving him ground from his head to his feet. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, Ibn Mani`, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of al-Nu`man ibn Bashir that Umar ibn al-Khattab was asked about sincere repentance. He said: It is for a man to repent from a bad deed and never return to it again. Ahmad, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Repentance from a sin is for a man to repent from it and never return to it again. In its chain of transmission is Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri, who is weak. The authentic hadith is mawquf, as it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi. al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he said: Sincere repentance expiates every bad deed. This is in the Qur’an, and then he recited this verse. Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: On the Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believe with him, their light will proceed (Al-Ba’th: 117), he said: There is no one among the monotheists who will not be given light on the Day of Resurrection. As for the hypocrite, his light will be extinguished, and the believer will be afraid of what he saw of the hypocrite’s light being extinguished, so he will say: Our Lord, perfect for us our light.
66:9: His statement: 9- O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites meaning with the sword and argument. We have already discussed this verse in Surat Bara’ah. And be harsh upon them meaning be strict with them in calling them to Islam and use harshness in ordering them to follow the Shari’ah. Al-Hasan said: meaning strive against them by implementing the prescribed punishments on them, for they were committing crimes that warrant the prescribed punishments. And their refuge is Hell meaning their destination is it: meaning the disbelievers and the hypocrites. And wretched is the destination meaning the place of return to which they will return.
66:10: 10- God sets forth an example for those who disbelieve. It has been mentioned more than once that an example may be intended to present a strange situation by which another similar situation is known in strangeness: that is, God made an example for the condition of these disbelievers, and that no one can replace another. The wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. This is the first object, and an example is the second object according to what we have already explained, but it was delayed to connect to it what explains and clarifies its meaning. They were under two of Our righteous servants, namely Noah and Lot: that is, they were under the protection of their marriage. But they betrayed them, that is, they betrayed them. Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: by disbelief. It was also said that Noah's wife used to tell the people that he was crazy, and Lot's wife used to inform his people about his guests. There is a consensus that no prophet's wife ever committed adultery. It was also said that their betrayal was hypocrisy. It was said that they betrayed them with gossip, But it did not avail them at all against God, meaning that Noah and Lot did not benefit them at all because they were two wives, nor did they ward off God’s punishment due to their honor with God. And it was said, ‘Enter the Fire with those who enter,’ meaning that it was said to them in the Hereafter, or upon their death, Enter the Fire with those who enter from among the disbelievers and sinners. Yahya ibn Salam said: God set forth an example for those who disbelieved, warning Aisha and Hafsa against disobeying the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when they conspired against him. How well said it! Mentioning the wives of the prophets after mentioning their story and their conspiring against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) provides the most complete guidance and most eloquent indication that the intention was to frighten them along with the rest of the mothers of the believers. And it is clear that even though they were under the protection of the best of God’s creation and the Seal of His Messengers, that did not avail them anything from God, and God protected them from the sin of that demonstration by the true and sincere repentance that they had undertaken.
66:11: 11- “And God presents an example to those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh.” This is similar to the previous example: that is, God made the situation of Pharaoh’s wife an example for the believers, encouraging them to remain steadfast in obedience, adhere to the religion, and be patient in times of hardship. They say that the violence of disbelief will not harm them, just as it did not harm Pharaoh’s wife, who had been under the control of the most disbelieving of disbelievers. Through their faith in God, they entered the Gardens of Bliss. When she said, ‘My Lord, build for me, near You, a house in Paradise.’ The adverbial phrase is related to strike or example. That is, build for me a house close to Your mercy, or in the highest degree of those close to You, or in a place where no one can do anything except with Your permission, which is Paradise. And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, that is, from himself and the evil deeds he committed. And save me from the wrongdoing people. Al-Kalbi said: They are the people of Egypt. Muqatil said: They are the Copts. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: God saved her in the most honorable way and raised her to Paradise, so she eats and drinks.
66:12: 12- And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity is in apposition to the wife of Pharaoh: meaning, God presents an example to those who believe, Mary, the daughter of Imran: meaning, her condition and description. It was said that the verb that precedes Mary is understood as an accusative: meaning, And remember Mary. The purpose of mentioning her is that God, the Exalted, combined for her the honor of this world and the Hereafter and chose her over the women of the worlds, despite her being among a disbelieving people. Who guarded her chastity meaning from indecencies. The explanation of this has been presented in Surat An-Nisa. The commentators said: What is meant by the chastity here is the bosom, as God says: Then We breathed into it of Our spirit meaning that Gabriel breathed into the bosom of her garment and she became pregnant with Jesus. And she believed in the words of her Lord meaning His laws that He legislated for His servants. It was said that what is meant by the words here is Gabriel’s saying to her, I am only the Messenger of your Lord verse. Muqatil said: What is meant by the words is Jesus. The majority of scholars read and you believed with emphasis, while Hamza Al-Umawi, Ya'qub, Qatadah, Abu Majlaz, and Asim, in one narration from him, read it with emphasis. The majority of scholars read with words with the plural, while Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Al-Jahdary read with a word with the singular. The majority of scholars read and his books with the singular, while the people of Basra and Hafs read his books with the plural. According to the majority of scholars, what is meant is the gender, so it is in the plural sense, and they are the books revealed to the prophets. And she was of the devout Qatadah said: Of the people who obey their Lord. Ata' said: Of the praying ones, she used to pray between Maghrib and Isha'. It is possible that the devout refers to her relatives and clan, from whom she was a member, and they were obedient people of a righteous and obedient household. He said: Of the devout ones, and he did not say of the devout ones because of the predominance of males over females. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, and they betrayed them, that he said: They did not commit adultery. As for the betrayal of Noah’s wife, she used to say to the al-Nas 114:He is crazy. As for the betrayal of Lot’s wife, she used to guide the guest, that was their betrayal. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: He said: No prophet’s wife ever betrayed anyone. Ibn `Asakir narrated it with a chain of narration from the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu`ab narrated on the authority of Salman, who said: The wife of Pharaoh was tortured by the sun, but when they left her, the angels would shade her with their wings, and she would see her house in Paradise. Abd bin Humaid narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that Pharaoh pegged his wife with four pegs, made her lie on her chest, and placed a millstone on her chest, facing her towards the sun. She raised her head to the sky and said, My Lord, build for me, near You, a house in Paradise, until His saying, from the wrongdoers. So God made her house available to her in Paradise and she saw it. Ahmad, Al-Tabarani and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “The best women of Paradise are Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, Fatimah bint Muhammad, Maryam bint Imran and Asiyah bint Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh, along with what God has told us of her story in the Qur’an. She said, “My Lord, build for me, near You, a house” verse. In the two Sahihs and others, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Many men attained perfection, but none attained perfection among women except Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, Maryam bint Imran and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. The superiority of Aisha over other women is like the superiority of tharid over all other foods.” And Wakee’ narrated in Al-Ghurar on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, he said: from his group.
67:1: It is called Surat Tabarak, Al-Waqiyah, Al-Munjiyyah, and Al-Maniyah, and it has thirty verses. It is a Meccan surah. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion. Ibn Ad-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Surah Tabarak Al-Mulk was revealed in Mecca. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Ad-Durais, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is a surah from the Book of God that is only thirty verses long that interceded for a man until he was forgiven: ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion.’” At-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith. At-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ad-Diya’ in Al-Mukhtara on the authority of Anas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is a surah in the Qur’an that argued over its reciter until it admitted him into Paradise: ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion.’” At-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Nasr, and Al-Bayhaqi in Ad-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “One of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pitched his tent over a grave, not realizing it was a grave. Then, there was a grave of a man who was reciting Surat Al-Mulk until he completed it. He came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘It is the protector, it is the savior. It will save him from the punishment of the grave.’” At-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: This is a strange hadith with this chain of transmission. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Tabarak is the protector from the punishment of the grave. An-Nasa’i also narrated it, who authenticated it, and Al-Hakim. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Rafi’ ibn Khadij and Abu Hurayrah that they heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “Surat Tabarak was revealed to me, and it consists of thirty verses all at once. It is the protector in the graves.” Abd ibn Humayd narrated in his Musnad, as well as At-Tabarani, Al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said to a man: Shall I not entertain you with a hadith that will make you happy? He said: Yes. He said: Read Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion and teach it to your family, all your children, the boys in your house, and your neighbors. For it is the savior and the debater. It will argue on the Day of Resurrection before its Lord for its reader, and ask that God save him from the torment of the Fire and save its reciter from the torment of the grave. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I would like it to be in the heart of every person of my nation. His saying: 1- Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion. Tabarak is a verbal noun derived from barakah blessing, and barakah means growth and increase. It was also said that He is exalted and glorified above the attributes of created beings. It was also said that He is eternal, meaning He has no beginning or end to His existence. Al-Hasan said: Tabarak is sanctified. The verbal noun is for emphasis, and hand is a metaphor for power and control. The dominion is the dominion of the heavens and the earth in this world and the hereafter. He honors whomever He wills and humiliates whomever He wills, raises whomever He wills and abases whomever He wills. It was also said that what is meant by dominion is the dominion of prophethood, and the first is more appropriate because applying it generally is more praiseworthy and eloquent, and there is no point in specifying it. And He has power over all things, meaning He is of supreme power, nothing is beyond His power. He disposes of His dominion as He wishes, from bestowing favors and vengeance to raising, lowering, giving, and withholding.
67:2: 2- Who created death and life. Death is the severing of the connection of the soul to the body and its separation from it. Life is the connection of the soul to the body and its contact with it. It was said that it is that which can be sensed, and it was said that it is that which necessitates a thing to be alive, and it was said that what is meant is death in this world and life in the hereafter. Death was mentioned before life because the origin of things is the absence of life, and life is incidental to them. It was also said that death is closer to subjugation. Muqatil said: He created death: meaning the sperm, the embryo, and the clot, and life means He created him as a human being and created the soul in him. It was said that He created death in the form of a ram that does not pass by anything without dying, and He created life in the form of a horse that does not pass by anything without coming back to life. This was said by Muqatil and Al-Kalbi. It was mentioned in the Qur’an, Say, ‘The Angel of Death who is set over you will take you’ and His statement, And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve and His statement, Our messengers take them and His statement, God takes the souls at the time of their death and other verses, To test you which of you is best in deed. The lam is related to creation: meaning, He created death and life to treat you as one who tests you to see which of you is best in deed, so He may reward you accordingly. It was also said that the meaning is: To test you which of you remembers death the most and fears it the most. It was also said that which of you is the quickest to obey God and the most wary of what God has forbidden. Al-Zajjaj said: The lam is related to the creation of life, not the creation of death. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra’ also said: His statement, to test you does not use the verb any, because between test and any there is an implied verb, as you say: I tested you to see which of you is most obedient. Similar to this is his statement, Ask them which of them is responsible for that, meaning ask them, then see which of them. So which of you in the verse is the subject and predicate, which is better, because the question does not have what precedes it affect it. And the use of the comparative form, even though the test includes all of their deeds, which are divided into good and bad, not just into good and best, is to indicate that what is meant by the essence and the original purpose of the test is to reveal the perfection of the goodness of the doers of good. And He is the Exalted in Might, meaning the Victorious Who is not defeated, the Forgiving for whoever repents and returns.
67:3: 3- Who created seven heavens in layers. The relative pronoun may be an adjective, a clarification, or a substitute for the Almighty, the Forgiving, and it may be disconnected from it as a predicate of a deleted subject, or accusative of praise, and tabaqan is an adjective for seven heavens: meaning some of them are above others, and it is the plural of nature like mountain and mountains, or the plural of layer like spaciousness and spaciousness, or the source of tabaq, it is said: tabaq mutabahaqan and tabaqan, and in this way the description is with the source for emphasis or with the deletion of an added word: meaning having layers, and it may be accusative as a source with a deleted verb, meaning stacked in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Gracious any discrepancy. This sentence is a second adjective for seven heavens or a resumption to confirm what came before it, and the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone who is suitable for it, and min is added to emphasize the negation. The majority read it as min tatafawāl while Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it as tafawāl with a shaddah without an alif. These are two dialects: like ta'ahud and ta'ahudh, and tahamul and tahamul. The meaning in both readings is: You do not see in the creation of the Most Gracious any contradiction, discrepancy, crookedness or inconsistency. Rather, it is level and upright, indicating its Creator. Although its forms and descriptions differ, they are the same in this respect. Then return your gaze; do you see any futur? The futur means the cracks, fissures and breaches. That is, return your gaze until it becomes clear to you through observation. He first informed that there is no discrepancy in His creation, then he ordered the recurrence of the gaze in this to increase emphasis and attain reassurance. Mujahid said: Ad-Dahhak said: The futur is shuqūq, the plural of fatr, which is a cleft. Qatadah said: Do you see any flaw? As-Suddi said: Do you see any khuruq? Its root is from taftar and infitar, which means cracking and splitting. From this comes the saying of the poet: He built for you the sky without pillars and adorned it, and there is nothing in it but faults. And the other said: I split the heart and then put your love back in it, so why is the breakfast complete?
67:4: 4- "Then look again" means twice, time after time. The accusative is in the verbal noun, and the meaning of dual is repetition, as in "Labbaik and sa'dayk", meaning one look after another, even if it is repeated. The reason for the command to look again in this manner is that one may not see what one thinks is a fault in the first or second look. This is why He said first, "What inconsistency do you see in the creation of the Most Gracious? Then He said second, Then look again. Then He said thirdly, Then look again a second time." This is more effective in establishing the argument and more conclusive for the excuse. "The sight will return to you humbled." That is, the sight will return to you humiliated and subdued, unable to see any of that. It was said that the meaning of "shattered" is: distant and banished from seeing what it perceived as a fault. It is said, "I banished the dog," meaning I distanced it and drove it away. The majority of scholars read "will turn back" in the jussive mood as an answer to the command. Al-Kisa’i read in a narration with the nominative case as a resumption of and he is exhausted meaning tired and exhausted. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning he was exhausted before he saw a defect in the sky. It is a fa’il with the meaning of fa’il from hasur, which means exhaustion. It is said: he has lowered his sight, yahsir hasuran: meaning he is tired and exhausted. From this comes the saying of the poet: I looked at her in the pebbles of Mina, and he looked back at me, disappointed.
67:5: 5- And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps God Almighty explained after creating the heavens and making them free from defect and flaw that He adorned them with this adornment, so they became in the best creation, most perfect image and most delightful form. The oath is brought to highlight the perfection of care. Lamps is the plural of lamp, which is a lamp. The planets are called lamps because they shine like the illumination of a lamp. Some of the planets, even if they are in a heaven other than the nearest heaven, appear as if they are all in the nearest heaven, because the heavenly bodies do not prevent seeing what is above them that has illumination, because they are polished, transparent bodies. And We have made them missiles for the devils meaning We made the lamps missiles with which the devils are pelted. This is another benefit besides the first benefit, which is that they are an adornment for the nearest heaven. The meaning is that the devils are pelted with them to eavesdrop. Ramjoom is the plural of Rajm with the fat-ha, and it is originally a verbal noun that refers to what is pelted with, as in their saying: The dirham was struck by the prince, meaning its strike. It is permissible for it to remain as a verbal noun and for it to be an added noun. Deleted: meaning of stoning, and the source is plural based on its types. It was said that the pronoun in His statement: And We made it refers back to the lamps with the deletion of an added word: meaning its meteors, which is its fire taken from it, not it itself, according to His statement: Except he who snatches a snatch, and is pursued by a piercing flame. The reason for this is that the lamps with which God adorned the lowest heaven do not disappear and are not stoned. This is what Abu Ali al-Farisi said in answer to someone who asked him: How can the lamps be an adornment while they are stones? Al-Qushayri said: And more exemplary than this statement is to say: They are an adornment before the devils are stoned with them. Qatada said: God created the stars for three purposes: to adorn the sky, to missiles target the devils, and as signs to guide people on land and sea. Whoever speaks about them in any other way has spoken about them without knowledge, has transgressed and been unjust. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: And We made them as conjectures for the devils among mankind, who are the astrologers. And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze, meaning, We have prepared for the devils in the Hereafter, after they are burned in this world by meteors, the punishment of the Blaze, meaning the punishment of the Fire. The Blaze is the most intense burning. It is said that the fire is blazing, so it is raging.
67:6: 6- And for those who disbelieve in their Lord from among the disbelievers of the children of Adam, or from among the disbelievers of both groups, is the punishment of Hell. The majority of scholars read punishment in the nominative case as the subject and predicate of for those who disbelieve. Al-Hasan, Al-Dahhak, and Al-A’raj read it in the accusative case as an apposition to the punishment of the Blaze. “And wretched is the destination” is what they will end up to, which is Hell.
67:7: 7- When they are thrown into it meaning they are thrown into it as wood is thrown into fire they will hear from it a sighing meaning a sound like the sound of donkeys when they first bray, which is the ugliest of sounds. His saying to it is in the accusative case as a state: meaning existing for it, because it is originally an adjective, but when it was brought forward it became a state. Ata’ said: The sighing is from the disbelievers when they are thrown into the fire, and the phrase while it is boiling is in the accusative case as a state: meaning while it is boiling with them like a boiling cauldron. From this is the saying of Hassan: You left your pot with nothing in it, while the donkey's pot was boiling and seething.
67:8: 8- It almost bursts apart from rage meaning it almost bursts apart from the rage it feels towards them. Ibn Qutaybah said: It almost bursts apart from the rage it feels towards the disbelievers. The majority of scholars read tamyaz with one light taa', while the original is tamyaz with two taa's. Talhah read it with two taa's according to the original. Al-Bazzi read it on the authority of Ibn Kathir with a shaddah by assimilating one taa' into the other. Ad-Dahhak read it with an alif and one ta’, and the original is tamatayiz. Zayd ibn Ali read it with tamayiz from maza yamiz. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state, or in the nominative case as another predicate of a subject. The sentence Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them is a resumption to explain the state of its people, or in the accusative case as a state of the agent of tamayiz. The group is a group of al-Nas 114:that is, whenever a group of disbelievers are thrown into Hell, their keepers from the angels will ask them a question of rebuke and reprimand. Did there not come to you in this world a warner warning you of this Day and cautioning you against it.
67:9: And the sentence 9 - "They said, 'Yes, a warner has come to us'" is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said: So what did they say after this question? He said: They said, 'Yes, a warner has come to us, so he warned us and frightened us and informed us of this Day. 'But we denied' that warner 'and said, "God has not sent down anything" of the things on your tongues. 'You are only in great error', meaning in going astray from the truth and far from the right path. The meaning is that he said: Every group of you is telling the keepers of Hell what he said to the one to whom he was sent: What are you, O messengers, in what you claim that God has sent down to you verses with which you warn us, except in going astray from the truth and far from the right path, a great amount that cannot be measured.
67:10: Then he narrated another statement they said after that statement, saying: 10- And they said, ‘If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.’ That is, if we had been listening to what the messengers addressed to us, or reasoning about any of it, we would not have been among the people of the Fire, and among those who will be tormented in the Blaze, namely the devils, as mentioned previously. Al-Zajjaj said: If we had been listening as one who understands, or reasoning as one who discerns and sees, we would not have been among the people of the Fire.
67:11: When they confessed this confession, God the Almighty said: 11- So they acknowledged their sin for which they deserved the punishment of the Fire, which is disbelief and denial of the prophets. So, away with the companions of the Blaze! meaning, far with them from God and His mercy. Sa'id bin Jubayr and Abu Salih said: It is a valley in Hell called Al-Sahaq. The majority read Fasahaqan with a sukoon on the ha'. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Ja'far read it with a damma, and they are two dialects like saht and ar'ab. Al-Zajjaj and Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: Fasahaqan is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning, God crushed them completely. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: The analogy was Ishaq, so the verbal noun came with the deletion, and the lam in for the companions of the Blaze is for clarification as in Hayt lak. Abd bin Hamid narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Seven heavens in layers, he said: One above the other. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement, You do not see in the creation of the Most Gracious any discrepancy, he said: It does not miss some of it with scattered discrepancies. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him regarding his statement, Of the discrepancies, he said: Of the crack. And regarding his statement, Do you see any crack? he said: Cracks. And regarding his statement, Disgraced, he said: Abasement. And he is weary, he said: Weak and exhausted. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him. He said: The crack is the weak. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him. Of the crack, he said: Of the crack or defect. And regarding his statement, The sight turns back to you, he said: It returns to you. Disgraced, he said: Abasement. And he is weary, he said: Weak and does not see anything. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him. Disgraced, he said: Abasement. And he is weary, he said: Weak and returned. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, It almost separates, meaning it disperses. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority, It almost separates, meaning it separates from one another. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, So be destroyed, meaning it is far away.
67:12: His statement: 12- Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen When the Almighty finished mentioning the conditions of the people of Hell, He mentioned the people of Paradise. Unseen is a state of the subject or the object: that is, absent from Him, or absent from them. The meaning is that they fear His punishment even though they have not seen Him, so they believe in Him out of fear of His punishment. It is possible that the meaning is: they fear their Lord while they are absent from the eyes of people, and that is in their seclusion, or what is meant by unseen is that the punishment is hidden from them because they are in this world, and they will only be on the Day of Resurrection. So the ba in this case is causal. For them is forgiveness is great, with which God forgives their sins, and a great reward, which is Paradise. Similar to this verse is His statement: Whoever fears the Most Merciful unseen.
67:13: Then the Almighty returned to addressing the disbelievers, saying: 13- Whether you conceal your speech or declare it aloud. This sentence is a new beginning, intended to explain the equivalence of concealment and declaration in relation to the knowledge of God Almighty. The meaning is: Whether you conceal your speech or declare it aloud in the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then all of that is known to God, and nothing of it is hidden from Him. The sentence He is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts is an explanation for the aforementioned equivalence, and what is in the breasts is what is hidden in the hearts.
67:14: The question in His statement: 14- Does He not know who created? is for denial, and the meaning is: Does He not know the secret and the hidden thoughts of the hearts of who created that and brought it into existence? The relative pronoun is an expression for the Creator, and it is permissible for it to be an expression for the creation, and in knows there is a pronoun that refers to God: that is, does God not know the creation that is part of His creation? For the secrets and the public and the hidden thoughts of the hearts are part of His creation. And the phrase And He is the Subtle, the Expert is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of knows: that is, He whose knowledge of what is in the hearts is subtle, the Expert of what they conceal and hide of matters, nothing of that is hidden from Him.
67:15: Then He, the Almighty, bestowed His favor upon His servants, saying: 15- It is He who made the earth submissive to you, meaning easy and soft for you to settle on, and He did not make it rough so that it is impossible for you to rest or walk on it. Submissive in origin means that which is obedient and humbles itself to you and does not find it difficult for you. The source is humiliation, and the fa in His statement: walk in its paths is to arrange the command to walk according to the aforementioned making, and the command is for permission. Mujahid, Al-Kalbi, and Muqatil said: Its paths are its roads, edges, and sides. Qatadah and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: Its paths are its mountains. The origin of the word mankab is the side, and from it comes the word mankab shoulder, and from it comes the wind nakba, because it comes from one side and not the other. And eat of His provision, meaning from what He has provided for you and created for you on the earth. And to Him is the resurrection, meaning and to Him is the resurrection from your graves, not to any other place. And in this is a severe threat.
67:16: Then He, glory be to Him, frightened the disbelievers. He said: 16- Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you up? Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: It means the punishment of He who is in the heaven. It was said that He who is in the heaven is His power, authority, throne, and angels. It was also said that He who is in the heaven is the angels. It was also said that it means Gabriel. The meaning of that He will cause the earth to swallow you up is that He will uproot it while it is covered with you, as He did with Qarun after He made it subservient to you, walking in its paths. His statement: that He will cause the earth to swallow up is a budāl ishtmal of the relative pronoun: that is, do you feel secure that He will cause the earth to swallow you up? Or it is an omission of min: that is, that He will cause the earth to swallow you up. Then suddenly it is in turmoil means it is agitated and moves in a state other than its state of stillness. The majority of scholars read a'mantum with two hamzas. The Basrans and Kufians read it with a light pronoun. Ibn Kathir read it by changing the first to a waw.
67:17: Then the Almighty repeated the threat to them in another way, saying: 17- Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send upon you a storm of stones? That is, stones from the sky, as He sent them upon the people of Lot and the companions of the elephant. It was also said that it was a cloud with stones in it, and it was also said that it was a wind with stones in it. Then you will know how My warner is. That is, My warning if you suffer the punishment and this knowledge does not benefit you. It was also said that the warner here is Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him. This was said by Ata’ and Ad-Dahhak. The meaning is: You will know My Messenger and his truthfulness, and the first is more appropriate. The statement that He will not send upon you a storm of stones is like the statement in that He will cause the earth to swallow you up. It is either a substitute for inclusion, or an estimation of from.
67:18: 18- And those before them denied meaning those before the disbelievers of Mecca from the disbelievers of the past nations, such as the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, the people of Lot, the companions of the thicket, the companions of the messengers, and the people of Pharaoh. So how was My reproach meaning how was My reproach to them for the terrible punishment I inflicted upon them.
67:19: 19- Have they not seen the birds above them with wings spread out? The hamza is for interrogation and the waw is for conjunction with an implied meaning: they were heedless and did not look. The meaning of with wings spread out is that they spread their wings in the air and [flatten them] when they fly. And they fold means they close their wings. An-Nahhas said: When a bird spreads its wings, it is said to be spread out, and when it folds them, it is said to be folded, as if it is folding them. This is the meaning of flying, which is spreading the wing and folding it after spreading it. From this, Abu Kharash said: The night takes the initiative, as it is moving under the wing, spreading out and contracting. Rather, He said: And they grasp and did not say they grasp as He said they spread out, because grasping is renewed sometimes and sometimes, while spreading out is the original, as it was said. And it was said that the meaning of and they grasp is their grasping their wings when stopping from flying, not grasping them while flying. The phrase None holds them up except the Most Gracious is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of they grasp, or it is a new sentence to clarify the perfection of the power of God, the Most High. The meaning is: None holds them up in the air when flying except the Most Gracious, who is able to do all things. Indeed, He is All-Seeing of all things, nothing is hidden from Him, whatever it may be.
67:20: 20- Is this he who is your army to aid you other than the Most Merciful? The question is for rebuke and rebuke, and the meaning is that you have no army to protect you from God’s punishment, and the army is the party and the protection. The majority read amn with a shaddah on the mim because of the assimilation of the mim of am into the mim of min, and am means bal, and there is no way to estimate the hamza after it as is the common practice in estimating the disconnected am with bal and the hamza, because after it here is the interrogative min, so that estimation is unnecessary. The interrogative min is the subject and the demonstrative pronoun is its predicate, and the relative pronoun with its clause is an attribute of the demonstrative pronoun, and yansurkum is an attribute of jund, and min dun ar-Rahman is in the accusative case as a state of the agent of yansurkum, and the meaning is: Rather, from this insignificant one who is, in your opinion, an army for you, exceeding the victory of the Most Merciful. Talha bin Masraf read it with a light mim and a heavy mim of the second, and the phrase the disbelievers are only in delusion is parenthetical, confirming what came before it, denouncing them for what they are in of misguidance, and the meaning is: the disbelievers are only in great delusion on the part of Satan who deceives them with it.
67:21: 21- Is it He who provides for you, if He were to withhold His provision? The discussion of this is like the discussion of the previous one in reading and parsing: that is, who is He who provides you with provisions from rain and other things, if God were to withhold that from you and prevent it from you? Rather, they persisted in insolence and aversion. That is, they were not affected by that, rather they persisted in their stubbornness and arrogance towards the truth and their aversion to it, and they did not consider or think. The answer to the condition is omitted because what preceded it indicates it: that is, if He were to withhold His provision, then who would provide for you other than Him? Insolence is stubbornness and tyranny, and aversion is straying. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen, he said: Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, and Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement, in its slopes, he said: its mountains. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority, he said: its edges. At-Tabarani, Ibn Adi, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’b, and Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: God loves the faithful, professional servant. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Rather, they persist in insolence and aversion, he said: in misguidance.
67:22: God the Almighty set forth an example of the polytheist and the monotheist to clarify their condition and explain their outcome, saying: 22- Is one who walks prone on his face better guided? The one who is prone and the one who is prone is the one who falls on his face. It is said: I threw him over so he fell and fell. It was also said that it is the one who lowers his head and does not look right, left, or forward, so he is not safe from stumbling and falling on his face. It was also said that it refers to the blind person who cannot find his way and his walking keeps turning him on his face. Qatada said: He is the disbeliever who falls on his face disobeying God in this world, so God will gather him on the Day of Resurrection on his face. The hamza is for rhetorical questioning: that is, is the one who walks on his face better guided to the destination he wants? Or the one who walks upright straight, looking at what is in front of him on a straight path that is, on a level road with no crookedness or deviation in it? The predicate of min is omitted because the predicate of min of the first is more guided to it. It was said that there is no need for that, because min of the second is conjoined with min of the first, conjoining a singular to a singular, like you saying, Is Zaid standing or Amr? It was said that what is meant by the one who walks prone on his face is the one who will be herded on his face to the Fire, and the one who walks upright is the one who will be herded on his feet to Paradise. This is like the statement of Qatadah that we mentioned, and similar to it is His statement, And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces.
67:23: 23- Say, ‘It is He who created you.’ God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform them that God is the One who created them in the first creation. And made for them hearing so that they might hear, and sight so that they might see. The reason for singling out hearing while using the plural of sight is that it is a verbal noun that can be used for both little and much. We have already explained this in other places with more explanation. And hearts are the hearts with which they contemplate God’s creations. So here God the Almighty mentioned that He has given them that by which they can perceive what is heard, seen, and understood, to clarify the argument, cut off the excuse, and rebuke them for not being grateful for God’s blessings. For this reason He said, You give little thanks. The word little is in the accusative case as an adjective for a deleted verbal noun, and what is added for emphasis: meaning, give little thanks or for a little time. It was said that what He meant by little thanks is the absence of it from them. Muqatil said: It means that you do not thank the Lord of these blessings and thus unify Him.
67:24: 24- Say, ‘It is He who has dispersed you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.’ God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform them that God is the One who created them on the earth, spread them out therein, and dispersed them over its surface, and that He will gather them for recompense to Him, not to anyone else.
67:25: Then the Almighty mentioned that they are hastening the punishment, saying: 25- And they say, 'When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?' That is, when will this promise that you mention to us of the gathering, the Resurrection, the Fire, and the punishment come to pass, if you are truthful in that? The address from them is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers who were with him, and the answer to the condition is omitted, and the meaning is, if you are truthful, then inform us of it or explain it to us. This is mockery and ridicule from them.
67:26: Then when they said this statement, God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to respond to them, saying: 26- Say, ‘Knowledge is only with God.’ That is, the knowledge of the time of the Hour is with God, and no one else knows it. Similar to this is His saying: Say, ‘The knowledge thereof is only with my Lord.’ Then He informed them that he was sent to warn, not to inform of the unseen, saying: I am only a clear warner. I warn you and frighten you of the consequences of your disbelief, and I explain to you what God has commanded me to explain.
67:27: Then God the Almighty mentioned their condition when they witnessed the punishment, saying: 27- So when they saw it approaching meaning they saw the punishment close. Zalfa is a verbal noun meaning the subject: i.e. approaching or a state of the object of ra'aw with the estimation of an added word: i.e. of proximity and nearness. Or a circumstance: i.e. they saw it in a place of proximity. Mujahid said: i.e. close. Al-Hasan said: clearly. Most of the commentators said: what is meant is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: what is meant is the punishment of Badr. It was also said that they saw what they were promised of the punishment close to them, as indicated by His statement: And to Him you will be gathered. It was also said that when they saw their evil deeds close, the faces of those who disbelieved will be made ugly meaning they will be blackened and covered with gloom and humiliation. It is said that something becomes ugly, meaning it is bad, meaning it is bad. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that evil became apparent therein: that is, that torment distressed them, so that what indicated their disbelief appeared on their faces because of it, like His statement, {On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black.} The majority of scholars read it with a kasra on the seen without ishmām. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, Al-Kisa’i and Ibn Muhaysin read it with ishmām. And it will be said, ‘This is that for which you used to call,’ meaning, it will be said to them as a rebuke and a rebuke. This present, visible torment is the torment for which you used to call in this world, meaning, you used to ask for it and hasten it in mockery. The meaning of call is supplication. Al-Farra’ said: You call upon from supplication means you wish and ask, and this is what most of the commentators said. Al-Zajjaj said: This is that for which you used to call upon falsehoods and hadiths. It was said that the meaning of call upon is you lie. This is according to the reading of the majority of scholars, call upon with a shaddah. It is either from supplication, as most said, or from ja’wā as Al-Zajjaj and those who agreed with him said. The meaning is that they used to claim that there is no resurrection, no gathering, no Paradise, and no Hell. Qatada, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Yaqub, and Ad-Dahhak readتاُدونin a lightened form, and its meaning is clear. Qatada said: It is their saying, Our Lord, hasten our portion for us. Ad-Dahhak said: It is their saying, O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, the verse. An-Nahhas said: Taddu and Taddu'un have the same meaning, just as you say qaddar and iqtaddar, and ghadda and ghada, except that af'al means something that has passed one thing after another, and fa'al can be used for both little and much.
67:28: 28- “Say, ‘Have you considered: if God should destroy me and those with me, or have mercy on us and not punish us, then who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?’” That is, who can prevent them and secure them from the punishment? The meaning is that no one can save them from that, whether God destroys His Messenger and the believers with him, as the disbelievers had hoped, or He gives them respite. It has also been said that the meaning is: We are, with our faith, between fear and hope, so who can protect you, with your disbelief, from the punishment? The explicit word was used in place of the implicit word to accuse them of disbelief and to clarify that it is the reason for their failure to be saved.
67:29: 29- "Say, 'He is the Most Gracious. We have believed in Him'" alone, associating no partner with Him. And upon Him we have relied not on anyone else. Reliance means entrusting matters to Him, the Almighty and Majestic: Then you will know who is in manifest error from among us and from you. This is a severe threat while conveying the statement in a fair manner. The majority of scholars read you will know with the superlative as an address. Al-Kisa'i read it with the subjunctive as a predicate.
67:30: Then the Almighty argued with them about some of His blessings, and frightened them by taking that blessing away from them, saying: 30- Say, ‘Have you considered if your water were to become sunken in?’ That is, tell me if your water were to sink into the ground to the point that it no longer exists in it at all, or it were to go into the ground to a faraway place such that buckets could not reach it. It is said that the water sunken in means it dried up, and sunken is a description with a verbal noun for emphasis, just as it is said a just man. Something similar to this was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Kahf. Then who can bring you flowing water? That is, apparent, visible to the eyes, and reachable to the buckets. It was said that it is from the meaning of water, meaning abundant. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: flowing. The meaning of flowing was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Mu’min. Ibn Abbas recited: Then who can bring you fresh water? Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Is one who walks prone? He said: In misguidance. Is one who walks upright? He said: Guided. Al-Khatib narrated in his history and Ibn al-Najjar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever has a toothache, let him place his finger on it and recite this verse: ‘It is He who produced you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts. Little do you give thanks.’” Al-Daraqutni narrated in al-Afrad on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever has a toothache, let him place his finger on it and recite these two verses seven times: ‘And it is He who produced you from one soul, then there is a place of rest and a place of storage’ until ‘they understand’ and ‘It is He who produced you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts. Little do you give thanks.’ Then he will recover, by God’s permission.” Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: If your water were to become sunken in, he said: Entering the earth. Then who can bring you flowing water? He said: Running water. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, If your water were to sink, he said: It would return to the ground. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, With flowing water, he said: It is apparent. Abd ibn Humayd also narrated on his authority, With flowing water, he said: Sweet.
68:1: It is fifty-two verses It is Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata', and Jabir. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah that from the beginning to the words, We will name him on the snout is Meccan, and from after that to the words, of the righteous is Medinan, and the rest of it is Meccan. This is what Al-Mawardi said. Ibn Al-Durais narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Whenever the opening of a surah was revealed in Mecca, it was written in Mecca, then God would add to it what He willed. The first of the Quran to be revealed was Iqra' Bismi Rabbik, then Nun, then Al-Muzzammil, then Al-Muddaththir. An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from him that he said: Surah Nun was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar narration from Aisha. His saying: 1- Nun Abu Bakr, Warsh, Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa’i, Ibn Muhaisin and Ibn Hubayrah read it with the assimilation of the second nun from its spelling into the waw, and the rest read it with the idhhar, and Abu Amr and Isa bin Omar read it with the fathah, implying a fa’l. Ibn Amir, Nadr and Ibn Ishaq read it with the kasrah, implying an oath, or because of the meeting of two sukoon letters. Muhammad bin Al-Sameefa’ and Harun read it with the damma, based on the construction. Mujahid, Muqatil and Al-Suddi said: It is the whale that carries the earth, and Al-Hamadhani, Ata’ Al-Khurasani and Al-Kalbi said the same once. It was said that the nun is the last letter of the letters of Ar-Rahman. Ibn Zayd said: It is an oath by which God swore. Ibn Kaysan said: It is the opening of the surah. Ata’ and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is the nun from victory and supporter. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: God swore by His victory for the believers. It was also said that it is a letter of the alphabet, like the opening letters at the beginning of the surahs that begin with it. We have already shown you what is true about such opening letters at the beginning of Surah Al-Baqarah. The waw in His statement, By the Pen is the waw of the oath. God called it the Pen because of what it contains of eloquence, and it applies to every pen that writes with. A group of commentators said: What is meant by it is the pen with which the Preserved Tablet was written. God swore by it to glorify it. Qatada said: The Pen is one of God's blessings upon His servants. And what they write is a relative pronoun, meaning, and what they write. The pronoun refers to the owners of the pen indicated by its mention, because mentioning the writing instrument indicates the writer. The meaning is, and what they write: they write everything that is written, or the guardians, as mentioned above. It is permissible for ma to be a source, meaning, and he wrote them. It was also said that the pronoun refers to the pen specifically, by virtue of attributing the action to the instrument and treating it like rational beings.
68:2: The answer to the oath is his statement: 2- You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. "Ma is a negative particle, You is its subject, and Bi Majnun" is its predicate. Al-Zajjaj said: "You is the subject of Ma, and Bi Majnun" is its predicate. His statement, "Bi Majnun" is a statement that falls in the middle: that is, madness has been negated from you by the grace of your Lord, just as one says, "You, by the grace of God, are sane. It was said that the Ba is related to an implied noun that is a state, as if it was said, You are innocent of madness, mingled with the grace of God, which is prophethood and general leadership. It was said that the Ba" is for the oath: that is, you, by the grace of your Lord, are not a madman. It was also said that the grace here is mercy, and the verse is a response to the disbelievers when they said, "O you upon whom the message has been sent down, indeed, you are mad.
68:3: 3- And indeed, for you is a reward meaning a recompense for the burdens of prophethood that you have borne and the various hardships that you have endured. Unmeasured meaning not cut off. It is said that you cut the rope. Mujahid said: Unmeasured means not calculated. Al-Hasan said: Unmeasured means not clouded by grace. Ad-Dahhak said: A reward without work. It was also said: Unmeasured. It was also said: Not graced upon you by people.
68:4: 4- And indeed, you are of a great moral character. It was said that it refers to Islam and religion. Al-Wahidi narrated this from the majority. It was also said that it refers to the Qur'an. This was narrated from Al-Hasan and Al-Awfi. Qatadah said: It refers to what he obeyed of God's commands and refrained from of what God prohibited. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that you are of the moral character that God commanded you to have in the Qur'an. It was also said that it refers to His kindness to His nation and His honoring them. It was also said that it means: You are of a noble nature. Al-Mawardi said: This is what appears to be the case. The true meaning of morality in the language is what a person takes upon himself of good manners. It was proven in Sahih on the authority of Aisha that she was asked about the morality of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so she said: His morality was the Qur'an. This sentence and the one before it are connected to the sentence in response to the oath.
68:5: 5- Then you will see, and they will see. That is, you will see, O Muhammad, and the unbelievers will see when the truth becomes clear and the veil is lifted, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection.
68:6: 6- Which of you is bewitched? The ba is an extra letter for emphasis: that is, which of you is bewitched by madness? This is what Al-Akhfash, Abu Ubaidah, and others said. Similar to it is the saying of the poet: We are the sons of Ja'dah, the companions of the foreigners. We strike with the sword and hope for relief. It was said that the letter ba is not redundant, and al-muftun is a verbal noun that comes in the form of maf’ul, like al-ma’qul and al-maysur, and the meaning is: which of you is the al-fitun or al-fitnah, and from this is the saying of the poet Al-Ra’i: Even if they leave no flesh for his bones, nor any reason for his heart. Meaning rationally. Al-Farra’ said: The preposition ba has the meaning of fi: meaning, which of you is the one who is afflicted, is it in the same group as you, or in the other group? This is supported by the reading of Ibn Abi Ubla: which of you is afflicted. It was also said that the discussion was based on the deletion of a noun of action: meaning, which of you has the one who is afflicted been afflicted, so the noun of action was deleted and the noun of action was used in its place. This was also narrated from Al-Akhfash. It was also said that the afflicted is the tormented, from the Arabs’ saying fat-tahir-dahab bi-naar you heat gold with fire meaning you heat it, and from it is His statement: The Day they are tempted by the Fire, and it was also said that the afflicted is the devil, because he is afflicted in his religion, and the meaning is: which of you is the devil. Qatada said: This is a threat to them of the punishment on the Day of Badr, and the meaning is: a veil and the people of Mecca will see, when the punishment descends upon them at Badr, which of you is the afflicted.
68:7: And the sentence 7 - Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way is an explanation for the sentence before it, as it includes the judgment of them as insane for opposing what is beneficial to them in this life and the hereafter, and choosing what is harmful to them in both. The meaning is: He is most knowing of who has strayed from His way that leads to happiness in both worlds, and He is most knowing of those who are guided to His way that leads to that happiness in this life and the hereafter. So He will reward every worker for his work, if good then good, and if evil then evil.
68:8: 8- So do not obey the deniers. God Almighty forbade him from siding with the polytheists, who were the leaders of the infidels of Mecca, because they were calling him to the religion of his fathers, so God forbade him from obeying them, or it is a hint to others that he should not obey the infidels, or what is meant by obedience is merely to be considerate by showing something contrary to what is in the mind.
68:9: God forbade him from that, as indicated by His statement: 9- They wish that you would be lenient so that they would be lenient. For lenient means to be gentle, to forgive, and to be accommodating. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is, If you were lenient, they would be lenient with you. Al-Kalbi said the same. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: They wish that you would disbelieve so that they would persist in disbelief. Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas said: They wish that you would lie so that they would lie. Qatadah said: They wish that you would abandon this matter so that they would go with them. Al-Hasan said: They wish that you would be accommodating with them regarding your religion so that they would be accommodating with you. Mujahid said: They wish that you would incline to them and abandon the truth that you are upon so that they would incline towards you. Ibn Qutaybah said: They wanted him to restore their gods for a while, and worship God for a while. His statement, they would be accommodating is in apposition to became accommodating and falls under the scope of if, or it is the predicate of a deleted subject: i.e., they are accommodating. Sibawayh said: Qalun claimed that in some copies of the Qur’an it is wadda ulta tadhanu they would anoint themselves with oil without a nun and the accusative is in response to the wish understood from wadda, and what is apparent from the language in the meaning of idhan is what we mentioned first.
68:10: 10- And do not obey every swearer meaning one who swears falsely a lot. Insignificant is a fa'il from the word insignificance, which means lack of opinion and discernment. Mujahid said: He is the liar. Qatada said: He who commits much evil, and so did Al-Hasan. It was also said that he is the wicked, weak person, and it was said that he is the insignificant one in the sight of God, and it was said that he is the humiliated, and it was said that he is the lowly one.
68:11: 11- Hammaz musha'a banimim The slanderer who backbites people. Ibn Zayd said: He is the one who backbites his brother. It was also said that the slanderer is the one who mentions people to their faces, and the backbiter is the one who mentions them behind their backs. This is what Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Hasan, and Ata' bin Abi Rabah said. Muqatil said the opposite of this. The one who spreads gossip among people to cause trouble between them. It is said that he goes around spreading gossip among people, and from this is the saying of the poet: A master is like an ant's house, he has no good for his master except his gossiping. It is said that gossip is the plural of gossip.
68:12: 12- "Preventer of good" meaning miserly with money and not spending it on its rightful use. It was also said that it refers to the one who prevents his family and clan from converting to Islam. Al-Hasan said: He tells them, "Whoever among you converts to the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him in any way. Transgressor and sinner meaning someone who transgresses the limits in injustice and commits many sins.
68:13: 13- Atal Al Wahidi said: The commentators say that he is someone who is harsh in nature and has a foul disposition. Al Farraa said: He is someone who is very argumentative about falsehood. Al Zujaj said: He is the rough and harsh one. Al Layth said: He is the glutton who is a greedy person. It is said that you pulled a man violently, you pulled him violently, and from this comes the saying of the poet: We knock on it, but we do not ride it After that, he is a bastard meaning that after he was considered a bastard among his faults, he was a bastard. A bastard is someone who is attached to the people but is not one of them. It is taken from the linum hanging from the throat of a sheep or goat, and from it is the saying of Hassan: A fornicator who is called by men increases as the width of the legs increases Saeed bin Jubair said: The wicked is known for his evil. It was said that he was from Quraysh and had a tail like a sheep’s tail. It was also said that he was the oppressor.
68:14: 14- If he was a man of wealth and children is related to His statement: Do not obey, meaning do not obey those who have these faults because he is a man of wealth and children. Al-Farra and Al-Zajjaj said: That is, because he was, and the meaning is: Do not obey him for his wealth and children. Ibn Amir, Abu Ja'far, Al-Mughira and Abu Haywah read if he was with one extended hamza as a question. Hamzah, Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read if he was: with two light hamzas, and the rest read it with one hamza as a statement. According to the question reading, the intended meaning is a rebuke and a reprimand, as he made the reward for the blessings that God bestowed upon him of wealth and children his disbelief in Him and in His Messenger. Nafi' read it in a narration from him with a kasra on the hamza as a condition.
68:15: 15- When Our verses are recited to him, he says, ‘Legends of the ancients.’ This is a new sentence that serves as an explanation for the prohibition. The meaning of Legends of the ancients has been presented in more than one place.
68:16: 16- We will brand him on the snout meaning we will brand him by cauterizing his snout. Abu Ubaidah, Abu Zaid, and Al-Mubarrad said: The snout is the nose. Muqatil said: We will brand him black on the nose, because his face will blacken before entering the Fire. Al-Farra' said: Although the snout is specifically marked, it is in the same way as the face, because some parts of the face reveal the other parts. Al-Zajjaj said: In the Hereafter, he will have the knowledge by which the people of the Fire will be known, from the blackening of their faces. Qatada said: We will attach something to him that will not leave him, and Ibn Qutaybah preferred this. He said: The Arabs say: He has branded him with the brand of evil, meaning he has attached a disgrace to him that will not leave him. The meaning is: God has attached a disgrace to him that will not leave him, like the brand on the snout. It was said that the meaning of We will brand him is: We will smash him with the sword. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The meaning is: We will brand him for the worst of wine. Wine is sometimes called the snout, and from this is the saying of the poet: You spend your day having fun and enjoying yourself, while at night you drink from the hoses. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh in al-`Azmah, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma` wa’l-Sifat, al-Khatib in his Tarikh, and al-Dhiya` in al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The first thing that God created was the pen. He said to it, ‘Write.’ It said, ‘O Lord, what should I write?’ He said, ‘Write the destiny.’ From that day on, it wrote down what would happen until the Hour comes. Then the book was folded and the pen was raised. His Throne was over the water, and the steam rose, and the heavens burst forth from it. Then He created the letter Nun the Noon and spread out the earth over it, and the earth over the letter Nun. The letter Nun trembled, and the earth shook.
