The mountains stood firm, and the mountains will stand firm over the earth until the Day of Resurrection.” Then Ibn Abbas recited: “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.” Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: “The first thing that God created was the pen. He said to it, ‘Write.’ It wrote down what would happen until eternity.” Ibn Jarir narrated from Muawiyah ibn Qurra, on the authority of his father, with a similar hadith. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: “God created the nun, which is the inkwell, and the pen. He said: ‘Write.’ He said: ‘What should I write?’ He said: ‘Write what will be until the Day of Resurrection.’” Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Hurayrah, with a similar hadith. ‘Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The nun is the inkwell. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The nun is the fish upon which the earth rests, and the pen with which our Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, wrote down destiny, its good and its evil, its harm and its benefit. ‘And what they write down,’ he said: The noble scribes.” ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it through various chains of narration from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And what they write down, he said: What they write. ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, And what they write down, he said: What they know. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa`d ibn Hisham who said: I came to Aisha and she said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: His character was the Qur’an. Do you not read the Qur’an: Indeed, you are of a great moral character. Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in al-Dala’il and al-Wahidi narrated on her authority that she said: “No one had a better character than the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). No one from his companions or from his family called upon him except that he said, ‘At your service.’ For this reason, God revealed: “Indeed, you are of a great moral character.” Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated on the authority of Abu al-Darda' who said: "Aisha was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: 'His character was the Qur'an. He was pleased with what God pleased and displeased with what God displeased." Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Abdullah al-Jadali who said: "I said to Aisha: 'How was the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)?' She said: 'He was neither obscene nor vulgar, nor did he make a rowdy noise in the marketplaces. He did not repay evil for evil, but rather he would pardon and overlook." Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: Then you will see, and they will see, meaning: You will know and they will know on the Day of Resurrection. Which of you is afflicted? He said: The devil. They used to say that he was a devil and that he was insane. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse: Which of you is insane. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse: They wish that you would compromise so they would compromise, meaning: If you would make concessions to them so they would make concessions. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority: And do not obey every worthless swearer, the verse. He said: He meant Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi who said: When the people pledged allegiance to Yazid, Marwan said: It is the way of Abu Bakr and Umar. Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr said: It is not the way of Abu Bakr and Umar, but it is the way of Heraclius. Marwan said: This is what was revealed about him: And he who said to his parents, ‘Fie upon you both’ 1:17. Aisha heard that and said: It was not revealed about Abdur-Rahman, but it was revealed about your father: And do not obey every worthless oath-taker, a slanderer, going about with calumnies. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: And do not obey every worthless oath-taker, a slanderer, going about with calumnies was revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). We did not recognize him until after that, Zanim was revealed to him. We recognized him as a hump like the hump of a sheep.” Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: The ‘atal’ is the impostor, and the ‘zanim’ is the suspicious person who is known for evil. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Asakir narrated on his authority that he said: The ‘zanim’ is the impostor. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Hakim also narrated from him - who authenticated it - that he said: The zanim is the one who is known for evil, just as a sheep is known by its zank. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him that he said: He is the man who passes by people, and they say he is a bad man. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: zanim, he said: An oppressor. It has been said that these verses were revealed about Al-Akhnas bin Shuraiq, and it has been said about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah.
68:17: His statement: 17- Indeed, We tested them meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, for God tested them with hunger and famine because of the supplication of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Testing is a test, and the meaning is: We gave them wealth so that they would be grateful, not so that they would be arrogant. So when they became arrogant, We tested them with hunger and famine as We tested the companions of the garden whose story is well-known among them, and that was that it was in the land of Yemen, two farsakhs from Sana'a, belonging to a man who fulfilled God's right in it. Then he died and it went to his sons, so they prevented the people from its goodness and were miserly with God's right in it. Al-Wahidi said: They are a people from Thaqeef who were Muslims in Yemen and inherited from their father an estate that had gardens, crops, and palm trees. Their father used to give the poor a share of everything in it at harvest time. His sons said: The wealth is little, and the children are many, and we cannot do as our father did. They resolved to deprive the poor, and their end was as God has related in His Book. Al-Kalbi said: There were two farsakhs between them and Sana’a. God tested them by burning their garden. It was said that it was a garden that was in Suran, and Suran was a farsakh from Sana’a. The people of this garden were a short time after Jesus was taken up. When they swore that they would surely cut it down in the morning. That is, they swore that they would surely cut it down entering in the morning. Cutting down means cutting down the fruit and crops. The accusative case of in the morning is in the state of the agent of to cut down from it. The kaf in as we have tested is an attribute of a deleted source: that is, we tested them with a test as we have tested them. Ma is a source, or in the sense of which, and idha is an adverbial phrase for to test and to cut down from it is the answer to the oath.
68:18: 18- And they do not make an exception means they do not say God willing. This sentence is a new sentence explaining what they did or a condition. It was said that the meaning is: They do not make an exception for the poor from the amount that their father used to give them, as Ikrimah said.
68:19: 19- And a tour from your Lord swept over it while they were asleep. That is, a tour from God Almighty swept over that paradise. It was said that the tour was a fire that burned it until it became black. This is what Muqatil said. It was also said that the tour was Gabriel who uprooted it. The phrase while they were asleep is in the accusative case as a state.
68:20: 20- So I became like a harvest meaning like a thing whose fruits have been harvested: i.e. cut off, fa'il with the meaning of maf'ul. Al-Farra' said: Like a harvest, like a dark night, and from this is the saying of the poet: Your dark night has become long, and it does not give birth to a dark morning. Meaning: It was burned and became like a black night. He said: As-Sareem is black ash in the language of Khuzaymah. Al-Akhfash said: It means like the morning that has passed from the night, meaning that it has dried up and become white. Al-Mubarrad said: As-Sareem is the night, and As-Sareem is the day: meaning this passes from this, and that from this. It was said that the night was called As-Sareem because its darkness cuts off movement. Al-Muwarij said: As-Sareem is the sand because nothing beneficial can stand on it. Al-Hasan said: Good was cut off from it: meaning it was cut off.
68:21: 21- They called to each other in the morning meaning they called to each other as they entered in the morning.
68:22: Muqatil said: When they woke up, some of them said to each other 22- Go to your tillage. And in his saying Go to your tillage, it is the explanatory particle because in the call there is the meaning of saying, or it is the source: that is, that you go, and what is meant is go out in the morning, and what is meant by tillage is the fruits and the crops if you are determined that is, intending to harvest, and going to the morning is transitive with to and upon, so there is no need to include in it the meaning of approaching as it was said, and the answer to the condition is omitted: that is, if you are determined, then go to the morning, and it was said that the meaning of determined is continuing in the resolve, from your saying a sharp sword.
68:23: 23- So they set out, speaking quietly to one another. That is, they went to their paradise, speaking quietly to one another so that no one would know about them. It is said that someone was quiet and did not speak. This is from the saying of Duraid ibn al-Summah: Even if I do not perish bored and die in humiliation, everyone will think badly of me. It was said that the meaning is: They hide themselves from people so that they do not see them, and they attack them as they attack their father at harvest time.
68:24: The first is more appropriate, based on His statement: 24- That no poor person shall enter it today upon you, for the word that explains the aforementioned whispering, as it contains the meaning of the statement. The meaning is: Some of them whispered this statement to one another, which is, No poor person shall enter this Paradise today upon you, and he asks you to give him from it what your father used to give him.
68:25: 25- And they went forth with might and main Harad means prevention and intent. Qatada, Muqatil, Al-Kalbi, Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: Harad here means intent, because the one who intends something is aversive. It is said: Harad yahrid if he intends, you say: Harada haradaka: meaning I intended your intent, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: A torrent came from God, raging like the raging of the enclosed paradise. Abu Ubaidah, Al-Mubarrad and Al-Qutaybi said: On hardness on prevention, from their saying the camels became hardened, meaning they gave little milk. The hardened camels are those with little milk. Al-Suddi, Yafyan and Al-Sha’bi said: On hardness on anger, and from this comes the saying of the poet: If the horses came running full of anger and rage And the other said: They shed the blood of lions And from it was said a lion who is a lion. It was narrated from Qatada and Mujahid also that they said: On hardness meaning on envy. Al-Hasan also said: on need and poverty. And it was said on hardness: alone, it is said that someone is hard, he is hardened, hardan or harud: if he moved away from his people and settled down alone from them and did not mix with them, and Al-Asma’i and others said the same. Al-Azhari said: Hard is the name of their village, and Al-Suddi said: it is the name of their paradise. The majority read Hard with a sukoon on the ra’. Abu Al-Aliyah and Ibn Al-Samee’ read it with a fatha, and the accusative of Qadireen is in the state. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of Qadir is: they were able and built upon it. Qatada said: they are able to protect their paradise in their eyes. Al-Sha’bi said: it means able to protect the poor.
68:26: 26- So when they saw it, meaning when they saw their paradise and witnessed the plague that had befallen it and destroyed what was in it, they said, ‘Indeed, we are astray,’ meaning some of them said to one another: We have lost our way to paradise and this is not it.
68:27: Then when they reflected and realized that it was their paradise, and that God Almighty had punished them by destroying the fruits and crops in it, they said: 27- Rather, we are deprived, meaning we were deprived of our paradise because of our resolve to prevent the poor from its goodness. So they changed their first statement to this statement. It was said that the meaning of their statement Indeed, we are astray is that they went astray from the right path because of what they had done.
68:28: 28- Their middle one said, meaning the best, wisest, and most virtuous of them, Did I not tell you, ‘Why do you not glorify God?’ That is, why do you not glorify God? He means that you make an exception. Exception is called glorification because it is a glorification of God and an acknowledgment of Him. This indicates that their middle one ordered them to make an exception, but they did not obey him. Mujahid, Abu Salih, and others said: Their exception was glorification. An-Nahhas said: The origin of glorification is to sanctify God Almighty, so glorification was placed in the place of God willing. It was said that the meaning is: Why do you not ask God for forgiveness for your actions and repent to Him for this intention that you have resolved upon? The middle one had said that to them, and when he said that to them after they had seen Paradise in that condition.
68:29: 29- “They said, ‘Glory be to our Lord. Indeed, we were wrongdoers.’” That is, to glorify Him from being wrongdoers in what He did to our garden, for that was because of the sin we committed. It was said that the meaning of their glorification is seeking forgiveness: that is, we seek forgiveness from our Lord for our sin. Indeed, we were wrongdoers to ourselves in our withholding from the poor.
68:30: 30- So some of them turned to others, blaming each other meaning they blamed each other for preventing the poor and their intention to do so.
68:31: Then they cried out for woe upon themselves, as 31- They said, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors.’ That is, disobedient and overstepping the limits set by God by withholding from the poor and making no exceptions. Ibn Kaysan said: That is, we were transgressors in the favors of God, and we did not thank them as our fathers had been thankful for them before.
68:32: Then they returned to God and asked Him to compensate them with something better than it, so they said: 32- Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. When they confessed their sin, they asked God, the Almighty, to give them in exchange something better than their paradise. It was said that they made a covenant among themselves and said, If God gives us in exchange something better than it, we will do as our father did. So they supplicated to God and beseeched Him, and He gave them in exchange something better than it. The majority of scholars read yubbaddulna with a light pronunciation, while Abu Amr and the people of Medina read it with a heavy pronunciation. These are two dialects. Substitution is changing the essence of a thing or changing its description. Substitution is raising something entirely and replacing it with another, as mentioned in Surah Saba': Indeed, we are towards our Lord aspiring. That is, seeking good from Him, hoping for His forgiveness, returning to Him. It is transitive with ila, and it is only transitive with an or fi to include the meaning of returning.
68:33: 33- Such is the punishment meaning like the punishment with which We tested them and the people of Mecca, the punishment of this world. The punishment is a delayed subject, and so is its predicate. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew meaning more severe and greater if the polytheists knew that it was like this, but they did not know. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, As We have tested the companions of the garden, he said: They were people from Abyssinia. Their father had a garden and used to feed the poor from it. Then their father died and his sons said: Our father was truly a fool who used to feed the poor. They swore that they would harvest it in the morning, and that they would not feed a poor person. Ibn Jarir narrated: And a group of people swept over it, he said: It is a command from God. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Beware of disobedience, for a person may commit a single sin and thus forget a door to knowledge. And a person may commit a sin and thus be deprived of a provision that had been provided for him.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “And a group of people from your Lord swept over it while they were asleep. So it became like a harvested field,” they were deprived of the good of their garden because of their sin. Abdur-Razzaq, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, like a barren field, he said: like a black night. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, and they whisper, he said: secrets and hidden speech. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority, on a mighty force, he said: someone with power. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, indeed, we are astray, he said: we were led astray from our paradise. They also narrated on his authority, the most just of them said, he said: the most just of them.
68:34: When the Almighty finished mentioning the state of the disbelievers and likening their trial to the trial of the people of the aforementioned garden, He mentioned the state of the righteous and what good He has prepared for them. He said: 34- Indeed, for the righteous are gardens of pleasure with their Lord. That is, those who are certain that which would necessitate His wrath from disbelief and sins with Him, the Almighty and Majestic, in the Hereafter are gardens of pure pleasure, untainted by turbidity and unmarred by the fear of its disappearance.
68:35: 35- Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals? The question is for denial. The leaders of the infidels of Quraysh saw their abundant fortune in this world and the little fortune of the Muslims in it, so when they heard the mention of the Hereafter and what God would give the Muslims in it, they said: If what Muhammad claims is true, then our situation and their situation would be like what it is in this world. So God said, refuting them and responding to them: Shall We treat the Muslims like the verse, and the fa is for connecting to an implied word like its counterparts.
68:36: Then God rebuked them, saying: 36- What is the matter with you? How do you judge? This crooked judgment is as if the matter of retribution is entrusted to you, and you decide it as you wish.
68:37: 37- Or do you have a book in which you study? That is, you read in it and find the obedient like the disobedient. Similar to this is the Almighty’s saying: Or do you have a clear authority? * Then produce your book. Then the Almighty said: Indeed, you will have therein whatever you choose. The majority read it with a kasra on in as an object of to study: that is, you study in the book.
68:38: 38- Indeed, you will have in it whatever you choose. When the lam was introduced, the hamza was broken, as in his saying: I knew that you were indeed a wise man with the kasra, or as a narration of the studied, as in his saying: “And We left for him among later generations * Peace be upon Noah among the worlds.” It was said that the speech was completed when he said: You study, then he began and said: Indeed, you will have in it whatever you choose, meaning that you will not have that. Talha bin Masraf and Al-Dahhak read that you will have in it whatever you choose with the opening of the hamza, on the basis that the factor in it is you study with the addition of the lam of emphasis, and the meaning of you choose is you choose and desire.
68:39: Then the Almighty increased the rebuke by saying: 39- Or do you have oaths upon Us that are binding? That is, firm, binding, and infinite covenants. The meaning is, do you have oaths upon God that you have taken as a pledge that He will admit you into Paradise? His statement, until the Day of Resurrection is related to what is implied in for you, that is, they are fixed for you until the Day of Resurrection. We will not depart from our pledge until He judges you on that Day. The response to the oath is His statement, You will have what you judge. Because the meaning of Or do you have oaths is, Or did We swear to you? Al-Razi said: The meaning is, Or did We guarantee you and swear to you with firm, infinite oaths? It was said that the speech was completed when He said, until the Day of Resurrection, then He began by saying, You will have what you judge. That is, the matter is not like that. The majority of scholars read binding in the nominative case as an attribute of oaths. Al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Ali read it in the accusative case as a state of oaths, because it was specified by the description, or from the pronoun in for you or from the pronoun in upon us.
68:40: 40- Ask them which of them is responsible for this. That is, O Muhammad, ask the infidels, rebuking and rebuking them, which of them, by this incorrect ruling, can guarantee that they will have in the Hereafter what the Muslims have in it. Ibn Kaysan said: The leader here is the one who stands up with the argument and the claim. Al-Hasan said: The leader is the Messenger.
68:41: 41- Or do they have partners who share this statement with them and agree with them in it? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful in what they say. It is or to make it impossible, and the answer to the condition is omitted. It was said that the meaning is, Or do they have partners who will make them like the Muslims in the Hereafter?
68:42: 42- The Day the shin shall be laid bare. "The Day is an adverbial phrase for His statement, So let them bring it on the Day the shin shall be laid bare. It is also permissible for it to be an adverbial phrase for an implied verb, Remember the Day the shin shall be laid bare." Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said about His statement, "On the shin," about the severity of a matter. Ibn Qutaybah said: The origin of this is that when a man encounters a serious matter that requires seriousness, he rolls up his sleeves, so the uncovering of the shin is used as a metaphor for severity. And Durayd ibn al-Summah recited: The sleeve of the garment is halfway out of his leg. Patiently waiting for the evacuation. He came out in the best way. He said: The interpretation of the verse is the Day when the matter becomes intense, just as something becomes intense that requires one to uncover one’s shins. Abu Ubaidah said: When the war or the matter becomes intense, it is said that the matter has uncovered its shins. The origin of this is that whoever falls into something that requires seriousness will roll up his shins, so the shin and uncovering were borrowed to refer to the place of intensity. This is what others among the linguists said, and the Arabs have used this in their poetry, including the saying of the poet: A brother of war, if war bites him, he bites it, and if war rolls up its leg, he rolls it up. And the other said: And the horses gallop at sunrise, and the war has begun against us. Another saying: She has revealed her leg, so hurry up and find war with you, so hurry up Another saying also in the year: She revealed her red leg, revealing the flesh of her veins. It was said that the stem of something is its origin and foundation, like the stem of a tree. The stem of man: that is, the day the stem of the matter will be revealed and its truths will be made clear. It was said that the stem of Hell will be revealed, and it was said that the stem of the Throne, and it was said that it is an expression of nearness, and it was said that the Lord, glory be to Him, will reveal His light. What is the truth will come at the end of the research. And when the river of God comes, the river of Maqal will be nullified. The majority read yakshufu with the greeting in the passive form. Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abi Ubla read takashuf with the superior form in the active form: that is, the severity or the hour. It was read with the superior form in the passive form, and it was read with the letter noon, and it was read with the superior form with the damma and the kasra of the sheen from akshaf al-amr: that is, it entered into the revelation. And they are called to prostrate, but they are unable. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: All of creation prostrates to God in one prostration, and the disbelievers and hypocrites remain, wanting to prostrate, but they are unable, because their backs have dried up and do not soften for prostration. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: The veil will be lifted and those who believed in God in this world will fall and prostrate to Him. The others will be called to prostrate but will not be able to, because they did not believe in God in this world.
68:43: 43- Their eyes will be humbled is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun they call, and their eyes is raised by it as an active participle, and the attribution of humility to the eyes, which is submission and humility due to the appearance of its effect in them Humiliation will overwhelm them meaning severe humiliation, regret and remorse will overwhelm them And they used to be called to prostration meaning in this world while they were sound meaning free from illnesses and able to act. Ibrahim Al-Tamimi said: They are called with the call to prayer and the call to prayer but they refuse. Saeed bin Jubair said: They hear Come to success but they do not respond. Kaab Al-Ahbar said: By God, this verse was only revealed about those who stay away from congregational prayers. It was said that they are called with the obligation directed at them by the Shari'ah but they do not respond. The phrase while they are sound is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun they call.
68:44: 44- Leave Me and he who denies this hadith meaning, come between Me and him, and leave his affair to Me, and I will suffice you. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is, do not let your heart be preoccupied with him; leave his affair to Me, and I will suffice you. The fa indicates that what comes after it is connected to what came before it. Min is in the accusative case as an apposition to the first-person pronoun, or as an accusative complement. What is meant by this hadith is the Qur'an. Al-Suddi said: It was also said that it refers to the Day of Resurrection. In this there is consolation for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The phrase We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know is a new statement of how they will be punished, as understood from his statement, Leave Me and he who denies this hadith. The pronoun refers to min in light of its meaning. The meaning is: We will seize them with the punishment unawares and drive them to it, step by step, until We cause them to fall into it from where they do not know that this is a form of enticement, because they think it is a blessing and do not think about its consequences and what they will encounter at the end. Sufyan al-Thawri said: He bestows blessings upon them and makes them forget to be grateful. Al-Hasan said: How many are lured by kindness, how many are infatuated by praise, and how many are deceived by concealment. Luring means abandoning haste, and its origin is transfer from one state to another. It is said that someone lured someone, meaning he extracted what he had little by little. It is also said that he brought him to such and such and lured him, meaning he brought him closer to it gradually, so he gradually did so.
68:45: Then the Almighty mentioned that He gives respite to the wrongdoers, saying: 45- And I will grant them respite meaning I will grant them respite so that they may increase in sin. The explanation of this has already been mentioned in Surat Al-A’raf and Surat At-Tur. The root of mulāwa is a period of time. It is said that God granted him respite, meaning He extended his period. The mulā is shortened: the wide earth, named thus because of its extension. Indeed, My plan is firm, meaning strong and intense, so nothing escapes Me. The Almighty called His benevolence a plan, just as He called it a lure, because it is in the form of a plan, considering its consequences, and He described it as firm because of the strength of its effect in causing destruction.
68:46: 46- Or do you ask them for a reward? God Almighty returned the speech to what came before in His statement: Or do they have partners? That is, or do you seek from them a reward for what you are calling them to of belief in God? So they are burdened with a heavy fine. The fine is the penalty: that is, they are burdened with the penalty of that reward, and burdened: that is, it is heavy for them to bear because of their stinginess in spending money, so they turned away from answering you for this reason, and the question is for rebuke and reprimand of them, and the meaning is: that you did not ask them for that and you did not demand it from them.
68:47: 47- Or do they have the unseen, so they write down meaning the Preserved Tablet, or everything that is hidden from them, so they write down from that unseen whatever they want of the arguments that they claim prove their statement, and they dispute with you based on what they write of that and they rule for themselves according to what they want and thereby do not need to answer you or comply with what you say.
68:49: 49- Had it not been for the grace of his Lord overtaking him meaning, had the owner of the whale not been overtaken by a grace from God, which was His guidance to repent, and God accepted his repentance, he would have been cast out onto the open shore meaning, he would have been thrown out from the belly of the whale onto the surface of the vegetation-free earth, and he was blamed meaning, he would be blamed and condemned for the sin he committed and would be expelled from mercy. The sentence is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun he was cast out. Ad-Dahhak said: The grace here is prophethood. Saeed bin Jubair said: His previous worship. Ibn Zayd said: It is his calling out, saying: “There is no god but You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.” It was said: He was blamed and cast out. It was said: He was guilty. The majority read "tadarakhu" in the past tense, while Al-Hasan, Ibn Hurmuz, and Al-A'mash read it with a shaddah on the dal. The original is tatadakaruquhu with two ta's in the present tense, but it was assimilated. This reading is based on the past tense. Abi, Ibn Mas'ud, and Ibn Abbas read "tadarakhu" with the feminine ta'.
68:50: 50- So his Lord chose him meaning He selected him, selected him, and chose him for prophethood. And made him among the righteous meaning those who were perfect in righteousness and protected him from sin. It was said that He restored prophethood to him and made him intercede for himself and for his people and sent him to one hundred thousand or more, as mentioned above.
68:51: 51- And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes. “In” is the light form of the heavy form. The majority of scholars read li-zaliqunuka with a damma on the ya’ from azlaquhu meaning he made his foot slip. It is said azlaquhu ‘an mawakihi if he moved him away. Nafi’ and the people of Medina read it with a fatha from zalaqa ‘an mawakihi meaning he moved away. Al-Harawi said: That is, they would attack you with their eyes and make you slip from the position in which God has established you out of enmity towards you. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas’ud, Al-A’mash, Mujahid, and Abu Wa’il read “li-yadh-ha-da-wa... Al-Zajjaj said about the verse: The opinion of the linguists and exegetes is that due to the intensity of their hatred and enmity, they almost knock you down with their looks of hatred. This is used in speech, as when someone says, “He looked at me with a look that almost knocked me down,” or a look that almost consumed me. Ibn Qutaybah said: God does not mean that they strike you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye strikes with his eye what pleases him. Rather, He means that when you recite the Quran, they look at you with intense enmity and hatred that almost makes you fall, as the poet said: They clash if they meet in a council, looking at the ground that removes the footholds When they heard the message meaning when they heard the Qur’an because they hated it so much. When is a circumstantial noun in the accusative case, They almost made you slip. It was said that it is a particle, and its answer is omitted because what preceded it indicates it, meaning when they heard the message, they almost made you slip. And they say, ‘Indeed, he is mad.’ Meaning, they attribute madness to him when they hear him reciting the Qur’an.
68:52: God responded to them by saying: 52- And it is only a reminder for the worlds. The sentence is a new sentence, or in the accusative case as a state of the subject of they say: meaning that the state is that it is a reminder and clarification of all that they need, or an honor for them, as God the Almighty said: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people. It was said that the pronoun refers to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that he is a reminder for the worlds or an honor for them. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: "Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. Whoever used to prostrate in this world for show and to be heard will remain, and he will go to prostrate, but his back will become a single flat surface." This hadith is authenticated through chains of narration in the two Sahihs and others, and some of its wording is longer, and it is a famous and well-known hadith. Ibn Mandah narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah regarding the verse, he said: God the Almighty will uncover His shin. And Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mandah narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding the verse, he said: His shin will be uncovered, Blessed and Exalted be He. Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma` wa’l-Sifat The Names of God and His angels narrated it – and he declared it weak – and Ibn `Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the verse, he said: From a great light, before which they will fall down in prostration. Al-Faryabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Mandah and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha`i, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas regarding the verse, he said: A great matter will be uncovered. Then he said: War has begun over the shin. He said: Ibn Mas`ud said: His shin will be uncovered, and every believer will prostrate, and the back of the disbeliever will harden and become a single bone. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma` wa’l-Sifat from Ibn `Abbas that he was asked about His statement: The Day the shin will be uncovered, he said: “If something of the Qur’an is hidden from you, then seek it in poetry, for it is the diwan of the Arabs. Haven’t you heard the saying of the poet: The war started against us Ibn Abbas said: This is a day of great distress. Something similar to this was narrated from him through other chains of transmission. God Almighty has enriched us in interpreting this verse with what is authentic from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as you know. This does not require embodiment or likening, for there is nothing like it. Leave every saying when Muhammad says, for he who believes in his religion is like a risk Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, {And they were called to prostration while they were safe}, he said: They are the disbelievers who were called in this world while they were safe, but today they are called while they are afraid. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab on his authority regarding the verse, he said: A man hears the call to prayer but does not respond to the prayer. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority regarding the statement of God, {that they might slip you with their eyes}, he said: They might save you with their eyes.
69:1: It is fifty-one verses, and it was said fifty-two It was revealed in Mecca. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone's opinion. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Haqqah was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abu Barzah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite Al-Haqqah and similar surahs in the dawn prayer. His statement: 1- Al-Haqqah is the Resurrection, because the matter will be fulfilled in it, and it will be fulfilled in itself without a doubt. Al-Azhari said: It is said: I overcame him, so I overcame him, I defeated him, so I defeated him. The Resurrection is the Haqqah because it will overtake every person who is defeated in the religion of God with falsehood and will bring to account every disputant. In As-Sahah it says: He will dispute with him over minor matters. It is also said: He has no right, no right, and no dispute. The affiliation of the dispute. Al-Haqqah, Al-Haqqah, and Al-Haqq are three meanings. Al-Wahidi said: It is the Resurrection according to all commentators. It was called thus because it is the one with the inevitable matters, and it is the truthful and necessarily true, and all the rulings of the Resurrection are true and necessarily exist. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Muraj said: Al-Haqqah is the Day of Truth. It was also said that it was called thus because every person on it is deserving of being rewarded for his knowledge. It was also said that it was called Hell for some people, and Paradise for some people.
69:2: It is a subject and its predicate is his saying: 2- What is the Inevitable? The interrogative what is a second subject and its predicate is the Inevitable, and the sentence is the predicate of the first subject, and the meaning is: what is it in its state or its characteristics? It was said that the interrogative what is the predicate of what comes after it, and this sentence, even if its wording is the wording of an interrogative, its meaning is to glorify and magnify its status, as you say: Zayd, what Zayd? We have already explained this meaning in Surat Al-Waqi’ah.
69:3: Then the Almighty increased in magnifying its matter, glorifying its status, and terrifying its condition, saying: 3- And what will make you know what is the Inevitable? That is, what will make you know what it is? It is as if you do not know it if you do not witness it and see the horrors in it, as if it is outside the circle of the knowledge of created beings. Yahya bin Salam said: It came to my attention that everything in the Quran is and what will make you know? He made Him know it and taught it, and everything He said in it and what will make you know He informed him of it. What is the subject, and its predicate is perception. "What is the Inevitable is a sentence consisting of a subject and a predicate, and its position is in the accusative case by dropping the preposition, because I know takes the second object with the letter ya" as in His statement: "nor do I make you know it." So when the interrogative sentence is attached to it, it is in the position of the second object. Without the hamza, it takes one object with the letter "ba like I knew about such and such." But if it means knowledge, it takes two objects. The sentence "and what will make you know is conjoined with the sentence What is the Inevitable.
69:4: 4- Thamud and Aad denied the Calamity, meaning the Resurrection. It was called thus because it will strike people with its terrors. Al-Mubarrad said: By the Calamity he meant the Quran that was revealed to their prophets in this world, and they used to frighten them with it so they would lie about them. It was also said that the Calamity is derived from the word Qar’ah because it elevates some people and brings down others, but the first is more correct. The Calamity would be placed in place of the pronoun of Al-Haqqah to indicate the enormity of its terror and the awfulness of its condition. The sentence is a new sentence to explain some of the conditions of Al-Haqqah.
69:5: 5- As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the transgressor. Thamud were the people of Salih. This was explained in more than one place, as was their homes and where they were. The transgressor is the cry that exceeded the limit. It was said that it was due to their transgression and disbelief. The root of transgression is exceeding the limit.
69:6: 6- And as for ‘Aad, they were destroyed by a furious wind. ‘Aad were the people of Hud. This was explained before, and their homes and where they were were mentioned in more than one place. The furious wind is the one with intense cold. It is taken from sar which means cold. It was also said that it is a very loud wind. Mujahid said: The very poisonous, and the violent one that was stubborn about obedience, as if it rebelled against its treasurers, so it did not obey them and they were not able to repel it due to its fierce blowing, or it rebelled against ‘Aad, so they were not able to repel it. Rather, it destroyed them.
69:7: 7- He subjected it to them for seven nights. This sentence is a new sentence to explain how they were destroyed. The meaning of He subjected it is to set it in power, as Muqatil said, and it is also said that He sent it. Al-Zajjaj said: He established it upon them as He willed. Subjugation is the use of something with power. It is possible that this sentence is an attribute of a wind, or it is a state of it to specify it with the attribute, or of the pronoun in intense. "And eight days is conjoined with seven nights, and the accusative of decisive" is in the state: meaning of decisiveness, or in the source with an implied verb: meaning it decisively destroys them, or as a direct object. Decisiveness is succession, so if something is consecutive and its beginning is not cut off from its end, it is called decisiveness. Al-Zajjaj said: What the language requires in the meaning of his saying decisively: meaning it decisively destroys them, annihilating them and eliminating them. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: I severed them and destroyed them. Al-Farra’ said: Al-Hasoom is following, from the root hasaam al-da’, which means a large disease, because its owner is cauterized with an iron, then that is continued on him. From this is the saying of Abu Dawud: A long time separates them, during which decisive years follow one another. Al-Mubarrad said: It is from your saying hasamat al-shay’ meaning you cut it off and separate it from something else. It was said that hasam means extermination, and the sword is called husam because it stops the enemy from what he wants to achieve in his enmity. The meaning is: that it hasama them, meaning it cut them off and made them go away. From this comes the saying of the poet: Then He sent a scorching, barren wind that swirled around them and was decisive. Ibn Zayd said: That is, He finished them off and did not leave a single one of them. It was narrated that he said: He finished the days and nights until He completed them, because they began with the rising of the sun on the first day and ended with the setting of the sun on the last day. Al-Layth said: Al-Hasum is bad luck, that is, it cuts off goodness from its people, like his saying, in unlucky days. There is a difference of opinion as to when it began. Some say it was Sunday morning, some say Friday morning, and some say Wednesday morning. Wahb said: These days are what the Arabs call the days of the old woman. They were very cold and had a strong wind. The first day was Wednesday and the last day was Wednesday. Then you will see the people therein fallen down. The address is to whoever is suitable for it, assuming that if he had been present at that time he would have seen that. The pronoun in therein refers to the nights and days. Some say it refers to the violent wind, but the former is more appropriate. Falling down is the plural of fallen down, meaning dead. As if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. That is, fallen or decayed palm tree roots. It is also said that they are empty, with no cavity in them. Palm trees are both masculine and feminine. Similar to this is His statement: As if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. The explanation of this has already been given, and it is to describe the enormity of their bodies. Yahya ibn Salam said: He only said empty because their bodies were devoid of their spirits, like hollow palm trees.
69:8: 8- Do you see any remnant of them? That is, any remaining group, or any remaining soul, or any remnant, with the word remnant being a verbal noun like consequence and well-being. Ibn Jurayj said: They remained alive for seven nights and eight days in the torment of the wind, and when they reached evening on the eighth day, they died, and the wind carried them and threw them into the sea.
69:9: 9- And Pharaoh came and those before him meaning from the disbelieving nations. The majority read before him with a fatha on the qaf and a sukoon on the ba: meaning and those who came before him from the past centuries and the bygone nations. Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba: meaning and those who are on his side from his followers. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid chose the second reading based on the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy and those with him, and based on the reading of Abu Musa and those who meet him. And the overturned The majority read al-mu'taffikat in the plural and they are the cities of the people of Lot. Al-Hasan and Al-Jahdary read al-mu'taffika in the singular, and the lam is for the genus, so it is in the meaning of afla plural, and the meaning is: And the overturned came with the sinful meaning with the sinful action, or the mistake as a verbal noun. What is meant is that it came with polytheism and sins. Mujahid said: with sins. Al-Jurjani said: with the great mistake.
69:10: 10- So they disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord meaning every nation disobeyed the Messenger sent to it. Al-Kalbi said: It was Moses, and it was said Lot because that is closer. It was said that Messenger here means message, and from this is the saying of the poet: The informers lied. I did not reveal any secret to them, nor did I send them a messenger. That is, with the message, So He seized them with a severe seizure, meaning that God seized them with a severe seizure, greater than the seizures of other nations. The meaning is that it was extremely severe. It is said, My Lord, something grows: if it increases and multiplies. Al-Zajjaj said: It exceeds the seizures. Mujahid said: Severe.
69:11: 11- When the water overflowed meaning it exceeded its limit in height and height, and that was in the time of Noah when his people persisted in disbelief and denied him. It was also said that it overflowed his guardian angels out of anger for his Lord and they were unable to hold it back. Qatada said: It exceeded everything by fifteen cubits. We carried you in the ship meaning in the loins of your fathers, or We carried them and We carried you in their loins, giving precedence to those addressed over those absent. The ship is Noah's ark, and it was called a ship because it flowed in the water. The place of in the ship is the accusative case as a state: meaning We raised you above the water while you were in the ship.
69:12: Since the purpose of mentioning the stories of the nations and the punishment that befell them was to deter this nation from following their example in disobeying the Messenger, He said: 12- That We may make it a reminder for you, meaning, Let us make these matters mentioned to you, O nation of Muhammad, a lesson and an admonition by which you may prove the great power of God and the wonder of His creation, or Let us make this action, which is the saving of the believers and the drowning of the disbelievers, a reminder for you. And a retentive ear will retain it, meaning, an ear that has retained what it heard will memorize it after hearing it. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said, I memorized such-and-such, meaning, I memorized it in my soul, I memorized it, and I memorized the knowledge and I memorized what I said, all in one meaning, and I stored the goods in the vessel. And everything that you memorize in something other than your soul is said, I memorized it, with an alif, and when you memorize it in your soul, you memorized it without an alif. Qatadah said in his interpretation of the verse: An ear that heard and understood what it heard. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is for every ear to memorize it as an admonition for whoever comes after. The majority read memorized it with a kasra on the 'ayn. Talha bin Masraf, Hamid Al-A'raj, and Abu Amr, in a narration from him, read the word with a sukoon on the 'ayn, likening this word to womb womb and witness witness, even though it is not one of those words. Al-Razi said: It was narrated from Ibn Kathir with a sukoon on the 'ayn, making the letter of the present tense with what follows it as one word, so he lightened it and made it sukoon, just as the middle letter of thigh thigh, liver liver and shoulder shoulder was made sukoon. The first is more appropriate, as this is from the category of making the connection run like the pause, as in the reading of the one who read and what makes you feel with a sukoon on the ra'. Al-Qurtubi said: There was a difference in the reading of Asim and Ibn Kathir: meaning you understand it.
69:13: 13- And when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast This is the beginning of explaining the Inevitable Event and how it will happen after explaining the matter of the destruction of the deniers. Ata' said: He means the first blast. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said he means the last blast. The majority of scholars read a single blast in the nominative case in both of them, on the basis that the blast is raised as a substitute, and one is to emphasize it, and it is good to make the verb masculine because of the separation. Abu Al-Sammak read them in the accusative case, on the basis that the substitute is the preposition and noun. Al-Zajjaj said: His statement in the Trumpet takes the place of something whose agent is not named.
69:14: 14- And the earth and the mountains were carried meaning they were lifted from their places and uprooted from their foundations by the Divine Power. The majority of scholars read hamalta with a light mim. Al-A'mash, Ibn Abi Ubla, Ibn Muqsim, and Ibn Amir, in one narration from him, read it with a heavy mim for emphasis or transitivity. They were crushed with one crushing meaning they were broken with one crushing and no increase, or they struck each other with one blow until they became a heap of sand and scattered dust. Al-Farra' said: He did not say fadakun because he made all the mountains as one whole. Similar to this is the saying of God the Almighty: Have those who disbelieve not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them? It was said that dakata means they were spread out with one spreading, and from this comes the word andakka the camel's hump when it spreads out on its back.
69:15: 15- On that day the event will occur meaning the Day of Resurrection will come.
69:16: 16- And the heaven will split, and on that Day it will be frail. That is, it will split open with the descent of the angels in it, so on that Day it will be weak and flimsy. Al-Zajjaj said: Everything that is very weak and has become frail is called waha. Al-Farra’ said: Waha means it will crack.
69:17: 17- And the angels are on its edges meaning the angels are on its edges and sides. The plural of rajā is rajwān, and its dual is rajwān, like qaffā and qafwān. The meaning is that when the sky, which is their dwellings, splits, they will take refuge at its edges. Ad-Dahhak said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will command the lowest heaven to split, and the angels will be at its edges until the Lord commands them to descend to the earth and surround the earth and whoever is on it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The meaning is that the angels are on the edges of the world: meaning they will descend to the earth. It was also said that when the sky becomes pieces, the angels will stand on those pieces that are not cracked in themselves. And the Throne of your Lord will be borne above them that Day meaning that eight angels will carry it above their heads on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that it will be eight rows of angels, and no one knows their number except God. It was also said that it will be eight parts out of nine parts of the angels, as was said by Al-Kalbi and others.
69:18: 18- On that Day you will be exposed meaning the servants will be exposed to God for their reckoning. Similar to it is And they will be exposed before your Lord in rows. This exposure to Him, glory be to Him, is not so that He knows what He does not know. Rather, it is an exposure to testing and rebuke through deeds. The phrase Nothing about you will be hidden is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun you will be exposed meaning you will be exposed while nothing of your beings, your words, or your actions, whatever they may be, is hidden from God, glory be to Him. The interpretation is: any hidden soul or hidden action. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Al-Haqqah is one of the names of the Resurrection. Al-Faryabi, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said: “God did not send any rain except by measure, nor a drop of water except by measure, except on the day of Noah and the day of Aad. As for the day of Noah, the water overflowed its reservoirs and they had no way to control it.” Then he recited: Indeed, when the water overflowed. As for the day of Aad, the wind was violent against its reservoirs and they had no way to control it. Then he recited: by a furious, violent wind. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Ali ibn Abi Talib. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I was aided by the north wind, and Aad was destroyed by the west wind. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “The keeper of the treasury over Aad was only as strong as a ring from the wind. It attacked the keeper and came out from the sides of the doors. That is why He said: ‘with a violent, furious wind.’ He said: ‘Its fury attacked the keeper.’” Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: ‘with a violent, furious wind.’ He said: ‘Overpowering.’ Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Humaid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Taybarani, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding His statement: ‘severely.’ He said: ‘Consecutive.’ Abd bin Humaid and Ibn Jarir narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: ‘severely.’ He said: ‘Consecutive.’ In another version: ‘Consecutive.’ Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: ‘As if they were trunks of palm trees.’ He said: ‘They are their roots.’ And regarding His statement: ‘Empty.’ He said: ‘Ruined.’ Sa`id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him regarding his statement, When the water overflowed, he said: It overflowed its storehouses and descended. No water descended from the sky except by measure or scale except in the time of Noah, when it overflowed its storehouse and descended without measure or weight. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym in al-Hilyah narrated from Makhul from Ali ibn Abi Talib regarding his statement, And a listening ear will receive it, he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me: I asked God to make it your ear, O Ali. Ali said: I never heard anything from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and then forgot it. Ibn Kathir said: It is a mursal hadith. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Wahidi, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Asakir and Ibn al-Najjar narrated from Buraydah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Ali: “God has commanded me to bring you close and not to make you pass judgment, and to teach you, and to understand, and it is your right to understand. So this verse was revealed: “And a listening ear will receive it,” so you are a listening ear, for Ali.” Ibn Kathir said: It is not authentic. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement, A listening ear, that he said: An ear that understands God. Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba’th on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b regarding his statement, And the earth and the mountains will be borne away and crushed with a single crushing, that he said: They will become dust on the faces of the disbelievers, not on the faces of the believers. This is the meaning of His statement, “There will be faces, that Day, upon them will be dust. A darkness will cover them.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So on that Day they will be frail, that is, torn apart. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And the angels will be over its corners, that he said: On its edges, on that part of it that has not yet collapsed. Abd ibn Humayd and Uthman ibn Sa’id al-Darimi narrated in al-Radd ‘ala al-Jahmiyyah, Abu Ya’la, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib in Tali al-Talkhis also narrated on his authority regarding his statement, And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day, that he said: Eight angels in the form of mountain goats. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him through various chains of transmission regarding the verse. He said: It is said that there are eight rows of angels, and no one knows their number except God. It is also said that there are eight angels whose heads are at the Throne in the seventh heaven and their feet are in the lowest earth. They have horns like the horns of a wild mountain goat. The distance between the base of one of their horns and its end is five hundred years. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Musa that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection three times. As for the two presentations, they will be arguing and making excuses. As for the third, at that time the scrolls will be scattered among the hands, and I will take hold of them with my right hand and I will take hold of my left.” Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated something similar in al-Ba’th from Ibn Mas’ud.
69:19: When God Almighty mentioned the presentation, He mentioned what will be in it, saying: 19- But as for he who is given his record in his right hand, meaning he is given his record that the guardians wrote down of his deeds, he will say, ‘Here, read my record,’ He says that with joy and happiness. Ibn Al-Sikkit and Al-Kisa’i said: The Arabs say: Ha ya rajul, and for the dual, Ha’uma ya rajulan, and for the plural, Ha’um ya rijal. It was said that the original form was ha’ukum, but the hamza was replaced with the kaf. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning of ha’um is Come. Muqatil said: Come, and it was said: Take, so it is a verbal noun, and it may be an explicit verb due to the connection of prominent raised pronouns to it, and it has three languages as is known in the science of grammar, and his statement: his book is the object of his statement: Iqra`u because it is the closer of the two verbs, and the object of ha`um is deleted and indicated by the object of iqra`u and the meaning is: Ha`um his book, Iqra`u his book, and the ha` in his book, his account, his sultan, and his wealth is the ha` of silence. The majority of scholars read in these by adding the ha` when stopping and connecting, in accordance with the orthography of the Mushaf. If it were not for that, it would have been deleted when connecting as is the case with the ha` of silence. Abu Ubaid chose to deliberately stop on it to conform to the language in adding the ha` in the pause and to conform to the script, meaning the script of the Mushaf. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Hamid, Mujahid, Al-A`mash, and Ya`qub read by deleting it when connecting and by adding it when stopping in all of these expressions. This reading was narrated from Hamza, and Abu Hatim chose this reading to follow the language. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Muhaisin that he read it without it, whether connected or stopped.
69:20: 20- Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account. That is, I knew and was certain in this world that I would be held accountable in the Hereafter. It was also said that the meaning is: I thought that God would take me to task for my misdeeds, but He has favored me with His forgiveness and has not held me accountable. Ad-Dahhak said: Every thought in the Qur’an from a believer is certainty, and from a disbeliever it is doubt. Mujahid said: Thought of the Hereafter is certainty, and thought of this world is doubt. Al-Hasan said about this verse: The believer has good thoughts about his Lord, so he does good deeds for the Hereafter, and the disbeliever has bad thoughts about his Lord, so he does bad deeds. It was said that the expression thought here indicates that belief is not undermined by the thoughts that come to mind, which are often inseparable from theoretical sciences.
69:21: 21- So he is in a pleasant life meaning in a life that is pleasing and not unpleasant, or one that is pleasing: meaning its owner is satisfied with it. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Farra’ said: Pleasant means pleasant like his saying: gushing water meaning gushing forth. He attributed to the life what belongs to its owner, and this was from the metaphor in the attribution.
69:22: 22- In a high paradise meaning a high place because it is in the sky, or high in status, or great in souls.
69:23: 23- Its fruits are within easy reach. Al-Qatuf: the plural of qatf, with a kasra on the qaf, is the fruit that is picked. Al-Qatf, with a fatha, is the verbal noun, and al-Qataf, with a fatha and a kasra, is the time of picking. The meaning is that its fruits are close to whoever eats them, whether standing, sitting, or lying down.
69:24: 24- Eat and drink meaning they will be told to eat and drink in Paradise at ease meaning eat and drink at ease, without any disturbance or bitterness for what you put forth in the past days meaning because of the righteous deeds you did in this world. Mujahid said: They are the days of fasting. But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say in grief and distress for what he saw of his bad deeds.
69:25: 25- I wish I had not been given my book. That is, I had not been given my book.
69:26: 26- And I did not know what my account was meaning I did not know: what my account was because it was all up to him.
69:27: 27- Oh, would that it had been the final judgment. That is, would that the death I died had been the final judgment, and that I had never lived again after it. The meaning of the final judgment is that it is the final judgment that ends life. The meaning is that he wished for eternal death and no resurrection because of what he saw of the evil of his deeds and the torment that would befall him. The pronoun in Oh, would that it had been refers to the death he had already died, even if it was not mentioned, because because it was obvious, it was like the one mentioned. Qatada said: He wished for [death], and there was nothing in this world that he hated more than it, and worse than death is that which death looms over. It was said that the pronoun refers to the state he saw when reading the book, and the meaning is: Oh, would that this state had been the death that was decreed for me.
69:28: 28- My wealth did not avail me meaning it did not protect me from God’s punishment at all, as ma is negative or interrogative, and the meaning is: what did my wealth avail me at all?
69:29: 29- My authority has perished from me meaning my proof has perished from me and gone astray from me. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, As-Suddi, and Ad-Dahhak said. Ibn Zayd said: It means my authority in this world, which is dominion. It was also said that it means my control over my limbs. Muqatil said: It means when his limbs testified that he was polytheistic.
69:30: Then God Almighty says: 30- Seize him and chain him, meaning, tie his hands to his neck with chains.
69:31: 31- Then throw him into Hell meaning, throw him into Hell. The meaning is: Do not throw him into anything but Hell, which is the great fire.
69:32: 32- Then in a chain seventy cubits long, so follow it. The chain is an ordered ring, and its cubit is its length. Al-Hasan said: God knows best which cubit it is. Nawf Al-Shami said: Each cubit is seventy cubits, each cubit is further than the distance between you and Mecca. Nawf was in the spacious Kufa. Muqatil said: If a ring of it were placed on the top of a mountain, it would melt like lead melts. The meaning of follow it is make it enter it. It is said that you entered the road if you put it in it. Sufyan said: We were informed that it enters a hole until it comes out of its mouth. Al-Kalbi said: It is followed by a thread through a pearl. Suwaid bin Abi Najih said: I was informed that all of the people of Hell are in that chain. The chain is mentioned first to indicate exclusivity, like Hell is mentioned first.
69:33: Sentence 33 - He did not believe in God Almighty is an explanation of what preceded it.
69:34: 34- And he does not encourage the feeding of the poor meaning he does not encourage feeding the poor from his own money, or he does not encourage others to feed him, and he puts food in place of feeding just as giving is put in place of giving, as the poet said: I am an infidel after you denied my death and gave me the terrifying money That is, after giving you, and it is permissible for food to have its meaning other than being used as a source, and the meaning is: that he does not urge himself or others to give the same food to the poor, and in making this a counterpart to abandoning faith in God of the encouragement to give charity to the poor and satisfy their need, and urging oneself and people to do that is what indicates most eloquently and provides the most complete benefit that preventing them is one of the greatest crimes and most severe sins.
69:35: 35- He will have no close friend here today meaning that on the Day of Resurrection in the Hereafter he will have no close friend who will benefit him or intercede for him, because it is a day on which the close will flee from his close friend, and the beloved will flee from his beloved.
69:36: 36- And no food except from two washings meaning he will have no food to eat except from the pus of the people of Hell, and what is washed from their bodies of [pus] and pus. Ghuslān is a verb from washing. Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: It is a tree that the people of Hell eat. Qatadah said: It is the worst of food. Ibn Zayd said: No one knows what it is or what Zaqqum is except God the Most High. And God the Almighty said in another place: And they will have no food except from thorny thorns so it is possible that thorns are the two washings. It was said that there is an inversion of the two meanings in this statement, and the meaning is that he has no hot water today except from two washings, on the basis that hot water is hot water. And no food meaning they will have no food to eat. There is no recourse to this inversion and inversion.
69:37: And sentence 37 - None shall eat it except the sinners is an adjective for ghaslin, and what is meant are the people of sins and the masters of transgressions. Al-Kalbi said: What is meant is polytheism. The majority read al-khaati'un with a hamza, and it is an active participle of khata if someone does something wrong deliberately, and the one who does it unintentionally is the one who does it unintentionally. Al-Zuhri, Talhah ibn Musarraf, and Al-Hasan read al-khaati'un with a damma on the ba' instead of a hamza. Nafi' read it in a narration from him with a damma on the ta' without a hamza.
69:39: 39- So I swear by what you see and what you do not see. This is a response to the polytheists’ statement, as if to say: The matter is not as you say, nor is it redundant. The meaning is: So I swear by what you see and what you do not see. Qatada said: I swear by all things, what is seen and what is not seen, so this includes all created things. It was said that la is not redundant, but rather it negates the oath, meaning I do not need an oath because the truth is clear in that, and the first is more appropriate.
69:40: 40- Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger. That is, the Qur’an is the recitation of a noble Messenger, meaning that the Messenger is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or it is the word conveyed by a noble Messenger. Al-Hasan, Al-Kalbi, and Muqatil said: He means Gabriel, and the evidence for that is His statement: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger, * Possessor of power and secure in the presence of the Lord of the Throne. In any case, the Qur’an is not the word of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor the word of Gabriel, peace be upon him, rather it is the word of God, so it is necessary to assume the recitation or conveyance.
69:41: 41- And it is not the saying of a poet as you claim because it is not from the types of poetry nor similar to it. You believe little meaning you believe a little faith, and you believe a little belief, and ma is redundant.
69:42: 42- nor by the word of a soothsayer as you claim, for soothsaying is another matter that has nothing in common with this. You remember little means you remember little, or for a short time you remember, and ma is redundant, and little in both places means negation: that is, you do not believe and you do not remember at all.
69:43: 43- A revelation from the Lord of the Worlds. The majority of scholars read it in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: i.e., it is a revelation. Abu Al-Sammak read it in the accusative case as a source with an implied verb: i.e., it was sent down, and the meaning is: It is the statement of a noble Messenger, and it is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds on his tongue.
69:44: 44- And even if you fabricated against Us some sayings meaning even if the Messenger, who is Muhammad, or Gabriel, as mentioned above, said that. Fabrication is making up a statement, and the meaning is: If he made up his own mind to do that and came up with it on his own authority. Slander is called fabrication because it is a forced statement, and every liar makes up his own lies. The majority of scholars read you say in the active form. It was also read in the passive form with some being raised. Ibn Dhakwan read and you say in the present tense. The sayings are the plural of sayings, and sayings are the plural of saying.
69:45: 45- We would have seized him by the right hand meaning with his right hand. Ibn Jarir said: This statement was made to express humiliation, as is the custom of people in seizing the hand of the one they are punishing. Al-Farra', Al-Mubarrad, Al-Zajjaj, and Ibn Qutaybah said: We would have seized him by the right hand meaning with force and power. Ibn Qutaybah said: He used the right hand in place of force because the strength of everything is in its right hand. This is similar to the saying of the poet: If a banner is raised for glory, a godmother will meet it on the right. And the other said: When I saw the sun shining, I took what I needed from it with my right hand.
69:46: 46- Then We would have cut off his aorta. The aorta is a vein that runs in the back until it connects to the heart. It is a depiction of his destruction by the most horrific thing that a slave does to those who are angry with him. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators say that it is the strings of the heart. End quote. And from this is the saying of the poet: If you reach me and carry my burden, Araba, then shine with the blood of the veins
69:47: 47- There is none of you who can prevent it meaning there is none of you who can prevent us from it and push us away from it, so how could he undertake to lie about God for your sake while he knows that if he were to undertake to do so, We would punish him and you would not be able to repel him? And prevention and deterrence, preventing is an attribute of one, or the report of what of Hijaziyyah.
69:48: 48- And indeed, it is a reminder for the righteous. That is, the Qur’an is a reminder for the righteous because they are the ones who benefit from it.
69:49: 49- And We know that among you are deniers. That is, some of you deny the Qur’an, so We will punish them for that, and in this there is a severe threat.
69:50: 50- And indeed, it is a regret for the disbelievers. That is, the Qur’an is a regret and remorse for the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection when they witness the reward of the believers. It was said that it is their regret in this world when they were not able to oppose it when it was told to them by producing a surah like it.
69:51: 51- And it is the absolute truth meaning that the Qur’an, because it is from God, is the truth, so there is no doubt about it and no suspicion about it.
69:52: 52- So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great, meaning, declare Him free from what is not befitting of Him. It was also said, Pray for your Lord, but the first is more appropriate. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Indeed, I thought, he said: I was certain. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, Its fruits are within reach, he said: Nearby. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Humaid, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ regarding the verse, he said: A man may take from its fruits while standing. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Then follow it, he said: The chain will enter his anus and then come out of his mouth, then they will string it around as locusts are strung around a stick and then it will be roasted. Abu Ubaid, Abd bin Humaid, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, he said: God has a chain from which the cauldrons of Hell have been boiling since He created Hell until the Day when it will be thrown around the necks of people. God has saved us from half of it through our faith in God the Almighty, so be eager to feed the poor, O Umm Al-Darda’. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The ghuslān are blood, water and pus that flows from their flesh. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khurdi on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: If a bucket of ghuslān were poured into this world, the people of this world would stink. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Ghuslān is the name of a food from the foods of the people of Hellfire. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority: So I swear by what you see and what you do not see means: by what you see and what you do not see. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: We would have seized him by the right hand he said: by power. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he said: Al-wateen is the vein of the heart. Al-Faryabi, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim also narrated on his authority that he said: Al-wateen is the tendon of the heart. Al-Mundhir and al-Hakim also narrated and authenticated it on his authority that he said: It is the cord of the heart in the back.
70:1: It is said that Surat Al-Ma'arij consists of forty-four verses. It is a Meccan surah. Al-Qurtubi said: By consensus. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Sa’ala was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar narration on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. His saying: 1- A questioner asked about an imminent torment. The majority of scholars read asked with a hamza, while Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read it without a hamza. Whoever adds a hamza, it is from asal which is the widespread language, and it either includes the meaning of supplication, so it is transitive with ba as you say I called for such and such, and the meaning is: a supplicant called for an imminent torment upon himself. It is also possible for it to be in its original form and ba to mean about, as in his saying: ask someone knowledgeable about it. Whoever does not add a hamza, it is either from the category of alleviation by changing the hamza to an alif, so its meaning is the same as the reading of whoever adds a hamza, or it is from saylan, and the meaning is: a valley in Hell called sayil flowed, as Zaid ibn Thabit said. This is supported by the reading of Ibn ‘Abbas sal and it was said that sal means to seek, and the meaning is: a seeker sought a torment for the disbelievers, so the ba is redundant as in his saying grown with oil, and the first interpretation is the apparent one. Al-Akhfash said: It is said that we went out to ask about so-and-so and so-and-so. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: If it is from the question, then its origin is to take two objects, but it is permissible to limit it to one of them and to take it transitive with a preposition.
