This questioner is Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith when he said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. He was among those who were killed patiently on the day of Badr. It was said that he was Abu Jahl, and it was said that he was Al-Harith ibn Al-Nu’man Al-Fahri. The first is more appropriate for what will come. Abi and Ibn Mas’ud read salā sal like malā mal on the basis that the origin is sā’il, so the ‘ayn was deleted for ease, just as it was said that shak is in sha’ik al-silāh. It was said that the questioner is Noah, peace be upon him, who asked for the punishment for the disbelievers. It was also said that he is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who called for punishment against them. His saying with a punishment to come means either in this world, like the day of Badr, or in the hereafter.
70:2: And his saying: 2- for the disbelievers is another description of the torment: meaning that it is for the disbelievers, or related to something that is real, and the lam is for the reason, or it is asked to include the meaning of called, or in the place of raising, estimating: it is for the disbelievers, or the lam is in the meaning of upon, and this is supported by Abu’s reading of a torment that will befall the disbelievers. Al-Farra’ said: The estimation is that the torment of the disbelievers will befall them, so reality is an attribute of the torment, and the phrase there is no repeller for it is another description of the torment, or a state of it, or a new sentence, and the meaning is: that no one can repel that torment that is befalling him.
70:3: And His statement: 3- From God is related to reality: meaning reality from His side, glory be to Him, or to a motive: meaning there is no motive from His side, the Most High: Of the Ascending Stairways meaning of the degrees through which the angels ascend. Al-Kalbi said: They are the heavens, and He called them Ascending Stairways because the angels ascend through them. It was said that Ascending Stairways are the ranks of God's blessings upon creation. It was said that Ascending Stairways are greatness, and it was said that they are the rooms. Ibn Masoud read Dhul-Ma'arij with the addition of a ya', and it is said that Ma'arij and Ma'arij are like Miftah and Mafatih.
70:4: 4- The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him meaning they ascend through the levels that God has made for them. The majority of scholars read ascends with a fat-ha, while Ibn Mas’ud and his companions, Al-Kisa’i and Al-Sulami read it with a dhamma. The Spirit is Gabriel, mentioned alone after the angels due to his honor. This is supported by His statement: The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down. It was also said that the Spirit here is another great angel other than Gabriel. Abu Salih said: It is from God’s creation in the form of people, but they are not from people. Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb said: It is the spirit of the dead person when it is taken, but the first is more appropriate. The meaning of to Him is to the place they will end up at. It was also said that it is to His Throne. It was also said that it is like the saying of Abraham, Indeed, I am going to my Lord, meaning to where my Lord has commanded me, on a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. Ibn Ishaq, Al-Kalbi, and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: meaning, the angels ascended to the place where they are located at a time the extent of which, if anyone else were to ascend, would be fifty thousand years. Mujahid also said the same. Ikrimah said: It was narrated from Mujahid that the duration of the life of this world is this amount. No one knows how much has passed or how much remains, and no one knows that except God. Qatadah, Al-Kalbi, and Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: What is meant is the Day of Resurrection, meaning that the extent of the matter on that day, if someone other than Him were to take charge of it, would be fifty thousand years, while He, the Exalted, would finish it in an hour. It was also said that the duration of the servants’ standing for judgment is this amount, then after that the people of Paradise and the people of Hell will settle in Hell. It is said that the duration of the Day of Resurrection for the unbelievers is fifty thousand years, and for the believers it is the duration between noon and afternoon. It is said that this duration was mentioned for the sake of illustration and imagination, due to the height of those ascents and the distance of their extent, or because of the length of the Day of Resurrection, considering the hardships and difficulties it contains, just as the Arabs describe the days of hardship as long and the days of joy as short, and they liken the short day to the thumb of a quail, and the long day to the shadow of a spear. From this is the saying of the poet: And a day like the shadow of a spear, its length was shortened, the blood of the wineskin was cut short for us, and the flowers lined up It was said in the speech that there is an inversion: that is, there is no repeller for it from God, the Lord of the Ascending Stairways. On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him. We have previously combined this verse with His statement in Surat As-Sajdah, On a Day the measure of which is a thousand years, so refer to it. It was said in the combination that from the lowest part of the world to the Throne is fifty thousand years, and from the highest of the lowest heaven to the Earth is a thousand years, because the thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and the distance between the lowest heaven and the bottom of the Earth is five hundred years. So the meaning is that if the angels ascend from the lowest part of the world to the Throne, the distance of that would be fifty thousand years, and if they ascend from this earth that we are in to the interior of this heaven, which is the lowest heaven, the distance of that would be a thousand years. And we will come at the end of the discussion with what supports this from Ibn Abbas.
70:5: Then God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be patient, saying: 5- So be patient with beautiful patience. That is, be patient, O Muhammad, with their denial of you and their disbelief in what you have brought, with beautiful patience, without worry or complaint to anyone other than God. This is the meaning of beautiful patience. It was said that it is when the one afflicted among the people does not know that he has been afflicted. Ibn Zayd and others said: It was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
70:6: 6- They see it as far off meaning they see the punishment that will befall them, or they see the Day of Resurrection as far off: meaning not happening because they do not believe in it. So the meaning of far off is remote and impossible, and it does not mean that they see it as far off and not near. Al-A’mash said: They see the resurrection as far off because they do not believe in it, as if they are ruling it out as impossible, just as you say to someone you are debating, This is far off, meaning it will not happen.
70:7: 7- And We see it near meaning we know it will be near, because what is coming is near. It has also been said that the meaning is: And We see it as easy in Our power, not difficult or impossible, and the sentence explains the command to be patient.
70:8: Then the Almighty informed us when the punishment will befall them, saying: 8- The Day the sky will be like molten copper. The adverbial phrase is related to an implied noun indicated by a real event, or in apposition to His statement: On a Day, assuming it is related to a real event, or related to something close, or implied to come after it: that is, the Day when, etc., such and such was, or in apposition to the pronoun in We see, and the first is more appropriate. The meaning is that the punishment will befall them The Day the sky will be like molten copper. Molten copper is what is melted of copper, lead, and silver. Mujahid said: It is the pus from blood. Ikrimah and others said: It is the dregs of oil, and its interpretation has been presented in Surat Al-Kahf and Al-Dukhan.
70:9: 9- And the mountains will be like wool meaning like dyed wool. Wool is only called wool if it is dyed. Al-Hasan said: The mountains will be like wool, which is red wool, and it is the weakest wool. It was said that wool is the wool with colors, so he likened the mountains to it in their formation of colors as in his saying: white and red "and black ravens, so when they are dried and flown in the air they resemble patterned wool when the wind blows it.
70:10: 10- And no intimate friend will ask a intimate friend meaning, no intimate friend will ask his intimate friend about his condition on that Day, due to the severity of the horrors that have befallen them, which have made a relative forgetful of his relative, and a friend forgetful of his friend, as God the Almighty said: Every man among them, that Day, will have enough to make him indifferent to his intimate friend. It was also said that the meaning is: No intimate friend will ask about a intimate friend, so the preposition was dropped and the verb was connected. The majority of scholars read No intimate friend will ask about a intimate friend. It was also said that the second object was dropped, and the meaning is: No one will ask him for his victory or intercession. Abu Ja`far, Abu Haywah, Shaybah, and Ibn Kathir, in a narration from him, read it in the passive form. Al-Bazzi narrated this reading from Asim, and the meaning is: No intimate friend will ask about the presence of his intimate friend. It was also said that this reading is based on the omission of the preposition, meaning: No intimate friend will ask about a intimate friend, but rather every person will be asked about himself and his deeds.
70:11: And the sentence 11- they see them is a new sentence, or an attribute of His saying: intimate friend meaning every intimate friend sees his intimate friend, none of them is hidden from anyone else. And there is no creature on the Day of Resurrection except that he is the focus of attention of his companion, and they do not ask questions nor speak to each other because each one of them is busy with himself. Ibn Zayd said: God sees the disbelievers in the Fire who led them astray in this world and they are the leaders who are followed. And it was said that His saying: they see them refers to the angels: meaning they know the conditions of the people and nothing is hidden from them. And the pronoun in they see them is plural, and they refer to the two intimate friends, based on the meaning of generality, because they are two indefinite nouns in the context of negation. The majority read they see them with emphasis, and Qatadah read it with emphasis. Then the Almighty began speaking and said: The criminal would wish that he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day. What is meant by the criminal is the disbeliever, or every person who commits a sin that deserves Hell, if he could ransom himself from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection that has befallen him.
70:12: 12- his sons, his wife, and his brother These are the dearest and most honorable people to him, so if he had accepted their ransom, he would have ransomed himself with them and been saved from the torment that had befallen him. The sentence is a new sentence to show that the preoccupation of every criminal with himself reached the point of the Day of Redemption from the torment by whomever was mentioned. The majority read from the torment of that Day by adding torment to that Day. Abu Haywah read it with the tanween of torment and cutting off the addition. The majority read that Day with a kasra on the meem, while Nafi', Al-Kisa'i, Al-A'raj, and Abu Haywah read it with a fatha on it.
70:13: 13- And his clan that shelters him meaning his closest relatives who include him in bloodlines or in times of hardship and to whom he seeks shelter. Abu Ubaid said: The clan is below the tribe. Tha'lab said: They are their closest fathers. Al-Mubarrad said: The clan is a part of the body. A man's clan is called a fashlah as it resembles a part of him. Malik said: The clan is the one that raises him.
70:14: 14- And all those on earth meaning, the criminal would wish that he could ransom himself with all those on earth, from the two heavy burdens and other creatures. His statement, Then He would save him is connected to ransoms meaning, on the day if he ransomed himself, then the ransom would save him. The connection with Then is because it indicates the improbability of salvation. It was said that wishes requires an answer, as in His statement, They would wish that you would compromise so they would compromise. The answer is Then He would save him, and the first is more appropriate.
70:15: And His saying: 15- No is a deterrent to the criminal from that friendship, and a clarification of the impossibility of what he wanted of ransom, and No comes with the meaning of truly and with the meaning of no while including the meaning of deterrence and restraint, and the pronoun in His saying: It is a blazing fire is for Hell, and its derivation is from blazing in the fire, which is blazing, and it was said that its origin is laza meaning the continuation of torment, so one of the two dhas was changed to an alif, and it was said that laza is the second level of the levels of Hell.
70:16: 16- Naz'ah li-shwa The majority read Naz'ah in the nominative case as a second predicate for in, or predicate of a deleted subject, or laza is a substitute for the accusative pronoun, and Naz'ah is the predicate of in, or that Naz'ah is an attribute of laza on the assumption that it is not a proper noun, or the pronoun in inha is for the story, and laza is the subject and Naz'ah is its predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of in. Hafs read from Asim, Abu Amr in a narration from him, Abu Haywah, al-Zughfranī, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Muqsim Naz'ahan in the accusative case as a state. Abu Ali al-Farsi said: It is far-fetched to carry it as a state because there is nothing in the speech that acts on the state. It was said that the agent in it is what the speech indicates of the meaning of talthathi, or the accusative case as a specification, and shwa is the extremities, or the plural of shawwat, which is the scalp, and from this is the saying of al-A'sha: She said, His money has turned his hair white. Al-Hasan and Thabit Al-Bunani said: It strips away the flesh and skin from the bones, leaving nothing behind. Al-Kisa’i said: It refers to the joints. Abu Salih said: It refers to the extremities of the hands and feet.
70:17: 17- You call upon whoever turns away meaning you call upon the blazing fire of whoever turns away from the truth in this world and turns away meaning they turn away from it.
70:18: 18- And he gathered and stored meaning he gathered the money and put it in a container. It was said that it says to me, O polytheist, to me, O hypocrite. It was also said that the meaning of you call is you perish. The Arabs say: May God call you, meaning He destroyed you. It was also said that it is not a verbal call, but that her calling them enables her to punish them. It was also said that what is meant is that the keepers of Hell call upon the disbelievers and hypocrites, so the call is attributed to the Fire, by way of attributing what is for the state to the place. It was also said that it is a metaphor and imagination, and there is no call in reality. The meaning is that their destination is to it, as the poet said: We descended into the valley among our leaders, calling to our companions the mute, groaning one. The mute fly is the fly that does not call. This is a criticism of the one who has collected money, stored it, and hoarded it, but did not spend it on charitable causes, or did not pay its zakat. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Humayd, Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, A questioner asked, that he was Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith. He said, O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky. And regarding his statement, a punishment to come to pass, that is, it will come to pass. For the disbelievers, there is none to avert it * From God, Lord of the Ascending Stairways, that is, the Possessor of degrees. Abd bin Humayd and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, A questioner asked, that he said, a valley in Hell flowed. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, Lord of the Ascending Stairways, that he said, Lord of the lofty heights and virtues. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement, On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The end of His Command from the lowest parts of the earth to the end of His Command above the seven heavens is the measure of fifty thousand years. And on a Day the measure of which is a thousand years, he said: By that he means that the Command descends from the heaven to the earth and from the earth to the heaven in one day, so that is the measure of a thousand years, because the distance between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, he said: The thickness of each earth is five hundred years, and the thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and between each earth is five hundred years, and from heaven to heaven is five hundred years, so that is his statement, On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba’th also narrated from him regarding his statement, On a Day the measure of which is a thousand years of those which you count, he said: This is in this world, the angels ascend on a Day the measure of which is a thousand years of those which you count. And regarding his statement, On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, this is the Day of Resurrection, which God has made for the disbeliever the measure of fifty thousand years. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi also narrated from him regarding his statement, On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: If you had estimated it, it would be fifty thousand years of your days. He said: He means the Day of Resurrection. We have already mentioned from Ibn Abbas the pause in combining the two verses in Surat As-Sajdah. Ahmad, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th from Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri who said: It was said, O Messenger of God, a day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, how long is this day? He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is made light for the believer until it is easier for him than an obligatory prayer that he prays in this world. In its chain of transmission is Darraj from Abu Al-Haytham, and they are both weak. Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Ba’th from Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, who said: The length of the Day of Resurrection has not been estimated for the believers except as the time between Dhuhr and Asr. Al-Hakim At-Tirmidhi narrated in Nawadir Al-Usul from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, So be patient with beautiful patience, he said: Do not complain to anyone but me. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Ban Al-Mundhir, Al-Khatib in Al-Muttafaq wa Al-Muftariq, and Al-Dhiya in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The Day the sky will be like molten copper, he said: Like the dregs of oil. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: They will see them, they will recognize each other and get to know each other, then they will flee from each other. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, One who pulls out the hair, he said: It will pull out the mother of the head.
70:19: His saying: 9- Indeed, mankind was created impatient. It is said in Al-Sahah: Panic in the language is the most intense greed and the worst and most obscene impatience. It is said panic with a kasra, so it is panic and panic with emphasis. And Ikrimah said: It is impatience.
70:20: Al-Wahidi said: The commentators say that the interpretation of panic is what follows it, meaning his statement: 20- If evil touches him, he is impatient.
70:21: Al-Wahidi said: The commentators say that the interpretation of panic is what follows it, meaning his statement: 21- If evil touches him, he is impatient * And if good touches him, he withholds it meaning if poverty, need, sickness, or something similar befalls him, then he is impatient: that is, he is very impatient. And if good touches him, such as wealth, fertility, plenty, or something similar, then he withholds and holds back a lot. Abu Ubaidah said: The impatient is the one who, if good touches him, does not give thanks, and if evil touches him, he is not patient. Tha’lab said: God has interpreted the impatient as: He who, if evil touches him, shows intense impatience, and if good touches him, he is miserly with it and people withhold it from him. The Arabs say: A she-camel is impatient and irritable if she walks quickly and lightly. From this comes the saying of the poet: A fox complained that if you turned away from her, she would be embarrassed and if you faced her, she would be frightened. Al-Dha’laba: the fast camel. The nouns frightened, “angry,” and manuwa are in the accusative case because they are predetermined or realized conditions due to them being the natures of the human being. The two adverbials are used for frightened and manuwa.
70:22: 22- Except those who pray meaning those who establish prayer. It was said that what is meant by them are the people of monotheism: meaning that they do not have those characteristics of panic, anxiety, and refusal, and that they have praiseworthy characteristics and pleasing traits, because their faith and what they have held fast to of monotheism and the religion of truth deters them from having those characteristics, and compels them to have good characteristics.
70:23: Then He, the Most High, explained it by saying: 23- Those who are constant in their prayers meaning nothing distracts them from them, and nothing turns them away from them. Constantly does not mean that they pray forever. Al-Zajjaj said: They are those who do not move their faces from the direction of the Qiblah. Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj said: It is the voluntary prayers. Al-Nakha’li said: What is meant by those who pray are those who perform the prescribed prayers, and it was said that it is those who pray at its appointed time. The verse refers to all believers, and it was said that it refers to the Companions in particular. There is no basis for this specification since every believer is described as one of those who pray.
70:24: 24- And those in whose wealth there is a recognized right. Qatada and Muhammad ibn Sirin said: What is meant is the obligatory zakat. Mujahid said: Other than zakat. It was also said: It refers to maintaining kinship ties. The apparent meaning is zakat because it is described as being a recognized right and because it is linked to prayer. The explanation of the beggar and the deprived has been presented in full in Surat Adh-Dhariyat.
70:25: 25- For the needy and the deprived.
70:26: 26- And those who believe in the Day of Judgment meaning the Day of Recompense, which is the Day of Resurrection, do not doubt it or deny it. It was said that they believe in it through their deeds, so they exhaust themselves in acts of obedience.
70:27: 27- And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord meaning they are afraid and apprehensive despite their acts of obedience, out of contempt for their deeds and acknowledgment of what is due from God Almighty upon them.
70:28: Sentence 28 - Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not safe confirms the content of what preceded it, explaining that this is something that no one should be safe from, and that everyone has the right to fear it.
70:29: 29- And those who guard their private parts to His saying: Then it is those who are the transgressors. Its interpretation has been presented in full in Surat Al-Mu’minun.
70:30: 30- Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed.
70:31: 31- But whoever seeks beyond that - then it is those who are the transgressors. Its explanation has been presented in full in Surat Al-Mu’minun.
70:32: 32- And those who are to their trusts and their covenants attentive. That is, they do not fail in any of the trusts with which they are entrusted, nor do they break any of the covenants they make. The majority of scholars read li-la-maanaatihim in the plural. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaisin read li-la-maanaatihim in the singular, but what is meant is the genus.
70:33: 33- And those who uphold their testimonies meaning they uphold them against whoever they are against, whether near or far, high or low, and they do not conceal them or change them. We have already discussed the testimony in Surat Al-Baqarah. The majority of scholars read uphold their testimonies in the singular form, while Hafs and Ya’qub, and it is a narration from Ibn Kathir, read it in the plural form. Al-Wahidi said: The singular form is more appropriate because it is a verbal noun, and whoever puts it in the plural goes for the difference in the testimonies. Al-Farra’ said: The reading of monotheism is indicated by the Almighty’s statement: And uphold the testimony for God.
70:34: 34- And those who are constant in their prayers meaning, in their remembrances, pillars, and conditions, not failing in any of them. Qatada said: in their ablution, bowing, and prostration. Ibn Jurayj said: What is meant is voluntary prayer. He repeated the mention of prayer because of the difference in what He described them with first, and what He described them with second. The meaning of constant is that one does not become distracted from it by anything, as mentioned previously. The meaning of conserving is that one observes the matters without which prayer is not valid. It was said that what is meant is that they conserve it after performing it, so that they do not do anything that would nullify it or invalidate its reward. The relative pronouns were repeated to indicate that each of those descriptions, due to His Majesty, deserves to have a separate description.
70:35: And the reference in his saying: 35- Those is to those described with those attributes in gardens, honored meaning they are settled there, honored with various types of honors. The predicate of the subject is his saying: in gardens and his saying: honored is another predicate, and it is possible for the predicate to be honored, and in gardens is related to it.
70:36: 36- So what is the matter with those who disbelieved before you, that they are rushing about? That is, what is the matter with them, that they are rushing about you? Al-Akhfash said: rushing about, and from this is the saying of the poet: In Mecca, its people, and I saw them rushing to it to listen. It was said that the meaning is: Why do they rush to you and sit around you and do not do what you command them? And it was said: Why are they so quick to deny? And it was said: What is wrong with those who disbelieve that they rush to listen to you and deny you and mock you? Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is: Rushing and looking at you. Qatada said: Intending. And it was said: Rushing towards you, stretching out their necks, looking at you with longing.
70:37: 37- On the right and on the left, two groups meaning on the right and left of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, there are scattered groups. And two groups is with azzah, which is a group of people. From this comes the poet’s saying: We are at his house, and the night is dark at his doors, and we are in mourning The shepherd said: Khalifa Al-Rahman, my clan has become proud of you. Antara said: And a horn I left with me, and the bird has a strong nerve on it. It is said that its origin is Azwa from Al-Azwa, as if each group attributes itself to someone other than the one to whom the other attributes itself. It says in Al-Sahah: Azwa is a group of people, and the Haa replaces the Baa, and the plural is Azzi and Azun, and his saying: on the right and on the left is related to Azin, or to Mahtaayin.
70:38: 38- Does every man among them aspire to enter a Garden of Delight? The commentators said: All the polytheists say, If these people enter Paradise, we will enter before them. So the verse was revealed. The majority of scholars read that he enters in the passive form. Al-Hasan, Zaid bin Ali, Talhah bin Musarraf, Al-A'raj, Yahya bin Ya'mar, Abu Raja', and Asim, in a narration from him, read it in the active form.
70:39: Then God Almighty responded to them and said: 39- No indeed! We created them from that which they know. That is, from the filth that they know, so this arrogance is not appropriate for them. It was said that the meaning is: We created them for the sake of what they know, which is compliance with the command and prohibition and exposure to reward and punishment as in His saying: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. And from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: Did you decide to innovate with the family of Layla and did you dare to visit the one who loves you? Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about the anxious person and he said: It is as God says: When evil touches him, he is impatient, but when good touches him, he withholds it. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority: Anxious he said: The greedy. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in al-Musannaf on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud: Those who are constant in their prayers he said: At their appointed times. Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn: Those who are constant in their prayers he said: The one who does not turn away during his prayer. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir: Those who are constant in their prayers he said: They are the ones who do not turn away when they pray. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated something similar from him through another chain of narration. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then what is the matter with those who disbelieved before you that they are rushing about? He said: They are looking. On the right and on the left in groups. He said: The group of people turned away to the right and left, mocking him. Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the mosque while we were in separate groups, and he said: What is the matter with you that I see you in groups? Ahmad, Ibn Majah, Ibn Sa`d, Ibn Abi `Asim, Al-Bawardi, Ibn Qani`, Al-Hakim, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu`ab, and Al-Dhiya` narrated on the authority of Bishr bin Jahash, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited God's Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So what about those who disbelieved before you? They are hasty. Until His saying: "No indeed. Indeed, We created them from that which they know." Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spat into his palm and placed his finger on it and said: God says, O son of Adam, how can you outstrip Me when I created you from something like this, until, when I proportioned you and made you proportionate, you walked between two cool places, and the earth was slow from you. So you gathered and withheld until, when it reached the collarbones, I said, Or the time for charity has come.
70:40: His statement: 40- "So I swear is an extra la" as mentioned earlier, and the meaning is: So I swear "by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests" meaning the East and West of every day of the year. The majority of scholars read "the Easts and the Wests" in the plural, while Abu Haywah, Ibn Muhaysin, and Hamid read it in the singular.
70:41: 41- Indeed, We are able * to substitute for them better than them meaning, to create better than them, more obedient to God when they disobeyed Him, and to destroy these people. And We are not to be outdone meaning, we are to be defeated if We wished to do so. Rather, We do what We wish, nothing escapes Us and nothing is beyond Our power. But Our will and foreknowledge required Us to delay the punishment of these people and not replace them with another creation.
70:42: 42- So leave them to plunge into falsehood and play. That is, leave them to plunge into their falsehood and play in their worldly life, and occupy yourself with what you have been commanded to do and do not let their situation be too difficult for you, for you are only required to convey the message. until they meet the Day they are promised. Which is the Day of Resurrection. This verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword. The majority of scholars read it as they will meet. Abu Ja`far, Ibn Muhaysin, Hamid, and Mujahid read it as until they meet.
70:44: 44- Their eyes will be humbled is in the accusative case, in the state of the pronoun they will disperse, and their eyes will be raised to it. Humility is humiliation and submission: meaning they will not raise them to what they expect of the punishment. Humiliation will overwhelm them means severe humiliation will overwhelm them. Qatada said: It is the blackness of the faces, and from it is the word a teenage boy: if puberty overwhelms him. It is said he humiliated him with the kasra, he humiliated him, meaning it overtook him. Similar to this is His statement: Nor will darkness or humiliation overwhelm their faces, and the reference in His statement: that is to what was mentioned previously. It is a subject and its predicate is the Day which they were promised, meaning that which they were promised in this world through the tongues of the messengers has overtaken them and is present, and what God promised them of His punishment has befallen them, even if it is future, so it is considered as something that has already happened because it has come to pass. Sa`id ibn Mansur, `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests, that he said: The sun has a place where it rises every day and a place where it sets, different from its place of rising and different from its place of setting yesterday. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, To a place they hasten, that he said: To a place of knowledge they hasten.
71:1: It has twenty-nine or twenty-eight verses and is Meccan. Ibn Al-Durais, Al-Nahhas, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, who said: Indeed, We sent Noah was revealed in Mecca. His saying: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people. It has been mentioned previously that Noah was the first messenger sent by God, and he is Noah, son of Lamech, son of Methuselah, son of Akhnon, son of Cainan, son of Seth, son of Adam. The length of his stay among his people, the entirety of his lifespan, and the age at which he was sent were mentioned in Surat al-Ankabut 29:Warn your people. That is, warn, as it is a source. It is also possible that it is the explanatory particle, because sending has the meaning of saying. Ibn Mas’ud read warned without that, and that is based on the assumption of saying, that is, So We said to him, ‘Warn,’ before there comes to them a painful punishment, that is, a punishment of extreme pain, which is the punishment of the Fire. Al-Kalbi said: It is what befell them of the flood.
71:2: Sentence 2- He said, ‘O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner.’ is a resumption of rhetorical resumption in the sense of a question, as if it was said: So what did Noah say? He said: He said to them, etc. The meaning is: Indeed, I am to you a warner of God’s punishment, frightening you, and explaining what will save you.
71:3: 3- Worship God and fear Him and obey me. “That” is the explanatory particle of warner, or it is the source: that is, worship God and do not associate anyone with Him and fear Him: that is, avoid what will cause you to fall into His punishment and obey what I command you to do, for I am a messenger to you from God.
71:4: 4- He will forgive you some of your sins. This is the answer to the command. Min is for partiality: meaning some of your sins, which are those that occurred before obeying the Messenger and answering his call. Al-Suddi said: The meaning is He will forgive you your sins, so Min is redundant in this case. It was also said that what is meant by some is that which is not related to the rights of people. It was also said that it is to clarify the type. It was also said that He will forgive you of your sins what you seek forgiveness for. "And He will delay you for a specified term." That is, He will delay your death to the maximum period that God has determined for you on the condition of faith and obedience, beyond what He has determined for you, assuming that you remain in disbelief and disobedience. It was also said that delay means blessing in their lives if they believe and lack of blessing in them if they do not believe. Muqatil said: He will delay you until the end of your appointed terms. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, He will delay you from the punishment so that you die a death other than that of those who are uprooted by punishment. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is that He will not cause you to die by drowning, burning, or killing. "Indeed, the term of God, when it comes, cannot be delayed." That is, whatever punishment He has decreed for you based on your remaining in disbelief, if it comes while you are remaining in disbelief, it will not be delayed, but will inevitably occur, so hasten to believe and obey. It was also said that the meaning is: Indeed, the term of God, which is death, when it comes, you will not be able to believe. It was also said that the meaning is: If death comes, it will not be delayed, whether it is with a punishment or without a punishment. "If you only knew," that is, some knowledge, you would have hastened to what I have commanded you to do, or you would have known that when the term of God comes, it will not be delayed.
71:5: 5- He said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have called my people night and day.’ That is, Noah said, calling to his Lord and narrating to Him what had happened between him and his people, and He knew it better than him: I have called my people to what You commanded me to call them to of faith, a constant call, night and day, without falling short.
71:6: 6- My supplication only increased their flight from what I had called them to and their distance from it. Muqatil said: It means distancing themselves from faith, and attributing the increase to the supplication because it is its cause, as in His statement: It increased their faith. The majority of scholars read my supplication with a fat-ha on the ya', while the Kufians, Ya'qub, and al-Duri, on the authority of Abu Amr, read it with a sukun on it. The exception is empty.
71:7: 7- And whenever I called them to be forgiven meaning whenever I called them to the cause of forgiveness, which is belief in You and obedience to You, they put their fingers in their ears so that they would not hear My voice, “and covered their faces with them so that they would not see Me. It was also said that they put their garments over their heads so that they would not hear My words, so covering their ears in this way is an additional blocking of the ears. It was also said that it is a metaphor for enmity. It is said that someone wore the garments of enmity, and it was also said that they covered themselves with their garments so that He would not recognize them and call them. “And they persisted” meaning they persisted in disbelief and did not abandon it or repent from it. And they were arrogant about accepting the truth and obeying what He commanded them with extreme arrogance.
71:8: 8- Then I called them openly meaning, I showed them the call and declared it to them.
71:9: 9- Then I announced to them meaning I called them openly with the supplication and I whispered to them secretly meaning I whispered the supplication to them secretly, it was said that the meaning is that a man calls after another, speaking to him secretly between him and him, and the intended meaning is that he called them in different ways and different ways. But that did not work with them. Mujahid said: The meaning of announced is spoken out, and it was said that the meaning of secretly is: I came to them in their homes and called them there. The word publicly is in the accusative case because supplication can be made public or not. So, publicly is from supplication, like their saying: He sat cross-legged. It is permissible for it to be an adjective of a deleted source: meaning a public supplication, or for it to be a source in the place of a state: meaning openly. The meaning of then is to indicate the distance between the states, because speaking publicly is more severe than speaking secretly, and combining the two is more wrong than either of them. The public read inni with a silent yaa, while Abu Amr and the Haramiyyun read it with a fatha.
71:10: 10- “So I said, ‘Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever-Forgiving.’” That is, ask Him for forgiveness for your previous sins with sincere intentions. Indeed, He is ever-Forgiving. That is, He is ever-forgiving of sinners. It was said that the meaning of ask forgiveness is: repent from disbelief. Indeed, He is ever-Forgiving of those who repent.
71:11: 11- He sends down upon you abundant rain meaning He sends down water from the sky upon you, so there is an implied meaning in this. It was said that what is meant by the sky is rain, as in the poet’s saying: If the sky descends upon the land of a people, we will take care of them, even if they are angry. Al-Mudrar: Al-Durur, which is the milking by rain. Its accusative case is either as a state of the sky, and it is not made feminine because Mif’alan is not made feminine. A woman says: Mi’nath and Mudhkar. Or it is an adjective for a deleted source: meaning sending abundantly. We have already discussed this in Surat Al-An’am. The word Yirsul is made jussive because it is the answer to the command.
71:12: This verse is evidence that seeking forgiveness is one of the greatest causes of rain and obtaining various types of provisions. That is why God said: 12- And He will give you increase in wealth and children and provide for you gardens meaning orchards and provide for you rivers flowing. Ata’ said: The meaning is He will increase your wealth and children. Noah, peace be upon him, informed them that their faith in God would bring them together with abundant fortune in the Hereafter, fertility and wealth in this world.
71:13: 13- What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? That is, what excuse do you have for abandoning hope? Hope here means fear: that is, what is the matter with you that you do not fear God? Reverence comes from reverence, which is glorification. The meaning is that you do not fear the truth of His greatness, so you unify Him and obey Him. Do not hope is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun for those being addressed, and the factor in it is the meaning of stability in for you. Among the applications of hope to fear is the saying of Al-Hudhali: If a bee stings him, he will not be stung by it Saeed bin Jubair, Abu Al-Aaliyah and Ata bin Abi Rabah said: Why do you not hope for God’s reward and fear His punishment? Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: Why do you not care about God’s greatness? Qatrib said: This is a Hijazi dialect. Hudhayl, Khuza’ah and Mudar say: I did not hope, I did not experience. Qatadah said: Why do you not hope for God’s reward for your faith? Ibn Kaysan said: Why do you not hope that He will reward you for your reverence and worship of God with good? Ibn Zayd said: Why do you not perform acts of obedience to God? Al-Hasan said: Why do you not recognize God’s right and thank Him for His blessings?
71:14: And the sentence 14- And He has created you in stages is in the accusative case as a state: meaning that the state is that He, glory be to Him, has created you in different stages: a sperm-drop, then a lump of flesh, then a clot until the completion of creation as was explained in Surat Al-Mu'minun. And the stage in the language is bitter, and Ibn Al-Anbari said: The stage is the state and its plural is stages, and it was said stages are children then young men then old men, and it was said that the heights are their differences in actions, sayings and morals, and the meaning is: How do you fall short in reverence for the One who created you in these wonderful stages.
71:15: 15- Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers? The address is to whomever is appropriate for it, and the intent is to prove by the creation of the heavens the perfection of His power and the wonder of His creation, and that He is the One worthy of worship. The layers are identical, one above the other, each heaven over the other like domes. Al-Hasan said: God created seven heavens upon seven earths, between each heaven and heaven and earth and earth He created and commanded. The confirmation of this has been presented in His statement: And of the earth the like of them. The accusative of tabaqan is a verbal noun, you say tabaqah as tabaqan and tabaqan, or a state meaning the essence of layers, so tabaq was deleted and tabaqan was used in its place. Al-Farra’ permitted the genitive of tabaqan in places other than the Qur’an as an adjective.
71:16: 16- And He made the moon a light therein meaning illuminating the face of the earth. He made the moon in the heavens even though it is in the lowest heaven, because if it is in one of them, then it is in them, as Ibn Kaysan said. Al-Akhfash said: Just as you say, The Banu Tamim came to me, meaning some of them. Qatrib said, in them means with them, meaning He created the moon and the sun along with the creation of the heavens and the earth, as in the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: And will someone whose last period was thirty months enjoy three conditions? That is, with three conditions: And He made the sun a lamp, that is, like a lamp for the people of the earth, so that they may continue to do what they need for sustenance.
71:17: 17- And God caused you to grow from the earth as a plant meaning that God created Adam from the surface of the earth, and the meaning is: He created you from it as a creation. So, growing was borrowed for creating because it is more indicative of occurrence and formation. And plant is either a verbal noun for anbat with the omission of the extra letters or a verbal noun for a deleted verb: i.e. He caused you to grow from the earth and you grew as a plant. Al-Khalil and Al-Zajjaj said: It is a verbal noun for a deleted verb: i.e. He caused you to grow from the earth and you grew as a plant. Al-Khalil and Al-Zajjaj said: It is a verbal noun based on the meaning, because the meaning of anbatakum is: He made you grow as a plant. And it was said that the meaning is: God caused you to grow from the earth as a plant, so plant according to this is the direct object. Ibn Bahr said: He caused them to grow in the earth in size after smallness and in height after shortness.
71:18: 18- Then He will return you to it meaning to the earth and bring you out a final bringing you out meaning He will bring you out of it by resurrection on the Day of Resurrection.
71:19: 19- And God has made the earth a carpet for you meaning He has spread it out and extended it for you to roll over on it as you roll over on your carpets in your homes.
71:20: 20- So that you may take from it wide paths meaning wide roads. Fajaj is the plural of fajj, which is the wide road, as Al-Farra’ and others said. It was also said that fajj is the path between two mountains. This has been fully explained in Surat Al-Anbiya’ and in Surat Al-Hajj. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, They put their fingers in their ears, he said: so that they would not hear what he was saying. And covered themselves with their garments, he said: so that they would not be recognized. And were arrogant with great arrogance, he said: they abandoned repentance. Sa’id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, And covered themselves with their garments, he said: they covered their faces so that they would not see Noah or hear his words. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’b also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, Why do you not have due respect for God? He said: you do not know the greatness of God. Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi also narrated on his authority, Dignity, he said: greatness. Regarding his statement, And He has created you in stages, he said: a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, he said: you do not fear punishment for Him nor do you expect a reward for Him. Abdul Razzaq narrated in Al-Musannaf on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people bathing naked, without any garments on them. He stood and called out at the top of his voice, ‘What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God?’” Abdul Razzaq, Abdul ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: “The faces of the sun and the moon are towards the sky and their backs are towards the earth. I will recite to you that it is from the Book of God, ‘And He made the moon a light therein and made the sun a lamp.’” Abdul ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh narrated in Al-Azmah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: It gives light to the inhabitants of the heavens as it gives light to the inhabitants of the earth. Abdul ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: “Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-As and Ka’b Al-Ahbar met and there had been some disagreement between them, so they rebuked each other, but that went away. Abdullah ibn Amr said to Ka’b, ‘Ask me whatever you wish, and do not ask me about anything unless I tell you that which confirms what I say from the Quran.’ He said to him, ‘Have you seen the light of the sun and the moon? Is it in the seven heavens as it is on the earth?’” He said: Ya-Sin 36:Have you not seen the statement of God: God created seven heavens in layers * And made the moon a light within them and made the sun a lamp. And Abd bin Hamid and Abu Sheikh in Al-Azma and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And made the moon a light within them meaning: His face is in the sky towards the Throne and his back is towards the earth. And Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Saleh on his authority: And made the moon a light within them meaning: He created when He created them a light for the people of the earth, and there is nothing of His light in the sky. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority: wide paths meaning: different paths.
71:21: His saying: 21- Noah said, ‘My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me’ meaning they continued to disobey me and did not answer my call. He complained about them to God, the Almighty, and He delayed it by saying that they disobeyed him and did not follow him, and He knows best about that. And they followed one whose wealth and children only increase him in loss meaning the lesser ones followed their leaders, and the wealthy among them whose abundance of wealth and children only increased them in misguidance in this world and punishment in the hereafter. The saying of the people of Medina, Ash-Sham, and Asim and his children is with the opening of the waw and the lam. The rest read it with the sukoon of the lam, and it is a language for children, and it is permissible for it to be a plural, and its investigation has been presented. The meaning of and they followed is that they continued to follow them, not that they innovated the following.
71:22: 22- And they plotted a great plot meaning a great and immense plot. It is said: big and big and big like amazing and amazing and amazing and “beautiful... are readers for someone who reads a lot. Ibn Al-Sikkit recited: White hunts hearts and seizes the hearts of Muslims with beauty The majority read kabaran with emphasis. Ibn Mahisan, Hamid, and Mujahid read it with emphasis. Abu Bakr said: It is the plural of kabir big, as if he replaced dhunub sins or af'ail deeds, and that is why he described it as plural. Isa ibn Umar said: It is a Yemeni dialect. There is a difference of opinion about their plot: What was it? Some say it was to incite their lowly ones to kill Noah. Others say it was to deceive the people with the wealth and children they were given, until the weak said: If it were not for the truth, they would not have been given these blessings. Al-Kalbi said: It is the wife and children they gave to God. Muqatil said: It is the words of their leaders to their followers: Do not abandon your gods. Others say their plot was their disbelief.
71:23: 23- "And they said, 'Do not abandon your gods,' meaning, do not abandon the worship of your gods, which were the idols and images that they had, and which the Arabs later worshipped. This is what the majority said: "And do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr." Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: These are the names of righteous people who lived between Adam and Noah. After them, a people arose who followed their example in worship. Satan said to them, "If you made images of them, it would be more energizing for you and more likely to worship them." So they did. Then a people arose after them and Satan said to them, "Those who were before you worshipped them, so worship them." So the worship of idols began at that time, and these images were given these names because they made them in the image of those people. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others said: These were names of the sons of Adam, and Wadd was the eldest of them. Al-Mawardi said: As for Wadd, it is an idol that is worshipped. It was named Wadd because of their love for it. After the people of Noah, Kalb was in Dumat al-Jandal, according to Ibn Abbas, Ata’, and Muqatil. Their poet said about it: Welcome, my friend, for it is not permissible for us to indulge in women, and religion has become strange. As for Suwa’, he was for Hudhayl on the coast of the sea. As for Yaghuth, he was for Ghataif from Murad in Al-Jarf from Saba’ according to Qatada. Al-Mahdawi said: For Murad then for Ghatafan. As for Ya’uq, he was for Hamdan according to Qatada, Ikrimah and Ata’. Al-Tha’labi said: He was for Kahlan bin Saba’, then he inherited it until it came to be in Hamdan. Malik bin Namad Al-Hamadani says about him: God blesses in this world and clears but does not clear, He hinders but does not feather As for Nasr, it was owned by Al-Kalaa’ of Himyar, according to Qatada and Muqatil. The majority of scholars read Wada with a fatha on the waw. Nafi’ read it with a damma. Al-Layth said: Wadad with a damma on the waw was an idol of the Quraysh, and with a fatha it was an idol that belonged to the people of Noah, and ‘Amr ibn Wadad was named after it.” It is stated in As-Sahah that Wadad with a fatha is watid in the dialect of the people of Najd, as if they made the ta’ sukun and assimilated it into the dal. The majority of scholars read Wala Yaghuth and Ya’quq without a tanween. If they are Arabic, then the reason for preventing them from being declined is due to the verb form and the verb form. If they are foreign, then it is due to foreignness and being a proper noun. Al-A’mash read Wala Yaghuth and Ya’quq with a damma. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: This is a mistake. The reason for mentioning these idols specifically, despite their inclusion under the category of gods, is because they were the largest and most important of their idols.
71:24: 24- And they have led many astray meaning their leaders and chiefs have led many people astray. It has also been said that the pronoun refers to the idols, meaning that many people have been led astray because of them, as in the saying of Abraham: My Lord, indeed they have led many people astray and the pronoun of those who have reason was applied to them because the disbelievers who worship idols believe that they have reason. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error is in apposition to My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed Me and the apparent was placed in place of the implicit to record their wrongdoing. Abu Hayyan said: It is in apposition to have led astray, and the meaning of misguidance is: except punishment. This is what Ibn Bahr said, and he provided evidence for that with his saying: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness, and it has also been said: except loss, and it has been said: except a trial in wealth and children, and it has been said: loss, and it has been said: misguidance in their deceit.
71:25: 25- "Because of their sins they were drowned. Ma" is an additional emphasis, and the meaning is: "Because of their sins", meaning because of them and because of them they were drowned in the flood. "So they were admitted to the Fire" after that, which is the Fire of the Hereafter, and it was said that it is the torment of the grave. The majority read "their sins in the sound plural, and Abu Amr read their sins in the broken plural, and Al-Jahdary, Amr bin Ubaid, Al-A'mash, Abu Haywah, and Ashhab Al-Uqayli read their sins" in the singular. Ad-Dahhak said that they were tormented with the Fire in this world along with drowning in one case: they were drowning in Janat and burning on one side. The majority read "they were drowned from they were drowned, and Zayd bin Ali read they were drowned" with emphasis. "So they found no helpers for themselves other than God", meaning they did not find anyone to prevent them from God's torment and ward it off from them.
71:26: 26- And Noah said, ‘My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller.’ This is connected to Noah said, ‘My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me.’ When Noah, peace be upon him, despaired of their belief and their abandonment of disbelief, he called for their destruction. Qatada said: He called for their destruction after it was revealed to him, None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so God answered his call and drowned them. Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Muqatil, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Ibn Zayd, and Atiyya said: He only said this when God brought forth every believer from their loins and the wombs of their women, and made the wombs of the women and the loins of the fathers barren seventy years before the punishment, and some say forty. Qatada said: There was no child among them at the time of the punishment. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Ali said: If God had destroyed their children with them, it would have been a punishment from God to them and justice towards them, but He destroyed their offspring and children without punishment, then He destroyed them with punishment. The meaning of Diyar is: whoever inhabits a house. Its origin is Diyar on the pattern Fay’al, from Dara Yadwar, so the waw was changed to a Ya and one of them was assimilated into the other, like Al-Qiyam, its origin is Qayyam. Al-Qatibi said: Its origin is from Dar, meaning someone who resides in a house. It is said: There is no one in the house Diyar, meaning anyone. It is also said: Diyar is the owner of the house, and the meaning is: Do not leave anyone of them without destroying him.
71:27: 27- If you leave them, they will mislead your servants meaning if you leave them on earth, they will mislead your servants from the path of truth and they will not give birth except to wicked, disbelieving people meaning except to wicked people who abandon your obedience and are ungrateful for your blessings: meaning very ungrateful for them, and the meaning is: except for those who will be wicked and disbelieve.
71:28: Then when he invoked against the disbelievers, he followed it with a supplication for himself, his parents, and the believers, saying: 28- My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and they were believers, and his father was Lamech son of Methuselah, as mentioned above, and his mother was Simha bint Enosh. It was also said that he meant Adam and Eve. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said that by his parents he meant his father and grandfather. Sa'id ibn Jubayr read and my parents with a kasra on the dal for the singular. And for whoever enters My house, Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi said: It means his mosque. It was also said that it means his home in which he resides. It was also said that it means his ship. It was also said that it means whoever enters His religion. The accusative of believer is in the state of being a state: that is, for whoever enters My house characterized by the quality of faith, but leaves it not characterized by this quality, like his wife and son who said: I will seek refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water. Then he generalized the supplication, saying: And for the believing men and believing women, meaning forgive everyone characterized by faith, male and female. Then he returned to invoking God against the unbelievers, saying: And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction, meaning do not increase those who are characterized by injustice except in destruction, loss, and devastation. His invocation includes every wrongdoer until the Day of Resurrection, just as his invocation for the believing men and women includes every believing man and woman until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: {And do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa’, nor Yaghuth, nor Ya’uq, nor Nasr}, he said: These idols were worshipped at the time of Noah. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: The idols that were worshipped among the people of Noah came to be among the Arabs. As for Wadd, it belonged to Kalb in Dumat Al-Jandal; as for Suwa’, it belonged to Hudhayl; as for Yaghuth, it belonged to Murad and then to Banu Ghatif; as for Ya’uq, it belonged to Himyar, to the family of Dhi Al-Kila’, names of righteous men from the people of Noah. When they perished, Satan inspired their people to erect idols next to their assembly where they used to sit and name them after them, so they did, but they were not worshipped until those people perished and knowledge was abrogated, so they were worshipped.
72:1: It is twenty-eight verses. It was revealed in Mecca. Al-Qurtubi said: According to everyone’s opinion. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Jinn was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Aisha and Ibn Az-Zubayr. His statement: 1- Say, ‘It has been revealed to me.’ The majority of scholars read awhi as a quadriliteral verb. Ibn Abi Ubla, Ibn Iyas, and Al-‘Atki, on the authority of Abu ‘Amr, read wahy as a triliteral verb, and these are two dialects. There is a difference of opinion as to whether the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw them or not. The apparent meaning of the Qur’an is that he did not see them, because the meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, to your nation, it has been revealed to me through the tongue of Gabriel that a group of the jinn listened. Similar to this is His statement: And when We directed to you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an. This is supported by what is proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not recite to the jinn, nor did he see them. ‘Ikrimah said: The surah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite is Read in the name of your Lord who created. What indicates more to this has been mentioned in Surah Al-Ahqaf. His statement: A group of jinn listened. This is the one that takes the place of the subject, and for this reason, an was opened, and the pronoun indicates the matter. According to the Kufians and Akhfash, it is permissible for the preposition and noun to take the place of the subject. The group is the name of a group of between three and ten. Ad-Dahhak said: The jinn are the offspring of the jinn and they are not devils. Al-Hasan said: They are the offspring of Iblis. It was said that they are subtle rational bodies that are dominated by naziness and whims. It was also said that they are a type of abstract spirits. It was also said that they are human souls that have separated from their bodies. Scholars have differed over whether the believing jinn will enter Paradise, just as the disobedient jinn will enter Hell, based on the statement in Surat al-Mulk 67:And We have made them missiles to drive away the devils, and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze, and the statement of the jinn in what will follow in this surah: But as for the transgressors, they will be fuel for Hell, and other verses. Al-Hasan said: They will enter Paradise, and Mujahid said: They will not enter it, even if they are turned away from Hell. The first is more appropriate, because of His statement in Surat al-Jinn 72:No man or jinn had touched them before them. In Surat Ar-Rahman there are other verses that indicate this, so refer to them. We have already mentioned that the truth is that God did not send messengers to them from among themselves, rather all the messengers were from among mankind. And if His statement: Did there not come to you messengers from among you? suggests otherwise, then the apparent meaning is refuted by many verses in the Noble Book indicating that God, the Exalted, did not send messengers from among the children of Adam. These discussions would take a long time to discuss, and what is meant is to indicate with the shortest phrase: And they said, ‘Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur’an.’ That is, they said to their people when they returned to them: that is, we heard words recited that were wondrous in their eloquence and rhetoric. It was also said that they were wondrous in their exhortations, and it was also said that they were blessed. Wonderful is a verbal noun used to describe for emphasis, or by deleting the complement: that is, of wonder, or the verbal noun in the sense of the active participle: that is, astonishing.
72:2: 2- It guides to the right path meaning to the right path of things, which is the truth and correctness, and it was said to be to the knowledge of God, and the sentence is another description of the Qur’an So we believed in it meaning we believed in it that it is from God and we will not associate with our Lord anyone of His creation and we will not take another god with Him, because He is the One who is unique in His Lordship, and in this there is a rebuke to the disbelievers among the children of Adam as the jinn believed by hearing the Qur’an once and benefited from hearing a few verses from it and realized with their minds that it is the word of God and believed in it, while the disbelievers among mankind did not benefit, especially their leaders and noble ones, from hearing it multiple times and reciting it to them at different times while the Messenger from among them recited it to them in their tongue. Indeed, God defeated them in the most humiliating way and killed them in the most hideous way, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe if they only knew.
72:3: 3- And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Ibn ‘Amir, Hafs, Alqama, Yahya ibn Waththab, Al-A’mash, Khalaf, and Al-Sulami read and that He, the Most High with a fat-ha on ‘an, and they read it the same way in what comes after it that is conjoined to it, and that is eleven topics up to His saying: And that when ‘Abdullah stood up. The rest read with a kasra in all of these places except in His saying: And that the mosques belong to God, for they agreed on the fat-ha. As for those who read with a fat-ha in these places, it is in conjunction with the place of the preposition and noun in So we believed in it, as if it was said, So we believed in him and we believed that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord, etc. As for those who read with a kasra in these places, it is in conjunction with We heard, so they said: We heard a Qur’an, and they said, He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord, etc. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid chose the kasra reading because it is all from the speech of the jinn and what is reported from them in the saying, And they said, ‘Indeed, we have heard.’ Abu Ja`far and Shu`bah read it with the fatha in three instances, which are, And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord.
72:4: 4- And that our fool used to say "And that there were men among mankind" They said: Because it is from the revelation, and they broke what remained because it is from the speech of the jinn. The majority read "And that when Abdullah stood up" with the fat-ha because it is conjoined with his saying: That he listened. Nafi', Ibn Amir, Shaibah, Zur bin Hubaish, Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal from Asim read it with the kasra in this place in conjunction with "So we believed in him with that previous estimation, and they agreed on the fat-ha in That he listened as they agreed on the fat-ha in That the mosques and in And if they had been upright and they agreed on the kasra in So they said, Indeed we have heard and Say, I only call upon my Lord and Say, I do not know and Say, Indeed, I do not control you. And the word Jadd" according to the linguists means greatness and majesty. It is said, "Jadd in my eyes" means great, so the meaning is: The greatness and majesty of our Lord became elevated, and this is what Ikrimah and Mujahid said. Al-Hasan said: What is meant is His richness, and from this, fortune is called jadd, and a man who is jaddud means protected. In the hadith: And richness does not benefit one who is rich from you, Abu Ubaid and Al-Khalil said: That is, wealth does not benefit one who is rich from you, meaning that only obedience benefits him. Al-Qurtubi and Al-Dahhak said: His richness is His favors and blessings upon His creation. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: His kingdom and authority. Al-Suddi said: His command. Saeed bin Jubair said: And that He, the Most High, is the richest of our Lord, meaning, our Lord is Most High. It was also said that His richness is His power. Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hussein and his son Ja’far Al-Sadiq and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God has no richness, but the jinn said it out of ignorance. The majority read jadd with a fatha on the jim, while Ikrimah, Abu Haywah and Muhammad bin Al-Samee’ read it with a kasra on the jim, which is the opposite of frivolity. Abu Al-Ashhab read jadd Rabbana meaning His richness and benefit. It was also narrated from Ikrimah that he read it with the tanween of jad and raising rabbiyyana as a substitute for jad “He did not take a wife or a son.” This is a statement of the transcendence of His Majesty, glory be to Him. Al-Zajjaj said: Exalted is the majesty and greatness of our Lord from taking a wife or a son. It is as if the jinn were pointing out with this the error of the disbelievers who attribute companions and children to God, and cleared God, glory be to Him, of them. And that our foolish one used to say an outrage against God. The pronoun in it refers to the statement or the command. Our foolish one may be the subject of kana, and yaqoob may be the predicate of kana, and its subject may be a pronoun referring to the statement or the command. Kana may be redundant. What they mean by their foolish one is their disobedient ones and polytheists. Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj, and Qatadah said: They meant Satan by it. Excessiveness is exaggeration in disbelief. Abu Malik said: Injustice. Al-Kalbi said: Lying. Its origin is straying from the goal and exceeding the limit. From this is the saying of the poet: In any case, they ruled over you and went too far, and that is only when the trouble comes to you
72:5: 5- And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never tell a lie about God. That is, we thought that mankind and the jinn would not lie about God, that He has a partner, a wife, or a son. Therefore, we believed them in that until we heard the Quran, and we knew the falsehood of what they said and the falsehood of what we thought of them as truthfulness. The accusative of falsehood is as a source emphasizing to say, because lying is a type of saying, or an attribute of a deleted source: that is, a false saying. Ya'qub, Al-Jahdary, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read that you would never tell is from to say, so according to this reading falsehood is the object.
72:6: 6- And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn. Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd, and others said: When a man from the Arabs settled in a valley, he would say: I seek refuge with the master of this valley from the evil of the foolish ones of his people. So he would spend the night in their neighborhood until morning. Then this verse was revealed. Muqatil said: The first to seek refuge with the jinn were people from Yemen, then from Banu Hanifa. Then it spread among the Arabs. When Islam came, they sought refuge with God and abandoned them. And they increased them in burden. That is, the jinn increased the burden of those who sought refuge with them from among the human beings: that is, in foolishness and transgression. Did they become arrogant and rebellious? Or the seekers of refuge from among the human beings increased the burden of those who sought refuge with the jinn, because those sought refuge with them used to say: We are the masters of the jinn and mankind. Mujahid and Qatadah said the first, and Abu Al-Aaliyah, Qatadah, Al-Rabi' bin Anas, and Ibn Zayd said the second. In Arabic, al-Rahaq means sin and committing indecent acts. A man is Rahaq if he is like that. From this comes his saying, Humiliation overwhelms them, meaning it overwhelms them. From this comes the saying of al-A’sha: Nothing benefits me without seeing her. Can a lover be healed unless he is exhausted? Meaning a sin. It was said that fatigue means fear: meaning that the jinn increased the humanity by seeking refuge with them out of fear of them. It was also said that a human would say: I seek refuge with so-and-so, one of the leaders of the Arabs, from the jinn of this valley. This is supported by what was said that the word men is not applied to the jinn, so his saying men is a description of those from among the human beings who seek refuge with him: meaning they seek refuge with them from the evil of the jinn. So his saying men is a description of those from among the human beings who seek refuge with him: meaning they seek refuge with him from the evil of the jinn. This is far-fetched. Applying the word men to the jinn, even if we assume it is not linguistically correct, does not prevent it from being applied to them here for the sake of similarity.
72:7: 7- And that they assumed, just as you assumed, that God would not resurrect anyone. This is from what the jinn said to mankind: meaning, the jinn assumed, just as you, O mankind, assumed, that there will be no resurrection. It was also said that the meaning is: And mankind assumed, just as you, O jinn, assumed, meaning that they do not believe in resurrection just as you do not believe.
72:8: 8- And we touched the heaven This is also from the saying of the jinn: meaning we sought report as is our custom and found it filled with guards of angels guarding it from eavesdropping. Guards is the plural of guard, and strong is an adjective for guards: meaning strong. And meteors is the plural of meteor, which is the flame taken from the fire of the star as was explained previously in the interpretation of His statement: And We made them missiles for the devils. The place of His statement: filled with strong guards is the accusative as the second object of we found, because it takes two objects, and it is permissible for it to take one object, so the place of the sentence is the accusative as a state with the estimation of had, and guards is accusative as a specification, and its description as singular is in consideration of the word, as it is said the righteous predecessors: meaning the righteous.
72:9: 9- And we used to sit therein in stations to listen meaning, and I am in stations that are for listening, and stations is the plural of seat, the name of a place, and that is because the rebellious jinn used to do that in order to hear report from the angels of heaven and deliver it to the priests, so God Almighty guarded it by sending His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, with burning meteors, and this is the meaning of His saying: So whoever listens now will find a meteor lying in wait for him meaning lying in wait for him to throw it, or for him to prevent him from hearing, and His saying: now is an adverbial phrase for the state and is a metaphor for the future, and the accusative of watched is as an attribute of meteor, or an object for it, and it is singular, and it is permissible for it to be a collective noun like guards. They differed as to whether the devils were pelted with meteors before his mission or not. Some said: That was not the case. Al-Wahidi narrated on the authority of Muammar who said: I said to Al-Zuhri: Were stars pelted during the pre-Islamic era? He said: Yes. I said: What do you think of His statement: And we used to sit therefrom? He said: It became more severe and intensified when Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent. Ibn Qutaybah said: Stoning had occurred before his mission, but it was not as severely guarded after his mission. They used to seek help from others in some cases, but when he was sent, they were completely forbidden from doing so. Abdul Malik ibn Sabur said: The sky was not guarded during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, but when Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent, the sky was guarded, the devils were pelted with meteors, and they were prevented from approaching the sky. Nafi’ ibn Jubayr said: During the period, the devils would hear but would not be pelted, but when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent, they were pelted with meteors. This has already been discussed.
72:10: 10- And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them a right course. That is, we do not know whether evil is intended for the people of the earth because of this guarding of the heavens, or whether their Lord intends for them a right course: that is, good. Ibn Zayd said: Iblis said: We do not know whether God intended by this prevention to send down a punishment upon the people of the earth or to send a messenger to them. The rise of ashar is a preoccupation, or a beginning, and its good is what comes after it. The first is more appropriate, and the sentence is a substitute for the two objects of nadree. It is more appropriate that this is from the words of the jinn among themselves.
