72:11: And it is not from the words of Satan as Ibn Zayd said: 11- And among us are the righteous meaning some said to each other when they called their companions to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And we were before listening to the Qur’an among us who were described as righteous and among us less than that meaning a people less than that: meaning less than those described as righteous. And it was said that by the righteous he meant the believers, and by those who are less than that the disbelievers, and the first is more appropriate. And the meaning of we were divided ways is scattered groups and different types, and the piece is a piece of something, and the people became divided: if their conditions were scattered, and from this is the saying of the poet: The Constrictor, the Expander, the Guide to His obedience in the trial of people, when their desires are severe Meaning: We had different ways, or our ways were different ways, or we were like different ways. From this is the saying of Labid: The eye has not reached all its desire on the day when the horses walk in the saddle He also said: I said, and Zaid was helpless, the day Amr’s cavalry turned away Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak said: Different religions. Qatada said: Different desires. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: They were Muslims, Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians. Mujahid said the same. Al-Hasan said: The jinn are like you: Qadariyyah, Murji'ah, Rafidah, and Shi'ah. Al-Suddi said the same. Aaaa
72:12: 12- And we were certain that we would never fail God on earth. “Suspicion” here means knowledge and certainty: that is, we knew that we would never fail God on earth wherever we were, and that we would never escape Him if He wanted something from us. And we would never fail Him by fleeing from it, that is, by escaping from it, so it is a source in the place of a state.
72:13: 13- And when we heard the guidance meaning the Qur'an we believed in it and we confirmed that it is from God and we did not deny it as the disbelieving mankind did. So whoever believes in his Lord will not fear loss or oppression meaning he will not fear a decrease in his work and reward, nor will he be beset by injustice or harm. Loss is a decrease, and oppression is aggression and tyranny. The meaning is: he will not fear that his good deeds will be decreased or his bad deeds will be increased. The definition of oppression was mentioned earlier. The majority of scholars read Bakhsan with a sukoon on the kha'. Yahya ibn Waththab read it with a fatha on it. Yahya ibn Waththab and Al-A'mash read fa la khaf in the jussive mood as a response to the condition, and there is no basis for this after the introduction of the fa'. The interpretation is: he does not fear, and the matter is clear. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with a group of his companions, intending to go to the Ukaz market. The devils were prevented from receiving report from heaven, and meteors were sent down upon them. The devils returned to their people, and they said: What is wrong with you? They said: We have been prevented from receiving report from the heavens, and meteors have been sent down upon us. They said: “Nothing has prevented you from receiving report from the heavens except something that has happened. So travel to the east and west of the earth to find out what this matter is that has prevented you from receiving report from the heavens.” Those who had headed towards Tihamah turned back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was in Nakhl, heading for the market of Ukaz, and he was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur’an, they listened attentively to it and said: This, by God, is what has prevented you from receiving report from the heavens. Then they returned to their people and said: O our people, indeed we have heard an amazing Qur’an * It guides to the right path, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord. Then God revealed to His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened.” What was revealed to him was the words of the jinn. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding His statement: “Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened,” that he said: They were from the jinn of Nasibin. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord, he said: His favors and His greatness. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse, he said: His command and His power. Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami narrated - al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, regarding his statement, And that our foolish one used to say, he said: Iblis. Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Uqayli in al-Du'afa, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azmah, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah ibn Abi al-Sa'ib al-Ansari who said: I went out with my father to Madinah on some errand, and that was the first time the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was mentioned in Makkah. He gave us shelter at a shepherd's house to spend the night. When midnight came, a wolf came and took a lamb from the sheep. The shepherd jumped up and said: O Amer of the valley, I am your neighbor. A crier called out: O Sarhan, release him. The lamb came running until it entered the sheep. Then God revealed to His Messenger in Makkah: And there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: So they increased them in burden, he said: Sin. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said: When people in the pre-Islamic era would camp in a valley, they would say: We seek refuge with the Master of this valley from the evil in it. Nothing would be more infatuated with them than they were. This is what He said: And they increased them in burden. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu’aym, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The devils had seats in the heavens where they would hear the revelation. When they heard a word, they would add nine to it. As for the word, it would be true, but what they added would be false. When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was sent, they were denied their seats. They mentioned that to Iblis, for stars had not been shot before that, so he said to them: This is nothing but something that has happened on earth. So he sent his soldiers and they found the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) standing in prayer between two mountains in Mecca. They came to him and informed him, and he said: This is the event that has happened on earth. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: And among us are the righteous and among us are less than that, meaning: Among us are Muslims and among us are polytheists. And we were of different ways means various desires. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him: And he will not fear loss or burden, meaning: He will not fear a decrease in his good deeds nor an increase in his bad deeds.
72:14: His statement: 14- And among us are the Muslims meaning those who believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And among us are the Qasitun meaning the unjust and oppressors who deviated from the path of truth and inclined toward the path of falsehood. It is said that someone is qasti unjust and aqsat just meaning that someone is just. And whoever submits - those have sought out the right path meaning they have sought the path of truth. Al-Farra’ said: They have followed guidance.
72:15: 15- As for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hellfire. That is, they will be fuel for the fire that will be kindled by them just as it is kindled by the unbelieving people.
72:16: 16- And if they were to adhere to the way This is not from the words of the jinn, but rather it is connected to that a group of jinn listened and the meaning is: And it was revealed to me that the matter is if the jinn or mankind or both of them adhered to the way, which is the way of Islam, and we have mentioned before that the reading agreed to open that here. Ibn al-Anbari said: And the opening here is to imply an oath of its interpretation, and by God if they were to adhere to the way as he did, it is said in speech, By God, if I stood up, I would stand up as in the saying of the poet: By God, if you were free, you would not be free, nor would you be free. He said: Or on the basis of It was revealed to me that he listened, “And if they had been steadfast,” or on the basis of We believed in it: meaning we believed in it, and that if they had been steadfast. The majority read it with a kasra on the waw of law due to the meeting of two sukoon letters. Ibn Waththab and Al-A’mash read it with a damma on it, We would have given them abundant water, meaning abundant and ample. Muqatil said: Abundant water from the sky, and that was after the rain had been withheld from them for seven years. Ibn Qutaybah said: The meaning is, if they had all believed, We would have made this world ample for them. Abundant water is used as an example because all good and provision comes from rain. This is like His statement, And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared God 17:1, and His statement, And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect 18:1, and His statement, “Seek forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers * And give you increase in wealth and children” 19:2. It was said that the meaning is: If their father had been steadfast in his worship of God and had prostrated to Adam and not disbelieved, and if his children had followed him in Islam, We would have bestowed blessings upon them. Al-Zajjaj chose this. Abundant water means abundant in the Arabic language.
72:17: 17- To test them therein meaning, to test them and know how to be grateful for those blessings. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is that if they had remained steadfast in the path of disbelief that they are upon and were all disbelievers, We would have expanded their provisions as a deception and enticement until they were tempted by it, so We would have punished them in this world and the Hereafter. Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, Zayd ibn Aslam and his son Abd ar-Rahman, a-Thumali, Yaman ibn Zayyan, Ibn Kaysan, and Abu Majlaz said the same. They provided evidence for this with the verse: But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the gates of every [good] thing and the verse: And had it not been that mankind would have become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses (al-An'am 2:17). The first is more correct. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord - He will drive him into a steadily ascending punishment meaning, whoever turns away from the Qur'an, or worship, or admonition, or all of that - He will drive him into a steadily ascending punishment, meaning difficult and arduous. The majority read Naslakahu with an open noon. The Kufians and Abu Amr, in a narration from him, read it with a lower yaa. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this reading because of the statement: from the remembrance of his Lord and not from our remembrance. Muslim ibn Jundub, Talha ibn Musarraf and al-A'raj read it with a damma on the noon and a kasra on the lam, from aslakahu, and the majority read it from salakahu. In the language, as'ad means hardship. You say tas'ad bi al-amr the matter is difficult for you, and it is the source of sa'ada he ascended, it is said sa'dan he ascended and sa'uda he ascended, so it describes the torment as an exaggeration, because the tormentor ascends: that is, it rises above him and overcomes him so that he cannot bear it. Abu Ubaid said: As'ad is a source: meaning a torment that has ascended. Ikrimah said: As'ad is a smooth rock in Hell that one is forced to climb, so when he reaches the top, he descends into Hell, as in His statement: I will exhaust him with a great ascent. Ascension is the difficult obstacle.
72:18: 18- And that the mosques are for God. We have already mentioned the agreement of the reciters here on the opening, so it is connected to the fact that he listened: meaning, it was revealed to me that the mosques are specifically for God. Al-Khalil said: The meaning is because the mosques. And the mosques are the places that were built for prayer in. Saeed bin Jubair said: The jinn said, How can we come to the mosques and witness the prayer with you when we are far from you? So it was revealed. Al-Hasan said: He meant by it all places because the whole earth is a mosque. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Talq bin Habib said: He meant by the mosques the limbs on which the servant prostrates, which are the feet, knees, hands, and forehead. He says, These are the limbs that God has bestowed upon you, so do not prostrate with them to anyone other than God, for that will deny the blessing of God. Ata’ said the same. It was said that the mosques are the prayer because prostration is among its pillars. Al-Hasan said, So do not invoke anyone with God from His creation, whoever he may be.
72:19: 19- And that when Abdullah stood up We have already mentioned that the majority of scholars read here with a fat-ha on an, in apposition to that he listened: that is, it was revealed to me that the matter was when Abdullah stood up, and he is the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, called upon Him meaning called upon God and worshipped Him, and that was in Batn Nakhl as mentioned earlier, when the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, stood up to pray and recite the Quran. We have also mentioned the reading of those who read with a kasra on in here, and in it is ambiguity and distance from the intended meaning. They almost formed a crowd around him: that is, the jinn almost formed a crowd around the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, due to their crowding around him to hear the Quran from him. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of labdan is to ride on top of each other, and from this is derived this labood that is spread out. The majority of scholars read labdan with a kasra on the lam and a fat-ha on the ba. Mujahid, Ibn Muhaisin and Hisham read it with a damma on the lam and a fatha on the ba. Abu Haywah, Muhammad ibn al-Samifa’, al-Uqayli and al-Jahdari read it with a damma on the ba and the lam. Al-Hasan, Abu al-Aaliyah and al-A’raj read it with a damma on the lam and a shaddah on the ba’ with a fatha. According to the first reading, the meaning is what we have mentioned. According to the reading with a damma on the lam, the meaning often varies, as in the statement, I destroyed wealth in abundance. It was also said that the meaning is: The polytheists almost mounted one another in spite of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: When Abdullah Muhammad began his call to Islam, mankind and the jinn conspired to extinguish it, but God refused except to support him and complete His light. Ibn Jarir favored this view. Mujahid said: Labdan: meaning groups, and it is from the verb Talabd something on something, meaning it gathered, and from it is the labd that is spread out due to the accumulation of its wool, and everything that you stick tightly together, you have made labduh. The hair on the back of a lion is called Labd, and the plural is Labd. And a lot of locusts are called Labd. And Labd, with a damma on the lam and a fatha on the ba, is used to refer to something permanent, and from it the eagle of Luqman was called Labd due to its long life, and it is what is meant by the saying of Al-Nabigha: He who has been unfair to Labed has been unfair to her
72:20: 20- Say, ‘I only call upon my Lord’ meaning Abdullah said, I only call upon my Lord and worship Him, “and I do not associate anyone with Him from His creation. The majority of scholars read said, while Asim and Hamza read say as a command. The reason for its revelation was that the infidels of Quraysh said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have come with a grave matter, and you have caused enmity among all people, so turn back from this, and we will protect you.
72:21: 21- Say, ‘Indeed, I have no power to cause you harm or to bring you any good.’ That is, I am not able to ward off any harm from you or bring you any good. It has been said that harm is disbelief and that right guidance is guidance. The first is more appropriate because the two indefinite nouns occur in the context of negation, so they encompass all harm and all right guidance in this world and the next.
72:22: 22- Say, ‘None can protect me from God’ meaning, no one can ward off His punishment from me if He inflicts it upon me. And I will not find besides Him a refuge meaning, a shelter, a place of protection, and a safeguard. Al-Kalbi said: An entrance into the earth like a tunnel, and it was said: A path and a way, and the meaning is close, and from it the poet said: Oh, the anguish of my soul, and the anguish that is useless to me, and there is no escape from God’s decree
72:23: The exception in His statement: 23- "Except a message from God" is from His statement I do not possess: meaning I do not possess any harm or guidance except conveying from God, for in it is the greatest guidance, or from a refuge: meaning I will not find any refuge other than Him except conveying. Muqatil said: That is what will protect me from His punishment. Qatada said: Except a message from God, for that is what I possess by God's grace, as for disbelief and faith, I do not possess them. Al-Farra' said: But I convey to you what I was sent with, so on this basis it is disjointed. Al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative case as a substitute for his saying in search of God, meaning I will not find anyone other than Him to seek refuge in except that I convey what comes from God. His saying and His messages is in apposition to conveying, meaning except conveying from God and His messages. This is what Abu Hayyan said, and he preferred it. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger in the command to monotheism because the context is then for him is the fire of Hell. The majority read it with a kasra on in as a new sentence. It was read with a fatha on the hamza because what comes after the fa’ of recompense is in the position of introduction, and the meaning is that his recompense is that for him is the fire of Hell, or his judgment is that for him is the fire of Hell. The accusative of abiding therein is in the state: meaning in the fire or in Hell, and the plural is in consideration of the meaning of from, just as monotheism in his saying “then for him is in consideration of its wording. His saying “forever” is an emphasis on the meaning of eternity: meaning abiding therein without end.
72:24: 24- Until, when they see what they are promised meaning the punishment in this world or in the Hereafter. The meaning is that they will remain as they are in insisting on disbelief and enmity towards the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the believers until, when they see what they are promised, they will know who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number meaning who has weaker soldiers to help them and fewer in number, the believers or the believers?
72:25: 25- Say, ‘Indeed, I do not know whether that which you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a term.’ That is, I do not know whether the punishment you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a term. That is, an end and a duration. God, the Exalted, commanded him to say this to them when they said to him, When will this that He has promised us be? Ata’ said: He means that no one knows the Day of Resurrection except God alone, and the meaning is that knowledge of the time of the punishment is a knowledge of the unseen that no one knows except God. The majority of scholars read my Lord with a sukoon on the ya’. Al-Haramiyan and Abu Amr read it with a fatha. And in man is a weaker relative pronoun, and and is the predicate of a deleted subject: that is, it is weaker. The clause is the relative clause, and it is permissible for it to be an interrogative raised as a subject, and and is its predicate. The clause is in the accusative case as the two objects of I know. His saying is near is an advanced predicate and what you are promised is a delayed subject.
72:26: 26- The Knower of the Unseen The majority of scholars read it in the nominative case as a substitute for my Lord, or an explanation of it, or the predicate of a deleted subject, and the sentence is a resumption confirming what came before it regarding lack of knowledge. It was also read in the accusative case as an expression of praise. Al-Sarri read the knowledge of the unseen in the form of a verb and the accusative of the unseen, and the fa in He does not reveal His unseen to anyone is to arrange the lack of revelation based on His uniqueness in knowledge of the unseen: that is, He does not know the unseen that He knows, which is that which is hidden from any of His servants.
72:27: Then He made an exception and said: 27- Except for a Messenger whom He has chosen meaning, except for the Messenger whom He has chosen or whom He has chosen from among them to reveal to him some of His unseen, so that this would be evidence of his prophethood. Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars said: When He, the Most High, praised Himself for knowledge of the unseen and kept it to Himself without His creation, this was evidence that no one knows the unseen except Him. Then He made an exception for the Messenger whom He has chosen, so He entrusted them with whatever He willed of His unseen by way of revelation to them, and made it a miracle for them and a true proof of their prophethood. The astrologer and those who are similar to him, who strike with pebbles, look into the palm of their hands, and throw mud at them, are not among the Messenger whom He has chosen and reveal to them whatever they wish of His unseen. He is an unbeliever in God, slandering Him with his conjecture, guesswork, and lies. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Except for a Messenger whom He has chosen, that is Gabriel, and there is some error in this. It was said that what is meant by His statement: Except whomever He has chosen of messengers, for He will inform him of some of His unseen is that which is related to his message, such as miracles, the rulings of obligations, the reward for deeds, and what he explains of the conditions of the Hereafter, not the unseen that is not related to his message, such as the time of the Hour and the like. Al-Wahidi said: This is evidence that whoever claims that the stars guide him to what will happen has disbelieved in what is in the Quran. He said in Al-Kashaf: "This nullifies the miracles, because those to whom they are attributed, even if they are approved saints, are not messengers. God has singled out the messengers from among those approved of with knowledge of the unseen. It also nullifies soothsaying and astrology, because their practitioners are the furthest thing from approval and most likely to lead to wrath." Al-Razi said: "In my view, the verse does not indicate anything of what they said, since there is no generality in His unseen, so it can be interpreted as referring to one unseen, which is the time of the Resurrection, because it occurs after His statement: "What you are promised is near" Al-Qur'an 14:1. If it is said: "What is the meaning of the exception in that case?" We said: Perhaps when the Day of Resurrection approaches He will reveal it. How could it not? He said: The Day the heaven will split with clouds and the angels will be sent down in [elaborate] descent, so the angels will know at that time when the Day of Resurrection will come. Or it is an isolated exception: that is, whoever He chooses as a Messenger, He will place guardians before him and among His creation to protect him from the evil of the rebellious jinn and mankind. What indicates that it does not mean that He does not inform anyone of anything of the unseen is that it is proven, almost by mutawatir repeated transmission, that Shaqqa and Satih were soothsayers and were known through the hadith of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before his appearance. They were famous for this knowledge among the Arabs until Khosrau returned to them. So it is proven that God, the Most High, may inform other than the messengers of something of the unseen. Also, the people of all religions agree that the interpreter of dreams can tell of future matters and he is truthful in them. Also, Sultan Sanjar bin Malik Shah transferred a soothsayer from Baghdad to Khorasan and asked her about future matters, and she informed him of them, and she fulfilled her promise. He said: People who are well-versed in the science of theology and wisdom informed me that she spoke of unseen matters in detail, and it was in accordance with what she spoke of. Abu al-Barakat went to great lengths in his explanation of her condition in his book, The Interpretation of the Word, and said: I investigated her condition for thirty years and became certain that she spoke of the unseen in a precise manner. We also observe this in those who receive true inspiration, and it may also be found among magicians. We may also see the astrological rulings being in accordance with each other, even if they differ. If we were to say that the Qur’an indicates something contrary to these perceptible matters, the Qur’an would be challenged, and the interpretation would be as we have mentioned.” End of his statement. I said: As for his statement, There is no formula of generality in His unseen, this is false, because adding a verbal noun and a generic noun are forms of generality, as stated by the imams of Usul and others. As for his statement, Or it is a disjunctive exception, this is a mere claim that the Qur’anic system rejects. As for his statement, Indeed, Shaqqa and Sutaih, etc., they lived at a time when devils eavesdropped and relayed what they heard to soothsayers, who would mix truth with falsehood, as is proven in the authentic hadith. And in His statement, Except for he who snatches a snatch and similar verses, the subject of soothsaying has been explained in this Shari’ah, and that it was a path to some of the unseen by means of the eavesdropping of devils until that was prevented by the mission of Muhammad. They said, “And indeed, we have sought the heaven but found it filled with stern guards and flaming fires. And indeed, we used to sit therein in stations to listen. But whoever listens now will find a flaming fire lying in wait for him.” So the subject of soothsaying at the time when it existed is specified by his evidence, and it is part of what specifies this generality, so his claim that he brought soothsaying into this verse does not apply. As for the story of the woman that he mentioned, it is a myth. Even if we assume that any of the report he narrated about her actually happened, it would be like what was mentioned in the hadith, Indeed, among this nation are those who innovate, and among them is Umar. In this case, it would be like a specification of the generality of this verse, with no end to it. As for what he dared to say about God and His Book in his last statement, if we were to say that the Qur’an indicates the opposite of these tangible matters, then the Qur’an would be attacked. It would be said to him, “This is not the first of your slips or lapses. How many similar and analogous things do you have that the vein of your philosophy pulsates with, and that Satan has run after, due to your confusion in the discussions of your interpretation. I wonder at you! Could what has reached you of the story of this woman and the like cause the Qur’an to be attacked? How excellent is what some of the writers of our time have said: When a fly seeks to cover the sun, it spreads its wings over it. And I said from the verses: The winds blocked it with a wing and met the morning light with a lamp If you say: “Then it has been established by this Qur’anic evidence that God reveals to whomever He wills of His Messengers His secrets of the unseen. Does the Messenger whom God has revealed to whomever He wills of His secrets of the unseen have the right to inform some of his nation of it?” I say: Yes, and there is nothing wrong with that. It has been proven from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of this, which is not hidden from anyone who is knowledgeable of the pure Sunnah. Among this is that he stood in a position in which he informed of what would happen until the Day of Resurrection, and he did not leave out anything related to tribulations and the like. Those who memorized it memorized it, and those who forgot it forgot it. Likewise, it has been proven that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informed Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman of the tribulations that would occur after him, until the most prominent Companions asked him about it and they returned to him. It is proven in Sahih and other sources that “Umar ibn al-Khattab asked him about the tribulation that is surging like the waves of the sea, so he said: There is a door between you and it, so Umar said: Will it be opened or broken? He said: It will be broken. Umar knew that it was the door, and breaking it would kill him.” As in the well-known authentic hadith, it was said to Hudhayfah: Did Umar know that? He said: Yes, he knew that the night before tomorrow. Similarly, it is proven that he informed Abu Dharr of what would happen to him, and that he informed Ali ibn Abi Talib of the report of Dhu al-Thadiyah, and similar things of which there are many, and if they were collected, a separate book would be published about them. Once this is established, there is no reason why some of the righteous of this nation are not alone in receiving some of the report of the unseen that God revealed to His Messenger, and that His Messenger revealed to some of his nation, and that these some of the nation revealed to those who came after them. Thus, the miracles of the righteous are of this type, and all are from the divine abundance through the Prophetic side. Then God, the Almighty, mentioned that He protects the unseen that the Messenger is informed of, saying: For He will make a guard precede him and behind him. The sentence is a confirmation of the revelation derived from the exception. The meaning is that God, the Almighty, places a guard of angels before and behind the Messengers to protect him from the devils’ exposure to what He revealed to him of the unseen. Or He places a guard of angels before and behind the revelation to protect it from the devils stealing it and then throwing it to the soothsayers. What is meant is from all sides. Ad-Dahhak said: God did not send a prophet except that there were angels with him to protect him from the devils, lest they take the form of an angel. So if a devil comes to him in the form of an angel, they say, This is a devil, so beware of him. And if an angel comes to him, they say, This is the messenger of your Lord. Ibn Zayd said: Watchdogs means guardians who protect the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, from the jinn and devils in front of him and behind him. Qatadah and Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab said: They are four guardian angels. Al-Farra’ said: What is meant is Gabriel. He said in Al-Sahah: The people watch, like guards, and it is the same in singular, plural, and feminine. The watch is for the thing that is watched, it is said: he watched him, he watches him, watching, and watching is watching, and the watch is the place of watch.
72:28: 28- That he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord. The lām is related to yaslaka, and what is meant by it is knowledge related to the actual conveyance. An is the lightened form of the heavy an, and its subject is the pronoun of the matter, and the predicate is the sentence, and the messages are an expression for the unseen that was intended to be revealed to whomever God chose as a messenger, and the pronoun in abhaghū refers to monitoring. Qatādah and Muqatil said: So that Muhammad may know that the messengers before him conveyed the message just as he conveyed the message, and in it there is an omission related to the lām: i.e. We informed him of our preservation of the revelation so that he may know that the messengers before him were in the same state of conveying. It was said that Muhammad may know that Gabriel and those with him conveyed to him the messages of his Lord, said Sa’īd ibn Jubair. It was said that the messengers may know that the angels conveyed the messages of their Lord. It was said that Iblis may know that the messengers conveyed the messages of their Lord without confusion. Ibn Qutaybah said: That is, so that the jinn may know that the messengers had conveyed what was revealed to them and that they were not the ones who conveyed it by eavesdropping on them. Mujahid said: So that he who denied the messengers may know that the messengers had conveyed the messages of their Lord. The majority of scholars read li-ya’lam with a fat-ha on the ta’ in the active form. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Hamid, Ya’qub, and Zayd ibn Ali read it with a damma on the ya’ in the passive form: That is, so that people may know that what He has taught them is unseen. Ibn Abi Ubaidah and al-Zuhri read it with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the lam: And He encompassed what they have, meaning what the angels who are watching Him have, or what the messengers who conveyed His messages have. The clause is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of yaslaka with an implied qad: That is, while the state is that the Almighty has encompassed what they have of conditions. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: “So that he may know that their Lord has encompassed what they have before they received His messages. ‘And He has counted all things precisely’ of all the things that have been and that will be. It is connected to ‘has encompassed’, and ‘a number’ may be in the accusative case as a specification, transferred from the direct object: that is, He has counted the number of all things as in His statement: ‘And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth’. It may also be in the accusative case as a source, or in the place of the circumstance: counted. The meaning is that His knowledge of things is not in general terms, but rather in detail: that is, He has counted each individual of His creations individually. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “The unjust” are those who deviate from the truth. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the statement, And if they had remained steadfast in the way, he said: had carried out what they were commanded to do. We would have given them abundant water, he said: a flowing stream. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi who said: Umar said: And if they had remained steadfast in the way, we would have given them abundant water to test them with it. He said: wherever there is water, there is wealth, and wherever there is wealth, there is temptation. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, To test them with it, he said: to test them with it. Regarding the statement, And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord - He will drive him into a gradual punishment, he said: a level of punishment that he ascends. Hannad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Hakim narrated and he authenticated on his authority regarding the statement, He will drive him into a gradual punishment, he said: a mountain in Hell. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority, an gradual punishment, he said: there is no rest in it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, regarding his statement, And that the mosques belong to God, that he said: On the day this verse was revealed, there was no mosque on earth except the Sacred Mosque and the Mosque of Elijah in Jerusalem. Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym narrated in Al-Dala’il from Ibn Mas`ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out before the migration to the outskirts of Mecca and drew a line for me and said, ‘Do not tell me anything until I come to you.’ Then he said, ‘Do not let anything you see frighten you.’ So he went a little further, then sat down and there were black men who looked like Zutt men, and they were as God Almighty said, ‘They almost flocked to him in droves.’” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: “When they heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting the Qur’an, they almost rode him out of greed for what they heard, and they came close to him, but he did not know about them until the Messenger came to him and began to recite, ‘Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened.’” And Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Tirmidhi - who authenticated it - Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Dhiya’ in Al-Mukhtara also narrated from him regarding the verse: “When the jinn came to the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - while he was praying with his companions, they bowed as he bowed and prostrated as he prostrated. They were amazed at the obedience of his companions, so they said to their people when Abdullah stood up to call upon him: ‘They almost crowded around him.’” Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him: When Abdullah stood up to call upon him, meaning he called upon God. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him: They almost crowded around him, meaning they were helping him. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him: And He does not disclose His secret to anyone * Except to a messenger with whom He is pleased, meaning, God informed the Messenger of the revelation of the secret and revealed to him what was revealed to him of the secret and what God decrees, for no one knows that except Him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, observers. He said: They are angels who guard the Messenger of God from the devils until what he was sent to them is made clear to them, so that the polytheists will say, We have conveyed the messages of their Lord. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, he said: “God did not send down a verse from the Qur’an to His Prophet except that four angels memorized it and guarded it until they delivered it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he recited, “The Knower of the unseen, and He reveals His secret to no one, except to a messenger with whom He is pleased. Then He causes to march before him and behind him guards,” meaning the four angels, that he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord.
73:1: It is nineteen verses, and it was said twenty verses It is a Meccan surah. Al-Mawardi said: All of it is according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and Jabir. He said: Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: Except for two verses of it: And be patient over what they say and the one that follows it. Al-Tha’labi said: Except for the words: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand to the end of the surah, for it was revealed in Medina. Ibn Al-Durais, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: O you wrapped in a cloak was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr. Al-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Muzzammil was revealed in Mecca except for two verses: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand just before Al-Bazzar, Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat, and Abu Nu’aym in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: The Quraysh gathered in Dar Al-Nadwa and said: Give this man a name that will turn people away from him. They said: He is a soothsayer. They said: He is not a soothsayer. They said: He is a madman. They said: He is not a madman. They said: He is a magician. They said: He is not a magician. So the polytheists dispersed on that basis. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was informed, he wrapped himself in his garments and covered himself with them. Then Gabriel came to him and said: O you who is wrapped in garments! O you who is wrapped in garments! Al-Bazzar said, after narrating it through Mu’alla ibn Abd al-Rahman, that a group of scholars narrated from Mu’alla and they accepted his hadith, but if he is the only one who narrates hadiths, they are not corroborated. Abu Dawud and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “I spent the night with my aunt Maymunah, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) got up to pray at night. He prayed thirteen rak’ahs, including the two rak’ahs of Fajr. I estimated that he stood in each rak’ah according to the amount of ‘O you who is wrapped in garments.’” His saying: 1- O you who is wrapped in a garment Its original form is al-Mutazzammil but the ta' was assimilated into the zay. Wrapping oneself in a garment is the act of wrapping yourself in a garment. The majority of scholars read al-Mutazzammil with assimilation. Abu al-Mutazzammil read it according to the original form. Ikrimah read it with a soft zay. An example of this reading is the saying of Imru' al-Qais: As if Thabir was in the midst of many troubles, and the people were in a grave wrapped in a blanket This address is to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and there is a difference of opinion regarding its meaning. A group said that he (peace and blessings be upon him) used to wrap himself in his clothes when Gabriel first came to him with the revelation, fearing him until he felt comfortable with him. It was also said that the meaning is: O you who are wrapped in prophethood and committed to the message. This is what Ikrimah said. He used to read O you who are wrapped in prophethood with a soft zay and a fatha on the meem, a passive participle. It was also said that the meaning is: O you who are wrapped in the Quran. Ad-Dahhak said: He wrapped himself in his clothes for his sleep. It was also said that it was in the language of the polytheists to mean bad speech, so he wrapped himself in his clothes and shuffled around, so O you who are wrapped around and O you who are wrapped up in your garments were revealed. It has been proven that when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) heard the voice of the angel and looked at him, he trembled, so he went to his family and said: Wrap me up, cover me up. This was addressed to him (peace and blessings be upon him) at the beginning of the revelation. Then after that, he was addressed with prophethood and the message.
73:2: 2- Stand up at night except a little meaning stand up for prayer at night. The majority read it as qum with a kasra on the meem due to the meeting of two sukoon. Abu as-Sammak read it with a damma following the damma of the qaf. Uthman ibn Jinni said: The purpose of this vowel is to avoid the meeting of two sukoon, so with whichever vowel you move, the purpose has been achieved. The accusative of the night is a circumstantial noun. It was said that the meaning of qum is pray, and it was expressed and used as a metaphor for it. There was a difference of opinion as to whether this standing that he was commanded to do was obligatory or voluntary. What was narrated about that will come, God willing. His saying except a little is an exception from al-Layl 92:meaning pray the entire night except a little of it, and a little of something is less than half, and it was said less than a sixth, and it was said less than a tenth. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: What is meant by a little here is a third.
73:3: And we have been relieved from this difference by his saying: 3- Half of it etc., and the accusative of half of it as a substitute for the night. Al-Zajjaj said: Half of it is a substitute for the night, and except a little is an exception from half, and the pronoun in from it and upon it refers to half. The meaning is: Get up half of the night or subtract a little from half to a third, or add a little to two-thirds, so it is as if he said: Get up two-thirds of the night, or half of it or a third of it. It was said that half of it is a substitute for his saying a little. So the meaning is: Get up all night except half of it or less than half of it or more than half of it. Al-Akhfash said: Half of it means or half of it as one says: Give him a dirham, two dirhams, three, meaning or two dirhams or three. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: Or reduce from half a little to a third, or increase from half to two-thirds, giving him ample time for his standing at night and giving him the choice of these hours for standing. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group with him would stand according to these amounts, and that was difficult for them, so a man would not know how much he had prayed or how much of the night remained, so he would stand all night until God made it easier for them. And it was said that the two pronouns in from it and upon it refer to less than half, as if he said: Stand for less than half of it or stand for less than that less, or increase it a little, and that is very far-fetched. What appears is that half of it is a substitute for a little, and the two pronouns refer to the half that was substituted for a little. There is a difference of opinion about what abrogated this command. Some say it is His statement: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it to the end of the surah. Some say it is His statement: He knows that you cannot enumerate it and some say it is His statement: He knows that there will be among you ill and some say it was abrogated by the five daily prayers. This is what Muqatil, Al-Shafi’i and Ibn Kaysan said. Some say it is His statement: So recite what is easy for you thereof and Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin said that the night prayer is obligatory upon every Muslim, even if it is enough to milk a sheep.
73:4: 4- And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation meaning recite it slowly and contemplatively. Ad-Dahhak said: Recite it letter by letter. Az-Zajjaj said: It means to clearly pronounce all the letters and to give them their due pronunciation. The origin of measured recitation is arrangement, coordination and good organization. Emphasizing the verb with the infinitive indicates exaggeration in a way that does not confuse some letters with others, and does not diminish the pronunciation of the letter from its known point of articulation while fulfilling its proper vowel.
73:5: 5- Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word meaning, We will reveal the Quran to you, and it is a weighty word. Qatada said: By God, His obligations and limits are heavy. Mujahid said: What He has made lawful and unlawful. Al-Hasan said: Acting upon it. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Heavy in promise and threat, and what He has made lawful and unlawful. Muhammad bin Ka’b said: Heavy in the sense of generous, from their saying, So-and-so is heavy upon me, meaning, he is generous to me. Al-Farra’ said: Heavy and dignified, not light and trivial, because it is the speech of our Lord. Al-Husayn bin Al-Fadl said: Heavy, and only a heart supported by success and a soul adorned with Tawheed can bear it. It was said that it was described as being truly heavy because it was proven that when revelation came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was on his camel, it would place its udders on the ground and it would not be able to move until He had relieved it.
73:6: 6- The rising of the night means its hours and times, because it arises first and foremost. It is said that something originated, originates: if it began and came one thing after another, then it is emerging. And God originated it, so it arose. From this comes the word the clouds originated: if it began, so nashay'ah is the active participle of nashaa yansha', so it is nashay'ah. Al-Zajjaj said: The rising of the night is everything that originates from it: i.e. occurs, so it is nashay'ah. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The whole night is nashay'ah, meaning that the rising hours of the night, so the description was sufficient for the described noun. It was said that the rising of the night is the soul that arises from its bed for worship: i.e. rises, from nashaa from his place: if he gets up. It was said that nashaa in Abyssinian means standing up at night. It was also said that standing up at night is called na'isha if it is after sleeping. Ibn al-A'rabi said: If you sleep at the beginning of the night then you get up, then that is the establishment and emergence, and from it comes nashaa'ah al-layl. It was said that the early morning is the time between sunset and evening, because the meaning of nasha is began. From this comes the saying of Naseeb: If it were not for the saying Naseeb is a young girl, I would have said to myself The young ones Ikrimah and Ata’ said: The early part of the night is the beginning of the night. Mujahid and others said: It is the entire night, because it begins after the day. This is the preferred view of Malik. Ibn Kaysan said: It is getting up at the end of the night. It is stated in As-Sahah: The early part of the night is its first hours. Al-Hasan said: It is what comes after the last ‘Isha’ prayer until dawn. It is more intense in constancy. The majority of scholars read constancy with a fatha on the waw and a sukoon on the ta’, shortened. Abu Hatim preferred this reading. Abu Al-Aliyah, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Mujahid, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamid, Ibn Muhaisin, Al-Mughirah, and Abu Haywah read it with a kasra on the waw and a fatha on the ta’, longened. Abu Ubaid preferred this reading. So the meaning according to the first reading is that prayer in the early part of the night is more difficult for the worshipper than prayer during the day, because the night is for sleeping. Ibn Qutaybah said: The meaning is that it is heavier on the worshipper than the other hours of the day, from the Arab saying: The sultan’s pressure became heavy on the people, meaning what they were required to do under him was heavy for them. And from this is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): O God, make Your pressure severe on Mudar. The meaning according to the second reading is that it is more in agreement, meaning in compliance, from their saying: I agreed with so-and-so on such-and-such, meaning in agreement with him. Mujahid and Ibn Abi Malekah said: Meaning, more in agreement between the hearing and sight, the heart and the tongue, because the sounds and movements are cut off during it. And from this: So that they may agree with the number of what God has forbidden, meaning that they may agree. Al-Akhfash said: More intense standing. Al-Farra' said: It means more steadfast for work and more lasting for whoever wants to increase his worship. The night is the time when one is free from being occupied with earning a living, so his worship is lasting and does not stop. Al-Kalbi said: More energetic and more upright in speech meaning more intense in speech and more steadfast in recitation due to the presence of the heart and calm voices, and more upright and continuous in what is correct, because the voices are quiet and the world is still, so the worshipper is not disturbed by what he is reciting. Qatadah and Mujahid said: It means more correct for recitation and more steadfast in speech, because it is the time for understanding. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: I stand a little: It means more upright because the mind is free at night. Al-Kalbi said: It means I speak clearly about the Quran. Ikrimah said: It means I am more energetic and sincere and more blessed. Ibn Zayd said: It is more likely to understand the Quran, and it was said that supplications are answered more quickly.
73:7: 7- Indeed, for you during the day is much swimming. The majority read sabhan with a silent ha': meaning, managing your needs, coming and going, and going and coming. And sabhan means running and turning, and from it swimming in water by turning over its body and legs, and a horse sabikh: meaning fast running. And it was said that sabhan is free time: meaning, you have free time during the day for needs, so pray at night. Ibn Qutaybah said: meaning, managing, coming and going in your needs and chores. Al-Khalil said: You have sabhan during the day: meaning, sleep, and tasabbah means stretching out. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, if you miss something at night, you have free time during the day to make up for it. Yahya bin Ya'mar, Abu Wa'il, and Ibn Abi Ubla read sabkha with a voiced kha'. It was said that the meaning of this reading is: concealment, spaciousness, and rest. Al-Asma’i said: It is said that God relieved you of the fever, meaning He eased it. The heat became lighter and lessened. From this comes the poet’s saying: So, worry has overwhelmed you, and know that if the Most Gracious has decreed something, it will happen. That is, may your worries be relieved. And tasbikh is the type of cotton that is woven after carding. From this comes the saying of Al-Akhtal: So send them to scatter the dust as you scatter the fluffy cotton strings. Tha'lab said: Sabkh with the voiced kha' means hesitation and disturbance, and sabkh means stillness. Abu Amr said: Sabkh means sleep and idleness.
73:8: 8- And remember the name of your Lord meaning call upon Him by His beautiful names. It was also said that you should recite in the name of your Lord at the beginning of your prayer. It was also said that you should mention the name of your Lord in His promise and threat to increase your obedience to Him and keep away from disobeying Him. It was also said that the meaning is: Continue remembering your Lord day and night and do that often. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is pray to your Lord and devote yourself to Him completely meaning that you devote yourself to Him completely by being occupied with His worship. Devotion is disconnection. It is said that you cut something off and distinguished it from others. A devotional charity means that it is cut off from the owner’s money. It is also said that the monk is devotional because he is cut off from people. From this comes the saying of the poet: It lights up the darkness at night like a beacon of a devout monk. He replaced devotion with devoutness to maintain the pauses. Al-Wahidi said: Devotion is the rejection of the world and what is in it and the seeking of what is with God.
73:9: 9- Lord of the East and the West Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr and Ibn Amir read Lord in the genitive case as an attribute of your Lord, a substitute for it, or an explanation of it. The rest read it in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is there is no god but He or as a predicate of a deleted subject: i.e. He is the Lord of the East. Zayd ibn Ali read it in the accusative case as a praise. The majority read the East and the West in the singular, while Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas read the Easts and the Wests in the plural. We have already explained the East and the West, the two Easts and the two Wests, and the Easts and the Wests. Then take Him as a Disposer of affairs means if you know that He is the one who is specialized in lordship, then take Him as a Disposer of affairs: i.e., someone who takes care of your affairs and relies on Him in all of them. It was said that He is a guarantor of what He promised you of reward and victory.
73:10: 10- And be patient over what they say of harm, insults, and mockery, and do not be alarmed by that, and leave them with gracious leave, meaning do not confront them or be preoccupied with rewarding them. It was said that it should be gracious leave without alarm, and this was before the command to fight.
73:11: 11- And leave Me and the deniers meaning leave Me and them and do not worry about them, for I will suffice you in their matter and take revenge on them for you. It was said that it was revealed about those who coveted the Day of Badr, and they were ten and their mention has been mentioned before. Yahya bin Salam said: They are the sons of Mughira. Saeed bin Jubair said: I was informed that they were twelve of the affluent meaning the masters of wealth, plenty, luxury and pleasure in this world. And grant them respite for a little meaning a little respite as an adjective for a deleted source, or a little time as an adjective for a deleted time, and the meaning is He granted them respite until their appointed times have passed, and it was said that the punishment of this world was sent down upon them as on the Day of Badr.
73:12: The first is more appropriate, because of his saying: 12- Indeed, with Us are shackles and what follows, for it is a threat to them of the torment of the Hereafter. Ankar is the plural of nakl, which is the shackle, as al-Hasan, Mujahid, and others said. Al-Kalbi said: Ankar: shackles, and the first is more well-known in the language, and from it is the saying of al-Khansa’: They came to you and you cut off their shackles, while before you they were not cut off. Muqatil said: They are types of severe torment. Abu Imran al-Joni said: They are chains that cannot be removed, and Jahneh meaning a blazing fire.
73:13: 13- And food that chokes meaning it does not go down the throat but sticks in it, neither going down nor out. Mujahid said: It is Zaqqum. Al-Zajjaj said: It is Adh-Dari’ as he said: They will have no food except from Adh-Dari’ He said: It is the thorns of the ‘Usaj. Ikrimah said: It is a thorn that sticks in the throat and does not enter or come out. A choke is a wound in the throat, which is something that sticks in it, whether bone or otherwise. The plural is ghuss. And a painful torment meaning another type of torment other than what was mentioned.
73:14: 14- The Day the earth and mountains will shake The adverbial phrase is either Bazraani sow me, or Al-Settlement the stability related to it with Us, or it is an adjective for a torment, so it is related to something omitted: i.e., a torment that will befall on the Day it shakes, or it is related to something painful. The majority of scholars read Tarjaf shatters with a fatha on the taa and a damma on the jim, in the active form. Zayd ibn Ali read it in the passive form, taken from arjafaha to shake and disturb with those on it, and trembling is a severe earthquake and thunder. And the mountains will become a heap of sand means that mountains will be formed, and it was expressed in the past tense to confirm its occurrence. A heap is a mass of sand, and al-Muhayil is that which passes under the feet. Al-Wahidi said: i.e., flowing sand: it is said of everything that you send, whether dirt or food, You make it heap. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi said: Al-Muhayil is that which, if you step on it with your foot, it slips from under you, and if you take it beneath it, it pours down. From this is the saying of Hassan: Zainab's home was known as the sand dune, like the line of revelation on the lush paper.
73:15: 15- Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you. The address is to the people of Mecca, or to the infidel Arabs, or to all infidels, and the Messenger is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning is: He will bear witness over you on the Day of Resurrection regarding your deeds, just as We sent to Pharaoh a Messenger, meaning Moses.
73:16: 16- But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger whom We sent to him, and he denied him and did not believe in what he brought. The position of the Kaf is in the accusative case as it is an adjective for a deleted verbal noun, and the meaning is: Indeed, We sent to you a Messenger, but you disobeyed him, just as We sent a Messenger to Pharaoh, but he disobeyed him. So We seized him with a terrible punishment, meaning severe, heavy, and harsh. The meaning is: We punished Pharaoh with a severe, harsh punishment by drowning. In it is a warning to the people of Mecca that a punishment similar to what befell him would befall them, even if the type of punishment differs. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning heavy and harsh. From this, rain is called waabal. Al-Akhfash said: severe. The meaning is close. From this comes the word waabal bad food, meaning that it is not enjoyed. From this comes the saying of Al-Khansa’: The day when the horsemen of Malik were attacked, they were eaten to death.
73:17: 17- So how can you guard yourselves meaning how can you guard yourselves if you disbelieve meaning if you remain in your disbelief of a Day meaning the torment of a Day that will turn the children into grey-haired men because of its severity: meaning the children will become old men, and grey hair is the plural of grey-haired. This could be literal, and that they will become like that, or it could be a metaphor, because whoever witnesses the great horror, his strength will diminish, his limbs will weaken, and he will become like an old man in weakness and loss of strength. This is a severe rebuke and a great rebuke to them. Al-Hasan said: Meaning how can you guard yourselves against a Day that will turn the children into grey-haired men if you disbelieve? Ibn Mas`ud and `Atiyyah recited it this way, and a Day is the object of the verb to guard yourselves. Ibn al-Anbari said: Some of them put the word day in the accusative case because they disbelieved, and this is ugly. The children are the young boys.
73:18: Then he increased the description of that day with severity, saying: 18- The sky will be split by it, meaning it will be cracked by it due to its severity and great horror. The sentence is another description of the day, and the ba is causal. It was said that it has the meaning of fi: meaning it will be split in it. It was also said that it has the meaning of lam: meaning it will be split for it. He said munfatar and did not say munfatarah because the sky is considered to be something, since it has changed, and nothing remains of it except what is expressed by something. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: He did not say munfatarah because its metaphor is the ceiling, as al-Shafi’i said: If He raised the sky to a people, we would join the sky and the clouds. This is as in His statement: And We made the sky a protected ceiling. Al-Farra’ said: The sky is masculine and feminine. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: It is from the same category as spreading locusts and green trees, and hollowed-out palm trunks. He also said: That is, the sky is bursting like they say a nursing woman: that is, one who breastfeeds by way of lineage, and its bursting is for the descent of the angels as He said: When the sky is split and His statement: The heavens almost burst from above them. It was said that it is burst by: that is, by God and what is meant is by His command, and the first is more appropriate. His promise was to be fulfilled, that is, and God’s promise of what He promised of resurrection, judgment, and other things was to come to pass without fail. The verbal noun is added to its subject, or Today’s promise was to be fulfilled, so the verbal noun is added to its object. Muqatil said: His promise was that He would make His religion prevail over all religions. Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Muhammad ibn Nasr in his Book of Prayer, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham that he said: “I said to Aisha: ‘Tell me about the night prayer of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).’ She said: ‘Do you not recite this Surah, “O you encased in a cloak”? I said: ‘Yes.’ She said: ‘God enjoined the night prayer at the beginning of this Surah. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions stood for a year until their feet swelled. God held the end of it in the heavens for twelve months, then He revealed the alleviation at the end of this Surah, so the night prayer became voluntary after it had been enjoined.’” This hadith has been narrated on her authority through various chains of narration. Ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Muhammad ibn Nasr, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas that he said: ‘When the beginning of al-Muzzammil was revealed, they would stand for approximately the same amount of time as they stand in Ramadan until the end of it was revealed. There was a period of about a year between its beginning and end.’” And Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Nasr narrated on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami, who said: When the verse, O you who are wrapped in a cloak, was revealed, they stood for a year until their feet and legs became swollen, until the verse, Then recite as much of it as is easy for you, was revealed, and the people were relieved. Abu Dawud narrated in his Naskh, Ibn Nasr, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas said: In Al-Muzzammil, Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, half of it was abrogated by the verse in which it says, He knew that you could not enumerate it, so He turned to you in forgiveness, so recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an and the rising of the night was the first part of it. He says, “This is more likely to enable you to enumerate what God has enjoined upon you of standing at night, because when a person sleeps, he does not know when he will wake up. His statement, “I stand for a little while” is more likely to enable him to understand the recitation of the Qur’an. His statement, Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion means a long period of rest. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it from him regarding his statement, O you who are wrapped up, he said, You have wrapped up this matter, so carry it out. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding the verse as well, he said, He wraps himself up in the clothes. Al-Firyabi narrated from Abu Salih also from him, And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation, he said, You recite two or three verses, then stop, not wasting time. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Munayyir in his Musnad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Muhammad ibn Nasr also narrated from him, And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. He said: Clear it clearly. Al-Askari narrated in Al-Mawa’iz on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, with a similar hadith. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Nasr, and Al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated from Aisha, “Whenever revelation came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was on his she-camel, it would lower its hump and could not move until it was relieved, and it would recite, ‘Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word.’” Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Nasr, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, Indeed, the rising of the night, he said: The night prayer in the language of the Abyssinians, when a man rises, they say ‘rise’. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from him, he said: The rising of the night is its beginning. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Nasr also narrated from him, he said: The entire night is rising. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated - and authenticated it - on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: The rising of the night in Abyssinia is the night prayer. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated in Al-Musannaf, Ibn Nasr, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The rising of the night is between sunset and night prayers. `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Nasr, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim in Al-Kuna narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion, he said: The exertion is freeing oneself for one’s needs and sleeping. Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: When the verse: And leave Me and the deniers of ease and grant them respite for a little was revealed, it was only a short time until the Battle of Badr occurred. `Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, Indeed, with Us are shackles, he said: chains. `Abd ibn Humayd and `Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id Al-Zuhd, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it and al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A choking food He said: The tree of Zaqqum. Al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated on his authority regarding his statement: A spreading sand dune He said: The spreading sand is what if you take something from it, the rest of it follows you. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: A spreading sand dune He said: The flowing sand. And regarding his statement: A severe and devastating seizure He said: Severe. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited: “He turns the children into gray hair” He said: That is on the Day of Resurrection, and that is the day when God will say to Adam: Arise and send from your descendants a group to the Fire. He will say: How many, O Lord? He said: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine, and one will be saved. That was difficult for the Muslims, and when he saw that in their faces, he said: The children of Adam are many, and Gog and Magog are from the children of Adam. Not a single one of them dies until a thousand men inherit him from his loins. So in them and those like them is a Paradise for you.” Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud something similar but in a shorter form. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of `Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn `Abbas regarding his statement, The sky will be split by it, that he said: Full in the language of Abyssinia. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority that he said: “Heavy. Heavy.” Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority regarding the verse that he said: It means the sky will be split.
73:19: The reference in his saying: 19- Indeed, this is to what came before of the verses, and the reminder and admonition, and the reference to all the verses of the Qur’an, to what is in this surah only so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way meaning he may take through obedience, the most important type of which is monotheism to his Lord, a path that will lead him to Paradise.
73:20: 20- Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand in prayer nearly two-thirds of the night. The meaning of nearest is less. Nearest is used as a metaphor for it because when the distance between years gets close, the time between them becomes shorter. And half of it is in apposition to nearest. “And a third of it” is in apposition to half of it. The meaning is that God knows that His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stands in prayer for less than two-thirds of the night, and stands half of it, and stands a third of it. Ibn Kathir and the Kufians read it in the accusative case. The majority read and a half of it and a third of it in the genitive case in apposition to two-thirds of the night. The meaning is that God knows that His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stands in prayer for less than two-thirds of the night, and less than half of it, and less than a third of it. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose the reading of the majority because of the statement, He knows that you will not count it. So how can they stand for half of it and a third of it when they cannot count it? Al-Farra' said: The first reading is more likely to be correct because he said: Less than two-thirds of the night. Then he explained the same few “and a group of those with you” as being connected to the pronoun in stand up: meaning, a group of your companions stand up that amount with you. And God determines the night and the day meaning, He knows the amounts of night and day according to their true nature and is unique to Him alone, and you do not know that truly. Ata' said: He means that the knowledge of what you do does not escape Him. Meaning, He knows the amounts of night and day, so He knows the amount of time you spend standing up during the night. He knows that you will not be able to count it means that you will not be able to do it. He knows the amounts of night and day truly... In that there is an omitted pronoun of the subject. It was also said that the meaning is: You will not be able to do the night prayer. Al-Qurtubi said: The first is more correct, because the night prayer is never entirely obligatory. Muqatil and others said: When the verse, Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little * Half of it, or subtract a little from it, * Or add to it, was revealed, it was difficult for them. A man would not know when half of the night was, or a third of it, so he would stand until morning for fear of making a mistake. Their feet would swell and their colors would fade, so God had mercy on them and made it easier for them, saying, He knew that you could not enumerate it, meaning, He knew that you could not enumerate it, because if you increased it, it would be burdensome for you and you would need to undertake something that is not obligatory, and if you decreased it would be difficult for you. So He turned to you in forgiveness, meaning, He returned to you with pardon and gave you permission to omit standing in prayer. It was also said, So He turned to you in forgiveness of the obligation of standing in prayer when you were unable to do so. The root of repentance is return, as mentioned above. So the meaning is: He returned you from being burdensome to [making it light], and from difficulty to ease. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an, meaning, recite in the night prayer what is easy for you and what is easy for you from it without anticipating a specific time. Al-Hasan said: It is what we recite in the Maghrib and Isha prayers. Al-Suddi said: Also, whoever recites one hundred verses in one night, the Qur’an will not challenge him. Ka'b said: Whoever recites one hundred verses in a night will be recorded among the devout. Sa'id said: Fifty verses. It was said that the meaning of recite as much of it as is easy for you is to pray as much of the night prayer as is easy for you. Prayer is called the Qur'an, as in His statement: And the Qur'an of dawn. It was said that this verse abrogated the night prayer and half of it, and the reduction from the half, and the addition to it. It is possible that what this verse includes is an established obligation, and it is possible that it was abrogated, as in His statement: "And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a position of praise." Al-Shafi'i said: It is obligatory to seek evidence from the Sunnah for one of the two meanings. We found the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) indicating that there is no obligation of prayer except the five. Some people have said that the night prayer was abrogated with regard to him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and with regard to his ummah. It was said that the estimated amount was abrogated, but the original obligation remained. It was said that it was abrogated for the Ummah, but remained obligatory for him (peace and blessings be upon him). The first opinion is that the night prayer was abrogated in general for him (peace and blessings be upon him) and for his Ummah. His statement, So recite as much of it as is easy for you does not indicate that any obligation remained. If what is meant by it is recitation from the Qur’an, then it is found in the Maghrib and ‘Isha’ prayers and the confirmed voluntary prayers that follow them. If what is meant by it is night prayer, then the night prayer is found in the Maghrib and ‘Isha’ prayers and the voluntary prayers that follow them. Also, the authentic hadiths that clearly state that the questioner said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), Do I have to do anything else? meaning the five daily prayers? He said, No, unless it is a voluntary prayer, indicate that nothing else is obligatory. Thus, the obligation of night prayer and its prayer was lifted from the Ummah, just as the obligation of that was lifted from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) with his statement, And during part of the night, pray voluntary prayers with it. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said about his statement, So recite as much of it as is easy for you, this was in the early days of Islam, then it was abrogated by the five daily prayers for the believers. This was specifically proven for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as He said: And establish prayer. Then God, the Almighty, mentioned their excuse, saying: He knows that there will be among you some who are ill, so they will not be able to stand at night, and others who travel throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God, meaning they travel there for trade and profit, seeking from God’s provisions what they need for their livelihood, so they are not able to stand at night, and others who fight in the cause of God, meaning the mujahideen, so they are not able to stand at night. Here, God, the Almighty, mentioned three reasons for the dispensation and the lifting of the obligation of standing at night. He lifted it from the entire ummah because of these excuses that some of them have. Then He mentioned what they should do after this dispensation, saying: So recite what is easy of it, and the explanation of this was mentioned earlier. The repetition is for emphasis. And establish prayer, meaning the obligatory prayer, which is the fifth because of its strength. And give zakat, meaning what is obligatory on wealth. Al-Harith Al-Ukali said: It is Zakat Al-Fitr because Zakat on wealth became obligatory after that. It was also said that it is voluntary charity, and it was also said that it refers to all good deeds. And loan God a good loan means spend in the way of goodness from your hopes in a good manner. Its explanation has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Hadid. Zayd ibn Aslam said: A good loan is spending on one’s family. It was also said that it refers to spending in jihad. It was also said that it refers to paying the obligatory Zakat in a good manner, so it is an explanation of His statement: And give zakat. The first is more appropriate because of His statement: And whatever good you send forth for yourselves - you will find it with God. The apparent meaning is general: any good, whether mentioned or not, is better and greater in reward than what you delay until death or bequeath to be given after your death. The accusative of good is because it is the second object of you will find it. The pronoun is a separating pronoun, and the majority of scholars have read it in the accusative case.
