Abu al-Sammak and Ibn al-Samee’ read it in the nominative case, so that he is the subject and the best is its predicate. The sentence is in the accusative case as the second object of you find him. Abu Zayd said: It is the language of Tamim, they raise what comes after the separating pronoun. Sibawayh recited: You yearn for Laila, and you left her and were with her in public. You are more capable. The majority also read and greater in the accusative case, in apposition to good. Abu al-Sammak and Ibn al-Samee’ read it in the nominative case, just as they read good in the nominative case and reward in the accusative case as a distinction. And seek forgiveness from God, meaning ask Him for forgiveness for your sins, for you will not be free from sins that you commit. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning He is very forgiving to those who seek His forgiveness, and very merciful to those who seek His mercy. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), So recite as much of it as is easy for you. He said: One hundred verses. Ad-Daraqutni and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan and Hasanat on the authority of Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: “I prayed behind Ibn Abbas, and in the first rak’ah he recited ‘Al-Hamdu Lillah Rabb Al-‘Alamin’ and the first verse of Surat Al-Baqarah, then he bowed. When we finished, he turned to us and said: ‘God says: “So recite as much of it as is easy for you.”’” Ibn Kathir said: This is a very strange hadith that I only saw in Al-Tabarani’s Mu’jam. Ahmad and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded us to recite Al-Fatihah and whatever is easy for us.” We already mentioned in the first discussion of this surah what was narrated that these verses mentioned here abrogate the obligation of night prayer, so refer to it.
74:1: It has fifty-six verses, and it is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Muddaththir was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar statement on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr. It will be mentioned later that the beginning of this surah was the first part of the Qur’an to be revealed. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: When the revelation began to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Gabriel came to him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw him on two paths between the sky and the earth like a glittering light. He was startled and fell unconscious. When he regained consciousness, he went to Khadija and called for water and poured it over him, saying: Cover me, cover me. So they covered him with a blanket, and he said: 1- O you who are wrapped up in your garments, arise and warn. The meaning of O you who are wrapped up in your garments is O you who are covered with them. The original form is al-mutaddathir, but the t was assimilated into the d to make them similar. The majority of scholars have read it with assimilation, and Abu Al-Mutaddathir read it according to the original form. The dithaar is what is worn over the shayar, and the shayar is what is next to the body. Ikrimah said: The meaning is O you who are wrapped up in prophethood and its burdens. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is a far-fetched metaphor because he was not a prophet at that time.
74:2: 2- Rise and warn meaning get up and frighten the people of Mecca and warn them of the punishment if they do not submit, or get up from your bed, or get up with determination and resolve. It was said that the warning here is informing them of his prophethood, and it was also said that he informed them of monotheism. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is get up, pray, and command the prayer.
74:3: 3- And your Lord, so magnify meaning, glorify your Master, Owner, and Reformer of your affairs. This is to describe Him, glory be to Him, with pride and greatness, and that He is greater than to have a partner as the disbelievers believe, and greater than to have a wife or a son. Ibn Al-Arabi said: What is meant by it is the glorification of sanctification and purification by removing opposites, companions, and idols. No one should be taken as a protector other than Him, no one should be worshipped other than Him, and no action should be seen for anyone other than Him, and no blessing except from Him. Al-Zajjaj said: The fa in fa-kbar has the meaning of recompense, just as it has in fan-an-dhar. Ibn Jinni said: It is like your saying Zayd, so strike, meaning Zayd, strike, so the fa is redundant.
74:4: 4- And your garments purify refers to the garments worn according to the linguistic meaning. God the Almighty commanded him to purify his garments and keep them free from impurities, and to remove whatever had fallen into them. It was said that what is meant by garments is deeds, or the heart, or the soul, or the body, or the family, or the religion, or morals. Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and Abu Razin said: That is, your deeds, so put them right. Qatada said: Your soul, so purify from sin, and the garments refer to the soul. Saeed bin Jubair said: Your heart, so purify. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qais: So separate my clothes from your clothes and let them fall off Akrima said: The meaning is that he dressed her without treachery or immorality. He said: Haven’t you heard the poet say: Praise be to God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I hide from treachery. The poet is Ghailan bin Salamah Al-Thaqafi. Among the uses of clothes to refer to the soul is the saying of Antarah: I pierced his clothes with a long spear. The generous man is not forbidden to use spears. And the other said: The clothes of Bani Awf are pure and clean Al-Hasan and Al-Qurazi said: The meaning is and your morals are pure because the human being’s morals encompass his conditions as his clothes encompass his soul. From this is the poet’s saying: Yahya is not to be blamed for bad character, and Yahya is pure and free Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is and your clothes, so shorten them, because shortening the garment is further from impurities if they are dragged on the ground. Tawus said the same, but the first is more appropriate because it is the literal meaning. There is no use of clothes as a metaphor for other things due to a connection with its context that indicates that it is what is meant when it is generalized. There is no disagreement about such a principle, I mean taking it literally when generalized. The verse is evidence of the obligation of clothes to be pure in prayer.
74:5: 5- And avoid the abomination. In the language, the meaning of rajz is torment. There are two pronunciations for it: kasra or damma. Polytheism and idol worship are called rajz because they are the cause of rajz. The majority read rajz with kasra on the ra. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Hafs, and Ibn Muhaisin read it with damma. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: rajz is the idols, as in His statement: So avoid the abomination of idols. Ibn Zayd said the same. Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i said: rajz is the sin, and abandonment is abandonment. Qatada said: rajz is Isaf and Na'ilah, and they are two idols that were near the House. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi', and Al-Kisa'i said: rajz with damma is the idol, and rajz with kasra is the torment. Al-Suddi said: rajz with damma on the ra is the threat, and the first is more appropriate.
74:6: 6- And do not bestow a favor, hoping to get more The majority read La tamanna without idgham, while Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Yaman, and Al-Ashhab Al-Uqayli read it with idgham, and the majority read Tastathkar with the nominative case as a state: that is, do not bestow a favor while you are hoping to get more. It was also said that it was with the deletion of An, and the original is Do not bestow a favor, hoping to get more, but when it was deleted, it was raised. Al-Kisa'i said: If An is deleted, the verb is raised. Yahya bin Waththab and Al-A'mash read Tastathkar with the addition of An. Al-Hasan and Ibn Abi Ubla also read Tastathkar with the accusative case as a substitute for Tamannan as in his saying: He will encounter sins * doubled for him, and the saying of the poet: When you come to visit us in our lands, you will find abundant firewood and a blazing fire. Or the jussive mood to make the connection take the place of the pause: as in the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Today I drink without committing any sin against God or being excessive. With the sukoon of ashrab. This reading has been objected to, because his saying tastaghmur cannot be a substitute for tamaana, because tamaana is not tamaana, and it cannot be an answer to a prohibition. The early Muslims differed over the meaning of the verse. Some said that it means: Do not consider your Lord a favor for the burdens of prophethood you bear, like someone who thinks his burden is too much because of someone else. Others said: Do not give a gift seeking something better than it. This was said by Ikrimah and Qatadah. Ad-Dahhak said: God forbade this for His Messenger, because he was commanded with the most noble of manners and the most sublime of morals, and He permitted it for his ummah. Mujahid said: Do not be too weak to consider good deeds to be plentiful, like the saying a strong rope when it is weak. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Do not intend your deeds to be plentiful in your eyes. Ibn Kaysan said: Do not consider a deed too much for yourself, for your deeds are a favor from God to you, as He has provided you with a path to His worship. Others said: Do not consider prophethood and the Quran to be a favor to people, taking a reward from them, believing it to be too much. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: Do not give your wealth out of flattery. Zayd ibn Aslam said: If you are given a gift, give it to your Lord.
74:7: 7- And for the sake of your Lord be patient meaning for the sake of your Lord, so be patient in obeying Him and fulfilling His obligations. The meaning is: for the sake of your Lord and His reward. Muqatil and Mujahid said: Be patient in the face of harm and denial. Ibn Zayd said: You have undertaken a great matter, and the Arabs and non-Arabs fought you, so be patient in it for the sake of God. It was also said: Be patient under its resources, for the decree of God is His. It was also said: Be patient in the face of trials, and it was also said: Be patient in the face of commands and prohibitions.
74:8: 8- When he beats the trumpet. The trumpet is a noun derived from the verb naqr, as if it is his custom to beat it to make a sound. Naqr in the speech of the Arabs is the sound, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Lower it by clicking what you raised They say, We will blow the name of a man when he calls upon him. What is meant here is the blowing of the trumpet, and what is meant is the second blowing, and it was said the first. We have already discussed this in Surat Al-An’am and Surat An-Nahl, and the fa is for causality, as if it was said: Be patient with their harm, for before them is a terrible day in which they will meet the consequences of their actions.
74:9: The factor in if is what is indicated by his saying: 9- Then that Day will be a difficult Day * for the disbelievers. Its meaning is that the matter will be difficult for them. It was said that the factor in it is what is indicated by that because it is an allusion to the knocking, and that Day is a substitute for if, or a subject and its predicate is a difficult Day, and the sentence is the predicate of that, and it was said that it is an adverbial phrase for the predicate because the estimate is the occurrence of a difficult Day.
74:10: And his saying: 10- Not easy is an emphasis on its difficulty for them, because its not being easy was understood from his saying, A difficult day.
74:11: 11- "Leave me and he whom I created alone" meaning [leave me], and it is a word of threat and warning, and the meaning is: Leave me and He who created him while he was alone in his mother's womb, with no wealth or children. This is on the basis that "alone" is in the accusative case as a state of the relative pronoun or of the deleted pronoun referring to it. It is also possible that it is a state of the "ya in dharni": meaning leave me alone with him, for I will suffice you in taking revenge on him, and the first is more appropriate. The commentators said: He is Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah. Muqatil said: He is saying leave me alone with him, for I will be alone with his destruction. He was mentioned specifically because of his great disbelief and ingratitude for the blessings of God upon him. It was also said that by "alone" he meant the one whose father is not known, and it was said about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah that he was abandoned.
74:12: 12- And I made for him abundant wealth meaning abundant, or it is extended with increase and growth little by little. Al-Zajjaj said: Wealth that is not cut off from him. Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira was famous for having an abundance of wealth of various kinds. It was said that he would obtain from the proceeds of his wealth a million thousand dinars, and it was said four thousand dinars, and it was said a thousand dinars.
74:13: 13- And sons as witnesses meaning, He made for him sons who were present with him in Mecca, who did not travel nor did they need to be separated in search of a livelihood due to their father’s abundant wealth. Ad-Dahhak said: There were seven born in Mecca, and five born in Taif. Saeed bin Jubair said: There were thirteen sons. Muqatil said: There were seven, all men, three of whom embraced Islam: Khalid, Hisham, and Al-Walid bin Al-Walid. After the revelation of this verse, Al-Walid’s wealth and children continued to decrease until he died. It was said that the meaning of witnesses is that whenever he was mentioned, they were mentioned with him. It was also said that they witnessed what he witnessed with him and carried out what he did.
74:14: 14- And I made it easy for him meaning I made life easy for him, gave him a long life, and made him a leader among the Quraysh. Tamheed among the Arabs means preparation, and from this comes the word cradle of a child. Mujahid said: It is money, one on top of the other, just as a bed is made easy.
74:15: 15- Then he desires that I should have more meaning that after all of this he desires more due to his great greed and intense desire, along with his ingratitude for blessings and his associating partners with God. Al-Hasan said: He did not desire that I should enter Paradise, and he used to say: If Muhammad is truthful, then Paradise was not created except for me.
74:16: Then God, the Exalted, deterred him and rebuked him, saying: 16- No, meaning I will not add anything to it. Then He explained that by saying: Indeed, he was obstinate toward Our verses, meaning he was stubborn toward them and disbelieved in what We revealed of them to Our Messenger. It is said that someone is stubborn if he opposes the truth and rejects it, and he knows it, so he is stubborn and obstinate. The obstinate is the one who goes off the path and deviates from the intended path. From this is the saying of Al-Harithi: If you ride, make me the middle one, for I am old and cannot bear to be stubborn. Abu Saleh said: Obstinate means distant. Qatada said: Denying. Muqatil said: Averse.
74:17: 17- I will exhaust him with climbing meaning I will burden him with a lot of torture, which is an example of the difficult and unbearable torture he will encounter. It was said that the meaning is: he will be burdened with climbing a mountain of fire, and exhaustion in the speech of the Arabs means that a person carries a heavy thing.
74:18: Sentence 18 - He thought and estimated is an explanation for the previous threat: that is, he thought about the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what was revealed to him of the Qur’an, and he estimated in his mind: that is, he prepared the speech in his mind. The Arabs say: I prepared something if you estimated it, and I estimated something if you made it ready. This is because when he heard the Qur’an, he did not stop thinking about what to say in it, and he estimated in his mind what to say.
74:19: So God condemned him and said: 19- He killed him however he decreed meaning he cursed and tortured however he decreed: meaning in whatever state he decreed from speech, as is said in speech: I will strike him however he did: meaning in whatever state he was in. And it was said that the meaning is: he overcame and defeated however he decreed, and from this is the saying of the poet: Your eyes did not shed tears except to strike with your arrows at the tenths of the heart of the murderer Al-Zuhri said: He was tortured, and this is a form of supplication against him.
74:20: The repetition in his saying: 20- Then he killed as he decreed is for exaggeration and emphasis.
74:21: 21- Then he looked meaning with what he could reject or criticize the Qur’an, or he thought about the Qur’an and contemplated what it was.
74:22: 22- Then he frowned meaning he frowned when he did not find a slur to slander the Qur’an. Frowning is the source of frowning, which is shortened to frowning, and it was said that he frowned in the faces of the believers, and it was said that he frowned in the face of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he became sad meaning his face turned dark and changed. From this is the saying of the poet: We woke up in Tamim on the morning of Al-Haffar with a tangible meteor shower in its entirety And the other said: I was disturbed by her aversion and her turning away from my needs and her stubbornness. It is said that a frown appears on the face after a conversation, while a pimple appears on the face before it. The Arabs say: A basir face if it has changed and darkened. Al-Raghib said: Basr means hastening evil before its time, like a man basr his need: meaning he asked for it at the wrong time. He said: And from this is his saying: He frowned and was angry meaning he showed a frown before its time and before its appointed time. The people of Yemen say: Basr al-Markab and absara: meaning it stopped, neither advancing nor falling behind. And we have become absara: meaning we have reached the basur.
74:23: 23- Then he turned away and was arrogant meaning he turned away from the truth, went to his family, and was too proud to believe.
74:24: 24- He said, 'This is nothing but magic that is being passed on.' That is, it is being passed on to someone else and made to appear to them. Magic means presenting falsehood as truth, or deception, as was explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. It is said, I passed on the hadith by its chain of transmission, if you mentioned it on the authority of someone else. From this is the saying of Al-A'sha: What you fought over is clear to the listener and the effect.
74:25: 25- This is nothing but the word of mankind meaning that it is the word of mankind, and not the word of God, and it is a confirmation of what came before it. It will come that Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira only said this statement to please his people after he admitted that it has sweetness and that it has freshness, and so on until the end of his words.
74:26: And when he said this statement that God related about him, God Almighty said: 26- I will cast him into Hellfire, meaning I will cast him into Hellfire. Saqar is one of the names of Hellfire and one of the levels of Hellfire. It was said that this sentence is a substitute for his saying, I will force him to ascend.
74:27: Then the Almighty exaggerated in describing the Fire and its severity, saying: 27- And what will make you know what Saqar is? That is, what will make you know what it is? The Arabs say: And what will make you know what such and such is if they want to exaggerate its matter, magnify its importance, and magnify its severity. What is the first subject, and the phrase What is Saqar is the predicate of the subject.
74:28: Then he explained its condition, saying: 28- It leaves nothing and spares nothing. The sentence is resumed to explain the condition of Saqar and reveal its description. It was said that it is in the accusative case as a state, and the factor in it is the meaning of glorification, because his saying: And what will make you know what Saqar is? indicates glorification, so it is as if he said: They considered Saqar to be great in this condition, and the first is more appropriate, and the object of the two verbs is omitted. Al-Suddi said: It leaves them no flesh and spares them no bone. Ata' said: It leaves no living person in it and spares no dead person. It was said that they are two words with one meaning, repeated for emphasis, like you say: Turn away from me, and turn away from me.
74:29: 29- A glare for mankind The majority of scholars read Lawha in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject. It was also said that it is an adjective for Hellfire, but the former is more appropriate. Al-Hasan, Atiyah Al-Awfi, Nasr bin Asim, Isa bin Omar, Ibn Abi Ubla, and Zaid bin Ali read it in the accusative case as a state or as a specification for intimidation. It is said: laha yaluhu: meaning it appeared, and the meaning is: it appears to mankind. Al-Hasan said: Hell will appear to them until they see it clearly, like his statement: And Hellfire will be brought into view for whoever sees. It was also said that the meaning of Lawha yaluhu is that it changes them and blackens them. Mujahid said: The Arabs say: laha yaluhu the glare of heat, cold, sickness, and sadness, if it changes them. This is more likely than the former, and the majority of commentators agreed with it. An example of this is the saying of the poet: Hind was surprised when she saw me pale, saying, Something painted by the heavens. Any jealousy, and from this is the saying of Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj: A wave of it after a body and lust, your thin wave folds for the race Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is that she is thirsty for good report, and he recited: She gave me a drink on a board of water, a drink that God gave to the generous ones. What is meant by humans is either the visible skin of a human being, as most have said, or what is meant by it is the people of Hell among mankind, as Al-Akhfash said.
74:30: 30- Over it are nineteen. The commentators said: He means over the Fire are nineteen angels who are its guardians. It was also said that they are nineteen classes of angels, and it was also said that they are nineteen rows of their rows, and it was also said that nineteen leaders with each leader a group of angels, and the first is more appropriate. Al-Tha’labi said: This is not denied, for if one angel takes the souls of all creation, it would be more appropriate for there to be nineteen over the punishment of some of creation. The majority read it as nineteen with a fat-ha on the sheen from ten. Abu Ja’far ibn al-Qa’qa’ and Talhah ibn Sulayman read it with a sukoon on it. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman said: The first part of the Qur’an to be revealed was O you who are wrapped up in your cloak. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir said to him: They say that the first part to be revealed was Read in the name of your Lord who created. Abu Salamah said: I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah about that and I said to him the same as you said. Jabir said: I will not tell you anything except what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told us. He said: “I stayed in Hira’ and when I had finished staying in Hira’ I dismounted and was called. I looked to my right but did not see anything, and I looked to my left but did not see anything, and I looked behind me but did not see anything. I raised my head and saw the angel who had come to me in Hira’ sitting on a throne between the heaven and the earth. I was terrified by him, so I went back and said: Cover me. So they covered me. Then the following was revealed: “O you who are wrapped up in your cloak, arise and warn” until His saying: and avoid abomination. There will come in Surat Iqra’ what indicates that it is the first surah to be revealed, and the combination is possible. Al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and authenticated it, O you who are wrapped up in your cloak, so he said: Wrap this matter up, so carry it out. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, O you who are wrapped up in your cloak, he said: the one sleeping. And your garments purify, he said: Do not let the clothes you wear be from false earnings. And shun uncleanliness, he said: idols. And do not bestow favors, seeking more, he said: Do not give something seeking something better. Al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim also narrated, and authenticated it on his authority, And your garments purify, he said: from sin. He said: In Arabic, it means clean clothing. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority, And your garments purify, he said: from treachery, do not be treacherous. Sa`id bin Mansur, `Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Anbari, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of `Ikrimah, on his authority also, that he was asked about his statement: And your garments purify. He said: Do not wear them on treachery. Then he said: Do you not hear the words of Ghailan bin Salamah: Praise be to God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I cover myself with treachery. At-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan also narrated from him: And do not bestow a favor expecting more. He said: Do not give a man a gift other men would give you more than him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him: Then when the trumpet is blown. He said: The Trumpet. A difficult Day. He said: A severe one. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him: Leave Me and he whom I created alone. Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira said: Al-Hakim narrated - who authenticated it - and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala’il also narrated from him: Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and recited the Quran to him, and it was as if he felt pity for him. report of that reached Abu Jahl, so he came to him and said: O uncle, your people want to collect wealth for you to give it to you, but you came to Muhammad to offer what he had given you. He said: The Quraysh know that I am one of the wealthiest of them. He said: Then say something about him that will convey to your people that you deny it and that you dislike it. He said: What should I say? By God, there is no man among you who knows more about poetry than I do, neither its rajaz, nor its qasida, nor the poetry of the jinn. By God, this man who says this does not resemble anything of this. By God, his words have sweetness and a freshness to them. They are fruitful at the top and abundant at the bottom. They rise and whatever rises, and they crush what is beneath them. He said, "By God, your people will not be satisfied until you say something about it. He said, Then let me think. When he had thought, he said, This is magic that is being passed on, it is being passed on from others. Then the verse, Leave Me and he whom I created alone" was revealed. Abd al-Razzaq transmitted this from Ikrimah as a mursal. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and others transmitted it as well. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Umar ibn al-Khattab that he was asked about the statement, "And I have given him abundant wealth," he said: The yield of a month by a month. Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn Abbas, "And I have given him abundant wealth," he said: A thousand dinars. Hannad narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, regarding his statement, I will make him ascend, he said: It is a mountain in Hell that they are required to climb. Every time they place their hands on it, they melt, but when they lift them up, they return to what they were. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, obstinately, he said: Denial. Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: Ascent is a mountain in Hell that the disbeliever ascends for seventy autumns, then he falls and remains in it like that forever. Al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: It is strange and we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Lahi’ah on the authority of Diraj. Ibn Kathir said: It contains strangeness and oddity. End quote. A group narrated it on the authority of Abu Saeed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ascent is a rock in Hell that the disbeliever is dragged on his face. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, who said: A mountain in Hell. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him regarding his statement, It leaves nothing and spares nothing, he said: It leaves nothing of them, and if they are replaced by another creation, it spares nothing to return them to the path of the first punishment. Abd ibn Humayd also narrated from him, A burner for mankind, he said: It burns the skin, burning it and changing its color, so it becomes blacker than night. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, A burner, he said: A burner. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Ba’th from al-Baraa’ that a group of Jews asked some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the keepers of Hell, and he said: God and His Messenger know best. Then Gabriel came and informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and at that moment the following was revealed to him: Over them are nineteen.
74:31: When the words of God Almighty were revealed: Over it are nineteen, Abu Jahl said: Muhammad has only nineteen helpers. Muhammad frightens you with nineteen, and you are the dark ones. Is it possible for every hundred men among you to strike one of them and then emerge from the Fire? Abu al-Ashd, a man from Banu Jumah, said: O people of Quraysh, when the Day of Resurrection comes, I will walk in front of you, pushing ten with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder, and we will proceed to enter Paradise. Then God revealed: 31- And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels, meaning We have not made the administrators of the Fire and those who punish those in it except angels. So who can bear the angels and who can overcome them? So how will you, O disbelievers, attempt to overcome them? It was said that He made them angels because they are different from the created beings of jinn and humans, and are not affected by the tenderness and compassion that affects gatherings. It was also said that they are the most upright of God’s creation in His right and in anger for His sake, and the most powerful and strongest in strike. And We did not make their number except as a trial meaning misguidance for those who underestimated their number and as a trial for them. The meaning is: We did not make their number this number mentioned in the Qur’an except as a misguidance and trial for them, until they said what they said so that their punishment would be doubled and God’s wrath upon them would increase. It was said that the meaning of except a trial is except a torment, as in His statement: On the Day when they will be tested over the Fire, meaning they will be tormented. The lam in His statement: that those who were given the Scripture may be certain is related to we made, and what is meant by the People of the Scripture are the Jews and Christians regarding the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because what is in the Qur’an agrees with what is in their books. And those who believe may increase in faith. It was said that what is meant are those who believed from the People of the Scripture, such as Abdullah ibn Salam. It was said that what is meant are the believers from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning is: that they may increase in certainty to their certainty because they saw the agreement of the People of the Scripture with them. The phrase and let not those who were given the Scripture and the believers doubt confirms what was mentioned previously regarding certainty and the increase in faith. The meaning is to negate doubt from them regarding the religion, or that the number of the guards of Hell is nineteen. There is no doubt in reality from the believers, but it is a way of exposing others who have doubts before it. And that those in whose hearts is a disease and the disbelievers may say, ‘What does God intend by this as an example?’ What is meant by those in whose hearts is a disease are The hypocrites. Even though the Surah was revealed in Mecca and there was no hypocrisy at that time, it is a prediction of what would happen in Medina. Or what is meant by the disease is merely the occurrence of a third and doubt, which would happen among the disbelievers. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The Surah was revealed in Mecca and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca, so the disease in this verse is disputed. What is meant by His statement, and the disbelievers, are the disbelievers among the Arabs of Mecca and others. The meaning of What did God intend by this as an example? is that He intended by this strange number to make the example strange. Al-Layth said: The example is the modern, and from it is His statement, The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised, meaning its story is the report about it. Thus does God leave astray whom He wills, meaning like that misguidance mentioned previously. And His statement, And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve. “God leaves astray whom He wills” of His servants, and the kaf is an attribute of a deleted source. And guides whom He wills of His servants. The meaning is: Like that misguidance is for the disbelievers and guidance is for the believers. God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. It was also said that the meaning is: Thus God misguides from Paradise whom He wills and guides to it whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. That is, He knows the number of His creation and the number of His multitudes of angels and others. Only He alone has the power to know that. Ata’ said: He means the angels whom He created to torment the people of Hell. None knows their number except God. The meaning is that the keepers of Hell, even though they are nineteen, have helpers and soldiers from among the angels that none knows except God, the Most High. Then He, the Most High, returned to mentioning Saqar and said: And it is only a reminder to mankind. That is, Saqar and what is mentioned about the number of its keepers are only a reminder and an admonition to the world. It was also said that and it is meaning the proofs, arguments and the Qur’an are only a reminder to mankind. Al-Zajjaj said: The fire of this world is a reminder of the fire of the Hereafter, but this is far-fetched. It was also said that it meaning the number of the keepers of Hell is only a reminder to mankind so that they may know the perfection of God’s power and that He does not need helpers and supporters. It was also said that the pronoun in and it is refers to the soldiers.
74:32: Then the Almighty deterred and warned the deniers, saying: 32- No, by the moon. Al-Farra’ said: No is a conjunction for the oath. The meaning is: meaning, by the moon. It was also said that the meaning is: truly, by the moon. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning is to refute the claim of whoever claims that he can resist the keepers of Hell: meaning, the matter is not as he says. Then He swore to that effect by the moon and what comes after it, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse.
74:33: 33- And the night when it departs meaning it has gone. The majority read when with the addition of an alif, dabar with the weight of daraba as an adverbial phrase for the future. Nafi', Hafs and Hamza read idh without an alif, adbara with the weight of akram as an adverbial phrase for the past. Dab and adbara are two dialects, just as one says aqbal al-zaman time has approached and qabal al-zaman time has passed. One says dabar al-layl and adbara night if it has turned away and gone.
74:34: 34- And the morning when it dawns meaning it becomes bright and clear.
74:35: 35- It is one of the greatest things. This is the answer to the oath, and the pronoun refers to Saqar: that is, Saqar is one of the greatest disasters or calamities, and great is the plural of greatest. Muqatil said: Greave is one of the names of Hellfire. It was said that it is: that is, their denial of Muhammad is one of the greatest things. It was said that the establishment of the Hour is one of the greatest things, and from this is the saying of the poet: O son of Al-Mualla, one of the greatest calamities of the age and the deaf of others has descended. The majority of scholars read li-ahadah with a hamza, while Nasr ibn Asim, Ibn Muhaisin, and Ibn Kathir, in one narration from him, read inna li-ahadah without a hamza. Al-Kalbi said: By al-kabir he meant the levels and gates of Hell.
74:36: 36- A warner to mankind The word warner is in the accusative case as a hal of the pronoun in it, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. It was narrated from him, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Ali Al-Farsi that it is a hal of his saying rise and warn, meaning rise, O Muhammad, and warn while you are a warner to mankind. Al-Farra' said: It is a verbal noun meaning warning, accusative with an implied verb. It was also said that it is in the accusative case as a distinguishing feature of one because it includes the meaning of organization, as if it was said the greatest of the great warnings. It was also said that it is a verbal noun accusative with warned mentioned at the beginning of the surah. It was also said that it is in the accusative case with an implied I mean, and it was also said that it is in the accusative case with the estimation of call, and it was also said that it is in the accusative case with the estimation of call or relay. It was also said that it is an object for which, and the estimation is: And indeed, it is one of the great things for the sake of warning mankind. The majority read it in the accusative case, while Abi bin Ka'b and Ibn Abi Ubla read it in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning, she is a warner, or he is a warner. There is a difference of opinion about the warner. Al-Hasan said: It is the Fire. It was also said: It is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Razin said: The meaning is: I am a warner to you from it. It was also said: The Qur’an is a warner to humanity because of what it contains of promise and threat.
74:37: 37- For whoever among you wills to advance or delay is a substitute for saying to mankind: that is, a warner for whoever among you wills to advance to obedience or delay it, and the meaning is: that the warning has been given to everyone who has believed and disbelieved. It was said that the doer of the will is God, the Most High: that is, for whoever among you wills to advance in faith or delay in disbelief, and the former is more appropriate. Al-Suddi said: For whoever among you wills to advance to the Fire mentioned above or delay to Paradise. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When Abu Jahl heard nineteen over it, he said to the Quraysh 106:May your mothers be bereaved of you! I hear Ibn Abi Kabsha telling you that the keepers of Hell are nineteen and you are the most numerous. Is every ten of you unable to strike a man from the keepers of Hell? Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority regarding His statement: And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve, that Abu al-Ashd said: Leave me alone with the keepers of Hell and I will take care of their burden for you. He said: “I was told that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described the keepers of Hell and said: Their eyes are like lightning, and their mouths are like rocks. They drag their hair. They have the strength of two heavy burdens. One of them accepts a nation from among the people and drives them, with a mountain on his neck until he throws them into the Fire and throws the mountain on them.” Al-Tabarani narrated in Al-Awsat and Abu Al-Shaykh on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them about the night of his Isra’. He said: So Gabriel and I ascended to the lowest heaven, and there I saw an angel called Ismail, who was the master of the lowest heaven, and before him were seventy thousand angels, with each angel’s army of one hundred thousand. He recited this verse: ‘And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him.’” Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The heaven groaned, and it is true that it should groan. There is not a finger’s space in it but an angel is prostrating on it.” And it was narrated by At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib. It is narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr as a mursal. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, When it departs, he said: The end of its darkness. Musaddad narrated in his Musnad, and Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God, And the night when it departs, so he remained silent until it was the last part of the night and he heard the call to prayer. He called to me, O Mujahid, this is when the night has departed. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the statement of God, For whoever among you wills to advance or fall behind, he said: Whoever wills may follow the obedience of God, and whoever wills may fall behind it.
74:38: His saying: 38- Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned. That is, it is taken by its deeds and is mortgaged to them, either to save it or to ruin it. The word raḥīnah is a noun meaning a pledge, like shimah meaning character. It is not an adjective. If it were an adjective, it would have been said raḥīn, because fa’il is the same for both masculine and feminine forms. The meaning is: Every soul is a pledge for its earnings, not to be released.
74:39: 39- Except the companions of the right hand for they will not be held hostage by their sins, but will be set free by their good deeds. There is disagreement about their identification. Some say they are the angels, others say they are the believers, others say they are the children of Muslims, others say they are those who were on Adam’s right hand, others say they are the people of truth, others say they are those who rely on virtue rather than work, and others say they are those whom God chose to serve Him.
74:40: 40- In gardens is in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, and the sentence is a resumption of the answer to a question that arose from what preceded it. It is possible that in gardens is a state of the people of the right hand, or a state of the subject of they ask each other, or an adverbial phrase for they ask each other. His saying, they ask each other may be in its proper context: that is, they ask each other, or it may mean they ask: that is, they ask others, like his invitation and his calling, so it is in the first way.
74:41: 41- About the criminals is related to they ask each other: that is, they ask each other about the conditions of the criminals. In the second case, about is redundant: that is, they ask the criminals.
74:42: And His statement: 42- What has brought you into Hellfire? This is based on the estimation of the statement: that is, they ask about the criminals, saying to them: What has brought you into Hellfire? Or they ask them, saying to them: What has brought you into Hellfire? The sentence, in both estimations, is in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is: What has brought you into Hellfire? You say, I threaded the thread into such-and-such: if you entered it. Al-Kalbi said: A man from the people of Paradise will ask a man from the people of Hellfire by name, saying to him: O so-and-so, what has brought you into Hellfire? It was said that the angels will ask about their relatives, so the angels will ask the polytheists, saying to them: What has brought you into Hellfire? Al-Farra' said: This strengthens the idea that the people of the right hand are the children, because they do not know about sins.
74:43: 43- They said, ‘We were not among those who prayed.’ That is, among the believers who prayed to God in this world.
74:44: 44- And we did not feed the poor meaning we did not give charity to the poor. It was said that these two are based on the obligatory prayer and the obligatory charity, because there is no punishment for anything other than what is obligatory, and in it is evidence that the infidels are addressed by the religious laws.
74:45: 45- And we used to engage in vain talk with the vain talkers meaning we used to mingle with the people of falsehood in their falsehood. Qatada said: Whenever someone went astray, we went astray with him. Al-Suddi said: We used to lie with the liars. Ibn Zayd said: We used to engage in vain talk with the vain talkers about the matter of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, which is their saying that he is a liar, a madman, a magician, and a poet.
74:46: 46- And we used to deny the Day of Judgment meaning the Day of Recompense and Accountability.
74:47: 47- Until the certainty comes to us, which is death, as in His saying: And worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you.
74:48: 48- So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them meaning the intercession of the angels and the prophets as it benefits the righteous.
74:49: 49- So why are they turning away from the reminder? The reminder is the reminder of the Qur’an’s admonitions. The fa is to arrange the denial of their turning away from the reminder in relation to what preceded it of the reasons for turning towards it. The turning away is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in the object of the preposition and the noun: meaning, what happened to them while they were turning away from the Qur’an, which contains the great reminder and the great admonition.
74:50: Then he likened their aversion to the Qur’an to donkeys, saying: 50 As if they were frightened donkeys. The clause is a state of the pronoun in exposing due to the overlap, and the meaning of frightened is repellent. It is said to flee and to be frightened, like to be amazed and to be amazed, and what is meant are donkeys and wild animals. The majority read mustanafarah with a kasrah on the fa’: that is, frightened. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a fathah: meaning frightened and terrified. Abu Hatim and Abu ‘Ubaid chose the second reading. It was said in Al-Kashshaf: The frightened one is intensely frightened, as if she is seeking the aversion of herself from her gathering of him and forcing her to do it.
74:51: 51- She fled from Qasoora meaning from the archers who shot at her. Qasoora is the archer, and its plural is Qasoora. This was said by Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ibn Kaysan. It was also said that it is the lion, as was said by Ata' and Al-Kalbi. Ibn Arafa said: From Qasr, meaning subjugation, because it subjugates wild beasts. It was also said that Qasoora means the voices of people. It was also said that Qasoora in the Arabic language means the lion and in the language of the Abyssinians it means the archers. Ibn Al-A'rabi said: Qasoora is the beginning of al-Layl 92:meaning she fled from the darkness of the night. Ikrimah said the same, and the first is more appropriate. Every strong person among the Arabs is Qasoora, and from this is the saying of the poet: Oh girl, be good for the sake of her maternal uncles and the cruel people. And from it is the saying of Labid: If we shout a shout in our dew, the devout and strong men will come to us And from its application to the lion, the poet said: A hidden enemy that heroes warn of, as if it were a weak lion
74:52: 52- "But every man of them desires to be given spread out pages." This is in apposition to something understood and required by the situation, as if it were said that they are not satisfied with that reminder, but rather he desires. The commentators said: The infidels of Quraysh said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: There will be at the head of every man of us a book spread out from God that you are the Messenger of God. The pages are books, the singular of which is sahifah, and the spread out is the open one. Similar to this verse is the saying of God Almighty: "Until you bring down to us a book that we can read. The majority of people read spread out" with emphasis. Saeed bin Jubair read it with emphasis. The majority also read it with a damma on the ha' of sahuf. Saeed bin Jubair read it with a sukoon.
74:53: Then God Almighty deterred them from this statement and warned them, saying: 53- No, but they do not fear the Hereafter, meaning the torment of the Hereafter, because if they feared the Fire, they would not have proposed the verses. It was said that no means truly.
74:54: Then he repeated the deterrence and warning to them, saying: 54- No, it is a reminder, meaning the Qur’an, or truly it is a reminder, and the meaning is: that he remembers by it and is admonished by its sermons.
74:55: 55- So whoever wishes to remember it will be admonished. That is, whoever wishes to be admonished by it will be admonished.
74:56: Then He, glory be to Him, returned the will to Himself, saying: 56- And they do not remember except that God wills. The majority of scholars read they remember with the lower ya’. Nafi’ and Ya’qub read it with the upper ya’, and they agreed on the alleviation. His statement, except that God wills, is an exception devoid of the most general conditions. Muqatil said: Except that God wills for them guidance. He is the One worthy of piety, meaning He is the One worthy of being feared by the righteous by abandoning His sins and performing acts of obedience to Him. And the One worthy of forgiveness, meaning He is the One worthy of forgiving the believers for their neglected sins, and He is the One worthy of accepting the repentance of the repentant sinners, thus forgiving their sins. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Every soul will be held in pledge for what it has earned, that he said: Taken by its deeds. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, regarding the statement of God, Except the companions of the right hand, that he said: They are the Muslims. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Faryabi, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Except the companions of the right hand, that he said: They are the children of the Muslims. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Until the certainty comes to us, that he said: Death. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, regarding the statement of God, Fleeed from a lion, that he said: They are the archers, the men who shoot bows. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: The lion is the men who shoot arrows. Sa`id ibn Mansur, `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Jamrah who said: I said to Ibn `Abbas: Qasura is a lion. He said: “I do not know of it in the language of any Arab. `A lion refers to a group of men.” Sufyan ibn `Ayninah, `Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: From qasura means the sound of people, meaning their voices. Ahmad, al-Darimi, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya`la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn `Adi who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited this verse: He is worthy of piety and forgiveness, and said: “Your Lord says: I am worthy of being feared, so let him not associate with Me. But whoever fears Me and does not associate with Me, then I am worthy of being forgiven.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Ibn `Umar and Ibn `Abbas.
75:1: It is forty verses It is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Dala'il narrated, through various chains of transmission, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Qiyamah was revealed, and in another version, Surat I swear by Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr, who said: Surat I swear by Mecca was revealed. His statement: 1- I swear by the Day of Resurrection. Abu Ubaidah and a group of commentators said: La is redundant, and the meaning is: I swear. Al-Samarqandi said: The commentators agreed that the meaning of “La Aqsam is I swear. They differed in the interpretation of La. Some of them said: “It is redundant, and its redundancy is common in the speech of the Arabs, as in His statement: “What prevented you from prostrating?” meaning from prostrating, and lest the People of the Book know. From this is the saying of the poet: I remembered Laila, and I was overcome with passion, and my heart almost couldn't break. Some of them said: It is a response to their words when they denied the resurrection, as if he said: The matter is not as you mentioned. I swear by the Day of Resurrection. This is the opinion of Al-Farra’ and many grammarians, like God saying: No, by God. So there is no response to a statement that preceded it. An example of this is the poet’s saying: No, by your father, O daughter of Al-Amiri, the people will not claim that I am fleeing. It was said that it is for negation, but not for negating the oaths, rather for negating what it indicates of the greatness and magnificence of the thing sworn by. It is as if the meaning of I do not swear by such-and-such is: I do not magnify it by my oath by it with the greatness it deserves, for it is worthy of more than that. It was said that it is for negating the oaths because the matter is clear. We have already discussed this in the interpretation of His statement, So I do not swear by the positions of the stars. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kathir, in a narration from him, and Al-Zuhri and Ibn Hurmuz, read to swear without an alif, on the basis that the lam is the lam of initiation. The first statement is the most correct of these statements, and Al-Razi objected to it with what does not detract from its strength nor weaken its strength. God’s swearing by the Day of Resurrection is for magnifying and glorifying it, and God may swear by whatever He wishes of His creation.
75:2: 2- And I swear by the self-reproaching soul. Some people said that God swore by the self-reproaching soul just as He swore by the Day of Resurrection, so the speech in this la is like the speech in the first, and this is the opinion of the majority. Al-Hasan said: He swore by the Day of Resurrection and did not swear by the self-reproaching soul. Al-Tha'labi said: The correct view is that He swore by both of them, and the meaning of the self-reproaching soul is the soul that blames its owner for his shortcomings, or blames all souls for their shortcomings. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is the soul of the believer. The believer is never seen except blaming himself for what he intended by such-and-such, or what he intended by such-and-such. The wicked person does not reproach himself. Mujahid said: It is the one who blames what he has missed and regrets, so he blames himself for the evil he did not do? And for the good, why did he not do more of it? Al-Farra' said: There is no soul, righteous or wicked, except that it blames itself. If it has done good, it says: Why had I not done more? And if it has done evil, it says: I wish I had not done it. Therefore, the speech is not in the context of praising oneself, so swearing by it is good and permissible. It was said that the blaming one is the blameworthy one, so it is a quality of blame. This is what those who denied that it is an oath used as evidence, since the soul of the sinner has no danger to swear by. Muqatil said: It is the soul of the disbeliever blaming himself and regretting in the Hereafter what he neglected in his duty to God, but the first is more appropriate.
75:3: 3- Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? What is meant by man is the human species, and it was said that he is the disbelieving human, and the hamza is for denial, and that is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its subject is a deleted pronoun of the proper place, and the meaning is: Does man think that the proper place is that We will not assemble his bones after they have become dust, then create them anew? That is a false assumption, for We will assemble them, and what this statement indicates is the answer to the oath. Al-Zajjaj said: I swear by the Day of Resurrection and by the self-reproaching soul that He will assemble the bones for the resurrection, so this is the answer to the oath. Al-Nahhas said: The answer to the oath is deleted: that is, that He will resurrect, and the meaning is that God the Almighty will resurrect all parts of the human being, and He only specified the bones because they are the mold of creation.
75:4: 4- Yes, We are able to put together his fingers. Yes is an affirmation of what comes after the negation to which the question is drawn. Pausing on this wording is a good pause, then beginning the speech with the words able and the accusative of able as a state: that is, yes, We gather them together, able. The state is from the pronoun of the understood verb. It was said that the meaning is: yes, We gather them, able, able. Al-Farra' said: that is, We are able, and we are strengthened, able to do more than that. He also said: It is appropriate to put it in the accusative case as a repetition: that is, yes, it is sufficient for us to be able. It was said that the meaning is: yes, we were able. Ibn Abi Ubla and Ibn Al-Samee' read yes, We are able as a subject: that is, yes, We are able. The meaning of to put together his fingers is that we put some of them together, and return them as they were, how delicate and small they are. So how about the larger organs? So the Almighty drew attention with the fingers. And the fingers are in relation to the rest of the limbs, and the ability to resurrect them and return them as they were is more deserving of ability than returning the small, delicate fingers that contain joints, nails, delicate veins, and small bones. This is the reason for mentioning them specifically, and this is what Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Qutaybah said. The majority of commentators said: The meaning of the verse is that we made the fingers of his hands and feet one thing, like the camel’s hoof and the donkey’s hoof, a single sheet with no cracks in it, so he is not able to benefit from them in delicate works such as writing, sewing, and the like, but we separated his fingers so that he may benefit from them. And it was said that the meaning is: Rather, we are able to return man to the form of animals, so how about in the image he was in? The first is more deserving, and from this is the saying of Antarah: Death is at my disposal if I touch my fingers with my hands. Then he pointed out to the rest of the members.
75:5: 5- Rather, man wants to commit sins before him is an apostrophe for does he think? Either as a question like it, and he shifted from the rebuke with that to the rebuke with this, or as an affirmation that moved to it from the question. The meaning is: Rather, man wants to commit his sins before the times that lie ahead, and before the time that lies ahead, so he commits the sin and delays repentance. Ibn al-Anbari said: He wants to commit sins as long as he lives, and he has no intention of going back on the sin he is committing. Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He says, I will repent, but he does not repent until death comes to him, and he is in the worst of states. Ad-Dahhak said: It is hope, he says, I will live and be satisfied with this world, but he does not remember death. The root of immorality is deviation from the truth, so it is true for anyone who deviates from the truth in word or deed. From this is the saying of the poet: I swear to God Abu Hafs Omar It was not touched by any hole or trace Forgive him, O God, if he did so at dawn.
75:6: And sentence 6 - He asks, 'When is the Day of Resurrection?' is a resumption to explain the meaning of explodes. The meaning is: He asks, When is the Day of Resurrection? This is a question of exclusion and mockery.
75:7: 7- If the sight is dazzled meaning he is startled and bewildered by the lightning of a man: if he looks at lightning and his sight is dazzled. The majority read barq with a kasra on the ra'. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala', al-Zajjaj and others said: The meaning is he is bewildered and does not blink. From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: If Luqman the Wise had appeared before my eyes as a traveler, they would have flashed. Al-Khalil and Al-Farra’ said: Baraq in the broken form means to be frightened, astonished and confused. The Arabs say about a stunned person: He has been struck by lightning, so he is [Baraq]. Al-Farra’ recited: Be patient with yourself and do not neglect me. Heal the wounds and do not be stricken. That is, do not be alarmed by the many wounds you have. Nafi’ and Aban on the authority of Asim read barq with a fatha on the ra’, meaning his sight flashed from the intensity of his staring into death. Mujahid and others said: This is at the time of death. It was also said that barq yabraq means slitting his eyes and opening them. Abu Ubaidah said: Fatha and kasra on the ra’ are two meanings.
75:8: 8- And the moon was eclipsed The majority read it as khasaf with a fatha on the kha and seen, in the active form. Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa, Al-A'raj, Ibn Abi Ubla, and Abu Haywah read it with a damma on the kha and a kasra on the seen, in the passive form. The meaning of khasaf al-qamar is that its light is gone and will not return as it does when it is eclipsed in this world. It is also said khasaf if all of its light is gone, and kasaf if some of its light is gone.
75:9: 9- And He gathered the sun and the moon meaning their light was both lost. He did not say gathered because the feminine is metaphorical. This was said by Al-Mubarrad. Abu Ubaidah said: It is to give precedence to the masculine over the feminine. Al-Kisa'i said: It is carried to mean the gathering of fires. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra' said: He did not say gathered because the meaning is between them in the loss of their light. It was said that He gathered them in their rising from the west, black, rounded, and dark. Ata' said: He gathered them on the Day of Resurrection, then they are thrown into the sea and they become the Great Fire of God. It was said that the sun and moon will be gathered, so there will be no alternation of night and day. Ibn Mas'ud read: He gathered the sun and moon.
75:10: 10- On that Day man will say, ‘Where is the escape?’ That is, when these things happen, he will say, Where is the escape? meaning, fleeing. Fleeing is a noun meaning escaping. Al-Farra’ said: It may be the place of escaping, and from this is the saying of the poet: Where is the escape while the rams butt heads, and every ram that flees from them will be disgraced? Al-Mawardi said: It has two possible meanings: One of them is: Where is the escape from God, the Most High, out of shyness before Him? And the second is: Where is the escape from Hell, out of caution from it? The majority read Ayna al-Mafar with a fatha on the meem and the fa’ as a verbal noun, as mentioned above. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatadah read it with a fatha on the meem and a kasra on the fa’ as a place name, meaning where is the place of escape? Al-Kisa’i said: They are two dialects, like Madab and Madab, Musah and Musah. Al-Zuhri read it with a kasra on the meem and a fatha on the fa’, meaning a person who is good at fleeing. From this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: A cunning, a fleeing, a retreating, all together, like a boulder that a torrent has thrown down from above. Any good job.
75:11: 11- No, no burden meaning no mountain, no fortress, no refuge from God. Ibn Jubayr said: No escape and no protection. In the language, burden is what a person takes refuge in, such as a fortress, mountain, or other. From this, Tarafa said: Bakr learned that we are different in opinion and in the mind is a burden Another said: By my life, a young man will not be burdened with death or humiliation. Al-Suddi said: When they were frightened in this world, they would take refuge in the mountains. God said to them: No burden will protect you from Me on that Day. And no is for deterrence, or to negate what came before it, or in the sense of truly.
75:12: 12- To your Lord, that Day, is the final destination. That is, the reference, the end, and the destination, not to anyone else. It was also said that judgment among the servants is to Him, not to anyone else. It was also said that the final destination is stability where God establishes it.
75:13: 13- On that Day, man will be informed of what he sent forth and what he left behind. That is, he will be informed on the Day of Resurrection of what good and evil he did. Qatada said: About what he did of obedience, and what he delayed of obedience and did not perform. Zayd ibn Aslam said: About what he sent forth of his wealth and what he left behind for his heirs. Mujahid said: About the beginning and end of his deeds. Ad-Dahhak said: About what he sent forth of obligatory duties and what he left behind. Al-Qushayri said: This information will be given on the Day of Resurrection when deeds are weighed, and it may also be at the time of death. Al-Qurtubi said: The former is more evident.
75:14: 14- Rather, man is a witness against himself. The word insight is used to describe man, and against himself is related to insight. Al-Akhfash said: He made him the witness, just as you say to a man: You are an argument against yourself. It was also said that the meaning is: His limbs will testify against him regarding what he did, as in His statement: On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them as to what they used to do. Al-Farra’ recited: As if the wise man had an eye that saw his seat or a view that he was watching The meaning is: Rather, man's limbs bear witness against him. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Qutaybi said: This ha' in basira is what the grammarians call the ha' of exaggeration, as in their saying: `alamah. It was also said that what is meant by basira are the two scribes who write down what is good and bad from him, and the ta' in this case is for the feminine. Al-Hasan said: That is, one who is aware of his own faults.
75:15: 15- And if he presents his excuses meaning if he apologizes and argues for himself, it will not benefit him. It is said excuse and excuses. Al-Farra' said: meaning if he apologizes, then there is someone against him who will deny his excuse. Al-Zajjaj said: The excuses are the curtains, and the singular is mu'dhar: meaning if he lowers the curtain wanting to hide himself, then his forgetting is a witness against him. This is what Al-Dahhak and Al-Suddi said: And the curtain in the language of Yemen is called mu'dhar, and the curtain in the language of Yemen is called mu'dhar, this is what Al-Mubarrad said, and from it is the saying of the poet: But she was stingy with us for an hour and made excuses for herself that day. The first is more appropriate, and this is what Mujahid, Qatadah, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Zayd, Abu al-`Aliyah, and Muqatil said. Similar to this is His statement: On the Day when the wrongdoers’ excuses will not benefit them, and His statement: And they will not be given permission to make excuses, and the poet’s statement: It is not good for a person to excuse himself when no one else can excuse him.
75:16: 16- "Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would move his lips and tongue when reciting the Qur'an before Gabriel finished reciting the revelation, out of concern that he would memorize it, may God bless him and grant him peace. So this verse was revealed: That is, do not move your tongue with the Qur'an when the revelation is being given to him, to hasten it for fear that it will slip away from you. Similar to this is His statement: "And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you" verse.
75:17: 17- Indeed, it is for Us to collect it in your chest so that nothing of it is lost to you and its recitation meaning to confirm its recitation on your tongue. Al-Farra’ said: Recitation and Quran are two sources. Qatada said: Then follow its Quran: meaning its laws and rulings.
75:18: 18- So when We have recited it meaning We have completed its recitation to you through the tongue of Gabriel then follow its recitation meaning its recitation.
75:19: 19- Then it is for Us to make it clear meaning to explain what is permissible and what is forbidden in it and to clarify what is unclear in it. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that it is for Us to send it down to you as an Arabic Qur’an that contains clarification for the people. It was also said that the meaning is: It is for Us to make it clear in your language.
75:20: 20- No! Rather, you love the immediate. "No!" is to deter from haste and encourage patience. It was also said that it is to deter those who do not believe in the Quran and consider it clear from the disbelievers. Ata' said: meaning, Abu Jahl does not believe in the Quran and its explanation. The people of Medina and the Kufians read it as "but you love.
75:21: 21- Wa tadharoon with the superlative in both verbs. The rest read them with the subjunctive in both. According to the first reading, the address is to them as a rebuke and a rebuke. According to the second reading, the address is directed back to the human being because it means people. The meaning is: You love this world and abandon the afterlife and do not work for it.
75:22: 22- Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, meaning soft, fresh, and beautiful. It is said: a radiant tree or a radiant meadow, meaning beautiful and soft. The freshness of life is its beauty and joy. Al-Wahidi and the commentators said: They say luminous, bright, and shining.
75:23: 23- Looking at her Lord This comes from looking: meaning looking at her Creator and Master of her affairs. Looking: meaning looking at Him, this is what the majority of scholars said, and what is meant by it is what is transmitted in many authentic hadiths that the servants will look at their Lord on the Day of Resurrection as they look at the moon on the night of the full moon. Ibn Kathir said: This, praise be to God, is agreed upon by the Companions, the Followers, and the righteous predecessors of this nation, as it is agreed upon by the Imams of Islam and the guides of mankind. Mujahid said: Looking here means awaiting the reward they will have from God, and something similar was narrated from Ikrimah. It was said that this is only authentic from Mujahid alone. And the statement of the speaker: I looked at so-and-so is nothing but seeing with the eye. When they mean waiting, they say: I looked at him, as in the saying of the poet: If you give me an hour of time, it will benefit me with Umm Jundub. If they want to see the eye, they say: I looked at him, as the poet said: I looked at her and the stars were like monks' lamps [Tshb Lfa'al] And the other said: I look at you as a poor man looks at a rich man. That is, I look at you with a look of humiliation, as a poor person looks at a rich person. There are many Arabic poems and words about this. Faces is the subject, and it is permissible to begin with it even though it is an indefinite noun because the situation is one of detail, and fresh is an adjective for Faces, and Yawmi-Dhinna is an adverbial phrase for fresh. If the situation were not one of detail, then describing the indefinite noun with fresh would have been a justification for beginning with it. However, the situation of detail on its own justifies beginning with an indefinite noun.
75:24: 24- And faces that Day will be gloomy, meaning gloomy, scowling, and gloomy. It is stated in As-Sahah: A man’s face will be gloomy, meaning dark. As-Suddi said: Gloomy means changed, and it was also said: Yellow, and what is meant by faces here are the faces of the disbelievers.
75:25: 25- You think that he will do something to her Faqra: a great disaster. It is said that Faqra broke him: meaning he broke the vertebrae of his back. Qatada said: Faqra is evil. Al-Suddi said: destruction. Ibn Zayd said: entering the fire. The origin of Faqra is the tattooing on the camel's nose with iron or fire until it reaches the bone. This is what Al-Asma'i said. From this is their saying: He did something to him Faqra. Al-Nabigha said: Father, I have a grave that is still in front of me, and an axe blow is above my head, and it is a shard. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement, I swear by the Day of Resurrection, He said: Your Lord swears by whomever He wills of His creation. I said: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul, He said: The self-reproaching soul. I said: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? Yes, We are able to proportion his fingertips, He said: If We had willed, We could have made him hoofed or hoofed. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: The self-reproaching soul, He said: The blameworthy one. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mundhir also narrated on his authority: He said: The one who blames for good and evil, saying: If only I had done such and such. Ibn Mundhir also narrated on his authority: He said: Regrets what has passed and blames himself for it. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority: Rather, man desires to commit sin ahead of him, He said: To move forward. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding the verse: He is the disbeliever who denies the reckoning. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: It means hope, he says: Work and then I will repent. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in Dhamm Al-Amal and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab also narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: He brings forward the sin and delays repentance. Al-Faryabi, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab also narrated from him: Rather, man wants to commit sin before him, he says: I will repent. He asks, ‘When is the Day of Resurrection?’ He said: He says, When is the Day of Resurrection? He said: So he explained to him, When the sight is dazzled. Ibn Jarir narrated from him, he said: When the sight is dazzled, meaning death. Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Mas’ud regarding his statement, No burden, he said: No fortress. Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of narration from Ibn Abbas, he said: No burden, he said: No fortress or refuge. In another version: No protection, and in another version: No mountain. Abdur-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Mas`ud, regarding the statement of God, {Man will be informed that Day of what he sent forth and what he left behind}, that is, what he sent forth of deeds and what he left behind of a tradition that those who came after him followed, whether good or evil. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas, that he said, what he sent forth of disobedience and what he left behind of obedience, so he will be informed of that. Abdur-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated through various chains of narration from him, regarding the statement of God, {Nay, man is a witness against himself}, that he testifies against himself alone, {even if he were to present his excuses}, that he said, even if he were to make an excuse. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, {Nay, man is a witness against himself}, that he said, his hearing, sight, hands, feet and limbs, {even if he were to present his excuses}, that he said, even if he were to strip off his clothes. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was struggling with the revelation, moving his tongue and lips for fear that it might slip away from him, wanting to memorize it. Then God revealed: “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.” He said: It means that it is upon Us to collect it in your chest and then you recite it. So when We have recited it means: when We have revealed it to you. Then it is upon Us to make it clear so listen to it and be silent. Then it is upon Us to make it clear that is, to make it clear with your tongue. In another version: It is upon Us to recite it. After that, whenever Gabriel came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he would lower his head. In another version: Listen. Then when he had gone, he would recite it as God had promised him. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, So when We have recited it, meaning, We have made it clear, “then follow its recitation,” meaning, act according to it. Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated in Zawa’id az-Zuhd on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding his statement, No! Rather, you love the immediate, he said, The world, its evil and its good, has been hastened for them, and the Hereafter has been hidden. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, he said, Soft. Ibn Mundhir, al-Ajurri in al-Shari’ah, al-Lalaka’i in al-Sunnah, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ru’yah narrated on his authority, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, he said, He means their beauty, “Looking at their Lord,” he said, Looking at the Creator. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority, Looking at their Lord, he said, Looking at the face of their Lord. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Some faces on that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord. He said: They will look at their Lord without any manner, limit, or known description. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: “The people said: O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Do you find difficulty in seeing the sun when there are no clouds? They said: No, O Messenger of God.
