He said: Do you find difficulty in seeing the moon when it is full when there are no clouds? They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: You will see Him on the Day of Resurrection like that.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated a similar hadith from Abu Hurairah. We have already mentioned that the hadiths about seeing God are mutawatir, so we will not elaborate on them. They will be discussed in a separate book. Those who denied and ruled them out did not rely on anything suitable to adhere to, neither from the Book of God nor from the Sunnah of His Messenger. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Daraqutni, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The lowest in status of the people of Paradise will be he who looks at his gardens, wives, blessings, servants, and couches for a distance of a thousand years. The most honored of them in the sight of God will be he who looks at His face morning and evening.” Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. Ahmad narrated in al-Musnad from his hadith with the wording: The best of them in status will be he who looks at the face of God twice each day. Al-Nasa'i, Al-Daraqutni - who authenticated it - and Abu Nu'aym narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “We said, ‘O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord?’ He said, ‘Do you see the sun on a cloudless day and the moon on a cloudless night?’ We said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘You will see your Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, to the point that one of you will address his Lord, and He will say, ‘My servant, do you recognize such and such a sin?’ He will say, ‘Have You not forgiven me?’ He will say, ‘It is by My forgiveness that I have become this.’”
75:26: His statement: 26- No! is a deterrent and a warning: meaning, it is far-fetched for the disbeliever to believe in the Day of Resurrection. Then he resumed, saying: When it reaches the collarbones, meaning, the soul or spirit reaches the collarbones, which is the plural of collarbone, and it is a bone between the opening of the throat and the shoulder. The soul reaching the collarbone is a metaphor for healing from death. Similar to it is his statement: Why then, when it reaches the throat? It was said that the meaning of No, truly is: truly, that the one being led to God when it reaches the collarbones, and the intention is to remind them of the severity of the situation when death descends. Duraid bin Al-Summa said: And many a calamity I defended against, even though their souls reached their collarbones.
75:27: 27- And it was said, 'Who can perform incantations?' That is, who was present when the person who had the incantation saw it came to him and who would heal him with his incantation? Qatada said: They sought doctors for him, but they could not help him at all against God's decree. Abu Qilabah said the same, and from this is the saying of the poet: Does a boy have protection from the daughters of death, or does he have a ruqyah to protect him from the baths of death? Abu al-Juza' said: It is from the root raqa, which means to ascend. The meaning is: Who will ascend with his soul to heaven, the angels of mercy or the angels of torment? It was also said that the Angel of Death says this, because the soul of the unbeliever hates the angels being near it.
75:28: 28- And he thought it was the separation meaning the one whose soul had reached the level of advancement was certain that it was the separation from the world, from family, money, and children.
75:29: 29- And the leg was entwined with the leg meaning his leg was entwined with his leg when death descended upon him. The majority of commentators said: The meaning is that hardships befell him one after the other. Al-Hasan said: They are his two legs when they are entwined in the shroud. Zayd ibn Aslam said: The leg of the shroud was entwined with the leg of the dead person. It was also said that his legs died and his shins dried up and could not carry him, although he had been traveling on them. Ad-Dahhak said: Two severe matters came together for him: the people were preparing his body, and the angels were preparing his soul. Ibn Zayd said the same. The Arabs only mention the leg in times of great hardship and great tribulations, and from this their saying: The war rose up against the leg. It was also said that the first leg is the torture of his soul when his soul departs, and the other leg is the severity of the resurrection and what comes after it.
75:30: 30- To your Lord, that Day, is the return. That is, to your Creator on the Day of Resurrection, the return. This is the gathering of the servants to God, to Him they will be driven.
75:31: 31- He neither believed nor prayed meaning he did not believe in the message nor in the Quran, nor did he pray to his Lord. The pronoun refers to the human being mentioned at the beginning of this Surah. Qatada said: He neither believed in the Book of God nor did he pray to God. It was also said: He neither believed in his heart nor acted with his body. Al-Kisa'i said: La means lam, and Al-Akhfash said the same: The Arabs say: La dhahab meaning he did not go, and this is widespread in the speech of the Arabs, and from it: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a lot, and which servant of yours is there but pain?
75:32: 32- But he denied and turned away meaning he denied the Messenger and what he brought, and turned away from obedience and faith.
75:33: 33- Then he went to his family, swaggering. That is, he strutted and strutted in his walk, proud of that. It is said that it is derived from the word mati, which means the back, and the meaning is that he twists his mount. It is also said that its root is yatamattat, which means stretching out and being heavy: that is, he is heavy and lazy about calling people to the truth.
75:34: 34- It is better for you, then better.
75:35: 35- It is better for you, then better * then better for you, then better meaning woe is yours. Its original form is May God give you what you hate. The lam is an extra letter as in Hereafter for you. This is a severe threat, and the repetition is for emphasis: meaning, it will be repeated to you time after time. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took Abu Jahl by the hand, then said: It is better for you, then better. Abu Jahl said: With what do you threaten me that neither you nor your Lord can do anything to me, and I am the most honored of the people of this valley. So this verse was revealed. It was said that its meaning is: Woe to you, and from this is the saying of Al-Khansa: I had some worries for myself, so what is best for myself is best for her And on the saying that it is woe, it was said that it is from the inverted form, as if it was said: Woe to you, then the weak letter was delayed. And it was said that the meaning of repeating this word four times is, woe to you while alive, woe to you while dead, woe to you on the Day of Resurrection, and woe to you on the day you enter the Fire. And it was said that the meaning is: Blame is more appropriate for you than abandoning it. And it was said that the meaning is: You are more appropriate and deserving of this punishment, said Tha’lab. And Al-Asma’i said: The meaning of awla in the speech of the Arabs is approaching destruction. Al-Mubarrad said: It is as if he is saying: I have approached destruction and I have approached it, and its origin is from wali, which means closeness. And Al-Farra’ recited: It is more appropriate for you to be loyal Any boat that you have, and he also recited: It is better for someone who is upset to be sad
75:36: 36- Does man think that he will be left neglected? That is, neglected, not commanded, not forbidden, not held accountable, and not punished. Al-Suddi said: It means neglected, and from this comes the word sada camels grazing without a shepherd. It was also said that the meaning is: Does man think that he will be left in his grave like this forever, not resurrected?
75:37: And the sentence 37- Was he not a drop of ejaculated semen? is a new sentence: that is, was that human being not a drop of semen that is emitted into the womb? Semen is called semen because of its appearance, and a drop is a small amount of water. It is said that water drips. The majority of scholars read was he not with a lower vowel indicating that the pronoun refers to the human being. Al-Hasan read it with a higher vowel indicating that the pronoun refers to the sperm. Hafs, Ibn Muhaysin, Mujahid, and Ya'qub read it with a lower vowel indicating that the pronoun refers to the sperm. This reading was narrated from Abu Amr, and Abu Hatim chose it.
75:38: 38- Then he was a clot meaning after the sperm there was a clot: meaning blood Then He created meaning He determined by making it a formed lump Then He proportioned meaning He adjusted him and completed his development and breathed the spirit into him.
75:39: 39- And He made from it meaning it came from the human being, and it was said from the semen the two mates meaning the two types of the human species. Then He explained that by saying: the male and the female meaning the man and the woman.
75:40: 40- Is not that meaning is not the One who created this wondrous creation and determined it able to give life to the dead meaning that He restores bodies by resurrection as they were in this world, for bringing back is easier and less burdensome than starting over. The majority read able and Zayd ibn Ali read is able as a present tense verb. The majority read gives life by making it accusative with an. Talhah ibn Sulayman and al-Fayyad ibn Ghazwan read it with a sukoon for ease, or to make the connection similar to the pause as mentioned previously. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And it will be said, ‘Who will ascend?’ He said: His soul will be snatched away until it is in his collarbones. It will be said, ‘Who will ascend with his soul? The angels of mercy or the angels of torment. And the leg will be entwined with the leg. He said: The world, the Hereafter and the angels of torment will be entwined around him, as to which of them will ascend with him.’ Abd bin Hamid narrated on his authority, And it will be said, ‘Who will ascend?’ Say, Who will ascend? Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, And the leg will be entwined with the leg. He said: The last day of the days of the world and the first day of the days of the Hereafter, so hardship will be met with hardship, except for whom God has mercy. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, Stretching himself. He said: He strutted. Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about the statement: It is more fitting for you, then more fitting. Was it something that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Abu Jahl of his own accord, or was it something that God commanded him to do? He said: Yes, he said it of his own accord, then God revealed it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: To be left in vain. He said: Negligently. 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Anbari narrated on the authority of Salih Abu al-Khalil who said: "When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this verse: 'Is He not able to give life to the dead?' He would say: 'Glory be to You, O God, and indeed.'" Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib who said: When this verse was revealed: Is He not able to give life to the dead? the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Glory be to You, my Lord, and indeed. Ibn al-Najjar narrated in his history, “On the authority of Abu Umamah that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say when he recited this verse: ‘Yes, and I am of the witnesses to that.’” Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever among you recites ‘By the Fig and the Olive’ and reaches the end of it, ‘Is not God the best of judges?’ let him say, ‘Yes, and I am of the witnesses to that.’ And whoever recites, ‘I swear by the Day of Resurrection’ and reaches the words, ‘Is He not able to give life to the dead?’ let him say, ‘Yes.’ And whoever recites, ‘By the angels sent forth in succession’ and reaches, ‘Then in what statement after it will they believe?’ let him say, ‘We believe in God.’” And in its chain of transmission is an unknown man. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you recite ‘I swear by the Day of Resurrection’ and you reach ‘Is He not able to bring the dead to life?’ then he said: ‘Yes.’”
76:1: It is thirty-one verses The majority said: It is Medinan. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: It is Meccan. An-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. It was said that it is Meccan from the verse: Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur’an gradually until the end of the surah, and what precedes it is Medinan. Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: “An Abyssinian man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: ‘Ask and inquire.’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, you have been given preference over us in colors, images, and prophethood. Do you think that if I believe in what I believe in and do what I do, will I be with you in Paradise?’ He said: ‘Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the whiteness of the blacks in Paradise can be seen from a distance of a thousand years.’ Then he said: ‘Whoever says: There is no god but God, will have a covenant with God. And whoever says: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, one hundred thousand good deeds and twenty-four thousand good deeds will be written for him.’ This Surah was revealed: ‘Has there not been over man a period of time? ’ until the verse: ‘a great kingdom.’ The Abyssinian said: ‘My eyes see what your eyes see in Paradise.’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He complained until his soul left. Ibn Umar said: ‘I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) lowering him into his grave with his hand.’” Ahmad narrated in Az-Zuhd on the authority of Muhammad ibn Mutraf who said: A trustworthy man told me that a black man used to ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about glorifying and declaring God’s oneness. Umar ibn Al-Khattab said to him: You have spoken too much to the Messenger of God. He said: Calm down, Umar. And the verse, Has there not been over man a period of time? was revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until, when Paradise was mentioned, the black man sighed and his soul left him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: He died longing for Paradise. Ibn Wahb narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Zayd, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi - who authenticated it - Ibn Majah, Ibn Munie’, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - and Al-Dhiya’ narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited ‘Has there not been over man a period of time?’ until he finished it, then he said: ‘Indeed, I see what you do not see and hear what you do not hear. The heaven groaned, and it has the right to groan. There is not in it the space of four fingers but there is an angel placing his forehead in prostration to God. By God, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much, and you would not take pleasure in women on your beds, and you would go out to the high places, beseeching God, the Almighty and Majestic.” Al-Wahidi narrated from the commentators and the meanings of the meanings that 1- hal here means qad and not an interrogative. Sibawayh, Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra' and Abu Ubaidah said this. Al-Farra' said: hal can be a denial and it can be a predicate. This is from the predicate because you say: Did I give you? you confirm that you gave him. Denial is to say: Is anyone capable of such a thing? It was said that even though it has the meaning of qad, it has the meaning of a question. The original is ahl ata, so the meaning is: has he come? The interrogative is for confirmation and approximation. What is meant by human here is Adam. Qatada, Al-Thawri, Ikrimah, Al-Suddi and others said: A period of time. It was said that it was forty years before the soul was breathed into him. It was also said that he was created from clay for forty years, then from aged black mud for forty years, then from clay for forty years, so his creation was completed after one hundred and twenty years. It was said that the time mentioned here is not known in its duration. It was also said that what is meant by human is the children of Adam, and the time is the period of pregnancy. The phrase was not a thing worth mentioning is in the accusative case as a state of human, or in the nominative case as a description of the time. Al-Farra', Qatrib and Tha'lab said: The meaning is that he was a body formed of dust and clay that is not mentioned, is not known, and its name or what is meant by it is not known. Then the spirit was breathed into him and he became mentioned. Yahya ibn Salam said: He was not a thing worth mentioning among creation, even though he is something worth mentioning with God. It was also said that what is meant by mention here is not informing, because the Lord's informing about beings is eternal. Rather, mention is in the sense of danger and honor, as in His statement: And indeed, it is a mention for you and your people. Al-Qushayri said: It was not mentioned to creation, even though it was mentioned to God, the Exalted. Al-Farra' said: He was a thing but was not mentioned. So the negation was directed to the restriction. It was also said that the meaning is: Times have passed and Adam was not a thing, nor a creation, nor mentioned to any of creation. Muqatil said: There is an inversion in the speech, and its interpretation is: Has there come a time when he was not a thing worth mentioning, because he created him after creating all animals, and no animal was created after him.
76:2: 2- Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop. What is meant by man here is the son of Adam. Al-Qurtubi said: Without dispute. And the sperm-drop is the water that drips, which is semen. And any small amount of water in a vessel is a sperm-drop, and its plural is sperm. Mixed mixtures is an adjective for sperm-drop, which is the plural of mixed or mixed, and it means the mixtures, and what is meant is the sperm-drop of the man and the sperm-drop of the woman and their mixing. It is said that this is mixed with this, so it is mixed: meaning that this is mixed with this, so it is mixed. Al-Mubarrad said: Mixed means mixed, and here it is the mixing of sperm-drop with blood. Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj said: They throw out every hasty mixture that has not covered its skin with the blood of mixtures. Al-Farra’ said: Amshaj is the mixing of the man’s semen, the woman’s semen, blood, and the leech. It is said that this is mashj if it is mixed. It is also said that amshaj is the redness in the whiteness and the whiteness in the redness. Al-Qurtubi said: This is a saying preferred by many linguists. Al-Hudhali said: As if the feathers and the hilt of the blade were tied to it, mixed together. This is because the man's semen is thick and white, while the woman's semen is yellow and thin, so a child is created from them. Ibn al-Sikkit said: mixtures are the humours because they are mixed from different types and natures from which a human being is created. It was said that mixtures is a singular word like barmah a'shaar, and this is supported by its occurrence as an adjective for sperm. The phraseبتاله We test him is in the accusative case as a hal state of the subject ofَقَقَقباباWe created him, meaning intending to test him. It is also permissible for it to be a hal state of the human being, and the meaning is: We test him with good and evil and with obligations. Al-Farra' said: Its meaning, and God knows best, is We made him hearing and seeing Nabatlih. It is an introduction meaning a delay, because the test does not occur until after the completion of creation. According to this, this state is estimated, and it was said that it is concomitant. It was said that the meaning ofتتِلtest is to transfer him from one state to another in a metaphorical manner, but the former is more appropriate.
76:3: Then God the Almighty mentioned that He gave him what would make the trial valid, so He said: 3- Indeed, We showed him the way, be he grateful or ungrateful. That is, We showed him and made known to him the path of guidance and misguidance, good and evil, as in His statement: And We showed him the two ways. Mujahid said: That is, We made known the path to misery and happiness. Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Abu Salih said: The way here is its emergence from the womb, and it was said that it is its benefits and harms that he is guided to by his nature and perfect mind. The accusative of grateful and ungrateful is in the state of the object of We guided him: that is, We enabled him to follow the path in both of his states. It was said that it is in the state of path as a metaphor: that is, We made known to him the path, either the path of gratitude or the path of ungratefulness. Makki narrated from the Kufians that his statement either is a conditional if after which ma was added: that is, We made known to him the path whether he is grateful or ungrateful. Al-Farra' chose this option, but the Basrans do not permit it because the conditional in does not enter into nouns unless a verb is implied after it, and the implied verb is not valid here because it would have been necessary to raise Shakeran and Kafur ungrateful. A verb can be implied that makes Shakeran and Kafur in the accusative case, and its meaning is: If We created him grateful, then grateful, and if We created him ungrateful, then ungrateful. This is according to the reading of the majority, Either grateful or ungrateful with a kasra on the hamza of either. Abu al-Sammak and Abu al-Ajaj read it with a fatha, and with a fatha it is either a conjunction in the language of some Arabs, or it is a detail and its answer is understood. It was said that Shakeran and Kafur are in the accusative case by implying kan, and the meaning is: whether he is grateful or ungrateful.
76:4: Then the Almighty explained what He has prepared for the disbelievers, saying: 4- Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains, shackles, and a Blaze. Nafi’, Al-Kisa’i, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Hisham from Ibn Umar read salasil with the tanween. Qanbal from Ibn Kathir and Hamzah stopped without an alif, and the rest stopped with an alif. The reason for those who read salasil with the tanween, even though it has the plural plural form, is that they intended to establish proportionality because what precedes it, either thankful or ungrateful, and what follows it, shackles and a Blaze, is tanween, or according to the language of those who decline all indeclinables, as Al-Kisa’i and other Kufians reported from some Arabs. Al-Akhfash said: We heard some Arabs decline all indeclinables, because connecting is in indeclinable nouns and leaving the indeclinable is due to an obstacle in them. Al-Farra’ said: It is in the language of those who put all nouns in the genitive case, except for their saying: He is more charming than you, as they do not put it in the genitive case. Ibn al-Anbari recited in this regard the words of Amr ibn Kulthum: As if our swords are within us and within them, and are bludgeons in the hands of our players. This includes the poet’s saying: And when men saw Yazid, you would see them with bowed necks and lowered eyes. With the breaking of the seen from Nawaks, and the saying of Labid: And Hasour Astar, let me die with similar hangings He also said: Kindly and generously [helps] with the dew, he allowed the desires of her sheep to be mixed with it It was said that the tanween is to conform to the script of the Meccan, Medinan and Kufic copies of the Qur’an, as it is with an alif in them. It was also said that this tanween is a substitute for the letter of emphasis, and that connecting is like stopping. The chains have been explained previously, and the dispute over them is whether they are shackles or what is placed on necks, as in the poet’s saying: But chains and shackles surrounded the necks [Plural] A chain that hands are chained to their necks. The fire is the intense fuel. The interpretation of the fire has been presented above.
76:5: Then the Almighty mentioned what He has prepared for the grateful, saying: 5- Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup. Abrar: the people of obedience and sincerity, and truthfulness is the plural of barr or barr. It says in As-Sahah: The plural of barr is abrar, and the plural of barr is barrarah. So-and-so is righteous to his Creator and is righteous towards Him: that is, he obeys Him. Al-Hasan said: Righteousness is that which does not harm even the ants. Qatada said: The righteous are those who fulfill the right of God and fulfill their vows. The cup in the language is the vessel in which a drink is contained, and if there is no drink in it, it is not called a cup, and there is no reason to specify it with a bottle, rather it is made of glass, gold, silver, china, and other things. The cups of the Arabs were of different kinds, and the cup may be used to refer to wine itself, as in the saying of the poet: I drank a cup of pleasure and another I used to treat myself with it Her temperament was camphorous meaning it mixed with her and she was mixed with it. It is said that he mixed it, he mixes it, mixing it, and from this the poet said: As if the causal link from the house of Ras was its temperament of honey and water And the saying of Amr ibn Kulthum: Umm Amr turned the cup away from us, and the cup flowed to the right. Aged, as if the leaves in it become hot when water mixes with them And from it is the body’s temperament, which is the mixture that mixes it with. It was said that camphor is the name of a spring in Paradise called Kafoori. The wine of Paradise is mixed with the water of this spring. Qatadah and Mujahid said: It is mixed for them with camphor and they are sealed with musk. Ikrimah said: Its temperament is its taste. It was also said that camphor is in its smell, not its taste. It was also said that camphor is meant in its whiteness, pleasant smell, and coolness, because camphor is not drunk, as in His statement: Until He makes it fire, meaning like fire. Ibn Kaysan said: Its fragrance is musk, camphor, and ginger. Muqatil said: It is not the camphor of this world, but God called what is with Him what is with you so that hearts may be guided to it. The sentence is in the genitive case as an attribute of cup. It was said that if it is redundant here: meaning from a cup mixed with camphor.
76:6: 6- A spring from which the servants of God drink. The word ain is in the accusative case as a substitute for kafur because its water is as white as camphor. Makki said: It is in the place of min kas cup with the omission of an adjective, as if it were said: They drink wine, the wine of a spring. It is also said that it is in the accusative case as the object of they drink: that is, a spring from a cup. It is also said that it is in the accusative case as a specification, as stated by Al-Akhfash. It is also said that it is in the accusative case with an implied verb explained by what follows: that is, they drink a spring from which the servants of God drink. The first is more appropriate, and the phrase the servants of God drink from it is an attribute of ain. It is also said that the ba in yusharb bih is redundant. It is also said that it has the meaning of whom as stated by Al-Zajjaj. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Abi Ubla: yusharbhu the servants of God drink from it. It is also said that yusharb implies the meaning of yultaz enjoys, and it is also said that it is related to yusharb, and the pronoun refers to the cup. Al-Farra’ said: He drinks it and he drinks with it are the same in meaning, as if he drinks with it, quenches his thirst with it, and benefits from it. He recited the words of Al-Hudhali: They drank seawater and then rose He said: And similarly, he spoke good words, and spoke good words. They make it gush forth means they drag it to wherever they want and benefit from it as they wish and its water follows them to every place they want to reach, so they split it like a river is split and gushes here and there. Mujahid said: They lead it wherever they want and it follows them wherever they incline, it inclines with them, and the phrase is another description of the cursed one.
76:7: And the sentence 7- They fulfill their vows is a new sentence introduced to explain the reason for which they were provided what was mentioned, as well as what was conjoined to it. The meaning of vow in the language is affirmation, and the meaning is: They fulfill what God has made obligatory upon them of acts of obedience. Qatadah and Mujahid said: They fulfill the obedience to God of prayer, Hajj, and the like. Ikrimah said: They fulfill when they vow to God, the Most High. A vow in Islamic law is what a person obligates himself to do, so the meaning is: They fulfill what they have made obligatory upon themselves. Al-Farra' said: There is an implied meaning in the speech: that is, they used to fulfill their vows in this world. Al-Kalbi said: They fulfill the covenant: that is, they complete the covenant. The first is to interpret the vow here as referring to what the servant has obligated himself to do without specifying it. And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread. What is meant is the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of the spreading of its evil is its dissemination and spread. It is said that he spread, he spread, he spread, he spread, and it is a verb from the root word to fly. From this is the saying of Al-A’sha: So she became a wound in my heart, and her distance caused a wide-spread rift. The Arabs say: The crack in the bottle or the glass spread, meaning it extended. They also say: The fire spread, meaning it became widespread. Al-Farra' said: The spread means the elongated one. Qatada said: The evil of that day spread until it filled the heavens and the earth. Muqatil said: "Its evil was widespread in the heavens, so they split and the stars scattered, and the angels were terrified. And on the earth, the mountains were blown away and the waters sank."
76:8: 8- And they feed food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive. That is, they feed these three types of people food, in spite of their love for it and its scarcity. Mujahid said: In spite of its scarcity, their love for it, and their desire for it. So his statement, in spite of his love, is in the accusative case as a state: meaning, being in love with it. Similar to this is his statement, You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. It was said: In spite of the love of feeding, due to their desire for good. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: In spite of the love of feeding. It was said that the pronoun in in his love refers to God: that is, they feed food out of love for God: that is, they feed with a feeding that is out of love for God.
76:9: This is supported by His statement: 9- "We feed you only for the sake of God." The needy miserable is the one who is destitute, i.e., the poor person, or someone who is poorer than the poor person. What is meant by orphan is the orphans of the Muslims, and the captive who is taken prisoner and imprisoned. Qatadah and Mujahid said: The imprisoned captive. Ikrimah said: The captive is the slave. Abu Hamza al-Thamali said: The captive is the woman. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: This feeding abrogated the verse on charity and the verse on the sword regarding the captive non-Muslim. Another said: Rather, it is decisive. Feeding the needy and the orphan is based on awareness, and feeding the captive is for the sake of preserving his life until the ruler makes a choice regarding him. The phrase "We feed you only for the sake of God" is in the accusative case as a state of saying: that is, they say, "We feed you only, or saying, We feed you only," meaning that they complete this, but God did it from their hearts, so He praised them for that. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: They did not complete it with this, but God knew it in their hearts, so He praised them, and He knew from His praise that they did that out of fear of God and the loss of His reward. We do not want from you any reward or thanks, meaning we do not ask you to reward us for this feeding, nor do we want you to thank us, rather it is purely for the sake of God. This sentence confirms what came before it, because whoever feeds for the sake of God does not want a reward nor does he ask for thanks from the one who fed him.
76:10: 10- Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day of stern and distressful. That is, we fear the punishment of a Day characterized by these two attributes. The meaning of frowning is that it is a day on which faces will frown, whoever it is and its severity, so the meaning is that it is frowning. Al-Farra’, Abu Ubaidah, and Al-Mubarrad said: A day of stern and severe distress. Al-Farra’ recited: Our cousins, do you remember our affliction upon you when it was a day of calamities? Al-Akhfash said: The Qamatarir is the most severe of days and the longest in affliction, and from it the poet said: Flee when the dust of war rises and the gloomy, cloudy day enters it. Al-Kisa’i said: It rained today and blossomed: if it was very difficult and intense. From this comes the poet’s saying: Banu Harb, we have ordered them to be given a mount, and whoever meets us that day will flee. Mujahed said: Frowning is in the lips, and the frowning is in the forehead and eyebrows, so he made them among the characteristics of the one who is changed on that day because of the hardships he sees, and Ibn al-A’rabi recited: He can fish with a broken stick, and it rains for an hour and then dies. Abu Ubaidah said: Yaqa Qatmarir means contracted between the eyes and eyebrows. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said that the she-camel has rained: if it raises its tail, gathers its two drops of rain, and throws with its nose the preceding drops, and he made the m an additional letter.
76:11: 11- So God saved them from the evil of that Day meaning, instead of the frowning faces of the disbelievers, He gave them radiance on their faces and joy in their hearts. Ad-Dahhak said: Freshness is the whiteness and purity in their faces. Saeed bin Jubair said: Goodness and splendor. It was also said that freshness is the effect of a blessing.
76:12: 12- And He rewarded them for what they patiently endured meaning because of their patience with the obligations, and it was said with poverty, and it was said with hunger, and it was said with fasting. It is better to interpret the verse as referring to patience with everything that patience entails in obedience to God, the Most High. Ma is a source, and the interpretation is: because of their patience Paradise and silk meaning He admitted them into Paradise and clothed them in silk, which is the clothing of the people of Paradise, instead of abandoning it in this world, in compliance with what was mentioned in the Shari’ah about its prohibition. The apparent meaning of these verses is general for everyone who fears the Day of Resurrection, feeds for the sake of God, and fears His punishment. The reason, even though it is specific, as will come, is taken into consideration with the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. The reason in the revelation is included under its generality primarily. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Has there come upon man? He said: Every human being. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding the statement of God, mixed substances, he said: Their mixed substances are their veins. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, from a sperm-drop mixed substances, he said: The man’s semen and the woman’s semen when they mix. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, he said: Mixed substances are of various colors: the man’s sperm is white and red, and the woman’s sperm is green and red. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, he said: The mixed substances are what comes out after urinating, like cutting a string, and from them a child is born. Abd Al-Razzaq and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority, regarding the statement of God, and a captive, he said: He is the polytheist. Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: ‘poor’ he said: poor, ‘orphan’ he said: fatherless, ‘captive’ he said: slave and prisoner.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: ‘and they feed the poor’ he said: this verse was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib and Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: ‘a gloomy day’ he said: narrow, ‘tight’ he said: long Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, {A Day gloomy and frowning,} he said: “It will constrict what is between the eyes.” Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The one who is frowning is the one whose face is constricted. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, And he will meet them with radiance and joy, he said: Radiance will be on their faces and joy will be in their hearts.
76:13: His statement: 13- "Reclining therein on couches is in the accusative case as a hal of the object of He rewarded them, and the operator here is He rewarded, and the operator therein is they were patient", because patience was only in this world, and Abu al-Baqa' allowed it to be an attribute of Paradise. Al-Farra' said: If you wish, you can make "reclining" a subordinate clause, as if he said: He rewarded them with a Paradise reclining therein. Al-Akhfash said: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a praiseworthy one, and the pronoun "from therein refers to Paradise, and the couches are the beds in the chambers, and its explanation has been presented in Surat al-Kahf They will see therein neither sun nor freezing cold The sentence is in the accusative case as a hal of the object of He rewarded them, so it is a synonymous hal, or from the pronoun in reclining", so it is an overlapping hal, or another attribute of Paradise, and freezing cold is the most intense cold, and the meaning is: they will not see in Paradise the heat of the sun nor the cold of freezing cold, and from this is the saying of al-A'sha: A soft, sweet little girl who has never seen the sun or cold Tha’lab said: Zamharir is the moon in the language of Tayy, and he recited the following verse by their poet: And the night of its darkness has clouded its parts, and the freezing cold has not blossomed It is narrated that it did not appear: meaning the moon did not rise. The explanation of this was presented in Surah Maryam.
76:14: 14- And its shades are drawn low upon them. The majority of scholars read Daniyyah in the accusative case, in apposition to the place where they do not see, or to those reclining, or as a description of something omitted: i.e. a garden that is drawn low, as if he said: And He will reward them with a garden that is drawn low. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a description of the garden that was mentioned earlier. Al-Farra' said: It is in the accusative case for praise. Abu Haywah read Daniyyah in the nominative case as an advanced predicate and its shades as a delayed subject, and the sentence is in the accusative case as a state. The meaning is: The shades of the trees are close to them, covering them with an increase in their comfort, even if there is no sun there. Muqatil said: It means its trees are close to them. Ibn Mas'ud read And its fruits are made lowly upon them as in apposition to Daniyyah as if he said: and made lowly. It is permissible for the sentence to be in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in upon them, or it is permissible for it to be a new sentence. Al-Qatuf means the fruits. The meaning is that its fruits were made subservient to those who eat them, making them subservient in abundance, such that the standing, the sitting, and the lying down can eat them, and neither their hands nor thorns can hold them back from it. An-Nahhas said: The submissive is the one that is close to reach. And from this is their saying, a submissive wall, meaning short. Ibn Qutaybah said: I was made submissive, I brought it close, from their saying, a submissive wall, meaning it was short in thickness. And it was said, I was made submissive, meaning it was made obedient and not resistant to being picked however they wished.
76:15: 15- And they will be served with vessels of silver and cups meaning that servants will go around to them if they want to drink from vessels of silver. Cups is the plural of cup, which is a large jug that has no spout or handle. From this comes the saying of Adi: Reclining, the door is knocked on, and the servant seeks him with a cup Its interpretation was mentioned in Surat al-Zukhruf 43:They were crystals, crystals of silver. That is, in describing the crystals in terms of their purity and the whiteness of silver. Their purity is the purity of glass, and their colour is the colour of silver.
76:16: Nafi', Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr 16- read Qawarira * Qawarira with the tanween in both of them while connected, and with a pause on them with an alif. The reason for this reading was presented in the explanation of His statement: Salasil from this surah, and we explained there the reason for inflecting what has the plural plural form, so refer to it. Hamzah read without the tanween in both of them and without pausing with an alif. The reason for this reading is apparent because they are both improper for the plural plural form. Hisham read without the tanween in both of them and with a pause on them with an alif. Ibn Kathir read with the tanween of the first but not the second and with a pause on the first with an alif, Jun the second. Abu Amr, Hafs and Ibn Dhakwan read without the tanween in both of them, and with a pause on the first with an alif but not the second. The sentence is in the genitive case as an attribute of Cups. Abu Al-Baqa' said: The repetition is good because it is connected to clarifying its origin. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: God made the vessels of the people of Paradise from silver, so it combined the whiteness of silver and the purity of glass. Al-Zajjaj said: The vessels in this world are made of sand, so God made known the excellence of those vessels that their origin is silver, so that what is inside can be seen from the outside. The phrase they measured it by a measure is an attribute of the vessels. The majority read they measured it by a measure with a fat-ha on the qaf in the active form, meaning the cupbearers from the servants who go around to them measured it according to what the drinkers of the people of Paradise need, without any increase or decrease. Mujahid and others said: Their rewards are according to the amount of their quenching, without any increase or decrease. Al-Kalbi said: That is more delicious and more appetizing. It was also said: The angels measured it, and it was also said that the drinkers of Paradise measured it according to the amount of their desires and needs, so it came as they intended in form, without any increase or decrease. Ali, Ibn Abbas, As-Salami, Ash-Shaabi, Zaid bin Ali, Ubaid bin Umair, and Abu Amr, in one narration from him, read it with a damma on the qaf and a kasra on the dal, in the passive voice: i.e. I made it for them according to their will. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: It is from the chapter on the heart. He said: Because the true meaning is to say: I measured them, not they measured it, because it means they were able to do it. Abu Hatim said: The meaning is: I measured the vessels according to their watering place, so the object of the unspecified verb is omitted. Abu Hayyan said: The closest interpretation of this anomalous reading is to say: He measured their watering place from it, an estimation, so the complement was omitted, becoming qadruhu. Al-Mahdawi said: The meaning of the last reading goes back to the meaning of the first reading, and it is as if the original was qadruhu alayhi, so the preposition was omitted, as Sibawayh recited: I swear that the love of Iraq will be consumed by time and that love will be consumed by the village of Sous I swear to love Iraq.
76:17: 17- And they will be given to drink there a cup whose mixture is of ginger. It has been previously stated that a cup is a vessel containing wine, and if it is empty of wine, then it is not called a cup. The meaning is that the people of Paradise will be given to drink in Paradise a cup of wine mixed with ginger. The Arabs used to enjoy mixing drinks with ginger because of its pleasant aroma. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Ginger is the name of the spring from which those brought near to God drink. Muqatil said: It is ginger that does not resemble the ginger of this world.
76:18: 18- "A spring therein called Salsabil The word ain is in the accusative case as a substitute for cup". It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case by an implied verb: i.e. they are given to drink from a spring, and it is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case by removing the preposition: i.e. from spring. Salsabil is a delicious drink, taken from smoothness. The Arabs say: This is a smooth drink, and Salsal and Salsabil: i.e. pleasant and delicious. Al-Zajjaj said: Salsabil in the language is the name for water that is extremely smooth, with a strong flow that flows down their throats. From this is the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit: They give them a cup of pure nectar from the rose of the gecko.
76:19: 19- And there will circulate among them immortal youths When God finished describing their drink, their vessels, and the cupbearers who give them that drink. The meaning of immortal is that they will remain as they are of youth, freshness, and radiance, they will not age or change. It was said that the meaning of immortal is that they will not die. It was also said that immortality means adornment: that is, adorned. When you saw them, you would think them to be scattered pearls When you looked at them, you would think them to be scattered pearls because of their beauty, the purity of their colors, and the freshness of their faces. Ata' said: He means in the whiteness of their color and its beauty, and when pearls are scattered from a thread on a carpet, they are more beautiful than them when strung together. The scholars of semantics said: They were likened to scattered pearls because they are scattered in service. If they were in a row, they would have been likened to arranged pearls. It was also said that they were likened to scattered pearls because they are quick in service, unlike the houris, whom they likened to hidden pearls because they are not subject to service.
76:20: 20- And if you see, then you will see bliss and a great kingdom. That is, if you cast your gaze there, meaning in Paradise, you will see indescribable bliss and a great kingdom whose value is immeasurable. Then is an adverb of place, and the governing factor is I saw. Al-Farra’ said in his speech: What is implied: that is, and if you see what is then, like his saying: Indeed, what is between you has been severed, meaning what is between you. Al-Zajjaj said, objecting to Al-Farra’: It is not permissible to omit the relative pronoun and leave the clause, but I saw is transitive in meaning to then. The meaning is: If you see with your gaze, then, and by then he means Paradise. Al-Suddi said: Bliss is what one enjoys, and the great kingdom is the angels’ asking permission to enter. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said the same. It was said that I saw does not have a verbal, implied, or intended object, but rather its meaning is: wherever your gaze falls in Paradise, you will see bliss and a great kingdom.
76:21: 21- Aalihim thiyab al-nadas Nafi', Hamzah and Ibn Muhaisin read Aalihim with a sukoon on the ya' and a kasra on the ha' as the predicate and thiyab as the subject, or that aalihim is the subject and thiyab is the subject, even if the description is not used, as is the doctrine of Al-Akhfash. Al-Farra' said: It is raised as a subject, and its predicate is thiyab al-nadas, and the active participle is intended to mean the plural. The rest read it with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the ha' as an adverbial phrase in the nominative case as the predicate and thiyab is the subject, as if it were said fawqhum thiyab. Al-Farra' said: Aalihim means above them, and so said Ibn Atiyyah. Abu Hayyan said: “Aal and ‘Aaliyah are active participles, so for them to be adverbials, they need to be derived from Arabic speech. Al-Zajjaj had preceded him and said: This is something we do not know of in adverbials. If it were an adverbial, why would it not be permissible to make the ya’ sukoon? Rather, it is in the accusative case as a state due to two things: One of them is the ha’ and the mim in his statement: “[There circulate among them]” meaning upon the righteous. Boys the highest of the righteous. Clothes of fine silk meaning they circulate among them in this state. The second is that it is a state of the boys: meaning if you saw them, you would think they were scattered pearls, as the clothes are high above their bodies. Abu ‘Ali al-Farisi said: The factor in the state is either that He met them with freshness and joy, or that He rewarded them for their patience. He said: It is permissible for it to be an adverbial. Ibn Sirin, Mujahid, Abu Haywah, and Ibn Abi ‘Ubla read: upon them, and it is a reading with a clear meaning and apparent significance. Abu ‘Ubaid chose the first reading based on Ibn Mas‘ud’s reading: Upon them. The majority read it by adding clothes to fine silk. Abu Haywah and Ibn Abi Ubla read it with the tanween of thiyab, separating it from the addition, and raising sundas and khidr and istabraq on the basis that sundas is an adjective for clothes, because sundas is a type of clothing, and that khidr is an adjective for sundas, because it can be green or not, and that istabraq is in apposition to sundas, meaning and the clothes of istabraq. The majority of reciters differed regarding khidr and istabraq while agreeing on sundas being in the genitive case by adding clothes to it. Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim and Ibn Muhaisin, read khidr in the genitive case as an adjective for sundas and in the nominative case as an apposition to clothes, meaning they are wearing clothes of fine silk and are wearing heavy silk. Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read khidr in the nominative case as an adjective for clothes, and in the genitive case as an adjective for sundas. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid chose this reading because khidr is the best adjective for clothes, so it is in the nominative case, and istabraq is of the same type as sundas. Nafi` and Hafs read it with the nominative case of Khidr and Istabraq because Khidr is an adjective for the garments, and Istabraq is in apposition to garments. Al-A`mash, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read it with the genitive case of Khidr and Istabraq because Khidr is an adjective for Sandas, and Istabraq is in apposition to Sandas. They all read it with the inflection of Istabraq, except Ibn Muhaisin, who did not inflect it. He said, Because it is foreign. There is no justification for this because it is indefinite, unless he says that it is a proper noun for this type of garments. Sandas is a fine type of brocade. Istabraq is the coarse type, and their explanations have already been presented in Surat Al-Kahf. And they were adorned with bracelets of silver is in apposition to They circulate around them. God the Almighty mentioned here that they will be adorned with silver bracelets, and in Surah Fatir They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold, and in Surah Al-Hajj They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls. There is no contradiction between these verses, as it is possible to combine them by making them bracelets of gold, silver, and pearls, or what is meant is that they will wear gold bracelets sometimes, silver bracelets sometimes, and pearl bracelets sometimes, or that each person will wear whatever his soul desires of that. It is permissible for this sentence to be in the accusative case as a state of the subject pronoun, with the estimation And their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink. This is another type of drink that God bestows upon them. Al-Farra’ said: He says it is pure, not impure, as it was described as impure in this world. The meaning is that this drink is pure, not like the wine of this world. Muqatil said: It is a spring of water at the gate of Paradise. Whoever drinks from it, God will remove whatever deceit, rancor, and envy was in his heart. Abu Qilabah and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: Food is brought to them, and when it is the end of it, pure drink is brought to them. They drink until their stomachs swell from it and sweat flows from their bodies like the scent of musk.
76:22: 22- This was a reward for you meaning it will be said to them: This which was mentioned of the types of blessings was a reward for your deeds: meaning a reward for them. And your effort was appreciated meaning your work in this world in obedience to God was pleasing and accepted. God Almighty’s gratitude for the work of His servant is His acceptance of his obedience. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: Zamharir is intense cold. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘The Fire complained to its Lord and said: ‘O Lord, some parts of me have consumed others.’ So He made for it two breaths: one in the summer and one in the winter. The intensity of the cold that you experience is from its Zamharir, and the intensity of the heat that you experience in the summer is from its poisonous winds.” Al-Faryabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hunad ibn al-Sarri, Abd ibn Humayd, Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa’id al-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba`th narrated on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn `Azib regarding the statement of God, and its shades will be brought low over them, “and its fruits will be made accessible,” will be near, “will be made lowly... Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Baath from Ibn Abbas who said: Vessels of silver and their clarity is like the clarity of glass bottles. Measure it by measurement he said: It was measured for the palm of the hand. Abd Al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from him who said: If you took some silver from this world and struck it until it became the size of a fly’s wing, you would not be able to see the water behind it, but the glass bottles of Paradise are as white as silver in the clarity of glass bottles. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him who said: There is nothing in Paradise except that you have been given something similar to it in this world except glass bottles of silver. Al-Firyabi also narrated from him regarding his statement: Measure it by measurement he said: They brought it according to the size of the mouth, not leaving anything behind it and not desiring anything after it. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him Measure it by measurement he said: The cupbearers measured it. Ibn Al-Mubarak, Hanad, Abd bin Hamid, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Baath on the authority of Ibn Amr, who said: The lowest-ranking person in Paradise is he who has a thousand servants working for him, each servant doing work that his companion is not doing. And he recited this verse: When you see them, you will think them to be scattered pearls.
76:23: His statement: 23- Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur’an to you gradually. That is, We separated it into sections and did not send it down all at once. It was also said that the meaning is: We sent it down to you, and you did not bring it forth from your own initiative, as the polytheists claim.
76:24: 24- So be patient for the decision of your Lord meaning for His judgment, and among His judgments and judgments is the delay of your victory until a term required by His wisdom. It was said that this was abrogated by the verse of the sword And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate meaning do not obey anyone who commits a sin or goes too far in disbelief, as God the Almighty forbade them from that. Al-Zajjaj said: The alif here is more emphatic than the waw alone because if you say: Do not obey Zayd and Amr, and he obeys one of them, then he is not disobedient, because God ordered him not to obey both of them. So if he says: Do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate, this indicates that each of them is worthy of being disobeyed, just as if you say: Do not contradict Al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin, then you have said that they are both worthy of being followed, and each of them is worthy of being followed. Al-Farra' said: Or here is equivalent to not, as if he said: nor ingrates. It was said that what was meant by his saying: sinful was Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, and by his saying: or ungrateful was Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, because they both said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Return from this matter and we will satisfy you with money and marriage.
76:25: 25- And remember the name of your Lord in the morning and the evening. That is, constantly remember Him at all times. It has also been said that the meaning is: Pray to your Lord at the beginning and end of the day. The beginning of the day is the dawn prayer, and the end of it is the afternoon prayer.
76:26: 26- And during part of the night prostrate to Him meaning pray Maghrib and Isha. It was also said that what is meant is praying during some of the night without specifying, and min is for partiality in any case. And glorify Him a long night meaning purify Him from that which is not befitting of Him, so what is meant is remembrance by glorification whether in prayer or otherwise. It was also said that what is meant is voluntary prayers at night. Ibn Zayd and others said: This verse was abrogated by the five daily prayers. It was also said that it is an encouragement. It was also said that it is specific to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him).
76:27: 27- Indeed, these people love the immediate meaning the disbelievers of Mecca and those who agree with them. The meaning is that they love the immediate home, which is the worldly home. And they leave behind them a heavy Day meaning they leave and call behind them, meaning behind them or before them and in front of them, a severe and difficult day, which is the Day of Resurrection. It is called heavy because of the hardships and horrors it contains. The meaning of them leaving it behind them is that they do not prepare for it and do not care about it. They are like someone who throws something behind his back out of negligence and belittlement of it, even though in reality they are facing it and it is in front of them.
76:28: 28- We created them meaning We began their creation from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh until their creation was complete, and no one else had any role or effort in that, neither sharing nor being independent. And We strengthened their limbs. Literacy means strength of creation. It is said that God strengthened the limbs of so-and-so, meaning He strengthened his creation. Mujahid, Qatadah, Muqatil, and others said: We strengthened their creation. Al-Hasan said: We strengthened their joints, some to others, with veins and nerves. Abu Ubaid said: It is said that a horse is strong in limbs, meaning in creation. Labid said: The face is very strong, the guard is very strong, the one who is knitted is very strong Al-Akhtal said: From every shunner, he is very captivating, his leadership is smooth, you would imagine him strutting Ibn Zayd said: Asr means strength, and it is derived from isar, which is the strap with which the saddlebags are tied. And from this is the saying of Ibn Ahmar, describing a horse: He walks on strong paths, the scent of ingots is not enough for the cricket And if We willed, We could replace them with others like them. That is, if We willed, We could destroy them and bring forth someone more obedient to God than them. It was also said that the meaning is: We would transform them into the most disgusting form and the ugliest creation.
76:29: 29- Indeed, this is a reminder meaning that this Surah is a reminder and an admonition. So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way meaning a path by which to approach Him, and that is through faith and obedience. What is meant is His reward or His Paradise.
76:30: 30- And you do not will except that God wills meaning you do not will to take a path to God except that God wills, so the matter is up to Him, not up to them, and good and evil are in His hand. There is no one who can prevent what He gives, nor give what He prevents. The will of the servant is abstract and does not bring good nor ward off evil, even if he is rewarded for his righteous will, and is compensated for intending good as in the hadith Actions are but by intentions, and for each person there is but what he intended. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning you do not will except by the will of God. Indeed, God is All-Knowing, All-Wise in His commands and prohibitions: meaning, He is eloquent in knowledge and wisdom.
76:31: 31- He admits into His mercy whomever He wills meaning He admits into His mercy whomever He wills, or He admits into His Paradise whomever He wills of His servants. Ata' said: Whoever's intention is sincere, He will admit him into His Paradise. And for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment The noun the wrongdoers is in the accusative case because what precedes it is in the accusative case, meaning He admits into His mercy whomever He wills and He punishes the wrongdoers: meaning the polytheists. And He has prepared for them is an explanation of this implied word. The preferred form is the accusative, although the nominative case is permissible. The majority of scholars recited the nominative case. Abaan ibn Uthman recited it in the nominative case as a subject, and the reason for that is that there was no verb after it that could be applied to it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We strengthened their joints, meaning He created them. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, And We strengthened their joints, meaning they are the joints.
77:1: It is fifty verses It is Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir. Qatadah said: Except for one verse, which is the verse: {And when it is said to them, Bow down, they do not bow down}, which is Medinan. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas. An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Mursalat was revealed in Mecca. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "While we were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a cave in Mina, Surat Al-Mursalat was revealed in a soft breeze. He was reciting it and I could catch it from his mouth, and his mouth was moist with it. Suddenly, a snake jumped on us. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, "Kill it." We rushed to it and it went away. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, "I have been protected from your evil as you were protected from its evil." Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Abbas that Umm Al-Fadl heard him reciting: {By the messengers sent forth in a soft breeze} and she said: O my son, your recitation of this Surah reminded me of it. It is the last thing I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recite in the Maghrib prayer." His saying: 1- And those sent forth in gusts. The majority of commentators said: They are the winds. It was also said that they are the angels, and this is what Muqatil, Abu Salih, and Al-Kalbi said. It was also said that they are the prophets. According to the first, the Almighty swore by the winds sent for what He commanded them to do, as in His saying: And We sent the fertilizing winds, and His saying: He sends the winds, and other than that. According to the second, the Almighty swore by the angels sent with His revelation, His commands, and His prohibitions. According to the third, the Almighty swore by His messengers sent to His servants to convey His laws. The accusative of in gusts is either because it is an object for which: meaning those sent for the sake of gusts, which is the opposite of indefiniteness. From this is the saying of the poet: He who does good will not lose his reward. Customs between God and people will not be lost. Or that it is a state meaning successive, one following the other like the mane of a horse. The Arabs say: The people marched to so-and-so in one group, meaning they headed towards him. And they are against so-and-so like the mane of a hyena, meaning they ganged up on him. Or that it is a source, as if he said: And the messengers sent forth in succession, meaning successive. Or that it is accusative by removing the preposition, meaning and the messengers sent forth in the group. The majority read in the group with a sukoon on the ra’, and ‘Isa ibn ‘Umar read it with a damma. It was said that what is meant by the messengers is the clouds because of what they contain of blessings and curses.
77:2: 2- The violent storms are the strong blowing winds. Al-Qurtubi said without any difference: It is said that something is blown away if it is destroyed and ruined, and a she-camel is blown away if it blows its rider away like a wind in speed, and it is said that the war swept away the people if it took them away, and it was said that they are the angels assigned to the winds, blowing them away, and it was said that they blow away the soul of the disbeliever, and it was said that they are the destructive signs such as earthquakes and the like.
77:3: 3- And the spreaders meaning the winds bring rain and they spread the clouds, or the angels who are in charge of the clouds spread them or spread their wings in the air when the revelation comes down, or it is the rains because they spread the plants. Ad-Dahhak said: He means what is spread of the books and the deeds of the sons of Adam. Ar-Rabi' said: It is the resurrection by spreading the souls, and he used the and here because it is a resumption of another section.
77:4: 4- The distinguishing verses means that the angels come with what distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between what is lawful and what is unlawful. Mujahid said: It is the wind that separates the clouds and disperses them. It was narrated from him that they are the verses of the Qur’an that distinguish between truth and falsehood. It was also said that they are the messengers who distinguished between what God has commanded and what He has forbidden.
77:5: Al-Hasan said the same: 5- Fal-Malqiyyat are the angels. Al-Qurtubi said unanimously: meaning the one who receives the revelation to the prophets. It was also said that it is Gabriel, and he was given the plural name to glorify him. It was also said that they are the messengers who deliver to their nations what God has revealed to them. Qatrib said. The majority read Fal-Malqiyyat with a sukoon on the lam and a soft qaf, an active participle. Ibn Abbas read it with a fatha on the lam and a double qaf from talqiyyat which is delivering speech to the addressee. The most likely view is that the first three refer to the winds, and the fourth and fifth refer to the angels, and this is what was chosen by Al-Zajjaj, Al-Qadi and others.
77:6: 6- Excuse or vow are in the accusative case as a substitute for mention, or as a direct object, and the agent in both is the verbal noun, as in His statement: Or feeding on a day of famine * an orphan or as a direct object for it: meaning for the excuse and warning, or as a state with the known interpretation: meaning excused or warned. The majority of scholars read them with a sukoon on the dhal in both. Zayd ibn Thabit and his son Kharijah ibn Zayd and Talhah read them with a damma. Al-Haramiyan, Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read them with a sukoon in excuse and a damma in vow. The majority of scholars read excuse or vow as a conjunction with aw. Ibrahim al-Taymi and Qatadah read them with a conjunction with waw without an alif. The meaning is that the angels receive revelation as an excuse from God to His creation and a warning of His punishment, as al-Farra' said. It was also said: an excuse for those who are right and a warning for those who are wrong. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: It is possible that the excuse and the vowel with the heavy emphasis are the plural of the excuser and the vowel, as in his saying: This is a warner from the first vows, in which case it is in the accusative case as a state of throwing, meaning they throw the reminder in a state of excuse and warning, or two objects of the verb remembered, meaning he remembered an excuse or a vow. Al-Mubarrad said: They are with the heavy emphasis, and the singular is the excuse and the vowel.
77:7: Then the Almighty mentioned the answer to the oath, saying: 7- You are only promised something that will happen. That is, what you are promised of the coming of the Hour and the Resurrection will inevitably happen.
77:8: Then the Almighty explained when this will happen, saying: 8- Then when the stars are extinguished, meaning their light is erased and their radiance is gone. It is said that something is extinguished: if it is obliterated and its trace is gone.
77:9: 9- And when the sky is split open meaning it is opened and split. Similar to this is His statement: And the sky is split open and becomes doors.
77:10: 10- And when the mountains are blown away meaning they are quickly uprooted from their place. It is said: I blew something away or I blew it away meaning you took it quickly. Al-Kalbi said: It was leveled to the ground. The Arabs say: The she-camel blew away the grass meaning it grazed it. It is also said that it was made like the grain that is blown away by the blower, and from this is his saying: And the mountains were uprooted but the first is more appropriate. Al-Mubarrad said: Blown away means uprooted from their places.
77:11: 11- And when the messengers are gathered together The hamza in aqtat is a substitute for the damma waw, and every waw that has a damma and its damma is necessary can be replaced with a hamza. Abu Amr, Shaibah, and Al-A'raj read with a waw, while the rest read with a hamza. Time: the appointed time at which the thing that is postponed will be, and the meaning: He made a time for it to separate and judge between them and the nations as in His statement, the Most High, The Day when God will gather the messengers. It was said that this is in this world: meaning the messengers were gathered for their appointed time that was set for them in bringing down the punishment on those who denied them, and the first is more appropriate. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said: meaning He made a time for the Day of Judgment and Judgment. It was said that aqtat means that it was sent for known times according to what God knew about it.
77:12: 12- For what day have You set a deadline? This question is for glorification and amazement: that is, for what great day will the servants be amazed by its severity and its increased terrors? The deadline has been set for them to gather. The sentence is the subject of an implied statement that is an answer to if, or in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in I set a deadline. Al-Zajjaj said: What is meant by this timing is to clarify the time in which they will be brought forth to bear witness against their nations.
77:13: Then he explained this day, saying: 13- The Day of Judgment. Qatada said: On it, people will be judged according to their deeds, as to Paradise or Hell.
77:14: Then he magnified that day and said: 14- And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is? That is, what will make you know about the Day of Judgment means that it is a wondrous and tremendous matter whose magnitude cannot be measured. What is the subject and you is its predicate, or the opposite, as Sibawayh chose.
77:15: Then he mentioned the state of those who denied that Day, saying: 15- Woe, that Day, to the deniers. That is, woe to them on that terrible Day. Wale is a root noun that has become a substitute for fa’il, and it has been changed to the nominative case to indicate steadfastness. Woe is destruction, or it is the name of a valley in Hell. He repeated this verse in this Surah because he divided the woe among them according to the degree of their denial, for every denier of something has a punishment other than his denial of something else, and perhaps something he denied is a greater crime than denying something else, so he is divided from the woe according to the degree of that denial.
77:16: Then the Almighty mentioned what He did to the disbelievers among the past nations, saying: 16- Did We not destroy the former peoples? The Almighty informed us of the destruction of the disbelievers among the past nations, from Adam to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muqatil said: He means the punishment in this world when they denied their messengers.God
77:17: 17- Then We will follow them with the others meaning the infidels of Mecca, and those who agreed with them when they denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The majority of scholars read We will follow them in the nominative case as a resumption, meaning then we will follow them. Abu al-Baqa' said: It is not conjoined because the conjoining requires the meaning to be: We destroyed the first ones, then We made the others follow them in destruction. This is not the case because the destruction of the others has not yet occurred. The nominative case is indicated by Ibn Mas'ud's reading: Then we will follow them, and it was narrated from al-A'raj and al-Abbas on the authority of Abu Amr: We will follow them in the accusative case as a conjunction to We will destroy. Shihab al-Din said: It is based on making the verb conjoined with the entire sentence from His statement: Have We not destroyed?
77:18: 18- Likewise We deal with the criminals meaning, we deal with them like that terrible act, meaning whoever will be destroyed later on, and the kaf is in the accusative case as an adjective for a deleted source: meaning, we deal with every polytheist like that destruction, either in this world or in the hereafter.God
77:19: 19- Woe on that Day to the deniers. That is, woe on the Day of Destruction to those who deny the Books of God and His Messengers. It was said that the first woe is for the torment of the Hereafter, and this is for the torment of this world.
77:20: 20- Did We not create you from a despised water? That is, a weak and insignificant one, which is the sperm.
77:21: 21- So We placed him in a secure place, meaning a secure place, which is the womb.
77:22: 22- To a known extent meaning to a known extent, which is the duration of pregnancy, and it was said until it is formed.
77:23: 23- "Faqdurna The majority of scholars read Faqdurna" with a light pronunciation. Nafi' and Al-Kisa'i read it with a heavy pronunciation from "Al-Taqdir". Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: They are two expressions with the same meaning. You say: I estimated such-and-such, and I estimated it. "Fan'ma' al-Qadirun" means: We are the best of the ones who are able. It was said that the meaning is: We estimated it to be short or tall. It was also said that the meaning of "Qaddurna is our kingdom.
77:24: 24- Woe, that Day, to the deniers of Our ability to do that.
77:25: Then He showed them His wonderful creation and His great power so that they might reflect. He said: 25- Have We not made the earth a receptacle? The meaning of kaft in the language is: to gather and collect. It is said that someone kaft something: if he gathered and collected it. From this, a bag or a pot is called kaft. The meaning is: Did We not make the earth a receptacle for the living on its surface and the dead in its interior, gathering and gathering them? Al-Farra’ said: He means that it gathered them alive on its surface in their homes and dwellings.
77:26: And she wraps them up dead in her belly: that is, she holds them, and this is the meaning of his statement: 26- living and dead. And Sibawayh recited: Generous when the snakes retreat to their holes from the frost Abu Ubaidah said: Kafat is a container, and from it the poet said: Today you are alive on earth and tomorrow you will be included in the palm of your hand That is, in a grave. It was said that the meaning of making it a kafatan is that what comes out of a person of waste is buried in it. Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubaidah said: The living and the dead are two descriptions of the earth: that is, the earth is divided into the living, which is that which grows, and the dead, which is that which does not grow. Al-Farra’ said: The accusative of the living and the dead is due to the falling of the kafatan on it: that is, did We not make the earth a kafatan for the living and the dead? So if the nun is added, what comes after it is accusative. It was said that it is accusative as a state of the earth: that is, from it such and such, and from it such and such. It was said that it is a source described by it for emphasis. Al-Akhfash said: Kafatan is the plural of kafta, and the earth is meant by it the plural, so it was described by the plural. Al-Khalil said: Takatuf is turning something over from back to front or front to back. It is said that the people retreated to their homes: that is, they went.
