77:27: 27- And We placed therein firm, lofty mountains meaning tall mountains. Firm mountains are fixed ones, and tall ones are tall ones, and everything that is high is lofty. And We gave you to drink sweet water meaning sweet, and sweet water is sweet water from which one drinks and with which one quenches one’s thirst. Muqatil said: All of this is more amazing than the resurrection.
77:28: 28- Woe, that Day, to those who deny the blessings We bestowed upon them, of which this is one. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: And the angels sent forth in gusts. He said: They are the angels sent forth in gusts. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud: And the angels sent forth in gusts. He said: The wind. And the scatterers scattered. He said: The wind. Ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim narrated, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated that a man came to Ali ibn Abi Talib and said: What are the angels sent forth in gusts? He said: The winds. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the angels sent forth in gusts. He said: The wind. And the scatterers scattered. He said: The angels. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him, And the messengers sent forth in gusts, he said: the angels. And those who distinguish, he said: the angels, distinguished between truth and falsehood. And those who cast down the Reminder, he said: by sending down. Sa’id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Mas’ud, he said: Woe is a valley in Hell in which the pus of the people of Hell flows, so it is made for the deniers. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas, From despised water, he said: weak. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, Kafatan, he said: we were. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, Lofty mountains, he said: lofty mountains. And in His statement, Furat, he said: torment.
77:29: 29- Go back to what you were doing is an estimation of the saying: that is, it is said to them as a rebuke and a reprimand.
77:30: 30- Go to that which you used to deny in this world, the keepers of Hell will say to them: meaning, go to the torment which you used to deny, which is the torment of the Fire. Go to a shade of three branches meaning, to a shade of smoke from Hell that has risen, then splits into three groups in which you will be until the reckoning is over. This is the nature of a great smoke when it rises, it branches out into branches. The majority of scholars read Go in both instances in the imperative form for emphasis. Ruways read from Ya'qub in the past tense in the second instance: meaning, when they were ordered to go, they complied and went. It was said that what is meant by the shade here is the canopy, which is a tongue of fire that surrounds them. Then it branches out into three branches and shades them until their reckoning is over, then they go to the Fire. It was also said that it is the shade of hot water, as in His statement: In scorching wind and scalding water, and a shade of scalding water as mentioned above.
77:31: Then God Almighty described this shade as a mockery of them, saying: 31- No shade, nor does it protect against the flame. That is, it does not provide shade from the heat nor protect against the flame. Al-Kalbi said: It does not ward off the heat of Hell from you.
77:32: Then God the Almighty described the Fire, saying: 32- It throws out sparks like palaces. That is, every spark of its sparks that it throws out is like a palace among palaces in its size. Sparks are what fly apart from the Fire, and palace is a huge building. It is said that palace is the plural of qasra with a silent sad like hamr and humrah and tamar and tamarah, and it is the singular of thick, solid firewood. Saeed bin Jubayr and Al-Dahhak said: They are the roots of the large trees, and it was said that they are its necks. The majority read kalqasr with a sukoon on the sad, and it is the singular of palaces as mentioned above. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Hamid and Al-Salami read it with a fatha on the sad: meaning the necks of palm trees, and qasra is the plural of qasr and qasrat. Qatadah said: The necks of camels. Saeed bin Jubayr read it with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the sad, and it is also the plural of qasra like badr and badrah and qasaa and qasaa. The majority read sharrar with a fatha on the shin. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Muqsim read it with a kasra and an alif between the two ra’s. Isa read it likewise, except that he opens the sheen, which is incorrect.
77:33: Then he likened the sparks in terms of their color, saying: 33- As if they were yellow camels, which is the plural of camel, which are camels or the plural of camel. The majority read Jamalah with a kasra on the jim. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read Jamalah, which is the plural of camel. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and Abu Raja’ read Jamalat with a damma on the jim, which are the ropes of ships. Al-Wahidi said: Safar means black according to the commentators. Al-Farra’ said: Safar is the blackness of camels. You do not see a black camel unless it is tinged with yellow, that is why the Arabs called black camels Safar. It was said that sparks, when they fly and fall, have the color of fire, and are similar to black camels. From this comes the saying of the poet: These are my horses and these are my riders, their young ones are as yellow as raisins That is, they are black. It was said that this statement is linguistically impossible, that something could be tainted with a small amount, and then all of it could be attributed to that taint. So it is surprising that someone would say this, as God the Almighty said: Yellow camels. It was answered that its face is that fire was created from light, so it is luminous. Then when God created Hell, which is the place of fire, He filled that place with that fire, and sent to it His power and His wrath, so it became black from His power and increased in blackness, and became blacker than anything, so its sparks are black because they are from a black fire. I said: This answer does not refute what the speaker said, because his words are in consideration of what occurred in the Noble Book here of its description as being yellow. So if the matter was as the respondent mentioned, of the blackness of the fire and the blackness of its sparks, then God would have said: As if they were black camels. But if the Arabs call black yellow, then there is no problem, because the Qur’an was revealed in their language, and trustworthy people have transmitted that from them, so what is in the Qur’an here was based on this Arabic usage.
77:34: 34- Woe, that Day, to those who deny God’s messengers and His signs.
77:35: 35- This is a Day when they will not speak meaning they will not speak. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: On the Day of Resurrection there are situations, in some of which they will speak, and in others their mouths will be sealed so they will not speak. We have already mentioned this combination in more than one place. It was said that this is a reference to the time when they will enter Hell and at that time they will not speak, because the situations of questioning and accountability have passed. Al-Hasan said: They will not speak with an argument even if they speak. The majority of scholars read Day in the nominative case as the predicate of the demonstrative pronoun. Zayd ibn Ali, Al-A'raj, Al-A'mash, Abu Haywah, and Asim, in a narration from him, read it with the fat-ha as a construction because it is added to the verb, and its place is the nominative case as a predicate. It was said that it is the accusative case as a circumstantial case. The reference here is to what came before of the threat, as if it was said that this punishment mentioned will be on a Day when they will not speak.
77:36: 36- And they will not be given permission to apologize. The majority read yu'dhin in the passive voice, while Zayd ibn Ali read nor will they be given permission in the active voice: meaning, God will not give them permission: meaning, they will not have permission from God to apologize without making the apology a cause for the permission, as if it were in the accusative case. Al-Farra' said: The fa in yitadhirun is in agreement with yu'dhin, and this was permitted because the endings of the sentences are with nun. If he had said yitadhirun, it would not be in accordance with the verses. He also said, It is not decreed against them so that they die in the accusative case, and both are correct.
77:37: 37- Woe, that Day, to those who deny what the messengers called them to and warned them of its consequences.
77:38: 38- “This is the Day of Judgment. We have gathered you and the former peoples.” That is, it will be said to them: This is the Day of Judgment on which creation will be judged and truth will be distinguished from falsehood. The address in We have gathered you is to the disbelievers during the time of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by the former peoples are the disbelievers of past nations.
77:39: 39- If you have a plan meaning if you are able to plan a plan now, then plan it. This is a rebuke and a rebuke to them. Muqatil said: He is saying if you have a plan then plan it for yourselves. It was also said that the meaning is: If you are able to wage war then wage war. It was also said that this is from the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so it is like the words of Hud 11:Then plot against me all together and do not wait.
77:40: 40- Woe, that Day, to the deniers because their weakness and the invalidity of what they were doing in this world will become clear to them.
77:41: Then the Almighty mentioned the believers, saying: 41- Indeed, the righteous will be among shades and springs meaning in the shades of trees and palaces, not like the shade that the unbelievers have from smoke or fire as mentioned above. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: What is meant by the righteous are those who avoid associating partners with God, because the Surah from beginning to end is a rebuke to the unbelievers for their disbelief. Al-Razi said: This verse must have been mentioned for this purpose, otherwise the Surah would have been disjointed in its structure and arrangement. The structure is only completed by the promise being to the believers because of their faith. As for making it a reason for obedience, that is not befitting of the structure, so he said. What is meant by springs are rivers, and by fruits is what one enjoys, which their souls desire and lusts call for.
77:42: 42- And fruits of whatever they desire.
77:43: 43- Eat and drink in happiness for what you used to do. That is, this will be said to them. The sentence is understood as saying, and it is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun of the righteous. The ba is for causality: that is, because of what you used to do in this world of righteous deeds.
77:44: 44- Thus do We reward the doers of good. That is, We reward the doers of good for their deeds with such a great reward. The majority of scholars read in the shade. Al-A’mash, Al-Zuhri, Talhah, and Al-A’raj read in the shade, which is the plural of shadow.
77:45: 45- Woe on that Day to the deniers as they will be in great misery, while the believers will be in eternal bliss.
77:46: 46- Eat and enjoy yourselves a little, for indeed, you are criminals. The sentence, with the estimation of the saying, is in the accusative case as a state of the deniers: meaning woe is certain for them in the event that they are told this as a reminder of their state in this world, or this is said to them in this world, and the criminals are the polytheists who associate partners with God, and although this is in the wording an order, in meaning it is a threat and a great deterrent.
77:47: 47- Woe, that Day, to the deniers. He repeated it to increase the rebuke and reprimand.
77:48: 48- And when it is said to them, ‘Bow down,’ they do not bow down. That is, when they are commanded to pray, they do not pray. Muqatil said: This was revealed about Thaqeef who refused to pray after the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded them to do so. They said, We will not bow down, for it is a disgrace to us. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, There is no good in a religion in which there is no bowing down or prostrating. It was also said that this will only be said to them in the Hereafter when they are called to prostrate but they are unable to. It was also said that what is meant by bowing down is obedience and humility.
77:49: 49- Woe, that Day, to those who deny the commands and prohibitions of God Almighty.
77:50: 50- So in what statement after it will they believe? That is, in what statement after the Qur'an will they believe if they do not believe in it? The majority read they believe with a subjunctive ending indicating absence. Ibn Amir, in a narration from him, and Ya'qub read it with a superjunctive ending indicating address. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, with sparks like palaces, he said: like a huge palace. And his statement, yellow camels, he said: pieces of copper. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Faryabi, Hanad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abis who said: I heard Ibn Abbas being asked about his statement, it throws out sparks like palaces, he said: We used to raise the wood to a height of three cubits or less, and raise it up for the winter and call it palace. He said: I heard him being asked about his statement, yellow camels, he said: the ropes of ships are gathered together until they are like the waists of men. And the wording of Al-Bukhari is: We used to raise the wood to a height of three cubits or more and raise it up for the winter and call it palace. like a yellow camel, the ropes of ships are gathered together until they are like the waists of men. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority that he read it like palace with the qaf and the sad open. And he said palace of palm trees means necks. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that he said: The Arabs in the pre-Islamic period used to say: Bring us the firewood, and it would be cut to the size of an arm or two. Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement: throwing sparks like palaces, he said: It is not like trees or giants, but rather like cities and fortresses. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: like palaces, he said: It refers to palaces. And regarding his statement: yellow camels, he said: Camels. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: Nafi’ bin Al-Azraq asked Ibn Abbas about his statement: This is a Day when they will not speak, “You will not hear except a whisper,” And they will turn to one another, questioning each other, and Here, read my book, so he said to him: Woe to you, have you asked anyone about this before me? He said: No. He said: If you had asked, you would have been lost. Didn't God say: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count? He said: Yes. He said: For each amount of a day of these days there is a color. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when it is said to them, 'Bow down,' they do not bow down, meaning: They will be called on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate but they will not be able to because they did not prostrate to God in this world.
78:1: It is called Surat An-Naba, and it has forty verses, and it was said that it has forty-one verses. It is a Meccan verse according to all the narrations. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: What are they asking about? was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar narration on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. His statement: 1- About what are they asking one another? Its original form is about what, so the nun was assimilated into the mim, because the mim shares the nasal sound with it, as al-Zajjaj said. The alif was deleted to distinguish the predicate from the interrogative, and likewise in fim and mmm and the like, and the meaning is: about what thing are they asking one another? The majority read ‘amma without the alif for the reason we mentioned, and Abi, Ibn Mas’ud, ‘Ikrimah, and ‘Isa read it without it, and from this is the saying of the poet: Why did he insult me, you scoundrel, like a pig wallowing in filth? But it is rare and is not permitted except in case of necessity. Al-Bazzi read the letter baa’ al-sakt instead of the letter alif, and this was narrated from Ibn Kathir. Al-Zajjaj said: The word is an interrogative word, and the meaning is to magnify the story, as you say: What do you want? if you magnify its importance. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent and informed them of the Oneness of God and the Resurrection after death, and recited the Quran to them, they began to ask each other: What did Muhammad bring and what did he bring? So God revealed: About what are they asking each other? Al-Farra’ said: Asking is for some to ask each other, like in confrontation. It can also be used to mean that they talk about it even if there is no question between them. God the Most High said: And some of them turned to others, asking each other. “One of them said, Indeed, I had a companion al-Ma’ 2:17. This indicates that it is a conversation, and the word ma is used to seek the truth of things, and this requires that the sought-after be unknown. So He made the great thing, the essence of which the mind is incapable of encompassing, as if it were unknown. That is why God the Most High used the word ma.
78:2: Then the Almighty mentioned their question about what and explained it by saying: 2- About the Great report. The Almighty first mentioned it in the form of a question in an ambiguous manner so that their minds would be directed to it and their understandings would turn to it. Then He explained it in a way that indicates its greatness and magnification, as if it was said: About what are they asking? Did I inform you of it? Then it was said in the form of an answer: About the Great report of the manner of His statement: Whose is the dominion today? It belongs to God, the One, the Prevailing. The preposition and the noun are related to the verb that preceded it, or to what indicates it. Ibn Atiyyah said: Most grammarians said: About the Great report is related to the apparent they are asking, as if He said: Why are they asking about the Great report? It was said that it is not related to the mentioned verb, because it would have been necessary to enter the interrogative letter, so the interpretation would be: About the Great report? So it would have been necessary for they are asking to be related to another understood word. Rather, that report, meaning the Qur’an, was great because it informs about monotheism, the belief in the Messenger, and the occurrence of the Resurrection. Ad-Dahhak said: It means report of the Day of Resurrection, and Qatada said the same.
78:3: And it has been proven that the great report is the Qur’an by His saying: 3- about which they differ for they differed about the Qur’an, some of them made it magic, some of them poetry, some of them divination, and some of them said it was legends of the ancients. As for the resurrection, the disbelievers agreed at that time to deny it. It can be said that there was a difference of opinion about the resurrection in general, so the believers believed in it and the disbelievers denied it, so there was a difference of opinion about it from this perspective, even if there was no difference of opinion about it among the disbelievers themselves in terms of submission and concession. And what indicates that it is the Qur’an is His saying, the Most High: Say, ‘It is a great report * From it you are turning away.’ And what indicates that it is the resurrection is that it is what the polytheists most disapproved of and their foolish minds rejected.:Also, the sects of the infidels differed among themselves regarding the resurrection. The Christians affirmed the spiritual resurrection, and a sect of the Jews affirmed the physical resurrection. The Torah explicitly mentions the word Paradise in the Hebrew language as Janna’idha with an open jim, then a silent noon, then a broken ‘ayn, then a silent ta’, then a voiced dhal, followed by an alif. The Gospel explicitly states in many places the resurrection, and that there will be bliss for the obedient and torment for the disobedient. Some sects of the infidel Arabs denied the resurrection, as God said about them, “It is not but our worldly life. We die and we live, and we will not be resurrected.” A sect among them was not certain of its denial, but rather doubted it, as God said about them, saying, We think only an assumption, and we are not certain. And He also said about them, saying, “And I do not think that the Hour will occur. And if I should return to my Lord, indeed, I will have with Him [the best] reward.” So the differences arose among the sects of infidelity in this manner. It has been said that the pronoun in His statement they ask each other refers to the believers and the disbelievers because they were all asking about it. As for the Muslim, he increases in certainty, preparation, and insight into his religion. As for the disbeliever, it is mockery and ridicule. Al-Razi said: It is possible that they are asking the Messenger and saying: What is this that he promises us regarding the matter of the Hereafter? The relative pronoun is in the genitive case as an attribute of the report after describing it as being great, so it is described as great and characterized by the occurrence of disagreement over it.
78:4: 4- No, they will know is a deterrent and warning to them. This indicates that those who differ about it are the infidels, and with it what was said about the disagreement between them and the believers is dispelled, because the deterrence and threat are directed only at the infidels. It was said that no means truly, then he repeated the deterrence and warning and said:
78:5: 5- Then both will know is used to exaggerate the emphasis and severity of the threat. The majority of scholars read the two verbs with the sub-ya' in the third person. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ibn Dinar, and Ibn Amir, in one narration from him, read them with the superlative in the addressee role. Ad-Dahhak read the first with the sub-ya' and the second with the sub-ya'. Ad-Dahhak said: Also, Then both will know" means the disbelievers, the consequence of their denial. "Then both will know" means the believers, the consequence of their belief. It was also said the opposite. It was also said that it is a threat followed by another threat. It was also said that the meaning is "Then both will know at the time of death, Then both will know" at the time of resurrection.
78:6: Then He, the Almighty, mentioned His wonderful creation and His great power so that they would know His Oneness and believe in what His Messenger brought. He said: 6- Have We not made the earth a resting place?
78:7: Then He, the Almighty, mentioned His wonderful creation and great power so that they would know His Oneness and believe in what His Messenger brought. He said: 7- Have We not made the earth a resting place * and the mountains pegs meaning Our ability to do these things mentioned is greater than Our ability to resurrect. The mattress is the cushion and the bed as in His statement: Who has made the earth a bed for you The majority read it as mattress while Mujahid, Isa and some of the Kufians read it as cradle meaning that it is like a cradle for a child, which is what is made for him so he sleeps on it. And pegs is the plural of peg: meaning We made the mountains pegs for the earth so that it would remain still and not move as one anchors tents with pegs. This is evidence that the question between them is about the matter of resurrection, not about the Qur’an, nor about the prophethood of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, as has been said, because this evidence is only suitable to be used as evidence for resurrection.
78:8: 8- And We created you in pairs is connected to the negative present tense, which is included in its ruling, so it is in the same power as We created you. What is meant by pairs here are the types: that is, males and females. It was also said that what is meant by pairs are the colors, and it was also said that this includes every pair of creatures, from ugly and beautiful, tall and short.
78:9: 9- And We have made your sleep a rest meaning rest for your bodies. Al-Zajjaj said: Slumber is to stop moving and the soul in the body: meaning We have made your sleep a rest for you. Ibn Al-Anbari said: We have made your sleep a severance of your deeds, because the root of sabt is to cut off, and it was said that its root is to stretch out. It is said that a woman sabt her hair: if she loosened it and let it down, and a man is masbout Al-Khalq meaning his creation is stretched out, and when a man wants to rest he stretches out, so sleep is called slumber. It was said that the meaning is: And We have made your sleep death, and sleep is one of the two deaths, so the one who is masbout is similar to the dead, but the soul has not left him, and from this is the saying of the poet: And the folded relatives, as for its day, it is Saturday and as for its night, it is a curse This includes His statement: God takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep, the verse, and His statement: And it is He who takes you by night.
78:10: 10- And We have made the night as a covering meaning, We clothe you in its darkness and cover you with it as a garment covers you. Saeed bin Jubayr and Al-Suddi said: meaning, a resting place for you. It was also said that what is meant by it is what covers one when sleeping, such as a blanket or the like. This is far-fetched, because the making was applied to the night, not to what the sleeper covers himself with when he sleeps.
78:11: 11- And We made the day for livelihood meaning a time for livelihood, and livelihood is living, and everything that is lived by is livelihood, and the meaning is: God made the day bright for them so that they may strive to do what is necessary for their livelihood and what God has allotted them of provisions.
78:12: 12- And We built above you seven strong heavens. He means seven heavens of strong creation and perfect construction. That is why He described them as strong and the thickness of each one of them is a journey of five hundred years, as was mentioned.
78:13: 13- And We made a blazing lamp refers to the sun, and made here means created, and so is His statement: And We made your sleep [a place of] rest and what follows, because these verbs are transitive to two objects, so they must include the meaning of a verb that transits to them, such as creation, making, and the like. It was said that made means establishment and innovation in all of these instances, and what is meant by it is the formative establishment that means estimation and leveling. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Wahhaj is the igniter, and he is the one who blazed. It is said that the fire blazed blazingly and blazingly. Muqatil said: He placed in it a free light, and blaze combines light and heat.
78:14: 14- And We sent down from the clouds abundant water. The mu'asarat are the clouds that are squeezed with water but have not yet rained, like a woman whose menstruation is approaching. This is what Sufyan, Ar-Rabi', Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Ad-Dahhak said. Mujahid, Muqatil, Qatadah, and Al-Kalbi said: They are the winds, and the winds are called mu'asarat. It is said that the wind squeezes, squeezes, and stirs up dust. Al-Azhari said: They are the winds with cyclones, because the winds bring about rain. Al-Farra' said: The mu'asarat are the clouds from which rain is extracted. An-Nahhas said: These sayings are correct. The wind that brings rain is called mu'asarat, and the winds fertilize the clouds, so it rains. It is possible that these sayings are one saying, and the meaning is: And We sent down from the clouds abundant water. It is said in As-Sihah: The mu'asarat are the clouds that are squeezed with rain, and the people asr means they were rained on. Al-Mubarrad said: It is said that a cloud is a squeezer, meaning one that holds water, squeezing it out little by little. Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Al-Hasan, Ibn Jubayr, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The squeezers are the heavens. And thajjaj means pouring down abundantly in succession. It is said that the water thajja means it flowed abundantly, and thajjah means it made it flow. Al-Zajjaj said: thajjaj is pouring rain. Ibn Zayd said: Thajjajan kathi.
78:15: 15- To bring forth thereby grain and plants meaning to bring forth from that water grain for sustenance: such as wheat, barley, and the like, and plants are what animals eat of grass and other plants.
78:16: 16- And gardens intertwined meaning orchards intertwined with each other due to their branching. Al-Alaf has no singular, like awzaa' and akhifa. It was also said that its singular is laf, with a kasra or damma on the lam, as mentioned by Al-Kisa'i. Abu Ubaidah said: Its singular is lafif, like sharif and ashraaf. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Kisa'i that it is the plural of plural, it is said that Jannah is lafa' and nasb is laf, and the plural is laf with a damma on the lam, like hamr, then this plural is alfaaf, and it was also said that it is the plural of mutalifah, with the deletion of the extra letters. Al-Farra' said: Paradise is that which has palm trees, and Paradise is that which has vines.
78:17: 17- Indeed, the Day of Judgment is a time appointed meaning a time, a gathering, and an appointment for the first and the last, in which they will reach what they were promised of reward and punishment. It was called the Day of Judgment because God will judge between His creation on it. This is a beginning of explaining what they are asking about regarding the Resurrection. It was said that the meaning of a time appointed is that it is a limit by which the world is set and ends, and it was said that it is a limit for the creation to which they will end.
78:18: 18- The Day the Trumpet is blown, then you will come in droves meaning the Day the Trumpet is blown, which is the horn in which Israfil will blow, and what is meant here is the second blast which is for the resurrection, then you will come meaning to the place of presentation, in droves meaning groups by groups, and groups by groups, which is the plural of group, and the accusative of The Day the Trumpet is blown is as a substitute for the Day of Separation, or an explanation of it that is useful to increase its magnification and terror, even if the separation is after the blowing, and it is permissible for it to be accusative with the omission of I mean, and the accusative of in droves is as a state of the subject of you come, and the fa in you will come is eloquent and indicates something omitted: meaning then you will come to the place of obligation immediately after that in droves.
78:19: 19- And the heaven was opened, and it became gates is in apposition to blow, and the past tense indicates that it happened, i.e. it was opened for the angels to descend. And it became gates as in His statement: And the Day the heaven is split open with clouds and the angels are sent down in succession. It was said that the meaning of opened is that it was cut into pieces like gates. It was also said that its gates are its paths. It was also said that it dissolves and scatters until it becomes gates. It was also said that every servant has two gates in the heaven: a gate for his provision and a gate for his deeds. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, the gates will be opened. The apparent meaning of His statement, And it became gates is that they all became gates, but that is not what is meant, rather what is meant is that it became with many gates. Ibn Amir, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read opened without a vowel. The rest read it with a shaddah.
78:20: 20- And the mountains will be set in motion and will become a mirage. That is, they will be set in motion from their places in the air, and uprooted from their places, and will become scattered dust, and the observer will think it is a mirage. The meaning is that the mountains will become like nothing, just as a mirage makes the observer think it is water, but it is not water. It was said that the meaning of set in motion is that they will be blown away from their roots. And similar to this is His statement: And you will see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass as the passing of clouds. The Almighty has mentioned the conditions of mountains in different ways, but the combination between them is that you say: The first of their conditions is crushing, which is His statement: And the earth and the mountains will be borne and crushed with a single crushing. The second of their conditions is that they will become like patterned wool, as in His statement: And the mountains will be like carded wool. The third of their conditions is that they will become like dust, which is His statement: And the mountains will be swept away with a complete pulverization, and they will be scattered dust. The fourth of their conditions is that they will be blown away and carried by the winds, as in His statement: And you will see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass as the passing of clouds. The fifth of their conditions is that they will become a mirage, meaning nothing, as in this verse.
78:21: Then the Almighty proceeded to detail the rulings of the chapter, saying: 21- Indeed, Hell is an ambush. Al-Azhari said: The ambush is the place where the observer ambushes the enemy. Al-Mubarrad said: An ambush where they ambush: meaning it is prepared for them, where its keepers ambush the disbelievers. Al-Hasan said: There is a guard at the door, and no one will enter Paradise until he passes by them. Whoever brings a pass will enter, and whoever does not bring a pass will be imprisoned. Muqatil said: A confinement, and it was said a path and a passageway. It was said in Al-Sahah: The one who watches over something is the one who watches it. It is said that he watches it, and watching is watching, and the watch is the place of observation. Al-Asma'i said: I watched him, I observed him. The meaning of the verse is that Hell was, in the judgment and decree of God, a place of observation where the keepers of Hell watch the unbelievers to torment them therein. Or it is itself a place of observation for those unbelievers who come to it, just as the watchman watches for those who pass by it and come to them. The word al-marsad is a form of exaggeration like al-mi'tar and al-mi'mar, so it is as if Hell often awaits the unbelievers.
78:22: Then he mentioned who is a target for him, saying: 22- For the transgressors is a place of return meaning a place to which they will return. The target is the place of return. It is said that someone returned, if he went back. The transgressor is the one who transgressed with disbelief. For the transgressors is an adjective for the target, related to something omitted. And a target is a substitute for a target. It is permissible for for the transgressors to be in the accusative case as a state of a place of return that was brought before it because it is indefinite.
78:23: 23- Labithin fiha is in the accusative case of the implied pronoun in al-Thaghīn. The majority of scholars read Labithin with an alif. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read Labithin without an alif. The accusative case of Ahqāb is in the adverbial case: meaning staying in the Fire as long as the ahqāb exist, and they never end. Whenever a ahqāb passes, another ahqāb comes, which is the plural of ahqāb with two ḍammah, which means time. Ahqāb is the age. Al-ḍawwur with a ḍamma on the ha' and a ḍawwur with a ḍamma on the qaf, it is said that it is eighty years. Al-Wahidi narrated from the commentators that it is eighty-odd years, a year is three hundred and sixty days, a day is one thousand years of the days of this world. It is said that the ahqāb is a time for their drinking of boiling water and pus, and when it ends, they will have another type of punishment. Al-Suddi said: Al-ḍawq is seventy years. Bashir ibn Ka'b said: Three hundred years. Ibn 'Umar said: Forty years, and it was also said: Thirty thousand years. Al-Hasan said: None of you knows what the epochs are, but they have said that they are one hundred epochs, and each epoch is seventy thousand years, and today is like a thousand years. It was said that the verse is interpreted to refer to the sinners who will emerge from the Fire, but what we mentioned first is preferable, that the intended meaning of the verse is perpetuity, not restriction. Al-Wahidi narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: By God, it is nothing but that when an epoch passes, another enters, then another, and so on forever.
78:24: And sentence 24 - They will not taste therein any coolness or drink. And sentence 24 - They will not taste therein any coolness or drink.
78:25: And the sentence 25 - They will not taste therein any coolness or drink * except scalding water and pus-filled water is a new sentence to explain what it includes, that they will not taste in Hell or in the ages any coolness that will benefit them from its heat, nor any drink that will benefit them from its thirst, except scalding water, which is hot water, and pus-filled water, which is the pus of the people of Hell. It is possible that it is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun of the transgressors, or an attribute of the ages, and the exception is discontinuous according to those who make the coolness sleep, and it is possible that it is connected from His saying: a drink. Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Abu Ubaidah, Al-Kisa'i, Al-Fadl ibn Khalid, and Abu Mu'adh Al-Nahwi said: The coolness mentioned in this verse is sleep, and from this is the saying of Al-Kindi: Her sheets became cold on me, so the cold turned me away from her and from kissing her. Meaning sleep. Al-Zajjaj said: Meaning they will not taste therein the coolness of the wind, nor shade, nor sleep, so he made the coolness include these things. Al-Hasan, Ata’, and Ibn Zayd said: Coolness: Meaning a spirit and a resting place. The majority read ghassaqan with a light sun. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a shaddah on the seen. Its interpretation and the interpretation of al-Hameem and the disagreement over them were presented in Surah Sad. And the sentence 25 - They will not taste therein any coolness or drink * except scalding water and pus-filled water is a new sentence to explain what it includes, that they will not taste in Hell or in the ages any coolness that will benefit them from its heat, nor any drink that will benefit them from its thirst, except scalding water, which is hot water, and pus-filled water, which is the pus of the people of Hell. It is possible that it is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun of the transgressors, or an attribute of the ages, and the exception is discontinuous according to those who make the coolness sleep, and it is possible that it is connected from His saying: a drink. Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Abu Ubaidah, Al-Kisa'i, Al-Fadl ibn Khalid, and Abu Mu'adh Al-Nahwi said: The coolness mentioned in this verse is sleep, and from this is the saying of Al-Kindi: Her sheets became cold on me, so the cold turned me away from her and from kissing her. Meaning sleep. Al-Zajjaj said: Meaning they will not taste therein the coolness of the wind, nor shade, nor sleep, so he made the coolness include these things. Al-Hasan, Ata’, and Ibn Zayd said: Coolness: Meaning a spirit and a resting place. The majority read ghassaqan with a light sun. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a shaddah on the seen. Its interpretation and the interpretation of al-Hameem and the disagreement over them were presented in Surah Sad.
78:26: 26- A recompense in accordance with their deeds means in accordance with their actions. A recompense is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, and according is an adjective for it. Al-Farra' and Al-Akhfash said: We rewarded them with a recompense that corresponded with their deeds. Al-Zajjaj said: They were given a recompense that corresponded with their deeds. Al-Farra' said: Al-Wifaq is the plural of Al-Wafaq, and Al-Wafaq and Al-Muwaaqif are one and the same. Muqatil said: The punishment corresponded with the sin, for there is no sin greater than evil and no punishment greater than the Fire. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: Their deeds were evil, so God brought them that which would harm them.
78:27: 27- Indeed, they did not expect an account. That is, they did not expect the reward of an account. Al-Zajjaj said: They did not believe in resurrection, so they hoped for their account. The sentence explains why they deserved the aforementioned reward.
78:28: 28- And they denied Our signs blasphemously meaning they denied the Qur'anic verses, or they denied something more general than them, with a blatant denial. Fa'al is one of the verbal nouns of tafa'al. Al-Farra' said: It is an eloquent Yemeni dialect, you say liar kadhdhaban and riqqat al-qamis khiraqan. He said in As-Sahah: And they denied Our signs liar kadhdhaban is one of the verbal nouns of the doubled form because its verbal noun may come in the form taf'il like at-talkil, fa'al like kadhdhab, taf'ala like tawsiyah, and maf'al like wa-tashaqnahum kullu ma'muf'al and we tore them apart, each one torn. The majority of scholars read kadhdhaban with the shaddah. Ali ibn Abi Talib read it with the tafsir. Abu Ali Al-Farsi said that both the tafsir and the shaddah are verbal nouns of denial. Ibn Umar read kadhdhaban with the damma and the shaddah, the plural of kadhdhab. Abu Hatim said that it is accusative as a state. Al-Zamakhshari said: According to this reading, it may mean someone who is eloquent in lying. You say: a lying man, just as you say: good-looking and miserly.
78:29: 29- And everything We have recorded in a book. The majority of scholars read and everything in the accusative case, indicating the preoccupation: meaning, And We have recorded everything We have recorded. Abu Al-Sammak read it in the nominative case, indicating the beginning, and what follows it is its predicate. This sentence is parenthetical between the cause and the effect. The accusative case of book is in the verbal noun for We have recorded it because We have recorded it means We wrote it. It was also said that it is in the accusative case, indicating the state: meaning, written. It was said that what is meant is We wrote it in the Preserved Tablet so that the angels would know it. It was also said that what is meant is what the guardians wrote for the angels of their deeds. It was also said that what is meant by it is knowledge because what was written was further from being forgotten. The first is more appropriate, based on His statement: And everything We have recorded in a clear register.
78:30: 30- So taste [the punishment], for We will not increase you except in torment. This sentence is caused by their disbelief and denial of the verses. Al-Razi said: This fa is for recompense, so he pointed out that the command to taste is caused by what was previously explained about the ugliness of their actions, and the increase in their torment is that every time their skins are roasted through, He replaces them with other skins, and every time the fire subsides, God increases their blazing fire. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On the Great report, he said: The Qur’an: This is narrated on the authority of a group of the Successors. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding His statement, And We made a blazing lamp, he said: luminous, And We sent down from the pressed clouds, he said: the clouds, plentiful water, he said: pouring down. Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Ya’la, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mundhir also narrated on his authority, plentiful water, he said: pouring down. Ash-Shafi’i, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud regarding His statement, And We sent down from the pressed clouds plentiful water, he said: God sends the wind, and it carries the water, and the clouds pass by it, and it flows like a she-camel flows down, and the plentiful water descends from the sky, like al-Ghazali, and the winds disperse it, so it descends in scattered forms. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Anbari narrated in Al-Masahif on the authority of Qatadah, he said: In the recitation of Ibn Abbas, And We sent down from the pressed clouds means the winds. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding his statement: {And gardens intertwined}, he said: Intertwined. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him regarding the verse: He said: He says: Some of them intertwined with others. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him regarding his statement: {And the mountains will move and become a mirage}, he said: The mirage of the sun. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him: {And abiding therein for ages}, he said: Years. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Hunad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, he said: Ali ibn Abi Talib asked Hilal al-Hijri: What do you find about the periods in the Book of God? He said: We find it to be eighty years, each year of which is twelve months, each month has thirty days, each day is a thousand years. Sa`id ibn Mansur and al-Hakim narrated - and he authenticated it - from Ibn Mas`ud regarding the verse: He said: One period is eighty years. Al-Bazzar narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: A period is eighty years, a year is three hundred and sixty days, and a day is like a thousand years of what you count. Abd bin Hamid narrated from him that he said: A ḥaqb is eighty years, and today it is like one-sixth of the world. Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. Al-Suyuti said: With a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: They will abide therein for ḥaqb. He said: A ḥaqb is a thousand months, a month is thirty days, and a year is twelve months, three hundred and sixty days, each day of which is a thousand years of your reckoning, so a ḥaqb is thirty thousand years. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami narrated from Ibn Umar that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “God will not bring forth from the Fire one who has entered it until he has remained in it for ḥaqb. A ḥaqb is eighty-odd years, each year is three hundred and sixty days, and a day is a thousand years of your reckoning.” Ibn Umar said: So let no one assume that he will be brought forth from the Fire. Sa’id bin Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abdullah bin Amr that he said: One ḥaqb is eighty years. Ibn Jarir narrated a similar hadith from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn as-Samit who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A ḥaqb is forty years. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan regarding His statement, They will abide therein for ages and His statement, except what your Lord wills, that they are regarding the people of monotheism from the people of the Qiblah. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud who said: The bitter cold of Hell will be for them as a form of torment, because God says, They will not taste therein any coolness or drink. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They will not taste therein any coolness or drink * Except scalding water, that its heat has reached its peak. And ghasaqan, that its heat has reached its peak. And if a man lowers a vessel to his mouth, the scalp of his face falls off, until only rattling bones remain.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, A recompense commensurate with their deeds, that he said: It will be commensurate with their deeds. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: No verse has ever been revealed to the people of Hell more severe than this: So taste [its [good], for We will not increase you except in punishment. They will be in more torment from God forever.
78:31: His saying: 31- Indeed, for the righteous there is attainment. This is the beginning of explaining the state of the believers and what God has prepared for them of good after explaining the state of the disbelievers and what God has prepared for them of evil. The word mafaz is a source meaning victory and attainment of a blessing and what is desired and salvation from the Fire. From this, the desert is called a wilderness, as an expression of optimism for salvation from it.
78:32: Then the Almighty explained this wilderness, saying: 32- Gardens and grapes. Their accusative case is that they are a substitute for the wilderness, a substitute of inclusion, or a substitute for each of each, by way of exaggeration, by making these things themselves a wilderness. It is possible for the accusative case to be by implying I mean. And if the wilderness is in the sense of victory, then an omitted complement is estimated: that is, the victory of gardens, which is the plural of garden: which is the enclosed orchard, and grapes are the plural of grapes: that is, grape vines.
78:33: 33- And young maidens of equal age. Young maidens are the plural of Ka'bah, which means a well-proportioned woman. It is said: The slave girl became well-proportioned, and she sighed, meaning that they are young women whose breasts have become well-proportioned and have become like heels in their chests. Ad-Dahhak said: Young maidens are virgins. Qays ibn Asim said: How many noble horses have we kept, and how many maidens who did not know what misery is? Omar bin Abi Rabia said: And I was wronged, not because I feared, but because I was three virgins and a press And peers: those of equal age. This has been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah.
78:34: 34- And a full cup meaning brimming. Al-Hasan and Qatada ibn Zayd said: meaning brimming and overflowing. It is said, I filled the cup meaning I overflowed it. From this comes the poet’s saying: Shall I not drink from the pure water that the cupbearer gave you from its pure water in your full cup? Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: Dahaqan means consecutive, one after the other. Zaid bin Aslam said: Dahaqan means clear. What is meant by kas is the well-known vessel, and it is not called a kas unless it contains a drink.
78:35: 35- They will hear therein no idle talk or lying meaning they will not hear in Paradise any idle talk, which is false speech, nor lying: meaning they will not lie to one another. The majority read kadhdhban with a shaddah, but Al-Kisa'i read it here with a tafsir and agreed with the group on the shaddah in his statement: And they denied Our signs as a liar which was mentioned earlier in this surah to clearly state his action there. We have already mentioned the disagreement over kadhdhban, is it from the verbal nouns of tafa'il or mufa'ala?
78:36: 36- A reward from your Lord meaning He rewarded them with what was mentioned above as a reward. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is He rewarded them with a reward, and so is giving meaning He gave them a gift accountably. Abu Ubaidah said: sufficient. Ibn Qutaybah said: abundant. It is said I considered so-and-so: meaning I gave him a lot of gifts, and from this is the saying of the poet: We give the newborn to the neighborhood if he is hungry, and we consider him to be hungry if he is not hungry. Ibn Qutaybah said: We give him until he says ‘sufficient for me’. Al-Zajjaj said: Hisab means what is enough for them. Al-Akhfash said: It is said, I think that such and such means it is enough for me. Al-Kalbi said: He held them to account and gave them ten for the good deed. Mujahid said: Hisab means measure meaning that what is due to him in the promise of the Lord, the Most High, is determined. He promised ten for the good deed, and He promised to a people seven hundred times that, and He promised to a people a reward that has no end or measure, as in His statement: Only the patient will be given their reward in full, without account. Abu Hashim read Hisab with a fatha on the ha’ and a shaddah on the seen, meaning sufficiency. Al-Asma’i said: The Arabs say, Hasabat a man with a shaddah, if you honored him. And from this is the saying of the poet: If his guest comes to him, he thinks he is Ibn Abbas read Hassan with the letter nun.
78:37: 37- Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Gracious. Ibn Mas`ud, Nafi`, Abu `Amr, Ibn Kathir, Zayd on the authority of Ya`qub, and al-Mufaddal on the authority of `Asim read Lord and the Most Gracious in the nominative case, with Lord being the subject and the Most Gracious being its predicate, or with Lord being the predicate of an implied subject, meaning He is Lord, and the Most Gracious is His attribute, and they do not possess is the predicate of Lord, or with Lord being the subject, and they do not possess being the predicate of the second subject, and the sentence being the predicate of the first subject. Ya`qub, in a narration from him, and Ibn `Amir and `Asim, in a narration from him, read them in the genitive case, with Lord being a substitute for your Lord, and the Most Gracious being its attribute. Ibn Abbas, Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read the verse with the first in the genitive case as a substitute, and the second in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: i.e. He is the Most Gracious. Abu Ubaidah preferred this reading and said: This is the most just reading. He lowered Lord because of His closeness to your Lord, so it is an attribute of Him, and raised the Most Gracious because of His distance from Him, as a new sentence. Its predicate is they do not possess any speech from Him meaning they do not possess the right to ask except for what He has given them permission. Al-Kisa’i said: they do not possess any speech from Him regarding intercession except with His permission. It was also said that speech means speech, i.e. they do not possess the right to address the Lord, glory be to Him, except with His permission. The evidence for this is no soul speaks except with His permission. It was also said that he meant the disbelievers, while the believers intercede. This sentence may be in the accusative case as a state, as explained above, or it may be a new sentence confirming what Lordship conveys of greatness and pride.
78:39: And the reference in His saying: 39- That is to the Day of their resurrection in that state, and it is a subject and its predicate is Today it is lawful meaning the existing, real, and realized So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way of return meaning a reference to which he returns through righteous deeds, because if he does good, it brings him closer to God, and if he does evil, it distances him from Him, and the meaning of to his Lord is to the reward of his Lord. Qatada said: A way of return: a path.
78:40: Then God increased the fear of the disbelievers by saying: 40- Indeed, We have warned you of an imminent torment, meaning the torment in the Hereafter, and everything that is coming is imminent. Similar to this is His statement: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof. This is what Al-Kalbi and others said. Qatada said: It is the torment of this world because it is the closer of the two torments. Muqatil said: It is the killing of Quraysh at Badr, and the first is more appropriate because of His statement: The Day a man will see what his hands have put forth, for the adverbial phrase is either a substitute for torment or an adverbial phrase for an implied noun that is a description of it: i.e. an existing torment. The Day a man will see means he will see what he has put forth of good or evil. Ma is a relative pronoun or an interrogative. Al-Hasan said: “The person here is the believer, meaning he finds work for himself. As for the disbeliever, he does not find work for himself and wishes to be dust. It was said that what is meant by this is the disbeliever in general. It was also said that it refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, but the first is more appropriate, because of the statement: “And the disbeliever will say, ‘Oh, I wish I were dust!’” The disbeliever is in contrast to the person, and what is meant is the disbeliever who wishes to be dust because of what he sees of the types of torment that God has prepared for him. The meaning is that he wishes that he was dust in this world and was not created, or dust on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that what is meant by the disbeliever is either ignorance, or Awwab Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi, or Iblis. The first is more appropriate due to the general meaning of the wording, and the specific reason does not contradict it, as was mentioned more than once.” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, for the righteous is attainment, he said: a place of refuge. And full-breasted maidens, he said: breasts, of equal age, he said: levels. And a full cup, he said: full. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And a full cup, he said: it is the full, replete, and continuous one. You may have heard Al-Abbas say, O boy, give us a drink and pour it over for us. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, dahaqan, he said: Darakkan. Abd bin Hamid also narrated on his authority, he said: If there is wine in it, then it is not a cup. Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on his authority that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The Spirit is an army from among the soldiers of God. They are not angels. They have heads, hands, and feet. Then he recited, ‘The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in ranks,’ and said, ‘These are an army and those are an army.’” Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, The Day the Spirit will stand, and said, He is an angel who is among the greatest angels in creation. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said, “The Spirit is in the fourth heaven, and it is greater than the heavens and mountains, and the angels. It glorifies God twelve thousand times every day. From each glorification, God creates an angel from among the angels who will come on the Day of Resurrection in a single row.” Abu Al-Shaykh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Gabriel will stand on the Day of Resurrection before the Almighty, his limbs trembling with fear of God’s punishment. He will say: ‘Glory be to You! There is no god but You! We have not worshipped You as You should be worshipped.’ The distance between his shoulders will be like the distance between the east and the west. Have you not heard the statement of God, ‘The Day the spirit and the angels will stand in rows?’” Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on his authority regarding his statement, The Day the spirit will stand, that he means when the souls of the people will stand from the angels between the two blasts, before the souls are returned to the bodies. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on his authority, and he said correctly, that he said: There is no god but God. Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Baath wa al-Nushur on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: All of creation will be gathered on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:the beasts, the animals, the birds, and everything else. The punishment of God will be so severe that even the horned ones will be taken from the horned ones. Then He will say: Become dust. That is when the unbeliever will say: Oh, I wish I were dust.
79:1: It is called Surat Al-Sahira. It has forty-five verses, and some say forty-six verses. It is a Meccan surah without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat An-Nazi'at was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. God Almighty swears by these things that He mentioned, which are the angels who extract the souls of the servants from their bodies as the one who extracts the bow extracts it, reaching its full potential. And likewise what is meant by the active ones, the swimmers, the forerunners, and the departing ones: meaning the angels. The conjunction with the union of all is to place the descriptive difference in the position of the intrinsic difference, as in the poet’s saying: To the venerable king, son of the hero, and lion of the battalion in the crowded This is the saying of the majority of the Companions, the Followers, and those who came after them. Al-Suddi said: 1- An-Nazi’at are the souls when they are drowned in the chests. Mujahid said: It is death that pulls the soul. Qatada said: It is the stars that are pulled from one horizon to another, from their saying: Naza’a ilaihi if he went, or from their saying Naza’at bil-Habl meaning that they set and disappear and rise from another horizon. Abu Ubaidah, Al-Akhfash, and Ibn Kaysan said the same. Ata’ and Ikrimah said: An-Nazi’at are bows that are pulled out with arrows, and immersing the nazi’ in the bow means that it is stretched to the maximum extent until it reaches the blade. Yahya bin Salam said: It pulls out the grass and scatters. It was said that by the pullers he meant the raiding archers. The accusative of gharaqan is because it is a verbal noun with the deletion of the extra letters: meaning drowning. The accusative for it is what precedes it because it meets it in meaning: meaning drowning in the conflict where it pulls them out from the ends of the bodies, or in the state: meaning those with drowning. It is said that he drowned in something, he drowns in it: if he penetrated it and reached his limit.
79:2: 2- The meaning of "and the active ones" is that they activate the souls, i.e. they extract them from the bodies, as the rope is activated from the camel's hand, if it is loosened, and the man activates the bucket from the well, if he takes it out. Active means to pull quickly, and from this comes the knot that is easy to untie. Abu Zaid said: I activated the rope, I activated it actively, I tied it, and I loosened it, and I extended the rope, i.e. I extended it. Al-Farra' said: He recited the rope, i.e. he loosened and activated, i.e. he tied the rope to his hands. Al-Asma'i said: A well that is active, i.e. one with a low bottom, from which the bucket comes out with one pull, and a well that is active, i.e. one from which the bucket does not come out until it is very active. Mujahid said: It is death that activates the human soul. Al-Suddi said: It is the souls when they are active from the feet. Ikrimah and Ata’ said: They are the shackles that incite arrows. Qatada, Al-Hasan and Al-Akhfash said: They are the stars that move from horizon to horizon, meaning they go. It is said in As-Sahah: And the Nashihat Nashitan: meaning the stars from one constellation to another like a bull that moves from one country to another, and worries incite their owner. Abu Ubaidah and Qatadah said: They are the wild beasts when they move from one country to another. It is said that the Nashihat are for the souls of the believers, and the Nazihat are for the souls of the disbelievers, because they gently pull the soul of the believer and violently pull the soul of the disbeliever. His saying: Nashitan is a verbal noun, and so are sabahan and sabah.
79:3: 3- "And the swimming ones" are the angels swimming in the bodies to extract the soul as a diver swims in the sea to extract something from it. Mujahid and Abu Saleh said: They are the angels who descend from the sky, hurrying to the command of God, as a noble horse is called a swimming one if it runs quickly. Mujahid also said: The swimming ones are death swimming in the souls of the children of Adam. It was said that they are the swimming horses in conquest, and from this is the saying of Antarah: Horses learn when they swim in the pools of death Qatada and Al-Hasan said: They are the stars swimming in their orbits, as in His statement: And each in an orbit floats. Ata’ said: They are the ships swimming in the water. It was said that they are the souls of the believers swimming out of longing for God.
79:4: 4- Those who precede in precedence are the angels according to the majority opinion as mentioned above. Masruq and Mujahid said: The angels precede the devils in revelation to the prophets. Abu Ruq said: They are the angels who preceded the son of Adam in goodness and righteous deeds, and something similar was narrated from Mujahid. Muqatil said: They precede the souls of the believers to Paradise. Al-Rabi’ said: They are the souls of the believers who precede the angels out of longing for God. Mujahid also said: It is death that precedes man. Qatada, Al-Hasan and Muammar said: They are the stars, some of which precede others in walking. Ata’ said: They are the horses that precede in jihad. It was said that they are the souls that precede the bodies to Paradise or Hell. Al-Jurjani said: The conjunction of those who preceded with the letter fa’ is because they are caused by the one before it, meaning if you had said he stood up and he went with the letter waw, the standing would not have been a cause of the going.
79:5: Al-Wahidi said: This is not consistent with his statement: 5- "those who manage an affair" because it is far-fetched to make precedence a cause for management. Al-Razi said: It is possible to respond to what Al-Wahidi said: It was commanded to swim, so it raced, so it managed what it was commanded to manage. Thus, these are actions that are connected to each other, like his statement: Zaid spoke, so he went. And when they raced in acts of obedience and hastened to them, their trustworthiness became apparent, so management was delegated to them. The response to this is that precedence is not a cause of management, like swimming being the cause of precedence and standing being the cause of going. Mere connection does not necessitate causality and being caused. It is better to say that the conjunction with "fa in those who manage an affair is similar to what preceded it, in conjunction with fa", and does not require a point as what preceded it needed, because the point is only required for the difference between what comes after and what comes before, not for its conformity and agreement with it. "those who manage an affair" Al-Qushayri said: They agreed that what is meant here are the angels. Al-Mawardi said: There are two opinions: One of them is the angels, which is the opinion of the majority. The second is that they are the seven planets, as narrated by Khalid bin Ma'dan from Muadh bin Jabal. There are two views on their management of affairs: One is managing their rising and setting. The second is managing the conditions He has decreed for them. The meaning of the angels' management of affairs is that they descend with what is lawful and what is unlawful and their details. The doer of management in reality is God, the Almighty, but when the angels descend with it, they were described with it. It was said that when the angels were commanded to manage the people of the earth in the winds, rain, and other things, they were called managers. Abdur-Rahman bin Sabat said: The management of the affairs of this world is to four angels: Gabriel, Michael, Azrael, and Israfil. Gabriel is in charge of the winds and the armies, Michael is in charge of the rain and plants, Azrael is in charge of taking souls, and Israfil descends with the matter. The answer to the oath by these matters by which God swore is omitted: i.e., by the extractors, and so on and so forth, that you will be resurrected. Al-Farra' said: "It was omitted because the listeners would know it, and this is indicated by his statement, 'Will we then be decayed bones?' It was also said that the answer to the oath is his statement, 'Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears,' meaning that on the Day of Resurrection, the mention of Moses and Pharaoh is a lesson for whoever fears. Ibn al-Anbari said: This is ugly because the conversation between them was prolonged. It was also said that the answer to the oath is, 'Has the story of Moses reached you?' because the meaning is, 'It has reached you.' This is very weak. It was also said that the answer is...
79:6: 6- "The Day the Earthshakes" meaning the Day the Earthshakes will be followed by the subsequent one. Al-Sijistani said: This could be an example of advancing or delaying, as if he said: So they are about to meet Al-Sahira and An-Nazi'at. Ibn Al-Anbari said: This is a mistake because the letter "fa" does not begin a sentence, and the first is more appropriate. "The Day the Earthshakes means the accusative of this circumstance as a response to the oath, or by implying remember, and the trembling is the disturbed, it is said rajaf yarjaf" if it is agitated, and what is meant here is the great shout that has hesitation and disturbance like thunder, and it is the first blast at which all creation dies, and the subsequent one is the second blast that will be at the resurrection, and it is called subsequent because it follows the first blast, this is what the majority of commentators said. Ibn Zayd said: The trembling is the earth, and the subsequent one is the hour. Mujahid said: The earthquake is followed by the shout. It has been said that the trembling is the disturbance of the earth and the earthquake is the following. The origin of the trembling is movement, and what is meant here is not just movement, rather the trembling here is taken from their saying: The thunder trembled, trembling, trembling and trembling: if its sound appeared, and from this the arajif were named because of the disturbance of sounds in them and the appearance of sounds in them, and from this the poet said: You threaten me with rumors, you son of a bitch, while rumors contain meanness and cowardice.
79:7: Location 7 - The second blast will follow it is the accusative case as a state of the trembling one, and the meaning is: You will be resurrected on the day of the first blast while the second blast follows it.
79:8: 8- On that Day, hearts will be trembling. Hearts is the subject, and on that Day is the subject of trembling, and trembling is an adjective of hearts.
79:9: And sentence 9- "Their eyes will be humbled" is report of hearts and the trembling is the agitated and anxious when they witness the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. The majority of commentators said: meaning fearful and terrified. Al-Suddi said: Moving from their places, similar to "when the hearts are at the throats." Al-Mu'arraj said: Agitated and agitated. Al-Mubarrad said: Turbulent, it is said that the heart dries up and throbbed: if it fluttered as it is said it must be rushed and agitated, and ijaf: is a quick walk, so the origin of wajeef is the agitation of the heart, and from it is the saying of Qays ibn al-Khatim: The Bani Jahjabi and their people, our livers will dry up because of them Their eyes will be humbled: meaning the eyes of their owners. The noun was omitted, and humbled means submissive. What is meant is that humiliation and submission will appear on them when they witness the horrors of the Day of Resurrection, like His statement, humbled by humiliation. Ata’ said: He means the eyes of those who died as non-Muslims. This is indicated by the fact that the context is about those who deny the resurrection.
79:10: 10- They say, ‘Shall we indeed be returned to the grave?’ This is a narration of what those who deny the resurrection say when it is said to them that you will be resurrected: that is, shall we be returned to our first state and the beginning of our affair, so that we become alive after our death. It is said that someone returned to his grave: that is, he returned from where he came. The grave among the Arabs is a name for the beginning of something and the beginning of an affair, and from this is their saying that someone returned on his grave: that is, on the road from which he came. And it is said that the people fought at the grave: that is, when they first met. And the road from which he came was called a grave because of his influence on it by walking on it, so it is a grave in the sense of dug up. And from this is the saying of the poet: Excavating on baldness and gray hair, God forbid, is such foolishness and shame That is, shall I return to what I was like in my youth in terms of flirting after my gray hair and baldness? It was said that the word hafir means urgent, and the meaning is: We will be returned to the world. It was said that the word hafir means the land in which their graves are dug, and from this is the poet’s saying: I swear I will not forget you, so know that until people return to the grave Meaning: We will be returned to our graves alive. This is what Al-Khalil and Al-Farra’ said, and Mujahid also said the same. Ibn Zayd said: The hole is the fire, and he provided evidence for this with his statement: That then will be a losing end. The majority of scholars read it as in the hole, while Abu Haywah read it as in the pit.
79:11: 11- "Shall we, when we are decayed bones?" That is, worn out and crumbling. It is said that the bone decays nakhra if it wears out, and this is an emphasis on the denial of al-Qiyamah 75:that is, how will we be brought back to life and resurrected if we are decayed bones? The agent in "if is implied and indicated by mardu'dun": that is, will we, when we are decayed bones, be brought back and resurrected despite them being the furthest thing from life? The majority read it as "nakhra, while Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr read it as nakhra". Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading, while Al-Farra', Ibn Jarir, and Abu Mu'adh Al-Nahwi preferred the second reading. Abu Amr Ibn Al-Ala' said: The decaying one is the one that has not decayed yet: that is, it has not worn out and will inevitably decay. It was said that they are one and the same. The Arabs say: The thing decayed, so it is nakhra and nakhra, and greed, so it is greedy and greedy, and so on. Al-Akhfash said: They are both languages, whichever you read is good. The poet said: The old man who was obese and crawling on a crooked path with nodules remained there. Meaning on crooked legs. It was also said that the nakhrah is the one whose edges were eaten away and only the middle remained, and the nakhrah is the one that was completely rotten. Mujahid said that nakhrah means thrown down as in his saying: crumbs. It was read if we were and when we were with the question and without it.
79:12: Then God, the Almighty, mentioned another statement they made, saying: 12- They said, ‘That then is a losing return.’ That is, a return that is a loss because of the loss that befalls its owners. The meaning is that they said, If we are sent back after death, we will surely lose because of what Muhammad says that will befall us after death. It was said that the meaning of losing is false, meaning it will not happen. This is what Al-Hasan and others said. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said, A losing return for whoever denies it. Qatadah and Muhammad bin Ka’b said, That is, if we are sent back after death, we will surely lose in the Fire. They only said this because they were threatened with the Fire. The return means the return, and the plural is karat.
79:13: And His statement: 13- "It is only a single blast" is an explanation of what is indicated by what preceded regarding their ruling out the resurrection of rotten bones and the revival of the dead. The meaning is: Do not rule that out, for it is only a single blast, and that was the revival and the resurrection. What is meant by the blast is the shout, which is the second blast with which the resurrection will take place. It was said that the pronoun in His statement: It is only a single blast refers to the synonym previously mentioned.
79:14: 14- "Then they will be in the Sahirah" meaning, then the creatures who had died and been buried will be alive on the face of the earth. Al-Wahidi said: What is meant by the Sahirah is the face of the earth, and this is the apparent meaning according to everyone. Al-Farra' said: It was given this name because animals sleep and stay awake in it, and it was said because they stay awake in its desert out of fear of it, so it was given this name. From this comes the saying of Abu Kathir Al-Hudhali: They respond awake as if her warmth and her sorrow were the curtains of a dark night. And the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: And in it is the meat of Sahara, and the sea, and what they eat therein is their abode. He wants the meat of an animal of a sleepless land. It was said in As-Sahah: As-Sahiyah is the face of the earth, and from it is His statement: Then they are in As-Sahiyah. He said: As-Sahiyah is a white land, and it was said that it is a land of silver in which God the Almighty was not disobeyed, and it was said that As-Sahiyah is the seventh land that God the Almighty will bring and hold creation accountable for it. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: As-Sahiyah is the land of Ash-Sham. Qatada said: It is Hell, meaning that these disbelievers are in Hell, and it is only called As-Sahiyah because they do not sleep in it due to the continuity of their torment.
79:15: And the sentence 15 - Has there come to you the story of Moses? is a new sentence intended to console the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for his people's denial and that they will be afflicted with the same as those who came before them who were stronger than them. The meaning of Has there come to you is: It has come to you and reached you. This is on the assumption that he heard from the stories of Pharaoh and Moses what he knows of their story. And on the assumption that this is the first thing that was revealed to him concerning them, then the meaning is a question: Has his story come to you? I will tell you about it.
79:16: 16- When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa The circumstance is related to the hadith La ataak due to the difference in their times. The story of Moses and Pharaoh has already been mentioned in more than one place, but it is not sufficient.
