The difference of opinion among the reciters regarding Tuwa in Surah Taha has already been mentioned. The sacred valley: the blessed and purified. Al-Farra' said: Tuwa is a valley between Medina and Egypt. He said: It is modified from Taw, just as Umar modified it from Amir. He said: I prefer the declension, as I did not find an equivalent in the modified word. It was said that Tuwa means O man in Hebrew, so it is as if it was said O man, go. It was also said that the meaning is: The sacred valley was blessed twice, but the first is better. The explanation of this has already been mentioned.
79:17: 17- Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. It was said that it is based on the estimation of the statement, and it was said that it is an explanation of the call: that is, he called him with a call that is his saying, Go. And it was said that it is based on the deletion of the explanatory that, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Masoud that I go, because in the call there is the meaning of a statement, and the phrase for he has transgressed is an explanation of the command or the obligation to comply: that is, he exceeded the limit in disobedience, arrogance, and disbelief in God.
79:18: 18- Say to him Would you like to be purified? That is, his saying after you reach him, Would you like to be purified? which is to purify yourself from polytheism? Its root is tatazka, so one of the two ta's was deleted. The majority read tazakka with a light pronunciation. Nafi' and Ibn Kathir read it with a shaddah on the zay, assimilating the ta' into the zay. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' said that the meaning of the light pronunciation is you will be a pure believer, and the meaning of the shaddah reading is charity. In the speech there is an implied subject related to to, and the estimation is: Do you have a desire, or do you have a direction, or do you have a way to purification? Similar to this is their saying, Do you want to do good? They mean, do you have a desire for good? And from this is the saying of the poet: Would you like me to do it for you? I know what makes the narrator so tired.
79:19: 19- And I guide you to your Lord so that you may fear Him meaning I guide you to worship Him and to believe in His Oneness so that you may fear His punishment. The fa is to link fear to guidance, because fear only comes from a guided and righteous person.
79:20: 20- So he showed him the greatest sign. This fa is the eloquent one because it reveals omitted speech, meaning that he went and said to him what he said of what God had related in more than one place, and he answered him with what he answered until he said: If you have brought a sign, then bring it. At that point, he showed him the greatest sign. There is disagreement about what the greatest verse is. Some say it is the staff, some say it is his hand, some say it is the splitting of the sea, and some say it is all of the nine verses he brought.
79:21: 21- So he denied and disobeyed. That is, when he showed him the great sign, he denied Moses and what he brought and disobeyed God Almighty and did not obey Him.
79:22: 22- Then he turned away means he turned away and turned away from the faith. He strives means he spreads corruption on earth and strives to oppose what Moses brought. It was also said that he turned away fleeing from the snake, striving out of fear of it. Al-Razi said: The meaning of he turned away is he approached, striving, just as one says he approached something, meaning he began to do such-and-such. So he used he turned away instead of he approached so that it would not be described as approaching.
79:23: 23- So he gathered meaning he gathered his soldiers to fight and battle, or he gathered the magicians to oppose, or he gathered the people to attend to witness what would happen, or he gathered them to prevent him from the snake. Then he called out, saying, ‘I am your Lord, the Most High.’ Meaning he said to them in a loud voice, or he ordered someone to call out this statement.
79:24: The meaning of 24- I am your highest lord is that there is no lord above me. Ata' said: He had made small idols for them and commanded them to worship them and said: I am the lord of your idols. It was also said that by being their lord he meant that he was their leader and their master. The first is more appropriate because of what He said in another verse: I know of no god for you other than me.
79:25: 25- So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. Punishment is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun: meaning He seized him with a punishment, or it is a verbal noun for a deleted verb: meaning God seized him and punished him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first, or a verbal noun emphasizing the meaning of the sentence. What is meant by the punishment of the Hereafter is the torment of the Fire, and the punishment of the first is the torment of this world by drowning. Mujahid said: The torment of the beginning of his life and the end of it. Qatada said: The Hereafter is His statement, I am your highest lord, and the first is His denial of Moses. It was said that the Hereafter is His statement, I am your highest lord, and the first is His statement, I did not know of any god for you other than Me, and there were forty years between the two words. It is permissible for punishment to be in the accusative case as an object for it: meaning God seized him as a punishment. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case by removing the preposition: meaning with a punishment. Al-Zajjaj preferred that it is a confirmed verbal noun. He said: Because the meaning of God seized him is: God punished him, so it was taken out of its meaning, not its wording. Al-Farra’ said: That is, God took him as a punishment, meaning as a punishment. And punishment is the name for what is made a punishment for others, that is, a penalty for them. It is said that someone punished someone, meaning he punished him. The root of the word is from refusal, and from this comes refusal to take an oath, and refusal is a restriction.
79:26: 26- Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears. That is, what is mentioned about the story of Pharaoh and what was done to him is a great lesson for whoever fears God and is pious to Him, and is afraid of His punishment and is wary of His wrath. Saeed bin Mansour and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, regarding his statement, {And those who pull out violently}, he said: They are the angels who pull out the souls of the disbelievers. {And those who snatch them out energetically}, he said: They are the angels who pull out the souls of the disbelievers between the nails and the skin until they extract them. {And those who swim in glide}, they are the angels who swim with the souls of the believers between the heaven and the earth. {And those who race in race}, they are the angels who outpace each other with the souls of the believers to God. {And those who manage the affair}, they are the angels who manage the affairs of the servants from year to year. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, {And those who pull out violently}, he said: They are the souls of the disbelievers, they are pulled out, then revived, then drowned in the Fire. Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it on his authority, {And those who pull out violently * And those who snatch them out energetically}, he said: Death. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, And those who snatch forth drowningly, he said: The angels who take the souls of the disbelievers until His saying, And those who swim glide freely, he said: The angels. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Mu`adh ibn Jabal, he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me: "Do not tear people apart, lest the dogs of Hell tear you apart. God said: "And those who snatch forth vigorously," do you know what that is? I said: O Prophet of God, what is that? He said: Dogs in Hell that snatch up flesh and bones." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that Ibn al-Kawwa` asked him about those who manage the affairs, he said: They are the angels who manage the remembrance of the Most Gracious and His command. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the mention of death on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: those who manage the affairs are angels who are with the Angel of Death, attending to the dead when their souls are taken. Some of them ascend with the spirit, some of them say Ameen to the supplication, and some of them seek forgiveness for the dead until the funeral prayer is performed over him and he is lowered into his grave. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, On the Day the Great Earthquake trembles, he said: The first blast, Followed by the second blast, he said: The second blast, Hearts that Day will be trembling, he said: Fearful, Will we then be returned to the Hereafter? he said: Life. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b who said: “When a quarter of the night had passed, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would get up and say: O people, remember God. The Great Earthquake has come, followed by the second. Death has come with what is in it.” Abu Al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The earth will shake violently and its people will be shaken, and it is about which God says, ‘On the Day the Great Earthquake trembles, followed by the second. ’ He said: Like a ship in the sea, tossed with its people, like a lamp suspended from its edges.” Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Hearts that Day will be trembling, he said: Fearful and moving. And Abd bin Hamid narrated on his authority: Shall we indeed be returned to the grave? He said: A new creation. Abu Ubaid narrated in his book, Fada’il, and Ibn al-Anbari in Al-Waqf wa al-Ibtida, and Abd bin Hamid, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that he was asked about his statement: Then they are about to attack the one who watches over them, so he said: The one who watches over them is the face of the earth. In another version he said: The entire earth is watching over them. Do you not see the words of the poet: Sea fishing and night fishing Al-Bayhaqi also narrated in Al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat from him, Would you like to be purified? He said: Would you like to say, There is no god but God. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, Then God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: His statement, I am your highest Lord. The first one said: His statement, I have not known of any god for you other than Me. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abdullah bin Amr, who said: There were forty years between his two statements.
79:27: His statement: 27- Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? That is, is your creation after death and resurrection more difficult in your opinion and estimation, or the creation of the heaven? The address is to the disbelievers of Mecca, and the purpose is to rebuke and reprimand them, because the One who was able to create the heaven, which has this enormous mass and contains the wonders of creation and marvels of power that are clear to observers, how could He be unable to restore bodies that He caused to die after He created them the first time? Similar to this is His statement, the Most High: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. And His statement: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Then He, the Most High, explained how He created the heaven, saying: He constructed it * He raised its ceiling and proportioned it. That is, He made it like a building raised above the earth, and He raised its ceiling: that is, its top in the air.
79:28: His saying: 28- raised its thickness is an explanation of the building. It is said samakat something: meaning you raised it in the air. And samaq something means it rose. Al-Farra’ said: Everything that carries something from a building or other is a thickness. A masmuk building and a samak hump mean high. And samaukat means the heavens. And from this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: He who made the sky high built for us a house whose pillars are stronger and taller Al-Baghawi said: He raised its ceiling means its roof. Al-Kisa’i, Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj said: The discussion ended with His statement: The mother of the sky He built it because it is related to the sky, and the meaning is: The mother of the sky that He built, so He omitted which, and such omission is permissible. The meaning of He proportioned it is that He made it level in creation and proportionate in form, with no unevenness, crookedness, cracks or fissures in it.
79:29: 29- And He covered its night Ghatash means darkness: i.e. He made it pitch black. It is said that the night covered and God covered it, just as it is said that the night was dark and God made it pitch black. A man who is aghtash and a woman who is ghatash are not guided. Al-Raghib said: Its origin is from aghtash, which is the one who has blindness in his eye, and from it is a desert that is ghatash in which one cannot find one's way, and taghātash means blindness. Al-A'sha said: At night, the mob covers the desert, and the sound of its drivers comforts me. And he said: And he risked their lives and deceived them Meaning, the darkness of night enveloped them. He added the night to the sky because night occurs with the setting of the sun, and the sun is added to the sky. And brought forth its morning light, meaning He made its bright day appear with the light of the sun. He expressed the day with the morning light because it is the most honorable and pleasant of its times. He added it to the sky because it appears with the appearance of the sun, and it is related to the sky.
79:30: 30- And the earth after that He spread it out meaning after creating the heaven. The meaning of dahā is to extend it. This indicates that the creation of the earth came after the creation of the heaven. There is no contradiction between this verse and what came before in Surat Fussilat, where He said: Then He directed Himself to the heaven. Rather, the plural is that He, glory be to Him, created the earth first, not rolled out, then He created the heaven, then He spread it out to the earth. We have already discussed this in detail there, and we have also discussed this at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, when He said: It is He who created for you all that is on the earth. Some of the people of knowledge have mentioned that ba’d means with, as in His statement: He became an adulterer after that. It has also been said that ba’d means before, as in His statement: And We had already written in the Psalms after the remembrance, meaning before the remembrance. The plural we have mentioned is more appropriate, and it is the statement of Ibn Abbas and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it. It is said that I spread something out, adhawwa, meaning I extended it. The nest of an ostrich is also called adha because it is spread out on the earth. Al-Mubarrad recited: He rolled it out, and when he saw it settled on the water, he set mountains on it. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: And He spread out the creation in it when He spread it out, and they understood its inhabitants until the call came. Zaid bin Amr bin Nufail said: I surrendered my face to the One to whom the earth surrendered, carrying heavy rocks. He rolled it out, and when it was level, He strengthened it with His hands and fixed mountains on it. The majority read the land in the accusative case as an occupation, while Al-Hasan, Amr ibn Maymun, Ibn Abi Ubla, Abu Haywah, Abu Al-Samak, Amr ibn Ubayd, and Nasr ibn Asim read it in the nominative case as an initial case.
79:31: 31- He brought forth from it its water and its pasture meaning He caused rivers, seas and springs to gush forth from the earth and brought forth from it its pasture: meaning the plants that graze. Its pasture is a verbal noun with a mim: meaning its grazing, and it is originally the place of grazing. The sentence is either a statement and an explanation of its spreading out, because habitation is not achieved by mere expansion, rather one must settle the matter of livelihood in terms of food and drink. Or it is in the accusative case as a state.
79:32: 32- And the mountains He has fixed firmly meaning He has fixed them firmly in the earth and made them like pegs for the earth to be firm and stable and not to shake with its people. The majority of scholars have read the mountains in the accusative case as an active participle. Al-Hasan, Amr ibn Maymun, Abu Haywah, Abu as-Samaka, Amr ibn Ubayd and Nasr ibn Asim have read it in the nominative case as an introductory participle. It has also been said that perhaps the reason for mentioning the bringing forth of water and pasture before sending down the mountains, with the anchoring coming before it, is to emphasize the matter of food and drink.
79:33: 33- For your enjoyment and your livestock meaning a benefit for you and your livestock of cows, camels and sheep. The word for enjoyment is in the accusative case as a source: meaning He provided you with enjoyment from that, or it is a source from a different wording, because His statement: He brought forth from it its water and its pasture means He provided enjoyment from that, or as an object for it: meaning He did that for the sake of enjoyment. He only said: For you and your livestock because the benefit of what was mentioned of the rolling and bringing forth the water and pasture is for them and their livestock, and pasture includes what people and animals eat.
79:34: 34- Then when the Greatest Calamity comes meaning the greatest disaster that looms over all other calamities. Al-Hasan and others said: It is the second Trumpet Blast. Ad-Dahhak and others said: It is the Day of Resurrection. It was called thus because it looms over everything due to its great horror. Al-Mubarrad said: The Greatest Calamity among the Arabs is the uncontrollable calamity. I think it was taken from their saying: The horse ran tamim tamim meaning it exhausted its effort in running, or The water filled meaning it filled the entire river. Another said: It is from the word tamam al-sail meaning it buried the well, and tamming means burying. Mujahid and others said: The Greatest Calamity is that which delivers the people of Paradise to Paradise and the people of Hell to Hell. The fa indicates the order of what comes after it based on what came before it. The answer to the question "If it is said that it is His statement: "But as for he who transgressed", and it was said that it was omitted: meaning that the matter is thus, or they witnessed, or knew, or the people of Hell were admitted to Hell and the people of Paradise to Paradise.
79:35: Abu al-Baqa' said: The factor in it is its answer, and it is the meaning of 35- The Day when man remembers because it is accusative due to an implied verb: I mean the Day when he remembers, or the Day when he remembers will be such and such. It was said that the adverbial phrase is a substitute for if, and it was said that it is a substitute for the greater catastrophe. The meaning of man remembering what he strove for is that he remembers what he did of good or evil, because he sees it recorded in his books of deeds. Ma is a verbal noun or a relative pronoun.
79:36: 36- And Hellfire will be made manifest to whoever sees is in apposition to came, and the meaning of made manifest is: made manifest in a way that is not hidden from anyone. Muqatil said: Its cover will be removed so that people can see it. It was also said, For whoever sees from the disbelievers, not from the believers. What appears is that it will be made manifest to everyone who sees. As for the believer, he will know by seeing it the extent of God’s blessing upon him by being safe from it. As for the disbeliever, his grief will increase upon grief and his regret will increase upon his regret. The majority of scholars read For whoever sees with a lower ta’a, while Aisha, Malik ibn Dinar, Ikrimah, and Zayd ibn Ali read it with a higher ta’a, meaning for whoever sees Hellfire, or for whoever you see, O Muhammad. Ibn Mas’ud read For whoever sees with the past tense.
79:37: 37- But as for he who transgressed meaning he exceeded the limit in disbelief and sins.
79:38: 38- And he preferred the life of this world meaning he preferred it over the Hereafter and did not prepare for it or do its deeds.
79:39: 39- For Hell is his abode meaning his home, and the definite article replaces the noun it is added to, and the meaning is: it is his home in which he resides and his abode to which he takes refuge and nothing else.
79:40: Then he mentioned the second of the two categories, saying: 40- But as for he who feared the position of his Lord, meaning he feared his position before his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Rabi’ said: The position on the Day of Reckoning. Qatadah said: He is saying that God, the Almighty, has a position that the believers fear. Mujahid said: It is his fear of God, the Almighty, in this world when committing a sin, so he desists from it. Similar to His statement: For he who feared the position of his Lord are two Gardens, but the first is more appropriate. And he forbade the soul from desire, meaning he restrained it from inclining toward the sins and forbidden things that it desires. Muqatil said: It is the man who intends to commit a sin, then he remembers his position for reckoning, so he abandons it.
79:41: 41- For Paradise is the abode meaning the home in which he resides and the place to which he takes refuge, and nothing else. 42- “They ask you about the Hour: when will it arrive?” That is, when will it occur and come to pass. Al-Farra’ said: meaning when it will arrive at its destination, like the anchorage of a ship. Abu Ubaidah said: The anchorage of a ship is when it reaches its destination. The meaning is: They ask you about the Hour: when will [God] establish it? This has already been explained in Surat Al-A’raf.
79:43: 43- What do you have to do with its remembrance? That is, what do you have to do with the remembrance of the Resurrection and the questioning about it, O Muhammad? The meaning is: You have no knowledge of it or its remembrance, only God Almighty knows it. This is a denial and response to the polytheists’ question about it: That is, what do you have to do with it that they ask you about it and you do not know it.
79:44: 44- To your Lord is its destination meaning the destination of its knowledge, for no one else has knowledge of it. This is like His saying: Say, ‘Its knowledge is only with my Lord’ and His saying: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. So how can they ask you about it and demand from you an explanation of the time of its occurrence?
79:45: 45- You are only a warner of him who fears it. That is, a warner of those who fear the Hour. This is your duty, and you are not required to do anything else, such as informing about the time of the Hour and similar matters of which God has kept knowledge to Himself. Warning is specific to those who fear, because they are the ones who will benefit from the warning, even though it is a warner for every accountable person, Muslim or disbeliever. The majority of reciters read the verse by adding warner to what follows it. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abu Ja`far, Talhah, Ibn Muhaysin, Shaybah, al-A`raj, and Hamid read it with the tanween. This reading was narrated from Abu `Amr. Al-Farra` said: Adding the tanween and leaving it out in Mundhir is correct, as in Baghdad Amarhu his affair is accomplished and Weaken the plot of the disbelievers. Abu `Ali al-Farisi said: It is permissible for the addition to be for the past tense, as in darab Zayd yesterday.
79:46: 46- It will be as if, on the Day they see it, they had not remained [in the world] except an evening or its morning. That is, except for the time of the last or first part of the day, or the time of the morning that follows that evening. What is meant is the reduction of the duration of this world, as He said: They had not remained except for an hour of a day. And it was said that they had not remained in their graves except an evening or its morning. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj said: What is meant by adding the morning to the evening is adding it to the day of the evening, according to the custom of the Arabs. They say: I will come to you in the morning or its evening, and I will come to you in the evening or its morning, so the evening means the end of the day, and the morning means the beginning of the day. And from this is the saying of the poet: We have become prosperous in her house, barren, hostile to the ends of her day Crescent Eve or its secrets The sentence is a report of what the warning indicates regarding the speed of the arrival of the one warned of. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, He raised its ceiling, he said: He built it, and covered its night, he said: He made its night dark. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, and covered its night, he said: He made its night dark, and brought forth its day, he said: He brought forth its day. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, and after that He spread out the earth, he said: with that. Abd Ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority that a man said to him: Two verses in the Book of God contradict each other. He said: You only came from your own opinion. He said: Read, Say, ‘Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days?’ until he reached, Then He directed Himself to the heaven, and His statement, and after that He spread out the earth, he said: God created the earth before He created the heaven, then He spread out the earth after He created the heaven. Rather, His statement, He spread it out, means He extended it. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him that he said: Daha means He brought forth from it water and pasture, split rivers in it, and made in it mountains, sand, paths, hills, and everything in between in two days. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him that he said: The catastrophe is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about the Hour, so the verse, What are you to do with its remembrance? was revealed. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Aisha that she said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept asking about the Hour until God revealed, “What are you to do with its remembrance? To your Lord is its final destination.” Then he stopped and did not ask about it.” Abd ibn Humayd, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Tariq ibn Shihab that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) frequently mentioned the Hour until the verse, What are you to do with its remembrance? To your Lord is its final destination? was revealed, so he stopped. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas. Al-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission: The polytheists of Mecca asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said, When will the Hour come? mockingly. So God revealed, “They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when will it come?” meaning its arrival. What do you have to do with its remembrance? meaning, you, O Muhammad, have no knowledge of it. To your Lord is its limit. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said, “Whenever the Bedouins came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, they would ask him about the Hour. He would look at the youngest person among them and say, ‘If this one lives, your Hour will have come upon you.’”
80:1: It is called Surat Al-Saffarah, and it has forty-one or forty-two verses. It is Meccan according to everyone. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Abasa was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar statement on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. His saying: 1- He frowned and turned away meaning his face darkened and he turned away. It is also read Abasa with emphasis.
80:2: 2- If the blind man came to him is an object for which: that is, because the blind man came to him, and the operator in it is either frowning or turning away, according to the difference between the Basrans and Kufians in the dispute over whether the preferred option is to apply the first or the second? The commentators have agreed that the reason for the revelation of this verse was that some of the nobles of Quraysh were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had hoped that they would convert to Islam. Then Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum approached, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not want Ibn Umm Maktum to interrupt his conversation, so he turned away from him, and this was revealed. This will be explained at the end of the research, God willing.
80:3: 3- "And what makes you know that perhaps he will be purified?" God the Almighty turned to addressing His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), because speaking directly is more appropriate for reproach: that is, what would make you aware of his condition that you would turn away from him? The phrase "perhaps he will be purified" is a new sentence to clarify that he has a matter that negates turning away from him: that is, perhaps he will purify himself from sins through righteous deeds because of what he learns from you. The pronoun in "perhaps" refers to the blind man, and it was said that it refers to the disbeliever: that is, what makes you know that what you hoped for from the one you were busy talking to about the blind man, that he will be purified or remembered? The former is more appropriate. The word of hope is in consideration of the one to whom the speech is directed to draw attention to the fact that turning away from him, while he is expected to be purified, is not permissible. The majority read "that the blind man came to him" as a statement without a question, and the reason for this is what was mentioned above. Al-Hasan read an ja’ihu with a long vowel as a question. According to this reading, it is connected to a deleted verb indicated by ‘abas and tawala. The meaning is: when the blind man came to him, he turned away and turned away. Similar to this verse is His statement in Surat Al-An’am, And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, and His statement in Surat Al-Kahf, And do not let your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life.
80:4: And his statement: 4- Or he remembers is in apposition to is purified and is included with it in the ruling of hope: that is, or he remembers and takes heed from what he has learned of sermons so the remembrance benefits him that is, the sermon. The majority read so it benefits him in the nominative case, while Asim ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa, As-Salami, and Zur ibn Hubaysh read it in the accusative case as a response to the hope.
80:5: 5- But he who is self-sufficient meaning he is wealthy and rich, or is self-sufficient in faith and in the knowledge you have.
80:6: 6- So you attend to him meaning you listen to his words. Attending means paying attention. The majority of scholars read tasada with a light pronunciation, dropping one of the two ta's for the sake of brevity. Nafi' and Ibn Muhaisin read it with a shaddah due to assimilation. This further discourages him, may God bless him and grant him peace, from approaching them and listening to their words.
80:7: 7- And there is nothing wrong with you if he does not become Muslim or is guided. That is, what is wrong with you if he does not submit or is guided? You are only responsible for conveying the message, so do not worry about the matter of someone like this among the disbelievers. It is possible for ma to be negative: that is, there is nothing wrong with you if the one you confronted and turned towards does not become purified. The sentence would be in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun confronted.
80:8: Then the Almighty increased the rebuke to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: 8- And as for he who comes to you striving, meaning he comes to you while he is hurrying to come to you, asking you to guide him to goodness and admonish him with God’s admonitions.
80:9: Sentence 9- And he fears is a state of the subject of strives in the overlap, or of the subject of came to you in the synonymy.
80:10: 10- So you are distracted from it meaning you are preoccupied with it and turning away from it, and the same is true of I was distracted. His saying: Preoccupation and neglect, it is said I was distracted from the matter meaning I was preoccupied with it, and the same is true of I was distracted.
80:11: And His saying: 11- "No" is a deterrent to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, from what he was reprimanded for: meaning, do not do after this action of yours the same of turning away from the poor, and confronting the rich and being preoccupied with him, while he is not one of those who purify themselves from the guidance that came to you from the people of purification and acceptance of admonition. This action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is from the category of leaving what is best, so God, the Exalted, guided him to what is best for him. "Indeed, it is a reminder," meaning that these verses or surah are an admonition that should be taken admonition from, accepted, and acted upon, and all your nation should act upon it. "So whoever wills, let him remember it," meaning whoever desires it, let him take admonition from it, memorize it, and act upon it. And whoever turns away from it, as the one who is self-sufficient does, then there is no need to pay attention to his matter. It was said that the two pronouns in "it and in his remembrance" refer to the Qur'an, and the feminine of the first is due to the feminine of its predicate. It was also said that the first refers to the surah, or the previous verses. The second is for the reminder because it is in the sense of remembrance.
80:12: It was said that the meaning of 12- Whoever wills, let him remember it is that whoever God wills, He inspires him and makes him understand the Qur’an so that he may remember it and be admonished by it, and the first is more appropriate.
80:13: Then the Almighty informed about the greatness and majesty of this reminder, saying: 13- In scriptures, meaning that it is a reminder contained in scriptures. The preposition and its object are an attribute of reminder, and what is between them is an interruption. The scriptures are the plural of scripture, and the meaning of honored is that it is honored by God because of the knowledge and wisdom it contains, or because it was revealed from the Preserved Tablet. It was said that what is meant by scriptures are the books of the prophets, as in His statement: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
80:14: The meaning of 14- exalted is that it is of high status with God, and it was said that it is raised to the seventh heaven. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: Honored, meaning the Preserved Tablet. Exalted means in the seventh heaven. Ibn Jarir said: Exalted in status and mention, and it was said that it is raised from doubt and contradiction. Purified means pure, and none touch it except the purified. Al-Hasan said: Purified from all filth. Al-Suddi said: Protected from the disbelievers, and they cannot reach it.
80:15: 15- In the hands of scribes. Sifra is the plural of safar, like kataba and katib, and the meaning is: that it is in the hands of scribes from the angels who copy the books from the Preserved Tablet. Al-Farra’ said: The safrah here are the angels who travel with the revelation between God and His Messenger, from the word safarah, which means striving between people, and he recited: I do not leave the embassy among my people, nor do I walk without a close relative Al-Zajjaj said: The book is called a book safar with a kasra on the seen, and the book is a traveler, because its meaning is that it is clear. It is said that the morning became bright, and that a woman uncovered her face, and from this, she traveled between the people asfar safarah, meaning she reconciled between them. Mujahid said: They are the noble angels who record the deeds of the servants. Qatadah said: The safarah here is the reading because they read the books. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They are the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
80:16: Then the Almighty praised the scribes, saying: 16- Noble and pious. That is, noble in the sight of their Lord. This is what Al-Kalbi said. Al-Hasan said: Noble in avoiding sins, so they raise themselves above them. It was also said that they are honored to be with the son of Adam when he is alone with his wife, or when he relieves himself. It was also said that they give precedence to the benefits of others over their own. It was also said that they are honored to the believers by asking forgiveness for them. And righteous is the plural of barr like kufrah and kafir: that is, pious, obedient to their Lord, sincere in their faith, and its explanation has been mentioned above.
80:17: 17- Killing man, how ungrateful he is! That is, cursing the ungrateful man, how intense his ungratefulness is. It was also said that he was punished. It was also said that what is meant by it is Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, and the meaning of how ungrateful he is is amazement at the excess of his ungratefulness. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is, be amazed at his ungratefulness. It was also said that what is meant by man is the one mentioned previously in His statement, But he who is self-sufficient. It was also said that what is meant by it is the genus, and this is the most appropriate, so every ungrateful person who is intensely ungrateful is included under it, and whoever was the primary reason for the revelation of the verse is included under it.
80:18: Then the Almighty mentioned what this disbeliever should have considered in order to be deterred from his disbelief and cease his transgression, saying: 18- From what did He create him? That is, from what did God create this disbeliever? The question is for confirmation.
80:19: Then he explained that by saying: 19- From a sperm-drop He created him meaning from a despised water, and this is to belittle him. Al-Hasan said: How can someone who came out of the urinary tract twice be arrogant? The meaning of and He proportioned him is that He made him proportioned and prepared him for his own interests, and created for him hands, feet, eyes, and all the other tools and senses. It was said that He proportioned him in stages from one state to another, a sperm-drop then a clot until his creation was complete.
80:20: 20- Then the path was made easy for him meaning He made the path to good and evil easy for him. Al-Suddi, Muqatil, Ata’, and Qatadah said: He made it easy for him to emerge from his mother’s womb, but the former is more appropriate. Similar to this is His statement: And We showed him the two ways and the path being in the accusative case by an implied noun indicated by the aforementioned verb: meaning He made the path easy, He made it easy for him.
80:21: 21- Then He caused him to die and buried him. That is, after He caused him to die, He made him have a grave in which to be buried, out of respect for him. He did not make him one of those who are thrown on the face of the earth to be eaten by wild beasts and birds. This is what Al-Farra’ said. Abu Ubaidah said: He made a grave for him and ordered that he be buried in it. He did not say his grave, because the one who buries someone is the one who buries him with his own hand. This is the saying of Al-A’mashi: If she rested a dead person on her chest, he would live and not be transferred to the grave
80:22: 22- Then if He wills, He will resurrect him meaning, then if He wills to resurrect him, He will resurrect him: meaning He will bring him back to life after his death. The resurrection is linked to the will to indicate that its time is not specific, but rather it is dependent on the will. The majority read ansharuhu with an alif, and Abu Haywah narrated on the authority of Nafi’ and Shu’ayb ibn Abi Hamza that he resurrected it without an alif, and they are two eloquent languages.
80:23: 23- No, he has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded. No, this is a deterrent and warning to the disbelieving human being: that is, the matter is not as he says. The meaning of he has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded to do is that he has not fulfilled what God commanded him to do in terms of obeying Him and avoiding His sins. It was also said that it refers to humans in general, and that he has not done what God commanded him to do over a long period of time because he is not free from shortcomings. Al-Hasan said: That is, he truly did not do what he was commanded to do. Ibn Fawrak said: That is, no, he has not yet fulfilled what this disbeliever was commanded to do in terms of faith. Rather, he was commanded to do what he had not yet fulfilled. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Stopping at both is ugly, but stopping at His command is good. According to this, both means truly. It was also said that the meaning is: when all individuals of a human being have not yet fulfilled what he was commanded to do, rather, he has failed to do it: some through disbelief, and some through disobedience, and only a few have fulfilled what God commanded them to do.
80:24: Then the Almighty proceeded to enumerate His blessings upon His servants so that they would be grateful for them and refrain from being ungrateful for them after mentioning the blessings related to His occurrence. He said: 24- So let man look at his food. That is, let him look at how God created his food which He made the cause of his life? And how He provided him with the means of livelihood to prepare for the happiness in the hereafter. Mujahid said: Its meaning is let man look at his food: that is, at its entrance and exit, and the former is more appropriate.
80:25: Then He, the Almighty, explained that by saying: 25- Indeed, We poured down water in torrents. The majority of reciters read indeed with a kasra as a new sentence. The Kufians and Ruways on the authority of Ya'qub recited it with a fatha as a substitute for his food, a substitute of inclusion because the rain falling was a reason for obtaining the food, so it is like what includes it, or by estimating the lam of reason. Al-Zajjaj said: The kasra is for the beginning and resumption, and the fatha is to mean a substitute for the food. The meaning is: So let man consider that We poured down water in torrents, and by pouring down water he meant rain. Al-Hasan bin Ali recited it with a fatha and imala.
80:26: 26- Then We split the earth with a split meaning We split it with the plants that emerge from it due to the rain falling, a wonderful split with what emerges from it in terms of smallness, largeness, shape, and form.
80:27: Then he explained the reason for this split and what it happened for, saying: 27- Then We caused to grow in it grain, meaning the grains that nourish it, and the meaning is: that the plant continues to grow and increase until it becomes grain.
80:28: And His statement: 28- And grapes is in apposition to grain: meaning, and We caused grapes to grow therein. It was said that it is not a necessary consequence of apposition to restrict the conjoined with everything that restricted the conjoined to, so there is no harm in the growth of grapes not having a crack in the ground. Al-Qadhab: is the fresh grass that is cut time and time again, to which animals cling. That is why it is called Qadban, based on the source of Qadabah: meaning he cut it, as if it were cut repeatedly in the same way. Al-Khalil said: Al-Qadhab is the fresh alfalfa, and when it dries, it is the grass. He said in Al-Sahah: Al-Qadbah and Al-Qadhab are fresh. He said: And the place where it grows is Maqsaba. Al-Qatibi and Tha'lab said: The people of Mecca call grapes Al-Qadhab. And the olive is what oil is squeezed from, and it is the well-known olive tree, and Al-Nakhl is the plural of Nakhl.
80:30: 30- And gardens of Ghalib is the plural of garden, which is an orchard, and the Ghalib are the great ones with thick necks. Qatada and Muqatil said: The Ghalib is the one that is intertwined with each other. It is said: a man is Aglab: if he has a large neck, and the lion is called Aglab because it has a solid neck that does not turn except all around. Al-Ajjaj said: I still twist my back and head on the day of separation until I became like most people The plural of aghlab and ghalbaa is ghalab, just as the plural of ahmar and hamraa is hamra. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: ghalab are the noble palm trees. Also from Ibn Zayd and Ikrimah: they are those with thick middles and trunks. Fruit is what people eat from the fruits of trees such as grapes, figs, peaches and the like. Ab is everything that the earth produces that people do not eat or plant of pasture and other types of irrigation. From this is the saying of the poet: Our grandfather Qais and Najd are our home, and our father and Al-Mukraa are in it Ad-Dahhak said: Father is everything that grows on the face of the earth. Ibn Abi Talha said: It refers to fresh fruits. It was also narrated from Ad-Dahhak that he said: It refers specifically to figs, but the first is more appropriate.
80:32: 32- For your enjoyment and for your livestock.
80:33: Then the Almighty proceeded to explain the conditions of the Resurrection, saying: 33- So when the Deafening Blast comes meaning the blast on the Day of Resurrection. It is called a deafening blast because of its loudness, as it deafens the ears, meaning it deafens them so that they cannot hear. It was also said that it was called a deafening blast because the ears listen to it, from the saying asak ila kadha meaning he listened to it. The first is more correct. Al-Khalil said: The deafening blast is a blast that deafens the ears until it deafens them with its loudness. The root of the word in the language is taken from the word sak hard hitting. It is said that someone hit someone with a stone, meaning they hit it with it. The answer to if is omitted, as indicated by His saying: Every person among them that Day will have enough to occupy him. That is, when the Deafening Blast comes, everyone will be busy with himself.
80:34: The circumstance in His statement: 34- The Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother, and his father, and his wife, and his children is either a substitute for if it came, or it is accusative with an implied meaning: i.e. I mean, and it is an explanation of the deafening noise, or a substitute for it built on the fat-ha, and He specifically mentioned these people because they are the closest relatives, and their children are the ones with the most tenderness and compassion, so fleeing from them is only due to great terror and a terrible calamity.
80:35: 35- And his mother and his father.
80:36: 36- And his wife and his children.
80:37: 37- For every man, that Day, will be concerned to distract him from his relatives. That is, on the Day of Resurrection, each person will have concerns that will distract him from his relatives and divert him from them. It was said that he flees from them out of fear of them demanding what is between them. It was also said that he flees from them so that they do not see the hardship he is in. It was also said that it is because he knows that they will not benefit him or avail him at all, as God the Almighty said: On the Day when no protector will avail another at all. The sentence is a new sentence introduced to explain the reason for fleeing. Ibn Qutaybah said: Yughnihu means it will distract him from his relatives. From this it is said: Aghni ‘anni wajha means divert it. The majority of scholars read yughnihu with the voiced ghayn. Ibn Muhaysin read it with the silent ‘ayn and the fatha on the ya’: meaning it concerns him, from anahu al-amr if it concerns him.
80:38: 38- On that Day some faces will be radiant. Faces is the subject, even though it is a general noun because it is in the context of detail, and this is one of the justifications for starting with an indefinite noun. On that Day is related to it, and radiant is its predicate. The meaning of radiant is: bright and shining, and they are the faces of the believers because they will know then what bliss and honor they will have. It is said that the morning has dawned: if it has illuminated. Ad-Dahhak said: radiant from the effects of ablution, and it was said from standing in prayer at night.
80:39: 39- Laughing and cheerful meaning happy with the great reward she received.
80:40: Then when he finished mentioning the state of the believers, he mentioned the state of the disbelievers, saying: 40- And faces that Day will be covered with dust meaning dust and a darkening of what they see of the punishment that God has prepared for them.
80:41: 41- A darkness will overwhelm it meaning it will be covered and covered by blackness and eclipse. It was also said that it means humiliation, and it was also said that it means severity. In the speech of the Arabs, qatr means dust. This is what Abu Ubaidah said, and he recited the words of Al-Farazdaq: Crowned with the king's robe, followed by a regiment, above which you can see the banners and the qatra What Abu Ubaidah said before mentioning dust is rejected, as it is the same as qubra. Zaid bin Aslam said: qutra is what rises to the sky, and qubra is what descends to the ground.
80:42: 42- Those meaning the owners of the faces are the disbelieving immoral ones meaning those who combine disbelief in God and immorality. It is said that fajar means immorality, and fajar means lying. Its root is deviation, and the immoral person is the one who deviates from the truth. At-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated that Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aishah who said: “This verse was revealed about Umm Maktum, the blind man. He came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and began to say: ‘O Messenger of God, guide me. ’ While there was a prominent polytheist with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept turning away from him and turning to the other, saying: ‘Do you see anything wrong with what I am saying? ’ He would say: ‘No, for this is why it was revealed.” ’ ‘Abd al-Razzaq, ‘Abd ibn Humayd and Abu Ya’la narrated on the authority of Anas who said: “‘Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum came while he was speaking to Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and he turned away from him. Then God revealed: ‘He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. ’ After that, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to honor him.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was conversing privately with Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and he was often trying to stand up to them and was eager for them to believe, a blind man called Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum came walking towards them while he was conversing with them. Abdullah began to recite a verse from the Qur’an to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: ‘O Messenger of God, teach me from what God has taught you.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned away from him, frowned, turned away, disliking his words and turning to the others. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had finished his private conversation and was about to return to his family, God took some of his sight away, and he shook his head. Then God revealed the verse: ‘He frowned and turned away.’ When what was revealed about him was revealed, the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) honored him and spoke to him and said to him: ‘What is your need? Do you want anything?’ And when he left him, he said: ‘Do you need anything?’” Ibn Kathir said: There is something strange about it, and its chain of transmission has been criticized. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, In the hands of scribes, meaning scribes. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, In the hands of scribes, meaning readers in Nabataean. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, Noble and pious, meaning angels. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: He who recites the Quran and is proficient in it will be with the noble and pious scribes, and he who recites it and finds it difficult will have two rewards. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas, Then the path is made easy for him, meaning his emergence from his mother’s womb. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding his statement, So let man look at his food, he said, at his entrance and exit. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated from Ibn Abbas, So let man look at his food, he said, at his excrement. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him, We poured down water in torrents, he said, Then We split the earth into fragments, he said, about plants. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding his statement: And reeds, he said: Alfalfa means the cattail. And gardens of thickets, he said: Tall. And fruits and Abba, he said: Fresh fruits. Abd Ibn Humaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him. He said: Gardens are all intertwined things, and Ghalab is what is thick, and Abba is what the earth grows that animals eat but people do not eat. Abd Ibn Humaid and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him. And gardens of thickets, he said: Trees in Paradise that one seeks shade under but do not bear anything. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him. He said: Abba is grass and pasture. Abu Ubaid narrated in his Fada’il and Abd Ibn Humaid from Ibrahim Al-Taimi who said: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq was asked about Abba, what is it? He said: Which sky will shade me and which land will bear me if I say about the Book of God what I do not know? Abd Ibn Humaid narrated from Abdullah Ibn Yazid who said: A man asked Umar about his statement: And Abba, and when he saw them saying that, he turned to them with a whip. Ibn Sa'd, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab, and al-Khatib narrated on the authority of Anas that Umar recited on the pulpit: And We cause to grow therein grain and grapes until the verse: and vines. He said: We know all of this, but what is vines? Then he raised a stick that was in his hand and said: By God, this is an exaggeration, so what is it that you do not know what vines are? Follow what has been made clear to you in this Book and act upon it, and whatever you do not know, leave it to its Lord. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Noise is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: bright, he said: shining. And regarding His statement: darkness will overwhelm it, he said: hardship and humiliation will cover it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: Qatrah, he said: blackness of the face.
81:1: It consists of twenty-nine verses. It is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Surah When the sun is wrapped up was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Aisha and Ibn Az-Zubayr. Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, Ibn Al-Mundhir, At-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Whoever would like to look at the Day of Resurrection as if he is seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite: ‘When the sun is wrapped up,’ ‘When the sky is split,’ and ‘When the sky is split.’” His saying: 1- When the sun is wrapped up. The rising of the sun is by an omitted verb that is explained by what follows it as being occupied. This is according to the Basrans. As for the Kufians and Akhfash, it is raised as a beginning. And takwir is the plural, and it is taken from kar turban on the head, yakruhu. Al-Zajjaj said: He wrapped as the turban is wrapped. It is said: I wrapped the turban on my head, I wrap it up, and I wrapped it up, meaning I rolled it up. Abu Ubaidah said: It was wrapped up like the rolling up of the turban, it was wrapped up and gathered. Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim said: It was thrown down, and from this it is rolled up, so it fell down. Qatadah and Al-Kalbi said: Its light went away. Mujahid said: It vanished. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: The sun is gathered together, then it is wrapped up and thrown down. So the conclusion is that takwir either means wrapping its mass, or wrapping its light, or throwing it down.
81:2: 2- And when the stars are scattered meaning they fall, swoop down and become scattered. It is said that a bird is scattered from the air: if it swoops down. The root of nakdaa is pouring down. Al-Khalil said: It is said that the saying ankadara alayhim means if they come in groups and are scattered against them. Abu Ubaidah said: It is scattered like an eagle is scattered. Al-Kalbi and Ata' said: The sky will rain stars on that day, and there will not be a star in the sky except that it will fall on the earth. It was said that its swooping down means its light is extinguished.
81:3: 3- And when the mountains are set in motion meaning they are uprooted from the earth and set in motion in the air. From this is His statement: And the Day We set the mountains in motion and you see the earth exposed.
81:4: 4- And when the ten-month-old camels are neglected The 'Ashar are the pregnant camels that have their young in their bellies. One of them is 'Ashra', and she is the one that has been pregnant for ten months and that continues to be their name until she gives birth. The 'Ashar was specified because it is the most precious and valuable property to the Arabs, and the meaning of 'Atallat' is left neglected without a shepherd, and that is because of what they witnessed of the great terror. It was said that this is by way of a metaphor because on the Day of Resurrection there will be no ten-month-old camel, but rather what is meant is that if a man had a ten-month-old camel on that day or ten-month-old camels, he would leave them and not pay attention to them, being preoccupied with the terror he will face on the Day of Resurrection. And the end of the discussion, God willing, will indicate that this is in this world. It was said that the 'Ashar are the clouds, because the Arabs liken them to the pregnant ones, and from this is His statement: And the pregnant ones are pregnant and neglecting them is the lack of rain. The majority read Atallat with a shaddah, and Ibn Kathir read it in a narration from him with a light 'Atallat. It was said that what is meant is that the houses are neglected and cannot be inhabited, and it was said that the land whose crops are tithed is neglected and cannot be cultivated.
81:5: 5- And when the wild beasts are gathered together Wild beasts are all wild land animals. The meaning of gathered is: they are sent out so that some of them may exact retribution from others, so the horned one will exact retribution from the horned one. It was said that their gathering is their death, and it was said that with their estrangement from people today and their dispersal in the deserts, they will be gathered to them on that day. The majority read hashara with a light pronunciation, while Al-Hasan and Amr bin Maymun read it with a heavy pronunciation.
81:6: 6- And when the seas are lit up meaning lit up and become a blazing fire. Al-Farra' said: They are filled by becoming one sea. It was narrated on the authority of Qatada and Ibn Hibban that the meaning of the verse is: They dry up and not a drop remains in them. It is said that I lit the pool asjaratuhu sajran if I fill it. Al-Qushayri said: It is from sajratu tanur asjaratuhu sajran if I heat it up. Ibn Zayd, Atiyya, Sufyan, Wahb and others said: It was lit up and became a fire. It was said that the meaning of sajratu is that it becomes red like blood, from their saying sajra' spring, meaning red. The majority read sajratu with a shaddah on the jim. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a light jim.
81:7: 7- And when souls are paired meaning a righteous man will be paired with a righteous man in Paradise, and an evil man will be paired with an evil man in Hell. Ata' said: The souls of the believers will be paired with the wide-eyed houris, and the souls of the disbelievers will be paired with the devils. It was also said that each form will be paired with its form in authority, as in His statement: Gather together those who did wrong and their mates. Ikrimah said: And when souls are paired meaning the souls will be paired with the bodies. Al-Hasan said: Every person will be paired with his own group: the Jews with the Jews, the Christians with the Christians, the Magians with the Magians, and everyone who worships something other than God will be paired with each other, the hypocrites with the hypocrites, and the believers with the believers. It was also said that the seducer will be paired with the one who seduced him, whether a devil or a human, and the obedient will be paired with the one who called him to obedience from among the prophets and believers. It was also said that souls will be paired with their deeds.
81:8: 8- And if the buried alive girl is asked meaning the one buried alive. When the Arabs gave birth to a daughter, they would bury her alive for fear of shame or need. It is said: he buried [wada] wada, so he is wa'id, and the one who is done to is maw'ud. Its origin is taken from the weight because she is buried, and the dirt is spread over her, making her heavy and she dies. From this, and their preservation does not burden him meaning it does not weigh him down. From this is the saying of Mutammam ibn Nuwayrah: And a buried girl in a cave And from it the saying of the rajaz poet: I named her if she was born she will die and the grave is a guarantor of the in-laws I threw away The majority read al-maw'adah with a hamza between two silent waws like al-maw'udah. Al-Bazzi read it in a narration from him with a dammah then a silent waw. Al-A'mash read al-maw'adah with the weight of al-muzzah. The majority read sa'alat in the passive voice, and Al-Hasan read it with a kasrah on the seen from sala yaseel.
81:9: The majority read 9- "I asked in the passive voice, and Al-Hasan read it with a kasra on the seen from sala yaseel". The majority read "Qalta with a light s" in the passive voice, and Abu Jaafar read it with a shaddah for emphasis. Ali, Ibn Masoud, and Ibn Abbas read I asked in the active voice, Qalta with a damma on the final taa. The meaning of I asked according to the reading of the majority is that directing the question to her was to show the utmost anger at her killer to the point that he did not deserve to be addressed or asked about that, and in it is a rebuke and severe rebuke to her killer. Al-Hasan said: God wanted to rebuke her killer because she was killed without a sin, and in the copy of Abu Jaafar it is: And when the buried girl is asked, for what sin did you kill me?
81:10: 10- And when the records are spread out meaning the records of deeds are spread out for the reckoning, because death will cover them and they will be spread out at the reckoning, so every person will stand at his record and know what is in it, and he will say: What is this book that leaves out nothing small or great but that it has enumerated it? Nafi', Asim, Ibn Amir, and Abu Amr read Nashra with a light pronunciation. The rest read it with a heavy pronunciation to indicate abundance.
81:11: 11- And when the sky is scraped away Scraping means to tear off due to intense adhesion, so the sky is scraped like the skin is scraped off a ram. Scraping with the letter Qaf is a dialect for scraping, and it is the reading of Ibn Masoud. Al-Zajjaj said: It was scraped away like the ceiling is torn away. Al-Farra' said: It was removed and folded. Muqatil said: It revealed what was hidden in it. Al-Wahidi said: The meaning of scraping is that you lift something from something that had covered it.
81:12: 12- And when Hellfire is set ablaze meaning it is set ablaze for the enemies of God with intense fervor. The majority of scholars read set ablaze with a light pronunciation, while Nafi', Ibn Dhakwan, and Hafs read it with a shaddah because it is set ablaze time and time again. Qatada said: Its blaze is the wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam.
81:13: 13- And when Paradise is brought near meaning it is brought near to the righteous and brought close to them. Al-Hasan said: They are brought near to it, not that it is moved from its place. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning of brought near is beautified. The first is more appropriate because zulfa in Arabic speech means closeness. It was said that these twelve matters are: six of them are in this world, and they are from the beginning of the surah to His saying: And when the seas are set ablaze, and six are in the hereafter, and they are: And when the souls are paired until here.
81:14: 14- A soul will know what it has brought meaning that what is meant is the time extending from this world to the Hereafter, but not in the sense that it knows what it knows in every part of this extended time. Rather, what is meant is that it knows what it has brought when the scrolls are spread out: meaning what good or evil it has done. The meaning of what it has brought is what it has brought of its deeds, and what is meant is the presence of the scrolls of deeds, or the presence of the deeds themselves, as it has been reported that deeds are depicted in images that indicate them and are known by them. The indefiniteness of self is useful for establishing the aforementioned knowledge for an individual soul, or for some of them, to indicate that its establishment for all of its individuals is so apparent and clear that it is not hidden from anyone. This is indicated by His statement: On the Day every soul will find present what it has done of good. It has been said that it is possible that this is to indicate that if a soul knows at that time what it has brought, then every soul must correct its deeds for fear that it is the one that knew what it brought. How can it be that every soul knows it, in the manner of saying to someone you are advising, Perhaps you will regret what you did, and perhaps a person will regret his action.
81:15: 15- So I swear by the stars that retreat La is redundant as was previously explained and what was said about it in the beginning of Surah al-Qiyamah 75:meaning I swear by the stars that retreat, which are the planets. They are called Al-Khans, from Khanas: if it is late because they retreat during the day and are hidden and not seen, and they are Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury as mentioned by the commentators. The reason for mentioning them specifically from among the other stars is that they face the sun and cross the galaxy. It was said in Al-Sahah: Al-Khans are all the planets, because they retreat at sunset, or because they are hidden during the day, or it is said that they are the wandering planets among them and not the fixed ones. Al-Farraa said: They are the five planets mentioned, because they retreat in their paths, and they sweep: that is, they are hidden as gazelles sweep in the cave, and it is said that they are called Al-Khans because they delay, because they are the wandering planets that return and straighten out. It is said that he delayed khanasa anhu or that he fell behind yakhnas khanusan, and that he left him behind akhnasa ghayruhu and that he went behind him and passed him by. Al-Khans means the nose falling behind the face with a slight elevation of the bridge of the nose.
81:16: The meaning of 16- al-jawar is that it runs with the sun and the moon, and the meaning of al-kans is that it returns until it disappears under the light of the sun, so its knūs is its return, and its kanūs is its disappearance under its light. It was also said that its knūs is its disappearance during the day, and its kanūs is its setting. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They are the stars that disappear during the day and when they set, and the meanings are close because they inform the sight during the day because they are hidden and are not seen, and they appear at night and are swept away at the time of their setting. It was also said that what is meant by them are wild cows because they are described as knūs, al-jawar, and kans. Ikrimah said: al-Khans are cows and al-kans are gazelles, so they disappear when they see a person, and they shrink back and retreat and enter their hiding place. It was also said that they are the angels. The first is more appropriate because of the mention of night and morning after this, and al-kans is taken from al-kanās in which the wild beasts hide, and al-Khans is the plural of Khanis and Khanasa, and al-kans is the plural of Kanas and Kanasah.
81:17: 17- And the night when it covers Linguists said: It is one of the opposites. It is said that the night covers: when it comes, and covers: when it goes away.
81:18: And what is indicated here by ‘adbar’ is his statement: 18- And the morning when it breathes. Al-Farra’ said: The commentators are in agreement that the meaning of ‘asaa is ‘adbar’, as al-Jawhari reported it from him. Al-Hasan said: It approached with its darkness. Al-Farra’ said: The Arabs say ‘asaa al-layl’ when it approaches, and ‘asaa al-layl’ when it departs. This does not contradict what was previously reported from him, because he reported from the commentators that they are in agreement that its meaning in this verse refers to ‘adbar’, even though in origin it is shared between ‘adbar’ and ‘idbar’. Al-Mubarrad said: It is one of the opposites. He said: The two meanings go back to one thing, which is the onset of darkness at the beginning and its departure at the end. Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj said: Oh Hind, how quickly you became a miserable child after you were just a young man. Imru' al-Qais said: Even if we wished, when we came near, we would have a share of his fire. And he said: Water is running down the old quarter And the morning when it breathes. Breathing in origin: is the breeze emerging from the stomach. The morning breathes its approach, because it approaches with spirit and breeze, so that was made a metaphor for it breathing. Al-Wahidi said: Breathed: meaning its light extended until it became day, and from this it is said of the day when it increases it breathes. It was said that when it breathes means it splits and cracks, and from this the bow breathes: meaning it cracked.
81:19: Then the Almighty mentioned the answer to the oath, saying: 19- Indeed, it is the word of an honored Messenger, meaning Gabriel, because he brought it down from God Almighty to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He added the word to Gabriel because he was the one who sent it. It was said that what is meant by the Messenger in the verse is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the first is more appropriate.
81:20: Then He described the aforementioned Messenger with praiseworthy descriptions, saying: 20- Of strength, firmly established with the Lord of the Throne. That is, of great strength in carrying out what he was charged with, as in His saying: of great strength. The meaning of of great strength with the Lord of the Throne is that he has a high status and a secure position with God, the Exalted. It is in the accusative case as a state of secure. Its origin is a description, but when it is brought forward, it becomes a state. It is also permissible for it to be an attribute of a Messenger. It is said, So-and-so has a position with so-and-so, meaning he has a position and status with Him. Abu Saleh said: Among his status with the Lord of the Throne is that he enters seventy tents without permission.
81:21: The meaning of 21- "Obeyed" is that he is obeyed among the angels, they return to him and obey him. "Then Trustworthy The majority read then with a fatha as a circumstance of place for something distant, and the factor in it is Obeyed" or what comes after it, and the meaning is that he is obeyed in the heavens or trustworthy in them: that is, he is trusted with the revelation and other things. Hisham, Abu Ja`far, and Abu Haywah read it with a damma as a conjunction, and the conjunction with it is to slacken the rank because what comes after it is greater than what comes before it. And whoever said that what is meant by the Messenger is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then the meaning is that he has the power to convey the message to the nation, he is obeyed and they obey him. Whoever obeys God is trustworthy with the revelation.
81:22: 22- And your companion is not mad. The address is to the people of Mecca, and what is meant by their companion is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning is: O people of Mecca, Muhammad is not mad. He mentioned him with the description of companionship to indicate that they know about his situation, and that he is not like what they accuse him of, madness or anything else, and that they fabricated that against him knowing that he is the most sane and perfect of people. This sentence is included in the answer to the oath, so God Almighty swore that the Qur’an was brought down by Gabriel, and that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is not as they say, that he is mad, and that he brings the Qur’an from his own madness.
81:23: 23- And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon. The lam is the answer to an omitted oath: that is, by God, Muhammad certainly saw Gabriel on the clear horizon: that is, at the rising of the sun from the east, because if the sun rises from this horizon, then it is clear, because things are seen from its direction. It is said that the clear horizon is: the regions of the sky and its sides, and from this is the saying of the poet: We have taken the regions of the heavens upon you. We have its two moons and the rising stars. Rather, God the Almighty said: And he had certainly seen him on the clear horizon, even though he had seen him more than once, because this time he saw him in his form with six hundred wings. Sufyan said: He saw him on the eastern horizon of the sky. Ibn Bahr said: On the western horizon of the sky. Mujahid said: He saw him [towards Ajyad], which is the east of Mecca. Mubeen is an attribute of the horizon, said Al-Rabi’. It was said that it is an attribute of the one who saw him, said Mujahid. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: And Muhammad has certainly seen his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and this has been discussed previously in Surat An-Najm. 24- And he meaning Muhammad, peace be upon him, is not stingy with the unseen meaning the report from heaven and what he learned of what was hidden from the people of Mecca. Stingy with someone who is accused: meaning he is trustworthy in what he conveys from God, the Most High. It was also said that he is stingy with someone who is miserly: meaning he is not stingy with revelation, nor is he negligent in conveying it. The reason for this difference of opinion is the difference of the reciters. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Al-Kisa'i read bidhanin with a dotted dhad: meaning with someone who is accused, and suspicion is accusation. Abu Ubaid preferred this reading and said: Because they were not stingy but called him a liar. The rest read bidhanin with a dotted dhad: meaning with someone who is miserly, from the root word dhanan bis-shay', meaning to be stingy. Mujahid said: meaning he is not stingy with you about what he knows, but rather he teaches creation the words of God and His rulings. It was also said that what is meant is Gabriel, that he is not stingy with the unseen, but the first reading is more appropriate.
81:25: 25- And it is not the word of an accursed devil. That is, the Qur'an is not the word of a devil from the eavesdropping devils who are stoned with meteors. Al-Kalbi said: He says that the Qur'an is neither poetry nor divination as the Quraysh said. Ata' said: He means by devil: the white devil who used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the form of Gabriel, wanting to tempt him.
81:26: Then He, the Most High, rebuked them and said: 26- So where are you going? That is, where are you turning away from this Qur’an and from obeying it? This is what Qatada said. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is which path are you taking that is clearer than this path that has been made clear to you. It is said: Where are you going? And where are you going? Al-Farra’ narrated on the authority of the Arabs: The Levant has gone, “Iraq has left,” and The market has set out, meaning to it. He said: We heard it in these three letters, and he recited to some of Banu Uqayl: Hanifa shouted at us when she saw us, and what kind of land does shouting take? You want to go to any land, so delete to.
81:27: 27- It is only a reminder to the worlds. That is, the Qur’an is only an admonition to all of creation and a reminder to them.
81:28: And His saying: 28- For whoever among you wills to be upright is a substitute for the worlds by repeating the preposition and the object of the will to be upright, meaning for whoever among you wills to be upright in the truth, faith, and obedience.
81:29: 29- And you do not will except that God, Lord of the worlds, wills. That is, you do not will righteousness except that God wills that will. So He, the Most High, informed them that the will lies in granting success to Him, and that they are not able to do that except by the will and guidance of God. Similar to this is His, the Most High, saying: And no soul can believe except by God’s permission. And His saying: And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered together before them all things in front of them, they would not have believed unless God willed. And His saying: Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills. And there are many Qur’anic verses with this meaning. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, When the sun is wrapped up, he said: It darkens. And when the stars are scattered, he said: They have changed.
