Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Daylami narrated on the authority of Abu Maryam that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said regarding the verse, When the sun is wrapped up, he said: It is wrapped up in Hell. And when the stars are scattered, he said: They are scattered in Hell. So everyone who is worshipped other than God will be in Hell, except for Jesus and his mother. Had they been pleased to be worshipped, they would have entered it. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Six verses of this surah are in this world, and people are looking at them, and six they are looking at in the Hereafter. When the sun is wrapped up to And when the seas are set ablaze, this is in this world, and people are looking at it. And when the souls are paired to And when Paradise is brought near, this is in the Hereafter. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated in Al-Ahwal, and Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, who said: Six signs will occur before the Day of Resurrection. While the people are in their markets, the sunlight has gone. Then, between them, they will be like that when the mountains will fall on the face of the earth, and it will move, shake, and mix, so the jinn will flee to the humans and the humans will flee to the jinn. The animals, birds, and wild animals will mix, and they will swarm with one another. And when the wild beasts are gathered together, he said: mixed, And when the ten-year-olds are neglected, he said: their people have neglected them, And when the seas are set ablaze, he said: The jinn are to the humans, We bring you the report, so they set out to the sea, and behold, it is a blazing fire. While they are like that, the earth will crack with a single crack, up to the seventh earth and up to the seventh heaven. While they are like that, a wind will come upon them and kill them. Al-Faryabi, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when the wild beasts are gathered together, that he said: The beasts will be gathered together when they die, and everything will be gathered together when they die except for the jinn and mankind, for they will meet on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Khatib in Al-Muttafaq wa Al-Muftariq narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, And when the wild beasts are gathered together, that he said: Everything will be gathered together on the Day of Resurrection, even the livestock. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Baath on his authority, too, regarding his statement, And when the seas are set ablaze, that he said: They are set ablaze until they become fire. Al-Tabarani narrated on his authority, They will be set ablaze, that he said: Their water will mix with the water of the earth. And Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu`aym in al-Hila, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba`th narrated on the authority of al-Nu`man ibn Bashir on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab regarding his statement, And when souls are paired, he said: A righteous man will be paired with a righteous man in Paradise and an evil man will be paired with an evil man in Hell. This is how souls are paired. In another narration: Then he recited, Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of al-Nu`man ibn Bashir with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Al-Bazzar, Al-Hakim in Al-Kuna, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab who said: Qais ibn Asim Al-Tamimi came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: I buried eight daughters alive during the pre-Islamic era. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Free a slave for each one. He said: I am a camel owner. He said: Then sacrifice a camel for each one. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when Paradise is brought near, he said: It is brought near. Sa’id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding his statement: So I swear by the stars that recede, he said: They are the stars that sweep away at night and recede during the day and are not seen. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority regarding his statement: So I swear by the stars that recede, he said: “Five stars: Saturn, Mercury, Jupiter, Bahram, and Venus. Nothing crosses the galaxy other than them.” Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Khatib in Kitab Al-Nujum narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, saying: They are the seven stars: Saturn, Bahram, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, the sun, and the moon. Their inclination is their return, and their sweeping is their setting during the day. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Ibn Saad, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Tabarani, and Al-Hakim narrated and authenticated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding his statement, {By the retreating stars, the swift stars}, that he said: They are wild cows. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: They are the cows sweeping into the shade. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, that he said: They sweep for themselves at the roots of trees, hiding there. Ibn Jarir also narrated on his authority, that he said: They are the gazelles. Ibn Rahawayh, Abd bin Hamid, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib regarding his statement, {By the swift stars}, that he said: They are the stars. And Abd bin Hamid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Al-Khans means cows, and Al-Jawar Al-Kanas means gazelles. Haven’t you seen how they sweep with their necks and look out their eyes when they are in the shade? Abu Ahmad Al-Hakim narrated in Al-Kuna on the authority of Abu Al-Udays who said: We were with Omar bin Al-Khattab when a man came to him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is Al-Jawar Al-Kanas? Omar stabbed the man’s turban with a stick and threw it off his head. Omar said: Are you a Kharijite? By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Omar bin Al-Khattab, if I found you shaved, I would remove the lice from your head. This is strange, for the Kharijites were not present in the time of Omar nor were they mentioned at that time. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And the night when it covers He said: When it departs, And the morning when it breathes He said: When the day begins at the break of dawn. Al-Tabarani narrated on his authority: When it covers He said: The approach of its blackness. Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority: Indeed, it is the statement of a noble Messenger He said: Gabriel. Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu`aym in Al-Dala’il narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, And indeed he saw him on the clear horizon, meaning he saw Gabriel with six hundred wings that filled the horizon. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas concerning the verse, saying: Gabriel meant that Muhammad saw him in his true form at the Lote Tree of the Limit. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, by the clear horizon, meaning the seventh heaven. Sa`id ibn Mansur, `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite badhanin with a ḍād, and he said: with miserliness. Sa`id ibn Mansur, `Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he recited and he is not [according to] the unseen with a ḍād, and he said: he is not accused. Al-Daraqutni narrated in Al-Afrad, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Khatib in his Tarikh on the authority of Aisha that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite badhanin with a ḍād. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: When the verse, For whoever among you wills to go straight, was revealed, they said: The matter is up to us: if we wish we will go straight, and if we wish we will not go straight, then Gabriel descended to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: They have lied, O Muhammad! And you do not will except that God, Lord of the worlds, wills.
82:1: It is nineteen verses It is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When the sky is cleft asunder was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: “Mu’adh stood up and performed the ‘Isha’ prayer and prolonged it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Are you a tempter, Mu’adh? Where are you regarding ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’, ‘Ad-Duha’ and ‘When the sky is cleft asunder’?” The original hadith is in the two Sahihs, but without the mention of When the sky is cleft asunder. An-Nasa’i presented it earlier. In Surat At-Takwir, the hadith was presented: Whoever would like to see the Day of Resurrection with his own eyes, let him recite ‘When the sun is wrapped up’, ‘When the sky is cleft asunder’ and ‘When the sky is split asunder’. His saying: 1- When the sky is split. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: Its splitting is its cleft as in His saying: And the Day the sky will be split with clouds and the angels will be sent down in a gradual descent. And splitting means slitting. It is said: I split it and it split, and from this comes the word the camel’s fang split: when it comes out. It was said that what is meant is that it split here because of the angels’ descent from it, and it was said that it split out of awe of God.
82:2: 2- And when the stars are scattered meaning they fall in separate places: it is said I scattered something or I scatter it.
82:3: 3- And when the seas burst forth meaning when some of them burst forth into others, becoming one sea, and the fresh water and salty waters mixing together. Al-Hasan said: The meaning of blow forth is that their water is gone and dries up. These things will happen before the Hour, as mentioned in the surah before this one.
82:4: 4- And when the graves are scattered meaning their soil is turned upside down and the dead in them are taken out. It is said that someone scattered, yabsharat, yabsharat, baathrah: if the soil is turned upside down. It is also said that someone scattered the belongings, meaning they are turned upside down. And the basin was scattered and dug up: if you demolished it and made its top its bottom. Al-Farra’ said: Scattered means what was in its bottom was taken out. This is one of the signs of the Hour, that the earth will bring forth its gold and silver.
82:5: Then the Almighty mentioned the answer to what was mentioned before, saying: 5- A soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind. The meaning is that it will know it when the records are spread out, not at the Resurrection, because that is a single time from the Resurrection until the people of Paradise go to Paradise and the people of Hell go to Hell. The discussion of the singular soul here is as mentioned before in the first Surah in His statement, A soul will know what it has brought forth. The meaning of what it has put forward and what it has left behind is what it has put forward of good or evil deeds, and what it has left behind of good or bad practices, because it will have the reward for what it has established of good practices and the reward of those who act upon them, and it will bear the burden of what it has established of bad practices and the burden of those who act upon them. Qatada said: What it has put forward of disobedience and what it has left behind of obedience. It was also said: What it has put forward of an obligatory act and what it has left behind. It was also said: The beginning and end of its deeds. It was also said that the soul will know at the Resurrection what it has put forward and left behind in general knowledge, because the obedient one will see the effects of happiness, and the disobedient one will see the effects of misery. As for detailed knowledge, that is only obtained when the records are spread out.
82:6: 6- O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord? This is addressed to the disbelievers: that is, what has deceived you and tricked you so that you have disbelieved in your Generous Lord who favored you in this world by perfecting your creation and your senses, made you rational and understanding, and provided for you and bestowed upon you His blessings, none of which you can deny? Qatada said: His Satan who had power over him deceived him. Al-Hasan said: His evil Satan deceived him. It was also said: His foolishness and ignorance. It was also said: God’s wrath deceived him if He did not hasten to punish him the first time. This is what Muqatil said.
82:7: 7- Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you. That is, He created you from a sperm-drop, when you were nothing. Then He proportioned you to a man who hears, sees, and understands. So He balanced you means He made you balanced. Ata' said: He made you upright, balanced, and of good form. Muqatil said: He created you justly in the eyes, ears, hands, and feet. The meaning is: He made the limbs He created for you justly. The majority of scholars read fa-adlaka with a shaddah, while Asim, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read it with a sukoon. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid chose the first reading. Al-Farra' and Abu Ubaid said: This is indicated by His statement: Indeed, We created man in the best stature. The meaning of the first reading is that He, glory be to Him, made his limbs balanced, with no discrepancy in them. The meaning of the second reading is that He directed and inclined him to whatever form He wished, either handsome or ugly, long or short.
82:8: 8- In whatever form He willed, He assembled you In whatever form is related to assembled you, and ma is an additional word, and willed is an attribute of form: that is, He assembled you in whatever form He willed from the various forms. This sentence is like an explanation of His saying: Then He made you just and the interpretation is: Then He assembled you justly in whatever form He willed. It is permissible for it to be related to something omitted as a state: that is, He assembled you in whatever form. Abu Hayyan reported from some of the commentators that it is related to your justice. It was objected to that because any is at the beginning of the sentence, so what precedes it does not affect it. Muqatil, Al-Kalbi and Mujahid said: In whatever resemblance of a father or mother, maternal uncle or paternal uncle. Makhul said: If He wills [a male] and if He wills a female.
82:9: And His statement: 9- No is to deter and warn against being deceived by God's generosity and making it a pretext for disbelief in Him and sinning against Him. It is also possible that it means truly. His statement, Rather, you deny the Judgment is a refutation of an implied sentence to which the speech is directed, as if it were said: After the deterrence, you are not deterred from that, but rather you go beyond it to what is greater than it, which is the denial of the Judgment, which is the recompense, or the religion of Islam. Ibn al-Anbari said: It is good to stop at the Judgment and on your knees, and No is ugly. The meaning is: Rather, O people of Mecca, you deny the Judgment, meaning the reckoning. Rather is to deny something that came before and to confirm something else, and the denial of the Resurrection was known to them even if it was not mentioned. Al-Farra' said: No, the matter is not as you were deceived by it. The majority read you deny with the superlative as addressing. Al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, and Shaibah read it with the subjunctive as absent.
82:10: And the sentence 10- And indeed, over you are guardians is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of the verb you lie: meaning, you lie, while the state is that over you is someone who will repel your denial. It may also be a new sentence introduced to explain what invalidates their denial. The guardians are the angels who guard the deeds of the servants and record them in the records. God, the Almighty, described them as being honored by Him, writing down whatever He commands them to do of the servants' deeds.
82:12: Sentence 12- They know what you do is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun writers, or as a description, or as a new sentence. Al-Razi said: The meaning is to express astonishment at their state, as if he said: You deny the Day of Judgment, while God's angels are assigned to you, writing down your deeds until you are held accountable for them on the Day of Resurrection. Similar to this is the statement of God the Almighty: "On the right and on the left is one seated. Not a word does he utter but there is an observer by him, ready to record it."
82:13: Then the Almighty explained the state of the two groups, saying: 13- Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. The sentence is a new sentence to confirm this meaning for which it was presented, and it is like His Almighty saying: A group will be in Paradise and a group will be in the Blaze.
82:14: 14- And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire.
82:15: 15- They will burn it on the Day of Judgment is an attribute of Hellfire. It may be in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in the object of the preposition and noun, or as a new answer to an implied question, as if someone said, What is their state? So it was said, They will burn it on the Day of Judgment, meaning the day of recompense which they used to deny. The meaning of they will burn it is that they will be forced to endure its blazing heat and scorching heat on that day. The majority of scholars read they will burn it in the unstressed form as an active voice, and it was read with a shaddah as a passive voice.
82:16: 16- And they will not be absent from it meaning they will never leave it nor will they be absent from it, rather they are in it. It was said that the meaning is: They were not completely absent from it before that, rather they were finding its heat in their graves.
82:17: Then He, the Almighty, glorified that day, saying: 17- And what will make you know what is the Day of Judgment? Then what will make you know what is the Day of Judgment? That is, the Day of Recompense and Accountability. He repeated it to magnify its value, magnify its importance, and intimidate its matter, as in His statement: The Calamity * What is the Calamity * And what will make you know what is the Calamity? and The Inevitable * What is the Inevitable * And what will make you know what is the Inevitable? The meaning is: What made you aware of what is the Day of Judgment? Al-Kalbi said: The address is to the disbelieving person.
82:18: 18- Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
82:19: 19- The Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul, and the command that Day belongs to God. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read Day in the nominative case as a substitute for Day of Judgment, or as a predicate of a deleted subject. Abu Amr read in the narration Day with the tanween and the separation from the addition. The rest read it with the fatha as a fatha of syntactic construction with the estimation of I mean or I remember, so it is a direct object, or as a fatha based on its addition to the sentence according to the opinion of the Kufians, and it is in the nominative case as a predicate of a deleted subject, or as a substitute for Day of Judgment. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case, except that it is built on the fat-ha because it is added to the statement: does not possess. And what is added to the incapable may be built on the fat-ha, even if it is in the nominative case. What he mentioned is only permissible according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh if the addition is to a past tense verb. As for a future tense verb, it is not permissible according to them. Al-Zajjaj was agreed upon by Abu Ali Al-Farsi, Al-Farraa and others. The meaning is that no soul possesses anything of benefit or harm for another soul. And the command on that Day is God's alone. He does not possess anything of the command except Him, whatever it may be. Muqatil said: It means that a disbelieving soul has any benefit. Qatadah said: There is no one there who decides or makes anything except God, Lord of the worlds. The meaning is that God does not possess anything of the matters of that day as He possessed them in this world. Similar to this is His statement: To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To God, the One, the Prevailing. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when the seas overflow, he said: Some of them into others. Concerning his statement, And when the graves are scattered, he said: They are searched. Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, regarding his statement, A soul will know what it has put forward and left behind, he said: Whatever good it has put forward and whatever righteous practices it has left behind, which it acts upon without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hakim narrated, and authenticated it, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever follows a good example and follows it will have a reward like that of those who follow him, without that detracting from their reward. But whoever follows an evil example and follows it, will bear its burden and a burden like that of those who follow it, without that detracting from their burden.” Hudhayfah recited, A soul will know whatever it has put forward and left behind. Sa`id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of `Umar ibn al-Khattab that he recited this verse, What has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord? He said, God deceived him because of his ignorance. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas that he said, “God appointed two guardians over the son of Adam: one at night and two during the day, who record his deeds and write down his impact.”
83:1: It consists of thirty-six verses. Al-Qurtubi said: It is Meccan according to Ibn Masoud, Al-Dahhak and Muqatil, and Medinan according to Al-Hasan and Ikrimah. Muqatil said: It is also the first Surah revealed in Medina. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: It is Medinan except for eight verses from the words: {Indeed, those who commit crimes} to the end. Al-Kalbi and Jabir ibn Zayd said: It was revealed between Mecca and Medina. Al-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah Al-Mutaffifin was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr. Ibn Al-Durais narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah Al-Mutaffifin was the last to be revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Shu’ab. Al-Suyuti said with a saheeh chain of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, they were the worst people in measure, so God revealed: {Woe to those who defraud}, and after that they improved their measure. His statement: 1- Woe to those who defraud. Woe is the subject, and the justification for starting with it is that it is a supplication, and if it were in the accusative case, it would be permissible. Makki and Al-Mukhtar said: In Wail and the like, if it is not a noun with a genitive ending, it is nominative, and the accusative is permissible, but if it is in the genitive ending or a definite noun, the accusative is [al-Khasariya] for it, like His statement: Woe to you, do not slacken. Al-Muttaffifin is its predicate, and Al-Muttaffif is the one who reduces, and its true meaning is taking a small amount in measure or weight: i.e., a small and insignificant amount. Linguists said: Al-Muttaffif is derived from Al-Taffaf, which means little, so Al-Muttaffif is the one who reduces the right of his companion by decreasing it from the right in measure or weight. Al-Zajjaj said: The one who reduces the measure and scale is called Mutaffif because he hardly steals in the measure or scale except a small and insignificant amount. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Mubarrad said: Al-Muttaffif is the one who cheats in measure and weight. What is meant by Woe here is the severity of the torment, or the torment itself, or extreme evil, or it is a valley in Hell. Al-Kalbi said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came to Medina and they were mistreating others in their measure and weight, and taking full weight for themselves. So this verse was revealed. Al-Suddi said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came to Medina and there was a man there called Abu Juhayna, who had two measures with which he measured and with which he measured. So God revealed this verse. Al-Farra’ said: After the revelation of this verse, they have been the best people in measuring until this day.
83:2: Then God the Almighty explained who the defrauders are. He said: 2- Those who, when they take a measure from people, take in full meaning they take in full the measure and measure. Al-Farra’ said: They take in full from people and upon and from in this context are used interchangeably. It is said I took in full from you meaning I took in full from you. And you say I took in full on you meaning I took what was due from you. Al-Zajjaj said: When they take in measure from people, they take in full the measure and weight from them. He did not mention they weighed because buying and selling are done by measure and weight, so one indicates the other. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: It means those who, when they buy for themselves, take in full the measure and weight, but when they sell and weigh for someone else, they take less.
83:3: And this is the meaning of his saying: 3- And when they measure or weigh for them, they lose meaning they measure for them or weigh for them, so the lam was deleted and the verb transitive to the object, so it is from the category of deletion and connection. Similar to it is I advised you and I advised you, this is what Al-Akhfash, Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said. Al-Farra' said: I heard a Bedouin woman say: When the people come, we go to the merchant and he fills us with the mudd and the madd until the next season. He said: This is from the speech of the people of Al-Hijaz and those of Qais who lived near them. Al-Zajjaj said: It is not permissible to stop at kalawa until it is connected with the pronoun. Some people make it an emphasis: that is, an emphasis: that is, an emphasis of the pronoun implied in the verb, so they allow stopping at kalawa or waznawa. Abu Ubaid said: Isa bin Umar used to make them two letters, and stop at kalawa or waznawa, then say they are losing. He said: I think Hamza's reading is like this. Abu Ubaid said: The preferred option is for them to be one word for two reasons: One of them is the writing, and that is why they were written without an alif, and if they were disconnected, they would have been measured or weighed with an alif. The other is that it is said: I measured you and weighed you, meaning I measured for you and weighed for you, and this is Arabic speech, just as one says: I believed you and I saved for you, and I earned you and I earned for you, and I thanked you and I thanked you, and so on. It was said that it is with the deletion of the complement and the place of the complement to it, and the complement is the measured and the weighed: that is, if they measured their measured, or weighed their weighed, and the meaning of yakhsiroon is: they decrease, like his saying: And do not lose the balance, and the Arabs say: I lost the balance and I made it worse.
83:4: Then He, the Almighty, frightened them and said: 4- Do they not think that they will be resurrected? The sentence is a new sentence intended to emphasize the horror and enormity of what they did of cheating and to express astonishment at their state in daring to do it. The reference in His saying: those is to those who cheat, and the meaning is: that it does not occur to them that they will be resurrected and will be held accountable for what they do. It was said that the thought here means certainty: that is, those people are not certain, and if they were certain, they would not have reduced the measure and weight. It was also said that the thought is in its original form, and the meaning is: if they are not certain of the resurrection, why do they not think of it so that they may ponder it and search for it and abandon what they fear of its consequences? The Great Day is the Day of Resurrection, and it was described as great because it is a time for those great matters of resurrection, accountability, and punishment, and the entry of the people of Paradise into Paradise and the entry of the people of Hell into Hell.
83:6: Then He spoke about that Day, saying: 6- The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds. The circumstance is in the accusative case with the word resurrected mentioned before it, or with an implied verb indicated by resurrected. That is, they will be resurrected on the Day when mankind will stand, or as a substitute for the place of day, or with the omission of I mean, or it is in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, or in the genitive case as a substitute for the word day. It is built with the fat-ha in these two cases because it is added to the verb. Al-Zajjaj said: A Day is in the accusative case with the word resurrected," meaning: Do they not think that they will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection? The meaning of "The Day when mankind will stand" is the day when they will rise from their graves for the command of the Lord of the worlds, or for His recompense, or for His reckoning, or for His judgment and decree. Describing the Day as being great, with people standing before God in submission on it, and describing Him, glory be to Him, as the Lord of the worlds, indicates the greatness of the sin of the minor, the greatness of his sin, and the enormity of his punishment. It was said that what is meant by His saying: On the Day when people will stand is that they will stand up in their sweat up to the middle of their ears. It was also said that what is meant is that they will stand up to the rights of the servants upon them. It was also said that what is meant is the Messengers standing up before God to judge, and the first is more appropriate.
83:7: And His statement: 7- No! is for deterrence and warning to those who cheat and are heedless of the Resurrection and what comes after it. Then He resumed by saying: Indeed, the book of the wicked is in Sijjin. According to Abu Hatim, No has the meaning of truly connected to what comes after it, meaning: Truly, the book of the wicked is in Sijjin.
83:8: And the prisoner is what God the Almighty explained it with in His saying: 8- "And what will make you know what is the prison? * It is an inscribed book." So He informed us of this that it is an inscribed book: that is, written. It was said that it is a book that includes the evil deeds of the devils, the unbelievers, and the philosophers, and the word prisoner is a name for it. Qatada, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Muqatil, and Ka'b said: It is a rock under the seventh earth that is turned over, and the book of the wicked is placed under it. Mujahid said the same. So in the speech according to this saying there is an omitted complement, and the meaning is: the place of the inscribed book. Abu Ubaidah, Al-Akhfash, Al-Mubarrad, and Al-Zajjaj said: "In prison" means in confinement and severe constriction, and the meaning is: as if they are in confinement. He made that an evidence of the baseness and humiliation of their status.
83:9: Al-Wahidi said: Some people mentioned that His statement: 9- "A Book Marked" is an explanation of Sijjin, and this is far-fetched because Sijjin is not part of the Book at all, according to what we have narrated from the commentators. The correct view is to make it an explanation of the Book mentioned in His statement: "Indeed, the Book of the wicked" on the assumption that it is a Book Marked: meaning written, its letters have been made clear. End quote. The first is what we have mentioned, and the meaning would be: Indeed, the Book of the wicked, among whom are the defrauders: meaning, what is written of their deeds or the writing of their deeds is in that Book that records the ugly deeds, which is Sijjin. Then he mentioned what indicates its enormity and greatness, so he said: "And what will make you know what Sijjin is?" Then he explained it by saying: "A Book Marked." Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of His statement: "And what will make you know what Sijjin is" is that this is not something you or your people knew. Qatadah said: The meaning of Marked is that a human being has a mark for them, as if he knows a sign by which he is known to be an unbeliever. Muqatil said the same. They differed about the nun of sajīn. Some said that it is original and derived from sijn, which means confinement, and it is an exaggerated construction like khamir, sakir, and fasiq, from wine, drunkenness, and immorality. Abu Ubaidah, al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjaj said the same. One said: This is weak because the Arabs did not know sajīn. The response to this is that the narration of these imams establishes the evidence and indicates that it is from the language of the Arabs. From this is the saying of Ibn Muqbil: And the company beats the whites of the suburb with a beating that the heroes communicated with the prisoner It was said that the letter nun is a substitute for the letter lam, and the root is sajil, derived from sajil, which is the book. Ibn Atiyyah said: Whoever said that sajil is a place, then kitab is raised as the predicate of in, and the adverbial phrase in sajil is omitted. Whoever made it an expression for the book, then kitab is the predicate of a deleted subject, the estimation is: it is a book, and this speech is an explanation of sajil what is it? That is what he said. Ad-Dahhak said: Marqum is sealed in the Himyarite language, and the root of raqm is writing. The poet said: I will number the pure water to you, even though you are far away, if water has a number
83:10: 10- Woe on that Day to the deniers. This is connected to His saying: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, and what is between them is an interruption. The meaning is: Woe on the Day of Resurrection to whoever denied the Resurrection and what the Messengers brought.
83:11: Then the Almighty mentioned these deniers, saying: 11- Those who deny the Day of Judgment. The relative pronoun is an attribute of the deniers, or a substitute for it.
83:12: 12- And none denies it except every transgressor and sinner. That is, an immoral, unjust person who transgresses in sin and is immersed in its causes.
83:13: 13- When Our verses are recited to him, revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, he says, ‘Legends of the ancients,’ meaning their stories and falsehoods that they embellished. The majority of scholars read when they are recited with two fat-has. Abu Haywah, Abu al-Samak, al-Ashhab al-Uqayli, and al-Salami read it with a ta’.
83:14: And His statement: 14- "No!" is to deter and admonish the sinful aggressor from that false statement and to belie him. His statement: "Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts" explains the reason that led them to say that the Qur'an is legends of the ancients. Abu Ubaidah said: "Their hearts have covered themselves with a covering and a covering. Whatever overcomes you and overcomes you has covered you and covered you." Al-Farra' said: It is that they have committed many sins and transgressions, so it has covered their hearts, and that is the covering over them. Al-Hasan said: It is sin upon sin until the heart is blinded. Mujahid said: The heart is like the palm of the hand, and he raised his palm, and when he sinned, he would contract and close his finger, and when he committed another sin, he would contract and close another until he closed all of his fingers until his heart was sealed. He said: And they used to think that this was the covering. Then he recited this verse. Abu Zaid said: It is said that a man has become black with rust, if he has fallen into something from which he cannot escape and cannot bear it. Abu Muadh the grammarian said: Ruin is when the heart becomes black with sins, and stamping is when something is stamped on the heart, which is more severe than rust, and locking is more severe than stamping. Al-Zajjaj said: Ruin is like rust that covers the heart like a thin cloud, and the same is true of ghayn.
83:15: Then the Almighty repeated the deterrence and warning, saying: 15- "No indeed! Indeed, on that Day they will be veiled from their Lord. It was also said that No indeed" means: indeed, they - meaning the disbelievers - will never see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection. Muqatil said: It means that after the presentation and reckoning, they will not look at Him as the believers look at their Lord. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Just as He veiled them from His Oneness in this world, He will veil them from seeing Him in the Hereafter. Al-Zajjaj said: This verse is evidence that God, the Almighty, will see Him on the Day of Resurrection. Were it not for that, there would be no benefit in this verse. And the Almighty said: "Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, * Looking at their Lord." Thus, the Almighty informed us that the believers will look, and He informed us that the disbelievers will be veiled from Him. It was also said that this is a metaphor for their humiliation by the humiliation of one who is veiled from entering upon kings. Qatadah and Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: It means that He will not look at them with His mercy nor purify them. Mujahid said: They are veiled from His honor, and Ibn Kaysan said the same.
83:16: 16- Then they will surely enter Hellfire meaning they will enter Hellfire and remain in it, never leaving it. Then [the rank will be lowered], because entering Hellfire is more severe than humiliation and deprivation of dignity.
83:17: 17- Then it will be said, ‘This is what you used to deny.’ That is, the keepers of Hell will say to them, rebuking and reprimanding them: This is what you used to deny in this world, so look at it and taste it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: No people break a covenant except that God gives power over them to their enemy, and they do not give less in measure except that they are deprived of vegetation and are afflicted with famine. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds until one of them will be submerged in his sweat up to the middle of his ears. At-Tabarani, Abu Shaykh, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba’th narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said regarding this verse: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds. He said: How will it be when God gathers you together like arrows gathered in a quiver for fifty thousand years, without looking at you? Abu Ya’la, Ibn Hibban and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds will be for the duration of half a day of fifty thousand years, so that will be easy for the believer as the sun sets until it sets.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: When the people are gathered together, they will stand for forty years. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from his hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: O Messenger of God, how great will be the standing of people before the Lord of the Worlds on the Day of Resurrection? He said: A thousand years without permission being given to them. Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated in Az-Zuhd, and Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated through Shamr bin Atiyyah that Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b Al-Ahbar about the statement, No indeed! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin. He said, “The soul of the wicked ascends to the heavens, but the heavens refuse to accept it. So he descends with it to the earth, but it refuses to accept it. So he enters with it beneath seven earths until he reaches Sijjin, which is the cheek of Satan. Then a book is brought out for it from beneath the cheek of Satan, which is sealed and placed beneath the cheek of Satan.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said, Sijjin is the lowest of the earths. Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said, Al-Falaq is a covered pit in Hellfire, but as for Sijjin, it is open. Ibn Kathir said, It is a strange, rejected hadith that is not authentic. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Aisha, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said, Sijjin is the seventh lowest earth. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar hadith from Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Abd ibn Hamid, Ibn Majah, Al-Tabarani, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Ba’th narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik who said: When death approached Ka’b, Umm Bishr bint Al-Bara’ came to him and said: If you meet my son, give him my greetings. He said: May God forgive you, Umm Bishr, we are too busy for that. She said: Didn’t you hear the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: The soul of the believer roams freely in Paradise whenever it wishes, and the soul of the disbeliever is in Sijjin? He said: Yes. She said: So it is. Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated something similar on the authority of Salman. Ahmad, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Tirmidhi - who authenticated it - Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim - who authenticated it - Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu’ab narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When a servant commits a sin, a black spot is placed on his heart. If he repents, desists, and seeks forgiveness, his heart is polished. But if he returns to it, the blackness increases until it covers his heart. This is the rust that God Almighty mentioned in the Qur’an: ‘No! Rather, what they were earning has rusted over their hearts.’”
83:18: His statement: 18- No! is for deterrence and warning from what they were doing. Repetition is for emphasis. The phrase Indeed, the book of the righteous is in 'Illiyeen is a new sentence to explain what it includes. It is possible that Klla means truly, and the righteous are the obedient ones, and their book is their scrolls of good deeds. Al-Farra' said: Illiyeen is a height after a height with no limit. The reason for this is that it is derived from the plural of Ali from uluw. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the elevation of places. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: It is parsed like the plural because it is in the form of a plural and does not have a singular from the form of thirty, "twenty, and qansrin." It was said that it is a proper noun for the register of good deeds in which the deeds of the righteous are recorded. Al-Wahidi narrated from the commentators that it means the seventh heaven. Al-Dahhak, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: He means the seventh heaven in which are the souls of the believers. Al-Dahhak said: It is the Lote Tree of the Limit, to which everything related to God's command ends and they do not go beyond it. It was also said that it means Paradise. Qatada also said: It is above the seventh heaven at the right foot of the Throne. It was said that ‘Aliyyin’ is an attribute of the angels, for they are in the highest assembly, just as it is said that so-and-so is among the sons of so-and-so, meaning among them.
83:19: 19- And what will make you know what is ‘Ulyun? It is an inscribed book. That is, what will make you know, O Muhammad, what is ‘Ulyun’ in terms of glorification and exaltation of ‘Ulyun? Then he explained it by saying: An inscribed book, that is, written. The discussion of this is like the discussion that preceded it in His statement: And what will make you know what is ‘Sijjin’? It is an inscribed book.
83:21: Phrase 21- It will be witnessed by those brought near is another description of the Book, meaning that the angels will attend that written book, and it was said that they will witness what is in it on the Day of Resurrection. Wahb and Ibn Ishaq said: The ones brought near here are Israfil, so when the believer performs a righteous deed, the angels ascend with the scroll and it has a light that shines in the heavens like the light of the sun on earth until it reaches Israfil and he seals it.
83:22: Then the Almighty mentioned their state in Paradise after mentioning their book, saying: 22- Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss. That is, the people of obedience will be in great bliss, the extent of which cannot be measured.
83:23: 23- They are looking upon couches. The couches are the beds in the chambers. It was previously mentioned that the word couch does not refer to a bed unless it is in a chamber. Al-Hasan said: We did not know what couches were until a man from Yemen came to us and claimed that a couch, to them, is a chamber in which there is a bed. The meaning of they are looking is that they are looking at what God has prepared for them of honors. This is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, and others said. Muqatil said: They are looking at the people of Hellfire. It was also said that they are looking at His Face and Majesty.
83:24: 24- You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss meaning, if you see them, you will know that they are among the people of bliss because of what you see in their faces of light, beauty, whiteness, joy and splendor. The address is to every person who sees that which is appropriate for that. It is said that the plant is radiant: if it blossoms and shines. Ata’ said: That is because God increased their beauty and colors in a way that no describer can describe. The majority of scholars read ta’arafa with a fatha on the first letter and a kasra on the ra’, and nadhra with a nasb. Abu Ja’far ibn al-Qa’qa’, Ya’qub, Shaybah, Talhah and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a damma on the first letter and a fatha on the ra’, in the passive form, and nadhra with a damma as a substitute.
83:25: 25- And they will be given to drink from a sealed nectar. Abu Ubaidah, Al-Akhfash, Al-Mubarrad, and Al-Zajjaj said: Nectar is wine that has no adulteration or spoilage, and sealed is that which has a seal. Al-Khalil said: Nectar is the best wine. In As-Sahah, nectar is the yellowness of wine. Mujahid said: It is old, white, pure wine. From this is the saying of Hassan: They are watered with roses of geckos, and upon them is a papyrus that claps with pure nectar. Mujahed said: Sealed means sealed with clay, as if he meant sealing with clay, and the meaning is: that it is forbidden for any hand to touch it until its seal is broken for the righteous.
83:26: Saeed bin Jubair and Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i said: Its seal is its last taste, and this is the meaning of his saying: 26- Its seal is musk meaning its last taste is the scent of musk. When the drinker lifts his mouth from the end of his drink, he will smell its scent like the scent of musk. It was said that its vessels, such as cups and jugs, are sealed with bisque instead of clay, as if it is a metaphor for the perfection of its preciousness and the pleasantness of its scent. The point is that the sealed and the sealed things are made of clay and the like. The majority read it as its seal and Ali, Alqamah, Shafiq, Ad-Dahhak, Tawus and Al-Kisa'i read it as its seal with a fat-ha on the kha and the ta and an alif between them. Alqamah said: Have you not seen a woman say to the perfumer: Make his seal musk? Meaning its end. The seal and the seal are close in meaning, except that the seal is the noun and the seal is the verbal noun, as Al-Farra' said. He said in As-Sahah: And the seal is the clay with which it is sealed, and so said Ibn Zayd. Al-Farazdaq said: And you are by my side, the dead, and I prefer the closing covers And for that let the competitors compete meaning let those who desire desire. The reference in His statement: that is to the nectar described with that attribute. It was said that fi means to meaning, and to that let those who are quick to work hasten as in His statement: For the likes of this let the workers work. The origin of competition is quarreling over something and fighting over it, with each person wanting to be alone with it without the other. It is said that I thought something was precious to me meaning I thought it was precious to me and did not want it to come to me. Al-Baghawi said: Its origin is from the precious thing that people crave for, so each one wants it for himself and is miserly with it towards others, meaning he is stingy with it. Ata’ said: The meaning is, let the racers compete. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: Let the disputants compete.
83:27: And His saying: 27- And its mixture is of Tasneem is in apposition to its conclusion is musk which is another description of nectar: meaning, the mixture of that nectar is of Tasneem, which is a drink poured upon them from above, and it is the most noble drink of Paradise. The root of tasneem in the language is elevation, so it is a spring of water that flows from above to below, and from this comes the hump of a camel due to its height on its body, and from this comes the tasneem of graves.
83:28: Then he explained that, saying: 28- A spring from which the nearest to God drink. The accusative of 'ayn is an expression of praise. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a state of being. It is permissible for 'ayn to be a state of being while it is a solid, not derived noun, due to its being described by His statement: They drink from it. Al-Akhfash said: It is accusative with yasqunu they give to drink, meaning they give to drink from a spring, or from a spring. Al-Farra' said: It is accusative with tasnim they give to drink, as it is a verbal noun derived from sanam hump, as in His statement: Or feeding on a day of famine * an orphan. The first is more appropriate, and Al-Mubarrad said the same. It was said that the ba in bah is redundant, meaning he drinks it, or in the sense of from: meaning he drinks from it. Ibn Zayd said: It has reached us that it is a spring flowing from beneath the Throne. It was said that the nearest to God drink from it pure, and the cup of the companions of the right hand is mixed with it.
83:29: Then the Almighty mentioned some of the ugliness of the polytheists, saying: 29- Indeed, those who committed crimes - namely, the infidels of Quraysh and those who agreed with them in disbelief - were laughing at those who believed - meaning, in this world, they used to mock the believers and ridicule them.
83:30: 30- And when they pass by them meaning when the believers pass by the disbelievers while they are sitting in their gatherings, they wink at each other from the word ghams which is a gesture with the eyelids and eyebrows: meaning they wink at each other, and gesture with their eyes and eyebrows, and it was said that they taunt them about Islam and criticize them for it.
83:31: 31- And when they return meaning the disbelievers to their families from their gatherings they return in jest meaning admiring and enjoying what they are doing, joking about the believers, insulting them, mocking them and ridiculing them. Turning away means turning away. The majority read it as fakihin but Hafs, Ibn al-Qa’qa’, al-A’raj and al-Sulami read it as fakihin without an alif. Al-Farra’ said: They are two dialects, like greed and greed, and danger and danger. It was previously explained in Surat al-Dukhan that fakih means the arrogant and haughty person, and fakih means the soft and indulgent person.
83:32: 32- And when they see them, meaning when the infidels see the Muslims in any place, they say, ‘Indeed, these are astray,’ in their following of Muhammad, their adherence to what he brought, and their abandonment of the present comforts. It is possible that the meaning is: And when the Muslims see the infidels, they say this statement, and the first is more appropriate.
83:33: And sentence 33 - And they were not sent over them guardians is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of the verb they said: that is, they said that because they were not sent over the Muslims from God as guardians over them to preserve their conditions and actions.
83:34: 34- So today those who believe - meaning the Day: the Last Day - will laugh at the disbelievers meaning: that the believers on that day will laugh at the disbelievers when they see them humiliated and defeated and that the punishment has befallen them, just as the disbelievers laughed at them in this world.
83:35: The phrase on couches, looking is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of they laugh: that is, they laugh at them, looking at them and at the terrible state they are in. The explanation of couches has already been presented previously. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: When the people of Paradise want to look from their homes at the enemies of God while they are being tormented in the Fire, they laugh at them as they laughed at them in the world. Abu Salih said: The people of the Fire will be told, Come out and its gates will be opened for them. When they see that they have been opened, they will head towards it wanting to leave, while the believers are looking at them on couches. When they reach its gates, they will be closed in their face. This is what God says: So today those who believe laugh at the disbelievers.
83:36: 36- Is the reward of the disbelievers for what they used to do? The sentence is a resumption to explain that the punishment has befallen the disbelievers for what they did in this world of laughing at the believers and mocking them. The question is for confirmation, and garment means rewarded. The meaning is: Are the disbelievers rewarded for what they used to do to the believers? It was said that the sentence is in the accusative case because they are looking. It was also said that it is an implied statement: that is, some of the believers say to one another: Is the reward for the disbelievers? The reward is what comes back to the servant in return for his work and it is applied to good and evil. Ibn al-Mubarak, Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Shamr ibn Atiyyah that Ibn Abbas asked Ka'b al-Ahbar about the statement, Indeed, the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyyin. He said, "When the soul of the believer is taken, it is taken up to the heavens, and the gates of heaven are opened for it, and the angels meet it with glad tidings until it reaches the Throne. The angels ascend, and a parchment is brought out for it from beneath the Throne, which is numbered, sealed, and placed beneath the Throne to know its salvation for the Day of Judgment." Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, In 'Illiyyin, he said, Paradise. Concerning the statement, witnessed by those brought near, he said, The people of the heavens. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, A prayer following a prayer, with no idle talk between them, is a record in 'Illiyyin. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding the statement, The freshness of delight, he said, It is a spring in Paradise from which they perform ablution and bathe, and the freshness of delight flows over them. Abd bin Hamid, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Baath narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding the statement of God, {and they are given to drink from a sealed nectar}, he said: The nectar is wine, and the sealed they will find its conclusion to be the taste of musk. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding the statement of God, {sealed}, he said: mixed, its seal is musk he said: its taste and smell. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Baath on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, {from a nectar}, he said: wine, and the statement of God, {sealed}, he said: sealed with musk. Al-Faryabi, Al-Tabarani, Al-Hakim who authenticated it and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud regarding the statement of God, {its seal is musk}, he said: It is not a seal with which they seal, but it is mixed with musk. Have you not seen any of your women say, Its mixture is of such and such perfume. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, Its seal is musk. He said: It is a white drink like silver with which they seal their last drink. If a man from the people of this world were to put his fingers into it and then take them out, no living being would remain without smelling its fragrance. Abd Al-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Abd bin Humaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Tasneem is the most honorable drink of the people of Paradise. It is pure for the righteous and is mixed for the companions of the right hand. Ibn Al-Mubarak, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, Abd bin Humaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, Its mixture is of Tasneem. He said: It is a spring in Paradise that is mixed for the companions of the right hand and those brought near drink it pure. Abd bin Humaid and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the statement: Mixed with Tasneem, He said: This is among what God says: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes.
84:1: It is twenty-three verses, and it was said twenty-five verses It is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surat Al-Inshiqaq was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi’ that he said: “I prayed the Isha prayer with Abu Hurayrah and he recited ‘When the heaven is split asunder’ and prostrated. I said to him, and he said: ‘I prostrated behind Abu Al-Qasim (peace be upon him), and I will continue to prostrate during it until I meet him.’” Muslim, the Sunan scholars and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: “We prostrated with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) during ‘When the heaven is split asunder’ and ‘Read in the name of your Lord.’” Ibn Khuzaymah, Ar-Ruwayani in his Musnad and Ad-Diya’ Al-Maqdisi in Al-Mukhtara narrated on the authority of Buraydah that the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to recite ‘When the heaven is split asunder’ and similar surahs in the Dhuhr prayer.” His statement: 1- When the sky is split is like his statement, When the sun is wrapped up in the implication of the verb or its absence. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said that its splitting is one of the signs of the Day of Resurrection, and the meaning of its splitting is its bursting with white clouds as in His statement, And the Day the sky will split with clouds. And it was said that it will split from the galaxy, and the galaxy is the gate of the sky. There is a difference of opinion regarding the answer to if. Al-Farra’ said: She gave permission, and the waw is redundant, as is the case with laqa. Ibn al-Anbari said: This is a mistake, because the Arabs do not insert the “waw except with hatta even if, as in his statement: until when they came to it and its doors were opened and with lama when, as in his statement: So when they both submitted and he laid him down upon his forehead, * And We called to him Al-Anbari 2:11. It is not inserted with anyone other than these two. It was said that the answer is his statement: Then you will meet him, meaning you will meet him, and Al-Akhfash said the same. Al-Mubarrad said: “There is an inversion in the speech: O mankind, indeed you are striving towards your Lord with great striving, so you will meet Him when the sky is split open.” Al-Mubarrad also said: The answer is his statement: But as for he who is given his book in his right hand, and Al-Kisa’i said the same. The meaning is: If the sky is split, then he who is given his book in his right hand, his ruling is such and such. It was said that it is O man with the omission of the fa, and it was said that it is O man with the omission of the saying: that is, it is said to him, O man. It was said that the answer is omitted, its meaning is: you were sent, or every man will meet his work. It was said that it is what was stated explicitly in Surat al-Takwir 81:that is, this soul has known, on the assumption that if is conditional. It was said that it is not conditional and it is accusative by an omitted verb: that is, remember, or it is a subject and its predicate is the second if and the waw is additional and its meaning is: the time of the splitting of the sky is the time of the spreading of the earth.
84:2: The meaning of 2- and she gave permission to her Lord is that she obeyed Him in giving permission, which is listening to something and paying attention to it. And she had the right means that she had the right to obey, submit, and listen. Among the uses of permission in listening is the poet’s saying: Deaf when they hear good things mentioned to them, but when they hear bad things mentioned to them, they listen. And the other said: If they give permission for something suspicious, they fly away with it, rejoicing at my absence. But if they give permission for something good, they bury it. It was said that the meaning is: And God fulfilled for her the obligation to obey His command to split, meaning He made it a reality for her to do so. Ad-Dahhak said: She obeyed, and she had the right to obey her Lord because He created her. It is said that so-and-so has the right to do such-and-such, and the meaning of her obedience is that she does not refrain from what God wanted for her. Qatada said: She had the right to do that, and many say the same: If it is a reproach, then welcome and she deserves our reproach. I said:
84:3: 3- And when the earth is spread out meaning it is extended as leather is spread out, and its mountains are crushed until it becomes a smooth plain in which you will not see any crookedness or unevenness. Muqatil said: It is leveled like the extension of leather, so that no building or mountain will remain on it except that it is entered into it. It is also said that it is extended, meaning it is increased in its breadth, from madad, which means increase.
84:4: 4- And it cast out what was in it meaning it took out what was in it of the dead and treasures and cast them onto its back and was free of that. Saeed bin Jubair said: It cast out what was in its belly of the dead and was free of the living who were on its back. Similar to this is His statement: And the earth cast out its burdens.
84:5: 5- And she listened to her Lord meaning she heard and obeyed what He commanded her to do regarding throwing down and abandoning herself and she fulfilled her duty meaning she made it true by listening to that and submitting to it. The meaning of the two verbs was explained before this.
84:6: 6- O mankind refers to the human race, so it includes both believers and unbelievers. It has also been said that it refers to unbelieving humans, but the former is more appropriate because of the details that will follow. Indeed, you are striving toward your Lord with exertion. Toil in Arabic means to strive for something with effort, without distinguishing between whether that thing is good or bad. The meaning is that you are striving toward your Lord in your work or to meet your Lord. It is derived from the verb kadah to scratch his skin. Ibn Muqbil said: Life is nothing but two tarts, one of which I die, and the other I struggle to live. Qatada, Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kabī said: Do a deed for your Lord and then meet Him means that you will meet your deed. The meaning is that you will inevitably meet the reward for your deed and the reward and punishment that result from it. Al-Qatibi said: The meaning of the verse is: Indeed, you are striving meaning working hard and striving to make a living until you meet your Lord. Meeting means encounter, meaning you will meet your Lord with your deed. It was also said that it will be meeting the book of your deeds, because your deed has already been completed.
84:7: 8- But as for he who is given his record in his right hand, and they are the believers.
84:8: 8- Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning. There is no discussion about it. Muqatil said: Because his sins will be forgiven, but he will not be brought to account for them. The commentators said: It means that his bad deeds will be presented to him, then God will forgive them, so it is an easy reckoning.
84:9: 9- And he will return to his family, rejoicing. That is, after the easy reckoning, he will return to his family who are in Paradise from his clan, or to his family who were his in this world, from wives and children who preceded him to Paradise, or to those whom God has prepared for him in Paradise from the houris and immortal boys, or to all of these, rejoicing and happy with the goodness and honor he has been given.
84:10: 10- But as for he who is given his record behind his back, Al-Kalbi said: Because his right hand is chained to his neck, and his left hand is behind him. Qatada and Muqatil said: The panels of his chest and bones will be loosened, then his hand will enter and exit from his back, and he will take his record likewise.
84:11: 11- Then he will call for destruction meaning when he reads his book he will say: Woe to me, what destruction! And destruction is perdition.
84:12: 12- And he will burn in a Blaze meaning he will enter it and suffer the heat and intensity of its fire. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Asim read it with a fatha on the yaa, a sukoon on the sad, and a soft lam. The rest read it with a damma on the yaa, a fatha on the lam, and a shaddah on it. Ismail Al-Makki narrated on the authority of Ibn Kathir, and so did Kharijah on the authority of Nafi', and Ismail Al-Makki narrated on the authority of Ibn Kathir that they read it with a damma on the yaa and a sukoon on the sad from the root yashli.
84:13: 13- He was happy among his family meaning he was happy among his family in this world, following his desires and lusts out of arrogance and wickedness, because the afterlife did not cross his mind. The sentence explains what came before it.
84:14: Sentence 14- Indeed, he thought that he would never return is an explanation for him being happy in this world with his family. The meaning is that the reason for that happiness was his thought that he would not return to God nor be resurrected for judgment and punishment because of his denial of resurrection and his rejection of the Hereafter. In his saying, that he would never return, there is a lightened form of the heavy form, with what is in its scope, replacing the two objects of thought. To return in the language means to return. It is said that he returned: if he returned. Al-Raghib said: To hesitate in a matter, and from this we seek refuge in God from injustice after hesitation in a matter after continuing with it. To question a speech means to review it, and to consult it is to refer and to go back. Ikrimah and Dawud ibn Abi Hind said: Yahwar is an Ethiopian word and it means to return. Al-Qurtubi said: “Al-Hawr in the speech of the Arabs means to return, and from this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘O God, I seek refuge in You from Al-Hawr after Al-Kawr,’ meaning from returning to deficiency after increase. And likewise Al-Hawr with the dammah, and in the proverb ‘Hawr in Mahhar’: meaning deficiency in deficiency. And from this is the saying of the poet: And the blood is shed and the people are brought to the houris The houri also means destruction, and from this the rajaz poet said: In a well, there is no secret and no hair Abu Ubaidah said: That is, in the well of Hour, and there is no redundancy.
84:15: 15- Yes, indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him. Yes is an affirmation of the negation with lan: meaning, yes, he will surely be resurrected and resurrected. Then he explained that by saying, Indeed, his Lord was ever Seeing of him. Meaning, He was All-Knowing of him and of his deeds, and nothing of them was hidden from Him. Al-Zajjaj said: He was All-Knowing of him before He created him, knowing that he would return to Him.
84:16: 16- So I swear by the twilight la is redundant as mentioned previously in similar phrases. We have already mentioned the difference of opinion regarding it in Surat Al-Qiyamah, so refer to it. The twilight is the redness that occurs after sunset until the time of the final 'Isha' prayer. Al-Wahidi said: This is the opinion of all the commentators and linguists. Al-Farra' said: I heard some Arabs say: He was wearing a dyed garment as if it were the twilight, and it was red. Al-Qurtubi narrated this from most of the Companions, Followers, and jurists. Asad ibn Umar and Abu Hanifa said: In one of the two narrations from him, it means whiteness. This opinion has no basis or justification in either the Arabic language or Islamic law. Al-Khalil said: The twilight is the redness from sunset and its redness at the beginning of the night until close to darkness. The books of language and Islamic law agree on this, and from it is the saying of the poet: Rise up, boy, I mean, do not be confused by time with a cup filled with twilight Another said: Red as twilight
84:17: Mujahid said: The twilight is the whole day, don't you see it? He said: 17- And the night and what it covers. Ikrimah said: It is what remains of the day, and they both said this because of His statement after it: And the night and what it covers. So it is as if God the Almighty swore [by the light] and the darkness, and there is no basis for this, although it has been narrated from Ikrimah that he said: The twilight that is between sunset and evening, and it has been narrated from Asad bin Omar to return, And the night and what it covers. Wasq, according to the linguists, means to join something together. It is said that the camels are gathered together: if they are gathered and connected, and the shepherd brings them together. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators say: And what was gathered and joined, revealed, and wrapped, and the meaning is that it gathered and joined what was spread out during the day in its disposition, and that is because when the night comes, everything goes to its shelter, and from this is the saying of Dabi' bin Al-Harith Al-Barjami: I and you will come to you like someone who is holding something that his fingers have not reached. Akrima said, And what was driven means what was driven of something to its place of refuge. So he made it from the market, not from the gathering. It was also said, And what was driven means what was concealed and covered. It was also said, And what was driven means what was carried. And everything that you carried, you have carried. The Arabs say, I will not carry it as long as my eyes have carried the water, meaning I carried it. And the she-camel was driven, it was driven a wasqan, meaning it carried. Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: And what was driven and what was carried of darkness, or what was carried of the stars. Al-Qushayri said: The meaning of carrying is to gather and gather, and the night carries everything with its darkness. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: And what was driven: meaning what is done in it of praying at night and seeking forgiveness in the early hours of the morning, but the first is more appropriate.
84:18: 18- And the moon when it is full meaning it comes together and is complete. Al-Farra’ said: Its fullness means it is full, gathered, and straight on the night of the thirteenth and fourteenth to the sixteenth. It is derived from the verb wasq which means gathering. Al-Hasan said: It became full means it became full and gathered. Qatada said: It became round. It is said: I fed it so it became full, just as one says: I connected it so it became connected. It is also said: The matter of so-and-so is “massive, meaning gathered and regular. It is also said: Something is consistent if it is continuous.
84:19: 19- You will surely ascend from one level to another. This is the answer to the oath. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read Latarakubun with a fatha on the unified letter as addressing one person, namely the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), or anyone who is suitable for him. This is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-'Aliyah, Masruq, Abu Wa'il, Mujahid, Al-Nakha'i, Al-Sha'bi, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. The rest read it with a damma on the unified letter as Khataliban for the plural, namely the people. Al-Sha'bi and Mujahid said: O Muhammad, you will surely ascend from heaven to heaven. Al-Kalbi said: It means that you will ascend in them. This is according to the first reading. It was also said that it means: Level after degree and rank after rank in closeness to God and His exalted status. It was also said that the meaning is: You will surely ascend from one state to another, each state matching the other in difficulty. It was also said that the meaning is: O man, you will surely ascend from one state to another, from your being a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then alive, dead, rich, and poor. The address is to the human mentioned in His statement: O man, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with great striving. Abu Ubaid and Abu al-Hatim preferred the second reading. They said: "Because the meaning is more similar to the people than to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)." 'Umar read liyarrakban with the ta'ihah and the damma of the unified letter as a statement. It was narrated from him and Ibn 'Abbas that they read it in the third person and with the fatha of the unified letter: That man will surely ascend. It was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas that they read it with the kasrah of the present tense letter, which is a dialect. It was also read with the fatha of the present tense letter and the kasrah of the unified letter as an address to the self. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: The moon will surely ride through stages of secretion and its beginning, but this is far-fetched. Muqatil said: stage after stage means death and life. Ikrimah said: A suckling, then a weaned child, then a young man, then an old man. The place of stage is the accusative as an attribute of stage meaning stage passing stage, or as a state of the pronoun you will ride meaning passing, or passing.
84:20: 20- So why do they not believe? The question is for denial, and the fa is for arranging what comes after it of denial and amazement with what came before it of the conditions of the Day of Resurrection or other than it, based on the previous difference. The meaning is: What is it with the disbelievers that they do not believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what he brought of the Qur’an, despite the existence of reasons for believing in that.
84:21: 21- And when the Qur’an is recited to them, they do not prostrate. This conditional clause and its answer are in the accusative case as a state: meaning, what prevents them from prostrating and submitting when the Qur’an is recited? Al-Hasan, Ata’, Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Why do they not pray? Abu Muslim said: What is meant is submission and humility. It was also said that what is meant is the prostration itself known as the prostration of recitation. There has been a disagreement as to whether this is one of the places of prostration when reciting or not. The evidence for prostration has been presented in the opening of this surah.
84:22: 22- Rather, those who disbelieve deny meaning they deny Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the book he brought that includes proof of monotheism, resurrection, reward, and punishment.
84:23: 23- And God knows best what they conceal, meaning what they conceal in their hearts of disbelief. Muqatil said: They conceal their actions. Ibn Zayd said: They collect good and bad deeds, taken from the container that collects what is in it, and from this is the saying of the poet: Goodness is more lasting, even if it takes a long time, and evil is the most evil provision you can have. It is said that he memorized it, and he memorized the hadith, meaning he memorized it, and from this comes a listening ear.
84:24: 24- Then give them tidings of a painful punishment. That is, make that like good tidings for them, because His knowledge of that in the manner mentioned requires that they be punished. Painful means hurtful and hurtful, and the speech is not intended to mock them.
84:25: 25- Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is a reward uninterrupted. This exception is discontinuous: that is, but those who combine faith in God and righteous deeds - for them is a reward with God uninterrupted: that is, not cut off. It is said, I cut the rope: if you cut it, and from this is the saying of the poet: You see their creation from the speed of the return of semen as if it were dust. Al-Mubarrad said: Al-Manin is dust, because it cuts it behind it, and every weak person is Manin and Mannoon. It was said that the meaning of Ghair Mannoon is that he does not bestow it upon them, and it is permissible for the exception to be connected if it is meant from among them who believed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding his statement, When the heaven is split, he said: The heaven will be split from the galaxy. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And she listened to her Lord and was obedient, he said: She heard when He spoke to her. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, And she listened to her Lord and was obedient, he said: She obeyed and was obedient to obedience. Al-Hakim narrated on his authority and authenticated it, he said: She heard and obeyed. And when the earth is extended, he said: On the Day of Resurrection. And casts out what is in it, he said: It casts out what is in it of the dead, and abandons them.
