Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated on his authority, And casts out what is in it, he said: The golden bracelets. Al-Hakim narrated. Al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The earth will be extended on the Day of Resurrection like the extension of a hide, then there will be for the son of Adam only a place for his feet. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, you will be striving towards your Lord with great exertion, he said: Doing a deed. And meeting Him, he said: He will meet your deed. Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: No one is brought to account except that he will be destroyed. I said: Doesn’t God say: But as for him who is given his record in his right hand, * He will be brought to account with an easy reckoning? He said: That is not the reckoning, but the presentation, and whoever is called to account will be destroyed. Ahmad, ‘Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: “I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say in one of his prayers: ‘O God, call me to account with an easy reckoning.’ When he finished, I said: ‘O Messenger of God, what is an easy reckoning?’ He said: ‘That his record be looked at and he will be forgiven, for whoever is called to account will be destroyed.’” In some wordings of the first hadith and this other hadith: Whoever is called to account will be punished. Al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Bayhaqi and al-Hakim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There are three things in whom God will call to account with an easy reckoning and admit him into Paradise by His mercy: giving to the one who deprived you, forgiving the one who wronged you, and connecting with the one who severed you.” Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, He calls for destruction, he said: Woe. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, He thought that he would never be resurrected, he said: He would never be resurrected. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, That he would never be resurrected, he said: That he would never return. Samawayh narrated in his Fawa'id on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, he said: The twilight is the redness. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The twilight is the entire day. Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the night and what it covers, he said: And what is included in it. Abu Ubaid narrated in his Fada'il, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, And what it covers, he said: And what it gathers. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, And the moon when it is full, he said: When it is even. Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Anbari narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about his statement: And the night and what it covers. He said: And what it gathers. Have you not heard the statement: We have she-camels that are fast and easy to graze, if only they could find a driver. Abd ibn Humayd narrated from him, And the moon when it is full, he said: the thirteenth night. Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, You will surely ascend from one level to another, one state after another. Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn Abbas, You will surely ascend from one level to another, one state after another. He said: This is your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Ubayd in al-Qira’at, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Mani’, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he used to recite, You will certainly ascend from one level to another, meaning with a fat-ha on the ba’ of tarakun. He said: He meant your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one state after another. Al-Tayalisi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Tabarani narrated from him that he said: You will certainly ascend, O Muhammad, the sky, one level after another. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mundah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas’ud that he recited, You will certainly ascend from one level to another, meaning with a fat-ha on the ba’. He said: You will certainly ascend, O Muhammad, from one sky to another. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saeed ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu’ab narrated from him, You will surely ascend from one level to another. He said: It means the sky will crack, then split, then turn red. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi also narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: The sky will be like molten metal, and it will be rose-colored like oil, and it will be weak, and it will crack, and it will be one state after another. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And God knows best what they conceal, he said: They conceal.
85:1: It has twenty-two verses, and it is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Ad-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: By the sky with constellations was revealed in Mecca. Ahmad narrated: Abd Al-Samad narrated to us, Zuraiq bin Abi Salma narrated to us, Abu Al-Muhazzam narrated to us on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite in the last evening prayer: By the sky with constellations and By the sky and the nightcomer. At-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Shaybah in Al-Musannaf, Ahmad, Ad-Darimi, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, An-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, At-Tabarani, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Samurah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite in the noon and afternoon prayers: By the sky and the nightcomer and By the sky with constellations. His statement: 1- And the heaven with the mansions. The discussion of the mansions has already been presented in the interpretation of His statement, He has placed in the heaven mansions. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak said: They are the stars, and the meaning is: And the heaven with the stars. Ikrimah and Mujahid also said: They are palaces in the heaven. Al-Minhal ibn Amr said: They are those with good character. Abu Ubaidah, Yahya ibn Salam, and others said: They are the mansions for the planets, and they are twelve mansions for twelve planets, and they are Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. The mansions in the speech of the Arabs mean: palaces, and from this is His statement: And if you were in lofty towers, The mansions of these stars were likened to palaces because they descend into them. It was said that they are the gates of the heaven, and it was said that they are the mansions of the moon. The origin of the tower is appearance, and it was named thus because of its appearance.
85:2: 2- And the promised day meaning the promised day, which is the Day of Resurrection.
85:4: 4- He killed the companions of the trench. This is the answer to the oath, and the lam in it is implied, which is the apparent meaning, and this is what Al-Farra and others said. It was also said that its meaning is: He killed, so the lam and qad were deleted, and based on this the sentence is declarative, and it appears that it is a supplication, because the meaning of killed is to curse. Al-Wahidi said: According to everyone’s opinion, and supplication is not an answer to an oath, so it was said that the answer is his statement: Indeed, those who persecuted the believers. It was also said that his statement: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe. Al-Mubarrad said this: It was objected to due to the length of the chapter. It was said that it is understood and indicated by his statement: He killed the companions of the trench, as if he said I swear by these things that the infidels of Quraysh are cursed as the companions of the trench were cursed. It was also said that the meaning of the answer is: You will be resurrected, and Ibn Al-Anbari chose this. Abu Hatim al-Sijistani and Ibn al-Anbari also said: There is an estimation and a delay in the speech: meaning, the people of the trench and the sky with the constellations were killed. It was objected to that by saying that it is not permissible to say: By God, Zayd stood up. The trench is the great rectangular crack in the ground like a trench, and its plural is akhādīd. From this comes the word khid for the channels of tears, and the mukhada because the cheek is placed on it. It is said that a man’s face is takhdud if there are grooves in it from an abscess. From this comes the saying of Tarafa: A face as if the sun had cast its cloak over it, pure in color and unblemished. The hadith of the People of the Trench will be explained, God willing.
85:5: The majority read 5- The fire of fuel with the fire in the genitive case as a badal ishtalm of the trench because the trench includes it, and the one of fuel is a description of it as a great fire, and fuel: the wood that is lit with, and it was said that it is a badal kull of kull, not a badal ishtalm. And it was said that fire is in the genitive case as a jawar, this is what Makki narrated from the Kufians. The majority read with the fatha on the waw of fuel, and Qatada, Abu Raja and Nasr bin Asim read with the damma. Ashhab Al-Uqaili, Abu Haywah, Abu Al-Samak Al-Adawi, Ibn Al-Sameefa and Isa read with the fire in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning it is the fire, or as the subject of a deleted verb: meaning you burned the fire.
85:6: 6- When they were sitting by it The agent in the adverbial phrase is killed: meaning they were cursed when they surrounded the fire sitting on things that were close to it and brought near to it. Muqatil said: meaning sitting by the fire, exposing them to disbelief. Mujahid said: They were sitting on chairs by the trench.
85:7: 7- And they are witnesses to what they do to the believers meaning those who dug the trench, namely the king and his companions, to what they do to the believers of exposing them to the fire so that they return to their religion are witnesses: meaning present, or some of them will testify to each other before the king that he did not fall short in what he was commanded. And it was said that they will testify to what they did on the Day of Resurrection, then their tongues, hands and feet will testify against them. And it was said that on means with, and the meaning is: and they are witnesses to what they do to the believers. Al-Zajjaj said: God knows the story of a people whose insight and the truth of their faith reached the point that they were patient to be burned in the fire for the sake of God.
85:8: 8- And they did not find fault with them meaning they did not deny them or criticize them except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy: meaning, except that they believed in God, the Prevailing, the Bearer in every situation. Al-Zajjaj said: They did not find fault with them for any sin except their belief, and this is like his saying: Do you find fault with us except that we believed in God? This is an emphasis on praise with something resembling blame, as in his saying: There is nothing wrong with them except that the residents are entertained by them, away from their families, homelands and servants. The other said: There is no defect in her except the shape of her eyes, just like the shape of the eyes of a free-ranging bird. The public read naqamū with a fathah on the nūn, while Abu Haywah read it with a kasrah, and the eloquent one reads it with a fathah.
85:9: Then the Almighty described Himself with what indicates greatness and magnificence, saying: 9- To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And whoever is like this, then he is worthy of believing in Him and unifying Him. And God is Witness over all things. Nothing of what they did to the believers is hidden from Him. In this is a severe threat to the people of the trench, and a promise of good for those of those believers whom they tortured for their religion.
85:10: Then the Almighty explained what He has prepared for those who did to the believers what they did of burning, saying: 10- Indeed, those who have put the believing men and believing women to trial and then have not repented will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning Fire. That is, they burned them with fire. The Arabs say: fatanat al-shay’ meaning they burned it. Fattanat al-dirham or al-dinar means if you put it in the fire to see its quality. It is said that a dinar is fatanat, and the goldsmith is called fattan. And from this is His statement: {On the Day when they will be tested over the Fire, they will be burned. It was said that the meaning of they tested the believers is that they tested them in their religion so that they would abandon it, but they did not repent from their evil deeds and abandon their disbelief and their temptation. So for them is the punishment of Hell. That is, for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of Hell because of their disbelief. The clause is in the nominative case as the predicate of in, or the predicate is for them. And the punishment of Hell is raised by it as an agent. The fa is to include the subject with the meaning of a condition, and its abrogation by an does not harm, contrary to Al-Akhfash. And for them is the punishment of burning. That is, for them is another punishment in addition to the punishment of their disbelief, which is the punishment of burning that they inflicted upon the believers. It was said that burning is a name for Hell, like blazing fire. It was said that they are tormented in Hell with freezing cold, then they are tormented with the punishment of burning. So the first is the punishment of its cold, and the second is the punishment of its sea. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: The punishment of burning afflicted them in this world, and that is because the fire rose from the trench to the king and his companions and burned them. Al-Kalbi said the same.
85:11: Then the Almighty mentioned what He has prepared for the believers who were burned in the fire, saying: 11- Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds The apparent meaning of the verse is general, so those who were burned in the trench because of their faith are included in this primarily. The meaning is that those who combine faith and righteous deeds for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow: that is, for them, because of faith and righteous deeds, are gardens with this description. The manner in which rivers flow beneath the gardens has been mentioned in more than one place, and we have explained that if what is meant by gardens is the trees, then the flow of rivers beneath them is clear. If what is meant by it is the earth that encompasses them, then the underneath is in consideration of its visible part, which is the trees, because they cover its courtyard. The reference in His saying: that is to what was mentioned previously of what God has prepared for them: that is, what is mentioned is the great triumph which no other triumph is equal to, comparable to, or comparable to, and triumph is the attainment of what is sought.
85:12: And sentence 12 - Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe is a resumption of the address to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, based on what God Almighty has of punishment for those who disobey Him, and forgiveness for those who obey Him: meaning His punishment of the tyrants and oppressors is severe, and punishment means taking violently, and describing it as severe indicates that it has been doubled and intensified, and similar to this is His statement: Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe.
85:13: 13- It is He who begins and repeats. That is, He creates first in this world and brings them back to life after death. This is what the majority said. It was also said that He begins the punishment of burning for the unbelievers in this world and then repeats it for them in the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir chose this view, and the first is better.
85:14: 14- And He is the Forgiving, the Loving meaning He is the One who forgives the sins of His believing servants and does not disgrace them because of them. He is the One who loves the obedient among His friends. Mujahid said: The Loving is for His friends, so it is a verb with the meaning of a fa'il. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning of the Loving is the Most Merciful. Al-Mubarrad narrated on the authority of Ismail Al-Qadi that the Loving is the one who has no children, and he recited: I ride in the fear, naked, docile, winged, friendly, and affectionate That is, she has no children to yearn for. It was said that al-Wadud means al-Mawaddud, meaning that His righteous servants love and adore Him. This is what al-Azhari said. He said: It is also possible for fa’ul to have the meaning of fa’il, meaning that He loves them. He said: Both attributes are praiseworthy, because if He, the Most High, loves His obedient servants, then this is a favor from Him, and if His knowledgeable servants love Him, it is because of what is established in them of His generous kindness.
85:15: The majority read 15- Possessor of the Glorious Throne by raising the word Majid as an adjective for Possessor, and this reading was chosen by Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. They said: Because glory is the ultimate in generosity and favor, and God, the Most High, is the one described with that. The Kufians except Asim read it with the accusative as an adjective for the Throne. God, the Most High, described His Throne as generous, as in the end of Surat Al-Mu'minun. It was said that it is an adjective for your Lord, and separating them does not harm because they are attributes of God, the Most High. Makki said: It is report after report, and the first is better. The meaning of Possessor of the Throne is: Possessor of dominion and authority, as one says: So-and-so is on his royal throne, and from this is the saying of the poet: They saw my throne with cracks on its sides, so when it was cracked, they set me apart. And the other said: If they kill you, their thrones will be destroyed by Otaiba bin Al-Harith bin Shihab. It was said that it means the Creator of the Throne.
85:16: 16- Fa'al li-ma yurayid meaning from showing and repeating. Ata' said: He is not unable to do anything He wants and nothing He asks for is prevented from Him. The nominative case of Fa'al is as the predicate of a deleted subject. Al-Farra' said: It is a nominative case of repetition and resumption, because it is a purely indefinite noun. Ibn Jarir said: The nominative case of Fa'al, which is a purely indefinite noun, follows the i'rab of Al-Ghafur Al-Wadud. He only said Fa'al because what He wants and does is extremely frequent.
85:17: Then the Almighty mentioned the report of the disbelieving crowds, saying: 17- Has there come to you the report of the armies? The sentence is a resumption of what came before of the severity of His might, the Almighty, and His being the doer of what He wills. It contains consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: meaning, has there come to you, O Muhammad, the report of the disbelieving crowds who reject their prophets and are mobilized against them?
85:18: Then He talked between them and said: 18- Pharaoh and Thamud which is a substitute for the soldiers. What is meant by Pharaoh is him and his people, and what is meant by Thamud are the well-known people, and what is meant by their story is what occurred from them of disbelief and stubbornness and what was inflicted upon them of punishment, and their story is well-known and it is mentioned repeatedly in the Noble Book in more than one place, and He limited it to the two groups because their matter was well-known among the People of the Book and the polytheists of the Arabs, and He indicated by them their likes.
85:19: Then he turned away from comparing these infidels who were present in his time, may God bless him and grant him peace, to those mentioned above, and he explained that they were more severe in their disbelief and denial than them, so he said: 19- Rather, those who disbelieved are in denial, meaning, rather, these polytheists among the Arabs are in severe denial of you and what you have brought, and they did not take heed from those who came before them from the infidels.
85:20: 20- And God is encompassing them from behind. That is, He is able to bring down upon them what He brought down upon those. To encompass something means to limit it from all sides. This is a metaphor for their not being saved because what is encompassed by it does not escape the encompassing One.
85:21: Then the Almighty responded to their denial of the Qur’an, saying: 21- Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, meaning it is the ultimate in honor, generosity, and blessing, because it is an explanation of what God has prescribed for His servants of religious and worldly rulings. It is not, as they say, poetry, divination, and magic.
85:22: 22- In a Preserved Tablet meaning written in a tablet, which is the Mother of the Book, preserved with God from the devils' reach. The majority of scholars read Preserved in the accusative case as an adjective for the Tablet. Nafi' read it in the nominative case as an adjective for the Qur'an, meaning, Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an preserved in a tablet. The reciters agreed to open the lam of lawh except for Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Ibn as-Samee', who read it with a damma. Muqatil said: The Preserved Tablet is to the right of the Throne. It was said that what is meant by Lawh with a damma on the lam is the air above the seventh heaven. Abu al-Fadl said: The Lawh with a damma on the lam means the air, and Ibn Khalawayh said the same. It is stated in As-Sahah: The Lawh with a damma means the air between the heaven and the earth. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Buruj the constellations are palaces in the sky. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about “the sky with constellations,” and he said: The stars. He was asked about His statement, Who has placed constellations in the sky, and he said: The stars. And about His statement, in lofty constellations, he said: The palaces.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And the Promised Day, and a witness and one witnessed, that he said: The Promised Day is the Day of Resurrection, and the witness is Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah, which is the greatest pilgrimage. So God made Friday a celebration for Muhammad and his nation and favored him over all of creation, and it is the master of days in the sight of God, and the most beloved of deeds to God, and in it there is an hour when no Muslim servant prays and asks God for good except that He gives it to him. Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed day is the Day of Arafah, and the witness is Friday. The sun does not rise or set on a day better than it. In it is an hour when no believing servant supplicates to God for good happens to it except that God answers him, and no one seeks refuge from anything except that He protects him from it.” Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: And the witness and the witnessed. He said: The witness is the Day of Arafah and Friday, and the witnessed is the promised day on the Day of Resurrection. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed is the Day of Sacrifice, and the witness is Friday. Ibn Jarir, Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witness is Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Jubayr ibn Mut’im, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said regarding the verse: The witness is Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Abd ibn Humayd narrated a similar hadith from Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Saeed ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The master of days is Friday, and it is the witness, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah. This is a mursal from the mursals of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab. Ibn Majah, al-Tabarani and Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu al-Darda’ that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Increase your prayers upon me on Friday, for it is a witnessed day witnessed by the angels. Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib regarding the verse: The witness is Friday and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali that a man asked him about the verse: And a witness and the witnessed. He said: Have you asked anyone before me? He said: “Yes, I asked Ibn Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: The day of sacrifice and Friday.” He said: No, but the witness is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Then he recited, And We have brought you as a witness over these and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited, That is a Day when mankind will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day. Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and al-Saghir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Ali regarding the verse, he said: The witness is my grandfather, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited, Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and That is a witnessed Day. Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, and the witness is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited, That is a Day when mankind will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, he said: The witness is God, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, he said: The witness is God. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, he said: The witness is God, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. I said: These interpretations of the Companions may God be pleased with them have differed as you can see, and so have the interpretations of the Successors after them. Those who provided evidence cited verses in which God mentioned that something is a witness or witnessed, making it evidence that what is meant by the witness and witnessed in this general verse. However, this is not evidence that the witness and witnessed mentioned in this context are the same witness and witnessed mentioned in another verse. Otherwise, His statement here, a witness and a witnessed, would have to be everything that is mentioned in the Noble Qur’an or the pure Sunnah, that testifies that it is witnessed. Not some of what they used as evidence, despite their differences, are more valid than others, and no one has said that. If you say: Is there in the marfu’ (upon whom be peace) that you mentioned from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, the hadith of Abu Malik, the hadith of Jubair ibn Mut’im, and the mursal hadith of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab that designates this promised day, the witness and the witnessed? I said: As for the Promised Day, these narrations in which it is mentioned do not differ, rather they agree that it is the Day of Resurrection. As for the witness, in the first hadith of Abu Hurairah it is Friday, and in his second hadith it is Friday, and in the mursal of Sa`id it is Friday, and in his second hadith it is the Day of Arafah and Friday, and in the hadith of Abu Malik it is Friday, and in the hadith of Jubayr it is Friday, and in the mursal of Sa`id it is Friday. So these hadiths agree on it, and the addition of the Day of Arafah to it in the second hadith of Abu Hurairah does not harm. As for the witnessed, in the first hadith of Abu Hurairah it is the Day of Arafah, and in the second hadith it is the Day of Resurrection, and in the hadith of Abu Malik it is the Day of Arafah, and in the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mu`tam it is the Day of Arafah, and likewise in the hadith of Sa`id, it has been determined in these narrations that it is the Day of Arafah, and they are more valid than that narration in which he stated that it is the Day of Resurrection. So from the sum of this we obtain the validity of what the majority of the Companions, Followers, and those after them went with, that the witness is Friday and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah. As for the Promised Day, we have mentioned that there was consensus that it is the Day of Resurrection. And Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Suhayb that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There was a king among the kings who came before you, and that king had a soothsayer who used to soothsay for him. The soothsayer said to him: ‘Find me a boy who is intelligent, or he said, intelligent and able to teach him my knowledge. I fear that if I die, this knowledge will be cut off from you and there will be no one among you who can teach it.’ So they looked for him as he had described, and ordered him to bring that soothsayer and to visit him. The boy kept going to him. There was a monk in a monastery on the boy’s way, and the boy kept asking that monk every time he passed by. He kept asking him until he told him, and he said: ‘I only worship God.’ The boy kept staying with that monk and was slow to respond to the soothsayer. The soothsayer sent word to the boy’s family that he was rarely there. The boy informed the monk of that, and the monk said to him: ‘If he asks you where you have been, say with my family. If your family asks you where you have been, say with my family.’ “I was? So he told them that I was with the priest, and between them the boy passed by a large group of people who had been trapped by a beast, which was said to be a lion. The boy took a stone and said: “O God, if what that monk says is true, then I ask You to kill this beast, and if what the priest says is true, then I ask You not to kill it.” Then he threw and killed the beast. The people said: Who killed it? They said: The boy. The people were alarmed and said: This boy has learned knowledge that no one else has. A blind man heard him and came to him and said: If you restore my sight, then you will have such and such. The boy said: I do not want this from you, but tell me, if your sight is restored, will you believe in the One who restored it? He said yes. So he prayed to God and his sight was restored to him, and the blind man believed. The report of their matter reached the king, so he sent for them and brought them and said: I will kill each one of you in a way that I would not kill his companion. So he ordered the monk and the man who was blind, and he placed the saw on the parting of one of them and killed him, and he killed the other in a different way. Then he ordered the boy and said: Take him to such-and-such a mountain and throw him from his head. So they took him to that mountain. When they reached the place from which they wanted to throw him, they began to rush down from that mountain and fall until none of them remained except the boy. Then the boy returned, and the king ordered that they take him to the sea and throw him in. So they took him to the sea, and God drowned those who were with him and saved him. The boy said to the king: You will not kill me until you crucify me and throw me and say when you throw me: In the name of God, Lord of the boy. So he ordered him to pray, then he threw him and said: In the name of God, Lord of the boy. So the arrow crackled in his temple, and the boy put his hand on The place of the arrow then he died. The people said: This boy has learned knowledge that no one else has. We believe in the Lord of this boy. The king was asked: Are you alarmed that three people have opposed you? All of these scholars have opposed you. He said: Dig a trench and throw wood and fire into it. Then gather the people and say: Whoever renounces his religion we will leave him alone, and whoever does not we will throw into this fire. So he started throwing them into that trench and said: God says: The companions of the trench were killed * The fire fueled until he reached The Almighty, the Praiseworthy. As for the boy, he was buried and then taken out. It is mentioned that he was taken out during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab with his finger on his temple as he had placed it when he was killed. This story has some different wording. Muslim narrated it at the end of Sahih Muslim on the authority of Hudbah ibn Khalid on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila on the authority of Suhaib. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Affan on the authority of Hammad on his authority. An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sulayman on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Mahmud ibn Ghailan and Abd ibn Hamid on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Thabit. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib regarding the verse, The Companions of the Trench, he said: They are the Abyssinians. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: They are people from the Children of Israel who dug a trench in the ground and lit a fire in it, then they made men and women stand by that trench and expose themselves to it. Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated who authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, he said: And the heaven with its mansions to the verse, And a witness and what is witnessed, he said: This is an oath based on Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe to the end of it. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, Indeed, it is He who begins and repeats, he said: He begins the punishment and repeats it. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma’ wa’l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, The Loving, he said: The Beloved. And regarding the verse, Possessor of the Majestic Throne, he said: The Generous. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: In a Preserved Tablet, he said: I was informed that it is the Tablet of Remembrance, a single tablet in which is the Remembrance, and that that Tablet is of light, and that it is a journey of three hundred years. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: The Preserved Tablet that God mentioned in His statement: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, in a Preserved Tablet, is on the forehead of Israfil. Abu al-Shaykh narrated, and al-Suyuti said with a good chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God created the Preserved Tablet as a journey of one hundred years, then He said to the Pen before He created creation: Write My knowledge in My creation, so what will happen flowed until the Day of Resurrection.
86:1: It has seventeen verses, and it is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: By the sky and the nightcomer was revealed in Mecca. Ahmad, Al-Bukhari in his history, Al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Khalid Al-Adwani, “He saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the market of Thaqif, standing on a bow or a staff when he came to them seeking victory from them. He heard him recite “By the sky and the nightcomer” until he finished it. He said: I memorized it in the pre-Islamic era, then I recited it in Islam. He said: Thaqif called me and said: What did you hear from this man? So I recited it, and those of Quraysh who were with them said: We know our companion best. If we knew what he was saying was true, we would follow him.” 1- By the heaven and the nightcomer. God Almighty swears by the heaven and the nightcomer, which is the piercing star as stated in the revelation. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: God swore by the heaven and the nightcomer, meaning the stars that come at night and disappear during the day. Al-Farra’ said: The nightcomer is the star because it rises at night, and whatever comes to you at night is a nightcomer. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Mubarrad said the same: And from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: And like you, a pregnant woman who has been knocked on the door, and a nursing mother who has been distracted by amulets that have been changed. He also said: Haven't you seen that whenever I come knocking, I find her fragrant, even if she is not fragrant? There is a difference of opinion about Al-Tariq, is it a specific star or a type of star? Some say it is Saturn, some say it is the Pleiades, some say it is the one that the devils throw at, and some say it is a type of star. It says in Al-Sahah: Al-Tariq is the star that is called the morning star, and from it is the saying of Hind bint Utbah: We, Tariq's daughters, walk on cushions That is, our fathers are like the shining star in honor. The origin of the word to knock is penetrating. So, the one who intends to come at night is called tariq because he needs to knock to arrive. Some people said that to knock may occur during the day. The Arabs say, I came to you today, knocking twice. This is based on the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I seek refuge in You from the evil of the night and day visitors, except for a visitor who knocks with good.
86:2: Then the Almighty explained what the Nightcomer is, to magnify its importance after glorifying it by swearing by it, saying: 2- And what will make you know what the Nightcomer is? It is the piercing star. Piercing means shining, and from this it is said that the star pierced holes and holes if it illuminated, and its holes are its light, and from this the poet said: He spread it among the people until it was as if there was a fire lit in the highlands with holes. Al-Wahidi said: Al-Tariq refers to everything that knocks at night. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have known what was meant by it if he had not made it clear by saying: The piercing star. Mujahid said: The piercing, glowing one. Sufyan said: Everything in the Qur’an, And what do you know? He has informed us of, but everything for which He said: And what do you know? He has not informed us of.
86:3: 3- The statement, The piercing star, is raised as if it is the predicate of a deleted subject, and the sentence is a resumption of the answer to an implied question that arose from what preceded it, as if it was said, What is it? So it was said, It is the piercing star.
86:4: 4- Indeed, every soul has a protector over it. This is the answer to the oath, and what is between them is an objection. The difference of opinion among the reciters about lama has been mentioned previously in Surah Hud. Whoever reads it with a light in is the lightened one from the heavy one, which contains the pronoun of the matter, which is its subject, and the lam is the distinguishing letter. Ma is an additional letter: meaning, the matter is that every soul has a protector over it. Whoever reads it with a shaddah, inna is a negative letter, and lama means illa: meaning, there is no soul but that it has a protector over it. Ibn Aamer, Aasim, and Hamza have read it with a shaddah here. The rest have read it with a lightened letter. It has been said that the protector is God, the Almighty, and it has been said that it is the mind that guides them to what is good and restrains them from what is bad. The first is more appropriate, based on His statement: And indeed, over you are guardians, and His statement: And He sends guardians over you, and His statement: He has guardians before him and behind him who guard him. The guardian in truth is God Almighty, as in His statement: So God is the best guardian, and the guardianship of the angels is from His guardianship because they are by His command.
86:5: 5- So let man consider from what he was created. The fa indicates that the fact that every soul has a guardian requires man to reflect on the beginning of his creation so that he may know God’s ability to accomplish what is less than that of resurrection. Muqatil said: The one who denies the resurrection means from what he was created from what thing God created him. The meaning is: So let him consider with contemplation and reasoning so that he may know that the One who created him from a pure substance is able to restore him.
86:6: 6- He created from gushing water The sentence is a new chapter in answer to an implied question. Water is semen, and gushing means pouring. It is said I poured the water meaning I poured it. It is said gushing water meaning it is poured, like A satisfied life meaning pleasing. Al-Farraa' and Al-Akhfash said: Gushing water means poured into the womb. Al-Farraa' said: The people of Al-Hijaz make the subject mean the object in much of their speech, like their saying: A hidden secret meaning concealed, and They are erect meaning erected, and A sleeping night and the like. Al-Zajjaj said: From gushing water, it is said Dare', Qays and Nabel meaning one with a shield, bow and arrows. God the Almighty meant the water of the man and the woman because man is created from them, but He made them one water because they mix.
86:7: Then he described this water, saying: 7- It comes forth from between the backbone and the ribs meaning the back of the man, and the ribs of the woman, and the ribs are the plural of taraba, which is the place of the necklace on the chest, and the child is only from the two waters. The majority read comes forth in the active form. Ibn Abi Ubla and Ibn Muqsim read it in the passive form. And in the back: which is the back, there are languages. The majority read it with a damma on the sad and a sukoon on the lam, and the people of Mecca read it with a damma on the sad and the lam. The Yemeni read it with a fatha on them, and it is said salib on the weight of qalib. And from it is the saying of Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib: Transfer from loins to uterus In his famous verses in praise of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. We have already discussed this when interpreting his statement: those from your loins. It was said that the clavicles are what is between the breasts. Ad-Dahhak said: The clavicles of a woman are the hands, feet, and eyes. Saeed bin Jubayr said: They are the neck. Mujahid said: They are what is between the shoulders and the chest. It was also narrated from him that he said: They are the chest. It was also narrated from him that he said: They are the collarbones. Az-Zajjaj narrated that the clavicles are the juice of the heart, and from it the child is born. It is well-known in the language that they are the bones of the chest and throat, and from this is the saying of Duraid bin As-Summah: If you turn back, we will seize you by your backs, and if you accept, we will seize you by your collarbones. Akrima said: The collarbones are the chest, and he recited: A system of pearls on her collarbones He said in Al-Sahah: The singular of taraba is taraba, which are the bones of the chest. Abu Ubaidah said: The plural of taraba is tarib, and from this is the saying of Al-Muthaqab Al-Abdi: And the gold of Benin on a tree like the color of ivory, without branches And the saying of Imru' al-Qais: Her collarbones are polished like a chain Al-Zajjaj narrated: The ribs are four ribs on the right side of the chest, and four ribs on the left side of the chest. Qatada and Al-Hasan said: The meaning is: It comes out from the man’s back and the woman’s ribs. Al-Farra’ narrated that something like this comes from the Arabs, meaning from between the backbone, from the backbone. It was said that the man’s semen descends from the brain, and this does not contradict what is in the verse, because if it descends from the brain, it descends from between the backbone and the ribs. It was said that the meaning is: It comes out from all parts of the body, and this does not contradict what is in the verse, because the attribution of its exit to between the backbone and the ribs is based on the fact that the majority of parts of the body are the backbone and the ribs and what is adjacent to them and above them from which it descends.
86:8: 8- He is indeed Able to return him. The pronoun in He is indeed refers to God, the Exalted, because of the meaning of His statement: He created him. The One who created him is God, the Exalted, and the pronoun in He returned him refers to the human being. The meaning is that God, the Exalted, is able to return the human being, i.e., to resurrect him after death. This is what a group of commentators said. Mujahid said: On the basis that the water returns to the urethra. Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: On the basis that the water returns to the loins. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: If you wish, you can return him from old age to youth, from youth to childhood, and from childhood to sperm. Ibn Zayd said: He is indeed Able to hold back that water so that it does not come out. The first is more evident, and it was preferred by Ibn Jarir, Ath-Tha'labi, and Al-Qurtubi.
86:9: 9- The Day when secrets are exposed. The agent in the adverbial phrase according to the first interpretation is He returned it, and it was said that it is capable. It was objected that it is necessary to specify the ability to this day, and it was said that the agent in it is understood: that is, He returns it on the Day when secrets are exposed, and it was said that the agent in it is understood, and it is remember, so it is a direct object. As for the saying of those who said that what is meant is the return of the water, then the agent in the adverbial phrase is understood, and it is remember, and the meaning of secrets are exposed: they are tested and known, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: Before today you used to despise me, but today you will test me and afflict me. That is, I test you and you test me, I test you and you test me, and the secrets: what is hidden in the hearts of beliefs, intentions, etc., and what is meant here is the presentation of deeds and the publication of records, then the good among them is distinguished from the bad, and the worthless from the valuable.
86:10: 10- For him there is no power or helper meaning that man has no power within himself to protect himself from God's punishment, nor any helper to protect him from what has befallen him. Ikrimah said: These kings will have no power or helper on the Day of Resurrection. Sufyan said: Power is the clan, and a helper is an ally, and the former is more appropriate.
86:11: 11- And the sky with its returning rain. Returning is the rain. Al-Zajjaj said: Returning is the rain because it comes and returns and is repeated. Al-Khalil said: Returning is the rain itself, and return is the plant of spring. Linguists said: Returning is the rain. Al-Mutanakhal said, describing his sword: White as a camel, a messenger who, if he reveals his secret to a reveler, is alone Al-Wahidi said: “Raja’ is rain according to all commentators. However, what he narrated from all commentators is questionable, because Ibn Zayd said: Raja’ is the sun, moon, and stars that return in the sky, rising from one side and setting in another.” Some commentators said: Dhat al-Raja’ is the same as the angels, because they return to them with the deeds of the servants. Some of them said: “Dhat al-Raja’ means: the one with benefit.” The reason for naming rain Raj’an is what Al-Qaffal said, that it is taken from the repetition of sound, which means its return. Likewise, rain is called Raj’an because it returns time after time. It was said that the Arabs used to claim that the clouds carry water from the seas of the earth, then return it to the earth. It was also said that the Arabs named it Raj’an as a sign of optimism that it would return to them, and it was also said that it is because God returns it time after time.
86:12: 12- And the land with its cracks is what the land cracks from of plants, fruits and trees, and the crack is the cleft because it cracks the land so it cracks for it. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Farra’ said: It cracks with plants. Mujahid said: And the land with the paths that the water cracks, and it was said that it has the fields because it cracks them, and it was said that it has the dead because it cracks for them at the resurrection. In conclusion, if the crack is a name for a plant, then it is as if he said: And the land with plants. And if what is meant by it is the cleft, then it is as if he said: And the land with the cleft from which plants and the like emerge.
86:13: The answer to the oath is his saying: 13- It is a decisive statement, meaning that the Qur’an is a statement that distinguishes between truth and falsehood by clarifying each one of them.
86:14: 14- And it is not a joke meaning it was not meant as a joke, it is serious and not a joke, and a joke is the opposite of seriousness. Al-Kumait said: You find us every day and joke
86:15: 15- They are plotting a plot meaning they are plotting to invalidate the true religion that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. Al-Zajjaj said: They are deceiving the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and showing that they are contrary to him.
86:16: 16- And surely a plot meaning that He lured them in from where they did not know, and He rewarded them for their plot. It was said that it was what God inflicted upon them on the day of Badr of killing and captivity.
86:17: 17- So grant them respite means delay them, and do not ask God, the Exalted, to hasten their destruction, and be satisfied with what He plans for you in their affairs. His saying, Give them respite is a substitute for give them respite, give them respite and give them respite means to postpone, and give them respite in a matter means to wait and wait. The accusative of slowly is as a verbal noun emphasizing the mentioned verb or an adjective for a deleted verbal noun: that is, give them respite slowly: meaning soon or a little. Abu Ubaidah said: Slowly in the speech of the Arabs is the diminutive of rud, and he recited: As if she is walking on a road Meaning, slowly. It is said that the diminutive of arowad is the source of rod, the diminutive of tarkhīm. It comes as a verb, such as rawid Zaydan, meaning give him time. It comes as a state, such as the people walked slowly, meaning slowly. Al-Jawhari mentioned the meaning of this, and the research is completed in the science of grammar. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, {And the heaven and the nightcomer}, that he said: Your Lord swears by the nightcomer: And everything that comes to you at night is a nightcomer. Ibn Jarir narrated from him, regarding His statement, {Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it}, that he said: Every soul has guardians over it from among the angels. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azmah narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, {The piercing star}, that he said: The shining star. {Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it}, that he said: Except for a guardian over it. Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him, {It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs}, that he said: What is between the neck and the throat. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, regarding the verse, that he said: The ribs of a woman, which is the place of the necklace. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him, that he said: The ribs are between the breasts of a woman. Al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, from him, that he said: The ribs are four ribs on each side from the lowest of the ribs. And Abd bin Hamid and Ibn Al-Mundhir also narrated from him, He is able to bring him back, he said: to make the old man young and the young man old. Abd Al-Razzaq, Al-Firyabi, Abd bin Hamid, Al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Al-Shaykh in Al-Azmah, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the sky with its paths, he said: rain after rain. And the earth with its fissures, he said: its cracking to reveal vegetation. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, And the earth with its fissures, he said: its cracking to reveal vegetation. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, And the earth with its fissures, he said: it cracks with the permission of God, revealing wealth and vegetation. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, it is a decisive statement, he said: the truth. And it is not in jest, he said: falsehood. And regarding his statement, Give them respite for a while, he said: shortly.
87:1: It is said that Surat Al-Sabh is nineteen verses. It is Meccan according to the majority of scholars. Ad-Dahhak said: It is Medinan. Ibn Ad-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Surah Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr and Aisha. Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib that he said: “The first of the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to come to us were Mus’ab ibn ‘Umair and Ibn Umm Maktum, and they began to recite the Qur’an to us. Then came ‘Ammar, Bilal and Sa’d, then ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattab with twenty, then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came. I never saw the people of Medina rejoice over anything as much as they did over him until I saw the little girls and boys saying: This is the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has come. He did not come until I had recited “Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High” in a similar Surah.” Ahmad, Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of ‘Ali that he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) loved this Surah: ‘Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High.’” Ahmad, Muslim and the Sunan scholars narrated on the authority of An-Nu'man ibn Bashir that "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite on the two Eids and on Fridays: 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' and 'Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming'. If it fell on a Friday, he would recite them both." In another version: And sometimes they would come together on the same day and he would recite them both. There are ahaadeeth on this topic. Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) "used to recite in the noon prayer: 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High'." Abu Dawud, An-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ad-Daraqutni, Al-Hakim and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to pray Witr by reciting: 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High', 'Say: O you disbelievers', and 'Say: He is God, the One'." Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recite in the Witr prayer in the first rak’ah ‘Subhan God’, and in the second ‘Say: O you disbelievers’, and in the third ‘Say: He is God, the One’ and the two Mu’awwidhat.” In the two Sahihs, it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Mu’adh: Why did you not pray ‘Subhan Ismi Rabbik Al-A’la’, ‘By the sun and its brightness’, and ‘By the night when it covers’? His statement: 1- Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High meaning, declare Him free from everything that is not befitting of Him. Al-Suddi said: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High means, Magnify Him. It was said that the name here was inserted for the purpose of glorification, as in the statement of Labid: Until the year, then peace be upon you both. And whoever cries for a full year has apologized. Meaning: Glorify your Lord, the Most High. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning is, glorify the name of your Lord so that no one else can be called by it, so do not be forced into this. It was also said that the meaning is: glorify the naming of your Lord and your remembrance of Him so that you do not mention Him except in a humble and reverent manner, and with respect for His remembrance. Al-Hasan said: The meaning of glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, is to pray to Him. It was also said that the meaning is: Pray with the names of God, not as the polytheists pray by whistling and clapping. It was also said that the meaning is: Raise your voice in remembrance of your Lord, and from this is the saying of Jarir: God made the faces of Taghlib ugly whenever the pilgrims glorified God and praised Him. The highest is an attribute of the Lord, and it was said of the name, and the first is more appropriate.
87:2: And His statement: 2- Who created and proportioned is another attribute of the Lord. Al-Zajjaj said: He created man level, and the meaning of proportioned is: He made his stature even. Al-Dahhak said: He created him and proportioned his creation. It was also said that He created the bodies and proportioned the minds. It was also said that He created man and prepared him for accountability.
87:3: 3- And He Who has decreed and guided is another attribute of the Lord, or it is conjoined with the relative pronoun before it. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Al-Kisa'i, and Al-Salami read has decreed without a vowel, while the rest read it with a shaddah. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said: He decreed the creation of the male and female of the beasts, so He guided the male to the female on how to approach her. Mujahid said: He guided man to the path of good and evil, happiness and misery. It was also narrated from him that he said about the meaning of the verse: He has decreed happiness and misery, and guided to right conduct and misguidance, and guided the livestock to their pastures. It was also said that He decreed their provisions and sustenance, and guided them to their livelihoods if they were humans, and to their pastures if they were wild. Ata' said: He made for every beast what is good for it and guided it to it. It was also said that He created benefits in things, and guided man to the method of extracting them from them. Al-Suddi said: He decreed the period of the fetus in the womb to be nine months, more or less, then He guided it to exit the womb. Al-Farra' said: It means that He has decreed, so He has guided and led astray, so one of them is sufficient. There are other interpretations of the verse other than what we have mentioned. The first is not to specify an individual or individuals to which the words hada and hada apply except with evidence that points to them. In the absence of evidence, it is interpreted as that to which the meaning of the two verbs applies, either as a substitute or as a comprehensive one. The meaning is: He has decreed the kinds of things, their types, their attributes, their actions, their sayings, and their terms, so He has guided each one of them to what it issues from and what is appropriate for it, and He has made it easy for what it was created for, and He has inspired it with the matters of its religion and its world.
87:4: 4- And He Who brought forth pasture is another attribute of the Lord: meaning He caused the grass to grow and the green plants that the livestock graze on.
87:5: 5- And He made it ghathaa' awwa meaning He made it, after it was green, ghathaa: meaning dry chaff like the chaff that is on the paths, ahwa: meaning black after its greenness, and that is because when the grass dries it turns black. Qatada said: ghathaa is the dry thing, and when the grass and the grass are broken and dry they are called ghathaa and hashim. Imru' al-Qais said: As if the top of the brazier’s head were a spindle’s wheel in the morning from the torrent and the scum The accusative of ghathaa is as the second object, or as a state, and aha is an adjective for it. Al-Kisa’i said: It is a state of the pasture: i.e., he brought it out dark from the intensity of greenery and watering, so he made it ghathaa after that. Dark is taken from hawwa, which is a blackness that tends toward green. It is said in Al-Sahah: Hawwa is the brownness of the lip, and from it is the saying of Dhu Al-Rummah: Lamia has honey on her lips, a moustache on her teeth, and a gum on her gums.
87:6: 6- We will make you recite, and you will not forget. That is, We will make you able to recite, and you will not forget what you recite. The sentence is a resumption of explaining his (peace and blessings of God be upon him) specific guidance after explaining the general guidance, which is his (peace and blessings of God be upon him) guidance to memorize the Quran. Mujahid and Al-Kalbi said: When Gabriel would come down to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with revelation, he would not finish reciting the last verse until the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had recited the first, for fear that he would forget it. So, We will make you recite, and you will not forget was revealed.
87:7: And His statement: 7- Except what God wills is an exception devoid of the most general of effects: meaning, do not forget anything you recite except what God wills you to forget. Al-Farra' said: He, the Almighty, did not will that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, forget anything, as in His statement: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. And it was said, except what God wills that you forget and then remember after that. So, he may have forgotten, but he remembers and does not forget anything completely. And it was said that it means abrogation: except what God wills to abrogate its recitation. And it was said that the meaning of do not forget is: do not abandon an action except what God wills you to abandon in order to abrogate it and remove its ruling. And it was said that the meaning is: except what God wills to delay its revelation. And it was said that the no in His statement: do not forget is for prohibition. The alif is added to protect the comma, as in His statement: And they led us astray from the path, meaning do not neglect to read it and remember it. Indeed, He knows what is said aloud and what is hidden. The sentence explains what preceded it: that is, He knows what is apparent and what is hidden, what is declared and what is kept secret. Its appearance is general, so what is said about the aloud recitation is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, memorized from the Qur’an, and what is hidden is what was abrogated from his chest, and what is said about the aloud recitation is the declaration of charity, and what is hidden is its concealment, and what is said about the aloud recitation is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting the Qur’an aloud with Gabriel’s recitation for fear that it would escape him, and what is hidden is what is in his soul that calls him to the aloud recitation.
87:8: 8- And We will make easy for you the easy way is in apposition to We will make you recite, and what is between them is an interruption. Muqatil said: That is, We will make easy for you the work of Paradise. It was also said that We will guide you to the way that is easier and simpler. It was also said that it is the easy Sharia, which is the easy Hanafiyyah. It was also said that We will make the revelation easy for you so that you will memorize it and act upon it. The first is to interpret the verse in general terms: That is, We will guide you to the easy way in religion and in this world in every matter of their affairs that is directed towards you.
87:9: 9- Then remind, if the reminder benefits meaning, O Muhammad, admonish the people with what We have revealed to you and guide them to the ways of goodness and direct them to the laws of religion. Al-Hasan said: It is a reminder to the believer and an argument against the disbeliever. Al-Wahidi said: Whether it benefits or not, and he did not mention the second case like His statement: garments to protect you from the heat (al-Baqarah 2:17). Al-Jurjani said: The reminder is obligatory even if it does not benefit, so the meaning is: Whether the reminder benefits or not. It was said that it is specific to specific people, and it was said that it means what: meaning, then mention what the reminder benefits, because the reminder is beneficial in all cases, and it was said that it means had, and it was said that it means when. What Al-Wahidi and Al-Jurjani said is more appropriate, and Al-Farra' and An-Nahhas preceded them in saying it. Al-Razi said: His statement, If the reminder benefits, is to draw attention to the more noble of the two situations, which is the presence of the benefit for which the reminder was prescribed. The conditional if on the purchase does not necessarily mean that it does not exist when that thing does not exist. This is indicated by verses, including this verse, and the statement of God Almighty: And be grateful to God if it is Him that you worship, and His statement: It is a sin for you to shorten the prayer if you fear, for shortening is permissible when there is fear or not. And His statement: There is no blame upon them if they return to each other if they think they can keep within the limits of God, and returning to each other is permissible without this suspicion. So this condition has benefits, including what was mentioned above, and among them is the encouragement to benefit from the reminder, as a man says to the one who guides him: I have made it clear to you if you are intelligent, and it is a warning to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the reminder will not benefit them, or this may be in repeating the supplication. As for the first supplication, it is general.
87:10: Then God Almighty explained the difference between those who are benefited by the reminder and those who are not benefited by it, saying: 10- He who fears will be reminded. That is, he who fears God will be admonished by your admonition, and his fear and righteousness will increase with the reminder.
87:11: 11- And the most wretched of the unbelievers avoids it meaning [and avoids] the remembrance and keeps away from it the most wretched of the unbelievers because of their persistence in disbelieving in God and their immersion in His sins.
87:12: Then he described the most wretched, saying: 12- The one who will enter the Great Fire, meaning the great and terrible one, because it is hotter than the others. Al-Hasan said: The Great Fire is the fire of Hell. The Lesser Fire is the fire of this world. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the lowest level of Hell.
87:13: 13- Then he will neither die therein nor live therein meaning he will neither die therein and find rest from the torment he is in, nor will he live a life from which he will benefit. From this is the poet’s saying: O soul, do not die, lest its suffering should be ended, nor live a life that has any taste. Then there is the laxity in the degrees of severity, because the hesitation between death and life is more terrible than the one who prays in the Great Fire.
87:14: 14- Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself meaning, he who purifies himself from polytheism, believes in God, establishes His Oneness, and acts in accordance with His laws. Ata' and Ar-Rabi' said: He whose deeds are pure and growing. Qatadah said: He is purified by righteous deeds. Qatadah, Ata' and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It was revealed regarding Zakat Al-Fitr. Ikrimah said: A man would say: I present my Zakat before my prayer. The root of Zakat in the language is growth. It was said that what is meant by this verse is the Zakat on all wealth. It was also said that what is meant by it is the Zakat of deeds, not the Zakat on wealth, because what is most commonly said about wealth is that it is purified, not that it is given Zakat.
87:15: 15- And he mentioned the name of his Lord and prayed. It was said that the meaning is: He mentioned the name of his Lord with fear, so he worshipped Him and prayed to Him. It was also said that he mentioned the name of his Lord with his tongue, so he prayed: that is, he performed the five daily prayers. It was also said that he mentioned his place of standing and his return, so he worshipped Him, and it is like the first statement. It was also said that he mentioned the name of his Lord by saying Allahu Akbar at the beginning of the prayer because it is not valid except by mentioning Him, which is his saying: Allahu Akbar. It was also said that he mentioned the name of his Lord on the way to the place of prayer, so he prayed. It was also said that it means to voluntarily perform a prayer after paying zakat. It was also said that what is meant by prayer here is the Eid prayer, just as what is meant by purification in the first verse is zakat al-fitr. The distance of this statement is clear because the surah was revealed in Mecca, and zakat al-fitr and the Eid prayer were not made obligatory except in Medina.
87:16: 16- Rather, you prefer the life of this world. This is an interruption of an implied statement indicated by the context: i.e., you do not do that, but you prefer the fleeting pleasures of this world. The majority of scholars read you prefer with the superior verb as addressing someone, and this is supported by Abu's reading: Rather, you prefer. Abu 'Amr read it with the subjunctive verb as addressing someone else. It was said that what is meant by the verse is the disbelievers, and what is meant by preferring the life of this world is being content with it and feeling secure in it and completely turning away from the Hereafter. It was also said that what is meant by it is all people, both believers and disbelievers, and what is meant by preferring it is something more general than that, which most people are not free from, such as preferring the worldly aspect to the Hereafter, and focusing on attaining its benefits and paying more attention to it than to acts of obedience.
87:17: 17- And the Hereafter is better and more lasting is in the accusative case as a state of the subject of you give preference: meaning, while the reality is that the Hereafter, which is Paradise, is better and more lasting than this world. Malik ibn Dinar said: If this world were made of gold that would perish, and the Hereafter were made of pottery that would remain, then it would be necessary to give preference to pottery that would remain over gold that would perish. So how can it be so when the Hereafter is made of gold that would remain, and this world is made of pottery that would perish?
87:18: And the reference in his saying: 18- This is to what came before of success, if he is purified and what comes after it, and it was said that it is a reference to the entire surah, and the meaning of in the first scriptures is that it is established in them.
87:19: And His statement: 19- The scriptures of Abraham and Moses instead of the first scriptures. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: By His statement: Indeed, this and the Hereafter are better and more lasting. They said: The scriptures of God, the Almighty, were revealed one after the other that the Hereafter is better and more lasting than this world. Al-Hasan said: The scriptures of God, the Most High, were revealed one after the other that this is in the first scriptures, and this is His statement: He has certainly succeeded to the end of the surah. The majority of scholars read Indeed, in the first scriptures * The scriptures of Abraham with a damma on the ha' in both instances. Al-A'mash, Harun, and Abu Amr, in a narration from him, read it with a sukoon in both instances. The majority of scholars read Ibrahim with an alif after the ra' and with a ya' after the ha'. Abu Raja' read it by deleting both and opening the ha'. Abu Musa and Ibn al-Zubayr read Ibrahim with two alifs. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani who said: “When the verse, ‘So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High,’ was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us, ‘Include it in your bowing.’ When the verse, ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High,’ was revealed, he said, ‘Include it in your prostration.’” There is no objection to its chain of transmission. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Abbas that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High,’ he would say, ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’” Abu Dawud said: Waki’ differed with him on this matter. Shu’bah narrated it on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abbas as a mursal. It was also narrated with a chain of transmission ending with Ibn Abbas that whenever he recited Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, he would say: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. In a wording narrated by Abd ibn Hamid, he said: “When you recite ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High,’ then say: ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’” Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, and Ibn al-Anbari narrated in al-Masahif from Ali ibn Abi Talib that he recited Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, and said: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, while he was praying. It was said to him: Are you adding to the Qur’an? He said: No, we were only commanded to do something, so I said it. Al-Faryabi, Sa’id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Hamid, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash’ari that he recited Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, on Friday and said: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Hakim who authenticated it narrated on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar reciting, Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, and he said, Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. This is how it is recited by Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr that he recited, Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, and he said, Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, while he was praying. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the verse, Then He made it stubble, he said, Black chaff, he said, Change. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority that he said, "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would memorize the Qur'an for fear that he would forget, so it was said to him, 'We have spared you that,' and 'We will recite to you, and you will not forget' was revealed." Al-Hakim narrated something similar on the authority of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, Except what God wills, meaning: Except what I will, so I will make you forget. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, And We will ease you to ease, he said, for good. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, And We will ease you to ease, meaning Paradise. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself, he said, He who bears witness that there is no god but God, and shuns rivals to Him, and bears witness that I am the Messenger of God, and mentions the name of his Lord and prays, he said, They are the five daily prayers, maintaining them and observing their times. Al-Bazzar said, It is not narrated on the authority of Jabir except through this chain of narration. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself, he said, From polytheism, and mentions the name of his Lord, he said, He declares the Oneness of God, and prays, he said, The five daily prayers. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself, he said, He who says, There is no god but God." Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim in Al-Kuna, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated on the authority of Kathir Ibn Abdullah Ibn Amr Ibn Awf, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He used to order the payment of Zakat Al-Fitr before praying the Eid prayer and would recite this verse: ‘Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays.’” And in another version he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about Zakat al-Fitr, and he said: ‘He has succeeded who purifies himself.’ He said: ‘It is Zakat al-Fitr.’” Katheer ibn Abdullah is very weak. Abu Dawud said about him: He is one of the pillars of lying.
