Al-Tirmidhi authenticated a hadith from his chain of transmission, and he made a mistake in that, but what supports it is what Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: ‘He has succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays.’ Then he would distribute the Zakat al-Fitr before going out to the prayer place on the day of Eid.” These two hadiths do not indicate that this was the reason for revelation, rather in them he, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the verse and his saying: It is Zakat al-Fitr. It could be intended that it is something to which purification is attributed. We have already mentioned that the surah was revealed in Mecca, and there was no Eid prayer or Zakat al-Fitr in Mecca. Abd ibn Hamid and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri: He has succeeded who purifies himself. He said: He was given Zakat al-Fitr before going out to Eid. And he mentioned…” He said: He went out to the Eid and prayed. Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: This verse was revealed regarding giving Zakat al-Fitr before the Eid prayer: Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself, * And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: What do you think of His statement: Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself for the Eid prayer? He said: I had not heard of that, but for all Zakat. Then I asked him again and he said to me: And all Sadaqah. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Tabarani and Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Shu’ab Al-Iman on the authority of Urfajah Al-Thaqafi who said: I recited to Ibn Mas’ud: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. When he reached: Rather, you prefer the life of this world, he stopped reciting and turned to his companions and said: We prefer this world over the Hereafter. The people remained silent. He said: We prefer this world because we have seen its adornments, women, food and drink, and the Hereafter has been turned away from us, so we have chosen this immediate life and abandoned the deferred life. He said: Rather, you prefer the life of this world with the letter ya. Al-Bazzar, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God’s Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him): Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses, that he said: It is all in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Sa’id Ibn Mansur, Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on his authority, regarding the verse: This surah was abrogated from the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. In another version: This surah is in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Abd Ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “I said: O Messenger of God, how many books has God revealed?” He said: One hundred and four books.
88:1: It has twenty-six verses, and it is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, Al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-Ghashiyah was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar narration on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr. The hadith of Al-Nu’man ibn Bashir was mentioned above, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ and Al-Ghashiyah in the Eid prayer and on Fridays. His statement: 1- Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming? A group of commentators said: Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming? This is what Qatrib said: That is, O Muhammad, the report of the Overwhelming has come to you. It refers to the Resurrection because it will overwhelm creation with its horrors. It was said that keeping Ha here in its interrogative meaning that implies amazement at what is reported and eagerness to hear it is more appropriate. Most commentators have said that what is meant by Al-Ghashiyah here is the Resurrection. Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: “Al-Ghashiyah is the Fire that will overwhelm the faces of the disbelievers, as in His statement: “And the Fire will overwhelm their faces.” It was said that Al-Ghashiyah refers to the people of the Fire because they will overwhelm it and rush into it, but the first is more appropriate. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is, If the report of the Overwhelming has not come to you.
88:2: 2- Some faces, that Day, will be humbled The sentence is a new sentence in answer to an implied question, as if it were asked: What is it? Or it is a new sentence in grammatical terms to explain what it includes, that there will be faces on that Day described by this mentioned characteristic. Faces is raised as a subject even though it is indefinite because it occurs in a place of detail. An example of this has been presented in Surah Al-Qiyamah and Surah An-Nazi'at. The tanween in Yawmidheen replaces the complement: meaning the Day of the Overwhelming. Al-Khasha'iyyah means the submissive and humbled. Every silent, diminished word is said to be khasha'i. It is said that the voice is khasha'i low if it is low, and khasha'i fi salat means that he is humble and lowers his head. What is meant by faces here are their owners. Muqatil said: He means the disbelievers because they were too arrogant to worship God. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: Humbled in the Fire. It was also said that he meant the faces of the Jews and Christians in particular. The first is more appropriate.
88:3: His saying: 3- Working and tiring The meaning of working is that she does a hard job. Linguists said: When a man is persistent in his walk, it is said: He worked, he does a job. And when the clouds continue to be light, it is said: He has worked, he does a job. It was said that this work is dragging chains and shackles and wading in the fire Nasbah meaning tiring. It is said that he is tired in the hereafter because of what she will encounter of God's punishment. It was said that his saying: Working in this world since there is no work in the hereafter means that she works in this world with disbelief and sins, and is tired in that. And it was said that she is working in this world, tiring in the hereafter, but the first is more appropriate. Qatada said: Amalah nasibah means she was too arrogant to obey God in this world, so God made her work and cast her into Hell by dragging heavy chains, carrying shackles, and standing barefoot and naked in the open areas. On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: She did not work for God in this world and did not set herself up, so I made her work and cast her into Hell. Al-Kalbi said: They will be dragged on their faces in Hell. He also said: They will be ordered to climb an iron mountain in Hell, and they will be set up there with the most severe hardship by handling the chains and shackles and wading through the Fire as camels wade through mud. The majority of scholars read Amalah nasibah in the nominative case as two other predicates of the subject, or as an assumed subject, and they are two predicates of it. Ibn Muhaisin, 'Eesa, Hamid, and Ibn Kathir, in a narration from him, read them in the accusative case as a state or as a blame.
88:4: And his saying: 4- You will be burned in a blazing Fire is another predicate for the subject. That is, you will enter a blazing Fire in the heat. It is said that the day was hot and the oven was hot: meaning their heat was intense. Al-Kisa'i said: It is said that the day was hot and they heated it with the same meaning. The majority read You will be burned with a fatha on the ta' as an active verb. Abu Amr, Ya'qub, and Abu Bakr read them with a damma on both of them as a passive verb. Abu Raja' read with a damma on the ta', a fatha on the sad, and a shaddah on the lam. The pronoun refers to the faces according to all of these readings, and what is meant are their owners as mentioned above, and so is the pronoun.
88:5: 5- They will be given to drink from a boiling spring. What is meant by aniya is the one that is extremely hot, and aniya is that whose heat has reached its peak, from inaa meaning to delay. It is said anaahu yu’anihu inaan meaning he delayed it and held it back, as in His statement: They will circulate between it and scalding water. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators said that if a drop of sperm from it were to fall on the mountains of the world, they would melt.
88:6: When God the Almighty mentioned their drink, He followed it with mentioning their food, saying: 6- They will have no food except from Dharee’ It is a type of thorn called shabraq in the language of Quraysh when it is fresh, and when it dries, it is Dharee’. This is what Mujahid, Qatadah, and other commentators said. It was said that it is a deadly poison, and when it dries, no animal will approach it or graze it. It was also said that it is something thrown out by the sea called Dharee’ from the sustenance of livestock, not from the sustenance of people. When camels graze from it, they are not satisfied and die of emaciation. Al-Khalil said: Dharee’ is a green plant with a foul smell that is thrown out by the sea. The majority of linguists and commentators said the first, and from this is the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb: The sharq al-rayyan grazed until it withered and became weak, and the sharq became clear about it. Al-Hudhali said about camels and their poor pasture: And he was imprisoned in the pyramid of the poor, all of them were horns with bloody hands and barren. Saeed bin Jubair said: Adh-Dharee’ is stones, and it was also said that it is a tree in the fire of Hell. Al-Hasan said: It is some of the torment that God has hidden. Ibn Kaysan said: It is a food in which they humiliate themselves and beseech God to be saved from it. It was called thus because the one who eats it beseeches God to forgive him for its unpleasantness and roughness. An-Nahhas said: It may be derived from Ad-Dharee’ which means humiliated, meaning that whoever drinks it will be afflicted with humiliation and submissiveness. Al-Hasan also said: It is Zaqqum, and it was also said that it is a valley in Hell. It was mentioned previously in Surat al-Haqqah 69:So for him this Day there is no close friend here, nor any food except from ghuslān (al-Haqqah 69:19). Ghaslān is not Adh-Dharee’, as mentioned previously. The two verses are combined by saying that Hell has levels, so some of their food is Adh-Dharee’, and some of their food is Ghaslān.
88:7: Then God the Almighty described the thorny plant, saying: 7- It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger. That is, the thorny plant neither fattens its eater nor wards off hunger. The commentators said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: Our camels get fat from the thorny plant. So, It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger was revealed. They lied in their statement, because camels do not eat the thorny plant nor go near it. It was also said that they were confused about it and thought it was like any other beneficial plant.
88:8: Then the Almighty proceeded to explain the state of the people of Paradise after finishing explaining the state of the people of Hell, saying: 8- Faces on that Day will be radiant, meaning full of grace and joy, and they are the faces of the believers. Their faces will become radiant when they saw the outcome of their affair and what God has prepared for them of good that is beyond description. Similar to this is His saying: You will recognize in their faces the radiance of pleasure.
88:9: Then he said: 9- She is satisfied with her efforts, meaning she is satisfied with the knowledge she did in this world, because she was given a reward that satisfied her and made her eyes happy. What is meant by faces here are their owners, as mentioned above.
88:10: 10- In a high Paradise meaning a high place, higher than other places, or of high status because it contains everything that the soul desires and the eyes delight in.
88:11: 11- You will not hear therein vain talk. The majority of reciters read You will not hear therein with a fatha over the first letter and a nasb over laghiyah: meaning you, the one being addressed, will not hear, or you will not hear those faces. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr recited it with a damma over the first letter, passive voice, and raised laghiyah. Nafi' recited it with a damma over the first letter, passive voice, and raised laghiyah. Al-Fadl and Al-Jahdary recited it with a fatha over the second letter, active voice, and raised laghiyah. Laghw is idle speech. Al-Farra' and Al-Akhfash said: Meaning you will not hear therein a word of vain talk. It was said that what is meant by this is lying, slander, and disbelief. Qatada said this. Mujahid said: Meaning cursing. Al-Farra' said: You will not hear therein an oath swearing falsely. Al-Kalbi said: You will not hear in Paradise an oath, whether righteous or wicked. Al-Farra’ said: “Also, you will not hear the word ‘idle’ in the speech of the people of Paradise, because they only speak with wisdom and praise to God Almighty for the eternal bliss He has provided them with. This is the most correct of the sayings, because the indefinite noun in the context of negation is a form of generality, and there is no reason to specify this with a particular type of idle talk except with a specification that is suitable for specifying. ‘idle’ is either an attribute of a deleted described word: i.e., a idle word, or a idle soul, or a source: i.e., you will not hear idle talk in it.”
88:12: 12- In it is a flowing spring. It was mentioned in Surah Al-Insan that it contains springs. The spring here means springs, as in His statement: Every soul knows. The meaning of flowing is that its waters flow and gush with various types of delicious drinks. Al-Kalbi said: I do not know whether it is water or something else.
88:13: 13- In it are raised couches meaning high and lofty, or of high status.
88:14: 14- And cups placed. It was previously mentioned that cups is the plural of cup, and that it is a cup without a handle. The meaning of placed is that it is placed in their hands for them to drink from.
88:15: 15- And cushions lined up Cushions: pillows. Al-Wahidi said: According to everyone's opinion, the singular is namraqa with a damma on the noon, and Al-Farra' added, hearing it from the Arabs, namraqa with a kasra on it. Al-Kalbi said: Pillows lined up one next to the other, and from this is the saying of the poet: We pass the cup between our drink and Abu Qaboos over the cushions The other said: Old men and young men, their faces beautiful, on lined couches and pillows He said in Al-Sahah: Al-Namaraq and Al-Namaraqa are small pillows, and so is Al-Namaraqa with a kasra in the language, narrated by Yaqub.
88:16: 16- Scattered carpets means rugs, the singular of which is zarbi and zarbiyyah. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Farra' said: The carpets are the rugs that have a fine nap, the singular of which is zarbiyyah, and the spread out is the one said by Qatada. Ikrimah said: one on top of the other. Al-Wahidi said: It is possible that the meaning is: that they are scattered in the gatherings. Al-Qatibi said the same. Al-Farra' said: The meaning of mashthothah is many, and it appears that the meaning of bath is: scattering with abundance, and from it and He spread therein every creature.
88:17: 10- Do they not look at the camels - how they were created? The question is for rebuke and rebuke, and the fa is for connecting to an implied word as in similar examples that have been mentioned more than once. The sentence is intended to confirm the matter of resurrection and provide evidence for it, as is what follows it. How is in the accusative case with what follows it, and the sentence is in the genitive case as a substitute for inclusion from the camels. The meaning is: Do they deny the matter of resurrection and rule out its occurrence? Do they not look at the camels, which are the majority of their livestock and the largest of the creatures they see, how they were created with what they are in terms of the wondrous creation of their large body, increased strength, and wondrous descriptions. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' said: He singled out camels because they are quadrupeds that kneel, so loads are carried on them, whereas other quadrupeds cannot be carried unless they are standing. Az-Zajjaj said: He alerted them to a great aspect of His creation, which He has tamed for the young, leading them, making them kneel, making them stand up, and placing heavy loads on them while they are kneeling, so they can stand up under the weight of their load. This is not the case with any other pregnant animal. So He showed them a great aspect of His creation to demonstrate His Oneness. Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: The elephant is the greatest wonder. He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs have had a long history with it. It is a pig whose back is not ridden, whose meat is not eaten, and whose milk is not milked. Camels are among the most precious and valuable possessions of the Arabs. They eat pits and dung and produce milk, and the young boy takes hold of their reins and goes with them wherever he wants, despite their being great in themselves. Al-Mubarrad said: The camels here are large pieces of clouds, which is contrary to what the scholars of tafsir and linguistics have stated. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Asma’i that he said: Whoever reads khalqat with a light pronunciation means a camel, and whoever reads it with a heavy pronunciation means a cloud.
88:18: 18- And to the sky, how it was raised. That is, it was raised above the earth without pillars in a way that cannot be understood or comprehended by the mind. It was also said that it was raised so that nothing could reach it.
88:19: 19- And to the mountains, how they are fixed on the earth, a firm anchor that does not sway, tilt, or move.
88:20: 20- And to the earth, how it was spread out meaning it was extended. The word sat means to spread something out. The roof of a house is called satah if it is flat. The majority of scholars read sataht in the passive voice with a lightened sat. Al-Hasan read it with a shaddah. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn al-Samee' and Abu al-Aaliyah read khalaqt, raised, nasb and sataht in the active voice with a damma on the ta in all of them.
88:21: Then the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to remind, saying: 21- Then remind, and the fa is to arrange what comes after it according to what comes before it: meaning, preach to them, O Muhammad, and frighten them. Then He explained the command to remind, saying: You are only a reminder, meaning that you are not required to do anything else.
88:22: 22- And You have no control over them Al-Musaytir and Al-Mutasir with seen and sad: the one who has power over something to supervise it and oversee its affairs. This is in Al-Sahah, meaning you have no control over them to the point that you force them to believe. This was abrogated by the verse of the sword. The majority read Bumsaytir with sad, and Hisham and Qunbal read it with seen in a narration. Khalaf read it by making the sad sound like zay. Harun Al-Aawar read it with a fatha on the ta as a passive participle.
88:23: 23- Except for he who turns away and disbelieves. This is an isolated exception: that is, but for he who turns away from preaching and reminding.
88:24: 24- Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment, which is the eternal punishment of Hell. It was said that it is an exception connected to His statement, Then remember, meaning, remember everyone except the one whose faith has cut him off and who has turned away, so he deserves the greatest punishment. The first is more appropriate. He said the greatest because they were punished in this world with hunger, famine, killing, and captivity. Ibn Mas'ud read, For God will punish him, and Ibn Abbas and Qatadah read, Except for whoever turns away, as if it were the ala that is for warning and introduction.
88:25: 25- To Us is their return meaning their return after death. It is said that someone returned, and from this is the saying of Ubayd ibn al-Abrash: Every absent person repents, but the one absent from death does not return. The majority of scholars readيْابهمwith a stressed yaa, while Abu Jaafar and Shaiba read it with a stressed yaa. Abu Hatim said: The stressed yaa is not permissible, and if it were, something similar would have been permissible inصْامandصلة" night prayer. It was also said that they are two meanings. Al-Wahidi said: "As forيْابهمwith a stressed yaa, it is unusual and no one except Az-Zajjaj permitted it."
88:26: 26- Then it is upon Us to bring them to account meaning their punishment after their return to God through resurrection. Then is for the gradual decreasing of the rank due to the distance in severity of the account from the rank of the return. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Ghashiyah is one of the names of the Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority: Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming? He said: The Hour. Some faces that Day will be humbled, working, weary. He said: Working and weary in the Fire. They will be given to drink from a boiling spring. He said: It is the one that has been burning for a long time. They will have no food except from thorny thorns. He said: The burning shabraq. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority: Some faces that Day will be humbled, working, weary. He said: It means the Jews and Christians, who will be humbled and their work will not benefit them. They will be given to drink from a boiling spring. He said: It has reached boiling point. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement: They will be roasted in a blazing Fire. He said: Hot. They will be given to drink from a boiling spring. He said: Its heat has reached its climax. They will have no food except from thorny thorns. He said: From a tree of fire. Abd ibn Humayd also narrated on his authority: Except from thorny thorns. He said: The burning shabraq is dry. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, You will not hear therein any idle talk, meaning you will not hear any harm or falsehood. Regarding his statement, Therein are raised couches, he said, one above the other. And cushions, he said, seating areas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, And cushions, he said, the resting places. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him, You have no control over them, he said, a tyrant. Except for he who turns away and disbelieves, he said, his reckoning is with God. Abu Dawud also narrated from him in his Naskh, You have no control over them, then he abrogated that and said, Kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him, Indeed, to Us is their return, he said, their return.
89:1: It is thirty verses, and it was said twenty-nine verses It is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Ad-Durais, An-Nahhas in his Naskh, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: By the dawn was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr and Aisha. An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Jabir who said: “Muadh performed a prayer, then a man came and prayed with him, but he prolonged it. He prayed in a corner of the mosque and then left. report of that reached Muadh, so he said: ‘Hypocrite.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was mentioned about that and he said: ‘O Messenger of God, I came to pray, but it prolonged it for me, so I left and prayed in a corner of the mosque, then I loaded my camel.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Are you a tempter, O Muadh? Where are you from ‘Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High,’ and ‘By the sun and its brightness,’ and ‘By the dawn,’ and ‘By the night when it covers you?’” 1- By the dawn - God swore by these things as He swore by other creations. There was a difference of opinion about the dawn by which God swore here. Some said it is the known time, and it was called dawn because it is the time when darkness bursts forth from the day every day. Qatada said: It is the dawn of the first day of the month of Muharram, because the year begins from it. Mujahid said: He means the Day of Sacrifice. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the dawn of Dhul-Hijjah.
89:2: Because God linked the days to it, saying: 2- and ten nights meaning ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah, and this is what Al-Suddi and Al-Kalbi said. It was also said that the meaning is: and the dawn prayer or the Lord of dawn. The first is more appropriate. The answer to this oath and what follows it is His statement: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful thus said Ibn Al-Anbari, and it was also said that it was omitted because the context indicates it: meaning that He will reward everyone according to his deeds, or that He will punish. Abu Hayyan estimated it based on what the end of the surah before it indicated: meaning, and the dawn, etc., for their return to Us and their reckoning is upon Us. This is very weak, and even weaker than it is the statement of those who said that the answer is His statement: Is there in that an oath for one of sense? And that hal means already, because this can never be an oath by. and ten nights are the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah according to the majority of commentators. Ad-Dahhak said: They are the last days of Ramadan, and it was said that they are the first ten days of Muharram until the tenth day of Ashura. The majority of scholars read layal with tanween, and ashar is an adjective. Ibn Abbas read ashar nights with the addition of ashar. It was said that what was meant was ashar nights, but it should have been said ashar because the counted item is masculine. The response to this is that if the counted item is omitted, both interpretations are permissible.
89:3: 3- By the even and the odd Shafa' and Witr include all things, even and odd. It was also said that they are the even and odd of the nights. Qatada said: Shafa' and Witr are the even and odd of the prayer, from it shafa' and from it witr. It was also said that shafa' is the day of Arafah and the day of sacrifice, and witr is the night of the day of sacrifice. Mujahid and Atiyyah Al-Awfi said: Shafa' is creation, and witr is God, the One, the Eternal Refuge. Muhammad ibn Sirin, Masruq, Abu Salih, and Qatadah said the same. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is the Maghrib prayer, in which there are two rak'ahs, and witr is the one rak'ah. Ad-Dahhak said: Shafa' is the tenth of Dhul-Hijjah, and witr is the three days of Mina. Ata' said the same. It was also said that they are Adam and Eve, because Adam was odd, so he made an even with Eve. It was also said that shafa' is the degrees of Paradise, which are eight, and witr is the levels of Hell, which are seven. Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said the same. It was also said that shafa' is Safa and Marwah, and witr is the Kaaba. Muqatil said: Ash-Shafa' is the days and nights, and Ash-Witr is the day after which there is no night, which is the Day of Resurrection. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Ash-Witr is God, the Exalted, and He is also Ash-Shafa', as He says: There are not three who confer privately but He is the fourth of them (Al-Quds 13:1-14). Al-Hasan said: What is meant by Ash-Shafa' and Ash-Witr is the whole number, because a number is never devoid of them. It was also said that Ash-Shafa' is the mosque in Mecca and Medina, and Ash-Witr is the mosque in Jerusalem. It was also said that Ash-Shafa' is the proofs of the Quran, and Ash-Witr is the singular. It was also said that Ash-Shafa' is the animal because it is male and female, and Ash-Witr is the inanimate. It was also said that Ash-Shafa' is what is named, and Ash-Witr is what is not named. You will not be hidden from the clear omission and apparent weakness in most of these sayings, and the reliance in determining the definition is based on mere false opinion and erroneous thought. What should be relied upon and what must be adhered to is what is indicated by the meaning of shafa' and witr in the speech of the Arabs, and they are two well-known and clear words. Shafa' among the Arabs means even, and witr means odd. So what is meant by the verse is either the number itself or what is true of the counted items as shafa' or witr. If evidence is provided to specify one of the counted items in the interpretation of this verse, then if the evidence indicates that it is the intended one and nothing else, then that is fine. But if the evidence indicates that it is one of the things covered by this verse, that does not prevent it from including something else. The majority of scholars read wal witr with a fatha on the waw. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read it with a kasra, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and his companions. These are two dialects. The fatha is the dialect of Quraysh and the people of Hijaz, and the kasra is the dialect of Tamim. Al-Asma'i said: Every odd is odd. The people of Hijaz open it and say witr in odd. Yunus narrated from Ibn Kathir that he read it with a fatha on the waw and a kasra on the ta'. It is possible that this is a third dialect, or that he transferred the kasra of the ra' to the ta' to make the connection similar to a pause.
89:4: 4- And the night when it departs The majority read delivers without the ya' in both connected and paused pronunciation, following the orthography of the Qur'an. Nafi' and Abu Amr read without it in paused pronunciation and without it in connected pronunciation. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Ya'qub read without it in connected pronunciation and paused pronunciation. Al-Khalil said: The ya' is dropped from it to match the beginnings of the verses. Al-Zajjaj said: I prefer the deletion because it is a separator and the ya's are deleted from separators. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs sometimes delete the ya' and suffice with a kasra before it. Some of them recited: Enough, a hand that does not befit a generous dirham and another that gives blood with the sword What is appropriate: that is, what you hold on to. Al-Mu'arraj said: I asked Al-Akhfash about the reason for dropping the ya' from yusra, so he said: I will not answer you until you spend the night at the door of my house for a year. So he spent the night at the door of his house for a year, and he said: The night does not flow, but rather it flows in it, so it is diverted from its direction, and everything that you divert from its direction you reduce its i'rab. Do you not see his saying: And your mother was not a rebel, and he did not say bughya, because he diverted it from baghiyah. And there is a consideration in what Al-Akhfash said, because if something is diverted from its meaning for some reason, this does not necessitate diverting its wording from some of what it deserves. If that were true, it would be required in all rational and verbal metaphors, and the necessary is false, so the required is like it. The origin here is to prove the ya’, because it is the lam of the present tense verb in the nominative case. The cause was not deleted from the causes except to follow the orthography of the Qur’an and to agree with the heads of the verses, making the pauses run like rhymes. The meaning of and the night when it departs is if it passes, like his saying: and the night when it departs and and the night when it sets in darkness. It was said that the meaning of is easy is to travel in it, as one says a sleeping night and a fasting day, as in the saying of the poet: You blamed us, O Umm Ghilan, in the night, and you slept, while the night of the mounts was not asleep. This is what Al-Akhfash, Al-Qutaybi and others among the scholars of semantics said, and the first is what the majority of commentators said. Qatada and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: And the night when it departs means it comes and approaches. An-Nakha’i said: It means it is equal. Ikrimah, Qatada, Al-Kalbi and Muhammad bin Ka’b said: It is the night of Muzdalifah in particular because it is the place where people gather to obey God, the Most High. It was also said to be the Night of Decree because mercy spreads during it. The most correct opinion is that no night is singled out over another.
89:5: 5- Is there in that an oath for one of sense? This question is to confirm the greatness of what the Almighty swore by and its magnificence from these mentioned matters, and the reference by His saying: that to those matters, and the reminder of the interpretation of the mentioned: that is, is there in that mentioned: from the matters by which We swore an oath: that is, something sworn by that is worthy of being confirmed by the report for one of sense that is, intellect and mind, so whoever has intellect and mind knows that what God swore by from these things is worthy of being sworn by, and similar to this is His saying: And indeed, it is an oath, if you only knew, a great one. Al-Hasan said, for one of sense means forbearance. Abu Malik said: for one who is concealed from people. The majority said: Stone is the mind. Al-Farra' said: They all go back to one meaning, forbearance, forbearance, and concealment, they all mean the mind. The root of stone is prevention, it is said to someone who controls himself and prevents himself: he is a man of stone, and from it is called stone because of his resistance due to its hardness, and from it is the ruler's stone on someone: meaning he prevented him. He said: The Arabs say: He is strong-willed, if he is self-controlled and in control of himself.
89:6: Then the Almighty mentioned, in his way of evidence, the punishment that befell some groups of the infidels because of their disbelief, stubbornness, and denial of the messengers, as a warning to the infidels in the era of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to frighten them that what befell them would befall them, saying: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Aad - Iram, who had lofty pillars? The majority of scholars read the word with the tanween of 'Aad, so that 'Aad is an apposition to 'Aad, and what is meant by 'Aad is the name of their father, and 'Iram is the name of the tribe or a substitute for it, and it is not permissible to decline 'Iram due to the definite article and femininity. It was also said that what is meant by 'Aad are the children of 'Aad, and they are the first 'Aad, and those who came after them are called the other 'Aad, so the mention of 'Iram is in the way of apposition or a substitute, to indicate that they are the first 'Aad, not the other 'Aad. And it is necessary to estimate an attribute in both opinions: meaning the people of Iram, or the tribe of Iram? For Iram is the grandfather of 'Aad, because 'Aad is the son of 'Aws the son of 'Iram the son of Sam the son of Nuh. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-'Aliyah read it by adding 'Aad to 'Iram. The majority read Iram with a kasra on the hamza and a fatha on the ra and the meem. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah and Al-Dahhak read Iram with a fatha on the hamza and the ra. Muadh read it with a sukoon on the ra for ease of reading. It was also read by adding Iram to the word Dhat al-Imad. Mujahid said: Whoever reads with a fatha on the hamza likened them to Iram which are the landmarks, the singular of which is Iram. There is an inversion in the speech: meaning, the dawn and so on. Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. Have you not seen? Meaning, has your knowledge not reached what your Lord did to Aad? This vision is a vision of the heart, and the address is to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), or to anyone who is suitable for it. The matter of Aad and Thamud was well-known among the Arabs, because their lands were connected to the lands of the Arabs, and they used to hear from the People of the Book about the matter of Pharaoh. Mujahid also said: Iram was a nation among the nations. Qatadah said: It is a tribe from Aad, and it was said that they are two Aad, so the first is Iram. From this is the saying of Qays ibn al-Ruqayyat: An ancient glory built by the first of them who lived in Aad and before them Iram Muammar said: Iram was the meeting place of Ad and Thamud. It was said that Ad was Iram and Ad was Thamud, and the two tribes were named after Iram. Abu Ubaidah said: They are two Ad, but the first is Iram. The meaning of Dhat al-Imad is: of strength and intensity, taken from the strength of the pillars, as Ad-Dahhak said. Qatadah and Mujahid said: They were people of pillars that moved in the spring, and when the vegetation became turbulent, they returned to their homes. Muqatil said: Dhat al-Imad means their height, a man among them was twelve cubits tall, and it is said that a man of tall stature is Imad. Abu Ubaidah said: Dhat al-Imad is of tallness, it is said that he returned with a pillar if he was tall. Mujahid and Qatadah said: He was also a pillar for their people, it is said that so-and-so is the leader and pillar of the people, meaning their master. Ibn Zayd said: Dhat al-Imad means the strength of the building with pillars. It is said in As-Sahah: Pillars are tall buildings, masculine and feminine. Amr ibn Kulthum said: If the pillars of the neighborhood fall down, we will prevent those who follow us. Akrima and Saeed Al-Maqburi said: It is Damascus. Ibn Wahb and Ashab narrated it on the authority of Malik. Muhammad bin Kaab said: It is Alexandria.
89:8: 8- The like of which had not been created in any land This is an attribute of Aad: that is, the like of that tribe had not been created in height, strength, and power. They are the ones who said, Who is stronger than us? Or an attribute of the village according to the opinion of those who said: Iram was the name of their village or the land they lived in. The first is more appropriate, and is indicated by the reading of Abi, The like of which had not been created in any land. It was said that Iram means destruction. Ad-Dahhak said, Iram of the Pillars: that is, He destroyed them and turned them into dust, and Shahr ibn Hawshab said the same. A group of commentators have mentioned that Iram of the Pillars is the name of a city built of gold and silver, its palaces, houses, and orchards, and that its pebbles were gems and its soil was musk. It had no companions or inhabitants from among the children of Adam, and that it kept moving from place to place, sometimes in Yemen, sometimes in Syria, sometimes in Iraq, and sometimes in other countries. This is a blatant lie that would not be supported by anyone with the slightest discernment. Al-Tha'labi added to his interpretation, saying: "Abdullah bin Qilabah entered this city during the time of Mu'awiyah. This is lie upon lie and slander upon slander. Islam and its people have been afflicted with a terrible calamity, great misfortune, and a major tragedy because of the example of these liars and impostors who dare to lie, sometimes about the Children of Israel, sometimes about the Prophets, sometimes about the righteous, and sometimes about the Lord of the Worlds. This evil has multiplied and increased in number because of the leadership of a group of those who have no knowledge of the authenticity of narrations from the weak and the fabricated, in classifying and interpreting the Noble Book. They have introduced these various superstitions, fabricated tales, and concocted myths into the interpretation of the Book of God, the Most High. They have distorted, changed, and altered. Whoever wants to understand some of what we have mentioned should look at my book, which I have entitled "The Collected Benefits of Fabricated Hadiths."
89:9: Then the Almighty linked the other tribe, which is Thamud, to the tribe of Aad, saying: 9- And Thamud who hewed out the rocks in the valley. They are the people of Salih, and they were named after their grandfather Thamud bin Aabir bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah. The meaning of hewed out the rock is to cut it. Jawb means to cut, and from this he jaab al-bilad means to cut it, and from this the name jib al-qamis is given because it means to cut. The commentators said: The first to carve mountains and rocks were Thamud, so they built 1700 cities, all of them from stone. From this is His Almighty saying: They carve out of the mountains, homes, secure. They used to carve out the mountains and excavate them, and make those excavations into homes to live in. His saying, in the valley is related to hewed out, or to an omitted word as a state of the rock, which is Wadi al-Qura. The majority read Thamud without inflection as the name of the tribe, so it contains femininity and definiteness. Yahya ibn Waththab read it with the declension as her father's name. The majority also read Bilwad without the yaa in both connected and paused pronunciation, following the orthography of the Qur'an. Ibn Kathir read it with it in both. Qanbal, in a narration from him, read it with it in connected pronunciation but not paused.
89:10: 10- And Pharaoh, the lord of the stakes, meaning he had soldiers who had many tents that they fastened with stakes. Or he made the soldiers themselves stakes because they fastened the king as stakes fastened tents. It was also said that he had stakes with which he tortured people and tied them to them. This was explained previously in Surat Sad.
89:11: 11- Those who transgressed in the land The relative pronoun is an attribute of Aad, Thamud, and Pharaoh: that is, each group of them transgressed in their land, rebelled, and acted insolently. Transgression is exceeding the limit.
89:12: 12- And they increased corruption therein through disbelief, disobedience to God, and injustice towards His servants. It is possible for the relative pronoun to be in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject: meaning, they are the ones who transgressed, or in the accusative case as a form of blame.
89:13: 13- So your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment meaning He poured down upon them and cast down upon those groups a scourge of punishment, which is what He punished them with. Al-Zajjaj said: He made the sound with which He struck them the punishment. It is said: He poured down a cloak upon someone, meaning He threw it upon him. From this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: So God poured the best dye on him, and he had a supporter among the people. And from it the other said: Have you not seen that God has made His religion manifest and poured upon the disbelievers a scourge of torment? The meaning of [whip] of torment: a portion of torment. The mention of the whip is an indication that the great torment that He brought upon them in this world is like a whip in comparison to what He has prepared for them in the Hereafter when compared to all other torments. It was said that the whip was mentioned to indicate the severity of what befell them, and the whip was, for them, the ultimate torment. Al-Farra’ said: It is a word that the Arabs say for every type of torment. The origin of that is that the whip is their torment with which they are tormented, so it was used for every torment if it is, for them, the ultimate torment. It was said that its meaning is: a torment that mixes with flesh and blood, from their saying saatahu yaswatuhu swata’an: meaning he mixed it. So the whip is the mixing of one thing with another, and from this is the saying of Ka’b ibn Zuhair: But it is a trait that has been controlled by her blood, grief, passion, disloyalty and change The other said: Oh, if our blood were to be spilled, it would flow until no blood touches another. Another said: Its middle is a reprehensible opinion and not successful, so I am not able to level it with meanings
89:14: 14- Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. We have already mentioned the statement of those who said that this is the answer to the oath. The first is that the answer is omitted, and this sentence is an explanation of what preceded it, and it indicates that the same thing that happened to those unbelievers will happen to the disbelievers of his people, peace and blessings be upon him. The meaning of ever watchful is that He watches the deeds of every person until He rewards them for good with good and for evil with evil. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: That is, the path of the servants is upon Him, and no one escapes Him. Watchful and watchful: the path. Its explanation was presented in Surah Bara'ah, and it was also presented in His statement: Indeed, Hell is ever an ambush. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, By the dawn, that he said: The dawn of the day. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority that he said: It means the dawn prayer. Sa'id ibn Mansur, Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab, and Ibn Asakir also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, By the dawn, that he said: It is Muharram, the dawn of the year. Authentic hadiths have been reported about the virtue of fasting the month of Muharram, but they do not indicate that it is what is meant by the verse, neither by conformity, nor by implication, nor by commitment. Ahmad, Al-Nasa'i, Al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: By the dawn, and ten nights, and the even and the odd. He said: The ten are the ten days of Al-Adha, and the odd is the Day of Arafah, and the even is the Day of Sacrifice. In another version: They are the nights of Dhul-Hijjah. Abd ibn Humayd narrated on the authority of Talha ibn Abdullah that he and Abu Salamah ibn Abdur-Rahman entered upon Ibn Umar. Ibn Umar invited them to lunch on the Day of Arafah. Abu Salamah said, Aren’t these the ten nights that God mentioned in the Qur’an? Ibn Umar said, How do you know? He said, I have no doubt. He said, Yes, and he had doubts. There are hadiths that have been narrated about the virtues of these ten nights, but none of them indicates that they are what is meant by what is mentioned in the Qur’an here in any way. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement, and ten nights, that they are the last ten days of Ramadan. Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about the even and the odd prayers, and he said, They are prayers, some of which are even and some of which are odd. In its chain of transmission is an unknown man, who is the one who narrated it on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn. It has been narrated on the authority of Imran ibn ‘Isam on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn without the unknown man being mentioned. Al-Tirmidhi said, after narrating it with the chain of transmission that includes the unknown man: It is a strange hadith that we do not know of except through the hadith of Qatadah. Ibn Kathir said: I think that stopping it with Imran ibn Husayn is more likely, and God knows best. He said: Ibn Jarir did not definitively say anything about the even and the odd. Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Jarir narrated this hadith with its chain of transmission ending with Imran ibn Husayn, so this strengthens what Ibn Kathir said. Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, and the even and the odd, he said: Everything that is even is two, and the odd is one. At-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, and As-Suyuti said with a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Ayyub, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “He was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: Two days and a night, the Day of Arafah and the Day of Sacrifice, and the odd is the night of Sacrifice, the night of Jumu’ah.” Ibn Jarir narrated from Jabir that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The even are the two days, and the odd is the third day. Abdur-Razzaq, Saeed bin Mansour, Ibn Saad, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr that he was asked about the even and the odd, so he said: The even is the statement of God, the Most High: But whoever hastens [to perform the ritual prayer] in two days, there is no sin upon him (al-Sha’b 4:17), and the odd is the third day. In another version: The odd is the middle of the days of Tashreeq. Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Sha’b narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The even is the Day of Sacrifice and the odd is the Day of Arafah. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority: And by the night when it departs he said: When it departs. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he recited And by the dawn until the verse: When it departs he said: This is an oath that your Lord is watching. Al-Faryabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bayhaqi in Ash-Sha’b narrated through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement: An oath to one of reason he said: To one of reason, intellect and foresight. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding his statement: Baad * Iram he said: By Iram he means the one who is doomed. Don't you see that you say Iram, the sons of so-and-so, of the pillars meaning their height is like pillars. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Miqdam bin Ma'di Karib "on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he mentioned "Iram of the pillars" and said: A man from them would come to a rock, carry it on his shoulder and throw it on any tribe he wanted, thus destroying them." In its chain of transmission is an unknown man because Mu'awiyah bin Salih narrated it on the authority of someone who narrated it to him on the authority of Al-Miqdam. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: they carved out the rocks in the valley he said: they pierced them. Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority regarding the verse: he said: they carved houses out of the mountains. And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes he said: The stakes are the soldiers who strengthen his command. Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to Ibn Masoud, regarding the verse: Of the Stakes, he said: Pharaoh staked his wife with four stakes, then he placed a huge millstone on her back until she died. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful, he said: He hears and sees. Al-Hakim narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to Ibn Masoud, regarding the verse: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful, he said: Beyond the Sirat are bridges: a bridge over which is trust, a bridge over which is kinship, and a bridge over which is the Lord, the Almighty and Majestic.
89:15: When He, the Almighty, mentioned that He is watching, He mentioned what indicates the difference in the conditions of His servants when they encounter good and when they encounter evil, and that the aspiration of their eyes and most of their goals is this world, so He said: 15- But as for man, when his Lord tests him meaning tests him and tries him with blessings and honors him and favors him meaning honors him with money and expands his provision he says, ‘My Lord has honored me’ rejoicing in what he has attained and delighted with what he has been given, not thanking God for that, nor does it occur to him that this is a test for him from his Lord and a trial of his condition and a revelation of what he contains of patience, impatience, gratitude for the blessing and ingratitude for it. What is in His saying: when is redundant, and His saying: and honors him and favors him is an explanation of the test, and the meaning of honored me is that He favors me with what He has given me of money and bestows upon me of blessings due to my greater deserving of that and my being a subject for it, and man is the subject, and its predicate is, so He says, My Lord Akramna, and the letter Fa was added to it to include the meaning of the condition and the adverbial phrase between the subject and the predicate, even if it came first in wording, it came after in meaning: that is, as for man, he says, My Lord, honor me at the time of his trial with bounty. Al-Kalbi said: Man is the disbeliever, Abi bin Khalaf. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Umayyah bin Khalaf, and it was said that it was revealed about Utbah bin Rabi’ah and Abi Hudhayfah bin Al-Mughira.
89:16: 16- And when He tests him that is, tests him and treats him as someone who tests him and restricts his provision that is, restricts it and does not expand it for him, nor does He expand it for him then he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me’ that is, He has treated me with disgrace. This is the description of the disbeliever who does not believe in the Resurrection, for he has no honor except this world and the expansion of its pleasures, and no humiliation except missing it and not attaining what he wants of its adornments. As for the believer, honor for him is that God honors him through his obedience and grants him success in the work of the Hereafter. It is possible that it is meant for man in general because of his lack of awareness that what he has attained of good and what he has suffered of evil in this world is only for choice and testing, and that this world as a whole is not worth a mosquito’s wing to God, and if it were worth a mosquito’s wing, He would not have given the disbeliever among us a drink of water. Nafi’ recited with the addition of the ya’ in akramaan and ahannan in connection and deleting them in stopping. Ibn Kathir, in the narration of Al-Bazzi from him, and Ibn Muhaisin and Ya’qub, recited with the addition of them in connection and stopping. The rest recited with the deletion of them in connection and stopping, following the orthography of the Qur’an and to agree with the beginnings of the verses. The original is to add it because it is a noun. Among the deletions is the saying of the poet: And the one whose age is apparent when he is standing up for it, they deny it That is, he denied me. The majority read fa-qadar with a light yaa, while Ibn ‘Amir read it with a heavy yaa, and these are two dialects. Al-Hamyan and Abu ‘Amr read rabbi with a fatha on the yaa in both cases, while the rest made it sukun.
89:17: And His statement: 17- No is a deterrent and rebuke to the person who said what he said in both cases, because God, the Exalted, may expand provision and expand blessings for a person, not to honor him, and restrict it for him, not to humiliate him, but to test and examine him, as mentioned above. Al-Farra' said: No in this instance means that the servant should not have been like this, but rather he should praise God for wealth and poverty. Then God, the Exalted, moved from explaining the evil of man's words to explaining his evil deeds, saying: Rather, you do not honor the orphan. The shift to the address is for the purpose of rebuking and reprimanding, according to the majority reading, with the superior form. The majority read you urge, "you eat, and you love" with the superior form as the address in them. Abu Amr and Ya'qub read them with the subjunctive form, and the plural in these verbs is based on the meaning of "human," because what is meant by it is the genus: that is, rather, you have deeds that are uglier than what was mentioned, which is that you neglect honoring the orphan, so you consume his wealth and prevent him from the surplus of your wealth. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Qudamah ibn Maz’un, who was an orphan in the care of Umayyah ibn Khalaf.
89:18: 18- And do not urge one another to feed the poor. The majority of scholars read tahādhunu from ḍah ala kadha meaning to tempt him with it, and its object is omitted: meaning do not urge yourselves, or do not urge one another to that, nor command it, nor guide one another to it. The Kufians read tahādhunu with a fat-ha on the ta’ and the ha’ followed by an alif, and its original form is tahādhunu, but one of the two ta’s was omitted: meaning do not urge one another. Al-Kisa’i, in a narration from him, and Al-Salami read tahādhunu with a damma on the ta’ from al-ḍhād, which means to urge. His statement, ‘ala ta’mīm al-miskin is related to tahādhunu, which is either a verbal noun, meaning to feed the poor, or a name for the food, and it is with an omitted complement, meaning to provide food to the poor, or to give food to the poor.
89:19: 19- And you devour the inheritance Its origin is warath, then the taa was replaced with the damma waw, as in the words tijaah and wajah, and what is meant by it is the money of orphans who inherit from their relatives, as well as the money of women, because they did not give inheritance to women and children and they ate their money eating what meaning eating heavily, and it was said that the meaning of what they gathered, from their saying: I lammat the food: if you ate it all. Al-Hasan said: He eats his share and the share of the orphan, and Abu Ubaidah said the same. The origin of lam in the speech of the Arabs is: gathering, it is said that I lammat the thing lammah lamma: I gathered it, and from this is their saying: God lammed sha’tahu: meaning he gathered what was scattered of his affairs, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: I will not leave a brother who does not blame you for his disheveled hair. Al-Layth said: “Al-Lam means to gather intensely. From this comes the word ‘a gathered stone’ and ‘a gathered battalion’. The eater gathers the tharid, collects it, and then eats it.” Mujahid said: He fools foolishly. Ibn Zayd said: When he eats his own money, he gathers the money of others and eats it, without thinking about what he has eaten of bad and good.
89:20: 20- And you love money with an intense love meaning a great deal of love. A great deal means a lot. It is said that the water is abundant in the basin, meaning it is plentiful and collects. A great deal means the place where water collects.
89:21: Then the Almighty repeated the deterrence and warning to them, saying: 21- No! meaning, this is not how you should act. Then the Almighty resumed, saying: When the earth is pounded to powder, and in it is a warning to them after the deterrence and warning. Dakk means breaking and pounding, and the meaning here is that it was shaken and moved, one movement after another. Ibn Qutaybah said: Its mountains were pounded to powder until they were level. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning they shook and crushed each other. Al-Mubarrad said: meaning they were spread out and their height was gone. Walak said: The high place was brought down by spreading out. We have previously discussed pounding in Surat Al-A'raf and in Surat Al-Ahqaf, and the meaning is that it was pounded time after time. The accusative of the first Dakkan is as a verbal noun emphasizing the verb, and the second Dakka is an emphasis on the first, as Ibn Asfour said. The accusative case may be in the state of being: that is, in the state of it being crushed time after time, as one says: I taught him arithmetic, chapter by chapter, and I taught him writing, letter by letter. The meaning is: He repeatedly crushed it until it became scattered dust.
89:22: 22- And your Lord has come meaning His command and decree came and His signs appeared. It was said that the meaning is that doubts were removed on that day and knowledge was made apparent and became necessary, just as doubt is removed when something that was doubted comes. It was also said that His dominance and authority came, and that He is the only One in command and management, without assigning any of His servants any of that. And the angels, rank upon rank is in the accusative case of rank upon rank as a state: meaning lined up, or with ranks. Ata’ said: He means the ranks of the angels, and the people of each heaven are a row on their own. Ad-Dahhak said: When the people of each heaven descend on the Day of Resurrection, they will be in a row surrounding the earth and everyone in it, so they will be seven rows.
89:23: 23- And Hell will be brought forth on that Day That Day is in the accusative case because of the verb to bring forth, and the one who takes the place of the subject of Hell. Makki considered it possible that that Day will be the one who takes the place of the subject, but that is not the case. Al-Wahidi said: A group of commentators said: It will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection, bound by seventy thousand reins, with each rein being seventy thousand angels pulling it until it is placed on the left of the Throne, and there will not remain any close angel or sent prophet who will not kneel, saying, O Lord, my soul, my soul. And what this is transmitted from a group of commentators, traced back to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), will come, God willing. On that Day man will remember This That Day is a replacement for the previous That Day: that is, on the day Hell will be brought forth, man will remember. That is, he will be admonished and remember what he missed and regret what he did in this world of disbelief and sins. It was said that his saying: On that second day is a substitute for his saying: When it is crushed and the factor in both of them is his saying: Man will remember “And how will he remember?” meaning, and from where will he remember and take heed? And it was said that it is with the omission of an adjective: meaning, and from where will he benefit from the remembrance? Al-Zajjaj said: Repentance is apparent, and from where is the repentance?
89:24: 24- He says, ‘Oh, I wish I had sent forth good deeds for my life’ The sentence is a resumption of the answer to an implied question, as if it was said: What does a person say? It is also permissible for it to be a badal ishtimal from his saying: He remembers, and the meaning is: He wishes that he had sent forth good deeds and righteous actions. The lam in ‘for my life’ means for the sake of my life, and what is meant is the life of the hereafter, for it is life in truth, because it is eternal and uninterrupted. It was said that the lam means ‘in’, and what is meant is the life of this world: that is, ‘Oh, I wish I had sent forth righteous deeds during my life in this world so that I might benefit from them today’. The first is more appropriate. Al-Hasan said: By God, he knew that he would experience a long life in which there would be no death.
89:25: 25- On that Day, no one will be punished with His punishment. That is, on the day that the time mentioned of the circumstances will come to pass, no one will be punished with the punishment of God.
89:26: 26- And no one shall be bound like his binding or no one shall undertake the punishment and binding of God except Him, since the matter is entirely His. The two pronouns in both estimations in His punishment and binding are God, the Almighty and Majestic, and this is according to the reading of the majority, punishes and binds are in the active form. Al-Kisa'i read them in the passive form, so the two pronouns refer to the human being: that is, no one shall be punished like the punishment of that human being, and no one shall be bound like his binding. What is meant by the human being is the disbeliever: that is, no one who is not a disbeliever shall be punished like the punishment of the disbeliever. It was said that it refers to Iblis, and it was said that it refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is that no one shall be punished like the punishment of this specific disbeliever, and no one shall be bound with chains and shackles like his binding, due to his extreme disbelief and stubbornness. It was said that the meaning is that no one will be tormented in his place, nor will anyone be chained in his place, so no ransom will be taken from him. It is like His statement: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Torment means torture, and chaining means binding. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose the reading of Al-Kisa’i. He said: The ha’ in both instances is a pronoun for the disbeliever, because it is established that no one will be tormented like the torment of God. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: It is permissible for the pronoun to refer to the disbeliever according to the reading of the group: that is, no one will torment anyone like the torment of this disbeliever.
89:27: When the Almighty finished narrating the conditions of the wretched, He mentioned some of the conditions of the happy, saying: 27- O reassured soul. The reassured soul is the one that is calm and certain of faith and the Oneness of God, and has reached the snow of certainty such that no doubt or suspicion mingles with it. Al-Hasan said: It is the believing, certain soul. Mujahid said: It is the one satisfied with God's decree, knowing that what missed it could not have befallen it, and that what befell it could not have missed it. Muqatil said: It is the one who is safe and reassured. Ibn Kaysan said: It is the one who is reassured by the remembrance of God. It was also said: It is the one who is sincere. Ibn Zayd said: It is the one who is reassured because she is given good tidings of Paradise at death and at the resurrection.
89:28: 28- Return to your Lord meaning return to God pleased with the reward He has given you pleasing to Him. It was also said that it was said that it was said that it was said that it was said that it was to His appointed time, and it was also said that it was to His command. Ikrimah and Ata’ said: The meaning of Return to your Lord is to the body you were in, and Ibn Jarir preferred this. This is indicated by the reading of Ibn Abbas, So enter into My servant in the singular, but the first is more appropriate.
89:29: 29- So enter among My servants meaning among the group of My righteous servants, and be among them and join their ranks.
89:30: 30- And enter My Paradise with them. It was said that she will be told to return to her Lord when she leaves this world, and she will be told: Enter among My servants and enter My Paradise on the Day of Resurrection. What is meant by the verse is every reassured soul in general, and this does not contradict its being revealed for a specific soul, so the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason. Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, devouring what, he said: a great deal. And regarding his statement, a great deal of grain, he said: very much. And Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, devouring what, he said: very much. And Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, when the earth is pounded to powder, he said: it is moved. Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Hell will be brought forth on that Day with seventy thousand reins, with each rein seventy thousand angels pulling it. And Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and how will he be remembered? He said: How will he be? And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on his authority, regarding his statement, on that Day no one will be punished verse, he said: No one will be punished with the punishment of God, and no one will be bound with the bonds of God. Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Dhiya in Al-Mukhtara also narrated from him regarding the statement of God, O reassured soul, he said: the believing one. Return to your Lord, he said: to your body. He said: “This verse was revealed while Abu Bakr was sitting, so he said: O Messenger of God, how good this is. He said: This will indeed be said to you.” Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu`aym in Al-Hilyah narrated a similar mursal from Sa`id ibn Jubayr. Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi narrated a similar mursal from Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq in Nawadir Al-Usul. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, O reassured soul, the one who believes. Ibn Jarir also narrated from him regarding the verse, he said: the souls will be returned to the bodies on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding the statement of God, Return to your Lord, well-pleased, he said: with what you have been given of reward, well-pleased with its deeds, and enter among My servants, the believers. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: Ibn Abbas died in Taif, and a bird that had never been seen before came and entered his coffin, then did not come out of it. When he was buried, this verse was recited on the edge of the grave, but we do not know who recited it: O reassured soul, * Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing * And enter among My servants * And enter My Paradise. Abu Nu`aym narrated a similar verse in Al-Dala’il on the authority of Ikrimah.
90:1: It is said that Surat La Aqsam consists of twenty verses. It is Meccan without dispute. Ibn Al-Durais, An-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Surat Al-I swear by this city was revealed in Mecca. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar narration on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr. His saying: 1- I do not swear is an extra la, and the meaning is I swear by this country. We have already discussed this in the interpretation of I do not swear by the Day of Resurrection. Among the extra la in speech other than in an oath is the poet’s saying: I remembered Laila, and I felt a sense of longing, and my heart almost didn't crack. That is, it cracks. And from that is His statement: What prevented you from prostrating? That is, from prostrating. Al-Wahidi said: The commentators agreed that this is an oath by the Sacred City, which is Mecca. The majority read I swear, but Al-Hasan and Al-A’mash read I swear without an alif. It was said that it is a negation of the oath, and the meaning is: I do not swear by this city if you are not in it after you leave it. Mujahid said: There is no response to the one who denies the resurrection, then he began by saying I swear, and the meaning is: The matter is not as you think, but the first is more appropriate. The meaning is: I swear by the Sacred City in which you are residing. Al-Wasiti said: What is meant by the city is Medina, and while it is contrary to the consensus of the commentators, it is also refuted by the fact that the surah was revealed in Mecca, not Medina.
90:2: And the sentence of his statement: 2- And you are residing in this country is parenthetical, and the meaning is: I swear by this country.
90:3: 3- "And by a father and that which he begot. Indeed, We created man into toil." This sentence was interrupted between them, and the meaning is: And among the hardships is that someone like you, whose sanctity is great to Me, would be made permissible in this country just as hunting is made permissible outside the sanctuary. Al-Wahidi said: Permissibility, lawful, and place of abode are one and the same, and it is the opposite of forbidden. God made Mecca permissible for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of the conquest until he fought. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "It was not permissible for anyone before me, and it will not be permissible for anyone after me. It was only permissible for me for an hour of a day." He said: The meaning is that when God mentioned the oath by Mecca, this indicated its great value despite it being sacred. So He promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He would make it permissible for him until he fought in it and conquered it through his hand. This is a promise from God Almighty that He would make it permissible for him so that he would be permissible in it. End quote. So the meaning is: And you will be permissible in this country in the future, as in His statement: Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die. Mujahid said: The meaning is that whatever you do in it, you are permissible. Qatada said: You are residing in it and you are not sinful: meaning that you are not committing in this land what is forbidden for you to commit, unlike the polytheists who commit disbelief and sins therein. It was said that the meaning is: I do not swear by this land while you are residing in it and it is your place. According to the view that la is a negative particle that is not redundant, the meaning would be: I do not swear by it while you are residing in it, so you are more deserving of being sworn to. According to the view that it is redundant, the meaning would be: I swear by this land where you are residing as an honor to you and to glorify your status because it has become great and noble by your residency in it, and has increased over and above what it was of honor and greatness. However, this is if it is established in the Arabic language that the word hal comes with the meaning of hal, and just as it is permissible for the sentence to be parenthetical, it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a state, and a father and that which he begot is in apposition to al-balad. Qatada, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan and Abu Salih said: And the father means Adam, and what was born means and what was born from his children. He swore by them because they are the most amazing thing that God created on the face of the earth because of what they possess of eloquence, intellect and management, and among them are prophets, scholars and righteous people. Abu Imran Al-Jawni said: The father is Abraham, and what was born are his offspring. Al-Farra’ said: Ma refers to people, like His statement: what is good for you. It was also said that the father is Abraham, and the offspring is Ishmael and Muhammad, peace be upon him. Ikrimah and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: And the father means the one to whom children are born, and what was born means the barren woman who does not have children. It is as if they made ma a negative, but this is far-fetched. This is not correct except by implying the relative pronoun: that is, and the father and what was born. Implying the relative pronoun is not permissible according to the Basrans. Atiyyah Al-Awfi said: It is general and applies to every parent and offspring of all animals, and this is the preferred opinion of Ibn Jarir.
90:4: 4- Indeed, We created man into toil. This is the answer to the oath, and man is this human species, and liver: hardship and difficulty. It is said I suffered the matter: I endured its severity, and man continues to struggle with the world and endure its hardships until he dies. The origin of liver is severity, and from it the word to harden milk: if it becomes thick and intense, and it is said a man’s liver is pain: if his liver is in pain, then it is used for every severity and hardship, and from it the saying of Abu Al-Asbagh: I have a cousin who, if people were in trouble, would still be holding back arrows and throwing them at me. Al-Hasan said: He endures the calamities of this world and the hardships of the Hereafter. He also said: He endures gratitude for prosperity, and endures patience in adversity. He is never without one of the two. Al-Kalbi said: This verse was revealed about a man from Banu Jumah called Abu Al-Ashdayn. He used to take a leather skin and put it under his feet and say: Whoever removes me from him will have such-and-such. He would pull it ten times until it was torn apart but his feet would not move. He would put it under his feet and say: Whoever removes me from him will have such-and-such. He would pull it ten times until it was torn apart but his feet would not move. He was one of the enemies of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
90:5: And in it was revealed 5- Does he think that no one will have power over him? meaning because of his strength, and the meaning of in a liver in this case is: in a strong nature, and it was said that the meaning of in a liver is that he is bold of heart and hard of liver. Does he think that no one will have power over him? meaning that the son of Adam thinks that no one will have power over him and that no one will take revenge on him, or Abu al-Ashdayn thinks that no one will have power over him, and that is the lightened form of the heavy form, and its subject is a pronoun of an implied matter.
90:6: Then God the Almighty informed us about this man's statement, saying: 6- He will say, 'I have spent a great deal of wealth,' meaning, a great deal of it accumulated on top of one another. Al-Layth said: Wealth accumulated is wealth that is not feared to perish due to its great amount. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: He says, I have spent a great deal of wealth in enmity towards Muhammad. Muqatil said: This was revealed about Al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal: He sinned, so he sought a fatha from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who ordered him to atone. He said, My wealth has been spent on atonements and expenses since I entered the religion of Muhammad. The majority of scholars read labdan with a damma on the lam and a fatha on the ba with a shaddah. Abu Ubaidah said: Labda is a verb from talbid, which means a great deal of wealth piled up on top of one another. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a verb for abundance. It is said that a man has smashed a lot, if he smashes a lot. Al-Farra' said: The singular form is labdah, and the plural is labd. This has been explained previously in Surah Al-Jinn.
90:7: 7- "Does he think that no one saw him?" That is, does he think that no one saw him? Qatada said: Does he think that God, the Exalted, did not see him or ask him about his money, from where he earned it, and where he spent it? Al-Kalbi said: He was lying and did not spend what he said, so God said: Does he think that God did not see that from him, whether he did it or did not do it, whether he spent it or not?
90:8: Then God Almighty mentioned the blessings He bestowed upon them so that they might take heed. He said: 8- Did We not give him two eyes with which he could see?
90:9: 9- And a tongue with which he speaks, and two lips with which he covers his mouth. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, Did we not do to him what indicates that God is able to resurrect him? The lām of the word lip has been omitted, and its root is shufha lip, as evidenced by its diminutive form, shufīha.
90:10: 10- And We showed him the two high ways. Najd: the road is high. The commentators said: We showed him the path of good and the path of evil. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, did we not make known to him the path of good and the path of evil, showing him the two high roads. Ikrimah, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Al-Dahhak said: Najd: the two breasts because they are like the two roads for the child’s life and livelihood, and the first is more appropriate.
